The new gate was designed as a Roman triumphal arch, inspired by the Arch of Constantine in Rome, symbolizing Frederick the Great's victory.

Major_Events.Description: Two side entrances for pedestrians were added under Frederick William IV to accommodate increased pedestrian traffic.
The city wall was demolished, leaving the Brandenburg Gate as a free-standing structure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Brandenburg Gate features two distinct sides designed by two architects. The inner, city-facing side was designed by Carl von Gontard with a rendered facade, pilasters, and trophies. The outer side, designed by Georg Christian Unger, is more elaborate, resembling the Arch of Constantine with projecting Corinthian pairs of columns and prominent decorative sculpture. The gate uses the Corinthian order and resembles a Roman triumphal arch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Brandenburg Gate is culturally significant as a symbol of Frederick the Great's victories in the Seven Years' War. Its Roman-inspired architecture reflects the influence of classical antiquity in Prussian art and architecture. It also served as a key entry point to Potsdam, connecting the city to Brandenburg.
world knowledge.Details: The gate stands at the western end of Brandenburger Straße, leading into the city center pedestrian zone towards the Church of Peter and Paul. It was named after the town of Brandenburg, as people had to pass through it to reach the town.

world knowledge.Name: Zaisan Memorial
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Zaisan Memorial honors allied Mongolian and Soviet soldiers killed in World War II. It features a circular painting depicting scenes of friendship between the people of the USSR and Mongolia, including Soviet support for Mongolia's independence declaration in 1921, the defeat of the Japanese Kwantung Army at Khalhkin Gol in 1939, victory over Nazi Germany, and Soviet space flights such as Soyuz 39 which carried the first Mongolian into space, Jugderdemidiin Gurragchaa.

Major_Events.Description: A tank memorial, previously located on a crossroads between Zaisan and the city center, was moved to the foot of the hill. It features a Soviet tank from a brigade paid for by the Mongolian people, with a map showing the route the brigade took from Moscow in 1943 to its participation in the fall of Berlin in 1945.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The memorial includes a circular painting and a monument accessible by climbing three hundred steps from the uppermost parking lot on the hill.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The memorial is culturally significant as it commemorates the alliance between Mongolia and the USSR during World War II and celebrates their shared history and achievements.
world knowledge.Details: Zaisan is a popular meeting point for school outings and graduation festivities. In recent times, more and more modern luxury housing developments have popped up near the Zaisan region, making it popular as an elite residential district. Visitors who climb the steps are rewarded with a panoramic view of the entire city of Ulaanbaatar in the valley below, as well as the Tuul River flowing past the city.

world knowledge.Name: Flamborough Head
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Flamborough Head is a promontory on the Yorkshire coast of England, known for its sheer white chalk cliffs. It features two standing lighthouse towers, the oldest dating from 1669. The cliffs provide nesting sites for many thousands of seabirds and are of international significance for their geology. The headland has been designated a Special Area of Conservation and a Site of Special Scientific Interest. It has played a role in historical events such as the Battle of Flamborough Head during the American War of Independence.

Major_Events.Description: A Franco-American squadron fought the Battle of Flamborough Head with a pair of Royal Navy frigates in the American War of Independence on 23 September 1779. In the engagement, USS Bonhomme Richard and Pallas, with USS Alliance, captured HMS Serapis and HM hired armed ship Countess of Scarborough, the best-known incident of Captain John Paul Jones's naval career.
During the evening of 23 August 2006, a lightning bolt hit a buttress on the cliffs, sending 100 tonnes of rock into the sea.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The headland features two lighthouse towers, the oldest dating from 1669 and the Flamborough Head Lighthouse built in 1806. The cliffs exhibit a complete sequence of Chalk Group North Sea Basin strata, dated from 100 to 70 million years ago. The site includes cave habitats, stacks, natural arches, and blowholes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Flamborough Head is culturally and historically significant due to its role in the Battle of Flamborough Head, its designation as a Special Area of Conservation and a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and its importance as a habitat for seabirds. It has also been featured in literature and television programmes.
world knowledge.Details: Flamborough Head has been designated a Special Area of Conservation (SAC) by the British Government's Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC). The cliffs at Flamborough Head are designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest for both geological and biological significance. The headland is the only chalk sea cliff in the north and exhibits a complete sequence of Chalk Group North Sea Basin strata. Seabirds such as northern gannets, kittiwakes and Atlantic puffins breed abundantly on the cliffs. The site has been featured in the television programme Seven Natural Wonders and the ITV drama Scott & Bailey.

world knowledge.Name: Koza Han
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Koza Han is a historic caravanserai in Bursa, Turkey, built by Sultan Bayezid II in 1490. It was a significant center for silk trade during the Ottoman Empire, providing lodging for merchants, storage for goods, and workshops for craftsmen. The han has undergone several restorations and continues to house silk shops, cafés, and tea gardens.

Major_Events.Description: Sultan Bayezid II ordered the construction of the Koza Han.
The Koza Han opened in September 1491.
The han underwent restoration.
The han underwent restoration.
The han underwent restoration.
The small mosque at the center of the han was restored.
The small mosque at the center of the han was restored.
Queen Elizabeth II visited the han with Turkish President Abdullah Gül.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Koza Han is built in alternating layers of brick and stone, featuring a rectangular floor plan with a large central courtyard. It has a two-story gallery with small vaulted rooms, a central octagonal stone mosque on pillars, and a monumental stone and brick portal decorated with spiral moulding and geometric tile patterns.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Koza Han is culturally significant as a historic caravanserai that played a crucial role in the silk trade during the Ottoman Empire. It represents the economic and architectural heritage of Bursa, the first capital of the Ottoman Empire.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Caravanserai (lodging for merchants, storage for goods, workshops for craftsmen)
world knowledge.Details: The han is part of 'Bursa and Cumalıkızık: the Birth of the Ottoman Empire' and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014. It continues to house silk shops, cafés, and tea gardens, maintaining its historical role in the silk trade.

world knowledge.Name: Three Crosses
world knowledge.Address: Hill of Three Crosses, Kalnai Park, Vilnius, Lithuania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Three Crosses is a prominent monument in Vilnius, Lithuania, on the Hill of Three Crosses. According to legend, seven Franciscan friars were beheaded on this hill. Wooden crosses have been present since the early 17th century. In 1916, a concrete monument was designed by Antoni Wiwulski but was torn down in 1950 by Soviet authorities. A new monument was erected in 1989 by Stanislovas Kuzma after the design by Henrikas Šilgalis.

Major_Events.Event: Erection of the original concrete monument
Major_Events.Description: A concrete monument designed by Antoni Wiwulski was erected during German occupation in World War I.
The monument was torn down by Soviet authorities on May 30, 1950.
The monument was rebuilt by Stanislovas Kuzma after the design by Henrikas Šilgalis and unveiled on June 14, 1989.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument consists of three large crosses made of reinforced concrete. The rebuilt crosses are 1.8 meters higher than the original 1916 version.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Three Crosses are a symbol of Vilnius and its Christian heritage. They commemorate the martyrdom of Franciscan friars and have become an integral part of the city's skyline.
world knowledge.Details: The monument was depicted on the 50 litas banknote. A panorama of the Vilnius Old Town can be observed from a small observation deck at the base of the crosses. Broken pieces of the old monument can be seen several meters below the rebuilt monument.

world knowledge.Name: Tykocin Synagogue
world knowledge.Address: 2 Kozia Street, Tykocin, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tykocin Synagogue is an historic former Jewish synagogue building, completed in 1643 in the Mannerist-early Baroque style. It was disused as a synagogue during World War II, repurposed for profane uses, and later restored in the late 1970s to serve as a Jewish museum.

Major_Events.Event: Desecration and repurposing as a warehouse
Major_Events.Description: During the Nazi occupation of Poland, the synagogue was desecrated and then set up as a warehouse.
A fire damaged the interiors of the synagogue.
The synagogue was thoroughly restored in the late 1970s, including the historic wall paintings and the Torah Ark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in the Mannerist-early Baroque style using brick, featuring elaborate decorative wall paintings and a Torah Ark.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The synagogue is a significant historical site representing Jewish heritage in Poland, attracting 40,000 tourists annually and generating local economic activity.
world knowledge.Details: A former Beit Medrash across the street has been restored and is used as a city museum. Although no Jews live in Tykocin, the synagogue remains a tourist attraction with a cafe serving 'Jewish-style' food and a bed-and-breakfast.

world knowledge.Name: Place Kléber
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Largest square at the center of Strasbourg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Barfüsserplatz ('Square of the Barefoot Nuns') due to a Franciscan monastery, later renamed Waffenplatz ('Arms Square'), and finally Place Kléber in 1840 after French general Jean-Baptiste Kléber. During German occupation (1940–1944), it was renamed after Karl Roos. The square is central to Strasbourg's historic center, classified as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.

Major_Events.Description: The square was renamed in honor of French general Jean-Baptiste Kléber.
During German occupation, the square was renamed after Karl Roos, a local ethnically German politician.
Kléber's remains were buried under his statue in the square after being held at Château d'If for 18 years.
The inner decoration of the Aubette, destroyed in the 1930s, was restored and made accessible to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Aubette, built by Jacques François Blondel, features inner decoration by Hans Arp, Theo van Doesburg, and Sophie Taeuber-Arp, described as 'the Sistine Chapel of abstract art'. The square includes a statue of Kléber designed by Philippe Grass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The square is a central landmark in Strasbourg, reflecting the city's historical and cultural evolution. It honors Jean-Baptiste Kléber and serves as a hub for communal activities like the Christkindelsmärik (Christmas market). The Aubette's restoration highlights its importance in abstract art.
world knowledge.Details: A large fir tree (30 m) from the Vosges mountains is erected annually on the southwest of the square, where inhabitants deposit gifts for the poor during the Village du Partage ('Village for Sharing'). Kléber's heart is kept in an urn in the caveau of the Governors beneath the altar of the St. John Chapel in Les Invalides, Paris.

world knowledge.Name: Alcazaba of Badajoz
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 9th century, with major reconstructions in the 12th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alcazaba of Badajoz is an ancient Moorish citadel built by the Almohads in the 12th century, although it probably existed from the 9th century when Badajoz was founded. It served as the residence of the rulers of the taifa of Badajoz in the 11th and 12th centuries. It was declared a national monument of Spain in 1931. Badajoz was founded by Abd-al Rahman Ibn Marwan in 875. The current line of walls date mostly from the Almohad age, with traces of earlier work from 913 and 1030. The last Muslim restoration was carried out by Abu Yahya ibn Abi Sinan in the 13th century, shortly before the city was captured by the Christian King Alfonso IX of León. During the Peninsular War (1805-1813), the citadel was successfully stormed by allied-British, Spanish & Portuguese forces under the command of the Duke of Wellington.

Major_Events.Description: Badajoz was founded by Abd-al Rahman Ibn Marwan after he was expelled by Mérida but was given the chance to found a new city.
The Almohad caliph Abu Yaqub Yusuf rebuilt the fortress, giving it its current appearance.

Major_Events.Event: Capture by Christian King Alfonso IX of León
Major_Events.Description: The city was captured by the Christian King Alfonso IX of León after the last Muslim restoration by Abu Yahya ibn Abi Sinan.
The citadel was successfully stormed by allied-British, Spanish & Portuguese forces under the command of the Duke of Wellington, weakening the Napoleonic hold on Western Spain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The citadel is bounded by the Guadiana river and the Rivillas torrent. It features a parapet, towers, and a palace with several baths and mosques. The Great Mosque, which was turned into a church, Santa María de Calatrava, had five naves separated by arches supported by columns, and external buttresses. The Palace of the Dukes of Feria, built in Renaissance style with Mudéjar elements, has a trapezoidal plan and a cloister. The Espantaperros Tower, built in 1169, has an octagonal plan and is surmounted by a small temple added in Mudéjar style in the 16th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Alcazaba of Badajoz is culturally and historically important as it represents the Moorish influence in Spain, served as a residence for rulers, and played a strategic role in controlling the passage from Portugal to central Iberia. It was declared a national monument of Spain in 1931.
world knowledge.Details: The Alcazaba includes a large park and is home to the Provincial Archaeological Museum. The Great Mosque was converted into a church, Santa María de Calatrava, which acted as the cathedral of Badajoz until the construction of the current one. The Military Hospital, now home to the Library of Extremadura, was another building of the Muslim palace converted after the Christian conquest.

world knowledge.Name: Sof Omar Caves
world knowledge.Area: East Bale Province, Oromia Region, Ethiopia
world knowledge.Address: East Bale Zone, Oromia Region, Ethiopia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sof Omar Caves is the longest cave in Ethiopia at 15.1 kilometres (9.4 mi) long. It was the longest cave in Africa when surveyed in 1972. The caves are sacred to both Islam and the local Oromo traditional religion. They are known for their many pillars, particularly in the 'Chamber of Columns'. The site was added to UNESCO's tentative list in 2011.

Major_Events.Description: The caves were discovered in 1897.
Arthur Donaldson Smith recorded his visit to the cave in 1894.
An Italian expedition visited the caves in 1913.
Henri Breuil conducted archaeological investigations in the area in 1934.

Major_Events.Event: Exploration and Survey by Eric Robson, Chris Clapham, and Kabir Ahmed
Major_Events.Description: Eric Robson, Chris Clapham, and Kabir Ahmed explored and surveyed the cave, recording 8 km of passage.
A British Expedition to Ethiopia explored and surveyed the caves, discovering 6.1 kilometres (3.8 mi) of new passages, bringing the survey total to 15.1 kilometres (9.4 mi).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cave is formed along a network of joints: one set runs approximately north to south and the other east to west. This zig-zag of passages runs in an approximately southeasterly direction. Sof Omar has 42 entrances, but generally only four are useful for gaining entrance. The cave features the 'Chamber of Columns', a unique feature in the world of caves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The caves are sacred both to Islam and the local Oromo traditional religion. They have long been a religious center and are known for their many pillars, particularly in the 'Chamber of Columns'.
world knowledge.Details: The caves are situated to the east of Ginnir, in the East Bale Zone of the Oromia Region in southeastern Ethiopia, through which the Weyib River (Gestro River) flows. The caves are known for their many pillars, particularly in the 'Chamber of Columns'. The site was added to UNESCO's tentative list in 2011. The caves have been explored and surveyed by various expeditions, including a British Expedition in 1972 that discovered 6.1 kilometres (3.8 mi) of new passages, bringing the survey total to 15.1 kilometres (9.4 mi).

world knowledge.Name: Tarrafal de São Nicolau
world knowledge.Location: Western part of the island of São Nicolau
world knowledge.Address: Tarrafal de São Nicolau Municipality, São Francisco de Assis, 3121, Cape Verde
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tarrafal de São Nicolau is a city in the western part of the island of São Nicolau, Cape Verde. It became an anchorage for whaling ships in the 19th century, and fish processing infrastructure was built, leading to further growth of the settlement. The settlement became a town in the early 1990s and a city in 2010. The port of Tarrafal was constructed in 1991.

Major_Events.Description: The settlement of Tarrafal de São Nicolau became a town in the early 1990s.
Tarrafal de São Nicolau was elevated to city status in 2010.
The port of Tarrafal was constructed in 1991, featuring 2 quays, a roll-on/roll-off ramp, and a passenger terminal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The port of Tarrafal features 2 quays, a roll-on/roll-off ramp, and a passenger terminal. The total length of the quays is 137 m, and the maximum depth is 7 m.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tarrafal de São Nicolau is culturally significant as the most populous settlement on the island of São Nicolau and as the main port of the island, facilitating connections to other islands in Cape Verde.
world knowledge.Details: Tarrafal de São Nicolau has ferry connections to the islands of São Vicente (Mindelo) and Santiago (Praia).

world knowledge.Name: Bodleian Library
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bodleian Library is the main research library of the University of Oxford, founded in 1602 by Sir Thomas Bodley. It is one of the oldest libraries in Europe and the second-largest in Britain. It operates under the Legal Deposit Libraries Act 2003, making it one of six legal deposit libraries for works published in the UK. The library has a continuous history dating back to 1602, with roots in the 14th century under Thomas Cobham, Bishop of Worcester. It was revitalized by Thomas Bodley in 1598 and formally re-opened in 1602.

Major_Events.Description: The library was formally re-opened under the name 'Bodleian Library' after being revitalized by Sir Thomas Bodley.
Thomas Bodley made an agreement with the Stationers' Company to receive a copy of every book registered with them, significantly expanding the library's collection.
The New Bodleian building was completed, designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, to provide additional space for the library's growing collection.
The New Bodleian building was rebuilt and reopened as the Weston Library, offering improved facilities for readers and visitors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Bodleian Library occupies a group of five buildings: the 15th-century Duke Humfrey's Library, the 17th-century Schools Quadrangle, the 18th-century Clarendon Building and Radcliffe Camera, and the 20th- and 21st-century Weston Library. The Schools Quadrangle features the Tower of the Five Orders, ornamented with columns of each of the five orders of classical architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bodleian Library is one of the most important academic libraries in the world, with a vast collection of over 13 million items. It has played a crucial role in the preservation and dissemination of knowledge, serving as a legal deposit library and a major research hub. Its historical significance and architectural beauty make it a cultural icon.
world knowledge.Details: The Bodleian Library operates as a reference library, and documents may not be removed from the reading rooms. It has a strict policy on copying material, with personal photocopying permitted for most post-1900 publications. The library's collections include books, journals, newspapers, magazines, sound and music recordings, maps, prints, drawings, and manuscripts. It also offers digital access to many of its archives through its Digital Bodleian service.

world knowledge.Name: Waverley Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Waverley Abbey, founded in 1128 by William Giffard, Bishop of Winchester, was the first Cistercian abbey in England. It served as the motherhouse to several other Cistercian monasteries. The abbey faced numerous challenges, including severe flooding and financial difficulties, leading to its suppression in 1536 during King Henry VIII's Dissolution of the Monasteries. The site has since been partially demolished, with its stone reused in local buildings.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by William Giffard, Bishop of Winchester, as the first Cistercian abbey in England.
The abbey was severely flooded, leading to crop failure and necessitating reconstruction.
Waverley Abbey was suppressed as part of King Henry VIII's Dissolution of the Monasteries.
Waverley Abbey House was converted into a military hospital, treating over 5,000 soldiers during World War I.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey followed the typical arrangement of English monasteries, with a church, cloister, chapter house, dormitories, and refectory. The remains include the vaulted undercroft of the lay brothers' refectory, walls of the monks' dormitory, and traces of the chapter house and church transepts. The site also features earthworks of fishponds and a water supply system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the first Cistercian abbey in England, Waverley Abbey holds significant historical and cultural importance. It played a crucial role in the spread of the Cistercian order in England and was the motherhouse to several other monasteries. The site has been featured in literature and film, adding to its cultural legacy.
world knowledge.Details: The ruins of Waverley Abbey are managed by English Heritage and are open to the public. The site includes a nearly 500-year-old yew tree, which won the UK Tree of the Year competition in 2022. The abbey precinct contains numerous WWII relics, including anti-tank gun emplacements and pillboxes. Waverley Abbey House, built within the former abbey precinct, is now used as a training and conference center by the Christian not-for-profit organisation, CWR.

world knowledge.Name: Cái Răng Floating Market
world knowledge.Area: Cái Răng district, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
world knowledge.Address: Hau River, near Cái Răng Bridge, about 7 kilometers from the center of Can Tho
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cái Răng Floating Market is a wholesale floating market specializing in the trade of vegetables and fruits on the Hau River. It developed because waterways played a near-exclusive role in transportation. As trade demand increased, people gathered at river junctions, making them ideal spots for trading. Today, although the road network has expanded significantly, leading to the disappearance of many floating markets, tourism activities have allowed Cái Răng Floating Market to evolve into a more sustainable form.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as a national intangible cultural heritage
Major_Events.Description: Cái Răng Floating Market was recognized as a national intangible cultural heritage by the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism of Vietnam.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The market is characterized by the use of boats, primarily 'ghe bầu' (large, flat-bottomed boats), as the main means of transport and loading. Each boat is like a floating house, equipped with potted plants, pets, and modern amenities like color TVs, DVD players, and motorbikes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cái Răng Floating Market is considered a cultural symbol of the waterway region, attracting many visitors, especially foreign tourists. It is one of the most prominent tourist attractions in Can Tho.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Wholesale market specializing in vegetables and fruits, and a unique tourist attraction
world knowledge.Details: The market opens at around 2–3 AM, with peak activity from 4–6 AM. Goods are advertised by hanging a sample of the goods on a long pole, a method known as 'beo hang.' The market is closed or operates on a limited basis during the Lunar New Year and Doan Ngo Festival. Visitors can reach the market by renting a boat at Ninh Kieu Wharf or by taking a car to An Binh Market and then renting a boat. The boat fare is 100,000 VND per person.

world knowledge.Name: Green Gate
world knowledge.Address: Between Long Market (Długi Targ) and the River Motława, Gdańsk, Poland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Green Gate in Gdańsk, Poland, is one of the city's most notable tourist attractions. It was built as the formal residence of Poland's monarchs and reflects Flemish architectural influence. It spans the Long Market and Long Street, together comprising the Royal Route. The Green Gate was inspired by the Antwerp City Hall.

Major_Events.Description: The future Queen of Poland, Marie Louise Gonzaga, was entertained here from 11–20 February 1646.
In the late 18th century, the Nature Society was housed here, but soon moved to the Naturalists' House (Research Society House).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Dutch-Flemish mannerism, inspired by the Antwerp City Hall. Designed by Reiner van Amsterdam, an Amsterdam architect, with construction plans by Hans Kramer from Dresden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Green Gate is culturally and historically important as it was built as the formal residence of Poland's monarchs and reflects Flemish architectural influence in Gdańsk. It is part of the Royal Route and is a notable tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Today, the Green Gate houses the National Museum in Gdańsk. It is used for exhibitions, meetings, conferences, and shows. The Gdańsk office of former Polish President Lech Wałęsa is located in one of the rooms.
world knowledge.Details: The Green Gate was designated as part of 'Gdańsk – city within the 17th-century fortifications' on 1994-09-08. It has a reference number M.P. 1994 nr 50 poz. 415 [ 1 ].

world knowledge.Name: Sidi Bou Said
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sidi Bou Said is a town in northern Tunisia named after Abu Said al-Baji, a religious figure who lived there. It was previously called Jbel el-Menar. In the 12th/13th century, Abu Said Ibn Khalaf Yahya al-Tamimi al-Beji established a sanctuary there and was buried there after his death in 1231. In the 18th century, wealthy citizens of Tunis built residences in Sidi Bou Said. During the 1920s, Rodolphe d'Erlanger introduced the blue-white theme to the town.

Major_Events.Description: Abu Said Ibn Khalaf Yahya al-Tamimi al-Beji established a sanctuary in the village of Jabal el-Menar.
Rodolphe d'Erlanger introduced the blue-white theme to the town.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town is known for its extensive use of blue and white colors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sidi Bou Said is a town of artists and has been home to or visited by many notable artists and intellectuals. It is also a significant tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: Sidi Bou Said can be reached by a TGM train from Tunis to La Marsa. Ennejma Ezzahra, the home of Rodolphe d'Erlanger, is now a museum with a collection of musical instruments and organizes concerts. The town has a reputation as a hub for artists and has been home to members of the École de Tunis. Former Tunisian President Beji Caid Essebsi and film director Moufida Tlatli were born in Sidi Bou Said. Azzedine Alaïa's house in the town is now an art gallery.

world knowledge.Name: Murambi Genocide Memorial Centre
world knowledge.Address: Near the town of Murambi, Rwanda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Murambi Technical School, now known as the Murambi Genocide Memorial Centre, is one of six major centres in Rwanda that commemorate the 1994 genocide against Tutsi in Rwanda. It was the site of a massacre during the 1994 Rwandan genocide where Tutsis were lured into a trap by the bishop and mayor, claiming that French troops would protect them. On April 16, 1994, an average of 65,000 Tutsis traveled to the school. After defending themselves for a few days using stones, the Tutsi were overrun on April 21. Some 20,000 Tutsi were murdered at the school, and almost all of those who managed to escape were killed the next day when they tried to hide in a nearby church. The memorial was founded on 21 April 1995 and contains 50,000 graves. The school building is now a genocide museum exhibiting the skeletons and mummified bodies of some of the thousands of people killed in Gikongoro Province in 1994.

Major_Events.Description: On April 16, 1994, an average of 65,000 Tutsis traveled to the school. After defending themselves for a few days using stones, the Tutsi were overrun on April 21. Some 20,000 Tutsi were murdered at the school, and almost all of those who managed to escape were killed the next day when they tried to hide in a nearby church.

The memorial was founded on 21 April 1995 and contains 50,000 graves. The school building is now a genocide museum exhibiting the skeletons and mummified bodies of some of the thousands of people killed in Gikongoro Province in 1994.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site contains 50,000 graves and the school building is now a genocide museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Murambi Genocide Memorial Centre is one of six major centres in Rwanda that commemorate the 1994 genocide against Tutsi in Rwanda. It serves as a reminder of the atrocities committed during the genocide and honors the victims.
world knowledge.Details: The site contains 50,000 graves. The school building is now a genocide museum exhibiting the skeletons and mummified bodies of some of the thousands of people killed in Gikongoro Province in 1994. Among the bodies currently displayed are those of children and infants. Only 34 people are thought to have survived the massacre in Murambi.

world knowledge.Name: Cabrini Medical Center
world knowledge.Address: 227 East 19th Street, New York, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cabrini Medical Center of New York City was created in 1973 by a merger of two Manhattan hospitals, Columbus Hospital and Italian Hospital. Columbus Hospital was founded in 1892 by the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus to address the needs of Italian immigrants. Italian Hospital was founded in 1937 by the Italian Hospital Society. The combined organization took the name Cabrini Health Care Center after Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini. It closed in 2008 due to financial difficulties.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Columbus Hospital and Italian Hospital
Major_Events.Description: Columbus Hospital and Italian Hospital merged to form Cabrini Health Care Center, later known as Cabrini Medical Center.
Cabrini Medical Center closed permanently due to financial difficulties, leading to patients and staff seeking other health care and employment.
Cabrini Medical Center filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing assets of $46 million and liabilities of $167 million.

Major_Events.Event: Sale to Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center
Major_Events.Description: The five buildings formerly housing the medical center were purchased by Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center for $83.1 million, with plans to open an outpatient cancer facility.
The property was sold to developers and transformed into a luxury condo complex known as Gramercy Square, reusing some of the buildings while razing others and building new.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cabrini Medical Center was significant for its role in addressing the health needs of Italian immigrants and for its early expertise in treating AIDS during the epidemic in the 1980s. It was named after Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini, a canonized saint who was instrumental in its founding.
world knowledge.Details: Following the closure, the property was sold to developers and transformed into a luxury condo complex known as Gramercy Square. The former emergency room is now a garden. Condo sales began in 2016 after several years of development. The development of the former Cabrini site has led to members of the City Council and NYS Assembly exploring limitations on what can be done with Mount Sinai Beth Israel upon its closure and sale.

world knowledge.Name: Tours station
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first railway station for Tours (called L’Embarcadère) was built in 1846 by Phidias Vestier. The current passenger building was constructed between 1896 and 1898 under the direction of architect Victor Laloux. It was established to merge the equipment of Paris-Orléans and the State Railways. The station has been listed as a monument historique since 28 December 1984.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the current passenger building
Major_Events.Description: The current passenger building was constructed under the direction of architect Victor Laloux, merging the equipment of Paris-Orléans and the State Railways.
The station was listed as a monument historique on 28 December 1984.
The station underwent a refurbishment of its interior and facade work, including the laying of gold leaf as initially planned by Laloux.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the first Tours tramway
Major_Events.Description: Annexes to the station were destroyed, and new access was created on the west facade to facilitate access to the new Gare de Tours station.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building brings together four materials: stone (for the facade and its statues), iron (as the supporting structure), cast iron (especially for the decoration of the interior columns) and glass (with two large canopies on the facade to provide lightness and transparency). It features four allegorical limestone statues of cities by Jean Antoine Injalbert (Bordeaux and Toulouse) and Jean-Baptiste Hugues (Limoges and Nantes). The painted earthenware panels were produced by Eugène Martial Simas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tours station is a historic railway station that has played a significant role in the development of the city's transportation infrastructure. Its architectural design and historical value have earned it a listing as a monument historique. The station also serves as a cultural landmark with its allegorical statues and artistic elements.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway station serving the city of Tours and connecting various regional and national rail lines.
world knowledge.Details: The station is situated on the Paris–Bordeaux railway, the Tours–Saint-Nazaire railway, and the non-electrified Tours–Le Mans railway. It is a terminus for most TGV trains, with nearby Gare de Saint-Pierre-des-Corps serving high-speed rail. The station is connected to the Fil bleu urban transport network, including line A of the Tours tramway and various bus lines. In 2018, the station's annual usage was estimated at 4,690,784 passengers, rising to 5,863,480 if non-passengers are included.

world knowledge.Name: Changgyeonggung Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Changgyeonggung is a palace located in Seoul, South Korea. It was built in the mid-15th century by King Sejong for his father, Taejong. Originally named 'Suganggung', it was renovated and enlarged in 1483 by King Seongjong, receiving its current name. The palace suffered destruction during Japan's attempts to conquer Korea and invade China in the late 15th to 16th centuries. It was rebuilt by successive Joseon Kings but was largely destroyed again by the Japanese in the early 20th century to make room for a modern park. During the Japanese colonial period, a zoo, botanical garden, and museum were built on the site. After independence and the Korean War, the zoo was restocked and later relocated in 1983 to Seoul Grand Park.

Major_Events.Description: Many structures were destroyed during Japan's attempts to conquer Korea and invade China.

Major_Events.Event: Destruction by Japanese in the early 20th century
Major_Events.Description: The palace was largely destroyed by the Japanese to make room for a modern park.

Major_Events.Event: Relocation of zoo and botanical garden
Major_Events.Description: The zoo and botanical garden were relocated to Seoul Grand Park.
Crown Prince Sado was sealed alive in a rice chest by order of his father, King Yeongjo, and died eight days later.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Changgyeonggung Palace is culturally and historically important as a symbol of Korea's royal heritage and its resilience through periods of destruction and reconstruction. It also holds significance due to the tragic event of Crown Prince Sado's death.
world knowledge.Details: The palace was designated as a historic site on January 18, 1963. It is also known by its Hangul name '창경궁' and Hanja name '昌慶宮'.

world knowledge.Name: Metrocentro Managua
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Metrocentro Managua is a shopping center in Managua, Nicaragua, developed and operated by the Salvadorean Grupo Roble. The construction of the first phase of the shopping center was finished in 1974. Due to the Revolution and Civil War of 1979, further development was halted until 1998 when it was renovated and extended with more store space and the building of the four-star Hotel Real InterContinental Metrocentro Managua. In 2004, a third renovation took place, adding more than 25,000 m2 (270,000 sq ft) of new commercial space and a two-level parking space.

Major_Events.Description: The first phase of the shopping center was finished.
The shopping center was renovated and extended with more store space and the building of the four-star Hotel Real InterContinental Metrocentro Managua.
More than 25,000 m2 (270,000 sq ft) of new commercial space and a two-level parking space were added.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Metrocentro Managua is a significant commercial and social hub in Managua, Nicaragua, contributing to the local economy and providing a central space for shopping, dining, and entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The shopping center is home to 120 stores, a food court, a supermarket, and a movie theater. It is developed and operated by the Salvadorean Grupo Roble.

world knowledge.Name: Al-Hamidiyah Souq
world knowledge.Address: Inside the old walled city of Damascus next to the Citadel
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 600 metres (2,000 ft) long and 15 metres (49 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Al-Hamidiyeh Souq dates back to the Ottoman era and was built along the axis of the Roman route to the Temple of Jupiter around 1780 during the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid I, and later extended during the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid II. It is the largest and central souk in Syria, located inside the old walled city of Damascus next to the Citadel.

Major_Events.Description: The souq was built along the axis of the Roman route to the Temple of Jupiter during the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid I.
The souq was extended during the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid II.
The souq was one of the treasures featured in the BBC documentary 'Around the World in 80 Treasures' presented by Dan Cruickshank.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The souq is covered by a 10-metre (33 ft) tall metal arch and is about 600 metres (2,000 ft) long and 15 metres (49 ft) wide. The ancient Roman Temple of Jupiter stands 40 feet tall in its entrance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Al-Hamidiyeh Souq is one of the most popular shopping districts in Syria, lined with hundreds of shops selling traditional crafts, jewelry, clothes, and food. It is a significant cultural and historical site in Damascus, reflecting the city's rich history and heritage.
world knowledge.Details: Before the ongoing Syrian Civil War, it was one of Damascus's main attractions and was visited by many tourists, including Europeans and Gulf Arabs. Despite the war, it remains a popular attraction for locals and Syrians. Peaceful protests and demonstrations have taken place in the nearby Medhat Pasha Souq, which extends from the Al Hamidiyah Souq.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Ounalom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Ounalom is a wat located on Sisowath Quay in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, near the Royal Palace of Cambodia. It was established in 1443 and is the most important wat of Phnom Penh, serving as the center of Cambodian Buddhism. It was damaged during the Khmer Rouge period but has since been restored.

Major_Events.Event: Damage during the Khmer Rouge period
Major_Events.Description: The wat was damaged during the Khmer Rouge regime but has since been restored.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main complex houses a stupa that contains what is believed to be an eyebrow hair of The Buddha and an inscription in Pali.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Ounalom is the most important wat of Phnom Penh and the center of Cambodian Buddhism. It houses a relic believed to be an eyebrow hair of The Buddha, making it a significant religious site.
world knowledge.Details: The name of Wat Ounalom commemorates one of the holiest relics in Cambodia, a hair (lom) from the whorl (unna) between the eyebrows of the Buddha.

world knowledge.Name: Wright Brothers National Memorial
world knowledge.Area: Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, USA
world knowledge.Address: Wright Brothers National Memorial, Kill Devil Hills, NC 27948, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Commemorates the first successful, sustained, powered flights in a heavier-than-air machine by Wilbur and Orville Wright from 1900 to 1903. Authorized as Kill Devil Hill Monument on March 2, 1927, and designated a national memorial on December 4, 1953.

Major_Events.Description: The granite monument was dedicated on November 14, 1932, with Orville Wright as the guest of honor.
Celebrated the 100th anniversary of the Wright brothers' first flight, attended by President George W. Bush, astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, and others.
A single-engine plane crashed while trying to land at the First Flight airport in the memorial, killing all five occupants.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Deco style visitor center designed by Rogers & Poor and National Park Service. The memorial features a 60-foot granite monument atop Kill Devil Hill, with stainless steel and nickel doors and relief panels depicting the history of flight.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Marks the site of the first powered, controlled, sustained flight in history, a pivotal moment in aviation and technological advancement.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic site and memorial dedicated to the Wright brothers and their achievements in aviation.
world knowledge.Details: The memorial includes a visitor center with exhibits on the Wright brothers' experiments, a life-size replica of the 1903 Wright Flyer, and a full-scale model of the 1902 glider. The site also features markers for the four flights made on December 17, 1903, and reconstructed sheds used by the Wright brothers. The memorial is co-managed with Fort Raleigh National Historic Site and Cape Hatteras National Seashore.

world knowledge.Name: Basilica Cistern
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basilica Cistern, also known as Cisterna Basilica, is the largest of several hundred ancient cisterns beneath Istanbul, Turkey. It was built during the reign of Byzantine emperor Justinian I in the 6th century. Originally located under a large public square, the Stoa Basilica, it served as a water filtration system for the Great Palace of Constantinople and other buildings on the First Hill. The cistern continued to provide water to the Topkapı Palace after the Ottoman conquest in 1453. Its existence was forgotten by many until the 16th century when it was rediscovered by the French traveller Petrus Gyllius.

Major_Events.Description: The city was devastated by the Nika riots, leading to the reconstruction and enlargement of the cistern by Emperor Justinian.
The French traveller Petrus Gyllius rediscovered the cistern and recorded his experience of being rowed through it.
The first major repairs were carried out by the architect Muhammad Ağa of Kayseri.
The second major repair was completed during the reign of Sultan Abdulhamid II.
The cistern was opened to the public on 9 September 1987 after restoration.
The cistern was closed for restoration and earthquake-proofing, reopening in 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cistern is an underground chamber approximately 138 metres by 65 metres, supported by 336 marble columns, each 9 metres high, arranged in 12 rows of 28 columns. The columns are mainly in the Ionic and Corinthian styles, with some Doric capitals. The ceiling is supported by cross-shaped vaults and round arches. The cistern features two columns with Medusa heads, oriented sideways and inverted to negate the Gorgons' gaze.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Basilica Cistern is culturally and historically significant as a major engineering achievement of the Byzantine Empire, providing water to the Great Palace of Constantinople and later to the Topkapı Palace. It is also a popular tourist attraction and has been featured in various films, novels, and video games.
world knowledge.Details: The cistern has been featured in various cultural works, including the 1963 James Bond film 'From Russia with Love', Dorothy Dunnett's historical novel 'Pawn in Frankincense', the 2009 film 'The International', the 2011 video game 'Assassin's Creed: Revelations', Jean-Baptiste Andrea's film 'Brotherhood of Tears', and Dan Brown's novel 'Inferno' and its 2016 film adaptation. It is also featured in 'Age of Empires IV' as one of the two Castle Age Landmarks of the Byzantines.

world knowledge.Name: Srinagarind Dam
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 140 metres (460 ft) tall and 610 metres (2,000 ft) long
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Srinagarind Dam is an embankment dam on the Khwae Yai River in Si Sawat District of Kanchanaburi Province, Thailand. It was named after Princess Srinagarindra. Feasibility studies were carried out between May 1967 and May 1969, and designs were completed from September 1970 to December 1977. Construction began in 1974 and was completed in 1980. The first generator was commissioned in 1980 and the last in 1991. The original cost was estimated at US$45 million but increased to US$114 million due to reinforcement required for the fault line foundation.

Major_Events.Description: Feasibility studies for the dam were carried out between May 1967 and May 1969.
Designs for the dam were completed from September 1970 to December 1977.
Construction of the dam began in 1974.
Construction of the dam was completed in 1980.
The first of the dam's generators was commissioned in 1980.
The last of the dam's generators was commissioned in 1991.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Srinagarind Dam is a 140 metres (460 ft) tall and 610 metres (2,000 ft) long embankment dam. It contains a reservoir with a capacity of 17,745 million cubic metres (14.386×10^6 acre⋅ft). The dam's power station has an installed capacity of 720 MW and contains three 120 megawatts (160,000 hp) Francis turbines and two 180 MW Francis pump-turbines.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The dam was named after Princess Srinagarindra and serves as a significant infrastructure for river regulation and hydroelectric power generation in Thailand.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: River regulation and hydroelectric power generation
world knowledge.Details: The dam's power station has a 720 megawatts (970,000 hp) capacity, of which 360 megawatts (480,000 hp) is pumped storage. The pump-turbines generate electricity during peak hours and return water from the lower reservoir back into the upper reservoir during off-peak hours.

world knowledge.Name: Olomouc astronomical clock
world knowledge.Address: Part of the northern wall of the town hall of Olomouc
world knowledge.Physical_Area: The arched alcove is approximately 14 meters high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Olomouc Astronomical Clock was built in the 15th century and has undergone several reconstructions. The current appearance dates from 1955, reflecting the socialist realism style. It is one of the few heliocentric clocks in the world. The clock has a rich history, including damage during World War II and subsequent restorations.

Major_Events.Description: The first undisputed mention of the clock is from 1519.
The clock was damaged by a grenade in May 1945 by retreating Nazi German soldiers.
The clock was completely rebuilt in 1955 by Karel Svolinský in the Socialist realism style.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The clock features a heliocentric dial, with lower and upper dials representing the earthly and heavenly spheres, respectively. It includes animated figurines of proletariat figures, a mosaic depicting the Ride of the Kings, and allegorical representations of the twelve seasons and two traditional festivals. The clock also has sixteen bells cast in 1898.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Olomouc Astronomical Clock is culturally significant as one of the few heliocentric clocks in the world. It reflects the historical and political changes in the Czech Republic, particularly the socialist realism period. The clock is also a notable example of astronomical and artistic craftsmanship.
world knowledge.Details: The clock was featured in the opening scenes of the 1969 Czech film 'The Joke' based on the book by Milan Kundera. The oldest parts of the current clock are from 1898, when it was equipped with a heliocentric dial by Eduard Korfhage. The clock's carillon plays three folksongs: 'Daleká, šeroká cesta přes Holomóc', 'Vrbe jož se zelenajó', and 'Za Náměšťó na kopečko hádajó se o děvečko'.

world knowledge.Name: Jacob's Well
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jacob's Well, also known as Jacob's Fountain or the Well of Sychar, is a Christian holy site located in Balata village, a suburb of the Palestinian city of Nablus in the West Bank. The well, currently situated inside an Eastern Orthodox church and monastery, has been associated in religious tradition with the biblical patriarch Jacob for roughly two millennia. The well is mentioned in the New Testament Gospel of John as the scene of Jesus's encounter with the Samaritan woman. The site has been identified as the place where Jesus held his conversation with the Samaritan woman since the 330s AD and has been used for Christian baptisms. Over the centuries, several churches have been built and destroyed at the site, including a Byzantine church, a Crusader-era church, and a modern church built in 1893.

Major_Events.Description: The Byzantine church was destroyed during the Samaritan revolts.
A new church was built at the site, likely due to the support of Queen Melisande.
The church was destroyed following Saladin's victory over the Crusaders in the Battle of Hittin.
A new church was built by the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate.
The church was destroyed by the 1927 Jericho earthquake.
The custodian of the well was found hatcheted to death inside the crypt housing the well.
The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem declared Philoumenos a saint thirty years after his death.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The well has a narrow opening, just wide enough to allow the body of a man to pass through with arms uplifted, and this narrow neck, which is about 4 ft. long, opens into the well itself, which is cylindrically shaped, and opens about 7 ft. 6 in. in diameter. The well and upper part of the well are built of masonry, and the well appears to have been sunk through a mixture of alluvial soil and limestone fragments, till a compact bed of mountain limestone was reached, having horizontal strata which could be easily worked; and the interior of the well presents the appearance of having been lined throughout with rough masonry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jacob's Well is a significant Christian holy site, associated with the biblical patriarch Jacob and the New Testament narrative of Jesus's encounter with the Samaritan woman. It has been a site of pilgrimage and religious veneration for centuries. The well is also important to the Samaritans and has been a focal point of various historical and religious events.
world knowledge.Details: Jacob's Well is located 76 meters (249 ft) from Tell Balata in the eastern part of the city of Nablus within the grounds of the Bir Ya'qub monastery. The well is accessed by entering the church on the monastery grounds, and descending the stairs to a crypt where the well still stands, along with 'a small winch, a bucket, ex-voto icons and lots of lit candles.'

world knowledge.Name: Panama Canal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Panama Canal is an artificial 82-kilometer waterway in Panama that connects the Caribbean Sea with the Pacific Ocean. It was constructed to provide a shorter and safer route for maritime trade between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, avoiding the lengthy and hazardous route around the southernmost tip of South America. The canal's construction was one of the largest and most difficult engineering projects ever undertaken. It was initially started by France in 1881 but was halted due to engineering problems and high worker mortality. The United States took over the project in 1904 and completed it in 1914. The canal has since played a crucial role in global trade and economic growth.

Major_Events.Description: France began construction of the canal but halted in 1889 due to engineering challenges and high worker mortality.
The United States took over the construction of the canal after France abandoned the project.
The Panama Canal was officially opened on August 15, 1914, significantly reducing maritime travel time between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
A major expansion of the canal was completed, allowing for the transit of larger Neopanamax ships.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The canal consists of artificial lakes, several improved and artificial channels, and three sets of locks. The original locks are 33.5 meters wide, and the expansion added a third, wider lane of locks. The canal uses a lock system to raise and lower ships, with Gatun Lake serving as a key reservoir. The new locks feature sliding gates and water-saving basins that reuse 60% of the water per transit.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Panama Canal is a symbol of human ingenuity and engineering prowess. It has had a profound impact on global trade, reducing travel time and costs for maritime commerce. The canal has also influenced economic growth in both developed and developing countries and has been a key factor in the development of global trade routes.
world knowledge.Details: The canal is managed by the Panama Canal Authority and handles over 5% of global trade annually. It has faced challenges such as water shortages and competition from alternative routes like the Suez Canal. The expansion in 2016 allowed for the transit of larger ships, further enhancing its capacity and importance in global trade.

world knowledge.Name: Cellular Jail
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cellular Jail, also known as 'Kālā Pānī', was a British colonial prison in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands used for exiling criminals and political prisoners during India's struggle for independence. Many notable independence activists were imprisoned there. The jail originally had seven wings, but only three remain today due to damage from earthquakes and demolitions. It now serves as a national memorial monument.

Major_Events.Description: The building suffered extensive damage during the earthquake.
The Japanese captured the Cellular Jail and repurposed bricks for constructing bunkers.
The Cellular Jail was declared a National Memorial by Prime Minister Morarji Desai.
The centenary of the jail's completion was marked with celebrations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Cellular Jail was a puce-colored brick building with seven wings radiating from a central tower, based on Jeremy Bentham's panopticon design. Each wing had three stories with 696 solitary cells, each measuring 4.5 by 2.7 meters. The design ensured isolation and prevented communication between prisoners.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cellular Jail is a symbol of India's struggle for independence. It housed many freedom fighters and revolutionaries who were subjected to harsh conditions. Today, it serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made for India's freedom.
world knowledge.Details: The jail now hosts guided tours and a sound-and-light show narrating the trials of the inmates. It was also the setting for the 1996 Malayalam film 'Kaalapani' and features in Arthur Conan Doyle's novel 'The Sign of the Four'.

world knowledge.Name: Tosa Shrine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tosa Shrine is a Shinto shrine located in Kochi, Japan, and is the ichinomiya of the former Tosa Province. Its origins are unknown, but legend states it was founded when Emperor Yuryaku exiled Hitokoto-no-nushi no kami to Tosa Province. The shrine was first historically recorded in 675 AD in the Nihon Shoki. It was promoted to the highest rank in 940 AD for its role in suppressing the Fujiwara no Sumitomo rebellion. The shrine was destroyed multiple times, including by a typhoon in 1224 and during the Sengoku period around 1509. It was reconstructed by Chōsokabe Motochika in 1571 and further developed during the Edo Period by the Yamauchi clan.

Major_Events.Description: The shrine was promoted to the highest rank due to successful prayers for the suppression of the rebellion.
The shrine was completely destroyed by a typhoon.
The shrine was destroyed during the wars of the early Sengoku period.
The current Honden, Heiden, and Haiden were completed.
Following the Meiji restoration, the shrine was renamed Tosa Jinja and designated a National Shrine, 2nd rank.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shrine's current structures, including the Honden, Heiden, and Haiden, date back to 1571. The Rōmon tower gate was added in 1631, and a drum tower in 1649. Several structures are designated National Important Cultural Properties.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tosa Shrine is the ichinomiya of the former Tosa Province and holds significant historical and religious importance. It is associated with legends involving Emperor Yuryaku and has been a center of worship for centuries. The shrine's Shinane Festival is one of the three major festivals of Kochi.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious worship and cultural heritage site
world knowledge.Details: The shrine enshrines the deities Ajisukitakahikone and Hitokotonushu no kami. Its main festival is held annually from March 11–13. An archaeological excavation in 2003 uncovered foundations of medieval structures on the shrine's premises.

world knowledge.Name: Zama (Tunisia)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zama, also known as Xama, is a town in Tunisia best known for its association with the Battle of Zama, in which Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal on 19 October in 202 BC, ending the Second Punic War. The Battle of Zama was a victory for the Roman Republic and diminished the power of Ancient Carthage. The battle did not in fact take place in the vicinity of Zama. Polybius states that Hannibal, after first camping at Zama, moved to another camp just before the battle; and Livy says that Scipio's camp, near which the battle took place, was at Naraggara, present-day Sakiet Sidi Youssef on the border between Tunisia and Algeria. More than one town in what became the Roman province of Africa was called Zama. The Zama associated with the battle is likely to be the Zama Regia mentioned in Sallust's account of the Jugurthine War as besieged unsuccessfully by Quintus Caecilius Metellus Numidicus. Later, Zama Regia was the capital of Juba I of Numidia (60–46 BC) and so, in the view of the Oxford Classical Dictionary, it was called Zama Regia (Royal Zama). Scullard prefers the suggestion that the town got the appellation "Regia" before the destruction of Carthage in 146 BC, indicating that it was not under Carthaginian control and belonged to the kingdom of Numidia. In 41 BC Zama Regia was captured by Titus Sextius, who, having previously been one of Julius Caesar's legates in Gaul, was then governor of the province of Africa on behalf of the Second Triumvirate. As a Roman town, Zama Regia is mentioned in an inscription found at Rome as "Colonia Aelia Hadriana Augusta Zama Regia", showing that under Hadrian (Publius Aelius Hadrianus Augustus), it had been granted the rank of colonia. Zama Regia is mentioned also in the Tabula Peutingeriana. Polybius used the Greek phrase Ζάμα Μείζων, corresponding to Latin Zama Maior, and implying the existence of a smaller town called Zama, a Zama Minor. The town was in antiquity the seat of a Christian bishopric which survives today as a titular see of the Roman Catholic Church. A Bishop Dialogus of Zama Maior was at the Council of Carthage (411), and a Bishop Marcellus of Zama Minor participated in the Synod of Carthage of AD 255. Barthélemy Adoukonou is the current Bishop. Both Zama are included in the Catholic Church's list of titular sees, which does not use the name "Zama Regia". It is agreed that one Zama must have been at present-day Jama, 30 kilometres north of Maktar, and a shorter distance west-northwest of Siliana. An incomplete inscription found here mentions "Zama M...", interpreted by some as "Zama Maior", by others as "Zama Minor". Recent systematic excavation of Jama has discovered another incomplete inscription that appears to refer unambiguously to it as "Zama Regia". This seems to put paid to the views expressed by Scullard and others that Jama corresponds neither to Sallust's description of Zama Regia nor to the distances indicated in the Tabula Peutingeriana. It appears also to indicate that the towns called Zama were two, not three. Other sites taken into consideration are Sidi Abd el Djedidi, situated 40 kilometres east of Jama, and Sebaa Biar, the latter of which seems to fit Sallust's account better.

Major_Events.Description: Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal, ending the Second Punic War.
Zama Regia was captured by Titus Sextius, who was then governor of the province of Africa on behalf of the Second Triumvirate.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zama is culturally and historically important due to its association with the Battle of Zama, which marked a significant turning point in the Second Punic War and the decline of Carthaginian power. It was also the capital of Juba I of Numidia and later became a Roman colonia under Hadrian.
world knowledge.Details: The town was in antiquity the seat of a Christian bishopric which survives today as a titular see of the Roman Catholic Church. Recent systematic excavation of Jama has discovered an incomplete inscription that appears to refer unambiguously to it as "Zama Regia".

world knowledge.Name: Al-Madina Souq
world knowledge.Address: Located at the heart of the Syrian city of Aleppo within the walled ancient part of the city
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al-Madina Souq is the largest covered historic market in the world, serving as a major trade center for imported luxury goods and local products. It is part of the Ancient City of Aleppo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986. Many sections were destroyed or ruined during the Syrian conflict starting in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Many sections of the souq and other medieval buildings in the ancient city were destroyed, ruined or burnt as a result of fighting between the Syrian opposition and the Syrian Armed Forces.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Long and narrow alleys, khans (caravanserais) with beautiful façades and entrances with fortified wooden doors, and smaller market-places called caeserias.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it represents a historic trading hub where various cultures and goods from as far as China, Mesopotamia, Europe, and the Fertile Crescent met.
world knowledge.Details: Most of the souqs date back to the 14th century and are named after various professions and crafts. It accommodated traders and their goods in khans and caeserias, which functioned as workshops for craftsmen.

world knowledge.Name: Casa dos Bicos
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in the early 16th century in the Alfama neighbourhood, Casa dos Bicos survived the 1755 Lisbon earthquake. It was abandoned as a residence and used as a warehouse until the 20th-century renovation. It became the headquarters of the José Saramago Foundation and a location of the Museum of Lisbon.

Major_Events.Description: The earthquake caused significant damage to the residence, destroying the principal façade and two floors.
The building was restored and adapted for the 18th European Art, Science and Culture Exposition.
The Direção Regional de Cultura de Lisboa incorporated the building in the Special Protection Zone.

Major_Events.Event: Head office of José Saramago Foundation
Major_Events.Description: The Casa dos Bicos became the head office of the José Saramago Foundation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house has a curious façade of spikes, influenced by Italian Renaissance palaces and Portuguese Manueline styles. It is a rectangular building of four floors with irregular fenestrations and a tiled roof. The principal façade is decorated in diamond-shape protrusions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Casa dos Bicos is historically important as it survived the 1755 Lisbon earthquake and represents a blend of Italian Renaissance and Portuguese Manueline architectural styles. It now serves as a cultural hub housing the José Saramago Foundation and the Museum of Lisbon.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum and headquarters of the José Saramago Foundation
world knowledge.Details: The interior has been substantially altered from its early conceptions, and includes a steep, clear marble staircase with bold lines and contrasting black walls.

world knowledge.Name: Beni Hasan
world knowledge.Address: Approximately 20 kilometers south of modern-day Minya, Egypt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beni Hasan is an ancient Egyptian cemetery primarily used during the Middle Kingdom (21st to 17th centuries BCE). It was the burial site for provincial governors and elite officials of the Oryx Nome. The site includes tombs from the Old Kingdom but gained prominence during the Middle Kingdom. A temple dedicated to the goddess Pakhet, constructed by Hatshepsut and Thutmose III, is located to the south of the cemetery. The tombs are famous for their paintings and inscriptions, which depict daily life, warfare, and include Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the temple dedicated to Pakhet
Major_Events.Year: During the reign of Hatshepsut and Thutmose III (15th century BCE)
Major_Events.Description: A subterranean temple was built to honor the local goddess Pakhet, later identified by the Greeks as Artemis.
John Garstang excavated 888 shaft tombs in the lower cemetery, revealing Middle Kingdom burial practices.

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of Pyramid Texts in tomb BH33
Major_Events.Description: Martin Bommas identified Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts in the burial chamber of governor Baqet II, marking a breakthrough in understanding the transmission of these texts after the Old Kingdom.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tombs are rock-cut and carved into limestone cliffs. The elite tombs feature an outer court and a rock-cut pillared room (chapel) with a shaft leading to the burial chamber. The tombs are decorated with paintings and inscriptions depicting daily life, warfare, and religious texts. The temple to Pakhet is subterranean.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Beni Hasan is culturally significant as it provides insight into the burial practices, governance, and daily life of Middle Kingdom Egypt. The tombs' paintings and inscriptions are renowned for their quality and historical value. The discovery of Pyramid Texts in tomb BH33 has advanced the understanding of religious texts' transmission.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Burial site for provincial governors and elite officials of the Oryx Nome.
world knowledge.Details: There are 39 ancient tombs here, with four accessible to the public. The tombs are divided into an upper cemetery for the elite and a lower necropolis with simpler shaft tombs. The site reflects the reorganization of government during the 12th Dynasty, where the power of nomarchs was curtailed, and governors were appointed by the king.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Phumin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Phumin is the most famous temple in the city of Nan, renowned for its cruciform ubosot constructed in 1596 and restored during the reign of Phra Chao Anantaworritthidet (1852-1892). It is unique for being built as if on the back of two immense snakes (Nagas). The temple features four entrances, each preceded by a small corridor with finely decorated, point-shaped structures, indicating its royal origin. The interior is supported by twelve teak pillars decorated with gold on black and red lacquer, and the ceiling is finely decorated. The altar supports four Sukhothai-style Buddhas in the Bhūmisparsa mudrā pose.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was restored during the reign of Phra Chao Anantaworritthidet.
The East of the Nan valley area was yielded to the French, which is referenced in the temple's murals.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Wat Phumin is a good example of Thai Lue architecture, featuring a cruciform ubosot with four entrances, each preceded by a small corridor topped by a finely decorated, point-shaped structure. The interior is supported by twelve teak pillars decorated with gold on black and red lacquer, and the ceiling is finely decorated. The altar supports four Sukhothai-style Buddhas in the Bhūmisparsa mudrā pose. The murals illustrate the Khattana Kumara Jataka and the Nimi Jatakas, as well as scenes of local life, with influences from Thai Lue, Chinese, and European styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Phumin is culturally significant for its unique architecture, which reflects Thai Lue traditions and influences from Sukhothai, Lao, and Chinese styles. The temple's murals are of great value, depicting local life and historical events, including the arrival of the French in the region. It is also a religious site that houses important Buddhist artifacts and serves as a center for teaching and meditation.
world knowledge.Details: The temple's murals include two famous scenes: a man whispering to the ear of a woman and a portrait that could be of king Phra Chao Anantaworritthidet. The large paintings on each side of the main entrance show a Chinese influence, reflecting the origins of the Thai Lue people.

image_name: Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso

world knowledge.Name: Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso
world knowledge.Location: Real Sitio de San Ildefonso (Segovia), Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso, known as La Granja, is an early 18th-century palace in the small town of San Ildefonso, located in the hills near Segovia and 80 kilometres (50 mi) north of Madrid, within the Province of Segovia in central Spain. It became the summer residence of the kings of Spain from the 1720s during the reign of King Philip V. The palace is in a restrained Baroque style, surrounded by extensive gardens in the formal Jardin à la française style with sculptural fountains. It is now open to the public as a museum.

Major_Events.Description: King Philip V began building a new palace and gardens modeled on Versailles.

Major_Events.Event: Opened as exclusive property for the monarch
Major_Events.Description: The palace became the summer residence of the kings of Spain.
A major fire damaged the palace, resulting in the loss of much of the interior decoration and contents.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is in a restrained Baroque style, with extensive gardens in the formal Jardin à la française style. The gardens feature sculptural fountains and are one of the best examples of 18th-century European garden design in Spain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso is culturally and historically important as it served as the summer residence of the kings of Spain and is a prime example of 18th-century European garden design. It also played a significant role in Spanish royal history, hosting many royal weddings, burials, state treaties, and political events.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is now part of the Patrimonio Nacional of Spain and is a popular tourist attraction. The gardens extend over 1,500 acres (6.1 km2) and feature twenty-six sculptural fountains representing themes from classical mythology. The original waterworks and piping are still functional, relying purely on gravity to project water up the fountain jets.

world knowledge.Name: Sardarapat Memorial
world knowledge.Address: Village of Araks, Armavir Province, Armenia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sardarapat Memorial is a memorial complex dedicated to the Battle of Sardarabad, which took place between May 21 and 29, 1918. This battle was a pivotal moment in Armenian history, as it marked the successful defense against Turkish troops, ensuring the survival of the Armenian nation. The memorial was designed by architect Rafael Israelyan, with sculptures by Ara Harutyunyan, Arsham Shahinyan, and Sambel Minasyan. The complex includes a 26-meter-high bell tower, winged oxen made of red tufa, and ancient-style Armenian-winged lions. The memorial also features a memorial garden for Karabakh (Arstakh) martyrs.

Major_Events.Event: Commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the Battle of Sardarapat
Major_Events.Description: A memorial park was laid out on the spot of the battlefield.
The President of Armenia, the Prime Minister of Armenia, and the President of Artsakh visit to lay a wreath at the monument.

Major_Events.Event: Centennial celebrations of the Armenian state
Major_Events.Description: A ceremonial military parade was held at the memorial, featuring hundreds of soldiers in historical uniforms and veterans of the first Nagorno-Karabakh War.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The memorial complex includes a 26-meter-high bell tower, winged oxen made of red tufa, and ancient-style Armenian-winged lions. The entrance is flanked by the winged oxen, and a flight of steps leads to a square where the bell tower rises. The bell tower is a trellised structure with twelve bells that ring every year on the day of the historic victory.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sardarapat Memorial is a symbol of pride and survival for the Armenian people. It marks the site of a crucial battle that ensured the survival of the Armenian nation against overwhelming odds. The memorial is a testament to the resilience and determination of the Armenian people in the face of adversity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Memorial complex dedicated to the Battle of Sardarabad
world knowledge.Details: The memorial complex also includes the Sardarapat Ethnography and Liberation Movement History Museum, which is adjacent to the outdoor monument. The museum provides further historical context and artifacts related to the Battle of Sardarabad and the broader Armenian liberation movement.

world knowledge.Name: Golestan Palace
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 16th century, renovated in the 18th century, rebuilt in 1865
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Golestan Palace, also known as the Rose Garden Palace, was built in the 16th century, renovated in the 18th century, and finally rebuilt in 1865. It served as the official royal Qajar complex in Tehran. The palace complex includes gardens, royal buildings, and collections of Iranian crafts and European gifts from the 18th and 19th centuries. It was used for formal receptions during the Pahlavi era and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013.

Major_Events.Description: The coronation of Reza Shah took place in the Golestan Palace.

Major_Events.Event: Coronation of Mohammad Reza Shah and Shahbanu Farah
Major_Events.Description: The coronation of Mohammad Reza Shah and Shahbanu Farah was held in the Golestan Palace.

Major_Events.Event: Inscription as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The Golestan Palace was proclaimed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site during the 37th session in Phnom Penh.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Golestan Palace Complex consists of 17 structures, including palaces, museums, and halls. It features various architectural styles and materials, including Iranian mirror-work (Ayeneh-kari) and European influences. Notable structures include the Marble Throne, the Brilliant Hall, the Mirror Hall, and the Windcatcher Mansion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Golestan Palace is culturally and historically significant as the former official royal Qajar complex in Tehran. It represents the architectural and artistic achievements of the Qajar dynasty and serves as a symbol of Iran's rich cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The Golestan Palace Complex includes three main archives: the photographic archive, the library of manuscripts, and the archive of documents.
