Major_Events.Description: The statue was unveiled on 23 August 1913.
The statue has been severely vandalized several times.
The statue was moved to Expo 2010 in Shanghai, where it remained until 20 November 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Bronze statue depicting the Little Mermaid sitting on a rock, inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The statue is a Copenhagen icon and a major tourist attraction, symbolizing the cultural heritage of Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale.
world knowledge.Details: A similar statue of The Little Mermaid, created in 2000 by Kristian Dahlgard, is located at Larvotto beach in Monaco, honoring the Danes living in Monaco and marking the 50th year of Prince Rainier III's reign.

world knowledge.Name: Huaqing Pool
world knowledge.Area: Mount Li, Qinling, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China
world knowledge.Address: Mount Li, Qinling, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Almost three millennia of documented history, with notable constructions during Zhou, Qin, Han, and Tang dynasties
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Huaqing Pool, also known as Huaqing Hot Springs, is a complex of hot springs with a history spanning nearly three millennia. It served as the location for palaces built by King You of the Zhou dynasty, Qin Shi Huang of the Qin dynasty, and Wu Han of the Han dynasty. During the Tang dynasty, Emperor Taizong and Xuanzong expanded the site, with Xuanzong rebuilding it in 723 as part of the Huaqing Palace. The site is famous for the romance between Emperor Xuanzong and his consort Yang Guifei. It suffered damage during the An Lushan rebellion and was also the scene of the 1936 Xi'an Incident.

Major_Events.Description: Considerable damage was done to the site during the rebellion.
Chiang Kai-shek was kidnapped by former warlord Zhang Xueliang and forced to participate in a United Front with the Chinese Communist Party to oppose Imperial Japan.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site features hot springs utilizing locally-occurring geothermal heating. It includes historical palaces built during various dynasties, with the Tang dynasty's Huaqing Palace being the most notable.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Huaqing Pool is culturally significant due to its long history, association with Chinese emperors, and its role in famous historical events and literature, such as Bai Juyi's poem 'Song of Everlasting Regret'. It is also a symbol of the Tang dynasty's opulence and romance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a royal bathing and leisure site; now functions as a major tourist attraction.
Notable_Visitors: King You of the Zhou dynasty
world knowledge.Details: Huaqing Pool is currently classified as a AAAAA scenic area by the China National Tourism Administration and is an important tourist spot. It is located approximately 25 kilometers east of Xi'an.

world knowledge.Name: Gurara Waterfalls
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height: 30 m (98 ft), Width: 200 m (656 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gurara Waterfalls was discovered by a Gwari hunter called Buba in 1745. Europeans discovered it in 1925 and found it as a recreation centre. Prior to this, the waterfalls was worshipped by local communities. The waterfalls and river were named after two deities called Gura and Rara.

Major_Events.Description: Discovered by a Gwari hunter named Buba.
Discovered by Europeans who found it as a recreation centre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Segmented waterfall with a height of 30 m and a width of 200 m.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Worshipped by local communities before European discovery. Named after deities Gura and Rara.
world knowledge.Details: Gurara Waterfalls has a semi-arid climate with average yearly temperatures around 68°F (20°C). Rainy season occurs from May to September, and dry season lasts from October to April. Winds blow from the southwest at speeds of 10-38 kilometers per hour. There are plans to develop it into a resort with a recreation centre and a seven-star hotel.

world knowledge.Name: Surigao Strait
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Max. length: 75 km (47 mi), Max. width: 25 km (16 mi)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Surigao Strait is a strait in the southern Philippines, between the Bohol Sea and Leyte Gulf of the Philippine Sea. It is located between the regions of Visayas and Mindanao. According to legend, the strait was named after Solibao, a Negrito chieftain, who lived at the outlet of the Surigao River. Migrating Visayan fishermen gradually formed a settlement there, and when Spanish explorers visited the place, they probably misheard the name as Surigao instead of Solibao. A different theory explains that Surigao may be derived from the Spanish word surgir, meaning 'swift water' or 'current'.

Major_Events.Description: Ferdinand Magellan and his crew were the first Europeans to sail through the strait during the first circumnavigation of the Earth.

The American battleships of the U.S. 7th Fleet Support Force commanded by Rear Admiral Jesse B. Oldendorf were able to 'cross the T' against Vice Admiral Shoji Nishimura's Southern Force; nearly all of which, including the battleships Yamashiro and Fusō, were sunk. All but one of these American battleships had been in Pearl Harbor during the Japanese sneak attack and either damaged or sunk and subsequently refloated and repaired.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Surigao Strait is culturally and historically significant due to its role in maritime navigation, its legendary naming origin, and its pivotal role in the Battle of Surigao Strait during World War II.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Maritime route for transportation and navigation
world knowledge.Details: The strait is deep but has a strong current, up to 8 knots (15 km/h; 9.2 mph). The northern entrance of the Surigao Strait is marked by a navigation light on Suluan Island. The Hibuson island lies at the north end of the Surigao Strait. It is regularly crossed by numerous ferries that transport goods and people between Visayas and Mindanao. The ferries stop at Liloan, Southern Leyte and Surigao City in Surigao del Norte.

world knowledge.Name: Ho Chi Minh Trail
world knowledge.Location: Runs from North Vietnam to South Vietnam through Laos and Cambodia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Network of roads and trails spanning rugged mountains and dense jungle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ho Chi Minh Trail was a logistical network of roads and trails that ran from North Vietnam to South Vietnam through Laos and Cambodia. It provided support to the Viet Cong and the People's Army of Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Construction began following the North Vietnamese invasion of Laos in July 1959. The trail was named after North Vietnamese leader Hồ Chí Minh and was a critical supply route for the North Vietnamese forces.

Major_Events.Description: The invasion marked the beginning of the construction of the Ho Chi Minh Trail.
The first systematic bombardment of the Ho Chi Minh Trail by the U.S. Air Force.
A South Vietnamese incursion into Laos to disrupt the trail, which ultimately failed.
A major North Vietnamese offensive that utilized the trail for logistical support.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The trail consisted of a network of 5.5-metre-wide dirt roads, foot and bicycle paths, truck parks, supply bunkers, storage areas, barracks, hospitals, and command and control facilities. It was concealed from aerial observation by natural and man-made camouflage.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ho Chi Minh Trail is culturally and historically significant as a symbol of North Vietnamese resilience and ingenuity during the Vietnam War. It played a crucial role in the eventual unification of Vietnam under communist rule.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Logistical supply route for the North Vietnamese forces during the Vietnam War.
world knowledge.Details: The trail was able to effectively supply troops fighting in the south, an unparalleled military feat, given it was the site of the single most intense air interdiction campaign in history. The trail was later expanded and modernized, including the construction of a petroleum pipeline and paved roads.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Gratot
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Gratot is a ruined medieval castle built by the Argouges family in the 14th century, undergoing transformations until the 18th century. It was neglected in the 19th century, used as a fodder warehouse, and abandoned in the early 20th century. Restoration efforts by volunteers began in 1968, focusing on clearing rubble and rebuilding structures. The castle is now classified as a Monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture.

Major_Events.Description: A team of volunteers began restoring the castle, removing tonnes of rubble and clearing undergrowth. Reconstruction included rebuilding two towers and restoring the 18th-century pavilion.
The castle was classified as a Historic monument by the French Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle features a mix of architectural styles, including a medieval round tower with a spiral staircase, an 18th-century pavilion with Mansart roof, and the Fairy Tower with octagonal base and gargoyles. The main residence has large windows and high spire lights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a significant historical site in Normandy, reflecting medieval and 18th-century architecture. It is associated with the legend of Melusina, adding to its cultural allure. It serves as a cultural center hosting artistic events and exhibitions.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is open to the public year-round, with a welcome desk and gift shop during summer months. It features a moat with a three-arched bridge, outbuildings from the 16th century, and an exhibition on its history. The Fairy Tower is linked to a local legend about a fairy wife. Annual visitor numbers reached 12,600 in 2003.

world knowledge.Name: Huaca Pucllana
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Over 500 meters in length, 100 in width, and 22 in height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Huaca Pucllana is a great adobe and clay pyramid built from seven staggered platforms. It served as an important ceremonial and administrative center for the Lima Culture, which developed in the Peruvian Central Coast between 200 AD and 700 AD. The pyramid was constructed to allow elite clergymen to express their religious power and control over natural water resources. The site also shows influences from the Wari Culture (500 - 1000 AD).

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of the Señor de los Unkus tomb
Major_Events.Description: The first tomb within the ceremonial center to be discovered completely intact, containing three adult burial shrouds and a sacrificed child.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed from adobe and clay with seven staggered platforms. The structure is surrounded by a plaza and a large wall dividing it into ceremonial and administrative sections. The ceremonial section includes benches and pits for offerings, while the administrative area contains small clay structures and adobe huts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Huaca Pucllana is culturally significant as a ceremonial and administrative center for the Lima Culture, reflecting their religious practices and societal structure. It also shows the influence of the Wari Culture, indicating cultural interactions in ancient Peru.
world knowledge.Details: The site includes remains from the Wari Culture, particularly the tomb of the Señor de los Unkus, which contained three adult burial shrouds and a sacrificed child. The pyramid was built to demonstrate the religious power and control of the elite clergymen over natural water resources.

world knowledge.Name: Jayawijaya Mountains
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jayawijaya Mountains, formerly known as the Orange Range, are the eastern mountain range of the Maoke Mountains in the central highlands region of the Indonesian part of New Guinea. The range extends for 370 kilometres (230 mi) east of the Sudirman Range to the Star Mountains. Its highest point is Puncak Mandala at 4,760 metres (15,617 ft). The Baliem River has its source in the range.

Major_Events.Description: The Eternity Glaciers' depth has declined from 32 m (105 ft) in 2010 to 8 m (26 ft) in 2021, projected to vanish by 2026 due to climate change and strong El Niño weather patterns.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jayawijaya Mountains are culturally significant as they are part of the Maoke Mountains and are home to indigenous communities like the Ketengban. The range also includes the Jayawijaya Mountains Wildlife Refuge.
world knowledge.Details: The range's Eternity Glaciers are projected to vanish by the year 2026, due both to climate change and strong El Niño weather patterns. The glaciers' depth has declined from 32 m (105 ft) in 2010 to 8 m (26 ft) in 2021.

world knowledge.Name: Piazza San Carlo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Piazza San Carlo, previously known as Piazza Reale, Piazza d'Armi, and Place Napoléon, is one of the main city squares in Turin, Italy. It was laid out in the 16th and 17th century and is an example of Baroque style.

Major_Events.Description: On 3 June 2017, a robbery attempt followed by a loud bang caused panic, and a subsequent stampede during a screening of the 2017 UEFA Champions League Final in Turin, killing three people and injuring at least 1,672.
On 14 May 2019, the victims of the 2017 stampede were commemorated with a plaque in the piazza.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The square is an example of Baroque style, with porticos designed by Carlo di Castellamonte around 1638. The 1838 Equestrian monument of Emmanuel Philibert by Carlo Marochetti is located at the center of the square. The twin churches of Santa Cristina and San Carlo Borromeo close the southern edge of the square.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Piazza San Carlo is a historic and cultural hub in Turin, hosting various historical and social events, including election rallies, concerts, sports events, and live TV shows. It was also a proposed location for the Eurovision Village at the Eurovision Song Contest 2022.
world knowledge.Details: The square has become a regular stage for various historical and social events, including election rallies, concerts, sports events (like the 2006 Winter Olympics or Juventus matches) and live TV shows. It was one of the proposed locations for the Eurovision Village at the Eurovision Song Contest 2022, before Parco del Valentino was eventually chosen as the location for the village. The Rockin' 1000 pre-recorded a performance of John Lennon's "Give Peace a Chance" in the square for the opening of the Eurovision final.

world knowledge.Name: Kohima War Cemetery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kohima War Cemetery is a memorial dedicated to soldiers of the 2nd British Division of the Allied Forces who died in the Second World War at Kohima, the capital of the Indian state of Nagaland in April 1944. The soldiers died on the battleground of Garrison Hill in the tennis court area of the Deputy Commissioner's residence. According to the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, which maintains this cemetery among many others in the world, there are 1,420 Commonwealth burials of the Second World War at this cemetery, and a memorial to an additional 917 Hindu and Sikh soldiers who were cremated in accordance with their faith.

Major_Events.Description: In March 1944, the Japanese 15th Army attacked the British troops stationed in Kohima and Imphal in northeast India with intent to prevent an attack on Burma. In the first week of April, the Japanese attacked at Kohima and Imphal via Mizoram from the Indo-Burma border, to destroy the supply bases of the British. They laid siege on the Allied forces stationed at Kohima and also at Imphal.
On the 60th anniversary of the end of World War II in 2005, a memorial service was held at the Kohima War Cemetery attended by 41 members of the Royal British Legion.
Ten years later another memorial service was held in the cemetery, attended by senior British Army officers, to commemorate the 70th anniversary of the Battle of Kohima.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cemetery is set in peaceful surroundings with well-manicured grassland in which roses bloom in season. The cemetery is sited at the exact location where the battle was fought, and provides a panoramic view of the city of Kohima. It is marked at its two ends by tall, concrete structures engraved with the cross. Between the two structures, along the sloping ground, a series of terraces of 3–5 metres (9.8–16.4 ft) in height have been created; these contain stone markers embedded with bronze plaques carrying the name of each Commonwealth soldier who died on the Kohima battlefield. These markers are made distinctly visible by a white wash.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kohima War Cemetery is culturally and historically significant as it commemorates the soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima, which was a turning point for the Allied forces in the Second World War. The battle halted the Japanese invasion of India and forced their retreat. The cemetery also honors Hindu and Sikh soldiers who were cremated in accordance with their faith.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Memorial for soldiers who died in the Second World War
world knowledge.Details: The cemetery includes two memorial crosses, one at the upper end and the other at the lower end. The upper-end memorial commemorates the names of the Indian and Sikh soldiers who were part of the British Indian Army and died on the battlefield. The lower-end memorial is dedicated to the 2nd Division and features a 15 feet tall stone fixed over a dressed stone platform. The site also includes a cherry tree near the tennis court where the battle was fought, with a small brass plaque reading 'For Your Tomorrow, We Gave Our Today'. Close to the Garrison Hill, memorials for the 2nd Battalion, the Dorsetshire Regiment, and several other regiments have been established.

world knowledge.Name: Lenin's Mausoleum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lenin's Mausoleum is the resting place of Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin, whose preserved body has been on public display since shortly after his death in 1924. The mausoleum was designed by Alexey Shchusev and incorporates elements from ancient mausoleums. It has served as a viewing stand for Soviet leaders during military parades on Red Square.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the first wooden mausoleum
Major_Events.Description: A wooden tomb was built in Red Square close to the Moscow Kremlin Wall, ready on 27 January 1924, the same day Lenin's coffin was placed inside.
The stone mausoleum, made of marble, porphyry, granite, and labradorite, was completed on 10 November 1930.

Major_Events.Event: Evacuation of Lenin's body during World War II
Major_Events.Description: During the Second World War, Lenin's body was evacuated to Tyumen in Siberia due to the threat of Moscow being captured.
The embalmed body of Joseph Stalin, which had been placed next to Lenin's, was removed as part of de-Stalinization and buried in the Kremlin Wall Necropolis.
The mausoleum underwent foundation reconstruction and was reopened on 30 April 2013.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mausoleum, designed by Alexey Shchusev, incorporates elements from ancient mausoleums such as the Step Pyramid, the Tomb of Cyrus the Great, and the Temple of the Inscriptions. It is constructed of marble, porphyry, granite, and labradorite. The structure includes a vestibule, Mourning Hall, and two staircases. The sarcophagus is made of two inclined conical glasses held together by a bronze frame.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lenin's Mausoleum is a symbol of Soviet history and the legacy of Vladimir Lenin. It has been a site of political and cultural significance, serving as a viewing stand for Soviet leaders during military parades and as a place of pilgrimage for those who revere Lenin's contributions to the Soviet Union.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Memorial and resting place of Vladimir Lenin
world knowledge.Details: Lenin's body has been on almost continuous public display since 1930. The mausoleum is open to the public on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays from 10:00–13:00. Entrance is free, but visitors are required to show respect: photography, filming, talking, smoking, and wearing hats (for men) are forbidden. The preservation of Lenin's body has been funded by the Soviet government and later by private donations. In 2016, the Russian government announced it would spend 13 million rubles to preserve Lenin's body.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Quintin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Quintin is a castle in Quintin, Côtes-d'Armor, Brittany, France. It was partly built in 1775 and has been listed as an official monument since 1983.

Major_Events.Description: The Château de Quintin was recognized as an official monument by the French government.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Quintin is a historic site in Brittany, representing the architectural and cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a castle or château in France is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan is the main Buddhist temple of Nakhon Si Thammarat Province in southern Thailand. The main stupa, Phra Borommathat Chedi, was built by King Sri Dhammasokaraja in the early-13th century CE to establish a symbol for the Theravada Buddhism sect in the province. The temple is believed to house a tooth of Gautama Buddha. The city of Nakhon Si Thammarat was a prominent city in the ancient kingdom of Tambralinga and was part of the Srivijaya empire until the early-13th century. The stupa and other religious edifices were built over 100 years after construction of the original stupa began and underwent several restoration works.

Major_Events.Description: The annual temple festival held on the occasion of Magha Puja, celebrated on the full moon day in February. The celebrations are marked by a procession with a robe, known as Phra Bot, joined in a single piece to wrap around the bell-shaped body of the main stupa and the chedis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple complex is built in a rectangular plan over 5.14 hectares and is enclosed by brick walls. The principal stupa, Phra Borommathat Chedi, is a bell-shaped stupa built in the early-13th century. The stupa is surrounded by 22 sculpted standing elephants and has an umbrella-like spire formed with 52 rings. The cloister is covered with coloured tiles and lined with numerous Buddha images. The temple complex also includes a museum, chapels, and a mondop with a two-tiered roof.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan is one of the most important sites of Theravada Buddhism, believed to contain the relics of Gautama Buddha. The temple has played a significant role in spreading and strengthening Theravada Buddhism in the region. It is also a symbol of Nakhon Si Thammarat Province and features on the obverse of the 25 satang coin.
world knowledge.Details: The temple was nominated to a tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 2012. Jatukam Ramathep amulets, consecrated in the temple, are believed to act as lucky charms, drawing visitors from across the nation.

world knowledge.Name: Rumi Darwaza
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rumi Darwaza, also known as the Turkish Gate, was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784. It was modeled after the Sublime Porte in Istanbul and served as an entrance to Old Lucknow and later to a palace that was demolished by the British Raj after the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

Major_Events.Description: Following the rebellion, the British Raj demolished the palace that the Rumi Darwaza once led to.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Rumi Darwaza is an example of Awadhi architecture, distinct from Mughal architecture. It features a big arch with a half-spherical dome on top, built using thin burnt clay bricks and lime-crushed brick aggregate mortar. The gate is adorned with intricate carvings of flowers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rumi Darwaza is culturally significant as a symbol of Lucknow's rich history and architectural heritage, reflecting the influence of Awadhi and Turkish architectural styles.
world knowledge.Details: The Rumi Darwaza is located between Bara Imambara and Chota Imambara and is adjacent to the Asafi Imambara and Teele Wali Masjid.

world knowledge.Name: Kasbah Amridil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kasbah Amridil is a historic fortified residence or kasbah in the oasis of Skoura, Morocco. Originally founded in the 17th century as a ksar (fortified village), it was expanded in the 19th century into a kasbah by M'hamed Ben Brahim Nasiri, a local privileged family member. The kasbah was built as compensation for Nasiri's services in educating the sons of Madani El Glaoui. It is considered one of the most impressive kasbahs in Morocco and was featured on the Moroccan 50 dirham note.

Major_Events.Description: The kasbah made an appearance in the 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The kasbah follows Moroccan (Berber) architecture, made from rammed earth or mudbrick with square corner towers and geometric decoration. The main house has four levels arranged around a central courtyard, with additional towers and a garden added during recent restorations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kasbah Amridil is culturally significant as a prime example of Moroccan Berber architecture and for its historical role in the region. It is a symbol of the traditional oasis architecture and the socio-political history of the Nasiri family.
world knowledge.Details: The kasbah is still owned and maintained by the Nasiri family, who live in one part of the building. Other parts have been restored to serve as a museum showcasing traditional architecture and local artifacts, including tools, an olive press, a bread oven, and an old well.

image_name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations

world knowledge.Name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 80 metres (260 ft) length, 70 metres (230 ft) width, 91 metres (299 ft) height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Monument to the Battle of the Nations (German: Völkerschlachtdenkmal) is a monument in Leipzig, Germany, to the 1813 Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations. Paid for mostly by donations and the city of Leipzig, it was completed in 1913 for the 100th anniversary of the battle at a cost of six million goldmarks. The monument commemorates the defeat of Napoleon's French army at Leipzig, a crucial step towards the end of hostilities in the War of the Sixth Coalition.

Major_Events.Description: The Völkerschlachtdenkmal was inaugurated in the presence of about 100,000 people including the Emperor, and all the reigning sovereign rulers of the German states.

The monument was the last stronghold in the city to surrender. 300 soldiers, men of the Volkssturm and boys of the Hitler Youth under the command of Oberst Hans von Poncet, were holding out in the monument, but after a direct artillery hit inside the structure, von Poncet was convinced to surrender following long negotiations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The structure is 91 metres (299 ft) tall. It contains over 500 steps to a viewing platform at the top, from which there are views across the city and environs. The structure makes extensive use of concrete, and the facings are of granite. It is widely regarded as one of the best examples of Wilhelmine architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monument commemorates the defeat of Napoleon's French army at Leipzig, a crucial step towards the end of hostilities in the War of the Sixth Coalition. It is widely regarded as one of the best examples of Wilhelmine architecture and stands as a symbol of German unity and national pride.
world knowledge.Details: The monument was designed by Bruno Schmitz and constructed over an artificial hill. It features a pyramidal shape for a clear view of the surroundings. The base is 124 metres (407 ft) square. The main structure, at 91 metres (299 ft), is as of 2013 still the tallest monument in Europe. The monument includes a crypt, a Hall of Fame, and an observation platform. It is surrounded by oaks and evergreens, symbolizing masculine strength and feminine fecundity.

world knowledge.Name: Gdańsk Shipyard
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gdańsk Shipyard, formerly known as Lenin Shipyard, was founded in 1946 on the sites of the former German shipyards, Schichau-Werft and Danziger Werft, which were damaged in World War II. It gained international fame in 1980 when the Solidarity trade union was founded there, marking the beginning of organized resistance to Communist dictatorship in Eastern Europe. The shipyard has undergone several name changes and ownership transformations, including becoming a joint stock company in 1990 and being privatized in 2007. It has produced over 1000 seagoing ships and now specializes in LNG/LPG transport ships, passenger-car ferries, and container vessels.

Major_Events.Description: The Solidarity trade union, led by Lech Wałęsa, was founded at the Gdańsk Shipyard, marking the beginning of organized resistance to Communist dictatorship in Eastern Europe.

French electronic music composer Jean Michel Jarre performed a multimedia concert at the shipyard to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the Solidarity movement, attracting 170,000 spectators and over 6 million television viewers.
David Gilmour, guitarist for Pink Floyd, played a concert at the shipyard to celebrate the anniversary of the Polish revolution as part of the Solidarity movement, attracting 50,000 spectators.
A fire occurred during a concert by the band Golden Life in the Gdansk Shipyard Hall, leading to the death of 7 people. The cause was arson, but the perpetrator was never identified.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shipyard is located on the western side of Martwa Wisła and on Ostrów Island, with a design office responsible for the design and construction of ships.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gdańsk Shipyard is culturally and historically significant as the birthplace of the Solidarity movement, which played a crucial role in the collapse of Communism in Eastern Europe. Its Gate Number Two has become a pilgrimage destination.
world knowledge.Details: The shipyard now employs around 2,200 workers, down from over 20,000 in its peak. It operates as part of the Repair Group, producing specialized ships for international clients. The European Union has backed a restructuring plan for the shipyard. About 77 companies operate on the grounds, including GSG Towers, which builds steel towers for wind turbines.

world knowledge.Name: Volcán de Colima
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Volcán de Colima, also known as Volcán de Fuego, is part of the Colima Volcanic Complex (CVC) consisting of Volcán de Colima, Nevado de Colima, and the eroded El Cántaro. It is the youngest of the three and as of 2015 is one of the most active volcanoes in Mexico and in North America. It has erupted more than 40 times since 1576. One of the largest eruptions was on January 20–24, 1913. Despite its name, only a fraction of the volcano's surface area is in the state of Colima; the majority of its surface area lies over the border in the neighboring state of Jalisco, toward the western end of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt.

Major_Events.Description: One of the largest eruptions occurred on January 20–24, 1913.
A strong explosion occurred at 06:27 UTC on January 18, 2017, spewing volcanic ash up to 4 km above the crater.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stratovolcano with andesite lava containing 56-61% SiO2. The currently active cone is within a large caldera probably formed by a combination of landslides and large eruptions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Designated a Decade Volcano due to its history of large eruptions and its location in a densely populated area, making it the most dangerous volcano in Mexico.
world knowledge.Details: The volcano is monitored by the Colima Volcano Observatory at the University of Colima, Mexico. In 2018, a webcam was installed close to the volcano, allowing real-time observation of volcanic activity.

world knowledge.Name: Kyoto Imperial Palace
world knowledge.Address: Kyoto Imperial Palace, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,300 metres (4,300 ft) north to south and 700 metres (2,300 ft) east to west
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kyoto Imperial Palace was the former palace of the Emperor of Japan until the capital was moved to Tokyo in 1869. It was preserved in 1877 and is now open to the public. The palace has been rebuilt eight times, with the current structure completed in 1855, modeled after the Heian period architecture.

Major_Events.Description: The capital functions were moved to Tokyo, and the palace lost much of its function.
The enthronement ceremony took place at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.
The enthronement ceremony took place at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.
The declaration of the restoration of imperial rule (osei fukko) was made here.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features traditional Heian period architecture with gabled and hipped roofs, cypress wood construction, and vermilion-painted gates. Key buildings include the Shishinden (Hall for State Ceremonies), Seiryōden (Emperor's Habitual Residence), and Kogosho (Court Room). The layout was modeled after the Tang capital, Chang'an.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kyoto Imperial Palace is a symbol of Japan's imperial history and cultural heritage. It was the residence of the Emperor for centuries and remains a site of important ceremonies and traditions, such as the Aoi Matsuri procession.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former imperial residence and site of state ceremonies; now a historic site open to the public.
world knowledge.Details: The palace grounds include the Sentō Imperial Palace gardens and the Kyoto State Guest House. The Shishinden houses the Imperial throne (Takamikura) and the August Seat of the Empress (Michodai). The palace is part of the larger Kyōto-gyoen, a public park. The Imperial Household Agency conducts public tours of the buildings.

world knowledge.Name: Jog Falls
world knowledge.Location: Siddapur taluk of Uttara Kannada district and Kargal town of Shimoga district, Karnataka, India
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 253 m (830 ft) height, 472 m (1,549 ft) average width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jog Falls is a waterfall on the Sharavati river and is the second highest plunge waterfall in India. It is a segmented waterfall which depends on rain and season to become a plunge waterfall. The falls are major attractions for tourists and is ranked 36th in the list of free-falling waterfalls, 490th in the world by list of waterfalls by total height, 128th in the list of single-drop waterfalls in the World by the waterfall database.

Major_Events.Description: The power station has been operational since 1948 and is of 120 MW capacity, one of the largest hydroelectric stations in India at that time and a small source of electric power for Karnataka now.
The capacity was increased subsequently and currently generates 240 MW of power.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Sharavathi, flowing over a very rocky bed about 250 yards (230 m) wide, reaches a tremendous chasm, 290 m (950 ft) deep, and the water comes down in four distinct falls, Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jog Falls is a major tourist attraction and holds significance in the field of hydroelectric power generation in India.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourist attraction and hydroelectric power generation
world knowledge.Details: The Tourism Department has built steps from the viewpoint at the top, where the waterfall can be seen from across, to the bottom of the hill. There are approximately 1,400 steps made to reach the bottom of the hill. Associated with the waterfall is the nearby Linganamakki Dam across the Sharavati River. The water released from the dam adds to the beauty of the waterfalls in the monsoon season.

world knowledge.Name: Hazuri Bagh Baradari
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hazuri Bagh Baradari is a baradari of white marble located in the Hazuri Bagh of Lahore, Pakistan. It was built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh, the Sikh ruler of Punjab to celebrate his capture of the Koh-i-Noor diamond from Shuja Shah Durrani in 1813.

Major_Events.Description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh captured the Koh-i-Noor diamond from Shuja Shah Durrani, leading to the construction of the Hazuri Bagh Baradari.
The pavilion was damaged by lightning, reducing it from two storeys to one.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pillars support delicate cusped arches. The central area, where Maharaja Ranjit Singh held court, has a mirrored ceiling. The pavilion originally consisted of two storeys.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hazuri Bagh Baradari is culturally significant as it was built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh to commemorate his capture of the Koh-i-Noor diamond, symbolizing the Sikh rule in Punjab.
world knowledge.Details: This article about Lahore is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it. This Pakistan location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Ancient Elis
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Elis is an ancient district in Greece, corresponding to the modern regional unit of Elis. It was located in southern Greece on the Peloponnese, bounded by Achaea, Arcadia, Messenia, and the Ionian Sea. The polis of Elis controlled much of the region, and the city of Elis was formed through synoecism in 471 BC. Elis held authority over Olympia and the Olympic games. The region was traditionally allied with Sparta but joined Argos and Athens against Sparta during the Peloponnesian War. Elis was a democracy by around 500 BC and continued to be so until 365 BC when an oligarchic faction took control. The region was divided into three districts: Koilē Elis, Pisatis, and Triphylia.

Major_Events.Description: The city of Elis was formed through synoecism, a process of amalgamation of smaller communities into a larger political entity.
The first recorded Olympic Games were held in Olympia, which was under Elian control.
Elis fought against Sparta in the Battle of Mantinea during the Peloponnesian War.
The Eleans destroyed the city of the Pisatans, who had attempted to reclaim their right to host the Olympic Games.
The Olympic Games were ended by Theodosius, two years before the Gothic invasion under Alaric I.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Elis had significant structures related to the Olympic Games, including gymnasia, a palaestra, and the House of the Hellanodikai. The ancient theater of Elis, built in the fourth century BC, had a capacity of 8,000 people and is one of the most well-preserved ancient theaters in Greece.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Elis is culturally significant as the region that controlled Olympia and the Olympic Games, which were a major Panhellenic event. The games influenced the political and social structure of Elis, and the region played a key role in the history of ancient Greece.
world knowledge.Details: Elis was a traditional ally of Sparta but joined Argos and Athens against Sparta during the Peloponnesian War. The region was divided into three districts: Koilē Elis, Pisatis, and Triphylia. The city of Elis was the capital of the city-state of Elis and was located at the exit of the river Peneios. The first excavations in Elis were carried out from 1910 to 1914 by the Austrian Archaeological Institute. Today, Elis is a small village built over the ruins of the ancient town.

world knowledge.Name: Terracotta Army
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Terracotta Army is a collection of terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China. It is a form of funerary art buried with the emperor in 210–209 BCE with the purpose of protecting him in his afterlife. The figures were discovered in 1974 by local farmers in Lintong County, outside Xi'an, Shaanxi, China.

Major_Events.Description: Discovered by local farmers digging a well approximately 1.5 km east of the Qin Emperor's tomb mound at Mount Li.
Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site during the 11th Session.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The figures are life-sized, typically ranging from 1.75 meters to about 2 meters in height. They vary in height, uniform, and hairstyle in accordance with their portrayed rank. The figures were originally painted with ground precious stones and other colors, but much of the color coating has flaked off over time. The construction involved assembly line production, with specific parts manufactured and assembled after being fired.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Terracotta Army is a significant archaeological discovery that provides insight into the military, artistic, and technological advancements of the Qin Dynasty. It is considered one of the greatest archaeological finds of the 20th century and a masterpiece of funerary art.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Funerary art to protect Qin Shi Huang in his afterlife.
world knowledge.Details: The Terracotta Army is part of a much larger necropolis, which includes bronze carriages, terracotta figures of entertainers, officials, stone armor suits, and more. The tomb itself remains unopened, possibly due to concerns over preservation of its artifacts. The figures were manufactured in workshops by government laborers and local craftsmen using local materials. The site has been the subject of numerous international exhibitions, drawing millions of visitors worldwide.

world knowledge.Name: Tell el-Dab'a
world knowledge.Construction_Period: End of the 12th Dynasty through the 13th Dynasty
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tell el-Dab'a is the modern name for the ancient city of Avaris, the capital of the Hyksos. It was occupied by Asiatics and became a large city with a mixture of Near Eastern and Egyptian cultures. It was a military rival to the Egyptians until its defeat and partial abandonment at the end of the Second Intermediate Period. The site was later fully abandoned following the construction of Pi-Ramesses under Ramesses II.

Major_Events.Description: Initial excavation of the site.
Excavated 20km north, mistakenly believing it was Avaris.
Confirmed the site as Avaris.
Confirmed Habachi's hypothesis and revealed the Hyksos capital was Tell el-Dab'a.
Documented in archaeology and surviving papyrus.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Buildings combine Egyptian and Canaanite architectural styles. Residences, tombs, and temples were discovered. The temples exhibit Egyptian and Canaanite styles with entrances in the north wall and orientation NNW-SSE. Temple I is in the Egyptian style with three sanctuaries and evidence of an altar. Minoan wall paintings were found, showing techniques and themes characteristic of Minoan frescos.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tell el-Dab'a represents a significant period of cultural interaction between Near Eastern and Egyptian societies. It was the capital of the Hyksos and a major military rival to the Egyptians. The site provides insights into the burial practices, trade relations, and artistic influences of the time.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ancient capital city and archaeological site.
world knowledge.Details: The society of Tell el-Dab’a interacted with individuals from other regions, influencing their frescos. The site has evidence of trade relations with Cyprus, indicated by Cypriot pottery. The Hyksos citadel was constructed towards the end of the Hyksos Period. The weighing system of the New Kingdom may have stemmed from the shekel weighing system used here. Ezbet Rushdi, a nearby village, has a temple and settlement from the Middle Kingdom period.

world knowledge.Name: Kings Landing Historical Settlement
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kings Landing is a living history museum in New Brunswick, created around buildings saved from the Mactaquac Dam headpond. It represents rural New Brunswick from 1820-1920, featuring original buildings moved and remodeled to specific historical years. The site was developed starting in the late 1960s to preserve cultural aspects that would otherwise be lost.

Major_Events.Description: A recreation of the controversy surrounding the formation of Canada, featuring actors portraying historical figures Charles Fisher and William Needham. Visitors are encouraged to participate by asking questions and voting.
The site was unofficially opened to the public.
The site was officially opened to the public on July 20, 1974.
Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip visited the site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site features more than a dozen original buildings from the 19th and early 20th centuries, including houses, trade shops, and barns. These buildings have been moved and remodeled to reflect specific years in their history. The complex also includes appropriate livestock and working trades buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kings Landing is culturally significant as it preserves and represents the rural life and heritage of New Brunswick during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It serves as a living museum, engaging visitors with costumed interpreters and period activities.
world knowledge.Details: Kings Landing hosts workshops on 19th-century tasks and crafts such as candle making, beekeeping, and woodworking. The site is continuously updated with new buildings and features to enhance the visitor experience.

world knowledge.Name: Quinta das Lágrimas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a hunting ground for the Portuguese royal family, later belonging to the University of Coimbra and a religious order. Acquired by the Osório Cabral de Castro family in 1730, who built the palace. Partially destroyed by fire in 1879 and rebuilt in a different style.

Major_Events.Description: A large part of the palace was lost during a fire.
The palace was rebuilt by Miguel Osório Cabral de Castro in a style different from the original.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace building has a central body and two lateral ones. The lateral bodies feature a balcony with a railing of square columns on their façade. To the right there is a chapel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Associated with the tragic love story of Prince Pedro and Inês de Castro. The estate is reportedly haunted by the ghost of Inês. The 'Fonte das Lágrimas' (Fountain of Tears) is a significant feature on the property.
world knowledge.Details: The name 'Quinta das Lágrimas' (Estate of Tears) comes from the legend of Prince Pedro and Inês de Castro. The fountain, 'Fonte das Lágrimas', is said to have originated from Inês' tears and her blood still stains its stone bottom. The estate is classified as an 'Imóvel de Interesse Publico' (Building of Public Interest) by the IPPAR.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Mehun-sur-Yèvre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Mehun-sur-Yèvre is a medieval castle with origins dating back to antiquity. The major remains are from the early 13th century and later 14th century. It was transformed into a princely residence by John, Duke of Berry in 1367. The castle is largely ruined today but was an excellent example of late Gothic and early Renaissance architecture.

Major_Events.Event: Death of Charles VII of France
Major_Events.Description: Charles VII of France died in the castle on July 22, 1461.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is built on a trapezoid plan, originally with a tall cylindrical tower at each corner and a rectangular tower in the middle of one of the long sides. The keep and the west tower still stand to their full height, each capped with intricate defensive machicolations. Manuscript illustrations indicate the castle also had a large chapel above the principal entrance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle has been classified as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture since 1840, highlighting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a fortress, later transformed into a princely residence.
world knowledge.Details: The castle represents an excellent example of late Gothic architecture and early Renaissance architecture. It was largely ruined in the 18th century.

world knowledge.Name: Talatal Ghar
world knowledge.Address: Rangpur, 4 kilometres from present-day Sivasagar, Assam, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Talatal Ghar is an 18th-century palace and military base located in Rangpur, Assam, India. It is the largest monument built during the Ahom era. Initially constructed by King Rudra Singha with semi-permanent materials, it was later rebuilt with major additions in bricks by King Rajeswar Singha. The palace originally had seven storeys, with three underground floors and two secret tunnels. It served as an army base and had royal apartments on the upper floors. Over time, the structure has deteriorated, and the underground floors were sealed during the British era.

Major_Events.Description: The upper floor chambers made of wood and timber were burnt during the Moamaria rebellion.
The palace suffered damage during the Burmese invasions.
The underground floors were sealed and filled during the British era.
Archaeological excavations unearthed buried structures, including brick platforms, pathways, and ceramic objects.
A survey conducted by IIT Kanpur and the Archaeological Survey of India did not reveal the existence of any secret tunnels.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Talatal Ghar features mixed architecture with seven storeys, including three underground floors. It was constructed using bricks and an indigenous type of cement made from sticky rice grain, swan eggs, etc. The palace had two secret tunnels, one leading to the Dikhow River and the other to the Garhgaon Palace. The structure includes long corridors, numerous rooms, and isolated chambers used for various purposes such as stables, store rooms, and royal apartments. The interior and exterior were once engraved with reliefs of hunting scenes, floral designs, and deities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Talatal Ghar is culturally significant as the largest monument from the Ahom era, reflecting the architectural and military ingenuity of the time. It served as a key military base and royal residence, playing a crucial role in the region's history. The structure's design and construction techniques are a testament to the Ahom kingdom's engineering prowess.
world knowledge.Details: The Talatal Ghar was surrounded by a brick fortification and an earthen fort with water-filled dikes. It included a Gola Ghar for storing gunpowder and ammunition. The palace's royal apartments and prayer house were located on the upper floors, with only a few rooms remaining today. The structure's irregular shape and dilapidated condition betray its former grandeur.

world knowledge.Name: Cahokia Mounds
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cahokia Mounds is the site of a pre-Columbian Native American city (c. 1050–1350 CE) directly across the Mississippi River from present-day St. Louis. It was the largest and most influential urban settlement of the Mississippian culture, which developed advanced societies across much of what is now the Central and Southeastern United States. The city's original name is unknown, but the mounds were later named after the Cahokia tribe, a historic Illiniwek people living in the area when the first French explorers arrived in the 17th century.

Major_Events.Description: Cahokia experienced rapid growth and construction, becoming a major urban center.
The site was designated a National Historic Landmark on July 19, 1964.
Cahokia Mounds was designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1982.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cahokia Mounds features 80 remaining earthen mounds out of the original 120, including Monks Mound, the largest pre-Columbian earthen construction in the Americas north of Mexico. The mounds are divided into three types: platform, conical, and ridge-top. The city was laid out with a symbolic quadripartite worldview, oriented toward the four cardinal directions, and included large plazas, a grand plaza, and a palisade with protective bastions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cahokia Mounds is considered the largest and most complex archaeological site north of the great pre-Columbian cities in Mexico. It is a National Historic Landmark and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its significance in understanding the Mississippian culture and pre-Columbian urban societies in North America.
world knowledge.Details: Cahokia Mounds was a major center for the Mississippian culture, with trade links extending to the Great Lakes and the Gulf Coast. The site includes Monks Mound, a massive platform mound with four terraces, and the Cahokia Woodhenge, a series of large timber circles used for astronomical observations. The site is managed by the Illinois Historic Preservation Division and supported by the Cahokia Mounds Museum Society.

world knowledge.Name: Adelaide Gaol
world knowledge.Area: Park 27 / Tulya Wardli, Adelaide Park Lands
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Adelaide Gaol is a former Australian prison located in the Park Lands of Adelaide, South Australia. It was the first permanent prison in the state, operating from 1841 to 1988. The gaol was built due to the need for secure housing for prisoners after temporary facilities proved inadequate. Over its 147 years of operation, it housed around 300,000 inmates and witnessed significant historical events, including public executions and overcrowding crises. After its closure, it was converted into a museum and tourist attraction.

Major_Events.Description: On Christmas Eve 1840, the first prisoners (14 debtors) were transferred from the old temporary gaol to the newly constructed Adelaide Gaol.
Joseph Stagg was the first prisoner executed publicly outside the gaol gate for his involvement in a cattle duffing gang.
The 'New Building' was used as a military detention barracks, and the gallows were used for a civilian execution in 1944.
The gaol was decommissioned and later reopened as a museum and tourist attraction under the South Australian Department for Environment and Heritage.
Excavations revealed evidence of the first settlers' camp and indigenous activity, with five distinct historical layers uncovered.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gaol features a radial plan with cellblocks and exercise yards accessible from a central point called 'The Circle.' The design was based on England's Pentonville prison, with two completed towers (one ornate). The original construction used ashlar stonework, which was more expensive than initially planned. Over time, renovations included modernized facilities, but some structures (like the Deputy Keeper's residence) were later demolished for not fitting the architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Adelaide Gaol is one of the two oldest surviving buildings in South Australia (alongside Government House). It represents the state's penal history, including public executions, overcrowding, and reforms. The site also holds archaeological significance, revealing early settler and indigenous activity. Today, it serves as a museum, offering educational tours and preserving dark historical narratives.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Formerly a prison; now a museum, tourist attraction, and function center.

Details.Managed by: Department of Environment, Water and Natural Resources
Details.Tour Information: Guided tours (60 minutes) are available for schools and the public, with interactive activities. Self-guided tours run daily from 10 am to 4 pm. Ghost tours operate at night.
Details.Dame Roma Mitchell Gardens: A community garden within the gaol walls, formerly tended by prisoners, now maintained by volunteers to provide produce for the homeless and needy.
Details.Executions: 45 of South Australia's 66 executions (1840–1964) occurred here, including the only woman (Elizabeth Woolcock) and the youngest (William Ridgway, 19).

world knowledge.Name: Mount Bandai
world knowledge.Area: Inawashiro-town, Bandai-town, and Kitashiobara village, Yama-Gun, Fukushima prefecture
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Bandai is an active stratovolcano with a history of eruptions dating back approximately 290,000 years. It was originally called 'Iwahashi-yama,' meaning 'a rock ladder to the sky.' The mountain experienced a significant eruption in 1888, which caused a sector collapse, buried villages, and led to the formation of several lakes. The eruption marked the first major disaster for the modern Japanese government, prompting extensive research and relief efforts.

Major_Events.Description: A phreatic eruption caused the north side of Kobandai to collapse, resulting in debris avalanches and lahars that buried five villages and killed 477 people. The eruption also formed lakes Hibara, Onogawako, Akimotoko, and Goshikinuma.

The Enichi Temple was founded one year after an earlier eruption of Mount Bandai. It serves as a central site for mountain worship and is surrounded by peaks including Mount Bandai, Mount Mayadake, and Mount Azuma.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stratovolcano with multiple peaks, including Bandai (main peak), Akahani, and Kushigamine. The mountain's shape varies depending on the viewing angle, appearing tidy from the south (Omotebandai) and wild from the north (Urabandai) due to its collapse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Bandai is one of Japan's 100 famous mountains and was selected as one of the top 100 geographic landmarks in Japan. It is also certified as a geopark. The mountain holds religious significance due to its association with the Enichi Temple and mountain worship traditions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural landmark, volcanic research site, and destination for hiking and tourism.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Bandai is part of the Bandai-Asahi National Park. Its official altitude was re-measured in 2010 as 1,816.29 m (5,959.0 ft). The mountain's name is sometimes referred to as 'Aizu Fuji' or 'Aizu Bandai.' The 1888 eruption led to significant government relief efforts, including involvement by the Japanese Red Cross, and a monument was erected in Goshikinuma to honor relief contributors.

world knowledge.Name: New Athos Cave
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The New Athos Cave, known as the 'Bottomless Pit', was explored in 1961 by an expedition of four: Zurab Tatashidze, Arsen Okrojanashvili, Boris Gergedava, and Givi Smyr. Since 1975, it has been a major tourist attraction, featuring its own underground railway.

Major_Events.Description: An expedition of four explored the cave, which was previously known as the 'Bottomless Pit'.
The cave became a major tourist attraction, featuring an underground railway.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Karst cave with 9 major cavities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cave is a significant natural landmark and tourist attraction in Abkhazia, known for its unique karst formations and historical exploration.
world knowledge.Details: The cave has four entrances and is accessible to the public. It was opened as a show cave in 1961 and features an underground railway.

world knowledge.Name: Utsunomiya Station
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Utsunomiya Station is a historic railway station in Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan, operated by JR East and JR Freight. It opened on July 16, 1885, and has since been a key transportation hub.

Major_Events.Description: The station was opened on July 16, 1885, as part of the Tōhoku Main Line.
The station became a stop for the Tōhoku Shinkansen and Yamagata Shinkansen lines.
Planned extension of the light rail line to the West Exit and beyond, scheduled for the 2030s.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The station features elevated Shinkansen platforms designed for 16-car trains, with separate inbound and outbound platforms. Local train platforms are a mix of island and individual platforms for 15-car trains. LED information signboards are present on the concourse and platforms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Utsunomiya Station is a vital transportation hub in Tochigi Prefecture, connecting Tokyo with northern Japan. It plays a significant role in regional travel and commerce.
world knowledge.Details: The station is served by the Tōhoku Shinkansen, Yamagata Shinkansen, Tōhoku Main Line (Utsunomiya Line), and Nikkō Line. It also connects to the Utsunomiya Light Rail and bus terminals. In fiscal 2019, it averaged 37,374 daily passengers. Track 4 has been unused since August 27, 2023.

image_name: Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca

world knowledge.Name: Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca, also known as Castillo del Morro, is a fortress on the coast of Santiago de Cuba. Designed by Giovanni Battista Antonelli in the early 1600s, it was built to protect the city from pirate attacks. Construction began in 1638 and was completed in 1700, though work was sporadic. The fortress is considered the best-preserved example of Spanish-American military architecture and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

Major_Events.Description: English freebooters led by Christopher Myngs took control of Santiago for two weeks, destroyed part of the fortification, and captured the artillery.
The fortress was damaged by a series of earthquakes between 1675 and 1692, and reconstruction was carried out under Francisco Pérez.
Parts of the fortress were converted into a prison for political prisoners, while the rest remained a military base.
The fortress was used again during the United States' fleet attack on Santiago de Cuba.
The fort was restored by Francisco Prat Puig after falling into disrepair during the 20th century.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fortress was designed by Giovanni Battista Antonelli and adapted to the steep sides of the promontory. It features four main levels, three large bulwarks for artillery, and a large warehouse cut into the rock. The citadel was constructed on a series of terraces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca is culturally and historically significant as the best-preserved example of Spanish-American military architecture. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
world knowledge.Details: The fortress was initially built to defend against pirate attacks and later served as a prison and military base. It has undergone multiple reconstructions due to damage from earthquakes and attacks.

world knowledge.Name: Bazaar of Arak
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bazaar of Arak is one of the first constructed buildings in the city of Arak (central Iran). The bazaar complex, containing a public bath, a mosque, water reservoirs, passages, and caravansary, was built at the time of Fath-Ali Shah Qajar by Yusef Khan-e Gorji in the middle of Sultan Abad (Arak's former name). The bazaar and the city of Sultan Abad were built simultaneously, although no exact date has been recorded for the establishment of the bazaar. The first buildings in Arak bazaar were built in the 19th century by the order of the time governor of Arak, Sepahdar Aazm.

Major_Events.Description: Arak and its bazaar became an important center for struggle against foreign investments.
The reservoir was demolished by Arak's municipality to make room for a new school.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Bazaar of Arak is based on a pre-designed plan with geometrically symmetrical routes. The buildings are mainly made of bricks, with gypsum and lime also used. Wooden joists in clay have made the buildings stronger. Sheets of copper and lead are used in columns' bases. The special architectural design keeps the inside of the bazaar cool in summer and warm in winter.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bazaar of Arak is culturally and historically important as a center for economic, social, and political activities. It has been a main center for storing goods and economic exchanges, a place where different social and ethnic groups meet, and a center for rebellion and strikes in Iran's history.
world knowledge.Details: The Bazaar of Arak contains a public bath, a mosque, water reservoirs, passages, and caravansary. It is centered at Chahr Soogh, the junction of two north–south and east–west paths that end to four ancient city gates. The bazaar is now finding its way in internal and global trades, exporting commodities produced in Iran such as dried fruit, handicrafts, and handmade carpets.

world knowledge.Name: Democracy Monument
world knowledge.Address: Bowon Niwet subdistrict, Phra Nakhon district, Bangkok, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Commissioned in 1939 to commemorate the 1932 Siamese coup d'état, which led to the establishment of a constitutional monarchy in Thailand. The monument was designed by Chitrasen Aphaiwong and features sculptures by Corrado Feroci. It was built by Christiani & Nielsen and intended to symbolize the new, Westernized Bangkok envisioned by Field Marshal Plaek Phibunsongkhram.

Major_Events.Description: Mass student demonstrations against Thanom Kittikachorn's military regime.
Protests triggered a military coup.
Scores of Thais were killed protesting against General Suchinda Kraprayoon's regime.
Rally point for the People's Democratic Reform Committee against Pheu Thai Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra.
Rallying point for protestors against the government.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Deco and Khana Ratsadon architecture. The monument features a carved representation of a palm-leaf manuscript box holding the Thai Constitution of 1932, guarded by four wing-like structures representing the four branches of the Thai armed forces. The wings are 24 meters high, and the central turret is 3 meters high. The monument includes relief sculptures depicting the armed forces as champions of democracy and the personification of the Thai people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Democracy Monument commemorates the transition to a constitutional monarchy in Thailand and has served as a rallying point for democracy activists throughout its history. Despite its origins as a propaganda piece for the Phibun regime, it has gained legitimacy through its association with significant democratic movements.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public monument commemorating the 1932 Siamese coup d'état and the establishment of a constitutional monarchy.
world knowledge.Details: The monument was highly unpopular at the time of its construction due to the eviction of local residents and the cutting down of hundreds of shade trees. The relief sculptures at the base of the monument are propagandistic, depicting the armed forces as the personification of the Thai people and champions of democracy. The monument has become a symbol of democratic struggle in Thailand, despite its controversial origins.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Fère-en-Tardenois
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Fère-en-Tardenois is a ruined castle originally constructed in 1206. It was transformed around 1528 by Anne de Montmorency and enlarged in 1555 with the addition of a Renaissance bridge carrying a covered gallery. The castle served as a model for numerous other castles due to its seven towers on an enormous artificial motte.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the original castle began, featuring seven towers on an enormous artificial motte.
Anne de Montmorency, companion of Francis I, transformed the castle.
The castle was enlarged with the addition of a famous Renaissance bridge carrying a covered gallery, possibly involving architect Jean Bullant and sculptor Jean Goujon.
The castle was listed as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle originally had seven towers on an enormous artificial motte covered in slabs of sandstone. It was later transformed with Renaissance elements, including a bridge carrying a covered gallery. The quality of the sculptures, stone, and colors suggests the involvement of skilled artisans like Jean Bullant and Jean Goujon.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Fère-en-Tardenois is culturally significant as a model for numerous other castles and for its Renaissance transformations. It is also a listed monument historique, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Ownership of the castle is shared by the département and a private company. It is open to the public and has been listed as a monument historique since 1862.

world knowledge.Name: Zaanse Schans
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zaanse Schans is a neighbourhood of Zaandam, known for its collection of historic windmills and wooden houses relocated from the wider region north of Amsterdam for preservation. It derived its name from the river Zaan and its original function as a sconce against Spanish troops during the Eighty Years' War of Dutch independence.

Major_Events.Description: Old buildings from the Zaanstreek region were relocated to Zaanse Schans using lowboy trailers for preservation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Historic windmills and wooden houses representing Zaanse timber construction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zaanse Schans is a protected village scene due to its architectural-historical and landscape value. It is an anchor point of the European Route of Industrial Heritage and a major tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: Zaanse Schans houses seven museums, including the Weavers House, the Cooperage, and the Bakery Museum. It is served by Zaandijk Zaanse Schans railway station, 18 minutes from Amsterdam Centraal station. The neighbourhood attracts millions of visitors annually, with debates on reducing overcrowding.

world knowledge.Name: Heian Shrine
world knowledge.Address: 97, Okazaki-Nishi-tenno-cho, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto-shi, Kyoto Prefecture, JAPAN, 606-8341
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Heian-jingu Shrine was built in 1895 as a partial reproduction of the Heian Palace for the 1100th anniversary of the establishment of Heian-kyō. It was initially part of the Industrial Exposition Fair. After the exhibition, it was preserved as a shrine dedicated to Emperor Kanmu, and later Emperor Kōmei was added in 1940. The shrine suffered a fire in 1976, which destroyed several buildings, including the main sanctuary, but they were reconstructed by 1979.

Major_Events.Description: The shrine was originally built as the main monument for the Industrial Exposition Fair, celebrating the 1100th anniversary of Heian-kyō.
A fire destroyed nine buildings, including the main sanctuary. Reconstruction was completed in 1979 using donations.
One of Kyoto's most important festivals, featuring a procession from the old Imperial palace to the shrine, carrying mikoshi of Emperors Kanmu and Kōmei.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shrine is a 5/8 scale reproduction of the Chōdōin (Emperor's palace) in the late Heian Period style. It features Shichigensya-Nagare-zukuri architecture, a large red entrance gate replicating the Outenmon, and one of Japan's largest torii. The main palace mirrors the Kyoto Imperial Palace's 11th–12th century design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Heian Shrine is a Beppyō Jinja (top-ranked shrine) and an important cultural property of Japan. It honors Emperors Kanmu and Kōmei and serves as a symbol of Kyoto's historical and cultural heritage. The shrine hosts major festivals and events, blending traditional and modern culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Kanmu and Emperor Kōmei, used for worship, festivals, weddings, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The shrine's garden, designed by Ogawa Jihei VII, spans half the land area and features rare species like Acheilognathus cyanostigma and Japanese pond turtles. Adjacent to Okazaki Park, it is surrounded by cultural institutions like the Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art and the Kyoto City Zoo. Parts of the 2003 film 'Lost in Translation' were filmed here.

world knowledge.Name: Melrose Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St Mary's Abbey, Melrose is a partly ruined monastery of the Cistercian order in Melrose, Roxburghshire, in the Scottish Borders. It was founded in 1136 by Cistercian monks at the request of King David I of Scotland and was the chief house of that order in the country until the Reformation. The abbey is known for its many carved decorative details, including likenesses of saints, dragons, gargoyles, and plants. It was rebuilt after several attacks and is now maintained by Historic Environment Scotland as a scheduled monument.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by Cistercian monks at the request of King David I of Scotland.

Major_Events.Event: Attack by Edward II of England
Major_Events.Description: Much of the abbey was destroyed and later rebuilt by order of King Robert the Bruce.

Major_Events.Event: Attack by Richard II of England
Major_Events.Description: The abbey was burned and rebuilt over a period of about 100 years.

Major_Events.Event: Final assault by Oliver Cromwell's troops
Major_Events.Description: The abbey was bombarded during the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of Robert the Bruce's heart
Major_Events.Description: A lead container believed to hold the embalmed heart of Robert the Bruce was found below the Chapter House site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey was built in the Gothic manner and in the form of a St. John's Cross. It features many carved decorative details, including likenesses of saints, dragons, gargoyles, and plants. The east end of the abbey was completed in 1146, and other buildings in the complex were added over the next 50 years.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Melrose Abbey is culturally and historically significant as the first Cistercian abbey in Scotland and the chief house of that order in the country until the Reformation. It is known for its intricate carvings and as the burial site of several Scottish kings and nobles, including the heart of Robert the Bruce.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey is maintained by Historic Environment Scotland and is part of the Borders Abbeys Way walk. It has been featured in literature, video games, and inspired the design of a church in the United States. In 2019, the site received 61,325 visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Buland Darwaza
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed by Mughal emperor Akbar in 1573 to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. It serves as the main entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri.

Major_Events.Event: Commemoration of Akbar's victory over Gujarat
Major_Events.Description: The gate was erected to celebrate Akbar's conquest of Gujarat.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Made of red and buff sandstone, the gateway is 54 meters high, featuring a semi-octagonal plan with two smaller triple-storeyed wings, three kiosks on top surrounded by thirteen smaller domed kiosks, and smaller turrets. It includes a long flight of 42 steps, arched niches, small laudas, and marble inlays highlighting the courtyard of the Jama Masjid.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Buland Darwaza is significant for its Mughal architecture and as a symbol of Akbar's military victories. It also features Islamic inscriptions and verses from the Quran, reflecting the religious and cultural ethos of the time.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Main entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri
world knowledge.Details: The gateway includes a Persian inscription recording Akbar's conquest of Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. An Islamic inscription on the main gateway quotes Jesus, advising against worldly attachments. Verses from the Quran are carved in Naskh script along the top, drawn by Khwaja Hussain Chishti.

world knowledge.Name: Valaste Falls
world knowledge.Address: Between Ontika and Valaste in Toila Parish of Ida-Viru County
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valaste Falls is the highest waterfall in Estonia and neighboring regions, formed by Valaste Creek as it flows over the Baltic Klint near the Gulf of Finland. It is a popular tourist attraction, known for its freezing spray in winter.

Major_Events.Description: The viewing platform was taken out of service and the stairs to it were closed.
A new staircase with platforms and walkways to the shore of the Gulf of Finland was built and opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site features a double spiral staircase to reach the bottom of the cliff and a viewing platform offering views of the falls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valaste Falls is a significant natural landmark in Estonia, attracting tourists for its height and scenic beauty.
world knowledge.Details: The waterfall has a parking lot, explanatory signs, and a trail with a double spiral staircase. The viewing platform was closed in 2013, and a new staircase was opened in 2018.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Bromo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Bromo is an active somma volcano and a Hindu pilgrimage site, part of the Tengger mountains in East Java, Indonesia. It is the most active and famous peak in the massif, standing at 2,329 meters (7,641 ft). The name Bromo comes from the Javanese pronunciation of Brahma, the Hindu god of creation. The area is a major tourist destination and is included in the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park. The volcano is located in the middle of a plain called 'Sea of Sand,' a nature reserve protected since 1919.

Major_Events.Description: The eruption led to the death of two people who were hit by rocks from the explosion.
In November 2010, Mount Bromo's activity status was raised to 'alert' due to increasing tremor activity and shallow volcanic earthquakes. The volcano began violently erupting ash on 26 November 2010.

During the Hindu festival of Yadnya Kasada, the Tenggerese people travel up the mountain to make offerings of fruit, rice, vegetables, flowers, and livestock to the mountain gods by throwing them into the caldera. This ritual originates from a 15th-century legend.
