world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mount Bromo is characterized by its somma volcano structure, with a crater at its summit. The area includes the 'Sea of Sand' plain and the Hindu temple Pura Luhur Poten, which is built from natural black stones from nearby volcanoes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Bromo holds significant cultural and religious importance for the Javanese Hindus, particularly the Tenggerese people. It is a site of pilgrimage and the annual Yadnya Kasada festival, where offerings are made to the mountain gods. The temple Pura Luhur Poten is a central place of worship for the Tenggerese community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Volcano, Hindu pilgrimage site, tourist destination
world knowledge.Details: Mount Bromo is part of the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park and is one of the most visited tourist destinations in East Java. The volcano is known for its frequent eruptions and the stunning 'Sea of Sand' plain. The nearby Mount Batok is often mistaken for Mount Bromo due to its prominence in the caldera. The area is also home to the Hindu temple Pura Luhur Poten, which plays a significant role in the local Tenggerese culture.

world knowledge.Name: Trevi Fountain
world knowledge.Address: Via De' Crocicchi, Via Poli and Via Delle Muratte, Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height: 26.3 metres (86 ft), Length: 49 metres (161 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Trevi Fountain is an 18th-century fountain designed by Italian architect Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762. It marks the terminal point of the 'modern' Acqua Vergine, a revived aqueduct that supplied water to ancient Rome. The fountain is the largest Baroque fountain in Rome and one of the most famous fountains in the world.

Major_Events.Description: Refurbished to remove discoloration caused by smog.
Stonework was scrubbed, cracks and other areas of deterioration were repaired, and recirculating pumps were installed.
Sponsored by Fendi, this restoration included the installation of more than 100 LED lights to improve nighttime illumination.
Activists of the climate group Ultima Generazione dyed the water with charcoal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fountain is made from Travertine stone and features a giant order of Corinthian pilasters. It includes a triumphal arch, niches with statues of Abundance and Salubrity, and Tritons guiding Oceanus's shell chariot. The design incorporates elements of Baroque and Rococo styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Trevi Fountain is culturally significant as one of the most famous fountains in the world and a symbol of Rome. It is associated with the tradition of throwing a coin into the fountain to ensure a return to the city. The fountain has appeared in numerous films and is a popular tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The fountain's water is supplied by the Acqua Vergine aqueduct, which is still in use today. An estimated 3,000 euros are thrown into the fountain each day, with the money donated to charity. The fountain has been replicated in various locations around the world, including Brazil, Las Vegas, Seoul, and Guatemala.

world knowledge.Name: Spanish Arch
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Spanish Arch (Irish: An Póirse) and the Caoċ Arch (Irish: An Póirse Caoċ, "blind arch") in Galway city, Ireland, are two remaining arches on the Ceann an Bhalla ("Front Wall"). The two arches were part of the extension of the city wall from Martin's Tower to the bank of the River Corrib, as a measure to protect the city's quays, which were in the area once known as the Fish Market (now Spanish Parade). It was constructed during the mayoralty of Wylliam Martin in 1584, being called ceann an bhalla (the head of the wall). In the 18th century the Eyre family of Eyrecourt, County Galway, created an extension of the quays called The Long Walk and created the arches to allow access from the town to the new quays. The designation "Spanish" is not historical to this period and was likely known as the Eyre Arch when built.

Major_Events.Description: The arches were partially destroyed by the tsunami generated by the 1755 Lisbon earthquake.
Part of the Arch housed the Galway City Museum until 2006, when the museum was moved to a new, dedicated building located just behind the Arch.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: archway, part of a former city wall
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a historical landmark, the Spanish Arch appears in several media works set in Galway, including the 1957 film The Rising of the Moon.
world knowledge.Details: The Long Walk is a promenade to one side of the Arches.

world knowledge.Name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
world knowledge.Address: 60 kilometres north of Lijiang City, Yunnan, China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 15 kilometres in length, maximum depth of 3,790 meters
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tiger Leaping Gorge is a scenic canyon on the Jinsha River, a primary tributary of the upper Yangtze River. It is part of the Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas World Heritage Site. Legend says the name comes from a hunted tiger escaping by jumping across the river at the narrowest point.

Major_Events.Event: First successful navigation of the gorge
Major_Events.Description: The first known successful attempt to sail through the gorge was made by the first expedition to float down the entire length of the Yangtze, starting at the river's high source at the Gelandandong glacier lake.
The area was officially opened to foreign tourists, but had already attracted adventurous backpackers in the 1980s.
The Chinese government floated proposals for a hydroelectric dam on the Jinsha River. The project was abandoned in December 2007 due to potential environmental and cultural impacts.
The Chinese government closed the gorge to visitors because a new lower road was being built. Many trekkers still hiked the high road in spite of its closure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gorge features steep cliffs, rapids, and a variety of micro-ecosystems. The hiking path ("the high road") is well-maintained and marked, although sometimes narrow. The lower road is a stretch of pavement crossed by several waterfalls and frequently beset by rockslides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tiger Leaping Gorge is one of the deepest and most spectacular river canyons in the world. It is inhabited primarily by the indigenous Nakhi people, whose primary subsistence comes from grain production and hiking tourism. The gorge is part of the Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The gorge is located where the river passes between the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and the Haba Snow Mountain. The inhabitants of the gorge are primarily the indigenous Nakhi people. The area was officially opened to foreign tourists in 1993. Natural crystals are mined from areas in and surrounding the Tiger Leaping Gorge. The weather is generally mild, with abundant rainfall and plenty of sunshine. Hiking the length of the gorge is possible, with both high and low roads available for trekking.

world knowledge.Name: Ekʼ Balam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ekʼ Balam was a significant Mayan kingdom from the Preclassic until the Postclassic period. It became the capital of the polity controlling the region around the beginning of the Common Era. The city thrived from 770 to 840 CE but saw a dramatic population decline during the Postclassic period, eventually becoming vacant. It was rediscovered in the late 1800s by Désiré Charnay, with extensive excavation occurring in the late 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The city thrived and became a rich resource for understanding northern Classic Maya cities.
Rediscovered by archaeologist Désiré Charnay.
Mapped by Bill Ringle and George Bey III, with the Acropolis excavated by Leticia Vargas de la Peña and Víctor Castillo Borges.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site features 45 structures, including the Acropolis which houses the tomb of king Ukit Kan Leʼk Tok'. The layout includes two concentric defensive walls, with the inner wall encompassing 9.55 hectares. The buildings follow the northern Petén architectural style, with sacbé roads extending in the four cardinal directions, symbolizing a 'four-part cosmos'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ekʼ Balam is culturally significant for its well-preserved plaster on the tomb of Ukit Kan Lek Tokʼ and its extensive hieroglyphic texts, including the 'Mural of the 96 Glyphs'. It provides valuable insights into the northern Classic Maya cities and their architectural and cultural practices.
world knowledge.Details: The site is surrounded by defensive walls, with the inner wall being highly decorative and the outer wall purely defensive. The Acropolis contains significant wall paintings and vault capstones depicting the lightning deity. The site's sacbé roads are considered sacred and extend in the four cardinal directions.

world knowledge.Name: Biak Archipelago
world knowledge.Area: Cenderawasih Bay (or Geelvink Bay), Papua province, eastern Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Biak Islands, also known as the Schouten Islands or Geelvink Islands, were first sighted by Europeans in 1526 by Portuguese navigator Jorge de Menezes. The archipelago was later explored by Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra in 1528 and named Islas de Oro. Dutch explorer Willem Schouten explored the islands in 1615, and they were subsequently named after him. The islands have a history of tributary ties with the Tidore Sultanate and were mapped by various Portuguese, Spanish, and Dutch cartographers.

Major_Events.Description: Portuguese navigator Jorge de Menezes sighted the islands and named them 'Islands of Papuas'.
Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra landed on Yapen and named the islands 'Islas de Oro'.
Dutch explorer Willem Schouten explored the islands, which were later named after him.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Biak Islands are culturally significant due to their historical exploration by European navigators, their ties to the Tidore Sultanate, and their unique biodiversity. The islands are also part of the Coral Triangle, known for its marine biodiversity.
world knowledge.Details: The Biak Islands are among the most densely populated parts of Papua province and are home to a highly endemic avifauna, with over 100 bird species, 11 to 16 of which are endemic. The islands also have endemic mammals, butterflies, and a spider. The seas around the islands are part of the Coral Triangle, and there are two marine protected areas: the Biak Numfor Locally Managed Marine Area and the Padaido Marine Recreation Park.

world knowledge.Name: Po Lin Monastery
world knowledge.Address: Ngong Ping Plateau, Lantau Island, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Po Lin Monastery is a Buddhist monastery founded in 1906 by three monks from Jiangsu Province, China. Initially known as 'The Big Hut', it was renamed to its present name in 1924. The monastery is known for its main temple housing three bronze statues of the Buddha and many Buddhist scriptures. The Tian Tan Buddha, a giant statue completed in 1993, is an extension of the monastery.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Chi Chuk Lam Nunnery
Major_Events.Description: Three nuns ordained at Po Lin Monastery established a private nunnery called Chi Chuk Lam on Lantau's Lower Keung Hill, dedicated to Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy.
A giant Buddha statue, an extension of the monastery, was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery features prominent architectural structures such as the Main Shrine Hall of Buddha and the Hall of Bodhisattva Skanda.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Po Lin Monastery is a significant Buddhist site in Hong Kong, known for its religious artifacts, architectural beauty, and the Tian Tan Buddha statue. It plays a vital role in the local Buddhist community and attracts numerous visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery is noted for making wooden bracelets sold near the Tian Tan Buddha statue. The Ngong Ping 360, including a gondola lift and Ngong Ping village, was built near the monastery.

world knowledge.Name: Fajã dos Cubres
world knowledge.Address: Ribeira Seca, São Jorge, Central Group, Azores, Portugal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fajã dos Cubres is a permanent debris field, known as a fajã, built from the collapsing cliffs on the northern coast of the civil parish of Ribeira Seca, in the municipality of Calheta, island of São Jorge, in the Portuguese archipelago of the Azores. The size of the fajã has been attributed to the 9 July 1757 earthquake, considered the most violent tectonic quake that occurred in the Azores. This seismic event was characterized by violent movements of land (landslides, collapses, and rockfalls) that were responsible for the creation of several fajãs on the island, such as the Fajã of Ponta Nova, and the growth of pre-existing fajãs.

Major_Events.Description: The most violent tectonic quake in the Azores, characterized by violent movements of land (landslides, collapses, and rockfalls) that were responsible for the creation of several fajãs on the island, such as the Fajã of Ponta Nova, and the growth of pre-existing fajãs.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Hermitage of Nossa Senhora das Lurdes
Major_Events.Description: The Hermitage of Nossa Senhora das Lurdes was open to the faithful on 18 October 1908. It was offered to the public by António Faustino Nunes, a native of this fajã and later emigrant to California.
During the 1980 earthquake several buildings were damaged.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fajã is an irregular form, with four small islets, and is heavily influenced by tidal waters, due to the diffusion of salt water into the lagoon. The settlement constitutes a unique countryside, with a mix of buildings with modern and older amenities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The fajã is culturally significant due to its unique geological formation, historical events such as the 1757 earthquake, and the presence of the Hermitage of Nossa Senhora das Lurdes. It is also important for its diverse marine and migratory bird populations and its unique ecosystem.
world knowledge.Details: The fajã has a variety of typical marine flora and fauna, and its lagoon has become a natural refuge for diverse marine and migratory birds. Nesting birds include the Cory's shearwater, common snipe, yellow-legged gull, and the common tern. Annually, farmers bring cattle down to the fajã to graze. Although prohibited now, at one time fishing occurred in the lagoon, mostly mullet and anchovies, using netting techniques. The fajã is accessible by a winding road that descends the northern cliffs from the village of Norte Pequeno. Until 1993 this was a dirt roadway, and crossed many small bridges, where water drained from the plateau, but it was eventually asphalted by regional authorities.

world knowledge.Name: Land's End
world knowledge.Address: Land's End, Penzance, Cornwall, TR19, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Land's End is a headland and tourist complex in western Cornwall, England, known as the most westerly point of mainland England. It has been a tourist destination for over three hundred years and is associated with various historical and cultural references, including Arthurian literature and the mythical lost land of Lyonesse.

Major_Events.Description: Four schoolchildren died in what is known as the Land's End disaster.
Land's End received worldwide publicity as the starting point of the 2012 Summer Olympics torch relay.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cliffs are made of granite, an igneous rock, resistant to weathering, with steep cliff faces. Two varieties of granite are present: coarse-grained with large phenocrysts of orthoclase and finer-grained with fewer and smaller phenocrysts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Land's End is culturally significant as the most westerly point of mainland England and is often used to suggest distance in the UK. It is also associated with Arthurian literature and the mythical lost land of Lyonesse.
world knowledge.Details: Land's End is a popular venue for rock climbers and has been designated part of an Important Plant Area for rare species of flora. The area includes attractions such as children's playgrounds, recorded music, and a night-time firework spectacular called 'Magic in the Skies'.

world knowledge.Name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
world knowledge.Address: Constitution Gardens, adjacent to the National Mall, northeast of the Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C., U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is a U.S. national memorial honoring service members of the U.S. armed forces who served in the Vietnam War. The site is dominated by two black granite walls engraved with the names of those who died or remain missing as a result of their service in Vietnam and South East Asia during the war. Designed by Maya Lin, it is an example of minimalist architecture. The Wall was completed in 1982 and later supplemented with the statue Three Soldiers in 1984 and the Vietnam Women's Memorial in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: The memorial was dedicated on November 13, 1982, as part of a five-day ceremony called the "National Salute to Vietnam Veterans."
A bronze statue named Three Servicemen was added to the memorial site, depicting three soldiers looking at the Wall in solemn tribute.
A memorial dedicated to the women of the United States who served in the Vietnam War, most of whom were nurses, was added to the site.

Major_Events.Event: Dedication of In Memory Memorial Plaque
Major_Events.Description: A plaque was dedicated to honor veterans who died after the war as a result of injuries suffered in Vietnam but who fall outside Department of Defense guidelines.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The memorial consists of two adjoining black granite walls, each 246 feet 9 inches long, composed of 72 panels polished to a high finish. The walls taper from 8 inches tall at their extremities to 10.1 feet tall at the apex where they meet. The design is symbolic of a "wound that is closed and healing" and exemplifies the Land art movement of the 1960s. The stone for the panels was quarried in Bangalore, India.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is culturally and historically important as it honors the service and sacrifice of U.S. armed forces members during the Vietnam War. It serves as a place of healing and reflection for veterans, families, and visitors. Despite initial controversy over its minimalist design, it has become one of America's most revered memorials.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Memorial honoring U.S. service members who served in the Vietnam War.
world knowledge.Details: The memorial includes the names of 58,320 service members who died or remain missing as of May 2018. Names are listed in chronological order of casualty dates. The memorial also features the Three Soldiers statue and the Vietnam Women's Memorial. It receives around three million visitors annually and is maintained by the National Park Service. Items left at the memorial are collected and stored by the NPS Museum Resource Center.

world knowledge.Name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Greyfriars Kirkyard is the graveyard surrounding Greyfriars Kirk in Edinburgh, Scotland. It was established in 1561–1562 after royal sanctions were granted to replace the churchyard at St Giles' Cathedral. The Kirkyard has been a burial site since the late 16th century and is associated with the Covenanting movement, which began with the signing of the National Covenant here in 1638. It also served as a makeshift prison for Covenanters after the Battle of Bothwell Bridge in 1679. The Kirkyard is known for its historic monuments and its connection to Greyfriars Bobby, the loyal dog who guarded his master's grave.

Major_Events.Description: The Covenanting movement began with the signing of the National Covenant in Greyfriars Kirkyard on 28 February 1638.
Following the defeat of the militant Covenanters at Bothwell Brig in 1679, some 1200 Covenanters were imprisoned in a field to the south of the churchyard.

Major_Events.Event: Vandalism of Sir George MacKenzie's tomb
Major_Events.Description: Two teenage boys entered the tomb of Sir George MacKenzie, broke open coffins, and stole a skull, narrowly escaping imprisonment for violating sepulchres.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Kirkyard features enclosed burial lairs with solid stone walls or iron railings to deter grave robbing, as well as two low ironwork cages called mortsafes. It also displays some of Scotland's finest mural monuments from the early 17th century, rich in symbolism of mortality and immortality, such as the Death Head, Angel of the Resurrection, and the King of Terrors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Greyfriars Kirkyard is culturally significant for its association with the Covenanting movement, its historic monuments, and its connection to Greyfriars Bobby, a symbol of loyalty. It is also a protected category A listed building.
world knowledge.Details: The Kirkyard is operated by the City of Edinburgh Council in liaison with a charitable trust. It is associated with Greyfriars Bobby, whose statue is located opposite the graveyard's gate. The sealed south-west section, known as the Covenanters' Prison, is accessible during the day by special arrangement or through guided tours.

world knowledge.Name: Fengjia Night Market
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fengjia Night Market was established in 1963 alongside Feng Chia College of Engineering and Business (now Feng Chia University). The market's popularity grew, stimulating business in the nearby residential military dependents' village. Over time, food stands and restaurants expanded to surrounding streets such as Wen-hua Road, Fengjia Road, Fuxing Road, and Xi'an Street. In 2006, the Fengjia Shopping Town managing committee was established, bringing the night market under the governance of Taichung city. In 2015, the market was commended by the Ministry of Economic Affairs for its management, tourist friendliness, and sustainable practices.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Fengjia Shopping Town managing committee
Major_Events.Description: The Department of Economic Development of Taichung established a managing committee to oversee the night market and surrounding areas, bringing unlicensed operations under city governance.

Major_Events.Event: Commendation by Ministry of Economic Affairs
Major_Events.Description: The night market was recognized for excellency in management, friendliness to tourists, and sustainable environmental practices.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fengjia Night Market is culturally significant as one of the largest and most popular night markets in Taiwan, known for its vibrant atmosphere, diverse food offerings, and role in local commerce and tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The market is located next to Feng Chia University and is also referred to as Fengjia Shopping Town or Wenhua Night Market. It covers areas such as Feng Chia Night Market, Bento Street, and others.

world knowledge.Name: Kyōto Station
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kyōto Station first opened in 1877 and has undergone several reconstructions, including in 1914, 1952, and the current structure in 1997. It has served as a major transportation hub and witnessed significant historical events, including imperial motorcades during World War II and a tragic crush incident in 1934.

Major_Events.Description: The first Kyoto Station opened for service by decree of Emperor Meiji.
77 people were crushed to death when a few thousand gathered to bid farewell to naval recruits.
The 1914 Renaissance-inspired station burned to the ground.
The current Kyoto Station, designed by architect Hiroshi Hara, opened to commemorate Kyoto's 1,200th anniversary.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current station exhibits many characteristics of futurism, with a slightly irregular cubic façade of plate glass over a steel frame. It is 70 meters high and 470 meters from east to west, with a total floor area of 238,000 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kyōto Station is a symbol of modernity in a city known for its cultural heritage. Its completion spurred high-rise developments in Kyoto and it serves as a major transportation hub, connecting various regions of Japan.
world knowledge.Details: Kyōto Station is Japan's second-largest station building and one of the country's largest buildings, incorporating a shopping mall, hotel, movie theater, Isetan department store, and several local government facilities under one 15-story roof. It is served by JR West, JR Central, Kintetsu Railway, and Kyoto Municipal Subway. The station has been featured in films such as 'Gamera 3: Revenge of Iris' and 'Lost in Translation'.

world knowledge.Name: Nonthaburi Pier
world knowledge.Address: Tambon Suan Yai, Amphoe Mueang Nonthaburi, Nonthaburi Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nonthaburi Pier, also known as Nonthaburi Pier (Pibul 3), is a historic pier on the Chao Phraya River. It is considered one of the main piers of Nonthaburi, alongside Pak Kret Pier. The pier is located next to the Nonthaburi Clock Tower and the Old Nonthaburi City Hall, a teak building from the reign of King Rama VI, which now serves as a provincial museum and is registered as an ancient monument by the Fine Arts Department.

Major_Events.Description: The annual King’s Cup regatta takes place around the mid-year at the Chao Phraya River, near Nonthaburi Pier.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pier is adjacent to the Old Nonthaburi City Hall, a teak antique building from the reign of King Rama VI.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nonthaburi Pier is a significant transportation hub and a historic site, reflecting the cultural and historical heritage of Nonthaburi Province. The adjacent Old Nonthaburi City Hall, now a museum, adds to its cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Nonthaburi Pier is the last stop for all boats of the Chao Phraya Express Boat (except the green flag boat). It also offers a cross-river ferry service to Bang Si Mueang. The area around the pier features restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries, banks, clothes shops, and a market, and serves as a terminal for many bus routes.

world knowledge.Name: Codrington College
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Codrington College is an Anglican theological college founded in 1745 with the bequest of Christopher Codrington. It is one of the oldest Anglican theological colleges in the Americas. The college was initially funded by profits from sugar cane estates and slave labor. It has undergone several periods of closure and reconstruction due to hurricanes and economic downturns. It was affiliated with the University of Durham from 1875 to 1965 and is now affiliated with the University of the West Indies at Cave Hill.

Major_Events.Description: Codrington College was founded with the bequest of Christopher Codrington, who left his sugar cane estates and land to the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts to establish a religious college in Barbados.
A hurricane severely damaged the college, leading to its closure until 1797.
The college was almost completely destroyed by a hurricane but was subsequently rebuilt.
A fire gutted the college.
Codrington College entered into an affiliation with Durham University, allowing graduates to receive Durham degrees in classics or theology.

Major_Events.Event: Affiliation with University of the West Indies
Major_Events.Description: Codrington College became affiliated with the University of the West Indies at Cave Hill.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original building was designed by Colonel Christian Lilly in 1713, modeled after a University of Oxford college. The main building is constructed of coral stone and features a central portico with a pediment and three high arches. The chapel has a vaulted ceiling and is paneled with ebony, lignum vitae, and cordia wood. The campus includes the Principal's Lodge, which was originally the Consett plantation great house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Codrington College is one of the oldest Anglican theological colleges in the Americas and has played a significant role in the religious and educational history of Barbados and the Caribbean. Its founding was unique in its intention to benefit the Afro-Caribbean population, although it was initially funded by slave labor.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theological education and training for Anglican priests
world knowledge.Details: Codrington College offers undergraduate and graduate programs in theology, including a Licentiate in Theology, Bachelor of Arts in Theology, and advanced degrees such as Master of Philosophy and Doctor of Philosophy in theology. The college also maintains archives related to the churches of the West Indies. The governance of the college and the Codrington Estates was transferred to local control in 1976, with the establishment of the Codrington Trust.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Phia Wat
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Phia Wat is a Buddhist wat located in Muang Khoun, the former capital of Muang Phuan in the 14th century. It was constructed in 1322 by Chao Lan Kham Khong to house the first Buddhist statue in Xiangkhouang, brought from Burma. The wat was destroyed by invading Chinese forces in 1375, rebuilt, destroyed again during the First Indochina War in 1953, and rebuilt in 1954. It was bombed by the US airforce during the Second Indochina War, leading to its collapse, but the Buddha statue survived with significant damage. A new temple was constructed after the war.

Major_Events.Description: Invading Chinese forces destroyed the complex and cut off the arm of the Buddha statue.
Wat Phia Wat was destroyed during the First Indochina War.
Wat Phia Wat was rebuilt after its destruction in 1953.
Wat Phia Wat was bombed by the US airforce, leading to its collapse.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Phia Wat is culturally and historically important as it housed the first Buddhist statue in Xiangkhouang and has survived multiple destructions and reconstructions, symbolizing resilience and the enduring presence of Buddhism in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The Buddha statue at Wat Phia Wat survived significant damage from multiple wars and is a key artifact in the temple's history.

world knowledge.Name: White Cliffs of Dover
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The White Cliffs of Dover are a region of English coastline facing the Strait of Dover and France. They are composed of chalk with streaks of black flint, deposited during the Late Cretaceous. The cliffs have great symbolic value in Britain, forming a symbolic guard against invasions from continental Europe. They have been a celebrated UK landmark and have featured on commemorative postage stamps.

Major_Events.Description: A section of coastline encompassing the cliffs was purchased by the National Trust.
A large chunk of the cliff edge, as large as a football pitch, fell into the Channel.
Further large sections collapsed on 15 March 2012.
Further large sections collapsed on 4 February 2020.
Further large sections collapsed on 3 February 2021.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cliffs are composed of chalk with streaks of black flint, deposited during the Late Cretaceous. The chalk face shows horizontal bands of dark-coloured flint, composed of the remains of sea sponges and siliceous planktonic micro-organisms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The White Cliffs of Dover have great symbolic value in Britain, forming a symbolic guard against invasions from continental Europe. They are a celebrated UK landmark and have featured on commemorative postage stamps. During World War II, they were a welcoming sight for allied troops during the Dunkirk evacuation.
world knowledge.Details: The cliffs are part of the Dover to Kingsdown Cliffs Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation. They are home to a variety of wildlife, including migratory birds, butterflies, and rare plants. The National Trust manages the area, working to preserve its natural and historical significance.

world knowledge.Name: Gourock Outdoor Pool
world knowledge.Location: Albert Road, Gourock, Inverclyde, Scotland, PA19 1NQ
world knowledge.Address: Albert Road, Gourock, Inverclyde, Scotland, PA19 1NQ
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 33.3 metres (109 ft), Width: 15 metres (49 ft), Depth: 3.5 metres (11 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gourock Outdoor Pool is the oldest heated swimming pool in Scotland, opened in 1909. It uses salt water from the Firth of Clyde, heated and maintained at a minimum temperature of 29 °C (84 °F). The pool underwent a major improvement project from 2010 to 2011, which included replacing the changing accommodation with a modern leisure centre.

Major_Events.Description: The pool was closed for a major improvement project, which included replacing the changing accommodation with a modern leisure centre, incorporating an enlarged gymnasium and lift access.
A 2004 photograph of the pool by Martin Parr was used as the album cover for The Ballad of Darren by rock band Blur.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pool is a salt water public lido with a modern leisure centre, including upgraded changing facilities, a gymnasium, and lift access.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gourock Outdoor Pool is culturally significant as the oldest heated swimming pool in Scotland and for its use in popular culture, such as being featured on the album cover of The Ballad of Darren by Blur.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public swimming pool and leisure facility
world knowledge.Details: The pool is heated and uses salt water taken from the Firth of Clyde. It opens from May to the first week in September and is managed by Inverclyde Leisure Trust.

world knowledge.Name: Plaza Miranda
world knowledge.Location: Quezon Boulevard and Hidalgo Street, Quiapo, Manila, Philippines
world knowledge.Address: Quezon Boulevard, Hidalgo Street and Evangelista Street, Quiapo, Manila, Philippines
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Plaza Miranda is a public square in Quiapo, Manila, inaugurated in its current form by Mayor Arsenio Lacson in 1961. It is named after José Sandino y Miranda, the Philippines' Secretary of the Treasury between 1833 and 1854. The plaza has been a center of Philippine political discourse and was the site of the 1971 Plaza Miranda bombing. It underwent a ₱49 million renovation in 2000 and now serves as a freedom park.

Major_Events.Description: Two grenades were launched at a political rally of the Liberal Party, killing nine people.
A rally led by Sen. Jose W. Diokno where 50,000 people protested the impending martial law declaration of the Marcos dictatorship.
The plaza underwent a ₱49 million renovation, giving it a more modern design and adding new architectural elements.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The plaza is paved with granite tiles and surrounded by Neo-Gothic architectural details inspired by the Quiapo Church's architecture. It features two grand entrance arches bearing the coat of arms of Manila, a larger grand arch at the south side, and several historical markers and monuments.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Plaza Miranda is a significant site for political discourse and protests in the Philippines. It is also known for its association with fortune-telling and the sale of lucky charms, as well as its historical events and architectural elements.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Freedom park for assemblies and protests
world knowledge.Details: The plaza is lit at night by floodlights and has a sound system controlled from a control room in the Lacson Underpass. Notable buildings around the plaza include the F&C Tower, the Times Theater, and the Plaza Miranda branch of Mercury Drug. The area around R. Hidalgo Street is known as the 'photographers' haven' due to the presence of photography-related shops.

world knowledge.Name: Kakira Sugar Works
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kakira Sugar Works Limited, often called Kakira Sugar Works, is a leading sugar manufacturer in Uganda, the third-largest economy in the East African Community. The main factories of the company are located in the town of Kakira, in Jinja District, Eastern Uganda. This location lies approximately 16 kilometres (9.9 mi), by road, northeast of Jinja, the nearest large town. Kakira is located approximately 100 kilometres (62 mi), by road, east of Kampala, the capital of Uganda and the largest city in that country. The coordinates of the main factory are:0°30'36.0"N, 33°17'24.0"E (Latitude:0.5100; Longitude:33.2900). In addition to the factories in Kakira, the company maintains a corporate office along 5th Street, in Bugoloobi, in Kampala Industrial Area, and offices and warehouses, in Kakira, Jinja and Kampala. Kakira Sugar Works is the largest manufacturer of sugar in Uganda, producing an estimated 165,000 metric tonnes of sugar annually, accounting for about 47 percent of the national output in 2011. Kinyara Sugar Works in  Masindi District is Uganda's second-largest sugar manufacturer, accounting for about 31% of annual national output. Sugar Corporation of Uganda Limited (SCOUL), in Buikwe District, accounts for about 17% of national production. The remaining 5% (about 15,000 metric tonnes annually), is produced by Sango Bay Estates Limited, in Sango Bay, Kyotera District. The sugar produced by the companies is marketed to the Eastern African countries of South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda. Kakira Sugar Works is the flagship business of the Madhvani Group of Companies, the largest conglomerate in Uganda, accounting for over 10% of the gross domestic product (GDP) of Uganda in 2010. Kakira Sugar Works possesses its own social infrastructure : free schools for employees' children, roads, hospitals, staff housing. In 1920, the Vithaldas Haridas & Company, under the management of Muljibhai Madhvani, a twenty-six-year-old Indian-born Ugandan businessman, entrepreneur, industrialist and philanthropist, purchased 800 acres (3.2 km2) of land, in Kakira, between Jinja and Iganga, for the purpose of starting a sugar factory. Muljibhai later became the managing director of Vithaldas Haridas & Company. That sugar complex, later renamed Kakira Sugar Works, opened in 1930. By adding to the original parcel of land, through purchases, the company land holdings at Kakira, were in excess of 9,500 hectares (37 sq mi), as of April 2009. The sugar manufacturing complex at Kakira employs over 7,500 people, according to the company website. In 1987, Kakira Sugar Works went through a $59.38 million rehabilitation program funded by the World Bank and the African Development Bank. In 2000, the Madhvani group acquired 100% of Kakira Sugar Works' shares. Kakira Sugar Works is a (100%) subsidiary of the Madhvani Group, based in Kakira, Uganda. The Group's shareholding is private and is not widely, publicly known. As of November 2013[update], Kakira Sugar Works Limited had gone through a USh 191 billion (about US$75 million) factory expansion and upgrade. USh 76.5 billion (about US$30 million), was raised through a 10-year corporate bond on the Uganda Securities Exchange, and the remainder was sourced from local banks. This upgrade boosted the factory's sugarcane crushing capacity to 7,500 tonnes per day. The co-generation capacity of Kakira Power Station, was also increased from 22 Megawatts to 52 Megawatts. In November 2016, Kakira Sugar Works started production of industrial-grade ethanol, distilled from molasses, produced as a by-product of sugar manufacturing. The ethanol distillery, was constructed by Praj Industries of India, at a cost of USh 133 billion (US$36.6 million). The distillery is expected to process the 74,000 metric tonnes of molasses that the sugar mill produces annually, into 20,000,000 litres (4,399,385 imp gal; 5,283,441 US gal) of "fuel grade anhydrous ethanol".

Major_Events.Description: Kakira Sugar Works went through a $59.38 million rehabilitation program funded by the World Bank and the African Development Bank.
The Madhvani group acquired 100% of Kakira Sugar Works' shares.

Kakira Sugar Works Limited had gone through a USh 191 billion (about US$75 million) factory expansion and upgrade. USh 76.5 billion (about US$30 million), was raised through a 10-year corporate bond on the Uganda Securities Exchange, and the remainder was sourced from local banks. This upgrade boosted the factory's sugarcane crushing capacity to 7,500 tonnes per day. The co-generation capacity of Kakira Power Station, was also increased from 22 Megawatts to 52 Megawatts.

Kakira Sugar Works started production of industrial-grade ethanol, distilled from molasses, produced as a by-product of sugar manufacturing. The ethanol distillery, was constructed by Praj Industries of India, at a cost of USh 133 billion (US$36.6 million). The distillery is expected to process the 74,000 metric tonnes of molasses that the sugar mill produces annually, into 20,000,000 litres (4,399,385 imp gal; 5,283,441 US gal) of "fuel grade anhydrous ethanol".

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main factories of the company are located in the town of Kakira, in Jinja District, Eastern Uganda. The sugar manufacturing complex at Kakira employs over 7,500 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kakira Sugar Works is the flagship business of the Madhvani Group of Companies, the largest conglomerate in Uganda, accounting for over 10% of the gross domestic product (GDP) of Uganda in 2010. It possesses its own social infrastructure : free schools for employees' children, roads, hospitals, staff housing.
world knowledge.Details: Kakira Sugar Works is the largest manufacturer of sugar in Uganda, producing an estimated 165,000 metric tonnes of sugar annually, accounting for about 47 percent of the national output in 2011. The sugar produced by the companies is marketed to the Eastern African countries of South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.

world knowledge.Name: Paradise Cave
world knowledge.Address: Gmina Chęciny, powiat kielecki, województwo świętokrzyskie, Poland
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 240 m (790 ft), Depth: 8 to 17.5 m (26 to 57 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Paradise Cave is a horizontal karstic limestone cave located inside the Malik hill, to the south of Kielce. Discovered in 1963 by Józef Kopeć and Feliks Wawrzeńczak, it was opened to the public in 1972 after extensive research. The limestones date from the Middle Devonian epoch, approximately 350 million years ago. The cave has traces of Neanderthal occupancy from the late Pleistocene, 50 to 60 thousand years ago.

Major_Events.Description: Discovered by Józef Kopeć and Feliks Wawrzeńczak, students of a local technical school.
After extensive research and documentation by geologists Tymoteusz Wróblewski and Zbigniew Rubinowski, the cave was opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cave features corridors leading through five chambers and caverns, ornamented with speleothems such as stalactites, stalagmites, and columns of calcified rock deposited over tens of thousands of years.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Regarded as one of Poland's most beautiful caves, it attracts numerous visitors due to its historical value and ecological integrity. It also contains significant archeological and paleontological discoveries, including traces of Neanderthal occupancy and fossilized bones of Paleolithic fauna.
world knowledge.Details: The cave maintains an internal temperature of 8 to 10 °C (46 to 50 °F; 281 to 283 K) and 95 percent humidity to preserve its historical value and ecological integrity. A maximum of fifteen people accompanied by a guide are admitted every fifteen minutes. An info center in front of the entrance exhibits archeological and paleontological discoveries, including a replica of a Neanderthal camp and Mousterian assemblages.

world knowledge.Name: Castello Monforte
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castello Monforte is a castle and defensive complex in Campobasso, Italy. Its origin is disputed, with some sources dating it to 1459, built for Count Nicola II dei Monforte-Gambatesa, while others suggest it dates back to Norman times. After damage from the 1456 earthquake, it was refurbished by Cola Monforte. The castle was abandoned in the 17th century, used as a temporary cemetery in the 19th century, and bought by the city of Campobasso in 1861.

Major_Events.Description: The castle suffered damage and was subsequently refurbished by Cola Monforte.
The castle was abandoned and began to deteriorate.
The castle was used as a temporary cemetery.
The castle was bought by the city of Campobasso.
The Italian Order of Architects criticized the city of Campobasso for not involving them directly in the redevelopment project.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Castello Monforte is a significant historical and defensive complex in Campobasso, reflecting the region's medieval history and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The complex houses the Campobasso Monforte meteorological station and the Chiesa di Santa Maria Maggiore.

world knowledge.Name: Maqam Echahid
world knowledge.Address: Heights of Algiers, municipality of El Madania, west of the Bois des arcades, east of Diar el Mahçoul, north of the plaza shopping center Riadh El Feth
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height of 92 metres (302 ft), turret diameter of 10 metres (33 ft), turret height of 7.6 metres (25 ft), dome height of 6 metres (20 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Maqam Echahid, also known as the Martyr's Memorial, is a concrete monument commemorating the Algerian War. It was opened on July 5th, 1982, on the 20th anniversary of Algeria's independence. The monument, shaped like three standing palm leaves, shelters the 'Eternal Flame' and features statues of soldiers representing stages of Algeria's struggle for independence. It was erected on the site of an ancient military fort.

Major_Events.Description: The monument was inaugurated by President Chadli Bendjedid in February 1986.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument consists of three stylized fins that join mid-height, built by the Canadian company Lavalin. It features an Islamic style turret with a dome, resting on an esplanade that burns an 'eternal flame'. The structure includes a crypt, an amphitheater, and the National Museum of El Mujahid (underground).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Maqam Echahid is a symbol of Algeria's struggle for independence and honors the martyrs of the Algerian War. It is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Algeria.
world knowledge.Details: The project to build the memorial was initiated by President Houari Boumedienne and completed under President Chadli Bendjedid. The construction was a technological challenge due to the site's location on a steep cliff and the high seismicity of the region. The monument was designed by Bashir Yelles and Marian Konieczny, with contributions from other Algerian artists and engineers.

world knowledge.Name: Flatford Mill
world knowledge.Address: Flatford, East Bergholt, Suffolk, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Flatford Mill is a Grade I listed watermill on the River Stour at Flatford in East Bergholt, Suffolk, England. According to the date-stone the mill was built in 1733, but some of the structure may be earlier. Attached to the mill is a 17th-century miller's cottage which is also Grade I listed. The property is in Dedham Vale, a typically English rural landscape. The mill was owned by the artist John Constable's father and is noted, along with its immediate surroundings as the location for many of Constable's works. It is referred to in the title of one of his most iconic paintings, Flatford Mill (Scene on a Navigable River), and mentioned in the title or is the subject of several others including: Flatford Mill from a lock on the river Stour; Flatford Mill from the lock (A water mill); The Lock. The Hay Wain, which features Willy Lott's Cottage, was painted from the front of the mill. The mill was listed in 1955. It is owned by the National Trust which leases it to the Field Studies Council who have run it as a field centre since 1943. The National Trust also owns nearby properties, Bridge Cottage, Valley Farm and Willy Lott's Cottage.

Major_Events.Description: Flatford Mill was officially listed as a Grade I building, recognizing its historical and architectural significance.
The National Trust leased Flatford Mill to the Field Studies Council, which has operated it as a field centre since then.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beam architectural style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Flatford Mill is culturally significant as it was owned by the father of the famous artist John Constable and served as the location for many of his iconic paintings, including 'Flatford Mill (Scene on a Navigable River)' and 'The Hay Wain'.
world knowledge.Details: The mill is located in Dedham Vale, a typically English rural landscape. It is part of a group of properties owned by the National Trust, including Bridge Cottage, Valley Farm, and Willy Lott's Cottage.

world knowledge.Name: Kilmainham Gaol
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Cells were roughly 28 square metres in area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kilmainham Gaol is a former prison in Kilmainham, Dublin, now a museum run by the Office of Public Works. Many Irish revolutionaries, including the leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising, were imprisoned and executed here by the UK Government. It was originally called the 'New Gaol' and was intended to replace an older prison. It was officially named the County of Dublin Gaol and was run by the Grand Jury for County Dublin.

Major_Events.Description: Leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were imprisoned and executed here by the UK Government.
97 women went on hunger strike in Kilmainham Gaol after all of their privileges had been denied without explanation.
Kilmainham Gaol was decommissioned as a prison by the Irish Free State government.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration and opening as a museum
Major_Events.Description: The prison was restored and opened to the public as a museum on 10 April 1966.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The prison features Victorian architecture with cells roughly 28 square metres in area. A small hanging cell was built in 1891, located on the first floor between the west and east wings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kilmainham Gaol is culturally and historically significant as a site of oppression and suffering, and as a monument to the struggle for Irish national independence. It housed many Irish revolutionaries and was a key location during the 1916 Easter Rising and the Irish War of Independence.
world knowledge.Details: Kilmainham Gaol is one of the biggest unoccupied prisons in Europe. It now houses a museum on the history of Irish nationalism and offers guided tours. The prison has been used as a filming location for various TV series and music videos, including the U2 song 'A Celebration' and the AMC series 'Into the Badlands'.

world knowledge.Name: Giants' grave
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Giants' grave is a type of Sardinian megalithic gallery grave built during the Bronze Age by the Nuragic civilization. They were collective tombs and can be found throughout Sardinia, with 800 being discovered there.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: There are two general types of giants' tomb. In the so-called 'slab type', uncut slabs are buried on end in the ground, and are arranged side-by-side. There is usually a central stele, which is the largest slab (up to 4 m in height) and has a doorway cut through it. The sepulchres have a characteristic rectangular plan with an apse. The burial chamber is usually 5 to 15 metres long and 1 to 2 metres high. The structures were originally covered by a mound resembling the shape of an overturned ship. Near the entrance an obelisk (betile in Sardinian) is usually found, which symbolizes the gods or ancestors who watched over the dead. The so-called 'block type' tombs are made of rectangular-cut blocks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Giants' graves are culturally and historically important as they represent the burial practices and architectural skills of the Nuragic civilization during the Bronze Age. They also symbolize the gods or ancestors who watched over the dead.
world knowledge.Details: There are also structures similar to the block-type giants tombs on the island of Malta, in the United Kingdom and in Menorca (naveta).

world knowledge.Name: Pillory of Bragança
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pillory of Bragança is a 15th-century sculpted stone column with symbolic political, administrative, and judicial significance. It was erected over a four-step octagonal platform and is located in the civil parish of Sé, Santa Maria e Meixedo, municipality of Bragança. The column is classified as a National Monument since 1910.

Major_Events.Description: D. Sancho I conceded the municipality's foral, ordering the reconstruction of the pillory while promoting the region's growth.
Afonso II confirmed the municipal charter established by his predecessor, which was later extended by D. Afonso III on 20 May 1253.

Major_Events.Event: First fair conceded to the region
Major_Events.Description: For a period of 16 days, allowing merchants and vendors to sell goods at the site.
Bragança's growth was progressive and cumulative, finally resulting in its reclassification as a city by Afonso V.
D. Manuel ordered that the dismembered body parts of sentenced peasants be moved to another area of the town due to the nuisance caused by their exhibition on the pillory.
D. Manuel ordered the construction of a new pillory when he conceded its inhabitants the privilege of not suffering the pillory for delinquency in the village.

Major_Events.Event: Pillory moved to Praça de Santiago
Major_Events.Description: The pillory was removed from its old square and moved to the Praça de Santiago.
Bragança was divided into two: the older quarter became the town of Bragança, while the other evolved into the city of Bragança.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pillory consists of a cylindrical column erected over a square platform, sculpted with zoomorphic symbols, anthropomorphic scenes, and the shield of the city of Bragança. Its structural design and sculptural ornamentation are characteristic of the Manueline era. The base resembles a proto-historic, Lusitanian bore carved in a rough, stocky appearance, with short legs. The main shaft is crossed by four arms sculpted in zoomorphic images, where rings were fixed to hold the prisoners, still preserving their holes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pillory of Bragança is culturally and historically important as a symbol of political, administrative, and judicial authority. It represents the region's growth and the socio-judicial institutions established by the House of Bragança. It is also a unique example of Manueline architecture and a National Monument since 1910.
world knowledge.Details: The pillory is located within an isolated area of the urbanized area of Sé, Santa Maria e Meixedo, in a square within the Castle of Bragança, near the keep tower, occupying an area where the old Church of São Pedro was located, opposite an area of village homes.

world knowledge.Name: Baraha Kshetra
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Barahachhetra is one of Nepal's oldest shrines mentioned in Puranas including Brahma Purana, Varaha Purana and Skanda Purana and even mentioned and glorified in the Mahabharata epic. The temple was rebuilt by Juddha Shamsher in 1991 BS after being demolished by the earthquake of 1990 BS.

Major_Events.Description: A semi-Kumbha Mela has been organizing since 2058 B.S. in Chataradham, Sunsari. The second event was held in 2070 B.S. for the duration of a month. More than 600,000 people visited for Kumbha Asnan in the Koshi in the year 2070.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features a dome structure with 9 monuments including those of Laxmi, Panchayan, Guruvarah, Suryavarah, Kokawarah, and Nageshwar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Barahachhetra is a significant Hindu and Kirat pilgrimage site, one of the Char Dham in Nepal. It is associated with the Varaha incarnation of Vishnu and hosts major festivals like Prabodhini Ekadashi to Kartik Purnima and Maghe Sankranti.
world knowledge.Details: Pilgrims visit throughout the year, with special festivities during Kartik Purnima and Makar Sankranti. The site is also known for its ancient statues, some over 1500 years old.

world knowledge.Name: Bagnell Dam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bagnell Dam impounds the Osage River in Missouri, creating the Lake of the Ozarks. It was built by the Union Electric Company (now Ameren) to generate hydroelectric power. Construction started in 1929 and was completed in 1931, providing jobs during the Great Depression. The dam was a significant engineering feat at the time, creating one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.

Major_Events.Description: Construction on Bagnell Dam started, providing jobs during the Great Depression.
Bagnell Dam was completed, creating the Lake of the Ozarks.
Bagnell Dam was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
A major structural project added 66 million pounds of concrete to the dam's structure.
The bridge underwent a rehabilitation project, reopening in April 2022.
The dam's floodgates were completely open in response to the 2019 Midwestern U.S. floods.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Concrete gravity dam, 148 feet (45 m) tall, 2,543 feet (775 m) long, including a 520-foot (160 m) spillway and a 511-foot (156 m) power station. Features 12 floodgates and a walled-off thirteenth spillway opening.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bagnell Dam is a historic engineering marvel that created the Lake of the Ozarks, one of the largest man-made lakes in the world. It provided economic benefits during the Great Depression and remains a key hydroelectric power source.
world knowledge.Details: The dam's power station has eight generators with a maximum capacity of 215 megawatts, providing power to 42,000 homes. The Lake of the Ozarks has a surface area of 55,000 acres (22,000 ha) and over 1,150 miles (1,850 km) of shoreline. The dam is owned by Ameren and was designed by Stone & Webster.

world knowledge.Name: Guwenhua Jie
world knowledge.Address: Ancient Culture Street, west bank of the Hai River, Tianjin, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Guwenhua Jie, also known as Tianjin's Ancient Culture Street, is a historic pedestrian pathway complex that preserves the architectural style of the Qing dynasty. It was officially opened on New Year's Day in 1986. The area is classified as a AAAAA scenic area by the China National Tourism Administration. The Niangniang Palace, a temple to the sea-goddess Mazu, is located at its center and was first constructed in 1326 under the Yuan Dynasty.

Major_Events.Description: Tianjin Ancient Culture Street was opened on New Year's Day in 1986.
An ancient government road from the Ming Dynasty was found, though large-scale excavation was not conducted due to architectural constraints.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex features Qing dynasty architecture. The Niangniang Palace includes structures like the Opera Tower, Flag Pole, Temple Gate, Memorial Archway, Front Hall, Main Hall, Canon-Storing Pavilion, Qisheng Temple, Bell-Drum Tower, Side Hall, and Zhangxian Pavilion. The Main Hall is built on a high platform, typical of mid- to late-Ming Dynasty wooden structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The landmark is one of the three major surviving Mazu temples in China and one of the oldest. It serves as a center for marine sacrifice and cultural rituals, including celebrations for the sea-goddess Mazu's birthday. The area is also significant for its historical and architectural preservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural and religious site, tourism, and historical preservation.
world knowledge.Details: The Niangniang Palace is a key feature, dedicated to the sea-goddess Mazu. The Yuhuangge Taoist Temple, built in 1368, is one of the oldest buildings in Tianjin. Experts have suggested restoring the historical Zhili Public Welfare Services museum within the temple to form the 'Yuhuangge Historical Museum.' The area hosts annual folk flower fairs to commemorate Mazu's birthday on the 23rd day of the third lunar month.

world knowledge.Name: Anandpur Sahib
world knowledge.Address: Anandpur Sahib, Rupnagar, Punjab, India, PIN: 140118
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Anandpur Sahib, founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur in 1665, is one of the most sacred religious places in Sikhism. It is where the last two Sikh Gurus, Guru Tegh Bahadur and Guru Gobind Singh, lived. Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa Panth here in 1699. The city has been a significant pilgrimage site and the venue of the annual Hola Mohalla festival.

Major_Events.Description: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa Panth on the day of the Vaisakhi festival in 1699 after an elaborate ceremony, which included baptizing the Panj Pyaras.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was tortured and beheaded for refusing to convert to Islam under the orders of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
The 300th anniversary of the founding of the Khalsa was celebrated at Anandpur Sahib.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The city features several Gurdwaras with unique architectural styles, including Takhat Sri Kesgarh Sahib. Historical structures have been reconstructed, often encased in marble, with some original features lost over time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Anandpur Sahib is a central pilgrimage site in Sikhism, marking the birthplace of the Khalsa Panth. It holds immense religious and historical importance for Sikhs worldwide.
world knowledge.Details: Anandpur Sahib is located near the Sutlej River and is known for its annual Hola Mohalla festival, which attracts millions of Sikhs. The city is home to Takhat Sri Kesgarh Sahib, one of the five Takhts in Sikhism. The Virasat-e-Khalsa Museum and the world's tallest khanda at Panj Piara Park are notable landmarks.

world knowledge.Name: Herbert Hoover National Historic Site
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Herbert Hoover National Historic Site commemorates the life of Herbert Hoover, the 31st president of the United States. Hoover spent the first eleven years of his life in West Branch, Iowa. The site includes his birthplace cottage, a blacksmith shop similar to his father's, the first West Branch schoolhouse, and the Quaker meetinghouse where his family worshiped. The site was established in 1965 and includes the Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum.

Major_Events.Description: The site was established as a unit of the National Park System to commemorate Herbert Hoover's life.

Major_Events.Event: Dedication of Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum
Major_Events.Description: The library and museum were opened on Hoover's 88th birthday, dedicated by Harry Truman.
The site's boundary was expanded to include additional acreage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site features several historic buildings, including Hoover's birthplace cottage (a two-room board and batten timber structure), a reconstructed blacksmith shop, an 1853 schoolhouse, and a Quaker meetinghouse. The buildings reflect the modest, rural architecture of late 19th-century Iowa.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The site preserves the early生活环境 of Herbert Hoover, showcasing his humble beginnings and the values that shaped his life. It also serves as a memorial to his presidency and humanitarian work, including his efforts during World War I and World War II.
world knowledge.Details: The site includes a tallgrass prairie, designated as a National Recreation Trail in 1981, and the graves of Herbert Hoover and his wife, Lou Henry Hoover. The Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum, located on the site, houses Hoover's presidential papers and memorabilia. The site also features a statue of the Egyptian deity Isis, a gift from the people of Belgium in gratitude for Hoover's famine relief efforts.

world knowledge.Name: Global village
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The term 'global village' was coined by Canadian media theorist Marshall McLuhan in the 1960s. It describes the phenomenon of the world becoming more interconnected due to the propagation of media technologies. McLuhan's concept was based on the understanding of people moving towards involving personal interactions worldwide and the consequences that ensue simultaneously with their causes. The term signifies all parts of the world being brought together by the internet and other electronic communication interconnections.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The global village is culturally significant as it represents the interconnectedness of the world through media and technology. It has implications for forming new socially meaningful structures within the context of culture, impacting human relations, and fostering international density. The concept has led to increased awareness of global responsibilities and the ability for individuals to interact with others from various social groups and countries around the world.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary function of the global village is to facilitate interconnectedness and communication across the world through media and technology.
world knowledge.Details: The global village framework involves individuals transcending the micro-, meso- and macro-dynamics of their life on a daily basis, getting involved in complex communities of networks stretching worldwide. Electronic media have the ability to impact individuals differently based on various factors such as religion, politics, beliefs, and business. The concept has expanded the ability to create and view media texts, and it has called for the westernisation of the world. McLuhan argued that the global village ensures maximal disagreement on all points, creating more discontinuity, division, and diversity.

world knowledge.Name: Ngwenya Mine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ngwenya Mine is considered the world's oldest mine, with mining activities dating back 41,000 to 43,000 years. It was initially used by Early Man for extracting red ochre, and later for iron smelting and iron ore export. The mine played a significant role in the economic development of the region during the 1960s and 1970s. It was operated by the Swaziland Iron Ore Development Company (SIODC) and later by Salgaocar Swaziland Limited until 2014. The site has faced environmental issues and corruption scandals related to mining activities.

Major_Events.Description: The Swaziland Iron Ore Development Company (SIODC) started mining operations, leading to economic development in the area.
The visitor center, donated by the Republic of China in Taiwan, opened to the public.
Salgaocar Swaziland Limited ceased mining activities due to environmental and financial issues.
The visitor center was destroyed by fire, resulting in the loss of ancient artifacts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mine consists of an ancient site called the Lion Cavern and a modern-operations mine that is now flooded. The visitor center, which no longer exists, housed ancient tools and artifacts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ngwenya Mine is culturally significant as the oldest known mine in the world. It was used by Early Man for red ochre extraction and later by Bantu tribes for iron smelting. The site is also associated with the history of rock paintings and iron trade in Africa.
world knowledge.Details: The mine was submitted to UNESCO's list of World Heritage Sites in 2008 but was not accepted. It has faced environmental pollution, corruption scandals, and the destruction of its visitor center in 2018. Plans to revive mining activities have been announced but remain uncertain.

world knowledge.Name: Vitosha Boulevard
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vitosha Boulevard, originally an unadjusted street during the Ottoman rule, was named Vitoshka ulitsa after Bulgaria's Liberation in 1883. Initially built with low one-storey houses, it transformed into a major trade street during the Interwar period with the construction of massive public buildings. It has undergone several renovations, including in 2007 and 2015, to restore its historical style and enhance its pedestrian zones.

Major_Events.Description: A renovation aimed to restore the style of 1930s Sofia, adding historical benches, street lights, Art Nouveau kiosks, green areas, fountains, open-air bars, and a clock tower at St Nedelya Church.
Reconstruction works on the boulevard started.
Another renovation completed the entirely pedestrian zone of the boulevard between Patriarch Evtimiy Blvd. and Alabin Str.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The boulevard features a mix of historical and modern architectural styles, with Art Nouveau kiosks, historical benches, and street lights. The area includes significant buildings like the National Palace of Culture and the Palace of the Courts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vitosha Boulevard is the main commercial street in Sofia, known for its high-end fashion outlets, restaurants, and bars. It is a popular meeting place and a symbol of Sofia's urban development and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The boulevard is named after Vitosha, the mountain near Sofia. It was ranked the world's 22nd most expensive trade street in a 2007 study by Cushman & Wakefield, Inc. The pedestrian part of the boulevard is served by several metro and tram lines.

world knowledge.Name: Cliffs of Moher
world knowledge.Area: Southwestern edge of the Burren region
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 14 kilometres (9 miles) long, up to 214 metres (702 ft) high
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Formed between 313 and 326 million years ago
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cliffs of Moher are sea cliffs in County Clare, Ireland, named after an old promontory fort called Mothar or Moher. They have been a significant tourist destination and are part of the Burren and Cliffs of Moher Geopark, recognized by UNESCO.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Sir Cornelius O'Brien, a round stone tower near the midpoint of the cliffs.
The fort was demolished to provide material for a lookout/telegraph tower during the Napoleonic wars.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Cliffs of Moher Visitor Experience
Major_Events.Description: A modern visitor centre built into a hillside, featuring interactive media displays and environmentally sensitive design.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cliffs consist mainly of beds of Namurian shale and sandstone, with various coastal landforms such as sea caves, sea stacks, and sea stumps.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cliffs of Moher are one of the most popular tourist destinations in Ireland, recognized by UNESCO, and a signature point on the Wild Atlantic Way tourist trail.
world knowledge.Details: The Cliffs of Moher have appeared in numerous films and music videos, and they are an Important Bird Area with a diverse range of wildlife. The site is accessible via Bus Éireann route 350 and a privately operated shuttle bus from Doolin.

world knowledge.Name: Devil's Bit
world knowledge.Address: North-west of Templemore, County Tipperary, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Devil's Bit, historically called Sliabh Aildiúin and Bearnán Éile, is a mountain in County Tipperary, Ireland. According to legend, the devil took a bite out of the mountain, creating a gap and spitting out the Rock of Cashel. It was historically significant during the Lughnasa festival. The Book of Dimma, an illuminated manuscript, was supposedly discovered in a cave on the mountain in 1789. The mountain was also the site of a mass anti-tithe meeting in 1832.

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of the Book of Dimma
Major_Events.Description: An illuminated manuscript copy of the four Gospels, written in the 8th century, was supposedly discovered in a cave on the mountain.
A meeting part of a wider campaign against the payment of tithes to the Church of Ireland by the majority Catholic population.
A cross was erected on the Rock in celebration of the Marian Year dedicated by the Roman Catholic Church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mountain features a notable gap in its contour, known as the Devil's Bit. A cross, erected in 1953-1954, stands 45 feet high with a span of 25 feet. The base of the cross is 340 tons and 5 feet squared, 10 feet deep. A statue of the Virgin Mary was erected in 1988 on the eastern side of the Rock.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mountain is culturally significant due to its association with local legends, historical events like the anti-tithe meeting, and its role in the Lughnasa festival. The discovery of the Book of Dimma adds to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The mountain offers expansive views of the surrounding countryside, with claims that nine counties can be viewed from the summit. There is a military firing range on the western slopes. The tower on the approach to the summit is known as Carden's Folly, built by the Carden family, who were prominent landlords in the area.

world knowledge.Name: Angel of Independence
world knowledge.Address: Paseo de la Reforma, Downtown Mexico City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Angel of Independence, officially known as Monumento a la Independencia, was built in 1910 during the presidency of Porfirio Díaz to commemorate the centennial of the beginning of Mexico's War of Independence. It was designed by architect Antonio Rivas Mercado and later became a mausoleum for the most important heroes of that war. The monument has become a focal point for both celebration and protest.

Major_Events.Description: The monument was inaugurated on September 16, 1910, the 100th anniversary of the Grito de Dolores, the battle cry by Father Miguel Hidalgo that initiated Mexican independence. The ceremony was attended by President Díaz and many foreign dignitaries.

The monument was restored after the sculpture of the Winged Victory fell and broke during an earthquake on July 28, 1957. Sculptor José Fernández Urbina was in charge of the restoration, which lasted more than a year.

Following feminist demonstrations against gender-based violence and feminicides, the monument was affected by acts of vandalism and graffiti. The Government of Mexico City closed access for restoration, which concluded in October 2021.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Angel of Independence is a victory column on a roundabout, resembling the July Column in Paris, Nelson's Column in London, the Victory Column in Berlin, and the Columbus Monument in New York City. The base is quadrangular with bronze sculptures symbolizing law, war, justice, and peace. The column is 36 metres (118 ft) high, made of steel covered with quarried stone, and features a Corinthian-style capital adorned by four eagles. The statue of Nike, the Greek goddess of Victory, crowns the column, made of bronze covered with 24k gold.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Angel of Independence is one of the most recognizable landmarks in Mexico City, symbolizing the nation's independence and serving as a mausoleum for its heroes. It has become a focal point for both celebration and protest, reflecting its deep cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The monument includes a mausoleum for the heroes of the Mexican Independence, an eternal flame honoring these heroes, and a viewpoint above the capital. Visitors may enter the monument, view the memorial plaques, and climb to the top of the tower. The climb is arduous, with about 200 steps, equivalent to a 14-story building. The monument is a traditional gathering place for celebrations and political rallies.

world knowledge.Name: Flatiron Building
world knowledge.Address: 175 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan, New York City, NY 10010
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Flatiron Building, originally the Fuller Building, is a 22-story steel-framed triangular building designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg. It was completed in 1902 and is one of New York City's most iconic skyscrapers. The building's name derives from its triangular shape, resembling a cast-iron clothes iron. It was developed as the headquarters of the Fuller Company and has undergone several ownership changes and renovations over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The Flatiron Building was completed and opened on October 1, 1902, as the headquarters of the Fuller Company.
The Flatiron Building was designated a New York City landmark by the Landmarks Preservation Commission.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The Flatiron Building was designated a National Historic Landmark.
The building's owners announced plans to convert the Flatiron Building into residential condominiums, with completion expected by 2026.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Flatiron Building is a vertical Renaissance palazzo with Beaux-Arts styling. It features a steel frame, glazed terracotta facade, and limestone base. The building's triangular shape is due to its location at the intersection of Fifth Avenue and Broadway. The facade is divided into three sections: a three-story base, a midsection with oriel windows, and a capital with double-height arches. The building's prow is a distinctive feature, with rounded corners and decorative details.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Flatiron Building is a quintessential symbol of New York City and one of the world's most iconic skyscrapers. Its unique triangular shape and prominent location have made it a popular subject for artists, photographers, and filmmakers. The building is also significant for its early use of steel-frame construction and its influence on the development of skyscrapers.
world knowledge.Details: The Flatiron Building has been featured in numerous films, TV shows, and artworks. It was also the subject of a trademark dispute in 1999. The building's wind currents at its base famously caused women's skirts to blow up, leading to the phrase '23 skidoo.' The building is currently undergoing renovation for conversion into residential condominiums, expected to be completed by 2026.
