world knowledge.Name: Grande Poste d'Alger
world knowledge.Address: Boulevard Mohamed-Khemisti, Alger Centre municipality in Algiers, Algeria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Algiers Central Post Office, known as Grande Poste d'Alger, was designed by architects Jules Voinot and Marius Toudoire and constructed in 1910. In 2015, the state converted it into a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The state turned the building into a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Algerian, Neo-Moorish style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a significant historic site and the largest post office building in Algeria, reflecting the architectural and cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a post office, now a museum

world knowledge.Name: Fishbourne Roman Palace
world knowledge.Address: Fishbourne, West Sussex grid reference SU838047, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fishbourne Roman Palace is the largest known Roman residence north of the Alps, built around 75 AD, thirty years after the Roman conquest of Britain. It was a grand palace with formal gardens, mosaics, and extensive architectural features. The palace underwent several alterations before being destroyed by fire around 270 AD. The site was rediscovered in 1805 and extensively excavated in the 1960s, revealing a complex history of pre-Roman and Roman activity.

Major_Events.Description: The full-size palace with four residential wings surrounding a formal courtyard garden was built, incorporating an earlier proto-palace.
The north wing of the palace was completely destroyed in a fire, leading to the abandonment of the site.
The site was accidentally discovered during the construction of a new home, leading to subsequent excavations.
Archeologist Barry Cunliffe led the first major excavations, uncovering significant portions of the palace and its history.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace featured four residential wings surrounding a formal courtyard garden, with elaborate mosaics, under-floor central heating, and a bathhouse. The gardens were surrounded by colonnades, and the palace included state rooms, a ceremonial reception room, and private apartments. The decoration included wall paintings, stucco mouldings, and opus sectile marble panels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fishbourne Roman Palace is culturally significant as the largest Roman residence north of the Alps, reflecting the opulence and influence of Roman Britain. It provides insights into Roman architectural practices, garden design, and the social hierarchy of the time. The site also offers evidence of pre-Roman human activity, challenging earlier assumptions about the area's history.
world knowledge.Details: The site of the palace was later used as a burial ground during the early Saxon period. A museum was erected over the excavated remains by the Sussex Archaeological Society, which continues to preserve and research the site. The museum includes re-planted gardens with authentic Roman plants. The palace was closed temporarily in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic but has since reopened to the public.

world knowledge.Name: Mandalay Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mandalay Palace, located in Mandalay, Myanmar, is the last royal palace of the last Burmese monarchy. Constructed between 1857 and 1859 as part of King Mindon's founding of the new royal capital city of Mandalay, the palace follows traditional Burmese palace design. It was the primary royal residence of King Mindon and King Thibaw. The palace ceased to be a royal residence on 28 November 1885 when British troops captured it during the Third Anglo-Burmese War. Much of the palace was destroyed during World War II, and a replica was rebuilt in the 1990s.

Major_Events.Description: British troops captured the palace, ending its role as a royal residence and seat of government.
Much of the palace was destroyed by Allied bombing; only the royal mint and the watch tower survived.
A replica of the palace was rebuilt using traditional and modern building techniques.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is designed in traditional Burmese architectural style, featuring one-storey buildings with spires indicating the importance of the area. The palace compound is surrounded by a walled fort and a moat. The walls are 3 m thick at the base and 1.47 m at the top, with 48 bastions and 12 gates, each representing a zodiac sign. The palace buildings are constructed using teak and feature intricate carvings and gilded decorations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mandalay Palace is a primary symbol of Burmese sovereignty and identity. It represents the last era of Burmese monarchy and is a major tourist destination, symbolizing the cultural and historical heritage of Myanmar.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official Residence of the King of Konbaung Dynasty
world knowledge.Details: The palace's formal name in Burmese is Mya Nan San Kyaw, meaning 'The Famed Royal Emerald Palace'. It is also known as the 'Great Golden Royal Palace'. The palace was reconstructed in the 1990s using both traditional and modern materials, including corrugated sheet metal for roofing and concrete. The palace compound includes the Clock Tower, the Tooth-Relic Tower, the Royal Mint, and the Watch Tower, among other structures.

world knowledge.Name: Santa Lucía riverwalk
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Santa Lucia riverwalk is an artificial river located in Monterrey, Mexico. Construction began in 1996 but was halted for nine years due to economic reasons. It resumed in 2005 and was completed in 2007. It was inaugurated by Mexican President Felipe Calderon Hinojosa, Nuevo León's governor Natividad González Parás, and Monterrey's mayor Adalberto Madero in celebration of the 197th anniversary of the Mexican War of Independence.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by Mexican President Felipe Calderon Hinojosa, Nuevo León's governor Natividad González Parás, and Monterrey's mayor Adalberto Madero in celebration of the 197th anniversary of the Mexican War of Independence.
The riverwalk was part of the 2007 Universal Forum of Cultures' attractions.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is one of the most important attractions in Monterrey and was part of the 2007 Universal Forum of Cultures' attractions.
world knowledge.Details: The Santa Lucia riverwalk is an artificial river that serves as a significant cultural and tourist attraction in Monterrey.

world knowledge.Name: Nova Sintra
world knowledge.Address: São João Baptista, Brava Municipality, Cape Verde
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nova Sintra is a city in the central part of the island of Brava in southwestern Cape Verde. It serves as the seat of the Brava Municipality. The settlement is named after Sintra, the summer residence of the Portuguese kings. Since 2010, Nova Sintra has been a city.

Major_Events.Event: Submission to UNESCO's World Heritage Sites tentative list
Major_Events.Description: The historic center of Nova Sintra was submitted to the tentative list of UNESCO's World Heritage Sites.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nova Sintra is culturally significant as it is named after Sintra, the summer residence of the Portuguese kings, and its historic center has been submitted to UNESCO's World Heritage Sites tentative list.
world knowledge.Details: Agriculture is the predominant source of income on Brava. Tourism is less developed, but there are a few small hotels and guest houses. Nova Sintra has a hot semi-arid climate (Köppen BSh) and is cooler than the low-lying areas of the island. Its average rainfall is 418 millimetres (16.5 in), and its average temperature is 20.3 °C (68.5 °F). The coldest month is February with an average of 18.0 °C (64.4 °F) and the warmest is September with an average of 22.4 °C (72.3 °F).

world knowledge.Name: Wat Saket
world knowledge.Address: Boripat Road, Khwaeng Ban Bat, Khet Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok 10100, Thailand
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Ayutthaya period (renovated many times during the Rattanakosin period)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Saket dates back to the Ayutthaya era, originally known as Wat Sakae. It was renovated and renamed by King Rama I when Bangkok became the capital. The temple is home to Phu Khao Thong, an artificial hill and chedi that became a significant structure despite initial construction failures. The temple has served various roles, including as a cremation site and a lookout tower.

Major_Events.Description: During the reign of King Rama II, cholera spread from Penang to Bangkok, leading to over 30,000 deaths. Wat Saket became a primary site for receiving and cremating the dead.

Major_Events.Year: Reign of King Rama III to Rama V
Major_Events.Description: King Rama III initiated the construction of a large chedi, which collapsed due to the soft soil. The structure eventually formed a natural hill, later topped with a small chedi by King Rama IV and completed by King Rama V.

Major_Events.Year: Since the reign of King Rama V
Major_Events.Description: An annual festival is held every November, featuring a candlelight procession up Phu Khao Thong and a Loi Krathong festival with various traditional games and shows.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features Thai architecture with significant use of Carrara marble in its modern construction. The site includes Phu Khao Thong, a steep artificial hill with a golden chedi on top.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Saket is culturally significant as a historical Buddhist temple that has witnessed key events in Bangkok's history, including epidemics and royal renovations. Phu Khao Thong has become a symbol of the city and a popular tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: Wat Saket was traditionally used as a cremation site outside the city walls, accessed through the 'ghost gate.' The temple is also known for its association with vultures during the cholera epidemics, a grim reminder of the past. The annual festival and Phu Khao Thong continue to draw visitors and devotees.

world knowledge.Name: Ta Prohm
world knowledge.Address: Near the city of Siem Reap, Cambodia, approximately one kilometre east of Angkor Thom and on the southern edge of the East Baray
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ta Prohm, originally called Rajavihara, was founded by the Khmer King Jayavarman VII as a Mahayana Buddhist monastery and center of learning dedicated to his mother. It was built in the Bayon style in the late 12th century and early 13th century. The temple was home to more than 12,500 people, with an additional 80,000 inhabitants in the surrounding villages. After the fall of the Khmer Empire in the 15th century, the temple was abandoned and neglected until conservation efforts began in the early 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was completed and dedicated as a Mahayana Buddhist monastery and center of learning.
The temple was abandoned after the fall of the Khmer Empire.
Ta Prohm was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation of the Hall of Dancers
Major_Events.Description: A renovation of the Hall of Dancers was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Ta Prohm is a typical 'flat' Khmer temple with five rectangular enclosing walls surrounding a central sanctuary. The temple is oriented to the east, with entrance gopuras at each of the cardinal points. The design includes face towers similar to those found at the Bayon, and the temple features galleried inner enclosures, libraries, satellite temples, and the Hall of Dancers. The temple was built without mortar, and trees have grown out of the ruins, creating a distinctive appearance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ta Prohm is culturally significant as a Mahayana Buddhist monastery and center of learning founded by King Jayavarman VII in honor of his family. The temple's unique integration with the jungle and its depiction in the film 'Lara Croft: Tomb Raider' have made it a popular tourist destination. It is also significant for its architectural style and its role in the history of the Khmer Empire.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious site (Mahayana Buddhist monastery and center of learning)
world knowledge.Details: Ta Prohm is known as the 'Tomb Raider Temple' due to its depiction in the film 'Lara Croft: Tomb Raider'. The temple features stone reliefs of devatas, meditating monks, and dvarapalas. The trees growing out of the ruins, including the silk-cotton tree and strangler fig, are a distinctive feature. The temple has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1992, and conservation efforts have been undertaken by the Archaeological Survey of India and APSARA.

world knowledge.Name: Ichijōdani Asakura Family Historic Ruins
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 500 meters east-west width and 3 kilometers length
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ichijōdani Asakura Family Historic Ruins were controlled by the Asakura clan for 103 years during the Sengoku period. The area was fortified in 1471 by Asakura Toshikage, who constructed hilltop fortifications, walls, and gates. It became a major cultural, military, and population center, with a peak population of over 10,000 inhabitants. The Asakura clan maintained good relations with the Ashikaga shogunate but came into conflict with Oda Nobunaga, leading to the destruction of Ichijōdani in 1573.

Major_Events.Description: Asakura Toshikage fortified the valley by constructing hilltop fortifications, walls, and gates.
Oda Nobunaga razed Ichijōdani to the ground during the siege.
Excavation of the ruins began, revealing the shape of the whole town, including residences, temples, and streets.
The site was designated as a Special National Historic Site.

Major_Events.Event: Designation of Artifacts as Important Cultural Property
Major_Events.Description: 2,343 artifacts were designated as Important Cultural Property.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site includes restored samurai residences, merchants' quarters, and streets. Four Japanese gardens were unearthed and partially restored. The ruins of Ichijōdani Castle are located on a nearby hill.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The site is a significant historical and cultural landmark, representing the Asakura clan's influence during the Sengoku period. It was a major cultural, military, and population center, and its artifacts and gardens are nationally recognized.
world knowledge.Details: Approximately 1,700,000 relics were found at the ruins, with 2,343 designated as Important Cultural Properties. Many artifacts are displayed at the Ichijodani Asakura Family Site Museum. The site was designated as a Place of Scenic Beauty in 1991 for its restored gardens.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Suthat Thepwararam
world knowledge.Address: 146 Bamrung Mueang Rd, Wat Ratchabophit, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Suthat Thepwararam is a royal temple of the first grade, initiated by King Rama I in 1807 and completed during the reign of King Rama III in 1847 or 1848. It houses significant Buddha images, including Phra Sri Sakyamuni, moved from Sukhothai Province. The temple features 28 Chinese pagodas symbolizing the 28 Buddhas born on earth. It was submitted to UNESCO for consideration as a World Heritage Site in 2005.

Major_Events.Description: King Rama I initiated the construction of Wat Suthat Thepwararam.
The temple was completed during the reign of King Rama III.
The temple was submitted to UNESCO for consideration as a World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features intricate wooden doors carved by King Rama II, 28 Chinese pagodas, and significant Buddha images including Phra Sri Sakyamuni, Phra Buddha Trilokachet, and Phra Buddha Setthamuni. The temple's ordination hall and meeting hall are notable for their religious and artistic significance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Suthat Thepwararam is culturally significant as a royal temple of the first grade, housing important Buddha images and symbolizing the rich Buddhist heritage of Thailand. Its submission to UNESCO highlights its global cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The temple is associated with the saying "Pret Wat Suthat" due to the belief in preta, a kind of undead in Buddhist and Siamese belief, appearing in front of the temple at night. The Sao Chingcha, or Giant Swing, a towering Hindu structure, stands in front of the temple.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Central Terminal
world knowledge.Address: 89 East 42nd Street, Manhattan, New York City
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grand Central Terminal was built by and named for the New York Central Railroad; it also served the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad and, later, successors to the New York Central. Opened in 1913, the terminal was built on the site of two similarly named predecessor stations, the first of which dated to 1871. Grand Central Terminal served intercity trains until 1991, when Amtrak consolidated its New York operations at nearby Penn Station.

Major_Events.Description: The terminal opened on February 2, 1913, replacing the previous Grand Central Station.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as a National Historic Landmark
Major_Events.Description: Grand Central Terminal was declared a National Historic Landmark.
A major renovation of the terminal was completed, restoring its original grandeur.
The terminal celebrated its 100th anniversary with various events and displays.
The new Long Island Rail Road station beneath Grand Central Terminal opened as part of the East Side Access project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts style designed by Reed and Stem and Warren and Wetmore. Features include a monumental Main Concourse with a celestial ceiling, ornate facades, and extensive use of marble and granite. The terminal has 44 platforms and 67 tracks, all below ground level.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grand Central Terminal is one of the world's most famous railway stations and a symbol of New York City. It is a National Historic Landmark and a major tourist attraction, known for its architectural beauty and historical importance. The terminal has been featured in numerous films, television shows, and literary works.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Commuter rail terminal serving Metro-North Railroad and Long Island Rail Road, with connections to the New York City Subway and bus services.
world knowledge.Details: Grand Central Terminal is the third-busiest train station in North America. It features a variety of retail stores, restaurants, and cultural attractions, including the Grand Central Market and the Grand Central Oyster Bar. The terminal's Main Concourse is famous for its four-sided brass clock and celestial ceiling mural.

world knowledge.Name: Benedictine Sisters of Erie
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Benedictine Sisters of Erie are a Benedictine priory in Erie, Pennsylvania, established in 1856. Known for their social and anti-war activism, they have been involved in various community and educational initiatives since their founding.

Major_Events.Event: Formation of the Benedictine Sisters of Erie
Major_Events.Description: Mother Benedicta Rapp and five Benedictine sisters arrived in Erie and established the first daughter house of the Benedictine Sisters of Elk County.

Major_Events.Event: Appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show
Major_Events.Description: The Sisters, under the group name "Sisters-66", appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show after a successful musical performance in Erie.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of John XXIII Home For Senior Citizens
Major_Events.Description: The priory began running the John XXIII Home For Senior Citizens, which was later handed over to a lay person in 1994.

Major_Events.Event: Anti-war activism during the Vietnam War
Major_Events.Description: The Sisters refused to allow military recruiters to visit St. Benedict Academy and organized "die-ins" in protest of the war.
The priory installed a wind generator to harness local natural resources.
The Sisters began holding vigils at sites of homicides to reclaim the sites for nonviolence.
A Republican Party operative accused the Sisters of voter fraud, which they refuted, emphasizing their nonpartisan status.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Benedictine Sisters of Erie are culturally significant for their long-standing commitment to social justice, education, and community service, as well as their activism in anti-war and environmental causes.
world knowledge.Details: The Sisters have been involved in various educational and community initiatives, including running schools, child care centers, and art programs. They also manage housing for seniors and low-income disabled residents.

world knowledge.Name: Ring of Brodgar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ring of Brodgar is a Neolithic henge and stone circle in Mainland, Orkney, Scotland. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site known as the Heart of Neolithic Orkney. The site is the only major henge and stone circle in Britain which is an almost perfect circle. It is generally thought to have been erected between 2500 BCE and 2000 BCE, and was the last of the great Neolithic monuments built on the Ness.

Major_Events.Description: An excavation project undertaken to settle the age issue and help answer other questions about the site.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as part of the Heart of Neolithic Orkney World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The Ring of Brodgar was included in the Heart of Neolithic Orkney World Heritage Site during the 23rd session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stone circle is 104 metres in diameter, originally with up to 60 stones, of which only 27 remained standing at the end of the 20th century. The stones are set within a circular ditch up to 3 metres deep, 9 metres wide, and 380 metres in circumference. The ditch was carved out of the solid sandstone bedrock.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ring of Brodgar is a site of major importance due to its proximity to other ancient sites such as the Ness of Brodgar, the Standing Stones of Stenness, and the Maeshowe tomb. It is considered the finest known truly circular late Neolithic or early Bronze Age stone ring.
world knowledge.Details: The site is managed by Historic Environment Scotland and has been subject to conservation efforts due to access issues. It features in literature and video games, such as Kathleen Fidler's novel 'The Boy with the Bronze Axe' and the game 'Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura'.

world knowledge.Name: Casbah of Algiers
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Casbah of Algiers is the citadel of Algiers in Algeria and the traditional quarter clustered around it. It was founded on the ruins of old Icosium in the 10th century. In 1992, UNESCO proclaimed it a World Cultural Heritage Site due to its remains of the citadel, old mosques, Ottoman-style palaces, and a traditional urban structure associated with a deep-rooted sense of community.

Major_Events.Description: Shortly after the French conquest, the French governor moved into Dar Hassan Pacha.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Napoleon III and Eugénie de Montijo
Major_Events.Description: Napoleon III and Eugénie de Montijo visited the Casbah.
The Casbah played a central role during the Algerian War of Independence, serving as the epicenter of the insurgency planning of the National Liberation Front (FLN).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Casbah features masonry and mosques dating from the 17th century, including Ketchaoua Mosque, Djama’a al-Djedid, Djamaâ el Kebir, and Ali Bitchin Mosque. It also contains several palaces such as Dar Aziza, Dar Mustapha Pacha, Palace of the Dey, and Dar Hassan Pacha.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Casbah of Algiers is culturally and historically significant as it represents a traditional urban structure with deep-rooted community ties. It contains important historical and religious buildings, and it played a pivotal role in the Algerian War of Independence.
world knowledge.Details: The Casbah of Algiers is vulnerable to sea level rise and has been included in the list of African cultural sites threatened by flooding and coastal erosion by the end of the century, particularly under high greenhouse gas emission scenarios. Restoration efforts have been plagued by delays and corruption, and the area suffers from overpopulation and neglect.

world knowledge.Name: Nebet Tepe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nebet Tepe is one of the hills of Plovdiv where the ancient town was founded. The earliest settlements on Nebet Tepe are dated back to 4000 BC. The site was first settled by Thracians, later expanded by Philip II of Macedon and the Roman Empire. As the town expanded, Nebet Tepe became the citadel of the town's acropolis. There are remains of the city's walls, towers, and a postern from the time of Justinian leading down to the Maritsa river. Today, the archaeological complex on the hill is one of the most popular tourist sights in Plovdiv and a cultural monument of national significance.

Major_Events.Description: The earliest settlements on Nebet Tepe are dated back to 4000 BC.

Major_Events.Event: Expansion by Philip II of Macedon
Major_Events.Description: The site was expanded by Philip II of Macedon.
The site was further expanded by the Roman Empire.
A secret tunnel in the rocks under the North wall was built during the reign of Justinian.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The oldest part of the walls on the hill dating from the 4th c. BC was built with large syenite blocks closely fitted together with minimal clearance between adjacent stones and no use of mortar, typical for ancient cyclopean masonry. The remains of the Western wall with the imposing quadrangular tower and its entrance are evidence of the Hellenistic period. There are also thick stone walls from later periods and other ancient buildings. A unique postern with staircase from Roman times: a secret tunnel in the rocks under the North wall built in the 6th century AD during the reign of Justinian. Water reservoirs used for water supply were also located on the hill. A large rectangular water reservoir with a volume of 350 m3 is preserved in the Southern part of Nebet Tepe.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nebet Tepe is one of the most popular tourist sights in Plovdiv and a cultural monument of national significance. The name "Nebet" comes from the Turkish words nevbet (meaning "guard") and tepe (meaning "hill") or "The hill of the guards". It is assumed that in ancient times the garrison that guarded the city was located on the hill. The hill has another name in ancient times - "The hill of Musaeus", which is associated with the Thracian Musaeus who was the most talented student of Orpheus.
world knowledge.Details: Excavations from 2016 have brought to light a Roman wall bastion dating from the 1st c. AD.

world knowledge.Name: Arlington National Cemetery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arlington National Cemetery was established during the American Civil War after the Arlington Estate was confiscated from Confederate General Robert E. Lee's family. It is the largest cemetery in the United States National Cemetery System and is managed by the U.S. Department of the Army. The cemetery has over 400,000 graves and conducts approximately 27 to 30 funerals each weekday.

Major_Events.Description: The cemetery was established during the American Civil War after the Arlington Estate was confiscated from Robert E. Lee's family.
Private William Henry Christman was the first soldier buried in Arlington.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Arlington National Cemetery Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
A $35 million expansion plan to utilize Arlington woodland, Fort Myer, and Navy Annex land for additional burial space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cemetery features a variety of memorials and structures, including the Arlington Memorial Amphitheater, the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, and the USS Maine Mast Memorial. The amphitheater is built of Imperial Danby marble from Vermont, and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is made from Yule marble quarried in Colorado.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arlington National Cemetery is a symbol of honor and sacrifice for the United States military. It serves as the final resting place for many of the nation's heroes, including Medal of Honor recipients, presidents, and notable military figures. The cemetery is also a site for national ceremonies and memorials.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Military cemetery and national memorial site

Details.Eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans, active duty service members, and certain family members are eligible for burial. Specific eligibility criteria apply for ground burial and inurnment in the columbarium.

world knowledge.Name: Wreck of the Ten Sail
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wreck of the Ten Sail is a historic shipwreck event that occurred on 8 February 1794, involving ten ships of a convoy traveling from Jamaica to the United States and Britain. The ships wrecked on the reef off the East End of Grand Cayman. Local residents bravely rescued the crews and passengers, though eight people died. The event has become a significant part of Caymanian history and folklore.

Major_Events.Description: Ten ships wrecked on the reef off the East End of Grand Cayman during a storm. Local residents rescued the crews and passengers, but eight people died.
Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip visited the site and dedicated a memorial plaque and park on the 200th anniversary of the shipwreck.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wreck of the Ten Sail is culturally significant as it is commemorated in Caymanian folklore and history. It is often cited as the reason for the Cayman Islands' tax-free status, though this is based on legend rather than documented evidence. The event is remembered for the bravery of the local residents who rescued the shipwrecked individuals.
world knowledge.Details: A park with a Maritime Trail, a brass and stone memorial, and a viewing platform exists to commemorate the event. The memorial plaque and park were dedicated by Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip in 1994. The site includes ten embedded cement blocks representing the ten ships that were wrecked.

world knowledge.Name: Château du Haut-Koenigsbourg
world knowledge.Address: Commune of Orschwiller, Bas-Rhin département, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château du Haut-Koenigsbourg is a medieval castle located in the Vosges mountains, strategically overlooking the Upper Rhine Plain. It was used by successive powers from the Middle Ages until the Thirty Years' War when it was abandoned. It was rebuilt from 1900 to 1908 at the behest of German Kaiser Wilhelm II. The castle has a rich history, including ownership by the Hohenstaufen family, dukes of Lorraine, and Habsburg emperors. It was besieged and burned during the Thirty Years' War and later restored as a symbol of German civilization.

Major_Events.Description: A Burg Staufen (Castrum Estufin) is documented, built unlawfully by Duke Frederick II of Swabia.

Major_Events.Event: Siege and burning by Protestant Swedish forces
Major_Events.Description: During the Thirty Years' War, the castle was besieged for 52 days and then burned and looted.
The castle was rebuilt under architect Bodo Ebhardt to reflect medieval Alsatian and German civilization.
The restored Hohkönigsburg was inaugurated in the presence of Kaiser Wilhelm II.
After World War I, the castle was confiscated by France under the Treaty of Versailles.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle was rebuilt in a medieval style, with some improvisations due to lack of historical information. The Keep tower is about 14 meters too tall, and the main dining hall has a higher roof than originally. The restoration aimed to reflect the castle's state on the eve of the Thirty Years' War, with defensive systems suited to artillery of the time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a symbol of Alsatian history and German romantic nationalism. It reflects Kaiser Wilhelm II's ideas of Germanic civilization and was intended to legitimize the House of Hohenzollern. Today, it is a major tourist attraction and a monument historique.
world knowledge.Details: The castle attracts over 500,000 visitors annually. It was listed as a monument historique in 1862 and classified in 1993. Parts of the 1937 film 'La Grande Illusion' by Jean Renoir were shot here. Nearby is the ruin of Château de l'Oedenbourg (Petit-Koenigsbourg). A replica of the castle exists in Berjaya Hills, Malaysia.

world knowledge.Name: Pico Cão Grande
world knowledge.Area: Caué District, São Tomé Island, Parque Natural Obô de São Tomé
world knowledge.Address: Vila Clotilde, 3 km to the east; São João dos Angolares, 9 km to the east
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 663 m (2,175 ft) elevation, 370 m (1,210 ft) prominence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pico Cão Grande is a needle-shaped volcanic plug formed by magma solidifying in the vent of an active volcano, part of the Cameroon line of volcanoes. It is composed mainly of phonolite.

Major_Events.Description: A Portuguese team of climbers made the first attempt to climb Pico Cão Grande.
A Japanese team consisting of Yosuke Takahashi, Kenichi Moriyama, and Naotoshi Agata achieved the first successful ascent in February 1991.
Gareth Leah from England and Sergio Almada from Mexico established a new bolt-protected route named Nubivagant, graded F8b (5.13d).
Spanish brothers Iker and Eneko Pou established a new route called Leve Leve, graded F8b+ (5.14a), and made the first all-free ascent of Nubivagant.
A team of Americans, Sam Daulton and Remy Franklin, made another all-free ascent of Nubivagant.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Needle-shaped volcanic plug composed mainly of phonolite, with moss growing on the rocks due to high moisture content.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pico Cão Grande is a significant natural landmark in São Tomé and Príncipe, known for its unique geological formation and challenging climbing routes.
world knowledge.Details: Climbing Pico Cão Grande is difficult due to the moss-covered rocks and presence of snakes. The first successful ascent was in 1991, and several challenging routes have been established since then, including Nubivagant and Leve Leve.

world knowledge.Name: Castillo de Jagua
world knowledge.Address: Near the entrance to the Cienfuegos Bay, Cienfuegos, Cuba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castle of Jagua is a fortress located south of Cienfuegos in Cuba, near the entrance to the Cienfuegos Bay. It was originally named 'Castillo de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles de Jagua' and was built in 1742 by King Philip V of Spain to protect the bay from pirates. The fortress played a crucial role in safeguarding the bay and the city of Cienfuegos, which was founded in 1819. The fort is built in solid limestone and features several floors, a well, a watch tower, and a moat with a drawbridge that remains in perfect condition.

Major_Events.Description: The fortress was built by King Philip V of Spain to protect the bay from pirates.
The city of Cienfuegos was founded by French colonists, and the fortress became essential for protecting its harbor.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fortress is built in solid limestone and features several floors, a well, a watch tower, and a moat with a drawbridge that remains in perfect condition. It is an example of Spanish Colonial architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Castillo de Jagua is a significant example of Cuban colonial architecture and played a crucial role in protecting the bay and the city of Cienfuegos from pirates. It remains an important historical site and a symbol of Cuba's colonial past.
world knowledge.Details: The fortress is located in front of the entrance to the bay. Nearby is the abandoned Nuclear City that was never completed due to the disintegration of the USSR. The fortress has been featured on Cuban banknotes, specifically the 10-peso 'Exchange Certificate' issued during the 1980s, which depicted the castle on its back.

image_name: Misión San Francisco Javier de Viggé-Biaundó

world knowledge.Name: Misión San Francisco Javier de Viggé-Biaundó
world knowledge.Address: San Javier, Baja California Sur, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Misión San Francisco Javier de Viggé-Biaundó was a Spanish mission established by Jesuits in 1699 on the Baja California peninsula. It aimed to convert the local Cochimí Native Americans to Christianity. The mission was abandoned in 1701 due to a threatened Indian revolt but reestablished in 1702. It was moved to its present location in 1710 due to water scarcity. The mission played a significant role in the region's colonial history and the spread of Christianity.

Major_Events.Description: The mission was founded by Jesuits to convert the local Cochimí Native Americans to Christianity.
The mission was abandoned due to a threatened Indian revolt.
The mission was reestablished by Juan de Ugarte.
The mission was moved to its present location due to water scarcity.
Miguel del Barco constructed what has been called "the jewel of the Baja California mission churches."
The mission was deserted by 1817.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mission church is noted for its stone construction and is considered a significant example of colonial architecture in Baja California. Miguel del Barco's work between 1744 and 1758 is particularly notable.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mission is culturally significant as one of the earliest and most enduring Spanish missions in Baja California. It played a key role in the spread of Christianity and the colonial history of the region. The mission also represents the interaction between European settlers and the indigenous Cochimí people.
world knowledge.Details: The mission was dedicated to Francis Xavier, a Navarrese Catholic missionary and saint. The church has been restored and is maintained by Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History. The village of San Javier at the site of the former mission had a population of 131 in 2010. Several introduced plant species, such as date palms, grapes, citrus, and ancient olive trees, continue to exist or be grown at the mission.

world knowledge.Name: Wat Phra Singh
world knowledge.Address: End of Rachadamnoen Road, Chiang Mai, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wat Phra Singh, originally named Wat Lichiang Phra, was established in 1345 by King Phayu to house the ashes of his father, King Kham Fu. The temple was renamed after the Phra Buddha Sihing statue was brought to the temple in 1367. It underwent significant restoration in the 1920s under Khru Ba Srivichai and again in 2002. The temple was abandoned during Burmese rule from 1578 to 1774 and was later restored by King Kawila in 1782.

Major_Events.Description: King Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII) bestowed upon Wat Phra Singh the status of Royal temple of the first grade.
King Kawila restored the temple, built the ubosot, and enlarged the chedi.

Major_Events.Event: Extensive renovations by Khru Ba Srivichai
Major_Events.Description: The temple complex underwent extensive renovations under the famous monk Khru Ba Srivichai.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Wat Phra Singh UK
Major_Events.Description: A Wat was established in Runcorn, Cheshire, England with the support of Wat Phra Singh and the President of the Council for Thai Buddhist Monks in the UK.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple complex includes a chedi, wihan, ubosot, Ho Trai (temple library), and is guarded by Singhs (lions). The main entrance is at the end of Rachadamnoen Road.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wat Phra Singh is culturally significant as a Royal temple of the first grade and houses the important Phra Buddha Sihing statue. It plays a central role in the Songkran festival, where the statue is paraded through the streets of Chiang Mai.
world knowledge.Details: The temple complex was named Wat Lichiang Phra before receiving the Phra Buddha Sihing statue in 1367. The statue's head was allegedly stolen in 1922, and it is possible that the current statue or its head is a copy. During restoration in 1925, three funerary urns believed to contain royal ashes were discovered but have since been lost. The temple also supported the establishment of a Wat in Runcorn, England, in 2013.

image_name: Quốc Học – Huế High School for the Gifted

world knowledge.Name: Quốc Học – Huế High School for the Gifted
world knowledge.Physical_Area: One of the largest high school campuses of Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded on October 23, 1896, Quốc Học - Huế is the third oldest high school in Vietnam. It was established to coach students who would serve the feudal colonial government, with French as the main subject. The school has undergone several reconstructions and relocations, notably during the confrontation against French Colonialists. It was officially renamed as Quốc Học – Huế High School for the Gifted in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: Quốc Học – Huế High School was established to coach students who would serve the feudal colonial government.
The school was reconstructed with buildings made of brick and tiles, following Western European architecture.
The school was moved into two places: Binh Tri Thien School in Huong Khe, Hà Tĩnh province and Huynh Thuc Khang School in Đức Thọ, Hà Tĩnh Province.
The school was officially renamed as Quốc Học – Huế High School for the Gifted.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The school features French architectural-designed buildings, large shady trees, and stone benches. The construction is solid and comfortable, with most of the original architecture still existing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Quốc Học – Huế is culturally and historically important as one of the oldest and most prestigious high schools in Vietnam. It has produced notable political leaders, including Ho Chi Minh, and is recognized for its strong academic results and high-quality education.
world knowledge.Details: The school has a library, English and French labs, computer rooms, science labs, a soccer field, basketball court, badminton courts, swimming pool, medium stadium, hall, and cafeteria. It offers specialized classes in subjects like Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Vietnamese Literature, History, Geography, English, Japanese, and French. The school also hosts various extra-curricular clubs and annual events like the Quoc Hoc Anniversary Festival and Quoc Hoc Prom Night.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary
world knowledge.Address: Wigan Lane, Wigan, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, also known as the Wigan Infirmary, originated from the Wigan Dispensary established in King Street in 1796. The current facility's foundation stone was laid in 1870, and it was opened by the Prince and Princess of Wales in 1873. It joined the National Health Service in 1948 and has undergone several expansions, including a major extension in 2004.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone for the current facility in Wigan Lane was laid by the Earl of Crawford.
The new building, designed by Thomas Worthington and Joseph Hanson, was opened by the Prince and Princess of Wales.
The infirmary joined the National Health Service.
A major extension, in the same architectural style as the original building, was completed.
A new ward dedicated to treating COVID-19 patients, named Bryn Ward, was opened with 50 beds, 27 of which were for intensive care.
A new £7.6 million community assessment unit with 21 beds was opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Thomas Worthington and Joseph Hanson, the building features a consistent architectural style, including the major extension completed in 2004.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The infirmary is a significant health facility in Greater Manchester, providing essential medical services since the 18th century and playing a crucial role during the COVID-19 pandemic.
world knowledge.Details: The infirmary is managed by the Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust. It has an Accident & Emergency department and has undergone several expansions to meet growing healthcare demands.

world knowledge.Name: Fontana Maggiore
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fontana Maggiore is a masterpiece of medieval sculpture located in the center of Piazza IV Novembre in Perugia. It was designed by Frà Bevignate da Cingoli and built to celebrate the arrival of water in the city's acropolis via a new aqueduct. The fountain was constructed with the collaboration of several talented professionals, including hydraulic engineer Boninsegna Veneziano and melter Rosso Padellaio. The marble reliefs were carved by Nicola Pisano and his son Giovanni Pisano. The fountain was damaged by the earthquake of 1348 and underwent several restorations, including in 1948/49 and 1995/99.

Major_Events.Description: The fountain was damaged by the earthquake of 1348, leading to a random reconstruction of the tile order.
The fountain was refurbished for the first time.
The fountain underwent another refurbishment.
The Italian Posts issued a 40 Lire stamp dedicated to Fontana Maggiore as part of the 'Fontane d’Italia' collection.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fountain consists of two concentric polygonal marble basins with a bronze cup on top. The lower basin has 25 mirrors divided into tiles representing the 12 months of the year, each associated with zodiac symbols and scenes of daily life and farming work. The upper basin features 24 statues of saints and mythological and biblical characters. The fountain was made of stone from Assisi and assembled in the center of the square.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fontana Maggiore is a symbol of Perugia and represents the harmonization of Judeo-Christian and ancient Greek-Roman civilizations. It highlights the importance of water as a sacred element and celebrates the city's history and daily life through its intricate carvings and statues.
world knowledge.Details: The fountain inspired the construction of the Sturinalto fountain in Fabriano in 1285. In the early 20th century, it was refurbished by architect Giuseppe Sacconi. The lower basin's tiles depict scenes of manual labor and liberal arts, while the upper basin's statues include representations of important historical and mythological figures. Latin verses carved on the fountain invite viewers to examine and interpret its intricate details.

world knowledge.Name: Cape St George Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Jervis Bay Village, Jervis Bay Territory, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape St George Lighthouse was constructed in 1860 and was active until 1889. It was controversially built in an incorrect location, leading to navigation issues. The tower was destroyed between 1917–1922 by the Royal Australian Navy to avoid confusion in daylight. The ruins remain and are listed on the Commonwealth Heritage List.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was controversially built in an incorrect location, leading to navigation issues. It was commissioned despite objections from the Pilots Board.
The lighthouse was deactivated and replaced by Point Perpendicular Light due to its poor visibility and incorrect siting.
The tower was used for target practice by the Royal Australian Navy and destroyed to avoid confusion in daylight.
The ruins were listed on the Commonwealth Heritage List for their historical and maritime significance.
In 1887, Harriet Parker, daughter of the Assistant light keepers, was accidentally shot dead. In 1895, Edward Bailey, the Chief Lighthouse Keeper, drowned while fishing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse was constructed from limestone with a cylindrical tower shape. It had a foundation made of Sydney sandstone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The ruins are significant for their association with the development of navigational aids in Australia and their incorrect siting, which adds to their historical and landmark significance. They are also an integral part of Australia's maritime history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid for ships entering Jervis Bay.
world knowledge.Details: The site is managed by the Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community and the Department of the Environment, Water, Heritage and the Arts as part of the Booderee National Park. The ruins are accessible to the public, though the ruins themselves are closed. The park service has stabilized the ruins against further decay.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Pirou
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Pirou was initially built of wood, then of stone in the 12th century and belonged to the lords of Pirou. It was constructed near the shore of the English Channel to protect the town of Coutances and a strategic shallow-water harbor. As the coastline receded, the castle lost its strategic significance. It was transformed into Lord Adnan's penthouse during the 18th century and began to deteriorate. In 1968, it was listed in the Inventaire supplémentaire des Monuments historiques, and restoration was initiated by the abbot Marcel Lelégard.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was rebuilt in stone during the 12th century.
The castle was converted into Lord Adnan's penthouse.
The castle was listed in the Inventaire supplémentaire des Monuments historiques by the French Ministry of Culture.
Restoration was begun on the initiative of the abbot Marcel Lelégard.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle now lies in the middle of an artificial pond, with a stone bridge replacing the original drawbridge. The curtain walls from the 12th century enclose two residential houses from the 16th and 18th centuries. A barn on the premises houses a locally-made tapestry in the style of the Bayeux Tapestry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Pirou is culturally significant due to its historical role in protecting the region, its preservation through the French Revolution, and its association with local legends, such as the tale of the Lord of Pirou transforming into geese to escape Viking invaders.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built for defense, now serves as a tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The castle can be visited as a tourist attraction (note that it closes during lunchtime). A famous legend of Normandy originates in the castle, involving the Lord of Pirou and his family transforming into geese to escape Viking invaders.

world knowledge.Name: El Mirador
world knowledge.Historical_Background: El Mirador is a large pre-Columbian Middle and Late Preclassic Maya settlement, located in the north of the modern department of El Petén, Guatemala. It flourished from about the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD, reaching its height from the 3rd century BC. The site experienced a hiatus of construction and perhaps abandonment for generations, followed by re-occupation and further construction in the Late Classic era, and a final abandonment about the end of the 9th century.

Major_Events.Description: Ian Graham spent some time there making the first map of the area.
An archaeological project under the direction of Bruce Dahlin at Catholic University of America and Ray Matheny at Brigham Young University began detailed investigations.

Major_Events.Event: Major investigation, stabilization, and conservation programs initiated
Major_Events.Description: Richard D. Hansen, a senior scientist from Idaho State University, initiated major investigation, stabilization, and conservation programs at El Mirador with a multi-disciplinary approach.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: El Mirador features monumental architecture from 10 to 72 meters high, including triadic structures consisting of large artificial platforms topped with a set of 3 summit pyramids. Notable structures include El Tigre (55 meters high) and La Danta temple (72 meters high). The structures were originally faced with cut stone decorated with large stucco masks depicting the deities of Maya mythology.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: El Mirador is culturally and historically important as one of the largest and earliest Maya cities, providing insights into the development of Maya civilization. It is considered by some archaeologists to be one of the largest ancient structures in the world.
world knowledge.Details: El Mirador is part of the Mirador-Calakmul Karst Basin of northern Guatemala. The site includes causeways (sacbeob) linking important architectural compounds and neighboring sites. The area is threatened by deforestation, looting, and destruction caused by logging road construction. Since 2003, the Global Heritage Fund has been working to preserve and protect Mirador.

world knowledge.Name: Murabba Palace
world knowledge.Address: King Abdulaziz Historical Center, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Murabba Palace is a historic palace in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, built by King Abdulaziz. It served as his official workplace and main residence from 1938 until his death in 1953. The palace was transformed into a museum and opened to the public in 1999. It introduced novel technologies like automobiles, electricity, and water closets to Saudi society. The palace was part of the first major expansion of Riyadh in the 20th century.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the council of ministers
Major_Events.Description: King Saud inaugurated the council of ministers with a ceremony in the Murabba Palace.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and opening as a museum
Major_Events.Description: The palace was renovated and converted into a museum, becoming open to the public.

Major_Events.Event: Visit of General Secretary Xi Jinping
Major_Events.Description: General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party Xi Jinping visited the palace during his trip to Saudi Arabia.

Major_Events.Event: Dinner with US President Donald Trump
Major_Events.Description: US President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump attended a dinner organized by King Salman at the palace.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace reflects Najdi architecture with features like solid masses, covered streets, and courtyards. It is a complex of residential buildings, service facilities, and the diwan of the king, surrounded by a courtyard and a huge brick wall with nine gates. The building is cubic in shape, made of bricks, indigenous stones, tamarisk trunk, and palm-leaf stalks. The walls are straw-reinforced adobe with engraved ornaments, and the ceiling is supported by local acacia wood beams decorated with geometric patterns.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Murabba Palace is culturally significant as it was the residence and court of King Abdulaziz, the founder of modern Saudi Arabia. It introduced several modern technologies to the region and represents the architectural and urban patterns of Najd. The palace is now a museum preserving the history and heritage of Saudi Arabia.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is part of the King Abdulaziz Historical Center. It includes a memorial hall, a photographic archive center, and exhibits of historic garments and crafts. The ground floor houses guards' rooms and storage areas, while the upper floor contains salons and waiting rooms for visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Fleckenstein
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Château de Fleckenstein is a ruined castle built on a sandstone summit in the Middle Ages. It was owned by the Fleckenstein family until 1720, then passed to the Vitzthum d'Egersberg family, and later to private owners before becoming state property in 1919. The castle was modified and modernized multiple times, captured by French troops in the 17th century, and destroyed in 1689. Restoration work occurred after 1870, around 1908, and since 1958.

Major_Events.Event: Capture by French troops under Marshall Vauban
Major_Events.Description: The castle was captured without resistance from the defenders.
The castle was completely destroyed.
The castle was designated as a historical monument by the French Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in the shape of a 52 m long boat, the castle features a sandstone structure with a rainwater collection system, cistern, and hoist. Remains include Romanesque steps, troglodyte rooms, and a well tower dating from the 13th or 14th century. The stairwell tower is decorated with the arms of Friedrich von Fleckenstein and his wife.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a significant historical site due to its long history, unique architecture, and role in regional conflicts. It reflects medieval construction techniques and the feudal system of the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Fortress and residence of the Fleckenstein family.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is located near the French-German border, accessible by road or hiking trails. It has undergone multiple restorations and is a popular historical site.

world knowledge.Name: Itsukushima Shrine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Itsukushima Shrine is a Shinto shrine on the island of Itsukushima (Miyajima), known for its 'floating' torii. It was established as a significant religious site during the Heian period, with major contributions from Taira no Kiyomori in 1168. The shrine has undergone several reconstructions, including by Mōri Motonari in 1571. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

Major_Events.Description: The first torii was erected by Saeki Kuramoto during the reign of Empress Suiko.

Major_Events.Event: Major renovation by Taira no Kiyomori
Major_Events.Description: Taira no Kiyomori, a prominent noble, heavily contributed to the shrine's construction during his time as governor of Aki Province.

Major_Events.Event: Rebuilding of the honden by Mōri Motonari
Major_Events.Description: Mōri Motonari, lord of Chōshū Domain, rebuilt the honden after violating the island's sacred purity by battling there in 1555.
The shrine was severely damaged by Typhoon Songda, leading to temporary closure for repairs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shrine is built in the Shinden-zukuri style, with pier-like structures over the water to create the illusion of floating. The main hall (honden) is an eight-by-four bay structure with a cypress bark roof, white stucco walls, and vermilion woodwork. The iconic 50-foot vermilion torii gate is made of decay-resistant camphor wood and reflects the Ryōbu Shintō style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Itsukushima Shrine is one of Japan's most iconic Shinto shrines and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is renowned for its 'floating' torii, sacred island setting, and association with the Taira clan. The shrine embodies the harmony between architecture and nature, a key aspect of Japanese aesthetics.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Shinto shrine dedicated to the three daughters of Susano-o no Mikoto, goddesses of seas and storms.
world knowledge.Details: The shrine complex includes the Honsha shrine, Sessha Marodo-jinja, and 17 other structures. It houses treasures like the Heike Nōkyō sutras. The island is considered sacred, and strict purity rules prohibit births, deaths, and burials on it. The shrine is a popular tourist attraction, with an entrance fee of 300 yen.

world knowledge.Name: Château Frontenac
world knowledge.Area: Old Quebec, Quebec City, Quebec, Canada
world knowledge.Address: 1, rue des Carrières, Quebec City, Quebec G1R 4P5
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fairmont Le Château Frontenac, commonly referred to as the Château Frontenac, is a historic hotel in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada. The hotel is situated in Old Quebec, within the historic district's Upper Town, on the southern side of Place d'Armes. The Château Frontenac was designed by Bruce Price, and was built by the Canadian Pacific Railway company. The hotel is managed by Fairmont Hotels and Resorts. Opened in 1893, the Châteauesque-styled building has 18 floors; its 79.9-metre (262-foot) height is augmented by its 54-metre (177-foot) ground elevation. It is one of the first completed grand railway hotels, and was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981. The hotel was expanded on three occasions, with the last major expansion taking place in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: During this conference, officials including American President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Sir Winston Churchill, and Canadian Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King, discussed strategy for World War II.

During this conference, officials including American President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Sir Winston Churchill, and Canadian Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King, discussed strategy for World War II.
This hotel was used as the filming location for the final scene in Alfred Hitchcock's film I Confess, featuring Montgomery Clift and Anne Baxter.
The hotel saw another expansion, with the addition of the new wing that included a pool, fitness centre, and outdoor terrace.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Châteauesque architectural style used throughout the hotel would later serve as a template for other Canadian grand railway hotels erected in the late-19th to early-20th century. The central fortress-like tower design is derived from medieval châteaux found throughout France's Loire Valley. Châteauesque elements include the hotel's asymmetrical profile, with steeply pitched roofs, massive circular and polygonal towers and turrets, ornate gables and dormers, and tall chimneys. The exterior base of the hotel is largely made of grey stone ashlar, with steel framing running up the building, Glenboig brick cladding. Materials that make up the interior of the building includes mahogany panelling, marble staircases, carved stone, wrought iron, and glass roundels. However, as opposed to the other Châteauesque-styled buildings found in France, the Château Frontenac did not utilize elements of Italianate architecture, instead placing a greater emphasis on Gothic elements. The hotel also draws certain elements from Victorian style of architecture, with rich polychromatic surfaces throughout its exterior.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château Frontenac is one of Canada's grand railway hotels built by the Canadian Pacific Railway. The Châteauesque architectural style used throughout the hotel would later serve as a template for other Canadian grand railway hotels erected in the late-19th to early-20th century. The hotel was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981.
world knowledge.Details: The Château Frontenac includes 610 guest rooms and suites spread throughout the hotel building. Eight executive suites were renovated into specialty 'themed rooms'. Most of the suites are themed to the heads of state and government that have visited the hotel, such as the Trudeau-Trudeau Suite, named after two Canadian Prime Ministers, Pierre Elliott Trudeau, and Justin Trudeau. The Churchill Suite and Roosevelt Suite are two suites named after attendees of the First and Second Quebec Conferences, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and American President Franklin D. Roosevelt, respectively. Other suites themed in honour of world leaders include the Charles de Gaulle, named after the former President of France, and the Elizabeth II, named for the former Queen of Canada. Aside from world leaders, the hotel also offers suites themed to Alfred Hitchcock, a director who filmed much of I Confess at the hotel; William Cornelius Van Horne, the second President of the Canadian Pacific Railway; and Celine Dion. The Celine Dion Heritage Suite utilizes an Art Deco style throughout the suite, decorated with images from Dion's family photographer. A number of rooms at the Château Frontenac are also occupied by restaurants and other food-based services. As of 2018, three restaurants operate within the hotel: 1608 Wine and Cheese Bar, Bistro Le Sam, and Champlain. As a part of Fairmont Hotels and Resorts' larger 'Bee Sustainable' program, the Château Frontenac hosts four queen honey bees in hives on the hotel's rooftop garden. The honey is harvested three times a year and is used by the hotel's restaurants. The hotel has nearly 70,000 honey bees producing 295 kilograms (650 lb) of honey per year. The hotel's rooftop apiary also operates a pollinator hotel. The Château was the recipient of the 2022 Global Hotel of the Year Award.

world knowledge.Name: Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Makhonjwa Mountains are a range of small mountains and hills known for having some of the oldest exposed rocks on Earth, estimated to be between 3.2 and 3.6 billion years old. The area has yielded some of the oldest undisputed signs of life on Earth and provides insight into the Precambrian environment. Gold was discovered in the area in the late 19th century, leading to a gold rush and the founding of Barberton. The region was designated a World Heritage Site in 2018.

Major_Events.Description: Gold was discovered near Kaapsehoop, leading to a gold rush in 1884 and the founding of Barberton.
The Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Scientists reported evidence of the largest terrestrial meteor impact event to date, estimated to have occurred about 3.26 billion years ago.
Extraterrestrial organic materials were found in 3.3-billion-year-old volcanic rocks at the Makhonjwa Mountains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The area consists of rocky hills, moist grassy uplands, and forested valleys. It contains some of the oldest exposed rocks on Earth, including komatiites, an unusual type of ultramafic volcanic rock.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Makhonjwa Mountains are culturally and historically significant due to their extreme age and exceptional preservation, providing insight into early life on Earth. They are also known as the 'Genesis of life' and are a key site for geological and paleontological research.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural heritage site, geological research, and tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The mountains lie on the eastern edge of the Kaapvaal craton and cover an area of 120 by 60 kilometres, with altitudes ranging from 600 to 1,800 metres above sea level. The region has a mean annual precipitation of 600–1,150 millimetres, with wet summers and dry winters. Mining was historically significant, but current activities include timber harvesting and grazing. Commercial plantations grow pine and eucalyptus.

world knowledge.Name: Hopewell Rocks
world knowledge.Area: Bay of Fundy, New Brunswick, Canada
world knowledge.Address: Hopewell Rocks Provincial Park, Hopewell Cape, New Brunswick, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hopewell Rocks, also known as the Flowerpot Rocks, are rock formations caused by tidal erosion in the Hopewell Rocks Ocean Tidal Exploration Site at the Hopewell Rocks Provincial Park. These formations consist of red-brown sedimentary conglomerate, sandstone, and minor mudstone rock from the Carboniferous Hopewell Cape Formation. The retreat of glaciers and the large volume of water in the Bay of Fundy have significantly shaped these formations.

Major_Events.Description: On March 14, 2016, a part of Elephant Rock collapsed, with approximately 100 to 200 tonnes of rock falling to the ground, closing off a passageway.
A similar formation collapsed at the nearby Fundy Trail Parkway on February 24, 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The formations are sea stacks caused by tidal erosion, consisting of red-brown sedimentary conglomerate, sandstone, and minor mudstone rock. The erosion has resulted in their unusual shapes, with the base eroded faster than the tops.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hopewell Rocks are a significant natural landmark due to their unique formation and the extreme tidal range of the Bay of Fundy, which is one of the highest in the world. They are a popular tourist attraction and a site of geological interest.
world knowledge.Details: Visitors are advised to stay for a full tidal cycle to fully appreciate the tides and formations. The high tide can reach up to 16 metres (52 ft), making it one of the highest average tides in the world. The area supports a variety of biological productivity, and various shorebirds are often seen flocking to nest and feed in the area.

world knowledge.Name: Naasa Hablood
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Naasa Hablood, also known as Two Breasts Mountain, are twin hills made up of granite and sand. They are named for their distinctive conical shape resembling breast buds.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Granite and sand formations with a conical shape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The hills are a notable natural landmark in Somalia, recognized for their unique shape and cultural naming.
world knowledge.Details: Located on the outskirts of Hargeisa, they are a popular hiking destination.

world knowledge.Name: Newmills Corn and Flax Mills
world knowledge.Location: R250, Churchill road, beside Newmills Bridge on the south bank of the River Swilly, 5 kilometres west of Letterkenny in the small town of Milltown
world knowledge.Address: R250, Churchill road, Milltown, County Donegal, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Newmills Corn and Flax Mills is a grain mill located in County Donegal, Ireland. It features one of the largest operating waterwheels in the country. The millrace is 1 km long and powers two separate millheels, one for grinding oats and barley and the other for flax. The mills have been in operation since the early 19th century and were owned by various individuals, including Joseph Hunter, John Devine, and Patrick Gallagher. The mills were purchased by the state in 1986 for preservation as a national monument and were restored in 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The mills were purchased by the state for preservation as a national monument.
A group of Irish and international volunteers restored the mills and millrace under the direction of the Office of Public Works.
Patrick Gallagher made extensive improvements to the corn mill, including fitting the waterwheel present today and improving the machinery within the mill.
During the Second World War, P.F. Gallagher took advantage of the revival of the flax industry when the British Government offered grants to increase the production of flax.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mill is a three-storey building powered by a 7.63-metre waterwheel manufactured by J. Stevenson's Strabane Foundry in 1867. The waterwheel turns at three revolutions a minute, generating eight horsepower. The building also houses a kiln for drying grain. The milling process is highly mechanised, using hoists, belts, pulleys, and elevators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Newmills Corn and Flax Mills is recognised as the best example of a mill complex in County Donegal. It played a significant role in the local farming economy and was an important part of the industrial heritage of the region. The mills were preserved as a national monument due to their historical and cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The original family home, shop, and pub still on the grounds are also owned by the National Monuments Section of the Office of Public Works and are presently undergoing renovation.

world knowledge.Name: Laxey Wheel
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Diameter: 72 feet 6 inches (22.10 m), Width: 6 feet (1.8 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Laxey Wheel, also known as Lady Isabella, is the largest surviving original working waterwheel in the world. It was built in 1854 to pump water from the Glen Mooar part of the Great Laxey Mines industrial complex. Named after the wife of Lieutenant Governor Charles Hope, it was maintained by Manx National Heritage as part of the Great Laxey Wheel & Mines Trail. The mine employed over 600 miners at its peak, producing lead, copper, silver, and zinc until it closed in 1929. The Manx Government bought the wheel and site in 1965, restored it, and placed it under the control of Manx National Heritage in 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The wheel was built to pump water from the Glen Mooar part of the Great Laxey Mines industrial complex.
The Great Laxey Mines, which employed over 600 miners, closed.
The Manx Government bought the wheel and site.
The wheel was restored and placed under the control of Manx National Heritage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian style water wheel with a diameter of 72 feet 6 inches (22.10 m) and a width of 6 feet (1.8 m). It is a backshot wheel, primarily made of wood with key mechanical parts made of metal. The wheel features a closed pipe system that collects water from local springs and streams, causing the wheel to rotate in a 'reverse' direction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Laxey Wheel is culturally significant as the largest surviving original working waterwheel in the world. It represents the industrial heritage of the Isle of Man and is a symbol of the island's mining history. It also features on the reverse of the £20 notes issued by the Isle of Man Government.
world knowledge.Details: The wheel has two pieces of music dedicated to it: one penned by Stuart Slack and the other by Helen Barley, both entitled 'The Laxey Wheel'. It revolves approximately three times per minute and is part of the Great Laxey Wheel & Mines Trail.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Montlhéry
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Montlhéry is a castle with ruins dating from various periods, most notably the 10th, 11th, 13th, and 14th centuries. The present 13th-century castle succeeded earlier structures. It has a rectilinear pentagonal plan with five surviving towers, one of which serves as the keep. The castle was connected to scientific experiments by notable figures like Pierre Gassendi, Claude Chappe, and Alfred Cornu.

Major_Events.Event: Measurement of the speed of sound
Major_Events.Description: Pierre Gassendi conducted experiments related to the speed of sound at the castle.
Claude Chappe performed experiments with optical telegraphy at the castle.

Major_Events.Event: Measurement of the speed of light
Major_Events.Description: Alfred Cornu measured the speed of light at the castle.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle features a rectilinear pentagonal plan with five surviving towers, one of which is a prominent keep. A gate tower protected the entrance, and there may have been a second court or bailey extending in front of the gate, as well as a chapel inside the lower court.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is historically significant due to its long construction history and its role in scientific experiments. It has been listed as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture since 1840.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic site and former defensive structure
world knowledge.Details: Visitors today can see the keep, the well, the moat, and the remains of the curtain wall. The castle is state property and has been listed as a monument historique since 1840.

world knowledge.Name: Gaza Seaport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gaza Seaport is a planned seaport in the Gaza Strip, first mentioned in the Oslo I Accord in 1993. Construction began in July 2000 but was halted due to the Second Intifada and Israeli military actions. The 2005 Agreement on Movement and Access re-announced the project, but construction has not resumed as of 2014. In 2024, a temporary port was proposed by the U.S. to facilitate humanitarian aid.

Major_Events.Description: Announced the establishment of a Gaza Sea Port Area.
Determined that construction could commence on 1 October 1999.
Construction began on 18 July 2000.
Construction was halted due to the Second Intifada and Israeli military actions.
Re-announced the start of the seaport construction.
President Joe Biden announced a plan for the U.S. military to construct a temporary port on the Gaza Coast for humanitarian aid.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gaza Seaport is significant as a symbol of Palestinian sovereignty and economic independence. Its construction and operation have been central to various peace agreements and international negotiations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seaport for commerce and humanitarian aid
world knowledge.Details: The project has faced numerous obstacles, including political disputes, Israeli military actions, and funding issues. The temporary port proposed in 2024 aims to address humanitarian concerns during the Israel–Hamas War.

world knowledge.Name: Đông Ba Market
world knowledge.Address: Trần Hưng Đạo Road, Huế, Thừa Thiên Huế province, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Đông Ba Market, with a history of over a hundred years, is a traditional market in Huế, Vietnam. Originally located outside the Eastern Gate of the citadel, it was known as "Quy Giả market". After being burnt down in 1885, it was rebuilt in 1887 by Emperor Đồng Khánh. In 1899, Emperor Thành Thái ordered its reconstruction at its current location. The market has undergone several renovations, including major ones in 1967 and 1987.

Major_Events.Event: Battle of the Huế Imperial City
Major_Events.Description: The market was completely burnt down.
The market was rebuilt after being burnt down.
The market was reconstructed at its current location as part of Huế city's urban planning.
The market was demolished and rebuilt, but the construction was incomplete due to the Tet Offensive.
A major renovation took place to keep the market operating.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The market originally had 48 roofed stalls and a well for water supply. It has undergone several renovations, maintaining its traditional market structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Đông Ba Market is a landmark of the former capital city of Vietnam and represents the traditional market culture of Huế. It is a popular local market and a significant part of the city's history and daily life.
world knowledge.Details: The market sells a variety of goods, from fresh produce and fish to clothing, toys, shoes, and handicrafts. It is busiest in the early morning but remains open all day.

world knowledge.Name: Haghpat Monastery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Haghpat Monastery, also known as Haghpatavank, is a medieval Armenian monastery complex built between the 10th and 13th century.
