It was founded by Queen Khosrovanuysh, wife of the Bagratid king Ashot III, probably in 976. The monastery was strategically located to overlook the Debed River and afford protection and concealment. It has been damaged by earthquakes and armed attacks but remains largely intact.

Major_Events.Description: Prosh Khaghbakian led a force of Georgians and Armenians to support Mongol troops in the siege. The city was captured after two years, and Christian relics, including the hand of the Apostle St Bartholomew, were brought to Haghpat Monastery.
An earthquake destroyed parts of the monastery, which were not restored until fifty years later.
Haghpat Monastery, together with Sanahin Monastery, was placed on UNESCO's World Heritage List for representing the highest flowering of Armenian religious architecture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery features Armenian architectural style with a central dome resting on four imposing pillars. The outside walls have triangular recesses, and the complex includes several churches, chapels, a belltower, a library, and a refectory. The Cathedral of Surb Nshan is a typical example of tenth-century Armenian architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Haghpat Monastery is a masterpiece of religious architecture and a major center of learning in the Middle Ages. It represents the blending of Byzantine ecclesiastical architecture and traditional vernacular architecture of the Caucasian region.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery is surrounded by hamlets and features several khachkars (cross-stones), including the 'Amenaprkich' khachkar from 1273. It is an increasingly popular tourist site.

world knowledge.Name: Dieng Plateau
world knowledge.Address: Banjarnegara Regency and Wonosobo Regency, Central Java, Indonesia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 6 km north to south and 14 km west to east
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dieng Plateau is a volcanic plateau in Central Java, Indonesia, known for its ancient Hindu temples dating back to the Mataram Kingdom era. The plateau was a significant religious center for Hinduism, particularly for the worship of Shiva. The area is characterized by its high elevation, fertile land, and unique subtropical climate. The plateau's name derives from Old Javanese, meaning 'place of the ancestors' or 'place where the gods reside.'

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of temples by Thomas Stamford Raffles
Major_Events.Description: Thomas Stamford Raffles, during his tenure as Governor of the Dutch East Indies, visited Dieng and reported the discovery of around 400 ancient temples and archaeological sites.

Major_Events.Event: Reactivation of water channel by J. Kinsbergen
Major_Events.Description: J. Kinsbergen reactivated the water channel called Gangsiran Aswatama and excavated several archaeological remains in Dieng.

Major_Events.Event: Archaeological research by H. L. Melville
Major_Events.Description: H. L. Melville conducted extensive research on the Dieng plateau, leading to the documentation of 104 archaeological findings, including temple structures and loose artifacts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temples in Dieng are among the oldest known stone structures in Java, with influences from South Indian architecture. The temples are grouped into three clusters: Arjuna, Dwarawati, and Gatotkaca, with the Bima temple standing separately. The structures are predominantly dedicated to the worship of Shiva, evidenced by the presence of phallus, yoni, statues, and inscriptions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dieng Plateau is culturally significant as a former religious center for Hinduism, particularly for the worship of Shiva. The plateau's high elevation and fertile land made it an ideal location for sacred buildings, reflecting the ancient Javanese belief in the connection between the earth and the divine. The temples and archaeological remains provide valuable insights into the religious practices and architectural styles of the Mataram Kingdom.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious site and place of worship
world knowledge.Details: Dieng Plateau is the highest plateau on the island of Java, with an average elevation of over 2,100 meters above sea level. The area is known for its cold climate, with temperatures occasionally dropping below freezing, a phenomenon known as Bun Upas. The plateau is also a significant producer of potatoes in Indonesia and has geothermal energy resources used for power generation. The region is surrounded by volcanic complexes, with some craters still active today.

world knowledge.Name: Souq Waqif
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Souq Waqif is a historic marketplace in Doha, Qatar, dating back to the late 19th to early 20th centuries. It was a central trading hub for Bedouins and locals, primarily dealing in livestock. The souq underwent a significant restoration in 2006 after a fire in 2003, preserving its traditional Qatari architecture.

Major_Events.Description: A fire destroyed most of the souq, leading to a government-led restoration project.
The restoration of Souq Waqif was completed, preserving its historical and architectural identity.
An event featuring WWE wrestlers that attracted a large number of spectators.
The souq saw a significant increase in tourism as fans gathered to celebrate and support their teams.
The souq became a gathering place for fans from various nationalities, celebrating with chants and national flags.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Traditional Qatari architecture with buildings refurbished to maintain historical authenticity. Traditional heating methods using wood and bamboo from Asia are employed.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Souq Waqif is a cultural and historical landmark in Qatar, representing traditional Qatari commerce and architecture. It serves as a tourist attraction and a hub for cultural events and festivals.
world knowledge.Details: Souq Waqif includes a variety of shops selling traditional garments, spices, handicrafts, and souvenirs. It also features restaurants, shisha lounges, pet stalls, and a falcon souq. The souq is home to the first hotel in Qatar, Bismillah, and a 980-seat indoor theatre known as Al Rayyan Theatre.

world knowledge.Name: Convento de San Marcos
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Convento de San Marcos was originally a 12th-century convent and hospital for pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago. It served as the main residence for the Order of Santiago in the Kingdom of León. The medieval building was demolished in the 16th century due to poor condition, and a new structure was built with funding from Ferdinand the Catholic. The building underwent significant expansions and renovations over the centuries, including during the Spanish Civil War when it was used as a concentration camp. Today, it operates as a luxury parador hotel, church, and museum.

Major_Events.Description: The Infanta Sancha of Castile donated funds to construct a modest building for pilgrims and the poor.
The medieval building was demolished, and a new structure was commissioned by Ferdinand the Catholic.
The building was used as a concentration camp, housing up to 7,000 prisoners at a time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features a highly ornamental plateresque facade. The main facade was constructed in the 16th century, with expansions in the 18th century that mimicked the original design. Key architects included Juan Orozco (church), Martin Villarreal (front facade), and Juan de Badajoz el Mozo (cloister and sacristy).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Convento de San Marcos is one of the most important Renaissance monuments in Spain and a key architectural jewel of León. It played a significant role in the Camino de Santiago and served as the main residence for the Order of Santiago. Its history as a concentration camp during the Spanish Civil War adds to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: Today, the Convento de San Marcos is part of the state-owned Paradores chain and remains a significant stop on the Camino de Santiago. It includes a consecrated church and a museum.

world knowledge.Name: Château du Tournel
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château du Tournel is a ruined feudal castle that was the former seat of the Barons of Tournel, one of the eight baronies of Gévaudan. It was destroyed during the French Wars of Religion by Huguenot troops under Matthieu Merle. The castle was built on a rocky outcrop dominating the upper valley of the Lot and served as a strategic possession for the Tournel family. It was abandoned after the wars and has been maintained since the 20th century.

Major_Events.Event: Destruction during the French Wars of Religion
Major_Events.Description: The castle was destroyed for the first time during the French Wars of Religion by Huguenot troops under Matthieu Merle.

Major_Events.Year: After the French Wars of Religion
Major_Events.Description: The castle was completely abandoned without being restored after the wars.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle was composed of six towers and was built on a rocky outcrop. It had seven entrances and passages close to the cliff, making it a well-defended site.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château du Tournel was a significant feudal castle and the seat of the Barons of Tournel. It played a strategic role in medieval Gévaudan and is now a historic site with an explanatory trail for visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The castle appeared on the record sleeve of Chant des Partisans by Yves Montand in 1955. It was featured in the 2005 film Saint-Jacques... La Mecque and the 2008 season of the French TV show Hero Corp.

world knowledge.Name: Bellapais Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bellapais Abbey is the ruin of a monastery built by Canons Regular in the 13th century on the northern side of the small village of Bellapais, now in Turkish-controlled Northern Cyprus. It was originally founded by Aimery de Lusignan and was consecrated as the Abbey of St. Mary of the Mountain. The site has served various roles, including as a residence for the Bishop of Kyrenia, a place of refuge from Arab raids, and later as a museum and concert venue.

Major_Events.Description: The monastery was founded by Aimery de Lusignan and consecrated as the Abbey of St. Mary of the Mountain.
The Genoese raided Kyrenia, stripping Bellapais Abbey of anything portable and of value.
Following the Ottoman conquest of Kyrenia, the Premonstratensians were expelled, and the abbey was given to the Greek Orthodox Church of Cyprus.
During British control of Cyprus, the British Army used the abbey's refectory as a hospital and later undertook repairs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey consists of a church and a cloister, with monastic buildings surrounding the cloister. The church, dating to the 13th century, is the best-preserved part of the complex, featuring Gothic design elements, intricate carvings, and Italian murals. The refectory is noted for its Gothic design, pulpit, and windows offering views of the countryside.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bellapais Abbey is culturally significant as a historical religious site that reflects the architectural and religious history of Cyprus. It has served as a place of worship, refuge, and cultural events, and it is a key example of Gothic architecture in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The site is also a museum, hosting a restaurant and a cafe. The Abbey's refectory serves as a venue for concerts and lectures. The abbey features a fortified gate, a church with a flat roof and belfry, a cloister with 18 arches, and a Gothic refectory. The chapter house contains a Gothic stone carving, and the canons' cells were located above the chapter house and undercroft.

world knowledge.Name: Telemark Canal
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 105 kilometres (65 mi) long, 72 metres (236 ft) elevation difference
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Telemark Canal connects the towns Skien and Dalen in southern Norway by linking several long lakes in the Skien watershed through a series of 18 locks. It originally consisted of two canals: the Norsjø–Skien Canal, built in 1854–1861, and the Bandak–Norsjø Canal, opened in 1892. The canal was mainly built for transport of goods and passengers, log floating, and to prevent flooding. It was seen as "the eighth wonder" in Europe at the time it was finished.

Major_Events.Description: The Bandak–Norsjø Canal was opened by the Minister of Labour Hans Hein Theodor Nysom.
The canal was selected as the millennium site for Telemark county.
The Bandak-Norsjø Canal was made a National Cultural Heritage in June 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The canal consists of 18 locks, with the biggest staircase lock being Vrangfoss, which has five chambers and a lifting height of 23 metres (75 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Telemark Canal is culturally significant as it was seen as "the eighth wonder" in Europe at the time of its completion. It was selected as the millennium site for Telemark county and was featured in the Telemarkskanalen – minutt for minutt slow television documentary in 2012. The Bandak-Norsjø Canal was designated a National Cultural Heritage in 2017.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transport of goods and passengers, log floating, flood prevention, and tourism
world knowledge.Details: The riverboats Henrik Ibsen and Victoria travel with tourists from Skien to Dalen via Kviteseid. Victoria has traveled the Norsjø–Skien Canal since 1882, and the Bandak–Norsjø Canal since its opening. There are 18 lock chambers at 8 different locations.

world knowledge.Name: Tomb of Esther and Mordechai
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tomb of Esther and Mordechai is a mausoleum in Hamadan, Iran, believed by Iranian Jews and Christians to house the remains of the biblical Queen Esther and her cousin Mordechai. It is a significant pilgrimage site for Jews and Christians in Iran. The structure is thought to date back to the 1600s, with some evidence suggesting earlier origins. The site has been a focal point of Jewish tradition in Iran, though its historical accuracy is debated. It has undergone various restorations and has been the subject of multiple historical accounts and legends.

Major_Events.Description: The tomb, along with other religious sites, was targeted in an arson attack, causing minimal damage and smoke damage. The incident was condemned by Jewish organizations worldwide, but the Iranian government did not respond to calls for an investigation.
The tombs were desecrated during the Israel-Hamas conflict in Gaza.
Following the Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus, the shrine was attacked with Molotov cocktails, resulting in minor damage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tomb consists of an outer and inner chamber surmounted by a dome approximately 15 meters high. The dome was once covered with blue tiles, most of which have fallen away. The structure includes inscriptions and oaken coffins with historical texts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tomb is the most important pilgrimage site for Jews and Christians in Iran, believed to house the remains of Queen Esther and Mordechai. It holds significant religious and historical importance for the Iranian Jewish community.
world knowledge.Details: The site has been the subject of various historical and archaeological debates, with some scholars suggesting it may be the tomb of Shushandukht, a Jewish consort of the Sasanian king Yazdegerd I. Local legend claims a pit between the tombs leads directly to Jerusalem. The tomb has faced multiple attacks and desecrations, particularly in the context of regional conflicts.

world knowledge.Name: Hell Cave
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hell Cave (Slovene: Jama Pekel) is a karst cave in the settlement of Zalog pri Šempetru in Slovenia. The cave's dark, black entrance inspired the idea that the Devil lived inside. Other stories of the name's origin say that one of the rocks near the entrance was thought to look like the Devil or that warm water vapour drifting from the cave in the winter had an eerie effect. The cave is more than three million years old. Finds of human bones in the cave prove that the cave was used as a shelter by early inhabitants of Europe. Wooden footbridges were set up in the cave in 1860, making it accessible to visitors. The cave became better known between 1860 and 1870, when it was explored by Anton Franz Reibenschuh, a professor from Graz. It was also explored at the end of the 19th century by Ivan Kač, a municipal secretary in Žalec. The speleologist Anton Suwa died in the cave in 1969. In 1972 the cave was opened to the public and it was visited by 25,000 people the following year. It has been managed by the local tourist association since 1972.

Major_Events.Description: Wooden footbridges were set up in the cave, making it accessible to visitors.
The cave became better known when it was explored by Anton Franz Reibenschuh, a professor from Graz.
The cave was explored by Ivan Kač, a municipal secretary in Žalec.
The speleologist Anton Suwa died in the cave.
The cave was opened to the public and visited by 25,000 people the following year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cave is 1,159 m long and has two levels. Peklenščica Creek runs through the caverns of the lower part of the cave and comes bursting out of a siphon as the highest-elevation accessible subterranean waterfall in Slovenia. The upper part of the cave is dry, but full of cave formations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cave's name and dark entrance have inspired local folklore, associating it with the Devil. It has been a significant shelter for early inhabitants of Europe and is now a notable tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The cave is more than three million years old. It has been managed by the local tourist association since 1972.

world knowledge.Name: Santiago General Cemetery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Santiago General Cemetery was established in 1821 after Chile's independence. Bernardo O'Higgins set aside more than 85 hectares of land for its foundation. It is one of the largest cemeteries in Latin America with an estimated two million burials. The cemetery is filled with ornate mausoleums, lush gardens, and numerous sculptures.

Major_Events.Description: The cemetery was established after Chile's independence, with Bernardo O'Higgins inaugurating the Alameda de las Delicias and setting aside land for the cemetery.

Major_Events.Event: Exhumation and reburial of Salvador Allende
Major_Events.Description: Salvador Allende's remains were exhumed from the Santa Ines cemetery and transported in a solemn procession to the Santiago General Cemetery following democratic changes in Chile.
The historical portion of the cemetery was designated as a national monument.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cemetery features ornate mausoleums, lush gardens, and numerous sculptures. The main entrance is crowned by a dome and preceded by the Plaza La Paz, which has a monument dedicated to the people who died in the Church of the Company Fire.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Santiago General Cemetery is the final resting place for many influential people in Chile, including most of the deceased Presidents. It also has a memorial to the people who were 'disappeared' during the dictatorship of Augusto Pinochet.
world knowledge.Details: The cemetery serves as a true urban park for Santiago and can be accessed via Cementerios metro station. It is one of the largest cemeteries in Latin America with an estimated two million burials.

world knowledge.Name: Villa Savoye
world knowledge.Address: 82, Rue de Villiers 78300 Poissy, Yvelines, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Villa Savoye is a modernist villa designed by Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier and his cousin Pierre Jeanneret. Built as a country retreat for the Savoye family, it exemplifies Le Corbusier's 'five points' of architecture and is a landmark of the International style. After surviving proposals for demolition, it was designated a French historical monument in 1965 and later restored. In 2016, it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier.'

Major_Events.Description: The villa was completed but not habitable until 1931 due to design changes and construction issues.
Occupied first by Germans (used as a hay store) and later by Americans, causing severe damage.
Became France's first modernist building to be designated a historical monument.
Inscribed as part of 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier.'

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Reinforced concrete structure embodying Le Corbusier's 'Five Points': pilotis (elevated supports), free floor plan, horizontal ribbon windows, free façade design, and roof garden. Features a ramp leading to a solarium, curved glazing for car access, and golden section proportions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A seminal work of modern architecture, Villa Savoye represents the International style and Le Corbusier's architectural principles. Its influence is global, and it is studied as a benchmark for modernist design.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country retreat; now a museum open to visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The villa faced structural and leakage issues due to its experimental design. Restorations occurred in 1963-1997. It inspired replicas worldwide, including a black version in Canberra, Australia. Le Corbusier's last 'white villa,' marking the end of an architectural phase.

world knowledge.Name: Zuma Rock
world knowledge.Address: Madalla, Suleja Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,125 m (3,691 ft) elevation, 300 m (980 ft) prominence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zuma Rock is a large natural monolith composed of gabbro and granodiorite, located in Niger State, Nigeria. It was used for a defensive retreat by the Gbagyi people against invading tribes during intertribal wars. The rock was found in the 15th century by the Zuba people, who called it 'zumwa', meaning 'a place of guinea fowls'. It holds profound spiritual significance for the Gwari people, who believe it to be a protective deity. The rock is also depicted on the 100 naira note.

Major_Events.Event: Defensive retreat by the Gbagyi people
Major_Events.Description: Used as a defensive retreat by the Gbagyi people against invading neighbouring tribes during intertribal wars.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by District Officer of Abuja
Major_Events.Description: The District Officer of Abuja, the Sarkin Malamai, and Sulaimanu Barau visited the rock and the fetish village to investigate local legends and myths surrounding the rock.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Large natural monolith composed of gabbro and granodiorite, rising approximately 300 metres above its surroundings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zuma Rock is culturally and spiritually significant to the Gwari and Koro people, who believe it to be a protective deity with healing powers. It is also a symbol of Nigerian geography and heritage, depicted on the 100 naira note.
world knowledge.Details: Zuma Rock is steeped in local folklore and legends, with some natives believing it to be inhabited by unseen evil spirits or used as a den for ritualists. Nearby is an uncompleted Zuma Rock Hotel, believed by some to be haunted. The rock continues to be a site of mystery and cultural importance.

world knowledge.Name: Santa Cueva de Covadonga
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Santa Cueva de Covadonga is a Catholic sanctuary located in the Picos de Europa mountains in Asturias, northern Spain. It is dedicated to the Virgin of Covadonga and is the site of the first battle of the Reconquista in 718. The cave's origin as a cult site is controversial, with Christian tradition linking it to Pelagius and a hermit venerating the Virgin Mary. The first construction in the cave dates back to the reign of Alfonso I of Asturias, who built a chapel to commemorate Pelagius's victory over the Muslims. The cave was later renovated in the 19th century, and the current chapel is of Romanesque style.

Major_Events.Description: The first battle of the Reconquista took place here, where Pelagius's forces achieved a significant victory against the Muslims.
A fire destroyed the medieval Marian statue, and the current wooden image of the Virgin and Child was donated by the Cathedral of Oviedo in 1778.
Benito Sanz y Forés promoted the renovation of the cave and laid the first stone of the new chapel dedicated to the Virgin.
During the civil war, the Virgin image disappeared and was later found in the Embassy of Spain in France.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cave was initially covered with wood, and the current chapel is of Romanesque style, designed by Luis Menéndez-Pidal and Alvarez.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The shrine of Covadonga is culturally and historically significant as the site of the first battle of the Reconquista and as a major Catholic sanctuary dedicated to the Virgin of Covadonga. It holds a central place in the history of the Kingdom of Asturias and is a symbol of Christian resistance and faith.
world knowledge.Details: The cave is also the burial site of several members of the royal family of Asturias, including Pelagius, whose remains were moved to the Holy Cave of Covadonga by order of Alfonso X of Castile.

world knowledge.Name: Limes Germanicus
world knowledge.Area: Germania Inferior, Germania Superior, and Raetia
world knowledge.Location: From the North Sea outlet of the Rhine to near Regensburg on the Danube
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Limes Germanicus, or 'Germanic Limes', was a line of frontier fortifications that bounded the ancient Roman provinces of Germania Inferior, Germania Superior, and Raetia, dividing the Roman Empire and the unsubdued Germanic tribes. It was constructed using natural boundaries like rivers or earth banks and ditches with wooden palisades and watchtowers. The frontier changed over time due to advances and retreats from external threats. At its height, it stretched from the North Sea outlet of the Rhine to near Regensburg on the Danube. The Limes Germanicus was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2005 (Upper Germanic & Rhaetian Limes) and 2021 (Lower Germanic Limes).

Major_Events.Description: Domitian pushed out from Moguntiacum, extended Roman territory east of it, and enclosed the whole within a systematically delimited and defended frontier.
The remnants of the Upper Germanic & Rhaetian Limes were inscribed on the List of UNESCO World Heritage Sites as Frontiers of the Roman Empire.
The Lower Germanic Limes were inscribed on the World Heritage List.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Limes Germanicus consisted of a natural boundary such as a river or an earth bank and ditch with a wooden palisade and watchtowers at intervals. A system of linked forts was built behind them. The potentially weakest part was the gap between the Rhine and Danube, which was heavily guarded with forts and towers arranged in depth and in multiple layers. The limes itself was a relatively simple construction, similar to the fortification that a travelling troop of Roman soldiers would construct every evening to protect their camp from attacks. It had a deeper ditch and a higher mound than a camp fortification, with stakes or a simple stone wall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Limes Germanicus is culturally and historically important as it represents the frontier of the Roman Empire and the division between the Roman Empire and the unsubdued Germanic tribes. It is a testament to Roman engineering and military strategy, and its remnants provide valuable insights into Roman border defenses and the interactions between the Roman Empire and Germanic tribes.
world knowledge.Details: The Limes Germanicus included at least 60 forts and 900 watchtowers. The Saalburg is a reconstructed fortification and museum of the Limes near Frankfurt. The first emperor who began to build fortifications along the border was Augustus, shortly after the devastating Roman defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest in 9 AD. The Limes Germanicus was never able to prevent whole Germanic tribes from entering the territory of the Roman Empire, but it provided an early warning system, deterrence of casual small-scale raiding, and the ability to counteract attacks while the enemy was still near the border fortresses and garrisons.

world knowledge.Name: Hargeisa War Memorial
world knowledge.Location: Freedom Square, Independence Avenue, Hargeisa, Somaliland
world knowledge.Address: Freedom Square, Independence Avenue, Hargeisa, Somaliland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hargeisa War Memorial is a monument in Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland, set up to commemorate the Somaliland War of Independence. It symbolizes the struggle for the people of Somaliland. The city of Hargeisa suffered extensive destruction during the conflict, with up to 90% of the city destroyed due to aerial bombardment and artillery shelling by the Somali Air Force under the regime of Siad Barre. The memorial is located in Hargeisa's Freedom Square and features a MiG-17 fighter aircraft of the Somali Air Force that crashed nearby.

Major_Events.Description: The Somali Air Force conducted large-scale aerial bombing and artillery shelling of Hargeisa, resulting in the destruction of up to 90% of the city and the displacement of its population.
The Hargeisa War Memorial was rebuilt to a more appealing standard and architecture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The memorial consists of a MiG-17 fighter aircraft of the Somali Air Force, which crashed nearby. The fresco underneath shows a woman holding the flag of Somaliland looking towards the sky in hope.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hargeisa War Memorial is a symbol of the struggle for independence and resilience of the people of Somaliland. It commemorates the victims of the indiscriminate aerial bombardment of the city, part of the Isaaq genocide conducted by the Somali dictator Siad Barre.
world knowledge.Details: The memorial is located in Hargeisa's Freedom Square. In 2020, it was rebuilt to a more appealing standard and architecture.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Afadja
world knowledge.Address: Near the villages of Liati Wote and Gbledi Gbogame, Afadjato South District and Hohoe Municipality, Volta Region, Ghana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Afadja, known as Afadjato to the Ewe people, is one of the highest mountains in Ghana. The name 'Afadja' comes from the Ewe word 'Avadzeto', meaning 'at war with the bush'. The mountain is part of the Agumatsa sub-range of the West Africa Mountains. The Ewe people named it after a war with wild animals and an encounter with an itching plant that prevented them from reaching the summit.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Afadja is culturally significant as it is named after a historical event involving the Ewe people and wild animals. It is also a major tourist attraction in the Volta Region, known for its natural beauty, nearby waterfalls, and diverse flora and fauna.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Afadja is located near the Ghana-Togo border and is part of the Agumatsa Range. The area is known for its lush green mountains, tropical forests, and diverse wildlife, including over 33 species of mammals and 300 butterfly species. Nearby attractions include Tagbo Falls and Wli Falls, the highest waterfall in West Africa.

world knowledge.Name: Lazzaretto of Ancona
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lazzaretto of Ancona, also called the Mole Vanvitelliana, is a pentagonal 18th-century building built on an artificial island as a quarantine station for the port town of Ancona, Italy. It was commissioned by Pope Clement XII and designed by the architect Luigi Vanvitelli. Originally built to house possibly-infected travellers and goods arriving in the port, who had to remain there forty days, it has since taken on various functions including a military citadel and a sugar refinery. Now it is used as a site of the museum Tattile Omero and for various exhibitions.

Major_Events.Description: The site was repurposed as a military citadel.
The site was converted into a sugar refinery.
There was a failed attempt to sabotage the Italian naval resources by 60 infiltrating Habsburg sailors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Lazzaretto of Ancona is a pentagonal building constructed on an artificial island, featuring a central Neoclassical tempietto dedicated to Saint Roch. The design reflects the rationalistic and functional ensemble common to many works of late Enlightenment architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Lazzaretto of Ancona is culturally significant as a historical quarantine station that played a crucial role in managing public health in the 18th century. Its architectural design and varied historical uses make it an important landmark in Italian history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a quarantine station, now a museum and exhibition site
world knowledge.Details: The island is separated from the land by a channel called 'Mandracchio' and was originally connected to the mainland by only one link. It is now connected by three bridges. The building's pentagonal shape and its comparison to contemporary architectural works in Naples, such as the Royal Hospice and Hospital for the Poor and the Cemetery of the 366 Fossae, highlight its unique design and historical context.

world knowledge.Name: National Library of Russia
world knowledge.Address: Corner of Nevsky Avenue and Sadovaya Street
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Library of Russia (NLR), located in Saint Petersburg, is the first and one of three national public libraries in Russia. Established in 1795 by Catherine the Great, it was originally known as the Imperial Public Library. It was based on the Załuski Library, the famous Polish national library built by Bishop Załuski in Warsaw, which had been seized by the Russians in 1794 after the Partitions of Poland. The library has undergone several name changes throughout its history and is currently ranked among the world's major libraries. It has the second biggest library collection in the Russian Federation and serves as the All-Russian Information, Research and Cultural Center.

Major_Events.Description: The Imperial Public Library was established by Catherine the Great.
The Imperial Public Library was inaugurated on 14 January 1814.
The library was renamed the National Library of Russia.
The library remained open during the Siege of Leningrad.
The National Library began a large-scale digitization project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed in a Neoclassical style by architect Yegor Sokolov.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The NLR is a treasury of national heritage and serves as the All-Russian Information, Research and Cultural Center. It has aimed for comprehensive acquisition of the national printed output and has provided free access to its collections.
world knowledge.Details: The National Library of Russia has a collection of 36,475,000 items, including 15,000,000 books. It operates under the Legal Deposit Law and provides free access to its reading rooms. The library has a budget of 569,200,000 RUB ($23,400,000) and employs 1,850 people. It is currently managed by Director Alexander Vershinin.

world knowledge.Name: Mausoleum of Ahmad Shah Durrani
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mausoleum of Ahmad Shah Durrani is one of the most important historical monuments in Kandahar, Afghanistan. Ahmad Shah Durrani, known as Ahmad Shah Baba, ruled the Durrani Empire from Kandahar between 1747 and 1772.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The graceful octagonal monument stands on a basaltic platform, with a plain beige brick exterior decorated with numerous niches of contrasting heights and depths, delicately outlined with yellow and green, green and blue tiles. Tall minarets connected by a floral balustrade top the main body of the monument, and another set of short minarets atop a series of shallow niches outlined in blue surround a drum crowned with a dome of glistening blue tile. The soffits of the main arches are decorated in a honeycomb pattern composed of half circles centered with lapis lazuli and gold to resemble flowers. The interior is richly decorated with gorgeous Afghan carpets on the marble floor and brilliantly painted and gilded floral decoration of the dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mausoleum of Ahmad Shah Durrani is culturally and historically significant as the resting place of Ahmad Shah Durrani, the founder of the Durrani Empire and the modern state of Afghanistan. The site also includes the Friday Mosque with the Shrine of the Cloak, believed to be worn by the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
world knowledge.Details: The sarcophagus is made of Afghan marble and covered with a gold-embroidered cloth of deep wine velvet. Beside it, there is a table holding fine copies of the Quran and a glass cabinet containing a gold-inlaid helmet and gauntlets together with a sceptre inlaid in silver and embellished with a two-headed bird, which Ahmad Shah Durrani used in battle.

world knowledge.Name: Da Lat station
world knowledge.Address: Da Lat, Lâm Đồng Province, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Da Lat station is a railway station on the Da Lat–Thap Cham Railway line in Vietnam, serving the town of Da Lat. Designed in 1932 by French architects Moncet and Reveron, it was opened in 1938. The station was largely unused after the Vietnam War but was partially restored in the 1990s as a tourist attraction. It is notable for its unique architectural style, combining Art Deco with elements of native Cao Nguyen communal houses.

Major_Events.Description: The station was opened, becoming one of the first colonial-style buildings in the area.
The Da Lat–Thap Cham line fell out of use due to bombardments and sabotage.
A 7 km section of the line was restored and returned to active use as a tourist attraction.
The station was recognized as a national historical monument.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the Art Deco style by French architects Moncet and Reveron, the station incorporates high, pointed roofs characteristic of Cao Nguyen communal buildings. The three roofs represent the three peaks of Lang Biang mountain. The station features multicoloured glass windows, a large clock, and a Porte-cochère supported by columns.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Da Lat station is culturally significant for its unique architectural style, blending Art Deco with local Central Highlands elements. It is recognized as a national historical monument and serves as a symbol of the region's colonial and railway history.
world knowledge.Details: The station was designed by French architects Moncet and Reveron and opened in 1938. It was largely unused after the Vietnam War but was partially restored in the 1990s. The station is notable for its Art Deco style with elements of Cao Nguyen communal houses and was recognized as a national historical monument in 2001.

world knowledge.Name: Nurek Dam
world knowledge.Area: Border of Khatlon district and Districts of Republican Subordination
world knowledge.Address: Nurek, Border of Khatlon district and Districts of Republican Subordination, Tajikistan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nurek Dam is an earth-fill embankment dam on the Vakhsh River in Tajikistan, constructed by the Soviet Union between 1961 and 1980. It was the tallest dam in the world at the time of its completion and remains the second tallest man-made dam. Its primary purpose is hydroelectric power generation, and it supplies a significant portion of Tajikistan's electricity.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the Nurek Dam started in 1961.
The power station's first generator was commissioned in 1972.
The last generator was commissioned in 1979.
The entire project was completed in 1980.
The dam's turbines were redesigned and retrofitted to increase capacity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Nurek Dam is uniquely constructed with a central core of cement forming an impermeable barrier within a 300 m (980 ft)-high rock and earth fill construction. The volume of the mound is 54 million m³. It includes nine hydroelectric generating units.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Nurek Dam is culturally and historically significant as a major engineering feat of the Soviet Union and a critical source of hydroelectric power for Tajikistan, meeting a substantial portion of the nation's electricity needs.
world knowledge.Details: The reservoir formed by the Nurek Dam, known simply as Nurek, is the largest reservoir in Tajikistan with a capacity of 10.5 km³. The reservoir is over 70 km (40 mi) in length and is used for irrigation of agricultural land. It is suspected that the reservoir may have caused induced seismicity when being impounded.

world knowledge.Name: Phnom Bakheng
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Phnom Bakheng is a Hindu temple in the form of a temple mountain in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. Dedicated to Shiva, it was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman (889–910). Located atop a hill, it is nowadays a popular tourist spot for sunset views of the much bigger temple Angkor Wat, which lies amid the jungle about 1.5 km to the southeast. The large number of visitors makes Phnom Bakheng one of the most threatened monuments of Angkor. Since 2004, World Monuments Fund has been working to conserve the temple in partnership with APSARA. Phnom Bakheng, built more than two centuries before Angkor Wat, was once the main temple in the Angkor region. It was the central architectural feature of a new capital called Yasodharapura, established by Yasovarman when he moved the court from the old capital, Hariharalaya, in the southeast Roluos area. Later in its history, Phnom Bakheng was converted into a Buddhist temple.

Major_Events.Event: Consecration of the Phnom Bakheng temple
Major_Events.Description: An inscription dated 1052 AD and found at the Sdok Kak Thom temple in present-day Thailand states in Sanskrit: 'When Sri Yasovardhana became king under the name of Yasovarman, the able Vamasiva continued as his guru. By the king's order, he set up a linga on Sri Yasodharagiri, a mountain equal in beauty to the king of mountains.' Scholars believe that this passage refers to the consecration of the Phnom Bakheng temple approximately a century and a half earlier.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Phnom Bakheng is a symbolic representation of Mount Meru, home of the Hindu gods, a status emphasized by the temple's location atop a steep hill 65 m above the surrounding plain. The temple is built in a pyramid form of seven levels, representing the seven heavens. At the top level, five sandstone sanctuaries, in various states of repair, stand in a quincunx pattern—one in the center and one at each corner of the level's square. Originally, 108 small towers were arrayed around the temple at ground level and on various of its tiers; most of them have collapsed. The temple sits on a rectangular base and rises in five levels and is crowned by five main towers. One hundred four smaller towers are distributed over the lower four levels, placed so symmetrically that only 33 can be seen from the center of any side. Thirty-three is the number of gods who dwelt on Mount Meru. Phnom Bakheng's total number of towers is also significant. The center one represents the axis of the world and the 108 smaller ones represent the four lunar phases, each with 27 days. The seven levels of the monument represent the seven heavens and each terrace contains 12 towers which represent the 12-year cycle of Jupiter. According to University of Chicago scholar Paul Wheatley, it is 'an astronomical calendar in stone.'
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Phnom Bakheng is culturally and historically important as it was once the main temple in the Angkor region and the central architectural feature of a new capital called Yasodharapura. It is a symbolic representation of Mount Meru, home of the Hindu gods, and serves as an astronomical calendar in stone. Its conversion into a Buddhist temple later in its history also adds to its cultural significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hindu temple (later converted into a Buddhist temple)
Notable_Visitors: Lara Croft (fictional character from Tomb Raider)
world knowledge.Details: The view of the Angkor Wat from the top of Phnom Bakheng is featured in the movie Tomb Raider (when Lara Croft looks through the binoculars upon arriving in Cambodia).

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Abdul Samad Building
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sultan Abdul Samad Building is a late-19th century building located along Jalan Raja in front of Dataran Merdeka and the Royal Selangor Club in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Originally housing the offices of the British colonial administration, it was renamed in 1974 after Sultan Abdul Samad, the reigning sultan of Selangor when construction began.

Major_Events.Description: The building was officially opened by Sir Frank Swettenham, the General Resident of the time.
The British Union Jack was lowered for the last time at midnight on 30 August 1957 when the clock started chiming, and the Malayan flag was hoisted for the first time.
A massive renovation was undertaken, taking six years to complete with a total cost of RM 17.2 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features an Indo-Saracenic, Neo-Mughal, or Moorish architectural style. It has a central clock tower 41 metres in height, flanked by two lower towers, all topped by copper-clad onion domes. The facade stretches over 137.2 metres along Jalan Raja.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is a major landmark in Kuala Lumpur and serves as the backdrop for important events such as the National Day Parade and the ushering in of the New Year. It symbolizes Malaysia's colonial past and its journey to independence.
world knowledge.Details: The building now houses the offices of the Ministry of Information, Communications and Culture of Malaysia. It has undergone several renovations and refurbishments, including the installation of new colour-changing LED lights in 2012. The building is accessible within walking distance west of Masjid Jamek LRT Station.

world knowledge.Name: Tomb of Khải Định
world knowledge.Address: Châu Chữ mountain, near Huế, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tomb of Khải Định, officially Ứng Mausoleum, was built for Khải Định, the twelfth Emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty of Vietnam. It blends Vietnamese architecture with Western styles. Construction began in 1920 and was completed in 1931, six years after Khải Định's death. The tomb became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 as part of the Complex of Hué Monuments.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the tomb began on 4 September 1920.
Khải Định died before the tomb was completed.
A three-day funeral procession took place in late January 1926, traveling from the Imperial City to the unfinished tomb.
The tomb was completed under Bảo Đại, Khải Định's son and successor.
The tomb was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with other Nguyễn dynasty structures in Huế.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tomb features a blend of Vietnamese architecture with Western styles, including Baroque, Gothic, and Neoclassical elements. It is largely made of concrete, steel, iron, and slate. The entrance features a grand staircase, a triple-arched memorial gateway, and wrought iron gates made in France. The tomb complex includes a salutation court with stone figures, a two-tiered octagonal reinforced concrete stele pavilion, and the Thiên Định Palace with five connected halls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tomb of Khải Định is culturally significant as it represents the final resting place of the twelfth Emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty and showcases a unique blend of Vietnamese and Western architectural styles. It is part of the Complex of Hué Monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The tomb is open to the public for visiting. The interior of the Thiên Định Palace is lavishly decorated with intricate glass and porcelain decorations, nine intricate dragons on the ceiling, and a collection of Khải Định's personal memorabilia. The center of the palace contains the altar room, Khải Thành Palace, and a temple with Khải Định's grave and a bronze statue of his likeness.

world knowledge.Name: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height: 22 m (72 ft), Width: 12 m (39 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall, meaning a meeting point between sky and land, is one of the main tourist attractions on Jeju Island. It is characterized by its trachyte andesite rocks and is sourced from a spring in the Somban Stream. The waterfall is part of the three famous waterfalls of Jeju, alongside Cheonjeyeon Waterfall and Jeongbang Waterfall.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The waterfall is natural, with large volcanic rocks forming landbridges for tourists. It features an artificial pond at the bottom, 20 m (66 ft) deep, maintained by two small dams.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The waterfall is culturally significant as a natural monument and a popular tourist site, especially when illuminated at night. It is also known for its diverse plant and animal life, including the marbled eel, classified as Natural Monument no. 27 in Korea.
world knowledge.Details: Visitors must walk on a landscaped trail to reach the waterfall. Along the path, there are traditional Korean rafts, koi fish, and three piles of stacked rocks, where people used to pray for family health and prosperity. The area is rich in subtropical flora and fauna, including Elaeocarpus sylvestris var. ellipticus, Psilotum nudum, and Castanopsis cuspidata var. sieboldii.

world knowledge.Name: China Millennium Monument
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The China Millennium Monument is a monumental complex designed to evoke both a monumental Chinese altar and a sundial. It was championed by CCP official Zhu Xiangyuan and completed in 1999 ahead of the Millennium celebrations. Since 2006, it has housed the Beijing World Art Museum. The monument is imbued with references to ancient Chinese philosophy, geomancy, numerology, and Bagua, as well as themes connected to 20th-century Chinese Communist Party discourse.

Major_Events.Description: Principal Chinese venue for the Millennium celebrations.
Officially inaugurated on Chinese New Year, 5 February 2000.

Major_Events.Event: Celebration of Beijing's selection for 2008 Summer Olympics
Major_Events.Description: Main venue for the July 2001 celebration of Beijing's selection to host the 2008 Summer Olympics.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Beijing World Art Museum
Major_Events.Description: Housed the Beijing World Art Museum from 2006 onwards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument features a truncated conic base representing earth (Kūn) and a sundial-shaped rotunda representing heaven (Qián). The rotunda can rotate around a vertical axis and supports an inclined metal spire called the "Time and Space Probing Pin." The base's diameter is 85 meters, and the rotating sundial's is 47 meters. The monument faces south in accordance with Feng Shui principles and includes a 270-meters-long causeway with bronze plates inscribed with events of China's history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monument symbolizes five thousand years of Chinese nationhood and incorporates elements of ancient Chinese philosophy, geomancy, and numerology. It reflects the CCP's efforts to re-embrace pre-Communist Chinese legacies and emphasizes the harmony of China's 56 ethnic groups. The monument also serves as a cultural venue, housing the Beijing World Art Museum.
world knowledge.Details: The monument includes the Great Century Hall, adorned with a 5-meter-high circular wall featuring episodes of Chinese history in stone relief. A 140-meters-long circular corridor features 40 bronze statues of important figures of Chinese culture and science. The monument is surrounded by a green space carved out from Yuyuantan Park, featuring two rotundas, one with a monumental Chinese bell (Century Bell) and the other left empty. The Beijing World Art Museum focuses on temporary exhibitions due to the lack of a significant permanent collection.

world knowledge.Name: Suzdal Kremlin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Suzdal Kremlin is the oldest part of the city of Suzdal, Russia, dating from the 10th century. It was originally a fortress or citadel which was the religious and administrative center of the city. It is most notably the site of the Cathedral of the Nativity. Together with several structures in the neighboring city of Vladimir, it was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992. The fortress was strategically located on a bend of the Kamenka river on three sides and a moat to the east. It was surrounded by earthen ramparts that remain to the present day. A settlement to the east became home to the secular population - shopkeepers and craftsmen, while the Kremlin proper was the home of the prince, the archbishop, and the high clergy. From the 13th to the 16th centuries, several monasteries and churches were constructed, including the Cathedral of the Nativity, the Intercession Convent, and the Monastery of Our Saviour and St. Euthymius.

Major_Events.Description: The Suzdal Kremlin, along with several structures in the neighboring city of Vladimir, was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Suzdal Kremlin was originally a fortress or citadel, strategically located on a bend of the Kamenka river on three sides and a moat to the east. It was surrounded by earthen ramparts that remain to the present day. The site includes the Cathedral of the Nativity, the Intercession Convent, and the Monastery of Our Saviour and St. Euthymius.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Suzdal Kremlin is culturally and historically important as the oldest part of the city of Suzdal and a key religious and administrative center. It is part of the White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The Suzdal Kremlin is part of the 'Kremlin of Suzdal and Cathedral of the Nativity' which is included in the White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Name: Venta Rapid
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Venta Rapid is a waterfall on the Venta River in Kuldīga, western Latvia. It is the widest waterfall in Europe at 249 metres (817 ft) across, and becomes as wide as 275 metres (902 ft) during spring floods. The height of the falls varies from 1.80 to 2.20 metres (5 ft 11 in to 7 ft 3 in) depending on the level of water in the river. The waterfall is formed by Devonian dolomite and its formation is due to the difference in hardness of mineral between its lower and upper parts. The town of Kuldiga was established here because the falls formed an obstacle on the Venta medieval inland shipping route.

Major_Events.Description: Duke of Courland Jacob Kettler planned to dig a bypass to avoid the waterfall. Excavation started on the right bank of the river, but the idea was abandoned because the dolomite was too hard and the work was too slow and difficult.

Russia had plans to create a network of canals to unite all the seas of its European part. The idea was to create waterways between the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea across the Venta, Neman and Dnieper rivers. Turkish prisoners of war were commandeered to build a canal, but the dolomite bedrock was too hard to dig and the river was not wide and deep enough for shipping. Construction was discontinued in 1831, but the canal was dug around the waterfall 30 years later.
The Venta Rapid was designated a natural monument of Latvia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The waterfall is formed by Devonian dolomite and its formation is due to the difference in hardness of mineral between its lower and upper parts. The upper, more convex parts sometimes collapse and fall into the river, causing the waterfall to slowly recede.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The waterfall is culturally and historically important as it is the widest waterfall in Europe and has been a significant natural feature in the region since medieval times. It has influenced the development of the town of Kuldiga and has been the subject of various legends and historical events.
world knowledge.Details: The waterfall is visited by 130,000 tourists annually. A wooden path for walking and observation was made along the river and the waterfall. Fishing is prohibited during the spawning season. The famous Kuldiga brick bridge, built in 1874 and renovated in 2008, is located 240 m from the waterfall and is the longest operating brick bridge in Europe.

image_name: Gobustan State Historical and Cultural Reserve

world knowledge.Name: Gobustan State Historical and Cultural Reserve
world knowledge.Address: West of the settlement of Gobustan, about 40 miles (64 km) southwest of the center of Baku
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1966 to preserve prehistoric rock carvings, mud volcanoes, and musical stones. It acquired national status in 2006 and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
A Latin inscription was discovered on a large rock near Boyuk-Dash mountain, indicating the presence of Roman troops in the region.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of Mud Volcanoes Tourism Complex
Major_Events.Description: The Mud Volcanoes Tourism Complex was inaugurated, featuring various attractions and facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The reserve features prehistoric rock carvings, mud volcanoes, and musical stones. The rock carvings depict various scenes from prehistoric life, including hunting, dancing, and tribal activities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The reserve is culturally significant due to its prehistoric rock carvings, which provide insights into the lives of ancient populations in the Caucasus. It also contains unique natural features like mud volcanoes and musical stones.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Preservation and exhibition of prehistoric rock carvings and natural features
world knowledge.Details: The reserve includes the Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape, which has over 6,000 rock carvings dating back 5,000-20,000 years. It also features the Gaval Dash, a natural musical stone, and numerous mud volcanoes. The Petroglyph Museum functions within the reserve, and the Mud Volcanoes Tourism Complex offers various attractions.

world knowledge.Name: Institut de France
world knowledge.Address: Quai de Conti, 6th arrondissement, Paris, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Institut de France was established in 1795 by the National Convention. It is a learned society grouping five académies, including the Académie Française. The building was originally constructed as the Collège des Quatre-Nations by Cardinal Mazarin in 1661 as a school for students from new provinces attached to France under Louis XIV.

Major_Events.Description: The Institut de France was established on 25 October 1795 by the National Convention.
Xavier Darcos took office as the Institut de France's chancellor on 1 January 2018, succeeding Gabriel de Broglie.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was originally constructed as the Collège des Quatre-Nations by Cardinal Mazarin. The inscription over the façade reads "JUL. MAZARIN S.R.E. CARD BASILICAM ET GYMNAS F.C.A M.D.C.LXI", indicating its construction in 1661.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Institut de France is a prestigious learned society that manages approximately 1,000 foundations, museums, and châteaux. It awards prizes and subsidies, totaling over €27 million per year in 2017. It has served as a model for other institutions like the Royal Society of Canada and the Lebanese Academy of Sciences.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Learned society and management of foundations, museums, and châteaux.
world knowledge.Details: The Institut de France is under the protection of the President of France. It includes five académies: Académie Française, Académie des inscriptions et belles-lettres, Académie des sciences, Académie des Beaux-Arts, and Académie des sciences morales et politiques. The current chancellor is Xavier Darcos (since 2018).

world knowledge.Name: Jelgava Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jelgava Palace is the largest Baroque-style palace in the Baltic states. It was built in the 18th century based on the design of Bartolomeo Rastrelli as a residence for the Dukes of Courland in their capital of Mitau (today's Jelgava). The site had borne the residence of the former Courland dukes of the Kettler dynasty and, before that, a medieval castle belonging to the Livonian Order. Construction started in 1738 but was halted in 1740 due to Ernst Johann von Biron's fall from grace. Work resumed in 1762 after Biron's return from exile, and the palace was completed in 1772.

Major_Events.Description: Following Ernst Johann von Biron's fall from grace, all construction work was stopped.
Part of the palace was damaged by fire.
Louis XVIII of France and his family lived in the palace.
The northern part of the palace was damaged by fire.
The palace was looted and burned by the retreating West Russian Volunteer Army.
The palace suffered heavy damage during battles for Jelgava.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is the largest Baroque-style palace in the Baltic states. It originally consisted of two wings connected to the main building forming a U-shape. In 1937, a fourth building was added by Eižens Laube, effectively closing the perimeter. The facade design is noted for lacking rhythmic diversity and plastic richness, atypical for Rastrelli's works. The palace did not feature a garden, and the parade yard originally faced the urban panorama of Jelgava.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jelgava Palace is culturally and historically important as the residence of the Dukes of Courland and for its role in housing French royalty fleeing the French Revolution. It also features the burial vault of the Dukes of Courland, containing 21 sarcophagi and nine wooden coffins.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a residence for the Dukes of Courland, it now houses the administration and three faculties of the Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies.
world knowledge.Details: The palace's burial vault in the south-east basement contains the remains of all Dukes of Courland from the Houses of Kettler and Biron, buried between 1569 and 1791. The crypt was relocated to the palace in 1819.

world knowledge.Name: Istana Maziah
world knowledge.Address: Bukit Puteri, Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu, Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Istana Maziah is the official palace of the Sultan of Terengganu, built to replace Istana Hijau which was destroyed in a fire. Construction faced delays due to funding issues and was completed in 1903. It has undergone several refurbishments and additions over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone of Istana Maziah was laid on May 31, 1895, during the reign of Sultan Zainal Abidin III.
The palace was completed and inaugurated on August 7, 1903, with the 'upacara naik istana' ceremony marking the Sultan's move into the new palace.
Refurbishments were carried out during the reign of Sultan Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah.
Further additions were made to the Istana buildings in 1972 and 1998.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Istana Maziah is a two-story building with a coffee brown color, blending modern and traditional architecture. It features tall shuttered windows resembling a French chateau. The early foundations were built from a mixture of chalk, clay, sand salts, egg whites, lime, and honey.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Istana Maziah is the official venue for important royal functions and receptions for dignitaries. It symbolizes the culture and traditions of Terengganu, with Dataran Maziah featuring a replica of betel chewing instruments known as Tepak Sirih.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official palace of the Sultan of Terengganu
world knowledge.Details: The palace was designed by Tengku Chik Abu Bakar bin Tengku Abdul Jalil, with contributions from other designers. Wood for construction was sourced from Dungun, and bricks and chalk were handled by Tengku Besar Paduka Indera. The palace has undergone several refurbishments and additions over the years.

world knowledge.Name: Foxton Locks
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Foxton Locks are ten canal locks consisting of two 'staircases' each of five locks, located on the Leicester line of the Grand Union Canal. They form the northern terminus of a 20-mile summit level. The locks were opened on 1 October 1813. The Foxton Inclined Plane, built in 1900, was dismantled in 1926 but a project to re-create it commenced in the 2000s. The locks are the largest flight of staircase locks on the English canal system.

Major_Events.Description: The locks were opened on 1 October 1813.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the Foxton Inclined Plane
Major_Events.Description: The Foxton Inclined Plane was built to resolve operational restrictions imposed by the lock flight.

Major_Events.Event: Dismantling of the Foxton Inclined Plane
Major_Events.Description: The Foxton Inclined Plane was dismantled due to lack of commercial success.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in the European Route of Industrial Heritage
Major_Events.Description: The locks became part of the European Route of Industrial Heritage, recognizing their importance as an industrial heritage site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The locks are staircase locks, where each lock opens directly into the next. They are equipped with side pounds to save water. The locks are narrow beam with light gates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Foxton Locks are the largest flight of staircase locks on the English canal system and are a popular tourist attraction. They are part of the European Route of Industrial Heritage, recognizing their historical and industrial importance.
world knowledge.Details: The locks are usually staffed during the cruising season from Easter to October and padlocked outside operating hours to prevent water shortages. The area is popular with ramblers and enthusiasts. The Foxton Canal Museum, located in the former boiler house for the plane's steam engine, covers the history of the locks and the plane, the lives of the canal workers, and other aspects of the local canal. The museum opened in 1989 and is accredited by the Museums, Libraries and Archives Council.

world knowledge.Name: Place Bellecour
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 312 m by 200 m (6.2 ha or 15 acres)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The square originated from a vineyard called Bella curtis in the late 12th century. It became a public square in 1604 under Henry IV's order. The current layout and statue were established in the 18th and 19th centuries, with the square undergoing several name changes reflecting France's political shifts.

Major_Events.Description: An altar dedicated to Liberty was erected during the French Revolution.
The original statue of Louis XIV was destroyed during the French Revolution to make cannon.

Major_Events.Event: Installation of New Louis XIV Statue
Major_Events.Description: A new equestrian statue of Louis XIV by François-Frédéric Lemot was erected.
A statue of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and the Little Prince was erected to commemorate the aviator's centenary.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Large open square without greenery, featuring an equestrian statue of Louis XIV, allegorical statues of the Saône and Rhône, and two pavilions housing a tourist office and art gallery.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the largest open squares in Europe and a central focus of Lyon. It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site and serves as the kilometer 0 point for Lyon.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public square and cultural hub, hosting events, tourism services, and commercial activities.
world knowledge.Details: The square is a major transportation hub with a metro station (Bellecour) and several bus lines. It is surrounded by key shopping streets and landmarks like Vieux Lyon and Lyon Cathedral.

world knowledge.Name: Huasca de Ocampo
world knowledge.Location: Central Mexico, 34 km from Pachuca, 16 km from Real del Monte
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Huasca de Ocampo is a town and municipality in Hidalgo, Mexico, established in the 18th century. It was developed by Pedro Romero de Terreros, who built mining haciendas that made him the richest man in the world. The area's economy shifted from mining to agriculture and tourism, with haciendas converted into luxury hotels. It is part of the Pueblos Mágicos program due to its preserved architecture and natural surroundings.

Major_Events.Description: Pedro Romero de Terreros developed mining haciendas, making Huasca a significant mining center.
Santa María Regla Hacienda was converted into a luxury hotel, marking a shift towards tourism.
Huasca de Ocampo became part of the federal Pueblos Mágicos tourism program due to its preserved architecture and cultural heritage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features white sandstone buildings with pitched red roofs, thick walls, and stone-paved streets. The main parish church, dedicated to John the Baptist, has Baroque-style altars and a relief carving of the Archangel Michael. The mining haciendas, such as Santa María Regla and San Miguel Regla, retain original structures like smelting ovens, aqueducts, and chapels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Huasca de Ocampo is culturally significant for its historical mining haciendas, preserved colonial architecture, and role in Mexico's mining history. It is also known for its pottery, traditional crafts, and festivals like the Feast of John the Baptist.
world knowledge.Details: Huasca de Ocampo is known for its natural attractions like the Basaltic Prisms of Santa María Regla, trout farms, and ecotourism activities. The town has over 15 inns and hotels, and it is a popular weekend destination for visitors from Mexico City.

world knowledge.Name: Gobarau Minaret
world knowledge.Address: Center of the city of Katsina, northern Nigeria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gobarau Minaret is a 50-foot edifice located in the center of the city of Katsina, the capital of Katsina State. It was built during the reign of Sarkin (King) Katsina, Muhammadu Korau (1445 – 1495 AD), the first Muslim ruler of the ancient Kingdom of Katsina. The mosque's origin is attributed to the efforts of the influential Islamic scholar Sheikh Muhammad Abdulkarim Almaghili, who taught in Katsina in the late fifteenth century. The mosque was built to serve as a center for spiritual and intellectual activities, inspired by mosques found in Timbuktu. It later became a school and a famed institution of higher Islamic education. The mosque and its tower were renovated by Sarkin Katsina Muhammadu Kabir Usman (1981–2008).

Major_Events.Description: The mosque was built during the reign of Sarkin Katsina, Muhammadu Korau, and was inspired by mosques in Timbuktu.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation of the mosque and tower
Major_Events.Description: The mosque and its tower were renovated by Sarkin Katsina Muhammadu Kabir Usman.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hausa Architecture
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gobarau Minaret is an early example of Muslim architecture in Katsina, a city known as a theological center. It has become a symbol of the city and is a tourist attraction site.
world knowledge.Details: A popular myth about the origin of Gobarau involves Mallam Jodoma, who pointed his staff at a direction, and the Ka'abah appeared. The tower was also used for spotting invading armies. Today, Gobarau is a tourist attraction site, along with the Kusugu well in Daura.

world knowledge.Name: Ishtar Gate
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 15 metres high, foundations extended 14 metres underground
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ishtar Gate was the eighth gate to the inner city of Babylon, constructed by King Nebuchadnezzar II. It was part of a grand walled processional way leading into the city. The gate was dedicated to the Babylonian goddess Ishtar and featured glazed bricks with depictions of dragons, bulls, and lions symbolizing the gods Marduk, Adad, and Ishtar.

Major_Events.Description: German archaeologist Robert Koldewey led the excavation of the site, uncovering the gate's foundations and reconstructing the smaller frontal gate in the Pergamon Museum in Berlin.
After the end of the First World War, the smaller frontal gate was reconstructed in the Pergamon Museum in Berlin.
The Ishtar Gate and Processional Way were used for a New Year's procession, part of a religious festival celebrating the beginning of the agricultural year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gate was constructed using glazed brick with alternating rows of bas-relief mušḫuššu (dragons), aurochs (bulls), and lions. The bricks were covered in a blue glaze to represent lapis lazuli. The gate was a double gate with a smaller frontal gate and a larger posterior section. The roof and doors were made of cedar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ishtar Gate is culturally significant as a symbol of the Neo-Babylonian Empire's grandeur and religious devotion. It represents the power of the gods Marduk, Adad, and Ishtar and was a key part of Babylon's religious and ceremonial life.
world knowledge.Details: The gate's inscription is written in Akkadian cuneiform and was a dedication by Nebuchadnezzar. A reconstruction of the gate and Processional Way was built at the Pergamon Museum in Berlin. The gate has been a subject of controversy regarding the repatriation of cultural artifacts to Iraq.

world knowledge.Name: Cluny Abbey
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Largest church in Christendom until St. Peter's Basilica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cluny Abbey was a former Benedictine monastery founded in 910 by William I, Duke of Aquitaine. It became a leading center of western monasticism, known for its strict adherence to the Rule of St. Benedict. The abbey was largely destroyed during the French Revolution in 1790 and further demolished in the early 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by William I, Duke of Aquitaine, as a Benedictine monastery dedicated to Saints Peter and Paul.
Cluny became the most prestigious and wealthy monastic institution in Europe, leading the Cluniac Reforms.
The abbey was sacked and mostly destroyed, with only a small part surviving.
Excavations were conducted by Kenneth John Conant, revealing the abbey's extensive remains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed in the Romanesque architectural style, with three successive churches (Cluny I, II, and III). Cluny III was the largest church in Europe until the 16th century, featuring stone vaults, elaborate decorations, and a centralized layout.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cluny Abbey was a pivotal center of monastic reform and religious influence in medieval Europe. Its centralized governance model and liturgical practices shaped Western monasticism and ecclesiastical architecture. The abbey also played a key role in the Christianization of Europe and the spread of Romanesque art and architecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Benedictine monastery dedicated to prayer, liturgical worship, and monastic reform.

Details.Surviving_Structures: Southern transept, bell-tower, and lower parts of the west front towers (approx. 10% of original structure).
Details.Modern_Use: Center of the École nationale supérieure d'arts et métiers (ENSAM).
Details.Artifacts: Held at Musée de Cluny in Paris and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

world knowledge.Name: Charlottenhof Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Charlottenhof Palace, also known as Charlottenhof Manor, is a former royal palace located southwest of Sanssouci Palace in Sanssouci Park at Potsdam, Germany. It served as the summer residence of Crown Prince Frederick William (later King Frederick William IV of Prussia). The palace and its surrounding park are part of the Berlin-Potsdam Palaces and Parks system. The land was purchased by King Frederick William III of Prussia and given to his son Frederick William and his wife Elisabeth Ludovika in 1825. The architect Karl Friedrich Schinkel, with the help of his student Ludwig Persius, remodeled an existing farmhouse into a Neoclassical palace. The palace and park were named 'Charlottenhof' in honor of Maria Charlotte von Gentzkow, who owned the property from 1790 to 1794.

Major_Events.Description: Charlottenhof Palace became part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style, designed by Karl Friedrich Schinkel and Ludwig Persius. The palace was built on the foundations of an old farmhouse and resembles a Roman villa. The interior features ten rooms with largely intact designs, including the distinctive tent room, which is decorated with blue and white striped wallpaper.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Charlottenhof Palace is culturally significant as a former royal residence and a fine example of Neoclassical architecture. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin', reflecting the historical and architectural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is administered by the Stiftung Preußische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin-Brandenburg. The park area was designed by landscape architect Peter Joseph Lenné, who transformed it into an English garden with trees, lawn, and water features, linking it to the older Sanssouci Park.

world knowledge.Name: Poulnabrone dolmen
world knowledge.Address: parish of Kilcorney, the Burren, County Clare, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Poulnabrone dolmen is a large dolmen located in the Burren, County Clare, Ireland. It dates to the early Neolithic period, with estimates from 3800 and 3200 BC. It was constructed on a unique karst landscape formed from limestone laid down around 350 million years ago. The dolmen was built by Neolithic farmers, who chose the location either for ritual, as a territorial marker, or as a collective burial site.
