When the site was excavated in 1986 and again in 1988, around 33 human remains, including those of adults and children, were found buried underneath it.

Major_Events.Description: Excavations led by Ann Lynch revealed around 33 human remains and various stone and bone objects buried within the chamber.
Two phases of conservation were undertaken to stabilize the tomb, overseen by Ann Lynch.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Poulnabrone dolmen consists of a slab-like tabular capstone supported by two pillar stones on either side, creating a chamber that tapers eastwards. The trapezoidal capstone is 3.9 m (13 ft) in length, between 2 m (6 ft 7 in) and 3 m (9.8 ft) wide, and is 0.3 m (1 ft 0 in) thick. The portal stones are positioned at either side of the lower side of the capstone, marking the tomb's entrance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Poulnabrone dolmen is culturally significant as it is one of the best-known dolmens in Ireland, dating back to the Neolithic period. It serves as a testament to the ritual practices and burial customs of early Neolithic farmers.
world knowledge.Details: Poulnabrone dolmen is located on a low circular mound measuring c. 10 m (33 ft) in diameter. The site is east of the Poulanine and Glensleade valleys, beyond which are the rocky Baur and Poulnabrucky hills. The monument may have served as a territorial marker in the Neolithic landscape. Radiocarbon dating indicates that the tomb was probably used as a burial site between 3800 and 3200 BC. The findings are now at the Clare Museum, Ennis, loaned from the National Museum of Ireland.

world knowledge.Name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
world knowledge.Address: Harpers Ferry, Iowa, just north of Marquette
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Effigy Mounds National Monument preserves more than 200 prehistoric mounds built by pre-Columbian Mound Builder cultures, mostly in the first millennium CE, during the later part of the Woodland period of pre-Columbian North America. Numerous effigy mounds are shaped like animals, including bears and birds.

Major_Events.Description: Effigy Mounds was proclaimed a National Monument on October 25, 1949.

Major_Events.Event: Featured in America the Beautiful Quarters Program
Major_Events.Description: In 2017, the Effigy Mounds were featured in the America the Beautiful Quarters Program.
From 1999 to 2009, Superintendent Phyllis Ewing oversaw more than $3 million in illegal construction of boardwalks, trails and other structures that damaged irreplaceable archaeological artifacts.

Major_Events.Event: Bone theft by Superintendent Thomas Munson
Major_Events.Description: In July 2016, Thomas Munson, Superintendent for 20 years of the Effigy Mounds National Monument, was sentenced to several days in prison after pleading guilty to stealing bones in 1990 of 40 ancient Native Americans.

In 2022, the National Park Service and leaders of the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska (ITKN) signed a first-of-its-kind agreement establishing the first Tribal Sister Park relationship between a U.S. national park and a Tribal Nation’s National Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Prehistoric earthworks by mound builder cultures, with mounds in the shape of mammals, birds, or reptiles. The largest, Great Bear Mound, measures 42 meters from head to tail and rises over a meter above the original ground level.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Numerous federally recognized tribes have linguistic and cultural ties to the ancestral peoples who built the effigy and other earthwork mounds at the monument site. The monument preserves significant prehistoric cultural artifacts and provides insight into the Mound Builder cultures.
world knowledge.Details: The monument contains 2,526 acres (10.22 km²) with 206 mounds, of which 31 are effigies. The park has 14 miles of hiking trails. The visitor center contains museum exhibits highlighting archaeological and natural specimens, an auditorium, and book sales outlet. The monument is noted for being in the Driftless Area, an area of North America which escaped glaciation during the last ice age.

world knowledge.Name: Australian War Memorial
world knowledge.Address: Australian War Memorial, Anzac Pde, Campbell, ACT, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Australian War Memorial (AWM) is a national war memorial, museum, and archive dedicated to all Australians who died as a result of war, including peacekeeping duties. Plans to build it were initiated after World War I, formally established in 1925, and opened to the public in 1941. Its scope expanded over time to include all conflicts involving Australians.

Major_Events.Description: The AWM was formally established through federal legislation.
The AWM was officially opened to the public on Remembrance Day.

Major_Events.Event: Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier
Major_Events.Description: The tomb was installed inside the Memorial Building's Hall of Memory.
The National Capital Authority approved the AWM's expansion plans, including the demolition of Anzac Hall.
Director Kim Beazley announced the memorial would cover the Australian Frontier Wars for the first time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Memorial Building is designed in an Art Deco style with Byzantine and Egyptian motifs. It features interpenetrating masses, pylons, and a domed Hall of Memory. Newer buildings like ANZAC Hall and the CEW Bean Building were designed by Denton Corker Marshall, with modern and functional designs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The AWM is a symbol of national remembrance for Australians who died in wars. It serves as a museum, archive, and a place for commemorative services, reflecting Australia's military history and sacrifices.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Commemoration, education, and preservation of Australia's military history.
world knowledge.Details: The AWM includes the Memorial Building, ANZAC Hall, the CEW Bean Building, and a sculpture garden. It features galleries dedicated to various conflicts, the Hall of Valour, and the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. The memorial hosts nightly Last Post services and national ceremonies for Anzac Day and Remembrance Day.

world knowledge.Name: Kelso Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kelso Abbey is a ruined Scottish abbey in Kelso, Scotland, founded in the 12th century by Tironensian monks. It was established at Roxburgh in 1128 by King David I of Scotland. The abbey became one of the wealthiest and grandest in Scotland, despite facing numerous attacks and destructions, particularly during the Wars of Scottish Independence and the Rough Wooing. It effectively ceased to function in the mid-16th century due to a combination of physical assaults and the Scottish Reformation. The abbey fell into ruin and was later partially dismantled for building materials.

Major_Events.Description: Kelso Abbey was founded by King David I of Scotland at Roxburgh.
The abbey was dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint John.

Major_Events.Event: Attack during the Wars of Scottish Independence
Major_Events.Description: The abbey was attacked and damaged during the Wars of Scottish Independence.
The infant King James III was hastily crowned at Kelso Abbey following the death of his father, James II.
The abbey sustained major damage during attacks ordered by Henry VIII as part of the Rough Wooing.
The abbey was disestablished under the Scottish Reformation, leading to its eventual ruin.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey was a large, formidable building with a semi-military Romanesque style. It featured two crossings, each with single towers, a design relatively rare in Europe. The surviving west tower and transept indicate a strong, fortress-like structure. The earliest remains include rounded arches from around 1128, with later additions such as a triforium and clerestory. The masonry suggests there was no nave vaulting. The ruins include the west tower, transepts, and vestibule, with the north transept gable being the most intact surviving face.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kelso Abbey is culturally and historically significant as one of the wealthiest and grandest abbeys in Scotland, reflecting the importance of Roxburgh as a major economic and administrative centre in the medieval period. Its history of survival and destruction during key historical events, such as the Wars of Scottish Independence and the Rough Wooing, highlights its resilience and the turbulent history of the Scottish Borders.
world knowledge.Details: The ruins of Kelso Abbey are cared for by Historic Scotland and are part of the Borders Abbeys Way walk. There is no entrance charge to visit the site. The abbey's remains include the west tower crossing and part of the infirmary. A memorial cloister to the 8th Duke of Roxburghe, designed by Reginald Fairlie, was added in 1933. The site has not been fully excavated in modern times.

world knowledge.Name: Ciudad Vieja
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ciudad Vieja was the second site of Santiago de los Caballeros de Guatemala, the colonial capital of the country. Founded in 1527, it was destroyed by a catastrophic lahar from Volcan de Agua in 1541, leading to its abandonment. The site is significant for its role in the early colonial history of Guatemala.

Major_Events.Description: The city was destroyed by a catastrophic lahar from Volcan de Agua, leading to its abandonment. Among the casualties was the governor Beatriz de la Cueva.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ciudad Vieja is culturally significant as the second colonial capital of Guatemala, reflecting the early Spanish colonial efforts in the region.
world knowledge.Details: Ciudad Vieja has a subtropical highland climate (Köppen: Cwb). The modern Ciudad Vieja municipality is surrounded by Sacatepéquez Department municipalities.

world knowledge.Name: Donjon de Niort
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Two square towers linked by a 15th-century building, dominating the Sèvre Niortaise valley
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Donjon de Niort is a medieval castle started by Henry II Plantagenet and completed by Richard the Lionheart. It served as a strategic base for the English Crown in western France. The castle was damaged during the Wars of Religion and later served as a prison in the 18th century. It was classified as a monument historique in 1840 and now functions as a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The townspeople of Niort were besieged by Poitevin lords, leading to a blockade that lasted several years. The castle became the sole supplier for the town.
The castle returned to English control.
Niort alternated between French and English domination until it was securely placed under the French crown by Du Guesclin.
The duc de Berry restored the castle, improving residential parts, adding windows, fireplaces, and decorative elements.
The north tower collapsed, weakening the rest of the building. It was later restored by engineer Artus.
The castle was classified as a monument historique.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle consists of two square towers (28m and 23m tall) with circular turrets at the corners and semicircular buttresses. The Romanesque architecture features high-quality dressed stones closely jointed. The interiors are spartan with no chimneys, large windows, or decorative sculpture. A 15th-century building links the towers, and the structure originally included a drawbridge and a dry moat 8m deep.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Donjon de Niort is a significant example of medieval military architecture and reflects the historical conflicts between English and French control in the region. It now serves as a museum, preserving Poitevin culture and history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a military fortress, later used as a prison, and now a museum.
world knowledge.Details: The castle houses museum collections and offers a beautiful view over the town and the Sèvre Niortaise from its roof. The outer walls and twelve towers, along with other structures like the drawbridge, have disappeared over time. The remains of some towers were uncovered during the building of the modern market.

world knowledge.Name: Hobart Synagogue
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hobart Synagogue is the oldest synagogue building in Australia, constructed in 1845. It was built as the Hobart Jewish community began to emerge in the 1830s. The land was originally part of the garden of former convict Judah Solomon. The synagogue was consecrated on 4 July 1845 and has served as the focal point of Jewish culture in Hobart ever since.

Major_Events.Description: The Hobart Hebrew Congregation Synagogue was consecrated on 4 July 1845.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The synagogue is a rare example of Egyptian Revival style architecture, featuring trapezoidal windows and columns with lotus capitals. It was designed by Hobart Town architect James Thomson, a Scottish convict who was pardoned in 1829.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hobart Synagogue is the oldest synagogue in Australia and a rare surviving example of Egyptian Revival style synagogue architecture. It is listed on the Tasmanian Heritage Register and serves as the focal point of Jewish culture in Hobart.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Synagogue for Orthodox and Progressive Jewish services
world knowledge.Details: The synagogue has a seating capacity of 150 and features hard benches at the back for Jewish convicts who were marched in under armed guard in the early days. The Tasmanian Jewish community reached a low point in the early 1970s with fewer than 100 Jews recorded in Hobart, but the 2021 census recorded 376 Jews in Tasmania.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Clisson
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Clisson is a castle in Clisson, France, built in the 13th century. It was a significant fortified site on the frontiers of the Duchy of Brittany. The castle underwent several modifications over the centuries, including modernization for artillery in the 15th century. It was burned during the War in the Vendée and later restored in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: Most of the present castle was built in the 13th century by Guillaume de Clisson on a rocky outcrop dominating the Sèvre Nantaise.
Olivier III de Clisson incorporated the gatehouse into a massive quadrilangular keep.
The fortifications were modernised to permit the use of artillery, and the castle was enlarged to the west with a new rectangular enclosure.

Major_Events.Event: Burning during War in the Vendée
Major_Events.Description: The town and its castle were burned by the Infernal columns of Jean-Baptiste Kléber during the War in the Vendée.
The remains of the castle were classed as a monument historique by a French Ministry of Culture decree.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle features an irregular polygon shape flanked by round towers, a quadrilangular keep, and extended curtain walls with a barbican. It includes artillery casemates and three terraced bastions on the south.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a significant historical site in France, representing medieval and Renaissance architecture. It was a key fortified location in Brittany and has been depicted by notable artists like Jean Metzinger and André Derain.
world knowledge.Details: The castle was the subject of Jean Metzinger's painting 'Le château de Clisson' (1905) and a drawing by André Derain. It was sold to the Conseil général of the Loire-Atlantique in 1962, who carried out important restoration works.

world knowledge.Name: Pontigny Abbey
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1114 (founding), with church construction likely starting in 1138
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pontigny Abbey was founded in 1114 as the second daughter house of Cîteaux Abbey. It became a significant Cistercian monastery, known for its sanctity and influence, establishing 22 other monasteries. It was suppressed during the French Revolution in 1791, with only the church surviving. It was later re-founded in 1843 by the Fathers of St. Edmund, became private property in 1909, and in 1941 became the mother house of the Mission de France.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as a Cistercian monastery by Hugh of Mâcon under the guidance of Stephen Harding of Cîteaux.
The abbey was pillaged and burnt by the Huguenots, with only the relics of Saint Edmund being saved.
The abbey was suppressed, and most of its buildings were destroyed except for the church.

Major_Events.Event: Re-founding by Fathers of St. Edmund
Major_Events.Description: The abbey was re-established as a community by J. B. Muard.
The philosopher Paul Desjardins bought the abbey and held intellectual conferences known as "Decades of Pontigny" from 1910 to 1939.

Major_Events.Event: Becoming mother house of Mission de France
Major_Events.Description: The abbey became the mother house of the Mission de France, a territorial prelature.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Regional Council of Burgundy
Major_Events.Description: The abbey was bought by the Regional Council of Burgundy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey church is an early example of Gothic style, with construction likely beginning in 1138. The surviving structures include the church and the southern wing (refectory and dormitories of the lay brothers).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pontigny Abbey is culturally significant as a historic Cistercian monastery, a center of intellectual activity in the early 20th century, and a stopping-point on the pilgrimage route to Santiago de Compostela. It also played a role in the development of Chablis wine.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a Cistercian monastery, later served as a parish church, intellectual meeting place, seminary, and now a historic site.

Details.Burials: The abbey church contains burials of notable figures, including Saint Edmund of Abingdon.
Details.Vineyards: The monks of Pontigny cultivated vineyards, establishing the original vineyard for Chablis wine.
Details.Pilgrimage: The abbey is a stopping-point on one of the pilgrimage routes to Santiago de Compostela.

world knowledge.Name: Plaza Garibaldi
world knowledge.Address: Eje Central (Lázaro Cárdenas) between Calle República de Honduras and Calle República de Peru, Mexico City
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Plaza Santa Cecilia, it was renamed in 1920 in honor of Lt. Col. Peppino Garibaldi, who joined the Maderistas during the Mexican Revolution. The plaza is known as Mexico City's home of mariachi music, with the Salón Tenampa being a central hub for mariachi bands since the 1920s.

Major_Events.Description: Renamed in honor of Lt. Col. Peppino Garibaldi after the Mexican Revolution.
The area was designated as a "Barrio Mágico" by the city.
The plaza was a site of Bicentennial Celebrations in Mexico City.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The plaza features a kiosk, arcade, and statues of great Charro singers. The surrounding area includes bars, restaurants, and nightclubs, with the Salón Tenampa being a prominent establishment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Plaza Garibaldi is culturally significant as the heart of mariachi music in Mexico City, attracting musicians and visitors from around the world. It represents a key aspect of Mexican musical heritage and has been a focal point for celebrations and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The plaza and surrounding neighborhoods are undergoing extensive renovations to improve safety and revitalize the area. Plans include the Museum of Tequila and Mezcal, a School of Mariachi, and the Paseo de los Idolos de la Música Mexicana. The area is part of the Bellas Artes-Garibaldi Tourism Corridor, with improvements in infrastructure, security, and tourism facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Spice Bazaar
world knowledge.Address: Eminönü quarter, Fatih district, Istanbul, Turkey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Spice Bazaar, also known as Mısır Çarşısı (Egyptian Bazaar), is one of the largest bazaars in Istanbul. It was built in 1660 with revenues from the Ottoman eyalet of Egypt. The bazaar was originally named 'New Bazaar' but later got its current name due to its funding source. It is part of the külliye (complex) of the New Mosque and was designed by the court architect Koca Kasım Ağa. Construction began under Mustafa Ağa following the Great Fire of 1660. The bazaar has been a center for spice trade in Istanbul, though other types of shops are gradually replacing spice sellers.

Major_Events.Description: The fire began on 24 July 1660 and lasted for about 49 hours, destroying many neighborhoods in Istanbul. This event led to a major rebuilding and redevelopment effort, including the construction of the Spice Bazaar.
The construction of the New Mosque, which had been halted between 1603 and 1660, was completed in 1665. The Spice Bazaar is part of the mosque's külliye.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Spice Bazaar is a covered bazaar designed by the court architect Koca Kasım Ağa. It is part of the külliye of the New Mosque and features a traditional Ottoman architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Spice Bazaar is culturally significant as it has been a center for spice trade in Istanbul for centuries. It is also part of the külliye of the New Mosque, reflecting the integration of commerce and religion in Ottoman society.
world knowledge.Details: The Spice Bazaar has a total of 85 shops selling spices, Turkish delight and other sweets, jewellery, souvenirs, and dried fruits and nuts. It is the most famous covered shopping complex after the Grand Bazaar in Istanbul.

world knowledge.Name: Long Tieng
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Long Tieng is a Laotian military base that served as a town and airbase operated by the Central Intelligence Agency of the United States during the Laotian Civil War. It was referred to as Lima Site 98 (LS 98) or Lima Site 20A (LS 20A). At its peak in the late 1960s, it had a population of 40,000, making it the second largest city in Laos, though it never appeared on maps. The base was established in 1962 and became one of the largest US installations on foreign soil by 1966. It was often described as "the most secret place on Earth" and was a major site during the Vietnam War.

Major_Events.Description: North Vietnamese forces launched a four-pronged attack on Long Tieng, encircling the site and capturing several facilities. Despite heavy casualties, the defenders, a mixture of Hmong, Thai, and Lao, managed to hold key positions with reinforcements from CIA-led Thais and irregulars from southern Laos.

Following the defeat of the final defensive outpost, US Brigadier General Heinie Aderholt planned an evacuation. Between May 10 to May 14, 1975, US C-130s and C-46s airlifted people from the airbase to US bases in Thailand. Major General Vang Pao and CIA officer Jerry Daniels were among the last to leave, with tens of thousands of fighters and refugees left behind.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Long Tieng was located in a valley at 3,100 feet elevation, surrounded by limestone mountains. The CIA headquarters, known as "Sky," was located in the shadow of karst outcrops. The town itself had one paved road with tin shacks on either side, housing eating shops, food stalls, and living quarters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Long Tieng became the largest Hmong settlement in the world during the Secret War. It was a significant site for the Hmong people, who ran various businesses and supported the military efforts. The base's history is a testament to the Hmong's role in the Laotian Civil War and their subsequent struggles.
world knowledge.Details: Long Tieng was incorporated into the restricted Xaisomboun Special Zone in 1994, which was dissolved in 2006. Xaisomboun Province was created in 2013, and the base is still maintained by the Laotian military. The area's history was documented in the 2008 film 'The Most Secret Place on Earth.' A charter school in Saint Paul, Minnesota, named Long Tieng Academy, closed in 2012.

world knowledge.Name: Bellu Cemetery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Șerban Vodă Cemetery, commonly known as Bellu Cemetery, is the largest and most famous cemetery in Bucharest, Romania. It was established in 1858 on a plot of land donated by Baron Barbu Bellu.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bellu Cemetery is a cultural attraction in Bucharest, known for its historical significance and as the resting place of many notable figures.
world knowledge.Details: The cemetery is open every day from 8:30 AM to 8 PM. Visiting hours may differ on public holidays.

world knowledge.Name: Kolomna Kremlin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kolomna Kremlin is a fortress in Kolomna, Russia, built under the Russian Tsar Vasily III. Before its reconstruction in 1531, it was made of wood. The Kremlin features many Russian churches and monasteries, including the Uspensky cathedral, the Voskresenky church, and the Spassky monastery (14th century). It is believed that the construction was headed by Italian architect Aleviz Friazin, who also worked on the Moscow Kremlin.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Kolomna Kremlin exhibits Italian architectural features, similar to northern Italian fortresses like Turin, Milan, and Verona. It includes machicolations, combat parapets with dovetail-shaped merlons, and faceted towers. The walls and towers were designed to defend against cannon fire, with numerous embrasures for firearms. Originally, the Kremlin had 17 towers, four of which had gates, but only 7 towers and two parts of the wall remain today.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kolomna Kremlin is culturally significant as a historic fortress that showcases the blend of Russian and Italian architectural styles. It represents the defensive architecture of the period and is a key historical site in Russia.
world knowledge.Details: The main gates were located at the northern and southern ends of the complex. The remaining towers include the Mihaelovskie Gates and the Melynychnie Gates.

world knowledge.Name: Pannonhalma Archabbey
world knowledge.Address: Pannonhalma, Győr-Moson-Sopron County, Western Transdanubia, Transdanubia, Hungary
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 996 by Prince Géza, it is one of the oldest historical monuments in Hungary. It became the center of the Benedictine order and was built in honor of Saint Martin of Tours. The monastery has undergone several reconstructions and expansions over its 1000-year history, including significant Baroque additions in the 17th and 18th centuries. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1996.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by Prince Géza as the first Hungarian Benedictine monastery.
The abbey and its surroundings were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The complex was entirely reconstructed and renovated in preparation for its millennium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey features a mix of architectural styles including Romanesque, Gothic, Baroque, and Classicist. Notable structures include the Basilica with the Crypt, the Cloisters, the monumental Library, the Baroque Refectory, and the Archabbey Collection.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The abbey is a significant cultural and religious center in Hungary, with a rich history spanning over a millennium. It houses important historical documents and artifacts, including the oldest surviving document to use the Hungarian language.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey is supplemented by the Benedictine High School, a boys' boarding school. It also has a winery that was revived after the fall of Communism, with 37 hectares of vineyards. The abbey's library contains 360,000 volumes, and its archives hold valuable documents from the first centuries of Hungarian statehood.

world knowledge.Name: Ruins of Kachari Rajbari
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ruins of Kachari Rajbari are a set of medieval monuments located in Dimapur, Nagaland, in Northeast India. Their history dates back to the 10th century when they appeared during the Kachari civilization. The Kachari Rajbari Ruins are a series of mushroom domed pillars created by the Kachari Kingdom, which ruled Dimapur before the Ahom invasion into the territory during the 13th century. Their origin and purpose are largely mysterious. The pillars are not well maintained. Some pillars still stand in all their glory but others have crumbled down. It is believed that a game similar to chess was played there with the mushroom domes.

Major_Events.Description: The Ahom Kingdom invaded the territory of the Kachari Kingdom, leading to the decline of the Kachari Rajbari.
Lieutenant Grange, Assistant Political Agent to the colonial government in Assam, undertook his first expedition to the Naga Hills and documented the ruins of Kachari Rajbari.
Ahom king Suhungmung and his son attacked Dimapur by ascending the river Timā (Dima or Dhansiri).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Kachari Rajbari Ruins are a series of mushroom domed pillars. The tallest pillar was about 15 feet, and the smallest one at the southern end was 8 feet and 5 inches. Most of these pillars were around 12 to 13 feet. The lotus was evident in all of the carved work. The entrance gateway was described as a fine solid mass of masonry, flanked on both sides by octagonal turrets of bricks with false windows of ornamental moulded brick work.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ruins of Kachari Rajbari are culturally significant as they represent the architectural and historical legacy of the Kachari Kingdom, which ruled Dimapur before the Ahom invasion. They provide insight into the early history of the Dimasas and the region's pre-colonial past.
world knowledge.Details: The pillars were in three parallel rows. The form of the town, or palace enclosure, was an oblong square running parallel to the Dhansiri river. Through oral tradition, it was built by Chokradoz, the fourth king of Cachar. Early colonial descriptions by successive British administrators fail to mention any clear trace of temples and images at the ruins, raising doubt about the scale and intensity of Brahmanisation in the early history of the Dimasas.

world knowledge.Name: Vakil Bazaar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vakil Bazaar is a historic bazaar located in central Shiraz, Iran. It was constructed during the reign of Karim Khan Zand in the mid to late 1760s.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bazaar is built in the Persian architectural style and serves as a welfare structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vakil Bazaar is an important cultural and historical site in Iran, reflecting the architectural and economic practices of the Zand era.
world knowledge.Details: The bazaar was designed by Karim Khan Zand and constructed by a team of engineers from the Zand territories. It is a significant landmark in Shiraz County.

world knowledge.Name: Villaggio Mall
world knowledge.Address: Al Waab street, Aspire Zone, Doha, Qatar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Villaggio Mall is a shopping mall located in the Aspire Zone in the west end of Doha, the capital city of Qatar. It was built along with the Aspire Zone for the 2006 Asian Games. The mall was partially re-opened on September 20, 2012, after meeting strict safety standards following the May fire that resulted in 19 deaths.

Major_Events.Description: On 28 May 2012, a major fire broke out in the Villaggio Mall, resulting in 19 deaths, including 13 children and four staff members trapped in the Gympanzee nursery. The fire was caused by an electrical fault at the Nike store. The incident led to significant legal proceedings and safety reforms.
The mall was partially re-opened on September 20, 2012, after meeting strict safety standards following the May fire. It has since fully reopened with expansions and extra capacity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The interiors are Italianate-themed, resembling an Italian hill town, and feature a 150-meter long indoor canal with gondolas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Villaggio Mall is a significant commercial and entertainment hub in Doha, featuring over 200 stores, including many international brands, and the Gondolania Theme Park. It was built for the 2006 Asian Games and has become a landmark in the Aspire Zone.
world knowledge.Details: The mall contains the Gondolania Theme Park, which includes the Gondolania Ice Rink, one of two ice hockey rinks in Qatar, a ten-pin bowling center, and a roller coaster. It has direct access to the Aspire Tower hotel and a nearby Doha Metro station.

world knowledge.Name: Reis Magos
world knowledge.Address: Reis Magos, Bardez, North Goa, Goa, 403114, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Reis Magos is a village located on the northern bank of the Mandovi River in Bardez, Goa, famous for the Reis Magos Fort and the Reis Magos Church. The fort was erected in 1551 to protect the narrowest point at the mouth of the Mandovi estuary and was enlarged and re-erected in 1707. It served as a residence for viceroys, a fortress, and later as a prison until 1993. The church, built in 1550 on the ruins of a pagoda, is the first church in Bardez. The fort was restored in 2008 and is now a cultural centre and tourist attraction.

Major_Events.Description: The fort was built to protect the narrowest point at the mouth of the Mandovi estuary.
The fort was enlarged and re-erected.
The fort was occupied by the British Army.
The fort was restored and converted into a cultural centre and tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fort is surrounded by sturdy laterite walls studded with typically Portuguese turrets. It commands a splendid view and is defended by 33 guns. The church bears a crown on its façade and the royal arms on its sanctuary.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Reis Magos is culturally and historically important due to its fort and church, which are significant landmarks in Goa's history. The fort played a crucial role in protecting the Mandovi estuary and served as a residence for viceroys and a prison. The church is the first in Bardez and built on the ruins of a pagoda.
world knowledge.Details: The fort was used as a residence for viceroys and later converted to a fortress. It was occupied briefly by the British Army and served as a prison until 1993. Restoration work began in 2008 with funds from the Helen Hamlyn Trust, INTACH, and the Government of Goa. The fort is now a cultural centre and tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem is a Grade II listed public house in Nottingham which claims to have been established in 1189, although there is no documentation to verify this date. The building rests against Castle Rock, upon which Nottingham Castle is built, and is attached to several caves, carved out of the soft sandstone. These were reputedly originally used as a brewhouse for the castle, dating from the medieval period. The earliest known reference to the name 'Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem' was in 1799. Before being known by its current name, it is believed that the pub was named 'The Pilgrim' and references to this name date back to 1751. The current name is believed to come from the belief that pilgrims or crusaders would stop at the inn on their journey to Jerusalem. Some elements of the pub's name are misunderstood in the modern day: 'Ye Olde' is properly pronounced 'the old' and 'trip' refers to a stop on a journey, rather than the journey itself. Locals often use a shortened version of the name, 'the Trip'. Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem is one of several pubs claiming to be the oldest in England – others that claim to be the oldest include Ye Olde Salutation Inn and The Bell Inn, also in Nottingham, and Ye Olde Fighting Cocks in St Albans in Hertfordshire. The pub claims that it was established in 1189 AD – the year that Richard the Lionheart became king and Pope Gregory VIII called for a Third Crusade to the Holy Land; however, there is no documentation to verify this date. Evidence suggests that caves in the rock against which the pub is built were used as a brewhouse for Nottingham Castle, and may date from around the time the castle was built in 1067. The oldest parts of the current building were likely constructed between 1650 and 1660, though a map by John Speed shows a previous building in existence in 1610. By 1751 the building was being used as an inn with the name The Pilgrim, and was shortly after that date purchased by William Standford. The first record of the use of the name Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem dates from 1799. Brew House Yard acquired its name after 1680.

Major_Events.Description: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem was designated as a Grade II listed building on 11 August 1952.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building rests against Castle Rock and is attached to several caves carved out of soft sandstone. The oldest parts of the current building were likely constructed between 1650 and 1660.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem is culturally significant as one of several pubs claiming to be the oldest in England. It is associated with the medieval period and the Third Crusade, and its name reflects the historical journey of pilgrims or crusaders to Jerusalem.
world knowledge.Details: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem is often referred to as 'the Trip' by locals. It is located in Brew House Yard, which acquired its name after 1680.

world knowledge.Name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves
world knowledge.Address: 3 kms south of Bhubaneswar in Odisha, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves, formerly called Kattaka Gumpha or Cuttack caves, are partly natural and partly artificial caves of archaeological, historical and religious importance. They were carved out as residential blocks for Jain monks during the reign of King Kharavela. Udayagiri means 'Sunrise Hill' and has 18 caves while Khandagiri has 15 caves. The caves are known for their finely and ornately carved structures and inscriptions.

Major_Events.Description: The Hathigumpha inscription, written by Raja Kharavela, the king of Kalinga, provides significant historical information about his reign and achievements.
The caves were renovated during the reign of Uddyotakeshari of the Somavamshi dynasty, adding sculptures of Jain Tirthankaras and Sasana Devis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The caves are partly natural and partly artificial, with finely and ornately carved structures. They include double-storeyed monasteries, relief sculptures, and intricate carvings depicting Jain religious themes, royal scenes, and various animals. Notable caves include Ranigumpha, Hathi Gumpha, and Ganesha Gumpha.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The caves are of great archaeological, historical, and religious importance, particularly for Jainism. They are listed as a 'Must See' Indian Heritage site by the Archaeological Survey of India and are considered an Adarsh Smarak Monument.
world knowledge.Details: The caves are situated on two adjacent hills, Udayagiri and Khandagiri. Udayagiri has 18 caves, and Khandagiri has 15. The Hathigumpha inscription is a key source of historical information about King Kharavela. The caves feature various sculptures and reliefs, including those of Jain Tirthankaras, Sasana Devis, and royal scenes.

world knowledge.Name: Sony Pictures Studios
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sony Pictures Studios is an American television and film studio complex located in Culver City, California. Founded in 1912 as Inceville Studios, it was later known as Triangle Studios and then Goldwyn Studios before becoming the home of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) from 1924 to 1986. The studio was sold to Lorimar-Telepictures in 1986 and later acquired by Sony in 1989. Sony invested $100 million to renovate the complex, which now houses Columbia Pictures, TriStar Pictures, and Screen Gems.

Major_Events.Description: A massive fire destroyed Vault #7 in Lot 3, resulting in the loss of hundreds of silent-era films, including Lon Chaney's 'London After Midnight'.
Sony acquired the studio lot from Warner Communications and renamed it Columbia Studios, later investing $100 million in renovations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The studio complex features a mix of historic and modern structures, including sound stages, administration buildings, and art deco elements. The original Greek colonnade entrance from Triangle Studios still stands as a Culver City historical landmark.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sony Pictures Studios is a significant landmark in the history of American cinema, having been the production site for numerous classic films and television shows. It was the original home of MGM, known for iconic films like 'The Wizard of Oz' and 'Singin' in the Rain'.
world knowledge.Details: The studio lot is open to the public for daily tours and currently houses 16 sound stages. It is also the filming location for long-running game shows like 'Jeopardy!' and 'Wheel of Fortune'.

world knowledge.Name: Concepción (volcano)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Concepción is one of two volcanoes (along with Maderas) that form the island of Ometepe, situated in Lake Nicaragua in Nicaragua, Central America. It is an active stratovolcano that forms the northwest part of the Isla de Ometepe. The volcano is considered 'pristine' due to no influence from other volcanoes on its growth, and its cone is highly symmetrical. Its growth occurs in phases based on weaknesses of the crust it rests on, causing shifts and further volcanic growth.

Major_Events.Description: The last eruption of Concepción occurred on 16 May 2024. Its eruptions are characterized by frequent, moderate-sized explosions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stratovolcano with a highly symmetrical cone, resting on a 1-kilometer-thick base of Quaternary lacustrine mudstones.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Concepción is a significant natural landmark in Nicaragua, attracting adventure seekers from around the world who travel to Ometepe Island to climb it. The volcano is also notable for its frequent eruptions and active fumaroles.
world knowledge.Details: Since 1883, Concepción has erupted at least 25 times. Active fumaroles are present just north of its summit crater. The volcano is surrounded by tropical forest with numerous trails leading to its ash-covered peak.

world knowledge.Name: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
world knowledge.Address: Across from the Hassan Tower, Rabat, Morocco
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a historic site in Rabat, Morocco, containing the tombs of King Mohammed V and his two sons, King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. Commissioned by Hassan II after Mohammed V's death in 1961, the mausoleum was designed by Vietnamese architect Cong Vo Toan, blending traditional Moroccan craftsmanship with modern materials. It was constructed on the esplanade of the ruined Almohad-era mosque, adjacent to the Hassan Tower, and completed in 1971.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the mausoleum was commissioned by Hassan II following the death of Mohammed V.
The mausoleum was completed, and Mohammed V's body was transferred here.
Prince Abdallah, son of Mohammed V, was buried in the mausoleum.
King Hassan II, son of Mohammed V, was buried in the mausoleum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mausoleum is a rectangular structure made of reinforced concrete covered with white marble. It features Moorish arches, a pyramidal green roof, and polylobed arches with sebka motifs. The interior includes a mahogany wood dome with colored glass, zellij tiling, and a white onyx cenotaph of Mohammed V. The complex also includes a mosque and a museum pavilion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mausoleum pays tribute to Mohammed V and his efforts to promote Moroccan identity through traditional craftsmanship. It is a symbol of Moroccan heritage and history.
world knowledge.Details: The complex includes a mosque and a museum pavilion dedicated to the Alaouite dynasty. A reader of the Quran is often present in the mausoleum.

world knowledge.Name: Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak is a vaulted-brickwork 'beehive' (tholos) tomb located near Kazanlak in central Bulgaria. It is part of a large royal Thracian necropolis in the Valley of the Thracian Rulers near the ancient capital of Seuthopolis. The tomb dates back to the fourth century BC and has been on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list since 1979. The paintings in the tomb are Bulgaria's best-preserved artistic masterpieces from the Hellenistic period.

Major_Events.Description: The Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site during the 3rd Session.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tomb features a narrow corridor leading to a round, domed chamber. Both areas are painted and decorated with murals created in fresco, depicting a Thracian couple at a ritual funeral feast. The walls were painted with a sanguine or dark reddish color. The dome mural shows a seated couple, musicians, horses, and various ceremonial scenes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tomb is culturally significant as it represents the artistic and burial practices of the Thracian civilization. The murals are considered masterpieces of Hellenistic art and provide insight into Thracian culture and rituals.
world knowledge.Details: To preserve the delicate paintings, the tomb is not open to the public. A full-size and exact replica was built nearby for public access. The seated woman from the tomb mural is depicted on the reverse of the Bulgarian 50 stotinki coin issued in 2005.

world knowledge.Name: Banteay Srei
world knowledge.Address: Banteay Srei District, Siem Reap, Cambodia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Banteay Srei is a 10th century CE Cambodian temple dedicated to the Hindu gods Shiva and Parvati. It was built by the courtiers Vishnukumara and Yajnavaraha, who served as counsellors to King Rajendravarman II. The temple was originally named Tribhuvanamaheshvara and was surrounded by a town called Ishvarapura. It underwent further expansion and rebuilding in the 11th century CE and remained in use until the 14th century CE. Rediscovered in 1914, it was restored in the 1930s using anastylosis.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was consecrated on 22 April 967 CE.
André Malraux stole four devatas in 1923, leading to his arrest and the return of the figures.
Banteay Srei was restored through the first important use of anastylosis at Angkor.
A drainage system was installed to prevent water damage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Banteay Srei is built largely of red sandstone, known for its intricate carvings. The temple features miniature-scale buildings, decorative lintels, and pediments depicting mythological scenes. The site consists of three concentric rectangular enclosures with a causeway leading to the sanctuary. The temple is known for its elaborate decorative wall carvings and small dimensions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Banteay Srei is considered the jewel of Khmer art due to its intricate carvings and well-preserved state. It is a significant example of 10th-century Khmer architecture and Hindu religious art.
world knowledge.Details: The temple has been subject to pilfering and vandalism, with some original statues replaced by concrete replicas. A statue of Shiva and Parvati was moved to the National Museum in Phnom Penh for safekeeping. The temple's modern name, Banteay Srei, translates to 'citadel of the women' or 'citadel of beauty,' likely referring to the intricate carvings and small dimensions of the buildings.

world knowledge.Name: Manhyia Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Manhyia Palace is the seat and official residence of the Asantehene. It was built in 1925 by the British after they demolished the Aban Palace during the War of the Golden Stool. The palace was offered to Asantehene Nana Prempeh I upon his return from exile, and he paid for it in full. It has served as the residence of two kings and was converted into a museum in 1995 after the new palace was built.

Major_Events.Description: The British demolished the original palace with explosives during this war.
The old palace was converted into a museum after the new palace was built.
The Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Jubilee Hall was commissioned as a multi-purpose convention centre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features Asante architecture from the early 1900s, with a two-story building, open verandas, a large courtyard, and statues of past kings and queens. It blends traditional Asante styles with modern architecture, including an outdoor space, entrance lobby, commercial kitchen, conference room, wine bar, and a main hall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Manhyia Palace is culturally significant as the seat of the Asantehene and a symbol of the Asante Kingdom's heritage. It houses artifacts and serves as a museum showcasing the history and culture of the Asante people.
world knowledge.Details: The palace includes the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Jubilee Hall, a multi-purpose convention centre. The museum displays artifacts such as furniture used by kings, the bronze head of Osei Agyeman Prempeh II, and life-sized wax effigies of past kings and queens.

world knowledge.Name: Amphawa Floating Market
world knowledge.Address: Amphawa District, Samut Songkhram Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Amphawa was a small community that prospered in trade and agriculture. The floating market served as the communication center of the Samut Songkhram province, with houses located along the river for easier transport by boat. People traded on boats and earned a living.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The market features many old wooden houses and a natural setting, reflecting the traditional lifestyle of the locals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Amphawa Floating Market is a popular tourist attraction that showcases the traditional Thai way of life, including river-based commerce, local cuisine, and the beauty of fireflies at night.
world knowledge.Details: The market operates from Friday to Sunday, 15:00–22:00. It offers various activities such as boat trips to see fireflies, cycling, and visiting nearby temples. The market is known for its seafood, Thai desserts, and souvenirs. Visitors can also participate in morning alms-giving to Buddhist monks.

world knowledge.Name: Kejetia Market
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kumasi Central Market, also known as Kejetia Market, is an open-air marketplace in Kumasi, a city in the Ashanti Region of Ghana. Established in 1924, it was modeled after British markets to house large numbers of vendors. It has faced challenges such as poor infrastructure and hygiene conditions, leading to redevelopment efforts starting in 2015.

Major_Events.Description: The market was established in 1924, modeled after British markets to accommodate a large number of vendors.
In August 2015, the Government of Ghana announced a redevelopment plan for the entire market.
The first phase of the redevelopment project, valued at US$259,425,000, was completed in late 2018, including a brand new market with about 8,420 stores.
The second phase of the redevelopment project commenced on 2 May 2019, estimated to cost around US$248 million and financed by Deutsche Bank.
In January and March 2016, fires destroyed more than 200 shops and vendors' property.

On 28 June 2022, the market was taken off the national grid over huge debts that had accrued for 14 months. Power was restored following a 20 percent payment of the GH¢5.2 million debt owed the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The market is an open-air marketplace with over 8,000 stores and stalls, making it the largest single market in West Africa. The redevelopment project includes modern facilities and infrastructure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kejetia Market is culturally significant as the largest single market in West Africa, serving as a major hub for trade and commerce in the Ashanti Region. It plays a crucial role in the local economy and daily life of the people of Kumasi.
world knowledge.Details: The market has over 8,000 stores and stalls, with about 50,000 daily visitors and 20,000 vendors. The redevelopment project is ongoing, with the second phase yet to be completed.

world knowledge.Name: Daecheong Dam
world knowledge.Address: 16 km north of Daejeon, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Daecheong Dam is a multi-purpose dam on the Geum River, providing flood control, water supply, and hydroelectric power generation. Construction began in 1975 and was completed in 1980. It is operated by the Korea Water Resources Corporation.

Major_Events.Description: The dam was formally commissioned on 1 December 1980.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Daecheong Dam Water Culture Center
Major_Events.Description: A water-themed cultural museum was established on 6 July 2004, featuring exhibition halls, a theater, information center, and an observatory.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The dam is a combination of concrete gravity and embankment construction, with a central clay core. It is 72 m (236 ft) high and 495 m (1,624 ft) long.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The dam is significant for its role in flood control, water supply, and hydroelectric power generation. It also supports local agriculture and reduces salinity in downstream areas. The Daecheong Dam Water Culture Center highlights the cultural and environmental aspects of the area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose dam (flood control, water supply, hydroelectric power generation)
world knowledge.Details: The dam impounds the Geum River, creating a reservoir with a storage capacity of 1,490,000,000 m³ (1,207,963 acre⋅ft). It has an installed hydroelectric capacity of 90 MW and generates around 240 million kWh annually. The reservoir is meso-stratified and experiences nutrient and organic matter loading, particularly during the heavy rainfall season. The area around the reservoir includes scenic roads, Hyeonamsa Temple, and Munuihyanggyo Confucian School.

world knowledge.Name: Kovilj Monastery
world knowledge.Address: Kovilj, Novi Sad, Bačka, Vojvodina, Serbia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded by Saint Sava in the 13th century, the monastery has been a significant cultural and religious site in Serbia. It has undergone multiple renovations and expansions due to damage from wars and natural decay. The monastery is dedicated to the Saint Archangels Gabriel and Michael and has been a center of Serbian Orthodox spirituality and culture.

Major_Events.Description: Founded to commemorate the diplomatic success of Saint Sava in preventing a war between King Stefan the First-Crowned and King Andrew II of Hungary.
After the Treaty of Karlowitz, the monastery was restored by surviving monks with help from settlers.
The present stone church was built in the Morava architectural school style.
The monastery was looted and burned during the Hungarian Revolution of 1848.
The monastery underwent significant renovation and expansion, including the construction of a new konak and winter chapel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in the Morava architectural school style of Serbo-Byzantine architecture, resembling Manasija and Ravanica. The church features a unique iconostasis painted by Aksentije Marodić, influenced by the Renaissance, with non-canonical elements such as the depiction of The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monastery is a protected cultural monument and is considered one of the most beautiful and monumental cultural-historical objects in Bačka. It has played a crucial role in the preservation of Serbian Orthodox traditions and has been a center for Byzantine chanting and monastic farming.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery is known for its honey and rakia production, with a brotherhood of 30 monks cultivating 50 ha of land and keeping 200 bee hives. It also has a drug rehabilitation center, Zemlja živih, which helps young drug addicts through a program that includes agricultural work and artistic activities.

world knowledge.Name: Awa Shrine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Awa Shrine is a Shinto shrine in Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Its foundation date is unknown, but tradition attributes it to the Inbe clan during Emperor Jimmu's reign. It was patronized by Minamoto no Yoritomo in the Kamakura period and recognized as the ichinomiya of Awa Province. Destroyed by an earthquake in 1499, it was rebuilt in 1593 by Satomi Yoshinari and later by the Satomi clan. The Tokugawa shogunate granted it stipends in 1616 and 1637. In 1875, it was designated an Imperial shrine of the first rank under State Shinto.

Major_Events.Description: The shrine was completely destroyed by a large earthquake.
The shrine was rebuilt after its destruction.
The shrine was designated as an Imperial shrine of the first rank under the Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The present Honden dates from 1881 and was renovated in 2009.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Awa Shrine is one of two shrines claiming the title of ichinomiya of former Awa Province. It holds historical importance as a site patronized by notable figures like Minamoto no Yoritomo and the Tokugawa shogunate. Archaeological investigations revealed Jōmon and Kofun period artifacts, adding to its cultural value.
world knowledge.Details: The shrine's main festival is held annually on August 10. It is a ten-kilometer walk from Tateyama Station on the JR East Uchibo Line. Archaeological findings include bronze mirrors, clay vessels, and skeletons of 22 people.

world knowledge.Name: Anne Hathaway's Cottage
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Anne Hathaway's Cottage is a twelve-roomed farmhouse where Anne Hathaway, the wife of William Shakespeare, lived as a child. The earliest part of the house dates to 1463, and it was expanded between 1610 and 1624. The Hathaway family moved there in 1542, and it was passed down through the family until financial problems forced them to sell it in 1846. The Shakespeare Birthplace Trust acquired it in 1892 and restored it after a fire in 1969.

Major_Events.Description: The cottage was badly damaged in a fire but was restored by the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust.
Horticulturist Ellen Willmott was commissioned to redesign the garden, incorporating plants mentioned in Shakespeare’s plays.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house features timber framing, typical of vernacular Tudor architecture, with multiple chimneys to spread heat evenly. It was originally a three-roomed building with one floor, later expanded to include a higher part in the 17th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cottage is culturally significant as the childhood home of Anne Hathaway, the wife of William Shakespeare, and provides insight into the life and times of the Hathaway family and Tudor architecture.
world knowledge.Details: Full-size replicas of Anne Hathaway's cottage have been built around the world. The garden features designs by Ellen Willmott, including flower beds named Miss Willmott’s garden, with plants mentioned in Shakespeare’s plays.

world knowledge.Name: Kegon Falls
world knowledge.Area: Nikkō National Park, Tochigi Prefecture, Honshū, Japan
world knowledge.Address: Lake Chūzenji, Nikkō National Park, near the city of Nikkō, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total height: 97 metres (318 ft), Total width: 7 metres (23 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kegon Falls was formed when the Daiya River was rerouted by lava flows. It is located at Lake Chūzenji, the source of the Oshiri River. The falls are known for their scenic beauty and cultural significance, as well as being a site associated with tragic events.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as one of the "Eight Views"
Major_Events.Description: Kegon Falls was recognized as one of the "Eight Views" that best showed Japan and its culture in the Shōwa period.

Major_Events.Event: Listing as one of "Japan’s Top 100 Waterfalls"
Major_Events.Description: The Japanese Ministry of the Environment listed Kegon Falls as one of "Japan’s Top 100 Waterfalls".

Misao Fujimura, a Japanese philosophy student and poet, committed suicide by jumping from Kegon Falls, leaving a farewell poem. This event was sensationalized and led to the falls becoming a notorious spot for suicides.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural plunge waterfall with a single drop, formed by lava flows. About twelve smaller waterfalls are situated behind and to the sides, leaking through cracks between the mountain and the lava flows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kegon Falls is celebrated for its scenic beauty and is a symbol of Japan's natural wonders. It holds cultural importance as one of the "Eight Views" of the Shōwa period and one of "Japan’s Top 100 Waterfalls". However, it is also infamously associated with suicides, particularly among Japanese youth.
world knowledge.Details: The falls are particularly popular in autumn for viewing fall colors. The site has been the subject of literary and media attention due to its association with tragic events, including the suicide of Misao Fujimura and subsequent suicides by others.

world knowledge.Name: Newstead Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Newstead Abbey, originally an Augustinian priory founded by King Henry II around 1170, was converted into a domestic home after the Dissolution of the Monasteries. It is best known as the ancestral home of Lord Byron. The priory was rebuilt and extended in the late 13th and 15th centuries. It was granted to Sir John Byron by Henry VIII in 1540, who converted it into a country house. The estate passed through several generations of the Byron family, including the famous poet Lord Byron, who inherited it in 1798. The Abbey has undergone various renovations and changes in ownership, and it is now owned by Nottingham City Council.

Major_Events.Description: The priory was surrendered to the Crown, and the monks were granted pensions. The property was later granted to Sir John Byron, who converted it into a country house.
George Gordon Byron inherited Newstead Abbey at the age of 10, becoming the 6th Baron Byron. The estate influenced his poetry and personal identity.
Thomas Wildman, a former schoolmate of Byron, purchased the Abbey for £94,500, easing Byron's financial troubles.
Sir Julien Cahn presented Newstead Abbey to Nottingham Corporation, and it has since been owned by Nottingham City Council.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Newstead Abbey features a mix of medieval and Gothic architectural styles. The original 13th-century ecclesiastical buildings were largely ruined during the Dissolution of the Monasteries, but significant parts were later converted into a country house. The Abbey includes a Great Hall, Prior's Lodgings, and a chapel, with later additions and renovations by various owners.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Newstead Abbey is culturally significant as the ancestral home of the famous poet Lord Byron, who was influenced by the estate's history and decay. It is also a Grade I listed building and represents the transition from monastic life to aristocratic residence in English history.
world knowledge.Details: The Abbey houses a museum containing Byron memorabilia and hosts weddings and other events. It is currently on the national buildings at risk register due to water ingress, and Nottingham City Council is seeking funding for remedial works.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Caen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Caen was built around 1060 by William the Conqueror. It played a significant role in Norman strategy and policy. Over the centuries, it saw several engagements during the Hundred Years' War and was bombed during World War II. The castle has undergone various modifications and restorations, including recent efforts to reveal and preserve its medieval traces.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was built by William the Conqueror, who later successfully conquered England in 1066.

A royal court celebration for Christmas in the Aula of Caen Castle brought together Henry II and his sons, the future kings of England Richard the Lionheart and John Lackland, receiving more than a thousand knights.
Caen Castle, along with all of Normandy, was recaptured by the French Crown. Philip II reinforced the fortifications.
The castle saw several engagements during the Hundred Years' War.
The keep was pulled down during the French Revolution by order of the National Convention.
The castle, used as a barracks during World War II, was bombed and seriously damaged.
Archaeologist Michel de Boüard started excavations in 1946 to uncover medieval traces. The Musée des Beaux-Arts was installed in 1967 and opened in 1971.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle was constructed on a hillock and features large ramparts, two main entrances (porte sur la ville and porte des champs) reinforced by barbicans, and a dry moat. The keep, now razed, had a large square section with round towers at each corner. The curtain walls date mostly from the 15th century, with some parts from the 12th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Caen is a significant historical and cultural landmark, representing Norman medieval architecture and history. It has been officially classed as a Monument historique since 1997 and serves as a museum showcasing medieval artifacts and art.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a defensive fortress, the castle now serves as a museum and historical site.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is one of the largest in Western Europe. Recent restoration efforts include the removal of 6,000 m³ of earth to reveal the north-west wall of the 12th century, uncovering a 15th-century private house cellar, a powder magazine, and traces of a 14th-century forge. The base of the keep has been cleared, and ongoing excavations continue to uncover historical details.

world knowledge.Name: Castle of Rocca Calascio
world knowledge.Address: Municipality of Calascio, Province of L'Aquila, Abruzzo, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castle of Rocca Calascio is a mountaintop fortress built exclusively for military purposes, intended to accommodate troops and not as a residence for nobles. Construction began in the 10th century as a single watchtower, with a walled courtyard and four cylindrical towers added in the 13th century. The fortress was damaged by the 1461 L'Aquila earthquake and was not rebuilt.

Major_Events.Description: The fortress was badly damaged by an earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 7 to 8 on the Richter Scale.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built of stone and masonry, the fortress features a walled courtyard with four cylindrical towers at the corners around a taller inner tower. The lower half is built with distinctively larger stones to make its base impenetrable.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Castle of Rocca Calascio is the highest fortress in the Apennines and lies within the Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park. It has been used as a filming location for several movies, including 'Ladyhawke,' 'The Name of the Rose,' and 'The American.'
world knowledge.Details: Near the fortress is Santa Maria della Pietà, an octagonal church built in the 17th century. The fortress overlooks the Plain of Navelli and is located alongside the high plain of Campo Imperatore.

world knowledge.Name: Malbork Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork, commonly known as Malbork Castle, is a brick gothic castle complex built in the 13th century and significantly expanded in the 14th century. It was constructed by the Teutonic Order, a German Catholic religious order of crusaders, and named Marienburg in honour of Mary, mother of Jesus. The castle served as a Polish royal residence and the seat of Polish offices and institutions until the First Partition of Poland in 1772. It was under German rule for over 170 years until 1945. UNESCO designated it a World Heritage Site in 1997.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was sold by Bohemian mercenaries to King Casimir IV of Poland in lieu of indemnities.
The castle was besieged following the Teutonic Order's defeat at the Battle of Grunwald. Heinrich von Plauen successfully led the defence.
The castle came under Prussian rule.
More than half the castle was destroyed during fighting in the area.
The castle was designated a World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is a classic example of a medieval fortress and the largest brick castle in the world. It consists of three separate castles – the High, Middle, and Lower Castles, separated by multiple dry moats and towers. The castle has several subdivisions and numerous layers of defensive walls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Malbork Castle is culturally and historically important as it represents the power and influence of the Teutonic Order during the medieval period. It is also a symbol of Polish and German history and has been designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Polish national Historic Monument.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a fortress by the Teutonic Order, it later served as a Polish royal residence and now functions as a museum.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is the largest brick complex in Europe and has undergone significant restoration since 1962. It houses the Castle Museum and features an amber exhibition. The castle's principal church, dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary, was restored in 2016.

world knowledge.Name: Riegersburg Castle
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 3 kilometres of walls with 5 gates and 2 trenches, 108 rooms
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Riegersburg Castle is a medieval castle situated on an extinct volcano above the town of Riegersburg in the Austrian state of Styria. The castle was built on a hill which had once been an ancient volcano. The history of the castle begins in the year 1122. The first knight who is known to have lived there is Rudiger von Hohenberg. Over the centuries the castle had many different owners, but only few played an important role. The most important owner was the baroness Katharina Elisabeth von Wechsler, who finished the castle between 1637 and 1653, making it one of the biggest and strongest castles in the country. The castle was a safe place for the people nearby, sometimes offering refuge inside its walls for a few thousand during conflicts with the Turks and Hungarians.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was taken by the 10th Guards Rifle Division of Soviet forces advancing towards Graz on 8 May 1945.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is built on the petrified remains of the solidified molten interior of a large stratovolcano. The ancient basalt of the hill was used to build the castle. It is surrounded by 3 kilometres of walls with 5 gates and 2 trenches and it contains 108 rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Riegersburg Castle is culturally and historically important due to its long history dating back to the medieval period, its role as a refuge during conflicts, and its architectural uniqueness being built on an extinct volcano. It also houses a museum that showcases the history of the castle and exhibits on witches and sorcerers.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is owned by the Princely Family of Liechtenstein, who live in a house in the town of Riegersburg. The castle serves as a museum with 25 out of the 108 rooms open to tourists. Sixteen of the rooms show the history of Riegersburg Castle and nine deal with witches and sorcerers.

world knowledge.Name: Valdštejn Castle
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Second half of the thirteenth century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valdštejn Castle is an early Gothic fortress built by the Counts of the Waldstein family. It was occupied by the Hussites after 1420 and later by robber barons. In 1621, the abandoned castle was bought back by the Waldsteins, whose most illustrious member was Albrecht von Wallenstein. During the Baroque period, they built a pilgrimage church dedicated to John of Nepomuk in 1722 on the ruins of the castle.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was occupied by the Hussites after 1420.
The abandoned castle was bought back by the Waldsteins.
A pilgrimage church dedicated to John of Nepomuk was built on the ruins of the castle during the Baroque period.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Early Gothic fortress with later Baroque additions, including a pilgrimage church.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valdštejn Castle is significant as an early Gothic fortress and for its later Baroque additions, reflecting the historical and architectural evolution of the region. It is also notable for its association with the Waldstein family and Albrecht von Wallenstein.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is located in the cliff dwelling city of Hruboskalsko, in the Bohemian Paradise (Český ráj).

world knowledge.Name: Turaida Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Turaida Castle, originally named Fredeland ('Land of Peace'), was constructed in 1214 by the Livonian Brothers of the Sword under the direction of Albert, Archbishop of Riga. It was built on the site of a previous wooden Livonian castle. The castle underwent several modifications over the centuries, including the addition of a southern tower in the 14th century and a western tower in the 15th century to accommodate firearms. It was abandoned after a fire in 1776 and fell into ruin. Restoration and archaeological work began in 1976, revealing much of its earlier state.

Major_Events.Description: One of the biggest battles of the Livonian crusade between Estonian tribes and Livonian Brothers of the Sword.
The Livonian Order was decisively defeated by the residents of Riga allied with the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under command of Vytenis.
The castle was abandoned after a fire and gradually became ruinous.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is a classic red-brick construction typical of the Baltic crusading orders. It features a main tower, a semi-rounded western tower, and a southern tower. The inner yard contains domestic buildings and living accommodations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Turaida Castle is a significant historical site in Latvia, representing the medieval architecture and the history of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword and the Teutonic Order. It is a key part of the Turaida Museum Reserve and offers insights into the Gauja Livonians and the region's history.
world knowledge.Details: The castle dominates the Museum Reserve and offers exhibitions about the history of the brick castle and the Gauja Livonians. From the main tower, visitors can view the unique landscape of the Gauja valley and the territory of the Turaida Museum Reserve.

world knowledge.Name: Rozafa Castle
world knowledge.Address: Near the city of Shkodër, Albania
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Rises 130 metres (430 ft) above sea level
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rozafa Castle, also known as Shkodër Castle, is a historic castle near Shkodër, Albania. It was originally an Illyrian stronghold and has been controlled by various empires and kingdoms throughout history, including the Roman Empire, Byzantine Empire, and Ottoman Empire. The castle is significant for its role in the Third Illyrian War and its transformation from a Venetian Catholic church to a mosque after the Ottoman conquest.

Major_Events.Description: The Illyrian king Gentius was defeated by the Roman army led by L. Anicius Gallus, leading to the fall of the Illyrian kingdom.
The Ottoman Empire captured the city of Shkodër after a prolonged siege.
Another significant siege during the Balkan Wars.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is constructed primarily of limestone and brick. The visible walls are mostly of Venetian construction, and it includes the ruins of a 13th-century Venetian Catholic church that was later transformed into the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Mosque.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rozafa Castle is culturally significant due to its long history and the legend of Rozafa, which involves human sacrifice and immurement to ensure the castle's construction. The castle is also an important symbol of Albanian heritage and resistance.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is part of the Archaeological Park of Albania and is associated with the legend of Rozafa, which reflects the worship of the earth mother goddess in Albanian folk beliefs. Local traditions involve using limestone deposits from the castle for medicinal purposes.

world knowledge.Name: Gözne Castle
world knowledge.Address: Gözne town, Toros Mountains, Mersin Province, Turkey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gözne Castle is a medieval castle built with distinctive Armenian masonry. It served as a fortified estate house and protected a strategic route linking the Mediterranean coast to Çandır Castle and Lampron, the main seats of Het'umid power in the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.

Major_Events.Description: An extensive photographic survey and plan of Gözne Castle was made in 1979.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site consists of two fortified chambers without connecting masonry walls. The east building has a vaulted rectangular hall, a defensive doorway, four towers, five extremely narrow windows, and a single embrasured loophole. The west building is a two-story hexagonal tower-donjon with two doors and three windows. Projecting corbels at the top once supported fighting platforms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is historically significant as a fortified estate house and for its role in protecting a strategic route during the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is accessible only from the north, via Gözne town. It is located at an altitude of 1,120 metres and is open to visits. Recently, a picnic area was established to the north of the castle.

world knowledge.Name: Hochosterwitz Castle
world knowledge.Address: near Sankt Georgen am Längsee, east of Sankt Veit an der Glan, Carinthia, Austria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hochosterwitz Castle is considered one of Austria's most impressive medieval castles. It has a history dating back to the Bronze Age and was first mentioned in an 860 deed.
