The castle has been through various ownerships, including the Archdiocese of Salzburg, the Sponheim dynasty, and the Osterwitz noble family. It was fortified in the 16th century by Baron George Khevenhüller to defend against Turkish invasions. The castle has remained in the Khevenhüller family since then and is a major tourist attraction.

Major_Events.Event: Siege by Countess Margaret of Tyrol
Major_Events.Description: According to legend, the castle was besieged by the troops of Countess Margaret of Tyrol. The garrison deceived the invaders by slaughtering their last ox, filling it with grain, and throwing it over the wall to pretend they had ample provisions.
The castle was badly damaged by numerous Turkish campaigns in the 15th century.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation by Bishop Matthäus Lang von Wellenburg
Major_Events.Description: Emperor Maximilian I handed the castle to Bishop Matthäus Lang von Wellenburg, who undertook a substantial renovation project.
Baron George Khevenhüller fortified the castle, building an armory and 14 gates to defend against Turkish invasions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rock castle with 14 gates, each equipped with different defense mechanisms. The castle is built on a 172-metre high dolomite rock and features a 620-metre long pathway leading up to the castle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hochosterwitz Castle is a landmark of Carinthia and a major tourist attraction. It is considered one of Austria's most impressive medieval castles and has a rich history dating back to the Bronze Age. The castle's unique fortification and historical events contribute to its cultural significance.
world knowledge.Details: Some parts of the castle are open to the public from Easter to the end of October. Tourists can walk the 620-metre long pathway through the 14 gates up to the castle. The castle rooms hold a collection of prehistoric artifacts, paintings, weapons, and armor. A 1:25 miniature scale model of the castle can be seen at Minimundus in Klagenfurt.

world knowledge.Name: Kost Castle
world knowledge.Address: Libošovice municipality, Jičín District, Hradec Králové Region, Czech Republic
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kost Castle, a Gothic castle, was founded by Beneš von Wartenberg before 1349 and completed by his sons Peter and Marquard von Wartenberg in a high Gothic style. It has retained most of its original features and is well preserved. The castle has been owned by several noble families, including the Zajíc von Hasenburg, Schellenberg, Biberstein, and Lobkowicz families.

Major_Events.Event: Move of Zajíc von Hasenburg family
Major_Events.Description: The Zajíc von Hasenburg family moved to the castle after Nicolaus von Hasenburg married Skunka, the widow of Peter von Wartenberg.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is known for its donjon, called Bílá věž ("white tower"), protected by two circles of fortress walls. It features a trapezoid-like ground-plan tower designed to minimize damage from catapult attacks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kost Castle is a well-preserved example of Gothic architecture and has been owned by several notable noble families, contributing to its historical importance in the Czech Republic.
world knowledge.Details: Unlike most other castles in Bohemia, it does not lie on a hill but on a spit between two brooks. The trapezoidal tower's corners face the areas of most likely catapult attacks to minimize damage.

world knowledge.Name: Poenari Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Poenari Castle, also known as Poenari Citadel, is a ruined castle in Romania which was a home of Vlad the Impaler. Constructed around the beginning of the 13th century by Wallachians, it became the main citadel of the Basarab rulers in the 14th century. Vlad III the Impaler repaired and consolidated the structure in 1459, making it one of his main fortresses. The castle was abandoned in the first half of the 16th century and was in ruins by the 17th century. It suffered damage from earthquakes in 1913, 1940, and 1977 but was slightly repaired. Since 2009, the site has been administered by the Argeș County Museum.

Major_Events.Description: A landslide caused by an earthquake brought down parts of the castle which crashed into the river far below.
An earthquake caused further damage to the castle.
An earthquake caused further damage to the castle.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is situated on top of a mountain and accessed by climbing 1,480 concrete stairs. It is located on the plateau of Mount Cetatea, facing the west side of the Transfăgărășan, on a canyon formed on the Argeș River valley, close to the Făgăraș Mountains.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Poenari Castle is culturally and historically important due to its association with Vlad the Impaler, who is often linked to the Dracula legend. It has been featured in various media, including television series, novels, and documentaries, further cementing its place in popular culture.
world knowledge.Details: A smaller replica of Poenari Castle was built in 1906 in Bucharest in Carol Park. It serves currently as home to the National Office For The Cult of Heroes and is open for public twice in a year: on the Heroes’ Day and on the Romanian Army National Day (25 October). Poenari Castle has been featured in various media, including the BBC Worldwide/Starz television series Da Vinci's Demons, The Hardy Boys/Nancy Drew Mysteries, Dan Simmons' novel "Children of the Night", and the Fallout 3 video game. It was also featured as a haunted location in Ghost Hunters International.

world knowledge.Name: Pszczyna Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pszczyna Castle, originally constructed in the 13th century or earlier in Gothic style, was rebuilt in Renaissance style in the 17th century and later transformed into a Baroque-Classical style palace. It served as a residence for Polish Piast dukes, the German von Promnitz noble clan, and the German von Pless family. It became state property in 1936 and was turned into a museum in 1946.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was reconstructed in Baroque Revival architecture by French architect Gabriel-Hippolyte Destailleur.
The palace hosted William II, German Emperor, and military discussions with generals like Erich Ludendorff and Paul von Hindenburg.
The complex was occupied by the Wehrmacht following the German-Soviet invasion of Poland.
After serving as a Soviet military hospital, the palace was turned into a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally Gothic, rebuilt in Renaissance and later Baroque-Classical styles. Features Baroque Revival architecture with a Chamber of Mirrors, Art Nouveau dining hall, and Grand Staircase designed by Destailleur.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the most beautiful castle residences in Poland, voted as one of the "Seven Architectural Wonders of the Silesian Voivodeship." It reflects the history of Polish, Silesian, and German nobility and is a significant cultural and historical landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The Royal Apartments, also known as the Apartamenty Cesarskie, are fully recreated with original furnishings. The palace also features rooms of Princess Mary Theresa Olivia Cornwallis-West von Pless, decorated with her pictures and hunting trophies.

world knowledge.Name: Chęciny Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chęciny Royal Castle was built in the late 13th century in Chęciny, Poland. It fell into ruin in the 18th century and remains in that state to this day. The construction of the fortress probably began in the late 13th century. It is certain that the castle existed in 1306, when king Władysław I the Elbow-high gave it to the Archbishop of Kraków, Jan Muskata. A year later, under the pretext of detection of a plot against the royal power, the castle returned to the king. It played a significant role as a place of concentration of troops departing for war with the Teutonic Knights. After the death of Władysław the Elbow-high the stronghold was enlarged by Casimir III the Great. At that time Chęciny become a residence of the king's second wife Adelaide of Hesse. In following years it was also a residence of Elisabeth of Poland, Queen of Hungary, Sophia of Halshany and her son Władysław III of Varna and Bona Sforza. Later it was used for many years as a state prison. Among imprisoned here were Michael Küchmeister von Sternberg future Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, Andrzej Wingold, Jogaila's half-brother and Warcisław of Gotartowice. In the second half of the 16th century, the castle began to decline. In 1588 the parliament ordered to transfer the castle's inventories to the Chęciny Church and in 1607, during the Zebrzydowski Rebellion the fortifications and buildings were partially destroyed and burned. The castle briefly regained its former glory due to reconstruction initiated by Stanisław Branicki, starost of Chęciny, but in 1655-1657 it was almost completely destroyed by Swedish-Brandenburgian and Transylvanian troops. The destruction was completed in 1707 during another Swedish occupation. Then, the last residents left the castle. Over the next century the medieval walls become a source of building material for local villagers.

Major_Events.Description: The fortifications and buildings were partially destroyed and burned.
The castle was almost completely destroyed.
The destruction of the castle was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Polish Gothic
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle played a significant role as a place of concentration of troops departing for war with the Teutonic Knights and was used as a state prison. It was also a residence for several notable historical figures.
Notable_Visitors: Elisabeth of Poland, Queen of Hungary
world knowledge.Details: The castle fell into ruin in the 18th century and remains in that state to this day. Over the next century the medieval walls become a source of building material for local villagers.

world knowledge.Name: Darłowo Castle
world knowledge.Address: Darłowo, West Pomeranian Voivodeship in Poland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Castle of the Pomeranian Dukes - the only Gothic castle located on the coast of the Baltic Sea in Poland. The castle's construction began in 1352, in the reign of Bogusław V, whose reign began the alliance with the Hanseatic League. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the castle was used as a warehouse and a prison. In 1930, the castle was turned into a museum. The castle was enlarged and modernised in the fifteenth and sixteenth century, becoming a worthy royal residence. The greatest expansion of the castle was done under the reign of Eric of Pomerania, who rebuilt the castle to that of the design of his previous residence, Kronborg Castle. He also modernised the castle's defensive fortifications, and built a second defence line, in the form of dikes around the castle. The following expansion of the castle was done under the reign of Duke Bogusław X, when a new wing was built. The next changes were done by Duke Barnim XI. After a great fire, which devastated the castle in 1624, the last Duke of the House of Pomerania, Bogusław XIV, rebuilt the castle. However, he did not restore the castle to its original architectural style. The castle lost many of its defences, and a chapel was built inside the Duke Hall. After the duke's death, his widow, Duchess Elżbieta, took over the castle, and lived there until her death.

Major_Events.Description: The castle's construction began in 1352, in the reign of Bogusław V.
The castle was rebuilt under the reign of Eric of Pomerania.
A great fire devastated the castle in 1624.
The castle was turned into a museum in 1930.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic style, close to a square layout with a tower measuring 24 metres in height. The castle was modernised and expanded several times, with defensive fortifications and a second defence line in the form of dikes around the castle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The only Gothic castle located on the coast of the Baltic Sea in Poland, it served as a residence for the Pomeranian Dukes and played a significant role in the region's history, including alliances with the Hanseatic League.
world knowledge.Details: The town of Darłowo was given the title of The Royal City of Darłowo (Królewskie Miasto Darłowo, Polish).

world knowledge.Name: Křivoklát Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Křivoklát Castle was founded in the 12th century and belonged to the kings of Bohemia. It was built as a large, monumental royal castle during the reign of Otakar II of Bohemia, later rebuilt by King Wenceslaus IV, and enlarged by King Vladislaus II. The castle was damaged by fire several times, turned into a harsh prison, and deteriorated until the 19th century when the Fürstenberg family reconstructed it after a fire in 1826. The family owned the castle until 1929.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was reconstructed after a fire in 1826 by the Fürstenberg family.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Monumental royal castle with Gothic elements, later rebuilt and enlarged by various kings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Křivoklát Castle is protected as a national cultural monument and represents a significant part of Czech history and heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum, tourist destination, and place for theatrical exhibitions
world knowledge.Details: Collections of hunting weapons, Gothic paintings, and books are stored at the castle.

world knowledge.Name: Gaziantep Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: First used as an observation point during the Hittite Empire, it was expanded into a castle during Roman rule. It underwent further expansion and renovation under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I between AD 527 and 565. The castle saw changes during the reign of the Ayyubids in the 12th and 13th centuries, as well as the Ottoman Empire, and played an important role during the Turkish War of Independence of the early 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: On 6 February 2023, the castle was severely damaged by two consecutive earthquakes. Some of the eastern and southern bastions collapsed, and iron railings and walls around the castle were seriously damaged.
Restoration work began in September 2023 with the support of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and it is estimated that the castle will open its doors to tourists at the end of 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The walls are built of stone and the castle has 12 bastions. The castle has been renovated numerous times.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle played an important role during the Turkish War of Independence of the early 20th century. It is now used as the Gaziantep Defence and Heroism Panoramic Museum, showcasing the city's defense against French forces after the fall of the Ottoman Empire.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Gaziantep Defence and Heroism Panoramic Museum
world knowledge.Details: The castle is currently undergoing restoration and is estimated to reopen to tourists at the end of 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Castle of Siklós
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Castle of Siklós is a medieval castle built by Baron János György Benyó in the 13th century in Siklós, Hungary. It has been owned by various families, including the Soklyosi, Garai, and Batthyány families. The castle was captured by the Ottoman Turks in 1543 and later nationalized in 1948. It was heavily damaged during World War II and restored starting in 1955, eventually opening as a museum and hotel.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was first mentioned in a charter from 1294, named as the property of the Soklyosi family.
The castle was taken away from the Soklyosi family by King Sigismund as punishment for a failed rebellion.
Disgruntled nobles led by Count György II Benyóvszky temporarily imprisoned King Sigismund in the castle.
After a three-day battle, the castle was captured by the Ottoman Turks.
The castle was nationalized by the state.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and opening to the public
Major_Events.Description: The castle was renovated in 2009 and opened to the public in 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is noted for its Gothic and Renaissance style architecture. The oldest building is in the southern part of the residential wing, and it houses a chapel built in the 14th and 15th centuries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Castle of Siklós is culturally and historically significant as a medieval castle that has witnessed various historical events, including ownership changes, battles, and nationalization. It serves as a museum and hotel, preserving its rich history.
world knowledge.Details: Legend has it that a giant snake guarded the treasures in the basement. The castle was built and owned by the Benyóvszky de Siklósvar branch of the family until it was nationalized in 1948.

world knowledge.Name: Kaninë Castle
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 3rd century BC, Reconstructed in the 6th century AD
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kaninë Castle, located in the village of Kaninë near Vlorë, Albania, is one of the oldest settlements in the Vlora region. Originally built in the 3rd century BC, it was transformed into a fortress town in the 4th century AD and reconstructed by Justinian I in the 6th century AD. It served as the center of the Principality of Valona in the 14th century.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was transformed into a fortress town.
The castle was reconstructed by Justinian I.

Major_Events.Event: Center of the Principality of Valona
Major_Events.Description: The castle became the center of the Principality of Valona.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is built on the side of the Shushicë Mountain, about 380 meters above sea level, and covers an area of 3.6 hectares. It was constructed on the site of an ancient settlement.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kaninë Castle is historically significant as one of the oldest settlements in the Vlora region and for its role as the center of the Principality of Valona in the 14th century.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is open to the public and is a notable historic site in Albania.

world knowledge.Name: Paphos Castle
world knowledge.Area: Western end of the city port
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a Byzantine fortress built to protect the port, destroyed in the earthquake of 1222, rebuilt and expanded by the Lusignans in the 13th century, restored by the Ottomans in 1592. It served as a military stronghold, salt depot, and now a tourist attraction.

Major_Events.Description: The original Byzantine fortress was destroyed.
The castle was restored by the Turkish governor of Cyprus, Ahmet Pasha.
The castle resisted the Genoese invasion.
The castle was one of the few not captured by the Mamluks.
The castle was destroyed after 16 days of fierce fighting.
The castle ceased to be used for military purposes and became a salt depot.
The castle was devastated, and repairs were completed in 1969.
The castle was hit by Turkish air and naval forces but suffered no serious damage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Medieval style, large rectangular tower with a closed courtyard, small square tower on the roof, 12 ramparts for cannons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Represents one of the most characteristic landmarks of Paphos, serves as a setting for the annual Paphos Outdoor Cultural Festival, and is a significant historical and architectural site.
world knowledge.Details: Admission is €2.50, visiting hours are 8:30-17:00 in winter and 8:30-19:30 during summer. The ground floor is wheelchair accessible, but the upper floor is not. The castle has been the subject of several archaeological excavations.

world knowledge.Name: Ogrodzieniec Castle
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Situated on the top of 515.5-metre-high Castle Mountain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ogrodzieniec Castle is a ruined medieval castle with origins in the 14th century. It was rebuilt several times and has a long history of ownership changes, battles, and reconstructions. The castle was partly burnt by Swedish troops in 1655 and suffered a major fire in 1702, after which it was never rebuilt. It was nationalized after World War II and opened to visitors in 1973.

Major_Events.Description: The first stronghold on the site was razed to the ground.

Major_Events.Event: Capture by Austrian archduke Maximilian III
Major_Events.Description: The castle was captured during a conflict over the Polish-Lithuanian throne.
The castle was partly burnt by Swedish troops.
Over half of the castle burned in a fire set by troops of Charles XII of Sweden.
The castle was nationalized and preserved for visitors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a Gothic castle, it was later rebuilt in the Renaissance style. The castle is well integrated into the surrounding rocks, with defensive walls closing the circuit formed by the rocks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is part of the Trail of the Eagles' Nests, a hiking trail connecting several well-known castles in the region. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and TV series, including 'The Witcher' and 'Janosik.'
world knowledge.Details: The castle is said to be haunted by the 'Black Dog of Ogrodzieniec,' a local folklore figure. Fragments of Renaissance frescoes of lilies are still visible on the bottom floor. A nearby chapel in Podzamcze village contains original elements from the castle chapel.

world knowledge.Name: Ēdole Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ēdole Castle, originally built for the bishop of Courland between 1264 and 1267, was later owned by the Baltic-German Baron von Behr and his descendants from 1561 until 1920. It underwent significant expansions and reconstructions, particularly in the 16th century and from 1835 to 1841, transforming it into one of the first examples of Neo-Gothic architecture in Kurzeme. The castle was partly burned during the Russian Revolution of 1905 and subsequently remodeled between 1906 and 1907.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was partly burned during the Russian Revolution of 1905.
The castle underwent a major reconstruction to become one of the first samples of Neo-Gothic architecture in Kurzeme.
A household yard and tower were built, and the façade was remodeled with its Gothic forms preserved.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic Revival architecture, originally consisting of two residential buildings linked by a stone wall, surrounded by a landscape park. The castle features Neo-Gothic architectural elements and a remodeled façade with preserved Gothic forms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ēdole Castle is considered an architectural and archaeological monument of national importance in Latvia, representing a significant period in the region's history and architectural evolution.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is situated on the banks of Ēdole Lake and is an example of Gothic Revival architecture. It has undergone several reconstructions and expansions, reflecting its historical and architectural significance in Latvia.

world knowledge.Name: Frederiksborg Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built as a royal residence for King Christian IV of Denmark-Norway, replacing an older castle acquired by Frederick II. It became the largest Renaissance residence in Scandinavia. After a serious fire in 1859, it was rebuilt and reopened as the Danish Museum of National History in 1882.

Major_Events.Description: A serious fire destroyed most of the building, but the Chapel, the Audience Chamber, and the Privy Passage were not seriously damaged. Reconstruction was funded by public subscription and contributions from J. C. Jacobsen.
The treaty signed in the castle ended the Great Northern War between Sweden and Denmark-Norway.
During the Second Northern War, the castle was captured by the Swedes who took most of its artworks as war reparations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in the Flemish and Dutch Renaissance style (Northern Mannerism) with red brick, stepped gables, towering spires, and light sandstone decorations. The symmetry of the main structure is broken by the large bell tower on the Chapel Wing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is culturally and historically important as it was the first Danish castle built inland for purely recreational purposes rather than for defense. It houses the Danish Museum of National History and contains the largest collection of portrait paintings in Denmark.
world knowledge.Details: The castle features prominently in literature and media, including Theodor Fontane's novel 'Irretrievable', the 1978 Olsen-banden film 'The Olsen Gang Sees Red', the 19th season of 'The Amazing Race', and the 5th episode of 'La casa de papel'. It is also a principal setting in Rose Tremain's novel 'Music and Silence'.

world knowledge.Name: Ambras Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ambras Castle is a Renaissance castle and palace located in the hills above Innsbruck, Austria. It was built in the 16th century on the site of an earlier 10th-century castle. The cultural and historical importance of the castle is closely connected with Archduke Ferdinand II, who served as its resident from 1567 to 1595. Ferdinand II was a prominent collector of art and transformed the medieval fortress into a Renaissance castle as a gift for his wife Philippine Welser. The castle houses one of the oldest museums in the world, featuring collections of armor, art, and natural wonders.

Major_Events.Description: Archduke Ferdinand II ordered the transformation of the medieval fortress into a Renaissance castle for his wife Philippine Welser.
Ambras Castle served as the residence of Archduke Ferdinand II and his family.
The castle was converted into a museum and subsequently renovated.
A comprehensive restoration took place of the Spanish Hall, the Upper Castle residential quarters, and the inner courtyard.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Ambras Castle is a Renaissance-style castle featuring the Spanish Hall, a notable example of German Renaissance architecture with intricate wood-inlay ceilings and walls adorned with 27 full-length portraits of the rulers of Tyrol. The Lower Castle contains armories and the Chamber of Art and Wonders, while the Upper Castle houses the Habsburg Portrait Gallery.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ambras Castle is culturally significant as one of the oldest museums in the world, housing extensive collections of art, armor, and natural wonders. It is closely associated with Archduke Ferdinand II, a prominent patron of the arts and a significant figure in Habsburg history.
world knowledge.Details: Ambras Castle is part of the Kunsthistorisches Museum Vienna and is a federal museum of the Republic of Austria. It features the Spanish Hall, the Chamber of Art and Wonders, and the Habsburg Portrait Gallery, among other notable collections.

world knowledge.Name: Český Krumlov Castle
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Second largest castle and chateau complex in the Czech Republic
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Český Krumlov Castle dates back to 1253 when the first castle was built by the Vítkovci family. It came under the Rosenberg family’s control in 1302, who initiated a significant Renaissance makeover. By the 17th century, the castle was under the Eggenberg family, who were responsible for Baroque renovations. In 1717, it passed to the Schwarzenbergs. It was transferred to the Czech provincial properties in 1947 and became a national monument in 1989. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1992.

Major_Events.Description: The first castle was built by the Vítkovci family.
The castle came under the Rosenberg family’s control, who initiated a significant Renaissance makeover.
The Eggenberg family were responsible for Baroque renovations and expansions to the castle.
The Schwarzenberg property, including Český Krumlov, was transferred to the Czech provincial properties.
The entire area was declared a national monument.

Major_Events.Event: Added to UNESCO World Heritage List
Major_Events.Description: The castle was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle stands on a steep and long rocky headland. It includes the Lower Castle with an old palace and tower from the 13th century, the Upper Castle (Rosenberg Palace), the unique five-story Cloak Bridge from 1764, and the Český Krumlov Baroque Theatre from 1767. The castle gardens are in the late baroque style with a cascade fountain from the middle of the 18th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a national heritage site and a major tourist attraction. It is the second most visited castle in the Czech Republic and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is said to be haunted by the White Lady, supposedly the ghost of Perchta of Rosenberg. The revolving auditorium has been located in the gardens since 1959.

world knowledge.Name: Vyborg Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vyborg Castle is a medieval fortress built by the Swedes in 1293 during the Third Swedish Crusade. It served as a strategic stronghold for the Swedish realm in the Karelian region and played a significant role in the Swedish–Novgorodian Wars. The castle was constructed on the site of a pre-existing Karelian fortress and became a key defensive structure against Russian invasions. Over the centuries, it underwent various renovations and expansions. It was captured by the Russians in 1710, returned to Finnish hands in 1812, and annexed by the Soviet Union in 1944. Today, it houses the Vyborg Regional Museum.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was besieged by the Russians, but the defenders were saved by the 'Viborg blast,' a mysterious explosion that scared the Russians away.
As a result of border changes in World War II, Vyborg was annexed by the Soviet Union.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main castle has an irregular four-cornered layout with the immense tower of St. Olav as its biggest section. The tower is 3–4 storeys tall, varying in places. Outer defensive works surround the main castle, following the islet's coastlines.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vyborg Castle is culturally and historically significant as it represents the medieval Swedish influence in the Karelian region and its role in the Swedish–Novgorodian Wars. It is one of the three major castles of Finland and serves as a symbol of the region's complex history.
world knowledge.Details: The castle was originally built as the easternmost outpost of the medieval Kingdom of Sweden. It is located on a little islet in the innermost corner of the Gulf of Finland. The town of Vyborg evolved around the castle, but it had to be moved to its present location due to lack of space. The castle owes its present appearance to extensive restorations undertaken in the 1890s.

world knowledge.Name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is China's first national forest park, established in 1982. It is part of the larger Wulingyuan Scenic Area, which was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992. The park is known for its unique pillar-like formations resulting from physical erosion.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as China's first national forest park
Major_Events.Description: The park was officially recognized as China's first national forest park.
Wulingyuan Scenic Area, which includes Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
One of the park's quartz-sandstone pillars was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' in honor of the movie Avatar.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon Glass Bridge
Major_Events.Description: The world's longest and highest pedestrian glass bridge was opened, though it was temporarily closed due to high visitor numbers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features unique pillar-like formations formed by physical erosion, dense foliage, and quartz-sandstone pillars. Notable structures include the Bailong Elevator, the world's tallest outdoor lift, and several gondola lift systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park's pillar-like formations are a distinct hallmark of the Chinese landscape and have inspired ancient Chinese paintings and modern films like Avatar. It is a significant natural heritage site and a major tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes the Bailong Elevator (326 m tall), the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon Glass Bridge (430 m long and 300 m high), and three gondola lift systems. It was also designated as a UNESCO global geopark in 2004.

world knowledge.Name: Thomond Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Thomond Park is a stadium in Limerick, Ireland, owned by Munster Rugby. It has a rich history in rugby, known for its unique atmosphere and traditions. The stadium underwent significant redevelopment in 2008, increasing its capacity to 25,600. It is famed for its noise during play and silence during goal kicks. Munster Rugby had a 12-year unbeaten run in the Heineken Cup here until 2007. The stadium also hosted historic matches, including Munster's 12–0 victory over the All Blacks in 1978.

Major_Events.Description: Munster celebrated their historic 12–0 victory over the All Blacks in front of 12,000 fans.
Munster retained a 12-year unbeaten run at Thomond Park in the Heineken Cup until Leicester Tigers broke the streak with a 13–6 win.
The stadium was redeveloped, increasing its capacity to 25,600 with new stands and facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Best Rugby Stadium in the World
Major_Events.Description: Thomond Park was awarded the title of 'Best Rugby Stadium in the World' following a global vote by rugby supporters.
Thomond Park hosted the Irish heats of the 2011 Special Olympics World Summer Games.
Thomond Park hosted Rugby League matches, including Ireland vs. France in 2011 and Ireland vs. Australia in the 2013 Rugby League World Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Thomond Park originally consisted of two pitches, the main pitch and a training pitch, with terracing and a stand. The redevelopment in 2008 added two new stands, increasing seating capacity to 15,100 and terrace capacity to 10,530. The stadium features grass surface and modern facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Thomond Park holds a special place in rugby due to its unique history and atmosphere. It is renowned for its passionate fans, traditional songs like 'The Fields of Athenry' and 'Stand Up and Fight,' and the respectful silence during goal kicks. The stadium is a symbol of Munster Rugby's pride and heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Rugby stadium, also used for football matches and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: Thomond Park has hosted various sports events, including rugby, football, and Rugby League matches, as well as concerts. It is known for its electric atmosphere and has been a key venue for Munster Rugby and international matches. The stadium's naming rights were retained as Thomond Park, with individual stands sold for sponsorship.

world knowledge.Name: Story Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Story Bridge is a heritage-listed steel cantilever bridge spanning the Brisbane River. It was constructed as part of a public works program during the Great Depression and opened in 1940. It is named after John Douglas Story, a prominent public servant who advocated for its construction. The bridge was designed by John Bradfield and based on the Jacques Cartier Bridge in Montreal. It was initially tolled until 1947 and has since become a significant transport and cultural landmark in Brisbane.

Major_Events.Description: Construction on the bridge began on 24 May 1935, with the first sod turned by Premier William Forgan Smith.
The Story Bridge was opened on 6 July 1940 by Sir Leslie Orme Wilson, Governor of Queensland.
The toll for using the bridge was removed in 1947.
Road traffic was halted so pedestrians could celebrate the 50th anniversary of the bridge's construction.
The bridge was closed to road traffic on 5 July 2015 to celebrate the 75th anniversary, attracting almost 75,000 visitors.
A three-metre-high safety barrier was installed to prevent suicides, completed in December 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel cantilever bridge design, heavily based on the Jacques Cartier Bridge in Montreal. The bridge features 1.25 million rivets, a concrete decking with Trinidad pitch topping, and sodium lighting. It has one pier on the northern bank and two piers on the southern bank (main pier and anchor pier).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Story Bridge is the longest cantilever bridge in Australia and a heritage-listed structure. It is a key transport link in Brisbane and a popular tourist attraction, featuring in annual Riverfire fireworks displays and offering bridge climbs. It was named a Q150 Icon of Queensland for its role as a 'structure and engineering feat'.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries motor vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians across the Brisbane River, connecting northern and southern suburbs of Brisbane.

Details.Heritage Status: Listed on the Queensland Heritage Register in 1992
Details.Awards: Received a Historic Engineering Marker from Engineers Australia in 1988
Details.Suicide Prevention: Safety barriers and hotline telephones installed in 2015
Details.Recent Issues: As of 2025, the bridge is at risk of collapse and may need tolls to fund restoration works. Footpaths have been closed indefinitely.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio da Ressacada
world knowledge.Address: Carianos neighborhood, Florianópolis, Santa Catarina, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Aderbal Ramos da Silva, commonly called Estádio da Ressacada, was inaugurated on November 15, 1983, replacing the old Estádio Adolfo Konder. It was built on a plot near Hercílio Luz International Airport and designed by architect Davi Ferreira Lima. The stadium honors Aderbal Ramos da Silva, a former president of the Santa Catarina Football Federation and governor of the state.

Major_Events.Description: Vasco da Gama beat Avaí 6-1, with the first goal scored by Vasco da Gama's Vilson Tadei.
The stadium lights were inaugurated on May 31, 1986.
Avaí beat Blumenau 2-1 in the Campeonato Catarinense final, setting a record attendance of 25,735.

Major_Events.Event: Paul McCartney concert (On the Run Tour)
Major_Events.Description: Paul McCartney performed in front of 30,000 fans, marking his first concert in the city.
Paul McCartney is scheduled to perform another concert at the stadium in October 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Davi Ferreira Lima, the stadium features a grass surface and a capacity of approximately 17,800 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Avaí Futebol Clube and has hosted matches for the Brazilian national football team and Olympic team. It also serves as a venue for major concerts, attracting international artists like Paul McCartney.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium should not be confused with Blumenau's former stadium, which was also called Estádio Aderbal Ramos da Silva but was nicknamed DEBA and had a smaller capacity. The current stadium was renovated in 2006.

world knowledge.Name: Maracanã Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Maracanã Stadium was opened in 1950 to host the FIFA World Cup. It was built in less than two years but was only fully completed in 1965. The stadium has hosted numerous significant football matches, concerts, and other sporting events, including the 2014 FIFA World Cup and the 2016 Summer Olympics and Paralympics. It was named after journalist Mário Filho in 1966 and has undergone several renovations over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the decisive match where Uruguay defeated Brazil 2-1, known as the 'Maracanazo'.
Hosted several matches, including the final, and underwent major renovations for the event.
Hosted the opening and closing ceremonies, as well as football matches.
Hosted the final of the tournament for the second consecutive time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed with a two-tier configuration, the stadium was later renovated with a one-tier seating bowl and a fiberglass tensioned membrane roof covering 95% of the seats. The facade is grayish, and the seats are colored yellow, blue, and white, representing the Brazilian national colors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Maracanã Stadium is a symbol of Brazilian football and culture. It has hosted some of the most iconic matches in football history, including the 1950 World Cup final, and is deeply tied to the identity of Rio de Janeiro and Brazil. It is also a landmark of sports journalism, named after Mário Filho, a prominent sports journalist.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Association football stadium, also used for concerts and other sporting events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's popular name derives from the Maracanã River. It has a record attendance of 173,850 (officially) and has hosted crowds of over 100,000 on 284 occasions. It is the largest stadium in Brazil and the third largest in South America. The stadium has faced maintenance issues post-2016 Olympics, including power shutoffs and vandalism.

image_name: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium

world knowledge.Name: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Sector-3 Nava Raipur, Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium, also known as the Nava Raipur International Cricket Stadium, is a 65,000-seater venue in the city of Nava Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India. It became the country's 50th international cricket venue in 2023. It is one of the largest cricket stadiums in India in terms of boundary dimensions. Inaugurated in 2008, this ground hosted its first ever match in 2010, when the Canada national cricket team arrived in India and played a practice match against the Chhattisgarh state team. In 2013, the stadium was declared as a second home venue for the Delhi Daredevils in the Indian Premier League (IPL) and has since hosted many of the team's matches. The first International cricket match played here was an ODI between India and New Zealand in 2023, which was won by India. The stadium is named after Veer Narayan Singh Binjhwar, a landlord from Sonakhan who spearheaded the 1857 Sepoy Rebellion in Chhattisgarh.

Major_Events.Description: The first International cricket match played here was an ODI between India and New Zealand, which was won by India.
The first International T20I match played here was between India and Australia.
The Stadium hosted a Half-Marathon, with the theme "Let us run" on 16 December 2012 to mark Vijay Diwas.

The 2020-21 Road Safety World Series was postponed on 24 March 2020 after four matches due to COVID-19 lockdown in India. After almost a year, the tournament resumed with the announcement of all the matches to be played in Raipur with all COVID-19 guidelines being followed allowing only 50% audience capacity of the stadium. The tournament hosted matches between 5 and 21 March 2021.
Four matches of Celebrity Cricket League 2023 were played in Raipur between 18 February and 19 February at Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Cricket Stadium in Raipur.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has been built with the facilities of a modern sports arena. The media facilities as well as the corporate boxes have been renovated and roofs cover the rest of the ground to provide comfort during hot periods. The 22-yards strip usually offers a good balance between the bat and the ball.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after Veer Narayan Singh Binjhwar, a landlord from Sonakhan who spearheaded the 1857 Sepoy Rebellion in Chhattisgarh. It is one of the largest cricket stadiums in India in terms of boundary dimensions and has been compared to The Gabba in Australia by international commentators. BCCI had adjudged the pitch and ground of Shaheed Veer Narayan International Cricket Stadium as the Best pitch and Best ground of the Central Zone for the year 2017–18.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is situated in sector-3 of Naya Raipur Near Sendh Lake, close to the Swami Vivekananda Airport in Naya Raipur. It is 21 km away from Raipur. The construction of the stadium began in the year 2006 and was completed in 2008 at the cost of Rs 145 Crore. It is built and owned by the Government of Chhattisgarh. The stadium has also hosted eight T20 matches of the 2014 Champions League Twenty20. These consisted of two Group Stage games, plus all six Qualifier matches. The Qualifier matches were double-headers. For the first time in the history of CLT20, the qualifiers were sold out.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Town City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Town City Hall is a large Edwardian building built in 1905, located in Cape Town's city centre. It was designed as the result of a public competition by architects Harry Austin Reid and Frederick George Green. The building was formally opened by the Mayor of Cape Town, Hyman Liberman. It has served as a significant cultural and political venue, including Nelson Mandela's first public speech after his release from prison in 1990.

Major_Events.Description: Nelson Mandela made his first public speech from the balcony of Cape Town City Hall on February 11, 1990, hours after his release from prison.
Following a fire at the National Assembly building, the City Hall hosted President Cyril Ramaphosa's State of the Nation Address on February 10, 2022.
On March 2, 2022, the hall was lit up in the colours of the Ukrainian flag to show support during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
A statue of Nelson Mandela was unveiled on the balcony on July 24, 2018, marking the spot where he made his 1990 speech.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is constructed from honey-coloured oolitic limestone imported from Bath, England. It features an organ with 3165 pipes, a turret clock with Westminster chimes, and a carillon installed as a World War I memorial. The architectural style is Edwardian.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The City Hall is a symbol of political and cultural significance in South Africa, notably for Nelson Mandela's historic speech. It serves as a venue for major cultural events, including concerts and art exhibitions, and is a key landmark in Cape Town.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a city hall, it now serves as a venue for creative and cultural events, including concerts by the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra and the annual Festive Lights Switch On event.
world knowledge.Details: The City Hall no longer houses the city offices but remains a central cultural venue. It was documented in 3D by the Zamani Project between 2017 and 2018, creating a permanent digital record for research and conservation. The building was renovated in 2018 and features a 3D model and virtual tour available online.

world knowledge.Name: Drayton Manor Resort
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Drayton Manor Resort is a family theme park, zoo, and accommodation built on the grounds of the former Drayton Manor, which was built in 1835 for Sir Robert Peel. The mansion was reduced to ruins by 1926, and the land was requisitioned by the British Army during World War II. After the war, entrepreneurs George and Vera Bryan bought the land and opened a small amusement park in 1950. Over the years, the park expanded, adding more rides and attractions, including a zoo in 1954. The park has undergone several ownership changes and expansions, including the addition of themed areas like Thomas Land and Vikings.

Major_Events.Event: Girl's drowning on Splash Canyon Rapids ride
Major_Events.Description: An 11-year-old girl fell out of a raft on the Splash Canyon Rapids ride, slipped into a deeper pool of water, and drowned. The park was temporarily closed, and the ride remained closed until summer 2021.
The park suffered flood damage and was required to remain shut until July 2020.
The park entered administration and was bought by the Looping Group, which owns various parks, zoos, and aquariums around Europe.
A fire started in a toilet block in the Thomas Land area of the park. The blaze was deemed accidental by investigators.
A new themed area called Vikings opened, featuring three new rides and a rethemed Buffalo roller coaster.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Gold Rush roller coaster
Major_Events.Description: The park announced the opening of an Intamin family thrill Lift and Launch Coaster called Gold Rush.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features various themed areas with rides and attractions, including Thomas Land and Vikings. The park also includes a 15-acre zoo with over 100 species from around the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Drayton Manor Resort is one of the largest amusement parks in the UK and has been a popular family destination for decades. It is significant for its historical roots, having been built on the grounds of the former Drayton Manor, and for its role in the local tourism industry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park, zoo, and family resort
world knowledge.Details: Drayton Manor Resort offers a range of family-friendly events throughout the season, including Halloween-themed attractions and night rides. The park also features a 4-star hotel with 150 guest rooms, including 15 Thomas & Friends themed bedrooms. The Camping and Caravanning Club have a site at Drayton Manor with 90 pitches, glamping tents, and a children's playground.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Sevan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Sevan is the largest body of water in Armenia and the Caucasus region. It has significant economic, cultural, and recreational value. Historically, it was known by various names such as Sea of Gegham, Lychnitis, and Gokcha. The lake was heavily exploited during the Soviet period for irrigation and hydroelectric power, leading to ecological degradation. Efforts to restore the lake's water level began in the 1960s with the construction of tunnels to divert water from other rivers.

Major_Events.Event: Soviet exploitation for irrigation and hydroelectric power
Major_Events.Description: The lake's water level dropped by around 20 m (66 ft) and its volume reduced by more than 40% due to irrigation and hydroelectric power generation projects.
A tunnel was completed to divert water from the Arpa River to the lake, helping to halt the decline in water level.
A second tunnel was completed to divert water from the Vorotan River, further helping to restore the lake's water level.
The Armenian government established public beaches to make the lake more accessible to citizens.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Sevan is considered the "jewel" of Armenia and is recognized as a national treasure. It has significant cultural, recreational, and spiritual value. The lake is home to historical monuments such as the Sevanavank monastery and a field of khachkars in Noratus.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Source of irrigation water, hydroelectric power, fish, recreation, and tourism

Details.Ecosystem: The lake's ecosystem has been heavily impacted by human activity, including the introduction of non-native species like common whitefish and goldfish. The endemic Sevan trout is endangered.
Details.Wildlife: The lake and its vicinity host over 200 bird species, including the Armenian gull. It is also a migration stop for various raptors and waterbirds.
Details.Pollution: The lake faces pollution from agricultural, domestic, and industrial waste, including heavy metals like vanadium, selenium, and copper.
Details.Tourism: Lake Sevan is a popular tourist destination with beaches, resorts, and recreational activities like swimming, jet skiing, and windsurfing.

world knowledge.Name: Sapporo Dome
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Opened in 2001, the Sapporo Dome is a multi-purpose stadium primarily used for association football and baseball. It has hosted numerous significant events, including matches during the 2002 FIFA World Cup, the 2020 Summer Olympics, and the 2017 Asian Winter Games. The stadium was renamed to Daiwa House PREMIST DOME in 2024 due to a naming rights contract.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted three matches: Germany vs Saudi Arabia, Argentina vs England, and Italy vs Ecuador.
Served as a football venue.
Hosted the opening ceremony.
Hosted two matches.
Hosted opening and closing ceremonies, and featured indoor and nighttime skiing events.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Hiroshi Hara, the stadium features a fixed roof and a unique sliding pitch system that allows it to switch between an artificial turf field for baseball and a natural grass pitch for football. The conversion process involves rotating lower bowl bleachers and retracting main bowl seats to accommodate the different sports.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sapporo Dome is a significant landmark in Japan due to its innovative design and its role in hosting major international sporting events. It is a symbol of modern engineering and multi-functional stadium design.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for association football and baseball.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 42,065 for football and 42,270 for baseball. It is the home field of Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo and was previously home to the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters. The stadium also hosted Rally Japan in 2008 and 2010. Renovations in 2009 increased capacity and added facilities for food outlets, media, and changing rooms. The stadium's surface will remain soccer-only starting in 2023 as the baseball team moves to a new stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Olimpico
world knowledge.Address: Viale dello Stadio Olimpico, Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stadio Olimpico, originally named Stadio dei Cipressi and later Stadio dei Centomila, was constructed under the fascist regime as part of the Foro Italico sports complex. It was expanded and renovated multiple times, including for the 1960 Summer Olympics and the 1990 FIFA World Cup. The stadium has hosted numerous significant sporting events and concerts, becoming a central venue in Italian sports and culture.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and track-and-field events.
Hosted six matches, including the final where West Germany defeated Argentina.
Hosted the finals of the 1968 and 1980 European Championships.
Hosted four UEFA Champions League finals, including the 2009 final between FC Barcelona and Manchester United.
Annual athletics event part of the Diamond League since 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a rectangular field with grass surface, covered by a Teflon and fiberglass membrane roof supported by steel and concrete structures. It includes two grandstands (Tevere and Monte Mario) and two hemicycle stands (Curva Nord and Curva Sud). The roof was added during the 1988–90 renovation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stadio Olimpico is a symbol of Italian sports history, hosting major international events and serving as the home ground for AS Roma and SS Lazio. It is also a venue for concerts and cultural events, making it a multifunctional landmark in Rome.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose sports venue (association football, athletics, rugby union) and concert venue.

Details.Architects: E. Del Debbio, L. Moretti, C. Valle, A. Vitellozzi, M. Clerici

world knowledge.Name: Kuban Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kuban Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Krasnodar, Russia, first opened on 30 October 1960 with an initial capacity of approximately 20,000 people. The first match was played on 14 May 1961 between FC Kuban Krasnodar (then called Spartak Krasnodar) and PFC Dynamo Stavropol (then called Spartak Stavropol). The capacity was later doubled with the building of a second floor, and floodlights were installed.

Major_Events.Description: FC Kuban Krasnodar (then called Spartak Krasnodar) played PFC Dynamo Stavropol (then called Spartak Stavropol).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with grass surface, featuring a second floor added later and floodlights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is the home of PFC Kuban Krasnodar and the now-amateur FC Kuban Krasnodar, serving as a significant sports venue in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches and other sports events
world knowledge.Details: The stadium holds 35,200 people and was most recently renovated in 2016.

world knowledge.Name: Rock of Cashel
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rock of Cashel, also known as Cashel of the Kings and St. Patrick's Rock, is a historical site located dramatically above a plain at Cashel, County Tipperary, Ireland. According to local legends, the Rock of Cashel originated in the Devil's Bit, a mountain 20 miles north of Cashel when St. Patrick banished Satan from a cave, resulting in the Rock's landing in Cashel. The Rock of Cashel was the traditional seat of the kings of Munster as early as the 4th century and prior to the Norman invasion. In the 5th century, the Eóganachta clan built a fortress at Cashel retaining supremacy there for hundreds of years. In 977, Brian Boru was crowned there as king and made Cashel his capital. In 1101, the King of Munster, Muirchertach Ua Briain, donated his fortress on the Rock to the Church.

Major_Events.Event: Conversion of the King of Munster by Saint Patrick
Major_Events.Description: Cashel is reputed to be the site of the conversion of the King of Munster by Saint Patrick.
Brian Boru was crowned as king and made Cashel his capital.
The King of Munster, Muirchertach Ua Briain, donated his fortress on the Rock to the Church.

During the Irish Confederate Wars, Cashel was sacked by English Parliamentarian troops under Murrough O'Brien, 1st Earl of Inchiquin. The Irish Confederate troops there were massacred, as were the Catholic clergy, including Theobald Stapleton. Inchiquin's troops looted or destroyed many important religious artefacts.
The main cathedral roof was destroyed by Arthur Price, the Anglican Archbishop of Cashel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The picturesque complex has a character of its own and is one of the most remarkable collections of Celtic art and medieval architecture to be found anywhere in Europe. Cormac's Chapel, the chapel of King Cormac Mac Carthaigh, was begun in 1127 and consecrated in 1134. It is a sophisticated structure, with vaulted ceilings and wide arches, drawing on contemporary European architecture and infusing unique native elements. The cathedral, built between 1235 and 1270, is an aisleless building of cruciform plan, having a central tower and terminating westwards in a massive residential castle. The Hall of the Vicars Choral was built in the 15th century. The oldest and tallest of the structure is the well preserved round tower 28 metres high, dating from c.1100.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rock of Cashel is culturally and historically important as the traditional seat of the kings of Munster and a significant religious site. It is one of the most remarkable collections of Celtic art and medieval architecture in Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The entire plateau on which the buildings and graveyard lie is walled. In the grounds around the buildings an extensive graveyard includes a number of high crosses. Scully's Cross, one of the largest and most famous high crosses here, originally constructed in 1860 to commemorate the Scully family, was destroyed in 1976 when lightning struck a metal rod that ran the length of the cross. The remains of the top of the cross now lie at the base of the cross adjacent to the rock wall. The Rock of Cashel has become a tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Six Flags México
world knowledge.Address: Tlalpan forest and borough, Mexico City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Six Flags México is an amusement park located in the Tlalpan forest and borough, on the southern edge of Mexico City, Mexico. It is owned and operated by Six Flags, and is the most visited theme park in Latin America with 2.8 million annual visitors. It was previously known as Reino Aventura when it was Mexican-owned and featured the orca whale Keiko (from the movie Free Willy) as its principal attraction. The park opened on March 3, 1982, as the largest theme park in Latin America. It underwent significant remodeling in 1992 and reopened in 1993 with new rides. In 1999, Premier Parks bought Reino Aventura and renamed it Six Flags México, adding numerous new attractions.

Major_Events.Description: Reino Aventura opened as the largest theme park in Latin America with a mascot named Cornelio, a purple cartoon dragon.
The park was closed for remodeling and added new rides, reopening in 1993 as El Nuevo Reino Aventura.
Premier Parks bought Reino Aventura for an estimated $59 million and renamed it Six Flags México, adding 20 new attractions.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Superman el Último Escape
Major_Events.Description: The park opened the Superman el Último Escape roller coaster.
The park opened The Dark Knight roller coaster.
The park opened The Joker, a Gerstlauer spinning coaster.
The park opened Medusa Steel Coaster, featuring steel tracks and multiple inversions.
The park opened the Wonder Woman Coaster.
Carlos Joel Garza Marines fell ten meters from the Rueda India and broke his legs.
Abdiel Alexey suffered a head injury after flying out of an unsecured seat on El Pingüino.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of roller coasters, water rides, and themed attractions, including Batman: The Ride, Kilahuea, and Medusa, a wooden roller coaster. The park has undergone several renovations and additions since its opening, incorporating modern steel tracks and multiple inversions in its roller coasters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Six Flags México is the most visited theme park in Latin America, attracting 2.8 million annual visitors. It has played a significant role in the entertainment industry in Mexico and has been a major tourist attraction since its opening. The park has also been involved in various cultural events and festivals, such as the Festival del Terror and Christmas in the Park.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates year-round, remaining closed some Mondays and Tuesdays. It features 9 roller coasters and 2 water rides. The park has a website for visitors to access more information. In 2011, the park opened Terminator X: A Laser Battle for Salvation, an indoor themed laser tag attraction. In 2015, the park announced the addition of Skyscreamer, a Funtime Starflyer. In 2016, the park announced Justice League: Battle For Metropolis 4D. In 2017, the park announced The New Revolution Virtual Reality Coaster and a new water park called Hurricane Harbor.

world knowledge.Name: Leicester Guildhall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Guildhall in Leicester, England, is a timber-framed building dating from around 1390. It served as the town hall until 1876 and was the meeting place for the Guild of Corpus Christi and later the Corporation of Leicester. It was used for council meetings, feasts, court sessions, and theatrical performances. The building played a significant role during the English Civil War and has been associated with notable historical figures, including William Shakespeare and Oliver Cromwell.

Major_Events.Description: During the English Civil War, the Mayor and corporation received demands from Prince Rupert for £2,000. Decisions regarding the city's fate were made at the Guildhall, including the Royalist attack on the city.
Archaeologists confirmed the discovery of Richard III's remains in a nearby location during a press conference held at the Guildhall.
After plans to demolish the dilapidated building, restoration work was completed, and the Guildhall was opened as a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Medieval style timber-framed building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Guildhall is a Grade I listed building and part of a conservation area. It is historically significant for its role in Leicester's governance, its association with the Guild of Corpus Christi, and its connections to notable historical events and figures, including Shakespeare and the English Civil War. It is also reputedly Leicester's most haunted building.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a meeting place for the Guild of Corpus Christi and later the Corporation of Leicester, now used as a museum and performance venue.
world knowledge.Details: The Guildhall library includes the New Testament in Greek from the 15th century. It was also Leicester's first police station from 1836. The building is associated with the legend of King Leir, which may have inspired Shakespeare's King Lear. It has appeared on TV programmes like Most Haunted due to its reported hauntings.

world knowledge.Name: Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium, nicknamed The Cathedral, is a multi-purpose stadium in Enugu, Nigeria. It was originally the sports ground of the Nigerian Railway Corporation and was taken over by the defunct Eastern Nigeria Government. It served as a rallying point for sportsmen and women in the eastern region until the Nigeria/Biafra civil war. After the war, it was refurbished with hostel facilities to accommodate athletes and housed the state's sports council. It was further renovated in 1986 and again in 1999 for the FIFA U-20 World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium staged important matches, including Nigeria's loss to Mali in the quarter-finals.
The stadium hosted matches in Group D, which comprised Turkey, Costa Rica, Burkina Faso, and New Zealand.
44,000 people attended the match between Enugu Rangers and Enyimba FC, making it the best-attended match in the NPFL during that season.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has an artificial turf and a new videomatrix scoreboard, designed to give it a more modern and technologically driven edifice.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after the first president of the Republic of Nigeria, Nnamdi Azikiwe, and serves as a significant sports venue in Nigeria, particularly for football. It is the home stadium of Enugu Rangers and has hosted major international tournaments.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone several renovations, including in 1970, 1986, and 1999. It was one of the hosting stadiums for the FIFA U-17 World Cup Nigeria 2009. During the 2023-24 NPFL season, Enugu Rangers drew an average home attendance of 20,672, the highest in the league.

world knowledge.Name: Kyocera Dome Osaka
world knowledge.Address: 3-chōme−2−1, Chiyozaki, Nishi Ward, Osaka, Osaka, Japan
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Left: 100.0 m, Left-Center: 116.0 m, Center: 122.0 m, Right-Center: 116.0 m, Right: 100.0 m
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kyocera Dome Osaka, originally named Osaka Dome, opened in 1997 as the home field of the Osaka Kintetsu Buffaloes. After the merger between the Orix BlueWave and Osaka Kintetsu Buffaloes in 2005, it became one of the homes of the Orix Buffaloes. The Hanshin Tigers also use the stadium for their season openers and August home games due to high school baseball tournaments at Koshien Stadium. Kyocera Corporation acquired naming rights in 2006, renaming it Kyocera Dome Osaka.

Major_Events.Description: Mixed martial arts fights held at the dome.
Mixed martial arts fights held at the dome.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Nikken Sekkei, Ltd., the dome features a retractable roof and a seating capacity of 55,000 for events and 36,627 for baseball games.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Japan, hosting professional baseball games and major events. It is culturally important as a home field for the Orix Buffaloes and a secondary venue for the Hanshin Tigers.
world knowledge.Details: Kyocera Document Solutions Incorporated has been advertising at Osaka Dome since April 2003. The naming rights contract was initially for five years and has been renewed several times. The stadium was delayed in renaming to Kyocera Dome Osaka until July 1, 2006, due to the reorganization of the Dome Company.

world knowledge.Name: Beijing World Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beijing World Park is a theme park opened on October 25, 1993, designed to allow visitors to see the world without leaving Beijing. It features miniature replicas of famous global landmarks and offers cultural experiences.

Major_Events.Description: Selected as one of the three protest zones during the 2008 Summer Olympics.
Hosted a Thai elephant that performed four times a day from May to October.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes miniature replicas of around 100 famous global landmarks, constructed with attention to detail and materials resembling the originals. Examples include the Great Pyramids made of 200,000 white marble bricks and Red Square replicated with over 5 million red bricks. The entrance features a Gothic castle, Roman corridor, and granite relief sculptures, with an Italian-style terrace garden inside.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park serves as a cultural and educational attraction, showcasing global landmarks and traditions, and offering immersive experiences such as dance performances and parades representing various cultures.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement and cultural education through miniature replicas and live performances.
world knowledge.Details: The park consists of two main parts: the scenic portion with miniature landmarks arranged according to their global locations, and the shopping, dining, and entertainment area modeled after Euro-American architecture. Visitors can explore the park via speedboat tours, monorail, or battery-operated cars. The nearby Beijing Dabaotai Western Han Dynasty Mausoleum is located 0.5 km southeast of the park's south entrance.

world knowledge.Name: Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, known for sponsorship reasons as Ülker Stadium Fenerbahçe Şükrü Saracoğlu Sports Complex, is a football stadium located in the Kadıköy district of Istanbul, Turkey. It is the traditional home venue of major Turkish multi-sport club Fenerbahçe S.K.. The stadium was inaugurated in 1908 and renovated between 1929 and 1932, 1965 and 1982, and 1999 and 2006. Before the stadium was built, the field was known as Papazın Çayırı (lit. 'the priest's meadow'). The field became the very first official association football pitch of Turkey, where the first league games of the Istanbul Football League were all held consecutively. In 1908, the local teams in the league needed a regular football field, so this land was leased from the Ottoman Sultan Abdul Hamid II for 30 Ottoman gold pounds a year. The total construction cost was 3,000 Ottoman gold pounds. The name was changed to the 'Union Club Field' after the club which made the highest donation for construction of the ground.

Major_Events.Description: On 4 October 2006, after numerous inspections by UEFA, Ülker Stadium was selected to host the 2009 UEFA Cup Final, which went down in history as the last Final of the UEFA Cup football tournament, which was rebranded as the UEFA Europa League starting from the 2009–10 season.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hybrid grass surface, designed by Zehra Aksu and Adnan Aksu.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it is the traditional home venue of Fenerbahçe S.K., one of Turkey's most prominent football clubs. It has hosted numerous important football matches and events, including the 2009 UEFA Cup Final. The stadium's history dates back to the early 20th century, making it a landmark in Turkish football history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone several renovations, including periods between 1929–1932, 1965–1982, and 1999–2006. The construction cost was US$85 million ($133 million in 2024 dollars). The stadium has a capacity of 47,430 (all-seater) and features 64 executive suites. In 2015, Ülker secured naming rights of the stadium in a 10-year deal worth $90 million, officially renaming the stadium Ülker Stadium Fenerbahçe Şükrü Saracoğlu Sports Complex.

world knowledge.Name: Alton Towers
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a private estate of the Earls of Shrewsbury, Alton Towers' grounds were opened to the public in 1860 to raise funds. Inspired by Disneyland, it was transformed into a theme park in 1980 with the installation of its first roller coaster and several new rides.

Major_Events.Description: Transformation into a theme park with the installation of its first roller coaster and several new rides.
Sixteen people were injured on The Smiler ride, with two individuals requiring leg amputations. Merlin Entertainments was fined £5 million for health and safety breaches.
The resort's largest annual event celebrating Halloween with temporary scare maze attractions, scare zones, and extended opening hours.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is divided into 11 themed areas, including Towers Street, Mutiny Bay, Katanga Canyon, Gloomy Wood, Forbidden Valley, Dark Forest, The Towers & Gardens, The World of David Walliams, X-Sector, Adventure Land, and CBeebies Land. Features include roller coasters, water rides, and themed attractions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Alton Towers is one of the most visited theme parks in the UK and Europe, known for its innovative rides and attractions. It has played a significant role in the development of the theme park industry in the UK.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theme park and resort complex offering entertainment, rides, and accommodation.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates seasonally from mid-March to early November, with many hotels and amenities open year-round. Special events include Scarefest, Oktoberfest, Fireworks, and Christmas. The resort also features a water park, mini-golf, and multiple hotels.

world knowledge.Name: Fehmarn Sound Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects the German island of Fehmarn with the German mainland near Großenbrode
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 963 m (3,159 ft 5 in) in length, 21 m (68 ft 11 in) in width, 67 m (219 ft 10 in) in height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fehmarn Sound Bridge connects the German island of Fehmarn with the German mainland near Großenbrode. It was opened on April 30, 1963, and was declared a historic monument in 1999. The bridge was built during the Cold War and includes six explosive vaults embedded below the approach road on the mainland side.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on April 30, 1963, connecting Fehmarn with the German mainland and replacing ferry services.
The bridge was declared a historic monument by the State Office for Protection of Historical Monuments of Schleswig-Holstein in Kiel.
In 2023, the bridge underwent renovation, including the replacement of all steel wires.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a 963-metre-long network arch bridge constructed of steel. It includes two steel arches, 248 metres in length, which reach 45 metres above the main deck. The bridge carries road and rail, with a single rail track, a pedestrian walkway, and a two-lane roadway.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fehmarn Sound Bridge is a symbol of both Fehmarn and Schleswig-Holstein. It was declared a historic monument in 1999 and has played a significant role in connecting the island of Fehmarn with the German mainland, improving transportation and commerce.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by engineers G. Fischer, T. Jahnke, and P. Stein from the firm Gutehoffnungshütte Sterkrade AG, Oberhausen-Sterkrade, with architectural design assistance from Gerd Lohmer. During the Cold War, six explosive vaults were embedded below the approach road on the mainland side. A Fehmarn Belt Tunnel is under construction between Denmark and Germany, but the Fehmarn Sound Bridge will remain in place for pedestrians and local road traffic.

world knowledge.Name: Chongqing Olympic Sports Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chongqing Olympic Sports Center is a sports venue built in 2004, featuring a multipurpose stadium with a seating capacity of 58,680. It serves as the home stadium for Chongqing Lifan F.C. of the Chinese Football Association Super League and is also a popular venue for concerts.

Major_Events.Description: Mariah Carey began her The Elusive Chanteuse Show tour in China at the stadium on October 15, 2014.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Chongqing Olympic Sports Center is an important sports and entertainment venue in Chongqing, hosting major football matches and concerts, contributing to the cultural and sporting life of the city.
world knowledge.Details: The sports center is served by Olympic Sports Center station on the Loop line of Chongqing Rail Transit. It is owned by the Municipality of Chongqing and operated by the Chongqing Sports Bureau.

world knowledge.Name: Great Yarmouth Pleasure Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pleasure Beach Great Yarmouth is an amusement park that opened in 1909. It was developed on sand dunes leased by Charles B. Cochran, featuring attractions like the Scenic Railway and Katzenjammer Castle. Over the years, it expanded under various owners, including John Henry Iles and Pat Collins, adding rides like the Roller Coaster in 1932. The park has undergone continuous improvements and remains a popular tourist destination.

Major_Events.Description: The Scenic Railway was extensively damaged by fire but was quickly rebuilt and reopened the same year.
The Roller Coaster, purchased from the Colonial Exhibition in Paris, opened and remains the park's most popular ride.
John Collins sublet the site to Botton Brothers Limited, who introduced new rides and improvements.
The pop group Madness recorded scenes for their music video 'House of Fun' at the park.
The Gardens were introduced as a relaxation area with amenities like Sara's Tearooms and a miniature golf course.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Premier Inn and Beefeater
Major_Events.Description: An 81-bedroom Premier Inn hotel and Beefeater restaurant opened, part of a scaled-back version of 'The Edge' project.
