The resort also features eight restaurants, including notable ones like Siniikaung Bistro, Ruth’s Chris, and Johnny Rockets. The facility underwent significant renovations in 2018 to enhance guest experience.

world knowledge.Name: Las Vegas Club
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Original location: 1908 (Las Vegas Hotel), 1930 (Las Vegas Club); Second location: 1905 (Overland Hotel), 1949 (Las Vegas Club)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Las Vegas Club was a historic hotel and casino located on the Fremont Street Experience in downtown Las Vegas. It originated as the Las Vegas Hotel in 1908 and later became the Las Vegas Club in 1930. It relocated to the Overland Hotel site in 1949. Over the years, it underwent multiple ownership changes and expansions, becoming a sports-themed casino before closing in 2015 and being demolished for the Circa Resort & Casino.

Major_Events.Description: The original Las Vegas Hotel opened at 19 Fremont Street.
The Las Vegas Club opened diagonally across from the Overland Hotel, replacing the Smoke House casino.
The Las Vegas Club moved to the Overland Hotel site at 18 Fremont Street after lease issues at its original location.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Jackie Gaughan and Mel Exber
Major_Events.Description: The casino was purchased for $1 million and later themed around sports.
Two hotel towers were added, and a $35 million expansion in 1996 included a stadium-themed casino.
The hotel portion closed in April 2013 due to financial struggles.
The casino closed on August 20, 2015, after being sold to Derek and Greg Stevens.

Major_Events.Event: Demolition and Replacement by Circa Resort & Casino
Major_Events.Description: The Las Vegas Club was demolished, and the Circa Resort & Casino opened on the site in October 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Las Vegas Club featured a sports-themed design inspired by Ebbets Field, with a facade resembling a baseball stadium. The 1996 expansion included a casino area designed like a stadium with murals of fans. The building had mirrored panels and a brass statue of a baseball player.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Las Vegas Club was a historic downtown Las Vegas casino known for its sports memorabilia and themed attractions. It played a role in the development of Fremont Street as a gaming and entertainment hub.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hotel and casino with a sports theme, featuring gaming, dining, and entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The Las Vegas Club housed the Sports Hall of Fame, displaying rare sports memorabilia, including items from the Brooklyn and Los Angeles Dodgers. It struggled in later years due to competition from the Las Vegas Strip and was eventually demolished for redevelopment.

world knowledge.Name: Harrah's Las Vegas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Harrah's Las Vegas originally opened as the Holiday Inn Center Strip in 1972 and the Holiday Casino in 1973. It was renamed Harrah's Las Vegas in 1992 after ownership changes. The property has undergone multiple renovations and expansions, transitioning from a riverboat theme to a Carnival/Mardi Gras theme. It is now owned by Vici Properties and operated by Caesars Entertainment.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Holiday Inn Center Strip
Major_Events.Description: The hotel portion opened on February 1, 1972.
The casino portion opened on July 2, 1973.
The property was renamed Harrah's Las Vegas in April 1992 after The Promus Companies ended its franchise agreement with Holiday Inn.
Four men robbed the casino cage at gunpoint, leading to a police chase and their eventual arrest.
The resort underwent a major renovation, removing the riverboat theme and introducing a Carnival/Mardi Gras theme.
Caesars Entertainment sold the land to Vici Properties for $1.14 billion, with a 15-year leaseback agreement.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed with a riverboat façade, the resort transitioned to a Carnival/Mardi Gras theme in 1997. The property includes three towers (14-story, 23-story, and 35-story) and features a 90,637 sq ft casino. The exterior has undergone multiple redesigns, including the addition of a 450-foot-long Mississippi-style riverboat in 1990, later replaced by a mural and jester statues.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Harrah's Las Vegas is a landmark on the Las Vegas Strip, known for its historical transitions and entertainment offerings. It has hosted numerous shows and entertainers, contributing to Las Vegas's reputation as an entertainment hub.

Details.Permanent shows: Menopause The Musical, Mac King (2000–2021), Tenors of Rock (2017–2019), X Country
Details.Notable restaurants: Flavors, The Buffet (until 2020), Fulton Street Food Hall, Oyster Bar, Ruth's Chris Steak House, Toby Keith's I Love This Bar & Grill (2005–2020)

world knowledge.Name: Grand Sierra Resort
world knowledge.Address: 2500 East Second Street, Reno, Nevada, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as MGM Grand Reno in 1978, the property has undergone multiple ownership changes and rebrandings, including Bally's Reno (1986–1992) and Reno Hilton (1992–2006). It was acquired by The Meruelo Group in 2011 and renamed Grand Sierra Resort. The resort has seen several renovations and expansions, with a recent $1 billion-plus expansion project announced in 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The property opened as MGM Grand Reno, modeled after its Las Vegas counterpart, with 1,015 rooms and a casino.
Bally Manufacturing acquired the property for $550 million, renaming it Bally's Reno.
Hilton Hotels purchased the property for $83 million, renaming it Reno Hilton and investing $86 million in renovations.
The property was sold to Grand Sierra Resort Corp for $151 million and rebranded as Grand Sierra Resort.
The Meruelo Group purchased the property for $42 million and initiated a $25 million renovation program.
The resort announced a 10-year, $1 billion-plus expansion project, including a new hotel tower, residential units, and a 10,000-seat arena.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features a modern theme with a 27-floor hotel tower, a large casino floor, and multiple entertainment venues. The original MGM-like ceilings were retained in the casino during renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Grand Sierra Resort is a major entertainment and hospitality hub in Reno, hosting events like the Miss USA and Miss Teen USA competitions. It has a rich history of ownership changes and renovations, reflecting the evolution of the casino and hotel industry in Nevada.
world knowledge.Details: The resort features 1,990 guest rooms, 12 restaurants, a 25,000 sq ft nightclub, a driving range, and a 2,995-seat concert venue. It also hosts the local furry convention, Biggest Little Fur Con, since 2013. The property has undergone multiple renovations, with the most recent improvements completed in 2015. A $1 billion expansion project is planned, including a new hotel tower and arena.

world knowledge.Name: Bally's Lake Tahoe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as Park Tahoe in 1978, the property has undergone several ownership and branding changes, including Caesars Tahoe and MontBleu Resort Casino, before becoming Bally's Lake Tahoe in 2021. It has been a prominent casino and entertainment venue in Lake Tahoe, hosting numerous famous artists and events over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The casino first opened as Park Tahoe, built by Park Cattle Co.
Caesars World took over the property under a 25-year lease, renaming it Caesars Tahoe and remodeling it with a Roman theme.
Caesars Entertainment sold the resort to Columbia Sussex for $45 million to avoid antitrust issues.
Columbia Sussex rebranded the property as MontBleu Resort Casino & Spa.
Tropicana Entertainment, including MontBleu, was acquired by Eldorado Resorts.
The property was sold to Bally's Corporation and rebranded as Bally's Lake Tahoe.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Daniel, Mann, Johnson & Mendenhall in 1978, with renovations by Worth Group. The property features a 48,456 sq ft casino and a 438-room hotel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bally's Lake Tahoe has been a significant entertainment and gaming destination in Lake Tahoe, hosting top artists, comedians, and celebrities. It was also the host hotel and title sponsor of the American Century Championship golf tournament until 2004.
world knowledge.Details: The property includes a 1,200-seat showroom, Opal Nightclub, Blu Nightclub, Onsen Spa, Puzzle Room, Tahoe Axe & Darts, and notable restaurants like Ciera Steak + Chophouse. It underwent a $25-million remodel in 2015, upgrading guest rooms, the casino, and the showroom.

world knowledge.Name: Sugarloaf Point Light
world knowledge.Address: Seal Rocks Road, Myall Lakes National Park, Seal Rocks, Mid-Coast Council, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sugarloaf Point Light, also known as Seal Rocks Lighthouse, is an active lighthouse located on Sugarloaf Point, about 3 kilometres southeast of Seal Rocks. It was the first lighthouse designed by James Barnet and built by John McLeod. It guards Seal Rocks, a treacherous rock formation to the south. The lighthouse was added to the Commonwealth Heritage List on 22 June 2004, the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 22 February 2019, and the Register of the National Estate on 10 April 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was completed and first lit on 1 December 1875.
The light was converted to electricity, raising its intensity to 1,000,000 cd.
The lighthouse was automated, and a caretaker remained on-site until 2006-2007.
The lighthouse was added to the Commonwealth Heritage List on 22 June 2004.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 15-metre tall cylindrical tower with a balcony and lantern, featuring an external spiral stairway. It is constructed of rendered brick and painted white. The tower has two stories, divided by a concrete floor, with a fuel store on the ground level. The lantern room is reached by an internal flight of iron steps. The lighthouse retains its original Messrs Chance Bros lantern and features a domed oil store and heavily bracketed upper balcony, characteristic of James Barnet's architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sugarloaf Point Light is significant as the first major lightstation in the 'highway of lights' along the NSW coastline. It is associated with Colonial Architect James Barnet and Captain Francis Hixson. The lighthouse is also important for its association with the Worimi people, who traditionally occupied the area. The site is recognized for its heritage values and is part of the Myall Lakes National Park.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid for shipping along the NSW coastline.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority, while the structures are maintained by the Land and Property Management Authority. The lightstation complex includes a Head Keeper's cottage, two Assistant Keepers' cottages, a signal house, and a paint store. The cottages were renovated in 2006 and are now used for overnight accommodations. The lighthouse is complemented by a compact group of mid-Victorian buildings, all constructed of blue and white painted cement rendered brickwork.

image_name: Suzanne Dellal Centre for Dance and Theatre

world knowledge.Name: Suzanne Dellal Centre for Dance and Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Suzanne Dellal Centre for Dance and Theatre was established in 1989 by the family of Jack Dellal in honor of Suzanne, the late daughter of Zehava and Jack Dellal, along with the Municipality of Tel Aviv-Yafo, the Tel Aviv Foundation, and the Israeli Ministry of Culture and Education. It was built on the site of three late-19th century school buildings, which were reconstructed and restored to create the performing arts centre. The Centre was designed to rejuvenate the Neve Tzedek neighborhood and provide a home for contemporary dance in Israel.

Major_Events.Description: The Suzanne Dellal Centre was awarded the Israel Prize, the country's highest cultural honour, for its contributions to the art of dance in Israel.
The Centre underwent reconstruction, which included the addition of the new Zehava and Jack Dellal Studio, a flexible performance-studio space built on the roof of the central building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Centre was designed by architect Elisha Rubin, who preserved as much of the original late-19th century school buildings as possible. The main building's façade was reinforced, and internal walls were redesigned to meet the needs of the theatre. The complex was designed to allow free movement, with a central square serving as a courtyard and pedestrian walkway. The construction materials maintain the historic quality and atmosphere of the location.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Suzanne Dellal Centre is culturally significant as it has become the home and anchor of all artistic endeavours in the field of contemporary dance in Israel. It has uplifted the art of dance in Israel, broadened the circle of dance-lovers, and allowed Israeli dance to make its mark on the world.
world knowledge.Details: The Centre has a spacious multi-level campus consisting of four performance halls, rehearsal studios, a restaurant and cafe, and wide plazas that host outdoor performances and events. It has initiated and hosted many of Israel's dance platforms, such as Shades in Dance, International Exposure, Tel Aviv Dance, and Curtain Up.

world knowledge.Name: Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre
world knowledge.Address: Centre culturel Tjibaou, Rue des accords de Matignon, Tina B.P. 378 98845, Nouméa Cedex, Nouméa, New Caledonia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre celebrates the vernacular Kanak culture, the indigenous culture of New Caledonia, amidst political controversy over the independent status sought by some Kanaks from French rule. It was designed by Italian architect Renzo Piano and named after Jean-Marie Tjibaou, the leader of the independence movement who was assassinated in 1989. The centre was established to promote Kanak linguistic and archaeological heritage, handicrafts, and arts.

Major_Events.Description: The cultural centre was inaugurated in May 1998, following the design competition won by Renzo Piano in 1991.
The precursor to the cultural centre was the first cultural festival held in 1975 in New Caledonia, which was a focused celebration of Kanak culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The centre features ten large conical cases or pavilions patterned on the traditional Kanak Grand Hut design, arranged in three groups along a 250-metre ridge. The structures are built with laminated wood, concrete, coral, aluminium, glass, tree bark, and stainless steel. The design incorporates traditional Kanak building traditions with modern international architecture, including climate control features like nacos and a double roof system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The centre is a symbol of the recognition of Kanak identity and a gesture of restitution by the French government. It serves as a cultural hub for the promotion and preservation of Kanak heritage and contemporary art.
world knowledge.Details: The cultural centre includes exhibition halls, a theatre, a multimedia library, conference halls, studios for creative activities, and a school for teaching local art forms. It also houses the Fund for Contemporary Kanak and Oceanian Art, which includes over 600 contemporary works from Australia and the Pacific Islands.

world knowledge.Name: Sangaste Castle
world knowledge.Address: Sangaste, Otepää Parish, Valga County, Estonia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sangaste Castle was built between 1879 and 1881 by Friedrich Berg, who was inspired by English castles. The castle was designed by architect Otto Pius Hippius and features 99 rooms, adhering to a rule of not having more than 100 rooms. It later served as a Soviet Pioneer Camp, expanding to 149 rooms. The castle is an impressive example of Gothic Revival architecture in the Baltic States.

Major_Events.Description: In September 2023, Sangaste Castle was put up for auction for 2.6 million euros.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is built in a neo-Gothic style with influences from Tudor architecture. It features a tall tower at the main entrance, a large entrance hall with excellent acoustics, and various shaped towers, steps, and protruding or recessed building parts. The castle originally included a glass-roof winter garden, which is no longer present. The interior includes a Gothic ballroom, a Spanish Room, an English-style hunting room, and numerous bedrooms and functional rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sangaste Castle is considered one of the most impressive examples of Gothic Revival architecture in the Baltic States. It reflects the architectural aspirations and lifestyle of the Baltic nobility in the late 19th century.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a residence for Friedrich Berg, it later served as a Soviet Pioneer Camp and is now open to the public.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is open to the public and features 99 rooms, adhering to a rule of not having more than 100 rooms. It was designed by architect Otto Pius Hippius and built for Friedrich Berg, who was inspired by English castles.

world knowledge.Name: Médanos de Coro National Park
world knowledge.Address: Near the city of Coro on the road that leads to Paraguaná
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Médanos de Coro National Park was created in 1974 to protect part of the Paraguana xeric scrub ecoregion. It lies on the Médanos Isthmus and covers desert and coastal habitat, including salt marshes.

Major_Events.Description: Severe floods struck Venezuela, and heavy rain formed four lagoons in the dunes, a circumstance never witnessed before by park guards.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is significant for its unique desert landscape, massive sand dunes, and ecological diversity, including being an Important Bird Area.
world knowledge.Details: The park is made up of three zones: an alluvial plain, an aeolian plain with three types of dunes, and a littoral plain with mangrove swamps. The sand dunes, known as Médanos, can reach 40 m in height and are constantly transformed by the wind. Flora consists mainly of thorny shrubs, and fauna includes lizards, rabbits, anteaters, and foxes. Visitors can explore the dunes by camel.

world knowledge.Name: Franz Mayer Museum
world knowledge.Address: Av Hidalgo 45. Centro Histórico 06300, Mexico City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Franz Mayer Museum, opened in 1986, houses Latin America’s largest collection of decorative arts amassed by Franz Mayer over fifty years. The museum is located in the former San Juan de Dios monastery and hospital, an 18th-century structure rehabilitated for the museum. Franz Mayer, a stockbroker and financial professional, collected fine artworks, books, furniture, ceramics, textiles, and other decorative items from Europe, Asia, and Mexico, dating from the 15th to the 20th centuries. The museum continues to acquire new pieces, hosts temporary exhibits, and offers various cultural activities.

Major_Events.Description: The Franz Mayer Museum was opened to the public in the former San Juan de Dios monastery and hospital.
The museum inaugurated a temporary exhibit called 'Susurros' (Whispers) dedicated to the history of the collection.
The Ruth D. Lechuga Center for Popular Art Studies opened in the basement of the museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the former San Juan de Dios monastery and hospital, an 18th-century structure with three original rooms of the cloister: a dining hall, a storage room, and a chapel restored to its colonial look.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses Latin America’s largest collection of decorative arts, preserving everyday items that were often not considered worth preserving. It also serves as a center for the study and appreciation of decorative arts and their influence on contemporary design.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has 9,500 pieces of art, 1,400 pieces of ceramics, and 10,000 books, with only 28% on display at any time. It hosts frequent temporary exhibits, guided tours, courses, lectures, concerts, and children's workshops. The museum also has a café located in the main courtyard, which has been planted with a garden.

world knowledge.Name: Philopappos Monument
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Philopappos Monument is an ancient Roman mausoleum dedicated to Gaius Julius Antiochus Epiphanes Philopappos, a prince from the Kingdom of Commagene. It was erected by his sister Julia Balbilla and the citizens of Athens to honor his memory. The monument is located on Mouseion Hill, southwest of the Acropolis.

Major_Events.Description: Excavations were carried out at the monument.
Conservation work was undertaken at the monument.
Archaeologists H. A. Thompson and J. Travlos conducted small additional excavations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument is a two-story structure built of white Pentelic marble on a socle made of porous marble and veneered with slabs of Hymettian marble. It features a frieze representing Philopappos as a consul and statues of three men: Antiochus IV, Philopappos, and Seleucus I Nicator.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monument reflects the high position Philopappos held within Athenian society and serves as a testament to the cultural and historical connections between Athens and the Kingdom of Commagene.
world knowledge.Details: Only two-thirds of the façade remains, and the tomb chamber behind the façade is completely destroyed except for the base. The monument was apparently still intact in 1436 but was destroyed after this time. Parts of the monument were used for the construction of the minaret in the Parthenon under the Ottomans.

world knowledge.Name: Blackpool Sands, Dartmouth
world knowledge.Historical_Background: This Devon location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.
world knowledge.Details: Blackpool Sands is a private shingle beach open to the public near Dartmouth, Devon. There is a charge for parking in the high season, a cafe and a shop. The beach is stony especially with thick coarse, pebbles rather than sandy, and therefore not suitable for younger children or the building of sandcastles.

world knowledge.Name: Schloss Benrath
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Schloss Benrath (Benrath Palace) is a Baroque-style maison de plaisance (pleasure palace) erected for the Elector Palatine Charles Theodor and his wife, Countess Palatine Elisabeth Auguste of Sulzbach, by his garden and building director Nicolas de Pigage. It has been proposed for designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building, the central corps de logis, is flanked by two arched symmetrical wings, the maisons de cavalière, which originally housed the servants. The ensemble includes a circular pond (Schlossweiher) in the north and a long rectangular pond (Spiegelweiher) on the southside. The palace is surrounded by a Baroque square hunting park with two crossing diagonal alleys and a circular alley.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Schloss Benrath is culturally significant as a well-preserved example of Baroque architecture and as a proposed UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum (main building), Museum for European Garden Art (east wing), Museum of Natural History (west wing)
world knowledge.Details: The main building corps de logis is a museum with guided tours, and sometimes music concerts are performed. The two wings house two museums since 2002: the Museum for European Garden Art in the east wing and the Museum of Natural History in the west wing.

image_name: Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Bandar Cassia (Batu Kawan) in Seberang Perai with Batu Maung on Penang Island
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 24 km (15 mi) in length, with 16.9 km (10.5 mi) over water
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge, also known as the Penang Second Bridge, is a dual carriageway toll bridge in Penang, Malaysia. It is the second bridge to link Penang Island to the mainland after the Penang Bridge. Construction began in November 2008 and was completed in February 2014. The bridge was officially opened on 1 March 2014 and named after the fourteenth Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Tuanku Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah of Kedah. It is the longest bridge in Malaysia and the second longest in Southeast Asia.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began in November 2008.
The bridge was officially opened on 1 March 2014 and opened to traffic on 2 March 2014.
A ramp leading to the still under construction Penang Second Bridge at Batu Maung interchange collapsed on 6 June 2013, killing one person.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is designed based on the double 'S' curvy concept due to geological reasons. It is the longest bridge in the world installed with High Damping Natural Rubber Bearing, an effective seismic isolation system that enables the bridge to withstand high intensity earthquakes. The bridge is the first in Malaysia to be installed with seismic expansion joints.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a High Impact Project launched under the Ninth Malaysia Plan and is seen as a key catalyst in the socio-economic development of Malaysia's Northern Corridor Economic Region. It was named after the fourteenth Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Tuanku Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah of Kedah.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (bridge connecting Penang Island to the mainland)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was constructed by UEM Builders Sdn Bhd and China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC). The project was completed with a major loan from China. The bridge is maintained by Jambatan Kedua Sdn Bhd (JKSB). The toll for the bridge is collected one way when crossing from the mainland to Penang Island. The bridge features two toll plazas: the Penang Second Bridge Integrated Toll Plaza and the Penang Second Bridge Toll Plaza. The bridge also has a highway patrol unit, JKSB Ronda, which provides assistance to commuters.

world knowledge.Name: Sissinghurst Castle Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sissinghurst Castle Garden was created by Vita Sackville-West and her husband Harold Nicolson in the 1930s. It is one of the most famous gardens in England and is designated Grade I on Historic England's register of historic parks and gardens. The site has been occupied since the Middle Ages, with the present-day buildings dating back to the 1530s. The garden was transformed from a farmstead into a world-renowned garden over thirty years. After Sackville-West's death in 1962, the estate was donated to the National Trust.

Major_Events.Description: Vita Sackville-West and Harold Nicolson began transforming the farmstead into a garden.
The estate was donated to the National Trust after Vita Sackville-West's death.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden design is based on axial walks that open onto enclosed gardens, termed 'garden rooms'. The White Garden is particularly influential, with a palette of white, silver, grey, and green. The garden contains an internationally respected plant collection, particularly old garden roses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sissinghurst Castle Garden is culturally significant as one of the most famous gardens in England, influencing horticultural thought and practice. It is also significant in LGBTQ culture due to Vita Sackville-West's life and work.
world knowledge.Details: The garden was first opened to the public in 1938. It is now one of the National Trust's most popular properties, receiving nearly 200,000 visitors in 2017. The garden continues to influence garden design worldwide and is a major tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Kanger Valley National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kanger Valley National Park, also known as Kanger Ghati National Park, was established in July 1982. It is located in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, India, and is known for its biodiversity, landscape, waterfalls, and subterranean limestone caves. The park is named after the Kanger River, which flows through it.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features highly heterogeneous land formations, including low flat areas, steep slopes, plateaus, valleys, and stream courses. It is known for its subterranean limestone caves with dripstones and flowstones, including stalactites and stalagmites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its rich biodiversity and the presence of the Bastar hill myna, the state bird of Chhattisgarh. It is also home to a sizable tribal population and is a popular destination for hikers, wildlife enthusiasts, and researchers.
world knowledge.Details: The park extends from the Teerathagarh waterfalls in the west to the Kolab river in the east, spanning an average length of 33.5 km and an average width of 6 km. It is one of India's densest national parks and is known for its flora and fauna, including tigers, leopards, and various bird species. The park also has remarkable geological diversity, with rock formations from the Cuddapah and Vindhyan groups. The Kanger River is a lifeline for the park and the surrounding region, and the park is a catchment area for the Godavari River.

world knowledge.Name: Point King Lighthouse
world knowledge.Area: Great Southern region of Western Australia
world knowledge.Address: Princess Royal Harbour, Albany, Western Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Point King Lighthouse was the first navigational light for the Port of Albany and the second lighthouse to be built on the West Australian coastline. It was constructed in 1858 following the anticipation of the return of the profitable mail boat service from England via Albany after the Crimean War. The lighthouse was deactivated in 1911 and fell into disrepair, with conservation efforts beginning in the late 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was constructed and first lit on New Year's Day 1858, serving as a navigational aid for the Port of Albany.
The lighthouse was deactivated and made redundant.
The Albany City Council allocated A$20,000 to stabilize the ruins of the lighthouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original lighthouse featured a square wooden tower 17 feet (5 m) high, equipped with an oil-fired light. The keeper's house was situated 47 feet (14 m) above the high water mark. The current structure is a cylindrical tower with a balcony and beacon, painted white, and powered by solar energy.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Point King Lighthouse is historically significant as the first navigational light for the Port of Albany and the second lighthouse on the West Australian coastline. It represents early maritime navigation and colonial infrastructure in Western Australia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid for ships entering Princess Royal Harbour.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was designated as a State Registered Place on 13 December 1996. It has a focal height of 42 metres (138 ft) and a range of 12 nautical miles (22 km; 14 mi). The light characteristic is FI W 3s.

world knowledge.Name: Scrub Island (British Virgin Islands)
world knowledge.Area: Caribbean Sea, Lesser Antilles, Virgin Islands
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 230 acres (0.93 km²), including Big Scrub (170 acres) and Little Scrub (60 acres). 1.6 mi (2.6 km) long.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Scrub Island was formed by volcanic activity and has been inhabited for about 5000 years, first by Ciboney and later Arawak Indians. Discovered by Christopher Columbus in 1493, it was later used by pirates and privateers. The British took control in 1672. The island is now home to the Scrub Island Resort Marina and Spa, the first resort development in the British Virgin Islands in over 15 years.

Major_Events.Description: Discovered by Christopher Columbus during his second voyage.
The British took control of the island.
Scrub Island Resort Marina and Spa was built, marking the first resort development in the British Virgin Islands in over 15 years.
The Scrub Island Resort went into bankruptcy protection due to unpaid loans.
The resort emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Luxury private island resort designed by architecture firm OBM International USA, featuring 52 guest accommodations, villas, a spa, restaurants, and a marina.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Scrub Island has a rich history of indigenous settlement, European discovery, and pirate activity. It is now a significant luxury tourism destination in the British Virgin Islands.
world knowledge.Details: The island is fringed by three beaches, features protected coves, nature trails, and is virtually vehicle-free. The resort's marina offers 55 slips, including five for mega yachts. The shallows surrounding the island are popular for snorkeling and diving. The most convenient international airport is San Juan, Puerto Rico, with connecting flights to Beef Island/Tortola.

image_name: Osh State Academic Uzbek Music and Drama Theater named after Babur

world knowledge.Name: Osh State Academic Uzbek Music and Drama Theater named after Babur
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Osh State Academic Uzbek Music and Drama Theater named after Babur is the oldest professional theater in Kyrgyzstan and the second oldest in Central Asia. It was founded in 1914 by Rahmonberdi Madazimov, a teacher from Russian-native schools in Osh. The theater has played a significant role in the development of theatrical and musical arts in the region, particularly in southern Kyrgyzstan. It has undergone several reconstructions in 1929, 1979, and 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The theater was founded by Rahmonberdi Madazimov, marking the beginning of professional theater in Kyrgyzstan.
An amateur theater group was formed under the leadership of Rahmonberdi Madazimov, contributing to the development of theatrical art in Kyrgyzstan.
A circle was formed within the drama troupe, which played a crucial role in the development of both theatrical and musical arts in southern Kyrgyzstan.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theater is culturally significant as it is the oldest professional theater in Kyrgyzstan and has been a cornerstone in the development of theatrical and musical arts in the region. It is named after Babur, a historical figure in Central Asia, and continues to be a vital cultural institution.
world knowledge.Details: The theater has a capacity of 1000 people and is owned by the Ministry of Culture, Information and Tourism of the Kyrgyz Republic. It has undergone several reconstructions in 1929, 1979, and 2012.

world knowledge.Name: His Majesty's Theatre, London
world knowledge.Historical_Background: His Majesty's Theatre, originally opened in 1897, has a rich history of hosting significant theatrical productions, including the establishment of the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art (RADA) by Herbert Beerbohm Tree. It has been a venue for premieres of works by notable playwrights and composers, and has specialized in musicals since the First World War, notably hosting long-running shows like 'The Phantom of the Opera'.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was opened in 1897, designed by Charles J. Phipps for Herbert Beerbohm Tree.

Major_Events.Event: Premiere of 'The Phantom of the Opera'
Major_Events.Description: The world premiere of Andrew Lloyd Webber's 'The Phantom of the Opera' took place at His Majesty's Theatre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Charles J. Phipps in a style inspired by the French Renaissance, the theatre features a Corinthian colonnade and a large, flat stage, reputedly the first of its kind in Britain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: His Majesty's Theatre is culturally significant for its contributions to British theatre, including the development of RADA and its role in popularizing musical theatre in the UK.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has undergone several renovations and ownership changes, most recently being owned by LW Theatres. It continues to host major theatrical productions, maintaining its status as a key venue in London's West End.

world knowledge.Name: Birla Mandir, Jaipur
world knowledge.Address: Birla Mandir, Jawahar Lal Nehru Marg, Tilak Nagar, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302022, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Birla Mandir, Jaipur, also known as Lakshmi Narayan Temple, is a Hindu temple constructed by the B.M. Birla Foundation in 1988. It is built entirely of white marble and is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Lakshmi and god Vishnu (Narayan). The land for the temple was reportedly sold to the Birla family by a Maharaja for one rupee. Construction began in 1977 under the direction of Ramanauj Das and Ghanshyam Birla and was completed in 1988.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was officially opened on February 22, 1988.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple is made of white marble and features a modern architectural style. It has four distinct parts: the sanctum, tower, main hall, and entrance. The temple has three towers, symbolizing the three main faiths of India, and stained glass windows depicting traditional Hindu stories. Marble sculptures reference Hindu mythology, and the temple includes statues of Hindu deities such as Lakshmi, Narayan, and Ganesh inside, while figures like Christ, the Virgin Mary, St. Peter, Buddha, Confucius, and Socrates are depicted on the outer walls. The temple is built on a raised platform, making it a prominent feature in the Jaipur skyline, especially when illuminated at night.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Birla Mandir is culturally significant as a modern Hindu temple that incorporates elements of various religions and philosophies, reflecting India's diverse cultural heritage. It serves as a place of worship and a symbol of the philanthropic efforts of the Birla family.
world knowledge.Details: The temple grounds include gardens and a small gift shop. Below the temple lies the B. M. Birla Family Museum and the Sri and Smt. G. P. Birla Gallery, which contain photographs of the temple's construction and the Birla family's philanthropic contributions, as well as treasures belonging to the Birla family. Statues of its founders, Rukmani Devi Birla and Braj Mohan Birla, are located outdoors in covered pavilions, facing the temple with hands folded in namaskāra mudra.

world knowledge.Name: Misamis Occidental Aquamarine Park
world knowledge.Location: National Highway Ozamiz-Oroquieta, Tudela, 7202 Misamis Occidental, Philippines
world knowledge.Address: National Highway Ozamiz-Oroquieta, Tudela, 7202 Misamis Occidental, Philippines
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Misamis Occidental Aquamarine Park is a tropical resort and habitat for various marine mammals. It was developed as part of the Misamis Occidental Aquamarine Development and Protection Program (MOADPP) launched in 2002 to convert the area into an ecotourism site, enhancing revenue generation while prioritizing environmental preservation. The park includes facilities such as hotels, cottages, a mini zoo, function halls, restaurants, incubators, and a mangrove reforestation area. MOAPY Island was established as a haven for rescued dolphins and fish, and for aquaculture production. The Australian Agency for International Development (AUSAID) supported livelihood projects to provide alternative income sources for local families.

Major_Events.Event: Launch of Misamis Occidental Aquamarine Development and Protection Program (MOADPP)
Major_Events.Description: Initiative aimed at converting the park into an ecotourism site, focusing on environmental preservation and revenue generation.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Misamis Occidental Aquamarine Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was officially opened to the public in February 2003.
Dolphin Island is undergoing rehabilitation and is temporarily closed to visitors until further notice.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of facilities including hotels, cottages, a mini zoo, function halls, restaurants, incubators, and a mangrove reforestation area. MOAPY Island serves as a haven for rescued dolphins and fish, and for aquaculture production.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park plays a crucial role in the local community's livelihood by providing job opportunities and supporting environmental preservation. It also serves as an ecotourism site, attracting visitors and contributing to the local economy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ecotourism site and habitat for marine mammals
world knowledge.Details: The coastal region of Misamis Occidental extends over 162 kilometers and features an ecosystem rich with shoals and reefs, essential for the local population's livelihood. The tourism boom linked to the Aquamarine Park has augmented job opportunities for the community. The park's website is www.misocc.gov.ph/tourism/.

world knowledge.Name: Skarnsund Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Norwegian County Road 755, Inderøy Municipality, Norway
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Skarnsund Bridge was constructed to replace the Vangshylla–Kjerringvik Ferry, providing easier access to the central areas of Innherred. It is the only road crossing of the Trondheimsfjord. The bridge was financed partly through tolls and was listed as a cultural heritage in 2007. The bridge connected the municipalities of Mosvik and Inderøy, which merged in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened by King Harald V on 19 December 1991, after he took the last ferry across the fjord. A monument, the King's Stone, bearing the signature of the king, is located at the resting place on the Mosvik side.
Toll collection lasted from 1991 to 24 May 2007, financing 30% of the bridge's cost. The bridge was paid off three years before schedule.
The Norwegian Directorate for Cultural Heritage listed the bridge as a protected cultural heritage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Skarnsund Bridge is a concrete cable-stayed bridge with a span of 530 metres (1,740 ft), making it one of the world's longest cable-stayed bridges. The two pylons are 152 metres (499 ft) tall. The deck is 2.15 metres (7.1 ft) deep and 13 metres (43 ft) wide, with two lanes for automobiles and one for pedestrians and bicycles. The bridge was built to withstand winds up to 48.5 metres per second (159 ft/s) and earthquakes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant as it replaced a ferry service, improving connectivity in the region. It has won several awards, including Betongtavlen (1992), Beautiful Roads Award (1994), and the international FIP Award (1994). It was also listed as a protected cultural heritage in 2008.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Road bridge providing a crossing over the Skarnsundet strait and the Trondheimsfjord.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge used 19,600 cubic metres (25,600 cu yd) of concrete and has 208 cables with a total length of 33 kilometres (21 mi). The cables can be replaced separately if needed. The bridge was the longest cable-stayed bridge in the world by the length of main span upon completion but has since lost the title.

world knowledge.Name: Zhenhai Tower (Guangzhou)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height: 28 meters, Width: 31 meters, Depth: 16 meters
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1380 during the Ming dynasty by Yongjia Marquis Zhu Liangzu (朱亮祖). It was the highest building in Guangzhou at the time and served as the city's symbol until the Five Goats Statue was built.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Five-story pagoda-style tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Symbol of Guangzhou before the Five Goats Statue was built and a historic landmark representing the city's heritage.
world knowledge.Details: Also known as the Five-Story Pagoda. Transcriptions: Hanyu Pinyin - Wǔcéng Lóu, Jyutping - ng5 cang4 lau4. Literal meaning: Five-Story Building.

world knowledge.Name: Yamadera Basho Memorial Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum was established to commemorate the 300-year anniversary of poet Matsuo Bashō's visit to Yamadera, which he chronicled in 'Oku no Hosomichi (The Narrow Road to the Deep North)'. It opened on July 9, 1989, as part of Yamagata's 100-year anniversary celebrations.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened on July 9, 1989, to celebrate the 300-year anniversary of Bashō's visit to Yamadera and Yamagata's 100-year anniversary.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The buildings are designed in traditional sukiya-zukuri tea ceremony room style by architect Masao Nakamura.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum chronicles Bashō's life and his contributions to the literary style of haiku, preserving his legacy and promoting cultural programs related to literature and haiku.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Biographical museum dedicated to Matsuo Bashō and his literary works.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is located near the Yamadera temple and features many writings by Bashō, as well as literati and artists from his time and later. It includes traditional Japanese style meeting rooms and tea rooms used for tea ceremonies and cultural programs, such as seminars on literature and haiku taikai poetry writing contests in both Japanese and English. The official website is yamadera-basho.jp.

world knowledge.Name: Master Chandgiram Sports Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium is named after Haryanvi wrestler Chandgi Ram and is now under the administration of Major Dhyanchand Sports College, Saifai.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted this national-level hockey championship.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The sports complex includes a 20,000-capacity Astroturf hockey field with a synthetic running track, a multipurpose hall for badminton and wrestling, an international-standard swimming pool, and a Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Centre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports facility in Uttar Pradesh, offering training in various sports and hosting national-level events. It is also a Global Certified Field by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports complex for training and hosting events in hockey, badminton, wrestling, swimming, and other sports.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is used by Sports Authority of India, Major Dhyanchand Sports College, Saifai (for hockey and swimming), and Uttar Pradesh Government's Saifai Sports Hostel. It also serves students from the nearby residential sports college for hockey, wrestling, badminton, and swimming facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Kocher Viaduct
world knowledge.Address: Near Schwäbisch Hall, Kocher valley, Germany
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,128 metres (3,701 ft) length, 31 metres (102 ft) width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kocher Viaduct is the highest viaduct in Germany and was the bridge with the tallest pillars in the world before the Millau Viaduct was completed in 2004. It was constructed to conduct the Autobahn 6 across the Kocher valley between Heilbronn and Nuremberg.

Major_Events.Description: The Kocher Viaduct lost its status as the bridge with the tallest pillars in the world upon the completion of the Millau Viaduct in France.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The viaduct is a prestressed-concrete girder bridge with nine spans covering a length of 1,128m. The outer two spans are 81m each, while the remaining seven are 138m each. Pillar height varies from 40m to 178m. The bridge table is 31m wide.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kocher Viaduct is a significant engineering feat and a notable landmark in Germany. A museum in Geislingen am Kocher below the bridge tells the viaduct's story and displays dinosaur fossils found during the construction of the motorway.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conducts the Autobahn 6 across the Kocher valley
world knowledge.Details: A museum in the village of Geislingen am Kocher below the bridge not only tells the viaduct's story but also displays dinosaur fossils found during the construction of the motorway.

world knowledge.Name: Nivedita Setu
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Bally, Howrah with Dakshineswar, Kolkata
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 880 metres (2,890 ft) long, 29 metres (95 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nivedita Setu was constructed to alleviate traffic on the aging Vivekananda Setu, which opened in 1932. It is named after Sister Nivedita, a social worker-disciple of Swami Vivekananda. The bridge was designed to complement the nearby Dakshineswar Kali Temple and handle modern traffic demands.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began by Larsen & Toubro.
The bridge was opened to traffic in a record time.
Received an Award of Excellence from the American Segmental Bridge Institute, USA.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-span extradosed bridge with seven continuous spans of 110 m each, totaling 880 m. It features 254 pre-stressed concrete girders, 14m high pylons with supporting cables, and deep-well foundations. It is India's first single-profile cable-stayed bridge with short pylons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named after Sister Nivedita, reflecting its cultural and historical importance. Its design respects the nearby Dakshineswar Kali Temple by ensuring the pylons do not overshadow the temple.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Roadway bridge carrying the Belghoria Expressway, part of NH-12, facilitating high-speed traffic across the Hooghly River.

Details.Maintained_by: Second Vivekananda Bridge Tollway Company Pvt. Ltd
Details.Architect: Consulting Engineering Services (CES) International Bridge Technologies Inc. (IBT)
Details.Construction_cost: ₹ 650 crore (equivalent to ₹ 23 billion or US$270 million in 2023)

world knowledge.Name: Jayu Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jayu Park, also known as Freedom Park, is the first Western-style park in Korea, established in 1888. It has undergone several name changes and management transitions, reflecting Korea's modern and contemporary history. The park was managed by the Foreign Residents' Association initially, then by Incheon after 1914. It was a significant site during the March First Movement in 1919 and the Korean War, where more than half of the park was destroyed. The park was renamed Jayugongwon after the statue of Douglas MacArthur was built in 1957.

Major_Events.Description: Hanseong Provisional Government was declared in the park.
More than half of the park was destroyed.
The park was renamed Jayugongwon after the statue was built.
A pro-North Korea group protested for the removal of the MacArthur statue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Western-style urban park with statues, a small zoo, and a memorial.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jayu Park is culturally significant as it reflects Korea's modern and contemporary history, including its colonial period, the March First Movement, and the Korean War. It is also renowned for its cherry blossom blooming season.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located on a bluff overlooking Incheon's harbor and prominently features a statue of General Douglas MacArthur. It also houses a number of other statues, a small zoo, and a memorial to the Joseon–United States Treaty of 1882.

world knowledge.Name: Waltham Forest Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first civic building in the area was a single-storey public hall in Orford Road, Walthamstow, dating back to the first half of the 19th century. It was replaced by an Italianate-style town hall in 1866. After becoming an urban district in 1895 and a municipal borough in 1929, a purpose-built town hall was constructed on the site of Chestnuts Farm. The foundation stone was laid in 1938, and the building was completed in 1942 despite interruptions from World War II.

Major_Events.Description: The assembly hall hosted a concert performance by Yehudi Menuhin.
The assembly hall hosted a concert performance by Plácido Domingo.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh
Major_Events.Description: Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh visited the town hall and had lunch with civic officials.
The building hosted the Antiques Roadshow.
The building hosted the Antiques Roadshow again.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Philip Dalton Hepworth in the stripped classical style, the building is constructed of Portland stone. It features a symmetrical main frontage with 19 bays, a three-bay full-height portico with piers supporting a frieze, and a tall copper-clad clock tower. The council chamber projects to the rear, with five statues and six relief sculptures by John Francis Kavanagh.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a Grade II Listed Building and serves as the headquarters of Waltham Forest London Borough Council. It has hosted significant cultural events and notable visitors, including Queen Elizabeth II.
world knowledge.Details: The assembly hall was used as a British Restaurant during World War II. The town hall underwent extensive renovation completed in 2021, including the creation of Fellowship Square and the Queen Elizabeth II memorial garden with a copy of The Arch by Henry Moore.

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Marcello Melani
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stadio Marcello Melani, originally named Stadio Comunale, was opened on 25 June 1966. It replaced the smaller stadium 'Monteoliveto' where Pistoiese played around 600 official matches. The stadium was renamed in 2006 to honor Marcello Melani, the president of Pistoiese from 1974 to 1984, during which the club earned its only promotion to Serie A.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated with a friendly match between Pistoiese and Vasco de Gama, ending 1–2.
The stadium was renamed to honor Marcello Melani, former president of Pistoiese, who led the club to its only Serie A promotion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features grass surface and includes stands such as Curva Sud for visiting supporters and a main west stand for home supporters. The Curva Nord and east side terraced stand are currently closed.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant as the home ground of U.S. Pistoiese 1921 and for its role in the club's history, including its only promotion to Serie A under Marcello Melani's presidency.
world knowledge.Details: As of the 2021–22 season, only the Curva Sud and the main west stand are in use. The stadium has undergone renovations in 1980 and 2000.

world knowledge.Name: Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built in 1933 as a gift for Delhi from the Maharaja of Bhavnagar. Originally named the Irwin Amphitheatre, it was designed by Anthony S. DeMillo and opened by Lord Willingdon. It was renamed National Stadium before the 1951 Asian Games and later had Dhyan Chand's name added in 2002. The stadium underwent major reconstruction in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: Served as the venue for the 1st Asian Games.
Host venue for the 2010 Men's Hockey World Cup.
Field hockey venue for the 2010 Commonwealth Games.
Hosted the fourth edition of Jashn-e-Rekhta, the Urdu festival of India.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a multipurpose stadium, it was redesigned with a rectangular seating bowl, three synthetic pitches (two international standard, one for practice), foldable floodlight towers, and air-conditioning. The main field seats 16,200 spectators, with barrier-free provisions for physically challenged individuals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named after legendary Indian field hockey player Dhyan Chand, the stadium is a symbol of India's rich hockey heritage. It has hosted major international events, reinforcing its importance in sports history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is adjacent to the Indian Coast Guard Headquarters. It features two competitive flood-lit pitches with 2,200 lux illumination for high-definition TV transmission, change rooms, relaxation lounges, and a VVIP lounge. Power supply is backed by generator sets and battery uninterrupted power supply.

world knowledge.Name: Patliputra Sports Complex
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The sports complex was inaugurated on 1 March 2012 with the first Women's World Cup Kabaddi Championship in India. It was built at an approximate cost of ₹19.98 Crore and is owned by the Bihar State Sports Authority and the Directorate of Youth Welfare and Sports.

Major_Events.Event: First Women World Cup Kabaddi Championship
Major_Events.Description: Inaugural event with participation from 16 countries.
Hosted seven league matches with the home team Patna Pirates.

Major_Events.Event: All India Federation Cup Wrestling tournament
Major_Events.Description: Held in March 2012.
Held in December 2012.
Concluded at the indoor stadium of the complex.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern state-of-the-art complex with facilities for both indoor and outdoor games, including a 400-meter athlete track, swimming pool, and accommodation for 200 sportspersons. Divided into four wings: Outdoor, Indoor, Coaches, and Hostel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hosts significant national and international sports events, promoting sports culture in Bihar and India.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose sports complex hosting various sports events and training facilities.
world knowledge.Details: The outdoor stadium, Patliputra Stadium, has a capacity of 20,000 spectators, while the indoor stadium holds 3,500. The complex includes a hostel with 227 rooms and is used for athletics, football, kabaddi, rugby sevens, and other sports.

world knowledge.Name: Chongqing Science and Technology Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chongqing Science and Technology Museum was initiated with a ground-breaking ceremony on 7 January 2006, and construction began in October 2006. It was opened to the public on 9 September 2009.

Major_Events.Description: The ceremony marked the beginning of the construction of the museum.
The museum was officially opened to the public on this date.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by Guida Moseley Brown Architects. It is located on a plot of 37 mu and features modern architectural elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum serves as an educational hub for science and technology in Chongqing, providing free access to school children and featuring an IMAX theatre.
world knowledge.Details: The museum cost 567 million RMB to build. It is centrally located near the Chongqing Grand Theatre and the confluence of the Jialing River and the Yangtze River. It features an IMAX theatre and is free for school children.

world knowledge.Name: Himmelbjerget
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height difference of 121 m from Julsø lake to the top
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Himmelbjerget, meaning 'The Sky Mountain' or 'The Mountain of Heaven', is a hill in Denmark that has been a center for gatherings and celebrations for over 200 years. It was once believed to be the highest point in Denmark until 1847. A red brick tower was erected in 1875 to honor King Frederik VII and his role in establishing Denmark's first constitution in 1849.

Major_Events.Description: A 25.1 m tall tower was built to honor King Frederik VII and his role in giving Denmark its first constitution in 1849.

Major_Events.Event: Commemoration of women's right to vote
Major_Events.Description: A monument was erected to commemorate women's right to vote in Denmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hill features a 25.1 m tall red brick tower erected in 1875, along with several other monuments honoring individuals and historical events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Himmelbjerget is culturally significant as a historical gathering place and for its role in celebrating the birth of the Danish nation. The tower and monuments commemorate key events in Danish history, including the establishment of the constitution and women's suffrage.
world knowledge.Details: Himmelbjerget is one of the highest natural points in Denmark, with a height difference of 121 m from the lake Julsø below to the top. It is a popular destination for hiking and offers magnificent views. The historic steamship Hjejlen still ferries visitors to the hill from Ry and Silkeborg.

world knowledge.Name: Trbovlje Power Station
world knowledge.Address: Bank of the Sava River near Trbovlje, Slovenia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Trbovlje Power Station was a lignite-fired power station built in 1964-1968 and became operational in 1966. It consisted of two units: a 125 MW steam unit and a 63 MW gas unit. The original power station was built in 1915. The plant was operated by Termoelektrarna Trbovlje d.o.o. and was used as a reserve unit for the Slovenian electric system. The Trbovlje Chimney, built in 1976, is the tallest flue-gas stack in Europe. The station was decommissioned in 2016.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the new power station
Major_Events.Description: The new power station was built and became operational in 1966.
The 360-meter high flue-gas stack was built, becoming the tallest in Europe.
It was announced that the power station would be shut down.
The power station was finally closed after several years dormant.
Climbers Janja Garnbret and Domen Škofic climbed an artificial climbing route up the 360-meter chimney for the film 360 Ascent.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The power station consisted of two units: a 125 MW steam unit and a 63 MW gas unit. The Trbovlje Chimney, built in 1976, is 360 meters high and required 11,866 cubic meters of concrete and 1,079 tons of reinforcing steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Trbovlje Power Station played a significant role in the electrification and modernization of Slovenia, particularly in the Trbovlje region. The Trbovlje Chimney is a notable architectural and engineering feat, being the tallest flue-gas stack in Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The power station was primarily fueled by lignite, with natural gas as a secondary fuel. It had a nameplate capacity of 188 MW. The station was decommissioned in 2016 after several years of dormancy. The Trbovlje Chimney was used to ensure emissions were removed from the deep, narrow valley under all weather conditions.

world knowledge.Name: University of Saskatchewan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Saskatchewan (U of S, or USask) is a Canadian public research university, founded on March 19, 1907, and located on the east side of the South Saskatchewan River in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada. An "Act to establish and incorporate a University for the Province of Saskatchewan" was passed by the provincial legislature in 1907. It established the provincial university on March 19, 1907 "for the purpose of providing facilities for higher education in all its branches and enabling all persons without regard to race, creed or religion to take the fullest advantage".

Major_Events.Description: The University of Saskatchewan was established by an act of the provincial legislature.
The university awarded its first degrees.
The Canadian Light Source synchrotron, one of the largest and most innovative investments in Canadian science, opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original buildings were built using native limestone – greystone – which was mined just north of campus. Over the years, this greystone became one of the most recognizable campus signatures. When the local supply of limestone was exhausted, the university turned to Tyndall stone, which is quarried in Manitoba.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Saskatchewan is the largest education institution in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan and is one of Canada's top research universities. It is a member of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities (the 15 most research-intensive universities in Canada).
world knowledge.Details: The university offers over 200 academic programs and is home to the Canadian Light Source synchrotron, the Vaccine and Infectious Disease Organization, and Innovation Place Research Park. It has a tricameral governance structure consisting of a Board of Governors, University Council, and Senate.

world knowledge.Name: Angus L. Macdonald Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1.3 kilometres (0.81 mi) long, 11.5 metres (34.8 feet) wide, 102.9 metres (337.69 feet) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Angus L. Macdonald Bridge is a suspension bridge crossing Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia, Canada. It opened on April 2, 1955, and is named after the former premier of Nova Scotia, Angus L. Macdonald, who had died in 1954 and had been instrumental in having the bridge built. The bridge was designed by Philip Louis Pratley, one of Canada's foremost long-span bridge designers.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge opened on April 2, 1955, and originally cost $11.5 million.
The original two lanes and one sidewalk and utility corridor were expanded to three lanes, with the centre lane being reversible to assist with traffic flow during peak periods.
Every piece of steel that makes up the suspended spans, except the towers and two main cables, were replaced. The replacement portion of the project was completed in February 2017.
The bridge became toll-free as of March 14, 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a design similar to the Lions Gate Bridge in Vancouver. The bridge features an orthotropic deck, which is 35% lighter than the old one, and has pedestrian and bicycle lanes attached to the outside of the structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a vital transportation link between Halifax and Dartmouth and is named after a prominent political figure in Nova Scotia. It has also been the site of notable events, including a suicide by environmental activist Tooker Gomberg and a lawsuit by the Department of National Defence.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Motor vehicle, pedestrian, and bicycle transportation across Halifax Harbour.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge regularly experiences traffic congestion during rush hours. Large commercial vehicles are not permitted to cross and must use the wider MacKay Bridge to the northwest. Public transit buses are allowed to cross, and the bridge links several Halifax Transit routes. The bridge has safety barriers installed along 100% of its pedestrian walkways.

world knowledge.Name: Saint Louis Science Center
world knowledge.Address: 5050 Oakland Ave, St. Louis, Missouri, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded as a planetarium in 1963, the Saint Louis Science Center evolved into a major science museum complex. It was initially funded by a city bond issue, with significant contributions from James Smith McDonnell. The center expanded over the years, including a major addition in 1991 and the GROW pavilion in 2016.

Major_Events.Description: The planetarium opened with a unique design by Gyo Obata and equipment donated by James Smith McDonnell.

Major_Events.Event: Reopening as Saint Louis Science Center
Major_Events.Description: The planetarium was remodeled and reopened as the Saint Louis Science Center.
A new building opened across from the Planetarium, increasing the size of the Science Center by a factor of seven.
An air-supported building was added to host traveling exhibitions and events.
The museum’s largest major addition in 25 years was completed, focusing on agriculture and technology.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original planetarium was designed by Gyo Obata with a unique, futuristic shape. The complex includes a five-story domed OMNIMAX theater and a Skybridge connecting buildings over I-64. The GROW pavilion features a flexible, open floor plan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Saint Louis Science Center is one of the largest science centers in the United States and has been a leader in public science education. It features innovative exhibits and technology, including a rare ZEISS UNIVERSARIUM Mark IX Star Projector.
world knowledge.Details: The Science Center includes a ZEISS UNIVERSARIUM Mark IX Star Projector, one of only three in the United States. It also features an OMNIMAX theater with state-of-the-art projection and sound technology. The center has hosted notable exhibitions such as Body Worlds and Star Trek: The Exhibition.

world knowledge.Name: Cerro Catedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cerro Catedral is a mountain located 19 kilometres (12 mi) from San Carlos de Bariloche, and inside the Nahuel Huapí National Park, in Patagonia, Argentina. The complex is one of the most important ski resorts in South America and the Southern Hemisphere.

Major_Events.Description: The 1st South American Ski Mountaineering Championship in combination with the last race of the 2005 South American Ski Mountaineering Cup and the 2nd International Open of ski mountaineering was carried out on the Cerro Catedral.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cerro Catedral is one of the most important ski resorts in South America and the Southern Hemisphere, popular due to the views of the Nahuel Huapi lake.
world knowledge.Details: The complex has a skiable area of 6 km2 (2.3 sq mi), 48 km (30 mi) of ski runs, and a lift capacity of 35,000 skiers per hour. There are a number of hotels and hostels at the foot of the mountain, and a summer hikers' hut called Refugio Lynch on one of the tops of the mountain. During the summer, the Refugio Frey and a camping accommodate trekkers and rock climbers next to Tonček lagoon, near the Torre Principal; Catedral's highest point. The climate is affected by the altitude, with higher elevations classified as an alpine or tundra climate and lower elevations as a cool mediterranean climate. Cerro Catedral has the highest frequency of days with snowfalls in Argentina, averaging 98 days per year.

world knowledge.Name: Mendel Museum of Masaryk University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mendel Museum was established in 2002 with international cooperation, primarily supported by the Austrian society VFG and affiliated scientists and patrons. It became an institution of Masaryk University in 2007. Located within the Augustinian abbey in Old Brno, the museum honors Gregor Johann Mendel, the Augustinian abbot and father of genetics, who conducted his groundbreaking studies on plant heredity there.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum promotes the legacy of Gregor Johann Mendel, who is recognized as the father of genetics. It highlights his contributions to biology, meteorology, and bee breeding, and serves as a bridge between academic science and the public. It also supports educational initiatives for students and applicants at Masaryk University.
world knowledge.Details: The museum frequently stages short-term art exhibitions, integrating art into its scientific and educational mission. It aims to raise awareness about Mendel’s work and the fields of study available at Masaryk University.

world knowledge.Name: Museum Ludwig
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Museum Ludwig, established in 1976, emerged as an independent institution from the Wallraf-Richartz Museum. It was founded after chocolate magnate Peter Ludwig endowed 350 modern artworks valued at $45 million, leading the City of Cologne to build a dedicated museum for works made after 1900. The current building, designed by architects Peter Busmann and Godfrid Haberer, opened in 1986 near the Cologne Cathedral. The museum was separated from the Wallraf Richartz Museum in 1994.

Major_Events.Description: Lawyer Josef Haubrich donated his collection of art from 1914 to 1939 to the city of Cologne, which became part of Museum Ludwig.
Museum Ludwig was established as an independent institution after Peter Ludwig's endowment of modern artworks.
The new building designed by Peter Busmann and Godfrid Haberer opened near the Cologne Cathedral.
Museum Ludwig was separated from the Wallraf Richartz Museum and given sole use of the building on Bischofsgartenstrasse.
Museum Ludwig collaborated with the Bell Art Center to organize an unofficial retrospective of Anselm Kiefer in China, which led to the temporary loss of artworks.
Museum Ludwig restituted several artworks looted by the Nazis to the heirs of Alfred Flechtheim and Curt Glaser.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed by architects Peter Busmann and Godfrid Haberer and opened in 1986. It is located near the Cologne Cathedral and houses the Kölner Philharmonie.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Museum Ludwig is one of the most important museums for modern art in Germany, with significant collections of Pop Art, Abstract, and Surrealism. It holds one of the largest Picasso collections in Europe and the most comprehensive collection of early Russian avant-garde artworks outside Russia.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses the Kölner Philharmonie and is located near the Heinrich-Böll-Platz, a public square designed by Dani Karavan. The museum also awards the Wolfgang Hahn Prize annually to international artists. It has restituted several artworks looted by the Nazis to their rightful heirs.

world knowledge.Name: Tivoli Theatre, Brisbane
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tivoli Theatre was a prominent theatre in Brisbane, operating from 1914 until its closure in 1965 and demolition in 1969. It was located opposite the Brisbane City Hall, on the site of the present King George Square. The theatre was designed by architect Henry E. White in an Art Nouveau style and could accommodate 1800 people on three levels. It featured innovative cooling systems and a rooftop garden theatre. The theatre was initially used for live performances and later adapted for films. It was purchased by the Brisbane City Council in 1963 and demolished as part of the King George Square development.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened on 15 May 1915 with a production of the Tivoli Follies in the auditorium and a vaudeville production in the rooftop theatre.
The theatre was renovated to provide more seating, changing from a live theatre venue to one more suited for film audiences. Two galleries were removed to make way for a single dress circle.
Additional renovations to the foyer and auditorium took place.
The theatre was purchased by the Brisbane City Council in 1963, closed in 1965, and demolished in 1969 as part of the King George Square development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tivoli Theatre was designed in an Art Nouveau style by architect Henry E. White. It featured three levels with a capacity for 1800 people, an air cooling system, ruby red carpets, and a rooftop garden theatre with open sides for ventilation and steel shutters to keep out rain. The facade had Oriental influences.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tivoli Theatre was a significant cultural venue in Brisbane, hosting live performances and films. It was part of the Rickard Tivoli circuit of Australia and played a role in the city's entertainment history. Its innovative design and cooling systems were notable for the time.
world knowledge.Details: Programs from the theatre are held in the Fryer Library of the University of Queensland. The theatre had a rival in the Empire Theatre, also located in Albert Street, which drew bigger crowds. Smoking was permitted in the rooftop theatre, and during hot summer months, the rooftop garden was a more desirable venue. The building had two entrances, allowing two production companies to co-exist on site with separate audiences.

world knowledge.Name: Swiss National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Swiss National Museum, established in 1898, is part of the Musée Suisse Group, affiliated with the Federal Office of Culture. The museum building, designed by Gustav Gull in the historicist style, resembles French Renaissance city chateaus and is located adjacent to Central Station and the Platzspitz park in Zurich. Its inauguration was filmed by François-Henri Lavanchy-Clarke, the first non-French concessionary of the Lumière brothers.

Major_Events.Description: The museum's inauguration was filmed by François-Henri Lavanchy-Clarke, the first non-French concessionary of the Lumière brothers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building, designed by Gustav Gull, is in the historicist style and resembles French Renaissance city chateaus. It features dozens of towers, courts, and a park on a peninsula between the rivers Sihl and Limmat.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Swiss National Museum is one of the main sights of the Old Town district of Zurich and showcases Swiss history from prehistory through ancient times, the Middle Ages, to the 20th century. It houses a rich collection of gothic art, chivalry, liturgical wooden sculptures, panel paintings, carved altars, and Swiss coins.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes a Collections Gallery, an Armoury Tower, a diorama of the Battle of Murten, and a Coin Cabinet. Zunfthaus zur Meisen near Fraumünster church houses the porcelain and faience collection of the Swiss National Museum. The boats of the Zürichsee-Schifffahrtsgesellschaft start their round trips on the Limmat through the city of Zürich at the Swiss National Museum. The closest tram/trolleybus stop is Bahnhofquai/HB.

world knowledge.Name: Balkh University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Balkh University is a public university located in Mazar-i-Sharif, capital of Balkh Province in northern Afghanistan. Established in 1986, the university has about 18,000 students and is the third-largest in Afghanistan after Kabul University and Nangarhar University. Faculties include medicine, engineering, economics, journalism, literature, law, and science.

Major_Events.Description: The government of Pakistan expanded the university by adding the Liaquat Ali Khan Faculty of Engineering, a 10 million dollar separate block, completed in 2012.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Balkh University plays a significant role in the education and rebuilding of Afghanistan, offering various faculties and contributing to scientific research and cultural development.
