world knowledge.Details: The university publishes scientific journals titled 'Balkh Scientific Journal' and 'Marafat', which feature the works and research of lecturers. It also has a monthly outlook newspaper and a journalistic monthly newspaper. Students have access to the university's library, and there are dedicated facilities for sports, physical education, and sporting events.

world knowledge.Name: Odesa International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 7 km southwest from Odesa city centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Odesa International Airport is an international airport serving Odesa, the third largest city in Ukraine. It was built in 1961 and has undergone several expansions and upgrades, including the construction of a new terminal completed in 2017. The airport has faced significant events, including the discovery of a mass grave during expansion work in 2021 and a missile strike in 2022.

Major_Events.Event: Airspace closure due to Russian invasion
Major_Events.Description: On 24 February 2022, Ukraine closed airspace to civilian flights due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
During expansion work in 2021, workers found a mass grave containing 5,000-8,000 skeletons believed to be victims of the Holodomor.
On 30 April 2022, a Russian missile struck the newly constructed runway, destroying it. Ukrainian officials stated that a Bastion missile was used, and no one was hurt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a new terminal with an area of 26,000 square meters, designed to handle 1,000 passengers per hour. It includes 16 check-in desks, four telescopic gangways, and five bus pick-up points. The main runway was extended in 2007, and the airport has ILS CAT I status.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a major gateway to Odesa and has played a significant role in the region's transportation and economic development. The discovery of a mass grave during expansion work highlights its historical and cultural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving both domestic and international flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport's runways were or are co-used by the Ukrainian Air Force. In 2019, an international competition was held for the best idea of a sculpture-symbol of the city's air gates, with Ukrainian artist Stepan Ryabchenko's sculpture 'Sphere' winning first place. As of 24 February 2022, all passenger flights have been suspended indefinitely.

world knowledge.Name: Luceafărul Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1949 as the Puppet Theatre, it became the Theatre for Children and Youth in 1973. In 1987, it was renamed Luceafărul (The Evening Star) Theatre.

Major_Events.Event: International Theatre Festival for Young Audience (FITPT)
Major_Events.Description: A festival hosted every year in October, dedicated to young audiences.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Specializes in plays for families and young audiences, contributing to cultural education and entertainment for younger generations.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a main hall with a capacity of 450 and a small hall with a capacity of 150.

world knowledge.Name: Al-Azhar Park
world knowledge.Address: qism al-Darb al-Ahmar, Historic Cairo, Egypt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al-Azhar Park was created by the Historic Cities Support Programme of the Aga Khan Trust for Culture, funded by Aga Khan IV as a grant to Cairo. The project transformed a 500-year-old dump into a public park, uncovering and restoring the historic Ayyubid Wall during excavation. The park opened in May 2005 and is listed as one of the world's sixty great public spaces by the Project for Public Spaces.

Major_Events.Description: Aga Khan IV decided to create the park after seeing the Al-Darassa hill filled with wreckage and ruins.
Works of excavation, grading, and soil replacement began, moving over 1.5 million cubic meters of rubble and soil.
A 1.5-kilometer section of the historic Ayyubid Wall and two city gates (Bab al-Barqiyya and Bab al-Mahruq) were uncovered and restored.
Al-Azhar Park was opened to the public, featuring traditional Islamic gardens blended with modern elements.
A socio-economic development program was initiated to improve living conditions, restore historical monuments, and provide training and micro-credits to the local population.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park integrates traditional Islamic landscape traditions, including bustan-like orchards, shaded sitting areas (takhtaboush), Fatimid archways, Persian and Timurid water channels, and fountains. The design features central terraced formal gardens, Mamluk multicolored stonework, sunken gardens, intersecting waterways, and bold Islamic geometry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Al-Azhar Park is culturally significant as it revitalized a historic area of Cairo, preserved Islamic architectural and landscape traditions, and uncovered the Ayyubid Wall. It also spurred socio-economic development in the impoverished Darb al-Ahmar neighborhood, promoting education, employment, and heritage conservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and urban revitalization project
world knowledge.Details: The park project included the construction of a reservoir and integration of three cisterns for Cairo's water supply. A future 'Urban Plaza' at the northern end will house the Museum of Historic Cairo, showcasing Islamic heritage artifacts. The project aligns with UN Millennium Development Goals by addressing poverty, environmental sustainability, and global partnerships.

world knowledge.Name: New Plymouth Coastal Walkway
world knowledge.Address: From near Port Taranaki to Tiromoana Crescent in Bell Block, New Plymouth, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Coastal Walkway is a foreshoreway constructed in 1999 as a 7-kilometre long walkway. It was extended in 2010, 2014, and 2016 as part of a joint programme by NPDC and NZTA to encourage active transport.

Major_Events.Description: The Coastal Walkway was originally constructed as a 7-kilometre long walkway.
The walkway was extended by 3 kilometres to Bell Block.
The walkway was extended to Tiromoana Crescent in Bell Block, bringing the total length to 12.7 kilometres.
The walkway was extended with the Mangati Pathway, linking the coastal route across Bell Block along the Mangati Reserve to SH3.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The walkway runs through a number of bridges, most notably, the Te Rewa Rewa Bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The walkway is part of a programme to encourage active transport and has received numerous awards.
world knowledge.Details: The walkway stretches from near Port Taranaki, past the central city, through Hickford Park, past Bell Block Beach and to Tiromoana Crescent in Bell Block, north-east of New Plymouth.

world knowledge.Name: Tbilisi Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tbilisi Zoological Park is the oldest and largest zoo in Georgia, located in the country's capital of Tbilisi. Founded in 1927, it was designed by a group of Georgian and Russian specialists and expanded in the 1930s. The zoo faced significant challenges, including economic collapse in the 1990s and a devastating flood in 2015, which resulted in the loss of nearly half of its inhabitants and three keepers.

Major_Events.Description: On 14 June 2015, the swollen Vere river flooded the zoo, resulting in the death of several animals and the escape of many others, including a hippopotamus, lions, tigers, bears, and wolves. Some animals were recaptured, but several were shot by emergency forces. The zoo lost nearly half of its inhabitants, as well as three keepers who lived onsite.

The Tbilisi Zoo was established by the decision of the Tbilisi City Council on 10 February 1927. It was designed by a group of Georgian and Russian specialists and initially consisted of 4 sections: Caucasian or Local; Fauna of the USSR; Exotic animals; Agricultural animals.

The zoo fell into disrepair as a result of economic collapse and political unrest in post-Soviet Georgia, with a large portion of its funding coming from city budget cuts. More than half of the animals at the zoo had died of starvation or cold since 1991.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo was designed by a group of Georgian and Russian specialists and initially consisted of 4 sections: Caucasian or Local; Fauna of the USSR; Exotic animals; Agricultural animals. A project developed by the Australia-based architecture firm Hassell was proposed for relocation, including an entrance hub, boulevard, a secondary hub with playground and café, inner zoo, and an outer open range zoo as well as woodland areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tbilisi Zoo is the oldest and largest zoo in Georgia, representing a significant cultural and historical landmark in Tbilisi. It has played a role in conservation, education, and recreation for nearly a century, despite facing numerous challenges.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo experienced a modest revival in the late 2000s, including the opening of a marine aquarium in 2007. It belongs to the Tbilisi City Hall and largely depends on funding allocated from the city budget. The current director of the Tbilisi Zoo is Zurab Gurielidze.

world knowledge.Name: Ulu Temburong National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ulu Temburong National Park is the first national park to be established in Brunei, protected since 1991. It covers about 40% of the Temburong District and is known as the 'Green Jewel of Brunei'. The park is an important ecotourism centre and hosts the Ulu Ulu Resort.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Ulu Temburong National Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was established as the first national park in Brunei.

The Ulu Ulu Resort was opened in November 2008, marking a historical milestone in Brunei tourism as the first Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between a private tour company and the Government of Brunei Darussalam.

Major_Events.Event: Suspension of operations due to Covid-19
Major_Events.Description: The partnership was forced to suspend operation on 20 June 2020 due to the Covid-19 Pandemic despite aid from the Ministry of Finance & Economy's support.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features an extensive network of boardwalks, bridges, and stairways, 7 kilometres in length, and a canopy viewing walkway built with steel towers supporting the cable way, rising to a height of 50 metres above the forest floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a prime example of Brunei's successful forest protection policy and is an important ecotourism centre. It is part of the Heart of Borneo international conservation agreement.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains unspoiled jungle and is known for its tropical lowland rain forests, diverse flora and fauna, and important ecotourism activities. It is under the control of the Forestry Department of the Ministry of Primary Resources and Tourism. The Kuala Belalong Field Studies Centre, established by Universiti Brunei Darussalam in 1990, serves as a key research, teaching, and training site for the international research community.

world knowledge.Name: Wuzhizhou Island
world knowledge.Address: Off the coast of Hainan Province, China, approximately 30 kilometres northeast of Sanya
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Taoist priest Wu Huacun of the Qing dynasty built a house on the island after arriving in search of a place to create the 'elixir of life'. The island is also known as 'Lover's Island' due to its irregular butterfly or heart shape.

Major_Events.Description: A construction project began to create a marine ecology area, including a 'sea ranch' with artificial reefs over an area of approximately 66.6 hectares, funded by a private investment of about US$3 million.

Major_Events.Event: National Marine Ranch Demonstration Zone establishment
Major_Events.Description: As of September 2020, a National Marine Ranch Demonstration Zone was established, with 6 of the planned marine ranches under construction, aligned with the overall plan for the construction of Hainan Free Trade Port.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The island is known for its natural beauty, diverse plant and marine life, and its historical association with Taoist culture. It is also a popular tourist destination and a site for marine ecology conservation.

Details.Plant_Varieties: Over 2,700 plant varieties, including exotic flowers and trees such as Alsophila spinulosa and Dracaena draco.
Details.Marine_Life: Numerous species such as sea cucumbers, urchins, and tropical fish.
Details.Shape: Irregular butterfly shape or heart shape, hence called 'Lover's Island'.

world knowledge.Name: Morey's Piers
world knowledge.Address: 3501 Boardwalk, Wildwood & North Wildwood, New Jersey, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Morey's Piers & Beachfront Waterparks is a seaside amusement park located on The Wildwoods' boardwalk in Wildwood and North Wildwood, New Jersey. The park has been family owned and operated since 1969 and was run by second generation Morey Brothers, Will and Jack. Morey's Piers has more than 100 rides and attractions across its three amusement piers and two beachfront waterparks.

Major_Events.Description: 11-year-old Abiah Jones died after falling between 100 and 150 feet from the Giant Wheel. Investigators were unable to determine how the girl, who was riding alone, got out of the gondola. A report by the state Department of Community Affairs found the ride's restraints to be working properly and suggested that to get out of the car, a passenger probably would have had to stand. The report recommended that children be forbidden from riding the Ferris wheel alone.

The Sea Serpent roller coaster suffered its first ever accident, injuring 14 of the 23 riders on board, some of whom were stranded upside down. According to Will Morey, chief executive officer of the Morey Organization, the accident was thought to have been due to a wheel coming off a rear axle, causing the coaster train to jerk to a stop midway through the ride, as it was looping backwards.

A bomb threat was delivered to Wildwood Police Department via 9-1-1 call targeting all three Morey's amusement piers. A mass evacuation was ordered and a major emergency response followed. A meticulous search was conducted and finished with no explosives or Weapons of Mass Destruction found.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Morey's Piers features three amusement piers and two beachfront waterparks with over 100 rides and attractions. The piers include Surfside Pier, Mariner's Pier, and Adventure Pier, each with unique rides and attractions. The waterparks include Ocean Oasis Water Park + Beach Club and Raging Waters Water Park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Morey's Piers is a family-owned and operated seaside amusement park that has been a staple of The Wildwoods' boardwalk since 1969. It is known as "America's Boardwalk" and offers a variety of rides, attractions, and waterparks that cater to families and thrill-seekers alike.
world knowledge.Details: Morey's Piers operates from April to October for rides and piers, and from May to September for waterparks. The park has undergone several expansions and rebrandings over the years, including the addition of new rides and attractions. Notable rides include The Great Nor'easter, Giant Wheel, The Great White, and various water slides and lazy rivers.

world knowledge.Name: Macombs Dam Bridge
world knowledge.Area: Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City
world knowledge.Address: Connects 155th Street and Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard in Manhattan with Jerome Avenue and 161st Street in the Bronx
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Macombs Dam Bridge is a swing bridge across the Harlem River in New York City, connecting Manhattan and the Bronx. The first bridge at the site was constructed in 1814 as a dam, which was later replaced by a wooden swing bridge in 1861. The current steel span was built between 1892 and 1895 and was designed by Alfred Pancoast Boller. It is the third-oldest major bridge still operating in New York City and was designated a New York City Landmark in 1992.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the current steel span
Major_Events.Description: The current steel span of the Macombs Dam Bridge was constructed between 1892 and 1895, replacing the earlier wooden swing bridge.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a New York City Landmark
Major_Events.Description: The Macombs Dam Bridge and the 155th Street Viaduct were designated as a New York City Landmark on January 14, 1992.
The New York City Department of Transportation conducted a $145 million overhaul of the bridge, replacing the deck and renovating structural elements.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Macombs Dam Bridge is a swing bridge with a camelback design. It features a swinging span over the Harlem River, which pivots around a small masonry island. The bridge's trusswork consists of concave chords running along the top, tapering up toward a square section in the center of the span, topped by four finials. The design includes Gothic Revival-style abutments and ornamental iron railings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Macombs Dam Bridge is culturally and historically significant as the third-oldest major bridge still operating in New York City. It is a key transportation link between Manhattan and the Bronx and has been designated a New York City Landmark. The bridge's design and engineering are also notable, with its swing span being the oldest remaining in New York City that retains its original span.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation bridge connecting Manhattan and the Bronx
world knowledge.Details: The Macombs Dam Bridge is composed of an over-water span and the 155th Street Viaduct, both designed by Alfred Pancoast Boller. It carries four vehicular lanes and two sidewalks, with a total width of 65 feet (20 m). The bridge's swinging span weighs 2,400 short tons and is turned by two concentric drums. The bridge is operated and maintained by the New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT).

world knowledge.Name: Kimbolton Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kimbolton Castle is a country house in Kimbolton, Cambridgeshire, England. Originally a medieval castle, it was converted into a stately palace and was the family seat of the Earls and Dukes of Manchester from 1615 until 1950. It was the final home of King Henry VIII's first wife, Catherine of Aragon, who was imprisoned there and died in 1536. The castle underwent several reconstructions, including works by notable architects such as Sir John Vanbrugh, Nicholas Hawksmoor, and Robert Adam. It now houses Kimbolton School.

Major_Events.Description: Catherine of Aragon was sent to Kimbolton Castle in April 1534 for refusing to give up her status or deny the validity of her marriage to King Henry VIII. The fenland climate damaged her health, and she died in the castle on 7 January 1536.
The castle was purchased by Sir Henry Montagu, later created 1st Earl of Manchester, in 1615. It remained the family seat of the Earls and Dukes of Manchester until 1950.

Major_Events.Event: Reconstruction by Charles Montagu, 1st Duke of Manchester
Major_Events.Description: Charles Montagu, 4th Earl of Manchester, who was created 1st Duke of Manchester in 1719, had many works of reconstruction carried out between 1690 and 1720, including the rebuilding of the south wing by Sir John Vanbrugh and Nicholas Hawksmoor.
Alexander Montagu, 10th Duke of Manchester, sold the castle and 50 acres to Kimbolton School in 1951.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle features Tudor fragments and Baroque architectural styles. It was originally a medieval castle but was converted into a Tudor manor house and later reconstructed in the Baroque style. Notable architects involved in its design and reconstruction include Henry Bell, Sir John Vanbrugh, Nicholas Hawksmoor, and Robert Adam.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kimbolton Castle is culturally and historically significant as the final home of Catherine of Aragon, the first wife of King Henry VIII. It also served as the family seat of the Earls and Dukes of Manchester for over three centuries and showcases architectural contributions from some of the most notable architects of their time.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently serves as a school (Kimbolton School); historically a country house and family seat.
world knowledge.Details: The castle grounds include Warren House, a Grade II* listed folly converted in the late 18th century and renovated by the Landmark Trust between 2011 and 2012. Many members of the Montagu family are buried at St Andrew's Church in Kimbolton, with several monuments and a family vault located there.

world knowledge.Name: Dunrobin Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dunrobin Castle is a stately home in Sutherland, in the Highland area of Scotland, and the family seat of the Earl of Sutherland, Chief of the Clan Sutherland. Its origins lie in the Middle Ages, but most of the present building and the gardens were added by Sir Charles Barry between 1835 and 1850. The castle has undergone several expansions and alterations, making it the largest house in the north of Scotland. It was used as a boarding school for seven years before being opened to the public.

Major_Events.Description: The Jacobites under Charles Edward Stuart stormed Dunrobin Castle without warning, as the Clan Sutherland supported the British government. The 17th Earl of Sutherland narrowly escaped.
During the First World War, the building was in use as a naval hospital when a fire damaged the roof and much of the interior, confined to the newer additions by Barry.
The house became a boarding school for boys, taking on forty boys and five teachers in its first year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Dunrobin Castle features a mix of Scottish Baronial and French Renaissance architectural styles. The castle includes a 14th-century tower, 17th-century and 18th-century extensions, and 19th-century additions by Sir Charles Barry. The exterior has elements inspired by the work of the French architect Viollet-le-Duc, such as the pyramidal roof over the main entrance. The interior includes a large quadrangular pile of four stories with towers at each corner, and a main stairway decorated with portraits of the Leveson-Gower family.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dunrobin Castle is culturally and historically significant as the family seat of the Earl of Sutherland and Chief of the Clan Sutherland. It represents centuries of Scottish history, including its role in the Jacobite Rising of 1745 and its transformation into a public heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The castle has 189 rooms, making it the largest in the northern Highlands. It includes a museum displaying trophy heads of animals, ethnographic items, and archaeological artefacts. The gardens, inspired by the French formal style of the Gardens of Versailles, feature parterres set around circular pools with fountains. The castle is open to visitors between April and October each year, with falconry displays held in the gardens.

world knowledge.Name: Mermaid Beach
world knowledge.Area: Coastal suburb of the City of Gold Coast
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mermaid Beach is named after the cutter HMS Mermaid, which explorer John Oxley sailed aboard in 1823 when he discovered the nearby Tweed and Brisbane rivers. During World War II, it was used by US servicemen and named Los Angeles Beach and Miami Beach. The area was developed in the 1920s with the auction of the Mermaid Beach Estate.

Major_Events.Description: Magic Mountain, Nobby Beach opened up in 1962.
The first McDonald's restaurant in Queensland opened in Mermaid Beach on 24 August 1975.

Major_Events.Event: Dedication of St James' Anglican Church
Major_Events.Description: St James' Anglican Church was dedicated on 11 November 1977 by Assistant Bishop Ralph Wicks.

Major_Events.Event: Closure of St James' Anglican Church
Major_Events.Description: The closure of St James' Anglican Church was approved by Assistant Bishop Ron Williams on 15 August 1993.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mermaid Beach is culturally significant as a historical coastal suburb named after the HMS Mermaid, which played a role in the exploration of Queensland. It also has a notable history during World War II and development in the 20th century.

Details.Bounding_Areas: Bounded by Mermaid Waters canals to the west, Pacific Ocean to the east, Broadbeach to the north, and Miami to the south.
Details.Transport: Gold Coast Highway passes through Mermaid Beach; Gold Coast Oceanway (a pedestrian path) travels along Hedges Avenue.
Details.Education: No schools in Mermaid Beach, but primary schools in Broadbeach and Mermaid Waters, and a secondary school in Mermaid Waters.
Details.Community_Groups: Mermaid Beach branch of the Queensland Country Women's Association meets at QCWA Hall at 43 Ventura Road.

world knowledge.Name: Rabindra Sarobar
world knowledge.Address: Flanked by Southern Avenue to the north, Shyamaprasad Mukherjee Road to the west, Dhakuria to the east and the Kolkata Suburban Railway tracks to the south
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Dhakuria Lake, it was developed by the Calcutta Improvement Trust in the early 1920s. The lake was excavated under the leadership of Cecil Henry Bompass, M.R. Atkins, and Prabodh Chandra Chatterjee. It was renamed Rabindra Sarovar in May 1958 as a tribute to Rabindranath Tagore.

Major_Events.Description: The lake was renamed in honor of Rabindranath Tagore, a Bengali writer and Nobel Laureate.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in National Lake Conservation Plan
Major_Events.Description: The Ministry of Environment and Forests included Rabindra Sarobar in the National Lake Conservation Plan to address environmental degradation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Artificial lake surrounded by gardens, parks, and recreational complexes. The area includes children's parks, gardens, and auditoria.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rabindra Sarobar is a significant recreational area in Kolkata, named after Rabindranath Tagore, and serves as a popular spot for locals and tourists alike. It is also an important site for biodiversity, hosting a variety of flora and fauna.
world knowledge.Details: The lake covers 73 acres, with the remaining 119 acres covered by shrubs and trees. It is home to 11,000 trees, including palash, African tulip, ashok, and shimul. The area supports a diverse range of birds, fungi, and dragonflies. Despite its popularity, the lake faces environmental challenges due to pollution and increased tourist activity.

world knowledge.Name: Palace of Laeken
world knowledge.Address: Avenue du Parc Royal / Koninklijk Parklaan, 1020 Laeken, City of Brussels, Brussels-Capital Region, Belgium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palace of Laeken, originally named the Palace of Schonenberg, was built between 1782 and 1784 for the Governors of the Habsburg Netherlands. It was partly destroyed by fire in 1890, after which it was rebuilt and extended. Significant modifications were undertaken at the beginning of the 20th century during the reign of King Leopold II. It has been the official residence of the King of the Belgians and the Belgian royal family since 1831.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was partly destroyed by fire and subsequently rebuilt and extended.
King Leopold I was received at the palace on the day of his coronation.
Napoleon stayed at the palace with the Empress Joséphine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical Neo-Palladian style, originally designed by Charles de Wailly and later modified by Alphonse Balat and Charles Girault. The palace features a 'U' shape with the main façade and includes the Royal Greenhouses of Laeken.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Palace of Laeken is the official residence of the King of the Belgians and has been a significant site for Belgian royalty since 1831. It also houses the Royal Greenhouses, which are a notable architectural and botanical landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential palace for the Belgian royal family
world knowledge.Details: The Royal Domain of Laeken includes extensive gardens, lakes, a golf course, and artworks. The gardens are landscaped in English style and contain various pavilions, including the Chinese Pavilion and the Japanese Tower. The Royal Greenhouses are open to the public for three weeks each year during the flowering period. The palace has a more sober and intimate character compared to the Royal Palace of Brussels.

world knowledge.Name: Kelham Island Museum
world knowledge.Address: Alma Street, alongside the River Don, Sheffield, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kelham Island Museum is an industrial museum located on a man-made island resulting from the construction of a mill race in the 12th century. The island was named after Kellam Homer, the Town Armourer, who owned a grinding workshop in 1637. The site has a rich industrial history, including John Crowley's Iron Foundry (1829-1890s), a power station (1899-1930s), and various workshops. The museum now occupies these premises and houses exhibitions on science and Sheffield industry.

Major_Events.Description: The museum suffered heavy damage with water over a metre deep, causing £1.5 million in damages. It was closed for 18 months and reopened in September 2008.
The site is now protected by new flood defences completed in December 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum includes former industrial buildings such as Russell Works, which now houses the Hawley Gallery and the Crucible Shop. The site features a mix of historical industrial architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its preservation of Sheffield's industrial heritage, including exhibits like the River Don Engine, the Bessemer converter, and the prototype Sheffield-Simplex car. It is an Anchor Point of the European Route of Industrial Heritage (ERIH).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Industrial museum showcasing Sheffield's industrial and scientific history.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses the workshop of Stan Shaw, a little mester, who demonstrated knife making until his death in 2021. It also contains the Benjamin Huntsman Clock, the first manufactured object to contain Crucible Cast Steel, and a large photographic archive used for local history books.

world knowledge.Name: Grafton Bridge (New South Wales)
world knowledge.Address: Bent Street, Grafton, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grafton Bridge is a heritage-listed bascule truss bridge that carries Bent Street and the North Coast railway line across the Clarence River in Grafton, New South Wales, Australia. It was conceived in 1915, with the design changed in 1922 to accommodate vehicular traffic. Construction began in 1927 and was completed in 1932. The bridge was built by the New South Wales Public Works Department with steelwork from Clyde Engineering. It was formally opened by Governor-General of Australia Sir Isaac Isaacs on 19 July 1932. The bridge's bascule span was operational from 1932 until 1969 but can no longer be raised due to an added water main. A parallel bridge, Balun Bindarray Bridge, opened in 2019 to handle high traffic volumes.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the Grafton Bridge began after planning started in 1921.
The bridge was formally opened by Governor-General of Australia Sir Isaac Isaacs on 19 July 1932.
The bascule span was sealed shut and can no longer be opened due to an added water main and decline in shipping along the Clarence River.
The bridge was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.
A parallel bridge, Balun Bindarray Bridge, opened to traffic on 12 December 2019 to handle high traffic volumes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Grafton Bridge is a double-deck bascule truss bridge made of steel with concrete piers. It is the only double-deck road/rail structure in New South Wales. The upper level supports a two-way road, and the lower level supports a rail bridge, a water main, and footbridges on either side. The bridge originally had a lift span to allow river traffic, which is no longer operational.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a rare example of a double-deck road/rail structure in New South Wales and is historically, scientifically, architecturally, and socially significant. It completed the North Coast standard gauge line between Sydney and Brisbane in 1932. The bridge and its remnant spans of the 1915 timber viaduct are important relics of the development of the north coast railway.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge serves as a transportation link for motor vehicles, railway lines, water supply, and pedestrians, connecting the Grafton central business district with South Grafton.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge's heritage listing includes three remnant spans of the 1915 timber viaduct south of Grafton railway station. A new parallel bridge, Balun Bindarray Bridge, was opened in 2019 to alleviate traffic. The original bridge remains in use alongside the new one.

world knowledge.Name: Yamagata Museum of Art
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yamagata Museum of Art opened in Yamagata, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan, in 1964. The Museum's annex opened in 1968. In 1985 the new three-story main building opened; the annex was renovated the following year.

Major_Events.Description: The Yamagata Museum of Art was initially opened.
The Museum's annex was opened.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the new main building
Major_Events.Description: The new three-story main building of the Museum was opened.
The annex was renovated following the opening of the new main building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum features a three-story main building, with an annex that was later renovated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses significant works of art, including pieces by Manet, Monet, Renoir, Cézanne, and Takahashi Yuichi, as well as Yosa Buson's six-panel byōbu of 1779, Oku no Hosomichi (Important Cultural Property). Many Impressionist works are from the collection of Yoshino Gypsum Co., Ltd, deposited at the Museum.
world knowledge.Details: The collection includes works by prominent artists and an Important Cultural Property. Many of the Impressionist works are from the collection of Yoshino Gypsum Co., Ltd, deposited at the Museum.

world knowledge.Name: Incheon Grand Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Incheon Grand Park is a park complex established in 1992, located in Namdong District, Incheon, South Korea. It is the biggest neighborhood park in Incheon.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a rose garden, arboretum, sculpture garden, sledding area, futsal court, camping site, soccer field, basketball court, archery range, dog park, inline skating rink, and children's playground. There are various walking trails, including one designed for barefoot walking.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the largest neighborhood park in Incheon, it serves as a significant recreational and cultural hub for the community, attracting 4 million visitors each year.
world knowledge.Details: The park is open all year and offers parking facilities. It is a popular destination for various outdoor activities and leisure.

world knowledge.Name: Mae Wong National Park
world knowledge.Area: Nakhon Sawan Province and Kamphaeng Phet Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mae Wong National Park was declared a national park on 14 September 1987 as the 54th national park of Thailand. It is located in the Dawna Range and is known for its rugged and hilly terrain, with the highest peak being Khao Mo Ko Chu at 1,964 m above sea level. The park was formerly home to hill tribes including Hmong, Yao, Muzer (Lahu), and Karen.

Major_Events.Event: Approval of Mae Wong Dam project
Major_Events.Description: Thailand's cabinet approved the 13 billion baht Mae Wong Dam project to address water shortages in the dry season and heavy floods in the wet season. Opponents argued it would eliminate around 1,760 hectares of low-lying forest and reduce animal habitats.
Environmental campaigner Sasin Chalermlap walked 388 kilometers to protest the dam. The Thai government later announced they would study a new alternative to the dam.

Major_Events.Event: Revival of Mae Wong Dam plans
Major_Events.Description: Plans to build the dam were revived by Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Chatchai Sarikulya, who sought an order under Section 44 of the interim charter to proceed with the project.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mae Wong National Park is culturally significant as it was once home to various hill tribes and is now a protected area that preserves Thailand's natural heritage and biodiversity.
world knowledge.Details: Mae Wong National Park is known for its notable places such as Mae Krasa, Mae Rewa, Mae Ki Waterfalls, Mokochu Peak, and Chong Yen. It is governed by the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation.

world knowledge.Name: Beihai Park
world knowledge.Address: Immediately northwest of the Forbidden City, Beijing, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beihai Park is a public park and former imperial garden first built in the 12th century. It was part of the Imperial City and opened to the public in 1925. The park was designed to imitate renowned scenic spots and architecture from various regions of China, particularly Jiangnan around the Yangtze Delta. It has undergone several redesigns and expansions under different dynasties, including the Jin, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties.

Major_Events.Description: Emperor Zhangzong of the Jurchen Jin dynasty had a country resort built northeast of Zhongdu, which included Taiye Lake and the Palace of Great Peace on Jade Flower Island.
Jade Flower Island was redesigned by various architects and officials, and Taiye Lake was enclosed within the walls of the Imperial City of the Yuan Empire's new capital Khanbaliq.
Taiye Lake was divided into three lakes described as the 'Northern', 'Central', and 'Southern Seas', forming part of the Western Garden within the Imperial City.
The Qianlong Emperor ordered rare calligraphy works to be carved into stone and displayed at the Pavilion of Reviewing the Past beside Beihai.

Major_Events.Event: Damage and repair of the White Dagoba
Major_Events.Description: The White Dagoba was destroyed by the 1679 Sanhe-Pinggu earthquake and rebuilt the following year. It was also damaged by the 1976 Tangshan earthquake and repaired the same year.

Major_Events.Event: Damage to the Hall of Received Light
Major_Events.Description: The Eight-Nation Alliance damaged the Buddha statue in the Hall of Received Light during the 1900 Battle of Beijing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beihai Park features a blend of architectural styles from various regions of China, including elaborate pavilions, canals, delicate gardens, and natural scenery. Key structures include the White Dagoba (a Tibetan-style stupa), the Five Dragon Pavilions, the Nine-Dragon Wall, and the Hall of Received Light. The park also includes Taihu rocks, Yuan jade jars, and centuries-old stelas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Beihai Park is one of the masterpieces of Chinese gardening and landscaping, designed to imitate renowned scenic spots and architecture from various regions of China. It reflects the cultural and historical influences of multiple dynasties and serves as a public park with significant historical and architectural value.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and former imperial garden
world knowledge.Details: Beihai Park contains numerous historically important structures, palaces, and temples, including the Temple of Everlasting Peace and the Chanfu Temple. The park's lake is connected to the Shichahai at its northern end. The name 'Beihai' means 'Northern Sea' and corresponds to the 'Central Sea' and 'Southern Sea' to the south, which are part of the restricted Zhongnanhai area. The park's design influenced other gardens, such as the Five-Pavilion Bridge and Lotus Tower in Yangzhou.

world knowledge.Name: Umzumbe
world knowledge.Location: Mouth of the Mzumbe River, approximately 5 km south-west of Hibberdene
world knowledge.Address: R102 between Hibberdene to the north and Melville to the south, approximately 16 km north of Port Shepstone and 98 km south-west of Durban
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The name of the river is derived from a band of Hlongwa cannibals who occupied the valley. The Hlongwa was almost wiped out by the Zulu king Shaka in 1828. The name 'Umzumbe' has been explained as meaning 'the dangerous river', 'the winding river', and 'wild bean river'.

Major_Events.Event: Defeat of the Hlongwa by Shaka
Major_Events.Description: The Hlongwa, a band of cannibals who occupied the valley, were almost wiped out by the Zulu king Shaka.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Umzumbe is a seaside resort with historical significance due to its association with the Hlongwa cannibals and the Zulu king Shaka. It is also a popular recreational area with a Blue Flag accredited beach.

Recreational_Features.Beaches: Umzumbe Beach is accredited as a Blue Flag Beach. Larger beaches in the vicinity include those in Hibberdene, Ramsgate, St Michael's-on-Sea, Uvongo, and Margate.
Recreational_Features.Spearfishing: Popular at Umzumbe point, a prime area for garrick and brusher.

world knowledge.Name: Anthi Karagianni Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anthi Karagianni Municipal Stadium, formerly the Kavala National Stadium, was built in 1970. It was renamed after the paralympic athlete Anthi Karagianni, who won three silver medals in the 2004 Paralympic Games.

Major_Events.Description: Anthi Karagianni, after whom the stadium is named, won three silver medals in these games.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass surface and a seating capacity of 10,550.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it is named after a notable paralympic athlete and serves as a key sports venue in Kavala.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches as the homebase of Kavala F.C.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by the Municipality of Kavala and operated by Kavala F.C. It does not have a scoreboard.

world knowledge.Name: Manouba University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Manouba University is a public university in Manouba, Tunisia. The National School of Computer Sciences (ENSI), an engineering school founded in 1984, is part of the university.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Manouba University is a significant institution of higher education in Tunisia, contributing to the country's educational and technological development.
world knowledge.Details: The National School of Computer Sciences (ENSI) is an engineering school founded in 1984 and is part of Manouba University.

world knowledge.Name: Príncipe Airport
world knowledge.Area: Príncipe Island, São Tomé and Príncipe
world knowledge.Address: 3 kilometres north of Santo António, Príncipe Island
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1968 during Portuguese colonial rule, Príncipe Airport is the only airport on Príncipe Island and one of three airports serving São Tomé and Príncipe. In 2012, the airport underwent modernization, including runway lengthening, completed in October 2015, funded by an $18 million investment from a South African firm.

Major_Events.Description: The Portuguese construction firm Mota-Engil was hired to modernize the airport, focusing on lengthening the runway to accommodate mid-size jets. The project was completed in October 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has 1 runway designated 18/36 with an asphalt surface. The runway was originally 1,320 by 30 metres but was lengthened to 1,750 metres during the 2012 renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Príncipe Airport is a vital transportation hub for Príncipe Island, facilitating both commercial and private air travel. Its modernization has supported the island's eco-tourism industry, including the construction of a five-star eco-tourism hotel.
world knowledge.Details: Príncipe Airport (IATA: PCP, ICAO: FPPR) is located at an elevation of 591 feet (180 m) above mean sea level. It is not certified for Instrument Flight Rules and has customs facilities, though these are only used for charter and private flights as there are no commercial international flights into Príncipe.

world knowledge.Name: N'Djamena Grand Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The N'Djamena Grand Mosque (French: Grande Mosquée de N'Djamena) is a mosque in N'Djamena, Chad. It was established in 1978.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is a significant Islamic place of worship in Chad, reflecting the country's Islamic heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque complex consists of libraries, lecture halls, and schools.

world knowledge.Name: Dali University
world knowledge.Address: Dali, Yunnan, People's Republic of China
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1978 (Dali Medical College & Dali Teachers College), 2001 (Dali University)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dali University traces its origins to Dali Medical College and Dali Teachers College, established in 1978. The two institutions merged in 2001 to form Dali University. It is located in the historical and cultural city of Dali, which was the capital of Nanzhao Country over 1,000 years ago.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Dali Medical College & Dali Teachers College
Major_Events.Description: The predecessors of Dali University were established.
Dali Medical College and Dali Teachers College merged to form Dali University.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Australia Consulate General in Chengdu
Major_Events.Description: The consul general and vice consul general of Australia consulate general in Chengdu visited Dali University.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Thailand's Ministry of Education
Major_Events.Description: A delegation from Thailand's ministry of education visited Dali University.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Republic of Suriname Ambassador
Major_Events.Description: The ambassador of the Republic of Suriname visited Dali University.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's buildings are a blend of ancient and contemporary art. The campus includes large academic buildings, dormitory buildings, libraries, parks, athletics facilities, department stores, dining halls, and administrative offices.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dali University is an international university with a high reputation in Southeast Asia and South Asia. It holds significant ethnic medicine literature and historical references of local culture over 1,000 years old. It is also known as 'University in the landscape, the landscape of the University' due to its scenic location.
Notable_Visitors: Mr. K Lakshminarayanan - MLA, Former Minister
Dr. Bikash Kali Das - Chinese Consultant
Consul General and Vice Consul General of Australia Consulate General in Chengdu
Delegation from Thailand's Ministry of Education
Vice President of Faculty of Education of Deakin University in Australia
Ambassador of Thailand's Foreign Office and Diplomatic Academy
Delegation of Burma’s Association of Culture and Education
South and South-east Asia Press Corps
Women's Basketball Team of St. Mary’s College of Maryland
Consul General of Pakistan Consulate General in Chengdu
Economic Counselor of Consulate General of Pakistan in Chengdu
world knowledge.Details: Dali University has two campuses: Ancient City campus and Water Lily Campus. It covers ten academic disciplines and has 49 undergraduate degree programs, 28 master's degree programs, and over 17,000 full-time students. The university library holds about 2.15 million volumes. It is ranked among the top universities in Yunnan Province and has established exchange programs with over 40 foreign universities.

world knowledge.Name: Pattaya
world knowledge.Location: Bang Lamung District, Chonburi Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pattaya evolved from a fishing village to a major tourist destination, especially after the Vietnam War when American servicemen began arriving for R&R. The city's name originates from the march of Phraya Tak and his army, who encountered local troops led by Nai Klom. The place where they met was called 'Thap Phraya', later changed to 'Phatthaya'.

Major_Events.Description: Pattaya was granted city status by the Thai government.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the Sanctuary of Truth
Major_Events.Description: Businessman Lek Viriyaphan began constructing the Sanctuary of Truth, which remains unfinished and is entirely made out of wood.
Nirun Wattanasartsaton became the first democratically elected mayor of Pattaya.
Torrential rain caused severe flooding, described as the worst in a decade, with water reaching up to two meters deep in some areas.
Pattaya was awarded the Integrity and Transparency Assessment award for the highest development category by the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Pattaya features a mix of modern and traditional Thai architecture, with notable structures like the unfinished Sanctuary of Truth, which is entirely made of wood.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pattaya is culturally significant as a major tourist destination in Thailand, known for its beaches, nightlife, and historical transformation from a fishing village to a bustling city. It also plays a key role in Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC).
world knowledge.Details: Pattaya is part of the Pattaya-Chonburi Metropolitan Area, the third-largest metropolitan area in Thailand. The city has a tropical wet and dry climate and is known for its beaches, nightlife, and tourism industry. It has also faced challenges such as flooding, pollution, and efforts to clean up its image from being associated with the sex industry.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio de la Cerámica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio de la Cerámica, originally named Campo del Villarreal, was inaugurated on 17 June 1923. It was renamed El Madrigal in 1925 and later to Estadio de la Cerámica in 2017 to honor the local ceramics industry. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including expansions in 1952, 1989, 1998-2001, and 2005 to meet UEFA Champions League requirements. It is the home venue of Villarreal CF and has hosted significant matches, including a Europa League match for Molde FK in 2021 due to COVID-19 restrictions.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated with a match between Castellón and Cervantes.
The stadium was first floodlit for night matches on 16 September 1973 for a third division match between Villarreal and Ibiza.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Estadio de la Cerámica
Major_Events.Description: Villarreal changed the name of its stadium from El Madrigal to Estadio de la Cerámica to recognize the local ceramics industry.

Major_Events.Event: Europa League match for Molde FK
Major_Events.Description: Norwegian club Molde FK played their Europa League last 32 home match at the ground due to COVID-19 travel restrictions in their own country.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a hybrid grass surface, 23,008 seats, and 30 VIP boxes with air conditioning, TV, and catering services. The facade is covered with yellow tiles to improve aesthetics and support the local tile industry. The stadium has undergone multiple renovations, including expansions of the pitch, stands, and facilities such as dressing rooms, VIP areas, and restaurants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Villarreal CF and a symbol of the local community. Its name change to Estadio de la Cerámica highlights the importance of the ceramics industry in the region. The stadium has also hosted international matches, contributing to its prestige.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 23,008 seats, making it the 26th-largest stadium in Spain and the 5th-largest in the Valencian Community. It is nicknamed the 'Feudo Amarillo' (Yellow Fief) and is located ten kilometres from the Mediterranean Sea at an altitude of 50 metres. The stadium has been renovated multiple times to meet modern standards, including UEFA Champions League requirements.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Logan
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Largest base circumference of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Logan is the highest mountain in Canada and the second-highest peak in North America after Denali. Named after Sir William Edmond Logan, a Canadian geologist and founder of the Geological Survey of Canada. It is located within Kluane National Park Reserve in southwestern Yukon. Due to active tectonic uplifting, Mount Logan is still rising in height. The first ascent was made in 1925 by an international team of climbers.

Major_Events.Description: An international team of climbers led by Albert H. MacCarthy reached the summit of Mount Logan for the first time.
A Geological Survey of Canada expedition fixed the current height of Mount Logan at 5,959 m using GPS.
Following the death of former Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau, there was a proposal to rename Mount Logan to Mount Trudeau, which was later dropped due to opposition.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mount Logan is a massive mountain with a massif that includes eleven peaks over 5,000 m. It is characterized by its significant ice cap and extreme cold temperatures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Logan is culturally significant as the highest peak in Canada and a symbol of Canadian natural heritage. It has also inspired cultural references, such as the name of the superhero Wolverine from X-Men.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Logan is not readily visible from the surrounding lowlands or the coast due to its position in the Saint Elias Mountains. It is the source of the Hubbard and Logan glaciers. Temperatures on the mountain are extremely low, with minimal snow melt leading to a significant ice cap. The mountain is still rising due to tectonic activity.

world knowledge.Name: Luostarinmäki
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Luostarinmäki Handicrafts Museum is an open-air museum in Turku, Finland. The area of Cloister Hill was developed relatively late for pre-fire Åbo, from around 1775, after another fire. The museum consists of 18 blocks of original 18th-century – early 19th-century buildings on their original location. The area was the only old residential area left in 1940, when the museum was opened, and it was the largest area to completely survive the Great Fire of Turku.

Major_Events.Description: The largest area of Cloister Hill completely survived the Great Fire of Turku.
The museum was opened as the only old residential area left in Turku.
The museum received the Golden Apple international tourism award as the only site in Scandinavia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of 18 blocks of original 18th-century – early 19th-century buildings on their original location. The buildings were refitted to the style of the Great Fire period, often involving removing ceilings of tongue and groove boards or restoring open fireplaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Luostarinmäki is culturally significant as it preserves the original 18th-century – early 19th-century residential buildings and provides insight into the life and occupations of the first inhabitants of Cloister Hill.
world knowledge.Details: The idea for the museum was put forward in a local newspaper article as early as 1908, but it was rejected for nearly 30 years. Nine blocks formed the original museum, with others being added in 1956. Expansion has continued since, with more buildings having their interiors refitted for display. Some residents remained living in the museum area even after it opened, the last resident, Hilma Mäenpää, remained there until her death in 1982.

world knowledge.Name: One World Trade Center
world knowledge.Address: 285 Fulton Street, Manhattan, New York City, New York
world knowledge.Historical_Background: One World Trade Center is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan, New York City. It was constructed following the destruction of the original World Trade Center in the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. The building is designed to be a symbol of resilience and rebirth.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of below-ground utility relocations, footings, and foundations began on April 27, 2006.
The tower's steel structure was topped out on August 30, 2012.
The final component of the skyscraper's spire was installed on May 10, 2013, bringing the building to its full height of 1,776 feet.
The building officially opened on November 3, 2014.
The One World Observatory opened on May 29, 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower features a contemporary modern architectural style with a symmetrical design that tapers on upper floors. It has a 185-foot tall windowless concrete base for security, and the upper floors form eight tall isosceles triangles. The building includes a 407.9-foot tall spire with a broadcasting antenna. The facade consists of angled glass fins protruding from stainless steel panels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One World Trade Center is a symbol of resilience and rebirth following the September 11, 2001 attacks. Its height of 1,776 feet is a deliberate reference to the year of the United States Declaration of Independence. The building is a prominent part of the New York City skyline and a major tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: One World Trade Center is the tallest building in the United States and the Western Hemisphere. It includes sustainable architecture features such as recycled materials, rainwater collection, and energy-efficient lighting. The building has an observation deck on floors 100-102, offering the highest vantage point in New York City. The tower is owned by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, with The Durst Organization managing the building.

world knowledge.Name: Istana Alam Shah
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Istana Alam Shah is the official palace of the Sultan of Selangor, located in southern Klang, the royal town of the state of Selangor, Malaysia. Between 1903 and 1957, there existed an older palace on the same site, known as Istana Mahkota Puri. It was built in 1903 during the rule of Sultan Sulaiman Shah, the fifth Sultan of Selangor, and the design closely resembles the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur. The Sultan lived in the palace for 35 years until his death in 1938. In the 1950s, it was briefly used as a student dorm for nearby schools. The palace was demolished in October 1957 and soon replaced by the present-day structure.

Major_Events.Description: The older palace, Istana Mahkota Puri, was demolished in October 1957 and replaced by the present-day Istana Alam Shah.
Extensive renovations were carried out by Sultan Salahuddin Shah in early 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace has 15 rooms and was built using wood and marble.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Despite the Sultan having two other official residences in Shah Alam and Putrajaya, most royal ceremonies (such as the coronation of a new Sultan) involving the Selangor royal family are held in Istana Alam Shah.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official palace of the Sultan of Selangor
world knowledge.Details: This article about a Malaysian building or structure is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it. This article about a palace is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Faux Namti Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Wantang Township, Pingbian County, Yunnan, China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Single-span of 55 m (180 ft), total length 67.2 m (220 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was constructed as part of the Kunming–Hekou Railway, the Chinese portion of the Kunming–Haiphong railway, during French colonial influence in the region. It was conceived to connect French Indochina to resource-rich Yunnan and facilitate trade.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began in March 1907 by the French Batignolles Construction Company.
The bridge was completed in December 1908 after overcoming significant engineering challenges.
The first train crossed the bridge on December 6, 1908.
The Hekou–Kunming leg of the railway, including the Faux Namti Bridge, opened on April 1, 1910.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge features a three-hinged metal arch with two triangular trusses arranged like an inverted V, resembling the Chinese character '人'. The trusses are joined at the center and riveted together, supported by ball joints anchored into notches in the cliff face. The bridge's design required novel construction methods due to the challenging terrain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a symbol of early 20th-century engineering ingenuity and Franco-Chinese colonial history. Its unique design and construction under difficult conditions make it a notable landmark in railway history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway bridge for the Kunming–Hekou Railway
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also known as Wujiazhai Railway Bridge or the Inverted V Bridge. It spans a gorge 102 m (335 ft) above the Sicha River. Construction was exceptionally difficult due to the remote location and height, leading to significant cost overruns.

world knowledge.Name: SeaWorld San Antonio
world knowledge.Area: Westover Hills District, San Antonio, Texas
world knowledge.Address: 10500 Sea World Drive, San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: SeaWorld San Antonio, initially named Sea World of Texas, was developed by Harcourt, Brace and Jovanovich and opened on May 27, 1988. It was built for $170 million and attracted 3.3 million visitors in its first year. The park has undergone several ownership changes, starting with Harcourt, Brace and Jovanovich, then Anheuser-Busch, Inc., followed by the Blackstone Group, and later China's Zhonghong Group. The park is now owned and operated by United Parks & Resorts. It is the largest marine-life theme park in North America and focuses on conservation, education, and animal rescue.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened on May 27, 1988, with 75,000 attendees. It was billed as the largest educational, marine-life theme park in the world.

Major_Events.Event: First orca born at the park
Major_Events.Description: Kayla (stage named 'Baby Shamu') was the first orca born at the park on November 26, 1988.
Harcourt, Brace and Jovanovich sold the park to Anheuser-Busch, Inc., due to financial difficulties.
Anheuser-Busch InBev sold the SeaWorld parks to the Blackstone Group.

Major_Events.Event: Announcement of last generation of orcas
Major_Events.Description: SeaWorld Entertainment announced that the current generation of orcas would be the last, and theatrical orca shows would be replaced with more naturalistic Orca Encounters.
SeaWorld San Antonio's Orca Encounter opened on February 22, 2020.
Catapult Falls, the world's first launched flume ride, opened to the public.

Major_Events.Event: Retheming of Sesame Street Bay of Play
Major_Events.Description: SeaWorld San Antonio rethemed their Sesame Street Bay of Play area to SeaWorld Rescue Jr., which opened on March 8, 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: SeaWorld San Antonio is a marine mammal park, oceanarium, and animal theme park featuring various exhibits and attractions, including Shamu Theater, Beluga Stadium, Discovery Point, and a penguin exhibit recreating the Falkland Islands. The park also includes Aquatica, a separate gated water park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SeaWorld San Antonio is significant for its focus on marine-life conservation, education, and animal rescue. It is accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) and is a member of the Alliance of Marine Mammal Parks and Aquariums (AMMPA). The park has one of the most prolific beluga breeding programs in the United States and has been selected as the permanent home for rescued marine animals.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Marine-life theme park, conservation, education, and animal rescue.
world knowledge.Details: SeaWorld San Antonio houses 5 orcas, 10 belugas, 16 bottlenose dolphins, and 7 Pacific white-sided dolphins. The park also features a large population of California sea lions, harbor seals, and otters. It has about 250 penguins of four species. The park operates year-round and includes 6 roller coasters and 3 water rides. The slogan is 'From Park to Planet' (See It Here, Save It There).

world knowledge.Name: Gimhae International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gimhae International Airport opened on August 1, 1976, replacing the old airport. It was named after the nearby city of Gimhae. A new domestic terminal was completed in May 1983, and a new international terminal opened on October 31, 2007. The airport has since become a hub for Air Busan and a focus city for Jeju Air, Jin Air, and Korean Air.

Major_Events.Description: Gimhae International Airport opened, shifting commercial air traffic from the old airport.
A new domestic terminal was completed.
A new international terminal was opened by President Roh Moo-hyun.
Lufthansa inaugurated service to Munich via Seoul, marking the first route between Busan and Europe.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two concrete runways: 18L/36R (2,743 m) and 18R/36L (3,200 m).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the primary airport serving the Busan–Gyeongnam area, it plays a crucial role in regional and international connectivity. Its shared use with military facilities also highlights its strategic importance.
world knowledge.Details: Gimhae International Airport is now beyond its design capacity, and a new airport is being built on Gadeokdo to meet growing demand. Photography and video of the apron, runway, and military stations are prohibited due to shared military use.

world knowledge.Name: Hoober Stand
world knowledge.Address: Lea Brook Lane, Wentworth, Rotherham, South Yorkshire
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hoober Stand was commissioned by Thomas Watson-Wentworth, Earl of Malton (later the 1st Marquess of Rockingham), to commemorate the quashing of the 1745 Jacobite rebellion. It was designed by architect Henry Flitcroft and constructed between 1746 and 1748 at a cost of £3,000.

Major_Events.Description: Built to commemorate the suppression of the 1745 Jacobite rebellion and to honor King George II.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is 30 metres tall, built in ashlar sandstone, and shaped as an equilateral triangle with rounded corners. It features a hexagonal cupola and a triangular viewing platform. The interior includes a helical stairway of 150 steps, lit by five stairway windows and two cupola windows. The three walls taper inward, creating an optical illusion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hoober Stand symbolizes the victory over the Jacobite rebellion and represents the unity of England, Scotland, and Ireland under one crown. It is a Grade II* listed building and one of several follies in the Wentworth Woodhouse park.
world knowledge.Details: Hoober Stand is situated on a ridge 157 metres above sea level, offering long-distance views on clear days. It is located near Wentworth Woodhouse and other follies like Needle's Eye and Keppel's Column. The inscription above the doorway dedicates the structure to King George II.

world knowledge.Name: Dar Batha
world knowledge.Address: Near Bab Bou Jeloud, Fes el-Bali, Fes, Morocco
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dar Batha, also known as Qasr al-Batḥa, is a former royal palace in Fez, Morocco, commissioned by Sultan Hassan I in the late 19th century and completed under Sultan Abdelaziz. It was converted into a museum of historical arts and crafts in 1915, now housing over 6,500 objects. The palace was part of a larger complex including Dar el-Beida and served as a summer residence and guest house.

Major_Events.Description: Dar Batha was converted into a museum of local arts, later becoming a national ethnographical museum and cultural center.
The palace underwent significant renovation.
Dar Batha was classified as a national monument.
A campaign to renovate Morocco's museums began, including Dar Batha.
Renovation works on the Batha Museum began with a projected cost of 15.6 million Moroccan dirhams, aiming to reopen as a Museum of Islamic Arts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features Alaouite, Moroccan, and Moorish architectural styles. It includes a vast rectangular courtyard surrounded by galleries and two main wings. The courtyard is decorated with colorful zellij mosaic tilework and ornamental fountains. The garden is a typical riad layout with an Andalusian style, divided into four parts with a central fountain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dar Batha is culturally significant as a former royal palace and now a museum preserving Moroccan heritage. It houses a vast collection of historical artifacts, including architectural fragments, Qur'ans, astrolabes, musical instruments, carpets, jewelry, and local ceramics.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses over 6,500 archaeological and historical art artifacts, including pieces from the Idrisid era, the 9th-century minbar of the Andalusian Mosque, and the 14th-century minbar of the Bou Inania Madrasa. The garden, arranged by landscape architect Jean-Claude Nicolas Forestier, features palm trees, jacarandas, and hibiscus, and hosts concerts and religious festivals.

world knowledge.Name: Sheffield City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sheffield City Hall is a Grade II* listed building in Sheffield, England. It was designed in 1920 by E. Vincent Harris but construction was delayed for 8 years due to the economic climate. Construction began on 27 June 1929 and was completed on 22 September 1932. It was originally proposed in 1916 as a Memorial Hall to commemorate the dead of the Great War but was renamed Sheffield City Hall by the time of completion. During the Second World War, a bomb exploded in Barkers Pool, damaging the building's pillars. In 2005, the City Hall was refurbished and re-developed at a cost of £12.5 million.

Major_Events.Description: A bomb exploded in Barkers Pool, damaging the building's pillars.
The City Hall and its surroundings were refurbished and re-developed at a cost of £12.5 million.
Oswald Mosley and the British Union of Fascists held a rally in the Hall.

Major_Events.Event: Winston Churchill Freedom of the City
Major_Events.Description: Winston Churchill was awarded the Freedom of the City in the Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-classical style with a giant portico. The Oval Hall seats 2,271 people. The Grand Willis III Organ is the largest in Sheffield with over 4,037 pipes, 75 stops, and four manuals. The Memorial Hall seats 425 people and the Ballroom seats 400 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sheffield City Hall is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Sheffield, serving as a venue for concerts and other events. It has hosted numerous notable performers and events, contributing to the city's cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Venue for concerts and other events
world knowledge.Details: The building is currently managed by the Sheffield City Trust under a 99-year lease and is operated by Sheffield International Venues. Due to financial pressures, it is due to be taken over by ASM Global in January 2025. A pair of four-foot high stone Art Deco lions, designed by John Hodge, were returned to the foyer of the City Hall in October 2017 as part of the building's 85th anniversary celebrations.

world knowledge.Name: Parque del Café
world knowledge.Address: 4 km south-west of Montenegro, 11 km west of Armenia, Quindío, Colombia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parque del Café was founded by the National Federation of Coffee Growers of Colombia and the Departmental Committee of Coffee Growers of Quindío, opening on 24 February 1995. The idea originated from Diego Arango Mora and his wife Margarita, who were inspired by the Sugar Museum in Valle del Cauca Department. Despite initial financial and political challenges, the park was successfully established and has grown into one of Colombia's top tourist attractions.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened on 24 February 1995, drawing 250,000 visitors in its first year.
The park received its five millionth visitor in 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park consists of two main areas: a museum and exhibition area detailing the history and culture of coffee production, and an amusement park with various rides and shows. The areas are connected by gondola lifts, a chairlift, and an ecological trail through a coffee plantation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parque del Café is culturally significant as it celebrates Colombia's coffee heritage, showcasing the history, culture, and process of coffee production. It has become a major tourist attraction, drawing over one million visitors annually.
world knowledge.Details: The park features 27 rides as of 2018, including three roller coasters, water rides, and other attractions such as animatronics shows, a global coffee garden, and food stalls. It also offers traditional Colombian architecture and live folkloric music on a vintage-style train.

world knowledge.Name: Halifax Stanfield International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Halifax Stanfield International Airport opened on August 1, 1960, replacing RCAF Station Shearwater as Halifax's primary airport. It was built to serve the Halifax region and adjacent areas in the Maritime provinces. The airport was named in honour of Robert Stanfield, the 17th Premier of Nova Scotia. It has undergone several expansions and renovations over the years to accommodate growing passenger traffic.

Major_Events.Description: Following the September 11 attacks, Halifax Stanfield International Airport participated in Operation Yellow Ribbon, accepting 47 diverted flights carrying approximately 7,300 passengers, more than any other Canadian airport involved in the operation.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Halifax Robert L. Stanfield International Airport
Major_Events.Description: On February 9, 2007, Prime Minister Stephen Harper formally renamed the airport to honour Robert Stanfield, the former Premier of Nova Scotia and federal Leader of the Official Opposition.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modernist terminal building designed by Gilleland and Strutt, with subsequent expansions including air bridges, a new international arrivals area, and a central lobby renovation. The terminal now includes 32 gate positions, with 13 using airbridges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a key transportation hub for the Halifax region and the Maritime provinces. It is named after Robert Stanfield, a respected political figure in Nova Scotia. The airport played a significant role during Operation Yellow Ribbon in 2001, providing refuge for thousands of stranded passengers.
world knowledge.Details: Halifax Stanfield International Airport is the 8th busiest airport in Canada by passenger traffic. It serves as a focus city for Air Canada, Porter Airlines, and WestJet, and is an operating base for several regional carriers. The airport has undergone numerous expansions and renovations, including the construction of a new international arrivals area, a parking garage, and a hotel. It is also designated as an emergency landing site for the Space Shuttle.

world knowledge.Name: Dream Island (amusement park)
world knowledge.Area: Nagatinsky Zaton district, Southern Administrative Okrug
world knowledge.Address: Andropov Avenue, Nagatinskaya Poima, Moscow, Russia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 100 hectares (total development area), 300,000 square meters (main building)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dream Island is the largest indoor theme park in Europe, opened on 29 February 2020. The project was developed by the company Regions with a total investment of $1.5 billion. Construction began in March 2016, was halted in early 2017 for financial reasons, but was re-financed and restarted by late 2017.

Major_Events.Description: The amusement park officially opened to the public on 29 February 2020.
Construction was halted in early 2017 for financial reasons but was re-financed and restarted by late 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building is styled as a fairytale castle with towers and stained glass. The central tower stands 75 meters tall. The park features Europe's largest glass dome to allow operation during Moscow's winters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dream Island is a major entertainment and cultural attraction in Moscow, featuring themed zones based on popular global franchises like Hotel Transylvania, The Smurfs, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, and Hello Kitty. It also includes promenades resembling streets of world capitals such as Rome, Barcelona, and London.
world knowledge.Details: The park has nine themed zones, including licensed areas from Sony Pictures, IMPS, Paramount, and Sanrio. The cost of entrance for a family of four at the opening was 11,000 rubles (about US$142). The park operates year-round.

world knowledge.Name: Kawaiahaʻo Church
world knowledge.Address: 957 Punchbowl Street and 553 S. King Street, Honolulu, Hawaii
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kawaiahaʻo Church is a historic Congregational church located in Downtown Honolulu on the Hawaiian Island of Oʻahu. It was the central church of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi and chapel of the Hawaiian royal family. The church is part of the Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site, designated a U.S. National Historic Landmark in 1962. The name comes from the Hawaiian phrase 'ka wai a Haʻo' ('the water of Haʻo'), referring to a spring and freshwater pool of a High Chiefess named Haʻo. The church was constructed between 1836 and 1842 using coral rock quarried from an offshore reef.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as a National Historic Landmark
Major_Events.Description: Kawaiahaʻo Church was designated a U.S. National Historic Landmark on December 29, 1962.

Major_Events.Event: Added to the National Register of Historic Places
