Major_Events.Description: The church was included in the National Register of Historic Places on October 15, 1966.
Kamehameha III, Kamehameha IV, Kamehameha V, and Kalākaua took their oaths of office to their constitutions at Kawaiahaʻo Church.
King Lunalilo was buried in a crypt near the front courtyard of the church, as he preferred burial in a church cemetery to the Royal Mausoleum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical Mediterranean Revival style, constructed of 14,000 slabs of coral rock quarried from an offshore reef. Designed by Rev. Hiram Bingham in the New England style of the Hawaiian missionaries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kawaiahaʻo Church is culturally and historically significant as the former central church of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi and chapel of the Hawaiian royal family. It is known as 'Hawaiʻi's Westminster Abbey' and has been a site of royal worship, state burials, and baptisms of aliʻi. The church continues to use the Hawaiian language in parts of its services and is the oldest church on Oʻahu.
world knowledge.Details: The upper gallery of the sanctuary is adorned with 20 portraits of Hawaiian royalty (Aliʻi). The church is part of the United Church of Christ and continues to be an active place of worship. It is also part of the Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site.

world knowledge.Name: Northern Culture Museum
world knowledge.Address: 2-15-25 Sōmi, Kōnan-ku, Niigata, Niigata Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Northern Culture Museum is an open-air museum featuring the mansion of a wealthy farming family (gōnō), gardens, and houses from the Edo period. It is located in the central area of the former Sōmi Domain, a subsidiary of the Shibata Domain.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum includes a well-known mansion, gardens, and houses from the Edo period, showcasing traditional Japanese architecture and design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and showcases the cultural heritage of wealthy farming families (gōnō) and the Edo period, offering insights into the historical lifestyle and architecture of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has a branch in Chūō-ku, Niigata. It is accessible via transit buses operated by Niigata Kotsu (S94 and S95 lines) from Niigata Station Bandai Exit, with a bus stop named 'Kami-sōmi Hakubutsukan-mae'. There is also a YOKO-BUS stop named 'Hoppō Bunka Hakubutsukan' that runs from Shin'etsu Main Line Ogikawa Station.

world knowledge.Name: Chandos House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chandos House is a Grade I listed building designed by Robert Adam, the most prominent architect in Georgian Britain. It was built speculatively with funds from the Adam family and banker Sir George Colebrooke. The house was later home to Anna Eliza Brydges, Duchess of Chandos, and served as the Austrian embassy for 25 years before being purchased by newspaper magnate Gomer Berry. It is currently owned by Cosmetic Doctor at Work Limited.

Major_Events.Description: The house was built by William Adam and Company, designed by Robert Adam, on a plot between another Adam house and the garden wall of Foley House.

Major_Events.Event: Duchess of Chandos declared a lunatic
Major_Events.Description: Following the death of the 3rd Duke of Chandos, the duchess was declared a lunatic, confined to the house, and lost control of her estates.
The unexpired portion of the lease was sold by the duchess's executors and purchased by the Austrian embassy, becoming the residence of Prince Esterházy.

Major_Events.Event: Austrian embassy moved to Belgrave Square
Major_Events.Description: The Austrian embassy relocated to Belgrave Square in Belgravia, where it remains today.
Newspaper magnate Gomer Berry bought the house from the 9th Earl of Shaftesbury, using it as his London home until 1959.

Major_Events.Event: Sale to Royal Society of Medicine
Major_Events.Description: The house was sold to the Royal Society of Medicine before being acquired by Cosmetic Doctor at Work Limited.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Robert Adam in Georgian style, the façade is made of Craigleith stone, possibly as an advertisement for the quarry west of Edinburgh.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chandos House is significant as the first of a series of large townhouses in London designed by Robert Adam, a leading architect of Georgian Britain. It also served as the Austrian embassy, hosting lavish entertainment, and was later owned by notable figures such as Gomer Berry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private townhouse, later served as the Austrian embassy, a private residence, and now owned by a commercial entity.
world knowledge.Details: The house is a Grade I listed building, reflecting its architectural and historical importance. It was built on land part of the Duke of Portland's estate and features prominently in the history of Georgian London.

world knowledge.Name: Amager Strandpark
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Amager Strandpark (Amager Beach Park) is a seaside public park in Copenhagen, Denmark. It is located on the island of Amager and includes an artificial island and offers a total of 4.6 km (2.9 mi) of beaches. The park was founded in 1934 and in 2005 a 2 km-long (1.2 mi) artificial island was added. The island is separated from the original beach by a lagoon which is crossed by three bridges.

Major_Events.Description: A 2 km-long (1.2 mi) artificial island was added to the park, separated from the original beach by a lagoon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach has two sections. The northern section has a natural beach environment with winding paths, broad sandy beaches and low dunes. The southern section offers a so-called city beach with a broad promenade and areas for ball play or picnicking. There is also a small marina and parking facilities at the southern end. The lagoon has low-water areas for children as well as a 1,000 m (3,300 ft) swimming course.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a popular recreational area for runners, swimmers, and kayakers. It includes a space for outdoor fitness training, a diving spot, and a grassy area known as Femøren, which is used for open-air rock concerts in summer. It is also a popular spot for skateboarders.
world knowledge.Details: The park is served by three metro stations: Øresund station to the north, Femøren station to the south, and Amager Strand station roughly in the middle. All stations are on the M2 line of the Copenhagen Metro. It is also easily reached on bicycle in about 15 minutes from the city centre. The water quality is usually very good, with salinity highly dependent on the current. The park features a large kayak club at the southern end of the artificial island with a cafe, rentals, and a sporting goods store. There are also sauna facilities and other amenities available near the kayak club area.

world knowledge.Name: Marrakech Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museum of Marrakech is housed in the Dar Mnebhi Palace, constructed at the beginning of the 20th century by Mehdi al-Mnebhi, a qaid of the Mnabha tribe and the vizier of war under Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz. The palace was later seized by the family of Pasha Thami El Glaoui during French rule. After Morocco regained its independence in 1956, the palace was seized by the state and converted to a girls' school in 1965. After a period of neglect, it was renovated by the Omar Benjelloun Foundation and converted into a museum in 1997.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was constructed by Mehdi al-Mnebhi, a qaid of the Mnabha tribe and the vizier of war under Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz.

Major_Events.Event: Seizure by Pasha Thami El Glaoui
Major_Events.Description: The palace was seized by the family of Pasha Thami El Glaoui while Mehdi al-Mnebhi was serving as ambassador in London.
After Morocco regained its independence in 1956, the palace was seized by the state and converted to a girls' school.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and conversion to a museum
Major_Events.Description: The palace was renovated by the Omar Benjelloun Foundation and converted into a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is an example of late 19th-century and early 20th-century Moroccan architecture, featuring a large central courtyard originally an open riad garden, now fully paved and roofed over. The courtyard is centered around several fountains and surrounded by roofed galleries and wall fountains, decorated with colorful zellij tilework and painted and carved cedar wood. The palace also includes roof terraces with a menzeh (pavilion), kitchens, and a hammam (bathhouse) with domed and vaulted chambers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum showcases traditional art objects from different regions of Morocco and different parts of its population, including weapons, carpets, costumes, pottery from Fez, Berber jewellery, Jewish liturgical objects, and more. It also holds exhibits of contemporary art and hosts cultural events such as theatre and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes numismatics, ceramics, and Moorish art. It is housed in the Dar Mnebhi Palace, which was constructed by Mehdi al-Mnebhi and later seized by Pasha Thami El Glaoui. After a period of neglect, the palace was renovated and converted into a museum in 1997 by the Omar Benjelloun Foundation.

world knowledge.Name: Groningen Airport Eelde
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Groningen Airport Eelde, originally named 'Hakenkampsveld', was officially opened in 1931. It was renamed 'Luchthaven Eelde' in 1933. During World War II, the German military occupied the airport. Since 1958, it has served European destinations and was renamed 'Groningen Airport Eelde' in 1988. The airport has played a significant role in regional aviation and training, including being the home base of the KLM Flight Academy.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened by mayor Jan Gerard Legro on 23 May 1931, with an air show attended by 40,000 visitors.
During World War II, the German military occupied the airport, expanding it and using it for fighter aircraft.
The main runway was extended from 1,800 meters to 2,500 meters, allowing for larger aircraft and increased capacity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two asphalt paved runways, with runway 05/23 measuring 2,500 meters in length. The airport has undergone several expansions and modernizations, including the construction of a new air traffic control tower and passenger terminal.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Groningen Airport Eelde is a key regional airport in the northeastern Netherlands, serving as an important hub for aviation training and regional connectivity. It has played a significant role in the region's infrastructure and development.
world knowledge.Details: Groningen Airport Eelde is accessible by car, bicycle, and bus, with connections to major railway stations in Assen and Groningen. It is home to the KLM Flight Academy and serves as a base for several aviation clubs and enterprises.

world knowledge.Name: Johnstown Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Johnstown Castle is a Gothic Revival castle located in County Wexford, Ireland. The first castle built on the estate was a tower house built in the late 12th century by the Esmonde family, Normans who came to southeast Ireland from Lincolnshire in the 1170s after the Norman invasion of Ireland (1169). The castle was bought by the Grogan family in 1692. Cornelius Grogan was hanged for his part in the 1798 Rebellion. The estate was restored to his brother John Knox Grogan in 1810, who, with his son, Hamilton Knox Grogan-Morgan, created Johnstown Castle as it stands today. The castle was designed by Daniel Robertson in the Gothic Revival style. During the First World War, Royal Naval Air Service airships were based at Johnstown Castle. The castle was taken over by the Department of Agriculture in 1945 and used for research into soils. It opened to the public in 2019 following a period of renovation.

Major_Events.Description: Oliver Cromwell spent a night on the estate in 1649, prior to the October 1649 Sack of Wexford. His Roundhead army used the land around Johnstown Castle to prepare.
Owner Cornelius Grogan was hanged for his part in the 1798 Rebellion; he had been commissary-general for the United Irishmen.
On 1 May 1944, the contents of the castle were sold off at a public auction lasting five days.
On 17 October 1945, the Johnstown Castle Agricultural College Act was ratified and the castle and Estate were formally handed over to the State by the family in lieu of death duties.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: A Gothic Revival castle of 4 storeys. Interior goods include the "Apostles' Hall", with wood carvings of saints, as well as oil paintings, carved oak hall benches, mahogany billiard tables, dressing tables, upholstered sofas, fire grates and brass fenders. A servants' tunnel, 86 metres (282 ft) in length, runs from the meat house to the kitchens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Johnstown Castle is culturally and historically important due to its long history dating back to the late 12th century, its role in significant historical events, and its Gothic Revival architecture. It also serves as a symbol of the agricultural research and education in Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The former stable yard houses the Irish Agricultural Museum. The castle is managed by the Irish Heritage Trust under curator Matt Wheeler, and work on conserving and restoring the building continues.

world knowledge.Name: University College Cork
world knowledge.Historical_Background: University College Cork (UCC) was founded in 1845 as Queen's College, Cork, under the Irish Universities Act 1908. It became University College, Cork, and later, National University of Ireland, Cork. The university was established to advance learning in Ireland and has grown to become one of the leading research institutes in the country.

Major_Events.Description: Established as Queen's College, Cork, under the Irish Universities Act 1908.
Became University College, Cork, under the Irish Universities Act 1908.
Renamed as National University of Ireland, Cork, under the Universities Act 1997.
Several UCC buildings were damaged by flooding, leading to the postponement of academic activities for a week.
UCC became the first university to achieve the ISO 50001 standard in energy management.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tudor Gothic quadrangle and early campus buildings were designed and built by Sir Thomas Deane and Benjamin Woodward. The university has expanded over the years with the addition of various buildings and facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UCC is a significant educational institution in Ireland, known for its research contributions and academic excellence. It has a rich history and is associated with the patron saint of Cork, Saint Finbarr.
world knowledge.Details: University College Cork (UCC) is a constituent university of the National University of Ireland, located in Cork. It was founded in 1845 as one of three Queen's Colleges. UCC has a diverse student body and offers a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programs. The university is known for its research excellence and has been named Irish University of the Year multiple times by The Sunday Times.

world knowledge.Name: Dorchester House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dorchester House was a mansion in Park Lane, Westminster, London, with various forms over time. The last version as a private residence was built in 1853 by Robert Stayner Holford. It was demolished in 1929 to make way for the present Dorchester Hotel. The site was originally part of the Manor of Hyde, given to William the Conqueror by Geoffrey de Mandeville. Joseph Damer acquired it in the 18th century, and a large building was constructed in 1751. It was named Dorchester House in 1792 after Damer became the Earl of Dorchester. In the early 19th century, it was purchased by Francis Seymour-Conway, 3rd Marquess of Hertford, and renamed Hertford House. After Hertford's death, it was rebuilt by Captain Robert Stayner Holford.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the last private residence
Major_Events.Description: Robert Stayner Holford built the last version of Dorchester House as a private residence.
Whitelaw Reid, the American Ambassador, held lavish Fourth of July celebrations at Dorchester House.
Whitelaw Reid hosted a dinner for Mark Twain, inviting about forty authors and artists, including Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.
The reception for the wedding of Whitelaw Reid's daughter Jean was held at Dorchester House, attended by King Edward and Queen Alexandra.
Former President Theodore Roosevelt stayed at Dorchester House for three weeks to attend the funeral of King Edward VII.

Major_Events.Event: World War I Auxiliary Home Hospital
Major_Events.Description: Dorchester House was used as an Auxiliary Home Hospital during World War I.
Dorchester House was demolished to make way for the new Dorchester Hotel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house was designed by Lewis Vulliamy, with a central staircase as a major feature. The staircase was praised for its grandeur. The dining room featured a chimneypiece sculpted by Alfred Stevens, regarded as one of his finest works. The library was specially designed to house Holford's large book collection. The Grand Saloon, green and red drawing rooms were notable for their design and art collections.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dorchester House was one of the more palatial buildings in London at the turn of the twentieth century and was frequently mentioned in publications of the time. It housed extensive art and book collections and was a venue for significant social and political events, including hosting notable figures like Mark Twain and Theodore Roosevelt.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Private residence, later used as the American Embassy and as an Auxiliary Home Hospital during World War I.
world knowledge.Details: The chimneypiece sculpted by Alfred Stevens is now housed in the Victoria and Albert Museum. The house was demolished in 1929, and the Dorchester Hotel was opened in 1931 on the same site.

world knowledge.Name: Khaptad National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Khaptad National Park is a protected area in the Far-Western Region, Nepal that was established in 1984. Khaptad Baba moved to the area in the 1940s to meditate and worship. He spent about 50 years as a hermit and became a renowned spiritual saint.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The landscape consists of moorland, steep slopes, and streams. Vegetation types include chir pine-rhododendron forest, oak forest and Himalayan fir-hemlock-oak forest and alder forest in riverine areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Khaptad Baba Ashram lies inside Khaptad National park. Khaptad Baba lived in Triveni located inside the national park and was known as a philosopher, physician, scientist, and astrologer.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Protected area for wildlife and nature conservation
world knowledge.Details: 567 species of flora have been recorded in the protected area. Current checklists include 23 mammals, 287 birds, and 23 amphibians and reptiles. Mammal species symbolic of the park are leopard, Himalayan black bear, wild dog, and musk deer. Bird species symbolic of the park include the impeyan pheasant, peregrine falcon, and white-rumped vulture.

world knowledge.Name: Abbey of Sainte-Trinité, Caen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Abbey of Sainte-Trinité, also known as Abbaye aux Dames, was founded as a Benedictine nunnery in the late 11th century by William the Conqueror and his wife Matilda of Flanders. It was completed in 1130. Matilda was buried in the choir in 1083. The abbey was suppressed during the French Revolution and later repurposed as a hospital in 1823. The church was last restored between 1990 and 1993.

Major_Events.Description: William the Conqueror and Matilda of Flanders founded the abbey as a Benedictine nunnery.
Construction of the abbey was completed.
Matilda of Flanders was buried in the choir under a slab of black marble.
The original spires were destroyed and replaced by balustrades in the early 18th century.
The nuns were dispersed, and the abbey was suppressed.
The abbey was repurposed as a hospital by the town council.
The vault was demolished and rebuilt.
The church underwent its last restoration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The façade has two large towers with doors leading to the aisles. The central portal's tympanum depicts the Trinity and the Four Evangelists. The nave has a gallery (triforium) and groin vault, the first of its type in Normandy. The transept houses the main altar, with the northern transept in Romanesque style and the southern transept featuring Gothic columns. The choir ends with an apse decorated by columns and a gallery with fantastic figures. There is also a crypt in honour of Saint Nicholas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The abbey is culturally and historically significant as one of the two major abbeys founded by William the Conqueror and Matilda of Flanders in Caen. It represents Norman Romanesque architecture and has played a key role in the religious and social history of Normandy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a Benedictine nunnery, later repurposed as a hospital, and now home to the Regional Council of Normandy.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey is also known as Abbaye aux Dames. It was granted the manor of Horstead in Norfolk by William II of England, leading to the establishment of Horstead Priory. The canonesses regular operated the hospital until 1908 when it became a nursing home.

world knowledge.Name: Chandrabhaga beach
world knowledge.Address: Chandrabhaga Beach, Konark, Puri district, Odisha, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chandrabhaga Beach is historically significant as a place of natural cure for lepers and is associated with legends involving Samba (Krishna's son) and Chandrabhaga, a sage's daughter. It has been a site for religious activities and is considered a holy shrine.

Major_Events.Description: Chandrabhaga beach became India's first to receive the Blue Flag certification, recognizing it as an environment-friendly and clean beach with international standard amenities.

Major_Events.Year: Every year on the 7th day of the full-moon fortnight of Magha month
Major_Events.Description: People gather to take a holy dip in the river, offer prayers to the Sun God, and enjoy the sunrise, commemorating the sacrifice of Chandrabhaga.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chandrabhaga Beach is culturally significant as a holy shrine and a place of religious and meditative activities. It is associated with ancient narratives and continues to inspire poets, artists, and lovers. The beach is also known for its marine resources and fishing community.

Details.Natural_Features: Chandrabhaga coral reef, one of the prominent living coral reefs of India, is located offshore from the beach.
Details.Facilities: Equipped with amenities of international standards for tourists, including a lighthouse nearby.
Details.Religious_Importance: Believed to be a place where Samba worshiped the Sun God after curing leprosy. The site is also linked to the legend of Chandrabhaga's sacrifice.
Details.Economic_Activity: A large colony of fishermen from rural areas of Vishakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh resides near the dried river-mouth.

world knowledge.Name: Hirkan National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hirkan National Park was established on February 9, 2004, on the basis of the former 'Hirkan State Reserve'. It was enlarged on April 23, 2008, from 29,760 hectares to 40,358 hectares. The park protects the humid subtropical and humid temperate forests in the Lenkoran Lowland and the Talysh Mountains, sheltering many endemic plant and animal species. It is part of the Caspian Hyrcanian (Girkan) mixed forests ecoregion.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established on February 9, 2004, replacing the former 'Hirkan State Reserve'.
The park was enlarged on April 23, 2008, from 29,760 hectares to 40,358 hectares.
A Caucasian leopard was caught on camera in March 2007, confirming its presence in the park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is characterized by lush deciduous broadleaved lowland and montane forests, including subtropical and temperate rainforests. It features a variety of endemic plant species and old-growth forests.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hirkan National Park is culturally and historically important due to its preservation of unique ecosystems and endemic species. It is part of the Caspian Hyrcanian (Girkan) mixed forests ecoregion, which is significant for its biodiversity and ecological value. The park is also under consideration for inclusion in UNESCO's World Heritage Site list.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of biodiversity and natural ecosystems
world knowledge.Details: The park is 99% covered by forests and is strictly protected. It is one of the largest contiguous forests in Azerbaijan, with no settlements or pastures interrupting its expanse. The park has a humid subtropical climate in the lowlands, an oceanic climate in the middle elevations, and a humid continental climate on the mountain peaks. It is home to many endemic and relict plant species from the Tertiary period, as well as various animal species, including the Caucasian leopard. The park is part of a reforestation program in the Lankaran Lowland to restore its ecology to a forested state.

world knowledge.Name: South Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: South Park is an American adult-animated sitcom created by Trey Parker and Matt Stone, and developed by Brian Graden for Comedy Central. The series revolves around four boys—Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, and Kenny McCormick—and their exploits in and around the titular Colorado town. The series became infamous for its profanity and dark, surreal humor that satirizes a large range of subject matter. Parker and Stone developed South Park from two animated short films, both titled The Spirit of Christmas, released in 1992 and 1995. The second short became one of the first viral Internet videos, leading to the series' production.

Major_Events.Description: South Park debuted with 'Cartman Gets an Anal Probe' on August 13, 1997, and quickly became a ratings success for Comedy Central.
A theatrical film, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, was released in June 1999 to commercial and critical success, garnering an Academy Award nomination.
In August 2021, South Park was renewed through 2027, and a series of television specials was announced for Paramount+.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: South Park has received critical acclaim and is included in various publications' lists of the greatest television shows. It has received numerous accolades, including five Primetime Emmy Awards and a Peabody Award. The show is known for its stringent social commentary and fearless lampooning of all that is self-important and hypocritical in American life.
world knowledge.Details: South Park is broadcast internationally in several countries and territories, including India, New Zealand, and several countries throughout Europe and Latin America on channels that are subsidiaries of Comedy Central and Paramount Media Networks. The show's style of animation is inspired by the paper cut-out cartoons made by Terry Gilliam for Monty Python's Flying Circus. The series has been nominated for the Emmy Award for Outstanding Animated Program eighteen times and has won the award four times.

world knowledge.Name: Parc des Hauteurs
world knowledge.Address: Fourvière, 5th arrondissement of Lyon, Lyon, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parc des Hauteurs is an urban park on Fourvière hill in Lyon, France. It encompasses the public spaces between the basilique de Fourvière and Loyasse cemetery. Throughout the 20th century, urban planning documents mention various projects for Fourvière hill. In 1906, architect Sined suggested building a park on the hill to remedy the shortage of parks in Lyon. In 1924 Camille Chalumeau suggested building a circular boulevard to take advantage of the panoramic views from the sight. After a landslide in 1930, construction on the hill was banned. Afterwards, there were several proposals to build a park, including by architect Giroud. He proposed the creation of a vast urban park between place Saint-Jean and the basilique Notre-Dame de Fourvière. Between 1930 and 1950 the Théâtre antique de Fourvière and the Odéon Antique were uncovered, after which the city acquired the lands in the area. The archaeological park was created and several buildings were destroyed to improve access to the hill. The Renaissance association of Vieux-Lyon was created in 1958 and has served to protect the area since 1964.

Major_Events.Description: A landslide killed 39 people, leading to a ban on construction on the hill.
The park was officially created, incorporating various historical and natural elements.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes the esplanade of Fourvière, created by engineer Joannès Blanchon between 1880 and 1896, connecting various landmarks such as the Passerelle des Quatre-vents, Loyasse fort, Loyasse cemetery, Jardin de la Visitation, Parc archéologique, and Jardin du Rosaire. The footpath was planned by landscapers Desvigne and Dalnoky, designed by architect Manuelle Gautrand and engineer Marc Malinowski. The park also contains the Loyasse cemetery, built in 1807, and the Chapelle Sainte-Philomène, constructed by Antoine-Marie Chenavard in 1839.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parc des Hauteurs is culturally significant as it integrates historical, religious, and natural elements of Lyon. It includes the basilique de Fourvière, Loyasse cemetery, and various gardens, reflecting the city's rich history and architectural heritage. The park also serves as a green space in an urban area, offering panoramic views of Lyon.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains the Jardin du Rosaire, a hydrangea garden, an old rose garden, and an orchard. The Maison de la Bréda, the Chapelle Sainte-Philomène, and the garden have been classified as monuments historiques since 2004. The cloister and convent of the Visitation Sainte Marie de Fourvière, built from 1854 to 1857, have been transformed into a hotel.

world knowledge.Name: Yushan National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yushan National Park is one of the nine national parks in Taiwan, named after Yushan, the highest peak in the park. It was established on April 10, 1985, and covers a large section of the Central Mountain Range. The park is known for its diverse climate zones, rich biodiversity, and significant geological features. It is also a potential World Heritage Site due to its flora and fauna.

Major_Events.Description: Yushan National Park was officially established on April 10, 1985.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features diverse geological formations, including fault lines, joints, and folding. It also contains numerous peaks, canyons, cliffs, and valleys, with an elevation difference of 3,600 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Yushan National Park is culturally significant due to its rich biodiversity, unique geological features, and historical evidence of early human occupation. It is also an important watershed for several major river systems in Taiwan.
world knowledge.Details: Yushan National Park is home to more than thirty peaks over 3,000 meters in elevation and contains half of Taiwan's native plant species. The park is also an important nesting ground for the Taiwanese population of Mountain hawk-eagle. Prehistoric relics found in the park provide evidence of early human occupation, and the park is currently inhabited by the Bunun aboriginal tribe.

world knowledge.Name: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park
world knowledge.Area: Cypress County, Alberta RM of Maple Creek No. 111, Saskatchewan, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park is a natural park in Canada straddling the Alberta/Saskatchewan boundary and jointly administered by the two provinces. It became Canada's first interprovincial park in 1989. The park consists of two protected areas: the West Block, which straddles the Alberta/Saskatchewan boundary, and the Centre Block, an additional area in Saskatchewan.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse landscape including lush forest, fescue grassland, and dry mixed-grass prairie. It includes several lakes, viewpoints, and recreational facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park protects the majority of the Cypress Hills landscape and is significant for its biodiversity and recreational opportunities. It is also adjacent to the Fort Walsh National Historic Site.
world knowledge.Details: The park offers a variety of activities year-round, including camping, hiking, swimming, skiing, and snowmobiling. It is home to approximately 700 species of plants and animals, including 14 species of orchids and five species of large hoofed mammals. The park also features several lakes, hiking trails, and winter amenities such as a tobogganing hill and snowmobile trails.

world knowledge.Name: Edinburgh Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in 1916 as RAF Turnhouse, it became a public airport on 19 May 1947. It has since grown to become the busiest airport in Scotland and the sixth busiest in the UK.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was originally opened as RAF Turnhouse, a military airfield.
The airport was officially opened for commercial traffic on 19 May 1947.
A new terminal was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 27 May 1977.
BAA sold Edinburgh Airport to Global Infrastructure Partners for £807.2 million.
Edinburgh Airport became the first in Scotland to record over 15 million passengers in a calendar year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern terminal designed by Sir Robert Matthew, with a 57-metre-tall air traffic control tower completed in 2005.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the busiest airport in Scotland, it plays a crucial role in connecting Scotland to the rest of the world and contributes significantly to the local economy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving commercial and private flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by Edinburgh Trams and is located near the M8 and M9 motorways. It handles over 15 million passengers annually and serves as a base for several airlines including easyJet, Jet2.com, Loganair, and Ryanair.

world knowledge.Name: John S. Thompsonbrug
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The John S. Thompsonbrug is a bridge over the Maas River, built in 1929 as part of the main road between 's-Hertogenbosch and Nijmegen. It was renamed in 2004 to honor John S. Thompson, a first lieutenant who led his platoon in capturing the bridge during Operation Market Garden in 1944.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was built as part of the main road between 's-Hertogenbosch and Nijmegen.
John S. Thompson led his platoon in an attack against the bridge, which was defended by German forces. The platoon successfully captured the bridge and destroyed enemy equipment.
The bridge was renamed to John S. Thompsonbrug in honor of Thompson's platoon's capture. Many veterans of World War II, as well as Thompson's wife, attended the ceremony.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally and historically significant due to its role in Operation Market Garden during World War II and its renaming to honor John S. Thompson and his platoon's bravery.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries provincial route N324 over the Maas River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge still carries the provincial route N324. During the 1944 attack, Thompson's platoon destroyed electrical equipment and cables suspected to be hooked up to demolitions, and a bazooka operator destroyed a nearby flak gun.

world knowledge.Name: Point Lonsdale Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Point Lonsdale, Borough of Queenscliffe, Victoria, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Point Lonsdale Lighthouse, also known as the Point Lonsdale Signal Station, was completed in 1902. It stands at the eastern end of the Bellarine Peninsula, overlooking The Rip, a treacherous navigable passage. The first navigation aid at Point Lonsdale was a signal station erected in 1852, followed by a red pillar beacon in 1856. The original Queenscliff Low Light was re-erected here in 1863 and replaced by the current concrete tower in 1902. The lighthouse was automated in 1999 but remains staffed for signal station operations.

Major_Events.Description: The current lighthouse was completed, replacing the earlier wooden structure.
Responsibility for the lighthouse passed from the state of Victoria to the Commonwealth.
The lighthouse was handed back to Victoria and classified as a 'Harbour Entrance Light'.
The lighthouse was automated, though the signal station remains staffed.
Celebrations marked the 100th anniversary of the lighthouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a cylindrical tower with a balcony and lantern, standing 21.3 metres tall. It is constructed of reinforced concrete and features a Chance Brothers lantern. The base includes an octagonal, two-storey brick signal station and observation room. The design is typical of early 20th-century lighthouses, with a white tower and black lantern and dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is of architectural, historical, and archaeological significance to Victoria. It reflects the importance of maritime navigation and trade in Port Phillip. The precinct includes rare structures like a foghorn shed and an explosives shed, and it is associated with the defence history of Port Phillip during both World Wars.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigation aid and signal station for commercial shipping entering Port Phillip.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse precinct is listed on the Victorian Heritage Register (H1517). The foghorn, restored in 2002, operates in foggy weather with a double blast every 30 seconds. Public access is available, and tours are conducted by the Queenscliffe Maritime Museum on Sundays. The surrounding waters are part of the Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park.

world knowledge.Name: Gaiety Theater (Manila)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gaiety Theater was a stand-alone art deco cinema house designed by Juan Nakpil, National Artist of the Philippines for Architecture, in 1935. It provided venues for early forms of entertainment like bodabil, a local adaptation of vaudeville, and later converted to movie theaters with the growth of Philippine cinema. It was first owned by Harry Brown, the American producer of La vida de Jose Rizal, the first feature film produced in the Philippines. During WWII, it was reopened under Japanese occupation with cheap tickets. It was later used as a place of worship by the Jesus is Lord Cosmopolitan Church. The theater was demolished in 2016 after years of deterioration.

Major_Events.Description: The Gaiety Theater was designed by Juan Nakpil and opened as an art deco cinema house.
Operation was stopped during WWII until Karl Nathan obtained permission from Japanese authorities to reopen it.
The theater was used by the Jesus is Lord Cosmopolitan Church for worship.
The theater was demolished after years of neglect and deterioration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art deco style cinema house designed by Juan Nakpil.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gaiety Theater was significant for its role in early Philippine cinema and entertainment, showcasing art films and serving as a cultural hub during its operational years.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a cinema and entertainment venue, later used as a place of worship.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was a plot setting in the 2010 horror film Cinco. Efforts to resurrect it in the 1990s failed, and it remained dilapidated until demolition.

world knowledge.Name: Hamburg Dungeon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hamburg Dungeon is a tourist attraction that provides a journey through Hamburg’s dark history in an actor-led, interactive experience. It is the first of its brand to be built in mainland Europe and is part of a chain that includes the London Dungeon and Berlin Dungeon.

Major_Events.Description: Visitors have to find their way through the terrible Great Fire of Hamburg that devastated much of the city.
A recreation of a Plague-ravaged Hamburg street, where the effect the killer disease had in the city is animated.

The story of the life of the infamous pirate Klaus Störtebeker, who used to plunder the Baltic and North Seas, is told via a brief video. Visitors are then taken on to a mock pirate ship to help fight in a nautical battle before witnessing the execution of the famous pirate.

Hamburg used to be prone to terrible flooding, with one of the worst being on Christmas Day 1717. Visitors are taken on a boat ride which is designed to look like a small raft to take them through the carnage of the city and to safety.
The graphic exhibition and show Cholera 1892 depicts the cholera epidemic which wiped out over a third of the population of Hamburg.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hamburg Dungeon is culturally significant as it explores the darker aspects of Hamburg’s history, including events like the Great Fire, the Plague, and the Cholera Epidemic, through interactive and immersive experiences.
world knowledge.Details: The Hamburg Dungeon has sister sites at the Berlin Dungeon, London Dungeon, York Dungeon, Edinburgh Dungeon, and Amsterdam Dungeon. Each Dungeon is based on the same theme but investigates the history of its area. The sites are owned by Poole-based Merlin Entertainments.

world knowledge.Name: The Blue Note (Columbia, Missouri)
world knowledge.Address: 17 North 9th Street, Columbia, Missouri 65201, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Blue Note is a music venue in Columbia, Missouri, established in 1980 by Richard King and Phil Costello. It is a contributing property to the North Ninth Street Historic District. The original location was at 912 Business Loop 70 East before moving to its current Ninth Street location in the early 1990s. In October 2014, the venue was sold to Matt Gerding and Scott Leslie.

Major_Events.Description: A five-part concert series held every summer.
The venue relocated to a restored vaudeville theater.

Major_Events.Event: Sale to Matt Gerding and Scott Leslie
Major_Events.Description: Ownership of the venue was transferred.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Restored vaudeville theater
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Blue Note is a significant music venue that has hosted numerous national musical acts and is a contributing property to the North Ninth Street Historic District. It is also notable for the legal case Bensusan Restaurant Corp. v. King over naming use on the internet.
world knowledge.Details: The Blue Note has a capacity of 835 and is known for hosting both established and up-and-coming artists. Formerly Mojo's, Rose Music Hall is located down the street and is often referred to as "The Blue Note's little sister." Forrest Rose Park, adjacent to Rose Music Hall, began hosting outdoor performances in 2008.

world knowledge.Name: Clifton Observatory
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as a windmill for corn in 1766, later converted to a snuff mill. Damaged by fire in 1777 and derelict until 1828 when artist William West rented it as a studio. Converted into an observatory by 1842. Sold in 1977 with public access maintained. Purchased by Ian Johnson in 2015.

Major_Events.Description: The mill was damaged by fire when the sails were left turning during a gale, causing the equipment to catch alight.
William West converted the building into an observatory with telescopes and a camera obscura.
The Merchant Venturers sold the observatory to Honorbrook Inns, with public access to the camera obscura maintained.
The observatory was bought by local entrepreneur Ian Johnson.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grade II* listed building, originally a windmill, later converted to an observatory. Features a camera obscura with a 5-inch convex lens and sloping mirror projecting images onto a circular table.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Used by artists of the Bristol School to draw the Avon Gorge and Leigh Woods. Contains historical artifacts and is a notable example of repurposed industrial architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The observatory includes a tunnel to St Vincent's Cave, which has historical significance as a chapel and place of refuge. The camera obscura has been operational since 1828. The site is on the Buildings at Risk Register.

world knowledge.Name: Dundee Contemporary Arts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dundee Contemporary Arts (DCA) is an art centre in Dundee, Scotland, established on 19 March 1999. The idea of establishing a visual arts centre in Dundee had been discussed since the mid-1980s, aiming to nurture students and graduates of Duncan of Jordanstone College of Art & Design and build upon the work of the Seagate Gallery and Dundee Printmakers' Workshop. The project also aimed to replace the part-time Steps Theatre with a full-time cinema. The initiative was led by Dundee Printmakers Workshop, forming a partnership between the Council, the University of Dundee, and Dundee Contemporary Arts. The building was designed by Richard Murphy Architects after winning an international design competition in July 1996. The final construction cost was £9 million.

Major_Events.Description: Dundee Contemporary Arts officially opened on 19 March 1999.

Major_Events.Event: Nomination for Art Fund Museum of the Year
Major_Events.Description: DCA was nominated for Art Fund Museum of the Year in 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building, designed by Richard Murphy Architects, is hailed as an innovative modern space. It features two contemporary art galleries, a two-screen cinema, a print studio, a learning and public engagement programme, a shop, and a café bar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: DCA is culturally significant as it supports contemporary arts, nurtures local talent, and provides a platform for artists and filmmakers. It was listed in the Royal Incorporation of Architects in Scotland (RIAS) top 10 of Scotland's top 100 buildings of the 20th century.
world knowledge.Details: The centre currently receives approximately 380,000 visitors per year. The website for DCA is dca.org.uk.

world knowledge.Name: Turvey Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Turvey Abbey was originally built in 1603, with parts possibly incorporating an even earlier structure. It has been home to various tenants, including the Brands, a Catholic recusant family, and later the Higgins family, who made significant repairs and additions. It is now a Benedictine priory.

Major_Events.Description: The original part of Turvey Abbey was built.
John Higgins built a new coach house, added balustrading, mullioned windows, a walled garden, and a Gothic summer house.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as Priory of Our Lady of Peace
Major_Events.Description: Turvey Abbey became a Benedictine priory for a Roman Catholic community of nuns.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is made of stone with a tile roof. It features additions such as a coach house with a clock, balustrading, mullioned windows, a walled garden, and a Gothic summer house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Turvey Abbey is significant for its historical architecture and its role as a Catholic recusant household. It now serves as a spiritual center for a Benedictine community.
world knowledge.Details: The Abbey is not open to the public, but the community welcomes guests. The adjacent "Monastery of Christ our Saviour" is not part of Turvey Abbey. A dovecote, which no longer belongs to the Abbey, is a Grade II listed building.

world knowledge.Name: Parc des Combes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parc des Combes is an amusement park located in Le Creusot, in Burgundy, France. The wooded park is a part of the Les Chemins de Fer du Creusot ("Creusot Railways" in English) tourist attraction, served by the Train des Combes tourist train. The park is located on an old Morvan valley. The 241 P 17 steam locomotive was first built between 1947 and 1949.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a roller coaster and karting on the top of the hill, near the tourist train station.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is part of the Les Chemins de Fer du Creusot tourist attraction, highlighting the region's railway heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates from April to October and includes 21 attractions, with 3 roller coasters and 3 water rides. The website is www.parcdescombes.com.

world knowledge.Name: Moscow International House of Music
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Moscow International House of Music was officially opened on September 28, 2003, as part of a cultural and business complex intended to be Moscow's equivalent of Lincoln Center. It was the first classical music hall constructed in the city in over a century. The project was financed entirely by the City of Moscow and cost US$200 million.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Moscow International Performing Arts Centre
Major_Events.Description: The center was inaugurated with the debut of the National Philharmonic of Russia under musical director Vladimir Spivakov.

Major_Events.Event: World premiere of Vladimir Martynov's opera Vita Nova
Major_Events.Description: Performed by the Kirov Opera in concert format as part of the 2003 Moscow Easter Festival.

Major_Events.Event: Moscow premiere of Krzysztof Penderecki's oratorio The Seven Gates of Jerusalem
Major_Events.Description: Performed by the National Philharmonic Orchestra.

Major_Events.Event: World premiere of Dimitri Arapis's Symphony No.3
Major_Events.Description: Performed by the State Symphony Orchestra and Capella of Russia, conducted by Valery Poliansky.

Major_Events.Event: World Premiere of Venus Rey Jr's song cycle "The Pavlova Songs"
Major_Events.Description: Performed by the Musica Viva Chamber Orchestra, featuring poems by Russian poet Vera Pavlova.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features a postmodern architectural style with a modernistic, cylindrical glass and steel design. The main concert hall is circular, similar to the Philharmonie in Berlin, and seats 1,735 people. The auditorium is composed largely of Siberian larch wood, known for its excellent acoustics. The center also includes a 575-seat chamber hall, a 532-seat theater, and other facilities such as sound studios, rehearsal halls, and an audio-video complex. The building is topped by a 9.5-meter-tall, 2 metric-ton treble clef covered in mosaic gold, designed by sculptor Zurab Tsereteli.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Moscow International House of Music is a significant cultural landmark in Russia, serving as a premier venue for classical music performances. It houses the largest organ in Russia and has hosted numerous world premieres and notable performances. The center was conceived as a home for the Russian National Orchestra and later became the base for the National Philharmonic Orchestra under Vladimir Spivakov.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts center and concert venue
world knowledge.Details: The center features the largest organ in Russia, with over 5,500 pipes, installed in 2004. It was designed and built by German firms Glatter-Goetz and Johannes Klais. The organ has 84 stops and weighs 30 tons. The center is part of the Riverside Towers complex, which includes business and hotel facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Quilty, County Clare
world knowledge.Location: County Clare, Irish Grid Reference R016751
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Quilty, historically known as Killty, is a small fishing village in County Clare, Ireland. It was formerly part of the west Clare Gaeltacht, an Irish-speaking community, until 1956. The area is known for its fishing industry, particularly lobster, salmon, bass, herring, and mackerel. The village has a rich history, including the rescue of the crew of the French ship Leon XIII in 1907.

Major_Events.Event: Rescue of the Leon XIII crew
Major_Events.Description: A French three-masted full-rigged ship, the Leon XIII, was driven onto rocky reefs in Quilty Bay. Local fishermen rescued the crew using currachs, small open boats, despite dangerous conditions.
Teigh Caech McMahon, with the help of the Earl of Desmond, stormed Tromoroe Castle on 17 February 1599.
O'Flaherty from Connacht attacked Tromoroe Castle on 1 May 1642, resulting in the deaths of Peter Ward, his wife, and heir.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The local Catholic church features a round tower visible from the surrounding countryside, built in remembrance of the Leon XIII rescue. The church's porch contains a replica of the Leon XIII in a glass bottle, and the ship's bell stands in front of the altar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Quilty is culturally significant for its fishing heritage, its history as part of the Irish-speaking Gaeltacht, and the heroic rescue of the Leon XIII crew. The village also has historical landmarks like Tromoroe Castle and Mutton Island, which has ties to Saint Senan and was used as a prison and signal tower.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Fishing village with historical and cultural landmarks.
world knowledge.Details: Mutton Island, across the bay from Quilty, was the site of a church founded by Saint Senan in the early 6th century. It later housed a signal tower built in the early 19th century and was used as a prison in the early 20th century. During certain tidal conditions, it is possible to walk from Seafield to Mutton Island along a limestone path. Quilty GAA club amalgamated with Kilmurry Ibrickane GAA club in the 1970s, with matches played at the former club grounds in the village.

world knowledge.Name: Parc Floral de la Source
world knowledge.Area: La Source neighbourhood, Orléans, Loiret, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The land was ceded to the monks of the Abbey Saint-Mesmin de Micy by Clovis in 510. From 1427, it belonged to various lords and noble families. The first major gardening work in the formal French garden style dates from the early 18th century. In 1959, the city of Orléans and the département acquired the estate, reserving 35 hectares for the park. The garden opened in 1964 as a recreational park and horticultural showcase.

Major_Events.Description: Attracted 2,300,000 visitors in six months, featuring 330 exhibitors, 700 producers from 11 countries, and 13,000 m² of glasshouses. Included attractions like a reconstructed Gaulois village.

Major_Events.Event: Voyage en chrysanthèmes et la ronde des fougères
Major_Events.Description: Exhibition showcasing chrysanthemums and ferns.

Major_Events.Event: Festival of exotic birds and orchids
Major_Events.Description: Exhibition featuring exotic birds and orchids.
Exhibition dedicated to irises.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park uses the natural contours of the site, featuring open spaces where flora, fauna, and minerals are juxtaposed. It includes formal French gardens, animal enclosures, floral and horticultural works, aviaries, and various themed gardens (e.g., iris garden, rose garden, tropical gardens).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is the most visited site in Loiret and has been awarded the status of Jardin remarquable by the French Ministry of Culture. It showcases a unique geographical position between Sologne and the Loire Valley and houses a specialist national collection of irises.
world knowledge.Details: The park features the source of the Loiret river at its center. It includes a children's playground and a 'train' that tours the site. Admission costs 6 € for adults, 4 € for children aged 6-16, and is free for those under 6. The park is closed on 1 January and 25 December.

world knowledge.Name: Toledo Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 120 metres (390 ft) length, 59 metres (194 ft) width, 44.5 metres (146 ft) height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Primatial Cathedral of Saint Mary of Toledo, also known as Toledo Cathedral, is a Catholic church in Toledo, Spain. It is the seat of the Metropolitan Archdiocese of Toledo. The cathedral is one of the three 13th-century High Gothic cathedrals in Spain and is considered the magnum opus of the Gothic style in Spain. It was begun in 1226 under the rule of Ferdinand III and completed in 1493 during the time of the Catholic Monarchs. The cathedral was modeled after the Bourges Cathedral and incorporates elements of the Mudéjar style.

Major_Events.Description: The church was consecrated for a second time in the year 587 after undergoing some alterations.
The construction of the cathedral began in 1227 under the rule of Ferdinand III.
The last Gothic contributions were made in 1493 when the vaults of the central nave were finished.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is built in the High Gothic style with five naves, a transept, and a double ambulatory. It features a combination of Gothic and Mudéjar architectural elements, including multifoiled arches in the triforium. The cathedral is constructed with white limestone from the quarries of Olihuelas, near Toledo.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Toledo Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as one of the most important Gothic cathedrals in Spain. It serves as the seat of the Metropolitan Archdiocese of Toledo and is a prime example of the fusion of Gothic and Mudéjar architectural styles. The cathedral also houses important religious artifacts and artworks.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is popularly known as Dives Toletana (The Rich Toledan). It includes the Mozarabic Chapel, which still uses the Hispano-Mozarabic Rite and music. The cathedral's construction was influenced by the French Gothic style and incorporates elements from the former city mosque that stood on the site.

world knowledge.Name: Kaeng Krachan National Park
world knowledge.Area: Phetchaburi and Prachuap Khiri Khan Provinces, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kaeng Krachan National Park is the largest national park in Thailand, established on 12 June 1981. It was declared a reserve in 1964 and later became the 28th national park of Thailand. The park was enlarged in December 1984 to include the boundary area between Phetchaburi and Prachuap Khiri Khan Provinces. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site on 26 July 2021.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: On 26 July 2021, the 21 nations of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee voted 12–9 to approve Kaeng Krachan's listing as a World Heritage Site.
The park was enlarged to include the boundary area between Phetchaburi and Prachuap Khiri Khan Provinces, adding an additional 273,125 rai ~ 437 square kilometres (169 sq mi).
Kaeng Krachan National Park became the 28th national park of Thailand on 12 June 1981.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park consists mainly of rainforest on the eastern slope of the Tenasserim Mountain Range. It includes the Kaeng Krachan Dam, which creates a lake covering an area of 46.5 km2.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kaeng Krachan National Park is culturally and historically significant as it is the largest national park in Thailand and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is also part of the Kaeng Krachan Forest Complex and has been included on the list of ASEAN Heritage Parks.
world knowledge.Details: The park is known for its biodiversity, including tropical and subtropical broadleaf tree species, palms, 91 species of mammals, and 461 bird species. It faces issues such as poaching, private plantations within its confines, and environmental concerns over infrastructure projects.

world knowledge.Name: Oxburgh Hall
world knowledge.Address: In the village of Oxborough, 7 miles south west of Swaffham, Oxborough, England
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Square moat about 75 metres on each side
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oxburgh Hall is a moated country house in Oxborough, Norfolk, England, built for Sir Edmund Bedingfeld in 1482. The Bedingfelds have lived at the hall since its construction, although ownership passed to the National Trust in 1952. The house underwent extensive refurbishment in the mid 19th century under John Chessell Buckler and Augustus Pugin.

Major_Events.Description: The house underwent extensive refurbishment under John Chessell Buckler and Augustus Pugin.

The Hall and gardens faced demolition but were saved when Sybil, Lady Bedingfeld, her daughter Mrs Frances Playford, and niece Mrs Violet Hartcup raised enough funds to buy Oxburgh back, then gave it to the National Trust in 1952.
The National Trust announced plans for the reversion of 175 acres of land at Oxburgh from farmland back to wildlife-friendly woods and pasture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Oxburgh Hall is an example of a late medieval, inward-facing great house, featuring a fortified gatehouse, Tudor architectural style, brick, stone, and slate materials, Flemish-style stepped gables, massive southeast tower, oriel windows overhanging the moat, and terracotta chimneys.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oxburgh Hall is culturally significant for its historical architecture, the priest hole constructed by Nicholas Owen, and the Oxburgh Hangings, needlework by Mary, Queen of Scots and Bess of Hardwick. It is also notable for its Grade I listing on the National Heritage List for England.
world knowledge.Details: The hall is known for its priest hole and the Oxburgh Hangings. It has been listed Grade I on the National Heritage List for England since 1951. The landscaped and formal gardens have been Grade II listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens since 1987.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Alberta Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Alberta Museum (RAM) is a museum of human and natural history in Downtown Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Established by the Government of Alberta in December 1967 as the Provincial Museum of Alberta, it received royal patronage from Queen Elizabeth II in 2005 and was renamed the Royal Alberta Museum. The museum moved to a new building in 2018, which is the largest museum in western Canada with over 7,600 square metres of exhibition space.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was established as the Provincial Museum of Alberta.
Queen Elizabeth II bestowed royal patronage, and the museum was renamed the Royal Alberta Museum.
The museum moved to a new building in Downtown Edmonton, which is the largest museum in western Canada.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by Raymond O. Harrison in 1967 and later by Ledcor and DIALOG in 2017. The new building features expansive galleries, an interactive children's gallery, and a bug room with live invertebrates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum chronicles Alberta's natural and cultural history and features extensive collections in cultural studies, Earth science, and life science. It also hosts travelling exhibitions from around the world.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include over 2,000,000 items, and it attracts more than 400,000 visitors annually. The new building was completed in 2016 and opened to the public in 2018. The total cost of the new building and moving was estimated at CAD $375.5 million.

world knowledge.Name: "Üns" Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The contemporary Theatre ÜNS was opened in Baku in 2006. The head of the project was professor Nargiz Pashayeva, who referred to the theatre as 'a creative stage'. The theatre is named after the root of the word 'ÜNSiyyət', which means friendship, communication, mutual understanding, and inner world of the individual. The theatre aims to elevate Azerbaijani theatre art by combining tradition and innovation. The building was reconstructed from a former transformer station built in the 1920s.

Major_Events.Description: The contemporary Theatre ÜNS was opened in Baku.
Art evenings were held within the framework of this project, aiming to bring together representatives of various types of modern art.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre building consists of two distinct and organically linked units: the reconstructed and refurbished building of the transformer station (room and stage) and the administrative building made of glass, metal, and plastics. The reconstruction was led by architect Oqtay Sattarov, and the interior decorations were done by artist Altay Sadygzade. The sound, light, video, and stage were elaborated and installed by a Russian company.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: ÜNS Theatre is culturally significant as it aims to rise the level of Azerbaijani theatre art by combining tradition and newness. It has hosted performances by renowned cultural personalities and directors, and has staged its own drama performances, musicals, recitals, concerts, and exhibitions.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has staged performances such as 'Final Restaurant' by Magsud Ibrahimbeyov, 'Shakespeare' by Elchin Efendiyev, musicals 'Baku' and 'Notre-Drame de Paris'. It has also hosted unforgettable performances by Russian director Roman Viktuk, including 'Edith Piaf, My Legionnaire' and 'Trees die while standing' based on the play by Alejandro Casona. Additionally, the theatre has hosted concerts by French musicians of Arab origin, performances of a Corsican ethnic choir, and concerts of jazz pianist Shahin Novrasli.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Tanlay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Tanlay was built during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries in Burgundy. It was initially reconstructed in Renaissance style by François de Coligny d'Andelot, who inherited the ruined site in 1547. Construction was halted during the Wars of Religion, when Tanlay served as a center of Huguenot resistance. The château was later completed by Michel Particeli d'Hemery under designs by Pierre Le Muet between 1643 and 1649. The property has remained in the same family since 1700.

Major_Events.Description: During the Wars of Religion, the château served as a center for Huguenot resistance.
The château was completed to designs by Pierre Le Muet during this period.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The château features limestone walls under tall sloping slate roofs, cylindrical towers at its four corners, and a symmetrical cour d'honneur. It is encircled by a rectilinear moat and approached via a bridge marked by paired obelisks. The architecture includes Renaissance elements, trompe-l'œil gallery paintings, and frescoes in the Tour de la Ligue.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Tanlay is renowned for its beauty, historical role in the Wars of Religion, and its association with Huguenot resistance. It is also notable for its artistic features, including trompe-l'œil paintings and frescoes depicting historical figures as Olympic deities.
world knowledge.Details: The château's grounds include a nymphaeum or théâtre d'eau designed by Pierre Le Muet, as well as remarkable canals and moats. The property has been in the same family since 1700, when the owner was created marquis de Tanlay.

world knowledge.Name: Yokohama Hakkeijima Sea Paradise
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yokohama Hakkeijima Sea Paradise is an amusement park that opened on May 8, 1993. It was developed by Yokohama Hakkeijima Inc., a company established in March 1988 by nine companies centered on Seibu Group and Prince Hotel. The park is located on an artificial island, Hakkeijima, created by Yokohama City.

Major_Events.Description: The whale shark exhibit opened on October 5, 2010, marking the first such facility in eastern Japan. The exhibit was discontinued after the whale shark died in 2019.
The aquarium introduced the JELLYFISHBOT, a garbage collection drone, to aid in environmental conservation efforts.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Mijikana Marine Life Institute
Major_Events.Description: The aquarium opened the "Mijikana Marine Life Institute" in collaboration with Tokyo University, focusing on educating visitors about the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals).
About 90 rare deep-sea creatures died during transfer to the aquarium due to a mechanical failure that caused the water temperature to rise. This incident drew criticism from animal rights groups.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features an aquarium with a pyramid-like appearance, spanning five floors with exhibits on the 1st, 3rd, and 4th floors. The 5th floor houses LABO12 and the Aqua Theater. The park also includes a tunnel-shaped water tank and a cylindrical water tank for dolphin and Ocean Sunfish exhibits. The design emphasizes close interaction with marine life.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Yokohama Hakkeijima Sea Paradise is a significant cultural and educational landmark, accredited as a Museum-equivalent facility by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology. It plays a role in marine conservation and education, with exhibits and programs focused on understanding and preserving marine life.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park and aquarium, providing entertainment, education, and conservation efforts related to marine life.

Details.Attendance: 4,770,000 visitors in 2007, ranking sixth among Asian amusement parks.
Details.Admission: Pay-as-you-go with options for day passes or individual attraction tickets.
Details.Conservation_Efforts: The aquarium collaborates with various institutions for breeding and studying sharks and rays, including the endangered sand tiger species. It established the Sand Tiger Breeding Council in 2015.
Details.Pop_Culture_Reference: Featured in the film 'Godzilla Against Mechagodzilla,' where it is destroyed by Godzilla.

world knowledge.Name: University of Latvia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Latvia was established in 1919, initially named the Higher School of Latvia. It was founded on the basis of the former Riga Polytechnic (1862). The university underwent several name changes during the Soviet and Nazi occupations, reverting to its current name in 1991 following Latvia's independence. It has been a central institution for higher education, science, and culture in Latvia.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Latvia was established, initially named the Higher School of Latvia.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to University of Latvia
Major_Events.Description: The institution was officially renamed the University of Latvia.
The university was renamed the Latvian State University during the Soviet occupation.
The university was renamed the University of Riga during the Nazi occupation.
The Supreme Council of the Republic of Latvia reconfirmed the Constitution of the University of Latvia, restoring its original name and attributes.
The EuroFaculty was established at the University of Latvia to support reforms in higher education.

Major_Events.Event: Merger with Riga Teacher Training Academy
Major_Events.Description: The Riga Teacher Training and Educational Management Academy was merged into the University of Latvia.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Latvia has been a central institution for higher education, science, and culture in Latvia, playing a crucial role in the country's academic and cultural development.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Latvia offers undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels of study. It consists of 6 faculties and various research institutes, including the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Institute of Geodesy and Geoinformatics. The university also has a number of amateur choirs, orchestras, dance groups, and a student theatre.

world knowledge.Name: University of Barcelona
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 4 campuses with 16 faculties and 9 affiliated centres
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Barcelona was established in 1450 under the royal prerogative granted by King Alfons el Magnànim. It evolved from a medical school founded by King Martí of Aragon in 1401. The university faced several challenges, including civil wars and financial difficulties, but it continued to grow and develop. It was closed by the Bourbon dynasty after the War of the Spanish Succession from 1714 until 1837. The university was restored to Barcelona during the liberal revolution under the reign of Isabella II. Over the centuries, it expanded its facilities and academic offerings, becoming one of the largest and most prestigious universities in Spain.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Barcelona was established under the royal prerogative granted by King Alfons el Magnànim.
The university was closed by the Bourbon dynasty after the War of the Spanish Succession.
The university was restored to Barcelona during the liberal revolution under the reign of Isabella II.
Work began on Elies Rogent's new building, which was completed in 1882.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's historic building, designed by Elies Rogent, is one of the first buildings constructed outside the ancient city walls of Barcelona. It features a mix of architectural styles, including Gothic and Renaissance elements, with sculptures and paintings commissioned from renowned artists.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Barcelona is a symbol of Catalonia's cultural and academic heritage. It has played a crucial role in the development of education and research in Spain and Europe. The university is also a center for Catalan language and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Barcelona is one of the largest universities in Spain, with 76,000 students. It offers 74 undergraduate programs, 349 graduate programs, and 48 doctorate programs. The university has 106 departments and more than 5,000 full-time researchers. It is home to three large research foundations: the Barcelona Science Park Foundation, the August Pi i Sunyer Biomedical Research Institute, and the Bellvitge Institute for Biomedical Research. The university has been ranked 1st in Spain in most of the 2024 rankings and is located around the 50th place in Europe.

world knowledge.Name: Moses Mabhida Stadium
world knowledge.Address: 44 Walter Gilbert Road, Stamford Hill, Durban, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Moses Mabhida Stadium is a soccer stadium in Durban, named after Moses Mabhida, a former general secretary of the South African Communist Party. It was built for the 2010 FIFA World Cup and serves as a multi-use venue for various events.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted five group games, one round game, and a semi-final match.
Hosted four group games, one quarter-final, and a semi-final.
Hosted a Twenty20 cricket match between South Africa and India, which India won by 21 runs. It was the biggest crowd for a cricket match on the African continent.
The award-winning gospel ensemble Joyous Celebration recorded their first outdoor recording at the stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a 350m long and 105m high arch inspired by the South African flag, representing unity. The roof is a 46,000m² Teflon-coated, glass-fibre membrane. The stadium includes a funicular to a viewing platform and a 550-step adventure walk. It has 120 corporate hospitality suites and adjustable seating capacity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium symbolizes the unity of South Africa and is named after a prominent anti-apartheid activist. It is a key venue for sports and cultural events, contributing to Durban's identity as a major events destination.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium for soccer, cricket, rugby, concerts, and other events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 55,500 (expandable to 75,000). It includes a sports institute and a transmodal transport station. Planned upgrades include a new Sky Car, Big Swing, bungee jump, zip line, and Compression Ring Walk to enhance visitor experience and commercial viability.

world knowledge.Name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica, Kochi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica, originally built by the Portuguese in 1505, was elevated to a cathedral by Pope Paul IV in 1558. It was spared by Dutch conquerors in the 17th century but demolished by the British in 1795. A new structure was commissioned in 1887 and consecrated in 1905. It was proclaimed a basilica by Pope John Paul II in 1984.

Major_Events.Description: The church was originally built by the Portuguese after securing permission from the King of Cochin.
Pope Paul IV elevated the Santa Cruz Church to the status of a Cathedral.
The British demolished the cathedral as part of their strategy to dismantle Catholic infrastructure in the region.
Bishop João Gomes Ferreira initiated the reconstruction, which was completed and consecrated in 1905.
Pope John Paul II elevated the cathedral to the status of a basilica.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The basilica exhibits a blend of Gothic and Indo-European architectural influences, with a predominantly white exterior and pastel-colored interior. It features two imposing spires, intricate frescoes, murals, seven large canvas paintings, stained glass windows, and ceiling paintings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica is one of the finest and most impressive churches in India, attracting tourists year-round. It is not only a place of devotion but also a center of historic significance, endowed with architectural and artistic grandeur.
world knowledge.Details: The basilica hosts the relic of The Holy Cross of Jesus Christ and a shrine dedicated to Our Lady of Fátima. It was designed by the Italian Jesuit brother and painter Fr. Antonio Moscheni and his disciple Fr. De Gama of Mangalore.

world knowledge.Name: Aligarh Muslim University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875, it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920 following the Aligarh Muslim University Act. The university was part of the Aligarh Movement, which aimed to establish a modern education system for the Indian Muslim populace.
