Major_Events.Description: Founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to provide modern education to Indian Muslims.
Following the Aligarh Muslim University Act, the college was upgraded to a university.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College And Hospital
Major_Events.Description: A medical school was established as part of the university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus includes heritage buildings such as Strachey Hall, Mushtaq Manzil, Asman Manzil, Nizam Museum, Lytton Library, Victoria Gate, and Jama Masjid. The Maulana Azad Library is a prominent seven-storied building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is an institution of national importance and has played a significant role in the education and empowerment of Indian Muslims. It has been a center for the Pakistan Movement and continues to be a prominent educational institution in India.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers over 300 courses and has 13 faculties, 7 colleges, 15 centers, 3 institutes, and 10 schools. It has a significant international student population and is ranked among the top universities in India and Asia. The campus includes 19 halls of residence, sports facilities, and cultural clubs.

world knowledge.Name: Waipapa Point Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Waipapa Point Lighthouse was built in response to the wreck of the passenger steamer SS Tararua on reefs off Waipapa Point on 29 April 1881, with the loss of 131 lives. It was first lit on 1 January 1884. It is one of the last two wooden lighthouses built in New Zealand.

Major_Events.Description: The passenger steamer SS Tararua wrecked on reefs off Waipapa Point, resulting in the loss of 131 lives.
The lighthouse was first lit on 1 January 1884.
The lighthouse was automated and keepers were withdrawn.
The lighthouse has been solar powered since 1988.
A new LED beacon was installed externally on the balcony of the lighthouse.
Restoration work ensured the lighthouse was weatherproof and secure from vandalism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a hexagonal wooden tower with a balcony and lantern. It is marked with a white tower, red trim, and a grey lantern dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Waipapa Point Lighthouse is culturally significant as it was built in response to a tragic maritime disaster and is one of the last two wooden lighthouses built in New Zealand. It is also a Heritage New Zealand Category 1 historic place.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was automated in 1975 and has been solar powered since 1988. A new LED beacon was installed in December 2008. Restoration work in 2008 ensured it was weatherproof and secure from vandalism. It is operated by Maritime New Zealand.

world knowledge.Name: Paoay Church
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 110 metres (360 ft), Width: 40 metres (130 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saint Augustine Parish Church, commonly known as Paoay Church, is a Roman Catholic church in the municipality of Paoay, Ilocos Norte in the Philippines. Completed in 1710, the church is famous for its distinctive architecture, a highlight of which are the enormous buttresses on the sides and the back of the building. It is declared as a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 1973 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the collective group of Baroque Churches of the Philippines in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: Some portions of the church were damaged in the 1865 and 1885 earthquakes but was later restored under the initiative of former First Lady, Imelda Marcos.
The restoration of the church's buttresses, walls, tower, and interior was announced in 2018.

Conservation of the church's exteriors was begun by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines in the second quarter of 2019 and completed in June 2020. The restored structure was turned over to the Laoag diocese in November 2020, and was reopened on November 15 of that year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Paoay church is the Philippines' primary example of a Spanish colonial earthquake baroque architecture. The most striking feature is the 24 huge buttresses of about 1.67 metres (5.5 ft) thick at the sides and back of the church building. Its walls are made of large coral stones on the lower part and bricks at the upper levels. The stone façade appear as massive pediment rising from the ground and is built leaning towards the front. Adjacent to the façade is a three-storey coral bell tower constructed separately from the church building on the right side resembling a pagoda.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: By virtue of Presidential Decree No. 260, Paoay Church was declared as a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 1973. The church was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with San Agustin Church in Manila; Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion Church in Santa Maria, Ilocos Sur; and Sto. Tomas de Villanueva Parish Church in Miagao, Iloilo on December 11, 1993.
world knowledge.Details: The church was featured in a scene in the 1993 romance film Saan Ka Man Naroroon, which was shot in Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur.

world knowledge.Name: Guarujá
world knowledge.Location: São Paulo state, Metropolitan Region of the Baixada Santista
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Guarujá, derived from the Tupi term 'agûarausá' meaning a type of crab, was founded on 2 September 1893. It is located on Santo Amaro Island and is known for its urbanized population and seasonal tourism. The city's name means 'narrow path' in Tupi language.

Major_Events.Description: Guarujá was founded on 2 September 1893.
The city celebrated its anniversary on 30 June 1934.
The Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team used Guarujá as their base during the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Guarujá is culturally significant as a popular weekend destination for families from São Paulo, known for its 27 beaches and nicknamed 'The Pearl of the Atlantic'. Its economy is driven by tourism and port-related activities.
Notable_Visitors: Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team
world knowledge.Details: Guarujá has 27 beaches, including Guaiúba, Tombo, Astúrias, Pitangueiras, Enseada, Pernambuco, Perequê, São Pedro, Tijucopava, Iporanga, Praia Branca, and Praia Preta. The city is twinned with several locations and is served by the Santos Air Force Base. Charles Oliveira, the former UFC lightweight champion, was born and raised in Guarujá. The city will be served by the Guarujá Civil Metropolitan Aerodrome in the future.

world knowledge.Name: Jay Prakash Narayan Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jay Prakash Narayan Airport is a domestic airport serving Patna, the capital of Bihar, India. It is named after the independence activist and political leader, Jayprakash Narayan. The airport is undergoing an ambitious expansion project to modernize and increase its capacity due to rising passenger traffic.

Major_Events.Description: The airport's international air service to Nepal was closed after the hijacking of Indian Airlines Flight 814, which was taken to Kandahar.
Construction of a new terminal began to accommodate the increasing passenger traffic and modernize the airport infrastructure.
The airport introduced the Digi Yatra facility to enable seamless check-in experiences for passengers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new terminal's interior design is inspired by Madhubani art and the ruins of Nalanda University. The design was created by Meinhardt and executed by Nagarjuna Construction Company Limited (NCC).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Jayprakash Narayan, a prominent independence activist and political leader. The new terminal's design reflects Bihar's cultural heritage through Madhubani art and Nalanda University's historical significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Domestic airport serving Patna and surrounding regions.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is the 14th busiest in India and handles over 4 million passengers annually. The new terminal, expected to be completed by May 2025, will have five aerobridges and the capacity to serve over 8 million passengers per year. The existing terminal will be demolished once the new terminal becomes operational. The airport is also planning to develop a civil enclave at Bihta Air Force Station to cater to larger aircraft.

world knowledge.Name: Swanage Pier
world knowledge.Address: Swanage Bay, Swanage, Dorset, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Swanage Pier is a Victorian pier built in 1895 for passenger ship services. It was constructed to serve the growing need for passenger steamers introduced by local businessman George Burt in 1874. The pier saw regular steamer services until 1966, after which it fell into disrepair. It was awarded Grade II listed status in 1976 and underwent major restoration by the Swanage Pier Trust, reopening in 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The pier was officially opened for traffic on 29 March 1897.
The pier was awarded Grade II listed status.
The pier was reopened after major restoration work by the Swanage Pier Trust.
The restored pier was awarded the Pier of The Year award by the National Piers Society.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian pier with ironwork fittings and timber piles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Swanage Pier is culturally significant as a historic Victorian pier that has been restored and continues to serve as a popular tourist attraction, diving site, and location for marine conservation activities.
world knowledge.Details: The pier hosts a diving school, small-scale ferry services, and an exhibition with an aquarium showcasing local marine life. It receives over 100,000 visitors annually and has been used as a filming location, including for the BBC's adaptation of 'Howards End' (2017).

world knowledge.Name: Hocking Hills State Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hocking Hills State Park is a state park in the Hocking Hills region of Hocking County, Ohio, United States. The area was formed over 330 million years ago, originally covered by the Atlantic Ocean. The landscape was shaped by the Appalachian Mountains and later by glacial activity. The park was established in 1924 and has since become a popular destination for hiking and nature exploration.

Major_Events.Description: Hocking County was created in Ohio.
Allowed the state to purchase the first parcel of land in Hocking Hills around Old Man's Cave.
Hocking Hills State Park was officially established.
Reforestation work was carried out by the Civilian Conservation Corp and inmates from the Hocking Honor Camp.
Hocking Hills State Park Lodge and Conference Center opened, offering 81 guest rooms and other amenities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features natural rock formations, waterfalls, and recess caves formed by geological processes. The landscape includes Black Hand Sandstone formations, gorges, and hemlock forests.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant for its natural beauty, geological history, and recreational opportunities. It is also notable for its influence on Jeff Smith's comic book series Bone, which was inspired by the park's landscapes.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains over 25 miles (40 km) of hiking trails, seven separate hiking areas (Ash Cave, Cantwell Cliffs, Cedar Falls, Conkle's Hollow, Old Man's Cave, Rock House, and Hemlock Bridge Trail to Whispering Cave), and offers camping facilities, a lodge, and cabins. The area is popular with tourists and features many private inns, campgrounds, and other attractions. Rare plants and wildlife can be found in the park.

world knowledge.Name: Champ de Mars
world knowledge.Address: 7th arrondissement, between the Eiffel Tower and the École Militaire
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally part of the Grenelle area used for market gardening, the Champ de Mars was transformed into a military drilling ground in 1765 with the construction of the École Militaire. It has since hosted numerous historical events, including the first hydrogen-filled balloon launch in 1783, French Revolution festivals, and several Expositions Universelles.

Major_Events.Description: Jacques Charles and the Robert brothers launched the world's first hydrogen-filled balloon from the Champ de Mars.
The first Bastille Day celebration was held on the Champ de Mars.

Major_Events.Event: Massacre on the Champ de Mars
Major_Events.Description: A massacre occurred during a demonstration against the monarchy.
A massive 'Altar of the Nation' was built for this festival, regarded as the most successful of its type in the Revolution.
Napoleon swore to uphold the Charter of 1815 during this ceremony.
An international art exhibition promoting peace, love, tolerance, and international understanding.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a leveled ground surrounded by a large ditch, an avenue of elms, and a fine grille-work fence. The Isle of Swans was attached to the shore for symmetry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Champ de Mars is culturally significant as a site of major historical events, including the French Revolution and several World Expositions. It is also a popular public space in Paris, known for its proximity to the Eiffel Tower.
world knowledge.Details: The Champ de Mars contains a basketball court and a football field. It was used as a filming location for the 1985 James Bond film 'A View to a Kill.' For the 2024 Summer Olympics and Paralympics, a temporary stadium was erected to host beach volleyball and blind football tournaments. The Grand Palais Éphémère was built in 2021 to host Olympic events and conventions.

world knowledge.Name: Archaeological Museum of Durrës
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Archaeological Museum of Durrës, established in 1951, is the largest archaeological museum in Albania. It is located near the beach and north of the museum are the 6th-century Byzantine walls, constructed after the Visigoth invasion of 481. The museum was seriously damaged and looted during the 1997 rebellion in Albania. It underwent a total reconstruction in 2010 and was reopened by Prime Minister Edi Rama on March 20, 2015, after four years of closure.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was seriously damaged and looted during the rebellion.
The museum was reopened by Prime Minister Edi Rama on March 20, 2015, after four years of closure.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses 3204 artifacts found in the nearby ancient site of Dyrrhachium, including an extensive collection from the Ancient Greek, Hellenistic, and Roman periods. Notable items include Roman funeral steles, stone sarcophagi, and a collection of miniature busts of Venus, reflecting Durrës's historical significance as a center of worship for the goddess.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is open from 9 am to 3 pm every day of the week, except Monday. It is operated by the Regional Directorate of Durrës Monuments and supported by the Albanian Institute of Archaeology and the Academy of Sciences. Plans are in place to make it a national museum due to the historical significance of its artifacts. The museum faces challenges due to its location near the sea, including erosion from the iodine content of salt and moisture and weathering.

world knowledge.Name: Richmond River Light
world knowledge.Address: Ballina Head, Ballina, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Richmond River Light, also known as Ballina Head Light or Ballina Light, was established with a temporary light in 1866. The current lighthouse was built in 1879 and lit in 1880. It was designed by James Barnet and is one of five similar lighthouses he designed. The lighthouse was automated in 1920 and electrified in the 1960s. It has undergone several modifications, including the demolition of its annexe and porch in 1940.

Major_Events.Description: A temporary light was installed at Ballina Head to guide ships into the Richmond River.
The current lighthouse was built and lit, designed by James Barnet.
The lighthouse was converted to acetylene gas and automated.
The annexe and porch connected to the lighthouse were demolished.
The lighthouse was electrified, and the light source was upgraded.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a cylindrical stone tower with a balcony and lantern, painted white. It is 25 feet (7.6 m) tall, with walls tapering from 19 inches (480 mm) at the bottom to 14 inches (360 mm) at the top. The tower has an oversailing bluestone platform supported by twelve bluestone corbels, topped by a metal dome housing the optical apparatus. Originally, it had a porch and a rectangular annexe, which were demolished in 1940.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Richmond River Light is a historic lighthouse that played a crucial role in guiding ships into the Richmond River. It is one of five similar lighthouses designed by James Barnet and is listed under the North Coast Regional Environmental Plan 1988 and the Ballina Local Environmental Plan 1987. It was also previously listed on the Register of National Estate held by the Australian Heritage Commission.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To serve as a navigational aid for ships entering the Richmond River.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is currently operated by Transport for NSW and managed by the New South Wales Department of Lands. The site is open to the public, but the tower is closed. The light characteristic is four white flashes every 16 seconds, with a range of 14 nautical miles (26 km; 16 mi). The current light source is a 28,000 cd, 1,000 Watt 120 Volt tungsten-halogen lamp, powered by mains electricity with a battery standby.

world knowledge.Name: La Fortaleza
world knowledge.Location: Old San Juan, San Juan, Puerto Rico
world knowledge.Address: 63 Calle Fortaleza, San Juan, Puerto Rico 00901
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Fortaleza, also known as the Palacio de Santa Catalina, is the official residence and workplace of the governor of Puerto Rico. It has served as the governor’s residence since the 16th century, making it the oldest executive mansion in continuous use in the New World. Built from 1533 to 1540 by orders of King Charles I of Spain, the structure was the first fortification constructed by the Spanish on San Juan Islet to defend San Juan Bay. It was designated a World Heritage Site in 1983.

Major_Events.Description: An attempt by a few nationalists to enter La Fortaleza intending to attack then-governor Luis Muñoz Marín. The 5-minute shootout resulted in four Nationalists dead and three guards seriously injured.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as United States National Historic Landmark

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Fortification, Spanish Renaissance, Neoclassical. The complex consists of a few attached buildings with formal living quarters on the second floor and private quarters on the third. It has two towers: the Astral Tower and the Homenaje Tower (Homage Tower). The Homage Tower houses the Santa Catalina Chapel with a colorful mosaic of 95,000 pieces in honor of the Holy Trinity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: La Fortaleza is culturally and historically important as the oldest executive mansion in continuous use in the Americas. It has served as the residence of the Governor of Puerto Rico since the 16th century and has been designated a World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: La Fortaleza has two towers: the Astral Tower and the Homenaje Tower (Homage Tower), which show that it was originally a military structure. The Homage Tower houses the Santa Catalina Chapel, where a colorful mosaic of 95,000 pieces in honor of the Holy Trinity stands out. In 1956, what could be the old kitchen of La Fortaleza was discovered in the Austral Tower. The paintings exhibited at La Fortaleza are on loan from the Institute of Puerto Rican Historical Culture and are changed according to the taste of the ruler of the day. Originally, La Fortaleza was painted salmon red, the characteristic color of the island's military installations of the time of Spanish colony. Its wooden doors were green and its columns were painted white with gold details. Three flags fly over La Fortaleza: the Puerto Rican flag, the American flag, and the Governor's white flag. The Hundido Garden was named Doña Inés Garden in honor of Doña Inés Mendoza, wife of former governor Luis Muñoz Marín, because that was her favorite spot at La Fortaleza, where she lived for 16 years.

world knowledge.Name: Kingston Maurward House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kingston Maurward House is a Grade I listed Georgian English country house. There has been a manor house at Kingston since the late 14th century, replaced in the late 16th century with a manor house which is still in the grounds. The present mansion was built by George Pitt (1663-1735) of Stratfield Saye House, cousin of William Pitt the Elder, between 1717 and 1720 on the estate brought to him by his second wife Lora, daughter of Audley Grey. The mansion was originally in red brick but was later clad in Portland limestone after derogatory comments from King George III.

Major_Events.Description: The house was flooded after a pipe burst above the main hall. Consultants discovered the room had been redecorated, leading to a restoration to its original form.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Georgian-style mansion with a projecting central section, originally built in red brick but later clad in Portland limestone. The building faces south, and the north facade is similar in design with the addition of a 20th-century porch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The house is a Grade I listed building, and its gardens are Grade II* listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. It represents Georgian architecture and has historical ties to notable figures like George Pitt and King George III.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Used by Kingston Maurward College for educational purposes and private functions.
world knowledge.Details: The grounds of Kingston Maurward are open to the public and include farm areas and extensive gardens. The house and grounds are owned by Kingston Maurward College. Also in the grounds is Kingston Maurward Manor House, built in 1590, which is now a private residence.

world knowledge.Name: Cathedral of Saint Demetrius
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of Saint Demetrius was finished in 1197 during the reign of Grand Prince Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir-Suzdal, dedicated to Saint Demetrius of Thessaloniki. It is part of the White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal and was included in the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1992. The cathedral has undergone several renovations, the most extensive in 1832, and is now part of the Vladimir-Suzdal open-air museum.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was completed under the reign of Grand Prince Vsevolod the Big Nest.
The cathedral underwent significant renovation, including the removal of structures connecting it to the palace and replacement of some exterior blocks.
The cathedral was included on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is made from local white limestone blocks, cubic in form with four interior columns supporting the drum and cupola. The exterior walls are divided into three bays with zakomara at the top, separated by a horizontal arcade frieze. The cathedral features extensive shallow relief carvings covering the upper half of the exterior walls, influenced by Bogolyubovo, Balkan, and Armenian churches. The carvings include animals, plants, figures, and ornamental patterns, with figural scenes in each zakomara.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is culturally significant as it reinforces the authority of the prince by linking it to ancient kings, biblical figures, and military leaders through its iconographic program. It is also an important example of 12th-century Russian architecture and artistry.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral was originally connected to Vsevolod’s palace and was for his personal use. The interior features a few surviving frescoes from the late 12th century, with the best work likely done by Byzantine masters. The icon of the Virgin of Vladimir, located in the nearby Cathedral of Dormition, may have inspired the frescoes.

world knowledge.Name: Ushenish Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ushenish Lighthouse is an active lighthouse in South Uist, Outer Hebrides, Scotland. It was designed by engineers David and Thomas Stevenson and established in 1857. It incorporated a new 'condensing' apparatus developed by Thomas Stevenson as an improvement to the dioptric system. The lighthouse was automated in 1970, one of the first major automatic lights. The gas-operated Dalen beacon was monitored from Neist Point Lighthouse, on Skye.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was automated, one of the first major automatic lights.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 12 metres (39 ft) cylindrical masonry tower with balcony and lantern, white tower, black lantern, ochre trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is significant for its early adoption of automation and its innovative 'condensing' apparatus developed by Thomas Stevenson.

world knowledge.Name: The Concourse, Chatswood
world knowledge.Address: 409 Victoria Avenue, Chatswood, New South Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The site originally housed the first Willoughby Town Hall built in 1903, which also functioned as the Council Chambers. It was shared with the Council Pound, the School of Arts, and the Ku-ring-gai Masonic Lodge. In 1967, a three-storey administration building was constructed, with a fourth floor added in 1980. The current cultural complex was built after demolishing the old structures.

Major_Events.Description: The Concourse was officially opened on 17 September 2011 by then Governor of New South Wales Marie Bashir and mayor of Willoughby, Pat Reilly.
Production by Willoughby Theatre Company.
Hosted at The Concourse.
Production by Willoughby Theatre Company.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Francis-Jones Morehen Thorp architects, the complex includes a public open space, a 500-seat theatre, rehearsal spaces, a 1,000-seat concert hall, cafés, retail and commercial outlets, a boutique hotel, and a multi-purpose exhibition hall. It also features car parking over two basement levels and a 5,000 m3 stormwater detention tank as part of an integrated water management system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Concourse serves as a major cultural hub in Chatswood, hosting a wide range of events from musicals to corporate events. It includes facilities like Chatswood Library and Art Space, which promote local art and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural centre hosting performances, exhibitions, and community events.
world knowledge.Details: The Concourse features Art Space, a 92 m2 exhibition space for local artists and collectives, and Chatswood Library, which is over 5,000 m2 in size. The library includes custom lighting designed by KLIK Systems. The complex cost approximately $162 million to construct.

world knowledge.Name: Château de la Roche-Jagu
world knowledge.Address: Ploezal, Côtes-d'Armor, Brittany, France, near Pontrieux
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de la Roche-Jagu is a 15th-century fortified house built to monitor and control movement on the river Trieux. It was classified as a historical monument in 1930 and has been owned by the Council of the department of the Côtes-d'Armor since 1958, following a bequest by Viscount Gaetan d'Ales. The château was restored in 1968 and now serves as a cultural and public event space.

Major_Events.Description: The château was restored by the Council of the department of the Côtes-d'Armor.
A storm devastated the park, leading to restoration efforts led by landscape gardener Bertrand Paulet.
The gardens were designated as Remarkable Gardens for their medieval-inspired design.
The park was designated as an Écojardin for its ecological management and respect for biodiversity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The château is a single building with a fortified design, featuring a walkway overlooking the river for defense, stone mullioned windows on the first floor, and a reworked roof on higher floors. The ground floor kitchen remains in its original medieval state. The entrance is through a door surmounted by a niche.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The château is historically significant for its role in controlling river traffic and as a well-preserved example of a 15th-century fortified house. It now serves as a cultural hub with exhibitions, concerts, and public events. The gardens are recognized for their design and ecological management.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural exhibitions, public events, and park management
world knowledge.Details: The 30-hectare park includes themed walkways, a 350-year-old oak tree, medieval-inspired gardens, a camellia collection, and sculptures. The park and gardens are free to visit, and nature workshops are organized. The château hosts guided visits and themed exhibitions, such as the 2006 flax exhibition and the 2018 spices exhibition.

world knowledge.Name: Greenville County Museum of Art
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Greenville County Museum of Art (GCMA) is an art museum located in Greenville, South Carolina. Its collections focus mainly on American art. In 1963, the South Carolina General Assembly established the Greenville County Museum Commission. The art association acquired its first permanent home with the purchase of the Gassaway Mansion in 1958. In 1974 GCMA moved into its modernist building. The museum is nationally known for three collections: the Southern Collection, a survey of American art using southern-related examples; Andrew Wyeth: The Greenville Collection; and a collection of contemporary art unrivaled in the state.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Greenville County Museum Commission
Major_Events.Description: The South Carolina General Assembly established the Greenville County Museum Commission.
The art association acquired its first permanent home with the purchase of the Gassaway Mansion.
GCMA moved into its modernist building, which is almost 90,000 square feet.
The museum deaccessioned the Alma Thomas painting Alma's Flower Garden, selling it in a private transaction to an unidentified buyer for $2.8 million, sparking controversy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modernist building with spacious exhibition galleries, a museum shop, art storage, a 190-seat auditorium, and classrooms for studio instruction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is nationally known for its collections of American art, particularly the Southern Collection, Andrew Wyeth: The Greenville Collection, and a collection of contemporary art. It holds the largest and most complete collection of Wyeth watercolors owned by any public museum in the world.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's “Southern Collection” explores the breadth of American art and history through the Southern experience from the colonial era to the present. The GCMA is home to an important collection of modernist works by South Carolina native African-American artist William H. Johnson. The museum boasts individual works by such twentieth-century masters as George Bellows, Mary Cassatt, Josef Albers, and Philip Guston. The collection includes 117 works by Jasper Johns, 77 by Stephen Scott Young, and 88 by Andrew Wyeth. By virtue of a tax millage, GCMA operations are supported by Greenville County, while program support comes from private sources. The Greenville County Museum of Art is open Wednesday through Sunday.

world knowledge.Name: Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium is a football stadium in Seville, Spain, named after the club's former president, Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. It replaced the Estadio de Nervión and was inaugurated on 7 September 1958. The stadium was expanded over the years, reaching a maximum capacity of 77,000 spectators before being reduced to its current capacity of 42,714 seats after renovations in the mid-1990s. The land for the stadium was acquired in 1937, and the first stone was laid in 1956.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the semi-final match between West Germany and France.
The final match between Steaua București and Barcelona was held here.
The final match between Eintracht Frankfurt and Rangers took place at this stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was designed by architects James Cox and Manuel Muñoz Monasterio. It features an all-seater configuration with a grass surface and has undergone several renovations, including in 1996 and 2017.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Sevilla FC and for hosting major football events, including the 1982 FIFA World Cup and UEFA finals. It is also known for the legend that the Spain national team has never lost an international match here.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is nicknamed 'La Bombonera' or 'La Bombonera de Nervión' due to its location in the Nervión neighborhood. In May 2018, the club announced plans to expand the stadium's capacity to 47,000 seats.

world knowledge.Name: New Cathedral of Salamanca
world knowledge.Physical_Area: One of the largest cathedrals in Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The New Cathedral of Salamanca, officially known as the Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, was constructed to accommodate the growing population of Salamanca, particularly due to the influence of the University. It was built alongside the Old Cathedral, which was preserved despite initial plans to demolish it. The construction spanned from 1513 to 1733, incorporating Late Gothic, Plateresque, and Baroque styles. The cathedral was commissioned by Ferdinand V of Castile and designed by architects Antón Egas and Alonso Rodríguez. It suffered damage from the Lisbon earthquake in 1755, which led to significant repairs, including the reconstruction of the dome and reinforcement of the bell tower.

Major_Events.Description: The earthquake caused significant damage to the cathedral, including cracks and broken stained glass windows. The dome had to be rebuilt, and the bell tower was reinforced.
The cathedral was officially completed after over two centuries of construction, blending Gothic, Plateresque, and Baroque architectural styles.
The cathedral was declared a national monument by royal decree, recognizing its historical and architectural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The New Cathedral of Salamanca is a blend of Late Gothic, Plateresque, and Baroque styles. It features a rectangular plan with three naves and two niche chapels. The cathedral's bell tower stands at 93 meters high, making it one of the tallest in Spain. The interior is characterized by its Gothic uniformity, with flying buttresses and buttresses on the exterior. The cathedral also includes a Baroque dome over the transept and a Neoclassical dome rebuilt after the Lisbon earthquake. The interior is notable for its triforium, replaced by two tribunes running around the perimeter, and the use of star-shaped vaults.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The New Cathedral of Salamanca is culturally significant as one of the last Gothic-style cathedrals built in Spain. It represents the transition from Gothic to Renaissance architecture, retaining much of its Gothic character while incorporating Baroque elements. The cathedral is also important for its historical association with the University of Salamanca and its role as the seat of the diocese of Salamanca. It is a symbol of the city's religious and academic heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The New Cathedral of Salamanca was built without demolishing the Old Cathedral, with the south wall of the new structure resting on the north wall of the old one. The cathedral's construction was influenced by the demographic growth of Salamanca, particularly due to the University. The cathedral features a rich interior with various chapels, altarpieces, and artworks, including the Chapel of San José, the Chapel of the Christ of the Battles, and the Chapel of the Virgin of Solitude. The cathedral also houses two organs and numerous sculptures and paintings, reflecting its artistic and religious importance.

world knowledge.Name: Al-Faw Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al-Faw Palace, also known as the Water Palace, was commissioned in the 1990s by former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to commemorate the Iraqi military’s recapture of the Al-Faw Peninsula during the Iran–Iraq War. The palace features opulent architecture and a surrounding artificial lake, and was reportedly used by Saddam for duck hunting. It was named after al-Faw, a city located in the al-Faw peninsula in the far south-east of Basra. The palace was built in honor of the soldiers who freed the city from Iranian control, and its walls were inscribed with epitaphs celebrating their victory. Despite UN sanctions, 2,000 workers were devoted to the project, including craftsmen from Morocco, Egypt, Sudan, and Iraqi convicts who supplied much of the manual labor. The palace was surrounded by a large moat and luxurious villas, including one built for Saddam's mother.

Major_Events.Description: Iranian units captured the Al-Faw Peninsula.
The Iraqi military succeeded in liberating the Al-Faw Peninsula.
The palace was bombed by an F-16 as a 'show of force' during the invasion.
A ceremony was held to commemorate the end of the Iraq War, and the American flag was lowered with the Iraqi flag left to be flown outside the palace.
The palace was rehabilitated and chosen to be the headquarters for a new university.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the American University of Baghdad
Major_Events.Description: The private American University of Baghdad was opened in al-Faw Palace, offering an American-styled education system.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features Islamic and Neo-Babylonian architectural styles. It is located in the middle of an artificial lake that diverts from the Tigris River, with a large bridge being its only access. The exterior is made of stone and Italian marble, with gold plating in every bathroom. The palace includes an octagonal-shaped rotunda that is three stories large, with 25-foot ceilings and ornate chandeliers. The main door is 10 meters high with vaulted ceilings and marble floors. Saddam's initials are engraved on the walls, columns, and ceilings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Al-Faw Palace is culturally and historically significant as it was built to commemorate the Iraqi military’s recapture of the Al-Faw Peninsula during the Iran–Iraq War. It also served as a symbol of Saddam Hussein's opulence and power. The palace has been used for various purposes over the years, including as a military headquarters and now as the home of the American University of Baghdad.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a palace, now serves as the headquarters for the American University of Baghdad.
world knowledge.Details: The palace contains over 62 rooms and 29 bathrooms. It was the first palace that UN teams entered when searching for weapons of mass destruction, but none were found. After the 2003 invasion, it was used as a prison for Saddam Hussein and later as the headquarters for the Multi-National Force - Iraq (MNF-I) and the Joint Operations Center (JOC). The palace is surrounded by high walls with preconstructed security towers, contributing to its security. The artificial lake surrounding the palace is home to a special breed of large bass dubbed the 'Saddam bass' and large carp. In 2009, comedian Stephen Colbert hosted a week of The Colbert Report from the palace in partnership with United Service Organizations.

world knowledge.Name: Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Unorganized Territory of Fort Snelling, Minnesota, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally Speedway Field in 1919, renamed Wold–Chamberlain Field in 1923, and later Minneapolis–St. Paul Metropolitan Airport/Wold-Chamberlain Field in 1944. Renamed to its current form in 1948. Developed from a race track to a major international airport serving the Twin Cities.

Major_Events.Description: First hangar constructed for airmail services.
Named after World War I pilots Ernest Groves Wold and Cyrus Foss Chamberlain.
Ground broken in 1958, completed in 1962 with 24 gates.
First built in 1986, rebuilt in 2001.
Sound insulation for homes around the airport due to aircraft noise concerns.
Ranked best airport in the US and Canada for traveler satisfaction.
Recognized as the world's most punctual international airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Terminal 1 designed by Lyle George Landstrom of Cerny Associates, featuring bi-level concourses with jet bridges. Terminal 2 designed for charter and low-cost airlines. Expansions include Concourses A, B, C, and G with modern amenities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Major economic driver for the Twin Cities, generating $15.9 billion annually and supporting 87,000 jobs. Key hub for Delta Air Lines and home to Sun Country Airlines. Serves as a joint civil-military airport with significant Air Force and Air National Guard presence.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public/Military international airport serving commercial, cargo, and military flights.

Terminals.Terminal 1: Named after Charles Lindbergh, 131 gates total, international arrivals in Concourse G.
Terminals.Terminal 2: Named after Hubert Humphrey, used for charter and low-cost airlines.

Transportation.Public Transit: Blue Line light rail connects terminals and serves downtown Minneapolis and Mall of America.

world knowledge.Name: Blois Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Blois Cathedral, originally a collegiate church dedicated to Saint Solenne, began construction in the 12th century. The current structure, built in Late Gothic style, was started in 1544. The nave was destroyed in a 1678 storm and reconstructed between 1680-1700. It was elevated to cathedral status in 1697 and dedicated to Saint Louis. The Chapel of Notre-Dame was added in 1860. The cathedral suffered damage during World War II, leading to restoration projects, including new stained-glass windows installed in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The nave was destroyed in a storm and later reconstructed between 1680-1700.
The church was elevated to cathedral status and dedicated to Saint Louis.
American bombardment destroyed most of the cathedral's glass-work.
New stained-glass windows by Jan Dibbets and Jean Mauret were installed as part of a restoration project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is in the Late Gothic style with Neoclassical elements. It features a bell-tower in Renaissance style with Ionic and Corinthian columns, a dome, and a lantern-tower. The west front combines Late Gothic and early Neoclassical styles, with medieval elements like gargoyles and pinnacled buttresses, and Neoclassical elements like a triangular pediment and medallions. The cathedral has a long nave with side aisles, side chapels, a chancel with a pentagonal apse, and an ambulatory. The crypt contains traces of a Carolingian church.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Blois Cathedral is a national heritage site of France (Monument historique) and the seat of the Diocese of Blois. It represents a blend of Late Gothic and Neoclassical architectural styles and holds historical and religious importance. The cathedral's restoration and preservation efforts highlight its cultural value.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral's organ console was gifted by Louis XIV in 1704. The crypt contains tombs of the Bishops of Blois and traces of a Carolingian church. The stained-glass windows cover 33 bays with a combined surface area of over 360m². The bell-tower holds seven bells tuned to C, D, E, F, G, C#, and D#.

world knowledge.Name: Arkansas Agricultural Experiment Station
world knowledge.Location: Fayetteville, Monticello, Jonesboro, Pine Bluff, and various research centers across Arkansas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Arkansas Agricultural Experiment Station (AAES) was established in 1888 with matching federal funding from the Hatch Act of 1887. It is the statewide research component of the University of Arkansas System's Division of Agriculture. The University of Arkansas was established in 1871 under the Morrill Land-Grant Colleges Act of 1862. The College of Agriculture was established in 1905, and the Division of Agriculture was created in 1959 as a separate statewide unit of the University of Arkansas System.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Agricultural Experiment Station
Major_Events.Description: The Arkansas legislature established the Agricultural Experiment Station with matching federal funding from the Hatch Act of 1887.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the College of Agriculture
Major_Events.Description: The College of Agriculture was established due to increased student interest and expanded research programs.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the Arkansas Cooperative Extension Service
Major_Events.Description: The Arkansas Legislature appropriated matching funds to secure Smith-Lever federal funds to create the Arkansas Cooperative Extension Service.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the Division of Agriculture
Major_Events.Description: The U of A Board of Trustees created the Division of Agriculture as a separate statewide unit of the University of Arkansas System.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The AAES is culturally and historically important as it represents the land-grant mission of providing higher education, research, and public service in agriculture. It plays a critical role in advancing agricultural technology, supporting local producers, and addressing environmental and food security issues.
world knowledge.Details: The AAES and Cooperative Extension Service (CES) work together to develop and test new agricultural technology and extend it to the public. Research faculty and staff are based on five university campuses, at five Research and Extension Centers; six research stations and seven specialized units. AAES scientists conduct basic and applied research in major areas such as production and processing of important Arkansas plant and animal commodities, environmental issues, food safety and security, human, family and community development, and human nutrition and health.

world knowledge.Name: Ghibli Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ghibli Park is a theme park based on the movies produced by Studio Ghibli. It was first announced in 2017, with construction starting in 2020, and opened on 1 November 2022. The park is located within the grounds of the Expo 2005 Aichi Commemorative Park, which hosted the World Expo 2005. The area, also known as Moricoro Park, previously hosted two Studio Ghibli exhibitions in 2008 and 2015.

Major_Events.Description: Toshio Suzuki, the producer of several Studio Ghibli movies, announced plans for the theme park, initially focusing on My Neighbor Totoro.
Construction of Ghibli Park began, with plans to open in 2022.
Ghibli Park opened on 1 November 2022 with three initial areas: Ghibli's Grand Warehouse, Hill of Youth, and Dondoko Forest.
The Valley of Witches area opened on 16 March 2024, completing the park's five main themed areas.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features five main themed areas based on Studio Ghibli movies, each with unique designs and attractions. These include recreations of iconic buildings and scenes from the films, such as Satsuki and Mei's house from My Neighbor Totoro, the Air Destroyer Goliath from Castle in the Sky, and a life-sized replica of Howl's Moving Castle. The park emphasizes walkthrough exhibitions and photo opportunities rather than large rides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ghibli Park celebrates the rich legacy of Studio Ghibli's animated films, which are beloved worldwide for their storytelling, artistry, and cultural themes. The park offers fans an immersive experience into the worlds created by Hayao Miyazaki and other Studio Ghibli filmmakers, preserving and promoting their cultural impact.
world knowledge.Details: The park is accessible via Aichikyūhaku-kinen-kōen Station and does not have a private parking lot. It features areas like Ghibli's Grand Warehouse (with a cinema showing exclusive short films), Hill of Youth (based on Howl's Moving Castle and Whisper of the Heart), Dondoko Forest (featuring Satsuki and Mei's house), Mononoke Village (based on Princess Mononoke), and Valley of Witches (inspired by Kiki's Delivery Service and Howl's Moving Castle). The park is designed to be low-impact with no large rides, focusing instead on immersive experiences and photo opportunities.

world knowledge.Name: Kailua, Hawaii
world knowledge.Address: Kailua, Honolulu County, Hawaii, United States, 96734
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 7.77 sq mi (20.13 km²) land, 2.82 sq mi (7.31 km²) water
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kailua was the residential seat of Oʻahu rulers during the reign of King Kākuhihewa and his successors. After the Battle of Nuʻuanu in 1795, the political capital moved to Honolulu. The name 'Kailua' means 'two seas' or 'two currents,' referring to two fishponds or currents in the area.

Major_Events.Description: King Kamehameha the Great defeated the Oʻahu army, leading to the relocation of the political capital from Kailua to Honolulu.
Barack Obama vacationed in Kailua, staying at the Plantation Estate and Oahu Lani, sparking increased tourism interest.
Honolulu County Mayor Rick Blangiardi signed Bill 41 into law, imposing restrictions on short-term rentals to reduce tourist volume.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kailua is culturally significant as a former seat of Oʻahu rulers and home to ancient temple ruins like Ulupo Heiau. It is also known for its beaches, water sports, and as a winter vacation spot for Barack Obama.
world knowledge.Details: Kailua Beach is a top destination for windsurfing, kitesurfing, sea kayaking, and stand-up paddleboarding. The area includes Kawainui Marsh, the largest wetland in Hawaii, and Lanikai Beach, rated one of the world's top beaches. The community has faced tensions over tourism growth, leading to legislative measures like Bill 41.

image_name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire de Narbonne

world knowledge.Name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire de Narbonne
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée d'Art et d'Histoire de Narbonne was established in 1833 through the initiative of Paul Tournal. Its collections were formed from purchases, gifts, bequests, and deposits, rather than a previous collection. The museum is housed in the Palace of the Archbishops, which features important decorative elements from the 17th to the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded by Paul Tournal, beginning its collections through acquisitions and donations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the former archbishops' rooms within the Palace of the Archbishops. The building showcases decorative features from the 17th century to the major restorations of the 19th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is one of Narbonne's two main museums and is particularly known for its ancient faïence collection and remarkable orientalist paintings. It preserves and displays fine and decorative arts, contributing to the cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include ceramics, furniture, miniature paintings, and Limoges enamels. The faïence collections are particularly rich, featuring pieces from the 17th and 18th centuries from Nevers, Moustiers, Marseille, and Rouen.

world knowledge.Name: Travis County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Travis County Courthouse, built in 1931, replaced earlier courthouses from 1855 and 1876. It was expanded in 1958 and 1962. The courthouse was renamed in 2005 to honor Heman Marion Sweatt, a key figure in the Civil Rights Movement. It has served as the center of county government and judicial functions, including housing a jail until 1990.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was completed and opened on June 27, 1931, replacing the previous courthouse.
The jail on the top floors was expanded to additional floors.
Inmates sued over poor conditions, leading to the jail's closure in 1990 after a federal order.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Heman Marion Sweatt Travis County Courthouse
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was renamed in honor of Heman Marion Sweatt, whose civil rights case was heard there.
A $287 million bond proposal for a new courthouse was rejected by voters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse is a six-story steel-and-concrete building clad with cream-colored limestone in the PWA Moderne style. It features symmetrical rectangular forms, recessed vertical window bays, and neoclassical flourishes. The interior has Art Moderne and Art Deco finishes. Designed by Page Brothers, the building was constructed by H.E. Wattinger.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its role in the Civil Rights Movement, particularly the Sweatt v. Painter case, which challenged racial segregation in education. It is also an example of Depression-era public architecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Houses civil and criminal trial courts, county government offices, and judicial functions.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse originally included a jail on the top floors, which was closed in 1990 due to poor conditions. Plans for a new courthouse were rejected in 2015, leading to renovations and the acquisition of a nearby federal courthouse for additional space.

world knowledge.Name: Ponte Conde de Linhares
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1633-34 under the direction of the Viceroy of Portuguese India, Miguel de Noronha, 4th Count of Linhares, after whom it is named. It was designed and built by the Jesuits of the College of St. Paul in Old Goa. The bridge was built on alluvial soil and stabilized with the trunk of the iliadola briformis (Zambo tree), using laterite stone for the superstructure. It was initially built for horse-drawn carriages but has since handled motor vehicles.

Major_Events.Description: The 2014 edition of the Panaji Carnival started at Ribandar-Merces Junction on the causeway.
The bridge was damaged due to continuous tidal motion. Protective measures, including a wall and traffic diversions, were initiated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The causeway is supported by three arches on the eastern side and thirty-eight arches on the western side. Built using laterite stone and stabilized with the trunk of the Zambo tree. Originally designed for horse-drawn carriages but adapted for motor vehicles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the oldest bridges in Goa, it holds historical importance as a feat of Portuguese colonial engineering. It was once considered the longest bridge in the world at the time of its completion. The bridge is also associated with local traditions, including a legend that it was built by Jesuits in a single night using the light of a single lamp.
world knowledge.Details: In the 1980s, mangrove trees were planted on the southern bank to prevent erosion. In 2014, the Government of Goa proposed building a parallel bridge for traffic and adding tourist attractions like food stalls and toy trains on the existing structure. The causeway is maintained by the Goa Public Works Department, which has imposed speed restrictions and diverted heavy vehicle traffic to preserve the structure.

world knowledge.Name: Changsha Huanghua International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Huanghua Town, Changsha County, Changsha, Hunan, China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Terminal 1: 39,000 square metres (420,000 sq ft), Terminal 2: 212,000 m2 (2,280,000 sq ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Changsha Huanghua International Airport was opened in August 1989, replacing Changsha Datuopu Airport, which is now a military air base. From 1957 to 1989, Datuopu Airport served as a dual-use military and civil airport for Changsha. The Hunan Provincial Government proposed the construction of a new airport in October 1984, which was approved by the State Council of China. Construction for Huanghua Airport began in June 1986, and it was opened on 29 August 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The 34,000 m2 (370,000 sq ft) Terminal 1-A, which cost 40.4 million CNY, was opened. The airport was capable of handling 4.6 million passengers per year.
Lengthening of runway 18/36 from 2,600 metres (8,500 ft) to 3,200 metres (10,500 ft) and the addition of Terminal 2 which went into operation in 2011.
China Southern Airlines began service to Frankfurt, Germany on 23 June 2014.

The new 3,800-by-60-metre (12,470 ft × 200 ft) Code-4F runway was built parallel to the current 18/36 runway and lies 380 metres (1,250 ft) to the east. The second runway officially came into use on 30 March 2017.
The renovated Terminal 1 of the Changsha Huanghua International Airport resumed operation on 16 May 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Terminal 2's main building is 39.9-metre (131 ft) tall, 672 metres (2,205 ft) in length and 168 metres (551 ft) in depth, and is the largest single steel-truss structure in Hunan. The terminal has 22 bridge gates, 80 check-in counters, 24 self-checkin kiosks, 24 security checkpoints, and more than 6,390 seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As of 2022, it was the 12th busiest civil airport in China, the second busiest in South Central China after Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport and the busiest in Central China. It serves as a major hub in China and is expected to handle 90 million passengers annually at its ultimate capacity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Changsha, the capital of South Central China’s Hunan province, and the Greater Changsha Metropolitan Region comprising the nearby cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has two terminal buildings. Terminal 1 serves Air China, Chengdu Airlines, Joy Air, Okay Airways, Tibet Airlines, Shandong Airlines, Shenzhen Airlines and Kunming Airlines. Terminal 2 is the fifth largest airport terminal in mainland China. The airport is managed by the Hunan Airport Authority, a publicly owned corporation managing all five airports in Hunan Province.

world knowledge.Name: Pankritio Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pankritio Stadium is a multi-purpose sports stadium completed on 31 December 2003 and officially opened on 11 August 2004. It was built to host matches for the 2004 Summer Olympic football tournament. The stadium's construction began in the late 1980s but was postponed until Greece won the bid for the 2004 Olympics, after which construction resumed in 2001.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted 10 matches, including men's and women's group stage, quarterfinals, and a women's semi-final match.
First Greek Cup Final held in Heraklion since 1931.
Major athletics event hosted at the stadium.
Athletics competition held at the stadium.

Major_Events.Event: Deep Purple and Vasilis Papakonstantinou Concert
Major_Events.Description: Music concert held at the stadium.
Record attendance of 27,950 spectators for a Superleague match.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern sports venue with a capacity of 26,240 seats, featuring a grass field, LED scoreboard, and multi-functional facilities including tracks, gyms, and meeting rooms. Designed by Vassilis Floudas & Associates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the most modern sports venues in Greece, significant for hosting Olympic events and serving as a key football and athletics venue. It also holds cultural importance for hosting concerts and local sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium complex includes two football grounds, an 8-lane track, a 6-lane auxiliary track, indoor gym, swimming pool, and multi-purpose halls. It has faced structural issues with its roof, leading to temporary closures. Renovations in 2025 aim to meet UEFA category standards. The stadium serves as the home ground for Ergotelis and OFI Crete FC, and occasionally hosts Greece national team matches.

world knowledge.Name: Studio Theatre, Łódź
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Studio Theatre in Łódź, built in 1870, is one of the oldest theatres in the city. Initially staging Russian plays due to Russian influence, it faced decline post-World War I but regained prominence after World War II. It became linked with the Leon Schiller National Higher School of Film, Television and Theatre in 1958 and was renamed multiple times, finally becoming the Studio Theatre in 2002. It serves as a venue for student performances and artistic projects.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Theatre of Łódź's Soil
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was renamed and linked with the Leon Schiller National Higher School of Film, Television and Theatre.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Julian Tuwim's Studio Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was renamed in honor of Julian Tuwim.
The theatre officially became the property of the Leon Schiller National Film School.
The theatre won the Golden Mask award for the best play for the spectacle of Sergi Belbel's 'Łoże' directed by Karolina Szymczak.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Studio Theatre is a significant cultural institution in Łódź, historically linked to the Polish Film School and the education of renowned artists like Roman Polański, Andrzej Wajda, and Krzysztof Kieślowski. It continues to be a hub for theatrical education and innovation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre and educational venue for the Leon Schiller National Higher School of Film, Television and Theatre.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has two scenes with capacities of 120 and 60 audience members. It hosts graduation spectacles, independent artistic projects, and festivals such as The Festival of Theatrical Schools and Drama Workshops 'Drama in Progress'.

world knowledge.Name: Porto Santo Airport
world knowledge.Address: Vila Baleira, Porto Santo Island, Madeira
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Porto Santo Airport is an international airport located in Vila Baleira, the capital of Porto Santo Island, Madeira. The island of Porto Santo was the first of the Madeira Islands to obtain an airport. Its runway was built in 1959 with an initial length of 2,000 m. The first aircraft to land at this airport was a TAP Air Portugal Douglas DC-4, on 20 July 1960. The airport's infrastructure has improved over time, with increases to the runway length and in ramp surface. The last improvements were finalized on 28 August 1995, with the inauguration of a new passenger terminal and a new increase in runway length.

Major_Events.Description: A TAP Air Portugal Douglas DC-4 was the first aircraft to land at Porto Santo Airport.
A new passenger terminal was inaugurated, and the runway length was increased to 3,000 m.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a 3,000 m × 45 m asphalt/concrete runway, with VOR and NDB approaches available.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Porto Santo Airport is significant as it was the first airport in the Madeira Islands, facilitating connectivity and economic development for the region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is managed by ANA Aeroportos de Portugal. The Maneuver Aerodrome no 3 (AM3), a Portuguese Air Force forward air base, shares its aeronautical facilities with the Porto Santo Airport. It supports permanent detachments of Squadron 502 (EADS CASA C-295 aircraft) and Squadron 751 (AgustaWestland EH101 helicopters), focusing on search and rescue missions.

world knowledge.Name: Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was named after Birsa Munda, a tribal leader and freedom fighter from Jharkhand. It was constructed for the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup, marking the fourth time India hosted the event and the second time in Odisha. The foundation stone was laid by Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik in February 2021, and it was inaugurated on 5 January 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was one of the two venues for the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup, jointly hosted in Bhubaneswar and Rourkela.
The stadium was inaugurated by Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on 5 January 2023.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: World-class, fully seated hockey-specific stadium with Astro-Turf surface. It is the largest all-seater field hockey stadium in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named after Birsa Munda, a revered tribal freedom fighter, the stadium symbolizes pride for tribal communities and India's hockey legacy. It holds the Guinness World Record for the largest fully seated hockey arena.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hosting international and national field hockey matches.
world knowledge.Details: Officially recognized by Guinness World Records as the largest fully seated hockey arena. Constructed by Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (IDCO) at a cost of ₹260 Crore ($31 million). It has a seating capacity of 20,011 permanent seats and is the fourth-largest field hockey stadium globally.

world knowledge.Name: Medici Chapels
world knowledge.Address: Piazza Madonna degli Aldobrandini, Florence, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Medici Chapels are two chapels built between the 16th and 17th centuries as an extension to the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence. They include the Sagrestia Nuova, designed by Michelangelo, and the larger Cappella dei Principi, a collaboration between the Medici family and architects. The chapels were intended to celebrate the Medici family, patrons of the church and Grand Dukes of Tuscany.

Major_Events.Description: A concealed corridor with drawings by Michelangelo on its walls was discovered under the New Sacristy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Sagrestia Nuova, designed by Michelangelo, features a cubical space surmounted by a dome, with gray pietra serena and whitewashed walls. The Cappella dei Principi is octagonal, surmounted by a tall dome 59 metres high, and entirely covered with marbles inlaid with colored marbles and semi-precious stone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Medici Chapels are culturally significant as they celebrate the Medici family, who were patrons of the church and Grand Dukes of Tuscany. The chapels also showcase the architectural and artistic contributions of Michelangelo and other notable artists of the time.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mausoleum or mortuary chapel for members of the Medici family
world knowledge.Details: The Sagrestia Nuova was the first architectural essay of Michelangelo, intended as a mausoleum for the Medici family. The Cappella dei Principi, designed by Matteo Nigetti, is an opulent expression of court art, featuring six grand sarcophagi and coats of arms of Tuscan cities under Medici control.

world knowledge.Name: La Pedrera, Rocha
world knowledge.Location: Route 10, about 8 kilometres northeast of La Paloma
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Pedrera is a village and resort on the Atlantic Coast in the Rocha Department of Uruguay. Although it has a very small permanent population, in summer it is an important coastal resort.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: La Pedrera is famous for its proximity to the Valle de la Luna, which extends to Santa Isabel de la Pedrera.

Details.Climate: Cfb
Details.Source: Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Uruguay

world knowledge.Name: Ancon Hill
world knowledge.Address: Adjacent to the township of Ancón, Panama City, Panama
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ancon Hill was used for administration of the Panama Canal and was under U.S. jurisdiction as a part of the Panama Canal Zone until being returned to Panama in 1977. It includes the highest point in Panama City and is now a reserve. The hill has been a significant landmark since the pirate Henry Morgan sacked Panama City in 1671, and it became a national symbol in 1906 after Amelia Denis de Icaza wrote her poem about its annexation.

Major_Events.Description: The pirate Henry Morgan sacked Panama City, and his scouts first climbed Ancon Hill to gain knowledge of the local defenses.
Amelia Denis de Icaza wrote a poem about the annexation of Ancon Hill, making it a national symbol.

Major_Events.Event: First ship to transit the Panama Canal
Major_Events.Description: The SS Ancon, named after Ancon Hill, was the first ship to officially transit the Panama Canal.

Major_Events.Event: Return of Ancon Hill to Panama
Major_Events.Description: Ancon Hill was returned to Panama following the 1977 Panama Canal Treaty, and a large Panamanian flag was flown atop the hill.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hill is largely undeveloped and includes a jungle. It contains an abandoned underground bunker, two broadcast towers at the summit, and a small road that reaches them. The lower slopes contained residences and Gorgas Hospital, while higher up were the residence of the Governor of the Canal Zone and Quarry Heights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ancon Hill is culturally significant as a national symbol of Panama, a site of historical events, and a natural reserve within an urban area. It is also associated with the Panama Canal and the country's struggle for sovereignty.
world knowledge.Details: Ancon Hill is a popular jogging and hiking trek, offering views of diverse vegetation and wildlife. It is protected and managed by the Asociación Nacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (ANCON).

world knowledge.Name: Nashville International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1937 as Berry Field, named after Col. Harry S. Berry, the Tennessee administrator for the Works Progress Administration. The current terminal was built in 1987, and the airport took its current name in 1988. It has undergone several expansions and renovations over the years to accommodate growing passenger and flight volumes.

Major_Events.Description: The airport opened with much fanfare, including parades, an air show, and an aerial bombardment display by the 105th Aero Squadron.
The airfield was requisitioned by the United States Army Air Forces Air Transport Command as the headquarters for the 4th Ferrying Command for movement of new aircraft overseas.
The new terminal was completed, featuring three main concourses and a distinctive three-story atrium.
American Airlines closed its hub at Nashville, citing the aftermath of the early 1990s recession and the lack of local passengers.
The terminal underwent extensive renovations, including updates to food and vending services, flight information systems, and baggage-claim areas.
British Airways inaugurated nonstop service to London, restoring transatlantic service for the first time since 1995.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern terminal with three main concourses and a smaller commuter concourse radiating from a distinctive three-story atrium. The runways are made of concrete, and the terminal has undergone several renovations to improve passenger amenities and infrastructure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nashville International Airport is the busiest airport in Tennessee and serves as a major gateway to the Nashville metropolitan area. It has played a significant role in the region's transportation and economic development, including supporting the growth of local industries and businesses.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial and military flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by I-40 and the WeGo Route 18 bus. Future plans include potential light rail connections to downtown Nashville and a station stop for proposed Nashville–Atlanta passenger rail. The airport also hosts Joint Base Berry Field, home to the 118th Wing and the 1/230th Air Cavalry Squadron Tennessee Army National Guard.

world knowledge.Name: Citadel Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Citadel Theatre was founded on October 12, 1965, in a former Salvation Army Citadel on 102 Street. It moved to its current location in 1976. The first production was 'Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?' in 1965. It is the third largest regional theatre in Canada.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre's first production was 'Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?' by Edward Albee.
The Citadel Theatre moved to its current building on Churchill Square, designed by architect Barton Myers.
The Citadel Theatre hosted its first Queer Prom event, which became an annual celebration for LGBTQ+ youth.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Barton Myers, the building features a 'waterfall of glass' with glass panels covering roughly 60% of the exterior. It includes multiple theatres, an art gallery, a lounge, and a restaurant.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Citadel Theatre is a major venue for theatre arts in Edmonton and has been a supportive ally to the LGBTQ+ community. It has staged many productions by queer playwrights and hosted events like Queer Prom.
world knowledge.Details: The Citadel Theatre houses the Maclab, Shoctor, and Rice Theatres, Zeidler Hall, the Tucker Amphitheatre, and the Foote Theatre School. It has been the workplace of three gay Artistic Directors and has produced plays with queer themes such as 'The Glass Menagerie' and 'Kiss of the Spider Woman.'

world knowledge.Name: Bajra Sandhi Monument
world knowledge.Address: In front of the Bali Governor's Office in Denpasar, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bajra Sandhi Monument is a monument to the struggles of the Balinese people throughout history. It represents the long history of struggle of the Balinese people, including the invasion of the Dutch in 1906 and 1908, which saw the deaths of over 1,000 Balinese people, many of whom were civilians. The monument also highlights the introduction of Hinduism and the Majapahit era.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by President Megawati Sukarnoputri on 14 June 2003.
The monument was the 10th pit stop of The Amazing Race 28.
The monument was the Finish Line of The Amazing Race Asia 5.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument is rectangular and follows the architectural principles of the "Tri Mandala." It consists of three parts: the main building (Utama Mandala) with three floors. The ground floor contains administrative rooms, a library, and exhibition halls with a central lake called the Puser Tasik. The first floor contains 33 dioramas focusing on the struggles of the Balinese people. The second floor is a meditative space providing a panoramic view of Denpasar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monument is culturally and historically important as it represents the struggles of the Balinese people, particularly during Dutch colonialism, and highlights the introduction of Hinduism and the Majapahit era.
world knowledge.Details: The monument was built in 1987, completed in 2001, and opened to the public in 2004. It is managed by the Bali Museum and owned by the Bali Government. The structural engineer was Ir. Ida Bagus Yadnya.

world knowledge.Name: Baruva Beach
world knowledge.Location: Baruva, Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Address: Baruva, Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Baruva Beach is one of the oldest beaches in Andhra Pradesh. It was used as a seaport until 1948. A commemorative pillar on the beach marks the sinking of a cargo ship nearby in 1917.

Major_Events.Description: A cargo ship sank near Baruva Beach, and a commemorative pillar was placed on the beach in remembrance of the event.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Baruva Beach is culturally significant as one of the oldest beaches in Andhra Pradesh and a former seaport. It is also referred to as the 'second Goa of India'.
world knowledge.Details: Baruva Beach is situated on the east coast of the Bay of Bengal, approximately 27 kilometers from Palasa. It is known for its historical significance and natural beauty.

world knowledge.Name: Thanh Hóa Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Near Thanh Hóa, Thanh Hóa Province, North Vietnam
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 540 feet (160 m) long, 56 feet (17 m) wide, about 50 feet (15 m) above the river
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built by the French during the colonial era in Vietnam, the Thanh Hóa Bridge was sabotaged by the Viet Minh in 1945. Rebuilt by the Vietnamese starting in 1957, it became a vital link for road and rail traffic in North Vietnam. During the Vietnam War, it was a strategic target for U.S. forces due to its importance in supplying the Viet Cong in South Vietnam. Despite numerous attacks, the bridge was not destroyed until 1972.

Major_Events.Event: First U.S. Air Force and Navy attacks
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was targeted by U.S. forces in Operation Rolling Thunder, but initial attacks failed to destroy it.
The bridge was finally destroyed by U.S. Air Force F-4 Phantoms using laser-guided bombs and U.S. Navy A-7s with conventional bombs.
The bridge was restored after its destruction in 1972.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge was a grey metallic construction resting on a central concrete pier and concrete abutments at each extremity. It allowed the passage of both road and rail traffic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Thanh Hóa Bridge became a symbol of resistance for the North Vietnamese during the Vietnam War. It was nicknamed 'Dragon's Jaw' and was seen as a testament to the Vietnamese people's will to defend their country.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was a strategic target during the Vietnam War due to its role in supplying the Viet Cong in South Vietnam. It withstood hundreds of attacks before being destroyed in 1972. The destruction of the bridge marked a significant moment in the use of precision-guided munitions in modern warfare.

world knowledge.Name: Genoa Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Genoa Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Lawrence, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Genoa, Italy. Consecrated in 1118 by Pope Gelasius II, it was built between the 12th and 14th centuries with later additions. The cathedral features Romanesque and Gothic styles, with significant restorations and additions in the 16th and 17th centuries.
