It has been a central religious and cultural site in Genoa, surviving historical events such as a fire in 1296 and a World War II bombing in 1941.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by Pope Gelasius II.
A fire caused by fights between Guelphs and Ghibellines led to partial restoration and rebuilding.
A British battleship shelled the cathedral, but the bomb did not explode, leaving the structure largely unharmed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral combines Romanesque and Gothic architectural styles. The main facade is Gothic, while the secondary naves and side covers are Romanesque. The bell tower and dome were added in the 16th century. The interior features frescoes, sculptures, and artworks from various periods.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Genoa Cathedral is a significant religious and historical site, serving as the seat of the Archbishop of Genoa. It reflects the city's medieval heritage and its role in the Crusades. The cathedral's survival of historical events, such as the 1941 bombing, adds to its cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral houses a museum, the Museum of the Treasury, which contains valuable artifacts, including the Sacro Catino, believed to be the chalice used by Christ during the Last Supper. The cathedral's art collection includes works by Luca Cambiaso, Barocci, and Lazzaro Tavarone, among others.

image_name: Lithuanian National Opera and Ballet Theatre

world knowledge.Name: Lithuanian National Opera and Ballet Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1920 as Operos vaidykla in Kaunas, Lithuania, the theatre moved to Vilnius in 1948 and to its current building in 1974. It was declared a national institution and renamed the Lithuanian National Opera and Ballet Theatre on 1 July 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The first performance at the theatre, marking its founding.

Major_Events.Event: First ballet performance of Léo Delibes' Coppélia
Major_Events.Description: The first ballet performed at the theatre.
The theatre moved to a new building designed by architect Elena Nijolė Bučiūtė.
The theatre was officially renamed the Lithuanian National Opera and Ballet Theatre.
A major renovation was announced, focusing on modernizing the building's infrastructure and reducing energy consumption.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Elena Nijolė Bučiūtė, the building features modern architecture with a focus on functionality and aesthetics.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is a significant cultural institution in Lithuania, performing both Western repertory works and national operas. It plays a crucial role in promoting Lithuanian culture and arts.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a capacity of 984 seats. It is located in the Old Town of Vilnius. As of 2024, Ms. Laima Vilimienė is the general manager. The theatre performs national operas such as Vytautas Klova's Pilėnai and Bronius Kutavičius' Lokys.

world knowledge.Name: Khrabrovo Airport
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Khrabrovo, 24 kilometers north of Kaliningrad, Russia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Khrabrovo Airport, also known historically as Powunden Airfield, serves Kaliningrad and is located 24 kilometers north of the city. It has a dual role as a civilian airport and a military base. The airport was established in 1922 with the first scheduled international route from Königsberg to Moscow. During World War II, it was used for military purposes. Post-war, it was transferred to the Civil Air Fleet of the USSR in 1945 but continued to host military aircraft. The airport saw significant developments in the 1950s and 1960s, transitioning back to civil air transport. Major upgrades and ownership changes occurred in the 1990s and 2000s, with significant modernization efforts leading up to the 2018 FIFA World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: Joint Russian–German venture Deruluft started flights on the first scheduled international route, from Königsberg (Devau airport) to Moscow.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to Civil Air Fleet of the USSR
Major_Events.Description: After World War II, the airport was transferred to the Civil Air Fleet of the USSR, though military aircraft continued to be based there.
Marked the beginning of operations with Tupolev Tu-134 aircraft.
A new terminal was put into operation as part of preparations for the 2018 FIFA World Cup.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of terminal reconstruction and runway enlargement
Major_Events.Description: The reconstruction of the passenger terminal and the runway enlargement were officially finished on 27 April 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern passenger terminal, a reinforced and lengthened runway, new radiotechnical, lighting, and weather forecast equipment, new aircraft parking spaces, and a high-speed taxiway.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Khrabrovo Airport is significant as the primary airport serving Kaliningrad, a key Russian exclave. Its historical role in international aviation and its continued use as a military base highlight its strategic importance. The airport's modernization for the 2018 FIFA World Cup underscores its role in international events and regional connectivity.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is connected to Kaliningrad Main Bus/Railway Station by bus line No. 244э. It serves both domestic and limited international destinations, with a significant portion still dedicated to military use by the Russian Navy and National Guard.

world knowledge.Name: Madurodam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Madurodam is a miniature park and tourist attraction in The Hague, Netherlands, featuring 1:25 scale model replicas of famous Dutch landmarks, historical cities, and large developments. It was opened in 1952 and named after George Maduro, a Dutch law student and war hero who died in Dachau concentration camp in 1945. The park was funded by George Maduro's parents as a memorial to their son. The park's net proceeds go towards various charities in the Netherlands.

Major_Events.Description: Madurodam was officially opened on 2 July 1952, with Princess Beatrix appointed as its mayor.
Due to declining public interest, Madurodam underwent a large-scale renovation at a cost of €8 million, reopening in April 2012.
The life-sized attraction Hof van Nederland, explaining the beginning of the Netherlands in 1572, was opened on 19 July 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Madurodam features 1:25 scale model replicas of famous Dutch landmarks, historical cities, and large developments. The park is divided into three themes: water, historical cities, and The Netherlands as an inspiration for the world. The miniatures are meticulously researched and constructed, with attention to detail in shape, color, and other properties. The park also includes scaled-down flora and street decorations, with 'residents' that change clothing according to the season.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Madurodam is culturally significant as it showcases Dutch history, architecture, and culture in a miniature form. It serves as a memorial to George Maduro, a war hero, and its net proceeds support various charities in the Netherlands. The park has inspired similar projects worldwide, including Storybook Land at Disneyland and Catalunya en Miniatura in Spain.
world knowledge.Details: Madurodam features interactive elements such as small coin slots that trigger various activities, and chipped cards that visitors use to access video footage and in-depth information. The park also includes a 3D selfie photo booth called Fantasitron, where patrons can have 3D models of themselves created. The park's youth council, composed of The Hague students, plays a role in managing charities supported by Madurodam.

world knowledge.Name: Królikarnia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Królikarnia, meaning 'The Rabbit House', is a historic classicist palace in Warsaw, Poland, originally built as a rabbit warren for King Augustus II the Strong. Constructed between 1782 and 1786 for Charles Thomatis, Count de Valéry, by royal architect Domenico Merlini, it was modeled after the Villa Rotonda in Vicenza, Italy. The palace has served various roles, including a residence for Tadeusz Kosciuszko during the Kościuszko Uprising, and has been rebuilt multiple times after being destroyed by fire in 1879 and by German bombardments during World War II in 1939 and 1945. Since 1965, it has housed the Xawery Dunikowski Museum of Sculpture.

Major_Events.Description: Built for Charles Thomatis by Domenico Merlini.
Tadeusz Kosciuszko resided in the palace.
The palace was partly destroyed by fire and later rebuilt.
The palace was completely destroyed by German bombardments.
Rebuilt to house the Xawery Dunikowski Museum of Sculpture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style, modeled after the Villa Rotonda in Vicenza, Italy.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Królikarnia is culturally significant as a historic palace that has survived multiple destructions and reconstructions, now serving as a museum dedicated to Polish sculptor Xawery Dunikowski. It also plays a role in Polish history, having been a residence for Tadeusz Kosciuszko during the Kościuszko Uprising.
world knowledge.Details: The Królikarnia Park features a sculpture park with exhibits from the National Museum's collections. The museum also organizes temporary exhibits of contemporary art by Polish and foreign artists.

world knowledge.Name: Zhejiang Museum of Natural History
world knowledge.Address: 6 West Lake Cultural Square, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum was founded in 1929 as the West Lake Museum after the West Lake Exposition. It was renamed Zhejiang Museum in 1953 and became an independent natural history museum in 1984. The Hangzhou branch was completed and opened to the public in 2009, and the Anji branch was opened in 2018.

Major_Events.Description: The exposition included departments of aquatic products, plants, animals, insects, precious stones, mining products, and a zoo, leading to the foundation of the West Lake Museum.
After the founding of the People's Republic of China, the museum was renamed.
The natural history department became an independent museum under its current name.
The Hangzhou branch was completed and opened to the public.
The Anji branch was opened in Anji County.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is the provincial natural history museum of Zhejiang province, housing over 200,000 life science and earth science specimens. It provides research and education, preserving and showcasing natural history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural history museum exhibiting specimens and providing research and education.
world knowledge.Details: The museum exhibits specimens of natural history and is home to life science and earth science specimens compromising some 200,000 items at the Hangzhou branch. The museum also provides research and education.

world knowledge.Name: Metz–Nancy–Lorraine Airport
world knowledge.Address: Goin, 16.5 km southeast of Metz, France
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Terminal building: 7500 square metres, Cargo terminal: 3,600 square metres
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Metz–Nancy–Lorraine Airport opened to the public on October 28, 1991, replacing Nancy–Essey and Metz–Frescaty airports. It was a regional hub for DHL from 2000 to 2006. In 2015, it rebranded as 'Lorraine Airport' in English but reverted to its French name 'Lorraine Aéroport' in 2023 due to a court ruling.

Major_Events.Description: The airport opened to the public on October 28, 1991, replacing Nancy–Essey and Metz–Frescaty airports.
The airport rebranded itself as 'Lorraine Airport' in English only.
A court ruled that the rebranding violated the Toubon law, and the airport reverted to its French name 'Lorraine Aéroport'.
The runway was lengthened to 3050 m and refurbished to handle all types of large aircraft.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The terminal building is about 7500 square metres with 14 check-in desks, 2 gates, and 2 luggage claim belts. The cargo terminal is 3,600 square metres. The runway is 3,050 m long and paved.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a key transportation hub for the Lorraine région of France, facilitating travel and commerce. It replaced older airports and has adapted to modern aviation needs.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving Metz and Nancy, France
world knowledge.Details: The airport is open 24/7. It could accommodate up to 500,000 passengers per year and handle up to 60,000 tonnes of freight per year. A shuttle bus to Nancy and Metz meets every departing and arriving flight, costing 8 euros and taking about 30 minutes. Airlines operate regular scheduled and charter flights here.

world knowledge.Name: Matera Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 40 metres (130 ft), Width: 55 metres (180 ft), Height (max): 60 metres (200 ft), Spire(s): one, Spire height: 90 metres (300 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Matera Cathedral, dedicated to the Virgin Mary under the designation of the Madonna della Bruna and to Saint Eustace, was built in the 13th century in Apulian Romanesque style. It stands on the highest point of Matera, replacing the ancient Church of Saint Eustace. Construction began in 1203 when Pope Innocent III elevated Matera to an archdiocese, and it was completed in 1270. The cathedral has undergone several dedications and modifications over the centuries, including Baroque-style interior decorations in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: Pope Innocent III raised Matera to the rank of an archdiocese in union with Acerenza.
The cathedral was completed in 1270.
Pope Urban VI instituted the feast of the Visitation and dedicated the cathedral to Santa Maria della Bruna.

Major_Events.Event: Translation of Saint John of Matera's relics
Major_Events.Description: The relics of Saint John of Matera were translated to the cathedral.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is built in Apulian Romanesque style with a Latin cross ground plan and three naves separated by round arches supported by columns with stone capitals. The west front features a rose window of sixteen rays and a 52-meter-high campanile. The interior received Baroque-style decorations in the 17th and 18th centuries, including gilded stuccoes and frames.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Matera Cathedral is a significant religious and cultural landmark, representing the history and faith of the region. It is dedicated to the Virgin Mary and Saint Eustace, both protectors of the city. The cathedral's architecture and artworks reflect the artistic and religious developments over centuries.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral contains several notable artworks, including an Italo-Byzantine fresco of the Madonna della Bruna and Child, relics of Saint John of Matera, carved wooden choir stalls, a sculptural group of a Pesebre, a painted limestone crib, and a 14th-century fresco depicting the Last Judgment. The high altar features an altarpiece by Fabrizio Santafede depicting The Virgin with Saints.

world knowledge.Name: PowerPark
world knowledge.Historical_Background: PowerPark was founded by Jorma Lillbacka, an entrepreneur and financier from Alahärmä. It has grown into a major amusement park with significant investments and high visitor numbers. It has been rated the best leisure center in Finland multiple times.

Major_Events.Description: The main karting track, resembling an F1 circuit, has hosted the Karting World Championship.
A worker died after being hit by the Typhoon ride while retrieving a shoe. The park was closed early, and crisis aid was provided to workers and customers.
PowerPark was awarded the South Ostrobothnia Tourism Prize.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a large-scale karting track resembling an F1 circuit, a hectare-large indoor track (the largest in Europe), amusement rides, a restaurant, a large hotel, and a camping area with cottages.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: PowerPark is a major leisure and entertainment destination in Finland, recognized as the best leisure center multiple times. It contributes significantly to local tourism and economy.

Details.Operating_Season: May to August (rides area) / throughout the year

world knowledge.Name: Coney Island
world knowledge.Area: Southwestern section of Brooklyn, New York City
world knowledge.Location: New York City, New York, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 4 miles long and 0.5 miles wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally settled by Dutch settlers in the 17th century, Coney Island became a seaside resort by the mid-19th century and later a major amusement area. It has undergone various redevelopment phases and remains a popular entertainment destination.

Major_Events.Description: Luna Park opened as one of the first major amusement parks in Coney Island, featuring exotic landscaping and electric lights.
Dreamland, another major amusement park, burned down and was never rebuilt.
The boardwalk was built to disperse crowds and provide better access to the beach.
Caused significant damage to the amusement parks, aquarium, and businesses in Coney Island.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features a mix of historic and modern amusement rides, including the Wonder Wheel, Cyclone roller coaster, and Parachute Jump. The area also includes the Riegelmann Boardwalk and various entertainment venues.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Coney Island is an iconic symbol of American amusement parks and seaside entertainment. It has played a significant role in the development of roller coasters, sideshows, and other amusement innovations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Entertainment and recreation, including amusement parks, beaches, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: Coney Island is home to two amusement parks, Luna Park and Deno's Wonder Wheel Amusement Park, as well as various rides and attractions. The area hosts annual events such as the Mermaid Parade and the Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest. It is also known for its diverse population and historical significance as a summer resort and amusement destination.

world knowledge.Name: Greenland (amusement park)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The park's predecessor, Mitsui Miike Lake Development Co. Ltd., was founded in 1964 by the Mitsui Miike Coal Mine Group. The project began in July 1966 with the development of a tourism-focused fruit farm, children's playground, boat lake, and hotel. The company merged into the Miike mine's Miike Coal Mine Construction Co., Ltd. in 1976, became independent in 1980, and was renamed "Mitsui Greenland Co., Ltd." in 1990. In 2005, Mitsui Mine sold its shares to the Saibu Gas Group, and the Mitsui name was removed from the park in 2006.

Major_Events.Description: The park's name was shortened from "Mitsui Greenland" to simply "Greenland" after the closure of the Mitsui Miike Coal Mine.
Kyūshū's first rotating swing style ride was developed, costing 500 million yen.
The park announced it would operate with 22 days of closure per year from January 2024 to secure staff holidays and strengthen safety checks.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features 81 rides, including a 105m Ferris wheel "Rainbow", 10 rollercoasters, and trackless trains for travel around the hilly area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Greenland is among the largest amusement parks in Kyūshū and boasts the most attractions of any amusement park in Japan. It is a significant recreational and tourism hub in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park and resort, offering entertainment, rides, and leisure facilities.
world knowledge.Details: The total Greenland Resort has an area of 300 hectares, including the amusement park, a golf course, hotel, onsen, and shopping mall. The park has operated 365 days a year since opening, with closures only due to extreme weather or COVID-19. It is run by Greenland Resort Co. Ltd., a part of the Saibu Gas Holdings Group.

world knowledge.Name: Mahidol University
world knowledge.Location: Salaya, Phaya Thai, Bangkok Noi, Kanchanaburi, Nakhon Sawan, Amnat Charoen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded as part of Siriraj Hospital in 1888, initially as the University of Medical Science in 1943, and renamed in 1969 by King Bhumibol Adulyadej in honor of his father, Prince Mahidol of Songkhla. It has expanded from health sciences to a wide range of academic fields.

Major_Events.Description: Renamed by King Bhumibol Adulyadej in honor of his father, Prince Mahidol of Songkhla.
The Salaya campus was opened on 23 July 1983, becoming the main campus for freshman-year students.
Expanded to Kanchanaburi to offer students more learning opportunities in rural communities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Urban and rural campuses with modern facilities, including the Prince Mahidol Hall, a 2,000-seat multi-purpose hall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Recognized as Thailand's top university, it plays a crucial role in the country's education, research, and development, particularly in health sciences.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Research university offering undergraduate and graduate programs in various fields.
world knowledge.Details: Mahidol University has 17 faculties, six colleges, nine research institutes, and six campuses. It offers a range of academic programs in health sciences, science and technology, and social sciences and humanities. The university has a significant budget for graduate research programs and is part of several international academic networks.

world knowledge.Name: Valley of Love
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valley of Love is a 2015 French film directed by Guillaume Nicloux, starring Gérard Depardieu and Isabelle Huppert. It tells the story of two French people who used to be a couple and had a son 31 years ago. They reunite after the son's death, having received a letter asking them to visit five places in Death Valley, which will make the son reappear.

Major_Events.Description: The film was selected to compete for the Palme d'Or at the 2015 Cannes Film Festival.
The film won the César Award for Best Cinematography at the 41st César Awards.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The film explores themes of loss, reconciliation, and the supernatural, and is significant for its portrayal of the complex emotions surrounding the death of a child.
world knowledge.Details: The film was produced through Les Films du Worso and LGM Cinéma, with co-production support from DD Productions, France 3 Cinéma and Belgium's Scope Pictures. It was pre-bought by Canal+ and received backing from the CNC, Soficinéma, Cinémage, Cofinova and Palatine Etoile Soficas. Filming in California began on 8 September 2014. The film was released in France on 17 June 2015 and in the United States in November 2015.

world knowledge.Name: Uvs Lake
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Uvs Lake is a highly saline lake in an endorheic basin, primarily in Mongolia with a smaller part in Russia. It is the largest lake in Mongolia by surface area, covering 3,350 km² at 759 m above sea level. The lake is a remainder of a huge saline sea that covered a much larger area several thousand years ago.

Major_Events.Description: Lake Uvs and its surrounding wetlands were designated as a Ramsar site on 22 March 2004.

Major_Events.Event: Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The Uvs Lake Basin was listed as a natural World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 2003.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Uvs Lake Basin is one of the largest intact watersheds in Central Asia, containing 40,000 archaeological sites from historically famous nomadic tribes such as the Scythians, the Turks, and the Huns. It is also a transboundary patrimony and one of the largest sites inscribed in the World Heritage List.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural reserve and migratory bird habitat
world knowledge.Details: Uvs Lake has a length of 84 km and a width of 79 km, with an average depth of 6 m. It is fed by several rivers including the Tesiin gol, Kharkhiraa River, and Turuun River. The lake freezes over from October to May and has a salinity of 18.8 per mille. It is home to 29 different species of fish, including the Potanini altai osman. The basin spans the geoclimatic boundary between Siberia and Central Asia, with temperatures ranging from −58 °C in winter to 47 °C in summer. The area is home to 173 bird species and 41 mammal species, including the globally endangered snow leopard, argali, and Asiatic ibex.

world knowledge.Name: Ōhori Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ōhori Park was originally part of a moat for Fukuoka Castle, created by Kuroda Nagamasa by reclaiming part of a cove. The park was later reconstructed by Fukuoka City, modeled on the West Lake of China, and opened in 1929. The area also includes historical ruins from Fukuoka Castle, discovered under the former Heiwadai Stadium.

Major_Events.Description: A fireworks festival is held here every August.
Heiwadai Stadium, which stood near Ōhori Park, was demolished after its closure in 1997. The stadium was home to several NPB franchises and was built over the ruins of Fukuoka Castle.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modeled after the West Lake of China, featuring a large moat and scenic beauty.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ōhori Park is a registered Place of Scenic Beauty in Japan, reflecting historical and cultural importance due to its origins as part of Fukuoka Castle and its reconstruction as a public park.
world knowledge.Details: The Fukuoka Art Museum and the United States Consulate are nearby. The former Heiwadai Stadium, which was located near the park, was home to several baseball teams before its demolition. Archaeological ruins from Fukuoka Castle were discovered under the stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Twelfth Night Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Cintra Road, Bowen Hills, Brisbane, Queensland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Twelfth Night Theatre was founded by Rhoda Mary Felgate as an amateur theatre company in 1936. It started with a small group of actors and staged 21 plays in its first three years. The theatre moved to its current location in Bowen Hills in 1971 after its former building was demolished for the Turbot Street Bypass. The new theatre was designed by Vitaly Gzell and funded by the theatre, the Johnstone family, and the Myer family. The theatre turned professional in an attempt to secure government funding but was eventually sold to the State Government. It is now privately owned by Ken and Gail Wiltshire and remains a significant cultural venue in Brisbane.

Major_Events.Description: Rhoda Mary Felgate founded the Twelfth Night Players as an amateur theatre company to perform important plays with improving amateurs.
The company moved to Wickham Terrace, occupying two floors for rehearsals and teaching.
The company obtained Gowrie Hall on Wickham Terrace, which became their small theatre.
The theatre moved to its current location in Bowen Hills after the demolition of its former building due to the Turbot Street Bypass construction.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Twelfth Night Theatre Club
Major_Events.Description: The theatre club opened with a 12-to-12 liquor license, a first under new provisions, and was notable for granting women equal status at the bar.
The original Twelfth Night Theatre Company folded due to financial difficulties.
An Australian season of Allo Allo was staged, featuring actors from the original British television series.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre was designed by Vitaly Gzell and is part of a cultural enclave that includes the Johnstone Gallery. The complex includes a main theatre and a smaller basement area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Twelfth Night Theatre is a significant cultural landmark in Brisbane, having hosted many notable actors and productions. It played a key role in the theatre history of Queensland and remains the only privately owned theatre in Australia.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has hosted numerous productions, including British comedies and works by Noël Coward. It also ran a successful Junior Theatre Workshop, training many actors. The theatre is currently owned by Ken and Gail Wiltshire and receives no public funding.

world knowledge.Name: White City Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: White City Stadium in London, England, was built for the 1908 Summer Olympics. It hosted a variety of events including the finish of the first modern marathon, swimming, speedway, boxing, show jumping, athletics, stock car racing, concerts, and a match at the 1966 World Cup. The stadium was also a major venue for greyhound racing from 1927 until its closure in 1984. It was demolished in 1985 and the site is now occupied by White City Place.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted various events including the finish of the first modern marathon, swimming, and athletics.
Hosted the premier greyhound racing event until its closure.
Hosted the match between Uruguay and France due to Wembley's unavailability.
The stadium was demolished and the site is now occupied by White City Place.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by engineer J. J. Webster and completed in 10 months by George Wimpey. The stadium had a seating capacity of 68,000, a running track 24 ft wide (7.3 m) and three laps to the mile (536 m), and a 35-foot-wide (11 m), 660-yard (600 m) cycle track. The infield included a swimming and diving pool.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium was a significant venue for the 1908 Summer Olympics, greyhound racing, and various other sports and entertainment events. It played a crucial role in the history of British sports and entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was also used for stock car racing, speedway, and major boxing events. It hosted the second British Empire Games and the fourth Women's World Games in 1934. The site is now occupied by White City Place, formerly BBC White City.

world knowledge.Name: Church of the Holy Rude
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Church of the Holy Rude is the medieval parish church of Stirling, Scotland, founded in 1129 by David I of Scotland. The current structure dates from the 15th century, with additions in the 16th century. It is associated with the Scottish monarchy, hosting royal baptisms and coronations, including the coronation of King James VI in 1567.

Major_Events.Description: King James VI was crowned King of Scots in the church on 29 July 1567. The ceremony was performed by Adam Bothwell, Bishop of Orkney, and John Knox preached a sermon.
During the Wars of the Three Kingdoms, the church and churchyard suffered damage from musket shots fired from Stirling Castle.
The church was restored, and the fine oak beam roof was re-exposed.

Major_Events.Event: Partnership with Stirling District Tourism Ltd
Major_Events.Description: The church announced a partnership with Stirling District Tourism Ltd to promote the site as a tourist destination.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic style with a length of 60.96 m (200 ft 0 in), one spire of 25.91 m (85 ft 0 in) height, and six bells. The church features a semi-octagonal apse that inspired St Leonard's-in-the-Fields Church in Perth.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Church of the Holy Rude is culturally and historically significant as one of the oldest buildings in Stirling, associated with the Scottish monarchy, and one of three churches still in use in Britain that have been the sites of coronations.
world knowledge.Details: The church contains many fine stained glass windows from the late 19th century. The churchyard, dating from the 16th century, includes the Valley Cemetery with statues by Alexander Handyside Ritchie and a unique stone depicting body-snatching.

world knowledge.Name: Versova Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Vesave, Versova was a small fishing village of the Kolis, the oldest inhabitants of Mumbai. It came under Portuguese rule in the late medieval period, during which the Our Lady of Health Church was constructed. The area was later taken over by the Marathas in 1739 and then by the British in 1774. The British established a training facility in 1800, which was later moved due to a fever epidemic. Versova has historically been a center for trade, particularly in dry fish.

Major_Events.Description: Afroz Shah and volunteers initiated a massive clean-up effort, removing over 5,300,000 kilograms of trash from Versova beach over 21 months.
Olive Ridley sea turtles returned to Versova beach for the first time in 20 years to nest, with hatchlings observed heading toward the sea.
Started to help the Koli fishing community with extra income.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Versova is known for its beach and the Versova Fort. The area also features the Our Lady of Health Church, built during Portuguese rule.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Versova is culturally significant as the home of the Kolis, the original inhabitants of Mumbai. The beach clean-up efforts have gained global recognition, and the return of Olive Ridley sea turtles highlights its ecological importance. The Versova Koli Seafood Festival celebrates the local fishing community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential neighborhood and historical site with ecological significance.
world knowledge.Details: Versova beach underwent a massive clean-up effort in 2016, labeled as the largest ever beach clean-up. Afroz Shah, who led the initiative, was honored with the 'Champion of the Earth' award by the United Nations Environment Programme. The area is surrounded by mangroves that support diverse marine life. The native Koli population manages fishing activities through a cooperative society.

world knowledge.Name: Copernicus Science Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Copernicus Science Centre is a science museum located on the bank of the Vistula River in Warsaw, Poland. It was established on 1 June 2005 and opened its first module on 5 November 2010. The centre is the largest institution of its type in Poland and one of the most advanced in Europe. It has been visited by over 8 million people since its opening.

Major_Events.Description: The first module of the Centre building was opened on 5 November 2010 with five galleries.
The planetarium 'The Heavens of Copernicus' opened on 19 June 2011.
Since 2008, the Copernicus Science Centre together with Polish Radio has organized the Science Picnic, Europe's largest outdoor science-popularization event.
The Centre hosted the ECSITE conference, one of the most important events in the field of science centres and museums in the world.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building design was developed by young Polish architects from the firm RAr-2 in Ruda Śląska, who won an architectural competition for the Copernicus Science Centre facility in December 2005, with engineers Buro Happold.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Copernicus Science Centre is a significant cultural institution in Poland, promoting science education and interactive learning. It is one of the most advanced science museums in Europe and has attracted millions of visitors since its opening.
world knowledge.Details: The Copernicus Science Centre contains over 450 interactive exhibits that enable visitors to carry out experiments and discover the laws of science for themselves. It also features a modern planetarium, various laboratories, and organizes numerous events and workshops to popularize science.

world knowledge.Name: Bà Nà Hills
world knowledge.Address: Hòa Vang district, west of the city of Da Nang, South Central Coast of Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bà Nà Hills, originally known as Bà-nà or Pà-nà in the Cham language, was a place of worship for the most important goddess of the Champa tribes before the Islamic era. It was founded in 1919 by French colonists and later expanded by Sun Group. It is located 1,500 meters above sea level, offering views of the East Sea and surrounding mountains.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Ba Na Cable Car
Major_Events.Description: The Ba Na Cable Car, opened on 29 March 2013, holds the world record for 'longest non-stop single track cable car', at 5,801 metres in length.
In 2021, Ba Na Hills added their sixth cable car to the park, made by Doppelmayr and managed by Sun World, Sun Group.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hill station features a mix of colonial and modern architecture, with notable structures like the Golden Bridge and Linh Ứng Temple.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bà Nà Hills is culturally significant as it was originally a place of worship for the Champa tribes and later developed into a major tourist attraction by French colonists and Sun Group. It offers a unique blend of cultural history and modern entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The station is advertised as 'the Da Lat of Danang province' by local tourism authorities. It is located 42 kilometres from Da Nang and features a cooler climate due to its elevation. The latest tourist attraction is the Golden Bridge (Cầu Vàng).

world knowledge.Name: South Colombian University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Universidad Surcolombiana, also known as USCO, is a public, national university based primarily in the city of Neiva, Huila, Colombia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a public and national university, it plays a significant role in higher education in Colombia.
world knowledge.Details: This Colombian university, college, or tertiary institution related article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Pontardawe Arts Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pontardawe Arts Centre is a multi-purpose cultural venue in Pontardawe, Neath Port Talbot, Wales. It was converted from the former Pontardawe Public Hall and Institute, built in 1908 and opened by Adelina Patti. The building had gone out of use and was derelict when a scheme to improve provision for the arts in the town was conceived by Lliw Valley Borough Council in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: The Arts Centre opened in October 1996.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pontardawe Arts Centre is a significant cultural venue in the region, hosting various arts and community events. It also houses Oriel Lliw, a gallery displaying exhibitions by local, national, and international artists.
world knowledge.Details: The building is owned by Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council and receives core funding from the Arts Council of Wales. It is home to the Clydach and District Amateur Operatic Society, Class Act Theatre School, and the Pamela Miller School of Ballet.

world knowledge.Name: Browne Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Browne Park has been the home of rugby football in Central Queensland since 1890. It was named in 1958 in honor of Jack Browne, a long-serving president of Rockhampton Rugby League. The park has undergone several redevelopments, including in 2004 and plans for future upgrades.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted a match of the 2008 Rugby League World Cup, where Tonga beat Scotland in the 7th Place Playoff, attracting a crowd of almost 6,000.

Hosted multiple NRL games, including matches between the Wests Tigers and Cronulla-Sutherland Sharks, and St George Illawarra Dragons and North Queensland Cowboys, as well as an Elimination Final between Parramatta Eels and Newcastle Knights.
A scheduled NRL game between St. George Illawarra Dragons and South Sydney Rabbitohs was cancelled hours before kick-off due to a COVID-19 outbreak.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rectangular football stadium with grass surface, featuring the George Street Grandstand with 614 bucket seats, new lighting towers, and an irrigation system. Future redevelopment plans include a new grandstand seating nearly 4,000 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Considered the spiritual home of rugby league in Central Queensland, Browne Park has hosted significant rugby events and is a central venue for local and regional competitions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium hosting rugby league, rugby union, and soccer matches.
world knowledge.Details: Browne Park has a seating capacity of approximately 5,200, with plans to expand to 10,000 seats. It is owned by the Queensland Government and operated by Rockhampton Leagues Club. The venue has hosted various rugby league events, including junior and senior competitions, and has been a focal point for community and sporting events in Rockhampton.

world knowledge.Name: Świnoujście Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first lighthouse was built in 1828 when the town was part of the Kingdom of Prussia. The current structure dates from 1857. It was damaged during World War II but survived due to the refusal of the German keeper to destroy it. The damage was repaired in 1959, and the lighthouse was restored in 1998–2000 for the new Millennium.

Major_Events.Description: The first lighthouse was built when the town was part of the Kingdom of Prussia.
The current lighthouse structure was built.
The tower was restored to repair spalled brickwork, changing its shape to the current round form.
The tower was damaged during World War II but survived due to the refusal of the German keeper to destroy it.
The damage from World War II was repaired.
The lighthouse was restored and reopened to the public in August 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is built of yellow bricks and is unpainted. The base is octagonal with a gallery, and the tower itself is round with a second gallery and a lantern. It has a cylindrical shape with a balcony and lantern rising from an octagonal prism basement with a balcony.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the fifteenth tallest traditional lighthouse in the world, the tallest brick lighthouse, and the tallest in Poland. It is also an immovable monument in Poland.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse has a 1st order Fresnel lens and emits a white light 4s on, 1s off; red light southwestward. The view from the top gallery is about 45 kilometres (28 mi) in clear weather. There are 300 steps up to the second gallery. The museum and tower are open Monday through Friday.

world knowledge.Name: Cape St. Francis
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Ponta das Quiemadas by Bartolomeu Dias due to fires he spotted while sailing past.

Major_Events.Description: The adjacent village, St Francis Bay, was the site of 'ten-million-to-one' surfing waves seen in the surf/travel documentary.
The landmark was featured in the film starring Scott Eastwood.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Known as one of the best surfing locations due to its geological location, making it susceptible to swell year-round from large low-pressure systems between Antarctica and the southern tip of Africa.
world knowledge.Details: The village is home to the Seal Point Lighthouse and the Irma Booysen Floral Reserve, which hosts many species of flowers and plants. The population demographics include 94.7% White, 3.5% Black African, and 1.8% Coloured, with English (55.6%) and Afrikaans (42.1%) as the primary languages.

world knowledge.Name: Third Bridge over Panama Canal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Atlantic Bridge is the third bridge over the Panama Canal, completed in 2019. It was designed to replace the nearby Panama Canal Ferry and provide a permanent connection between Bolivar Highway and the undeveloped western area.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge and access viaducts commenced in January 2013.
The main span of the bridge was joined into a single span on 6 September 2018.
The bridge was unveiled by Panama President Laurentino Cortizo and Panama Canal Administrator Jorge Quijano on 2 August 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a double-pylon, double-plane, concrete girder, cable-stayed bridge with a main span of 530 metres (1,740 ft) and two side spans of 230 metres (750 ft). It is made of prestressed concrete and has a height of 212.5 m (697 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Atlantic Bridge is significant as it is the only bridge north of the Culebra Cut and provides a vital connection over the Atlantic entrance to the Panama Canal, enhancing local infrastructure and transportation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries four lanes of traffic, pedestrians, and bicycles, serving as a key transportation link.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by HPDI and Louis Berger Group and constructed by Vinci Construction Grands Projets. It was awarded to Vinci Construction for an offer price of US$366 million in 2012. The bridge is also known as Puente Atlántico and is owned by the Panama Canal Authority.

world knowledge.Name: Juneau International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Located seven nautical miles (8 mi, 13 km) northwest of the central business district of Juneau, Alaska
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Juneau International Airport was used by the United States Army Air Forces during World War II as a transport link between combat bases in the Aleutians and airfields in the mainland United States. It also facilitated the transport of Lend-Lease aircraft to the Soviet Union. Over the years, it has been served by various airlines including Pan American World Airways, Pacific Northern Airlines, Western Airlines, and Alaska Airlines.

Major_Events.Description: Used by the United States Army Air Forces as a transport link between combat bases in the Aleutians and airfields in the mainland United States.
The jet age arrived in Juneau during the early 1960s, with Pan Am operating Boeing 707 jetliners and Pacific Northern operating Boeing 720 jets.
Delta Air Lines returned to Juneau offering seasonal and then year-round service, competing with Alaska Air and reducing fares to Seattle by almost half.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 8/26 with an asphalt surface measuring 8,857 by 150 feet (2,700 x 46 m) and one seaplane landing area designated 8W/26W, measuring 4,600 by 150 feet (1,402 x 46 m).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Juneau International Airport is a regional hub for all air travel in Alaska, serving as a critical transportation link for a region with no direct road access. It has played a significant role in both military and civilian aviation history.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is categorized as a primary commercial service (nonhub) airport. It serves as a hub for bush carriers and major U.S. air carriers like Alaska Airlines. Alaska Airlines operates Boeing 737-700 jet freighter cargo flights into Juneau. For the 12-month period ending December 31, 2017, the airport had 108,885 aircraft operations, averaging 298 per day.

world knowledge.Name: Dueodde
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Extends some 30 kilometres (19 mi) almost without interruption
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dueodde was originally a large sandy area. In the eighteenth century, it was planted with pines and grasses to reduce sand drift. During World War II, the German Wehrmacht constructed gun batteries (Bornholm Süd) in the area, which were left unfinished.

Major_Events.Description: Pines, Ammophila, and Leymus grasses were planted to reduce sand drift.
German Wehrmacht constructed gun batteries (Bornholm Süd) but left them unfinished when soldiers were transferred to Norway.
The tallest lighthouse on Bornholm was built, offering panoramic views.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Dueodde Lighthouse is the tallest on the island. The area features vast sand dunes, pine and spruce forests, and salt-tolerant shrubs. The beach has fine white sand and dunes rising up to 12 metres (39 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dueodde is a protected area known for its fine white sand, which has been used for hour glasses. It is a popular tourist destination and features significant natural and historical elements.
world knowledge.Details: Dueodde is the largest beach on Bornholm, reachable by a short walk from the bus stand. The sea water is shallow for about 100 metres (330 ft) before deepening. The beach is crowded in July and August, with boardwalks along the sand. Nearby buildings include Dueodde Vandrerhjem & Campground, Restaurant Granpavillonen, and Dueodde Badehotel. The sand from Dueodde is also sent to Sahara beach on Bornholm.

world knowledge.Name: Moher Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Moher Tower is the stone ruin of an old Napoleonic-era watchtower built in 1808. It stands on Hag's Head, at the southern end of the Cliffs of Moher. The current tower was built close to the site of a much earlier promontory fort, known as Mothar or Moher, which was demolished in 1808 to provide material for the new tower. The tower was built during the Napoleonic Wars as part of a series of towers along Atlantic coasts to counter fears of invasion during Napoleon's reign in Europe.

Major_Events.Description: The earlier fortification, known as Mothar or Moher, was demolished to provide material for the new lookout/signaling tower.
The current tower was built during the Napoleonic Wars as a lookout/signaling tower to counter fears of invasion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a single, nearly square, tower with two rectilinear bartizans protruding from the top of its eastern wall, and one from the western wall. It incorporated a fireplace on at least 2 floors and had a dry stone roof which has since mostly caved in.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower is a historical remnant of the Napoleonic Wars and serves as a refuge for visitors during storms. It is also a habitat for native birds like choughs.
world knowledge.Details: In summer, the tower ruin is occupied by many choughs and similar birds native to the area. The tower is sometimes used as a refuge by visitors to the Cliffs of Moher who become stranded on the southern cliff path during storms that blow in from the Atlantic.

world knowledge.Name: Durgam Cheruvu Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Near Inorbit Mall, Madhapur, Hyderabad, Telangana, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was proposed by the Government of Telangana to ease traffic congestion between Jubilee Hills and Hitech City, reducing travel time from 40-60 minutes to 10 minutes. Originally planned with 3-5 pillars, environmental concerns led to a cable-suspension design with 2 pillars. Construction was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Major_Events.Description: Held on 24 January 2021.
Opened on 25 September 2020 by Telangana Minister K. T. Rama Rao and Minister of State for Home Affairs, Government of India G. Kishan Reddy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Extradosed cable-stayed bridge with 2 pillars, each having 13 cables on each side. The bridge carries 6 lanes (3 lanes each way) and accommodates pedestrians and bicycles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge has become a major tourist attraction and a popular location for Telugu film shoots. It features a floating restaurant and musical fountains.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To ease traffic congestion between Jubilee Hills and Hitech City.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is the longest cable-stayed bridge in Hyderabad. Construction was carried out by L&T (Larson and Toubro) at a cost of ₹184 crore. Since its opening, it has significantly reduced travel time in the area.

world knowledge.Name: Preah Monivong National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Preah Monivong Bokor National Park, established in 1993, is located in the Dâmrei Mountains of southern Cambodia's Kampot Province. It was designated as an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2003. The park includes the abandoned Bokor Hill Station, built by French colonialists in 1921, and a Catholic church from 1928. The park is named after King Sisowath Monivong, who died here in 1941 and ordered the construction of a Buddhist temple in 1924. The park has become a popular tourist destination, featuring the Thansur Bokor Highland Resort, built in 2012, and a 29-meter tall statue of Lok Yeay Mao, constructed in 2010.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Preah Monivong National Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was inaugurated along with most other national parks in Cambodia.
The park was recognized as an ASEAN Heritage Park.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Thansur Bokor Highland Resort
Major_Events.Description: A large luxury hotel was built within the park.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Lok Yeay Mao Statue
Major_Events.Description: A 29-meter tall statue of the mythic heroine Lok Yeay Mao was erected in the park.

Major_Events.Event: Master Plan for Bokor City Development Project
Major_Events.Description: The government announced a plan to develop 18,987 hectares of the park for residents, tourism, and businesses by 2035.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features the abandoned Bokor Hill Station, a remote settlement built by French colonialists in 1921, and a Catholic church from 1928. A Buddhist temple was constructed in 1924 under the order of King Sisowath Monivong.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its historical association with King Sisowath Monivong, the presence of the abandoned Bokor Hill Station, and the Lok Yeay Mao statue, which is a symbol of protection in Cambodian Buddhism. It is also one of two ASEAN Heritage Parks in Cambodia.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located in the Dâmrei Mountains, with most of its area about 1,000 metres above sea level. The highest peak is Phnom Bokor at 1,081 metres. Forest types include dipterocarp, deciduous, tropical evergreen, and mangrove forests. The park is home to various animal species, including elephants, pileated gibbons, gaurs, bantengs, Indian civets, dholes, and Asiatic black bears. Bird life includes chestnut-headed partridges and green peafowls. The park has experienced deforestation, losing about 9% of primary forest between 2001 and 2019.

world knowledge.Name: Bafoussam Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bafoussam Airport serves Bafoussam, the capital of the West Province of Cameroon. It is a public airport operated by the government.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a single runway with the direction 15/33, length of 2,500 meters (8,203 feet), and an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a key transportation hub in the West Province of Cameroon, it facilitates regional connectivity and economic activity.
world knowledge.Details: Bafoussam Airport (IATA: BFX, ICAO: FKKU) is an airport serving Bafoussam, capital of the West Province of Cameroon. This article about an airport in Cameroon is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: King Shaka International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: King Shaka International Airport was conceptualized due to the limitations of Durban International Airport, which had a runway too short for large aircraft like the Boeing 747. The new airport was built to accommodate international and domestic services, replacing Durban International Airport. It opened on May 1, 2010, just before the 2010 FIFA World Cup. The airport was designed by Osmond Lange Architects and Planners and cost approximately R6.8 billion (about US$900 million).

Major_Events.Event: Opening of King Shaka International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport opened its doors to passengers on May 1, 2010, 41 days before the start of the 2010 FIFA World Cup.
On January 27, 2014, an Airbus A380-841 of British Airways landed at KSIA, becoming the first A380 to do so. The aircraft was used for training and operated many flights in and out of the airport.

Major_Events.Event: British Airways direct link to London
Major_Events.Description: British Airways inaugurated a direct link to London's Heathrow Airport in October 2018, which was later suspended due to the COVID-19 pandemic in December 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The passenger terminal is split into two levels: arrivals on the lower floor and departures on the upper floor. It has 72 check-in counters, 18 self-service kiosks, 34 aircraft parking bays, and 16 jet bridges. The terminal is designed to handle 7.5 million passengers per year. The cargo terminal is located to the north of the passenger terminal and has an initial capacity of 150,000 metric tons of cargo per year.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after King Shaka, the leader of the Zulu nation in the early 19th century, reflecting the cultural heritage of the region. It serves as a key transportation hub for Durban and the surrounding areas, facilitating both domestic and international travel.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International and domestic airport serving Durban, South Africa.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is part of the Dube TradePort, which includes a trade zone, cargo terminal, and agricultural export zone. It handles approximately 5 million passengers annually and is the third busiest airport in South Africa. The airport is accessible from the N2 freeway and R102 road, with plans for future rail access. Environmental concerns during construction included the impact on a nearby colony of barn swallows, which was mitigated through studies and radar monitoring.

world knowledge.Name: Ḥa'il Regional Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ha'il International Airport (Arabic: مطار حائل الدولي, IATA: HAS, ICAO: OEHL) is an airport serving Ha'il (also spelled Hail), the capital of the Ha'il Province in Saudi Arabia.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 18/36 with an asphalt surface measuring 3,720 by 45 metres (12,205 ft × 148 ft).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving Ha'il and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport resides at an elevation of 3,331 feet (1,015 m) above mean sea level. Airlines offering regularly scheduled passenger service include international flights offered by non-domestic airlines.

world knowledge.Name: Mekarsari Fruitgarden
world knowledge.Address: Mekarsari Cileungsi, Bogor Regency, West Java, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mekarsari Fruitgarden, or Taman Buah Mekarsari, is a biodiversity conservation center of tropical fruits, from all regions in Indonesia and other parts of the world. It serves as a place of cultivation research, breeding, and propagation of superior seeds, which are then disseminated to farmers and the general public.

Major_Events.Description: The park was temporarily closed for renovation and opened again in February 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes various tourist facilities such as a recreation lake/water park, Baby Zoo, Deer Leopard, Garden Center, Greenhouse Melon, Coconut Outbound, Carrion Flower, Kids Fun Valley, observation tower, Waterfall Building, Pongo show, Three Dimensional trick Art museum, and House of Hobbit.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mekarsari Fruitgarden is significant as a biodiversity conservation center and a hub for agricultural research and education, promoting the cultivation and dissemination of superior tropical fruit seeds.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Biodiversity conservation, agricultural research, and tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The park is about 25 km south of the city center of Jakarta but within the Greater Jakarta metropolitan area. It offers educational shows like the Theater of Science with Professor Durio, focusing on fruit and food themes.

world knowledge.Name: Petnica Science Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Petnica Science Center (PSC) was founded in 1982 as a Yugoslavian scientific center for elementary and high school high-achieving students, for extracurricular activities, supervised by university professors, researchers from various Yugoslav and (mostly) Serbian Institutes, and research assistants and graduate and postgraduate students. It is considered the biggest and probably the oldest such center in South Eastern Europe.

Major_Events.Description: Reconstruction of Petnica's facilities began in 2010, including various upgrades and improvements.

Petnica International (PI) is one of the PSC programs held in English, organized once a year for international participants aged 17 to 21. Students plan and realize real-life scientific projects in one of 15 disciplines. PI takes place in July and August every year and lasts for 15 days.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Petnica Science Center is a significant institution for extracurricular, formal, and informal science education in South Eastern Europe. It has organized over 3000 programs for nearly 50,000 students and science teachers in 15 disciplines of science, technology, and humanities. It plays a crucial role in fostering scientific education and research in the region.
world knowledge.Details: Petnica Science Centre is located in the village Petnica, near Valjevo (Western Serbia). It has fully equipped boarding facilities with 100-bed dormitories and a restaurant, and possesses numerous laboratories, classrooms, a big and multi-functional library with a carefully designed Teaching Resource Center. Students and teachers have access to a rich library with over 40,000 books and journals, and a computer database with thousands of electronic journals and books. PSC has 35 computers dispersed through its facilities, which are accessible 24-hours a day, and laboratories and professional workshops of different types and functions. PSC is a member of the National research and education network - National Academic Internet Network (AMRES), and is connected, by optical cables, to its 10 Gbit/s grid and internet. PSC owns various types of teaching and research-grade equipment used for students' individual projects and research activities.

world knowledge.Name: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally an insect-infested marsh called 'Choushuizi' (smelly waters), it became a racecourse during the late Qing dynasty. Converted into an airport by the Japanese in 1927, it was later controlled by the Soviet Air Forces after WWII and transferred to the Chinese PLA Air Force in 1955. Converted to a civil airport in 1973, it has undergone multiple expansions due to increasing air traffic.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was opened after being converted from a racecourse by the Japanese.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to Chinese PLA Air Force
Major_Events.Description: Control of the airport was transferred from the Soviet Air Forces to the Chinese PLA Air Force.
The military airfield was converted into a small civil airport.
An arsonist set the aircraft on fire, causing it to crash in Bohai Bay, killing everyone on board.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a 3,300-meter runway (class 4E), 135,000 square meters of terminal buildings, 42 aircraft parking places, and 2,600 car parking places. The terminal building covers 71,000 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the busiest airport in Northeast China, it plays a crucial role in regional and international connectivity. Its history reflects the geopolitical changes in the region, from Japanese occupation to Soviet control and eventual Chinese administration.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Dalian and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is a hub for Dalian Airlines and a focus city for China Southern Airlines and Hainan Airlines. Due to capacity constraints, it is being replaced by the new Dalian Jinzhouwan International Airport. It is served by Dalian Metro Line 2 and multiple bus lines.

world knowledge.Name: Curracloe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Curracloe (Irish: Currach Cló, meaning 'marsh of the impression') is a village in County Wexford, Ireland. It is linked to the long and sandy Curracloe Strand (beach) 4 km (2.5 mi) to the east. The area sees an influx of holiday travelers every summer.

Major_Events.Event: Filming of D-Day sequence in Saving Private Ryan
Major_Events.Description: Ballinesker Beach and Curracloe Strand were used for the filming of the D-Day sequence in Saving Private Ryan, due to their similarity to Omaha Beach in Normandy. Filming began on 27 June 1997 and lasted for two months. The village of Curracloe lacked three-phase electricity but was connected when the film company decided to film there.

Major_Events.Event: Filming of Irish beach scene in the movie Brooklyn
Major_Events.Description: Curracloe Strand was also used for the Irish beach scene in the movie Brooklyn.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Curracloe Strand is culturally significant as it was used as a filming location for major films such as Saving Private Ryan and Brooklyn, due to its resemblance to Omaha Beach in Normandy.
world knowledge.Details: Curracloe is located around 8 kilometres (5 mi) northeast of Wexford town, on the R742 road at the junction with the R743 road. It is a popular destination for holiday travelers who stay in bed & breakfast inns, mobile homes, and caravan parks.

world knowledge.Name: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Jiaxing and Ningbo in Zhejiang province
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hangzhou Bay Bridge was the subject of various feasibility studies for over a decade before the final plans were approved in 2003. Construction was completed on June 14, 2007, and it was opened to the public on May 1, 2008. The bridge significantly shortened the travel distance between Ningbo and Shanghai from 400 km to 180 km.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge was completed on June 14, 2007.
An opening ceremony was held on June 26, 2007.
The bridge was opened to the public on May 1, 2008, after a period of testing and evaluation.
The service centre was slightly damaged in a fire on March 23, 2010.
The service centre opened to tourists on December 19, 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a cable-stayed bridge with two separate cable-stayed portions. It was constructed using steel piles instead of concrete piles to resist corrosion from high tidal forces. The bridge features a design that withstands adverse conditions, including high tidal bore forces, earthquakes, and typhoon winds. The towers supporting the tension cables are designed with an outward bend to transfer wind loads effectively.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hangzhou Bay Bridge is a significant engineering feat that has improved transportation and economic connectivity in the region. It has shortened travel time between Ningbo and Shanghai, enhancing the competitiveness of the Beilun Port and facilitating trade in the Yangtze River Delta region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Highway bridge connecting Jiaxing and Ningbo, carrying six lanes of G15 Shenyang–Haikou Expressway and G92 Hangzhou Bay Ring Expressway.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge includes a service centre called 'Land between the Sea and the Sky' in the middle, which features shopping, exhibition, parking, restaurant facilities, a hotel, and a 145.6 m-high lookout tower. The bridge was built in a challenging environment with high tides, typhoons, and difficult sea soil conditions. Engineers used innovative construction techniques, such as low-strength early-stretching technology for box girders and steel pipes to release toxic methane gas discovered underground.

image_name: Smith Center for the Performing Arts

world knowledge.Name: Smith Center for the Performing Arts
world knowledge.Address: 361 Symphony Park Avenue, Las Vegas, Nevada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Smith Center for the Performing Arts is a performing arts center located at Symphony Park in Downtown Las Vegas, Nevada. It was designed in the Neo Art Deco style by David M. Schwarz, echoing the design elements of the Hoover Dam. The center features a 17-story carillon tower containing 47 bells and is the first performing arts center in the nation to be Gold LEED certified. Groundbreaking began on May 26, 2009, and it opened on March 10, 2012. The center was conceived to address the lack of a dedicated performing arts venue in Las Vegas, which was one of the largest cities in the country without one. The project was funded by a $150 million donation from the Donald W. Reynolds Foundation and $105 million in bonds repaid through a car rental fee initiated by Clark County and the State of Nevada.

Major_Events.Description: Groundbreaking for the $470 million complex began on May 26, 2009.
The Smith Center for the Performing Arts opened on March 10, 2012.
In 2010, it was announced that the Lied Discovery Children's Museum would move to the Smith Center, replacing an originally proposed 600-seat theater that was scrapped from the plans in 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Smith Center is designed in the Neo Art Deco style, inspired by the Hoover Dam and featuring elements from the Nebraska State Capitol and Bullocks Wilshire in Los Angeles. The façade is made of white Indiana limestone, and the center includes a 17-story carillon tower with 47 bells. The design incorporates numerous detail elements based on the Hoover Dam and 1920s motifs, including a winged sculpture in the center lobby modeled after the dam's Winged Figures of the Republic statues. The center also features artwork by local artists from the Las Vegas Art Museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Smith Center for the Performing Arts is culturally significant as it provides a dedicated venue for a variety of performances, including international music, dance companies, and Broadway productions. It is the home of the Las Vegas Philharmonic and Nevada Ballet Theatre. The center also fosters arts awareness and aims to revitalize the downtown area. It is the first performing arts center in the nation to be Gold LEED certified.
world knowledge.Details: The Smith Center features three main venues: Reynolds Hall, Myron's Cabaret Jazz, and the Troesh Studio Theater. The center also includes an outdoor park plaza serving as an additional concert venue. The campus includes the new home of the Discovery Children's Museum (formerly Lied Discovery Children's Museum). The center hosts Broadway productions such as Book of Mormon, Wicked, The Lion King, and Hamilton.

world knowledge.Name: Audi Soap Museum
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 17th century (with parts possibly dating back to the 13th century)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The soap workshop was originally built in Sidon by the Hammoud family in the 17th century. During the 19th century (around 1880), the Audi family became the owner and turned it into a family residence. It was abandoned in the 1980s during the Lebanon War. In 1996, the Audi Foundation began restoring the building, and the Soap Museum opened in November 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The Audi Foundation started restoring the abandoned building.
The Soap Museum officially opened to the public.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of gift shop in Beirut
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened a gift shop in Beirut.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building is an old soap factory built in the 17th century, with parts possibly dating back to the 13th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum traces the history of soap making in the Levant, showcasing its development and manufacturing techniques. It also preserves artifacts found during onsite excavations and represents a significant cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The Audi Foundation, headquartered at the Soap Museum, collaborates with Mahmud al-Sharkass and his family to craft luxury soaps sold in the museum's gift shop.

world knowledge.Name: National Archaeological Museum, Athens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Archaeological Museum in Athens was established in 1829 by Ioannis Kapodistrias. It was initially located in Aigina and later moved to various locations until 1858 when an international architectural competition was announced for its current location. The museum's construction began in 1866 and was completed in 1889, funded by the Greek Government, the Greek Archaeological Society, and the society of Mycenae. Major benefactors included Eleni Tositsa, who donated the land, and Demetrios and Nikolaos Vernardakis, who funded its completion. The museum was renamed in 1881 by Prime Minister Charilaos Trikoupis. During World War II, the museum was closed, and its artifacts were buried for protection. It reopened in 1945 and has undergone several expansions and renovations since.

Major_Events.Description: The first national archaeological museum in Greece was established by Ioannis Kapodistrias in Aigina.
An international architectural competition was announced for the location and design of the new museum.
The construction of the museum's building was completed using funds from the Greek Government, the Greek Archaeological Society, and the society of Mycenae.
The museum was closed during World War II, and its artifacts were buried for protection.
The museum reopened under the direction of Christos Karouzos and Semni Karouzou.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and reopening for the Athens Olympics
Major_Events.Description: The museum underwent a major renovation and reopened in time for the Athens Olympics, including aesthetic and technical upgrades.
The Greek government approved plans for a 20,000 square metre underground extension, expected to be completed by 2028.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum has an imposing neo-classical design, popular in Europe at the time, and is in accordance with the classical style artifacts it houses. The initial plan was conceived by Ludwig Lange and later modified by Panagis Kalkos, Armodios Vlachos, and Ernst Ziller. The building features a large neo-classic design garden at the front, decorated with sculptures. The museum has undergone several expansions, including the construction of a new east wing in the early 20th century and a two-storeyed building in the 1930s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Archaeological Museum in Athens is considered one of the greatest museums in the world, housing the richest collection of Greek Antiquity artifacts worldwide. It is a vital repository of Greek cultural heritage, showcasing artifacts from prehistory to late antiquity. The museum's collections include significant finds from various archaeological sites across Greece, making it a cornerstone of Greek history and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections are organized into sections, including prehistoric, Cycladic, Mycenaean, Egyptian, and Stathatos collections. Key highlights include the famous marble figurines from the Aegean islands, golden funerary masks from Mycenae, and the bronze statue of the princess-priestess Takushit. The museum also houses a 118-year-old library of archaeology with rare ancient art, science, and philosophy books. The museum is accessible by the Athens metro, with the nearest station being Victoria Station. It features a gift shop, café, and is fully wheelchair accessible.

world knowledge.Name: Théâtre Marigny
world knowledge.Address: located at the corner of Avenue des Champs-Elysées and Avenue Marigny, 8th arrondissement of Paris
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as a panorama in 1883 by architect Charles Garnier, it was converted into a theatre in 1894 by Édouard Niermans. It became a home for operetta and musical theatre. Over the years, it hosted various troupes and performances, including the Renaud-Barrault company in 1946 and later became a cinema. It was acquired by the Artemis Group in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The panorama was converted into a theatre-in-the-round for summer musical spectacles by Édouard Niermans.
The hall was enlarged and modernized by Volterra, opening with a revival of Monsieur Beaucaire by André Messager.
The Théâtre Marigny welcomed a troupe from the Comédie-Française to form the Renaud-Barrault company.

Major_Events.Event: 20th anniversary celebration of Brigitte Bardot Foundation
Major_Events.Description: François Pinault and his wife put the entire facility at the disposal of the Brigitte Bardot Foundation for its 20th anniversary celebration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed as a panorama by Charles Garnier, later converted into a theatre by Édouard Niermans. The hall was enlarged and modernized in 1925.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Théâtre Marigny has been a significant venue for operetta, musical theatre, and boulevard shows. It has hosted notable performances and troupes, contributing to Paris's cultural and theatrical heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a main hall with a capacity of 1,024 and a smaller Popescu salon with a capacity of 311. It was acquired by the Artemis Group in 2000, with Robert Hossein and later Pierre Lescure as directors.

world knowledge.Name: Eden Beach Puducherry

Major_Events.Description: Certified by the Foundation for Environment Education (FEE), Denmark as one of the eight Indian beaches with the Blue Flag tag

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Known for its white sands, clear waters, and surrounding coconut groves, enhancing its scenic appeal with nearby Chunnambar Backwaters
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Eco-friendly tourism and recreational beach activities
world knowledge.Details: Situated 10 km from Puducherry city, between Paradise Beach and the Arts & Crafts Village. Accessible via Ariyankuppam–Veerampattinam Road with parking facilities. Offers designated swimming zones monitored by lifeguards and follows strict environmental policies under the Blue Flag program.

world knowledge.Name: Granada Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica of the Incarnation is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Granada, Spain, and the seat of the Archdiocese of Granada. It was built on top of the city's main mosque after the reconquest of Granada in 1492. Construction began in 1518 in the center of the old Muslim Medina. The cathedral combines Renaissance and Gothic architectural styles and took 181 years to complete. It features a unique circular capilla mayor and a Renaissance dome with a Gothic floor plan.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the cathedral began on 25 March 1523.
The cathedral was completed on 24 December 1704 after 181 years of construction.
The cathedral was dedicated to the Incarnation on 1 December 1946.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral combines Renaissance and Gothic styles.
