The fire was brought under control by fire crews from the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service with five fire engines and six specialist appliances involved. A faulty heating element within the reptile house is believed to have caused the fire.

Major_Events.Event: Rescue of Yampil the Asiatic black bear
Major_Events.Description: The zoo re-homed Yampil, a 12-year-old Asiatic black bear that was rescued from a zoo in Donetsk province after being injured by shelling during the Russian invasion. Yampil was one of only seven survivors from the nearly 200 animals at the zoo and was discovered by Ukrainian soldiers when they recaptured the area in 2022. The zoo created a £200,000 appeal to fund the construction of a new enclosure for the bear. Yampil died following an anaesthetic procedure in July 2024 during treatment for ongoing health problems.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The zoo is culturally significant for its efforts in animal rescue and conservation, particularly in rehoming animals from conflict zones and other distressing situations. It has gained recognition for its contributions to animal welfare and education.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo originally began as an attraction in the garden centre owned by founders Brian and Shirley Curran. The couple had placed a rabbit enclosure inside the centre to entertain children while their parents shopped. The couple are passionate about animals and began to accept rescued animals for the public and zoos. Early arrivals included a hedgehog, a 28-year-old ring-tailed lemur from Edinburgh Zoo, animals from Gorgie City Farm, wallabies, and an emu that were rescued from an animal sanctuary in Fife, and a number of African spurred tortoises seized by customs inspectors. The zoo's expansion was supported by donations from local supporters and substantial fundraising campaigns, which have funded the construction of new enclosures for larger rescue animals. Notable additions to the zoo include a £150,000 fundraising appeal in 2015 to create a habitat for four male lions rescued from a Belgian circus.

world knowledge.Name: Storstrøm Bridge
world knowledge.Area: Between the islands of Falster and Masnedø
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Storstrøm Bridge is a road and railway arch bridge that crosses Storstrømmen between the islands of Falster and Masnedø in Denmark. It was the main road connection between the islands until the Farø Bridges were opened in 1985. It is still part of the railway connection between the islands of Lolland, Falster, and Zealand. The bridge was designed by the bridge department at the Danish State Railways (DSB), headed by Anker Engelund, and constructed by Dorman, Long & Co. and Christiani & Nielsen. It was opened by King Christian X on 26 September 1937.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened by King Christian X on 26 September 1937, attended by more than 40,000 people.
On 18 October 2011, rail traffic was canceled after a crack in one of the spans was discovered. Further investigation revealed a total of 11 cracks between 17 and 55 cm in length.
The bridge reopened to light rail traffic on 21 November 2011 and to regular rail traffic on 23 January 2012.
Due to the poor condition of the bridge, the Danish government decided to build a new bridge. Parliamentary agreement was reached on 21 March 2013, and the construction act was passed on 26 May 2015.
The groundbreaking ceremony for the new Storstrøm Bridge took place on 27 September 2018.

Architectural_Characteristics.Main_Spans: Three tied-arch main spans with lengths of 103.9 m, 137.8 m, and 103.9 m
Architectural_Characteristics.Approach_Spans: 50 spans with piers spaced alternately 57.8 m and 62.2 m apart
Architectural_Characteristics.Piers: 49 piers of different heights, extending to a maximum water depth of 13.8 metres
Architectural_Characteristics.Foundations: Concrete foundations cast on the excavated bed of the sea, inside a cofferdam

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Storstrøm Bridge is a significant infrastructure project in Denmark, connecting the islands of Falster and Masnedø. It has been a vital part of the railway connection between the islands of Lolland, Falster, and Zealand, and is on the rail line between Copenhagen and Hamburg, Germany. The bridge was also featured in a short documentary by Carl Th. Dreyer, one of Denmark's most famous filmmakers.

Details.Current_Status: Set to be demolished once the new bridge is completed

New_Bridge.Features: Electrified double-tracked railway allowing speeds of 200 km/h, two road lanes allowing 80 km/h, and a foot and bicycle path
New_Bridge.Expected_Completion: Road traffic in 2025 and rail traffic in early 2027

Details.Film_Reference: In 1950, Carl Th. Dreyer made a short documentary about the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Çeşnigir Bridge
world knowledge.Address: between Karakeçili and Köprüköy in Kırıkkale Province, Turkey
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 110 m (360 ft) long, 6 m (20 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Çeşnigir Bridge is a medieval bridge built during the period of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum. Tradition says that the army of Timur passed over the bridge on their way to the Battle of Ankara in 1402. The architect Mimar Sinan supervised its reconstruction as part of preparations for the Egyptian Expedition of Yavuz Sultan Selim. It underwent further repairs during the 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The army of Timur passed over the bridge on their way to the Battle of Ankara.
The bridge was reconstructed under the supervision of architect Mimar Sinan for the Egyptian Expedition of Yavuz Sultan Selim.
The bridge was closed to vehicle traffic due to the rise in water level after the construction of the Kapulukaya Dam.
Restoration work was carried out by the 4th Region Highways Directorate.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is built of cut stone and features 12 arches, nine primary ones and three others to reduce the weight of the abutments. It is a noted example of Seljuk architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Çeşnigir Bridge is a significant example of medieval Seljuk architecture and has historical importance due to its association with Timur's army and the Battle of Ankara.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was open to vehicle traffic until 1989 and is now only open to pedestrians. It was restored in 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Baltrum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Baltrum has existed since the first century BC and AD. It was first mentioned in a document in 1398 as Balteringe. The island has undergone significant changes due to wind and sea conditions, losing land on its west coast while gaining some on the east coast. It was a fief under Duke Albert I of Bavaria and later belonged to the East Frisian chieftains. The island suffered from storm surges and shifting sand dunes, leading to the abandonment of villages. Tourism began in 1876, and it became a seaside health resort in 1966.

Major_Events.Description: Baltrum was mentioned as Balteringe in a document of enfeoffment.
The island was disrupted into several pieces and became mostly uninhabitable, leading to the desertion of the Western village.
Baltrum became a seaside resort, though tourism grew slowly.
Baltrum was approved as a seaside health resort by the state of Germany.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island has two merged villages, Ostdorf and Westdorf, with no official street names but house numbers based on construction dates. The island is protected by groynes, wooden palisades, and revetments. It is a car-free island with transportation mainly by horse-drawn carriages.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Baltrum is the smallest inhabited East Frisian Island and part of the Lower Saxony Wadden Sea National Park. Its name may derive from Old Frisian or the Norse god Baldr. The island's history and unique car-free environment make it culturally significant.
world knowledge.Details: Baltrum is a car-free island with a population of around 500, swelling to 3,500 during summer. It has a ferry terminal, a small airstrip, and is reachable by guided mudflat walks at low tide. The island features attractions like an indoor seawater swimming pool and a miniature golf course. The highest point is a 19.3-meter coastal dune with a viewing platform.

world knowledge.Name: Winchester Mystery House
world knowledge.Address: 525 South Winchester Boulevard, San Jose, CA 95128
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Winchester Mystery House was the personal residence of Sarah Winchester, widow of firearms magnate William Wirt Winchester. The mansion is renowned for its size, architectural curiosities, and the myths surrounding its construction. Sarah Winchester moved to California in 1885 and began expanding the original farmhouse into a sprawling mansion with a maze-like design. The house became a tourist attraction after her death in 1922.

Major_Events.Description: The earthquake severely damaged the mansion, collapsing the seven-story tower and most chimneys, destroying one wing, and leaving doors and staircases leading to nowhere.
The house was designated as a California Historical Landmark (CHISL No. 868).

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The house was added to the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP reference No. 74000559).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian and Gothic-style mansion with Romanesque features. The house features intricate woodwork, art glass windows, Lincrusta wall coverings, and unusual design elements such as doors and staircases leading to nowhere. The mansion includes 160 rooms, 2,000 doors, 10,000 windows, 47 stairways, 47 fireplaces, 13 bathrooms, and 6 kitchens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Winchester Mystery House is culturally significant due to its unique architecture, the legends surrounding Sarah Winchester, and its reputation as a haunted location. It reflects the eccentricities of its owner and the Victorian era's architectural trends.
world knowledge.Details: The house is surrounded by myths, including claims that Sarah Winchester built it to appease the ghosts of those killed by Winchester rifles. However, historical evidence suggests these stories are exaggerated or fabricated. The house is now owned and operated by Winchester Mystery House, LLC, and tours emphasize its mysterious and haunted reputation.

world knowledge.Name: Bahrain Financial Harbour
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bahrain Financial Harbour is a waterfront commercial development project located on the northern shore of Manama, the capital city of Bahrain. Costing $1.5 billion and covering an area of 380,000 square metres, the two main Harbour Towers were officially opened in May 2007. It is now completed and is considered a beacon of human engineering and design. The project was constructed on reclaimed land on the former site of the Manama pier.

Major_Events.Description: The two main Harbour Towers were officially opened in May 2007.

Construction of the rest of the project, including the Bahrain Performance Centre, residential Diamond Tower, and Villamar apartment buildings, was delayed largely due to the Great Recession and the Bahrain uprising.
Construction of the Harbour Heights Towers resumed after being put on hold in 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The project consists of multiple construction phases, including the two tallest twin-towers, Harbour Tower East and Harbour Tower West, which are 260 m (853 ft) tall with 53 floors. The Harbour Mall is a six-storey building housing the Bahrain Stock Exchange and various investment firms. The Harbour Heights Towers are residential skyscrapers with 54, 43, and 52 storeys, featuring apartments, villas, and penthouses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bahrain Financial Harbour is a significant landmark in Bahrain, representing modern engineering and design. It serves as a hub for financial and commercial activities in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The project includes a row of luxury homes alongside a commercial waterfront promenade. Construction of the $150 million project started in 2016 after its building permit was issued.

world knowledge.Name: Saint George Tower, Hilandar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The tower is a medieval defensive structure dedicated to Saint George, located in the Serbian Orthodox Hilandar Monastery. The initial construction phase likely dates to the end of the 12th century by Serbian Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja. The second phase includes the chapel at the top of the tower, which was frescoed around 1260.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Serbian Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja.
Included the addition of the chapel at the top of the tower, which was frescoed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Medieval defensive structure with a chapel at the top. Part of Hilandar's fortress wall, located on the south side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower is a significant part of the Hilandar Monastery, a Serbian Orthodox site, and represents medieval Serbian and Orthodox Christian heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Defensive structure and religious site (dedicated to Saint George).
world knowledge.Details: The tower is one of two towers on Hilandar's fortress wall, the other being the larger Tower of Saint Sava on the eastern side.

world knowledge.Name: Stavropol State Agrarian University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stavropol State Agrarian University is a state institution of higher education in Stavropol, Northern Caucasus. It was originally established in 1930 as a result of the reorganization of the Moscow Zootechnic Institute. Over the years, it underwent several name changes and expansions, including the integration of other institutes and the establishment of various departments. In 1994, it was transformed into the Stavropol State Agricultural Academy and later renamed Stavropol State Agrarian University in 2001.

Major_Events.Description: As a result of Moscow Zootechnic Institute’s reorganization, four education institutions were established, including the precursor to Stavropol State Agrarian University.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Northern Caucasian Zootechnic Institute
Major_Events.Description: Krasnodar Sheep-breeding Institute and Taganrog Institute Department of dairy&meat cattle breeding joined the Institute, leading to its renaming.

Major_Events.Event: Awarded Order of the Red Banner of Labour
Major_Events.Description: The Institute was awarded for its merits in training highly skilled agrarian specialists and implementing scientific achievements into agrarian performance.

Major_Events.Event: Transformed into Stavropol State Agricultural Academy
Major_Events.Description: The State Higher Education Committee decided to transform the Institution into the Stavropol State Agricultural Academy.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Stavropol State Agrarian University
Major_Events.Description: The Academy was renamed as Stavropol State Agrarian University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stavropol State Agrarian University is a significant institution in the Northern Caucasus region, known for its contributions to agricultural education and research. It has played a crucial role in training highly skilled agrarian specialists and implementing scientific achievements into agrarian performance.
world knowledge.Details: The University has the right to perform education activities including 126 programs of HPE (specialist, bachelor, master's degree program), with 18,500 students. Its structure consists of 9 faculties, 51 chairs, 90 innovation labs and centers, techno-park 'UniverAgro', publishing complex 'AGRUS', 32 minor innovation ventures, a horse physical culture school, a vivarium, and a research library. The University has 66 countries-members, 136 strategic partners, and 51 branch chairs on the basis of employers. It is a member of the Great University Charter since 2008.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Gran Canaria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio de Gran Canaria is a football stadium in Las Palmas, Canary Islands, Spain. It was opened in 2003 as a multi-purpose stadium to become the successor of the old Estadio Insular. The stadium was inaugurated on 8 May 2003 with a friendly between UD Las Palmas and Anderlecht. From 11 November 2014, the stadium went under restructuring works which lasted for 16 months to turn the venue into a football-specific stadium.

Major_Events.Description: A friendly between UD Las Palmas and Anderlecht was played in front of a full-capacity seats. The match ended 2–1 in favour of Las Palmas. The first scorer in the stadium was Rubén Castro.
Record attendance of 32,037.
The stadium will host matches in the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Football-specific stadium with seats close to the playing ground, designed by Pedro Medina Guillermo Ortego Carretero.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest stadium in the Canary Islands by capacity and the 14th-largest in Spain. It is a significant sports venue and will host matches in the 2030 FIFA World Cup.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches, home to UD Las Palmas.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 32,400 seats, which is planned to be upgraded to over 40,000 for the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The running track was removed during restructuring works in 2014-2016 to turn the venue into a football-specific stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Moller Villa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Moller Villa was built by Eric Moller, a Swedish shipping magnate, in 1936. The design is supposedly based on a sketch drawn by Moller's daughter from a dream she had. The mansion has been occupied by Japanese military and the Kuomintang in the past, later becoming the headquarters for the Communist Youth League Shanghai Branch.

Major_Events.Description: The Hengshan Group began to renovate the villa, preserving its original architectural style.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The villa features a distinctive Scandinavian style with Gothic and Tudor gables, spires, and steeples, and includes Chinese touches such as glazed tiles. Beyond the front gate with its two stone lions is a large lawn which encircles a tomb for Moller's favourite horse and other pets.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Moller Villa is a notable example of colonial-era architecture in Shanghai, blending Scandinavian and Chinese architectural elements. Its unique design and historical associations make it culturally significant.
world knowledge.Details: The building now houses a hotel. The mansion is built in a distinctively Scandinavian style with some Chinese touches such as glazed tiles.

world knowledge.Name: Blue Bayou and Dixie Landin'
world knowledge.Address: 18142 Perkins Road, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Blue Bayou Waterpark and Dixie Landin' are adjacent amusement parks in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Blue Bayou is a water park, and Dixie Landin' is a dry amusement park with thrill rides. Dixie Landin' was built in 1999, incorporating some rides from the now-defunct Fun Fair Park.

Major_Events.Event: Child injury on 'Over the Rainbow' ride
Major_Events.Description: A 2-year-old boy broke his arms and legs after falling at least 25 feet from the 'Over the Rainbow' ride.
A woman fell to her death from the now-defunct Xtreme roller coaster.
The parks were fined $25,295 by the U.S. Department of Labor for allowing minors to work more than eight hours a day.
The parks suffered moderate damage, including destruction of the Coca-Cola stage and damage to multiple attractions and buildings.
Additional damage occurred, including to a storage building alongside the Lazy River.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Blue Bayou features water attractions like a lazy river, wave pool, and various slides, marketed as 'The Land of the Giants.' Dixie Landin' includes thrill rides, kiddie rides, roller coasters, and flat rides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The parks are significant as major recreational attractions in Baton Rouge, offering a mix of water-based and dry amusement rides for all ages.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement and water parks providing entertainment and recreational activities.

Attractions.Blue Bayou: 20 attractions including a lazy river, behemoth bowl, quadruple aqualoop, wave pool, and ProSlide Tornado.
Attractions.Dixie Landin': 27 attractions including an S&S combo drop tower, log flume, three roller coasters, and various flat rides.

world knowledge.Name: Lushan Geopark
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lushan Geopark is located in the region around Mount Lu, Jiujiang. The protected area extends from the Yangtze River to the Poyang Lake basin. It features the effects of Quaternary glaciation and exceptional geological upthrown fault scarps from the Quaternary age.

Major_Events.Description: Mount Lu became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Lushan Geopark became a member of Global Geoparks Network.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features landscapes including Mount Lu, other mountains and summit peaks, valleys, gorges, gullies, rock formations, natural caves, and waterfalls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The area contains large numbers of Taoist and Buddhist temples, as well as several landmarks of Confucianism. It is recognized for its geological and cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The park is a popular visitor and tourist attraction, and is a cooler summer destination. It is also known as 庐山世界地质公园 in Simplified Chinese and 廬山地質公園 in Traditional Chinese, with the Hanyu Pinyin transcription being Lúshān Dìzhì Gōngyuán.

world knowledge.Name: Genesian Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Genesian Theatre is an amateur theatre company based in Sydney, Australia, named in honour of Saint Genesius, patron saint of actors. Formed in 1944 by members of the Sydney Catholic Youth Organisation, it has since evolved into a community theatre in the heart of the Sydney central business district. The theatre has been operating from historic St John The Evangelist Church in Kent Street since January 1954. The church dates from 1868 and has served as both a church and a poor school until 1932 when it became the Kursaal Theatre, housing the Sydney Repertory Company. In 1938 it became the first Matthew Talbot Hostel.

Major_Events.Description: Formed by members of the Sydney Catholic Youth Organisation.

Major_Events.Event: Move to St John The Evangelist Church
Major_Events.Description: The Genesian Theatre began operating from the historic St John The Evangelist Church in Kent Street.
The Catholic Church sold the building to a developer for over $6 million, requiring the theatre company to vacate by November 2018. The company later negotiated to remain until 2020.
The company reopened at a hall at St Joseph's Church in Rozelle following renovations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Historic church building dating from 1868, previously serving as a church, poor school, theatre, and hostel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Genesian Theatre is culturally significant as a long-standing community theatre in Sydney, fostering local talent and providing a platform for amateur theatre productions. It is also housed in a heritage-listed building with a rich history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Community theatre producing six main stage productions each year, along with classes, workshops, and other activities.
world knowledge.Details: Membership is open to any members of the community over the age of 18. Members can participate in all aspects of theatre production, including acting, designing, back-stage work, directing, and administration. The church is heritage listed.

world knowledge.Name: Rinia Park
world knowledge.Address: Bordered by Dëshmorët e Kombit Boulevard to the east, Bulevardi Gjergi Fishta and Bajram Curri Boulevard to the south, Rruga Ibrahim Rugova to the west and Rruga Myslym Shyri to the north
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1950 during the communist era as part of a major urban development program after World War II. Initially a family park, it became a free space for youth. After the end of communism in 1991, illegal buildings sprang up, and the park became notorious for Tirana's underworld. In 2000, the park was cleaned up, with 130 buildings demolished and over 45,000 cubic metres of waste removed.

Major_Events.Description: Illegal buildings were razed, and the park was replanted, removing over 45,000 cubic metres of waste.
Celebrated on March 14, this festival marks the end of winter and the rebirth of nature. In Tirana, festivities include a city marathon and a circus show in Rinia Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Main landmark is a white, terraced building on its western edge, housing cafés, restaurants, the Regency Casino, fountains, and a bowling lane. The building's architecture has been likened to a James Bond film villain's den or described as spider-shaped.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rinia Park is culturally significant as the central public park of Tirana, reflecting the city's history from the communist era to modern times. It hosts the annual Summer Festival, celebrating Albanian traditions and the rejuvenation of spirit.
world knowledge.Details: The park is also known for the Taivani Center and water fountain on its western perimeter. It was ironically called 'Taiwan' during the communist era, standing in front of the communist 'Block' across the Lana River.

world knowledge.Name: Sessions House, Surbiton
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sessions House was built in 1898 to serve as civic offices for the Surbiton local board. It became the headquarters of the Municipal Borough of Surbiton in 1936 and later served as a courthouse after the creation of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames in 1965. It was converted for judicial use as a venue for holding the quarter sessions, then re-designated as Surbiton Crown Court in 1971. After Crown Court sittings ceased in 1997, it was used as an immigration appeal court and later as a learning disability centre.

Major_Events.Description: The building was completed to serve as civic offices for the Surbiton local board.
The building became the headquarters of the Municipal Borough of Surbiton.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames
Major_Events.Description: The building ceased to be the local seat of government and was converted for judicial use.
The building was re-designated as Surbiton Crown Court.
Crown Court sittings moved to a new location in Kingston upon Thames.
The building was converted for use as a learning disability centre managed by 'Your Health Care'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed in the Edwardian Baroque style. It features a symmetrical main frontage with five bays, an arched doorway with a fanlight on the ground floor, a wrought iron balcony, a round-headed window with the borough coat of arms and a pediment above on the first floor, and a cupola containing a clock at roof level.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sessions House is a Grade II listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance. It served as a key civic and judicial building in Surbiton for over a century.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as civic offices, it later served as a courthouse and then as a learning disability centre.
world knowledge.Details: The building was designated as a Grade II listed building on 6 October 1983 (Reference no. 1358440). After falling vacant in 2009, it was repurposed for various uses, including as an Asylum and Immigration Tribunal office.

image_name: Parish Church of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary, Mellieħa

world knowledge.Name: Parish Church of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary, Mellieħa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Parish Church of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary is a Roman Catholic parish church in Mellieħa, Malta, dedicated to the Nativity of Mary. The parish of Mellieħa was first established in the 15th century or earlier but was abandoned due to attacks from Barbary pirates. The parish was re-established in 1844. Construction of the church began in 1881, with the first stone blessed on 5 September 1883. The church was blessed on 5 September 1897, and construction lasted until 1898. The bell towers and dome were completed between 1920 and 1940, and the church was consecrated on 18 February 1930.

Major_Events.Description: The first stone of the church was blessed by parish priest Francis Maria Magri on 5 September 1883.
The church was blessed by Bishop Pietro Pace on 5 September 1897.
The church was consecrated by Bishop Mauro Caruana on 18 February 1930.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church has two bell towers and a dome, making it a prominent landmark in the Mellieħa skyline. It features Baroque architecture and is constructed primarily of limestone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is a significant religious and cultural landmark in Mellieħa, dedicated to the Nativity of Mary. It serves as a parish church and has historical importance due to its long-standing presence and role in the community.
world knowledge.Details: The interior of the church is adorned with paintings by Maltese artists Giuseppe Calì and Lazzaro Pisani. The limestone used for construction was sourced from a local quarry, and the local population assisted in transporting the materials.

image_name: Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre

world knowledge.Name: Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre is a museum in the village of Great Missenden in Buckinghamshire, England. Children's and short story writer Roald Dahl lived in the village in Gipsy House for 36 years until his death in 1990. The museum was officially opened on 10 June 2005 by Cherie Blair and open to the public on 11 June 2005. It is housed in an old coaching inn and yard, which has been converted into a museum at a cost of £4.5 million. Funding was provided by the Dahl family, Dahl's publishers, charitable foundations and corporate and private donors.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened on 10 June 2005 by Cherie Blair and open to the public on 11 June 2005.
In 2008 the museum won the 'Best Small Visitor Attraction' award from Enjoy England, the website of the country's official tourist board.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in an old coaching inn and yard, which has been converted into a museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses all of Dahl's main papers: his manuscripts, business and personal correspondence and his 'Ideas Books'. It also offers regular workshops and hosts events that help to enhance creativity and writing skills.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is run by an independent registered charity.

world knowledge.Name: Chad National Museum
world knowledge.Address: Opposite the Palace of January 15, next to the National Library, N'Djamena, Chad
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chad National Museum, established on October 6, 1962, initially operated in temporary quarters under the name Chadian National Museum, Fort-Lamy. It moved to the former town hall in 1964. The museum has faced challenges, including the loss and looting of many artifacts during the Chadian–Libyan War between 1978 and 1987. It was revitalized in 1996 under the National Research Support Center, with a paleontology room opened in 1999 due to significant fossil discoveries in the Djurab Desert.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was established in temporary quarters.
The museum moved to the former town hall near the Place de l'Indépendance.
Many artifacts were lost and looted during this period.
A paleontology room was opened following significant fossil discoveries in the Djurab Desert.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses collections related to popular arts and traditions, archaeology, history, paleontology, and Islamic heritage. It also features exhibits dedicated to the Sao culture and paleoanthropology, including casts of important fossils like Tchadanthropus uxoris, Abel (Australopithecus bahrelghazali), and Toumaï (Sahelanthropus tchadensis).
world knowledge.Details: The museum's prehistory room includes items related to pebble culture, Paleolithic implements, and artifacts from the Angamma cliff. It also features a reproduction of a hunting scene from the first millennium B.C. and a collection of baked bricks, human masks, bronze objects, and bone tools from the Bouta-Kabira sanctuary.

world knowledge.Name: Chatsworth House
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main house (excluding wing): approx 81,000 sq ft
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chatsworth House is a stately home in the Derbyshire Dales, England. The seat of the Duke of Devonshire, it has belonged to the Cavendish family since 1549. It stands on the east bank of the River Derwent, across from hills between the Derwent and Wye valleys, amid parkland backed by wooded hills that rise to heather moorland. The house holds major collections of paintings, furniture, Old Master drawings, neoclassical sculptures and books. It is a Grade I listed property from the 17th century, altered in the 18th and 19th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: Underwent a £14-million restoration.
Princess Victoria (later Queen Victoria) and her mother, the Duchess of Kent, visited Chatsworth, where the Princess had her first formal adult dinner at the age of 13.
Queen Victoria and Prince Albert returned to enjoy an array of illumination in the gardens, in the conservatory and on the fountains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: English Baroque, Italianate architectural style. The house features a richly appointed Baroque suite of state rooms, a Painted Hall, and a Great Chamber with a painted ceiling of a classical scene by Antonio Verrio. The 6th Duke built a gatehouse and a North Wing in an Italianate style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chatsworth House is culturally significant as a symbol of English heritage and aristocratic life. It has been chosen several times as Britain's favourite country house and is a Grade I listed property. The house and its collections reflect centuries of art, history, and architecture.
world knowledge.Details: Chatsworth House is built on sloping ground, lower on the north and west sides than on the south and east sides. The original Tudor mansion was built in the 1560s by Bess of Hardwick in a quadrangle layout. The house has 126 rooms, with nearly 100 of them closed to visitors. The garden attracts about 300,000 visitors a year and covers 105 acres. The park covers 1,000 acres and is open to the public free of charge all year round, except for the south-east section, which is used for breeding by herds of red and fallow deer.

world knowledge.Name: Manchester–Boston Regional Airport
world knowledge.Area: State of New Hampshire, Greater Boston
world knowledge.Address: Manchester and Londonderry, New Hampshire, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Manchester–Boston Regional Airport, opened in 1927, is the busiest airport in New Hampshire and the fifth-largest in New England by passenger volume. It was initially named Manchester Airport until 2006 when it was renamed to highlight its proximity to Boston. The airport played a significant role during World War II as an Army Air Force base and has since evolved into a key regional transportation hub.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed to emphasize its proximity to Boston, aiming to attract more travelers.

Major_Events.Event: World War II Army Air Force Base
Major_Events.Description: The airport served as a military base during World War II, housing troops and anti-submarine squadrons.
A new 158,000-square-foot terminal opened to accommodate larger jets and increasing passenger traffic.
Runway 17/35 was extended to 9,250 feet, enabling non-stop flights to Las Vegas.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two asphalt runways: Runway 17/35 (9,250 x 150 ft) and Runway 6/24 (7,651 x 150 ft). The terminal, designed by HNTB and Lavallee Brensinger, includes modern facilities and a parking garage with solar panels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As New Hampshire's primary commercial airport, it serves as a vital transportation link for the region. It also houses the Aviation Museum of New Hampshire, preserving the state's aviation history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial, cargo, and general aviation needs.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is a hub for Wiggins Airways and Freight Runners Express. It handles significant cargo operations for FedEx, UPS, and Amazon. Despite declines in passenger traffic post-2005, it remains a critical facility for northern New England, with ongoing efforts to attract new airlines and destinations.

world knowledge.Name: Klosterneuburg Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1114 by Saint Leopold III of Babenberg, the abbey was consecrated in 1136 and has undergone several renovations, including Baroque and Gothic styles. It has served as a significant religious and cultural institution throughout its history.

Major_Events.Description: The abbey church was consecrated after 22 years of construction.
Leopold III was canonized by Pope Innocent VIII, making the abbey an important pilgrimage site.
The monastery was defended successfully during the Ottoman siege of Vienna.
The abbey church underwent significant Baroque remodeling.
The Nazis suppressed the canonry and confiscated the buildings and properties.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey features a mix of Gothic and Baroque styles, with two spires and significant Baroque remodeling. The complex includes a castle tower, a Gothic chapel, and the Verduner Altar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Klosterneuburg Abbey is culturally significant as a historical religious site, a pilgrimage destination, and a center for art and wine production. It houses important artifacts like the Verduner Altar and has played a role in Austrian history.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey has a rich history of wine production and owns extensive vineyards. It also engages in social projects, funding initiatives like child protection centers and women's aid projects. The abbey has been governed by 66 provosts over its nearly 900-year history.

world knowledge.Name: Anegada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Anegada is the northernmost of the British Virgin Islands, formed from coral and limestone rather than volcanic origin. It is flat and low, with the highest point being about 28 feet above sea level. Its name is derived from the Spanish for "flooded land", tierra anegada.

Major_Events.Description: The eye of Hurricane Earl passed 15 to 20 miles north of Anegada at category 4, causing significant damage and major flooding on the south side. There were no reported serious injuries.

The eye of Hurricane Irma passed 12 miles south of Anegada at category 5, causing major damage. Some people evacuated to Tortola, but most remained on the island. There were no reported serious injuries.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Anegada is known for its unique coral and limestone formation, miles of white sand beaches, and the 18-mile-long Horseshoe Reef. It is also significant for its salt ponds, which support unique fauna and are designated as a Ramsar Site.
world knowledge.Details: Anegada is the only inhabited British Virgin Island formed from coral and limestone. It has a population of 450 as of 2024. The island is known for its bonefish population, making it a popular destination for fly fishing. The reef has caused hundreds of shipwrecks, making it an important scuba diving destination. The island also has a Headstart facility for the Anegada rock iguana, and an annual Iguana Festival is held to celebrate the island's native species.

world knowledge.Name: Neapoli Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Neapoli Stadium is a football stadium completed in 1965, primarily used for football matches and serving as the home field for Ionikos FC.

Major_Events.Description: Record attendance of 6,565 spectators.

Major_Events.Event: Rugby Sevens' finals of the Hellenic Rugby Federation
Major_Events.Description: The stadium was used for the Rugby Sevens' finals on June 13, 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface with a seating capacity of 5,500 (or 4,999 as per Infobox).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium holds cultural importance as the home field for Ionikos FC and has hosted significant sporting events, including record-attendance football matches and rugby finals.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium and occasional venue for rugby matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has two main supporters' groups: the Association of Ionikos Nikaias Supporters and the Fan Club of Agios Georgios. It is owned by Ionikos FC.

world knowledge.Name: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park is a deer national park located in Vanasthalipuram, Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It was named after Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, in commemoration of his 2500th nirvan anniversary in the year 1975. The place where the park is located was once a private hunting ground for the Nizam, rulers of Hyderabad. A deer park was set up in order to preserve this precious heritage and rehabilitate it.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established to commemorate the 2500th nirvan anniversary of Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it was established to commemorate the 2500th nirvan anniversary of Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, and to preserve the heritage of the former private hunting ground of the Nizam, rulers of Hyderabad.
world knowledge.Details: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park is the largest green lung space in the city of Hyderabad. It is home to a few hundred blackbucks (the state animal of Andhra Pradesh), chitals, porcupines, water monitors, short-toed eagles, Indian pond herons, egrets, kingfishers, cormorants, and several other bird species. The park is maintained by the TS Forest Department, and guided tours are available within the park. There is an entry fee for people who wish to enter the park by safari vehicle to view the animals.

world knowledge.Name: Prince Gong's Mansion
world knowledge.Address: North of Shichahai Lake, Xicheng District, Beijing, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally constructed for Heshen, a corrupt official in the Qing dynasty, the mansion was later given to Prince Gong, a Manchu prince and influential statesman. It served as a university in the early 20th century and was later used by a factory during the Cultural Revolution. It was restored and opened as a tourist attraction in 1996.

Major_Events.Description: The mansion was constructed for Heshen, a prominent court official in the reign of the Qianlong Emperor.
The Jiaqing Emperor accused Heshen of corruption, had him executed, and gave the mansion to Prince Qing.
The Xianfeng Emperor gave the mansion to his sixth brother, Prince Gong.
Prince Gong's grandson offered the property as a mortgage to the Order of Saint Benedict, who restored it for use as Furen Catholic University.
The mansion was used by the Beijing Air Conditioning Factory during the Cultural Revolution.
The mansion was declared a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level.
The buildings and gardens became a tourist attraction.
Renovation works were completed during the 2008 Summer Olympics.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mansion consists of large siheyuan-style courtyards, two-story buildings, and a grand Peking opera house. The garden features pavilions, artificial hills with rocks from Lake Tai, and ponds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mansion is one of the most exquisite and best-preserved imperial mansions in Beijing, showcasing the lives of Manchu nobles and aspects of the Qing dynasty. It is included on the World Monuments Fund's 2018 list of monuments at risk.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion includes a garden with 20 scenic spots and an eight-meter-long stele bearing the Chinese character for 'fortune' based on the calligraphy of the Kangxi Emperor. It has undergone significant renovations, including a 200 million yuan project starting in 2005. The Beijing opera house inside stages various forms of Chinese opera.

world knowledge.Name: Cavan County Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cavan County Museum is dedicated to the history of County Cavan and is housed in the former Convent of St Clare in Ballyjamesduff. Established in 1996, the museum collects, conserves, and displays the material heritage and culture of County Cavan over its 6000-year history.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a 19th-century former convent of the Poor Clare nuns, comprising exhibition spaces and gardens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and showcases the 6000-year history of County Cavan, including artifacts from prehistoric to modern times, and features exhibitions on the Great Famine, local singer Percy French, and the Poor Clares.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include the Killycluggin Stone, the Lavey Sheela na gig, costumes in the Pighouse Collection, and GAA paraphernalia. It also features a replica World War I trench built to the original specifications used by the Royal Irish Fusiliers. The museum collaborates with the Fermanagh County Museum through the "Connecting People, Places and Heritage Project" and hosts temporary exhibitions of local and national artists. It is designated by the National Museum of Ireland to collect archaeological finds.

world knowledge.Name: Old Town Hall, Bawtry
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main assembly hall: 48 feet (15 m) long and 27 feet (8.2 m) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Old Town Hall was commissioned by local businessmen in 1889 under the Bawtry Public Hall Company. It was designed in the Victorian style, built in red brick with a stucco front, and officially opened in 1890. Due to a population decline in the early 20th century, the venture failed, and the building was sold in 1916. Over the years, it served as a working men's club, car showroom, florist, and art gallery. In 2024, plans were approved for an extension.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid by Francis Raynes, chairman of the Bawtry Public Hall Company, on 26 April 1890.
The building was officially opened by Francis Raynes on 9 October 1890, attended by Lord Houghton.
The building was converted into a working men's club in the 1930s.
The building was converted into an art gallery with the insertion of a mezzanine floor.
Plans were approved to extend the building to the rear, providing two apartments and a commercial space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian style, constructed of red brick with a gabled stucco front, three bays wide. Central bay contains the doorway, outer bays have round-headed windows with moulded surrounds. Decorated with seven pilasters surmounted by finials. Gable topped by a lead-clad cupola with a weather vane.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Old Town Hall represents the civic and social history of Bawtry, reflecting its economic and population changes over time. Its Victorian architecture and varied uses highlight the town's adaptability and heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a public hall, later repurposed as a working men's club, car showroom, florist, art gallery, and commercial space.
world knowledge.Details: The building had a reading room by 1901. An illuminated striking clock was installed at the time of its opening. The commercial space was later let to a fashion retailer, Fairfax & Favor.

world knowledge.Name: LeVeque Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The LeVeque Tower is a 47-story skyscraper in Downtown Columbus, Ohio. At 555 feet 5 inches (169.29 m) it was the tallest building in the city from its completion in 1927 to 1974, and remains the second-tallest today. Designed by C. Howard Crane, the Art Deco skyscraper was opened as the American Insurance Union Citadel in 1927 and at the time was the fifth tallest building in the world. Built at a cost of $8.7 million, the tower's design incorporates ornate ornamentation and a terracotta facade, and it was designed with 600 hotel rooms in two wings as well as an attached performance venue, the Palace Theatre. After the American Insurance Union went bankrupt in the Great Depression, the tower was renamed the LeVeque-Lincoln Tower in 1946, and later the LeVeque Tower in 1977.

Major_Events.Description: Groundbreaking for the tower took place on September 23, 1924.
An accident occurred underground that killed four workers when a toxic gas was accidentally released during the setting of the caissons.
The building was dedicated on September 21, 1927. When complete, it was the tallest building in Columbus and the fifth tallest building in the world.
After the American Insurance Union went bankrupt, the tower was renamed the LeVeque-Lincoln Tower.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The tower was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The name was officially changed to the LeVeque Tower.
The tower was converted into a mixed-use development, including a hotel, apartments, condominiums, offices, and a restaurant.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the Art Deco or Art Moderne style, the building took inspiration from Byzantine architecture. The design featured a large number of figures situated 495 feet and higher along the building's façade and around its pinnacle, including eagles with wingspans up to 22 feet and giants and angels up to 26 feet tall. The building's exterior is wrapped in cream-colored terracotta, and the interior contains marble imported from Italy and Belgium, with public spaces decorated with bronze and mosaics. The building lobby was designed with a marble floor with a bronze plaque containing the building's horoscope.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The LeVeque Tower is a symbol synonymous with Columbus and one of the city's most well-recognized landmarks. It was the first landmark that was easily visible from around the city. The tower quickly became important to radio broadcasting in the city, housing several radio stations. It has also been a significant part of the city's skyline and history, representing the growth and development of Columbus.
world knowledge.Details: The LeVeque Tower was originally named the American Insurance Union Citadel and was designed by architect C. Howard Crane. It was the tallest building in Columbus until 1974. The tower has undergone several ownership changes and renovations, most recently being converted into a mixed-use development in 2017. The building also houses the Palace Theatre, a historic performance venue that has hosted numerous famous performers over the years. The tower's design includes unique features such as a horoscope plaque in the lobby and was once intended to accommodate mooring for zeppelins.

world knowledge.Name: Lac d'Allos
world knowledge.Area: Parc National du Mercantour, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lac d'Allos is an alpine lake with historical significance dating back to the twelfth century when it was called Levedone. It is the largest natural high-altitude lake in Europe.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural lake with a maximum depth of 50 meters (160 feet) and a surface elevation of 2,230 meters (7,320 feet). Dominated by Mont Pelat (3,052 meters).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lac d'Allos is culturally significant as the largest natural high-altitude lake in Europe and a notable feature of the Parc National du Mercantour.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural landmark and part of the national park.
world knowledge.Details: The lake is situated nearby the municipality of Allos. It covers 60 hectares and has a depth of 50 meters. This Alpes-de-Haute-Provence geographical article is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Graciosa Airport
world knowledge.Address: Barro Vermelho, between Dores and Ponta da Barca, Santa Cruz da Graciosa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Graciosa Airport was projected in 1973, with the project and topographical surveys concluded in 1976. It was built by the Azorean Regional Government between September 1979 and July 1981, and its runway was inaugurated on July 11, 1981. The original small air terminal was replaced by a new one, inaugurated on October 1, 2001.

Major_Events.Description: The runway of Graciosa Airport was inaugurated on July 11, 1981.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the new air terminal
Major_Events.Description: The new air terminal was inaugurated on October 1, 2001, replacing the original small air terminal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway that is 1,385 meters long with an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Graciosa Airport is significant as a key transportation hub for Graciosa Island, facilitating connectivity within the Azores and beyond.
world knowledge.Details: Graciosa Airport (IATA: GRW, ICAO: LPGR) is located 2 km west northwest of Santa Cruz da Graciosa. It is operated by ANA – Aeroportos de Portugal, SA and serves regular scheduled and charter flights.

world knowledge.Name: Myrtle Grove, Bingley
world knowledge.Address: Myrtle Park, Bingley, West Yorkshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Myrtle Grove dates back to the mid-18th century, originally consisting of a house, farm, and Quaker meeting-house. The current Georgian-style mansion was built in 1770 by Dr. Johnson Atkinson. It served as a private residence until acquired by Bingley Urban District Council in the early 20th century, becoming the town hall in 1926. It ceased being the local seat of government in 1974 and is now used as offices by Bradford Council.

Major_Events.Description: Dr. Johnson Atkinson demolished existing buildings and commissioned the current Georgian-style mansion.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition by Bingley Urban District Council
Major_Events.Description: The council acquired the Myrtle Park estate for the town, progressively moving staff into Myrtle Grove from 1923.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as Grade II listed building
Major_Events.Description: Myrtle Grove was officially designated as a Grade II listed building on 9 August 1966.

Major_Events.Event: Cessation as local seat of government
Major_Events.Description: After the formation of the enlarged Bradford Council, Myrtle Grove ceased to be the local seat of government.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Georgian style mansion built in ashlar stone with a symmetrical main frontage of nine bays. Features include a central doorway flanked by Doric order pilasters, sash windows, rusticated quoins, and a high hip roof finished in Westmorland slate. Flanked by a stable block and coach house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Myrtle Grove is a Grade II listed building with historical significance as the former headquarters of Bingley Urban District Council. It reflects the Georgian architectural style and has associations with notable historical figures, including John Wesley.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, later the town hall for Bingley Urban District Council, and now offices for Bradford Council.
world knowledge.Details: The building was referred to as a 'little paradise' by John Wesley. It played a role in the development of local governance and public services in Bingley, including the establishment of a public library and mechanics institute.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Tanzania
world knowledge.Address: Shaaban Robert Street, next to the botanical gardens in Kivukoni ward in Ilala District, Dar es Salaam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Tanzania (NMT) is a consortium of several Tanzanian museums established to preserve and showcase objects from the history and natural environment of Tanzania. It originated from the National Museum of Dar es Salaam, founded in 1934 by Tanganyika governor Harold MacMichael. The consortium includes six additional museums, each dedicated to different aspects of Tanzanian history and culture. The museum was expanded in 1963 and now focuses on the history of Tanzania, including significant archaeological finds and ethnographic collections.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the National Museum of Dar es Salaam
Major_Events.Description: The museum was established by Tanganyika governor Harold MacMichael.
A second building was added, and the museum shifted its focus to the history of Tanzania.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by German Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier
Major_Events.Description: The President asked for forgiveness for the acts of violence committed during German colonial rule and announced the return of skulls of resistance fighters to Tanzania.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Museum of Tanzania preserves and showcases the cultural and natural heritage of Tanzania, including significant archaeological finds, ethnographic collections, and historical artifacts. It plays a crucial role in educating the public about Tanzania's history and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum for Natural and General history
world knowledge.Details: The National Museum of Tanzania includes several museums, such as the Village Museum, the National History Museum, the Arusha Declaration Museum, the Mwalimu Julius K. Nyerere Memorial Museum, the Majimaji Memorial Museum, and the Dr. Rashid M. Kawawa Museum. The museum also organizes cultural events and maintains 90 historical buildings and monuments.

world knowledge.Name: Victoria Beach, Manitoba
world knowledge.Location: Southeastern shores of Lake Winnipeg, approximately 100 kilometres (62 mi) north of Winnipeg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Victoria Beach was initially known as L'Île-à-la-Biche by the Voyageurs. The Victoria Beach Investment Company was founded in 1910 to develop the area as a summer resort. The municipality was incorporated in 1919. The area evolved from a summer resort with railway access to a car-accessible community by the 1960s. It has a rich history of commercial fishing, mink ranching, and recreational development.

Major_Events.Event: Founding of Victoria Beach Investment Company
Major_Events.Description: The company was founded to develop the area as a summer resort.
The Municipality of Victoria Beach was officially incorporated.
A road was completed to connect Albert Beach to the rest of Victoria Beach, reducing reliance on the railway.
The last mink ranch in Victoria Beach closed, marking the end of an era.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The area features cottages, a golf course, tennis courts, and a community clubhouse. The pier, rebuilt in 1949, is a notable structure with a foundation of massive rocks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Victoria Beach is culturally significant as a historic summer resort community with fine beaches and recreational amenities. It also has a history of antisemitism in the mid-20th century, reflecting broader social issues of the time.
world knowledge.Details: Victoria Beach is the smallest rural municipality in Manitoba by area. It has a permanent population of 689 but swells to over 5,000 in summer. Motor vehicles are restricted during summer months, with exceptions for deliveries and contractors. The area features a yacht club, marina, baseball field, and other recreational facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Victoria Memorial, Kolkata
world knowledge.Address: 1, Queens Way, Maidan, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Victoria Memorial is a large marble monument built by the British Raj in memory of Queen Victoria, the Empress of India from 1876 to 1901. It is the largest monument to a monarch anywhere in the world. The idea for the memorial was proposed by Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, shortly after Queen Victoria's death in 1901. The construction was funded by voluntary subscriptions from the people of India and was completed in 1921.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid by George, the Prince of Wales.
The Victoria Memorial was formally opened to the public by the Prince of Wales, the future Edward VIII.
The Kolkata gallery, showcasing the visual history of Kolkata, was opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Victoria Memorial is designed in the Indo-Saracenic style, blending British, Mughal, Venetian, Egyptian, and Deccani architectural influences. It is constructed of white Makrana marble and features a central dome, four subsidiary domes, high portals, and domed corner towers. The building is 338 by 228 feet and rises to a height of 184 feet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Victoria Memorial is a symbol of the British Raj in India and serves as a museum that preserves the history and culture of the colonial era. It is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Kolkata and is a significant cultural and historical landmark in India.
world knowledge.Details: The Victoria Memorial houses 25 galleries, including the royal gallery, the national leader's gallery, and the Kolkata gallery. It has a vast collection of artifacts, paintings, and rare books. The gardens surrounding the memorial cover 64 acres and feature statues of notable historical figures. The memorial is managed by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

world knowledge.Name: RK Beach
world knowledge.Location: Beach Road, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Address: Beach Road, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: RK Beach gets its name from the Ramakrishna Mission ashram situated near the beach.
world knowledge.Details: Ramakrishna Beach also known as R K Beach is situated on the east coast of Bay of Bengal in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. It is located near Dolphin's Nose. APSRTC runs buses to this area along these routes.

world knowledge.Name: Cahors Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Nave: 44 x 20 m; Domes: 32 m high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cahors Cathedral, also known as Cathédrale Saint-Étienne de Cahors, is a Roman Catholic church built in the 11th century by bishop Gerard de Cardaillac over a 7th-century church erected by St. Didier of Cahors. It was consecrated by Pope Calixtus II on September 10, 1119, and completed around 1135. The cathedral reflects the transition between late Romanesque and Gothic architectural styles and served as a fortified edifice due to the bishops' feudal power.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by Pope Calixtus II on September 10, 1119.
The façade was renovated by Guillaume de Labroue, cousin of Pope John XXII, giving it a fortified appearance.
The Flamboyant Gothic-style cloister was built by bishop Anthony of Luzech.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Gothic and Romanesque styles. It has a sturdy, fortified appearance with a porch surmounted by a bell tower enclosed between two towers. The nave is 44 x 20 m wide, with two massive 32 m-high domes in Byzantine style. The apse is Gothic on a Romanesque base, with three chapels and sculptures. The cathedral lacks a transept and includes a Flamboyant Gothic-style cloister.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cahors Cathedral is a national monument and an important example of the transition between Romanesque and Gothic architecture. It houses significant relics, such as the Holy Cap, and features medieval frescoes and paintings. The cathedral's history reflects the feudal power of the local bishops.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral contains 14th-century frescoes depicting the stoning of St. Stephen and eight prophets. It also has a museum of Religious Art in the St. Gaubert Chapel, which features Italian Renaissance paintings and 15th-century frescoes of the Last Judgement.

world knowledge.Name: Pudong Football Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pudong Football Stadium, completed in October 2020, is the home of Chinese Super League club Shanghai Port. Construction began on 28 April 2018. It was initially planned to host the 2023 AFC Asian Cup final and one semi-final, but China withdrew from hosting due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Major_Events.Event: 2020 League of Legends World Championship Final
Major_Events.Description: The venue hosted the final match of the 2020 League of Legends World Championship, which was also the inaugural event at the stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The white metal exterior design of the stadium is reminiscent of a Chinese porcelain bowl. Designed by HPP Architekten.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a modern sports venue in Shanghai, serving as a hub for football and esports events, contributing to the city's cultural and sporting landscape.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is currently named SAIC Motor Pudong Arena due to sponsorship reasons. It has a capacity of 37,000 and features a grass surface. Owned by the Shanghai Sports Bureau.

world knowledge.Name: Worth County Courthouse (Northwood, Iowa)
world knowledge.Address: Central Ave. between 10th and 11th Sts. Northwood, Iowa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Worth County Courthouse in Northwood, Iowa, was built in 1893 in a Romanesque style. It is the second courthouse for the county, replacing the first one built in 1879. The current courthouse was constructed following an election that confirmed Northwood as the county seat. The building underwent renovations in 1938 and an expansion in 1990, which included new offices, a jail, and a conference room. A Civil War cannon, erected in 1996, is located on the grounds.

Major_Events.Description: The first courthouse was built with a contributed total of $5,075, but only $4,400 was used. It was made of bricks and considered plain.
The current courthouse was built in brick with a limestone base, featuring a small tower. It replaced the first courthouse after an election confirmed Northwood as the county seat.
The courthouse was enlarged and remodeled, including the replacement of the first tower.
A Civil War cannon, manufactured at the Northwood Foundry and Fort Pitt Foundry, was erected on the courthouse grounds by the Worth County Sesquicentennial Commission.
The expansion included new offices, a new jail, and a conference room.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romanesque style, constructed in brick with a limestone base. Features a small tower, originally with a taller roof and sharply-pointed gablets.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its association with county government and the political power and prestige of Northwood as the county seat. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1981.
world knowledge.Details: The first courthouse was built with the agreement that the land could be subdivided among contributors if it reverted to the original owners. Only $4,594 of the donated $5,000 was used to build the current courthouse. The Civil War cannon was previously located on the north bank of Shell Rock River.

world knowledge.Name: Cadbury World
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cadbury World is a visitor attraction in Bournville, Birmingham, England, featuring a self-guided exhibition tour, created and run by the Cadbury Company. The tour tells the history of chocolate, and of the Cadbury business. Planning for a new chocolate-based attraction commenced in 1988, with the Bournville site decided upon. Cadbury World was opened on 14 August 1990 by Morgan Anderson on Cadbury's Bournville manufacturing site at a cost of £6 million. The attraction has expanded and developed its content through 'continuous improvement'. It was formally opened by then Prime Minister John Major on 12 April 1991.

Major_Events.Description: Cadbury World was opened on 14 August 1990 by Morgan Anderson on Cadbury's Bournville manufacturing site at a cost of £6 million.

Major_Events.Event: Formal Opening by Prime Minister John Major
Major_Events.Description: Cadbury World was formally opened by then Prime Minister John Major on 12 April 1991.
In 2022, it was announced that Merlin Entertainments were to take over the running of the attraction, subject to the approval of the Competition and Markets Authority.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cadbury World features 14 zones which tell the story of chocolate and the Cadbury business through various static sets, animatronics, video presentations, multi-sensory cinema, interactive displays and activities, and staff demonstrations. The Bournville Experience (Opened in 2007 replacing the Cadbury Collection Museum) explains the background to the development of the site on which it is located. 4D Chocolate Adventure, constructed in 2014, replaces Essence which in turn replaced Cadburyland before it, and incorporates a 3D cinema.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cadbury World is culturally significant as it tells the history of chocolate and the Cadbury business, which is now part of Mondelez, the world's second largest confectionery manufacturer. It is one of Birmingham's largest leisure attractions, attracting over 500,000 visitors each year, especially children and students. The estate features a respected education programme linking back directly to the educational advancements and interests of the company's original founders.
world knowledge.Details: Cadbury World provides a Chocolate afternoon tea. In August 2019, Heritage Interactive installed seven interactive panels in the Aztec Jungle. A second location in Dunedin, New Zealand, closed in May 2018. In 2018, the factory closed to make way for a new NZ$1.4 billion hospital to replace the existing Dunedin Hospital. Mondelez vice-president Banfield confirmed that the former Cadbury site had been sold to the Ministry of Health for an undisclosed amount. The closure of Cadbury World led to the loss of 39 jobs. During the demolition, business records from Hudson & Co from 1899 to 1988 were discovered in a cupboard. Hudson & Co amalgamated with Cadbury Fry in 1929.

world knowledge.Name: Down Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Down Cathedral, the Cathedral Church of the Holy and Undivided Trinity, is a Church of Ireland cathedral located in Downpatrick, Northern Ireland. It stands on Cathedral Hill and is one of two cathedrals in the Diocese of Down and Dromore. The cathedral has a rich history dating back to the Celtic church period, with significant events including the arrival of St Malachy in 1124, the expulsion of the older monastic community by Sir John de Courcy in 1177, and its restoration after the Down Cathedral Act of 1790.

Major_Events.Description: Restoration of the ruined 14th-century cathedral was initiated after an act of the Irish Parliament granted £1,000 for the purpose.
The cathedral reopened for divine service on 23 August 1818.
The cathedral underwent a second major restoration during which it was closed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building today is mainly the original chancel from the 15th century, with a vestibule and tower added. It houses an 11th-century granite font and contains crosses from the 9th, 10th, and 12th centuries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Down Cathedral is culturally significant as it is the burial place of St Patrick, believed to have died in 461. It also preserves ancient crosses and has a long history tied to the Christianization of Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral grounds contain the burial place of St Patrick and a replica of a weathered high cross made of granite. The original cross is now displayed in the Down County Museum. The cathedral also features two small stone crosses from the 12th century.

image_name: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi (Ouro Preto)

world knowledge.Name: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi (Ouro Preto)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Church of Saint Francis of Assisi is a Rococo Catholic church in Ouro Preto, Brazil. Its construction began in 1766 after a design by the Brazilian architect and sculptor Antônio Francisco Lisboa, also known as Aleijadinho. The church's interior decorations were completed towards the end of the 19th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the Seven Wonders of Portuguese Origin in the World.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The church was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its architecture and historical significance regarding eighteenth-century gold mining.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church features Rococo and Baroque styles with intricate gilded carvings, high-reliefs, and a soapstone frontispiece. It includes circular bell towers and an oculus closed by a relief, which were original features in Brazilian religious architecture at the time. The interior is richly decorated with golden woodwork, statues, and paintings, including a notable ceiling painting by Manuel da Costa Ataíde titled 'Glorification of Our Lady Among Musician Angels'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is a prime example of colonial Portuguese architecture and Rococo style in Brazil. It reflects the wealth and cultural influence of the gold mining era in Minas Gerais. The church is also central to Holy Week celebrations, which renew local visions of economic prosperity and cultural identity.
world knowledge.Details: The church was designed by Aleijadinho, a prominent Brazilian architect and sculptor of mixed-race heritage. His work is celebrated for its contribution to Brazilian colonial architecture. The church's design and decorations are emblematic of the Rococo and Baroque styles, with significant influence from Portuguese architecture. The city of Ouro Preto, where the church is located, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its well-preserved colonial architecture.

world knowledge.Name: Oregon Shakespeare Festival
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1935 by Angus L. Bowmer, the Oregon Shakespeare Festival (OSF) is a regional repertory theatre in Ashland, Oregon. It began with performances of Shakespearean plays and has since expanded to include a wide range of classic and contemporary plays. The festival has grown significantly over the years, welcoming millions of visitors and becoming a major cultural and economic force in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The Oregon Shakespeare Festival was founded by Angus L. Bowmer, with performances of 'Twelfth Night' and 'The Merchant of Venice'.
The Festival welcomed its millionth visitor.
The Festival welcomed its 10-millionth visitor.
The Festival welcomed its 20-millionth visitor.
The Festival was forced to close due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
OSF announced an emergency fundraising campaign to raise $2.5 million to continue the season.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The festival campus includes three theatres: the outdoor Allen Elizabethan Theatre, the indoor Angus Bowmer Theatre, and the Thomas Theatre. The Allen Elizabethan Theatre is patterned after London's 1599 Fortune Theatre, with a thrust stage and Elizabethan-style façade. The Angus Bowmer Theatre features a flexible stage with hydraulic lifts, and the Thomas Theatre offers configurable seating arrangements for intimate or experimental productions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Oregon Shakespeare Festival is a major cultural institution, known for its high-quality productions of Shakespearean and contemporary plays. It has a significant economic impact on the region and attracts visitors from around the world. The festival also plays an active role in the community, participating in local celebrations and offering educational programs.
world knowledge.Details: The festival operates annually from April to December, offering 800 to 850 performances of various plays. It has three theatres: the Allen Elizabethan Theatre, the Angus Bowmer Theatre, and the Thomas Theatre. The festival also includes educational programs, community events, and a free outdoor "Green Show" during the summer months. OSF is a non-profit organization with a significant endowment and a large volunteer workforce.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Breton Highlands National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Breton Highlands National Park is a Canadian national park on northern Cape Breton Island in Nova Scotia. It was the first national park in the Atlantic provinces of Canada and covers an area of 948 square kilometres (366 sq mi). The park features mountains, valleys, waterfalls, rocky coastlines, and the Cape Breton Highlands, a tundra-esque plateau. It includes the highest point in Nova Scotia, White Hill, at 533.5 m (1,750 ft) above sea level. The park is known for its steep cliffs and deep river canyons that carve into a forested plateau bordering the Atlantic Ocean.

Major_Events.Description: Parks Canada started a four-year project with the Unama'ki Institute of Natural Resources, among other partners, to begin regional boreal forest restorations within this park.
Parks Canada transferred eighteen western moose (nine bulls, nine cows) from Alberta's Elk Island National Park to this national park.

Country folk singer Taylor Mitchell died as a result of her injuries and blood loss due to coyotes attacking her while she was hiking by herself on the Skyline Trail. This incident became the only recorded fatal coyote assault on an adult as well as a Canadian.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse landscape including mountains, valleys, waterfalls, rocky coastlines, and a tundra-esque plateau. It includes the highest point in Nova Scotia, White Hill, at 533.5 m (1,750 ft) above sea level. The park is known for its steep cliffs and deep river canyons that carve into a forested plateau bordering the Atlantic Ocean.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cape Breton Highlands National Park is culturally and historically significant as the first national park in the Atlantic provinces of Canada. It is known for its stunning natural beauty, diverse wildlife, and important ecological restoration projects. The park is also an Important Bird Area and is home to a variety of mammals, birds, and aquatic life.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains 26 marked hiking trails, including the Skyline Trail. It features five main saltwater ocean beaches and two freshwater lakes.
