The park is also home to the Highlands Links, an 18-hole golf course designed by Stanley Thompson, ranked as one of the top 100 courses in the world and the best public course in Canada. The park is governed by Parks Canada and is one of 42 in Canada's system of national parks.

image_name: Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul

world knowledge.Name: Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
world knowledge.Address: 18th St. and Benjamin Franklin Parkway at Logan Square, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul is the head church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Philadelphia. It was designed by Napoleon LeBrun to plans by the Reverend Mariano Muller and the Reverend John Tornatore and built between 1846 and 1864. Its dome and Palladian facade, by John Notman, were added after 1850. The interior was decorated by Constantino Brumidi. The cathedral was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1971. It has been the site of two Papal Masses, one celebrated by John Paul II in 1979, the other by Francis in 2015.

Major_Events.Event: Papal Mass by John Paul II
Major_Events.Description: Celebrated by Pope John Paul II.
Celebrated by Pope Francis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is presented in a Roman-Corinthian style of architecture, modeled after the Lombard Church of St. Charles (San Carlo al Corso) in Rome. Its Palladian façade and aqua oxidized-copper dome are in the Italian Renaissance manner. The interior features an oversized apse of stained glass and red antique marble in proportions reminiscent of Roman churches. A baldachin (canopy) over the main altar and the three altars on each of the side aisles point up this Italian Renaissance flavor. The ceiling mural in the dome, The Assumption of the Virgin into Heaven, was painted by Constantino Brumidi in 1868.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul is the largest Catholic church in Pennsylvania and one of the most architecturally notable structures in the city of Philadelphia. It has been the site of significant religious events, including Papal Masses, and is a symbol of the Catholic faith in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The basilica was designed by Napoleon LeBrun based on plans drawn up by the Reverend Mariano Muller and the Reverend John B. Tornatore, and by John Notman who added the dome and facade. The crypt under the main altar contains the remains of most of the bishops and archbishops, and of several other clergymen, of Philadelphia.

world knowledge.Name: Sihanouk International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 20 kilometres east of Sihanoukville City, Sihanoukville Province, Cambodia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally constructed in the 1960s with Soviet assistance, the airport experienced dormancy during and after the Khmer Rouge era. It formally reopened on 5 January 2007 after significant upgrades, including runway extension and taxiway widening.

Major_Events.Description: The airport formally reopened on 5 January 2007 after upgrades.
Scheduled passenger flight service was discontinued until 2011 following the crash.
Cambodia Angkor Air started a tri-weekly service from Angkor International Airport in Siem Reap on 14 December 2011.
The airline adjusted its service to operate a triangle route, Siem Reap-Sihanoukville-Phnom Penh-Siem Reap, starting on 31 March 2013.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Runway extended to 3,300 metres to accommodate 4E class aircraft, with widened taxiways and an added cargo apron.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named after King Norodom Sihanouk, the airport is a key infrastructure in Cambodia, reflecting the country's development and connectivity.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is also known as Kang Keng Airport. The IATA code KOS is derived from Sihanoukville's alternative name, 'Kampong Som'. It is Cambodia's third largest international airport.

world knowledge.Name: Nameri National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nameri National Park was declared a reserve forest on 17 October 1978. It was set up as a Nameri Sanctuary on 18 September 1985 with an area of 137 km². Another 75 km² was added on 15 November 1998 when it was officially established as a National Park. It was declared a Tiger Reserve in the year 2000.

Major_Events.Description: Nameri National Park was declared a reserve forest.
Nameri was set up as a Nameri Sanctuary with an area of 137 km².
Nameri was officially established as a National Park with an additional 75 km².
Nameri National Park was declared a Tiger Reserve.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nameri National Park is significant for its biodiversity and as a habitat for various endangered species, including the Bengal tiger. It is also culturally important for its historical role in conservation and as a site for golden mahseer angling, which was banned in 2011.
world knowledge.Details: Nameri National Park is located in the foothills of the eastern Himalayas and shares its northern boundary with the Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary of Arunachal Pradesh. It is home to over 600 floral species and various wildlife, including Bengal tigers, Indian leopards, and numerous bird species. The park faces threats from logging and human-animal conflicts, particularly with elephants.

world knowledge.Name: Lengpui Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lengpui Airport is the first airport in India to be constructed by a State Government. It serves Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram, and was built to improve connectivity in the region. The airport was constructed at a cost of ₹ 979 crore and was completed in a record time of two years and two months. Before its construction, Aizawl was 130 km from the nearest railway head at Bairabi and 205 km from the nearest airport at Silchar.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was completed in February 1998, after two years and two months of construction.
Starting from 21 April 2021, Lengpui Airport is undergoing a renovation project that will result in an upgraded terminal and an elevated roadway.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a 2,500-metre runway with many hilly streams running underneath. It is one of the airports in India with a table top runway, which creates an optical illusion requiring a precise approach from pilots. The airport has a Cat I instrument landing system for low-visibility conditions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lengpui Airport is significant as it was the first airport in India to be constructed by a State Government. It has greatly improved connectivity for the people of Mizoram, particularly for Aizawl, the state capital.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Domestic airport serving Aizawl and surrounding regions.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is currently undergoing a renovation project funded under North East Special Infrastructure Development Schemes (NESIDS) and the Special Central Assistance (SCA) at a cost of Rs. 19.59 crores. It offers flights connecting to Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati, Imphal, and Silchar. A Helicopter service by Pawan Hans connects Aizawl with various towns in Mizoram.

world knowledge.Name: Conkouati-Douli National Park
world knowledge.Address: Near the villages of Cotovindou and Louléma along the border between Congo and Gabon, at the point of intersection with National Route 5
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 7,955 km² (including 4,121 km² of marine park and 3,833 km² of land)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Conkouati-Douli National Park is a UNESCO-recognised coastal national park established by the Presidential Decree No. 99-136 on 14 August 1999. It has been part of an active area of conservation since at least 1980 and includes areas of the former old reserve of Conkouati. The original reserve covered nearly 300,000 ha but was reduced to 144,294 ha by a legal provision in 1989. From 1994 to 1999, the IUCN recognised that the area was critically endangered and collaborated with PROGECAP-GEF Congo with financing from the World Bank. The park has been managed by various organizations, including the Ministry for National Forestry Commission and the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS), and currently by the NGO Noé since 2019.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established by the Presidential Decree No. 99-136 on 14 August 1999.
The IUCN recognised that the area was critically endangered and collaborated with PROGECAP-GEF Congo with financing from the World Bank.
The NGO Noé began managing the park's conservation initiatives.
A public-private partnership agreement (PPP) was signed, signaling a renewed commitment to biodiversity conservation, sustainable development, and community involvement.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is characterised by dense forests, mixed with wetlands, floodplain forests, and lagoons. It includes the Noumbi River, mangroves like Rhizophora racemosa and Avicennia nititta, and aquatic vegetation such as Vossia cuspidata and Ctenium newtonili. The savannas are dominated by various grasses and plants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is an important part of native local culture, with around 7,800 people living in and around the park divided into 31 villages. The coastal residents are mainly Vili people, an ethnic group of fishers and traders that settled there in the 13th century. The villages along the forest road contain a mix of over 30 different ethnic groups.
world knowledge.Details: The park is the most biodiverse in the country and includes the only protected marine area in Congo. It is home to around 7,000 central chimpanzees, 900 western lowland gorillas, 900 forest elephants, and many other species. It is a Ramsar site for its importance for migratory and wetland birds and has been designated an Important Bird Area (IBA) by BirdLife International. The park also has endangered turtle and dolphin populations. Local ecosystems are vulnerable to industrial threats from logging, mining, petroleum production, and commercial fishing. Since the beginning of 2024, the oil company Congo Holding United plans to drill for oil near and inside the park, posing a massive risk to its rich biodiversity and indigenous people.

world knowledge.Name: Lodi Gardens
world knowledge.Address: Between Khan Market and Safdarjung's Tomb on Lodi Road
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lodi Gardens is a city park in New Delhi, India, containing architectural works from the 15th century by the Lodi dynasty, who ruled parts of northern India and Pakistan from 1451 to 1526. The site includes Mohammed Shah's Tomb, the Tomb of Sikandar Lodi, the Shisha Gumbad, and the Bara Gumbad. It is now protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Bara Gumbad and mosque
Major_Events.Description: Built during the reign of Sikander Lodi, the Bara Gumbad was constructed as a gateway to either the attached three-domed mosque or a large walled enclosure.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Tomb of Mohammed Shah
Major_Events.Description: Built by Ala-ud-din Alam Shah as a tribute to Mohammed Shah, the last of the Sayyid dynasty rulers. The tomb is octagonal with Hindu-style chhatris and other architectural features.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gardens feature a blend of Hindu and Islamic architectural styles. Notable structures include the Bara Gumbad, Shisha Gumbad, Tomb of Sikandar Lodi, and Tomb of Mohammed Shah. The Bara Gumbad has a large rubble-construct dome, while the Shisha Gumbad is noted for its glazed tiles. The Tomb of Mohammed Shah includes Hindu-style chhatris, arches, verandahs, and sloping buttresses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lodi Gardens is an important archaeological site due to the limited remaining architecture from the Sayyid and Lodi periods. It showcases a unique blend of Hindu and Islamic architectural styles and serves as a popular spot for morning walks.
world knowledge.Details: The gardens are situated between Khan Market and Safdarjung's Tomb on Lodi Road. They contain several historical monuments, including the Bara Gumbad, Shisha Gumbad, Tomb of Sikandar Lodi, and Tomb of Mohammed Shah. The site is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

world knowledge.Name: Karachi Safari Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Karachi Safari Park, opened in 1970, is a public-funded, 'family-only' safari park. It was inaugurated by Lieutenant General Atiq-ur-Rehman and was an independent project of the then Karachi Municipal Corporation. In 1995, an independent zoo, safari, and aquarium department was created. It is now an independent wing of the Community Development Department of City District Government of Karachi and has been designated as a 'family park'.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by Lieutenant General Atiq-ur-Rehman.
An independent zoo, safari, and aquarium department was created.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features a zoo, viewing facilities like a chairlift and safari tracks, and two natural lakes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Designated as a 'family park', it serves as a significant recreational area for families in Karachi.
world knowledge.Details: Karachi Safari Park is an independent wing of the Community Development Department of City District Government of Karachi (defunct) and is a member of SAZARC.

world knowledge.Name: Universidad de las Américas Puebla
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1940 by Dr. Henry L. Cain and Dr. Paul V. Murray, originally as Mexico City College. It evolved into a significant educational institution in Latin America, known for its diverse academic programs and research initiatives.

Major_Events.Description: The university was added to the list of approved universities by the Veterans Administration, allowing veterans to study with financing from the United States' government.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to University of the Americas
Major_Events.Description: The institution changed its name to 'University of the Americas' and was divided into three schools: Mexico City College, School of Arts and Sciences, and the Graduate School.
The university moved to its new campus in Cholula, Puebla, funded by the Mary Street Jenkins Foundation and the International Development Agency.
The university became a member of the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools (SACS), one of the few in Latin America to achieve this accreditation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus includes 38 buildings on 180 acres, featuring a mix of modern and historical architecture, including the Capilla del Arte, a historical Art Nouveau style building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UDLAP is one of the most prestigious universities in Latin America, known for its academic excellence, research contributions, and cultural programs. It has a significant impact on regional development and education.
world knowledge.Details: UDLAP offers a wide range of academic programs and is known for its research initiatives, sports teams (the Aztecs), and cultural events. It has a unique housing system similar to those in the United States and is accredited by several educational bodies.

world knowledge.Name: Osaka Tower
world knowledge.Address: Beside the headquarters of Asahi Broadcasting Corporation (ABC), Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Osaka Tower was an observation and radio tower built in 1966. It served as a relay for radio communication for taxi companies and featured a two-story observation deck. The tower was closed to the public in 1997 due to heightened security measures and was demolished in 2009 after ABC relocated its headquarters.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was completed at a cost of 400 million yen, with an observation deck accommodating 270 persons and an elevator for 30 persons. 4,000 visitors attended the inauguration.
The 'Sky Studio' was installed on the second floor of the observation deck, broadcasting a morning show with weather, traffic conditions, etc.
The observation deck was closed to the public due to heightened security measures following incidents like the 1994 mail bomb incident.
The tower was demolished after ABC moved its headquarters to Fukushima-ku, Osaka, in 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower was constructed with metal tubing in a quadratic lattice structure, designed to handle vibrations and wind velocities up to 90 metres per second (300 ft/s). It was painted white below the observation deck and red and white above it.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Osaka Tower was a notable landmark in Osaka, serving both as an observation tower and a radio communication hub. It was a part of the city's skyline and cultural identity for over four decades.
world knowledge.Details: The tower had an elevator that could carry 30 persons up to the observation deck, which could accommodate 270 persons. It relayed radio communication for taxi companies and was a significant structure in Osaka until its demolition.

world knowledge.Name: Buriram Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Buriram Airport, also known as Buri Ram Airport, is located in Ron Thong subdistrict, Satuek district, Buriram province in northeastern Thailand. It was opened on 14 October 1996.

Major_Events.Description: The Department of Airports announced a 700 million baht second passenger terminal will be built at Buriram airport, increasing the airport's capacity from 750,000 per year to 1.7 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 04/22 with an asphalt surface measuring 2,100 by 45 metres (6,890 ft × 148 ft).
world knowledge.Details: In 2019, the Department of Airports announced plans to extend the length of the runway to accommodate larger aircraft in the future.

world knowledge.Name: Ala-Archa Nature Park
world knowledge.Address: Approximately 35 km south of Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1976, the Ala-Archa Nature Park is an alpine national park in the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan. It is named after the river Ala-Archa, which flows through it. The park covers about 165 square kilometers and includes the gorge of the river Ala-Archa and the surrounding mountains. The park is known for its diverse flora and fauna, including the rare snow leopard.

Major_Events.Event: First photograph of a snow leopard
Major_Events.Description: A park camera photographed a snow leopard for the first time in May 2017.
Every May 1, hundreds of people camp out in the valley and climb Mount Komsomolets for the Alpinada festival.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes a small reservoir on the Kargay-Bulak river, a Soviet climbing base (Ratsek Hut), and various trails leading to glaciers, peaks, and valleys.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, and the traditional esteem held by the Kyrgyz people for the archa (juniper) tree. It is also a popular destination for outdoor activities and has been recognized as the most popular tourist site in Kyrgyzstan.
world knowledge.Details: The park is open year-round and offers activities such as hiking, horse trekking, skiing, and mountain climbing. There is a nominal fee for entering the park. The park's altitude ranges from about 1,500 meters at the entrance to a maximum of 4,895 meters at Semenov-Tian-Shansky Peak. It includes more than 20 small and large glaciers and some 50 mountain peaks.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Nuevo Vivero
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Cívitas Nuevo Vivero is a multi-use stadium in Badajoz, Spain. It was built in 1999 to replace Estadio El Vivero, which was located in the east part of the city. The stadium is the home ground of CD Badajoz and has hosted several international football matches.

Major_Events.Description: Spain beat Cyprus 8–0 in a UEFA Euro 2000 qualification group match.
Spain beat Liechtenstein 4–0 in a qualification group match for the UEFA Euro 2008.
Spain beat Portugal 2–0 in a qualification game for the UEFA Women's Euro 2017.

Major_Events.Event: 2022 World Cup UEFA Group B match
Major_Events.Description: Spain beat Georgia 4–0 in a 2022 World Cup UEFA Group B match.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium is a purpose-built arena with a natural grass surface and a capacity of 14,898 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it hosts football matches for CD Badajoz and has been the venue for several international matches, including games for the Spain national team and the women's national team.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches and other sporting events

world knowledge.Name: L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue
world knowledge.Location: Southeastern France, on the Sorgue river
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as 'Insula', the town officially adopted the name of 'L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue' on 18 August 1890, taking the latter part of its name from the river Sorgue, to which it owed much. As early as the 12th century, the river served defensively as a moat around ramparts which surrounded the town until 1795. The river also served as a source of food and industry: fishing and artisan mills for oil, wheat, silk, paper, woolenry, rugs and dyeing. A busy commerce developed until there were two annual fairs and two weekly markets. The current Sunday open-air market originated on 9 November 1596.

Major_Events.Description: The town officially adopted the name of 'L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue' on 18 August 1890.
The current Sunday open-air market originated on 9 November 1596.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features many attractive water wheels throughout the town, still in working order.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue is famous for its many antique shops and hosts antique markets most Sundays. It has many waterside cafés and restaurants, all within walking distance of each other. The town is twinned with Penicuik in Scotland and Anagni in Italy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourism and commerce, particularly known for antiques and markets.
world knowledge.Details: L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue had a population of 20,042 as of 2019. Politically, the commune is in the arrondissement of Avignon within the department of Vaucluse, in the région of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur.

world knowledge.Name: Namysłów Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Namysłów Town Hall was built in the second half of the fourteenth century. Originally constructed in Gothic style, it was later rebuilt in the Renaissance style. It underwent renovation in 2002 and is recognized as one of the most beautiful cultural heritage points in Namysłów. It was added to the list of Registered Cultural Heritage in 1964.

Major_Events.Description: The town hall was renovated to preserve its historical and architectural significance.
The town hall was added to the list of Registered Cultural Heritage with the position 939/64.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built out of brick, the town hall resembles the letter L from a bird's eye view. The main building has two levels. The tower has a four-sided lower part and an eight-sided upper part with a walkway and pinnacles. The bulbous octagonal spire is Baroque, made from copper plate, and topped with a bearing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Namysłów, representing Gothic and Renaissance architectural styles. It is a central point in the old town square and serves as a symbol of the city's heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the municipal government in Namysłów, housing various institutions and authorities, including a ZUS branch, the Kluczbork Resident Prosecutor's Office, notaries, and Pod Aniołami Restaurant.
world knowledge.Details: Every day at 12.00, a Namysłów bugle call composed by Eugeniusz Odoj is played with three trumpets from the town hall.

world knowledge.Name: Charles Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 515.8 metres (1,692 ft), Width: 9.5 metres (31 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Charles Bridge is a medieval stone arch bridge that crosses the Vltava river in Prague, Czech Republic. Its construction started in 1357 under the auspices of King Charles IV, and finished in the early 15th century. The bridge replaced the old Judith Bridge built 1158–1172 that had been severely damaged by a flood in 1342. This new bridge was originally called Stone Bridge (Kamenný most) or Prague Bridge (Pražský most), but has been referred to as 'Charles Bridge' since 1870.

Major_Events.Description: A flood damaged three pillars.
The third arch broke down after one of the pillars lowered, being undermined by the water (repairs were finished in 1503).
The Old Town Bridge Tower served as a deterrent display of the severed heads of the victims to stop Czechs from further resistance.
The Swedes occupied the west bank of the Vltava, and as they tried to advance into the Old Town the heaviest fighting took place right on the bridge.
Five pillars were severely damaged and, although the arches did not break down, the traffic on the bridge had to be greatly restricted for some time.

Another disastrous flood struck Prague and severely damaged Charles Bridge. Three arches were torn down by the great pressure and two pillars collapsed from being undermined by the water, while others were partly damaged.

A capital repair of the bridge took place based on a collaboration among various scientific and cultural institutes. The stability of the pillars was reassured, all broken stone blocks were replaced, and the asphalt top was removed.
Google celebrated the 660th anniversary of Charles Bridge with a Google Doodle.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Charles Bridge is a stone arch bridge with a total length of 515.8 metres (1,692 ft) and a width of 9.5 metres (31 ft). It has 16 arches shielded by ice guards and is protected by three bridge towers. The bridge is decorated by a continuous alley of 30 statues and statuaries, most of them baroque-style, originally erected around 1700, but now all have been replaced by replicas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the only means of crossing the river Vltava until 1841, Charles Bridge was the most important connection between Prague Castle and the city's Old Town and adjacent areas. This land connection made Prague important as a trade route between Eastern and Western Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is currently undergoing a twenty-year process of structural inspections, restoration, and repairs. The process started in late 2019, and is expected to cost 45–60 million CZK (US$1.9–2.6 million). The avenue of 30 mostly Baroque statues and statuaries situated on the balustrade forms a unique connection of artistic styles with the underlying Gothic bridge. Most sculptures were erected between 1683 and 1714. They depict various saints and patron saints venerated at that time. The most prominent Bohemian sculptors of the time took part in decorating the bridge, such as Matthias Braun, Jan Brokoff, and his sons Michael Joseph and Ferdinand Maxmilian.

world knowledge.Name: University of Iowa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Iowa was founded on February 25, 1847, just 59 days after Iowa was admitted to the Union. It is the oldest and largest university in the state. The university was the first public university in the United States to admit men and women on an equal basis and has a history of pioneering in education, including the development of the Master of Fine Arts degree and the Iowa Writers' Workshop.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Iowa was founded on February 25, 1847, just 59 days after Iowa was admitted to the Union.
The university became the first public university in the United States to admit men and women on an equal basis.
Flood waters breached the Coralville Reservoir spillway, damaging more than 20 major campus buildings. The reconstruction and renovation work took a decade.
UNESCO designated Iowa City the world's third City of Literature, making it part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network.
A shooting took place on campus on November 1, 1991. Six people died in the shooting, including the perpetrator, and one other person was wounded.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Pentacrest reflects the Beaux-Arts in addition to Greek Revival architectural styles and the Collegiate Gothic architecture, which is dominant in sections of the campus east of the Iowa River. The Old Capitol was once the home of the state legislature and the primary government building for the State of Iowa but is now the symbolic heart of the university.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Iowa is a leading public research university with a strong emphasis on creative writing, arts, and sciences. It is home to the Iowa Writers' Workshop, which has produced numerous Pulitzer Prize winners. The university has a rich history of innovation in education and research.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Iowa is organized into 12 colleges offering more than 200 areas of study and 7 professional degrees. It is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity". The university's 22 varsity athletic teams, the Iowa Hawkeyes, compete in Division I of the NCAA and are members of the Big Ten Conference. The university is also known for its extensive collection of public art and its commitment to sustainability.

world knowledge.Name: Sumburgh Head Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sumburgh Head Lighthouse is the oldest lighthouse in Shetland, built by Robert Stevenson in 1821. It was automated in 1991, and the keepers' houses were converted into holiday accommodation. The foghorn, installed in 1906, was restored in 2015 and sounds on special occasions. The site is now owned by the Shetland Amenity Trust, which restored the facilities and opened a visitor center in 2014.

Major_Events.Description: A fog bell was presented after the loss of the Royal Victoria in 1864. The bell now hangs in the parish church at Dunrossness.
An active foghorn was installed, replacing the fog bell. It was originally traversable in azimuth.
The lighthouse was automated, and the keepers' houses were converted into holiday accommodation.
The foghorn was restored and now sounds on special occasions.
The Shetland Amenity Trust restored the lighthouse facilities and built a visitor center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 17-meter tall cylindrical masonry tower with a balcony and lantern, painted white with a black lantern and ochre trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sumburgh Head Lighthouse is a category A listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance. It is the oldest lighthouse in Shetland and represents the engineering legacy of Robert Stevenson. The surrounding area is a bird reserve managed by the RSPB.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse complex includes offices for the RSPB, which manages the surrounding bird reserve. The Northern Lighthouse Board operates the light, while the Shetland Amenity Trust owns the site. The foghorn was restored in 2015 and is sounded on special occasions.

world knowledge.Name: Glenveagh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Glenveagh is the second-largest national park in Ireland, located in County Donegal. It includes Glenveagh Castle and its grounds, Lough Veagh, and much of the Derryveagh Mountains. The park was established in 1986 and is the only national park in Ulster. The estate was founded by Captain John George Adair, who built Glenveagh Castle and evicted 44 families during the 1861 famine, earning him the nickname 'Black Jack Adair'. The estate passed through several owners before being bequeathed to the Irish state in the 1970s.

Major_Events.Description: Captain John George Adair evicted 44 families (224 people) from their blackhouses during the famine.
Golden eagles, which were formerly extirpated, were reintroduced into the park.
Glenveagh was officially established as a national park.
Many native and non-native trees and plants were cleared from the park, and the water and pipe system was updated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Glenveagh Castle and its gardens, which display a multitude of exotic and delicate plants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Glenveagh is culturally significant as the only national park in Ulster and the second-largest in Ireland. It is home to the largest herd of red deer in Ireland and reintroduced golden eagles. The park's history includes the controversial actions of its founder, Captain John George Adair.
world knowledge.Details: Glenveagh is managed by the NPWS National Parks and Wildlife Service. The park covers 170 square kilometres and includes much of the Derryveagh Mountains, Lough Veagh, and Glenveagh Castle on its shores.

world knowledge.Name: Nagoya TV Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nagoya TV Tower, now known as Chubu Electric MIRAI TOWER, is the oldest TV tower in Japan. It was completed in 1954 and is located in the center of Hisaya Ōdori Park. The tower has been a significant landmark in Nagoya and has undergone a name change in May 2021.

Major_Events.Description: The famous movie monster, Godzilla, pulled the tower down in the movie Mothra vs. Godzilla.
The tower was destroyed again in the 1992 remake, Godzilla vs. Mothra, this time by the monster Battra.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Chubu Electric MIRAI TOWER
Major_Events.Description: In May 2021, the tower was given a new name, the Chubu Electric MIRAI TOWER.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is 180 metres high and closely resembles the Eiffel Tower. It has two main observation decks at 90 metres (Sky Deck) and 100 metres (Sky Balcony), a restaurant and gallery at 30 metres, and previously included a bowling alley at the top.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Nagoya TV Tower is a historic and iconic structure in Japan, being the oldest TV tower in the country. It has appeared in popular culture, including movies like Mothra vs. Godzilla and the anime Seraph of the End.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a TV tower, it now serves as an observation and tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The tower is known under the nickname 'Thunder Tower' due to its nighttime illumination. It appeared in the anime Seraph of the End as a sniping point for characters Yoichi Saotome and Shinya Hiragi.

world knowledge.Name: Manitoba Theatre for Young People
world knowledge.Address: 2 Forks Market Road Winnipeg, Manitoba R3C 4X1
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1965 as Actors' Showcase, incorporated in 1977. Became a professional theatre devoted to young people in 1982 under Artistic Director Leslee Silverman. Moved to the Canwest Performing Arts Centre (now Shaw Performing Arts Center) in 1999.

Major_Events.Event: Move to Canwest Performing Arts Centre
Major_Events.Description: MTYP moved to a new 28,000 square feet facility in The Forks, built to house the theatre and its school.
MTYP's finance and administration manager embezzled over $90,000 from the theatre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Black-box style theatre with a 315-seat Main Stage and a smaller rehearsal hall. The complex includes four classroom studios, production and wardrobe shops, a greenroom, two full dressing rooms, a box office, and lobby.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of only two Theatre for Young Audiences (TYA) institutions in Canada with a permanent residence, and the only one offering a full season of plays for teens. Provides extensive theatre education and outreach programs, including free classes for Indigenous youth.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre for children and young adults, offering performances, education, and outreach programs.
world knowledge.Details: MTYP's annual attendance exceeds 100,000. The theatre school serves over 1,600 children and teens. The Aboriginal Arts Program is the largest of its kind in Canada, serving over 500 Indigenous youth. The operating budget is $2.2 million, with revenue from fundraising (20%), government grants (30%), and earned revenue (50%). The facility cost $5.6 million to build, with $1.2 million remaining debt as of 2012.

world knowledge.Name: Hereford Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: St Owen's Street, Hereford, Herefordshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hereford Town Hall is a municipal building that replaced the original Market Hall, an ornate timber Tudor-style building completed in 1620. The original structure was modified in 1792 due to structural concerns and later demolished in 1862. The current building was constructed in the early 20th century to serve as the seat of local government.

Major_Events.Description: Princess Beatrice of the United Kingdom laid the foundation stone for the new town hall on 13 May 1902.
Queen Elizabeth II, accompanied by the Duke of Edinburgh, visited the town hall and unveiled a plaque on 24 April 1957.
A programme of restoration works to the façade was completed in July 2019.
Following the loss of HMS Antelope during the Falklands War, the mast head and other artifacts were recovered and displayed in the town hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Henry Cheers in the Edwardian Baroque style, the building features terracotta facings, a symmetrical main frontage with seven bays, oriel windows, towers with domes, an arched doorway with rusticated columns, mullioned tri-partite windows, and an open pediment containing a coat of arms with an oculus above.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a Grade II* listed building and represents the civic pride and historical continuity of Hereford. It replaced the original Market Hall, which was a significant architectural landmark in its own right.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Municipal building and home of Hereford City Council
Notable_Visitors: Princess Beatrice of the United Kingdom
world knowledge.Details: The town hall was the headquarters of Hereford City Council for much of the 20th century and later served as the local seat of government for Hereford District Council. It became the home of the newly formed Hereford Town Council in April 2000, which was redesignated Hereford City Council in October 2000.

world knowledge.Name: Kiu Tsui Beach
world knowledge.Address: Kiu Tsui Beach, Sharp Island, Sai Kung District, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kiu Tsui Beach is a gazetted beach managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department of the Hong Kong Government. It has been rated as good to fair by the Environmental Protection Department for its water quality over the past twenty years.

Major_Events.Event: Temporary closure due to sewage leak
Major_Events.Description: The beach was temporarily closed due to sewage leakage into the sea near the beach from the Sai Kung Sewage Treatment Works, caused by Typhoon Mangkhut.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach features barbecue pits and is known for its scenic environment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kiu Tsui Beach is a quieter alternative to its neighbor, Hap Mun Bay Beach, and is appreciated for its water quality and scenic views of Pak Sha Chau, Cham Tau Chau, and Tai Chan Chau.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational beach with facilities for barbecuing and swimming.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is accessible by kai-to from Sai Kung Public Pier and is smaller and quieter compared to Hap Mun Bay Beach. It offers views of nearby islands and is managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department.

world knowledge.Name: Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhuj
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhuj is a Hindu temple constructed by Swaminarayan, the founder of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya. The temple was built in 1823 under the guidance of Vaishnavanand Swami, who was sent by Swaminarayan to oversee the construction. The temple was dedicated to the deities Nar Narayan and Radha Krishna. The temple was severely damaged in the earthquake on 26 January 2001, and plans were made to construct a new temple nearby.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was constructed under the guidance of Vaishnavanand Swami, who was sent by Swaminarayan to oversee the project.
The temple was severely damaged in the earthquake that struck Bhuj on 26 January 2001.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features a central sanctum sanctorum housing the idols of Nar Narayan Dev and Harikrishna Maharaj. The eastern dome seats RadhaKrishna Dev and Harikrishna Maharaj, while the western dome seats Ghanshyam Maharaj. The inner temple square, Roop Chowki, houses images of Ganapati and Hanuman.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The temple is culturally significant as it is associated with Swaminarayan, the founder of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya. It serves as a place of worship and a center for the community, especially for followers of the Swaminarayan faith.
world knowledge.Details: The temple was constructed by Swaminarayan and is dedicated to the deities Nar Narayan and Radha Krishna. It was severely damaged in the 2001 earthquake, and plans were made to construct a new temple nearby. The temple complex includes an Akshar Bhavan that treasures personal items of Swaminarayan.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Giulite Coutinho
world knowledge.Address: Mesquita, Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Giulite Coutinho, also known as Estádio Édson Passos, is a multi-use stadium built in 2000. It was inaugurated on January 23, 2000, with a match where America beat a Rio de Janeiro State Combined Team by 3–1. The first goal was scored by Sorato of the Rio de Janeiro State Combined Team.

Major_Events.Description: America beat a Rio de Janeiro State Combined Team by 3–1. The first goal was scored by Sorato.
The stadium's attendance record of 9,009 was set on March 5, 2006, when America and Flamengo drew 2–2.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface with a capacity of 13,544 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant for hosting home matches of Fluminense, America Football Club, and Nova Iguaçu, contributing to local football culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches and other sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by America Football Club and is also known as Estádio Édson Passos.

world knowledge.Name: Arniston House
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Temple, Midlothian, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arniston House is a historic Georgian mansion designed by William Adam in 1726 for Robert Dundas, the Lord President of the Court of Session. The western third of the house was added by John Adam in 1753. The estate was originally a royal hunting park in the Middle Ages and later owned by the Knights Templar. It came into the Dundas family in 1571 and has been expanded and improved over the centuries.

Major_Events.Description: William Adam designed the house for Robert Dundas, but construction was delayed due to financial issues and was completed after 1753 by John Adam.
Architects Wardrop and Brown added a new entrance hall to the north front.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is a three-storey Georgian mansion with a basement. The north entrance front features nine bays with a colossal order of Ionic columns and a pediment. The south garden front is plainer with a pediment. The interiors include a two-storey galleried saloon with decorative plasterwork by Joseph Enzer and Rococo dining and drawing rooms by the Adam brothers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arniston House is culturally significant as a well-preserved example of Georgian architecture and for its association with the Dundas family, prominent figures in Scottish history. It also reflects the architectural influence of James Gibbs and the landscape design of Thomas White.
world knowledge.Details: The house is still occupied by members of the Dundas family, who open it to the public for guided tours during the summer months. The estate includes a semi-formal park and a 19th-century formal garden.

world knowledge.Name: San Miguel Mission
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 24 feet (7.3 m) wide, 70 feet (21 m) long, and 25 feet (7.6 m) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: San Miguel Chapel is a Spanish colonial mission church in Santa Fe, New Mexico, originally built around 1610. It is often referred to as the oldest church building in the continental United States. The church was rebuilt twice, once in the mid to late 17th century, and again in 1710 following the Pueblo Revolt. The wooden reredos, which includes a wooden statue of Saint Michael dating back to at least 1709, was added in 1798.

Major_Events.Description: The Pueblo people rose up in a coordinated rebellion to drive the Spanish from New Mexico, damaging the church.

Major_Events.Event: Rebuilding under Don Agustín Flores Vergara
Major_Events.Description: The church was rebuilt under the direction of Don Agustín Flores Vergara, with the same layout as the earlier building, except that the apse was changed from rectangular to trapezoidal.
The church was restored, rebuilding the bell tower and stabilizing the walls with stone buttresses.
The church underwent remodeling, removing arched openings and a pitched metal roof added in 1887.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Adobe construction in the Romanesque fortress church style, with heavily buttressed walls and battlements on the flat roof. The church has a single rectangular nave and a trapezoidal apse. The walls are approximately 5 feet (1.5 m) thick. The ceiling is supported by wooden vigas, with two square beams dating to 1710. The choir loft is supported by a heavy, corbeled beam spanning the width of the nave.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: San Miguel Mission is often referred to as the oldest church building in the continental United States. It is a contributing property in the Barrio De Analco Historic District, a U.S. National Historic Landmark. The church represents the Spanish colonial mission efforts and the cultural blending of Spanish and native influences.
world knowledge.Details: The church's wooden reredos dates to 1798 and includes a wooden statue of St. Michael the Archangel from 1709. The bell tower once housed a bell mistakenly dated 1356, later corrected to 1856. The church is still active, with weekly Mass offered on the 1st Sunday of the month at 3pm as of 2020.

world knowledge.Name: United States Naval Observatory
world knowledge.Address: Northwest Washington, D.C., at the northwestern end of Embassy Row
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2000-foot circle of land atop Observatory Hill
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1830 as the Depot of Charts and Instruments, it is one of the oldest scientific agencies in the United States. It was relocated in 1893 to its current location in Northwest Washington, D.C. to escape light pollution. The observatory has contributed significantly to astronomy, timekeeping, and navigation, including the discovery of the moons of Mars and the development of universal time.

Major_Events.Description: The observatory was moved from Foggy Bottom to its current location to escape light pollution.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The facilities were listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The house on the grounds became the official residence of the vice president of the United States.
The observatory discovered the moons of Mars using the 26-inch refractor telescope.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The observatory features historic buildings and telescopes, including the 26-inch refractor telescope and the 40-inch Ritchey–Chrétien telescope. The site includes a large astronomy library and the vice president's residence.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The USNO is a key institution in the history of American astronomy and timekeeping. It has contributed to scientific advancements such as the measurement of the speed of light, solar eclipse observations, and the development of universal time. It also serves as the official residence of the vice president.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Scientific and military facility producing geopositioning, navigation, and timekeeping data for the U.S. Navy and Department of Defense.
world knowledge.Details: The USNO operates two Master Clock facilities, provides precise time to the GPS satellite constellation, and maintains a dark-sky observatory near Flagstaff, Arizona. It also houses the largest astronomy library in the United States and a significant collection of rare physics and astronomy books.

world knowledge.Name: Kadıköy Haldun Taner Stage
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The building was constructed as the first modern market hall in Istanbul between 1925 and 1927. It stood vacant for ten years before being used by the fire department and as a depot for scrap vehicles. Purposeful usage began in the 1940s until the mid-1970s. After renovation in 1984, it was assigned to Istanbul University for use as a conservatory in 1986. The ground floor was transformed into a theatre venue in 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The building was renovated and later assigned to Istanbul University.
The ground floor of the building was transformed into a theatre venue.

Major_Events.Event: Redesign for Istanbul 2010 European Capital of Culture
Major_Events.Description: The building was redesigned according to the needs of the City Theatres for the Istanbul 2010 European Capital of Culture events.
Restoration works were started by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality, planned to last 620 days.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally constructed as a modern market hall, the building was later repurposed for theatrical use. It underwent redesign in 2008 to meet the needs of the City Theatres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is named in honor of the Turkish playwright Haldun Taner (1915-1986) and serves as an important cultural venue in Istanbul.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a seating capacity of 286. It is owned by Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality and operated by its City Theatres (Şehir Tiyatroları) division.

world knowledge.Name: Cabo Polonio
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cabo Polonio is a hamlet located in the eastern coast of Uruguay in the Rocha Department. It has no roads leading to it and is accessible by walking through the dunes or by 4×4 vehicles. The region has no electricity or running water for the few houses of this town, and wind power and a few generators are used to power some of the posadas and grocery store. There is a lighthouse that gets power from the national grid. Residents obtain water from nearby water wells or collecting rain water.

Major_Events.Description: The government has included the area into the SNAP (Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas) National System of Protected Areas.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cabo Polonio is the setting for events spread over a 36-year period in Carolina de Robertis' novel Cantoras.
world knowledge.Details: Cabo Polonio sits on the tip of a peninsula that extends into the Atlantic Ocean. The ocean side of the peninsula experiences strong waves, while the bay interior to the peninsula is sheltered. At the top end, a lighthouse stands over boulders tumbling into the sea. Three small, rocky islands dot the coast nearby. Near to the village is a colony of sea lions. The shore also has mobile sand dunes, in which the sand is blown by the wind and the dunes change their position over time. The village land is shared by the Uruguayan government and private owners.

world knowledge.Name: Geauga Lake
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Geauga Lake was established in 1887 as a local recreation area adjacent to a lake of the same name. It evolved from a picnic and swimming spot into a major amusement park with rides, roller coasters, and a water park. Over the years, it underwent multiple ownership changes, expansions, and rebrandings, including as Six Flags Ohio and Six Flags Worlds of Adventure, before closing permanently in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: Geauga Lake was established as a recreation area with picnics and swimming.
A steam-powered carousel was installed, marking the beginning of the park's amusement ride offerings.
The park's first roller coaster, the Big Dipper, was constructed.
Olympic medalist Johnny Weissmuller set a new world record in the 220-yard freestyle swim in the park's pool.
A tornado caused significant damage, including to the Big Dipper, but the park was rebuilt.
A fire destroyed the park's bowling alley, theater, dance hall, and roller rink, leading to a shift in focus to rides and swimming.
Funtime, Inc. purchased the park and expanded its rides and amenities.
Premier Parks rebranded the park as Six Flags Ohio, adding new roller coasters and attractions.
Six Flags purchased SeaWorld Ohio and combined the two parks into Six Flags Worlds of Adventure.
Cedar Fair acquired the park and renamed it Geauga Lake once more.
Cedar Fair announced the permanent closure of the amusement park side, with the water park operating until 2016.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Geauga Lake featured a mix of amusement park structures, including roller coasters, water rides, and themed areas. Notable structures included the Big Dipper roller coaster, a hand-carved 1926 Marcus Illions carousel, and later additions like the Wildwater Kingdom water park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Geauga Lake was a beloved regional amusement park with a rich history spanning over a century. It was a significant recreational destination for families in Ohio and played a role in the development of amusement parks in the United States. Its closure marked the end of an era for many locals who cherished memories of the park.
world knowledge.Details: Geauga Lake's property has since been repurposed for housing developments, retail establishments, and a planned public park. The park's legacy is remembered through street names and plaques honoring its history.

world knowledge.Name: Albufera Natural Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Albufera Natural Park, located in the province of Valencia, Valencian Community, Spain, is a protected natural area. It was referred to by the Romans as Nacarum Stagnum and in Arabic poems as "Mirror of the Sun". The park was designated a natural park on July 8, 1986, by the Generalitat Valenciana. The area has a rich history, including its mention in the novel 'Cañas y barro' by Vicente Blasco Ibáñez in 1902. The park has undergone various legal and management changes over the years, including the approval of the Special Protection Plan in 1990 and the Natural Resources Management Plan in 1995.

Major_Events.Description: The Generalitat Valenciana designated the Albufera area as a natural park.
The Special Protection Plan document for the Natural Park was approved, though it was later overturned by the Supreme Court of Spain.

Major_Events.Event: Approval of Natural Resources Management Plan
Major_Events.Description: Decree 96/1995 approved the Natural Resources Management Plan (PORN) of the Albufera Hydrographic Basin.

Major_Events.Event: Approval of Albufera Master Plan for Use and Management
Major_Events.Description: Decree 259/2004 established the Albufera Master Plan for Use and Management (PRUG).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Albufera Natural Park features a shallow coastal lagoon with an average depth of 1 meter, surrounded by rice fields and a narrow sandy coastal bar stabilized by a pine forest. The park includes a network of ravines, acequias, and canals that have been in place since Roman and Muslim times.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Albufera is culturally and historically significant as one of the few preserved lagoons in the Valencian Community. It has been a subject of literary works and has played a role in the region's agricultural and fishing practices. The park supports endangered species and serves as a migratory corridor for numerous avian species.
world knowledge.Details: The Albufera Natural Park is subdivided into four regions or comarcas: Ribera Alta, Ribera Baixa, Horta Sud, and the City of Valencia. The park is accessed via several roads, including the El Saler highway (V-15) and the CV-401. The climate is Mediterranean, with mild temperatures and significant precipitation during the autumn season. The park's hydrological basin is primarily fed by the Júcar and Turia rivers, and it includes a network of acequias that collect water from springs and surrounding areas. The park is home to a variety of flora and fauna, including endangered species like the fartet and the samaruc.

world knowledge.Name: Princess Auto Stadium
world knowledge.Address: University of Manitoba, 315 Chancellor Matheson Road, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Princess Auto Stadium, formerly known as Investors Group Field and IG Field, is an outdoor stadium located on the University of Manitoba campus. It opened in 2013 and is home to the Winnipeg Blue Bombers of the Canadian Football League (CFL), the University of Manitoba Bisons football team, Valour FC of the Canadian Premier League (CPL), the Winnipeg Rifles of the Canadian Junior Football League (CJFL), and the Manitoba Fearless of the Western Women's Canadian Football League (WWCFL). The stadium was also a host venue for the 2015 FIFA Women's World Cup.

Major_Events.Event: First home game of the Winnipeg Blue Bombers
Major_Events.Description: The Winnipeg Blue Bombers played their first home game at Investors Group Field on June 27, 2013, losing 38–33 to the Montreal Alouettes.
The stadium hosted the 103rd Grey Cup in 2015.
Winnipeg was one of six Canadian cities that hosted the FIFA Women's World Cup. The stadium hosted several matches, including Group D matches and others.
The National Hockey League (NHL)'s Heritage Classic was held at the stadium on October 23, 2016, where the Winnipeg Jets lost 3–0 to the Edmonton Oilers.
An NFL preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and Oakland Raiders was held at the stadium on August 22, 2019.
The stadium is scheduled to host the 112th Grey Cup in 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a capacity of 32,343 and is partially covered with a corrugated metal roof. It includes a restaurant, 52 suites, a walk of fame, and other amenities. The playing surface is FieldTurf Vertex.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Winnipeg, hosting major events such as the Grey Cup, FIFA Women's World Cup, and NHL Heritage Classic. It is also home to multiple football teams, making it a central hub for sports in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium underwent a $2 million refurbishment ahead of the 2024 Blue Bombers season and in preparation for the 112th Grey Cup. It has faced several legal and financial disputes during its construction and operation, including lawsuits over construction deficiencies and cost overruns. The stadium's naming rights were originally held by Investors Group and later IG Wealth Management before being acquired by Princess Auto in 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Chaguaramas, Trinidad
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chaguaramas was leased to the United States in 1940 for the construction of a naval base under the Destroyers for Bases Agreement. The base was scaled back in 1956 and returned to Trinidad and Tobago control in 1963. It was also the location slated for the construction of the capital of the short-lived West Indies Federation and where the Treaty of Chaguaramas was signed in 1973, establishing CARICOM.

Major_Events.Event: Lease to the United States for Naval Base Trinidad
Major_Events.Description: Under the Destroyers for Bases Agreement, the peninsula was leased to the United States for the construction of a naval base.

Major_Events.Event: Return to Trinidad and Tobago control
Major_Events.Description: The area was returned to Trinidad and Tobago control after being scaled back in 1956.

Major_Events.Event: Signing of the Treaty of Chaguaramas
Major_Events.Description: The treaty established CARICOM, the Caribbean Community and Common Market.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chaguaramas is culturally significant as the site of the Treaty of Chaguaramas, which established CARICOM. It also supports one of the few remaining areas of dry forest in western Trinidad and is a popular recreational area for activities such as cycling, kayaking, and mountain biking.

Details.Marinas: Several marinas provide repair services, on-land boarding services, refueling, and mooring for yachts.
Details.Wildlife_Conservation: Hunting is strictly prohibited under the Conservation and Wildlife Act of 1960. Efforts have been made to preserve birds on Gasparee Island by maintaining large trees that provide shelter.
Details.Transportation: The area is about 14 km from Port of Spain, with most roadways lying close to the coastline.

world knowledge.Name: Eagles' Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eagles' Bridge is a bridge over the Perlovska River in downtown Sofia, Bulgaria. It was constructed in 1891 by Czech architect Václav Prošek, his brother Jozef, and his cousins Bohdan and Jiří. The bridge is named after the four statues of eagles on it, symbolically its protectors and patrons.

Major_Events.Description: Protests against construction on Vitosha mountain and the Dyuni nature spot on the Black Sea coast.
Scenes of violence during winter protests and massive peaceful gatherings during summer protests.
The bridge was repeatedly blocked by protesters with barricades, and tent camps were established.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Václav Prošek, with four statues of eagles symbolically protecting the bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant landmark in Sofia, symbolizing the city's history and culture. It is featured on the reverse of Bulgarian 20 levs banknotes issued in 1999 and 2007.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is located near the Vasil Levski National Stadium, the Monument to the Soviet Army, Borisova gradina park, Lake Ariana, and Sofia University. It is serviced by the Sofia University Metro Station of Sofia Metro M1 line and the M3 line Orlov most Metro Station, which opened in August 2020.

world knowledge.Name: Italian Chapel
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Italian Chapel is a highly ornate Catholic chapel built during the Second World War by Italian prisoners of war, who were housed on Lamb Holm while constructing the Churchill Barriers. The chapel was constructed from limited materials, primarily Nissen huts, and decorated by the prisoners, most notably Domenico Chiocchetti. It was restored in the 1960s and 1990s and remains a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of reconciliation.

Major_Events.Description: Domenico Chiocchetti returned to assist in the restoration of the chapel.
A special Mass was held to mark the 70th anniversary of the chapel, with Angela Chiocchetti, daughter of Domenico Chiocchetti, singing Panis angelicus.
Professional art restorer Antonella Papa restored the chapel's frescoes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The chapel is constructed from two Nissen huts joined end-to-end, with a corrugated interior covered in plasterboard. The altar and altar rail were made from concrete, and the interior was decorated by the prisoners. The facade is made of concrete, concealing the shape of the hut and giving the appearance of a traditional church. Light holders were made from corned beef tins, and the baptismal font was crafted from a car exhaust covered in concrete.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Italian Chapel is a symbol of reconciliation and a testament to the creativity and resilience of the Italian prisoners of war. It is a popular tourist attraction and a Category A listed building, representing a unique piece of wartime history and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Place of worship and tourist attraction
world knowledge.Details: The chapel is still used for worship and receives over 100,000 visitors annually. It has been the subject of books by Philip Paris and a novel by Kirsten Mckenzie. The chapel's frescoes were restored by Antonella Papa in 2015 and 2017.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Sorell Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cape Sorell Lighthouse was constructed and first lit in 1899. It is the only structure remaining from a brick complex that originally included the tower, three houses, and an engine room. The station was automated in 1971 and converted to solar power in 1998. Further automation occurred in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was constructed and first lit in 1899.
The station was automated in 1971.
The light was converted to solar power in 1998.
Further automation occurred in 2012.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 40-metre-high conical brick tower with a balcony and lantern. It is marked with a white tower and lantern dome, and a grey lantern.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cape Sorell Lighthouse is heritage-listed on the Australian Heritage Register, reflecting its historical and cultural importance as a navigational aid and remnant of maritime history.

Details.Light_Characteristic: Group of two flashes every fifteen seconds (Fl (2) 15s.)
Details.Light_Range: White: 32 kilometres (20 mi), Red: 19 kilometres (12 mi)

world knowledge.Name: Daejeon Convention Center
world knowledge.Address: 107 Expo-ro, Yuseong District, Daejeon, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Daejeon Convention Center (DCC) is the sole convention center for the city of Daejeon, managed by the Daejeon Tourism Organization. The first building, DCC1, was opened in 2008, followed by the larger DCC2 in 2022, which was built on the site of the former Daejeon Trade Exhibition Hall.

Major_Events.Description: The first building of the Daejeon Convention Center, known as DCC1, was opened with four exhibition halls and three medium-sized meeting rooms on the first floor, and two grand ballrooms on the second floor.

The second building, DCC2, was opened with a usable space of 49,754 square meters, roughly four times the size of DCC1. It can accommodate 8,000 people and features four exhibition halls on the first floor and three meeting rooms on the third floor.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: DCC1 and DCC2 are multi-story structures designed for exhibition and conference purposes. DCC2 is a three-story building with four exhibition halls on the first floor and three meeting rooms on the third floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Daejeon Convention Center is a key facility for hosting exhibitions, conferences, and other large-scale events in Daejeon, contributing to the city's tourism and economic development.
world knowledge.Details: DCC2 was built on the site of the former Daejeon Trade Exhibition Hall. The center is managed by the Daejeon Tourism Organization and is the sole convention center in the city.

world knowledge.Name: Kilrush
world knowledge.Location: Near the mouth of the River Shannon in the south-west of County Clare
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 16th Century (town origins), major development in the 18th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kilrush, meaning 'Church of the Woods', has existed since the 16th century with evidence of an older church ruin suggesting a much older history. The Vandeleur family, of Dutch origin, became prominent landlords in the 18th century, developing the town significantly. The town prospered during the Napoleonic Wars but suffered during the Great Famine (1845–1849). The arrival of the West Clare Railway in the late 19th century helped the town recover. Kilrush is now a listed Heritage Town of Ireland.

Major_Events.Description: Brought much hardship to Kilrush, with famine, evictions, fever, and cholera reducing the population significantly.
Kilrush was the host venue for the National Famine Commemoration.
Kilrush was twinned with the town of Plouzané in Brittany, France.
Kilrush won a gold medal in the European-wide horticultural and environmental competition.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town layout was designed by John Ormsby Vandeleur, with many street names deriving from Vandeleur family names. Notable buildings include Kilrush Town Hall (completed in 1808) and the now-demolished Kilrush House (built in 1808). The old port now features a 120-berth marina.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kilrush is a listed Heritage Town of Ireland and was once part of the West Clare Gaeltacht (Irish-speaking community). It has a rich history tied to the Vandeleur family and the Great Famine. The town hosts a 1500-year-old monastic settlement at Scattery Island, founded by St. Senan, featuring one of the oldest and tallest round towers in Ireland.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic coastal town with tourism, maritime activities, and retail services.

Details.Transportation: Kilrush is on the N67 and N68 roads, with bus services by Bus Éireann and Clare Bus. The nearest airport is Shannon Airport. The town was once a terminus of the West Clare Railway, now partially restored as a tourist attraction.
Details.Education: Kilrush has two primary schools (St. Senans NS and Gaelscoil Uí Choimin) and one secondary school (Kilrush Community School).
Details.Recreation: Kilrush has an 18-hole golf course, the Western Yacht Club, and sports facilities for tennis, football, rugby, and athletics. The West Clare Triathlon Club is based here.
Details.Wildlife: A large pod of Bottlenose dolphins resides year-round in the Shannon estuary, with dolphin-watching tours available.
Details.Economy: Historically reliant on agriculture and trade, the town saw economic boosts from the Moneypoint power station (now declining) and modern retailers like Tesco and Aldi.
Details.Tourist_Attractions: Scattery Island, Kilrush Creek Marina, Vandeleur Walled Garden, and the restored West Clare Railway section at Moyasta.

image_name: Basilica of Saints Nazarius and Celsus

world knowledge.Name: Basilica of Saints Nazarius and Celsus
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Internally measuring 59 m in total length, 16 m in nave width, and 36 m along the transept
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 6th century (original), first half of the 12th century (completed), end of the 13th century (reconstructed)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The original church is thought to have been constructed in the 6th century during the reign of Theodoric the Great, ruler of the Visigoths. It was built on the site of a Carolingian cathedral. Around the end of the 13th century, the cathedral was reconstructed in the Gothic style. It remained the cathedral of Carcassonne until 1803. The church was elevated to a minor basilica in 1898.

Major_Events.Description: Pope Urban II visited the town and blessed the building materials for the construction of the cathedral.
The church was elevated to a minor basilica.
The Church of Saints Nazarius and Celsus obtained the status of historical monument.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The basilica's floor plan is based on a Latin cross. The oldest part is the Romanesque tripartite nave. The main entrance is a Romanesque portal of five receding arches over two doors. The transept and choir were rebuilt in the Gothic style. The central stained glass window of the choir from 1280 is one of the oldest ones in the south of France.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a national monument and represents the Gothic-Romanesque architectural tradition. The basilica is historically significant as it was the cathedral of Carcassonne until 1803 and is associated with important historical figures and events.
world knowledge.Details: The sandstone basilica features a fortress façade on the west wall, common for medieval Languedocian church buildings. The larger windows in the Gothic part permit better illumination compared to the darker Romanesque nave. The central stained glass window depicts the life of Jesus in 16 medallions.

world knowledge.Name: Bridge of Sighs, Cambridge
world knowledge.Address: St John's College, Cambridge, Cambridge, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bridge of Sighs in Cambridge, England is a stone covered bridge at St John's College, Cambridge. It was built in 1831 and crosses the River Cam between the college's Third Court and New Court. The architect was Henry Hutchinson. It is named after the Bridge of Sighs in Venice, although they have little architecturally in common beyond the fact that they are both covered bridges with arched bases. The bridge, a Grade I listed building, is a Cambridge attraction and Queen Victoria is said to have loved it more than any other spot in the city.

Major_Events.Description: A 1928 Austin 7 was punted down the river using four punts that had been lashed together, then hoisted up under the bridge using ropes.
A Bond or Reliant Regal three-wheeler car was dangled under the bridge.
The bridge was a filming location for Elizabeth: The Golden Age.
The bridge was a filming location for The Theory of Everything.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Covered arch bridge made of stone, designed in the Gothic Revival style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a Grade I listed building and a notable attraction in Cambridge. It has been a favorite spot of notable figures such as Queen Victoria and former Singaporean Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Pedestrian bridge connecting parts of St John's College.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge can be seen in the music video for the song "High Hopes" by Pink Floyd. It was a filming location for Elizabeth: The Golden Age in 2007 and The Theory of Everything in 2014.

world knowledge.Name: Lanhydrock House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lanhydrock House, a country house and estate in Cornwall, UK, dates from the 1620s. It was acquired by Sir Richard Robartes in 1620 and later passed through the Robartes and Agar-Robartes families. The house was extensively rebuilt after a fire in 1881. It has been owned and managed by the National Trust since 1953.

Major_Events.Description: A major fire destroyed the south wing and caused extensive damage to the central section. The fire started in the kitchen and was fanned by strong winds. The house was rebuilt in the following years.
The 7th Viscount Clifden gave the house and approximately 160 hectares of parkland to the National Trust to manage death duties, ensuring its preservation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is constructed of grey granite with a four-sided layout around a central courtyard. The current building largely dates from late Victorian times, with a U-shaped plan. The Long Gallery in the north wing features fine plaster work.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lanhydrock House is a Grade I listed building and is significant for its historical architecture and extensive Victorian collections. It is also notable for its gardens and ancient woodland.
world knowledge.Details: The house is open to the public and offers one of the longest tours of any National Trust property. It has been used as a filming location, including for a 1996 film version of Twelfth Night. The estate includes an Important Plant Area designated for its ancient woodland and lichens.

world knowledge.Name: Shaikh Zayed University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shaikh Zayed University (SZU), originally named Afghan University Peshawar, was established in 2000 in Peshawar. It was relocated to Khost by the order of former Afghan President Hamid Karzai and officially registered in 2003. The university was named after Shaikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the first President of the United Arab Emirates, who sponsored the construction of its campus in Khost. The new campus was inaugurated in March 2008.

Major_Events.Description: Originally established as Afghan University Peshawar.
Moved to Khost by order of former Afghan President Hamid Karzai.
New campus officially inaugurated.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SZU is a significant educational institution in Afghanistan, named after Shaikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, reflecting the UAE's support for Afghan education. It is the only university in Afghanistan with a faculty in computer science and one of 11 institutions with e-learning facilities.
world knowledge.Details: SZU has 9 faculties and more than 3,000 students. It includes a private radio station for journalism, a hostel for students, and medical training at Khost Hospital. The university provides sports facilities and a library for students. It is supported by USAID for e-learning facilities.

world knowledge.Name: University of Regina
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Regina was founded in 1911 as a private denominational high school of the Methodist Church of Canada. It began an association with the University of Saskatchewan as a junior college in 1925, became the Regina Campus of the University of Saskatchewan in 1961, and achieved autonomy as the University of Regina in 1974. The university has grown significantly, with a focus on experiential learning and research.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as a private denominational high school of the Methodist Church of Canada.

Major_Events.Event: Association with the University of Saskatchewan
Major_Events.Description: Became a junior college offering accredited university courses.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed as Regina Campus of the University of Saskatchewan
Major_Events.Description: Attained degree-granting status as a second campus of the University of Saskatchewan.

Major_Events.Event: Achieved autonomy as the University of Regina
Major_Events.Description: Became an independent university.
The university hosted the Canada Summer Games, with many events taking place in the newly completed Centre for Kinesiology, Health and Sport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original campus design and initial buildings were in a stark concrete modernist style by Minoru Yamasaki, the architect of the original World Trade Center in New York. The campus features interconnected buildings with sunken, landscaped courts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Regina is culturally significant as a major educational institution in Saskatchewan, with a focus on experiential learning, research, and community engagement. It has a strong emphasis on Indigenous education and support for Francophone communities.
