world knowledge.Details: The University of Regina offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs, including cooperative education and internships. It has a significant international student population and is known for its commitment to Indigenous education and support for Francophone communities. The university is also home to several federated and affiliated colleges, including Campion College, Luther College, and the First Nations University of Canada.

world knowledge.Name: Inverquharity Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Inverquharity Castle is a 15th-century tower house constructed by Alexander Ogilvie, 2nd Lord Inverquharity. The lands came to the Ogilvie family around 1420. A wing was added in the 16th century to form an L-plan castle. It was later sold in the late 18th century, decayed, and was restored in the 1960s.

Major_Events.Description: A dispute between Alexander Ogilvy of Inverquharity and the son of the Earl of Crawford culminated in this battle, where both were killed.
The castle was sold for £611,000 after being restored and inhabited by the previous owners for 40 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a rectangular tower, later expanded into a four-storey L-plan castle. Features a 15th-century yett (iron gate). Restored in the 1960s with the wing rebuilt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A Category A listed building, representing Scottish medieval architecture and the historical conflicts of the Ogilvie family.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Private family home (originally a defensive tower house).
world knowledge.Details: Featured in a BBC documentary in 2014 about its sale. The original iron gate (yett) is still in place.

world knowledge.Name: Beverley Minster
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beverley Minster, originally a collegiate church, was founded by Saint John of Beverley around 700 AD. It survived the Dissolution of the Monasteries as a parish church and is now one of the largest parish churches in the UK. The church has undergone several reconstructions and expansions, particularly after a fire in 1188, and is a Grade I listed building. It is known for its Gothic architecture and historical significance as a pilgrimage site.

Major_Events.Description: A fire seriously damaged the minster and the town, leading to a complete rebuilding of much of the church.
The Black Death likely halted construction work on the nave.
The minster was reduced to the status of a parish church, and the college of secular canons was dissolved.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beverley Minster is a Gothic masterpiece with English Gothic style. It features Purbeck Marble shafts, stiff-leaf carving, and a richly decorated canopy over the tomb of Lady Eleanor Percy. The church also includes 68 16th-century misericords, a frith stool from Anglo-Saxon times, and a massive treadwheel crane in the central tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Beverley Minster is culturally and historically important due to its origins as a pilgrimage site for Saint John of Beverley, its architectural significance as a Gothic masterpiece, and its role in the religious and social history of England.
world knowledge.Details: Beverley Minster has been featured in various films and TV series, including 'Lease of Life' (1954), 'Victoria' (2016-7), 'King Charles III' (2017), and 'Gunpowder' (2017). The church also contains a large organ with an original manual from 1769, which has been expanded and restored over the years.

world knowledge.Name: Massey Hall
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 16,000 sq ft (1,500 m2) in Phase One; 124,000 sq ft (11,500 m2) in Phase Two
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Massey Hall is a performing arts theatre in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, opened in 1894. It was a gift to the people of Toronto from industrialist Hart Massey, built in memory of his son Charles. The hall has hosted a wide range of events, including concerts, public memorials, speaking tours, and boxing matches. It was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981 and underwent major renovations from 2013 to 2022.

Major_Events.Description: A notable jazz concert featuring Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, Bud Powell, Charles Mingus, and Max Roach.
Neil Young's performance was recorded and later released as a live album.
Rush recorded the live album at Massey Hall.
Ronnie Hawkins celebrated his 60th birthday with a concert at Massey Hall.
Matthew Good's performance was released as a live album.
Folk-rock band Whitehorse released an EP comprising covers of songs by other musicians who had played the hall.
Canadian rock band Spirit of the West performed at Massey Hall, documented in a film.
Russell Peters' appearances were recorded for his Netflix stand-up special.
The Tragically Hip performed with Feist on lead vocals.
Singer-songwriter Ron Sexsmith staged a retrospective concert at the hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Massey Hall features a neoclassical facade with Moorish arches inspired by the Alhambra Palace and Louis Sullivan's Chicago Auditorium. The interior is Moorish Revival architecture, and the foyer is finished in Art Deco style. The hall has 30 stained glass windows depicting famous composers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Massey Hall is culturally significant as a historic performing arts venue known for its outstanding acoustics and extensive history of concerts by artists of many musical genres. It was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981.
Notable_Visitors: Duke and Duchess of Cornwall and York (future King George V and Queen Mary)
world knowledge.Details: Massey Hall is operated by The Corporation of Massey Hall and Roy Thomson Hall, a non-profit charitable organization. It underwent a two-phase renovation from 2013 to 2022, which included the construction of a new seven-story addition called the Allied Music Centre. The renovation restored the hall's historic elements and introduced modern amenities, including a retractable seating system, enhanced audio and lighting systems, and improved accessibility.

world knowledge.Name: Kaliningrad Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was constructed for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, hosted four matches during the tournament, and replaced the Baltika Stadium as the home of FC Baltika Kaliningrad. The project faced challenges, including bankruptcy of the initial construction company and flooding risks due to its location on Oktyabrsky Island.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted four matches during the tournament.
The first match was played on 11 April 2018 between FC Baltika and PFC Krylia Sovetov Samara.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium is a two-tier structure with a VIP section, equipped with modern security systems and over 700 CCTV cameras. Its design is based on the Allianz Arena in Munich, which hosted matches during the 2006 World Cup in Germany.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant as the westernmost venue of the 2018 FIFA World Cup and serves as a modern sports and entertainment hub in Kaliningrad.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches, other sporting events, conferences, and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was initially named Kaliningrad Stadium but was later rebranded as Rostec Arena for sponsorship reasons in August 2023. The construction cost exceeded the anticipated budget, reaching €257 million. The seating capacity was reduced from 35,016 to 25,000 after the World Cup for FC Baltika Kaliningrad's use. The stadium is equipped with advanced security systems, including extensive CCTV coverage.

world knowledge.Name: Errigal
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 751 m (2,464 ft) elevation, 688 m (2,257 ft) prominence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Errigal is the tallest peak of the Derryveagh Mountains and the tallest peak in County Donegal. It is also the most southern and the highest of the mountain chain called the 'Seven Sisters'. The mountain is known for its pinkish glow of quartzite in the setting sun and its ever-changing shape depending on the viewing direction. In legend, Errigal is said to have been named by the Fir Bolg who worshipped it as they had Mount Olympus. The name comes from the Old Irish airecal, meaning 'oratory', possibly referring to the mountain as a place of prayer.

Major_Events.Description: Errigal was voted 'Ireland's Most Iconic Mountain' by Walking & Hiking Ireland.
Fáilte Ireland apologised for using the name 'Mount Errigal' in its brochure, rather than the proper name.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mountain composed of quartzite, known for its pinkish glow in the setting sun and ever-changing shape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Errigal is culturally significant as the tallest peak in County Donegal and part of the 'Seven Sisters' mountain chain. It holds legendary status among the Fir Bolg and is a popular destination for hikers and nature enthusiasts.
world knowledge.Details: Errigal is part of the Derryveagh Mountains and is the most southern, steepest, and highest of the 'Seven Sisters' mountain chain. The nearest peak is Mackoght, also known as Little Errigal or Wee Errigal. The mountain is noted for its quartzite glow and changing shape. The official name is An Earagail or Errigal, and it should not be confused with the hotel named 'Mount Errigal' in Letterkenny.

world knowledge.Name: Gordie Howe International Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Detroit, Michigan, USA, and Windsor, Ontario, Canada
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2.5 km (1.6 mi) in length, 37.5 m (123 ft) in width, 220 m (722 ft) in height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gordie Howe International Bridge, initially proposed in the early 2000s, was developed to provide a new international crossing between Detroit and Windsor, addressing traffic flow issues and reducing reliance on the privately owned Ambassador Bridge. The project faced significant opposition from Ambassador Bridge owner Manuel Moroun, who filed lawsuits to halt construction. The bridge is named after Canadian ice hockey legend Gordie Howe, who played for the Detroit Red Wings. Construction began in 2018 and is expected to be completed by September 2025.

Major_Events.Description: The U.S. and Canadian governments confirmed the construction of a new border crossing between Detroit and Windsor.
Environmental permits for the project were approved in both the U.S. and Canada.
Construction officially began after the selection of the 'Bridging North America' consortium.
The bridge was officially named after Gordie Howe during an event attended by Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper.
The U.S. and Canadian bridge towers reached their final heights of 220 m (722 ft).
The two sides of the bridge were permanently connected in June 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a cable-stayed design with two A-shaped towers, each 220 m (722 ft) tall. It features a 853 m (2,800 ft) main span, the longest of any cable-stayed bridge in North America. The bridge includes six lanes for automotive traffic and a dedicated bicycle and pedestrian path. The road deck is supported by 216 cable stays, and the bridge has a clearance of 46 m (151 ft) above the Detroit River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes the strong economic and cultural ties between Canada and the United States. It is named after Gordie Howe, a hockey legend who bridged Canadian and American sports culture. The project also includes public art and community benefits, reflecting its importance to local residents on both sides of the border.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To provide a high-capacity, uninterrupted freeway connection between Interstate 75 in Michigan and Highway 401 in Ontario, facilitating trade and travel between the U.S. and Canada.

Details.Toll_Collection: Tolls will be collected on the Canadian side only.
Details.Community_Benefits: US$20 million allocated for local community projects, including park improvements and home renovations.
Details.Public_Art: Includes murals by local artists, a sculpture by Michael Belmore, and architectural lighting by Douglas Coupland.
Details.Connections: Links to the Rt. Hon. Herb Gray Parkway in Canada and Interstate 75 in the U.S., with a multi-use path connecting to regional trail networks.

world knowledge.Name: The Kagawa Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kagawa Museum is a prefectural museum in Takamatsu, Japan, dedicated to the history and art of Kagawa Prefecture. The museum opened in 2008, consolidating the three institutions of the Kagawa Prefectural Cultural Hall (opened 1966); Seto Inland Sea Folk History Museum (opened 1973); and Kagawa History Museum (opened 1999); the first two institutions now operate as annexes of The Kagawa Museum.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Kagawa Prefectural Cultural Hall
Major_Events.Description: One of the precursor institutions to The Kagawa Museum.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Seto Inland Sea Folk History Museum
Major_Events.Description: One of the precursor institutions to The Kagawa Museum.
One of the precursor institutions to The Kagawa Museum.
The three precursor institutions were consolidated into The Kagawa Museum, with the first two operating as annexes.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is dedicated to preserving and showcasing the history and art of Kagawa Prefecture, making it an important cultural institution in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The Kagawa Museum (香川県立ミュージアム, Kagawa Kenritsu Myūjiamu) is a prefectural museum in Takamatsu, Japan. This article related to a museum in Japan is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Juhu
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Juhu, originally an island, was known as 'Juvem' by the Portuguese. It was inhabited by Agris, Kunbis, and Koli people. The Church of St. Joseph was built in 1853. In the 1890s, Jamsetji Tata planned to develop the area but the scheme was abandoned after his death. The Bombay Flying Club commenced operations in 1929. Juhu has been a significant location in Indian aviation history and was a key site during the Indian independence movement.

Major_Events.Event: Maiden voyage of J. R. D. Tata
Major_Events.Description: J. R. D. Tata made his maiden voyage to Juhu Airport from Drigh Road airstrip, Karachi, via Ahmedabad, carrying mail in a Puss Moth aircraft.
Mahatma Gandhi visited Mumbai and took several walks along Juhu Beach. A famous photograph of him poking his grandson Kanaa during a walk on the beach was taken.
Bhaktivedanta Swami (Srila Prabhupada) started the Hare Krishna Movement and built ISKCON Temple in Juhu.
A group of terror suspects detonated a bomb in a Juhu hotel, as well as in a number of other locations.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Juhu is culturally significant as a historical site in Indian aviation, a location associated with the Indian independence movement, and as a hub for Bollywood celebrities and Mumbai's business elite. It is also known for the annual Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations.
world knowledge.Details: Juhu is known for its beach, which is a tourist attraction and a destination for shooting films. The area is home to many Bollywood celebrities and is referred to as the 'Beverly Hills of Bollywood'. The Juhu Citizen Welfare Group, formed in 2002, represents the activism of Juhu residents.

world knowledge.Name: Matsushima
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Matsushima is a group of islands known for their scenic beauty, considered one of the Three Views of Japan. It has been celebrated in poetry and visited by notable figures like Matsuo Bashō.

Major_Events.Description: Despite its proximity to the disaster, Matsushima suffered relatively little damage due to protection by the islands. The initial tsunami was 3.2 metres, followed by a second wave of 3.8 metres. Three people were confirmed killed in Matsushima, with 18 killed while out of town.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural landscape featuring pine-covered islands
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Matsushima is celebrated as one of the Three Views of Japan and has inspired poetry and art. Nearby cultural properties include Zuigan-ji, Entsū-in, Kanrantei, and the Satohama shell mound.
world knowledge.Details: Matsushima is accessible from Sendai by train, with Matsushima-Kaigan Station near major attractions. Tourists can view the islands from cruise boats or rent bikes to explore the shore. The area offers four well-known viewing spots: Magnificent View, Beautiful View, Enchanting View, and Grand View.

world knowledge.Name: Castelvecchio Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Castelvecchio Museum is located in a medieval castle in Verona, Italy. The museum underwent restoration by architect Carlo Scarpa between 1959 and 1973, which enhanced the building's appearance and exhibits. Scarpa's architectural style is evident in details like doorways, staircases, furnishings, and fixtures designed for specific artworks. The renovation balanced new and old elements, revealing the original building's history.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum showcases Carlo Scarpa's architectural style, with detailed designs for doorways, staircases, furnishings, and fixtures. The renovation carefully balanced new and old elements, revealing the history of the original building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its collection of sculpture, statues, paintings, ancient weapons, ceramics, gold works, miniatures, and old bells. It also features numerous paintings and frescoes from the 14th century.
world knowledge.Details: The museum displays a collection of sculpture, mostly from the Romanesque period of Verona, and paintings, including numerous works from the 14th century.

world knowledge.Name: Mackinac Bridge
world knowledge.Address: St. Ignace and Mackinaw City, Michigan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mackinac Bridge connects the Upper and Lower peninsulas of Michigan. Envisioned since the 1880s, it was designed by engineer David B. Steinman and completed in 1957 after decades of planning and construction struggles. It replaced ferry services and became an iconic symbol of Michigan.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge opened to traffic on November 1, 1957, and was formally dedicated on June 25, 1958.
The bridge achieved its 100 millionth crossing on June 25, 1998.
The 50th anniversary of the bridge's opening was celebrated on November 1, 2007.

Major_Events.Event: National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark Designation
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was designated as a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark by the American Society of Civil Engineers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge design with deep stiffening trusses and an open-grid roadway to reduce wind resistance. The road deck is shaped as an airfoil for stability in high winds up to 150 mph (240 km/h).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an iconic symbol of Michigan and a vital transportation link between the state's two peninsulas. It is also a significant engineering achievement and a popular tourist destination.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (connects Upper and Lower peninsulas of Michigan via Interstate 75)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has a toll system, with current rates at $4.00 for automobiles and $5.00 per axle for trucks. It undergoes continuous maintenance, including a seven-year painting cycle. The bridge is featured in various media, including documentaries, TV shows, and commemorative stamps.

world knowledge.Name: Butler County Courthouse (Kansas)
world knowledge.Address: 205 W. Central Avenue, El Dorado, Kansas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Butler County Courthouse was constructed in 1909 in El Dorado, Kansas, designed by George P. Washburn & Sons. It serves as the main county courthouse for Butler County, which was organized on February 11, 1859. The courthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was completed and began serving as the main county courthouse for Butler County.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its historical and architectural significance and added to the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romanesque Revival style, featuring a central clock tower, four octagonal corner towers, a statue of the Goddess of Justice, and a hipped roof with cross gables. Constructed with red brick, typical of George P. Washburn's designs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a notable example of Romanesque Revival architecture and represents the work of architect George P. Washburn. It is one of nine surviving Romanesque courthouses designed by Washburn and serves as a historical and functional landmark in Butler County.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse is still in operation and offers self-guided tours during normal working hours. The County Clerk maintains land records from 1887 and birth and death records from 1887 to 1911.

world knowledge.Name: Wrigley Mansion
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Over 16,000 square feet (1,500 m²), 24 rooms, 12 bathrooms
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wrigley Mansion in Phoenix, Arizona, is a landmark building constructed between 1929 and 1931 by chewing-gum magnate William Wrigley Jr. It is also known as William Wrigley Jr. Winter Cottage and as La Colina Solana. William Wrigley died in 1932, shortly after its completion.

Major_Events.Description: Geordie Hormel bought the mansion and made it available for meetings, conventions and similar functions.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Wrigley Mansion was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mission/Spanish Revival and Spanish Colonial styles, extensive tilework shipped from Wrigley's factory in Catalina, designed by architect Earl Heitschmidt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mansion is a designated Phoenix Point of Pride and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It represents the legacy of William Wrigley Jr. and serves as a historical and architectural landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Private club for meetings, conventions, and events
world knowledge.Details: The mansion sits atop a 100-foot (30 m) knoll with views of greater Phoenix. It was constructed at a cost of $1.2 million by the William Simpson Construction Company. The Wrigleys used this, the smallest of their houses, for only a few weeks a year. The mansion has been Winner of The Knot Weddings for 2011, 2009, and 2008.

world knowledge.Name: Argentine National Congress Palace
world knowledge.Area: Balvanera at its limit with Monserrat
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palace of the Argentine National Congress was constructed between 1898 and 1906, with aesthetic details completed until 1946. It was designed by Italian architect Vittorio Meano and completed by Argentine architect Julio Dormal. The building was officially accepted by Congress on 12 May 1906. Over time, it proved too small, leading to the construction of an annex in 1974. From 1976 to 1983, it housed the Legislative Advisory Commission (CAL), a group of officers from the three Armed Forces.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was officially inaugurated in May 1906.
Construction of the Annex, which holds the Deputies' offices, was started due to the building's insufficient size.
Replicas of the statues designed by Lola Mora were inaugurated by President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner at the opening of the regular session.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is in Neoclassical style, largely made of white marble with elaborately furnished interiors, especially in the Lost Steps Hall and the Blue Room. It is crowned by a bronze-plated dome 80 metres in height, weighing 3,000 tonnes, weathered to green color. The main entrance, called the Entrada de Honor, is exclusively used for ceremonial purposes. A 8 metres high quadriga sculpture by Victor de Pol, made of bronze and weighing 20 tonnes, stands in front of it.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Palace of the Argentine National Congress is a National Historic Landmark and serves as the seat of the Argentine National Congress. The Kilometre Zero for all Argentine National Highways is marked on a milestone at the Congressional Plaza, next to the building. The palace is a symbol of the Argentine Republic and its democratic institutions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the Argentine National Congress
world knowledge.Details: The palace used to have a barber shop in the basement but it was demolished. The dome is lit during Argentina's national holidays and other special occasions. The Congressional Plaza, built by French Argentine urbanist Charles Thays, faces the palace and is popular among tourists and protesters alike.

world knowledge.Name: Old North Church
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Old North Church, officially Christ Church in the City of Boston, is the oldest standing church building in Boston and a National Historic Landmark. It played a pivotal role in Paul Revere's midnight ride on April 18, 1775, signaling the movement of British troops and marking the start of the American Revolutionary War.

Major_Events.Description: On April 18, 1775, the church's sexton, Robert Newman, hung two lanterns in the steeple to alert patriots about British military movements, leading to the Battles of Lexington and Concord.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The church was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 15, 1966.
The church was designated a National Historic Landmark on January 20, 1961.
On April 18, 1975, President Gerald Ford visited the church and delivered a speech commemorating its historical significance, lighting a third lantern.
On July 11, 1976, Queen Elizabeth II attended a service at the church during the U.S. Bicentennial celebrations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church features Georgian architectural style, designed by William Price. It includes box pews, brass chandeliers from 1723, and an organ built by Thomas Johnston in 1759. The steeple has been rebuilt multiple times due to damage from hurricanes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Old North Church is a symbol of American liberty due to its role in the American Revolution. It also reflects the social and economic dynamics of colonial Boston, including its ties to the Atlantic trade and slavery.

Details.Bells: Eight change ringing bells cast by Abel Rudhall in 1744, maintained by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Guild of Bellringers.
Details.Crypt: Contains approximately 1,100 bodies, including notable figures like Major John Pitcairn and Captain Samuel Nicholson.
Details.Clough House: A historic building behind the church, now serving as a gift shop and part of the National Register of Historic Places.
Details.Recent_Research: Focuses on the experiences of Black and Indigenous congregants, such as the Humphries family, to bridge gaps in historical knowledge.

world knowledge.Name: Parque de María Luisa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Parque de María Luisa is a public park in Seville, Spain, originally part of the gardens of the Palace of San Telmo. Donated to the city in 1893 by the Infanta Luisa Fernanda, Duchess of Montpensier, it was redesigned by Jean-Claude Nicolas Forestier starting in 1911. The park was a central location for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929, which led to the construction of notable structures like the Plaza de España.

Major_Events.Description: The exposition showcased Spain's industry and technology, with many buildings constructed in the park for the event, including the Plaza de España.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a 'Moorish paradisical style' with tiled fountains, pavilions, walls, ponds, and lush plantings. Notable structures include the Plaza de España, the Fountain of Lions, and the Queen's sewing box, which is the oldest Neo-Mudéjar style building in Seville.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is Seville's principal green area and serves as a botanical garden. It is culturally significant for its historical background, architectural beauty, and role in the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to many monuments, ponds, and fountains, including the Fountain of Lions and the Water-lily Pool. It also features educational panels about plant species and is known for its large population of doves, parakeets, ducks, and swans. The Plaza de España, a principal building from the 1929 exposition, is now used for government offices.

world knowledge.Name: Alexandria National Museum
world knowledge.Address: Tariq Al-Horreya Street (former Rue Fouad), Alexandria, Egypt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alexandria National Museum is housed in a renovated Italianate mansion built in 1926, which was originally the home of a wood salesperson and later served as the United States consulate. It was inaugurated as a museum on 31 December 2003 by Hosni Mubarak.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened by Hosni Mubarak on 31 December 2003.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is an Italian-style palace with three floors, located around a large garden, and includes a basement. It was a meeting place for the Egyptian upper-class society of Alexandria.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum narrates the story of Alexandria and Egypt through its collection of around 1,800 artifacts, including jewelry, weapons, statuary, numismatics, and glassware. A highlight is a sculpture believed to be of Alexander the Great.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections are spread over three floors, focusing on different historical periods. Most artifacts were sourced from other Egyptian museums.

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Angelo Massimino
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Stadio Cibali, the stadium was built in 1935 by architect Raffaele Leone and inaugurated in 1937. It was renamed in 2002 after former Catania chairman Angelo Massimino. The stadium has undergone several renovations and hosted significant football matches and events.

Major_Events.Description: A national team match held at the stadium.

Major_Events.Event: Italy vs United States football match
Major_Events.Description: A national team match held at the stadium.
The stadium hosted the closing event of the 1997 Summer Universiade.
The stadium hosted the main games of the Military World Cup.
The match reached a record of about 28,200 paying spectators.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features an 8-lane athletics track, a training ground (Cibalino), a volleyball court (PalaSpedini), an external basketball court, and various offices. It has undergone several restyling projects, including the installation of mixed natural/synthetic pitches and new seating.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is one of the most well-known in Italy and has been a central venue for football in Catania. It holds historical importance for the city and has been a stage for significant sporting events and local culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium primarily for football matches, home of Calcio Catania.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a current certified capacity of 20,016 seats, with plans for further redevelopment to install 20,806 new seats. It has hosted various sports competitions and is undergoing renovations to improve facilities, including the press stand, access tunnel, and seating areas.

world knowledge.Name: Duthie Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Duthie Park is a public park in the Ferryhill area of Aberdeen, Scotland located near the River Dee. It comprises 44 acres of land given to the council in 1881 by Miss Elizabeth Crombie Duthie of Ruthrieston, in memory of her uncle and of her brother. She purchased the land for £30,000 from the estate of Arthurseat. The park was opened in 1883 after it was gifted to the city by Miss Elizabeth Crombie Duthie in 1880 for the 'wellbeing and recreation of Aberdeen residents'.

Major_Events.Description: A round of It's A Knockout, featuring a team from Aberdeen against a team from Arbroath, was staged in Duthie Park on 10 May 1970 and transmitted on BBC1 on 13 May 1970.
An episode of the children's programme Play School, transmitted Monday 3 May 1976, visited Duthie Park in 1976.

The park underwent a £5 million pound refurbishment with funding provided by the Heritage Lottery Fund and Aberdeen City Council. The original 1883 plans were consulted in order to restore some of the long-lost features. Work was completed in 2013 and the official reopening was on 30 June 2013.

The J.J.R. Macleod memorial statue was unveiled on 12 October 2023. This celebrated the 100th anniversary of Macleod's joint award of the Nobel Prize for Medicine or Physiology in 1923, for his role in the discovery of Insulin.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features the David Welch Winter Gardens with tropical and arid houses which contain the second largest collections of bromeliads and of giant cacti respectively in Great Britain. The gardens contain a range of plants including tree ferns, Spanish moss, anthuria, and banana trees. The Japanese Garden is an outdoor area of the Winter Gardens, opened in 1987 to commemorate the dead of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The park also includes a standing statue of the Greek goddess Hygieia atop a decorative Corinthian column with four recumbent lions at the base, and the Duthie Fountain made of pink Peterhead granite with four carved swans with folded wings supporting a polished basin.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Duthie Park is culturally significant as a public space dedicated to the wellbeing and recreation of Aberdeen residents. It houses the David Welch Winter Gardens, which are notable for their plant collections, and the Japanese Garden, which commemorates the dead of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The park also features various statues and memorials, including the J.J.R. Macleod memorial statue and the statue of Hygieia, the goddess of health.
world knowledge.Details: The park has undergone a £5 million pound refurbishment with funding provided by the Heritage Lottery Fund and Aberdeen City Council. The original 1883 plans were consulted in order to restore some of the long-lost features. Work was completed in 2013 and the official reopening was on 30 June 2013. The refurbished park cafe was reopened in 2017 and is operated by the same company as the cafe at Hazlehead Park. An interactive musical art installation, called Hornchestra, was installed in 1975. It consisted of a set of horns mounted on a 39 ft. pole activated to play different notes by standing on underground foot pads and was donated by the Electrical Association for Women's Aberdeen branch. The installation was later referred to as the Honking Horns.

world knowledge.Name: Wiltern Theater
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pellissier Building and Wiltern Theatre, built in 1931, is a landmark Art Deco complex at the corner of Wilshire Boulevard and Western Avenue in Los Angeles. Originally designed as a vaudeville theater, it opened as the Warner Brothers Western Theater. After falling into disrepair in the late 1970s, it was saved from demolition by preservationists and underwent extensive renovation in the 1980s. It has since been a prominent performing arts venue.

Major_Events.Description: After a four-year renovation, the Wiltern Theatre reopened to the public on May 1, 1985, with performances by the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater company.
Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers played a show at the theater, which was used for Petty's first official live release, 'Pack Up the Plantation: Live!'
Madonna performed 10 concerts at the venue as part of her Madame X Tour.
The Wiltern was used as a polling place for the presidential election.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex is clad in blue-green glazed architectural terra-cotta tile and features French Zig-Zag Moderne styling. The Wiltern Theatre's interior includes decorative plaster and tile work, colorful murals by Anthony Heinsbergen, and a dramatic sunburst ceiling design. The tower has narrow vertical windows creating the illusion of greater height.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wiltern Theatre and Pellissier Building are considered among the finest examples of Art Deco architecture in the United States. They are listed on the National Register of Historic Places and declared a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument. The preservation of the Wiltern was a significant victory for architectural heritage conservation in Los Angeles.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Commercial offices and performing arts venue
world knowledge.Details: The Wiltern Theatre originally seated 2,344 but was modified in 2002 to allow configurations from 1,850 seated to 2,300 standing-room-only. It houses one of the largest theater pipe organs in the western United States. The venue is operated by Live Nation and has hosted numerous concerts, Broadway-level performances, and film events.

world knowledge.Name: Aalborg University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Aalborg University (AAU) was founded in 1974 as a public university with campuses in Aalborg, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. The movement for a university in the North Jutland Region began in 1961, and after years of advocacy, the university was established. It has since grown to become a leading institution in interdisciplinary and problem-based education, known as the Aalborg Model.

Major_Events.Description: Aalborg University Center (AUC) was inaugurated by Queen Margrethe II of Denmark on 1 September 1974.
Aalborg University Center (AUC) changed its name to Aalborg University (AAU).
Aalborg University - Esbjerg was established through a merger between the engineering college in Esbjerg and Aalborg University.
Aalborg University Copenhagen was formed in collaboration with the engineering college in Copenhagen.

Major_Events.Event: Appointment of UNESCO Chair in problem-based learning
Major_Events.Description: Aalborg University was appointed as UNESCO Chair in problem-based learning due to its innovative educational model.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aalborg University is culturally significant for its innovative approach to education, known as the Aalborg Model, which emphasizes interdisciplinary, problem-based learning. It is also recognized globally for its contributions to engineering, technology, and sustainable development.
world knowledge.Details: Aalborg University (AAU) is an international public university with campuses in Aalborg, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. It offers bachelor's, master's, and PhD degrees in various fields, including humanities, social sciences, information technology, design, engineering, exact sciences, and medicine. AAU is known for its interdisciplinary and problem-based approach to education and research, and it has been ranked highly in global university rankings for its contributions to engineering and sustainable development.

world knowledge.Name: Al-Quds University
world knowledge.Address: Abu Dis, University Street, Jerusalem Governorate, Palestine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al-Quds University is a public university established in 1984 through the merger of several local institutions in Jerusalem. It was founded by Zuhair Al-Karmi and is one of the highly ranked universities in Palestine. The idea of establishing a university in Jerusalem dates back to 1931, but it was hindered by the Israeli occupation and other political factors. The university has faced numerous challenges, including military attacks and political pressures from the Israeli government.

Major_Events.Description: Al-Quds University was established through the merger of several local institutions in Jerusalem.
The Israeli army launched 26 separate attacks on the university campus in Abu Dis, resulting in 1,769 injuries to students and staff.
Brandeis University and Syracuse University terminated their partnerships with Al-Quds University following a controversial demonstration.

Major_Events.Event: Al-Quds Academy for Global Justice Launch
Major_Events.Description: Al-Quds University launched the Al-Quds Academy for Global Justice, focusing on international criminal law and human rights.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus in Abu Dis features Islamic architecture, with notable facilities such as the Andalusian Garden, Abu Jihad Center, Meet Math Museum, and Science Museum. The Old City campus also follows Islamic architectural design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Al-Quds University is culturally significant as it represents Palestinian resilience and educational advancement despite ongoing political and military challenges. It is a symbol of Palestinian identity and academic excellence in the region.
Notable_Visitors: Palestinian Justice Minister Ali Abu Diak
world knowledge.Details: Al-Quds University has multiple campuses in Jerusalem, Ramallah, and Hebron. It offers a wide range of academic programs and has partnerships with international institutions like Bard College. The university has faced significant political and military pressures from the Israeli government, including threats of closure and military attacks on its campuses.

world knowledge.Name: Corran Point Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Corran Point, Highland, Scotland, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Corran Point Lighthouse is an active lighthouse located at Corran Point on the west side of the Narrows of Loch Linnhe. It was built in 1860 as a project by Thomas Stevenson and David Stevenson. It was the first lighthouse to be automated in 1898.

Major_Events.Description: The first lighthouse to be automated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Masonry tower, cylindrical with balcony and lantern, white tower with black lantern and ochre trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a historic structure built by notable engineers Thomas Stevenson and David Stevenson, and it represents early advancements in lighthouse automation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Active lighthouse aiding navigation in the Narrows of Loch Linnhe.

Details.Light_source: Electric Flashing Mains Powered LED Cluster Optic
Details.Range: white: 10 nautical miles (19 km; 12 mi), red: 7 nautical miles (13 km; 8.1 mi), green: 7 nautical miles (13 km; 8.1 mi)
Details.Characteristic: Iso WRG 4s 12m 10-7M Corran Point Lighthouse [Fl.2.0sec. - ec. 2.0 sec.] [Sectors: R.132°-195°, W.-215°, G.-020°, W.-030°, R.-069°]

world knowledge.Name: Imam Khomeini International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The airport was conceived before the 1979 revolution to alleviate congestion at Mehrabad Airport. Construction began in 1977 but was delayed due to the revolution and the Iran-Iraq war. It was initially managed by a Turkish-Austrian consortium but was shut down shortly after opening due to security concerns. The airport reopened in 2005 under Iranian management and has since expanded to include a second terminal.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was shut down shortly after its initial opening by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, citing security concerns over foreign management.
The airport reopened under the management of a consortium of four Iranian airlines.
A second terminal, the Salaam International Terminal, was completed and inaugurated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two terminals, with Terminal 1 shaped like an arc merging into the desert horizon. It has two runways, one partially made of concrete and the other entirely of asphalt. An instrument landing system was installed in 2009, making it the first airport in Iran to have one.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Ruhollah Khomeini, the founder of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and symbolizes Iran's efforts to engage with the international community. It represents a significant shift in Iran's approach to foreign investment and infrastructure development.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Tehran and the surrounding metropolitan area.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is a hub for multiple airlines and handles all international flights to Tehran. It is accessible via the Tehran–Qom and Tehran–Saveh freeways and is served by a station on Line 1 of the Tehran Metro. In 2019, it handled 7.27 million passengers, making it the third busiest airport in Iran.

world knowledge.Name: Hardwick Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hardwick Hall in Derbyshire is an architecturally significant country house from the Elizabethan era, a leading example of the Elizabethan prodigy house. Built between 1590 and 1597 for Bess of Hardwick, it was designed by the architect Robert Smythson, an exponent of the Renaissance style. Hardwick Hall is one of the earliest examples of the English interpretation of this style, which came into fashion having slowly spread from Florence. Its arrival in Britain coincided with the period when it was no longer necessary or legal to fortify a domestic dwelling.

Major_Events.Description: The British Army's 1st Parachute Brigade was formed at Hardwick Hall in 1941. The Airborne Forces Depot and Battle School was located on the grounds of the estate from 1942 to 1946.

After ownership for centuries by the Cavendish family and the line of the Earl of Devonshire and the Duke of Devonshire, ownership of the house was transferred to the Treasury in 1956 and then to the National Trust in 1959.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hardwick Hall was designed by Robert Smythson in the late 16th century. The windows are exceptionally large and numerous at a time when glass was a luxury, leading to the saying, 'Hardwick Hall, more glass than wall.' The Hall's chimneys are built into the internal walls of the structure, in order to give more scope for huge windows without weakening the exterior walls. Each of the three main storeys has a higher ceiling than the one below, the ceiling height being indicative of the importance of the rooms' occupants: least noble at the bottom and grandest at the top.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hardwick Hall is culturally significant as a leading example of the Elizabethan prodigy house and one of the earliest examples of the English interpretation of the Renaissance style. It was conceived to be a conspicuous statement of the wealth and power of Bess of Hardwick, the richest woman in England after Queen Elizabeth I.
world knowledge.Details: Hardwick Hall contains a large collection of embroideries, mostly dating from the late 16th century, many of which are listed in the 1601 inventory. Some of the needlework on display in the house incorporates Bess's monogram 'ES', and may have been worked on by Bess herself. There is a large amount of fine tapestry and furniture from the 16th and 17th centuries. Hardwick is open to the public. It has a fine garden, including herbaceous borders, a vegetable and herb garden, and an orchard. The extensive grounds also contain Hardwick Old Hall, a slightly earlier house which was used as guest and service accommodation after the new hall was built. The Old Hall is now a ruin.

world knowledge.Name: Green Park Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Civil Lines area, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Green Park Stadium is named after a British woman named Green who used to practice horse riding in the area during the 1940s. It is the only stadium in India with a student gallery and has the largest manually operated scoreboard in the world. The stadium hosted India's first Test win over Australia in December 1959, which was also the first match played on a turf wicket here.

Major_Events.Description: India v England, 12–14 January 1952
Hosted the 500th Test match played by the Indian team.
India v Sri Lanka, 24 December 1986
India v England, 26 January 2017
Hosted four Vivo IPL matches on 19 and 21 May 2016 and on 10 and 13 May 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a manually operated scoreboard (the largest in the world) and video screens for international matches. It is nicknamed 'Billiards Table' and 'Woolmer's turf' after the late cricket coach Bob Woolmer.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Green Park Stadium is a significant cricket venue in India, hosting numerous international matches and being the home ground of the Uttar Pradesh cricket team. It holds historical importance as the site of India's first Test win over Australia in 1959.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International cricket stadium hosting Test matches, ODIs, T20Is, and domestic cricket events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is situated near the river Ganga and is under the control of the Sports Department of Uttar Pradesh. It has hosted 22 Tests, 14 ODIs, and 1 T20I as of 19 August 2017. The ends of the stadium are named Mill Pavilion End and Hostel End after nearby landmarks Elgin Mill and DAV College.

world knowledge.Name: Anzali Lagoon
world knowledge.Address: Near Bandar-e Anzali, Gilan Province, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Anzali Lagoon, also known as Anzali Wetland Complex, is a coastal lagoon in the Caspian Sea. It has been listed in the Ramsar Convention since 21 December 1975. The lagoon has decreased in size since the 1930s due to factors like siltation, pollution, and increased upstream irrigation. It was once a significant commercial fishing area but has faced ecological challenges in recent decades.

Major_Events.Description: Anzali Lagoon was listed in the Ramsar Convention, recognizing its importance as a wetland of international significance.
Commercial fishing in the lagoon ceased due to factors like siltation, pollution, and eutrophication, reducing annual catches to less than 100 tons.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Anzali Lagoon is culturally and ecologically significant as a habitat for native and migratory birds, a spawning ground for aquatic animals, and a unique ecosystem with diverse plant and animal species. It is one of the few Iranian wetlands registered in the Ramsar Convention.
world knowledge.Details: The lagoon is home to the Selke Wildlife Refuge and the Siahkesheem Marsh. It has faced challenges such as pollution, eutrophication, and habitat degradation. The wetland supports over 100 bird species, 50 fish species, and hundreds of plant species. It plays a strategic role in the ecological balance of the Caspian Sea region.

world knowledge.Name: Rasht
world knowledge.Area: Central District of Rasht County, Gilan province
world knowledge.Address: Central District, Rasht County, Gilan Province, Iran
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 13th century (modern history dates back to the Safavid era)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rasht has a history dating back to the 13th century, with its modern history beginning in the Safavid era as a major silk trade center. It played a significant role in the Constitutional Revolution of Iran and was known as the 'Gate of Europe' due to its trade connections with Russia and Europe. The city has seen various historical periods, including the Sassanid era, Rashidun conquest, and influences from Russian and British colonialism.

Major_Events.Description: The people of Rasht played a prominent role in instigation and radicalization of the revolution.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic
Major_Events.Description: Mirza Kuchak Khan established this short-lived republic with the support of the Russian Red Army.
Rasht was recognized as a creative gastronomy city under UNESCO.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rasht features a mix of traditional and modern architecture. The city's older architectural texture is being replaced with modern skyscrapers and apartments due to high humidity damaging aged buildings. Notable buildings include the famous municipal building in the Square of Municipality, constructed circa 1900.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rasht is culturally significant as Iran's gateway to Europe, a major trade and tourist center, and a city with a rich history in the silk trade and constitutional movements. It is known for its unique gastronomy, humid subtropical climate, and as the 'City of Rain'. The city has contributed significantly to Iranian literature, education, and industry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Rasht serves as the capital of Gilan province and is a major trade, tourism, and cultural center. It is also an industrial hub with a focus on textiles, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture.

Details.Climate: Humid subtropical (Köppen: Cfa), known for high humidity and rainfall
Details.Notable_Foods: Mirza Ghassemi, vavishka, nargesi, baghala ghatogh, ashpal (roe), Reshteh khoshkar, Zeitoun Parvardeh
Details.Sports: Football (Damash Gilan, Sepidrood Rasht), wrestling, judo, weightlifting
Details.Transportation: Rasht railway station, Sardar Jangal International Airport
Details.Twin_Cities: List not provided in the source

world knowledge.Name: Dixon Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dixon Park is a football stadium that underwent improvements in the spring of 2010 to meet IFA Premiership standards, including new seating and modern facilities.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a small seated stand with changing rooms and club offices, covered standing areas behind each goal, and a standing area opposite the stand. It has an artificial surface and no scoreboard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dixon Park is culturally significant as the home of Ballyclare Comrades F.C. and a key sports venue in Northern Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 2,398 with 538 seats. The Comrades Social Club is located right beside the ground. Improvement works included a new 350-seat stand and additional seating in the visitors' enclosure behind the goal.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Vila Capanema
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Vila Capanema, originally named Estádio Durival Britto e Silva, was built in 1947 as a landmark event for Clube Atlético Ferroviário. It was designed by architect Rubens Maister of the Thá construction company. The stadium became Paraná Clube's home after the dissolution of Clube Atlético Ferroviário in 1971 and the foundation of Paraná Clube in 1989. It was modernized in 2006, increasing its capacity to 20,083 fans.

Major_Events.Description: The first match was played on January 23, 1947, between Fluminense Football Club and Clube Atlético Ferroviário, with Fluminense winning 5-1. The first goal was scored by Fluminense's Careca.
The stadium hosted two matches during the 1950 FIFA World Cup: Spain vs. USA (Spain won) and Paraguay vs. Sweden (2-2 draw).
The American rock band Pearl Jam performed at the stadium on November 9, 2011, as part of their 20th anniversary tour.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Rubens Maister, the stadium features a grass surface and was one of the most modern and comfortable stadiums in Curitiba for many years.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it was one of the largest in Brazil upon its inauguration and hosted matches during the 1950 FIFA World Cup. It remains an important sports venue in Curitiba.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium, primarily for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was named after Colonel Durival Britto e Silva, president of the RFFSA, and was built under the leadership of Heron Wanderley, then president of Clube Atlético Ferroviário. It was modernized in 2006, increasing its capacity to 20,083 fans.

world knowledge.Name: University of Zadar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Zadar, founded in 2002, traces its lineage to 1396, making it the oldest higher education institution in Croatia and one of the oldest in Europe. It was originally established as a theological seminary by the Dominicans and later became the first institute of higher learning in the country. After ceasing operations in 1807, it was reconstituted in 1956 as a satellite campus for the University of Zagreb and later became part of the University of Split. In 2002, it was fully refounded as an independent institution.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Zadar was originally founded by the Dominicans as Universitas Iadertina, a theological seminary.
The university ceased being an independent institution, and its functions were taken over by other local universities.
The University of Zagreb reconstituted it as a satellite campus for the Faculty of Philosophy division.
The Croatian Parliament passed an act to allow for its full-fledged refounding as an independent institution.
The university implemented the Bologna Process, improving its international profile and enabling collaborative research and student exchange programs.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Zadar is culturally and historically significant as the oldest higher education institution in Croatia and one of the oldest in Europe. It has played a pivotal role in the development of education and research in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Zadar includes 27 university departments and has founded four research centres: the Centre for Adriatic Onomastic Research, the Stjepan Matičević Centre, the Centre for Karst and Coastal Research, and the Centre for Interdisciplinary Marine and Maritime Research - CIMMAR. It also has two active centres for professional and teaching activities: the Centre for Gymnastics and Student Sport, and the Centre for Foreign Languages.

world knowledge.Name: Uludağ
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Uludağ, known as the ancient Mysian or Bithynian Olympus, is a mountain in Bursa Province, Turkey. It has been a significant site since ancient times, with hermitages and monasteries during the Middle Ages. The mountain was a center for monastic resistance against iconoclast emperors and later opposed urban monasticism. Saint Joannicius the Great, a notable Byzantine monk, lived here as a hermit. The area also hosted an abandoned wolfram mine, operational from 1974 to 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The ski resort hosted CEV Snow Volleyball European Tour events.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Uludağ is culturally significant as the highest mountain in the Marmara region and a historical center for monasticism. It is also a popular destination for winter sports and summer activities, attracting tourists and nature enthusiasts.
world knowledge.Details: Uludağ is accessible by car or cable-car from Bursa, which is about 22 km away. The cable-car has stops at Kadiyayla and Sarialan. The park features diverse habitats ranging from oak savanna to alpine meadows, hosting a variety of wildlife including rare birds and butterflies. The area is also known for its rich flora, including colorful primroses, crocuses, and grape hyacinths. Wolf packs roam the mountain, adding to its ecological diversity.

world knowledge.Name: Bydgoszcz Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Martin and St. Nicholas Cathedral, commonly known as Bydgoszcz Cathedral, is a Catholic church built in the 15th century. It was elevated to cathedral status on March 25, 2004, by Pope John Paul II. The church has a Gothic style and serves as a parish church and cathedral of the Diocese of Bydgoszcz. It houses a shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary and is the most valuable architectural monument of the Old Town.

Major_Events.Description: Elevated to cathedral status by Pope John Paul II.
Registered on the Kuyavian-Pomeranian heritage list.
A fire destroyed some elements of the building, including the wooden roof.
Funded by the Kingdom of Prussia, the church was refurbished and reconsecrated.
Artillery shells burned the roof and destroyed stained glass windows during the liberation of Bydgoszcz.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is built in Brick Gothic style with a closed chancel facing east, three naves, and a square tower on the south. It features a double-decker porch with arcades, a Renaissance oak door, and a Baroque turret roof lantern. The interior displays Baroque decor from the 17th century, with seven Baroque altars and a Gothic painting of the Madonna with the Rose.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Bydgoszcz, representing the city's religious heritage and architectural evolution. It is a symbol of the Roman Catholic faith in the region and has been a center for major religious events and ceremonies.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is located on the Brda riverside and is part of the Old Town. It has a capacity of 1800 seats and features a single spire. The church's cemetery was active until 1809, and the building has undergone several renovations, including recent works from 2013 to 2015 to recondition the roof and other structural elements.

world knowledge.Name: Alphabetic Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alphabetic Tower, completed in December 2011, symbolizes the uniqueness of the Georgian alphabet and people. It was designed by Spanish company CMD Domingo y Lázaro Ingenieros and cost $65 million to build. The structure combines the design of DNA in its double helix pattern, holding 33 letters of the Georgian alphabet.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was inaugurated in December 2011.
In May 2015, Batumi City Hall decided to lease the tower to an unnamed Spanish company for 20 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is composed of eleven modules of cantilever trusses of steel tubes, forming two bodies: the interior contains the communication core with panoramic elevators and stairs, while the exterior supports the structure and displays the Georgian alphabet letters. At the top is a glass sphere made of triangular elements fixed over steel profiles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower symbolizes the uniqueness of the Georgian alphabet and people, representing cultural pride and identity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The tower serves as a tourist attraction with a TV studio, restaurant, and observatory deck.
world knowledge.Details: The tower features a revolving restaurant on the third floor, offering panoramic views of the city and the Black Sea. The fourth floor is an observatory deck, and the fifth floor showcases a tuned mass damper. Despite its construction, the tower has remained largely unused, with maintenance costs of 700,000 GEL per year. As of 2017, the restaurant is open for visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Bagram Airfield
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bagram Airfield, also known as Bagram Air Base, was originally built by the Soviet Union in the 1950s during the Cold War. It has served as a key military base for various forces, including the Soviet Union, the United States, and the Afghan Armed Forces. The base has been a focal point in the Soviet-Afghan War, the US-led invasion of Afghanistan, and the subsequent conflicts in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The airfield was originally built by the Soviet Union during the Cold War.
The base was secured by US and UK forces during the US-led invasion of Afghanistan.
The base fell to Taliban forces after the withdrawal of US troops.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airfield features two concrete runways, multiple large hangars, a control tower, numerous support buildings, and various housing areas. It also has extensive ramp space and aircraft dispersal areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bagram Airfield has been a strategic military base in numerous conflicts, including the Soviet-Afghan War and the US-led invasion of Afghanistan. It has played a crucial role in regional military operations and has been a symbol of foreign military presence in Afghanistan.
world knowledge.Details: Bagram Airfield has been a critical military base for various forces, including the Soviet Union, the United States, and the Afghan Armed Forces. It has seen significant expansion and modernization, particularly during the US occupation. The base has been involved in numerous major military operations and has been a focal point in the conflicts in Afghanistan.

world knowledge.Name: Arena Omsk
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Arena Omsk was a 10,318-seat multi-purpose arena in Omsk, Russia. It opened in 2007, replacing Sports-Concerts Complex Viktora Blinova as the home of Kontinental Hockey League ice hockey team, Avangard Omsk. The arena was designed by Austrian company AMR, and construction began on March 16, 2004. The first ice hockey game was played on August 31, 2007, as part of the 2007 Super Series, a junior hockey challenge between Canada and Russia. The original owner was Roman Abramovich, who donated it to Avangard Omsk in 2012. In 2018, the arena was found to be structurally deficient and was demolished in September 2019. G-Drive Arena was built in its place and opened in September 2022.

Major_Events.Description: Played as part of the 2007 Super Series, a junior hockey challenge between Canada and Russia.
The arena was found to be structurally deficient and was demolished in September 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Austrian company AMR.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Served as the home of the Kontinental Hockey League ice hockey team, Avangard Omsk, and hosted significant events such as the 2007 Super Series.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose arena, primarily for ice hockey.
world knowledge.Details: The original owner of the arena was Roman Abramovich, who donated it to Avangard Omsk in 2012. The demolition was completed in September 2019, and G-Drive Arena was built in its place, opening in September 2022 for the KHL 2022–23 season.

world knowledge.Name: Ajinomoto Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ajinomoto Stadium was founded in March 2001 in Chōfu, Tokyo, on land formerly used by United States Forces Japan. It was the first stadium in Japan to sell its naming rights, which went to Ajinomoto Co., Inc. The stadium has hosted various sports events, concerts, and even served as a shelter for survivors of the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.

Major_Events.Description: Saudi Arabia's national team used the stadium as their main training ground.
The stadium was used as a shelter for survivors.
Hosted the opening ceremony, opening match, and 7 other matches including the Bronze Final.
The stadium was the rugby venue for the 2020 Summer Olympics and was known as Tokyo Stadium during the event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a capacity of 49,970 and is divided into two levels: upper (20,600 seats) and lower (29,370 seats). The stand is divided into four sections (main, back, north, and south sides). The upper level and upper tiers of the lower level are covered by a roof made of Teflon (main and back) and polycarbonate (both sides). The main stand houses media and hospitality boxes, VIP rooms, and a reception hall. Two large LED displays are installed on both sides. The pitch is sunk below the level of the land around the stadium to comply with height limitations near the airport.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ajinomoto Stadium is culturally significant as it was the first stadium in Japan to sell its naming rights. It has hosted major international events like the Rugby World Cup and the Summer Olympics, and has served as a shelter during natural disasters.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for football, rugby, concerts, and other events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the home of J1 League football clubs FC Tokyo and Tokyo Verdy. It is often used for non-sport events like concerts and flea markets. The ground was originally designed for both athletics and football games, but is currently used mainly for football. An athletics track was installed in 2013 for the National Sports Festival of Japan, but artificial turf is still used over the track for football matches.

world knowledge.Name: Burton Cummings Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Burton Cummings Theatre, originally known as the Walker Theatre, was built by local impresario Corliss Powers Walker. It opened in 1907 and was designed to be fireproof following the principles of Chicago's Auditorium theatre. The theatre hosted live performances until 1933, after which it was converted into a cinema. It was restored and reopened for live performances in 1991 and renamed after Burton Cummings in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre had its grand opening on 18 February 1907 featuring Puccini's Madame Butterfly.
The first performance was by Pollard's Lilliputian Opera Company on 17 December 1906, before the building was fully completed.

Major_Events.Event: Political Meeting Leading to Winnipeg General Strike
Major_Events.Description: The theatre hosted a political meeting of the Winnipeg Trades and Labour Council and the Socialist Party of Canada that led to the Winnipeg General Strike.
The theatre was converted into a cinema by Odeon Cinemas' Canadian subsidiary, with the first film being Blood on the Sun.
The theatre was restored to its original architectural features and reopened as a venue for live performances.
The theatre was renamed after local musician Burton Cummings.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre was designed by Montreal architect Howard C. Stone with a fireproof steel cage system, concrete or terracotta encased structural members, and fire-retarding metal doors. The interior features Italian marble, plasterwork, gilt trim, velvet carpets, silk tapestries, murals, and crystal chandeliers. The auditorium has vaulted ceilings reaching 60 feet in height, huge sidewall arches, 2 curving balconies, a fly tower, and broad wings. The stage area is nearly 25 metres wide, 12 metres deep, and 21 metres high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is designated as a National Historic Site of Canada and a Provincial Heritage Site. It played a significant role in the cultural and political life of Winnipeg, hosting performances, political rallies, and events related to the labour and women's suffrage movements.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre was leased to True North Sports & Entertainment in 2014, who undertook critical repairs and later purchased the building. Signage on the front of the building was updated in 2017.

world knowledge.Name: Delaware Legislative Hall
world knowledge.Address: 411 Legislative Avenue, Dover, Delaware, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Delaware Legislative Hall is the state capitol building of Delaware. It was designed in the Colonial Revival architecture style by E. William Martin and Norman M. Isham, and built 1931–1933, with wings added in 1965–1970 and 1994. The original capitol of Delaware was the State House (now known as the Old State House), located on The Green in Dover. It was commissioned originally by Kent County as the Kent County Court House, and was constructed from 1787 to 1791, when it became the State House. The State House was used until the completion of Legislative Hall.

Major_Events.Description: The main building was constructed during the Great Depression under the direction of the State Buildings and Grounds Commission.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of north and south wings
Major_Events.Description: Flanking north and south wings were added, giving each member of the Assembly an office in addition to a desk in one of the legislative chambers.
Two more wings were added to the east side, providing more office space for legislators and staff as well as hearing and caucus rooms.
The entire interior of Legislative Hall was renovated in a three-phase project, including refurbishment of both the House and Senate chambers as well as the lobby, cafeteria, and many offices.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Colonial Revival style, built of red brick with white wooden trim. The design resembles many architectural details of Old Colony House in Newport, Rhode Island.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Legislative Hall is the state capitol building of Delaware and houses the chambers and offices of the Delaware General Assembly. It is also home to the Hall of Governors, which includes portraits of all but one of Delaware's past governors, and other portraits of political and military figures.
world knowledge.Details: In addition to the chambers of the Delaware House of Representatives and Senate, the Legislative Hall also includes space used by the General Assembly's two nonpartisan staff agencies, the Division of Research and the Office of the Controller General, as well as offices for the Governor and Lieutenant Governor while the General Assembly is in session.

world knowledge.Name: Ría de Arousa
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Largest of the Rías Baixas, maximum depth of 69 meters
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ría de Arousa is a saline estuary and one of the five Rías Baixas in Galicia, Spain. It is known for its rich marine life and is the area of greatest mussel production in the world. Whales are starting to reappear along its coasts where whaling industries once thrived.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ría de Arousa is culturally significant for its rich marine life, mussel production, and the reappearance of whales. It is also known for its white grape Salnés varieties used in Albariño wine production.
world knowledge.Details: The Ría de Arousa has numerous islands and islets, including Arousa Island, A Toxa, Sálvora, and Cortegada. The main rivers flowing into it are the Ulla River and the River Umia. The northern zone is relatively steep with the Serra da Barbanza near the coast, while the southern zone is a flood zone with extensive sand banks and bivalve cultivation.

world knowledge.Name: Bessastaðir
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bessastaðir was first settled in 1000 and became one of Snorri Sturluson's farms in the 13th century. After Snorri's murder in 1241, it was claimed by the King of Norway and became a Royal stronghold. It resisted an attack by Turkish slave raiders in 1627. In the late 18th century, it was converted into a school before becoming a farm again. It was purchased by poet and statesman Grímur Thomsen in 1867 and later owned by editor and parliamentarian Skúli Thoroddsen and his wife Theodóra Thoroddsen. In 1941, it was donated to the state as a residence for the Regent and later the President of Iceland.

Major_Events.Description: Bessastaðir became one of Snorri Sturluson's farms.
Bessastaðir resisted an attack by Turkish slave raiders.
Sigurður Jónasson donated Bessastaðir to the state as a residence for the Regent and later the President of Iceland.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bessastaðir is the official residence of the President of Iceland and has a long history as a significant site in Icelandic history, including its association with Snorri Sturluson and its role as a Royal stronghold.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official residence of the President of Iceland
world knowledge.Details: Bessastaðir is located about 15 kilometres from Reykjavík and has been a prominent site in Icelandic history since its settlement in 1000.

world knowledge.Name: Sani Pass
world knowledge.Location: Border of KwaZulu Natal, South Africa and Mokhotlong, Lesotho
world knowledge.Address: Road between Himeville, KwaZulu-Natal and Mokhotlong, Lesotho
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sani Pass is a mountain pass used historically by the San people and later the Bantu to cross the Drakensberg Mountains. In 1922, the Basutoland government constructed a 2-metre track accessible by pack animals. From 1949, David Alexander established a transport business using jeeps. The pass became a tourist attraction from 1956 and was improved in 1958. The Mokhotlong Mountain Transport Company continued the route after Alexander's business ended. The pass has undergone several upgrades since 2006.

Major_Events.Description: Organised by the Sports Car Club and sponsored by The Star newspaper.
Construction work for the first phase of the Sani Pass upgrade.
South African Department of Environmental Affairs and Tourism approved phase 2.
South African Environmental Affairs Minister approved tarring of phase 2.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steep gravel road with gradients up to 1:3, often covered with snow and ice in winter. The pass is being upgraded with improved storm-water drainage systems and retaining walls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sani Pass is culturally significant as a historical route used by indigenous peoples and later as a vital transport link between South Africa and Lesotho. It is also a popular tourist destination for adventure drives.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mountain pass for transportation and tourism
world knowledge.Details: The pass is often closed due to adverse weather conditions, especially during winter. South African emigration at the bottom of the pass prohibits unsuitable vehicles, while Lesotho border agents at the summit generally allow all types of vehicles to attempt the descent. The respective border control stations open at 6:00 and close at 18:00. The South African/Lesotho border is at the summit of the pass, which lies entirely within South Africa.

world knowledge.Name: Jeju International Airport
world knowledge.Location: Jeju City, Jeju Province, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jeju International Airport, opened in 1968, is the second-largest airport in South Korea. It serves many mainland destinations in South Korea and international destinations in mainland China, Hong Kong, Japan, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore. The airport is one endpoint of the world's busiest airline route, Jeju to/from Seoul-Gimpo.

Major_Events.Description: Due to the airport operating far beyond its designed passenger capacity, it was announced in 2023 that Jeju's second airport would be constructed in Seongsan-eup, near the southern city of Seogwipo. This US$5.1 billion project has faced significant delays and controversies due to concerns the airport would negatively impact Jeju's groundwater sources, as well as protected species living in the area.
In 2019, the airport passed the 30 million passenger milestone despite being designed to handle a maximum of 26 million passengers.
In 2020, the number of international visitors dropped due to COVID-19. However, the Seoul-Jeju route remained the busiest in the world and flight delays are still common.
