world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jeju International Airport is culturally significant as it serves as a major gateway to Jeju Island, a popular holiday spot in South Korea. The airport facilitates tourism and economic activity on the island.
world knowledge.Details: Jeju International Airport (IATA: CJU, ICAO: RKPC) is located in Jeju City. The airport has two runways with asphalt surfaces. In 2019, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport announced a US$4.18 billion construction plan for a new airport near Seogwipo City, which was later cancelled due to environmental concerns. A new US$5.1 billion airport plan was provisionally approved in 2023 with no project completion date set.

world knowledge.Name: Baxter County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Baxter County Courthouse was built in 1941 to replace an older courthouse deemed unsafe in 1939. Baxter County was established in 1873, and the county seat was initially located in the Jacob Wolf House in Norfork, which is now the oldest standing county courthouse in Arkansas. The new courthouse was constructed with the help of the Works Progress Administration (WPA) during a period of economic depression in the 1940s. It was unveiled in 1943 and housed county offices, a courtroom, lawyer offices, and the county library.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was built to replace the old unsafe structure and was approved as a WPA project.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places on May 26, 1995.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as part of the Mountain Home Commercial Historic District
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was designated as part of the Mountain Home Commercial Historic District on June 15, 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Moderne style, designed by architect T. Ewing Shelton.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its role in the county's history and its architectural style. It is also part of the Mountain Home Commercial Historic District and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Served as the county courthouse, housing county offices, a courtroom, and other functions.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse was expanded from two to three stories to comply with a 1912 state law preventing county seats from moving out of three-story buildings. Many offices have since moved out of the courthouse.

world knowledge.Name: Bempton Cliffs
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 6 miles (10 km) long, over 330 feet (100 m) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bempton Cliffs is a section of precipitous coast at Bempton in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England. It is run by the RSPB as a nature reserve and is known for its breeding seabirds. The hard chalk cliffs are relatively resistant to erosion and offer many sheltered headlands and crevices for nesting birds.

Major_Events.Description: A series of 22 panels of phonetic birdsong by artist Adrian Riley were commissioned by the RSPB and installed across the site near habitats appropriate to the birdsong in each panel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hard chalk cliffs with sheltered headlands and crevices for nesting birds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bempton Cliffs is home to the only mainland breeding colony of gannets in England and supports around 10% of the United Kingdom population of kittiwakes. It is also a significant site for Atlantic puffins, which are now endangered along the Yorkshire coast.
world knowledge.Details: The cliffs run about 6 miles (10 km) from Flamborough Head north towards Filey and are over 330 feet (100 m) high at points. There are good walkways along the top of the cliffs and several well-fenced and protected observation points. The Atlantic puffins at Bempton Cliffs tend to nest in rock crevices, whereas burrows are used at most UK sites. Their numbers may be adversely affected by a reduction in local sand eel numbers caused by global warming.

world knowledge.Name: Château d'O
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Château d'O, also known as Domaine d'O, is one of the chateaux, old country mansions or follies, built by wealthy merchants from the 18th century onwards, surrounding the French city of Montpellier.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The South entrance leads to the 18th century mansion, while the North entrance leads to modern buildings, including Théâtre Jean-Claude Carrière.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is now a main sight of the city of Montpellier.
world knowledge.Details: Part of the venue includes Théâtre Jean-Claude Carrière. The article about this landmark is a stub and can be expanded on Wikipedia.

world knowledge.Name: Monte Verde
world knowledge.Address: Eastern part of the island of São Vicente, Cape Verde
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Monte Verde, meaning 'green mountain' in Portuguese, is the highest point on the island of São Vicente, Cape Verde, with an elevation of 744 m. It is part of the Natural Park Monte Verde and is known for its unique flora and less arid conditions compared to the rest of the island.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stratovolcano
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Monte Verde is culturally significant due to its unique ecosystem, which includes 93 inventoried species of flora, 17 of which are endangered. It is a key area for the conservation of endemic flora of São Vicente.
world knowledge.Details: The mountain is located 6 km east of the city centre of Mindelo. It features typical vegetation in its inaccessible parts, including Limonium jovibarba, Sonchus daltonii, Lobularia canariensis subsp. fruticosa, and Campylanthus glaber subsp. spathulatus.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Ruca Che
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Ruca Che is an indoor arena and multi-purpose stadium in the city of Neuquén, capital of the homonymous province and largest city in the Argentine Patagonia. It was built in 1995 to host the Americas Basketball Championship. The name of this sport venue is in the mapuche language: the word Ruka means house while Che means people. Therefore, this is the House of the People.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was built to host the Americas Basketball Championship.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Indoor arena and multi-purpose stadium designed by AIASA.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The name 'Ruca Che' reflects the Mapuche heritage, meaning 'House of the People,' symbolizing a communal space for the community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for sports and events
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is regularly used by Gigantes del Sur for the Serie A1 (Argentine men's volleyball league) and Independiente de Neuquén for the Torneo Federal de Básquetbol (third level of Argentine basketball). It also includes an auxiliary gym, outdoor basketball courts, volleyball facilities, and a parking lot for 150 vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: Kurá Hulanda Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kurá Hulanda Museum is an anthropological museum in Curaçao, specializing in the Atlantic slave trade. It was opened in April 1999 as an initiative of Jacob Gelt Dekker, who was approached by the Government of Curaçao to develop the western quayside in Otrobanda. Dekker restored derelict buildings on the quay and market to their original condition and established the museum to display the history from the capture in Africa to the relocation in the Americas, as well as the cultural heritage of the slaves on the culture of Curaçao and the Caribbean.

Major_Events.Description: The Kurá Hulanda Museum opened in April 1999, specializing in the Atlantic slave trade.
The luxury Kurá Hulanda Hotel & Lodge, located next to the museum, was declared bankrupt in October 2013.
In November 2013, the Kurá Hulanda Hotel & Lodge was sold to GHL Hotels, a Colombian hotel chain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of 15 restored buildings, maintaining their original condition.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally and historically important as it highlights the Atlantic slave trade and its impact on the culture of Curaçao and the Caribbean.
world knowledge.Details: The museum was established by Jacob Gelt Dekker, who also opened the Kurá Hulanda Hotel & Lodge next to the museum. The hotel was later sold to GHL Hotels in 2013.

world knowledge.Name: Baishatuo Railway Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Between Jiangjin District and Dadukou District, Chongqing, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Baishatuo Yangtze River Railway Bridge was the first bridge over the Yangtze River in Chongqing and only the second bridge along the main stretch of the river between Yibin and the river mouth in Shanghai. Only the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge, completed in 1957, pre-dates the Baishatuo Railway Bridge.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was closed on 24 April 2019 and replaced by the New Baishatuo Yangtze River Railway Bridge. The old bridge is to be demolished because it is considered too low as the water level is to be raised by a dam.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Truss bridge made of steel with a total length of 825 metres (2,707 ft) and a longest span of 80 metres (260 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge was a significant infrastructure project in China, being one of the earliest bridges over the Yangtze River, and played a crucial role in the development of railway transportation in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway bridge carrying two tracks of the Chongqing-Guiyang Railway.
world knowledge.Details: There are now over 50 bridges which cross the river downstream of the Baishatuo Railway Bridge. The new replacement bridge is a six-track cable-stayed bridge, with four tracks for passenger operations on its upper deck and two tracks for freight operations on its lower deck.

world knowledge.Name: University of Kinshasa
world knowledge.Area: Lemba, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
world knowledge.Address: Lemba, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Kinshasa, colloquially known as UNIKIN, was established in 1954 as Lovanium University during Belgian colonial rule. It became the premier university of the Democratic Republic of the Congo after the division of the National University of Zaire (UNAZA) in 1981. The university has faced significant challenges, including infrastructure deterioration and financial difficulties, but continues to be a leading educational institution in the country.

Major_Events.Description: The university was initially established as Lovanium University during Belgian colonial rule.
The university was established following the division of the National University of Zaire (UNAZA).
The first nuclear reactor in Africa, TRICO I, was built at the university.
President Félix Tshisekedi launched initiatives to enhance housing conditions, focusing on rehabilitating student residences.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university campus spans 400 hectares and includes various academic buildings, student residences, and research facilities. The Notre-Dame de la Sagesse chapel is strategically located on the campus.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Kinshasa is the premier university of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and has played a significant role in the country's educational and scientific development. It has been a center for higher education and research, attracting notable figures and contributing to national development.
world knowledge.Details: The university has twelve academic divisions and offers a wide range of programs. It has faced infrastructure challenges but continues to be a leading institution in the country. The university hosted the first nuclear reactor in Africa, TRICO I, and has a significant history in nuclear research. It also hosts the Cisco Academy, focusing on technology and computer networks.

world knowledge.Name: Crane Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Crane Beach was established in 1945 as a gift from Florence Higinbotham Crane, daughter-in-law of Richard T. Crane, and her family. The property is a part of the larger Crane Estate, along with Castle Hill and the Crane Wildlife Refuge, and is owned and maintained by The Trustees of Reservations.

Major_Events.Description: Mr. and Mrs. Richard T. Crane, Jr. began a tradition of inviting all the Ipswich school children to the beach for a day in 1911 to celebrate their son, Cornelius’, 6th birthday. Ever since, the tradition of Crane Beach Day has been repeated.

In 2011, the schools celebrated the 100th anniversary of the event. Several students, with birthdays closest to the day of the event, arrived at the beach by boat like they would when the tradition was started. There were people hired to impersonate the Crane family and greet people as they got to the beach, a replica of the old Ipswich Lighthouse, and even a special ice cream flavor dedicated to Cornelius (called “Cornelius Crunch”). In addition, every student received a celebratory t-shirt to wear to the beach, featuring a picture of Cornelius on his 6th birthday.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Crane Beach is an important nesting site for the threatened piping plover. The 2006 International Piping Plover Breeding Census estimated that only 3,884 plovers remained. According to the same 2006 census, Crane Beach was home to 19 breeding pairs and 40 total adults.
world knowledge.Details: Crane Beach is open year-round, and is free to Ipswich residents with the purchase of a yearly beach parking sticker. Non-residents must pay a fee to enter ($40 on weekends during peak season per car, as of 2024). In the summer months there is a refreshment bar, and the restrooms, showers and changing facilities are open year-round. The Cape Ann Transportation Authority (CATA) provides summer weekend bus service between the Ipswich MBTA train station and Crane Beach. The 1968 movie The Thomas Crown Affair starring Steve McQueen features a scene where McQueen’s character drives a dune buggy across this beach. The beach scenes of 2019 version of the movie Little Women also were filmed on the property.

world knowledge.Name: Majdanek State Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Majdanek State Museum is a memorial museum and education centre founded in the fall of 1944 on the grounds of the Nazi Germany Majdanek death camp located in Lublin, Poland. It was the first museum of its kind in the world, devoted entirely to the memory of atrocities committed in the network of concentration, slave-labor, and extermination camps and subcamps of KL Lublin during World War II. The museum performs several tasks including scholarly research into the Holocaust in Poland. It houses a permanent collection of rare artifacts, archival photographs, and testimony.

Major_Events.Description: The camp was liberated by the advancing Red Army on 23 July 1944.
18,400 Jews were killed at Majdanek on 3 November 1943, during the largest single-day, single-camp massacre of the Holocaust.
A monument dedicated to Holocaust victims was erected on the grounds of the former Nazi extermination camp.
A massive fire at one of the barracks in Majdanek destroyed some 7,000 pairs of prisoners' shoes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum includes largely intact gas chambers and crematoria. The monument consists of three parts: the symbolic Pylon (gate, 11 meters tall and 35 meters wide), the road, and the Mausoleum, containing a mound of ashes of the victims.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally and historically important as it preserves the memory of the atrocities committed during the Holocaust and serves as a place of education and remembrance.
world knowledge.Details: The museum was awarded the Gold Medal Gloria Artis for outstanding contributions to Polish culture in 2009. It also serves as the main branch of the nearby Sobibór Museum since 1 May 2012. The museum advises against bringing children under 13 due to the need for quiet behavior.

world knowledge.Name: Rajaji National Park
world knowledge.Address: Haridwar, Dehradun and Pauri Garhwal districts, Uttarakhand, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rajaji National Park was named after C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji), a prominent leader of the Freedom Struggle, and the first and last Governor-General of independent India. The area was created as Rajaji Sanctuary in 1948, and in 1983, three wildlife sanctuaries in the area, namely Chilla, Motichur and Rajaji, were merged into one. In 2015, the government approved a proposal to grant Rajaji National Park the status of a tiger reserve.

Major_Events.Description: The area was created as Rajaji Sanctuary.
Three wildlife sanctuaries in the area, namely Chilla, Motichur and Rajaji, were merged into one.
The government approved a proposal to grant Rajaji National Park the status of a tiger reserve.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Broadleaved deciduous forests and riparian vegetation, shrubland, grasslands and pine forests form the main habitats in the park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rajaji National Park is culturally significant as it is named after C. Rajagopalachari, a prominent leader of the Freedom Struggle, and the first and last Governor-General of independent India.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of wildlife and natural habitat
world knowledge.Details: Rajaji National Park is located in the Sivalik Hills and encompasses an area of 820 km². It is home to a diverse range of wildlife including Indian elephant, Bengal tiger, Indian leopard, and over 315 species of birds. The park is divided into two parts by the Ganga river, with the western part consisting of Rajaji and Motichur sanctuaries, and the eastern part being Chilla sanctuary.

world knowledge.Name: Jiangyin Yangtze River Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Jiangyin and Jingjiang, Jiangsu, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jiangyin Yangtze River Bridge was completed in 1999 to mark the 50th anniversary of the Chinese Revolution of 1947. It was the first long-span suspension bridge designed in China and was the longest suspension bridge in China at the time of completion. It held the record for the furthest downstream bridge on the Yangtze until 2008.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on September 28, 1999, with Jiang Zemin cutting the ribbon and naming the bridge.
Received an award for outstanding achievement in bridge engineering, recognized for its vision and innovation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a main span of 1,385 meters, constructed with flat streamlined steel box girders. The concrete towers are 190 meters tall, and the bridge has a clearance of 50 meters for river navigation. The steel deck was assembled using pre-assembled units weighing up to 500 metric tons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an engineering icon in China, representing significant advancements in bridge construction. It was a milestone in China's infrastructure development and remains a key transportation link.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries the G2 Beijing-Shanghai Expressway with three lanes in both directions and pedestrian sidewalks.
world knowledge.Details: The total investment for the bridge was 2.728 billion yuan. It was constructed by Cleveland Bridge & Engineering Company, with cable bands manufactured by Goodwin Steel Castings. The bridge was designed to accommodate heavy traffic and significant river navigation needs.

world knowledge.Name: Brickwall House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brickwall House, formerly known as Down House School and Brickwall House School, is a country house in Northiam, East Sussex, England. It was home to the Frewen family for over three hundred years. The house is now run as a dyslexia school (Frewen College) and also serves as a wedding venue. The timber-framed Tudor house dates to 1617. Down House School was established in 1910 by Seaburne Godfrey Arthur May Moens, an amateur historian born in India. The school was evacuated to Herefordshire during the Second World War and upon its return settled at Brickwall House. The school changed its name to Brickwall House School, and then to Frewen College after Admiral Sir John Frewen GCB transferred the school into an educational trust. Since 1972, the school has specialized in dyslexia and related learning difficulties.

Major_Events.Description: Down House School was established by Seaburne Godfrey Arthur May Moens, an amateur historian born in India.
The school was evacuated to Herefordshire during the Second World War.
Upon its return from evacuation, the school settled at Brickwall House.
The school was renamed Frewen College after Admiral Sir John Frewen GCB transferred the school into an educational trust and began specializing in dyslexia and related learning difficulties.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Timber-framed Tudor house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brickwall House is a Grade I listed building, indicating its exceptional architectural and historical importance. It has been home to the Frewen family for over three hundred years and has served as an educational institution for over a century.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently serves as a dyslexia school (Frewen College) and a wedding venue.
world knowledge.Details: This article about an East Sussex building or structure is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Onikan Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1930 and named after King George V in 1936. Between 1963 and 1973, it was known as the Lagos City Stadium. Renovated and reopened in the 1980s. Renamed to Mobolaji Johnson Arena in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was banned for use for the rest of the season by the Nigeria Football League when a pitch invasion injured many members of the Warri Wolves after a scoreless draw with First Bank.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oldest stadium in Nigeria, used for football matches and cultural activities.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for football matches and cultural activities.
world knowledge.Details: Home stadium of 1472 FC, First Bank FC, Ikorodu City FC, Inter Lagos, Julius Berger FC, Prince Kazeem Eleku FC, Smart City FC, Sporting Lagos, Stationery Stores FC, and Valiant FC. Capacity of 10,000 people.

world knowledge.Name: Wheatleigh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wheatleigh is a historic country estate built in 1893 by Henry H. Cook, a New York-based businessman who made his fortune in the railroad and banking businesses. The estate was designed by Peabody and Stearns and landscaped by Frederick Law Olmsted. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982. The property has served as a hotel since 1976 but was listed for sale in 2024.

Major_Events.Description: Wheatleigh was built as a country estate for Henry H. Cook.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Wheatleigh was recognized for its historical and architectural significance.
The property was listed for sale for $15 million after discontinuing hotel operations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is a large 2+1⁄2-story masonry building with Mediterranean Revival styling, organized in a U shape. It is built out of buff brick with terra cotta trim. The water tower is 100 feet (30 m) in height, built out of brick in three octagonal stages.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wheatleigh is one of the few surviving great Berkshire Cottages of the late 19th century. It was designed by the prominent architectural firm Peabody and Stearns and landscaped by Frederick Law Olmsted. The estate played a role in the establishment of Tanglewood, the summer home of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private country estate, now historically significant property previously operated as a hotel.
world knowledge.Details: The estate was originally 250 acres (100 ha) but was reduced to 22 acres (8.9 ha). It includes the main house and a water tower, with the latter being one of the tallest structures in Berkshire County when completed. The property was owned by the Boston Symphony Orchestra between 1949 and 1957.

world knowledge.Name: Nemours Mansion and Gardens
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 200-acre (81 ha) country estate with a 47,000 sq ft (4,400 m2) mansion
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nemours Estate was created by Alfred I. du Pont in 1909–10 as a gift for his second wife, Alicia. It was named for the north-central French town of Nemours, which was affiliated with his great-great-grandfather, Pierre Samuel du Pont de Nemours. The mansion was designed by Carrère and Hastings in the Louis XVI style of French architecture.

Major_Events.Description: The estate underwent a 3-year, $39 million renovation, which included refurbishing furniture, fabrics, tapestries, interior finishes, paintings, and sculptures, as well as replacing the electrical system and repairing the reflecting pool.
The Nemours Estate reopened its gates on May 1, 2008, after the extensive renovation.

The state of Delaware filed suit against the duPont Trust and Nemours Foundation, claiming the trustees were not following duPont's intentions and that Delaware was not receiving their proper yearly distribution.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: French neoclassical mansion designed in the Louis XVI style of French architecture. The estate features jardin à la française formal gardens, patterned after the gardens of Versailles surrounding the Petit Trianon at the Château de Versailles. The mansion contains rare 18th-century French furniture and an eclectic collection of notable antiques, works of art, and tapestries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Nemours Estate is culturally significant for its architectural grandeur, historical connection to the du Pont family, and its extensive collection of art and antiques. It is also notable for having the most developed and largest jardin à la française-style landscape park in North America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a private residence, the estate now serves as a historic house museum and cultural landmark.
Notable_Visitors: Jessie du Pont (Alfred I. du Pont's third wife)
world knowledge.Details: The mansion contains a rare Louis XVI musical clock by David Roentgen and Peter Kinzing, a clock made for Marie Antoinette, a chair from the 1937 coronation of King George VI, and a chair from Independence Hall. The estate's gardens include plantings, fountains, pools, a carillon tower, statuary, and a pavilion surrounded by naturalized woodlands. The estate is owned by the Nemours Foundation and shares grounds with the Nemours Children's Hospital, Delaware.

world knowledge.Name: Thamar University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Thamar University, also called Dhamar University, is a Yemeni public university in the city of Dhamar. It was inaugurated on August 24, 1996. The inception of the university dates back to 1990 when the Faculty of Education was established at Dhamar as a teaching center of Sana'a University. In 1996, Republican Decree No. 150 for 1996 was signed by the President of the Republic Ali Abdullah Saleh to establish Dhamar University. Various faculties were opened in subsequent years, and faculties in Al Bayda’a and Rada’a were separated in 2009 to become an independent university.

Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Education was established at Dhamar as a teaching center of Sana'a University.
Republican Decree No. 150 for 1996 was signed by the President of the Republic Ali Abdullah Saleh to establish Dhamar University.

Major_Events.Event: Separation of Al Bayda’a and Rada’a faculties
Major_Events.Description: Faculties in Al Bayda’a and Rada’a were separated from Dhamar University and became an independent university of Al Bayda’a.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Thamar University is a significant educational institution in Yemen, serving over 136,000 undergraduate and graduate students from across the country and abroad. It plays a crucial role in higher education and scientific research in Yemen.
world knowledge.Details: Thamar University has faculties of Arts and Language, Applied Science, Agriculture and Veterinary Science, Administrative Sciences, Computer and Information Technology, Dental, Medical, Engineering & Dams, and Education. It also has training centers such as the Continuing Learning Institute. The university has more than 520 faculty members, both native and expatriate, from Arab and foreign countries.

world knowledge.Name: Maritime Museum of New Caledonia
world knowledge.Address: Near the Betico ferry terminal, Nouméa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Maritime Museum of New Caledonia is largely dedicated to the history of French colonial exploration in the Pacific. It includes objects retrieved from the frigates Astrolabe and Boussole, which were wrecked under the captaincy of Jean-François de Galaup de Lapérouse. The museum occupies a former maritime station donated by the Autonomous Port of New Caledonia.

Major_Events.Description: The museum opened in 1999.
A commemorative stamp was issued to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the museum.
The museum was renovated in 2013, which involved the creation of new galleries.
The museum opened a new temporary exhibition on the history of the cruise and the journey by sea from France to the territory.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum occupies a former maritime station.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum focuses on French maritime histories, including colonial exploration, missionary activity, and the history of nickel. It also contains objects from other voyages to New Caledonia during the colonial period.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes artefacts collected from the wrecks of the frigates Astrolabe and Boussole, captained by Jean-François de Galaup de Lapérouse. It also contains objects relating to other voyages to New Caledonia, missionary activity, and the history of nickel. The collection includes the skull of a pygmy blue whale. The museum runs educational activities for primary and secondary school students. Museologists have commented that the museum focuses on French, rather than indigenous, maritime histories.

world knowledge.Name: Buskett Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Buskett Gardens, forming one of the few woodland areas in Malta, are located in the fertile valley of Wied il-Luq in Rabat. Indigenous forests once covered Malta, but trees were cut down for shipbuilding and agriculture. The gardens were planted by the Knights Hospitaller as a hunting reserve. The presence of the gardens is known since the post-Roman Republic period, with pagan sexual celebrations later replaced by Christian celebrations of St. Peter and St. Paul.

Major_Events.Event: Grand Master Claude de la Sengle retreats to Buskett
Major_Events.Description: Grand Master Claude de la Sengle retreated to Buskett when his health began to deteriorate, and died at Mdina two months later.
Hundreds of people flock to the gardens to eat traditional Maltese rabbit stew, listen to folk music, and enjoy the annual agricultural show.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gardens contain broadleaved deciduous woodland, native coniferous woodland, sclerophyllous garrigue and maquis shrubland, and groves of fruit trees. Dominant tree species include Oak, Carob, Olive, Aleppo Pine, White Poplar, Ash, and Elm.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gardens are one of the few woodland areas in Malta and are culturally significant for their historical use as a hunting reserve and for hosting the Feast of Imnarja. They are also an Important Bird Area, supporting large numbers of bird species.
Notable_Visitors: Grand Master Claude de la Sengle
world knowledge.Details: The Verdala Palace, an official residence of the President of Malta, stands on the edge of the gardens. The palace was built in 1588 as a summer residence and hunting lodge and is now the President's summer residence. The gardens are very popular with the Maltese people for walks and picnics and are at their best in the spring.

world knowledge.Name: Podgorica Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Podgorica Airport began its history of civil aviation on 29 May 1928 with the landing of an Aeroput Potez 29/2 biplane. Passenger air traffic started on 5 May 1930. The airport was used by Axis powers during World War II and was bombed by the Allies. Scheduled passenger service began on 8 April 1946. The airport moved to its current location in 1961 and underwent significant expansion in 1977. Ownership transferred to Airports of Montenegro on 23 April 2003, and major upgrades were completed in 2006.

Major_Events.Description: Landing of an Aeroput Potez 29/2 biplane on a grass runway in Ćemovsko polje.
An Aeroput Farman F.300 landed at an airfield near Stara Varoš, carrying passengers.
The airport was used by Axis powers and bombed by the Allies.
Three weekly flights on the Podgorica-Belgrade route began.
Construction of a new passenger terminal building, apron extension, taxiway system overhaul, and updated airfield lighting system.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Single passenger terminal building with 5,500 m² floor area, designed to handle up to a million passengers per year. Features a single runway (2,500 meters long and 45 meters wide) with a parallel taxiway.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Podgorica Airport is a key transportation hub for Montenegro, serving the capital city and the surrounding region. It plays a crucial role in connecting Montenegro to international destinations and supports the country's tourism and economic activities.
world knowledge.Details: Podgorica Airport shares a runway with the Montenegrin Air Force Podgorica Airbase. The airport has ICAO classification 4E ILS Cat I, with ILS landing possible only on runway 36. The airport is accessible by the Podgorica–Bar highway and has a train stop on the Belgrade–Bar railway, though it is not a convenient option for transfer to central Podgorica.

world knowledge.Name: Iron Pot Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Iron Pot island, Storm Bay, at the mouth of the Derwent River, Hobart, Tasmania, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iron Pot Lighthouse, constructed in 1832 with convict labour, is the oldest lighthouse in Tasmania and the oldest original tower in Australia. It was the first lighthouse in Australia to use locally manufactured optics and became the first Australian lighthouse to use solar power in 1977. The lighthouse was built in response to several shipwrecks and groundings in the area, including the Bombay (1830), SS Lintrose (1832), and the Princess Royal (1832).

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was constructed with convict labour on Iron Pot island to improve navigation safety in Storm Bay.
The original lighting apparatus was upgraded due to complaints from ship owners about insufficient light.

Major_Events.Event: Introduction of incandescent petroleum vapour burner
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse introduced a new lamp using vaporised kerosene, significantly increasing the light's intensity.
The lighthouse became automated, leading to the demolition of the keeper's house in 1921.
The lighthouse became the first in Australia to use solar power, marking a shift to sustainable energy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is an 11-metre tall square-based obelisk made of sandstone blocks 1.5 metres thick. It features a square tower with a balcony and lantern, marked with a white tower and a red horizontal band on the top. The construction used rubble masonry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Iron Pot Lighthouse is culturally and historically significant as the oldest lighthouse in Tasmania and the oldest original tower in Australia. It represents early maritime navigation technology and convict labour history. It is also notable for being the first Australian lighthouse to use solar power.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To serve as a navigational aid for ships entering the Derwent River and Storm Bay.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is automated and closed to the public. It is located 17.5 kilometres south-east of Hobart and is regularly circumnavigated by tourism operator Pennicott Wilderness Journeys. The island was named after magnetic pulses observed by Matthew Flinders in 1798 that disoriented compasses.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Centenario
world knowledge.Location: Avenida Dr. Américo Ricaldoni y Federico Videla, Parque Batlle, Montevideo, Uruguay
world knowledge.Address: Avenida Dr. Américo Ricaldoni y Federico Videla, Parque Batlle, Montevideo, Uruguay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Centenario was built between 1929 and 1930 to host the inaugural 1930 FIFA World Cup and to commemorate the centenary of Uruguay's first constitution. It is listed by FIFA as one of the football world's classic stadiums and was declared the first Historical Monument of World Football on 18 July 1983.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted ten matches of the 1930 FIFA World Cup, including both semi-final matches and the final match where Uruguay defeated Argentina 4–2.
The stadium hosted the final of the Copa Sudamericana on 20 November 2021.
The stadium hosted the final of the Copa Libertadores on 27 November 2021.
Estadio Centenario is expected to host the opening match of the 2030 FIFA World Cup to celebrate the centennial of the inaugural World Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has four grandstands separated by four lanes: the Olympic Tribune, Colombes, Amsterdam, and America Tribune. It features a grass surface, VIP boxes, press boxes, and a panoramic elevator in the Torre de los Homenajes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Estadio Centenario is culturally significant as it was built for the inaugural FIFA World Cup and commemorates Uruguay's first constitution. It is the national stadium of Uruguay and a symbol of the country's football heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has hosted numerous concerts by national and international artists. It is equipped to accommodate visitors with disabilities, featuring wheelchair-accessible seating areas, elevators, ramps, and dedicated restroom facilities. The Uruguayan Football Museum, located under the Olympic grandstand, highlights the sporting achievements of the Uruguayan national team.

world knowledge.Name: Dover Beach
world knowledge.Location: Strait of Dover, facing Calais, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: "Dover Beach" is a lyric poem by the English poet Matthew Arnold, first published in 1867. The poem is set on the shore of the English ferry port of Dover, where Arnold spent his honeymoon in 1851. The poem reflects Arnold's discontent with the state of society and the loss of faith in the modern age.

Major_Events.Description: The poem was first published in the collection New Poems.
Arnold spent his honeymoon in Dover, which inspired the poem.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The poem is culturally significant for its exploration of themes such as the loss of faith, the human condition, and the search for meaning in a changing world. It has influenced numerous writers, poets, and even legal opinions.
world knowledge.Details: The poem has been referenced in various novels, plays, poems, films, and songs. It has also provided a source for titles and has been cited in legal opinions, including a concurring opinion by U.S. Supreme Court Justice William Rehnquist.

world knowledge.Name: Valluvar Kottam
world knowledge.Address: Intersection of Kodambakkam High Road and Village Road, Nungambakkam, Chennai, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valluvar Kottam is a monument in Chennai dedicated to the classical Tamil poet philosopher Valluvar. It was conceived and executed by the then Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu M. Karunanidhi during the 1970s. Designed by South Indian traditional architect V. Ganapati Sthapati, it was inaugurated in April 1976 by the then President of India Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by the then President of India Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.
Renovated at a cost of ₹ 6 million.
Renovation started at a cost of ₹ 8.5 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument consists of a decorative arch, an auditorium that can accommodate around 3,500 people, and the Kural Manimandapa, where all the 1,330 couplets from all 133 chapters of the Kural literature are inscribed on bas-relief. The hallmark of the monument is the 39-meter-high (128-foot) stone car, a replica of the famed temple chariot of Thiruvarur. The chariot is made of around 3000 blocks of granite stone from Tiruvannamalai and weighs 2,700 tonnes. The four giant-sized wheels of the chariot measure 11 feet in diameter and 2 feet in thickness. A life-size statue of Valluvar has been installed in the chariot, which is adorned with Kalamkari drawings. The bottom portion of the chariot features bas relief sculptures depicting all the 133 chapters of the Kural text. The central auditorium measures 220 feet by 100 feet and is said to be Asia's largest at the time of its construction. The roof of the monument has a terraced garden with two large pools.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valluvar Kottam is Chennai's biggest Tamil cultural centre, dedicated to the classical Tamil poet philosopher Valluvar. It serves as a significant cultural and historical landmark, celebrating Tamil literature and heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The monument is visited by an average of about 700 people during weekdays and 1000 people during weekends. It is maintained by the memorial section of the information and public relations department of the state government.

world knowledge.Name: Guildhall, London
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Guildhall is a municipal building in the Moorgate area of the City of London. The current building dates from the 15th century, but evidence suggests a guildhall existed at the site since at least the early 12th century. It has been used as a town hall for several hundred years and remains the ceremonial and administrative centre of the City of London. The site was also the location of the London Roman Amphitheatre, the largest in Roman Britain. The first documentary reference to a London Guildhall is dated 1127 or 1128. The building has undergone several restorations, including after the Great Fire of London in 1666 and the Second Great Fire of London in 1940.

Major_Events.Description: The Great Hall was partially damaged and restored in 1670 with a flat roof.
The timber roof added in 1866 was destroyed during a Luftwaffe fire-raid and replaced in 1954.
The infamous Zong case, which focused public outrage about the transatlantic slave trade, was heard at Guildhall.
The pianist Frédéric Chopin made his last public appearance on a concert platform at Guildhall.
The marathon route of the 2012 Summer Olympics passed through Guildhall Yard.
A lunch was held at Guildhall to mark the 40th year of the Queen's reign, where she made her famous 'annus horribilis' speech.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Guildhall is a Grade I-listed building with a medieval great hall. The present grand entrance, in 'Hindoostani Gothic', was added in 1788 by George Dance. The building has undergone several restorations, with the most recent major restoration in 1954 designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott. The West Wing, built between 1970 and 1975, is designed in a modernist style and is separately listed as a Grade II building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Guildhall is the ceremonial and administrative centre of the City of London and its Corporation. It has been the site of significant historical events, trials, and public appearances. The building is also associated with the legends of Gog and Magog, two giants defeated by Brutus and chained to the gates of his palace on the site of Guildhall. The Guildhall continues to host important events, including the Lord Mayor's Banquet.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Municipal building serving as the ceremonial and administrative centre of the City of London.
world knowledge.Details: Guildhall hosts many events throughout the year, including the Lord Mayor's Banquet, where the Prime Minister makes a major world affairs speech. The building also houses the Guildhall Art Gallery and Guildhall Library, a public reference library with specialist collections on London. The members' bar in the Guildhall is a highly subsidised facility for members of the Court of Common Council and the Court of Aldermen.

world knowledge.Name: Mines View Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mines View Park is an overlook park on the northeastern outskirts of Baguio in the Philippines. It overlooks the mining town of Itogon, particularly the abandoned gold and copper mines of the Benguet Corporation, and offers a glimpse of the Amburayan Valley.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The observation deck is situated below a winding stone-covered stairway close to the parking area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Provides a historical view of the mining activities in the region and the natural beauty of the Amburayan Valley.
world knowledge.Details: Located on a land promontory 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) from downtown Baguio.

world knowledge.Name: Ping An International Finance Centre
world knowledge.Address: 5033 Yitian Road, Futian District, Shenzhen, Guangdong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ping An Finance Centre is a supertall skyscraper completed in 2017, commissioned by Ping An Insurance and designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates. It is the tallest building in Shenzhen and the second tallest in China. The building was intended to have an antenna to surpass the Shanghai Tower, but this was scrapped due to potential flight path obstructions.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid on 29 August 2009.
Construction was temporarily halted due to suspected use of unprocessed sea sand in concrete, which could corrode the steel structure.
The building was topped out on 30 April 2015, reaching a height of 599.1 metres (1,966 ft).
The building was completed on 28 March 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features a stainless-steel facade weighing approximately 1,700 metric tons (3,700,000 lb). It has a width-to-height aspect ratio of 1:10, 115 floors, and an 11-story podium. The structure includes eight main columns, with dimensions ranging from 6 by 3.2 m (19 ft 8 in by 10 ft 6 in) at the base to 2.9 by 1.4 m (9 ft 6 in by 4 ft 7 in) at the top. The building also has a five-level basement and 33 double-deck elevators traveling at speeds up to 10 m/s (2,000 ft/min).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ping An Finance Centre represents the economic growth and modernization of Shenzhen. It houses the headquarters of Ping An Insurance and features an observation deck, Free Sky, which offers panoramic views of the city. The building's design reflects the achievements of its main tenant and contributes to Shenzhen's skyline.
world knowledge.Details: The observation deck, Free Sky, is located on floor 116 at a height of 562.5 m (1,845 ft), making it the highest observation deck in a building at the time. It includes a transparent viewing area, interactive experience area, and special display area showcasing youth cultures with Shenzhen characteristics. The building also includes a 5-star Park Hyatt hotel and a retail bridge connecting it to the South Tower. Despite its prominence, nearly 30% of the office space remained vacant in 2019.

world knowledge.Name: Murtala Muhammed International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) is an international airport located in Ikeja, Lagos State, Nigeria. Initially built during World War II, it was named after Murtala Muhammed, the fourth military ruler of Nigeria. Originally known as Lagos Airport, it was renamed in 1976 following his assassination. A new international terminal, modeled after Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, was constructed in the 1970s and opened in 1979. The airport has undergone significant improvements over the years, including the construction of a new domestic terminal (MMA2) in 2007 and a new international terminal in 2022.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed after Murtala Muhammed following his assassination.
A new international terminal, modeled after Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, was opened.
A new domestic terminal, known as MMA2, was commissioned.
A new international terminal with the capacity to process 14 million passengers annually was commissioned.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features an international and a domestic terminal, with the international terminal modeled after Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. The new international terminal, commissioned in 2022, is designed to handle 14 million passengers annually.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Murtala Muhammed International Airport is a major hub for air travel in Nigeria and serves as a key gateway to the country. It is named after Murtala Muhammed, a significant figure in Nigerian history, and has played a crucial role in the development of aviation in Nigeria.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as the main base for Nigeria's largest airline, Air Peace, and several other Nigerian airlines. It includes the headquarters of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, and the Accident Investigation Bureau. The airport has undergone significant improvements in recent years, including the repair of malfunctioning infrastructures, the opening of new restaurants and duty-free stores, and the revival of bilateral air services agreements.

world knowledge.Name: Neot Kedumim
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Neot Kedumim, the Biblical Landscape Reserve in Israel, is a Biblical garden and nature preserve located near Modi'in, midway between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. It was established in 1964 by Noga Hareuveni, who implemented his parents' dream of creating a biblical landscape reserve. The park covers an area of about 2,500 dunams and features various natural and agricultural landscapes inspired by the Hebrew Bible.

Major_Events.Event: Allocation of land for the project
Major_Events.Description: Land was allocated for the project with the help of Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion.
Neot Kedumim and Noga Hareuveni were awarded the Israel Prize for their special contribution to society and the State of Israel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neot Kedumim comprises a series of natural and agricultural landscapes, including the Forest of Milk and Honey, the Dale of the Song of Songs, Isaiah's Vineyard, and the Fields of the Seven Species. The park features restored ancient terraces, wine presses, and ritual baths, along with hundreds of varieties of cultivated plants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Neot Kedumim is culturally significant as it re-creates the physical setting of the Hebrew Bible, embodying the landscapes that shaped biblical values and provided a rich vocabulary for expressing them. It serves as an educational and spiritual resource, connecting visitors to the biblical heritage of Israel.
world knowledge.Details: Neot Kedumim offers pre-booked organized tours and is accessible to individuals who can roam the site on their own with maps provided by the park. The park's website is www.neot-kedumim.org.il.

world knowledge.Name: State Opera (Prague)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The State Opera, originally known as the New German Theatre, was opened in 1888 to serve the German-speaking community in Prague. It underwent several name changes, including Smetana Theatre and Prague State Opera, reflecting its evolving cultural and political roles. It became part of the National Theatre of the Czech Republic in 1992 and has hosted numerous performances and notable artists.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the New German Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened with Richard Wagner's opera 'Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg' under the direction of Angelo Neumann.
The theatre was closed due to political and financial pressures amid the growing Nazi threat.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Theatre of the Fifth of May
Major_Events.Description: After WWII, the theatre was repurposed for Czech opera, starting with Bedřich Smetana's 'Brandenburgers in Bohemia'.
The theatre was renamed the Smetana Theatre and became part of the National Theatre under the Czech Communist Party government.
After the Velvet Revolution, the theatre regained independence and was renamed the Prague State Opera.
The opera's ballet corps merged with the Prague Chamber Ballet to form the Prague State Opera Ballet.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre features a spacious auditorium with elaborate neo-rococo décor, designed by the Viennese firm Fellner & Helmer and Prague architect Alfons Wertmüller.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The State Opera is a cultural landmark with a rich history of promoting both German and Czech opera. It has hosted internationally renowned artists and served as a refuge for artists fleeing Nazi Germany. Its avant-garde productions and contributions to opera and ballet have made it a significant institution in European cultural history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Opera house hosting performances of opera, ballet, and other cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The Prague State Opera maintains a Documentation Centre to preserve its history and reconstruct lost archives. It publishes historical materials and hosts charitable events. The theatre stages approximately 300 performances annually and continues to innovate with new productions and world premieres.

world knowledge.Name: Liaohe Bridge
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Five-span cable-stayed structure, 866 meters in length, longest span of 436 metres (1,430 ft)
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge crossing the East Liao River
world knowledge.Details: The Liaohe Bridge is a bridge over the Eastern Liao River in Yingkou, Liaoning, China. The bridge is a five-span cable-stayed structure 866 meters in length.

world knowledge.Name: Lauder Greenway Estate
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lauder Greenway Estate, also known as Copper Beech Farm, was built in 1896 for industrialist John Hamilton Gourlie. It was purchased by the Lauder Greenway family in 1905 and remained in their hands for most of its existence. The estate was expanded and donated portions of its land for public use, such as Island Beach. It was sold in 2015 and again in 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The estate was purchased by Dr. James C. Greenway and his wife Harriet Lauder Greenway, niece of Andrew Carnegie.
James and Harriet Greenway gifted one of the islands to the town of Greenwich, which now serves as Island Beach.
The estate was sold for $120,000,000 to an unnamed buyer.
The estate was sold again for $138,830,000 on August 2, 2023.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: French Renaissance style mansion with stone-and-shingle construction. The main house spans 15,000 square feet across four floors, featuring 12 bedrooms, 7 full baths, and 2 powder rooms. Includes a cherry wood-paneled library, oak-columned dining room, garden room, solarium, wine cellar, and staff quarters. The grounds feature a carriage house, greenhouses, a 16-sided pool, tennis court, and sunken gardens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The estate is the largest surviving Gilded Age mansion in Connecticut and was once the most expensive home in the United States. It is associated with the Lauder and Greenway families, including Harriet Lauder Greenway, niece of Andrew Carnegie.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a private island, roughly one mile of water frontage, and a private beach. It features a 1,500-foot driveway, a gatehouse, and a century-old apple orchard. The property was expanded to over 100 acres at its peak before land donations reduced its size.

world knowledge.Name: Ramna Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ramna Park, initially developed during the British colonial era, has evolved from a vast empty expanse known as Ramna Plains into a significant urban green space. It was formally inaugurated in 1949 and has undergone several transformations over the years, including beautification and renovation works.

Major_Events.Event: Civic reception for Queen Elizabeth II
Major_Events.Description: Queen Elizabeth II received a warm civic reception at Ramna Park during her visit to Dhaka.

Two bombs exploded at Ramna Park during the Pohela Boishakh celebrations, resulting in the deaths of 10 individuals and injuries to several others. Members of the Islamist group Harkat-ul-Jihad al-Islami were convicted in connection with the incident.

Ramna Park was closed to the public as a precautionary measure to mitigate the spread of the Coronavirus pandemic. During this period, a beautification drive was undertaken, and the park was reopened towards the end of 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a lake at its core, walkways, garden paths, a bud-shaped water tower, and a diverse range of trees and flowering plants. Enhancements include deepening and extending the lake, constructing walkways, and implementing irrigation systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ramna Park is culturally significant as it hosts the yearly Bengali New Year celebrations (Pohela Boishakh), which kick off at dawn with cultural performances. It is also known as the "lungs of Dhaka City" and serves as a popular public space for recreation and cultural events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Urban green space and recreational area
world knowledge.Details: Ramna Park contains 71 species of flowering plants, 36 species of fruit trees, 33 species of medicinal plants, and 41 species of forestry plants. The yearly Pohela Boishakh celebrations are marked by traditional music, dance, and attire. The park was reopened in 2022 after a significant renovation project.

world knowledge.Name: Phayao Lake
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Phayao Lake, known as Kwan Phayao in Thai, is the largest freshwater lake in northern Thailand and the fourth largest in the country. It originated from the collapse of the lithosphere about 70 million years ago. The lake was formed by the construction of a dam in 1935, which created a large swamp. Over time, the lake has undergone significant changes, including periods of degradation and rejuvenation efforts.

Major_Events.Description: The Department of Fisheries constructed a dam on the Ing River, which led to the formation of Phayao Lake.
A floodgate was completed to control water levels, which caused flooding and transformed natural swamps into large reservoirs.
The Hydro and Agro Informatics Institute (HAII) and other agencies initiated efforts to rejuvenate the lake, including building dikes, removing weeds, and stocking native fish.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Phayao Lake is culturally significant as it provides natural resources that support the local community's livelihood. It has been a vital source of water, fish, and fertile land for agriculture. The lake also has historical importance as it was once an urban area with numerous temples.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Freshwater lake supporting local ecology and community
world knowledge.Details: Phayao Lake is rich in biodiversity, with about 50 species of fish and various aquatic plants. The lake's water storage capacity was increased by 370,000 cubic meters through rejuvenation efforts, benefiting 16,500 families and 43,785 rai of farmland. The land around the lake is fertile, and the area has a temperate climate with an average rainfall of 1,064 mm per year.

world knowledge.Name: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 20th-largest art museum in the world by public gallery area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1870 in Copley Square, moved to current location in 1909. Initially housed in the Boston Athenæum, it has grown to become one of the most comprehensive art collections in the Americas with over 450,000 works.

Major_Events.Description: The museum moved from Copley Square to its current Fenway location, designed by architect Guy Lowell.

Major_Events.Event: Art of the Americas Wing opening
Major_Events.Description: The new wing opened, featuring artwork from North, South, and Central America, designed by Foster and Partners.
The museum was closed from March 12 to September 25 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
MFA employees voted to unionize and went on strike due to workplace conditions and compensation issues.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical design with a 500-foot granite façade and grand rotunda. Features various wings added over time, including contemporary designs by I.M. Pei and Foster and Partners.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Houses one of the most comprehensive art collections in the Americas, including the largest collection of Japanese art outside Japan. It plays a significant role in art education and community engagement.

Details.Collection_Highlights: Over 450,000 works, including 8,161 paintings, extensive Japanese art collection, and contemporary works.
Details.Special_Exhibitions: Regularly hosts special exhibitions on various art topics, often featuring borrowed items from other museums.
Details.Accessibility: Offers accommodations for visually, audibly, or physically impaired visitors, including special tours and programming.
Details.Controversies: Faced allegations of racial insensitivity in 2019 and controversies over exhibitions like 'Philip Guston Now' in 2022.

world knowledge.Name: Paradise Point, Pakistan
world knowledge.Address: Hawkes Bay Road or Mubarak Goth Road, Karachi, Pakistan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Paradise Point is a sandstone rock promontory on the Arabian Sea, once featuring a natural arch. It was a popular tourist destination before 2017, offering beachside activities, amusement parks, and restaurants. Due to security concerns related to the nearby Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, the beach was closed to tourism in 2017 and is now a reservation of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission.

Major_Events.Description: The federal government of Pakistan allowed the Ministry of Energy to acquire the area, designating it as a reservation of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission and closing the beach for tourism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Sandstone rock promontory with a former natural arch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Paradise Point was a major tourist attraction in Karachi, offering recreational activities and scenic views of the Arabian Sea. Its closure highlights the balance between tourism and security in sensitive areas.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a tourist beach; now a restricted reservation for the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is located near other popular beaches such as Sandspit Beach, Hawke's Bay, and Clifton Beach. Access now requires clearance due to security concerns related to the Karachi Nuclear Power Plant.

world knowledge.Name: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1962 to accommodate larger jet aircraft, it was formerly known as Haile Selassie I International Airport. It has undergone multiple expansions to handle increasing passenger traffic and larger aircraft.

Major_Events.Event: New runway and control tower operational
Major_Events.Description: The new runway and control tower became operational to accommodate larger jet aircraft.
An expansion plan was announced to increase the airport's capacity.
The new terminal, one of Africa's largest, was opened, capable of handling about 3,000 passengers an hour.

Major_Events.Event: New cargo terminal and maintenance hangar opened
Major_Events.Description: The new cargo terminal and maintenance hangar were opened, capable of accommodating three to four aircraft at a time.
A $27.9 million expansion project was announced to increase aircraft parking capacity.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the expansion to Terminal 2.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two terminals with a total of 11 gates, modern security and baggage handling systems, and facilities capable of handling large aircraft like the Boeing 747 and Airbus A380.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the main hub of Ethiopian Airlines, it serves as a crucial gateway for international travel to and from Ethiopia and the African continent.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is the main hub of Ethiopian Airlines and serves as a base for the Ethiopian Aviation Academy. It has undergone multiple expansions to handle increasing passenger traffic and larger aircraft, with further expansions planned to increase capacity to 60 million passengers by 2029.

world knowledge.Name: Linnanmäki
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Linnanmäki is an amusement park in Helsinki, Finland, opened on 27 May 1950. It is owned by the non-profit Children's Day Foundation, which operates the park to raise funds for Finnish child welfare work. The park was established by six Finnish child welfare organisations and has since expanded from its initial leased area. The park is built on a hill named Vesilinnanmäki, referencing two historic water towers.

Major_Events.Description: The amusement park was opened to raise funds for child welfare work.

Major_Events.Event: Fatal accidents on Vuoristorata roller coaster
Major_Events.Description: Two fatalities occurred due to rider negligence, one involving an unsecured brakeman and another a guest who stood up during the ride.
The dunk tank attraction was closed following criticism from a women's organisation for being demeaning to women.
Linnanmäki welcomed its 50-millionth visitor in August 2006.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of rides and attractions, including eight roller coasters, tower rides, a Ferris wheel, and a river rapids ride. The park is built on a hill and includes two historic water towers, one of which houses an indoor roller coaster. The layout is compact and densely packed with rides and attractions in close proximity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Linnanmäki is the oldest and most popular amusement park in Finland, serving as a significant cultural and recreational landmark. It is also notable for its contributions to child welfare, having donated over €130 million to the cause since its inception.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park and fundraising for child welfare
world knowledge.Details: Linnanmäki is visited by about a million guests annually. The park features 42 rides, including the iconic Vuoristorata wooden roller coaster and the historic Karuselli carousel. Admission is free, but rides require tickets or a wristband. The park hosts events like the iik!week horror festival and Valokarnevaali (Carnival of Light). The Peacock theatre and Sea Life aquarium are year-round attractions. The park is accessible by tram and bus from Helsinki's city centre.

world knowledge.Name: Angel Stadium
world knowledge.Address: 2000 Gene Autry Way, Anaheim, California, US
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Angel Stadium is a ballpark in Anaheim, California, United States. Since its opening in 1966, it has been the home venue of the Los Angeles Angels of Major League Baseball (MLB). It was also the home of the Los Angeles Rams of the National Football League (NFL) from 1980 to 1994. The stadium is often referred to by its unofficial nickname 'The Big A'.

Major_Events.Description: First All-Star Game to be played on prime-time television.
Hosted the MLB All-Star Game.
Hosted the MLB All-Star Game.
Hosted the 2002 World Series, which the Angels won over the San Francisco Giants.
Caused the left-field Jumbotron to collapse onto the upper deck seats beneath it.
Hosted a 6-hour, 31-minute game between the Angels and the Boston Red Sox that extended for 19 innings.
Eric Dickerson broke the NFL single-season rushing record in game 15 of the 1984 season, finishing with 2,007 yards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed by Noble W. Herzberg and Associates (1966), with renovations by HOK Sport, Robert A. M. Stern, and Walt Disney Imagineering. Features include a 'California Spectacular' with geysers and a mountainside, outfield bleacher pavilions, and a video display board.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Angel Stadium is the fourth-oldest active ballpark in the majors and has been a significant venue for baseball, football, concerts, and other cultural events. It is a landmark in Southern California and has hosted numerous historic sports milestones.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Baseball stadium (home of the Los Angeles Angels), also used for football, concerts, and other events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone several renovations, including a major one in 1997-1998 to return it to a baseball-only facility. It features a 'Big A' sign in the parking lot, which is a Southern California landmark. The stadium has hosted numerous concerts, movies, and other events, and is designated to host baseball events for the 2028 Summer Olympics.

world knowledge.Name: Museum of Croatian Archaeological Monuments
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museum of Croatian Archaeological Monuments is the only museum in Croatia dedicated to researching and presenting cultural artifacts of the Croats in the Middle Ages, particularly from the 7th to the 15th centuries. It was founded in Knin in 1893, moved to Sinj, then Klis, and finally to Split where it is housed in a purpose-built museum complex opened in 1976.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded in Knin.
The museum was moved to Split and opened in a purpose-built museum complex.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum holds the largest collection of early medieval wicker, clay figurines, and old Croatian Latin epigraphic monuments in Europe. It is significant for its focus on the cultural artifacts of the Croats during the Middle Ages, particularly the early medieval Croatian state from the 9th to the 12th century.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's holdings consist mainly of jewellery, weapons, and items of daily use, including many stone artifacts from old Croatian church interiors.

world knowledge.Name: Malta Aviation Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Malta Aviation Museum is an aircraft museum situated on the site of the former Royal Air Force airfield in the village of Ta'Qali, on the island of Malta. The museum, based in three hangars, covers the history of aviation on the island with exhibits, particularly from the Second World War and post-war periods. The museum is involved in the preservation and restoration of aircraft, some of which are in airworthy condition.

Major_Events.Description: The museum received two Romney huts from the former RAF Luqa.

Major_Events.Event: New Main Exhibition Hangar funded by the EU
Major_Events.Description: A new Main Exhibition Hangar was funded by the EU.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is based in three hangars, including a purpose-built hangar opened in 2005.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum covers the history of aviation on the island of Malta, particularly from the Second World War and post-war periods, and is involved in the preservation and restoration of aircraft.
world knowledge.Details: Exhibits include airframes from the Second World War period, several examples restored from casualties of the Battle of Malta. The space includes the museum entrance and restoration workshop.

world knowledge.Name: Château d'Ouchy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château d'Ouchy (Castle of Ouchy) is a hotel built on the site of an old medieval castle in Lausanne, Switzerland by Jean-Jacques Mercier between 1889 and 1893. It was first constructed by the Bishop of Lausanne as a tower on the banks of Lake Léman around 1170. A century later, it was rebuilt and transformed into a fortified residence for bishops, particularly for Guillaume de Varax. It was also used as a prison. The castle was abandoned and its tower reduced to ashes in 1609. The canton of Vaud recovered it after the departure of the Berneses and sold off part of the land to Jean-Jacques Mercier in 1885. The new owner radically transformed the castle by demolishing the ruins and old buildings, leaving only the tower.

Major_Events.Description: Many of the leading figures of the Treaty of Lausanne were staying at the hotel. There is a plaque at Château d'Ouchy commemorating the peace treaty.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-gothic style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château d'Ouchy is historically significant as it was originally a medieval castle and later transformed into a hotel. It played a role in the Treaty of Lausanne.
world knowledge.Details: The hotel belongs to the hotel division of the Sandoz Family Foundation. It has 7 floors, 50 rooms, and 1 restaurant. The architect was Francis Isoz.

world knowledge.Name: Mottram Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mottram Hall was built around 1750 by William Wright for his son. It has been owned by six generations of the Wright family before being sold in 1922. It has been used as a hotel since the mid-1970s.

Major_Events.Description: The hotel underwent improvements and refurbishment at a cost of £5.5 million, including a new restaurant, refurbishment of bedrooms, creation of conference suites, and restoration of the Garden Suite.
The hotel was sold by Aprirose to the hotel group Champneys, owned by Dorothy and Stephen Purdew.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed of Flemish bond orange brick with buff sandstone dressings, with a Kerridge stone slate roof, nine brick chimneys, and a facade with projecting end pavilions which have 20th-century extensions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mottram Hall is a designated Grade II* listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The house was built for William Wright's son Randle, who died soon after its completion. The estate was passed through several heirs before being sold in 1922. It was later bought by Walter Pownall, who enjoyed gardening and held open days to the public. The building has been used as a hotel since the mid-1970s.

world knowledge.Name: Holme Hall, Bakewell
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Holme Hall near Bakewell, Derbyshire, is a privately owned 17th-century country house. It was built in 1627 for Barnard Wells of Stoke Hall (Derbyshire), gentleman. The house was constructed on the site of a previous manor house. The Eyres held the manor until 1802 when the estate was sold under an order of Chancery to Robert Birch, who sold it in 1820 to Thomas John Gisborne, second son of Rev Thomas Gisborne of Yoxall. When Francis Gisborne died in 1881, the estate passed to his brother William Gisborne.

Major_Events.Description: The house was built for Barnard Wells of Stoke Hall (Derbyshire), gentleman.

Major_Events.Event: Sale of estate to Robert Birch
Major_Events.Description: The estate was sold under an order of Chancery to Robert Birch.

Major_Events.Event: Sale of estate to Thomas John Gisborne
Major_Events.Description: Robert Birch sold the estate to Thomas John Gisborne, second son of Rev Thomas Gisborne of Yoxall.
When Francis Gisborne died, the estate passed to his brother William Gisborne.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original entrance front to the south has three storeys and three bays, the central one projecting to create a full-height entrance porch, and the outer bays having canted bay windows to second-floor height. The windows are transommed and mullioned and the parapets are crenellated. To the rear is a plainer three-storey four-bay block and to the right a late 17th-century lower block of three bays.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Holme Hall is a Grade I listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Holme Hall is a Grade I listed building, designated on 13 March 1951 with reference number 1246166. It is privately owned.

world knowledge.Name: Yichang Olympic Sports Centre Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Yichang Olympic Sports Centre Stadium is a multi-purpose sports complex developed under Hubei Province’s urban revitalization strategy. It was constructed by China Construction Third Bureau and is managed by Yichang City Construction Investment Co., Ltd. The project aims to host national and international competitions while promoting community fitness and tourism.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the national championship event.
The opening ceremony featured video projections and light shows on the stadium’s roof and walls.

Major_Events.Event: International Dance Sports Open and China-Europe Dance Sports Competition
Major_Events.Description: Hosted international and national dance sports competitions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a modular architecture allowing flexible use for sports, exhibitions, and public gatherings. It includes a 40,000-seat Class A stadium with a FIFA-standard football field and athletics track, an 8,000-seat gymnasium, a 1,700-seat Olympic-standard swimming pool, and specialized facilities for badminton and shooting. The design emphasizes eco-friendly systems and integrates green spaces covering 200,000 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium serves as a key venue for provincial and national sports events, cultural performances, and public recreation. It is part of a larger sports park designed to integrate competitive sports, leisure, and urban development, boosting local tourism and urban development.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose sports complex hosting sports events, cultural performances, and public recreation.
world knowledge.Details: The complex is located near the Yangtze River and is promoted alongside Yichang’s natural attractions like the Three Gorges. It attracts over one million annual visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Fergana International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fergana International Airport serves the city of Fergana, the capital of Fergana Region in Uzbekistan.
