From 1960, the 194th Guards Military-Transport Aviation Regiment was based at the airport, moving from Sredne-Belaya in the Far East. In early 1992, the unit came under Uzbek Air Force control.

Major_Events.Description: The 194th Guards Military-Transport Aviation Regiment moved to Fergana International Airport from Sredne-Belaya in the Far East.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to Uzbek Air Force control
Major_Events.Description: The 194th Guards Military-Transport Aviation Regiment came under the control of the Uzbek Air Force.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 18/36 with an asphalt surface measuring 2,860 by 50 metres (9,383 ft × 164 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fergana International Airport is one of the biggest airports in Uzbekistan, serving as a key transportation hub for the Fergana Region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is at an elevation of 625 metres (2,051 ft) above mean sea level. It is owned by Uzbekistan Airports AJ and operated by International Airport Fergana LLC.

world knowledge.Name: Falkirk Wheel
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Falkirk Wheel is a rotating boat lift that connects the Forth and Clyde Canal with the Union Canal. It was opened in 2002 as part of the Millennium Link project, reconnecting the two canals for the first time since the 1930s. The project aimed to regenerate central Scotland's canals and reconnect Glasgow with Edinburgh.

Major_Events.Description: Queen Elizabeth II opened the Falkirk Wheel as part of her Golden Jubilee celebrations. The opening was delayed a month due to flooding caused by vandals.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Falkirk Wheel consists of two opposing arms extending 15 m (49 ft) beyond the central axle, taking the shape of a Celtic-inspired double-headed axe. It features two water-filled caissons, each with a capacity of 250,000 litres, and uses a gearing mechanism to keep the caissons level.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Falkirk Wheel is a symbol of modern engineering and a key part of the Millennium Link project, which revitalized central Scotland's canal system. It is the only rotating boat lift of its kind in the world.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Rotating boat lift to connect two canals
world knowledge.Details: The Falkirk Wheel raises boats by 24 metres (79 ft) and features a visitor center and boat trips. Since its opening, it has attracted around 5.5 million visitors and 1.3 million boat trips.

world knowledge.Name: Marrickville Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: 96-106 Illawarra Road, Marrickville, New South Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The original Marrickville Town Hall, opened in 1879, is the oldest civil building in Marrickville and the fourth oldest Town Hall in Sydney. It was replaced in 1922 by a new town hall at 303 Marrickville Road. The original building was purchased by the Department of Education in 1922 and later became part of Marrickville Public School until 1985. The site was later developed for pensioner housing.

Major_Events.Description: The original Marrickville Town Hall was opened.
A two-storey addition was added, along with a portico and steps with lion couchant sculptures.
The original town hall was replaced by the current Marrickville Town Hall at 303 Marrickville Road.
The original town hall was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register.
A sculpture of Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, was unveiled as a memorial to World War I casualties.
A modern 4-meter bronze statue of Nike was unveiled to replace the deteriorated original.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original building features a two-storey extension added in 1883, incorporating a portico and steps with lion couchant sculptures. The design is attributed to Edmund Blacket of Blacket & Son.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is significant for its association with the development of local government in Sydney and provides a physical record of the early history of the municipality. It is the oldest civil building in Marrickville and the fourth oldest Town Hall in Sydney.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former town hall, later used as part of Marrickville Public School.
world knowledge.Details: The original town hall at 96-106 Illawarra Road was listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999. The new town hall at 303 Marrickville Road was officially opened on 11 February 1922.

world knowledge.Name: Tewkesbury Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tewkesbury Abbey, originally a Benedictine monastery, was founded in 1092 by Robert Fitzhamon and Giraldus, Abbot of Cranborne. The present building, started in 1102, is one of the finest examples of Norman architecture in Britain. It became a parish church after the dissolution of the monasteries in 1539. The abbey has undergone several restorations, notably by George Gilbert Scott in the late 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: During the Wars of the Roses, defeated Lancastrians sought sanctuary in the abbey. The victorious Yorkists forced their way in, leading to bloodshed and the abbey's temporary closure for purification.
The last abbot, John Wakeman, surrendered the abbey to King Henry VIII's commissioners. The townspeople saved it from destruction by purchasing it for £453.
Flood waters from the River Severn reached inside the abbey, causing significant damage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey is renowned for its massive Romanesque crossing tower, considered the largest and finest in England. It features Norman architecture with Caen stone imported from Normandy. The structure includes a rood screen from 1892 and three organs, including the historic Milton Organ.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tewkesbury Abbey is a significant example of Norman architecture and a key historical site in England. It has served as a centre for worship since the 7th century and houses numerous tombs and memorials of local aristocracy. The abbey's survival through the dissolution of the monasteries highlights its importance to the local community.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey has a ring of twelve bells, overhauled in 1962, with additional bells cast in 1991 and 2020. It hosts regular services, including Parish Eucharist, choral Mass, and Evensong, accompanied by its choirs and organs. The abbey's churchyard contains war graves of two World War II Royal Air Force personnel. Photography inside the abbey is restricted.

world knowledge.Name: National Institute of Technology, Kurukshetra
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Institute of Technology Kurukshetra (NIT Kurukshetra or NITKKR) is a public technical and research university established in 1963 as the Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra. It was renamed to National Institute of Technology under the NIT Act in 2002 and given Deemed University status. It was accredited with the status of Institute of National Importance (INI) in December 2008.

Major_Events.Event: Accreditation as Institute of National Importance
Major_Events.Description: In December 2008, NIT Kurukshetra was accredited with the status of Institute of National Importance (INI).

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to National Institute of Technology
Major_Events.Description: In 2002, the Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra was renamed to National Institute of Technology under the NIT Act and given Deemed University status.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: NIT Kurukshetra is one of the 31 National Institutes of Technology established and administered by the Government of India. It plays a significant role in advancing technical education and research in India.
world knowledge.Details: NIT Kurukshetra offers undergraduate B.Tech., postgraduate M.Tech., and Ph.D. programmes in various engineering fields, sciences, humanities, and social sciences. It also offers an MBA degree. Admissions are based on the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) for Indian students and the Direct Admission of Students Abroad (DASA) scheme for foreign students. The institute is ranked 81st among engineering colleges in India by the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) in 2024.

world knowledge.Name: University of Kufa
world knowledge.Address: P.O Box 21, Kufa, Najaf Governorate, Iraq, Kufa, Najaf, 540011, Iraq
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Kufa is one of Iraqi universities located in Kufa, Iraq. It was founded on December 23, 1987, with only two faculties: Education for Women and Medicine. The Faculty of Medicine was established roughly a decade earlier and was affiliated with Al-Mustansiriyah University. Over the years, the university expanded to include 22 faculties in various majors and 109 departments.

Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Jurisprudence was established in 1958, closed by Saddam Hussein's regime in 1991, and reopened in 2003–2004.
The Faculty of Medicine was established in 1977 and transferred to Kufa in 1984.
The University of Kufa was founded on December 23, 1987, with two faculties: Education for Women and Medicine.
The Faculty of Arts was initiated in 1989 with two departments: History and Arabic Language.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Administration and Economy
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Administration and Economy was founded in 1993.
The Faculty of Science was founded in 1993 with Biology and Chemistry departments.
The Faculty of Engineering was established in 1993.
The Faculty of Agriculture was founded in 1997.
The Faculty of Pharmacy was founded in 1999.
The Faculty of Law was initiated in 2004 on the basis of the law department which was affiliated with the Administration Faculty.
The Faculty of Dentistry was founded in 2006.
The Faculty of Nursing was founded in 2006.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Veterinary Medicine
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine was established in 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Computer and Mathematics sciences
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Computer and Mathematics sciences was founded in 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Physical education
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Physical education was founded in 2009.
The Faculty of Education was founded in 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Basic Education
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Basic Education was founded in 2009.
The Faculty of Archaeology was founded in 2011.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Urban Planning
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Urban Planning was established in 2011.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Political Sciences
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Political Sciences was established in 2013.
The Faculty of Languages was established in 2014.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Postgraduate Studies
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Postgraduate Studies was founded in 2017.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Kufa is culturally and historically significant as it has grown to become one of the leading universities in Iraq, offering a wide range of academic programs and contributing to the education and development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Kufa comprises 22 faculties in different majors and has 109 departments. The university seeks to expand the number of faculties and departments of uncommon majors needed in the labor market. The university's website, uokufa.edu.iq, ranked first among Iraqi universities websites in July 2011 within the Spanish Webometrics. The University of Kufa now ranks 2815 globally and is the 3rd university in Iraq.

world knowledge.Name: Space Needle
world knowledge.Area: Lower Queen Anne, Seattle, Washington, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair in Seattle, Washington. It was designed as an observation tower and quickly became an iconic symbol of the city. The design was a collaboration between Edward E. Carlson and John Graham, Jr., inspired by a balloon tethered to the ground and a flying saucer concept. The tower was completed in less than a year and was the tallest structure west of the Mississippi River at the time.

Major_Events.Description: The Space Needle was built as the centerpiece of the 1962 World's Fair, drawing over 2.3 million visitors.
The Seattle Landmarks Preservation Board designated the Space Needle a historic landmark on April 19, 1999.
The Legacy Light (Skybeam) remained lit for eleven days in response to the September 11 attacks.
The Space Needle's roof was repainted in its original 'Galaxy Gold' color to celebrate its 50th anniversary.
A major renovation added an all-glass floor, floor-to-ceiling glass panels, and upgraded internal systems at a cost of $100 million.

Architectural_Characteristics.Design_Features: Hourglass profile, tripod base, revolving restaurant, observation deck, and a top-floor antenna spire.
Architectural_Characteristics.Structural_Resilience: Designed to withstand winds of up to 200 mph (320 km/h) and earthquakes up to 9.0 magnitude.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Space Needle is an enduring symbol of Seattle and the Pacific Northwest. It represents innovation and the futuristic vision of the 1962 World's Fair. It has appeared in numerous films, TV shows, and sports team logos, further cementing its cultural impact.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Observation tower, tourist attraction, and revolving restaurant.

Details.Restaurants: Originally housed the Space Needle Restaurant and Emerald Suite, later replaced by SkyCity (now closed).
Details.Lighting_Feature: Legacy Light (Skybeam) used for special occasions and holidays.
Details.Renovations: Multiple renovations, including the 2000 overhaul and the 2017-2018 Century Project.
Details.Pop_Culture_Appearances: Featured in films like 'Sleepless in Seattle,' 'Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me,' and TV shows like 'Frasier' and 'Grey's Anatomy.'
Details.Suicides: Three recorded suicide jumps led to improved safety netting and fencing.
Details.BASE_Jumping_Incidents: Six recorded jumps (four authorized, two illegal).

world knowledge.Name: Valencia Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valencia Airport, also known as Manises Airport, opened in 1933 and had its first regular flight in 1934. It is the tenth-busiest Spanish airport in terms of passengers and second in the Valencian Community after Alicante. The airport has flight connections to about 20 European countries and handled 8.53 million passengers in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: The first regular flight occurred one year after the airport opened.
Ryanair closed its hub at Valencia Airport following a dispute over subsidies by the airport authorities.
Delta Air Lines inaugurated a route to New York City, Valencia's first transatlantic service, but later made it seasonal due to low ticket sales and ultimately severed the link in 2012.
Ryanair reopened its base at Valencia Airport.
Air Transat will begin seasonal flights to Montreal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Valencia Airport consists of a single terminal built in three stages. The landside hall has three check-in areas, and the airside area features gates 1-22, with gates 1-4 designated for non-Schengen flights. The regional terminal opened in 2007, allowing walk-boarding for flights by Iberia Regional and low-cost carriers. The sole operational runway was lengthened by 50 meters in 2007.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valencia Airport is a significant transportation hub in the Valencian Community, facilitating travel and commerce. It has played a crucial role in connecting Valencia with other European countries and, briefly, with New York City.
world knowledge.Details: Valencia Airport is situated 8 km west of Valencia and is adjacent to the Autovía A-3 highway. It is connected to the city by a regular bus line and the Metrovalencia network, which links the airport to the city center, the main railway station, and the port of Valencia.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Couto Pereira
world knowledge.Address: Rua Ubaldino do Amaral, 37, Curitiba, PR, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was constructed under the initiative of Major Antônio Couto Pereira, who was Coritiba's president during the late 1920s and early 1930s. Originally named Estádio Belford Duarte, it was later renamed in honor of Major Couto Pereira in 1977. The stadium has undergone several renovations and expansions, including the addition of floodlights in 1942 and major upgrades in 2005 and 2014.

Major_Events.Description: Coritiba beat América 4–2, with the first goal scored by Coritiba's Gildo.
Coritiba beat Avaí 4–2 in the first match under the new floodlights.
80,000 spectators watched Coritiba beat São Paulo 2–1.
70,000 people attended the event.
Part of their Music of the Spheres World Tour, becoming the first headline artist to play the venue twice.
Part of the Got Back Tour, setting a stadium record for revenue and attendance per concert.
Part of the Bruno Mars 2022-2024 Tour.
Part of the Guts World Tour, marking her first performance in Brazil and first stadium performance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features Bermuda 419 grass on a 109 x 72-meter field, with modern amenities such as 43 restrooms, 20 snack bars, 5 locker rooms, and a parking lot with 400 spaces. It includes 25 luxury boxes, a press room, and electronic turnstiles. The seating is numbered, and the stadium has elevators for press and authorities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a historic venue for Coritiba Foot Ball Club and has hosted significant cultural and sporting events, including concerts by international artists and visits by prominent figures like Pope John Paul II. It also houses a gallery showcasing the club's trophies and history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a current capacity of 40,502 spectators, with facilities including a club store ('Sou 1909'), modern luxury boxes, and a gallery honoring former president Amâncio Moro and ex-player Belfort Duarte. The field dimensions were expanded in 2005, and the stadium features a state-of-the-art drainage system and redesigned goalposts for player safety.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio de Pituaçu
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Governador Roberto Santos, commonly known as Estádio de Pituaçu, was built in 1979 and named after Roberto Santos, a former governor of Bahia and federal deputy. It became a key stadium in Bahia after the demolition of Fonte Nova stadium. The stadium underwent renovations in 2008-2009 to expand capacity and comply with the Brazilian Supporters' Statute.

Major_Events.Description: Bahia beat Fluminense de Feira 2-0; the first goal was scored by Bahia's Douglas.
Vitória beat Bahia 2-0, setting an attendance record of 18,418.
Bahia defeated Ipitanga 4-0.
Brazil beat Chile 4-2.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Football stadium with grass surface, initially built with a capacity of 32,157, later expanded to 34,000.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is an important sports venue in Bahia, serving as the home stadium for Esporte Clube Bahia during the construction of Arena Fonte Nova. It honors Roberto Santos, a prominent political and academic figure in Bahia.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by the Government of Bahia, the stadium is set to expand its capacity to 34,000 and has hosted significant football matches, including a World Cup qualifier.

world knowledge.Name: Geffen Playhouse
world knowledge.Address: 10886 Le Conte Avenue Los Angeles, California, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Geffen Playhouse was built in 1929 as the Masonic Affiliates Club for students and alumni at UCLA. It was one of the first twelve structures built in Westwood Village. Originally named the Contempo Theatre and later the Westwood Playhouse, the property was purchased by UCLA in 1993. The theater was renamed in 1995 after media mogul David Geffen donated $5 million. It underwent renovations in 2005, adding a new theater.

Major_Events.Description: The theater was renamed after David Geffen donated $5 million.
The Geffen reopened after a $17-million renovation, retaining the main 500-seat theater and adding a new 125-seat Audrey Skirball-Kenis Theater.

Major_Events.Event: Naming of the Gil Cates Theater
Major_Events.Description: The main stage was named the Gil Cates Theater in honor of its founder.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Stiles O. Clements. The courtyard fountain features pieces from Malibu Potteries, with patterns matching those in the Adamson House dining room.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Geffen Playhouse is a significant cultural landmark in Los Angeles, known for its contributions to theater arts and its historical architecture. It serves as a hub for theatrical productions and special events, fostering cultural enrichment in the community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Regional theater producing plays and special events.
world knowledge.Details: The Geffen Playhouse offers five plays per season in the Gil Cates Theater and three plays per season in the Audrey Skirball Kenis Theater. It was founded by Gilbert Cates and is currently operated by Geffen Playhouse Inc. under the ownership of UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television.

world knowledge.Name: Wet'n'Wild Toronto
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in 1986 as Sunshine Beach, later renamed Wild Water Kingdom, and now known as Wet'n'Wild Toronto. The park has undergone several expansions and renovations, including a major rebuild in 2016 by Premier Parks, LLC. It features numerous water attractions and has shifted to a family-focused approach.

Major_Events.Description: An 18+ beach-themed party lasting till 3am, held annually until the 2015 closure.
A pool party hosted by Drake and P. Reign.
A fitness training event based on U.S. Marine Corps training, led by former drill instructor Sgt. Tony Austin.
Organized by radio station Z103.5.
A military obstacle course competition raising over $25,000 for Rethink Breast Cancer.
Summer of Soca Festival.
Summer of Reggae Festival, a two-day concert event.
Included Carnival Kingdom, Caribana's largest outdoor concert.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of water attractions including water slides, a wave pool, a lazy river, a zip-line, and kid's splash areas. The wave pool is the fourth largest in Canada and was retrofitted to be saltwater in 2009.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wet'n'Wild Toronto is a significant recreational destination in the Greater Toronto Area, offering family-friendly water attractions and hosting various cultural and entertainment events.
world knowledge.Details: The park was closed in 2015 and 2016 for major renovations and reopened in 2017 under new ownership. It also faced closures in 2020 due to COVID-19 restrictions. The park features partnerships with food-service chains like Pizza Pizza and Mr. Sub, and has a mascot named Hugo the Hippo.

world knowledge.Name: Universal Volcano Bay
world knowledge.Address: Universal Orlando Resort, Orlando, Florida, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Universal Volcano Bay Water Theme Park, or Volcano Bay, is a tropical-themed water park at Universal Orlando Resort in Orlando, Florida. It replaced Wet 'n Wild as Universal Orlando Resort's only water park, the third theme park overall and was the first water park constructed by Universal Creative. Construction began in 2015, and the park officially opened on May 25, 2017.

Major_Events.Description: Universal Orlando Resort officials submitted plans for a new water park attraction to be located on their property near the Cabana Bay Beach Resort.
Volcano Bay officially opened to the public on May 25, 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is themed around Polynesian culture, with a central 200-foot-tall (61 m) volcano named 'Krakatau' featuring waterfalls during the day and lava flows at night. The park includes wave pools, thrill slides, lazy rivers, and rapids slides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Volcano Bay is significant as Universal Orlando Resort's first water park constructed by Universal Creative and as a major entertainment attraction in Florida. It reflects Polynesian cultural themes and offers a unique tropical-themed water park experience.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Water theme park providing entertainment and recreational activities.
world knowledge.Details: The park's attractions are located in four themed areas inspired by various Polynesian islands and cultures. The park has appeared in several television shows, including 'Impractical Jokers,' 'Food Network Star,' and 'Top Chef Junior.' The park operates year-round with heated water in winter. Initial reviews praised the park's appearance and theming but criticized the lines and the TapuTapu ride reservation system.

world knowledge.Name: University of Texas at Austin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) is a public research university founded in 1883. It is the flagship institution of the University of Texas System and has grown to become a major center for academic research, with significant contributions in various fields. The university has a rich history, including its establishment post-Texas independence, its role in desegregation, and its development into a leading educational institution.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Texas officially opened its doors on September 15, 1883.
The first Black students entered the university's undergraduate class in the fall of 1956.
On August 1, 1966, Charles Whitman barricaded the observation deck in the tower of the Main Building, killing 14 people and wounding others before being shot by police.
The university's official name was changed from 'The University of Texas' to 'The University of Texas at Austin' to reflect the growth of the University of Texas System.
The first presidential library on a university campus was dedicated on May 22, 1971.
The university transitioned to online classes for the spring 2020 semester due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Large student and faculty protests occurred on April 24, 2024, demanding a ceasefire in the Gaza war and divestment from companies profiting from Israel's actions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features the Beaux-Arts Main Building with a 307-foot tower designed by Paul Philippe Cret. The university has a mix of historic and modern buildings, including the Blanton Museum of Art and the Norman Hackerman building. The campus also has an extensive tunnel system used for utilities and communications.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UT Austin is a leading public research university with significant contributions to academia, sports, and culture. It is known for its diverse student body, extensive research programs, and vibrant campus life. The university has produced numerous notable alumni, including Nobel Prize winners, Pulitzer Prize winners, and Olympic medalists.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Texas at Austin is a major center for academic research, with research expenditures totaling $1.06 billion for the 2023 fiscal year. It houses seven museums and seventeen libraries, including the Lyndon B. Johnson Presidential Library and the Blanton Museum of Art. The university's athletics teams, the Texas Longhorns, have won numerous national championships. The campus spans 1,438.5 acres and includes the main campus in central Austin and the J. J. Pickle Research Campus in north Austin.

world knowledge.Name: Crescent City Connection
world knowledge.Address: Mississippi River, New Orleans, LA, USA
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 13,428 ft (4,093 m) length, 52 ft (16 m) width (westbound), 92 ft (28 m) width (eastbound)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Crescent City Connection (CCC), formerly the Greater New Orleans (GNO) Bridge, is a pair of cantilever bridges that carry U.S. Highway 90 Business over the Mississippi River in New Orleans. It is the farthest downstream bridge on the Mississippi River and the widest and most heavily traveled bridge on the lower Mississippi. The first span opened in 1958 as the longest cantilever bridge in the world at the time, and the second span opened in 1988. The bridges were renamed in 1989 following a public contest.

Major_Events.Description: Toll collections were halted to aid evacuation. The bridge was the only open highway into or out of the east bank of Orleans Parish after the storm. Gretna police set up a controversial roadblock on the bridge, refusing passage to evacuees on foot.
Toll collection was nullified due to a judicial decision and later defeated in a referendum, ending tolls on the bridge.
An annual event held on the first Saturday in September following Labor Day, using the HOV lanes of the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Twin steel truss cantilever bridges with a total length of 13,428 ft (4,093 m) and a longest span of 1,575 ft (480 m). The bridges feature decorative lights along the top profile lines.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an iconic part of New Orleans' skyline and has been featured in films and TV shows. It is the most heavily traveled bridge on the lower Mississippi and a critical transportation link for the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation bridge carrying U.S. Highway 90 Business over the Mississippi River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was the first in the United States to use electronic toll collection. It has been used as a filming location for movies like 'Déjà Vu' and '21 Jump Street', as well as TV shows like 'NCIS: New Orleans' and 'The Amazing Race 32'.

world knowledge.Name: Wimborne Minster
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Saxon period with Norman and Gothic additions
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wimborne Minster is a Saxon church with Norman and Gothic architecture. It is known for its chained library and the tomb of King Æthelred, elder brother of Alfred the Great. The church also houses the tombs of John Beaufort, Duke of Somerset, and his duchess, the maternal grandparents of King Henry VII of England.

Major_Events.Description: An annual event of traditional folk dance and music, it has become the focal point for one of the largest gatherings of dance teams and musicians in the South of England.
Held as part of Guy Fawkes celebrations, this event is a county record and is well supported by many thousands of people from the town and surrounding areas.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church features Saxon, Norman, and Gothic architectural styles. It is constructed using Dorset Limestone and New Forest Stone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wimborne Minster is culturally significant due to its historical architecture, the presence of the chained library, and the tombs of notable historical figures such as King Æthelred and the grandparents of King Henry VII.
world knowledge.Details: The town of Wimborne Minster is known for its preserved 15th-, 16th-, and 17th-century buildings, the Tivoli Theatre, and the model town, which is one of the largest and longest-established model towns in England.

world knowledge.Name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary, also known as Pakshi Kashi of Karnataka, is the largest bird sanctuary in Karnataka. It comprises six islets on the banks of the Kaveri river. The islets were formed when an embankment across the Kaveri river was built between 1645 and 1648 by the then king of Mysore, Kanteerava Narasimharaja Wadiyar. The ornithologist Salim Ali observed that the islets formed an important nesting ground for a large variety of birds and persuaded the king of Mysore to declare the area a protected area in 1940. The sanctuary was designated as a protected Ramsar site on 15 February 2022.

Major_Events.Description: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary was designated as a protected Ramsar site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The sanctuary comprises six islets with riverine reed beds covering the banks of the islands, while the islands themselves are covered in broadleaf forests, with dominant species being Terminalia arjuna (Arjun tree), bamboo groves, and Pandanus trees. Eucalyptus and acacia trees have also been planted.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is culturally and historically significant as it is the largest bird sanctuary in Karnataka and an important nesting ground for a large variety of birds. It was designated as a protected Ramsar site in 2022, highlighting its ecological importance.
world knowledge.Details: The sanctuary is maintained by the Forest Department of Karnataka and attracts about 3 lakh visitors annually. It is home to roughly 170 bird species, including the painted stork, Asian openbill stork, common spoonbill, woolly-necked stork, black-headed ibis, lesser whistling duck, Indian shag, stork-billed kingfisher, egret, cormorant, Oriental darter, spot-billed pelican, and heron. During winter months, as many as 40,000 birds congregate at Ranganathittu, some migrating from Siberia, Latin America, and parts of north India. The sanctuary also hosts numerous small mammals, including bonnet macaque, smooth-coated otter, colonies of flying fox, common palm civet, Indian gray mongoose, and a population of monitor lizards. The mugger crocodile or marsh crocodile is a common inhabitant of the riverine reed beds, and Ranganathittu has the largest freshwater crocodile population in Karnataka state. Ranger-guided boat tours of the isles are available throughout the day. The Salim Ali Interpretation Centre, maintained by the Forest Department, screens a 4-minute documentary to special interest groups.

world knowledge.Name: Delaware Art Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1912 as the Wilmington Society of the Fine Arts in honor of artist Howard Pyle. The museum's collection focuses on American art and illustration from the 19th to the 21st century, and the English Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood movement.

Major_Events.Event: Founding of the Wilmington Society of the Fine Arts
Major_Events.Description: Established to honor Howard Pyle, with an initial collection of over 100 paintings, drawings, and prints purchased from Pyle's widow.
The WSFA rented three rooms in the New Library Building in downtown Wilmington.
Samuel Bancroft's estate donated a collection of Pre-Raphaelite works and 11 acres of land for a new museum building.
The new building opened, housing the WSFA and the Wilmington Academy of Fine Arts.
The museum took out a $24.8 million loan for expansion, leading to financial difficulties during the 2008 crisis and subsequent art sales.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architects Victorine & Samuel Homsey and associate architect G. Morris Whiteside II. The building has undergone multiple expansions, including in 1956, 1970, 1987, and 2005.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum holds the largest and most important collection of British Pre-Raphaelite art and manuscript materials in the United States, as well as significant American illustration and modern art collections.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features a 9-acre Sculpture Park, the Helen Farr Sloan Library and Archives, studio art classes, a children's learning area, a cafe, and a museum store. It hosts about ten special exhibitions annually and offers around 100 educational programs each year.

world knowledge.Name: Cafeteria New Beach
world knowledge.Address: 18+1⁄2 miles of Castle Peak Road, So Kwun Wat, New Territories, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Golden Beach was one of the first artificial beaches constructed in Hong Kong, following the private beach at Tai Pak in Discovery Bay. It was built in 1994 using about 74,000 cubic metres of sand and opened to the public in 1995, originally under the management of the Regional Council. In 2000, management was transferred to the Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD).

Major_Events.Description: The beach was replenished with about 7,900 cubic metres of sand.
The LCSD hired the CEDD to conduct remedial works at Golden Beach, including replenishment of sand, construction of gabion walls, and groynes, at a cost of HK$7.2 million.
More than 18 lorry-loads worth of rubbish washed up on the beach in one 24-hour period.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Golden Beach features a 480-metre-long promenade with tropical trees and flowers, refreshment kiosks, a hotel, a shopping centre, and a volleyball court. It is the largest public beach in Tuen Mun District.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Golden Beach is one of the most well-attended beaches in Hong Kong, known for its recreational value and as a training ground for the Hong Kong national beach volleyball team.

Details.Water_Quality: Usually classified as Grade 2 (Fair), with occasional Grade 1 (Good). During the 2016 swimming season, it ranked Grade 2 for about 85% of tests and Grade 1 about 15% of the time.
Details.Attendance: Average attendance in 2016 was 1,941 on weekdays, 4,438 on weekends and holidays, and 670,350 during the bathing season.
Details.Erosion_Issues: Golden Beach suffers from serious sand loss, eroding by up to two metres per year due to its oblique position to prevailing wave direction. Part of the beach was closed in 2008 due to worsening conditions.
Details.Marine_Refuse: The beach faces a worsening problem with marine refuse, often bearing Simplified Chinese characters, suspected to originate from Mainland Chinese ships.

world knowledge.Name: Fortaleza–Pinto Martins International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The airport originated from a runway built in the 1930s and was used by Ceará Flying School until 2000. It became an important Allied base during World War II. Named after Euclides Pinto Martins, a pioneer aviator, in 1952. Upgraded to international status in 1997. Operated by Infraero from 1974 to 2017, then by Fraport Brasil.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Pinto Martins Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport's original name, Cocorote Airport, was changed to honor Euclides Pinto Martins.
The airport was upgraded to international status under Portaria 393 GM5.

Major_Events.Event: Investment plan for 2014 FIFA World Cup
Major_Events.Description: Infraero unveiled a BRL 525 million investment plan to upgrade the airport for the 2014 FIFA World Cup.
The airport was auctioned to Fraport AG for 30 years, leading to major renovations.
The renovation of the passenger terminal was completed, increasing capacity to 4 million passengers per year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern passenger terminal with a two-story extension, 14 aircraft parking positions, and a 2,755 m asphalt runway. The terminal includes a 60-position check-in area and a redesigned road system with a viaduct.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Euclides Pinto Martins, a pioneer in aviation, and played a key role in South Atlantic operations during World War II. It serves as a major hub for LATAM Brasil and is a vital transportation link for Fortaleza and northeastern Brazil.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public and military airport serving domestic and international flights.

world knowledge.Name: Boughton House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Boughton House is a country house in Northamptonshire, England, built by Ralph Montagu, 1st Duke of Montagu, after inheriting the estate in 1683. The house has a medieval core but its exterior reflects 17th-century French chateau architecture, earning it the nickname 'The English Versailles'. The house has remained virtually unchanged since the 17th century and is now one of the seats of the Duke of Buccleuch.

Major_Events.Description: Unknown scores of Italian Baroque music, including by Vivaldi, were discovered in the Montagu Music Collection at Boughton.
Boughton became the venue for the Greenbelt festival, a festival of arts, faith, and justice held annually in England since 1974.
Boughton was a location for the Ridley Scott film Napoleon (2023).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Boughton House has a medieval core but its exterior is designed in the style of a 17th-century French chateau, influenced by the Palace of Versailles. The house features baroque state rooms and a formal garden designed on the golden ratio.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Boughton House is culturally significant for its architectural beauty, its extensive collections of art, furniture, and armoury, and its well-preserved baroque state rooms. It is also known for its French-inspired gardens and its historical association with the Montagu, Douglas, and Scott families.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Country house and venue for events, weddings, and tours
world knowledge.Details: Boughton House is open to the public for guided tours on specific dates. It has been used as a filming location for various productions, including Les Misérables (2012) and An American Aristocrat's Guide to Great Estates (2020). The house is also known for its extensive collections, including notable paintings by El Greco and Thomas Gainsborough, and one of the finest privately held armouries in the country.

world knowledge.Name: Leuven Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: Grote Markt, Leuven, Flemish Brabant, Belgium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Town Hall of Leuven was built in a Brabantine late-Gothic style between 1439 and 1469. The initial construction was led by Sulpitius Van Vorst, followed by Jan Keldermans II, and later by Matheus de Layens. The building underwent renovations in the 19th century and survived both World Wars with minor damage.

Major_Events.Description: The Town Hall was built in phases, with initial construction starting in 1439 and completing in 1469 under the direction of Matheus de Layens.
Renovations were made necessary by centuries' worth of decay.
The building remained standing amid the devastation of Leuven, escaping with only minor damage.
A bomb strike in front of the building caused damage; repairs were completed in 1983.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in a Brabantine late-Gothic style, the Town Hall features ornate architecture with lace-like detail. It has three main stories with pointed Gothic windows, a gallery parapet, a steep roof with dormers, and octagonal turrets. The building is adorned with 236 statues in canopied niches, with corbels carved with Biblical scenes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Town Hall is a symbol of Leuven's rich history and architectural heritage. Its intricate design and historical importance make it a key landmark in the city.
world knowledge.Details: The interior accommodates an interesting collection of artwork, including sculptures by Constantin Meunier and Jef Lambeaux. Inside can also be seen the portraits of the Leuven mayors since 1794.

world knowledge.Name: Miyazaki Prefectural Art Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in Miyazaki, Japan, in 1995. The collection focuses on artists from or associated with Miyazaki Prefecture and also includes works by Picasso, Klee, and Magritte.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant due to its collection of works by both local artists and internationally renowned artists like Picasso, Klee, and Magritte.
world knowledge.Details: This article related to a museum in Japan is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: University of Buea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Buea was founded as a university center in 1985 and became a full-fledged university in 1992 following a government decree that re-organized state universities in Cameroon. It is regarded as the best university in Cameroon and is one of two English-speaking universities in the country, following the British system of education. It serves citizens from both anglophone and francophone regions of Cameroon and from neighboring countries such as Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Buea was established as a full-fledged university following a government decree that re-organized state universities in Cameroon.

Major_Events.Event: Introduction of Master of Science Degree in Disaster Risk Management
Major_Events.Description: The University introduced a new Master of Science Degree in Disaster Risk Management, aimed at equipping participants with skills to address natural and man-made hazards and disasters in the Central African Sub-Region, particularly in Cameroon.

Major_Events.Event: Agreement with Biaka University Institute of Buea
Major_Events.Description: An agreement was signed to strengthen the relationship between the University of Buea and the Biaka University Institute of Buea, mentoring BUIB in academic activities, particularly in the introduction of new postgraduate programs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus is situated at the foot of Mount Cameroon and features modern facilities, including lecture halls, teaching research laboratories, libraries, and sports complexes. The campus spans over 1,000 acres and is connected to an optic fiber link to Camtel, a telecommunications company.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Buea is culturally significant as it serves as a hub for education and research in Cameroon, attracting students from both anglophone and francophone regions and neighboring countries. It plays a leadership role in the educational sector and is involved in various research and capacity-building projects.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Buea has a student population of over 13,000, including 50 physically and visually disabled students. It has 300 permanent and 200 part-time teaching staff, and 473 support staff. The university offers undergraduate and graduate programs in various fields of study and has a School of Postgraduate Studies. It is engaged in diverse research activities and capacity-building projects, including projects funded by international organizations such as the World Health Organization, Medicine for Malaria Venture, and Wellcome Trust-Oxford University. The university also has linkages with foreign universities and is affiliated with the University of Manchester and the Association of Commonwealth Universities.

world knowledge.Name: Imatong Mountains
world knowledge.Area: Eastern Equatoria, South Sudan and Northern Region, Uganda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Imatong Mountains are located in southeastern South Sudan and extend into Uganda. They are known for their rich biodiversity and have been affected by human activities such as deforestation and subsistence farming. The mountains have a history of being a haven for the Lord's Resistance Army during the Second Sudanese Civil War.

Major_Events.Description: Samuel Baker was the first European to visit the region, traveling in the northwest and west of the area.
Emin Pasha traveled along the eastern foothills of the mountains and then southwest to the White Nile.
The Lord's Resistance Army used the mountains as a haven during the Second Sudanese Civil War, leading to significant violence and ecological disruption.
Over 400 people were massacred by the LRA in the Imotong area.
The Imatong Mountains became part of South Sudan when the country was established.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Imatong Mountains are culturally significant due to their rich biodiversity and unique flora and fauna, which are found nowhere else in South Sudan. They are also important to the local Nilotic communities who practice subsistence farming and raise livestock.
world knowledge.Details: The Imatong Mountains are the highest in South Sudan, with Mount Kinyeti reaching 3,187 metres. The range has an equatorial climate and supports diverse wildlife, although it has been increasingly degraded by human activities. The mountains are drained by several rivers and have a variety of vegetation zones, from lowland semi-evergreen forest to montane forest and heather thicket. The area has been proposed for conversion into a National Park to balance community needs, commercial plantations, and biodiversity conservation.

world knowledge.Name: Senedd
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Senedd, officially known as the Welsh Parliament, is the devolved, unicameral legislature of Wales. It was established by the Government of Wales Act 1998, following the result of the 1997 referendum. Initially known as the National Assembly for Wales, it was renamed to Senedd Cymru or the Welsh Parliament in May 2020. The Senedd makes laws for Wales, agrees to certain taxes, and scrutinises the Welsh Government.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the National Assembly for Wales
Major_Events.Description: The National Assembly for Wales was created by the Government of Wales Act 1998, following the result of the 1997 referendum.
The National Assembly for Wales was renamed to Senedd Cymru or the Welsh Parliament when section 2 of the Senedd and Elections (Wales) Act 2020 came into force.
The Welsh Assembly passed its first Act, the Local Government Byelaws (Wales) Act.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Senedd building was designed by the Richard Rogers Partnership and built by Taylor Woodrow. It uses traditional Welsh materials, such as slate and Welsh oak, in its construction. The design is based around the concepts of openness and transparency. The building is environmentally friendly, using an Earth Heat Exchange system for heating, rainwater collection for flushing toilets and cleaning windows, and a wind cowl to funnel natural light and air into the debating chamber.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Senedd is culturally significant as it represents the devolved governance of Wales, allowing for the creation of laws and policies specific to the Welsh context. It is a symbol of Welsh autonomy and democracy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary function of the Senedd is to serve as the devolved legislature of Wales, making laws, agreeing to certain taxes, and scrutinising the Welsh Government.
world knowledge.Details: The Senedd comprises 60 members who are known as members of the Senedd (Aelodau o'r Senedd). Members are elected for a five-year term of office under an additional member system, with 40 members representing constituencies and 20 members representing electoral regions. The Senedd's powers include health, education, economic development, transport, the environment, agriculture, local government, and some taxes.

world knowledge.Name: Peterhouse, Cambridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Peterhouse is the oldest constituent college of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1284 by Hugh de Balsham, Bishop of Ely. It has a rich history of academic excellence and notable alumni in various fields.

Major_Events.Description: Peterhouse was founded by Hugh de Balsham, Bishop of Ely, as the first college of the University of Cambridge.
Peterhouse was the first college in the University to have electric lighting installed, provided by Lord Kelvin to celebrate the college's six-hundredth anniversary.
Women were admitted to Peterhouse for the first time under the mastership of Hugh Trevor-Roper.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Peterhouse features a mix of architectural styles, including Gothic, Renaissance, and Modern Movement. Notable buildings include the Chapel, the Burrough's Building, and the William Stone Building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Peterhouse is culturally significant as the oldest college in the University of Cambridge, with a long history of academic achievement and notable alumni in science, politics, and the arts.
world knowledge.Details: Peterhouse is one of the wealthiest colleges in Cambridge, with assets exceeding £350 million. It has a strong tradition of communal dining, known as 'Hall', and hosts a biennial white-tie ball during May Week celebrations.

image_name: Holy Assumption of the Virgin Mary Church

world knowledge.Name: Holy Assumption of the Virgin Mary Church
world knowledge.Area: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Alaska, United States
world knowledge.Address: Mission and Overland Streets, Kenai, Alaska
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Completed in 1896, it is the oldest-standing Russian Orthodox church in Alaska and was a major center for the assimilation of the local Native population. Alaska became a diocese in the Russian Orthodox Church in 1840, and the Church's popularity in the Kenai Peninsula region grew, particularly among the Kenaitze, the native people of the peninsula. Bishop Innocent created six parishes in Alaska, including one for the Kenai region. The first chapel was built that same year by the Russian-American Company near the village of Kenai within Fort St. Nicholas. The first priest to serve the parish, Igumen Nikolai Militov, arrived in 1844 and served until his death in 1869.

Major_Events.Description: Built by the Russian-American Company near the village of Kenai within Fort St. Nicholas.
Built on a different portion of the lot.
Built from logs in the Pskov style, replacing the 1849 structure.
Completed later after the church construction.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the Chapel of St. Nicholas
Major_Events.Description: Built over the graves of Igumen Nikolai, his assistant and reader Makari Ivanov, and an unrecorded monk.
The church site, including the rectory, cemetery, and chapel, was declared a National Historic Landmark.

Major_Events.Event: Added to the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Added shortly after being declared a National Historic Landmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built from logs in the Pskov style, that is in the shape of a ship. The interior contains an elaborate iconostasis.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the oldest-standing Russian Orthodox church in Alaska and was a major center for the assimilation of the local Native population. The church served as a vital method of assimilating the natives to the Russian culture. In addition to religious and educational purposes, the church served as an administrative and judicial center for the region.
world knowledge.Details: The church is a member of the Orthodox Church in America Diocese of Alaska and further the Kenai Deanery. The rectory was built in 1881 and is considered the oldest building in the Peninsula. The Chapel of St. Nicholas sits on the site of the original chapel, across the street from the church, on a bluff overlooking the confluence of the Kenai River and Cook Inlet.

world knowledge.Name: Covesea Skerries Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built following a storm in 1826 that sank 16 vessels, the lighthouse was constructed despite initial opposition. It was designed by Alan Stevenson and completed in 1846. The lighthouse was automated in 1984 and deactivated in 2012. It is now owned by the Covesea Lighthouse Community Company for tourism development.

Major_Events.Description: A storm sank 16 vessels, leading to demands for lighthouses at Tarbat Ness and Covesea Skerries.
The Covesea Skerries Lighthouse was completed at a cost of £11,514.
The lighthouse was automated and remotely monitored from Edinburgh.
The lighthouse was deactivated after a North Cardinal buoy with radar was installed.
The lighthouse was sold to the Covesea Lighthouse Community Company for tourism development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 36-meter cylindrical masonry tower with balcony and lantern, white tower with black lantern.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Designed by Alan Stevenson of the renowned Stevenson lighthouse engineering dynasty, the lighthouse is a Category A listed building and an iconic landmark with historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a navigational aid, now a tourism hub.
world knowledge.Details: The original lens is displayed at the Lossiemouth Fisheries and Community Museum. The lighthouse was designated a Category A listed building on 26 January 1971.

world knowledge.Name: Winton Castle
world knowledge.Address: Between Pencaitland and Tranent, East Lothian, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Winton Castle is a historic building set in a large estate between Pencaitland and Tranent in East Lothian, Scotland. The origins of the castle date from 1480 when George, 4th Lord Seton, commenced the building of Wintoun Castle. The castle has passed through the hands of several eminent families and has undergone various restorations and improvements over the centuries.

Major_Events.Description: Edward Seymour, Earl of Hertford, all but destroyed Wintoun Castle after bombardment and burning.
George Seton, 5th Earl of Winton was captured at the Battle of Preston, leading to the confiscation of his assets, titles, and lands.
Prince Charles Edward Stuart requisitioned Winton to garrison his troops.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Anglo-Scottish Renaissance, with Tudor style additions. The castle contains ornate and intricate plaster ceilings, fine furniture, family treasures, and many paintings by notable Scottish painters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Winton Castle is considered a masterpiece of Scottish Renaissance architecture and is a category A listed building. It has been a private residence and is now run as an exclusive-use events venue.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is situated off the B6355 road approximately 0.5 miles (0.80 km) north of Pencaitland. The gardens are terraced to the banks of St. David's Loch and up to the walled garden. There are several routed walkways, open to the public, passing through the estate woodlands and along the banks of the Tyne Water.

world knowledge.Name: Saint Mary Church of Tabriz
world knowledge.Address: Corner of North Shariati (north Shahnaz) and Jomhuri avenues, Dik Bashi neighborhood, Tabriz, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: An older church was built at this site in the 12th century AD. The church was destroyed in a disastrous earthquake in 1780 AD, and the present building was built on its ruins from 1782 to 1785 in Safavid style. It is the largest and oldest Christian church in Tabriz and a notable centre for Armenian national and religious ceremonies.

Major_Events.Description: The church – as well as the whole city – was destroyed in a disastrous earthquake in 1780 AD.
The present building was built on the ruins of the destroyed church from 1782 to 1785 in Safavid style.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is built in Armenian and Safavid styles. It has a belfry standing on four square columns with four arches and biblical paintings between the columns. The tabernacle was built in the style of Armenian architecture, with parts dating back to the 12th century AD. The base is made of limestone, while the walls and pillars are of stone and brick, and the vault is of brick.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the largest and oldest Christian church in Tabriz and a notable centre for Armenian national and religious ceremonies. It has served as the seat of the Azarbaijan Armenian archbishop and is governed by a board of Armenian peers.
world knowledge.Details: The church is located in the historical Dik Bashi neighborhood in the center of Tabriz. The oldest gravestone in this church dates back to the 16th century AD. The Tabriz Armenian Museum next to the church is run by the Armenian Prelacy of Tabriz.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Byron Light
world knowledge.Area: Far North Coast of New South Wales
world knowledge.Address: Lighthouse Road, Byron Bay, Cape Byron, Byron Shire, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Byron Light, also called Cape Byron Lightstation, is an active heritage-listed lighthouse and now interpretative centre, interpretative space, maritime museum, administration office, retail building, accommodation, tourist attraction and visitor attraction located at Cape Byron on the Far North Coast of New South Wales, Australia. It was designed by Charles Harding and Cecil W. Darley and built from 1899 to 1901 by Messrs Mitchell & King. It is also known as Cape Byron Lightstation (including moveable items), Byron Bay Lighthouse, Cape Byron Headland and Cape Byron Headland Reserve. The property is owned by NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to the Commonwealth Heritage List
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was added to the Commonwealth Heritage List on 22 June 2004.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to the New South Wales State Heritage Register
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 22 February 2019.
The opening by the Premier took place on 1 December 1901.
The station was fully automated in 1989, and the last lighthouse keeper departed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Cape Byron Lighthouse is a circular tower, approximately 22m in height to the top of the lantern. Built of precast concrete blocks on a mass concrete foundation, the tower includes a concrete circular staircase with metal balustrade to its upper chambers and second floor. A metal staircase continues to the lantern room. The lighthouse includes a 13 inch Chance Bros & Co lantern on a Henry-Lepaute mercury float pedestal. The lighthouse has a concrete balcony with a trachyte balustrade.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cape Byron Lightstation is the most well known and highly visited lightstation in Australia. Standing on the most eastern point of Australia, the sweep of the light is clearly visible from the Byron Bay township which serves to reinforce its presence in the environment and evokes a sense of identity and "ownership" by the local community. The headland is also a significant tourist attraction in Australia due to the unique interaction of the natural and cultural factors and the evocative image of the tower standing against a dramatic coastal environment.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid, tourist attraction, and cultural heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is very well known, attracting more than 500,000 visitors per year. It is also a popular site for whale watching, with Southern Cross University's Whale Research Centre located at the lighthouse. The lighthouse is located at the end of Lighthouse Road, east of Byron Bay. The site is open from sunrise to sunset, and paid parking is available at the site, and the tower is open to guided tours every day except Christmas Day, reservations are not required. The lighthouse can also be visited on foot from Byron Bay township via the Cape Byron Walking Track.

world knowledge.Name: Yaquina Head Light
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Yaquina Head Light, also known early in its existence as the Cape Foulweather Lighthouse, is a lighthouse on the Oregon Coast of the United States, established in 1873. It is located in Lincoln County, near Newport at Yaquina Head. The tower stands 93 feet (28 m) tall, and is the tallest lighthouse in Oregon. Made in Paris in 1868 and shipped to Oregon, Yaquina Head Light was first lit August 20, 1873, and automated in 1966.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was automated.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was listed in the National Register of Historic Places.
17 servicemen were stationed at Yaquina Head to keep a lookout for enemy ships.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Conical tower made of brick on basalt rock foundation, standing 93 feet (28 m) tall with 114 steps. Features a first order Fixed Fresnel lens made in Paris in 1868.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Yaquina Head Light is the tallest lighthouse in Oregon and has been a significant navigational aid since 1873. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is managed as part of the Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse still uses its original 1868 French-made, 1st order, Fixed Fresnel lens, visible 19 miles (31 km) out to sea. The 100-acre (40 ha) site was established by Congress as an Outstanding Natural Area in 1980. The Bureau of Land Management manages the Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area, including the lighthouse. The Yaquina Head Interpretive Center opened in 1997 and includes exhibits about the history and preservation of the lighthouse, and the marine life found in tide pools and along the coast. The lighthouse was used as the setting for the 'Moesko Island Lighthouse' in the 2002 film The Ring, and also appeared in Hysterical (1983) and The Nancy Drew Mysteries 1977 television series episode 'The Mystery of Pirate's Cove'.

world knowledge.Name: Mannheim Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mannheim Palace, originally the main residence of the Prince-electors of the Electorate of the Palatinate of the House of Wittelsbach, was constructed in the 18th century. Elector Karl III Philip decided to make Mannheim the Palatinate's new capital in 1720, leading to the construction of the palace on the site of the old Friedrichsburg fortress. The palace was part of a trend among German princes to create grand new residences. Construction began in 1720 and was completed in 1760. The palace saw its zenith during the reign of Elector Charles Theodor, who later moved his court to Munich in 1778. The palace suffered significant damage during World War II but has since been extensively renovated.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Mannheim Palace began on June 2, 1720, as part of Elector Karl III Philip's decision to make Mannheim the new capital of the Palatinate.
Construction of Mannheim Palace was completed, marking the end of a 40-year building process.
Mannheim Palace was heavily bombed and partly destroyed during World War II.
The palace underwent extensive renovation with private donations and government funding totaling more than 54 million euros.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mannheim Palace is a large Baroque palace, one of the biggest in Europe and the second largest in Baroque style after Versailles. It features a 450-meter-long front, a central Mittelbau with representative halls, and wings including the Ehrenhof West and Ehrenhof Ost. The palace has been repainted in bright ochre/yellow, and the Mittelbau has been thoroughly rebuilt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mannheim Palace is culturally significant as the former residence of the Prince-electors of the Palatinate and as a symbol of the Baroque era in Germany. It played a central role in the political and cultural life of the region and continues to be an important historical and architectural landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: University of Mannheim's central building complex
world knowledge.Details: Part of the palace is used today by the University of Mannheim, housing key institutions such as the rectorate and the main library. The palace also includes the Schlosskirche (palace church), the law section, and Mannheim's Amtsgericht (lower district court). The Ehrenhof includes a bunker from World War II, now used as occasional exposition space for modern and urban art.

world knowledge.Name: Punta Hermosa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Punta Hermosa is one of 43 districts of the Lima Province in Peru. It was founded on April 7, 1954. The area used to be a resort/vacation district where visitors stayed only temporarily, but has recently seen an urban expansion and an increase in permanent year-round residents.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Punta Hermosa is culturally significant for its beaches, which are visited by thousands of people every summer.
world knowledge.Details: Punta Hermosa borders the Pacific Ocean on the west; the Lurin, and Pachacámac districts on the north; Huarochirí Province's, district of Santo Domingo de los Olleros on the east; and the Punta Negra district on the south. The district is divided into 4 populated centers (Spanish: Centros Poblados). It is connected to Lima by the Pan-American Highway. The current mayor is Carlos Fernández (2023–2026).

world knowledge.Name: St George's Hill
world knowledge.Address: St George's Hill, Weybridge, Surrey, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St George's Hill is a private gated community developed by W. G. Tarrant in 1911. It was originally a wooded wilderness that transformed into a hillside studded with mansions. The area has a rich history, including an Iron Age hillfort and the 1649 Diggers' movement. It has been a prestigious residence for wealthy individuals and celebrities.

Major_Events.Description: Led by Gerard Winstanley and William Everard, a group began to 'dig and sow' on St George's Hill, which they regarded as common land. They faced opposition and eventually left by September of that year.
Developer Walter George Tarrant purchased 964 acres of the ancient common land and began developing it into a private estate.
The estate was restricted to the public, becoming a fully private gated community.
Environmental campaigner George Monbiot and supporters squatted on the hill to commemorate the Diggers' occupation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The earliest mansions were built in the Arts and Crafts style. The estate features a mix of architectural styles reflecting its development over the decades.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St George's Hill is culturally significant as a symbol of wealth and exclusivity. It has been home to numerous celebrities and high net worth individuals. Its history includes the Diggers' movement, which is a notable part of British social history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential community with additional recreational facilities
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes St George's Hill Golf Club, designed by Harry Colt in 1912, and St George's Hill Lawn Tennis Club, opened in 1915. The estate is known for its security features, including automatic number plate recognition technology. It is a popular residence for wealthy individuals, including many from former Soviet states.

world knowledge.Name: Angra do Heroísmo City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Angra do Heroísmo City Hall is a medieval structure constructed to house the municipal council/authority, situated in the civil parish of Sé, municipality of Angra do Heroísmo, on the Portuguese archipelago of the Azores. The first organized municipal meeting occurred in 1474. The building has undergone several renovations and has served various administrative functions over the centuries.

Major_Events.Description: The first organized municipal meeting occurred on the site of the current building.
An earthquake caused damage to many buildings in the city, including the City Hall.
The building was remodeled, resulting in the refurbishment and expansion of the municipal square.
Angra received the title of Sempre Leal Cidade (Always Loyal City) due to its notable actions.
Angra was named capital of Portugal under the Regency of Angra during the Liberal Wars.
A decision was made to construct a new building, which was inaugurated in 1866.
An extreme earthquake caused significant damage to the property.
The building was included within the classified areas of the Central Zone of the City of Angra do Heroísmo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The municipal hall is a simple, rectangular plan covered in tiled ceiling. The two-floor facade is decorated in cornerstone with fenestrated sills on the first floor, and with the second floor encircled by stone terminating in plain cornices, decorated in white. The main facade is oriented to the west, and includes five sections, with rectangular frontispiece and jagged cornices, crowned by a marble feminine statute, representing the city of Angra. The ground floor includes three sections, separated by pilasters that includes a central portico with arched doorway and lateral sections with corresponding square doors surmounted by semi-circular rounded windows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Angra do Heroísmo City Hall is culturally and historically important due to its long-standing role as the administrative center of the city and its architectural significance as a medieval structure. It has witnessed and been part of numerous historical events, including the Liberal Wars and the establishment of the Regency of Angra.
world knowledge.Details: The municipal palace is situated in the centre of the historic centre of Angra do Heroísmo, adapted to the slope at the end of a block and flanked by roadways. Its western facade is occupied by a large square, called Praça Velha, paved with Portuguese pavement stone, forming geometric shapes and punctuated by trees. The building has been renovated several times, with notable changes in 1610-1611, 1847-1866, and after the 1980 earthquake.

world knowledge.Name: University of Oregon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Oregon (UO) is a public research university founded in 1876. It was established by the Oregon State Legislature and initially named Oregon State University. The university has grown significantly over the years, expanding its academic programs, facilities, and research initiatives. It has faced challenges such as state disinvestment and financial difficulties but has also benefited from substantial private donations, particularly from Phil Knight, co-founder of Nike. The university is known for its strong athletic programs, particularly in track and field, and its complex relationship with Nike.

Major_Events.Description: The Oregon State Legislature established the university, initially naming it Oregon State University.
The university opened its doors with 155 students and five faculty members.
The first graduating class consisted of five students.

Major_Events.Event: Proposals to Merge with Oregon State University
Major_Events.Description: Proposals to merge the university with what is now Oregon State University were defeated both times.

Major_Events.Event: Admission to Association of American Universities
Major_Events.Description: UO was admitted into the Association of American Universities (AAU).

Major_Events.Event: Filming of National Lampoon's Animal House
Major_Events.Description: The cult classic film was shot on the university campus.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Independent Board of Trustees
Major_Events.Description: UO became an independent public body governed by the Board of Trustees of the University of Oregon.
UO hosted the 2022 World Athletics Championships, the first time the event was held in the United States.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of historic and modern buildings, many planned around major quadrangles. Notable buildings include University Hall (1876) and Villard Hall (1886), both designated National Historic Landmarks. The campus is also known for its arboretum with over 500 species of trees. Recent construction projects include Matthew Knight Arena and the Phil and Penny Knight Campus for Accelerating Scientific Impact.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Oregon is culturally significant for its contributions to education, research, and athletics. It is known for its strong track and field programs and its association with Nike. The university has also played a role in popular culture, serving as the filming location for National Lampoon's Animal House. Additionally, it is recognized for its sustainable design practices and commitment to environmental responsibility.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public research university offering undergraduate and graduate degree programs.
world knowledge.Details: The university is organized into nine colleges and schools, offering 420 degree programs. It has a diverse student body from all 50 U.S. states and 91 countries. UO is a member of the Association of American Universities and is classified as an R1: Doctoral University with very high research activity. The university has a strong athletic tradition, with 28 NCAA team championships, and is known for its track and field program. The mascot is the Oregon Duck, and the fight song is "Mighty Oregon." The university has a long-standing relationship with Nike, co-founded by alumnus Phil Knight, who has donated over $1 billion to the university.

world knowledge.Name: Wild Adventures
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wild Adventures was founded in 1996 by Kent Buescher and his wife Dawn Buescher on a plot of farmland outside of Valdosta, Georgia. It started as a small petting zoo known as Liberty Farms D&L and has since expanded to include rides, exotic animals, and a water park. The park was purchased by Herschend Family Entertainment in 2007 after the original owners filed for bankruptcy.

Major_Events.Description: Splash Island, the park's water park, opened as the largest expansion at the time, featuring a 100-meter drop double slide.
Herschend Family Entertainment purchased Wild Adventures for $34.4 million after the original owners filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
Wild Adventures was temporarily shut down due to the COVID-19 pandemic but reopened in July 2020.
A new children's section was created using old rides that were repainted and renovated to match the theme of the area.
A new themed area was added, featuring relocated and renamed rides.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Wild Adventures is a zoological theme park with a mix of animal exhibits, roller coasters, flat rides, and a Polynesian-themed water park. The park features various themed areas such as Discovery Outpost and Oasis Outpost.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wild Adventures is a significant regional attraction, offering a combination of animal exhibits and amusement park rides. It serves as a family-friendly destination and contributes to the local economy.
world knowledge.Details: Wild Adventures is owned by Herschend Family Entertainment and managed by Jon Vigue. The park features six roller coasters, nine water rides, and live shows. It operates seasonally from mid-March through December. The park's slogan is 'Creating Memories Worth Repeating.'

world knowledge.Name: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 51 acres (207,000 m² total floor space, 22,500 m² main pitch)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was constructed as part of North Korea's efforts to showcase its strength and legitimacy following the awarding of the 1988 Summer Olympics to Seoul. It opened on 1 May 1989, initially with a capacity of 150,000, and was the largest stadium ever built in Asia at the time. It has hosted mass performances celebrating North Korean leaders and national pride, notably the Arirang Festival.

Major_Events.Event: 13th World Festival of Youth and Students
