Major_Events.Description: The first major event hosted at the stadium, organized to promote North Korea's international standing and held shortly after its opening.
A massive gymnastics and artistic performance involving over 100,000 participants; recognized by Guinness World Records in 2007 as the largest gymnastics display.
The largest professional wrestling pay-per-view event ever, with two days of events attended by 150,000 and 190,000 spectators respectively.
Two-year renovation project which reduced capacity to 114,000 through modernization and replacement of bench seating with individual seats.
President Moon Jae-in of South Korea gave a speech with Kim Jong Un to 150,000 spectators, emphasizing themes of peace and reunification.

Major_Events.Event: Xi Jinping Visit and Grand Performance
Major_Events.Description: A special event called 'Invincible Socialism' hosted in honor of the 70th anniversary of China–North Korea relations.
A national celebration concert attended by Kim Jong Un and high-ranking officials, establishing the stadium as the primary New Year venue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a scalloped roof with 16 arches arranged in a ring, designed to resemble a magnolia blossom. It rises over 60 meters (200 ft) and spans eight stories. The main pitch covers 22,500 m², and the total floor space exceeds 207,000 m². It originally seated up to 150,000 and currently holds 114,000 after renovation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a central venue for North Korea's political and cultural propaganda, particularly through mass performances celebrating the leadership and national unity. It is a powerful symbol of state grandeur and spectacle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium (football, athletics, mass games, performances)
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the second largest in the world by seating capacity and remains expandable to 150,000. It hosts sports events and iconic mass performances like the Arirang Festival. The surface is artificial turf. Originally called the Rungrado May Day Stadium, it was renamed to emphasize the 1st of May as International Workers' Day.

world knowledge.Name: Ahmed Ben Bella Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ahmed Ben Bella Airport, formally Es-Sénia Airport, is located 4.7 nm south of Oran, Algeria. During World War II, it was used by the French Air Force and later by the Vichy government. It was a primary objective during the Operation Torch landings in 1942. After its capture, it was used by the United States Army Air Forces Twelfth Air Force during the North African Campaign. Post-war, it served as a stopover for Air Transport Command. A new runway was constructed and became operational in 2009. The airport currently has two terminals, with a new international terminal inaugurated in 2022.

Major_Events.Description: La Sénia Airport was a primary objective during the assault on Oran. It was attacked by Allied forces and captured by Company B of the 1st Armored Regiment.
A new 9,843 feet long runway 07R/25L became operational on 12 February 2009.
A new international terminal with a surface area of 41,000 m2 was inaugurated on 23 June 2022 by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has two runways made of concrete. The new international terminal is equipped with photovoltaic panels and has six telescopic gangways.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a significant transportation hub in Algeria, serving the second largest city, Oran, which is an important industrial, educational, and cultural center.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is composed of two terminals, one for domestic flights and the other for international flights. The new international terminal, Terminal 3, has a capacity of 3.5 million passengers, extendable to 6 million passengers per year.

image_name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

world knowledge.Name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
world knowledge.Address: 151 Third Street, San Francisco, California, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 170,000 square feet (16,000 m²) of exhibition space
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1935 as the first museum on the West Coast devoted solely to 20th-century art, SFMOMA has grown into one of the largest museums in the United States for modern and contemporary art. It was initially located in the Veterans Building in Civic Center before moving to its current Mario Botta-designed home in 1995. A major expansion by Snøhetta was completed in 2016.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded under director Grace L. McCann Morley as the San Francisco Museum of Art, initially located in the Veterans Building.
The museum opened in its Mario Botta-designed home in the SoMa district.
Following a three-year closure for expansion by Snøhetta, the museum re-opened with more than double the gallery space.
The exhibition drew more than 400,000 visitors during its three-month run, setting a record for the museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original 1995 building by Mario Botta features a central, skylighted atrium with galleries rising around it, and a distinctive black-and-white striped silo. The 2016 expansion by Snøhetta includes a large-scale vertical garden, a free-access gallery with glass walls, and facades clad with Fibre-Reinforced Plastic panels. The building achieved LEED Gold certification.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SFMOMA is a leading institution for modern and contemporary art, with an internationally recognized collection of over 33,000 works. It was one of the first museums to recognize photography as an art form and has played a significant role in promoting 20th and 21st-century art on the West Coast.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum of modern and contemporary art

world knowledge.Name: Paris Nanterre University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Paris Nanterre University was established in 1964 as a satellite campus of the Sorbonne and gained independent status in 1970. It was originally part of the University of Paris and became one of its successor universities. The campus was a center for the May '68 student rebellion and has since grown into one of France's most prestigious universities, known for law, humanities, and social sciences.

Major_Events.Description: The campus was at the center of the May '68 student protests, earning nicknames like 'Nanterre, la folie' (Mad Nanterre) and 'Nanterre la rouge' (Red Nanterre).
The university gained independent legal status as 'University of Paris-X' and adopted an American-style campus model.
The university was renamed from 'University of Paris West' to 'Paris Nanterre University.'

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Urban campus with modern concrete and glass structures, featuring facilities such as an Olympic-sized swimming pool and a stadium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of France's most prestigious universities, known for its contributions to law, humanities, and social sciences. It has produced numerous influential alumni, including heads of state, cabinet officials, and business leaders.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers competitive programs in law, economics, and humanities, with partnerships with grandes écoles like ESSEC and Ecole Polytechnique. It hosts international summer and winter universities, fostering Franco-German and European academic collaboration. The campus is the second largest in France and welcomes 35,000 to 40,000 students annually.

world knowledge.Name: University of Mumbai
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1857 following a dispatch from Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of Control, to Governor-General Lord Dalhousie. It was modeled on the University of London. The first departments were the Faculty of Arts at Elphinstone College in 1835 and the Faculty of Medicine at Grant Medical College in 1845. The university was renamed from University of Bombay to University of Mumbai in 1996.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Mumbai was established following a dispatch from Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of Control, to Governor-General Lord Dalhousie.
The first degrees awarded were Bachelor of Arts and Licentiate in Medicine.
Cornelia Sorabji became the university's first female graduate.
The university was renamed from University of Bombay to University of Mumbai.
The first phase of restoration of Rajabai Clock Tower started in 2013 and was completed in May 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Rajabai Clock Tower, modeled on the clock tower of the Palace of Westminster in London, is 85 meters tall and has five storeys. It houses the University of Mumbai's library.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Mumbai is one of the largest university systems in the world and has played a significant role in the educational development of India. It has a rich history and has produced many notable alumni.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education institution offering courses in science, commerce, and the arts.
world knowledge.Details: The university has over 549,000 students on its campuses and affiliated colleges. It has signed Memoranda of Understanding with several international universities including the University of Amsterdam, University of Bath, and Oxford University.

world knowledge.Name: Taipei Main Station
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 149 m (488 ft 10 in) long and 110 m (360 ft 11 in) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first rail station in Taipei was completed in Twatutia in 1891 during Qing rule. It was relocated and rebuilt multiple times, with the current underground station completed in 1989 as part of the Taipei Railway Underground Project to alleviate traffic congestion.

Major_Events.Description: The first rail station in Taipei was completed in Twatutia during Qing rule.
The station was relocated to the east of its current location.
The station was rebuilt to accommodate growing passenger traffic.
The current underground station was completed, and railway service was moved to the new building.
The metro station connected to the basement of the railway station opened to passenger traffic.
The station became a terminus for Taiwan High Speed Rail trains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rectangular building with six stories above ground and four stories below ground. Features a large ticketing hall with a skylight, underground passageways, and multiple platforms for different rail services.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Taipei Main Station is the busiest station in Taiwan and a major transportation hub, connecting Taipei Metro, Taiwan High Speed Rail, and Taiwan Railway. It plays a crucial role in the daily lives of millions of commuters and travelers.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation hub (metro, railway, and high-speed rail)
world knowledge.Details: The station underwent renovation work from February to October 2011, including basement restroom renovations, retail space preparations, and improvements to fire and evacuation regulations. Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki was chosen to design two skyscrapers adjacent to the station, which will be 76 and 56 stories tall.

world knowledge.Name: Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria is the Italian national paintings collection of Umbria, housed in the Palazzo dei Priori, Perugia. Its origins lie in the foundation of the Perugian Accademia del Disegno in the mid-16th century. The collection was formally named after Pietro Vannucci in 1863 and moved to the Palazzo dei Priori in 1878. It became the Regia Galleria Vannucci in 1918 and was later renamed Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria. The museum's current form was inaugurated in 2006.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the Perugian Accademia del Disegno
Major_Events.Description: The Academy began to assemble a collection of paintings and drawings.

Major_Events.Event: Formal naming of the civic paintings collection
Major_Events.Description: The collection was named after Pietro Vannucci.
The collection moved into the third floor of the Palazzo dei Priori.
The pinacoteca became the Regia Galleria Vannucci under the patronage of the king.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the current museum path
Major_Events.Description: The museum was inaugurated in its current form.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the Palazzo dei Priori, a historic building in Perugia. The exhibition spaces occupy two floors and are spread across 40 rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses the greatest representation of the Umbrian School of painting, ranging from the 13th to the 19th century, and is particularly strong in the fourteenth through sixteenth centuries. It features works by notable Italian artists such as Arnolfo di Cambio, Nicola Pisano, Duccio, Fra Angelico, and Piero della Francesca.
world knowledge.Details: The collection includes Renaissance and Medieval paintings and sculptures, with particular attention given to Umbrian masters like Benedetto Bonfigli, Bartolomeo Caporali, Fiorenzo di Lorenzo, Perugino, and Pintoricchio. The museum also has an exhibition space for temporary collections on the second floor, which changes several times a year.

world knowledge.Name: Bunaken National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bunaken National Park is a marine park established in 1991, located in the north of Sulawesi Island, Indonesia. It is among the first of Indonesia's marine parks and covers a total area of 890.65 km², 97% of which is marine habitat. The park is representative of Indonesian tropical water ecosystems, consisting of seagrass plains, coral reefs, and coastal ecosystems.

Major_Events.Description: Bunaken National Park was formally established as a national park.

Major_Events.Event: Application to UNESCO World Heritage List
Major_Events.Description: Indonesia submitted an application to UNESCO for including the park on the World Heritage List.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bunaken National Park is culturally and ecologically significant as it is located near the center of the Coral Triangle, providing habitat to 390 species of coral and many marine species. It is representative of Indonesian tropical water ecosystems and is a key area for marine biodiversity.
world knowledge.Details: The park is known for its rich coral ecosystem, including a 25–50 metre vertical coral wall. It is home to about 2000 species of fish, marine mammals, reptiles, birds, mollusks, and mangrove species. The area is densely populated with 22 villages inside the park comprising about 35,000 people. Tourism is strongly developed, with activities like scuba diving and snorkeling being popular. The park has faced threats such as coral mining, anchor damage, blast fishing, and trash, but conservation efforts have been made to reduce these impacts.

world knowledge.Name: Hengqin International Finance Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hengqin International Finance Center is a mixed-use skyscraper completed in 2020, symbolizing the Chinese legend of flood dragons coming from the sea, representing the region's strength and power. It was designed to bring together skills from Zhuhai, Macau, Hong Kong, and Shenzhen.

Major_Events.Description: Received the Asia Pacific Property Awards in 2014.
Received the AAP Architecture Prize in 2017.
Received the MUSE Design Awards in 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower features a swirling design representing flood dragons, with glass and metal panels covering the elevations. It has a reinforced concrete structural system and includes 69 floors (+4 underground). The four components of the tower rise from the podium's side, symbolizing the collaboration of Zhuhai, Macau, Hong Kong, and Shenzhen.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower symbolizes the strength and power of the region through its design inspired by the Chinese legend of flood dragons. It represents the coming together of skills from Zhuhai, Macau, Hong Kong, and Shenzhen.
world knowledge.Details: The development includes class A office space, conference and exhibition facilities, commercial apartments, and retail spaces. Traditional and commercial areas are situated in the lower level for convenient entry, offices are located halfway up the tower, and apartments are at the top.

world knowledge.Name: Carroll County Courthouse, Eastern District
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Carroll County Courthouse was built in 1881 shortly after Berryville replaced Carrollton as the county seat, and before Eureka Springs was chosen as the county's western seat. It has been repeatedly enlarged and now houses the Heritage Center Museum of the Carroll County Historical Society.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its historical significance and added to the National Register of Historic Places.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as part of Berryville Commercial Historic District
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse became part of the Berryville Commercial Historic District, further recognizing its cultural and historical importance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Three-story brick structure with a truncated hip roof, and a pair of four-story towers at its front corners, which are topped by pyramidal roofs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a historic landmark representing the judicial and administrative history of Carroll County. It now serves as a museum, preserving local heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a courthouse; now functions as the Heritage Center Museum.
world knowledge.Details: The building was designed by architect J.P. Fancher. NRHP reference number: 76000392.

world knowledge.Name: Pocitos
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pocitos is an upscale seaside barrio of Montevideo, Uruguay. It emerged as a seaside resort in the 19th century and was formally inaugurated in 1886 under the name of Nuestra Señora de los Pocitos. The name originates from the habit of washerwomen who made wells (Spanish: Pozos) in the clean sand to wash their clothes. Initially an independent town, it was absorbed by Montevideo's urban expansion. In 1906, a tram line connected it to the Customs House in Ciudad Vieja, increasing its popularity. The area became a residential hub in the 1920s and 1930s, with significant real estate development by the 1950s.

Major_Events.Description: A tram line was inaugurated, connecting Pocitos to the Customs House in Ciudad Vieja, making the area more accessible.
A multipurpose stadium in Pocitos hosted matches of the first FIFA World Cup, including the first goal in World Cup history.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The neighborhood features high-rise apartment buildings, old neoclassical and eclectic mansions, and architecturally notable buildings combining styles like eclecticism and neoclassical. Notable structures include the Gran Hotel Pocitos, Casa de Felipe Yriart, Williman House, and Public School No. 17.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pocitos is culturally significant as one of Montevideo's most famous beaches and an affluent residential area. It played a role in Uruguay's history, hosting the first FIFA World Cup and housing notable historic buildings declared National Historic Monuments.
world knowledge.Details: Pocitos Beach is located on the coast of the Río de la Plata, known for its high salinity and waves. It is popular for sports and features the Arenas del Plata Stadium, a venue for beach sports. The Pocitos Rambla is 2 kilometers long, with yacht clubs and restaurants. The neighborhood is connected to the central business district by Spain Boulevard and Brazil Avenue, where many embassies are located in historic mansions.

world knowledge.Name: Nagasaki Prefectural Art Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum opened in 2005, replacing the former Nagasaki Prefectural Museum and Art Museum which closed in 2002. It houses artworks related to Nagasaki and Spanish art collected by Suma Yakichiro, a special envoy to Spain during World War II.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Nagasaki Prefectural Art Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened to the public, replacing the former Nagasaki Prefectural Museum and Art Museum.

Major_Events.Event: Closure of Nagasaki Prefectural Museum and Art Museum
Major_Events.Description: The former museum closed to make way for the new Nagasaki Prefectural Art Museum and Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Kengo Kuma.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its collection of artworks related to Nagasaki and Spanish art, reflecting the historical connections between Japan and Spain.
world knowledge.Details: The collection includes works of Spanish art collected by Suma Yakichiro, special envoy to Spain during the Second World War. Alongside the Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture, it supersedes the former Nagasaki Prefectural Museum and Art Museum.

world knowledge.Name: Federal University of Espírito Santo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Federal University of Espírito Santo (Ufes) is the largest and most important university in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil. Founded in 1954, it integrates teaching, research, and outreach programs in all fields of knowledge. It comprises four campuses and 27 online learning centers throughout the state.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded, integrating teaching, research, and outreach programs.
The university expanded to include campuses in Vitória, Alegre, and São Mateus.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university covers over 300,000 m² of floor space across its campuses, with facilities including theaters, art galleries, libraries, museums, and a planetarium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ufes is a public university offering free, high-quality education and is a leader in research and outreach in Espírito Santo. It is ranked among the top universities in Brazil and Latin America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education, research, and community outreach
world knowledge.Details: Ufes has almost 25,000 students in over 100 undergraduate courses and 64 graduate programs. It publishes nearly 1,000 research papers annually and has over 500 ongoing outreach projects. The university also provides facilities like a veterinary hospital, a university hospital, and a marine station.

world knowledge.Name: Carrasco International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Ciudad de la Costa, Canelones, Uruguay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Carrasco/General Cesáreo L. Berisso International Airport is the main international airport of Uruguay. It was inaugurated in 1947 and is named after Cesáreo L. Berisso, a pioneer of Uruguayan aviation. The airport has undergone several upgrades, including the construction of a new terminal in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: The original passenger terminal was inaugurated.
Construction began on a new terminal parallel to Runway 06/24.
The new terminal, designed by Uruguayan architect Rafael Viñoly, was inaugurated.
Regular passenger flights were suspended due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new terminal, designed by Rafael Viñoly, has four jetways, separate floors for arrivals and departures, and a large viewing area on the top floor. It can handle up to 3 million passengers a year with room for expansion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a significant hub for international travel in Uruguay and has been cited as one of the most efficient and traveler-friendly airports in Latin America. It also hosts an air base of the Uruguayan Air Force and an aeronautical museum.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as the main operational hub of cargo and charter passenger airline Air Class Líneas Aéreas. It is located 19 km from downtown Montevideo and is served by public transit and a private taxi service. The airport also houses the Oficina de Investigación y Prevención de Accidentes e Incidentes de Aviación (OIPAIA) and the General Cesareo Berisso Air Force Base.

world knowledge.Name: East Bengal Ground
world knowledge.Address: Maidan area, near Fort William and Eden Gardens, Kolkata
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 100 metres by 60 metres (109.4 yd x 65.6 yd)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The East Bengal Ground, initially known as National AC Ground, became the home stadium of East Bengal and Aryan. East Bengal Club was formed in 1920 and started playing at Kumortuli Park Ground before moving to Calcutta FC Ground. In 1924, East Bengal shared the ground with Mohun Bagan until 1963 when Mohun Bagan moved out. Aryan F.C. started sharing the ground thereafter. The ground has undergone several renovations, including in 1996, 2016, and 2018 when floodlights were installed.

Major_Events.Description: The new Club Office or "Tent" was inaugurated by the oldest member of the East Bengal Club, Mr. Shankar Pillai, in the presence of club legends like Ahmed Khan and Byomkesh Bose.

Floodlights were installed at the East Bengal Ground, making them the biggest among the three Maidan clubs of Kolkata. The first match under floodlights was played in the 2018–19 Calcutta Premier Division.

Major_Events.Event: Practice ground for Argentina football team
Major_Events.Description: The ground served as the practice ground for the Argentina football team during the 1984 Nehru Cup.
The ground hosted a number of matches for the 2019 Durand Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has galleries on three sides. The west side is the member's gallery with modern facilities like bucket seats and elevators. The east and north side galleries are made of temporary wooden and steel structures. The playing pitch is 100m x 60m. The club tent and main office are located adjacent to the stadium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The East Bengal Ground is culturally significant as the home stadium of East Bengal Club, one of the most popular football clubs in India. It has been a venue for numerous important football matches, including the Calcutta Football League and IFA Shield. The ground also played a role in the historic rivalry between East Bengal and Mohun Bagan.
world knowledge.Details: The ground has a capacity of 23,500 people. It is owned by the Eastern Command (India) and operated by the Indian Football Association. The surface is grass, and it features a manual scoreboard. In 2023, a luxurious VVIP lounge named after Krishanu Dey was built at the ground.

world knowledge.Name: Coventry Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral Church of Saint Michael, commonly known as Coventry Cathedral, is the seat of the Bishop of Coventry and the Diocese of Coventry within the Church of England. The city has had three cathedrals. The first was St Mary's, a monastic building, from 1102 to 1539, of which only a few ruins remain. The second was St Michael's, a 14th-century Gothic church designated as a cathedral in 1918, which remains a ruined shell after its bombing during the Second World War, apart from its tower and spire, which rise to 284 feet (87 metres). The third, consecrated in 1962, is the new St Michael's Cathedral, built immediately adjacent to the ruins and tower of the former cathedral, which is a symbol of war-time destruction and barbarity, but also of peace and reconciliation.

Major_Events.Description: The second St Michael's Cathedral was bombed almost to destruction during the Coventry Blitz by the German Luftwaffe.

The new St Michael's Cathedral was consecrated on 25 May 1962 by Cuthbert Bardsley, Bishop of Coventry, with Benjamin Britten's War Requiem premiered in the new cathedral on 30 May to mark its consecration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new Coventry Cathedral was designed by Basil Spence in a modernist style, built next to the remains of the old one. It features a huge tapestry of Christ by Graham Sutherland, a sculpture of the Mater Dolorosa by John Bridgeman, and stained glass windows by John Piper, Lawrence Lee, Keith New, and Geoffrey Clarke.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Coventry Cathedral is a symbol of peace and reconciliation, particularly following its destruction during the Second World War. It houses the Cross of Nails, a symbol of peace and reconciliation across the world, and is known for its innovative services and strong emphasis on reconciliation.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is also home to a pipe organ by Harrison & Harrison, recognised as one of the finest in the UK. It has a strong emphasis on the Bible and aims to be a centre for good preaching and training for the diocese. The cathedral runs regular mission events and has a strong influence of reconciliation within its theology.

world knowledge.Name: Sala Keoku
world knowledge.Address: Near Nong Khai, Thailand, in immediate proximity of the Thai-Lao border and the Mekong river
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sala Keoku is a park featuring giant fantastic concrete sculptures inspired by Buddhism and Hinduism. It was built by and reflects the vision of Luang Pu Bunleua Sulilat and his followers. The park shares the style of Sulilat's earlier creation, Buddha Park on the Lao side of Mekong, but is marked by even more extravagant fantasy and greater proportions.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features giant concrete sculptures, some reaching 25m, including a monumental depiction of Buddha meditating under the protection of a seven-headed Naga snake. The Sala Keoku pavilion is a three-story concrete building with domes resembling a mosque, housing related artifacts and Sulilat's mummified body. The Wheel of Life is a circular multi-part group of sculptures representing the karmic cycle of birth and death.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sala Keoku is culturally significant for its unique and extravagant representations of Buddhist and Hindu themes, reflecting the vision of Luang Pu Bunleua Sulilat. It serves as a spiritual and artistic landmark in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Park with religious and artistic sculptures
world knowledge.Details: The park is located near the Thai-Lao border and the Mekong river. It includes a three-story pavilion constructed following Sulilat's plans after his death, and the Wheel of Life, an enigmatic installation representing the karmic cycle of birth and death.

world knowledge.Name: Fargodome
world knowledge.Address: 1800 University Dr N, Fargo, North Dakota, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fargodome is an indoor athletic stadium and convention center located on the campus of North Dakota State University (NDSU) in Fargo, North Dakota. It opened in 1992 and is owned and operated by the city despite being built on the university's campus. The facility is not an actual dome, its seating capacity is 18,700 for football and over 25,000 for full arena concerts. Its approximate elevation at street level is 900 feet (275 m) above sea level.

Major_Events.Description: Fargodome opened on December 2, 1992.
The USA Wrestling 16U/Junior National Wrestling Championships (Women’s and Men’s Freestyle, Men’s Greco-Roman) takes place every year in the Fargodome in the month of July.

The stadium video boards were replaced with 12 new interior displays featuring SMD LED technology including two large 30'x100' High Definition video/scoreboards on each endzone, 12'x24' screens behind those large screens for those seated behind the board, and four large 20'x22' High Definition video boards (one in each corner).

The stadium replaced its aging AstroTurf with a newer version. It cost the Fargodome $1.1 million, which it paid for using the stadium reserve funds, that also included upgrades to the Magic Carpet system that rolls out the turf onto the stadium floor.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was originally planned to be modeled on the Tacoma Dome but have an inflatable roof. However, as the design evolved, it was decided to have a fixed hard roof, although the dome name stuck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fargodome is the home field of the Bison football team, which competes in the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) at the Division I level in the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS). The stadium also hosts the university's commencement ceremonies as well as many large concerts, other sporting events, and trade shows.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Indoor athletic stadium and convention center
world knowledge.Details: The Fargodome is currently studying an expansion of its permanent seating. The current capacity is 18,700 with an additional 100 seats to be added during the winter 2015. The addition of 5,000 to 7,500 seats has been discussed since 2011, but is now being seriously considered after several straight years of sold out NDSU Bison football games. That would bring the total capacity for football games to around 25,000. The additional seating would require major structural changes to the dome, including moving the press boxes from the east side to the west side. The west side has been reinforced and could handle extra levels, whereas the east side has a lobby that was not designed to bear any extra load.

world knowledge.Name: Palazzo del Te
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Palazzo del Te, or simply Palazzo Te, is a palace in the suburbs of Mantua, Italy. It is an example of the mannerist style of architecture, and the acknowledged masterpiece of Giulio Romano. Constructed for Federico II Gonzaga, Marquess of Mantua, as a palace of leisure, the site was originally the family stables built in 1502. The palace was designed by Giulio Romano, a pupil of Raphael, and features extensive frescoes and decorative elements. It was sacked in 1630 during the War of the Mantuan Succession and later restored. Today, part of the palace houses the Museo Civico del Palazzo Te.

Major_Events.Description: During this war, Mantua and the palace were sacked over three days by an Imperial army of 36,000 Landsknecht mercenaries. The palace was looted and remained an empty shell for some time.
Emperor Charles V visited the palace and elevated Federico II of Gonzaga from Marquess to Duke of Mantua.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is an example of Mannerist architecture, designed by Giulio Romano. It features a square house with a cloistered courtyard, formal gardens, and colonnaded outbuildings. The four exterior façades have flat pilasters against rusticated walls, with irregular spans between columns. The interior is decorated with extensive frescoes, including the Sala di Psiche, Sala dei Cavalli, and Sala dei Giganti.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Palazzo del Te is culturally significant as a masterpiece of Mannerist architecture and for its historical role as a palace of leisure for the Gonzaga family. It also houses the Museo Civico del Palazzo Te, which contains a collection of Mesopotamian art.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Palace of leisure, now partially a museum
world knowledge.Details: Part of the Palazzo today houses the Museo Civico del Palazzo Te (Civic Museum of Palazzo del Te), endowed by the publisher Arnoldo Mondadori. It contains a collection of Mesopotamian art.

world knowledge.Name: Runcorn Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as Halton Grange, a mansion for Thomas Johnson, a local industrialist. It was later purchased by Runcorn Urban District Council in the 1930s and converted into their offices. Since 1974, it has been the meeting place for Halton Borough Council.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Runcorn Urban District Council
Major_Events.Description: The house and the remainder of the grounds were purchased by Runcorn Urban District Council for £2,250 and converted into their offices.
The Duke of Gloucester visited the town hall as part of celebrations for the 1,100th anniversary of the town.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Italianate villa style, rendered exterior, slate roof, two storeys with a belvedere rising to four storeys. Features include a Tuscan portico, triple round-headed windows, rusticated quoins, and a geometrical staircase with cast iron balusters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grade II listed building, significant for its historical and architectural value. It houses important artworks and has been a central administrative building for over a century.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Meeting place for Halton Borough Council and civic offices.
world knowledge.Details: The building includes a mayor's parlour, members' room, committee rooms, reception rooms, and a kitchen. The entrance hall has a mosaic floor, possibly by Minton, and the staircase features stained glass depicting Runcorn's coat of arms. The building also houses two large paintings by Andrea Casali.

world knowledge.Name: Pergamon Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pergamon Museum was built by order of Emperor Wilhelm II according to plans by Alfred Messel and Ludwig Hoffmann in Stripped Classicism style. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999 due to its architecture and its testimony to the evolution of museums as architectural and social phenomena. The museum was severely damaged during World War II, and many of its artifacts were taken by the Red Army, with some still remaining in Russia. The museum underwent renovations starting in 2014 and was completely closed in 2023, with a partial reopening expected in 2027.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was built according to plans by Alfred Messel and Ludwig Hoffmann.
The museum was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List due to its architecture and cultural significance.
The museum was severely damaged during air attacks on Berlin, and many artifacts were taken by the Red Army.
The museum was reopened in East Berlin after the war.
The museum was completely closed for renovation, with a partial reopening expected in 2027.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in the Stripped Classicism style, the museum features a large three-wing building designed by Alfred Messel and Ludwig Hoffmann.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pergamon Museum is culturally significant due to its extensive collection of ancient artifacts, including the Pergamon Altar and the Ishtar Gate, and its role in the evolution of museum architecture. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses the Antikensammlung, Vorderasiatisches Museum, and Museum für Islamische Kunst. It is part of the Museum Island complex and is undergoing extensive renovations, with a partial reopening expected in 2027.

world knowledge.Name: Pitzhanger Manor
world knowledge.Address: Mattock Lane, Ealing, London, W5 5EQ, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pitzhanger Manor is an English country house famous as the home of neoclassical architect Sir John Soane. Built between 1800 and 1804 in what is now Walpole Park, Ealing, it was intended as a domestic space to entertain guests and a family home for a dynasty of architects. The house has undergone several restorations, including a major conservation project from 2015 to 2019 to restore it to Soane’s original designs.

Major_Events.Description: Soane purchased the estate for £4,500 and redesigned the house, retaining parts of the original structure.
Pitzhanger Manor and Gallery was opened to the public as a heritage attraction.
A three-year project restored the Grade I listed building to Soane’s original designs and upgraded the contemporary Gallery.
Pitzhanger Manor & Gallery reopened to the public, revealing Soane’s original design for the first time in over 175 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Pitzhanger Manor is highly neoclassical in design, with elements of Italian Renaissance architecture. Features include quartered and canopy dome ceilings, inset mirrors, wooden panelling, meanders, caryatids, ionic columns, and iconographic eagles with laurel wreaths. Soane incorporated Romano-Grecian influences and his own motifs, such as a masterful use of light and shadow.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pitzhanger Manor is culturally significant as a rare example of a building designed, built, and lived in by Sir John Soane. It showcases his architectural vision and houses part of his collection of paintings and classical antiquities. The Manor also serves as a public museum and gallery, hosting contemporary art exhibitions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country villa for entertaining guests and a family home, now a heritage attraction and contemporary art gallery.
world knowledge.Details: Pitzhanger Manor was conceived as a country villa where 200 guests could be entertained. It has been used as a public library, a museum, and a gallery. The site includes a war memorial for the men of Ealing who died in the World Wars. The Manor is also a registered film location and has featured in various productions. The adjacent Pitzhanger Gallery hosts contemporary art exhibitions.

world knowledge.Name: Alaska State Capitol
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alaska State Capitol is the building that hosts the Alaska Legislature and the offices of the Governor of Alaska and Lieutenant Governor of Alaska. Located in the state's capital, Juneau, the building was opened on February 14, 1931, as a federal building. After Alaska gained statehood in 1959, the building became home to the Alaska Legislature and has retained the function ever since. Construction for a capitol building was partly funded by the United States Congress, but they refused to give more funding. Local citizens managed to pay the rest of the cost for land, which was then given to the government.

Major_Events.Description: Construction on the building began on September 18, 1929.
Construction ended on February 2, 1931.
The building was dedicated on February 14, 1931.
The Alaska Statehood Act granted Alaska permission to settle in the building.
The State of Alaska undertook a 4-year, $33 million project to provide seismic upgrades to the building as well as further restore the building to its original appearance.

Major_Events.Event: Statue of William H. Seward erected
Major_Events.Description: A statue of William H. Seward was erected in front of the Capitol to commemorate the 1867 Alaska Purchase.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is six stories high and made from brick-faced reinforced concrete, with a facade of Indiana limestone on the first two floors. The portico has four columns made of Tokeen marble from Prince of Wales Island, which is also used for interior trim. Because it lacks the large landscaped grounds of most state capitols, it could appear to be simply an office building. It is one of only eleven state capitols that do not feature a dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Alaska State Capitol is culturally and historically important as it hosts the Alaska Legislature and the offices of the Governor of Alaska and Lieutenant Governor of Alaska. It represents the political and administrative center of the state and has been a focal point for governance since Alaska gained statehood in 1959.
world knowledge.Details: Outside the building is a replica of the Liberty Bell, of the type given to all states and territories by the federal government in 1950 to help raise support for savings bond drives. The lobby features clay murals titled Harvest of the Land and Harvest of the Sea, representing hunting and fishing, as well as a bust of Alaska Native activist Elizabeth Peratrovich. Offices and committee rooms fill the ground and first floors. The second floor houses the chambers of the Alaska Senate and Alaska House of Representatives, as well as committee rooms. The walls feature the work of early Juneau photographers Lloyd Winter and Percy Pond, and busts of the first two U.S. senators from Alaska, Bob Bartlett and Ernest Gruening. The Alaska Governor and Lieutenant Governor's offices are located on the third floor. The executive office doors are made of black birch, with hand carvings depicting Alaskan industry. The "Hall of Governors" features portraits of governors and lieutenant governors of Alaska from the District of Alaska era to the present. More legislative offices and committee rooms occupy the fourth floor. The fifth floor holds legislative finance committees. Many areas of the building have been restored to their original 1930s appearance, especially on the second and fifth floors—the latter originally had federal courtrooms.

world knowledge.Name: Simien Mountains National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Simien Mountains National Park is the largest national park in Ethiopia, established in 1969 by Clive Nicol. It covers the highest parts of the Simien Mountains, including Ras Dashan, the highest point in Ethiopia. The region has been inhabited and cultivated for at least 2,000 years. The park was inscribed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1978 due to its outstanding biodiversity and spectacular landscape. It was added to the List of World Heritage in Danger in 1996 due to population declines of native species but was removed from the list in 2017 after stabilization of those species.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established by Clive Nicol, who wrote about his experiences in 'From the Roof of Africa'.

Major_Events.Event: Inscribed as a World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The park was inscribed by UNESCO due to its outstanding biodiversity and spectacular landscape.

Major_Events.Event: Added to the List of World Heritage in Danger
Major_Events.Description: Due to serious population declines of some of its characteristic native species, the park was added to the List of World Heritage in Danger.

Major_Events.Event: Removed from the List of World Heritage in Danger
Major_Events.Description: With the stabilization of the populations of native species, the park was removed from the List of World Heritage in Danger.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features spectacular landscapes with serrated mountain peaks, deep valleys, and 1,500-meter-high sheer cliffs formed by volcanic flood basalts from the Paleogene period. The area is rich in perforated basalt and serves as an ideal catchment basin for water conservation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and historically significant due to its unique biodiversity, including endangered species like the Ethiopian wolf and the walia ibex. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its outstanding natural beauty and ecological importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of biodiversity and natural landscapes
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to a number of endangered species, including the Ethiopian wolf, walia ibex, gelada baboon, and caracal. It also hosts over 50 species of birds, such as the bearded vulture. The park is managed under the National Reserve Act, focusing on protecting representative species and working with local residents to reduce pressure on park resources. Environmental education and training programs are essential for maintaining the park's universal values and gaining local cooperation.

world knowledge.Name: Biarritz Aquarium
world knowledge.Address: Esplanade du Rocher de la Vierge, 64200 Biarritz, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Biarritz Aquarium, also known as le Musée de la Mer (Museum of the Sea), is an aquarium in Biarritz. The building, in art deco style, was opened in 1933. It went through the first renovation in 1992 to add an important collection of marine animals. An extension was added between 2009 and 2011 which doubled the visiting area and added more tanks, at the expense of space for birds.

Major_Events.Description: Added an important collection of marine animals.
Doubled the visiting area and added more tanks, at the expense of space for birds.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art deco style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The aquarium serves as a museum of the sea, showcasing marine life and educating the public about oceanic ecosystems.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is laid out across 4 floors. Website: www.museedelamer.com.

world knowledge.Name: Salzburg Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Salzburg Museum was founded in 1834, initially as a collection of military memorabilia from the Napoleonic wars. It became the official town museum of Salzburg after the Revolution of 1848. The museum faced significant destruction during World War II but was rebuilt and relocated several times. It finally reopened in the Neue Residenz in 2005 and received the European Museum of the Year Award in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: A small collection of military memorabilia was made accessible to the public to formalize the memories of the Napoleonic wars.
After the Revolution of 1848, the collection became the official town museum of Salzburg.
The museum was hit by bombs during World War II, leading to significant destruction and loss of objects.
The museum reopened in the Neue Residenz after decades of debate about its location.

Major_Events.Event: European Museum of the Year Award
Major_Events.Description: The museum received the European Museum of the Year Award.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the Neue Residenz, adapted by Kaschl – Mühlfellner, with original construction by Vincenzo Scamozzi.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Salzburg Museum is significant for its role in preserving and showcasing the artistic and cultural history of Salzburg and its region. It has been recognized internationally, receiving the European Museum of the Year Award in 2009.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has several side-branches, including the Domgrabungsmuseum, Spielzeugmuseum (Toy Museum), and Festungsmuseum (Fortress Museum). It is owned by the city and state of Salzburg and the Salzburg Museum Association.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Óscar Quiteño
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Óscar Quiteño is a multi-purpose stadium in Santa Ana, El Salvador. It was inaugurated on February 3, 1963 and built by the Institute of Rural Development. The stadium was named after the goalkeeper Óscar Alberto Quiteño, who died in a friendly match against Orión of Costa Rica in 1964. The stadium is currently used mostly for football matches and is the home stadium of Club Deportivo FAS.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated on February 3, 1963 with a match between C.D. FAS and the Gold of Mexico, which was won by the latter.
The stadium underwent renovations between 2007 and 2010 to improve its facilities.
In June 2014, remodeling work was done to prepare the stadium for the CONCACAF Champions League tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a capacity of 17,500 people, with 4 lighting towers, 10 access doors, and 6 doors to the court. The field is covered with Bermuda New Zealander grass and measures 105 x 70 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after Óscar Alberto Quiteño, a goalkeeper who died during a friendly match in 1964. It is the third largest stadium in El Salvador and holds significant cultural importance as the home stadium of Club Deportivo FAS.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by the Municipal Office of Santa Ana and operated by Club Deportivo FAS. It has a record attendance of 20,000 and features an electronic scoreboard. The stadium has undergone several renovations and is planned for further expansion to increase its capacity to 22,500.

world knowledge.Name: Basilica of St. John
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basilica of St. John is a Minor Basilica of the Catholic Church in the Drake neighborhood of Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It is also a parish church in the Diocese of Des Moines. The church building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Bishop Henry Cosgrove of the Diocese of Davenport established St. John's Parish in 1905. Its territory had been taken from St. Ambrose Parish. The school was the first building built by the parish. A chapel on the second floor served the parish as its church. The first Mass was celebrated on Christmas Day in 1905. The parish became a part of the newly established Diocese of Des Moines in 1911. The cornerstone for the present church was laid on September 19, 1926. The finished church was dedicated by Bishop Thomas W. Drumm on December 4, 1927. The church was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 8, 1987. Pope John Paul II elevated St. John's Church to a Minor Basilica on October 4, 1989.

Major_Events.Description: Bishop Henry Cosgrove of the Diocese of Davenport established St. John's Parish.
The basement of the present church was completed and used by the parish until the upper church was completed.
The cornerstone for the present church was laid on September 19, 1926.
The finished church was dedicated by Bishop Thomas W. Drumm on December 4, 1927.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of the baldachin and high altar
Major_Events.Description: The baldachin and high altar, designed by Maginnis & Walsh, were added.
The stained glass windows were installed between 1947 and 1953.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The church was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 8, 1987.
Pope John Paul II elevated St. John's Church to a Minor Basilica on October 4, 1989.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Basilica of St. John is designed in the Romanesque Revival style, specifically the Lombardy Romanesque style found in Northern Italy. The church is built of Indiana limestone with a random ashlar pattern on the exterior. The building measures 138 by 80 feet (42 by 24 m) and features a 115-foot (35 m) campanile on the west rear. The interior is finished in plaster cast and travertine marble with a barrel-vaulted coffered ceiling covered in gold leaf. The church has a seating capacity of 900 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Basilica of St. John is culturally and historically significant as a Minor Basilica of the Catholic Church and a parish church in the Diocese of Des Moines. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is an example of Romanesque Revival architecture. The church has played a central role in the Catholic community of Des Moines since its establishment in 1905.
world knowledge.Details: The Basilica of St. John features a 1963 Casavant Frères Ltée. pipe organ with 1,998 pipes. The church has suffered water damage from fires in 1961 and 1970 but was not seriously damaged. The parish has been active in community service, including the creation of the Churches United Shelter in 1992 to combat homelessness in the Des Moines area.

world knowledge.Name: Sea of Galilee
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sea of Galilee, also known as Lake Tiberias, is a freshwater lake in Israel. It is the lowest freshwater lake on Earth and the second-lowest lake in the world. The lake has been called by different names throughout its history, usually depending on the dominant settlement on its shores. It is situated in northeast Israel, between the Golan Heights and the Galilee region, in the Jordan Rift Valley, formed by the separation of the African and Arabian plates. The lake has significant historical and religious importance, particularly in Christianity, as it is associated with many events in the life of Jesus.

Major_Events.Description: Bar Kokhba's revolt was put down, leading to the banning of Jews from Jerusalem and the shift of Jewish culture and learning to the Galilee region.
Sultan Saladin defeated the armies of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, cutting them off from the fresh water of the Sea of Galilee.

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of the Ancient Galilee Boat
Major_Events.Description: An ancient fishing boat from the 1st century AD, known as the Jesus Boat, was discovered on the northwest shore during a drought.
Israel captured the Golan Heights, which contain some of the sources of water for the Sea of Galilee.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lake is characterized by its natural formation, with an asymmetrical bottom—steeper in the east and gentler in the west. The area is rich in basalt and other igneous rocks due to past volcanic activity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sea of Galilee is culturally and historically significant due to its association with many events in the life of Jesus, as described in the New Testament. It is also a key site for Jewish history and culture, particularly during the Roman period and the compilation of the Jerusalem Talmud.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Freshwater lake, tourism, fishing, and water supply.
world knowledge.Details: The Sea of Galilee is fed by the Upper Jordan River and local runoff, with its outflow controlled by the Degania Dam. It is a major source of water for Israel, supplying approximately 10% of the country's drinking water needs. The lake supports a significant commercial fishery and is an important site for tourism, particularly for Christian pilgrims. The lake's water level is monitored and regulated, and it has faced ecological stress due to over-extraction of water and droughts.

world knowledge.Name: Cauchie House
world knowledge.Address: Rue des Francs / Frankenstraat 5, 1040 Etterbeek, Brussels-Capital Region, Belgium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cauchie House is a historic town house in Brussels, Belgium, designed by the architect, painter, and designer Paul Cauchie. Built in 1905 in Art Nouveau style, it is notable for its allegorical sgraffito decoration. Paul Cauchie and his wife Caroline Voet designed and decorated the house, which was intended to showcase their work and serve as a home-workshop.

Major_Events.Event: Proposal for Adventures of Tintin museum
Major_Events.Description: In 1979, there was a proposal to turn the Cauchie House into an Adventures of Tintin museum, with the cooperation of Hergé, the creator of Tintin. Hergé officially agreed to the project on Christmas Day, 1980, but the project did not come to fruition.

The basement was converted into a gallery exhibiting photos, paintings, and archive documents related to the house's restoration and the artistic activities of Paul and Lina Cauchie. The ground floor was restored to its original appearance, and the upper floors were converted into apartments.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Nouveau style with allegorical sgraffito decoration. The house is a unified work of art (Gesamtkunstwerk), blending architecture, painting, sculpture, and decorative arts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cauchie House is culturally significant as a prime example of Art Nouveau architecture and the Gesamtkunstwerk concept. It showcases the artistic collaboration between Paul Cauchie and his wife Caroline Voet, and it played a role in the preservation of Art Nouveau buildings in Brussels.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a home-workshop to showcase the work of Paul Cauchie and Caroline Voet; now a historic house with a gallery and apartments.
world knowledge.Details: The house features the phrase 'Par Nous — Pour Nous' (By Us — For Us) on its façade, emphasizing its personal and artistic significance. The basement houses a gallery with photos, paintings, and archive documents related to the house's history and restoration.

world knowledge.Name: Songdo Convensia
world knowledge.Area: Songdo International City, Incheon Free Economic Zone
world knowledge.Address: Songdo IBD Songdo International City, Incheon Free Economic Zone, Incheon, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Songdo Convensia Convention Center is the first project completed in Songdo IBD and opened for business on October 7, 2008. It was donated to the City of Incheon by Gale International and POSCO E&C and is managed by Incheon Tourism Organization.

Major_Events.Description: Songdo Convensia was used as the main filming location in episode 81 of the South Korean variety show Running Man.
Songdo Convensia was used as the main filming location in episodes 12 to 15 of the South Korean survival show Loud filmed live from August 21 to September 11, 2021.
Songdo Convensia was used as the location of the media center and International Broadcast Center for the 2014 Asian Games.
Songdo Convensia is the chosen venue for the biannual 2023 Rubik's Cube World Championships, organized by Korea Cube Culture United, Rubik's, and the World Cube Association.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and BAUM, the innovative design elicits thoughts of the Sydney Opera House. The main exhibition hall has one of the largest column-free spans (472.4 ft) in Asia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Songdo Convensia is a landmark structure in Korea, hosting international conferences, trade shows, and meetings. It has also become a popular filming location for commercials and music videos.
world knowledge.Details: Facilities available at Songdo Convensia include two main exhibition halls, 23 conference rooms, and 3 ballrooms. It features wireless internet capabilities, RFID card systems, voice recognition cameras, and interpretation in 8 languages. Recently, it received LEED New Construction 2.2 Certified rating, becoming the first convention facility to be LEED certified in Asia.

world knowledge.Name: Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport, previously known as Beirut International Airport, is the only operational commercial airport in Lebanon. It opened on 23 April 1954, replacing the smaller Bir Hassan Airfield. The airport was named after former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri in 2005 following his assassination. It has undergone significant reconstruction and expansion, especially after the Lebanese Civil War, and remains a key hub for Middle East Airlines.

Major_Events.Description: Israeli commandos destroyed 14 civilian aircraft, causing serious devastation to the Lebanese aviation industry.
241 American servicemen were killed in a bombing at the airport.
The airport sustained significant damage from missile strikes by the Israeli Air Force, rendering runways inoperative.
The airport sustained moderate damage to terminal buildings from a massive explosion in Beirut.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern terminal with two wings (East and West) connected by a main terminal, forming a U-shaped building. It has 23 gates, 19 with jetways, and advanced lighting and instrument landing systems on its concrete runways.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is Lebanon's main port of entry and a symbol of the country's resilience through decades of conflict. It is named after Rafic Hariri, a key figure in Lebanon's modern history.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is managed by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and serves as the hub for Middle East Airlines. It has undergone multiple expansions and renovations, including the construction of a new terminal in 1998 and 2002. The airport handles millions of passengers annually and is expected to expand further with a second terminal by 2035.

world knowledge.Name: Old Vicksburg Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Spans Mississippi River on Old US 80, Vicksburg, Mississippi and Delta, Louisiana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Old Vicksburg Bridge, also known as Mississippi River Bridge, is a cantilever bridge carrying one rail line across the Mississippi River between Delta, Louisiana and Vicksburg, Mississippi. It was built by the Vicksburg Bridge & Terminal Co. during 1928-1930 and has three cantilevered truss spans and three Parker truss spans. Until 1998, the bridge was open to motor vehicles and carried U.S. Route 80 (US 80) across the Mississippi River. It is now only a railroad bridge, though one road lane runs through the bridge for inspection by workers. It was replaced by the new Vicksburg Bridge, a short distance down river, for vehicle crossings.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cantilever bridge with three cantilevered truss spans and three Parker truss spans.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is historically significant as part of the Historic Bridges of Mississippi and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railroad bridge with a service lane for inspections.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was originally open to motor vehicles and carried U.S. Route 80 (US 80) across the Mississippi River until 1998. It now serves as a railroad bridge with a service lane for inspections. During its operational period for vehicles, a unique system was used to accommodate tractor-trailer traffic, involving railroad-style signal towers at each end of the bridge to manage crossings safely.

world knowledge.Name: Berjaya Times Square Theme Park
world knowledge.Address: 5th to 8th floors of Berjaya Times Square, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Berjaya Times Square Theme Park, formerly known as Cosmo's World, is an indoor amusement park located in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It was conceived as the largest indoor, all-weather, all-ages entertainment destination in the region and is the second largest indoor amusement park in Malaysia.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The amusement park is divided into two themed areas: Galaxy Station and Fantasy Garden. It features 12 rides, including one roller coaster, and various amenities such as shopping, food and beverages, Kidz Theatre, Entertainment Stages, Kidz Playground, and Cosmo's Party World.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theme park is a significant entertainment destination in Malaysia, offering a unique indoor experience for visitors of all ages.
world knowledge.Details: The amusement park is located on the 5th to 8th floors of Berjaya Times Square and is designed to be an all-weather, all-ages entertainment destination. It features 12 rides and is divided into two themed areas: Galaxy Station and Fantasy Garden.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Islas Malvinas
world knowledge.Address: Av. Álvarez Jonte 4180 Buenos Aires Argentina
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Islas Malvinas is a football stadium owned and operated by Club Atlético All Boys. It opened in 1963 after the club moved from their previous location on Segurola street due to the sale of the land. The stadium was named 'Islas Malvinas' in 1982 after the Falklands War. It has undergone several renovations, including the addition of a second tier and new lighting systems.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was officially inaugurated on September 28, 1963, before a match vs Deportivo Riestra in the Primera C championship.
The stadium was renamed 'Islas Malvinas' after the Falklands War, with a plaque unveiled before a match vs Defensores de Belgrano.
The stadium underwent a major renovation, including the renovation of the press box, new luxury suites, and the restructuring of the second tier.
President of Venezuela Nicolás Maduro gave a speech at the stadium as part of a political event organized by Kirchnerist groups.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium initially had two grandstands, one made of wood and another of concrete. Over the years, it has been expanded with additional stands, including a second tier on the Mercedes street side and a new cement stand replacing the wooden one. The stadium also features a lighting system and luxury suites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium's name reflects Argentina's claims of sovereignty over the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas). It has also hosted numerous concerts and political events, making it a significant cultural and political venue in Buenos Aires.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has hosted various concerts since 1984, featuring both local and international artists. It has a capacity of 21,500 spectators and is a key venue for Club Atlético All Boys.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Tourville Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cape Tourville Lighthouse is an unmanned, automatic lighthouse built in 1971 by private contractors (Hurburgh and Olbrich). It was constructed to provide better guidance for bulk carriers carrying wood chips from the Triabunna wood chip mill, replacing the nearby Cape Forestier Lighthouse on Lemon Rock.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was built to replace the Cape Forestier Lighthouse, with minimal disruption to the surrounding National Park. The top of the granite headland was levelled by blasting to provide the base for the lighthouse and parking area.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse features a cylindrical concrete tower with a balcony and lantern, standing 11 feet (3.4 m) tall. It is painted white and has a focal height of 126 feet (38 m). The light has an intensity of 160,000 cd and a range of 28 nautical miles (52 km; 32 mi), with a characteristic flash pattern of Fl (3) W 10s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse serves as an important navigational aid for maritime traffic, particularly for wood chip carriers operating near the Freycinet Peninsula. It represents advancements in automated lighthouse technology and minimal environmental disruption during construction.
world knowledge.Details: Operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority, the lighthouse was built alongside the new lighthouse at Point Home near Triabunna. The road and powerline were constructed through virgin eucalypt forest with minimal disruption to the National Park.

world knowledge.Name: Kütahya Dumlupınar University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kütahya Dumlupınar University was established on 11 July 1992 as a public university. It originated from the Faculty of Kütahya Economics and Administrative Sciences, which was established on 12 October 1974. The university has established close ties with international institutions and is a member of the European University Association.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded with the governmental decree numbered 3837, which also established four faculties and two institutes.
Faculties of Arts and Sciences, Education, Fine Arts, and Physical Education were transformed into faculties.
Bilecik University was founded, and Kütahya Dumlupınar University was divided into one faculty and four vocational schools.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus houses various faculties, institutes, libraries, health centers, and sports facilities. The Germiyan campus includes vocational schools and sports facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is a significant educational institution in Turkey, fostering international collaborations and contributing to the academic and cultural development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers a wide range of academic programs and research opportunities. It has extensive library resources, computing services, and research laboratories. The university also provides dormitory facilities for students.

world knowledge.Name: Zvartnots International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Near Zvartnots, 15 km west of Yerevan, Armenia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zvartnots International Airport was opened in 1961 and has since undergone several renovations and expansions. It became the main international airport of Armenia after the country's independence from the Soviet Union in the 1990s. A new cargo terminal was constructed in 1998, and significant renovations were made in the 2000s, including the opening of a new departures and arrivals terminal in 2011.

Major_Events.Description: Following Armenia's independence, the airport saw increased cargo shipments, leading to the construction of a new cargo terminal in 1998.
A new gate area and arrivals hall opened, and the airport's fire services were improved.
Zvartnots airport was named 'Best Airport In the CIS' during the Emerging Markets Airports Award ceremonies held in Dubai.
Armenia officially expelled Russian border guards who had been stationed at the airport.
Belavia Flight 1834 crashed on takeoff, resulting in injuries but no fatalities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features modern terminal buildings with facilities designed to handle international traffic, including a new departures and arrivals terminal opened in 2011.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zvartnots International Airport is culturally significant as the main international gateway to Armenia, facilitating travel and commerce since its opening in 1961.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Yerevan and Armenia.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a Dufry duty-free shop, Converse Bank business class lounge, HayPost office, pharmacy, dining options, and several ATMs. It also features a new flight information display system, automated and biometric-identification systems, and 150 surveillance cameras. The airport is accessible via the M5 highway and offers various parking and rental car options.

world knowledge.Name: Powerhouse Museum
world knowledge.Area: Greater Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Address: 500 Harris Street, Ultimo, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 30,000 square metres (proposed new venue in Parramatta)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Powerhouse Museum originated from the Technological, Industrial, and Sanitary Museum of New South Wales, established in 1879. It evolved through various names and locations, eventually settling in the converted Ultimo Power Station in 1988. The museum has played a significant role in preserving and showcasing technological and industrial advancements, as well as decorative arts and sciences.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as Technological, Industrial, and Sanitary Museum
Major_Events.Description: Founded to exhibit industrial and design innovations to improve living standards and health.
The museum moved to a converted electric tram power station, marking a new era as the Powerhouse Museum.
Controversial plan to move the museum to Parramatta, later revised to keep the Ultimo site and build an additional venue in Parramatta.
The Ultimo site closed for up to three years for significant upgrades and redevelopment.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Federation-style building, originally a power station, featuring a reticulated steam system to drive steam machines. The design by Lionel Glendenning won the Sir John Sulman Medal for architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Powerhouse Museum is a key cultural institution in Sydney, showcasing over 500,000 objects related to technology, science, and design. It is a popular tourist destination and a significant part of New South Wales' heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum of technology, science, engineering, and design, with exhibitions on transport, communication, space, and environmental challenges.

Details.Collections: Over 500,000 objects including the oldest operational rotative steam engine (Whitbread Engine), Locomotive No. 1, and the Catalina Flying Boat Frigate Bird II.
Details.Exhibitions: Permanent and temporary exhibitions on topics such as space, ecology, computing technology, and popular culture, including Star Wars and Harry Potter.
Details.Facilities: Main centre in Ultimo, with additional locations at Sydney Observatory and Powerhouse Castle Hill. Powerhouse Parramatta is due to open in 2025.
Details.Management: Owned by the New South Wales Government, with CEO Lisa Havilah as of 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Hålogaland Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,533 metres (5,030 ft) total length, 1,145 metres (3,757 ft) longest span
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hålogaland Bridge is a suspension bridge that crosses the Rombaksfjorden in Narvik Municipality, Norway. It was built to shorten driving distances and improve connectivity in the region. Construction began in 2013 and was completed in 2018, with the bridge opening to traffic on 9 December 2018.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began on 18 February 2013.
The bridge was inaugurated and opened to traffic on 9 December 2018.
Narvik Airport, Framnes, was closed on 1 April 2017 as part of the financing plan for the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a suspension bridge made of reinforced concrete and steel. It has a total length of 1,533 metres (5,030 ft) and a longest span of 1,145 metres (3,757 ft). It features two lanes and was designed to withstand Arctic conditions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hålogaland Bridge is the second-longest bridge span in Norway and the longest suspension bridge within the Arctic Circle at the time of its construction. It significantly improves transportation in the region and has been featured in media, including the Science Channel show 'Building Giants.'
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge serves as part of the European Route E6 highway, improving connectivity between Narvik, Bjerkvik, and Bjørnfjell.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge cost 2.2 billion kr and was financed through state grants and tolls. It replaced the Rombak Bridge for the E6 highway reroute. The project also included 4.9 kilometres of new road, two smaller tunnels, and an avalanche protection tunnel. The bridge was constructed by the Chinese company Sichuan Road and Bridge Group.

world knowledge.Name: Fajara
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Prior to the arrival of the first tourists in the 1960s, the inhabitants' living revolved largely around fishing. Fajara is becoming an increasingly popular tourist destination with around 20 hotel complexes on the beach and many more inland.

Major_Events.Event: Arrival of pioneering Swedish tourist Bertil Harding
Major_Events.Description: Bertil Harding Highway is named after the pioneering Swedish tourist who arrived in 1965.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fajara is home to notable figures such as Isatou Njie-Saidy, a former Vice-President of the Gambia, the former US Ambassador, and was the home town of the late Sir Dawda Kairaba Jawara, a former Prime Minister of the Gambia and the first President of the Gambia.
