world knowledge.Details: The Medical Research Council is located within a fenced complex on Atlantic Boulevard. There is also a large military camp. Bertil Harding Highway is one of the town's main thoroughfares.

world knowledge.Name: University of Pécs
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Pécs is one of the largest higher education institutions in Hungary, with a history dating back to 1367 when it was founded by King Louis I the Great. It is the first university in Hungary and the fourth in Central Europe. The modern university was established in 1912 and moved to Pécs in 1921. It merged with other institutions in 2000 to form the current University of Pécs.

Major_Events.Description: King Louis I the Great founded the university with the permission of Pope Urban V.
The Royal Hungarian Elizabeth University was founded in Pozsony (Bratislava).
The university was moved to Pécs after Bratislava became part of Czechoslovakia.
The university merged with the Janus Pannonius University and the Medical University of Pécs to form the current University of Pécs.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Pécs is culturally and historically significant as the first university in Hungary and a major educational institution in Central Europe. It has played a crucial role in the development of higher education in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Pécs has approximately 24,000 students, including over 5,500 international students from more than 110 countries. It offers a wide range of programs in various fields and is known for its English and German language courses. The university has ten faculties and numerous research institutes, contributing significantly to academic and scientific development.

world knowledge.Name: Borgestad Church
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Borgestad Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Skien Municipality in Telemark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Borgestad. The earliest existing historical records of the church date back to the year 1398, but the church was not built that year. The church was probably located on a site about 200 metres to the southwest of the present church site. In the early 1900s, Prime Minister Gunnar Knudsen gave land and financed the construction of a new church in Borgestad. The new building was designed by Henrik Nissen. Construction of the new building began in the winter of 1903–1904 and continued until 1906. The new church was consecrated on 24 May 1907.

Major_Events.Description: The new church was consecrated on 24 May 1907.
In April 2011, there was an arson attempt on a bench outside Borgestad church, the same night that the Østre Porsgrunn Church burned down due to arson.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The white, stone church was built in a long church design in 1907 using plans drawn up by the architect Henrik Nissen. The new limestone long church was inspired by English country churches. It has an asymmetrically placed bell tower, which was popular at the time. The church has an entrance in the south, and in the north is a choir which is surrounded by vestries. The church was decorated with stained glass by Emanuel Vigeland in 1918–1919 and it was painted inside by Ulrik Hendriksen in 1921.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Borgestad Church is a significant religious site in the region, representing the architectural and cultural heritage of the Church of Norway in Telemark county. It was financed by Prime Minister Gunnar Knudsen, adding to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The church seats about 382 people. The building received electric lighting for its fiftieth anniversary in 1957.

world knowledge.Name: Beef Island
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beef Island is an island in the British Virgin Islands, located to the east of Tortola and connected by the Queen Elizabeth Bridge. It is the site of the Terrance B. Lettsome International Airport, the main commercial airport serving the British Virgin Islands. The island has faced environmental controversies over development projects.

Major_Events.Description: A five-star hotel with a golf course and marina was proposed for development near Hans Creek. The project was delayed after challenges from the British Virgin Islands Heritage Conservation Group due to environmental concerns.
The Virgin Islands Environmental Council (VIEC) won a lawsuit against the government, ruling that the development project at Hans Creek was illegal under the Fisheries Regulations.
The Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court of Appeal invalidated the 2009 ruling, stating that Hans Creek had not been correctly made a protected area, thus legalizing the original planning permission.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Beef Island is culturally significant as a key transportation hub for the British Virgin Islands and as a site of environmental activism. The island's development controversies highlight the tension between economic growth and environmental conservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (site of Terrance B. Lettsome International Airport) and tourism (Trellis Bay market, restaurant, and beach).
world knowledge.Details: Trellis Bay, located east of the airport, features a market, restaurant, coffee shop, local craft shops, and a beach. Long Bay is west of the airport. The island has been a focal point for environmental activism, particularly regarding the protection of habitats such as salt ponds, coral reefs, and mangroves.

world knowledge.Name: Barisal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Barisal is one of the oldest municipalities and river ports in Bangladesh. It was part of ancient kingdoms like Vanga, Gangaridai, and Samatata. The region was ruled by various dynasties including Khadga, Pala, Chandra, Sena, and Deva. It was later conquered by Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji and became part of the Delhi Sultanate and Bengal Sultanate. During the Mughal period, it was a semi-independent area due to conflicts between Muslims and Hindu chiefs. The city was known as Bangala in ancient times and later as Chandradvipa, Ismailpur, and Bacola. The British established Barisal municipality in 1876, and it was upgraded to a City Corporation in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: Barisal municipality was established during British rule in India.
Barisal was upgraded to a City Corporation on 25 July 2002.
The Lakhutia zamindar estate was destroyed during the 1950 East Pakistan Riots.
The Lakhutia estate was further destroyed during the 1971 Bangladesh genocide.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Barisal's buildings are diverse and built over a long period, with no particular architectural style. Notable heritage buildings include the Lakhutia zamindar estate with Shiva temples and large ponds, and Durga Sagar, the largest pond in southern Bangladesh with coconut trees and brick walls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Barisal is culturally significant as one of the oldest municipalities and river ports in Bangladesh. It was once called the Venice of the East or the Venice of Bengal. The city has a rich history under various dynasties and sultanates and is a major financial hub. The natural phenomenon 'Barisal guns' is named after the city.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Administrative, financial, and cultural hub of Barisal Division and District.
world knowledge.Details: Barisal is the third largest financial hub in Bangladesh. It has a population of approximately 533,000 (2023 census) and covers an area of 58 km². The city is known for its river port, educational institutions, and sports facilities. Major rivers in the area include the Kirtankhola, Arial Khan, Khoyrabad, Kalijira, and Sandha. The climate is a mix of dry-winter humid subtropical and tropical savanna. The city is home to the Barisal Divisional Stadium and the Fortune Barishal cricket team. Barisal Airport and Barisal River Port are key transport links.

world knowledge.Name: St. James Theatre, Auckland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The St James Theatre was built in 1928 to replace the older Fuller's Opera House, which had burnt down two years prior. It was initially designed for vaudeville acts and later began showing films. The theatre has hosted various live performances and films until its closure in 2007 due to fire damage. Restoration work is scheduled to begin in 2024.

Major_Events.Description: Built to replace the Wellesley Street Fullers' Opera House, which had burnt down in 1926. It cost £80,000 and took 9 months to complete.
The theatre started screening films alongside stage performances.
The facade and vestibule were renovated for Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip's visit to New Zealand.
The theatre was damaged by a blaze and subsequently closed.
The New Zealand government contributed $15 million towards the restoration, matching previous contributions from the Auckland Notable Properties Trust and Auckland Council.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The interior is a mixture of traditional theatre and American cinema design, featuring a Spanish Colonial style with marble steps and statuettes. Influences include Victorian and Edwardian theatres and modern American movie palaces. It has three tiers of seating and originally had a large terrazzo foyer.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The St James Theatre is registered as a category 1 building with Heritage New Zealand, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. It has hosted significant cultural events, including performances by the Bolshoi Ballet Company and the Royal Variety Performance.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre was managed by Norman Hayward from 1935 and later purchased by Kerridge Theatres in 1945. Additional cinemas (Odeon, Westend, and Regent) were added to the building in 1957, 1966, and 1982. The Odeon cinema was the first public space in New Zealand with full air conditioning. Restoration work is scheduled for 2024.

world knowledge.Name: San Telmo Museoa
world knowledge.Address: Zuloaga plaza, 1, 20003 San Sebastián, Basque Country, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: San Telmo Museoa, established on 5 October 1902, is a museum dedicated to Basque society, culture, arts, and history. It originally occupied a small location but moved to its current site, a former Dominican monastery, in 1932. The museum underwent significant renovations and reopened in 2011 with modern facilities, aiming to be a cultural venue that bridges past and future.

Major_Events.Description: The museum moved to the San Telmo monastery, featuring a concert conducted by Manuel de Falla and murals by Josep Maria Sert.
The museum reopened after a two-year renovation, introducing modern facilities and a new conceptual approach as a museum of Basque society and citizenship.

Major_Events.Event: Special Mention in European museum contest
Major_Events.Description: The museum received a Special Mention in the best European museum contest organized by the Museum Forum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original building complex, constructed in the 16th century, features a transitional style between Gothic and Renaissance, known as 'Elizabethan' style. The recent extension includes modern pavilions with a façade made of 3,000 molten aluminum panels mimicking erosion holes on rock, integrating vegetation and natural lighting.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: San Telmo Museoa is the oldest museum in the Basque Country, showcasing the region's rich intellectual and patrimonial legacy. It serves as a cultural hub that addresses contemporary Basque culture and history in a global context.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum of Basque society, culture, arts, and history
world knowledge.Details: The museum's permanent exhibition includes a variety of items ranging from funerary steles to modern objects like bicycles and football jerseys. It also hosts temporary exhibitions on diverse topics, such as Federico Fellini, Pier Paolo Pasolini, and the Basque artistic group Gaur. The museum's renovation project, designed by architects Fuensanta Nieto and Enrique Sobejano, features a modern extension that integrates with the historic site, providing additional space for cultural and commercial uses.

world knowledge.Name: Margam Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Margam Castle is a late Georgian country house built for Christopher Rice Mansel Talbot. Designed by Thomas Hopper, the castle was constructed in a Tudor Revival style over a five-year period, from 1830 to 1835. The site had been occupied for some 4,000 years. A Grade I listed building, the castle is now in the care of Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council. The castle stands within Margam Country Park, the former estate to the house.

Major_Events.Description: A fire caused substantial damage to the castle, leading to a restoration project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is of two-storeys, constructed in finely-cut ashlar from a quarry at nearby Pyle. Entry is through an elaborate porch, and the house is crowned by a prospect tower modelled on that at Melbury. The design is highly asymmetrical with irregular gables, turrets, parapets, bay, lancet and oriel windows, groups of chimney stacks and a great deal of heraldic decoration.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Margam Castle is a Grade I listed building and is considered to have an accumulation of architecture and sculpture unparalleled in Wales. It is a significant example of Tudor Revival architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The castle was designed by Thomas Hopper with Edward Haycock Snr as supervisory architect. It features elements borrowed from Lacock Abbey and Melbury House. The castle has links with photography, including being the location of the earliest known Welsh photograph. It is currently in the care of Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council and is part of Margam Country Park.

world knowledge.Name: South China University of Technology
world knowledge.Address: Wushan Campus (North Campus): 381 Wushan Rd, Tianhe District; University Town Campus (South Campus): 382 Waihuan Dong Rd, HEMC, Panyu District; Guangzhou International Campus (GZIC): 777 Xingye Dadao Xi, Panyu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The South China University of Technology (SCUT) is a public university in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. It is affiliated with the Ministry of Education and co-sponsored with the Guangdong Provincial People's Government. The university is part of Project 211, Project 985, and the Double First-Class Construction.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded in 1952.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SCUT is a key institution in China's higher education system, contributing to technological and scientific advancements. It is part of prestigious national projects like Project 985 and Double First-Class Construction.

Details.Motto: 博学慎思 明辨笃行
Details.Motto_in_English: Study Extensively, Enquire Accurately; Discriminate Clearly, Practise Earnestly
Details.Academic_affiliation: Project 985 Double First-Class Construction Excellence League Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao University Alliance (GHMUA)
Details.Transcriptions: Standard Mandarin Hanyu Pinyin Huánán Lǐgōng Dàxué

world knowledge.Name: Teslim Balogun Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Teslim Balogun Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Surulere, Lagos, Nigeria. It was started in 1984 under the administration of military governor Gbolahan Mudasiru, but construction stalled under military regimes, becoming a white elephant. It was completed in 2007 after 23 years, costing over N1.3 billion. The stadium was named after Nigerian former professional footballer Teslim Balogun.

Major_Events.Event: 18th Mobil Track and Field Athletics Championship
Major_Events.Description: The first sporting event held in the stadium.
The first football game held in the stadium.
Hosted the Nigerian FA Cup final.
Hosted some matches in the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup youth tournament.
Hosted the final of the 2009 Federation Cup.
Main venue of the 18th National Sports festival.
Held at the Olympic Standard swimming pool of the stadium during Nigerian Independence day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was designed by Nigerian Architect Onafowokan Michael Olutusen in 1981 and later completed by Nigerian Architect O.C. Majoroh of Majoroh Partnership in 2007. It utilizes principles of sustainable architecture, incorporating elements of green architecture with a 70:30 ratio of softscape to hardscape. The design follows tropical modernism, considering climate with terraces for airflow and cross ventilation. Between 2023 and 2024, the facade was redesigned in a Modern Contemporary Architectural style using ACM panels and multi-coloured panels. The roof members are suspended on steel trusses to protect viewers from adverse weather.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as a major sports venue in Nigeria, hosting international and local football matches, athletics championships, and national sports festivals. It is named after Teslim Balogun, a Nigerian football legend, and has played a key role in promoting sports in Lagos and Nigeria.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium primarily for football matches and athletics events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 24,325 people and features a FIFA Star Two artificial turf, FIFA Grade seats with backrest, digital scoreboard, state-of-the-art changing rooms, security gadgets with CCTV cameras, and generating sets. It sits adjacent to the Lagos National Stadium and has been used by the Nigeria national rugby league team. It was once occupied by homeless people and area boys before its completion.

world knowledge.Name: Ibirapuera Park
world knowledge.Address: Between Av. República do Líbano, Av. Pedro Alvares Cabral, and Av. IV Centenário
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ibirapuera Park was the first metropolitan park in São Paulo, designed along the lines of other great English landscape gardens built in the 20th century in major cities around the globe, but inspired on modern drafts from the landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx. It was inaugurated on 21 August 1954 for the 400th anniversary of the city of São Paulo with buildings designed by architect João Felipe Pereira and landscape by agronomist Otávio Augusto Teixeira Mendes. In the 90s, its green areas were graded heritage-listed status by the city and the state of São Paulo to avoid further construction and keep its historical gardens and green open spaces preserved. In 2016, the complex of buildings designed by Oscar Niemeyer, alongside Zenon Lotufo, Hélio Uchôa Cavalcanti, and others, in the park were also registered as national landmark by the National Historic and Artistic Heritage Institute.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated on 21 August 1954 for the 400th anniversary of the city of São Paulo.
Green areas were graded heritage-listed status by the city and the state of São Paulo to avoid further construction and keep its historical gardens and green open spaces preserved.

The complex of buildings designed by Oscar Niemeyer, alongside Zenon Lotufo, Hélio Uchôa Cavalcanti, and others, in the park were registered as national landmark by the National Historic and Artistic Heritage Institute.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed along the lines of other great English landscape gardens built in the 20th century in major cities around the globe, but inspired on modern drafts from the landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx. Buildings designed by architect João Felipe Pereira and landscape by agronomist Otávio Augusto Teixeira Mendes. Complex of buildings designed by Oscar Niemeyer, alongside Zenon Lotufo, Hélio Uchôa Cavalcanti, and others.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ibirapuera is one of Latin America's largest urban parks, together with Chapultepec Park in Mexico City and Simón Bolívar Park in Bogota, and its iconic importance to São Paulo is often internationally comparable to that of Central Park in New York City. The park is often cited as one of the most vibrant and photographed parks in the world, as together with its large area for leisure, jogging and walking, it hosts a vivid cultural scene with museums, a music hall, and popular events such as São Paulo Fashion Week, congresses and trade shows. It is claimed to be the most visited urban park in South America, is listed as one of the best parks in the world, and has been described as "a green oasis at the heart of a concrete jungle".
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Urban park for leisure, jogging, walking, and hosting cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The park has been managed for decades by the city of São Paulo, but the local government plans to concession all its parks' management to private hands, starting with Ibirapuera Park. Since 2014, the park also has the support of the Ibirapuera Park Conservancy (Parque Ibirapuera Conservação), a strong community nonprofit that supports park stewardship and conservation actions through a capital improvement plan, engagement projects and volunteer work. Admission to the park has been free since 1954, and it is open from 5am until midnight every day.

world knowledge.Name: El Ferdan Railway Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Longest span: 1,100 feet (340 m), Width: 12.6 m (41 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The El Ferdan Railway Bridge is the longest swing bridge in the world, spanning the Suez Canal. The first bridge was completed in 1918, but was later removed. Subsequent bridges were built and destroyed due to wars and accidents. The current bridge was constructed in 2001 by a consortium led by German Krupp.

Major_Events.Description: Completed for the Sinai Military Railway, later removed after WWI.
Built during WWII, damaged by a steamship and removed in 1947.
Double swing bridge completed, but rail traffic was severed in 1956 due to war.
Replacement bridge completed, destroyed in 1967 during the Six-Day War.
Constructed by Krupp, with a main span of 340 m.
A second swing bridge spanning the new eastern shipping lane started operating.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cantilever Bridge with a swing span, made of steel, 8 spans, longest span of 340 m.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is part of a major drive to develop the areas surrounding the Suez Canal, including other significant projects like the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel and the Suez Canal Bridge. It is a critical infrastructure piece for Egypt's rail network.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway transportation across the Suez Canal.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was not functional for a while due to the 2015 Suez Canal expansion. A second swing bridge was constructed to span the new eastern shipping lane, completing the railway connection. The bridge is part of Egypt's efforts to reconnect the Sinai Peninsula to the national rail network.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Finland
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Exhibition area more than 3,100 m² (33,000 sq ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Finland presents Finnish history from the Stone Age to the present day. The Finnish National Romantic style building, designed by Gesellius, Lindgren, Saarinen, reflects Finland's medieval churches and castles. The museum was built from 1905 to 1910 and opened to the public in 1916. It was named the Finnish National Museum after Finland's independence in 1917. The museum is currently closed due to a renovation and expansion project, with its reopening postponed indefinitely due to budget cuts.

Major_Events.Description: An explosion occurred at the National Museum in the Silver Room, caused by methane leaking into a broom cupboard. Most display cases and 49 pieces out of more than 200 silver objects were damaged, although most of them only mildly. Nobody was hurt. All objects were successfully repaired the same year, and the Silver Room was re-opened to the public in early 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building reflects Finland's medieval churches and castles. The architecture belongs to national romanticism, and the interior mainly to Art Nouveau. The entrance hall ceiling has ceiling frescoes in the national epic Kalevala theme, painted by Akseli Gallén-Kallela.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum presents Finnish history and culture from the Stone Age to the present day. It houses significant collections, including coins, medals, orders, decorations, silver, jewellery, weapons, and artifacts from Finnish prehistory, the Swedish Kingdom Period, the Russian Empire Era, and Finnish folk culture. It also includes the Mesa Verde artifacts from the cliff dwellings of Colorado, donated by Gustaf Nordenskiöld.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's entrance hall ceiling frescoes, painted by Akseli Gallén-Kallela, can be seen without an entrance fee. The museum is part of the Finnish Heritage Agency under the Ministry of Culture and Education. The museum was re-opened in July 2000 after its last thorough renovation. In 2019, it was decided to return a portion of the Mesa Verde artifacts to the representatives of the indigenous people of the United States of America, with some 600 items to be kept and exhibited.

world knowledge.Name: Silesian Museum (Katowice)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Silesian Museum in Katowice was founded in 1929 by the Silesian Sejm during the region's recovery from the Silesian Uprisings. It was one of the largest museums in Poland during the interbellum period. The Nazi Germans moved the collection to Bytom and demolished the building in 1940. The museum was reinstated in 1984 in the former Grand Hotel in Katowice. In 2015, a new main location was opened on the site of the former Katowice coal mine, reusing some historical buildings from the mining complex, with primary exhibition space underground.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded by the Silesian Sejm.
The Nazi Germans moved the collection to Bytom and tore the building down.
The museum was reinstated in the former Grand Hotel in Katowice.
A new main location was opened on the site of the former Katowice coal mine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new museum reuses some of the historical buildings from the mining complex, with primary exhibition space underground.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the history and art of the Silesian region, including works by notable Polish artists.
world knowledge.Details: Permanent exhibitions and attractions include works by Polish artists such as Stanisław Wyspiański, Olga Boznańska, Jan Matejko, and others. Contemporary artists on display include Edward Dwurnik, Tadeusz Kantor, Zdzisław Beksiński, and more.

world knowledge.Name: Pasighat Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pasighat Airport was established in 1962 during the Sino-Indian War. It saw little use after the war until the Indian Air Force signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh to develop the airstrip in 2009. The IAF took over the airstrip in February 2010, and it was upgraded with an Air Traffic Control Tower, an apron for parking aircraft, a perimeter road, and a security wall. The upgraded airstrip was inaugurated in August 2016.

Major_Events.Description: The upgraded airstrip was inaugurated by Kiren Rijiju in August 2016, and a Sukhoi Su-30MKI fighter of the Indian Air Force landed on the airstrip as part of the inaugural function.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features an asphalt runway (16/34) measuring 2,060 m (6,760 ft) in length. It includes an Air Traffic Control Tower, an apron for parking aircraft, a perimeter road, and a security wall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pasighat Airport is significant for its role in regional connectivity and its historical background related to the Sino-Indian War. It serves as a vital transportation hub for Pasighat and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Domestic airport serving Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Details: Pasighat Airport (IATA: IXT, ICAO: VEPG) is located beside the banks of the Brahmaputra River, about 3 km (1.9 mi) away from the town centre. It is operated by the Airports Authority of India and serves as a public airport.

world knowledge.Name: Ivano-Frankivsk International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ivano-Frankivsk International Airport is an international airport located in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, approximately 4.4 km from the town center. It has maintained border and customs operations since 1992 and is located at the site of the former village of Opryshivtsi. The airport is a joint military-civil airfield, with the civilian part guarded by the Chernivtsi Detachment. The military section includes a second concrete runway now used as a parking lot and a large apron still in use by the Ukrainian Air Force, specifically the 114th Tactical Aviation Brigade with Mikoyan MiG-29 fighter jets.

Major_Events.Description: On 24 February 2022, Ukraine closed its airspace to civilian flights due to the Russian invasion. The airport was significantly damaged by a Russian airstrike on 11 March 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a concrete runway (10/28) with a length of 8,226 ft (2,507 m) and a second concrete runway (6,325 ft / 1,928 m) used by the military. The civilian terminal is located northwest of the military apron.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a crucial transportation hub for the Ivano-Frankivsk region, providing access to nearby tourist destinations such as the Bukovel ski area, Vorokhta, and the Carpathian National Nature Park. It also plays a dual role as a military airfield, contributing to national defense.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a traffic capacity of 400 passengers per hour. As of 24 February 2022, all passenger flights have been suspended indefinitely due to the Russian invasion. The airport's website is ifo.aero.

world knowledge.Name: Pier Arts Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pier Arts Centre was established in 1979 to house a collection of fine art donated by Margaret Gardiner. The buildings have a rich history, originally serving as a merchant's house and Hudson's Bay Company offices in the 18th and 19th centuries. The property was later used as a lodging house and hostel before being converted into an art gallery.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Pier Arts Centre
Major_Events.Description: The Pier Arts Centre was established to house Margaret Gardiner's collection of fine art.
The original listed buildings and pier were extended by Reiach & Hall Architects, creating a new building at the harbour's edge.

Major_Events.Event: Art exhibition by Orkney primary schools
Major_Events.Description: Students from primary schools around Orkney, including Stromness Primary School, contributed their artwork to an exhibition at the Pier Arts Centre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original 18th-century building features a finely panelled drawing room and historic merchant's offices. The 2007 extension by Reiach & Hall Architects blends modern architecture with the historic pier structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pier Arts Centre is culturally significant as it houses a collection of British Modernist art and serves as a hub for contemporary art exhibitions and events. It also preserves the history of Orkney's maritime and merchant heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The Pier Arts Centre curates a year-round programme of changing exhibitions and events. The collection includes over 180 works, spanning from 1929 to the present day, with a focus on British Modernism and contemporary international art.

world knowledge.Name: Chicago Cultural Center
world knowledge.Address: 78 E. Washington St., Chicago, IL, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chicago Cultural Center, opened in 1897, is a Chicago Landmark building operated by Chicago's Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events. Originally the main library of the Chicago Public Library, the building was converted in 1978 to an arts and culture center. It is considered one of the most comprehensive arts showcases in the United States.

Major_Events.Description: The building was converted from the main library of the Chicago Public Library to an arts and culture center at the instigation of Commissioner of Cultural Affairs Lois Weisberg.
The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places on July 31, 1972.
The building was designated as a Chicago Landmark on November 15, 1976.
A display of art by Ukrainian artists, organized by the Foundation for International Arts and Education with the National Art Museum of Ukraine.

Major_Events.Event: Richard Hunt: Sixty Years of Sculpture
Major_Events.Description: A major exhibition of sixty sculptures spanning Hunt's career.
Kerry James Marshall was commissioned to produce an inaugural mural for a public arts program, an homage to women who have contributed to the culture of Chicago.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed in a generally neoclassical style, with Italian Renaissance elements. It is capped with two stained-glass domes, set symmetrically atop the two wings. The building has 3-foot-thick masonry walls faced with Bedford Blue Limestone on a granite base. It features a 40 ft diameter Tiffany-designed stained glass dome containing over 60,000 individual pieces of glass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the nation's first free municipal cultural center, the Chicago Cultural Center is one of the city's most popular attractions and is considered one of the most comprehensive arts showcases in the United States. It houses the city's official reception venue and serves as headquarters for the Chicago Children's Choir.
world knowledge.Details: The Chicago Cultural Center underwent an extensive renovation during 2021–2022 to restore the original beauty of the building, including the restoration of the art glass dome and decorative finishes in the Grand Army of the Republic rooms. The center features more than 1,000 programs and exhibitions annually covering a wide range of the performing, visual and literary arts.

world knowledge.Name: Bitexco Financial Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bitexco Financial Tower is a skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. At its completion in 2010, it became the tallest building in Vietnam and kept this status until January 2011, when it was surpassed by Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower. The tower was designed by Carlos Zapata, who drew inspiration for its unique shape from Vietnam's national flower, the Lotus.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was officially inaugurated on 31 October 2010.
The Bitexco Financial Tower was chosen to celebrate high-altitude fireworks and laser display for the 2015 New Year's Eve and the 40th Anniversary of the Reunification Day.
Since 2011, Bitexco Financial Tower has hosted the annual HCMC Skyrun, Vietnam's longest running stair climbing race.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Futuristic architectural style, designed by Carlos Zapata Studio, inspired by Vietnam's national flower, the Lotus. The building features 68 floors above ground and three basements, with a height of 262.5 metres (861 ft). The tower is enveloped by 6,000 sleek glass panels, each individually cut to unique specifications.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bitexco Financial Tower is culturally significant as it represents the rapid economic growth and modernization of Ho Chi Minh City and Vietnam. Its unique design, inspired by the Lotus, symbolizes Vietnam's national identity.
world knowledge.Details: The tower includes Vietnam's first non-rooftop helipad on the 52nd floor, which extends 22 meters out from the main structure. The Saigon Skydeck, located on the 49th floor, offers 360-degree panoramic views of Ho Chi Minh City. The tower operates Otis double-deck elevators, the fastest in Southeast Asia at the time of installation. The building has received several international awards, including the "Excellence in structure engineering awards 2011".

world knowledge.Name: Wharf Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Pier 4/5, 15 Hickson Road, Dawes Point NSW 2000 Sydney Australia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately the size of 1.5 rugby fields
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wharf Theatre is part of the Sydney Theatre Company, located on Pier 4/5 of the former Sydney port facility in Walsh Bay at Dawes Point. The first jetty in the area was constructed in 1829. In 1979, the Sydney Theatre Company proposed restoring the derelict finger wharves at Walsh Bay, leading to the theatre's establishment in 1984. The theatre underwent renovations in 2018 and reopened in 2021.

Major_Events.Description: Work on Pier 4/5 was completed by H.D Walsh.
The Wharf Theatre was officially opened by Premier Neville Wran after redevelopment by architect Vivian Fraser.
The theatre closed for renovations in 2018 and reopened in February 2021 with modernised facilities.
The theatres won the RAIA President's Award for Recycled Buildings in 1985 and the New South Wales Enduring Architecture Award and the National Award for Enduring Architecture in 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre features two performance spaces (Wharf 1 and Wharf 2) with a wooden walkway lined with framed posters. Large windows offer views of Sydney Harbour Bridge and the harbour. The design incorporates the influence of water, reflected in the company's logo and use of blue. The refurbishment retained the industrial character of the wharf.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wharf Theatre is a key venue for Sydney's performing arts scene and is part of the Sydney Theatre Company. It is recognized for its innovative reuse of industrial heritage and has received national architecture awards. It is also mentioned in National Geographic Traveler: Sydney as a notable cultural venue.
world knowledge.Details: The Wharf Theatre contains two theatres: Wharf 1 with 339 seats and Wharf 2 with 205 seats. The Theatre Bar at the End of the Wharf offers views of Luna Park and the North Shore skyline. The restoration cost $3.7 million and took 56 weeks to complete.

world knowledge.Name: Kinnoull Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kinnoull Hill is a historically significant site with connections to William Wallace, who is said to have hidden in a cave here. The hill also features Kinnoull Tower, a folly built in the 18th century by Thomas Hay, 9th Earl of Kinnoull, inspired by castles along the Rhine. The hill has been a notable location for centuries, with mentions by Jane Austen and others.

Major_Events.Description: Kinnoull Hill was awarded Green Flag status for its well-managed green spaces.
Several tragic suicide incidents have occurred at the hill, including the deaths of Daniela Smith and her children in 2002, and Forfar Athletic player Jack Syme in 2015.
Kinnoull Hill Woodland Park came runner up in Scotland's Finest Woods Awards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Kinnoull Tower is a folly built to resemble castles along the Rhine, featuring a modest castle design with a tower overlooking the River Tay. The tower is a Category B listed structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kinnoull Hill is culturally significant for its historical connections to William Wallace, its 18th-century folly (Kinnoull Tower), and its literary mentions by Jane Austen. The hill also holds modern significance as a managed woodland park and a site of tragic events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural landmark and recreational area (Woodland Park)
world knowledge.Details: Kinnoull Hill Woodland Park is managed by Forestry and Land Scotland and Perth & Kinross Council. The park features woodland sculptures by Pete Bowsher, reflecting local wildlife. The hill has also been associated with the discovery of wild roses in 1793. The Kinnoull Campus of De La Salle College in Melbourne, Australia, is named after this hill. A beer called Kinnoull Red, named for the hill, was released by Abernyte Brewery.

world knowledge.Name: Academic Hall
world knowledge.Address: Francis Quadrangle, University of Missouri, Columbia, MO
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Academic Hall was the original main building of the University of Missouri, dedicated in 1843 and destroyed by fire in 1892. It served as both an educational and administrative facility. The building was designed by Stephen Hills, who also designed the first Missouri State Capitol. The surviving Ionic columns, known as The Columns, are now a symbol of the university.

Major_Events.Description: During the American Civil War, Academic Hall was used to house Union soldiers and intern Confederate prisoners. Classes were suspended for 10 months due to troop occupation and staff losses. The Union troops caused significant damage, including the destruction of 467 library volumes used for fires.

Academic Hall was destroyed by fire on January 9, 1892, rumored to have been caused by the first electric light bulb west of the Mississippi River. The fire gutted the building, leaving only the six Ionic columns standing. The library collection was a total loss except for checked-out books.

After the fire, there was a movement to demolish the remaining Columns, but protests led by Columbia citizen Jerry S. Dorsey and an architect's reassurance of their structural integrity saved them. The Columns became a symbol of the campus.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Academic Hall featured a domed central section of three stories with two wings added in 1885. The building was constructed with brick fired on campus and limestone from Hinkson Creek Valley. The six Ionic columns are the most recognizable architectural feature.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Columns of Academic Hall are the most recognizable symbol of the University of Missouri, representing resilience and history. The building played a key role during the Civil War and its remains are a focal point of the Francis Quadrangle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Educational and administrative facility for the University of Missouri.
world knowledge.Details: The U.S. government settled a damage claim in 1915, which funded the construction of the Memorial Gateway. The Columns were nearly demolished in 1893 but were saved due to public protest and structural reassurances.

world knowledge.Name: Everglades National Park
world knowledge.Location: Miami-Dade, Monroe, & Collier counties, Florida, United States (25°18′45″N 80°41′15″W)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Everglades National Park was established to protect the southern 20% of the original Everglades, the largest tropical wilderness in the U.S. and the largest wilderness east of the Mississippi River. It was the first national park created to preserve a fragile ecosystem rather than scenic landscapes. The park has faced significant ecological threats due to human activity, including water diversion, urban development, and invasive species.

Major_Events.Description: The U.S. House of Representatives authorized the creation of Everglades National Park.
President Harry Truman dedicated the park, coinciding with the release of Marjory Stoneman Douglas's book 'The Everglades: River of Grass.'
The park was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Congress approved CERP, the largest environmental restoration in history, to restore water flow and ecosystems in the Everglades.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features diverse ecosystems including sawgrass marshes, mangrove forests, hardwood hammocks, and marine environments. It lacks traditional architectural structures but includes visitor centers and trails designed to minimize environmental impact.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Everglades is culturally significant as a unique ecosystem supporting rare and endangered species. It is vital for water recharge in South Florida and has been a focal point for conservation efforts. Indigenous tribes like the Tequesta and Calusa once inhabited the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of a fragile ecosystem, recreation, and education.
world knowledge.Details: The park is part of the Great Florida Birding Trail and is ideal for dark sky observations. It faces threats from urban development, water diversion, invasive species, and climate change. Restoration efforts are ongoing to preserve its ecosystems.

world knowledge.Name: Smoky Cape Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Smoky Cape, Arakoon, east of South West Rocks, Kempsey Shire, New South Wales, Australia, within Hat Head National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Smoky Cape Lighthouse was constructed to aid maritime navigation near the Macleay River entrance. Named by Captain James Cook in 1770 due to observed fires, the area became significant for shipping. The lighthouse was designed by Colonial Architect James Barnet and completed in 1891. It played a role in maritime safety, with over 20 shipwrecks recorded nearby. The lighthouse was automated in 1988 and remains operational under the Australian Maritime Safety Authority.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first exhibited on 15 April 1891, with an official ceremony on 29 April 1891.
Management was transferred to the Commonwealth due to its status as a coastal light under the Lighthouses Act of 1911.
The lighthouse was automated, reducing the need for manual operation.
Added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Octagonal mass concrete tower with a single-story pavilion entrance, cast-iron staircase, and gunmetal balustrade. Features a first-order Fresnel lens and Chance Brothers lantern. The design is unique for its use of in-situ concrete and octagonal shape, chosen for ease of construction. The complex includes a head keeper's residence, assistant keepers' cottages, and underground water tanks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Smoky Cape Lighthouse is a notable example of late Victorian industrial maritime technology and Colonial Architect James Barnet's work. It holds significance for Aboriginal communities due to mythological associations and for Europeans as a historic maritime outpost. The lighthouse is a tourist attraction and part of Hat Head National Park, offering whale-watching opportunities.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is one of the last major complexes designed by James Barnet and retains its original optic system. It is maintained by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority and classified by the National Trust of Australia (NSW). The head keeper's cottage operates as a bed and breakfast, while other cottages serve as holiday houses. The site includes remnants of World War II military installations.

world knowledge.Name: Abha International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Abha International Airport is an airport in Abha, the capital of Asir Province in Saudi Arabia. The site was a new construction area between the cities of Khamis Mushait and Abha, and served both equally. Construction of the airport started in mid-1975 by Laing Wimpey Alireza. Earlier, domestic flights had been handled at the military airport near Khamis Mushait. The airport became operational in 1977. The construction was carried out by Bin Trif Airport Ltd.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was initially attacked by the Yemeni Houthi movement on 12 June 2019, injuring 26 people.
On 23 June 2019, the Houthis launched another attack on the airport, leaving a Syrian national dead and 21 injured.
The airport was attacked again by missiles on 2 July 2019, leaving nine injured.

Another attack against the airport by Houthi forces occurred on 31 August 2020, when a bomb-laden drone was detected flying to it and intercepted, along with a remotely controlled boat off the Red Sea, which was also filled with explosives and ready for an attack.

On 10 February 2021, Houthis used four drones to carry out a drone strike on the airport, damaging a civilian aircraft (a Flyadeal Airbus A320) and starting a fire. A Houthi spokesman said the attack was in response to coalition airstrikes and other actions in Yemen.
On 31 August 2021, the airport was again attacked by Houthi drones, leaving 8 wounded.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 13/31 with an asphalt surface measuring 3,350 by 45 metres (10,991 ft × 148 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Abha International Airport serves as a crucial transportation hub for the Asir Province, connecting it domestically and internationally. It has been a target in the Yemeni civil war, highlighting its strategic importance.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has services to several domestic airports within the Kingdom. It also offers international flights to Aden and Sanaa in Yemen, Cairo in Egypt, Doha in Qatar, and nonstop flights to Dubai and Sharjah in the UAE.

world knowledge.Name: Ziarat
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ziarat is a city in the Ziarat District of the Balochistan province in Pakistan. It was previously part of Sibi district and was announced as a separate district on July 1, 1986. The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where the founder of Pakistan spent some of his last days, is located here.

Major_Events.Description: On October 29, 2008, Ziarat and surrounding areas were struck by an earthquake doublet. The first tremor, 6.2 magnitude, lasted a couple of seconds, followed by a magnitude-6.4 tremor that lasted almost 30 seconds, destroying many mud houses and several government buildings. More than 200 people were killed, and over 50,000 were left homeless. Landslides cut off many roads, making the area less accessible to emergency responders. Pakistani military helicopters were used to reach mountainous and remote locations.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ziarat is culturally significant due to the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where the founder of Pakistan spent some of his last days. It is also surrounded by the lush green Ziarat Juniper Forest, home to some of the oldest juniper trees in the world, with some trees being 4000 years old.
world knowledge.Details: Ziarat is surrounded by the Ziarat Juniper Forest, known locally as Sanober, which covers about 110,000 hectares and is believed to be the second largest of its kind in the world. The indigenous tribes are primarily Kakar and Tareen (including Raisani). Ziarat has a continental climate and remains quite cool in summer compared to other cities in Pakistan.

world knowledge.Name: Babeș-Bolyai University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Babeș-Bolyai University, established in 1581 as Academia Claudiopolitana, underwent several reorganizations over the centuries, eventually taking its current form in 1959 through the merger of Bolyai University (founded in 1945) and Victor Babeș University (founded in 1919). It is the largest Romanian university with about 50,000 students and offers study programmes in Romanian, Hungarian, German, English, and French.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as a Jesuit college by Stephen Báthory, King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania and Prince of Transylvania.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Bolyai University and Victor Babeș University
Major_Events.Description: The current form of Babeș-Bolyai University was established through the merger of Bolyai University and Victor Babeș University.
The university introduced an educational system based on multiculturalism and multilingualism.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Babeș-Bolyai University is a multicultural institution with study programmes in Romanian, Hungarian, German, English, and French. It is the principal institution that educates members of the Hungarian minority in Transylvania and has a significant role in promoting cultural and linguistic diversity.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 22 faculties and offers bachelor's, master's, and PhD degrees. It is affiliated with numerous international organizations, including the Guild of European Research-Intensive Universities, European University Association, and International Association of Universities. The university also has several museums and a large student housing infrastructure.

world knowledge.Name: Pleiku Airport
world knowledge.Address: Near the city of Pleiku, Gia Lai Province, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pleiku Airport was designated as Air Base 62 by the Republic of Vietnam Air Force (VNAF) in December 1962. It was expanded during the Vietnam War and served as a major air base for the VNAF and United States Air Force. After 1975, it was developed into a civil airport.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was designated by the Republic of Vietnam Air Force (VNAF) as Air Base 62.
The airport was expanded and became a major air base for the VNAF and United States Air Force.
After the Vietnam War, the airport was developed into a civil airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway with a length of 2,400 meters and a surface of asphalt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pleiku Airport played a significant role during the Vietnam War as a major air base for both the Republic of Vietnam Air Force and the United States Air Force.
world knowledge.Details: Pleiku Airport (IATA: PXU, ICAO: VVPK) is a regional airport located near the city of Pleiku within Gia Lai Province in southern Vietnam. This article about a Vietnamese airport is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Akhmad Kadyrov Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Akhmad Kadyrov Mosque, located in Grozny, Chechnya, is one of the largest mosques in Russia. It stands on the site of the former Presidential Palace, destroyed during the First Chechen War. Named after Akhmad Kadyrov, the first president of the Republic of Chechnya, the mosque was commissioned by the mayor of Konya, Turkey. It was officially opened on October 16, 2008, in a ceremony attended by Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov and Russian Prime Minister Vladimir Putin.

Major_Events.Description: The mosque was officially opened in a ceremony attended by Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov and Russian Prime Minister Vladimir Putin.
The mosque participated in the "Russia 10" competition and took second place. Ramzan Kadyrov withdrew the mosque from the competition due to alleged voting irregularities.
Gabon issued a commemorative coin featuring the Akhmad Kadyrov Mosque.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque is designed in the Late Classical Ottoman style, inspired by the Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) in Istanbul. It features a central dome (16 meters in diameter, 32 meters in height) and four minarets, each 62 meters tall. The exterior and interior walls are made of marble and travertine, with the interior decorated in white marble. The mosque includes 36 chandeliers inspired by Islam's holiest sites, and the mihrab is made of white marble, creating an illusion of infinite space.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is a symbol of Chechnya's revival and resilience after the First Chechen War. It is named after Akhmad Kadyrov, a key figure in Chechen history, and serves as a central place of worship and cultural identity for the Chechen people.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque is part of an Islamic architectural complex that includes the Russian Islamic University, the Kunta-Haji, and the Spiritual Administration of Muslims of the Republic of Chechnya. It has a high seismic resistance and is located on the banks of the Sunzha River within a 14-hectare park. The mosque can accommodate over 10,000 worshippers, with an additional 10,000 able to pray in the summer gallery.

world knowledge.Name: Jurassic Skyline
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 53 metres (174 feet) high, 140 tons in weight
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jurassic Skyline tower, originally known as the Weymouth Sea Life Tower, was an observation tower on Weymouth Pier in Weymouth, Dorset, England. It opened on 22 June 2012 and was designed as a temporary tourist attraction. The tower was funded by private money and operated by Merlin Entertainments. It was dismantled after its closure in August 2019 due to declining visitor numbers.

Major_Events.Description: The tower opened on 22 June 2012.
On 5 September 2017, the gondola became stuck, and 13 people were winched off by helicopter.
The tower was announced to be permanently closed in August 2019 and was subsequently removed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower stood 53 metres (174 feet) high with a clear-fronted passenger gondola that could turn a full 360 degrees as it rose. It accommodated 69 passengers at a time. The tower was designed in Germany and built in Hungary and France before being shipped in sections to be assembled on site. A total of 1,100 tons of concrete was used during building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower was a notable tourist attraction in Weymouth, offering panoramic views of the English Channel, Weymouth town, the beach, the Pavilion, the Old Harbour, Nothe Gardens, the Nothe Fort, and Portland Harbour. On clear days, views extended down the Dorset coast to Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door.
world knowledge.Details: The tower's original five-year permission was extended in 2017 for a further five years. It was sold to another company after its closure and dismantled. The idea of the tower was put forward in 2009-10, and Weymouth was selected due to its far-reaching vistas and closeness to the Sea Life Park.

world knowledge.Name: Kalibo International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kalibo International Airport serves the general area of Kalibo, the capital of the province of Aklan in the Philippines, and is one of two airports serving Boracay. It is one of the two classified international airports on the island of Panay and is among the busiest airports in Western Visayas. The airport has undergone significant upgrades and expansions, including the construction of a new terminal building and runway extensions.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the airport's new terminal building commenced as part of a ₱130-million fund pledged by President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo for the upgrade of the airport.
A 200-meter extension of the runway was due to open by the end of 2017, extending the current 2,187-meter runway to 2,387 meters.
A ₱17.9-million expansion and rehabilitation project for the terminal building began as part of the Build! Build! Build! program.
The entire rehabilitation project, including the terminal, apron pavement, and nearby facilities, was inaugurated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a single 2,500-meter runway with a width of 45 meters, running in a direction of 05°/23°. It features a two-level passenger terminal building with check-in counters, security checks, pre-departure areas, airline offices, kiosks, restaurants, and pasalubong centers. The international passenger terminal building can accommodate 406 passengers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kalibo International Airport is a key gateway for tourism in the Philippines, particularly for Boracay, and plays a significant role in the economic development of Western Visayas.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is classified as an international airport by the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines and has among the highest international flight activity in Western Visayas. It is the fastest growing airport in the Philippines in terms of passenger traffic.

world knowledge.Name: Free Life Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 70.8 metres (232 ft) long, 5.8 metres (19 ft) wide, 7.4 metres (24 ft) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1571 with funds collected by monk Xingchao from Cimen Temple. During the Ming and Qing dynasties, local monks held ceremonies on the bridge to release live fish into the port. It was part of "The Ten Views of Zhujiajiao" and was rebuilt in 1812 during the Jiaqing Emperor's reign.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was originally built with funds collected by monk Xingchao.
The bridge was rebuilt during the Jiaqing Emperor's reign.
Designated as a municipal level cultural heritage by the Shanghai Municipal Government.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stone arch bridge with five arches, featuring ultra-thin piers and modest size changes for a gentle slope. It spans naturally across the river.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is historically significant as it was part of "The Ten Views of Zhujiajiao" and was used for ceremonial fish releases by monks. It is also the largest stone bridge in Shanghai.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is the largest stone bridge in Shanghai and has been a significant cultural and historical landmark since its construction in 1571.

world knowledge.Name: SDAT Astroturf Hockey Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Located at the foot of the Kathiresan Malai Murugan Kovil (Kathiresan Kovil) Hill, near Tiger Cave, Kovilpatti, Tamil Nadu, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built in 2016 and opened in 2017 by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu. It has hosted several national-level hockey tournaments.

Major_Events.Event: 11th All India Lakshmi Ammal Hockey Trophy Men's Team
Major_Events.Description: National level hockey trophy match

Major_Events.Event: 11th Hockey India Junior Men's Championship Trophy
Major_Events.Description: National level hockey championship

Major_Events.Event: 12th Hockey India Junior Men's Championship Trophy
Major_Events.Description: National level hockey championship with 30 junior men's teams participating

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Artificial turf surface, modern sports facility
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a key venue for hockey in Tamil Nadu, hosting national tournaments and serving as the home ground for the Kovilpatti team.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu, the stadium has a capacity of 2,000 spectators. It cost ₹7 crore (US$830,000) to construct. Public transit options include two-wheelers and TNSTC buses.

world knowledge.Name: Dushanbe International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dushanbe International Airport is an international airport in Dushanbe, the capital of Tajikistan. It is the main hub for Somon Air and is the home base for Tajik Air, which also has its headquarters on the property. The first airport in the country was built in 1924 in the city currently known as Dushanbe. A new airport was built in November 1929 to serve Stalinabad (past name of Dushanbe). The current airport complex was put into operation in 1964 and has been reconstructed several times over the years. A new French-built terminal, which can serve 1.5 million passengers a year, was opened on 3 September 2014.

Major_Events.Description: On 7 September 1992, during the first months of the Tajikistani Civil War, President Rahmon Nabiyev and an entourage of his were on their way to the airport when they were ambushed by opposition forces. At the terminal, Nabiyev was forced to resign, practically at gunpoint, after a meeting and discussions with the armed opposition in the VIP lounge, before being released. Tanks and troops were reportedly stationed at the terminal during the whole ordeal.

A new French-built terminal, which can serve 1.5 million passengers a year, was opened on 3 September 2014. France provided Tajikistan a long-term, low-interest €20 million loan. Tajikistan's own contribution was €19 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a French-built terminal capable of serving 1.5 million passengers annually. The runway is 10,210 ft long with an asphalt-concrete surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dushanbe International Airport is a significant transportation hub in Tajikistan, serving as the main hub for Somon Air and the home base for Tajik Air. It has played a crucial role in the country's history, including during the Tajikistani Civil War.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is jointly used for civil and military purposes. It is owned and operated by the Government of Tajikistan. The elevation of the airport is 2,575 ft (785 m) above mean sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio de la UNSA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built by the University of San Agustín in the early 1990s and named after the Virgin Chapi. The stadium was largely financed by a lottery fund-raiser held by the university itself. It is the biggest stadium in Arequipa and the fourth one in Peru. The stadium was first opened on 11 November 1993.

Major_Events.Description: First game played was between Ingeniería Geofísica and Mecánica Eléctrica; Ingeniería Geofísica won 1–0.
Local FBC Melgar faced Alianza Lima; the match ended in a 1–1 draw.
The stadium hosted the XIII Bolivarian Games.
Second leg of the 2003 Copa Sudamericana Finals between local Cienciano of Cusco and Argentinian River Plate. Cienciano defeated River Plate 1–0 to lift Peru's first international club trophy.

The stadium was selected to be a venue for the 2004 Copa América. Arequipa hosted the first four group matches of Group C involving the national football teams of Costa Rica, Brazil, Paraguay, and Chile.
Pope John Paul II visited the city of Arequipa in which the coronation of the Virgin of Chapi took place on a field that would eventually become the site of the monumental stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass surface and a capacity of 40,370 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it is the biggest stadium in Arequipa and the fourth one in Peru. It has hosted major events like the Bolivarian Games, Copa América, and a Copa Sudamericana final. It is also named after the Virgin Chapi, reflecting local religious and cultural values.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches and large events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was going to be one of the five venues for the 2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup. It is the home stadium of football clubs Melgar of the Peruvian Primera División and IDUNSA of the Copa Perú.

world knowledge.Name: Museum of the Rockies
world knowledge.Address: 600 W. Kagy Boulevard, Bozeman, Montana, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museum of the Rockies was founded in 1957, funded in part by a gift from Caroline M. McGill. Originally affiliated with Montana State University, it is now also an affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution. The museum focuses on the physical and cultural history of the Rocky Mountains and houses one of the largest collections of dinosaur fossils in the world.

Major_Events.Description: The museum acquired over 10,000 photographs and negatives from the heirs of Albert, Alfred and Chris Schlechten, chronicling the Bozeman and Yellowstone National Park areas from about 1905 until the late 1970s.
A Tyrannosaurus Rex skeleton was discovered and remained in Montana, exhibited at the museum, marking a shift in the museum's paleontological significance.
The museum became an affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution, gaining greater access to the collections and programs of that institute.

Major_Events.Event: Discovery of soft tissue in T. rex
Major_Events.Description: Soft tissue remains were discovered in the thigh bone of a Tyrannosaurus, later brought to the museum.

Major_Events.Event: Groundbreaking of Curatorial Center for the Humanities
Major_Events.Description: The museum broke ground on a new $4 million, 20,000-square-foot Curatorial Center for the Humanities, which will provide storage and curatorial space for the museum's humanities collection.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum includes the Tinsley House, a 100+ year-old log house moved to the museum site in 1989, and the Taylor Planetarium, a 40 ft, 104-seat domed theater. The new Curatorial Center for the Humanities is designed by Slate Architecture of Helena.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and tells the stories of Montana and the Northern Rockies, educating visitors about the region's rich history, including its Paleontological roots. It is Montana's official repository for Paleontological specimens and part of the Montana Dinosaur Trail.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include 300,000 objects covering over 500,000,000 years of history. It houses the largest Tyrannosaurus skull ever discovered and is home to 13 Tyrannosaurus Rex specimens, including one of only two complete skeletons found. The museum offers educational programs, symposiums, and traveling exhibits on various topics.

world knowledge.Name: Ngorongoro Conservation Area
world knowledge.Address: Ngorongoro District, 180 km west of Arusha City, Arusha Region, Tanzania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Tanzania. It is named after the Ngorongoro Crater, a large volcanic caldera within the area. The area has been inhabited by various hominid species for 3 million years, with pastoralists replacing hunter-gatherers a few thousand years ago. The Maasai pastoralists, who arrived in the 1800s, named the crater after the sound produced by the cowbell. The area was first visited by Europeans in 1892, and it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979.

Major_Events.Description: The establishment of Serengeti National Park led to the relocation of Maasai pastoralists to Ngorongoro, increasing the population of Maasai and livestock in the Crater.
The Ngorongoro Conservation Area was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its natural significance.
The area received Mixed Heritage Status, recognizing its cultural significance related to human evolution and human-environment dynamics.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is culturally significant due to its long sequence of crucial evidence related to human evolution and human-environment dynamics. It is also home to the Maasai community, who have a long history of pastoralism in the area.
world knowledge.Details: The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is part of the Serengeti ecosystem and is contiguous with the Serengeti National Park. It is home to a wide variety of wildlife, including the black rhinoceros, African buffalo, and lions. The area also contains Olduvai Gorge, one of the most important paleoanthropological sites in the world. The conservation area is unique in Tanzania as it allows human habitation while protecting wildlife. However, restrictions on land use have generated tension between local Maasai communities and conservation authorities.

world knowledge.Name: Bryngarw Country Park
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 15th century (Bryngarw House), 1986 (official opening as a country park)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bryngarw Country Park is a Grade II listed park and garden on the Cadw/ICOMOS Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in Wales. The park was officially opened on May 23, 1986, after extensive reclamation work. Bryngarw House, thought to have been built in the 15th century, was extensively modified over the centuries and served various purposes, including as a farmhouse, private residence, and council accommodation before being restored and integrated into the park.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a Key Strategic Site
Major_Events.Description: The park was designated as a Key Strategic Site under the Valleys Partnership Initiative Action Program, leading to funding for environmental improvements.
The park won its first Green Flag Award for its excellent use of green space, well-maintained facilities, and high standard of safety and security.

Major_Events.Event: Official Opening as a Country Park
Major_Events.Description: Bryngarw Country Park was officially opened after five years of reclamation and construction work.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of broadleaf, coniferous, and mixed woodland, meadows, wetlands, formal gardens, and areas for amenity use. Bryngarw House, a historic building, is surrounded by formal gardens, including a lawn, shrubbery, lake, and oriental gardens. The park also includes a network of paths, a visitor center, and a café.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bryngarw Country Park is culturally significant as a Grade II listed park and garden, recognized for its historical and ecological value. It has been awarded multiple Green Flags for its maintenance and environmental standards. The park also plays a role in local biodiversity conservation and sustainable tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes various ecological zones such as Coed Waunpiod west and east, Sycamore wood, Coed Kensington, Rhos pasture, and wet woodland. It is home to diverse flora and fauna, including species like speckled wood butterflies, wood mice, kingfishers, and otters. The park also features a spring-fed lake, ornamental ponds, and an adventure play area.

world knowledge.Name: Palermo Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Palermo Cathedral is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Palermo, dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary. It was erected in 1185 by Walter Ophamil, the Norman archbishop of Palermo, on the site of an earlier Byzantine basilica that was later turned into a mosque by the Arabs. The cathedral has undergone various additions and restorations, with the last major restoration in the 18th century.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the cathedral began under Walter Ophamil, the Norman archbishop of Palermo.
The cathedral underwent significant alterations and restorations, including the addition of the neoclassical dome and other architectural changes.
Palermo Cathedral was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site during the 39th session.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a blend of Norman, Islamic, Gothic, Baroque, and Neoclassical styles. It has a Latin cross plan with a nave and two aisles, a neoclassical dome, and various Gothic-Catalan elements. The interior includes a wooden choir, marble statues, and a meridian used for astronomical observations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Palermo Cathedral is a significant cultural and historical landmark due to its architectural diversity and its role in the religious and political history of Sicily. It houses the tombs of several royal and imperial figures, including Emperor Henry VI, Frederick II, and Roger II.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral contains a meridian built in 1801 by astronomer Giuseppe Piazzi, used for standardizing time and calendar measurements. It also houses the Treasury, which includes sacred vestments, monstrances, chalices, and the gold crown of Constance of Aragon.

world knowledge.Name: Pladda Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pladda Lighthouse is an active 18th century lighthouse situated at the southern end of the island of Pladda in western Scotland. The lighthouse dates from 1790 and was designed by Thomas Smith. It was the first light on the Clyde to be commissioned by the Commissioners of the Northern Lights. It had both an upper and a lower light to distinguish it from the three other lighthouses in the Firth of Clyde. In 1876, Pladda was about the third station to have a foghorn. The 'double lights' were replaced by a powerful flashing system in 1901. Lightkeepers were withdrawn in 1990 when the lighthouse was automated; it is now remotely monitored from the Northern Lighthouse Board's headquarters in Edinburgh.

Major_Events.Description: Pladda was about the third station to have a foghorn.
The 'double lights' were replaced by a powerful flashing system.
Lightkeepers were withdrawn when the lighthouse was automated; it is now remotely monitored from the Northern Lighthouse Board's headquarters in Edinburgh.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse tower is 29 metres (95 ft) in height; there are 128 steps to the top. It is a cylindrical masonry tower with white tower, black lantern, and ochre trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pladda Lighthouse was the first light on the Clyde to be commissioned by the Commissioners of the Northern Lights. It features extensively in Peter Hill's 2003 book 'Stargazing: Memoirs of a Young Lighthouse Keeper' and was a filming location for 'Queen Victoria Syndrome', the first episode of season 5 of The Crown.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse's light (three white flashes every 30 seconds) is visible for 17 nautical miles (31 kilometres) under normal conditions. It uses a hyperradiant Fresnel lens and has a focal height of 40 m (130 ft).

world knowledge.Name: Aeroparque Jorge Newbery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jorge Newbery Airfield, commonly known as Aeroparque, is an international airport 2 km northwest of downtown Buenos Aires, Argentina. It was originally proposed by Mayor Carlos Noel in 1925, with plans and zoning disputes following. The airport was designed by Aeronautics Secretariat engineer Víctor Acuña in 1945 and inaugurated in 1947 as Aeroparque 17 de Octubre. It began operations in January 1948 and has since undergone several expansions and renovations.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inaugurated as Aeroparque 17 de Octubre.
Following the coup against President Juan Perón, the airport was renamed in honor of Jorge Newbery, a pioneer of Argentine aviation.
The airport was re-inaugurated following expansions, including a new terminal and extended runway.
The airport's operations were privatized and transferred to Aeropuertos Argentina 2000.
The runway was extended by 180 meters.
Terminals III and IV were inaugurated, doubling the airport's passenger capacity.
All international flights (except to Uruguay) were moved to Ezeiza Airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features multiple terminals with a total area of 65,000 m², a concrete runway, and facilities designed to accommodate a high volume of passengers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aeroparque Jorge Newbery is a key transportation hub in Argentina, serving as the main hub for domestic flights and connecting Buenos Aires with various South American destinations. It has played a significant role in the development of Argentine aviation and has been a witness to several historical events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving domestic and regional flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has been involved in several crashes from 1959 to 2017, including the LAPA Flight 3142, one of the deadliest aviation accidents in Argentina's history. Plans to merge it with Ezeiza International Airport were considered but ultimately dropped.
