The airport has undergone significant expansions to accommodate increasing passenger traffic and wide-body aircraft.

world knowledge.Name: Eden Gardens
world knowledge.Location: Near Maidan, B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata, West Bengal, India
world knowledge.Address: Gostho Paul Sarani, Maidan , B. B. D. Bagh Kolkata , West Bengal India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eden Gardens is an international cricket stadium in Kolkata, India. Established in 1864, it is the oldest and second-largest cricket stadium in India and third-largest in the world. The stadium currently has a capacity of 68,000. It is operated by Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) and is the home ground of the Kolkata Knight Riders. It houses the headquarters of Cricket Association of Bengal. Eden Gardens is often referred to as home of Indian cricket and has also been described as "cricket's answer to the Colosseum" and called the "Mecca of Indian cricket", due to it being the first purpose-built ground for the sport.

Major_Events.Event: India v. Sri Lanka in 1996 Cricket World Cup Semi-Final
Major_Events.Description: Eden Gardens witnessed a record crowd of 110,564 in the 1996 India Vs Sri Lanka Cricket World Cup Semi Final.
The 2016 ICC World Twenty20 final was held at the stadium, with the West Indies beating England in a closely fought encounter.

Due to unsafe conditions arising from the incomplete renovations, the ICC withdrew the India vs. England match from the Eden Gardens. This match, scheduled on 27 February 2011, was played in Bengaluru at M.Chinnaswamy Stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium's capacity was expanded to 100,000 from 40,000 for the 1987 World Cup. The expansion also included renovations to the press area. 42 columns were added to provide the support for large roofs and multi-tiered covered stands. Even after the renovation, not all seats were covered, and many sections lacked individual seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Eden Gardens is often referred to as home of Indian cricket and has also been described as "cricket's answer to the Colosseum" and called the "Mecca of Indian cricket", due to it being the first purpose-built ground for the sport.
world knowledge.Details: Eden Gardens stands have been named after prominent local cricketers and soldiers. On 22 January 2017, two stands were named after Indian cricketers - Sourav Ganguly and Pankaj Roy while two more were named after cricket administrators - BN Dutt (BCCI President 1988 to 1990) and Jagmohan Dalmiya (BCCI President 2001–04, 2013 - interim, 2015). Dalmiya served as ICC President from 1997 to 2000. On 27 April 2017, 4 stands were named after Indian soldiers - Colonel Neelakantan Jayachandran Nair, Havildar Hangpan Dada, Lieutenant Colonel Dhan Singh Thapa and Subedar Joginder Singh Sahnan. Lt Col Thapa and Subedar Singh are Param Vir Chakra awardees - the highest wartime military decoration in India while Col Nair and Havildar Dada are Ashok Chakra - the highest peacetime military decoration. In 2024, a stand was decided to be dedicated to star Indian pacer and the highest ODI wicket taker among women, Jhulan Goswami. It was unveiled on January 22, 2025.

world knowledge.Name: Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Dandong, Liaoning, China and Sinŭiju, North P'yŏngan, North Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge was constructed by the Imperial Japanese Army during its occupation of Korea and Manchukuo. It was renamed from the Yalu (Amnok) River Bridge in 1990. The bridge and an older nearby bridge were repeatedly bombed during the Korean War by the USAF to disrupt supply lines. The older bridge was left in ruins, while the newer bridge was repaired and put back into use after the war.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was built during the Japanese occupation of Korea and Manchukuo.
The USAF repeatedly attacked and destroyed the bridges to cut off Chinese military supplies to North Korea. The older bridge was left in ruins, while the newer bridge was repaired after the war.
The bridge was renamed from Yalu (Amnok) River Bridge to Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel bridge carrying one lane of AH1, road, and rail traffic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge serves as a symbol of the relationship between China and North Korea and is a major tourist attraction in China. The nearby Yalu River Broken Bridge is preserved as evidence of the destruction during the Korean War.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (road and rail) between China and North Korea.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is part of the Yalu (Amnok) River Scenic Area, a major tourist attraction in China rated AAAA. Tourist boats offer views of both bridges and the North Korean waterfront. Pedestrians are not allowed to cross the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Sanaa University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sana'a University was established in 1970 as the first and the primary university in the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen), now the Republic of Yemen. It started with two faculties: the Faculty of Sharia and Law and the Faculty of Education. Over time, it expanded to include 20 faculties by 2005, with 12 at the main campus in Sanaa and eight others at different branches throughout the country. Postgraduate studies began in the early 1980s.

Major_Events.Description: Sana'a University was established as the first university in the Yemen Arab Republic.

Specialties within the Faculty of Education were developed into three new faculties: Arts, Science, and Education. The Business Department in the Faculty of Sharia and Law became an independent faculty.
Sanaa University began offering postgraduate studies.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sanaa University is culturally and historically significant as the first university in the Yemen Arab Republic, playing a crucial role in the development of higher education in Yemen.
world knowledge.Details: Sanaa University is currently organized with 17 faculties and includes several accommodation buildings for staff and students. It is partnered with the Kuwait University Hospital for medical students.

world knowledge.Name: Place Carnot
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Place des Victoires during the First Empire, it underwent several name changes including Place Louis XVI, Place Louis XVIII, Place de la Liberté, Place de la République, Place Napoléon, and Place Perrache. It was officially named Place Carnot on 18 February 1889 in honor of Lazare Carnot, a Hero of the Revolution.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the Allegory of the Republic statue
Major_Events.Description: The statue was inaugurated by French President Sadi Carnot, grandson of Lazare Carnot.
French President Sadi Carnot was assassinated by an Italian anarchist during his second trip to Lyon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Nineteenth-century buildings of five or six floors, decorated and well maintained, line the north and east sides of the square. The Catholic University of Lyon is on the west side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Place Carnot is historically significant due to its various name changes reflecting the political changes in France and its association with Lazare Carnot, a Hero of the Revolution.
world knowledge.Details: The square features a playground for children, a carousel, a small sports ground, and hosts 140 cabins during the Christmas market. There is a farmers' market on Wednesdays from 16:00 to 19:30 on the north side of the square. It is bordered by the Rue de Condé and can be accessed by the Rue Victor-Hugo, through the Rue Henri IV and Rue Auguste Comte. To the south, it follows the Cours de Verdun and the Perrache Multimodal Hub, a major public transit hub linked to the railway station. Traboule leads to the Cours Charlemagne, either from the lobby of the Perrache railway station, or through underneath.

world knowledge.Name: Riga Technical University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Riga Technical University (RTU) is the oldest technical university in the Baltic countries, established on October 14, 1862. It was previously known as 'Riga Polytechnical Institute' and 'Riga Polytechnicum'. The university evolved from the Riga Polytechnical Institute, which was established in 1958 by separating the engineering departments from the Latvian State University. It was renamed Riga Technical University in 1990 and has since expanded to become the largest STEM-oriented university in Latvia.

Major_Events.Description: Riga Polytechnicum was established as the first polytechnical institute in Imperial Russia, offering degrees in agriculture, chemistry, engineering, mechanics, trade, and architecture with education in German.
As part of Russification, the university was nationalized and renamed Riga Polytechnical Institute, with the language of instruction changed to Russian.
During World War I, the Riga Polytechnical Institute was evacuated to Moscow, where it operated until 1918.
The Riga Polytechnic Institute was re-established by splitting off the engineering departments from the State University of Latvia.
The university was renamed Riga Technical University and has since expanded to nine faculties.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university campus is urban, covering 11.8 hectares, with buildings reflecting various architectural styles from its long history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: RTU is culturally significant as the oldest technical university in the Baltic countries and a major center for STEM education. It has played a pivotal role in the development of technical education and architecture in the region.
world knowledge.Details: RTU is one of the eight holders of the European University of Technology (EUt+). It has been ranked highly in various international university rankings, including QS World University Rating and Times Higher Education Rating. The university is known for its strong focus on sustainability and planet protection, being recognized as the 14th best in the world in this field in 2020.

world knowledge.Name: Roosevelt Campobello International Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Roosevelt Campobello International Park preserves the house and surrounding landscape of the summer retreat of Franklin D. Roosevelt, Eleanor Roosevelt, and their family. The cottage was given as a wedding present to Franklin and Eleanor in 1908 by Franklin's mother Sara Roosevelt. In August 1921, Roosevelt was stricken by a severe paralytic illness, believed to be polio, leaving him permanently paralyzed from the waist down. The property was later deeded to the governments of the U.S. and Canada by Armand Hammer after Eleanor's death in 1962, leading to the creation of the park in 1964.

Major_Events.Description: Franklin D. Roosevelt was stricken by a severe paralytic illness, believed to be polio, leaving him permanently paralyzed from the waist down.
The Roosevelt Campobello International Park was established on July 7, 1964, through an international treaty signed by Canada and the United States.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cottage is built in the Shingle Style and was designed by Willard T. Sears.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it preserves the summer retreat of Franklin D. Roosevelt, who became the 32nd President of the United States, and his family. It symbolizes the close relationship between Canada and the United States.
world knowledge.Details: The park is jointly managed and staffed by the governments of Canada and the United States. It includes the 19th-century vacation cottage, related outbuildings, gardens, hiking trails, a visitor center, and a gift shop. The park is an affiliated area of Parks Canada and the U.S. National Park Service.

world knowledge.Name: Duke Chapel
world knowledge.Address: Duke University, Durham, North Carolina, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 210 feet (64 m) tall, nave measures 291 feet (89 m) long, 63 feet (19 m) wide, and 73 feet (22 m) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Duke University Chapel is an ecumenical Christian chapel and the center of religion at Duke University. Completed in 1935, it was the last of the original buildings to be built on West Campus. Designed by Julian Abele and Horace Trumbauer, it is built in the Collegiate Gothic style and stands as one of the tallest buildings in Durham County.

Major_Events.Description: The chapel was first used during Commencement while still under construction.
The chapel was formally finished and dedicated on June 2, 1935.
The chapel closed for a year due to necessary restoration work on the ceiling.
The chapel reopened on May 11, 2016, after restoration.

Major_Events.Event: Removal of Robert E. Lee statue
Major_Events.Description: The statue of Robert E. Lee was removed from the chapel's entrance portal after being vandalized during nationwide protests against Confederate memorials.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Collegiate Gothic style with large stones, pointed arches, and ribbed vaults. Features a 50-bell carillon, three pipe organs, and stained-glass windows. The nave and transepts are constructed from Guastavino tile. The chapel is cruciform with a nave, transepts, a Memorial Chapel, and a crypt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The chapel is the center of religion at Duke University and has connections to the United Methodist Church. It houses significant historical and religious artifacts, including stained-glass windows depicting biblical scenes and figures, and serves as a place for reflection, prayer, and university ceremonies.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ecumenical Christian chapel and center of religion at Duke University
world knowledge.Details: The chapel features a 50-bell carillon, three pipe organs (including the Kathleen McClendon Organ, the Benjamin N. Duke Memorial Organ, and the Brombaugh Organ), and 77 stained-glass windows. The Memorial Chapel houses the sarcophagi of Washington Duke and his sons, James B. Duke and Benjamin N. Duke. The crypt beneath the Memorial Chapel contains the remains of several important figures in Duke University's history. The chapel's bell tower is modeled after the Bell Harry Tower of Canterbury Cathedral and is not open to the public except during special times for students.

world knowledge.Name: Boulevard Theater (Miami)
world knowledge.Address: 7770 Biscayne Boulevard Miami, Florida United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Boulevard Theater opened on Thanksgiving Day, November 21, 1940, as part of the Paramount Theatres chain. It was hailed as "the finest neighborhood theater in the South" and featured modern amenities like air conditioning, acoustical walls, and neon lighting. Over the years, it has served as a movie theater, nightclub, and adult entertainment venue under various names such as Pussycat, Black Gold, Club Madonna II, and Gold Rush Cabaret. It was purchased by Leroy Griffith in 1970 and has been a subject of community activism due to its adult entertainment offerings.

Major_Events.Description: The theater debuted with a matinee showing of 'Rhythm on the River,' starring Bing Crosby and Mary Martin.

Griffith purchased the theater for $165,000, renamed it the Pussycat, and repurposed it into three sections: the Pussycat (adult films), the Kitty Cat (female performers), and the Tomcat (male performers).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Weed & Reeder, the theater featured modern amenities for its time, including a massive air conditioning system, acoustical walls, and neon lighting.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Boulevard Theater is a notable example of mid-20th century theater architecture and reflects the evolution of entertainment venues from traditional movie theaters to adult entertainment clubs. Its history highlights changes in cultural and social norms over the decades.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a movie theater, now an adult nightclub (Gold Rush Cabaret).
world knowledge.Details: The theater has undergone several name changes and operational shifts, including periods as a nightclub and adult movie theater. Community activists have attempted to shut it down due to its adult entertainment offerings.

world knowledge.Name: Telford Town Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Telford Town Park has a rich history dating back to the Anglo-Saxon period when the area was cleared for farming. The land was later used by Cistercian monks in the 13th century and saw significant industrial activity during the Industrial Revolution, including coal and ironstone mining. The park was developed in the 1970s by the Telford Development Corporation to provide a 'Green Lung' for the new industrial town. It was designated a Local Nature Reserve due to its diverse habitats and wildlife.

Major_Events.Description: Telford Town Park was voted the UK's Best Park in a public competition organized by Fields in Trust.
A memorial to commemorate the Holocaust was unveiled on Holocaust Memorial Day by David Wright MP and Dr Eve Clevenger.
Telford parkrun, a weekly 5 km event, became extremely popular with runners, joggers, and walkers of all ages and abilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of woodland, heathland, grassland, and pools, with remnants of industrial structures such as pit mounds and quarries that have been reclaimed by nature.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Telford Town Park is culturally significant as it provides a green space in the heart of an industrial town, preserves the area's industrial heritage, and supports diverse wildlife. It also hosts community events and memorials honoring local and historical significance.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located off Junction 5 of the M54, within walking distance of Telford's main bus station and Telford Central railway station. It hosts a variety of wildlife, including endangered species such as bats and newts. The park also features memorials, including one honoring residents of the Telford and Wrekin borough who died serving their country since World War I.

world knowledge.Name: The Priory, Beech Hill
world knowledge.Address: Southeast of Beech Hill, Berkshire, on the banks of the River Loddon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a hermitage associated with Beaumys Castle, later converted into Stratfield Saye Priory. The priory was dissolved in 1399. The land was leased from 1558 to 1665 by the Harrison family, who likely built the current house in 1648.

Major_Events.Description: The priory was dissolved.
The Harrison family built the current house, as indicated by the date on the central porch.
The granary at The Priory was designated as a listed building on 28 January 1987.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Two-storey, three-gabled house built of red English bond brick. Features a central porch dated 1648. Northwest of the house are a dovecote and granary. The late 17th-century garden is bounded by brick buildings and a small canal.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Historic Grade II* listed building, representing Elizabethan architecture and the transition from religious to residential use.
world knowledge.Details: The granary at The Priory, approximately 60 metres to the north, is also a listed building with reference number 1117132. The house is located on the banks of the River Loddon.

world knowledge.Name: Papineau-Leblanc Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Laval, Quebec and Montreal, Quebec, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Papineau-Leblanc Bridge was one of the first cable-stayed spans in North America. It is part of Quebec Autoroute 19 and connects Laval and Montreal, spanning Rivière des Prairies. The Leblanc portion of the name comes from a street in Laval named after Alpha Leblanc, a local landowner. In 2000, a proposition to rename the bridge after Pietro Rizzuto was rejected as the original name was already entrenched in local culture.

Major_Events.Description: A proposition to rename the bridge after the late Pietro Rizzuto was initially approved, then rejected by the Commission de Toponymie du Québec, which ruled that the name Papineau-Leblanc was already entrenched in local culture and non-controversial.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed bridge fabricated from weathering steel with an orthotropic deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the first cable-stayed bridges in North America and a key transportation link between Laval and Montreal. The bridge's name reflects local history and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries 6 lanes of Autoroute 19, connecting Laval and Montreal.
world knowledge.Details: The freeway ends abruptly at the southern end of the bridge at the intersection of Henri Bourassa Boulevard, where Autoroute 19 follows Avenue Papineau down to Quebec Autoroute 40. Most locals refer to this bridge as Papineau. Daily traffic in 2013 was 56,000.

world knowledge.Name: Théâtre des Célestins
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Théâtre des Célestins is a historic theater in Lyon, France, named after a former Celestine convent and church that occupied the site from 1407 to 1789. The first theater was inaugurated in 1792, but it was destroyed by fire in 1871. The current building, designed by Gaspard André, was inaugurated in 1877 and later repaired after another fire in 1880. It has been continually used for over 200 years and is now a municipal theater run by the City of Lyon.

Major_Events.Description: The first theater building was inaugurated on 9 April 1792.
The first theater building was destroyed by fire in 1871.
The current theater building, designed by Gaspard André, was inaugurated on 1 August 1877.
The theater was damaged by fire on the night of 25–26 May 1880, requiring repairs by Gaspard André.
A major rebuild occurred between 2002 and 2005, adding a second auditorium, the Célestine, with a capacity for 130 people.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Gaspard André, the theater features a blend of contemporary and classical architectural elements. The building has undergone several renovations, including repairs after fires and a major rebuild in the early 2000s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Théâtre des Célestins is one of the few theaters in France with over 200 years of continual usage. It has hosted numerous notable actors and productions, contributing significantly to French theater history and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The theater has a contemporary and classical repertoire and produces new works. It is directly run by the City of Lyon and has hosted many famous actors and musicians throughout its history. The site was originally a convent and church of the Celestine order before being converted into a theater.

world knowledge.Name: Iqbal Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Iqbal Stadium, originally known as Lyallpur Stadium, National Stadium, and City Stadium, was established in the early 1970s to accommodate the growing popularity of cricket in Faisalabad. It was renamed Iqbal Stadium in honor of Pakistan's national poet, Muhammad Iqbal. The stadium hosted its first Test match in 1978 between Pakistan and India and has since been a key venue for both international and domestic cricket.

Major_Events.Description: Pakistan v India, marking the first Test match held at the stadium.
Pakistan v India, marking the last Test match held at the stadium.
Pakistan v New Zealand, marking the first One Day International held at the stadium.
Pakistan v Bangladesh, marking the last One Day International held at the stadium.
The stadium underwent renovations on March 11, 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern and well-equipped stadium with 9 cricket pitches, including 4 added in 2016.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Iqbal Stadium is culturally significant as a major cricketing venue in Pakistan, hosting numerous historic matches and being named after the national poet, Muhammad Iqbal. It has been a key site for Pakistan's domestic cricket tournaments and international matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is situated 2 km from the city center and has faced weather-related challenges, including fog and bad light. It has hosted memorable performances and significant cricketing events, including the 2019–20 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy and the 2024–25 Champions One-Day Cup. There are rumors it may host the upcoming Pakistan Super League edition and a Test match against England in October 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Via del Mare
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stadio Ettore Giardiniero - Via del mare, known as Stadio Via del mare, is a multi-purpose stadium in Lecce, Italy. It was built in 1966 and is the home of U.S. Lecce. The stadium replaced the old Stadio Carlo Pranzo and was inaugurated on 11 September 1966. It has undergone several renovations, including in 1976, 1985, and 2019. The stadium was named after Ettore Giardiniero, a former mayor of Lecce, in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated on 11 September 1966 with a friendly match between U.S. Lecce and Spartak Moscow.
The stadium was almost completely rebuilt and capacity greatly increased to 55,000 seats due to Lecce's first promotion to Serie A.
The stadium hosted a speech by Pope John Paul II.
The stadium hosted the Italia Wave festival featuring artists like Lou Reed, Kaiser Chiefs, and Paolo Nutini.
The stadium hosted a friendly match between Lecce and Valencia, won by Valencia 0–3.

Major_Events.Event: Friendly match: Inter vs Real Betis
Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted a friendly match between Inter and Real Betis, won by Inter 1–0.
The stadium hosted a 2018 International Champions Cup match between Inter and Lyon, won by Inter 1–0.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a capacity of 40,670 seats, with red and yellow seats (the colors of U.S. Lecce). It features a grass surface and includes the Curva Nord, Curva Sud, Tribuna, and Distinti sections. The Tribuna Est has an inscription of "U.S. Lecce".
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of U.S. Lecce and for hosting major events, including football matches, concerts, and a speech by Pope John Paul II. It is a symbol of local pride and sports culture in Lecce.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was initially built with a capacity of 16,000 spectators, which was increased to 20,500 in 1976 and then to 55,000 in 1985. The capacity was later reduced to 40,670 seats to ensure all seats were numbered. The stadium was controversially not selected as a venue for the 1990 FIFA World Cup, with funding instead going to the Stadio San Nicola in Bari. In 2007, the press room was named after local journalist Sergio Vantaggiato. On 1 November 2007, a lightning strike during a training session killed Antonio De Giorgi, a U.S. Lecce equipment manager. During the 2009–10 season, the stadium hosted home matches for Gallipoli as their stadium was unfit for Serie B.

world knowledge.Name: Huangpu Stadium
world knowledge.Details: The Huangpu Sports Centre Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium with a capacity of 12,000 people.

image_name: Montagne de Reims Regional Natural Park

world knowledge.Name: Montagne de Reims Regional Natural Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Montagne de Reims Regional Natural Park was officially designated as a regional natural park in 1976. It is organized around the Montagne de Reims, a wooded range of hills covered by vineyards that produce the region's eponymous sparkling wine, Champagne.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its vineyards that produce Champagne, a globally renowned sparkling wine. It is also a protected area aimed at preserving the natural and cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes several communes as members. It is managed by the Fédération des parcs naturels régionaux de France. More information can be found on its official website: www.parc-montagnedereims.fr.

world knowledge.Name: Parc Borély
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parc Borély was created in the 17th century by Joseph Borely, a French ship owner and merchant, who bought land for a country house, Château Borély. The estate was enlarged in the 18th century by Joseph Borély, who constructed a bastide. In the mid-19th century, the land passed to Paulin Talabot and later to the city of Marseille, which commissioned landscape architect Jean-Charles Adolphe Alphand to design the park with three distinct parts. The park has undergone several modifications, including the addition of a promenade in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: Joseph Borely bought land for a country house, Château Borély, and created the initial park.
Joseph Borély expanded the estate and constructed a bastide (Provençal country house).

Major_Events.Event: Design of the park by Jean-Charles Adolphe Alphand
Major_Events.Description: The city of Marseille commissioned Alphand to design the park with three distinct parts: a French garden, an English landscape park, and a horse racing track.
A promenade of two hectares was laid out between the park and the sea.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features three distinct gardens: a Garden à la française with lawns, basins, and rows of trees; an English landscape garden with a lake, statues, fountain, cascade, and playground; and a renovated race track. The park also includes the Château Borély and a former pavilion by the lake.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parc Borély is classified by the French Ministry of Culture as one of the Remarkable Gardens of France. It is a significant green space in Marseille, combining historical, botanical, and recreational elements.
world knowledge.Details: The park adjoins the Jardin botanique E.M. Heckel. It originally housed a botanical garden from 1880 to 1915, which later moved to a different site adjoining the park. The park connects to the sea by a promenade and to the neighboring botanical garden.

world knowledge.Name: Allenby Bridge
world knowledge.Area: Balqa Governorate, Jordan and West Bank, Israel
world knowledge.Address: Near Jericho in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Al-Karameh in Jordan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was first built by the Ottomans in 1885. It was rebuilt by British general Edmund Allenby in 1918. It has been destroyed multiple times, including during the 1927 Jericho earthquake, the Night of the Bridges operation in 1946, and the Six-Day War in 1967. A modern crossing was constructed in 1994 after the Israel-Jordan peace treaty.

Major_Events.Description: The Ottoman government built the first bridge at this site.
British general Edmund Allenby built a bridge over the remnant of the Ottoman predecessor.
The bridge collapsed into the river due to the earthquake.
The bridge was destroyed by the Palmach, severing a main overland connection between Mandatory Palestine and Transjordan.
The bridge was destroyed again during the war and replaced with a temporary truss-type bridge in 1968.
A new modern paved crossing was built adjacent to the older wooden one after the Israel-Jordan peace treaty.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a modern paved crossing constructed in 1994, replacing older wooden and truss-type bridges. It is the lowest fixed water crossing in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant border crossing between the West Bank and Jordan, serving as the sole designated exit/entry point for West Bank Palestinians travelling abroad by land. It is named after British general Edmund Allenby and Jordan's King Hussein.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Border crossing for pedestrians and vehicles between the West Bank and Jordan.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is operated by the Israel Airports Authority on the West Bank side and the Public Security Directorate on the Jordanian side. Israeli citizens are generally not permitted to use the terminal, except for Israeli Muslims performing Hajj or Umrah. The Jordanian side has a branch of the Bank of Jordan for currency exchange. Travel permits from both Israeli and Jordanian authorities are required for Palestinians.

world knowledge.Name: Brooks County Courthouse (Texas)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brooks County Courthouse was built after Brooks County separated from Starr County in 1911. Initially, officials met in rented spaces until the courthouse was constructed in 1914. The courthouse was named after Judge James A. Brooks, who played a key role in the county's formation. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2012 and designated a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1977.

Major_Events.Description: A bond election was held to fund the courthouse and new roads, passing 344 to 9. However, it was not approved due to political issues with precinct 4 voters seeking separation.
After precinct 4 separated to form Jim Hogg County, Brooks County voters approved the bond issue again, leading to the courthouse's construction.
The courthouse's opening was celebrated with a public picnic and a parade led by the local high school band, honoring Judge James A. Brooks.
The courthouse was recognized for its historical significance in Texas.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its architectural and historical importance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Classical Revival style, designed by Alfred Giles, built by Westlake & Mizell.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a symbol of Brooks County's formation and governance, honoring Judge James A. Brooks, a key figure in its creation. Its architectural design and historical role make it a significant landmark.
world knowledge.Details: Renovation began on the courthouse in 2006. The structure was initially planned by architect Atlee B. Ayres before Alfred Giles was selected for the final design.

world knowledge.Name: Tenno Beach
world knowledge.Address: Suzaki neighborhood, Shimoda city, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Suzaki Imperial Villa was acquired by the Imperial Household Agency after the Numazu Imperial Villa was given to the city of Numazu. It is located on the west bank of Sagami Bay at the southern tip of Izu Peninsula near where the waters of the bay mix with the Kuroshio Current offshore. The Villa was the location of a marine biology laboratory managed by Emperor Shōwa, who used to visit it for some ten days in spring, summer and winter, and complemented the similar laboratory he operated at the Hayama Imperial Villa on the opposite side of the bay.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: One-story building of western architectural design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The villa is a residence owned by the Japanese Imperial Family, and used on infrequent intervals as an informal summer retreat. Research from the laboratory has resulted in a number of technical monographs.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Informal summer retreat for the Japanese Imperial Family and marine biology research.
world knowledge.Details: The adjacent private beach is informally known as Tenno Beach, or Emperor Beach. The bay is not deep, providing safety for the Emperor's family. The beach is surrounded by beautiful rock formations, which further limits public access.

world knowledge.Name: International Finance Centre (Hong Kong)
world knowledge.Address: 8 Finance Street Central, Hong Kong, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The International Finance Centre (IFC) is a skyscraper and integrated commercial development on the waterfront of Hong Kong's Central District. It consists of two skyscrapers (1 IFC and 2 IFC), the IFC mall, and the Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong. 2 IFC is the second-tallest building in Hong Kong and the 38th-tallest building in the world. The development was constructed and is owned by IFC Development, a consortium of Sun Hung Kai Properties, Henderson Land, and Towngas.

Major_Events.Description: One International Finance Centre was opened on 6 July 1998, towards the end of the Asian financial crisis.
Two International Finance Centre was completed on 18 October 2003, at the height of the SARS epidemic.

Financial Times, HSBC, and Cathay Pacific put up an advertisement on the facade that stretched more than 50 storeys, covering an area of 19,000 m² (200,000 sq ft) and a length of 230 m, making it the world's largest advertisement ever put on a skyscraper.
The Four Seasons Hotel was completed and opened in October 2005. It is the only Four Seasons Hotel in Hong Kong.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: IFC consists of two skyscrapers: 1 IFC (210 m tall, 39 stories) and 2 IFC (412 m tall, 88 storeys). The buildings feature advanced telecommunications, raised floors for flexible cabling management, and nearly column-free floor plans. 2 IFC is one of relatively few buildings in the world equipped with double-deck elevators. The design is by César Pelli & Association Architects, with structural engineering by Ove Arup & Partners.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: IFC is a prominent landmark on Hong Kong Island and a symbol of the city's financial prowess. The building's floor numbers omit inauspicious numbers like 14 and 24 due to Cantonese cultural beliefs. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority Information Centre on the 55th floor showcases Hong Kong's monetary history and is open to the public.

Details.Tenants: Banco Santander, BNP Paribas, Citadel, UBS, and many other financial institutions.
Details.Hotel: Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong, with 399 guest suites and 519 serviced apartments.
Details.Mall: IFC Mall, a 4-storey luxury shopping mall with brands like Lane Crawford and Apple Store.
Details.Film Appearances: Featured in films like 'Lara Croft: Tomb Raider – The Cradle of Life', 'The Dark Knight', and 'Godzilla vs Kong'.

world knowledge.Name: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
world knowledge.Address: Near the northeast corner of the city of Pyongyang, North Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, originally built as the Kumsusan Assembly Hall in 1976, served as the official residence of Kim Il Sung, the founder of North Korea. After his death in 1994, it was renovated into a mausoleum to house his preserved body. Following the death of Kim Jong Il in 2011, his remains were also placed in the palace. The building was renamed in 2012 and serves as a national landmark and memorial.

Major_Events.Description: Kim Il Sung died of a heart attack, and his body was embalmed and placed in the palace.
The palace was converted into a mausoleum for Kim Il Sung at an estimated cost of $100 million to $900 million.
Kim Jong Il died, and his body was later embalmed and placed in the palace alongside his father.
The building was formally renamed the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun on the 70th anniversary of Kim Jong Il's birth.
The palace was reopened to the public after months of renovations, featuring new exhibits and a park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern and neoclassical architectural style. The building features long halls (some up to 1 kilometer in length), marble columns, and a large front square. The interior includes travelators, a dust-blowing machine, and glass sarcophagi for the preserved remains.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is the largest mausoleum dedicated to a Communist leader and the only one housing multiple individuals. It symbolizes the eternal leadership of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il in North Korea and is a central site for national rallies and mourning.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mausoleum and memorial for Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, as well as a national landmark and tourist site.
world knowledge.Details: The palace includes exhibits of personal belongings, awards, and gifts received by Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il. Foreign visitors can only access the palace on official government tours. Photography and smoking are prohibited inside. The palace grounds include a park and flower garden, open to locals and visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Kardinia Park (stadium)
world knowledge.Address: Kardinia Park, South Geelong, Victoria, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kardinia Park has been a sporting venue since the 19th century, initially as a secondary football ground in Geelong. It became the primary home of the Geelong Football Club in 1941 after Corio Oval was commandeered during World War II. Over the years, it has undergone multiple redevelopments to become a modern stadium with a capacity of 40,000.

Major_Events.Description: Kardinia Park hosted its first AFL Final, a qualifying final between Geelong and Fremantle Dockers.
The stadium hosted its first international cricket match, a T20 between Australia and Sri Lanka.
The first stadium concert in Australia post-COVID-19 pandemic, attended by 30,000 fans.
The Dalai Lama visited the stadium, with a subsequent visit in 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features multiple grandstands including the Reg Hickey Stand, Players Stand, Premiership Stand, Brownlow Stand, and Joel Selwood Stand. It has undergone extensive redevelopment over two decades, costing A$340 million, to increase capacity and modernize facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kardinia Park is a significant sporting and cultural hub in regional Australia, known as the home ground of the Geelong Football Club. It hosts major events in AFL, cricket, soccer, and concerts, contributing significantly to the local economy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for sports (AFL, cricket, soccer) and entertainment events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is nicknamed 'The Cattery' by fans. It has a reputation as a challenging venue for visiting teams due to Geelong's strong home record. The redevelopment has been nicknamed 'Pork Barrel Park' due to political funding controversies. The stadium is currently named GMHBA Stadium due to naming rights.

world knowledge.Name: Ikon Park (stadium)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Princes Park, also known as Ikon Park, is a historic Australian rules football ground located in Carlton North, Melbourne. It was Carlton Football Club's VFL/AFL home ground from 1897. The ground has hosted numerous significant events, including VFL grand finals during World War II and the inaugural AFL Women's match in 2017. Over the years, it has undergone several redevelopments, including the construction of stands and modern training facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The grand final between Carlton and South Melbourne attracted a record crowd of 62,986.
The match between Carlton and Collingwood attracted a capacity crowd of 24,568.
The Western Bulldogs defeated Brisbane 27 to 21 in front of a crowd of 7,083.
Brisbane defeated North Melbourne 44 to 27 in front of a crowd of 12,616.

Major_Events.Event: Second Ashes test of the 1992 Great Britain Lions tour
Major_Events.Description: The visitors defeated Australia 33–10.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The ground features several stands, including the Alderman Gardiner Stand (completed in stages between 1909 and 1913) and the Robert Heatley Stand (opened in 1932). The Legends Stand, completed in 1997, features a curved modern roof structure. The venue has undergone modern renovations, including an indoor training facility and administration building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Princes Park is culturally significant as one of Melbourne's historic suburban football grounds and the long-time home of the Carlton Football Club. It played a key role in the development of Australian rules football and has hosted numerous significant matches, including VFL grand finals and the inaugural AFL Women's game. The ground is also notable for its contributions to women's football and community sports.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Australian rules football ground, also used for cricket, rugby, and other sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The ground has been known by several names due to naming rights deals, including Optus Oval, MC Labour Park, Visy Park, and currently Ikon Park. It has hosted various sports, including cricket, rugby league, and association football. Public transport to the venue is primarily by tram along Royal Parade or Lygon St. The venue has undergone significant redevelopments, including upgrades for women's football facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Subic Bay International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Naval Air Station Cubi Point, it was part of the Subic Naval Base of the United States Navy. The U.S. Navy initiated the project in 1950 to enhance Seventh Fleet capabilities. It was commissioned on 25 July 1956 and turned over to the Philippine government in November 1992 after the U.S. withdrawal. It was converted to an international airport in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: The $100 million facility was commissioned, comprising an air station with an adjacent pier capable of docking the Navy's largest carriers.
The eruption buried Cubi Point in 18–36 inches of ash, leading to the U.S. withdrawal and the eventual turnover of the facility to the Philippine government.
The airport ushered in its first commercial flight from Taiwan via Makung.
NAS Cubi Point was converted to Cubi Point International Airport.

Major_Events.Event: Formal opening of Subic Bay International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was formally opened on 30 September 1996.
FedEx Express relocated its hub to Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport in China.
The airport was used for repatriation flights of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW) facilitated by Philippine Airlines.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a 2,744-meter-long asphalt runway and a passenger terminal capable of handling 6 million passengers per year.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is historically significant as a former U.S. naval air station and now serves as a key transportation hub in the region, supporting both commercial and military operations.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is also a base for the flight school Aeroflite Aviation Corp since 2006. It hosted a number of wide-bodied aircraft during the seventh APEC Summit in 1996. In 2022, the government established Naval Operating Base Subic, enhancing its role in territorial disputes in the South China Sea.

world knowledge.Name: Friedrichs Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Friedrichs Bridge is a bridge in Berlin, one of several crossing the Spree between Museum Island and the mainland portion of Mitte. Since its creation in 1703, the bridge has been repeatedly renovated. It is considered a protected monument.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is considered a protected monument.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge connecting Museum Island and Mitte
world knowledge.Details: This article about a bridge in Germany is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it. This article about a Berlin building or structure is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Gandhara University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gandhara University is a private university chartered by the Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It was the first private medical university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, founded in October 1995 by surgeon Muhammad Kabir. The university provides specialized training in the health sciences and is recognized by the Higher Education Commission (Pakistan) and accredited by the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gandhara University is culturally and historically significant as the first private medical university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, contributing to the advancement of health sciences education in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university encompasses specialized departments for teaching in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, paramedical technologies, nursing, physiotherapy, and public health. It is affiliated with the College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan for postgraduate dental courses. The Journal of Gandhara Medical and Dental Sciences (JGMDS) is recognized by the Higher Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan, and is the official journal of Gandhara University.

world knowledge.Name: Valère Basilica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Valère Basilica, also known as Valère castle, is a fortified Roman Catholic church located on a hill in Sion, Switzerland. It was built between the 12th and 13th centuries and has served as a significant religious and administrative center. The site was included in the Federal Inventory of Sites and Monuments of National Importance in 1977. The basilica obtained the rank of minor basilica in 1987 during the visit of Pope John Paul II.

Major_Events.Description: The site was included in the Federal Inventory of Sites and Monuments of National Importance due to the large number of protected species present on Valère Hill.
The church obtained the rank of minor basilica in the Roman Catholic tradition during the visit of Pope John Paul II.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The basilica combines Romanesque and Gothic architectural styles. It features a semi-circular apse, Gothic ribbed vaults, a rood screen, and a famous pipe organ from 1435. The structure includes larch wood elements and a Gothic marble statue of the Madonna with the baby Jesus.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valère Basilica is culturally significant as a representation of the spiritual and secular power of the Prince-Bishops of Sion. It is also notable for its historical architecture and the preservation of its ancient pipe organ, one of the oldest functioning in the world.
world knowledge.Details: The basilica is situated on Valère Hill at 615 meters above sea level, facing the Château de Tourbillon. It is surrounded by a fortified village and walls. The site is home to various protected species of flora and fauna. The pipe organ, believed to have been built in 1435, is arranged to resemble a church and remains largely unchanged since its construction.

world knowledge.Name: Austin–Bergstrom International Airport
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1942 (as Bergstrom Air Force Base), converted to civilian airport in 1999
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The airport lies on the site of Bergstrom Air Force Base, named after Captain John August Earl Bergstrom, an officer who was the first person from Austin to be killed in World War II. The base was decommissioned in the early 1990s, and the land reverted to the city, which used it to replace Robert Mueller Municipal Airport as Austin's main airport in 1999.

Major_Events.Description: Austin–Bergstrom International Airport opened to the public on May 23, 1999, replacing Robert Mueller Municipal Airport.
British Airways inaugurated a flight to London's Heathrow Airport, the airport's first scheduled transatlantic service.
A three-gate South Terminal opened on April 13, 2017, built by a private company, LoneStar Airport Holdings, under a 40-year lease.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Barbara Jordan passenger terminal was originally conceived as an 18-gate terminal facility with a footprint of a bit more than 500,000 square feet (46,000 m2). It has since been expanded to include 34 gates, six of which are capable of handling international flights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a significant transportation hub for the Greater Austin metropolitan area and reflects the city's growth and economic importance. The terminal features a live music stage, aligning with Austin's reputation as "The Live Music Capital of the World".
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving commercial, cargo, and general aviation needs.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is undergoing a major expansion program, entitled "Journey With AUS", to accommodate rapid growth in travel demand. Plans include a new arrivals and departures hall and the construction of Concourse B with 20 gates, expandable to 40 in the future. The airport also has a secondary terminal, the South Terminal, used by ultra-low-cost carriers.

world knowledge.Name: Hornby Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: South Head, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hornby Lighthouse, also known as South Head Lower Light or South Head Signal Station, was constructed in 1858 following the loss of two ships, the Dunbar in August 1857 and the Catherine Adamson in October 1857. It was designed by Mortimer Lewis and is the third oldest lighthouse in New South Wales. The lighthouse has been in continuous use since the 1840s as a controlling point for shipping entering and leaving Port Jackson.

Major_Events.Description: Built to prevent further shipwrecks after the loss of the Dunbar and Catherine Adamson.
The lighthouse was automated and demanned.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service
Major_Events.Description: Following classification by the National Trust in 1975, the site was transferred from the Army to the NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on NSW State Heritage Register
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: A solid sandstone tower with connected watch keepers quarters, octagonal in plan with four levels and a basement. The tower features a cantilevered iron and timber catwalk and a metal pitched roof with an observation fleche. The staff quarters are in an 'I' plan with enclosed verandahs, constructed from locally quarried sandstone with timber verandahs and picket fences. The tower is painted with distinctive red and white vertical stripes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A dominant Sydney landmark and the site of the first navigational beacon in Australia, providing warning to mariners. It is an important example of early Victorian public work associated with port activities and has been in continuous use since the 1840s.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Lighthouse and signal station for controlling shipping entering and leaving Port Jackson.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is operated by the Sydney Ports Corporation, while the site is managed by the NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service as part of the Sydney Harbour National Park. The site is open to the public, but the tower itself is closed. The light's current characteristic is a white light showing two seconds on, three seconds off, visible for 15 nautical miles.

world knowledge.Name: Yangmingshan
world knowledge.Area: Taipei and New Taipei City, Taiwan
world knowledge.Address: Majority of park within Taipei city limits; partially in Beitou and Shilin Districts (Taipei), and Wanli, Jinshan, Sanzhi, and Tamsui Districts (New Taipei)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called 'Grass Mountain' during the Qing Dynasty due to sulfur theft prevention tactics. Renamed Yangmingshan in 1950 to honor Ming Dynasty scholar Wang Yangming. Initially planned in 1962 as Taiwan's first national park (Daiton National Park) during Japanese rule in 1937.

Major_Events.Description: Taiwan's first national park, designated during Japanese rule.
President Chiang Kai-shek renamed Grass Mountain to honor Wang Yangming.
Initial planning covered 28,400 hectares, including Mount Kwan-in and Tatun Volcanic Group.
Yangmingshan National Park was officially established.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural volcanic landscape with andesite rocks, featuring ridges, valleys, lakes, waterfalls, basins, fumaroles, sulfur deposits, and hot springs. Notable geological sites include Xiaoyoukeng's 'landslide terrain' and Seven Star Mountain (dormant volcano).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Symbolizes Taiwan's volcanic geology and biodiversity. Commemorates Wang Yangming's philosophical legacy. A key site for cherry blossoms, hiking, and hot springs, blending ecological and cultural tourism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: National park for conservation, recreation, and education.

Details.Flora_and_Fauna: 1,360 vascular plant species (e.g., Taiwan isoetes), 168 butterfly species, 122 bird species. Semi-feral cattle are a notable attraction.
Details.Climate: Humid subtropical (Köppen: Cfa) with cool, foggy winters and warm, stormy summers. Affected by typhoons (June–October).
Details.Trails_and_Attractions: Hiking trails to Seven Star Mountain (1,120 m), Xiaoyoukeng's fumaroles, Menghuan Pond, Lengshuikeng, and sulfur hot springs.
Details.Governance: Managed by Yangmingshan National Park Headquarters (National Park Service).

world knowledge.Name: Cosmosphere
world knowledge.Address: 1100 North Plum Street, Hutchinson, KS 67501, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cosmosphere grew from a planetarium established on the Kansas State Fairgrounds in 1962. It is now an international science education center and space museum housing the largest combined collection of US and Russian spaceflight artifacts in the world.

Major_Events.Description: The Carey Digital Dome Theater upgraded from IMAX to 4K digital projection system.
The Justice Planetarium transitioned from an optical starball projection system to the Spitz Sci-Dome XD digital projection system.
Three of the museum's oldest galleries (German Gallery, Redstone and Sputnik Gallery, and Kennedy Theater) began renovations, including repainting and updating exhibits with new graphics and sound.

A routine audit revealed missing items, leading to the indictment of former director Max Ary for stealing and selling artifacts for personal profit. Ary was convicted in 2005 and sentenced to three years in prison.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The facility includes the Hall of Space Museum, Justice Planetarium, Carey Digital Dome Theater, Dr. Goddard's Lab, and CosmoKids. The exterior features authentic Redstone and Titan II launch vehicles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cosmosphere is the only Smithsonian affiliate museum in Kansas and houses the largest collection of Russian space artifacts outside of Moscow. It plays a significant role in space education and preservation of spaceflight history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Space Museum and International Science Education Center
world knowledge.Details: The Cosmosphere's SpaceWorks division has restored flown U.S. spacecraft for museums globally, including artifacts for the Smithsonian. It built props for movies like Apollo 13 and TV series like From the Earth to the Moon. The museum's collection includes a Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird, Liberty Bell 7, Gemini 10 space capsule, and Apollo 13 Command Module Odyssey. A Moon rock from Apollo 11 is also on display.

image_name: Sierra de San Pedro Mártir National Park

world knowledge.Name: Sierra de San Pedro Mártir National Park
world knowledge.Address: Ensenada Municipality, Mexicali Municipality, Baja California, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sierra de San Pedro Mártir National Park is a national park in the Mexican state of Baja California. The area was first explored by Native people and later by Europeans in 1701 by Eusebio Francisco Kino under Dominican orders. The park was officially created by decree on April 26, 1947, and is known for its pine trees, granite rock formations, and the highest peak in Baja California, Picacho del Diablo.

Major_Events.Description: The park was officially created by decree on April 26, 1947, with 72,909 hectares set aside and declared protected by the Mexican Federal government.
Captive-born California condors were re-introduced to the wild in the Sierra San Pedro Martir, the first time they have been seen in the range since 1937.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features rugged mountain ranges with drastic topological changes, covered with pine forests and surrounded by large deserts. It includes the highest peak in Baja California, Picacho del Diablo, and several deep canyons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its historical exploration by Jesuit and Dominican orders, its unique flora and fauna, and its role in the re-introduction of the California condor. It also houses the National Astronomical Observatory, which is the second most important in Latin America.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to the National Astronomical Observatory, built in 1971, which houses Mexico's largest optical telescope. The park's diverse ecosystems include coniferous forests, chaparral, and desert shrub, and it supports a variety of wildlife including mule deer, bighorn sheep, and the California condor.

world knowledge.Name: Reading Blue Coat School
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1646 by Richard Aldworth as 'Aldworth's Hospital' to educate poor male children. Initially located in Reading, it moved to Holme Park, Sonning, in 1947. The school evolved from a charity institution to a modern co-educational private school.

Major_Events.Description: Richard Aldworth founded the school with a bequest of £4,000 to educate poor male children.
The school relocated to Holme Park, Sonning, due to post-war educational reforms and expansion needs.
A new classroom block with modern facilities and environmental features was opened.

Major_Events.Event: Poppy Planting at Tower of London
Major_Events.Description: A pupil planted the last poppy in the 'Blood Swept Lands and Seas of Red' installation commemorating WWI.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The school features a mix of historic and modern buildings, including the Holme Park mansion, the Richard Aldworth Building (with ground-source heat pumps and rainwater recycling), and a sports hall. Traditional Bluecoat attire (gown, yellow stockings, buckled shoes) was originally worn.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the oldest schools in England, with deep roots in charitable education and Anglican tradition. It reflects the evolution of British educational institutions from the 17th century to the present.
Notable_Visitors: The Rt. Hon. Theresa May MP

Details.Houses: Aldworth, Hall, Malthus, Norwood, Rich, West
Controversies: Convictions of former staff members for historical sexual abuse and indecent offenses.
Details.Film_Locations: Used for films, documentaries, and TV programmes.

world knowledge.Name: Princess Juliana International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Near Simpson Bay Lagoon, Sint Maarten
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a US military airstrip in 1942, it became a commercial airport in 1943. Named after Queen Juliana of the Netherlands, who landed there in 1944. The airport has undergone several renovations and modernizations since its inception.

Major_Events.Description: The first commercial flight landed on 3 December 1943.
Queen Juliana of the Netherlands visited the island using the airport.
The airport suffered significant damage when Hurricane Irma struck the island as a Category 5 hurricane.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern terminal building with 30,500 square metres of floor space, 46 check-in desks, 10 transit desks, and 13 boarding gates. It includes 20 immigration booths and five exit-control booths.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a major gateway for the smaller Leeward Islands and is famous for its low-altitude flyover landing approaches over Maho Beach, making it a popular spot for plane-spotters.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as a hub for Winair and is equipped with VOR/DME and NDB. It has a single runway measuring 7,546 by 148 feet and operates daily from 07:00 to 21:00.

world knowledge.Name: Schauspielhaus Wuppertal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Schauspielhaus Wuppertal was a theatre for plays in Wuppertal, Germany. It was opened in 1966 and closed in 2013. The theatre was built after all theatres in Wuppertal were damaged in World War II. It was designed by Gerhard Graubner and initially had 745 seats. Due to financial constraints, it was later reduced to 135 seats and eventually closed.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was opened with performances of Gotthold Ephraim Lessing's 'Nathan der Weise' and Else Lasker-Schüler's 'Die Wupper'. Heinrich Böll delivered a speech titled 'Die Freiheit der Kunst' (Freedom in the art) during the inauguration in the presence of president Heinrich Lübke.
Due to major repair needs, the theatre was reduced to a 135-seat studio theatre called 'Kleines Schauspielhaus' operating in the foyer.
The theatre was permanently closed on 30 June 2013 after protests by citizens delayed the closure. The last performance was held on this date.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is structured in three elements, following its functions. The building is symmetrical in layers of different height with white walls accented by a 'Fensterband', a horizontal arrangement of narrow windows. The entrance hall is on the ground floor, including two atriums with Japanese gardens. The great hall is above it, with slightly curved outer walls and seats arranged in 20 rows in the style of an amphitheatre. The stage house is a high cube situated next to the river Wupper.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Schauspielhaus Wuppertal was a significant cultural venue in Wuppertal, hosting plays, operas, and productions by the Tanztheater Wuppertal created by Pina Bausch. It was also protected as an architectural monument since June 2000.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre for plays, later also hosting opera and dance theatre productions.
world knowledge.Details: The building has been considered for further use as an international archive for the dance theatre or an extension of the Von der Heydt Museum, but this depends on major renovation funding. The theatre was closed due to financial constraints and the inability to fund necessary repairs.

world knowledge.Name: Wales Millennium Centre
world knowledge.Address: Bute Place, Cardiff Bay, Cardiff, Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wales Millennium Centre is Wales' national arts centre located in the Cardiff Bay area of Cardiff, Wales. It was conceived to replace the Cardiff Bay Opera House project, which was rejected due to funding issues. The centre was designed to reflect Welsh culture and was funded through a combination of public and private sources, including a significant donation from South African businessman Donald Gordon.

Major_Events.Description: The centre was officially opened during the weekend of 26–28 November 2004, with a series of events including speeches, performances, and a fireworks display. The opening was attended by notable figures such as Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, and the Prince of Wales.
Phase 2 of the centre, which includes the BBC Hoddinott Hall, opened on 22 January 2009 with an inaugural concert performed by the BBC National Orchestra of Wales.
A refurbishment of Phase 1 included the opening of an immersive theatre space called Bocs, a redesigned foyer, and new ticketing office, among other improvements.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed by Jonathan Adams of Percy Thomas Architects, with Arup Acoustics as the acoustic designer. The exterior is clad in multi-coloured Welsh slate, and the interior features hardwood bands, glass, and steel. The design reflects Welsh materials and culture, with a focus on natural textures and local materials.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wales Millennium Centre is a symbol of Welsh culture and arts, housing eight arts organisations and serving as a venue for opera, ballet, contemporary dance, and musicals. It is a major cultural hub in Wales and a significant landmark in Cardiff Bay.
world knowledge.Details: The centre comprises several performance spaces, including the Donald Gordon Theatre, BBC Hoddinott Hall, and Weston Studio Theatre. It also houses rehearsal rooms, dance studios, and function rooms. The building's design incorporates Welsh slate, steel, wood, and glass, reflecting the natural landscape and industrial heritage of Wales.

world knowledge.Name: Juhu beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Juhu was originally an island in the nineteenth century, inhabited by Agris, Kunbis, Koli people, and Goans. The Portuguese called it 'Juvem' and built the Church of St. Joseph in 1853. It became a prominent area with the development of Juhu Beach and Juhu Aerodrome, India's first civil aviation airport. The area is now known for its affluence and as a hub for Bollywood celebrities.

Major_Events.Event: Maiden voyage of J. R. D. Tata
Major_Events.Description: J. R. D. Tata made his maiden voyage to Juhu Airport from Drigh Road airstrip, Karachi, via Ahmedabad, carrying mail in a Puss Moth aircraft.
Mahatma Gandhi visited Juhu Beach during the Indian independence movement. A statue of him was installed, and a lane was named Gandhigram Road in his honor.
A group of terror suspects detonated a bomb in a Juhu hotel, among other locations.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Juhu is culturally significant as a historic and affluent suburb of Mumbai, home to many Bollywood celebrities and business elites. It is also known for Juhu Beach, a popular tourist destination and site for the annual Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. The area has historical ties to India's civil aviation and independence movement.

Details.Climate: Uniform throughout the year, with summers reaching 35°C (95°F) and winters remaining hot. Monsoons occur from mid-June to September.
Details.Cuisine: Known for 'Mumbai style' street food like bhelpuri, pani puri, and sev puri at the beach food court.

world knowledge.Name: Parque El Ejido
world knowledge.Address: Avenue Patria, Itchimbía neighborhood, Old Centre, Quito, Ecuador
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parque El Ejido was established as public property for grazing horses and cattle after the Spanish foundation of Quito. It served as a firing squad and punishment ground from the 16th to early 20th centuries. In 1922, it was officially turned into a recreational green space named 'Parque de Mayo' to celebrate the centenary of the Battle of Pichincha. It is now known as Parque El Ejido and is the third-largest park in Quito.

Major_Events.Description: An angry mob burned the bodies of President Eloy Alfaro and three of his followers after dragging them through the streets.
The exterior perimeter of the park was rehabilitated for the Habitat III Conference, including improvements to access routes, pavements, and lighting.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park's design follows late 19th and early 20th-century European urbanism, with an asymmetrical layout of curved pathways meeting in an eccentric circle at the center. It features a trapezoidal shape and is surrounded by four road arteries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parque El Ejido is culturally significant as a historical site that has evolved from a grazing area and punishment ground to a major recreational space. It is part of the Quito Historic Center, a World Heritage Site, and hosts exhibitions, traditional games, and cultural performances.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to 1,470 species of native plants and has a high concentration of heritage trees. It features an open-air gallery for art and handicrafts, sports courts for traditional games, and areas for children's games. The park also has an open-air food court serving traditional Ecuadorian dishes.

world knowledge.Name: University of Zimbabwe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Zimbabwe (UZ) is a public university in Harare, Zimbabwe. It was opened in 1952 as the University College of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, and was initially affiliated with the University of London. It was later renamed the University of Rhodesia, and adopted its present name upon Zimbabwe's independence in 1980. UZ is the oldest university in Zimbabwe.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established as the University College of Rhodesia and Nyasaland.
The university was renamed University of Zimbabwe upon Zimbabwe's independence.
Thousands of students protested the arrests of two student leaders, leading to clashes with riot police and mass arrests.
The university hosted the Eighth Assembly of the World Council of Churches.
Grace Mugabe was awarded a doctorate in sociology under controversial circumstances, leading to widespread criticism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus spans 299 hectares in the affluent Mount Pleasant suburb, featuring 171 buildings including academic facilities, student residence halls, staff housing, and sporting facilities. The campus includes a seasonal wetland and the College Green, a popular site for social events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Zimbabwe is the oldest and most prestigious university in Zimbabwe, playing a crucial role in the country's higher education and research. It has been a center for academic and political discourse, particularly during significant historical events such as Zimbabwe's independence and subsequent political changes.
world knowledge.Details: The university has eleven faculties offering a wide variety of degree programmes and many specialist research centres and institutes. It has faced criticism for awarding fraudulent degrees to members of the Robert Mugabe regime, most notably First Lady Grace Mugabe. The university has also been a site of significant student protests and political activism.

world knowledge.Name: Shah Amanat Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 950 m (3,117 ft) long, 24.47 m (80 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shah Amanat Bridge is the second bridge constructed across the Karnaphuli River in Bangladesh and the first major extradosed bridge in the country. It connects the southern parts of Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, and the hilly district of Bandarban. It is named after Chittagong's 18th-century Islamic Saint Shah Amanat.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on 8 September 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Extradosed bridge design, prestressed concrete material, 950 m long, 24.47 m wide, with five piers, three 200 m extradosed main spans, two 115 m side spans, and a 130 m approach viaduct section. It includes four lanes for vehicles, two 1.5 m lanes for manual transports, and 1.5 m walkways on each side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named after Chittagong's 18th-century Islamic Saint Shah Amanat and is a significant infrastructure project in Bangladesh, connecting key regions and facilitating transportation.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was constructed by China Major Bridge Construction at a cost of Taka 590 crore, including a foreign exchange component of Taka 3.72 billion provided by the Kuwait Fund. It has a 0.5 km approach road in the city end and one km approach road at the Patiya end.

world knowledge.Name: Maine State Music Theatre
world knowledge.Address: 1 Bath Road, Brunswick, Maine, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded as Brunswick Music Theatre (BMT) in 1959 by Victoria Crandall, it became Maine State Music Theatre (MSMT) in 1988 to reflect its statewide influence. It is one of the few remaining musical theatres in New England. MSMT remained committed to Brunswick despite opportunities to relocate, purchasing and renovating the Maine Line Bus Garage in 2000s for administrative and technical facilities. The theatre survived the COVID-19 pandemic with community support.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Maine State Music Theatre
Major_Events.Description: Changed from Brunswick Music Theatre to reflect statewide influence.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase of Maine Line Bus Garage
Major_Events.Description: Renovated into administrative offices, rehearsal spaces, and technical facilities.
First canceled season in 2020, followed by limited events in 2021. Full return in 2022.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the few remaining professional musical theatres in New England, contributing to regional arts and nurturing emerging theatre artists through its Educational Fellowship Program.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Regional theatre producing musicals, concerts, and Theatre for Young Audiences series.
world knowledge.Details: MSMT operates a costume rental branch (MSMT Costumes) since 2010, including costumes from the original West End production of Spamalot. It has a capacity of 598 and presents a summer season of four musicals.

world knowledge.Name: Madeira Botanical Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Madeira Botanical Garden (Portuguese: Jardim Botânico da Madeira) is a botanical garden in Funchal, Madeira, opened to the public in 1960. The area was previously part of an estate belonging to the family of William Reid, founder of Reid's Hotel.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden is divided into six areas: Arboretum is located in the north part of the Garden, succulent plants in centre-east, agro-industrial plants in the center, palm trees in the south. Remaining parts of the Garden are covered with flowers and other flora species.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gardens include a bird park (Louro Bird Park) and a three-room Natural History Museum. There is a collection of around 300 exotic birds, including Blue and Yellow Macaw, Cockatoo, Parrots and Lory in the exotic bird park.
world knowledge.Details: The garden receives more than 345,000 visitors per year. Website: ifcn.madeira.gov.pt

world knowledge.Name: Theatro José de Alencar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Theatro José de Alencar was officially opened on June 17, 1910. Its cornerstone was laid in 1896, but the original design was not realized. Construction was authorized in 1904, and works officially started in 1908. Cast iron parts of the theater structure were imported from Glasgow, Scotland. The theater underwent reforms in 1974-1975 and 1989-1990, including the addition of an annex building. It was listed as a historic structure by the National Historic and Artistic Heritage Institute in 1975.

Major_Events.Description: The cornerstone was laid in the center of the square of the Marquis Herval (today square José de Alencar), but the original design was not realized.
Construction of the Theatro José de Alencar was officially authorized by law 768 of August 20.
Works officially started on June 6, 1908.
The theater was officially opened on June 17, 1910.
The theater garden, imagined by Captain Bernardo José de Mello, was built during a reform that lasted from 1974 to April 1975.
The annex building was incorporated into the Theatro José de Alencar during a pension reform from 1989 to 1990.
The theater was listed as a historic structure by the National Historic and Artistic Heritage Institute on November 17, 1975.
