world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater features eclectic architecture in the Art Nouveau style. It includes a 120-seat auditorium, foyer, stage space, and an annex building. Cast iron parts of the structure were imported from the Saracen Foundry in Glasgow, Scotland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Theatro José de Alencar is a significant cultural landmark in Brazil, showcasing Art Nouveau architecture and serving as a hub for performing arts. It houses various cultural institutions and spaces, including the Center for the Arts Scenic, Teatro Morro do Ouro, and the Chamber Orchestra of Eleazar de Carvalho. Its historic listing underscores its importance to Brazil's cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The theater complex includes the Teatro Morro do Ouro (capacity for 90 people), the square Mestre Pedro Boca Rica (outdoor stage and seating for 600 people), the Chamber's Carlos, Gallery Cotoco Ramos, four study rooms and tests, cenotécnica workshops, costume and lighting workshops, the College of Dance of Ceará, the College of Theater Director, Office of Sea Dragon, the Chamber Orchestra of Eleazar de Carvalho, and the course Fundamentals of Theater.

world knowledge.Name: National Palace (Guatemala)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palacio Nacional de la Cultura, also known as "Palacio Verde", is a significant symbol of Guatemala City. It was the most important building in Guatemala and served as the headquarters of the president. The building is the origin of all the roads in the Republic and features a spot known as Kilometro Cero (Kilometer Zero). It is currently a museum and is used for important government acts. The first Government House was built in 1528, and the current palace was inaugurated on November 10, 1943.

Major_Events.Description: The National Palace was completed and inaugurated on November 10, 1943.
The building survived the earthquake of February 4, 1976, which had a magnitude of 7.5 on the Richter scale.
On March 23, 1982, young officers from the Guatemalan Army deposed President Fernando Romeo Lucas García and replaced him with General Efraín Ríos Montt.
On June 30, 1982, General Ríos Montt established special jurisdiction tribunals to judge leftist criminals, which were headquartered in the National Palace.
General Óscar Humberto Mejía Víctores led a coup d'état that deposed General Ríos Montt on August 8, 1983, ending the special tribunals.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The National Palace features a blend of Spanish Baroque and Spanish Renaissance architectural styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Palace is a symbol of Guatemala City and has played a central role in the country's political history. It is the origin point for all roads in the Republic and is a site of significant cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The building is also known as "Palacio Verde" and is currently used as a museum and for important government acts.

world knowledge.Name: Celtic Park
world knowledge.Address: The Celtic Way Parkhead, Glasgow, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Celtic Park, also known as Parkhead or Paradise, is the home of Celtic Football Club. It was originally opened in 1888, but moved to its current location in 1892 due to increased rent. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including a major rebuild between 1994 and 1998 to comply with the Taylor Report, which mandated all-seater stadia for major clubs. Celtic Park is the largest football stadium in Scotland and the eighth-largest in the United Kingdom.

Major_Events.Description: Record attendance of 83,500 set on 1 January 1938.
Hosted the opening ceremony of the 2014 Commonwealth Games.
Hosted the Pro14 final between Leinster and Glasgow, the first rugby union match played at the stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Celtic Park is a rectangular stadium with a capacity of 60,411. It features four stands: North, Jock Stein (West), Lisbon Lions (East), and Main (South) Stands. The North Stand is notable for its cantilevered upper tier over a cemetery. The Main Stand, originally built in 1929, is the oldest part of the stadium and has undergone several renovations, including a new roof in 1971 and a facade rebuild in 1988.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Celtic Park is culturally significant as the home of Celtic Football Club, a club with deep roots in the Irish immigrant community in Scotland. The stadium is known as 'Paradise' by fans and has hosted numerous significant football matches, concerts, and other events. It is a symbol of the club's history and success, particularly under the management of Jock Stein in the 1960s and 1970s.
world knowledge.Details: Celtic Park has been used for various events beyond football, including concerts, religious gatherings, and the opening ceremony of the 2014 Commonwealth Games. The stadium has also hosted Scotland national football team matches and other significant football events. It is considered one of the most iconic football stadiums in the UK, known for its atmosphere and history.

world knowledge.Name: Dalhousie University
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Studley campus, 79 acres (32 ha); Agricultural Campus, 151 acres (61 ha)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dalhousie University was established in 1818 by George Ramsay, 9th Earl of Dalhousie, as a non-sectarian college. It faced financial difficulties and sporadic operations until it was reorganized in 1863 and renamed The Governors of Dalhousie College and University. It formally became Dalhousie University in 1997 after merging with the Technical University of Nova Scotia.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by George Ramsay, 9th Earl of Dalhousie, as a non-sectarian institution.
The first class was held after financial difficulties delayed the start of operations.
The college was reorganized and renamed The Governors of Dalhousie College and University.
Margaret Florence Newcombe became the first female graduate, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree.

Major_Events.Event: Merger with Technical University of Nova Scotia
Major_Events.Description: Dalhousie University merged with the Technical University of Nova Scotia, expanding its faculties and programs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's buildings vary in age and style, from Hart House (1864) to the Collaborative Health Education Building (2015). The campus includes a mix of historic and modern structures, with facilities for academics, athletics, and student life.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dalhousie University is a major public research university in Canada, known for its contributions to education, research, and community engagement. It has a rich history and has produced numerous notable alumni, including Nobel laureates, politicians, and business leaders.
world knowledge.Details: Dalhousie University offers over 200 degree programs in 13 undergraduate, graduate, and professional faculties. It is a member of the U15 group of research-intensive universities in Canada. The university has a strong focus on marine research and sustainability, and it operates several campuses in Halifax and Bible Hill, Nova Scotia.

world knowledge.Name: Stoney Creek Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Rogers Pass, Glacier National Park, between Revelstoke and Golden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stoney Creek Bridge is a Canadian Pacific Railway (CP) truss arch bridge in southeastern British Columbia. It was the highest timber bridge ever built and the second highest bridge in North America at the time of its construction. The original bridge was completed in 1885, but was replaced in 1894 due to the need for a stronger structure to support heavier locomotives. The bridge has undergone several modifications and evaluations over the years to accommodate increasing train loads.

Major_Events.Description: The original Stoney Creek Bridge was completed in early August 1885 after seven weeks of construction. Challenges included a confined workspace, unstable rock foundation, a flash flood, and a forest fire that destroyed lumber for the bridge.
The original bridge was replaced with an 82-metre high, 148-metre long structure incorporating a 102-metre steel arch span. This was done to support heavier locomotives.
The Canadian Bridge Co. installed truss arches outside the existing ones to widen each side by 1.5 metres and replaced deck lattice girder spans with deck plate girders.

Six cars of a westbound freight derailed on the bridge when the train lost momentum on the steeper grade and stopped with the cars on the bridge. Restarting on the curve caused the lighter middle cars to lift from the track.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a truss arch design made of wrought iron. The 1894 replacement structure is 148 metres long and 82 metres high, with a 102-metre steel arch span. The design could support the combined weight of two mountain region locomotives initially, and later modifications allowed it to support four locomotives with a combined weight of 1,100 tons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge and its locale have been the subject of numerous Canadian Pacific promotional photographs that have gained iconic status. It has also been featured in television commercials to promote the railway. The bridge represents CP's engineering prowess in conquering the mountainous terrain of eastern British Columbia.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is located in Glacier National Park and is part of the Rogers Pass area. It ranks second to the Lethbridge Viaduct in Western Canada in terms of height. The bridge has been evaluated multiple times for load capacity, most recently in 1999. The western approach includes a sharp bend that limits train speeds to 40 kilometres per hour. Since 1988, the bridge has primarily handled lighter eastbound trains.

world knowledge.Name: Al Shouf Cedar Nature Reserve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al Shouf Cedar Nature Reserve is the largest natural reserve in Lebanon, covering 5.3% of the country's territory. It is located on the slopes of Jebel Baruk mountain and includes the Lebanon cedar forests of Barouk, Maaser el Shouf, and Ain Zhalta-Bmohray. The reserve is an Important Bird Area (IBA) and Eco-tourism area, hosting 32 species of wild mammals, 200 species of birds, and 500 species of plants. The Barouk mountain comprises limestone rocks from the Pliocene, with significant tectonic activity dividing the mountains of Lebanon into the Anti-Lebanon and Mount Lebanon ranges. The reserve is also known for its efforts to conserve the cedar of Lebanon and its rich biodiversity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cedar forests of Lebanon are the oldest documented forests in history, featuring prominently in ancient Sumerian literature, including The Epic of Gilgamesh. The Shouf region is a nexus of many cultures, religions, and historical events, with landmarks such as the cave castle of Tyron Niha and the Fakhreddine Fortress.
world knowledge.Details: The reserve is home to 25 internationally and nationally threatened species, 48 endemic species, and 14 rare species. It also hosts 24 tree species, including the cedar of Lebanon, and has a rich variety of reptiles and amphibians. The reserve's annual rainfall averages 1,200 mm, and the mean annual temperature is 11.3°C. The area is crucial for agriculture irrigation and supplies water to several villages in the Shouf and western Bekaa regions.

world knowledge.Name: Butterfly Theater
world knowledge.Address: 212 W. Wisconsin Avenue Milwaukee, Wisconsin United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Butterfly Theater opened in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on September 2, 1911. It was built by Otto Meister and became nationally known. The theater operated from 1911 to 1930 and was demolished in 1930 to make way for the Warner Theatre.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened to 1,500 people and showed several movies. A six-piece orchestra played and the Loos Brothers sang a duet called 'My Hula Hula Love'.
A film in the projection room caught fire, forcing patrons to evacuate. The film operator prevented the fire from spreading until firemen arrived.
Warner Brothers purchased the Butterfly Theater and other buildings on the site to build a new theater and hotel. The Butterfly Theater was demolished in 1930.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater featured a 27 ft wide illuminated butterfly facade with 1,000 light bulbs. It had marble floors, canaries in gilded cages, crystal chandeliers, and a mirrored staircase. The interior included a $10,000 pipe organ, leather-upholstered seats, and 25 box-seats on the main floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Butterfly Theater was a notable example of early 20th-century movie palaces, known for its lavish decor and innovative features like fireproofing and air circulation. It was a prominent entertainment venue in Milwaukee during its operation.
world knowledge.Details: The theater claimed to be almost fireproof and advertised that the air was 'completely changed every 3 minutes.' Admission was initially 10 cents, later raised to 25 cents during World War I. The architect was August Willmanns, and the building cost was $200,000. The theater's facade featured a terra-cotta butterfly with a woman's body at its center.

world knowledge.Name: Sapporo Satoland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sapporo Satoland was established in 1995 as an agricultural-themed amusement park. It contains remains from the early Satsumon period (9th to early 10th century), providing clues about the origin of agriculture in Hokkaidō. The park was expanded in 2004 and has been managed by the Sato Mirai Project Group since 2006.

Major_Events.Description: The Sapporo Snow Festival moved its site from Makomanai to Satoland, featuring huge snow slides and a maze. The event later moved to the Sapporo Community Dome (Tsudome) in 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes food processing facilities, event venues, farms, pastures, flower gardens, and a park golf ground. The Satoland Centre has a restaurant and meeting rooms, while the Satoland Interchange Hall is designed for events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sapporo Satoland is culturally significant for its agricultural theme and historical relics from the Satsumon period, which help understand early farming practices in Hokkaidō. It also serves as a venue for festivals and educational programs.
world knowledge.Details: The park offers agricultural experience programs such as butter, sausage, and ice cream making. A bus and carriage run around the park. It has a free parking lot for 1,800 vehicles and is located near Moerenuma Park. Visitors can eat organic vegetables grown in Hokkaidō at the restaurant and shops.

world knowledge.Name: Kozhikode Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kozhikode Beach has been a prominent place for public meetings and was a center of the city 100 years ago. The beach road was renamed 'Gandhi Road' in 1934 after Gandhi's visit. The downtown shifted to Mananchira in the 1970s, then to Mavoor Road in the 1980s, and later to Thondayad Bypass and Palazhi in the 2010s. Valiyangadi, part of the beach area, was historically significant for trade between European and Arab traders.

Major_Events.Description: The beach road was renamed 'Gandhi Road' after Gandhi visited Kozhikode in 1934.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach has paved stones, illumination, and includes Lions Park for children and an aquarium. The Mishkal Masjidh, a 700-year-old mosque, features 47 doors, 24 carved pillars, and a large prayer hall accommodating 400 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kozhikode Beach is culturally significant as a historical trade center, a site for public meetings, and a vibrant part of the city's social and economic life. Valiyangadi and the beach area reflect the rich history of Malabar trade and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreation, public gatherings, and historical site
world knowledge.Details: The beach is accessible through four road overbridges and has a long drive from Beypore in the south to Kappad in the north. Nearby areas include Valiyangadi, Gujarathi Street, Halwa Street, and shopping localities like Nalam Gate. The beach area also features landmarks such as Mishkal Masjidh, Tagore Centenary Hall, and Gandhi Peace Foundation.

world knowledge.Name: Shizuoka Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shizuoka Stadium ECOPA is a sports stadium that opened in 2001 as the centerpiece of the larger Ogasayama Sports Park. It has hosted numerous major sporting events, including matches during the 2002 FIFA World Cup and the 2019 Rugby World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: First major event held at the stadium on May 12, 2001, between Shimizu S-Pulse and Júbilo Iwata, with a record crowd of 52,959.
Hosted matches including Belgium versus Russia in the group stage and the quarter-final match between Brazil and England.
Served as the main stadium for the event.
Used as one of the venues for the first Rugby World Cup held in Asia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a grass surface and is fully equipped for track and field events. It is part of the larger Ogasayama Sports Park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant venue for major sporting events in Shizuoka Prefecture and has hosted international events like the FIFA World Cup and Rugby World Cup. The walk from Aino Station to the stadium features sixteen works of art commemorating the 2002 World Cup.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium primarily used for football, track and field, and other major sporting events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 50,889. It is owned by Shizuoka Prefecture and operated by the Shizuoka Prefectural Football Association. Next to the stadium is the indoor Ecopa Arena used for various performances and shows. Aino Station, a fifteen-minute walk from the stadium, provides access, with shuttle buses available during major events.

world knowledge.Name: Phuket International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Phuket International Airport (IATA: HKT, ICAO: VTSP) is an international airport serving the island of Phuket and its province in southern Thailand. It is located 32 km (20 mi) north of downtown Phuket in the Mai Khao subdistrict of Thalang district. The airport plays a major role in Thailand's tourism industry, as Phuket is a popular resort destination. It is the third-busiest airport in Thailand in terms of passengers, after Suvarnabhumi Airport and Don Mueang International Airport in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region.

Major_Events.Description: The expansion and renovation project was completed at a cost of 5.14 billion baht, increasing the airport's capacity to handle 12.5 million passengers annually and enhancing the total capacity from 6.5 million to 20 million passengers per year.

Major_Events.Event: Record of 15.1 million arrivals and departures
Major_Events.Description: The airport set a record of 15.1 million arrivals and departures in 2016, up 17.8 percent from 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Phuket International Airport features three distinct terminals to manage its air traffic. Terminal 2 is designated for international flights, while Terminal 3 handles domestic flights. Terminal X, specifically intended for charter flights, was opened in February 2014.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Phuket International Airport plays a major role in Thailand's tourism industry, as Phuket is a popular resort destination. It facilitates international and domestic travel, contributing significantly to the region's economy and cultural exchange.
world knowledge.Details: Phuket International Airport underwent a significant expansion and renovation project, which was completed in 2016 at a cost of 5.14 billion baht. This expansion increased its capacity to handle 12.5 million passengers annually. Overall, the expansion enhanced the airport's total capacity from 6.5 million to 20 million passengers per year. In light of the airport's congestion and limited space for further expansion, a proposal for a rail link from Krabi International Airport was put forward in 2012. A proposal for a new international airport has been put forward, aimed at serving three provinces: Phang Nga, Phuket, and Krabi. The construction of this airport is planned to be carried out in two phases, but the entire proposal was put on hold in 2022.

world knowledge.Name: Xupu Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Xuhui and Pudong districts, Shanghai, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Xupu Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge over the Huangpu River in Shanghai, China, connecting the city's Xuhui and Pudong districts. It opened in 1997 and is part of the S20 Outer Ring Expressway.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to traffic, connecting Xuhui and Pudong districts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed design with a height of 217 meters (712 feet) and a longest span of 590 meters (1,936 feet).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant infrastructure project in Shanghai, facilitating transportation between Xuhui and Pudong districts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries 8 lanes of the S20 Outer Ring Expressway over the Huangpu River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is owned by Shanghai Foundation Engineering Co. and was designed by the Shanghai Municipal Engineering Design Institute. It is preceded by the Minpu Bridge and followed by the Lupu Bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Charles University
world knowledge.Area: Prague, Hradec Králové, Plzeň, Brandýs nad Labem
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Charles University, established in 1347, is the oldest university north of the Alps and east of Paris. It was founded by Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV and modeled on the University of Paris. The university has played a significant role in the cultural and intellectual history of Central Europe, including the Hussite movement and the Velvet Revolution.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV, modeled on the University of Paris.
King Wenceslaus IV granted the Bohemian masters three votes, leading to the emigration of foreign professors and students.

Major_Events.Event: Division into German and Czech Universities
Major_Events.Description: Charles-Ferdinand University was divided into German and Czech sections.
Students and faculty of the university played a significant role in the peaceful overthrow of the communist regime.
A mass shooting occurred at the university, resulting in 14 deaths and 25 injuries.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The oldest building, Karolinum, is situated in the Old Town of Prague and serves as the university's center. It has been serving the university since 1386.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Charles University is a symbol of Czech national identity and intellectual heritage. It has been a center of learning and cultural exchange for centuries, influencing the development of Central European thought and education.
world knowledge.Details: Charles University consists of 17 faculties and is ranked among the top universities in Central and Eastern Europe. It is a founding member of the 4EU+ European University Alliance and participates in numerous international academic programs.

world knowledge.Name: St. Anne's Museum Quarter
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally an Augustinian nunnery, St. Anne's Priory, built in late Brick Gothic style. It served as a monastery for unmarried women in Lübeck, dedicated to Saint Anne. Closed during the Reformation in 1532, it later became a poorhouse and then a prison. The priory and church were partially destroyed by fire in 1843. Converted into a museum in 1912, it opened in 1915. It now houses significant collections of medieval art and cultural history.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the Augustinian nunnery and church in late Brick Gothic style.
The monastery was closed during the Reformation; the last nuns left.
Parts of the monastery and church were destroyed by fire.
The senate of Lübeck decided to convert the monastery into a museum.
The museum opened with some delay due to World War I.
Modern addition of the Kunsthalle, which exhibits modern art.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Late Brick Gothic style with preserved original rooms including the cloister, refectories, Remter, chapter house, and sacristy. Modern addition for special exhibits.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Houses Germany's largest collection of medieval sculpture and altar-pieces. Part of the Lübeck World Heritage site, it reflects the cultural and historical evolution of Lübeck from medieval times to the 19th century.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes the largest collection of medieval polyptychs in Germany, significant sculptures, and a collection of home decor items showing the lifestyle from medieval times to the 1800s. The Kunsthalle exhibits modern art and has a notable collection of self-portraits.

world knowledge.Name: Qatar National Library
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Qatar National Library (QNL) was announced by Sheikha Moza bint Nasser on 19 November 2012, during a ceremony celebrating the 50th anniversary of the Dar Al Kutub Al Qatariyya. It serves as a national library, a research-level university library, and a central metropolitan public library. The building was designed by Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas and opened in April 2018.

Major_Events.Description: Sheikha Moza bint Nasser announced the plans for the new national library during a ceremony celebrating the 50th anniversary of the Dar Al Kutub Al Qatariyya.
The new building of Qatar National Library, designed by Rem Koolhaas, opened to the public in April 2018.
The official inauguration ceremony was held on 16 April 2018, with His Highness the Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani placing the one-millionth book on the shelves.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas, the building features state-of-the-art facilities including collaborative and individual learning spaces, a children's library, a teen and young adult collection, computer labs, digital media production facilities, performance spaces, a restaurant, a café, an assistive technology area, and a writing center.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: QNL plays a crucial role in preserving and providing access to global knowledge, including heritage content relevant to Qatar and the region. It also supports education and research at all levels and serves as a community meeting place.
world knowledge.Details: QNL offers a wide variety of books and e-books in multiple languages, including fiction and non-fiction, bestsellers, and classics. It also provides access to international scholarly databases, academic journals, and digital resources. The Heritage Library includes rare books, manuscripts, and materials related to Arab-Islamic civilization. QNL is also involved in digitizing heritage material and making it accessible through the Qatar Digital Library.

world knowledge.Name: East Coast Railway Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built in 2008 at a cost of Rs 6 crore. It has four turfs for practice and one of the best drainage systems in the state. It hosted its first Ranji Trophy match in November 2008.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted its first Ranji Trophy match in November 2008.
A few Twenty20 matches during the first edition of the Odisha Premier League were hosted at this venue.

Major_Events.Event: Orissa-Punjab Elite Group B Ranji Trophy tournament league match
Major_Events.Description: The stadium was used for the Orissa-Punjab Elite Group B Ranji Trophy tournament league match, inaugurated by General Manager of East Coast Railway AK Vohra.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features four turfs for practice and a high-quality drainage system. It also includes a huge manual scoreboard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant for cricket in Odisha, hosting important matches like the Ranji Trophy and Odisha Premier League, and serving as the home ground for the Odisha cricket team.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 1,720 and is operated by the Odisha Cricket Association. It serves as the home ground for the Odisha cricket team.

world knowledge.Name: Belgrad Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Belgrad Forest is a mixed deciduous forest adjacent to Istanbul, Turkey, named after the village settled by Serbs deported from Belgrade in 1521. It has been an important water resource since the Eastern Roman Empire and was protected by the Ottomans. The forest houses many plant, bird, and animal species and is a popular recreational area.

Major_Events.Description: Thousands of Serbs were deported to Constantinople from Belgrade, leading to the naming of the forest after the village they settled in.
Suleiman the Magnificent commissioned the Ottoman architect Sinan to upgrade the water supply system, resulting in a series of magnificent aqueducts.
The motorway running over the bridge affected the northern part of the forest, raising concerns about its protection.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest contains several historical reservoirs and aqueducts, including the Maǧlova Aqueduct, Kemerburgaz aqueduct, and Uzunkemer, built during the Ottoman period.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Belgrad Forest is culturally significant as a historical water resource for Constantinople and Istanbul, a protected natural area, and a popular recreational site.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is a popular destination for walking, jogging, hiking, and picnicking. It features nine nature parks, the Atatürk Arboretum, and several picnic areas, including Büyük Bent. The forest is under protection but faces challenges from urban expansion and infrastructure development.

world knowledge.Name: Sherborne Castle
world knowledge.Address: Sherborne, Dorset, England, within the parish of Castleton
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built by Sir Walter Raleigh as Sherborne Lodge in the 16th century, it was later extended by the Digby family in the 1620s. The estate includes the ruins of the 12th-century Sherborne Old Castle, which was a fortified palace of Roger de Caen. The castle played a role in the English Civil War and was slighted in 1645. The gardens were laid out in the 18th century, featuring a lake designed by Capability Brown.

Major_Events.Description: Sir Walter Raleigh built Sherborne Lodge as a new house for temporary visits.
The Digby family added four wings to Sherborne Lodge, forming the mansion now known as Sherborne Castle.
During the English Civil War, the old castle was besieged by Parliamentarians and slighted afterward.
Capability Brown designed the lake that separates the old and new castles.
The mansion was used by the Red Cross as a hospital.

Major_Events.Event: Use as headquarters for D-Day commandos
Major_Events.Description: The mansion served as the headquarters for the commandos involved in the D-Day landings.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a four-storey rectangular building with four polygonal corner turrets, later extended with four wings in a similar architectural style. The entrance was disguised in one of the corner towers to maintain symmetry. The mansion features progressive design elements for its time, including a winder stairwell and direct access to the hall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sherborne Castle is a significant example of Tudor architecture and later extensions. It has historical importance due to its association with Sir Walter Raleigh, the Digby family, and its role in the English Civil War. The estate's gardens and ruins of the old castle are also notable, designed by Capability Brown and listed as Grade I.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a lodge for temporary visits, later extended into a mansion. Now serves as a historic site open to the public.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion and the ruins of the old castle were designated as Grade I listed in 1951. The gardens are Grade I listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. The estate hosts special events such as concerts and fireworks displays. The old castle is leased by English Heritage and accessed separately from the rest of the estate.

world knowledge.Name: Greenway Estate
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Greenway Estate, originally known as Greynway, was first mentioned in 1493 as a crossing point of the River Dart. The Tudor mansion, Greenway Court, was built in the late 16th century by Otto and Katherine Gilbert. The current Georgian-style house was built by Roope Harris Roope in the late 18th century. The estate was later owned by Agatha Christie and her husband, Max Mallowan, until their deaths. It was acquired by the National Trust in 2000 for its significance as a writer's home.

Major_Events.Description: Greenway Court was built by Otto and Katherine Gilbert, members of a Devon seafaring family.
Roope Harris Roope built the existing house in Georgian style.
Agatha Christie and her husband, Max Mallowan, purchased the estate.
Greenway House was made a Grade II* listed building by English Heritage.
The National Trust acquired the estate for its significance as a writer's home.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tall, late-Georgian, stuccoed house with gardens containing plants from the southern hemisphere. The house features a billiard room, study, and bedrooms in the east wing (demolished in 1938).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Greenway Estate is culturally significant as the former home of Agatha Christie, one of the most famous crime writers of all time. The estate and its surroundings inspired several of her novels and short stories. It is also notable for its historical connections to the Gilbert family and its Georgian architecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic house and gardens open to the public, serving as a museum and cultural site.
world knowledge.Details: The estate features large riverside gardens with plants from the southern hemisphere and a Barn Gallery showcasing work by contemporary local artists. Greenway was used as a setting in several of Agatha Christie's novels, including 'Dead Man's Folly' and 'The Mysterious Mr Quin'. The ITV series 'Agatha Christie's Poirot' also filmed an episode at the house. The estate housed children who were war evacuees during WWII, inspiring the novel 'Death at Greenway' by Lori Rader-Day.

world knowledge.Name: Humboldt University of Berlin
world knowledge.Address: Unter den Linden boulevard, Berlin, Germany
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established by Frederick William III in 1810, the university was initially named the University of Berlin. It was renamed the Royal Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin in 1828 and received its current name in 1949 in honor of Alexander and Wilhelm von Humboldt. It played a significant role in the development of the Humboldtian model of higher education, influencing universities worldwide.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established by Frederick William III on the initiative of Wilhelm von Humboldt, Johann Gottlieb Fichte, and Friedrich Daniel Ernst Schleiermacher.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Royal Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed in honor of its founder, Frederick William III.
During the Cold War, the university was located in East Berlin, and the Free University of Berlin was established in West Berlin.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Humboldt University of Berlin
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed in honor of Alexander and Wilhelm von Humboldt.
Books by 'degenerates' and opponents of the Nazi regime were burned in the Opernplatz square.
After German reunification, the university underwent significant restructuring, aligning it with West German academic standards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building, Prinz-Heinrich-Palais, was constructed in Baroque style from 1748 to 1753. It was rebuilt after World War II from 1949 to 1962.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is culturally and historically significant for pioneering the Humboldtian model of higher education, which emphasizes the unity of teaching and research. It has been associated with numerous Nobel laureates and influential thinkers.
world knowledge.Details: The university is divided into nine faculties and offers degree programs in 171 disciplines. It has three campuses: Campus Mitte, Campus Nord, and Campus Adlershof. The university library contains about 6.5 million volumes and is one of the largest in Germany. It is ranked 120th globally in the 2024 QS World University Rankings and 87th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings.

image_name: Church and Convent of Saint Antony

world knowledge.Name: Church and Convent of Saint Antony
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Church and Convent of Saint Antony is a 17th-century Roman Catholic church constructed by the Franciscans during the settlement of Pernambuco. It was the third Franciscan convent in Brazil, destroyed during the Dutch occupation, and later rebuilt. It was designated a historic structure by the National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage (IPHAN) in 1938.

Major_Events.Description: The church and convent were pillaged during the Dutch occupation. The church was first attacked and pillaged on May 1, 1632 during mass, and reoccupied in 1635. The Franciscan monks were arrested in 1639 for maintaining contact with Franciscans in Salvador, Bahia, and were deported to Itamaraca Island. The church and convent were abandoned until 1654 with the departure of the Dutch.
The church and convent were used as a headquarters by revolutionary troops.
The church was designated a historic structure by the National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage (IPHAN).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is built in the Franciscan Baroque style of colonial Brazil. The façade dates to 1660 and was subsequently renovated, divided into three parts horizontally and five parts vertically. The interior features richly designed elements, including panels of azulejos, baroque woodcarving and gilding, and fine carved furniture. The barrel vault of the nave has a large ceiling painting depicting the lives of Franciscan saints. The sacristy includes a lavabo made of lioz marble imported from Portugal.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church and convent are significant as one of the earliest Franciscan convents in Brazil and for their role in the colonial history of Pernambuco. It houses the Pinacoteca Museum of Igarassu, which contains one of the most important collections of Franciscan art in Latin America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious worship and historical preservation (now houses the Pinacoteca Museum of Igarassu).
world knowledge.Details: The church and convent are located in the Historic Center of Igarassu, protected as an urban architectural ensemble since 1972. The Pinacoteca Museum of Igarassu, opened in 1957, includes 24 paintings from the 17th and 18th centuries, notably those from the Church of São Cosme e São Damião in Igarassu. Four paintings depict an epidemic that devastated Pernambuco in 1685.

world knowledge.Name: University of Mauritius
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Mauritius (UoM) is the national university of Mauritius, established in December 1965 by the University of Mauritius Ordinance, incorporating the existing School of Agriculture. It was further defined by the University of Mauritius Act in 1971. The university was inaugurated by Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, on March 24, 1972. The Faculty of Agriculture, the oldest faculty, was founded in 1914 and incorporated into the university in 1966.

Major_Events.Description: Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, accompanied by His Royal Highness Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, inaugurated the University of Mauritius.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Mauritius is the oldest and largest university in the country, playing a significant role in the educational and cultural development of Mauritius.
world knowledge.Details: The university comprises six faculties: Agriculture, Engineering, Information, Communication and Digital Technologies, Law & Management, Ocean Studies, Science, and Social Studies & Humanities. It also includes several centers such as the Centre for Innovative Lifelong Learning (CILL), the Centre for Information Technology & Systems (CITS), and the Centre for Biomedical and Biomaterials Research (CBBR). The Students’ Union represents the interests of all students.

world knowledge.Name: Oswestry Guildhall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oswestry Guildhall has undergone several transformations since the early 16th century. The first guildhall was a plain stone-fronted building with a high clock turret. A second neoclassical-style building was erected in 1782, which later became the headquarters of the Oswestry Municipal Borough Council in 1835. The current Renaissance-style building, designed by Henry Cheers, was constructed in 1893 after the previous building was found unstable. It served as the local seat of government until 2009 and now houses the Attfield Theatre and local museum.

Major_Events.Description: A neoclassical-style municipal building was erected on the west side of Bailey Head.
The second municipal building was designated as the guildhall after the area became a municipal borough in 1835.
The current Renaissance-style guildhall was built after the previous one was deemed unstable.
The guildhall underwent major restoration works, financed in part by the Heritage Lottery Fund, and was re-opened by the Lord Lieutenant of Shropshire.

Major_Events.Event: Cessation as local seat of government
Major_Events.Description: The guildhall ceased to be the local seat of government when Shropshire Council was formed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current guildhall is built in the Renaissance style with ashlar stone. It features an asymmetrical main frontage with four bays, a round-headed doorway flanked by Doric order pilasters, a Venetian window on the first floor, and a three-light mullion window on the second floor. The design includes a shaped gable with a stone inscribed with the construction date.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oswestry Guildhall is a Grade II listed building and has been a central part of the town's civic life since the 16th century. It reflects the architectural and historical evolution of Oswestry and continues to serve as a cultural hub with the Attfield Theatre and local museum.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally the meeting place of Oswestry Municipal Borough Council, it now serves as the home of the Attfield Theatre, local museum, and meeting place for Oswestry Town Council.
Notable_Visitors: Bishop of St Asaph, William Lloyd
Lord Lieutenant of Shropshire, Algernon Heber-Percy
world knowledge.Details: The guildhall contains a landscape by G. Bonner depicting the second guildhall. It was designated as a Grade II listed building on 15 May 1986 (Reference no. 1367321).

world knowledge.Name: Casa Rull Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Casa Rull Museum is a historic house in La Massana, Andorra, named for the Rull family, landowning farmers. It gained prominence when the Perich family of wealthy merchants married into the family in 1757. The house dates to 1732 but is on the site of earlier structures owned by the Rulls. It burnt down in the late 19th century, leaving only the stone walls, and was afterwards rebuilt. In 2000, the Andorran government opened the house as a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The house suffered a severe fire that started in the oven and burnt all of the wooden structure, leaving only the stone walls. The houseowner at the time sold livestock and took out loans to fund the rebuilding of Casa Rull.
The Andorran government opened the house as a museum on 9 June 2000.

Over the Christmas and New Year period of 2021/2022, the house hosted an exhibition of rural life in Andorra portrayed through Playmobil dioramas, featuring 500 figures from the collection of Chile-born Andorra resident Daniel Arellano.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building consists of three storeys plus an attic. It was originally constructed in 1723 on the site of two earlier buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Casa Rull Museum represents the historical and cultural heritage of Andorra, showcasing the life of landowning farmers and the rise of the Perich family as a prominent petite bourgeoisie class. It provides insight into rural life in Andorra during the 18th and 19th centuries.
world knowledge.Details: The museum shows the house as it might have been in the late 19th century when it was occupied by the Perich family. It costs 5 euros to enter with a supplement for a guided tour. It is part of the Andorra Museumpass scheme and is on the Andorran government museums "rural habitat" itinerary.

world knowledge.Name: Horta Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Horta Airport was inaugurated on 24 August 1971 by President Almirante Américo Tomás. It was remodeled and reinaugurated in December 2001 to serve the islands of the Central Group and expanded to support domestic connectivity to Lisbon. The airport is an important economic tool in the region and a vital connection to smaller aerodromes in outlying islands.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inaugurated by President Almirante Américo Tomás.
TAP Air Portugal initiated direct flights between Horta and Lisbon using a Boeing 737 named Ponta Delgada.
The airport was remodeled and reinaugurated to serve the Central Group islands and expanded for domestic connectivity.
A refurbished control tower was inaugurated, allowing the airport to oversee the Central and Western Group of islands.
Runway grooving was undertaken by the company Proysesa.
Contamination of gasoline tanks resulted in flights being refueled on other islands, primarily Lajes Field on Terceira.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The three-story terminal building is divided operationally, with departures and arrivals on the same floor (street-level), a cafe and lounge on the first floor, and runway-level departures lounge and logistics. The street-level departures and arrivals concourses are situated on opposite ends of the terminal. The first-floor cafe/lounge features an exterior observation deck with a view of the runway, control tower, and the distant island of Pico.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Horta Airport is a vital economic and transportation hub for the Azores, connecting the islands of the Central Group and providing essential domestic connectivity to Lisbon. It plays a crucial role in the region's economy and serves as a key link to smaller aerodromes in outlying islands.
world knowledge.Details: Horta Airport (IATA: HOR, ICAO: LPHR) is located in the parish of Castelo Branco, 9.5 km southwest of the center of Horta. It serves as an important economic tool in the region and a vital connection to smaller aerodromes in outlying islands. The airport has undergone several renovations and expansions, including the installation of a Wide Area Multilateration (WAM) system in the control tower to monitor aviation within the airspace. Plans for further expansion and the installation of satellite technology to assist in low visibility landings are in place. The airport operates regular scheduled and charter flights with various airlines.

world knowledge.Name: Montacute House
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 106 hectares of parkland and 4 hectares of gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Montacute House is a late Elizabethan mansion built for Sir Edward Phelips, a prominent lawyer and politician. It is one of the few prodigy houses to have survived almost unchanged from the Elizabethan era. The house was designated as a Grade I listed building, and its gardens are also listed at the highest grade on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in England.

Major_Events.Description: Montacute House was acquired by the National Trust, becoming one of the Trust's first great houses.
During World War II, Montacute House was requisitioned by the army, and American soldiers were billeted in the surrounding parkland before the Normandy landings.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Montacute House is built in the English Renaissance style, featuring Dutch gables, large mullioned windows, and perfect symmetry. The house is constructed of local Ham Hill stone and has a 172-foot Long Gallery, the longest in England.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Montacute House is culturally significant as a well-preserved example of late Elizabethan architecture and for its role in English history. It has been used as a filming location for several films and television dramas.
world knowledge.Details: Montacute House is open to the public and has been used as a filming location for various films and TV shows, including 'Sense and Sensibility' and 'Wolf Hall'. The house and its gardens are listed as Grade I on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in England.

world knowledge.Name: Shimotsui-Seto Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Seto Bridge was conceived to connect Honshū and Shikoku islands, addressing transportation challenges and safety concerns after a tragic ferry collision in 1955. The project, part of the Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project, overcame delays like the 1973 oil shock and was completed in 1988. It fulfilled a century-old vision of improving connectivity in the region.

Major_Events.Description: A collision of two ferries in dense fog off Takamatsu killed 171 people, including 100 students, prompting the need for a safer crossing.
Construction began after the Environment Assessment Report was published, following delays due to the 1973 oil shock.
The bridge was officially opened to road and rail traffic by then-Crown Prince Akihito.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a double-decked system with an upper deck carrying four lanes of highway traffic (Seto-Chūō Expressway) and a lower deck with two railway tracks (Seto-Ōhashi Line). It spans 13.1 km, with the longest section, the Minami Bisan-Seto Bridge, extending 1,100 meters. The structure used 3.646 million cubic meters of concrete and 705,000 tons of steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes Japan's engineering prowess and fulfills a long-standing vision of uniting Honshū and Shikoku, enhancing regional connectivity and economic growth. It also honors the memory of those lost in the 1955 ferry disaster.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (road and rail connectivity between Honshū and Shikoku)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge consists of six named bridges and five viaducts. It was designed to potentially accommodate future Shinkansen tracks. The initial toll fee for crossing was ¥6,300. The project cost approximately US$7 billion and resulted in 17 worker fatalities during construction.

world knowledge.Name: Boğaziçi University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Boğaziçi University, originally founded as Robert College in 1863, was the first American college outside the United States. It was established by Christopher Robert and Cyrus Hamlin. In 1971, it was transformed into a public university by the Republic of Turkey, retaining its academic staff and facilities from Robert College.

Major_Events.Description: Robert College's university section was turned over to the Republic of Turkey and renamed Boğaziçi University.

Major_Events.Event: Appointment of Melih Bulu as Rector
Major_Events.Description: Melih Bulu was appointed as rector by the Turkish government, leading to widespread protests and resistance from faculty and students.
Melih Bulu was dismissed from the rectorship by President Erdoğan.

Major_Events.Event: Appointment of Naci İnci as Rector
Major_Events.Description: Naci İnci was appointed as rector despite receiving a 95% no confidence vote from the faculty.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's campuses include historic buildings from Robert College, such as Hamlin, Washburn, Theodorus, Dodge, Albert Long, and Anderson Halls. The architecture reflects a blend of historical and modern styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Boğaziçi University is a major center for higher education in Turkey, known for its liberal approach and fostering an interdisciplinary and international research environment. It has a rich history tied to the American educational system and has played a significant role in Turkish academia.
world knowledge.Details: Boğaziçi University operates on seven campuses in Istanbul, including the South Campus, North Campus, Hisar Campus, Uçaksavar Campus, Kandilli Campus, Kilyos Sarıtepe Campus, and Anadolu Hisarı Campus. The university is known for its strong academic programs and has been ranked highly in various international university rankings. The university has faced significant political interference in recent years, leading to protests and resistance from the academic community.

world knowledge.Name: Co-Cathedral of Logroño
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Co-cathedral of Santa María de la Redonda is located in Logroño, in La Rioja, Spain. The name 'redonda' refers to the rounded shape of an earlier church on the site. It had the status of collegiate church from the 15th century when Logrono became a city. The present building was raised to the rank of cathedral in the 20th century. It belongs to the Roman Catholic Diocese of Calahorra y La Calzada-Logroño, which has two other cathedrals.

Major_Events.Description: It has been protected by a heritage listing (currently Bien de Interés Cultural) since 1931.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church has two elaborately decorated towers, each containing a set of bells. The sidewall of the church has a clock split into three faces: one each for the hour, minute and second. The entrance to the church is set in an alcove filled with Christian sculptures, protected by high iron gates and netting to prevent people or birds entering. The towers are similarly netted but the famous storks which inhabit Logroño can still nest on the highest ledges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Co-cathedral of Santa María de la Redonda is culturally and historically important as it represents the religious heritage and architectural development in Logroño, Spain. It has been a significant religious site since the 15th century and continues to be a place of worship and cultural interest.
world knowledge.Details: Gillis Coignet, born in 1535 in Antwerp and died in 1599 in Hamburg, painted those panels in Antwerp in 1584, according to the wooden footnote of the painting Annunciation. The panels arrived at this church from the chapel of the Lordship of Somalo near Nájera. Their owners acquired them in Paris at the beginning of the 20th century and placed them in the chapel.

world knowledge.Name: Perth Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Perth Airport was established in 1938 on land originally granted to John Scott. It began as a military airfield during World War II before transitioning to civilian use in 1944. The airport was renamed from Guildford Aerodrome to Perth Airport in 1953 and has since undergone significant expansions to accommodate growing passenger and aircraft traffic.

Major_Events.Description: Australian National Airways (ANA) flew the first commercial service from the aerodrome to Adelaide using Douglas DC-3 aircraft.
The airport was officially renamed from Guildford Aerodrome to Perth Airport, marking its growing importance as an international and domestic hub.
The arrival of the Boeing 747 highlighted the need for further terminal expansions due to increased passenger demand.
The new International Terminal was opened by Prime Minister Bob Hawke, significantly increasing the airport's capacity.

Major_Events.Event: Privatization under Perth Airport Pty Ltd
Major_Events.Description: The airport was leased to Perth Airport Pty Ltd for 99 years as part of the Federal Government's airport privatization program.
Qantas' Airbus A380 made its first visit to Perth as part of a promotional tour.
Terminal 2 was officially opened, providing enhanced facilities for regional flights.
Qantas commenced non-stop flights from Perth to London Heathrow using Boeing 787s.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features multiple terminals with modern designs, including the tallest control tower in Australia. Terminals are equipped with advanced passenger facilities, including free Wi-Fi, observation decks, and dedicated spotting areas. The runways are designed to accommodate large aircraft like the Boeing 747 and Airbus A380.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Perth Airport is a vital transportation hub for Western Australia, connecting the region domestically and internationally. It plays a key role in the state's economy, particularly during the mining boom, and has historical significance as one of Australia's oldest continuously operating airports.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International, domestic, and general aviation airport serving Perth and surrounding regions.
world knowledge.Details: Perth Airport is the fourth busiest airport in Australia by passenger movements. It serves as a hub for Qantas, Virgin Australia, and other regional airlines. The airport has faced challenges such as noise complaints from nearby residents but has also received awards for service quality. Future plans include terminal consolidation, a new runway, and a hotel by 2027.

world knowledge.Name: Yamanashi Prefectural Museum
world knowledge.Address: 1501-1 Misaka-chō, Narita, Fuefuki, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yamanashi Prefectural Museum opened in Fuefuki, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan in 2005. The collection relates to the natural history, history, and culture of Yamanashi Prefecture; special exhibitions are also held.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened to the public on 15 October 2005.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it showcases the natural history, history, and culture of Yamanashi Prefecture.
world knowledge.Details: Takes about 10 minutes to visit. This article related to a museum in Japan is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Szeged Synagogue
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 48 m (157 ft), Width: 35 m (115 ft), Height: 49 m (161 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Szeged Synagogue, also known as the Great Synagogue and the New Synagogue, is a Neolog Jewish congregation and synagogue located in Szeged, Hungary. It was designed by Lipót Baumhorn after winning an 1897 design competition and completed in 1902. It is considered a prime example of the unique fin de siècle Hungarian blending of Art Nouveau and Historicist styles.

Major_Events.Description: Lipót Baumhorn won the design competition for the synagogue.
The synagogue was completed and opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The synagogue features a blend of Art Nouveau and Moorish Revival styles. The interior includes a 48.5 meters tall domed ceiling, Gothic Revival elements, Roman columns, and stained glass by Miksa Róth. The Torah Ark alludes to the Holy of Holies in the Temple of Solomon, using sittimwood from the banks of the Nile and hinges shaped like the Hyssop plant.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Szeged Synagogue is the second largest in Hungary and the fourth largest in the world. It is a significant example of Hungarian Jewish architecture and a tourist attraction, also serving as an events center and concert hall.
world knowledge.Details: The synagogue has a capacity of 1,300 seats and features four domes with an inner dome height of 32 m (105 ft). It is constructed primarily of brick.

world knowledge.Name: University of Nottingham
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1881 – University College Nottingham, 1948 – Received royal charter
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Nottingham is a public research university in Nottingham, England. It was founded as University College Nottingham in 1881, and was granted a royal charter in 1948. The university traces its origins to both the founding of an adult education school in 1798, and the University Extension Lectures inaugurated by the University of Cambridge in 1873.

Major_Events.Description: University College Nottingham was established, preparing students for examinations of the University of London.
University College Nottingham was incorporated as the University of Nottingham, gaining the power to confer degrees.
The University of Nottingham became the first university in the UK to be awarded an Athena SWAN Gold Award for its commitment to advancing gender equality.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's architecture includes the neo-gothic Arkwright Building and the Trent Building, an imposing white limestone structure with a distinctive clock tower. The Jubilee Campus features modern and unique architecture, including Aspire, a 60-metre tall artistic structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Nottingham is a prestigious institution with a rich history and significant contributions to education and research. It is a member of the Russell Group and has produced notable alumni, including Nobel Prize winners.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Nottingham has campuses in the UK, Malaysia, and China. It is organized into five faculties: Arts, Engineering, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science, and Social Science. The university has a strong focus on research and has received numerous awards and recognitions for its contributions to academia and society.

world knowledge.Name: Chien Tang River Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Qiantang River Bridge is a combined road and railway bridge across the Qiantang River at Hangzhou in Zhejiang Province, China. It was designed by Mao Yisheng and built by Dorman Long. Construction started on 8 August 1934 and was completed on 29 September 1937.

Major_Events.Event: Destruction preparations during the Battle of Shanghai
Major_Events.Description: On 17 November 1937, during the Battle of Shanghai, the Bridge Construction Office was ordered to make preparations to blow up the bridge to delay the advancing Imperial Japanese Army.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Two-tier truss bridge comprising 16 spans
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is significant as an early example of modern bridge engineering in China and for its role during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a bridge in Asia is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Musée Bossuet
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée Bossuet is the art and history museum of the town of Meaux, France. Situated in the old episcopal palace, it takes its name from the famous orator and theologian, Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet, Bishop of Meaux from 1681 to 1704. The episcopal palace was built in the twelfth century around 1160, then rebuilt in the seventeenth century. The Bossuet garden, a formal garden in the French style, was created in the seventeenth century during the episcopate of Dominique Séguier.

Major_Events.Description: The Bossuet garden was opened to the public as a city park and took the name of the great prelate.
The collections expanded thanks to the legacy of the chemist and collector Henri Moissan.
The neuro-biologist Jean-Pierre Changeux enriched the museum with forty works, the last of which entered the collection in 2006.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The episcopal palace is a mix of medieval and Renaissance styles. The south facade is built of brick and stone, with large cross windows, representing eighteenth-century work. The north facade is representative of the Grand Siècle style. The lower rooms date from the second half of the twelfth century, and the chapels were expanded and redesigned in the fifteenth century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses collections of paintings, sculptures, and decorative arts, showcasing different schools of painting from the sixteenth to the twentieth centuries. It also preserves the memory of Bishop Bossuet and the history of Meaux.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include many pictures of the successive Bishops of Meaux and portraits of Bishop Bossuet by Hyacinthe Rigaud and Pierre Mignard. The Bossuet garden is a formal garden in the French style with the shape of a miter.

world knowledge.Name: Q&A Stadium Miyagi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Miyagi Stadium, also known as Q&A Stadium Miyagi for sponsorship reasons, was opened in March 2000. It has undergone name changes due to sponsorship agreements, initially known as Miyagi Stadium (2000–2014), then Hitomebore Stadium Miyagi (2014–2020), and currently Q&A Stadium Miyagi. The stadium's design evokes images of Date Masamune, a daimyō of Mutsu Province.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted three matches.
Hosted the event.
Planned football venue.
Hosted six matches, becoming the first stadium to host matches at both a men's FIFA World Cup and a women's FIFA U-20 World Cup.
Hosted matches against Slovakia, Honduras, Uruguay, and El Salvador.
Pop-music group SMAP held two outdoor concerts at the venue.
Held two days concert at the venue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Crescent-shaped roof extending past the edge of the stadium, football field surrounded by a nine-lane track, large video screen and scoreboard installed in the northern end.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium's design is inspired by Date Masamune, a historical figure in the region. It has hosted significant international and national sports events, contributing to its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's capacity is 49,133. Rifu Station is the closest train station, nearly 3.5 kilometers from the stadium. For major events, bus transportation is usually available from Izumi-Chūō and Sendai Stations. A spur from the Sanriku Expressway was built before the World Cup for easier access by car.

world knowledge.Name: Winnebago County Courthouse (Forest City, Iowa)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Winnebago County Courthouse is a historic building and active courthouse. Early county records were destroyed in an 1861 fire, making it difficult to determine where court proceedings were held in the county's early years. County voters petitioned for a $20,000 courthouse, but the Board of Supervisors deemed the plans too extravagant and opted for a smaller, less expensive structure. The courts ruled the Board acted inappropriately and awarded $3,500 in compensation. The present Romanesque Revival style building was completed in 1896 for about $25,000. An addition was added in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: Early county records were destroyed in a fire, making it difficult to trace early court proceedings.
The present Romanesque Revival style courthouse was completed for about $25,000.
An addition was added on the west side of the courthouse.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse is a two-story buff-colored brick structure with a basement level composed of coarse stone. It features a main entrance in a recessed area behind three arches, a large square clock tower rising five stories on the northeast corner, and a hipped roof with pyramid-shaped roofs on the projecting pavilions on three corners. The tower roof has been shortened.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its association with county government and the political power and prestige of Forest City as the county seat.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Active courthouse and county government building
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse was designed by Minneapolis architect F.W. Kinney from the firm of Kinney & Orth and built by contractor Martin Bumgardner and F.A. Gross. Funds were raised through local subscriptions. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1981 (NRHP reference No. 81000275).

world knowledge.Name: Vinnytsia State Pedagogical University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Vinnytsia Mykhailo Kotsiubynskyi State Pedagogical University was established in 1912. It started as a Teachers Training Institute and has undergone several transformations and name changes over the years. It became a People's Educational Institute in 1920, was named after V.I. Lenin in 1922, and was transferred to Kamyanets-Podilskiy in 1924. It returned to Vinnytsia and became a Pedagogical Technical school in 1925, and later a higher educational establishment in 1926. It was named after N. Ostrovskiy in 1937 and became a State Teachers` Training Institute in 1935. It was reorganized into a Pedagogical University named after M. Kotsiubynsky in 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The order establishing Teachers Training Institute in Vinnytsia was issued on June 5, 1912, and it opened on July 1, 1912.
The Teachers' Training Institute was reorganized into a People's Educational Institute (PIE).
Vinnytsia People's Educational Institute (PIE) was named after V.I. Lenin.
The institute was reorganized into Pedagogical University named after M. Kotsiubynsky.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is a significant educational institution in Ukraine, contributing to the preparation of highly skilled human resources for Ukrainian folk education. It has been recognized as one of the best pedagogical establishments in Ukraine.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 3 educational buildings, 5 hostels for 2800 places, a ‘Pedagog’ Sanatorium-Preventorium, and various facilities including a dining hall, cafeterias, a sporting complex, and an Artistic Center. It offers a wide range of departments and laboratories, and it has a strong focus on research and student self-government.

world knowledge.Name: Norderney
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Norderney is the youngest of the seven East Frisian islands, existing in its present form since the middle of the 16th century. It was originally part of the larger island Buise, which split during the Grote Mandrenke flood of 1362. The island grew in size over the years and became a significant fishing and trade hub. In 1797, it became the first German resort on the North Sea. The island's economy shifted to tourism in the 18th century, attracting the rich and famous.

Major_Events.Description: Split the larger island Buise into two parts, with Norderney being the eastern remnant.
The remaining part of Buise disappeared into the North Sea, leaving Norderney as the surviving island.

Major_Events.Event: First German resort on the North Sea
Major_Events.Description: Norderney became the first German resort on the North Sea, marking the beginning of its tourism industry.

Major_Events.Event: Crown Prince Georg of Hannover's visits
Major_Events.Description: Crown Prince Georg of Hannover visited Norderney, leading to the island becoming a popular destination for the rich and famous.
The wooden cape building was constructed to help mariners identify the island. It was replaced with a stone building in 1870.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island features a mix of traditional and resort-style architecture. The cape building, a local landmark, was originally wooden and later replaced with stone. The island also has a windmill built in 1862.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Norderney is culturally significant as the first German resort on the North Sea and a historic hub for fishing and trade. Its status as a National Park also highlights its environmental importance. The island's flag and coat of arms reflect its maritime heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourism and conservation (part of the Lower Saxon Wadden Sea National Park).
Notable_Visitors: Crown Prince Georg of Hannover, Herzog von Cumberland

Details.Municipal_Status: Gained in 1946, belongs to the Aurich Kreis (county).
Details.Beach: 14-kilometre (8.7 mi) long sandy beach on the northern side.
Details.Transportation: Ferry service from Norddeich pier, airport with a 1,000-metre (3,300 ft) runway.
Details.Climate: Maritime climate with mild winters and warm summers, more sunshine hours than the mainland.
Details.Special_Features: Nudist beach east of Weiße Düne (White Dune) beach.

world knowledge.Name: Kings Park
world knowledge.Details: Kings Park or King's Park may refer to:

world knowledge.Name: Newland Park
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Originated as a hamlet before mid-18th century, developed in the 19th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Newland was originally a hamlet in a partially swampy agricultural area near the crossroads of Cottingham and Beverley-Hull turnpikes. Extensive enclosure and drainage took place after 1766, and it developed as a preferred place for Hull merchants in the 19th century. The urban spread of Hull reached Newland by the early 20th century, and over the next half-century, the village was surrounded by housing and other developments.

Major_Events.Description: Extensive enclosure and drainage took place after 1766, transforming the swampy agricultural area.
The future parish church, St John's, was built in 1833, and in 1862 the ecclesiastical parish of Newland was established as separate from Cottingham.

Major_Events.Event: Urban spread of Hull reaches Newland
Major_Events.Description: By the beginning of the 20th century, the urban spread of Hull had reached Newland, and over the next half-century, the village was surrounded by housing and other developments.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Kingston upon Hull Municipal Training College
Major_Events.Description: The college was established and later became part of the University of Humberside, now part of Hull University.
The modern Humberside Police headquarters was built in 2012.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Newland features a mix of architectural styles, including Georgian, Victorian, and Arts and Crafts. Notable structures include St John's Church (1833, perpendicular style in yellow brick with ashlar dressings), the former Endsleigh convent (1876, expanded), and the Newland Park Estate (developed c. 1877, with houses in various styles including Arts and Crafts).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Newland is culturally significant as a former village that developed into a suburb of Hull, reflecting the urban expansion and historical development of the area. It includes important educational institutions like Hull University and historical buildings such as St John's Church and the Sailor's Orphan Homes.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential, educational, and commercial area with historical landmarks.
world knowledge.Details: The modern area of Newland includes the former site of the Kingston upon Hull Municipal Training College, Newland Park Estate, Newland Allotments, and Newland Avenue areas. Other notable structures include the former Endsleigh convent, former Sailor's Orphan's Homes, and the modern Humberside Police headquarters. The area is a mixture of housing, educational buildings, and open spaces, including playing fields and allotments.

world knowledge.Name: Jardin des plantes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1635 as the Royal Garden of Medicinal Plants by King Louis XIII, it evolved into France's main botanical garden and the headquarters of the National Museum of Natural History. It played a key role in scientific research, including botany, chemistry, and evolution studies. The garden and its buildings were classified as a national historical landmark in 1993.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as Royal Garden of Medicinal Plants
Major_Events.Description: Founded by an edict of King Louis XIII for medicinal plant research and education.

Major_Events.Event: Transformation into Museum of Natural History
Major_Events.Description: During the French Revolution, the garden was merged with the Cabinet of Natural Sciences to form the Museum of Natural History.
Allied American troops (2nd DB) were stationed here after the Liberation of Paris from Nazi Germany.
The entire garden and its buildings were classified as a monument historique.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features a mix of French formal garden design, Beaux-Arts architecture, and modern iron-and-glass structures. Key buildings include the Grand Gallery of Evolution (iron and glass construction), neoclassical greenhouses, and Art Deco winter gardens. The Gloriette de Buffon is the oldest metallic structure in Paris.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jardin des Plantes is a cornerstone of French scientific history, contributing to botany, evolution theory, and natural sciences. It houses invaluable collections, including 7.5 million plant specimens and 30 million animal specimens. The garden and its museums are often called "the Louvre of the Natural Sciences."
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Botanical research, education, and public display of plant and animal specimens.

Details.Collections: Herbarium (7.5 million plants), zoological specimens (30 million), minerals, and fossils.
Galleries: Gallery of Paleontology and Comparative Anatomy
Gardens: Grand Labyrinth (historic hill with viewing platform)
Details.Zoo: Ménagerie du Jardin des Plantes (founded in 1795), second-oldest public zoo in the world.

world knowledge.Name: Grande Arche
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Grande Arche de la Défense, originally called La Grande Arche de la Fraternité, is a monument and building in the business district of La Défense, west of Paris. It was one of the Grands Projets of François Mitterrand and was designed as a late-20th-century version of the Arc de Triomphe, symbolizing humanity and humanitarian ideals rather than military victories. The construction began in 1985 and was completed in 1989, with its inauguration on July 14, 1989, marking the bicentennial of the French Revolution.

Major_Events.Description: The Grande Arche was inaugurated on July 14, 1989, with grand military parades celebrating the bicentennial of the French Revolution.
The roof section was closed in 2010 following an accident involving marble tiles peeling off. It reopened in 2017 after renovations.
