world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Grande Arche is a 110-meter-high cube with a prestressed concrete frame covered with glass and Bethel Granite. It is turned at an angle of 6.33° about the vertical axis to accommodate its foundations. The void contains skeletal shafts for panoramic lifts and a PTFE-and-fibreglass tensile-membrane sunshade known as the 'Cloud'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Grande Arche completes the line of monuments that forms the Axe historique running through Paris. It symbolizes humanitarian ideals and is a modern counterpart to the Arc de Triomphe.
world knowledge.Details: The Grande Arche houses government offices, including the Bureau d'Enquêtes sur les Événements de Mer (BEAmer) and the French Land Transport Accident Investigation Bureau. The roof features panoramic views of Paris, a restaurant, and an exhibition area dedicated to photojournalism. The original Carrara marble cladding was replaced with Vermont granite due to structural issues caused by freezing temperatures.

world knowledge.Name: Sriwijaya University
world knowledge.Address: Jl. Palembang - Prabumulih Raya KM 32-UNSRI Indralaya, Ogan Ilir, South Sumatra, Indonesia , Indralaya and Palembang , South Sumatra , Indonesia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Indralaya Main Campus: 712 hectares, Bukit Besar Campus: 32.5 hectares
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sriwijaya University (UNSRI) was established on October 29, 1960, and is one of the major state universities in Indonesia. The idea to establish a college in South Sumatra emerged in the early 1950s, leading to the formation of the South Sumatera’s Faculty Committee. The university has grown significantly, with its main campus in Indralaya and a secondary campus in Palembang. UNSRI has achieved high accreditation and international recognition in various university rankings.

Major_Events.Description: Sriwijaya University was officially inaugurated on November 3, 1960, with President Sukarno signing the charter.
The new campus in Indralaya was officially inaugurated by President Suharto on March 6, 1997.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features modern educational facilities spread across its two main campuses. The Indralaya Main Campus is designed to support a wide range of academic and extracurricular activities, while the Bukit Besar Campus serves as a hub for vocational and advanced degree programs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sriwijaya University plays a crucial role in the development and advancement of sciences, technologies, arts, and cultures in Indonesia. It is a center for research and education, contributing significantly to the intellectual and cultural landscape of South Sumatra and beyond.
world knowledge.Details: Sriwijaya University offers a wide range of academic programs across its 10 faculties, including vocational, bachelor, master, and doctoral programs. The university is affiliated with several international educational organizations and has received high accreditation ratings.

world knowledge.Name: Saint John Harbour Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Three spans measuring 125 metres (410 ft), 250 metres (820 ft), and 125 metres (410 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Saint John Harbour Bridge was constructed to address the growing industrial and residential needs in Saint John and surrounding communities. It was built as a cooperative project between federal, provincial, and municipal governments, replacing the old Reversing Falls Bridge. The bridge's location and construction were controversial, impacting navigation and leading to the demolition of historic structures like Union Station.

Major_Events.Description: Contracts for the four main piers were signed in September 1965.
The bridge opened on August 17, 1968, as part of the Saint John Throughway project.
The Harbour Bridge Authority increased the cash-toll from $0.25 to $0.50 for regular commuter traffic.
Tolls were eliminated, and the toll building was later demolished.
An agreement was announced to eliminate the toll, wipe away a $22.6 million debt, and fund $35 million in structural repairs.
Management of the bridge was transferred to the New Brunswick Department of Transportation and Infrastructure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hollow box, haunched girder structure carrying four lanes of traffic across three spans.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a critical infrastructure piece for Saint John, facilitating traffic flow and connecting communities. Its construction and location decisions reflect mid-20th-century urban planning challenges and controversies.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge's construction prevented high-clearance vessels from navigating the upper part of the Saint John Harbour and led to the closure of Navy Island as an island within the Inner Harbour. The tolls, initially set at 25 cents, were eliminated in 2010 after years of debate and financial negotiations.

world knowledge.Name: Hampden House
world knowledge.Address: Great Hampden, between Great Missenden and Princes Risborough, Buckinghamshire
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 14th century (King John's tower), Elizabethan (core), 17th century (rebuilding), 18th century (alterations)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hampden House is a country house named after the Hampden family, who owned the site from before the Norman Conquest until 1938. The house has undergone several phases of construction and alteration, including Elizabethan, 17th-century brick rebuilding, and 18th-century classical additions. The Hampden family faced financial difficulties, leading to the sale of parts of the estate. The house was later used as a school and by Hammer film company before being restored in the late 20th century.

Major_Events.Event: Jousting quarrel involving the Black Prince
Major_Events.Description: Legend states that King Edward III and the Black Prince stayed at Hampden House, where a quarrel during jousting led to the prince being punched by his host, resulting in the forfeiture of some estates to the crown.

Major_Events.Event: John Hampden's refusal to pay Ship Money tax
Major_Events.Description: John Hampden refused to pay the Ship Money tax imposed by Charles I, leading to his prosecution and becoming a public hero known as 'The Patriot'.
Richard Hampden's investment in the South Sea Bubble led to financial ruin for the family, forcing the sale of large parts of the estate.
The house was restored to its former glory after years of deterioration, with state rooms refurbished and upper floors converted into offices (later bedrooms).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house features a mix of architectural styles: 14th-century clunch tower with Gothic windows, Elizabethan core, 17th-century brick rebuilding, and 18th-century classical additions. The north and west ranges showcase Strawberry Hill Gothic. Interior highlights include rococo ceilings, marble fireplaces, and a 60-foot-long Great Hall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hampden House is significant for its long association with the Hampden family, including John Hampden, a key figure in English history. The house reflects centuries of architectural evolution and is a Grade I listed building. It also gained cultural relevance through its use in films and TV series.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a family residence, now used as a wedding venue and occasional filming location.
world knowledge.Details: The grounds feature 'The Glade', an avenue bordered by rhododendrons and ancient oaks, and the parish church with Hampden family memorials. The house is not open to the public but is available for weddings and events.

world knowledge.Name: Tuttle Creek Lake
world knowledge.Area: Flint Hills region of northeast Kansas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tuttle Creek Lake is a reservoir on the Big Blue River built by the Army Corps of Engineers primarily for flood control. It was authorized by the Flood Control Act of 1938, with construction beginning in 1952 after the Great Flood of 1951 highlighted the need for such infrastructure. The lake began filling in 1962, submerging several towns in the process.

Major_Events.Description: This flood inundated Manhattan, Topeka, and Kansas City, causing over $725,000,000 in damages and providing impetus for the construction of Tuttle Creek Dam.
The dam (still under construction) was closed on July 4, 1959, diverting the river through the completed intake tower ('The Tubes').
The partially completed dam contained a record snow melt, preventing an estimated $15,243,000 in damages.
The dam held back floodwaters up to 63 feet above normal, necessitating the first release of the spillway. This event created the 'Little Grand Canyon' formation downstream.
Heavy rains caused high water levels, leading to evacuations but no spillway release. The intake tower discharged a near-record 30,000 cubic feet per second.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The dam is a large earthen embankment with concrete structures including an intake tower ('The Tubes') and a spillway with 18 gates. The spillway features a 600-foot concrete-lined chute followed by a 7,000-foot unlined chute designed to erode during releases.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lake serves as a crucial flood control measure for the Kansas River basin and provides recreational opportunities. It also submerged several towns during its creation, creating a cultural memory of displacement. The spillway erosion during the 1993 flood exposed significant geological formations that are valuable for scientific study.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Flood control, with secondary functions including water conservation, recreation, and maintaining water quality downstream.

Details.Recreational_features: Tuttle Creek State Park with 1,200 acres including nature trails, camping sites, and an artificial beach
Details.Music_festivals: Hosted Country Stampede (1996-2018) and will host Rock The Plains (starting 2025)
Details.Geological_features: Exposes five formations of upper-Carboniferous and lower-Permian rock, showing evidence of ancient marine environments
Details.Seismic_considerations: Dam reinforced in 2010 against potential earthquakes from the nearby Humboldt fault line
Details.Submerged_towns: Cleburne, Randolph, Garrison Cross, and Stockdale (only Randolph was rebuilt elsewhere)

world knowledge.Name: Hobart Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hobart Airport was commissioned in 1956 as the primary regular public transport airport, initially named Llanherne Airport. It was built to replace Cambridge Airport, which was only suitable for light aircraft. The airport has undergone several expansions and upgrades, including runway extensions and terminal developments, to accommodate increasing passenger numbers and larger aircraft.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened as the primary regular public transport airport for Hobart.
The Federal Government corporatised the airport with the establishment of the Federal Airports Corporation.
The runway was upgraded and lengthened to cater for jet aircraft.
The domestic and international terminals were connected to meet new Commonwealth legislation requiring all checked luggage to be X-rayed.
Air New Zealand recommenced direct international flights to Auckland after a hiatus since 1998.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a combined international and domestic terminal with modern facilities. The runway is constructed with an asphaltic concrete surface and is suitable for all Code E aircraft operations. The terminal buildings have been expanded multiple times to accommodate increasing passenger traffic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hobart Airport is the principal airport of Tasmania and serves as a critical gateway for both domestic and international travel. Its southern location makes it an ideal base for flights to Antarctica, supporting Australia's Antarctic research efforts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving domestic and international flights, including regular services to Antarctica.

Details.Owner: Queensland Investment Corporation (35%), Schiphol Group (35%), CareSuper (30%)
Future_Plans: Doubling the size of the terminal
Upgrading the runway to accommodate Airbus A350 and Boeing 787 aircraft
Potential development of a second runway for general aviation

world knowledge.Name: Buntun bridge
world knowledge.Address: Tuguegarao City, Cagayan to Solana, Cagayan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Buntun Bridge was constructed over the Cagayan River, the largest river basin in the Philippines. The project began under President Carlos P. Garcia in 1959, continued under President Diosdado Macapagal, and was completed under President Ferdinand Marcos. It was the longest bridge in the Philippines upon its opening in 1969 until surpassed by the San Juanico Bridge in 1973.

Major_Events.Description: Attended by President Carlos P. Garcia on December 11, 1960.
The bridge was practically completed by May 10, 1969, and opened to vehicular traffic on June 1, 1969, by First Lady Imelda Marcos.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel truss bridge with 14 Japanese steel spans and concrete and asphalt materials. It has a total length of 1,369 m (4,491 ft), a width of 9.60 m (31 ft), and a height of 37 m (121 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Buntun Bridge is a significant infrastructure project that links Tuguegarao City to Solana and serves as a gateway to Cagayan's provincial capital. It is also a monitoring point for water levels during floods and offers picturesque views of the Cagayan River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge forms part of the Santiago–Tuguegarao Road (N51) and is a major junction of the Pan-Philippine Highway. It has become a traffic chokepoint, prompting the construction of additional bridges along the Cagayan River. A popular belief is that the bridge is long enough for a person to recite the entire Philippine National Anthem while traversing.

image_name: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts

world knowledge.Name: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts was established on May 1, 1936, and is located in Tennōji Park. It focuses on Japanese and East Asian art.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its extensive collection of Japanese and East Asian art, with over 8400 items.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's website is osaka-art-museum.jp.

world knowledge.Name: The English Theatre Frankfurt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The English Theatre Frankfurt is continental Europe's largest English-speaking theatre, founded in 1979. It has undergone several relocations and transformations, becoming a significant cultural institution in Frankfurt. The theatre has produced over 190 productions, including German premieres of notable plays and musicals.

Major_Events.Description: Frankfurt's first English-language theatre is founded in Sachsenhausen by Kevin Oakes, Jon Johnson, Mary Jackson, and Ken Elrod.
The theatre moves from Sachsenhausen into a larger space in the Hamburger Allee.
The theatre relocates to a 230-seat facility in Frankfurt's famous Kaiserstraße.

Major_Events.Event: First German theatre to stage a play by August Wilson
Major_Events.Description: The English Theatre in Frankfurt became the first German theatre to stage a play by August Wilson ("Fences").
The theatre moves into its new 300-seat home, sponsored by the Dresdner Bank (now Commerzbank).
Commerzbank files an action for eviction after negotiations with the new investor failed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre has two levels, with a gallery upstairs and a performance space downstairs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The English Theatre Frankfurt is culturally significant as it is the largest English-speaking theatre in continental Europe, promoting English language and theatre education. It has produced numerous premieres and has a diverse audience, including both native German speakers and the English-speaking community.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre produces a mixture of classics, comedies, thrillers, and contemporary plays as well as musicals. It has a casting agent and stage manager based in London, and rehearsals take place in London before continuing in Frankfurt. The theatre also hosts exhibitions, readings, and cabaret shows.

world knowledge.Name: Hallgrímskirkja
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hallgrímskirkja is a Lutheran parish church in Reykjavík, Iceland, named after the Icelandic poet and cleric Hallgrímur Pétursson. Designed by State Architect Guðjón Samúelsson, the church was commissioned in 1937 and completed in 1986. It is the largest church in Iceland and one of the tallest structures in the country. The church's design was inspired by Iceland's landscape, particularly its basalt formations, and it has become a symbol of national identity.

Major_Events.Description: The crypt beneath the choir was consecrated.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of the steeple and wings
Major_Events.Description: The steeple and side wings of the church were completed.
The nave of the church was consecrated, marking the completion of the church.

Major_Events.Event: Installation of the Johannes Klais pipe organ
Major_Events.Description: The large pipe organ built by Johannes Klais was completed and installed in the church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hallgrímskirkja features Expressionist Neo-Gothic architecture, with a distinctly curved spire and side wings. The design resembles Iceland's landscape, particularly its basalt formations. The church consists of a tower, a nave, and a sanctuary, with the sanctuary's cylindrical shape evoking Viking war helmets. The church also has a 74.5-meter (244 ft) tall spire and a 74.37-meter (244 ft) dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hallgrímskirkja is an important symbol of Iceland's national identity. Its unique design, inspired by the country's natural landscape, has made it one of Reykjavík's most recognizable landmarks. The church also houses significant artworks, including a statue of Jesus by Einar Jónsson and a statue of Leif Erikson by Alexander Stirling Calder.
world knowledge.Details: The church includes a carillon of bells, two large pipe organs, and an observation deck with a lift that offers views of Reykjavík and the surrounding mountains. The statue of Leif Erikson in front of the church was a gift from the United States in 1930, commemorating the 1000th anniversary of Iceland's parliament.

image_name: Basilica della Santissima Trinità di Saccargia

world knowledge.Name: Basilica della Santissima Trinità di Saccargia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basilica della Santissima Trinità di Saccargia is a church in Codrongianos, northern Sardinia, Italy. It was finished in 1116 over the ruins of a pre-existing monastery and consecrated on October 5 of the same year. Its construction was ordered by the giudice (judge) of Torres Constantine I and entrusted to Camaldolese monks who founded an abbey here. The church was later enlarged in Pisane style, including the addition of the tall bell tower. The portico on the façade is also probably a late addition, attributed to workers from Lucca. The church was abandoned in the 16th century until it was restored and reopened in the early 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The church was consecrated on October 5, 1116.
The church was restored and reopened after being abandoned in the 16th century.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The construction is entirely in local stone (black basalt and white limestone), with a typical appearance of Pisan Romanesque style. It includes a tall bell tower and a portico on the façade, attributed to workers from Lucca.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Basilica della Santissima Trinità di Saccargia is one of the most important Romanesque sites in Sardinia.

world knowledge.Name: Mark Taper Forum
world knowledge.Address: 135 North Grand Avenue, Los Angeles, California, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mark Taper Forum is a 739-seat thrust stage at the Los Angeles Music Center, designed by Welton Becket and Associates. It opened in 1967 as part of the Los Angeles Music Center, the West Coast equivalent of Lincoln Center. Named for real estate developer Mark Taper, it is operated by the Center Theatre Group alongside the neighboring Ahmanson Theatre and the Kirk Douglas Theatre. The theater has hosted numerous innovative and politically provocative plays since its opening.

Major_Events.Description: The dedication took place on April 9, 1967, at an event attended by Governor Ronald Reagan.
A $30-million renovation led by Rios Clementi Hale Studios was completed, updating the theater's facilities while preserving its circular shape. The theater reopened on August 30, 2008.
In June 2023, the Center Theatre Group announced an indefinite pause of shows at the Mark Taper Forum. It re-opened a year later.
A memorial was held in the actor Richard Jordan's honor on October 8, 1993, the same day his final movie Gettysburg was released.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the style of New Formalism, the perfectly circular Taper features a distinctive decorated drum with a lacy precast relief by Jacques Overhoff. The lobby includes a curving, abalone wall by Tony Duquette. The thrust stage juts into a classical, semicircular amphitheater, creating an intimate relationship between audience and performer.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mark Taper Forum is renowned for its innovative and politically provocative plays, establishing a definition of a 'Taper play' as one which is provocative, political, and liberal. It has hosted world premieres of notable plays and has won 5 Tony Awards.
world knowledge.Details: The auditorium was renamed the Amelia Taper Auditorium after a $2 million gift from the S. Mark Taper Foundation. The theater has presented plays such as 'The Devils,' 'Zoot Suit,' 'Children of a Lesser God,' and 'Angels in America.' The renovation in 2008 increased the number of women's restrooms, updated seating, and improved accessibility.

world knowledge.Name: Bursa Atatürk Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bursa Atatürk Stadium was a multi-purpose stadium in Bursa, Turkey, primarily used for football matches and was the home ground of Bursaspor. The site had a stadium since 1930, with a capacity of 300. The stadium was demolished in 2016 and replaced by the Bursa Metropolitan Stadium.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was extensively refurbished after Bursaspor's Championship winning season 2009–10 to meet UEFA regulations and participate in the 2010-11 UEFA Champions League. The capacity was increased from 18,517 to 25,213, and exterior upgrades were made.
The stadium was demolished in 2016 after the opening of the new Bursa Metropolitan Stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium had a grass surface and underwent renovations in 2010 to increase capacity and meet UEFA standards. The new Bursa Metropolitan Stadium, which replaced it, features a fully covered roof inspired by hexagonal figures from the Green Mosque of Bursa, with sustainable design elements including solar panels and energy-efficient materials.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium was a significant venue for football in Bursa and hosted Bursaspor's matches. It was also a candidate for hosting UEFA Euro 2016. The new stadium, Timsah Arena, is a modern architectural landmark and a meeting point for locals.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was demolished in 2016 and replaced by the Bursa Metropolitan Stadium, which has a seating capacity of 43,761 and features sustainable design elements such as solar panels and energy-efficient materials.

world knowledge.Name: Sovremennik Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Chistoprudny Boulevard 19A Basmanny District, Moscow Russia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sovremennik Theatre was founded in 1956 by a group of young Soviet actors during the Khrushchev Thaw. Among the founders, all of whom graduated from Moscow Art Theatre School-Studio, were Oleg Yefremov, Galina Volchek, Igor Kvasha, Liliya Tolmachyova, Yevgeny Yevstigneyev and Oleg Tabakov. The debut production was Victor Rozov's play Forever Alive. The theatre's first artistic director, Oleg Yefremov, left in 1970. It was then led by Galina Volchek until her death.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was founded by a group of young Soviet actors, including Oleg Yefremov, Galina Volchek, Igor Kvasha, Liliya Tolmachyova, Yevgeny Yevstigneyev, and Oleg Tabakov, during the Khrushchev Thaw. The debut production was Victor Rozov's play Forever Alive.
The theatre's first artistic director, Oleg Yefremov, left the theatre.
After Oleg Yefremov's departure, Galina Volchek became the leader of the theatre until her death.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sovremennik Theatre is culturally significant as it was founded during the Khrushchev Thaw, a period of relative liberalization in the Soviet Union. It has been a prominent venue for contemporary theatre in Russia, showcasing works by notable playwrights and actors.
world knowledge.Details: The name "Sovremennik" means "Contemporary". The theatre is accessible via public transit at Chistye Prudy, Turgenevskaya, and Sretensky Bulvar stations of the Moscow Metro.

world knowledge.Name: Béthanie (Hong Kong)
world knowledge.Address: 139, Pok Fu Lam Road, Hong Kong Island
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Béthanie was built in 1875 as a sanatorium by the Paris Foreign Missions Society for priests and missionaries to recover from tropical diseases. It later served various purposes, including a printing press, university storage, and now as part of the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. It was declared a monument in 2013.

Major_Events.Description: Japanese troops ransacked the building, confiscated goods, and forced the missionaries to leave. The grounds were devastated, and the building was left bare.
The Fathers sold Béthanie to Hongkong Land for redevelopment, but the site was deemed too difficult to develop. It was later acquired by the Hong Kong government under a demolition order.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration by Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts
Major_Events.Description: After a three-year restoration project costing HK$80 million, Béthanie reopened as part of the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, housing educational facilities, performance venues, and a museum.
Béthanie was officially declared a monument, recognizing its historical and architectural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Gothic style with symmetrical cylinders, ogive, tracery, stained glass, and Gothic arched windows. Features include high ceilings, pitched roofs, flying buttresses, and rib vaults. The George C. Tso Memorial Chapel is a notable example of neo-Gothic architecture within the complex.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Béthanie is one of Hong Kong's few examples of French colonial architecture and represents the cultural interchange between Eastern and Western influences. It played a significant role in the history of French missionaries in Asia and contributed to the development of Hong Kong's architectural identity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a sanatorium for missionaries, now serves as part of the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, housing educational facilities, performance venues, a chapel, and a museum.
world knowledge.Details: Béthanie includes the George C. Tso Memorial Chapel, Béthanie Theatre, School of Film and Television, Museum of Béthanie, Jackie Chan Screening Room, and Sir Y.K. Pao Studio. It received a UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Award in 2008 for its restoration. The site also has historical ties to the discovery of Hong Kong's floral emblem, the bauhinia.

world knowledge.Name: Bhisho Airport
world knowledge.Address: Right side of the N2 national road toward Peddie
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bhisho Airport, also known as Bulembu Airport, is a local airport in Eastern Cape, South Africa, which serves Bhisho and King William's Town. The airport was the hub of the short-lived Ciskei International Airways from 1986 to 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The President of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), President Sheik Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, landed at the airport following a R20 million upgrade paid for by the UAE. The landing was controversial as it followed the announcement that the UAE had released the Gupta family from custody and so would not be extraditing them to face charges for state capture in South Africa.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Runway (08/26) is 2,500 m long with asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is significant for its role in regional transportation and its historical association with Ciskei International Airways.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Local airport serving Bhisho and King William's Town.
Notable_Visitors: Sheik Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
world knowledge.Details: Bhisho Airport lies 594 m (1,950 ft) above sea level. The airport was controversially used by the President of the UAE in 2023 amid political tensions related to the Gupta family extradition case.

world knowledge.Name: Ullswater
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ullswater is a glacial lake in Cumbria, England and part of the Lake District National Park. It is the second largest lake in the region by both area and volume, after Windermere. The lake was formed after the last ice age by a glacier scooping out the valley floor, which then filled with meltwater. Ullswater was formed by three glaciers. The origin of the name Ullswater is uncertain, with theories suggesting it may derive from Old Norse personal name Ulfr or the Norse god Ullr.

Major_Events.Event: Visit of Wilhelm II, German Emperor
Major_Events.Description: Wilhelm II visited Ullswater and toured the lake on the MY Raven, which was re-fitted to act as a royal yacht.

Major_Events.Event: World water speed record set by Donald Campbell
Major_Events.Description: Donald Campbell set the world water speed record on Ullswater on 23 July 1955, when he piloted the jet-propelled hydroplane 'Bluebird K7' to a speed of 202.32 mph (325.53 km/h).
A 20 miles (32 km) walking route the Ullswater Way was officially opened in 2016 by writer and broadcaster Eric Robson.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Ullswater is a typical Lake District 'ribbon lake', formed by glacial activity, with surrounding hills giving it the shape of an extenuated 'Z' with three segments or reaches winding through them.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ullswater has been a tourist destination since the mid-18th century and became a fashionable holiday destination for the British aristocracy by the 1890s. It is also significant for its association with William Wordsworth, who was inspired to write his famous poem 'Daffodils' after seeing daffodils growing on the shores of Ullswater.
world knowledge.Details: Ullswater is home to the Ullswater Yacht Club and the Lord Birkett Memorial Trophy, held annually on the first weekend in July. The lake also features the Aira Force waterfall and is partly within the National Trust's Ullswater and Aira Force property. In 1962, Lord Birkett led a campaign to prevent Ullswater from becoming a reservoir, and he is commemorated with a plaque on Kailpot Crag.

world knowledge.Name: Hortobágy National Park
world knowledge.Address: Counties of Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén, Heves, Hajdú-Bihar and Jász-Nagykun-Szolnok, Hungary
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hortobágy is an 800 km² national park in eastern Hungary, rich with folklore and cultural history. It was designated as a national park in 1973 (the first in Hungary) and elected among the World Heritage Sites in 1999. The park is Hungary's largest protected area and the largest semi-natural grassland in Europe. The site was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999 because of its long cultural history (stretching back more than four millennia), its scenery, and its testimony to traditional methods of pastoralism.

Major_Events.Description: Hortobágy was designated as the first national park in Hungary.

Major_Events.Event: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List
Major_Events.Description: Hortobágy was recognized as a World Heritage Site due to its cultural history and natural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features traditional T-shaped sweep wells, the Nine-holed Bridge, and a landscape dotted with mirages of trees shimmering in the reflected heat of the puszta (steppe).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hortobágy is culturally significant for its long history of traditional pastoralism, its unique landscape, and its role in Hungarian folklore. It also serves as a dark sky preserve and is home to various species of wildlife.
world knowledge.Details: Hortobágy is a steppe with Hungarian Grey cattle, racka, Italian Mediterranean buffalo, and Nonius horses tended by mounted herdsmen called Csikós. It provides habitat for various species including Roe deer, European wildcat, Red fox, European ground squirrel, and 342 species of birds. The area is also an important stopover site for migratory species of birds. Additionally, the park is home to a herd of Przewalski's horses, a breeding center for Taurus cattle, and an animal hospital and zoo for rescued animals.

world knowledge.Name: Vilkolakis Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vilkolakis Theatre, also known as Werewolf Theatre, was a private experimental theater in Kaunas, Lithuania. Established as an artists' club in 1919, it evolved into a cabaret show and theater under the leadership of Antanas Sutkus. Known for its parodies and satires of current events, the theatre closed in 1925 due to financial difficulties and government troubles.

Major_Events.Description: Founded on 4 May 1919 as a club for artists, with notable founders including Vytautas Pranas Bičiūnas, Kazys Binkis, and Balys Sruoga.
First theatre performances directed by Antanas Sutkus on 18 January 1920.
Under Sutkus' leadership, Vilkolakis started organizing cabaret evenings featuring improvised theatre performances satirizing Lithuanian politics and culture.
In November 1921, the cabaret evenings grew into an experimental theatre with more scripted performances.
The play criticized the War School of Kaunas and military officers, leading to accusations against Sutkus and the eventual closure of the theatre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre operated in a rented 238-seat hall on Maironis Street in Kaunas. Performances incorporated elements of Lithuanian folklore, Italian commedia dell'arte, and Russian cabaret, combining parody, caricature, grotesque, and pantomime.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vilkolakis Theatre was culturally significant for its sharp political and social commentary, blending entertainment with critique. It played a key role in Lithuanian interwar theatre, despite its short existence.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre struggled financially and faced government opposition. Many performances were improvised and not recorded, making historical reconstruction difficult. Only two scripted plays were published, with several surviving in manuscripts and many others lost. The theatre frequently toured Lithuanian cities, incorporating local events into its plays.

world knowledge.Name: Brno City Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brno City Theatre (Czech: Městské divadlo Brno; MdB) is a repertoire theatre in Brno, Czech Republic, that focuses on dramatic and music production, mainly musical theatre. The former Svobodné divadlo (Free Theatre) on Falkensteiner Street was founded closely after World War II, in summer 1945, by people around director Milan Pásek, supported by professor Jiří Kroha. Since its beginning it hosted mainly young artists, which sought to found second theatre in the city (the first one was Mahenovo divadlo (Mahen Theatre), where they could perform plays by contemporary writers. The theatre has changed its name by the time: Městské a oblastní divadlo (Municipal and Regional Theatre), Krajské oblastní divadlo (County and regional theatre) and in 1962 Divadlo bratří Mrštíků (Mrštík Brothers Theatre). In 1988, by decision of a new regulation, the theatre was merged with some quite genre different theatres – satirical theatre Večerní Brno and puppet theatre Loutkové divadlo Radost. After the Velvet revolution the theatre was renamed the Městské divadlo Brno (Municipal Theatre Brno) and in 1990 Jan Kolegar was elected as its director. Jan Moša, former producer, dramatist and since 1990 the artistic director of drama, became the director in 1992. He was responsible for the reconstruction of insufficient places at former cinema on Lidická street, where the theatre now resides.

Major_Events.Description: The MdB went through reconstruction, mainly modification of the theatre scene itself. In addition to changes of building the ensemble of theatre was also renewed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Roman Mach and Josef Kubín – musical scene Heinrich Fanta – dramatical scene Miroslav Melena – dramatical sc. reconstruction
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The MdB is one of the theatres with very good ensemble and wide audience. The actors of this theatre were awarded with several Thalia Awards and Alfréd Radok Awards. The theatre has even walk of fame for its most brilliant actors since 2000.
world knowledge.Details: The building of the theatre is located on Lidická street in town square Brno-center. It has two acting areas – dramatical scene (capacity 365 places) and musical theatre scene (capacity 680 places). As of 2011, the manager and director of the theatre is Stanislav Moša, art manager of the musical ensemble is Petr Gazdík and operetta manager is Igor Ondříček. The theatre also has its own orchestra, so the audience can experience live scenic music. In the 1990s the MdB has focused mainly on quality musical theatre production, using graduates of the musical acting classes at the Janáček Academy of Music and Performing Arts. There are many different art pieces in both of theaters musical and dramatic repertoire, lot of space is dedicated for many new works, which are often written directly for MdB. The classical pieces (e.g., Devotion to the Cross by Pedro Calderón de la Barca) are also played often.

world knowledge.Name: Ho Technical University
world knowledge.Address: Ho Municipal District, Volta Region, Ghana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ho Technical University, formerly Ho Polytechnic, is a public tertiary institution in the Volta Region of Ghana. It started in 1968 as a technical institute providing pre-technical education. By 1972, it upgraded its courses and in 1986, it became a Polytechnic. It gained full tertiary institution status in 1993 under the Polytechnic Law 321, which was replaced in 2007 by the Polytechnics Act (Act 745). The university offers Master of Technology (MTech), Bachelor of Technology (BTech), Higher National Diploma (HND), and Non-Tertiary Programmes.

Major_Events.Description: The institution was upgraded from a technical institute to a Polytechnic.
The institution became a fully-fledged tertiary institution under the Polytechnic Law 321.
The Polytechnic Law 321 was replaced by the Polytechnics Act (Act 745).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ho Technical University is one of the premier national tertiary institutions in the Volta Region, providing advanced education in technical, business, and vocational disciplines.
world knowledge.Details: The university has five faculties and offers Master of Technology (MTech) Programmes affiliated with the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) on a sandwich basis.

world knowledge.Name: Nonnberg Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nonnberg Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in Salzburg, Austria. Founded around 712/715 by Saint Rupert of Salzburg, it is the oldest continuously existing nunnery in the German-speaking world. The monastery complex is a protected monument and part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.

Major_Events.Description: The abbey church was re-built after a blaze in 1006, with the support of Emperor Henry II, who attended the consecration in 1009.
The abbey church was largely destroyed in a fire of 1423 and was reconstructed between 1464 and 1509.
The church underwent a refurbishment in the Baroque style in the 1880s.
The Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg, including Nonnberg Abbey, was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Abbey was selected as the main motif for the Austrian Nonnberg Abbey commemorative coin, the first in the 'Great Abbeys of Austria' series.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey features Romanesque and Gothic architectural styles. The late Gothic winged altar with the statue of Mary is the centrepiece of the abbey church.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nonnberg Abbey is culturally and historically significant as the oldest continuously existing nunnery in the German-speaking world and part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Salzburg. It is also notable for its association with Maria von Trapp, whose life inspired 'The Sound of Music'.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey's endowment was provided by the Agilolfing duke Theodo of Bavaria and his successor Theodbert. The nuns, all of noble birth, held extended estates up the Salzach river in the south of the city. The obligation of nobility for the nuns was abolished in 1848. The convent's possessions were later augmented by Emperor Henry II. The Benedictine rule was implemented under Archbishop Conrad I of Salzburg in the early 12th century. The nuns sing Gregorian Chorals every morning. About 195 manuscripts dating from the 14th to the 18th century have been copied to film by the Hill Museum and Manuscript Library. Some scenes from 'The Sound of Music' were filmed at the abbey.

world knowledge.Name: Vamizi Island
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vamizi Island, originally called Amisa, was visited by Arab sailors in the 15th century. Portuguese traders were attracted by its Maluane cloth industry. Other industries included indigo, timber, ivory, manna gum, and turtle shells. In the early 1990s, conservation efforts began, and in 2006, the Vamizi Island Lodge was opened by Nelson Mandela.

Major_Events.Description: In September 2020, Vamizi Island was captured by ISIL-aligned militants. Residents were evicted, and tourist hotels were destroyed. The island was recaptured by Mozambican forces later that month.
The Vamizi Island Lodge, a sixteen-room luxury hotel, was opened by Nelson Mandela, establishing the island as a leading luxury resort in East Africa.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vamizi Island is recognized for its luxury tourism and conservation projects, including protection of coral reefs, reef fish, and turtle populations. It is also historically significant for its early industries and trade.
world knowledge.Details: Vamizi Island is home to over 180 species of coral and 400 species of reef fish. It features some of the best-unspoilt coral reefs, including 'Neptune's Arm,' considered one of the world's top ten dive sites. The island has six private villas and has created numerous jobs for the local population through construction projects.

world knowledge.Name: Eiffel Bridge, Ungheni
world knowledge.Address: between Ungheni, Moldova and Ungheni, Romania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Eiffel Bridge is a bridge over the River Prut and a checkpoint between Moldova and Romania. It was initially built for railway purposes and later became a strategic construction. The first metal bridge was designed by Russian engineer Nikolai Belelubsky and completed in 1876. It was used by Russian troops in 1877 but only came into civilian use in 1881 after a prolonged testing process. The bridge was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times during World War II.

Major_Events.Description: A Russian diplomatic agent and Gheorghe Costaforu signed a rail junction convention, ratified in 1873.
The Iași-Ungheni railway was opened.
The Chișinău-Cornești-Ungheni railway was opened by the Russian Empire in preparation for the Russo-Turkish War.
The first metal bridge was completed.
The bridge came into civilian use after a 5-year testing process.
The bridge was blown up by retreating Russian troops.
The bridge was rebuilt for the needs of German-Romanian troops.
The bridge was bombed.
The bridge was rebuilt by the Russians.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Metal bridge designed by Russian engineer Nikolai Belelubsky.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a strategically positioned construction and serves as a checkpoint between Moldova and Romania, playing a significant role in regional transportation and history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway and road bridge, border checkpoint
world knowledge.Details: Today, the bridge remains a strategically positioned construction under the supervision of border guards.

world knowledge.Name: Accra Sports Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Accra Sports Stadium, formerly named the Ohene Djan Stadium, is a multi-use stadium located in Accra, Ghana, mostly used for association football matches. It was inaugurated in 1962 by a football match played between Accra XI and Kumasi XI. The stadium was renamed after Ohene Djan, the country's first Director of Sports, in 2004 after renovations. Its renaming was controversial and opposed by the Ga people. The name was changed back to 'Accra Sports Stadium' in 2011 without any official announcement. It has since been reverted. The stadium was rebuilt, upgraded, and modernized to meet FIFA standards for the 2008 African Cup of Nations, with work completed in October 2007. It was inaugurated with a four-nation tournament that Ghana won (the Zenith Cup).

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated by a football match played between Accra XI and Kumasi XI.
The stadium was renamed after Ohene Djan, the country's first Director of Sports, after renovations.

Major_Events.Event: Name change back to Accra Sports Stadium
Major_Events.Description: The name 'Ohene Djan Stadium' on the stadium building was changed to 'Accra Sports Stadium' without any official announcement.
The stadium was rebuilt, upgraded, and modernized to meet FIFA standards for the 2008 African Cup of Nations.

Ghanaian David Kotei, the World Boxing Council's world Featherweight champion, lost his championship to Mexican-American Danny Lopez by a 15 rounds unanimous decision. The event featured a bout between Sulley Shittu and Felix Figueroa, which Shittu won by 8 rounds decision. The crowd for this event has been estimated at over 100,000 fans.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a grass surface and was designed by architects Alexander Barov and Mrs. Lomax.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Accra Sports Stadium is culturally and historically important as a major sports venue in Ghana. It has hosted significant events such as the 2008 African Cup of Nations, the 1978 African Cup of Nations final, and numerous professional boxing events. It is also the home of one of Africa's most popular football clubs, Hearts of Oak, and has been a venue for Ghana's national team matches.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium, primarily for association football matches and rugby union.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is also the home of Accra Lions FC and Great Olympics. During the 2000 African Cup of Nations in Ghana and Nigeria, the stadium hosted nine matches. As of August 2020, the venue has hosted 91 professional boxing programs.

image_name: Church of Our Lady of Victories

world knowledge.Name: Church of Our Lady of Victories
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Church of Our Lady of Victories, also known as the Shrine of the Infant Jesus of Prague, was originally built as a chapel dedicated to the Holy Trinity in 1584. It was later expanded into a larger church for German Lutherans around 1611. After the Battle of White Mountain in 1620, the church was re-Catholicized and consecrated to Our Lady of Victories and Saint Anthony of Padua in 1624. The church has undergone several reconstructions and is now administered by the Discalced Carmelites.

Major_Events.Event: Consecration to Our Lady of Victories
Major_Events.Description: The church was consecrated to Our Lady of Victories and Saint Anthony of Padua after the Counter-Reformation.

Major_Events.Event: Pontifical Coronation of the Infant Jesus of Prague
Major_Events.Description: Pope Leo XII granted the first pontifical decree of canonical coronation to the Infant Jesus of Prague.
Pope Benedict XVI crowned the image of the Infant Jesus of Prague during his Apostolic visit to the Czech Republic.
The Discalced Carmelites returned to the church after two hundred years of absence.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is built in the Baroque style with a front facade constructed in 1664, featuring a statue of Our Lady with the Child Jesus above the entrance. A tower was added in 1669. The interior includes the Chapel of Our Lady and the Chapel of the Holy Cross, with altar paintings by Petr Brandl.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is culturally significant as the home of the Infant Jesus of Prague, a revered statue with a widespread cultus, particularly in Spain. It is also part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Prague's Historic Center.
world knowledge.Details: The church houses a museum related to the Infant of Prague and is under the parish administration of the Church of St. Thomas in Mala Strana. The former monastery now serves as the office of the Ministry of Education, Youth, and Sports.

world knowledge.Name: Shah-Do Shamshira Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shah-Do Shamshira Mosque, translating to Mosque of the King of Two Swords, was built during the reign of Amanullah Khan (1919–1929). It was modelled after the Ortaköy Mosque in Istanbul and features Italian decorative stucco, described as ‘Afghan Baroque’. The mosque is located next to the tomb of Chin Timur Khan, a Mughal general and cousin of Babur, who played a significant role in the Battle of Khanwa. The area also includes the tombs of Babur and other prominent Muslim commanders who invaded India from Afghanistan.

Major_Events.Description: Farkhunda Malikzada was murdered at the shrine on 19 March 2015.
The mosque was fully renovated in June 2021.

Major_Events.Event: Assassination Attempt on Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada
Major_Events.Description: In May 2024, the Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF) claimed to have carried out an assassination attempt against Taliban leader Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada while he was visiting the mosque, resulting in the death of three of his special security guards and injury to another.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque is a yellow two-story structure with Italian decorative stucco, creating an ‘Afghan Baroque’ effect. Its design is unusual for Islamic religious architecture and was modelled after the Ortaköy Mosque in Istanbul.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is culturally significant due to its unique architectural style and its location next to the tomb of Chin Timur Khan, a prominent Mughal general. It also serves as a reminder of the historical Muslim conquests in India and the establishment of Muslim rule over northern India.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque is located on Andarabi Road, just off the Kabul River and the Shah-Do Shamshira bridge in the center of Kabul. It is situated next to the tomb of Chin Timur Khan and near the tombs of Babur and other prominent Muslim commanders.

world knowledge.Name: Trowbridge House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed in 1859 as the residence of William P. Trowbridge, sold in 1869. Leased by the U.S. government in the early 20th century for office space, purchased in 1950. Housed various government offices including the Commission of Fine Arts, The President’s Drug Advisory Council, White House Millennium Council, and others. Renovated in 2015 to serve as a presidential residence for former U.S. presidents visiting the capital.

Major_Events.Description: Built as the residence of William P. Trowbridge.
Purchased by the United States government for office use.
Renovated to serve as a residence for former U.S. presidents visiting Washington, D.C.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Italianate architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Serves as a historic building with government and presidential significance, replacing the Presidential Townhouse as a guest residential facility for former presidents.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official residence for former U.S. presidents visiting Washington, D.C.
world knowledge.Details: Abuts the back of the President's Guest House (Blair House) and is next to 712 Jackson Place, which houses the Harry S. Truman Scholarship Foundation.

world knowledge.Name: Miller Theater (Philadelphia)
world knowledge.Address: 250 S. Broad St. Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as the Sam S. Shubert Theatre in 1918 by The Shubert Organization to memorialize their brother Sam, who died in a railroad accident. The theater has undergone several ownership changes and renovations, including modernization in 1986 and renaming in 1991 to honor John W. Merriam. In 2022, it was renamed Miller Theater after Alan B. Miller donated funds for restorations.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened with a road production of the musical 'Chu Chin Chow' featuring Florence Reed.

Major_Events.Event: Ownership transfer to the Academy of Music
Major_Events.Description: The theater came under the ownership of the Academy of Music and later the University of the Arts.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by the Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts
Major_Events.Description: The theater was purchased by the Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts, now The Philadelphia Orchestra and Ensemble Arts.
The theater was renamed in honor of Alan B. Miller, a founding board member of the Kimmel Center, who donated funds for restorations and upgrades.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building stands seven stories high with the theater on the first level and six floors used for offices and classrooms. Designed by architect Herbert J. Krapp, it reused the marble staircase from the demolished Horticultural Hall in its interior design. Renovations were made in 1958, and the stage and sound were modernized in 1986.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Miller Theater is Philadelphia's most continuous location for touring Broadway shows and has hosted numerous acclaimed Broadway, off-Broadway, and one-night performances. It has been a cultural hub featuring performances by notable artists such as George Gershwin, Al Jolson, John Barrymore, Helen Hayes, Katharine Hepburn, Sammy Davis Jr., Angela Lansbury, and Laurence Olivier.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venue for Broadway shows, concerts, and other theatrical performances.
world knowledge.Details: The theater is located within the Avenue of the Arts cultural district. It has a capacity of 1,870 and has been active since 1918. Public transit options include SEPTA buses and PATCO Speedline.

world knowledge.Name: Niranjan Shah Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium, it was later renamed Khandheri Cricket Stadium and eventually Niranjan Shah Stadium in 2024. It is Gujarat's first solar-powered stadium and was built to host first-class and international cricket matches. The stadium was constructed on agricultural land acquired in 2004 and became operational in 2008.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted its first international match, an ODI between India and England.
Hosted its first T20I match between India and Australia, which India won by six wickets.
Hosted its first Test match between India and England, which ended in a draw.
The stadium was renamed in honor of Niranjan Shah, a former first-class cricketer and honorary secretary of the Saurashtra Cricket Association.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: State-of-the-art cricket stadium with a media box designed similarly to Lord's Cricket Ground in London. Features include spacious dressing rooms with luxurious seating, multiple aisles and entrances for spectator movement, and a 90-yard outfield. The West Stand and Pavilion Stand have over 60 hospitality boxes. The stadium is part of a larger sports complex planned to include venues for other sports.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant cricket venue in India, hosting international and domestic matches. It is also notable for being Gujarat's first solar-powered stadium, contributing to sustainability efforts in sports infrastructure.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cricket stadium hosting international, domestic, and first-class matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 28,000 spectators and is owned and operated by the Saurashtra Cricket Association. It features two playing fields: a main one with a 90-yard outfield and a smaller one with a 70-yard outfield for practice and district-level matches. The stadium has implemented a solar rooftop system generating 82,000 units annually, saving approximately ₹54,600 monthly in electricity bills. Future plans include expanding green power generation and establishing an academy.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio São Januário
world knowledge.Address: Vasco da Gama, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: São Januário, officially Estádio Vasco da Gama, was built as the home ground of CR Vasco da Gama after the club faced racial discrimination in the 1920s. It became a symbol of resistance against racism in Brazil and was the largest stadium in the Americas until 1930. It also holds historical importance as Brazilian president Getúlio Vargas delivered speeches here, including announcing the first Brazilian work laws.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated on April 21, 1927, with a match between Vasco and Santos, which Santos won. It was the largest stadium in the Americas at the time.
President Getúlio Vargas used the stadium's tribune to announce the first Brazilian work laws.
The São Januario Aquatics Centre hosted an event of the FINA Swimming World Cup.
After years of derbies being held at Maracanã, Vasco played a derby against Flamengo at São Januário, winning 1–0.
The Municipal Chamber of Rio de Janeiro approved a renovation project for São Januário, with plans to increase capacity to 48,000–57,000 fans.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was designed by architect Ricardo Severo and features a grass field, a main court with 2,500 seats, a smaller secondary court (forninho), an aquatic center, and a chapel (Capela de Nossa Senhora das Vitórias). The trophy room houses approximately 8,000 trophies and memorabilia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: São Januário is a symbol of resistance against racism in Brazil, stemming from Vasco da Gama's refusal to dismiss Black players in the 1920s. It also holds historical importance due to its use by President Getúlio Vargas for major announcements. The stadium has a deep connection with the local favela, Barreira do Vasco, where the club runs social projects.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium and multi-sport complex (swimming, other events).
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was the largest in Brazil until 1940 and the largest in Rio de Janeiro until 1950. It has undergone renovations in 2006 and 2012, with further expansions planned. The chapel on-site is considered so important that renovation plans excluding it have been rejected. The stadium is also a hub for the local community, with many residents employed by the club and dependent on matchday commerce.

world knowledge.Name: Little Belt Bridge (1970)
world knowledge.Area: Between Jutland (Jylland) and the island of Funen (Fyn)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,700 metres long, 33.3 metres wide, 120 metres high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The New Little Belt Bridge was built to alleviate congestion on the Old Little Belt Bridge due to increasing car traffic between Jutland and Funen. It was opened by King Frederik IX on 21 October 1970.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened by King Frederik IX on 21 October 1970.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a main span of 600 metres, pylons reaching 120 metres, and a maximum clearance of 44 metres from the sea. The bridge has heating in the road deck to keep it free of ice and snow in winter.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a vital transportation link between Jutland and Funen, and it has been featured in popular culture, such as in the film 'The Olsen Gang in Jutland.'
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Motorway bridge carrying the European route E20 with three-lane carriageways.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is toll-free and features six lanes. It was designed by Orla Mølgaard-Nielsen and appears in the film 'The Olsen Gang in Jutland' at 0:12:11, marking the Olsen Gang's arrival to Jutland.

world knowledge.Name: St. Thomas Cathedral Basilica, Chennai
world knowledge.Address: 38 Santhome High Road, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Thomas Cathedral Basilica, officially known as St Thomas Cathedral Basilica and National Shrine of Saint Thomas, is a minor basilica of the Catholic Church in India. The present structure dates back to 1523 AD, built by the Portuguese over the tomb of Thomas the Apostle. It was renovated in 1896 in the Neo-Gothic style favoured by British architects in the late 19th century. The church was made a cathedral in 1606 by Pope Paul V and was elevated to the dignity of a minor basilica in 1956 by Pope Pius XII. It was declared a National Shrine in 2004 by the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India.

Major_Events.Description: The church was consecrated in 1523 after being built by the Portuguese over the tomb of Thomas the Apostle.
Francis Xavier visited the shrine and lived for about one year in the presbytery of the Santhome Church before leaving for his mission in Ilha Formosa (Taiwan).
The church was made a cathedral in 1606 by Pope Paul V with the creation of the Diocese of Saint Thomas of Mylapore.
The church was rebuilt in 1896 by the British in the style of Gothic Revival architecture.
Pope Pius XII honoured the cathedral church by elevating it to the dignity and rank of a minor basilica.

Major_Events.Event: Visit of Pope John Paul II
Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II visited the church in 1986.
The church was declared a National Shrine in 2004 by the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church exhibits the Gothic Revival architecture style of the late 19th century. It has a rib vault ceiling made of teak wood, with marble and granite used in other parts of the construction. The church features 16 windows and 34 stained glass panels, with a main stained glass over the altar representing Thomas the Apostle touching the wound of Christ. The statue in the main altar represents 'Thomas the Apostle as priest and Jesus Christ as king'. The church has two spires, with the primary spire serving as a bell tower and the second spire indicating the position of the believed tomb of Thomas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is culturally and historically significant as it is built over the tomb of Thomas the Apostle, who is believed to have come to South Asia to preach the Gospel. It is a major pilgrimage site for Catholics and has been recognized as a National Shrine. The church also holds relics claimed to be of Thomas the Apostle and features a 200-year-old British pipe organ.
world knowledge.Details: The church has an adoration chapel for silent moments before the Blessed Sacrament. A gold-painted wooden statue of Mother Mary, referred to as Our Lady of Mylapore, was brought from Lisbon in 1523. The feast of Mylai Matha is celebrated in December with special prayers, procession, rosary, and benediction. A wooden pole at the church is believed by worshippers to have been washed ashore and erected by Thomas the Apostle, which they believe saved the church from the 2004 tsunami.

world knowledge.Name: Zadar Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of St. Anastasia is the Roman Catholic cathedral of Zadar, Croatia, and the largest church in Dalmatia. Its origins date back to a Christian basilica built in the 4th and 5th centuries, with the current structure largely constructed in the Romanesque style during the 12th and 13th centuries. The cathedral has been submitted to UNESCO's Tentative List of World Heritage Sites. It holds the relics and sarcophagus of Saint Anastasia, received during the time of Bishop Donatus. The cathedral was heavily damaged during the siege of Zadar in 1202 and underwent significant repairs throughout the 13th century. It was reconsecrated in 1285 and completed in 1324. The bell tower was built in two stages, with the upper floors completed in 1893.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was heavily damaged during the siege by the Venetians and Crusaders.
The cathedral was reconsecrated after extensive repairs following the siege.
The bell tower was completed under the design of Sir Thomas Graham Jackson.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Pope John Paul II
Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II visited the cathedral on one of his last international travels.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The façade, completed in 1324, has two orders with three portals, a large Romanesque-style rose window, and a smaller Gothic-style rose window. The interior has a nave and two aisles separated by stone pillars and pylons. The presbytery is elevated, with a 12th-century crypt beneath it. The church includes a hexagonal baptistery, a chapel of St. Barbara, and a bell tower built in two stages. The cathedral also houses various altars, statues, and frescoes, including the Zadar Polyptych by Vittore Carpaccio.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is the largest church in Dalmatia and holds significant religious and historical importance as the seat of the Archdiocese of Zadar. It houses the relics of Saint Anastasia and has been a site of major historical events, including the siege of Zadar and visits by notable figures such as Pope John Paul II. Its architectural and artistic elements, including the Zadar Polyptych, contribute to its cultural value.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral has been submitted to UNESCO's Tentative List of World Heritage Sites. It includes a hexagonal baptistery restored in 1989 after being destroyed in the 1943 bombing of Zadar. The museum of art within the church houses the Zadar Polyptych, an early work by Venetian painter Vittore Carpaccio.

world knowledge.Name: Tribhuvan International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Gauchaur Airport, it was established in 1949. The first flight landed on 23 April 1949. It was renamed Tribhuvan Airport in 1955 and later Tribhuvan International Airport in 1964. It has been a significant hub for international and domestic flights in Nepal.

Major_Events.Description: The first flight landed at Gauchaur Airport on 23 April 1949.
The first charter flight took place between Gauchaur and Calcutta on 20 February 1950.
The first scheduled service linked Kathmandu to Patna, Kolkata, and Delhi on 20 February 1950.
The airport was inaugurated by King Mahendra and renamed Tribhuvan Airport.
Tribhuvan International Airport witnessed its first jet aircraft, a Lufthansa Boeing 707.
The first Concorde landed at Tribhuvan International Airport on 11 October 1987.
Airport surveillance radar (ASR) and secondary surveillance radar (SSR) were officially inaugurated on 9 September 1998.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a single 3,350 metres runway with a slope of 1.2%. It has two terminals: one for international and one for domestic traffic. The international terminal can handle up to 1350 departing passengers per hour, while the domestic terminal has a capacity of 765 passengers per hour.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As Nepal's main international airport, it serves as a crucial gateway for tourism and commerce, connecting Nepal to over 40 destinations in 17 countries. It is also a starting point for Mount Everest international tourists.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is located 1 km from Pashupatinath Temple and 6 km east of the city centre. It is a hub for several airlines, including Nepal Airlines and Himalaya Airlines. The airport has undergone several expansions and upgrades, including the extension of the runway and the construction of new terminals.

world knowledge.Name: University of Guilan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Guilan was founded in 1974 as a collaborative effort between Iran and West Germany. It began with 170 students and 10 faculty members in the faculty of engineering and faculty of literature, offering courses such as Civil Engineering and German Literature.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Recognized as the largest and one of the most premier academic institutions in northern Iran, the University of Guilan plays a significant role in higher education and research in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Guilan offers degrees in 55 fields for Bachelors, 35 fields for Masters, and seven fields for PhD studies. It has a department in Caspian Sea studies and publishes the Caspian Journal of Environmental Sciences. The university is spread over four campuses housing nine faculties, as well as an International Campus and some research centers.

world knowledge.Name: Lavaca County Courthouse
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by LaGrange, 2nd, 3rd, and Main Sts., Hallettsville, Texas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lavaca County Courthouse is the fifth structure serving as county seat for Lavaca County, originally "La Baca" County. It was built in 1897 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its historical and architectural significance.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as a Texas State Antiquities Landmark
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was further recognized for its historical importance at the state level.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Richardsonian Romanesque-style courthouse, strongly influenced by H.H. Richardson's design of the Allegheny County Courthouse in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is a raised three-story limestone building, cruciform in plan, with a hipped roof and pyramidal roofs and dormers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its architectural style and its role as the county seat of Lavaca County. It reflects the historical development and governance of the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serving as the county courthouse and seat of government for Lavaca County.
world knowledge.Details: Designed by architect Eugene T. Heiner and built by A.T. Lucas. It is a Texas State Antiquities Landmark and a National Register of Historic Places listed property.

world knowledge.Name: Apartheid Museum
world knowledge.Address: Gold Reef City complex, Johannesburg, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Apartheid Museum illustrates apartheid and the 20th-century history of South Africa. It was opened in November 2001 as part of the Gold Reef City complex in Johannesburg.

Major_Events.Event: Celebration of the end of apartheid
Major_Events.Year: Annually (at least five times a year)
Major_Events.Description: Events are held to celebrate the end of apartheid and the start of multiracial democracy for the people of South Africa.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it documents the history of apartheid in South Africa and promotes the values enshrined in the South African Constitution: Democracy, Equality, Reconciliation, Diversity, Responsibility, Respect, and Freedom.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features exhibits such as 'The Pillars of the Constitution,' 'Race Classification,' 'Journeys,' and 'Segregation,' which illustrate the racial divisions and policies of apartheid. Visitors experience the museum through randomly assigned entry points (white or non-white) to simulate apartheid-era segregation.

world knowledge.Name: First Folio Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Mayslake Peabody Estate, Oak Brook, Illinois
world knowledge.Historical_Background: First Folio Theatre was a not-for-profit theater company affiliated with the Actors' Equity Association. Founded in 1996, it was originally named First Folio Shakespeare Festival and was located on the grounds of the Mayslake Peabody Estate. It utilized the 'Folio Method' developed by Patrick Tucker of the Royal Shakespeare Company, which employs the text of William Shakespeare's First Folio to illuminate textual clues for actors and audiences. The theatre ceased operations in February 2023 after 25 years due to the retirement of its Founding Executive Director David Rice.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was founded as First Folio Shakespeare Festival on the grounds of the Mayslake Peabody Estate.
First Folio Theatre's first venue was its outdoor stage, adjacent to the Portiuncula Chapel, allowing up to 500 audience members.
The chamber theater, located in the formal library of Mayslake Hall, seated 80 and was used for intimate productions.
The Event Hall, located in the Retreat Wing of Mayslake Hall, seated up to 130 and became the primary indoor venue.
First Folio Theatre ceased operations after its last performance in February 2023 due to the retirement of its Founding Executive Director.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre utilized multiple venues: an outdoor stage (built in 1997), a chamber theater (opened in 2004), and the Event Hall (opened in 2008). The outdoor stage allowed lawn seating for up to 500, the chamber theater seated 80, and the Event Hall seated up to 130.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: First Folio Theatre was listed as a Major Festival in the book 'Shakespeare Festivals Around the World' and was known for its use of the Folio Method, which revived interest in Shakespeare's First Folio. It also had a significant educational outreach program, impacting over 125,000 students in Illinois and Iowa.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre company specializing in Shakespearean performances and educational outreach.
world knowledge.Details: First Folio Theatre's Educational Outreach program offered four touring shows and an artist-in-residence program, reaching over 125,000 students. The programs were included in the Illinois Arts Council's Arts Tour Roster, and the theatre was chosen as the Artists-in-Residence for the Quad Cities Arts Program in November 2006.

world knowledge.Name: Reims Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Notre-Dame de Reims, known in English as Reims Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral dedicated to the Virgin Mary. It was the traditional location for the coronation of the kings of France and is considered one of the most important works of Gothic architecture. The cathedral was founded by Bishop Nicasius in the early 5th century, and the present structure was built to replace an earlier church destroyed by fire in 1210. It was severely damaged during World War I and restored in the 20th century. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991.

Major_Events.Description: Clovis I, the King of the Franks, was baptized here by Saint Remigius, marking the beginning of the tradition of royal coronations at Reims.
Joan of Arc played a key role in the coronation of Charles VII during the Hundred Years' War.
The cathedral was severely damaged by German shelling during World War I, leading to extensive restoration work.
The cathedral, along with the former Abbey of Saint-Remi and the Palace of Tau, was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list.

Features.West_Façade: Harmonic design with two towers, three portals, and a large rose window.
Features.Nave: Exceptional length and unity of style with four-part rib vaults and flying buttresses.
Features.Transept: Wider and higher than the nave, originally intended to have four towers.
Features.Choir: Double ambulatory leading to five radiating chapels.
Features.Organ: Fifth largest in France with 6,600 pipes, 85 stops, and four keyboards.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Reims Cathedral is a symbol of French monarchy and Christianity, being the traditional site for the coronation of French kings. It is a masterpiece of Gothic architecture and a major tourist destination, attracting about one million visitors annually. Its historical and artistic importance is recognized by its UNESCO World Heritage status.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Roman Catholic cathedral and archiepiscopal see of the Archdiocese of Reims.

world knowledge.Name: Statue of Unity
world knowledge.Address: Narmada Valley Kevadiya, Narmada, Gujarat, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Statue of Unity is the world's tallest statue, dedicated to Vallabhbhai Patel, a key figure in India's independence and political integration. The project was announced in 2010 by Narendra Modi, then Chief Minister of Gujarat, and construction began in October 2013. It was inaugurated on 31 October 2018, the 143rd anniversary of Patel's birth.

Major_Events.Description: Narendra Modi, then Chief Minister of Gujarat, laid the foundation stone on 31 October 2013, the 138th anniversary of Patel's birth.
The statue was inaugurated by Narendra Modi, then Prime Minister of India, on 31 October 2018, the 143rd anniversary of Patel's birth.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The statue is made of steel framing, reinforced by concrete and brass coating, with bronze cladding. It has a height of 182 metres and is built to withstand winds of up to 180 kilometres per hour and earthquakes measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale. The design includes a slenderness ratio between 16 and 19, with two 250-tonne tuned mass dampers for stability.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Statue of Unity is a tribute to Vallabhbhai Patel's role in India's independence and political integration. It symbolizes national unity and engineering prowess.
