world knowledge.Details: The statue is divided into five zones, with three accessible to the public. It includes a museum, memorial garden, and a viewing gallery at 153 metres. The project was executed by Larsen & Toubro, with a total cost of ₹27 billion. It has attracted millions of visitors since its opening.

world knowledge.Name: Maison Saint-Gabriel
world knowledge.Area: Pointe-Saint-Charles, Le Sud-Ouest, Montreal, Quebec, Canada
world knowledge.Address: Pointe-Saint-Charles, Le Sud-Ouest, Montreal, Quebec, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Maison Saint-Gabriel Museum is dedicated to preserving the history, heritage, and artifacts of the settlers of New France in the mid-17th century. It was established as a farm by Marguerite Bourgeoys in 1662 and has been administered by the Sisters of the Congregation of Notre Dame of Montreal for over 300 years. The site was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: Paul de Chomedey de Maisonneuve conceded land in Pointe-Saint-Charles to Marguerite Bourgeoys to establish a farm.
Marguerite Bourgeoys bought land adjacent to hers, which included a house and a barn, later becoming the Maison Saint-Gabriel.
The old farmhouse burned down in 1693, and the house was reconstructed in 1698, incorporating the original foundation and creamery.
The house was classified as a historic monument by the Ministère de la Culture, des Communications et de la Condition féminine.
The site was designated a National Historic Site of Canada.
The Jeanne-LeBer house was officially incorporated into the Maison Saint-Gabriel Museum as the Catherine-Crolo pavilion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The rebuilt house features a two-storey body, oak frame, ash beams, and lean-tos, capturing the essence of 17th-century structural design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Maison Saint-Gabriel preserves the heritage of Marguerite Bourgeoys and the Congregation of Notre Dame of Montreal, showcasing rural living in New France and educating visitors about the history and culture of the settlers.
world knowledge.Details: The museum hosts over 15,000 artifacts, including domestic objects, religious clothing, furniture, materials of correspondence, and tools. It features gardens that recreate 17th-century vegetable gardens and honor the women of the Congregation. The museum also includes the Catherine-Crolo pavilion, which houses a gift shop, tea room, and cultural activity room.

world knowledge.Name: Eastern Beach (Victoria)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eastern Beach was developed from an eyesore with steep cliffs into a popular recreation area. Initial redevelopment plans were proposed in 1914, with construction beginning in 1927. The shark-proof swimming enclosure and children's pool were completed in 1939. The area declined from the 1960s but was restored in the 1990s as part of the Waterfront Geelong developments.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of concrete stairway, terraces, and dressing sheds
Major_Events.Description: Opened by the Mayor of Geelong, Cr Solomon Jacobs, on 20 December 1929.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of shark-proof swimming enclosure and children's pool
Major_Events.Description: Opened by Cr Solomon Jacobs on 28 March 1939. The enclosure could accommodate 10,000 bathers.
A tramway extension along Corio Terrace opened in October 1940 to cater to beachgoers.
The City of Greater Geelong announced restoration plans, including rebuilding the boardwalk and enclosure, renovating facilities, and opening the Beach House restaurant.
The original diving tower was reinstated but modified for safety reasons.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Deco style buildings, including a kiosk, dressing room pavilion, and shark-proof sea bath. Many structures are listed on the Victorian Heritage Register.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Eastern Beach is a historic recreational area that reflects the Art Deco architectural style. It has been a focal point for community events and remains a symbol of Geelong's waterfront development.
world knowledge.Details: Eastern Beach hosts festivals, concerts, and the annual Geelong Carols by the Bay concert. The precinct was initially built as an investment in the city, costing £40,000 ($80,000). The area was restored in the 1990s as part of broader waterfront redevelopment efforts.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Tianzhu
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tianzhu Mountain, also known as Mount Wan, is a significant mountain in Anhui, China. It has ancient names including Mount Huo, Mount Heng, and Taiyue. The mountain's name 'Wan' is the origin of the provincial abbreviation for Anhui. It features 45 peaks collectively over 1000 meters above sea level, with the highest point at 1,760 meters.

Major_Events.Description: Mount Tianzhu was certified as a National Geopark.

Major_Events.Event: Admitted as a UNESCO Global Geopark
Major_Events.Description: Mount Tianzhu was admitted as a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mountain features natural landscapes such as spectacular peaks and rocks, secluded caves, and canyons. One notable site is the Mystery Valley, a maze-like valley formed by fallen rocks with 53 caves creating a complex maze.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Tianzhu is culturally significant as it is the origin of the provincial abbreviation 'Wan' for Anhui. It is also recognized for its natural beauty and geological importance, being a UNESCO Global Geopark.
world knowledge.Details: The mountain has two paths to reach the top, with the west path being the easier one. It was also certified as a regional geopark under the Asia Pacific Geopark Network before becoming a UNESCO Global Geopark.

world knowledge.Name: The Tank Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tank Museum, previously known as the Bovington Tank Museum, is a collection of armoured fighting vehicles at Bovington Camp in Dorset, South West England. It was established in 1947 and traces the history of the tank with almost 300 vehicles on display. The museum is the official museum of the Royal Tank Regiment and the Royal Armoured Corps and is a registered charity.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened to the public in 1947, although the collection had been housed in a shed since the 1920s.
The museum established its own YouTube channel in January 2010, which has gained over 100 million views by April 2023.
An exhibition created for the 100th anniversary of the Tank Museum, exploring the cultural impact of tanks through toys, games, models, and media.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tank Museum is culturally significant as it houses the largest collection of tanks and armoured vehicles in the world, including the only working Tiger I tank and the oldest surviving combat tank, the Mark I. It also serves as a memorial to the Royal Armoured Corps soldiers who died in service.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes Tiger 131, the only surviving Tiger I tank in operable condition, which appeared in the 2014 film Fury, and the replica Mark IV tank built for the film War Horse. The museum also played a role in the Russo-Ukrainian War by providing blueprints and track samples of Soviet equipment for use by Ukraine.

world knowledge.Name: University of Limpopo
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1959 (as University of the North), merged in 2005
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Limpopo is a public university formed on 1 January 2005 by the merger of the University of the North and the Medical University of South Africa (MEDUNSA). The University of the North was established in 1959 under the apartheid regime's policy of separate ethnically-based institutions. It was a center of resistance to apartheid in the 1960s, 70s, and 80s. After apartheid, the university underwent various reorganizations but survived. The MEDUNSA campus split in 2015 to become the Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of University of the North
Major_Events.Description: Established under the apartheid regime's policy of separate ethnically-based institutions of higher learning.

Major_Events.Event: Merger to form University of Limpopo
Major_Events.Description: Formed by the merger of the University of the North and the Medical University of South Africa (MEDUNSA).
The MEDUNSA campus split to become the Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is significant for its role in resisting apartheid and its mission to provide education in a rural context, focusing on solutions for Africa. It was a 'model' university under apartheid, showcasing the regime's policies, but also a center of resistance.

Details.Motto: The University of Limpopo for human and environmental wellness in a rural context; finding solutions for Africa!

world knowledge.Name: Chichester Festival Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Oaklands Park Chichester , West Sussex , PO19 6AP England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chichester Festival Theatre is a theatre and Grade II* listed building situated in Oaklands Park in the city of Chichester, West Sussex, England. Designed by Philip Powell and Hidalgo Moya, it was opened by its founder Leslie Evershed-Martin in 1962. The smaller and more intimate Minerva Theatre was built nearby in 1989. The inaugural Artistic Director was Sir Laurence Olivier, and it was at Chichester that the first National Theatre company was formed. Chichester's productions would transfer to the National Theatre's base at the Old Vic in London.

Major_Events.Description: The opening productions in 1962 were: The Chances by John Fletcher (first production 1638) which opened on 3 July; The Broken Heart (1633), by John Ford, opened 9 July; Uncle Vanya (1896), by Anton Chekov, opened 16 July.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Philip Powell and Hidalgo Moya
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chichester Festival Theatre is culturally significant as it was the site where the first National Theatre company was formed under the direction of Sir Laurence Olivier. It has a rich history of producing classic and contemporary plays, and its productions frequently transfer to London or tour nationally and internationally.
world knowledge.Details: The Festival Season usually runs from April to October and includes productions from classics to contemporary writing and musicals, reaching an audience of 230,000. Productions originated at Chichester frequently transfer to London or tour nationally and internationally. A range of additional events is designed to add to the experience of visiting the theatre, including performances, cabarets, family days, tours and talks. Through the winter months, the Theatre presents touring productions and a Christmas show mounted by Chichester Festival Youth Theatre. The Theatre runs a large and active Learning, Education and Participation programme for all ages; its Youth Theatre is one of the largest in the country, with over 800 members. The Theatre is a registered charity and is chaired by Mark Foster. Justin Audibert has been the artistic director since April 2023, sharing the leadership of the theatre with Executive Director Kathy Bourne.

world knowledge.Name: Qualicum Beach
world knowledge.Location: Strait of Georgia on Vancouver Island's northeastern coast
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Established as a village in 1943, as a town in 1983
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Qualicum Beach is a town on Vancouver Island, known for its natural environment and retirement community. The area was originally inhabited by the Qualicum First Nation, with a history of smallpox epidemics and settlement by Europeans in the 19th century. The town developed with the arrival of the railway and became a tourist destination.

Major_Events.Description: The area was deserted due to the smallpox epidemic brought by settlers.
Qualicum Beach was officially incorporated as a village.
Qualicum Beach was changed to town status.
The town's primary grocery store was destroyed by a fire.
The Town of Qualicum Beach purchased St. Andrews Lodge to transform it into a waterfront park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features a mix of architectural styles, including Georgian Revival (Crown Mansion) and Tudor (St. Andrews Lodge). The Old School House (TOSH) is a historic building converted into an arts centre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Qualicum Beach is culturally significant for its Indigenous history, retirement community, and as a tourist destination. It is also known for its arts and cultural events, such as the Farmers Market and the Brant Wildlife Festival.
Notable_Visitors: Princess Elizabeth and the Duke of Edinburgh (1951)

Details.Climate: Mediterranean climate with cool, wet winters and warm, dry summers
Notable_Features: Milner Gardens (70-acre estate with old-growth trees)
The Old School House (TOSH) arts centre
Transportation: Qualicum Flight Center (scenic and charter flights)
Details.Wildlife: Black-tailed deer, Roosevelt elk, black bear, cougar, raccoons, rodents
Details.Government: Council-manager form of government, mayor Teunis Westbroek (as of 2022)

world knowledge.Name: University of West Bohemia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of West Bohemia in Pilsen was founded in 1991 through the merger of the College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering and the Faculty of Education in Plzeň. The College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering was established in 1949 as part of the Czech Technical University in Prague and became independent in 1953. The Faculty of Education was established in 1948 as a subsidiary of the Faculty of Education, Charles University in Prague, and became independent in 1953. Both institutions merged in 1991 to form the University of West Bohemia.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering and Faculty of Education
Major_Events.Description: The University of West Bohemia was formed by the merger of the College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering and the Faculty of Education in Plzeň.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Faculty of Law
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Law was established as part of the University of West Bohemia.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Faculty of Philosophy and Art
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Philosophy and Art was established as part of the University of West Bohemia.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Faculty of Health Care Studies
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Health Care Studies was established when the Private College in Plzeň merged with the University of West Bohemia.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Faculty of Art and Design
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Art and Design was established as part of the University of West Bohemia.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of West Bohemia is a significant educational institution in the Czech Republic, contributing to the academic and professional development of students in various fields. It plays a crucial role in the cultural and intellectual life of Plzeň and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of West Bohemia consists of nine faculties, which are the basic units of the university. These faculties implement their own academic programs, with departments and institutes responsible for course delivery and research.

world knowledge.Name: Flehe Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,166 metres (3,825 ft) long, 41.7 metres (137 ft) wide, 146.47 metres (480.5 ft) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Flehe Bridge was opened in 1979 to relieve transit traffic south of Düsseldorf on the South Bridge (B 1), which was the only southern access from the left bank of the Rhine to Düsseldorf. It also connected the A 46 with the A 57.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to connect the A 46 motorway from the left bank of the Rhine with the Bergisches Land on the right bank and the south of Düsseldorf.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Flehe Bridge is a single tower cable-stayed bridge with a reinforced concrete suspension tower shaped like an inverted Y. It has a 368 metres (1,207 ft) river opening and a 13-section foreland bridge made of prestressed concrete. The bridge does not cross the Rhine at right angles to preserve the area of water procurement of the old water company Flehe.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important part of the motorway ring around Düsseldorf and serves as a key transit route connecting various regions. Its unique design and engineering make it a notable landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge includes pedestrian and cycle paths. The handles of the pylons accommodate an elevator and stairs above the roadway. The bridge has three vehicle lanes and a hard shoulder in each direction.

world knowledge.Name: Puente del Alamillo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alamillo Bridge was constructed as part of infrastructure improvements for Expo 92, held on large banana farms on the island of La Cartuja. It was designed by Santiago Calatrava and completed in 1992. The bridge's design was inspired by Calatrava's 1986 sculpture 'Running Torso'.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was constructed as part of infrastructure improvements for Expo 92, which was held on large banana farms on the island of La Cartuja.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Alamillo Bridge is a cantilever spar cable-stayed bridge with no backstays or anchorage. It consists of a single straight steel-shell tower, infilled with reinforced concrete and inclined backward, counterbalancing a 200 m span with thirteen pairs of cables. The bridge deck consists of a hexagonal steel-box-beam spine with side steel wings cantilevered off the hexagonal spine supporting the traffic decks. The top of the hexagonal spine serves as an elevated footway and cycle lane.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge represented the soaring aspirations of the city of Seville in preparation for Expo '92. It is visible from the top of La Giralda, linking Seville's past and present. The bridge is widely acclaimed aesthetically and is the first cable-stayed bridge balanced solely through the weight of the massive tower.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries three lanes of motor vehicles on each side and has a separate and elevated center lane for pedestrians and bicycles.
world knowledge.Details: The original intent was to build two symmetrical bridges on either side of the island, but the Alamillo's singular asymmetric design was chosen. The bridge features a lookout at the top of the inclined tower, accessible by a stairway enclosed within the tower. Similar bridges designed by Calatrava include the Sundial Bridge in Redding, California, the Mesoghion Avenue Footbridge in Athens, and the Chords Bridge in Jerusalem.

image_name: Holme Hall, East Riding of Yorkshire

world knowledge.Name: Holme Hall, East Riding of Yorkshire
world knowledge.Address: Holme-on-Spalding-Moor, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Holme Hall is an 18th-century country house built for Lord Langdale. The Langdale family has lived in the Beverley area since the 14th century. The house was renovated around 1720 by William Wakefield, and a chapel was added in 1766 by John Carr. The estate passed through several generations, including the Stourton family, before being sold in 1920 to be used as a convent. It later became a Sue Ryder Care Home until its closure in 2018.

Major_Events.Description: Built to designs of William Wakefield for Lord Langdale.
Chapel added by John Carr.
Sold to be used as a convent for fifty years.
Taken over by Sue Ryder Care and used as a residential care home for adults with neurological conditions.
The Sue Ryder Care Home closed in February 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Two-storey rendered brick construction with tile and Westmorland slate roofs, featuring a 5-bay frontage. Designed by William Wakefield, with a chapel added by John Carr.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Holme Hall is a grade II* listed building, reflecting 18th-century architectural style and the history of the Langdale and Stourton families. It also served as a care home, contributing to the local community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country house, later used as a convent and then a care home.
world knowledge.Details: The Langdale family inherited estates in Houghton and Etton through marriage in the 14th century. Marmaduke Langdale, a Royalist commander in the English Civil War, was created the 1st Baron Langdale of Holme in 1658. The estate passed to the Stourton family after the 5th Baron's death in 1771.

world knowledge.Name: Galata Tower
world knowledge.Address: Galata part of the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul, Turkey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Galata Tower, originally built as a watchtower at the highest point of the mostly demolished Walls of Galata, is a medieval Genoese tower in Istanbul. It was first built in 1348 during an expansion of the Genoese colony in Constantinople. After the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453, the tower was turned into a prison and later used as a fire lookout. It has undergone several renovations and is now a museum and exhibition space.

Major_Events.Description: The original tower built by Emperor Justinian was destroyed by the Crusaders.
Hezarfen Ahmed Çelebi supposedly strapped on wings and made the first intercontinental flight from the tower's roof.
The tower's conical roof was destroyed during a storm and remained without a roof until restoration in 1965-1967.
The tower was splendidly restored and reopened as a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romanesque style, masonry structure, stone material, 62.59 m (205 ft) tall, 11 floors, external diameter of 16.45 m (54.0 ft), internal diameter of 8.95 m (29.4 ft), walls 3.75 m (12.3 ft) thick.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Galata Tower is a symbol of Beyoğlu and Istanbul, representing the city's rich history and cultural heritage. It is a popular tourist attraction offering a 360-degree view of Istanbul.
world knowledge.Details: The tower has been renovated multiple times, including significant restorations in 1965-1967 and 2020. It features an observation deck at 51.65 m (169.5 ft) and is 61 m (200 ft) above sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Ranchi University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ranchi University is a public state university established on 12 July 1960 by an Act of the Bihar legislature. It was initially a teaching cum affiliating university and covered all degree colleges of present-day Jharkhand. Over the years, its jurisdiction was reduced due to the creation of new universities like Vinoba Bhave University, Nilamber Pitamber University, and Kolhan University. Currently, it has jurisdiction over five districts: Ranchi, Gumla, Khunti, Simdega, and Lohardaga.

Major_Events.Description: Ranchi University was established by an Act of the Bihar legislature.

Major_Events.Event: Bifurcation to create Vinoba Bhave University
Major_Events.Description: Ranchi University's jurisdiction was reduced by nearly half when Vinoba Bhave University was created.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Nilamber Pitamber University and Kolhan University
Major_Events.Description: Ranchi University was further divided to create Nilamber Pitamber University and Kolhan University.
Ranchi University was awarded a 'B+' grade by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ranchi University is a significant educational institution in Jharkhand, offering a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs. It plays a crucial role in higher education and research in the region.
world knowledge.Details: Ranchi University has 15 constituent colleges and 29 affiliate colleges under its jurisdiction, offering courses in various fields including medical, nursing, engineering, and liberal arts. The university has faced several administrative and financial challenges, including embezzlement scandals and issues with staff appointments.

world knowledge.Name: Chae Son National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a Forest Park, Chae Son was designated Thailand's 58th National Park on 28 July 1988. The park is home to Chae Son waterfall, caves, and hot springs, and its mountains form part of the Khun Tan Range, serving as an important water source for the surrounding area.

Major_Events.Description: Chae Son was officially designated as Thailand's 58th National Park on 28 July 1988.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chae Son National Park is culturally significant for its natural beauty, including waterfalls, hot springs, and diverse flora and fauna. It plays a vital role in the local ecosystem and is a popular destination for nature enthusiasts.
world knowledge.Details: The park features the six-tiered Chae Son Waterfall, other waterfalls like Mae Peak and Mae Koon, sulfurous hot springs, and numerous cave systems. Its forests are mixed deciduous and deciduous dipterocarp, housing a variety of tree species. Wildlife includes Phayre's leaf monkey, sambar deer, and numerous bird species like the white-rumped shama and red junglefowl.

world knowledge.Name: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, established on 12 November 2000, is a state art museum in Vaduz, Liechtenstein. It was built by Swiss architects Meinrad Morger, Heinrich Degelo, and Christian Kerez. The museum houses international modern and contemporary art and the national art collection of Liechtenstein. The museum's foundation was influenced by a gift of ten paintings in 1967, leading to the establishment of the State Art Collection of Liechtenstein in 1968. The current building was realized with support from private donors, the government of Liechtenstein, and the city of Vaduz, and was officially donated to the Principality of Liechtenstein as a millennium gift in August 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein was formally opened on 12 November 2000.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of Hilti Art Foundation exhibition building
Major_Events.Description: In May 2015, the new Hilti Art Foundation exhibition building was added to the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building is a 'black box' of tinted concrete and black basalt stone with river pebbles embedded in the exterior. It features six exhibition rooms arranged around two diametrically opposed staircases, allowing diagonal views through the building. The Hilti Art Foundation building, designed as a cube, complements the museum's architecture and shares a unified presence with it.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein is an important cultural institution in Liechtenstein, housing the national art collection and international modern and contemporary art. It plays a significant role in the public image of Liechtenstein and promotes artistic diversity by focusing on 20th and 21st-century works, especially sculptures and installations.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes works from the 19th century to the present, with a focus on abstract and minimal art, conceptual art, and Arte Povera. It has collaborated with other museums to acquire significant collections, such as the Rolf Ricke collection in 2007. The Hilti Art Foundation exhibition building, added in 2015, showcases works from classical modernism to the present, including pieces by Gauguin, Picasso, and Klee.

world knowledge.Name: Wollongong Showground
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally used for agricultural shows and greyhound racing, the stadium was officially opened in 1911 when rugby league began playing there. It became the home ground for the Illawarra Steelers NRL team from 1982 to 1998 and remains a key venue for rugby league and soccer. The stadium has undergone several upgrades, including the addition of grandstands and corporate facilities.

Major_Events.Description: Fiji defeated France 42-6 during the 2008 Rugby League World Cup.
Hosted two pool games: Canada vs Tonga and France vs the United States.
Hosted its first Charity Shield match.
Australia played Samoa in the 2014 Four Nations tournament.

Major_Events.Event: First top-flight soccer match since NSL demise
Major_Events.Description: Sydney FC played Newcastle Jets in the A-League.
Hosted Elton John as part of his Once In a Lifetime Tour.

Major_Events.Event: First Super League game outside Europe
Major_Events.Description: Wigan Warriors faced Hull FC in a historic match.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with grass surface, featuring grandstands (northern, southern, and western), corporate facilities, and a scoreboard. The western grandstand seats 6,170, increasing total capacity to 23,750.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A key sporting venue in the Illawarra region, hosting major rugby league, soccer, and rugby union events. It has historical significance as the former home of the Illawarra Steelers and current home of the St. George Illawarra Dragons and Wollongong Wolves.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is also used by the Illawarriors rugby union team and hosts the Illawarra Rugby Grand Final. Public transport and limited street parking are available, with shuttle services on game days. Critics have suggested relocating the stadium to a more suitable site due to parking and accessibility issues.

world knowledge.Name: University of Luxembourg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Luxembourg was founded in 2003 by combining four existing education and research institutes: the Centre universitaire, Institut supérieur d'études et de recherches pédagogiques, Institut supérieur de technologie, and Institut d'études éducatives et sociales. It is the only public university in Luxembourg.

Major_Events.Description: During the COVID-19 pandemic in Luxembourg, the university switched to remote learning and later hybrid learning.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the Institute for Advanced Studies (IAS)
Major_Events.Description: The university founded the Institute for Advanced Studies (IAS) to promote interdisciplinary research projects.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Luxembourg is the only public university in the country, offering multilingual education and focusing on interdisciplinary research in areas such as digital transformation, medicine and health, and sustainable and societal development.
world knowledge.Details: The university has three campuses: the Belval Campus, the Kirchberg Campus, and the Limpertsberg Campus. It offers 18 bachelor's degrees, 46 master's degrees, and doctorates. Courses are taught in multiple languages, including French, English, German, and Luxembourgish. The university has three faculties and four interdisciplinary centres. As of 2023, it has 7,000 students, including 1,000 doctoral candidates, and 2,400 staff. The university has received 15 ERC grants since 2006 and has 22 industrial, public, and public-private chairs.

world knowledge.Name: Sehlabathebe National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sehlabathebe National Park is located in the Maloti Mountains in Qacha's Nek District, Lesotho and is part of the Maloti-Drakensberg World Heritage Site. The park was first established on 8 May 1969 and since then, is recognised as important in terms of biological diversity and cultural heritage.

Major_Events.Event: Added to UNESCO World Heritage Site Tentative List
Major_Events.Description: This site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Tentative List on October 8, 2008, in the Mixed (Cultural + Natural) category.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The landscape is dominated by grasslands of various types. The park features cliffs, waterfalls, pools, rock dwellings, and rock art. It is known for its scenery with unique rock formations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is important for its biological diversity and cultural heritage. It contains 65 rock art sites and other forms of previous habitation. It is part of the Maloti-Drakensberg World Heritage Site and is recognized as an Important Bird Area (IBA) by BirdLife International.
world knowledge.Details: The park is situated in the south-east corner of Lesotho at an average elevation of some 2,400 metres above sea level. It contains habitats supporting a range of Afro-Alpine and Sub-Alpine plants, mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish. Some of the park's species are endangered, including the Maluti redfin, Cape vulture, and bearded vulture. The Sehlabathebe water lily is an endangered aquatic plant. The park is currently run under the Ministry of Tourism, Environment, and Culture jurisdiction.

world knowledge.Name: Kloster Allerheiligen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kloster Allerheiligen is a former Benedictine monastery founded by Eberhard von Nellenburg in 1049. It was consecrated by Pope Leo IX and completed in 1064. The monastery played a significant role in the development of Schaffhausen and was directly subordinate to the Pope. It underwent various renovations and expansions over the centuries, particularly during the Romanesque period. The abbey was abolished during the Reformation in Switzerland in 1524, and its buildings were repurposed. Today, it houses the Museum zu Allerheiligen.

Major_Events.Description: The monastery was founded by Eberhard von Nellenburg and consecrated by Pope Leo IX.
The construction of the monastery was completed.
The abbey was abolished during the Reformation, and the Cathedral became the second main city church.
Michael Eggendorfer, the last abbot, initiated the last renovations of the monastery.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery was modeled on the church buildings of the Cluny Abbey. It features a cloister, garden, two-winged convent buildings, and domestic buildings. The church has a three-aisled Basilica with a three-apsed choir, a transept, and a double tower facade. The monastery underwent Romanesque expansions between 1150 and 1250, including the construction of the cathedral tower, herb garden, hospital, and novitiate.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kloster Allerheiligen is culturally and historically significant as the oldest building in Schaffhausen and a former Benedictine monastery. It played a crucial role in the development of the city and was directly subordinate to the Pope. The monastery's buildings and library are listed in the Swiss inventory of cultural property of national and regional significance as Class A objects of national importance.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery now houses the Museum zu Allerheiligen, which includes an art museum, a natural history museum, and the monastery garden. The museum features extensive permanent collections and temporary exhibitions, focusing on archeology, history, art, and natural history. The museum is closed on Mondays and is open from 11:00 to 17:00. Public transportation is provided by the S-Bahn Zürich lines S16, S22, and S33, as well as local bus lines.

world knowledge.Name: Centro Desportivo Olímpico - Estádio
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Grass pitch (105m x 68m) surrounded by an 8-lane athletic track and a long jump area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Estádio Campo Desportivo, it was reconstructed and renamed in 2005 for the East Asian Games. It is the largest sporting complex in Macau and serves as the home ground for the Macau football team.

Major_Events.Description: High-profile international football match.
Exhibition match featuring FC Barcelona.

Major_Events.Event: Manchester United vs. Shenzhen friendly match
Major_Events.Description: Exhibition match featuring Manchester United.

Major_Events.Event: Chelsea F.C. vs. Guangzhou Pharmaceutical friendly match
Major_Events.Description: Exhibition match featuring Chelsea F.C.

Major_Events.Event: Southampton F.C. vs. Guangzhou R&F friendly match
Major_Events.Description: Exhibition match featuring Southampton F.C.

Major_Events.Event: 2018 AFC Champions League quarter final second leg
Major_Events.Description: Match between Tianjin Quanjian (China) and Kashima Antlers (Japan).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass pitch, 8-lane athletic track, and long jump area. Originally had only the West Stand roofed, but post-renovation, the stadium has increased capacity and improved facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest sporting complex in Macau, hosting major local and international football and athletic events. It symbolizes Macau's commitment to sports and international competitions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hosting football matches and athletics events, serving as the home ground for the Macau football team.
world knowledge.Details: Part of the Olympic Sports Center in Taipa, which includes a 900-seated indoor stadium, a hockey centre, a practicing track, and several tennis courts. The stadium was renovated in 2005 to increase capacity for the East Asian Games.

world knowledge.Name: Saïd Business School
world knowledge.Address: Park End Street, Oxford, England, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saïd Business School is the business school of the University of Oxford. Business and management classes started at Oxford in 1965 with the founding of the Centre of Management Studies, later relaunched as Templeton College. In 1988, a committee recommended the creation of a new School of Management Studies, which was established in 1990. In 1996, the school re-branded as Saïd Business School after a £28 million donation from Wafic Saïd. New premises were built on Park End Street and opened in 2001. The Thatcher Business Education Centre was opened on the same site in 2012 after a further donation from Saïd.

Major_Events.Description: The school was re-branded after a £28 million donation from Wafic Saïd.
New premises were built on Park End Street and opened.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Thatcher Business Education Centre
Major_Events.Description: The centre was opened after a further donation from Wafic Saïd.
The school acquired an old power station in Osney to convert into a Global Leadership Centre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed by Edward Jones and Sir Jeremy Dixon.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Saïd Business School is a leading provider of management education and is part of the prestigious University of Oxford. It plays a significant role in shaping future business leaders and has a strong international reputation.
world knowledge.Details: Saïd Business School offers a range of degree programmes including MBA, Executive MBA, MSc in Financial Economics, MSc in Major Programme Management, and MSc in Law and Finance. It also offers an undergraduate programme in Economics and Management. The school is part of the University of Oxford's Social Sciences Division and has a strong international presence with students from various nationalities.

world knowledge.Name: Varda Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Hacıkırı (Kıralan) village, Karaisalı district, Adana Province, Turkey
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 172 m (564 ft) long, 98 m (322 ft) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Varda Viaduct was designed and built by Imperial German engineers as part of the Baghdad Railway, connecting Berlin with Basra to supply oil to German industry. The construction was commissioned to Philipp Holzmann & Cie, with design by German Winkler and Greek-Ottoman Nicholas Mavrogordato. The viaduct was completed in 1912 and went into service in 1916.

Major_Events.Description: Minister of War Enver Pasha was the first Ottoman high official to pass over the Varda Viaduct.
Shortly before the end of World War I, the bridge was used by retreating German troops.

Major_Events.Event: Featured in James Bond film Skyfall
Major_Events.Description: The viaduct was featured in the opening chase scene of the film.
The viaduct was featured in the film directed by Ali Aydin.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The viaduct is a stone arch structure with eleven ashlar arch spans. The central portion has three 30 m (98 ft) arches, with spandrel arches over the piers, and is flanked on each side by four arch spans. The viaduct is curved with a radius of curvature of 1,200 m (3,900 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Varda Viaduct is a significant engineering feat and part of the historic Baghdad Railway. It represents the collaboration between the Ottoman Empire and Germany during the early 20th century and has been featured in popular films, increasing its cultural visibility.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway viaduct for the Konya-Yenice railway
world knowledge.Details: The viaduct is locally known as "Alman Köprüsü" or "Koca Köprü" (German Viaduct or Big Viaduct). It crosses the Çakıt Deresi (formerly Giaour Dere) and is owned by the Turkish State Railways (TCDD). The nearest railway station is Hacıkırı, about 500 m (1,640 ft) away.

world knowledge.Name: Kučanska Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kučanska Mosque is a part of the cultural heritage of Rožaje, built in 1830 by the believers of the Kučanska mahalla, named after their area of origin, the Kuči region. The ground on which the mosque is built was given by Jakup ef. Kardović, one of the most influential persons in the history of Rožaje. The mosque has undergone several renovations but has largely been preserved in its original form.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque features Ottoman architecture with a standard base used for mosques in the area. It includes a timber gallery, roof, and minaret made of wood, specifically borovina (pine). The open gallery has been enclosed with glazing during renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is a significant part of the cultural heritage of Rožaje, representing the Islamic faith and the history of the Kuči region. It is preserved in its original form, unlike some other mosques in the area.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque is still active and has undergone a number of renovations while maintaining most of its original form.

world knowledge.Name: Washington County Courthouse (Minnesota)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1870 in Stillwater, Minnesota, the Washington County Courthouse served as the center of Washington County government for over a century until 1975. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971 for its state-level significance in architecture and government/politics. After the construction of a new government center in 1975, the historic courthouse was restored and adapted for community and cultural events.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was completed and began serving as the center of Washington County government.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its state-level significance in architecture and government/politics.
The courthouse ceased to be the primary government center and was repurposed for community and cultural events.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Augustus Knight of St. Paul in the Italianate style, the courthouse features a limestone foundation, brick facade, and a prominent dome, cupola, and flagpole. It reflects the county's wealth during the lumber industry boom.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is one of the oldest standing courthouses in Minnesota and a rare example of monumental public architecture from the mid-19th century. It symbolizes the county's historical and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as the county government center; now functions as a venue for community, cultural, and private events.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse cost $60,000 to construct (equivalent to $1,349,857 in 2024). Restoration efforts have been funded through donations and grants. The facility is available for rental to help offset maintenance costs.

image_name: Edgar Allan Poe House and Museum

world knowledge.Name: Edgar Allan Poe House and Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Edgar Allan Poe House and Museum is the former home of American writer Edgar Allan Poe in the 1830s. It was opened as a writer's house museum in 1949 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 1972. The house was saved from demolition in the 1930s by the Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore.

Major_Events.Description: The home was opened as The Baltimore Poe House by the Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore.
The house was designated a National Historic Landmark on November 11, 1972.
The museum closed to the public in October 2012 due to a loss of funding by the city of Baltimore.
The museum was reopened to the public on October 5, 2013, under the auspices of Poe Baltimore, a non-profit organization.

Major_Events.Event: Entered into United For Libraries Literary Landmarks Register
Major_Events.Description: Poe House was entered into the American Library Association's United For Libraries Literary Landmarks Register, the first historical site in Maryland to be so honored.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Poe House is a 2+1⁄2 story two-bay brick structure with a gabled metal roof. The front door is on the left side of the west elevation, at the top of a wood stoop. The house retains the majority of its original woodwork. A single gabled dormer is centered in the west roof, and a two-story ell projects from the south side of the main block.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The house is culturally significant as the former home of Edgar Allan Poe, one of America's most influential writers. It serves as a museum dedicated to his life and works and is a key site for Poe enthusiasts and literary historians.
world knowledge.Details: The house hosts the International Edgar Allan Poe Festival & Awards annually. It was featured in popular culture, including HBO's The Wire and Telltale Games' The Walking Dead. The museum previously displayed Poe-related artifacts such as a lock of his hair, a piece of his coffin, and original china belonging to John Allan.

world knowledge.Name: Guangzhou Opera House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Designed by Zaha Hadid, the Guangzhou Opera House opened on 9 May 2010. It was the result of an international architectural competition in April 2002, where Zaha Hadid's 'double pebble' design was selected. The groundbreaking ceremony was held in early 2005, and it has since become one of the three biggest theatres in China alongside Beijing's National Centre for the Performing Arts and Shanghai's Shanghai Grand Theatre.

Major_Events.Event: Premiere production of Puccini's opera Turandot
Major_Events.Description: Directed by American filmmaker Shahar Stroh, this marked the opening of the opera house. Turandot had been a controversial opera in China in previous years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Deconstructivism style, conceived as two rocks washed away by the Pearl River. The structure features a freestanding concrete auditorium within an exposed granite and glass-clad steel frame.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Guangzhou Opera House is the biggest performing centre in southern China and one of the three largest theatres in the nation. It represents a significant cultural and architectural milestone in modern China, designed by the renowned architect Zaha Hadid.
world knowledge.Details: The project cost 1.38 billion yuan (approx. US$200 million). The opera house has a seating capacity of 1804 in its Opera Hall. Architectural critic Jonathan Glancey praised it as 'at once highly theatrical and insistently subtle.'

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Brianteo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stadio Brianteo was built in 1988 as a replacement for the Stadio Gino Alfonso Sada. Initially planned with an athletics track, the design was modified during construction. It was inaugurated on 28 August 1988 with a Coppa Italia match against Roma. Since September 2020, it has been commercially known as the U-Power Stadium.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugural match ended 2–1 for Monza.
Performed during his Dangerous World Tour in front of 46,000 people.
Performed during his The One Tour.
Match between Italy and Wales.
Record attendance of 16,917 vs AC Milan.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a covered grandstand, originally planned to include an athletics track which was later removed.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a key sports and entertainment venue in Monza, hosting football matches, rugby games, and concerts by internationally renowned artists.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports and entertainment venue, primarily for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by the Municipality of Monza and operated by AC Monza. The surface is grass, and the capacity is 17,102. The project manager was Giorgio Battistoni.

world knowledge.Name: Théâtre Rive Gauche
world knowledge.Address: 6, rue de la Gaîté, 14th arrondissement of Paris
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a cabaret club, later transformed into a cinema, it became the Théâtre Rive Gauche in 1994, replacing the large Edgar Theatre created in 1986 by Alain Mallet. The façade was reconstructed in 2008 due to deterioration.

Major_Events.Description: 50 private theatres in Paris, including Théâtre Rive Gauche, formed the Association pour le Soutien du Théâtre Privé (ASTP) and the Syndicat National des Directeurs et Tourneurs du Théâtre Privé (SNDTP), launching the 'Theatres Parisiens Associés'.
Éric-Emmanuel Schmitt became the director of the Théâtre Rive Gauche in association with producer and comedian Bruno Metzger.
Actor and director Steve Suissa joined the theatre.
The season opened with two world premieres: 'Miss Carpenter' by Marianne James and Sébastien Marnier, and 'The Guitrys', a new play by Éric-Emmanuel Schmitt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The façade was decorated by the French painter Pierre Clayette in 1994.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is a notable venue for contemporary productions in Paris and has hosted significant cultural events and performances.
world knowledge.Details: The auditorium has 400 seats. It is owned by the Edgar Entertainment Society, which also owns the Edgar Café and the Edgar Theatre. Notable productions include 'M. Ibrahim and the Flowers of the Koran', 'Billie Holiday', and 'The Confrontation'.

world knowledge.Name: Khau Phạ Pass
world knowledge.Area: Mù Căng Chải District, Yên Bái Province
world knowledge.Address: National Highway 32, between Văn Chấn District and Mù Căng Chải District, Yên Bái, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Khau Phạ Pass, known as 'sky-high horn' in the Thái language, is a significant mountain pass in Vietnam. It is renowned for its terraced rice paddies and is situated in a region inhabited by H'Mông and Thái ethnic minorities. The pass is characterized by its rugged terrain, dense fog, and surrounding pristine forests.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pass is a natural formation with no specific architectural style. It features dozens of sharp bends, weak red basalt soil foundation, and is prone to erosion and falling stones.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Khau Phạ Pass is culturally significant due to its association with the H'Mông and Thái ethnic minorities, who cultivate the terraced rice paddies. It is also important for its natural beauty and the rare species found in the surrounding forests.
world knowledge.Details: The pass is located at an altitude of over 1,200 meters above sea level, with a temperate climate year-round. It is especially dangerous to drive on foggy days due to the lack of barriers or warning signs. The area experiences temperatures below zero degrees in winter, sometimes resulting in snow cover.

world knowledge.Name: Doi Tung
world knowledge.Area: Mae Fa Luang District, Chiang Rai Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Doi Tung is a mountain in the Thai highlands, known for its steep rise near the Thailand-Myanmar border. It is the highest point of the Doi Nang Non, a subrange of the Daen Lao Range, in the 'Golden Triangle' area. The mountain's bedrock is mostly limestone and granite, with deciduous forest below 1,000 m and evergreen vegetation above. The population consists of various tribes, including Akha, Lahu, Tai Lue, and Lawa. The area has a significant Buddhist temple, Wat Phra That Doi Tung, dating back to 911. The Doi Tung Development Project has significantly improved the local economy, and the Doi Tung Royal Villa, former residence of Princess Mother Srinagarindra, now serves as a museum.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Wat Phra That Doi Tung
Major_Events.Description: The Buddhist temple was established on top of the hill, becoming an important pilgrimage site.
The project aimed at improving the local economy and has led to a sixfold increase in per capita incomes by 2016.

Major_Events.Event: Reforestation and fight against opium trade
Major_Events.Description: Princess Mother Srinagarindra encouraged reforestation and helped local tribes transition from opium poppy cultivation to other crops.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The area features a Buddhist temple with historical significance and a royal villa that now serves as a museum. The Mae Fah Luang Gardens are a botanical park with flowers and plants growing among rock formations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Doi Tung is culturally significant due to its historical Buddhist temple, the royal villa of Princess Mother Srinagarindra, and its role in the economic and social development of the local hill tribes. The area is also known for its successful transition from opium cultivation to sustainable agriculture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious site, museum, and botanical park
world knowledge.Details: The mountain is part of the 'Golden Triangle' and has a population of about 11,000 people from various tribes. Coffee plantations cover 15 km² with 3.5 million coffee trees, providing income for nearly 900 families. The area has been reforested and is now a model for sustainable development.

world knowledge.Name: Rode Hall
world knowledge.Address: Odd Rode, Cheshire, near Stoke-on-Trent, England
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 10 acres (4 ha) of gardens, 2-acre (1 ha) walled kitchen garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rode Hall is a Georgian country house, the seat of the Wilbraham family since 1669. The estate was purchased from the Rode family, who owned it since the 14th century. The original timber-framed manor house was replaced by a brick-built structure in the early 18th century, with a second building added in 1752. The two were joined in 1800. The hall has undergone multiple alterations and restorations, including work by notable architects and designers.

Major_Events.Description: Roger Wilbraham purchased the estate from his cousin Randle Rode for £2,400.
The original timber-framed manor house was replaced by a brick-built seven-bay building.
A second five-bay building was constructed under the guidance of architects William and David Hiorne.
The two houses were joined to form the present Rode Hall.
The hall was opened to the public by Sir Randle John Baker Wilbraham, 7th Baronet.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rode Hall consists of two joined brick-built houses in Flemish bond. The older part has seven bays, projecting bays with ashlar quoins, and a hipped roof with a central octagonal bellcote. The newer part has five bays, a central portico with ionic columns, and French windows with cast iron balconies. Interiors feature rococo plaster ceilings, mahogany bookcases, and decorative plasterwork by architects like Thomas Farnolls Pritchard and Lewis Wyatt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rode Hall is a Grade II* listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance. It represents Georgian country house design and contains significant collections of period paintings, furniture, and porcelain. The surrounding parkland and gardens are Grade II listed. The hall remains a family residence and is open to the public, contributing to local heritage and tourism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Country house and family residence, now also a public heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The hall features large collections of period paintings, furniture, and porcelain by Chelsea, Bow, and Royal Worcester. The gardens include an Italian Garden, a walled kitchen garden, and structures like a grotto, ice house, and obelisk. The estate hosts events like the Just So Festival and a monthly farmers' market. The tearooms use produce from the kitchen garden.

world knowledge.Name: Václav Havel Airport Prague
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Václav Havel Airport Prague, originally named Prague Ruzyně International Airport, was founded in 1937 to replace Kbely Airport as the city's principal airport. It has undergone several reconstructions and extensions in 1956, 1968, 1997, and 2006. In 2012, it was renamed after Václav Havel, the last president of Czechoslovakia and the first president of the Czech Republic. The airport has played a significant role in Czechoslovak and Czech civil aviation history.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was seized by Soviet paratroopers on the night of 20–21 August 1968, facilitating the landing of Soviet troops and transports for the invasion of Czechoslovakia.
The airport was renamed after Václav Havel on 5 October 2012, on what would have been his 76th birthday.
The main runway 06/24 was reconstructed due to poor technical conditions, with the second and third stages merged to finish the work in 2013.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a central check-in building (Terminal 4) designed by architect Adolf Benš, which received a Diploma and Gold Medal at the 1937 International Art and Technical Exhibition in Paris. The airport has two main passenger terminals, two general aviation terminals, and a cargo facility.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a significant hub for international travel in the Czech Republic and has a rich history tied to the country's political and economic changes. It was renamed in honor of Václav Havel, a prominent figure in Czech history.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as a hub for Smartwings and an operating base for Ryanair and Eurowings. It has two runways in service: 06/24 and 12/30. Plans for expansion include a new concourse and a railway connection to Prague city center, expected to be completed by 2033. The airport handled over 16 million passengers in 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Daegu National Museum
world knowledge.Address: Hwanggeum-dong, Suseong District, Daegu, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Daegu National Museum is a national museum that opened on December 7, 1994. It was built as a cultural facility to research, preserve, exhibit, and educate visitors on the cultural heritage of Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do. It holds approximately 30,000 artifacts, mainly archaeological objects from Daegu and North Gyeongsang Province region.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Ancient Culture Hall, Medieval Culture Hall, and Textiles and Clothing Hall
Major_Events.Description: On July 19, 2010, the Ancient Culture Hall, the Medieval Culture Hall, and the Textiles and Clothing Hall were opened to the public.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it preserves and exhibits the cultural heritage of Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do, providing educational resources and research opportunities.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's website is available at daegu.museum.go.kr/contents/siteMainLang.do?lang=ENG.

world knowledge.Name: University of Huddersfield
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1825 – Huddersfield Science and Mechanics' Institute 1992 – university status
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Huddersfield is a public research university located in Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, England. It has been a University since 1992, but has its origins in a series of institutions dating back to the 19th century. It has made teaching quality a particular focus of its activities, winning the inaugural Higher Education Academy Global Teaching Excellence Award in 2017, and achieving a Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) Gold Award in 2017 and 2023. The university has also put an increasing focus on research quality, and as of 2022 more than three quarters of its academic staff hold a doctorate, the third highest rate in England.

Major_Events.Description: The institution was granted university status.
Queen Elizabeth visited the campus to lay the foundation stone of the Creative Arts Building.
The University of Huddersfield was named University of the Year at the Times Higher Education Awards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mixture of converted mill buildings and purpose-built facilities. Notable buildings include the Schwann Building, the Creative Arts Building, and the Oastler Building for Law and the School of Music, Humanities and Media.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Huddersfield is culturally significant for its contributions to education, research, and the local economy. It has a strong focus on teaching quality and research excellence, and it hosts annual events like the Huddersfield Contemporary Music Festival and Huddersfield Literature Festival.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Huddersfield has a main campus in Queensgate, south-east of Huddersfield town centre. It has invested over £250 million in the campus, which features a mix of converted mill buildings and purpose-built facilities. The university is organized into several academic schools and has world-leading applied research groups in biomedical sciences, engineering and physical sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities.

world knowledge.Name: Yongdusan Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yongdusan Park, located on Yongdusan Mountain, has a rich history dating back to the Joseon period when it hosted a Japanese ethnic enclave. During the Japanese colonial period, Ryūtōsan Shrine was constructed here, which was destroyed after Korea's liberation in 1945. The mountain became a refuge for shanty towns during the Korean War, suffering multiple fires. The park has since become a symbol of Busan, featuring historical monuments and attractions.

Major_Events.Description: After Korea's liberation, the Ryūtōsan Shrine was destroyed by fire, which also charred nearby trees.
The mountain became crowded with shanty towns of refugees fleeing the Korean War, which were destroyed by fires twice.
The park, briefly named Unam Park after Syngman Rhee, was renamed back to Yongdusan Park after Rhee was ousted.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features the 120-meter-high Busan Tower, various historical monuments, and museums. The landscape includes 70 different species of trees and scenic views of Busan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Yongdusan Park is a symbol of Busan, reflecting its historical struggles and resilience. It houses significant monuments like the statue of Yi Sun-sin and the commemorative monument for the April 19th anti-government student protests. The park also hosts traditional arts performances and contains unique museums like the Museum of World Folk Instruments and the Exhibition Hall of World Model Boats.
world knowledge.Details: The park turns into a festival site every Saturday from March through November, hosting traditional arts performances. It also contains the Museum of World Folk Instruments and the Exhibition Hall of World Model Boats, which showcase various musical instruments and model boats, respectively.

world knowledge.Name: Museum Speelklok
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Museum Speelklok, previously known as Museum van Speeldoos tot Pierement, is a museum in Utrecht, Netherlands, specializing in self-playing musical instruments. Since 1984, it has been housed in the centre of Utrecht in a former church called Buurkerk. The museum originated from an exhibition of mechanical organs and other musical automata in Utrecht in the summer of 1956, which led to the creation of a permanent national museum dedicated to mechanical musical instruments.

Major_Events.Description: For its 50-year Jubilee, the museum held a special exhibition featuring very special instruments loaned from renowned museums including the Hermitage Museum, the Louvre, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, and the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.

Swedish musician Martin Molin's retired Marble Machine was transported to Museum Speelklok as a temporary attraction in Summer 2017. Molin's visit to the museum in 2016 inspired him to build the Marble Machine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Housed in the central medieval Buurkerk (citizens' church), the museum features a variety of self-playing musical instruments including music boxes, musical clocks, pianolas, barrel organs, and a turret clock with a carillon.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Museum Speelklok is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases a wide array of self-playing musical instruments, which are an important part of musical and mechanical history. The museum's restoration workshops are leaders in their field, known for their excellent standards.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's website is www.museumspeelklok.nl. Swedish musician Martin Molin announced a weekly video series on YouTube known as 'Music Machine Mondays' that showcased various instruments from the museum.

world knowledge.Name: Norwood Oval
world knowledge.Address: cnr The Parade and Woods St, Norwood, South Australia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Football: 165m x 110m; Baseball: Left Field – 320 feet (98m), Center Field – 390 feet (120m), Right Field – 290 feet (88m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Norwood Oval was built in 1901 and officially opened in 1906 to host football matches. It has been used for various sports including Australian rules football, baseball, soccer, rugby league, and American football. The oval is owned by Norwood, Payneham & St Peters Council but managed by the Norwood Football Club.

Major_Events.Description: Norwood played against the newly formed Sturt Football Club on 4 May 1901.
20,280 fans watched an SANFL match between Norwood and Port Adelaide.
Norwood defeated Port Adelaide by six goals.
Norwood triumphed over East Perth.
The Adelaide Crows women's team played home games at Norwood Oval, including during the AFLW's inaugural season in 2017 and Gather Round matches in 2023 and 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface with grandstand seating for up to 3,900 people. The oval features four modern light towers of television standard positioned at the corners, replacing the original six towers from the 1950s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Norwood Oval is a significant sporting venue in Adelaide, hosting major football and baseball events. It is the home ground for the Norwood Football Club and the primary home ground of the Adelaide Crows in AFL Women's. The oval has a rich history in Australian rules football and baseball, contributing to the local and national sports culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports venue for Australian rules football, baseball, and other community events.
world knowledge.Details: Norwood Oval is currently known as Coopers Stadium due to sponsorship from Coopers Brewery. It has a capacity of 10,000 people and has hosted various sports including night football and baseball. The oval is one of two sporting venues in Adelaide named Coopers Stadium, the other being Hindmarsh Stadium. The Adelaide Crows women's team returned to playing the majority of their games at Norwood Oval in 2021 after redevelopment works in 2020.

world knowledge.Name: Wreck Beach
world knowledge.Area: Pacific Spirit Regional Park, Electoral Area A, British Columbia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wreck Beach is Canada's only legally recognized nudist beach dating back to at least the 1930s. The beach has historical significance as it was reclaimed from the sea in a joint venture with the Canadian Army and UBC to train cadets for beach landings in WWI. The earliest evidence of Indigenous peoples inhabitation dates back to 13,000 B.C., serving as hunting, fishing, logging, and spiritual connection grounds for the Musqueam Nation.

Major_Events.Description: A police raid yielded a dozen arrests, leading to a nude-in protest organized by The Georgia Straight with 3,000 participants. Charges were dropped, and the area was designated a "no-harm, no-foul zone" until 1991 when it was officially recognized as a nudist beach.

Major_Events.Event: Murder and rape of Christina (Tina) Joy Thompson
Major_Events.Description: A brutal murder and rape occurred at the top of the stairs, and a plaque remains in memory of the victim.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Wreck Beach Preservation Society
Major_Events.Description: Originally formed as Citizens Concerned for Coward's Cove in 1977, the group was renamed and has since advocated against various developments threatening the beach.
Permanent toilet outhouses were installed on the beach.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach features two tall concrete range/direction instrument towers from World War II, rocky and sandy shorelines, and a main trail with approximately 400 steps. The most popular area has 490 wooden steps and is lined by licensed vendors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wreck Beach holds cultural significance as a longstanding nudist beach, a site of Indigenous heritage, and a symbol of countercultural movements in the 1960s and 1970s. It is also a place of natural beauty and wildlife observation.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is clothing-optional and is popular among University of British Columbia students, faculty, and staff. Swimming is common, though the water is cold. The beach faces ongoing threats from development proposals, including condominiums, sea walls, and restaurant constructions. The Wreck Beach Preservation Society actively opposes these developments. Wildlife includes nesting herons, sea lions, kingfishers, and bald eagles.

world knowledge.Name: Eggenberg Palace, Graz
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eggenberg Palace is the most significant Baroque palace complex in Styria, Austria. It was constructed and expanded over centuries, starting from the Late Middle Ages. The palace reflects the wealth and influence of the House of Eggenberg, particularly Hans Ulrich von Eggenberg, who commissioned the Baroque expansion. The palace was designed by Giovanni Pietro de Pomis and incorporates Gothic and Baroque architectural styles. It was recognized as part of the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Sites in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: Hans Ulrich von Eggenberg commissioned the Baroque expansion of the palace, inspired by El Escorial in Spain.

Major_Events.Event: Wedding of Archduchess Claudia Felicitas of Tyrol
Major_Events.Description: Archduchess Claudia Felicitas of Tyrol was a guest in the palace on the occasion of her wedding to Leopold I, Holy Roman Emperor.

Major_Events.Event: UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site expansion
Major_Events.Description: Schloss Eggenberg was included in the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site listing, expanding the recognition of Graz Historic Old Town.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace combines Gothic and Baroque architectural styles. It features a rectangular plan with a central tower and four corner towers representing the four seasons. The palace has 365 exterior windows, symbolizing the days of the year, and 24 state rooms representing the hours in a day. The Planetary Room, with its cycle of paintings by Hans Adam Weissenkircher, is a highlight of the palace's interior.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Schloss Eggenberg is a symbol of the wealth and influence of the House of Eggenberg and represents the Baroque architectural and cultural heritage of Styria. Its inclusion in the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Sites highlights its global cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The palace houses several collections from the Universalmuseum Joanneum, including the Alte Galerie, Coin Collection, Roman Stonework Collection, and Archaeology Collection. The palace grounds feature extensive gardens, including a Planetary Garden and Lapidarium. The palace's design reflects humanist notions of astronomy, astrology, and alchemy, with its 365 windows and 24 state rooms symbolizing the cosmos.

world knowledge.Name: Conguillío National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Conguillío National Park is located in the Andes, in the provinces of Cautín and Malleco, in the Araucanía Region of Chile. Its name derives from the Mapuche word for 'water with Araucaria seeds'. It was declared a national park in 1950 and was designated by UNESCO as a Biosphere Reserve in 1983. The park is part of the Kütralkura Geopark, recognized by UNESCO's Global Geoparks Network in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: Conguillío National Park was officially declared a national park.
The park, along with Alto Bío Bío National Reserve, was designated by UNESCO as a Biosphere Reserve.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as part of UNESCO's Global Geoparks Network
Major_Events.Description: The park was recognized as part of UNESCO's Global Geoparks Network.
The last eruption of the Llaima volcano occurred on January 1, 2008, leading to the evacuation of about 150 tourists and employees of CONAF.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Conguillío National Park is culturally significant due to its unique landscapes, including the Llaima volcano, Sierra Nevada, and extensive forests of Araucarias and Nothofagus species. It is also known as Los Paraguas (The Umbrellas) due to the shape of the Monkey Puzzle trees. The park was used as a filming location for the BBC television series 'Walking with Dinosaurs.'
world knowledge.Details: The park is situated 120 km east of Temuco. It features attractions such as the Llaima volcano, Sierra Nevada, and various lakes and rivers. Activities include hiking, fishing, swimming, and rowing. The park is home to diverse flora and fauna, including Araucarias, Nothofagus species, and various mammals and birds. The best time to visit is between November and March when the climate is milder and the roads are in excellent condition.

image_name: Gladden Spit and Silk Cayes Marine Reserve

world knowledge.Name: Gladden Spit and Silk Cayes Marine Reserve
world knowledge.Address: 36 kilometres off the coast of Placencia, Belize
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gladden Spit and Silk Cayes Marine Reserve (GSSCMR) is a protected marine reserve in the central part of Belize's Barrier Reef. Established in 2003, it covers approximately 25,980 acres and lies 36 kilometres off the coast of Placencia. The reserve was declared on 18 May 2000, and in 2001, the feeding site of the whale sharks was declared a special protected zone. The reserve has been divided into several zones since 2003, including a general use zone, a no-take zone, a conch restoration zone, and a whale shark and reef-fish spawning aggregation conservation zone.

Major_Events.Description: The reserve was officially declared on 18 May 2000.

Major_Events.Event: Special protected zone for whale sharks
Major_Events.Description: The feeding site of the whale sharks was declared a special protected zone.
The reserve was divided into a general use zone, a no-take zone, a conch restoration zone, and a whale shark and reef-fish spawning aggregation conservation zone.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The reserve is culturally and historically significant due to its role in protecting marine biodiversity, particularly the spawning aggregations of reef fish and the presence of whale sharks. It is the only known place worldwide where whale sharks feed on the eggs of spawning reef fish. The reserve also supports significant populations of various bird species, making it an Important Bird Area (IBA).
world knowledge.Details: The reserve contains some of the healthiest parts of the reef system due to its elevation and good water quality. Gladden Spit hosts over 25 species of reef fish. Historically, fishermen have congregated here to harvest mutton snapper and grouper during their ten-day spawning aggregation period that occurs between March and June. The reserve also supports significant populations of several bird species, including white-crowned pigeons, red-footed boobies, roseate terns, Yucatan vireos, black catbirds, and golden-winged and cerulean warblers.

world knowledge.Name: Shenandoah National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shenandoah National Park was established to preserve and protect natural and cultural resources in Virginia's northern Blue Ridge Mountains. The park's creation involved significant land acquisition, often through eminent domain, displacing many long-time residents. The park was developed with infrastructure like Skyline Drive and facilities, partly through the Civilian Conservation Corps during the Great Depression.

Major_Events.Description: The park was officially established on December 26, 1935, after years of land acquisition and political efforts.

Major_Events.Event: Opening by President Franklin D. Roosevelt
Major_Events.Description: President Roosevelt formally opened the park on July 3, 1936.
Following a mandate in 1945, all park concessions were desegregated by 1950, ending the 'whites only' policy.
Peregrine falcons were reintroduced to the park, leading to successful nesting pairs by the end of the decade.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features Skyline Drive, a 105-mile scenic road designated as a National Historic Landmark, along with trails, lodges, and campgrounds. The landscape includes diverse ecosystems, waterfalls, and preserved wilderness areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Shenandoah National Park is significant for its preservation of natural beauty, biodiversity, and cultural history, including the displacement of mountain communities. It serves as a recreational and educational resource, showcasing the Appalachian region's ecology and history.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes over 500 miles of trails, including 101 miles of the Appalachian Trail, and features waterfalls, camping, and wildlife viewing. It is known for its dog-friendly policies and fly fishing opportunities. The park's climate supports diverse flora and fauna, including black bears, coyotes, and brook trout.
