Ranger-led programs and an Artist-in-Residence program enhance visitor experiences.

world knowledge.Name: War Remnants Museum
world knowledge.Area: District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
world knowledge.Address: 28 Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The War Remnants Museum, originally opened as the Exhibition House for US and Puppet Crimes in 1975, was established to display exhibits related to the First Indochina War and the Vietnam War. It underwent several name changes, reflecting shifts in political relations and perceptions, and is now one of the most popular museums in Vietnam.

Major_Events.Event: Opening as Exhibition House for US and Puppet Crimes
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened to display war crimes committed during the Vietnam War.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Exhibition House for Crimes of War and Aggression
Major_Events.Description: The museum dropped references to 'U.S.' and 'Puppet' from its name.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to War Remnants Museum
Major_Events.Description: Following the normalization of diplomatic relations with the United States, the museum adopted its current name.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum comprises several buildings with themed rooms and a walled yard displaying period military equipment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its role in documenting and educating about the impacts of the Vietnam War, including the use of Agent Orange and other war atrocities.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features exhibits such as 'tiger cages', a guillotine used by the French and South Vietnamese, and preserved human fetuses deformed by Agent Orange. It also hosts temporary exhibitions and has seen a shift towards a more reconciliatory tone in recent years.

world knowledge.Name: Museo Castillo Serrallés
world knowledge.Address: Cerro El Vigia (El Vigia Hill), Ponce, Puerto Rico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Museo Castillo Serrallés, also known as Museo de la Caña y el Ron, is an agricultural museum showcasing the history of sugar cane, the rum industry, and their impact on Puerto Rico's economy. The museum is housed in a four-story Spanish Colonial Revival style building constructed in the 1930s for the owner of Destileria Serralles, one of Puerto Rico's largest rum distilleries. The building, known as Castillo Serrallés, was designed by Pedro Adolfo de Castro. The museum opened on 20 February 1991 and is part of a complex that includes the Cruceta El Vigía, a Japanese Garden, and a butterfly garden.

Major_Events.Description: The museum officially opened to the public on 20 February 1991.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a four-story structure in the Spanish Colonial Revival style, designed by Pedro Adolfo de Castro. It features two huge terraces, an outside fountain, a symmetrical backyard garden, a luxurious hall, a spacious dining room, and an interior courtyard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is an iconic structure in Puerto Rico, highlighting the historical significance of the sugar cane and rum industries in the region. It also serves as a cultural hub, hosting local art exhibits and social events.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is administered by Patronato de Ponce, a non-profit organization. It operates with a yearly budget of $1.2 million and receives around 100,000 visitors annually. The museum offers guided tours and has four floors, each focusing on different aspects of the museum and the lives of its former owners. The surrounding landscape has been rejuvenated, featuring lush green grass, fountains, manicured shrubs, and lights, and is used for private events such as weddings and quinceañera celebrations.

world knowledge.Name: National Botanic Garden of Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Botanic Garden of Wales is located on the site of the former Middleton Hall estate, which was developed in the early 17th century by the Middleton family. Sir William Paxton acquired the estate in 1789 and transformed it into a water park with a new mansion designed by architect Samuel Pepys Cockerell. The estate was later sold to Edward Hamlin Adams in 1824, and after a period of decline, the mansion was gutted by fire in 1931. The site was eventually acquired by Carmarthenshire County Council and later developed into the National Botanic Garden of Wales, which opened to the public in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The garden was officially opened by Charles, Prince of Wales.
The garden received a financial package from the Welsh Assembly Government, Carmarthenshire County Council, and the Millennium Commission to secure its future.
The domed greenhouse scenes of the Doctor Who episode 'The Waters of Mars' were filmed in the garden's glasshouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features the world's largest single-span glasshouse, designed by Foster and Partners, which is 95 m long and 55 m wide with a roof containing 785 panes of glass. The Double Walled Garden has been rebuilt from ruins, and a new tropical glasshouse was added in 2007.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The garden is a center for botanical research and conservation, and it plays a significant role in preserving biodiversity. It also has historical significance due to its location on the former Middleton Hall estate and its association with Sir William Paxton's water park.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Botanical research, conservation, and visitor attraction
world knowledge.Details: The garden includes the Waun Las national nature reserve, which comprises 150 hectares of wildflower meadows and pastures. It also features a large collection of Welsh apple varieties and uses biomass recycling for heating facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Cathedral of Our Merciful Saviour
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of Our Merciful Saviour in Faribault is the oldest cathedral in Minnesota. Built 1862–1869, it was the first church in the Episcopal Church in the United States of America designed as a cathedral. Our Merciful Saviour was founded by Bishop Henry Benjamin Whipple, who is buried beneath the altar. In 1941 St. Mark's Episcopal Cathedral in Minneapolis was dedicated as the seat of the bishop for the Episcopal Diocese of Minnesota, but the Cathedral of Our Merciful Saviour retains its status as a full cathedral as well.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The cathedral and its guild house were added to the National Register of Historic Places.

Major_Events.Event: Boundary increase to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The bishop's residence was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic Revival style, designed by James Renwick Jr.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The oldest cathedral in Minnesota and the first church in the Episcopal Church in the United States of America designed as a cathedral.
world knowledge.Details: The architect, James Renwick Jr., also designed St. Patrick's Cathedral in New York, the Smithsonian Institution Building in Washington, D.C., and a very similar church, the Christ Church by the Sea in Colón, Panama.

world knowledge.Name: Ciniselli Circus
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Large stage (13 meters in diameter), stables (housing 150 horses)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Circus Ciniselli was the first brick-built circus in Russia, opened on 26 December 1877. Gaetano Ciniselli, an Italian circus performer, settled in Russia and inherited circuses in Moscow and Saint Petersburg in 1875. The Ciniselli family managed the circus until 1919 when they emigrated.

Major_Events.Description: High-profile entertainment event held at the circus.
Max Reinhardt's production featuring Alexander Moissi.
Iury Iurev revived the play using the original set.
Featured Maria Andreyeva and Feodor Chaliapin.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Brick-built circus with a large stage and stables, designed by architect Vasily Kenel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: First brick-built circus in Russia, housed the first circus museum in the world, and hosted high-profile entertainment events.
world knowledge.Details: Two halls in the building house the first circus museum in the world, opened in 1928, boasting more than 80,000 exhibits as of 2002.

world knowledge.Name: Certosa di San Martino
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Certosa di San Martino is a former monastery complex, now a museum, in Naples, southern Italy. It was finished and inaugurated under the rule of Joan I of Naples in 1368. During the first half of the 16th century it was expanded. Later, in 1623, it was further expanded and became, under the direction of architect Cosimo Fanzago, essentially the structure one sees today. In 1799 anti-clerical French forces of occupation suppressed the monastery and forced the monks to flee. In the ensuing decades the monks made several attempts to reestablish their charter house, with the last effort failing in 1866, when the state definitively confiscated the property.

Major_Events.Description: Anti-clerical French forces of occupation suppressed the monastery and forced the monks to flee.
The state definitively confiscated the property after the last attempt by the monks to reestablish their charter house failed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The structure was expanded in the first half of the 16th century and further expanded in 1623 under the direction of architect Cosimo Fanzago, becoming essentially the structure one sees today.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Certosa di San Martino is one of the most visible landmarks of Naples, perched atop the Vomero hill that commands the gulf. It houses the National Museum of San Martino with a display of Spanish and Bourbon era artifacts, as well as displays of the presepe—Nativity scene—considered to be among the finest in the world.
world knowledge.Details: The Certosa di San Martino was dedicated to St. Martin of Tours. Today, the buildings house the National Museum of San Martino.

world knowledge.Name: Headlands Beach State Park
world knowledge.Address: Mentor and Painesville Township, Ohio, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The state began acquiring land for the park during the period 1951-1952. It opened under the name Painesville Beach State Park in 1953, with its name changed to Headlands Beach two years later.

Major_Events.Description: The Plain Dealer of Cleveland ranked Headlands as Ohio's best beach.

Major_Events.Event: Listed among top 20 beaches in the United States
Major_Events.Description: CNN listed Headlands Beach among the top 20 beaches in the United States per the nomination of readers of 'CNN Travel.'

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a 35-acre beach for sunbathing, swimming, and beach glass hunting along with picnicking facilities and seasonal concessionaire. The breakwall at the eastern end of the park is surmounted by the Fairport Harbor West Breakwater Light.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Headlands Beach State Park is the longest natural beach in Ohio and attracts two million visitors annually. It is culturally significant for its natural beauty and recreational opportunities.
world knowledge.Details: The park is at the northern terminus of State Route 44 and the Buckeye Trail. It is between the Mentor Marsh and the Grand River, next to Fairport Harbor Coast Guard station and a Morton Salt mine, and abuts two other protected areas, Headlands Dunes State Nature Preserve to the east and Mentor Marsh State Nature Preserve to the west. As with other state parks in Ohio, both men and women are allowed to wear thong swimwear, and women are allowed to be topless, though discouraged by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources in the interest of promoting 'a wholesome family environment.'

world knowledge.Name: Kongou Falls
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 3.2 kilometres (2.0 mi) wide and up to 56 metres (184 ft) tall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chutes Kongou (also called the Koungou Falls) is a massive cataract located on the Ivindo River in Ivindo National Park. It is one of the strongest-flowing waterfalls in the world with an average flow of 900 cubic metres per second. The falls are within Ivindo National Park, created in 2002 to protect this beautiful and biologically diverse stretch of river.

Major_Events.Description: On 14 September 2007, President Omar Bongo Ondimba of Gabon confirmed that a dam would be built at the falls to provide electricity to a large iron mining project in Belinga further north. The dam would inundate a large part of the National Park and have a serious impact on local livelihoods. Due to opposition from the Gabonese people, this project has been stopped.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kongou Falls is reputed to be the most beautiful waterfall in Central Africa and is a major centre of fish biodiversity. The falls are a key feature of Ivindo National Park, which was established to protect the area's natural beauty and biodiversity.
world knowledge.Details: The decision to build a dam at Kongou Falls without prior environmental impact study or proper consultation was a sign of the growing power of the Minister of Mines and Petrol at a time when President Bongo's power was declining. The project has been stopped due to opposition from the Gabonese people.

world knowledge.Name: Elite Towers
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Elite Towers is a cluster of 34 towers located in the City of Arabia in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Currently, there are a few towers that are under construction; all others are approved. The tallest tower in the complex has a height of 290 m (951 ft). The number of floors for the towers range from 30 to 60. The towers in the complex consist of residential, office and hotel towers. The whole complex is a development by Ilyas and Mustafa Galadari Group.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex consists of 34 skyscrapers with heights ranging up to 290 m (951 ft) and floors ranging from 30 to 60. The towers include residential, office, and hotel spaces.
world knowledge.Details: The complex consists of 34 skyscrapers. Table entries without text indicate that information regarding building heights, and/or use has not yet been released.

world knowledge.Name: Kowloon Park
world knowledge.Area: Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Address: Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kowloon Park was formerly the site of the Whitfield Barracks of the British Army, with a former battery (Kowloon West II Battery) in the northwestern part of the park. The Urban Council redeveloped the site into Kowloon Park in 1970. More than 70 buildings were demolished to make way for the park. The first stage of the park was officially opened on 24 June 1970 by the then governor of Hong Kong, Sir David Trench. The park was completed from 1987 to 1989 at a cost of $300 million, funded by the then Royal Hong Kong Jockey Club.

Major_Events.Description: The first stage of the park was officially opened on 24 June 1970 by the then governor of Hong Kong, Sir David Trench. The opening was celebrated by a lion dance as well as a folk dance by students of the Tai Hang Tung Primary School PM Session. Music was provided by the band of the First Battalion, the Royal Welsh Fusiliers.

The park was completed at a cost of $300 million, funded by the then Royal Hong Kong Jockey Club. The park was "doubled" in size, expanding to the north and south, and the sports centre and swimming pool complex was built.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Hong Kong Avenue of Comic Stars
Major_Events.Description: The Hong Kong Avenue of Comic Stars opened in 2012. It features 24 figurines of local comic characters and 10 bronze handprints of local comic artists along a 100-metre path.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a floral clock, a Chinese garden set within an English landscape, an aviary, a tree walk, and preserved historic barracks. The commercial development "Park Lane Shopper's Boulevard" has gardens extending onto the building rooftops. The swimming pool complex includes four indoor heated pools and outdoor leisure pools.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kowloon Park is a reminder of Hong Kong's cosmopolitan cultural heritage, blending Chinese and English landscapes. It houses several museums, including the Hong Kong Heritage Discovery Centre and the Health Education Exhibition and Resource Centre. The park is also a significant venue for bird watching and hosts major swimming events.
world knowledge.Details: The park houses an indoor sports centre and a large aquatics centre. The pool complex is the most heavily used in Hong Kong, serving over 2000 swimmers daily. It is the only venue on the Kowloon side suitable for staging major or international swimming events. The park also features the Hong Kong Avenue of Comic Stars, a Conservation Corner, Color Garden, Chinese Garden, Bird Lake, and Fitness Trail. About 100 different wild bird species can be found in the park.

world knowledge.Name: Bubanj Memorial Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Memorial Park Bubanj is a World War II memorial complex built to commemorate the shooting and execution of more than 10,000 citizens of Niš and people from Serbia and other parts of the country. The site was used by German execution squads from February 1942 to September 1944 for mass exterminations of Serbs, Romani, and Jews. The victims were buried in trenches, and before the withdrawal of the Germans in 1944, captured Italians were ordered to dig up the trenches and burn the corpses to destroy evidence of the atrocities.

Major_Events.Description: The monument 'Three fists' by Yugoslav sculptor Ivan Sabolić was unveiled on 14 October 1963.

Major_Events.Event: Declaration as Historic Landmark of Exceptional Importance
Major_Events.Description: Bubanj Memorial Park was declared a Historic Landmark of Exceptional Importance and is protected by the Republic of Serbia.
A chapel built of glass and metal, designed by architect Alexander Buđevac, was added to the complex.
The entire memorial hill was redeveloped in 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex is arranged as a park with a memorial trail about half a mile long. The centrepiece is a marble relief measuring 23 by 2.5 metres, with five compositions symbolizing the 'killing machine'. Three concrete obelisks symbolize raised hands with clenched fists, depicting men's, women's, and children's hands that defy the enemy. A summer stage and a chapel built of glass and metal are also part of the complex.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bubanj Memorial Park is culturally and historically important as it commemorates the victims of mass executions during World War II and serves as a reminder of the atrocities committed by the German execution squads. It symbolizes resistance and the ultimate victory over oppression.
world knowledge.Details: The site is located 2 km from the Crveni Krst concentration camp, another Serbian Cultural Property of Great Importance. The entire area is intersected by trenches where the shooting victims were buried.

world knowledge.Name: Union Buildings
world knowledge.Address: Government Avenue, Vermeulen Street East, Church Street, the R104 and Blackwood Street, Pretoria, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Union Buildings were constructed to serve as the administrative seat of the Union of South Africa, formed in 1910. Designed by Sir Herbert Baker, they symbolize unity and reconciliation. The site was chosen for its prominence and historical significance, originally part of the farm 'Elandsfontein'. The buildings have witnessed key events in South African history, including presidential inaugurations and protests against apartheid.

Major_Events.Description: 20,000 women marched to the Union Buildings to protest against the pass laws of 1950, chanting 'Wathint' Abafazi, wathint' imbokodo!' ('strike the women, strike the rock'). This event is commemorated by National Women's Day.
Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first democratically elected president after apartheid, was inaugurated here, marking a new era in the country's history.
A 9-meter high bronze statue of Nelson Mandela was unveiled at the Union Buildings.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Union Buildings are designed in a neoclassical style with influences from the Italian Renaissance, Cape Dutch, and Edwardian styles. The structure is 285m long, with a semi-circular colonnade and two wings representing unity. The building features light sandstone, granite foundations, and indigenous materials like stinkwood and Rhodesian teak. The design includes an amphitheater, ornamental pools, and sculptures, with details such as carved teak fanlights and heavy wood furniture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Union Buildings are a symbol of South African democracy and unity, housing the offices of the President and serving as the site of presidential inaugurations. They are a national heritage site and a popular tourist attraction, representing the country's political life and history. The buildings also commemorate key events like the Women's March and Nelson Mandela's inauguration.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official seat of the South African Government and offices of the President of South Africa.
world knowledge.Details: The Union Buildings are surrounded by terraced gardens with indigenous plants and feature monuments like the Delville Wood War Memorial and statues of General Louis Botha and Nelson Mandela. The amphitheater was renamed the Nelson Mandela Amphitheatre in 2013. The buildings share duties with Cape Town as the seat of the South African Government and are a key landmark in Pretoria.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Danish Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Danish Theatre (RDT, Danish: Det Kongelige Teater) is both the national Danish performing arts institution and a name used to refer to its old purpose-built venue from 1874 located on Kongens Nytorv in Copenhagen. The theatre was founded in 1748, first serving as the theatre of the king, and then as the theatre of the country.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Danish Theatre is the national Danish performing arts institution, presenting opera, the Royal Danish Ballet, multi-genre concerts, and drama in several locations. It is under the control of the Danish Ministry of Culture.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre presents opera, the Royal Danish Ballet, multi-genre concerts, and drama in several locations. The Royal Danish Theatre organization is under the control of the Danish Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Navy Submarine Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Navy Submarine Museum at Gosport traces the international history of submarine development from the age of Alexander the Great to the present day, particularly focusing on the history of the Royal Navy Submarine Service. The museum's collection originated as the Submarine Branch Collection in 1963 and was officially recognized by the Ministry of Defence in 1967. It has undergone significant development since its inception, including the relocation outside HMS Dolphin in 1978 to allow public access.

Major_Events.Event: Official recognition by the Ministry of Defence
Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially recognized by the Ministry of Defence, along with the Fleet Air Arm Museum and the Royal Marines Museum.
The museum was moved outside HMS Dolphin, allowing full public access and the addition of HMS Alliance as a principal exhibit.
The new museum complex opened with HMS Alliance as the principal exhibit.
A climate-controlled building was opened to house Holland 1.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the history of submarine development, particularly the Royal Navy Submarine Service, offering insights into technological advancements and historical events related to submarines.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To educate the public about the history and development of submarines, particularly those used by the Royal Navy.
world knowledge.Details: Visitors can tour HMS Alliance with a submariner guide, explore the interactive science gallery, step on board the Royal Navy's first submarine Holland I (built in 1901), or wander around the museum exhibits. The museum also features a display entitled "From Pirate to Peacekeeper".

world knowledge.Name: Manisa 19 Mayıs Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium is named after the date 19 May 1919 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk set foot on land in Samsun to start the Turkish national independence movement.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium underwent renovation, boosting the capacity from 14,280 to 16,597, following the promotion of Manisaspor to the Turkish Süper Lig.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named in honor of the start of the Turkish national independence movement led by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the home ground of TFF First League team Manisa FK. It has hosted national team matches.

world knowledge.Name: Ephesus Archaeological Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ephesus Archaeological Museum is an archaeological museum in Selçuk near the Ancient Greek city of İzmir, Turkey. It houses finds from the nearby Ephesus excavation site. Its best-known exhibit is the ancient statue of the Greek Goddess Artemis retrieved from the temple of the goddess in Ephesus.

Major_Events.Description: The museum closed at the end of 2012, and reopened in November 2014 after extensive renovations.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses approximately 64 thousand pieces from the nearby Ephesus excavation site, including the ancient statue of the Greek Goddess Artemis.
world knowledge.Details: The other museum with a great number of Ephesus artifacts is the Ephesus Museum in Vienna.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Brissac
world knowledge.Address: Brissac-Quincé, Brissac Loire Aubance, Maine-et-Loire, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as a castle by the Counts of Anjou in the 11th century. Rebuilt in the 15th century by Pierre de Brézé. Acquired by René de Cossé in the 16th century. Severely damaged during the French Wars of Religion, it was rebuilt in 1611 by Charles II de Cossé with funds from King Henry IV. Ransacked during the French Revolution in 1792, it was restored starting in 1844.

Major_Events.Event: Meeting between Louis XIII and Marie de Medici
Major_Events.Description: King Louis XIII and his mother, Marie de Medici, met to discuss their differences at the château, reaching a temporary truce.
The château was ransacked during the French Revolution and lay in waste until restoration began in 1844.
The château was used as the temporary stadium for two battles of the original Japanese Iron Chef television show, aired on April 12, 1996.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tallest château in France with seven stories. Features Baroque architecture influences from the 17th century. Includes a luxurious gilded theatre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The château is a historic monument listed by the French Ministry of Culture. It represents the architectural and political history of France, particularly during the Renaissance and Baroque periods. It remains owned by the noble Cossé family, reflecting centuries of aristocratic heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic residence, tourist attraction, and event venue.
Notable_Visitors: Henry of Navarre (later King Henry IV of France)
world knowledge.Details: The château is open to the public for tours and overnight stays. It hosts the annual Val de Loire festival and has been featured in media such as the Brazilian magazine Caras and the Japanese visual novel Fate/Stay Night.

world knowledge.Name: Dunans Castle
world knowledge.Address: Glendaruel, Cowal Peninsula, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dunans Castle is an historic structure located in Glendaruel, on the Cowal peninsula, Argyll and Bute, Scotland. Originally a property at Dounens shown on maps in 1590, it was elaborated into its present mock castle form in 1864. It was home to the Fletcher Clan for over two centuries and was ruined by fire in 2001.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was gutted by fire on 14 January 2001 while being run as a hotel, leaving the building as a ruin. The fire began in the attic space and destroyed three floors, with only the pre-Victorian west wing surviving undamaged.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Franco-baronial "castle" form with four main apartments and six bedrooms, designed by architect Andrew Kerr.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dunans Castle is culturally significant as a historic structure and former home of the Fletcher Clan. It is also notable for its architectural style and the ongoing restoration efforts supported by the Dunans Charitable Trust.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is currently in very poor condition and remains in the at-risk category of the Buildings at Risk Register. The current owners operate a scheme where individuals can purchase "Laird or Lady packages" to support restoration efforts. The site also includes Dunans Bridge, an A-listed structure designed by Thomas Telford in 1815.

world knowledge.Name: Eastern University, Sri Lanka
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Eastern University Sri Lanka (EUSL) is a public university in Vantharumoolai, Eastern Province, Sri Lanka. It was established on 1 October 1986, preceded by the Batticaloa University College established on 1 August 1981. The university was developed to address the need for higher education in the Eastern Province. It has a main campus at Vantharumoolai, Trincomalee Campus at Trincomalee, and the Swami Vipulananda Institute of Aesthetic Studies (SVIAS) at Kalladi.

Major_Events.Description: The Batticaloa University College was established to fill the need for higher education in the Eastern Province.

Major_Events.Event: Upgrading to Eastern University, Sri Lanka
Major_Events.Description: The Batticaloa University College was upgraded to the Eastern University, Sri Lanka by a University Order dated 26 September 1986.
The Trincomalee Campus of the Eastern University was established from 15 June 2001.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Faculty of Health-Care Sciences
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Health-Care Sciences was established by Gazette notification dated 23 November 2005.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's main campus is located in Vantharumoolai, with additional campuses in Trincomalee and Kalladi. The buildings were restructured from the Vantharumoolai Madya Maha Vidyalayam, which was damaged by a cyclone in 1978.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Eastern University, Sri Lanka, plays a crucial role in providing higher education in the Eastern Province, particularly for the Tamil-speaking population. It also contributes to the cultural and socio-economic development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university has seven faculties: Science, Agriculture, Commerce & Management, Arts & Culture, Health-Care Sciences, Graduate Studies, and Siddha Medicine. It also has affiliations with the Association of Commonwealth Universities and the International Association of Universities. The university receives funding from the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Sri Lanka.

world knowledge.Name: Teatro degli Arcimboldi
world knowledge.Address: Converted Pirelli tire factory, Bicocca, Milan, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built over a 27-month period in anticipation of the closure and subsequent nearly three-year-long renovation of Milan's La Scala opera house in December 2001. It allowed the continuation of La Scala's 2001/2002 opera season.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated with a performance of Verdi's La traviata on 19 January 2002.
Following La Scala reopening on 7 December 2004, Teatro degli Arcimboldi expanded its program, hosting musicals and performances of jazz, classical and pop music.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Fan-shaped, two-level auditorium with 2,375 seats, designed by Vittorio Gregotti in collaboration with Mario Botta and Elisabetta Fabbri.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Served as a temporary venue for La Scala's performances during its renovation, ensuring the continuation of Milan's opera season. It continues to host diverse cultural performances.
world knowledge.Details: Located 4.5 miles from the city centre of Milan in a converted Pirelli tire factory.

world knowledge.Name: Chengyang Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chengyang Bridge, also known as Yongji Bridge or Panlong Bridge, is a covered bridge completed in 1912. It is one of several Fengyu bridges in the Dong Minority region and serves as a link between two populous villages.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a combination of bridge, corridor, veranda, and Chinese pavilion. It has two platforms, 3 piers, 3 spans, 5 pavilions, 19 verandas, and three floors. The piers are made of stone, the upper structures are mainly wooden, and the roof is covered with tiles. The bridge has wooden handrails on both sides. It has a total length of 64.4 meters and a corridor width of 3.4 meters, with a net height above the river of about 10 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant as a representation of Dong Minority architecture and craftsmanship. It is also notable for its poetic tribute by Guo Moruo, a famous Chinese author.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge serves as a link between two populous villages and functions as a covered bridge for pedestrians.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also called the Chengyang Wind and Rain Bridge or Panlong Bridge. Guo Moruo wrote a poem for the bridge after loving it at first sight.

world knowledge.Name: Wyandotte Caves
world knowledge.Area: Harrison–Crawford State Forest, Crawford County, Indiana
world knowledge.Address: Wyandotte Caves 7315 S Wyandotte Cave Rd Leavenworth, IN 47137
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 9.2 miles (14.8 km) of passageways on five levels
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wyandotte Caves began to form in the Pliocene Era, about 2 million years ago. The caves were used by Native Americans for nearly 4000 years before European arrival, with evidence of human activity potentially as far back as 8000 BC. European settlers discovered the cave around 1798, and it became a source of saltpeter and Epsom salts. Commercial tours began in 1850, making it the fourth oldest commercial cave in the United States.

Major_Events.Description: Wyandotte Caves were designated a National Natural Landmark.
The caves were closed to visitation to slow the spread of white-nose syndrome affecting the bat population.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Limestone caves with long open passageways and large rooms. Features include Monument Mountain (the world's largest underground mountain), helictites, and the tallest stalagmite in the world (Pillar of the Constitution). Siberts Cave contains various speleothems like stalactites, stalagmites, columns, flowstone, cave bacon, cave draperies, soda straws, popcorn, and rimstone dams.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wyandotte Caves are culturally significant due to their long history of use by Native Americans for mining aragonite and chert, their role in saltpeter production during the War of 1812, and their status as a National Natural Landmark and popular tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The caves are home to over 20 known animal species, including bats, cave salamanders, crayfish, and crickets. The temperature inside both caves maintains a constant 52°F (11°C). The caves are closed to the public from November 1 to February 28 to protect hibernating bats.

world knowledge.Name: University of Sassari
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Sassari was founded by Alessio Fontana, a member of the Imperial Chancellery of Emperor Charles V, in 1558. It officially opened in May 1562 and was initially run by the Jesuits. It is one of the oldest universities in Italy and has grown to include 11 faculties and over 40 departments, study centres, and institutes.

Major_Events.Event: Ranked first for best 'medium-sized' Italian university
Major_Events.Description: The University of Sassari earned first place in the rankings for the best 'medium-sized' Italian university by the Censis Research Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Fell to 6th position among best Italian universities
Major_Events.Description: In 2012, the University of Sassari fell to the 6th position among the best Italian universities.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Sassari is one of the oldest universities in Italy and plays a significant role in the educational and cultural development of the region. It has a rich history and has contributed to the academic and professional growth of its students.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Sassari is a public university located in Sassari, Italy. It was founded in 1562 and is organized into 13 departments. The university has over 18,000 students and about 700 teachers. It has collaborated internationally with organizations like TreeAndHumanKnot and RisingIndia ThinkTank to provide students with international experiences.

world knowledge.Name: Wyre Estuary Country Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wyre Estuary Country Park is located in Thornton-Cleveleys, Lancashire, England. Established in 1991, it is situated on the western banks of the 28-mile (45 km) long River Wyre, near its mouth at the Irish Sea at Fleetwood. The Wyre estuary forms part of the southern boundary of Morecambe Bay.

Major_Events.Description: The park has received a Green Flag Award.
The park has received a VisitEngland Award.

Major_Events.Event: Northwest Britain in Bloom Gold Awards
Major_Events.Description: The park received Northwest Britain in Bloom Gold Awards in the Large Park Category.

Major_Events.Event: Northwest Britain in Bloom Gold Awards
Major_Events.Description: The park received Northwest Britain in Bloom Gold Awards in the Large Park Category.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park's main feature is its network of footpaths that either follow the course of the river to the east, eventually leading to Skippool Creek, or an inland route over grassland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a popular destination for ornithologists and botanists. It is a starting point on the Wyre Way and has received several awards for its quality and beauty.
world knowledge.Details: From the park's car park, Fleetwood can be viewed to the north, and there are also vistas across the river to South Lakeland to the northeast, Over Wyre to the east and, beyond, the Bowland Fells. Cockle Hall, the former site of a cottage occupied by a family of thirteen, is located a short distance along the path. The ferryman who took people to and brought people from Wardleys Creek, on the opposite side of the river, also lived there. A café is situated just inside the main gates, at the end of River Road, while a boat ramp is located at the end of the car park on the left. Hillylaid Pool empties into the river after its 4.55 miles (7.32 km) journey.

world knowledge.Name: National Art Museum of Azerbaijan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Azerbaijan National Museum of Art was founded in 1936 in Baku and was named after Rustam Mustafayev in 1943. It consists of two 19th-century buildings and houses over 15,000 artworks, with 3,000 items on permanent display. The museum has undergone several significant events, including theft in 1993, reconstruction in 2006, and achieving European Museum Standard in 2011.

Major_Events.Description: Various artworks were stolen from the museum but were later retrieved.
The building was thoroughly reconstructed, and a new exhibition opened in 2009.
The museum was declared to meet European Museum Standard (EUMS), signifying high-quality museum services and professional experience.
The Museum held a multimedia Museum Night as part of a strategic partnership with the UN to promote sustainable development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of two 19th-century buildings. The first building features European and Russian art, while the second building houses Eastern art. The architectural style includes classical elements and plastic means on rustication's background, with porticoes on the main facade and loggias on the side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is the largest art museum in Azerbaijan and holds a significant collection of artworks from various periods and regions, including antique works, Middle Ages artifacts, and works by Azerbaijani, European, Russian, and Eastern artists. It plays a crucial role in preserving and showcasing Azerbaijan's cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes over 15,000 artworks, with 3,000 items displayed in 60 rooms. It also has a library with approximately 9,000 scientific books and monographs. The museum has hosted exhibitions in various countries, including Canada, Cuba, France, and Iraq.

world knowledge.Name: Galata Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 490 m (1,610 ft) long, 42 m (138 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Galata Bridge spans the Golden Horn in Istanbul, Turkey. It is the fifth bridge on the same site, with the first recorded bridge dating back to the 6th century during the reign of Justinian the Great. The current bridge was built in 1994, replacing earlier bridges from the 19th and 20th centuries. The bridge has played a significant role in Turkish literature, theater, poetry, and novels.

Major_Events.Description: The first recorded bridge over the Golden Horn was built during the reign of Justinian the Great.
Before the Fall of Constantinople, the Turks assembled a mobile bridge by placing their ships side-by-side across the Golden Horn.
Sultan Bayezid II solicited plans for a bridge, and Leonardo da Vinci designed an unprecedented single-span 280 m long bridge, which was not approved.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the first Galata Bridge
Major_Events.Description: The first Galata Bridge at the mouth of the Golden Horn was constructed out of wood at the request of the Valide Sultan.
The area was affected by British bombs during the bombing of Istanbul.
The fourth bridge was badly damaged in a fire and was later towed away.
The current Galata Bridge was completed and opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current Galata Bridge is a bascule bridge made of concrete. It is 490 m (1,610 ft) long with a main span of 80 m (260 ft). The deck is 42 m (138 ft) wide and features two vehicular lanes, tram tracks, and a walkway in each direction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Galata Bridge has long acted as a symbolic link between the old city of Istanbul and the modern districts of Beyoğlu. It has been featured in Turkish literature, theater, poetry, and novels, as well as in works by international authors like Virginia Woolf and Ben Elton. The bridge is also significant for its role in the development of modern Turkish rock music.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge serves as a transportation link, accommodating vehicles, trams, and pedestrians, and connecting the districts of Karaköy and Eminönü.
world knowledge.Details: The Galata Bridge has been the subject of many paintings and engravings due to its romantic appearance. It is sometimes suggested that the card game bridge acquired its name because British soldiers who invented it used to cross the Galata Bridge on their way to coffeehouses. The bridge also houses restaurants on its underside, adding to its cultural and social significance.

world knowledge.Name: Emo Court
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Emo, County Laois, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Emo Court is a large neo-classical mansion designed by architect James Gandon in 1790 for John Dawson, the first Earl of Portarlington. Construction began in the 1790s but was not completed until the 1860s under the third Earl of Portarlington. The house passed through several owners and was eventually taken over by the Irish state in the 1990s. It is now managed by the Office of Public Works and open to visitors.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Emo Court began under the direction of architect James Gandon for John Dawson, the first Earl of Portarlington.
John Dawson, the first Earl of Portarlington, died before the completion of Emo Court.
The third Earl of Portarlington completed the construction of Emo Court, bringing it to a state closely resembling its current form.
The Jesuits acquired Emo Court and used it as a novitiate, making significant interior changes to accommodate their needs.
The Jesuits sold Emo Court to Major Cholmeley Harrison, who commissioned the restoration of the house.
Major Cholmeley Harrison presented Emo Court to the President of Ireland, Mary Robinson, on behalf of the people of Ireland.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Emo Court features neo-classical architectural elements, including sash-style windows, pavilions, a balustrade, a hipped roof, and a large dome. The interior includes an octagonal entrance hall, a rotunda inspired by the Pantheon, and pilasters of Siena marble.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Emo Court is significant as one of the few houses designed by renowned architect James Gandon. It reflects the neo-classical architectural style and has a rich history tied to the Earls of Portarlington and the Jesuits. The estate is now a public heritage site, preserving its historical and architectural legacy.
world knowledge.Details: Emo Court's gardens cover 35 hectares of landscaped grounds, featuring formal areas, woodland walks, statues, and a 20-acre lake. The estate includes rare specimen trees, azaleas, rhododendrons, and camellias. The house and gardens are managed by the Office of Public Works and are open to the public.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Kamui
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Kamui is a natural landmark located on the western part of Shakotan, Hokkaido, Japan. It is known for its lighthouse and a historical tsunami event.

Major_Events.Description: An earthquake off the cape on 2 August 1940 resulted in a tsunami that killed ten people.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cape Kamui is a notable natural landmark in Hokkaido, Japan, and is recognized for its scenic beauty and historical events.
world knowledge.Details: Cape Kamui's lighthouse, the Cape Kamui Lighthouse, overlooks the Sea of Japan. The cape is also a subject of media and Wikipedia articles, though the article is currently a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Magdeburg Water Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 918 metres (3,012 ft) (690 m over land and 228 m over water)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Planning for the canal crossing dates back to at least the beginning of the 20th century. Work on the Mittellandkanal began in 1905, while work on the overall project continued until 1942, when all construction was halted due to World War II. After the war, the government of East Germany did not resume work on the project due to the lack of importance of east-west trade during the Cold War. After the reunification of Germany, the reestablishment of major water transport routes made the water bridge a priority again. Construction started in 1998, took six years, and cost €501 million.

Major_Events.Description: Construction was halted due to World War II.
After German reunification, construction resumed to reconnect major water transport routes.
The bridge was completed and opened to connect Berlin’s inland harbor network with the ports along the Rhine River.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beam Bridge design incorporating 24,000 tons of steel and 68,000 cubic meters of concrete. It spans the river Elbe with a total length of 918 meters (3,012 ft), width of 34 meters (112 ft), height of 6.25 meters (20.5 ft), and water depth of 4.25 meters (13.9 ft). It includes a double lock for vessels to descend from the bridge level to the Elbe-Havel Canal.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest canal underbridge in Europe, it facilitates direct commercial shipping between the Rhineland and Berlin without requiring ships to navigate the Elbe River. It symbolizes post-reunification infrastructure development in Germany.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigable aqueduct for commercial ships, pedestrians, and cyclists.
world knowledge.Details: Featured in the motion picture 'Hanna' and the film 'Vitou the Kong.' Connects the Mittellandkanal on the west side and Elbe-Havel Canal on the east side of the river Elbe.

world knowledge.Name: Eye of Kuruman
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Eye of Kuruman is a natural spring in Kuruman, South Africa, known as the largest natural spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Originally used by Tswana herders as a water hole, it became a crown reserve under British rule in 1885. The area was later segregated by race under Apartheid, with black cultivators evicted from using the water. The spring was declared a Provincial Heritage Site in 1992.

Major_Events.Description: The area was classified as part of the Crown Colony of British Bechuanaland, prohibiting Tswana people from using the stream.
Black cultivators were evicted from using water from The Eye and moved to Seodin, where irrigation was more difficult.

Major_Events.Event: Forced removal of black people from Seodin
Major_Events.Description: Apartheid legislation led to the forced removal of black people from Seodin.
The Eye of Kuruman was declared a Provincial Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Eye of Kuruman is a natural spring forming a small lake in the middle of the town. The cave from which the springs emerge is part of the dolomitic Ghaap Plateau, with streams of water flowing through various passages and emerging at the base of a cliff.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Eye of Kuruman is culturally significant as a historical water source for Tswana herders and later as a contested resource during British rule and Apartheid. It is also notable for being the largest natural spring in the Southern Hemisphere.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural spring supplying water to the town of Kuruman.
world knowledge.Details: The spring has a daily flow of about 20,000 cubic metres of crystal-clear, potable water. The cave has a constant temperature of about 21°C with 99% humidity. It was once home to bat species like the common bent-wing bat and Geoffroy’s horseshoe bat, but few remain due to human disturbance. Aquatic animals like Cixiidae and small flies are also found in the cave.

world knowledge.Name: Guangzhou Chimelong Tourist Resort
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of China's largest and most popular theme park resorts, featuring a variety of attractions including theme parks, zoological parks, a waterpark, and a circus.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theme park resort offering entertainment and leisure activities.

Components.Name: Chimelong Paradise
Components.Description: The resort's flagship park, one of China's largest and most popular theme parks with over 60 attractions.

Components.Name: Chimelong Water Park
Components.Description: The most visited waterpark in the world.

Components.Name: Chimelong Safari Park
Components.Description: An expansive zoological park featuring many rare animals from around the world.

Components.Name: Chimelong Birds Park
Components.Description: A zoological park primarily displaying birds.

Components.Name: Chimelong International Circus
Components.Description: Performances take place daily at the resort's large indoor theater.

Details.Hotels: Three hotels are located on site.

Transcriptions.Cantonese: gwong2 zau1 coeng4 lung4 leoi5 jau4 dou6 gaa3 keoi1

world knowledge.Name: O'Moore Park
world knowledge.Address: Portlaoise, County Laois, R32 CRF3, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: O'Moore Park has been in use as a GAA ground since 1888 and was acquired by Maryborough GAA Club in 1908. It was purchased as the county grounds in 1917, becoming one of the first grounds acquired by a county board, just six years after the purchase of Croke Park.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium underwent renovations, including the installation of floodlights, making it a frequent venue for club and county matches.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a stand with white seats against a background of blue seats spelling out "Laois Laois". It has a spectator capacity of about 22,000, with 6,500 seated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: O'Moore Park is the home of the Laois Gaelic football and hurling teams and is a significant venue for GAA matches in Ireland. It is frequently used as a neutral stadium for inter-county matches not involving Laois.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: GAA stadium for Gaelic football and hurling matches
world knowledge.Details: Under a new sponsorship deal, it is known as "Laois Hire O'Moore Park". The ground is located 0.5 km from Portlaoise town centre on the N80 road (Abbeyleix road). Its pitch is one of Ireland's best under weather conditions.

world knowledge.Name: T-Mobile Park
world knowledge.Address: 1250 First Avenue South, Seattle, Washington, U.S.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Field size: Left Field – 331 ft (101 m), Left-Center – 378 ft (115 m), Center Field – 401 ft (122 m), Right-Center – 381 ft (116 m), Right Field – 326 ft (99 m), Backstop – 69 ft (21 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: T-Mobile Park was built to replace the Kingdome after public funding was approved following the Mariners' 1995 postseason success. The stadium opened in 1999 and was initially named Safeco Field before T-Mobile acquired naming rights in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: Set the stadium's record attendance of 54,097.
Hosted as Safeco Field, won by the American League.
Hosted as T-Mobile Park, won by the National League.
Seattle Kraken defeated Vegas Golden Knights 3–0.
Chicago White Sox pitcher Philip Humber pitched the 21st perfect game in MLB history against the Mariners.
Mariners pitcher Félix Hernández pitched the 23rd perfect game in MLB history, the first in Mariners history.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Retractable roof ballpark with a seating capacity of 47,929. Features a Kentucky Blue Grass / Perennial Ryegrass blend surface. The roof covers approximately 9 acres and weighs 22 million pounds, taking 10-20 minutes to open or close.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Home of the Seattle Mariners, T-Mobile Park is a key part of Seattle's sports culture. It has hosted major events like WrestleMania, MLB All-Star Games, and the NHL Winter Classic. The stadium also features public art, including statues of Mariners legends like Ken Griffey Jr. and Edgar Martínez.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Baseball stadium and multi-purpose venue for events like concerts, soccer matches, and wrestling.

Details.Owner: Washington State Major League Baseball Stadium Public Facilities District
Details.Operator: Washington State Major League Baseball Stadium Public Facilities District
Details.Roof_Details: The roof does not fully enclose the ballpark, allowing wind and temperature to impact games. It is moved 300-500 times per year, mostly to manage the grass.
Details.Scoreboard: Second-largest HD video display scoreboard in MLB, over 11,000 square feet.
Details.Hall_of_Fame: Mariners Hall of Fame features plaques of inducted members like Ken Griffey Jr., Edgar Martínez, and Ichiro Suzuki.
Details.Concessions: Features a wide variety of food options, including local restaurants like Ivar's and Din Tai Fung. The 'Pen is a popular standing-room area with food and drink specials.

world knowledge.Name: Viru Viru International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The idea of having an airport in the city of Santa Cruz de la Sierra was conceived in 1965 by General René Barrientos, former president of Bolivia, with the intention of creating an intercontinental airport. Construction began shortly thereafter and was completed in 1983, replacing the obsolete El Trompillo Airport. Upon its inauguration, Viru Viru became a main gateway for international flights. Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano used Viru Viru as a hub before ceasing operations in 2008. In 1997, the government of Bolivia entered into a 25-year contract with Airport Group International to operate the three largest airports in Bolivia. In 2004, Spain's Abertis/AENA purchased TBI. SABSA was substituted in March 2022 by the newly established government agency Navegación Aérea y Aeropuertos Bolivianos (NAABOL), which now manages the airports in Bolivia.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inaugurated to replace the obsolete El Trompillo Airport and became a main gateway for international flights.
The government of Bolivia entered into a 25-year contract with Airport Group International to operate the three largest airports in Bolivia.
SABSA was substituted by the newly established government agency Navegación Aérea y Aeropuertos Bolivianos (NAABOL), which now manages the airports in Bolivia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport is able to handle widebody aircraft including the Boeing 747-400. It has a concrete runway with a length of 11,483 ft (3,500 m).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Viru Viru International Airport is Bolivia's largest international airport and serves as a main gateway for international flights. It is culturally significant as it represents Bolivia's connectivity with the rest of the world.
world knowledge.Details: The name "Viru Viru" originates from the indigenous Guarani language spoken in the area. Some researchers claim that the correct spelling of the term would be "Birubiru". The airport serves as a focus city for Bolivia's biggest airline Boliviana de Aviación and is a hub for Línea Aérea Amaszonas Transportes Aéreos Bolivianos.

world knowledge.Name: Buxton Opera House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Buxton Opera House, built in 1903 and designed by Frank Matcham, initially hosted live performances until 1927 when it was converted into a cinema. It was refurbished and reopened in 1979 as a venue for live performances. It has undergone several restorations, including a major one from 1999 to 2001, and continues to host a variety of performances.

Major_Events.Description: An annual opera-based festival that runs for about two weeks in mid-July, including a Handel opera and other rarely seen operas.
An annual three-week-long festival attracting audiences from all over the UK and abroad.
An annual music festival that saw a wide variety of musical performances over ten days each February.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Frank Matcham, the theatre features an orchestra pit added during the 1979 restoration. It underwent extensive internal and external restoration from 1999 to 2001, and further refurbishments in 2007 included new seats, air conditioning, and backstage improvements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Buxton Opera House is a significant cultural venue in the UK, hosting a variety of performances including opera, dance, musical theatre, and comedy. It is also home to the Buxton Festival and the International Gilbert and Sullivan Festival.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hosting live performances including opera, dance, musical theatre, pantomime, comedy, drama, children's shows, and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre complex includes the adjacent Victorian Pavilion, the 369-seat Pavilion Arts Centre, the Octagon Hall auditorium, a two-storey restaurant with a bar and gift shop, and a 93-seat studio theatre. It presents over 400 performances each year.

world knowledge.Name: Tron Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tron Theatre, located in Glasgow, Scotland, was formerly known as the Tron Kirk and began as the Collegiate Church of Our Lady and St. Anne. The current Tron Theatre Company started as the Glasgow Theatre Club in 1978 and took over the almost derelict Tron Kirk, originally built for the Church of Scotland in 1795. The theatre opened its doors on 10 May 1981 and has since become a significant venue for contemporary theatrical work, education, and outreach.

Major_Events.Description: The Tron Theatre opened its doors on 10 May 1981, marking the beginning of its role as a significant venue for contemporary theatrical work.
The theatre underwent a significant refurbishment in 1999, which included the addition of two notable contemporary sculptures by artist Kenny Hunter.

Major_Events.Event: World Premiere of 'Further than the Furthest Thing'
Major_Events.Description: The Tron Theatre Company presented the world premiere of 'Further than the Furthest Thing' by Zinnie Harris, which received universal critical acclaim and won four major awards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tron Theatre building, originally designed by James Adam in 1795, features a blend of historical and contemporary elements. The 1999 refurbishment added two notable contemporary sculptures by artist Kenny Hunter.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tron Theatre is culturally significant as a producing and receiving house for contemporary theatrical work, contributing to the development of theatre in Scotland and beyond. It has been a platform for emerging artists and playwrights, and its Education and Outreach department offers a range of activities to engage the community.
world knowledge.Details: The Tron Theatre has two notable contemporary sculptures that were added to the exterior of the theatre as part of its lottery funded refurbishment in 1999. The sculptures are of a large golden cherub and of a skull. The works are by artist Kenny Hunter.

world knowledge.Name: Art Tower Mito
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Opened in 1990 as part of the centennial celebrations of the municipality of Mito.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Arata Isozaki, based on the Boerdijk–Coxeter helix. Acoustical design by Nagata Acoustics. Features a 100-meter landmark tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: An arts complex contributing to the cultural landscape of Mito, featuring a concert hall, theater, and contemporary art gallery.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Arts complex (concert hall, theater, contemporary art gallery)
world knowledge.Details: Cost of construction was ¥9,711 million. Owned by Mito City. Includes a concert hall seating 680 and a theater for up to 636.

world knowledge.Name: Capitol Theatre, Sydney
world knowledge.Address: 3–15 Campbell Street, Haymarket, City of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The site of the Capitol Theatre has provided entertainment to the people of Sydney since the early 19th century. Initially a market place for produce and hay, it was later converted into the New Belmore Markets in 1893. The markets were commercially unsuccessful and were repurposed as a circus venue (Hippodrome) in 1916. In 1928, it was converted into an atmospheric theatre. The theatre underwent several changes in function and ownership, including a period of decline in the 1970s and 1980s, before being restored to its original grandeur in the 1990s.

Major_Events.Description: The New Belmore Markets opened as a covered market for fruit and vegetables but was not economically successful.
The site was leased to Wirth Brothers and converted into a circus and hippodrome venue, featuring elaborate circus acts and vaudeville shows.
The Hippodrome was remodeled into an atmospheric theatre designed by Henry Eli White and John Eberson, featuring an Italian garden-style interior.
The theatre underwent a massive two-year reconstruction costing over $30 million to restore it to its original 1928 grandeur.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Capitol Theatre is a brick building with stone cornices, terracotta capitals, rosettes, and tiled panels. The interior was designed as an atmospheric theatre, resembling an Italian garden or piazza, and features an internal imitation courtyard. The theatre is the only surviving atmospheric theatre in Australia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Capitol Theatre is important for its historical adaptation and reconstruction, demonstrating the course of cultural history in New South Wales. It is the only atmospheric theatre to survive substantially intact in Australia and is listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register and the Register of the National Estate.
world knowledge.Details: The Capitol Theatre is owned by Foundation Theatres and has a seating capacity of 2,094. It is located near Central Station and Capitol Square Light Rail. The theatre was listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.

world knowledge.Name: Brabourne Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Brabourne Stadium was built during the British Bombay era on reclaimed land along Marine Drive. It was India's first permanent sporting venue and was intended to be the 'Lord's of India'. The stadium was named after Lord Brabourne, the then Governor of Bombay, who facilitated the land acquisition. The Cricket Club of India (CCI) owns the stadium, which has hosted numerous significant cricket matches and other events since its inauguration in 1937.

Major_Events.Description: India vs West Indies, marking the stadium's debut as a Test venue.
Australia defeated West Indies in the final, held at Brabourne after renovations.
India played Australia in the first T20I on Indian soil.
Australia beat West Indies in the final held at Brabourne.
India vs Sri Lanka, marking the return of Test cricket to the venue after the longest gap between Tests at the same ground.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a three-story art deco nautical pavilion with rounded pediments, flagpoles, and port-hole windows. The pavilion includes dark wood wall paneling, decorative marble floors, and portraits of cricketers. Public stands (West, North, East) have cavernous, overhanging roofs. The design aimed to emulate Lord's Cricket Ground in England.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brabourne Stadium is a historic cricket venue that has hosted iconic matches, international tournaments, and cultural events. It symbolizes Mumbai's cricketing heritage and has been praised by legends like Keith Miller and Brian Lara. The stadium also hosted political speeches, concerts, and film events, making it a multifunctional cultural hub.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International cricket stadium and multipurpose event venue.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has hosted cricket, tennis, football, concerts, and political events. It was home to the Mumbai Indians (IPL) and Rajasthan Royals. The Cricket Club of India (CCI) maintains strict membership privileges, including pavilion access. The ground was designated a Heritage Grade IIB structure. Notable incidents include a crowd disturbance during a 1969 Test and Chris Cairns' infamous pool jump before an ODI in 1995.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Langano
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Surface area: 230 km² (89 sq mi), Max. length: 18 km (11 mi), Max. width: 16 km (9.9 mi), Max. depth: 46 m (151 ft), Surface elevation: 1,585 m (5,200 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Langano is a lake in the Oromia Region of Ethiopia, located 200 kilometers south of Addis Ababa. It is situated in the Main Ethiopian Rift and is known for being free of Bilharzia, making it popular among tourists and locals. The lake is rich in minerals, including high sulphur levels, which give it a brown color and are believed to have healing properties.

Major_Events.Description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake with its epicenter near the lake, which led to the formation of a 25–30 m tall geyser on Edo Laki Island.
A magnitude 6.2 earthquake with its epicenter near the lake.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Langano is culturally significant due to its popularity as a tourist destination, its unique mineral-rich waters believed to have healing properties, and its role as a safe freshwater lake free of Bilharzia in Ethiopia.
world knowledge.Details: The lake is surrounded by resorts and is popular for water sports. Wildlife around the lake includes hippos, monkeys, baboons, warthogs, and a variety of birds. The area is largely deforested, and many herders live around the lake. The geyser formed after the 1906 earthquake disappeared around 1966–1970, leaving a hot spring.

world knowledge.Name: National University of Cuyo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National University of Cuyo (UNCuyo) was established on March 21, 1939 by presidential decree 26971 to offer tertiary education in the Cuyo region (Mendoza, San Juan, and San Luis provinces). It initially incorporated existing higher education colleges and established regional affiliations in various fields. In 1973, the National University of San Juan and the National University of San Luis were established from its adjunct faculties, leading UNCuyo to concentrate its operations in Mendoza, with an additional campus in Río Negro Province: the Balseiro Institute.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established by presidential decree 26971 to provide tertiary education in the Cuyo region.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of National University of San Juan and San Luis
Major_Events.Description: The adjunct faculties of UNCuyo in San Juan and San Luis became independent universities, leading UNCuyo to focus on Mendoza and the Balseiro Institute in Río Negro.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UNCuyo is the largest center of higher education in Mendoza Province and plays a crucial role in regional education and research. It includes the Balseiro Institute, a leading institute for Physics research in Argentina.
world knowledge.Details: UNCuyo has 12 academic schools in Mendoza, a delegation in San Rafael, and the Balseiro Institute in San Carlos de Bariloche. It also includes the University Technological Institute and operates 7 high schools. Recent research by UNCuyo students has contributed to understanding nutrient retention in food preparation methods.

world knowledge.Name: Patriot Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Patriot Park is a theme park in Kubinka, Russia, themed around Russian military equipment and the Soviet Union's victory in World War II. It officially opened in 2016 and features interactive exhibits with military equipment, including a mini-Reichstag. The park has evolved over time with changing exhibits and additions like the 'Partisan Village' and the Aviation Museum of the Kubinka air base. The Main Cathedral of the Russian Armed Forces was completed in 2020.

Major_Events.Description: The park has hosted this forum since 2015.

On 5 August 2024, the park's head, Vyacheslav Akhmedov, and defence ministry official Major General Vladimir Shesterov were arrested for embezzling funds. On 29 August, General of the Army Pavel Popov was detained for misappropriating funds intended for the park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes military-themed exhibits, hangars for armored vehicles, a 'Partisan Village' with dugouts and other structures made authentically by soldiers, and the Main Cathedral of the Russian Armed Forces. The shooting range features 32 shooting bays, grandstands, and facilities for spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Patriot Park is culturally significant as it commemorates Russian military history and the Soviet Union's victory in World War II. It serves as an educational and interactive space for visitors to learn about military equipment and historical battles.
world knowledge.Details: The park incorporates the Aviation Museum of the Kubinka air base and the Kubinka Tank Museum. Plans for an Armed Force Museum are in progress. The shooting range covers over 160 hectares with a grandstand capacity of over 2,000 people.

world knowledge.Name: Ekiti State University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ekiti State University, originally established as Obafemi Awolowo University in 1982, has undergone several name changes and expansions. It was founded by Chief Michael Adekunle Ajasin, the first civilian governor of Ondo State. The university has grown significantly since its inception, now offering a wide range of academic programs and boasting a student population of over 25,000.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established as Obafemi Awolowo University by Chief Michael Adekunle Ajasin.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Ondo State University
Major_Events.Description: The university's name was changed to Ondo State University.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to University of Ado-Ekiti
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed University of Ado-Ekiti.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Ekiti State University
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed Ekiti State University.
The university was merged with the University of Education and the University of Science and Technology to form Ekiti University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ekiti State University is a significant educational institution in Nigeria, known for its contributions to higher education and its role in the development of the region. It has undergone several transformations, reflecting the political and administrative changes in the country.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers degree programs in 66 fields of academic specialization across various faculties and academic programs. It has a student population of over 25,000 and is partially residential with halls of residence for both male and female students. The university also has affiliate institutions approved by the National Universities Commission (NUC).

world knowledge.Name: Arena Place
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Two 19-story towers with about 390,000 square feet (36,000 m2) each, a 2,850-seat theater, and two nine-story parking garages with 2,200 spaces
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arena Place is a complex including two office towers and a theater. The Arena Theatre was built in 1965, with comedian Bob Hope as an investor. The towers were developed in the early 1980s by Melvin Lane Powers, who built a personal penthouse on top of one tower. Powers filed for bankruptcy, and the towers were later acquired by Lawrence Wong in 1989 and 1990. The complex underwent several ownership changes and renovations over the years, including a $6 million renovation in the 2000s.

Major_Events.Description: Powers filed for bankruptcy and attempted to claim Arena Tower I as his personal residence to prevent foreclosure. Bank of America repossessed the building and evicted Powers.
Lawrence Wong acquired Arena Tower I from Bank of America in 1989 and Arena Tower II from the Midland Bank of England in 1990.
The Arena Group and two limited partners bought the entire Arena Place complex from Lennar Partners for about $24.5 million.

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and re-opening of Arena Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The Arena Theatre underwent a $1 million renovation and re-opened on November 9, 2007, with new carpeting, lighting, sound systems, and other upgrades.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex includes two 19-story black office towers, a circular theater with all seats no further than 65 feet (20 m) from the stage, and two nine-story parking garages. The theater has on-site parking due to the garages. The penthouse in Arena Tower I featured a helicopter pad and a private swimming pool.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arena Place is a notable development in Houston, known for its unique theater design and the flamboyant history of its developer, Melvin Lane Powers. The complex has been a significant part of the local business and entertainment scene for decades.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Office space and live performance theater
world knowledge.Details: The complex is located near PlazAmericas (formerly Sharpstown Mall) and has proximity to the 610 Loop, Beltway 8, and the Westpark Tollway. As of 2016, Xerox Business Services managed a 400-seat call center for CVS Pharmacy in Arena Tower II. The College of Health Care Professions' Southwest Houston, TX Campus and China Airlines Houston Mini Office are also located in the complex.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Corregidora
world knowledge.Address: Avenida Luis Vega Monroy 409-4, Querétaro, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1985 as a collaboration between Mexican and European partners, Estadio Corregidora was a venue for the 1986 FIFA World Cup hosted by Mexico. It is named after Mexican War of Independence heroine Josefa Ortiz de Domínguez ('La Corregidora').

Major_Events.Description: Hosted matches as part of the FIFA World Cup.
On 5 March 2022, violent clashes broke out between Querétaro FC and Atlas FC fans during a match, leading to the suspension of the game and subsequent security investigations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Luis Alfonso Fernandez, the stadium features a capacity of 33,162 and is known for its efficient spectator exit system, allowing safe evacuation in under seven minutes. The playing surface is grass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of Mexico's largest football stadiums, Estadio Corregidora is a key sports and entertainment venue in Querétaro, hosting major concerts and football matches. It honors a national independence heroine.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was vetoed for one year by Liga MX authorities in March 2022 following the fan violence incident. It ranks among Mexico's largest football venues, behind Estadio Azteca, Estadio Olímpico Universitario, and others.

world knowledge.Name: Kunming Changshui International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kunming Changshui International Airport is an international airport serving Kunming, the capital of Southwestern China’s Yunnan province. It opened on 28 June 2012, replacing the old Kunming Wujiaba International Airport. The airport is a gateway to Southeast and South Asia and serves as a hub for several airlines.

Major_Events.Description: Seven construction workers died as an incomplete overpass collapsed.
11 workers were injured when a tunnel that was under construction collapsed.
The airport opened at 08:00 (UTC+8) on 28 June 2012.
