Kunming airport signed an agreement with VariFlight regarding the Airport Collaborative Decision Making system (A-CDM) installation to improve operational efficiency.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main terminal was designed by architectural firm SOM with engineering firm Arup. It features a large terminal building with 66 gates with jet bridges and a total of 88 gates available. The airport has two runways: one 4,500 meters long and the other 4,000 meters long.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a gateway to Southeast and South Asia, the airport plays a significant role in regional connectivity and economic development. It is also the second largest terminal building in China.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Kunming and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is connected to Kunming by a 13 km toll highway known as the Airport Expressway, as well as Provincial Road S101. Kunming Airport station, located within the airport, is the eastern terminus of Line 6 of the Kunming Metro. The airport handled over 47,000,000 passengers in 2024, making it the 47th busiest airport in the world and 4th busiest airport in China by passenger traffic.

world knowledge.Name: Mauritius Postal Museum
world knowledge.Address: Located at the harbour, beside the customs building in the center of the city
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The building was originally constructed as the General Post Office between 1865 and 1870. It replaced the previous General Post Office located in Government Street. The construction was supervised by surveyor general Morrison and cost between £10,000 and £11,000, employing about 80 workers. It officially opened in December 1870 and served as the main post office of Mauritius. In 1958, it became a listed building under the British Governor-general Sir Robert Scott. The postal museum opened in 2001, showcasing the island's postal and telecommunications history.

Major_Events.Description: The building was officially opened as the General Post Office.
The building was listed under Government Notice No. 614.
The building was repurposed as the Mauritius Postal Museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a good example of Victorian architecture of public colonial buildings during the reign of Queen Victoria, similar to those found in India, Sri Lanka, South Africa, Trinidad, and Guyana.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is culturally and historically significant as it represents the colonial architectural style and served as the main post office of Mauritius. It is also a listed building, protected under various national heritage acts.
world knowledge.Details: The museum displays exhibits on the island's postal and telecommunications history. However, the world-famous Red and Blue 'Post Office' Mauritius stamps are exhibited in the nearby Blue Penny Museum.

world knowledge.Name: Volta Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Volta Tower was a folly built in 1865 by William Harcourt Isham Mackworth-Dolben of Finedon Hall to commemorate the death of his eldest son, Lieutenant Commander William Digby Dolben, who drowned off the west coast of Africa in 1863. The tower collapsed in 1951 after standing for 86 years.

Major_Events.Description: Built by William Harcourt Isham Mackworth-Dolben to commemorate his son's death.
The tower collapsed on 16 November 1951, killing Florence Northen, who was inside at the time. Her husband, John Edgar Northen, survived as he was outside.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Circular tower with a gabled extension of one of the two floors, standing about 100 feet (30 m) high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower was built as a memorial and is commemorated in Finedon's town sign. It represents a historical folly and a tragic family history.
world knowledge.Details: The driveway to where Volta Tower stood still exists, and a farm and bungalow have been built on the site. Nothing remains of the tower today except for one carved stone figure of a cherub, which was auctioned in 2005 and bought by a Finedon resident.

world knowledge.Name: Taquarão
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built in 1983 after Taquaritinga was promoted to the Campeonato Paulista first division, as the club's existing stadium was not eligible for the competition. The city hall completed the construction in just three months. It is named after Adail Nunes da Silva, a four-time mayor of Taquaritinga.

Major_Events.Description: The first match played at the stadium was on May 1, 1983, where Taquaritinga beat Cruzeiro 5-2. The first goal was scored by Cruzeiro's Douglas Onça.
The stadium's highest attendance of 25,000 was recorded on June 10, 1983, when Taquaritinga beat Corinthians 2-0.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-use stadium with natural grass surface and a capacity of 18,805 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant local landmark due to its role in hosting football matches and its rapid construction to meet the needs of the Taquaritinga football club. It is named in honor of a prominent former mayor.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches and other sporting events
world knowledge.Details: Owned by the Taquaritinga City Hall, the stadium is also known as Estádio Municipal Adail Nunes da Silva.

world knowledge.Name: Papworth St Agnes
world knowledge.Address: Papworth St Agnes, Cambridge, CB23, England
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Various (e.g., Manor Farm built in 1585, St John the Baptist's Church rebuilt in 1530, 1848, and 1854)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Papworth St Agnes is a historic village in Cambridgeshire, England, with roots tracing back to at least the 12th century. The manor was owned by the Mallory family, and the village features medieval settlement remains. The church, mentioned in the Domesday Book, was rebuilt multiple times. The village declined in the mid-20th century but has seen some restoration since the 1970s.

Major_Events.Description: St John the Baptist's Church was declared redundant by the Church Commissioners, who proposed demolition. Villagers petitioned to save it, leading to restoration efforts.
18 acres were transferred from Papworth St Agnes to Papworth Everard during modern boundary adjustments.
The communal bakehouse was built and used for baking bread and pies for the village. It remains a central feature of the village.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The village features a mix of historic and modern buildings. Key structures include the Manor Farm (1585, framed and plastered), St John the Baptist's Church (rebuilt in Gothic style), thatched cottages, and the white brick Rectory (1847-8). The bakehouse is built of white bricks with a slate roof and an industrial chimney.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Papworth St Agnes is notable for its medieval origins, association with the Mallory family (possibly linked to Sir Thomas Malory), and well-preserved historic buildings. The village represents rural English heritage, with conservation areas and natural history sites.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential village with historical and cultural preservation.
world knowledge.Details: The village includes conservation areas, ridge and furrow remains from medieval farming, and a chalybeate spring (Nill Well). The bakehouse, church, and manor are key landmarks. Population has fluctuated, from 116 in 1921 to around 50 today. The parish lies in an area of 'Best Landscape' with natural history sites.

world knowledge.Name: Eden Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eden Park is a sports venue in Auckland, New Zealand, originally swampland used by Tāmaki Māori. It became a sports ground in 1900, primarily for cricket and rugby. Over the years, it has hosted numerous significant sporting events, including Rugby World Cup finals and Cricket World Cup matches.

Major_Events.Description: New Zealand v England
New Zealand defeated France 29–9
New Zealand defeated France 8–7
Hosted the final

Major_Events.Event: FIFA Women's World Cup Opening Match
Major_Events.Description: New Zealand beat Norway 1-0

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a three-tier South Stand and East Stand, with a capacity of 50,000 (expandable to 60,000 with temporary seating). It includes modern facilities such as food and beverage outlets, toilets, and corporate areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Eden Park is considered New Zealand's national stadium and is renowned for its challenging environment for visiting rugby teams. It has hosted multiple World Cup finals and is a significant venue for both rugby and cricket.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports venue for rugby union, cricket, rugby league, and association football, as well as concerts and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: Eden Park has undergone several redevelopments, most notably in 2010, increasing its capacity and modernizing facilities. It is owned and operated by the Eden Park Trust Board and is a central venue for major sporting and cultural events in New Zealand.

world knowledge.Name: Silesian Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Silesian Stadium is a sport stadium located in Silesian Park, Chorzów, Poland. It was inaugurated on 22 July 1956 with a match against East Germany. It was Poland's national stadium until the National Stadium in Warsaw was completed. The stadium underwent significant modernization from 2009 to 2017.

Major_Events.Description: Set a record attendance of 130,000 spectators.
Attracted 41,200 spectators.

Major_Events.Event: World Athletics Relays and European Team Championships Super League
Major_Events.Description: Hosted international athletics events.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a Mondo Sportflex Super X 720 track, a 43,000 square metre roof, new stands, lighting, video screens, and an improved sound system. It was designed by GMP Architekten.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Silesian Stadium has been a central venue for Polish football, athletics, and concerts. It has hosted numerous international events and is a key cultural and sporting landmark in Poland.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a fully covered capacity of 54,378. It hosted the athletics events of the 2023 European Games and is set to host the 2028 European Athletics Championships. It also hosted the final round of the Individual Speedway European Championship on 21 September 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Anísio Haddad
world knowledge.Address: Rua Joaquim Manoel Pires, 777, São José do Rio Preto, São Paulo state, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Estádio Anísio Haddad, commonly known as Rio Pretão, was built in 1968 and is named after Anísio Haddad, a former president of Rio Preto Esporte Clube. The stadium's inaugural match took place on April 21, 1968, with Ponte Preta defeating Rio Preto 4–1. The first goal was scored by Ponte Preta's Dicá.

Major_Events.Description: Ponte Preta beat Rio Preto 4–1, with the first goal scored by Ponte Preta's Dicá.
The stadium's attendance record of 17,845 was set when Catanduvense beat Rio Preto 1–0.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with natural grass surface and a capacity of 14,126.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in São José do Rio Preto, primarily used for football matches. It is named after a prominent local sports figure, Anísio Haddad.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by Rio Preto Esporte Clube and is nicknamed Rio Pretão, meaning Big Rio Preto.

world knowledge.Name: Radcliffe Camera
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Radcliffe Camera, designed by James Gibbs, was built between 1737 and 1749 to house the Radcliffe Science Library. Funded by the estate of physician John Radcliffe, it became a focal point of the University of Oxford. Initially a science library, it later merged with the Bodleian Library and now serves as a reading room.

Major_Events.Description: The Radcliffe Camera was completed and opened as the Radcliffe Science Library.
The library was officially inaugurated on 13 April 1749.
The building was occupied by students protesting against proposed changes to university funding and tuition increases.
The building was sprayed with orange paint by Just Stop Oil activists protesting Oxford University's links to fossil fuel companies.
Pro-Palestinian activists set up a tent encampment demanding that Oxford University divest from Israel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Radcliffe Camera is an early example of a circular library in England, built in the English Palladian style. It features a heavily rusticated ground stage, a central stage with Corinthian columns, and a lanterned dome. The construction used local stone from Headington and Burford, with a lead-covered dome and cupola.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Radcliffe Camera is a symbol of the University of Oxford and is often featured in visual representations of the university. It represents the legacy of John Radcliffe and the evolution of academic libraries in Oxford.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Academic library and reading room for the Bodleian Library.
world knowledge.Details: The Radcliffe Camera is not open to the public. It now holds books from the English, history, and theology collections, with space for around 600,000 books in rooms beneath Radcliffe Square. The building has undergone several modifications, including the addition of an underground book store and the Gladstone Link.

world knowledge.Name: Laguna Beach, California
world knowledge.Location: Southern California along the Pacific Ocean
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 8.89 sq mi (23.04 km²) land, 0.97 sq mi (2.51 km²) water
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Settled in the 1870s, founded in 1887, incorporated in 1927
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Laguna Beach was historically settled by Paleoindians, the Tongva people, and then Mexico before becoming part of the United States after the Mexican–American War. It was officially founded in 1887 and incorporated as a city in 1927. The city has a rich history as an artist community and tourist destination.

Major_Events.Description: An annual event featuring recreations of famous artworks using real people as models.
A fire that destroyed or damaged 441 homes and burned more than 14,000 acres.
Laguna Beach Council passed Ordinance 1624 to prohibit smoking in all public places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The city features American Craftsman Bungalows from the early 1900s and a mix of modern and historic structures. The natural landscape of beaches, rocky bluffs, and canyons has inspired plein air painters and landscape photographers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Laguna Beach is known as an open-minded artist village with a significant LGBTQ+ population. It has been a center for alternative culture and is home to numerous art festivals, museums, and cultural events.

Details.Climate: Cold semi-arid climate (BSk) with mild weather and abundant sunshine year-round.
Art_Festivals: Festival of Arts Fine Art Show
Laguna Beach Plein Air Painting Invitational
Details.Government: Council–manager form of government, with a non-partisan city council.
Details.Transportation: Served by Orange County Transportation Authority bus routes.
Details.Wildlife: Includes Lined Shore Crab, Black Oystercatchers, Barred Sand Bass, Spiny Lobsters, and Great White Egret.

world knowledge.Name: Rex-Theater (Wuppertal)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rex-Theater is a historically protected theatre in Wuppertal, originally built in 1887 as a restaurant and hotel with a performance hall called 'Salamander'. It claims to be one of the oldest cinemas in the world, showing its first film in 1889. Rebuilt as a movie theatre in the 1930s, it was destroyed in WWII and later reconstructed in 1951. It remains operational today.

Major_Events.Description: The first film was shown at the Salamander hall, leading the Rex-Theater to claim itself as virtually the oldest cinema in the world.
The Salamander was rebuilt as a movie theatre by architect Hans Becker and renamed the Apollo Theatre.
The Apollo Theatre was destroyed by fire during the bombing of Wuppertal in World War II.
The theatre was rebuilt by architect Hanns Rüttgers and reopened as Salamander-Filmbühne, later renamed Rex-Filmbühne due to a legal dispute.
The Rex Theatre was listed under the German monument protection act.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a glass performance hall, later rebuilt in a mid-20th century architectural style by Hanns Rüttgers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rex-Theater is one of the oldest cinemas in the world and the only postwar theatre still operating in Wuppertal, representing the evolution of film and entertainment culture in Germany.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre was renamed multiple times due to legal and historical reasons. It survived the decline of small theatres in the 1980s and continues to operate as a cultural landmark.

world knowledge.Name: Kensington Oval
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kensington Oval is a stadium located in the western part of Bridgetown, Barbados. It is the pre-eminent sporting facility on the island and is primarily used for cricket. Cricket at the Oval began in 1882 when the Pickwick Cricket Club assumed formal ownership of the ground. The first international match was held in 1895, and the first Test match was held in January 1930. The stadium was extensively rebuilt for the 2007 Cricket World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: West Indies v England
West Indies v England
West Indies v New Zealand
West Indies v England
West Indies v Australia
India v South Africa
West Indies v Sri Lanka
West Indies v South Africa
Australia v New Zealand
West Indies v England
Australia v Sri Lanka
Part of the Loud Tour

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was redesigned by Dipesh Patel from Arup Associates. The new design includes a jumbo TV screen, a jacuzzi area, and a large grassy hill for picnics. The outfield uses Tifway 419 hybrid Bermuda grass, and the pitch square was reconstructed with Princess Bermuda grass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kensington Oval is a significant cultural and sporting landmark in Barbados, hosting numerous international cricket matches and other events. It is a symbol of the island's rich cricketing heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The Kensington Oval has also hosted many non-cricket events, such as matches of the Barbados national football team, hockey, inter-school athletics, Miss Barbados pageants, and concert events. It was recognized by the Institution of Structural Engineers in 2008 for its design and construction.

world knowledge.Name: Anfiteatro Correa
world knowledge.Address: Via del Corea, vicinity of the former amphitheatre, Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anfiteatro Correa was an amphitheatre built in 1870 in Rome, Italy, on the remains of the Mausoleum of Augustus. It was later known as the Anfiteatro Umberto I and transformed into the Teatro Augusteo in 1908. The amphitheatre was built at the behest of the Portuguese Marquis Vincenzo Mani Correa, who owned a palace adjacent to the Mausoleum. The name 'Corea' derived from Romanesco dialect. The site initially hosted horse shows, tournaments, and fireworks, with a capacity of 1,000-3,000 spectators. It underwent several transformations and ownership changes before being demolished in 1936 as part of Mussolini's urban redevelopment.

Major_Events.Description: The amphitheatre was inaugurated on 3 July 1780, equipped with wooden scaffolding for horse shows, tournaments, and fireworks.
The velarium collapsed in late August 1826, killing one worker. Pope Leo XII imposed penalties and compensations for the accident.
The theatre hosted one of the first balloon flights in Rome.
The amphitheatre was refurbished into a concert hall, Teatro Augusteo, inaugurated on 16 February 1908 with a concert directed by Giuseppe Martucci.
The theatre was demolished in 1936 as part of Mussolini's campaign to isolate imperial monuments.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The amphitheatre was initially an outdoor venue with wooden scaffolding and bleachers, later equipped with a velarium. It was transformed into a concert hall in 1908, featuring a circular arena design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Anfiteatro Correa represents a significant historical and cultural landmark in Rome, reflecting the evolution of public entertainment venues from amphitheatres to concert halls. Its association with the Mausoleum of Augustus and its role in Roman cultural life underscore its importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Initially served as a venue for horse shows, tournaments, and fireworks; later transformed into a concert hall.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre's memory remains in the toponymy of Rome, with 'Via del Corea' named after Marquis Correa. The area was redeveloped in 1937, surrounding the Mausoleum of Augustus with rationalist buildings designed by Vittorio Ballio Morpurgo.

world knowledge.Name: Blue Planet Aquarium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Blue Planet Aquarium is a marine and freshwater aquarium located by the Cheshire Oaks retail and leisure complex in Ellesmere Port, Cheshire, England. When opened by Queen Elizabeth II in July 1998, it was the largest aquarium in the United Kingdom, and is still the largest in North West England. The £12 million building was designed by Manchester-based Buttress Fuller Alsop architects to resemble the shape of a crashing wave. It was built by Cheshire-based developer Deep Sea Leisure (now owned by Aspro Parks), who also built Deep Sea World in North Queensferry, Scotland.

Major_Events.Description: The Blue Planet Aquarium was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II in July 1998.
The aquarium's shark dive won the Visit Chester and Cheshire Awards 2010 category for Best Tourism Experience of the Year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The £12 million building was designed by Manchester-based Buttress Fuller Alsop architects to resemble the shape of a crashing wave. The interior houses tanks, pools and submerged tunnels designed to take the visitor through different habitats of the marine environment. The main aquarium tank holds 4,000,000 litres (1,100,000 US gal) and features a 71-metre (233 ft) underwater tunnel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Blue Planet Aquarium aims to enlighten, increase knowledge and raise interest in the marine environment using an interactive, entertaining and sustainable approach. It is the largest aquarium in North West England and contains more types of shark than anywhere else in Britain.
world knowledge.Details: Themed areas include Tropical Rivers, Lakes and Ponds, Where Land Meets the Sea, and Seas and Oceans. The aquarium contains many varieties of marine and freshwater fish, including more types of shark than anywhere else in Britain. It also keeps a variety of mammals, reptiles and amphibians.

world knowledge.Name: Cascade Park (amusement park)
world knowledge.Address: 1928 E Washington St, New Castle, Pennsylvania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Big Run Falls, the site was purchased by Col. Levi Brinton in 1892. In 1897, the New Castle Traction Company bought the property and developed it into an amusement park named Cascade Park. The park opened on May 29, 1897. Over the years, it expanded with various attractions, including roller coasters, a zoo, and a lake. In 1934, the Pennsylvania Power Company donated the park to the city of New Castle. The park faced decline in the mid-20th century but was later restored by community efforts in the 1980s.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened on May 29, 1897, after being developed by the New Castle Traction Company.
Attractions like a carousel, baseball field, theater, dance pavilion, roller coasters, zoo, and picnic grove were added.
Pennsylvania Power Company donated the park to the city of New Castle, stipulating it be used for public recreation.
Community volunteers restored the park, removing old rides and adding walking trails, playgrounds, and gardens.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features Victorian-style architecture and includes historic structures like the dance pavilion. The roller coaster Comet was built with a unique design utilizing the natural valley terrain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cascade Park is a historic amusement and nature park that reflects the early 20th-century entertainment culture. It is a community landmark with ongoing cultural events like the Back to the 1950s Weekend.
world knowledge.Details: The park was once home to the Comet roller coaster, which was damaged in 1982 and later torn down. Today, it serves as a nature park with walking trails, playgrounds, and hosts community events.

world knowledge.Name: Tho Xuan Airport
world knowledge.Address: Sao Vàng town, Thọ Xuân District, Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Thọ Xuân Airport, also known as Thanh Hoá Air Base or Bái Thượng Air Base, was built in 1968 and used as a forward staging base with MiGs temporarily deployed from other VPAF bases. It has been a site of multiple attacks during the Vietnam War, including significant damage to the runway in 1972. The airport is currently operated by Vietnam People's Air Force and is undergoing upgrades to become a mixed civilian/military airport.

Major_Events.Description: The airfield was attacked by B-52s, destroying one MiG-17 and cratering the runway.
The base was attacked by US Navy A-6s, causing further damage.
U.S. fighter-bombers attacked the base, cratering the runway.
The base was attacked again, causing additional damage to the runway.
The base was attacked on 11 and 12 November, resulting in six craters in the runway.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a concrete runway measuring 3,200 meters in length.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Thọ Xuân Airport is significant for its role during the Vietnam War as a military air base and its ongoing transformation into a mixed civilian/military airport, serving as a relief airport for Hanoi's Noi Bai International Airport.
world knowledge.Details: The airport handled 90,000 passengers in 2013, 160,000 passengers in 2014, and was estimated to serve 550,000 passengers in 2015, an increase of more than 300%. It is home to the VPAF 923rd Fighter-bomber Squadron operating the Sukhoi Su-30MKK.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Heriberto Hülse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Heriberto Hülse is a football stadium built in 1955, owned by Criciúma Esporte Clube. It honors Heriberto Hülse, Santa Catarina's governor (1958-1960), who donated the stadium floodlights. The inaugural match was played on 18 October 1955. The stadium's capacity was expanded after Criciúma won the Copa do Brasil in 1991 to meet Copa Libertadores requirements.

Major_Events.Description: Imbituba beat Comerciário 1–0, with the first goal scored by Imbituba's Valdo.
32,534 people attended the match between Criciúma and São Paulo (1-1 draw) in the Copa Libertadores.
Criciúma, managed by Luiz Felipe Scolari, won the Copa do Brasil after a 0–0 draw against Grêmio, leading to stadium expansion.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Criciúma Esporte Clube and for hosting key football matches, including the 1991 Copa do Brasil victory and Copa Libertadores games.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's maximum capacity was expanded from 15,000 to 25,000 after the 1991 Copa do Brasil win to meet Copa Libertadores requirements. Current capacity is 19,225.

world knowledge.Name: Mezcala Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Eduardo Neri / Tepecoacuilco de Trujano, Guerrero, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mezcala Bridge was built as part of the 1989–1994 highway restructuring program in Mexico, which reduced the distance of Highway 95 between Cuernavaca and Acapulco by 49 km. It was the world's tallest bridge from its opening in 1993 to 1998 and the highest bridge in Mexico at the time.

Major_Events.Description: A fire occurred in one of the cable systems when a coconut-carrying truck collided with two school buses. The fire damaged one cable and partially closed the bridge until repairs were completed.
As part of Mexico's bicentennial celebrations, Highway 95, including the Mezcala Bridge, was designated as part of "Ruta 2010", commemorating military campaigns led by José María Morelos.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed bridge with H-pylon supports and semi-fan arrangement. Features four adjacent main spans sustained by three consecutive harps of cable stays attached to three tall towers, with the central tower being 173 m (568 ft) high. Constructed with reinforced cement concrete piers and steel superstructure and cables.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a key infrastructure project that significantly reduced travel time between Mexico City and Acapulco. It also holds historical importance as part of Mexico's highway restructuring program and bicentennial celebrations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (toll bridge carrying Mexican Federal Highway 95D)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge spans the Balsas River (Mezcala River) and was designed by Mexican engineer Modesto Armijo. It suffered a cable fire in 2007, leading to studies on improving cable-stayed bridge safety. The bridge's design considered high seismic conditions and turbulent wind effects.

world knowledge.Name: Ely Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 163.7 m (537 ft), Height: 66 m (217 ft), Nave height: 21.9 m (72 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ely Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of the Holy and Undivided Trinity of Ely, is an Anglican cathedral in the city of Ely, Cambridgeshire, England. The cathedral can trace its origin to the abbey founded in Ely in 672 by St Æthelthryth (also called Etheldreda). The earliest parts of the present building date to 1083, and it was granted cathedral status in 1109. Until the Reformation, the cathedral was dedicated to St Etheldreda and St Peter, at which point it was refounded as the Cathedral Church of the Holy and Undivided Trinity of Ely. It is the cathedral of the Diocese of Ely, which covers most of Cambridgeshire and western Norfolk, Essex, and Bedfordshire. It is the seat of the Bishop of Ely and a suffragan bishop, the Bishop of Huntingdon.

Major_Events.Description: Ely Abbey was founded by St Æthelthryth (Etheldreda), a daughter of Anna, King of East Anglia. It was a mixed community of men and women.
Ely Abbey was reestablished as a community of Benedictine monks under the English Benedictine Reform.
Ely Abbey was granted cathedral status with the appointment of Hervey le Breton as the first Bishop of Ely.
The Norman central crossing tower collapsed, leading to the construction of the unique Octagon tower.
Ely Cathedral Priory surrendered to Henry VIII's commissioners during the Dissolution of the Monasteries.
Ely Cathedral was refounded by royal charter with the former prior Robert Steward as dean.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Ely Cathedral is built in a monumental Romanesque style with later additions in the English Gothic style. The cathedral features a cruciform plan with a central octagonal tower, a west tower, and a nave that is one of the longest in Britain. The building is constructed from stone quarried from Barnack in Northamptonshire, with decorative elements carved from Purbeck Marble and local clunch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ely Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as a major center of Christian worship since the 7th century. It is renowned for its architectural grandeur, particularly the Octagon tower, and its role in the history of the English church. The cathedral is also a major tourist destination, attracting around 250,000 visitors annually.
world knowledge.Details: Ely Cathedral sustains a daily pattern of morning and evening services and is the seat of the Bishop of Ely. It also houses the Stained Glass Museum, which contains a collection of stained glass from the 13th century to the present.

world knowledge.Name: The Lowry
world knowledge.Area: Salford Quays, Salford, Greater Manchester, England
world knowledge.Address: Salford Quays, Salford, Greater Manchester, England
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2,000 m² (22,000 sq ft) of gallery space
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lowry is a theatre and gallery complex at Salford Quays, named after the early 20th-century painter L. S. Lowry. It was developed as part of a regeneration plan by Salford City Council in 1988 to redevelop the derelict Salford docks. The project was completed in 2000 at a cost of £106 million, with significant funding from the National Lottery. The complex officially opened on 12 October 2000 by Queen Elizabeth II.

Major_Events.Description: The Lowry was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 12 October 2000.
The Lyric Theatre hosted the 2011 Royal Variety Performance.
The Lowry hosts the bi-annual Week 53 Festival, a flagship arts festival with a multi-disciplinary programme across music, dance, theatre, and performance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Lowry was designed by Michael Wilford with structural engineer Buro Happold and constructed by Bovis Construction. It features a triangular plan, a promenade encircling the building, and a large aerofoil canopy at the entrance clad with perforated steel. Much of the building is clad in stainless steel and glass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Lowry is culturally significant as a major arts and cultural venue in Greater Manchester. It is named after L. S. Lowry, a prominent local artist, and houses a significant collection of his works. The complex has been instrumental in the regeneration of Salford Quays and has been compared to the 'Bilbao effect' for its impact on urban renewal.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Arts centre, including theatre performances, art exhibitions, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The Lowry complex includes two theatres (Lyric and Quays) and a Studio, with a total capacity of 2,346 seats. It also features 2,000 m² of gallery space dedicated to the works of L. S. Lowry and other temporary exhibitions. The complex is close to the Imperial War Museum North and the Old Trafford football stadium, and is served by the MediaCityUK stop on the Metrolink tram network.

world knowledge.Name: Opernhaus Wuppertal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1905 as Stadttheater Barmen, it was severely damaged during World War II in 1943 and rebuilt from 1954 to 1956. It underwent further renovations in the 1970s and from 2006 to 2009. The building has been protected as an architectural monument since 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was severely damaged during an air raid on the night of 30 May 1943, which destroyed the hall completely and damaged the stage area.
The house reopened on 14 October 1956 with a gala performance of Paul Hindemith's Mathis der Maler, one of the first war-damaged theatres in Germany to resume operations.

Several world premieres took place at the Opernhaus Wuppertal, including Yvonne, Prinzessin von Burgund by Boris Blacher (1973), Die fünf Minuten des Isaak Babel by Volker David Kirchner (1980), Kyberiade by Krzysztof Meyer (1986), Erinys by Kirchner (1990), and Gormenghast by Irmin Schmidt (1998).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Carl Moritz in a style drawing on neo-Baroque and Jugendstil. The post-war reconstruction reduced some Jugendstil elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Opernhaus Wuppertal is a significant cultural venue for opera, plays, and dance performances, including those by the Tanztheater Wuppertal company founded by Pina Bausch. It is known for reviving lesser-known operas and hosting world premieres.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre hosting operas, plays, and dance performances.
world knowledge.Details: The opera house is the home base for Tanztheater Wuppertal, founded by Pina Bausch. Notable performances include Frühlingsopfer (1975), Café Müller (1978), Kontakthof (1978), and Nelken (2005). The venue is served by the Wuppertal Suspension Railway and Wuppertal-Barmen station.

world knowledge.Name: Gwalior Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1940 by the Royal Air Force (RAF) as a training base for pilots during World War II, it was transferred to the Indian Air Force (IAF) in 1947. Civil aviation began in 1958, marking the start of commercial connectivity. The airport has since expanded, including the addition of a second runway in 2009 and a new terminal building.

Major_Events.Description: JRD Tata and Nevill Vincent piloted a Waco YQC-6 biplane VT-AIX on the first airmail service between Gwalior and Bombay.
The Royal Air Force (RAF) used the airport as a training base for pilots during World War II, contributing to the Allied victory.
Civil aviation began, marking the start of commercial connectivity for Gwalior airport.
The second runway, built in February 2009, became operational in October 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two operational parallel runways and a new terminal building spread over 20,000 m², completed in 16 months. It includes modern amenities, rainwater harvesting, and a 2.5 GW solar power plant.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named after Vijaya Raje Scindia, a prominent political figure and Maharani of the erstwhile Gwalior State, the airport is a significant part of the region's history and development. It is the oldest and largest airport in Madhya Pradesh and the only airport in Central India with two runways.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Domestic airport serving the city of Gwalior and contributing to national security as an air force base.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is managed and operated by the Airport Authority of India. It is one of the four major airports in Madhya Pradesh and the closest airport to Kuno National Park. The new terminal building can handle 1,400 peak hour passengers, three times more than the previous terminal.

world knowledge.Name: Zurich Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rathaus in Zurich, Switzerland is Zurich's Town Hall. It served as the seat of government and administration of the Republic of Zurich until 1798. The canton of Zurich owns it since 1803, and it houses both legislative chambers, the cantonal parliament (German: Kantonsrat) as well as the City Parliament (German: Gemeinderat). It must be distinguished from the Stadthaus (City Hall), which is the seat of the city's executive government, the City Council (German: Stadtrat) and its administration. It is built on a fundament (foundation) anchored in the river Limmat and faces the Limmatquai (pedestrian area) at a pedestrian bridge, or the Rathausbrücke. The 17th-century building replaces an earlier Rathaus (city council chambers) built in 1397, which in turn replaced a 13th-century court house (Richthus).

Major_Events.Description: The current Zurich Town Hall was built during this period, replacing the earlier Rathaus built in 1397.

Major_Events.Event: Ownership transfer to the canton of Zurich
Major_Events.Description: The canton of Zurich took ownership of the Rathaus in 1803.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Rathaus is a 17th-century building built on a foundation anchored in the river Limmat. It faces the Limmatquai at a pedestrian bridge, the Rathausbrücke.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rathaus is an integral part of the medieval town on the right side of the Limmat. It has served as the seat of government and administration for Zurich for centuries, making it a significant historical and cultural landmark.
world knowledge.Details: Rathaus is also the name of a quarter within the Altstadt district. It is separated by the Hirschengraben from the Hochschulen quarter uphill to the east, and delimited by the Bellevue and Central squares to the south and north, respectively.

world knowledge.Name: The Milky Way (amusement park)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The park originated from the Stanburys' dairy farm, which collapsed due to EU milk quota changes in 1984. Trevor and Christine Stanbury diversified by opening the farm to the public, gradually transforming it into an amusement park.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Little Stars soft-play centre
Major_Events.Description: A soft-play area designed for children aged 0–6, including a sensory room for babies.
Awarded for his services to tourism in southwest England.
A DIY wedding venue in a converted 17th-century barn on the park's grounds.

Major_Events.Event: Listed among top UK amusement parks by Tripadvisor
Major_Events.Description: Recognized as one of the ten best amusement parks in Britain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of indoor and outdoor attractions, including converted farm buildings and purpose-built amusement structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a significant tourist attraction in Devon, recognized for its family-friendly activities and contributions to local tourism. It has won multiple awards, including Devon's Large Attraction of the Year (2023/24) and consistent recognition in Tripadvisor's Travellers Choice Awards since 2015.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park offering rides, shows, and family entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The park features roller coasters, adventure rides, indoor dodgems, bouncing pillows, Sci-Fi memorabilia (including Star Wars and Doctor Who costumes), a mini-train, birds of prey displays, archery, and large indoor soft-play areas. It also hosts events year-round, including weddings and an annual Santa's Grotto. The Lynbarn Railway, a narrow-gauge railway, is a renovated part of the old Lynton and Barnstaple Railway.

world knowledge.Name: Roxie Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Roxie Theatre is a historic former movie theater in the Broadway Theater District of Los Angeles, California. It opened in 1931 as the last theater to be built on Broadway. The site previously hosted Quinn's Superba Theatre from 1914 to 1922 and a coffee shop from 1923 to 1931. The theater was converted into a Spanish-language filmhouse in 1978 and closed in 1989. The lobby was converted into retail space, while the auditorium was left intact.

Major_Events.Description: The Roxie Theatre opened on November 25, 1931, with screenings of 'Honor of the Family' and the Laurel and Hardy film 'Come Clean'.
On August 4, 1943, 37-year-old Roxie Theatre manager Harry R. Metzger died of a heart attack while operating the box office.
On December 24, 1954, a woman committed suicide in the Roxie auditorium during a showtime. Authorities were unable to identify the body.
On June 27, 1958, Roxie usher Richard A. Studeny held theater manager Robert Brandtjen at gunpoint and fled with $1,200. Studeny turned himself in to police in Florida in December 1958.
On January 29, 1978, Metropolitan Theatres converted the Roxie programming to Spanish-language films.
The Roxie Theatre permanently closed in the summer of 1989. The auditorium was left intact while the lobby was converted into retail space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Roxie Theatre was designed by architect John M. Cooper in the Art Deco style. The facade features a central stepped gable with a vertical sign tower spelling 'Roxie' atop it, as well as chevrons and other geometric forms. A colorful terrazzo design on the ground of the building's entrance gained particular notoriety. The 1,600-seat auditorium was designed in a long, narrow orientation to optimize amplified sound. The theater also features a small stage, rigging, and a proscenium arch for live productions. The construction required over 35 miles of electrical wire, 15,000 pounds of sheet metal, and 120,000 bags of cement, as well as a 31-motor ventilation system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Roxie Theatre is culturally and historically significant as the last theater to be built on Broadway and the only one in the downtown section of Los Angeles built in the Art Deco style. It is part of the Broadway Theater and Commercial District and has been designated as a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a movie theater, later converted to a Spanish-language filmhouse.
world knowledge.Details: The Roxie Theatre was designated as part of the Broadway Theater and Commercial District (ID79000484) on May 9, 1979, and as a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument (LAHCM No. 526) on March 20, 1991. The auditorium has fallen into disrepair since the theater's closure, including water damage.

world knowledge.Name: Almudena Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of Saint Mary the Royal of the Almudena, commonly known as the Almudena Cathedral, is a Catholic cathedral in Madrid, Spain. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Madrid. Its construction began in 1883 and finished over a century later, when it was consecrated by Pope John Paul II in 1993. The cathedral was built on the site of a medieval mosque that was destroyed in 1083 when Alfonso VI reconquered Madrid. Construction was interrupted by the Spanish Civil War and resumed in 1950. The cathedral was completed in 1993 and consecrated by Pope John Paul II.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by Pope John Paul II.
The marriage of King Felipe VI, then crown prince, to Letizia Ortiz Rocasolano took place at the cathedral.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Neoclassical, Neo-Gothic, and Neo-Romanesque styles. The Neo-Gothic interior includes modern chapels and statues by contemporary artists. The Blessed Sacrament Chapel features mosaics by Fr. Marko Ivan Rupnik, and the icons in the apse were painted by Kiko Argüello. The Neo-Romanesque crypt houses a 16th-century image of the Virgen de la Almudena.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Almudena Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the seat of the Archdiocese of Madrid and for its long construction history that reflects the city's evolving architectural and religious landscape. It is also notable for hosting the royal wedding of King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is located opposite the Royal Palace and was designed by Francisco de Cubas. The Neo-Romanesque crypt houses a 16th-century image of the Virgen de la Almudena. Nearby along the Calle Mayor, excavations have unearthed remains of Moorish and medieval city walls.

world knowledge.Name: Namiseom
world knowledge.Address: Cheongpyeong Lake, Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Namiseom or Nami Island is a half-moon shaped river island formed as the land around it was inundated by the rising water of the Bukhan River due to the construction of Cheongpyeong Dam in 1944. The island is named after General Nami, who died at the age of 28 after being falsely accused of treason during the reign of King Yejong (r.1468–1470). The island was developed into an amusement park after a tour company arranged the grave of General Nami with soil.

Major_Events.Description: The construction of Cheongpyeong Dam led to the formation of Namiseom by inundating the surrounding land with water from the Bukhan River.
After Min Byeong-do bought the island in 1965, it began to be developed as a general resort by Gyeongchun Tourism Development Co., Ltd.
The area around Nami Island became the filming stage for the Korean Broadcasting System TV drama Winter Sonata, significantly increasing the number of Japanese tourists.
One of the longest zip lines in Asia was opened, gaining recognition after being featured in Korea's show “A day and a Half” in February 2016.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island features natural landscapes and recreational facilities, including a zip line and a self-declared micronation called the Naminara Republic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Namiseom is culturally significant due to its historical association with General Nami, its development as a tourist destination, and its role in popular culture through the TV drama Winter Sonata.
world knowledge.Details: Namiseom is home to the Naminara Republic, a self-declared micronation that advocates the concept of a nation. The island also features one of the longest zip lines in Asia, which reaches the island from an 80-meter tall tower located in Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi Province.

image_name: Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts

world knowledge.Name: Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Annenberg Center, founded in 1971, is a major cultural destination and crossroads in the performing arts, connecting Philadelphia regional audiences and the University of Pennsylvania through exposure to innovative human expression in theatre, music, and dance.

Major_Events.Description: The Center has hosted shows by performers ranging from the Jerusalem Symphony Orchestra to Ladysmith Black Mambazo.

Major_Events.Event: Popularization of Steve Reich and Philip Glass
Major_Events.Description: It helped to popularize the works of composers like Steve Reich and Philip Glass.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Annenberg facility was designed by Vincent G. Kling who also designed the Philadelphia Mint.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Annenberg Center highlights the value of the performing arts by presenting world-renowned and emerging artists and companies who express adventuresome perspectives on contemporary issues, timeless ideas, and diverse cultures.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre, dance and world music venue
world knowledge.Details: The Annenberg Center promotes critical thinking among its audiences, creating uniquely rewarding arts experiences. It has a capacity of 960 (Zellerbach Theatre), 211 (Prince Theatre), and 120 (Montgomery Theater).

world knowledge.Name: Darul Ridzuan Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum building was originally constructed in 1926 as a house for a wealthy tin miner named Foo Choong Kit. In 1950, the house was sold to Perak Government and used as the administrative center of the Department of Works. It was opened as a museum in 1992.

Major_Events.Description: The building was constructed as a house for a wealthy tin miner named Foo Choong Kit.
The house was sold to Perak Government and used as the administrative center of the Department of Works.
The building was opened as a museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building was constructed with British architectural style. It has two floors with eight rooms on the top floor and two rooms on the ground floor. Behind the main building there are another four rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum exhibits the history and development of the mining and agriculture sectors of Ipoh, highlighting its cultural and historical importance in the region.
world knowledge.Details: This article related to a museum in Malaysia is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Rwenzori Mountains National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rwenzori Mountains National Park is a Ugandan national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Rwenzori Mountains. Established in 1991, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994 due to its outstanding natural beauty. The park was inscribed on UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger between 1999 and 2004 due to insecurity and lack of resources.

Major_Events.Description: The park was officially established as a national park.
The park was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its natural beauty.
Rebel militias occupied the Rwenzori Mountains.

Major_Events.Event: List of World Heritage in Danger
Major_Events.Description: The park was listed as endangered due to insecurity and lack of resources.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and historically significant due to its outstanding natural beauty, diverse ecosystems, and unique flora and fauna. It is also important for its role in conservation and as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located in south-western Uganda on the east side of the western (Albertine) African rift valley. It borders the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Virunga National Park. The park includes most of the Rwenzori Mountains, which are higher than the Alps and are ice-capped. It features Mount Stanley, Margherita Peak (Africa's third highest peak), glaciers, snowfields, waterfalls, and lakes. The park is known for its diverse plant life, with five distinct vegetation zones. It is home to many endemic and endangered species, including forest elephants, chimpanzees, and various bird species. The park offers trekking and climbing routes, with the most popular being a seven-day circuit.

world knowledge.Name: Wallasey Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wallasey Town Hall was built to serve as the municipal building for Wallasey, which became a county borough in 1913. The foundation stone was laid by King George V in 1914. During World War I, it was used as a military hospital. After the war, it was converted back to its intended use and officially opened in 1920. It served as the headquarters of Wirral Council until 2023.

Major_Events.Description: King George V and Queen Mary laid the foundation stone for the town hall.
The building was used as a military hospital for wounded soldiers during World War I.
The town hall was officially opened as a municipal building on 3 November 1920.
The civic hall was badly damaged by bombing during World War II. King George VI and Queen Elizabeth inspected the damage.
Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh visited the town hall and waved to the crowd from the balcony.
The freedom of the Wirral was awarded to the 96 victims of the Hillsborough disaster at a ceremony in the town hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with a symmetrical main frontage featuring seventeen bays. The central section has a doorway on the ground floor and three tall round-headed sash windows on the first floor. The building includes a three-stage lantern with seated figures representing peace, courage, prudence, and industry. The building is 180 feet (55 m) high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a Grade II* listed building and has been a significant civic and cultural landmark in Wallasey. It has hosted royal visits, served as a military hospital, and been the site of important ceremonies.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Municipal building (formerly the headquarters of Wirral Council)
world knowledge.Details: The town hall features a civic hall with a proscenium arch and a panelled council chamber. An organ by Henry Willis & Sons, originally from City Hall in Dublin, was installed in 1926 but was destroyed during WWII. Salvaged parts were later used in New Zealand. A modern annex was completed in 1964. Works of art include a landscape of Liverpool Docks by Henry Melling.

world knowledge.Name: Captain George Flavel House Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The house was built in 1885 by George Flavel, a Columbia River bar pilot and one of the area's first millionaires. After Flavel's death in 1893, his wife and daughters lived in the house until their deaths. The house and its carriage house were listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The house and its carriage house were listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Queen Anne architectural style, designed by Carl W. Leick.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The house is a well-preserved example of Queen Anne architecture and is associated with George Flavel, a prominent figure in the region's maritime history. It is also known for its appearance in the film 'The Goonies'.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is owned and operated by the Clatsop County Historical Society. It is featured in the film 'The Goonies' as the museum where Mikey's father works as a curator.

world knowledge.Name: Falls Park
world knowledge.Area: Minnehaha County, South Dakota, United States
world knowledge.Address: north central Sioux Falls, South Dakota
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Falls Park is a public park surrounding the city's waterfalls. It includes a cafe, an observation tower, and the remains of an old mill. The park comprises over 128 acres just north of downtown, along the Big Sioux River. The mill opened in late 1881, consisting of a seven-story main structure built of Sioux quartzite quarried on site. Nearly $500,000 was spent on the construction of the state-of-the-art mill and its supporting structures. The mill could process 1,500 bushels each day. However, the mill closed by 1883, a victim of inadequate water power and a short supply of wheat. Little is known about the history of the Sioux quartzite barn on the northern edge of Falls Park. Oral history has suggested the building was constructed in the late 1800s as a part of a dairy/creamery operation, though there are no historical records to substantiate this. The City of Sioux Falls has owned the structure since 1917. At that time, animals performing city work were stabled there. The barn is now home to the Stockyards Ag Experience, a museum and learning center that connects visitors to agriculture.

Major_Events.Description: The mill opened in late 1881, consisting of a seven-story main structure built of Sioux quartzite quarried on site. Nearly $500,000 was spent on the construction of the state-of-the-art mill and its supporting structures. The mill could process 1,500 bushels each day.
The mill closed by 1883, a victim of inadequate water power and a short supply of wheat.
The City of Sioux Falls has owned the Sioux quartzite barn structure since 1917. At that time, animals performing city work were stabled there.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes the remains of an old mill built of Sioux quartzite. The mill was a seven-story main structure. The Sioux quartzite barn on the northern edge of Falls Park is also constructed of Sioux quartzite.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Falls Park is culturally significant as it includes some of Sioux Falls' oldest buildings and provides a connection to the city's agricultural and industrial history through the mill and the Stockyards Ag Experience.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes a cafe, an observation tower, and the remains of an old mill. The Falls Overlook Café is housed inside the 1908 Sioux Falls Light & Power Co. hydroelectric plant. The observation tower is connected to the visitor center, which offers guidance to visitors and sells souvenirs. The barn is now home to the Stockyards Ag Experience, a museum and learning center that connects visitors to agriculture.

world knowledge.Name: Government House, Hobart
world knowledge.Address: Lower Domain Road, Queens Domain, Hobart, Tasmania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Government House, Hobart, is the home and official residence of the governor of Tasmania. There have been three Government Houses in Hobart. The first was a wooden hut built in 1805, the second was constructed in 1817 but was poorly built and demolished in 1858. The current Government House was designed by William Porden Kay and completed in 1857. It is one of the best vice regal residences in the Commonwealth and features Gothic Revival architecture.

Major_Events.Description: Sir Henry Fox Young became the first governor to take up residence in the current Government House.
Governor General Sir Phillip Bennett initiated an annual open day for Government House.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic Revival style, early Victorian country house. Constructed with sandstone quarried on site, cedar and teak recycled from an old ship, and slate imported from Wales. Features bas-relief architectural sculptures, exceptional stonework, and individually carved sandstone chimney pots. The interior includes 73 rooms with Elizabethan and Jacobean Revival styles, and furniture imported from England.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Government House is regarded as one of the best vice regal residences in the Commonwealth. Its scale, detail, and finish are unequalled in Australia. It serves as a symbol of Tasmania's colonial history and governance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official residence of the governor of Tasmania and venue for receptions, dinners, and events.
world knowledge.Details: The House consists of 73 rooms, including the Main Hall, Dining Room, Ante-Drawing Room, Drawing Room, French Room, Ballroom, and Conservatory. The Conservatory was rebuilt to original designs in 1991. The grounds feature ornately designed English gardens and overlook the Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens and the Derwent estuary.

world knowledge.Name: Rakotzbrücke
world knowledge.Address: Kromlau (Upper Sorbian: Kromola), in the municipality of Gablenz (Jabłońc), Saxony
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Created in the 19th century on the grounds of a former feudal estate by Friedrich Herrmann Rötschke. After World War II, the park was nationalized by the government and remains free to enter (with a nominal parking fee).

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was renovated to preserve its structure, but crossing it remains forbidden for safety reasons.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is an example of an English landscape garden with many small ponds and lakes. Its most famous feature is the Rakotz Bridge (Devil's Bridge), which forms a perfect circle when reflected in the water. The bridge is made of artificially-formed basalt columns and spans 7.8 meters long and 6.5 meters wide.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park and the Rakotz Bridge are notable for their unique landscape design and the optical illusion created by the bridge's reflection. The bridge's basalt columns and its circular reflection make it a picturesque and culturally significant landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The name 'Rakotz' derives from the Upper Sorbian word for crab (rak). The bridge was commissioned in 1860 by Friedrich Herrmann Rötschke. Despite renovations, crossing the bridge is prohibited to protect both visitors and the structure itself.

world knowledge.Name: Mokattam
world knowledge.Area: Eastern Desert plateau, Southern Area of Cairo, Egypt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mokattam, also known as the Mukattam Mountain or Hills, is a plateau in the Eastern Desert and a district in Southern Cairo. Its name means 'cut off' or 'broken off' in Arabic, possibly referring to its division into three sections. Historically, it was an important quarry site for limestone used in ancient Egyptian construction. The area is also significant for the Zabbaleen people who live at its base and process Cairo's waste. It is notable in Coptic Church history due to a miracle attributed to Saint Simon the Tanner.

Major_Events.Description: According to Coptic tradition, the mountain moved up and down during a mass performed by Coptic Pope Abraham of Alexandria to prove the power of faith as described in the Gospel.
The hills are in the region of Fustat, the new capital founded by 'Amr ibn al-'As after the Muslim conquest of Egypt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Mokattam Formation is a limestone plateau, historically quarried for construction materials used in temples and pyramids. The area now includes urban developments like Uptown Cairo.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mokattam is culturally significant for its historical role in ancient Egyptian construction, its importance to the Zabbaleen community, and its religious significance in Coptic Christianity due to the miracle associated with Saint Simon the Tanner.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historically a quarry site; now a residential and commercial district with cultural and religious importance.
world knowledge.Details: The Mokattam district had 224,138 residents in 2017. It is home to the football team Misr Insurance and is near the top division club Al Mokawloon Al Arab SC. The area is also known for the real estate development Uptown Cairo by EMAAR Misr.

world knowledge.Name: Sunnyside North Beach
world knowledge.Address: Sunnyside Road, Mount Eliza, Victoria, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Designated as a legal nudist beach under the Nudity (Prescribed Areas) Act 1983. It is the only clothes-optional beach on the east side of Port Philip Bay.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Recognized as a legal nudist beach, providing a designated area for clothes-optional recreation.

Details.Legal_Status: Legal nudist beach under the Nudity (Prescribed Areas) Act 1983

Beach_Features.Tides: Not very high due to location on Port Philip Bay
Beach_Features.Adjacent_Beaches: South of Moondah Beach and north of Bidwell Beach

Access.Main_Access: From the right side of the car park at the end of Sunnyside Road, approximately 500 meters from the start of the nude beach

Path_Options.Dirt_Path: Winding path through scrub maintained by regulars
Path_Options.Beach_Access: Rocky section to navigate, rocks cleared and concrete used by regulars
Path_Options.Alternative_Access: Longer scenic walk southward from the car park at the end of Kunyung Road along Moondah Beach

Parking.Sealed_Carpark: Small sealed carpark at the end of Sunnyside Road

Amenities.Toilets: Located next to the car park
Amenities.Showers: Located next to the car park
Amenities.BBQs: Free electric barbeques at the far end of the carpark

Details.Signage: Signs at each end of the beach indicate the legal nude area

world knowledge.Name: Cape Jervis Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Cape Jervis, Fleurieu Peninsula, South Australia, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Jervis Lighthouse is a lighthouse located at the headland of Cape Jervis on the most westerly part of the Fleurieu Peninsula on the east coast of Gulf St Vincent in South Australia. It was first lit on 10 August 1871. In 1972, the original tower was replaced by a new tower.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first lit on 10 August 1871.
The original tower was replaced by a new tower.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Inverted-pyramidal (wider at the top than the bottom) concrete tower with balcony and lantern, white tower, height of 18 metres (59 ft), focal height of 23 metres (75 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse serves as a navigational aid and is part of Australia's maritime history.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority. Its light characteristic is Fl (4) W 20s.

world knowledge.Name: Elegushi Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Elegushi Beach is a private beach owned by the Elegushi royal family in Lekki, Lagos state. It is considered one of the best beaches in Lagos and Nigeria, attracting close to 40,000 guests every week, with Sundays being the most popular day.

Major_Events.Description: AXA Mansard’s employees joined AXA employees worldwide in clean-up activities, focusing on increasing cleanliness around the ocean and improving the coastal and ocean ecosystem.
Coca-Cola System cleaned up Elegushi Beach to mark World Environment Day, in collaboration with the Mental and Environmental Development Initiative for Children (MEDIC).

Major_Events.Event: Let’s Do It Campaign Nigeria and JCI clean-up
Major_Events.Description: The Let’s Do It Campaign Nigeria and the Junior Chamber International (JCI) collected 107 wastes from the beach environment.

Major_Events.Event: Food and Beverage Recycling Alliance clean-up
Major_Events.Description: The Food and Beverage Recycling Alliance conducted a cleanup exercise on the beach during the 2023 World Ocean Day, aiming to reduce plastic pollution and raise awareness about responsible waste disposal and recycling.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Elegushi Beach is culturally significant as one of the best beaches in Lagos and Nigeria, attracting a large number of visitors weekly. It also serves as a focal point for environmental awareness and clean-up activities.
world knowledge.Details: The beach entertains close to 40,000 guests every week, with Sundays being the most popular day. The gate pass is priced at 2000 naira flat rate, with possible discounts for groups. The beach has faced several climate and environmental issues, including the presence of various types of waste. Clean-up activities have been conducted by various organizations to address these issues.

world knowledge.Name: Nîmes–Alès–Camargue–Cévennes Airport
world knowledge.Area: Provence region, including the communes of Nîmes and Alès in the Gard department, the Camargue area and the Cévennes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nîmes Airport or Nîmes–Alès–Camargue–Cévennes Airport is an airport located 9 km (4.9 NM) south-southeast of the city of Nîmes, in the village of Saint-Gilles near Garons, France. It is also known as Garons Airport or Nîmes Garons Airport. The French navy (Marine Nationale) pulled out some years ago. Their former facilities are now used by the Armee de Terre. The Securite Civile flying base, formerly at Marseille (LFML), has moved to Garons.

Major_Events.Description: The European Commission launched an in-depth investigation into the financial arrangements that Nîmes Airport had with public authorities and Ryanair. The investigation would determine if public subsidies given to the airport, as well as rebates and marketing agreements with Ryanair, breached EU rules on state aid.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one paved runway designated 18/36 which measures 2,443 by 45 metres (8,015 ft × 148 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves the Provence region, including the communes of Nîmes and Alès in the Gard department, the Camargue area and the Cévennes.
world knowledge.Details: The airport currently has some commercial services, operated by Irish carrier Ryanair, as well as serving as a naval air base. The Securite Civile flying base, formerly at Marseille (LFML), has moved to Garons.

world knowledge.Name: Kallo Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Near the island of Mäntyluoto, Port of Pori
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first lighthouse in the area was built in 1851 but was destroyed three years later during the Crimean War. Its replacement was completed in 1885, and the current lighthouse was built in 1903, designed by architect Gustaf Nyström.

Major_Events.Description: The first lighthouse was built in the area.
The first lighthouse was destroyed as a result of the Crimean War.
A replacement lighthouse was completed after a three-decade delay.
The current lighthouse was built, designed by Gustaf Nyström.
The originally manually-operated fog horn was motorised.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The octagonal tower is constructed of iron over a granite base, with attached lighthouse keeper's accommodation made of timber. The light source consists of two separate lights positioned one on top of the other. The lighthouse also features a fog horn.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kallo Lighthouse is part of the Mäntyluoto area, which includes late 19th and early 20th-century buildings and has been designated as a nationally important built cultural environment by the Finnish Heritage Agency. It is also unusual among Finnish lighthouses for being reachable by car, making it a popular visitor destination.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To serve as a navigational aid for the shipping lane of the Port of Pori.
world knowledge.Details: The Mäntyluoto area includes the Pori pilot station, coast guard station, cafeteria, and the oldest yacht club in Finland, Segelföreningen i Björneborg. The lighthouse's light characteristic is Iso WRG 2s, with a range of 9.4 nautical miles.

world knowledge.Name: Umbrella Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The album cover of "Umbrella Beach" by Owl City features a picture of the beach at Santa Monica, California, taken from the Santa Monica Pier. The song was released as the third single from his second studio album, Ocean Eyes on May 17, 2010.

Major_Events.Description: The song was released as the third single from Owl City's second studio album, Ocean Eyes on May 17, 2010.
"Umbrella Beach" entered the UK Dance Chart on the week ending May 8, 2010, at number 25, later peaking at number 12.
The music video for "Umbrella Beach" premiered on April 16, 2010 via YouTube and was directed by Alexander Brown. The video was filmed in Hope Cove, England.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The song "Umbrella Beach" by Owl City is culturally significant as it represents a blend of indie-folk and electro-pop music, contributing to the broader music landscape of the early 2010s.
world knowledge.Details: The music video for "Umbrella Beach" tells the story of a boy who is trying to build a plane to cross the sea and go to another island. At the end of the video, a group of his friends help him push the plane down a hill for takeoff. It is not shown whether or not the plane successfully flies.

world knowledge.Name: Ballarat Regional Soccer Facility
world knowledge.Address: Morshead Park Stadium, Redan, Ballarat, Victoria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ballarat Regional Soccer Facility, also referred to as Morshead Park Stadium, was upgraded in 2013 with a $2.675 million investment from the City of Ballarat Council and the Federal Government to host training for National Teams in the 2015 Asian Cup. The facility includes new grandstands, lights, and returfing the field.

Major_Events.Description: The Ballarat Red Devils played their first game in the stadium on 3 May 2014, losing 1-2 to South Melbourne FC in the NPLV. South Melbourne player Milos Lujic scored the inaugural goal in the facility.

Major_Events.Event: Bahrain national football team training camp
Major_Events.Description: On 9 May 2014, Premier of Victoria Denis Napthine announced that the facility would host the Bahrain national football team for a sixteen-day training camp prior to the Asian Cup.
Western United played an A-League Men match against Wellington Phoenix at Morshead Park on 9 April 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The facility features a main grandstand seating 500, with standing capacity for 8,000 on viewing embankments. Temporary stands can increase total capacity to 12,000. There are three fully lit football fields, including the main pitch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The facility is significant as a regional soccer hub, hosting local teams like Ballarat City FC and major events such as training camps for national teams and A-League matches.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Association football stadium and training facility
world knowledge.Details: The facility adds 3,000 pitch hours of availability annually to local clubs. It was designed by k20 Architecture and cost $13.85 million to construct.

world knowledge.Name: Steel Pier
world knowledge.Address: 1000 Boardwalk, Atlantic City, New Jersey, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Steel Pier is a historic amusement park built on a pier in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Opened in 1898, it was one of the most popular venues in the United States for the first seven decades of the twentieth century, featuring concerts, exhibits, and an amusement park. It billed itself as the Showplace of the Nation and at its peak measured 2,298 feet (700 m). The pier has undergone several ownership changes, renovations, and reconstructions due to fires and storms. It continues to operate as an amusement pier and is one of the most successful family-oriented attractions in the city.

Major_Events.Description: The Steel Pier was opened on June 18, 1898, as an amusement park and entertainment venue.
A storm washed away part of Steel Pier, leading to its reconstruction by Edward L. Bader.
A fire caused significant damage to the pier, leading to its renovation by Frank Gravatt.
The Steel Pier was the venue where Miss America was crowned during these years.
Parts of the pier were damaged or lost during the Ash Wednesday Storm.
A fire six months before the opening of the 1970 season shortened the pier by about a third.
The current concrete structure of the pier dates from this year after the original wooden pier was destroyed in a 1982 fire.
The Steel Pier celebrated its 110th anniversary with free rides for a day.
A newer and bigger giant Ferris wheel was added to the pier, featuring LED lights.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The pier was built on iron pilings, using a concrete understructure with steel girders. The current structure is made of concrete, dating from 1993 after the original wooden pier was destroyed in a fire.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Steel Pier is culturally significant as a historic entertainment venue that hosted numerous famous acts, including musicians like Frank Sinatra, Al Jolson, Diana Ross and The Supremes, and events like the Miss America pageant. It was known as the 'Showplace of the Nation' and featured unique attractions like the High Diving Horse and the Human Cannonball.
world knowledge.Details: The pier operates as an amusement park with twenty-four rides, a helicopter station, an arcade, and food stands. It offers various ticket options, including discounts for families and military personnel. The pier is owned by Steel Pier Associates, LLC, and operates seasonally from April through October, with the Observation Wheel open from March to December.

world knowledge.Name: Sandavágur Church
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sandavágur Church (Faroese: Sandavágs kirkja; Danish: Sandevåg Kirke) is a distinctive red-roofed church in the town of Sandavágur in the Faroe Islands. The church was consecrated on 29 April 1917 and is the fifth in a series of churches built in the last 300 years.

Major_Events.Description: The church of Sandavá was consecrated on 29 April 1917.
A memorial was erected outside the church to one of the many ships that were sunk during the Second World War.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Distinctive red-roofed church
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is a significant religious site in the Faroe Islands and represents the continuation of a long tradition of church building in the region.
world knowledge.Details: This Faroe Islands location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Phuket FantaSea
