world knowledge.Historical_Background: Phuket FantaSea is a Thai nighttime cultural theme park created at a cost of over THB 3,500 million (US$ 100 million) and opened to the public on 20 December 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The park was opened to the public on 20 December 1998.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes a Thai culture theatrical show, a theme buffet restaurant, and a shopping street. The 'Palace of the Elephants' theater is a reproduction of a Sukhothai era stone elephant palace. The Golden Kinnaree Buffet Restaurant is designed in an Ayutthaya-era architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Phuket FantaSea showcases Thai culture through theatrical shows, architecture, and dining experiences, making it an important cultural attraction in Thailand.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural theme park and entertainment complex
world knowledge.Details: The park includes a Thai cultural show infused with illusion techniques and special effects, performed inside the 'Palace of the Elephants' theater. The Golden Kinnaree Buffet Restaurant is one of the largest buffet restaurants in the world. The Festival Village features a variety of shops, a game town, an a la carte restaurant, a fast food eatery, and bars.

world knowledge.Name: Addington Palace
world knowledge.Address: Addington, London Borough of Croydon, UK
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Addington Palace is an 18th-century mansion built close to the site of an earlier manor house belonging to the Leigh family. It served as the summer residence of the Archbishops of Canterbury between 1807 and 1897. The estate was later used by the Royal School of Church Music and as a wedding and events venue.

Major_Events.Description: The mansion was purchased for the Archbishops of Canterbury after Croydon Palace became dilapidated and inconvenient.
During the First World War, the mansion was taken over by the Red Cross and used as a fever hospital.
The mansion was leased to the Royal School of Church Music to house choirboys for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.
The house was Grade II* listed for its historical and architectural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Robert Mylne in the Palladian style, the mansion features single-storey wings and was later enlarged and modified by Richard Norman Shaw. The grounds and gardens were landscaped by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Addington Palace is culturally significant as the former summer residence of the Archbishops of Canterbury and for its association with the Royal School of Church Music. It also has historical ties to the Leigh family and the ancient recipe for Malepigernout, a spiced chicken porridge served at coronations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country mansion, it has served as a residence for archbishops, a school, a hospital, and a wedding and events venue.
Notable_Visitors: Members of the Royal School of Church Music
world knowledge.Details: The palace is surrounded by a park and golf courses, with much of the grounds leased by golf clubs. A large cedar of Lebanon, one of the Great Trees of London, stands next to the palace. The building was used as a wedding venue until the operating company went into liquidation in 2021.

world knowledge.Name: Fig Tree Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Burns Bay Road, Hunters Hill and Linley Point, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fig Tree Bridge replaced the original iron truss swing bridge opened in 1885, which was part of the first project to provide a fixed crossing of Sydney Harbour. The current bridge was built in conjunction with the Tarban Creek and Gladesville bridges as part of the planned North Western Expressway, which was later cancelled.

Major_Events.Description: The original iron truss swing bridge was opened, forming part of the first project to provide a fixed crossing of Sydney Harbour.
The current concrete girder bridge was opened, replacing the original bridge.
The bridge became part of the Seven Bridges Walk, a fundraising event run by the Cancer Council of NSW.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current bridge is a concrete girder bridge with a grade-separated footpath and cycleway. The piers and deck were designed to allow an additional two lanes to be provided, evident in the eccentric camber of the deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge serves as a vital crossing upriver from the Sydney Harbour Bridge and is part of the Seven Bridges Walk. The remnants of the original bridge, including its southern abutment and the wheel that operated the opening span, hold historical significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries Burns Bay Road motor vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles across the Lane Cove River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge does not carry a toll. The original bridge's southern abutment still exists and features a viewing platform accessible from Joubert Street, Hunters Hill. The wheel that once operated the opening span stands as a memorial.

world knowledge.Name: Brownsea Castle
world knowledge.Address: Brownsea Island, Poole Harbour, Dorset, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brownsea Castle, originally a Device Fort built by Henry VIII to protect Poole Harbour from French attacks, was later converted into a private residence. It played a role in the English Civil War, was restored multiple times, and eventually became a corporate hotel for the John Lewis Partnership.

Major_Events.Description: Built as a Device Fort by Henry VIII to defend Poole Harbour.
Occupied by Parliament forces and refortified.
The castle was gutted by a fire and later restored.
Acquired by the National Trust and leased to the John Lewis Partnership for restoration and use as a corporate hotel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a one-storey square blockhouse with a hexagonal gun platform, later expanded into a Palladian-styled country house with Jacobethan-styled extensions. Features include wood panelling, ornamental ceilings, and Venetian carved stone fireplaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brownsea Castle is a historical fortification that reflects England's coastal defense strategies during the Tudor period. Its later transformations showcase architectural trends from the 18th to 20th centuries.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a defensive fort, later a private residence, and currently a corporate hotel.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is a Grade II listed building and is not open to the public. It houses four cannons likely from the 17th or early 18th century and was part of the island's transformation under various owners, including landscaping and ornamental gardens.

world knowledge.Name: Lahemaa National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lahemaa National Park is the first area to be designated a national park of the former Soviet Union. It was established on 1 July 1971. The park is the largest in Estonia and one of Europe's biggest national parks. Its charter calls for the preservation, research and promotion of North-Estonian landscapes, ecosystems, biodiversity and national heritage. The name Lahemaa originates from the most thoroughly studied and visited part of the North Estonian coast, where four large peninsulas are separated from each other by four bays. Lahemaa translates roughly as 'Land of Bays'.

Major_Events.Description: Lahemaa National Park was established on 1 July 1971, becoming the first national park in the former Soviet Union.
During the height of the Cold War, the Soviet Union operated a large secret submarine base at Hara, which is now in ruins and located entirely within Lahemaa National Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse landscape including forests, raised bogs, coastal rocks, and boulders. It also contains four historic manors: Palmse manor, Vihula manor, Kolga manor, and Sagadi Manor, which is the most visited manor in Estonia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lahemaa National Park is culturally significant for its preservation of North-Estonian landscapes, ecosystems, biodiversity, and national heritage. It is one of the main tourist attractions in Estonia and plays a crucial role in the conservation of the region's natural and historical features.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Preservation, research, and promotion of North-Estonian landscapes, ecosystems, biodiversity, and national heritage.
world knowledge.Details: Lahemaa National Park is located 70 kilometers east of Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. It is bordered by the Gulf of Finland to the north and the Tallinn-Narva highway (E20) to the south. The park covers 747 km², including 274.9 km² of sea. It is rich in flora and fauna, with forests covering more than 70 percent of the area. The park is home to various wildlife, including boar, red deer, wolves, bear, and lynx. The coast is used by cranes as a stopover on their migration route. The park also features the ruins of a former Soviet submarine base near the Lahemaa lighthouse.

world knowledge.Name: Besseggen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Besseggen is a mountain ridge in Vågå Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. It is located in the Jotunheimen mountains within Jotunheimen National Park. The ridge runs between the lakes Gjende and Bessvatnet. It is known from act 1, scene 1 of Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt and is also described in the poem «Besseggen» by Ragnvald Skrede.

Major_Events.Description: A race across Besseggen organized by Norges Orienteringsforbund in cooperation with Den Norske Turistforening. The record time from 1963 is held by Reidar Andreassen with a time of 1 hour 16 minutes and 48 seconds. The women's record, set in 1963, is held by Valborg Østberg with a time of 1 hour 39 minutes and 47 seconds.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Besseggen is one of the most popular mountain hikes in Norway, with about 30,000 people walking the trip each year. It is also culturally significant due to its mention in Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt and the poem «Besseggen» by Ragnvald Skrede.
world knowledge.Details: The walk over Besseggen starts at Gjendesheim, up to the trail's highest point, Veslfjellet, down Besseggen, further over the relatively flat area Bandet, and ends at Memurubu. The trip is estimated to take about 5–7 hours to walk without rest stops. The large number of hikers has led to serious erosion on the trails, leading to a restoration project in 2005 involving placing stone plates on the trail to limit additional damage and prevent further erosion.

world knowledge.Name: Knight Center Complex
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The James L. Knight Center is a contemporary entertainment and convention complex located in Downtown Miami, Florida. It opened in 1982 and was named after newspaper publisher James L. Knight. Originally built as an exhibition hall to attract business conferences, trade shows, and conventions, it has since hosted numerous significant events, including Miss Universe, Miss USA, and the OTI Festival. The center has undergone several renovations and expansions to meet growing demands.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the Miss Universe pageant.
Hosted the Miss USA pageant.
Hosted the Miss Teen USA pageant.
Hosted the OTI Festival.
Hosted the draw for the 2024 Copa America Group Stage.
Hosted a special episode of AEW Dynamite.
Taped episodes of the game show Wheel of Fortune.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Contemporary entertainment and convention complex with multiple seating configurations, including theater-style seating for 4,605, classroom-style seating for 117, and an exhibit hall floor of 28,000 sqft.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The James L. Knight Center is a key venue in Miami for business, entertainment, and political events. It has hosted internationally acclaimed artists, significant pageants, and major sports events, contributing to Miami's cultural and economic landscape.
world knowledge.Details: The complex is located along the Miami River near Bayfront Park and is serviced by the Knight Center station for the Metromover. It has achieved significant milestones, including ranking number 19 worldwide among theaters with a capacity of 5,000 seats or less in 2024. The center continues to host a variety of sold-out events, attracting Miami’s diverse community.

world knowledge.Name: Christmas Island International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The airport was constructed in 1974, replacing the occasional Royal Air Force Short Sunderland flying boat services. The first commercial jet service from Perth, a TAA Boeing 727, arrived on 6 June 1974. The airport has since been a crucial link for the island, including during the Tampa affair in 2001 and plans for a satellite launch facility in the early 2000s.

Major_Events.Description: The first commercial jet service from Perth, a TAA Boeing 727, arrived on 6 June 1974.

During the Tampa affair, the airport experienced near-continuous traffic due to heightened Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) activity and Department of Immigration and Citizenship (DIAC) and media charters.
The Asia Pacific Space Centre planned to start satellite launches in 2004, requiring major airport extensions, including a 600 m runway extension.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 18/36 with an asphalt surface measuring 2,103 m × 45 m and a 2.3% mid-runway gradient.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a vital link for Christmas Island, connecting it to Australia and other regions. It has played a role in significant events like the Tampa affair and was part of plans for a satellite launch facility.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is classified as a Category 2 international airport for all arrivals, including those from Australia. It has a duty-free shop and licensed kiosk, and complimentary public Wi-Fi was introduced in 2018. The airport serves regular flights to the Australian mainland and receives weekly open charter flights from Jakarta and Kuala Lumpur.

world knowledge.Name: Coughton Court
world knowledge.Address: Main road between Studley and Alcester, Warwickshire
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Coughton Court is an English Tudor country house, a Grade I listed building, owned by the Throckmorton family since 1409. It was rebuilt by Sir George Throckmorton, a favorite of King Henry VIII. The house has been in the ownership of the National Trust since 1946, with the family holding a 300-year lease. The house has a long crenellated façade with a Tudor Gatehouse dating from after 1536, flanked by later wings in the Strawberry Hill Gothic style. The estate has significant historical connections, including the Throckmorton Plot of 1583 and the Gunpowder Plot of 1605.

Major_Events.Description: A plot to murder Queen Elizabeth I, with Coughton Court playing a role.
Some of the Gunpowder conspirators rode directly to Coughton Court after the plot's discovery.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house features a long crenellated façade with a Tudor Gatehouse built in the English Renaissance style, flanked by later wings in the Strawberry Hill Gothic style. The gatehouse has hexagonal turrets and oriel windows. The house was built around a courtyard, with the gatehouse used for deliveries and coaches. The gatehouse contains two secret rooms, one above the other, rediscovered in 1858.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Coughton Court is culturally significant due to its long history with the Throckmorton family, its architectural style, and its involvement in significant historical events such as the Throckmorton Plot and the Gunpowder Plot. It also served as a hiding place for priests during the persecution of Catholics in England.
world knowledge.Details: The house is open to the public but not all year round. It is set in extensive grounds including a walled formal garden, a river, and a lake. As of 2024, the house is undergoing extensive repairs to the roof and fabric of the building costing £3.3m, with the work set to be completed by June 2025. The house was used as a filming location for the BBC One series Father Brown in the episode The Mask of the Demon.

world knowledge.Name: Safa Park
world knowledge.Address: Bordered by Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Wasl Road, Al Hadiqa Street, and 55th Street, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Safa Park was created in 1975 on the outskirts of Dubai, an area previously inhabited by illegal immigrants from South Asia. These immigrants were later given amnesty and expelled for the park's creation. The park has undergone several redevelopments, including in 1984 and between 1989 and 1992, adding facilities and utilities. In 2014, part of the park was demolished for the Dubai Canal project.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by Dubai Crown Prince Shaikh Hamdan bin Mohammad bin Rashid Al Maktoum, this month-long fitness challenge involved preparations and renovations at the park.

Major_Events.Event: Partial Demolition for Dubai Canal Project
Major_Events.Description: The northeastern half of the park was fenced off and demolished to make space for the Dubai Water Canal project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features three lakes, over 200 species of birds, and 16,924 different trees and bushes. It includes grass covering around 80% of the area, a small forest, a hill with a waterfall flowing into a lake, and four entrances from nearby roads.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Safa Park is a significant urban green space in Dubai, offering recreational and environmental benefits to residents and visitors. It reflects Dubai's rapid urbanization and the government's efforts to provide public amenities.
Notable_Visitors: Shaikh Hamdan bin Mohammad bin Rashid Al Maktoum
world knowledge.Details: The park hosts a Flea Market every first Saturday of the month and offers sports activities like long tennis, cycling, football, and volleyball. It is located near major landmarks such as the Burj Khalifa, Emirates Towers, and Dubai World Trade Centre.

world knowledge.Name: Gladstone Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gladstone started as a cinderblock garage and was converted into a 230-seat theatre in 1982 by the Great Canadian Theatre Company (GCTC). In 2008, GCTC moved out, and the building was purchased and renovated by Steve Martin and Marilisa Granzotto. It became a hub for independent theatre companies, with Plosive Productions and SevenThirty Productions taking over operations in 2011. The theatre was incorporated as a not-for-profit in 2016 and has since housed multiple resident theatre companies.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was renovated at a cost of CA$500,000 and re-opened with Art Deco style decoration.
The Gladstone Theatre Inc. was incorporated, naming five Resident Companies committed to producing shows annually.
Don Fex, the former theatre manager, was removed for sexual harassment of a minor, leading to community backlash and an open letter with over 700 signatures calling for his dismissal.
The theatre faced criticism for a marquee sign reading '2021 - More Theatre, Less Drama please,' perceived as making light of the prior harassment situation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a cinderblock garage, the theatre was renovated in 2008 with Art Deco style decoration.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gladstone is known as 'Ottawa's Home of Independent Theatre,' hosting productions by local indie theatre companies and fostering diverse theatrical performances.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre seats approximately 230 persons and has housed productions by resident companies such as Plosive Productions, Bear & Co., Black Sheep Theatre, and others. It continues to be a key venue for independent theatre in Ottawa.

world knowledge.Name: Nebuta Museum Wa Rasse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum was conceived as part of the 'Basic Plan for the Rejuvenation of the Aomori Station area' in 2004 to maintain tourism and business in central Aomori after the opening of the Tōhoku Shinkansen and Shin-Aomori Station. It was designed to focus on the Aomori Nebuta Matsuri summer festival, which is a significant cultural event in the region.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Nebuta Museum Wa Rasse
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened to the public on 5 January 2011, showcasing Nebuta floats from the Aomori Nebuta Matsuri festival.
A privately owned Aomori Nebuta museum called Nebuta no Sato closed due to competition from Nebuta Museum Wa Rasse's more central location.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building's exterior features red, ribbon-like, vertical steel beams designed to evoke the visual sensation of light passing through Aomori's old-growth beech forests, as found in Shirakami-Sanchi, while controlling natural lighting inside the museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and promotes the Aomori Nebuta Matsuri festival, which was designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 1980 and one of the 100 Soundscapes of Japan by the Ministry of the Environment in 1996. It serves as a cultural hub for visitors to experience the festival's traditions and artistry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To display and educate visitors about the Aomori Nebuta Matsuri festival, including its history, floats, and interactive experiences.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features two floors of displays, including photographs, videos, and interactive activities related to the festival. It also offers a 30-minute 'Haneto' experience three times daily, allowing guests to emulate aspects of the festival. The main exhibition area showcases four Nebuta floats from the most recent festival, which are rotated annually.

world knowledge.Name: Wallace's Monument, Ayrshire
world knowledge.Address: Barnweil Hill, Craigie, South Ayrshire, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wallace's Monument, also known as the Wallace Tower or Barnweil Monument, was built to commemorate William Wallace during a period of Scottish desire for self-determination. It predates the 1869 Wallace Monument at Stirling. The name 'Barnweil' is derived from the medieval parish church of Barnweil, suppressed in the 17th century. The monument was designed by William Dobie and built by Robert Snodgrass, with land donated by Brigadier-General James George Smith-Neil.

Major_Events.Description: The monument was built to honor William Wallace, designed by William Dobie and constructed by Robert Snodgrass.
The lodge where the tower's warden lived was demolished, and its contents were moved to Ayr Town Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monument is a square-plan Gothic tower made of polished sandstone ashlar blocks. It is 60 ft (18 m) high and 12 ft (3.7 m) wide at the base. Features include a pinnacled parapet, spiral staircase, and bronze panels with inscriptions about William Wallace. The Wallace family coat of arms and motto 'Pro Libertate Patriae' are carved above the entrance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monument commemorates William Wallace, a national hero of Scotland, and symbolizes the struggle for Scottish independence. It is a Category A listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The tower was not provided with an endowment and became the responsibility of the Ayr Town Council and later South Ayrshire Council. It was initially staffed by a guide, but now it is closed to the public. The flag on the tower was traditionally flown at half-mast on significant dates related to William Wallace and General Neil of Barnweil.

world knowledge.Name: Byron Bay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Byron Bay, originally known as Cavvanbah (meaning 'meeting place'), is located on the traditional lands of the Bundjalung Nation. It was named by Lieutenant James Cook in 1770 after Vice Admiral John Byron. The area saw European settlement in the 1830s and was a hub for industries like cedar logging, gold mining, dairy, and whaling. The town became a popular tourist destination in the 1960s and 1970s, known for its surf culture and alternative lifestyle.

Major_Events.Description: Lieutenant James Cook named Cape Byron after Vice Admiral John Byron.
European settlers began arriving in the area.
A massacre occurred south of Suffolk Park.
The lighthouse was built at the easternmost point of mainland Australia.
Held in nearby Nimbin, this festival cemented Byron Bay's reputation as a hippy and alternative town.
A category 2 cyclone brought high winds and heavy rainfall to the area.
Arakwal Elders made a native title claim, leading to an Indigenous Land Use Agreement in 2001.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Byron Bay is culturally significant as a meeting place for Indigenous peoples, a historical industrial hub, and a modern center for alternative lifestyles, surfing, and tourism. It is also the easternmost point of mainland Australia.

Details.Climate: Humid subtropical climate with warm summers and mild winters

Transport.Air: Ballina Byron Gateway Airport (35 km south)
Transport.Road: Bus services from Sydney and Brisbane

world knowledge.Name: Arena Civica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arena Civica, officially Arena Gianni Brera, is a multi-purpose stadium in Milan, Italy, opened on 18 August 1807. It is one of the city's main examples of neoclassical architecture. Initially used for various events, including naval battles and performances, it later became a significant venue for football, rugby, and cultural events. It was renamed in 2003 to honor sportswriter Gianni Brera.

Major_Events.Event: First official match of Italy national football team
Major_Events.Description: The Italy national football team played their first official match here, defeating France 6–2.
Inter Milan moved to Arena Civica on a permanent basis until 1947.
The stadium was renamed in honor of sportswriter and journalist Gianni Brera.
Inter Women played their first match at the Arena Civica against AC Milan on 23 November 2023.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical architecture designed by Luigi Canonica.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arena Civica is culturally significant as a historic multi-purpose venue hosting sports, concerts, and cultural events. It was the site of Italy's first national football match and has been a key location for major performances and athletic events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium hosting football, rugby, concerts, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium can hold 10,000 to 30,000 spectators. It was the home pitch for Inter Milan from 1930 to 1947 and has been the home of Inter Women since 2023. It also hosts the annual Notturna di Milano athletics meeting and was the home ground of Amatori Rugby Milano until 2011.

world knowledge.Name: Siuna
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Siuna is a county-sized administrative municipality in Nicaragua, known for its gold mining history. The town was the site of La Luz Mining company, active from 1936 to 1968. The mine was shut down in 1968 due to damage to the hydroelectric plant. Currently, Calibre Mining owns the mine, but it is inactive. The population grew rapidly from the mid-1930s due to gold mining along the Ei River drainage basin.

Major_Events.Event: Shutdown of La Luz Mining company
Major_Events.Description: The mine was shut down due to damage to the hydroelectric plant.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Siuna is culturally significant due to its history of gold mining and the migration of various ethnic groups to the area for work. The town has a diverse population with a majority of Mestizo people and small percentages of Mayangna, Miskito, and Creole communities.
world knowledge.Details: Siuna is located approximately 318 kilometres northeast of Managua and 218 kilometres west of Puerto Cabezas. The municipality contains 204 rural communities and 20 neighborhoods. The population is primarily engaged in farming, with beans and corn as the primary crops. There is a growing focus on cacao production. Two universities, URACCAN and Martin Luther University, offer courses in Siuna. The NGO Bridges to Community is active in the area, working on projects related to education, health, and economic development. Siuna Airport is served by Avianca Nicaragua (La Costeña), and the town is accessible by bus from Managua and Waslala.

world knowledge.Name: Nagasaki Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nagasaki Airport was the first airport in the world to be built on the ocean, using an existing small island in Ōmura Bay. It replaced the former Omura Airport, which was transferred to the Japan Self-Defense Force in 2011. The airport's mainland portion originally served as an Imperial Japanese Navy airfield in 1923 and was converted into a civilian airport in 1955. The current island runway and terminal opened in 1975.

Major_Events.Description: The airport opened on May 1, 1975, becoming Japan's first full-scale airport built over water and the first in the world to be built on the ocean.
Nagasaki's first international service commenced in September 1979.
An Air France Concorde landed at Nagasaki Airport for the first time on September 2, 1990, during the Nagasaki Travel Expo, attracting 15,000 to 20,000 onlookers.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer of mainland portion to Japan Self-Defense Forces
Major_Events.Description: The mainland portion of the airport was transferred to the Japan Self-Defense Forces and renamed Omura Air Base.

Major_Events.Event: Resumption of international flights to Shanghai
Major_Events.Description: China Eastern Airlines resumed flights between Nagasaki and Shanghai in October 2023 after a hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport was constructed by flattening parts of Mishima Island's hills and reclaiming land around its shore. It features two runways with asphalt concrete surfaces: one 3,000 meters long and another 1,200 meters long. The airport is connected to the mainland by the 970-meter-long Mishima Ohashi Bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nagasaki Airport is historically significant as the first airport in the world to be built on the ocean and Japan's first full-scale airport over water. It represents innovative engineering and urban planning in response to geographical challenges.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving Nagasaki Prefecture, with domestic and international flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as a hub for Oriental Air Bridge. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, it hosted international flights to Hong Kong and Shanghai. The airport is accessible by bus from various cities in Nagasaki Prefecture and by ferry from Togitsu and Huis Ten Bosch theme park.

world knowledge.Name: University of Mohamed Khider Biskra
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Mohamed Khider Biskra is a non-profit public higher education institution established in 1983. It originated from three national institutes: National Institute of Hydraulics, National Institute of Architecture, and National Institute of Electrotechnics. These institutes became a university center in 1992 and were transformed into the University of Mohamed Khider Biskra in 1998. The university now has six faculties and offers a range of programs leading to bachelor's, master's, and doctorate degrees.

Major_Events.Description: The three national institutes became a university center by decree 295–92.
The university center was transformed into the University of Mohamed Khider Biskra by decree 219–98.
The university expanded to six faculties following executive decree 90-09.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Mohamed Khider Biskra is one of the 106 institutions of higher education in Algeria, playing a significant role in the educational and scientific development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 09 libraries with a capacity for 6,860 seats, containing 532,923 copies of 86,726 books and articles. It has 34 international agreements with universities and research institutions and 38 national agreements. The university's national rank is 05, and its international rank is 3166. It offers courses in various fields including exact, natural, and life sciences, law, economics, political science, human and social sciences, and physical and sports activities.

world knowledge.Name: Enchanted Kingdom
world knowledge.Address: RSBS Boulevard (San Lorenzo Road), Santa Rosa, Laguna, Philippines
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Enchanted Kingdom is a theme park in the Philippines founded by Mario and Cynthia Mamon. Inspired by their visits to local and international theme parks, they opened the park on October 19, 1995. The park faced financial difficulties during its early years, particularly during the 1997 Asian financial crisis, but has since grown to become a major attraction in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The park officially opened to the public on October 19, 1995.
The park faced significant financial difficulties during the 1997 Asian financial crisis.
The park's operations were halted multiple times due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with the last reopening on June 5, 2021.
The park began a 10-year expansion plan which includes redevelopment of the existing theme park and addition of new zones, a regional convention center, a water park, and a lifestyle center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features nine themed zones with various rides, shops, restaurants, and event venues. The design is fantasy-oriented, inspired by different eras and locations such as the Victorian Era, 1930s Coney Island, the Amazon Jungle, and the Space Age.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Enchanted Kingdom is culturally significant as it is the first major theme park in the Philippines and a member of the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAAPA). It promotes Filipino values and culture through its attractions and characters.
world knowledge.Details: The park hosts 31 rides and attractions, including the Space Shuttle roller coaster and the Wheel of Fate Ferris wheel. It also features four event venues and a mascot named Eldar the Wizard. The park does not pay royalties to outside sources for its characters and attractions, instead creating its own intellectual property.

world knowledge.Name: Great Blue Hill Observation Tower
world knowledge.Address: near the summit of Great Blue Hill, Milton, Massachusetts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Blue Hill Observation Tower, known locally as Eliot Tower, is a historic stone tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in the 1930s. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1980. The tower and its attached pavilion underwent restorative work in 2023-2024, including the removal of a 1950s-era utility room and improvements for disability access.

Major_Events.Description: Built by a Civilian Conservation Corps crew stationed in the Blue Hills, known for its rustic architecture.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The tower was added to the National Register of Historic Places on September 25, 1980.
Vandals destroyed the pavilion's original slate roof, which was later replaced with faux-slate material.
Restorative work included the removal of a 1950s-era utility room, creation of an educational space, and limited improvements for disability access.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is a 35-foot-tall (11 m) squat square structure made of rubblestone, topped by a pyramidal roof. It features wide rectangular openings beneath the roof and is joined to a single-story covered picnic pavilion made from the same material. The architectural style is CCC Rustic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower is a good example of the rustic architecture typical of CCC projects and offers panoramic views of Boston, Boston Harbor, and the South Shore. Its historical and architectural significance led to its inclusion on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Details: The tower is located near the summit of Great Blue Hill, adjacent to the Eliot Memorial Bridge. It provides views of about 270°, with only the view toward the actual hill summit obscured by vegetation. The actual summit is occupied by the Great Blue Hill Weather Observatory.

world knowledge.Name: Eling Park
world knowledge.Location: Chongqing Municipality, People's Republic of China
world knowledge.Address: Changjiang Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Eling Park was built in 1909 and was originally the home of Li Yaoting, a rich businessman at the end of the Qing Dynasty (1644–1911). The park was originally called Edingling ('Goose Nape Hill') due to its narrow and steep shape that resembles the nape of a goose. In 1958, a large-scale restoration was carried out on the site of the Li Garden, and the park became 'Eling Park'.

Major_Events.Description: A large-scale restoration was carried out on the site of the Li Garden, and the park was renamed 'Eling Park'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features special plant species and a newly built tower, the Liangjiang Pavilion, which provides a view of the entire city.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Eling Park is one of the key state parks of China and is noted as a national protected area of China. It is also known as 'courteous park' (宜园 Yí Yuán).
world knowledge.Details: Eling Park is also known as 'Goose Range Park' or 'Goose Hill Park'. It is home to special plant species and the Liangjiang Pavilion, which offers panoramic views of Chongqing.

world knowledge.Name: Bengaluru Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bengaluru Palace is a 19th-century royal palace located in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, built in an area that was owned by the Rev. John Garrett, the first principal of the Central High School in Bangalore. The palace was commissioned for the Maharaja of Mysore, Chamarajendra Wadiyar X, and currently belongs to the current head of the Wadiyar dynasty, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar.

Major_Events.Description: Iron Maiden's performance in 2007 was a historic gig named Eddfest in the subcontinent. The concert was part of the band's A Matter of Life and Death Tour. The concert is the largest paid concert ever to take place in India with an estimated 38,000 people in attendance with 4000 people watching from outside the venue without tickets. It marked the first visit of Iron Maiden to the Indian subcontinent, and the first major heavy metal concert to take place in the country.
Jay Sean, Ludacris and Flo Rida performed in Palace Grounds on 22 September 2011 for the opening ceremony of the Champions League T20.

Metallica performed at the palace grounds on 30 October 2011 as part of the Rock N India festival, their first show in India which was attended by 31,000 people. It would also turn out to be the last concert to take place as the state government and police stopped giving permission for any future musical events or concerts at the venue (all concerts banned).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tudor Revival architecture
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is a significant cultural and historical landmark in India, representing the royal heritage of the Wadiyar dynasty. It has hosted numerous international artists and events, making it a cultural hub.
world knowledge.Details: Today a legal battle between government and the Mysore royal family has seen a ban of commercial activities. Nevertheless, a number of private companies controlled by the royal family runs a number of wedding halls on the grounds. For the past 34 years the oldest security agency of Karnataka named Scorpion Security Ltd has their national headquarters inside the palace premises. Fun World is an amusement park situated in the palace grounds. This amusement park is allowed under permission from Smt Pramoda Devi Wadiyar, owner and legal heir to Late Sri Srikantadatta Narasimharaja Wadiyar. It has various joy rides, water park and snow room. The 1974 British film, Ghost Story, was filmed in the palace and grounds. It also featured in Krishna Shah's Shalimar in 1978, an Indo- American film starring Dharmendra, Zeenat Aman, Shammi Kapoor, Rex Harission, John Saxon and Sylvia Miles. Also the film Choron Ki Baaraat is extensively shot in this palace interior as well as surrounding. Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar has an important scene also shot outside the palace.

world knowledge.Name: Brecon Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brecon Cathedral, originally the church of Brecon Priory and then the Parish Church of St John the Evangelist, became Brecon Cathedral following the disestablishment of the Church in Wales in 1920 and the creation of the diocese in 1923. The site is thought to have been an earlier Celtic church. A new church was built in 1093 by Bernard de Neufmarché, a Norman knight who conquered the kingdom of Brycheiniog. The church was rebuilt and extended in the Gothic style in about 1215. It was known as the church of Holy Rood or Holy Cross in the Middle Ages due to a revered golden rood, which was destroyed in the Dissolution of the Monasteries in the 16th century. The church underwent significant restoration in the 19th century and the tower was strengthened in 1914.

Major_Events.Event: Disestablishment of the Church in Wales
Major_Events.Description: The church became Brecon Cathedral following the disestablishment of the Church in Wales.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the Diocese of Swansea and Brecon
Major_Events.Description: The church became the cathedral of the newly created Diocese of Swansea and Brecon.
The golden rood, an object of pilgrimage and veneration, was destroyed.
Major renovation of the church began after it had fallen into poor repair.
The tower of the cathedral was strengthened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features Gothic style architecture with a smoke-blackened roof built between 1237 and 1267. It has a characteristic round churchyard, indicative of its earlier Celtic church origins.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brecon Cathedral is a Grade I listed building and holds significant historical and religious importance as the seat of the Bishop of Swansea and Brecon. Its long history, architectural features, and role in the community make it a notable landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral has ten bells rung in the traditional full-circle manner, with the tenor bell weighing 16 cwt. Some of the buildings in the cathedral close have been converted into a diocesan centre, a heritage centre, an exhibition, a shop, and a restaurant named 'the Hours'. Charles Lumley, awarded the Victoria Cross during the Crimean War, was buried in the cathedral churchyard.

world knowledge.Name: L'Oceanogràfic
world knowledge.Location: Garden of the Turia, southeast of the city center of Valencia, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: L'Oceanogràfic is an oceanarium situated in the Garden of the Turia to the southeast of the city center of Valencia, Spain. It was designed by the architect Félix Candela and the structural engineers Alberto Domingo and Carlos Lázaro. It is integrated inside the cultural complex known as the Ciutat de les Arts i de les Ciències (City of Arts and Sciences). It was opened on 14 February 2003.

Major_Events.Description: L'Oceanogràfic was officially opened to the public on 14 February 2003.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The steel-fiber reinforced concrete thin-shell structure was designed by renowned architect Félix Candela, at age 87 in 1997, and structural engineers Alberto Domingo and Carlos Lázaro. The distinctive hyperbolic parabola (hypars) shape of the roof is reminiscent of the Los Manantiales Restaurant in Mexico City, which Candela designed in 1958.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: L'Oceanogràfic is the largest complex of its type in Europe and represents different marine habitats. It is an important part of the Ciutat de les Arts i de les Ciències, a cultural complex in Valencia.
world knowledge.Details: L'Oceanogràfic is home to 45,000 animals from 500 different species, including sharks, penguins, dolphins, sea lions, walruses (until 2019), beluga whales, birds, reptiles, and invertebrates. The park is divided into ten areas representing the Earth's major ecosystems. The aquariums utilize sea water pumped from the La Malva-Rosa beach. It can be reached via Metro, disembark at Alameda Station or through bus number 15, 25, and 95. It is also served by Metrovalencia Line 10 tram from its Oceanogràfic stop.

world knowledge.Name: Al-Asad Airbase
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Qadisiyah Airbase, it was built by Yugoslav companies under contract to the Iraqi government. It became the second largest US military airbase in Iraq during Operation Iraqi Freedom and has hosted various military units and notable visitors.

Major_Events.Description: The airbase came under an Iranian ballistic missile attack in retaliation for the killing of Quds Force leader Qasem Soleimani in a U.S. drone strike.
The airbase and surrounding region came under repeated attack by Islamic State (ISIL) militants.
President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump visited the airbase and addressed the troops.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The base includes hardened aircraft shelters nicknamed 'Yugos', public facilities like mosques, swimming pools, sports fields, and military facilities such as shelters for personnel and equipment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The base is significant for its role in military operations in Iraq, including Operation Iraqi Freedom and the fight against ISIL. It has also hosted numerous high-profile visitors and events.
world knowledge.Details: The base is self-sufficient with amenities including a reverse osmosis water purification plant, bottling plant, and various recreational facilities. It has been a major hub for military operations and logistics in Iraq.

world knowledge.Name: Torre Cepsa
world knowledge.Address: Pº de la Castellana 259, CTBA, Madrid, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Torre Cepsa, originally known as Torre Repsol, was designed by Lord Foster and intended to serve as the headquarters for Repsol YPF oil and gas company. During construction, Repsol relocated its headquarters, and the financial institution Caja Madrid purchased the building for €815 million in August 2007. In 2016, it was bought by Amancio Ortega, Europe's richest man and founder of Inditex, for €490 million. The tower is the second tallest in Spain and the 5th tallest in the European Union.

Major_Events.Description: Caja Madrid purchased the building for €815 million.
Amancio Ortega bought the tower for €490 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Norman Foster, the tower has a height of 248.3 m (815 ft) and 45 floors. It features a modern architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Torre Cepsa is a significant landmark in Madrid, representing modern architectural achievement and economic development. It is the second tallest building in Spain and the 5th tallest in the European Union.
world knowledge.Details: The tower was built by a joint venture of Dragados and Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas. It is managed by Gerens Hill and owned by Amancio Ortega. The current name refers to the former name of the energy company Moeve, previously known as Cepsa, which is headquartered in the tower.

world knowledge.Name: Treskow Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Treskow Bridge was first completed in 1904, named after Sigismund von Treskow. It was damaged during World War II and reconstructed in 1954. The bridge has undergone several renovations, including in 1981 and between 1999-2001.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was first completed based on plans by architect Karl Bernhard, featuring a steel arch and monumental elements like a lighthouse and grand stairways.
The bridge was widened to accommodate increased vehicle traffic, resulting in the loss of some original architectural elements.

Wehrmacht troops destroyed the bridge to hinder the Red Army's advance, though it did not prevent the Soviet forces from capturing Berlin. A temporary wooden pedestrian bridge was erected the same year.
The bridge was rebuilt using remnants of the original structure and reopened to traffic.
The bridge underwent thorough renovations during these periods to maintain its structural integrity and functionality.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed with a steel arch, monumental features like a lighthouse and grand stairways. The 1934 widening simplified some of the original design elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named after Sigismund von Treskow, an aristocrat and politician, and has been a vital river crossing in eastern Berlin since its inauguration, serving tram lines and connecting key districts.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is used by seven Berlin tram lines (21, 27, 37, 60, 61, 67, M17) and remains an important infrastructure for the city's public transport network.

world knowledge.Name: Edenhall
world knowledge.Address: Langwathby, Westmorland and Furness, Cumbria, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Edenhall is a clustered village and former civil parish, now in the parish of Langwathby. It originated from Eden Hall house, the seat of the Musgrave family of Hartley Castle. The hall was extended in the 1700s from materials salvaged from Hartley Castle, rebuilt in 1821 by Sir Robert Smirke, and again in the late 1860s in white stone in an Italianate style. The hall was demolished in 1934, leaving its 19th-century courtyard of stables and coach houses.

Major_Events.Description: The civil parish of Edenhall was merged into Langwathby.
The hall was demolished, leaving its 19th-century courtyard of stables and coach houses.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally extended in the 1700s, rebuilt in 1821 by Sir Robert Smirke, and again in the late 1860s in white stone in an Italianate style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Edenhall was home to the Luck of Edenhall, a 14th-century enamel and gilt glass beaker, now in the Victoria and Albert Museum. The hall and its history are tied to the Musgrave family, prominent members of the House of Commons.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential (originally the seat of the Musgrave family)
world knowledge.Details: Edenhall has a church called St Cuthbert's Church. The Luck of Edenhall, once owned by the Musgrave family, is a notable artifact now housed in the Victoria and Albert Museum. The hall's 19th-century courtyard has been divided into seven properties retaining some stables.

world knowledge.Name: Woodlea
world knowledge.Address: 777 Albany Post Road (US 9), Scarborough, New York 10510
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sleepy Hollow Country Club was founded in 1911 and is located in a historic Vanderbilt mansion named Woodlea, built in 1892–95. The mansion was originally owned by Colonel Elliott Fitch Shepard and his wife Margaret Louisa Vanderbilt Shepard. The estate became part of the Scarborough Historic District in 1984. The country club was established by a group of prominent businessmen, including Frank Vanderlip and William Rockefeller, who purchased the estate in 1910. Over the years, the club expanded its facilities and hosted numerous notable events.

Major_Events.Description: The country club was officially incorporated with 600 members, and the directors' first meeting took place at Vanderlip's office in New York.
The club constructed its first golf course, designed by Charles B. Macdonald and Seth Raynor.
William Rockefeller purchased 387 acres for the club, bringing its total area to 480 acres.

Major_Events.Event: Hosting U.S. Women's Amateur Golf Championship
Major_Events.Description: The club hosted the prestigious U.S. Women's Amateur Golf Championship.
The club underwent significant renovations, including the expansion of the snack bar building, exterior renovations, and the installation of solar panels.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Woodlea, the clubhouse, is designed in an Italian Renaissance Revival style with Beaux-Arts details. The exterior is made of buff-colored Italian brick with pale limestone trim. The house features pedimented pavilions, Ionic columns, balustrades, and large Palladian windows. The interior includes marble fireplaces, coffered ceilings, wood paneling, and extensive carved wood and plaster details. The stable and other outbuildings were also designed by McKim, Mead & White, using similar materials and styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sleepy Hollow Country Club is culturally significant due to its historical association with the Vanderbilt family and its role as a gathering place for prominent figures in American history. The clubhouse, Woodlea, is one of the largest privately owned houses in the U.S. and is a contributing property to the Scarborough Historic District. The club has hosted numerous high-profile events and has been featured in various films and television shows.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Private country club offering golf, tennis, swimming, horseback riding, and other recreational activities.
world knowledge.Details: The club features a 27-hole golf course, a pool complex, tennis courts, squash courts, a fitness complex, and a 45-horse boarding facility. The clubhouse has three dining rooms and can accommodate 400 guests. The club has 570 members and a staff of 60 year-round employees, increasing to 200 during peak season. The property has been used as a filming location for various TV shows and movies, including 'Pan Am,' 'The Good Wife,' 'Daredevil,' and 'Gotham.'

world knowledge.Name: Rupsha Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1.6 Km in length and 16.48 meters in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge is named after Khan Jahan Ali, a historical figure. It serves as a gateway to Khulna, connecting Southern districts of Bangladesh with the Port of Mongla, the second largest sea port of the country.

Major_Events.Event: Harassment by Purba Banglar Communist Party
Major_Events.Description: Workers at the construction site were harassed by Purba Banglar Communist Party who were trying to extort the firms involved in the construction of the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Bridge structure with a total length of 1.6 km and width of 16.48 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant as it connects the Southern districts of Bangladesh with the Port of Mongla, facilitating trade and transportation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Connects Khulna City Bypass over the Rupsa River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is maintained by Bangladesh Bridge Authority Ltd. It is located 4.80 km away from Khulna Town. The next upstream bridge is Noapara Boirab Bridge, and the next downstream is Rupsha Rail Bridge. A toll is required to use the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Tórshavn Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tórshavn Cathedral, established in 1788, is the second oldest received church of the Faroe Islands. It was built on Tinganes in the old town of Tórshavn. The early history of the church is complicated, with no church in the strict sense in Tórshavn during the Middle Ages, only perhaps a 'prayer house'. It was only in 1609 that a proper church was built on Tinganes. The current church was built in 1788 and consecrated in 1865. It has been the seat of the Bishop of the Faroes since 1990.

Major_Events.Description: The church was built on Tinganes in the old town of Tórshavn.
The church was consecrated on 17 December 1865.
The choir was extended by four metres and a new sacristy was built.
The choir was extended with an office and other secondary rooms.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is painted white and roofed with slate. It has one spire. The nave contains 44 benches, and the gallery contains 14. The altarpiece from 1647 is fitted on the north wall of the nave, with a painting of the Last Supper. The bell, acquired in 1708, originates from the ship Norske Löve and is decorated with palmettes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tórshavn Cathedral is one of the main attractions of Tórshavn and is culturally significant as the second oldest received church of the Faroe Islands. It has been the seat of the Bishop of the Faroes since 1990.
world knowledge.Details: The church belongs to the Evangelical-Lutheran national Church of the Faroe Islands. The painting of the Last Supper was restored in 1961. The bell is 30 cm tall, and the diameter of the outside rim is 41.5 cm.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Egyptian Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) is an archaeological museum in Giza, Egypt, about 2 kilometres from the Giza pyramid complex. It hosts over 100,000 artifacts from ancient Egyptian civilization, including the complete Tutankhamun collection. The museum is part of the 'Giza 2030' master plan and is designed to be the world's largest archaeological museum. The project was initiated with a foundation stone laid by then-Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in 2002, and construction began in 2012. The museum partially opened in February 2023, with the grand opening scheduled for 3 July 2025.

Major_Events.Description: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak laid the foundation stone of the Grand Egyptian Museum.
The 3,200-year-old Statue of Ramesses II was relocated from Ramses Square in Cairo to the GEM site.
Construction of the Grand Egyptian Museum began on 12 March 2012.
The museum opened partially in February 2023, allowing access to the main entrance hall and commercial areas.
The official grand opening of the museum is scheduled for 3 July 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is designed in a Pharaonic (Egyptian) architectural style. The building is shaped like a chamfered triangle in plan, with its north and south walls aligning directly with the Great Pyramid of Khufu and the Pyramid of Menkaure. The façade is made of translucent alabaster stone, and the front includes a large plaza filled with date palms. The design was selected through an international architectural competition won by Heneghan Peng Architects.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Grand Egyptian Museum is culturally significant as it houses over 100,000 artifacts from ancient Egyptian civilization, including the complete Tutankhamun collection. It serves as a major center for preserving and showcasing Egypt's rich heritage and is expected to become a global hub for archaeological research and cultural exchange.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary function of the Grand Egyptian Museum is to serve as an archaeological museum, showcasing artifacts from ancient Egyptian civilization and promoting cultural and educational activities.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes permanent exhibition galleries, temporary exhibitions, a children's museum, virtual and large format screens, a conference center, training center, and workshops. The project cost approximately $1 billion, with funding from Japanese loans, the Egyptian government, and international donations. The museum's logo was designed by Tariq Atrissi and cost 800,000 Egyptian pounds. The museum has hosted cultural events, including a musical concert by Egypt's soprano Fatma Said in January 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Great Mosque of Durrës
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Mosque of Durrës, also known as the Grand Mosque or New Mosque, was built in 1931 under the Kingdomship of King Ahmed Zogu on the site of an older mosque from Ottoman times. It was the largest mosque in Albania at the time of its opening. The mosque was designed by Italian architects as part of an Italian-Albanian cooperation, blending Islamic tradition with Durrës-style columns. It was closed in 1967 under the dictatorship of Enver Hoxha, and its minaret was torn down. The mosque was used as a Youth Centre until it was damaged by an earthquake in 1979. It was reopened in 1993 with the help of the International Islamic Relief Organization of the Muslim World League.

Major_Events.Description: The mosque was opened with a celebration that included many foreign delegations.
The mosque was closed under the dictatorship of Enver Hoxha, and its minaret was torn down.
The mosque was damaged by an earthquake.
The mosque was reopened with the help of the International Islamic Relief Organization of the Muslim World League.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque blends Islamic architectural traditions with Durrës-style columns, designed by Italian architects as part of an Italian-Albanian cooperation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Great Mosque of Durrës is culturally significant as it represents a blend of Islamic and local architectural styles and has survived periods of political and natural adversity. It is a symbol of the religious and cultural history of Albania.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque is also called the Grand Mosque to distinguish it from the Little Mosque, the Ottoman-era Fatih Mosque.

world knowledge.Name: Chekka
world knowledge.Location: Coastal town in North Lebanon, north of Râs ach-Chaq’a’ and Herri beaches, south of Enfeh and Tripoli
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chekka is believed to originate from the Canaanite word 'Chikitta', mentioned in the Amarna letters in Egypt as a coastal town. Modern history indicates resettlement around 300 years ago, with the fertile valley cultivated to establish a Maronite stronghold on the Lebanese coast. Many families moved from Mount Lebanon to Chekka at that time.

Major_Events.Description: The American University of Beirut's Faculty of Engineering investigated the potential of sustainable exploitation of the Chekka Bay submarine springs.
The Chekka soccer club won the north district soccer championship.
Speed Ball volleyball club was the champion of the Lebanese volleyball three years in a row and represented Lebanese volleyball in Tunisia in 2019.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chekka is a Maronite Christian stronghold with a rich cultural and religious heritage, home to many Maronite Christian, Greek Orthodox, and Greek Catholic churches. It also has a significant diaspora in Australia, Canada, France, the Persian Gulf, and the USA.
world knowledge.Details: Chekka is rich in freshwater submarine springs and home to some of the largest cement and paper factories in the eastern Mediterranean. The ancient process of extracting salt from the sea is still practiced here. The town has a Christian majority (91.44% of all registered voters), mostly Maronite Catholics (57.91%) and Greek Orthodox (28.28%), with a small Sunni Muslim minority (7.04%). The current Maronite archbishop of Tripoli, Joseph Soueif, was born in Chekka.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Jaffa Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cape Jaffa Lighthouse was originally built on Margaret Brock Reef near Cape Jaffa to aid navigation following the shipwreck of the SS Admella. Designed by George Wells and constructed from components made by Chance Brothers in England, it was operational from 1872 until 1973. The lighthouse was decommissioned after a new lighthouse at Robe began operation. The tower was relocated to Kingston SE in 1976 and now serves as a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was opened on 6 January 1872 after three years of construction.
The lighthouse was deactivated after 101 years of service when a new lighthouse at Robe became operational.
The lighthouse tower was moved to Kingston SE and repurposed as a museum.
The lighthouse was listed on the Register of the National Estate on 21 March 1978.
The lighthouse was added to the South Australian Heritage Register on 24 July 1980.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a Wells screw pile design, screwed into the ocean/reef rocks. It originally had eight rooms to accommodate two lighthouse keepers and their families. The structure used a Chance Brothers lantern visible up to 40 km (25 mi).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is significant for its role in maritime navigation and its unique screw pile design. It is now a museum preserving the history of lighthouse keepers and their families, as well as the tragic story of the Margaret Brock shipwreck.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a navigational aid; now a museum.
world knowledge.Details: The original platform on Margaret Brock Reef still stands as of 2022 and hosts a breeding colony of Australasian gannets. The museum features an interactive display about the Margaret Brock shipwreck and a log cabin quilt registered on the National Quilt Register. The lighthouse is open during South Australian school holidays.

world knowledge.Name: Mactan-Mandaue Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Barangay Pajo of Lapu-Lapu City and Mandaue City
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 854 m (2,802 ft), Width: 9 m (30 ft), Longest span: 145 m (476 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mactan–Mandaue Bridge, officially known as Serging Veloso Osmeña Jr. Bridge, is a truss bridge connecting Mandaue and Lapu-Lapu City in Metro Cebu. Construction began in 1970 and was inaugurated on July 4, 1973. It is popularly claimed to be designed and created solely by Filipino engineers. In April 2013, the bridge was renamed to honor former senator and Cebu Governor Sergio Osmeña Jr.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began a year after Mandaue was ordained as a chartered city.
The bridge was inaugurated on July 4, 1973.
The bridge was renamed to "Sergio Osmeña Jr. Bridge" in honor of the former senator and Cebu Governor Sergio Osmeña Jr.
The bill naming the bridge as the Serging Veloso Osmeña Bridge lapsed into law as Republic Act No. 11828 on June 2, 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Truss bridge design with a total length of 854 m (2,802 ft), width of 9 m (30 ft), and longest span of 145 m (476 ft). Designed by Ronald C. Cosep and Associates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant infrastructure project in the Philippines, connecting the islands of Cebu and Mactan. It is popularly claimed to be designed and created solely by Filipino engineers, symbolizing national engineering prowess.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Connects the cities of Mandaue and Lapu-Lapu City, facilitating transportation and commerce between the islands of Cebu and Mactan.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has only one pedestrian walkway, on the south side of the bridge. It is accessed via A. C. Cortes Avenue from Mandaue and Basak–Marigondon Road from Lapu-Lapu City. It sits astride the northern end of the Mactan Channel, a gateway to the Cebu International Port.

world knowledge.Name: José Amalfitani Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Avenida Juan B. Justo, 8900, Buenos Aires, Argentina
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was originally built as a temporary wooden structure between 1941 and 1943. The current cement facility was constructed between 1947 and 1951. It was renovated and enlarged in 1978 for the FIFA World Cup. Named after José Amalfitani, who was president of Vélez Sarsfield for 30 years, the stadium has served as the home for Vélez Sarsfield football club and the Argentina national rugby union team (Los Pumas).

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted three group stage matches after being refurbished with press boxes and additional upper stands.
Vélez Sarsfield defeated Platense 4–2 in the first match played under artificial lighting at the stadium.
The current cement stadium was officially opened on April 22, 1951.
English rock band Queen performed three concerts as part of The Game Tour, marking the first international concert at the stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium is built with cement and features grass surface. It includes modern lighting systems, press boxes, and upper stands. The field size is 105 x 70 meters with a capacity of 49,540 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Vélez Sarsfield football club and the Argentina national rugby union team. It has hosted major football and rugby events, international concerts, and is a landmark in Buenos Aires sports history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football and rugby stadium, also used for concerts and other major events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was the first in South America with a lighting system, inaugurated in 1969. It has hosted high-profile rugby matches, including games against the New Zealand All Blacks and South Africa. The Jaguares, an Argentine Super Rugby franchise, also played their home games here from 2016 to 2020.

world knowledge.Name: Khonghampat Orchidarium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Khonghampat Orchidarium was founded by the Manipur Forest Department in 1976. It is dedicated to the collection, cultivation, preservation, and display of a wide range of 500 varieties of orchids found in Manipur, including some of the rarest orchids in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Khonghampat Orchidarium is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases a wide variety of orchids native to Manipur, including rare species. It serves as an important center for botanical research and conservation.
world knowledge.Details: The peak blooming season of the orchid flowers is from April to July, with the finest visiting season being March to April. The orchidarium houses 500 orchid species, including many from genera such as Dendrobium, Vanda, and Rhynchostylis.

world knowledge.Name: Skerryvore Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Skerryvore, off the west coast of Scotland, 11 nautical miles southwest of Tiree
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Skerryvore is a remote island off the west coast of Scotland, known for its lighthouse, which is the tallest in Scotland. The lighthouse was built by Alan Stevenson between 1838 and 1844. The rocks have been a hazard to shipping for centuries, with over thirty ships wrecked in the area between 1790 and 1844. The lighthouse was automated in 1994 and is now monitored remotely.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was built with great difficulty due to the remote and hazardous location. The initial barrack was destroyed in a gale in 1838, but a stronger replacement was built. The lighthouse was completed in 1844 and shone without interruption until a fire in 1954.
A disastrous fire started on the seventh floor, causing significant damage. The keepers were rescued the next day, and the lighthouse was out of operation for five years during reconstruction.
The lighthouse was fully automated and is now monitored via a radio link to Ardnamurchan lighthouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is 156 feet (48 m) high with a base of 42 feet (13 m), narrowing to 16 feet (4.9 m) at the lantern gallery. The walls at the base are 9.5 feet (2.9 m) thick, and 2 feet (0.61 m) thick at the top. The structure weighs 4,308 long tons (4,377 tonnes) and is made of granite blocks quarried from Mull. The lightroom and lantern sit above nine apartments 12 feet (3.7 m) in diameter.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Skerryvore Lighthouse is considered one of the most graceful lighthouses in the world and is a significant engineering achievement. It has saved countless lives by preventing shipwrecks in the hazardous waters around the reef. The lighthouse is also a symbol of the perseverance and skill of its builders.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Lighthouse to aid navigation and prevent shipwrecks
Notable_Visitors: William Chambers, the Lord Provost of Edinburgh
world knowledge.Details: The Hynish tower on Tiree has been converted to house the Skerryvore Lighthouse Museum, run by the Hebridean Trust. It is now possible to visit Skerryvore with Tiree-based Tiree Sea Tours. The lighthouse has a helipad constructed in 1972 for relief trips. The shore station was initially at Hynish on Tiree, then moved to Erraid, and finally to Oban in the 1950s.

image_name: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Sameiro

world knowledge.Name: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Sameiro
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Sameiro is a significant Marian shrine in Portugal, established in the 19th century by Fr Martinho Silva. It was built during a period of revival in Marian devotion following the proclamation of the Immaculate Conception as dogma by Pope Pius IX in 1854. The sanctuary has grown over the decades to include various religious structures and art works.

Major_Events.Event: Canonical coronation of the Marian statue
Major_Events.Description: Pope Pius IX granted the decree of Canonical coronation to the Marian statue.

Major_Events.Event: Solemn crowning of a statue of Mary
Major_Events.Description: To celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception, one of the statues of Mary was solemnly crowned by the Papal Nuncio, Archbishop Giuseppe M'acchi, delegated by Pope Pius X.

Major_Events.Event: Visit of Pope John Paul II
Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II visited the sanctuary.
Pope John Paul II granted the shrine the Golden Rose, recognizing its services to the Catholic Church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is in neoclassical style, featuring a silver tabernacle on the main altar and a statue of Mary sculpted by Eugénio Maccagnani. The sanctuary includes various art works reflecting different aesthetic and religious styles, such as tile panels by Querubim Lapa and a large panel by Oscar Casares.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Sameiro is one of the most frequented places of Marian devotion in Portugal, surpassed in size only by the Sanctuary of Fátima. It holds a special place in Portuguese history and national identity, reflecting the country's deep Marian devotion.
world knowledge.Details: The sanctuary is part of a Marian Shrine Route in Portugal and includes a museum, a children's play area, and a large garden. It is located on Monte Sameiro, offering a renowned view over Braga and the Minho valley.

world knowledge.Name: Auberge de Castille
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Auberge de Castille, historically known as the Auberge de Castille et Portugal, is an auberge in Valletta, Malta. It was built in the Baroque style under the magistracy of Portuguese Grand Master Manuel Pinto da Fonseca in the 1740s, replacing a 1574 building erected to house knights of the Order of Saint John from the langue of Castile, León and Portugal. The original auberge, designed by Girolamo Cassar, was dismantled and completely rebuilt in the Spanish Baroque style between 1741 and 1744 by Andrea Belli. The building has served various roles, including as a headquarters for the French forces, the British Armed Forces, and currently as the Office of the Prime Minister of Malta.

Major_Events.Description: The Order of St. John was expelled from Malta, and the auberge became a headquarters for the French forces.
The British occupied Malta, and the auberge became the headquarters of the British Armed Forces in Malta.
The right side of the building was damaged by aerial bombardment.
The building was restored due to crumbling stonework and blackened façades.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Auberge de Castille is built in the Baroque style, featuring a two-storey building with a rectangular plan and a central courtyard. Its façade is divided into eleven bays defined by pilasters in the central bays or plain panelling in the outer bays. Ornate windows are set within recessed panels. The building has a continuous cornice, and its corners are rusticated. The main entrance is approached by a flight of steps, and the doorway is flanked by columns which support a trophy of arms and a bronze bust of Grand Master Manuel Pinto da Fonseca.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Auberge de Castille is a Grade 1 national monument and is listed on the National Inventory of the Cultural Property of the Maltese Islands. It is considered one of the finest buildings in Malta and is often used as a metonym to refer to the Prime Minister and his office.
world knowledge.Details: The building was included on the Antiquities List of 1925 and is linked to Auberge d'Italie through a World War II-era underground air-raid shelter. It was depicted on two commemorative coins minted in 2008 by the Central Bank of Malta.

world knowledge.Name: Hooiberg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hooiberg is a distinctively shaped, 165 m (541 ft) conical hill located at the heart of the island of Aruba. It has long been a prominent and recognizable landmark. Historically known as Orcuyo, it has had various names such as Cerro de Paja ó Pan de Azucar in Spanish, meaning 'hill of straw' or 'sugarloaf'. The Dutch named it Hooiberg, meaning 'haystack', due to its resemblance to a loose haystack. It is a Cretaceous-era tonalitic batholith and has been used as an orientation point and watchtower by indigenous peoples. In modern times, it has hosted radio and television masts and a navigation light.

Major_Events.Description: On October 13, 1990, extreme weather caused a landslide at Hooiberg, resulting in the death of Mrs. Frank, who was buried under mud and a boulder. The house was demolished, and the plot remains empty.
A concrete staircase with around 900 steps was built to facilitate the maintenance of radio and television masts and a navigation light. It has become a popular attraction.

Major_Events.Event: Adoption as emblem on coat of arms
Major_Events.Description: Hooiberg and Aloe vera were officially adopted as emblems on the coat of arms of Aruba on November 15, 1955.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Hooiberg is a conical hill composed of tonalite with subordinate trondhjemite, diorite, gabbro, norite, and hooibergite. It features a concrete staircase with approximately 587 steps as of 2022.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hooiberg is a prominent natural and cultural landmark in Aruba. It has been used as an orientation point by indigenous peoples and is a symbol of the island's history of food crop cultivation. It is also featured on the coat of arms of Aruba.
world knowledge.Details: Hooiberg is not the tallest geological formation on Aruba; Jamanota, at 188 m (617 ft), holds that title. The hill has been a popular starting point for surveying and has been used for various purposes, including hosting radio and television masts. The concrete staircase built in 1951 is a notable engineering feat and a popular attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Ísafjörður Airport
