Environmental_Issues.Pollution: Ganga river pollution from untreated sewage and industrial effluents

world knowledge.Name: Parlement of Rennes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Parlement of Rennes, also known as the Parlement of Brittany, was a sovereign court of justice under the French Ancien Régime. It was one of the parlements with its seat at Rennes, responsible for processing appeals of sentences issued by lower jurisdictions and possessing limited legislative powers. The nobles of Brittany defended the rights of the province, known as the 'Breton liberties', maintained under the treaty of union with France. The Parlement was abolished in 1789, and the building now houses the Rennes Court of Appeal.

Major_Events.Description: The building was severely damaged by fire on February 5, 1994, linked to violent demonstrations by local fishermen. It was restored and adapted to the requirements of the 21st century, with the Court of Appeal of Rennes resuming its activities there within five years.
The Parlement of Brittany, along with all other parlements, was abolished in 1789. The laws of August 16 and August 24, 1790, introduced the separation of judicial and administrative courts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed by city architect German Gaultier, with facades reviewed by Salomon de Brosse. It was sited in the heart of Rennes, where it has stood since 1655.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Parlement of Brittany played a significant role in defending the rights and privileges of the Breton nobility and the province's institutions. It was a key player in the political and judicial life of Brittany, resisting royal powers and maintaining Breton liberties.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a sovereign court of justice, the building now serves as the Rennes Court of Appeal.
world knowledge.Details: The Parlement processed appeals in civil matters, with judgments taking an average of two to five years. It confirmed 60% of judgments, divided in 30%, and left 10% unfinished. Over half of the procedures concerned succession, property, and obligations. The Parlement also had administrative prerogatives, such as guardianship of parishes and control of policing.

world knowledge.Name: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium
world knowledge.Location: 23 Tamaki Drive, Ōrākei, Auckland 1071, New Zealand
world knowledge.Address: 23 Tamaki Drive, Ōrākei, Auckland 1071, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium, originally named Kelly Tarlton's Underwater World, was opened in 1985 in Auckland, New Zealand. It was conceived by marine archaeologist and diver Kelly Tarlton. The aquarium was built in disused sewage storage tanks and introduced innovative acrylic shaping for curved tunnels and moving walkways for visitors.

Major_Events.Description: The aquarium opened after 10 months of construction, featuring a 110-metre tunnel in disused sewage tanks.
The facility expanded to include a replica of Captain Robert Falcon Scott's Antarctic hut and a colony of Antarctic penguins.
Stingray Bay, featuring a 350,000-litre open topped tank, was opened.
Village Roadshow purchased the facility for NZD $13 million.
Merlin Entertainments acquired the aquarium from Village Roadshow.
A $5.5 million upgrade was completed, introducing new exhibits and rebranding the aquarium as Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The aquarium features curved acrylic tunnels, moving walkways, and a seascape of caves and reefs created with concrete. The tanks were filled with marine creatures, including sharks and stingrays.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The aquarium is significant for its innovative design and contribution to marine education and conservation in New Zealand.
world knowledge.Details: The aquarium's main features include the Antarctic Encounter and the Underwater World, along with several other exhibits and education rooms. It is owned by Merlin Entertainments and is part of the global Sea Life Centres brand.

world knowledge.Name: Crosby Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Crosby Beach is part of the Merseyside coastline north of Liverpool in the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton, England. It has been stabilized since the mid-19th century to prevent high sea tides from reaching the first row of houses. The beach has faced issues with litter and erosion over the years, leading to various conservation efforts. It is also the permanent home of the Another Place sculptures by Antony Gormley since 2007.

Major_Events.Event: Awarded Keep Britain Tidy's Quality Coast Award
Major_Events.Description: The beach was recognized for its quality and cleanliness.
Antony Gormley's sculptures were permanently installed on the beach.
A machine was imported from America to clean the beach by sifting out litter.
Construction of a marina and recreation area began, including a promenade and floodlights.
Asbestos was found spread over a 2-mile stretch of the beach, likely from bombed buildings during The Blitz.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach features the Another Place sculptures by Antony Gormley, which are cast iron figures spread across the sand. The marina includes a promenade and floodlights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Crosby Beach is culturally significant due to its Another Place sculptures, which have become a major attraction. The beach has also been featured in the BBC drama Good Cop and has won awards for its quality and cleanliness.
world knowledge.Details: Crosby Beach has a red flag rating, indicating danger and advising visitors not to enter the water. It has faced issues with quicksand and litter over the years. The beach can be reached by foot from nearby railway stations or by car, with parking available at Crosby Leisure Centre. It received an average rating of 4.5/5 on Trip Advisor in July 2017.

world knowledge.Name: Misaki Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Misaki Park was opened on April 1, 1957, as part of the 70th anniversary celebration of Nankai Railway. It was an amusement park featuring attractions such as a zoo, dolphin show venue, and a large outdoor pool (seasonal). The park was operated by Nankai Electric Railway Co., Ltd. and closed on March 31, 2020.

Major_Events.Description: The park was opened as part of the 70th anniversary of Nankai Railway.
The park ceased operations on March 31, 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park consisted of an amusement park, a zoo, a dolphin show venue, and a large outdoor pool (open only in summer).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Misaki Park was a notable recreational destination in Osaka Prefecture, offering entertainment and leisure activities for families and visitors. It was a symbol of Nankai Railway's legacy and contribution to local tourism.
world knowledge.Details: Misaki Park was located near Misaki-koen Station on the Nankai Main Line, operated by Nankai Electric Railway. The park's website was available in both English and Japanese.

image_name: Holocaust Memorial and Tolerance Center of Nassau County

world knowledge.Name: Holocaust Memorial and Tolerance Center of Nassau County
world knowledge.Address: 100 Crescent Beach Rd, Glen Cove, New York 11542
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Holocaust Memorial and Tolerance Center of Nassau County (HMTC) is housed in the original Gold Coast Mansion "Welwyn", built in 1906. The mansion was part of the estate of Harold Irving Pratt, an American oil industrialist. After being neglected for 30 years, it was repurposed as a Holocaust memorial and tolerance center, opening in 1994. The center was established through the efforts of Nassau County Executive Thomas S. Gulotta and an interfaith commission.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Holocaust Memorial and Educational Center
Major_Events.Description: The center was officially opened as a museum and educational facility dedicated to Holocaust remembrance and tolerance education.
The garden, originally designed by the Olmsted Brothers, was restored and dedicated to the over one million children murdered in the Holocaust.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Louis Posner Memorial Library
Major_Events.Description: The library, Long Island’s most extensive collection of literature on the Holocaust, genocide, and anti-discrimination, was opened at the museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the original Georgian-style mansion "Welwyn", designed by Delano & Aldrich. The adjoining garden was designed by the Olmsted Brothers, an influential American landscape architectural firm.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The center serves as a memorial to the victims of the Holocaust and promotes tolerance and education to combat hatred, prejudice, and intolerance, including antisemitism, racism, and bullying.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Holocaust museum and tolerance education center
world knowledge.Details: The museum is open on Mondays to Fridays from 10:00 am to 4:30 pm, and on Saturdays and Sundays from 12:00 pm to 4:00 pm. The center includes the Louis Posner Memorial Library and a restored butterfly garden dedicated to the children who perished in the Holocaust.

world knowledge.Name: Washington County Courthouse (Iowa)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Washington County Courthouse is the third building used for court functions and county administration. The first courthouse was a frame building built in the 1840s, also used as a schoolhouse and church. The second courthouse was built in 1847, but the county was dissatisfied with the carpentry work. The present courthouse was built in 1887 for $75,000.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Individually listed as part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.

Major_Events.Event: Included in Washington Downtown Historic District
Major_Events.Description: Became a contributing property in the Washington Downtown Historic District.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian Romanesque style, featuring a variety of arch forms and a three-stage clock tower. Constructed of locally made bricks with stone trim. The bell in the clock tower is made of bronze, tin, and brass. Statues representing Justice and Liberty are located on the lower level of the tower. The south and west elevations have projecting pavilions that terminate in gable ends.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its association with county government and the political power and prestige of Washington as the county seat. It is considered an excellent example of Victorian Romanesque courthouses in Iowa.
world knowledge.Details: Designed by the Des Moines architectural firm of Foster & Liebbe, and built by Thomas Colwell and Hugh Colwell. The present main entrance was added at a later date.

world knowledge.Name: Rheinturm
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rheinturm is a 240.5-metre-high concrete telecommunications tower in Düsseldorf, Germany. Construction began in 1979 and was completed in 1981. It was inaugurated on 1 December 1981 and serves as a key telecommunications hub with an observation deck and revolving restaurant.

Major_Events.Description: The Rheinturm was officially inaugurated on 1 December 1981.
On 15 October 2004, an aerial antenna for DVB-T was mounted, increasing the tower's height.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Reinforced concrete structure, 240.5 metres high, with a revolving restaurant and observation deck. Features a light sculpture called Lichtzeitpegel, which functions as the largest digital clock in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rheinturm is the tallest building in Düsseldorf and a prominent symbol of the city. Its light sculpture, Lichtzeitpegel, is a unique attraction and a technological marvel.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Telecommunications tower with a restaurant and observation deck
world knowledge.Details: The observation deck is open to the public daily from 10:00 to 23:30. The light sculpture on the tower's shaft acts as a 24-hour clock, with six sets of lights representing hours, minutes, and seconds.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Gorge Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Near Cañon City, Colorado, within Royal Gorge Bridge and Park
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,260 ft (384 m) length, 18 ft (5.5 m) width, 955 ft (291 m) clearance below
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Gorge Bridge was constructed in 1929 as a tourist attraction, not for transportation purposes. It held the record for the highest bridge in the world from 1929 until 2001. The bridge is part of the Royal Gorge Bridge and Park, a 360-acre amusement park.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed in six months, opening on December 8, 1929.
A narrow gauge incline railway was added to reach the bottom of the gorge.
An aerial tram was opened, crossing the gorge just east of the bridge.

Major_Events.Event: National Register of Historic Places Listing
Major_Events.Description: The bridge and incline railway were listed in the National Register of Historic Places.
A wildfire destroyed most of the park's buildings and the aerial tram, but the bridge sustained minimal damage.
The park was partially reopened after rebuilding from the wildfire damage.
The park had a grand reopening with new attractions after completing $30 million in repairs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge made of steel with a timber deck. The main span is 880 ft (268 m), with towers 150 ft (46 m) high. The bridge has 1,292 wooden planks on its deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Gorge Bridge is a significant tourist attraction and engineering feat. It was the highest bridge in the world from 1929 to 2001 and remains the highest bridge in the United States. It is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is part of the Royal Gorge Bridge and Park, which includes various attractions such as a visitor center, gondolas, a zip-line, and a Skycoaster. The park has undergone significant renovations and rebuilding, especially after the 2013 wildfire. The bridge remains a popular destination, attracting nearly 350,000 visitors in 2015.

world knowledge.Name: Chiba Port Tower
world knowledge.Address: Chiba Port Park, Chūō-ku, Chiba, Chiba Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in commemoration of the population of Chiba Prefecture exceeding five million in 1983, due to rapid growth from the 1970s to 1980s caused by Tokyo's commuter belt expansion and Keiyō Industrial Zone development.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was opened to the public on June 15, 1986.
Chiba Port Tower is a key spot in the course of the International Chiba Ekiden, where runners make a turn in front of the tower.
From mid-November to late December, the tower is decorated with Christmas illuminations in the form of a large Christmas tree made of about 3,000 lights.
A monthly flea market held at the plaza in front of the tower, promoting eco-friendly activities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower has a lozenge-shaped cross-section, covered with mirrored glass that reflects sunlight, making it appear blue in fine weather. It features a dynamic damper system at the top to counteract oscillations during earthquakes and strong winds. The tower has four floors, with elevators connecting them.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower symbolizes the rapid growth and development of Chiba Prefecture. It serves as a key observation point, offering panoramic views of the surrounding area, and is a venue for cultural events like the International Chiba Ekiden and Christmas illuminations.
world knowledge.Details: The tower includes a shop selling Chiba-related goods, an exhibition room about Chiba Port, a theater, a kid's room, a view room with a luminous mural, a view coffee shop, and a main observation floor. Nearby attractions include Chiba Marine Stadium, Makuhari Messe, and Tokyo Disney Resort. The tower can withstand winds up to 60 m/s and earthquakes up to 7 on the Japan Meteorological Agency seismic intensity scale.

world knowledge.Name: Freiburg Minster
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Freiburg Minster, also known as Freiburger Münster or Münster Unserer Lieben Frau, is the cathedral of Freiburg im Breisgau, southwest Germany. Construction began around 1200 in Romanesque style under the last duke of Zähringen, Berthold V, and continued in Gothic style from 1230. It was built on the foundations of an original church from 1120. In 1827, it became the seat of the newly established Catholic Archdiocese of Freiburg. The cathedral's 116-meter tower, completed in 1330, is renowned for its beauty and is the only Gothic church tower in Germany completed in the Middle Ages that has survived to the present.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Catholic Archdiocese of Freiburg
Major_Events.Description: Freiburg Minster became the seat of the newly established Catholic Archdiocese of Freiburg.

Major_Events.Event: Survival of the tower during World War II bombing
Major_Events.Description: The tower survived the bombing raids of November 1944, which destroyed surrounding buildings, due to its lead anchors and the removal of windows by church staff.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The 116-meter tower is nearly square at the base, with a dodecagonal star gallery at its center, and transitions to an octagonal, tapered structure topped by a spire. The nave windows, donated by guilds, feature symbols of the guilds and some contain deep red colors from gold nanoparticles. The inner portal contains sculptures of the Ten Virgins.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Freiburg Minster is culturally significant for its architectural beauty, particularly its 116-meter tower, which is considered one of the most beautiful in the world. It is also historically important as the seat of the Catholic Archdiocese of Freiburg and for its survival through significant historical events, including World War II bombing.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral houses 19 bells, totaling 25 tonnes, making it one of the largest peals in Germany. It contains two important altars: the high altar by Hans Baldung and another by Hans Holbein the Younger. The Lenten cloth, restored in 2003, weighs over a ton and requires heavy machinery for transport. The cathedral is owned by the Münsterbauverein association, which invests millions of euros annually in its maintenance. The current architect in charge is Yvonne Faller, and the chair of the association is Sven von Ungern-Sternberg.

world knowledge.Name: Helong Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium is named after Marshal He Long, who was born in the same province and was a dedicated supporter of the Chinese "Three Major Ball Games" (三大球).

Major_Events.Description: Concert held on 25 December 2017
Concert held on 21 September 2018
Concert held on 15 September 2023
Concert held on 14-16 June 2024

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium is an all-seater with a roof covering all spectators and has a grass surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named after Marshal He Long, a significant historical figure in China, and serves as a major sports venue in Hunan province.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, currently used mostly for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 55,000 people and is operated by IRENA Group.

world knowledge.Name: Whareakeake
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 630 metres (2,070 ft) long, with 13 hectares (32 acres) of flat ground
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Whareakeake was a place of habitation for Māori people from early times until the Sealers' War skirmish of 1817. It was later occupied by European households and renamed 'Murdering Beach' until 1998 when the original name was restored.

Major_Events.Description: Captain James Kelly and his men were attacked by Māori at Whareakeake, resulting in the deaths of three settlers, including William Tucker. Kelly retaliated by killing many Māori and destroying canoes and villages.
The name 'Whareakeake' was officially restored in the Ngāi Tahu Claims Settlement Act, replacing the colonial name 'Murdering Beach'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site includes archaeological remains of a traditional Māori kāinga nohoanga (place of residence) and kāinga mahinga kai (place of food production), with evidence of a fenced fort, cemetery, sacred altar, and canoe anchorage.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Whareakeake is significant for its early Māori habitation, archaeological sites, and role in the Sealers' War. It is also a renowned surfing beach and a place of cultural heritage for Ngāi Tahu.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historically a place of residence and food production for Māori; now a recreational beach for surfing, swimming, and sunbathing.
world knowledge.Details: Whareakeake is known for its right-hand point break, making it a popular surfing spot. It is also used by naturists for nude bathing. The beach is accessible via Whareakeake Road, a steep one-lane gravel drive. Archaeological finds include moa bones, fish-hooks, weapons, amulets, and pounamu artefacts, including a medal from Captain James Cook's second voyage to New Zealand.

world knowledge.Name: Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion
world knowledge.Address: 2005 Lake Robbins Dr The Woodlands, TX 77380-1136
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion was conceived in 1982 as a regional summer home for the Houston Symphony in The Woodlands, Texas. Construction began in June 1989 after initial delays due to economic conditions. The Pavilion opened in April 1990 with concerts by the Houston Symphony, Frank Sinatra, Alabama, and Clint Black. It has undergone several expansions and renovations, including in 1994, 1998, 2000, and 2008-09 after damage from Hurricane Ike.

Major_Events.Description: The Pavilion's opening weekend featured successive concerts by the Houston Symphony, Frank Sinatra, Alabama, and Clint Black.
The Pavilion expanded to add 1,900 new reserved seats, increase lawn capacity by 1,100, and build new concession stands and restrooms.

The Pavilion was severely damaged by Hurricane Ike, leading to the cancellation of all remaining 2008 season concerts. The roof and stage were heavily damaged, and the facility was renovated with a new wind-resistant roof and additional seating.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Pavilion is an amphitheater with 6,500 covered seats and up to 10,000 uncovered lawn capacity. It features multiple plazas with concession stands and restrooms, a VIP suite (The Woodforest Bank Club), and a five-story parking garage connected via a pedestrian walkway. The roof is designed to withstand winds over 175 mph.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pavilion serves as a key cultural venue in Greater Houston, hosting performances by the Houston Symphony, Houston Grand Opera, Houston Ballet, and contemporary artists. It is a non-profit organization aimed at promoting both performing arts and contemporary entertainment.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Concert amphitheater and performing arts venue
world knowledge.Details: The Pavilion is owned and operated by The Center for the Performing Arts at The Woodlands and is a non-profit organization. It has been the second-most heavily used amphitheater in the world. Lawn seating is often provided free of charge during performances due to sponsor grants.

world knowledge.Name: Aberdare National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Aberdare National Park is a protected area in the Aberdare Mountain Range in central Kenya located east of the East African Rift Valley. Established in May 1950, it covers an area of 766 square kilometers and forms part of the Aberdare Mountain Range. The park contains a wide range of landscapes - from mountain peaks that rise to 4,000 metres (13,000 ft) above sea level, to their deep, v-shaped valleys intersected by streams, rivers, and waterfalls. Moorland, bamboo forests and rainforests are found at lower elevations. Aberdare National Park was established in 1950 with an aim to conserve and protect the Aberdare Mountains.

Major_Events.Description: Princess Elizabeth became Queen after the death of her father King George VI, whilst staying at the Treetops Hotel.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aberdare National Park is best known as the site where in 1952, Princess Elizabeth became Queen after the death of her father King George VI, whilst staying at the Treetops Hotel.
world knowledge.Details: Wildlife present in the protected area include lion, leopard, elephant, East African wild dog, giant forest hog, bushbuck, mountain reedbuck, waterbuck, Cape buffalo, suni, side-striped jackal, eland, duiker, olive baboon, black and white colobus monkey, and sykes monkey. Rarer sightings include those of the African golden cat and the bongo. Species such as the common eland, serval live in the higher moorlands. The Aberdare National Park also hosts a large eastern black rhinoceros population and over 250 bird species including the endangered Aberdare cisticola, Jackson's spurfowl, sparrowhawk, African goshawk, African fish eagle, sunbirds and plovers.

world knowledge.Name: Jantar Mantar, Varanasi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jantar Mantar is an observatory built in Varanasi in 1737 by Maharaja Jai Singh II of the kingdom of Amber (later called Jaipur). It is one of the five observatories constructed by Maharaja Jai Singh II, who was an astronomer with a deep interest in science and astronomy. He sent scholars to various countries to study the design, construction, and technology of observatories. The scholars returned with observations and manuals on astronomy, leading to the construction of these observatories between 1724 and 1737 in Jaipur, Mathura, New Delhi, Ujjain, and Varanasi. There is evidence suggesting the observatory might have been built centuries earlier, with references from 1772 indicating its existence for about 200 years.

Major_Events.Description: Maharaja Jai Singh II constructed the observatory to measure local time, altitude, and the declination of the Sun, stars, and planets, as well as to determine eclipses.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The observatory includes several special instruments designed to measure the motion, speed, and properties of stars and planets.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jantar Mantar is significant as a historical astronomical observatory that reflects the scientific advancements and interests of Maharaja Jai Singh II. It also serves as a testament to the rich astronomical heritage of India.
world knowledge.Details: Jantar Mantar was constructed with the aim of measuring local time, altitude, and the declination of the Sun, stars, and planets, as well as to determine eclipses. It also recorded the motion, speed, and properties of stars and planets using specialized instruments.

world knowledge.Name: Jihlava Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jihlava Zoo, originally established as Zookoutek Jihlava in 1957, transformed into a zoo in 1982. It was accepted as a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) in 1994.

Major_Events.Description: The zoo evolved from Zookoutek Jihlava into a full-fledged zoo.
The zoo was accepted as a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jihlava Zoo is significant for its role in the conservation and breeding of endangered species, particularly big carnivores, monkeys, and reptiles.
world knowledge.Details: Jihlava Zoo is located in a valley of the Jihlávka Stream and houses about 260 species of exotic animals, including endangered species. It is a member of EAZA and UCSZOO.

world knowledge.Name: Abbaye aux Dames, Saintes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Abbaye aux Dames was the first Benedictine nunnery in Saintes, founded in 1047 by Geoffrey II, Count of Anjou, and his wife Agnes. Agnes later retired to the nunnery and died there. One of its abbesses was Agnès of Barbezieux (1134–1174), whose relative, Eleanor of Aquitaine, was a generous donor to the abbey.

Major_Events.Description: The abbey was founded by Geoffrey II, Count of Anjou, and his wife Agnes.
The abbey was classified as a monument historique in 1948.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey church, Sainte-Marie-des-Dames, dates from the 12th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Abbaye aux Dames is culturally significant as the first Benedictine nunnery in Saintes and for its historical connections to figures like Eleanor of Aquitaine and Madame de Montespan.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey is located next to the town's Arch of Germanicus. Madame de Montespan was educated here.

world knowledge.Name: Miraflores Palace
world knowledge.Address: Urdaneta Avenue, Libertador Bolivarian Municipality, Caracas, Venezuela
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Miraflores Palace is the official dispatch and head office of the President of Venezuela. Construction began in 1884 as the family residence of Joaquin Crespo. It was acquired by the national administration in 1911 and became the official presidential residence and office. Over the years, it has undergone numerous modifications and expansions.

Major_Events.Description: The national administration acquired the property from General Félix Galavis at a cost of five hundred thousand bolívares, and Miraflores Palace became the official presidential residence and office.

Major_Events.Event: Murder of Vice-president Juan Crisóstomo Gómez
Major_Events.Description: Miraflores witnessed the murder of Vice-president Juan Crisóstomo Gómez, brother of President Juan Vicente Gómez.
The palace was declared a National Historical Monument.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Simón Bolívar Press Room
Major_Events.Description: The Simón Bolívar Press Room opened in February 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with European influences. The palace features fountains, corridors, and halls such as the Peruvian Sun Hall, Joaquín Crespo Hall, Vargas Swamp, Ambassador Hall, and Ayacucho Hall. The palace has undergone various modifications, including the addition of a Japanese garden, an administration building, and the Bicentennial square.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Miraflores Palace is a symbol of Venezuelan political history and has served as the official residence and office of the President of Venezuela. It is a National Historical Monument and houses significant historical documents and artifacts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government Building (Official dispatch and head office of the President of Venezuela)
world knowledge.Details: The Miraflores Historical Archive contains nearly 15 million pages of documents related to Venezuelan presidents. The palace features various rooms used for official events, diplomatic accreditation, and special occasions. Notable rooms include the Ayacucho Hall, Joaquín Crespo Hall, and Vargas Swamp Room. The palace also houses significant artworks and historical furniture.

world knowledge.Name: New Eskişehir Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The New Eskişehir Stadium opened to the public on 20 November 2016, replacing the club's former home, Eskişehir Atatürk Stadium. Despite requests to rename it to New Eskişehir Atatürk Stadium, the name remains unchanged.

Major_Events.Description: The match set the record attendance of 34,930 spectators on 27 March 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by HSY Yapı & Aras İnşaat, the stadium features 54 executive suites and has a capacity of 32,500 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is one of the main home stadiums of the Turkish national football team and serves as the home ground for Eskişehirspor, holding cultural importance for sports enthusiasts in Turkey.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's capacity has varied over the years: 34,930 (2016–2019), 32,507 (2019–2020), and 32,500 (2020–). It broke ground on 23 August 2013 and was built over a three-year period.

world knowledge.Name: Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art
world knowledge.Address: South bank of the River Tyne, Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art, opened in July 2002, is housed in a converted flour mill that operated from 1950 to 1984. The idea for the art centre emerged in the 1990s as part of the regeneration of Gateshead's riverside. The architectural design by Dominic Williams of Ellis Williams Architects retained much of the original structure while adapting it for its new purpose. The centre has hosted numerous exhibitions, events, and educational programs, becoming a significant cultural hub in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art opened to the public at midnight on July 13, 2002, with the inaugural exhibition B.OPEN, featuring works by notable artists such as Chris Burden, Carsten Höller, and Julian Opie.
Baltic hosted the Turner Prize, marking the first time the event was held outside of London or Liverpool Tate. The exhibition attracted 149,770 visitors.

Baltic closed in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and reopened in May 2021 with four exhibitions, including Baltic Open Submission, featuring works created during lockdown by 158 artists from the North East.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building retains the original brick façades and BALTIC FLOUR MILLS lettering. It features a 1,000 tonne steel frame, four main floors, and 13 separate levels designed to create a sense of disorientation. The east and west sides are fully glazed, offering views of the River Tyne. The interior includes glass, concrete, aluminium, Welsh Slate, 'Cor-Ten' steel, and Swedish pine.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Baltic is a key part of the post-industrial regeneration of Gateshead's riverside, transforming the area into a centre of modern architecture and culture. It has become a major hub for contemporary art, attracting millions of visitors and hosting significant events like the Turner Prize.
world knowledge.Details: Baltic has won several awards, including a RIBA award in 2003 and the National Lottery Awards prize for Best Arts Project in 2012. It emphasizes community engagement and local outreach, with initiatives like the Self-Publishing Artists' Market and partnerships with local universities.

world knowledge.Name: Ankara University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ankara University is a public research university in Ankara, the capital city of Turkey. It was the first higher education institution founded in Turkey after the formation of the Turkish republic in 1923. Established by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the first president of Turkey, it is one of the country’s leading educational institutions. The university's history dates back to the founding of the Faculty of Political Science in 1859, which was originally established in Istanbul as an institution to educate the Ottoman Empire's bureaucracy.

Major_Events.Description: Ankara University was initially established as Ankara Hukuk Mektebi on October 5, 1925.
Ankara University was formally established as a university on June 13, 1946.

Major_Events.Event: Award of Japanese Foreign Minister's commendation
Major_Events.Description: The Department of Japanese Language and Literature was awarded the Japanese Foreign Minister's commendation for their contributions to the promotion of Japanese language education in Turkey on December 1, 2020.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ankara University is culturally and historically significant as it was the first higher education institution founded in Turkey after the formation of the Turkish republic in 1923. It was established by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the first president of Turkey, and has played a crucial role in the country's educational and scientific development.
world knowledge.Details: Ankara University has 40 vocational programs, 120 undergraduate programs, and 110 graduate programs. It operates 41 research, application, and education centers, including the Turkish and Foreign Languages Research and Application Center (TÖMER), the Ankara University Kreiken Observatory, and the Ankara University Women Issues Research and Application Center (KASAUM). The university also has a Distance Education Center and various other specialized centers focusing on areas such as superconductivity, earthquake research, and child's culture.

world knowledge.Name: Savannah City Hall
world knowledge.Address: 2 East Bay Street, Savannah, Georgia, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Savannah City Hall is the seat of government for the city of Savannah, Georgia. Designed by architect Hyman Witcover, the building was constructed between 1904 and 1905 and opened in 1906. It replaced the City Exchange, built in 1799 and demolished in 1904. The building is a contributing property to the Savannah Historic District and was the first built solely to serve as the city's seat of government.

Major_Events.Description: Cornerstone laid on August 11, 1904, in a large ceremony.
Construction completed at a cost of $250,000.
Building officially opened on January 2, 1906.
The dome was covered in gold leaf.
Georgia Historical Society erected a historical marker at the city hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Renaissance Revival style with limestone and granite exterior, capped by a copper dome (later gilded with gold leaf in 1987). Initial plans included four statues of chariots on the building's corners, but financial limitations prevented their installation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is a symbol of Savannah's progressive spirit and indomitable energy in the early 20th century. It is a contributing property to the Savannah Historic District and represents the city's governmental history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government Building (seat of government for the city of Savannah)
world knowledge.Details: The building was constructed during the administration of Mayor Herman Myers, who pursued numerous public works projects. It is located across the street from the United States Customhouse and features one elevator.

world knowledge.Name: Bolaven Plateau
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Elevation ranges from 1,000 to 1,350 metres (3,280 to 4,430 ft) above sea level
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bolaven Plateau has had an important role in the greater history of Laos. The three most significant historical periods which have greatly affected the area are the French colonization of the region, the Phu Mi Bun Revolt, and the Vietnam War. Each event has had a significant effect upon the Plateau and given the area its own unique character and importance.

Major_Events.Description: The French first annexed territories east of the Mekong River and later annexed minor extensions of land to the west of the Mekong in 1904 and 1907. The period of French colonization in Laos is most significant because of the agricultural techniques acquired from the French by the inhabitants.
A major rebellion by local Lao Theung tribes (the Alak, Nyaheun and Laven) against French domination.

The Bolaven Plateau was one of the most heavily-bombed theatres of the Second Indochina War, US bombardment became unbearable in the late ’60s. Controlling the Bolaven Plateau was considered strategically vital to both the Americans and North Vietnamese, as evidenced by the staggering amount of UXO (unexploded ordnance) still lying around.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bolaven Plateau is culturally significant due to its historical events, ethnic diversity, and agricultural importance. The region is home to various Mon-Khmer ethnic groups, including the Laven, Alak, Katu, Taoy, and Suay, who follow animist belief systems and have recently adopted Buddhist beliefs. The plateau's agricultural production, particularly coffee, and its tourism industry contribute significantly to the region's economy.
world knowledge.Details: The Bolaven Plateau is known for its scenic waterfalls, ethnic minority villages, and coffee plantations. The region is also believed to be the site of a meteorite impact approximately 790,000 years ago, with its strewn tektites found across Asia, Australia, and Antarctica.

world knowledge.Name: Minami Bisan–Seto Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Seto Bridge was envisioned as early as 1889 by Jinnojo Ōkubo, a member of the Prefectural Parliament, who advocated for better transportation links in Shikoku. The idea gained urgency after a 1955 ferry disaster that killed 171 people, including 100 students. Construction began in 1978 after delays due to the 1973 oil shock and was completed in 1988. The bridge is part of the Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project and is the only route to carry rail traffic.

Major_Events.Description: A collision of two ferries in dense fog off Takamatsu killed 171 people, prompting calls for a safer crossing.
Construction started after the Environment Assessment Report was published, following delays from the 1973 oil shock.
The bridge was officially opened to road and rail traffic by then-Crown Prince Akihito.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Great Seto Bridge is a double-decked bridge system with two lanes of highway traffic on the upper deck and one railway track in each direction on the lower deck. It spans 13.1 kilometers and includes six named bridges and five viaducts. The longest span is the Minami Bisan-Seto Bridge at 1,100 meters. The bridge was constructed using 3.646 million cubic meters of concrete and 705,000 tons of steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes the unification of Honshū and Shikoku, fulfilling a century-old vision for improved transportation and communication. It is a critical infrastructure project that has significantly reduced travel time and enhanced economic and cultural exchange between the regions.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge carries the Seto-Chūō Expressway on the upper deck and the Seto-Ōhashi Line on the lower deck. The lower deck was designed to accommodate future Shinkansen tracks. The toll fee at opening was ¥6,300 for a one-way drive. The project cost US$7 billion and resulted in 17 worker fatalities during construction.

world knowledge.Name: Six Flags White Water
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in 1984 as White Water Atlanta, the park became part of the Six Flags family of parks in 1999. It was constructed by Silver Dollar City (now Herschend Family Entertainment) and was later sold to the group of limited partners that own Six Flags Over Georgia. The park has undergone several expansions and rebrandings over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The park was the site of an E. coli outbreak, which sickened at least ten children, including the son of then-Atlanta Braves baseball player Walt Weiss.
The park was sold to the group of limited partners that own Six Flags Over Georgia and was rebranded as Six Flags White Water.
Six Flags introduced the Flash Pass at Six Flags White Water, making it the first water park in the world to feature a virtual queue system for water rides.
White Water added Typhoon Twister, a five-story bowl slide.
Two individuals broke into the park and skateboarded down the Tornado water slide, causing an estimated $20,000 in damages.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is divided into four sections: Wildwater Lagoon, Pine Valley, Slippery Ridge, and Flash Flood Canyon. It features various water attractions including wave pools, lazy rivers, speed slides, and raft rides. The park also includes themed play areas for children and a large wave pool named Atlanta Ocean.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Six Flags White Water is the Southeast's largest water park and ranks among the top water parks in North America. It is a popular recreational destination for families and tourists, offering a variety of water-based attractions and entertainment options.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates seasonally from May through September and is marketed as a second gate to Six Flags Over Georgia. It features unique attractions such as the Flash Pass virtual queue system and the Dive-In Movies program. The park also previously included the American Adventures family entertainment center, which closed in 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Yahya Petra Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Federal Route 3 Wakaf Bharu-Kota Bharu-Kubang Kerian Highway
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sultan Yahya Petra Bridge is a major bridge in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, Malaysia, crossing the Kelantan River. It was constructed by Kien Huat Private Limited, a family firm of Tan Sri Lim Goh Tong, and opened in 1967 by the late Sultan of Kelantan, Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra ibni Almarhum Sultan Ibrahim. It was originally the first toll bridge in Malaysia. A second bridge project, consisting of a pair of bridges built on either side of the original bridge and a 1-km flyover, was completed in 2012, making it the only triple-carriageway bridge in the country.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened by the late Sultan of Kelantan, Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra ibni Almarhum Sultan Ibrahim.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of the second bridge project
Major_Events.Description: A pair of new bridges and a 1-km flyover were added, transforming it into the only triple-carriageway bridge in Malaysia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is an arch bridge with a total length of 2,800 feet. The original bridge remains a two-way bridge, while the new bridges carry one-way traffic each.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is significant as the first toll bridge in Malaysia and a key infrastructure project in Kelantan. It is named after the late Sultan Yahya Petra, reflecting its historical and cultural importance to the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Facilitating motor vehicle and pedestrian traffic across the Kelantan River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is maintained by the Malaysian Public Works Department (JKR) Kota Bharu. The original bridge was designed by the Government of Malaysia and the Malaysian Public Works Department (JKR), with construction by Kien Huat Private Limited.

world knowledge.Name: Peace Tower
world knowledge.Address: Centre Block of the Canadian parliament buildings, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Peace Tower replaced the Victoria Tower after it burned down in 1916. It was conceived as a memorial to Canadians who died in World War I. The cornerstone was laid in 1919, and the tower was completed in 1920. It was officially inaugurated in 1927.

Major_Events.Description: The Victoria Tower burned down, leading to the construction of the Peace Tower.
Prince Edward, Prince of Wales, laid the cornerstone of the Peace Tower.
The Peace Tower was officially inaugurated, and the Dominion Carillon was first played.
A two-year conservation project was undertaken to reverse deterioration of the masonry.
The clock stopped for the first time in 28 years.
The carillon was silenced for restoration, expected to last until 2027.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Peace Tower is a campanile in the Perpendicular Gothic style, standing 98 m (322 ft) tall. It features stone carvings, including approximately 370 gargoyles, grotesques, and friezes. The walls are made of Nepean sandstone, and the roof is reinforced concrete covered with copper. The tower includes a 4.8 m (16 ft) diameter clock face on each facade and a 53-bell carillon.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Peace Tower is a Canadian icon and serves as a memorial to Canadians who died in World War I. It has been featured on the Canadian twenty-dollar bill and symbolizes national pride and remembrance. The Memorial Chamber within the tower honors Canadian military personnel who died in various conflicts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The tower serves as a bell and clock tower, a memorial, and a national symbol. It also houses the Memorial Chamber and the Dominion Carillon.
Notable_Visitors: Prince Edward, Prince of Wales (later King Edward VIII)
world knowledge.Details: The Peace Tower's flagpole holds symbolic significance as the nation's flagpole, with strict protocols for flag display. The Memorial Chamber contains stained glass windows, marble panels, and the Books of Remembrance, which list all Canadian soldiers who died in service. The carillon, consisting of 53 bells, plays regular recitals and marks major occasions. The tower was the tallest building in Ottawa until the 1970s.

world knowledge.Name: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) was founded as University College of Engineering and Technology Malaysia (KUKTEM) on February 16, 2002. It was renamed to Universiti Malaysia Pahang (UMP) on February 1, 2007, and later to its current name on April 14, 2023, in honor of Sultan Abdullah. The university was granted autonomous status on November 28, 2015. Its main campus in Pekan began operations on July 27, 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as University College of Engineering and Technology Malaysia
Major_Events.Description: Founded by the Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's cabinet on February 16, 2002.
Renamed from University College of Engineering and Technology Malaysia (UTEC) to Universiti Malaysia Pahang (UMP) on February 1, 2007.
On November 28, 2015, UMPSA was granted autonomous status, gaining full control over financial, human resources, and administration.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah
Major_Events.Description: Renamed to honor the 16th Yang di-Pertuan Agong and current Sultan of Pahang, Sultan Abdullah, on April 14, 2023.
The main campus in Pekan began operations on July 27, 2009.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UMPSA is a public technical university specializing in engineering and technology, contributing significantly to Malaysia's educational and technological development.
world knowledge.Details: The main campus in Pekan can accommodate up to 10,000 students and 2,000 staff. It is home to four engineering faculties and one centre. The campus was used as the setting for the television comedy series 'Namaku Bedah' (2017). Coordinates: 3°32′35″N 103°26′10″E.

world knowledge.Name: Grim's Dyke
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grim's Dyke was built for painter Frederick Goodall and later became the home of dramatist W. S. Gilbert. It served as a rehabilitation center, film location, and was converted into a hotel in 1970. The house is named after the nearby prehistoric earthwork, Grim's Ditch.

Major_Events.Description: W. S. Gilbert died while attempting to save a girl from drowning in his lake.
The house was converted into the Grim's Dyke Hotel.
The statue was returned to Soho Square as per Lady Gilbert's will.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Richard Norman Shaw, the house features Gothic revivalism and late-Elizabethan style with high red-tiled gables, tall clustered chimneys, and leaded lights. It includes a studio, billiard room, and ornamental gardens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grim's Dyke is culturally significant as the home of W. S. Gilbert, co-creator of Gilbert and Sullivan operas. It also served as a film location and is a listed building.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, later a rehabilitation center, film location, and currently a hotel.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a lake, ornamental gardens, and was once home to exotic animals. The house and gatehouse are listed buildings. The hotel hosts Gilbert and Sullivan operas and other entertainments.

image_name: Drammen Museum of Art and Cultural History

world knowledge.Name: Drammen Museum of Art and Cultural History
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Drammen Museum of Art and Cultural History operates as a foundation created in 1996. The Foundation consists of the former Drammen Museum, founded in 1908, Drammen Art Society, founded in 1867 and Gulskogen Manor, which was established as a museum in 1959. The museum's main buildings are centered on Marienlyst manor (Marienlyst gård) which dates from approximately 1770.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's main buildings are centered on Marienlyst manor (Marienlyst gård) which dates from approximately 1770. Other properties include a museum building from 1930 containing the museum's administration, permanent exhibitions and collections, as well as Lyche pavilion from 1990 with the gallery, temporary exhibitions and museum café, Halling yard, together with other historic buildings, the oldest of which dating back to 1760s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum's collections come from throughout Buskerud, and covers areas such as folk art and handicrafts, commerce, transport, agriculture, art, costumes and traditional dresses, church art and industry. The museum has a large library, photographic collection and archives covering the history of both Drammen and Buskerud.
world knowledge.Details: The Fine Art Collection consists primarily of Norwegian art and contains masterpieces from the 1800s. Featured artists include Johan Christian Dahl, Peder Balke, Eilif Peterssen and Theodor Kittelsen. Information boards are presented solely in Norwegian. The museum website can be accessed in English.

world knowledge.Name: Daresbury Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Daresbury Hall is a former Georgian country house built in 1759 for George Heron. It descended in the Heron family until 1850, then became the property of Samuel Beckett Chadwick. By 1892, it was acquired by Sir Gilbert Greenall, later Baron Daresbury. During the Second World War, it was used as a military hospital and later as a residential home for handicapped people by the charity Scope from 1955. It became semi-derelict after being bought by a millionaire who died before restoration could take place.

Major_Events.Description: Used as a military hospital during the Second World War.
Used by the charity Scope as a residential home for handicapped people.
A large cannabis farm containing six hundred plants with an estimated street value of £750,000 was discovered in an annex at the estate.
The empty building was badly damaged by fire.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is constructed in a Georgian style in brown brick with stone dressings and has a slate roof. It has three storeys and seven bays with a stone plinth and stone bands between the storeys. Framing the middle three bays are rusticated pilasters, and similar quoins at the corners. All the windows are sash windows. Along the top of the house is a plain parapet, with a pediment above the central three bays.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Daresbury Hall is a designated Grade II* listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former country house, later used as a military hospital and residential home for handicapped people.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion was badly damaged by fire in 2016. There were plans to partly demolish and convert the house before the fire occurred.

world knowledge.Name: Izard County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Izard County Courthouse is the county's fourth courthouse, two of the first three having been destroyed by fire. It was built in 1938–1940 by crews from the National Youth Administration.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was built by crews from the National Youth Administration.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1993.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse is a two-story structure, built of rusticated gray limestone, with modest Art Deco styling.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is historically significant as it represents the fourth iteration of the county's courthouse, with two of the previous ones destroyed by fire. It also includes a World War I memorial featuring a marble doughboy statue erected in 1930.
world knowledge.Details: The grounds include a World War I memorial featuring a marble doughboy statue erected in 1930 in front of the courthouse. The NRHP reference number is 93001025.

world knowledge.Name: Sankey tank
world knowledge.Address: Malleshwaram, Vyalikaval, Sadashivanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sankey tank is an artificial lake constructed by Col. Richard Hieram Sankey of the Madras Sappers Regiment in 1882 to meet the water supply demands of Bangalore. It was also known as Gandhadhakotikere due to the nearby Government Sandalwood Depot. The tank was built as a safeguard against water shortages experienced during the Great Famine of 1876–78.

Major_Events.Event: Proposal to construct a multistory building
Major_Events.Description: Local builders proposed to construct a multistory building in the Sankey tank bed, which was challenged in the Karnataka Lok Adalat. The court ordered the Forest Department to repossess the land and recommended no construction within 100 m of lakes to protect water bodies.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Artificial freshwater lake with a catchment area of 1.254 km (0.8 mi), maximum depth of 9.26 m (30.4 ft), and a surface elevation of 929.8 m (3,050.5 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sankey tank is culturally significant as a historical water supply system for Bangalore and a protected natural area in the city.
world knowledge.Details: The lake was converted into a park by the Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewage Board (BWSSB) and the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) with funds from the Government of Karnataka. The Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) rejected a proposal to build an 18-floor luxury apartment block near the tank due to violations of environmental laws.

world knowledge.Name: Silvio Pettirossi International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Silvio Pettirossi International Airport is an international airport in Luque, Paraguay, serving Asunción and indirectly Clorinda, Formosa, in Argentina. Named after Paraguayan aviator Silvio Pettirossi, it was known as President Stroessner International Airport between 1980 and 1989. It was inaugurated on 11 June 1938 and has undergone several upgrades and expansions since.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inaugurated on 11 June 1938.
The airport's runway was constructed in the 1960s and resurfaced in 1985.
Runway repair work started in 2001 but was halted due to lack of funds, completed by early 2005.
On 31 July 2007, a group of five men stole US$1,000,000 from a money exchange at the airport.
New instrument landing systems began operating in November 2009, replacing the 1980 system.
Various improvements were made to the terminal in January 2013.
On 17 December 2015, Air Europa began service between Pettirossi and Madrid, Spain.
The airport ceased operating commercial flights for 7 months due to the COVID-19 pandemic, resuming in October 2020.
In November 2020, drugs disguised as parcels were found and seized at the airport.
Plans for a second terminal were unveiled in February 2021, to be started in 2022.
In October 2021, a new route operated by Paranair was announced between Pettirossi and Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia.
On 26 May 2023, renovation works of the north concourse were completed, greatly expanding the arrivals hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The terminal building is split into two international concourses: the south concourse having gates 1 to 4, and the north concourse having gates 5 and 6. The original passenger terminal is now used by Grupo Aerotáctico (GAT) of the Paraguayan Air Force.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Silvio Pettirossi, a notable Paraguayan aviator, and has served as a key international hub for Paraguay, connecting it to various global destinations.
world knowledge.Details: Silvio Pettirossi International Airport is the main international hub for LATAM Paraguay and Paranair. Some of its facilities are shared with the Ñu-Guazú Air Force Base of the Paraguayan Air Force. The airport has seen significant growth in passenger and flight numbers over the years and continues to undergo expansions and improvements to meet increasing demand.

world knowledge.Name: Botswana National Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Botswana National Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Gaborone, Botswana, primarily used for football matches. It was built in 1965 and opened in 1966. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including in 2008 and 2016, to increase its capacity and modernize its facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the opening and closing ceremonies as well as the track and field events for the 2nd African Youth Games.
The stadium was renovated to increase its capacity to 25,000 in anticipation of the country's 50th independence celebrations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has 10 stands, three of which are covered. The north and south ends each have three large stands, while the west side has three covered stands and the east end has one giant uncovered stand. The pitch is surrounded by an athletics track.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Botswana, hosting national and international football matches, athletics events, and other cultural events such as music festivals and national celebrations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for football matches and athletics events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is home to the Botswana national football team, the Zebras, and several Botswana Premier League clubs. It also hosts non-sporting events like Botswana Police Service Day, Botswana Defense Force Day, and Botswana Independence Celebrations. The stadium was renovated by Hitecon construction company to accommodate teams competing in the 2010 FIFA World Cup, although it was not used for that purpose.

world knowledge.Name: Tara (mountain)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tara is a mountain in western Serbia, part of the Dinaric Alps, known for its dense forests, high-elevation clearings, and karst caves. Initial protection efforts began in the 19th century, with the establishment of Tara National Park in 1981. The park was expanded in 2015 to include the protected area of "Zaovine Landscape of Outstanding Features". The mountain is also known for its medicinal plants, diverse wildlife, and historical significance, including evidence of ancient lead pollution and prehistoric settlements.

Major_Events.Description: Tara National Park was established in July 1981, encompassing a large part of the mountain and part of the Zvijezda mountain.
The National Assembly of Serbia adopted a new law that expanded Tara National Park to 249.92 km² by adding the protected area of "Zaovine Landscape of Outstanding Features".
The Zvijezda Canyon, the deepest canyon in Serbia, was discovered on 12 June 2010.

Major_Events.Event: Evidence of oldest lead pollution in Europe
Major_Events.Description: Research published in 2018 revealed evidence of the oldest lead pollution in Europe at the locality "Crveni Tepih", dated to 3600 BC.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The national park features a group of mountain peaks with deep picturesque gorges, including the Drina Gorge, Rača Gorge, and Derventa Gorge. The area is characterized by karst caves, pits, springs, and viewing points. The park also includes the Rača monastery, a Serbian Orthodox monastery with a rich history of scriptorium and manuscript copying.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tara is culturally significant for its rich biodiversity, historical settlements, and its role in Serbian literature and religion. The mountain is also known as the "lungs of Serbia" due to its extensive forest coverage. The Rača monastery is a cultural monument, and the mountain has been a refuge for hajduks during the Ottoman period.
world knowledge.Details: Tara National Park is a popular tourist destination with 10 scenic viewpoints, 290 km of hiking trails, and facilities for kayaking, rafting, and canyoning. The park is home to diverse flora and fauna, including rare species like the Serbian spruce and brown bears. The mountain is also known for its medicinal plants and locally made products such as woolen handcrafts, dairy products, and spirits. The area has faced challenges with illegal construction and waste management issues.

world knowledge.Name: Konpira Grand Theatre
world knowledge.Address: 1241 Kotohira-chō, Nakatado District, Kagawa Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Konpira Grand Theatre, also known as Kanamaru-za, is the oldest kabuki theatre in Japan. Originally constructed in 1835-1836, it was restored in 1976 to its Edo period appearance after being designated an Important Cultural Property in 1970. The theatre has undergone several name changes and ownership transitions, including periods of disuse and use as a movie theater.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was restored to its Edo period appearance after a fund-raising drive raised over US$2 million.
Designated as an Important Cultural Property by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the national government.
A troupe led by Nakamura Kichiemon II and Sawamura Sōjūrō IX performed plays, marking the beginning of annual month-long kabuki performances.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre features a tatami floor in the main seating section, box seats called masu, a rotating stage (mawari butai), trap doors (seri), and a unique 'mouse door' (nezumi kido) for crowd control. It also includes a karaido (empty well) for dramatic actor entrances and shōji panels for lighting control.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Konpira Grand Theatre is the oldest surviving kabuki theatre in Japan and serves as a vital cultural link to Edo-period performing arts. It is designated as an Important Cultural Property and hosts annual kabuki performances, attracting major actors from Tokyo and Osaka.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre was used as a filming location for the 1995 film 'Sharaku'. It features unique architectural elements like the karaido and nezumi kido, and maintains traditional seating and stage designs distinct from modern kabuki theatres.

world knowledge.Name: Nagai Park
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Large sports complex with multiple facilities including stadiums, botanical garden, swimming pool, and gymnasium
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Popular area for picnics during cherry blossom season due to its large number of cherry trees
world knowledge.Details: Facilities include three multipurpose sports stadiums (including the 50,000-seat Nagai Stadium), Nagai Botanical Garden (with over 1,000 species of trees and flowers), a swimming pool, gymnasium, and a tract of preserved local forest.

world knowledge.Name: Boraboy
world knowledge.Address: Boraboy, Taşova District, Amasya Province, Turkey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Boraboy is a mountain town with a beautiful lake, Lake Boraboy. Although no written documents exist about ancient Boraboy, there are a few ruins around the town. In a document dated 1257, early Turkmen settlers around Boraboy had been mentioned. The origin of the name Boraboy may either be a certain Bora Bey, a leader of a Turkmen tribe or the Greek wind god Boreas. The settlement was declared a seat of township in 1971. Between 1964 and 1994 the town was also called Gölbeyli ("lake lord").

Major_Events.Description: Boraboy was declared a seat of township in 1971.
Between 1964 and 1994, the town was called Gölbeyli ("lake lord").

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Boraboy is culturally significant due to its historical roots with early Turkmen settlers and its association with the Greek wind god Boreas. The town's agricultural activities, including apple, pear, and sugar cane production, as well as trout farming, beekeeping, and flour production, contribute to its local cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Boraboy is a village in the Taşova District, Amasya Province, Turkey. Its population is 732 (2021). Distance to Taşova is 17 kilometres (11 mi) and to Amasya is 58 kilometres (36 mi). The settled population was 819 as of 2013. This geographical article about a location in Amasya Province, Turkey is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Trinity Bridge, Saint Petersburg
world knowledge.Address: Connects Kamennoostrovsky Prospect with Suvorov Square, Saint Petersburg, Russia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Trinity Bridge is the third permanent bridge across the Neva River in Saint Petersburg. It was built by the French firm Société de Construction des Batignolles and completed in 1903 for the 200-year anniversary of Saint Petersburg. It was originally named after the Old Trinity Cathedral and has undergone several name changes, including Equality Bridge and Kirovsky Bridge.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was constructed by a French firm and completed in time for the 200-year anniversary of Saint Petersburg.
The bridge was renamed Equality Bridge following the Russian Revolution.
The bridge was renamed Kirovsky Bridge in honor of Sergei Kirov.
The bridge's original name, Trinity Bridge, was restored.
The bascule span was rebuilt as a one-winged, lifting design, extending its length to 43 meters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge features a bascule design with nine spans, including five permanent metallic riveted spans and a three-arch granite viaduct. It is decorated with cast iron gratings, granite pylons with lanterns, and Art Nouveau-style metallic lanterns. The central spans use a novel console-arch-beam system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Trinity Bridge is a symbol of the Franco-Russian Alliance and an important architectural landmark in Saint Petersburg. It is also associated with the legendary flight of Soviet pilot Valery Chkalov, who allegedly flew under the bridge in the 1930s.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge's design was the result of a contest won by French engineer Paul-Joseph Bodin and his team. It has undergone several reconstructions, including the remodeling of obelisks in 1955 and the rebuilding of the bascule span in the 1960s. The bridge is also referenced in popular culture, such as in Boris Grebenshchikov's song 'Under the Bridge, like Chkalov'.

world knowledge.Name: Underscar Manor
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Underscar Manor is a country house designed by Charles Verelst for William Oxley, a Liverpool textile merchant, and built in the Italianate style. It came into the ownership of James Tait Black in the early 20th century. The house was converted into a hotel in the 1970s and later became a private home again after being acquired by Alexander Mineev in 2010. Following Mineev's murder in 2014, it was bought by Jonathan Brown in August 2014.

Major_Events.Description: The house was designed by Charles Verelst for William Oxley and built in the Italianate style.
The house was converted for use as a hotel.
The house became a private home again when acquired by Alexander Mineev, a Russian oligarch.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by the Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh
Major_Events.Description: The Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh visited the house in October 2008.
Following Mineev's murder in Moscow in February 2014, the house was bought by Jonathan Brown in August 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Italianate style, designed by Charles Verelst.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Underscar Manor is a Grade II listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, later converted into a hotel, and then returned to private ownership.
world knowledge.Details: William Oxley, who built Underscar, was a successful Liverpool textile merchant. The house was commissioned in 1857, and the gardens were designed by landscape architect Edward Kemp. William Oxley died in 1871, and his wife Anna continued to live there until her death in 1890.

world knowledge.Name: Château d'Anjony
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château d'Anjony was built in the 15th century by Louis II d'Anjony, companion of Jean de Dunois and Joan of Arc. It was constructed near the towers of Tournemire, which had been held by his family and the Tournemires in joint fief since 1351. This dual ownership led to three centuries of bloody rivalry between the two families. The Tournemires left the area around 1650. The castle and its estate were classified as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture, with the castle (excluding the 18th-century attached building) classified in 1942.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Louis II d'Anjony, companion of Jean de Dunois and Joan of Arc.
The castle (excluding the 18th-century attached building) was classified as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle, built of reddish basalt, consists of a keep with four corner towers, with only one room on each floor. During the 18th century, a small wing was added in the then fashionable style. The low vaulted cellar in the basement was turned into a vast entrance hall. The main hall on the first floor has a coffered ceiling with three tiers of beams. The castle features fine furnishings and fittings, including tapestries from Aubusson and Flanders, a tester bed, and a reclining seat. The kitchen has a massive fireplace. The chapel, located in the southwest tower, has frescoes illustrating the life of Christ and a statue of Our Lady of Anjony. The Knights' Hall on the second floor has frescoes of Michel of Anjony and his wife, Germaine of Foix, and other frescoes illustrating the legend of the Nine Valiant Knights. The audience chamber on the third floor has diagonal faulting and walls hung with two large tapestries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château d'Anjony is one of the most remarkable castles in Upper Auvergne and is strategically located on the Tournemire promontory, dominating the Doire valley. Its historical and architectural significance, along with its fine furnishings and frescoes, make it a culturally important landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is located in a strategic position on the Tournemire promontory and dominates the rich landscape of the Doire valley with its four tall towers, 40 metres (130 ft). Notable objects in the Knights' Hall include a Florentine table inlaid with ivory, a Mudéjar-style secretaire, engraved silver dishes, and various Renaissance objets d'art.

world knowledge.Name: Khon Kaen Airport
world knowledge.Area: Ban Pet, Mueang, Khon Kaen, Thailand
world knowledge.Address: Ban Pet subdistrict, Mueang Khon Kaen district, Khon Kaen province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Khon Kaen International Airport, located in northeastern Thailand, has experienced significant growth since 2013, with an annual growth rate of 20 percent. In 2017, it handled around two million passengers. The Department of Airports has planned a two billion baht project to upgrade the airport by 2021, increasing passenger capacity from 2.8 million to five million per year and expanding the terminal from 16,500 m2 to 44,500 m2.

Major_Events.Description: Khon Kaen Airport was officially opened on February 6, 1963.
The Department of Airports signed a memorandum of understanding to upgrade Khon Kaen Airport, aiming to increase passenger capacity and expand the terminal.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Khon Kaen Airport is a significant transportation hub in northeastern Thailand, facilitating regional connectivity and economic growth.
world knowledge.Details: Khon Kaen International Airport (IATA: KKC, ICAO: VTUK) serves the city of Khon Kaen and is operated by the Department of Airports. The airport has a runway with a length of 10,007 ft (3,050 m) and an elevation of 670 ft (204 m) above mean sea level. In recent years, it has handled over 1.5 million passengers, with significant growth in aircraft movements and freight volume.

world knowledge.Name: Guiyang Longdongbao International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Guiyang Longdongbao International Airport was opened on 28 May 1997 and adopted its current name on 19 January 2006. It serves as the hub for Colorful Guizhou Airlines and a focus city for China Southern Airlines. The airport has undergone expansions to accommodate increasing passenger and cargo traffic.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened on 28 May 1997.
The airport adopted its current name, Guiyang Longdongbao International Airport, on 19 January 2006.
An expansion project was authorized and started in September 2010 to increase the annual passenger capacity to 15.5 million and cargo traffic to 220 thousand tons per year.
Hainan Airlines began a weekly flight to Paris, France, on 24 March 2019, marking the first international long-haul air travel from Guiyang and Guizhou Province.
In June 2017, the airport launched cooperation with VariFlight to install the Airport Collaborative Decision Making system (A-CDM) to improve on-time performance and safety.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a 3,500-meter and a 4,000-meter concrete runway, capable of accommodating wide-bodied aircraft like Boeing 747 and Airbus A330. The terminal spans approximately 34,000 m² (370,000 sq ft), handling over 2000 passengers per hour.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the primary international airport serving Guiyang and Guizhou Province, it plays a crucial role in regional connectivity, economic development, and tourism. It is also a hub for Colorful Guizhou Airlines, promoting local culture and travel.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving passenger and cargo flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by Longdongbao International Airport station on Line 2 of the Guiyang Metro and Longdongbao railway station, situated underneath the airport. In 2017, it was the 22nd busiest airport in mainland China with 18,109,610 passengers. It exceeded its design capacity of 5 million passengers per year in 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Jubilee Park, Jamshedpur
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jubilee Park was opened to the public in 1958 to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the establishment of Jamshedpur. It was a gift from the Tata Steel Company to the town of Tatanagar (Jamshedpur).
