Inspired by the Brindavan Gardens in Mysore, the park features a statue of Jamsetji Tata and is also known as the Mughal Gardens of Jamshedpur.

Major_Events.Description: The park is decorated with lights and fountains to celebrate Founder's Day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features Mughal-inspired gardens, fountains, and a statue of Jamsetji Tata. It includes various sections like a zoo, amusement park, and rose garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jubilee Park is a significant cultural and recreational hub in Jamshedpur, offering a space for outdoor activities, family outings, and community events. It is one of the largest urban parks in India and a symbol of the city's heritage.
world knowledge.Details: Jubilee Park includes attractions such as the Tata Steel Zoological Park, Nicco Jubilee Amusement Park, Jayanti Sarovar (Zoo Lake), Bat Island, Children's Park, and Rose Garden. It is known for its laser fountain show and is a popular wedding spot. The park is operated by Tata Steel and provides inner connectivity for visitors.

world knowledge.Name: National School of Drama
world knowledge.Address: Bahawalpur House, New Delhi, National Capital Territory of Delhi, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National School of Drama (NSD) was established in 1959 under the auspices of Sangeet Natak Akademi. It originated from a 1954 seminar proposing a central institution for theatre. The Asian Theatre Institute (ATI), established in 1958, was merged with NSD in 1959. It became an autonomous organization in 1975 and was granted deemed university status in 2005, which was revoked in 2011. NSD has played a pivotal role in promoting theatre in India through various initiatives, workshops, and festivals.

Major_Events.Description: National School of Drama was established under Sangeet Natak Akademi.
NSD became an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Culture.
First National Theatre Festival organized by NSD.
NSD was granted deemed university status, later revoked in 2011.
Celebrated at the annual theatre festival, Bharat Rang Mahotsav.
Silver Jubilee edition of Bharat Rang Mahotsav celebrated in India, Sri Lanka, and Nepal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: NSD's campus includes three auditoria, a studio theatre, and minor performance spaces. The open-air Meghdoot theatre is located under a banyan tree.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: NSD is a premier institution for theatre training in India, fostering contemporary and traditional theatre practices. It has significantly contributed to Indian theatre through its repertory company, festivals like Bharat Rang Mahotsav, and outreach programs.
world knowledge.Details: NSD has a professional performing wing, the National School of Drama Repertory Company, established in 1964. It also runs the Theatre-in-Education Company (Sanskaar Rang Toli) for children. NSD organizes various festivals, workshops, and extension programs across India and neighboring countries. Recent initiatives include short-term courses in acting and theatre direction.

image_name: Iglesia Parroquial Mayor del Espíritu Santo

world knowledge.Name: Iglesia Parroquial Mayor del Espíritu Santo
world knowledge.Address: Plaza Honorato del Castillo, Sancti Spíritus, Cuba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iglesia Parroquial Mayor del Espíritu Santo is the oldest church in Cuba, originally constructed in wood in 1522. It was destroyed by pirates and later rebuilt in stone in 1680. The 36-meter high bell tower, featuring gold, silver, and bronze bells, was added in the 18th century, with the cupola completed in the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The original wooden structure was destroyed by pirates, leading to its reconstruction in stone.
A 36-meter high bell tower featuring gold, silver, and bronze bells was added.
The cupola of the church was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally constructed in wood, later rebuilt in stone. Features a 36-meter high bell tower with gold, silver, and bronze bells, and a cupola.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the oldest church in Cuba and holds significant historical and religious importance in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The church is located two blocks south of the town's main square and is situated on the Plaza Honorato del Castillo.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Fernando Torres
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 2011 as an honour to Fernando Torres (who was born in the city of Fuenlabrada), the stadium was inaugurated on 1 September of that year in a friendly against Atlético Madrid, Torres' first club, with his parents as honorary guests.

Major_Events.Description: Friendly match to inaugurate the stadium, with Fernando Torres' parents as honorary guests.

Major_Events.Event: Copa del Rey match vs Real Madrid
Major_Events.Description: Real Madrid won 2–0 in a Copa del Rey match hosted at the stadium.
After CF Fuenlabrada's promotion to Segunda División, the stadium was renovated to meet LFP criteria.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-use stadium with grass surface, capacity of 5,400.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Named in honor of Fernando Torres, a famous footballer born in Fuenlabrada, symbolizing local pride and connection to football history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches, home stadium of CF Fuenlabrada.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by Fuenlabrada City Council, renovated in 2019 and 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Bordeaux Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bordeaux Cathedral, officially known as the Primatial Cathedral of St Andrew of Bordeaux, is a Catholic church dedicated to Saint Andrew. It was first mentioned in documents from 814 and consecrated by Pope Urban II in 1096. The cathedral underwent transformations from Romanesque to Gothic style, influenced by political changes, including English control over Aquitaine. It survived the French Revolution, during which it was repurposed and vandalized, and underwent extensive renovations in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was formally consecrated by Pope Urban II.

Major_Events.Event: Wedding of Eleanor of Aquitaine and Louis VII
Major_Events.Description: The 13-year-old Eleanor of Aquitaine married the future Louis VII of France in the cathedral.
The Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France, including Bordeaux Cathedral, were designated as a World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Key elements include the north portal (Portal of Spires), the Pey-Berland tower (Flamboyant Gothic), and the choir with radiating chapels. The nave has rib vaults and lierne vaults, and the elevation includes arcades, passageways, and high windows. The cathedral also has Renaissance decorative elements and 19th-century stained glass windows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bordeaux Cathedral is culturally significant as a key site on the Routes of Santiago de Compostela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has played a central role in the religious and political history of Aquitaine, hosting royal weddings and surviving the French Revolution. Its architecture reflects the transition from Romanesque to Gothic styles and includes contributions from notable figures like Archbishop Bertrand de Goth (Pope Clement V).

UNESCO.Official_Name: Part of Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France

Bells.Description: The cathedral has 4 bells in the Pey-Berland Tower: Marie, Ferdinand-André II, Marguerite, and Clémence.

Organ.Description: The grand organ, installed in 1982, is located on a tribune over the west front doorway.

Art_Collection.Description: The Marcadé collection includes 42 illuminations, paintings, sculptures, and liturgical objects donated by Canon Marcadé in 1947.

Transport.Description: The site is served by tramway lines A and B at Station Hôtel de Ville.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Annecy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Annecy is a perialpine lake formed about 18,000 years ago when large alpine glaciers melted. It is named after the city of Annecy, which marks the start of the Thiou, Lake Annecy's outflow river.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Annecy is a popular tourist destination known for its swimming and water sports. It is the third-largest lake in France, excluding the French part of Lake Geneva.

Details.Primary inflows: Ire, Eau morte, Laudon, Bornette and Biolon
Details.Additional_Info: A cycle path goes partially around Lake Annecy past Sevrier and St Jorioz to Ugine. It has an aim to reach Albertville. The lake is around 14 km long.

world knowledge.Name: University of Cantabria
world knowledge.Location: Santander, Torrelavega and Comillas, Cantabria, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Cantabria (UC) was founded in 1972 and comprises 15 schools and colleges. It was established by decree of the Council of Ministers of Spain with the name of University of Santander and renamed University of Cantabria thirteen years later. The university was created by the affiliation of several schools and colleges that were already established either independently or under other universities.

Major_Events.Description: Selected by the Government of Spain.

Major_Events.Event: First appearance in Academic Ranking of World Universities
Major_Events.Description: Ranked in the range of 151-200 best universities in the world in the field of Physics.
Present as an institution among the top 1,000 universities.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Cantabria is a significant educational institution in Spain, contributing to higher education and research. It is part of the Group 9 of Spanish Universities (G9) and the European alliance of universities EUNICE.
world knowledge.Details: The UC has signed numerous agreements with universities worldwide, including 216 with European Universities (Erasmus program), 64 with Latin American institutions, 8 with universities in the United States, and 1 with an Australian university. It is also a member of national and international university networks such as the Compostela Group of Universities and the Santander Network.

world knowledge.Name: Adams Museum & House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Adams Museum & House in Deadwood is considered the Black Hills' oldest history museum. It was founded by Deadwood businessman and former mayor W.E. Adams in 1930 as a gift to the city of Deadwood. The museum reflects the legends of Wild Bill, Calamity Jane, Deadwood Dick, and the Black Hills gold rush. The Historic Adams House, built in 1892 by Deadwood pioneers Harris and Anna Franklin, is an elegant Queen Anne-style house that symbolizes Deadwood's transition from a rough gold mining town to a wealthy and socially prominent community.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded by W.E. Adams as a gift to the city of Deadwood.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the Historic Adams House
Major_Events.Description: Built by Deadwood pioneers Harris and Anna Franklin, the house marked a new era of prosperity for Deadwood.
The museum was ranked number 3 by True West Magazine.
Won the Organizational Award and the Governor's Award for History display.

Major_Events.Event: American Association for State and Local History Award
Major_Events.Description: Received recognition from the American Association for State and Local History.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Historic Adams House is an elegant Queen Anne-style house, completely furnished with original Adams family furniture and restored interiors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and showcases the history of Deadwood and the Black Hills, including the legends of Wild Bill, Calamity Jane, and the gold rush era. It is a significant cultural landmark for understanding the region's transition from a mining town to a prosperous community.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features changing exhibits and special programs year-round. Notable exhibits include the J.B. Haggin Locomotive, the Thoen Stone, and Potato Creek Johnny's Gold Nugget. The Historic Adams House is located at 22 Van Buren Avenue and serves as a tribute to Black Hills pioneers.

world knowledge.Name: Permas Jaya Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Plentong, Johor Bahru District, Johor, Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was proposed in 1984 when Bandar Baru Permas Jaya was launched by Bandar Raya Developments Berhad (BRDB). It was completed in 1994 and was once the longest arch bridge in Southeast Asia. A second bridge was proposed in 2006 and completed in 2012 under the Iskandar Development Region plan.

Major_Events.Description: The first Permas Jaya Bridge was completed, becoming the longest arch bridge in Southeast Asia at the time.
The second Permas Jaya Bridge was constructed to provide a direct connection to the Johor Bahru East Coast Highway.
The second Permas Jaya Bridge was opened to road users on 1 March 2012.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Arch bridge design, constructed to shorten travel distance between Bandar Baru Permas Jaya and Johor Bahru city area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is significant for its role in improving transportation infrastructure in Johor Bahru and for once holding the record as the longest arch bridge in Southeast Asia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Motor vehicle and pedestrian bridge crossing Tebrau River and Plentong River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is maintained by the Malaysian Public Works Department (JKR) Johor Bahru and Majlis Bandaraya Johor Bahru (MBJB). The second bridge was constructed by the Government of Malaysia and the Malaysian Public Works Department (JKR).

world knowledge.Name: Council of Europe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Council of Europe (CoE) was founded in 1949 with the goal of upholding human rights, democracy, and the rule of law in Europe. It is Europe's oldest intergovernmental organisation, representing 46 member states. The organisation was established after World War II to promote cooperation and prevent future conflicts in Europe. The Council of Europe is distinct from the European Union, although they share some symbols like the European flag and anthem.

Major_Events.Description: The founding statute of the Council of Europe was signed by ten states, establishing the organisation.
The convention was adopted, creating the European Court of Human Rights to oversee compliance.
Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe following its invasion of Ukraine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Council of Europe's headquarters, the Palace of Europe, is part of the Quartier européen in Strasbourg. The area includes several modern and functional buildings, including the European Court of Human Rights and the Agora Building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Council of Europe is a cornerstone of European cooperation, promoting human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. It has played a key role in post-war reconciliation and the integration of Eastern European countries after the fall of communism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Regional intergovernmental organisation focused on human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.
Notable_Visitors: King Juan Carlos I of Spain
world knowledge.Details: The Council of Europe operates through international treaties and conventions, such as the European Convention on Human Rights. It has observer status at the United Nations and collaborates with other international organisations. The Council also works with non-member states and has external offices across Europe and beyond. Notable bodies include the European Court of Human Rights and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE).

world knowledge.Name: Marco Island, Florida
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 12.1 square miles (31.4 km2) land, 10.7 square miles (27.6 km2) water
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Marco Island's history dates back to 500 CE when the Calusa people inhabited the island. Spanish explorers named it La Isla de San Marcos in the mid-1500s. Development began in the late 1800s with the arrival of William Thomas Collier, who founded the village of Marco in 1870. The island incorporated as Collier City in 1927, was abolished in 1957, and reincorporated as a city in 1997.

Major_Events.Description: Anthropologist Frank Hamilton Cushing discovered Calusa artifacts, including the Key Marco Cat, on Key Marco.
William D. 'Capt. Bill' Collier opened a hotel on the island, known today as the Olde Marco Inn.
Devastated the island with an 8' storm surge.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Marco Island is culturally significant due to its Calusa artifacts, including the Key Marco Cat, and its development as an affluent beach community with resort amenities. It also has a tropical climate and scenic elevations relative to the generally flat south Florida landscape.

Details.Climate: Tropical wet and dry or savanna type (Aw under the Köppen system)

Transportation.Bridges: Collier Boulevard and San Marco Road (CR 92)
Transportation.Public Transit: Collier Area Transit's Route #21 and Route #121

Education.Public Schools: Operated by the District School Board of Collier County

Beaches.Private Access: Residents' Beach, Sarazen Park at South Beach

world knowledge.Name: Malmesbury Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Malmesbury Abbey, at Malmesbury in Wiltshire, England, is a former Benedictine abbey dedicated to Saint Peter and Saint Paul. It was one of the few English religious houses with a continuous history from the 7th century through to the Dissolution of the Monasteries. Founded around 676 by the scholar-poet Aldhelm, a nephew of King Ine of Wessex, the Abbey developed a reputation for academic learning. It was the site of an early attempt at human flight by the monk Eilmer of Malmesbury in the early 11th century. The Abbey was closed in 1539 by Henry VIII and sold to William Stumpe, who returned the abbey church to the town for use as a parish church.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as a Benedictine monastery by Aldhelm, a nephew of King Ine of Wessex.
The remains of King Æthelstan of Wessex were buried in the Abbey.
The 431 feet tall spire and tower collapsed in a storm, destroying much of the church.
The Abbey was closed by Henry VIII and sold to William Stumpe.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as Grade I listed building
Major_Events.Description: The church was designated as a Grade I listed building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally built as a Benedictine abbey, the current structure was substantially completed by 1180. The Abbey features a parvise (a room over the porch) that holds some examples of books from the abbey library. The building has suffered significant damage over the centuries, including the collapse of the spire in 1500 and the west tower around 1550.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Malmesbury Abbey is historically significant as one of the few English religious houses with a continuous history from the 7th century. It was a center of academic learning and is associated with notable figures such as Aldhelm and Eilmer of Malmesbury. The Abbey also played a role in the transcription of the Anglo-Saxon epic poem Beowulf.
world knowledge.Details: The Abbey remains in full use as the parish church of Malmesbury in the Diocese of Bristol. It contains a fine parvise with examples of books from the abbey library and holds Anglo-Saxon charters that provide source material for the history of Wessex and the West Saxon church. The current organ dates from 1984 and was built by E.J. Johnson of Cambridge.

image_name: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci

world knowledge.Name: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci in Milan, dedicated to painter and scientist Leonardo da Vinci, is the largest science and technology museum in Italy. It was opened on 15 February 1953 and inaugurated by Prime Minister Alcide De Gasperi. The museum is located in the ancient monastery of San Vittore al Corpo in Milan.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by Prime Minister Alcide De Gasperi

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Located in the ancient monastery of San Vittore al Corpo in Milan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest science and technology museum in Italy, dedicated to Leonardo da Vinci.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is divided into seven main departments, each with laboratories for children and young students. It includes sections on Transport, Materials, Energy, Communication, and Leonardo da Vinci, Art & Science.

world knowledge.Name: Barkatullah Khan Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Barkatullah Khan Stadium was established in 1986 and named after the 6th chief minister of Rajasthan. It is primarily used for cricket and has hosted several notable matches, including ODIs. The stadium underwent redevelopment with enhanced capacity and modern facilities.

Major_Events.Description: India vs Zimbabwe on 8 December 2000.
India vs West Indies on 21 November 2002.

Major_Events.Event: Sachin Tendulkar's First Century on Home Soil
Major_Events.Description: Sachin Tendulkar scored 146 runs against Zimbabwe in the third one-dayer, his highest score against Zimbabwe.
Zaheer Khan scored the most runs in a single over in one-dayers at this venue, with 25 runs off Henry Olonga's over.
Ajit Agarkar took his 100th wicket in his 67th match, becoming the seventh Indian to achieve this milestone.
Cricket returned to Jodhpur after nearly 20 years with the Legends League Cricket 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features floodlights by GE Electric, newly developed team dressing rooms, and stands for cameras to enhance live coverage. The ends are named Cox Cutir End and Residency Road End.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant cricket venue in Rajasthan, hosting international matches and notable cricketing events. It is named after a former chief minister, reflecting its regional importance.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's capacity is 30,000 people. It was announced for redevelopment in 2020 for IPL 2021 and international matches, with Rs.20 Crore allocated in the 2021 Rajasthan Budget. The stadium is owned by the Rajasthan Cricket Association and operated by the Jodhpur Development Authority.

world knowledge.Name: ICESI University
world knowledge.Area: Pance, Santiago de Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
world knowledge.Location: Pance, Santiago de Cali, Valle del Cauca, COL
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Icesi University, originally the initials of Instituto Colombiano de Estudios Superiores de Incolda, was founded in 1979 by a group of businessmen in the region. It is a private university located in Cali, Colombia. The campus is situated in the area of Pance, south of the city. In 2010, it became the first private university in southwestern Colombia to receive High Quality Institutional Accreditation. This accreditation was renewed in 2015 until 2021.

Major_Events.Description: Icesi University became the first private university in southwestern Colombia to receive High Quality Institutional Accreditation.

Major_Events.Event: Renewal of High Quality Institutional Accreditation
Major_Events.Description: The Ministry of National Education granted the renewal of the High Quality Institutional Accreditation until 2021.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Icesi University is culturally and historically significant as it was the first private university in southwestern Colombia to receive High Quality Institutional Accreditation. It offers a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs, and has established itself as a leading institution in higher education in Colombia.
world knowledge.Details: Icesi University offers 29 undergraduate programs, 1 Doctoral Program, 25 master's programs, and 21 medical-surgical specializations. It has five faculties: Administrative and Economic Sciences, Engineering, Law and Social Sciences, Natural Sciences, and Health Sciences. The university has received several accreditations, including AACSB, AMBA, and ABET. It also has international agreements with over 870 destinations worldwide, facilitating student exchange programs, internships, and short-term visits.

world knowledge.Name: Sani Abacha Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sani Abacha Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Kano, Kano State, Nigeria. It is named after General Sani Abacha, the deceased former military head of state.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted matches during the tournament.
Hosted matches during the tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface, multi-purpose stadium with a capacity of 16,000.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Kano Pillars F.C. and for hosting major international football events.
world knowledge.Details: During the 2017 NPFL season, Kano Pillars drew an average home attendance of 10,000, the highest ever recorded in the Nigerian league. The stadium is owned by the Nigerian Government.

world knowledge.Name: Memphis Pyramid
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Base sides of 591 feet (180 m), height of 321 feet (98 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Memphis Pyramid, originally conceived in 1954 by artist Mark C. Hartz, was built as a symbol for the city of Memphis, playing on its namesake in Egypt. It opened in 1991 as a multi-purpose arena but transitioned into a Bass Pro Shops megastore in 2015 after years of inactivity.

Major_Events.Description: The Grateful Dead performed two concerts at the arena on April 1 and 2, 1995.
Singer Mary J. Blige performed during her Share My World Tour.

Major_Events.Event: WWF St. Valentine's Day Massacre: In Your House
Major_Events.Description: A WWF pay-per-view event featuring Big Show's WWE debut.
Both bands played sold-out concerts at the arena.
A major professional boxing event where Lewis won by knockout.
A boxing match where Tyson won by knockout in the first round.
A concert commemorating the 25th anniversary of Elvis Presley's death.

Major_Events.Event: Church of God in Christ international holy convocations
Major_Events.Description: Annual religious gatherings held at the arena.

Major_Events.Event: Bob Seger & The Silver Bullet Band concert
Major_Events.Description: Reputed to be the last concert ever held in the Pyramid.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Pyramid-shaped structure with bronze glass-glazed exterior, designed by Rosser Fabrap International. Renovations by O.T. Marshall Architects included seismic retrofitting and retail adaptations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pyramid is a symbol of Memphis, reflecting its namesake in Egypt. It has hosted major sports, music, and entertainment events, and its transformation into a retail and recreational hub has revitalized the area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a multi-purpose arena, now a Bass Pro Shops megastore with retail, hotel, restaurants, and recreational facilities.
world knowledge.Details: The Pyramid includes a 100-room hotel (Big Cypress Lodge), an archery range, a shooting range, a laser arcade, a bowling alley, a saltwater aquarium, and an observation deck. It also features the tallest freestanding elevator in America and over 600,000 gallons of water features.

world knowledge.Name: Sokoine University of Agriculture
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sokoine University of Agriculture (SUA) traces its roots to 1965 when it emerged as a program of the then-international University of East Africa. When that was dissolved in 1970, the Tanzanian agriculture program fell under the purview of the University of Dar es Salaam. Finally, it was spun off as a university in its own right in 1984. The university was established on 1 July 1984 by Parliamentary Act No. 6 of 1984 and currently operates under the Universities Act No. 7 of 2005 and SUA Charter and Rules of 2007.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Sokoine University of Agriculture
Major_Events.Description: Sokoine University of Agriculture was established on 1 July 1984 by Parliamentary Act No. 6 of 1984.

Major_Events.Event: Separation from University of Dar es Salaam
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Agriculture, Forestry and Veterinary Sciences was separated from the University of Dar es Salaam to form Sokoine University of Agriculture.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SUA is named after Edward Sokoine, Tanzania's second prime minister, and plays a crucial role in agricultural education and research in Tanzania.
world knowledge.Details: SUA has five campuses and offers bachelor's, master's, and PhDs in various fields centered around agriculture. The university has four mandates: Training, Research, Consultancy, and Outreach. It also operates the Sokoine National Agricultural Library, which serves as the Tanzania National Agricultural Library.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Bicentenario de La Florida
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1986, the stadium was demolished and rebuilt in 2008 to comply with FIFA standards for the 2008 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup. The new stadium was inaugurated on November 12, 2008.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was selected as a venue, leading to its demolition and reconstruction to meet FIFA standards.
A music concert held at the stadium.
Part of their The Second Coming Tour.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Judson & Olivos Architects, the stadium features FieldTurf surface and has a capacity of 12,000 for football and 25,000 for concerts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports and entertainment venue in Santiago, hosting major football matches and concerts by international artists.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for football matches and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by Ilustre Municipalidad de la Florida and operated by Audax Italiano. It was renovated from January 28, 2008, to September 26, 2008, with a construction cost of CLP $11,804,156,704.

world knowledge.Name: Grandfather Mountain
world knowledge.Location: Avery / Caldwell / Watauga counties, North Carolina, U.S.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 5,946 ft (1,812 m) elevation, 2,444 ft (745 m) prominence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grandfather Mountain is a mountain, a non-profit attraction, and a North Carolina state park near Linville, North Carolina. It was privately owned until 2008 when the state purchased 2,600 acres for $12 million, adding it to the North Carolina State Park system. The Morton family established the Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation to continue operating the travel destination as an educational nature park.

Major_Events.Description: North Carolina purchased 2,600 acres of Grandfather Mountain from the Morton family for $12 million, adding it to the state park system.

Major_Events.Event: Grand opening of first office area
Major_Events.Description: The park celebrated the grand opening of its first office area, located 3 miles from the Profile Trail-head on NC 105.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural mountain terrain with rugged character, hidden caves, significant cliffs, and a mile-high swinging bridge built in 1952.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grandfather Mountain is culturally significant for its natural beauty, ecological diversity, and as the site of the Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, which celebrate Scottish ancestry. It is also a popular tourist attraction with historical and recreational value.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Nature preserve, tourist attraction, and state park

Details.Wildlife_habitats: Black bear, river otters, cougars, bald eagles, and elk
Details.Notable_features: Mile High Swinging Bridge, Nature Museum, Animal Habitats, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games
Details.Climate: Humid continental climate (Dfb) with cold, snowy winters and mild summers
Details.Nearby_parks: Multiple state parks and forests within 30 miles

world knowledge.Name: Tobu World Square
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tobu World Square is a theme park featuring over a hundred 1:25 scale models of famous buildings, including UNESCO-designated World Cultural and Heritage Sites, complete with 140,000 1:25 miniature people.

Major_Events.Description: A 1:25 scale model of the Tokyo Skytree was unveiled at the park. This is 26 metres tall, taller than the 19.95-metre replica of the New York World Trade Center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park contains detailed 1:25 scale models of famous buildings from around the world, including UNESCO World Cultural and Heritage Sites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park showcases miniature replicas of globally recognized landmarks, offering a unique cultural and educational experience.
world knowledge.Details: Between November and March the park has extended opening hours. During this time approximately 1.4 million red and blue lights illuminate the park. Buildings such as the Tokyo Sky Tree, the Eiffel Tower and the Duomo di Milano are lit up with LEDs and spotlights. There is also a 150-meter tunnel of lights that leads up to the Alpine Roses Park.

world knowledge.Name: Shere Hills
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shere Hills are a range of undulating hills and rock formations on the Jos Plateau, situated about 10 km east of the Jos metropolis, the capital of Plateau State in the Middle Belt region of Nigeria.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Shere Hills are the highest point of the Jos Plateau and form the third highest point in Nigeria.
world knowledge.Details: The Shere Hills have numerous high peaks, with the highest peak reaching a height of about 1,776 metres or 5,827 feet above sea level. They are the highest point of the Jos Plateau and form the third highest point in Nigeria after Chappal Waddi on the Mambilla Plateau averaging about 2,419 metres or 7,936 feet above sea level and Mount Dimlang (Vogel peak) on the Shebshi Mountains reaching a height of about 2,042 metres or 6,699 feet above sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Hàn River Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Longest span: 201 meters (659 ft) (x2), Clearance below: 25 meters (82 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hàn River Bridge is a cable-stayed swing bridge in Da Nang, Vietnam. It was built by the people of Da Nang and is the only swing bridge in Vietnam. The bridge plays a significant role in the cityscape of Da Nang. Shortly after its completion, the contractor, Phạm Minh Thông, was arrested for embezzlement and bribery, but the case was eventually dropped.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed and opened to the public in 2000.
Phạm Minh Thông, the contractor, was arrested for stealing money from the project and for bribery. However, the case was eventually dropped.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed swing bridge made of concrete. It has a unique design that allows it to swing on its axis to let shipping traffic pass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important part of Da Nang's cityscape and is the only swing bridge in Vietnam. It symbolizes the city's development and modernization.
world knowledge.Details: In the middle of the night, traffic is stopped from crossing the bridge, and it swings on its axis to allow shipping traffic to pass along the river. The bridge is brightly lit at night.

world knowledge.Name: University of Asmara
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Asmara (UoA) was a public university in Asmara, Eritrea. It was founded in 1958 by the 'Piae Madres Nigritiae' (Comboni Sisters) as the 'Catholic College of Santa Famiglia'. Initially, it provided education primarily for the Italian population. Over time, it evolved, offering Associate Diploma programs in arts, commerce, and sciences. The university underwent several reorganizations and was eventually closed in 2006, with its programs and accreditations transferred to other institutions like the Eritrea Institute of Technology.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Asmara was founded by the 'Piae Madres Nigritiae' (Comboni Sisters) as the 'Catholic College of Santa Famiglia'.
The university underwent a major reorganization under a new president, leading to an increase in student enrollment and the introduction of new courses and programs.

Students protested against the Ministry of Education's call for them to take leave during the rainy seasons and retrain as census workers. The conflict escalated, leading to violence against students.
The University of Asmara closed its doors in 2006, with its programs and accreditations transferred to other institutions.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Asmara was Eritrea's first university, playing a crucial role in the country's educational development. It was a symbol of higher education and cultural exchange, particularly during its early years when it catered to the Italian population and later expanded to serve the local community.
world knowledge.Details: The university was initially founded to provide education for the Italian population, but it later expanded to serve the local Eritrean community. It underwent several reorganizations and was eventually closed in 2006, with its programs and accreditations transferred to other institutions. The closure has been attributed to its centralization of higher education, which hindered the diversification of the Eritrean education sector.

world knowledge.Name: Kharkiv International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kharkiv International Airport is the main airfield serving Kharkiv, Ukraine's second largest city. The old terminal was built in the 1950s in a neoclassical style. A new modern international terminal was constructed to comply with UEFA regulations for the 2012 UEFA European Football Championship, with the old building renovated to become a VIP terminal. Since 2013, the airport operates a CATII instrument landing system (ILS). As of 24 February 2022, all passenger flights have been suspended indefinitely due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Major_Events.Description: A new modern international terminal was built to comply with UEFA regulations for the 2012 UEFA European Football Championship.
All passenger flights were suspended indefinitely due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The old terminal was built in the 1950s in a neoclassical style. The new terminal is modern and was constructed to meet UEFA standards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kharkiv International Airport is a key transportation hub for Ukraine's second largest city and played a significant role during the 2012 UEFA European Football Championship.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is well served by municipal transport and is connected to the city's wider network of roads and railways via Aeroflotska Street and the M03 national trunk road. It operates a CATII instrument landing system (ILS).

world knowledge.Name: Kalyani Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Near Kalyani Lake, opposite Kalyani Sub Divisional Court Building, Kalyani, West Bengal, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kalyani Stadium is a prominent sports venue in Kalyani, West Bengal, India, serving as an alternative location to Kolkata for hosting football matches and other sporting events. It has been remodeled with a modern structure and added facilities.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the Durand Cup, one of the oldest football tournaments in India.
Hosted the IFA Shield, a prestigious football tournament in India.
Hosted the Santosh Trophy, a national football championship in India.
Hosted the SAFF U-15 Championship, an international youth football tournament.
Regularly hosts matches of the Calcutta Football League.
Hosted the U-17 Women's Championship, an international youth football tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a 5-storied gallery, floodlights for night matches, a grass surface, and a manual scoreboard. It also includes a swimming pool and a well-equipped gymnasium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kalyani Stadium is culturally significant as it hosts national and international football matches, serving as a home ground for prominent Kolkata-based clubs like Mohun Bagan A.C., East Bengal F.C., and Mohammedan S.C. It plays a vital role in promoting football in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports venue for football matches and other sporting events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is 10 minutes away from Kalyani railway station and 5 minutes away from Kalyani Silpanchal railway station. Public transport options include autos, totos, and buses. It is owned and operated by Kalyani Municipality.

world knowledge.Name: Invercargill Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Invercargill Airport, established in 1938 on reclaimed land from the Waihopai/New River Estuary, has evolved from a basic airstrip to a fully secured international airport. It faced challenges like flooding and has undergone significant upgrades, including a new terminal in 2016. It serves as a crucial link for the southernmost region of New Zealand and has handled various aircraft types over the decades.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inoperable for two months due to severe flooding.
A new terminal was opened, replacing the old structure to meet modern safety and operational standards.
Invercargill Airport was designated as a fully secured international airport, allowing for direct international flights.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern single-storey terminal with efficient use of space, constructed with local materials to reflect regional identity. It includes advanced passenger and baggage handling facilities, and a premium lounge for frequent flyers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Invercargill Airport is the southernmost controlled airport in the Commonwealth, serving as a vital transportation hub for the Southland region. It supports local tourism and provides essential connectivity for residents and businesses.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport providing domestic and international air services.
world knowledge.Details: Invercargill Airport has a 2,210-meter runway capable of handling aircraft up to the size of Boeing 737 and Airbus A320. It is used for regular domestic flights, occasional international services, and as a diversion airport for flights to and from Queenstown. The airport also supports Antarctic flight diversion training and has hosted military exercises.

world knowledge.Name: University of Western Australia
world knowledge.Address: 35 Stirling Highway, Crawley, Western Australia, 6009, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Western Australia (UWA) was established in 1911 by an act of the Parliament of Western Australia. It is the oldest university in Western Australia and the sixth-oldest in Australia. Originally located in Perth's city center, the university moved to its current Crawley campus in 1932. UWA is a member of the Group of Eight and has a strong focus on research and academic excellence.

Major_Events.Description: UWA was established by an act of the Parliament of Western Australia.
The university moved from its original location in Perth's city center to the current Crawley campus.
UWA introduced the Doctorate of Philosophy degree, awarding its first PhD in 1950.
UWA celebrated its 100th anniversary and announced a goal to be ranked among the top 50 research universities globally by 2050.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Crawley campus features coastal limestone and Donnybrook sandstone buildings, including the iconic Winthrop Hall with Romanesque Revival architecture. The campus also includes the New Fortune Theatre, a replica of the original Elizabethan Fortune Theatre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UWA is a leading research university in Australia and a member of the prestigious Group of Eight. It has played a significant role in the educational and cultural development of Western Australia. The university's cultural precinct hosts various performances and events, contributing to the local arts scene.

Details.Campus: Suburban and regional with multiple sites

world knowledge.Name: Stellenbosch University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stellenbosch University (SU) is a public research university situated in Stellenbosch, a town in the Western Cape province of South Africa. It is the oldest university in South Africa and the oldest extant university in Sub-Saharan Africa, which received full university status in 1918. The origin of the university can be traced back to the Stellenbosch Gymnasium, which was founded in 1864. It became the Stellenbosch College in 1881, was renamed Victoria College in 1887, and finally became Stellenbosch University in 1918.

Major_Events.Description: The precursor to Stellenbosch University, the Stellenbosch Gymnasium, was founded.
The institution was renamed Victoria College.
Victoria College was granted full university status and renamed Stellenbosch University.
Specialists at the university performed the first successful penis transplantation on a 21-year-old man.
Stellenbosch University was the first African university to sign the Berlin Declaration on Open Access to Knowledge in the Sciences and Humanities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university is organized across five campuses in the Western Cape, including suburban, urban, and rural areas. The campuses feature a mix of historical and modern buildings, with facilities such as the Danie Craven Stadium, Coetzenburg Centre, and the Stellenbosch University Botanical Garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stellenbosch University is culturally significant as the oldest university in South Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa. It has played a pivotal role in the development of education and research in the region. The university is also notable for its multilingual policy, promoting Afrikaans, English, and Xhosa, and its contributions to space sciences, including the design and manufacture of Africa's first microsatellite, SUNSAT.

Details.Motto: Latin: Pectora roborant cultus recti (English: A sound education strengthens the spirit)
Details.Language_Policy: Promotes multilingualism with instruction in Afrikaans and English, and use of Xhosa in various contexts.
Details.Sports_Facilities: Includes Danie Craven Stadium, swimming pools, Coetzenburg Centre, playing fields, gymnasium, and football complex.
Details.Student_Life: 34 residence halls, student societies, radio station (MFM), publications like Die Matie and Kampusnuus, and annual events like SU Woordfees.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Jerai
world knowledge.Area: Kuala Muda and Yan Districts, Kedah
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,217 m (3,993 ft) elevation, 1,184 m (3,885 ft) prominence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Jerai, formerly known as Kedah Peak, is a mountain in Kedah, Malaysia. It was once an island called Pulai Serai before the sea levels receded, forming it into a mountain. The Jerai Formation, part of an eponymous geological formation, correlates with the Matchinchang Formation in Langkawi. It is composed of fully metamorphosed sandstone and shale, consisting of argillite, arenite, and porphyry facies.

Major_Events.Description: First ascent by local Kedahans

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Inselberg mountain type, composed of metamorphosed sandstone and shale.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Jerai is known as the Hausberg of Sungai Petani and offers a wide-angle view of surrounding areas, including Penang Island and the rice fields of Yan District. It has historical significance as it was once an island and is part of the Jerai Formation.
world knowledge.Details: The summit of Jerai has been developed into a hill resort, providing tourists with panoramic views of the surrounding areas.

world knowledge.Name: M&D's
world knowledge.Historical_Background: M&D's Scotland's Theme Park is an amusement park that opened in 1996. It has undergone expansions and faced financial difficulties, including going into administration in 2020 before being purchased later that year.

Major_Events.Description: Six people were stranded on the Tornado roller coaster due to high winds activating safety systems.
Nine people were stranded 60 ft above the ground for eight hours due to a mechanical failure.
A teenage girl's leg was trapped between a barrier and a splash back, causing a serious injury.
Three people were injured when the ride slipped on its track, and later a woman and three teenagers were stranded at the highest point.
Eight people were rescued after the ride became stuck 20 ft above the ground.
The roller coaster derailed, injuring ten people after hitting the main structure and coming to rest on the walkway.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features various rides and attractions, including roller coasters, water rides, fairground rides, an arcade, a theatre, Cosmic Bowl, and an indoor tropical house, Amazonia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: M&D's is known as "Scotland's Theme Park" and is a popular entertainment destination in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The park has 41 attractions, including 2 roller coasters and 1 water ride. It has undergone expansions and changes in rides over the years, including the removal and replacement of some attractions. The park's slogan is "Scotland's Theme Park" and its website is www.scotlandsthemepark.com.

world knowledge.Name: Botanical Garden of Curitiba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jardim Botânico de Curitiba, also known as the Botanical Garden of Curitiba, is a prominent park in Curitiba, the capital of the state of Paraná in southern Brazil. It was established in 1991 and designed in the style of French formal gardens. It houses a portion of the Federal University of Paraná campus and is a key tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features expansive gardens with fountains, waterfalls, and lakes. The principal greenhouse spans 458 square meters and is constructed in an Art Nouveau style with a modern metallic framework, resembling the mid-19th century Crystal Palace in London. The Botanical Museum is a wooden structure accessible via a wooden bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The garden is a key tourist attraction and landmark within Curitiba. It houses the Botanic Museum with a national reference collection of native flora and attracts researchers globally. It also includes the Museum of Franz Krajcberg, dedicated to the Polish-Brazilian artist known for his environmental advocacy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The main purpose of the landmark is to serve as a botanical garden and a center for botanical research and education.
world knowledge.Details: The garden includes a diverse array of botanical species from the Atlantic Forests of eastern Brazil. The Museum of Franz Krajcberg features multimedia classrooms, a 60-seat auditorium, and exhibition spaces showcasing works donated by visual artists. The Botanical Museum of Curitiba is home to the fourth-largest herbarium in Brazil. The surrounding area includes a pond with aquatic life, a lake, an auditorium, a library, exhibition spaces, a theater, tennis courts, and a cycle track.

world knowledge.Name: Zamora Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of Zamora is a Catholic cathedral in Zamora, in Castile and León, Spain, located above the right bank of the Duero. It remains surrounded by its old walls and gates. Built between 1151 and 1174, it is one of the finest examples of Spanish Romanesque architecture. The church was built under Bishop Esteban of the Diocese of Zamora, under the patronage of Alfonso VII and his sister, Sancha Raimúndez. The cathedral was consecrated in 1174 by bishop Esteban, and works continued under his successor Guillermo (1176–1192), including the transept. The cloister and the bell tower date to the first half of the 13th century.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by bishop Esteban.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building, in Romanesque style, is on the Latin cross plan; it has a nave and two aisles, a short transept and three semicircular apses. The transept is covered by barrel vault, the aisles by groin vault, and the nave by cross vault in late-Romanesque or Proto-Gothic style. Over the transept is the dome-tower, featuring 16 side narrow and tall semicircular windows enclosed in and between four turrets. These support two domes, an external one with a slightly pointed top, and an interior one with semicircular shape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cathedral of Zamora is one of the finest examples of Spanish Romanesque architecture and is a symbol of the city. Its dome is particularly notable and has inspired similar structures in other churches of the Duero valley.
world knowledge.Details: The Cathedral Museum, in the 17th century cloister, is notable particularly for its fine Flemish tapestries of the 15th–17th centuries depicting scenes from the Trojan War, Hannibal's Italian campaign, and the life of Tarquin the Etruscan king of Rome. Another treasure is a Late Gothic monstrance of 1515.

world knowledge.Name: Bondi Beach
world knowledge.Area: Eastern Suburbs, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bondi Beach is a popular beach and surrounding suburb in Sydney, originally inhabited by Aboriginal Australian peoples. The name 'Bondi' is derived from the Dharawal language. European settlement began in the early 19th century, and the beach became a public reserve in 1882. It has since grown into a major tourist destination and cultural hub.

Major_Events.Description: Five people drowned and over 250 were rescued after large waves struck the beach, pulling people into the sea.
Bondi Beach hosted the beach volleyball competition, with a temporary 10,000-seat stadium and other facilities constructed for the event.

Major_Events.Event: Guinness World Record for largest swimsuit photo shoot
Major_Events.Description: 1,010 women wearing bikinis participated in the photo shoot at Bondi Beach.
Bondi Beach was closed by the Government of New South Wales due to exceeding outdoor-gathering limits during the coronavirus pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Bondi Beach features a mix of architectural styles, including the Italianate, Federation, and Free Classical elements seen in the Hotel Bondi. The Bondi Pavilion is a community cultural centre with a theatre, gallery, and other facilities, reflecting early 20th-century design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bondi Beach is culturally significant as one of Australia's most famous beaches, a symbol of surf culture, and a hub for multicultural migration. It has been the setting for TV series like 'Bondi Rescue' and 'Bondi Vet,' and hosts numerous festivals and events. The beach is also historically important for its Aboriginal heritage and its role in the development of surf lifesaving.
Notable_Visitors: Peter James Paul Millhouse (Jhyimy 'Two Hats' Mhiyles)

Details.Hazards: The southern end has a rip current known as the 'Backpackers' Rip,' rated 7/10 for hazard. The northern end is gentler, rated 4/10.
Details.Wildlife: Pods of whales, dolphins, and occasionally fairy penguins can be seen during migration months.
Details.Facilities: Bondi Beach has Wi-Fi, a skate park, surf lifesaving clubs, and an underwater shark net. It is also connected by an Oceanway to other beaches.
Details.Heritage_Listings: Bondi Beach was added to the Australian National Heritage List in 2008.

world knowledge.Name: Mokolo Dam Nature Reserve
world knowledge.Address: 32 km south of Lephalale, Limpopo, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mokolo Dam Nature Reserve is a protected area of bushveld in the Limpopo province, South Africa. It almost surrounds the Mokolo Dam on the Mokolo River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The reserve is part of the Waterberg Biosphere and is significant for its biodiversity, including various bird species and fish.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and recreation (water sports, bird watching, fishing)
world knowledge.Details: The reserve features both sourveld and sweetveld. Attractions include water sports, birds, and fish such as largemouth bass, bream, carp, and catfish. Visitors must be cautious of crocodiles. Nearby landmarks include Marakele National Park and Lapalala Game Reserve.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Ghana
world knowledge.Address: 2 Barnes Road, Accra, Greater Accra, Ghana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Ghana, established in 1957, is the largest and oldest of the six museums under the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board (GMMB). It originated from the anthropology museum at Achimota College, founded by Charles Thurstan Shaw, and its collection was later donated to the University of Ghana in 1940. The museum opened on 5 March 1957 as part of Ghana's independence celebrations, with the official opening performed by Princess Marina. The museum closed in 2015 for restoration and reopened in 2022.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the National Museum of Ghana
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened on 5 March 1957 as part of Ghana's independence celebrations, with the official opening performed by Princess Marina.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration of the National Museum of Ghana
Major_Events.Description: The museum closed in 2015 for restoration and reopened in 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The structure was built by the Gold Coast Public Works Department with the help of British architects Denys Lasdun and Lindsay Drake. It is made out of concrete, with windows set in saw-toothed angles ninety degrees to the outer wall. A low saucer-shaped aluminium dome above an ambulatory leads to the rest of the building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it was part of Nkrumah's campaign to raise nationalism and awareness among the citizens of the newly unified nation. It hosts a collection of approximately 10,000+ objects, including archaeology, ethnography, and fine art, with a focus on Akan origin and African history.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes objects of archaeology, ethnography, and fine art, with a focus on Akan origin. It also features a library, a conservation laboratory, and an education hall. In the 1990s, exhibits about the history of the transatlantic slave trade were added.

world knowledge.Name: Millau Viaduct
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 2,460 m (8,070 ft), Width: 32.05 m (105.2 ft), Height: 343 m (1,125 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Millau Viaduct was constructed to alleviate traffic congestion near Millau in the Tarn valley, especially during holiday seasons. The project began with discussions in 1987, and after extensive planning and design competitions, construction started in 2001. The bridge was inaugurated on 14 December 2004 and opened to traffic on 16 December 2004.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was formally inaugurated on 14 December 2004.
The bridge was opened to traffic on 16 December 2004.
The bridge received the 2006 Outstanding Structure Award from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Millau Viaduct is a multiple-span cable-stayed bridge made of concrete and steel. It features seven masts, each 87 m (285 ft) high, with eleven pairs of cable-stays supporting the road deck. The deck is 2,460 m (8,070 ft) long and 32 m (105 ft) wide, with an inverse airfoil shape for stability in strong winds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Millau Viaduct is considered one of the greatest engineering achievements of modern times. It has significantly improved traffic flow and reduced journey times between Paris and southern France, as well as Spain. The bridge is also a symbol of architectural and engineering innovation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries four lanes of the A75 autoroute, providing a high-speed route across the Tarn valley.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge's construction cost approximately €394 million. It was financed by the Eiffage group, which operates the bridge under a concession to collect tolls for up to 75 years. The bridge is equipped with extensive monitoring systems to ensure structural integrity and safety.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Champlain
world knowledge.Address: New York / Vermont in the United States ; and Quebec in Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Champlain is a natural freshwater lake in North America, named after the French explorer Samuel de Champlain who encountered it in July 1609. It has served as a strategic waterway during colonial times, the Revolutionary War, and the War of 1812. The lake was briefly designated as the sixth Great Lake in 1998.

Major_Events.Description: A significant naval engagement during the Revolutionary War where American forces delayed British invasion.
A decisive battle during the War of 1812 that ended British invasions of the northern states.
Lake Champlain was briefly declared the sixth Great Lake, enabling neighboring states to access additional federal funds.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Champlain is culturally significant as a historical border between indigenous nations, a strategic military waterway, and a natural resource for recreation and drinking water. It is also famous for the legend of Champ, a lake monster.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural freshwater lake serving as a recreational, ecological, and historical resource.

Details.Primary_inflows: Otter Creek, Winooski River, Missisquoi River, Poultney River, Lamoille River, Ausable River, Chazy River, Boquet River, Saranac River, La Chute River
Details.Islands: 80 (Grand Isle, North Hero, Isle La Motte)
Details.Pollution_control: Lake Champlain Basin Program aims to reduce phosphorus inputs, toxic contamination, and non-native species.

world knowledge.Name: University of Sarajevo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Sarajevo is the largest and oldest university in Bosnia and Herzegovina, tracing its origins to 1537 as an Islamic madrasa. It was officially established in its modern form on December 2, 1949. The university has undergone several phases of development, including significant expansion during the Austro-Hungarian rule, post-World War II, and post-Bosnian War reconstruction. It has faced challenges such as war devastation and academic reorganization but remains a prestigious institution in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Sarajevo was officially established in its modern form on December 2, 1949, with the appointment of its first rector.
The university suffered significant damage during the Bosnian War and the siege of Sarajevo but managed to retain its continuity of work and life.
The university entered a phase of physical and academic renewal and reconstruction after the Bosnian War.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Sarajevo is a symbol of resilience and intellectual resistance, having survived war and devastation. It is a promoter of traditional, historical, cultural, scientific, and artistic values of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Southeastern Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Sarajevo comprises 32 faculties, academies, and colleges, further subdivided into 6 academic groups. It enjoys partnerships with over 120 universities in Europe, the US, Canada, and the Middle East. The university is affiliated with the European University Association and is working towards becoming a contemporary university of European origins.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Lodge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Royal Lodge has been the site of homes since the 17th century, with the present structure dating from the 19th century. It was expanded in the 1930s for the Duke of York, the future King George VI. The house has served as a residence for various members of the British royal family, including Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother and Prince Andrew, Duke of York. The Royal Chapel of All Saints was built on the grounds in the 1820s.

Major_Events.Description: The house was expanded with wings added on each flank for the Duke and Duchess of York (later King George VI and Queen Elizabeth).
Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother used the house as one of her country retreats until her death in 2002.
Prince Andrew, Duke of York, was granted a 75-year lease agreement by the Crown Estate, requiring significant refurbishments.
Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother died at Royal Lodge, with her daughter Queen Elizabeth II and niece Margaret Rhodes by her side.
The wedding reception for Princess Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank was held at Royal Lodge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The central section consists of three storeys, with two-storey wings, totalling about 30 rooms, including seven bedrooms. The house features a saloon (48 by 30 by 30 feet) and an original conservatory. The grounds include the miniature cottage Y Bwthyn Bach. The architectural style has evolved from Queen Anne style to cottage orné with thatched roofs, verandas, and a conservatory.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Royal Lodge is a Grade II listed building with significant historical ties to the British royal family. It has been a residence for multiple generations of royals and has hosted important events, including the wedding reception of Princess Eugenie. The house and its grounds reflect the architectural and cultural trends of their respective periods.
world knowledge.Details: The property is part of the Crown Estate and includes the main house, a Gardener's Cottage, the Chapel Lodge, six Lodge Cottages, and police security accommodation. The lease agreement for Prince Andrew specifies that the property cannot be commercially exploited and may only be assigned to his widow or daughters. The open market value of the property was estimated at least £30 million as of January 2022.

world knowledge.Name: Nathia Gali Beach
world knowledge.Location: Southern Pakistan, along the Arabian Sea coast
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Karachi was founded in 1729 as the fortified village of Kolachi. It grew in importance under British rule in the 19th century, becoming a major seaport and railway hub. After Pakistan's independence in 1947, Karachi became the national capital until 1959. It has since evolved into Pakistan's largest city and premier industrial and financial center, with a diverse population and significant cultural and economic influence.

Major_Events.Description: Karachi was founded as the fortified village of Kolachi by Sindhi Baniyas.
The British East India Company captured Karachi, transforming it into a major seaport and transportation hub.
Karachi became the capital of Pakistan, leading to a massive influx of Muslim refugees and a dramatic shift in demographics.
A controversial military operation aimed at restoring peace in Karachi by targeting political and criminal elements.
A crackdown by Pakistan Rangers to reduce violent crime and terrorism in the city.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Karachi features a mix of architectural styles, including neo-Gothic (Frere Hall, Empress Market), Indo-Saracenic (Mohatta Palace, Hindu Gymkhana), and modern Islamic (Masjid-e-Tooba, Quaid's Mausoleum). The city also has contemporary skyscrapers like the MCB Tower and Habib Bank Plaza.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Karachi is Pakistan's most cosmopolitan and diverse city, serving as the country's economic and cultural hub. It is known for its vibrant arts scene, culinary diversity, and historical landmarks. The city has played a pivotal role in Pakistan's history, from its founding to its development as a global city.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Karachi serves as Pakistan's premier industrial, financial, and transportation center. It is home to the country's largest ports, stock exchange, and numerous multinational corporations.

Details.Climate: Tropical semi-arid (Köppen: BSh)
Details.Major_Industries: Textiles, cement, steel, chemicals, food processing

world knowledge.Name: National Theater and Concert Hall
world knowledge.Address: 10048 Chung-Shan South Road, Zhongzheng, Taipei, Taiwan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Theater and Concert Hall were completed in 1987 as part of a memorial plaza project authorized by the Kuomintang government following the death of Chiang Kai-shek in 1975. The project cost TWD 7.4 billion. The buildings were designed to combine modern functionality with traditional Chinese palace architecture. They were officially opened as venues of the 'National Chiang Kai-shek Cultural Center' in October 1987.

Major_Events.Description: Launched Taiwanese society on a quick but peaceful transition from one-party authoritarian rule to pluralistic democracy.
The Ministry of Education consolidated the governing bodies of the National Theater and Concert Hall with those of the National Symphony Orchestra, National Chinese Orchestra, and National Chorus.
Commemorated the twentieth anniversary of the halls, featuring visits by renowned artists and ensembles.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The buildings combine modern functionality with traditional Chinese palace architecture. The interior facilities, stage lighting, and acoustics were designed with contributions from international companies like G+H Company of Germany and Philips of the Netherlands. The National Concert Hall features a large pipe organ by Flentrop Orgelbouw, which was the largest in Asia at the time of its installation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theater and Concert Hall are among the first major modern performing arts facilities in Asia. They play a significant role in Taiwan's cultural and diplomatic life, hosting top international artists and dignitaries. The venues are central to Taiwan's performing arts scene and have been a backdrop for key historical events, including the transition to democracy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venues hosting theater, concerts, and other cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The National Theater and Concert Hall host a wide range of events, including international festivals, local performances, and outdoor events on Liberty Square. The venues also house art galleries, libraries, shops, and restaurants. The National Theater includes a Performing Arts Library and publication offices for Taiwan's Performing Arts Review.

world knowledge.Name: Ebell of Los Angeles
world knowledge.Address: 743 S. Lucerne Boulevard, Los Angeles, California
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Site 160 by 450 feet (49 m × 137 m), surrounding a 65-by-120-foot (20 m × 37 m) patio area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ebell of Los Angeles is a women-led and women-centered nonprofit housed in a historic campus. It was formed in 1894 based on the principles of Adrian Ebell, a pioneer in women's education. The organization moved to its current location in 1927, designed by architect Sumner P. Hunt. The Ebell has been a hub for arts, learning, and service, hosting numerous performances, lectures, and community events.

Major_Events.Description: The Ebell was the site of aviator Amelia Earhart's last public appearance before attempting her around-the-world flight during which she disappeared.
Judy Garland was discovered at the Ebell while performing as Baby Frances Gumm.

Major_Events.Event: West coast premiere of The Desert Song
Major_Events.Description: The Wilshire Ebell Theater opened to the public with the west coast premiere of Sigmund Romberg's musical The Desert Song.
A major restoration of the Ebell complex commenced, including re-covering the theater's seats, refitting the stage, and installing new sound and lighting systems.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in an Italian Renaissance style with plaster facing and Italian clay tile roofing. The complex includes a 1,300-seat auditorium, a two-story clubhouse with a lounge, art salon, dining room, and a tile-roofed colonnade walkway and fountain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ebell of Los Angeles is culturally significant as a women-led organization promoting arts, education, and community service. It has hosted performances by world leaders and top artists, and is a designated historic structure at local, state, and national levels.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To uplift the Los Angeles community through arts, learning, and service.
world knowledge.Details: The Ebell complex includes numerous performance spaces, meeting rooms, and classrooms. The Wilshire Ebell Theatre is known for its acoustics and Barton pipe organ. The building has been designated as a historic structure with NRHP reference No. 94000401 and LAHCM No. 250.

world knowledge.Name: Morant Point Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Morant Point Lighthouse is on the easternmost tip of Jamaica and is the oldest lighthouse on the island. Erected in 1841 by Kru men from Africa, it is the first cast iron lighthouse built in the Western Hemisphere. It was designed by Alexander Gordon and built by George Grove. The lighthouse is listed by the Jamaica National Heritage Trust as a historic monument and is maintained by the Port Authority of Jamaica.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first lit in 1841.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse consists of a 30 m (100 ft) iron tube, cast in London in 1841, with a diameter of 5 m (18 ft) at the base and 3 m (11 ft) at the cap. It has a lantern and gallery, painted with red and white horizontal bands. A semicircular masonry wall has been built around the seaward side of the base to protect against surf during hurricanes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the oldest lighthouse on the island and the first cast iron lighthouse built in the Western Hemisphere. It is of considerable interest to historians of industrial technology and is listed as a national monument by the Jamaica National Heritage Trust.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse has a focal height of 35 metres (115 ft) and a range of 22 nmi (41 km; 25 mi). Its characteristic is Fl (3) W 20s.

world knowledge.Name: Great Falls Park
world knowledge.Address: Fairfax County, Virginia, USA. Nearest city: McLean, Virginia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Great Falls Park is a small National Park Service site in Virginia, United States. It is situated along the banks of the Potomac River and is a disconnected but integral part of the George Washington Memorial Parkway. The park features the Great Falls of the Potomac River and the remains of the Patowmack Canal, the first canal in the United States that used locks to raise and lower boats. The canal, partially funded by George Washington, began operating in 1785. The park also contains Native American petroglyphs and the ruins of the small town of Matildaville. Between 1906 and 1932, an amusement park operated at the falls. The park was transferred to the NPS in 1966.

Major_Events.Description: The Patowmack Canal, the first canal in the United States that used locks to raise and lower boats, began operating to give small barges the opportunity to skirt around the falls.
The canal was abandoned due to the completion of the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal on the opposite side of the river and the oncoming age of railroads.
An amusement park operated at the falls, featuring picnic grounds, a dance pavilion, and a carousel.
The park was transferred to the National Park Service from the Northern Virginia Parks system.
The carousel that operated between 1954 and 1972 was destroyed by a flood caused by Hurricane Agnes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features the remains of the Patowmack Canal, including stonework and wooden lock gates. Stonemason marks found on the stones are unique to each artisan and are identical to some found in foundation stones of the White House and the U.S. Capitol. The park also has viewing platforms, a visitor center, and hiking trails.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Great Falls Park is culturally and historically significant due to its association with George Washington, the Patowmack Canal (a Civil Engineering Landmark and Virginia Historic Landmark), and the presence of Native American petroglyphs. It also represents early engineering and transportation developments in the United States.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The park serves as a recreational area offering picnic grounds, hiking trails, rock climbing, and scenic views of the Great Falls of the Potomac River.
world knowledge.Details: The park has several viewing platforms overlooking the falls, 15 miles of hiking trails, and a visitor center. The falls total 76 feet over a series of major cascades and are rated Class 5-6 Whitewater. Entry into the water above the falls from the Virginia side is illegal. The park is open only during daylight hours and has a $20 entrance fee per car. On busy weekends, parking may fill up early, causing delays and temporary closures. The park does not permit camping.

world knowledge.Name: Appuldurcombe House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Appuldurcombe House began as a priory in 1100, later becoming a convent and then the Elizabethan home of the Leigh family. The large Tudor mansion was bequeathed in 1690 to Sir Robert Worsley, who began planning a replacement. The present house was begun in 1702 by architect John James. The house was greatly extended in the 1770s by Sir Richard Worsley, who commissioned Capability Brown to design the ornamental grounds. The house has seen various uses, including as a hotel, a school, and a monastic residence. It was damaged during World War II and is now mainly a shell, though partially restored and open to the public.

Major_Events.Description: The present house was begun in 1702 by architect John James.
The house was greatly extended by Sir Richard Worsley, who also commissioned Capability Brown to design the ornamental grounds.
A German Luftwaffe Dornier Do 217 dropped a mine near the house, causing significant damage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: English Baroque style, designed by John James. The house features a front section that has been re-roofed and glazed, with a small part of the interior recreated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Appuldurcombe House is historically significant as a large 18th-century English Baroque country house.
