It is also known as one of the most haunted places on the Isle of Wight, with frequent tales and claimed sightings of ghosts and other supernatural phenomena.
world knowledge.Details: The house is managed by English Heritage and is open to the public. It is known for its ghost walks held weekly during the summer holidays. As of January 2016, the house and surrounding estate were for sale for £4.75 million.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Chala
world knowledge.Location: Straddles the border between Tanzania and Kenya in east Africa
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 4.2 square kilometres (1.6 sq mi) to 4.5 square kilometres (1.7 sq mi)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Chala, also known as Lake Challa, is a crater lake that straddles the border between Kenya and Tanzania. The lake formed approximately 250,000 years ago. It is east of Mount Kilimanjaro, 8 kilometres north of Taveta, Kenya, and 55 kilometres east of Rombo District. The lake is surrounded by a steep crater rim with a maximum height of 170 metres.

Major_Events.Description: An 18 year old British woman was killed by a relatively small Nile crocodile while swimming at night in the lake. The Kenya Police Service said that the lake was 'infested' with crocodiles, while the Kenya Wildlife Service said, 'Crocodiles are found in Lake Chala and it is not regarded as safe to swim at all.'

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Chala is culturally significant due to its unique formation as a crater lake and its location straddling the border between Kenya and Tanzania. It is also home to the critically endangered Lake Chala tilapia (Oreochromis hunteri), which is found nowhere else in the world.
world knowledge.Details: Lake Chala's average annual rainfall is about 565 millimetres. The lake surface has an average annual evaporation of near 1,735 millimetres. Approximately 80 percent of the lake's inflow comes from groundwater, which is derived mostly from rainfall in the montane forest zone of Mount Kilimanjaro at an elevation of 1,800 to 2,800 metres. It takes about 3 months for groundwater to reach the lake. The groundwater flowed into the lake at an estimated annual volume of 8,390,000 cubic metres from 1964 through 1977. The only native fish in this lake is the Lake Chala tilapia (Oreochromis hunteri), which is considered critically endangered by the IUCN and now greatly outnumbered by other tilapia species that have been introduced to Lake Chala.

world knowledge.Name: Olbrich Botanical Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1952 and named for its founder, Michael Olbrich, the gardens are owned and operated jointly by the City of Madison Parks and the non-profit Olbrich Botanical Society.

Major_Events.Description: A 10,000-square-foot greenhouse housing over 750 plants representing over 70 families and over 550 different species and cultivars.

A gift to the University of Wisconsin–Madison from the Thai Chapter of the Wisconsin Alumni Association and the government of Thailand through its king, Bhumibol Adulyadej. It is one of only six sala outside of Thailand and one of two in the United States.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gardens feature several distinct areas including a Sunken Garden (traditional English garden with a reflecting pool), Thai Garden (with a Thai sala and reflecting pool), Rock Garden (simulating a mountain slope), Meadow Garden (perennial grasses and wildflowers), Herb Garden (medicinal, dye, and kitchen herbs), Rose Garden (over 700 varieties of roses), and the Bolz Conservatory (a glass pyramid greenhouse with tropical plants and birds).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gardens are a significant cultural and educational resource, featuring unique elements like the Thai sala, which is one of only six outside Thailand. The gardens also showcase diverse plant species and ecosystems, serving as a hub for horticultural education and conservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Botanical garden and conservatory for education, conservation, and public enjoyment.
world knowledge.Details: The Bolz Conservatory maintains a temperature between 65 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit (18-26°C) and a relative humidity of 70% or above. It houses species of birds including canaries, waxbills, and quail, as well as a koi pond. Admission to the gardens is free, but a small fee is charged for entry into the conservatory. Daily hours are 10am-6pm.

world knowledge.Name: Glynde Place
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Glynde Place is an Elizabethan Manor House built in 1569 by the forebears of the Viscounts Hampden. It is situated in the South Downs National Park and has been the family home of the Viscounts Hampden. The estate historically included large landholdings across Sussex, Hertfordshire, Essex, Cambridge, and Suffolk. The house underwent a major renovation from 2008 to 2013.

Major_Events.Description: Organized by the 7th Viscount Hampden and funded by the sale of one of the estate's paintings.
Held in the grounds of Glynde Place.
Takes place every summer in the grounds of Glynde Place.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Elizabethan architectural style, Grade I listed building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Glynde Place is a historically significant Elizabethan Manor House and a Grade I listed building, reflecting the architectural and cultural heritage of the Elizabethan era. It is also the family home of the Viscounts Hampden.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Country house and family residence, now open to the public for tours.
world knowledge.Details: The adjacent church was built in the eighteenth century. The gardens are Grade II* listed and open to the public. The estate was historically valued at £24,753 a year in the late 19th century.

world knowledge.Name: Rutherfurd Hall
world knowledge.Area: Allamuchy Township, Warren County, New Jersey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rutherfurd Hall is a historic house and estate built in 1902. It was the estate of Winthrop Chanler Rutherfurd and his wives Alice Morton Rutherfurd and Lucy Mercer Rutherfurd. The property represents the country life movement of the early 20th century, where wealthy individuals built large estates near major cities. After Alice's death, the property was donated to the Congregation of the Daughters of Divine Charity in 1948, who used it as a retreat, training center, and rest home for retired nuns. The property was later sold to the State of New Jersey and the Allamuchy Township School District in 2007.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The property was added as a historic district to the National Register of Historic Places for its significance in architecture and social history.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by President Franklin Delano Roosevelt
Major_Events.Description: President Franklin Delano Roosevelt visited the estate to meet with Lucy Rutherfurd.

Major_Events.Event: Property donated to the Daughters of Divine Charity
Major_Events.Description: The property was donated to the Congregation of the Daughters of Divine Charity, who used it as a retreat and training center, later as a rest home for retired nuns.

Major_Events.Event: Property sold to the State of New Jersey and Allamuchy Township School District
Major_Events.Description: The property was sold to the State of New Jersey and the Allamuchy Township School District.
The State of New Jersey awarded $50,000 to the school district for a preservation project at Rutherfurd Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tudor Revival brick and stone structure occupying three floors, with approximately 38 rooms (expanded to 50 rooms). Designed by Whitney Warren, with grounds designed by the Olmsted Brothers, featuring gardens, a boathouse, swimming beach, hydroelectric powerhouse, 9-hole golf course, and kennels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rutherfurd Hall is one of the last extant large country estates in New Jersey from the early 20th century, representing the country life movement. It is significant for its architecture, social history, and connection to notable figures like President Franklin Delano Roosevelt.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Community education and cultural facility, also rented for private functions.
world knowledge.Details: The property is located next to Allamuchy Mountain State Park. It is owned and managed by the Allamuchy Township School District, with support from the Rutherfurd Hall Foundation. The general information phone number is (908) 852–1894.

world knowledge.Name: Oaxaca International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oaxaca International Airport, officially known as Aeropuerto Internacional Xoxocotlán, is an international airport located in the municipality of Santa Cruz Xoxocotlán, a southern suburb of Oaxaca City, Mexico. It handles national and international air traffic for the Metropolitan Area of Oaxaca and a significant portion of the State of Oaxaca. The airport is operated by Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR) and derives its name from the Nahuatl word "xocotl," meaning "sour or sweet and sour fruit."
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The passenger terminal is a single-story building with a total area of 7,548 square metres. It accommodates both arrivals and departures for domestic and international flights. The departures area features a check-in area, a security checkpoint, and a departure concourse with a VIP lounge, snack bars, souvenir shops, and eight gates. The arrivals section includes customs and immigration facilities, a baggage claim area, and an arrivals hall with car rental services, taxi stands, snack bars, and souvenir shops.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is culturally significant as it serves as a major gateway for tourism and commerce in the Oaxaca region, contributing to the local economy and cultural exchange.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as the hub for the regional airline Aerotucán and offers passenger services for both domestic and international destinations. It also hosts military facilities for the Mexican Army, logistics and courier companies, and supports various aviation-related activities. The airport has a single runway designated as 01/19, which is 2,450 metres in length with an asphalt surface. The commercial aviation apron provides nine stands mainly designed for narrow-body aircraft, and the general aviation apron offers parking for fixed-wing aircraft and heliports for private aviation. The airport has the capacity to handle up to 22 operations per hour. Air Force Base No. 15 (BAM-15) is situated in the southern part of the airport, featuring an apron measuring 5,950 square metres, two hangars, and military facilities for Squadron 103, which currently operates Bell 212 aircraft.

world knowledge.Name: Miyazaki Airport
world knowledge.Address: 3.2 km south southeast of Miyazaki city, Miyazaki Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Miyazaki Airport opened in 1943 as an Imperial Japanese Navy base during World War II. It was a major base for kamikaze units beginning in February 1945, sending a total of 47 aircraft on suicide missions during operations such as the Battle of Okinawa.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was initially opened as an Imperial Japanese Navy base.
The airport served as a major base for kamikaze units, sending 47 aircraft on suicide missions during operations like the Battle of Okinawa.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway with asphalt concrete surface, 2,500 m in length and 8,202 ft in width.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Miyazaki Airport is significant for its historical role during World War II as a naval base and kamikaze launch site. It now serves as a key transportation hub for Miyazaki Prefecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving Miyazaki Prefecture and functioning as a hub for Solaseed Air.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is also known as Miyazaki Bougainvillea Airport. It is connected to various locations by bus and taxi, and has a railway line, the Miyazaki Kūkō Line, which connects the airport with the city center of Miyazaki and northern cities of the prefecture. The second floor houses the head office of Solaseed Air.

world knowledge.Name: Château Haut-Brion
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Château Haut-Brion is a French wine estate rated as a Premier Grand Cru Classé (First Growth). It is located in Pessac, just outside Bordeaux. The estate dates back to 1525 when Jean de Pontac married Jeanne de Bellon, who brought the land in her dowry. The vineyard's first vines were planted in 1423, and it became renowned in the 17th century under the Pontac family. It was classified as a First Growth in 1855 and has been owned by the Dillon family since 1935.

Major_Events.Description: The earliest documented cultivation of vines on the property.
Construction of the château was initiated by Jean de Pontac.
Haut-Brion wine was served at the court of King Charles II of England.
Haut-Brion was classified as a First Growth in the Bordeaux Wine Official Classification.
American banker Clarence Dillon purchased the estate.
The 1970 vintage of Haut-Brion ranked fourth in a historic wine competition.
Domaine Clarence Dillon acquired Château La Mission Haut-Brion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The château features traditional French architecture with a focus on functionality for wine production. The estate includes vineyards, fermentation vats, and aging cellars. The bottle design, introduced in 1958, emulates old decanter models.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Château Haut-Brion is culturally significant as one of the oldest and most prestigious wine estates in Bordeaux. It was the first estate to be named in English records (1660) and played a key role in establishing the reputation of Bordeaux wines internationally. Its wines have been enjoyed by historical figures such as Thomas Jefferson and Samuel Pepys.

Details.Varietals: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc
Wines_Produced: Le Clarence de Haut-Brion (second red wine)
La Clarté de Haut-Brion (second white wine)

world knowledge.Name: Guangxiang Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Yuecheng District of Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Guangxiang Bridge is a historic stone arch bridge originally built during the Eastern Jin Dynasty (317-420). It has been rebuilt numerous times due to war and natural disasters, with the current version completed in 1982.

Major_Events.Event: Listed as Major National Historical and Cultural Site
Major_Events.Description: On 6 May 2013, it was listed among the seventh batch of 'Major National Historical and Cultural Sites in Zhejiang' by the State Council of China.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stone arch bridge with a total length of 30.8 metres (101 ft), width of 4.9 metres (16 ft), and height of 5.5 metres (18 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named after the nearby Guangxiang Temple and is recognized as a Major National Historical and Cultural Site in Zhejiang.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Pedestrian and bicycle crossing over the Old City River
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is named after Guangxiang Temple (光相寺) near the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Astroland
world knowledge.Address: 1000 Surf Avenue, Coney Island, Brooklyn, New York City, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Astroland was a 3.1-acre amusement park in Coney Island, Brooklyn, New York City that opened in 1962. It was initially built as a 'space-age' theme park but later became known for its nostalgic and kitsch experiences. The park was developed by Dewey Albert and his associates through a series of acquisitions and featured rides like the Astrotower, Cape Canaveral Satellite Jet, Mercury Capsule Skyride, and Neptune Diving Bells. The park also operated the famous Cyclone roller coaster. Astroland closed on September 7, 2008, and was replaced by Luna Park in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: An early-morning fire wiped out much of the park, but it was rebuilt.
Astroland was sold by the Albert family for US $30 million to Thor Equities, which announced plans to redevelop the area as a $1.5 billion year-round resort. The plans never came to fruition.
Astroland closed on September 7, 2008, after no agreement could be reached between the Albert family and Thor Equities.
The Astrotower was demolished due to concerns about its structural integrity. The demolition began on July 3, 2013, and was completed by July 6, 2013.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Astroland featured a mix of 'space-age' themed rides and traditional carnival attractions. Notable rides included the Astrotower gyro tower, Cape Canaveral Satellite Jet, Mercury Capsule Skyride, and Neptune Diving Bells. The park also housed the famous Cyclone roller coaster.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Astroland was a significant part of Coney Island's amusement park history, offering a unique blend of futuristic and nostalgic experiences. It was a popular destination for locals and tourists alike and played a role in the cultural and recreational life of New York City.
world knowledge.Details: Astroland was replaced by Luna Park in 2010. The music video for Counting Crows' 'Big Yellow Taxi' was partly filmed at Astroland, and the official music video for Air Supply's 'Even the Nights Are Better' was mostly filmed at Astroland.

image_name: Estadi Municipal de Futbol de L'Hospitalet

world knowledge.Name: Estadi Municipal de Futbol de L'Hospitalet
world knowledge.Address: Feixa Llarga district, L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Catalonia, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built to host the baseball tournament at the 1992 Summer Olympics, the stadium was designed by Spanish architect Mario Correa. It was later reconverted to a football stadium in 1999. The venue, opened in July 1991 and seating 2500, was one of two used for baseball competitions at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, including the finals. During the 1992 games, seating was expanded to just under 7000.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was one of two venues used for baseball competitions at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, including the finals.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Spanish architect Mario Correa, the stadium features a grass surface and has a capacity of 6,740 seated spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it was originally built for the 1992 Summer Olympics and later repurposed for football, serving as the home of CE L'Hospitalet. It is part of a larger municipal sports complex known as Feixa Llarga.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is located approximately 700 metres from the Hospital de Bellvitge metro station, on line L1 of the Barcelona Metro. It is part of a municipal sports complex known as Feixa Llarga, which includes other facilities such as a rugby field and a sports center. The Estadi Municipal de L'Hospitalet should not be confused with the Camp Municipal de la Feixa Llarga, which is located a few meters away within the same sports complex.

world knowledge.Name: Octávio Frias de Oliveira Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Jornalista Roberto Marinho Avenue to Marginal Pinheiros, São Paulo, Brazil
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,600 metres (5,200 ft) total length for two roadways; 16 metres (52 ft) width for each roadway; 138 metres (453 ft) height (X-shaped tower)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Octavio Frias de Oliveira Bridge, locally known as 'Ponte Estaiada', is a cable-stayed bridge over the Pinheiros River in São Paulo, Brazil. It was opened in May 2008 and named after businessman Octavio Frias de Oliveira. The bridge was conceived by the São Paulo Municipality City Hall and designed by engineers of 'Enescil Engenharia e Projetos Ltda'. Construction was carried out by 'Construtora OAS Ltda' and cost R$233 million, including illumination.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was inaugurated on 10 May 2008.
Thieves stole 6 kilometres of wire worth R$200,000 (US$117,000).
Vandals broke into the bridge's control room and destroyed the panels.
Vandals stole 94 of the 142 searchlights of the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a cable-stayed bridge with two oppositely curved roadways suspended from a single concrete 'X'-shaped tower. It is made of concrete sustained by stainless steel cables, coated with polyethylene resistant to sunlight. The bridge is unique for having two curved roadways supported by a single pylon and features interlaced stay cables creating a crisscrossing geometric arrangement not found in any other cable-stayed bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an iconic landmark in São Paulo, known for its unique 'X'-shaped tower and innovative design. It is often illuminated for special occasions and used in automobile advertisements. The bridge represents modern engineering and architectural achievement in Brazil.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge connects the west end of Jornalista Roberto Marinho Avenue to the riverside expressway Marginal Pinheiros in the south area of São Paulo, facilitating vehicular traffic.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is lit up at the end of December with color effects like those on a Christmas tree. It is only accessible to motor vehicles, and viewing it up close requires intentional effort. The Pinheiros River it crosses is polluted. The bridge has faced several vandalism incidents, including theft of wires and searchlights.

world knowledge.Name: City Hall, Cork
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The City Hall, Cork is a civic building that houses the administrative headquarters of Cork City Council. It was commissioned to replace the old City Hall, which was destroyed in 1920 during the Irish War of Independence. The current building was designed by Alfred Jones and Stephen Kelly and constructed by John Sisk & Son. The foundation stone was laid by Éamon de Valera in 1932, and the building was officially opened in 1936. The cost was provided by the British Government as a gesture of reconciliation.

Major_Events.Event: Destruction of the old City Hall
Major_Events.Description: The old City Hall was destroyed by the Black and Tans during the Irish War of Independence as part of the Burning of Cork.
The foundation stone of the new City Hall building was laid by Éamon de Valera.

Major_Events.Event: First meeting in the new hall
Major_Events.Description: Cork Corporation held a meeting in the new hall for the first time when the Council Chambers were first opened.
The City Hall was officially opened by Éamon de Valera.
A major extension was completed by ABK Architects and opened that year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is described as one of the city's "monumental classical buildings" and features mosaics of the city arms on the floor of the entrance hall and the tympanum above the stage of the concert hall. A limestone plinth bearing the arms was erected outside the building in 1985.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The City Hall is significant as the administrative headquarters of Cork City Council and as a symbol of the city's resilience and reconstruction following its destruction during the Irish War of Independence.
world knowledge.Details: The cost of the new building was provided by the British Government in the 1930s as a gesture of reconciliation. A major extension was completed in 2007.

world knowledge.Name: University of the Philippines Tacloban
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of the Philippines Tacloban is an autonomous unit of the University of the Philippines system, established on May 23, 1973, in Tacloban, Philippines. It was initially recognized as a regional unit of the system and later placed under the administrative supervision of the University of the Philippines Visayas. The college sustained severe damage and lost members during Typhoon Yolanda in 2013. In 2023, it was elevated to an autonomous college of the UP System.

Major_Events.Description: The UP College Tacloban was established and recognized as a regional unit of the University of the Philippines system.
The college sustained severe damage and lost one employee and four students during Typhoon Yolanda.
UP Tacloban was elevated from being a campus of UP Visayas to an autonomous unit of the University of the Philippines System.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UP Tacloban is a significant educational institution in the Philippines, known for its high standards of education and competitive admission process. It plays a crucial role in the academic and cultural development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: UP Tacloban is divided into four academic divisions and houses three research and public service offices. It offers several highly regarded programs, including BS Accountancy, BS Biology, BS Management, and BS Computer Science. The college has a vibrant student body with over 2000 students and 48 student organizations.

world knowledge.Name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) is the largest art museum in Canada by gallery space. Founded in 1860, it is the oldest art museum in Canada. The museum was established by the Art Association of Montreal to encourage the appreciation of fine arts. It has grown significantly over the years, with multiple expansions and pavilions added to its campus.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the Art Gallery of the Art Association of Montreal
Major_Events.Description: The first building in Canada constructed specifically for housing an art collection was inaugurated by the Governor General of Canada, Sir John Douglas Sutherland Campbell.

The largest art theft in Canadian history occurred at the museum, with 18 paintings and other items stolen, including works by Rembrandt and Delacroix. Most of the stolen items have never been recovered.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the Michal and Renata Hornstein Pavilion for Peace
Major_Events.Description: The inauguration of this pavilion expanded the museum's campus, making it the eighteenth largest art museum in North America.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of five pavilions, including a 1912 Beaux Arts building designed by William Sutherland Maxwell and Edward Maxwell, and the modernist Jean-Noël Desmarais Pavilion designed by Moshe Safdie. The architecture ranges from classical to modernist styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The MMFA is a major cultural institution in Canada, housing a vast collection of art from various periods and regions. It plays a significant role in promoting art appreciation and education in Canada.
Notable_Visitors: Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
world knowledge.Details: The museum's permanent collection includes approximately 44,000 works. It is affiliated with several international and national museum associations, including the Canadian Museums Association and the International Group of Organizers of Large-scale Exhibitions.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Morelos
world knowledge.Address: Periférico Independencia, Independencia sector, near the base of Cerro del Quinceo, northwest Morelia, Michoacán, Mexico
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Field size: 110 m × 70 m (360 ft × 230 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Morelos was built in 1989 to replace Estadio Venustiano Carranza as the home of first division side Atlético Morelia. Initially planned as a site for the 1986 FIFA World Cup, construction was delayed due to foundation issues. The stadium was later financed privately by ticket sales and handed over to the state of Michoacán upon completion. It has hosted various events, including football matches, concerts, and religious gatherings.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was one of the venues for the 2011 FIFA U-17 World Cup.
Pope Francis spoke to an estimated 50,000 young people at the stadium during his first visit to Mexico.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has an irregular shape with areas behind the goals having one level and 32 rows, while the sides have 4 levels (one grandstand, one other seating area, and two box areas) and 49 stands. The surface is grass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after José María Morelos y Pavón, a hero of the Mexican War of Independence. It serves as a significant venue for sports, cultural, and religious events in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 35,000 and is currently the home of Atlético Morelia in the Liga de Expansión MX. It previously hosted Monarcas Morelia in the top division of Mexican football. The construction cost was US$20,000,000.00, and the architect was David Fuentes Arrona.

world knowledge.Name: University of Nouakchott Al Aasriya
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Nouakchott Al Aasriya was created in July 2016 from the merger of the University of Science, Technology and Medicine and the University of Nouakchott, which was established in 1981.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Nouakchott Al Aasriya was formed by merging the University of Science, Technology and Medicine with the University of Nouakchott.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a major educational institution in Mauritania, contributing to the academic and professional development of its students.
world knowledge.Details: The university has more than 12,000 students and operates across 5 campuses. Its website is http://www.una.mr.

world knowledge.Name: Arusha International Conference Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Arusha International Conference Centre (AICC) is the leading conference venue in Tanzania, fully owned by the Tanzanian Government and operated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs without subsidies. It was opened in 1977 and was formerly known as the EAC Headquarters.

Major_Events.Description: Simba Hall was expanded to accommodate 1,313 delegates from its former capacity of 1,000 for the 8th Sullivan Summit.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The AICC is a key venue for international conferences, workshops, seminars, and committee meetings in Tanzania, equipped with Simultaneous Interpretation Systems (SIS) that can handle up to 12 languages.
world knowledge.Details: The AICC has a total of 10 meeting rooms with a seating capacity of 10 to 1000 delegates. Major tenants include Simba Hall, which was expanded for the 8th Sullivan Summit.

world knowledge.Name: Guemar Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Guemar Airport is the airport for El Oued, Algeria. It was opened to civil aviation in 1955.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has two runways: Runway 13/31 is 3000 x 45 meters and Runway 02/20 is 2000 x 30 meters. Both runways have asphalt surfaces.
world knowledge.Details: Located near the community of Guemar, it lies about 20 kilometres north of El Oued. IATA: ELU, ICAO: DAUO.

world knowledge.Name: Musée de Picardie
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée de Picardie is the main museum of Amiens and Picardy, founded as the Musée Napoléon in 1802. The current building was purpose-built as a regional museum between 1855 and 1867, designed by architects Henri Parent and Arthur-Stanislas Diet. It was the first building in France constructed exclusively for the conservation and exhibition of artworks.

Major_Events.Description: The museum's collection, including the painting 'Diana and Endymion' by Jérôme-Martin Langlois, was evacuated to the Louvre for safekeeping. Some works, like the mentioned painting, were lost or destroyed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Second Empire style building designed by Henri Parent and Arthur-Stanislas Diet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses one of the largest regional collections in France, ranging from prehistory to the 19th century. It is a prototype for other French regional museums and features significant artworks, including frescoes by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and exhibition of artworks and historical artifacts.

Collections: Archaeological artifacts from prehistory to the 19th century
Mummified remains of an Egyptian woman named Setjaïmengaou (7th century BC)
Puys d'Amiens (Gothic art from Amiens Cathedral)
Paintings by French and foreign artists from the 17th to 20th centuries
Details.Annex: Hôtel de Berny, located near Amiens Cathedral
Notable_Artworks: Frescoes 'Peace and War' (1861) and 'Work and Rest' (1863) by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes
Painting 'Diana and Endymion' by Jérôme-Martin Langlois (1822, possibly in private collection of Madonna)

world knowledge.Name: Yunnan Provincial Museum
world knowledge.Address: No.6393, Guangfu Road, Guandu District, Kunming, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1951, the Yunnan Provincial Museum is a cultural heritage museum in Kunming, China. It houses an exhibition centered on Yunnan's ethnic minorities, as well as a collection of artifacts from tomb excavations at Jinning on the southern rim of Lake Dian.

Major_Events.Description: The new museum located at No.6393 of Guangfu Road in Guandu District officially opened its door to the public on May 18, 2015.

Several hundred paintings, calligraphy, and other artifacts that once belonged to Gao Yunhuai, a former Nationalist military officer, were confiscated by the Red Guards at the start of the Cultural Revolution.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its collection of artifacts related to Yunnan's ethnic minorities and historical relics from tomb excavations at Jinning. It also holds confiscated artifacts from the Cultural Revolution period.
world knowledge.Details: The old museum is on Wuyi Road in Wuhua District. As of 2001, the museum's curator was Li Kunsheng.

world knowledge.Name: Broken Chair
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 12 metres (39 feet) high, 5.5 tons of wood
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Broken Chair is a monumental sculpture in wood designed by Swiss artist Daniel Berset, and constructed by carpenter Louis Genève. It symbolises opposition to land mines and cluster bombs, and acts as a reminder to politicians and diplomats visiting Geneva. The sculpture was erected by Handicap International in front of the main entrance to the Palace of Nations in Geneva on 18 August 1997, where it was intended to remain for three months, until the signing of the Ottawa Treaty in December 1997 in Ottawa. Following ratification by 40 countries, the Treaty became effective as an instrument of international law on 1 March 1999. The failure of many countries to sign the Treaty and the strong public support for the sculpture caused it to be left in place until 2005, when it was removed to allow extensive remodeling of the Place des Nations. After completion of the work, it was reinstalled in the same place in front of the United Nations Office at Geneva on 26 February 2007.

Major_Events.Description: The sculpture was erected by Handicap International in front of the main entrance to the Palace of Nations in Geneva on 18 August 1997, where it was intended to remain for three months, until the signing of the Ottawa Treaty in December 1997 in Ottawa.

The sculpture was reinstalled in the same place in front of the United Nations Office at Geneva on 26 February 2007, officially dedicated by Handicap International to support the signature of an international treaty on a ban on cluster munitions, which was signed in Oslo in December 2008.

The monument was the target of an act of vandalism by topless members of the Ukrainian feminist protest group Femen, in protest Russia’s war against Ukraine and what they see as the U.N.'s failure to stop the conflict. One of the protestors used a chainsaw to make cuts in one of the legs of the chair.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Monumental sculpture in wood, depicting a giant chair with a broken leg
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The sculpture symbolises opposition to land mines and cluster bombs, and acts as a reminder to politicians and diplomats visiting Geneva.
world knowledge.Details: The work was the property of the sculptor until 2004, when he transferred ownership to Handicap International. Giant chair sculptures by other artists include Chair in the US, and the temporary The Writer by Giancarlo Neri on Hampstead Heath in London.

world knowledge.Name: Canobie Lake Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Canobie Lake Park was founded as a trolley park in 1902 on the shore of Canobie Lake. It initially featured botanical gardens and few amusement rides. After the decline of trolley travel, the park was closed in 1929 but was revived in 1931 by Patrick J. Holland, who installed new attractions like the Yankee Cannonball roller coaster. The park has been family-owned since 1958 and remains one of only thirteen operating trolley parks in the U.S.

Major_Events.Description: Canobie Lake Park opened on August 23, 1902, as a trolley park for the Massachusetts Northeast Street Railway Company.
The park closed on St. Patrick's Day in 1929 due to declining popularity after the trolley era ended.
Patrick J. Holland purchased the park at auction, restored it, and reopened it in 1932 with new attractions and electricity.
The wooden roller coaster Yankee Cannonball was installed, later designated as an ACE Roller Coaster Landmark in 2013.
The Arrow Development-designed Canobie Corkscrew, a looping steel roller coaster, was relocated from Old Chicago amusement park.
The park began hosting ScrEEEmfest, a Halloween event featuring haunted attractions and rides.
Untamed, a Gerstlauer Euro-Fighter coaster, was added as the park's first new roller coaster since 1987.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of classic and modern amusement rides, including wooden and steel roller coasters, dark rides, flat rides, and water attractions. Notable structures include the historic Yankee Cannonball roller coaster and the Mine of Lost Souls dark ride.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Canobie Lake Park is one of the few remaining trolley parks in the U.S. and has inspired cultural works like Stephen King's novel 'Joyland.' It has also been a filming location for movies and TV shows. The park's Dancehall Theater has hosted legendary performers like Duke Ellington and Frank Sinatra.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates seasonally from May to October and features over 50 attractions, including 3 roller coasters and 4 water rides. It hosts annual events like ScrEEEmfest and live performances by celebrity impersonators. The park also includes a water park area, Castaway Island, with a lazy river and water slides.

world knowledge.Name: Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
world knowledge.Address: Thomas Ave. Arlington County, Virginia, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as Washington National Airport in 1941, it was renamed in 1998 to honor President Ronald Reagan. The airport was built to replace the inadequate Washington-Hoover Airport and has since undergone multiple expansions and renovations.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
Major_Events.Description: Congress passed legislation renaming the airport in honor of the 40th U.S. president, Ronald Reagan.
A Boeing 737 crashed into the Potomac River after takeoff due to ice and snow on the wings, killing 74 people on board and four on the ground.
A mid-air collision between an American Eagle regional jet and a U.S. Army helicopter resulted in the deaths of all 67 passengers and crew.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern architectural style with terminals designed by Charles M. Goodman and César Pelli. The airport features a mix of original 1941 structures and modern expansions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the closest airport to the U.S. capital, it serves as a key transportation hub for government officials, tourists, and business travelers. Its historical significance includes its role in early U.S. aviation and its renaming to honor President Reagan.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial, military, and general aviation needs.
world knowledge.Details: The airport operates under strict perimeter rules limiting nonstop flights to 1,250 miles, with exceptions. It is a hub for American Airlines and hosts Coast Guard Air Station Washington. Recent controversies include safety concerns and air traffic control incidents.

world knowledge.Name: Tiumpan Head Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Tiumpan Head, Isle of Lewis, Outer Hebrides, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The idea for the Tiumpan Head Lighthouse was long promoted but refused for many years by the Board of Trade. After a recommendation by the Western Highlands and Islands Commission to additionally keep a watch on illegal trawlers, it was approved in May 1879. The lighthouse was designed by David and Charles Stevenson and built by John Aitken, at an estimated cost of £9000. The light was first exhibited on 1 December 1900. The lighthouse was automated in 1985 and is monitored from Edinburgh.

Major_Events.Description: The light was first exhibited on 1 December 1900.
Elizabeth II visited the lighthouse with the young Duke of Cornwall and Princess Anne. The seven-year-old heir to the throne sounded the first blast on a new fog siren.
The lighthouse was automated and is now monitored from Edinburgh.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 21-meter tall cylindrical masonry tower with a balcony and lantern. It has a white tower, black lantern, and ochre trim. The structure was designed by David and Charles Stevenson.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a category C listed building and played a role in monitoring illegal trawlers in the area. It also has historical significance due to its royal visit in 1956.
world knowledge.Details: The former keepers' accommodation is now home to kennels and a cattery. The fog signal was discontinued in 1984, and the fog horn building was demolished. The lighthouse has a focal height of 55 meters and a range of 25 nautical miles. Its light characteristic is Fl (2) W 15s.

world knowledge.Name: Rahmat International Wildlife Museum & Gallery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rahmat International Wildlife Museum & Gallery is a natural history museum in Medan, Indonesia. The museum displays collections of various wildlife from the smallest to the largest according to the habitat. Its founder, Rahmat Shah, is a fan of sport hunting and the conservation of nature. Through the museum, he invites visitors to better understand the diversity of wildlife that exist in the world and their importance.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was inaugurated on May 14, 1999.
The museum was renovated on November 28, 2013.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it promotes the understanding and conservation of wildlife diversity globally.
world knowledge.Details: The founder, Rahmat Shah, has traveled around various parts of the world to study the concept of conservation adopted by many countries in order to prevent extinction and increase wildlife populations and their habitats that remain stable throughout the period.

world knowledge.Name: University of Edinburgh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Edinburgh, founded in 1583, is one of Scotland's four ancient universities and the sixth-oldest university in the English-speaking world. It played a crucial role in the Scottish Enlightenment, contributing to Edinburgh's reputation as a leading intellectual centre, often referred to as the 'Athens of the North'.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Edinburgh was officially opened in 1583 after being founded by the town council under the authority of a royal charter from King James VI.
The university was at the centre of the Scottish Enlightenment, producing and attracting key figures such as David Hume, Adam Smith, and Joseph Black.
The Edinburgh Seven were the first group of matriculated undergraduate female students at any British university, studying medicine at the University of Edinburgh.
This act gave the university full authority over its own affairs, establishing governing bodies including a university court and a general council.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university occupies five main campuses in Edinburgh, including many buildings of historical and architectural significance, such as Old College and New College.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Edinburgh is culturally and historically significant due to its role in the Scottish Enlightenment, its contributions to science, literature, and philosophy, and its status as one of the world's leading research institutions.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Edinburgh is a member of several prestigious university associations, including the Russell Group, Coimbra Group, and Universitas 21. It has produced numerous notable alumni, including Charles Darwin, Alexander Graham Bell, and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. The university is also known for its significant contributions to medical and scientific research.

world knowledge.Name: Corcovado National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Corcovado National Park was established on October 24, 1975, to protect the largest primary forest on the American Pacific coastline and one of the few remaining sizable areas of lowland tropical forests in the world. The park is part of the Osa Conservation Area and is the largest park in Costa Rica, covering about a third of the Osa Peninsula. Historically, the area faced threats from logging, mining, and land development, which led to significant environmental degradation. The park was created in response to petitions from researchers and conservationists, and it has since become a crucial site for biodiversity conservation.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established to protect the area from logging and mining activities, which were causing significant environmental damage.
The Costa Rican government decided to evict illegal miners from the park to protect its biodiversity.

Major_Events.Event: Introduction of certified guides for visitors
Major_Events.Description: As of February 1, 2014, all visitors to Corcovado National Park must be accompanied by certified guides to ensure safety and conservation efforts.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Corcovado National Park is culturally and historically significant as it represents one of the last remaining areas of lowland tropical forest in the world. It is a critical habitat for numerous endangered species and plays a vital role in global biodiversity conservation. The park also reflects the ongoing struggle between conservation efforts and local livelihoods, highlighting the importance of sustainable development and community engagement in environmental protection.
world knowledge.Details: Corcovado National Park is home to a wide range of wildlife, including endangered species like Baird's tapir, harpy eagles, jaguars, and four species of sea turtles. The park features diverse vegetation zones, including montane forest, cloud forest, and mangrove, which support over 500 tree species. Despite its protected status, the park faces ongoing threats from illegal mining, hunting, and tourism. Conservation efforts are being made by various organizations and the Costa Rican government to protect the park's ecosystems and promote sustainable tourism.

world knowledge.Name: Windermere
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Windermere, also known as Lake Windermere, is the largest lake in England by length, area, and volume. It is a ribbon lake in Cumbria, England, and part of the Lake District. The lake was formed after the Last Glacial Maximum during the retreat of the British and Irish Ice Sheet between 17,000 and 14,700 years ago. It has been a popular holiday destination since the arrival of the Kendal and Windermere Railway's branch line in 1847. The Freshwater Biological Association was established on the shore of Windermere in 1929, contributing to early work on lake ecology and freshwater biology.

Major_Events.Description: Sir Henry Segrave broke the world water speed record on Windermere in his boat, Miss England II, at an average speed of 158.94 km/h (98.76 mph). On the third run, the boat capsized, resulting in the death of Segrave's mechanic, Victor Helliwell, and Segrave himself later died of his injuries.

The Lake District National Park Authority introduced a bylaw setting a 10-knot speed limit for all powered craft on the lake, with three existing 6-knot speed limits for all craft on the upper, lower, and middle sections of the lake. The new speed limits were enforced from 29 March 2005.

Windermere hosted the inaugural Great North Swim, a one-mile open water swim involving 2,200 swimmers. The event has since grown, with 6,000 swimmers participating in 2009, making it the largest open water swim in the UK.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Windermere is culturally significant as a popular holiday destination and for its contributions to freshwater biology and lake ecology. It has inspired numerous literary works, including those by William Wordsworth, Arthur Ransome, and Oscar Wilde. The lake is also associated with the 'Windermere Boys,' a group of 300 Jewish boys who survived Auschwitz and settled near Windermere in 1945.
world knowledge.Details: Windermere is the largest lake in England by length, area, and volume. It is a popular destination for boating, swimming, and other recreational activities. The lake is surrounded by picturesque landscapes and has been a source of inspiration for many poets and writers. It also plays a significant role in freshwater biology research, with the Freshwater Biological Association established on its shores in 1929.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Bouges
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Bouges is an 18th-century mansion built in 1765, likely by Ange-Jacques Gabriel, on lands acquired by Charles-François Leblanc de Manarval. It was modeled after the Petit Trianon at the Palace of Versailles. In 1818, it became the property of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord, who later gave it to his niece Dorothée de Courlande. The château was later owned by Tunisian general Mahmoud Benaiad and then purchased in 1917 by Henry Viguier and his wife, who restored it. The Viguiers left the house and its furniture to the French state in 1968.

Major_Events.Description: The château was built, likely by Ange-Jacques Gabriel, modeled after the Petit Trianon at the Palace of Versailles.
The château became the property of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord, who later gave it to his niece Dorothée de Courlande.
Henry Viguier and his wife purchased the château, restored it, and later donated it to the French state in 1968.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 18th-century mansion modeled after the Petit Trianon at the Palace of Versailles, featuring a park with landscape and formal French gardens, an arboretum, floral gardens, and large greenhouses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The château is classified as a monument historique, and its gardens are listed among the Notable Gardens of France by the Ministry of Culture. It is a significant example of 18th-century architecture and landscape design.
world knowledge.Details: The château and park were used as location scenes in the film 'Le Colonel Chabert' with Gérard Depardieu and Fanny Ardant. The property includes large stables later used as garages by the last owners.

world knowledge.Name: Marsden Point Oil Refinery
world knowledge.Address: Marsden Point, Whangārei, Northland, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Marsden Point Oil Refinery was the only significant oil refinery in New Zealand, operating from 1964 to 2022. It was owned and operated by the New Zealand Refining Company. The refinery was shut down in 2022 and dismantled. The point was named after Samuel Marsden. The refinery was initially built to meet increasing demand for petrol and petroleum products, with construction beginning in 1962 and officially opening in 1964. It underwent a major expansion in the 1980s as part of the Think Big policy, which significantly increased its capacity but also led to financial challenges.

Major_Events.Description: The refinery was officially opened on 30 May 1964, with an initial capacity of 52000 barrels a day.

A major expansion of the refinery began in 1981, including the addition of a hydrocracker and a 170-kilometre pipeline to transport petroleum products to Wiri, south Auckland. The project was completed in May 1986, two years behind schedule and at a final cost of $1.84 billion.
The refinery was shut down in April 2022, with the last crude oil shipment offloaded on 8 March 2022. The refinery was subsequently dismantled.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The refinery was a large industrial complex with various processing units, including a hydrocracker and a 170-kilometre pipeline. It was designed to handle a medium-sour blend of crude oil, nearly all of which was imported.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Marsden Point Oil Refinery was significant as the only major oil refinery in New Zealand, supplying 70% of the country's refined oil needs. It played a crucial role in the country's energy infrastructure and was a key part of the Think Big policy in the 1980s, which aimed to boost New Zealand's industrial capacity.
world knowledge.Details: The refinery used a medium-sour blend of crude oil, nearly all of which was imported. Most crude oil produced in New Zealand is light-sweet and is exported to refineries in Australia. The 168-kilometre underground Refinery-Auckland Pipeline (RAP) connected Marsden Point to the Wiri Oil Terminal in Auckland. The pipeline transported petrol, diesel, and jet fuel at up to 400,000 litres per hour. After its shutdown, Channel Infrastructure plans to use the site as an energy precinct.

image_name: Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan Airport

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan Airport
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Dutch colonial era before Indonesian independence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan International Airport began its new operational phase on 6 August 1997, with a new building and runway structure, replacing the old structure on the same site. The airport was initially used mainly for the Royal Dutch/Shell's activities in the Balikpapan area. It became public and commercial after its management was handed over to Direktorat Jenderal Perhubungan Udara of Republic Indonesia in 1960. The airport was managed by Perum Angkasa Pura I (PT Angkasa Pura I on present day) due to Government Regulation (PP) No.1 on 9 January 1987. The airport had been renovated twice from 1991 to 1997.

Major_Events.Description: The new terminal was tested on 22 March 2014 with a capacity of 10 million passengers per year. It covers an area of 110,000 square meters (1,200,000 square feet) with a Rp2 trillion ($178 million) investment.
The new terminal formally opened on 15 September 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a new terminal covering 110,000 square meters (1,200,000 square feet) with 74 check-in counters, 8 conveyor belts, 140,900 square meters (1,517,000 square feet) apron, and a multi-story parking building with 2,300 parking lots.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is the third busiest airport in Kalimantan and was named the second-best in service in the world for airports with annual handling capacity of 5 million to 15 million passengers in 2018 by Airports Council International.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving the city of Balikpapan and adjacent areas of East Kalimantan.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is equipped with a water recycling plant, 11 trunk alleys, air condition control of energy efficiency, and has significant energy consumption and waste production issues. Baggage theft has been a common issue at the airport.

world knowledge.Name: Srikantadatta Narasimha Raja Wadeyar Ground
world knowledge.Address: Manasagangotri campus, University of Mysore, Mysore, Karnataka
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The ground was constructed by the University of Mysore and inaugurated on 20 July 1993. It was later upgraded to a stadium in 1996/1997. The Karnataka State Cricket Association entered into a 20-year agreement with the university in 1997 to develop and maintain the ground.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted a game between Denmark women and Pakistan women.
Final match between Mumbai and Karnataka, which Mumbai won by 6 runs.
India v South Africa from 16–19 November 2014.
Pakistan v Denmark on 10 December 1997.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features Bermuda Grass and has a seating capacity of about 15,000. It has a pavilion complex constructed in 2007.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is an important venue for cricket in Karnataka, hosting various tournaments and matches. It is the second home ground for the Karnataka Cricket Team after the M.Chinnaswamy Stadium.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is known for its pitch, which is most suitable for batsmen but also provides assistance to bowlers with its pace and bounce. It has hosted various tournaments such as Karnataka Premier League, Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Vinoo Mankad Trophy, Cooch Behar Trophy, and CK Nayudu Trophy. The ground has notable records including the highest score of 619/8 dec by Karnataka vs Vidarbha and the highest individual score of 257 by CM Gautam vs Vidarbha.

world knowledge.Name: Martkopi monastery
world knowledge.Location: Martkopi, Gardabani Municipality, Kvemo Kartli, Georgia
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Martkopi, some 25 km east of Tbilisi
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 6th century, with structures from 17th to 19th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Martkopi monastery of the Deity is a Georgian Orthodox monastery with history dating back to stylite practices in the 6th century, linked with St. Anton, one of the Thirteen Assyrian Fathers. Most extant structures are from the 17th to the 19th century. The monastery is inscribed on the list of the Immovable Cultural Monuments of National Significance of Georgia.

Major_Events.Event: Became the seat of the bishop of Rustavi
Major_Events.Description: After Rustavi was destroyed in an invasion by Berke, ruler of the Mongol Golden Horde.
During the Georgian campaigns of Timur.
The monastery was fortified with a wall of 1,400 m length equipped with firing ports.
After the Persian-Georgian forces defeated the Ottoman troops, Nader Shah visited the monastery and donated money and presents.
Due to marauding Lesgian inroads, the bishop transferred his residence and parish to the village of Martkopi.
The church's dome and eastern wall collapsed.
The main church was rebuilt and frescoed by Russian painter Mikhail Troshchinsky in 1856.
Kyrion II, Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, was found shot in his own cell.
The monastery was closed down and the church building was converted into an orphanage and later into a recreational facility.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration to the Georgian Orthodox Church
Major_Events.Description: The monastery was restored to the Georgian Orthodox Church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery complex consists of the main dome church, a bell-tower, the Monk Anton's Pillar, and various other structures. The main church was rebuilt in the mid-19th century. The bell-tower, constructed in 1699, is similar to other contemporaneous bell-towers in Georgia with some Persianate flavor. The Monk Anton's Pillar, a tower rising to 30 metres, is believed to have served as a stylite hermitage.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The monastery is culturally and historically important due to its association with St. Anton, its role as a bishop's seat, its architectural features, and its status as a national cultural monument.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery complex is situated on the wooded southern slopes of the Ialno Range. The toponym Martkopi is derived from the Georgian epithet of St. Anton, Martodmqopeli, meaning "one who lives in solitude". The monastery enjoyed the favor of the kings of the eastern Georgian kingdom of Kakheti.

world knowledge.Name: Stade de Gerland
world knowledge.Address: 353, Avenue Jean-Jaurès, 69007 VII è Arrondissement, Lyon, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stade de Gerland was conceived in 1910 by Lyon's mayor Édouard Herriot and designed by architect Tony Garnier. Construction began in 1914 but was delayed by World War I, resuming in 1919 with the help of German POWs. It was inaugurated in 1926. Over the years, it underwent multiple renovations and expansions, including for UEFA Euro 1984 and the 1998 FIFA World Cup. It was the home of Olympique Lyonnais from 1950 to 2015 and later became the home of Lyon OU rugby club.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted matches, including Great Britain vs. Australia.
Hosted group stage matches.
Hosted group stage matches.
Hosted matches, including the semi-final where Cameroon's Marc-Vivien Foé tragically collapsed and died.
Hosted matches during the tournament.
Hosted the final between Great Britain and Australia, which ended in a 10-10 draw.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed by Tony Garnier with a cycling track and athletics track, later renovated by René Gagis and Albert Constantin. Features artificial turf, modern stands (Jean Bouin and Jean Jaurès), and a reduced seating capacity of 25,000 after renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A historic multi-purpose stadium in Lyon, hosting major sports events (World Cups, Euros) and concerts by iconic artists. It symbolizes Lyon's sporting heritage and urban development under Mayor Herriot.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium (rugby and football) and concert venue.
world knowledge.Details: Listed as a UEFA Category 3 stadium. Capacity reduced from 43,000 to 25,000 in 2017. Owned by the City of Lyon and operated by Lyon OU. Hosted the tragic incident involving Marc-Vivien Foé in 2003.

world knowledge.Name: Liechtenstein National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Liechtenstein National Museum is located in Vaduz, the capital city of Liechtenstein. The museum building dates back to 1438 and has served various roles including a princely tavern, customs house, and government seat. It underwent significant renovations and expansion from 1998 to 2008.

Major_Events.Description: The museum building was renovated and extended towards the mountain slope.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum displays artifacts about the history, culture, nature, and landscape of Liechtenstein, making it a key cultural institution in the country.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features 42 exhibit rooms across three buildings.

world knowledge.Name: Vērmane Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vērmane Garden is the oldest public garden in Riga, Latvia. It was originally created as Wöhrmann Park in 1814 on behalf of the Governor General of Governorate of Livonia Philip Paulucci. The park was sponsored by the Prussian Consul General to Riga Johann Christoph Wöhrmann and his mother Anna Gertrud Wöhrmann. It was inaugurated on 8 June 1817 as a fenced park with exotic trees, a rose garden, and a restaurant. The park expanded over the years with additions like a granite obelisk in 1829, a mineral water shop in 1836, and significant reconstructions in the 1860s and 1870s.

Major_Events.Description: The park was inaugurated with festivities as a fenced 0.8 hectares park with exotic trees, a rose garden, and a restaurant.
A granite obelisk was erected in the park as a posthumous memorial to Anna Wöhrmann.
Reconstructions were conducted according to a project by architect Heinrich Scheel.
The director of the Riga City Gardens and Parks Georg Kuphaldt expanded the park territory considerably.
The obelisk, which was dismantled prior to World War II, was recreated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features exotic trees, flower parterres, a granite obelisk, and a variety of plant species including Gleditschia triacanthos, Magnolia obovata, and Rhododendron catawbiense.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vērmane Garden is culturally significant as the oldest public garden in Riga, reflecting the city's historical and botanical heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The park was originally named Wöhrmann Park, a Latvian transliteration of the garden's original German name. It was created after the outskirts of Riga were burned down during the French invasion of Russia prior to the Siege of Riga.

world knowledge.Name: Kyungsung University
world knowledge.Address: Sooyoungryo 309, (Daeyeon 3Dong 314-79), Nam-gu district, Busan, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kyungsung University was established in 1955 by Reverend Dr. Kim Gil-Chang, originally as Kyungnam Teacher's College. It was reorganized and renamed Pusan Industrial University in 1979 and received official sanctioning as a general university in 1983. The name was changed to Kyungsung University in 1988 as part of its transition to an international university.

Major_Events.Description: Founded under the ideals of Christian love and service.

Major_Events.Event: Reorganization and renaming to Pusan Industrial University
Major_Events.Description: Expansion and improvement of facilities began.

Major_Events.Event: Official sanctioning as a general university
Major_Events.Description: Recognized as a comprehensive university.
Transition to an international university.
Held between South Korea and China regarding the Northeast Asia region.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kyungsung University is a significant educational institution in South Korea, known for its contributions to regional development and archaeological research, including the excavation of the Daeseong-dong site.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 10 undergraduate colleges, 7 graduate schools, 7 affiliated organizations, and 7 affiliated research institutes. It has over 13,000 students and 700 employees. The Kyungsung University Museum has been involved in significant archaeological excavations.

world knowledge.Name: Wayne County Building
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wayne County Building is a monumental government structure located in Downtown Detroit, Michigan. It formerly contained the Wayne County administrative offices and its courthouse. When completed in 1902, it was regarded as one of the most sumptuous buildings in Michigan. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The building was designated as a Michigan State Historic Site.
A renovation was carried out by Quinn Evans Architects and Smith, Hinchman & Grylls Associates.
Wayne County announced plans to relocate its offices to the Guardian Building.
The Wayne County Commission approved the sale of the building to 600 Randolph SN LLC for $13.4 million.
The building underwent a $7 million renovation focusing on exterior masonry, window restoration, and exterior lighting.
The building was put up for sale for an undisclosed price.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Roman Baroque Revival, Beaux-Arts, Neoclassical, Classical Revival. The building stands 5 floors and was built using copper, granite, and stone. The exterior is profusely ornamented with sculpture; the interior is finished in a variety of woods, marbles, tiles, and mosaics. The façade features a rusticated basement story and a balustrade between the third and fourth stories. At the main entrance, a broad flight of stairs leads up to a two-story Corinthian column portico. The structure boasts a tall, four-tiered, hipped roof central tower balanced by end pavilions. The courthouse tower was originally 227' 8½" tall; the copper dome and spire were redone in the 1960s, bringing its height to 247 feet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wayne County Building is culturally and historically significant as one of the most sumptuous buildings in Michigan and a fine example of Roman Baroque Revival architecture. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places and designated as a Michigan State Historic Site.
world knowledge.Details: The exterior architectural sculpture, including the Anthony Wayne pediment, was executed by Detroit sculptor Edward Wagner. The other sculptures, two quadrigas, Victory and Progress and four figures on the tower, Law, Commerce, Agriculture, and Mechanics, were sculpted by New York sculptor J. Massey Rhind, and made by Salem, Ohio resident William H. Mullins in 1903. On the other end of Campus Martius was the old Detroit City Hall, and they adorned the landscape as 'bookends'.

world knowledge.Name: Pennsylvania State Capitol
world knowledge.Address: 3rd and State Streets, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, U.S.A.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pennsylvania State Capitol is the seat of government for the U.S. state of Pennsylvania. The current capitol, known as the Huston Capitol, is the third state capitol building built in Harrisburg. The first, the Hills Capitol, was destroyed in 1897 by a fire. The second, the Cobb Capitol, was left unfinished when funding was discontinued in 1899. The building was designed by architect Joseph Miller Huston in 1902 and completed in 1906 in a Beaux-Arts style with decorative Renaissance themes throughout.

Major_Events.Description: President Theodore Roosevelt attended the building's dedication in 1906 and declared it "the handsomest building I ever saw."

The construction and subsequent furnishing cost three times more than the General Assembly had appropriated for the design and construction; architect Joseph Huston and four others were convicted of graft for price gouging.
The capitol was declared a National Historic Landmark during its centennial.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts, Renaissance Revival, Classical Revival styles of architecture. The facade is constructed out of granite from Hardwick, Vermont. The 94 ft-diameter dome is topped by the gilded brass statue of Commonwealth by Roland Hinton Perry. The dome features bright green Ludowici tiles and weighs 26,000 short tons. The interiors include hand-crafted tiles by Henry Chapman Mercer and murals by Edwin Austin Abbey and Violet Oakley.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pennsylvania State Capitol is often referred to as a "palace of art" because of its many sculptures, murals, and stained-glass windows, most of which are Pennsylvania-themed or Pennsylvanian-made. It represents the historical and governmental significance of Pennsylvania.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government Building (Seat of government for Pennsylvania, housing the legislative chambers for the Pennsylvania General Assembly, the Harrisburg chambers for the Supreme and Superior Courts of Pennsylvania, and the offices of the Governor and the Lieutenant Governor).
Notable_Visitors: Albert Edward (Prince of Wales, later King Edward VII)
world knowledge.Details: The capitol is 520 ft long and 272 ft tall. It houses 475 rooms and has four floors, not including a mezzanine and a basement. The Pennsylvania State Capitol Complex includes several buildings controlled by the Pennsylvania Department of General Services, centered on the capitol in Harrisburg. The capitol was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 2006.

world knowledge.Name: St Giles' Cathedral
world knowledge.Address: High Street and Parliament Square, St Giles (High) Kirk, Edinburgh, Scotland
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 196 feet (60 metres), Width: 125 feet (38 metres), Height: 52 feet (16 metres), Spire height: 145 feet (44 metres)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St Giles' Cathedral, also known as the High Kirk of Edinburgh, is a historic parish church of the Church of Scotland. It was likely founded in the 12th century and has been a focal point of Scottish history, including the Scottish Reformation and the Covenanters' Rebellion. The church was elevated to collegiate status in 1467 and became a cathedral in 1633. It has undergone significant alterations and restorations over the centuries, including major works in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: John Knox, the leader of the Scottish Reformation, became the minister of St Giles' and began the purging of Roman Catholic furnishings.
The signing of the National Covenant in response to Charles I's attempt to impose doctrinal changes on the Scottish Kirk, leading to the Bishops' Wars.
Significant restoration and alteration of the church's exterior and interior, including the addition of new doors and the removal of internal partitions.
Major restoration that removed the last internal partitions and introduced stained glass and an organ, among other changes.
Construction of the Thistle Chapel, designed by Robert Lorimer, as a chapel for the Order of the Thistle.
The coffin of Queen Elizabeth II lay at rest in St Giles' Cathedral for 24 hours, allowing the people of Scotland to pay their respects.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: St Giles' Cathedral features a mix of Gothic and Romanesque architectural styles. The church has a central tower with a distinctive crown steeple, a nave, choir, transepts, and multiple chapels. The interior includes stained glass windows, a pulpit, choir stalls, and a central communion table. The Thistle Chapel, added in the early 20th century, is a notable example of Gothic Revival architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St Giles' Cathedral is one of Scotland's most important medieval parish churches and is closely associated with the Scottish Reformation. It is often referred to as the 'Mother Church of World Presbyterianism' and has played a significant role in Scottish history, including hosting key events and figures such as John Knox and the Covenanters. The church is also a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of Edinburgh's heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Parish church of the Church of Scotland, hosting regular worship services, concerts, and special events.
world knowledge.Details: St Giles' Cathedral remains an active parish church and a major tourist attraction, drawing over a million visitors annually. It continues to host significant national and civic events, including services for the Order of the Thistle and the Scottish Parliament. The church's rich history, architectural beauty, and cultural importance make it a landmark of both Edinburgh and Scotland.

world knowledge.Name: Chandubi Lake
world knowledge.Area: Rabha Hasong Autonomous Council, Kamrup District, Assam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chandubi Lake was formed on 12 June 1897 by an earthquake that hit Assam. The forest in the area went down and became the lake.

Major_Events.Description: The lake was formed by an earthquake that caused the forest to subside and create the lake.
A festival where local village people perform traditional or cultural dance forms, and stalls offer local traditional food.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural lagoon formed in the lake.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chandubi Lake is a natural sightseeing and picnic spot, attracting migratory birds during winter. It is also a tourist destination, especially during the Changdubi festival.
world knowledge.Details: The lake offers fishing and rowing facilities. The psychological thriller Indian Hindi-language film Pepper Chicken was shot entirely in the jungles around this lake.

world knowledge.Name: Saddam Beach
world knowledge.Location: Coastal belt between Puthenkadapuram and Kettungal in Parappanangadi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Tipu Sultan Beach after the Mysore king Tippu Sultan. Renamed Saddam Beach in 1991 as an act of solidarity with Iraqi president Saddam Hussein after the Gulf War. The name was suggested by Indian maids working in the Gulf, especially Kuwait.

Major_Events.Description: Villagers renamed the beach to express solidarity with Saddam Hussein after the Gulf War.
During the invasion of Baghdad, villagers protested by boycotting Western goods and displaying posters of Saddam Hussein and Iraqi flags.

Major_Events.Event: Protest rally against Saddam Hussein's death sentence
Major_Events.Description: Villagers staged a protest rally against the death sentence of Saddam Hussein, shouting slogans against US President George W. Bush.
Supporters gathered at the beach to denounce the execution of Saddam Hussein, calling it cruel and shouting slogans against US President George W. Bush.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The beach is culturally significant as a symbol of solidarity with Saddam Hussein and his anti-imperialist stance. The villagers, mostly Muslim, admire his fight against US policies.
world knowledge.Details: The village connects to other parts of India through Parappanangadi town. National Highway No.66 passes nearby, linking to major cities like Mumbai, Cochin, and Trivandrum. The nearest airport is at Kozhikode, and the nearest major railway station is at Parappanangadi.

world knowledge.Name: Castles N' Coasters
world knowledge.Address: 9445 North Metro Parkway East, Phoenix, Arizona, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in 1976 as 'Golf N' Stuff', it was renamed 'Castles N' Coasters' in December 1991 after adding its Ride Park and expanding to 14 acres, which included two roller coasters and a multilevel arcade.

Major_Events.Description: Eleven people were stranded for nearly three hours after a free fall ride malfunctioned. The ride's cabin halted halfway up the tower, requiring firefighters to rescue the riders.
Two young boys suffered burns when the bumper boat they were in caught fire.
A twelve-year-old boy was seriously injured after falling from the Splashdown attraction and required emergency brain surgery.
22 people were stuck on the Desert Storm roller coaster after a long bolt broke, causing the cars to stall.
A man jumped out of the roller coaster onto the staircase catwalk after his lap bar restraint came loose.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in a Middle-Eastern motif with additional themes such as a Wild West-themed miniature golf course and log flume ride.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A popular family amusement center in Phoenix, offering a variety of attractions and rides, contributing to local entertainment and tourism.
