world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park and family entertainment center.
world knowledge.Details: Features include four outdoor 18-hole miniature golf courses, several rides, an indoor video game arcade, a go-kart track, bumper cars, bumper boats, two roller coasters (Patriot and Desert Storm), and thrill rides like Magic Carpet, Sea Dragon, Free Fall, and Sky Diver drop rides. The park's slogan is 'Arizona's Finest Family Fun and Thrill Park' and it attracts approximately 20,000 visitors annually.

world knowledge.Name: Pico Airport
world knowledge.Address: Located 8 km from Madalena, Pico Island, Azores, Portugal
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Runway length: 1,745 metres (5,725 ft), width: 45 metres (148 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pico Airport's construction began in 1976 under the Portuguese army and was completed by the Regional Government of the Azores. The runway was inaugurated on 25 April 1982, initially 1,200 metres long. It was extended in 1990 to 1,520 metres and again in the early 2000s to its current length of 1,745 metres.

Major_Events.Description: The runway was inaugurated at a length of 1,200 metres.
The runway was extended to 1,520 metres to accommodate new ATP aircraft.
The runway was extended to 1,745 metres to support medium-size jet or turboprop aircraft.
Pico Airport received its first direct flight from Lisbon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway oriented east to west, constructed with asphalt. It includes a terminal building, control tower, first aid station, firefighting centers, and a cargo warehouse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pico Airport is a vital infrastructure for the remote island of Pico, facilitating connectivity with mainland Portugal and other Azores islands, thus supporting local tourism and economy.
world knowledge.Details: Managed by SATA Gestão de Aeródromos, the airport operates with VFR or IFR flight rules and has an ILS system installed around 2010. Regular scheduled and charter flights are operated by various airlines.

world knowledge.Name: Sandy Point State Park
world knowledge.Area: Anne Arundel County, Maryland, United States
world knowledge.Address: Near the western end of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, Anne Arundel County, Maryland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sandy Point State Park was established in 1948 on the site of a former ferry landing that served the Chesapeake Bay Ferry System. The park opened in 1952 with segregated facilities, leading to a 1955 Supreme Court case (Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City v. Dawson) that mandated integration of public recreational facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened with racially segregated beaches and bathhouses.
The U.S. Supreme Court ordered the park to become integrated, extending the Fourteenth Amendment to state beaches and recreational facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes the Sandy Point Farmhouse, a historic structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Sandy Point Shoal Lighthouse, which stands in shallow water near the beach.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its role in the civil rights movement, particularly the Supreme Court case that ended segregation in public recreational facilities. It is also a popular recreational destination with over a million visitors annually.
world knowledge.Details: The park offers swimming beaches, fishing, crabbing, hiking, wildlife viewing, a nature center, picnicking, a marina store, and boat rentals. Adjacent Corcoran Woods forest preserve includes four miles of hiking trails. The park hosts the annual Maryland State Police Polar Bear Plunge in January to raise money for Special Olympics.

world knowledge.Name: Stage Front Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Cornellà and El Prat, Barcelona, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: RCDE Stadium, also known as Estadi Cornellà-El Prat, is an all-seater football stadium on the outskirts of Cornellà de Llobregat and El Prat de Llobregat, in the wider Barcelona urban area. It took three years to build and cost approximately €60 million. Opened in August 2009, it became the home of RCD Espanyol, replacing their previous stadium, the Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys. It is one of the potential host stadiums for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: Espanyol defeated Liverpool 3–0 in the stadium's inaugural match on 2 August 2009.
The stadium received a live concert of American hip hop group The Black Eyed Peas, during The E.N.D World Tour, in front of 30,000 fans.
German metal band Rammstein performed at the stadium as part of their Europe Stadium Tour 2019 with 33,825 fans in attendance.
British English pop singer Robbie Williams will perform at the stadium as part of his 2025 tour.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was designed by Mark Fenwick, Javier Iribarren (Reid Fenwick Asociados) and Esteban Gasulla (Gasulla Arquitectura y Gestió). It has a capacity of 40,000 seats, making it the tenth-largest stadium in Spain and the third-largest in Catalonia. The field size is 105 m × 68 m with a grass surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant as the home of RCD Espanyol and has hosted major football matches and concerts. It is also a potential host for the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The stadium has undergone several name changes due to sponsorship agreements and has been a venue for significant cultural and sporting events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is known as the Estadi Cornellà-El Prat because it is located on the borders of the municipalities Cornellà and El Prat. The club hopes to find a buyer for the naming rights for the stadium. After the death of club captain Daniel Jarque on 8 August 2009, it was proposed that the stadium should be renamed in his honour, but the club has not taken a definite stance on the subject. The stadium has had several naming sponsors, including Power8 Stadium and Stage Front Stadium, but has reverted to RCDE Stadium as of 1 July 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Der Aa-kerk
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Aa-kerk is a historic former parish church in the centre of Groningen, originally founded in 1247 as a chapel dedicated to Mary and Saint Nicholas. It became a parish church in 1247 and was transformed into a brick gothic church between 1425 and 1495. The church has undergone many alterations due to the iconoclasm during the Reformation, war damage, and natural phenomena. Today, it is used as a venue for concerts, theatre, exhibitions, parties, and meetings.

Major_Events.Description: Images of the Siege of Groningen in 1672 show the Aa-kerk without the top of the tower. After the war, a new wooden tower top was built.
On 23 April 1710, the tower spontaneously collapsed killing two people. In 1711, a new tower was built.
The first Schnitger organ in the church was built by Arp Schnitger in 1697. It was destroyed in 1710 when the tower collapsed.
The second Schnitger organ, originally built for the Broerkerk in Groningen, was transferred to the Aa-kerk in 1815.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Aa-kerk is a brick gothic church with a length of 76 m (249 ft 4 in), width of 25 m (82 ft 0 in), and height of 76 m (249 ft 4 in). The dome height (inner) is 26 m (85 ft). The church features three bells with the notes of F#, D#, and B, which are rung manually using ropes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Aa-kerk is a dominant feature in the skyline of Groningen and has played a significant role in the city's history. It was originally a chapel dedicated to Mary and Saint Nicholas, patron saint of fishermen, and later became a parish church. The church has witnessed major historical events, including the Siege of Groningen and the collapse of its tower. Today, it serves as a cultural venue.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Venue for concerts, theatre, exhibitions, parties, and meetings
world knowledge.Details: The current tower contains three bells cast by Crans of Enckhuysen in 1714. The church has housed several notable organs, including those built by Arp Schnitger and Raphael Rodensteen. The Bolsward organ, originally built in 1550, was transferred to the Aa-kerk in 1991.

world knowledge.Name: Koli National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Koli National Park preserves the traditional agricultural heritage of the area. The park was once a pagan sacrificial site, and was later used for slash-and-burn agriculture. While fields in the park are no longer slashed and burned, hay is cut yearly and traditional Finnish breeds of cow and sheep graze in the meadows of Koli.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features forested hills, rocky terrain, and a variety of biotopes. Notable structures include the Heritage Center Ukko and Hotel Koli. There are also many caves, such as Pirunkirkko, which is 34 metres long and 1–7 metres high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Koli National Park is culturally significant as it preserves traditional agricultural practices and has inspired many artists and composers, such as Jean Sibelius, Juhani Aho, and Eero Järnefelt. It is considered one of the best natural scenes in Finland.
world knowledge.Details: Koli National Park is divided into three main zones: the mountaintop zone, the culture zone, and the nature zone. The park offers a popular vantage point at the summit of Koli Hill, named Ukko-Koli, which provides a grand view over Pielinen Lake. There are two ski resorts in the area: Loma-Koli for families and Ukko-Koli for advanced downhill skiers.

world knowledge.Name: Namtok Sam Lan National Park
world knowledge.Address: Near Wat Phra Puttachai, Saraburi Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: During World War II, the Japanese Army occupied and used this area as an encampment, entailing the destruction of some of the park's forests. In 1960 the Thai government began the restoration of this forest and designated it a conservation area. On 2 June 1981, Namtok Sam Lan was designated a National Park.

Major_Events.Description: Namtok Sam Lan was designated a National Park on 2 June 1981.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features waterfalls, reservoirs, and forests. The forest consists of deciduous, mixed dipterocarp, and evergreen forest. Tree species include teak, Pterocarpus macrocarpus, Afzelia xylocarpa, Hopea odorata, Dipterocarpus tuberculatus, Shorea obtusa, Xylia xylocarpa, Shorea siamensis, and Lagerstroemia calyculata.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its natural beauty, diverse flora and fauna, and its historical use during World War II. It is also located near the cave temple Wat Phra Puttachai.
world knowledge.Details: The park's best-known attractions are its waterfalls, including the namesake Sam Lan Waterfall with three levels, each of about 5 metres (16 ft). Other waterfalls include Pho Hin Dat, Roi Kueak Ma, and Ton Rak Sai. The park is home to various animal species such as pig-tailed macaque, northern red muntjac, lesser Oriental chevrotain, wild boar, Finlayson's squirrel, and northern treeshrew. Bird species include brown shrike, greater coucal, green-billed malkoha, Javan pond-heron, long-tailed shrike, Oriental magpie-robin, plain prinia, plaintive cuckoo, puff-throated babbler, red junglefowl, sooty-headed bulbul, streak-eared bulbul, western koel, and white-rumped shama. The park is also noted for its various butterfly species.

world knowledge.Name: Tjuvholmen Sculpture Park
world knowledge.Area: Tjuvholmen neighborhood of Frogner borough in Oslo, Norway
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tjuvholmen Sculpture Park opened on 10 August 2012 as part of a £20 million development plan for Tjuvholmen. It was expanded in 2013 with several additional sculptures. The park's concept was developed in conjunction with the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened on 10 August 2012 as part of a £20 million development plan for Tjuvholmen.
The park was expanded with several additional sculptures.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park was designed by the Italian architect Renzo Piano. It consists of seven pieces of art created by notable international contemporary artists.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park features works by internationally renowned artists and stands out against the Oslofjord, with views of Akershus Castle, Akershus Fortress, and the Astrup Fearnley Museum of Modern Art. It is a significant cultural site for contemporary art.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes seven sculptures, one of which, "Things for a House on an Island" by Fischli and Weiss, allows viewers to look into the structure. Nearby, there is a beach open to the public.

world knowledge.Name: Workers Indoor Arena
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Workers' Gymnasium is an indoor arena located west of the Workers' Stadium in Beijing, China. It was inaugurated in 1961 for the 26th World Table Tennis Championships.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugural event for the Workers' Gymnasium.
Hosted the boxing events.
Hosted the Judo events.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Workers' Gymnasium is one of 11 Beijing-based venues renovated and upgraded for the 2008 Olympics, reflecting its importance in international sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The arena has a seating capacity of 13,000 (lower for Olympics). It was renovated and completed by 2008 for the Olympics.

image_name: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park

world knowledge.Name: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park
world knowledge.Address: Kui Buri District, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park is a marine national park established in 1966, making it the first coastal national park of Thailand. It covers 98 square kilometres, including Thailand's largest freshwater marsh. The park is known for its limestone hills, freshwater marshes, and diverse wildlife. The origin of the name 'Khao Sam Roi Yot' is undetermined, with local lore suggesting it means 'mountain with 300 peaks' or refers to a local plant.

Major_Events.Description: King Mongkut hosted European guests to observe a total solar eclipse on 18 August 1868. He calculated the date and location of the eclipse himself, proving more accurate than French astronomers. He contracted malaria during the event and died on 1 October.
Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park was officially established on 28 June 1966, with an original area of 61 square kilometres. It was enlarged to 98 square kilometres on 1 April 1982.
The Khao Sam Roi Yot Wetland was designated as a Ramsar site on 8 January 2008, recognizing its importance as a wetland of international significance.

In May 2020, archaeologists discovered 3,000-year-old cave paintings in the park, depicting humanlike figures, hunting scenes, and animal figures. In October 2020, more rock art dating back 2,000 to 3,000 years was discovered in unmapped caves.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features limestone hills, freshwater marshes, and marine areas. Notable sites include Phraya Nakhon Cave, which has a hole in the ceiling allowing sunlight to penetrate, and Khuha Kharuehat Pavilion, a historic site built for King Chulalongkorn's visit in 1890. The park also includes two white sand beaches and five uninhabited islands.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park is culturally significant as Thailand's first coastal national park and for its diverse ecosystems, including Thailand's largest freshwater marsh. The park is also known for its historical connections to King Mongkut and King Chulalongkorn, as well as its ancient cave paintings.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to a variety of wildlife, including rare species such as the mainland serow, dusky langurs, fishing cats, and Irrawaddy dolphins. It also features diverse bird species and marine life. The park's climate varies seasonally, with temperatures ranging from 18°C to 32°C throughout the year. The park's mangroves consist of various species, including grey mangrove, true mangrove, red mangrove, and herbaceous seepweed.

world knowledge.Name: Museo Soumaya
world knowledge.Address: Plaza Carso, Nuevo Polanco, Mexico City
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museo Soumaya is a private museum in Mexico City and a non-profit cultural institution with two museum buildings in Mexico City — Plaza Carso and Plaza Loreto. It has over 66,000 works from 30 centuries of art including sculptures from Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica, 19th- and 20th-century Mexican art and an extensive repertoire of works by European old masters and masters of modern western art such as Auguste Rodin, Salvador Dalí, Bartolomé Esteban Murillo and Tintoretto. The museum is named after Soumaya Domit, who died in 1999, and was the wife of the founder of the museum Carlos Slim.

Major_Events.Description: The new building in Plaza Carso was inaugurated on February 28, 2011, with a ceremonial ribbon cutting attended by notable guests including Felipe Calderón, Gabriel García Márquez, Evelyn Robert de Rothschild, and Larry King. It opened to the public on March 28, 2011.
In October 2015, the museum welcomed its five millionth visitor.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a 46-metre-high six-story building covered by 16,000 hexagonal aluminum tiles. The weight of the building is held by an exoskeleton of 28 vertical curved steel columns and seven beams encircling the structure. The floors are made of high quality marble imported from Greece. The top floor is opened so that it is illuminated by sunlight during the daytime.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its extensive collection of art spanning 30 centuries, including works by European old masters and modern western artists. It also holds the world's largest collection of pre-Hispanic and colonial era coins and the largest collection of casts of sculptures by Auguste Rodin outside France. The museum aims to increase the 'humanistic capital' of Mexico City by providing access to prestigious art collections locally.
world knowledge.Details: The museum was designed by Mexican architect Fernando Romero, engineered with Ove Arup and Frank Gehry, and cost $70 million to build. It features a library, restaurant, and a 350-seat auditorium. Admission to the museum is free of charge, with operating costs covered by Carlos Slim's fortune. The museum is part of a large mixed-use development, Plaza Carso, which cost almost $800 million to build.

image_name: United States Department of Agriculture South Building

world knowledge.Name: United States Department of Agriculture South Building
world knowledge.Address: 14th Street and Independence Avenue, SW Washington, D.C.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 458 feet (140 m) by 944 feet (288 m) in seven stories with 4500 rooms
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The U.S. Department of Agriculture South Building was built to house the expanded offices of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). Construction began in 1930 and was completed in 1936 due to the demand for more office space from Depression-era agriculture programs. The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: The South Building was completed, becoming the largest office building in the world until the completion of the Pentagon.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The building was recognized for its historical significance and added to the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a stripped-down example of Classicism, with plain detailing that borrows from Classical form and proportion. It features seven north–south wings connected at the ends by the Headhouse and Tailhouse. The 12th and 14th Street elevations are sheathed in limestone, while the C Street and Independence Avenue elevations use brick with limestone and terra cotta detailing. The interior is based on a rigid corridor network, with the departmental auditorium and library as exceptions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The South Building is significant for its historical role in housing USDA operations during the Depression era and its architectural style, which represents a transition from Classicism to Modern Movement in government buildings. It was also the largest office building in the world until the Pentagon was completed.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Office building for the United States Department of Agriculture
world knowledge.Details: The building was originally referred to as the 'Extensible Building' due to its phased construction. It was designed by Louis A. Simon of the Federal Office of the Supervising Architect. The building's 14th Street elevation features a monumental entrance with sixteen Corinthian columns and relief panels depicting animals native to the United States by sculptor Edwin Morris.

world knowledge.Name: Conneaut Lake Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Conneaut Lake Park was founded in 1892 as Exposition Park by Col. Frank Mantor as a permanent fairground and exposition for livestock, machinery, and industrial products from Western Pennsylvania. It evolved into a summer resort and amusement park, featuring classic rides like the Blue Streak roller coaster. The park has undergone multiple ownership changes, financial struggles, and renovations, remaining a regional tourist destination.

Major_Events.Description: A large portion of Hotel Conneaut was destroyed in a fire. The ghost of Elizabeth, a bride who supposedly died in the fire, is said to haunt the hotel.
The Blue Streak roller coaster was classified as "historic" by the American Coaster Enthusiasts group.
The Dreamland Ballroom was destroyed in a fire.
A fire destroyed the dockside restaurant and the beach front building.
Splash City water park was demolished, with only a portion of the Cliffhanger Falls water slide remaining before it was later torn down.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of historic and modern structures, including classic amusement rides like the Blue Streak roller coaster, a carousel, and various midways. Many original buildings were lost to fires and replaced with concrete block structures, such as the Dreamland Ballroom.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Conneaut Lake Park is a historic summer resort and amusement park, noted for its classic rides like the Blue Streak roller coaster. It has served as a regional tourist destination and is significant for its role in the history of amusement parks in the United States. The park also holds cultural importance as a community gathering place and a symbol of traditional amusement resorts.

Details.Owner: Keldon Holdings, LLC, Todd Joseph Fenstermacher
Details.Slogan: "A traditional amusement resort with something for everyone!" and "Where the past becomes the future!"
Details.Water_Park: Splash City (formerly operated from 1986-1994, 1996-2006, and 2009-2010; demolished in 2022)
Details.Kiddieland: A small, enclosed section of the park with rides for children, pony rides, and rebuilt restrooms after an arson fire in 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Manyara
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Manyara, also known as Lake Moya among the Iraqw people, is a shallow, alkaline lake in the Natron-Manyara-Balangida branch of the East African Rift. It is the seventh-largest lake in Tanzania by surface area. The lake is part of the Lake Manyara Biosphere Reserve, established in 1981 by UNESCO. The name 'Manyara' may come from the Maasai word 'emanyara', meaning a spiky enclosure around a family homestead, or from the Mbugwe word 'manyero', meaning a trough or place where animals drink water.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Lake Manyara Biosphere Reserve
Major_Events.Description: UNESCO established the Lake Manyara Biosphere Reserve as part of its Man and the Biosphere Programme.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Manyara is culturally significant due to its role in the local ecosystem and its importance to the Maasai and Mbugwe tribes. It is also a key site for biodiversity and is protected within the Lake Manyara National Park and UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
world knowledge.Details: Lake Manyara is a soda or alkaline lake with a pH near 9.5, and it is high in dissolved salts. The lake's depth and area fluctuate significantly, with a maximum depth of 3.7 m. It is fed by underground springs and rainwater-fed rivers. The lake is known for its large flocks of flamingos and other water birds. The lake is partly protected within the Lake Manyara National Park and is one of the seven Tanzanian UNESCO Man and Biosphere reserves. The lake faces environmental challenges due to unsustainable land and water use, leading to increased sedimentation rates.

world knowledge.Name: World Trade Center Mexico City
world knowledge.Address: Filadelfia S/N, Montecito 38 03810 Mexico City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally conceived as Hotel de México, the project was initiated in 1966 by Manuel Suárez y Suárez but faced financial and political challenges. The main tower was completed in 1972 but remained unfinished. In the mid-1980s, plans were made to convert it into an international business center. Renovation began in 1992, and it reopened as the World Trade Center México in 1995.

Major_Events.Description: The project was initiated but faced financial and political issues, leaving the tower unfinished despite completion in 1972.
The complex was renovated and repurposed as an international business center, opening as WTC México in 1995.
A 7,500-seat theater was added to the complex, primarily used for concerts and stage shows.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex features the 50-story Torre WTC, standing 172 m (564 ft) tall, with an antenna spire reaching 218 m (715 ft). It includes a convention center, cultural center, shopping center, luxury restaurant, observation gallery, and a hotel. The tower is equipped with a seismic detector and a facility management system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The WTC México is a significant business and cultural hub in Mexico City, housing important facilities like the Polyforum Cultural Siqueiros and serving as a landmark for international trade and events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Office building, convention center, and cultural venue
world knowledge.Details: The complex includes a 22-floor hotel, a multi-screen cinema, a revolving 45th-floor luxury restaurant, and a shopping center with a Sears anchor tenant. It is served by the Poliforum station of the Metrobús Bus rapid transit system. The tower also houses transmission facilities for several radio stations and previously hosted TV studios for XHTVM Canal 40.

world knowledge.Name: Gunung Timur Temple
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gunung Timur Temple is the largest Chinese temple in Medan, Indonesia, and possibly on the island of Sumatra. It was built in 1962 and dedicated to Dongyue Dadi. The temple serves as a center of faith for the Chinese community in Medan and is a multicultural icon, located near the Sri Mariamman Temple and Masjid Agung. It was founded jointly by Taoist and Buddhist communities in Medan and is also recognized as a historical site.

Major_Events.Description: The temple is filled with worshippers during the Chinese New Year celebration.
The temple is crowded during the Cap Go Meh festival, often featuring lion dance processions.
The temple is filled with worshippers during this festival.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features Chinese architectural style with ornate statues of lions and dragons at the entrance. The building is designed to face the Babura River, believed to bring good luck. It is decorated with red and yellow colors, considered lucky by the Chinese. The roof is adorned with a pair of green dragons facing each other with the sun in the middle. Inside, there is a large drum used during Chinese New Year, multiple altars, and 80 statues of deities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gunung Timur Temple is culturally significant as a center of faith for the Chinese community in Medan and a symbol of multiculturalism. It is also a historical site and a place of worship for both Taoist and Buddhist communities.
world knowledge.Details: The temple contains a large paved area with an impressively scaled incense burner, two covered badminton courts, a very large main hall, and is partly surrounded by a moat and walls. It features multiple altars with statues of deities, including Maitreya Buddha, Goddess Kwan Im, Tua Pek Kong, Thay Suei, Thien Kou, Pek Ho Kong, and Tho Te Kong.

world knowledge.Name: VTB Arena
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The VTB Arena – Dynamo Central Stadium is a multi-purpose sports complex built on the site of the old Central Dynamo Stadium, which was closed for demolition in 2008. The new complex was designed to include both a football stadium and an ice hockey venue. The project faced delays and was completed in 2018. The football stadium is named after legendary goalkeeper Lev Yashin.

Major_Events.Description: Dynamo Moscow vs. Spartak Moscow, initially scheduled for 10 March 2019, but moved due to pitch issues. The first official game was Dynamo Moscow vs. Arsenal Tula on 26 May 2019.
HC Dynamo Moscow vs. Avtomobilist Yekaterinburg on 4 January 2019, with Dynamo winning 2–0.
Imagine Dragons concert as part of their Evolve World Tour, later moved to Luzhniki Stadium due to construction delays.
Figure skating adaptation of 'Swan Lake' by Evgeni Plushenko on 20 December 2018.
Hosted on 17 February 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The initial concept was designed by Dutch architect Erick van Egeraat, featuring a football stadium and ice hockey arena inside the bowl of the former Dynamo Stadion. The final design was prepared by American firm MANICA Architecture. The complex includes modern facilities, adjustable seating capacities, and advanced technology like facial recognition systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The VTB Arena is a significant sports and entertainment hub in Moscow, hosting major football matches, ice hockey games, and concerts. It honors Lev Yashin, one of football's greatest goalkeepers. The arena has won awards, including the IV Sport Business Awards in 2020.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports and concert and entertainment complex

Details.Facial_Recognition: Installed at the end of 2020 to manage access and potentially replace tickets in the future.

world knowledge.Name: Old Town Hall, Westbury
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Old Town Hall was a gift to the town from Sir Manasseh Masseh Lopes, who acquired the manor of Westbury in 1810. It was completed in 1815 and served as a market hall, courtroom, and civic meeting place. The borough council was abolished in 1883, and the building was later repurposed for commercial use.

Major_Events.Description: The town hall was built as a gift from Sir Manasseh Masseh Lopes and completed in 1815.
A Russian gun captured during the Crimean War was placed outside the town hall.
The building underwent extensive refurbishment to convert it for commercial use, including filling in the ground floor for shops.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style, built in ashlar stone, with a symmetrical main frontage of three bays. The ground floor was arcaded, and the first floor featured an assembly room. The central bay had a blind alcove with a clock, and the roof had a frieze and pediment with the Lopes coat of arms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Old Town Hall is a Grade II* listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. It served as a key civic and judicial building in Westbury's history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a market hall, courtroom, and civic meeting place; later converted for commercial use.
world knowledge.Details: The building was used as a branch of the county library in the 1960s and later housed a South African restaurant and a firm of solicitors.

world knowledge.Name: University of Alberta
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Alberta was founded in 1908 by Alexander Cameron Rutherford, the first premier of Alberta, and Henry Marshall Tory, the university's first president. It was established through the Post-secondary Learning Act and is considered a 'comprehensive academic and research university' (CARU). The university has four campuses in Edmonton, an Augustana Campus in Camrose, and a staff centre in downtown Calgary. It has contributed significantly to Alberta's economy and has produced over 260,000 graduates, including 3 Nobel Prize winners and 72 Rhodes Scholars.

Major_Events.Description: The university organized the recruitment of staff and students for XI Canadian Field Ambulance and 'C' Company of the 196th (Western Universities) Battalion. 82 staff and students from the University of Alberta died during their service in the First World War.
The global influenza pandemic resulted in a two-month suspension of classes in the fall of 1918.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Breton Soil Plots
Major_Events.Description: The Breton Soil Plots were established at the faculty of agriculture to provide agricultural research on fertilization, usage, crop rotations, and farming practices on Gray-Luvisolic soils.
The university hosted the World University Games, the first time the event was held in North America.
The university faced significant funding cuts and job losses due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's original north campus consists of 150 buildings covering 50 city blocks. The campus features a mix of architectural styles, including the Arts Building, laboratories, and Power House designed by Percy Erskine Nobbs and Frank Darling. The Dentistry/Pharmacy Centre's distinctive cupola is a notable feature.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Alberta is a major economic driver for Alberta and has a significant cultural and historical impact. It has produced numerous notable alumni, including Nobel laureates, Rhodes Scholars, and prominent figures in various fields. The university's research and academic programs contribute to its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Alberta has 18 faculties and two affiliated colleges. It is a member of the U15 universities and the Worldwide Universities Network. The university's library system is rated 11th in North America and is the second-largest in Canada. The university has five distributed campuses, including the North Campus, Campus Saint-Jean, Augustana Campus, Enterprise Square, and South Campus. The university's research performance is notable, with over 400 distinct research laboratories and significant external research funding.

world knowledge.Name: Ko Phi Phi Don
world knowledge.Address: Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi District, Krabi Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ko Phi Phi Don is the largest island in the Phi Phi archipelago, largely made of limestone. It is the only island in the group with permanent inhabitants, mostly temporary workers servicing the tourist trade. The island was severely affected by a tsunami on 26 December 2004, which caused significant destruction and loss of life.

Major_Events.Description: A tsunami struck the island on 26 December 2004, resulting in over 1,000 deaths. Lohdalum Bay was hit the hardest, with most bungalows and restaurants destroyed. The tsunami lasted three minutes but nearly destroyed the whole island.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Non-volcanic island largely made of limestone, almost separated into two islands but connected by a strand of flat land where the largest settlement and most resorts are located.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ko Phi Phi Don is a significant tourist destination in Thailand, known for its natural beauty and marine life. It is part of the Hat Noppharat Thara-Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park. The island also holds a memorial for tsunami victims, with annual memorial services.
world knowledge.Details: The island faces environmental challenges due to underfunding and high tourist numbers, including solid waste management and freshwater shortages. The Phi Phi Islands produce an average of 25 tonnes of solid waste daily, increasing to 40 tonnes during high season. A 20 baht fee is charged to tourists to assist in waste management. The island's water supply is strained during the dry season, leading to groundwater contamination. Recommendations have been made to cap tourist numbers to preserve the island's carrying capacity.

world knowledge.Name: Kamuzu Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Rangeley Stadium during the colonial era to commemorate British civil servant William H. J. Rangeley. It later became known as Kamuzu Stadium, after Malawi's first President, Hastings Kamuzu Banda, when Malawi gained independence from Britain. The name was changed to Chichiri Stadium under President Bakili Muluzi but was restored to Kamuzu Stadium under President Bingu wa Mutharika in 2004.

Major_Events.Description: Main stands were designed and drawn by L Jeffery and Steve Price, with works completed in 1968.
The stadium was renovated, including the installation of a synthetic football pitch sponsored by FIFA through its GOAL programme.
President Peter Mutharika's inauguration ceremony was held at Kamuzu Stadium on 2 June 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Main stands designed by L Jeffery and Steve Price. Features an Act Global Artificial Turf, FIFA Certified.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after Malawi's first President, Hastings Kamuzu Banda, and has undergone name changes reflecting the country's political history. It is a significant sports venue in Malawi.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: Big Bullets and Be Forward Wanderers are tenants. The stadium has a capacity of 65,000 people, which can be limited for safety reasons.

world knowledge.Name: Royal British Columbia Museum
world knowledge.Address: 675 Belleville St, Victoria, BC V8W 9W2, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1886 as the British Columbia Provincial Museum, it was established to preserve British Columbian natural products and native artifacts. The museum merged with the British Columbia Provincial Archives in 2003. The 'Royal' title was approved by Queen Elizabeth II in 1987.

Major_Events.Description: The museum merged with the British Columbia Provincial Archives, enhancing its archival and historical collections.
Queen Elizabeth II approved the 'Royal' title for the museum during a royal tour.
The museum moved to its current location with a construction budget of $9.5 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building, opened in 1968, is a modern structure designed to house extensive collections and exhibitions. It includes three permanent galleries and hosts various touring exhibitions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its extensive collections of natural history, First Nations artifacts, and archival records. It plays a crucial role in preserving and showcasing the cultural and natural heritage of British Columbia.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes three permanent galleries: Natural History, Becoming BC, and the First Peoples Gallery. It houses over 7 million objects, including natural history specimens, artifacts, and archival records. The museum also operates traveling exhibitions and partners with the IMAX Victoria theater.

world knowledge.Name: Egyptian Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Egyptian Museum, established in 1902, houses the largest collection of Egyptian antiquities in the world. It was built to replace earlier museums in Azbakeya, Boulaq, and Giza. The museum's collections include over 120,000 items, with significant artifacts from ancient Egyptian history, including Pharaoh Tutankhamun's treasure. The museum has undergone several relocations and expansions, with the current building designed by French architect Marcel Dourgnon.

Major_Events.Description: The Boulaq Museum, a predecessor to the Egyptian Museum, suffered significant damage due to flooding of the Nile River.
The collections were moved to a former royal palace in the Giza district of Cairo.
The Egyptian Museum was officially opened in its current location in Tahrir Square.
The museum was broken into during the revolution, resulting in damage to artifacts and theft of around 50 objects.
22 royal mummies were transferred from the Egyptian Museum to the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization in Fustat.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by French architect Marcel Dourgnon in a neoclassical style. The building features large exhibition halls, a two-story library, and a garden with a memorial to famous Egyptologists. The design emphasizes functionality to accommodate the vast collection of artifacts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Egyptian Museum is a symbol of ancient Egyptian heritage and houses the world's largest collection of Pharaonic antiquities. It is a key cultural and historical institution, preserving artifacts that span thousands of years of Egyptian history.

Details.Opening_Hours: Daily from 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with special hours on Fridays from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM and from 1:30 PM to 7:00 PM
Details.Photography_Policy: Photography is not allowed inside the museum due to the negative effects of camera flashes on the artifacts. Personal photography is permitted for a fee of 50 EGP, except in the Hall of the Golden Mask and the Royal Mummy Halls.
Details.Ticket_Price: 240 EGP for a combined morning ticket for foreigners (museum and Mummies Hall)
Details.Library: The museum library houses over 50,000 books and volumes, including rare works on ancient Egyptian, Greek, Roman, and Near Eastern archaeology.

world knowledge.Name: Pont Neuf
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 232 metres (761 ft) in length, 22 metres (72 ft) in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pont Neuf is the oldest standing bridge across the river Seine in Paris, France. It was commissioned by Henry III and completed under Henry IV. The bridge was innovative for its time, being the first in Paris without houses built on it and featuring pavements for pedestrians. It has undergone several renovations and restorations over the centuries, including a major restoration from 1994 to 2007.

Major_Events.Description: Henry III laid the first stone, and construction began under the supervision of a building commission.
The bridge was completed and inaugurated by Henry IV after delays due to political unrest and the Wars of Religion.
A comprehensive restoration project was undertaken to preserve the bridge, completed in time for its 400th anniversary.
The art duo wrapped the Pont Neuf as part of a large-scale public art project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Pont Neuf is a stone arch bridge composed of two separate spans: one with seven arches joining the right bank to the Île de la Cité, and another with five arches joining the island to the left bank. It features 381 mascarons (stone masks) decorating its sides, each unique and depicting mythological figures. The bridge was designed without houses, a novelty at the time, and included pavements for pedestrians.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pont Neuf is a symbol of Parisian history and engineering. It was the first bridge in Paris without houses and introduced pedestrian pavements. The bridge has been a central gathering place for centuries, hosting markets, performances, and social interactions. It is also listed as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge for pedestrian and vehicular traffic across the Seine
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is decorated with 381 mascarons, each unique. It features a bronze equestrian statue of Henry IV, which was destroyed during the French Revolution and later rebuilt. The Pont Neuf was a hub of social and commercial activity in Paris for centuries, known for its lively atmosphere, street performers, and vendors. It has also been the subject of artistic works, including early photographs by Louis Daguerre and a wrapping project by Christo and Jeanne-Claude.

world knowledge.Name: Portland Observatory
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Portland Observatory is a historic maritime signal tower built in 1807 by Captain Lemuel Moody to facilitate two-way communication between ship and shore. It was used during the War of 1812 as a watch tower and remained operational until 1923. It is the only surviving maritime signal tower of its type in the United States.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Captain Lemuel Moody to solve visibility problems for merchants awaiting incoming ships.
Used as a watch tower during the war.
Renovated as part of the Works Progress Administration projects.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places.
Renovated to repair damage from moisture and powderpost beetles, winning a 2001 National Preservation Honor Award.
Recognized as a National Historic Landmark and National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 86-foot (26 m) tall observatory is octagonal (to lessen wind pressure) and lighthouse-shaped, with a fieldstone base of heavy loose rocks. It has a cupola that originally housed a P & J Dollond Achromatic Refracting Telescope. The structure has no basement but is stabilized by rock ballast and its octagonal design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Portland Observatory is the only remaining maritime signal station in the United States, representing early maritime communication methods. It was designated a National Historic Landmark for its historical and engineering significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a maritime signal tower for communication between ships and shore; now operates as a museum.
world knowledge.Details: The observatory is managed by Greater Portland Landmarks and offers guided tours from Memorial Day to Columbus Day. The cupola's balcony provides views extending from the seaward horizon to Mount Washington on clear days. The building retains original wood, distinguished by dark stain, while replacement wood is lighter in color.

world knowledge.Name: Al Ain National Museum
world knowledge.Area: Eastern Region of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
world knowledge.Address: Al Ain, Eastern Region of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, the UAE
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum, the oldest in the UAE, was built by the former UAE President, Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan, to house archaeological finds from the surrounding area, including the Hafit-era 'beehive' tombs near Mezyad. It was inaugurated by Sheikh Tahnoun bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, the Ruler's Representative in the Eastern Region, on 2 November 1971.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was inaugurated by Sheikh Tahnoun bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, the Ruler's Representative in the Eastern Region.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses archaeological finds from the surrounding area, including the Hafit-era 'beehive' tombs near Mezyad, and has two main sections on ethnographic and archaeological aspects of the country, especially around Al Ain.
world knowledge.Details: As of October 2018, there were plans to make restorations to the museum and fort.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Hiei
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Hiei is a mountain northeast of Kyoto, lying on the border between Kyoto and Shiga Prefectures. The temple of Enryaku-ji, the first outpost of the Japanese Tendai sect of Buddhism, was founded atop Mount Hiei by Saichō in 788. It rapidly grew into a sprawling complex of temples and buildings. Due to its position, it was thought to protect Kyoto from negative influences. The temple complex was politically powerful and influential during the Heian period (8th-12th centuries). Later schools of Buddhism in Japan were founded by ex-monks of the Tendai sect. The temple complex was razed by Oda Nobunaga in 1571 but was later rebuilt and remains the Tendai headquarters to this day.

Major_Events.Description: Saichō founded the temple of Enryaku-ji, the first outpost of the Japanese Tendai sect of Buddhism.
The temple complex was razed by Oda Nobunaga to quell the rising power of Tendai's warrior monks (sōhei).
The temple complex was rebuilt and remains the Tendai headquarters to this day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple complex of Enryaku-ji is sprawling and divided into three main areas, connected by foot trails. The complex includes numerous temples, shrines, and other buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Hiei is culturally significant as the birthplace of the Tendai sect of Buddhism in Japan. Many later schools of Buddhism were founded by ex-monks of the Tendai sect. The mountain has been featured in many folk tales and is known for its religious practices, such as the kaihōgyō (walking meditation).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious and spiritual site, hiking destination, and tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Hiei features the Garden Museum Hiei, themed on French impressionism, and a French-themed hotel, "L'hotel de Hiei." The mountain is popular for hiking, with a toll road and funiculars providing access. The temple complex of Enryaku-ji is the main attraction, spread over the mountain in three main areas. The mountain is also known for the practice of sennichi kaihōgyō, a rigorous walking meditation performed by monks.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Rochetaillée
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Rochetaillée is a ruined feudal castle originally constructed in the 12th century, with additional work completed in the 16th century. It has been listed as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture since 1930.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was officially recognized as a historical monument by the French Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Ruined feudal castle with construction elements from the 12th and 16th centuries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is a historical landmark representing medieval architecture and feudal history in the Loire region of France.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a feudal castle, now a historical site.
world knowledge.Details: This article about the castle is a stub, indicating that further details may be available through additional research or expansion.

world knowledge.Name: Tam Dil
world knowledge.Address: 6 km from Saitual, 64 km from Aizawl, Mizoram, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ṭam Dil is a reservoir lake with origins in Mizo folklore. According to legend, a widow was instructed by her deceased husband to care for a giant mustard plant, which was a harbinger of immense blessing. When her new husband uprooted the plant, the hole left behind filled with water, forming the lake. The name Ṭam Dil means "lake of the mustard."

Major_Events.Description: A new species of frog, Leptolalax tamdil, was described from this lake.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lake is a natural reservoir surrounded by small steep hills, reconstructed by the Fisheries Department, Government of Mizoram, for fishing purposes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ṭam Dil is culturally significant due to its origins in Mizo folklore and its role in local tourism and fishing.
world knowledge.Details: Lake-side resorts are maintained by the Tourism Department of Mizoram, enhancing its appeal as a tourist destination.

world knowledge.Name: Búzios
world knowledge.Location: State of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally occupied by the Tupinambá Indians, the area became a site for French pirates and smugglers in the 17th century. In the 18th century, it was known for whale hunting. The town grew into an agricultural and fishing community after the abolition of slave trade in 1850. It gained international fame after Brigitte Bardot's visit in 1964.

Major_Events.Description: The French actress's visit brought international attention to Búzios, transforming it into a popular tourist destination.
The abolition led Búzios to shift from smuggling and slave-trading to agriculture and fishing.
The Portuguese expelled the French due to conflicts with the Tupinambás, leading to a decline in the indigenous population.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Sant'Ana Chapel was built with rocks and whale oil, reflecting the historical whale-hunting practices in the area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Búzios is culturally significant for its transformation from a small fishing village to a worldwide tourist destination, influenced by its rich history involving indigenous populations, European settlers, and notable visitors like Brigitte Bardot.
world knowledge.Details: Búzios features 23 beaches, with the west coast offering calm waters and the east coast known for surfing. The town has a vibrant nightlife centered around Rua das Pedras. It has a tropical climate with temperatures ranging from 20°C to 30°C. The peninsula is 8 kilometers long and is served by Umberto Modiano Airport.

world knowledge.Name: Tennessee Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tennessee Theatre is a movie palace in the downtown core of Knoxville, Tennessee, United States. The theater was built in 1928 in the 1908 Burwell Building, considered Knoxville's first skyscraper. The theater and Burwell Building were added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982, and the theater was extensively restored in the early 2000s. The Tennessee Theatre currently focuses on hosting performing arts events and classic films, and is home to the Knoxville Opera and the Knoxville Symphony Orchestra.

Major_Events.Description: The theater first opened on October 1, 1928, with about 2,000 seats in the auditorium, billed as "Knoxville's Grand Entertainment Palace".

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The theater was placed in the National Register of Historic Places on April 1, 1982.
The theater reopened on January 14, 2005, after a $29.3 million restoration and renovation project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Chicago architects Graven & Mayger in the Spanish-Moorish style, incorporating elements from all parts of the world: Czechoslovakian crystals in the French-style chandeliers, Italian terrazzo flooring in the Grand Lobby, and Oriental influences in the carpet and drapery patterns. The theater was built by George A. Fuller, who also built the Flatiron Building in New York City.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tennessee Theatre is culturally significant as a historic movie palace and performing arts venue. It was designated "The Official State Theatre of Tennessee" and is home to the Knoxville Opera and the Knoxville Symphony Orchestra. It has hosted numerous Broadway productions and classic films, and has been featured in movies.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venue and movie theater
world knowledge.Details: The theater features a Wurlitzer organ, restored in 2001, and has been used as a filming location for movies such as October Sky and The Last Movie Star. The theater's seating capacity is now 1,645 patrons after renovations.

world knowledge.Name: Aston Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Aston Hall is a Grade I listed Jacobean house in Aston, Birmingham, England, designed by John Thorpe and built between 1618 and 1635. It is a leading example of the Jacobean prodigy house. The house was severely damaged after an attack by Parliamentary troops in 1643. It remained in the Holte family until 1817, when it was sold and leased by James Watt Jr. The house was purchased in 1858 by a private company for use as a public park and museum. After financial difficulties, it was bought by the Birmingham Corporation in 1864, becoming the first historic country house to pass into municipal ownership.

Major_Events.Description: The house was severely damaged, with some damage still evident, including a hole in the staircase from a cannonball.
Aston Hall became the first historic country house to pass into municipal ownership.
A pageant with around 10,000 performers was held in the grounds to commemorate the centenary of Birmingham becoming a borough.
A major renovation of Aston Hall was completed, allowing it to reopen to the public.
Aston Hall became home to a parkrun, a free, weekly timed 5 km run, which ceased running in August 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Jacobean architectural style designed by John Thorpe.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aston Hall is a leading example of the Jacobean prodigy house and holds significant historical importance as the first historic country house to pass into municipal ownership. It has been a community museum and is a Grade I listed building.
world knowledge.Details: Aston Hall is now a community museum managed by Birmingham Museums Trust. It is open to the public during spring, summer, and autumn months. The mansion was named the UK's top haunted heritage site in October 2019. The easternmost part of the grounds made way for the A38(M) motorway, which opened in 1972.

world knowledge.Name: University of Virginia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Virginia (UVA) is a public research university founded in 1819 by Thomas Jefferson. It contains his Academical Village, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The original governing Board of Visitors included three U.S. presidents: Jefferson, James Madison, and James Monroe. UVA has been a member of the Association of American Universities since 1904 and is known for its historic foundations, student-run honor code, and secret societies.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded by Thomas Jefferson and chartered by the Commonwealth of Virginia.
The Rotunda burned to a shell due to an electrical fire. It was later rebuilt by architect Stanford White.
Gregory Swanson sued to gain entrance into the university's law school, leading to the integration of UVA.
The Academical Village and nearby Monticello were designated as a joint World Heritage Site.
Three students were killed and two others injured in a shooting on a charter bus returning from a class trip.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's design revolves around the Academical Village, with the Rotunda as its centerpiece, inspired by the Pantheon in Rome. The Lawn is a grand, terraced green space surrounded by residential and academic buildings. The design includes ten Pavilions with unique classical architectural styles and walled gardens separated by Jeffersonian Serpentine walls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UVA is culturally significant as the first university in the United States to be designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It represents Jefferson's vision of an academic community focused on secular education and intellectual freedom. The university's honor system, secret societies, and architectural innovations have made it a model for other institutions.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers 48 bachelor's degree programs, 94 master's degree programs, and 55 doctoral degree programs. It has a strong emphasis on research, with significant contributions in fields like hypersonic flight and neuroscience. UVA's athletics programs have won multiple NCAA championships, and its alumni include Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and prominent political figures.

world knowledge.Name: Jack County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jack County Courthouse is the fourth courthouse building to serve the county, completed in 1940. It replaced an 1885 courthouse. The first courthouse was established in 1858 in an already-existing wooden building on the west side of the Jacksboro town square, which was remodeled at a cost of $800.

Major_Events.Description: The Jack County Courthouse was completed in 1940, replacing the previous 1885 courthouse.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2012.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a three-story structure with a basement, featuring a cast-in-place concrete structure sheathed in Texas limestone with marble spandrels. It is designed in the Modern Classical Style, with fluted pilasters separating recessed vertically ranked window and spandrel bays, and an entablature with low relief sculpture. The interior includes original decorative light fixtures, stone and wood paneled wall veneers, decorative moldings, door hardware, duct covers, and aluminum cashier window screens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jack County Courthouse is a rich example of the Modern Classical Style and retains a very high degree of architectural integrity. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, recognizing its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse was designed by Wichita Falls architects Voelker & Dixon in 1939 and built by Eckert-Fair Construction. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2012 (NRHP reference No. 12001002).

world knowledge.Name: Praia do Almoxarife
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Praia do Almoxarife is a civil parish in the municipality of Horta, on the island of Faial in the Azores. It was the beachhead of early settlement on the island, first used by explorers and then by new colonists. In 1466, Josse van Huerter and his Flemish compatriots landed here, initially hoping to discover precious metals. Despite early challenges, a small settlement persisted through the centuries. The parish has faced significant events, including a sack by English privateers in 1597 and damage from earthquakes, notably in 1926 and 1998.

Major_Events.Description: Josse van Huerter and his Flemish compatriots landed on the beach, initially hoping to discover precious metals.
English privateers sacked and burned down the buildings in the parish.
The earthquake destroyed 204 out of 220 houses in Praia do Almoxarife.
The parish church, Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Graça, was severely damaged by an earthquake and later repaired.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The parish features traditional island-style houses and the Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Graça, a baroque-style church rebuilt in 1758 with two side chapels and two tall towers. The church was severely damaged by an earthquake in 1998 and repaired afterwards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Praia do Almoxarife is culturally significant as the beachhead of early settlement on Faial and for its historical events, including the settlement by Flemish explorers and the sack by English privateers. The parish church and the tradition of masses of penance, devotion, and thanksgiving also highlight its cultural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourist destination and summer vacation spot
world knowledge.Details: Praia do Almoxarife has become an important summer destination and tourist center due to its long black sand beach. The community has developed a certain touristic infrastructure around Largo Coronel Silva Leal, the central square of Praia do Almoxarife.

image_name: Catedral de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe

world knowledge.Name: Catedral de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe
world knowledge.Address: Plaza Las Delicias Ponce, Puerto Rico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Catedral de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, also known as Ponce Cathedral, is the cathedral for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Ponce. Its history dates back to 1670 when a small chapel was built on the site. It has been damaged several times by fires and earthquakes. The current structure, completed in 1839, was declared a cathedral in 1924 by Pope Pius XI. It was reconstructed from 1931 to 1937 by architect Francisco Porrata Doria, who added a neoclassical facade.

Major_Events.Description: On 17 September 1692, the King of Spain, Carlos II, issued a Cédula Real (Royal Permit) designating the chapel as a parish church.
The original parish church was demolished in 1835 to build a larger church, which was completed and opened for worship in 1839.
Pope Pius XI declared the church a cathedral in 1924.
The church was reconstructed to a design by architect Francisco Porrata Doria, adding a neoclassical facade and other improvements.
The building was damaged and temporarily closed as a result of the 2020 Puerto Rico earthquakes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is designed in the neoclassical style with a cruciform plan, featuring a large dome at the crossing. The interior consists of a main nave and two large aisles separated by a series of eight arcades. The facade is pale blue and gray, while the interior is blue and beige. It has two three-story square towers, stained glass windows, and a large pipe organ.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Ponce and for its role in the religious and cultural life of Ponce. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984 and is a key part of the Ponce Historic Zone.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral hosts the annual event 'Las Mañanitas' on 12 December, celebrating the day of the Virgin of Guadalupe. It also holds a midnight Mass known as Misa de Gallo on 24 December. The building was damaged by the 2020 Puerto Rico earthquakes and temporarily closed.

world knowledge.Name: Crowdy Head Light
world knowledge.Address: Crowdy Head, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Crowdy Head Light is an active lighthouse located at Crowdy Head, a headland between Forster and Port Macquarie, New South Wales, Australia. The first station in the area was a pilot station established in 1860 at nearby Harrington, assisting ships navigating the entrance of the Manning River. The current lighthouse is the last of five lighthouses of similar design designed and built by James Barnet in 1878–80.

Major_Events.Description: The apparatus was converted to a carbide lamp (acetylene gas), with an intensity of 1,500 cd. The light was automated at the same time.
The pilot station was closed in the 1960s.
The light was converted to mains electricity.
The 4th order Fresnel lens was sold on eBay for $20,000 and is now on display at Sea Girt Light in New Jersey.
Conversion to an LED light source was completed with the addition of a Sealite SL-300 single tier high intensity beacon, with a range of 16 nautical miles.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The circular tower is capped by an oversailing bluestone platform supported by shaped bluestone corbels. It can be reached by a metal stair from the concrete slab which forms the ground floor and foundation for the buildings. The tower walls of stone bricks taper off from a thickness of 19 inches (480 mm) at the base to 14 inches (360 mm) at the top. A porch, roofed just above door height, connects the tower to a rectangular annexe, which originally contained a duty room for the keeper and a store for fuel. All the external walls of the structure are cement rendered and painted white. The platform is surmounted by a simple metal domed lantern which encloses the optical apparatus. A handrail at the platform perimeter is of white painted cast iron standards with wrought iron rails.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Crowdy Head Light is registered with the Register of the National Estate and is managed by Transport for NSW, while the site is managed by the New South Wales Department of Lands.
world knowledge.Details: The grounds of the lighthouse are open, but the tower is closed. The light is managed by Transport for NSW, while the site is managed by the New South Wales Department of Lands. The original light was a fixed white light from a 4th order catadioptric apparatus with an intensity of less than 1,000 cd. It was staffed by one keeper.

world knowledge.Name: Hollywood Theatre (Portland, Oregon)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hollywood Theatre is a historic movie theater built in 1926. It was commissioned by the theatre chain Jensen and Herberg and designed by architects Bennes and Herzog. The theater opened on July 17, 1926, with 1,491 seats, as a venue for vaudeville and silent movies. It became a Cinerama theater in 1961 and was later divided into three auditoriums in 1975. The theater became a non-profit organization in 1997 and underwent major renovations starting in 2011.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened as a venue for vaudeville and silent movies with 1,491 seats.
The theater utilized the ultra-widescreen Cinerama process until 1963.
Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey opened and ran for over 10 months.
The theater was divided into three auditoriums and ran second-run films.
The theater became a non-profit organization.
Renovations included new seats, screens, sound systems, and an updated paint job.
The theater became the sole remaining theater in Oregon with 70-millimeter capability.
Plans were announced to open an annex theater at Portland International Airport.
The Hollywood Theatre purchased the iconic Portland video store Movie Madness and its collection of over 90,000 movies.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in multiple styles including Spanish Colonial Revival (exterior) and after the Baths of Caracalla and Bernini (interior).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hollywood Theatre is a central historical landmark of the Hollywood District and was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983. It is considered a gem of Northeast Portland's historic culture and tradition and is the only theater in Oregon showing movies in 70mm film.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Movie theater showcasing first-run films, classic cinema, independent and experimental films, with a focus on repertory films on 35-millimeter and 70-millimeter.
world knowledge.Details: The theater is self-owned and operated by a non-profit organization. It has a main auditorium with a 50-foot screen and 384 seats, and two smaller auditoriums seating 111 each. The theater also hosts special guests and plans to open an annex theater at Portland International Airport.

world knowledge.Name: Parc Oriental de Maulévrier
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The park was created between 1899-1913 on the grounds of Château Colbert by noted Parisian architect Alexandre Marcel for the château's industrialist owner. After Marcel's death in 1928, the park fell into desolation for 40 years until restoration began in 1987. By 2004, the garden was named a "Jardin Remarquable" by the ministry of culture.

Major_Events.Description: The park was designed by Alexandre Marcel for the owner of Château Colbert.
Restoration began based upon photographs and memories.
The garden was named a "Jardin Remarquable" by the ministry of culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Japanese garden with Khmer elements, water features, a bridge, a pagoda, and about 300 plant species including azaleas, camellias, rhododendrons, and Japanese maples.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is the largest Japanese garden in Europe and reflects the fusion of Japanese and Khmer architectural styles. It is a significant example of early 20th-century landscape design and cultural exchange.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and cultural exhibition space
world knowledge.Details: The park contains a permanent exhibition of bonsai and ceramics. It is open daily except Monday in the warmer months; an admission fee is charged.

world knowledge.Name: Clermont Auvergne University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Clermont Auvergne University was created with the merger of Blaise Pascal University and the University of Auvergne on 1 January 2017. Discussions about the possibility of merging the two universities were started in 2012, and the merging was officially announced on 23 September 2013. The name of the new university was publicly announced in January 2015. The merging was officialized by a government decree on 13 September 2016, and effective as of January 1, 2017. On January 1, 2021, Clermont-Auvergne University status changed and it became an experimental public establishment (EPE) and integrated the National Polytechnic Clermont Auvergne Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Blaise Pascal University and University of Auvergne
Major_Events.Description: The two universities merged to form Clermont Auvergne University.
The merging was officially announced on 23 September 2013 by the two university presidents.
The name of the new university was publicly announced in January 2015.
The merging was officialized by a government decree on 13 September 2016.

Major_Events.Event: Status change to experimental public establishment
Major_Events.Description: Clermont-Auvergne University became an experimental public establishment (EPE) and integrated the National Polytechnic Clermont Auvergne Institute.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Clermont Auvergne University is a public research university with its main campus in Clermont-Ferrand, France. It comprises 22 components, divided into Training and Research Units (UFR, formerly faculties), Schools and Institutes (IUT). The university has several campuses in Clermont-Ferrand and throughout the Auvergne region.
world knowledge.Details: The university has several campuses in Clermont-Ferrand and throughout the Auvergne region. Near the city center of Clermont, there is the Carnot site to the east and the Gergovia site to the south. The Cézeaux campus is located further south in the neighboring town of Aubière. The Clermont Auvergne University Institute of Technology is also present in Aurillac, Clermont-Ferrand, Montluçon, Moulins, Le Puy and Vichy. The institute that trains teachers for the national public education is present in Chamalières, Moulins, Le Puy and Aurillac.

world knowledge.Name: Mapo Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Mapo District and Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mapo Bridge was constructed between 1968 and 1970, originally named Seoul Bridge. It was renamed Mapo Bridge in 1984. Due to increasing traffic and structural issues, a new bridge was constructed adjacent to the old one, completed in 2000. The old bridge was repaired and reopened in 2005 as the 2nd Mapo Bridge. The bridge has been a site of numerous suicide attempts, leading to various prevention measures.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was constructed and opened as Seoul Bridge.
The bridge was renamed from Seoul Bridge to Mapo Bridge.
A new bridge was constructed adjacent to the old one due to structural concerns.
The old bridge was repaired and reopened as the 2nd Mapo Bridge.
Samsung Life Insurance and Cheil Worldwide installed pictures, words, and a statue to deter suicides.
Barriers were extended, and AI monitoring was introduced to prevent suicides.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Girder bridge design, originally designed to carry up to 32 metric tons per vehicle. The bridge underwent significant repairs and reconstruction of the upper portion in the early 2000s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mapo Bridge is a significant transportation link in Seoul and has gained notoriety due to its high suicide rate. Efforts to prevent suicides have made it a symbol of both tragedy and resilience.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (10 lanes of National Route 46 and Seoul Subway Line 5 passes underneath through an underwater tunnel).
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has been a site of numerous suicide attempts, leading to various prevention measures including motion sensors, lights with encouraging phrases, and extended barriers. Despite initial failures, recent measures have reduced suicide attempts. The bridge is also known as the 'Bridge of Life' due to these efforts.

world knowledge.Name: Rwenzori Mountains
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 120 km (75 mi) long and 65 km (40 mi) wide
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Formed about three million years ago in the late Pliocene epoch
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rwenzori Mountains are a range of mountains located on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. They are the highest non-volcanic, non-orogenic mountains in the world. The mountains are occasionally identified with the legendary 'Mountains of the Moon', described in antiquity as the source of the Nile River. Modern European explorers observed the range beginning in the late nineteenth century. The mountains have been a sanctuary for various rebel groups throughout history.

Major_Events.Event: First traverse of the six massifs
Major_Events.Description: Polish climbers Janusz Chalecki, Stanisław Cholewa, and Leszek S. Czarnecki completed the first traverse of the six massifs of the Ruwenzori.
The Duke of Abruzzi mounted an expedition to the Ruwenzori, scaling the highest peaks and naming several of them.
The secessionist Rwenzururu movement fought an insurgency in the mountains.

Major_Events.Event: Allied Democratic Forces move into the mountains
Major_Events.Description: After being defeated across the border by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, some elements of the Allied Democratic Forces moved into the Rwenzori Mountains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mountains are composed of an uplifted block of crystalline rocks including gneiss, amphibolite, granite, and quartzite. They consist of six massifs separated by deep gorges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rwenzori Mountains are culturally and historically significant due to their association with the legendary 'Mountains of the Moon' and their role as a sanctuary for various rebel groups. They are also a World Heritage Site and support unique vegetation and biodiversity.
world knowledge.Details: The Rwenzori Mountains are known for their vegetation, ranging from tropical rainforest through alpine meadows to snow. The range supports its own species and varieties of giant groundsel and giant lobelia. The mountains are covered jointly by Rwenzori Mountains National Park in southwestern Uganda and the Virunga National Park in the eastern Congo. Climate change has significantly impacted the glaciers of the Ruwenzori, with a notable reduction in glacier area over the past century.

world knowledge.Name: Jeonju National Museum
