world knowledge.Address: 249 Ssukgogae-ro, Wansan-gu, Jeonju-si, Jeollabuk-do, 55070, Republic of Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jeonju National Museum is a national museum located in Jeonju, Jeollabuk-do, South Korea. It opened on October 26, 1990, as the ninth South Korean national museum.

Major_Events.Description: The Jeonju National Museum opened on October 26, 1990, as the ninth national museum in South Korea.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Main Building comprises three permanent exhibits: an Archeology room, a Fine Art room, a Folklore room, and one special exhibit room.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a national museum, it plays a crucial role in preserving and showcasing the cultural heritage of South Korea, particularly in the Jeollabuk-do region.
world knowledge.Details: This article related to a museum in South Korea is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Donnington Grove
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Donnington Grove is a Strawberry Hill Gothic mansion built in 1763 for James Pettit Andrews. It was later owned by William Brummell, who expanded the estate. The property was requisitioned by Allied Supplies in 1940 and later sold to Reginald Fellows. It remained in the Fellows family until the early 1990s, when it became a country club.

Major_Events.Description: The mansion was built for James Pettit Andrews in the Strawberry Hill Gothic style.
William Brummell expanded the estate to 800 acres, extended the house and stables, and erected entrance lodges.
The estate was requisitioned during World War II.
Donnington Grove was converted into a country club and golf course.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Strawberry Hill Gothic style, characterized by its Gothic revival elements and elaborate design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Donnington Grove is an example of Strawberry Hill Gothic architecture and has historical ties to notable figures like Beau Brummell and the Fellows family.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hotel, country club, and golf course
world knowledge.Details: The golf course was designed by Dave Thomas and features a mix of higher ground and parkland with trees and water hazards. The property was briefly named 'Parasampia' in the early 2000s before reverting to its original name.

world knowledge.Name: Hønefoss Church
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hønefoss Church is a historic church in the Ringerike municipality in Buskerud county, Norway. The original wooden church, designed by Christian Heinrich Grosch, was completed in 1862. It burned down on 26 January 2010 due to an electrical fault, and a new replacement church was constructed on the same site and opened in 2017.

Major_Events.Description: The church was inaugurated on 10 December 1862.
A new chapel was dedicated in 1894.
The church was restored and reopened in 1952.
The church burned down on 26 January 2010 due to an electrical fault in the heating system.
A new replacement church was constructed on the same site and opened in 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original church was designed in the Gothic Revival style by Christian Heinrich Grosch. It had a 40-meter (130 ft) church tower and accommodated approximately 350 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hønefoss Church is a significant historical and cultural landmark in the Ringerike municipality, serving as a religious and community center. Its destruction and subsequent reconstruction highlight its importance to the local community.
world knowledge.Details: The church had its own cemetery, burial chapel, crematorium, and a modern assembly room (Kirkestua). The fire in 2010 was caused by a faulty contact in a cable for the electric heating ovens, as concluded by the police investigation.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Villa of Monza
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Villa of Monza, also known as the Palace of Monza, is a neoclassical palace built by the Habsburgs as a private residence during the Austrian domination of the 18th century. It served as the residence of the viceroy during the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy and the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia. The villa was abandoned by the royal family after the assassination of King Umberto I in 1900. Today, it hosts exhibitions and houses the Artistic High School of Monza.

Major_Events.Description: King Umberto I was assassinated in Monza by anarchist Gaetano Bresci while attending a sports event.
After a long period of degradation, the villa underwent extensive renovation and was inaugurated on September 8, 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Royal Villa is a neoclassical building designed by Giuseppe Piermarini, inspired by Schönbrunn Palace and the Royal Palace of Caserta. It features a U-shaped plan with grand salons, halls, and royal apartments. The interior decoration includes stuccoes, frescoes, and furniture by renowned artists. The complex includes the Royal Chapel, the Cavallerizza, the Rotonda dell'Appiani, the Teatrino di Corte, and the Orangerie.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Villa of Monza is a symbol of the Austrian and Italian royal heritage. It represents the historical link between Vienna and Milan and is an important cultural site in Northern Italy.
world knowledge.Details: The villa, royal gardens, and park are managed by the Consorzio Villa Reale and Parco di Monza. It hosts temporary art exhibitions and annual events such as fireworks shows and concerts. The Consortium aims to promote tourism and cultural activities in the region.

world knowledge.Name: Solkan Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Solkan Bridge is a 219.7-meter arch bridge over the Soča River, originally built to carry the Bohinj Railway during the Vienna Secession period. It was officially opened in 1906. The bridge was designed by architect Rudolf Jaussner and engineer Leopold Oerley, with a central span built by Brüder Redlich und Berger and end viaducts by Sard, Lenassi & Co. Initially planned as a steel arched bridge, it was later constructed as a stone bridge due to the light soil conditions. It is the world's longest stone arch railroad bridge.

Major_Events.Description: The Bohinj Railway from Jesenice to Gorizia was inaugurated, with Austrian heir Franz Ferdinand traveling across the bridge.
Austrian soldiers destroyed the bridge using 930 kilograms of Ecrasite to prevent invading forces from using it.
The Italians rebuilt the bridge after World War I, completing it in 1927 with four sub-arches instead of the original five.

Major_Events.Event: Aerial bombing during World War II
Major_Events.Description: The bridge suffered minimal damage during World War II, with bombs missing the bridge or failing to explode.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Solkan Bridge is a stone arch bridge with a span of 85 meters, built using 4,533 stone blocks. It features a central stone arch and end viaducts, originally designed with five sub-arches but later rebuilt with four.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Solkan Bridge is culturally significant as the world's longest stone arch railroad bridge, representing early 20th-century engineering and architectural achievements. It played a crucial role in the Bohinj Railway and witnessed significant historical events during both World Wars.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was initially planned as a steel arched bridge but was changed to a stone bridge due to soil conditions. It was rebuilt after World War I and survived World War II with minimal damage.

world knowledge.Name: Sam Houston Ship Channel Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Sam Houston Tollway, Harris County, Texas
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,560 feet (480 m) (main bridge), 2 miles (3.2 km) (total length)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sam Houston Tollway Ship Channel Bridge, originally named the Jesse H. Jones Memorial Bridge, was opened in May 1982. It was acquired by the Harris County Toll Road Authority in 1994. The bridge was part of a larger project initiated in the 1950s and faced multiple funding and construction challenges before completion. It was the longest box girder span in the Western Hemisphere until 1997.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to traffic on May 6, 1982, becoming the longest box girder span in the Western Hemisphere.
Due to insufficient traffic volume, the bonds were refinanced at a higher interest rate of 12.625 percent.
Harris County took over the bridge from the Texas Turnpike Authority.
Cash tolls were eliminated, making the bridge EZ TAG only.
Construction began on a twin-span cable-stayed bridge to replace the existing one, with completion expected in 2025 and 2027.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a cantilevered concrete trapezoidal haunched hollow box girder bridge. It has a total length of 1,560 feet (480 m) for the main bridge and 2 miles (3.2 km) in total length. The longest span is 750 feet (230 m), and it has a clearance below of 175 feet (53 m).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant engineering feat and a critical transportation link over the Houston Ship Channel. It represents the evolution of bridge design and construction techniques in the United States.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries four lanes of the Sam Houston Tollway over the Houston Ship Channel, facilitating vehicular traffic in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge faced financial and traffic volume challenges post-construction. In 2018, a replacement project began, but design flaws caused delays. The new bridges will each carry four lanes of one-way traffic, with the existing bridge to be demolished upon completion of the southbound span. Electronic tolling continues throughout the project.

world knowledge.Name: University of Cauca
world knowledge.Address: Street 5 Number. 4-70, Popayan, Popayán, Cauca, Colombia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Cauca was created on April 24, 1827, by a decree by the President Francisco de Paula Santander and was installed on November 11, 1827. It has roots in the Major Seminary of Popayan, an educational establishment in colonial times that had a significant impact on the philosophical, political, and scientific ideas of the 18th century Enlightenment. The university has been a center of knowledge and democratic discourse in Colombia, with a dynamic research structure and numerous academic programs.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Cauca was founded by decree of President Francisco de Paula Santander.
The nationalization of the university was ratified by Law 65 of 1964.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Cauca is culturally and historically significant as it has been a center of education and democratic discourse in Colombia since its foundation. It has produced numerous notable alumni, including 17 graduates who have held the Colombian head of state. The university also has a valuable historical archive with documents from the colonial and independence periods.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Cauca offers 43 undergraduate programs and 48 postgraduate programs, including 29 specializations, 14 Masters, and 5 PhDs. It has a strong research focus and is affiliated with several academic organizations. The university's historical archive contains important documents from the colonial and independence periods, attracting historians and social scientists.

world knowledge.Name: St Mary's Cathedral, Killarney
world knowledge.Location: New Street, Killarney, County Kerry, Ireland
world knowledge.Address: New Street, Killarney, County Kerry, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Mary's Cathedral, Killarney, is the cathedral church of the Diocese of Kerry situated to the west of Killarney in County Kerry, Ireland. Designed by the renowned English architect Augustus Welby Pugin, who drew inspiration from the ruins of Ardfert Cathedral. Construction began in 1842 but was interrupted several times due to the great famine and lack of funds. The interior decorations were designed by James Joseph McCarthy, and the building was ready for regular worship in 1855. The spire and nave were completed in 1907 by the Irish architects Ashlin and Coleman of Dublin.

Major_Events.Description: The building was ready for regular worship.
The spire and nave were completed by the Irish architects Ashlin and Coleman of Dublin.
The cathedral was reordered under the direction of Bishop Eamonn Casey, resulting in the removal or damage of many original interior features.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic revival style, constructed with limestone. The width of the nave was based on medieval models found throughout Ireland and England. The west end features three tall lancet windows and a low entrance door. The stonework is an attractive mixture of brown and grey stone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Mary's Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the cathedral church of the Diocese of Kerry and for its Gothic revival architecture designed by Augustus Welby Pugin. Its design was inspired by the ruins of Ardfert Cathedral, and it stands as a notable example of 19th-century ecclesiastical architecture in Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral was reordered in 1973 under the direction of Bishop Eamonn Casey, which involved the removal of all internal Victorian plasterwork, the original reredos, altar, and screens. A new sanctuary was created at the crossing, and new liturgical furniture made of Tasmanian oak was installed.

world knowledge.Name: Western Digital Stadium Kitakami
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was opened in 1997 and was formerly known as Kitakami Stadium. Its naming rights were acquired by Western Digital LLC from October 2023 to September 2028.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface, multi-use stadium primarily for track and field events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Serves as a significant sports venue in Kitakami, Iwate, supporting local athletics and events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 22,000 people and is owned by the City of Kitakami, operated by the Kitakami Sports Association.

world knowledge.Name: William Jefferson Clinton Federal Building
world knowledge.Address: 12th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue, NW Washington, D.C.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The William Jefferson Clinton Federal Building is a complex of several historic buildings in the Federal Triangle, originally part of a blighted neighborhood known as Murder Bay. It was redeveloped in the 1930s under Treasury Secretary Andrew W. Mellon. The complex includes the former New Post Office Building, the Interstate Commerce Commission (ICC) building, and the Department of Labor Building. It was renamed in honor of President Bill Clinton in 2013.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of New Post Office Building
Major_Events.Description: The New Post Office Building was completed, designed by architects William Adams Delano and Chester Holmes Aldrich in a neoclassical style inspired by the Place Vendôme in Paris.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Ariel Rios Federal Building
Major_Events.Description: Congress renamed the New Post Office Building in honor of Ariel Rios, an undercover BATFE special agent killed in the line of duty.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to William Jefferson Clinton Federal Building
Major_Events.Description: The building was renamed in honor of former President Bill Clinton, and the designation was extended to include the adjacent ICC and Labor buildings.
The building was formally dedicated at a ceremony attended by Bill Clinton and former EPA Administrator Carol Browner.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical design with bas relief panels by Adolph Alexander Weinman. Features a seven-story marble spiral staircase with a chandelier and a chrome and brass globe. The exterior includes a semicircular façade inspired by the Place Vendôme in Paris.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is part of the Pennsylvania Avenue National Historic Site and represents a significant example of 1930s federal architecture. It houses New Deal artworks, which, while controversial, offer insight into the cultural attitudes of the era.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently serves as the headquarters of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Previously housed the Post Office Department, BATFE, and other federal agencies.
world knowledge.Details: The building complex includes the original New Post Office Building, the ICC Building, and the Department of Labor Building. It features preserved 1920s-1930s architectural details and a local branch post office called Benjamin Franklin Station. The building also flanks the historic Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium. Controversial New Deal murals in the building depict stereotypes of Native Americans, African Americans, and women, reflecting the cultural attitudes of the 1930s.

world knowledge.Name: Mardin Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mardin Museum was originally located in the Zincirli Medrese, a building constructed by the Artukids in the 14th century. The current museum building was constructed by the Syriac Catholic Church of Antioch in 1895. It served various purposes in the 20th century before being purchased by the Ministry of Culture, restored, and opened as a museum in 1995.

Major_Events.Description: The building was restored and opened as a museum by the Ministry of Culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is made of cut limestone with unique ornaments on internal and external vaults, arches, rails, and column heads. It is a three-storey building with reception, conference, exhibition, and resting halls on the ground floor, ethnography hall and library on the upper floor, and administrative offices and archaeology section on the uppermost floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses artifacts from various historical periods, including the Bronze Age, Assyrian, Urartu, Hellenistic, Achaemenid Empire, Roman Empire, Byzantine Empire, Seljuks, Artukids, and the Ottoman Empire, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include silver works from the Midyat district, such as necklaces, earrings, bracelets, anklets, diadems, hair jewelry, and copper and silver ornaments. Additionally, it exhibits clothes, swords, prayer beads, and coffee sets (locally known as mırra). Archaeological exhibits include tools, stamps, figurines, jewelry, ceramics, coins, tear bottles, and candles from various historical periods.

world knowledge.Name: Rwang Pam Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Ibrahim Dasuki Street, Off Zaria Bypass, Jos, Nigeria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium is primarily used for football matches and was previously used for track events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is the home venue for local football teams Plateau United, Pepsi F.A., and Mighty Jets F.C., making it significant for sports in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium, primarily for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 15,000 spectators. Means of transport available for reaching the stadium include cars, buses, and bikes.

world knowledge.Name: University of Jena
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Jena, officially the Friedrich Schiller University Jena, is a public research university established in 1558. It is one of the ten oldest universities in Germany and has been affiliated with six Nobel Prize winners. The university was renamed after the poet Friedrich Schiller, who was a professor of philosophy there. It played a central role in the emergence of German idealism and early Romanticism.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established on February 2, 1558, by Elector John Frederick of Saxony and his sons, after obtaining a charter from Emperor Ferdinand I.
The university was renamed Friedrich Schiller University in 1934, after the poet Friedrich Schiller who was a professor there.
Jena graduate Herbert Kroemer won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university is characterized by its historic buildings and modern facilities, including the university main building, the Botanical Garden, and various institutes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Jena is culturally and historically significant due to its role in the development of German idealism, early Romanticism, and its association with notable figures such as Friedrich Schiller, Johann Gottlieb Fichte, and G. W. F. Hegel. It has also been a center for political radicalism and scientific research.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Jena has around 19,000 students and 375 professors as of 2014. It is organized into 10 schools and focuses on both humanities and sciences. The university is affiliated with the Coimbra Group and the EUA. It has several notable collections open to the public, including the Jena Phyletisches Museum, the Ernst-Haeckel-Memorial Museum, and the Mineralogical Collection.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio de La Cartuja
world knowledge.Address: Isla de la Cartuja, Seville, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Completed in 1999 for the World Championships in Athletics, the stadium was expanded in 2025. It was part of Seville's bids for the 2004 and 2008 Summer Olympics. The stadium is currently managed by Sociedad Estadio Olímpico de Sevilla S.A., with ownership shared among various government entities and football clubs.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was completed for this event.
The final match between Celtic and Porto was held here.
The stadium hosted the Davis Cup final twice, with a temporary roof installed for the clay court.
The stadium was chosen to host four Copa del Rey finals.
The stadium replaced San Mamés Stadium in Bilbao as a host venue due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The stadium hosted two matches of the tournament.
The stadium was re-inaugurated after expansion to 70,000 seats.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a grass surface and was designed by architects Antonio Cruz Villalón and Antonio Ortiz García. The 2025 expansion included the removal of the athletics track and the addition of a glass roof.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is the 4th-largest in Spain and the largest in Andalusia. It has hosted significant sporting and musical events, contributing to its cultural importance in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The stadium is primarily used for football matches and major sporting events, but it also hosts concerts and other large gatherings.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 70,000 seats after the 2025 expansion. It is planned to host matches during the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The stadium has also been used for concerts by internationally renowned artists, setting attendance records for single-day concerts in Spain.

world knowledge.Name: Porto de Galinhas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Porto Rico (Rich Port) until 1850, it became a hub for illegal slave trading, where slaves were transported alongside guineafowl. The name 'Porto de Galinhas' originated from the traffickers' password 'Tem galinha nova no porto' ('There are new chickens in the port'). The municipality of Ipojuca was established on November 12, 1895.

Major_Events.Description: The municipality of Ipojuca, where Porto de Galinhas lies, was officially established.
The location became a center for illegal slave trading, leading to its current name.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Porto de Galinhas is culturally significant due to its historical role in slave trading and its current status as a top tourist destination. It has been voted 'Best Brazilian Beach' multiple times for its natural beauty, ecological trails, and proximity to Recife.
world knowledge.Details: Porto de Galinhas is famous for its bright-water beaches and natural pools. It is located 60 kilometers south of Recife and is renowned for its hotel infrastructure and accessibility. It has won the 'Best Brazilian Beach' award eight times in a row by Voyage & Tourism Brazilian magazine.

world knowledge.Name: Capesthorne Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Capesthorne Hall is a country house near the village of Siddington, Cheshire, England. The house and its private chapel were built in the early 18th century, replacing an earlier hall and chapel nearby. It has undergone several renovations and rebuilds, including after a major fire in 1861. The hall is privately owned by the Bromley-Davenport family and is open to the public for visits and events.

Major_Events.Description: The main part of the house was virtually destroyed by fire, leaving only the wings, the loggia, and part of the front wall.
The house was remodelled by Edward Blore, including the addition of an extension and a frontage in Jacobean style.
The hall was used by the Red Cross during the Second World War.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hall is built in red brick with ashlar dressings and slate roofs. It features a Jacobean architectural style with a symmetrical plan, including a central block in three storeys with lateral wings and turrets. The interior includes a drawing room, dining room, sculpture gallery, and various other rooms with panelled ceilings and ornate fireplaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Capesthorne Hall is a Grade II* listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance. It represents the evolution of English country house architecture through various periods and styles.
world knowledge.Details: The hall is surrounded by landscaped gardens, parkland, and a lake. It includes several listed structures such as a private chapel, gates, a bridge, an icehouse, and a lodge. The hall and its grounds are used for public visits, weddings, corporate events, and other special occasions.

world knowledge.Name: GreenWood
world knowledge.Historical_Background: GreenWood, formerly GreenWood Forest Park and The GreenWood Centre, is a family fun park opened by Stephen and Andrea Bristow in 1993. Initially an environmental education project, it evolved into a popular attraction with rides and activities. The park was sold to Continuum Attractions in 2017 after the Bristows retired.

Major_Events.Description: GreenWood opened with walks and guided tours as an environmental education project.
The park's popularity grew after the opening of a slide, attracting over 60,000 visitors that year.
An 11-year-old boy fell to his death after being wrongly attached to the zip wire ride. The incident led to calls for more regulations for zip wire rides.
A new water ride and solar panels were unveiled, generating 80% of the park's power requirements.
Stephen and Andrea Bristow retired and sold the park to Continuum Attractions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features adventure playgrounds, longbow shooting, slides, and rides, including the world's first people-powered roller coaster, the Green Dragon.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: GreenWood is significant for its environmental education initiatives, family-friendly attractions, and efforts to promote sustainability. It has received environmental awards and high rankings among UK theme parks.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Family fun park and environmental education center.
world knowledge.Details: The park attracts around 150,000 visitors annually. It has received funding from the Welsh Government for sustainable projects and was fined £45,000 for health and safety breaches related to the SwampFlyer accident. Stephen Bristow received an MBE in 2009 for services to the tourist industry in North Wales.

world knowledge.Name: University of Turku
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Turku was established in 1920 as a multidisciplinary public university in Turku, Finland. It was founded by the Finnish intelligentsia to provide a Finnish-speaking university, following the establishment of Åbo Akademi, a Swedish-speaking institution. The university has grown significantly since its founding and now includes multiple campuses and research stations.

Major_Events.Event: Founding of the University of Turku
Major_Events.Description: The University of Turku was founded on Kalevala Day (February 28) in 1920, following a successful fundraising campaign by 22,040 people. It was the first Finnish-speaking university in Finland.

Major_Events.Event: Merger with Turku School of Economics
Major_Events.Description: The Turku School of Economics merged with the University of Turku, forming a seventh faculty of the university.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Faculty of Technology
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Technology was established as the eighth faculty of the University of Turku.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Turku is culturally significant as it was the first Finnish-speaking university in Finland, established after the country gained independence. Its motto, 'The gift of a free people to free science,' reflects its role in promoting education and research in a newly independent nation.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Turku is a member of the Coimbra Group and the European Campus of City-Universities (EC2U). It has approximately 22,000 degree students and offers bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees in both Finnish and English. The university has eight faculties and several independent research units, including the Brahea Centre, Turku PET Centre, and Finnish Centre for Astronomy with ESO. The university is also involved in research projects in the Peruvian Amazon.

world knowledge.Name: Citadel Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Citadel Park in Poznań, Poland is a large park on the site of Fort Winiary, a 19th-century fortified area north of the city centre. It contains a military museum, military cemeteries, and the remains of some of the fortifications. The site is listed as one of Poland's official national Historic Monuments, designated on November 28, 2008. In the post-war period, the site of Fort Winiary was converted into Cytadela park, with most of the fortifications demolished, although some structures remain.

Major_Events.Description: The site was listed as one of Poland's official national Historic Monuments on November 28, 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park contains a military museum, military cemeteries, remains of fortifications, a rosarium, an amphitheatre, walkways, open spaces, and various open-air sculpture displays.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and historically significant due to its origins as Fort Winiary, its designation as a national Historic Monument, and its role as a site of military history and commemoration, including military cemeteries and museums.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located within the Stare Miasto district of Poznań, south of Winogrady. It features a Commonwealth cemetery with graves of prisoners-of-war from World War I and airmen from World War II, as well as Polish and Soviet cemeteries. A "Heroes' Monument" overlooks the cemeteries at the main entrance to the park.

world knowledge.Name: South Ural State University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: South Ural State University (SUSU) was established on December 15, 1943, as Chelyabinsk Mechanics and Technology Institute (CMTI). It underwent several name changes and restructurings, becoming Chelyabinsk Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in 1951, Chelyabinsk State Technical University (CSTU) in 1990, and finally South Ural State University in 1997. The university played a significant role during the Great Patriotic War, training engineering cadres for the tank industry. It has grown into one of the top universities in Russia, with a focus on engineering and technical education.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Chelyabinsk Mechanical Engineering Institute
Major_Events.Description: The institute was established to train engineering cadres for the tank industry during the Great Patriotic War.
The institute was renamed and restructured to include new faculties such as Power Engineering, Metallurgy, and Mechanical Engineering.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Chelyabinsk State Technical University
Major_Events.Description: The university expanded its focus to include liberal arts specialties.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to South Ural State University
Major_Events.Description: The university transformed from an engineering-focused institution to a classic university.
The university was included in a project aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of Russian universities globally.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building of the university was expanded with two additional storeys, a tower, and a steeple covered in gold-simulating titanium nitride in 2001–04, in line with its initial 'Stalinist' engineering project.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SUSU is one of the top universities in Russia and has played a significant role in the country's industrial and technical development. It has a strong connection to the military and has been involved in various research and development projects.
world knowledge.Details: SUSU comprises 12 institutes and schools, one faculty, a military training center, and four branches. It offers a wide range of programs, including bachelor’s, master's, specialist, and post-graduate programs. The university has a robust athletic foundation, with graduates including Olympic champions and members of national Olympic teams. It also has a large library, several museums, and a university television and radio company.

world knowledge.Name: Ürümqi Tianshan International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ürümqi Tianshan International Airport, originally named Ürümqi Diwopu International Airport, was opened to foreign passengers in 1973. It has been a hub for China Southern Airlines and a focus city for Hainan Airlines. The airport was renamed in March 2025. It has undergone several renovations and expansions, including the construction of Terminal 3 in 2009 and an ongoing expansion project set to complete in 2025.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was opened to foreign passengers.
The airport was renamed from Ürümqi Diwopu International Airport to Ürümqi Tianshan International Airport.
Terminal 3 was opened, increasing the airport's capacity to handle more passengers and cargo.
A new terminal building (T4) and two additional runways are expected to open, with previous terminals converted to cargo relay stations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a newly built runway of 3,600 meters in length, capable of accommodating large aircraft like the Boeing 747. The apron covers 110,000 square meters and can accommodate over 30 aircraft. Terminal 3 added 22 jet bridges and nearly 106,000 square meters of new terminal space.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a key transportation hub in Northwest China, facilitating international and domestic travel. It plays a significant role in the Belt and Road Initiative, enhancing connectivity between Europe and Asia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International and domestic air travel, cargo transport
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by Line 1 of Ürümqi Metro, with additional metro stations (Terminal T4 and Airport East) expected to open in 2025. It handles over 25 million passengers annually and serves as a hub for China Southern Airlines and Urumqi Air, with Hainan Airlines as a focus city.

world knowledge.Name: Latrobe Gate
world knowledge.Address: 8th and M Street, SE Washington, D.C., United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Latrobe Gate is the ceremonial entrance to the U.S. Navy's oldest shore establishment, the Washington Navy Yard. Designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe, it was built in 1806 and substantially altered in 1881. The gate survived the British invasion during the War of 1812, where the Navy Yard was burned, and was one of only three structures not destroyed. It has served as a continuously manned Marine guardhouse since 1881.

Major_Events.Description: The gate was designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe and constructed as the ceremonial entrance to the Washington Navy Yard.
The Washington Navy Yard was burned during the British invasion, but the Latrobe Gate was one of only three structures that survived the fire.
The gate was substantially altered, and a Marine barracks was constructed around and over it, making it the oldest continuously manned Marine guardhouse in the U.S.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Latrobe Gate was added to the National Register of Historic Places on August 14, 1973.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Latrobe Gate is an example of Greek Revival and Italianate architecture. The original Greek Revival design was considered daring and symbolic of democracy. The 1881 alteration added a two-story brick Italianate structure above the gate and three-story sections on each side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Latrobe Gate is one of the nation's oldest extant examples of Greek Revival architecture and is a contributing property to the Washington Navy Yard's status as a National Historic Landmark. It symbolizes the early architectural innovation and the U.S. Navy's historical roots.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ceremonial entrance to the Washington Navy Yard and continuously manned Marine guardhouse.
world knowledge.Details: The Marines manning the Latrobe Gate are responsible for raising and lowering the American flag outside the Chief of Naval Operations' (CNO's) house. It is located four blocks south of the Marine Barracks Washington.

world knowledge.Name: Denver Performing Arts Complex
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Denver Performing Arts Complex, also referred to as the 'Arts Complex', is one of the largest performing arts centers in the United States. It was developed to host a variety of performing arts and is managed by the City and County of Denver’s Arts & Venues and the Denver Center for the Performing Arts.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex spans four blocks and contains ten performance spaces with over 10,000 seats connected by an 80-foot-tall (24 m) glass roof. It includes theaters like the Ellie Caulkins Opera House, the Temple Hoyne Buell Theatre, and the Boettcher Concert Hall, among others.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Denver Performing Arts Complex is a significant cultural hub, hosting professional theater companies, Broadway musical tours, contemporary dance and ballet, chorales, symphony orchestras, opera productions, and pop stars. It is home to organizations like the Colorado Ballet, the Colorado Symphony, and Opera Colorado.

Performance_Spaces.Name: The Wolf Theater
Performance_Spaces.Features: Audio-enhancing walls and a thrust stage

Performance_Spaces.Name: The Donald R. Seawell Grand Ballroom
Performance_Spaces.Features: Panoramic views of the mountains, catering kitchen, freight elevator, tables, chairs, portable dance floor, moveable platform staging and lighting, audio, video, and projection systems

Sculpture_Park.Location: Southwest corner of the complex at N. Speer Blvd. and Champa St.

world knowledge.Name: Stadion Kantrida
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kantrida Stadium is a football stadium in Rijeka, Croatia, named after the Kantrida neighbourhood. It has been the home of HNK Rijeka football club since 1918. The stadium is uniquely situated between steep cliffs and the Adriatic Sea. It was initially a stone quarry before being converted into a football ground in 1911. The stadium has undergone several renovations and has hosted numerous significant football matches and events.

Major_Events.Description: A friendly match between Victoria and Građanski Zagreb.
Rijeka vs Osijek, with 22,000 spectators.
HNK Rijeka's Croatian First Football League clash against Slaven Belupo ended in a 3–3 draw.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium is known for its distinctive location between steep cliffs and the Adriatic Sea. It has a grass surface and seating capacity of 10,600. The stadium has undergone several renovations, with plans for a new state-of-the-art stadium to be built at the same location.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kantrida Stadium is regarded as one of the most original and beautiful stadiums in the world. It has been included in various lists of the world's most unusual and beautiful football stadiums. The stadium has hosted numerous significant football matches, including fixtures for the Croatia national football team.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is scheduled for significant reconstruction, with plans to build a new state-of-the-art stadium at the same location. The new stadium will accommodate 12,000 to 14,000 spectators and meet UEFA's fourth-category standards. The current stadium has hosted various events, including football matches, rock concerts, and international youth football tournaments.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Mali
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Mali began under French colonial rule as the Sudanese Museum, part of the Institut Français d’Afrique Noire (IFAN) under Théodore Monod. It was opened on February 14, 1953, under the direction of Ukrainian archaeologist Y. Shumowskyi. With the independence of the Republic of Mali in 1960, the Sudanese Museum became the National Museum of Mali, with the new objectives of promoting national unity and celebrating Malian traditional culture. On March 30, 1956, the National Museum moved into a new cemented structure, created by architect Jean-Loup Pivin from traditional Malian designs. Since the 1992 election of former archaeologist Alpha Oumar Konaré to Mali's presidency, the museum's funding has increased considerably, leaving it among the best in West Africa.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the National Museum of Mali
Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened on February 14, 1953, under the direction of Ukrainian archaeologist Y. Shumowskyi.
On March 30, 1956, the National Museum moved into a new cemented structure, created by architect Jean-Loup Pivin from traditional Malian designs.

Major_Events.Event: Collaboration with Aga Khan Trust for Culture
Major_Events.Description: In June 2006, Samuel Sidibé, the director of the National Museum of Mali, signed an agreement of collaboration with the Aga Khan Trust for Culture (AKTC) to improve the museum's information technology system and conservation facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's structure was created by architect Jean-Loup Pivin from traditional Malian designs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Museum of Mali promotes national unity and celebrates Malian traditional culture. It has a large collection of ethnographic, archeological, and West African art objects, as well as photographs, audio, and video recordings.
world knowledge.Details: The museum often hosts part of African Photography Encounters, a biannual photography activity. It has a large collection of 10,000 objects: mostly ethnographic, archeological or West African art objects. This collection is enriched by 40,000 photographs in black and white, 12,000 negatives, 500 audio recordings and 300 video recordings. The Collective for the National Museum of Mali aims to promote the digital presence of the museum and to mitigate risks induced by the COVID-19 crisis that could endanger the collections.

world knowledge.Name: Torreta de Guardamar
world knowledge.Address: Radio Estación Naval - Antena LF 380 metros - Guardamar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1962 by the US Navy, the Torreta de Guardamar is a 380-meter tall guyed radio mast used for transmitting orders to submerged submarines. It was later transferred to the Spanish Navy and is currently guarded by Spanish Marine Infantry.

Major_Events.Description: The transmitter was initially controlled by the US Naval Communication Station in Rota but was later transferred to the Spanish Navy for use in transmitting orders to submerged submarines stationed in Cartagena.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mast is a lattice structure with a triangular cross section, insulated from earth, and functions as a mast radiator. It is augmented by multiple cables connected to its top and running to anchors around the mast, which are electrically connected and divided by insulators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Torreta de Guardamar is the tallest architectural structure in both the Iberian Peninsula and the European Union, as well as the tallest military structure in Europe. It plays a critical role in naval communications.
world knowledge.Details: The installation is officially listed as "Estación Radio de Guardamar del Segura" and is marked as "Radio Estación Naval - Antena LF 380 metros - Guardamar". Unlike other VLF transmitters, it has no fixed frequency allocation by ITU and carries no callsign.

world knowledge.Name: Mar'ashi Najafi Library
world knowledge.Address: Near Fatima Masumeh Shrine, Qom, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ayatollah Marashi Najafi Library, founded in 1963, began as the personal library of Ayatollah Marashi Najafi, a prominent Islamic scholar. He collected rare texts to prevent them from being possessed by British colonial authorities. The library was expanded in 1974 and 1988. After his death in 1989, ownership and management passed to his son, Mahmoud Marashi Najafi. The library is now the third largest in Iran and the third largest Islamic library in the world, housing over 250,000 books, including 25,000 online.

Major_Events.Description: The library was established by Ayatollah Marashi Najafi.
The library underwent its first major expansion.
The library underwent its second major expansion.
Ayatollah Marashi Najafi passed away shortly after laying the foundation stone of a new library building.
The library began to be funded as a governmental institution under Resolution 205 of the Supreme Council of Cultural Revolution.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The library is culturally significant as it houses a vast collection of Islamic texts and rare books, preserving Islamic heritage and scholarship. It is also notable for its respect towards books of other religions, including Hebrew texts, which has garnered international respect.
world knowledge.Details: The library contains books in at least 30 different languages, including Turkish, Urdu, and Arabic. It is situated near the Fatima Masumeh Shrine and the tomb of Ayatollah Marashi Najafi. The library was initially personally financed by its founder and his descendants but has been funded by the government since 1997. The operation is overseen by Marashi Najafi's family in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance.

world knowledge.Name: La Feria de Chapultepec
world knowledge.Address: Near Constituyentes Metro station, Mexico City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Feria de Chapultepec was an amusement park in Mexico City, originally opened in 1964 as Juegos Mecánicos de Chapultepec by the Mexican government. It was later bought by Grupo CIE in 1992 and renamed La Feria Chapultepec Mágico. In 2015, Ventura Entertainment acquired it and renamed it back to La Feria de Chapultepec. The park closed definitively on 13 October 2019 after an accident on the Quimera roller coaster led to the revocation of its license by the Mexico City Government.

Major_Events.Event: Opening as Juegos Mecánicos de Chapultepec
Major_Events.Description: The park opened under the name Juegos Mecánicos de Chapultepec, operated by the Mexican government.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition by Grupo CIE and renaming
Major_Events.Description: Grupo CIE bought the park and renamed it La Feria Chapultepec Mágico.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition by Ventura Entertainment and renaming
Major_Events.Description: Ventura Entertainment bought the park and renamed it La Feria de Chapultepec.
An accident on the Quimera roller coaster killed two people and injured two others, leading to the park's closure.
The Mexico City Government revoked the park's license, leading to its permanent closure on 13 October 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park featured approximately 50 different rides and amusements, including several roller coasters, flat rides, and animal attractions. Notable roller coasters included Montaña Rusa (once the world's tallest roller coaster) and Quimera (the first roller coaster with three vertical loops). The park also had a zero-emission scenic train developed with the help of the National Autonomous University of Mexico.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: La Feria de Chapultepec was a significant amusement park in Mexico City, offering affordable entertainment compared to other North American parks. It housed record-holding roller coasters and innovative attractions like the zero-emission train, contributing to its cultural and recreational importance.
world knowledge.Details: After its closure, the property was cleaned and dismantled, with plans for a new park named Aztlán Parque Urbano. The selection process for a new owner was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The park had a multi-tiered pricing structure for ride passes, catering to different budgets and ride preferences.

world knowledge.Name: Reed College
world knowledge.Address: 3203 SE Woodstock Blvd, Portland, OR 97202, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Reed College is a private liberal arts college founded in 1908, named after Oregon pioneers Simeon Gannett Reed and Amanda Reed. It was established as a reaction against the prevailing model of East Coast, Ivy League education, emphasizing coeducational, nonsectarian, and egalitarian principles. The college has a reputation for rigorous academics and political progressivism.

Major_Events.Description: Reed College was founded with the first classes held in 1911. It was named after Oregon pioneers Simeon Gannett Reed and Amanda Reed.
After World War II, the college saw a dramatic increase in enrollment as veterans began attending.

Major_Events.Event: Refusal to Participate in U.S. News Rankings
Major_Events.Description: Reed College became the first educational institution in the U.S. to refuse participation in the U.S. News & World Report college rankings.
Students organized protests and demands for changes to the mandatory Humanities 110 course, leading to a revised curriculum in 2018.
The Aubrey R. Watzek Sports Center collapsed during Winter Storm Uri due to excess snow accumulation on the roof.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features Tudor-Gothic style architecture, modeled after the University of Oxford's St. John's College. Modernist buildings, such as the Psychology Building designed by Pietro Belluschi, are also present. The campus includes 21 academic and administrative buildings and 18 residence halls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Reed College is known for its rigorous academic environment, political progressivism, and unique traditions. It has produced numerous Rhodes Scholars, Fulbright Scholars, and PhD holders. The college is also notable for its unconventional approach to education, including de-emphasizing grades and fostering intellectual freedom.
world knowledge.Details: Reed College has a nuclear reactor operated by undergraduates, a unique requirement for a senior thesis and oral defense, and a strong emphasis on interdisciplinary studies. The college is also known for its traditions like Paideia, Renn Fayre, and the Doyle Owl prank.

world knowledge.Name: Iowa State Capitol
world knowledge.Address: Grand Ave. and E. 12th St. Des Moines, Iowa
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 364 ft (111 m) from north to south and 247 ft (75 m) from east to west
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iowa State Capitol, commonly called the Iowa Statehouse, is in Iowa's capital city, Des Moines. As the seat of the Iowa General Assembly, the building houses the Iowa Senate, Iowa House of Representatives, the Office of the Governor, and the Offices of the Attorney General, Auditor, Treasurer, and Secretary of State. The building also includes a chamber for the Iowa Supreme Court, although court activities usually take place in the neighboring Iowa Supreme Court building. The building was constructed between 1871 and 1886, and is the only five-domed capitol in the country.

Major_Events.Description: The cornerstone was laid on November 23, 1871, but much of the original stone deteriorated and had to be replaced. The cornerstone was relaid on September 29, 1873.
The capitol building was dedicated on January 17, 1884, and it was completed sometime in 1886.

A fire was started when the gas lights were being converted into electricity. The fire swept through the areas that housed the Supreme Court and Iowa House of Representatives. A major restoration was performed and documented, with the addition of electrical lighting, elevators, and a telephone system.
The dome was regilded at a cost of $79,938.
Work on the exterior restoration began in the spring of 1983 and was completed in nine phases. The entire project was completed in the fall of 2001, at a cost of $41 million.

Major_Events.Event: World Food Prize laureate award ceremony
Major_Events.Description: Since 1987, the World Food Prize laureate award ceremony is held annually in October in the House of Representatives chamber of the statehouse. The ceremony rivals that of the Nobel Prize, drawing over 800 people from more than 75 countries.

A two-week display of Baphomet and the seven tenets of the Satanic Temple was set up, with official approval, in the Iowa Capitol in December 2023. This drew criticism from Republican politicians. After the display was ruined, a failed Republican candidate for the Mississippi House of Representatives was charged with criminal mischief for allegedly vandalizing the display.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architectural design of the Capitol, rectangular in form, with great windows and high ceilings, follows the traditional pattern of 19th-century planning for public buildings. A modified and refined Renaissance style gives the impression of strength and dignity combined with utility. The exterior of the building is entirely of stone with elaborate columns and handsomely designed cornices and capitals. Iowa stone is the foundation for the many porticoes of the building. The building is brick with limestone from Iowa, Missouri, Minnesota, Ohio, and Illinois. The substructure is of dark Iowa stone topped by a heavy course of wari-colored granite cut from glacial boulders gathered from the Iowa prairie. The superstructure, or main part of the building, is of bluff colored sandstone from quarries along the Mississippi River in Missouri. The commanding feature is the central towering dome constructed of iron and brick and covered with tissue-paper thin sheets of pure 23-carat gold. The dome is surmounted by a lookout lantern that may be reached by long and winding stairs, and it terminates in a finial that is 275 ft (84 m) above the ground floor. Four smaller domes of simple design rise from the four corners of the Capitol. The marble grand staircase between the second and third floors is to the east and is the focal point of the building. Twenty-nine types of imported and domestic marble were used in the interior; and the wood used—walnut, cherry, catalpa, butternut, and oak—was nearly all from Iowa forests.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Iowa State Capitol is culturally and historically important as the seat of the Iowa General Assembly and the offices of the Governor, Attorney General, Auditor, Treasurer, and Secretary of State. It also functions as a living museum and state and international cultural facility. The building's architectural design and historical events, such as the World Food Prize laureate award ceremony, contribute to its cultural significance.
world knowledge.Details: The rotunda beneath the dome is 80 ft (24 m) in diameter. Around the rotunda on the frieze above the columns is the famous quotation from Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address. Extending the full width of the east wall over the staircase is the great mural painting Westward, an idealized representation of the coming of the people who made Iowa. In the central rotunda, suspended beneath the ceiling on wires is a very large banner of the insignia of the Grand Army of the Republic. The battle flags carried by the Iowa regiments in various wars are preserved in niches on the main floor. In the west hall is a plaque done by Nellie V. Walker in commemoration of the work of Iowa women in the fight for political equality and a memorial to those Iowans killed in Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Enduring Freedom. Also in the west hall is a model of the battleship USS Iowa on loan from the U.S. Department of the Navy. In the south hall across from the Governor's office is a collection of porcelain dolls representing the 41 Iowa First Ladies in miniature replicas of their inaugural gowns.

world knowledge.Name: Gürsel Aksel Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Üçkuyular, Göztepe, Konak district, İzmir, Turkey
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 34.651 m² building area, 94.541 m² total construction presence
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built as the new home ground for Göztepe S.K., commemorating Gürsel Aksel, a revered figure in the club's history. Construction began in 2017 and was completed in 2019, with the stadium officially opening in January 2020. It was designed to replace the old İzmir Atatürk Stadium and has since hosted significant football matches, including Turkish Cup finals.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was officially opened on 26 January 2020 with a Süper Lig match between Göztepe and Beşiktaş J.K., which Göztepe won 2–1. Halil Akbunar scored the first goal in the stadium's history.
The stadium hosted the Turkish Cup final on 18 May 2021, where Beşiktaş defeated Antalyaspor 2–0.
The stadium hosted another Turkish Cup final on 11 June 2023, where Fenerbahçe defeated İstanbul Başakşehir 2–0.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by DBArchitects, the stadium features a modern design with a grass playing field (105m × 68m), 41 executive suites, and a 650-meter-long walking track on the roof. It also includes a sports museum, exhibition halls, food courts, and an underground parking garage.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a symbol of pride for Göztepe S.K. and its fans, named after Gürsel Aksel, a legendary figure in the club's history. It serves as a modern sports and cultural hub in İzmir, hosting major football events and promoting healthy living.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 19,713 (all-seater) and a record attendance of 18,228. It is accessible via multiple ESHOT bus services from various districts and neighborhoods in İzmir. The construction cost was approximately ₺218,900,000.

world knowledge.Name: Finca Vigía
world knowledge.Location: 23.067742°N, -82.296417°W, San Miguel del Padrón, Havana, Cuba
world knowledge.Address: San Francisco de Paula Ward, San Miguel del Padrón, Havana, Cuba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Finca Vigía, also known as Lookout Farm, is a house in San Francisco de Paula Ward in Havana, Cuba. It was the residence of Ernest Hemingway from mid-1939 to 1960. The house was built in 1886 by Catalan architect Miguel Pascual y Baguer on a hill about 8 miles southeast of Havana. Hemingway purchased the property in December 1940 after marrying Martha Gellhorn. The estate was originally 15 acres with a farmhouse and included a guest house, tennis court, pool, and water wells. Hemingway wrote significant works here, including 'For Whom the Bell Tolls' and 'The Old Man and the Sea'. After the Cuban revolution, the property was expropriated by the Cuban government and turned into a museum.

Major_Events.Description: Hemingway purchased the property in December 1940 after marrying Martha Gellhorn.
After the Cuban revolution, the property was expropriated by the Cuban government and turned into a museum.
The home was restored by the Cuban government and reopened to tourists in 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house was built in 1886 by Catalan architect Miguel Pascual y Baguer. It features a farmhouse design with a guest house, tennis court, pool, and water wells. The property includes a 38 ft (12 m) wooden fishing boat named Pilar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Finca Vigía is culturally significant as the residence of Nobel Prize-winning author Ernest Hemingway. It is where he wrote some of his most famous works, including 'For Whom the Bell Tolls' and 'The Old Man and the Sea'. The property is now a museum dedicated to Hemingway, preserving his legacy and contributions to literature.
world knowledge.Details: The home has been listed as one of the 11 most-endangered historic sites and is on the World Monuments Fund's list of '100 most endangered sites'. Despite controversies over its condition, the Cuban government has maintained the house, contents, and grounds responsibly. The property includes Hemingway's 38 ft (12 m) wooden fishing boat Pilar.

world knowledge.Name: Quirinal Palace
world knowledge.Address: Via del Quirinale, Piazza del Quirinale, Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Quirinal Palace is a historic building in Rome, Italy, serving as the main official residence of the President of the Italian Republic. It was built in 1583 by Pope Gregory XIII as a papal summer residence. The palace has served as the residence for thirty popes, four kings of Italy, and twelve presidents of the Italian Republic. It was selected by Napoleon to be his residence as emperor, but he never stayed there due to the French defeat in 1814. The palace became the official royal residence of the Kings of Italy in 1871 and the official residence of the presidents of the Italian Republic in 1946.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was used as the location for papal conclaves in these years.
The Papal States were occupied militarily and annexed to the Kingdom of Italy.
The monarchy was abolished, and the palace became the official residence of the presidents of the Italian Republic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace was designed by Domenico Fontana and Carlo Maderno. It features a majestic courtyard, the Great Chapel designed by Carlo Maderno, and frescos by Guido Reni and Melozzo da Forlì. The palace grounds include famous gardens laid out in the 17th century. The palace has 1,200 rooms, including the Throne Room, Great Hall of Banquets, and various chapels and reception rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Quirinal Palace is culturally and historically important as it has served as the residence for popes, kings, and presidents, reflecting the political and religious history of Italy. Its architecture and art represent significant periods in Italian history.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is located on the Quirinal Hill, the highest of the seven hills of Rome. It includes the Quirinal Gardens, which extend over 4 hectares and feature a water organ and archaeological excavations of the original temple to the god Quirinus. The palace's rooms include the Throne Room, Great Hall of Banquets, and various chapels and reception rooms, each with historical and artistic significance.

world knowledge.Name: University of the Punjab
world knowledge.Address: Canal Road, Quaid-i-Azam Campus, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main Quaid-e-Azam Campus – 1,781 acres (721 hectares), Allama Iqbal Campus – 50 acres (20 hectares), Khanaspur Campus – 2.47 acres (1.00 hectare), Gujranwala Campus – 10 acres (4.0 hectares), Jhelum Campus – 32 acres (13 hectares)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of the Punjab (UoP), also referred to as the Punjab University (PU), is a public research university in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. Founded in 1882, its international influence has made it one of the most prestigious universities in South Asia; being the oldest and largest public sector one in the wider Punjab region, as well as in Pakistan. The first meeting of the University's Senate was on 14 October 1882 at Simla, which marked the formal establishment of the university. Punjab University was the fourth university to be established by the British colonial authorities in the Indian subcontinent.

Major_Events.Description: Punjab University College was established in Lahore, consisting of Punjab University Law College and Oriental College.

The fate of the university after the partition of India was deliberated at the Punjab Partition Committee, with representatives from East Punjab advocating for a division of the university. The senate of the university voted to split the university, and the matter reached the Partition Council at the centre, but a decision could not be made.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university has multiple campuses with varying architectural styles. The main Quaid-e-Azam Campus was established in 1958 and spans 1,781 acres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of the Punjab is culturally and historically significant as the oldest and largest public sector university in the Punjab region and in Pakistan. It has produced numerous notable alumni and has a strong influence in South Asia.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 19 faculties with 10 constituent colleges, 73 departments, centers, and institutes. It has 1006 full-time and 300 part-time faculty members involved in teaching/research and over 6,000 non-teaching/supporting staff with 45,678 on campus students. The library is one of the largest libraries among the universities of Pakistan, with more than 500,000 books, magazines, and periodicals.

world knowledge.Name: Parliament Building (Antigua and Barbuda)
world knowledge.Address: Queen Elizabeth Highway, St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Antigua and Barbuda Parliament Building is a two-storey structure that is the seat of the Parliament of Antigua and Barbuda. The building was inaugurated on 30 October 2006. The previous building was located on the nearby Parliament Drive.

Major_Events.Description: The building was inaugurated on 30 October 2006.
When a throne speech is held, the governor-general is welcomed by an honour guard of soldiers from the Antigua and Barbuda Defence Force at the building's south portico.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a two-storey structure with a central portion that includes a rotunda and four small wings. The roof of the rotunda is a small cone-shaped dome, with the remainder of the roofing being either flat or metal-roofed. Like other buildings in the complex, it is painted white. There are two parking lots, and a small guard booth.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is the seat of the Parliament of Antigua and Barbuda, making it a significant political and cultural landmark in the country.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the Parliament of Antigua and Barbuda
world knowledge.Details: When the building is not hosting sittings of Parliament, other events may be held in its rotunda. A large sign in Arial font reading 'Parliament of Antigua & Barbuda' is located nearby.

world knowledge.Name: Cathays Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cathays Park was formerly part of Cardiff Castle grounds. The area was developed in the early 20th century as a civic centre, with contributions from the Marquess of Bute. It includes several Edwardian buildings and a central park area, Alexandra Gardens. The area was designated as a conservation area in 1975.

Major_Events.Event: Cardiff Fine Arts, Industrial and Maritime Exhibition
Major_Events.Description: A six-month exhibition which included a boating lake, a wooden cycling track, and an electric railway.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase of land by local council
Major_Events.Description: The local council bought 59 acres of land from the Marquess of Bute for £161,000, with strict conditions on development.

Major_Events.Event: Investiture of Prince Charles as Prince of Wales
Major_Events.Description: The fountains on the City Hall Lawns were created to mark this event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The area features Edwardian Baroque style buildings, simplified classical designs, and modernist architecture. Notable buildings include the Temple of Peace, City Hall, the National Museum and Gallery of Wales, and several Cardiff University buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cathays Park is considered the finest civic centre in the British Isles. It is an outstanding example of an architectural ensemble that illustrates a significant stage in Welsh history and validates Cardiff's claim to city status and national capital.
world knowledge.Details: Cathays Park includes three formal gardens and a tree-lined park. The gardens are grade II on the Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in Wales. The area has seen various phases of development, with the most recent being the opening of Parc Mackenzie in 2023 to commemorate Millicent Mackenzie, the first woman professor in Wales.

world knowledge.Name: Brzeg Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brzeg Town Hall is a Renaissance building designed by Bernard Niuron. The first building housing the municipal government in Brzeg existed in the fourteenth century but was burned down in the town's great fire during the reign of George II of Brieg. The present town hall was built between 1569 and 1577. It was designed by the Italian architect Bernardo Niuron, assisted by the Italian builder Giacomo Parr. The building underwent minor alterations in some of its rooms, which were adapted for administrative purposes. In 1926, a Renaissance gate, from one of the Brzeg townhouses, was added to the southern façade. The Voivodeship Conservation Orders of 25 November 1949 and 10 January 1964 listed the town hall as a heritage monument.

Major_Events.Description: The first building housing the municipal government in Brzeg was burned down in the town's great fire during the reign of George II of Brieg.
The present town hall was built between 1569 and 1577, designed by Bernard Niuron and assisted by Giacomo Parr.
A Renaissance gate from one of the Brzeg townhouses was added to the southern façade.
The Voivodeship Conservation Orders of 25 November 1949 and 10 January 1964 listed the town hall as a heritage monument.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town hall is a Renaissance structure built in the town square, surrounded by an inner courtyard of townhouses. It has two storeys and a saddle roof. The most interesting part of the building is its western side, featuring two quadrangular towers with tented roofs and roof lanterns, and a five-axis loggia with semicircular arches on the ground floor. The façade is covered with sgraffito decorations from the seventeenth-century. There is a four-sided central tower with an octagonal cupola topped with a balustrade and two roof lanterns. The interiors have been preserved with halls and corridors of the original design, most notably the Hall of Councillors with its wall paintings and fine ceiling. The Stropowa Hall has a larch ceiling from 1646.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brzeg Town Hall is considered to be one of the most important Renaissance monuments in Poland.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the municipal government of Brzeg and housing several other institutions.
world knowledge.Details: Currently, the town hall functions as the seat of the city and several other institutions. It also houses a museum.

image_name: Taras Shevchenko Dnipro Academic Ukrainian Music and Drama Theatre

world knowledge.Name: Taras Shevchenko Dnipro Academic Ukrainian Music and Drama Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Taras Shevchenko Dnipro Academic Ukrainian Music and Drama Theatre is a 20th-century city theatre and architectural landmark in Dnipro, Ukraine. It was the nation's first professional theatre to hold national cultural importance status. Constructed in 1913, the theatre was situated in what was once the English Club. Established on 23 August 1918 in Kyiv, it became the country's first professional theatre. The theatre featured both domestic and foreign classic plays and had a successful tour of Ukraine in 1921–1922. The theatre was relocated to Dnipropetrovsk in 1927. During World War II, performers were relocated to Kazakhstan, where they continued their work. The theatre was rebuilt in 1979 and underwent several renovations in the 2000s. It was granted national cultural importance status in 2018.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was established on 23 August 1918 in Kyiv as the country's first professional theatre.
The theatre was relocated to Dnipropetrovsk in 1927.
The theatre was rebuilt in 1979 according to the design of architects V. Khalyavsky and E. Yashunsky.

Major_Events.Event: Granting of national cultural importance status
Major_Events.Description: President Poroshenko issued an executive order granting the theater national cultural importance status on 17 December 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The structure is two stories tall and has an uneven layout. The theatre was rebuilt in 1979 in accordance with the design of architects V. Khalyavsky and E. Yashunsky. Sculptor Y. Pavlov made bas-reliefs on the theatre front based on themes from stage shows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is culturally significant as it was the nation's first professional theatre to hold national cultural importance status. It has been a hub for spiritual and societal revival, promoting Ukrainian culture through performances of both domestic and foreign classic plays.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre's interior was renovated in 2009, and modern lighting equipment was purchased. The theatre commemorated its 95th anniversary in 2013. The chamber stage had a reconstruction and renovation in 2014, along with new lighting fixtures. In 2018, the theatre's exterior and interior were renovated, commemorating one hundred years since the theatre's founding in Kyiv.

world knowledge.Name: Shimoda Ropeway
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shimoda Ropeway, also known as Nesugatayama Ropeway, is an aerial lift line in Shimoda, Shizuoka, Japan. It began operation on April 1, 1961, and is operated by a subsidiary of Izukyū Corporation.

Major_Events.Description: The Shimoda Ropeway began operation on April 1, 1961.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Aerial lift line climbing Mount Nesugata, featuring an observatory with views of Port of Shimoda and the Pacific Ocean.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The ropeway provides scenic views and is a notable tourist attraction in Shimoda, offering a unique perspective of the surrounding natural beauty.
world knowledge.Details: The line is also called Nesugatayama Ropeway as it climbs Mount Nesugata. The observatory offers views of Port of Shimoda and the Pacific Ocean.

world knowledge.Name: Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord is a public park designed by Latz + Partner (Peter Latz) in 1991. The park was created to heal and understand the industrial past of the site, which was previously a coal and steel production plant abandoned in 1985. The design preserves much of the existing site, including polluted soils remediated through phytoremediation and repurposed structures. The park integrates elements of the site's industrial history, such as old railway systems, sewage canals, and steel plates, into its design, allowing visitors to connect with the past while experiencing the natural processes of change and decay.

Major_Events.Description: A planning procedure involving five international teams was held to design the park. Peter Latz’s design was selected for its innovative approach to preserving the site's industrial heritage.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of industrial and natural elements, including repurposed structures like concrete bunkers, gas tanks turned into scuba diving pools, and steel plates used in Piazza Metallica. The design incorporates walkways and waterways that follow the old railway and sewer systems, creating a dialogue between different areas of the park. The use of phytoremediation and the integration of decaying materials highlight the transient nature of the site.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord is culturally significant as it represents a successful integration of industrial heritage with ecological restoration. The park serves as a place for memory and reflection, allowing visitors to connect with the site's industrial past while experiencing its transformation into a natural landscape. It is considered a local hotspot for biodiversity and a model for the redevelopment of industrial brownfield sites.
world knowledge.Details: The park is divided into different areas based on existing conditions, such as plant growth and site divisions. It includes various programmatic elements like bunker gardens, scuba diving pools, and rock climbing walls. The park's design emphasizes the importance of memory and temporality, allowing visitors to create their own experiences and connections with the site. The park is part of the Ruhr Industrial Heritage Trail and is recognized for its ecological value and contribution to urban biodiversity.

world knowledge.Name: Worcester Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Worcester Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of Christ and Blessed Mary the Virgin, is a Church of England cathedral in Worcester, England. Founded in 680, it has undergone numerous reconstructions and restorations, blending Norman and Gothic architectural styles. It is the seat of the bishop of Worcester and a significant historical and religious site.

Major_Events.Description: The priory came to an end with King Henry VIII's Dissolution of the Monasteries, transitioning to a secular college.
During the Civil War, the cathedral was used to store arms and was ransacked by Parliamentary troops, resulting in significant damage.
The cathedral underwent major restoration work planned by Sir George Gilbert Scott and A. E. Perkins.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Worcester Cathedral features a blend of Norman and Gothic styles. It includes a multi-columned crypt from the Norman period, a perpendicular style tower, and various additions from the 11th to the 16th centuries. The cathedral also has a chapter house, cloister, and significant medieval misericords.
