world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Worcester Cathedral is a grade I listed building and part of a scheduled monument. It is culturally significant as the burial place of King John and Prince Arthur, and for its role in the history of the Church of England and the city of Worcester.
world knowledge.Details: Worcester Cathedral hosts annual graduation ceremonies for the University of Worcester and the honours celebration of the Royal Life Saving Society UK. It also has a rich musical history, being associated with the Three Choirs Festival and the composer Edward Elgar.

world knowledge.Name: Tenantry Column
world knowledge.Address: South of Alnwick town centre, Northumberland, England
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Column height: 83 feet (25 m); Platform circumference: 90 feet (27 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tenantry Column was erected in 1816 by the tenants of Hugh Percy, 2nd Duke of Northumberland in thanks for his reduction of their rents during the post-Napoleonic depression. The foundation stone was laid on 1 July 1816, and the column was completed after the Duke's death on 10 July 1817, being presented to his son, the 3rd Duke of Northumberland.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid on 1 July 1816, witnessed by a large audience. The ceremony was led by a band and flag bearers and attended by the architect, principal tenants, and clergymen. The 21 oldest tenants ceremoniously used a silver trowel to lay the stone, which was then blessed and doused with corn, wine, and oil.
The column was completed after the death of the 2nd Duke of Northumberland and was presented to his son, the 3rd Duke of Northumberland.
The column was granted protection as a listed building on 20 February 1952 and was upgraded to the highest category, grade I, on 25 August 1977.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The column is a Doric column standing 83 feet (25 m) tall, topped by a lion en passant, the symbol of the Percy family. The lion sits on a drum decorated with foliage and surmounted with an iron balcony. The base is surrounded by a circular granite platform with four additional lions on black marble plinths. The column features engraved panels, including the Percy family motto 'Esperance en dieu' (Hope is in God).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The column is a monument to the gratitude of the tenants for the rent reduction by the Duke of Northumberland during economic hardship. It also commemorates the Percy Tenantry Volunteers, a unit raised by the Duke to defend against potential French invasion. The column is a symbol of the relationship between the Percy family and their tenants.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Monument commemorating the rent reduction and the Percy Tenantry Volunteers
world knowledge.Details: The column is also known as 'The Farmer's Folly.' A muster roll of the Percy Tenantry Volunteers was sealed into the foundation. The lion atop the column has an unusually horizontal tail, said to point towards Scotland. The column is one of the first sights to greet visitors arriving in Alnwick from the south.

world knowledge.Name: Cliburn Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cliburn is a village in Cumbria, England, historically part of Westmorland. The name 'Cliburn' originates from 'clay stream' or 'stream by the bank'. The village features historical structures like Cliburn Hall, a Pele tower built in 1387, and St Cuthbert's Church, dating back to the 12th century. The village has seen various developments over the centuries, including the construction of bridges after a flood in 1822 and the establishment of a school in 1807.

Major_Events.Description: Robert de Cliburn built the three-storey Pele tower.
Richard Cliburn made alterations and additions to the hall.
The tower was given a gabled roof.
A powerful flood destroyed earlier bridges, leading to the construction of new ones.
The church was restored, with most windows dating from this period.
The station closed, and the station house became a private residence.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cliburn Hall is a three-storey Pele tower built in 1387, with alterations in 1567. It was decastellated in 1872 and given a gabled roof. St Cuthbert's Church has a nave and chancel from the 12th century, with most windows dating from the 19th-century restoration. The bridges (Cliburn Bridge and Cliburn Mill Bridge) are made of local red sandstone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cliburn is significant for its historical structures, including Cliburn Hall and St Cuthbert's Church, which reflect medieval and post-medieval architecture. The village's name and history are tied to its geographical features, such as the River Leith. The area also includes Cliburn Moss, a national nature reserve, and Whinfell Forest, a large wood and holiday park location.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential village with historical and cultural landmarks.
world knowledge.Details: Cliburn includes the hamlet of Town Head. The village pub, originally called the Railway Inn, was renamed the Golden Pheasant Inn after the station closed but has since closed. The rectory lies between the village and the former railway station. The population was 274 in 2011. The village is situated at crossroads on minor roads connecting Bolton, Penrith, Morland, and the A66(T).

world knowledge.Name: Swansea Civic Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as County Hall, it was designed as the principal administrative centre for the West Glamorgan County Council following the Local Government Act 1972. It was opened in July 1982 and later renamed Swansea Civic Centre in 2008 after local government reorganisation in 1996.

Major_Events.Description: Queen Elizabeth II, accompanied by the Duke of Edinburgh, visited the building on 20 April 1989.
The building was renamed Swansea Civic Centre on 19 March 2008, following local government reorganisation.
Swansea Council announced plans to redevelop the area, including the demolition of Swansea Civic Centre and the creation of a city beach.
In May 2021, the Twentieth Century Society placed the site on its Top 10 Buildings at Risk List.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the Brutalist style by C. W. Quick, featuring continuous bands of glazing with deep washed calcined flint panels above and below.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is significant as the principal administrative centre of Swansea Council and for its Brutalist architectural style. It also houses the busiest library in Wales.
world knowledge.Details: The complex includes the council chamber, offices, a public cafe, the central library, an exhibition space, archives service, and contact centre. The library made nearly 566,000 book loans during the year ended 31 March 2009, making it the busiest library in Wales and the tenth busiest library in the UK.

world knowledge.Name: Coquitlam City Hall
world knowledge.Address: Intersection of Pinetree Way and Guildford Way, Town Centre neighbourhood, Coquitlam, British Columbia, Canada
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 80,700 square feet (7,500 m2) for City Hall; 67,800 square feet (6,300 m2) for Public Safety Building
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Coquitlam City Hall was completed in 2001 as part of a two-building complex, which also includes the Public Safety Building housing the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) detachment. It was designed by Grant & Sinclair Architects Limited.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Grant & Sinclair Architects Limited, the complex consists of two buildings: City Hall and the Public Safety Building. City Hall is a three-storey structure housing council chambers, city office space, and a public library.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Coquitlam City Hall serves as the administrative hub for the city, housing the Coquitlam City Council and other municipal departments. It is a key civic landmark in the Town Centre neighbourhood.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Administrative and civic services, including city council meetings, municipal offices, and public library services.
world knowledge.Details: The Public Safety Building, part of the same complex, houses the RCMP detachment. The coordinates for the location are 49°17′04″N 122°47′36″W.

world knowledge.Name: Iringa Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Iringa Airport is an airport in Tanzania serving Iringa and the surrounding Iringa Region. It is 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) northeast of the municipality. The airport's single runway lies parallel to the A104 trunk road.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a single runway with a length of 1,670 meters (5,479 ft) and an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Details: Iringa Airport (IATA: IRI, ICAO: HTIR) is owned by the Government of Tanzania and operated by the Tanzania Airports Authority. It serves the city of Iringa and the surrounding region. The airport is located at an elevation of 4,678 feet (1,426 meters) above mean sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Sherborne Abbey
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 240ft (73m), Nave width: 66ft (23m), Width across transepts: 100ft (30.5m), Nave height: ~60ft (18m), Tower height: 109ft (33m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sherborne Abbey, originally the Abbey Church of St. Mary the Virgin, has served as a Saxon cathedral (705–1075), a Benedictine abbey church (998–1539), and since 1539, a parish church. The site has been occupied since Roman times, with evidence of a previous church beneath the Saxon cathedral. The Saxon Diocese of Sherborne was founded in 705 by King Ine of Wessex, and the Benedictine abbey was established in 998 by Bishop Wulfsige III. The abbey was dissolved in 1539 and converted into a parish church.

Major_Events.Description: The Saxon Diocese of Sherborne was founded by King Ine of Wessex, with St Aldhelm as the first bishop.
Bishop Wulfsige III established a Benedictine abbey at Sherborne.
The abbey was surrendered to King Henry VIII during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and became a parish church.
A riot in the town caused a fire that damaged much of the ongoing renovation work, resulting in permanent pink discoloration of the stone.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey features a mix of Saxon, Norman, and Perpendicular architectural styles. It includes a fan-vaulted nave, a central tower with the heaviest ring of eight bells in the world, and various chapels with distinct architectural elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sherborne Abbey is historically significant as one of the oldest ecclesiastical sites in England, having served as a cathedral, abbey, and parish church. It is a Grade I listed building and contains numerous historical artifacts, including the oldest candelabrum in England.
world knowledge.Details: The abbey contains several notable features, including the tomb of Sir John Horsey, who purchased the church after the Dissolution of the Monasteries, and the tomb of the poet Sir Thomas Wyatt. The abbey also has a number of stained glass windows, including the great east window designed by Clayton and Bell, and the great west window by John Hayward. The abbey's organ, installed in 1856, has undergone several rebuilds and remains a significant feature of the church.

world knowledge.Name: Port Macquarie Airport
world knowledge.Area: Port Macquarie, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Port Macquarie Airport is an airport in Port Macquarie, New South Wales, Australia. The airport is 2.25 nautical miles (4.17 km; 2.59 mi) west of the city centre and is owned and managed by the Port Macquarie-Hastings Council on behalf of its owners - the constituents of the Hastings. The ownership is not to be confused with the Port Macquarie Airport Proprietary Limited. Historically, a number of airlines have flown to the airfield, including Virgin Australia, JetGo, Bonza, Ansett Australia, Hazelton Airlines, Kendell Airlines, East-West Airlines, FlyPelican, and Brindabella Airlines.

Major_Events.Event: Virgin Blue commences direct scheduled services
Major_Events.Description: On 4 February 2008, Virgin Blue (now Virgin Australia) commenced direct scheduled services between Sydney and Port Macquarie. The flights operated daily in the morning. The service used to be operated by an Embraer E-170 aircraft, and was the first scheduled jet service for the airport. Connections were offered to all major Australian cities via Sydney. An increase to twice-daily service commenced 4 August 2008.

Major_Events.Event: Virgin Australia commences Brisbane to Port Macquarie service
Major_Events.Description: On 28 July 2011, Virgin Australia (in partnership with Skywest Airlines) announced its intention to commence a daily Brisbane to Port Macquarie service from October 2011. On 19 October 2011, Virgin Australia's ATR 72 departed on its first flight to Brisbane. The airline also announced that, as a result of the removal of Embraer 170 aircraft from its fleet, Sydney to Port Macquarie services would also be operated by ATR72 aircraft.

Major_Events.Event: Brindabella Airlines ceases connections to Brisbane
Major_Events.Description: Connections to Brisbane (via Coffs Harbour) by Brindabella Airlines ceased 31 December 2010, citing poor loads on the route.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Port Macquarie Airport is culturally significant as it serves as a vital transportation hub for the Port Macquarie region, facilitating connectivity to major Australian cities. It has played a key role in reducing fare prices and increasing competition on the Port Macquarie - Sydney route.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving Port Macquarie, New South Wales, Australia

Details.Direction: Direction Length Surface m ft 03/21 1,800 5,906 Asphalt

world knowledge.Name: Etihad Museum
world knowledge.Address: 1 Jumeira Road, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Etihad Museum, historically called the Union House and formerly as the al-Diyafah Palace and the Jumeirah Guesthouse, is a museum in Dubai, United Arab Emirates that collects, preserves, and displays the heritage of the United Arab Emirates in the areas of social, political, cultural, scientific, and military history. The historic signing of the Constitution of the United Arab Emirates, the raising of the first UAE flag, and the formation of the United Arab Emirates as a country on 2 December 1971 took place within the area that forms the museum today.

Major_Events.Event: Signing of the Constitution of the United Arab Emirates
Major_Events.Description: The founding fathers of the UAE signed the declaration that marked the formation of the UAE.

Major_Events.Event: Raising of the first UAE flag
Major_Events.Description: The first flag of the UAE was raised, symbolizing the birth of the nation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by Moriyama & Teshima Architects in the shape of a manuscript, with seven columns built into the museum to resemble the pens used to sign the original declaration. The building has eight permanent pavilions, each dedicated to different aspects of the UAE's history and formation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Etihad Museum is culturally significant as it preserves and displays the heritage of the United Arab Emirates, including the historic signing of the UAE Constitution and the formation of the nation. It serves as a testament to the country's history and the efforts of its founding fathers.
world knowledge.Details: The museum encompasses the Union house, the location where the emirate's founding fathers signed a declaration that marked the formation of the UAE in 1971 – it is now part of the museum complex. It costs 25 AED (6.81 USD) for an adult to visit it.

world knowledge.Name: Coral Bay, Cyprus
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 600m crescent of soft white sand, enclosed by a pair of limestone headlands. The coast is characterized by rocky headlands and sea caves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Popular tourist resort with EU Blue Flag certification for adhering to environmental and quality standards.
world knowledge.Details: Coral Bay beach carries an EU Blue Flag certification. The broader area of Coral Bay encloses another beach called Potima Bay, situated about 1.5 km / 1 mile away bordering the boundaries of Kissonerga village.

world knowledge.Name: University of Lorraine
world knowledge.Address: Nancy, Metz, Epinal, Thionville, Grand Est, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Lorraine was originally founded in 1572 in Pont-à-Mousson by Charles III, Duke of Lorraine, and Charles, Cardinal of Lorraine. It was transferred to Nancy in 1768, closed in 1793, and reopened in 1864. The current university was formed in 2012 by merging Henri Poincaré University, Nancy 2 University, Paul Verlaine University – Metz, and the National Polytechnic Institute of Lorraine.

Major_Events.Description: The original University of Lorraine was founded in Pont-à-Mousson by Charles III, Duke of Lorraine, and Charles, Cardinal of Lorraine.
The university was moved from Pont-à-Mousson to Nancy.
The university was closed by revolutionaries.
The university was reopened.
Henri Poincaré University, Nancy 2 University, Paul Verlaine University – Metz, and the National Polytechnic Institute of Lorraine merged to form the current University of Lorraine.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Lorraine is a major public research university in France, known for its historical roots and contributions to education and research. It plays a significant role in the cultural and academic life of the Lorraine region.

Details.Motto: Innovation through the dialogue between knowledge fields
Details.Museums_and_Gardens: Le préau, Espace Bernard-Marie Koltès, Maison pour la Science en Lorraine, Musée archéologique, Aquarium Museum, Musée de l’Histoire du Fer, Jardin Botanique Jean-Marie-Pelt

world knowledge.Name: American University in Bulgaria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The American University in Bulgaria (AUBG) is a private university in Blagoevgrad, Bulgaria. Established in 1991, AUBG is the first American-style, liberal arts undergraduate education institution in Eastern Europe. It was founded with the support of the U.S. and Bulgarian governments, the Open Society Institute, the City of Blagoevgrad, and the University of Maine.

Major_Events.Description: AUBG opened its doors in September 1991 with a first-year class of 208 students and 16 full-time faculty members.
AUBG launched its first Acceleration Program Elevate in 2019 to help student entrepreneurs and recent alumni start their first businesses.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: AUBG is culturally significant as the first American-style liberal arts university in Eastern Europe, fostering international education and cultural exchange. It has a diverse student body from over 40 countries and offers programs that are highly regarded in Bulgaria and internationally.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education institution offering undergraduate and graduate programs.
world knowledge.Details: AUBG offers a traditional American-style liberal arts education with a focus on double majors and minors. It has a diverse faculty from over 15 countries and offers exchange programs with universities in the U.S. and Europe. The university has a strong emphasis on innovation, entrepreneurship, and student involvement in clubs, sports, and media.

world knowledge.Name: Dolphin Oval
world knowledge.Address: Kippa-Ring, City of Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dolphin Stadium, originally known as Dolphin Oval, was constructed in the late 1970s on re-claimed land made available by the Redcliffe City Council. The Redcliffe Dolphins rugby league club, previously based at the Redcliffe Showgrounds, moved to this new location. The construction faced challenges due to the area's isolation, requiring additional infrastructure like sewerage pumps and underground power lines. The stadium has undergone several redevelopments, including phases completed in 2018 and 2020, and was renamed Moreton Daily Stadium before becoming Kayo Stadium in 2022.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the Queensland Cup Grand Finals in these years.
Brisbane Roar played the first ever A-League Men game at the venue against Melbourne City, attracting a sell-out crowd of 9387. The Roar won 4-3.
Due to COVID-19 outbreaks, the stadium hosted NRL matches, including a double-header featuring New Zealand Warriors vs Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs and Cronulla Sharks vs Newcastle Knights.
The stadium hosted the 2021 NRLW Grand Final between the St George Illawarra Dragons and the Sydney Roosters, the first NRLW Grand Final held outside of Sydney.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features grass surface, floodlighting, a perimeter playing fence, and a northern grandstand. Broadcast standard light towers were installed in 2023.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dolphin Stadium is significant as the home ground for the Redcliffe Dolphins rugby league club and has hosted numerous major sporting events, including NRL games and grand finals. It plays a key role in the local sports community and has adapted to modern needs through redevelopment.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium hosting rugby league, A-League football, and other major sporting events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone multiple naming changes, from Dolphin Oval to Moreton Daily Stadium and finally Kayo Stadium. It has a capacity of 10,000 (9,420 seats) and is owned and operated by the Redcliffe Dolphins. The venue has also been used by the Brisbane Roar A-League team for home matches.

world knowledge.Name: Yangon International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yangon International Airport is the primary and busiest international airport of Myanmar. It was built on the site of the former RAF Mingaladon in 1947. During World War II, the airfield served as an operating base for fighter aircraft and was used by the Japanese after they took over in 1942. The airport fell into disrepair for decades but underwent modernization starting in 2003, resulting in new terminals and extended runways.

Major_Events.Description: The Japanese began their attack on Burma, including an air raid on Mingaladon.
The outnumbered Allied forces retreated, and the Japanese took over the airfield.
A modernization program was launched, resulting in a new terminal and an extended 3414 m runway.
The new international terminal (T1) opened, increasing the airport's capacity to 6 million passengers annually.
The new domestic terminal (T3) opened, replacing the old domestic terminal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new terminal was designed by the CPG Corporation of Singapore and constructed by Asia World. It meets IATA service standards and complies with ICAO safety and security standards. The terminal can handle 900 arriving and 900 departing passengers simultaneously.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Yangon International Airport is culturally and historically significant as it was once regarded as the best airport in Southeast Asia and played a crucial role during World War II. It remains a key gateway to Myanmar.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as a hub for several airlines, including Mingalar Aviation Services, Air Thanlwin, Myanmar National Airlines, and Myanmar Airways International. It has undergone significant expansions and modernizations to increase its capacity and improve facilities. Plans are underway to build a new, larger airport, Hanthawaddy International Airport, away from Yangon.

world knowledge.Name: Kilis Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kilis Museum is located in a mansion named Neşet Efendi Konağı, built in 1927. The Ministry of Culture purchased the building in 1979. It served as the Kilis Public Library between 1986-2008 and was opened as a museum on 20 June 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The building was converted into a museum and opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is situated in a historic mansion, Neşet Efendi Konağı, built in 1927. The building features traditional architecture with rooms designed to reflect the lifestyle of Kilis citizens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its collection of archaeological finds from the region, including items from Oylum Höyük, and its ethnography section that showcases the cultural heritage of Kilis.
world knowledge.Details: The ground floor houses the archaeology section with exhibits from various historical periods, including Paleolithic, Neolithic, Bronze Age, Iron Age, Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine. The upper floor is dedicated to ethnography, featuring rooms that represent the guest room, bedroom, and kitchen of Kilis citizens with traditional furniture and mannequins.

world knowledge.Name: Tsing Ma Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Ma Wan Channel, New Territories, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Width: 41 metres (135 ft), Longest span: 1,377 metres (4,518 ft), Clearance below: 53 metres (174 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tsing Ma Bridge is a double-decked suspension bridge in Hong Kong, named after the islands of Tsing Yi and Ma Wan which it connects. It is the world's 17th-longest span suspension bridge and was the second longest at the time of its completion. The bridge was constructed as part of the Lantau Link, an infrastructure project to connect Lantau Island to the urbanized areas of Hong Kong, primarily to support the new Hong Kong International Airport at Chek Lap Kok.

Major_Events.Description: Construction work on the bridge began in May 1992.
The Lantau Link, including the Tsing Ma Bridge, was inaugurated on 27 April 1997 by former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher.
The Lantau Link was opened to traffic on 22 May 1997.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tsing Ma Bridge is a double-decked suspension bridge with a main span of 1,377 metres and a height of 206 metres. The bridge deck carries six lanes of automobile traffic on the upper deck and two rail tracks and two sheltered carriageways on the lower deck. The bridge was designed by Mott MacDonald and constructed by the Anglo Japanese Construction Joint Venture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tsing Ma Bridge is a vital transportation link in Hong Kong, connecting Lantau Island to the New Territories and supporting the Hong Kong International Airport. It is also a significant engineering achievement and a landmark in Hong Kong.
world knowledge.Details: The Tsing Ma Bridge is part of the Route 8 expressway and is monitored by the Wind and Structural Health Monitoring System (WASHMS). It has become a scenic spot with a visitor center and viewing platform on Tsing Yi Island. The bridge no longer charges tolls as of 27 December 2020.

world knowledge.Name: Istana Batu Royal Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Istana Batu Royal Museum was constructed in 1939 during the reign of Sultan Ismail ibni Sultan Muhammad IV as a wedding gift for his nephew Sultan Yahya Petra. Sultan Yahya Petra lived in the building until 1960 and moved to Kota Lama Palace once he ascended the throne. After he moved out, the building was renovated and became the official residence of Tengku Salwani binti Sultan Yahya Petra until 1969. The building eventually became the palace for Sultan Ismail Petra until 1972. Later, it was donated to Kelantan State Government. On 25 July 1991, the building was converted into a museum and officiated by Sultan Ismail Petra.

Major_Events.Description: The building was converted into a museum and officiated by Sultan Ismail Petra.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a yellow structure with interior rooms including the intersection, dining room, kitchen, drawing room, hallway, and bedroom.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum displays various belongings of the Sultan of Kelantan, such as photographs, costumes, artifacts, and furniture, preserving the cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum opens every day except Fridays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

world knowledge.Name: Mississippi State Capitol
world knowledge.Address: Fronting on Mississippi Street, between North President and North West Streets, Jackson, Hinds County, Mississippi
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 402 feet in width, 225 feet in depth, 171,000 square feet
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mississippi State Capitol, also known as the 'New Capitol,' has been the seat of the state’s government since 1903. It succeeded the old Mississippi State House and was designated as a Mississippi Landmark in 1986, a National Historic Landmark in 2016, and added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1969. The construction was initiated by Governor Andrew Houston Longino, and the design was selected through an architectural contest, with Theodore C. Link as the architect and Bernard R. Green as the consultant. The Capitol was completed in 1903, funded by a legal settlement with the Illinois Central Railroad. It originally housed all three branches of government but now primarily serves the Legislative branch.

Major_Events.Description: The Capitol was constructed on the site of the old Mississippi State Penitentiary, completed within 28 months at a cost of $1,093,641.
The Capitol underwent significant renovations, including the installation of mezzanine levels and restoration of public areas, costing $19 million.
The Capitol was designated a National Historic Landmark on October 31, 2016.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux Arts / Classical Revival style architecture. The exterior walls are Indiana limestone, and the base and stairs are Georgia granite. The central dome rises 180 feet above ground level, with a gold-plated copper eagle atop. The interior features over ten types of marble, stained and leaded glass windows by Louis Millet, and electric lighting with 4,750 fixtures. The Rotunda displays classical orders: Roman Doric, Ionic, and Composite capitals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Capitol is a symbol of Mississippi's government and history, representing the state's architectural and cultural heritage. It has been a focal point for political and social events and is a major tourist attraction in Jackson.
world knowledge.Details: The Capitol is open Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m., with guided tours available. It features a Hall of Governors with portraits of former governors, a gift shop, and public galleries for the Senate and House of Representatives. The Capitol Complex Improvement District (CCID) was created in 2017 to improve infrastructure and expand the jurisdiction of the Capitol Police, which has been a point of political controversy.

world knowledge.Name: McGill University
world knowledge.Address: 845 Sherbrooke St W, Montreal, Quebec H3A 0G4, Canada
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Downtown Campus: 32 ha (80 acres), Macdonald Campus: 650 ha (1,600 acres)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: McGill University was founded in 1821 by royal charter, bearing the name of James McGill, a Scottish merchant whose bequest in 1813 established the University of McGill College. The name was officially changed to McGill University in 1885. It is one of two members of the Association of American Universities located outside the United States and the only Canadian member of the Global University Leaders Forum.

Major_Events.Description: McGill College received a royal charter from King George IV, establishing it as a university with the power to confer degrees.
The name was officially changed from McGill College to McGill University.
Royal Victoria College opened as a residential college for women at McGill.

Major_Events.Event: World War I Memorial Hall dedication
Major_Events.Description: The War Memorial Hall was dedicated to honor students who enlisted and died in World War I and World War II.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features buildings constructed using local grey limestone, with many connected by indoor tunnels. Notable buildings include the Arts Building, Redpath Museum, and the Montreal Neurological Institute.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: McGill University is culturally and historically significant as one of Canada's oldest and most prestigious universities. It has produced numerous notable alumni, including 12 Nobel laureates, 149 Rhodes Scholars, and several Canadian prime ministers.
world knowledge.Details: McGill University offers degrees and diplomas in over 300 fields of study, with most students enrolled in the faculties of Arts, Science, Medicine, Education, Engineering, and Management. The university has a strong emphasis on research and is affiliated with several major research centers and networks.

world knowledge.Name: Big Pit National Coal Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Big Pit National Coal Museum is an industrial heritage museum in Blaenavon, Torfaen, Wales. It was a working coal mine from 1880 to 1980 and was opened to the public in 1983. The site is dedicated to the operational preservation of the Welsh heritage of coal mining during the Industrial Revolution. It is part of the Blaenavon Industrial Landscape, a World Heritage Site, and an Anchor Point of the European Route of Industrial Heritage.

Major_Events.Description: Big Pit was opened to the public as a charitable trust called the Big Pit (Blaenavon) Trust.

Major_Events.Event: Incorporation into National Museums and Galleries of Wales
Major_Events.Description: Big Pit Coal Museum was incorporated into the National Museums and Galleries of Wales as the National Mining Museum of Wales.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The Blaenavon industrial area, including Big Pit National Coal Museum, was named a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.
The Big Pit National Coal Museum won the prestigious Gulbenkian Prize, now known as Museum of the Year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The site includes several Grade II and Grade II* listed buildings, such as the Pit Head Building, Headframe & Tram Circuit, and the Miners' Bathhouse. The mine features authentic pit props and steel bands to hold up the mine roof, and water flows down a channel in the tunnels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Big Pit National Coal Museum is culturally significant as it preserves the heritage of coal mining in Wales, which played a crucial role during the Industrial Revolution. It is part of the Blaenavon Industrial Landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and serves as a reminder of the industrial history and the lives of miners.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features above-ground attractions such as a winding house, saw mill, pithead, and baths. Visitors are taken below ground to the pit bottom to tour the mine workings. The museum is still classified as a working pit, and visitors must wear safety gear, including a hard hat, safety lamp, and rebreather. The site has won several awards and is a significant tourist attraction in Wales.

world knowledge.Name: Magdeburg Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 120 m (393 ft 8 in), Width: 42.6 m (139 ft 9 in), Height: 32 m (105 ft 0 in)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Magdeburg Cathedral, officially the Cathedral of Saints Maurice and Catherine, is the oldest Gothic cathedral in Germany. It was constructed over 300 years, starting in 1209, and completed in 1520. The cathedral is the proto-cathedral of the former Prince-Archbishopric of Magdeburg and is now the principal church of the Evangelical Church in Central Germany. It houses the grave of Emperor Otto I the Great and his first wife Edith. The cathedral has survived numerous historical events, including the Thirty Years' War and World War II.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the current cathedral begins after the previous church was destroyed by fire in 1207.
The construction of the cathedral is completed with the placement of the ornamental cross on the north tower.
During the Thirty Years' War, Magdeburg is raided, and the cathedral serves as a refuge for survivors.
The cathedral suffers damage from Allied bombings, including the destruction of windows and parts of the structure.
The cathedral becomes a site for peace prayers and demonstrations, contributing to the German reunification process.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Magdeburg Cathedral is a Gothic basilica with two spires, the north tower standing at 100.98 m (331 ft 4 in) and the south tower at 99.25 m (325 ft 7 in). The cathedral features a nave with two aisles, a transept, and a cloister. The construction showcases the evolution of Gothic architecture in Germany, with Romanesque influences in the early phases. The cathedral lacks flying buttresses, which is unusual for Gothic cathedrals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Magdeburg Cathedral is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Germany. It is the oldest Gothic cathedral in the country and serves as the principal church of the Evangelical Church in Central Germany. The cathedral is also notable for housing the grave of Emperor Otto I the Great and for its role in the Protestant Reformation. Its rich history and architectural grandeur make it a symbol of Magdeburg and a testament to the region's historical and religious heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is undergoing reconstruction and has installed solar cells on its roof, making it one of the first churches in East Germany to do so. It also houses a significant collection of art, including the statue of Saint Maurice, which is one of the earliest representations of a black African in European art history.

world knowledge.Name: Lake Parz
world knowledge.Address: Dilijan National Park, east of Dilijan, Armenia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Parz, also known as Clear Lake, is a small lake located in the Dilijan National Park east of Dilijan in Armenia. It was formed by natural climatic changes.

Major_Events.Description: The Transcaucasian Trail was created to connect Parz Lake with the town of Dilijan and in the opposite direction with Gosh village and Gosh Lake. The trail was created through the building of new trail segments to connect existing trails or dirt roads together.
A new trail that loops around the lake was built.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Parz is a part of the Dilijan National Park and is a popular recreational area with a restaurant, paddle boats, ropes course, and zip lines.
world knowledge.Details: The lake has a surface elevation of 1,334 m (4,377 ft) and is surrounded by natural beauty, making it a popular spot for outdoor activities.

world knowledge.Name: Trang Airport
world knowledge.Location: Tambon Khok Lo, Amphoe Mueang Trang, Trang province, Thailand
world knowledge.Address: Tambon Khok Lo, Amphoe Mueang Trang, Trang province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Trang International Airport (IATA: TST, ICAO: VTST) is in Tambon Khok Lo, Amphoe Mueang Trang, Trang province in Southern Thailand, 7 km (4.3 mi) from downtown Trang. Despite being solely domestic, passenger numbers surged from 143 to almost 800 thousand from 2009 to 2017. It was planned to expand the terminal to 9,000 sq m. by mid-2019. The runway is planned to extend to 3,000 meters pending environmental review. A second passenger terminal was planned to be built by 2021, pushing capacity to 3.7 million a year.

Major_Events.Description: Trang Airport was opened on 13 December 1954.

world knowledge.Details: Trang International Airport (IATA: TST, ICAO: VTST) serves Trang province. It is located at coordinates 07°30′31.48″N 099°36′59.68″E, with an elevation of 20 m / 67 ft. The airport has a runway with a direction of 08/26, length of 2,100 m, and surface of asphalt (tarmac). In recent years, passenger numbers have significantly increased, leading to plans for terminal and runway expansions.

world knowledge.Name: Tomsk Polytechnic University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1896 as Tomsk Technological Institute of Emperor Nicholas II, it was established by the Ministry of National Education of the Russian Empire. The university has undergone several name changes and has been a significant center for technical education and research in Russia. It was involved in Project 5-100, aimed at elevating Russian universities to global prominence.

Major_Events.Description: The institute was renamed from Tomsk Technological Institute of Emperor Nicholas II to Tomsk Technological Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Dzerzhinsky Siberian Technological Institute
Major_Events.Description: The institute was renamed to Dzerzhinsky Siberian Technological Institute.
The institute was renamed to Tomsk Industrial Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Kirov Tomsk Polytechnic Institute
Major_Events.Description: The institute was renamed to Kirov Tomsk Polytechnic Institute.
The institute was renamed to Tomsk Polytechnic University.

The university was suspended from the Conference of European Schools for Advanced Engineering Education and Research (CESAER) and the European University Association (EUA) following support for the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building was constructed based on a project by Robert Marfeld, an academician of architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: TPU has been a pivotal institution in the development of technical education and research in Russia, contributing significantly to the country's industrial and scientific advancements.
world knowledge.Details: TPU was included in Project 5-100, a state program aimed at bringing at least five Russian universities into the 100 best universities in the world. It has been a member of several international associations and has conducted research projects within various European grant programs.

world knowledge.Name: Joypolis
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Joypolis is a chain of indoor amusement parks created by Sega, beginning with the original location in Yokohama, Japan, in 1994. Over time, parks opened in several cities in Japan and later China, featuring arcade games and amusement rides based on Sega's intellectual properties. Many parks have closed due to poor visitor numbers and managerial issues, with only four remaining operational as of 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The first Joypolis park opened in Yokohama, Japan, marking the beginning of Sega's 'Amusement Theme Park' concept.
The flagship Joypolis park opened in Odaiba, Tokyo, later becoming the only remaining Joypolis in Japan after refurbishments in 2000 and 2012.
A fatal accident occurred on the 'Viva! Skydiving' ride due to safety protocol violations, leading to a temporary closure of the park.
The first Joypolis park in China opened in Shanghai, followed by a second phase in 2016.
The first Joypolis venue in South China opened in Guangzhou, featuring 40 attractions.
The Qingdao Joypolis, the only Chinese venue directly owned by CA Sega Joypolis, closed permanently.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Indoor amusement parks with futuristic and video game-themed designs, featuring arcade games, VR attractions, and amusement rides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Joypolis represents Sega's venture into themed entertainment, blending video games, anime, and futuristic themes into immersive indoor amusement parks. It holds cultural significance as a pioneer in integrating gaming IPs into physical attractions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Indoor amusement park featuring arcade games, VR experiences, and themed rides.
world knowledge.Details: As of 2024, four Joypolis parks remain operational: Tokyo and Sendai (Japan), and Shanghai and Guangzhou (China). The parks are no longer fully controlled by Sega but operate under license agreements. The Tokyo location is the flagship park, while the Sendai venue focuses on sports-related activities under the 'Joypolis Sports' brand.

world knowledge.Name: Zumbi dos Palmares International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Campo dos Palmares Airport, it was renamed on 16 December 1999 to honor Zumbi dos Palmares, a pioneer of resistance to slavery in Brazil. The airport has undergone several expansions and changes in operation, including a major renovation in 2005 and a change in operator from Infraero to AENA in 2020.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Zumbi dos Palmares International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed to celebrate Zumbi dos Palmares (1645–1695), one of the pioneers of resistance to slavery in Brazil.
The airport underwent a major expansion, including the renovation of the passenger terminal and apron, and the extension of the runway to 2,602 meters.
AENA won a 30-year concession to operate the airport, taking over from Infraero.
AENA inaugurated modernization works, providing renovated spaces, large operational areas, and new quality parameters in management.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway with asphalt surface, measuring 2,602 meters in length. The passenger terminal and apron were renovated during the 2005 expansion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Zumbi dos Palmares, a significant figure in the resistance against slavery in Brazil, highlighting its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Maceió, Brazil, facilitating passenger, cargo, and aircraft operations.

image_name: Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet

world knowledge.Name: Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet, originally built on former marshland of the submerged Poltva River, was constructed between 1897 and 1900. It was designed by Zygmunt Gorgolewski, who utilized innovative engineering techniques such as a reinforced concrete base and the enclosure of the Poltva River underground. The theatre has undergone several name changes and renovations, reflecting the political and cultural shifts in the region. It was renamed in 2000 after Solomiya Krushelnytska, a renowned soprano of the early 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The Lviv Opera opened on October 4, 1900, with a grand gala attended by cultural elites and delegations from various European theatres.
The theatre underwent significant renovation during this period.

Major_Events.Event: First performance of Ukraine's national anthem
Major_Events.Description: The first performance of Ukraine's national anthem, 'Shche ne vmerla Ukrainy i slava, i volia,' was held at the theatre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet is built in the classical tradition with Renaissance Revival and Neo-Baroque architectural styles, incorporating elements of Art Nouveau. The building features stucco mouldings, oil paintings, Corinthian columns, pilasters, balustrades, cornices, statues, reliefs, and stucco garlands. The interior decoration was prepared by renowned Polish artists, including Stanisław Wójcik, Julian Markowski, and Tadeusz Barącz.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is a cultural landmark in Ukraine, reflecting the artistic and architectural achievements of the late 19th century. It has been a center for opera and ballet performances and has played a role in the cultural and political history of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre is located on Liberty Avenue in Lviv's historic Old City, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has a seating capacity of 1,100 and is owned by the National government. The building's façade is decorated with allegorical figures representing Comedy and Tragedy, and the top of the cornice is embellished with figures of muses. The building is crowned by large bronze statues symbolizing Glory, Poetry, and Music.

world knowledge.Name: Vinh University
world knowledge.Address: 182 Le Duan Street, Vinh City, Nghe An
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 14ha in Ben Thuy Truong Thi, 258ha in Nghi Loc district
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established on July 16, 1959 under Decree 375/ND, initially as College of Education Sub performance Vinh, renamed to Pedagogical University of Vinh in 1962, and finally to Vinh University in 2001. It has grown into a comprehensive university serving the North Central region of Vietnam.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as College of Education Sub performance Vinh under Decree 375/ND.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Pedagogical University of Vinh
Major_Events.Description: Renamed under Decision 637/QD by the Minister of Education.
Renamed under Decision No. 62/2001/QD-TTg by the Prime Minister.
Added to the list of universities to build a major university in the country under written consent 1136/TTg-KGVX.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Not explicitly described in the provided information.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vinh University is a key educational institution in the North Central region of Vietnam, providing high-quality human resources and contributing to the economic and social development of the region and country. It is also a center for scientific research and international cooperation.
world knowledge.Details: Vinh University is a multidisciplinary, multi-level institution offering 42 undergraduate, 28 master's, and 10 doctoral programs. It has nearly 36,000 students, including over 300 international students, and a staff of nearly 950. The university has received numerous awards and honors, including the Second Class Labor Decoration, Independence Medal, and Hero Labor title. It is also involved in international cooperation with over 30 universities and scientific organizations worldwide.

world knowledge.Name: Palm Cove
world knowledge.Address: Palm Cove, Cairns Region, Queensland, 4879, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Palm Cove is named after the palm trees lining its beach. The area was originally part of Djabugay (Tjapukai) traditional Aboriginal country. The first documented British visit was in 1873 by George Elphinstone Dalrymple. The land was bought by Albert Veivers in 1918, leading to development. Post-WWII, tourism increased. The first international hotel, Ramada Reef Resort, opened in 1986.

Major_Events.Description: George Elphinstone Dalrymple's coastal expedition visited the area, encountering Aboriginal resistance.
Veivers bought the land from Archdeacon Campbell, leading to road construction and increased property values.
Palm Cove was used as a training base for Australian soldiers during WWII.
First international hotel chain in Palm Cove, boosting tourism.

Major_Events.Event: Named Best Beach in the World
Major_Events.Description: Condé Nast Traveler rated Palm Cove as the number-one 'Best Beach in the World'.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Palm Cove is culturally significant for its Indigenous history, colonial encounters, and development as a tourist destination. It is also part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area and close to the Great Barrier Reef.

Details.Climate: Tropical, with summer temperatures between 24-33°C and winter temperatures between 14-26°C.
Details.Industry: Accommodation and Food Services sector (21.2% of residents in 2011).
Details.Education: No schools in Palm Cove; nearest schools are in Trinity Beach and Smithfield.
Details.Amenities: Three convenience stores, a post office, pharmacy, cafes, bars, restaurants, bicycle and scooter hire, watersports activities, and retail shops.
Details.Transportation: Connected by Captain Cook Highway and buses; nearest airport is Cairns International Airport.
Details.Attractions: Proximity to Great Barrier Reef and Daintree Rainforest, pristine beaches, palm tree-lined paths, fishing at Palm Cove jetty.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio da Várzea
world knowledge.Address: Avenida Cidade de Lisboa Praia, Santiago, Cape Verde
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio da Várzea is a multi-purpose stadium in Praia, Cape Verde, constructed around the mid-20th century. It was reopened in 2006 after renovations. The stadium has hosted numerous football matches and significant events, including the Amilcar Cabral Cup and various national championships.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the Amilcar Cabral Cup, which also led to the cancellation of the national championships that season.
Hosted the Amilcar Cabral Cup where the team defeated Senegal 1-0 and won the only title.
The first Cape Verdean Cup final took place in September 2007, won by Académica Praia.

Major_Events.Event: Field became artificial and synthetic turf
Major_Events.Description: On March 15, 2007, the field became artificial and synthetic turf due to the unfavorable climate for natural grass.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architectural type is early modernism. The exterior is colored stucco-peach with eight modernized square columns. The entrance gates and offices are located at the bottom inside, colored white. The middle is light brown with flaw windows and a circular window at the second floor. The stadium features balconies, thick glass staircase windows, and small squared windows on its upper floors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Estádio da Várzea is culturally significant as it is home to the four best football clubs in Cape Verde and has hosted numerous important football matches and events, including the Amilcar Cabral Cup and national championships.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by the city of Praia and operated by the Santiago South Regional Football Association. It has a capacity of 8,000 people and is home to several football clubs, including Sporting, CD Travadores, Académica, and Boavista FC. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including the addition of artificial grass and artificial lights. It is also used for music concerts and other events.

world knowledge.Name: Torqabeh
world knowledge.Location: Torqabeh District of Torqabeh and Shandiz County, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Torqabeh is a city in Torqabeh District of Torqabeh and Shandiz County, Razavi Khorasan province, Iran, serving as capital of both the county and the district. At the time of the 2006 National Census, the city's population was 13,158 in 3,668 households, when it was in Mashhad County. The following census in 2011 counted 16,718 people in 5,067 households, by which time the district had been separated from the county in the establishment of Binalud County. The 2016 census measured the population of the city as 20,998 people in 6,612 households.

Major_Events.Description: The city's population was 13,158 in 3,668 households.
The city's population was 16,718 people in 5,067 households.
The city's population was 20,998 people in 6,612 households.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Torqabeh is culturally significant as it serves as the capital of both Torqabeh and Shandiz County and Torqabeh District.
world knowledge.Details: This Torqabeh and Shandiz County location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Seoul Museum of Art
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Seoul Museum of Art was opened on August 19, 1988, in the Gyeonghuigung Palace area, a royal palace of the Joseon dynasty. In 2002, a larger main branch was opened behind Deoksugung Palace, replacing the Gyeonghuigung Branch as the main branch. The museum occupies the old Korean Supreme Court building, which was remodeled and renovated to house three floors of exhibition halls, an administration annex, and a basement with lecture halls, classrooms, and offices. The museum has two more branches in Seoul: SeMA Buk-Seoul in Nowon District and SeMA Nam-Seoul in Namhyeon-dong, Gwanak-gu.

Major_Events.Description: The Seoul Museum of Art was opened in the Gyeonghuigung Palace area with six exhibition rooms and an outdoor sculpture park.

The main branch of the museum was relocated to a larger building behind Deoksugung Palace, replacing the Gyeonghuigung Branch as the main branch. The new location is the old Korean Supreme Court building, which was remodeled and renovated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's main branch is housed in the old Korean Supreme Court building, which was remodeled and renovated. It features three floors of exhibition halls, an administration annex, and a basement with lecture halls, classrooms, and offices. The building was designed by Samoo Architects & Engineers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Seoul Museum of Art is a significant cultural institution in Seoul, offering a wide variety of services to the public, including art classes, docent programs, and lectures. It plays a crucial role in promoting Korean traditional arts and contemporary art.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's main branch offers low or no-cost public art classes in Korean traditional arts, docent programs in English and Korean, and lectures open to the public. Kim Hong-hee is currently the vice executive of the museum. The museum has two additional branches in Seoul: SeMA Buk-Seoul in Nowon District and SeMA Nam-Seoul in Namhyeon-dong, Gwanak-gu.

world knowledge.Name: Altai State University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Altai State University is a public research university in Barnaul, Russia. It was established by a decree by Leonid Brezhnev as the first multidisciplinary university in Altai Krai in 1973.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the first multidisciplinary university in Altai Krai, it plays a significant role in the region's educational and research landscape.
world knowledge.Details: Altai State University has the following departments: Arts, Biology, Chemistry, Geography, History, Law, Mathematics and IT, Mass Communication, Philology and Political Science, Physics and Technology, Education and Psychology, Sociology and International Institute of Economics, Management and Informational Systems. The university has affiliates in Biysk, Belokurikha, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod all in Altai Krai.

world knowledge.Name: Semenic-Caraș Gorge National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Semenic-Caraș Gorge National Park was declared a protected area by Law No. 5 of 6 March 2000 (published in Monitorul Oficial No. 152 on 12 April 2000). It features a typical karst and forest landscape and is characterised by its 300-year-old virgin beech forest, the only one in Europe.

Major_Events.Description: The Semenic-Caraș Gorge National Park was declared a protected area by Law No. 5 of 6 March 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a typical karst and forest landscape with 300-year-old virgin beech forest, the only one in Europe. It includes the Caraș Gorge, Caraș Springs, and various caves with diverse formations of stalactites and stalagmites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and historically important due to its unique 300-year-old virgin beech forest, diverse flora and fauna, and the presence of archaeological sites and historical ruins such as the thirteenth-century Grat Castle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Protected area (national park category II IUCN)
world knowledge.Details: The park contains a number of nature reserves, including the Caraș Gorge, the Caraș Springs, and various caves. Twenty archaeological sites have been discovered in the park.

world knowledge.Name: Hump Ridge Track
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hump Ridge Track, also called the Tuatapere Hump Ridge Track, is a 60-62 km walking track that is partly in Fiordland National Park in New Zealand. The track was opened in 2001 and is run privately on behalf of the Tuatapere Hump Ridge Track Charitable Trust. In 2019 it was announced that the track would become the eleventh of the New Zealand Great Walks, following upgrades. The track was opened as a Great Walk on 25 October 2024.

Major_Events.Description: An annual event where participants attempt to complete the entire track in under 24 hours. It was started in 2011 and walkers start early at midnight on a Friday in February with lights to guide their way. Any money raised goes to track maintenance.
The track was upgraded to become the eleventh of the New Zealand Great Walks, with improvements to the track standard, gradient, and facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The track includes boardwalks, staircases, and historic viaducts. The Percy Burn Viaduct is one of the world's largest wooden mill tramway viaducts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The track reflects the significant cultural and heritage values of the area, including early Māori hunting camps and historic logging sites. It is also a premier tramping track in New Zealand.
world knowledge.Details: The track is a three-day walk with between six and eight hours of walking each day. It includes options for helicopter access and guided tours. The area features dense forests, alpine views, beaches, and historic relics. The track is operated by a non-profit business, Tuatapere Hump Ridge Track Inc., on behalf of the Tuatapere Hump Ridge Track Charitable Trust.

world knowledge.Name: CureVac
world knowledge.Historical_Background: CureVac N.V. is a German biopharmaceutical company founded in 2000. It develops therapies based on messenger RNA (mRNA). The company has been involved in the development of vaccines for infectious diseases, including an early attempt to create a COVID-19 vaccine during the pandemic.

Major_Events.Description: Clinical trials for the CureVac COVID-19 Vaccine (CVnCoV) began in June 2020.
The German Federal Government invested €300 million in CureVac, with KfW holding a 23% stake in the company.
In June 2021, CureVac announced that CVnCoV displayed inadequate results in Phase III clinical trials with only 47% efficacy.
In October 2021, CureVac announced it would abandon further research into CVnCoV and focus on collaborating with GSK to develop improved mRNA vaccine technology.
On 14 August 2020, CureVac began public trading on the NASDAQ exchange under the ticker symbol CVAC, raising $213 million in its initial public offering.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: CureVac is significant for its pioneering work in mRNA-based therapies and vaccines, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's efforts have contributed to advancements in biotechnology and vaccine development.
world knowledge.Details: CureVac has entered into various collaborations with organizations, including agreements with Boehringer Ingelheim, Sanofi Pasteur, Johnson & Johnson, Genmab, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Eli Lilly and Company, GlaxoSmithKline, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative, and the government of Germany.

world knowledge.Name: Kyushu Ceramic Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum was built to contribute to the local cultural heritage and the development of ceramics and pottery culture throughout Kyushu, southern Japan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses valuable collections of ceramics and pottery, including the Kanbara Collection of old Imari from Europe and the Shibata Collection of Arita pottery, showcasing the region's rich ceramic heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features several collections: Shibata Collection, Kanbara Collection, Old Ceramics of Kyushu, Hakuu Collection, Takatori Collection, Aoki Ryuzan Works Collection, and Nakazato Hoan Works Collection.

world knowledge.Name: Portugal dos Pequenitos
world knowledge.Address: Santa Clara e Castelo Viegas, Coimbra, Portugal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Portugal dos Pequenitos, meaning 'Portugal of/for the Little Ones', is a miniature park in Coimbra, Portugal. It was initiated by Fernando Bissaya Barreto, a professor and politician, and designed by architect Cassiano Branco. The park features miniature replicas of Portuguese houses, monuments, and pavilions dedicated to former Portuguese colonies. The construction occurred in three phases: the first phase (1938-1940) focused on traditional homes and structures from Trás-os-Montes and Minho regions; the second phase in the mid-century showcased Portuguese monuments; and the third phase in the late 1950s included pavilions representing Portuguese overseas provinces. The park was integrated into the Bissaya Barreto Foundation in 1959 and has since undergone expansions and renovations.

Major_Events.Description: The construction of Portugal dos Pequenitos began in 1938.
The park became part of the Bissaya Barreto Foundation's heritage.
A new visitor center and sundial were added to the park.
The park recorded its highest number of yearly visitors at 331,000.

Major_Events.Event: Proposal for new monuments and regional houses
Major_Events.Description: The board proposed adding more Portuguese monuments and regional houses to the park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features miniature replicas of Portuguese houses, monuments, and pavilions representing Portuguese-speaking African countries, Brazil, Macau, India, and Timor. The structures are divided into three thematic areas: traditional regional architecture, Portuguese monuments, and ethnographic artefacts from Portuguese colonies.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Portugal dos Pequenitos is culturally significant as it showcases the architectural and cultural heritage of Portugal and its former colonies. It serves as an educational and recreational site, preserving and promoting Portuguese history and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The park is situated on the left bank of the Mondego River, near the Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Nova, Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Velha, and the Convent of São Francisco. It includes representations of monuments, traditional homes, and ethnographic artefacts, surrounded by native flora.

world knowledge.Name: McCormick Place
world knowledge.Historical_Background: McCormick Place is the largest convention center in North America. It was championed by Robert R. McCormick and opened in November 1960. The original building was destroyed in a fire in 1967 but was rebuilt and expanded over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The original building was destroyed in a major fire on January 16, 1967, despite being thought fireproof. The fire spread quickly due to combustible exhibits, shut-off hydrants, and lack of sprinklers, resulting in one fatality.
The replacement building, later called the Lakeside Center, opened on January 3, 1971, with a 300,000 square feet main exhibition hall.

Major_Events.Event: Transformation into a hospital during COVID-19
Major_Events.Description: In response to the COVID-19 crisis, the complex began transforming convention space into a 3,000-bed hospital, completed on April 30, 2020.
McCormick Place Lakeside Center implemented a project to make its windows more visible to birds, reducing bird collisions by over 95% during the fall migration season.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The East Building features dark steel and glass, contrasting with the original white structure. The North Building is white with twelve concrete pylons on the roof, resembling a rigged sailing ship. The South and West Buildings added significant exhibition and meeting space, with modern designs by tvsdesign.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: McCormick Place is a major hub for trade shows, conventions, and cultural events in Chicago. It is the largest convention center in North America and has played a significant role in the city's economic and cultural development.
world knowledge.Details: McCormick Place consists of four interconnected buildings and one indoor arena. It hosts major events like the Chicago Auto Show, International Home and Housewares Show, and National Restaurant Association Annual Show. The complex includes the Arie Crown Theater, Wintrust Arena, and McCormick Place Bird Sanctuary. It is served by multiple public transit options, including CTA buses and trains, Metra, and the South Shore Line.

world knowledge.Name: Clock Tower, St Albans
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 19.6 metres (64 ft) high, five floors including the roof
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Clock Tower was constructed between 1403 and 1412 as a protest against the power of St Albans Abbey to regulate time-keeping in the town. It is believed to be the only remaining medieval town belfry in England. The Tower was used as a semaphore station during the Napoleonic Wars and underwent restoration in 1866 by Sir Gilbert Scott.

Major_Events.Description: Built as a protest against St Albans Abbey's control over time-keeping.
Used as a semaphore station for the London to Great Yarmouth line.
Restored by Sir Gilbert Scott, with external masonry renewed and new features added.
Restoration works carried out by Smiths of Derby, funded by Historic England.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grade I listed belfry, 19.6 metres high with five floors. Exterior faced in flint with freestone dressings, quoins on each corner, and a stone battlemented parapet with gargoyles. Features cusped and ogee windows, and a 93-step spiral staircase leading to the roof.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Clock Tower is a symbol of the town's independence from the Abbey's control. It is a rare surviving example of a medieval town belfry and has played various roles in the town's history, including time-keeping and communication.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a bell tower, now a clock tower and historical landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The Tower contains two bells: Gabriel and the Market bell. Gabriel is inscribed with "Missi De Celis Habeo Nomen Gabrielis" and was rung for the Angelus and curfew. The current clock mechanism, installed in 1866, was designed by Lord Grimthorpe. The Tower is open to the public on weekends and bank holidays between Good Friday and the end of September, as well as during special events.

world knowledge.Name: Sabancı Cultural Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hacı Ömer Sabancı Cultural Center was established in 1976 as a joint project by Sabancı Holding and Turkish Education Foundation. It has been administered by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism since its opening. The center expanded in 1982 with the addition of a fine arts gallery and theater upgrades. It underwent renovation in 2007 with contributions from the Sabancı Foundation.

Major_Events.Description: Adana State Theatre opened its stage at the center.
The fine arts gallery was added, and the theater was expanded and modernized.
The center was renovated with contributions from the Sabancı Foundation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The center is a cultural complex featuring a theater hall, public library, fine arts gallery, and exhibition hall. The theater hall is equipped with modern facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sabancı Cultural Center is a key cultural hub in Adana, hosting theater performances, art exhibitions, and educational activities. It plays a significant role in promoting arts and culture in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural complex (Theatre, Fine Arts Gallery, Library, Exhibition Hall)
world knowledge.Details: The 368-seater theater hall hosts the Adana State Theatre and community theater groups, with regular performances from October to May. The center also houses a 200-seat library open year-round. The Sabancı Theater Festival is held here.

world knowledge.Name: Montrose Basin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Montrose Basin is a nearly circular tidal basin part of the estuary of the River South Esk. It has been designated as a Wildlife Reserve, Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest, Special Protection Area, and Ramsar Site. The basin has a variety of habitats including tidal mudflats, saltmarsh, reedbed, and fen. It has been a site for studying sea level fluctuations post the last glaciation and contains the largest area of saltmarsh in Angus. The basin has a rich biodiversity including large populations of invertebrates and over 213 species of birds. It has a history of human activity dating back to over 3,000 BCE and was exploited for seafood, especially Atlantic salmon and mussels. The basin was hit by a tsunami in 6,100 BCE due to the Storegga Slide in Norway.

Major_Events.Description: Montrose Basin was designated as a Wildlife Reserve managed by the Scottish Wildlife Trust.

Major_Events.Event: Formation of Montrose Basin Heritage Society
Major_Events.Description: The Montrose Basin Heritage Society was formed to gather information about the basin's history and archaeology.
Commercial fisheries for Atlantic salmon in the basin ended.
The basin was hit by a 70-foot high tsunami generated by the Storegga Slide in Norway.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Montrose Basin is culturally and historically significant due to its rich biodiversity, archaeological sites dating back over 3,000 BCE, and its history of seafood exploitation. It is also important for the study of sea level fluctuations post the last glaciation.
world knowledge.Details: The basin supports a large breeding population of eiders and has extensive mudflats home to large populations of invertebrates. A visitor centre was opened in 1995 by the Scottish Wildlife Trust on the south side of the basin at Rossie Braes.

world knowledge.Name: National Opera of Ukraine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kyiv Opera group was formally established in the summer of 1867 by Ferdinand Berger. Initially, the troupe performed at the City Theatre, which was constructed in 1856. The first performance was on November 8, 1867, with the opera 'Askold's Tomb' by Alexey Verstovsky. The original theatre was destroyed by fire on February 4, 1896, and a new building designed by Victor Schröter was opened on September 29, 1901. The theatre has undergone several name changes and has been a significant cultural institution in Ukraine.

Major_Events.Description: A fire erupted from an unextinguished candle, consuming the whole building and destroying one of the largest musical libraries in Europe along with numerous costumes and stage props.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the new theatre building
Major_Events.Description: The new building designed by Victor Schröter was opened with a performance of the cantata 'Kyiv' by Wilhelm Hartweld and the opera 'Life for the Tsar' by M. Glinka.

Major_Events.Event: Assassination of Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin
Major_Events.Description: During a performance of Rimsky-Korsakov's 'The Tale of Tsar Saltan', Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin was assassinated by Dmitry Bogrov.
The congress was held in the Opera House, known for the First Universal of the Ukrainian Central Council proclamation.

Major_Events.Event: World premiere of ballet based on the life of Olga of Kiev
Major_Events.Description: The ballet was performed to commemorate the 1500th anniversary of the city of Kyiv.

Major_Events.Event: Last performance before the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
Major_Events.Description: The opera 'Natalka Poltavka' was the last scheduled performance before the invasion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The exterior was designed in Neo-Renaissance style, and the interior was redesigned in a classical style called Viennese Modern. The stage is one of the largest in Europe, designed to the latest engineering standards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Opera of Ukraine is a significant cultural institution in Ukraine, representing the country's rich musical and theatrical heritage. It has been a platform for promoting Ukrainian culture and language, especially during the Soviet era when operas were performed in Ukrainian.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has toured extensively, including performances in Germany, France, Switzerland, Canada, the United States, Mexico, Denmark, Spain, Italy, Japan, Australia, Greece, Brazil, Estonia, Poland, China, Hungary, Austria, Holland, Belgium, Portugal, Turkey, and Oman. In 2017, Ukraine celebrated the 150th anniversary of the founding of the Taras Shevchenko National Academic Opera and Ballet Theater in Kyiv.

world knowledge.Name: Jiujiang Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Xunyang District of Jiujiang, Jiangxi Province / Xiaochi Town, Huangmei County, Hubei Province
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jiujiang Yangtze River Bridge is a combined road-rail bridge over the Yangtze River near the city of Jiujiang, Jiangxi Province in eastern China. Construction began in 1973 but due to work stoppages, the bridge was not completed until 1993. The bridge was originally designed to carry trucks weighing up to 30 tons, later raised to 55 tons in 2008, and then lowered to 20 tons in 2012 due to structural concerns.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed and opened to traffic after delays.
The tonnage limit for trucks was raised from 30 tons to 55 tons.
A crack was discovered in the bridge's steel structure, leading to the closure of the bridge to freight traffic.
The tonnage limit for trucks was lowered to 20 tons due to structural concerns.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge uses a combined arch and truss structure and is one of the longest continuous truss bridges in the world, with a longest span of 216 meters and a total truss length of 1,314 meters. The double-deck bridge carries four vehicular lanes and two sidewalks on the top deck and two railway tracks on the bottom deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a critical transportation link between Jiangxi and Hubei provinces, facilitating road and rail travel across the Yangtze River.
world knowledge.Details: The Jiujiang Fuyin Expressway Bridge, a cable-stayed bridge 10 kilometers upstream, opened in 2013.

world knowledge.Name: Victoria Mansion
world knowledge.Address: 109 Danforth Street, Portland, Maine, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Victoria Mansion, also known as the Morse-Libby House or Morse-Libby Mansion, was completed in 1860 as a summer home for hotelier Ruggles Sylvester Morse. It was designed by architect Henry Austin and features elaborate interior design, opulent furnishings, and early technological conveniences. The house was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1971 for its architectural significance as a well-preserved Italianate mansion. After Morse's death in 1893, the house was sold to Joseph Ralph Libby, whose family occupied it until 1928. The house was later saved from demolition by William H. Holmes and opened as a museum in 1941.

Major_Events.Description: The house was completed as a summer home for Ruggles Sylvester Morse.
The house and its contents were sold to Joseph Ralph Libby after Morse's death.
The last of the Libbys moved out, and the house was later abandoned.
William H. Holmes bought the house to preserve it as a museum.
The house was opened as the Victoria Mansion museum.
