During the Polish People's Republic (1945–89), the quality of productions was sometimes affected by government pressures.

Major_Events.Description: The first Polish opera, Maciej Kamieński's 'Poverty Made Happy', with Wojciech Bogusławski's libretto based on a comedy by Franciszek Bohomolec, was produced at the Radziwiłł Palace.

Major_Events.Event: Premiere of Chopin's Piano Concerto No. 1
Major_Events.Description: On 17 March 1830, Frédéric Chopin premiered his Piano Concerto No. 1 in E minor, Op. 11 at the National Theatre.
The National Theatre was revived under the Second Polish Republic after being closed following the November 1830 Uprising.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theatre is a symbol of Polish culture and history, representing the country's artistic and theatrical heritage. It played a key role in the development of Polish opera and theatre, and it is associated with notable figures such as Wojciech Bogusławski, known as the father of Polish National Theatre, and Frédéric Chopin.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre shares the Grand Theatre complex with Poland's National Opera. Opera was brought to Poland by future King Władysław IV Vasa in the early 17th century. The first public opera-theater in Poland, the Operalnia, was opened in 1748 in the Saxon Garden. From 1774, performances were held in the Radziwiłł Palace, and from 1779-1833 in a theatre building on Krasiński Square.

world knowledge.Name: Barishal Airport
world knowledge.Address: Rahamatpur area of Babuganj Upazila, 12 km north of Barisal city centre, beside Dhaka - Barisal Highway, Bangladesh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Barishal Airport was constructed in 1985 to meet the demand for quicker travel to the capital Dhaka. It was officially inaugurated on 3 December 1995 by President Abdur Rahman Biswas. The airport played a significant role during the relief operation after Cyclone Sidr in November 2007, aiding in the distribution of international relief goods.

Major_Events.Description: Officially inaugurated by President Abdur Rahman Biswas.
Played a crucial role in distributing international relief goods to cyclone-affected victims.

Major_Events.Event: Resumption of Biman Bangladesh Airlines Flights
Major_Events.Description: Biman Bangladesh Airlines resumed weekly flights after nine years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Runway: 5,995 ft (1,827 m) length, asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is vital for regional connectivity and has been instrumental in emergency relief operations, significantly impacting the local community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Domestic airport serving Barisal and surrounding areas.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has served 158,987 passengers between 1995 and 2009, with over 20,000 flights including passengers, training, cargo, and other flights. It saw the highest number of passengers in 1999 and the highest number of flights in 2000.

world knowledge.Name: Cathedral of the Assumption
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Assumption Cathedral may refer to any of a number of cathedrals consecrated to the Assumption of Mary in the Roman Catholic tradition.

world knowledge.Name: Bicton House, Devon
world knowledge.Address: Bicton College, Bicton, near Exmouth, East Devon
world knowledge.Construction_Period: late 18th- or early 19th-century (current structure built circa 1800)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bicton House is a historic manor with roots dating back to the Domesday Survey. Originally held by William Portitor, the king's door-keeper, it served as the king's gaol for Devon. Over centuries, it passed through various families including the Alabasters, Sachevilles, Coplestons, Denys, and Rolles. The current mansion was built by John Rolle, 1st Baron Rolle, replacing an earlier manor house. The estate was later leased to Devon County Council in 1947, becoming Bicton College.

Major_Events.Description: John Rolle, 1st Baron Rolle, replaced the old manor house with the existing three-storey mansion designed by architect James Wyatt.
The house and part of the grounds were leased to Devon County Council for the creation of Bicton Farm Institute, later Bicton College.
The property was sold to the council, though part of the grounds remain owned by the present Baron Clinton.
During the war, the house accommodated St Ronan's School, which has since relocated to Kent.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Three-storey mansion built in red brick and limestone, designed by James Wyatt. Features two extensive wings, a Gothic lodge, and a rustic inner lodge. The estate includes ancient beech and oak trees and an obelisk visible from most parts of the grounds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bicton House is a Grade II* listed building, with its park and gardens Grade I listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. It holds historical importance as a former royal gaol and a significant estate in Devon, associated with prominent families like the Rolles. The house also hosted an extensive art collection, including works by Rembrandt and Ruysdael.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a manor house and estate, now part of Bicton College campus.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes Bicton Arena, used for equestrian events, and is near the headquarters of the Clinton Devon Estates Company, which owns 25,000 acres of agricultural land in Devon. The manor was historically responsible for managing the county gaol, later moved to Exeter.

world knowledge.Name: Masjid al-Haram
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Masjid al-Haram, also known as the Sacred Mosque or the Great Mosque of Mecca, is considered the most significant mosque in Islam. It encloses the Kaaba in Mecca and is a central site for the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages. The mosque has undergone numerous renovations and expansions throughout history, starting from its establishment in 638 CE. It has been under the control of various caliphs, sultans, and kings, and is currently managed by the King of Saudi Arabia, titled the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques.

Major_Events.Description: The mosque's outer walls were raised, and it was expanded under the orders of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.
Mimar Sinan renovated the mosque, replacing the flat roof with domes and adding new support columns.
The walls of the Kaaba and the mosque suffered extensive damage during heavy rains and flash floods.
The mosque was renovated, adding a new stone arcade, three more minarets, and retiling the marble flooring.

Major_Events.Event: First major renovation under Saudi kings
Major_Events.Description: Four more minarets were added, the ceiling was refurnished, and the floor was replaced with artificial stone and marble.
Extremist insurgents seized the mosque, took hostages, and hundreds were killed in the ensuing siege.
A new wing and an outdoor prayer area were added to the mosque.
A crane collapsed onto the mosque, killing at least 111 people and injuring 394.
The mosque was closed at night, and the Umrah pilgrimage was suspended to limit attendance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque features seven minarets (with six more under construction), domes decorated with calligraphy, and marble columns. The oldest surviving parts of the building date back to the 1570 renovation by Mimar Sinan. The mosque has undergone extensive expansions, including the addition of prayer halls, gates, and modern amenities such as air conditioning and escalators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Masjid al-Haram is the holiest site in Islam, enclosing the Kaaba, which is considered the House of Allah. It is the destination for the Hajj pilgrimage, one of the Five Pillars of Islam, and the Umrah pilgrimage. The mosque is central to Islamic worship and holds immense religious and historical significance for Muslims worldwide.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque is the largest in the world and has undergone significant expansions to accommodate millions of pilgrims. It includes important sites such as the Black Stone, the Zamzam Well, Maqam Ibrahim, and the hills of Safa and Marwa. The mosque's expansion projects have raised concerns about the loss of early Islamic heritage due to the demolition of ancient buildings.

world knowledge.Name: Chaotianmen Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 1,741 m (5,712 ft), Width: 36.5 m (120 ft), Height: 142 m (466 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chaotianmen Bridge is a road-rail bridge over the Yangtze River in Chongqing, China. It opened on 29 April 2009 and is the world's longest through arch bridge.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to the public on 30 April 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Continuous steel truss arch bridge with tie girders, through arch design, carries six lanes of traffic with pedestrian walkways on the upper deck, and has two traffic lanes on each side with the Chongqing Metro Loop Line running down the middle on the lower deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant engineering feat and a key transportation link in Chongqing, symbolizing the city's modernization and infrastructure development.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has a main span of 552 m (1,811 ft) and a construction cost of 3.2 billion Yuan. It is a critical part of Chongqing's urban infrastructure, facilitating both vehicular and metro transit across the Yangtze River.

world knowledge.Name: Variety Playhouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as the Euclid Theatre in 1940, it served as a cinema before closing in 1962. After periods of disuse and repurposing, it was renovated and reopened as the Ellis Cinema in 1984. It transitioned to a live performance venue in 1989 under the name Variety Playhouse and has since become a prominent music venue.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened as a cinema with a staggered seating plan and neon marquee, showcasing films like 'My Favorite Wife.'

Major_Events.Event: Renovation and reopening as Ellis Cinema
Major_Events.Description: After extensive renovations, the theater reopened as the Ellis Cinema, dedicated to art films and repertory cinema.
The venue was repurposed for live performances, featuring classic motion picture stars and music acts.
The venue underwent significant renovations, including improvements to seating, bar areas, and acoustics, reopening with a performance by Tycho.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: World War II-era brick building with art deco or art moderne elements. Features a sloping floor in the main seating area, a balcony, and a lowered front pit area for dancing. The interior includes tiered mezzanines for tables and chairs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Variety Playhouse is a historic venue that has adapted to changing cultural needs, transitioning from a cinema to a beloved music venue. It hosts a wide variety of musical acts and has been recognized with multiple 'Best of Atlanta' awards.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Music venue hosting live performances across various genres.
world knowledge.Details: The venue is known for its excellent acoustics and has been used for recording live albums by various artists. It also features bars serving domestic and imported beers, liquor, wine, and theater snacks. The marquee is occasionally featured in Turner Classic Movies segments.

world knowledge.Name: Lamport Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lamport Hall in Lamport, Northamptonshire is a fine example of a Grade I listed building. It was developed from a Tudor manor but is now notable for its classical frontage. The Hall contains an outstanding collection of books, paintings, and furniture. The building includes The High Room with a magnificent ceiling by William Smith. It also has a library with 16th-century volumes and an early 19th-century cabinet room with Neapolitan cabinets which depict mythological paintings on glass. It is open to the public. Lamport Hall was the home of the Isham family from 1560 to 1976.

Major_Events.Description: Further major rebuilding of the south east front was completed.
The ground floor was opened to the public.
The trust caused controversy by advertising for musicians to perform for no fee at a dining event in the garden.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Hall is notable for its classical frontage and includes The High Room with a magnificent ceiling by William Smith. It also has a library with 16th-century volumes and an early 19th-century cabinet room with Neapolitan cabinets which depict mythological paintings on glass.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lamport Hall is culturally significant as a Grade I listed building with a rich history and an outstanding collection of books, paintings, and furniture. It was the home of the Isham family for over four centuries and is notable for its classical architecture and historical artifacts.
world knowledge.Details: Lamport Hall was used to depict Clarence House in the Netflix series The Crown. The exterior was also used to double for the stables at Windsor Castle. The Hall is open to the public and is cared for by the Lamport Hall Preservation Trust.

world knowledge.Name: St Michael Chapel
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Saint Michael Chapel was probably erected in the first half of the 14th century as a cemetery chapel inside the town walls. It served as a Slovak church, while the Cathedral of Saint Elisabeth was a German and Hungarian church. The chapel underwent several reconstructions, notably in 1902–1904 and 1998–2006, after which it was officially recognized as a church.

Major_Events.Description: The northern aisle was pulled down, and 17 old gravestones were bricked into the exterior walls to save them from destruction.
The chapel was reconstructed and consecrated on 22 January 2006 by Košice's archbishop, Alojz Tkáč, officially becoming a church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic style with a facade depicting Saint Michael the Archangel trampling the Devil, flanked by archangels Raphael and Gabriel. The interior features a stone tabernacle, the ornamental sculpture Ecce Homo, and remnants of wall paintings from the Middle Ages. The first municipal coat of arms in Europe (dated back to 1369) is above the door leading to the vestry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The chapel is historically significant as a Slovak church in contrast to the German and Hungarian Cathedral of Saint Elisabeth. It also houses the first municipal coat of arms in Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The lower part of the chapel was initially an ossarium, while the upper part served for offices for the deceased. The patron of the dead, Saint Michael the Archangel, is prominently featured on the facade.

world knowledge.Name: Cabo San Antonio Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Cabo San Antonio, Sandino, Pinar del Río Province, Cuba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cabo San Antonio Lighthouse marks the westernmost point of Cuba and serves as a boundary between the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of Mexico, as defined by the International Hydrographic Organization.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 23-meter tall cylindrical masonry tower with a balcony and lantern, painted white with a grey metallic lantern.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a key navigational landmark and marks the division between the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of Mexico.

world knowledge.Name: Puebla Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 97.67 m (320 ft) long, 51 m (170 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basilica Cathedral of Puebla, also known as the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, is the episcopal see of the Archdiocese of Puebla de los Ángeles. It is one of the most important buildings in the historic center of Puebla, declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. It was the first sumptuous temple built in the Americas, consecrated in 1649, ahead of the Metropolitan of Mexico, which was dedicated in 1653. The cathedral was founded by Philip II of Spain and built between the 16th and 17th centuries, replacing a previous structure. It was consecrated by Bishop Juan de Palafox y Mendoza on April 18, 1649, without being completely finished.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by Bishop Juan de Palafox y Mendoza on April 18, 1649.
The south tower of the cathedral was completed in 1737.
The Historic Centre of Puebla, including the cathedral, was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is primarily in the Herrerian style, with Neoclassical and Baroque elements. It features a rectangular shape with five naves, a Renaissance-style façade, and two towers that are 70 meters high. The interior includes 14 Doric columns, 74 columns in total, and 39 cupolas. The cathedral's dome is made of pumice stone to lighten its weight, and the building is illuminated by 124 windows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Puebla Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the first sumptuous temple built in the Americas. It represents the architectural and religious influence of Spain in the New World and is a key part of Puebla's historic center, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The cathedral also houses important works of art, including paintings, sculptures, and religious artifacts.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is part of the Historic Centre of Puebla, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has been a center of religious and cultural activity since its consecration in 1649. The cathedral's construction involved several architects, including Francisco Becerra and Juan Gómez de Trasmonte, and it was built over a period of 74 years. The cathedral's interior is richly decorated with works of art, including frescoes by Cristóbal de Villalpando and paintings by Miguel Cabrera. The cathedral also has a significant historical archive with documents dating back to the founding of the city.

world knowledge.Name: Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center
world knowledge.Address: 1010 North W.C. MacInnes Place Tampa, Florida, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Opened in July 1987 as the Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center, renamed in 2009 after David A. Straz, Jr., a Tampa banker and philanthropist. The center is owned by the City of Tampa and operated by a not-for-profit corporation.

Major_Events.Description: Presents premieres of musicals and plays that might move to Broadway.
Extensive multi-million dollar renovation included new wood floors on the stages, new cooler LED lighting, and improved dressing rooms for performers.
Following the murder of George Floyd, the center made a commitment to anti-racism, pledging to support the lives, art, stories, and culture of Black, Indigenous, and Persons of Color.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex consists of five distinct theaters, a rehearsal hall, retail shops, on-site restaurants, and banquet facilities. The Carol Morsani Hall features a 60-foot high proscenium, a playing depth of 55 feet, and a total stage width of 120 feet. The Ferguson Hall has a 40-foot wide by 30-foot high proscenium, a total playing depth of 50 feet, and a total stage width of 80 feet. The Jaeb Theater's stage is 40 feet wide by 20 feet deep. The TECO Energy Foundation Theater is a flexible space with no permanent stage. The Shimberg Playhouse is a smaller venue with 130 seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Straz Center is the second largest performing arts complex in the Southeastern United States and has a significant economic impact, generating $100 million annually and 100,000 hotel room nights a year. It hosts a leading Broadway series, grand opera, concerts, and other performances, attracting an average of 600,000 guests per year. The center also has extensive education programs through the Patel Conservatory, serving thousands of students annually.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venue hosting Broadway shows, opera, concerts, and other performances, as well as providing education programs.
world knowledge.Details: The center is home to resident companies and hosts annual events such as the Broadway Ball, Best of Tampa Bay, Eggstravaganza, and the International Thespian Society’s Florida State Thespian Festival. The Patel Conservatory features 20 studios, including dance studios, a sound/lighting laboratory, and a black box theater. The center also promotes anti-racism literature and initiatives.

world knowledge.Name: Alte Pinakothek
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alte Pinakothek is one of the oldest galleries in the world, housing a significant collection of Old Master paintings from the 14th to the 18th century. It was commissioned by King Ludwig I of Bavaria and designed by Leo von Klenze. The museum was severely damaged during World War II but was reconstructed and reopened in 1957. It is part of the Bavarian State Painting Collections.

Major_Events.Description: The Alte Pinakothek was inaugurated as one of the largest and most advanced museums of its time.
The museum was severely damaged by bombing during World War II.
The museum was reconstructed and reopened to the public.
Hans-Joachim Bohlmann splashed acid on three paintings by Albrecht Dürer, causing significant damage.
Wings of the museum were sequentially closed for renovation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Alte Pinakothek features a Neo-Renaissance exterior and was structurally advanced for its time, with skylights for natural lighting. The building became a model for museum architecture in Europe.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Alte Pinakothek is culturally significant for its extensive collection of Old Master paintings, which includes works by Albrecht Dürer, Peter Paul Rubens, and Rembrandt. It represents the artistic heritage of Bavaria and Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is part of the Bavarian State Painting Collections and houses over 800 paintings, with additional works displayed in associated galleries throughout Bavaria. It underwent significant renovations from 2014 to 2017.

world knowledge.Name: Frank Kitts Park
world knowledge.Address: Between Jervois Quay and the Lambton Harbour waterfront, Wellington, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Frank Kitts Park is a public park in Wellington, New Zealand, named after Sir Frank Kitts, a former mayor of Wellington. The park was established in 1976 on reclaimed land and an area formerly used for wharf sheds. It was originally known as Marine Park and was renamed in 1979 in memory of Sir Frank Kitts. The park has undergone several redevelopments, including a major one in 1990 by Lambton Harbour Management.

Major_Events.Description: The park was redeveloped by Lambton Harbour Management, a Council-owned organisation, and reopened in 1990. The redevelopment included the construction of a public carpark, a lawn area, a children's play area, and an amphitheatre.
A kinetic sculpture by Len Lye, Water Whirler, was installed near the children's play area. It oscillates and sprays water from many jets.
The playground was demolished and a $6 million redevelopment began, but construction stopped due to the builders going into liquidation. The playground was redesigned and reopened in February 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a covered public carpark with a lawn roof, a children's play area with a lighthouse-shaped slide, a small amphitheatre, a broad promenade, and several sculptures including the Albatross fountain, Water Whirler, and Fruits of the Garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Frank Kitts Park is culturally significant as a public space in Wellington, hosting numerous events and festivals. It also features several memorials and sculptures that commemorate historical events and figures, such as the mast from the ship Wahine and plaques commemorating various organisations and people.
world knowledge.Details: The park has been the subject of various redevelopment proposals, including plans for a traditional walled Chinese garden and a fale malae, a Pacific-focused venue. These proposals have been met with public controversy and have not yet been realised as of October 2024.

world knowledge.Name: George Square
world knowledge.Historical_Background: George Square is the principal civic square in Glasgow, named after King George III. It was initially laid out in 1781 but not developed for another twenty years. The square is surrounded by architecturally important buildings, including the Glasgow City Chambers. It features an important collection of statues and monuments dedicated to notable figures such as Robert Burns, James Watt, and Sir Walter Scott.

Major_Events.Description: A rally by skilled engineers campaigning for a 40-hour working week descended into violence between protesters and police, with military assistance being called in.
The square was closed for a two-month restoration project, including the replacement of the red asphalt concourse and cleaning of statues.
Scenes for the zombie movie World War Z were filmed in the square, utilizing its resemblance to Philadelphia's financial district.
Glasgow City Council voted to spend £15m on a makeover of the square in preparation for the 2014 Commonwealth Games, though plans were later canceled.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The square is surrounded by Georgian terraces and architecturally significant buildings, including the Glasgow City Chambers, designed by William Young. The square features a central 80-foot-high Doric column commemorating Sir Walter Scott, along with numerous statues and monuments.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: George Square is culturally and historically significant as the principal civic square of Glasgow, hosting numerous statues of notable figures and serving as a venue for public events, political gatherings, and annual Remembrance Day parades.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Civic square and public gathering space
world knowledge.Details: George Square has been the scene of political events, protests, and cultural activities. It is also a popular location for musical events, light shows, and ceremonies. The square has undergone various changes and restorations over the years, including a controversial plan to remove statues and monuments in 2012, which was ultimately canceled.

world knowledge.Name: Mandela House
world knowledge.Address: 8115 Vilakazi Street, Orlando West, Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nelson Mandela National Museum, commonly referred to as Mandela House, is the house on Vilakazi Street, Orlando West, Soweto, South Africa, where Nelson Mandela lived from 1946 to 1962. Mandela donated the house to the Soweto Heritage Trust on 1 September 1997, to be run as a museum. It was declared a National Heritage Site in 1999. The house has bullet holes and scorch marks from attacks, and hosts original furnishings and memorabilia.

Major_Events.Description: Mandela donated the house to the Soweto Heritage Trust to be run as a museum.
The house was declared a National Heritage Site.
After restoration and construction of a visitor center, the house was reopened to the public on 19 March 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Single-story red-brick matchbox house built in 1945, with bullet holes and scorch marks from attacks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mandela House is culturally significant as the former residence of Nelson Mandela, a key figure in the anti-apartheid movement and the first black president of South Africa. It symbolizes the struggle for freedom and democracy in South Africa.
world knowledge.Details: The house includes a visitors' center and a small museum. It was restored in 2008-2009 to address physical deterioration and improve visitor facilities. Mandela returned to the house after his release from prison in 1990 but moved out after 11 days. The property is now a popular tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Harewood House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Harewood House is a country house in Harewood, West Yorkshire, England. Designed by architects John Carr and Robert Adam, it was built between 1759 and 1771 for Edwin Lascelles, 1st Baron Harewood, a wealthy West Indian plantation and slave owner. The landscape was designed by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown. The estate was created by merging two adjacent estates, Harewood Castle estate and Gawthorpe estate. The house has been home to the Lascelles family since its construction and is now managed by the Harewood House Trust.

Major_Events.Description: The house was largely complete by 1765, with interiors designed by Robert Adam. The construction period was from 1759 to 1771.
The house acted as a resident convalescent hospital during the Second World War.
Princess Mary, the only daughter of George V, suffered a fatal heart attack while walking the grounds of Harewood.
Rock musician Elton John performed two concerts in the grounds.
The house was used as a filming location for the 2019 Downton Abbey film.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Palladian style, designed by John Carr and Robert Adam. The house features internal courtyards, formal parterres, and terraces added by Sir Charles Barry in the 1840s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Harewood House is a Grade I listed building and a member of the Treasure Houses of England. It is culturally significant due to its historical architecture, its connection to the Lascelles family, and its role in British history, including its links to the slave trade.
world knowledge.Details: Harewood House houses a collection of paintings by masters of the Italian Renaissance, family portraits, and modern art. The estate includes gardens, a Himalayan garden, an educational bird garden, and All Saints' Church. The Leeds Country Way and The White Rose Way pass through the estate. The house has been used as a filming location for various films and TV shows, including King Ralph, Emmerdale, and Victoria.

world knowledge.Name: Tabley House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tabley House is an English country house built to replace the nearby Tabley Old Hall. It was designed by John Carr for Sir Peter Byrne Leicester. The house and estate were owned by the Leicester family for almost 700 years until 1975. After being declined by the National Trust, it was acquired by the Victoria University of Manchester and later leased to a healthcare company. The estate was sold to the Crown Estate in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: Built to replace Tabley Old Hall, designed by John Carr for Sir Peter Byrne Leicester.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to Victoria University of Manchester
Major_Events.Description: After the death of Lt. Col. John Leicester Warren, the estate was passed to the university as per his will.
The 3,600-acre estate was sold to the Crown Estate for over £35 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Palladian style, symmetrical design, brick construction with stone dressings, large sandstone portico on the south front, pavilion wings connected by curved corridors. Interior features high-quality plasterwork by Thomas Oliver, woodcarving by Mathew Bertram and Daniel Shillito, and furniture by Gillow of Lancaster.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tabley House is a Grade I listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance. It is the only 18th-century Palladian country house in Cheshire. The house contains a significant collection of paintings and furniture collected by the Leicester family, including works by J.M.W. Turner, Richard Wilson, and others.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country house, now serves as a nursing home on the ground and top floors, with the first floor open to the public for tours, weddings, and events.
world knowledge.Details: The house is managed by the Tabley House Collection Trust, supported by The Friends of Tabley and volunteers. The first floor rooms, including the gallery, drawing room, and dining room, are open to the public during summer months. The estate includes listed buildings such as St Peter's Church, the ruins of Tabley Old Hall, and various lodges and outbuildings.

world knowledge.Name: Gir National Park
world knowledge.Address: Junagadh, Gir Somnath and Amreli Districts, Gujarat, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, also known as Sasan Gir, was established in 1965 in the erstwhile Nawab of Junagarh's private hunting area. It is the only area in Asia where Asiatic lions occur and is considered one of the most important protected areas in Asia due to its biodiversity. The park was established to protect the dwindling population of Asiatic lions, which had reduced to about a dozen by the end of the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The 14th Asiatic Lion Census conducted in May 2015 recorded a population of 523 lions, a 27% increase from the previous census in 2010.
The sanctuary was established to protect the Asiatic lion population, which had drastically declined due to hunting and habitat loss.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gir National Park is culturally and historically significant as it is the only place in Asia where Asiatic lions are found. It is a symbol of successful wildlife conservation efforts and is considered the jewel of Gujarat's ecological resources.
world knowledge.Details: Gir National Park is part of the Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests ecoregion. It is home to a diverse range of flora and fauna, including 38 species of mammals, 300 species of birds, 37 species of reptiles, and over 2,000 species of insects. The park is closed from 16 June to 15 October every year during the monsoon season. The Gir ecosystem is protected through the efforts of the government forest department, wildlife activists, and NGOs.

world knowledge.Name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,352 ft (412 m) length, 31 ft (9.4 m) width, 331 ft (101 m) height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Clifton Suspension Bridge spans the Avon Gorge and the River Avon, linking Clifton in Bristol to Leigh Woods in North Somerset. Designed by William Henry Barlow and John Hawkshaw based on an earlier design by Isambard Kingdom Brunel, it opened in 1864. The bridge is a Grade I listed building and is maintained by the Clifton Suspension Bridge Trust.

Major_Events.Description: Members of the University of Oxford Dangerous Sports Club made the first modern bungee jumps from the bridge.
The last Concorde flight flew over the bridge before landing at Filton Aerodrome.
The London 2012 Olympic Torch relay crossed over the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with wrought iron chains, roller-mounted saddles at the top of each tower, and a deck suspended by vertical wrought-iron rods. The bridge has three independent wrought iron chains per side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a distinctive landmark and symbol of Bristol, used in promotional materials and as a backdrop for films and television. It has hosted significant cultural events and is a Grade I listed building.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Road bridge for cars, pedestrians, and cyclists
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is managed by a charitable trust and funded by tolls. It has been the site of numerous historical events and is known for its architectural and engineering significance. The bridge has also been a site for suicide attempts, leading to the installation of suicide barriers in 1998.

world knowledge.Name: Tokushima Prefectural Museum
world knowledge.Address: Bunka-no-mori Park, Hachiman-chō, Tokushima, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tokushima Prefectural Museum is dedicated to the nature, archaeology, history, folklore, and art of Tokushima Prefecture. It first opened in 1959 and reopened in new premises in 1990.

Major_Events.Description: The museum first opened to the public.
The museum reopened in a new location.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and showcases the natural and cultural heritage of Tokushima Prefecture, making it an important institution for education and cultural preservation in the region.
world knowledge.Details: This article related to a museum in Japan is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Woodbine Mall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Woodbine Mall & Fantasy Fair is a shopping mall opened in 1985 by developer Cadillac Fairview. It was designed by Crang and Boake Incorporated and served as inspiration for the UK's MetroCentre. The mall has faced financial challenges, including unpaid taxes and being placed in receivership in 2023. It is home to Fantasy Fair, an indoor amusement park featuring nine full-sized rides, including a historic Charles I. D. Looff carousel.

Major_Events.Description: The mall was opened by developer Cadillac Fairview.
Rumours of closure due to proposed entertainment centre development at Woodbine Racetrack and store closures led to renovation plans by then-owners Darton Property.
Woodbine Mall Holdings Inc. was placed in receivership by Romspen Investment Corporation, with Ernst & Young appointed as receiver.
The 50-foot ferris wheel, claimed to be the only one in North America, was closed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Crang and Boake Incorporated, the mall spans two floors with a total retail floor area of 750,000 sq ft. It features an indoor amusement park, Fantasy Fair, with nine full-sized rides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Woodbine Mall is notable for housing Fantasy Fair, the largest indoor amusement park in Ontario, and a historic Charles I. D. Looff carousel. It has also been featured in various films and TV shows, contributing to its cultural footprint.
world knowledge.Details: The mall has over 130 stores and features Fantasy Fair, which includes a 50-foot ferris wheel (now closed) and a historic carousel. It has appeared in films like Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol and TV shows such as Animorphs, Shazam!, What We Do In The Shadows, and 8-Bit Christmas.

world knowledge.Name: Jampui Hills
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jampui Hills was occupied by the Mizo people in the 16th century. It was later vacated in the mid-1800s due to a disease called 'Zawnghri' and reoccupied in the early 20th century. The area has a rich history of Mizo chieftains and has been a center for orange cultivation since the 1960s.

Major_Events.Description: Started to promote tourism and celebrate the orange harvest. It attracted many tourists but was discontinued due to declining orange production.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jampui Hills is culturally significant for its Mizo heritage, traditional practices like jhum cultivation, and its role in orange and betel nut cultivation. It is also a hub for eco-tourism and cultural tourism.
world knowledge.Details: Jampui Hills is known for its scenic beauty, including sunrise and sunset views, floating clouds, and panoramic vistas. It has eco-tourism potential, with modern tourist lodges like Eden Tourist Lodge. The area is sparsely populated, offering a peaceful and eco-friendly environment for tourists. Local languages include Mizo, Kokborok, English, and Bengali.

world knowledge.Name: National Library of Argentina
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mariano Moreno National Library is the largest library in Argentina, originally named the Public Library of Buenos Aires and founded in September 1810 by decree of the first Government Junta of the May Revolution. It became the country's only national library in 1884. The library has had several locations and directors, including notable figures like Paul Groussac and Jorge Luis Borges. The current building was inaugurated on April 10, 1992.

Major_Events.Event: Founding of the Public Library of Buenos Aires
Major_Events.Description: Founded by decree of the first Government Junta of the May Revolution.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to National Library of Argentina
Major_Events.Description: Redefined its mission and formally changed its name.
The brutalist structure designed by Clorindo Testa, Francisco Bullrich, and Alicia Cazzaniga was inaugurated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Brutalist structure designed by Clorindo Testa, Francisco Bullrich, and Alicia Cazzaniga.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The library is a key institution in Argentina's intellectual and cultural history, named after Mariano Moreno, a significant figure in the May Revolution. It has housed many important collections and has been directed by notable intellectuals.
world knowledge.Details: The library's initial collection was gathered from the expropriated personal collection of Bishop Orellana and patriotic donations. It has undergone several relocations and has been enriched with important donations over the years.

world knowledge.Name: National Mosque of Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Mosque of Malaysia was built as a symbol of the country's independence, which was achieved peacefully on 31 August 1957. The idea for the mosque was proposed in 1957, and it was completed in 1965. It was designed to reflect the aspirations of the newly independent nation and is a modern architectural marvel in reinforced concrete.

Major_Events.Description: Malaya gained its independence from the British government on 31 August 1957.
The mosque was declared open by the third Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Tuanku Syed Putra of Perlis, on 27 August 1965.
The mosque underwent major renovations, including the recladding of the once-pink concrete roof with green and blue tiles.
The mosque celebrated its 50th anniversary on 27 August 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque features a 73-metre-high minaret and a 16-pointed star concrete main roof. The main roof is reminiscent of an open umbrella, while the minaret's cap resembles a folded umbrella. The folded plates of the concrete main roof are a creative solution to achieving larger spans in the main gathering hall. The mosque also includes reflecting pools and fountains throughout the compound.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Mosque of Malaysia is a symbol of the country's peaceful independence and its aspirations as a newly independent nation. It represents a modern approach to Islamic architecture and is a significant religious and cultural landmark in Malaysia.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque was built on the former site of the Venning Road Brethren Gospel Hall, which was acquired by the government in 1961. The original structure was designed by a team including UK architect Howard Ashley and Malaysians Ikmal Hisham Albakri and Baharuddin Kassim. The mosque is accessible within walking distance of Kuala Lumpur railway station and Pasar Seni station. It is also served by the free Go KL City Bus (Red Line).

world knowledge.Name: Victoria Leeds
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Victoria Leeds is a shopping district and leisure area in central Leeds, comprising the 1990 Victoria Quarter, an arcaded complex of restored 19th-century and contemporary shopping arcades, and the 2016 Victoria Gate development. It played a significant role in the regeneration of Leeds' city centre, featuring the largest work of stained glass in Europe. The district includes a casino and major stores such as Harvey Nichols and John Lewis and Partners.

Major_Events.Description: The Victoria Quarter opened as a network of interconnected, covered shopping spaces, forming an upmarket shopping district.
The Victoria Gate complex opened, merging with the Victoria Quarter to form the largest premium retail and leisure venue in Northern England.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Grade II* listed Victoria Quarter features restored Victorian and Edwardian arcades with a contemporary arcade created through the pedestrianisation and glazing over of Queen Victoria Street. The area includes the largest work of public art in Britain at the time, a 749-square-metre stained-glass roof designed by Brian Clarke.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Victoria Leeds is culturally significant for its role in urban regeneration and its architectural heritage, including the largest secular stained glass work in the world. It is often referred to as 'the Knightsbridge of the North'.
world knowledge.Details: Victoria Leeds includes 80 stores and services, 3 anchor tenants, and 800 parking spaces. The development was awarded the Leeds Award for Architecture and the Civic Trust Award.

world knowledge.Name: Birjand University of Medical Sciences
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Birjand University of Medical Sciences and Health Services (BUMS) is located in the Islamic Republic of Iran. This university has now more than 3300 students.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a public university, it plays a significant role in the education and training of medical professionals in the region.
world knowledge.Details: This Iran university, college or other higher education institution article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Nakhchivan International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nakhchivan International Airport is a civilian airport and Azeri military airbase located in Nakhchivan, the capital of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, a landlocked exclave of Azerbaijan. It was built in the 1970s.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has two runways: 14R/32L with a concrete surface measuring 3,300 by 45 metres and 14L/32R with an asphalt surface measuring 3,300 by 42 metres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It serves as a key transportation hub for the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, facilitating both civilian and military operations.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is at an elevation of 2,863 feet (873 m) above mean sea level. It served 526,155 passengers in the reported period with a 4.9% change from the previous year. Aircraft movements were 4,224 with a 5.6% change from the previous year.

world knowledge.Name: Centennial Bridge, Panama
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,052 m (3,451 ft) total span, 420 m (1,380 ft) main span
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Centennial Bridge was built to supplement the overcrowded Bridge of the Americas and to replace it as the carrier of the Pan-American Highway. It became the second permanent crossing of the Panama Canal upon its opening in 2004. The bridge was named for Panama's centennial, which occurred on 3 November 2003.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was inaugurated on 15 August 2004, although it was opened for traffic on 2 September 2005, when the new highways leading to it were finished.
Part of the access to the Centennial Bridge collapsed in December 2010, following heavy rain and flooding.
Full traffic was restored in November 2011 after the access collapse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed design with a total span of 1,052 m (3,451 ft). The main span is 420 m (1,380 ft) and clears the canal by 80 m (260 ft). The bridge is supported by two towers, each 184 m (604 ft) high. The deck carries six lanes of traffic across the canal. Designed to withstand earthquakes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Centennial Bridge is a major infrastructure project that alleviated congestion on the Pan-American Highway and represents Panama's modernization and centennial celebration.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries six lanes of the Pan-American Highway across the Panama Canal.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by a joint venture between T.Y. Lin International and the Louis Berger Group Inc, and constructed by German-based Bilfinger Berger Ingenieurbau GmbH. The architects were Elle Sokolow and Miguel Rosales. Structural engineering contracts were awarded to Leonhardt, Andrä and Partner. The West Tower was built about 50 m inland to allow space for the future widening of the Panama Canal.

world knowledge.Name: Awaji Yumebutai
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Awaji Yumebutai is a complex built near the epicenter of the 1995 Great Hanshin Awaji earthquake. It was designed by Tadao Ando, who had begun planning for the project (as a park) prior to the earthquake.

Major_Events.Description: The earthquake occurred near the site where Awaji Yumebutai was later built.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex includes the Hyakudanen ("hundred stepped gardens"), a group of 100 flower beds on an incline, arranged in grids spread over several levels. There are 1,575 steps and 235 flights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The name 'Yumebutai' ("Dream Stage") refers to the aim of restoring the ecology of the island, whose soil had been partly removed for land reclamation in Osaka. It symbolizes a place for dreaming and ecological restoration.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The complex serves as a conference center, hotel, and memorial.
world knowledge.Details: The hotel in the complex is operated as the Westin Awaji Island Resort. The site is metaphorically referred to as 'a place in which to dream' and focuses on ecological restoration.

world knowledge.Name: Los Cabos International Airport
world knowledge.Address: San José del Cabo, Baja California Sur, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Los Cabos International Airport was inaugurated in 1977 with an initial provisional terminal. It underwent substantial expansion and renovation in 1997, resulting in the construction of Terminal 1. Terminal 2 was added to facilitate increased international flights, and Terminal 3 was constructed adjacent to Terminal 2. The airport faced challenges due to a surge in holiday resorts and rapid regional population growth, leading to insufficient capacity during peak hours.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was inaugurated with an initial provisional terminal.
Substantial expansion and renovation resulted in the construction of Terminal 1.
The control tower received an upgrade with advanced technology during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Forum.
Hurricane Odile caused substantial damage, leading to an 18-day suspension of operations.
Terminal 3 was fully integrated with Terminal 2, adopting the name Terminal 2.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a single runway, designated as 16/34, measuring 3,000 metres with an asphalt surface. Terminal 1 covers an area of 16,580 square metres and manages arrival and departure facilities for domestic flights. Terminal 2 is a two-story structure with customs and immigration facilities, a baggage claim area, and a departure area with a 400-meter-long concourse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Los Cabos International Airport serves as the main gateway to the popular tourist destination of the Los Cabos region, attracting millions of tourists annually, predominantly from the United States and Canada. It plays a crucial role in connecting the Baja California Peninsula to Mainland Mexico and supports various activities in general and executive aviation.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is the sixth-busiest in Mexico and the 24th-busiest in Latin America by passenger numbers. It handles millions of passengers annually, with 61% traveling to or from international destinations. The airport operates two terminals and supports both domestic and international flights, including flights to 30 U.S. cities and 11 Canadian cities.

world knowledge.Name: Stowe Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stowe Gardens, formerly Stowe Landscape Gardens, are extensive, Grade I listed gardens and parkland in Buckinghamshire, England. Largely created in the 18th century, the gardens at Stowe are arguably the most significant example of the English landscape garden. Designed by Charles Bridgeman, William Kent, and Capability Brown, the gardens changed from a baroque park to a natural landscape garden, commissioned by the estate's owners, in particular by Richard Temple, 1st Viscount Cobham, his nephew Richard Grenville-Temple, 2nd Earl Temple, and his nephew George Nugent-Temple-Grenville, 1st Marquess of Buckingham.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as Grade I listed gardens
Major_Events.Description: Stowe Gardens were designated as Grade I listed gardens on 30 August 1987.
The gardens passed into the ownership of the National Trust in 1989.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gardens are notable for the scale, design, size and the number of monuments set across the landscape. Many of the monuments in the property have their own additional Grade I listing along with the park. These include: the Corinthian Arch, the Temple of Venus, the Palladian Bridge, the Gothic Temple, the Temple of Ancient Virtue, the Temple of British Worthies, the Temple of Concord and Victory, the Queen's Temple, Doric Arch, the Oxford Bridge, amongst others.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stowe Gardens are culturally and historically important as they are one of the most significant examples of the English landscape garden. They have been a tourist attraction for over 300 years and represent the evolution of garden design in 18th-century England.
world knowledge.Details: The gardens passed into the ownership of the National Trust in 1989, whilst Stowe House, the home of Stowe School, is under the care of the Stowe House Preservation Trust. The parkland surrounding the gardens is open 365 days a year.

world knowledge.Name: Aggtelek National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Aggtelek National Park is located in the Aggtelek Karst region of Northern Hungary. It was established in 1985 and became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1995, along with the Slovak Karst caves. The park is renowned for its limestone landscape and extensive cave systems, including the Baradla cave, the largest stalactite cave in Europe. The first written documentation of the caves dates back to 1549, and they have been used as a tourist attraction since 1920.

Major_Events.Description: Aggtelek National Park was founded to protect the unique limestone landscape and cave systems in the region.
The park was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site, recognizing its geological and ecological significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a limestone landscape with 280 caves of various sizes, including the Baradla cave, which is 26 km long. The Peace Cave includes a sanatorium for treating asthma.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aggtelek National Park is culturally and historically significant due to its unique geological formations and extensive cave systems. It is also important for its biodiversity and as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to various species including the fire salamander, hucul pony, common buzzard, eastern imperial eagle, European copper skink, white-throated dipper, red deer, Eurasian lynx, gray wolf, wild boar, crested tit, goldcrest, Eurasian bullfinch, hazel grouse, common kingfisher, red-backed shrike, old World swallowtail, scarce swallowtail, and the saga pedo.

world knowledge.Name: Fremont Bridge (Portland, Oregon)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2,154 feet (657 m) total length, 381 feet (116 m) height, 1,255 feet (383 m) longest span
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fremont Bridge is a steel tied-arch bridge over the Willamette River in Portland, Oregon. It was designed by Parsons, Brinckerhoff, Quade and Douglas and built by Murphy Pacific Corporation. It opened on November 15, 1973, and was named after John C. Fremont, an early explorer of the Oregon Country.

Major_Events.Description: A six-foot-long crack was found on the west span of the girder, requiring a $5.5 million redesign and repair.
The 6,000 short tons steel arch span was lifted 170 ft using 32 hydraulic jacks, setting a Guinness World Record for the heaviest lift ever completed.
An American flag and an Oregon flag were added atop the structure as part of the U.S. bicentennial celebration.
The bridge became the 26th Peregrine falcon nest site in Oregon after the raptor was placed on the U.S. Threatened and Endangered Species list in 1970.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel tied-arch bridge with two decks carrying vehicular traffic. The upper deck is signed westbound on US 30 and southbound on I-405, while the lower deck is signed eastbound on US 30 and northbound on I-405. The steel tie-girder is 18 feet tall and 50 inches wide. The center span is 902 feet long.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant due to its design influenced by the Portland Art Commission, its world record lift, and its role as a Peregrine falcon nest site. It is also named after John C. Fremont, a notable historical figure in Oregon.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries Interstate 405 and US 30 traffic between downtown and North Portland.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was modeled after the original 1964 Port Mann Bridge in Vancouver, British Columbia. It was fabricated in California and assembled at Swan Island Industrial Park before being floated to the construction site. The final cost was $82 million, mostly financed by the Federal Highway Administration. The bridge has 3.27 lane-miles on the arch bridge and 14.12 lane-miles on the ramps and approaches.

world knowledge.Name: Franklin County Courthouse and Jail
world knowledge.Address: 200 N. Kaufman St., Mount Vernon, Texas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Franklin County Courthouse and Jail in Mount Vernon, Texas was built in 1912. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2006. The listing includes two contributing buildings: the courthouse and the jail. The design of a prior Franklin County courthouse, built in 1875, was copied in the design of the Old Morris County Courthouse.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Franklin County Courthouse and Jail was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The Franklin County Courthouse and Jail was designated as a Texas State Antiquities Landmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse was designed by L.L. Thurman in Classical Revival style. It is a three-story sandstone building with full-height columned and pedimented porticoes on two sides and an octagonal, domed clock tower. The jail is a square two-story small building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Franklin County Courthouse and Jail is significant for its Classical Revival architecture and its role as a historic government building. It is also notable for being designed by L.L. Thurman, who also designed other courthouses listed on the National Register.
world knowledge.Details: The architect L.L. Thurman also designed the Jeff Davis County Courthouse and the Kinney County Courthouse, which are also listed on the National Register. The prior Franklin County courthouse, built in 1875, influenced the design of the Old Morris County Courthouse.

world knowledge.Name: Snowshoe Mountain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Snowshoe Mountain was discovered by Thomas "Doc" Brigham, who envisioned it as a ski resort. The area had been logged from 1905 to 1960 and was barren before the resort was established. It opened for skiing on December 13, 1974. Over the years, it expanded, purchased the Silver Creek ski area in 1992, and underwent various ownership changes, including acquisition by Tokyo Tower Development Company in 1990, Intrawest in 1995, and Alterra Mountain Company in 2017.

Major_Events.Description: The ski resort officially opened for skiing on December 13, 1974.
Snowshoe Mountain purchased the nearby Silver Creek ski area.
The resort was sold to Intrawest, a Canadian ski-resort operator.
Intrawest was acquired by Alterra Mountain Company.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features a village-style commercial and condominium real estate development, including Rimfire Lodge, Highland House, Allegheny Springs, The Seneca, and Expedition Station. The ski trails and lifts are named after local logging history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Snowshoe Mountain is a significant ski resort in the eastern United States, known for its winter activities and extensive mountain biking trails. It hosts events like the Grand National Cross Country Racing and is a regular stop on the UCI Mountain Bike World Cup. The resort also preserves local logging history through trail and lift names.
world knowledge.Details: Snowshoe Mountain is located on Cheat Mountain, with its highest point at Thorny Flat (4,848 ft). The resort includes 60 slopes and trails, with a vertical drop of 1,500 ft on two trails. It receives an average of 180 inches of snowfall annually and has 14 chairlifts with a capacity of 23,400 skiers per hour. The resort also features a golf course, wedding and convention areas, and summer outdoor activities. The Snowshoe Bike Park is renowned for its challenging downhill track.

world knowledge.Name: Fort Robinson
world knowledge.Area: Pine Ridge region of northwest Nebraska
world knowledge.Address: 2 miles west of Crawford on U.S. Route 20, Dawes and Sioux counties, Nebraska, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fort Robinson is a former U.S. Army fort and now a major feature of Fort Robinson State Park, a public recreation and historic preservation area. Established in 1873, it played a major role in the Sioux Wars from 1876 to 1890. It was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1960 and is part of the Fort Robinson and Red Cloud Agency historic district. The fort was used as a breeding and training center for horses and mules for the military, a K-9 corps training center, and a German prisoner-of-war camp during World War II. The U.S. Army abandoned the fort in 1947, and it was transferred to the U.S. Department of Agriculture before becoming a state park in 1956.

Major_Events.Description: Took place nearby in July 1876.
Crazy Horse surrendered at the fort along with his 1,100 followers on May 6, 1877, and was killed there on September 5 that year while resisting imprisonment.
Chief Morning Star (Dull Knife) led the Northern Cheyenne in an outbreak from the Agency. U.S. soldiers hunted down the escapees, killing men, women, and children.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as a quartermaster remount depot
Major_Events.Description: Fort Robinson became the world's largest quartermaster remount depot, used as a breeding and training center for horses and mules for the military.

Major_Events.Event: World War II K-9 corps training center and POW camp
Major_Events.Description: The fort was the site of a K-9 corps training center and a German prisoner-of-war camp during World War II.
The fort was transferred to the state of Nebraska and became Fort Robinson State Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The fort's historic buildings and sites include the 1904 blacksmith shop, the 1908 veterinary hospital, the 1887 officers' quarters, the 1875 guardhouse and adjutant's office, and the post cemetery. A quartermaster's stores building is now used as a playhouse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fort Robinson played a major role in the Sioux Wars and the history of the Northern Cheyenne. It was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1960 and is part of the Fort Robinson and Red Cloud Agency historic district. The fort is culturally significant for its role in military history, including the surrender of Crazy Horse and the Fort Robinson massacre.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public recreation and historic preservation area
world knowledge.Details: The Fort Robinson Museum is located in the 1905 post headquarters building. Exhibits focus on the fort's history, including its role guarding the Red Cloud Agency from 1874 to 1877, up through the housing of World War II German POWs from 1943 to 1946. The Trailside Museum of Natural History, operated by the University of Nebraska State Museum, is located in the historic Army Theatre building. Fort Robinson is also home to The Post Playhouse, a professional theatre company that produces live theatre during summer months.

world knowledge.Name: Paramount Theatre (Boston)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Paramount Theatre opened in 1932 as a 1,700-seat movie theatre, one of the first in Boston to play talking motion pictures. It closed in 1976 and much of its Art Deco interior was destroyed in the 1980s during asbestos removal. It was designated a Boston Landmark in 1984. Emerson College renovated and expanded the theatre in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: The Paramount Theatre opened as a 1,700-seat, single-screen movie theatre, one of the first in Boston to play talking motion pictures.
The theatre closed and much of its Art Deco interior was later destroyed during asbestos removal in the 1980s.
The building was designated a Boston Landmark by the Boston Landmarks Commission.
Millennium Partners agreed to restore the Paramount's facade, marquee, and vertical sign in exchange for city approval of their adjacent Ritz-Carlton Towers project.
Emerson College announced plans to renovate the theatre and build a performing arts facility, completing the $77 million project in 2010.
Emerson College celebrated the grand re-opening of the Paramount Theatre with Mayor Thomas Menino.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally featured Art Deco interior decoration. Renovated design by Elkus Manfredi Architects with acoustical consulting by Acentech Incorporated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of Boston's first movie theatres for talking motion pictures; designated a Boston Landmark; now a key performing arts venue for Emerson College.
world knowledge.Details: The renovated complex includes a 550-seat theater, black box theater, film screening room, rehearsal studios, sound stage, scene shop, classrooms, restaurant, and offices. Original architect was Arthur Bowditch.

world knowledge.Name: Express Avenue
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Express Avenue is a shopping mall in Chennai promoted by Express Infrastructure, a division of Express Newspapers Pvt. Ltd. It was built at a cost of ₹7,500 million (US$86 million) and is spread over 1,750,000-square-foot (163,000 m2), including 900,000-square-foot (84,000 m2) of leasable (retail) area. The mall is situated near the Royapettah Clock Tower and is built on an 8-acre site inside the historic Indian Express Estate.

Major_Events.Description: The mall was inaugurated on 26 May 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mall has four floors of retail space, a building for corporate offices, and a hotel. It features 26 lifts, 34 escalators, and 4 travelators. The atrium areas are covered with tensile fabric, and the center of the atrium is covered with glass. The mall has six atria with a height not less than 75 ft each.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Express Avenue is home to the largest gaming arcade in South India and hosts a mixture of shopping, business, and leisure. It is a prominent landmark in Chennai, offering a wide range of retail, entertainment, and dining options.
world knowledge.Details: The mall has 8 anchor tenants and 150 vanilla tenants. It includes a 44-room four-star boutique hotel, E Hotel, and a 50,000-square-foot (4,600 m2) food court with 25 counters. The entertainment portion of the mall is 70,000 square feet (6,500 m2), featuring an 08-screens multiplex with a capacity of 1,600 seats. The mall also has a play area for children called Fun City and a business chamber with over 200,000 sq ft (19,000 m2) of office space. The three-level basement parking can handle about 2,000 vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: San Francisco City Hall
world knowledge.Address: 1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place, San Francisco, California
world knowledge.Historical_Background: San Francisco City Hall is the seat of government for the City and County of San Francisco, California. Re-opened in 1915 in its open space area in the city's Civic Center, it is a Beaux-Arts monument to the City Beautiful movement that epitomized the high-minded American Renaissance of the 1880s to 1917. The present building replaced an earlier City Hall that was destroyed during the 1906 earthquake.

Major_Events.Description: The building was completed and officially opened after replacing the previous City Hall destroyed in the 1906 earthquake.

Major_Events.Event: Marriage of Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe
Major_Events.Description: Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe were married at City Hall.

Students from UC Berkeley, Stanford, and other local colleges protested against the House Un-American Activities Committee, leading to a police action where students were fire hosed down the steps beneath the rotunda.

Major_Events.Event: Assassination of George Moscone and Harvey Milk
Major_Events.Description: Former Supervisor Dan White assassinated Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk inside of City Hall.
The earthquake damaged the structure, twisting the dome four inches on its base, leading to a seismic retrofit.
City Hall reopened after its seismic upgrade, becoming the world's largest base-isolated structure at that time.
City Hall was closed from March 2020 until reopening on June 7, 2021, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts style with a dome taller than that of the United States Capitol by 42 feet. The building contains 7,900 tons of structural steel, faced with Madera County granite on the exterior and Indiana sandstone within, with finish marbles from Alabama, Colorado, Vermont, and Italy. The dome rises 307.5 ft above the Civic Center Historic District and has a diameter of 112 ft.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is a symbol of the City Beautiful movement and the American Renaissance. It has been the site of significant historical events, including political assassinations, protests, and notable weddings. The rotunda has hosted the lying in state of prominent figures like President Warren G. Harding and General Fredrick Funston.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government Building (seat of government for the City and County of San Francisco)
world knowledge.Details: The building's vast open space is more than 500,000 square feet and occupies two full city blocks. The upper levels of the Rotunda are public and handicapped accessible. The building features color changeable LED lighting at the outside of the Rotunda, and between the exterior columns, which change to coincide with different events happening in the city and elsewhere.

world knowledge.Name: Mugdock Country Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mugdock Country Park is a country park and historical site that includes the remains of the 14th-century Mugdock Castle, stronghold of the Grahams of Montrose, and the ruins of the 19th-century Craigend Castle, a Gothic Revival mansion and former zoo. The park has a moot hill and gallowhill, historical reminders of the baronial feudal right, held by lairds, of 'pit and gallows'. Also located in the park are the remains of numerous anti-aircraft trenches, which were established during World War II as part of the Clyde Basin anti-aircraft defense system.

Major_Events.Description: A music festival held in the park featuring performers like Emma Pollock, Dodgy, and Beats Antique.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park includes the remains of Mugdock Castle, a 14th-century stronghold, and Craigend Castle, a 19th-century Gothic Revival mansion. The park also features historical structures like a moot hill and gallowhill.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mugdock Country Park is culturally significant due to its historical structures, including Mugdock Castle and Craigend Castle, and its role in local history, including its use during World War II as part of the Clyde Basin anti-aircraft defense system. It also hosts cultural events like the Mugstock Music Festival.
world knowledge.Details: The park features natural attractions like Allander Water, Mugdock Loch, and Drumclog Muir, which provide popular walking and cycling routes. Visitor facilities include a visitor centre, cafe, garden centre, and restaurant. The park is served by the Mugdock and East Dunbartonshire Countryside Ranger Service. The West Highland Way, a long-distance footpath, passes through the outer areas of the park.

world knowledge.Name: Lightwater Valley
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lightwater Valley began as a small self-pick fruit farm in 1969, transitioning into a tourist attraction after a lake was excavated in 1976. The park evolved with the introduction of various rides and attractions, including the world's longest roller coaster, The Ultimate, in 1991. Ownership changed multiple times, with the Brighton Pier Group acquiring it in 2021. The park has continually adapted its attractions to focus on family-friendly experiences.

Major_Events.Description: The Ultimate, the world's longest roller coaster at the time, was opened, significantly boosting the park's popularity.
A fatal accident occurred due to faulty wiring and inadequate training, resulting in legal repercussions and safety reviews.
The park was sold for £5 million, with plans to focus on family-friendly attractions and potential redevelopment.
The iconic roller coaster was dismantled due to prohibitive costs of updating it to modern safety standards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of natural landscapes and constructed attractions, including roller coasters, water rides, and themed areas. The Ultimate was notable for its extensive wooden trestles and lengthy track designed with flexibility for temperature changes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lightwater Valley is a significant family adventure park in Yorkshire, known for its historical rides like The Ultimate and its evolution from a fruit farm to a major tourist attraction. It plays a key role in local tourism and family entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The park has 39 rides and attractions, including 2 roller coasters and 1 water ride. It operates seasonally from March to November and has undergone several rebrandings, with recent mascots including Ebor the Dragon and Rex the Valleysaurus. The park has also invested in renewable energy technologies, including biomass boilers and solar panels.

world knowledge.Name: Warner Grand Theater (Milwaukee)
world knowledge.Address: 212 W. Wisconsin Avenue, Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Warner Grand Theater, also known as the Bradley Symphony Center, was built in 1930 on the site of the 1,500-seat Butterfly Theater in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. It was designed by the architectural firm Rapp and Rapp and opened in 1931. The theater struggled during the Great Depression and underwent several ownership changes and name changes over the years. In 2017, it was purchased by the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra and renamed the Bradley Symphony Center in 2021.

Major_Events.Description: The theater was built on the site of the demolished Butterfly Theater and opened in 1931, attended by thousands of people.
The building was purchased by the Marcus Corporation and renamed "Centre".
The building was renamed "The Grand" to match the Grand Avenue Mall across the street.
The Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra purchased the vacant theater, leading to its renovation and renaming as the Bradley Symphony Center.
The Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra moved into the building and renamed it the Bradley Symphony Center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features an Art Deco style theater with a French Renaissance-style interior. The lobby is art-deco style, and the exterior is Moderne. The theater originally had a 28-rank Kimball pipe organ. The attached 13-story office building also has an Art Deco style exterior with polished granite on floors one through four.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Warner Grand Theater is a significant cultural landmark due to its historical role as a movie palace and its current use as the home of the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra. Its Art Deco architecture and rich history make it an important part of Milwaukee's cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was originally built by Warner Brothers and had a capacity of 1,799 seats. It underwent several name changes and periods of vacancy before being revitalized as the Bradley Symphony Center. The building's design and history reflect the architectural and cultural trends of the early 20th century.

world knowledge.Name: Wicklow Mountains National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wicklow Mountains National Park is a protected area in Ireland, one of eight national parks in the country. The park stretches through County Wicklow as well as small areas of South Dublin and Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown in County Dublin. It contains a variety of attractions that are popular with city dwellers seeking recreation, and areas visited by tourists and history enthusiasts. Chief among the historic sites is Glendalough, which features a collection of Early Medieval monastic structures associated with St Kevin, a hermit priest. Other sites include the Education Centre in Bolger's Cottage, on the Miners' Road by the Upper Lake, Glendalough, and remnants of mining villages.

Major_Events.Description: The park was officially opened in 1991 after being proposed for many years. An interpretative centre was financed in 1990.
An addition of 28.33 square kilometres (7,000 acres) to the park was announced.
The state purchased an additional 19.8296 square kilometres (4,900.0 acres) from a private party. The tract of land goes from Kippure down to Glenasmole Valley and Bohernabreena Reservoir.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of habitats including blanket bog, deciduous woods, coniferous woods, upland grassland, heath, exposed rocky areas, and scree. It also includes historic sites such as Glendalough with Early Medieval monastic structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and historically important due to its diverse natural habitats, historic sites like Glendalough, and its role in providing recreational opportunities and promoting nature conservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Protected area for nature conservation, recreation, and education
world knowledge.Details: Recreational activities available within the park include walking and hiking, rock climbing, rowing, diving, limited swimming and fishing, and many opportunities for sightseeing and photography. The park is managed by the National Parks and Wildlife Service under the Department of Arts, Heritage, Regional, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs. Park staff are responsible for nature conservation, promotion of research and education, public safety, and facilitation of good relations between the park and surrounding communities.

world knowledge.Name: Belasco Theater (Los Angeles)
