world knowledge.Address: 1050 S Hill Street, Los Angeles, California, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Belasco Theater is a historic theater in Downtown Los Angeles, California. Opened in 1926, it operated as a playhouse and briefly as a movie theater until its closure in 1950. It was later used for non-theater purposes, including as a church, before being renovated and reopened as a music venue in 2011. Live Nation became its operator in 2020.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened on November 1, 1926, with a production of the play Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.
The Belasco was a participant in the New Deal-era Federal Theatre Project, a program created to boost the arts after the Great Depression.
The theater closed on June 7, 1950, after being used for burlesque shows and film screenings.
The building was reopened as a music venue called The Belasco on March 19, 2011.
Live Nation became the operator of the facility in 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the Churrigueresque style by the architectural firm Morgan, Walls & Clements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Belasco Theater is culturally significant as a historic theater that has played various roles in Los Angeles' entertainment and cultural scene, from legitimate theater to music venue, and as a participant in the Federal Theatre Project during the Great Depression.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a playhouse, later a movie theater, then a church, and now a music venue.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was commissioned by oil tycoon Edward L. Doheny and was originally called the Doheny Theatre before being renamed in honor of New York playwright David Belasco. It was designated as a historic landmark on January 30, 1990, with reference number 476.

world knowledge.Name: Teatro Sá da Bandeira
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Five thousand square meters of covered area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Teatro Sá da Bandeira is the oldest performance venue in the city of Porto, opened in 1846. It was responsible for the first presentation of films produced in Portuguese and hosted some of the 19th century theater's biggest stars. Initially inaugurated as Teatro Circo, it underwent several reconstructions and name changes, finally becoming Teatro Sá da Bandeira in 1910. It was considered one of the best theaters in Porto, alongside the São João Theater.

Major_Events.Event: First presentation of films produced in Portuguese
Major_Events.Description: On 12 November 1896, Aurélio Paz dos Reis presented the first films made by a Portuguese.
Sarah Bernhardt performed several pieces including "La dame aux camélias" and "Fedora".

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Teatro Sá da Bandeira
Major_Events.Description: One week after the establishment of the Republic, the name Teatro do Príncipe Real was changed to Teatro Sá da Bandeira.
The Porto City Council purchased the theater for 2.1 million euros from the approximately 60 owners, heirs of five families.
The theater was purchased by Livraria Lello bookshop for 3.5 million euros.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater has undergone several reconstructions, with the current building dating from the late 19th century. It includes three stores and has a total of five thousand square meters of covered area. The building features electric lighting, which was a significant innovation at the time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Teatro Sá da Bandeira is culturally significant as the oldest performance venue in Porto and for its role in the introduction of Portuguese films. It has hosted notable performances and events, contributing to the cultural heritage of the city.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was sold by the Porto City Council in 2019 to Livraria Lello bookshop. It includes, in addition to the theater, three stores and has a total of five thousand square meters of covered area. The building also has two more cinemas.

world knowledge.Name: Belfast International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Belfast International Airport, originally known as Aldergrove Airport, was established in 1917 as a Royal Flying Corps training establishment during World War I. Civil traffic began in 1922, and the first scheduled passenger service started in 1933. The airport underwent significant development during World War II and became Northern Ireland's main civil airport in 1963. It was privatized in 1994 and has since seen continuous growth, handling over 6.7 million passengers in 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The first scheduled passenger service was started by the Scottish airline Midland & Scottish Air Ferries, consisting of two daily flights between Aldergrove and Renfrew Airport, Glasgow.

Major_Events.Event: Move of civil flights to Aldergrove
Major_Events.Description: Civil flights were moved to Aldergrove to take advantage of the large airfield, and a new terminal and apron were built.
The airport was privatized, with TBI becoming the new owner in 1996.
easyJet started operations from the airport with flights to London–Luton, establishing a large base and numerous routes.
Work began on a significant terminal expansion to accommodate new security scanning equipment, expected to be operational by summer 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two asphalt runways, a terminal building, and various passenger facilities. It has undergone several upgrades, including the construction of a new International Pier, lounge facilities, and car parks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Belfast International Airport is the main airport for Belfast and the busiest in Northern Ireland. It plays a crucial role in connecting Northern Ireland to various international destinations, contributing significantly to the region's economy and tourism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport for passenger and cargo transport
world knowledge.Details: The airport is owned and operated by Vinci Airports. It features flights to European metropolitan and leisure destinations, with easyJet being the largest airline operating from the airport. The airport has a CAA Public Use Aerodrome Licence and includes facilities for general aviation and private jets.

world knowledge.Name: Branko's Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Bridge across Sava in extension of Brankova Street, Belgrade, Serbia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 450 m (1,480 ft) long, with a central span of 261 m (856 ft) and side spans of 81 m (266 ft) each
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Branko's Bridge was built in 1956 on the foundations of the 1934 King Alexander Bridge, which was destroyed in World War II. It reconnected Belgrade and Zemun as the only motorway bridge at the time. The bridge was named after Branko Radičević, a Serbian romanticist poet, and is an extension of the Brankova Street.

Major_Events.Description: Built on the foundations of the destroyed King Alexander Bridge, it reconnected Belgrade and Zemun.
The bridge's capacity was doubled, resulting in a dual carriageway with three lanes in both directions.
The left pedestrian and bicycle path was closed due to deterioration, leading to years of protests and eventual renovation.
After five years of renovation, all lanes and the pedestrian and bicycle path were fully opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Continuous steel box girder bridge with central and side spans. It uses lower parts of the former King Alexander Bridge's pylons as outer constraints for its two secondary spans.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Branko's Bridge is a vital connection between Belgrade and New Belgrade, symbolizing post-war reconstruction and modernization. It also holds cultural significance due to its naming after Branko Radičević and its role in the city's transportation history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Motorway bridge connecting Belgrade and New Belgrade
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is crossed by nearly 90,000 vehicles daily and has a reputation as a suicide bridge, with around 40 suicide attempts annually. Plans for cultural and museum spaces under the bridge have been proposed but not fully realized.

world knowledge.Name: Oita Art Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oita Art Museum opened in Ōita, Ōita Prefecture, Japan, in 1999. The collection includes Nihonga, Yōga, Bungo Nanga, crafts, modern art, and the Important Cultural Property Materials relating to Tanomura Chikuden.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened to the public on 17 February 1999.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum houses a significant collection of Japanese art, including Important Cultural Property Materials related to Tanomura Chikuden, making it an important cultural institution in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes Nihonga, Yōga, Bungo Nanga, crafts, and modern art. This article related to a museum in Japan is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Century Theatre (Detroit)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1903 by the Twentieth Century Association and opened on December 26, the theater was the first building in Detroit to have a building permit issued in a woman's name. During The Great Depression, the Association disbanded and the theater foreclosed. The building housed a variety of businesses over the years until it finally closed in 1978. In 1990, developer Charles Forbes began a renovation to restore it. The Gem Theatre reopened on December 31, 1991, only to close again in 1997. Because of the fact it would be torn down due to Comerica Park, Forbes negotiated it so the theatre was moved five blocks away on November 10, 1997.

Major_Events.Description: The theater was opened on December 26, 1903, by the Twentieth Century Association.
The Twentieth Century Association disbanded, and the theater foreclosed.
The theater closed after housing various businesses over the years.
Developer Charles Forbes began a renovation to restore the theater.
The Gem Theatre reopened on December 31, 1991.
The Gem Theatre closed again in 1997.
The theater was moved five blocks away on November 10, 1997, to avoid demolition due to Comerica Park. It broke the 1986 Guinness Book of World Records for the heaviest building moved on wheels.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Century Theatre is culturally significant as it was the first building in Detroit to have a building permit issued in a woman's name. It is also notable for its relocation, which set a world record for the heaviest building moved on wheels.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theater hosting shows, weddings, and private events.
world knowledge.Details: The Century Theatre shares a lobby with the Gem Theatre. It has seating at cabaret tables and hosts quirky shows such as Forbidden Broadway, Menopause the Musical, and Late Nite Catechism. The theater building houses a restaurant, The Century Grille, and is a popular downtown Detroit destination for weddings and private events.

world knowledge.Name: Khan Jahan Ali Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Khan Jahan Ali Bridge is a bridge over the Rupsa River in Khulna, Bangladesh, named after Khan Jahan Ali. It serves as a crucial connection between the Southern districts of Bangladesh and the Port of Mongla, the second largest sea port in the country.

Major_Events.Event: Harassment by Purba Banglar Communist Party
Major_Events.Description: Workers at the construction site were harassed by the Purba Banglar Communist Party, who were attempting to extort the firms involved in the construction of the bridge.
The Khan Jahan Ali Bridge was officially opened on May 21, 2005.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is 1.6 km long and 16.48 meters wide, carrying the Khulna City Bypass over the Rupsa River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant as it is named after Khan Jahan Ali, a historical figure, and serves as a vital link between the Southern districts of Bangladesh and the Port of Mongla.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is maintained by the Bangladesh Bridge Authority Ltd. and is located 4.80 km away from Khulna Town. It is known as the gateway of Khulna due to its strategic importance in connecting the Southern districts with the Port of Mongla.

world knowledge.Name: Jai Vilas Mahal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jai Vilas Palace is a nineteenth-century palace in Gwalior, India, built in 1874 by Jayajirao Scindia, the Maharaja of Gwalior during the British Raj. It was designed by Sir Michael Filose and is a fine example of European architecture, combining styles of the Mughals and the Medici. The palace's major part now serves as the 'Jiwajirao Scindia Museum', which opened to the public in 1964, while a part remains the residence of some of his descendants.

Major_Events.Description: The major part of the palace was converted into a museum, showcasing the history and heritage of the Scindia family.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace combines Italian, Corinthian, and Tuscan architectural styles. The first storey is Tuscan, the second Italian-Doric, and the third Corinthian. The interior features gilt and gold furnishings, a huge carpet, and gigantic chandeliers. The Durbar Hall is 30 metres long, 15 metres wide, and 12 metres high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is culturally significant as it represents the opulence and heritage of the Scindia family, one of the prominent royal families in India. It also showcases the blend of European and Indian architectural styles, reflecting the cultural exchanges during the British Raj.
world knowledge.Details: The palace includes a large Durbar Hall, a grand staircase, and rooms lavishly decorated for the royal family. It also features unusual items such as cut glass furniture, stuffed tigers, and a ladies-only swimming pool with its own boat. The museum preserves the memory of the Scindia family's humble origins and their Maratha heritage. Notable historical items include a palanquin gifted by Mughal emperor Shah Alam II and a model silver train used for after-dinner brandy and cigars.

world knowledge.Name: Namtok Mae Surin National Park
world knowledge.Address: Mae Hong Son and Khun Yuam districts, Mae Hong Son Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Namtok Mae Surin National Park was designated Thailand's 37th National Park in 1981. It is known for its mountains, waterfalls, and caves, with the Mae Surin waterfall being its main attraction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is significant for its natural beauty, featuring rare flora and fauna, and is a protected area in Thailand.
world knowledge.Details: The park features deciduous and dipterocarp forests, pine forests in higher areas, and is home to a rare and indigenous lady slipper orchid. Animal species include Malayan sun bear, Asiatic black bear, serow, barking deer, lar gibbon, wild boar, python, and cobra. Bird life includes drongo and hornbill. The park's main attraction is the Mae Surin waterfall, which is 180 metres (590 ft) in height. Another notable waterfall is Pa Bong, a two-tier waterfall with a height of 30 metres (98 ft). Nam Hu Haichai Cave is notable for a water jet erupting from its interior walls at regular intervals of every 25 minutes.

world knowledge.Name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
world knowledge.Address: Near Osaka Bay, Osaka Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan was opened in May 1990 as part of the redevelopment of the Osaka Bay Area. It was the largest public aquarium in the world at the time of its opening. The aquarium was named by the general public and quickly became a major attraction, reaching 1 million visitors in 40 days and 2 million in 101 days. It has since become the most visited aquarium in Japan, with over 85 million visitors as of 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The aquarium opened to the public, becoming the largest public aquarium in the world at the time.
The aquarium reached 50 million visitors, the fastest among aquariums in Japan.
The aquarium became the most visited aquarium in Japan with 75 million visitors.
A ceremony was held to celebrate the achievement of 85 million total visitors.

Major_Events.Event: First successful conception of giant devil ray in captivity
Major_Events.Description: The aquarium achieved the first successful conception of a giant devil ray in captivity, although the offspring did not survive.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The aquarium was designed by Peter Chermayeff of Cambridge Seven Associates. The exterior features three color schemes representing earth, water, and fire, with a fish mural painted by Serge Chermayeff. The building uses 314 tonnes of acrylic glass for its tanks, with the largest single pane measuring six meters by five meters by thirty centimeters. The aquarium's unique water system fills tanks from the bottom and unloads from the top to maintain water clarity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan is a major cultural and educational landmark in Japan, known for its extensive marine life exhibits and research contributions. It is accredited as a Museum-equivalent facility by the Japanese government and is a member of the Japanese Association of Zoos and Aquariums. The aquarium plays a significant role in marine conservation and research, particularly for sharks and rays.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public aquarium and marine research facility
world knowledge.Details: The aquarium features 27 tanks in 16 main exhibits, including the Pacific Ocean tank, which holds 5,400 cubic meters of water and houses whale sharks, manta rays, and other large marine species. The aquarium also has a research center, the Osaka Aquarium Biological Research Institute of Iburi Center (OBIC), which conducts marine research and breeding programs. The aquarium's exhibits include habitats from the Ring of Fire area of the Pacific Ocean, such as the Aleutian Islands, Monterey Bay, and the Great Barrier Reef.

world knowledge.Name: Klagenfurt Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Klagenfurt Cathedral, originally built by Protestants in 1581 and dedicated to the Holy Trinity, was the largest Protestant church in Austria at that time. Commissioned by Christoph Windisch, Klagenfurt's first mayor, it was given to the Jesuits during the Counter-Reformation in 1600 and rededicated to Saints Peter and Paul. The church was destroyed by fire and rebuilt in 1724. In 1787, Bishop Franz Xaver von Salm-Reifferscheid made it the cathedral of the Diocese of Gurk.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Protestants and dedicated to the Holy Trinity.
Given to the Jesuits during the Counter-Reformation and rededicated to Saints Peter and Paul.
The church was razed to the ground by a fire and had to be rebuilt.
Bishop Franz Xaver von Salm-Reifferscheid made it the cathedral of the Diocese of Gurk.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Baroque style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Klagenfurt Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the largest Protestant church in Austria during its time, later becoming a key Catholic cathedral during the Counter-Reformation. It serves as the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Gurk-Klagenfurt and the main parish church of Klagenfurt.
world knowledge.Details: Also known as Klagenfurter Dom; Dom- und Stadtpfarrkirche Hll. Petrus und Paulus.

world knowledge.Name: Sellin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: First mentions of Sellin date to 1295. From 1880 on, the town gained importance as a Baltic Sea spa town. After the Wende in 1989, the building stock in the village was extensively renovated.

Major_Events.Description: Sellin Pier was rebuilt and was officially opened on 2 April 1998.
The historic centre has been thoroughly renovated as part of a programme of urban development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Wilhelmstraße, with its houses from the resort architecture period (turn of the 19th and 20th century), runs up to the steep coast, up to 30 metres high - where there is a steep flight of steps or a lift to Sellin Pier or the promenade on the South Beach (Südstrand).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sellin is a Baltic Sea spa town with historical significance dating back to the 13th century. It features the longest pier on Rügen and has been a popular resort destination since the late 19th century.
world knowledge.Details: Other sights are the Galerie Hartwich in the old fire station (Feuerwehrhaus), the Amber Museum with its associated workshop and the Gnadenkirche. The Sellin Amber Museum was founded in 1999 and is the only one on Rügen. The lake of Schwarzer See in the Granitz also belongs to the municipality and has been designated a strict nature reserve.

world knowledge.Name: Brizlee Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brizlee Tower was commissioned around 1777 to commemorate Lady Elizabeth Seymour, who died in 1776, by her husband Hugh Percy, 1st Duke of Northumberland. It was completed in 1781 and serves as a viewing platform for the Duke's park, landscaped by Capability Brown. The tower stands on Brizlee Hill, reputedly the site of a fire-beacon used to warn of approaching enemies.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was completed as a viewing platform and commemorative structure for Lady Elizabeth Seymour.
The tower was designated as a Grade 1 listed building in December 1969.
The tower underwent extensive renovation in the first decade of the 21st century due to water damage and corroded ironwork.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Brizlee Tower is a 26-metre-high elaborately ornamental tower in dressed stone, featuring a Gothic Revival style. It has six stages, with the lowest stage having an encircling verandah and the topmost stage surrounded by a projecting viewing platform or balcony, surmounted by a cast-iron fire basket. The tower is circular in plan with four slight rectangular projecting buttresses and an interior newel staircase lit through windows. The design is attributed to Robert Adam or John Adam, with influences from classical, Gothic, and Saracenic styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brizlee Tower is culturally significant as a Grade 1 listed folly, representing the Gothic Revival style and the Romantic landscape movement. It serves as a vantage point with extensive views over North Northumberland and the Borders, and it commemorates Lady Elizabeth Seymour. The tower's inscription reflects the Duke's pride in his landscaping achievements.
world knowledge.Details: The tower was placed on the Buildings at Risk Register due to water damage and corroded ironwork but was restored in the 2000s. While not generally open to the public, access has occasionally been permitted for charitable purposes.

world knowledge.Name: University of Lomé
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Lomé (French: Université de Lomé; abbreviated UL) is a public university in Togo, located in the capital Lomé. It is the country's largest university. It was founded in 1970 as the University of Benin (French: Université du Bénin) and adopted its current name in 2001.

Major_Events.Description: In May 2011, the government of Togo ordered the indefinite closure of University of Lomé after students started riots demanding better conditions and food. The riots began on Wednesday, 25 May 2011, and escalated through the rest of the week culminating in a clash on Friday between students and police which required the use of tear gas to disperse the roughly 500 rioting students. Authorities stated that the rioters were invading lecture halls, assaulting lecturers and other students, and destroying university property. The university was closed on Friday, 27 May 2011.

On 6 June, an agreement between the university and the students was reached as students affirmed their commitment to the new LMD academic system and that the university would improve the students' living conditions.

On 8 July, students and government representatives signed a formal agreement allowing current students to continue on the classic academic system or switch to the LMD system at their option and which stated that the government would invest 2.4 billion CFA francs (roughly US$4,800,000) into the construction of new lectures halls and versatile teaching blocks at the University of Lomé and the University of Kara.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Lomé is the largest university in Togo and plays a significant role in the country's education system.
world knowledge.Details: The head of the institution, Koffi Ahadzi Nonon, stated that the students were upset that the university had introduced a new academic system called LMD (translated as bachelor, master, doctorate) for which the students were unprepared. On 26 May 2011, the Embassy of the United States in Lomé, Togo, issued a warden message to U.S. citizens in Togo to avoid the university campus area until the riots had ceased and stating that tear gas may have been used on 25 May, against the demonstrators. On 15 June, the head of student organisation, the Movement for the Development of Togolese Students or MEET, was arrested for attempting to incite possible violent resistance. The head of Hacam — another student organisation — condemned the actions of the head of MEET.

world knowledge.Name: Indravati National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Indravati National Park is a national park located in Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh state in India. The park derives its name from the Indravati River, which flows from east to west and forms the northern boundary of the reserve with the Indian state of Maharashtra. It attained the status of a national park in 1981 and a tiger reserve in 1983, becoming one of the most famous tiger reserves in India.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Indravati National Park is among the most famous wildlife parks of Chhattisgarh. It is one of four Project Tiger sites in Chhattisgarh and is home to one of the last remaining populations of the endangered wild water buffalo.
world knowledge.Details: The park is reported to be largely under Naxal control as of 2022. The topography mainly comprises undulating hilly terrain with altitude ranging between 177 and 599 metres above the sea level. The vegetation is mainly of the tropical moist and dry deciduous type with predominance of bamboo, Sarai and teak. The park is home to a variety of wildlife including the endangered wild Asian buffalo, tigers, leopards, and a large variety of birds. The recommended season to visit the park is from 15 December to 15 June.

world knowledge.Name: Bale Mountains National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bale Mountains National Park is a national park in Ethiopia, encompassing an area of approximately 2,150 km² in the Bale Mountains and Sanetti Plateau of the Ethiopian Highlands. The park's Afromontane habitats have one of the highest incidences of animal endemicity of any terrestrial habitat in the world. It was nominated to the World Heritage Tentative List in 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Nomination to World Heritage Tentative List
Major_Events.Description: The park was nominated to the World Heritage Tentative List in 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Inscription as a World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The park was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2023 during the 45th Session.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is divided into five distinct habitats: Northern Grasslands, Northern Juniper Woodlands, Afro-alpine Meadows, Erica Moorlands, and Harenna Forest. It ranges from grassland areas around 3,000 m in elevation to Mount Tullu Demtu, the second highest point in Ethiopia at 4,377 m.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bale Mountains are the true ancestral home of the Oromo, the largest single ethnic group in the Horn of Africa. The park plays a vital role in climate control and water resources for over 12 million people in Ethiopia, Somalia, and Kenya.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to over 282 species of birds, including nine of the 16 species endemic to Ethiopia. It also hosts a variety of mammals, including the Ethiopian wolf, Mountain nyala, and African wild dog. The park faces threats from grazing, settlements, and domestic dogs, which pose a risk to the Ethiopian wolf population.

world knowledge.Name: Bahrain National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bahrain National Museum is the largest and oldest public museum in Bahrain. It was opened on 15 December 1988 by the Emir of Bahrain Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa. The museum complex covers 27,800 sq meters and is the country's most popular tourist attraction. It is believed to be the region's first modern museum. The museum was designed by Danish architects Krohn & Hartvig Rasmussen and constructed on an artificial peninsula overlooking the neighbouring island of Muharraq.

Major_Events.Description: The first exhibition of archaeological artifacts in Bahrain occurred at the Hidaya Boys School in Muharraq in collaboration with the Danish Archaeological Expedition sent to the Bahrain Fort.

Major_Events.Event: Cultural agreement signed between UNESCO and the Bahraini government
Major_Events.Description: A cultural agreement was signed between UNESCO and the Bahraini government which helped pave the way for the construction of a national museum.

Major_Events.Event: National museum first opened at Government House
Major_Events.Description: A national museum was first opened at Government House in Manama on 4 March 1970 by the head of state council at the time, Khalifa bin Salman Al Khalifa.
The museum celebrated its 25th anniversary by renovating the Hall of Dilmun Graves and hosting an international conference on museum development.

Major_Events.Event: Dilmun Burial Mounds recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The Dilmun Burial Mounds of Bahrain were recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum complex is made of two buildings spanning a floor space of 20,000 square meters. It was designed by Danish architects Krohn & Hartvig Rasmussen and constructed on an artificial peninsula overlooking the neighbouring island of Muharraq.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bahrain National Museum is culturally and historically important as it houses a collection of Bahrain's ancient archaeological artifacts covering around 5000 years of Bahrain's history. It is the largest and oldest public museum in Bahrain and is believed to be the region's first modern museum.
world knowledge.Details: The museum complex contains six permanent exhibitions, an educational hall, a gift shop, and a cafeteria, in addition to administrative offices, laboratories, and warehouses for the Conservation of holdings and parking. The museum's exhibits focus on artifacts and the history of the Dilmun civilization, the natural environment of Bahrain, and the customs and traditions of Bahrain prior to the discovery of oil in 1932.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum in New Delhi, also known as the National Museum of India, is one of the largest museums in India. Established in 1949, it holds a variety of articles ranging from the pre-historic era to modern works of art. It functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. The blueprint of the National Museum had been prepared by the Gwyer Committee set up by the Government of India in 1946. The museum has around 200,000 works of art, mostly Indian, but some of foreign origin, covering over 5,000 years.

Major_Events.Description: The exhibits were first displayed in the state rooms of the Rashtrapati Bhavan on 15 August 1949, and the rooms were formally inaugurated by C. Rajgopalachari, Governor General of India.
The new museum was inaugurated by Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, Vice-President of India, on 18 December 1960.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation Stone Laid for Final Phase
Major_Events.Description: A foundation stone was laid on 18 December 2017 for the third and final phase of the museum's expansion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current building of the National Museum was designed by the architect Ganesh Bikaji Deolalikar. The building has three floors with galleries radiating from a central garden court. The museum was planned to be built in phases to finally give it an octagonal shape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Museum is culturally and historically important as it houses over 200,000 works of art, covering over 5,000 years of Indian history. It includes artifacts from the Harappan civilization, sculptures, paintings, manuscripts, and more, representing the rich cultural heritage of India.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has various departments including archaeology, arms, armor, decorative arts, jewelry, manuscripts, miniatures, textiles, numismatics, epigraphy, Central Asian antiquities, anthropology, Pre-Columbian American and Western Art Collections. It also houses the National Museum Institute of History of Art, Conservation and Museology, which offers master's and doctoral level courses. The museum has a vast collection of over 200,000 works of art, of which only six to seven percent are displayed at any given time. The remaining are exhibited on a rotational basis or in temporary exhibitions.

world knowledge.Name: Wonhyo Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Yongsan District and Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wonhyo Bridge crosses the Han River in South Korea and connects the districts of Yongsan District and Yeongdeungpo District. It was completed in 1981 and was the 13th bridge built on the Han River. The bridge was initially tolled, but the tolls were removed after ownership was transferred to Seoul Metropolitan City in 1983.

Major_Events.Description: Construction started on the bridge on July 17, 1978.
The bridge opened on October 27, 1981.
Toll fees were introduced on December 10, 1981, but were later removed after ownership transfer.
Dongah Construction donated the bridge to Seoul Metropolitan City on February 1, 1983, leading to the removal of tolls.
Wonhyo Bridge was selected as the set for a fighting scene in the 2006 Korean film The Host directed by Bong Joon-ho.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The external appearance of Wonhyo Bridge is more dynamic than other bridges, which added tension for its use in the film The Host.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is culturally significant as it was featured in the popular Korean film The Host, and it plays a key role in connecting two major districts of Seoul.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (bridge connecting Yongsan District and Yeongdeungpo District)
world knowledge.Details: Wonhyo Bridge was the only bridge to have tolls at that time, which caused vehicles to avoid using it. The bridge was selected for The Host due to its dynamic appearance and the concept of a sewer under a bridge fitting the film's narrative.

world knowledge.Name: Asia Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Asia Park was built for the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul, South Korea. The park is located near Seoul Sports Complex.

Major_Events.Description: The park was built to support the 1986 Asian Games held in Seoul.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park was built to support the 1986 Asian Games, making it a significant site for sports and cultural events in Seoul.
world knowledge.Details: Sports Complex Station on Seoul Subway Line 2 is nearby.

world knowledge.Name: National Botanical Garden Shah Alam
world knowledge.Address: Taman Botani Negara Shah Alam, Bukit Cahaya Seri Alam, 40000 Shah Alam, Selangor Darul Ehsan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: National Botanic Gardens Shah Alam (TBNSA) was constructed on 24 April 1986, known as Taman Pertanian Bukit Cerakah (the Bukit Cherakah Agricultural Park). It is located in the Bukit Cherakah Forest Reserve that was constituted in 1909. In 1991, the name was changed to Taman Pertanian Malaysia Bukit Cahaya Seri Alam. In 2007, it was renamed to its current name, Taman Botani Negara Shah Alam. The garden was established on the forest reserve area of Bukit Cerakah which served as a reservoir for the water for the people of Shah Alam.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest is a red meranti-keruing forest, consisting of various Dipterocarpaceae such as Seraya and Meranti. There are also a few hills that can be hiked along the paved trail. The highest point is the Bukit Sapu Tangan (200m asl), on top of the hill, there's a lookout point that provides the view of the city of Shah Alam. The trails from the hill connect with adjacent forested areas outside TBNSA, including Shah Alam Community Forest.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: TBNSA is developed to provide a national scientific education centre and also act as a natural resource conservation centre for the development of botanical, horticultural, floricultural, agriculture, and other related fields in Malaysia. It also functions as a community awareness centre that aims to create excitement and induce the community to appreciate the beauty and benefit of our own local plant variety which is also our national heritage.
world knowledge.Details: TBNSA is open every Tuesday to Sunday. It has parking for 500 vehicles and had 383,329 visitors in 2016. The director as of August 2021 is Siti Zubaidah binti Mohamad.

world knowledge.Name: Warta Mouth National Park
world knowledge.Address: Chyrzyno, near Kostrzyn nad Odrą, Poland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Warta Mouth National Park is the youngest of Poland's 23 national parks, established on 19 June 2001. It was created in the region of the lowest stretch of the Warta river, up to its confluence with the Odra (Oder), which marks the Polish–German border. The park was created on the area of the former Słońsk Nature Reserve, which had existed since 1977, and parts of the Ujście Warty Landscape Park. The area was designated under the Ramsar Convention in 1984 to protect its swampy and muddy grounds, which are a haven for birds.

Major_Events.Description: The Słońsk Nature Reserve was established, which later became part of the Warta Mouth National Park.
The area was designated under the Ramsar Convention to protect its wetland ecosystems.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Warta Mouth National Park
Major_Events.Description: The Warta Mouth National Park was officially established on 19 June 2001.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and ecologically significant as it protects one of the most important regions for bird lairs in Poland. It is home to 245 species of birds, including several endangered species. The park also plays a crucial role in the conservation of wetland ecosystems, which are increasingly rare in Europe due to human activity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of wetland ecosystems and bird habitats
world knowledge.Details: The park is divided into two parts by the Warta river: the Southern part, which includes the former Słońsk reserve, and the Northern Polder. The Southern part serves as a seasonal lake for excessive water, with water levels rising up to four meters annually. The Northern part is rich in canals and is separated from the Warta by a levee. The park's ecosystem is threatened by the regrowth of bigger plants in meadows and pastures, which endangers bird lairs. The park's Board owns a small lodge and a guest-house for visitors, and there are walking and cycling trails, as well as nature walks through the most valuable parts of the Słońsk reserve. Since 1996, the Centre of Natural Education in Chyrzno has been organizing educational activities, including trips, ornithology camps, and ecology workshops.

world knowledge.Name: Sekong Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Near the town of Stung Treng, northeastern Cambodia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sekong Bridge was constructed with financial support from an interest-free loan provided by the Government of China. It was built to enhance regional connectivity and trade.

Major_Events.Description: Held in Stung Treng Province for the construction of the Sekong Bridge and National Road No.7.
The bridge, along with National Road No.7, was officially inaugurated on April 29, 2008, during a formal ceremony.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed by Shanghai Construction Group Co., the bridge spans the Sekong River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is also known as the 1st Cambodia-China Friendship Bridge, symbolizing the cooperation between Cambodia and China.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Enhancing regional connectivity and trade by connecting Stung Treng Province to National Road No.7, part of the Asian Highway Network AH11.
world knowledge.Details: The total project cost was $15 million USD. The bridge connects Stung Treng Province to National Road No.7, which runs from Skuon, Cambodia to Luang Prabang, Laos.

world knowledge.Name: Caye Chapel
world knowledge.Area: 16 miles (26 km) north-northeast of Belize City and 3 miles (4.8 km) south of Caye Caulker
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Caye Chapel was once owned by Isaiah Emmanuel Morter, Belize's first African millionaire. It is adjacent to the Bacalar Chico National Park and Marine Reserve (BCNPMR), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Major_Events.Event: Plans for development announced by Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts
Major_Events.Description: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts announced plans for the development of Caye Chapel, featuring approximately 50 private estate lots, 35 private residences, and 100 guest rooms and suites.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features an airstrip, 18-hole golf course (White Shark Golf Course), 25,000-square-foot (2,300 m2) clubhouse, and conference facilities. The golf course was co-designed by Greg Norman and Lorena Ochoa.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, the world's second longest barrier reef, and adjacent to a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was once owned by Belize's first African millionaire.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Private island with recreational facilities including golf, snorkeling, and fishing.
world knowledge.Details: The island is part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, home to the Great Blue Hole and other popular SCUBA diving destinations. It is possible to snorkel and fish around the island.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio José Rico Pérez
world knowledge.Address: Alicante, Spain, 2 miles outside Alicante city centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1974, the stadium is named after José Rico Pérez (1918–2010), the former chairman of Hércules CF. It hosted matches during the 1982 FIFA World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was one of the venues for the 1982 FIFA World Cup held in Spain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Francisco Llorens, the stadium is a multi-purpose sports venue with a capacity of 24,704 seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the home of Hércules CF and for hosting international football events like the 1982 FIFA World Cup.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the 25th-largest in Spain and the 4th-largest in the Valencian Community. It is owned and operated by Hércules CF.

world knowledge.Name: Heiwadai Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Heiwadai Park was constructed in 1939 to commemorate the 2,600th anniversary of Japan's Imperial establishment. The park's Peace Tower, originally named Hakko Ichiu Tower, was built in 1940 and has been a point of controversy due to its militaristic origins. The park became a popular honeymoon destination after Princess Takako Shimazu honeymooned there in 1960.

Major_Events.Description: The park was constructed to commemorate the 2,600th anniversary of Japan's Imperial establishment.
Originally named Hakko Ichiu Tower, it was built to memorialize the installment of Japan's first emperor, Jimmu. The tower was renamed after World War II.
The park became a favorite honeymoon destination for Japanese newlyweds after Princess Takako Shimazu honeymooned there.

Major_Events.Event: Sister Park Designation with Hibiya Park
Major_Events.Description: Hibiya Park was designated as Heiwadai's sister park in a ceremony where Heiwadai received doves from Hibiya.
The Peace Tower was the inception point for the torch relay of the 1964 Summer Olympics.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Peace Tower is a 36-metre (118 ft) structure designed by Jitsuzo Hinago, built from stones gathered from around the then-current extent of the Japanese empire. The Haniwa Garden features over 400 haniwa (terracotta clay figures) replicas of burial haniwa excavated at the site, depicting animals, boats, dancers, houses, and warriors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Heiwadai Park is culturally significant as a symbol of peace and a popular honeymoon destination. However, the Peace Tower's origins as a militaristic symbol have sparked controversy. The park also houses the Miyazaki Shrine, devoted to Emperor Jimmu, and serves as a historical site with its Haniwa Garden.
world knowledge.Details: The park's Haniwa Garden is 9,000 square metres (2.2 acres) in size and features over 400 haniwa figures. The Peace Tower's original inscription 'Hakkō ichiu' was removed after World War II but was later re-installed following the 1964 Summer Olympics. The tower remains a controversial symbol due to its militaristic origins.

world knowledge.Name: Attenborough Nature Reserve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Attenborough Nature Reserve is a nature reserve located 5 miles southwest of Nottingham city centre. It was established in 1966 on the site of former gravel pits used between 1929 and 1967. The site is owned and managed by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust, supported by Broxtowe Borough Council. The reserve was opened by Sir David Attenborough and has since been restored as wetland. The purchase of the site from Cemex UK was concluded in December 2020, following a £750,000 grant from Biffa Award.

Major_Events.Description: The reserve was opened by Sir David Attenborough.
The Attenborough Nature Centre was completed and opened by Sir David Attenborough.
The site was purchased from Cemex UK by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust with a £750,000 grant from Biffa Award.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The reserve features large lakes formed by flooded gravel pits, areas of scrub, grassland, native willow, and woodland. The Attenborough Nature Centre provides visitor services, educational facilities, a shop, refreshment point, and car park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The reserve is significant for its biodiversity, including over 250 bird species, and its role in conservation and education. It is part of the Attenborough Gravel Pits Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The Attenborough Nature Centre has won a Gold award for eco-tourism and was listed as number 9 in a top ten 'eco places in the world' by BBC Wildlife.
world knowledge.Details: The reserve covers 145 hectares of lakes, wetland, grassland, and scrub. It sits at the confluence of the River Erewash and the Trent. The Attenborough Nature Centre is open seven days a week and is surrounded by ponds. There are also two public bird hides.

world knowledge.Name: African Lion Safari
world knowledge.Historical_Background: African Lion Safari was founded by Gordon Debenham "Don" Dailley, a retired Canadian Army colonel, and opened on August 21, 1969. Initially, Dailley partnered with the Chipperfield family from England to purchase four farms in the Rockton, Ontario area. He bought out the Chipperfields in the early 1970s. The park remains privately owned and has focused on breeding endangered species, particularly Asian elephants, since the 1970s.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened its doors to the public on August 21, 1969.

Major_Events.Event: First successful Asian elephant birth from artificial insemination
Major_Events.Description: "Jake" became African Lion Safari's first successful Asian elephant birth from artificial insemination, and the first of its kind in Canada.
Animal rights activists staged a protest during the Safari's opening day to raise awareness about issues surrounding the use of exotic animals for entertainment.
Omar Norton, a part-time employee, was crushed to death by a bull elephant named Tusko while trying to break up a fight.
A couple driving through the game reserve were mauled by a Bengal tiger, leading to a lawsuit that was resolved in 2005 with a $2.5 million award.
A trainer was airlifted to hospital after being attacked by one of the safari's elephants.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features seven game reserves where animals roam freely in large enclosures ranging from 2 to 20 hectares. It includes a walking section with displays of exotic birds, primates, and Asian elephants. The reserves have various structures like rock formations, shelters, and feeding areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: African Lion Safari is significant for its conservation efforts, particularly in breeding endangered species like Asian elephants, cheetahs, and white rhinos. It is an accredited member of several international zoological associations and has contributed to reintroduction programs for various species.
world knowledge.Details: The park is involved in the International Species Survival Plans for several endangered species and has received awards for its care of cheetahs and giraffes. It has faced criticism from animal rights organizations for its treatment of elephants and other animals. The park is located 100 kilometers west of Toronto and is a popular tourist attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Chimney Rock State Park
world knowledge.Address: Chimney Rock, Rutherford County, North Carolina, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chimney Rock State Park was established on May 4, 2005, after the North Carolina General Assembly authorized its creation. The park was initially named 'Hickory Nut Gorge State Park' but was renamed to Chimney Rock State Park in July 2007. The land was originally purchased by Dr. Lucius B. Morse in 1902 and operated as a private park until 2007 when it was acquired by the state.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Hickory Nut Gorge State Park
Major_Events.Description: The North Carolina General Assembly authorized the creation of the park.
The Carolina Mountain Land Conservancy and The Nature Conservancy purchased a 1,568-acre tract of land to be added to the new state park.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Chimney Rock State Park
Major_Events.Description: The General Assembly renamed Hickory Nut Gorge State Park to Chimney Rock State Park.
The park suffered severe hurricane damage due to Hurricane Helene.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a 315-foot gneiss monolith named Chimney Rock, accessible by elevator, and a 404-foot waterfall, Hickory Nut Falls. The underlying geology includes Henderson Gneiss, Poor Mountain Formation, and Sugarloaf Gneiss, with notable exfoliation surfaces and joints producing large blocks and caves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chimney Rock State Park is culturally and historically significant for its natural beauty, geological features, and recreational opportunities. It provides habitat for rare flora and fauna and offers stunning views of the surrounding countryside.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: State park for recreation and conservation
world knowledge.Details: The park features hiking trails for all skill levels, views of the Devil's Head balancing rock, and diverse forest communities. It is owned and managed by the North Carolina Division of Parks and Recreation.

world knowledge.Name: Belle Vue Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Belle Vue Park is a large Victorian public park in the west of the city of Newport, in South Wales. It was awarded a Green Flag Award in 2008 and has maintained the status for over a decade since. The park is listed on the Cadw/ICOMOS Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in Wales. The land on which the park stands was a gift to Newport from Godfrey Morgan, 1st Viscount Tredegar in 1891 to provide a public park for its citizens. An open competition to design and construct the park was won by the Cumbrian landscape architect T. H. Mawson. The park opened on 8 September 1894.

Major_Events.Description: The Gorsedd Stone Circle was erected in 1896 for the National Eisteddfod, held in Belle Vue Park in 1897.
The bowling greens were opened in 1904.
A Tea House was added in 1910.
The bandstand and original series of cascades were restored in 2006.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Belle Vue Park has many features typical of a Victorian public park, including the conservatories and pavilion, bandstand and rockeries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it was a gift to the citizens of Newport and is listed on the Cadw/ICOMOS Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in Wales. It has maintained a Green Flag Award for over a decade.
world knowledge.Details: Belle Vue Park contains a number of rare specimens, including Himalayan Magnolias, Judas Trees, Tulip Trees, Ginkgo biloba, and Liquidambar. The park also features Belle Vue Tearooms, a social enterprise café, and hosts weddings and other events in its conservatories and bandstand.

world knowledge.Name: Helmántico Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Villares de la Reina, Salamanca, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1970, Helmántico Stadium was the home stadium of UD Salamanca until its dissolution in 2013. It was later acquired by Desarrollos Empresariales Deportivos S.L., and is now used by Salamanca CF UDS.

Major_Events.Description: The mini-stadium within Helmántico Stadium hosts an international athletic championship once a year.
Javier Sotomayor set the world record in high jump at the mini-stadium, which is officially named after him.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Antonio García Fernando Población, the stadium includes a main football field, a mini-stadium for training and athletics, swimming pools, and tennis courts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant for its role in local football and athletics, including hosting a world record in high jump. It remains a key sports venue in the Salamanca region.
world knowledge.Details: The mini-stadium is popularly called 'Pistas del Helmántico' and hosts matches for Salamanca CF UDS B. The stadium was auctioned after UD Salamanca's dissolution and is now owned by Desarrollos Empresariales Deportivos S.L.

world knowledge.Name: Champagne-Ardenne TGV station
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Champagne-Ardenne TGV station opened in 2007 along with the first phase of the LGV Est, a high-speed rail line running from Paris to Strasbourg. It is situated about five kilometres south of Reims.

Major_Events.Description: The station opened on 10 June 2007 as part of the LGV Est high-speed rail line.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Pierre-Michel Desgrange.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The station serves as a major transportation hub in the Grand Est region, connecting various cities and regions via high-speed rail.
world knowledge.Details: The station is a stop for TGV, Ouigo, and TER Grand Est services. It is directly connected to several major stations in Île-de-France and other regions. The station has appeared in seasons 3 and 7 of the TV show 'Jet Lag: The Game'.

world knowledge.Name: Hiroshima University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hiroshima University was established on May 31, 1949, following the merge of several national educational institutions in Hiroshima Prefecture after World War II. It was created from notable pre-war institutions such as the Hiroshima University of Literature and Science and Hiroshima School of Secondary Education. The university suffered damage from the atomic bomb in 1945 but was reconstructed and later relocated to Higashihiroshima between 1982 and 1995.

Major_Events.Description: Hiroshima University was chartered as a university under the new post-war education system.
The university's predecessor institutions suffered significant damage from the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima.
The university relocated from Hiroshima City to Higashihiroshima to expand its campus.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hiroshima University holds an important position among Japanese universities, being formed from notable pre-war institutions and playing a key role in post-war education and research. It is a symbol of resilience and reconstruction after the atomic bombing.

Details.Motto: Try New Things, Do New Things
Details.Affiliations: BME, CNU, FU, HMU, JMU, HHJ, UNPAR, LTU, LE, MU, RU, SU

world knowledge.Name: Milan Puskar Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mountaineer Field at Milan Puskar Stadium is an American football stadium in Morgantown, West Virginia, on the campus of West Virginia University. It opened in 1980 and serves as the home field for the West Virginia Mountaineers football team. The facility is named for Milan Puskar, a Morgantown resident and founder of Mylan Pharmaceuticals, Inc. who donated $20 million to the university in 2004. The original Mountaineer Field was located on the school's main campus but could not be expanded or modernized due to the proximity of campus buildings and roads. The new stadium was constructed on the former site of a golf course.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was dedicated on September 6, 1980, which also marked the first game for head coach Don Nehlen. Singer John Denver made an appearance and led the fans in the singing of his hit song "Take Me Home, Country Roads."
On November 20, 1993, 70,222 fans packed the stadium to watch the #9 ranked Mountaineers defeat #4 Miami.
The stadium hosted a National Football League pre-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Atlanta Falcons.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium's design was inspired by Jack Trice Stadium at Iowa State University. It features FieldTurf (since 2017), luxury suites, club seats, and multiple video scoreboards. The original construction cost was $22 million, with subsequent renovations and expansions adding modern amenities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a central part of West Virginia University's athletic culture and a symbol of state pride. The song "Take Me Home, Country Roads" is played at every home game, and the stadium hosts various community and high school events, reinforcing its role as a cultural hub.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: American football stadium and event venue
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone multiple renovations, including turf replacements, seating expansions, and the addition of luxury suites and video boards. It has also hosted high school football games, band festivals, and other community events. The most recent renovations in 2020 included a new video scoreboard, ribbon boards, and a sound system.

world knowledge.Name: Newburgh–Beacon Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Spanning the Hudson River between Newburgh and Beacon, New York
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 7,789 feet (2,374 m) and 7,855 feet (2,394 m); Longest span: 1,000 feet (300 m); Clearance below: 135 feet (41 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Newburgh–Beacon Bridge is a continuous truss toll bridge spanning the Hudson River, connecting Newburgh and Beacon in New York State. Originally planned as a four-lane bridge, funding issues reduced it to two lanes. The westbound span opened in 1963, and a second eastbound span was added in 1980 due to increased traffic from Interstate 84. The bridge was officially renamed in 1997 to honor Hamilton Fish III and Hamilton Fish IV, long-serving U.S. House Representatives.

Major_Events.Description: The original northern span opened, carrying one lane of traffic in each direction.
A second parallel span was opened to accommodate increased traffic, designed with three travel lanes and a bicycle path.
Tolls were abolished for westbound drivers, while eastbound tolls were doubled.
The bridge was renamed in honor of Hamilton Fish III and Hamilton Fish IV.
A $94.7 million project replaced the eastbound span's deck.
The bridge converted to all-electronic tolling on the eastbound span.
The walkway's curfew was removed, allowing 24/7 pedestrian access.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Twin-span continuous truss bridges made of steel. The eastbound span uses weathering steel (COR-TEN), which forms a protective brown layer. The westbound span was repainted brown to match. The bridge features a cantilever design with a main span of 1,000 feet and side spans of 602 feet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a critical transportation link over the Hudson River, facilitating interstate and local traffic. It was one of the first interstate-funded bike paths in the U.S. and is named after prominent political figures Hamilton Fish III and IV.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries Interstate 84 and New York State Route 52 across the Hudson River, connecting Newburgh and Beacon.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is maintained by the New York State Bridge Authority and carries approximately 65,000 vehicles daily. Tolls are collected eastbound only, with current rates at $1.65 for E-ZPass and $2.15 for tolls-by-mail. The bridge has undergone several renovations, including deck replacements and toll plaza reconfigurations.

world knowledge.Name: Blida 1 University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Blida 1 is a university located in Blida, Algeria. Founded in 1981 and named after Saad Dahlab, an Algerian nationalist and politician, the University of Blida 1 ranked 7th in Algeria, 4310th in the global 2023 rating, and scored in the Top 50% across 35 research topics.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Blida 1 is significant for its contributions to education and research in Algeria, hosting international students and producing notable alumni.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Blida 1's ranking is based on 3 factors: research output (EduRank's index has 4,642 academic publications and 32,116 citations attributed to the university), non-academic reputation, and the impact of notable alumni.

world knowledge.Name: Cocoa House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cocoa House was completed in July 1964 and commissioned in July 1965 by the government of Western Region, headed by Chief Samuel Ladoke Akintola. It was the first skyscraper in West Africa and the tallest building in Nigeria from 1965 to 1979. It was built from proceeds of agricultural commodities like cocoa, rubber, and timber from the then Western State of Nigeria.

Major_Events.Description: The entire building was gutted by fire on January 9, 1985, which began in the top floors from malfunctioning electrical equipment. It was closed from public use until it was renovated in August 1992 and re-opened for commercial use.

Major_Events.Event: Commissioning of Odu’a Museum and Hall of Fame
Major_Events.Description: The Odu’a Museum and Hall of Fame was commissioned by Professor Wole Soyinka in 2013.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 26-storey skyscraper, initially named 'Ile Awon Agbe' (House of Farmers) in Yoruba.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cocoa House is a source of joy and pride for the residents of Ibadan and Nigeria as a whole. It symbolizes the agricultural prosperity of the Western State of Nigeria and its historical significance as the first skyscraper in West Africa.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Office building for major firms and broadcasting companies.
world knowledge.Details: The building is managed by Wemabod Estates Limited, a subsidiary of O'dua group of companies, and is the property of Odu'a Investment Company Limited. It was proposed by Obafemi Awolowo with allocations from the proceeds of cocoa exportation and commissioned by the National Investment and Property Company (NIPC). A cocoa tree was planted in front of the building beside a water fountain, which influenced its name change to Cocoa House.

world knowledge.Name: Musée Saint-Remi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée Saint-Remi is housed in the former Abbey of Saint-Remi, founded in the 6th century. The abbey became prominent after acquiring the relics of St. Remigius in 553. It was richly endowed and served as a significant religious and educational center. The basilica was rebuilt in the 11th century, and the choir was reconstructed in the 12th century. The abbey and basilica were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991.

Major_Events.Description: The abbey's prominence grew after acquiring the relics of St. Remigius, leading to numerous donations.
Abbot Aviard initiated the reconstruction of the basilica, which was completed and consecrated by Pope Leo IX in 1049.
The choir was rebuilt to create a grander space for the shrine of St. Remy.
Many valuable objects were looted, and the Holy Ampulla used in French coronations was destroyed.
The abbey and basilica were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to their architectural and historical significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the former Abbey of Saint-Remi, featuring Romanesque and Gothic architectural elements. The basilica has a magnificent design with stained glass from the 12th century. The choir was rebuilt in the 12th century to enhance the shrine of St. Remy.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Musée Saint-Remi is culturally significant due to its association with St. Remigius, who converted Clovis I to Christianity. The abbey and basilica are key landmarks in early French monarchy history and were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site for their outstanding architecture and historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses tapestries from the 16th century, marble capitals from the 4th century AD, furniture, jewellery, pottery, weapons, and glasswork from the 6th to 8th centuries, medieval sculpture, and exhibits from Gallo-Roman and Gallic civilizations. It also features a permanent military exhibition.

world knowledge.Name: Muckle Flugga Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Muckle Flugga, Shetland, Unst, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Muckle Flugga lighthouse was built in 1854 by Thomas and David Stevenson, originally to protect ships during the Crimean War. It was first lit on 1 January 1858. The lighthouse was automated in March 1995. It is Britain's most northerly lighthouse and was renamed from North Unst Lighthouse to Muckle Flugga in 1964. The lighthouse inspired Robert Louis Stevenson's map of 'Treasure Island'.

Major_Events.Description: A temporary lighthouse was built 200 feet above sea level and lit on 11 October 1854 during the Crimean War. It was damaged by winter storms, leading to plans for a more permanent structure.
The permanent Muckle Flugga lighthouse was first lit on 1 January 1858.
The lighthouse was fully automated in March 1995.
The lighthouse was renamed from North Unst Lighthouse to Muckle Flugga.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 20 m (66 ft) high cylindrical masonry tower with a white tower, black lantern, and ochre trim. It has 103 steps to the top and a focal height of 66 m (217 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Muckle Flugga Lighthouse is culturally significant as Britain's most northerly lighthouse and for its association with Robert Louis Stevenson, who was inspired by Unst for the map of 'Treasure Island'. It is also a category A listed building.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To serve as a navigational aid for ships.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was used as a setting for the wartime comedy 'Back-Room Boy'. It was originally served by the Grace Darling, which launched from the boat house below the shore station in Burrafirth. Supplies were winched up by a blondin cable hoist. The shore station was sold off after automation and now partly hosts the Hermaness Visitor Centre.

world knowledge.Name: Comedy Theatre, Melbourne
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Comedy Theatre was built in 1928 and designed in the Spanish style with a Florentine-style exterior and wrought-iron balconies. The site previously hosted entertainment venues such as Rowe's American Circus (1842-1854) and the Royal Victoria Theatre (1854-1894). It was later replaced by Coppin's Olympic Theatre (1855-1894), which was eventually abandoned. The Comedy Theatre opened on 28 April 1928 and was operated by J.C. Williamson's for fifty years before being purchased by Paul Dainty in 1978. Since 1996, it has been owned and operated by Marriner Group.

Major_Events.Description: The Comedy Theatre officially opened on 28 April 1928.
Paul Dainty purchased the theatre for $800,000.
The theatre was acquired by Marriner Group, which has owned and operated it since.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Spanish style with a Florentine-style exterior and wrought-iron balconies.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of Melbourne's earliest play-houses, it has hosted notable productions and performers, contributing to the city's cultural and entertainment history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hosting commercial seasons of plays, smaller-scale musicals, comedy, and other entertainment events.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a seating capacity of 1003 and is diagonally opposite Her Majesty's Theatre.

world knowledge.Name: Outamba-Kilimi National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Outamba-Kilimi National Park was established as a game reserve in 1974 and formally gazetted as a National Park in October 1995. It was chosen for preservation due to its large chimpanzee population. The park is divided into two areas: Outamba (741 km²) and Kilimi (368 km²), named after Mount Outamba and River Kilimi, respectively.

Major_Events.Description: The park was formally recognized and protected as a National Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The terrain is mainly flat with a few hills and large rivers. Vegetation includes gallery forest, closed woodland, grassland, tall-grass savanna, and patches of closed-canopy forest. Both areas contain raffia palm swamp forest and riverine grassland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its diverse wildlife, including chimpanzees, hippopotamuses, forest elephants, and over a hundred bird species. It is also home to the Susu tribe, who live in and around the park and have ancestral sites within it.
world knowledge.Details: The park has a 1 km buffer zone where most villages are located. Restrictions are fewer here, allowing hunting (except for protected species) and farming. Simple one-bed and group huts made from local materials are available for visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Kuğulu Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kuğulu Park, also known as Swan Park, is a public park in the Çankaya district of Ankara, Turkey. It is known for its swans, which are a symbol of Ankara, and also houses ducks and geese. The park's pond was renovated in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: In June 2013, Kuğulu Park's waterfowl (35 birds) were evacuated temporarily to protect them from tear gas exposure during the 2013 Turkish protests. The park was a major meeting point for protestors and saw a Taksim Gezi Park-style encampment.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kuğulu Park is culturally significant for its swans, which are a symbol of Ankara, and its role as a major meeting point during the 2013 Turkish protests.
world knowledge.Details: The City of Vienna gave the park a gift of swans.

world knowledge.Name: Six Flags Hurricane Harbor Rockford
world knowledge.Address: Next to the interchange between Interstate 39/U.S. Route 51 and Interstate 90 near U.S. Route 20, Cherry Valley, Illinois, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built as Magic Waters in 1984 under private ownership, the park faced bankruptcy in 1986 due to low attendance. The Rockford Park District took over and revitalized it, leading to increased attendance. In 2019, Six Flags began operating the park and renamed it Six Flags Hurricane Harbor Rockford.

Major_Events.Event: Bankruptcy and takeover by Rockford Park District
Major_Events.Description: Private ownership filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, and the property was seized by Amcore Bank. The Rockford Park District took over and increased attendance by 50%.
A lazy river ride was added to the park.
An 80-foot-tall water coaster was added but removed in 2015 due to lawsuits over back injuries.
A dark tunnel tube slide 5 stories high was added.
A 65-foot-tall tube slide was added.
A 75-foot-tall speed slide ride was added.
The ride was removed due to 12 lawsuits over back injuries, with settlements totaling $2.53 million.
An AquaLoop water slide with a 45-degree inclined loop was added.
Six Flags began operating the park and renamed it Six Flags Hurricane Harbor Rockford.
The park's first water slide addition under Six Flags' operation, a 'tailspin' slide, was added.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features multiple water attractions, including pools, lazy rivers, water slides, and a water coaster. Notable structures include The Abyss (a dark tunnel tube slide), Typhoon Terror (a tube slide), and Tidal Wave (a tailspin slide).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a major water park in the Midwest, it serves as a popular recreational destination for families and thrill-seekers. Its evolution from Magic Waters to Six Flags Hurricane Harbor Rockford reflects broader trends in amusement park management and branding.

image_name: Natal Dunes State Park "Journalist Luiz Maria Alves"

world knowledge.Name: Natal Dunes State Park "Journalist Luiz Maria Alves"
world knowledge.Address: Along the coastal highway beside the neighborhoods of Mãe Luiza, Capim Macio and Ponta Negra, Natal, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Natal Dunes State Park was created by state decree 7,237 of 22 November 1977. It was the first environmental conservation unit in Rio Grande do Norte. The park protects an area of dunes and native vegetation along the coastal highway and is considered the second largest urban park in Brazil. It has been recognized by UNESCO as an integral part of the Atlantic Forest Biosphere Reserve.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established by state decree 7,237 on 22 November 1977.
The park benefited from an extensive overhaul of the facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features coastal dune herbs, shrubs, and trees, mainly Atlantic Forest but with some species of the caatinga and tabuleiro. It includes over 270 species of trees in 78 families. The public use area, the Bosque dos Namorados, covers about 7 hectares (17 acres) and has over 1,300 native Atlantic Forest trees. It contains the park headquarters, visitor center, library, research center, seedling nursery for native species, Brazil wood amphitheater, arts area, artificial lake, environmental control station, playground and track for jogging and hiking.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and environmentally significant as it protects an area of Atlantic Forest and dunes in the heart of the city of Natal. It is the first environmental conservation unit in Rio Grande do Norte and has been recognized by UNESCO as part of the Atlantic Forest Biosphere Reserve. The park supports research, leisure, ecotourism, education, and ecological awareness.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Environmental conservation, research, leisure, ecotourism, education, and ecological awareness.
world knowledge.Details: The park has a Management Plan and an Operation Plan that covers environmental management programs, public use and operations. It stages concerts, plays, lectures, exhibitions, and workshops. The administration maintains a nursery of native seedlings with a capacity of 16,000 seedlings used for recovery and reforestation. The park managers conduct environmental education programs in the communities that surround the park. On average, there are 150,000 visitors annually. Three interpretive trails totaling 6.5 kilometres (4.0 mi) describe elements of the dune ecosystem. The park is managed by IDEMA (Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente do Rio Grande do Norte).

world knowledge.Name: University of Lille
world knowledge.Address: Five university campuses in the Métropole européenne de Lille (Lille - Villeneuve d'Ascq - Roubaix - Tourcoing), Hauts-de-France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Lille has its origins in the University of Douai (1559) and resulted from the merger of three universities – Lille 1 University of Science and Technology, Lille 2 University of Health and Law, and Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III in 2018. It is one of the largest universities in France and one of the largest French-speaking universities in the world.

Major_Events.Description: Lille 1 University of Science and Technology, Lille 2 University of Health and Law, and Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III merged to form the University of Lille.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a French university of excellence
Major_Events.Description: The university was funded as one of the French universities of excellence, receiving an endowment of 500 million euros to accelerate its strategy in education, research, international development, and outreach.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university has multiple campuses with varied architectural styles. The Science and Technology campus features modern facilities, including the LILLIAD Learning Center Innovation, an ultra-modern scientific library with exhibition spaces and conference rooms. The Health campus is part of the largest university hospital complex in Europe.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Lille is a major center for education and research in France, contributing significantly to scientific, cultural, and social development. It has produced notable alumni and faculty, including Nobel Prize winners and prominent researchers.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Lille has 15 Schools and Divisions spread into six major domains. It operates the European Doctoral College and is a member of the CURIF (Coordination of French research-intensive universities). The university collaborates with numerous organizations and schools, including the Pasteur Institute of Lille, CHU Lille University Hospital, CNRS, INSERM, INRA, INRIA, École Centrale de Lille, and Sciences Po Lille.
