Afghanistan v South Africa
Afghanistan v Scotland
Afghanistan v Ireland
Pakistan v Sri Lanka
Pakistan v New Zealand
Pakistan v Sri Lanka
New Zealand v West Indies
Inaugural edition featuring several international cricket players
Hosted the final of the 2018 Blind Cricket World Cup
Hosted 11 group-stage matches
West Stand renamed the 'Sachin Tendulkar Stand' in honor of the Indian cricket legend
Hosted 11 group-stage matches (Semi-final)

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features 62-meter boundaries in long on, 58-meter in straight, and 65-meter in mid-wicket. It is the first GCC LED-lit cricket stadium using innovative and advanced control systems and DMX Technology. The pitch lighting system replaced 392 conventional metal Halide floodlights with 176 LED floodlights for energy conservation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sharjah Cricket Stadium is culturally significant as it has hosted numerous international cricket matches, including a record number of One Day Internationals (ODIs). It has been a neutral venue for Test matches and has played a pivotal role in promoting cricket in the UAE. The stadium is also notable for hosting the inaugural T10 Cricket League and the Blind Cricket World Cup Final.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 16,000 and is owned by the Bukhatir Group. It has been the home ground for the Afghanistan cricket team and has hosted matches for the Multan Sultans and Quetta Gladiators in the Pakistan Super League (PSL). The stadium was also a venue for the Indian Premier League (IPL) during the 2014, 2020, and 2021 seasons due to political and health-related issues in India.

world knowledge.Name: Baralt Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Downtown Maracaibo, at the northwestern corner of the historic Plaza Bolívar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Baralt Theatre is a significant cultural institution in Venezuela, located in downtown Maracaibo. It was initially built in the mid-19th century as a small performance hall and has undergone several reconstructions. The theatre is historically significant as the site of the first film screenings in Venezuela and was designated a National Monument in 1981.

Major_Events.Description: The first theatre began construction in 1839 on land donated by Don Miguel Antonio Baralt.
The neoclassical theatre, designed by Manuel de Obando, was inaugurated on 24 July 1883, coinciding with the birthday celebrations of Simón Bolívar.

Major_Events.Event: Reconstruction under Governor Vicente Pérez Soto
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was reconstructed in 1932, designed by Leon Jerome Hoet, to reflect the modernization of Maracaibo due to the oil industry's development.
The theatre was named a National Monument in November 1981, recognizing its cultural and historical significance.
After a long restoration process that began in 1986, the theatre reopened in 1998, preserving the original foundations and Hoet's designs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre features a neoclassical design with Art Nouveau elements in its facade, including balustrades and large arches in relief. The interior is adorned with art deco style paintings and frescoes by Antonio Angulo. The structure includes a gable roof made of zinc with trusses and uses windows and concrete latticework grilles for ventilation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Baralt Theatre is culturally significant as the site of the first film screenings in Venezuela and for its role in the country's cultural heritage. It is also a longstanding part of the historic center of Maracaibo.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a seating capacity of 3,000 and includes a main theatre area with a stage and restrooms, and a public area with a smoking area and restaurant. Guided tours are available in the mornings, lasting half an hour. The theatre hosts the Venezuelan National Short Film Festival annually in the last week of January.

world knowledge.Name: Loving County Courthouse
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by Pecos St., Collins St., Dallas St., and TX 302, Mentone, Texas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Loving County Courthouse is the first permanent courthouse in the county, built in 1935 to replace a temporary courthouse from 1931. It was constructed during an oil boom that briefly increased the county's population. The courthouse has played a minimal role in judicial proceedings due to the county's small population, but it remains a key symbol of local government.

Major_Events.Description: Oilman Norman C. Hill was sentenced to four years in prison for stealing $4,000 worth of piping.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its historical significance and added to the National Register of Historic Places on May 10, 2006.
Two jury trials were held, requiring the county's entire adult population for the jury panel. Establishing a jury was challenging due to Texas laws prohibiting relatives from serving together.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Evan J. Wood in the Moderne style, the two-story courthouse is the tallest building in Loving County.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a symbol of county government and the only significant government building in Loving County, the least populous county in the U.S. It reflects the region's brief oil boom and ongoing administrative role.
world knowledge.Details: As of summer 2011, a new courthouse annex was nearing completion across Collins Street. The single-story Southwestern-style building was expected to house the sheriff's and county clerk's offices, with floor space roughly equal to the main courthouse.

world knowledge.Name: Notley Abbey
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Notley Abbey was an Augustinian abbey founded in the 12th century by Walter Giffard, the second Earl of Buckingham, and his wife, Ermengard. It was one of the largest and richest Augustinian monasteries in the Oxford region. The abbey was dissolved by Henry VIII in 1538 and later regenerated in 1890. It was purchased by Laurence Olivier and Vivien Leigh in 1944 and later by Bijou Wedding Venues in 2006.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by Walter Giffard, the second Earl of Buckingham, and his wife, Ermengard, to house Augustinian canons.
Notley Abbey was dissolved by Henry VIII and given as an enfeoffment to John London.
A team from Oxford excavated the abbey, establishing a layout and timeline of the building's construction.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Laurence Olivier and Vivien Leigh
Major_Events.Description: The couple purchased the remains of the abbey after their home was destroyed in a bomb raid during the war.
Mark and Jo Cutmore-Scott purchased the abbey as part of their company, Bijou Wedding Venues, to host weddings and events.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally built in Romanesque style in the 12th century, with additions in Early English or transitional style around 1200. The eastern wing was extended in the early 14th century, and the central crossing was rebuilt in the perpendicular style in the 15th century. The main residence is L-shaped and two-storied, with Tudor-style windows added during the 1890 regeneration.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Notley Abbey is culturally significant as one of the largest and richest Augustinian monasteries in the Oxford region. It was visited by notable figures such as Henry IV and Henry V and was owned by celebrities Laurence Olivier and Vivien Leigh. Today, it serves as a wedding venue, preserving its historical and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a monastic house for Augustinian canons, now a wedding venue.
world knowledge.Details: Notley Abbey possessed several pieces of land, including Lower Winchendon, Chilton, Princes Risborough, and Stragglethorpe in Lincolnshire. The abbey's primary source of income came from tithes from appropriated churches. In 1944, Laurence Olivier and Vivien Leigh purchased the remains of the abbey and held parties there. The abbey was also used for the shooting of several films. Today, it is owned by Bijou Wedding Venues and hosts private weddings and events.

world knowledge.Name: Gouraya National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The national park of Gouraya is one of the coastal national parks of Algeria. It became an Algerian National Park in 1984 and was recognized as a biosphere reserve by UNESCO in 2004. The park is named after the Gouraya Mountain located within its boundaries.

Major_Events.Description: The park was officially designated as an Algerian National Park.
The park was recognized as a biosphere reserve by UNESCO.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its natural beauty, diverse flora and fauna, and its recognition as a UNESCO biosphere reserve. It is also home to a permanent Berber population.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located on a calcaro-dolomitic ground and includes many beaches and cliffs, making it a popular swimming destination. It is home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, including Barbary macaques and jackals. The park has a permanent population of 1,655 inhabitants across 13 villages of Berber origin.

world knowledge.Name: Căldărușani Monastery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Căldărușani Monastery is a Romanian Orthodox monastery established in 1638 by Matei Basarab, a prominent Wallachian ruler. It was built on the site of an older wooden skete, evidencing monastic activity at this location prior to its official founding. The monastery became known for its scriptorium and played a pivotal role in the development of the Romanian literary language.

Major_Events.Description: Căldărușani Monastery was established by Matei Basarab, a prominent Wallachian ruler.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architectural style of the monastery is predominantly Neoclassical, with elements that reflect the traditional Orthodox ecclesiastical design. The complex includes several buildings, notably the main church dedicated to Saint Demetrius, and smaller churches dedicated to other saints.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Căldărușani Monastery has been a significant center for Orthodox spirituality and Romanian culture. It is known for its educational and cultural contributions, including its scriptorium, printing press, and religious art. The monastery's art collection includes works by Nicolae Grigorescu and other Romanian artists, reflecting the rich spiritual and artistic traditions of the Romanian Orthodox Church.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery complex is listed as a historic monument and includes several significant buildings and a rich collection of Romanian art. It is located by the Căldărușani Lake and is surrounded by lush greenery.

world knowledge.Name: Henan Museum
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 100,000 square feet (total area), 78,000 square feet (floor space)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Henan Museum was established in June 1927 under the proposal of General Feng Yuxiang. It initially operated in Kaifeng before moving to Zhengzhou in 1961. The museum underwent significant development from 1930 to 1937, amassing substantial collections. During the Sino-Japanese War, key relics were moved to Chongqing, and some were later transported to Taiwan. After the war, the museum resumed operations and was remodeled in 1991, reopening in 1999 under its current name.

Major_Events.Description: Founded in June 1927 under the proposal of General Feng Yuxiang, initially located in Kaifeng.
The museum moved from Kaifeng to Zhengzhou following the relocation of the provincial capital.
The museum was remodeled and officially reopened to the public under the name 'Henan Museum'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building is pyramid-shaped, located at the center of the grounds. The design incorporates the artistic style and culture of central China, with additional buildings including a storeroom, electrified education building, combined service building, office building, and training building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Henan Museum is one of the oldest museums in China, housing over 130,000 cultural relics, including prehistoric artifacts, Shang and Zhou dynasty bronze vessels, and pottery and porcelain wares. It plays a crucial role in preserving and showcasing the history and culture of Henan Province and China.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: History and archaeology museum, featuring exhibitions of cultural relics, natural history specimens, and educational programs.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features advanced facilities such as an audio tour, magnified video-tape playing, computer consultation, and interactive facilities. It also has high-tech systems for security, building management, audio-visual education, service information, and cultural relics preservation.

world knowledge.Name: Bongoyo Island
world knowledge.Address: Kinondoni District, Dar es Salaam Region, Tanzania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bongoyo Island is a protected, uninhabited island under the Dar es Salaam Marine Reserve with the IUCN category II. It is the most frequently visited of the four islands of the Dar es Salaam Marine Reserve System (DMRS) and a popular daytrip for both tourists and Tanzanian residents alike for snorkelling and sunbathing. The island is home to some of Tanzania's largest specimens of endangered coconut crabs.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island has a very rocky shore and only two beaches. The entire island (apart from the beaches) is covered in dense forest and has a few walking trails. In the middle of the island, one finds the remains of a German colonial building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bongoyo Island is culturally significant as a popular tourist destination and a protected marine reserve, contributing to the conservation of marine biodiversity and providing recreational activities for visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The island is situated 2.5 km north of Dar es Salaam in the Indian Ocean. It is reachable by a 30-minute boat ride from the mainland, with the point of departure for most visitors being 'The Slipways' hotel complex on the western side of the Msasani Peninsula.

world knowledge.Name: Queen Emma Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 167 m (548 feet), Width: 9.80 m (32 feet)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Queen Emma Bridge is a pontoon bridge across St. Anna Bay on Curaçao island in the Dutch Caribbean. It connects the Punda and Otrobanda quarters of the capital city, Willemstad. It was named after Emma of Waldeck and Pyrmont, who was queen consort of the Netherlands during its construction. The bridge is hinged and opens regularly to enable the passage of oceangoing vessels.

Major_Events.Description: To celebrate the royal visit of Queen Juliana and Prince Bernhard.
Complete renovation of the bridge.
Complete renovation of the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Pontoon bridge design with a hinge mechanism that allows it to swing open for oceangoing vessels. Equipped with two diesel engines turning propellers mounted perpendicular to the length of the bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Locally known as the "Swinging Old Lady" due to its swinging mechanism. It is a significant landmark in Willemstad, connecting the Punda and Otrobanda quarters and facilitating pedestrian movement across St. Anna Bay.
world knowledge.Details: Originally a toll bridge from 1901-1934, individuals without shoes were permitted to cross the bridge without paying the toll. When the bridge swings open, two ferries provide free passage for pedestrians. Motor vehicle traffic ceased in 1974 when all such traffic was diverted to the newly opened Queen Juliana Bridge.

world knowledge.Name: WhiteWater World
world knowledge.Address: Dreamworld, Coomera, Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: WhiteWater World is a seasonal water park opened on 8 December 2006, owned and operated by Coast Entertainment. It was developed as a sister park to Dreamworld, with an initial investment of A$56 million. The park features Australian beach culture-themed attractions and has expanded over the years with new rides and facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened three weeks ahead of schedule with ten attractions, including The Green Room, The Rip, Super Tubes Hydrocoaster, and The BRO.
The Wedgie, Australia's first looping water slide, opened on 1 April 2011, featuring a trap-door release and a near-vertical 17-metre drop.
A $7-million investment was announced for a new waterslide complex named 'Fully 6', featuring six new body slides and multi-coloured natural light effects.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features four water slide towers with attractions grouped by thrill level, a large wave pool, and separate children's areas. The attractions are themed around Australian beach culture and include ProSlide and WhiteWater West designs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: WhiteWater World is recognized as one of the world's most water-efficient parks due to its sustainable water management and environmentally friendly technology. It offers a unique blend of thrilling and family-friendly attractions, contributing to its popularity as a tourist destination.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Water park offering recreational and entertainment activities.
world knowledge.Details: WhiteWater World operates seasonally from September to April, closing on Christmas Day and Anzac Day. The park includes 16 water slides, 2 pools, and 2 children's areas. Notable attractions include The Green Room, The Rip, The BRO, and The Wedgie. The park also features dining outlets, retail stores, and an events venue called The Shell.

world knowledge.Name: Jesse Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named New Academic Hall, it was completed in 1895 after the original Academic Hall burned down in 1892. Renamed in 1922 to honor retiring University President Richard Henry Jesse. The building has survived tornado damage in 1932, storm damage in 1982, and an arson fire in 1991.

Major_Events.Description: Academic Hall burned down, leaving only the six columns that now stand in the center of Francis Quadrangle. The fire was ignited by an electric chandelier during a debate.
A tornado ripped through Columbia and caused significant damage to the building.
A severe storm damaged Jesse Hall, resulting in renovations that included a new ball and new slate on the dome, tempered windows, reinforced beams, and a new paint job.
An arson fire caused $350,000-$500,000 in damage to the building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Morris Frederick Bell and fashioned after Richard M. Upjohn's Connecticut State House of 1872-1878. The dome stands 180 feet (55 m) tall, taller than the building it stands on. Originally featured a winged sphere atop the dome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the most photographic landmarks in Missouri and the most prominent contributing structure to the David R. Francis Quadrangle National Register of Historic Places District. The dome is illuminated at night, with color changes for special events like Homecoming and Engineers' Week.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Main administration building for the University of Missouri, housing the office of the chancellor, university registrar, graduate school, admissions, and financial aid. Also serves as a venue for graduations, university functions, and the University Concert Series.
world knowledge.Details: The building was completed at a cost of $250,000. The dome was first lit in October 1987 to commemorate MU's sesquicentennial celebration. Jesse Auditorium, originally seating 1,200, was renovated in 1953 and now seats 1,732. The novel 'Stoner' by John Williams (1965) features a slightly fictionalized version of Jesse Hall.

world knowledge.Name: Magritte Museum
world knowledge.Address: Place Royale / Koningsplein 1, 1000 City of Brussels , Brussels-Capital Region, Belgium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Magritte Museum is dedicated to the work of the Belgian surrealist artist René Magritte. It is housed in the Hôtel du Lotto, an 18th-century neoclassical townhouse on the Place Royale/Koningsplein. The building has served various purposes over the centuries, including as a hotel and a jewellery store, before being transformed into a museum. The Place Royale and its surrounding buildings bear witness to Belgium's independence, and the site was where the enthronement ceremony of Prince Leopold of Saxe-Coburg took place in 1831. The building was definitively protected from modification in 1951 and became part of the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium in 1962. The Magritte Museum was inaugurated on 20 May 2009 and opened to the public on 2 June 2009.

Major_Events.Event: Enthronement ceremony of Prince Leopold of Saxe-Coburg
Major_Events.Description: The enthronement ceremony of Prince Leopold of Saxe-Coburg, King of the Belgians, took place on 21 July 1831.

The façades and porticoes lining the Place Royale were recognised for their architectural and historical interest and were definitively protected from any modification by a classification order on the Belgian Heritage List.
The Magritte Museum was inaugurated on 20 May 2009 and opened to the public on 2 June 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a five-level neoclassical building dating from the late 18th century, known as the Hôtel du Lotto. The building features neoclassical architectural style with façades and porticoes lining the Place Royale.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Magritte Museum is culturally significant as it houses the largest collection of works by René Magritte, one of the most renowned surrealist artists. The museum also occupies a historically important building in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, which is tied to Belgium's independence and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The Magritte Museum displays some 200 original Magritte paintings, drawings, and sculptures, including notable works like 'The Return', 'Scheherazade', and 'The Empire of Light'. The museum also includes Magritte's experiments with photography from 1920 onwards and the short surrealist films he made from 1956 onwards. The works on display come mainly from donations and bequests from the artist's widow, Georgette Magritte, and his primary collector, Irène Hamoir Scutenaire.

world knowledge.Name: Núi Cốc Reservoir
world knowledge.Address: Approximately 25 kilometres west of the city of Thái Nguyên in Thái Nguyên Province, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Núi Cốc Reservoir is an artificial lake created on the Công River, a tributary of the Cầu River. It is associated with a local legend about 'Coc', a boy from a poor family, and 'Cong', a girl from a rich mandarin family. The lake and surrounding area are named after this legend.

Major_Events.Description: An ecotourism park with musical fountains was developed in March 2007, featuring a main fountain that raises to a height of over 40 metres, accompanied by music played on the khen, a local musical instrument.
A small hydropower plant with 3 units of 630 KW capacity each was commissioned in January 2010, generating about 2 MWh of energy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lake is an artificial reservoir with a storage capacity of 175 million cubic metres. It features 89 islets, a water park, an artificial dinosaur park, and an artificial cave system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lake is culturally significant due to the legend of Coc and Cong, which is deeply rooted in local folklore. It is also a popular tourist attraction with various recreational and cultural displays.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary functions of the reservoir include irrigation, aquaculture, hydropower generation, and recreational activities.
world knowledge.Details: The lake precinct is home to 40 species of birds and 15 species of mammals. It also features a breeding centre for Ardeola bacchus and Egretta spp. The lake waters are used for irrigation, aquaculture, and hydropower generation.

world knowledge.Name: Teylers Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Teylers Museum, established in 1778, was founded as a center for contemporary art and science by Pieter Teyler van der Hulst, a wealthy cloth merchant and banker. The museum's historic center is the neoclassical Oval Room, built in 1784. Teyler's will stipulated that his collection and fortune be used to establish a foundation for the promotion of religion, art, and science. The museum was designed to be a 'temple for the muses of the arts and sciences,' serving as a meeting place for scholars and housing various collections.

Major_Events.Description: The neoclassical Oval Room was opened for research, study, and public demonstrations.
A new entrance on the Spaarne was designed by Christian Ulrich, marking the museum's first centenary.
A large new wing was added to the museum, designed by Hubert-Jan Henket.

Major_Events.Event: Nomination for UNESCO World Heritage Site status
Major_Events.Description: The museum was nominated for UNESCO World Heritage Site status based on its history as a public knowledge institute.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum features a neoclassical design, with the historic Oval Room as its centerpiece. Over the centuries, it has been expanded with additional galleries, including the Numismatic Cabinet, Painting Galleries, and a new wing added in 1996. The museum's design reflects the Enlightenment ideals of independent discovery and education.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Teylers Museum is culturally significant as one of the oldest museums in the Netherlands and a pioneering institution for the promotion of art, science, and education. It represents the Enlightenment ideals of independent discovery and public access to knowledge. The museum's collections and archives have remained intact since its founding, making it a valuable resource for researchers and the public.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Art, natural history, and science museum
world knowledge.Details: The museum's holdings include fossils, minerals, scientific instruments, medals, coins, and paintings. It features works by Michelangelo, Raphael, Rembrandt, and other notable artists. The museum is open six days a week and is a member of the Museumvereniging (Museum Association).

world knowledge.Name: Zahedan Airport
world knowledge.Address: 6 kilometers northeast of the city of Zahedan, Sistan and Baluchestan Province, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zahedan Airport is an international airport located in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, southern Iran. It serves as a hub for both civilian and military operations, connecting different parts of Iran and countries south of the Persian Gulf.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zahedan Airport is significant for its role in connecting the remote Sistan and Baluchestan Province with other parts of Iran and international destinations, facilitating economic and cultural exchanges.

Details.Operator: Iran Airports Company, Islamic Republic of Iran Army Aviation, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Iranian Police Aviation

world knowledge.Name: University of Hradec Králové
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Hradec Králové (UHK) is a public university founded on 21 June 2000, tracing its roots back to 1959. It evolved from the Institute of Education in Hradec Králové, established in 1959 to train teachers for elementary education. In 1964, it became the Faculty of Education Hradec Králové. After the Velvet Revolution in 1989, the Pedagogical University of Hradec Králové was established in 1992. The university expanded with new faculties over the years, adopting its current name in 2000.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Institute of Education
Major_Events.Description: The Institute of Education in Hradec Králové was established to train teachers for elementary education.
The institution evolved into the Faculty of Education Hradec Králové.
The Pedagogical University of Hradec Králové was officially established.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to University of Hradec Králové
Major_Events.Description: The university adopted the name University of Hradec Králové.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of Faculty of Informatics and Management building
Major_Events.Description: The building of the Faculty of Informatics and Management was completed, costing 360 million CZK.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of Faculty of Science building
Major_Events.Description: The Faculty of Science building was completed after 21 months of construction, costing approximately 450 million CZK.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's Common Education Building was awarded 'Building of Year' in 1998. The Faculty of Informatics and Management building was completed in 2008, and the Faculty of Science building in 2016. The Rector's Sceptre, designed by Jan Hásek, features a linden leaf shape with a golden ball and a silver lion symbolizing the city of Hradec Králové.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Hradec Králové is culturally significant as a center for higher education in the Czech Republic, contributing to the development of education and research. Its architectural achievements and historical evolution reflect the country's educational reforms and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The university currently consists of four faculties: the Faculty of Education, Faculty of Informatics and Management, Philosophical Faculty, and Faculty of Science, all based on one campus known as Na Soutoku. The university has two halls of residence, the Palach Halls of Residence and Vít Nejedlý Halls of Residence, with a capacity of around 900 beds. The Rector's Sceptre, designed by Jan Hásek, was given to the university by the City of Hradec Králové. The Statutory emblem features a central crowned Czech lion holding a large letter 'G', representing part of the City of Hradec Králové emblem.

world knowledge.Name: Disney's Animal Kingdom
world knowledge.Address: Walt Disney World, Bay Lake, Florida, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Disney's Animal Kingdom Theme Park is a zoological theme park at Walt Disney World in Bay Lake, Florida, near Orlando. Owned and operated by The Walt Disney Company through its Experiences division, it is the largest theme park in the world. The park opened on Earth Day, April 22, 1998, and was the fourth theme park built at the resort. The park is dedicated and themed around natural environment and animal conservation, a philosophy once pioneered by Walt Disney.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened to the public on April 22, 1998, with several marketing events, including a two-hour prime time special about the making of Animal Kingdom on ABC.

Major_Events.Event: Pandora - The World of Avatar Opening
Major_Events.Description: A major expansion to the park, Pandora - The World of Avatar, opened to the public on May 27, 2017, as a joint venture with director James Cameron and his production company, Lightstorm Entertainment.
The park was closed from March 16 to July 11, 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Florida.

On September 9, 2023, it was announced that DinoLand U.S.A. would be replaced with a new area inspired by the American tropics, and It's Tough to Be a Bug! would be succeeded by a Zootopia-themed film in the Tree of Life Theater.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of real and artificial landscapes, including the Tree of Life, a 145-foot-tall (44 m), 50-foot-wide (15 m) artificial baobab tree. Special designs and provisions were incorporated throughout the park to protect the animals' welfare. Many buildings contain thatched roofs assembled by Zulu workers from South Africa, and parts of the park were designed to have an aged appearance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Disney's Animal Kingdom is the most-visited zoo in the world as of 2019. The park is accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums and the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums, indicating they have met or exceeded the standards in animal welfare, education, conservation, and research. The park is dedicated to natural environment and animal conservation, a philosophy once pioneered by Walt Disney.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Zoological theme park dedicated to animal conservation and education, combined with traditional theme park entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: Disney's Animal Kingdom is divided into seven themed areas: Oasis, Discovery Island, Pandora – The World of Avatar, Africa, Rafiki's Planet Watch, Asia, and DinoLand U.S.A. The park is home to approximately 2000 animals representing around 200 species. The park does not allow plastic straws, lids, or balloons to be used to protect the animals' habitats. The park is engaged in research and conservation efforts involving its animal species, with several successful births of elephants, giraffes, and white rhinoceros since its opening.

world knowledge.Name: Focke Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Focke Museum was formed in 1924 by the merger of a museum of industry and commerce and the previous historical museum. It is named after Johann Focke, a Bremen privy councillor. The museum complex includes buildings dating from the 16th to the 19th centuries and a main building that opened in 1964.

Major_Events.Description: The museum of industry and commerce and the historical museum merged to form the Focke Museum.
The main building of the Focke Museum, designed in classic modern style, was dedicated.
An extension known as the Schaumagazin was added to the main building, providing additional display space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main building is designed in classic modern style with ample use of glass. The extension is a cube clad in copper, connected to the main building by a glass-walled passageway. The complex includes historic buildings from the 16th to the 19th centuries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Focke Museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the history and art of Bremen, including regional crafts, pre-historic items, and industrial artifacts. It is also notable for its architectural design and the integration of historic buildings into the museum complex.
world knowledge.Details: The museum complex includes several historic buildings such as Haus Riensberg, the Eichenhof, Haus Mittlesbüren, and a barn from Tarmstedt. The parkland features sculptures, sundials, water features, and a botanical collection. The museum also manages the Oberneuland Mill, a protected landmark with exhibits on bread-making.

world knowledge.Name: Ankasa Conservation Area
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ankasa Conservation Area is located in southwestern Ghana, approximately 365 kilometers west of Accra, near the border with Côte d'Ivoire. It encompasses the Nini Suhien National Park to the north and the Ankasa Forest Reserve to the south. The park is approximately 500 square kilometers and consists largely of tropical evergreen rainforest. It is the only wildlife protected area in Ghana located in the wet evergreen tropical high rainforest belt.

Major_Events.Description: The Ankasa reserve, along with the Nini-Sushien National Park, has been designated an Important Bird Area (IBA) by BirdLife International because it supports significant populations of many bird species.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The area includes tropical evergreen rainforest, rivers with rapids and waterfalls, and basic camping facilities with shelters, toilets, and running water.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ankasa Conservation Area is significant for its rich biodiversity, including over 800 vascular plant species, 639 butterfly species, and more than 190 bird species. It is also home to various animal species such as elephants, bongos, leopards, western chimpanzees, and Diana monkeys.
world knowledge.Details: The forest has the most biological diversity of any in Ghana. Apart from the forest reserve, which was selectively logged until 1976, the rest of the protected area is almost intact.

world knowledge.Name: Cadore Viaduct
world knowledge.Address: Perarolo di Cadore, Province of Belluno, Veneto, north-east Italy
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 535 m (1,755 ft), Width: 13.3 m (44 ft), Height: 184 m (604 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cadore Viaduct is a road bridge in Italy, built by longitudinal launching by Mazzi. It opened in 1985 and is part of the SS51 Strada statale di Alemagana, maintained by ANAS. The route joins to become part of European route E66, reaching Austria near Innichen in South Tyrol.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed and opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Design: Rigid strut frame bridge, Material: Reinforced concrete and steel, Longest span: 255 m (837 ft), Main span held up by two 85m steel struts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important infrastructure in the southern Alps, facilitating transportation between Italy and Austria. It is part of the European route E66 and passes near notable landmarks like Tre Cime di Lavaredo.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Road bridge carrying SS51 Alemagna State Road
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is north of the northern terminus of the Autostrada A27 at Ponte nelle Alpi. The Calalzo–Padua railway passes under the bridge, and the former Dolomites Railway passed nearby to the north, around one mile away. The Slovenian capital of Ljubljana is eighty miles to the east.

world knowledge.Name: Bois de Vincennes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bois de Vincennes was part of the ancient forest surrounding the Roman town of Lutetia. It became a royal hunting ground in the 12th century and was later transformed into a public park by Emperor Napoleon III. The park has served various roles, including military training grounds and host to colonial expositions.

Major_Events.Description: Emperor Napoleon III and Georges-Eugène Haussmann transformed the area into a public park.
Showcased cultures and products of French colonies, featuring villages from different parts of the French Empire.
Hosted most events, including cycling at the newly built Velodrome.
The Dutch spy was executed by firing squad in the moat of the Château de Vincennes.
A larger showcase of French colonies, featuring pavilions, villages, and spectacular fountains.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features an English landscape garden with four lakes, a zoo, an arboretum, a botanical garden, a hippodrome, a velodrome, and picturesque architecture including the Temple of Love and a Swiss chalet. The Château de Vincennes includes a medieval donjon and La-Sainte Chapelle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bois de Vincennes is the largest public park in Paris, offering recreational space and historical landmarks. It reflects 19th-century landscape design and has hosted significant cultural and sporting events, including colonial expositions and the Olympics.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes attractions like Lac Daumesnil, Lac des Minimes, and a velodrome. It has been associated with prostitution rings related to human trafficking in recent years. The park's water features are fed from the Seine, and it contains an arboretum with 2000 trees.

world knowledge.Name: Oriel Park
world knowledge.Address: Oriel Park, Carrickmacross Road, Dundalk, County Louth, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oriel Park was established in 1919 on land known as 'Casey’s Field', owned by the Casey family. It was initially a simple field with rudimentary facilities, later developed into a football stadium. The club named it 'Oriel Park' after the medieval Irish kingdom of Airgíalla. Over the years, the stadium underwent several renovations and expansions, including major redevelopment in 1966–67 and the construction of the Youth Development Centre in 2010. In 2022, the ground was temporarily renamed 'Casey's Field' in honor of Des Casey, the club's Honorary President.

Major_Events.Description: European Cup Winners' Cup second round tie, setting the attendance record of 18,000.
European tie leading to increased capacity with extra terracing.
Domestic match where temporary seating increased capacity to approximately 5,000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Oriel Park features two covered stands, one on either side of the pitch. The main stand includes dressing rooms, club bars, offices, and a club shop. The 'Shed' stand houses the commentary box and principal camera position. The stadium has an all-weather pitch, installed in 2017, and includes uncovered seated terracing and standing areas. The Youth Development Centre (YDC), built in 2010, is located behind the 'Shed' stand.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oriel Park is culturally significant as the long-standing home ground of Dundalk F.C., a prominent Irish football club. It represents the club's history and community ties, having been leased from the Casey Family Trust since 1936. The stadium has hosted numerous important matches, including European competitions, and is a focal point for local football culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium and training facility for Dundalk F.C., also available for social events and bookings.
world knowledge.Details: Oriel Park has a capacity of 4,500 for domestic matches and 3,100 for European matches. It is serviced by Dundalk-Clarke railway station and local bus routes. The stadium has undergone various legal disputes over lease and ownership, notably resolved in 2017. Facilities include 'The Lilywhite Lounge' public bar and the Enda McGuill Suite for members.

world knowledge.Name: Oceans of Fun
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oceans of Fun is a tropically themed water park that opened on May 31, 1982, in Kansas City, Missouri, to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the adjacent Worlds of Fun amusement park. It was the largest water park in the state of Missouri at the time of its opening and is owned and operated by Six Flags Entertainment Corporation.

Major_Events.Description: Oceans of Fun announced the largest-ever expansion, including a new slide complex 65 feet tall with 6 new slides. The water park was completely renovated, and construction began in 2012.
Oceans of Fun added swan boats to Buccaneer Bay and Splash Island.

Major_Events.Event: Closure of Diamond Head and announcement of Riptide Raceway
Major_Events.Description: The park announced that Diamond Head would be closed at the end of the season to make way for Riptide Raceway, a mat racing slide that would be the world's longest of its kind at 486 feet long.
The park implemented a chaperone policy requiring guests ages 15 or younger to be accompanied by a chaperone at least 21 years old.
A 14-year-old boy was submerged for sixteen minutes in the wave pool and later declared brain dead. His organs were donated, and the park settled a wrongful death lawsuit for an unspecified sum.
A 6-year-old girl was pulled from Coconut Cove and later died from her injuries. The Coconut Cove section was shut down after the incident.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tropically themed water park with various water slides, wave pools, and other aquatic attractions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oceans of Fun is a significant recreational landmark in Missouri, offering family-friendly entertainment and water-based activities. It is part of the larger Worlds of Fun amusement park complex and is owned by Six Flags, a major player in the amusement park industry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Water park providing recreational and entertainment activities.

world knowledge.Name: Theatre in Dlouhá Street
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The theatre was originally constructed in 1929 in Old Town Prague with art deco designs by Emil Sušický and Pavlo Sydow. It was designed for operetta performances and opened on December 4, 1929. It operated until its closure by Nazi authorities in 1944. After the war, it reopened as a Soviet political education center for children. Following the Velvet Revolution, it reopened under its current program in 1996. In 2002, floods from the Vltava river damaged the theatre, requiring reconstruction and modernization, though some original features from the 1930s remain.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened with operetta performances.
The theatre was closed during World War II.

Major_Events.Event: Reopening as Soviet Political Education Center
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was repurposed for political education for children after the war.
The theatre reopened under its current program after the Velvet Revolution.
Floods from the Vltava river damaged the theatre, leading to reconstruction and modernization.
The theatre hosted its first performance with English subtitles.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art deco design by Emil Sušický and Pavlo Sydow. Some original features from the 1930s remain despite modernization.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is a significant cultural venue in Prague, known for its variety of performances and contributions to children's theatre through the Child in Dlouhá festival. It has been nominated several times for the Alfréd Radok Award and has won in the category Performance of the Year.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Repertoire theatre hosting a variety of performances, including children's theatre.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre is headed by Daniela Šálková, with key directors Hana Burešová and Jan Borna. Prominent actors include Miroslav Táborský, Jan Vondráček, Vlastimil Zavřel, Jaroslava Pokorná, and Klára Sedláčková. The theatre hosts the Child in Dlouhá / Dítě v Dlouhé festival focused on children's theatre. It was nominated several times for the Alfréd Radok Award in the category Theatre of the Year, with Grabbe's Don Juan and Faust and Sestra Úzkost winning Performance of the Year.

world knowledge.Name: Gjøvik Olympic Cavern Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gjøvik Olympic Cavern Hall is an ice hockey rink located within a mountain hall in Gjøvik, Norway. Opened in 1993, it was built for the 1994 Winter Olympics, where it hosted 16 ice hockey matches. The structure is the world's largest cavern hall for public use. The idea to build an underground ice rink came from Consulting Engineer Jan A. Rygh in 1988. The first drafts were made on a napkin in a restaurant. Construction started on 1 April 1991, and the hall opened on 6 May 1993.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted 16 ice hockey matches, including two quarter-finals and one semi-final.

Major_Events.Event: 1995 World Short Track Speed Skating Championships
Major_Events.Description: Hosted the championship, setting six world records during the event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hall is designed as a multi-use venue with a main hall, swimming pool, cafeteria, and telecommunications facility. The main hall cavern is 61 meters wide, 91 meters long, and 25 meters high. The design reflects Scandinavian folklore, with shotcrete on the walls, high-contrast lighting, and red as the main color. The hall is designed as an amphitheater with close contact between spectators and athletes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The hall is culturally significant as it reflects Norwegian culture and character, playing on Scandinavian folklore and the tradition of building mountain cavern halls in Norway. It is also the world's largest cavern hall for public use.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ice hockey rink and multi-use event venue
world knowledge.Details: The hall is located just west of the town center of Gjøvik, with the main hall 120 meters into the mountain. It is covered by 25 to 55 meters of bedrock. The facility also includes a 25-meter swimming pool and telecommunications installations. The hall duplicates as a civil defense facility, designed to withstand nuclear, conventional, and gas attacks. It has hosted Gjøvik Hockey since 1993 and various other sports and events.

world knowledge.Name: University of Tabriz
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,445 acres (2.3 sq mi; 584.8 ha) land and 80 acres (32 ha) buildings and offices
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Tabriz, founded in 1947, is the second oldest university in Iran. It started its activities under the name of the University of Azarabadegan with Faculties of Medicine, Agriculture, and Pedagogy in 1946. It was renamed as the University of Tabriz following the 1979 Islamic Revolution. In 1985, Tabriz University of Medical Sciences was separated from the University of Tabriz and continued its activities independently.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Tabriz was founded as the University of Azarabadegan.
Following the Islamic Revolution, the University of Azarabadegan was renamed as the University of Tabriz.
Tabriz University of Medical Sciences was separated from the University of Tabriz.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Tabriz is one of the top five high-ranked universities in Iran and is a center of excellence in higher education and research. It has a significant role in the educational and cultural development of the northwest region of Iran.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Tabriz is known for its strict academic standards and low GPA system, particularly in engineering fields. It has several research centers and is recognized as a Center of Excellence in multiple fields. The university has international affiliations and has signed 90 MOUs with different universities worldwide.

world knowledge.Name: Black Hills National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Forest headquarters in Custer, South Dakota; local ranger district offices in Custer, Rapid City, and Spearfish in South Dakota, and in Sundance, Wyoming
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Created as the Black Hills Forest Reserve by U.S. President Grover Cleveland after devastating wildfires in 1893. The Lakota people referred to the area as 'pahá sápa' (black hills), and the region was sacred to indigenous tribes. The forest was later redesignated as a National Forest in 1907 under the Forest Service.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Black Hills Forest Reserve
Major_Events.Description: Established by U.S. President Grover Cleveland to preserve the forest after wildfires.
Expanded the boundaries of the forest reserve and acknowledged preservation decrees.
Provided a 63-foot white spruce as the Capitol Christmas Tree.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Predominantly ponderosa pine forest with hardwoods like aspen, bur oak, and birch. Includes grassland prairie at lower elevations and mountainous terrain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sacred to indigenous peoples for vision quests, hunting, and trade. The forest preserves a significant ecological and cultural landscape in the Black Hills region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: National Forest managed for conservation, recreation, and sustainable resource use.
world knowledge.Details: The forest includes Black Elk Peak, the tallest mountain in South Dakota. It is home to diverse wildlife such as elk, moose, deer, black bears, cougars, and numerous bird species. Offers 30 campgrounds, 11 reservoirs for fishing, 450 miles of hiking trails, and over 5,000 miles of forest roads. Adjacent to national monuments like Jewel Cave and Mount Rushmore.

world knowledge.Name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bibi-Heybat Mosque is a mosque located in Baku, Azerbaijan. The existing structure, built in the 1990s, is a recreation of the mosque with the same name built in the 13th century by Shirvanshah Farrukhzad II Ibn Ahsitan II, which was completely destroyed by the Bolsheviks in 1934. The mosque includes the tomb of Ukeyma Khanum, a descendant of the Islamic Prophet Muhammad, and is a spiritual center for the Muslims of the region and one of the major monuments of Islamic architecture in Azerbaijan.

Major_Events.Description: The mosque was blown up in 1934 as a result of the Soviet anti-religious campaign.
After Azerbaijan gained its independence, President Heydar Aliyev ordered the construction of a new building for Bibi-Heybat Mosque at the same place where it was destroyed.
A dedication ceremony, attended by President Heydar Aliyev, was held on July 11, 1997.
The inauguration of the new mosque was held in May 1999.
A monument to Shirvanshakh Farruhzade and Heydar Aliyev were unveiled in 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The modern restored mosque is a classic example of the Shirvan architectural school. The mosque has three domes, which have kept the traditional corrugated galvanised iron shape of the old mosque, and two minarets. The domes are decorated with the green and turquoise mirrors, which are bordered with gilded inscriptions from Qur'an. The men's praying room is located on the south side of the complex, while women - on the north side. Between them is the mausoleum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bibi-Heybat Mosque is a spiritual center for the Muslims of the region and one of the major monuments of Islamic architecture in Azerbaijan. It includes the tomb of Ukeyma Khanum, a descendant of the Islamic Prophet Muhammad.
world knowledge.Details: The mosque was designed by Azerbaijani architect Sanan Sultanov. The builders used local varieties of limestone such as Gulbaht. On the inside the walls of marble carvings with calligraphic inscriptions such as muhaggah, Suls, Jami-Suls, Kufic, kufi-shatrandzh, musalsag, sofa and tugra. Also widely used such ornamental compositions as islimi, shukyufa, Bandy-Rumi, zendzhiri Selcuk (Seljuk chain), Shamsi, Jafari and Achma-yumma.

world knowledge.Name: Alvão Natural Park
world knowledge.Area: Vila Real, Douro & Tâmega, Norte, Portugal
world knowledge.Address: Municipalities of Mondim de Basto and Vila Real, Tâmega and Douro Subregions, northern Portugal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Alvão Natural Park is a protected area founded in 1983, located in northern Portugal. It was created under decree-law 237/83 and later integrated into the European Union's Natura 2000 designation to support conservation efforts. The park is characterized by its diverse geography, including the highest peak, Caravelas, and the lowest point along the Rio Olo.

Major_Events.Description: The park was established on June 8, 1983, under decree-law 237/83 as a classified natural park.
On August 28, 1997, the park was integrated into the European Union's Natura 2000 designation to support the conservation of habitats and species under threat within the EU.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The traditional architecture of the region is a distinct mountain style, especially in Ermelo and Lamas de Olo, influenced by the sociological and artisanal nature of the landscape, or in Fervença, influenced by agrarian necessity along a terraced landscape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Alvão Natural Park is culturally significant due to its diverse flora and fauna, traditional architecture, and its role in the conservation of natural habitats and species within the European Union.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of natural habitats and species
world knowledge.Details: The park has a temperate Atlantic climate with Mediterranean characteristics, characterized by heavy precipitation in winter and dry, warm summers. It features diverse vegetation, including oak trees, Common hazel, holly, chestnut, and laurel, and is home to various wildlife species such as Eurasian otters, Golden eagles, Wild boar, Roe deer, and Iberian emerald lizards.

world knowledge.Name: Panepirotan National Athletic Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Panepirotiko Stadio of Ioannina, commonly known as Panepirotiko Stadio, is a sports venue opened in 2002. It has been used by PAS Giannina for training sessions since 2004 and serves as the home stadium for AE Giannena and AO Velissarios FC.

Major_Events.Description: Konstantinos Argyros held a concert at the facility on 20 July 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The venue features a grass surface and includes a scoreboard. It has a seating capacity of 2,050 and parking for 500 seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Panepirotan National Athletic Center is a significant sports venue in Ioannina, serving as a training and match facility for various local sports clubs, including PAS Giannina, AE Giannena, and AO Velissarios FC.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports venue for training and matches
world knowledge.Details: The facility is owned by the General Secretariat of Sports and operated by PAS Giannina, AE Giannena, and AO Velissarios FC. Many sports clubs in the city use its facilities for training or matches.

world knowledge.Name: National Theatre, Nigeria
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Four times bigger than the Palace of Culture and Sports in Varna, Bulgaria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Theatre, Nigeria is the primary centre for the performing arts in Nigeria. It shares the same architectural design as the Palace of Culture and Sports in Varna, Bulgaria. Its construction was completed in 1976 in preparation for the Festival of Arts and Culture (FESTAC) in 1977. The construction was started by the military regime of General Yakubu Gowon and completed during the military regime of Olusegun Obasanjo.

Major_Events.Description: The National Theatre was completed in preparation for this festival.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming in honor of Prof. Wole Soyinka
Major_Events.Description: President Bola Tinubu renamed the National Arts Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, in honor of Nobel Laureate, Prof. Wole Soyinka.
President Olusegun Obasanjo announced plans to privatise the National Theatre, sparking controversy.
It was reported that the National Theatre has been sold to a Dubai-based conglomerate for the sum of 31.5 billion naira, and that the building will be converted to a duty-free shopping centre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The exterior was designed, shaped, and built to look like a military hat. It originally has a 5,000-seat Main Hall with a collapsible stage, and two capacity cinema halls, all equipped with facilities for simultaneous translation of 8 languages.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theatre is the primary centre for the performing arts in Nigeria and holds significant cultural importance as a venue for major cultural events and festivals.
world knowledge.Details: The National Theatre was designed and constructed by Bulgarian construction company (Techno Exporstroy). Alhaji Sule Katagum was a co-owner and also their chairman. It resembles the Palace of Culture and Sports in Varna, Bulgaria (completed in 1968).

world knowledge.Name: North Shore Music Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: North Shore Music Theatre is the largest operating regional theater in New England. It was founded in 1955 by theater producer Steven Slane, bandleader Ruby Newman, and attorney C. Henry Glovsky. Originally planned as a complex with a restaurant, bowling alley, swimming pool, and condominium, it eventually became a nonprofit theater in 1961. The theater has undergone several renovations, including capacity changes and recovery from a 2005 fire. After financial struggles and closure in 2009, it was acquired by Bill Hanney and reopened in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre suffered from a serious fire and slipped into debt.
The theatre failed to raise funds to continue operations, leading to cancellation of the season and closure. Over 4,000 prepaid ticket holders were not refunded.
Bill Hanney acquired the theatre and reopened it under new ownership.
The theatre closed temporarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic and reopened in 2021.
The theatre received criticism for casting non-Latino actors in lead roles for 'Evita', sparking debate about representation in theater.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Theatre-in-the-round, one of the few remaining in the United States. Originally had 1,000 seats, expanded to 1,800, and later reduced to 1,500 after renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest non-profit theater in New England, known for producing world premieres like the Tony Award-winning 'Memphis' and regional premieres of popular musicals. It also hosts an annual production of 'A Christmas Carol' and a Youth Performance Academy for child actors.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venue hosting concerts, musicals, and theatrical productions.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre continues to thrive under owner Bill Hanney, producing a five-show subscription series annually. It faced financial challenges due to management decisions like canceling 'A Christmas Carol' for 'High School Musical 2'. The 2025 season includes productions like 'Waitress', 'The Wizard of Oz', 'Grease', 'Rent', and 'The Cher Show'.

world knowledge.Name: Musée de la Romanité
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Musée de la Romanité is an archeological museum in the French city of Nîmes, opened on 2 June 2018. The museum's collection covers several periods of the history of Nîmes.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened to the public on 2 June 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by the French–Brazilian architect Elizabeth de Portzamparc, the museum is located in front of the Arena of Nîmes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum showcases the rich history of Nîmes, including its Roman heritage, making it an important cultural and educational site.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's website is museedelaromanite.fr.

world knowledge.Name: Bandra–Worli Sea Link
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 5.6 kilometres (3.5 mi) long, 2 x 20 metres (66 ft) wide, 126 metres (413 ft) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bandra–Worli Sea Link, officially known as Rajiv Gandhi Sea Link, is a 5.6 km long, 8-lane wide cable-stayed bridge that links Bandra in the Western Suburbs of Mumbai with Worli in South Mumbai. It was planned as part of the proposed Western Freeway to link the Western Suburbs to Nariman Point in Mumbai's main business district. The project was commissioned by the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) and built by the Hindustan Construction Company. The bridge was opened to the public on 24 March 2010.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the first four lanes
Major_Events.Description: The first four of the eight lanes of the bridge were opened to the public on 30 June 2009.
All eight lanes became operational on 24 March 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge features cable-stayed main spans and concrete-steel precast segment viaducts at either end. It includes pre-stressed concrete-steel viaducts, twin continuous concrete box girder bridge sections, and diamond-shaped 128 metres (420 ft) high concrete towers. The bridge was designed to withstand earthquakes measuring up to 7.0 on the Richter scale.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bandra–Worli Sea Link is a significant infrastructure project in Mumbai, reducing travel time between Bandra and Worli during peak hours from 20–30 minutes to 10 minutes. It is the second longest sea bridge in India and represents a major engineering achievement in the country.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation bridge connecting Bandra and Worli in Mumbai
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has a toll system with varying rates for different vehicle types. It is equipped with an electronic toll collection system, intelligent bridge management system (IBS), and mobile explosive scanners for security. The bridge is not accessible to pedestrians, two-wheeled, or three-wheeled vehicles, except on special occasions like World Environment Day.

world knowledge.Name: Jarrett Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jarrett Park is a multi-use stadium in Montego Bay, Jamaica, purchased by the St James Parish Council in 1957 to provide a permanent recreational venue for the residents. It hosted regional first-class cricket matches from 1965 to 2001 and the first Women's Test match in 1976. The stadium has been used by various football teams, including Montego Bay United FC and Wadadah FC, and has hosted international football matches.

Major_Events.Description: The first Women's Test match played by the West Indies Women against Australia Women.
Jarrett Park was selected as one of the host venues for the 2008 Caribbean Cup.
Jarrett Park was selected as one of the host venues for the 2011 CONCACAF U-17 Championship.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jarrett Park is culturally significant as a historic sports venue in Montego Bay, hosting cricket and football matches, including the first Women's Test match in the West Indies. It has been a hub for local and international sports events, contributing to the development of sports in Jamaica.
world knowledge.Details: Jarrett Park has a capacity of 4,000 people and has been used by various football teams, including Montego Bay United FC, Wadadah FC, and the Jamaica national football team. It hosted the 2008 Caribbean Cup and the 2011 CONCACAF U-17 Championship.

world knowledge.Name: Alexandra Bridge (Trans-Canada)
world knowledge.Area: Lower Fraser Canyon, southwestern British Columbia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 487 metres (1,598 ft) in length, 12.2 metres (40 ft) in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alexandra Bridge is a steel arch bridge across the Fraser River, replacing earlier ferries and bridges in the vicinity. Construction faced challenges like unexpected ground conditions, leading to design adjustments. Upon completion in 1962, it was the second-longest bridge of its type globally and remains the longest in the Fraser Canyon. It significantly improved transportation by allowing heavier loads and longer trailers, reducing reliance on the Hope-Princeton route. Later, the Coquihalla Highway reduced its traffic. Major rehabilitation and seismic retrofitting were completed in 2015-2018 and 2019.

Major_Events.Description: General Construction Co was awarded the substructure contract, but work was delayed due to unexpected ground conditions.
A.I.M. Steel was awarded the contract for the steel superstructure.
The steelwork was completed, making it the second-longest bridge of its type in the world at the time.
Highways Minister Phil Gaglardi officially opened the bridge, which cost $4 million and allowed heavier trucks to use the route.
Four aluminum fish sculptures were unveiled at the bridge ends, and a cairn commemorating the Royal Engineers' contribution to the Cariboo Road was placed.
The completion of the Coquihalla Highway reduced traffic on the Alexandra Bridge.
A $22.2 million project rehabilitated the deck, widened shoulders, and upgraded railings. Additional work was done in 2019 due to corrosion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel arch bridge with a 257-metre (843 ft) main span and steel girder approach spans with concrete decks. The bridge is 487 metres (1,598 ft) long and 12.2 metres (40 ft) wide.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a key transportation link in British Columbia, historically significant for enabling heavier loads and longer trailers. It also commemorates the Royal Engineers' role in building the Cariboo Road.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (carries Highway 1 across the Fraser River)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge crosses the Canadian National Railway (CN), Fraser River, and Canadian Pacific Railway (CP). It was preceded by the Second Alexandra Bridge and is owned by the British Columbia Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure.

world knowledge.Name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip garden, previously Model Floriculture Center, is a tulip garden in Srinagar, in the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It is the largest tulip garden in Asia. The garden was opened in 2007 with the aim to boost floriculture and tourism in the Kashmir Valley. It was formerly known as Siraj Bagh.

Major_Events.Description: An annual Spring festival to increase tourism by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. The festival showcases a variety of flowers in the garden.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built on a sloping ground in a terraced fashion consisting of seven terraces with an overview of the Dal Lake.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The garden is culturally significant as it boosts floriculture and tourism in the Kashmir Valley and is the largest tulip garden in Asia.
world knowledge.Details: The garden is home to around 73 varieties of tulips and 46 varieties of other flowers, including hyacinths, daffodils, and ranunculus, brought from Holland. In 2023, the garden received a record number of visitors, with 365,000 tourists visiting between March and April, including 3,000 foreign tourists.

world knowledge.Name: Hobart Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hobart Town Hall is a landmark sandstone building serving as the seat of the City of Hobart local government. Construction began in 1864, with the foundation stone laid on April 14, declared a public holiday and celebrated by a parade. It was completed in September 1866, marked by another public holiday and a gala ball. The building originally housed council chambers, police offices, the municipal court, and the State Library of Tasmania, which remained in use for nearly fifty years. The site was previously occupied by the former government house, demolished upon completion of the present government house.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid on April 14, 1864, declared a public holiday and celebrated by a parade.
The town hall was completed in September 1866, celebrated by a public holiday and a gala ball.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Town Hall organ
Major_Events.Description: The City of Hobart organ, built by J. W. Walker of London, was opened on March 17, 1870, in a concert by F. A. Packer, Albert Alexander RAM, and John Packer.
The portico was declared unsafe, and major restoration work was undertaken.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Renaissance style, inspired by the Palazzo Farnese in Rome. The building features an ornate Victorian auditorium and a notable organ.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hobart Town Hall is culturally significant as a historical government building and public auditorium. It houses the second finest organ in Australia and features well-known chandeliers installed by former Lord Mayor Doone Kennedy. The building is also open to periodic public tours.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serves as the seat of the City of Hobart local government, hosting council meetings and acting as a public auditorium.
world knowledge.Details: The Town Hall organ has been in use since 1870. The building's chandeliers were installed in the ballroom by former Lord Mayor Doone Kennedy. The Town Hall is open to periodic public tours, showcasing its ornate Victorian auditorium and historic organ.

world knowledge.Name: Itacoatiara
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Itacoatiara is one of the 48 official neighborhoods in Niterói, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The beach is known for its natural beauty and recreational activities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Itacoatiara is culturally significant for its natural beauty, recreational opportunities, and recognition as part of the Serra da Tiririca State Park, a UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve.
world knowledge.Details: Itacoatiara beach features fine golden sands and bright blue (sometimes green) water. It is dangerous for casual swimmers but ideal for water sports like surfing, bodysurfing, and bodyboarding. The beach has three main breaks: Costão, Meio, and Pampo. There is also a wave-sheltered small beach called Prainha. The area is popular among climbers, offering various climbing styles such as bouldering, traditional climbing, sport climbing, and aid climbing. The Serra da Tiririca State Park, located there, is a UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve.

world knowledge.Name: Hastings Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hastings Town Hall was built in 1881 to replace an earlier town hall from 1823. It served as the meeting place for Hastings Borough Council and became the headquarters of the county borough in 1888. The town hall was later refurbished and re-opened as the local register office in 2016.

Major_Events.Description: Officially opened by the mayor, Councillor W. F. Revill, on 7 September 1881.

Major_Events.Event: Receiving the colours of the 5th Battalion, Royal Sussex Regiment
Major_Events.Description: The mayor, Councillor E. Armitage Hocking, received the colours before the unit was deployed to France at the start of the First World War.
The mayor, Councillor William Perrins, set out from the town hall to meet King George V on his visit to the town near the end of the war.

Major_Events.Event: Refurbishment and re-opening as register office
Major_Events.Description: Following an extensive refurbishment, the town hall was re-opened as the local register office in March 2016.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the English Gothic style by architect Henry Ward. Features a symmetrical main frontage with three bays, an arched doorway, a stone balcony, and tall stained glass lancet windows with bar tracery. Four carved panels on the eastern side depict historical scenes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a Grade II listed building and has served as a significant civic and cultural hub in Hastings. Its architectural and historical importance is recognized, and it has played a role in key local and national events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as the meeting place for Hastings Borough Council and later as the local register office.
world knowledge.Details: The town hall was the subject of a design competition won by local architect Henry Ward. It features a council chamber and mayor's parlour internally. The borough council later moved to modern municipal offices, but the town hall remains an important landmark.

world knowledge.Name: Toronto Pearson International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Toronto Pearson International Airport, originally opened in 1938 as Malton Airport, is the largest and busiest airport in Canada. It was renamed in 1984 to honor Lester B. Pearson, the 14th Prime Minister of Canada and Nobel Peace Prize laureate. The airport has grown significantly since its inception, becoming a primary hub for Air Canada and other major airlines.

Major_Events.Description: The first scheduled passenger flight at Malton Airport was a Trans-Canada Air Lines DC-3 that landed on August 29, 1939.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Lester B. Pearson International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially renamed Lester B. Pearson International Airport on January 2, 1984, in honor of Toronto-born Lester B. Pearson, the 14th prime minister of Canada and recipient of the 1957 Nobel Peace Prize.

Major_Events.Event: Greater Toronto Airports Authority Assumes Management
Major_Events.Description: The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) assumed management, operation, and control of the airport in 1996.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two main passenger terminals, Terminal 1 and Terminal 3, designed by various architectural firms. Terminal 1 is a 346,000-square-metre facility with 58 gates, while Terminal 3 is a 178,000-square-metre facility with 46 gates. The airport also has an Infield Concourse that serves as an extension of Terminal 3.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Toronto Pearson International Airport is a vital transportation hub for Canada, serving as the primary global hub for Air Canada and a significant hub for other airlines. It plays a crucial role in connecting Canada to the rest of the world and is a symbol of the country's growth and international presence.
world knowledge.Details: Toronto Pearson International Airport handles approximately half of all the international air cargo in Canada. It has five runways, three aligned east–west and two north–south, and extensive cargo facilities. The airport also features a Central De-icing Facility, the largest in the world, and maintains a robust fire and emergency service. Additionally, it has a significant cultural impact, having been featured in music videos and songs by notable artists like Rush and Sloan.

world knowledge.Name: Sofia Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sofia Zoo in Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria, was founded by royal decree on 1 May 1888, and is the oldest and largest zoological garden in Southeast Europe. Initially located in the park of the former royal palace, it moved to a new 36-hectare site in 1982. The zoo has grown significantly over the years, housing a diverse range of species and becoming a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) in April 2023.

Major_Events.Description: Sofia Zoo was founded by royal decree on 1 May 1888.
The zoo moved from its original location in the city center to a new 36-hectare site about 4.5 kilometres south of Sofia.
Sofia Zoo became a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA), gaining new opportunities for animal conservation, breeding, and professional development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo features various enclosures and buildings designed to house different species, including a stone building for bears, a pool for pelicans, and pavilions for primates and predators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sofia Zoo is the oldest and largest zoological garden in Southeast Europe, playing a significant role in animal conservation and public education. Its membership in EAZA further enhances its importance in global conservation efforts.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo houses approximately 2,460 animals representing 312 species, including white rhinos, hippopotamus, elephants, zebras, and various primates and birds. It also has a veterinary clinic accessible to the public. In 2009, the zoo faced a heating crisis due to a gas supply dispute, requiring portable heaters to protect the animals.

world knowledge.Name: Chuvash National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chuvash National Museum in Cheboksary, Russia, is a cultural, educational, and research center of the Chuvash Republic. Founded in 1921, it is the largest repository of natural, historical, cultural, and theological artefacts of the Chuvash people and other ethnic groups.
