world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses 160,000 pieces related to the natural, historical, cultural, and theological aspects of the Chuvash people and other ethnic groups. It also includes the Society for the Study of the Native Land, which introduces the life and culture of the Chuvash people to the population of the Republic.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has four branches and houses the Society for the Study of the Native Land, an association of ethnographers. It is accessible via trolleybus and has a website at http://www.chnm.ru.

world knowledge.Name: Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof
world knowledge.Physical_Area: About two and a half times bigger than the old premises
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Early 16th century (original building), 1923 (partial demolition and replacement), 2010-2012 (renovation and extension)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum is housed in the Spanish Government building, one of the oldest non-religious buildings in Maastricht. Originally part of the ecclesiastical territory of the chapter of the church of Saint Servatius, it was rebuilt and enlarged in the early 16th century. The building acquired its name during the period when Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma and Governor of the Netherlands, signed the declaration that made William the Silent an outlaw. The building was restored several times and has served various purposes, including a print shop and a local history museum. Since 1973, it has housed the Wagner-De Wit art collection and, since 2019, it has been dedicated exclusively to photography.

Major_Events.Description: The facade on the ground floor was largely blind, except for an arched gateway. Late Gothic windows were added on the first floor.
Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma and Governor of the Netherlands, signed the declaration that made William the Silent an outlaw.
Part of the building was demolished and replaced in 1923 by a building now used as a bank.
The Wagner-De Wit collection was displayed in the building, then called Museum Spaans Gouvernement.
The museum closed for renovations and extensions, including a partial restoration of the facade and the addition of a neighbouring building.
The enlarged museum re-opened with rooms dedicated to important figures from Maastricht history.
The museum announced it would only show photography and changed its name to Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features late Gothic windows, an arcade in Liège Renaissance style, and a colonnade frieze with sculpted medallions. The facade was originally largely blind, with an arched gateway leading into the courtyard. The interior has been altered several times, with extra windows added on the ground floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is one of the oldest non-religious buildings in Maastricht and has historical significance as the Spanish Government building. It houses a museum that has evolved from displaying a diverse art collection to focusing exclusively on photography, reflecting the cultural and historical evolution of the city.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is a private institution that receives no government funding. It was sponsored by TEFAF in 2011, leading to the renaming of one of the period rooms as TEFAF-zaal. The museum's original collection included Dutch and Flemish paintings, sculpture, tapestries, furniture, glass, crystal objects, antique coins, and artifacts from the Far East. Since 2019, the museum has focused exclusively on photography and does not have a photography collection of its own, relying on loans for exhibitions.

world knowledge.Name: Benue State University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Benue State University is a state-owned university in Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria. It was founded in 1992 and initially served 306 students with 149 faculty. The university was established by the state government to augment the specialized academic offerings of the University of Agriculture, Makurdi. In 1991, the state government formed a 13-member steering committee to plan for and obtain approval for the university. The university began offering classes for the 1992/1993 school year in four colleges: Arts, Education, Sciences, and Social Science.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded and began offering classes in four colleges: Arts, Education, Sciences, and Social Science.
A new Central Library Complex, constructed with a grant from TETFund and designed to house 45,000 books and 3,000 students, was commissioned.
The university's Department of Mass Communication started a radio station, BSU FM on 89.9 MHz.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Benue State University is culturally significant as it serves as a major educational institution in Benue State, Nigeria, offering a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs. It plays a crucial role in the educational development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: Benue State University has eight faculties: Faculty of Administration, Faculty of Arts And Humanities, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Engineering/Tech/Env, Faculty of Law & Legal Studies, Faculty of Med/Pharm/Health Sciences, and Faculty of Social Sciences. The university's library complex, University Library and Information Services (ULIS), comprises units in various colleges and faculties. Athletic activities are handled by the Sports Unit, and the university participates in the Nigerian University Games Association. Facilities include a football field, basketball court, badminton court, volleyball court, and two tennis courts.

world knowledge.Name: Governor Francisco Gabrielli International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 8 kilometres northeast of the centre of Mendoza, Argentina
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Governor Francisco Gabrielli International Airport, also known as El Plumerillo International Airport, serves Mendoza, Argentina. It is operated by Aeropuertos Argentina 2000 and includes the El Plumerillo Military Air Base on its southern section.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is significant for its dual role as a public and military airport, serving the Mendoza region and hosting the 4th Air Brigade.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a concrete runway and served 1,813,623 passengers. It is located at an elevation of 2,310 ft (704 m) above mean sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Braga City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Braga Town Hall, located in Sé parish in Braga, Portugal, is the headquarters of the Câmara Municipal, the city's local government. It was built in the 18th century to replace previous Renaissance-style buildings, on the proposal of Archbishop D. José de Bragança, brother of João V of Portugal. Designed by architect André Soares, it is considered one of the most notable examples of Baroque architecture in the Iberian Peninsula. Construction began in 1753 and was completed in 1865. It was classified as a Property of Public Interest in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The construction of the Braga Town Hall, which began in 1753, was finally completed.

Major_Events.Event: Classification as Property of Public Interest
Major_Events.Description: The Braga Town Hall was classified as a Property of Public Interest.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a notable example of Baroque architecture, featuring two floors with eight large windows each. The facade is symmetrical, with a central section that includes a door-niche-pediment flanked by strong pilasters. The pediment highlights several cartouches and the main entrance, topped by an exquisitely carved niche housing the image of Nossa Senhora do Livramento.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Braga Town Hall is culturally significant as a prime example of Baroque architecture in the Iberian Peninsula and as a symbol of local governance in Braga.
world knowledge.Details: The building was constructed on the site of the old bullring. The image of Nossa Senhora do Livramento, originally from the old Town Hall, was moved to the Cathedral and later placed in the current Town Hall.

world knowledge.Name: King Power Mahanakhon
world knowledge.Address: 114 Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: King Power Mahanakhon, formerly known as MahaNakhon, is a mixed-use skyscraper in Bangkok, Thailand. It was opened in December 2016 and recognized as the tallest building in Thailand in 2016. The building was purchased by King Power group in April 2018, resulting in the name change from MahaNakhon to King Power Mahanakhon.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of King Power Mahanakhon began on 20 June 2011.
The building was completed in April 2016 and officially opened on 29 August 2016.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as tallest building in Thailand
Major_Events.Description: On 4 May 2016, the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) recognized King Power Mahanakhon as the tallest building in Thailand.
The building was purchased by King Power group in April 2018, resulting in the name change from MahaNakhon to King Power Mahanakhon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features an unconventional appearance with a glass curtain walled square tower and a cuboid-surfaced helix cut into the side of the building. The exterior has a pixelated ribbon that swirls around, creating balconies with city views. The glass walls are divided horizontally and vertically, giving the building a 'pixelated' and 'unfinished' appearance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: King Power Mahanakhon is culturally significant as it was the tallest building in Thailand upon its completion and represents modern architectural innovation in Bangkok. It also houses luxury residences and retail spaces, contributing to the city's skyline and economy.
world knowledge.Details: The building includes 10,000 square meters of retail space, 209 residences serviced by Ritz-Carlton, and The Standard Bangkok Mahanakhon hotel with 155 rooms. It also features a rooftop observation deck. The project has won several awards, including Best Luxury Condo Development 2014 and Best Thailand Development 2014.

world knowledge.Name: Takoradi Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Takoradi Airport, located in Sekondi-Takoradi, Ghana, served as a major refueling stop during World War II for the United States Army Air Forces Air Transport Command Trans-Africa Ferry Route. It was also used as a Royal Air Force station known as "RAF Takoradi," where crated aircraft shipped over the Atlantic were assembled before being flown to operational areas in North Africa. The airport played a significant role in the Lend-Lease aircraft program and was a base for 26 Squadron SAAF, which conducted anti-submarine and convoy protection patrols.

Major_Events.Description: Used as a major refueling stop for the Trans-Africa Ferry Route and as a Royal Air Force station for assembling crated aircraft.
26 Squadron SAAF based in Takoradi, flying Vickers Wellington bombers on anti-submarine and convoy protection patrols.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Runway 03/21: 1,751 meters (5,745 feet) with asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Takoradi Airport is historically significant for its role in World War II as a key transportation and assembly hub for aircraft and supplies. It also serves as a primary shore base for helicopter transfers to offshore oil platforms in Ghana's Jubilee Oil Field.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Military airport and primary shore base for offshore oil platform helicopter transfers.
world knowledge.Details: Takoradi Airport is the fourth busiest airport in Ghana, with 123,930 passengers in 2022. It is operated by the Ghana Air Force, which bases its 1 Squadron (Harbin Z-9H) and Flight Training School (Diamond DA-42) here.

world knowledge.Name: Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Between Paramaribo and Meerzorg, Commewijne District, Suriname
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge, also known as the Suriname Bridge and locally as Bosje Brug, is a bridge over the Suriname River. It is part of the East-West Link and was named after former president Jules Wijdenbosch. Constructed by Dutch constructor Ballast-Nedam, the bridge was opened on 20 May 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on 20 May 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge has two lanes and a total length of 1,504 metres, with the longest span being 155 metres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant infrastructure project in Suriname, facilitating transportation and economic development between Paramaribo and Meerzorg.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also known locally as Bosje Brug and was constructed by Dutch constructor Ballast-Nedam.

world knowledge.Name: Ancona Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ancona Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Cyriacus, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Ancona, central Italy. It stands on the site of the former acropolis of the Greek city, the Guasco hill. Excavations in 2016 indicated an Italic temple from the 3rd century BC, with a Christian church built on top in the 6th century. The current structure was built between 995 and 1015, enlarged in the late 12th to early 13th centuries, and restored in 1883. It suffered damage during World War I, World War II, and an earthquake in 1972, followed by restorations each time.

Major_Events.Description: A new church was built, keeping the original walls.
The church was enlarged.
The church was restored.
The church was damaged by bombings and subsequently rebuilt.
The church was damaged by bombings and subsequently rebuilt.
The church was damaged by an earthquake and subsequently restored.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is an example of mixed Romanesque-Byzantine and Gothic elements. It is built in white stone from Mount Conero, with apses protruding from the transept's ends and an elevated body, featuring a dome at the crossing. The exterior surfaces are decorated with Lombard bands. The bell tower, isolated, was built above a pre-existing late 13th-century tower. The façade has a 13th-century Romanesque portal with a round arch supported by columns on lions in Veronese red marble. The dome, one of the most ancient in Italy, has an ogival shape with a dodecagonal drum and a copper cover added in the 16th century. The interior follows a Greek cross plan, with re-used antique Roman columns and Byzantine capitals. The dome has pendentives with Byzantine-style figures of praying angels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ancona Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the seat of the Archbishop of Ancona and a major religious site in central Italy. It represents a blend of Romanesque-Byzantine and Gothic architectural styles and stands on a historically rich site dating back to the 3rd century BC.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral features a Chapel of the Crucifix with sgraffito decoration from 1189, a Crypt of Tears with remains of ancient structures, and the Madonna Chapel with a venerated 17th-century image of the Madonna. The northern transept houses the sepulchre of Blessed Girolamo Ginelli, made in 1509 by Giovanni Dalmata.

world knowledge.Name: Negros Museum
world knowledge.Address: Gatuslao St., Negros Occidental Provincial Capitol Complex, Bacolod, Philippines
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Negros Museum is a privately owned provincial museum situated in the Negros Occidental Provincial Capitol Complex in Bacolod, Philippines. The structure was built in 1925 as the Provincial Agriculture Building. Opened on March 17, 1996, the museum was formerly housed in the Provincial Capitol, which was reverted for government use in 2003. Since then, the exhibits have been transferred to the former Provincial Agriculture Building. The museum is the first of its kind to not house precious archaeological artifacts, but rather was designed to display Negrense lifestyle and society, which includes old furnishings and loaned items from ancestral houses. It also includes art exhibits and expositions from different local artists and foreign artists resident in the Negros Island Region. Art training and seminars are also conducted inside the museum.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened on March 17, 1996, initially housed in the Provincial Capitol.
In 2003, the museum was relocated to the former Provincial Agriculture Building after the Provincial Capitol was reverted for government use.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical, Art Deco
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its focus on Negrense lifestyle and society, showcasing old furnishings, loaned items from ancestral houses, and art exhibits from local and foreign artists. It also serves as a venue for art training and seminars.
world knowledge.Details: Negros Museum Cafe serves the needs of museum goers and walk-in guests, situated in the West Annex of the museum. It includes a separate entrance, which includes an open-air and an in-house station occasionally used for small theater plays and art exhibitions. The museum is managed by the Negros Cultural Foundation, which pays the Provincial Government a nominal rent of ₱1 for minimum compliance under law.

world knowledge.Name: Provisional Theatre (Prague)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Provisional Theatre was erected in 1862 as a temporary home for Czech drama and opera until a permanent National Theatre could be built. It opened on 18 November 1862 and functioned for 20 years, during which time over 5,000 performances were presented. The theatre played a key role in the Czech cultural revival following the abolition of absolutism in the Habsburg Empire.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened with a performance of Vítězslav Hálek's tragic drama King Vukašín.
The first opera performed at the theatre was Cherubini's Les deux journées.
The theatre staged the premieres of four of Bedřich Smetana's operas, including The Bartered Bride.
The Provisional Theatre building was incorporated into the structure of the National Theatre.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Provisional Theatre was a cornerstone of the Czech cultural revival, providing a venue for Czech drama and opera during a period of national awakening. It premiered works by key Czech composers like Bedřich Smetana and Antonín Dvořák.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre's first principal conductor was Jan Nepomuk Maýr, later replaced by Bedřich Smetana. Smetana established an independent school attached to the theatre, which closed after his resignation due to deafness. The theatre continued to operate during the National Theatre's closure after a fire in 1881.

world knowledge.Name: Fantasy Gardens
world knowledge.Address: Corner of Steveston Highway and No. 5 Road, Richmond, British Columbia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fantasy Gardens was a former amusement park in Richmond, British Columbia, known for its medieval-style stone buildings and Biblical Gardens. It was originally part of the Art Knapp's plant store chain and later became a Christian-themed amusement park under Bill Vander Zalm's ownership. The park was sold multiple times before being redeveloped into retail and residential properties.

Major_Events.Description: Bill Vander Zalm bought the gardens and established a Christian theme for the park. His later sale of the park led to conflict of interest charges and his resignation as Premier of British Columbia.
The property was sold to Chinese-born Filipino-Taiwanese businessman Tan Yu for $16 million.
The property was sold to local developer Townline Homes, which redeveloped it into retail property named The Gardens.
Fantasy Gardens was torn down, except for the Dutch Castle, which was preserved as a community landmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park featured medieval-style stone buildings and a Dutch Castle replica of Coevorden Castle. The Biblical Gardens included religious icons and a hedge carved into the shape of a Bible.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fantasy Gardens was culturally significant as a filming location for numerous movies, TV shows, and music videos. It also had religious and historical themes, including the Biblical Gardens and the Dutch Castle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally an amusement park and plant store, later redeveloped into retail and residential properties.
world knowledge.Details: The park's miniature railroad appeared in The X-Files episode "The Calusari." The Dutch Castle was donated to Vancouver by the city of Coevorden for Expo 86 and will become a City of Richmond-owned day care center. The site was used in various TV shows and movies, including Stargate SG-1, Supernatural, and Highlander: The Series.

world knowledge.Name: Davenham Hall
world knowledge.Address: Southeast of the village of Davenham, Cheshire, England
world knowledge.Construction_Period: mid to late 18th century (possibly before 1795), with substantial additions in early 19th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Davenham Hall was built for Thomas Ravenscroft to replace a timber-framed house called Davenham Lodge. It dates from the middle or later part of the 18th century, possibly shortly before 1795 when Ravenscroft died. The house was converted into a nursing home in 1980.

Major_Events.Description: The house was converted into a nursing home.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed in stuccoed brick with a slate roof. The house has two storeys with a symmetrical entrance front of six bays. The middle two bays feature a porch with four Tuscan columns and an entablature containing a triglyph. The central bays protrude slightly forwards and contain two windows, with a pediment above them and a parapet on each side. The interior includes Grecian plasterwork, a black marble chimneypiece in the entrance hall, delicate plasterwork and a marble chimneypiece decorated with dancing figures in the drawing room, a central staircase hall lit by a central dome with fan-shaped plasterwork, a staircase with a wrought iron baluster, and a first floor landing with a screen of four Doric columns.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Davenham Hall is a designated Grade II* listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former country house, now a nursing home
world knowledge.Details: The house is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II* listed building.

world knowledge.Name: Kacchi Dargah–Bidupur Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna and Bidupur in Hajipur, Bihar, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kacchi Dargah–Bidupur Bridge is currently under construction and will span the river Ganges, connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna and Bidupur in Hajipur in the Indian state of Bihar. Upon completion in 2025, it will be the longest bridge in India.

Major_Events.Description: Chief minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the construction of the bridge in August 2015.
Concrete-laying in a well foundation started on 19 July 2017 on the Raghopur side.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge will have 6 lanes of roadway and pedestrian pathways on each side. It involves the construction of 67 well foundations in the Ganga River and 20 well foundations in the 'Diyara' area on both sides of the river.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge will provide an easy roadway link between the northern and southern parts of Bihar and will connect two major national highways, NH 31 and NH 322. It will reduce the load on Mahatma Gandhi Setu and traffic in Patna.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Roadway bridge connecting Patna and Hajipur, facilitating transportation and reducing traffic congestion.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is being constructed by a joint venture of Daewoo E&C from Korea and L&T Construction from India, with a project cost of Rs 3,115 crore. It will also require the construction of 13.24 km (8.23 mi) of approach roads on both ends of the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Kuban State University
world knowledge.Address: 149 Stavropolskaya st., Krasnodar, Russian Federation, ph. +78612199501 , Krasnodar , Russia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded on September 19, 1920, Kuban State University has trained over 100,000 specialists, including over 1,000 international students. It is a participant in the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC). The university comprises 17 faculties, 16 branches, and over 40 educational and research centers.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Youth Cultural and Leisure Center
Major_Events.Description: Founded on December 1, 1994, it has held over 400 concerts, games, exhibitions, etc.
A corruption scandal erupted around a physical education teacher.

Major_Events.Event: Criminal case against professor Mikhail Savva
Major_Events.Description: A criminal case was initiated under fraud charges, with many considering it politically motivated due to his criticism of the FSB.
A student was expelled for 'immoral behavior' related to his makeup blog, amidst pressure on anti-war students.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kuban State University is a major educational and research institution in southern Russia, contributing significantly to regional development and international academic cooperation.
world knowledge.Details: KubSU has a system of additional education and carries out research on scientific and technical programs, Russian and international projects. It maintains international relations with over 50 educational institutes worldwide and is a member of the Eurasian Association. The university's library holdings amount to about 1,100,000 editions, including rare books from the 17th to early 20th centuries.

world knowledge.Name: Palace Green
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Palace Green is an area of grass in the centre of Durham, England, flanked by Durham Cathedral and Durham Castle, which together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Initially not part of the site itself, Palace Green was added to the UNESCO site in 2008.

Major_Events.Description: During the COVID-19 Pandemic, marquees on Palace Green were used as a testing centre run by the University.
The site of a student encampment for 43 days in May and June 2024 as part of the global pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses that year.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Palace Green is culturally significant as part of the Durham Castle and Cathedral UNESCO World Heritage Site, highlighting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Palace Green is situated on top of the narrow, high peninsula formed by a sharp bend in the River Wear. It is flanked by Durham Cathedral and Durham Castle, with Durham University buildings surrounding it. It is accessed by cobbled streets and a passageway, and is sometimes used by students as a croquet lawn. 'Palace Green' is also the name of a hymn tune written by Michael Fleming.

world knowledge.Name: Somerset Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Somerset Bridge is mentioned in the acts of Bermuda's first parliament, held in St. George's on 1 August 1620. Bridges were to be constructed at Somerset, the Flatts, and Coney Island. Additionally, the road from Somerset to Warwick was to be improved, and extended to Castle Point. The bridge appears on a 1624 map of Bermuda.

Major_Events.Description: Mentioned in the acts of Bermuda's first parliament, held in St. George's on 1 August 1620.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Somerset Bridge features a 32-inch bisected plank that opens manually to allow the passage of sailboat masts. This simple yet ingenious mechanism has made Somerset Bridge a subject of fascination for visitors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Somerset Bridge is reputedly the smallest working drawbridge in the world. It is also featured on Bermuda's $20 bill, highlighting its cultural significance.
world knowledge.Details: Somerset Bridge is known for its ingenious design as the world's smallest drawbridge. It crosses a small channel connecting the Great Sound with Ely's Harbour.

world knowledge.Name: Qingdao Guoxin Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Qingdao, Shandong, People's Republic of China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Qingdao Sports Center Stadium, officially known as Qingdao Conson Stadium, was originally invested by Qingdao Etsong Tobacco Group and opened in August 1999 as Etsong Sports Center Stadium. It served as the home stadium for Qingdao Etsong Hainiu and Qingdao Hailifeng. The stadium was abandoned in 2006 due to safety problems. Qingdao Conson Development Group took over in July 2008, renamed it, and renovated it in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was renovated from March to October 2012.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Qingdao, hosting association football matches and serving as a key part of the city's sports infrastructure.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily for association football matches
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 45,000 people. It was originally named Etsong Sports Center Stadium and was later renamed to Qingdao Conson Stadium after being taken over by Qingdao Conson Development Group.

world knowledge.Name: Colby College Museum of Art
world knowledge.Address: 5600 Mayflower Hill, Waterville, Maine, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1959, the Colby College Museum of Art has grown to include five wings and nearly 8,000 works. It specializes in American and contemporary art, with additional collections of Chinese antiquities and European paintings. The museum serves as a teaching resource for Colby College and a cultural destination for Maine residents and visitors.

Major_Events.Description: A major addition designed by E. Verner Johnson and Associates.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the Paul J. Schupf Wing
Major_Events.Description: Dedicated to the works of Alex Katz.
Designed by architect Frederick Fisher, it comprises 13 galleries and 9,000 square feet of exhibition space.
A monumental three-part Corten steel sculpture installed in the Paul J. Schupf Sculpture Court.

Major_Events.Event: Installation of Sol LeWitt's Seven Walls
Major_Events.Description: A concrete structure installed on the museum's east lawn.
Peter and Paula Lunder promised their collection of over 500 works of art to the museum.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of the Alfond-Lunder Family Pavilion
Major_Events.Description: A glass pavilion that completes the museum's circuit, providing new exhibition galleries, classrooms, and more.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum comprises five wings, including the Jetté Galleries, the Davis Gallery, the Paul J. Schupf Wing, the Lunder Wing, and the Alfond-Lunder Family Pavilion. The latter is a minimalist glass pavilion with a three-story wall drawing by Sol LeWitt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is a major cultural destination in Maine, specializing in American and contemporary art. It houses significant collections, including works by Alex Katz, John Marin, and James Abbott McNeill Whistler, and serves as a teaching resource for Colby College.
world knowledge.Details: The museum collaborates with the Bowdoin College Museum of Art and is part of the Lunder Consortium for Whistler Studies. It also houses the Terry Winters Print Archive and the Skowhegan School of Art lecture archive.

world knowledge.Name: Merseyside Maritime Museum
world knowledge.Address: Warehouse block D at the Albert Dock, along with the Piermaster's House, Canning Half Tide Dock and Canning Graving Docks
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Merseyside Maritime Museum is part of National Museums Liverpool and an Anchor Point of ERIH, The European Route of Industrial Heritage. It opened for a trial season in 1980 before fully opening in 1984 and expanding in 1986. The museum's collection began in 1862 and developed over the years, with significant contributions from maritime historian Robert Gladstone.

Major_Events.Description: Partially destroyed the shipping gallery created by Robert Gladstone in 1931.
Rarely-seen items related to Titanic were exhibited to mark the 100th anniversary of its sinking.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum occupies warehouse block D at the Albert Dock, along with the Piermaster's House, Canning Half Tide Dock and Canning Graving Docks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant due to its focus on maritime history, particularly the Titanic and the British ship Lusitania, and its role as part of the European Route of Industrial Heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes the History of the Ship gallery, the Port of Liverpool gallery, and the New Shipperies Exhibition. It also houses the Archives Centre previously known as the Maritime Archives and Library.

world knowledge.Name: Zurich Airport
world knowledge.Location: Kloten, Rümlang, Oberglatt, Winkel, and Opfikon, canton of Zurich
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zurich Airport is the largest international airport in Switzerland and the principal hub of Swiss International Air Lines. It was opened on 14 June 1948, replacing the Dübendorf airfield. The airport has undergone several expansions to accommodate increasing passenger traffic and modern aviation needs.

Major_Events.Description: Zurich Airport officially opened on 14 June 1948, replacing the Dübendorf airfield as the primary commercial airport for Zurich.

On 18 February 1969, four armed members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine attacked El Al flight 432, resulting in the death of the co-pilot and the killing of one of the terrorists.
Zurich Airport completed a major expansion project in 2003, which included the construction of a new midfield terminal (Dock E) and an automated underground people mover.
In 1999, the Parliament of the canton of Zurich approved the privatization of Zurich Airport, leading to the formation of Flughafen Zürich AG.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Zurich Airport features a modern design with three airside terminals (A, B, and E) connected to a central Airside Centre. The airport has three runways, with the longest being 3,700 meters. The terminals are designed to handle both Schengen and non-Schengen flights, with separate passenger flows for arrivals and departures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zurich Airport is a key transportation hub in Switzerland, serving as the main gateway for international travel. It plays a crucial role in the country's economy and connectivity, facilitating both business and leisure travel.
world knowledge.Details: Zurich Airport is owned by Flughafen Zürich AG, a publicly traded company. The airport has three runways and three terminals, with extensive facilities including shopping malls, restaurants, and a railway station. It is a major hub for Swiss International Air Lines and serves as a base for several other airlines. The airport is continuously expanding and modernizing to meet the demands of increasing passenger traffic and technological advancements.

world knowledge.Name: Trunk Bay
world knowledge.Area: St. John, United States Virgin Islands
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Divided into two halves: main Trunk Bay beach and Burgesman Cove
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Trunk Bay is named for the Leatherback turtle, which is endemic to the USVI and are locally known as trunks. It is part of the Virgin Islands National Park.

Major_Events.Event: Voted best beach in the world
Major_Events.Description: Trunk Bay was voted best beach in the world 2024 by "The World's 50 Best Beaches".

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Trunk Bay is culturally significant as it is consistently voted one of the top beaches in the world and is part of the Virgin Islands National Park.
world knowledge.Details: Amenities include a snack bar, showers and restrooms, a lifeguard, and an underwater trail for snorkeling its coral reef. Trunk Cay, a small grass-covered islet, sits in Trunk Bay and offers underwater snorkeling trails around the cay.

world knowledge.Name: Aleppo International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The history of the airport dates back to the beginning of the 20th century during the French Mandate. In 1924, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines made their first flight from Amsterdam to Batavia, Dutch East Indies, through the airport in Aleppo. The airport was upgraded and developed over the years until 1999 when the new current terminal was inaugurated.

Major_Events.Description: The airport briefly re-opened on 22 January 2014, welcoming its first civilian flight in more than a year, carrying foreign journalists to the city.
On 17 February 2020, Syrian Transport Minister Ali Hammoud announced that the airport would resume civilian operations, with the first flight from Damascus to Aleppo scheduled for 19 February.
On 1 March 2020, the airport was targeted by Turkish drone and artillery strikes during the Operation Spring Shield.
On 15 January 2021, scheduled flights to Beirut and Erbil were resumed after a hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
On 7 March 2023, the Israeli airstrikes hit the airport, targeting alleged Iranian weapons transfers.
On 30 November 2024, the Syrian Democratic Forces took control of the airport amidst the attack on Aleppo and the subsequent withdrawal of the pro-government forces.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a modern terminal which combines modern and Islamic architecture. The total area is 38,000 square meters over four floors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aleppo International Airport serves as a key transportation hub for the region, facilitating both civilian and military operations. It has played a significant role during various conflicts, including the Syrian Civil War.
world knowledge.Details: The airport capacity is 1.7 million passengers a year. It serves as a secondary hub for Syrian Air and Cham Wings Airlines. The airport has been targeted multiple times by Israeli airstrikes, causing significant damage and temporary closures.

world knowledge.Name: Civic Theatre (Auckland)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Civic Theatre, opened on 20 December 1929, is a heritage performing-arts theatre, live-music venue, and cinema in Auckland, New Zealand. It was built by Thomas O'Brien, who introduced the atmospheric cinema style to New Zealand. The theatre underwent a major renovation in the late 1990s and reopened on its 70th birthday in 1999. It struggled during the Great Depression and faced competition in the 1990s but was saved from demolition by a public campaign and refurbished by the Auckland City Council.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened amid great fanfare but faced challenges due to the Great Depression and unpopular film choices.
The theatre underwent a two-year conservation effort and reopened on its 70th birthday.
The theatre's interiors were used in Peter Jackson's remake of King Kong, standing in for a New York theatre called The Alhambra.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Civic Theatre is an example of the atmospheric theatre style, creating the illusion of an open sky with twinkling stars. It features an Indian-inspired foyer with seated Buddhas, twisted columns, and domed ceilings. The main auditorium imitates a Moorish garden with turrets, minarets, spires, tiled roofs, and two life-sized panther statues. The architectural style is Moorish Revival.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Civic Theatre is internationally significant as the largest surviving atmospheric cinema in Australasia and the first purpose-built cinema of its kind in New Zealand. It symbolizes the progressive spirit of Auckland and has been a major cultural and entertainment hub.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts venue, live-music venue, and cinema
world knowledge.Details: The theatre was managed by Auckland Live, a business unit of Auckland Unlimited. It was designated a heritage site on 27 June 1985 with reference number 100. The Wintergarden, an underground ballroom in the Civic complex, was a major entertainment centre for American soldiers during World War II.

world knowledge.Name: Gemeenlandshuis van Rijnland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gemeenlandshuis van Rijnland is the oldest Gemeenlandshuis in the Netherlands, retaining its function until the current century. It was built to house the Hoogheemraadschap, which dates back to the 12th century when the Oude Rijn river silted shut at Katwijk. The building was purchased in 1578 and has been used for water management purposes since then. It was renovated in 1598 to match the new Leiden town hall and redecorated in the 1660s-1670s by Pieter Post. The building underwent restorations in 1882 and 1878.

Major_Events.Description: The facade was renovated to keep up with the new Leiden town hall.
The interior was redecorated according to a design by Pieter Post.
Restoration activities were conducted due to damage caused by brown paint applied in the early 19th century.
Architect Pierre Cuypers conducted another restoration of the building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features a facade renovated in 1598 to match the Leiden town hall. The interior was redesigned by Pieter Post in the 1660s-1670s. The grandeur of the building reflects the wealth of the water board at the time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gemeenlandshuis van Rijnland is one of Rijnland's most valuable buildings and represents the oldest formal method of dike management in the Netherlands. It is a symbol of the historical and ongoing efforts in water management in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally the permanent residence of the dijkgraaf (official) and meeting hall for the Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland. Currently used for meetings and special occasions by the Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland.
world knowledge.Details: The building is open to the public each year on Monument Day and is available for use for weddings. The Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland's day-to-day seat of water management is now housed on the Archimedesweg in Leiden.

world knowledge.Name: Churchill Downs
world knowledge.Address: 700 Central Avenue Louisville, Kentucky United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Churchill Downs is a horse racing complex famed for hosting the annual Kentucky Derby. It officially opened in 1875 and was named for Samuel Churchill, whose family was prominent in Kentucky for many years. The first Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks were held in the same year. The track is named for John and Henry Churchill, who leased 80 acres of land to their nephew, Colonel Meriwether Lewis Clark Jr.

Major_Events.Event: First Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks
Major_Events.Description: The first Kentucky Derby, a Thoroughbred sweepstakes and part of today's horse racing Triple Crown, and the first Kentucky Oaks were held in the same year.
The famous twin spire grandstand was commissioned.
The winner of the Derby was adorned with a garland of roses, a tradition that began in 1896.
Churchill Downs was designated a National Historic Landmark.
Churchill Downs hosted its first-ever night race with an attendance of over 27,000.
An EF2 tornado hit the Louisville area, striking the stables and chapel at Churchill Downs, at EF1 intensity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The twin spires atop the grandstands are the most recognizable architectural feature of Churchill Downs. The dirt oval main track is one mile in circumference and is 79–80 feet wide, with a 120-foot-wide section for the starting gate. A turf track, inside the main track, is 7⁄8 mile in circumference and 80-foot wide.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Churchill Downs is culturally significant as the host of the Kentucky Derby, a premier event in horse racing and part of the Triple Crown. It is also a National Historic Landmark.
world knowledge.Details: Churchill Downs has hosted the Breeders' Cup on nine occasions, most recently on November 2 and 3, 2018. The racetrack is owned and operated by Churchill Downs Incorporated. The capacity of Churchill Downs is roughly 170,000 with the infield open for the Kentucky Derby. The track has undergone several renovations, including a $121 million renovation from 2001 to 2005 and the installation of a large ultra high-definition video board in 2013.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Wutai
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Wutai, also known as Wutaishan or Mount Qingliang, is a sacred Buddhist site at the headwaters of the Qingshui in Shanxi Province, China. It is one of the Four Sacred Mountains in Chinese Buddhism and is home to over 53 sacred monasteries, including some of China's most important temples. It has been a pilgrimage site since ancient times and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: Mount Wutai was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its cultural significance and historical importance in Buddhism.
China's National Tourism Administration named Mount Wutai a AAAAA tourist attraction.
The Wutaishan Airport in nearby Dingxiang County opened in December 2015.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in World Famous Summer Mountains List
Major_Events.Description: Mount Wutai was selected into the "2020 World Famous Summer Mountains List".

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in China's Famous Summer Mountains List
Major_Events.Description: Mount Wutai was selected into the "2020 China's Famous Summer Mountains List".

Major_Events.Event: Selection as Most Beautiful Geological Relic
Major_Events.Description: The planation surface of Mount Wutai was selected into the list of the most beautiful geological relics in Shanxi Province.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mount Wutai is home to some of the oldest wooden buildings in China, including the main hall of Nanchan Temple and the East Hall of Foguang Temple, built in 782 and 857, respectively. These buildings feature traditional Chinese architectural designs studied by experts in the field.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Wutai is a sacred Buddhist site and one of the Four Sacred Mountains in Chinese Buddhism. It is the home of the Bodhisattva of wisdom, Mañjuśrī, and has been a pilgrimage destination for centuries. The mountain also has historical ties to Tibetan Buddhism and Taoism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious pilgrimage, tourism, and cultural preservation
world knowledge.Details: Mount Wutai has a subarctic climate with an average annual temperature of 2.1°C (35.8°F) and annual rainfall of 672.6 mm (26.48 in). The mountain is surrounded by a cluster of flat-topped peaks, with the north peak being the highest at 3,061 m (10,043 ft). It is also known for its unusual five-colored clouds, believed to be manifestations of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.

image_name: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve

world knowledge.Name: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
world knowledge.Area: Chugach Census Area, Copper River Census Area, Southeast Fairbanks Census Area and Yakutat City and Borough, Alaska, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve is the largest national park in the United States, covering the Wrangell Mountains and a large portion of the Saint Elias Mountains. The park has been shaped by volcanism and glaciation, with its tall mountains uplifted by plate tectonics. The area was designated as a national monument in 1978 and established as a national park and preserve in 1980 by the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act.

Major_Events.Description: President Jimmy Carter designated the area as Wrangell–St. Elias National Monument using the Antiquities Act.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as National Park and Preserve
Major_Events.Description: The Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act converted the monument to a national park and preserve.
The park was included in the Kluane / Wrangell-St. Elias / Glacier Bay / Tatshenshini-Alsek UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features vast glacial landscapes, including Malaspina Glacier (the largest piedmont glacier in North America), Hubbard Glacier (the longest tidewater glacier in Alaska), and Nabesna Glacier (the world's longest valley glacier). The park also includes volcanic peaks like Mount Wrangell and Mount Churchill.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant for its stunning natural landscapes, rich biodiversity, and historical mining sites like the Kennecott copper mines, which are a National Historic Landmark. It is also important for subsistence hunting and fishing by local communities.
world knowledge.Details: The park and preserve form the largest area managed by the National Park Service, larger than nine U.S. states. It includes 60% of the permanently ice-covered terrain in Alaska and is part of an International Biosphere Reserve. The park is accessible by highway, gravel roads, and chartered aircraft, with facilities open from May to September.

world knowledge.Name: Nanki–Shirahama Airport
world knowledge.Area: Southern part of the Kii Peninsula
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nanki–Shirahama Airport is a third class airport located in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama, Japan. It opened in April 1968 with a 1200 meter runway. Flights connecting Tokyo, Osaka (Itami) and Nagoya were opened, but subsequently the Osaka and Nagoya flights withdrew. An 1800 meter runway on the eastern adjacent land was completed on March 9, 1996 with the aim of upgrading the capability of the airport to handle jet aircraft. This runway was later extended to 2000 meters.

Major_Events.Description: The airport opened with a 1200 meter runway and flights connecting Tokyo, Osaka (Itami), and Nagoya.
An 1800 meter runway was completed to upgrade the capability of the airport to handle jet aircraft. This runway was later extended to 2000 meters.
The airport began being operated by Nanki-Shirahama Airport, Inc., a special purpose company established by Industrial Growth Platform, Inc. and others.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a 2000 meter runway with an asphalt concrete surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nanki–Shirahama Airport is the only airport in Wakayama prefecture and the southernmost airport in Honshu. It serves the southern part of the Kii Peninsula and is primarily used by tourists visiting Nanki-Shirahama Onsen and locations further south.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving the southern part of the Kii Peninsula.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is located about 65 kilometers south-southeast of the city of Wakayama, which is the administrative and economic center of the prefecture. However, Kansai International Airport, which opened in 1994 is located closer, which had resulted in Nanki-Shirahama Airport being used mostly by tourists. The airport is operated by Nanki-Shirahama Airport, Inc., a special purpose company established by Industrial Growth Platform, Inc. and others, from April 1, 2019.

world knowledge.Name: Central Park
world knowledge.Address: Between Upper West Side and Upper East Side neighborhoods of Manhattan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Central Park is the first landscaped park in the United States, designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux. It was created to provide a green space for New York City's rapidly growing population and has since become a model for urban parks worldwide. The park was built on land acquired through eminent domain, displacing communities like Seneca Village. It has undergone several periods of decline and restoration, most notably under the Central Park Conservancy since 1980.

Major_Events.Description: The first areas of Central Park opened to the public, including the Lake.
Central Park was designated a National Historic Landmark for its cultural and historical significance.
The Central Park Conservancy was established to restore and manage the park, leading to significant improvements.
Christo and Jeanne-Claude's art installation 'The Gates' was displayed in Central Park, attracting over a million visitors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Central Park features a picturesque design with rolling meadows, wooded areas, lakes, and formal landscapes. Key architectural elements include Bethesda Terrace, Bow Bridge, Belvedere Castle, and numerous bridges and arches. The park's design emphasizes natural-looking plantings and landforms, with sunken transverse roadways to minimize visual impact.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Central Park is a cultural icon of New York City and one of the most visited urban parks in the world. It serves as a recreational and cultural hub, hosting concerts, performances, and public gatherings. The park's design influenced urban planning and landscape architecture globally.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Urban park for recreation, cultural events, and nature conservation

Details.Wildlife: Central Park is home to diverse flora and fauna, including over 20,000 trees, 250 bird species, and various mammals, reptiles, and amphibians.
Details.Attractions: Key attractions include the Central Park Zoo, Wollman Rink, the Great Lawn, the Ramble, and Strawberry Fields memorial.
Details.Management: Managed by the Central Park Conservancy in partnership with NYC Parks.
Details.Transportation: Accessible via multiple subway lines and bus routes, with pedestrian and bike paths throughout the park.

world knowledge.Name: Danga Bay
world knowledge.Address: Near Istana Bukit Serene, about 7 km from Johor Bahru's city centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Danga Bay is the largest recreational park in the city of Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia. It was developed by Tan Sri Datuk Lim Kang Hoo via Ekovest Berhad.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mixed residential-commercial development with a scenic waterfront facing the Straits of Johor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Johor Bahru's first and largest mixed residential-commercial development, contributing to the city's growth and tourism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational park and mixed residential-commercial development
world knowledge.Details: Large projects have been earmarked for this area, including a new financial and commercial hub, hotels, exhibition and convention centre, marina and upmarket residential properties. It is accessible from Skudai Highway (Federal Route 1) via the Danga Bay interchange and by Causeway Link (T30, T31, T32, T33) from Johor Bahru Sentral Bus Terminal.

world knowledge.Name: Anuradhapura Museum
world knowledge.Area: Anuradhapura District, North Central Province, Sri Lanka
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anuradhapura Archaeological Museum, originally known as Puravidu Bhavana, is the oldest and largest museum under the Department of Archaeology of Sri Lanka. Established on July 7, 1947, it was founded by Dr. Senarath Paranavithana. The museum was initially housed in a part of a hospital near Sri Maha Bodiya and Ruwanwalisa in Anuradhapura. Due to lack of facilities, it was later moved to the old administration building in Anuradhapura. The establishment of the museum was delayed as the building was used to accommodate flood victims in the 1940s. With the help of Nisshanka Wijeratne, the Anuradhapura Governor at the time, the museum acquired two buildings and was officially established under the efforts of Dr. Senarath Paranavithana.

Major_Events.Description: The Anuradhapura Archaeological Museum was officially established on July 7, 1947, under the prime effort of Dr. Senarath Paranavithana.
The museum was relocated to the old administration building in Anuradhapura after the building was made available following its use as a flood relief center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the old administration building (පරණ කච්චේරි ගොඩනැගිල්ල) and an adjoining two-storey recording building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Anuradhapura Archaeological Museum is culturally significant as it houses a vast collection of antiquities from various regions of Sri Lanka, including Buddha statues, relic caskets, drawings, puppets, coins, jewelry, beads, and other miscellaneous items. It also holds the largest inscription collection in Sri Lanka and features models of significant structures like the Abhayagiri Stupa, Jantāgara, and Paṁcāvāsa building.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is located near the Ruwanwalisaya Stupa, adjacent to the Anuradhapura Presidential House. It is one of the archaeological museums of Sri Lanka and is used to exhibit antiquities found from various regions of the country.

world knowledge.Name: Đầm Sen Park
world knowledge.Area: District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Before 1975, the land was wild marshland. Between 1976 and 1978, it was drained and cultivated by the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City. By 1983, the project covered around 30 hectares and was managed by the 11th District. In 1989, operation was transferred to Phu Tho Travel Service Company.

Major_Events.Description: The land was drained and turned over to cultivation by the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City.
Management of the project was delegated from the city to the 11th District.
Operation of the project was transferred to Phu Tho Travel Service Company.
A musical water show was built at a cost of 12 billion dong, featuring a specially designed stage with water sprays, laser lights, and films projected onto a 28-meter-high screen of water.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of themed areas including an electronic games zone, folk tales theater, antique castle, square, small west lake, Nam Tu royal garden, rock garden, water palace, dancing island, sea life center, subaquatic puppet theater, ancient Giac Vien pagoda, butterfly garden, fishing area, ky long display zone, tea store, adventure games zone, swan lake, horse’s gallop lake, western flower garden, ancient Rome-themed square, cultural square, water musical scene, bowling area, sport services area, crayfish fishing lake, Thuy Ta restaurant, children's play area, picture lamps, nine fragment edge, Monorail station, and Monorail track. The park also includes a 22-meter-high rock garden with waterfalls and caves, and a 2km monorail.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Đầm Sen Park is a significant cultural and recreational site in Ho Chi Minh City, offering a wide range of attractions and activities that reflect both Vietnamese and international themes. It is unique in Vietnam for features such as its monorail, adventure boats, and the Roman square with European flowers and classical Roman-style elements.
world knowledge.Details: The tropical garden contains more than 70 species of birds and 20 species of animals. The Nam Tu royal garden features an orchidaceous garden and valuable bonsai ornamental trees. The park's adventure playgrounds and activities, including slide yard, electric cars, high-speed slide train, and water park, are popular with teenagers. The musical water show, built in 2005, is based on a similar display in Sentosa Island, Singapore.

image_name: South African National Museum of Military History

world knowledge.Name: South African National Museum of Military History
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The South African National Museum of Military History in Johannesburg was officially opened by Prime Minister Jan Smuts on 29 August 1947 to preserve the history of South Africa's involvement in the Second World War. In 1975, the museum was renamed from the South African National War Museum and its function changed to include all conflicts that South Africa has been involved in. In 1999 it was amalgamated with the Pretoria-based Transvaal Museum and National Cultural History Museum to form the Northern Flagship Institution. In April 2010 Ditsong was officially renamed Ditsong Museums of South Africa and the SANMMH was renamed the Ditsong National Museum of Military History.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened by Prime Minister Jan Smuts on 29 August 1947 to preserve the history of South Africa's involvement in the Second World War.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to South African National War Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum was renamed from the South African National War Museum and its function changed to include all conflicts that South Africa has been involved in.
The museum was amalgamated with the Pretoria-based Transvaal Museum and National Cultural History Museum to form the Northern Flagship Institution.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Ditsong National Museum of Military History
Major_Events.Description: In April 2010 Ditsong was officially renamed Ditsong Museums of South Africa and the SANMMH was renamed the Ditsong National Museum of Military History.
On 30 November 1910 Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn laid a commemorative stone at the memorial.

Originally called the Rand Regiments Memorial and dedicated to British soldiers that lost their lives during the Second Boer War, it was rededicated on 10 October 1999 to all people who died during the Second Boer War and renamed the Boer War Memorial.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum includes a large memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves the history of South Africa's involvement in various conflicts, including the Second World War and the Second Boer War. It serves as a memorial to those who lost their lives in these conflicts.
Notable_Visitors: Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
world knowledge.Details: The museum is divided into a number of areas. The website for the museum is The Ditsong National Museum of Military History.

world knowledge.Name: The Mall Nakhon Ratchasima
world knowledge.Address: Mittraphap Road, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Previously known as The Mall Korat (Nakhon Ratchasima), it opened in 2000 and is the biggest shopping center in northeastern Thailand.

Major_Events.Description: The mall underwent renovation in September 2016, expanding its total retail floor area to 350,000 m².

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the largest shopping center in northeastern Thailand, it plays a significant role in the local economy and serves as a major hub for commerce and entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The mall features over 400 stores and services, 4 floors for retail, and a 9-floor office tower. It also provides parking for 3,500 vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: Kashima Soccer Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally, the predecessor team Sumitomo Steel S.C. played at the nearby Sumitomo Steel plant's athletic grounds before the creation of the J. League. The stadium was later built and became the home of Kashima Antlers.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted three matches during the tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface, football stadium with a capacity of 40,003.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Home stadium of the Kashima Antlers, a prominent team in the J1 League, and a venue for international football events like the 2002 FIFA World Cup.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by Ibaraki Prefecture and operated by Kashima Antlers. Expanded in 2001. Accessible via JR East Kashima Line at Kashima Soccer Station.

world knowledge.Name: University of Algarve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Algarve (UAlg), founded in 1979, is a Portuguese public higher education institution located in the southernmost region of mainland Portugal, the Algarve. It has its headquarters and two out of its three campuses in Faro (Gambelas and Penha) and another campus in Portimão. The university was created by law, resulting from the union of two preexisting institutions, the University of Algarve and the Polytechnic Institute of Faro. It has around 10,000 students, 20% of whom are international, from more than 90 nationalities.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Algarve was founded on 16 January 1979 when its foundation was voted in the Portuguese Parliament.
Gomes Guerreiro was appointed as the first rector of the university.
The medical school of the University of Algarve opened its doors to its first 32 new students.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Algarve is culturally significant as it is the only Portuguese university created by law and represents a unique integration of university and polytechnic systems. It plays a crucial role in the educational and cultural development of the Algarve region.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers over 40 graduate and 68 postgraduate programs, including 52 MSc and 16 PhD programs. It has around 700 permanent teaching and research staff and a university business incubator that supports startup companies. The Student Union of the University of Algarve (AAUAlg) organizes various activities, including sports, radio, and theater. The Portimão branch offers degrees in business management, tourism, and technical specialization courses.

world knowledge.Name: Semaphore, South Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Semaphore was first surveyed in 1849 and became a signal station for ships. It grew as a seaside destination with the construction of a hotel, jetty, and railway. The area thrived with tourism, carnivals, and cultural events but declined during the Great Depression. It remains a popular residential and tourist suburb.

Major_Events.Description: An official government signal station was established to record vessel details, water depth, tides, and cargo loading in Gulf St Vincent.
The Time Ball Tower was erected adjacent to the Signal Station.
The jetty was completed, initially 652 m long, later shortened to 585 m due to storm damage.
Local governance was centralized under the Corporate Town of Semaphore.

Major_Events.Event: World War I Memorial Clock Built
Major_Events.Description: A memorial clock was constructed at the landward end of the jetty.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features historic buildings like the Semaphore Library (formerly Mechanics Institute), Time Ball Tower, and the Odeon Star cinema. The jetty and foreshore are key structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Semaphore is a historic seaside suburb with cultural events like the Kite Festival and Greek Festival. It has heritage-listed sites and is a popular tourist destination.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential suburb and tourist destination with recreational beach, cultural events, and historic landmarks.

Details.Beach: Wide, low surf, popular for swimming but not surfing. Patrolled by Semaphore Surf Life Saving Club in summer.
Details.Transport: Served by buses (157, 333, 352, 353) and nearby Glanville railway station. Cycling paths available.
Details.Education: LeFevre Primary School, LeFevre High School, Dominican Primary School, and Portside Christian College nearby.
Details.Heritage_Sites: Includes Semaphore Library, Time Ball Tower, Odeon Star cinema, and historic jetty.
Details.Parking: Limited short-stay parking on Semaphore Road, long-stay carparks along the foreshore.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Rosanbo
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 14th century (fortified castle), 16th century (Gothic manor), 18th century (extensions), end of 19th century (new suites)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Rosanbo was originally a 14th-century fortified castle built to prevent Scandinavian invaders from ascending the Bô river. It was later extended with a Gothic manor in the 16th century. In the 18th century, it was further developed by Louis Le Peletier de Keranroux, who added a gallery and other features. Additional suites were designed in the late 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: Built on a strategic headland to prevent invasions.
The château was expanded with a Gothic-style manor.
Louis Le Peletier de Keranroux added a gallery and other features, transforming the old kitchen into a dining room and creating new small rooms.
Architect Lafargue designed new suites and restored parts of the château.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Square-shaped château with a mix of medieval, Gothic, and 18th-century architectural elements. Features include a gallery, wood-panelled dining room, private bathrooms, and boudoirs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Classified as a Monument historique (Historic Monument). It was the stronghold of the Coskaër de Rosanbo and Le Peletier de Rosanbo families and represents centuries of architectural evolution.
world knowledge.Details: The name 'Rosanbo' means 'rock on the Bô' in Breton, referencing its location overlooking the Bô river valley. The château has undergone multiple phases of development and restoration.

world knowledge.Name: Free University of Berlin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Free University of Berlin was founded in West Berlin in 1948 with American support during the early Cold War period as a Western continuation of the Friedrich Wilhelm University, which faced strong communist repression in East Berlin. The university was established by students and scholars to create an institution free from political influence.

Major_Events.Event: Formation of the Free University of Berlin
Major_Events.Description: The university was founded on 4 December 1948 in response to the political repression faced by the University of Berlin in East Berlin. The foundation was supported by American authorities and aimed to provide a free academic environment.

On 26 June 1963, John F. Kennedy delivered a speech at the Free University of Berlin, where he was awarded honorary citizen status. His speech addressed the future of Berlin and Germany, emphasizing the importance of freedom.

The Free University of Berlin was one of the main centers of the German student movement in 1968, which protested against authoritarianism, the Vietnam War, and other social issues. The movement led to significant societal changes in Germany.
The Free University of Berlin was conferred the title of 'University of Excellence' under the German Universities Excellence Initiative, recognizing its research and academic achievements.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of older buildings from the Kaiser Wilhelm Society and modern structures. Notable buildings include the Henry Ford Building, the Rost- und Silberlaube complex, and the Philological Library designed by Norman Foster. The campus is designed in a suburban and urban style, inspired by American campus models.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Free University of Berlin symbolizes academic freedom and resistance to political repression. It played a crucial role during the Cold War as a Western academic institution in Berlin and continues to be a leading research university in Germany.
world knowledge.Details: The Free University of Berlin is one of Germany's elite universities, known for its research excellence and interdisciplinary focus. It offers a wide range of degree programs and has a strong international presence with over 400 partnerships worldwide. The university is part of the Berlin University Alliance and has received significant funding through the German Universities Excellence Initiative.

world knowledge.Name: Anchorage Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anchorage Museum is a large art, history, ethnography, ecology, and science museum dedicated to studying and exploring the land, peoples, art, and history of Alaska. It opened in 1968 in a 10,000-square-foot building and has since expanded to its current size. It houses a collection of 25,000 objects and 500,000 historic photographs.

Major_Events.Description: The museum opened with an exhibition of 60 borrowed Alaska paintings, a collection of 2500 historic and ethnographic objects, and a staff of two.
The museum was first accredited in 1973 and has maintained its accreditation since.
The museum became the home for the Alaska office of the Smithsonian's NMNH Arctic Studies Center, which supports the museum's mission through research, education, and exhibitions.
The museum expanded to its current size of 170,000 square feet, featuring new galleries, an expanded library/archives, and improved visitor services.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was originally designed by Mitchell/Giurgola Architects. The 2010 expansion was planned by David Chipperfield Architects Ltd., featuring a unique façade with custom insulated fritted glass. The façade includes approx. 5900 m2 of custom insulated fritted glass, specially developed for the project.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is a cultural center for the community, showcasing Alaska's history, art, and ethnography. It hosts exhibitions and programs that represent the diversity of immigrant heritages in Alaska and the Far North. It is also an active member of the University of the Arctic, promoting education and research in the Arctic region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum (art, history, ethnography, ecology, and science)
world knowledge.Details: The museum welcomes over 180,000 annual visitors and is repeatedly ranked among Alaska's top ten visitor attractions. It operates under a long-term contract with the Municipality of Anchorage and is managed by the Anchorage Museum Association. The museum's permanent exhibits include an Alaska history gallery, Alaska art galleries, the Imaginarium Discovery Center science galleries, and the Smithsonian Arctic Studies Center.

world knowledge.Name: Orhei National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Orhei National Park is the first national park in Moldova, established in 2013. It is located in the Codri, a forested and hilly region in central Moldova. The park covers about 1% of the country's total area and features diverse landscapes, including forests, valleys, and the Răut River.

Major_Events.Description: Orhei National Park was officially designated as Moldova's first national park.
The cultural and natural reserve Old Orhei within the park was nominated as a candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage Site list.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of natural landscapes, ancient archaeological sites, medieval cities, monasteries, noble estates, and other historical structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Orhei National Park is culturally significant as it preserves Moldova's natural and historical heritage, including ancient archaeological sites, medieval cities, and monasteries. It also promotes eco-tourism and environmental conservation.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes several tourist attractions such as the Trebujeni landscape reserve, the Curchi tract, the Țigănești landscape reserve, and the city of the Golden Horde Shehr al-Jedid. It also features 5 monasteries, 4 noble estates, and a small museum of folk crafts in Ivancea. Various tourist routes for motorists, cyclists, pedestrians, and climbers have been established within the park.

world knowledge.Name: Heide Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Heide Park Resort, commonly known as Heide Park, is the largest amusement park in Northern Germany. It opened on 19 August 1978 with six rides. The site originally belonged to the Heidenhof Wildlife Park, which was named after a chapel built there in 1350. The park has grown significantly since its inception, featuring various attractions and themed areas.

Major_Events.Description: Heide Park opened with six rides: the Monzapiste, the Heide Park Express, the Oldtimerrundkurs, the Floßfahrt, the Wichtelhausenbahn, and the Hochbahn.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of Statue of Liberty replica
Major_Events.Description: A 1/3 scale replica of the Statue of Liberty (35 meters tall) was inaugurated on 4 July 1986 on the 100th anniversary of the original statue.
The dolphinarium was closed after the 2008 season due to protests.
Hotel Port Royal was opened with 150 family rooms and 16 suites.
A Holiday Camp with 81 wooden houses in Caribbean style was opened, offering a total of 536 beds.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features various themed areas, including Heide-Dorf (Heath Village), a replica of typical buildings from the Lüneburg Heath, and a Dutch section with a windmill and canal. The park's mascot is a bear called Wumbo.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Heide Park is a significant cultural and recreational landmark in Germany, attracting millions of visitors annually. It is part of the British-based Merlin Entertainments, which operates 123 attractions in 24 countries.
world knowledge.Details: The park is divided into five areas and currently has about 40 rides, including thrill rides like Colossos - Kampf der Giganten and Flug der Dämonen. Halloween in October is a special event. The park also features shows, a horror maze (Krake Alive!), and go-karts (extra charge). The music played at Heide Park is a combination of commercial tracks, library music, and commissioned music.

world knowledge.Name: Noorderplantsoen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Noorderplantsoen is an urban public park in the city of Groningen in the Netherlands, situated slightly north of the city center. Its name is Dutch for northern public garden. In 1874 the Vestingswet was passed. This law allowed cities to expand outside of the city walls and fortifications. Since the fortifications were no longer in use, they were transformed into a public park. The earth ramparts were incorporated in the park architecture and the moats were turned into ponds. The shape of the park still reflects the former purpose of the area: the long but narrow park curves around the old city.

Major_Events.Description: This cultural event takes place at the end of August and is visited by over 125,000 visitors. Many theater, dance and music groups from The Netherlands and abroad perform during this 11-day festival.
This run through the park is held annually in October or early November and attracts about 500 runners. In 2007 the 50th edition of the plantsoenloop took place.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architecture is of an English garden style, characterized by meandering paths and serpentine ponds, inspired by wild nature. The park includes an Art Nouveau bandstand and a small restaurant.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park was created from former city fortifications, reflecting the historical expansion of Groningen. It serves as a significant public space for cultural and recreational activities.
