world knowledge.Details: Until the mid-90s the Noorderplantsoen was split up by a busy road, but a referendum in 1994 decided - with a narrow majority - to close this road for motorized traffic.

world knowledge.Name: Kaftanzoglio Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built with money donated by the Kaftanzoglou Foundation, in honour of Lysandros Kaftanzoglou. At the time of its opening on 27 October 1960, it was one of the highest quality stadiums in the Balkans and the largest in Greece until 1982. It has undergone renovations in 2000 and 2002–2004.

Major_Events.Description: Attendance record set with 47,458 fans present, witnessing Greece defeat Switzerland by a 4–1 score.
Milan defeated Leeds United 1–0.
Hosted the event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Georgios Pantzaris, the stadium features a hybrid grass surface and includes a scoreboard. It has a seating capacity of 27,560 after renovations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Greece, having hosted major football matches, athletics events, and being a key venue for the 2004 Summer Olympics. It is named in honor of Lysandros Kaftanzoglou.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium hosting football matches and athletics events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the home of Iraklis Thessaloniki since 1960. It has hosted the Greek national championships in 2009, athletics at the Mediterranean Games, and the European Cup in athletics. The complex has faced issues with dilapidation and dereliction post-2004 renovations.

world knowledge.Name: Heceta Head Light
world knowledge.Address: Heceta Head Lighthouse State Scenic Viewpoint, Oregon Coast, 13 miles north of Florence, and 13 miles south of Yachats
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Heceta Head Light is a lighthouse on the Oregon Coast. It is named after the Spanish explorer Bruno de Heceta. Before European exploration, it was a frequent fishing and hunting spot for the Siuslaw tribe. The lighthouse was built in 1894 and has been a significant navigational aid. It was automated in 1963 and restored in 2013 to its 1894 appearance.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was completed and first lit.
The lighthouse was automated, ending the need for keepers.
The lighthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The lighthouse underwent extensive restoration to return it to its 1894 appearance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Conical tower attached to a workroom, made of brick/stuccoed construction, 56 feet (17 m) tall. Features a first-order Fresnel lens. Queen Anne–style keepers' house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is the strongest light on the Oregon Coast and is significant for its architectural and engineering contributions. It is also a part of the Siuslaw tribe's traditional lands and has historical importance due to its role in navigation and exploration.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is maintained by the Oregon Parks and Recreation Department. The assistant lighthouse keepers' house operates as a bed-and-breakfast inn managed by the U.S. Forest Service. The site was originally part of a larger parcel of land purchased by white settlers in 1888. The lighthouse's lens system was made by Chance Brothers and used a Fresnel lens that operated into the 21st century.

world knowledge.Name: Neanderthal Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Neanderthal Museum, established in 1996, is located at the site of the first Neanderthal man discovery in the Neandertal, Germany. It features exhibits centered on human evolution and includes an archaeological park, a Stone Age workshop, and an art trail named 'human traces'. The museum was designed by architects Zamp Kelp, Julius Krauss, and Arno Brandlhuber, and it attracts about 170,000 visitors annually.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was established on 10 October 1996 near the site where the renowned Neanderthal fossil was found.
The museum's multimedia exhibition was upgraded in 2006.
From March 2012 to October 2012, the museum hosted a special exhibition about monkeys, which attracted 43,000 visitors.
From 18 November 2012 to 17 March 2013, the museum featured a special exhibition on wolves, created by the Görlitz branch of the Naturmuseum Senckenberg.

Major_Events.Event: Current Special Exhibition: Ice Age Journey Greenland
Major_Events.Description: The current special exhibition, titled 'Ice Age Journey Greenland', is open until 3 November 2024 and explores the archaeology, history, and culture of Greenland.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by architects Zamp Kelp, Julius Krauss, and Arno Brandlhuber. It features a spiraling ramp that connects the four floors of the building, with exhibits arranged thematically around the central theme of human evolution.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it is located at the site of the first Neanderthal man discovery and provides extensive exhibits on human evolution. It also supports research and international excavations related to early human history.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes an archaeological park, a Stone Age workshop, and an art trail named 'human traces'. It also houses the NESPOS Society e.V., which provides an interactive database on anthropological and archaeological data related to Neanderthals. The museum has received numerous awards for its architecture, exhibits, website, and tourism between 1997 and 2009.

world knowledge.Name: Complutense University of Madrid
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Sprawling campus occupying the entirety of the Ciudad Universitaria district of Madrid, with annexes in Somosaguas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in Alcalá in 1293, relocated to Madrid in 1836. One of the oldest operating universities in the world, and one of Spain's most prestigious institutions of higher learning. It has played a major role in the political development of Spain since its founding.

Major_Events.Description: King Sancho IV of Castile granted the Archbishop of Toledo, Gonzalo Pérez Gudiel, a royal charter to found a studium generale in Alcalá de Henares.
Queen Regent Maria Christina suppressed the university in Alcalá and ordered its move to Madrid, where it took the name of Literary University.
The Central University became one of the first universities in the world to grant a doctorate degree to a woman.
Albert Einstein was awarded a Doctor of Science degree Honoris Causa by the Central University.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Complutense University of Madrid
Major_Events.Description: Following the political instability of the regime of Francisco Franco, the University of Madrid was renamed, dividing existing colleges between the Complutense University of Madrid and the Technical University of Madrid.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of historical and modern architecture, influenced by the German Bauhaus movement, particularly in the Schools of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Odontology.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Complutense University of Madrid is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in the world, with a long history of academic excellence and significant contributions to science, arts, and politics. It has hosted numerous notable figures and played a crucial role in Spain's political and intellectual development.
world knowledge.Details: The university enrolls over 86,000 students and offers nearly 80 majors, 230 individual degrees, and 221 doctorate programs. It has over 30 libraries, a rich archive of historical documents, and an extensive film collection. The university is ranked among the top 300 worldwide and is the largest university in Spain.

world knowledge.Name: Hamburg Rathaus
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed after the old city hall was destroyed in the great fire of 1842, the present building was designed by a group of seven architects led by Martin Haller. It was inaugurated in 1897 and cost 11 million German gold marks. The building symbolizes Hamburg's wealth and independence during a period of prosperity following the Franco-German War and the formation of the German Empire.

Major_Events.Description: The new city hall was officially opened on 26 October 1897, with the First Mayor Johannes Versmann receiving the key to the city hall.
A service of remembrance was held on the market-square for the victims of the North Sea flood.
Celebrations were held for Hamburger SV as German football champions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Renaissance style on the outside with historical elements inside. The building features a copper roof that has turned green over time. It has 647 rooms, a 112-meter-high tower with 436 steps, and a total area of 17,000 m2. The courtyard includes a Hygieia fountain, and the balcony is adorned with a mosaic of Hamburg's patron goddess Hammonia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hamburg City Hall represents the wealth and republican traditions of Hamburg. It is a symbol of the city's independence and historical significance. The building's design and decorations reflect Hamburg's pride and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of local government of Hamburg, housing the office of the First Mayor and the meeting rooms for the Parliament and the Senate.
world knowledge.Details: The city hall participates in the Long Night of Museums and is located near the Hamburg Stock Exchange, the main shopping street Mönckebergstraße, and the Binnenalster lake. The building's motto is 'Libertatem quam peperere maiores digne studeat servare posteritas' (The freedom won by our elders, may posterity strive to preserve it in dignity).

world knowledge.Name: Calypso Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Calypso Theme Waterpark is a waterpark located in Limoges, Ontario, Canada, about 35 kilometres (22 mi) east of Ottawa. The park opened to the public on June 7, 2010.

Major_Events.Description: During a one-month period in the summer of 2011, there were 10 injuries on Steamer, two of which resulted in spinal injuries. The park failed to shut down the ride and did not report the incidents until the end of the season in September.

On June 19, 2012, employees on Orange Bobsleigh prematurely sent a group of riders down the slide resulting in a collision between two tubes causing a rider to be thrown out of the slide onto the concrete below, knocking him unconscious.

In August 2012, an excess amount of chlorine was discharged into Calypso Palace sickening 20 people, 13 of whom had to be taken to hospital. Later that day, a power outage caused another discharge of chlorine into the pool, resulting in two more hospitalizations.

On April 13, 2015, Calypso Park was found guilty of six of the eleven charges it faced under Ontario's Technical Standards and Safety Act. They were fined $400,000 and forced to pay an additional $100,000 victim surcharge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features 35 waterslides, a wave pool (the largest in Canada), two lazy rivers, food outlets, shops, picnic areas, and a VIP area with private cabanas and suites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Calypso Park is a major recreational attraction in Ontario, offering a variety of water-based activities and entertainment for visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The park can accommodate 22,000 visitors per day. On average, the park receives 400,000 visitors each season. It is owned by EPR Properties and operated by Premier Parks, LLC. The operating season is from mid-June to September. Website: www.calypsopark.com

world knowledge.Name: Town Hall, Colombo
world knowledge.Address: In front of the Viharamahadevi Park, Colombo, Sri Lanka
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 108 m (354 ft) in length and 51.3 m (168 ft) in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Town Hall of Colombo is the headquarters of the Colombo Municipal Council and the office of the mayor of Colombo. It was constructed following a recommendation by Scottish town planner Professor Patrick Geddes in 1921. The design was selected through an international architectural competition in 1922, won by S. J. Edwards of Ralph Booty & Co. The building was funded by the Council's revenue without central government loans, which strained municipal finances for years.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid by the Mayor of Colombo, Thomas Reid, CCS.
The building was formally opened by Governor Sir Herbert Stanley KCMG.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style, heavily inspired by L'Enfant's Capitol Building in Washington, D.C. Features include a central dome, Corinthian columns (each 11.6 m in height), open courtyards, and original furnishings such as lamps and doors. The building's height equals its width (51.3 m).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Town Hall is a symbol of local governance and civic pride in Colombo. Its architectural grandeur and historical role as the seat of municipal administration make it a significant landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serves as the headquarters of the Colombo Municipal Council and the office of the mayor, including a council chamber and public library.
world knowledge.Details: The building's design was praised for its dignified layout, excellent lighting, and impressive dome and tower. Original features like the council chamber, furniture, and ornamental lamps remain intact despite renovations.

world knowledge.Name: Orchardton Tower
world knowledge.Address: Four miles south of Dalbeattie, and one mile south of Palnackie, in Buittle parish
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Orchardton Tower is a ruined tower house built by John Cairns after he was granted the lands of 'Irisbuitle' in 1456. It is unique as the only cylindrical tower house in Scotland, built around 200 years after such towers had gone out of fashion. The Cairns family and later the Maxwells were associated with the tower, which saw various historical events including feuds and the Jacobite rising of 1745.

Major_Events.Event: Grant of lands to John Cairns
Major_Events.Description: John Cairns was granted the lands of 'Irisbuitle', possibly in return for his support for James II in the struggle against the 'Black' Earls of Douglas.

Major_Events.Event: Murder of Thomas McLellan of Bombie
Major_Events.Description: William Cairns, grandson of John Cairns, was present at the murder of Thomas McLellan of Bombie outside St. Giles' Cathedral, Edinburgh.
The part of Orchardton including the castle was sold to Robert Maxwell, who later became a baronet.
Robert Maxwell, a descendant of the Maxwell family, took part in the Jacobite rising and was wounded at Culloden.
Robert Maxwell used stones from the original castle to build a new manor house, Orchardton Castle, a few miles away.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is 11m in height and around 9m in diameter, tapering slightly to the top. It features a corbelled parapet and a gabled caphouse covering the spiral stair. Inside, there is a vaulted cellar on the ground floor, a main room with a fireplace, deep windows with seats, and a carved lavabo or piscina. The tower is the only cylindrical tower house in Scotland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Orchardton Tower is culturally significant as the only cylindrical tower house in Scotland, representing a unique architectural choice for its time. Its history is intertwined with the Cairns and Maxwell families, and it inspired Sir Walter Scott's novel 'Guy Mannering'.
world knowledge.Details: The tower was located at the north east corner of a fortified yard or barmkin, which would have sheltered livestock and provided cellars, a bakehouse, and probably a hall built on an upper level. It is now in the care of Historic Environment Scotland as a Scheduled Ancient Monument.

world knowledge.Name: Fort Tryon Park
world knowledge.Area: Washington Heights and Inwood neighborhoods, Manhattan, New York City
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by 190th Street, Cabrini Boulevard, 192nd Street, Bennett Avenue, Broadway, Riverside Drive, and Henry Hudson Parkway, Manhattan, New York City
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fort Tryon Park is a public park located in the Washington Heights and Inwood neighborhoods of Manhattan. The area was known by the local Lenape tribe as Chquaesgeck and by Dutch settlers as Lange Bergh (Long Hill). During the American Revolutionary War, the Battle of Fort Washington was fought at the site of the park on November 16, 1776. The park was created by philanthropist John D. Rockefeller Jr., who bought the land and engaged the Olmsted Brothers firm to design it. The park was completed in 1935 and houses the Cloisters, a branch of the Metropolitan Museum of Art dedicated to medieval art.

Major_Events.Description: Fought on November 16, 1776, between 2,900 American soldiers and 8,000 invading Hessian troops hired by Great Britain. Despite the American Continental Army's strategic position at the top of Long Hill, they were defeated after holding out for two hours.
Philanthropist John D. Rockefeller Jr. bought the land and engaged the Olmsted Brothers firm to design the park. The park was completed in 1935 and dedicated on October 12, 1935.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Fort Tryon Park was added to the National Register of Historic Places on December 19, 1978.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as a New York City scenic landmark
Major_Events.Description: Fort Tryon Park was designated a New York City scenic landmark in 1983.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by the Olmsted Brothers, the park features Romanesque architectural style with extensive plantings, walking paths, and meadows. The park includes the Cloisters, a medieval art museum designed by Charles Collens, which incorporates several medieval buildings purchased in Europe and reassembled stone by stone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fort Tryon Park is culturally and historically important due to its role in the American Revolutionary War, its design by the Olmsted Brothers, and its housing of the Cloisters, a significant collection of medieval art. The park also serves as a green space in Upper Manhattan, offering views of the Hudson River and the Palisades.
world knowledge.Details: Fort Tryon Park contains numerous gardens, including the Heather Garden and Alpine Garden, as well as walking paths, meadows, and playgrounds. The park is built on Manhattan schist and contains examples of igneous intrusions and glacial striations. It is also home to the Cloisters, a branch of the Metropolitan Museum of Art dedicated to medieval art. The park hosts annual events such as the Medieval Festival and offers programs like yoga and tai chi classes.

world knowledge.Name: Larnach Castle
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 43 rooms, 35 acres of grounds, 300 acres home farm
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Larnach Castle, also known as 'Larnach's Castle', is a Gothic Revival mansion built by William Larnach, a prominent entrepreneur and politician. It was constructed between 1871 and 1887, with additions such as a ballroom completed in 1887. The castle has been privately owned by the Barker family since 1967 and is a significant tourist attraction in Dunedin.

Major_Events.Description: Larnach Castle was designated a New Zealand Landmark by Heritage New Zealand.
A direct descendant of William Larnach proposed to her spouse at the Castle.
Larnach Castle and the Camp Estate were used as locations for the Netflix film 'The Royal Treatment', representing the residence of the royal family of the fictional country Lavania.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic Revival style, constructed with materials such as basalt, yellow brick, Glasgow brick, Oamaru stone, Italian marble, and local Caversham sandstone. Features intricate ceilings carved by the Godfrey family.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Larnach Castle is culturally significant as one of New Zealand's few houses of this scale, a tourist attraction, and a site with a reputation for being haunted. It also holds the title of 'Garden of International Significance'.
world knowledge.Details: Larnach Castle operates as a significant tourist attraction, receiving approximately 120,000 guests per annum. It offers guided and self-guided tours, events, and accommodation. The castle has been featured in various television shows and films, including 'Ghost Hunters International' and 'The Royal Treatment'.

world knowledge.Name: Kirkintilloch Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: Union Street, Kirkintilloch, East Dunbartonshire, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kirkintilloch Town Hall was commissioned to replace the old tolbooth in West High Street, which had been completed in 1815. Due to rapid industrial expansion, population growth, and the deterioration of the tolbooth, civic leaders decided to procure a purpose-built town hall. The site selected in Union Street had previously been occupied by a school. The new building was designed by Walker and Ramsay of Glasgow in the classical style and opened in July 1906. It was renovated in 1931 and extended in 1959. The building was closed by East Dunbartonshire Council on 30 June 2004 due to the anticipated expense of restoring it. The Kirkintilloch Town Hall Preservation Trust was established to preserve and restore the Hall for community use. In the early summer of 2016, work began on redeveloping the hall into a centre for heritage, arts, and culture. The hall was officially reopened in November 2018.

Major_Events.Description: The town hall was officially opened in July 1906.
The building underwent renovations in 1931.
The building was extended in 1959.
The building was closed by East Dunbartonshire Council on 30 June 2004 due to the anticipated expense of restoration.
Work began on redeveloping the hall into a centre for heritage, arts, and culture in the early summer of 2016.
The hall was officially reopened in November 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed in the classical style by Walker and Ramsay of Glasgow. It features a symmetrical frontage with five bays along Union Street. The central section of three bays includes an unusual bowed triple-doorway on the ground floor with a frieze and cornice above, and six tall narrow windows on the first floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kirkintilloch Town Hall is a category B listed building and holds historical importance as a municipal building in Kirkintilloch. It serves as a centre for heritage, arts, and culture, reflecting the town's history and community development.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Municipal building, centre for heritage, arts, and culture
world knowledge.Details: The building was constructed of soft sandstone, which has led to issues with deterioration. In December 2011, parts of the ceiling had fallen, and there was considerable dampness and crumbling paintwork. Roman items, including pottery and a nail, were discovered in the building's car park during redevelopment in July 2016.

world knowledge.Name: Gelora Bung Karno Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Gelora, Tanah Abang, Central Jakarta, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gelora Bung Karno Main Stadium, originally named Senayan Main Stadium, was constructed as part of Sukarno's construction sprees before the 1962 Asian Games. It was built to meet the minimum requirement of a multi-sport complex for the games. The stadium was designed by Friedrich Silaban and partially funded by a special loan from the Soviet Union. It was renamed Gelora Bung Karno Main Stadium in 1962, following a Presidential Decree. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including significant updates in 2016-2018 for the 2018 Asian Games and Asian Para Games.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was constructed to host the 1962 Asian Games.
Match between Persib Bandung and PSMS Medan with a record attendance of 150,000 spectators.
The stadium hosted the final between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

Major_Events.Event: 2018 Asian Games and Asian Para Games
Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the ceremonies and athletics competitions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a gigantic ring-shaped facade known as 'temu gelang', designed to shade spectators from the sun and increase the grandeur of the stadium. The design was insisted upon by Sukarno despite initial objections from Soviet architects.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after Sukarno, the first president of Indonesia, and stands as a symbol of national pride and sports development in the country. It has hosted numerous significant sporting events and concerts, contributing to its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football matches and large events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a seating capacity of 77,193 and is the 28th largest association football stadium in the world. It features a new LED lighting system with 620 fixtures and an RGB lighting system on its facade. The 2016-2018 renovation cost Rp769.69 billion (approximately US$59 million). The complex is accessible via Palmerah railway station, Istora Mandiri station, and Transjakarta BRT corridors.

world knowledge.Name: University of Jos
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Jos was established in November 1971 as a satellite campus of the University of Ibadan. It became an independent institution in October 1975 under the military government of General Murtala Mohammed. The first students were admitted in January 1972, and the first Bachelor of Arts degree program began in October 1973. The university expanded its faculties over the years, adding post-graduate programs in 1977 and establishing the Faculties of Law and Environmental Sciences in 1978. In 2003, the Carnegie Corporation of New York granted the university $2 million to form its own fundraising department.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Jos was established as an independent institution under the military government of General Murtala Mohammed.
The Carnegie Corporation of New York granted the University of Jos $2 million to form its own fundraising department.
A 300-level student committed suicide due to frustration over the strike of the Academic Staff Union of Universities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university has multiple sites across a 5,800-acre campus. The campus includes various academic buildings, libraries, and residential facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Jos is a significant educational institution in Nigeria, contributing to the academic and professional development of thousands of students. It plays a crucial role in the cultural and intellectual life of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Jos has several faculties including Agriculture, Arts, Education, Engineering, Environmental Sciences, Law, Management Sciences, Natural Sciences, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Social Sciences, and Veterinary Sciences. The current President of the Students' Union Government is Jane Pwajok Kangyang. The university library, established in 1962, supports teaching, learning, and research.

world knowledge.Name: Van Buren County Courthouse (Iowa)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Van Buren County Courthouse was built in 1843 and is the oldest courthouse in Iowa. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977. The county was established in 1836, and the courthouse was constructed after voters chose Keosauqua as the county seat in 1838. The building has served as the only courthouse for the county and was the site of the first death penalty trial in Iowa history in 1845.

Major_Events.Event: First death penalty trial in Iowa
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse served as the location for a trial resulting in the first death penalty in Iowa history.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Greek Revival-style building constructed with native oak and locally manufactured brick. The exterior walls are 22 inches thick on the first floor and 18 inches on the second floor. Originally featured a 10-foot square tower and circular walnut staircases, which were later removed. Iron truss rods were installed for additional strength.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Van Buren County Courthouse is the oldest courthouse in Iowa and represents early 19th-century judicial and architectural history. It is a well-preserved example of Greek Revival architecture and a key part of Iowa's historical heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: County courthouse and active courtroom, also featuring historical displays and exhibits.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse underwent major interior restoration from 1981 to 1983 and exterior renovation in 1997, including ADA-compliant improvements. The county office building, constructed in 1896, is located south of the courthouse.

world knowledge.Name: Shiraz University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shiraz University, established in 1946, is one of the oldest and most prestigious modern universities in Iran. It was originally named Pahlavi University after the reigning Pahlavi dynasty. The university has played a significant role in the development of higher education in Iran, pioneering many doctoral programs and establishing a strong academic foundation. After the 1979 Islamic Revolution, the university underwent significant changes, including a name change to Shiraz University and a three-year closure during the Cultural Revolution to Islamize the institution. The university has continued to expand and influence the academic landscape in Iran, particularly in the southern region.

Major_Events.Description: The institution was elevated to university status and named after the Pahlavi dynasty.
All universities in Iran, including Shiraz University, were closed for three years to Islamize the institutions.

Major_Events.Event: Separation of Shiraz University of Medical Sciences
Major_Events.Description: The Iranian Ministry of Health, Treatment, and Medical Education took over the health and medical sciences schools, leading to the establishment of Shiraz University of Medical Sciences.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Shiraz University of Technology
Major_Events.Description: The former Electronic Industries College was named Shiraz University of Technology as an independent university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus was initially designed by American architect Minoru Yamasaki, who also designed the World Trade Center. The university features a mix of modern and traditional architectural elements, with contributions from various artists and architects, including Alvar Aalto.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Shiraz University is culturally and historically significant as one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in Iran. It has played a pivotal role in the development of higher education and research in the country. The university has also been a center for cultural and scientific exchange, particularly during the Pahlavi era when it had strong ties with American universities.
world knowledge.Details: Shiraz University is known for its rigorous academic standards and low GPA compared to other Iranian universities. It has been ranked among the top universities in Iran and has a strong focus on research and academic excellence. The university has a rich library system, including the Mulla Sadra Library and the Kharazmi Library, which house valuable collections of books, manuscripts, and electronic resources.

world knowledge.Name: Strand Theatre (San Francisco)
world knowledge.Address: 415 Geary Street near the corner of Mason Street in the Theatre District of San Francisco
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The American Conservatory Theater (ACT) is a nonprofit theater company founded in 1965 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, by theatre and opera director William Ball. It moved to San Francisco and has been a significant cultural institution, offering classical and contemporary theater productions and operating an acting school. The theater's primary home, the Toni Rembe Theater (formerly Geary Theater), was built in 1910 and has been a historic landmark since 1975.

Major_Events.Description: Founded in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, by William Ball in conjunction with the Pittsburgh Playhouse and Carnegie Mellon University.
ACT moved to San Francisco and established itself as a major theater company.
The Geary Theater was severely damaged by the earthquake, forcing the company to perform in other venues.
ACT opened a new theater at 1127 Market Street, featuring a 283-seat theater and a 120-seat event space.
Due to lack of funding, ACT discontinued its Master of Fine Arts program for actors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Walter D. Bliss and William B. Faville in the Classical Revival and Late Victorian styles. The Toni Rembe Theater (formerly Geary Theater) was built in 1910 and is a historic landmark.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: ACT is a cornerstone of San Francisco's cultural scene, known for its high-quality theater productions and its role in training actors. The theater has been a platform for both classical and contemporary works and has contributed significantly to the arts in the United States.
world knowledge.Details: ACT offers training through the Studio A.C.T., the Summer Training Congress, and Young Conservatory programs. The Young Conservatory, founded in 1971, focuses on theater training for youth. ACT was the first regional theater to use the title 'sound designer,' attributed to Dan Dugan in the late 1960s. The theater has also been involved in notable productions televised by PBS, such as 'Taming of the Shrew' and 'Cyrano de Bergerac.'

world knowledge.Name: Lviv Danylo Halytskyi International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lviv Danylo Halytskyi International Airport is an international airport in Lviv, Ukraine, located 6 kilometres from the central city. It is the second largest and busiest airport in Ukraine. The airport is named after King Daniel of Galicia, the historical founder of the city in 1256 AD. The airport was established in 1923 by Polish authorities as a permanent air base in Skniłów near Lviv. It was named after the Polish President Ignacy Mościcki in 1929. After World War II, Lviv became part of the Ukrainian SSR. The airport has undergone significant expansions, including a $200m project in preparation for Euro 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Ukraine closed airspace to civilian flights due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Lviv International Airport underwent a $200m expansion project, including a new terminal building and runway extension.
Terminal 1 was re-opened for domestic flights, with future plans to move charter flights to the terminal as well.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has two terminals (1 and A), with Terminal A opened in 2012. Terminal A has 29 check-in desks, nine gates (four with jetbridges), and can handle up to 3,000 passengers per hour. Facilities include four cafés, two duty-free shops, and two airport lounges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after King Daniel of Galicia, the historical founder of Lviv in 1256 AD. It serves as a key transportation hub in western Ukraine and has played a significant role in the region's connectivity, especially following the Russo-Ukrainian War in 2014.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as a hub for Wizz Air and SkyUp, and a focus city for Ukraine International Airlines, Wizz Air, LOT Polish Airlines, Ryanair, and SkyUp. It has an elevation of 1,071 ft (326 m) and features a concrete runway. The airport handled 1,834,051 passengers and 2,282 tons of cargo in recent data. It is served by public transport, including bus route 48 and trolleybus route 29, as well as taxis and car rental services.

world knowledge.Name: Vivekananda Setu
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vivekananda Setu, originally named Willingdon Bridge and later Bally Bridge, is a multispan truss bridge over the Hooghly River in West Bengal, India. It was built to provide direct road and rail connectivity between the Calcutta Port and the Howrah railway station. The bridge was constructed by Rai Bahadur Jagmal Raja and completed in 1931. It was the most expensive and difficult railway bridge constructed in India at that time.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on 29 December 1931, providing direct road and rail connectivity between Calcutta Port and Howrah railway station.
A new road bridge, Nivedita Setu, was constructed 50 meters downstream due to the weakening of Vivekananda Setu caused by ageing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a multispan truss bridge made of steel and stone. It consists of seven 110-meter main spans and two 24-meter land spans. The viaduct has 22 spans of 9.1-meter girders built on masonry piers with reinforced concrete piles. The main piers are founded on octagonal steel caissons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vivekananda Setu is historically significant as it was the first railway bridge to cross the Hooghly River, connecting the East and West banks of Kolkata. It is also located near the famous Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was originally named Willingdon Bridge after Viceroy of India, Freeman Freeman-Thomas, 1st Marquess of Willingdon. It was later renamed Bally Bridge and finally Vivekananda Setu. The bridge cost over ₹1 crore (US$110,000) in those years. The first train to cross the bridge was named Jagmal Raja Howrah Express. Due to ageing and heavy traffic, a second bridge, Nivedita Setu, was constructed in 2007 to handle heavy vehicles, while Vivekananda Setu now serves light vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: Mont Ventoux
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mont Ventoux has been climbed since prehistoric times, with the first recorded ascent by Jean Buridan before 1334. It gained fame through its inclusion in the Tour de France cycling race. The mountain was systematically stripped of trees from the 12th century onwards for shipbuilding, with some reforestation since 1860. A chapel was constructed on the top in the 15th century, and a meteorological station was built in 1882. The mountain's biological distinctiveness was recognized by UNESCO in 1990.

Major_Events.Event: First penultimate-day mountain top finish in the Tour de France
Major_Events.Description: Alberto Contador sealed his yellow jersey on Mont Ventoux.
British cyclist Tom Simpson died on the mountain from heat exhaustion, dehydration, and amphetamine use.

Major_Events.Event: Tour de France stage shortened due to high winds
Major_Events.Description: The stage was shortened by 6 km due to high winds at the summit, finishing at Chalet Reynard.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mountain's peak is bare limestone without vegetation or trees. A 50-metre-tall telecommunications mast was built in the 1960s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mont Ventoux is culturally significant due to its inclusion in the Tour de France, its historical ascents, and its unique biodiversity. It is also known as the "Beast of Provence" and the "Giant of Provence".
world knowledge.Details: Mont Ventoux is the highest mountain in the Provence region, standing at 1,910 m (6,270 ft). It is known for its strong winds, with speeds as high as 320 km/h (200 mph) recorded. The mountain is a popular destination for cyclists and hikers, with three main routes to the summit. It is also home to two small ski stations, Mont Serein and Chalet Reynard.

world knowledge.Name: Downer Theatre
world knowledge.Area: Upper East Side neighborhood, East Side of Milwaukee
world knowledge.Address: 2589 North Downer Avenue Milwaukee United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Downer Theatre is an historic cinema in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, opened in 1915. It was the oldest continually operating cinema in Milwaukee and became part of the Landmark Theatre chain in 1990. The theatre closed in September 2023 but reopened in April 2024 after being purchased by Milwaukee Film.

Major_Events.Description: The Downer Theatre was opened as part of a mixed-use complex on Downer Avenue.
The cinema was remodeled in a Streamline Moderne style, with a new marquee and green enamel plate exterior.
The Downer began to transition into a niche role as Milwaukee’s independent and art cinema under the leadership of longtime manager Estelle Steinbach.
The cinema was renovated and subdivided into a two-screen operation.
The theatre closed its doors in September 2023.
Milwaukee Film announced the reopening of the Downer Theatre, which officially reopened on April 12th, 2024, as part of the 16th Milwaukee Film Festival.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cinema was designed by Martin S. Tullgren in a Streamline Moderne style. It features a bright green and red neon marquee and is located inside a mixed-use two-story red brick structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Downer Theatre is culturally significant as the oldest continually operating cinema in Milwaukee and a landmark for independent and art cinema in the city.
world knowledge.Details: The two screens have a collective capacity for 440 patrons. The cinema has a small snack bar that serves candy, popcorn, and both alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks. The building also houses residential apartments, a bar, bookstore, and pizzeria.

world knowledge.Name: Detroit Institute of Arts
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Detroit Institute of Arts (DIA) was established in 1885 and has grown to become one of the largest and most significant art museums in the United States. It was originally named the Detroit Museum of Art and was renamed in 1919. The current building was designed by Paul Philippe Cret and opened in 1927. The museum has undergone expansions and renovations, including a major renovation in 2007.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Detroit Museum of Art
Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded as the Detroit Museum of Art after a successful art exhibition in 1883 inspired local citizens to establish a permanent museum.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Detroit Institute of Arts
Major_Events.Description: The museum was renamed and plans began for a new building to house its expanding collections.
The current Beaux-Arts, Italian Renaissance-style building designed by Paul Philippe Cret was dedicated.
A $158 million renovation and expansion project was completed, adding 58,000 square feet to the museum.
Readers of USA Today voted the Detroit Institute of Arts the No. 1 art museum in the United States.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts, Italian Renaissance style with white marble as the main exterior material. The original building was designed by Paul Philippe Cret, with later additions by Gunnar Birkerts and renovations by Michael Graves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The DIA is one of the most significant art museums in the United States, with an encyclopedic collection spanning ancient to contemporary art. It is particularly noted for its collections of American, European, African, and Asian art, as well as Diego Rivera's Detroit Industry murals.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes over 65,000 works, valued at up to $8.5 billion. It features significant works by artists such as Vincent van Gogh, Henri Matisse, Diego Rivera, and many others. The museum also includes a 1,150-seat theatre, a 380-seat hall for recitals and lectures, an art reference library, and a conservation services laboratory.

world knowledge.Name: Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral
world knowledge.Address: Bishop Street, Cork, T12 K710, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral is a Gothic Revival three-spire Church of Ireland cathedral in Cork city, Ireland. It is located on the south bank of the River Lee and dedicated to Finbarr of Cork, patron saint of the city. Christian use of the site dates back to the 7th century AD when Finbarr of Cork founded a monastery. The original building survived until the 12th century, when it either fell into disuse or was destroyed during the Norman invasion of Ireland. Around 1536, during the Protestant Reformation, the cathedral became part of the established church, later known as the Church of Ireland. The previous building was constructed in the 1730s but was widely regarded as plain and featureless. The cathedral's demolition and rebuild was commissioned in the mid-19th century by an Anglican church intent on strengthening its hand after the reforms of penal law. Work began in 1863, and resulted in the first major commissioned project for the Victorian architect William Burges, who designed most of the cathedral's architecture, sculpture, stained glass, mosaics, and interior furniture.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone of Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral was laid on 12 January 1865.
The cathedral was consecrated in 1870 by Bishop John Gregg.
The limestone spires of the cathedral were completed by October 1879.
A major restoration of the cathedral, costing £5 million, was undertaken, including the reinstatement and restoration of the twin trumpets held by the resurrection angel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral is built in the Gothic Revival style, designed by William Burges. The exterior is capped by three spires: two on the west front and one above the nave, at the crossing with the transept. The cathedral is mostly built from local stone sourced from Little Island and Fermoy. The entrances contain figures of over a dozen biblical characters, surmounted by a tympanum showing a Resurrection scene. The interior features intricate mosaics, stained glass windows, and detailed sculptures, including gargoyles modelled by Thomas Nicholls.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral is culturally and historically important as it is dedicated to Finbarr of Cork, the patron saint of Cork city. It represents the long-standing Christian heritage of the area, dating back to the 7th century. The cathedral is also significant as a masterpiece of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture, designed by William Burges, and is considered one of his greatest works in ecclesiastical architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral's style is Gothic Revival, Burges's preferred period, which he used for his own home, The Tower House, in London. He reused elements of unsuccessful designs he had produced for competitions for cathedrals at Lille and Brisbane. The shell of the building is mostly limestone, sourced from near Cork, with the interior walls formed from stone brought from Bath. The red marble came from Little Island, the purple-brown stone from Fermoy. The cathedral holds the book of estimates prepared for the decoration of the west front. Nicholls was paid £1,769 for the modelling, and Robert McLeod £5,153 for the carving. Burges took 10 per cent for the design, more than his usual 5 per cent, apparently due to his high level of personal involvement.

world knowledge.Name: Melbourne Ballpark
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Melbourne Ballpark was constructed after the Victorian Baseball Association lobbied the state government for a dedicated baseball and softball venue. It was opened in January 1990 after a decade of planning and opposition. The stadium has undergone several renovations and upgrades over the years.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted games between New Zealand, Australia, Samoa, and South Africa.
Hosted the ABL All-Star game six years in a row, cementing its reputation as the best baseball venue in the country.
Hosted the IBLA season, marking the first national championship game/series at the ballpark since the collapse of the ABL in 1999.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by CK Designwork Architects, the stadium features a synthetic infield (since 2012), grass outfield, and has undergone multiple renovations including seating adjustments and surface upgrades.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Melbourne Ballpark is a significant venue for baseball and softball in Australia, hosting national championships, ABL games, and international events. It is considered the premier baseball venue in the country.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of approximately 5,000 (2,200 seated). It has hosted motocross events and served as a waypoint for light aircraft visual flight rules (VFR) advisory lane of entry to Moorabbin Airport from 2008 to 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Nehru Setu
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Dehri-on-Son and Son Nagar, Bihar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nehru Setu is a railway bridge across the Son River, connecting Dehri-on-Son and Son Nagar, in Bihar. When it was built, it was the longest bridge in India and was believed to be the second longest bridge in the world. It was opened for traffic on 27 February 1900. The bridge was part of the Grand Chord line, which reduced the distance between Kolkata and Delhi by 80 km.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened for traffic on 27 February 1900.
Jawahar Setu, the road bridge carrying NH 2 and running parallel to the Nehru Setu, was constructed.
The opening of the 4.62 km Vembanad Rail Bridge pushed Nehru Setu to the second position as the longest rail bridge in India.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel girders resting on 93 stone pillars, each a hundred feet apart, form the rail bridge. The total length of the bridge over abutments is 3,064 metres (10,052 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nehru Setu is historically significant as it was the longest rail bridge in India for many years and played a crucial role in reducing the travel distance between Kolkata and Delhi. It remains an important infrastructure in Bihar.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway bridge for the Grand Chord railway track
world knowledge.Details: The Koilwar bridge preceded the Nehru Setu and was opened in 1862. An anicut was constructed across the Son, a little upstream of the present Nehru Setu and Jawahar Setu, in 1873–74. The Indrapuri Barrage was constructed, 8 km upstream, and commissioned in 1968. Its distance from Aurangabad is approximately 15 km and 10 km from Dehri On Sone.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Qatar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Qatar, designed by Jean Nouvel, opened on 28 March 2019, replacing the original museum established in 1975. The museum is built around the historic palace of Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani, which was restored and integrated into the new structure. The museum's design is inspired by the desert rose crystal, and it aims to celebrate Qatar's culture, heritage, and future.

Major_Events.Description: The original Qatar National Museum was inaugurated on 23 June 1975, enclosing the Old Amiri Palace and featuring a lagoon for traditional dhows and pearling equipment.
The museum was awarded the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1980.
The new National Museum of Qatar, designed by Jean Nouvel, opened to the public on 28 March 2019.

Major_Events.Event: Green Apple Award for Best Environmental Practices
Major_Events.Description: The museum received the Green Apple Award for Best Environmental Practices in September 2023.
The museum received a Carbon Neutrality Certificate in July 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is designed in the shape of a desert rose, with interlocking discs that create cavities to protect visitors from the desert heat. The building integrates the historic palace of Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani and features a 1.2 million ft² landscaped park, an artificial lagoon, and various facilities including restaurants, a café, and museum shops.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is a symbol of Qatar's national identity, celebrating its culture, heritage, and rapid modernization. It houses a vast collection of artifacts, including archaeological finds, Bedouin ethnographic materials, and historical documents, offering visitors a comprehensive view of Qatar's history and traditions.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections consist of approximately 8,000 objects, including archaeological artifacts, architectural elements, heritage household and traveling objects, textiles and costumes, jewelry, decorative arts, books, and historical documents. The museum also features an online platform called Explorer, launched in 2023, which provides access to online collections, an archaeology and heritage map, and an interactive timeline of the museum.

world knowledge.Name: Somali National University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Somali National University (SNU) was established in 1954 as Università Nazionale Somala under Italian U.N. Trusteeship. It became an official university in 1969 and initially used Italian as the language of instruction. The university closed in 1990 due to the civil war but reopened in August 2014. It was founded to train graduates for leading and technical roles in Somalia, with courses in economics, jurisprudence, agrarian studies, chemistry, medicine, engineering, and geology.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established as Università Nazionale Somala under Italian U.N. Trusteeship.
The Somali National University obtained official university status.
The university closed due to the civil war.
The university reopened in August 2014 after a refurbishing initiative costing US$55.2 million.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Somali National University is culturally significant as it was established to train the leading and technical cadres of Somalia, contributing to the nation's development and education system.
world knowledge.Details: The university had four main campuses, including Gaheyr Campus, and formerly had 14 departments. The language of instruction transitioned from Italian to Somali and English. Notable alumni include various influential figures in Somalia.

world knowledge.Name: St Mel's Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral Church of St Mel is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Ardagh and Clonmacnoise, located in the town of Longford in Ireland. Built between 1840 and 1856, with the belfry and portico as later additions, it has been considered the "flagship cathedral" of the Irish midlands region, Longford's "landmark building" and "one of the finest Catholic churches in Ireland". The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Mél (died 488), who came to Ireland with Saint Patrick and who was ordained bishop at Ardagh, County Longford.

Major_Events.Description: On Christmas Day 2009, the cathedral was destroyed by a fire in the early hours of the morning. The restored cathedral re-opened in December 2014.
The cathedral was consecrated on 19 May 1893.
The restored cathedral re-opened on Christmas Eve 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is a Neoclassical stone building, at the north-east side of the town. Construction began in 1840 to the design of Joseph B. Keane. The roof is supported by 24 limestone columns quarried at nearby Newtowncashel. The 1860 belfry was designed by John Bourke, and the 1889 portico was designed by George Ashlin. Harry Clarke studios designed the stained glass windows in the transepts. Ray Carroll designed the 1975 furnishings including "The Second Coming" tapestry behind the bishop's throne. Imogen Stuart designed "The Holy Ghost" above the baptismal font. The tapestry was produced by Donegal Carpets of Killybegs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St Mel's Cathedral is considered the "flagship cathedral" of the Irish midlands region, Longford's "landmark building" and "one of the finest Catholic churches in Ireland".
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral features a Carrara marble altar sculpted by Tom Glendon, a silver tabernacle created by Imogen Stuart and Vicki Donovan, a pipe organ consisting of 2,307 pipes, built by Fratelli Ruffatti, and stained glass windows designed by Kim en Joong, a Dominican priest. A silhouette image of St Mel's Cathedral features on the crest of League of Ireland club Longford Town. The cathedral is also depicted on the crest of all Co Longford GAA teams.

world knowledge.Name: Salisbury Cathedral
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 442 feet (135 m) in length, 234 feet (71 m) nave length, 78 feet (24 m) nave width, 84 feet (26 m) choir height, 225 feet (69 m) tower height, 404 feet (123 m) spire height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Salisbury Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary, is an Anglican cathedral in the city of Salisbury, England. It is regarded as one of the leading examples of Early English Gothic design. Built over a relatively short period, some 38 years between 1220 and 1258, it has a unity and coherence that is unusual in medieval English cathedrals. The tower and spire were completed by 1330. The cathedral's spire, at 404 feet (123 m), is the tallest in England.

Major_Events.Description: Foundation stones for the new building were laid on 28 April 1220 by the Earl and Countess of Salisbury.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of nave, transepts, and choir
Major_Events.Description: By 1258, the nave, transepts, and choir were complete.
The tower and spire were completed by 1330, making it the tallest spire in England.
The cathedral celebrated the 750th anniversary of its consecration.
The completion of a programme of external restoration begun in 1985 saw the removal of scaffolding that had stood around the building for some 37 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Early English Gothic design with a unity and coherence unique among English cathedrals. The cathedral features a tall and narrow nave, lancet windows, and a notable spire. The west front is of the screen-type, highly decorated with quatrefoil motifs, columns, trefoil motifs, and bands of diapering.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Salisbury Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as one of the leading examples of Early English Gothic architecture. It houses one of the four surviving original copies of Magna Carta and contains a clock which is among the oldest working examples in the world. The cathedral close is Britain's largest and contains many buildings of architectural and historical significance.
world knowledge.Details: Salisbury Cathedral is the mother church of the Diocese of Salisbury and is the seat of the Bishop of Salisbury. The cathedral close is Britain's largest and contains many listed buildings. The cathedral has been the subject of various literary and artistic works, including paintings by John Constable and novels by William Golding and Ken Follett. It also serves as a venue for cultural events and has been used for filming and broadcasting.

world knowledge.Name: Rainbow Beach
world knowledge.Address: Rainbow Beach Road, Rainbow Beach QLD 4581, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rainbow Beach is named after its rainbow-coloured sand dunes, which derive from rich mineral content. According to indigenous Kabi Kabi legends, the dunes were coloured when Yiningie, a spirit represented by a rainbow, plunged into the cliffs after battling an evil tribesman. The town was established in 1969 and has grown into a popular tourist destination.

Major_Events.Event: Rainbow Beach Family Fishing Classic & Expo
Major_Events.Description: Created as a means of driving tourism off-season, this event has been popular for nearly 40 years.
The town's war memorial, commemorating those who died in World War I and subsequent conflicts, was refurbished in 1993.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Rainbow Beach State School
Major_Events.Description: Rainbow Beach State School opened on 28 January 1986.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Anglican Church of the Good Shepherd
Major_Events.Description: The Anglican Church of the Good Shepherd opened on 15 September 1993. The church and hall were relocated from Yeronga in Brisbane and re-erected in Rainbow Beach after a 15-hour journey.
Rainbow Beach Library was opened in 2012.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features a mix of modern and relocated structures, such as the Anglican Church of the Good Shepherd, which was moved from Yeronga in Brisbane. The town's buildings cater to tourism, including hotels, motels, and caravan parks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rainbow Beach is culturally significant due to its indigenous legends, vibrant sand dunes, and role as a gateway to K'gari (Fraser Island). It is also a popular eco-tourism destination and a quiet holiday retreat.
world knowledge.Details: Rainbow Beach is a popular tourist destination, both in its own right and as a gateway to K'gari (Fraser Island), with a vehicle ferry frequently running to the southern point of K'gari. The town's economy is dominated by tourism, featuring quiet and idyllic holidays, fishing, and retirement getaways. Although it has a permanent population of about 1,000, about 70,000 visitors go to the town each year. The Cooloola Section of the Great Sandy National Park borders the town to the south, offering walking tracks and the northern end-point of the Cooloola Great Walk.

world knowledge.Name: La Rosaleda Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Rosaleda Stadium replaced the historic arena of Baños del Carmen and was first used on 13 April 1941 due to flooding. Officially inaugurated on 14 September 1941, it has been the home stadium of Málaga CF and hosted significant football events, including matches during the 1982 FIFA World Cup and the 2009 Peace Cup. The stadium underwent major renovations in 2000-2006 and is planned to host matches in the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted three matches during the tournament.
Hosted four matches, including a semi-final between Porto and Aston Villa.
Hosted the women's Copa de la Reina.
Hosted several matches and one of the finals.
Charity match between teams of Friends of Zidane and Friends of Ronaldo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Renovated in 2000-2006 with a capacity of 30,044 seats, featuring paths visors on the steps, closed-circuit television, private boxes, press boxes, and other amenities to comply with safety regulations. Designed by architect José Segui Pérez and the Sando-Vera joint venture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: La Rosaleda Stadium is a key football venue in Spain, hosting international tournaments, national team matches, and cultural events like concerts. It represents the sporting heritage of Málaga and Andalusia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium and multi-purpose event venue.
world knowledge.Details: Owned by the Municipality of Málaga, the Málaga Provincial Council, and the Government of Andalusia. It includes the Rosaleda Official Store Málaga CF and a medical center. The stadium has hosted concerts with over 60,000 spectators and is planned for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

world knowledge.Name: California Theatre (San Francisco)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 165 feet of frontage, 117 feet in depth, resting on 4 1/2 foot foundation walls
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The California Theatre was built in 1869 by William Ralston, treasurer of the Bank of California, and designed by S. C. Bugbee & Son. It was inspired by the acting of John McCullough and Lawrence Barrett. The theater was a major cultural hub, hosting numerous performances and notable actors until its demolition in 1888. It was rebuilt in 1889 but destroyed in the 1906 San Francisco earthquake. The site is now a California Historical Landmark.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened on January 18, 1869, with a performance of Bulwer-Lytton's play 'Money.' It quickly became the leading theater in the city.
The original theater was demolished and rebuilt in 1889.
The rebuilt theater was destroyed in the San Francisco earthquake and fire of 1906.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a California Historical Landmark
Major_Events.Description: The site was registered as California Historical Landmark #86.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original theater was a Corinthian-style temple with elaborate murals of San Francisco and a panoramic view of San Francisco Bay on the drop curtain. It featured a dress circle, gallery, and a 51-foot ceiling in the interior auditorium. The rebuilt theater in 1889 was fire-proof, with 19 exits, Roman arch entrance, and was the first on the West Coast to be lighted exclusively with electricity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The California Theatre was a major cultural and entertainment hub in San Francisco, breaking the hegemony of rival manager Thomas Maguire in the western theater world. It hosted numerous notable actors and performances, contributing significantly to the cultural life of the city during its time.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was the first on the West Coast to use calcium light (limelight) with parabolic reflectors. It enjoyed exceptional success in the mid-1870s due to good economic times following the discovery of the Comstock Lode. The theater's financial prospects were tied to the mining boom in Nevada. After the Bank of California failed in 1875 and Ralston's death, the theater went into decline. The new California Theatre in 1889 was the first on the West Coast to be lighted exclusively with electricity.

world knowledge.Name: Port of Jebel Ali
world knowledge.Address: Jebel Ali, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Port of Jebel Ali, also known as Mina Jebel Ali, is a deep port located in Jebel Ali, Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It was constructed in the late 1970s to supplement the facilities at Port Rashid. The port was inaugurated by Queen Elizabeth II on 26 February 1979.

Major_Events.Description: The port was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 26 February 1979.

Major_Events.Event: Golden Award for Best Seaport Overall
Major_Events.Description: On 9 April 2011, Port of Jebel Ali won the Golden Award for Best Seaport Overall from the Higher Committee for UAE Civil Seaports and Airports Security.
In 2017, a big port crane started to collapse. It hit a vehicle and building as it collapsed. People were able to escape.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The port is the largest man-made harbour in the world, covering over 134 square kilometres. It includes 67 berths, over one million square metres of container yard, and various storage facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jebel Ali Port is the world's ninth busiest port and the biggest and busiest port in the Middle-East. It plays a crucial role in the Maritime Silk Road, connecting trade routes from the Chinese coast to the Mediterranean and beyond.
world knowledge.Details: The port is managed by DP World and has become the port most frequently visited by ships of the United States Navy outside the United States. It is linked to Dubai's expressway system and to the Dubai International Airport Cargo Village, enabling efficient cargo transport. The port's expansion project, which commenced in 2001, aims to significantly increase its capacity, potentially making it the world's biggest container port.

world knowledge.Name: Cincinnati Music Hall
world knowledge.Address: 1241 Elm Street, Cincinnati, Ohio, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cincinnati Music Hall was completed in 1878 and built over a pauper's cemetery. It was designed by architect Samuel Hannaford and funded by Reuben Springer and other community leaders. The hall has served as a cultural hub for music and industrial expositions, undergoing major renovations in 1969–1975 and 2016–2017.

Major_Events.Description: Nominated Rutherford B. Hayes for the presidency.
Nominated Winfield S. Hancock for President and William H. English for Vice President.
A projection mapping event by the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra.
A $143 million renovation adding 30,000 square feet of usable space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian Gothic Revival Style with Venetian Gothic elements. Features include a steeply-pitched gable roof, corbelled brick, tracery on front windows, and a large Rose Window. The facility consists of three distinct buildings: Music Hall, North Exposition Building, and South Exposition Building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Recognized as a National Historic Landmark for its distinctive architecture and role in Cincinnati's cultural life. It is home to the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra, Cincinnati Opera, Cincinnati Ballet, and May Festival Chorus. It is also reputed to be one of the most haunted places in America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Classical music performance hall and event venue.
world knowledge.Details: The building includes Springer Auditorium (seating 2,289–2,439), Music Hall Ballroom (capacity 1,300), Corbett Tower, and Wilks Studio. It houses the iconic Music Hall Chandelier and has been featured in paranormal investigations. The hall was listed on the National Trust for Historic Preservation's most endangered historic places in 2014.

world knowledge.Name: Menstrie Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Menstrie Castle is a three-storey manor house in Menstrie, Clackmannanshire, near Stirling, central Scotland. It was home to Sir William Alexander, 1st Earl of Stirling, who was instrumental in founding the colony of Nova Scotia. The castle was restored in the 20th century and now incorporates holiday accommodation, private flats, and a museum. It was built around 1560 by the Alexander family, a sept of the Clan MacAlister. Sir William Alexander was born here around 1577 and later became a prominent figure in the Royal Household of James VI. The castle was burned in 1645 during the English Civil War and later sold to James Holborne of Menstrie. It was restored in the 1960s and is now a Category A listed building.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was burned by the Royalist James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose during the English Civil War.
The castle was restored by Clackmannanshire County Council, winning a Scottish Civic Trust award for restoration in 1962.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a small, L-plan tower house, the castle was extended in the 17th century into a U-plan house. A section of curtain wall closes the U, forming a courtyard. The restoration retained the fine 16th-century entrance arch but replaced stone on the ground floor either side of this arch. The eastern gable has fireplaces where a 17th-century extension was demolished.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Menstrie Castle is culturally significant due to its association with Sir William Alexander, 1st Earl of Stirling, who played a key role in the founding of Nova Scotia. The castle also represents the architectural and historical heritage of Scotland.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is managed by the National Trust for Scotland and is open to the public on a restricted basis by appointment. It also offers self-catering accommodation. Two rooms within the castle are occupied by an exhibition commemorating the link between Menstrie, William Alexander, and Nova Scotia.

world knowledge.Name: Adršpach-Teplice Rocks
world knowledge.Address: Near Adršpach and Teplice nad Metují, Czech Republic
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Adršpach-Teplice Rocks are a set of sandstone formations in the Czech Republic, named after nearby municipalities Adršpach and Teplice nad Metují. The site was a regional destination during the 19th and early 20th century, evidenced by stone inscriptions and postcards. It has been protected as a national nature reserve since 1933 and is part of the Broumovsko Protected Landscape Area since 1991.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Sandstone rock formations
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The site is culturally significant for its natural beauty and historical inscriptions. It is also an important breeding site for peregrine falcons and a popular destination for rock climbers and rock jumpers.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: National nature reserve and tourist destination
world knowledge.Details: The area is one of the largest permanent breeding sites of peregrine falcon in Europe, with some areas designated off limits to climbers and hikers to protect the birds.

world knowledge.Name: Léon-Mba International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Léon-Mba International Airport is the main international airport in Gabon, constructed in the 1950s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It serves as a crucial hub for international and regional transportation in Gabon.

Details.Direction: Direction Length Surface m ft 16/34 3,000 9,844 Asphalt

world knowledge.Name: Parc Astérix
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parc Astérix is a theme park in France based on the comic book series Asterix by Albert Uderzo and René Goscinny. Opened in 1989, the park was largely funded by the Barclays financial company and other investors, costing 850 million French francs to build. The location was chosen due to the transport network, with a private interchange connecting it to the A1 autoroute. The park was inaugurated by Jack Lang, then Minister of Culture, on 30 April 1989 after two years of work.

Major_Events.Description: Caused Parc Astérix's attendance to fall 30% and its revenue by 19%.
A festival held as a way of 'thumbing their noses' at Halloween.
The park opened for the first time during the Christmas holidays.
A Halloween event held for the park's 20th anniversary.
A new multi-launch roller coaster manufactured by Intamin, scheduled to open in 2021 but delayed to 2023 due to COVID-19 and woodcutting delays.
The park announced the closure of its dolphin and sea lion enclosure to focus on rides and other shows.
The park achieved a record yearly attendance of over 2.8 million visitors, marked by the opening of the new roller-coaster Toutatis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features rides and themes from historic cultures like the Gauls, the Romans, Ancient Greece, and Ancient Egypt, all in the visual style of the Asterix comic books, reusing characters, scenes, and sounds from the media.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parc Astérix is the 2nd most visited park in France and the 8th most visited in Europe. It is renowned for its large variety of roller coasters and its unique themes based on the Asterix comic series, blending historical cultures with the comic's visual style.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located approximately 35 km north of Paris, 32 km from Disneyland Paris, and 20 km from the historic Château de Chantilly. It is operated by Compagnie des Alpes and features many attractions and shows. In 2023, the park recruited around 2,000 people for the season, a record number compared to previous years.

world knowledge.Name: Inishowen
world knowledge.Location: Northernmost part of the island of Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Inishowen (Irish: Inis Eoghain, meaning 'island of Eoghan') is the largest peninsula on the island of Ireland. It includes Ireland's most northerly point, Malin Head, and the Grianan of Aileach, a ringfort that served as the royal seat of the over-kingdom of Ailech. The peninsula has a rich history dating back to early settlements, including the ruins of several castles and the fort at Grianán Aileach. It was named after Eógan mac Néill, son of Niall of the Nine Hostages, and has been influenced by various clans and historical events, including the Plantation of Ulster and O'Doherty's Rebellion.

Major_Events.Description: Sir Cahir O'Doherty, the Chief of the Name of Clan O'Doherty and Lord of Inishowen, launched a rebellion by burning Derry. After the defeat of the uprising, most of Clan O'Doherty's territory was awarded to Arthur Chichester.
Ireland's deadliest road accident happened at Inishowen in July 2010.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The peninsula features historical monuments, including the ruins of several castles and the Grianán Ailigh fort, which was the one-time seat of the High Kings of Ireland. The fort was restored in the nineteenth century, although some damage has resulted in the partial collapse of the south side wall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Inishowen is culturally significant due to its historical monuments, early settlements, and its role in Irish history, including the Plantation of Ulster and O'Doherty's Rebellion. It is also the starting (or ending) point of the Wild Atlantic Way and features the Inishowen 100 tourist route.
world knowledge.Details: Inishowen has several harbours, some of which are used for commercial fishing purposes, and a seasonal ferry service. The peninsula has a number of Gaelic football clubs and is home to the Inishowen Football League (IOFL) and Inishowen Rugby Club. Other sports in the area include cycling, golf, horse riding, kayaking, shooting, surfing, and rock climbing. The Inishowen Maritime Museum & Planetarium and Fort Dunree Military Museum are notable attractions.

world knowledge.Name: Doberan Minster
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Doberan Minster is the main Lutheran Church of Bad Doberan in Mecklenburg, Germany. It is the remaining part of Doberan Abbey, a former Cistercian monastery dedicated in 1368. The first abbey in Mecklenburg, founded in 1171, was used as the burial site for regional rulers and became important both politically and historically. The abbey greatly contributed to the cultural and economic development of Mecklenburg and became the centre of Christianity in this region. Even after the reformation and the dissolution of the abbey in 1552, the church continued to serve as the main burial place for the ruling Mecklenburg family and the place of worship for the Evangelical-Lutheran congregation.

Major_Events.Description: The first abbey in Mecklenburg was founded, becoming a significant political and historical site.
The Doberan Minster was dedicated as part of the Cistercian monastery.
The abbey was dissolved during the Reformation, but the Minster continued to serve as a church and burial site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Doberan Minster is a unique symbiosis of a high gothic cathedral building, based upon French cathedral style and elements of other Hanseatic churches as well as influence by the building code of the Cistercians. It features brick construction, with intricate Gothic detailing and a wealth of medieval liturgical furnishings, including the oldest winged altar in art history, a monumental cross altar, and the sculpted tomb of Danish Queen Margarete Sambiria.
