world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Minster is the most important medieval building in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and a prime example of medieval creativity and technical perfection. It is a unique and precious artistic monument in the coastal region of the Baltic Sea, with complete and historically important liturgical furnishings that are unmatched in northern Germany.
world knowledge.Details: The Minster contains numerous treasures, including the oldest winged altar in art history, a monumental cross altar, and the sculpted tomb of Danish Queen Margarete Sambiria. It also features a unique combination of Gothic architecture and Cistercian simplicity, with a wealth of medieval liturgical furnishings that have remained intact for centuries.

world knowledge.Name: Alexander County Courthouse (Illinois)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alexander County Courthouse is the latest in a series of courthouses erected in four towns across Alexander County. The county was created in 1819, and the courthouse has been relocated several times due to changes in the county seat. The current courthouse was built in the 1960s, replacing a Neoclassical building from 1865 that had deteriorated over time.

Major_Events.Description: Alexander County was created out of Union County and named after William M. Alexander, an early settler and House of Representatives member.
A brick courthouse was built in America, the first county seat, but the town declined due to an epidemic and steamboat landing issues.
The county seat moved to Unity, where a log courthouse was built in 1835 but burned down in 1842 due to a fire set by escaping prisoners.
The county seat moved to Thebes, where a new courthouse was built in 1848 for $4,400.
Cairo successfully challenged Thebes for the status of county seat, and a new Neoclassical courthouse was built in 1865.
The 1865 courthouse was destroyed and replaced by the current modernist building in the 1960s.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current courthouse is a modernist building, long and just one story tall. Much of the facade is brick with numerous windows, although the right end of the facade is concrete with no doors or windows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse represents the historical and governmental evolution of Alexander County, reflecting changes in county seats and architectural styles over time.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government building serving as the county courthouse for Alexander County.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse is located in Cairo, the county seat of Alexander County, Illinois. It is the latest in a series of courthouses built in the county since its creation in 1819.

world knowledge.Name: Sheikh Zayed Palace Museum
world knowledge.Area: Eastern Region of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
world knowledge.Address: Al Ain, Eastern Region of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, the UAE
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum is based in the palace of the former UAE President, Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan (1918–2004), and his family. It was originally built in 1937 on the western side of the Al Ain Oasis, the largest oasis in Al Ain. Sheikh Zayed lived here until 1966. It was made into a museum in 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was converted into a museum, showcasing the life and times of Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum presents many of the rooms in the palace, including an art gallery. Many of the rooms are of the majlis (meeting room for receiving visitors) type. In one of the courts there is a replica grand court tent, representing a link with Bedouin life. There is also a Land Rover similar to the one driven by Sheikh Zayed in the desert to visit Bedouin communities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it represents the life and heritage of Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the founding father of the UAE, and provides insight into the traditional Bedouin lifestyle.
world knowledge.Details: Behind the museum is the Al Ain Oasis, with an entrance close by, and a path leading through the oasis to the Al Ain National Museum.

world knowledge.Name: Florida State Capitol
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Florida State Capitol in Tallahassee, Florida, is an architecturally and historically significant building listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The first territorial government met in a log building. A capitol building was constructed in 1826 but never completely finished. It was torn down in 1839 to make room for the erection of the present structure, which was completed in 1845, just prior to Florida's entry into the United States as the 27th state. Several additions to the historic capitol have been made throughout the years.

Major_Events.Description: The Historic Capitol was restored to its 1902 appearance, including the Governor's Suite, Supreme Court, House of Representatives and Senate chambers, rotunda, and halls.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Florida State Capitol was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The Historic Capitol's cupola was restored, including new copper roofing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Classical Revival style with an elaborate art glass dome, red and white striped awnings, and a representation of the Florida State Seal over the entry columns. The New Capitol follows Neoclassicism, with an ornate grill surrounding a white-columned box.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Capitol is a symbol of Florida's political history and growth. It houses the Florida Historic Capitol Museum, which exhibits the state's political history. The building is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Details: The Capitol Complex includes the Historic Capitol (Old Capitol) and the New Capitol. The New Capitol houses executive and legislative offices and the chambers of the Florida Legislature. The Historic Capitol serves as a museum. The Capitol Complex is open to the public Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (excluding state holidays). The Observation Deck on the 22nd floor offers views of Tallahassee and features an art gallery and the Freedom Shrine.

world knowledge.Name: Tregarden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tregarden is a Grade II* listed large house built by the Barrett family in the late 16th century. The house became a farmhouse in the 19th century and is currently a restored manor house owned by the Tremayne family.

Major_Events.Event: Marriage of William Godolphin to the Barrett heiress
Major_Events.Description: The entrance archway is dated 1631, marking the marriage of William Godolphin to the Barrett heiress.
The Hearth Tax Returns for 1664 record the house as having 8 hearths.
Tregarden was listed as a Grade II* building on 4 November 1988.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is built to a traditional E-shaped Elizabethan plan. It is a two-storey house built of rubble stone with a regular slate roof. The chimney stacks are also rubble and have seventeenth century granite caps. The interior features original elements like a chamfered fireplace, well-preserved plasterwork, a sixteenth or early seventeenth century granite fireplace, and seventeenth century garderobes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tregarden is a well-preserved example of Elizabethan architecture and reflects the historical and cultural heritage of Cornwall. Its Grade II* listing underscores its architectural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a large house, later a farmhouse, and currently a restored manor house.
world knowledge.Details: The entrance archway has an inscription "1631" but the house likely predates this. The property was reroofed in the twentieth century.

world knowledge.Name: Turvey House and Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Turvey Estate was bought in 1786 from Charles Henry Mordaunt, Fifth Earl of Peterborough, by Charles Higgins, Sheriff of London in that year. John Higgins, a cousin of Charles Higgins, acquired part of the estate, and in the 1790s he built Turvey House. The house was likely designed by the architect, John Wing of Bedford. On his death in 1813, the estate was inherited by his eldest son Thomas Charles Higgins, High Sheriff of Bedfordshire in 1823. During the period from then until his death in 1865 there were many changes to the estate: the house was enlarged with an upper storey added in the 1830s, and modifications to the parkland included rerouting of driveways. The Higgins family name remained associated with the estate; in 1939 Prunella Higgins married Lieutenant Colonel Sir Hanmer Hanbury, and the current custodians are Charles (their grandson) and Grace Hanbury, the seventh generation of the family to live in the house.

Major_Events.Description: The estate was bought from Charles Henry Mordaunt, Fifth Earl of Peterborough, by Charles Higgins, Sheriff of London.
John Higgins built Turvey House, likely designed by architect John Wing of Bedford.
The estate was inherited by Thomas Charles Higgins, High Sheriff of Bedfordshire in 1823.

Major_Events.Event: Marriage of Prunella Higgins to Sir Hanmer Hanbury
Major_Events.Description: Prunella Higgins married Lieutenant Colonel Sir Hanmer Hanbury, continuing the family association with the estate.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is in Neoclassical style. The south-west front has seven bays, with Corinthian columns at the end bays; the north-east front has a tetrastyle Doric porch. South-west of the house is a terrace and a small parterre; north of the house there is a walled kitchen garden, an ornamental garden and pleasure grounds. Beyond this there is parkland, planted with oak, beech, ash, lime, maple and poplar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gardens and parkland are listed Grade II in Historic England's Register of Parks and Gardens, and the house is a Grade I listed building. The estate has been associated with the Higgins family for generations, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Venue for weddings, events and location shoots.
world knowledge.Details: The park, north-west of the village, is bounded on the west by the River Great Ouse and on the east by Carlton Road. The main entrance is near the parish church at the south end, where there is a stone lodge (Bottom Lodge, a Grade II listed building). A second entrance is on Carlton Road, also marked by a stone lodge (Top Lodge, Grade II listed), which leads to the courtyard on the north-eastern side of the house. The house is in the centre of the park, on a slight rise above the river; there is a commanding view to the south-west across the park towards the river and beyond.

world knowledge.Name: Croome Court
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Croome Court is a mid-18th-century Neo-Palladian mansion surrounded by extensive landscaped parkland. It was designed by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown for George Coventry, 6th Earl of Coventry, and represents Brown's first landscape design and major architectural project. The mansion and park have undergone various ownerships and uses, including as a school, a Hare Krishna center, and now as a tourist attraction managed by the National Trust.

Major_Events.Description: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown redesigned the house and estate for George Coventry, 6th Earl of Coventry.
The mansion was requisitioned during World War II by the Ministry of Works and briefly used as a refuge for the Dutch Royal family.
The mansion was restored and opened to the public by the National Trust after being purchased by the Croome Heritage Trust in 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Palladian style with Bath stone and limestone ashlar exterior. Features include a slate roof, pyramid roofs over corner towers, and Roman Doric and Ionic elements. Interior designed by Capability Brown and Robert Adam, with notable rooms such as the Saloon, Tapestry Room, and Long Gallery.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Croome Court is significant as the first major architectural and landscape project by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown, marking a seminal work in English landscape design. It also reflects the cultural and social history of the Coventry family and their estate.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion is managed by the National Trust and is part of a larger estate that includes parkland, gardens, and various follies and temples designed by Robert Adam and James Wyatt. The estate has been restored and is open to the public, offering insights into 18th-century architecture and landscape design.

world knowledge.Name: Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 5300 South Howell Avenue, Milwaukee, Wisconsin, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established in 1920 as Hamilton Airport, it was purchased by Milwaukee County in 1926 and renamed Milwaukee County Airport. Renamed General Mitchell Field in 1941 after Milwaukee native and air power advocate Brigadier General William 'Billy' Mitchell. The current terminal opened in 1955 and has undergone several renovations and expansions.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed in honor of United States Army General Billy Mitchell.
Mitchell Field was leased to the War Department for use as a World War II prisoner-of-war camp, housing over 3,000 prisoners.
The present terminal opened, designed by Leigh Fisher and Associates.

Major_Events.Event: Rebranding to Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed to highlight its location, though the old name is still used by the FAA and US government.
Following an accident in 2007, the airport expanded the runway safety areas.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The terminal features a mix of asphalt and concrete runways, with a main terminal building that has undergone several renovations and expansions. The terminal includes concourses, gates, and various amenities such as retail outlets, a food court, and a museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after General Billy Mitchell, a key figure in the development of the United States Air Force. It serves as a major transportation hub for the Milwaukee metropolitan area and surrounding regions, and has been recognized for its quality by the Airports Council International.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial, cargo, and military flights.

Details.Military_Use: Home to the 128th Air Refueling Wing of the Wisconsin Air National Guard.

world knowledge.Name: Flamenco Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Flamenco Beach was used as a weapons-testing ground by the United States Navy for more than 30 years until their departure in 1975. Two rusting M4 Sherman tanks left behind have become a unique feature of the beach.

Major_Events.Description: Flamenco Beach was ranked 3rd best beach in the world.

Major_Events.Event: Regained Blue Flag Beach international distinction
Major_Events.Description: Flamenco Beach was recognized for its environmental and quality standards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural beach with white sand, shallow turquoise waters, and a reef approximately a quarter mile off the coast where the surf breaks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Flamenco Beach is the top-ranked beach in Puerto Rico and one of the top beaches in the world. It is known for its pristine beauty, unique features like the graffiti-covered tanks, and its role as a major breeding ground for sea turtles.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public beach and popular tourist destination for swimming, camping, and scuba diving or snorkeling.

Details.Wildlife: Home to species of parrot fish, blue tang, multiple species of wrasse, and other Caribbean Sea fish species. Crustacean species such as Ghost Crab are also observed. Some 50,000 seabirds visit Culebra's Flamenco Peninsula each summer to nest. Leatherback and hawksbill sea turtles may be seen as the beaches are a major breeding ground for them.
Details.Facilities: Bathroom facilities, showers, lifeguard towers, kiosks selling food and beach accessories, and a designated camping area with potable water, bathrooms, and shower facilities.
Details.Access: Easy access from the town of Dewey where the ferry boat arrives.

world knowledge.Name: Istana Nurul Iman
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Istana Nurul Iman is the official residence of the Sultan of Brunei, Hassanal Bolkiah, and the seat of the Brunei government. It was designed by Filipino Visayan architect Leandro V. Locsin and completed in 1984. The palace is often at the centre of state occasions and royal hospitality.

Major_Events.Description: The palace receives about 110,000 visitors over a three-day period where the guests receive gifts of food as well as green packets containing money for young children.

Major_Events.Event: Ramadhan Tadarus and Tarawih prayer gathering
Major_Events.Description: The palace is open to Muslims during 10 days of the Ramadhan period for Tadarus and Tarawih prayer gathering.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Leandro Locsin with golden domes and vaulted roofs reflecting Brunei's Islamic and Malay influences. The interior was designed by Khuan Chew.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is a symbol of Brunei's Islamic and Malay heritage and serves as the official residence of the Sultan and the seat of the Brunei government.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official residence of the Sultan of Brunei and seat of the Brunei government
world knowledge.Details: The palace contains 1,788 rooms, 257 bathrooms, a banquet hall for 5,000 guests, a mosque for 1,500 people, a 110-car garage, an air-conditioned stable for 200 polo ponies, and five swimming pools. It also has 564 chandeliers, 51,000 light bulbs, 44 stairwells, and 18 elevators. The palace is not open to the public except during specific Islamic celebrations.

world knowledge.Name: The New Metroland
world knowledge.Address: Dunston, Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Metrocentre is a shopping and entertainment complex built on the former site of Dunston Power Station. It was financed by the Church Commissioners of England and developed by Cameron Hall Developments. The first phase opened in 1986, and it has since grown to become one of the largest shopping centres in the UK.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the first phase (Red Mall)
Major_Events.Description: The first phase of Metrocentre, the Red Mall, opened on 28 April 1986, featuring a large Carrefour supermarket and the first out-of-town branch of Marks & Spencer.
Metroland, Europe's largest indoor amusement park at the time, opened in February 1988 with rides including a rollercoaster, Ferris wheel, and dodgem cars.
The centre was sold to Capital Shopping Centres (later intu Properties) for £364 million, with the Church Commissioners retaining a 10% stake.

Metroland closed on 20 April 2008 despite local opposition, with proceeds from the final night going to charity. Many rides were scrapped or sold, with the rollercoaster relocating to The Big Sheep in Devon.
The centre was rebranded as intu Metrocentre following the renaming of its parent company, Capital Shopping Centres Group, to intu Properties.
Following the collapse of intu, the centre was rebranded as The Metrocentre, with Sovereign Centros overseeing asset management.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Metrocentre features five malls (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, and Platinum) with a mix of retail and leisure spaces. The Qube, an entertainment area, is clad with zinc and glass to distinguish it from the rest of the centre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Metrocentre is a significant retail and leisure hub in the UK, known for its size and variety of offerings. It has played a key role in the economic development of the region and has been a popular destination for shopping and entertainment since its opening.
world knowledge.Details: Metrocentre includes 210 shops, 63 restaurants, an Odeon cinema, Namco Funscape, Clip n’ Climb, Treetop Golf, and The Escapologist. It also features a large bus station, Metrocentre railway station, and approximately 10,000 parking spaces. The adjacent Metro Retail Park and MetrOasis provide additional retail and dining options.

world knowledge.Name: Asmara International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Asmara International Airport is the international airport of Asmara, the capital of Eritrea. Constructed by the Italian colonial authorities in 1922, it was the first airport in Italian Eritrea, initially named 'Aeroporto di Gura'. It served as the main military airport and began offering civilian and commercial flights in the mid-1930s. The airport has undergone several renovations and expansions, particularly after being nearly destroyed during World War II. It became an international portal following Eritrea's independence in the 1990s.

Major_Events.Description: An agreement was signed with British Imperial Airways to connect Asmara to Khartoum, starting a regular commercial route.
Ala Littoria launched an intercontinental connection called 'Linea dell'Impero' between Mogadishu-Asmara-Khartoum-Tripoli and Rome, lasting four days.
During the Eritrean-Ethiopian War, the airport was bombed by Ethiopia.
The airport was bombed again by Ethiopia during the Eritrean-Ethiopian War.
Lufthansa suspended service to Frankfurt via Jeddah due to issues with unconvertible nakfa in Eritrea.
After renewed relations with Ethiopia, the airport started accepting flights from Addis Ababa for the first time since the war.

Major_Events.Event: Ethiopian Airlines ordered to suspend flights
Major_Events.Description: The Eritrean Civil Aviation Authority ordered Ethiopian Airlines to suspend flights to Eritrea, citing various issues including luggage theft and price hikes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a small terminal, a short runway, and is located at a high altitude of 2300 m. It has undergone several renovations and expansions since its original construction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Asmara International Airport is culturally and historically significant as it was the first airport in Italian Eritrea and has played a crucial role in the region's aviation history, particularly during the colonial period and post-independence era.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has capacity restrictions due to its small terminal, short runway, and high altitude. It also serves as an Eritrean Air Force base. Lufthansa operated Airbus A340 aircraft on a FRA-JED-ASM service as recently as 2012.

world knowledge.Name: Wild Waves Theme Park
world knowledge.Address: 36201 Enchanted Parkway S, Federal Way, Washington
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wild Waves Theme & Water Park, originally opened as The Enchanted Village in 1977, has evolved through multiple ownership changes and expansions. It began as a small amusement park with a few rides and later incorporated a water park in 1984. The park has undergone several name changes and management transitions, including acquisitions by Six Flags, CNL Income Properties, and EPR Properties. It has grown to become the largest waterpark in the Northwest, featuring numerous rides and attractions.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened as The Enchanted Village with a half-dozen rides, a playground, wading pool, and petting zoo.
The 24-acre Wild Waves Waterpark opened adjacent to Enchanted Village, forming the combined amusement complex known as Enchanted Parks.
Jeff Stock sold his shares of Enchanted Parks, Inc., to Six Flags for $19.3 million.

Major_Events.Event: Name reversion to Enchanted Village and Wild Waves Water Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was split into two separate parks with separate entrances and ticketing options.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Wild Waves Theme and Water Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was renamed again to Wild Waves Theme and Water Park under new ownership by EPR Properties.
A 33-year-old man died in the Activity Pool due to drowning, with reports of missed rescue opportunities.
The park did not open due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with tickets and season passes rolled over into 2021.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of amusement rides and water attractions, including roller coasters, water slides, and pools. The layout includes separate areas for the theme park and water park, with various rides manufactured by companies like Zamperla and S&S Power.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wild Waves Theme & Water Park is a popular summer destination in the Pacific Northwest, offering entertainment and recreational activities for families and visitors. It holds historical significance as the Northwest's largest waterpark and has undergone several transformations reflecting changes in ownership and public demand.
world knowledge.Details: The park operates seasonally from May to October and features 4 roller coasters and 10 water rides. It has undergone multiple management changes, with current ownership by EPR Properties and operation by Premier Parks, LLC. The park's slogan is 'goWILD'.

world knowledge.Name: Killerton
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Killerton is an 18th-century house built by Sir Thomas Acland, 7th baronet, in 1778. The manor of Columbjohn was purchased by Sir John Acland, and the adjoining estate of Killerton was purchased by his nephew Sir Arthur Acland in 1612. The house and estate were given to the National Trust by Sir Richard Acland, 15th Baronet in 1944.

Major_Events.Description: The estate was given to the National Trust by Sir Richard Acland, 15th Baronet.
An archaeological dig discovered what is believed to be a footprint of an intended replacement home to the current Killerton, known as the lost house of Devon, designed by architect James Wyatt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Killerton House is a Georgian country house. The chapel was built in 1738 to the designs of Charles Robert Cockerell. The garden was created in the 1770s by John Veitch, featuring rhododendrons, magnolias, herbaceous borders, rare trees, an ice house, and a 19th-century summer house.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Killerton is significant for its historical architecture, landscape design, and collection of 18th- to 20th-century costumes. It also includes the remains of an Iron Age hill fort and evidence of Roman occupation.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a steep wooded hillside with the remains of an Iron Age hill fort (Dolbury) and evidence of Roman occupation. The house and Bear's Hut summerhouse are Grade II* listed buildings, and the gardens are Grade II* listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. The National Trust displays the house as a comfortable home with a collection of period costumes.

world knowledge.Name: Gawsworth Old Rectory
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gawsworth Old Rectory is a medieval house built around 1470 by rector George Baguley, with possible financial assistance from Sir Thomas Fytton (Fitton). It served as a rectory to St. James' Church until 1953. The house underwent restorations in c.1724 by rector William Hall and in 1873 by architect Richard Norman Shaw. It is now a private residence.

Major_Events.Description: Built by rector George Baguley, possibly with financial help from Sir Thomas Fytton (Fitton).
Restored by rector William Hall.
Restored by architect Richard Norman Shaw.
Sold for £3.25 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Timber-framed house with a rare surviving "open hall." Much of the timber framing is close studded, and the roof is of plain tiles. Described as "one of the best preserved medium-sized houses of the period in Cheshire."
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a Grade I listed building, recognized for its exceptional preservation and the rare survival of its open hall. It is considered an important example of medieval architecture in Cheshire.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a rectory to St. James' Church; now a private residence.
world knowledge.Details: The house is not open to the public. It was designated as a Grade I listed building on 25 July 1952 (Reference no. 1139496).

world knowledge.Name: Château de Thoiry
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Thoiry was built in the 16th century by Raoul Moreau, an alchemist and treasurer of the King of France. It was designed by architect Philibert de L'Orme to be in perfect harmony with nature, with the center arch marking the position of the sun during solstices. The castle, zoo, and botanical garden were opened to the public in 1965.

Major_Events.Description: The Château de Thoiry was opened to the public as a 150-hectare castle, zoo, and botanical garden.
A Southern white rhinoceros named Vince was found shot dead with one horn removed and another partially sawn off, marking the first reported live animal poaching at a European zoo.
A 37-year-old woman was severely injured after being attacked by three wolves in the American reserve area of the zoo, which she entered on foot despite safety warnings.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle was designed by architect Philibert de L'Orme to be in perfect harmony with nature, featuring a center arch that marks the position of the sun during the summer and winter solstices.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château de Thoiry is a significant historical and cultural site due to its 16th-century architecture, its role as a wildlife conservation and education center, and its unique blend of historical and natural attractions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement Park (castle, zoo, and botanical garden)
world knowledge.Details: The site includes a 240-acre African Reserve where animals roam freely, a walk-through zoo with various species, a maze, and several gardens. The castle remains the home of the Counts of La Panouse, with parts open to the public for tours led by costumed guides.

world knowledge.Name: Candie Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Candie Gardens is a park in St Peter Port, Guernsey, originally established as a Victorian pleasure gardens in 1894. The gardens were originally those of Candie House, and became a public park in 1894.

Major_Events.Description: Candie Gardens became a public park.
The statue was erected to mark Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee. It was cast in bronze by C B Birch and is a replica of those in Aberdeen and the Thames Embankment.
The statue was a gift from the French Government as thanks for the hospitality shown towards Victor Hugo during his exile on Guernsey. It was sculpted by Jean Boucher.
The Beatles performed two shows at the former Pavilion on 18 August 1963, their only performances on the island, promoted by Baron Pontin.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration of Victorian Public Flower Garden
Major_Events.Description: The Lower Gardens' rare surviving example of a Victorian Public Flower Garden was restored.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Upper Gardens feature panoramic views over the islands of Herm and Sark. The Lower Gardens feature a rare surviving example of a Victorian Public Flower Garden and two surviving greenhouses dating from 1792 and 1793.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Candie Gardens is culturally significant for its Victorian heritage, statues of Queen Victoria and Victor Hugo, and its role as a public park and cultural venue, including its connection to The Beatles' performance.
world knowledge.Details: The Upper Gardens feature the Guernsey Museum and an adjacent café in the former bandstand. The former Candie House is now the Priaulx Library. Café Victoria is located just behind the pavilion.

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II Airport
world knowledge.Address: KM.10 Talang Betutu District, Palembang, South Sumatra, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established as a civil airport in 1937, it was rebuilt during the Japanese occupation in 1942–1943. It became a joint civilian and military airfield in 1963, and was renamed to Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II Airport in 1985. The airport underwent significant expansions in 2005 and 2017 to accommodate increasing passenger traffic and the 2018 Asian Games.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was rebuilt during the Japanese occupation of Indonesia.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed in honor of Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II, the last sultan of Palembang.
The airport was expanded to accommodate the increased traffic during the 2018 Asian Games.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a three-floor passenger terminal, aerobridges, cargo terminals, and support buildings. The runway was extended to 3,000 meters x 60 meters, and the terminal area was expanded to 115,000 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II, a significant historical figure in Palembang. It serves as a major gateway to South Sumatra and has played a crucial role in regional development and international events like the 2018 Asian Games.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a passenger capacity of 4 million annually, with 43 check-in counters and an aircraft parking apron that can accommodate 19 aircraft. It is connected to the Palembang Light Rail Transit, which facilitates transportation to and from the airport.

world knowledge.Name: Kulturfabrik Moabit
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The building was constructed in 1911 by Ernst Scharnke for Wertheim, originally serving as a meat factory, biscuit factory, and other industrial uses. It was vacant and neglected from 1976 to 1991 due to its proximity to the Berlin Wall. After reunification, it was reopened in 1991 as Kulturfabrik Moabit, a cultural co-operative.

Major_Events.Description: After reunification, the building was reopened as a cultural co-operative, housing a cinema, theatre, and concert hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Former factory and warehouse building with industrial architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kulturfabrik Moabit serves as a cultural hub in Berlin, hosting various artistic and community events, and preserving the industrial heritage of the area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural co-operative (cinema, theatre, concert hall, art gallery, and community events).
world knowledge.Details: The Kulturfabrik Moabit includes associate members such as the Slaughterhouse club (live concerts), Fabriktheater club (theatre and jazz concerts), Filmrauschpalast club (art house cinema), and a café/pub. It also offers social and family work, childcare, and annual festivities like the Lange Nacht des Tauchens and Sommerfest.

world knowledge.Name: Tallinn Airport
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total warehouse space of ca 11,600 m²
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tallinn Airport, originally opened in 1936, is the largest international airport in Estonia. It was renamed Lennart Meri Tallinn Airport in 2009 after the former president of Estonia. The airport has undergone significant expansions and modernizations, including the construction of new terminals and runway extensions to accommodate growing passenger and cargo traffic.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened on 20 September 1936, although it had been operational since 1932.
The runway was extended to 3480 meters, making it the longest in the Baltic states.
The terminal was expanded by 35,000 m², increasing its capacity to handle twice as many passengers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a single asphalt/concrete runway, six taxiways, and seventeen terminal gates. The terminal building was expanded in 2008, resulting in a T-shaped layout with 18 new gates, separate lounges for Schengen and non-Schengen passengers, and a new restaurant and cafes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tallinn Airport is a key gateway to Estonia, reflecting the country's modernization and connectivity. It is named after Lennart Meri, a significant figure in Estonian history, symbolizing national pride and progress.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving passenger and cargo flights.
world knowledge.Details: Tallinn Airport aims for carbon neutrality by 2030, with plans to generate 40% of its electricity needs from solar farms. The airport has four cargo terminals and serves as a hub for several airlines, including airBaltic and SmartLynx Airlines Estonia. It also features an EXPO Center, a lending library, and an automatic border control system.

world knowledge.Name: Atlanta Beltline
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Atlanta Beltline is a 22-mile long multi-use corridor on a former railway corridor which encircles the core of Atlanta, Georgia. The project aims to reconnect neighborhoods and communities historically divided and marginalized by infrastructure, improve transportation, add green space, promote redevelopment, create and preserve affordable housing, and showcase arts and culture. The idea originated in a 1991 proposal by the Georgia Rails-to-Trails Conservancy and was further developed by Georgia Tech student Ryan Gravel in his 1999 master's thesis.

Major_Events.Description: The Atlanta Beltline Partnership was formed to advocate for the project.
Atlanta Beltline, Inc. was formed to develop the project.
The first trail to be built on the Beltline, the 2.4-mile West End Trail, was opened.
The first section of the Northside Trail opened.
The 3.2-mile Westside Trail was opened.
The James M. Cox Foundation gave $6 Million to the PATH Foundation to connect the Silver Comet Trail to the Atlanta Beltline.
The James M. Cox foundation announced a $30 million pledge to the PATH Foundation in support of the Northwest Beltline trails project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Beltline features multi-use paths, greenways, and repurposed industrial buildings. It includes trails for walking, bicycling, and rollerskating, as well as plans for a light rail streetcar system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Atlanta Beltline is culturally significant as it reconnects historically divided neighborhoods, promotes arts and culture, and revitalizes urban areas. It also addresses issues of transportation, green space, and affordable housing.
world knowledge.Details: The Beltline connects 45 diverse neighborhoods and will eventually include 33 miles of multi-use paths. It is expected to create 50,000 permanent jobs and bring $10 billion of economic development to the city. The project has faced criticism for contributing to gentrification in some areas.

world knowledge.Name: Évreux Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Évreux Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral of Our Lady of Évreux, is a Catholic church located in Évreux, Normandy, France. It was built in the 10th century, with parts of the lower nave dating from the 11th century. A fire in 1119 destroyed much of the earlier building. The cathedral underwent various phases of construction and restoration over the centuries, with significant contributions from figures like Gautier de Varinfroy and Jean Balue. The cathedral was thoroughly restored in 1896 and suffered damage during World War II, leading to further restorations.

Major_Events.Description: A fire destroyed much of the earlier building.
A thorough restoration was completed.
The cathedral suffered damage during World War II, including the destruction of stained glass windows and the spire.
The stained glass windows were restored by Jean-Jacques Grüber.
A new organ was built by the Atelier Quoirin of Saint-Didier.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Renaissance, Gothic, and late Gothic (Flamboyant) styles. It has a 7-bay aisled nave with twin towers in a post-medieval style. The plan is in a cross-style layout with a northern transept arm in a Gothic style. The choir is in an earlier Gothic architectural style, and the octagonal central tower with its elegant spire was constructed by Jean Balue. The nave has three stories with semicircular arches in the Norman style, rib-vaulted ceilings, and clerestory windows with Parisian tracery.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Évreux Cathedral is a national monument and the seat of the Bishop of Évreux. It is significant for its architectural styles, historical events, and religious importance. The cathedral's stained glass windows, carved wooden screens, and rose windows are masterpieces of their respective periods. It also represents the influence of important historical figures and the evolution of architectural techniques over centuries.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is devoted to Notre-Dame at Evreux, located 80 km west of Paris. The bishop's palace, a 15th-century building, adjoins the south side of the cathedral. The spire, called 'Clocher d’Argent', rises to a height of 78m after its reconstruction. The Virgin Chapel is the largest of the chapels in the cathedral, matching the size of other chapels in France at the time. The cathedral's organ contains around 4000 pipes.

image_name: Saint Mary Church of the Holy Belt

world knowledge.Name: Saint Mary Church of the Holy Belt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saint Mary of the Holy Belt (Um Al Zennar) Cathedral is a historical Syriac Orthodox cathedral in Homs, Syria. It is the seat of the Syriac Orthodox Archbishop of Homs and Hama. The present structure dates from 1852 under Bishop Julius Peter, but the site has been a place of Christian worship since 59 AD. The church once served as the headquarters of the universal church. It contains a venerated Holy Girdle believed to be a section of the belt of Mary, mother of Jesus.

Major_Events.Description: The church was damaged during confrontations between the armed opposition and the security forces.
The church was restored by an extensive effort of the faithful, and the Divine Liturgy was celebrated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church may rest on Byzantine foundations, and the present structure dates from 1852.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is one of the prominent churches of the Universal Syriac Orthodox Church and a Marian Pilgrim Centre. It contains a venerated Holy Girdle believed to be a section of the belt of Mary, mother of Jesus.
world knowledge.Details: The church is the Syriac church's equivalent of the Cincture of the Theotokos of the Greek Orthodox Church and Girdle of Thomas of the Catholic Church.

image_name: De Pont Museum of Contemporary Art

world knowledge.Name: De Pont Museum of Contemporary Art
world knowledge.Address: Wilhelminapark 1, 5041 EA Tilburg, North Brabant, Netherlands
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The De Pont Museum is a contemporary art museum in Tilburg, North Brabant, the Netherlands. It was named after the lawyer and businessman Jan de Pont (1915-1987). After his death, his estate provided for the establishment of a foundation (the Janivo Stichting) to stimulate contemporary visual art. With its founding director Hendrik Driessen, the decision was made to transform a Tilburg wool-spinning mill into a museum. Since its opening in 1992, the collection has grown to include more than 800 works by approximately eighty nationally and internationally known artists.

Major_Events.Description: The De Pont Museum opened its doors on September 12, 1992, after the refurbishment of a former wool-spinning mill by Benthem Crouwel Architects.
The museum expanded with a new wing designed by Benthem Crouwel Architects to accommodate film, video art, photography, and works on paper.
Anish Kapoor designed Sky Mirror for the museum's twenty-fifth anniversary, which was placed in Dutch public space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a former wool mill in Tilburg, which was refurbished by Benthem Crouwel Architects. The building maintains the factory's original character, with a spacious exhibition space and small wool-storage rooms. The museum has been expanded several times, including the addition of a project space, an auditorium, and a new exhibition space of 1100 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The De Pont Museum is significant for its role in stimulating contemporary visual art. It was among the first museums to be housed in a formerly industrial space, setting an example for future museums like Tate Modern in London. The museum's collection includes key works by internationally renowned artists, and it has introduced several artists to the Netherlands or given them their first major exhibition.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum of modern and contemporary art
world knowledge.Details: The museum's forecourt is named Meester J.H. de Pontplein after the founder. The museum has a distinctive entrance gate added in 2012 and a garden designed by landscape architect Sophie Walker. The museum's collection includes masterpieces such as Grapes (Ai WeiWei), Vertigo (Anish Kapoor), and The Greeting (Bill Viola).

world knowledge.Name: Gahirmatha Beach
world knowledge.Address: Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary, Kendrapara, Odisha, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gahirmatha Beach was notified as a marine wildlife sanctuary by the Government of Odisha on 27 September 1997. It is the only marine wildlife sanctuary in Odisha and is crucial for the conservation of olive ridley sea turtles.

Major_Events.Event: Mass nesting of olive ridley sea turtles
Major_Events.Description: In April 2017, at least 200,000 baby olive ridley turtles emerged from their pits within 24 hours, marking a significant event in turtle conservation.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gahirmatha Beach is the world's most important nesting beach for olive ridley sea turtles. It plays a vital role in the conservation of these turtles, which are listed as 'vulnerable' in the IUCN Red Data Book and protected under various international conventions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Wildlife conservation and nesting ground for olive ridley sea turtles
world knowledge.Details: The beach separates the Bhitarkanika Mangroves from the Bay of Bengal and is part of the Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary. The sanctuary includes a core area of 725.50 km² and a buffer zone of 709.50 km². Olive ridley sea turtles migrate here annually for mating and nesting, with nesting figures ranging between 100,000 to 500,000 each year. The turtles face threats from mass mortality due to fishing activities and other human interventions.

world knowledge.Name: Kongeparken
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kongeparken, also known as The King's Park, is an amusement park located in the village of Ålgård, near Stavanger in Norway. It was opened by Gabriel Ålgård on May 16, 1986, with an initial focus on outdoor activities such as BMX, roller-skating, and golf. Despite attracting over 200,000 visitors in its opening year, the park went bankrupt by July. In 1997, the Lund family, who had extensive experience in the amusement park industry, purchased Kongeparken. They revitalized the park by introducing new themes and activities, particularly around the theme of bears, which became central to the park's identity.

Major_Events.Description: Kongeparken was opened by Gabriel Ålgård on May 16, 1986, with a focus on outdoor activities such as BMX, roller-skating, and golf.
Despite attracting over 200,000 visitors in its opening year, Kongeparken went bankrupt by July 1986.
The Lund family, who had extensive experience in the amusement park industry, purchased Kongeparken in 1997 and revitalized it by introducing new themes and activities.

Major_Events.Event: Introduction of the Fossen water ride
Major_Events.Description: The Fossen water ride was introduced in 2013 as part of the park's ongoing efforts to add new attractions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Kongeparken features a variety of rides and attractions, including a roller coaster with spinning gondolas, a bobsleigh track, a do-it-yourself chocolate factory, and a children's fire station. The park is themed around bears, with notable attractions including a castle housing Brumle and Brumleline, the King and Queen of Bears.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kongeparken is the largest amusement park in the south-west of Norway and a major tourist destination in the county of Rogaland. It has won multiple awards both nationally and internationally. The park's theme of bears, particularly the story of Brumle and Brumleline, adds a unique cultural element that appeals to children and families.
world knowledge.Details: Kongeparken is targeted at children aged from three to 12 years old but also offers more challenging activities for older children. The park features over 50 rides, restaurants, and other attractions. New rides are introduced each year. The park also hosts 'Jul i Kongeparken' (Christmas in Kongeparken) in November and December, featuring fairy lights, Christmas trees, elves, carol singing, and family workshops.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Mário Helênio
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Municipal Radialista Mário Helênio, also known as Estádio Mário Helênio, was built in 1988 and is owned by the Juiz de Fora City Hall. It was named after the Juiz de Fora radio broadcaster Mário Helênio. In the late 1980s and early 1990s, the stadium was used by major Rio de Janeiro clubs due to the large number of supporters in the city.

Major_Events.Description: The inaugural match was played on October 30, 1988, when Sport Juiz de Fora beat Tupi 2–0. The first goal of the stadium was scored by Sport's André.
The stadium's attendance record stands at 62,180, set on October 30, 1988, when Sport Juiz De Fora and Tupi drew 2–0.

Major_Events.Event: Zico's Last Official Match for Flamengo
Major_Events.Description: On December 2, 1989, Zico played his last official match for Flamengo at Estádio Radialista Mário Helênio. Flamengo beat Fluminense 5–0.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it was used by major Rio de Janeiro football clubs in the late 1980s and early 1990s due to the large number of supporters in Juiz de Fora. It also hosted Zico's last official match for Flamengo.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a maximum capacity of 31,863 people. It is currently used mostly for football matches.

world knowledge.Name: Al Noor International School
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al Noor International School is a private school situated in Bahrain and founded on 6 September 1993 by private investors. The school teaches over 3000 students from more than 40 countries, mainly the United States, the United Kingdom, Bahrain, India, and Pakistan. It started with a programme of classes for primary levels in the district of Mahooz, prior to its relocation to the island of Sitra. It currently caters to the educational needs of students from over 40 countries and follows a curricular program made up of three types: British, Bahraini, and Indian.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The school is culturally significant as it provides education to a diverse student body from over 40 countries and offers a unique blend of British, Bahraini, and Indian curricula. It was named the second school in the Middle East to become a Cambridge Fellowship Center and the first in Bahrain.
world knowledge.Details: The school has six computer laboratories, and laboratories dedicated to Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. It follows the IGCSE course offered by the University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate as well as AS Level (Advanced Subsidiary Level), and A Level (Advanced Level) qualifications. The Indian curriculum follows the central board of secondary Education (CBSE), Delhi, and is widely recognized as one of the oldest educational systems in India. CBSE admissions are very sought after, and the curriculum gives students a unique advantage for higher studies. The school is affiliated to CBSE, Delhi. Grades range from kindergarten to Grade 12.

world knowledge.Name: Recklinghausen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Recklinghausen was first mentioned in 1017 as Ricoldinchuson and became the center of the surrounding Vest Recklinghausen by 1150. It received town privileges in 1236. The city experienced multiple ownership changes in the 15th and 16th centuries and was pawned to the Elector of Cologne in 1576. It was plundered several times during the Cologne War (1582–83, 1586, 1587). Recklinghausen was also the site of over 100 witchcraft trials (1514–1710). In the 19th century, it became the capital of a sovereign Principality of the Dukes of Arenberg and later a Bürgermeisterei. During World War II, it housed a prisoner-of-war camp and a forced labour camp.

Major_Events.Description: The city was plundered by partisan armies during the Cologne War, a feud over religious parity in Electorate of Cologne and electoral influence in the Holy Roman Empire.
Recklinghausen was the site of more than 100 witchcraft trials, with peaks in 1580/81 and 1588/89. The last convicted person, Anna Spickermann, was executed in 1710.
During World War II, Recklinghausen housed the Stalag XX-B prisoner-of-war camp and a forced labour camp. The city was bombed by the RAF in 1945 and captured by the US 137th Infantry.
Recklinghausen hosts the annual Ruhrfestspiele, a cultural festival with international theatrical productions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The city features the Ruhrfestspielhaus, a theater remodeled in 2001, which won the German Architecture Award. It also includes sculptures like 'Die Liegende Nr 5' by Henry Moore and a brick sculpture by Per Kirkeby.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Recklinghausen is culturally significant for its annual Ruhrfestspiele festival and its museum of icons, the largest outside the Orthodox world. The city also has historical importance due to its role in the Cologne War and witchcraft trials.
world knowledge.Details: Recklinghausen is home to an icon museum with over 1,000 Orthodox works and early Coptic Christian art. The city is connected by major motorways (A2, A43), the Rhein-Herne-Kanal, and two railway stations (Recklinghausen Hauptbahnhof and Recklinghausen Südbahnhof). The current mayor is Christoph Tesche (CDU).

world knowledge.Name: Jamshidieh Park
world knowledge.Address: Neighbourhood of Niavaran at the base of Kolakchal mountain, Tehran, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jamshidieh Park (or Jamshidieh Stone Garden) was established as a private garden by the Qajar prince and engineer Jamshid Davallu Qajar during the Pahlavi era. It became a public park in 1977 and was reconstructed and expanded with the addition of Ferdowsi garden in 1995.

Major_Events.Description: The private garden was converted into a public park.
The park was reconstructed and expanded with the addition of Ferdowsi garden.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stone garden's main waterfall and pond are central to the garden's design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jamshidieh Park is culturally significant as it was originally a private garden of a Qajar prince and later became a public space, reflecting the transition from private to public ownership in Iran's history.
world knowledge.Details: This Tehran County location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Modena Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Modena Cathedral, dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary and Saint Geminianus, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Modena, Italy. It was consecrated in 1184 and is an important Romanesque building in Europe. The site had two churches since the 5th century, but the discovery of Saint Geminianus' burial site led to the construction of this cathedral. The initial design was by Lanfranco, and the cathedral was later embellished by Anselmo da Campione and his heirs. It has been the archiepiscopal seat of the Archdiocese of Modena-Nonantola since 1986 and is designated as a World Heritage Site along with its bell tower, the Torre della Ghirlandina.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was consecrated by Pope Lucius III on July 12, 1184.
The cathedral and its bell tower were designated as a World Heritage Site during the 21st session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee.
The funeral of the famed tenor Luciano Pavarotti, a native of Modena, was held in the cathedral.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is a Romanesque building with a façade that exhibits different styles due to contributions by various architects and artists. It features a majestic rose-window added by Anselmo da Campione in the 13th century, two Roman-era lions supporting the entrance columns, and notable reliefs by Wiligelmus. The interior is divided into three naves, with a marble parapet by Anselmo da Campione portraying the Passion of Christ. The cathedral also houses a 14th-century wood crucifix and nativity scenes by Antonio Begarelli and Guido Mazzoni.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Modena Cathedral is culturally and historically significant as an important Romanesque building in Europe and a World Heritage Site. It is dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary and Saint Geminianus, Modena's patron saint. The cathedral's architecture and artworks, including the early Arthurian scene on the Porta della Pescheria, reflect the rich cultural heritage of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral's north portal, known as the Porta della Pescheria, features high relief carvings of secular scenes, including an early Arthurian scene dubbed the "Modena Archivolt." This scene is notable for depicting characters from the Arthurian legend, such as King Arthur, Guinevere, and Gawain, and is considered one of the earliest monumental sculptures to feature the Arthurian legend. The cathedral also houses the remains of Saint Geminianus in its crypt.

world knowledge.Name: Brukenthal National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Brukenthal National Museum was established in the late 18th century by Samuel von Brukenthal in his city palace. The collections were officially opened to the public in 1817, making it the oldest museum in modern-day Romania. Today, it comprises six museums located in different parts of Sibiu.

Major_Events.Description: The museum's collections were officially opened to the public, marking it as the oldest museum in modern-day Romania.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the Brukenthal Palace, which features architectural styles from the late 18th century. The Museum of History is part of a building considered the most important ensemble of non-religious Gothic architecture in Transylvania.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Brukenthal National Museum is culturally significant as it is the oldest museum in modern-day Romania and houses extensive collections of European art, historical artifacts, and scientific exhibits. It reflects the rich cultural and scientific heritage of Transylvania.
world knowledge.Details: The museum complex includes six museums: Art Galleries, Brukenthal Library, Museum of History, Museum of Pharmacology, Museum of Natural History, and Museum of Arms and Hunting Trophies. Each museum has its own distinct cultural programs and collections, ranging from European paintings to ancient medical instruments and natural history exhibits.

world knowledge.Name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
world knowledge.Area: Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area, Illinois, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) was established in 1867 as a public land-grant research university. Originally named 'Illinois Industrial University,' it was one of the 37 universities created under the first Morrill Land-Grant Act. The university has grown to become the flagship institution of the University of Illinois System, with over 59,000 students, making it one of the largest public universities in the United States. The university has a rich history of academic and research excellence, with significant contributions to various fields including engineering, computer science, and agriculture.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to University of Illinois
Major_Events.Description: The Illinois Industrial University officially changed its name to the 'University of Illinois,' reflecting its agricultural, mechanical, and liberal arts curriculum.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the Alma Mater statue
Major_Events.Description: The Alma Mater statue, a prominent campus landmark created by alumnus Lorado Taft, was unveiled on June 11, 1929.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
Major_Events.Description: The university name officially changed to the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign to establish a separate identity within the University of Illinois System.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the Carle Illinois College of Medicine
Major_Events.Description: The Carle Illinois College of Medicine, the first college created at Urbana-Champaign in 60 years, began classes in 2018.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of historic and modern buildings, with four main quads composing the center of the university. The campus is known for its landscape and architecture, including several buildings on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places such as Harker Hall, the Astronomical Observatory, and the Morrow Plots. The Undergraduate Library was constructed underground to preserve the adjacent Morrow Plots, the oldest continually used experimental agricultural fields in the United States.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is a world-leading institution in engineering and sciences, with significant contributions to technology, research, and education. It is culturally important as a hub for innovation and academic excellence, with a diverse student body and a strong tradition of student organizations and activities. The university's athletic teams, known as the Fighting Illini, are also a significant part of its cultural identity.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 16 schools and colleges offering over 150 undergraduate and 100 graduate programs. It is a member of the Association of American Universities and classified among 'R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity.' The campus library system is the fourth-largest university library in the United States by holdings. The university also hosts the National Center for Supercomputing Applications and has a significant impact on the local and global community through its research and innovation.

world knowledge.Name: Lusaka National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lusaka National Museum was created in collaboration with China in the 1980s, initially intended to focus on Zambian independence. By its official opening in October 1996, its focus had shifted to cultural history.

Major_Events.Description: The Lusaka National Museum officially opened to the public, focusing on cultural history.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum has two floors: an archaeological and historical section on the ground floor and a contemporary art gallery on the next floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum covers the history and culture of Zambia, from the Stone Age three million years ago to modern times, including pottery, tools, ornaments, sculptures, and paintings.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's ground floor features an archaeological and historical section, while the next floor houses a contemporary art gallery with sculptures and paintings.

world knowledge.Name: Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Ananda Coomaraswamy Mawatha, Colombo 07, Sri Lanka
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nelum Pokuna Theatre is a performing arts centre in Colombo, Sri Lanka. It was initially proposed by China in 2005 as a cultural theatre in memory of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's late husband Vijaya Kumaratunga. Construction began in 2006 and was completed in 2011. The theatre was officially opened on 15 December 2011 by Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapakse and China's Vice President of the Chinese Republican Committee, Sang Chiang.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was officially opened on 15 December 2011. The opening featured an opera produced by leading Sri Lankan artistes and a Chinese opera depicting the story of the fourth-century Chinese-Buddhist monk Fa-Hsien's travels to Sri Lanka.
The Theatre hosted its first symphony orchestra concert by the Commonwealth Festival Orchestra, with 87 musicians from the UK, India, and the Symphony Orchestra of Sri Lanka, conducted by James Ross.

Major_Events.Event: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting Opening Ceremony
Major_Events.Description: The Nelum Pokuna Theatre was the site of the opening ceremony of the 2013 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre features two permanent theatres—the main auditorium and an open-air theatre—and the ability to convert the front steps into an additional open-air theatre. The main auditorium has a 690 m² moving stage with the ability to raise and lower the orchestra pit. The building is designed by Kahawita De Silva & Associates and constructed by the Yanjian Group.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Nelum Pokuna Theatre is a significant cultural landmark in Sri Lanka, serving as a premier venue for performing arts, including music, concerts, theatre, and dance. It also hosts international conferences and events, symbolizing the cultural ties between Sri Lanka and China.
world knowledge.Details: The total estimated cost of the project is LKR 3,080 million, with LKR 2430 million provided by the Government of the People's Republic of China. The theatre is equipped with an auditorium with 1,288 seats, a library, training facilities, and parking for 500 vehicles. The venue has hosted various high-profile events, including the ABU Radio Song Festival 2014 (later moved) and the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in 2013.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) is a gravity dam on the Blue Nile River in Ethiopia. It was constructed to address Ethiopia's acute energy shortage and to export electricity to neighboring countries. The dam is the largest hydroelectric power plant in Africa and among the 20 largest in the world. The project was initiated in 2011 and completed in 2023, with significant regional controversy, particularly from Egypt, which depends heavily on the Nile for water.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone for the dam was laid on 2 April 2011 by Prime Minister Meles Zenawi.

Major_Events.Event: First phase of filling the reservoir
Major_Events.Description: The first phase of filling the reservoir began in July 2020, reaching a water level of 540 meters.
The dam produced electricity for the first time on 20 February 2022, delivering 375 MW to the grid.
The fourth filling of the reservoir was completed on 10 September 2023, with water levels reaching approximately 625 meters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The dam is a gravity dam made of roller-compacted concrete. It is 155 meters tall, 1,780 meters long, and has a structural volume of 10,400,000 m³. The dam features three spillways, two powerhouses with 13 turbines (2x 375 MW and 11x 400 MW), and a rock-filled saddle dam. The reservoir has a storage capacity of 74 km³ and a surface area of 1,874 km².
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The GERD is a symbol of Ethiopia's development and self-reliance. It is expected to significantly boost the country's economy by providing electricity and reducing energy shortages. The dam also represents a source of national pride, despite the regional controversies it has sparked, particularly with Egypt and Sudan.
world knowledge.Details: The GERD is expected to generate 5.15 GW of electricity, making it the largest hydroelectric power plant in Africa. The dam has been a source of significant regional tension, particularly with Egypt, which fears a reduction in the Nile's water flow. The project was funded through government bonds, private donations, and a loan from the Exim Bank of China. The dam's construction involved significant engineering challenges, including adjustments to the design to account for higher flow volumes and structural integrity concerns.

world knowledge.Name: Tapeley Park
world knowledge.Address: Tapeley Park, Westleigh, North Devon, England
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1704 (remodeled in the 19th century and early 20th century)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tapeley is a historic estate in the parish of Westleigh in North Devon, England. The present mansion house, Tapeley Park, was built or enlarged from an existing structure in about 1704, remodeled in the 19th century, and again in the early 20th century when pilasters, portico, pediment, and parapet were added to create a Queen Anne style building. The estate has passed through several prominent families, including the Clevland, Christie, and Giffard families. It was briefly turned into a hippie commune by Hector Christie in the late 20th century.

Major_Events.Description: The estate was inherited from the Clevland family by William Langham Christie of Glyndebourne in Sussex.

Tapeley Park was the subject of an episode of the Channel 4 television programme Country House Rescue, presented by the hotelier Ruth Watson, who advised on restoring the estate to a sound financial position.
Archibald Clevland, the only son of Augustus Saltren-Willett, died at the Battle of Inkerman as a cornet in the 17th Lancers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grade II* listed country house with Queen Anne style elements, including pilasters, portico, pediment, and parapet. The gardens are Grade II* listed and feature Italianate terraces, a working kitchen garden, and a permaculture garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tapeley Park is a significant historical estate with connections to prominent families and events, including the Glyndebourne Opera Festival. The gardens are notable for their design and public accessibility.
world knowledge.Details: The estate comprises about 6,000 acres, covering Saunton (including foreshore and beach), Braunton Burrows (sand dunes, partly a nature reserve and leased to the Ministry of Defence), Instow (including the foreshore purchased from the crown estate), and the village of Westleigh. The gardens are open to the public on a regular basis.

world knowledge.Name: Hasanuddin University
world knowledge.Address: Jl. Perintis Kemerdekaan Km. 10, Makassar, South Sulawesi, 90245, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hasanuddin University, abbreviated as Unhas, is one of the largest autonomous universities in Indonesia. Established on September 10, 1956, it is named after Sultan Hasanuddin, a former King of the Gowa Kingdom. The university's history began in 1947 as part of the Faculty of Economics of the University of Indonesia. It has since expanded to include 14 faculties and numerous degree programs.

Major_Events.Description: Hasanuddin University was officially established on September 10, 1956, through Government Regulation No. 23 of 1956.

The Tamalanrea Campus was inaugurated by President Soeharto on September 17, 1981, designed by Paddock Inc., Massachusetts, and built by OD 205, Netherlands in collaboration with PT Sangkuriang Bandung.
Hasanuddin University became one of several Autonomous Universities, freed from the need to seek Ministry approval for basic operations and budgetary matters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tamalanrea Campus was designed by Paddock Inc., Massachusetts, and built by OD 205, Netherlands in collaboration with PT Sangkuriang Bandung.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hasanuddin University is culturally significant as it is named after Sultan Hasanuddin, a former King of the Gowa Kingdom, and has played a crucial role in the development of higher education in Indonesia.
world knowledge.Details: Hasanuddin University has 14 faculties and offers a wide range of degree programs. It is one of the top universities in Indonesia and has achieved autonomous status, allowing it greater operational freedom.

world knowledge.Name: Mymensingh Zilla School
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mymensingh Zilla School (MZS) is a boys' public secondary school in Mymensingh, Bangladesh. The school was established as Hardinge School during the British Raj in 1846 and got the name Mymensingh Zilla School on 3 November 1853. It started as an English medium school called 'Hardinge School' at Mr. F. B. Camp's, the then Deputy Collector of the East India Company. The main and present school structures were built in 1912. The school had been used as a base of the British Army during World War II. It was also used as a training camp for freedom fighters during Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971.

Major_Events.Event: British Army base during World War II
Major_Events.Description: The school was used as a base of the British Army during World War II.

Major_Events.Event: Training camp for freedom fighters during Bangladesh Liberation War
Major_Events.Description: The school was used as a training camp for freedom fighters during Bangladesh Liberation War. More than 40 students sacrificed their lives fighting against the Pakistan Army.

Police fired tear-gas to subdue rioting Mymensingh Zilla School students. Sixty people were injured in the clash, which began when the students attempted to reoccupy part of their school hostel building that the government had recently given over to an adjacent primary training institute.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main and present school structures were built in 1912. The school compound was designed and reformed in 1965 by an American science teacher, Mr. Dril.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mymensingh Zilla School is one of the oldest and most prestigious schools in Bangladesh. It has a rich history dating back to the British Raj and has played significant roles during World War II and the Bangladesh Liberation War. The school has produced many notable alumni and has a strong tradition of academic and extracurricular excellence.
world knowledge.Details: The school provides education from the third through the tenth grade. Students choose between science and business studies streams from the ninth grade. The school has a strong tradition in sports, debate, music, and academic competitions. It has a BNCC team and scout activities. The school publishes a magazine called Oitijjho (Bengali: ঐতিহ্য).

world knowledge.Name: Walker Art Center
world knowledge.Address: 725 Vineland Place, Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 260,000 square foot, 8-story building on a 17-acre urban campus
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Walker Art Center began in 1879 as an art gallery in the home of lumber baron Thomas Barlow Walker. It was formally established as the Walker Art Gallery in 1927. With the support of the Federal Art Project of the Works Progress Administration, it became the Walker Art Center in January 1940. The current building, designed by Edward Larrabee Barnes, opened in 1971 and was expanded in 2005 by Herzog & de Meuron.

Major_Events.Description: With the support of the Federal Art Project, the Walker Art Gallery became the Walker Art Center.
The new building, designed by Edward Larrabee Barnes, opened.
A $67 million expansion designed by Herzog & de Meuron was completed, nearly doubling the size of the center.
The sculpture garden reopened after reconstruction, though delayed due to protests over Sam Durant's sculpture Scaffold.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original 1971 building was designed in a minimalist style with a plain, modular brick exterior and expansive white interior spaces. The 2005 expansion by Herzog & de Meuron features an abstract geometric tower made of aluminum mesh panels and glass windows, with windowed halls connecting to the original structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Walker is one of the most-visited modern and contemporary art museums in the U.S., known for its multidisciplinary approach and extensive collection of over 13,000 modern and contemporary art pieces. It is a leader in performance art, film, and new media, and has a significant impact on the local and global art community.
world knowledge.Details: The Walker Art Center's permanent collection includes books, costumes, drawings, media works, paintings, photography, prints, and sculpture. It hosts a variety of programs in visual arts, performing arts, film/video, and new media, and maintains an online presence through platforms like mnartists.org and the Walker Reader. The center is supported by state grants and private funding, with an endowment of $152 million as of 2011.

world knowledge.Name: Sultan Ahmad Shah Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sultan Ahmad Shah Mosque is Pahang's state mosque, named after Sultan Ahmad al-Mu’azzam Shah, the founder and first modern Sultan of Pahang. The original mosque, built in 1962, featured a space-age design with a large dome and a rocket-like minaret but was demolished in 1992 due to irreparable leakage. The current mosque was constructed between 1991 and 1993, featuring a more traditional Islamic design with four minarets and a large dome.

Major_Events.Description: Sultan Abu Bakar Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mu’azzam Shah officially inaugurated the original mosque.
The original mosque was demolished due to irreparable leakage during heavy rains.

Major_Events.Event: Grand reopening of the new mosque
Major_Events.Description: Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Al-Musta’in Billah and Syaikh Muhammad bin Abdullah as-Sabil officially marked the grand reopening of the new mosque.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mosque features a large dome, a smaller dome, and four minarets. The design is more traditional Islamic compared to the original space-age design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is culturally and historically significant as Pahang's state mosque and is named after Sultan Ahmad al-Mu’azzam Shah, the founder and first modern Sultan of Pahang.
Notable_Visitors: Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Al-Musta’in Billah
world knowledge.Details: The mosque was designed by DZJ Architect and Associates. The current Grand Imam is Tuan Haji Mohd Rizzal Bin Mohd Ali Nafiah, who assumed the position in February 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Spodek
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Spodek is a multipurpose arena complex in Katowice, Poland, opened on 9 May 1971.
