It was the largest indoor venue of its kind in Poland until it was surpassed by Tauron Arena in 2014. The idea of building a large venue originated in 1955, while Katowice was temporarily renamed Stalinogród. A contest was held to select the best design. Initially, it was to be constructed on the outskirts of town, but the Voivodeship National Council decided it should be built near the city center. A mining waste dump site classified "2A" was chosen for construction. The classification "2A" indicated medium mining damage with a possibility of local cave-ins. While excavating the foundations, the workers dug through coal instead of soil. Soon after construction began, rumors of design flaws in the new building spread, including the rumour that the dome would collapse when the scaffolding was removed. Because of this, in 1964, construction was halted for 18 months. Spodek's architects and chief engineers were present in the dome when the supports were dismantled as a statement against those rumors. Before opening the building to the public, as an endurance test, 3,500 soldiers marched throughout the hall; the vibration measurement was positive.

Major_Events.Description: Spodek was officially opened on 9 May 1971.
Spodek underwent renovation in 2011.
Spodek was expanded in 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Architects Maciej Gintowt and Maciej Krasiński designed the Spodek to employ the principle of tensegrity, as one of the first major structures to do so. For the roof they used an inclined surface held in check by a system of cables holding up its circumference. The structural engineer who conceived the unique tensegrity roof and made it work was Wacław Zalewski.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Spodek is a major contribution to the cultural significance of Katowice in Poland, especially for the younger generations. It has also been used as an unofficial logo for the city on posters promoting redevelopment in Katowice. Moreover, Spodek is home to ice hockey clubs in the winter months.
world knowledge.Details: Spodek hosts many important cultural and business events. Music concerts are especially common non-sport events. It can hold around 11,500 people, although this number is in practice limited to 10,000 or even 8,000 due to stage set-ups obscuring the view. Its Polish name refers to a flying saucer since its iconic shape resembles a UFO.

world knowledge.Name: Leipzig Zoological Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Leipzig Zoological Garden, or Leipzig Zoo, was first opened on June 9, 1878. It was taken over by the city of Leipzig in 1920 after World War I and now covers about 27 hectares (67 acres) and contains approximately 850 species. By 2020, the zoo featured six different theme worlds, aiming at providing habitats appropriate for the species on display.

Major_Events.Description: The massive greenhouse Gondwanaland opened, comprising an area larger than two football pitches (16,500 square metres). It has its own tropical climate and hosts 170 exotic animal species and around 500 different plant species from Africa, Asia, and South America.

The modern ape-world with spacious outdoor facilities was opened, allowing four species of primates to live in family groups. It also hosts a research centre in cooperation with the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo features six different theme worlds: the Founder's Garden, Gondwanaland, Asia, Pongoland, Africa, and South America. It includes large building projects such as Pongoland and Gondwanaland, the world's second-largest indoor rainforest hall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Leipzig Zoological Garden is internationally noted for its large building projects and species conservation efforts. It has been called the 'Zoo of the future' and is ranked as the best zoo in Germany and the second-best in Europe.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo hosts six different theme worlds and offers educational tours and special events. It has bred more than 2,000 lions, 250 rare Siberian tigers, and other carnivores like bears. The zoo is part of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) and the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA).

world knowledge.Name: House of Slaves
world knowledge.Address: Gorée Island, 3 km off the coast of Dakar, Senegal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The House of Slaves (Maison des Esclaves) and its Door of No Return is a museum and memorial to the victims of the Atlantic slave trade on Gorée Island. Constructed around 1776 by Nicolas Pépin, it was used as a holding center to export enslaved Africans. The museum, opened in 1962, was curated by Boubacar Joseph Ndiaye until his death in 2009. It is said to memorialize the final exit point of the slaves from Africa, although historians debate the number of slaves that actually passed through this building.

Major_Events.Event: Reconstruction and opening as a museum
Major_Events.Description: The House of Slaves was reconstructed and opened as a museum, largely through the work of Boubacar Joseph Ndiaye.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as UNESCO World Heritage site
Major_Events.Description: The Maison des Esclaves became a central part of the Gorée Island UNESCO World Heritage site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features dark, airless cells where enslaved people were held, with separate quarters for men, women, and children. The Door of No Return is a significant architectural element, symbolizing the final exit point of enslaved Africans.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The House of Slaves is a memorial to the victims of the Atlantic slave trade and serves as an important site for remembering the human toll of African slavery. It is a major draw for foreign tourists, particularly those descended from enslaved Africans, who often experience highly emotional reactions to the site.
world knowledge.Details: Despite academic debates about the number of slaves that actually passed through the House of Slaves, it remains a significant cultural and historical site. The museum attracts around 200,000 visitors annually and is a focal point for pilgrimages by African Americans seeking to reconnect with their heritage.

world knowledge.Name: Hluboká Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hluboká Castle, originally a Gothic castle built in the second half of the 13th century, was rebuilt several times throughout its history. It was expanded during the Renaissance, then rebuilt into a Baroque castle in the early 18th century, and finally reconstructed in the romantic style of England's Windsor Castle in the 19th century. The Schwarzenberg family owned the castle from 1661 until 1939, when the last owner emigrated to escape the Nazis. The castle was later confiscated by the Czechoslovak government after World War II and is now a National Cultural Monument of the Czech Republic.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was reconstructed in the romantic style of England's Windsor Castle under the direction of architects Franz Beer and F. Deworetzky.
The castle was confiscated by the government of Czechoslovakia after World War II under the Lex Schwarzenberg Act.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romantic Neo-Gothic château inspired by England's Windsor Castle, surrounded by a large English park.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hluboká Castle is considered one of the most beautiful castles in the Czech Republic and is a National Cultural Monument. It is also one of the most frequently visited castles in the country.
world knowledge.Details: The castle has been used as a filming location for movies such as 'Shanghai Knights' and 'Underworld: Blood Wars.' It also featured in the music video for K-pop soloist Park Jihoon's song 'L.O.V.E.' The castle is open to the public and houses exhibitions in its winter garden and riding-hall.

world knowledge.Name: Canton Tower
world knowledge.Address: Yuejiang Road West/Yiyuan Road, Haizhu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Canton Tower, originally named Guangzhou TV Astronomical and Sightseeing Tower, was constructed to serve as a multipurpose observation tower. It was designed to surpass the CN Tower in height and became operational in time for the 2010 Asian Games. The tower briefly held the title of the tallest tower in the world before being surpassed by the Tokyo Skytree. The naming of the tower was a subject of public contest and discussion, with 'Canton Tower' eventually chosen as the official English name.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the tower began with a groundbreaking ceremony.
The tower was structurally completed.
The tower became operational on 30 September 2010, in time for the 2010 Asian Games.
The rooftop observatory was officially opened to the public in December 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Canton Tower features a hyperboloid structure with a twisted shape, designed in the structural expressionism style. It consists of a lattice structure that densifies at the waist and opens up towards the top. The tower includes a 180 m open-air skywalk, outdoor gardens, observation decks, and a rotating restaurant. The design was inspired by the Adziogol Lighthouse and incorporates parametric design methods.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Canton Tower is a symbol of Guangzhou's modernity and prosperity. Its design and height reflect the city's ambition and technological advancement. The tower's naming and public involvement in its naming contest highlight its cultural importance to the local community.
world knowledge.Details: The tower includes various facilities such as TV and radio transmission equipment, observatory decks, revolving restaurants, 4D cinemas, and exhibition spaces. It also features the world's highest and longest open-air staircase, the Skywalk. The tower's lighting design uses LED technology for energy efficiency and dynamic light displays. At 604 meters tall, it is the second tallest tower in the world and the tallest in China.

world knowledge.Name: Cuttington University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cuttington University is a private university in Suacoco, Liberia. Founded in 1889 as Cuttington College by the Episcopal Church of the United States (ECUSA), it is the oldest private, coeducational, four-year, degree-granting institution in sub-Saharan Africa. It was established with a donation from Robert Fulton Cutting, treasurer of the ECUSA, to teach Liberian children about industry and agriculture. The university has educated generations of leaders for Liberia and West Africa, with its roots deeply tied to the history of the nation, the relationship between Liberia and the United States, and the Episcopal Church.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by the Episcopal Church of the United States in Cape Palmas, Liberia.
The college moved to Suacoco in Bong County, 120 miles north of Monrovia.
The school was looted, structures were damaged, and the campus was used as a training facility for militias. Operations were moved to an office in Virginia, USA, from 1990 to 1997.
The college reopened with a class of 103 students.
117 students graduated on the partially renovated campus.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus includes single-story white structures set among rolling hills, cotton trees, rice paddies, and native tropical plants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cuttington University is the oldest private, coeducational, four-year, degree-granting institution in sub-Saharan Africa. It has educated generations of leaders for Liberia and West Africa, playing a significant role in the nation's history and its relationship with the United States and the Episcopal Church.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education institution offering degrees in liberal arts and technical studies.
world knowledge.Details: The campus includes an affiliated hospital, Phebe Hospital. The university is a member of the Association of African Universities. It has restored regular telephone, electricity, and internet services since the end of the war and runs its own water treatment facility. The Cuttington University public radio and television stations resumed broadcasts in January 2010.

world knowledge.Name: Poldertoren
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Poldertoren was built as a water tower in 1959 to symbolize the unity of the Noordoostpolder and emphasize Emmeloord as the central town. It was designed by architect H. van Gent and J.W.H.C. Pot. The tower includes a carillon with 48 bells, each donated by villages in the Noordoostpolder.

Major_Events.Description: The water company of Overijssel offered a prize for the best design of a new water tower, which had to include a carillon and a visitor platform.
The ownership of the tower was transferred from the water company Vitens to the municipality of Noordoostpolder.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is constructed with 1,220 m3 of concrete, 185 metric tons of steel, 600,000 bricks, 624 metric tons of cement, and 7,200 drainpipes. It features a carillon and a visitor platform.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Poldertoren symbolizes the unity of the Noordoostpolder and serves as a central landmark for the region. It is not related to any church, ensuring no single religious group dominates the area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a water tower, now a cultural and historical landmark
world knowledge.Details: A replica of the Poldertoren exists in Japan. The tower has a water storage capacity of 1,850 m3 and features 243 steps leading to a visitor platform at 43.4 meters. The carillon includes 48 bells, with the heaviest weighing 2382 kilograms and the lightest 9.9 kilograms, each inscribed with messages from the villages of Noordoostpolder.

world knowledge.Name: Nether Lypiatt Manor
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in the early 1700s by an unknown architect for Judge Charles Coxe. Inherited by his son John in 1728 and passed down in the family until 1914. Bought by Arthur Stanton in 1914, then sold to Mr Corbett Woodall, who commissioned architect Peter Morley Horder to recondition the house. Bought by Gordon Woodhouse and his wife Violet Gordon Woodhouse in 1923. After Gordon's death in 1951, the property passed to Captain John Gwynne. In 1956–57, Frederick Nettlefold, with Jeremy Benson as his architect, rebuilt the roof. Bought by Prince and Princess Michael of Kent in 1980. Sold to Lord Drayson in 2006 and put up for sale again in 2023.

Major_Events.Description: Built by an unknown architect for Judge Charles Coxe.
Added by Morley Horder.
Frederick Nettlefold, with Jeremy Benson as his architect, lifted and completely rebuilt the roof in strict accordance with the original plan.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Prince and Princess Michael of Kent
Major_Events.Description: Became the country home of Prince and Princess Michael of Kent.
Purchased by the businessman and Labour life peer Lord Drayson for £5.75 million.
Launched in Country Life at a price of £11 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Compact, neo-Classical manor house forming a perfect square of 46 feet (14 m) on each side, with sash windows, tall chimneys, hipped roofs, and gate piers and railings. Originally had an attic storey with dormers, removed in 1844 but replaced by Horder c. 1923. Comprises four floors, including a tall basement and an attic floor. Features early 18th-century panelling and original stone fireplaces. A fine staircase runs from basement to attic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grade I listed building. Praised by architectural historian Mark Girouard as perfectly exemplifying the early 18th-century formal house in miniature. Possibly influenced the Governor's Palace in Williamsburg, Virginia. Gardens were worked on by renowned garden designer Rosemary Verey.
world knowledge.Details: The house has four reception rooms, eight bedrooms, and four bathrooms. The grounds have been re-developed with a series of new gardens, including a refurbished traditional flower garden in keeping with the original arts and crafts backbone of vistas and hedges. For a review of Nether Lypiatt Manor (with 27 photographs) see Christopher Hussey in Country Life, 19 and 26 May 1934, and for Morley Horder's restorations in particular, see R. Randal Phillips in idem, 24 March and 7 April 1923.

world knowledge.Name: Kadriorg Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kadriorg Palace is an 18th-century Petrine Baroque palace built by Peter the Great for his wife Catherine. It was designed by Nicola Michetti and constructed by Gaetano Chiaveri and Mikhail Zemtsov. The palace currently houses the Kadriorg Art Museum, displaying foreign art from the 16th to 20th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: The main building of the palace was completed.
Extensive restoration works of the palace and grounds took place.
The palace became state property after Estonia's independence.
The palace was restored and reopened to the public as a branch of the Art Museum of Estonia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Petrine Baroque style with profuse stucco decor. The great hall features Catherine's initials and elaborate stucco work attributed to Heinrich von Bergen.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kadriorg Palace is culturally significant as a symbol of Estonia's history and its connection to Russian royalty. It serves as a major art museum and a historical landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The palace currently houses the Kadriorg Art Museum, displaying foreign art from the 16th to 20th centuries. The museum's collection includes works by notable artists such as Bartholomeus van der Helst, Jacob Jordaens, and Ilya Repin.

world knowledge.Name: Centro Universitário Uninovafapi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Centro Universitário Uninovafapi (UNINOVAFAPI) is a higher education institution located in Teresina, capital of the Brazilian state of Piauí. It was inaugurated in 2000 with the ordinance of the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Culture.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The classes are equipped with a home-theater stereo sound system, datashow, and whiteboard. There are also air conditioners. Lab 1 has 25 computers programmed for academic sources and general search on the Internet. Lab 2 has 45 line up computers, source on intranet article system and general source at Internet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UNINOVAFAPI is a significant educational institution in Teresina, providing higher education and contributing to the academic and professional development of students in the region.
world knowledge.Details: To enter as a student, high school graduation from a recognized institution of education is required. Every twice a year there is access through the vestibular, one at the middle of the year right before winter vacations and another selective process in the end of the year, before the summer vacations. All the teachers have an MBA in the practice area as required to teach at the faculty. The library has full access to the students, teachers and faculty staff. A digital scanner system is in use for lending books, preventing the use of false identity.

world knowledge.Name: Dutch Reformed Church
world knowledge.Area: Kingdom of the Netherlands, Belgium, and South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Dutch Reformed Church was the largest Christian denomination in the Netherlands from the 16th century until 1930. It was founded during the Protestant Reformation in the Calvinist tradition and was influenced by theologians like John Calvin. The church played a significant role in Dutch society and was closely associated with the Dutch government until its disestablishment in 1795. It merged with other denominations in 2004 to form the Protestant Church in the Netherlands.

Major_Events.Description: The Synod of Emden is considered the founding event of the Dutch Reformed Church, establishing presbyterian church government.

Major_Events.Event: Merger into Protestant Church in the Netherlands
Major_Events.Description: The Dutch Reformed Church merged with the Reformed Churches in the Netherlands and the Evangelical Lutheran Church in the Kingdom of the Netherlands to form the Protestant Church in the Netherlands.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Dutch Reformed Church was the traditional denomination of the Dutch royal family and played a crucial role in Dutch society and governance. It was also a significant part of Afrikaner nationalism in South Africa and spread globally through Dutch colonization.
world knowledge.Details: The Dutch Reformed Church was the largest Protestant denomination in the Netherlands until the 20th century. It spread to various regions through Dutch colonization, including South Africa, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and the Americas. The church was involved in several theological controversies and splits, particularly in the 19th century. It merged with other denominations in 2004, though a minority formed the Restored Reformed Church.

world knowledge.Name: Ramoji Film City
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ramoji Film City is an integrated film studio facility established in 1996 by Telugu media proprietor Ramoji Rao. It is recognized as the world's largest film studio complex by the Guinness World Records. The site was developed with a focus on preserving its natural environment and ecological features, and it serves as a major hub for film production and a thematic holiday destination.

Major_Events.Event: First film shot at Ramoji Film City
Major_Events.Description: The first film to be entirely shot at Ramoji Film City was Maa Nannaku Pelli.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The film city encompasses a wide range of sets and production facilities, including permanent sets such as forests, gardens, mansions, apartment blocks, hotels, a railway station, and an airport, as well as 47 sound stages for indoor filming. The site also includes a central kitchen to support film crews.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ramoji Film City is culturally significant as it is the world's largest film studio complex and a major hub for film production in India. It also serves as a popular thematic holiday destination, attracting nearly 15 Lakh visitors annually.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Film production and thematic holiday destination
world knowledge.Details: Ramoji Film City is equipped with six hotels and provides internal transportation via vintage buses and air-conditioned coaches. It employs approximately 1,200 staff members and 8,000 agents, handling around 400–500 film productions annually across multiple Indian languages. The facility can accommodate up to 15 simultaneous shoots and features an amusement park, gardens, and film sets from notable productions such as Baahubali (2015) and Baahubali 2 (2017).

world knowledge.Name: Grips-Theater
world knowledge.Address: Altonaer Straße at Hansaplatz in the Hansaviertel, Berlin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1966 as a children's theatre at the Berlin Reichskabarett, GRIPS became a pioneer in sociocritical children's and youth theatre. It moved to its current location in 1974 after evolving from a student protest group into a professional theatre.

Major_Events.Description: Premiere of 'Stokkerlok und Millipilli', the GRIPS-Theatre's first sociocritical children's play, which won the Brother Grimm Award.
The theatre relocated to its current venue, a former cinema redesigned to place the audience close to the stage.
The musical 'Linie 1' premiered, becoming the GRIPS's most successful production and one of the most-performed German musicals worldwide.
Volker Ludwig stepped down as artistic director, succeeded by Stefan Fischer-Fels and later Philipp Harpain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was originally designed by Ernst Zinsser and Hansrudi Plarre for the 1957 Interbau exhibition. The GRIPS remodeled it with a stage surrounded by benches, placing actors at audience level. The entrance features a mosaic by Rainer Hachfeld.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: GRIPS is the first theatre worldwide to address children's and youth issues through sociocritical, humorous, and musical plays. Its works, like 'Linie 1', have been adapted globally, influencing theatre for young audiences and promoting child emancipation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Children's and youth theatre with sociocritical and emancipatory themes.
world knowledge.Details: GRIPS has staged over 1,500 performances in 40 languages worldwide. Notable alumni include actors Axel Prahl and Heinz Hoenig. The theatre produces at least four new plays annually and hosts 300+ performances per year. Its studio, GRIPS Podewil, opened in 1992.

world knowledge.Name: Goethe University Frankfurt
world knowledge.Address: Campus Westend: Theodor-W.-Adorno-Platz 1, Frankfurt am Main, Hessen, 60323, Germany
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1914 as a citizens' university, funded by the wealthy liberal citizenry of Frankfurt. Originally named Universität Frankfurt am Main, it was renamed in 1932 in honor of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe. The university has roots dating back to 1484 with the founding of the Johann Christian Senckenberg University Library. It has been influential in social research, natural sciences, and medicine, with 20 Nobel Prize winners affiliated with it.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded on 18 October 1914 as a citizens' university, funded by the wealthy liberal citizenry of Frankfurt.
The university was renamed in honor of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.
The university celebrated its 100th anniversary.
Birgitta Wolff became the first female president of the university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Westend Campus is dominated by the IG Farben Building, an example of the modernist New Objectivity style. New buildings, such as the House of Finance, follow this architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is culturally significant for its contributions to social research, natural sciences, and medicine. It has been a center for liberal and left-leaning thought, particularly during the Frankfurt School era. It also played a role in the German student movement of 1968.
world knowledge.Details: The university consists of 16 faculties and is involved in various research institutes, including the Max Planck Society. It is part of the IT cluster Rhine-Main-Neckar and the Rhine-Main-Universities (RMU) alliance. The university has a strong focus on law, history, and economics, with ambitions to become Germany's leading university for finance and economics. It offers an MBA program in cooperation with Duke University's Fuqua School of Business and has established the Deutsche Bank Prize in Financial Economics.

world knowledge.Name: Birmingham Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Birmingham Town Hall was opened in 1834 as a concert hall and venue for popular assemblies. It was built to replace St Philip's Church as the home for the Birmingham Triennial Music Festival, which aimed to raise funds for the General Hospital. The hall underwent major renovations between 2002 and 2007 and has hosted a diverse range of events, including music concerts, public meetings, and cultural performances.

Major_Events.Description: Premiere of Mendelssohn's oratorio 'Elijah' as part of the Triennial Musical Festival.

Major_Events.Event: First performance of Elgar's The Dream of Gerontius
Major_Events.Description: Premiere of Elgar's choral work 'The Dream of Gerontius' as part of the Triennial Musical Festival.

Major_Events.Event: Public protest meeting for Revd. Richard Enraght
Major_Events.Description: A public protest meeting in support of Revd. Richard Enraght, who was imprisoned under the Public Worship Regulation Act.

Major_Events.Event: Rioting during David Lloyd George's visit
Major_Events.Description: Rioting occurred during a visit by David Lloyd George.

Major_Events.Event: Coronation celebration of King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra
Major_Events.Description: The hall was illuminated in celebration of the coronation.
A £35 million refurbishment restored the hall to its original glory, including the restoration of its 6,000-pipe organ.

Major_Events.Event: Official reopening by TRH The Prince of Wales and The Duchess of Cornwall
Major_Events.Description: The hall was officially reopened after its major renovation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a free-standing Corinthian temple modelled on the Temple of Castor and Pollux in Rome. It features a tall rusticated stone podium, 14 bays running north to south, and 8 bays east to west. The columns are topped with capitals featuring Acanthus leaves in a distinctive interlocking spiral design. The building is constructed in brick faced with Penmon Anglesey Marble.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Birmingham Town Hall is a Grade I listed building and the first significant work of the 19th-century revival of Roman architecture in England. It has hosted premieres of major musical works, public protests, and performances by iconic musicians, making it a cornerstone of Birmingham's cultural and historical identity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Concert hall and venue for popular assemblies
world knowledge.Details: The hall features a 6,000-pipe organ originally installed in 1834, which was once the largest and most technologically advanced in the world. It is now managed by the registered charity Performances Birmingham Limited alongside Symphony Hall. The seating capacity is 1,086.

world knowledge.Name: Parliament of Rwanda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Parliament of Rwanda has consisted of two chambers since 2003. Rwanda had a unicameral legislature, National Assembly of Rwanda, established in January 1961. It was dissolved following the coup d'état of 1973. Rwanda had a unicameral legislature, National Development Council of Rwanda from 1982 to 1994. Unicameral Transitional National Assembly of Rwanda was established in 1994 following Rwandan Civil War. It was replaced in 2003 by a bicameral legislature. Rwanda's parliament has the highest percentage of women in a single house parliament worldwide. The government has reserved 24 out of the 80 seats in the Chamber of Deputies for women. The 24 seats allocated to women are divided up between each province and the city of Kigali, where they are elected by an assembly made up of various councils and committees members. More women were granted seats due to the effects of the Rwandan Genocide on the population. After the Genocide against the Tutsi, the population was made up of more women than men, and this was reflected in the makeup of Parliament.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of National Assembly of Rwanda
Major_Events.Description: Unicameral legislature established in January 1961.
National Assembly of Rwanda dissolved following the coup d'état of 1973.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of National Development Council of Rwanda
Major_Events.Description: Unicameral legislature established from 1982 to 1994.
Unicameral Transitional National Assembly of Rwanda established following the Rwandan Civil War.
Transitional National Assembly of Rwanda replaced by a bicameral legislature.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rwanda's parliament has the highest percentage of women in a single house parliament worldwide. The government has reserved 24 out of the 80 seats in the Chamber of Deputies for women. This reflects the impact of the Rwandan Genocide on the population, which resulted in a higher proportion of women.
world knowledge.Details: The Parliament of Rwanda (French: Parlement du Rwanda; Kinyarwanda: Inteko Ishinga Amategeko y’u Rwanda) is a bicameral legislature with the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate. The Speaker of the Senate is Iyamuremye Augustin, and the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies is Donatille Mukabalisa. The Chamber of Deputies has 80 members elected by proportional representation, and the Senate has 26 appointed members.

world knowledge.Name: Krymsky Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Spans the Moskva River, linking Zubovsky Boulevard to Krymsky Val street
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length 668 meters (bridge itself 262.5 meters), width 38.4 meters
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Krymsky Bridge is the fourth bridge on this site, replacing earlier wooden and steel bridges that were frequently damaged. The current bridge was completed in 1938 as part of Joseph Stalin's reconstruction of Moscow. It is the only suspension bridge in Moscow.

Major_Events.Description: The old bridge was moved 50 meters on temporary pillars to allow construction of the new bridge without interrupting traffic.
The current Krymsky Bridge was completed and opened to traffic.
The bridge deck was replaced, with traffic restrictions but no complete closure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel suspension bridge with eyebar chains made of SDS steel, supported by concrete counterweights. Features two 300-meter-long girders, 50-centimeter I-beams, and a concrete deck. Road width is 24 meters (6 lanes) with two 5-meter pedestrian lanes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is visually unique and a notable example of Soviet engineering. It was featured on Soviet postage stamps in 1939 and 1948.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries the Garden Ring road and pedestrian traffic across the Moskva River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge consumed nearly 10,000 tons of steel, equating to 1 metric ton per square meter of deck. Nearby metro stations are Park Kultury and Oktyabrskaya.

world knowledge.Name: Rufford Old Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rufford Old Hall is a National Trust property in Rufford, Lancashire, England. Built in about 1530 for Sir Robert Hesketh, only the Great Hall survives from the original structure. A brick-built wing in the Jacobean style was added in 1661, and a third wing was added in the 1820s. The hall was in the continuous ownership of the Hesketh family until 1936, when it was donated to the National Trust. There is some evidence to suggest that William Shakespeare may have performed in the Great Hall.

Major_Events.Description: Rufford Old Hall, with its collection of arms and armour and 17th-century oak furniture, was donated to the National Trust by Thomas Fermor-Hesketh, 1st Baron Hesketh.
A secret chamber, used as a priest hole in the 16th century, was discovered above the Great Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The timber-framed hall house with great hall, in a late medieval pattern which continued in use in Tudor times, was built for Sir Robert Hesketh in about 1530. The hall, which formed the south wing, is substantially as built, 46.5 feet (14.2 m) long and 22 feet (6.7 m) wide, with the timbers sitting on a low stone wall. The hall has a flagged floor, a stone chimney, five bays, and a hammerbeam roof. The five hammerbeams each terminate, at both ends, in a carved wooden angel. In 1661 a Jacobean style rustic brick wing was built at right angles to the great hall, and in the 1820s a third wing was constructed, formed out of the medieval domestic offices, and a castellated tower was built to join the Great Hall to the Charles II wing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rufford Old Hall is designated by English Heritage as a Grade I listed building. The hall is reputedly haunted by a grey lady, Queen Elizabeth I, and a man in Elizabethan clothing. There is some evidence to suggest that William Shakespeare may have performed in the Great Hall.
world knowledge.Details: The cottage, coach house and stables 10 metres (33 ft) east of the house are Grade II listed buildings. There are gardens and pasture to the rear and side of the hall, and woodland at the front. The Rufford Branch of the Leeds and Liverpool Canal, completed in 1781, passes very close to the site on the east side. A feature of the gardens is a pair of topiary squirrels.

world knowledge.Name: Mall Road, Shimla
world knowledge.Address: Mall Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed during British colonial rule, Mall Road is one of the main financial, commercial and business centres in Shimla. It features notable landmarks like Scandal Point, Gaiety Theatre, Kali Bari temple, and the Town Hall Building.

Major_Events.Description: The name Scandal Point arose from the commotion caused by the supposed elopement of a British lady with an Indian Maharaja. The Maharaja of Patiala had eloped with the daughter of the British Viceroy, leading to his banishment from Shimla by the British authorities.

Gaiety Theatre was opened on 30 May 1887. Many popular film personalities have performed on its stage. Today, it is primarily known for its social club and is used by schools in Shimla for performing arts.
A project was started in 2014 to restore the Town Hall Building to its original look, with more than 8 crore rupees spent in renovating this colonial architectural marvel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Mall Road features colonial-era architecture with notable structures like the Gaiety Theatre and the Town Hall Building, designed by Scottish Architect James Ransome. The area is reminiscent of the pre-independence era.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mall Road is culturally significant as a historical and commercial hub from the British colonial era. It houses important landmarks, temples, and theaters, and is a popular tourist destination for shopping and sightseeing.
world knowledge.Details: Mall Road has a number of showrooms, department stores, shops, restaurants, and cafes. A Himachal emporium offers handicraft products like locally designed woollen clothes, branded clothes, pottery items, wooden products, and jewellery. Automobiles, except emergency vehicles, are not allowed on this road.

world knowledge.Name: Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed in 2007 to host the 33rd National Games of India, the stadium was named in tribute to the late Indira Gandhi, the third Prime Minister of India. It has since hosted numerous national and international sporting events, including the 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup and the 2016 South Asian Games.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was constructed to host this event with a mostly standing capacity for 35,000 people.

Major_Events.Event: International friendly between India and Malaysia
Major_Events.Description: Played on 13 November 2011.

Major_Events.Event: 2018 World Cup qualifier between India and Nepal
Major_Events.Description: Played on 12 March 2015.
The stadium was the main venue for the games held in Guwahati and Shillong from 5 to 16 February 2016.
One of the venues for the tournament held in India. Individual seats were installed, reducing capacity to below 25,000.
Held on 3 and 4 February 2018.
Held on 15 February 2020.
On 14 April 2023, over 11,000 dancers and musicians performed the traditional Assamese Bihu dance, setting two world records.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: One-tier stadium with a grass surface, initially constructed with mostly standing capacity for 35,000 people. Only the main stand had a limited number of seats installed. Later, individual seats were added, reducing capacity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sporting venue in Assam, hosting major national and international events. It also holds cultural importance, as evidenced by the world record Bihu dance performance in 2023.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium used for athletic events, football matches, and other large gatherings.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the home ground of NorthEast United FC in the Indian Super League. It has also been used by I-League champions Aizawl FC and Minerva Punjab FC for AFC group stage matches. During the COVID-19 pandemic, isolation wards were constructed in the premises. The stadium was proposed by Inter Kashi for the 2025-26 season as their home stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Tongji Bridge (Yuyao)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tongji Bridge is a famous stone arch bridge with a long history. It was first constructed as a wooden bridge during the Northern Song dynasty (1041-1048) and later rebuilt in stone during the Yuan dynasty (1332). It underwent major repairs during the Qing dynasty (1729-1731). The bridge is also known as the First Bridge of Eastern Zhejiang.

Major_Events.Description: Constructed as a wooden bridge during the Qingli era of the Northern Song dynasty, originally named Dehui Bridge.
Destroyed in wars and reconstructed several times, including a name change to Hong Bridge.
Rebuilt using rocks by Buddhist monk Huixing and later completed by Taoist Li Daoning, renamed to Tongji Bridge.
Repaired and rebuilt by the local government during the Yongzheng era of the Qing dynasty, giving the bridge its current appearance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stone arch bridge with three spans (central span: 14.2 meters, two equal side spans), total length of about 50 meters, height of 6 meters, and 106 steps.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is the first large-sized arch bridge in the Eastern Zhejiang region and is a key cultural relic under city protection. It symbolizes historical engineering and cultural exchange between Buddhism and Taoism.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is still in use today with busy traffic. It is located near the Shunjiang Building (old city gate of Yuyao), and together they form a protected cultural site. A stone tablet beside the bridge bears an inscription indicating ships could pass under the bridge unobstructed.

world knowledge.Name: Siak Sri Indrapura Palace
world knowledge.Address: Jalan Sultan Syarif Kasim, Siak, Riau, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Siak Sri Indrapura Palace, also known as Istana Siak Sri Inderapura or Istana Matahari Timur, is a royal palace of the Sultanate of Siak Sri Indrapura. It was built by the 11th Sultan, Syarif Hasyim Abdul Jalil Syarifuddin, in 1889. The palace complex includes four palaces: Istana Siak, Istana Lima, Istana Padjang, and Istana Baru. The Moorish-style palace blends European, Malay, and Moorish architectural elements. The palace was transformed into a museum and contains royal ceremonial objects, including a gold-plated crown set with diamonds and a golden throne.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Siak Sri Indrapura Palace
Major_Events.Description: The palace was built by Sultan Syarif Hasyim Abdul Jalil Syarifuddin, who was inspired by his travels to the Netherlands and Germany.
The palace was converted into a museum, showcasing royal artifacts and historical objects.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features Moorish-style architecture with European influences, blending harmoniously with Malay and Moorish elements. The building consists of two floors, with six courtrooms on the lower floor and nine rooms on the upper floor. The palace is adorned with dragon ornaments and six eagle statues symbolizing courage. The complex also includes eight cannons and a temporary prison.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is culturally significant as it represents the history and heritage of the Sultanate of Siak Sri Indrapura. It showcases the blend of Malay, Arabic, and European architectural styles and houses important royal artifacts, including a multi-centennial musical instrument called the 'Komet.'
world knowledge.Details: The palace complex includes a royal cemetery, a courtroom called 'Balairung Sari,' and a flower room. The 'Komet,' a rare musical instrument, is still functional and used to play works by composers like Beethoven, Mozart, and Strauss.

world knowledge.Name: McCarthy Beach State Park
world knowledge.Address: French Township, Saint Louis County, Minnesota, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The park was established in 1945 after local citizens raised funds to purchase the land from a lumberman, following the death of the previous owner John A. McCarthy in 1943. The area had been a popular picnic and tenting ground for people from the Iron Range. Earlier, in 1895, the Swan River Logging Company built a railroad to Sturgeon Lake for logging purposes.

Major_Events.Event: Land purchase and establishment as a state park
Major_Events.Description: Local citizens raised funds to purchase the land to protect the timber, matching local money with state money to establish the park.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of railroad by Swan River Logging Company
Major_Events.Description: A railroad was built to Sturgeon Lake to haul logs to the Swan River, which were then floated down the Mississippi River to Minneapolis sawmills.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a northern boreal forest with stands of red and white pine and leatherleaf-black spruce lowlands. The landscape includes low rolling hills with steep sides (moraines) and valleys formed by glacial activity.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is significant for its natural beauty, diverse wildlife, and historical logging and recreational use. It serves as a protected area for numerous species and a recreational spot for locals and visitors.
world knowledge.Details: The park is home to 33 species of wildlife including white-tailed deer, black bears, timber wolves, chipmunks, red squirrels, raccoons, and several species of reptiles and amphibians. Over 175 species of birds visit the area. The glaciers that moved through the area shaped the current landscape, leaving moraines and forming lakes in the larger valleys.

world knowledge.Name: American Museum of Natural History
world knowledge.Address: 200 Central Park West, New York, NY 10024, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1869, the AMNH was established to promote the study of natural history. It opened in Central Park's Arsenal in 1871 before moving to its current location in 1877. The museum has grown significantly over the years, with numerous expansions and additions, including the Rose Center for Earth and Space in 2000 and the Richard Gilder Center for Science, Education, and Innovation in 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The American Museum of Natural History was established by Albert S. Bickmore and other prominent New Yorkers.
The museum first opened to the public in the Arsenal building in Central Park.
The museum moved to its permanent home in Theodore Roosevelt Park on the Upper West Side.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Hall
Major_Events.Description: The main entrance hall, dedicated to former U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt, was completed.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Rose Center for Earth and Space
Major_Events.Description: The modern planetarium and space science center opened, replacing the original Hayden Planetarium.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Richard Gilder Center
Major_Events.Description: The new addition focused on science education and innovation opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum complex comprises 25 interconnected buildings in various architectural styles, including Victorian Gothic, Beaux-Arts, and modern designs. The original building was designed by Calvert Vaux and J. Wrey Mould. The Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Hall features a Roman-style arch and grand interior spaces. The Rose Center is notable for its glass cube enclosing a spherical Space Theater.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The AMNH is one of the world's preeminent natural history museums, housing over 32 million specimens and artifacts. It plays a vital role in scientific research, education, and public engagement with science. The museum's dioramas and exhibits have educated generations about biodiversity, evolution, and human cultures.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural history museum, scientific research institution, and educational center

Details.Collections: About 32 million specimens including plants, animals, fossils, minerals, rocks, meteorites, and human cultural artifacts
Notable_Exhibits: Dinosaur fossils including Tyrannosaurus rex and Apatosaurus
Blue whale model in the Milstein Hall of Ocean Life
Habitat dioramas of animals from around the world
Educational_Programs: Richard Gilder Graduate School (offers PhD and MAT degrees)
Details.Library: Over 550,000 volumes including rare books and special collections
Details.Field_Station: Southwestern Research Station in Portal, Arizona

world knowledge.Name: Tiantai Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built in 1932 as Qingdao Municipal Stadium, modeled on the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, which hosted the 1932 Summer Olympics. It was renamed as Qingdao First Stadium in the 1950s and as Tiantai Stadium in November 2003.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modeled after the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, which hosted the 1932 Summer Olympics.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is one of the historical sports venues in Qingdao, reflecting the city's sports culture and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium, primarily for football matches, athletics, and rugby sevens.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 20,525 and was renovated in 2003. It is accessible via public transit at Zhongshan Park station on Line 3.

world knowledge.Name: New Town Hall (Hanover)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The New Town Hall in Hanover, Germany, was opened on 20 June 1913 after 12 years of construction. It replaced the Wangenheim Palace as the main seat of administration. The building was damaged during World War II bombing raids and was the site where the German state of Lower Saxony was proclaimed in 1946.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the New Town Hall
Major_Events.Description: The New Town Hall was opened in the presence of Emperor Wilhelm II, replacing the Wangenheim Palace as the main seat of administration.
The German state of Lower Saxony was proclaimed in the 38-metre-high hall of the New Town Hall.
The public space in front of the building, previously named Trammplatz, was renamed to Platz der Menschenrechte (Human Rights Plaza) due to Heinrich Tramm's association with National Socialism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: A magnificent, castle-like building of the era of Wilhelm II in eclectic style, erected on 6,026 beech piles. The dome is 97.73 metres high with a unique parabolic lift. The building features four city models of Hanover on the ground floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The New Town Hall is a significant architectural landmark in Hanover, representing the city's development and history. It is also notable for its unique dome lift and its role in the proclamation of Lower Saxony.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The residence of the Mayor and CEO, the head of the municipal administration.
world knowledge.Details: The dome's lift is unique in the world, following the parabolic shape of the dome. The lift climbs a 50-metre shaft at an angle of up to 17°. Over 90,000 people visited the tower in 2005. A new lift was installed in winter of 2007–08.

world knowledge.Name: Narayanhiti Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Narayanhiti Palace Museum was created in 2008 from the complex of the former Narayanhiti Palace following the 2006 revolution. The palace was originally built in 1963 by King Mahendra and served as the residence and principal workplace of the monarch of the Kingdom of Nepal. The site has a complex history, having been occupied by various prime ministers and their families before becoming a royal residence.

Major_Events.Description: King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya were among those killed in the royal massacre.
The Nepalese monarchy was abolished following the 2006 revolution, and the last king, Gyanendra, vacated Narayanhiti on 11 June 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace was designed by American architect Benjamin Polk, incorporating Nepalese architectural styles. It features a central tower, courtyards, gardens, and buildings. The interior is based on Late Victorian style, and the palace is divided into three parts: the guest wing, the state wing, and the private wing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is a national symbol of Nepal, reflecting the country's history and architectural heritage. It was the residence of the monarch and hosted significant state occasions.
world knowledge.Details: The palace complex includes notable spots such as Mahendra Manzil, Gorkha Baithak (the throne room), and Kaski Sadan (the reception hall). The royal crown jewels were put on display in October 2018. The palace stands on a floor space of 3,794 m2 (40838.28 sq ft) and has 52 rooms named after the 75 districts of Nepal.

world knowledge.Name: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Old Harbour, the town was renamed when the Costa Rican government institutionalized Spanish as the national language. It has a mix of native Costa Ricans, Costa Ricans of Jamaican descent, and European emigrants. The area is also home to the indigenous Bribri people.

Major_Events.Event: Evictions and demolitions due to Maritime Law violations
Major_Events.Description: Nine local businesses and residents were notified of impending evictions and demolitions for violating Costa Rica's Maritime Law. Seventy-six properties were cited as in violation, with the first phase of demolitions planned for November 2012.

Major_Events.Event: Legislative approval to permit residents to remain
Major_Events.Description: The Costa Rican legislature approved laws allowing residents whose homes were due to be demolished to remain, recognizing existing coastal towns and rectifying limitations of the Jairo Mora Sandoval Gandoca-Manzanillo Mixed Wildlife Refuge.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca is a culturally diverse town with a mix of native Costa Ricans, Costa Ricans of Jamaican descent, and European emigrants. It is also home to the indigenous Bribri people. The town is a popular tourist destination known for its beaches, surfing, and wildlife.
world knowledge.Details: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca is known for the biggest and most powerful wave in Costa Rica, Salsa Brava, and beautiful beaches like Playa Chiquita, Playa Negra, and Punta Uva. The Jaguar Rescue Centre is nearby. The town is a stop for tourists en route to the Panamanian border at Sixaola. It has a tropical climate with consistent temperatures year-round.

world knowledge.Name: Tsaghkadzor ski resort
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tsaghkadzor Ski Resort was opened in 1986 adjacent to the Tsaghkadzor Olympic Sports Complex. During Soviet times, lifts and sporting facilities were built to prepare athletes for the 1988 Winter Olympics. The resort was later modernized with old lifts replaced.

Major_Events.Description: A fourth lift was added, stretching from the end of the first stage towards an opposite hilltop, adding two trails.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features five lifts: one detachable quad and four double chairlifts, all manufactured and operated by Leitner Group. The first stage is a four-seater, while the others are double-seater chairlifts equipped with magic carpet boarding systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The resort was developed to prepare Soviet athletes for the 1988 Winter Olympics and has since become a popular ski destination in Armenia.
world knowledge.Details: The resort offers ski and snowboard rental, skiing instructors, and has three cafés located at the foot of the mountain and at the end of the first and second lifts. The skiing season typically runs from mid-December to March, with top slopes often fit for skiing in April.

world knowledge.Name: Løkke Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Across the Sandvikselva river at Sandvika
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Løkke Bridge is the first cast iron bridge in Norway, cast at the ironworks at Bærums Verk and installed in 1829. It was moved upstream in 1977 to allow for road widening and now serves as a cycle- and footbridge.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was cast at the ironworks at Bærums Verk and installed.
The bridge was moved upstream by several metres to allow for road widening, where it now serves as a cycle- and footbridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cast iron bridge with a span of 23 metres. The spandrels have ten circular holes, in decreasing sizes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is the first cast iron bridge in Norway and was painted by Claude Monet during his visit in 1895.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a road bridge, now serves as a cycle- and footbridge.
world knowledge.Details: Claude Monet made an oil painting of the bridge in 1895. The 73.4×92.5 cm work is now in the Art Institute of Chicago. It has been exhibited in Paris, Copenhagen, Stockholm, and Japan.

world knowledge.Name: Tagiyev's Theater
world knowledge.Address: at the corner of Gorchakovskaya and Merkurievskaya streets, Baku, Azerbaijan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Taghiyev’s Theater was the first theater in Baku, built in 1883 at the expense of the industrialist and philanthropist Haji Zeynalabdin Taghiyev. It staged both national plays and operas, as well as the works of world classics. The theater played a pivotal role in the development of Azerbaijani theater, hosting the premiere of the first Azerbaijani national opera 'Leyli and Majnun' by Uzeyir Hajibeyov in 1908. The building burned down several times and was rebuilt, eventually being demolished in 1992 and replaced by the Azerbaijan State Musical Theater.

Major_Events.Description: The premiere of the first Azerbaijani national opera 'Leyli and Majnun' by Uzeyir Hajibeyov took place at the Tagiyev's Theater.
A major fire broke out in the theater, destroying much of the building. This was the largest fire in the theater's history.
The theater was rebuilt and reopened with Leo Tolstoy's play 'The Fruits of Enlightenment'.
The theater building was demolished due to disrepair, and the Azerbaijan State Musical Theater was later built on its site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater was designed by architect Khrisanf Vasilyev. After a fire in 1899, it was reconstructed based on the project of civil engineer Pavel Kognovitsky. The building initially had a two-story auditorium, which was later expanded to three stories to accommodate more attendees.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tagiyev's Theater was instrumental in the development of Azerbaijani theater, providing a venue for national and international performances. It hosted the premiere of the first Azerbaijani opera and supported amateur artists and charitable causes. The theater also contributed to the development of the Armenian theatrical society in Baku.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was owned by Haji Zeynalabdin Taghiyev, who often provided the premises for free to amateur troupes and donated income to charitable causes. The building underwent several reconstructions due to fires and was eventually replaced by the Azerbaijan State Musical Theater in 1996.

world knowledge.Name: Jebel Shams
world knowledge.Address: northeastern Oman north of the town of Al-Hamra
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jebel Shams, known as the 'Mountain of Sun', is the highest mountain in Oman and part of the Jebel Akhdar Mountains within the Hajar range. It is named for being the first place to receive sunrise in Oman due to its high peak.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jebel Shams is culturally significant as it is the highest peak in Oman and a popular sightseeing destination. It also hosts Al Nakhur Canyon, known as the Grand Canyon of Arabia.
world knowledge.Details: The mountain has two summits: the North Summit, which is a restricted area occupied by a military base, and the South Summit, which is accessible for trekking via the W4 Trail. The North Summit is 3,009 m high, while the South Summit is 2,997 m high. The temperature ranges from around 20 °C in summer to less than 0 °C in winter.

world knowledge.Name: Rantau Panjang–Sungai Golok Bridge
world knowledge.Area: Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, Malaysia and Su-ngai Kolok, Narathiwat Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 109.73 m (360 ft) long, 11.58 m (38 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rantau Panjang–Sungai Golok Bridge, also known as the 'Harmony Bridge', is a road bridge crossing the Kolok River at the Malaysia-Thailand border. It connects Rantau Panjang in Malaysia with Su-ngai Kolok in Thailand. The bridge is part of the Asian highway network AH18 and was built by the governments of both countries. It was officially opened on 21 May 1973 by Malaysian Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak and Thai Prime Minister Field Marshal Thanom Kittikachorn.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on 21 May 1973 by Malaysian Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak and Thai Prime Minister Field Marshal Thanom Kittikachorn.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a beam bridge with box girders. The main part includes three spans, each 30.48 metres (100 ft) long, using prestressed concrete. Each end is connected to a ferroconcrete span, 9.14 m (30 ft) long. The road surface is 7.32 m (24 ft) wide with a 2.13 m (7 ft) wide walkway on each side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes the harmonious relationship between Malaysia and Thailand, facilitating cross-border travel and trade.
Notable_Visitors: Tun Abdul Razak bin Haji Dato' Hussein Al-Haj
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was constructed by Chang Loon Construction Co., Ltd., a Malaysian contractor, which won the bidding on 25 September 1970. The construction was completed on 20 March 1973, and the company had to pay an overtime penalty due to the delay in completion.

world knowledge.Name: Tamarack Resort
world knowledge.Address: West shore of Lake Cascade, southwest of Donnelly, Idaho
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 3,600 acres (2,124 state lease land, 1,484 private land)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tamarack Resort is a four-season destination resort in the western United States. It was the first new destination ski resort built in North America in 23 years when it opened in 2004. The resort has undergone multiple ownership changes, financial difficulties, and closures but has since been revitalized by new ownership.

Major_Events.Description: The alpine ski area officially opened with chairlift service on December 15, 2004.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by President George W. Bush
Major_Events.Description: President George W. Bush and First Lady Laura Bush stayed at Tamarack, giving the resort significant national exposure.
The resort was closed in March 2009 due to financial difficulties and reopened in December 2010 under new management.
Tamarack Resort Holdings acquired the resort, with plans to redevelop and expand the facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Reinstallation of Wildwood Express ski lift
Major_Events.Description: The Wildwood Express ski lift was reinstalled, adding more than 200 acres of skiable terrain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Village at Tamarack Resort consists of six separate buildings with 47,000 square feet of commercial space, including retail, restaurants, and luxury condominiums. Heated underground parking is available. The resort features a Robert Trent Jones II signature 18-hole golf course and multiple ski lifts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tamarack Resort is significant as the first new destination ski resort built in North America in over two decades. It has hosted notable visitors, including President George W. Bush, and has been a focal point for regional tourism and recreation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Four-season destination resort offering skiing, golf, mountain biking, and other recreational activities.
world knowledge.Details: Tamarack Resort has faced multiple financial and operational challenges but continues to develop as a premier destination. The resort features 1,100 acres of skiable terrain, 50 trails, and 7 chairlifts. It also offers a golf course, mountain biking, and Nordic trails.

world knowledge.Name: St. Nicholas Church, Stralsund
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Nicholas Church is the oldest of the three major parish churches of the Hanseatic city of Stralsund in Germany. Dedicated in 1279 to Saint Nicholas of Myra, the patron saint of sailors, it has been an Evangelical Lutheran church since 1524. It is one of the earliest examples of the introduction of the cathedral pattern of northern France into the Brick Gothic architecture of the Baltic region. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2002 as part of the historic centre of Stralsund.

Major_Events.Description: The church was dedicated to Saint Nicholas of Myra.
Altars and shrines were destroyed or stolen during the Protestant Reformation.
A fire destroyed the wooden spires of the towers.
The roof and windows of the church were damaged during World War II.
Repairs started after the damage from the bombing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is an example of Brick Gothic architecture. It was initially built as a hall church with a tower in 1234 and later rebuilt as a basilica after 1270, following the design of St. Mary's Church in Lübeck. The construction of the western tower began in 1300, and the nave between the two towers was completed around 1350. The church features a Baroque dome on the southern tower and a temporary roof on the northern tower. The church once housed 56 altars, many of which were removed after the Reformation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Nicholas Church is culturally and historically important as one of the earliest examples of Brick Gothic architecture in the Baltic region and as a key site in the Protestant Reformation. It is also part of the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the historic centre of Stralsund.
world knowledge.Details: The church features an astronomical clock built in 1394 by Nikolaus Lilienfeld, which is the oldest almost completely preserved astronomical clock in the Baltic region. The church also houses a high altar made by a Stralsund sculptor around 1480, which was partially destroyed during World War II and later restored. The church has two large and two small organs, and the medieval color patterns were restored starting in 1980.

world knowledge.Name: Archaeological Museum of Volos
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Archaeological Museum of Volos, also known as Athanasakeion Archaeological Museum of Volos, houses many exquisite finds from early 20th century and modern archaeological excavations in Thessaly. Exhibits include items from the Neolithic settlements of Dimini and Sesklo, the Geometric period, classical period, Hellenistic period, early Christian and Byzantine periods.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its extensive collection of artifacts from various historical periods, including the Neolithic, Geometric, classical, Hellenistic, early Christian, and Byzantine periods. It provides insights into the history and culture of Thessaly.
world knowledge.Details: Exhibits on display include jewelry, household utensils, agricultural tools, clay statuettes, statues, jointed statuettes, steles with relief work, and tombs transported in their entirety from archaeological sites. Outside the museum, there are reconstructions of Neolithic houses from Dimini and Sesklo.

world knowledge.Name: Dr. Juan A. Rivero Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Dr. Juan A. Rivero Zoo, officially named the Dr. Juan A. Rivero Zoo of Puerto Rico, also known as the Mayagüez Zoo, was a 45-acre (18 ha) zoological park located in Mayagüez, Puerto Rico, owned by the Government of Puerto Rico and operated by the Department of Natural and Environmental Resources, under the agency of the Company of National Parks of Puerto Rico. It was named in honor of Juan A. Rivero, its first director. It was Puerto Rico's only zoo and had an extensive collection of animals from all continents. The zoo closed to the public after the impact of Hurricane Maria in 2017 and fully ceased operations in 2023 after much scrutiny in its final years due to questionable health and treatment of their animals. All species were later relocated to sanctuaries across the United States after the closure.

Major_Events.Description: The zoo closed to the public after the impact of Hurricane Maria.
The zoo fully ceased operations in 2023 after much scrutiny in its final years due to questionable health and treatment of their animals.
Mundi, a female African savanna elephant, was relocated to Buckley's Elephant Refuge North America sanctuary in Attapulgus, Georgia.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The zoo was Puerto Rico's only zoo and had an extensive collection of animals from all continents. It was committed to animal welfare, especially those facing extinction, and had several conservation programs for the Puerto Rican crested toad, the plain pigeon, and the Andean condor.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo went through a major upgrade in 2003 with the addition of an aviary, arthropodary, and a butterfly exhibition. In March 2008, the zoo acquired two new giraffes and two desert warthogs to augment the African collection. The economic crisis related to the government debt crisis in Puerto Rico that began in 2014 led to issues with zoo maintenance and animal care. Despite the zoo being closed to the public after Hurricane Maria in September 2017, the zoo still had employed zookeepers to care for the animals, including two lion cubs that were born at the zoo in 2019. In 2020, FEMA had assigned $6.2 million to the zoo for repairs related to the hurricane. Within the zoo's final ten years alone, the zoo was cited for several violations of inhumane killings, including a puma, coatimundi, and a baboon that were 'not fit for exhibition'. The United States Department of Agriculture investigated the zoo and did not renew their federal permits. On May 23, 2022, it was announced that the zoo's male chimpanzee, Magnum, had died at the age of 39. On February 27, 2023, the permanent closure of the zoo was announced by order of the United States Department of Justice, following much scrutiny due to questionable health and malnourishment of their animals, as well as the treatment they were receiving. The efforts to relocate all species to sanctuaries were completed between February and June 2023, with assistance from the Puerto Rico Natural Resources Ranger Corps, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, and The Wild Animal Sanctuary in Keenesburg, Colorado.

world knowledge.Name: Kiunga Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kiunga Airport is an airport located in Kiunga, Papua New Guinea. The article about this airport is currently a stub on Wikipedia, indicating that more information is needed to fully document its history and significance.
world knowledge.Details: Kiunga Airport (IATA: UNG, ICAO: AYKI) is an airport in Kiunga, Papua New Guinea. This article about an airport in Papua New Guinea is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Cardiff Bay Barrage
world knowledge.Address: Between Queen Alexandra Dock and Penarth Head, Cardiff, Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cardiff Bay Barrage was one of the largest civil engineering projects in Europe during the 1990s. It was conceived to revitalize the derelict Cardiff docklands by creating a permanent freshwater lake, making the area more appealing for investment. The project was inspired by the redevelopment of Baltimore Inner Harbor in the US. Construction began in 1994 and was completed in 1999, with the barrage opening to the public in 2001.

Major_Events.Description: The sluice gates were closed at high water to retain seawater from the Bristol Channel, creating a freshwater lake.
The barrage was opened to the public, marking the completion of the project.
The barrage was used as a special stage during the 2010 Wales Rally GB.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The barrage is 1.1 km (0.68 mi) long and 7.96 m (26.1 ft) high, with five controlled spillways. It includes a fish pass for salmon, three locks for maritime traffic, and oxygenation systems to improve water quality.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cardiff Bay Barrage played a crucial role in the regeneration of the area, attracting new homes, shops, restaurants, and cultural attractions like the Wales Millennium Centre and The Senedd. It has won awards for engineering excellence and is a key feature in the transformation of Cardiff Bay into a thriving commercial and tourist district.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Barrage to impound freshwater and create a permanent lake, enhancing the area's appeal for development and tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The barrage has faced opposition from environmentalists and local residents due to concerns about cost, environmental impact, and potential damage to homes. It has also been criticized for the loss of intertidal mudflats, which affected bird populations. Despite these challenges, the barrage has significantly contributed to the area's regeneration and is a popular site for tourism and recreational activities.

world knowledge.Name: Point Perpendicular Light
world knowledge.Address: Point Perpendicular, Beecroft Peninsula, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Point Perpendicular Light was built to replace the inadequately located Cape St George Lighthouse. It was active from 1889 to 1993 and is believed to be the first lighthouse in New South Wales built of precast concrete blocks. The light was replaced in 1993 with a skeletal tower.

Major_Events.Description: The light was first lit on 1 May 1899 with a vaporized kerosene lamp and a Chance Bros. 1st order Fresnel lens.
The lighthouse was relit on 1 May 1999 to celebrate its centenary, with celebrations including a ball, art competition, and public tours.
The lighthouse was relit on 20–21 August 2005 for the International Lighthouse & Lightship Weekend.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is made from precast concrete blocks, cement-rendered inside and outside, with a circular shape and an internal diameter of 11 feet 9 inches. It has three stories with concrete floors, staircases, and a bluestone gallery and balcony. The tower is painted white with a blue trim and features a Waratah window above the main door.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Listed on the Commonwealth Heritage List, it is historically significant as the first lighthouse in New South Wales built of precast concrete blocks and for its role in maritime navigation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Lighthouse (originally for maritime navigation, now deactivated)
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was automated in 1993 and replaced with a skeletal tower. The site is now operated by the Department of Defence and used for gunnery practice. The original Fresnel lens remains installed in the lighthouse. Access to the historic lighthouse is restricted due to its location on a defence site.

world knowledge.Name: Sentosa
world knowledge.Area: Southern coast of Singapore's main island
world knowledge.Location: Separated from the main island of Singapore by Keppel Harbour, adjacent to Pulau Brani
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1970s (renamed and developed as a tourist destination)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a British military base and later a Japanese prisoner-of-war camp, renamed Sentosa in the 1970s to become a tourist destination. It has since developed into a major resort island with attractions like Universal Studios Singapore, Fort Siloso, and beaches.

Major_Events.Description: First-ever meeting between North Korean Chairman Kim Jong-un and U.S. President Donald Trump, held at Capella Singapore on Sentosa.
The island was renamed from Pulau Blakang Mati to Sentosa, meaning 'peace and tranquility' in Malay, derived from Sanskrit 'Santosha'.
Integrated resort featuring Universal Studios Singapore, a casino, and other attractions, opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features a mix of modern resort architecture, historical military forts (e.g., Fort Siloso), and artificial beaches. Includes cable car networks, themed parks, and luxury hotels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Symbolizes Singapore's transformation from a military outpost to a global tourist destination. Hosts significant historical sites and international events, blending leisure with cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourism and recreation, featuring resorts, beaches, theme parks, and historical sites.
world knowledge.Details: Sentosa is home to Resorts World Sentosa, Universal Studios Singapore, and several beaches. It has a rich history as a military base and POW camp, now repurposed for tourism. The island also hosts environmental sustainability initiatives and retains 25% of its natural greenery.

world knowledge.Name: Caramoan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Caramoan was named in 1619 by Spanish missionary friar Francisco de la Cruz Y Oropesa. Before the Spanish arrival, it was known as Guta de Leche by Dutch traders who operated a gold mine in Lahuy Island. The name Caramoan was derived from the sea turtle, 'Carahan', found in great numbers along the shores of the Peninsula.

Major_Events.Event: Founding by Francisco de la Cruz Y Oropesa
Major_Events.Description: Spanish missionary friar Francisco de la Cruz Y Oropesa founded a small settlement in a place called Baluarte.
The settlement was turned over to the administration of the Holy Bishopric.
Caramoan has hosted multiple international editions of the Survivor reality TV show, including U.S., Serbian, Israeli, Bulgarian, Swedish, Finnish, French, Indian, Romanian, and Czech versions.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Caramoan is culturally significant for its historical roots dating back to the Spanish colonial era and its international recognition as a filming location for the Survivor reality TV series. It is also known for its natural beauty, including white and pink sand beaches.
world knowledge.Details: Caramoan is known as the Emerging Paradise of the Pacific due to its stunning beaches and natural landscapes. It offers activities such as diving, swimming, snorkeling, and spelunking. The area is politically subdivided into 49 barangays and has a population of 51,728 people as of the 2020 census.

world knowledge.Name: Victoria and Albert Museum
world knowledge.Address: Cromwell Road, Kensington and Chelsea, London, SW7
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Victoria and Albert Museum (V&A) in London is the world's largest museum of applied arts, decorative arts, and design, housing a permanent collection of over 2.8 million objects. It was founded in 1852 and named after Queen Victoria and Prince Albert.
