Attendance suffered at the PCC.
The PCC doubled its advertising budget to promote local music, dance and food festivals.
Contestants display their skills with blazing swords.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Eight simulated tropical villages showcasing Polynesian arts and crafts, a lagoon for canoe rides, and a special exhibit dedicated to Rapa Nui (Easter Island).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The PCC preserves and showcases Polynesian culture, provides employment and scholarships for students, and is one of Hawaii's most popular tourist attractions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural tourist attraction and living museum
world knowledge.Details: The PCC features an evening show titled Hā–Breath of Life, a multicultural Polynesian show highlighting song and dance from the indigenous cultures of the South Pacific. The show features songs and dances throughout Polynesia, including the hula, tamure, otea, titi torea, haka, poi, meke, tauʻolunga, and Taualuga. The PCC also hosts special events such as the Moanikeala Hula Festival, the World Fireknife Championships, and the Micronesia Betelnut Festival. Visitors can participate in a luʻau, such as the Aliʻi Luʻau (Royal Feast), which offers traditional Polynesian fare, including pork cooked in an imu (an underground oven). The PCC has its own Special effect theater and a lagoon where visitors can take canoe rides accompanied by a guide or paddle by themselves.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Monte-Cristo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Monte-Cristo was built as a residence for writer Alexandre Dumas, designed by architect Hippolyte Durand. Dumas named it after his novel 'The Count of Monte Cristo'. Financial difficulties forced Dumas to sell it in 1848. It later served as the British School of Paris (1954-1964) and fell into disrepair until its restoration by local authorities. Since 1994, it has operated as a public museum dedicated to Dumas.

Major_Events.Description: Built for Alexandre Dumas at a cost of 500,000 francs.
Dumas sold the property for 31,000 francs due to financial difficulties.
The château served as the site of the British School of Paris.
The château and gardens were restored and opened as a public museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Renaissance style with three storeys. Façades decorated with floral motifs, angels, and musical instruments, featuring sculptures of historical writers above ground-floor windows. The main door displays Dumas' family shield. Includes the Moors Salon and a Neo-Gothic pavilion in the garden named 'Château d'If'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The château is a memorial to Alexandre Dumas, one of France's most celebrated writers, and reflects his literary legacy through its design and naming. It is a cultural landmark tied to his works, particularly 'The Count of Monte Cristo'.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, now a public historic museum.
world knowledge.Details: The garden features a Neo-Gothic pavilion used by Dumas as a writing office, named after the Château d'If from 'The Count of Monte Cristo'. The Moors Salon was restored by Hassan II of Morocco.

world knowledge.Name: Faux de Verzy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Faux de Verzy are dwarf beech, oak, and chestnut trees found in the forest of Verzy. The term 'fau' comes from Old French, meaning beech. The trees have been documented since the 6th century, with monks potentially cultivating them. The area has been a national reserve since 1932.

Major_Events.Description: The area was officially listed as a national reserve to protect the dwarf beeches.
Legend says Joan of Arc rested in the forest and climbed one of the dwarf beeches.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The trees are dwarf varieties, with twisted, bent, and pendulous trunks and branches. They grow no more than 4-5 meters high and have umbrella-like leaf spreads in summer.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Faux de Verzy are a unique natural phenomenon and a significant part of local folklore. They are associated with legends, including Joan of Arc's visit, and are considered a natural heritage site.
world knowledge.Details: The forest contains over 1,000 dwarf beeches, the largest concentration in the world. Some trees have names based on their shapes, such as 'the umbrella Fau' and 'the Fau of the bride.' Genetic mutation is the leading hypothesis for their dwarfism. Conservation efforts include pathways to protect roots and in vitro propagation.

world knowledge.Name: University of Tennessee
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 600 acres (240 ha) (main campus), Total: 2,128 acres (861 ha)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded as Blount College in 1794, renamed East Tennessee College (1807), East Tennessee University (1840), and finally University of Tennessee (1879). It became a land-grant institution in 1869. The university resisted desegregation until the 1950s and 1960s.

Major_Events.Description: Established as a non-sectarian, all-male, white-only institution.
Rechartered under a new name as part of the Compact of 1806 settlement.
Designated as Tennessee's recipient of Morrill Act funds, focusing on military, agricultural, and mechanical education.
Elevated from East Tennessee University to its current name.
Began limited desegregation despite state constitutional prohibitions.
First Black undergraduates admitted after Brown v. Board of Education.
Settlement of a 1968 lawsuit alleging continued segregation in Tennessee higher education, resulting in $77 million for diversity initiatives.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features a mix of historic and modern buildings, with uniform design codes implemented as part of a 25-year master plan. The iconic Ayres Hall is a notable structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oldest public university in Tennessee and oldest secular institution west of the Eastern Continental Divide. Known for research contributions, athletic programs, and historical role in education.

Details.Notable_Alumni: 9 Rhodes Scholars, James M. Buchanan (Nobel Prize in Economics), Pat Summitt (legendary basketball coach)
Details.Research_Affiliations: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, SEC Academic Consortium
Details.Student_Organizations: 450+ registered groups, including Greek life, media outlets, and sports clubs
Details.Athletics: NCAA Division I (SEC), 8 women's basketball national titles, famous "Pride of the Southland" marching band
Details.Controversies: Ranked most LGBTQ-unfriendly university by Princeton Review (2023), history of segregation

world knowledge.Name: Melbourne Rectangular Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Melbourne Rectangular Stadium, also known as AAMI Park, was built in 2010 as Melbourne's first large, purpose-built rectangular stadium. It addressed the need for a venue suitable for rugby league, rugby union, and association football, which were previously hosted at oval-shaped stadiums like the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) and Docklands Stadium. The stadium was part of Melbourne's bid for a Super Rugby team and was constructed to replace the older Olympic Park Stadium.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium's first match, featuring the Australian and New Zealand rugby league teams, with Australia winning 12–8.
Hosted the opening ceremony and seven matches, including the tournament opener and a quarter-final.
Hosted six matches, including group games and knockout stages.
Hosted matches in both years, with Australia defeating England in both instances.
Hosted the opening match and a quarter-final match.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by COX Architecture, the stadium features a 'Bioframe' design with a geodesic dome roof that covers much of the seating area while allowing light to reach the pitch. The exterior is covered with LED lights that can display various patterns and images. The stadium includes training facilities, office accommodations, and public amenities like bars and cafes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it fulfilled Melbourne's need for a dedicated rectangular stadium, enhancing the city's capability to host major rugby and soccer events. It has become a key venue for international and domestic sports, contributing to Melbourne's reputation as a sporting capital. The stadium has won awards for its iconic design and cultural impact.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for rugby league, rugby union, and association football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a seating capacity of 30,050 and features 24 corporate boxes, a dining room for 1,000 people, and facilities for various sports teams. It was renovated in 2023 with new video screens, LED lighting, and improved player and broadcasting facilities. The stadium's naming rights are held by AAMI until 2026. It has hosted numerous high-profile events, including concerts and international sports tournaments.

image_name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception

world knowledge.Name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception is a Catholic minor basilica and national shrine in Washington D.C. It is the largest Catholic church building in North America and is also the tallest habitable building in Washington, D.C. Its construction of Byzantine and Romanesque Revival architecture began on 23 September 1920. The basilica is dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary as the Immaculate Conception, designated as the principal Patroness accorded by Pope Pius IX on February 7, 1847.

Major_Events.Description: Archbishop Giovanni Bonzano, Apostolic Nuncio to the United States of America, celebrated Mass and blessed the site of the future National Shrine.
The first public mass ever offered at the shrine was held in the unfinished Crypt Church.

Major_Events.Event: Dedication of the Great Upper Church
Major_Events.Description: Thousands of Catholics gathered with the bishops for the dedication of the Great Upper Church.
Pope John Paul II raised the national shrine to the status of a minor basilica.
Pope Benedict XVI bestowed the Golden Rose upon the Basilica.
Pope Francis celebrated a Mass for the canonization of Saint Junípero Serra.
The final architectural element was completed with the installation of the 24 tons of Venetian glass in the central Trinity Dome.

Architectural_Characteristics.Materials: Thick masonry walls and columns, iridescent Pewabic Pottery tile, ceramic medallions, mosaics
Architectural_Characteristics.Dome: Trinity Dome covered in 47,000 gloss Ludowici shingle tiles arranged to form biblical patterns
Architectural_Characteristics.Features: 82 Marian chapels, Greek-styled interior crowned with numerous domes decorated in mosaics, largest radiant heating slab in the world (in 1959)

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The basilica is the largest Catholic church building in North America and is dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary as the Immaculate Conception, the patroness of the United States. It serves as a national shrine and a symbol of the Catholic faith in America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious site (Minor basilica and national shrine)

Details.Tradition: Roman Rite, various Eastern Catholic liturgies
Details.Access: Served by the Brookland–CUA station on the Red Line, roughly 550 yards (500 m) away.

world knowledge.Name: Graz Airport
world knowledge.Address: Abtissendorf, Feldkirchen and Thalerhof, Kalsdorf, Styria, Austria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Graz Airport, known as Flughafen Graz in German, is a primary international airport serving southern Austria. It began construction in 1913 with a grass runway and the first hangars, seeing its first flight in 1914. It was the site of Thalerhof internment camp during the Austro-Hungarian Empire. The airport has undergone several expansions and upgrades, including the construction of new terminal buildings and runway extensions to accommodate increasing passenger numbers.

Major_Events.Event: First domestic passenger flight in Austria
Major_Events.Description: The route Vienna–Graz–Klagenfurt was serviced.

Major_Events.Event: Regular flights linking Belgrade with Vienna
Major_Events.Description: Yugoslav flag carrier Aeroput started regular flights with stops in Zagreb and Graz.
Concorde visited the airport.
A Boeing 747 visited on the occasion of the airport's 70th anniversary.
Eurowings announced the establishment of an additional base at Graz Airport, featuring nine new routes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a passenger terminal building with shops, travel agencies, a restaurant, cafés, conference facilities, a bank, car rental, and service counters. The apron provides stands for aircraft up to the size of a Boeing 747 or An-124. There are no jet bridges; mobile stairways are used for boarding. The airport has a VIP lounge for business class customers and customers with priority status.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Graz Airport is significant as a major transportation hub in southern Austria, facilitating both domestic and international travel. It has played a role in the region's economic development and has historical importance as the site of the Thalerhof internment camp during the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is accessible via motorways A9 and A2. It features a bus stop next to the arrival area and is within walking distance of the Graz-Feldkirchen Airport Railway Station. The passenger terminal building has a maximum annual capacity of 750,000 passengers. While there are no scheduled cargo flights, charter flights are regularly conducted, especially for time-critical cargo like automotive parts.

world knowledge.Name: Little Moreton Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Little Moreton Hall is a moated half-timbered manor house built for the prosperous Cheshire landowner William Moreton in about 1504–08 and completed by successive generations of the family until about 1610. The house remained in the possession of the Moreton family for almost 450 years, until ownership was transferred to the National Trust in 1938. It has been fully restored and is open to the public from April to December each year.

Major_Events.Description: Little Moreton Hall was requisitioned by the Parliamentarians during the English Civil War and used to billet Parliamentary soldiers.
Ownership of Little Moreton Hall was transferred to the National Trust.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is a 16th-century half-timbered structure with three asymmetrical ranges forming a small, rectangular cobbled courtyard. It features a Long Gallery, timber framing with diagonal oak braces, and leaded panes in windows. The house stands on an island surrounded by a 33-foot wide moat.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Little Moreton Hall is a significant example of a Tudor-period manor house, showcasing medieval carpentry and architectural styles. It is a Grade I listed building and a Scheduled Monument, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Little Moreton Hall is open to the public from mid-February to December each year. The ground floor of the west range has been remodelled to include a restaurant and a tearoom, while a new building houses the visitor reception and shop. Services are held in the Chapel every Sunday from April until October.

world knowledge.Name: Ponte del Risorgimento
world knowledge.Address: Piazzale delle Belle Arti to Piazza Monte Grappa, Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Italian unification, Ponte del Risorgimento is the first bridge in Rome made of reinforced concrete. It was designed by Giovanni Antonio Porcheddu, who was the only Italian dealer of the patent of the Belgian François Hennebique at the time.

Major_Events.Description: On April 17, 1911, the bridge was inaugurated. During the ceremony, King Victor Emmanuel III offered Porcheddu the epithet 'King of reinforced concrete'. Porcheddu attended the demolition of the scaffolding on a boat below the arch of the bridge, demonstrating his confidence in the structure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is made of reinforced concrete and features a single arch design. It was a pioneering structure in Rome for its use of this material.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes the technological advancements and national pride during the Italian unification period. It is also notable for being the first reinforced concrete bridge in Rome.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge connecting Piazzale delle Belle Arti to Piazza Monte Grappa over the River Tiber.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge has two inscriptions on its bulwarks. It links the area of Lungotevere delle Armi to Piazzale delle Belle Arti.

world knowledge.Name: Tangkoko Batuangus Nature Reserve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first conservation area at Mount Tongkoko was established in 1919. The Duasaudara area was added in 1978, and the Batuangus and Batuputih areas in 1981, together encompassing a total of 8,718 hectares (21,540 acres). Visitation is only allowed in the Batuputih area.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Mount Tongkoko conservation area
Major_Events.Description: The first conservation area at Mount Tongkoko was established.
The Duasaudara area was added to the reserve.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of Batuangus and Batuputih areas
Major_Events.Description: The Batuangus and Batuputih areas were added to the reserve, encompassing a total of 8,718 hectares (21,540 acres).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tangkoko Batuangus Nature Reserve protects at least 127 mammal, 233 bird, and 104 reptile and amphibian species, many of which are endemic to the island. It is a popular destination for wildlife watching tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The reserve includes three mountains: Mount Tangkoko at 1,109 metres (3,638 feet), Mount Dua Saudara at 1,361 metres (4,465 feet), and Mount Batuangus at 450 metres (1,480 feet). Threatened species include the Celebes crested macaque, spectral tarsier, Sulawesi bear cuscus, and Sulawesi dwarf cuscus. Several Indonesian and international environmental organisations are involved with conservation efforts in the reserve. Habitat destruction and hunting pose serious threats to the reserve.

world knowledge.Name: Santa Fe Opera
world knowledge.Area: Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States
world knowledge.Address: 301 Opera Drive, Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1956 by John Crosby, the Santa Fe Opera (SFO) is an American opera company located 7 miles north of Santa Fe, New Mexico. It was built on a former guest ranch and has presented operas each summer festival season since July 1957. The company is known for introducing new operas and productions of standard operatic repertoire.

Major_Events.Description: The first performance was Puccini's Madama Butterfly on July 3, 1957, in the original open-air theatre.
A fire destroyed the original theatre on July 27, 1967, forcing the company to relocate to a local high school for the remainder of the season.
A new open-air theatre was completed and opened on June 26, 1968, with another performance of Madama Butterfly.
The current theatre, designed by James Polshek, opened in July 1998 after extensive reconstruction, featuring improved facilities and protection from the elements.
The opera introduced COVID-safe protocols, including a new position for a Covid Compliance and Safety Manager, and simulcasts of performances as drive-in theater events.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Crosby Theatre features an open-air design with no proscenium arch or fly system, and the sides of the house are open to the surrounding landscape. The stage roof is designed to provide protection while allowing views of the sunset. The theatre seats 2,128 plus 106 standees and includes an electronic titles system for translations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Santa Fe Opera is internationally recognized for its contributions to opera, including premieres of new works and innovative productions. It has staged 45 American premieres and 18 world premieres, fostering the careers of many notable singers through its Apprentice Program.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts center, specializing in opera productions.
world knowledge.Details: The Santa Fe Opera runs an annual summer festival from late June or early July to the third week of August, presenting five operas in rotating repertory. It features the Apprentice Program for Singers and Technicians, which has trained over 1,500 aspiring opera professionals. The opera house is also known for its tailgate dining tradition and stunning sunset views during performances.

world knowledge.Name: Universidad Autónoma de Chiriquí
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Autonomous University of Chiriquí (UNACHI) is a Panamanian university founded in 1995. It is the third autonomous state institution of higher education and the first in the western region of the country.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UNACHI is culturally significant as it provides higher education access to the western region of Panama, contributing to regional development and educational opportunities.
world knowledge.Details: The university consists of several faculties and has regional campuses and college extensions in the Chiriquí Province to increase access to higher education.

world knowledge.Name: Musée d'Orsay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée d'Orsay is housed in the former Gare d'Orsay, a Beaux-Arts railway station built from 1898 to 1900. It was converted into a museum in the 1970s to bridge the gap between the Louvre and the National Museum of Modern Art at the Georges Pompidou Centre. The museum officially opened in December 1986.

Major_Events.Description: Built as a railway station for the Chemin de Fer de Paris à Orléans, finished in time for the 1900 Exposition Universelle.
The station was converted into a museum to house French art from 1848 to 1914, including the largest collection of Impressionist and post-Impressionist masterpieces in the world.
The museum officially opened in December 1986 by then-president François Mitterrand.
A radical transformation of the museum, funded in part by an anonymous US patron, to implement new galleries and education opportunities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a Beaux-Arts railway station with a barrel vault atrium. The central nave was formed by the surrounding stone structures that were previously the building's train platforms. The interior was designed by Gae Aulenti, featuring elaborate gallery arrangements on three main levels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Musée d'Orsay holds the largest collection of Impressionist and post-Impressionist masterpieces in the world, including works by Monet, Manet, Degas, Renoir, Cézanne, Gauguin, and van Gogh. It is a key institution for understanding 19th and early 20th-century French art and culture.

Details.Collections: Mainly French art dating from 1848 to 1914, including paintings, sculptures, furniture, and photography. Notable collections include the Marlene and Spencer Hays Collection and over 2,200 sculptures.

world knowledge.Name: Central Radio & TV Tower
world knowledge.Address: 11 Xisanhuan Street, Haidian District, Beijing, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Central Radio & TV Tower is a 405-metre-tall telecommunications and observation tower in Beijing, China. It was the tallest structure in the city until 2018, when it was surpassed by China Zun. Completed in 1992, it was designed by Paulus Snoeren in the late 1980s and contains broadcasting equipment for China Central Television. The tower is a member of the World Federation of Great Towers.

Major_Events.Description: On May 10, 2004, the Central Radio and Television Tower adjusted the microwave signals of publicly transmitted China Central Television (CCTV) programs, with the signals of the Sports Channel and the Variety Channel being replaced by the Music Channel and the Children's Channel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower features a Modernism architectural style, with an antenna spire reaching 405 m (1,329 ft) and a top floor at 248 m (814 ft). It includes an observation deck at 238 m (781 ft) and a revolving restaurant.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower is a significant landmark in Beijing, providing panoramic views over the city and serving as a key telecommunications hub. It is also notable for its annual race to the top, involving two laps of the base and a climb of 1,484 steps to the observation deck.
world knowledge.Details: The tower has 4 floors opened to the public, including a lounge, toilets, and lifts to various levels. It also features exhibits on the history of famous people in China and how CCTV (Chinese TV program) works. The tower is located near Gongzhufen metro station and Yuyuantan Park.

world knowledge.Name: Jerusalem Biblical Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tisch Family Biblical Zoo in Jerusalem, popularly known as the Jerusalem Biblical Zoo, was opened in September 1940 as a small 'animal corner' on Rabbi Kook Street in central Jerusalem. It was founded by Aharon Shulov, a professor of zoology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. The zoo relocated several times due to complaints from neighbors and wartime conditions, eventually settling in its current location in Malha in 1993. The zoo is famous for its Afro-Asiatic collection of wildlife, many of which are described in the Hebrew Bible, and for its success in breeding endangered species.

Major_Events.Description: The zoo opened as a small 'animal corner' on Rabbi Kook Street in central Jerusalem.
The zoo moved to its current location in the Malha valley, 7 kilometres southwest of the city center.
The zoo logged a record 738,000 visitors in 2009.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo is built on two main levels with a motorized train taking visitors on a circular route. The park is landscaped with trees and shrubs native to Israel, many of which are mentioned in the Bible. The centerpiece of the lower level is an artificial lake with monkey exhibits. The zoo features a boat-shaped visitor's center resembling Noah's Ark, and the traditional zoo infrastructure of bars and cages has been replaced by open areas separated from the public by trenches, moats, bridges, and glass windows.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The zoo is culturally significant as it houses animals mentioned in the Hebrew Bible and focuses on the conservation of endangered species. It serves as a bridge between different cultural and religious groups in Jerusalem, attracting both Haredi families from northern Jerusalem and Muslim families from East Jerusalem.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo is a full member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) and the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA). It operates an animal medical center, conducts breeding programs for endangered species, and participates in national and international research projects. The zoo also focuses on public education and environmentalism, offering educational activities for children and maintaining a 'green' policy with its own sewage treatment system and recycling practices.

world knowledge.Name: Chimelong International Ocean Tourist Resort
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chimelong International Ocean Tourist Resort is a theme park resort developed by Chimelong Group with a 20 billion yuan investment. It began with the opening of Chimelong Ocean Kingdom in 2014 and has since expanded to include multiple theme parks, theaters, and hotels.

Major_Events.Event: Soft opening of Chimelong Ocean Kingdom
Major_Events.Description: The first theme park at the resort, designed by PGAV Destinations, had its soft opening in January 2014.

Major_Events.Event: Official opening of Chimelong Ocean Kingdom
Major_Events.Description: The park officially opened in March 2014.
The world's largest indoor theme park and aquarium, masterplanned by Legacy Entertainment, opened in 2023.
A new, larger indoor theater became the resort's primary circus theater venue on 26 July 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features a mix of indoor and outdoor theme parks, theaters, and hotels. Notable structures include Chimelong Spaceship (world's largest indoor theme park and aquarium) and Hengqin Island Theater. Future plans include an aerial tramway and artificial island with marine facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The resort is a major tourist destination in China, hosting performances like the Chimelong Hengqin International Circus City and the annual China International Circus Festival. It also contributes to the local economy and tourism industry.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theme park resort offering entertainment, accommodation, and cultural performances.

Future_Plans: Artificial island with marine theater and museum
Details.Transportation: Accessed by bus or car; internal transport includes walking and boat rides on the central canal.
Details.Hotels: Three hotels on site with a fourth under construction.

world knowledge.Name: People's Park (Xining)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: People's Park is an urban public park in central Xining, established in 1959 and expanded in 1964. The park was redesigned by Yao Jingquan, a graduate of Beijing Forestry University, who introduced an artificial lake as the centerpiece. The lake was dug by citizen volunteers and completed in three months. The park was reopened in 1965 after further construction.

Major_Events.Description: The park was first opened with a simple zoo.
Yao Jingquan redesigned the park, introducing an artificial lake and other features. Construction began in 1964, and the park was reopened in 1965.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features an artificial lake lined with willow trees and crossed with two arch bridges in the style of the Jiangnan region. The lake is divided into West Lake and East Lake by a walkway. A 200-meter arcade lines the west bank, and the Lakeview Tower offers panoramic views of the lake and Huangshui River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: People's Park is the largest park in downtown Xining and serves as a significant public space for recreation and cultural activities. Its design reflects a blend of local and Jiangnan architectural styles.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Urban public park for recreation and leisure
world knowledge.Details: The park's artificial lake is used for skating in winter and boating for the rest of the year. Water for the lake is sourced from the nearby Huangshui River. The excavated earth from the lake's construction was used to create an island in the middle of the lake, originally intended to host a six-story pagoda but replaced with a pavilion due to weight concerns.

world knowledge.Name: Papamoa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Māori settlement of Papamoa dates back to approximately 1400 CE with a significant pā complex overlooking the fertile plains and abundant coastal fisheries. Widespread Pākehā settlement of the area did not start until the early 1960s. Papamoa has since become one of the fastest-growing suburbs of Tauranga.

Major_Events.Description: On 2 December 2012, 299 people attempted to set a world record for skinny dipping at Papamoa Beach. The record failed as Guinness World Records required all swimmers to be in the water at the same time for a group photo.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Papamoa is culturally significant due to its long history of Māori settlement and its current status as a popular residential and holiday destination. The local Mangatawa or Tamapahore Marae is a meeting place for the Ngāi Te Rangi hapū of Ngā Pōtiki.
world knowledge.Details: Papamoa Beach is a clothing-optional beach by custom. It has 16 km of white sandy beach and is popular for fishing, surfing, and as a holiday retreat. The suburb has a large shopping area and several schools, including Papamoa College and multiple primary schools.

world knowledge.Name: Magic Kingdom
world knowledge.Address: Walt Disney World, Bay Lake, Florida, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Magic Kingdom Park is a theme park at the Walt Disney World Resort in Bay Lake, Florida. It opened on October 1, 1971, and is owned and operated by the Walt Disney Company through its Experiences division. The park was initialized by Walt Disney and designed by WED Enterprises. The park layout and attractions were based on Disneyland in Anaheim, California, and are dedicated to fairy tales and Disney characters.

Major_Events.Description: Magic Kingdom Park opened as the first part of the Walt Disney World Resort on October 1, 1971, commencing concurrently with Disney's Contemporary Resort and Disney's Polynesian Village Resort.
Mickey's Birthdayland opened to celebrate Mickey Mouse's 60th birthday.
Mickey's Toontown Fair closed on February 12, 2011, to make way for the expansion of Fantasyland.
Magic Kingdom has been closed temporarily because of nine hurricanes: Floyd, Charley, Frances, Jeanne, Wilma, Matthew, Irma, Ian, and Milton.
The park closed on September 11, 2001, due to the terrorist attacks that day.
Walt Disney World was closed from March 15, 2020, to July 11, 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is built over a series of tunnels called utilidors, allowing employees or VIP guests to move through the park out of sight. Because of Florida's high water table, the tunnels could not be put underground, so they were built at the existing grade, meaning the park is built on the second story. The park features a hub and spoke design with pathways leading to six themed lands. Main Street, U.S.A. is modeled after an idealized early-20th century American town, with buildings designed with forced perspective.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Magic Kingdom has become a cultural touchstone and symbol of modern American pop culture. It is the most visited theme park in the world, hosting 17.72 million visitors in 2023. The park is dedicated to fairy tales and Disney characters, representing the philosophy and life of Walt Disney.
world knowledge.Details: Magic Kingdom is divided into six themed lands: Main Street, U.S.A., Adventureland, Frontierland, Liberty Square, Fantasyland, and Tomorrowland. The park icon is Cinderella Castle, inspired by the fairy tale castle featured in the 1950 animated film. The park has a slogan: 'The Most Magical Place On Earth.' In 2024, a Disney executive confirmed that the park will expand with the addition of a 12-to-14-acre land located 'beyond Big Thunder.'

world knowledge.Name: Patterson Mansion
world knowledge.Address: 15 Dupont Circle NW, Washington, D.C., U.S.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Polygonal lot with dimensions: 128 feet 10 inches (south side), 64 feet 6 inches (southwest side), 164 feet 9 inches (northwest side), 132 feet 9 inches (east side). Building is four stories high with a basement, 60 feet high from sidewalk to roof ridgeline.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built by Robert Wilson Patterson, editor of the Chicago Tribune, completed in 1903. Used by the Patterson family for entertaining. Deeded to the American Red Cross in 1948, sold to the Washington Club in 1951. Renovated and expanded in 1955. Sold to developer SB-Urban in 2014 for $20 million. Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1972. Now operates as Oakwood Suites & Studios Dupont Circle Washington DC.

Major_Events.Description: Paint cans in the attic caught fire, causing fire and water damage. Repaired and completed by January 1903.
President Calvin Coolidge and his wife, Grace Coolidge, stayed here while the White House was under renovation.
Charles Lindbergh stayed at the mansion upon his return from his transatlantic flight. Crowds gathered outside, and iconic photos were taken.
The American Red Cross sold the mansion to the Washington Club for $450,000.
The Washington Club added a two-story addition on the east side of the mansion.
The Washington Club sold the mansion to developer SB-Urban for $20 million, leading to its conversion into apartments.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with Italianate decorative motifs. Exterior walls faced with white marble over stone. Features include a semi-elliptical concrete driveway, limestone quoins, decorative string courses, marble panels, and intricate carvings. Interior includes marble staircases, plaster walls, oak parquetry flooring, and Georgian-style fireplaces. Originally had 30 rooms and 10 bathrooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of two remaining mansions on Dupont Circle, contributing property to both the Dupont Circle Historic District and the Massachusetts Avenue Historic District. Notable for its association with the Patterson family, President Coolidge, and Charles Lindbergh. Represents the palatial residences built around Dupont Circle in the early 20th century.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, later used by the American Red Cross and the Washington Club. Now operates as a mixed-use property with apartments and hotel accommodations.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion has undergone several renovations and changes in ownership. It features a ballroom, library, dining room, and multiple bedroom suites. The Washington Club made significant alterations, including adding a two-story addition. The property was rebranded as Oakwood Suites & Studios Dupont Circle Washington DC in 2021, offering 92 residential apartments and hotel accommodations.

world knowledge.Name: Muncaster Castle
world knowledge.Address: Lake District National Park, Cumbria, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Muncaster Castle is a privately owned castle overlooking the River Esk, about a mile east of the west-coastal town of Ravenglass in Cumbria, England. The site may have Roman foundations. The estate was granted to Alan de Penitone in 1208. The oldest parts include the Great Hall and a 14th-century pele tower. It was extensively remodeled by Anthony Salvin between 1860 and 1866. During WWII, 700 works of art from the Tate Gallery were stored here. The Pennington family has owned the castle for at least 800 years.

Major_Events.Description: Henry VI fled to Muncaster Castle where Sir John Pennington sheltered him. Henry gave Sir John a Venetian glass drinking bowl, known as 'The Luck of Muncaster'.
700 works of art from the Tate Gallery were transferred to the castle for safekeeping.
The castle received part of a £35-million injection into the government's Culture Recovery Fund.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle includes a Great Hall and a 14th-century pele tower. It was extensively remodeled by Anthony Salvin in the 19th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Muncaster Castle is a Grade I listed building with historical significance dating back to the 13th century. It is associated with the Pennington family for over 800 years and has hosted significant historical events and figures.
world knowledge.Details: The castle hosts the Muncaster Castle parkrun 5k every Saturday morning. It features gardens, an aviary with raptor birds, and an indoor maze themed on the life of a field vole. The 'Luck of Muncaster' glass bowl and the legend of Thomas Skelton, the original 'Tom Fool', are notable aspects of its history.

world knowledge.Name: University of Zielona Góra
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Zielona Góra was founded on 1 September 2001 as a result of a merger between Zielona Góra's Pedagogical University, which was founded in 1971 and Technical University, which was founded in 1965. It is one of the newer universities in Poland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is one of the newer universities in Poland and plays a significant role in the educational landscape of the region.
world knowledge.Details: Main buildings are located in two campuses: "A" on Podgórna street and "B" on Wojska Polskiego street. The President's office is located near the Old Town on Licealna Street. The University of Zielona Góra runs 12 faculties and 1 branch faculty.

world knowledge.Name: Babelsberg Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Babelsberg Park is a 114-hectare park in Potsdam, Germany, designed by landscape artists Peter Joseph Lenné, Prince Hermann von Pückler-Muskau, and Karl Friedrich Schinkel. It was commissioned by Prince William I and his wife, Augusta. The park is part of the Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park's development involved various phases, including the addition of artificial lakes and the integration of the Böttcherberg hill. After the monarchy's demise in 1918, the park was managed by the Prussian state and later by the Berlin-Brandenburg Foundation for Prussian Palaces and Gardens.

Major_Events.Description: Babelsberg Park was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin.
The Berlin Wall was built, making parts of the park inaccessible until its fall in 1989.
After the fall of the Berlin Wall, the park was reconstructed and made accessible again.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a Neogothic palace, artificial lakes, terraces, promenade paths, flower beds, and the Golden Rose Staircase. The landscape design includes a network of paths, large individual trees, and younger trees planted close together to encourage growth.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Babelsberg Park is culturally significant as part of the Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It represents the development of landscape design and the artistic synthesis of the area around Potsdam.
world knowledge.Details: Babelsberg Park is managed by the Berlin-Brandenburg Foundation for Prussian Palaces and Gardens. The park has faced criticism from local residents for restrictive management practices, including bans on games and cycling. In 2008, some paths were reopened to cyclists. The park includes various buildings, viewing points, rest areas, and garden architecture.

world knowledge.Name: Mumbai Football Arena
world knowledge.Address: Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mumbai Football Arena is a football stadium in Mumbai, India, located in the Andheri Sports Complex. It is one of the few football-only built stadiums in the country. It has served as the home stadium of Mumbai City FC in the Indian Super League since 2016. The stadium was renovated in 2023 with the installation of bucket seats.

Major_Events.Description: India national football team played a FIFA international friendly on 3 September 2016, beating Puerto Rico national football team 4–1 in front of a packed stadium. This was the first international friendly hosted by the city in 61 years.
The stadium hosted the 2017 Hero Tri-Nation Series between India, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Mauritius, which was won by India after topping the table.

The stadium hosted all 7 matches of the 2018 Intercontinental Cup, in which the Indian men's football team played against Kenya, New Zealand, and Chinese Taipei in a four-way tournament. India beat Kenya 2–0 in the final to win the tournament.

It hosted the 2019 Indian Super League Final featuring Bengaluru FC and FC Goa. Bengaluru F.C won the match due to a late goal from defender and local boy Rahul Bheke. This was Bengaluru F.C's first Indian Super League final win after losing in the final the previous year against Chennaiyin FC.
It was one of the host venues of 2022 AFC Women's Asian Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Football-only stadium with grass surface and bucket seats installed in 2023. It features a scoreboard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as one of the few football-only stadiums in India and has hosted numerous international and domestic football events, including matches for the India national football team and the Indian Super League.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 7,000 spectators after renovations in 2023. It is owned by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation and operated by Mumbai City FC. The record attendance was 8,890 during the 2018 Intercontinental Cup. Aditya Thackeray and Ranbir Kapoor played an important role in the redevelopment of the stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Yamanashi Gakuin University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Yamanashi Gakuin was founded in 1946. Today, it is a comprehensive educational institution that includes a kindergarten, elementary school, junior and senior high school, junior college, university and graduate school. YGU sits at the core of the whole institution.

Major_Events.Event: Special prize from the Japan Olympic Committee
Major_Events.Description: Received in recognition of their excellence in world sports.

Major_Events.Event: Special award from Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology
Major_Events.Description: Received in recognition of their excellence in world sports.

Major_Events.Event: Special award from Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology
Major_Events.Description: Received in recognition of their excellence in world sports.
17 athletes participated in the event and two of them won gold medals.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Yamanashi Gakuin University is well known for a long-distance intercollegiate relay race and has produced 70 Olympians in its nearly 70-year history. It has received recognition from the Japan Olympic Committee and Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology for excellence in world sports.
world knowledge.Details: Yamanashi Gakuin University (YGU) is a private university in Kōfu, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It has a student population of 4,200, including 3,500 undergraduates, 40 postgraduates, 80 in iCLA Program, and 575 in Junior College. The university's colors are blue and red, and its website is www.ygu.ac.jp.

world knowledge.Name: Austral University of Chile
world knowledge.Address: Avenue Independencia #641, Valdivia, Los Ríos Region, Chile
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded on September 7, 1954, it is one of the eight original Chilean Traditional Universities. It operates as a nonprofit self-owned corporation under private law and receives significant state-funding. The idea of creating a university was presented to the national congress in the 1950s by the senator for Valdivia, Carlos Acharán Pérez de Arce, who later succeeded in consolidating the project.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded by decree on September 7, 1954, and inaugurated on March 12, 1955, by president Carlos Ibáñez del Campo.
UACh was granted autonomy from the University of Chile as law 16.848 was enacted, allowing UACh to decide its own plans and study programs.

Major_Events.Event: Incorporation of Instituto Profesional de Valdivia
Major_Events.Description: During the military regime's privatization of higher education, UACh incorporated the successor regional see of Universidad Técnica del Estado, the Instituto Profesional de Valdivia.
The university held the Valdivia International Film Festival for the first time to celebrate the 30th anniversary of its cinema Cine Club.
The Emilio Pugín building of the Faculty of Sciences caught fire, causing significant damage to research projects and equipment.
The student federation of UACh decided to go on strike due to dissatisfaction with the university administration's response to their requests.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UACh is one of the leading universities of Chile in matters of scientific research and has a significant impact on the cultural and educational landscape of the region. It hosts important cultural events like the Valdivia International Film Festival and operates several museums.
world knowledge.Details: UACh main campus, Isla Teja Campus, occupies the whole northwest of Isla Teja in Valdivia. The university has satellite campuses in Puerto Montt and Coyhaique. It is known for its research contributions and scientific publications. The university also has a botanical garden with around 950 plant species and operates several museums in Valdivia and southern Chile.

world knowledge.Name: Azhihe River Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Azhihe River Bridge is a 247-meter-high suspension bridge in Guizhou, China, and as of 2019, it was among the fifty highest bridges in the world.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge made of steel, with a height of 247 meters (810 ft) and a longest span of 283 meters (928 ft). Designed by the Major Bridge Reconnaissance Design Institute.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is significant for its engineering achievement, being one of the highest bridges in the world.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries the Shuihuang highway over the Azhihe River, connecting Guanling and Liupanshui.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is located on the Shuihuang highway between Guanling and Liupanshui.

world knowledge.Name: Cantacuzino Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cantacuzino Castle, completed in 1911, was built by architect Grigore Cerchez for Prince Gheorghe Grigore Cantacuzino. It replaced an old hunting lodge used by the Cantacuzino family. The castle served as their summer residence until 1930, was nationalized in 1948, and later restored and opened to the public.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was inaugurated, impressing with its style, beauty, and modern facilities for the time.
The castle was nationalized and became a sanatorium under the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
The castle was returned to Ioana Cantacuzino, the great-granddaughter of Prince Grigore Cantacuzino.
The castle was opened to the public, attracting tens of thousands of visitors annually.
The castle was used as a filming location for the Netflix series Wednesday.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Romanian style, made of carved stone on the outside and brick on the inside, with a concrete foundation and tile roof. The castle consists of four bodies: the central pavilion, service pavilion, administrative villa, and chapel. The central pavilion features a gallery of mural paintings on Cordoba leather and a collection of heraldry in the ballroom.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle holds great architectural, historical, documentary, and artistic value. It is a symbol of the Cantacuzino family's legacy and a notable example of Neo-Romanian architecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mansion (originally a summer residence, now a public tourist attraction)
world knowledge.Details: The castle is surrounded by a 3.5-hectare courtyard with a garden, fountains, and an anthropic cave. It also includes a wooden church dedicated to Saint George the Conqueror. Since 2015, the upper floor hosts an art gallery, and the courtyard features an adventure park and restaurants. The castle is privately owned and receives thousands of visitors annually.

world knowledge.Name: Dow's Hill Interpretation Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dow's Hill Interpretation Centre is located on a hill that was part of the estate of Archibald Dow, a civilian Royal Navy official. The land was acquired in 1789 for fortifications. Dow's House, built in 1732, served as a residence for senior garrison officers and later the Governor of the Leeward Islands before being destroyed by an earthquake in 1834. The museum was established in 1989 with funding from the Canadian International Development Agency.

Major_Events.Description: Dow's House was destroyed by an earthquake, which also ended the permanent presence of a garrison on the site.
The museum was established with a grant from the Canadian International Development Agency to cater to tourists.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is located close to the ruins of the governor's residence and includes a gift shop and café-cum-bar.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum provides a multimedia presentation of Antiguan history, from the first Amerindian settlers to the campaign for independence. It also offers tours of nearby historic sites, contributing to the preservation and promotion of Antigua's cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is operated by the Antigua and Barbuda National Parks Authority and is open daily from 9:00 to 17:00. It offers walking tours to nearby historic sites and a weekly 'Rum in the Ruins' tour where visitors enjoy rum cocktails while exploring the ruins.

world knowledge.Name: St. Mary Cathedral Basilica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Mary Cathedral Basilica is a Catholic church situated in Galveston, Texas. It is the primary cathedral of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and the mother church of Catholics in Texas, as well as a minor basilica. The cathedral was first constructed as a wooden-frame church in 1842, and later rebuilt using imported Belgian bricks in 1847. It was consecrated on November 26, 1848. The cathedral is notable for surviving the devastating 1900 Galveston hurricane with minimal damage. It was designated a Texas state historic landmark in 1968 and a national historic landmark in 1973. In 1979, Pope John Paul II elevated it to the status of a minor basilica.

Major_Events.Description: The small wooden-frame church was dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary by Bishop John Odin.

Major_Events.Event: Cornerstone laying for the new cathedral
Major_Events.Description: The cornerstone for the new cathedral was laid on March 14, 1847, with Father John Timon preaching the sermon.
The cathedral was consecrated on November 26, 1848, with Father John Timon as the principal speaker.
The cathedral survived the devastating 1900 Galveston hurricane with only minimal damage.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a Texas state historic landmark
Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was designated a Texas state historic landmark.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a national historic landmark
Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
Pope John Paul II elevated the cathedral to the status of a minor basilica.
The cathedral sustained significant water damage during Hurricane Ike and was closed for repairs until Easter 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is built in the Gothic architectural style using imported Belgian brick and mortar. It features three spires, with the tallest spire reaching 24.3 meters (80 ft). The cathedral measures 40 meters (130 ft) in length and 23 meters (75 ft) in width.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Mary Cathedral Basilica is the mother church of all Catholic dioceses in Texas and holds significant historical and cultural importance as the first Catholic cathedral in the state. It is a symbol of the early Catholic presence and growth in Texas.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral basilica sustained significant water damage during Hurricane Ike in 2008 and was closed for repairs until Easter 2014. Restoration efforts included roof replacement, pew rebuilding, and exterior masonry repairs. The cathedral continues to serve as a central place of worship for the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston.

world knowledge.Name: Sankt Peter-Ording
world knowledge.Location: Eiderstedt peninsula, North Sea coast, approx. 45 km southwest of Husum
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Beach approximately 12 kilometers long and up to one kilometre wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Ulstrup, the village was first documented in 1373. The name changed due to land loss to the North Sea. Viking settlements have been evidenced. The area faced challenges like wandering dunes and flooding, leading to the abandonment of churches and the planting of permanent vegetation in 1860. The community merged into St. Peter-Ording in 1967 and became part of North Friesland in 1970. The first hotel was built in 1877, and the first sanatorium in 1913. A strong iodine spring was found in 1953, leading to recognition as a North Sea spa and sulphur spring in 1958.

Major_Events.Description: Marked the beginning of St. Peter-Ording's importance as a beach resort.
Enhanced the area's reputation as a health resort.
Led to the construction of more curative facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as North Sea spa and sulphur spring
Major_Events.Description: Official recognition of the area's therapeutic qualities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Characteristic stilt houses on the beach, the first of which was built in 1911 and called 'Giftbude'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Peter-Ording is the only German seaside resort with a sulphur spring and is known for its therapeutic sea air and water. It has been used in several film and television productions, highlighting its cultural relevance.
world knowledge.Details: The municipality comprises five communities: Brösum and Norderdeich, Ording and Westmarken, Bad, Dorf and Wittendün, Süderhöft/Böhl. The area is part of the Schleswig-Holstein Wadden Sea National Park and features unique ecological aspects like salt meadows with natural ponds and puddles, supporting amphibians. The climate is maritime with mild winters and cool summers. The beach is popular for sail-racing due to its flat and smooth surface. Transportation improvements include the Husum–Bad St. Peter-Ording railway extension in 1932 and the construction of the Eidersperrwerk sea barrier.

world knowledge.Name: University of Havana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Havana (UH; Spanish: Universidad de La Habana) is a public university located in the Vedado district of Havana, the capital of Cuba. Founded on 5 January 1728, the university is the oldest in Cuba, and one of the first to be founded in the Americas. Originally a religious institution, today the university has 15 faculties (colleges) at its Havana campus and distance learning centers throughout Cuba. In 1842, the university changed its status to become a secular, royal and literary institution. Its name became Real y Literaria Universidad de La Habana (Royal and Literary University of Havana) and later, when Cuba was a free republic, the name was changed to Universidad Nacional (National University). The university had first been established in San Juan de Letrán (located in Villa de San Cristóbal in Old Havana) before it was transferred on 1 May 1902, to a hill in the Vedado area of Havana.

Major_Events.Description: The university changed its status to become a secular, royal and literary institution.
The university was transferred to a hill in the Vedado area of Havana.
After the government was taken over by Fulgencio Batista in 1952, the university became a center of anti-government protests. Batista closed the university in 1956.
The Castro administration re-opened the university in 1959.
Rutgers University–Camden and the University of Havana signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to formalize research and exchange opportunities for students and faculty.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The interiors of the building were decorated by Armando Menocal y Menocal. The seven frescos represent Medicine, Science, Art, Thought, Liberal Arts, Literature, and Law. At the main university entrance there is a bronze statue of Alma Mater created in 1919 by artist Mario Korbel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Havana is the oldest university in Cuba and one of the first to be founded in the Americas. It has played a significant role in the political and social history of Cuba, particularly during the Cuban Revolution.
world knowledge.Details: The university is made up of 16 faculties and 14 research centers in a variety of fields, including economics, sciences, social science and humanities. In total, up to 25 specialties are taught at the university. Now, it has about 60,000 degree students in regular classes.

world knowledge.Name: Green Zone
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Green Zone, also known as the International Zone of Baghdad, became prominent in 2003. It is a heavily fortified area that served as the headquarters of successive Iraqi regimes, including the Ba'ath Party. The area was originally home to military bases, government ministries, and presidential palaces inhabited by Saddam Hussein and his family. It was taken by US military forces in April 2003 and became the administrative center for the Coalition Provisional Authority until June 2004. The area has since been the seat of the Iraqi government and houses several embassies, including the largest U.S. embassy in the world.

Major_Events.Description: The Green Zone was taken by US military forces in April 2003 during the capture of Baghdad.
The Green Zone was hit by two suicide bombings in October 2004, which destroyed the bazaar and the Green Zone Cafe.
A bomb went off in the Iraqi Parliament cafeteria on April 12, 2007, killing Mohammed Awad and injuring 22 others.
Full control of the Green Zone was handed over to Iraqi security forces on January 1, 2009.
Following the assassination of Qasem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi Al-Muhandis, two Katyusha rockets struck within the Green Zone on January 8, 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Green Zone is surrounded by high concrete blast walls, T-Walls, and barbed wire fences. It includes former military bases, government ministries, and presidential palaces, with the largest being the Republican Palace.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Green Zone is culturally and historically significant as it has been the seat of successive Iraqi regimes, including the Ba'ath Party, and later the Coalition Provisional Authority. It represents a key area in the political and military history of Iraq, particularly during and after the US-led invasion in 2003.
world knowledge.Details: The Green Zone was frequently shelled by insurgents with mortars and rockets, though these attacks caused few casualties. It was opened to the public with certain restrictions on October 4, 2015, and parts of it were opened without restrictions on December 10, 2018. The area remains a symbol of the political and military changes in Iraq over the past two decades.

world knowledge.Name: Antikenmuseum Basel und Sammlung Ludwig
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Antikenmuseum Basel und Sammlung Ludwig (Basel Museum of Ancient Art and Ludwig Collection) is one of the many museums in the city of Basel, Switzerland and a heritage site of national significance. In 1961 the city of Basel decided to establish the museum to assemble the several antiquities in one place. It is located in several neighboring buildings, most prominently two designed by Melchior Berri in the early 19th century. One was designed for Johann Jakob Bachofen-Merian, the father to Johann Jakob Bachofen and the other for the Swiss merchant Isaac Iselin-Roulet. During several years the buildings were renovated and the museum was inaugurated in 1966. Initially the museum included only one of the two Berri buildings, the one constructed for Roulet, the other one being used by the cities Civil Register. In 1986 the also the building built for the Bachofen family, became a part of the museum. Having opened with about 650 m2 of exhibition room, until 1992 it has expanded to 3000 m2.

Major_Events.Description: The city of Basel decided to establish the museum to assemble the several antiquities in one place.
The museum was inaugurated after several years of renovation.
The building built for the Bachofen family became a part of the museum.
The museum expanded to 3000 m2 of exhibition room.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is located in several neighboring buildings, most prominently two designed by Melchior Berri in the early 19th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is devoted exclusively to the art of ancient civilizations from the 4th millennium BC to the 7th century AD. It is the only one of its kind in Switzerland, showing works of art from the Mediterranean region, predominantly from the period from 1000 BC to 300 AD. A central position is occupied by the collection of Greek vases and sculptures and the Ancient Egyptian section. Further objects are from the Near East and Cyprus.
world knowledge.Details: The museum shows works of art from the Mediterranean region, predominantly from the period from 1000 BC to 300 AD. A central position is occupied by the collection of Greek vases and sculptures and the Ancient Egyptian section. Further objects are from the Near East and Cyprus.

world knowledge.Name: West Wycombe Park
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of West Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: West Wycombe Park is a country house built between 1740 and 1800 near the village of West Wycombe in Buckinghamshire, England. It was conceived as a pleasure palace for the 18th-century libertine and dilettante Sir Francis Dashwood, 2nd Baronet. The house encapsulates the entire progression of British 18th-century architecture from early idiosyncratic Palladian to the Neoclassical. The mansion is set within an 18th-century landscaped park containing many small temples and follies. The house was given to the National Trust in 1943 by Sir John Dashwood, 10th Baronet, and remains the home of the Dashwood family.

Major_Events.Description: Sir John Dashwood, 10th Baronet, gave the house and grounds to the National Trust, on condition that he and his descendants could continue living in the house.
The house served as a depository for the evacuated Wallace Collection and as a convalescent home. The park was used for the inflation of barrage balloons.
Sir Francis Dashwood, 11th Baronet, embarked on a program of restoration and improvement, including the installation of a large equestrian sculpture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: West Wycombe Park is a country house with four façades that are columned and pedimented, three theatrically so. The house encapsulates the entire progression of British 18th-century architecture from early idiosyncratic Palladian to the Neoclassical. The mansion contains a series of 18th-century salons decorated and furnished in the style of that period, with polychrome marble floors and painted ceilings depicting classical scenes of Greek and Roman mythology. The gardens are among the finest and most idiosyncratic 18th-century gardens surviving in England, featuring many small temples and follies.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: West Wycombe Park is architecturally important as it encapsulates a period of 18th-century English social history, when young men returning from the Grand Tour with newly purchased acquisitions of art often built a country house to accommodate their collections and display in stone the learning and culture they had acquired on their travels. The house and gardens are listed as Grade I, reflecting their historical and architectural significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a pleasure palace, the house now serves as a family home, a venue for public visits, civil weddings, corporate entertainment, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The house is open to the public during the summer months and is a venue for civil weddings and corporate entertainment. The park is often the setting for large public concerts and firework displays. The estate remains in private hands, while the National Trust owns the house and gardens, the park, the village of West Wycombe, and the hill on which the Dashwood mausoleum sits.

world knowledge.Name: Naha Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Naha Airport, originally known as Oroku Aerodrome, was opened in 1933 as an Imperial Japanese Navy airfield. After World War II, it was taken over by the United States and renamed Naha Airport. It was returned to Japan in 1972 and has since undergone significant expansions and developments, including the addition of a second runway and new terminals.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was initially opened as an Imperial Japanese Navy airfield.
The airport was taken over by the United States after World War II and renamed Naha Airport.
Okinawa was returned to Japan, and the airport was transferred from US military control to the Japan Air Self-Defense Force.
A new international terminal was opened, followed by further expansions in 2016 and 2019.
A second parallel runway began operation on March 26, 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two runways with asphalt concrete surfaces. The domestic and international terminals are connected by a new building, and the airport has undergone significant expansions, including the addition of a low-cost carrier terminal and a six-lane under bay tunnel for auto transport.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Naha Airport is the primary air terminal for passengers and cargo traveling to and from Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. It is a vital hub for regional and international travel, connecting Okinawa with other parts of Japan and several Asian countries. The airport's significant improvement in global rankings highlights its growing importance and efficiency.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public and military airport serving as a hub for domestic and international travel, cargo transport, and military operations.
world knowledge.Details: Naha Airport is Japan's sixth busiest airport and handles scheduled international traffic to Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, and mainland China. It is a 24-hour airport and serves as a hub for Japan Transocean Air and Ryukyu Air Commuter. The airport has been ranked 91st in Skytrax’s World Top Airports 100 in 2024, showing significant improvement from its previous ranking. The airport is served by the Okinawa Urban Monorail (Yui Rail) and bus services to various parts of Okinawa Island.

world knowledge.Name: University of Kentucky
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded as the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Kentucky in 1865, the university evolved into a public land-grant research institution. It played a pivotal role in Kentucky's educational history, including racial integration milestones and expansion into a major research university.

Major_Events.Event: Founding as Agricultural and Mechanical College
Major_Events.Description: Established under the Morrill Land-Grant Act.
Began admitting female students.
Graduate programs racially integrated after a legal victory by Lyman T. Johnson.
Followed the Brown v. Board of Education decision.
Kentucky General Assembly mandated the university to become a Top 20 public research institution by 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mix of historic (e.g., Main Building, 1882) and modern structures (e.g., William T. Young Library). Campus features collegiate Gothic and contemporary styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kentucky's flagship university with major contributions to education, research, and athletics. A symbol of progress in racial integration and regional development.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public land-grant research university offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs.

Details.Athletics: NCAA Division I Wildcats (SEC), 8 men's basketball national championships, 24 cheerleading titles.
Details.Libraries: 7 libraries, including the William T. Young Library (largest public university book endowment in the U.S.).
Notable_Alumni: Thomas Hunt Morgan (Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine)

Controversies.Description: Criticism over racial disparities in fraternity/sorority systems.
Allegations of sexual misconduct in the swim program under former coach Lars Jorgensen.

world knowledge.Name: Gateway Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Gateway Stadium, it was renamed in 2011 after Otunba Dipo Dina, an assassinated political candidate. The stadium was renovated for the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was renovated to host matches for this international football tournament.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named in honor of Otunba Dipo Dina, reflecting its importance in local history and politics. It serves as a key sports venue in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium, primarily for football matches; home ground for FC Ebedei.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 20,000 people. This article about a Nigerian sports venue is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Saint John City Hall (New Brunswick)
world knowledge.Address: 15 Market Square, Saint John, New Brunswick E2L 1E8
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saint John City Hall is the home of the municipal government in the city of Saint John, New Brunswick. It was built in 1971 to replace the Old City Hall, which was constructed in 1878 after the Great Fire of Saint John. The first City Hall, built in 1797, was made of wood and stood near the current site.

Major_Events.Description: Led to the construction of the Old City Hall in 1878.
A fire started by a prisoner on the ground floor (used as a city jail) killed 21 men trapped in confinement.
Renovations were made to the City Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features 16 stories (originally 17) and includes three aluminum columns painted red, orange, and yellow at the exterior entrance, designed by Claude Roussel. The third floor has indoor connections to various nearby buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Saint John City Hall is a central hub for municipal governance and public services, symbolizing the city's resilience and growth after the Great Fire of 1877. Its unique architectural elements and historical events make it a notable landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government offices, meeting place for the Saint John City Council, and office of the Mayor of Saint John.
world knowledge.Details: The building was constructed by Toronto-based Corporation Eighteen Ltd. at a cost of $6 million (equivalent to $45.1 million in 2023). In 2018, the tower building was bought by Historica Developments CEO Keith Brideau, Alex Elias, and Dr. David Elias for $3 million. The third floor connects to the Saint John City Market, Market Square, the Saint John Free Public Library, and Brunswick Square.

world knowledge.Name: St Mary's Cathedral, Perth
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St Mary's Cathedral, officially the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Perth. It was constructed in three main phases, with the first phase completed in 1865. The cathedral was initially built due to the colony outgrowing its first Roman Catholic church, St John's Pro-Cathedral. The cathedral's construction faced delays due to funding and labor shortages. The second phase in the 1920s aimed to expand the cathedral but was interrupted by the Great Depression. The third phase completed the expansion in 2009, adding modern features while preserving historical elements.

Major_Events.Description: Bishop Rosendo Salvado laid the foundation stone of the cathedral.
The first stage of the cathedral was blessed and opened.
The redesigned sanctuary with a central altar and lectern was consecrated.
The cathedral was officially opened after the completion of the third phase of construction, which included a new spire, underground parish center, and improved accessibility.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features Academic Gothic style with Norman Gothic influences. It was constructed in three stages: Stage 1 (1863–1910) in Norman Gothic, Stage 2 (1926–1973) in Academic Gothic, and Stage 3 (2006–2009) with a modern curved design. Materials include clay bricks from Adelaide Terrace and marble from the Monastery of Saint Paul Outside the Walls. The cathedral has two spires, stained glass windows by John Hardman, and mosaic floors inspired by the Book of Kells.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St Mary's Cathedral is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Perth and a significant religious and historical landmark in Western Australia. It reflects the growth of the Catholic community in Perth and showcases a blend of Gothic architectural styles across different construction phases. The cathedral also houses the remains of Perth's first bishops, adding to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Religious worship and as the seat of the Archbishop of Perth.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral underwent significant restoration and expansion in the early 21st century due to structural issues. The project included replacing columns, reconfiguring walls, and adding a steel roof structure. The new design won multiple architectural awards. The cathedral also features a boys' choir, established in 1938, which is the oldest Catholic boys' choir in Australia.

world knowledge.Name: Komodo International Airport
world knowledge.Area: Labuan Bajo, Flores Island, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Komodo International Airport, formerly known as Mutiara II Airport, serves as a departure point for tours to Komodo National Park. It was granted international airport status on 2 April 2024. A new modern terminal was inaugurated on 27 December 2015, increasing passenger capacity from 150,000 to 1.5 million per year. The airport has undergone significant expansions to accommodate larger aircraft and increase passenger capacity.

Major_Events.Description: The first Boeing 737-800 successfully landed and took off at Komodo International Airport.
President Joko Widodo inaugurated a new modern terminal, increasing passenger capacity to 1.5 million per year.
The Ministry of Transportation granted international airport status to Komodo International Airport.
An Aviastar aircraft hit a group of cows upon landing, slightly damaging the aircraft.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway designated 17/35 with an asphalt surface measuring 1,650 by 30 meters. The runway has been extended to 2,250 meters to accommodate medium-class jet aircraft. The apron area is expanded to 20,200 square meters, with a domestic terminal of 6,500 square meters and an international terminal of 5,538 square meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is crucial for tourism in the region, serving as a gateway to Komodo National Park and facilitating increased tourist arrivals to Flores Island and its surroundings.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving domestic and international flights.
