world knowledge.Details: The airport is operated by a consortium of PT Cardig Aero Service and Changi Airports International under a 25-year public-private partnership. It is expected to accommodate up to 4 million passengers annually. The runway will be further extended to 2,750 meters, and the airport aims to operate 24 hours a day in the future.

world knowledge.Name: Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1544 (original), 1947 (reopened as Kaliningrad State Pedagogical Institute), 2005 (renamed to Immanuel Kant Russian State University), 2010–2011 (renamed to Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University (IKBFU) is a public university located in Kaliningrad, Russia. It claims to maintain the traditions of the University of Königsberg (Albertina), founded in 1544. After World War II, Königsberg was transferred to the Soviet Union and renamed Kaliningrad. The Albertina was closed, and the German population was expelled. In 1947, the university reopened as the Kaliningrad State Pedagogical Institute. It became Kaliningrad State University in 1967 and was renamed Immanuel Kant Russian State University in 2005. In 2010–2011, it was renamed Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University.

Major_Events.Description: The campus was severely damaged by British aerial bombing during World War II.

Major_Events.Event: Capture of Königsberg by the Red Army
Major_Events.Description: The Albertina was closed after Königsberg was captured by the Red Army.

Major_Events.Event: Reopening as Kaliningrad State Pedagogical Institute
Major_Events.Description: The university reopened under new leadership as the Kaliningrad State Pedagogical Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Immanuel Kant Russian State University
Major_Events.Description: During the celebrations of the 750th anniversary of the founding of Königsberg, President Vladimir Putin and Chancellor Gerhard Schröder announced the renaming of the university to Immanuel Kant Russian State University.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University
Major_Events.Description: The university underwent an enlargement and rebranding process, leading to its renaming as Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: IKBFU is culturally significant as it maintains the traditions of the University of Königsberg (Albertina), which was East Prussia's sole university and was known for its mathematics and astronomy. It is also notable for being the alma mater of Immanuel Kant, one of the most outstanding European philosophers.
world knowledge.Details: As of 2005, the university consisted of twelve faculties with courses ranging from Natural Sciences to the Humanities. It had approximately 12,800 students and 580 faculty staff. The university's Kant Society studies Kantian philosophy. In 2020, it was ranked #1,000+ in the Times Higher Education World University Ranking, and in 2022, it was ranked #2,350 in the Webometrics Ranking Web of Universities. A science park was established in 2008 to concentrate research potential. The university is among the top ten higher educational institutions in Russia for international cooperation.

world knowledge.Name: Milton Abbey School
world knowledge.Address: Milton Abbas, near Blandford Forum, Dorset
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Milton Abbey School was founded in 1954 as a co-educational private school. The site has a rich history, originally home to a Benedictine monastery founded in 964 by King Edgar. The abbey church dates back to the 10th century, with significant rebuilding after a fire in 1309. The Damer family acquired the property in 1752, demolishing parts of the abbey to build a new house and landscaped estate. The Hambro family later owned the property from 1852 until 1932, when it was sold and eventually became the school.

Major_Events.Description: King Edgar replaced the existing secular college with a Benedictine monastery.

Major_Events.Event: Fire and rebuilding of the abbey church
Major_Events.Description: The medieval church burned down and was rebuilt over the next century.
The abbey was dissolved, and the property came into the possession of the Tregonwell family.
The Damer family acquired the property and made significant alterations, including demolishing parts of the abbey and creating a landscaped estate.
The school was founded as a co-educational private institution.
The school was named BTEC School of the Year by Pearson.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The abbey church is built in a mixture of Ham stone, Chilmark stone, and flint, featuring decorated Gothic style from the mid-14th century with 15th-century details. The interior includes a Tree of Jesse window by Augustus Pugin, a 14th-century pulpitum and sedilia, a 15th-century reredos and pyx canopy, and a 16th-century monument to John Tregonwell. The main house was designed by William Chambers, with gardens by Capability Brown.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Milton Abbey School is culturally significant due to its historical roots as a Benedictine monastery and its architectural heritage. The abbey church contains medieval artifacts and monuments, including the tomb of the Earl and Countess of Dorchester. The school itself is notable for its educational achievements, including being named BTEC School of the Year in 2019.
world knowledge.Details: The school offers GCSEs, A-levels, and BTECs, and has facilities including a golf course, a 15th-century dining hall, and grounds designed by Capability Brown. The school has been used as a filming location for TV series and films, including 'To Serve Them All My Days' and 'The Browning Version.' The school also operates a farm to promote environmental awareness and self-sufficiency.

world knowledge.Name: Target Field
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Target Field is a baseball stadium in the historic warehouse district of downtown Minneapolis. Since its opening in 2010, the stadium has been the ballpark of Major League Baseball's Minnesota Twins. It is named for Target Corporation, which is headquartered in Minneapolis. The stadium hosted the 2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted the 2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game.
The 2022 NHL Winter Classic was held at the stadium on January 1, 2022. The St. Louis Blues defeated the Minnesota Wild 6-4.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Populous with Bruce Miller as principal lead, Target Field is a modern take on other Populous-designed stadiums such as Oriole Park at Camden Yards in Baltimore, PNC Park in Pittsburgh, and Oracle Park in San Francisco. The architects tried to avoid creating a replica of the old-style brick Camden Yards or modern urban design of the new Nationals Park. Instead, the design for the stadium employs local limestone, heated viewing areas and a heated field. The stadium does not have a roof, but there is a canopy above the top deck. The stadium is integrated with the intermodal Target Field station which connects the Metro Blue and Green Line light rail service with the Minneapolis terminus of the Northstar commuter rail line leading from the northwest.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Target Field is culturally significant as the home of the Minnesota Twins and a venue for major sports and entertainment events. It has been ranked as the number one baseball stadium experience in North America by ESPN The Magazine in 2010.
world knowledge.Details: Target Field was initially awarded LEED Silver Certification by the U.S. Green Building Council, the second LEED-certified professional sports stadium in the United States, after Oracle Park. In 2017, Target Field was recertified LEED Gold, the first sports site in the nation to be so designated. The stadium features a modernized version of the original "Minnie and Paul Shaking Hands" logo used on the team's original uniforms from 1961 until 1986. When a Twins player hits a home run, the Minnie and Paul sign lights up with strobe lights surrounding the Minnesota state outline and Minnie and Paul shake hands. The original flagpole from Metropolitan Stadium – completely restored – is located on the right field plaza.

world knowledge.Name: Pha Taem National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pha Taem National Park is a national park on the Mekong River in Ubon Ratchathani Province, northeast Thailand. It is notable for its Dipterocarp forest cover and extensive rock art on cliffs above the Mekong, estimated to be 3,000 years old. The park also features mushroom rocks and the largest flower field in Thailand. It was declared a national park on 31 December 1991. The area was once considered a prohibited location, believed to be protected by the holy, and was known as the "Mountain of Death". Archaeological research revealed prehistoric paintings dating back 3,000-4,000 years. The park was designated as the 74th national park of Thailand.

Major_Events.Description: Pha Taem National Park was declared a national park on 31 December 1991.
Prehistoric paintings dating back 3,000-4,000 years were discovered in the Pha Taem area.
Specimens of a new frog species, Fejervarya triora, were discovered in the park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is covered by Dipterocarp forest with Shorea obtusa, Shorea siamensis, and Dipterocarpus obtusifollus as the dominant species. There are also dry evergreen forests near streams.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pha Taem National Park is culturally significant due to its prehistoric rock art, which is among the oldest in the region. It is also a popular destination for witnessing the first sunrise of the New Year in Thailand.
world knowledge.Details: The park is habitat for various wildlife species, including Siamese hares, barking deer, civets, wild pigs, serow, and wild elephants that migrate from Laos. It is also the site of the largest flower field in Thailand and features several natural attractions such as Pha Chan, Soi Sawan Waterfall, Sao Chaliang, Tham Patihan, and Phu Na Tham.

world knowledge.Name: Jijiga University
world knowledge.Address: Abdi Mahamud Ahmed, Jijiga, Somali Region, Ethiopia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jijiga University is a university in Jijiga, the capital of the Somali Region, Ethiopia. It was established in 2005 with 714 students and expanded to take in approximately 1,500 students in 2008 and 2,800 students in 2009. It is one of the 13 newly founded governmental universities in Ethiopia.

Major_Events.Description: Jijiga University was established with 714 students.
The university expanded to take in approximately 1,500 students.
The university further expanded to take in approximately 2,800 students.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jijiga University is one of the 13 newly founded governmental universities in Ethiopia, playing a significant role in higher education in the Somali Region.
world knowledge.Details: The Jijiga University Faculty of Law was formed in 2004 and planned to graduate its first batch of graduates in July 2009. The faculty has an academic staff of over 25 and takes about 60 students each year in a regular program and over 500 summer in-service students.

world knowledge.Name: Xiamen University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Xiamen University (XMU) was founded in 1921 by Tan Kah Kee, a Chinese patriotic expatriate businessman in Singapore. Initially named Amoy University, it has grown into one of the top academic institutions in Southern China, with strengths in various disciplines. The university has played a significant role in China's higher education system and has expanded internationally, including the establishment of a campus in Malaysia in 2015.

Major_Events.Description: Tan Kah Kee donated 4 million dollars to endow Amoy University (later Xiamen University) in Xiamen, China.
The university was temporarily relocated to Changting in western Fujian to escape Japanese invasion.
Xiamen University was designated as a key university in China.
Xiamen University was selected to participate in Project 211, a Chinese government initiative to bolster top universities.
The university was selected for Project 985, another government initiative to fund top universities.
Xiamen University Malaysia Campus was established, marking the first large-scale international branch of a Chinese university.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition in Double First Class University Plan
Major_Events.Description: Xiamen University was recognized as a Class A institution in the Double First Class University Plan.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus is located at the foothills of mountains, facing the ocean and surrounded by Xiamen Bay. It features a blend of traditional and modern architecture, with facilities for humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and engineering. The Zhangzhou Campus replicates the main campus's architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Xiamen University is a symbol of educational excellence and international collaboration in China. It has a strong global presence, attracting students from overseas Chinese communities and fostering partnerships with over 300 universities worldwide. The university's founding by Tan Kah Kee, a prominent philanthropist, adds to its historical and cultural importance.
world knowledge.Details: Xiamen University is part of Project 211, Project 985, and the Double First-Class Construction. It has a high-speed information network rated first among Chinese universities and hosts over 45,000 students. The university has 16 Confucius Institutes in 13 countries and actively engages in international exchanges and collaborations.

world knowledge.Name: Lied Library
world knowledge.Address: University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV) campus, Paradise, Nevada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lied Library is the largest building on the UNLV campus, opened on January 8, 2001. UNLV Libraries, established in 1957, includes other campus libraries and has a collection of over one million volumes, access to over 20,000 online and print journals, and over 2 million additional resources of various media.

Major_Events.Description: The Lied Library was officially opened to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 5 stories high, designed by Welles Pugsley Architects, features automated storage and retrieval systems (LASR), integrated video network system (Safari), and RFID technology for collection management.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Houses the world’s largest and most comprehensive collection of gaming materials, serving researchers, gaming history enthusiasts, and the Las Vegas gaming business community. It also preserves architectural drawings of casinos and corporate papers of iconic Las Vegas neon signs.
world knowledge.Details: The Lied Automated Storage and Retrieval (LASR) unit uses industrial automated materials handling technologies. Special Collections and Archives includes corporate archives from major gaming corporations and architectural drawings of casinos. The Media and Computer Services Department provides advanced media viewing and listening capabilities.

world knowledge.Name: National Archaeological Museum Aruba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Archaeological Museum Aruba, originally known as the Archaeological Museum of Aruba, was established in 1981. In 2009, the museum moved to a new location and was reopened as the National Archaeological Museum Aruba. Its collections cover artifacts from 2500 BCE to the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The Archaeological Museum of Aruba was opened.
The museum moved to a new location and was reopened as the National Archaeological Museum Aruba.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is significant for its extensive collection of archaeological artifacts that trace the history of Aruba from 2500 BCE to the 19th century, providing valuable insights into the island's pre-Columbian and colonial past.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's website is www.manaruba.org. This Aruba-related article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it. This article related to a museum in the Caribbean is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Kobayr monastery
world knowledge.Address: Kobayr village, near Tumanyan, Lori Province, Armenia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kobayr is a 12th-century Georgian-Armenian monastery built in 1171 by the Kyurikid princes, a junior branch of the Bagratuni royal house of Armenia. It was a significant spiritual, cultural, and literary center in Northern Armenia during the Middle Ages. In the 1270s, the monastery was acquired by the Zakarians, who converted it into a Chalcedonian monastery, placing it under the Georgian Orthodox Church for some time. The monastery houses the tomb of Prince Shanshe Zakarian and features a bell tower built in 1279. It is currently undergoing renovation with funding from the governments of Armenia and Italy.

Major_Events.Description: The Zakarians, a noble Armenian dynasty, acquired the monastery and converted it into a Chalcedonian monastery, placing it under the Georgian Orthodox Church.
A bell tower was built to house the tombs of Zakarian and his wife Vaneni.
The building was consecrated by the monk George, son of Shahnshah of the Zakarian family.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery is built in the Armenian style, featuring frescoes of Christ, the twelve apostles, and other Christian figures. The ruins of the main church contain mural paintings in a mainly Byzantine style of the 11th century CE. The bell tower and the Chapel/Aisle adjoining the Big Church are notable architectural elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kobayr monastery is culturally and historically important as a spiritual, cultural, and literary center of Northern Armenia during the Middle Ages. Its unique blend of Armenian and Georgian influences, along with its historical frescoes and inscriptions, make it a significant site for understanding the region's religious and cultural history.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery is currently undergoing renovation funded by the government of Armenia with the assistance of the government of Italy. The mural paintings and inscriptions provide valuable insights into the religious and cultural practices of the time.

image_name: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity

world knowledge.Name: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
world knowledge.Address: Tunnel Mountain in Banff National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1933 as the Banff School of Drama, it evolved into a comprehensive arts and culture educational institution. It was granted full autonomy as a non-degree granting post-secondary educational institution in 1978. Renamed to Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity in 2016.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
Major_Events.Description: The institution was renamed to reflect its focus on arts and creativity.
284 staff members were laid off via Zoom, leading to concerns about the institution's commitment to its values.
The centre launched community radio programming on existing stations CFPE-FM and CFPF-FM.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The centre includes facilities like the Leighton Artists' Studios, Walter Phillips Gallery, and a writers' lounge, supporting artists across various disciplines.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It serves as a national and international hub for arts, culture, and creativity, offering programs in performing and fine arts, leadership training, and hosting numerous conferences and festivals.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Arts, cultural, and educational institution and conference complex
world knowledge.Details: The centre offers residencies, workshops, practicum programs, and hosts the Banff Summer Arts Festival. It also operates the Banff International Research Station for Mathematical Innovation and Discovery and manages significant art and archival collections.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Kleber Andrade
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Estadual Kleber José de Andrade, also known as Estádio Kleber Andrade, is a Brazilian football stadium built in 1983 by Rio Branco AC. It was named after Kleber José de Andrade, the president of Rio Branco AC during its construction. The stadium was sold to the Espírito Santo State Government in 2008. It replaced the older Estádio Governador Bley, which had a capacity of approximately 15,000 people.

Major_Events.Description: The inaugural match was played on September 7, 1983, when Rio Branco AC beat Guarapari EC 3–2. The first goal was scored by Rio Branco's Arildo Ratão.

The stadium's attendance record was set on September 21, 1986, when Rio Branco beat Vasco da Gama 1–0 in a match for the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A, with 32,328 attendees (some claim around 50,000 were present).
The stadium was used by the Cameroon national team for training before and during the 2014 FIFA World Cup.
The stadium was one of the four venues for the 2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface, capacity of 21,152 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Espírito Santo, hosting major football matches and events, including training for a national team during the 2014 FIFA World Cup and matches in the 2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was renovated between 2010 and 2014. It is owned by the Espírito Santo State Government since 2008.

world knowledge.Name: Tredegar House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tredegar House is a 17th-century Charles II-era mansion in Coedkernew, Newport, Wales. It was home to the Morgan family, later Lords Tredegar, for over five hundred years. The house was rebuilt in red brick between 1664 and 1672 by William Morgan. It has been under the care of the National Trust since 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Charles I visited Tredegar House during the English Civil War.
Godfrey Morgan fought in and survived the Charge of the Light Brigade at Balaclava.
The National Trust took over the running of the house and grounds from Newport City Council.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Carolean architectural style, built of red brick, described as the most splendid brick house of the seventeenth century in Wales.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tredegar House is one of the outstanding houses of the Restoration period in Britain and has been home to the influential Morgan family for over five hundred years.
world knowledge.Details: Tredegar House has been used as a filming location for various TV series including Doctor Who, Being Human, and Da Vinci's Demons. It hosts annual events such as an Easter Egg Hunt, Pirate's Day, and a Folk Festival. The house is also approved for marriages and civil ceremonies.

world knowledge.Name: National University of Colombia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1867 by an act of the Congress of Colombia, it is one of the largest universities in the country. The University City of Bogotá, also known as the White City, is the flagship campus designed by German educationalist Fritz Karsen and architect Leopold Rother. Construction began in 1935 under the government of Alfonso López Pumarejo.

Major_Events.Description: Established by an act of the Congress of Colombia.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of the University City of Bogotá
Major_Events.Description: Construction began under the government of Alfonso López Pumarejo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus is organized into an ellipse, divided into five parts, each containing one academic division and its respective departments. The buildings were constructed as prismatic blocks and painted white to give an austere and clean look. The shape of an owl can be seen from an aerial view, emblematic of a deep connection with wisdom and intuitive knowledge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National University of Colombia is one of the most selective and competitive universities in the country, part of the Golden Triangle of higher education in Colombia. It has produced the largest number of scientific papers published in peer-refereed publications in the country and ranks highly in Latin America.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers a wide selection of programs in both undergraduate and graduate levels, including medicine, engineering, social sciences, arts, and law. It was the first university in Colombia to open a computer science postgraduate program in 1967. The University City of Bogotá has 17 buildings declared national monuments and is a representation of the last 60 years of architecture in Colombia.

image_name: Nuestra Señora de Candelaria Parish Church (Mabitac)

world knowledge.Name: Nuestra Señora de Candelaria Parish Church (Mabitac)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Nuestra Señora de Candelaria Parish Church, informally known as Mabitac Church, is a Roman Catholic church located above Calvary or Kalbaryo Hill in Mabitac, Laguna, Philippines. It is under the jurisdiction of the Diocese of San Pablo. The church was originally built in 1618 and has undergone several reconstructions due to natural calamities and war. It is known for its 126 steps connecting the local road to the main church on top of the hill.

Major_Events.Description: The church was seriously damaged during the 1880 earthquake and repaired under the supervision of Father Antonio de la Fuente.
The church was severely damaged during the 1937 earthquake and was greatly improved into its interior since then.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church has a Spanish style façade and is made of Adobe stones. The belfry connected to the church is the remaining original structure of the original 1618 church.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is culturally significant due to its historical background, architectural style, and the festivity of the Three Kings every January 6, a re-enactment of the Magi's journey.
world knowledge.Details: The church is known for having a staircase of 126 steps, a panoramic view of the town of Sta. Maria and Laguna lake. The image of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria was commissioned between 1599 and 1600 by the alferez, Don Cristobal Mercado for Paco Church.

world knowledge.Name: Oslo Beach
world knowledge.Address: Alesund Road, Oslo Beach, Port Shepstone, 4240, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oslo Beach is a small coastal suburb that forms part of the coastal town of Port Shepstone. It is located along the South Coast of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Oslo Beach is a residential area with cultural diversity, as reflected in its population demographics and language distribution.

Emergency Services.Fire Station: Oslo Beach Fire Station, Alesund Road

Details.Retail: No retail facilities; nearest malls are in Port Shepstone CBD or Shelly Beach

world knowledge.Name: Lund's Tower
world knowledge.Address: South-west of Sutton-in-Craven village, North Yorkshire
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lund's Tower is a stone-built folly commissioned by James Lund in 1887. It is also known as Cowling Pinnacle, Sutton Pinnacle, the Ethel Tower, or the Jubilee Tower. The tower was built either to celebrate the birth or 21st birthday of Lund's daughter Ethel or to commemorate Queen Victoria's 1887 jubilee. James Lund was a wealthy textile manufacturer and landowner, and his estate was valued at £606,679 upon his death in 1903.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was built as a folly, possibly to celebrate the birth or 21st birthday of James Lund's daughter Ethel or to commemorate Queen Victoria's 1887 jubilee.
The tower was listed in the National Heritage List for England at Grade II in October 1984.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is 11 meters tall, constructed from squared-dressed stone with crenellated battlements. It features a plinth, an unreadable plaque, a stone-built spiral staircase of 39 steps, and a viewing platform.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lund's Tower is culturally significant as a folly with multiple local names and associations, including connections to James Lund's family and Queen Victoria's jubilee. It is also part of a pair of monuments known locally as the Salt and Pepper Pots, alongside Wainman's Pinnacle.
world knowledge.Details: Lund's Tower is also known as Cowling Pinnacle, Sutton Pinnacle, the Ethel Tower, or the Jubilee Tower. It is located near Wainman's Pinnacle, and the pair are referred to as the Salt and Pepper Pots. The tower was designed by the Keighley architectural firm of R. B. Broster & Sons.

world knowledge.Name: Armagh County Museum
world knowledge.Address: The Mall, Armagh, County Armagh, Northern Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Armagh County Museum is the oldest County Museum in Ireland, officially opened in 1937. The building was originally established as Charlemont Place National School and later used by the Armagh Natural History and Philosophical Society. It was rejuvenated by Armagh County Council in the 1930s and has since expanded its collections and facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened by James Caulfeild, 8th Viscount Charlemont, who was the Minister of Education for Northern Ireland at the time.
The museum underwent a major refurbishment, including the demolition of old buildings and the construction of a new red-brick extension.
The museum was transferred to the Ulster Museum due to the reorganisation of Northern Ireland's local government.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in National Museums Northern Ireland
Major_Events.Description: The museum became part of National Museums Northern Ireland following the Museums and Galleries (Northern Ireland) Order 1997.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum features a neoclassical facade with a red-brick extension built in the 1960s. The original building was designed by William Murray, a pupil of Francis Johnston.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses a vast collection of artefacts, including archaeological finds, art, costumes, and historical documents, representing the rich heritage of County Armagh and Northern Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include archaeology, art, costume, taxidermy, and a library. It has a significant art collection featuring works by local and Northern Irish artists. The museum also has a transport section with railway memorabilia and a collection of megalithic artefacts from South Armagh.

world knowledge.Name: Regent on Broadway
world knowledge.Address: Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Regent on Broadway is a large theatre in Palmerston North, New Zealand, originally designed in 1929 by Charles Hollinshed of Sydney. It was officially opened to the public on 4 July 1930. Initially used as a cinema and opera house, it closed in 1991 due to the decline of the movie industry. The Palmerston North City Council acquired the building in 1992 and restored it with significant community and government funding in the 1990s.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was officially opened to the public on 4 July 1930.
The Palmerston North City Council acquired the building in 1992 by swapping it with the previous owner for the Opera House.
The theatre was fully restored and renovated, with the project completed in May 1998.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The auditorium features painted panels on the roof, a carpeted staircase with marble sides, and a lobby with a special weave carpet manufactured by Feltex. The mezzanine floor has carved kowhaiwhai panels in the ceiling.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Regent on Broadway is listed as a Category 1 Historic Place by Heritage New Zealand and is considered one of the top four performing arts centres in the country. It remains the only large theatre in the greater Palmerston North area.
world knowledge.Details: The auditorium can seat 1393 people, with 721 on the ground floor and 672 in the circle. Some downstairs seating can be removed for functions. The venue includes several dressing rooms, a large function room, and a rehearsal studio used for various activities. It is one of New Zealand's busiest venues due to its wide range of activities.

world knowledge.Name: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary opened in 1981. The name 'Bonorong' is derived from an Australian Aboriginal language meaning 'native companion', though the origin of the nation is unknown.

Major_Events.Description: Bonorong Wildlife Rescue became Tasmania's first veterinary hospital dedicated to wildlife.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dedicated to the rescue, rehabilitation, and preservation of native Australian animals, Bonorong actively participates in various conservation projects, contributes to breeding programs, research initiatives, and advocacy for the protection of Tasmania's wildlife.

Details.Species: Eastern grey kangaroos, Tasmanian devils, wombats, sugar gliders, eastern quolls, sulphur-crested cockatoos, yellow-tailed black cockatoos, tawny frogmouths, echidnas, eastern bettongs
Details.Charity: Friends of Bonorong is a registered charity associated with the sanctuary, providing funding for urgent assistance to wildlife in crisis and supporting long-term conservation.
Details.Transport: Accessible via Briggs Road, Brighton with car parking on site. A private bus service called the Bonorong Shuttle departs from the Hobart CBD twice daily.

image_name: Estádio Doutor Jorge Ismael de Biasi

world knowledge.Name: Estádio Doutor Jorge Ismael de Biasi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was inaugurated on 22 March 1987 in a match between Novorizontino and Internacional de Limeira. It was named after Jorge Ismael de Biasi, who built the stadium with his own resources. In March 2020, the club inaugurated a new facade and honored Dr. de Biasi with a statue.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated with a match between Novorizontino and Internacional de Limeira.
The club inaugurated a new facade and honored Dr. de Biasi with a statue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-use stadium with natural grass surface, capacity of 14,096 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant as a sports venue in Brazil and is named after its builder, Jorge Ismael de Biasi, who constructed it with his own resources.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is sometimes known as Jorjão. It was renovated between 2015 and 2016. This article about a sports venue in Brazil is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Appanoose County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The first structure used for court purposes in Appanoose County was also used as a storeroom and a blacksmith's shop. The first true courthouse was a 24-by-20-foot structure built in 1848 for $160 in Centerville. After the county outgrew this building, court sessions were held in the Methodist and Presbyterian churches while another courthouse was built. It was a two-story, brick building built for $23,000. In 1891 it was declared unsafe and condemned. The present courthouse was built in 1903 and dedicated on September 12, 1904.

Major_Events.Event: Placed on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1981.

Major_Events.Event: Included in Courthouse Square Historic District
Major_Events.Description: In 1997 it was included as a contributing property in the Courthouse Square Historic District.
The courthouse was dedicated on September 12, 1904.
The courthouse was rededicated in a festive ceremony on September 12, 2004.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The two-story rusticated limestone structure is built on a high foundation. Its eclectic appearance combines large polygonal bays and rock-faced stone from the medieval revivals with classical details found in the pediments and the pilastered main entrance. A large round arch window is located over the main entrance, and the building is capped with a two-stage central clock tower. Architectural style: Late 19th and 20th Century Revivals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Appanoose County Courthouse is culturally and historically important as it represents the architectural and judicial history of the county. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is a contributing property to the Courthouse Square Historic District.
world knowledge.Details: The architects for the present courthouse was the Des Moines architectural firm of Wetherell and Gage. The contract, exclusive of heating and plumbing, was awarded to William Peatman, the amount of his bid being $69,900. The cornerstone was laid on May 21, 1903. NRHP reference No.: 81000225.

world knowledge.Name: Seymour Centre
world knowledge.Address: City Road and Cleveland Street, Chippendale Sydney, New South Wales Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Seymour Centre was constructed in 1975 following a bequest from Sydney businessman Everest York Seymour, who left funds for a building dedicated to the cultivation, education, and performance of musical and dramatic arts. The University of Sydney became the trustee of this bequest and commissioned the architectural firm Allen Jack+Cottier to design the performing arts centre.

Major_Events.Description: Internal refurbishments were carried out by Lahz Nimmo Architects.

The University of Sydney was awarded an A$40 million grant from the Australian Government's Restart Investment to Sustain and Expand (RISE) Fund, enabling 178 performances to 19,000+ audiences over 16 months.
The Wiggles performed at the Seymour Centre during their December 1996 concerts, featured in their first concert video, Wiggledance!.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Allen Jack+Cottier, the Seymour Centre features multiple performance spaces including The York Theatre (780 seats, thrust stage), The Everest Theatre (605 seats, end-stage with acoustic features), and The Reginald Theatre (200 seats, studio-style). The building also includes refreshment areas and a cabaret-style venue.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Seymour Centre serves as a hub for performing arts in Sydney, hosting a wide range of productions, festivals, and educational programs. It is a key venue for the University of Sydney's Department of Music and plays a significant role in Sydney's cultural and artistic community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts centre hosting theatre, music, dance, and spoken-word events, as well as educational programs and festivals.
world knowledge.Details: The Seymour Centre presents annual events such as the Seymour Sessions (a music series featuring emerging artists), the University of Sydney Revues, and hosts festivals like the Sydney Festival, Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras, Sydney Children's Festival, Sydney Fringe Festival, and Sydney Comedy Festival. Refreshments are available on each level, including a coffee cart and BBQ in the courtyard.

world knowledge.Name: Dollywood
world knowledge.Address: 2700 Dollywood Parks Blvd, Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, 37863-4102, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dollywood is a theme park jointly owned by Herschend Family Entertainment and Dolly Parton. Originally opened in 1961 as Rebel Railroad, it underwent several name changes and thematic shifts before becoming Dollywood in 1986. The park celebrates the life and music of Dolly Parton, Appalachian culture, and the history of East Tennessee.

Major_Events.Description: The park opened as Rebel Railroad, featuring a steam train, general store, blacksmith shop, and saloon with a Civil War theme.
The park was renamed and switched to a wild west theme similar to its sister park Tweetsie Railroad.
The Herschends renamed the park to Silver Dollar City Tennessee, aligning it with their original park in Branson, Missouri.
Dolly Parton became a co-owner, and the park was renamed Dollywood, reflecting her influence and vision.
Dollywood received the prestigious Liseberg Applause Award, recognized as the best theme park in the world.
A new 5-acre area, Wildwood Grove, opened as part of a $300 million expansion, featuring family-friendly attractions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Dollywood features a mix of traditional Appalachian crafts, music, and architecture, with themed areas reflecting historical eras and cultural elements of East Tennessee. The park includes replicas of historical buildings, such as Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, and modern thrill rides with thematic elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dollywood is a celebration of Appalachian culture, Dolly Parton's life and music, and the history of East Tennessee. It serves as a major tourist attraction, bringing jobs and economic growth to the region while preserving and promoting local traditions.
Notable_Visitors: Various national and local musical acts
world knowledge.Details: Dollywood hosts six major festivals annually, including the Smoky Mountain Christmas Festival. It has won numerous awards for its food, shows, and guest experience. The park is part of a larger entertainment complex that includes Dollywood's Splash Country, Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa, and Dolly Parton's Stampede Dinner Attraction.

world knowledge.Name: Robertson County Courthouse and Jail
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Robertson County Courthouse and Jail in Franklin, Texas, serves as the county courthouse for Robertson County. The jail was constructed in 1879 and the courthouse was completed in 1880. It was designed by Frederick Ernst Ruffini and built in the Second Empire style. Its signature mansard roof was removed in 1924 but was restored in the 2010s. It was listed as a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1968 and on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977.

Major_Events.Description: The jail was constructed by James P. Smith in 1879 for a cost of $11,485.
Construction on the courthouse was approved in 1881 and completed in 1882 at a total cost of $30,000.
Remodeling works were carried out by Hix McCanless. The original mansard roof was removed in favor of modernizing the building with a flat, Mission-type facade.

As part of a $500,000 plan to repair and restore several features, the interior was completely gutted and windows were repaned. The roof was also renovated and lowered. Another annex building was added for more office space.

Major remodels were completed, which reintroduced several original features that had been lost over the decades. The Mission-style parapet and awnings were removed entirely, and the roof as initially installed in 1882 was rebuilt. Modern steel windows were replaced with wooden frames. Inside, two original wooden staircases were reconstructed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse's rectangular footprint measures 81 ft 11 in (25.0 m) by 66 ft 5 in (20.2 m). Its exterior walls are made of Austin limestone. It was originally constructed in the Second Empire style. The roof—which was demolished in 1924 but restored in 2014—features corner pavilions and a central tower topped by mansard roofs inset with galvanized iron dormers. Clocks are set into the top of the tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Robertson County Courthouse and Jail is culturally and historically significant as it serves as the county courthouse for Robertson County and has been listed as a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1968 and on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse was designed by Frederick Ernst Ruffini. After Robertson County's organization in 1838, the county seat moved several times. Planning for the new courthouse-jail complex in Franklin began after the 1879 general election concluded the county seat would move there from Calvert. As planned by Austin architect Frederick Ernst Ruffini, the site was to be on the main public square.

world knowledge.Name: Zazerkalie (theatre)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The building was occupied by the Petersburg Actor's Club in the 1870s. The theatre was established in August 1987 by director A.V. Petrov and conductor P.A. Bubelnikov. It opened on 27 December 1987 with the opera "Bravo-Bravissimo, pioneer Anisimov or no one wants to sing" by L.A. Desyatnikov. The theatre was named after Lewis Carroll's "Through the Looking-Glass". The building is an architectural monument and is included in the Unified State Register of Cultural Heritage Sites of the Russian Federation.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was established by director A.V. Petrov and conductor P.A. Bubelnikov.
The theatre opened with the opera "Bravo-Bravissimo, pioneer Anisimov or no one wants to sing" by L.A. Desyatnikov.
"Zazerkalie" established the children's theatre, teaching acting skills, choreography, and scenic speech, as well as setting up children theatre performances.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is the former apartment building and the assembly hall of M. F. Ruadze, later the house of A. I. Pavlova. It is an architectural monument.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is culturally significant as it is a children's musical theatre that also caters to adult audiences. It has been awarded prizes like "Gold mask" and "Gold soffit" for its performances. The building is also a cultural heritage site of regional significance.
world knowledge.Details: The majority of productions draw on the repertoire of both children and adult audiences. Performances like "Love potion", "Kashtanka", "La Boheme" have been awarded "Gold mask" and "Gold soffit" prizes.

world knowledge.Name: Theatre of Nations
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1885 as the Korsh Theatre, one of the first privately-owned Russian theatres. After the Russian Revolution, it underwent several name and management changes. In 1987, it became the Theatre of Peoples' Friendship, later renamed the Theatre of Nations in 1991. The building underwent extensive renovations from 2007 to 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre reopened after extensive renovations, with reduced seating, a new small second stage, updated technical facilities, and added rehearsal rooms.
A collaboration with Latvian director Alvis Hermanis, adapting Vasily Shukshin's short stories for stage. The play has won several awards and continues to tour globally.
A play focusing on the relationship of Mikhail Gorbachev and his wife Raisa Gorbacheva, starring Yevgeniy Mironov and Chulpan Khamatova.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Mikhail Chichagov, the building originally featured modern technology like electric lighting. The 2012 renovation included state-of-the-art lighting, video, sound, and stage mechanics.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Theatre of Nations showcases international and experimental theatre, preserves cultural ties within the former Soviet Union, and promotes contemporary drama. It hosts significant festivals and has staged productions by renowned directors.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre and cultural center, hosting national and multinational arts festivals, experimental works, and international productions.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has no resident acting company but is led by Artistic Director Yevgeny Mironov. It focuses on contemporary drama and reinterpreted classics. Notable productions include 'Caligula,' 'Ivanov,' and 'The Seagull.' The theatre also hosts festivals like TERRITORIЯ, Opera Parade, and Mini-Avignon.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Kilimanjaro
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in Tanzania, the highest mountain in Africa, and the highest free-standing mountain above sea level in the world. It has been a significant cultural and geographical landmark for centuries, with its first recorded ascent by Hans Meyer and Ludwig Purtscheller in 1889. The mountain was incorporated into Kilimanjaro National Park in 1973 and is one of the Seven Summits, making it a major hiking and climbing destination.

Major_Events.Description: Hans Meyer and Ludwig Purtscheller became the first recorded climbers to reach the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro.
Mount Kilimanjaro was incorporated into Kilimanjaro National Park to preserve its ecosystem and promote tourism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mount Kilimanjaro is a large dormant stratovolcano composed of three distinct volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira. Kibo, the highest cone, is capped by an almost symmetrical cone with escarpments rising 180 to 200 m (590 to 660 ft) on the south side. The mountain's slopes host montane forests, cloud forests, and glaciers, including the Furtwängler Glacier, which is rapidly shrinking due to climate change.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Kilimanjaro holds cultural significance for the Chagga people, who traditionally lived on its slopes. The mountain is also a symbol of national pride for Tanzania and is featured in various literary works, songs, and films, including Ernest Hemingway's 'The Snows of Kilimanjaro' and Toto's song 'Africa'.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest stratovolcano in the East African Rift and maintains a glacier on its summit. It is drained by a network of rivers and streams, especially on the wetter southern side. The mountain's ice cap is rapidly shrinking, with projections indicating it may disappear entirely by the mid-21st century. Kilimanjaro National Park generates significant revenue from tourism, with seven official trekking routes available for climbers.

world knowledge.Name: Buck Island Reef National Monument
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Buck Island Reef National Monument protects Buck Island, a small, uninhabited 176-acre island about 1.5 miles north of the northeast coast of Saint Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands, and 18,839 acres of submerged lands, totaling 19,015 acres. It was first established as a protected area by the U.S. Government in 1948, with the intention of preserving “one of the finest marine gardens in the Caribbean Sea.” The U.S. National Monument was created in 1961 by John F. Kennedy and greatly expanded in 2001 by Bill Clinton, over the opposition of local fishermen.

Major_Events.Description: The U.S. Government established Buck Island as a protected area to preserve one of the finest marine gardens in the Caribbean Sea.
Buck Island was designated as a National Monument by John F. Kennedy.
Bill Clinton greatly expanded the boundaries of Buck Island Reef National Monument, despite opposition from local fishermen.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Buck Island Reef National Monument is culturally and historically significant as it preserves one of the finest marine gardens in the Caribbean Sea. It is one of the few places in the Virgin Islands where brown pelicans and threatened least terns nest. The underwater trail is one of only three in the United States, and the area supports a diverse marine ecosystem.
world knowledge.Details: Buck Island Reef National Monument attracts around 50,000 visitors a year. The 4,554-acre reef offers opportunities for snorkeling, including a marked underwater trail with plaques providing information about marine flora and fauna. The area is home to over 250 fish species and various marine life, including endangered sea turtles that nest on the island's beaches. The National Park Service has been monitoring the island for over 40 years, focusing on coral, fish, sea turtles, and bird nesting. Visitors are required to use authorized concessioners or have a permit to protect the natural environment.

world knowledge.Name: Mill River Fun Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mill River Fun Park was conceived by private sector investors during the 1980s based on economic development funding from the federal and provincial governments. Following an economic downturn in the early 1990s, the property was acquired by the provincial government and operated by the provincial parks system, though it was not considered a provincial park. In early 2017, the provincial government sold the park, along with other nearby properties, to Don McDougall, who subsequently closed the park and removed all attractions.

Major_Events.Description: The park was permanently closed in 2017, and all remaining attractions were demolished or sold. The area now contains walking trails open to the public.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park was a recreational destination in Prince Edward Island, offering various attractions such as a swimming pool, bumper boats, pirate ship, water slides, and more. Its closure marked the end of an era for local entertainment.
world knowledge.Details: The park included attractions like a swimming pool, bumper boats, pirate ship, water slides, children's swimming pool, and aqua rage. After its closure, the area was repurposed into walking trails.

world knowledge.Name: Charleston International Airport
world knowledge.Area: North Charleston, South Carolina, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The airport was founded in 1928 by the Charleston Airport Corporation. Initially privately developed, it was later acquired by the City of Charleston for passenger service. During World War II, it was used by the military, and post-war, it reverted to civilian use. In 1952, a joint-use agreement with the U.S. Air Force was established. The current terminal was built in the 1980s, and the airport has since expanded, including the addition of a Boeing 787 Dreamliner assembly plant in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: Boeing announced in 2009 that it would build a major plant at the airport for assembling the 787 Dreamliner. Limited operations began in July 2011, and the first aircraft was completed in April 2012.
British Airways launched seasonal flights to London's Heathrow Airport, marking Charleston's first transatlantic service.
Breeze Airways announced Charleston International Airport as a focus city, with service to 11 cities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current terminal, completed in 1985, was designed by Howard Needles Tammen & Bergendoff, Davis & Floyd, Inc., and Lucas & Stubbs. It features a consolidated TSA security checkpoint and two concourses (A and B) with a total of 18 gates. The terminal underwent a $200 million redevelopment project completed in 2016, adding five gates and renovating the interior.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Charleston International Airport is South Carolina's busiest airport and serves as a key transportation hub for the region. It also plays a significant role in the local economy, hosting Boeing's 787 Dreamliner assembly plant and supporting military operations through Joint Base Charleston.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is a joint civil-military facility operated by the Charleston County Aviation Authority under a joint-use agreement with Joint Base Charleston. It serves as a focus city for Breeze Airways and features two runways: 15/33 (9,001 ft × 200 ft) and 03/21 (7,000 ft × 150 ft). The airport offers parking, rental car services, and is served by CARTA's regional mass transit system.

world knowledge.Name: Mississippi Museum of Art
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mississippi Art Association was founded in 1911. By 1978, the Mississippi Museum of Art was founded, and it was located in the Arts Center of Mississippi until 2007.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The largest museum in Mississippi, housing a permanent collection including paintings by American, Mississippi, and British painters as well as photographs, collage artworks, and sculptures.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is located at the corner of 380 South Lamar Street and 201 East Pascagoula Street in Jackson, Mississippi.

world knowledge.Name: Pittodrie Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pittodrie Stadium, commonly referred to as Pittodrie, is an all-seater stadium in Aberdeen, Scotland. It has been the home ground of the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) club Aberdeen F.C. since they were formed in 1903. The stadium has been the location of a number of firsts in the field of stadium design, including the invention of the dugout, and in 1978 became one of the first all-seater stadiums in the United Kingdom.

Major_Events.Description: The first game, a 7–1 win over Dumbarton, was played on 2 September 1899.

Major_Events.Event: First all-seated stadium in Great Britain
Major_Events.Description: Pittodrie became the first all-seated stadium in Great Britain, after the south terracing was fitted with bench style seating.
Aberdeen fought back from 2–1 down in a European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final second leg tie against Bayern Munich to win 3–2.
The new Richard Donald stand was opened with a League Cup tie against Clydebank.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a Main Stand with padded seating for club officials and VIPs, several executive boxes, and a cantilever roof. The Richard Donald Stand is a cantilever construction with two tiers and a row of twelve executive boxes. The Merkland Stand is a covered enclosure with two pillars supporting the roof. The South Stand has seating and a cantilever roof, although some seats remain uncovered.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pittodrie Stadium is culturally significant as the home ground of Aberdeen F.C. and for its innovations in stadium design, including the invention of the dugout and being one of the first all-seater stadiums in the UK.
world knowledge.Details: Pittodrie Stadium has hosted fifteen Scotland international matches and four rugby union internationals. It has also been used for concerts by notable artists such as Elton John and Rod Stewart. The future of Pittodrie as a football stadium is uncertain, with plans in action for the club to move to a New Aberdeen Stadium.

world knowledge.Name: Carlsbad State Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The 44-acre park was established in 1933 as part of the California state park system.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Coastal bluffs, multiple staircases, and one ramp for beach access.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A protected beach offering recreational activities and camping, contributing to local tourism and outdoor culture.
world knowledge.Details: Popular activities include swimming, surfing, bodyboarding, scuba diving, fishing, and beachcombing. There are 220 campsites with amenities like showers, bathrooms, electricity, water, Wi-Fi, and a camp store.

world knowledge.Name: Nikortsminda Cathedral
world knowledge.Address: Nikortsminda, Racha-Lechkhumi and Kvemo Svaneti Province ( Mkhare ), Georgia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nikortsminda Cathedral was built in 1010–1014 during the reign of Bagrat III of Georgia and was repaired in 1534 by the King Bagrat III of Imereti. The three-storied bell-tower next to the cathedral was built in the second half of the 19th century. Frescoes inside the cathedral date from the 17th century. The cathedral is on the Tentative List for status as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Major_Events.Description: Built during the reign of Bagrat III of Georgia.
Repaired by King Bagrat III of Imereti.
Three-storied bell-tower built next to the cathedral.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Nikortsminda reflects the Georgian cross-dome style of architecture, following a six-conch-within-rectangle plan. The rectangular western apse has adjoining side chapels. The cathedral has a massive dome and unbroken arcatures as its twelve windows, which are decorated with ornamented architraves. The interior is decorated with frescoes from the 17th century and ornamental sculptural reliefs. The facades are covered with smoothly hewn stone and include unbroken arcatures and various rich ornaments, such as multiple-figured narrative reliefs and episodes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nikortsminda Cathedral is one of the most beautiful Georgian churches and cathedrals, showcasing the mastery of late-Medieval Georgian ecclesiastical art. It is on the Tentative List for status as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral follows a short-armed rectangular cross plan and has a short segment to the west. The interior space is enlarged by the altar apse bema and the western passage. The transition from the hexahedron of the round drum to the dome circle is effected by means of spheric pendentives. The decorations include episodes such as The Transfiguration, The Judgment Day, The Ascension of the Cross, and figures of Saint George and Saint Theodore, as well as real and mythic animals.

world knowledge.Name: Clumber Park
world knowledge.Address: Clumber and Hardwick, Nottinghamshire, England. Postcode: S80 3AZ
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Clumber Park is a country park that was the seat of the Pelham-Clintons, Dukes of Newcastle. Purchased by the National Trust in 1946, it is listed Grade I on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. The main house was demolished in 1938 after damage by several fires. The estate has a rich history dating back to its mention in the Domesday Book in 1086 and its transformation into a deer park in 1707.

Major_Events.Description: The main house was demolished to avoid a tax bill after suffering damage from fires and the economic impact of the First World War and the Great Depression.
A serious fire destroyed much of Clumber House, including valuable artworks.
The ornamental bridge suffered extensive damage after a car was deliberately driven into it.
A waste-bin, a National Trust van, and a barn known as The Bunk House were set alight in an arson attack.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features the longest double avenue of lime trees in Europe, a serpentine lake, and a Grade I listed Gothic Revival chapel. The walled kitchen garden includes a 450 ft long glasshouse and hosts national collections of apple varieties and rhubarb.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Clumber Park is culturally significant due to its historical association with the Dukes of Newcastle, its architectural features, and its role as a public park managed by the National Trust. It is one of the National Trust's top ten most visited properties.
world knowledge.Details: Clumber Park is over 3,800 acres in extent, including woods, open heath, and rolling farmland. It contains a variety of habitats and is home to ancient breeds of English Longhorn cattle and Jacob sheep. The park is used for walking, cycling, and has facilities for camping and picnicking. A parkrun takes place in the grounds every Saturday.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Palace of Brussels
world knowledge.Address: Place des Palais / Paleizenplein, 1000 City of Brussels, Brussels-Capital Region, Belgium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Palace of Brussels is the official palace of the King and Queen of the Belgians, located in the center of Brussels. It was built on the site of the former Palace of Coudenberg, which dates back to the Middle Ages. The current façade was constructed after 1900 under King Leopold II. The palace has served as a venue for state affairs, royal receptions, and official visits.

Major_Events.Description: Leopold III abdicated the throne in favor of his son, Baudouin.
Albert II abdicated the throne in favor of his son, Philippe.

Major_Events.Event: Civil marriage of King Baudouin and Queen Fabiola
Major_Events.Description: The civil marriage of King Baudouin and Queen Fabiola took place in the Throne Room.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is built in the Neoclassical style, with a symmetrical façade, grand staircases, and ornate interiors. It features a central wing with east and west wings surrounding large courtyards. The interior includes the Grand Staircase, Throne Room, Hall of Mirrors, and Empire Room, among others. The palace is surrounded by formal gardens in French and English styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Palace of Brussels is a symbol of the Belgian monarchy and serves as the official venue for state affairs, royal receptions, and international visits. It houses important works of art and historical artifacts, reflecting Belgium's rich cultural and political history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official palace of the King and Queen of the Belgians, used for state affairs and receptions.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is open to the public from 21 July (Belgian National Day) until the beginning of September. It houses the Royal Collection, which includes state portraits, furniture, and artifacts from Napoleon, Leopold I, and other historical figures. The palace also features modern art additions by Queen Paola.

world knowledge.Name: Jubilee Bridge, Innisfail
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jubilee Bridge spans the South Johnstone River connecting Innisfail and East Innisfail, Queensland, Australia. The bridge was constructed in 2011, replacing an earlier bridge built in 1923 which marked the 50th anniversary of the establishment of Innisfail. The idea of constructing a bridge in this location was first raised in 1907 by the Johnstone Shire Chairman, Charles Edward Joddrell. The bridge faced numerous challenges, including community opposition, funding issues, and structural problems over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The original Jubilee Bridge was officially opened on 28 September 1923 by the Queensland Premier Ted Theodore. The bridge was decorated with flags, streamers and palms. It cost £32,000 of which £20,000 was spent in Innisfail. One of the bridge piers was 72 feet (22 m) deep, the deepest on any traffic bridge in Australia.

The Jubilee Bridge was closed on 21 May 2010 after a review found the bridge to be unsafe. The bridge's closure created a 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) detour for those travelling between Innisfail and East Innisfail.

The new bridge was opened on 3 September 2011 with a ceremony attended by the then Premier, Anna Bligh, Queensland MP, Curtis Pitt and local Mayor Bill Shannon. The new bridge faithfully reproduces the Art deco features of the original bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new bridge faithfully reproduces the Art deco features of the original bridge. The original bridge had a width of 15.8 m (52 ft) and one of its piers was 72 feet (22 m) deep, the deepest on any traffic bridge in Australia at the time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jubilee Bridge is significant as it connects Innisfail and East Innisfail, facilitating transportation and commerce in the region. It also marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of Innisfail and represents the community's perseverance through various challenges over the years.
world knowledge.Details: The construction cost of the new bridge was A$21.6 million. The original bridge showed signs of sinking within a few years of its construction, leading to a 4-tonne weight limit and numerous repairs. The bridge's closure in 2010 created significant inconvenience for locals, highlighting its importance to the community.

world knowledge.Name: Terminal 21
world knowledge.Address: Multiple locations: Asok and Rama III in Bangkok, Korat, and Pattaya
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Terminal 21 is a chain of mixed-use complexes in Thailand, with the first location opening in October 2011. Each location is themed around different global cities, offering a unique shopping and cultural experience.

Major_Events.Description: The first Terminal 21 location opened in Bangkok, featuring a multi-storied retail area themed around global cities.
The second Terminal 21 location opened in Nakhon Ratchasima Province, featuring seven floors of retail space and a skydeck.
The third Terminal 21 location opened in Pattaya, featuring six floors of retail space and a 32-story hotel & residence.
The fourth Terminal 21 location opened in Bangkok, featuring nine floors of shops and a large parking area.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Each floor of Terminal 21 is decorated based on touristic cities and locations around the world, such as The Caribbean, Rome, Paris, Tokyo, London, Istanbul, San Francisco, and Hollywood. The decoration may differ amongst the branches, while the themes remain the same.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Terminal 21 is culturally significant for its unique theme-based shopping experience, which allows visitors to explore different global cultures within a single complex.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mixed-use development (retail, cinema, hotel, and residence)
world knowledge.Details: Terminal 21 is a 40,000-square-metre one-floor-one-themed shopping mall. Each location includes an SF Cinema City movie theatre and a hotel-and-residence operated by Centre Point Hospitality company. The Asok location features the longest escalators in Thailand, up to 36 meters.

world knowledge.Name: Okinawa World
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Gyokusendo Park, named after the Gyokusendo Caves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Showcases Ryukyuan culture and history, including traditional crafts, dances, and local wildlife.
world knowledge.Details: Features a traditional Ryukyuan village showcasing glass making, Eisa dancing, and Habu snakes. Website: en.gyokusendo.co.jp/okinawaworld/

world knowledge.Name: Pretoria City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pretoria City Hall was built in 1931 and inaugurated in 1935 to celebrate the city-status of Pretoria obtained in 1931. The design was chosen through a competition in 1926, won by F.G. McIntosh. Construction was delayed due to economic difficulties.

Major_Events.Description: The hall was inaugurated to celebrate Pretoria's city-status.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Semi-Italian classical style, featuring a tower with 32 bells donated by George Heys, the former owner of Melrose House.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The hall symbolizes Pretoria's city-status and historical development. It includes statues of significant figures and was a venue for cultural events like concerts and weddings.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a venue for concerts, events, and weddings. Currently closed to the public since 2016.
world knowledge.Details: The Pretorius Square lies in front of the building, featuring fountains and gardens. The hall is owned by the City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality and has been recently restored.

world knowledge.Name: Golden Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Ankleshwar to Bharuch in Gujarat, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Golden Bridge was built in 1881 by the British to create better access to trade and administration officials in Bombay (now Mumbai). Originally named the Narmada Bridge, it came to be known as the Golden Bridge due to the heavy expenditure incurred during construction. After independence, it became part of the national highway.

Major_Events.Description: In September 2023, the Golden Bridge experienced significant challenges due to severe flooding caused by continuous heavy rainfall and the release of water from the Sardar Sarovar Dam. The water level of the Narmada River near the bridge reached about 9 feet above the danger mark, leading to evacuations and temporary closure of the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Through arch bridge made of iron, designed by Sir John Hawkshaw.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant historical structure from the British colonial period, facilitating trade and administration. It remains an important transportation link in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Road bridge connecting Ankleshwar and Bharuch across the Narmada River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was contracted by the Bombay, Baroda, and Central India Railway and cost Rs 45.65 lakhs to build. The flow of heavy traffic was reduced after a new bridge on Narmada was built. During the 2023 floods, the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) were deployed for rescue operations.

world knowledge.Name: Neptun, Romania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Neptun is a summer resort built in 1972, part of a string of resorts including Olimp, Jupiter, Cap Aurora, and Venus. It is owned by the Importanne Resort corporation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Neptun hosts the summer residence of the president, Nufărul (The Water Lily). It is a notable summer destination on the Romanian seacoast.
world knowledge.Details: Neptun is located on a beach called 'At the flags' (Romanian: La steaguri). The marine climate features hot summers with average temperatures in June over 22°C, sunny days, and gentle winters with rare snows. The mean annual temperature is 11.2°C, and precipitation is low (under 400 mm yearly).

world knowledge.Name: Mount Takao
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Takao is closely associated with the Shinto-Buddhist tengu, supernatural creatures from Japanese folklore. The mountain is renowned for Shugendō, the mountain asceticism focusing on strict discipline. A Buddhist temple, Takaosan Yakuōin Yūkiji, is located on the mountain and belongs to the Shingon Buddhist sect.

Major_Events.Description: The Ken-Ō Expressway opened to traffic on March 28, 2012, involving the drilling of two 10 m tunnels through the heart of the mountain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mountain features a Buddhist temple, Takaosan Yakuōin Yūkiji, and numerous shrines and statues dedicated to tengu, Buddha, and other Buddhist and Shinto figures. The mountain also has a network of hiking trails, a suspension bridge, waterfalls, and observation decks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Takao is a popular hiking spot and a significant cultural site due to its association with Shinto-Buddhist tengu and Shugendō. It is also a popular spot for kōyō (autumn foliage) and hanami (cherry blossom viewing).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hiking, religious pilgrimage, and nature appreciation.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Takao is protected within Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park. It has eight hiking trails and attracts over 2.5 million annual visitors. The Tama Forest Science Garden is located at the mountain's base. The mountain is rich in wildlife, with more than 1,200 species of plants and a wide variety of native animals and insects. Visitors can choose to hike, take a funicular, or ride a ropeway to ascend the mountain. The Tōkai Nature Trail starts at Mount Takao and ends at Minoh, near Osaka.

world knowledge.Name: Jeonbuk National University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jeonbuk National University (JBNU) is one of ten Flagship Korean National Universities founded in 1947, located in Jeonju, South Korea. It was established following the liberation of the Republic of Korea by the Provincial fund within the framework of the Korean national university system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: JBNU is one of the Flagship Korean National Universities and has been ranked 551–560th in the world by QS Top Universities Ranking in 2023. It plays a significant role in the educational and research landscape of South Korea.
world knowledge.Details: Jeonbuk National University has grown to 16 colleges and 14 graduate schools (one general, nine specialized and four professional graduate schools). Its Jeonju campus provides educational, research, and support facilities for approximately 32,000 enrolled students, and 2,000 faculty and staff members. JBNU maintains cooperative programs with international educational institutions, and more than 500 international students are enrolled in its degree programs, in addition to around 100 international researchers.

world knowledge.Name: Caloundra Lighthouses
world knowledge.Address: 3 Canberra Terrace near Arthur Street, Kings Beach, Caloundra, Sunshine Coast Region, Queensland, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Caloundra Lighthouses are a heritage-listed pair of lighthouses that played an integral role in Queensland's coastal navigation from the 1890s to the 1970s. The first lighthouse, built in 1896, marked the entrance to the North West Channel, the safest entry to the Port of Brisbane. The second lighthouse, built in 1968, served as a signal station and radar station. Both structures are significant symbols of Caloundra's maritime and tourism history.

Major_Events.Description: The first lighthouse was built to guide mariners to the North West Channel, becoming a key navigation aid for the Port of Brisbane.
A new lighthouse and signal station were built to modernize navigation aids, incorporating radar and signal functions.
The 1896 lighthouse was moved to Woorim Park to save it from demolition, later returned to its original site in 1999.
The lighthouses were added to the Queensland Heritage Register for their historical and architectural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 1896 lighthouse is a conical, timber-framed structure clad in corrugated iron, standing 12 metres high with a domed lantern. The 1968 lighthouse is a reinforced concrete tower resembling an airport control tower, with a multi-faceted observation room and lantern. Both structures are substantially intact examples of their respective eras.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouses are important symbols of Caloundra's maritime history and early tourism. The 1896 lighthouse, in particular, is a cherished landmark featured in promotional materials and local logos. The site also holds significance for its role in World War II as an observation post.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as navigation aids for maritime traffic entering the Port of Brisbane. The 1968 lighthouse also functioned as a signal and radar station.
world knowledge.Details: The site includes the original lighthouse reserve, now a public park, with views over Caloundra, Moreton Bay, and the Glasshouse Mountains. The lighthouses are maintained by the Sunshine Coast Regional Council and are popular tourist attractions.

world knowledge.Name: Malabon Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Malabon Zoo, Aquarium and Botanical Garden, commonly known as Malabon Zoo, is a zoo situated in Malabon, Metro Manila, Philippines. It first opened around 1989 and was founded by Manny Tangco in Barangay Potrero in Malabon, Metro Manila. In March 2020, community quarantine measures imposed as a response to the COVID-19 pandemic forced the closure of the zoo to the public and caused financial strain to the zoo's maintenance. This led Tangco to launch an appeal for donations so he could still feed the zoo's animals, which was responded to by various private and public personalities.
