The zoo has since reopened on November 7, 2021.

Major_Events.Description: Community quarantine measures imposed as a response to the COVID-19 pandemic forced the closure of the zoo to the public and caused financial strain to the zoo's maintenance.
The zoo reopened on November 7, 2021, after being closed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Malabon Zoo has developed a reputation for naming its individual animals after public figures including former and current politicians, actors and actresses, and other celebrities.
world knowledge.Details: Among the animals kept in captivity include Bengal tigers, lions, bears, deer, orangutans, and snakes.

world knowledge.Name: Grenoble Alpes University
world knowledge.Address: Cities of Grenoble, Saint-Martin-d'Hères & Gières, in France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1339 by Humbert II of Viennois, the university has undergone several transformations, including splits and mergers, most notably in 1970 and 2016. It was restored under the name Université Grenoble Alpes in 2016 after merging three successor institutions. In 2020, it further merged with the Grenoble Institute of Technology, the Grenoble Institute of Political Studies, and the Grenoble School of Architecture.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded by Humbert II of Viennois to teach civil and canon law, medicine, and the liberal arts.
The university was split into four specialized institutions following the widespread civil unrest of May 1968.

Three of the University of Grenoble's successors—Joseph Fourier University, Pierre Mendès-France University, and Stendhal University—merged to restore the original institution under the name Université Grenoble Alpes.
The Grenoble Institute of Technology, the Grenoble Institute of Political Studies, and the Grenoble School of Architecture merged with the Université Grenoble Alpes.
The French Parliament granted the university the status of grand établissement.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features urban campuses with a mix of modern and traditional architecture. The Domaine Universitaire campus is known for its isolated, academic-focused design, often referred to as an "American campus." It includes facilities like the science library, administrative buildings, and the Louis-Weil amphitheater designed by Olivier-Clément Cacoub.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is a major scientific and cultural hub in Europe, contributing significantly to research and education. It hosts one of the four French institutes in artificial intelligence and collaborates with major research organizations like CNRS and CEA. The campus is also known for its rich vegetation and quality of student life.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public research university providing higher education and conducting advanced research in various fields.
world knowledge.Details: The university has a budget of €450 million, with 3,000 academic staff and 2,500 administrative staff serving 60,000 students. It is affiliated with Aurora, EUA, AUF, and SGroup. The Domaine Universitaire campus boasts 3,000 trees and an arboretum with over 250 species. The university is organized around two main campuses: Domaine Universitaire and Campus GIANT, with additional facilities in Valence, Chambéry, and other locations.

world knowledge.Name: National Film and Sound Archive
world knowledge.Address: McCoy Circuit, Acton, Australian Capital Territory, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA) is Australia's audiovisual archive, responsible for developing, preserving, maintaining, promoting, and providing access to a national collection of film, television, sound, radio, video games, new media, and related documents and artefacts. The collection ranges from works created in the late nineteenth century to the present day. The NFSA collection first started as the National Historical Film and Speaking Record Library in 1935, becoming an independent cultural organisation in 1984.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as an independent cultural organisation
Major_Events.Description: The National Film and Sound Archive was created as a separate Commonwealth collecting institution through an announcement in Parliament on 5 April 1984.
The name was changed to ScreenSound Australia in 1999, and changed again in early 2000 to ScreenSound Australia, National Screen and Sound Archive.
It reverted to its original name, National Film and Sound Archive, in December 2004.
The National Film and Sound Archive Act 2008 became law on 20 March 2008 and came into effect on 1 July 2008, making the NFSA a statutory authority.
In June 2023 the NFSA launched the NFSA Player, a new digital streaming platform for on-demand content.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is often classified as art deco, though its overall architectural style is technically 'Late 20th Century Stripped Classical', the style of ancient Greece and Rome but simplified and modernised. It features a symmetrical façade, a horizontal skyline, classical columns and a central entrance. The decorative foyer features images of native flora, fauna and Aboriginal art and motifs. Face masks of well-known scientists from the late 19th century and early 20th century are featured on the foyer's walls as a reminder of its previous incarnation as the Institute of Anatomy.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The NFSA is Australia's audiovisual archive, responsible for preserving and providing access to a national collection of film, television, sound, radio, video games, new media, and related documents and artefacts. It plays a crucial role in preserving Australia's audiovisual heritage and making it accessible to the public.

Details.Nearest_parking: Free parking surrounding the building on Liversedge Street
Details.Notable_holdings: A 2010 study compared the curatorial practices of accessioning and cataloging for NFSA collections and for YouTube with regard to access to older Australian television programs. It found the NFSA to be stronger in current affairs and older programs, and YouTube stronger in game shows, lifestyle programs, and 'human interest' material.
Details.Public_programs: The NFSA runs a public program from its Acton building, including new release and repertory cinema screenings at Arc Cinema, panel discussions and Q&As, conferences, audiovisual installations, festivals and live music.
Awards: Ken G Hall Film Preservation Award
NFSA Australian Cinematographers Society John Leake OAM Award for an Emerging Cinematographer
South East Asia Pacific Audiovisual Archives Association (SEAPAVAA) NFSA Preservation Award

world knowledge.Name: Carlow County Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Carlow County Museum, founded in 1973 by the Carlow Historical & Archaeological Society, documents the history of County Carlow. Originally housed in the old Christian Brothers' building and later in the Town Hall, it moved to the redeveloped Presentation Convent building in 2012. The museum is now operated by Carlow Town Council and Carlow County Council in association with the CHAS.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was reopened in the redeveloped Presentation Convent building, the last of the buildings to open in a new cultural quarter.

Major_Events.Event: Unveiling of Carlow 1916 Commemorative Stained Glass Panel
Major_Events.Description: As part of the Ireland 2016 Centenary Programme, the museum unveiled a stained glass panel by Peadar Lamb depicting Carlow's narrative on the 1916 Rising.
The museum hosted a special exhibition about St. Willibrord, Patron Saint of Luxembourg, and his County Carlow connection.

Major_Events.Event: Latest exhibit of Robert Hartpole's grave effigy
Major_Events.Description: The museum's latest exhibit is the grave effigy of Robert Hartpole, Constable of Carlow Castle and High Sheriff of Carlow, dating from 1594.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the redeveloped Presentation Convent building, which also houses the County Library and Archives.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it documents the history of County Carlow, including archaeological finds, social history, and folk life. It also holds notable objects such as the 19th century pulpit from Carlow Cathedral and items related to John Tyndall, Kevin Barry, Captain Myles Kehoe, and the Carlow Sugar Factory.
world knowledge.Details: The museum consists of four exhibition rooms with permanent and temporary displays. It is designated to collect archaeological finds by the National Museum of Ireland. The museum's website is www.carlowmuseum.ie.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Cuauhtémoc
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Cuauhtémoc is a football stadium in Puebla City, Mexico, designed by architect Pedro Ramírez Vázquez. It was inaugurated on October 6, 1968, during the pre-inauguration of the 1968 Summer Olympics. Named after the Mexican brewery Cuauhtémoc-Moctezuma, which funded most of its construction, the stadium has hosted major events like the 1970 and 1986 FIFA World Cups. It underwent significant renovations from November 2014 to November 2015, becoming the first stadium in Latin America with a facade entirely covered with ETFE.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted matches including Uruguay vs. Israel, Uruguay vs. Italy, and Uruguay vs. Sweden.
Hosted matches including Italy vs. Argentina, Italy vs. Korea Republic, Argentina vs. Uruguay (Round of 16), and Spain vs. Belgium (Quarter-finals).
Hosted two finals where Club Puebla emerged victorious.
Hosted the tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, the stadium originally had a capacity of 35,000, expanded to 42,648 for the 1986 World Cup, and later to 51,726 after renovations. It features a unique ETFE facade, the first of its kind in Latin America, and includes modern amenities and structural upgrades.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Estadio Cuauhtémoc is a significant sports landmark in Mexico, having hosted two FIFA World Cups and numerous international and domestic football events. It represents innovation in sports architecture and is a symbol of Puebla's sporting culture.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by the State of Puebla and operated by Club Puebla. It has hosted international tournaments like the CONCACAF Champions League and Copa Interamericana. The 2015 renovation introduced ETFE facade technology, making it a modern architectural marvel in Latin America.

world knowledge.Name: Vaucluse Bay Range Rear Light
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vaucluse Bay Range Rear Light is an active lighthouse located on the east side of the entrance to Vaucluse Bay. It serves as the rear range light companion to the Vaucluse Bay Range Front Light, guiding vessels into Vaucluse Bay. The distance between the two lights is 945 metres (3,100 ft). It is one of four lighthouses in a style sometimes called 'Disney Castle'.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first constructed.
The current lighthouse structure was first lit.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a cylindrical concrete tower with a balcony and lantern, standing 26 feet (7.9 m) tall. It has a white tower and conical roof. The light is shone through a window.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is part of a unique group of four lighthouses in a style sometimes referred to as 'Disney Castle', making it architecturally distinctive. It is also an active aid to navigation, contributing to maritime safety.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The lighthouse serves as a navigational aid, guiding vessels into Vaucluse Bay.
world knowledge.Details: The light is operated by the Sydney Ports Corporation. It is located on private land, not accessible to the public, but easily seen from 12 Wentworth Road. The lighthouse has a focal height of 275 feet (84 m) and a range of 5 nautical miles (9.3 km), with a light characteristic of F R.

world knowledge.Name: University of Tikrit
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tikrit University is an Iraqi university established in 1987. It is one of the largest universities in Iraq with over 30,000 students. Despite challenges due to the conflict in Iraq, it has reemerged as a respected institution of higher education and has sought to partner with other universities globally.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a significant institution of higher education in Iraq, contributing to the academic and professional development of its students and faculty.
world knowledge.Details: The university includes a wide range of colleges and is accredited by Accreditation Service for International Colleges and Universities (ASIC UK).

world knowledge.Name: Ullim Falls
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Developed by Kim Jong-il in 1999, with a resort completed in 2001. It has been marked by the North Korean government as a tourist destination.

Major_Events.Description: Kim Jong-il initiated the development of the falls.
A resort at Ullim Falls was completed.
Ullim Falls appeared in the 'Landscapes' series of North Korean stamps.
Ullim Falls appeared in the 'Autumn Landscapes' series of North Korean stamps.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Marked as a tourist destination by the North Korean government and featured on national stamps.
world knowledge.Details: The falls are also known as 울림 폭포 in Korean. They were featured in two North Korean stamp series: the 2005 'Landscapes' series and the 2017 'Autumn Landscapes' series.

world knowledge.Name: Hornibrook Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Between Brighton, Brisbane and Clontarf, City of Moreton Bay
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2.684 km in length, 7.92 m in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hornibrook Bridge was constructed as a response to high unemployment during the Great Depression and to end the isolation of the Redcliffe Peninsula. Designed by engineer Manuel Hornibrook, it was the longest road viaduct built over water in the Southern Hemisphere at the time of completion. It played a strategic role during World War II and was a catalyst for urban development in the Redcliffe Peninsula.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed and opened to road traffic on 4 October 1935, significantly reducing travel time between Sandgate and Redcliffe.
The bridge was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 7 October 1994 for its historical and architectural significance.
The bridge was closed to vehicular traffic with the opening of the Houghton Highway, remaining open only for pedestrians and cyclists.

The bridge was fully closed on 14 July 2010 after the opening of the Ted Smout Memorial Bridge. Most of the bridge was demolished in 2011 due to safety concerns, retaining only the portals and a small section for fishing.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge was a 2.684 km long timber and concrete viaduct with Art Deco concrete portals at each end. It featured a timber superstructure supported by reinforced concrete piers, with ironbark girders and tallowwood decking. The portals were designed by architect John Beebe and included toll facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hornibrook Bridge is significant for its role in Queensland's history as a major public work constructed during the Great Depression. It was a pioneering example of private enterprise in infrastructure development and played a key role in the growth of the Redcliffe Peninsula. Its architectural and engineering achievements are also notable.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a vehicular and pedestrian bridge, later used exclusively for pedestrians and cyclists until its closure.
Notable_Visitors: Arthur Edward Moore (Queensland Premier at the time of opening)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was colloquially known as the 'Humpity Bump' due to its buckled road surface. It was the longest vehicular traffic bridge in Australia until its closure in 1979. After demolition, the northern portal was repurposed as the Hays Inlet Fishing and Recreation Platform. The bridge was also recognized as one of the Q150 Icons of Queensland for its engineering feat.

world knowledge.Name: Grand World Scenic Park
world knowledge.Address: Dongpu, Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grand World Scenic Park was an amusement park featuring replicas of global landmarks. It opened in 1995 but faced financial troubles due to declining visitor numbers. By 2017, it was rented by a wedding photography business, with most attractions in disrepair. The land was eventually taken back by the government in 2022 after a period of abandonment.

Major_Events.Description: 40 men rampaged through the park, destroying equipment and attacking workers with weapons, injuring six security guards (one shot). Police arrested 13 people and seized 16 suspects.
After prolonged abandonment, the park operator reached an agreement with the government, leading to the land being reclaimed and repurposed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Featured replicas of global landmarks (specific structures not detailed).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Once a prominent amusement park showcasing international landmarks, reflecting early globalization trends in Chinese entertainment.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement park (later repurposed for wedding photography).
world knowledge.Details: Total investment: ~56.7 million yuan. Between 2005-2009, multiple disputes occurred over contracts, power supplies, and dormitories with Yongshida workers.

world knowledge.Name: Logan Botanic Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Logan Botanic Garden is a botanical garden near Port Logan on the Rhins of Galloway, at the south-western tip of Scotland. It is operated as part of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's Living Collection. The Garden adjoins the Logan Estate and Category A-listed House, which remain in private ownership. The Botanic Garden was established in 1869 and was gifted to Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh in 1969. The gardens were built around the ruins of Balzieland Castle. A new glasshouse was built at Logan in 2014, designed as a Victorian architecture conservatory, and is the first public glasshouse in the UK that is entirely heated by renewable/green energy sources.

Major_Events.Event: 50th Anniversary of becoming part of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
Major_Events.Description: The Garden celebrated 50 years since becoming part of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh.
The garden was badly affected by severe flooding.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features a new glasshouse built in 2014, designed as a Victorian architecture conservatory. It includes a Walled Garden with a formal fish pond, an eco-Conservatory housing South African plants, Tasmanian Creek area, and a Discovery Centre with various exhibitions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Logan Botanic Garden is culturally significant as 'Scotland's most exotic garden,' featuring a unique collection of plants from around the world, including species from Chile, Vietnam, Australia, and New Zealand. It is also home to several National Plant Collections and has been involved in botanical missions to Vietnam.
world knowledge.Details: The garden has a mild climate due to the influence of the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream, enabling the cultivation of plants that would not normally survive outdoors in Scotland. It houses around 2,500 species, including 120 threatened with extinction. Notable features include a mature collection of Trachycarpus fortunei (Chusan Palms), a significant collection of palm trees and tree ferns, and several Rhododendron species, including the extinct-in-the-wild Rhododendron kanehirai. The garden also has a Puya alpestris plant donated by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew in 2013, which bloomed in July 2024.

world knowledge.Name: Rovaniemi Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rovaniemi Airport was built in 1940 with two grass-surfaced runways. During the Continuation War, it served as an airbase and supply center for German Luftwaffe. It is the second busiest airport in Finland after Helsinki-Vantaa, as measured by the number of passengers and landings.

Major_Events.Description: The airport served as an airbase and supply center for German Luftwaffe.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features jet bridges and has asphalt runways. It is one of three airports in Finland with jet bridges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rovaniemi Airport is culturally significant as it serves as a gateway to Lapland, including Santa Claus Village and Santa Park. It is particularly busy during the Christmas season due to Santa Flights.
world knowledge.Details: Rovaniemi Airport is located about 10 kilometres north of Rovaniemi city centre. It is managed by Finavia and connected to the city centre by airport taxi and multiple bus connections. The airport is also used by F-18 fighter interceptors of Lapin lennosto and the Air unit of the Frontier guard of Lapland. In 2017, the airport served about 580,000 passengers.

world knowledge.Name: Sir Barry Bowen Municipal Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Formerly known as Belize City Municipal Airport, it was renamed after the late Belizean politician and entrepreneur Barry Bowen. It serves as a key airport for travel to Belize's cayes, offering faster access than by boat or water taxi.

Major_Events.Description: A project to upgrade and modernize the airport was initiated in 2012, including extending the runway, constructing a new access road, adding a taxiway, and installing a new lighting system. The project was completed in November 2016 at a total cost of BZ$17 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Runway surface: Asphalt; Direction: 12/30; Length: 940 m (3,084 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named in honor of Barry Bowen, a prominent Belizean politician and entrepreneur, and serves as a vital transportation hub for Belize City and its surrounding cayes.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport providing travel to Belize's cayes and serving as a central transportation hub for Belize City.
world knowledge.Details: The head office of Maya Island Air is located at the airport, and Tropic Air also operates a terminal here with multiple daily flights. Belize Shuttles and Private Transfers provide regularly scheduled shuttles from the airport to various destinations including Placencia, San Ignacio, Hopkins, and water taxi terminals.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Wickham Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Cape Wickham, King Island, Tasmania, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cape Wickham Lighthouse was established in 1861 in response to the sinking of the barque Cataraqui, which resulted in 400 deaths. It was built to warn of danger rather than guide to safety, contrary to typical lighthouses. The lighthouse was automated in the 1920s and was officially opened in 2011 by Governor-General Quentin Bryce, as it was discovered it had never been officially opened.

Major_Events.Description: The sinking of the barque Cataraqui resulted in 400 deaths, prompting the construction of the lighthouse.
The lighthouse was built to warn ships of the dangerous coastline.
The lighthouse was automated, and many surrounding buildings were demolished.
Governor-General Quentin Bryce officially opened the lighthouse during its 150th anniversary celebrations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 48-meter tall cylindrical stone tower with a balcony and lantern, painted white. It has eleven timber flights of stairs with twenty steps each.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is listed on the Commonwealth Heritage Register and is Australia's tallest lighthouse. It marks a historically dangerous area for ships and has associated remains of buildings and gravestones of shipwreck victims.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To warn ships of the dangerous coastline and prevent shipwrecks.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was originally staffed by a superintendent who faced conflicts with local inhabitants. Lightkeepers were highly self-sufficient, with only one supply ship visiting per year. Some resorted to looting and theft. The lighthouse is now operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority and has a light range of 24 nautical miles.

world knowledge.Name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kirstenbosch was founded in 1913 to preserve the flora native to South Africa, making it the first botanical garden in the world with this ethos. The land was previously used for timber harvesting and farming before being bequeathed to the nation by Cecil Rhodes in 1902. The garden was established by botanist Henry Harold Pearson, who worked under difficult conditions to develop the area. Over the years, it has been administered by various organizations, including the South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI).

Major_Events.Description: Kirstenbosch was established as a botanical garden with a focus on preserving indigenous plants.
The garden celebrated its 100th anniversary with the publication of a commemorative book.
Kirstenbosch won a gold medal and the President's Cup at the Chelsea Flower Show for its creative display featuring the quiver tree as an indicator of climate change.
Kirstenbosch was declared the International Garden of the Year by the International Garden Tourism Awards Body.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features a large conservatory (The Botanical Society Conservatory) exhibiting plants from various regions, including savanna, fynbos, and karoo. Outdoors, the focus is on plants native to the Cape region, with spectacular collections of proteas. The garden also includes historical elements like Van Riebeeck's Hedge, a Provincial Heritage Site.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kirstenbosch is culturally significant as the first botanical garden in the world dedicated to preserving indigenous flora. It plays a key role in botanical research, conservation, and education, and is a popular destination for both locals and tourists. The garden also hosts cultural events like outdoor concerts and exhibitions of Zimbabwean stone sculptures.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Botanical research, conservation, and public education.
world knowledge.Details: Kirstenbosch is part of the South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) and covers five of South Africa's six biomes. It includes the Compton Herbarium, which conducts research on plant species, particularly those of the winter rainfall region. The garden also features walking trails leading up Table Mountain and hosts annual summer concerts. Kirstenbosch has won 29 gold medals at the Chelsea Flower Show.

world knowledge.Name: Fairfield Beach (Fairfield)
world knowledge.Address: South of downtown Fairfield, extending south from Old Post Road to the Long Island Sound
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fairfield Beach is a neighborhood that originally had a variety of income levels, with small family farms and summer cottages. It began growing in popularity for year-round residents throughout the 1970s and 1980s. A recent surge in popularity has led to a building boom, with smaller old homes being replaced by larger new homes.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Many of the newer homes have been constructed in a distinctive architectural style known as "Nantucket" or "beach" style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fairfield Beach is a popular neighborhood with a mix of permanent residents and students, and it includes several beaches, parks, and community facilities.
world knowledge.Details: Residents are represented by several neighborhood organizations, including the Fairfield Beach Residents Association and the Fair Acres Association. The area includes Jennings Beach, Penfield Beach, Veterans Park, Fairfield Beach Club, South Benson Marina, and Roger Sherman Elementary School. Traditionally, many Fairfield University students have lived in the neighborhood, though their numbers have decreased in recent years due to rising property values and rents.

world knowledge.Name: Ai-Petri
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ai-Petri is a peak in the Crimean Mountains. The name is of Greek origin, translating to "St. Peter". It is known for being one of the windiest places in Crimea, with winds reaching speeds of 50 m/s (110 mph) for 125 days a year. The peak is located above the city of Alupka and the town of Koreiz. A military base located here was attacked in May 2024, resulting in the death of a Russian commander.

Major_Events.Description: A Russian commander was killed in the attack on the military base located at Ai-Petri.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ai-Petri is a significant natural landmark in Crimea, known for its extreme wind conditions and its role in the local geography. It forms one side of the Grand Canyon of Crimea.
world knowledge.Details: There is a cable car that takes passengers from a station near Alupka to the main area in Ai-Petri. The Ai-Petri massif makes up one side of the Grand Canyon of Crimea, with the other side being the Boyka massif.

world knowledge.Name: Melville, KwaZulu-Natal
world knowledge.Location: Coastal resort village between Port Shepstone and Hibberdene
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Melville is a quiet and small coastal village often regarded as an extension of Port Shepstone. It remains largely unspoilt with abundant indigenous subtropical vegetation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Melville is culturally significant as a largely unspoilt coastal village with indigenous subtropical vegetation, offering a quiet retreat.

Transportation.Shopping_Facilities: nearest in Port Shepstone and Hibberdene

world knowledge.Name: Tasek Merimbun
world knowledge.Address: Near Mukim Rambai, Tutong District, Brunei
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Merimbun Lake is the largest natural lake in Brunei, believed to have been discovered by Imbun, the son of a village head from Merangking Hilir in the Belait District. The area was settled by the Dusun Brunei and later became known as Tasek Merimbun. The name 'Merimbun' may also derive from a Chinese merchant named Eng Boon. The lake and surrounding area have historical significance as one of the first Dusun villages in the Tutong District. In 1967, it was identified as a potential wildlife sanctuary, and in 1984, it was designated as the first ASEAN Heritage Park.

Major_Events.Description: Tasek Merimbun was designated as the first ASEAN Heritage Park on 29 November 1984, recognizing its biodiversity and importance as a wildlife sanctuary.
The Tasek Merimbun Heritage Park was officially inaugurated on 27 May 2000 at the Tasek Merimbun Heritage Park Exhibition Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a picnic pavilion made from logs on one of its islands, and chalet facilities are available for researchers. The lake is known for its dark-colored water due to tannins from decaying leaves.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tasek Merimbun is culturally significant as one of the first Dusun villages in the Tutong District and as a site of early settlement and self-sufficient living. It is also recognized for its biodiversity and as a wildlife sanctuary.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Wildlife sanctuary, recreation center, flora and fauna conservation area, and research site
world knowledge.Details: Tasek Merimbun is home to a rich diversity of fauna, including endangered Storm's storks. Visitors can hire boats to explore the lake and its islands. The park has been designated by BirdLife International as an Important Bird Area.

world knowledge.Name: Votive Church, Szeged
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Width: 51 metres, Dome diameter (outer): 54 metres, Dome diameter (inner): 33 metres, Spire height: 81 metres
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Votive Church and Cathedral of Our Lady of Hungary is a twin-spired church in Szeged. Construction began in 1913 after a flood had destroyed most of Szeged. It was designed by Frederick Schulek and was completed in 1930. The construction of the church was a result of a pledge made by the inhabitants of Szeged to build a cathedral after the flood of March 1879. The construction was stopped because of World War I and was finally finished on 24 October 1930.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation was laid on 21 June 1914.
The construction was completed on 24 October 1930.
The church held its first mass on 25 October 1930.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The church is made mostly of brick, and has two towers, each 91 meters high, and a large dome in between. The front of the church has a Grecian cross and rose windows underneath. Below that is the 3-metre-tall statue of Madonna, the protector of Hungary since Stephen I. On each side of the statue there are paintings of the 12 Apostles. The church has many frescos, with the main one being "Our Lady of Hungary" behind the main altar. The dome's fresco was painted by László Patay.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church serves as the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Szeged–Csanád and is the fourth-largest church in Hungary. It is a significant cultural and religious landmark in Hungary.
world knowledge.Details: The church contains five bells, the largest of which is the Heroes Bell which weighs 8,537 kilograms (18,821 lb), is tuned to F0 and was made in 1927. It also contains one of the largest organs in Europe with 9740 pipes and 134 ranks. The church is located in Dóm Square Szeged, which is exactly the same size as Piazza San Marco in Venice, Italy.

world knowledge.Name: Noup Head Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Noup Head Lighthouse was constructed in 1898 by David A Stevenson for the Northern Lighthouse Board. It became automatic in 1964 and was converted to wind and solar power in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse became automatic, reducing the need for manual operation.
The lighthouse was converted to wind and solar power using a solar array.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 24 metres (79 ft) cylindrical masonry tower with balcony and lantern, white tower, black lantern, ochre trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a category B listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance in Scotland.

Details.Built_by: David Alan Stevenson, Charles Alexander Stevenson

world knowledge.Name: Guthrie Theater
world knowledge.Address: 818 South 2nd Street Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Guthrie Theater, founded in 1963, is a center for theater performance, production, education, and professional training in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The concept of the theater was born in 1959 in discussions among Sir Tyrone Guthrie, Oliver Rea, and Peter Zeisler, who were disenchanted with Broadway and aimed to create a theater with a resident acting company performing classic plays in rotating repertory.

Major_Events.Description: The Guthrie Theater opened with a production of Hamlet, featuring notable actors such as Hume Cronyn, Jessica Tandy, and Zoe Caldwell.

Major_Events.Event: Winning the Regional Theatre Tony Award
Major_Events.Description: The theater was recognized for its excellence with the Regional Theatre Tony Award.
The Guthrie moved to a new $125 million facility designed by Jean Nouvel, featuring three theaters and a cantilevered bridge to the Mississippi River.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original 1963 building was designed by Ralph Rapson with a 1,441-seat thrust stage by Tanya Moiseiwitsch. The 2006 facility, designed by Jean Nouvel, includes a thrust stage (1,100 seats), a proscenium stage (700 seats), and a black-box studio. The exterior features large panels displaying murals of past plays.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Guthrie Theater is a landmark of American regional theater, known for its high professional standards, resident acting company, and commitment to classic and contemporary plays. It has played a significant role in the cultural life of Minneapolis and the broader theater community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theater performance, production, education, and professional training
world knowledge.Details: The Guthrie Theater has undergone significant architectural changes, including a redesign by Liviu Ciulei in 1980 and a move to a new facility in 2006. It continues to be a leading institution in American theater.

world knowledge.Name: Hubei University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hubei University was founded in 1931 as Hubei Provincial Education College. The college moved between locations and changed its name several times during its half-century of development. Since 1984, it was renamed Hubei University.

Major_Events.Description: The institution was renamed from its previous name to Hubei University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hubei University is a significant educational institution in China, contributing to higher education and research in the region.

Details.Motto: 日思日睿 笃志笃行

world knowledge.Name: Chateau-sur-Mer
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chateau-sur-Mer is one of the first grand Bellevue Avenue mansions of the Gilded Age in Newport, Rhode Island. It was completed in 1852 as an Italianate villa for William Shepard Wetmore, a merchant in the Old China Trade. The mansion ushered in the Gilded Age of Newport and was the most palatial residence in Newport until the Vanderbilt houses in the 1890s. The house was remodeled in the 1870s by architect Richard Morris Hunt in the French Second Empire style, displaying major design trends of the late 19th century. It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2006.

Major_Events.Description: Chateau-sur-Mer was completed as an Italianate villa for William Shepard Wetmore.
The house was remodeled and redecorated in the French Second Empire style, greatly expanding its size and adding new architectural elements.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The house was recognized for its historical significance and added to the National Register of Historic Places.
Chateau-sur-Mer was declared a National Historic Landmark for its architectural and historical importance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Chateau-sur-Mer is constructed of Fall River Granite and initially designed in the Italianate style. It was later remodeled in the French Second Empire style, featuring a three-story wing, a porte-cochere, and a projecting four-story tower with a mansard roof. The interior includes a great hall with a 45-foot ceiling, an Eastlake-style billiard room, an Italianate library, a marble hallway, and a Renaissance Revival dining room. The house is a landmark of Victorian architecture, furniture, wallpapers, ceramics, and stenciling.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chateau-sur-Mer is culturally significant as one of the first grand mansions of the Gilded Age in Newport, marking the beginning of Newport's transformation into a summer resort for the wealthy. It represents the opulence and architectural trends of the late 19th century and is a well-preserved example of Victorian design and lifestyle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a private residence, it now serves as a museum open to the public.
world knowledge.Details: Chateau-sur-Mer was one of the few Newport 'cottages' built as a year-round residence. The Wetmore family, particularly George Peabody Wetmore, was active in Rhode Island politics, with George serving as Governor and later as a U.S. Senator. The house is now owned by the Preservation Society of Newport County, and the former carriage house and stables are being renovated by Salve Regina University as the Antone Center for visual art and preservation.

world knowledge.Name: Liverpool John Moores University
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1823 – Liverpool Mechanics' School of Arts, 1992 – Liverpool John Moores University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) traces its origins to the Liverpool Mechanics' School of Arts, established in 1823. It later became Liverpool Polytechnic and was granted university status in 1992. Named after Sir John Moores, a local businessman and philanthropist, the university has grown significantly, now serving over 28,000 students from more than 100 countries.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Liverpool Mechanics' School of Arts
Major_Events.Description: The institution that would later become Liverpool John Moores University was founded.
The institution merged with other colleges to form Liverpool Polytechnic.
Liverpool Polytechnic became Liverpool John Moores University under the Further and Higher Education Act 1992.
LJMU was awarded the Queen's Anniversary Prize for its contributions to education.

Major_Events.Event: Installation of Nisha Katona as Chancellor
Major_Events.Description: Nisha Katona, founder of Mowgli, was installed as Chancellor of the university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features a mix of Georgian and Victorian buildings, alongside modern facilities like the Tom Reilly Building, which houses sports and science facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: LJMU is culturally significant for its commitment to providing educational opportunities to people of all ages and backgrounds, embodying the ethos of its namesake, Sir John Moores. It is also known for its contributions to sports and exercise sciences and its role in the maritime industry.
world knowledge.Details: Liverpool John Moores University is a founding member of the Northern Consortium and is highly ranked for teaching and research in Sports and Exercise Sciences. It has over 27,000 students and offers more than 250 degree courses. The university has two main campuses in Liverpool and is known for its student sports teams and research contributions.

world knowledge.Name: Arví Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arví Park is an ecological nature preserve and Pre-Hispanic archeological site. It features sections of prehispanic construction, including antique buildings, water works, platforms, roads, gardens, and ditches. The park's trail, 'Camino Cieza de León' or 'Prehispanic Trail', is more than 1,500 years old.

Major_Events.Description: Cable Arví, also called Metrocable Line L, began commercial operation in February 2010, connecting Santo Domingo Savio station with Arví Ecotourism Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features prehispanic constructions including stone-built trails, water works, platforms, roads, gardens, and ditches.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arví Park is culturally significant due to its prehispanic archeological sites and its role as a major ecological and tourist attraction in Medellín.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ecological nature preserve and tourist attraction
world knowledge.Details: The park covers several municipalities of Antioquia, including Envigado, Bello, and Copacabana. It is equipped with 54 miles of walkable trails and is known for its wildflowers, butterflies, and trails. Activities include hiking, nature tours, cycling, and outdoor adventure sports. An outdoor food market is located next to the gondola station. The Piedras Blancas Ecological Hotel and its private reserve are adjacent to the park. The park can be reached from downtown Medellín via the metro station. Line L on the Medellín Metro goes to Arví Station, where there is a direct link to the metrocables that go to the park.

world knowledge.Name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded by William Barton Rogers in 1861 to address rapid scientific and technological advances, MIT has grown into a leading research university. It initially focused on laboratory instruction in applied science and engineering, later expanding into other disciplines. MIT played a significant role in World War II research and has been a pioneer in fields like computer science, artificial intelligence, and space technology.

Major_Events.Description: MIT was chartered on April 10, 1861, by William Barton Rogers to promote industrial education.
MIT relocated from Boston to its current campus in Cambridge, designed by William W. Bosworth.
MIT became a major center for military research, including radar development at the Radiation Laboratory.
Students and faculty protested MIT's involvement in defense research, leading to the divestment of the Instrumentation Laboratory.
MIT made course materials for over 2,000 classes available online for free, revolutionizing open education.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of neoclassical and modernist architecture. Notable buildings include the Great Dome (inspired by the Pantheon), the Stata Center (designed by Frank Gehry), and the MIT Chapel (designed by Eero Saarinen). The campus is known for its interconnected buildings and extensive tunnel system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: MIT is one of the world's most prestigious universities, renowned for its contributions to science, engineering, and technology. It has a strong culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, and hands-on learning, embodied by its motto 'Mens et Manus' (Mind and Hand). The institute has produced numerous Nobel laureates, Turing Award winners, and influential entrepreneurs.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Research university offering undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs in science, engineering, architecture, management, and humanities.

world knowledge.Name: La Défense
world knowledge.Historical_Background: La Défense is named after the statue 'La Défense de Paris' by Louis-Ernest Barrias, erected in 1883 to commemorate the soldiers who defended Paris during the Franco-Prussian War. Development as a business district began in 1958 with the construction of the Esso Tower, followed by the Centre of New Industries and Technologies (CNIT) the same year. The district evolved through multiple phases of skyscraper construction, becoming Europe's largest purpose-built business district.

Major_Events.Description: Built as part of the Tête Défense competition to complete the Axe historique.
A record-breaking free concert on Bastille Day, attracting two million spectators.
Marked by a huge fireworks display.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of Paris La Défense Arena
Major_Events.Description: Europe's largest indoor arena opened in La Défense.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: La Défense is characterized by modern glass and steel skyscrapers, with the tallest being Tour First (231 meters). The district features the Grande Arche, a monumental cube-shaped structure that aligns with the historical axis of Paris. The area also includes an open-air museum with 70 statues and modern art pieces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: La Défense is a symbol of modern Paris and France's economic power. It is Europe's largest business district and a hub for international corporations. The district also holds cultural importance due to its open-air museum and alignment with Paris's historical axis.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Business district, commercial hub, and cultural site.

Details.Education: Hosts multiple universities and business schools, including ESSEC and IESEG.
Details.Transportation: Served by RER line A and Paris Métro Line 1.
Details.Shopping: Westfield Les Quatre Temps mall with 220 stores and 48 restaurants.
Details.Future_Plans: La Défense 2006–2015 modernization plan aimed at expanding office and residential spaces.

world knowledge.Name: Chennai Mathematical Institute
world knowledge.Address: SIPCOT Information Technology Park, Siruseri, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1989 by the SPIC Science Foundation, the Chennai Mathematical Institute (CMI) started as the School of Mathematics. It became an independent institution in 1996 and was renamed SPIC Mathematical Institute. In 1998, it was renamed again to Chennai Mathematical Institute. It moved to its current campus in Siruseri in 2005 and was recognized as a deemed university in 2006.

Major_Events.Description: CMI moved to a new 5-acre campus in Siruseri, Chennai.
CMI was recognized as a university under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956.
CMI launched a summer fellowship programme inviting students from across India to work on research projects.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus includes academic buildings, a library block, and student hostels. The architecture is functional, designed to support academic and research activities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: CMI is a leading institution for higher education and research in mathematics, computer science, and physics in India. It has contributed significantly to the fields of algebraic geometry, theoretical computer science, and theoretical physics.
world knowledge.Details: CMI offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programmes in mathematics, computer science, and physics. It is known for its research in algebraic geometry, computational complexity theory, and string theory. The institute has a strong emphasis on bridging the gap between teaching and research. It also hosts an annual inter-collegiate student festival called Tessellate.

world knowledge.Name: Church of Santo Tomé, Toledo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded after the reconquest of Toledo by King Alfonso VI of León, constructed on the site of an old 11th-century mosque. Rebuilt in the 14th century by Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo, Lord of Orgaz, transforming the old minaret into a bell tower in Mudéjar style.

Major_Events.Event: Rebuilt by Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo
Major_Events.Description: The church was totally rebuilt by Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo, Lord of Orgaz, and the old minaret of the mosque was transformed into a bell tower in Mudéjar style.

Major_Events.Event: Burial of the Count of Orgaz
Major_Events.Description: According to legend, Saint Stephen and Augustine of Hippo appeared to place Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo in his burial, a miracle represented in the painting "Burial of the Count of Orgaz" by El Greco.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Three naves with crossing, covered by barrel vault and polygonal apse. Features a mixture of Mudéjar and Gothic styles, with a central dome in form of Rub el Hizb. Includes a bell tower with incrustations of glazed ceramics and a Visigothic plate-niche of white marble.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Contains the famous painting "The Burial of the Count of Orgaz" by El Greco, and represents a blend of Christian and Islamic architectural styles due to its history and construction.
world knowledge.Details: The church is opened on a daily basis to allow the public to view the painting. An entrance fee is charged.

world knowledge.Name: Gewiss Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was constructed in 1928 to replace Atalanta's previous grounds, initially named after fascist Mario Brumana. After World War II, it was renamed Stadio Comunale. It underwent several renovations, including expansions in the 1940s-1970s, removal of the running track in 1984, and modernization in the 1990s and 2010s. Atalanta purchased the stadium in 2017, and it was renamed Gewiss Stadium in 2019 due to a sponsorship deal.

Major_Events.Description: Atalanta played its first unofficial match at the stadium, a 4–2 victory against Triestina.
Atalanta defeated La Dominante Genova 2–0 in front of over 14,000 spectators.
A 1–1 draw against Inter had an attendance of over 43,000 spectators, a record for the stadium.
Atalanta recorded its record home attendance of 44,236 during a Champions League match against Valencia at San Siro.
Italy played a 1–1 draw with the Netherlands, a homage to Bergamo as an early epicenter of the COVID-19 pandemic in Italy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features two main stands (Tribuna Giulio Cesare and Curva Pisani/Curva Morosini), pitchside seating, luxury boxes, and modern facilities. It has undergone multiple renovations to improve capacity, accessibility, and UEFA compliance.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a symbol of Bergamo's football culture and Atalanta's rise in Serie A. It has hosted significant matches, including international games, and honors late players like Federico Pisani and Piermario Morosini.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium (home of Atalanta and occasional host of Italy national team matches).
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is also known as Gewiss Stadium for sponsorship reasons. It received the Most Valuable Field award during the Serie A Awards in 2023. Future renovations aim to increase capacity to 25,000 and add underground parking.

world knowledge.Name: Bay'ah Mosque
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bay'ah Mosque, also known as the Mosque of 'Aqaba Hill and the Aqabah Mosque, was built at the request of Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur in 761 CE at the site of al-Bay'ah, i.e. the place where the Islamic prophet Muhammad met with the Ansar (the supporters), and they took the pledge ('bay'ah', hence the name) of 'Aqaba.

Major_Events.Description: The Islamic prophet Muhammad met with the Ansar (the supporters), and they took the pledge ('bay'ah') of 'Aqaba.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Islamic Abbasid style with an open courtyard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mosque is significant as it marks the site where the Islamic prophet Muhammad met with the Ansar and they took the pledge of 'Aqaba.
world knowledge.Details: The Bay'ah Mosque is located below the Wadi Mina. This article about a mosque or other Islamic place of worship in Saudi Arabia is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Deal Island Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Deal Island Lighthouse is an inactive lighthouse located on Deal Island, part of the Kent Group National Park, Tasmania, Australia. It was built in 1848 and deactivated in 1992. It was the highest lighthouse in the Southern Hemisphere, standing 305 metres above sea level, and was sometimes visible from Wilson's Promontory, 80 kilometres away. Management and conservation are under the control of the Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service.

Major_Events.Event: Royal Australian Air Force A25 Airspeed Oxford aircraft crash
Major_Events.Description: During World War II, a Royal Australian Air Force A25 Airspeed Oxford aircraft crashed, killing all four crewmen. The aircraft wreck and their graves were about 15 metres apart at the bottom of the cliff. The bodies have since been disinterred and buried at Springvale, Victoria. Eyewitness accounts say the plane flew low over a ship which was actually a wreck, and then failed to regain enough height before hitting the cliff.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Granite tower, cylindrical shape with balcony and lantern, white tower and lantern, 22 metres (72 ft) in height, with a 1st order Fresnel lens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is historically significant as the highest lighthouse in the Southern Hemisphere and for its role in maritime navigation. It also has a connection to a WWII aircraft crash, adding to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse was automated in 1921 and deactivated in 1992. It had a focal height of 305 metres (1,001 ft) and a range of 24 nautical miles (44 km; 28 mi). The light characteristic was Fl (3) W 20s. The lighthouse sometimes had visibility issues in low cloud conditions due to its height.

world knowledge.Name: Peel Hall, Cheshire
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Ashton Hayes, Cheshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Peel Hall was built as a mansion in 1637 by Henry Hardware IV, a descendant of the former Lord Mayor of Chester. It was later reduced in size by 1812 and used as a farmhouse. Ownership fell into the hands of the Earls of Plymouth. The contemporary historian George Ormerod criticized its renovation in Tuscan style.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by King William III of England
Major_Events.Description: King William III of England visited Peel Hall, hosted by Colonel Roger Whitley, while traveling to the Kingdom of Ireland to fight in the Battle of the Boyne.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Peel Hall is constructed in sandstone with slate roofs and is in Jacobean style. It has an L-shaped plan, three storeys with a basement, and a symmetrical five-bay south front. The doorcase has a Tuscan architrave and a fanlight. The windows are mullioned and transomed.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Peel Hall is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II* listed building. Its historical significance includes its construction in the 17th century and its association with notable figures like King William III and the Earls of Plymouth.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a mansion, later used as a farmhouse.
world knowledge.Details: The garden wall and paddock wall of Peel Hall are also listed at grade II. The house was much reduced in size by 1812, with the two-tier entrance hall demolished and several entrances blocked up.

world knowledge.Name: Old Blenheim Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 232 ft 0 in (70.7 m) length, 26 ft 3 in (8.0 m) width, 30 feet (9.1 m) height
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Old Blenheim Bridge was a wooden covered bridge that spanned Schoharie Creek in North Blenheim, New York, United States. It had the second longest span of any surviving single-span covered bridge in the world. The bridge, opened in 1855, was also one of the oldest of its type in the United States. It was destroyed by flooding resulting from Tropical Storm Irene in 2011. Rebuilding of the bridge commenced in 2017 and was completed in 2018.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened for use.
The bridge was declared a National Historic Landmark.
The bridge was destroyed by flooding resulting from Tropical Storm Irene.
The bridge was rebuilt to replicate the original design.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: double-barreled long truss with center arch covered bridge
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge was one of the oldest and longest single-span covered bridges in the United States, recognized as a National Historic Landmark and a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally for vehicles, later maintained as a historic site open to pedestrians.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was rebuilt in 2017-2018 to replicate the original design, standing 15 feet higher to avoid future floods. The construction cost $6.7 million, funded 75 percent by FEMA and 25 percent by New York State. Preserved pieces of the original bridge were included as a memorial.

world knowledge.Name: Highlanes Gallery
world knowledge.Address: 36 St Laurence St, Drogheda, County Louth, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Highlanes Gallery is a public art gallery and visual arts exhibition centre in Drogheda, Ireland, which opened in 2006. The gallery is sited in a former Franciscan church.

Major_Events.Description: The Highlanes Gallery opened to the public on 4 October 2006.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gallery is located in a former Franciscan church, but specific architectural details are not provided.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Highlanes Gallery serves as a public art gallery and visual arts exhibition centre, contributing to the cultural landscape of Drogheda and County Louth.
world knowledge.Details: The gallery has public transit access via Drogheda bus station (550 m) and Drogheda train station (1.4 km). The nearest parking is at Bachelors Lane. More information can be found on their website: highlanes.ie.

world knowledge.Name: Chedly Zouiten Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Stade Géo André after a French sportsman killed during World War II, it was renamed in 1963 to honor Chedly Zouiten, a prominent figure in Tunisian football. It served as the main stadium in Tunis until it was surpassed by Stade El Menzah in 1967 and Stade 7 November in 2001. The stadium underwent significant renovations from 2009 to 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the 1965 Africa Cup of Nations.
Renovated for two meetings of the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features two grass football pitches, a handball field, a 400-metre track, two jumping pits, two shooting ranges, and a steeple river.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a significant sports venue in Tunisia, historically important for hosting major football events and serving as a key stadium in the capital before being replaced by larger and more modern facilities.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily used for football and other sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was closed on 17 November 2006 for renovation works costing 3.4 million dinars, which included updating the sanitation and drainage network, renovating the grandstand, press stand, bleachers, changing rooms, and electrical installations. It reopened on 20 May 2012.

world knowledge.Name: Saxon Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Saxon Garden is the oldest public park in Warsaw, Poland. Founded in the late 17th century, it was opened to the public in 1727 as one of the first publicly accessible parks in the world. Originally the site of Warsaw fortifications, it was extended during the reign of King Augustus II and attached to the 'Saxon Axis'. Initially a Baroque French-style park, it was transformed into a Romantic English-style landscape park in the 19th century. It was destroyed during and after the Warsaw Uprising and partly reconstructed after World War II.

Major_Events.Description: The Saxon Garden was opened to the public on 27 May 1727, becoming one of the first publicly accessible parks in the world.
The park was transformed from a Baroque French-style park into a Romantic English-style landscape park.
The park was destroyed during and after the Warsaw Uprising.
The park was partly reconstructed after World War II.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Saxon Garden was initially a Baroque French-style park with symmetrical axial designs, patterned parterres, gravel walks, and formally planted bosquets. It featured a central avenue leading directly to the palace, flanked by sculptures. The garden was inspired by the park of Versailles and included baroque flower gardens with pieces of turf, flower beds, hedges, and trees.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Saxon Garden is culturally significant as it is the oldest public park in Warsaw and one of the first publicly accessible parks in the world. It represents the evolution of garden design from Baroque to Romantic styles and is a testament to Warsaw's resilience and reconstruction after World War II.
world knowledge.Details: The Saxon Garden was designated as part of the historic city center of Warsaw with the Royal Route and Wilanów on 8 September 1994. It is open all year and accessible via public transit.

world knowledge.Name: Yerevan Opera Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Alexander Spendiaryan National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre, commonly known as the Yerevan Opera Theatre, officially opened on 20 January 1933 with a performance of Alexander Spendiaryan's opera Almast. The building was designed by architect Alexander Tamanian and consists of two concert halls: the Aram Khatchaturian Concert Hall with 1,400 seats and the Alexander Spendiaryan Opera and Ballet National Theatre with 1,200 seats. The theatre has played a significant role in promoting Armenian opera and ballet, hosting numerous performances and international tours.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre officially opened with a performance of Alexander Spendiaryan's opera Almast.
The entire building was finally completed after large-scale construction works.
The English National Ballet will perform 'Giselle' at the theatre on May 10 and 11, 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Alexander Tamanian, the building features two concert halls and reflects a blend of architectural styles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is a cornerstone of Armenian cultural heritage, promoting national opera and ballet. It has hosted numerous performances, including the first Armenian ballet 'Happiness' by Aram Khachaturian, and has toured internationally.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has performed more than 200 different operas and ballets by Armenian, Russian, and Western European composers. It received the status of National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre in 1956.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Nepal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Nepal, originally an Arsenal house built in 1824 by Prime Minister General Bhimsen Thapa, was transformed into a museum in 1928. It underwent several expansions and name changes, becoming the National Museum in 1968. The museum was established to preserve and exhibit rare and valuable art treasures and has evolved in its administrative and management systems over the years.

Major_Events.Description: Rana Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher added two wings to the main building and renamed it Silkhana Museum.
Rana Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher renamed it Nepal Museum and opened it to the public on February 12, 1939.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Judhha Jatiya Kala Bhavan
Major_Events.Description: Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher established the Judhha Jatiya Kala Bhavan in front of the Nepal Museum, opened to the public on April 18, 1943.
The museum was renamed the National Museum, a name that remains popular to this day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum comprises various buildings, gardens, and open spaces. The main building is a classical structure located on the Western side of the river Vishnu against a hilly background. It includes an Art Gallery, Buddhist Art Gallery, and Museum of Natural History.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Museum of Nepal is culturally significant as it preserves and exhibits rare and valuable art treasures, showcasing Nepal's rich history and biodiversity. It is an important destination for those interested in art and history.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has an auditorium with a sitting capacity of 142 participants, gardens, and is suitable for academic tours and family outings. It houses various galleries, including the Art Gallery, Buddhist Art Gallery, and Museum of Natural History, displaying metal works, wood and stone carvings, Buddhist paintings, sculptures, and ritualistic objects. The Military section features weapons and artifacts from ancient, medieval, and modern Nepal, and the Numismatic section preserves rare coins from the Licchavi era to modern times.

world knowledge.Name: Dubai Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dubai Museum is located in the Al Fahidi Fort, built in 1787, and is the oldest existing building in Dubai. The museum was opened by the Ruler of Dubai in 1971 to present the traditional way of life in the Emirate of Dubai. It includes local antiques, artifacts from African and Asian countries, and dioramas showing life in the emirate before the advent of oil. The fort served as a guard post, ruler's palace, garrison, and prison before being converted into a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened by the Ruler of Dubai to present the traditional way of life in the Emirate of Dubai.
A renovation was carried out by the former HQ of the Dubai ruler.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Al Fahidi Fort is square-shaped with towers occupying three of its corners. It was built of coral rock and mortar in several phases. The fort includes a reconstruction of the old city walls, a traditional boat (dhow) in the courtyard, and two cannons guarding the main gate. The internal halls contain old weapons, arms, and traditional musical instruments. The central courtyard features a bronze cannon, a well, and various types of boats, including a traditional summer house (Arish) made from weaved palm fronds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum showcases the history and culture of Dubai, including its pre-oil era, archaeological finds, and traditional way of life. It is a key site for understanding the emirate's heritage and its transformation over time.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes life-size dioramas, hologram-like movies, and information stands that depict the lives and times of the Bedouin people from the third millennium B.C. till today. Visitors can explore displays of pearl diving boats, swords, jewelry, and a spice souk. The museum also features archaeological finds from sites like Al Qusais and Jumeirah. Public transit access is available via Al Fahidi station on the Dubai Metro.

world knowledge.Name: Tottori Sand Museum
world knowledge.Address: 2083-17, Yuyama, Fukube-chō, Tottori, Tottori Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tottori Sand Museum was opened on November 18, 2006, in Tottori, Japan, by the Tottori Sand Dunes, displaying sand sculptures in temporary facilities. On April 14, 2012, it reopened as the world's first permanent indoor exhibition space dedicated to sand art, exhibiting works by fifteen international sculptors.

Major_Events.Description: Opened in temporary facilities displaying sand sculptures.
Reopened as the world's first permanent indoor exhibition space dedicated to sand art.
Won the 2021 Trip Advisor's choice award for places to visit.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Permanent indoor exhibition space dedicated to sand art. Sculptures are made only of sand and water.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is the world's first permanent indoor exhibition space dedicated to sand art, showcasing works by international sculptors. It highlights the unique art form of sand sculpture and attracts tourists globally.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum dedicated to sand art exhibitions.
world knowledge.Details: Each yearly exhibit starts in April and lasts until January of the following year. The sand sculptures are then deliberately destroyed and a new exhibit is prepared from January to April. The sand sculptor Katsuhiko Chaen is the chief sculptor. Despite the museum's proximity to the sand dunes, that sand cannot be used because the sand dunes are part of a protected national park. The sand came from a road building project.

world knowledge.Name: Fawley Court
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Large mixed-use grounds with extensive estate
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fawley Court is a historic country house with origins tracing back to the Domesday Book in 1065. It was rebuilt in 1684 for William Freeman, a plantation and slave owner. The estate has passed through various notable families, including the Whitelockes and Freemans, and was later used as Divine Mercy College by the Polish Congregation of Marian Fathers. It served as a cultural center for the Polish community in the UK until its sale in 2009.

Major_Events.Description: Fawley was the scene of fighting between Roundheads and Royalist troops commanded by Prince Rupert of the Rhine. Royalist soldiers ransacked the house.
The house was completely rebuilt for William Freeman, a plantation and slave owner, resulting in the current Neoclassical structure.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by William III of Orange
Major_Events.Description: William III of Orange stayed in the house during his march from Torbay to London during the Glorious Revolution.
The grounds were dramatically landscaped by Capability Brown for Sambrooke Freeman.
Fawley Court was requisitioned by the British Army and used for training special forces during World War II.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Polish Congregation of Marian Fathers
Major_Events.Description: The house and grounds were purchased by the Polish Congregation of Marian Fathers and used as Divine Mercy College and a cultural center for the Polish community.
The house was severely damaged by fire but was rebuilt with donations from the Polish community.
The estate was sold to a property investor for £13m, generating controversy within the Polish community.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with a large square brick and stone house featuring two tall storeys, plus basement and attic. The symmetrical plan includes an entrance hall, saloon, principal apartments, and staircases. The Ionic entrance portico on the west front was a later addition. The interiors feature early neoclassical decorations by James Wyatt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fawley Court is a Grade I listed building with significant historical and architectural importance. It served as a cultural center for the Polish community in the UK and housed a museum and library of national significance. The estate's history includes notable events and visitors, and it is reputed to have inspired Toad Hall in 'The Wind in the Willows.'
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a country house, later used as a school, religious house, and cultural center, now a country club.
world knowledge.Details: Fawley Court's grounds include a Gothic folly, a temple on Temple Island designed by James Wyatt, and St. Anne's Church, a Grade II listed building. The estate was landscaped by Capability Brown and features a private promenade along the River Thames. The house is associated with notable historical figures and events, including the Civil War and World War II.

world knowledge.Name: Strasbourg Cathedral
world knowledge.Address: Place de la Cathédrale, 67000 Strasbourg, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Strasbourg Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral of Our Lady of Strasbourg, is a Catholic cathedral in Strasbourg, Alsace, France. It is considered one of the finest examples of Rayonnant Gothic architecture, with significant Romanesque elements. Construction began in 1015 and was completed in 1439. The cathedral was the world's tallest building from 1647 to 1874 and remains the tallest extant structure built entirely in the Middle Ages.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was completed after centuries of construction, featuring a single spire due to changes in architectural plans.
The cathedral suffered significant damage during the French Revolution, including the destruction of statues and the conversion of the cathedral into a Temple of Reason.
The cathedral was a symbol for both warring parties. The stained glass was removed for safekeeping, and the cathedral was damaged by Allied bombing.
The cathedral was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List along with the historic centre of Strasbourg.

Architectural_Characteristics.Notable_Features: Rose window, astronomical clock, Pillar of Angels

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Strasbourg Cathedral is a masterpiece of Gothic architecture and a symbol of the cultural and historical ties between France and Germany. It is renowned for its intricate facade, towering spire, and the astronomical clock. The cathedral has inspired artists and writers, including Victor Hugo and Goethe.

Details.UNESCO_Reference: Inscribed in 1988 as part of the historic centre of Strasbourg.
Details.Restoration_Efforts: The cathedral has undergone numerous restorations, including major works in the 19th and 20th centuries to repair war damage and structural issues.
Details.Museums: Original works from the cathedral, including sculptures and stained glass, are displayed in the Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame.
Details.Bells: The cathedral has several historic bells, including the 'Totenglock' (Death bell) cast in 1447.

world knowledge.Name: Valencia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Valencia was founded as a Roman colony in 138 BC. It has been under Roman, Visigothic, Islamic, and Christian rule, becoming a major economic and cultural center in the Mediterranean. It played a significant role during the Spanish Civil War as the provisional capital of Republican Spain.

Major_Events.Description: Valencia was established as Valentia Edetanorum by Roman soldiers.
Valencia came under Moorish control, introducing new irrigation systems and crops.
King James I of Aragon captured Valencia, making it the capital of the Kingdom of Valencia.
The forced expulsion of Moriscos (converted Muslims) led to economic decline.
Valencia served as the provisional capital of Republican Spain.
Severe flooding led to the diversion of the Turia River and urban redevelopment.
Valencia hosted the prestigious yachting competition, boosting tourism and infrastructure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Valencia features a mix of Roman, Gothic, Baroque, and modernist architecture. Notable structures include the Valencia Cathedral (Gothic), La Lonja de la Seda (Gothic), and the City of Arts and Sciences (futuristic design by Santiago Calatrava).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Valencia is renowned for its festivals like Las Fallas (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), its culinary contributions (paella), and its historical role as a Mediterranean trade hub. It is a center of Valencian language and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Valencia serves as a political, economic, and cultural capital of the Valencian Community, with significant tourism, port activity, and educational institutions.

Details.Climate: Mediterranean with mild winters and hot summers.

world knowledge.Name: Rennes Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rennes Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Peter, has been a cathedral site since the 6th century. The earliest building was replaced by a Gothic cathedral in the 12th century. The west front collapsed in 1490, and the current façade was constructed in stages between 1541 and 1704. The nave and choir were demolished and rebuilt between 1756 and 1845 due to structural issues. The cathedral was extensively refurbished in the 19th century with gilt, stucco, and paintings.

Major_Events.Event: Collapse of the tower and west front
Major_Events.Description: The tower and entire west front of the Gothic cathedral collapsed.
A great stone fell from the roof of the choir, leading to the decision to demolish and rebuild the nave and choir.
The nave and choir were demolished due to structural instability, leaving only the towers and west front standing.
The rebuilding of the cathedral, which began in 1787 and was interrupted by the French Revolution, was finally completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Neoclassical and Gothic styles. The façade has neoclassical granite towers in four stages, completed over several centuries.
