world knowledge.Details: The construction cost of the cathedral was estimated at $4.5 million, partially funded by American Tom Monaghan, owner of Domino's Pizza. The cathedral has generated controversy regarding its architectural style and finance.

world knowledge.Name: Haus für Mozart
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1925, with subsequent reconstructions in 1926, 1938, post-WWII, and 2006
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established in 1925 by converting horse stables into a venue for the Salzburg Festival, it was the festival's first dedicated performance space. It underwent several reconstructions and name changes before its final renovation in 2006 for Mozart's 250th anniversary.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated with Hugo von Hofmannsthal's play 'Das Salzburger große Welttheater' directed by Max Reinhardt.
Rebuilt under the direction of Clemens Holzmeister after the first season.
Rebuilt by Benno von Arent after the Nazi annexation of Austria.
Reconstructed by Salzburg architects Hans Hofmann and Erich Engels.
Reconstructed and renamed to Haus für Mozart in honor of Mozart's 250th anniversary. Inaugurated with Mozart's opera 'Le nozze di Figaro' conducted by Nikolaus Harnoncourt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater has undergone multiple reconstructions, with the latest in 2006 featuring structural changes to the lobby area, three new entrances by Josef Zenzmaier, and a golden art-wall in the foyer by Michael Hammers. It now seats 1,580 people (1,495 seats and 85 standing places).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the first dedicated performance space for the Salzburg Festival, it holds historical importance in the festival's development. It is now the principal theater for Mozart and Rossini operas as well as Baroque stageworks, celebrating Mozart's legacy.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theater for operas and stageworks, primarily for the Salzburg Festival.
world knowledge.Details: The front of the building was used as the luxury hotel Nouveau Rothschild in the movie 'Knight and Day' starring Cameron Diaz and Tom Cruise.

world knowledge.Name: Singha Durbar
world knowledge.Address: Centre of Kathmandu, north of Babar Mahal and Thapathali Durbar, east of Bhadrakali Temple
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Singha Durbar, meaning 'Lion's Palace', was built by Chandra Shumsher JBR in 1908. Initially a private residence, it was sold to the Government of Nepal for 20 million Nepali rupees. It served as the official residence for prime ministers of the Rana dynasty until 1953 when it became national property. Post-1951, it was used to house government offices and both chambers of the Parliament of Nepal.

Major_Events.Description: A huge fire broke out, engulfing all three wings except the front-facing wing. Cannons were used to prevent the front wing from catching fire, and the area was later rebuilt on the old foundation.
Singha Durbar was seriously damaged during the April 2015 Nepal earthquake.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is a unique example of merging building traditions, including Palladian, Corinthian, Neoclassical mansions along with Baroque architecture. The State Hall is the largest and most decorated room, adorned with foreign imported art pieces like Murano glass crystal chandeliers, Belgian mirrors, English stained glass doors, and Italian marble floors with floral patterns in walls and ceilings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Singha Durbar is culturally and historically significant as it was one of the most exquisite and lavish palaces in the world until the 1950s. It played a central role in the governance of Nepal, housing the official residence of prime ministers and later government offices and the Parliament of Nepal.
world knowledge.Details: The palace compound is occupied by both chambers of the Parliament of Nepal (the Pratinidhi Sabha, or House of Representatives, and the Rashtriya Sabha, or House of the States). It holds 20 ministries and government offices. Singha Durbar is also the headquarters of Radio Nepal and Nepal Television.

world knowledge.Name: Seri Wawasan Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Seri Wawasan Bridge is one of the main bridges in the planned city Putrajaya, the new (2001) Malaysian federal territory and administrative centre. It was constructed to provide access to the Core Island, where the main government buildings are located.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Seri Wawasan Bridge is a futuristic asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a forward-inclined pylon, resembling a sailing ship. It features an inverted-Y shape concrete/steel pylon 96 metres high, with a main span of 165 metres supported by 30 pairs of forward stay cables. The bridge also includes 21 pairs of cable backstays and structural steel tie backs for counterbalance. The design includes a dual three-lane carriageway, a median, and a walkway cum cycle track.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant landmark in Putrajaya, symbolizing the city's modern and futuristic development as Malaysia's administrative centre. Its unique design and night-time lighting make it an iconic structure.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries motor vehicles and pedestrians, connecting Precinct 2 on the Core Island to the residential areas of Precinct 8 and 9.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also known as Bridge No. 9 and crosses Putrajaya Lake, an artificial lake created for natural cooling. It was designed by PJSI Consultants and constructed by Perbadanan Putrajaya. The bridge's total length is 240 metres, with a width of 37.2 metres and a longest span of 168.5 metres.

world knowledge.Name: Sandfly Bay
world knowledge.Address: Seal Point Road or Sandymount walking track, Dunedin, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Named for the sand which flies from the tall dunes surrounding the bay due to the windy nature of the coast, not for the sandfly insect.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural sandy bay with large dunes, cliffs, and rocky headlands. Features wooden hides constructed by the Department of Conservation for penguin viewing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A significant wildlife reserve hosting yellow-eyed penguins, New Zealand sea lions, and various seabirds. It is a popular tramping site and a location for naturist activities.

Wildlife.Yellow-eyed penguins: Significant colony, with viewing hides provided by DOC.
Wildlife.New Zealand sea lions: Frequently bask on the sand; public urged to maintain distance.
Wildlife.Seabirds: Spotted shags, sooty shearwaters, and variable oystercatchers commonly seen.
Wildlife.Kelp: Durvillaea antarctica (kelp) often washed up on the beach.

Access.Routes: Accessible from Seal Point Road or a walking track from Sandymount.
Access.Restrictions: Dogs not permitted; mountain-biking not allowed on tracks.

Activities.Tramping: Main track descends from Seal Point Road carpark across farmland and down to the beach.
Activities.Sports: Visitors use the beach for sports, including riding skateboards down sand dunes.
Activities.Naturism: Occasionally used for nude sunbathing; public nudity is legal where known to occur.

Safety.Penguins: Visitors asked to duck down to avoid scaring penguins away from nests.
Safety.Sea lions: Public urged to stay 10–15 metres away due to potential aggression.

world knowledge.Name: Sutton Hall, Sutton Lane Ends
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Middle of the 17th century, with additions and alterations in the late 18th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sutton Hall is a former country house that replaced a previous manor house. It was once the property of Sir Humphrey Davenport, Chief Baron of the Exchequer in 1631, and later passed by marriage to Sir Rowland Belasyse, an ancestor of the Earls of Fauconberg. In 1819, it was acquired by the Countess of Lucan and descended to her successors, the Lords Lucan, primarily used as a farmhouse. In the 1880s and 1890s, the property was rented by the explorers Theodore Bent and his wife Mabel Bent. In 2008, the building was substantially refurbished as a restaurant by Brunning and Price.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition by the Countess of Lucan
Major_Events.Description: The property was acquired by the Countess of Lucan and descended to her successors, the Lords Lucan, primarily used as a farmhouse.

Major_Events.Event: Rented by Theodore and Mabel Bent
Major_Events.Description: The property was rented by the explorers Theodore Bent and his wife Mabel Bent.
The building was substantially refurbished as a restaurant by Brunning and Price.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is constructed partly in stone and partly in timber framing, with a U-shaped plan. The arms of the 'U' end in irregular gables. The left gable is in stone, and the right is timber-framed. The upper storey of the right gable is jettied, the jetty being supported on brackets carved with wooden figures, one a knight in chain mail. Between the two wings is the former great hall. A 16th century chapel at the rear of the house, which has served at different times as stables and as a convent, now serves as the restaurant kitchens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sutton Hall is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II listed building. It is historically significant due to its association with notable figures such as Sir Humphrey Davenport and the Countess of Lucan, as well as its architectural features.
world knowledge.Details: Not far from the hall is a Bronze Age barrow or cairn, probably a cremation site, now much reduced in size.

world knowledge.Name: Henan University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Henan University was founded in 1912 as Henan Preparatory School for Studying in Europe and America. It underwent several name changes and mergers, becoming National Henan University in 1942, Henan Normal University in 1952, and finally Henan University in 1984. In 2000, it merged with Kaifeng Medical College and Kaifeng Normal College to form the new Henan University. In 2022, its legal registration address was moved from Kaifeng to Zhengzhou.

Major_Events.Description: Established as Henan Preparatory School for Studying in Europe and America.
Renamed National Henan University.
Renamed after departmental adjustments.
Merged with Kaifeng Medical College and Kaifeng Normal College to form the new Henan University.
Legal registration address changed from Kaifeng to Zhengzhou.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Three campuses: Minglun (original), Jinming (opened in 2002), and Longzi Lake (under construction).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Henan University is a key provincial institution and part of China's Double First-Class Construction, contributing significantly to higher education and research in Henan and China.

Details.Motto_in_English: To illustrate illustrious virtue; to renovate the people; and to rest in the highest excellence
Details.Campus: Three campuses: Minglun (original), Jinming (opened in 2002), and Longzi Lake (under construction)

world knowledge.Name: Troubridge Hill Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Troubridge Hill, Yorke Peninsula, South Australia, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Troubridge Hill Lighthouse was built as part of a project to downgrade the lighthouse on Troubridge Island to a low-powered automatic operation (later decommissioned) and establish a full-powered light on the nearby Yorke Peninsula coastline. It was constructed in 1980 and first lit in September 1980.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was built and first lit in September 1980 as part of a project to replace the Troubridge Island lighthouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is constructed from unpainted red brickwork with custom-made bricks, chosen for wind and earthquake loading design benefits. It has a conical shape with a balcony and lantern, stands 32 meters (105 ft) tall, and has no windows as it is intended for automatic operation. The lantern is white.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The innovative use of brickwork in the tower's construction won an award from the South Australian Clay Brick Association. It serves as an important navigational aid for maritime safety.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority and is powered by mains electricity. Its light characteristic is Fl (2) W 15 s, with a focal height of 62 meters (203 ft).

world knowledge.Name: Písek Stone Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Písek Stone Bridge is the oldest preserved early Gothic bridge in the Czech Republic. It spans the Otava River and is located in the south Bohemian town of Písek. It was probably built during the reign of Ottokar II of Bohemia. The bridge has been on the list of Czech cultural monuments since 1989 and became a national cultural monument in 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was exposed to a significant flood.
A flood caused the collapse of one of the bridge's towers.
The 'thousand year flood' tore off a stone wall and damaged railings and statues, but the bridge structure withstood the flood.
The cyclone damaged the Christ Cross on the bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is built on six pillars and has seven arches. It is constructed of stone and originally lacked sculptural decoration. Today, it features replicas of baroque sculptures. The bridge's design gives the impression of a 'small' Charles Bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Písek Stone Bridge is culturally and historically important as the oldest preserved early Gothic bridge in the Czech Republic and one of the rarest medieval bridges in Central Europe. It played a crucial role in the Golden Trail, connecting the Baltic areas with the Mediterranean.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is sometimes called the Stag Bridge due to a local legend. It was built on dry ground, and the river was redirected under it after completion. The bridge has undergone several reconstructions, including after the 2002 flood. Historical documents were discovered in the Christ Cross during its restoration in 2007.

world knowledge.Name: Drumpellier Country Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Drumpellier Country Park was formerly a private estate, gifted to the Burgh of Coatbridge in 1919 and designated as a country park in 1984. The park features two natural lochs, lowland heath, mixed woodlands, and open grassland. It has a rich history dating back to the Stone Age, with evidence of flint tools and an iron-age crannog. During the medieval period, it was the farming grange of the Monks of Newbattle Abbey. The Drumpellier estate was purchased in 1735 by Andrew Buchanan, a tobacco merchant, who built Drumpellier House. The estate was later gifted to Coatbridge and became a public park.

Major_Events.Description: The park was designated as a country park by the Monklands council, part of Strathclyde.
Since July 2019, the park has been the location of Drumpellier Country Parkrun.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features natural landscapes including lochs, woodlands, and open grassland. Drumpellier House, built in 1736, was the oldest part of the estate and was extended in the 1740s, 1750s, 1840, and 1850. The house was demolished in the 1960s.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Drumpellier Country Park is culturally significant due to its long history, from the Stone Age to its role as a medieval farming grange and later as a public park. It is also a site of natural beauty and ecological importance, featuring lochs that are part of a chain of kettle ponds formed during the last ice age.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes two natural lochs, one of which is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The lochs and the Monkland Canal attract many water birds. The park is also home to a variety of wild flora and fauna. The lochside path is approximately one mile long and suitable for bikes. The park now includes a golf course.

world knowledge.Name: Gopi Talav
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gopi Talav or Gopi Lake is a lake in the Gopipura locality in the city of Surat in Gujarat state of India. It was built circa 1510 CE by Malik Gopi, who was an affluent merchant and governor of Surat during the Gujarat Sultanate. In 2012, the lake was renovated by Surat Municipal Corporation and the area surrounding redeveloped as a recreational facility.

Major_Events.Description: The lake and the surrounding areas were renovated at the budget of around ₹22 crore (US$2.5 million). Around 90,000 square metres (970,000 sq ft) of land was renovated, where the 212 metres (696 ft) diameter lake covered almost 35,000 square metres (380,000 sq ft) of area.
The first phase was inaugurated on 5 December 2015 by Chief Minister of Gujarat, Anandiben Patel.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lake has a diameter of 212 metres (696 ft) and can hold 120,000,000 litres (26,000,000 imp gal; 32,000,000 US gal) of water. The renovated surroundings include amphitheater and fountain plaza.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lake is named after Malik Gopi, an affluent merchant and governor of Surat during the Gujarat Sultanate. The area he developed was called Gopipura, in his honour. The lake also finds mentions in travelogues of European visitors and in Sanskrit poetry.
world knowledge.Details: The redevelopment of the lake and the park around it is based on the renovation of Kankaria Lake in Ahmedabad. Water to the lake will be piped from the Tapi river on whose banks the city lies. The area has been divided into seven zones; the diamond zone, food zone, environment zone, history zone, communal harmony zone, textile zone and Surat nu Jaman.

world knowledge.Name: Villa Torlonia (Rome)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Villa Torlonia is a villa and surrounding gardens in Rome, Italy, formerly belonging to the Torlonia family. Designed by Neoclassical architect Giuseppe Valadier, construction began in 1806 for banker Giovanni Torlonia and was completed by his son Alessandro. Mussolini rented it from the Torlonia family for one lira a year as his state residence from the 1920s until 1943. After 1945, it was abandoned and decayed but was later restored and opened to the public as a museum by Rome's municipality.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Villa Torlonia begins under the direction of Giuseppe Valadier for Giovanni Torlonia.
Benito Mussolini rents the villa as his state residence, living there for 18 years.
The Allied High Command occupies the villa until 1947.
The villa is opened to the public after being purchased by the Municipality of Rome.
Restoration work begins, largely completing by the 2010s, except for the Moorish Conservatory.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The villa features Neoclassical architecture with landscaped gardens in the English 'picturesque' style. It includes structures like the False Ruins, Temple of Saturn, Tribuna con Fontana, Swiss Hut (later Casina delle Civette), Conservatory, Tower, Moorish Grotto, and Tournament Field. The Casina delle Civette is notable for its stained glass and majolica decorations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Villa Torlonia is culturally significant for its association with the Torlonia family, Mussolini's residence, and its collection of classical art and sculptures. It also houses a Jewish catacomb and serves as a museum showcasing historical artifacts and furniture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, now a public museum and cultural site.
world knowledge.Details: The villa's museum contains statuary from the Torlonia collection, furniture used by Mussolini, and works by artists like Bartolomeo Cavaceppi and Antonio Canova. The Casina delle Civette features stained glass and decorative motifs of little owls. The underground includes a Jewish catacomb and WWII-era air-raid shelters. The Teatro Villa Torlonia, restored in 2013, hosts occasional performances.

world knowledge.Name: Lake of Sainte-Croix
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lake of Sainte-Croix is a reservoir formed by the construction of the Sainte-Croix Dam between 1971 and 1974. The original village of Les Salles-sur-Verdon was destroyed to make room for the reservoir and was rebuilt on the shore.

Major_Events.Description: The dam was built to create the reservoir, which was put into service in 1974.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The dam is a reinforced-concrete arch dam, 94 metres high, 7.5 metres thick at its base and 3 metres thick at its crest.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lake marks the departmental border between Var and Alpes-de-Haute-Provence and is a significant source of hydroelectric power, generating 142 million kWh of electricity per year.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Reservoir for water storage and hydroelectric power generation
world knowledge.Details: The reservoir is fed by the Verdon river and holds a maximum of 761 million cubic metres of water. It features a sole island, the Île de Costebelle, part of the commune of Les Salles-sur-Verdon.

world knowledge.Name: TT Nagar Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Tatya Tope Nagar, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: TT Nagar Sports Complex, also known as TT Nagar Stadium, is a multi-purpose stadium in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India. It was opened in 1962 and renovated in 2013.

Major_Events.Description: The ground hosted its only first-class cricket match in 1982 between Madhya Pradesh cricket team and Vidarbha cricket team where home team won by 202 runs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex includes an indoor hall and an Olympic swimming pool among its facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Madhya Pradesh, hosting various sports events and promoting athletic activities in the region.
world knowledge.Details: Football, athletics, volleyball, hockey, basketball, badminton, cricket, handball, futsal, table tennis, judo, taekwondo, and wrestling are among the sports that can be played there. The complex is owned by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and operated by the Directorate of Sports & Youth Welfare Department. It has a capacity of 20,000 spectators.

world knowledge.Name: Kintai Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length of about 175 meters with a width of 5 meters
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kintai Bridge was built in 1673 by the third lord of Iwakuni Domain, Kikkawa Hiroyoshi, to replace previous wooden bridges destroyed by floods. It was designed with stone piers for greater strength and underwent periodic maintenance. The bridge remained intact for 276 years until it was destroyed by a flood in 1950 due to lack of maintenance during World War II. It was reconstructed in 1953 similar to the original.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was built by Kikkawa Hiroyoshi with stone piers to replace previous wooden bridges destroyed by floods.
The bridge was destroyed by a flood the year after its construction, leading to redesign of the stone piers for greater strength.
The bridge was declared a National Treasure in Japan.
The bridge was washed away by a flood from typhoon Kijia due to lack of maintenance during World War II.
The bridge was reconstructed similar to the original design.
All five bridge girders were restored for the first time in 50 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is composed of five sequential wooden arch bridges on four stone piers and two wooden piers on the dry riverbed. The three middle spans are 35.1 meters long, while the two end spans are 34.8 meters. The bridge was built without metal nails, using careful fitting of wooden parts and clamping with metal belts. The main wooden parts were covered with copper sheets for durability. The bridge was designed so that the wooden pathway could be lifted by flood waters to spare the main structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kintai Bridge is a historical wooden arch bridge and a National Treasure of Japan. It is a popular tourist destination, especially during the Cherry blossom festival and autumn color change of Japanese maples. The bridge represents traditional Japanese engineering and architectural techniques.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is located at the foot of Mt. Yokoyama, near Iwakuni Castle, and is part of Kikkou Park. It was periodically rebuilt every 20 years for the three middle spans and every 40 years for the two end spans as part of its maintenance.

world knowledge.Name: Museum of Cultures (Basel)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museum of Cultures in Basel is a Swiss museum of ethnography with significant collections from Europe, the South Pacific, Mesoamerica, Tibet, and Bali. It originated in the 1840s when Basel founded its Museum of Natural History and Ethnography. In 1849, it moved into a neoclassical building designed by Melchior Berri on the Münster hill. The ethnographic collection became independent in 1917. The museum was renamed in 1996 to reflect its focus on intercultural dialog.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Museum of Ethnology and Swiss Museum of Folklore
Major_Events.Description: The museum was renamed to reflect its dual mission of documenting local and foreign cultures.
The museum was renamed to emphasize its focus on promoting intercultural dialog.
The museum opened a new main entrance on the Münsterplatz, enhancing accessibility and distinct identity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical edifice designed by Melchior Berri, located on the Münster hill.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its large and important collections of artifacts from various cultures, its role in promoting intercultural dialog, and its status as a Swiss heritage site of national significance.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses about 300,000 objects and a similar number of historic photographs, making it the largest of its kind in Switzerland and one of the biggest in Europe. It also documents and preserves the local cultural legacy of Basel-City. Recent exhibitions have emphasized intercultural comparisons and dialog. Plans for further expansion are on hold for archaeological investigation of the museum courtyard, where evidence of late Roman settlement has been found.

world knowledge.Name: University of Fort Hare
world knowledge.Address: Main campus: Alice, Other: Bhisho, East London, Eastern Cape, South Africa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Fort Hare is a public university in Alice, Eastern Cape, South Africa. It was a key institution of higher education for Africans from 1916 to 1959, offering a Western-style academic education to students from across sub-Saharan Africa, creating an African elite. Fort Hare alumni were part of many subsequent independence movements and governments of newly independent African countries. Originally, Fort Hare was a British fort in the wars between British settlers and the Xhosa of the 19th century. Some of the ruins of the fort are still visible today, as well as graves of some of the British soldiers who died while on duty there. During the 1830s, the Lovedale Missionary Institute was built near Fort Hare.

Major_Events.Description: Fort Hare was established with Alexander Kerr as its first principal. D. D. T. Jabavu was its first black staff member who lectured in Latin and African languages.

With the passage of the Promotion of Bantu Self Government Act in 1959, it was nationalized and segregated along racial and tribal lines, and teaching in African languages rather than English was encouraged.

Major_Events.Event: Order of the Baobab in Gold
Major_Events.Description: The University of Fort Hare was awarded the Order of the Baobab in Gold for 'Exceptional contribution to Black academic training and leadership development on the African continent.'

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Fort Hare is culturally and historically important as it was a key institution in higher education for black Africans from 1916 to 1959. It offered a Western-style academic education to students from across sub-Saharan Africa, creating a black African elite. Fort Hare alumni were part of many subsequent independence movements and governments of newly independent African countries. It is the alma mater of well-known people including Nelson Mandela, Desmond Tutu, Robert Sobukwe, Oliver Tambo, and others.

Details.Motto: In lumine tuo videbimus lumen ("In your light we shall see the light"), from Psalm 36
Details.Official_name: Human Rights, Liberation and Reconciliation: Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites

world knowledge.Name: Huijin Center Guangzhou
world knowledge.Address: 650 Huangpu Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou 正南方向70米 邮政编码: 510655
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Huijin Center Guangzhou, also known as the Shimao Canton Financial Center (Tower 1), is an office building complex in Guangzhou, China. Built between 2014 and 2022, the complex is considered one of Guangzhou's top three landmark projects due to its ambitious planning, significant investment, and government support.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Tower 1 began.
Construction of Tower 2 began.
Both towers were completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex consists of two towers: Tower 1 stands at 320.6 m (1,052 ft) with 69 floors, and Tower 2 stands at 220 m (720 ft) with 50 floors. The structural system is reinforced concrete, with façades designed by Forster Engineering Consultants Co., Ltd. and interiors by Woods Bagot. Elevators are provided by Schindler Group.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Guangzhou Huijin International Center plays a key role in advancing Guangzhou's industrial sector, fostering growth in the high-end financial industry, and drawing in multinational financial companies.
world knowledge.Details: The complex is situated on a busy road overlooking the Huangpu District. It was designed by Gensler and is owned by the Shimao Group.

world knowledge.Name: Imperial College London
world knowledge.Address: South Kensington Campus, London SW7 2AZ, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Imperial College London was established in 1907 through the merger of the Royal College of Science, the Royal School of Mines, and the City and Guilds of London Institute. It was initially part of the University of London but became an independent university in 2007. The college has a rich history of scientific and technological advancements, with roots tracing back to the Royal College of Chemistry founded in 1845.

Major_Events.Event: Formation of Imperial College of Science and Technology
Major_Events.Description: Imperial College was established by merging the Royal College of Science, the Royal School of Mines, and the City and Guilds of London Institute.

Major_Events.Event: Merger with St Mary's Hospital Medical School
Major_Events.Description: Imperial College merged with St Mary's Hospital Medical School, expanding its medical education and research capabilities.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Imperial College Business School
Major_Events.Description: The Imperial College Business School was established, officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II.

Major_Events.Event: Independence from the University of London
Major_Events.Description: Imperial College became an independent university, no longer a constituent college of the University of London.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The main campus in South Kensington features a mix of historic and modern buildings, including the Royal School of Mines, the Royal College of Science, and the Queen's Tower. The campus is part of the cultural area known as Albertopolis, surrounded by museums and cultural institutions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Imperial College London is one of the world's leading universities in science, engineering, medicine, and business. It has produced numerous Nobel laureates, Fields Medalists, and influential scientists. The college is known for its contributions to scientific research, technological innovation, and its role in shaping public policy.
world knowledge.Details: Imperial College London is organized into four faculties: Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences, and Business. The college has a strong focus on interdisciplinary research and innovation, with numerous research centers and collaborations with institutions worldwide. It is also known for its entrepreneurial culture and emphasis on practical, career-oriented education.

world knowledge.Name: Elbow Cay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally populated by British loyalists fleeing the newly independent United States of America in 1785, it has survived on fishing, boat building, and salvage. The first known permanent residents arrived in 1785 in what was known as Great Harbour. Wyannie Malone, originally from Charleston, South Carolina and other British Loyalists left the United States for the nearest British territory in The Bahamas.

Major_Events.Description: Elbow Cay took a direct hit from Category 5 Hurricane Dorian, with sustained winds of 185 mph (295 km/h). The lighthouse survived. ABC News reported damage as 'catastrophic' and 'pure hell', throughout the island.
Elbow Cay suffered significant damage from Hurricane Floyd. It nearly cut a new inlet near White Sound. The road remains damaged to this day.
A faring from a SpaceX rocket drifted ashore on Elbow Cay.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Noted red-and-white-striped one-hundred-and-twenty-foot-tall (37-metre) lighthouse built in 1863.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Elbow Cay is culturally significant due to its history of British loyalists, its survival through fishing, boat building, and salvage, and its iconic lighthouse. It also serves as a tourist destination with its beautiful beaches and historical sites.
world knowledge.Details: Elbow Cay is located about 4 miles (6.4 kilometres) east of Marsh Harbour on Great Abaco Island. Most visitors fly into Marsh Harbour and take the ferry to either Hope Town at the Northern end of Elbow Cay or White Sound, a mid-island harbour and settlement developed in 1960. At the Southern end of the island is Tahiti Beach near Doros Cove. The Atlantic Ocean runs along the entire Eastern coast of Elbow Cay, while the South Abaco Sound is on the western coast. Hope Town originally served as the administrative centre of the Abacos, until it switched over to Marsh Harbour in the 1960s. The episodes 'My Soul on Fire' (Part 1 and 2) of the TV series Scrubs were filmed on the island for the Janitor and Lady's wedding. The lighthouse and other businesses were shown in the episode.

world knowledge.Name: North Mole Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: End of North Mole Drive, Fremantle Harbour, Western Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The North Mole Lighthouse began operation in 1906 at the entrance to Fremantle Harbour. It was designed by C. Y. O'Connor, an engineer responsible for the construction of Fremantle Harbour and the Goldfields Water Supply Scheme. The lighthouse and its technically identical yet green coloured partner on the south mole are the last remaining of their type. It has an 'indicative place' status of the Register of the National Estate and is a well-known landmark to seamen visiting the port.

Major_Events.Description: A severe storm affected the moles but did not seriously damage the lighthouse.
A severe storm affected the moles but did not seriously damage the lighthouse.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 15-metre (49 ft) tower is made of cast iron, painted red and features classical decorations. It has a tapered cylindrical tower with balcony and lantern. The markings include a red tower with white trim and lantern.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a well-known landmark to seamen visiting the port and has an 'indicative place' status of the Register of the National Estate. It and its partner on the south mole are the last remaining of their type.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To emit an occulting red light indicating the westernmost point of the harbour and its entrance.
world knowledge.Details: The occulting red light, emitted from a fixed lightsource at a focal plane height of 15 metres (49 ft) above sea level, is visible for 18 kilometres (11 mi). The position is a well used recreational fishing spot and a vantage point for ocean yacht racing and birdwatching.

world knowledge.Name: University of Winnipeg
world knowledge.Address: 515 Portage Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3B 2E9, Canada
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 23 buildings spreading over several full blocks of Downtown Winnipeg
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1894-1895 (Wesley Hall); various other buildings constructed or renovated over the years
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Winnipeg (UWinnipeg) was established in 1967 when United College received its charter. United College was formed in 1938 from the union of Manitoba College (founded in 1871) and Wesley College (founded in 1888). The university has grown significantly since its founding and has become a key institution in Winnipeg, contributing to downtown renewal and offering a range of undergraduate and graduate programs.

Major_Events.Description: Manitoba College and Wesley College merged to form United College.

Major_Events.Event: Chartering of the University of Winnipeg
Major_Events.Description: United College received its charter and became the University of Winnipeg.
The Buhler Centre was constructed to house the Faculty of Business and Economics, as well as PACE (Professional, Applied and Continuing Education).

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Axworthy Health & RecPlex
Major_Events.Description: The Axworthy Health & RecPlex opened, offering a range of sport and recreation facilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus includes a mix of historic and modern buildings. Wesley Hall, built in 1894-1895, is a stone-clad brick structure and is listed on the Registry of Historic Places of Canada. The Buhler Centre, designed by PSA+DPA+DIN collective, is a modern structure housing the Faculty of Business and Economics and other facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Winnipeg is culturally significant for its role in the development of Winnipeg's downtown area and its commitment to Indigenous education. It is the first university in Canada to mandate an Indigenous course requirement for all students.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Winnipeg is a member of several academic associations, including the Association of Universities and Colleges of Canada (AUCC) and the Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU). It has a growing research profile with several research centers and Canada Research Chairs. The university also has a strong focus on sustainability and community engagement, with initiatives like the University of Winnipeg Renewal Corporation (UWCRC) driving downtown redevelopment.

world knowledge.Name: Kiftsgate Court Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kiftsgate Court Gardens was created by three generations of women gardeners, starting with Heather Muir in the 1920s, continued by Diany Binny from 1950, and now maintained by Anne Chambers and her husband. The gardens are famed for their roses and have evolved over time with significant contributions from each generation. The house, Kiftsgate Court, was built in 1887-91 by Sydney Graves Hamilton, incorporating a Georgian facade moved from Mickleton Manor.

Major_Events.Description: Sydney Graves Hamilton built Kiftsgate Court, moving a Georgian facade from Mickleton Manor to the new site on Glyde Hill.
Heather Muir began creating the gardens, starting with a lawn, steps, and planting borders.
Anne and Jonathan Chambers undertook major modernization of the house, creating a separate flat and tea room.
The famous Kiftsgate rose, a scented climbing rose, was planted and later named by Graham Stuart Thomas in 1951.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Kiftsgate Court features a Georgian facade with a high portico, originally part of Mickleton Manor, moved to the new site. A large Victorian back was built behind the Georgian facade. The house has undergone internal alterations, including the division of a large ballroom into bedrooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kiftsgate Court Gardens is culturally significant for its beautiful and influential garden design, created by three generations of women gardeners. The gardens are famed for their roses and have been inspired by and compared to the nearby Hidcote Manor Garden. The Kiftsgate rose, one of the largest in Britain, is a notable feature.
world knowledge.Details: The gardens at Kiftsgate are known for their skilled color work and lush plantings, including the famous Kiftsgate rose, which is shade-tolerant and very vigorous. The garden's design was influenced by Hidcote Manor but is considered less formally planned. The Kiftsgate Hundred stone, an ancient meeting place for elders, stands nearby in Weston Park Wood.

world knowledge.Name: Puente de Piedra
world knowledge.Address: Connects Jirón Trujillo (Lima) and Jirón de la Unión (Rímac)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stone Bridge (Puente de Piedra) is a 17th-century bridge in Lima, Peru, connecting the districts of Lima and Rímac. It was built by architect Juan del Corral and was the city's only bridge until 1861. The bridge replaced an earlier 16th-century bridge destroyed by a flood in 1607. It played a crucial role in linking the northern and southern parts of the city and was a significant infrastructure project during the colonial era.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Spanish architect Juan del Corral during the mandate of Viceroy Juan de Mendoza y Luna, Marquis of Montesclaros.
A bronze statue of Felipe V, made by Baltazar Gavilán, was destroyed in an earthquake.
Important repairs were carried out during the viceroyalty of Joaquín de la Pezuela.
The bridge was widened and acquired its current form.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Vía Parque Rímac tunnel
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was lowered for the construction of the Vía Parque Rímac tunnel on the Yellow Line.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is made of stone masonry, and it was erroneously believed that the mortar was mixed with egg whites from sea birds to improve its consistency. It features a simple yet robust design typical of colonial-era infrastructure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant historical and cultural landmark, representing colonial-era engineering and urban development. It is part of Lima's historic centre, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The bridge also symbolizes the connection between the old walled city and the north bank of the Rímac River.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge connecting the districts of Lima and Rímac.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also known by several names, including Old Bridge (Puente Antiguo), Trujillo Bridge (Puente Trujillo), and Egg Bridge (Puente de Huevo). It was the only link between the north bank of the bridge and the old walled city until the 19th century. The bridge was declared a National and UNESCO World Heritage site in 1988.

world knowledge.Name: Shiraz Shahid Dastgheib International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shiraz International Airport is the main international airport of Fars province and the largest airport in the southern region of Iran. After undergoing renovation and redevelopment work in 2005, it was identified as the second most reliable and modern airport in Iran, after Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport, in terms of flight safety, including electronic and navigation control systems of its flight tower.

Major_Events.Description: The airport underwent renovation and redevelopment work, becoming the second most reliable and modern airport in Iran.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has two main passenger terminals connected to each other. Domestic Terminal or Terminal 1 is the older and larger, handling domestic flights within Iran. International Terminal or Terminal 2 is used for all scheduled and charter international flights. An international terminal is under construction for international flights, due to be built by 2024.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the main international airport of Fars province and the largest airport in the southern region of Iran, playing a crucial role in regional and international air travel.
world knowledge.Details: Shiraz International Airport (IATA: SYZ, ICAO: OISS) serves Shiraz and Fars. It is a hub for FlyPersia, Iran Airtour, Iran Aseman Airlines, and Pars Air. It is a focus city for Iran Air, Karun Airlines, Qeshm Air, and Taban Air. The airport has an elevation of 4,920 ft / 1,500 m and coordinates of 29°32′21″N 52°35′24″E. It has two runways with asphalt surfaces and handles significant passenger, aircraft, and cargo traffic.

world knowledge.Name: Auditorium Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Auditorium Theatre was designed by Dankmar Adler and Louis Sullivan and completed in 1889. It was built to make high culture available to the general public and to bolster Chicago's reputation after the Great Chicago Fire. The theatre hosted the Chicago Symphony Orchestra until 1904 and the Chicago Grand Opera Company until 1929. It was saved from demolition by Roosevelt University in 1946 and underwent major renovations in 1967.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre's grand opening featured performances and was attended by President Benjamin Harrison, Vice President Levi Morton, and other dignitaries.
The theatre was converted into a servicemen's center, housing and entertaining over 2.2 million servicemen.
After extensive renovations, the theatre reopened with a performance by the New York City Ballet.
The theatre hosted the NFL Draft for the first time outside New York City in fifty years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre is inspired by the Richardsonian Romanesque Style. It features 3,500 carbon filament light bulbs, unrivaled acoustics, air conditioning, 26 hydraulic lifts, and a 95-foot loft above the stage. The design emphasizes democratic seating with optimal sightlines for all patrons. The ornamentation includes natural elements like flowers and vines.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Auditorium Theatre is a landmark of architectural and cultural importance, representing Chicago's revival after the Great Fire and its commitment to making high culture accessible. It has hosted legendary performers and events, contributing to Chicago's reputation as a cultural hub.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre is owned by Roosevelt University and managed by an independent non-profit arts organization. It hosts over 200 performances annually, including dance, theater, and music. The venue also runs educational programs like 'Hearts to Art,' a summer camp for children who have lost a parent.

world knowledge.Name: Gwangju World Cup Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gwangju World Cup Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Gwangju, South Korea. It was initially named Gwangju World Cup Stadium to host some matches of the 2002 FIFA World Cup. In honour of the former South Korea national football team manager Guus Hiddink, who helped the team reach the World Cup semi-finals for the first time, the stadium is also called the Guus Hiddink Stadium.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted some matches of the 2002 FIFA World Cup.
Organised by Korea Foundation for International Culture Exchange.
Main venue of the 2015 Summer Universiade.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as it was a venue for the 2002 FIFA World Cup and is named in honour of Guus Hiddink, who played a pivotal role in South Korea's football history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is the home stadium of Gwangju FC of the K League and has a capacity of 40,245. It is managed by the Sports Support Division of the Culture & Sports Policy Office of the Gwangju Metropolitan City.

world knowledge.Name: Golden Ears Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Langley (south side) with Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge (north side)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 976 m (3,202 ft) (main spans), 2,410 m (7,910 ft) including approaches
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Golden Ears Bridge replaced a ferry service and was constructed to improve transportation across the Fraser River. It was named after the Golden Ears peaks in Golden Ears Provincial Park. The project involved significant archaeological discoveries, including 3,600-year-old artifacts.

Major_Events.Description: Construction officially began in June 2006.
Opened to traffic on June 16, 2009, replacing the Albion Ferry.
All tolls were removed starting September 1, 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Extradosed bridge design with six lanes, bike-pedestrian protected lanes, and eight pylons (four reaching 90 m high). Features golden metal eagle sculptures. Longest extradosed bridge in North America.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named after a local landmark and reflects the region's natural beauty. It also uncovered archaeological evidence of early indigenous farming practices.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (vehicles, pedestrians, bicycles) across the Fraser River.

Details.Toll_History: Initially tolled electronically, but tolls were removed in 2017. Bicycles, pedestrians, emergency vehicles, and TransLink buses were exempt.
Details.Traffic_Data: Averages 30,000 trips per weekday. Annual trips exceed 10 million, far surpassing the previous ferry traffic.
Details.Archaeological_Findings: Pottery shards, metal implements, and 3,600-year-old wapato (potatoes) were discovered during construction.
Details.Controversies: Criticism from the Coast Salish Katzie Nation regarding disturbance of a burial ground, and disputes over foreign labor usage during construction.

world knowledge.Name: Fernsehturm Stuttgart
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fernsehturm Stuttgart is a 216.61 m telecommunications tower in Stuttgart, Germany. It was the first telecommunications tower in the world constructed from reinforced concrete, serving as a prototype for many such towers worldwide. Although controversial at first due to its construction method and cost, it quickly became a well-known landmark of Stuttgart and a tourist attraction. The tower is located on the hill Hoher Bopser in the southern Stuttgart borough of Degerloch.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was completed and placed in service by Süddeutscher Rundfunk (today Südwestrundfunk – SWR).
The tower reached its current height of 216.61 m after the antenna was extended.
The tower was part of the German state visit of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom.
The tower was closed to the public for a review of fire safety regulations.
The tower was reopened with a refurbished entrance, shop area, and new fire safety precautions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is built in the Modernism architectural style, using reinforced concrete. It features an observation deck and carries conventional red air traffic warning lights along with three rotating xenon lamps similar to those used on lighthouses just above the observation deck.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fernsehturm Stuttgart is culturally significant as it was the first telecommunications tower in the world constructed from reinforced concrete, serving as a prototype for many such towers worldwide. It is a well-known landmark of Stuttgart and a popular tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The tower is located on the hill Hoher Bopser in the southern Stuttgart borough of Degerloch. It offers views of Stuttgart, from the forests and vineyards in and around Stuttgart to the Swabian Jura and the Black Forest. The Waldau-Stadion (Gazi-Stadion auf der Waldau) is located near the tower. The tower's construction was controversial due to its cost and new building method. Revenues from visitors reached the construction cost of 4.2 million DM within five years. The tower was closed to the public in 2013 for a fire safety review and reopened in 2016 with new safety precautions. Today, the tower only broadcasts several public FM radio stations, as the transmission of the ARD TV network's analogue service stopped in 2006.

world knowledge.Name: Varanasi Cricket Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Rajatalab area, beside Ring Road Phase-2, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Announced in April 2023, the Varanasi International Cricket Stadium is currently under construction and expected to be completed by December 2025. The foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 23 September 2023.

Major_Events.Description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone in the presence of cricket veterans like Sachin Tendulkar, Sunil Gavaskar, Ravi Shastri, and Dilip Vengsarkar, along with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and BCCI officials.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium's design draws inspiration from Lord Shiva, featuring trident-shaped floodlights, crescent-shaped roof covers, ghat-steps like seating arrangements, Bilva-patra shaped metallic sheets on the facade, and a Damaru-shaped media center.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Located in the holy city of Varanasi, the stadium's design pays homage to Lord Shiva, reflecting the city's spiritual and cultural heritage.

Details.Owner: Larsen and Toubro (for 30 years under Public-Private Partnership)
Details.Operator: Larsen and Toubro (for 30 years under Public-Private Partnership)
Details.Tenants: Kashi Rudras Uttar Pradesh cricket team, India national cricket team
Details.Facilities: 9 practice wickets, advanced drainage system, one outdoor ground, sufficient parking space, VVIP/VIP zone on the second floor of the south pavilion
Details.Connectivity: Well-connected to the city's airport, major railway stations, and bus station

world knowledge.Name: Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 16 km (9.9 mi) south-east of center of Budapest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Budapest Ferihegy International Airport, it was renamed in 2011 after Hungarian composer Franz Liszt. The airport was built to replace the obsolete Budaörs Airport and has since become the largest commercial airport in Hungary.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed in honor of Hungarian composer Franz Liszt on his 200th birthday.
The collapse of Malév, the national carrier, led to a significant drop in aircraft movements and cargo handling.
Sky Court, a new expansion project connecting Terminals 2A and 2B, was opened, increasing the airport's capacity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two runways and multiple terminals, including Terminal 2A and Terminal 2B. The design of the original traffic building was inspired by an aircraft from a top-side view.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a major hub for international travel in Hungary and serves as a key gateway to Central and Eastern Europe. It is named after Franz Liszt, a prominent figure in Hungarian culture.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is the headquarters and primary hub for Wizz Air and a base for Ryanair. It offers international connections primarily within Europe, but also to Africa, the Middle East, and the Far East. The airport has undergone several expansions and modernizations, including the construction of Sky Court and the refurbishment of Terminals 2A and 2B.

image_name: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology

world knowledge.Name: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology
world knowledge.Address: University Avenue, Kumargaon, Jalalabad Police Station, Sylhet, Bangladesh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1986, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST) is a public research university located in Kumargaon, Sylhet, Bangladesh. It is one of the leading universities in pioneering research and education in the physical sciences and engineering in the country. SUST was the first university in Bangladesh to adopt the American credit system and has been a pioneer in various academic and technological advancements.

Major_Events.Description: The first convocation of SUST was held on 29 April 1998.
The second convocation of SUST was held on 6 December 2007.
The third convocation of SUST was held on 8 January 2020.
The team from SUST became the world champion of NASA Space Apps Challenge among 1,395 local winning teams from around the world.
Seven teams from SUST got place among finalist 88 and achieved 15th spot in the world (highest individual achievement of an Asian University).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university campus spans 320 acres with a mix of modern and traditional architectural styles. The Central Library is known for its triangular shape.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SUST is often referred to as the 'Stanford of the East' due to its pioneering contributions in science and technology. It has a significant impact on the educational and technological landscape of Bangladesh.
world knowledge.Details: SUST is the first public university to introduce undergraduate programs in Software Engineering in Bangladesh. It has 28 departments under seven schools and six affiliated medical colleges. The university is known for its high research expenditure and has numerous academic and research collaborations with international institutes.

world knowledge.Name: Rafah Border Crossing
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rafah Border Crossing is the sole crossing point between Egypt and Palestine's Gaza Strip. It was opened by Israel after the 1979 peace treaty and remained under Israeli control until 2005, when it was transferred to Egyptian, Palestinian Authority, and EU control. Hamas' seizure of Gaza in 2007 led to a blockade, with the crossing opening only intermittently. Israel took control again in 2024 during the Gaza war but withdrew in 2025 as part of a ceasefire agreement.

Major_Events.Description: The crossing was opened by Israel after the 1979 peace treaty with Egypt.
Control was transferred to Egyptian, Palestinian Authority, and EU authorities.
After Hamas seized Gaza, Israel imposed a blockade, and Egypt closed the crossing, allowing only intermittent openings.
Israel took control of the crossing during the Rafah offensive but withdrew in 2025 as part of a ceasefire agreement.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The crossing includes the original Rafah land port (Salah al Din Gate) and a newer crossing point referred to as Al Awda (The Return). A commercial gate (Salah al-Din Gate) was opened in 2018 for truck traffic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rafah Border Crossing is a critical lifeline for Palestinians in Gaza, serving as the primary entry and exit point for people and goods. Its operation and control have been central to geopolitical tensions involving Israel, Egypt, Hamas, and the Palestinian Authority.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Border crossing for passengers and goods between Egypt and Gaza.
world knowledge.Details: The crossing has been a focal point of political and humanitarian issues, with frequent closures due to conflicts, blockades, and diplomatic disputes. It has also been used for smuggling tunnels and aid deliveries during crises. Egypt maintains control but requires Israeli approval for imports. The crossing's operation has varied under different Egyptian and Palestinian political regimes.

world knowledge.Name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
world knowledge.Address: 200 N. Arthur Ashe Blvd., Richmond, VA 23220
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Virginia Museum of Fine Arts (VMFA) was established in 1936, originating from a 1919 donation of 50 paintings by Judge John Barton Payne. It was one of the first state-funded art museums in the American South. The museum has undergone several expansions and now houses over 22,000 works, including significant collections of Fabergé eggs, modern and contemporary art, and African art. It is known for its innovative programs, such as the first 'Artmobile' in 1953 and extended night hours in 1960.

Major_Events.Description: The museum opened on January 16, 1936, designed by Peebles and Ferguson Architects in Georgian Revival and English Renaissance Revival styles.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition of the Lillian Thomas Pratt Fabergé collection
Major_Events.Description: The museum received a collection of 150 jeweled objects by Peter Carl Fabergé, including the largest public collection of Fabergé eggs outside Russia.
The world's first mobile tractor-trailer exhibit, bringing art to rural areas.
A $150-million expansion adding 165,000 square feet of gallery space, featuring a glass-walled atrium and a new sculpture garden.

Major_Events.Event: Installation of 'Rumors of War' by Kehinde Wiley
Major_Events.Description: A large-scale bronze sculpture commissioned by the museum, inspired by Confederate statues on Richmond's Monument Avenue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original building features Georgian Revival and English Renaissance Revival styles, influenced by architects Inigo Jones and Christopher Wren. Subsequent expansions include modernist and contemporary designs, such as the 2010 McGlothlin Wing with its glass-walled atrium and cascading fountain sculpture garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: VMFA is one of the largest art museums in North America by exhibition space and is notable for its comprehensive collections, free admission policy, and innovative programs. It anchors Richmond's Museum District and has played a key role in promoting arts education and accessibility in Virginia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Art museum and cultural center, featuring permanent and temporary exhibitions, educational programs, and performing arts events.
world knowledge.Details: The museum offers free admission except for special exhibits. It includes the Leslie Cheek Theater, a performing-arts venue, and has a fellowship program supporting Virginia artists. VMFA is accredited by the American Alliance of Museums and is a member of the French Regional & American Museums Exchange (FRAME).

world knowledge.Name: U2 Tower
world knowledge.Address: Corner of Sir John Rogerson's Quay and Britain Quay, South Docklands (SODO), Dublin, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The U2 Tower was a proposed skyscraper in Dublin, Ireland, intended to be the tallest building on the island. It was part of a regeneration effort by the Dublin Docklands Development Authority (DDDA) to transform the Docklands area. The project involved the rock group U2, who planned to have a recording studio in the building. The project faced multiple delays, design changes, and controversies before being cancelled in 2008 due to economic downturns. Later revival attempts also failed.

Major_Events.Description: The DDDA announced an architectural design competition for the tower, initially planned to be 60 metres tall, housing apartments and a penthouse recording studio for U2.
The initial winning design was disqualified after the DDDA lost the details of the submitting firm. A new winner, Burdon Dunne/Craig Henry (BCDH Architects), was later announced.
The DDDA revised the height of the U2 Tower from 60 metres to 120 metres, intending it to form a landmark entry with the also-cancelled Watchtower.
The DDDA's application for planning permission was approved, further increasing the tower's height to 130 metres.

Major_Events.Event: Design Change to Foster and Partners
Major_Events.Description: The winning bid for construction selected a new design by Norman Foster of Foster and Partners, replacing the original BCDH design.
The Dublin Docklands Development Authority announced the cancellation of the project due to unfavorable economic conditions.
The U2 Tower land was handed over to the National Asset Management Agency (NAMA) to settle debts.
Reports emerged of a plan to revive the project with a shorter 18-story tower, but this was later abandoned in favor of the Capital Dock development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The final design by Foster and Partners featured a tilted triangular shape with luxury apartments, a public viewing platform at 100m, and an acoustically insulated egg-shaped pod for U2's recording studio. The east and west facades had a crinkled 'fish scale' design with concealed balconies, while the north facade was sleek. The building was to include wind turbines and solar panels for energy generation. The structure would have straddled Sir John Rogerson's Quay, allowing traffic to pass beneath.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The U2 Tower was intended to be a landmark symbolizing Dublin's modernization and cultural vibrancy, partly due to its association with the globally renowned rock band U2. It also represented the DDDA's ambitious urban regeneration plans for the Docklands area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mixed-use: Residential apartments (luxury), commercial premises, and a recording studio for U2.
world knowledge.Details: The project faced controversies, including conflicts of interest (U2's involvement in the bidding consortium and familial ties between U2's manager and the original architect), community opposition over height and social housing concerns, and financial viability issues during the 2007-2008 economic crisis. The site is now occupied by the 79-metre Capital Dock development.

world knowledge.Name: Atakule
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Atakule is a 125 m high communications and observation tower located in the Çankaya district of central Ankara, Turkey. It was designed by architect Ragıp Buluç and opened on 13 October 1989 by President Turgut Özal. The tower is one of the primary landmarks of the city and can be spotted from almost anywhere in Ankara during clear days.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was officially opened by President Turgut Özal on 13 October 1989.
The shopping mall adjacent to the tower, Atrium, was closed due to loss of popularity and is now being rebuilt as a contemporary style shopping mall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower's design was created by architect Ragıp Buluç. It features an open terrace and a revolving restaurant named Sevilla, which makes a 360-degree rotation in one hour. Above Sevilla is another restaurant, Dome, located directly under the cupola. Under the terrace is a café named UFO. The bottom structures house a shopping mall and several indoor and outdoor restaurants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Atakule is one of the primary landmarks of Ankara and a symbol of the city. The name 'Atakule' combines 'Ata,' meaning 'ancestor' or 'father' (often referring to Mustafa Kemal Atatürk), and 'kule,' meaning 'tower,' reflecting its cultural and historical importance in Turkey.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Observation tower, Communications tower, Shopping mall, Restaurant
world knowledge.Details: The shopping mall adjacent to the tower, Atrium, was the first modern mall in Ankara and the second in Turkey after Galleria in Istanbul. It was opened on 13 October 1989 but was later closed due to competition from more modern shopping malls. The tower is now open to visitors after the rebuilding works of the shopping mall were completed. Atakule is very similar to Milad Tower in the capital of Iran.

world knowledge.Name: Funtown Splashtown USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Funtown Splashtown USA is a family-owned amusement park that began as Marvel Drive-In, a drive-in restaurant opened by Ken and Violet Cormier in 1960. Over the years, it expanded with additions like a mini-golf course, go-kart track, and various rides. In 1967, Ken Cormier and Andre Dallaire formed a partnership to establish Funtown USA, which later became Funtown Splashtown USA in 1996 with the addition of a waterpark.

Major_Events.Description: Ken and Violet Cormier opened Marvel Drive-In, marking the beginning of what would become Funtown Splashtown USA.
Ken Cormier and Andre Dallaire formed a partnership to establish Funtown USA, adding rides like the Zipper and Bayern Kurve.
Ken Cormier bought out the remaining Dallaire interest and renamed the park to Funtown Splashtown USA with the addition of a waterpark.
An expansion doubled the size of the waterpark and added two new thrill slides, Tornado and Mammoth.
An additional expansion added another 6 thrill slides to Splashtown.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of kiddie and carnival-style rides, a wooden roller coaster (Excalibur), a log flume (Thunder Falls), a drop tower (Dragon's Descent), and an indoor Scrambler (Astrosphere) with a laser and light show. The waterpark includes Pirate's Paradise, an interactive playground, and various water slides and pools.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Funtown Splashtown USA is a significant family entertainment destination in Northern New England, known for its rides and waterpark attractions. It represents the evolution of a small drive-in restaurant into a major amusement park, reflecting the growth of family-oriented entertainment in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The park features Northern New England’s tallest and longest wooden roller coaster, Excalibur, as well as New England's longest and tallest log flume, Thunder Falls. It also has a 220-foot-tall (67 m) Drop Tower called Dragon's Descent. The Astrosphere, an indoor Scrambler, is one of the park's most popular rides, featuring a state-of-the-art laser and light show. The Splashtown area includes Pirate's Paradise and various thrill slides.

world knowledge.Name: Trukhaniv Island
world knowledge.Address: Dnieper River, opposite Podil neighbourhood, Kyiv
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The island's name is derived from Tugor-khan, a historical figure. It came under the control of the Pustynno-Mykilsky monastery in 1534 and was returned to the city in 1698. The first buildings were erected in the early 19th century, and businesses appeared in the 1880s. During WWII, German forces destroyed the island settlements. Post-war, it was developed as a leisure center.

Major_Events.Description: Tourists visiting for the Eurovision Song Contest were housed on Trukhaniv Island.
Tourists visiting for the UEFA Euro 2012 were housed on Trukhaniv Island.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island is mostly covered by greenery and features leisure facilities such as cafés, restaurants, and sports complexes. The Park Pedestrian Bridge, built in 1957, connects the island to the mainland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Trukhaniv Island is a popular leisure destination with historical roots dating back to the medieval period. It is significant for its recreational facilities and its role in hosting tourists during major international events.
world knowledge.Details: The island is split by the distributary Bobrovnia, separating it into Ilya Muromets Island (north) and Trukhaniv Island (south). It is part of the Dnieper River's system of islands and is known for its clean beaches and outdoor activities like biking and cross-country skiing.

world knowledge.Name: Radin Inten II Airport
world knowledge.Address: Jalan Branti Raya, Branti, Natar, South Lampung Regency, Lampung, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Radin Inten II Airport, formerly Branti Airport, was built by the Japanese in 1942 during World War II to combat the Allied forces. It served as a home base for several Japanese airplanes and warplanes. After Indonesia declared independence, the airport was taken over by the Indonesian Air Force. In 1955, management was handed over to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The airport was handed over to the Lampung Residency in 1963. The runway and apron were completed in 1976, and the runway was extended in 1984-1987. A new terminal was inaugurated in 1995, and the airport was renamed Radin Inten II Airport. The terminal was expanded in 2016 to serve an estimated 3 million passengers. The airport served international routes from 2017 to 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The construction of the runway and apron was completed and inaugurated in June 1976 using the Fokker-28 MK-3000 aircraft.
The runway was extended by 330 meters to 1,850 meters.
A new terminal was completed and inaugurated by Minister of Transport Haryanto Dhanutirto on May 22, 1995. The airport was renamed Radin Inten II Airport.
The airport terminal was increased to three floors to serve an estimated 3 million passengers, with a four-storey parking building to accommodate 1000 vehicles.
On 2 April 2024, the Ministry of Transportation revoked the international status of the airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a three-floor terminal building and a four-storey parking building. The runway is 3,000 meters long with an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Radin Inten II (1834–1858), the last Sultan of Lampung. It is the only commercial airport in the Lampung province, serving as a crucial transportation hub for the region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by Puspa Jaya Taxi company from the first flight to the last flight daily. Taxes: Domestic - Rp 25,000, International - Rp 100,000. The Ministry of Transportation planned to build a railway line from Tanjung Karang to Radin Inten II Branti South Lampung to support development as an international airport, but this is unlikely to proceed now that the international status has been revoked.

world knowledge.Name: Langkawi Sky Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 125 m (410 ft) long, 1.8 m (5.9 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Langkawi Sky Bridge is a curved pedestrian cable-stayed bridge completed in 2005. It was designed to maximize the viewing experience, providing shifting perspectives as visitors walk along the bridge. The bridge was pre-fabricated in segments and lifted to the top of the mountain using Russian Kamov helicopters. It was constructed in 12 months and opened to the public in February 2005. The bridge was closed in July 2012 for maintenance and upgrading, partially reopening in February 2015 and fully accessible thereafter.

Major_Events.Description: The Langkawi Sky Bridge was officially opened to the public on February 27, 2005.
The bridge was closed in July 2012 for maintenance, upgrading, and structural strengthening.
The bridge partially reopened in February 2015 after maintenance, with full access restored later.
The SkyGlide, an inclined elevator linking the Langkawi Cable Car's Top Station to the Sky Bridge, opened in December 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a curved pedestrian cable-stayed bridge, 125 meters long and 1.8 meters wide, with five 25 m sections. It features steel railings and wire meshes on both sides. The bridge deck is suspended by four pairs of front-stay cables connected to an 81.5 m high single pylon. The design includes a wider curved central section connected to curved and straight sections, with triangular viewing platforms at each end. The bridge was pre-fabricated in segments and assembled on-site using helicopters and conventional winch systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Langkawi Sky Bridge is a significant tourist attraction in Malaysia, offering breathtaking views of the Langkawi archipelago. It has been featured in several films, including the 2006 Indian movie 'Don: The Chase Begins Again' and the 2007 Tamil movie 'Billa'. The bridge's unique design and construction have made it an engineering marvel and a symbol of modern architectural innovation in Malaysia.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is accessible via the Langkawi Cable Car to the Top Station, where visitors can take the SkyGlide inclined lift down to the bridge. A cheaper alternative is to walk 10–20 minutes along a steep mountain track. The bridge can carry up to 250 people and offers a unique viewing experience with its curved design and elevated position at 660 m above sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Vancouver City Hall
world knowledge.Address: 453 West 12th Avenue Vancouver, British Columbia V5Y 1V4
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vancouver City Hall is home to Vancouver City Council. The building was ordered by the Vancouver Civic Building Committee, designed by architect Fred Townley and Matheson, and built by Carter, Halls, Aldinger and Company. The building has a 12-storey tower with a clock on the top. The original City Hall was located on Main Street between 1897 and 1929. In 1929, City Hall moved into the Holden Building. After being elected mayor in 1934, Gerry McGeer appointed a committee to select the location for a new city hall. The panel recommended the Strathcona Park site, and City Council approved the selection in 1935. Construction began in 1936 and was completed the same year. George Clark Miller became the first mayor to occupy the new city hall in 1937. A four-storey east wing was added in 1968-1970. The original building was declared a Schedule A heritage building in 1976.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the new City Hall began on January 3, 1936, during Vancouver's Golden Jubilee.
The first cornerstone was laid by Mayor Gerry McGeer on July 2, 1936.
A 2.4-metre statue of Capt. George Vancouver, by Charles Marega, was unveiled on August 20, 1936, by the visiting Lord Mayor of London, Percy Vincent.
Construction was completed on December 1, 1936, and the building was opened in the same year.
George Clark Miller became the first mayor of Vancouver to occupy the new city hall on January 2, 1937.
Construction on a four-storey east wing was begun in 1968 and completed in 1970.
The original building was declared a Schedule A heritage building in March 1976.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Deco style, 12-storey tower (98 metres tall) with a clock on the top. The ceiling on the second floor of the rotunda was made of gold leaf from several British Columbia mines. Each lock plate on the outer doors displays the Vancouver Coat of Arms, and each door knob bears the monogram of the building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vancouver City Hall is culturally and historically significant as it was the first major Canadian city hall to be located outside its downtown. The building represents the growth and development of Vancouver and is a symbol of civic pride. The statue of Capt. George Vancouver and the gifts from the Lord Mayor of London, including a civic mace and a sprig from a tree in Isaac Newton's orchard, add to its historical value.
