world knowledge.Primary_Function: City hall, home to Vancouver City Council
world knowledge.Details: The building is served by Broadway–City Hall station on the SkyTrain's Canada Line. In 2012, city staff gradually started moving out when a study found it would not withstand an earthquake. A coat of arms was added in 1969.

world knowledge.Name: Kenroku-en
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kenroku-en, originally developed by the Maeda clan during the Edo period, is one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan. It evolved from the 1620s to the 1840s, with significant developments like the Tatsumi water channel in 1632 and the Renchitei garden in 1676. The garden was destroyed by fire in 1759 but was restored and expanded over the years, culminating in its public opening in 1874. It was designated a National Site of Scenic Beauty in 1922 and a National Site of Special Scenic Beauty in 1985.

Major_Events.Description: Completed by Maeda Toshitsune, this feature was later incorporated into the garden's waterways in 1822.
Built by the 5th daimyō Maeda Tsunanori, this garden was named Renchitei (lotus pond) and was later destroyed by fire in 1759.
Nearly the entire garden was destroyed, but the Shigure-tei teahouse survived.
Restoration began in 1774 under the 11th daimyō Harunaga, with further improvements like winding streams and expanded ponds completed by the 13th daimyō Nariyasu.
The garden was opened to the public on May 7, 1874.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as National Site of Scenic Beauty
Major_Events.Description: Recognized for its beauty and historical significance.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as National Site of Special Scenic Beauty
Major_Events.Description: Further recognition of its exceptional scenic and cultural value.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Kenroku-en is a strolling-style Japanese garden featuring meandering paths, a large pond, tea houses, and one of Japan's oldest fountains. The design incorporates the six attributes of a perfect landscape: spaciousness, seclusion, artifice, antiquity, waterways, and panoramas. Notable features include the Emerald Waterfall, Yugao-tei teahouse, and the Kaiseki Pagoda.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kenroku-en is considered one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan and is renowned for its beauty across all seasons. It represents the pinnacle of Japanese garden design, balancing the six contrasting attributes of an ideal landscape. The garden is a symbol of the cultural and historical legacy of the Maeda clan and the Edo period.
world knowledge.Details: Kenroku-en contains roughly 8,750 trees and 183 species of plants. It is particularly famous for its yukitsuri (snow ropes) in winter, which protect tree branches from heavy snow. The garden's name, meaning 'Garden of Six Attributes,' was inspired by a classical Chinese text and reflects its harmonious design. The grounds are open year-round during daylight hours with paid admission.

world knowledge.Name: Waseca County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Waseca County Courthouse was built in 1897 as the seat of government for Waseca County. The county seat was originally in Wilton but was moved to Waseca in 1870 after a popular vote due to the town's growth spurred by the Winona and St. Peter Railroad. The current courthouse replaced an earlier facility.

Major_Events.Description: The county seat was moved from Wilton to Waseca following a popular vote, driven by the town's growth due to the railroad. Records and furniture were moved overnight, and the new facility opened the next day.
The current Richardsonian Romanesque courthouse was built to replace the earlier facility, designed by Orff & Joralemon and constructed by J.D. Carroll for $55,833.

Major_Events.Event: National Register of Historic Places Designation
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its state-level significance in architecture and politics/government.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Two-story building of Kasota limestone and buff-colored brick with a large bell- and clock-tower. Features polished granite columns supporting triple arches at the entrance, wainscoting, oak woodwork, tiled fireplaces, etched glass, paneled doors, and marble flooring.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its Richardsonian Romanesque architecture and its role in the political and governmental history of Waseca County. Its construction marked the culmination of efforts to establish Waseca as the county seat.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of government for Waseca County
world knowledge.Details: Designed by Minneapolis architects Orff and Joralemon and constructed by J.D. Carroll of St. Paul Park. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982 (NRHP reference No. 82003070).

world knowledge.Name: Royal Armoury of Turin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Armoury of Turin, founded by Charles Albert, king of Sardinia, and opened to the public in 1837, is one of the world's most important collections of arms and armour. It is part of the Musei Reali di Torino, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997. The museum is housed in the Galleria Beaumont, designed by Filippo Juvarra in 1733 and decorated by Claudio Francesco Beaumont. The collection includes weapons and armour from the Savoy family, as well as prestigious diplomatic gifts and acquisitions from private collections.

Major_Events.Description: The Royal Armoury was founded by Charles Albert, king of Sardinia, and opened to the public.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion in UNESCO World Heritage list
Major_Events.Description: The Musei Reali di Torino, including the Royal Armoury, was included on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the Galleria Beaumont, designed by Filippo Juvarra in 1733 and decorated by Claudio Francesco Beaumont. The gallery features oil paintings on the ceiling depicting Stories of Aeneas and was completed by Benedetto Alfieri in 1762.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Royal Armoury of Turin is culturally significant as it houses one of the world's most important collections of arms and armour, reflecting the military history and heritage of the Savoy family and the kingdom of Sardinia. It is also part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Musei Reali di Torino.
world knowledge.Details: The collection includes the sword of San Maurizio, a 14th-century enamel horse bit from Naples, a 16th-century pistol belonging to Emperor Charles V, and weapons owned by Napoleon and the kings of Italy. The museum also features European, American, and oriental arms and armour.

world knowledge.Name: Bamboo Forest (Kyoto, Japan)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bamboo Forest, also known as Arashiyama Bamboo Grove or Sagano Bamboo Forest, is a natural bamboo forest in Arashiyama, Kyoto, Japan. It consists mostly of mōsō bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) and has several pathways for tourists and visitors. The Ministry of the Environment considers it a part of the soundscape of Japan.

Major_Events.Description: Prior to 2015, there was a charge to access the forest.
In the 2014 Indian film Jilla, the song "Kandangi Kandangi", performed by actor Vijay alongside singer Shreya Ghoshal, includes a segment filmed at the Sagano Bamboo Forest.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural bamboo forest with pathways for visitors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is considered part of the soundscape of Japan by the Ministry of the Environment. It is also located near significant cultural sites like the Tenryū-ji temple and the Nonomiya Shrine.
world knowledge.Details: The region experiences unpredictable weather, with a cool climate and bright sunlight. The summers are short, hot, and mostly cloudy. The winters are cold, windy, and partly cloudy. It is also wet year-round. Over the course of the year, the temperature typically ranges from 32 °F (0 °C) to 89 °F (32 °C). The summers last for approximately two months, from late June until mid-September, with an average daily high temperature above 80 °F (27 °C). The winters last for approximately three months, from early December to mid-March, with an average daily high temperature below 53 °F (12 °C).

world knowledge.Name: Neon Museum
world knowledge.Address: 770 North Las Vegas Boulevard, Las Vegas, Nevada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Neon Museum in Las Vegas, Nevada, features signs from old casinos and other businesses displayed outdoors. Efforts to establish a neon sign museum were underway in the late 1980s, but stalled due to a lack of resources. On September 18, 1996, the Las Vegas City Council voted to fund such a project, to be known as The Neon Museum. The organization started out by re-installing old signage in downtown Las Vegas, to attract more visitors to the area. Young Electric Sign Company (YESCO) had manufactured many neon signs in the city, and the company had a storage site for old signs, which would eventually become part of the Neon Museum collection. In 2000, as YESCO prepared to close its storage lot, the city provided the museum with land to start its own. Tours of the new site, known as the Neon Boneyard, began in 2001, by appointment only. The lobby of the former La Concha Motel, located on the Las Vegas Strip, was donated to the museum and moved there in 2006, eventually becoming its visitor center. Construction to convert the lobby began in May 2011, and the museum officially opened to the general public on October 27, 2012, eliminating the appointment system.

Major_Events.Description: The Las Vegas City Council approved the use of $150,000 in redevelopment funds toward the establishment of the Neon Museum.

Major_Events.Event: First project for the Neon Museum
Major_Events.Description: The Hacienda resort's Horse & Rider sign was refurbished and re-installed at the intersection of North Las Vegas Boulevard and Fremont Street.

Major_Events.Event: Neon Boneyard opens to the public
Major_Events.Description: Tours of the Neon Boneyard began by appointment only.
The Doumani family donated the shell-shaped lobby of the La Concha Motel to the museum, which was moved to the museum site in 2006.

Major_Events.Event: Public opening of the Neon Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum officially opened to the general public on October 27, 2012, eliminating the appointment-only system.
The museum announced plans to relocate to two larger, nearby sites within 18b The Las Vegas Arts District, with an expected opening around 2027.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum features a collection of vintage neon signs from old casinos and businesses, displayed outdoors in the Neon Boneyard. The visitor center is housed in the relocated lobby of the former La Concha Motel, which has a unique shell-shaped design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Neon Museum preserves the history of neon signage in Las Vegas, which dates back to the 1920s and became iconic in the city's identity, particularly for its hotel-casinos. The museum plays a key role in cultural preservation and education about the art and technology of neon signs.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes more than 200 signs, with some dating back to the 1930s. The oldest piece is a sign remnant from the Green Shack restaurant. The museum also hosts events such as weddings and art exhibits, including 'Lost Vegas: Tim Burton' in 2019-2020. A projection mapping show titled 'Brilliant!' reanimates unlit signs in the North Gallery. The museum receives approximately 200,000 visitors annually and plans to relocate to larger sites by 2027.

world knowledge.Name: Beaulieu Palace House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beaulieu Palace House is a 13th-century house in Beaulieu, Hampshire, United Kingdom. Originally part of Beaulieu Abbey, the estate was bought in 1538 by Thomas Wriothesley, 1st Earl of Southampton, following the Dissolution of the Monasteries. It is still owned and occupied by the earl's descendants, the Barons Montagu of Beaulieu. The house was extended in the 16th century, and again in the 19th century, and is today a fine example of a Gothic country house.

Major_Events.Description: King James stayed at Beaulieu in August 1613 and gave an audience to the Venetian ambassador Antonio Foscarini.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house was extended in the 16th century, and again in the 19th century, and is today a fine example of a Gothic country house. The inside of the house has been kept in a Victorian style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Beaulieu Palace House is culturally significant as it is a fine example of a Gothic country house and has been home to the Montagu family for centuries. It is also part of the Treasure Houses of England consortium.
world knowledge.Details: Although still home to the current Lord and Lady Montagu, parts of the house and gardens are open daily to the public. It is a member of the Treasure Houses of England consortium. Beaulieu is considered one of the most haunted places in Britain, with numerous paranormal investigations conducted at the site, including by Arthur Conan Doyle.

world knowledge.Name: Emirates Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Emirates Stadium, known as Arsenal Stadium for UEFA competitions, is a football stadium in Holloway, London, England. It has been the home stadium of Arsenal Football Club since its completion in 2006. The stadium was built to replace Arsenal's former home, Highbury, after the club was denied planning permission to expand Highbury. The relocation was considered the biggest decision in Arsenal's history since the appointment of Herbert Chapman in the 1920s. The stadium project faced financial difficulties but was completed in 2006 at a cost of £390 million. The stadium has been nicknamed "the Carpet" due to the quality of its pitch and groundsmanship.

Major_Events.Description: The Emirates Stadium was officially opened by Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh on 26 October 2006. The stadium hosted three non-full capacity events prior to its official opening, including Dennis Bergkamp's testimonial match against Ajax on 22 July 2006.
The record attendance of 60,383 was set during a Premier League match between Arsenal and Wolverhampton Wanderers on 2 November 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Emirates Stadium is a four-tiered bowl with translucent polycarbonate roofing over the stands but not over the pitch. The roof is supported by four triangular trusses made of welded tubular steel. The stadium features glass and steel construction, designed to sparkle in sunlight and glow at night. The pitch is 105 by 68 metres, and the stadium includes facilities for fans with disabilities, a sensory room, and 241 wheelchair accessible seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Emirates Stadium is culturally significant as the home of Arsenal Football Club, one of the most successful football clubs in England. The stadium hosts international football fixtures, music concerts, and other major events. It has undergone a process of "Arsenalisation" to restore visible links to Arsenal's history, including the installation of murals, statues, and other tributes to the club's heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The Emirates Stadium has a current seated capacity of 60,704, making it one of the largest football stadiums in England. The stadium is served by several London Underground stations, including Arsenal, Highbury & Islington, and Holloway Road. The stadium has been used for international football matches, music concerts, and as a conference centre. It has hosted bands such as Coldplay, Bruce Springsteen, and Green Day. The stadium is also known for its high-quality pitch, which has earned it the nickname "the Carpet."

world knowledge.Name: Werribee Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Werribee Park is the estate of a historical building in Werribee, Victoria, Australia. It was built by pioneering pastoralists Thomas Chirnside and his brother Andrew Chirnside from Scotland. The mansion and associated facilities were listed on the Victorian Heritage Register on 1 April 1987. From 1923 to 1973, it served as a Catholic seminary, Corpus Christi College. The Victoria State Government purchased the park in 1973, and it was opened as a tourist attraction in 1977.

Major_Events.Description: The park was purchased by the Victoria State Government.
The park was opened to the public as a tourist attraction.
The Werribee Park Mansion hosted two Elton John concerts as part of his Rocket Man Solo Tour.

Major_Events.Event: Let Them Eat Cake music festival
Major_Events.Description: The Werribee Mansion Grounds began hosting the Let Them Eat Cake music festival on New Year's Day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Italianate-style mansion built of brick with solid Barrabool-hill freestone facings. Designed by James H. Fox and constructed by Parlane Colquhoun.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Werribee Park is culturally significant as a historical estate showcasing the wealth and influence of the Chirnside family, pioneers of the pastoral industry in Victoria. It is also significant for its architectural style, its role as a Catholic seminary, and its current use as a tourist attraction and event venue.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private mansion, later a Catholic seminary, and now a tourist attraction and event venue.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes Werribee Park Mansion, the Victoria State Rose Garden, formal gardens, the Werribee Park National Equestrian Centre, the Werribee Open Range Zoo, a contemporary sculpture walk, and a natural riverine area. It also features the Mansion Hotel and Conference Centre. The Werribee Park Heritage Orchard, dating from the 1870s, is being restored by a community group. The estate hosts annual events such as the Werribee Christmas Carols, the harvest festival, the polo championships, and the Let Them Eat Cake music festival.

world knowledge.Name: Lido, Belgrade
world knowledge.Address: Great War Island, Zemun, Belgrade, Serbia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Small sandy beach, temporarily expanded by 300 meters in 2022
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lido is a non-residential urban neighborhood located on the northern tip of the Great War Island on the Danube. It was used as a beach by Zemun's residents before World War I and was officially arranged after the war. Named after the Lido in Venice, it was developed as a wild beach alternative to Ada Ciganlija. Despite its popularity among Zemun's inhabitants, it never matched Ada Ciganlija's fame. The beach suffered significant damage during the 2006 floods, with much of its infrastructure washed away. Efforts to restore and improve the beach were made in 2007 and 2008, including the reintroduction of a pontoon bridge and the addition of lifeguard services.

Major_Events.Description: The organization of the festival went disastrously due to bad weather and financial malversations of the organizers.
The floods washed away much of Lido's infrastructure, leading to a significant drop in visitors. The beach was not restored until 2007.
The Yugoslav army placed a pontoon bridge for the first time, relocated from Ada Ciganlija. The bridge has been placed each summer since 1996, except from 2006 to 2008 due to the floods.
Low water levels in the Danube temporarily expanded the beach by 300 meters and reduced water depth to knee-deep for over 200 meters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Lido is a small, pointed sandy beach with minimal accommodations, including several restaurants. It lacks permanent structures due to legal protections on the Great War Island.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lido is culturally significant as a historic and popular beach among Zemun's residents, offering an alternative to the more famous Ada Ciganlija. Despite its challenges, it remains a cherished recreational spot.
world knowledge.Details: Lido is accessible by boat or a seasonal pontoon bridge laid by the Serbian Armed Forces from July to September. The bridge is 375 meters long and often causes protests from local boatmen. The beach saw a temporary expansion in 2022 due to drought conditions.

world knowledge.Name: Felbrigg Hall
world knowledge.Address: Near Felbrigg village, South West of Cromer, Norfolk
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Felbrigg Hall is a 17th-century English country house near the village of that name in Norfolk. Part of a National Trust property, the unaltered 17th-century house is noted for its Jacobean architecture and fine Georgian interior. The estate originated with the Felbrigg family and passed to the Wyndham family, who built the hall. The last owner, Robert Wyndham Ketton-Cremer, bequeathed the estate to the National Trust in 1969.

Major_Events.Description: Robert Wyndham Ketton-Cremer, the last owner, left the estate to the National Trust upon his death.
The National Trust highlighted LGBT themes at Felbrigg Hall, including the widely known homosexuality of Robert Wyndham Ketton-Cremer.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house features Jacobean architecture with a fine Georgian interior. Above the entablature, the family arms and the projecting bays bear the words 'GLORIA DEO IN EXCELSIS' in pierced stone, surmounted by heraldic beasts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Felbrigg Hall is culturally significant for its well-preserved 17th-century architecture and its historical association with the Wyndham family. It is also notable for its gardens and the Great Wood, which is a Site of Special Scientific Interest.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a walled garden, an orangery, and orchards. The gardens are Grade II* listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. The estate is open to the public, with access to the grounds and several waymarked walks, including the Weavers' Way long-distance footpath. The National Trust's 'Prejudice and Pride' campaign in 2017 highlighted LGBT themes at the property, leading to some controversy.

world knowledge.Name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
world knowledge.Address: Padmanabhapuram, Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu, India
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Complex inside a granite fortress around four kilometers long
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed in 1601 by Iravi Varma Kulasekhara Perumal, the palace was rebuilt around 1750 by King Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma, who dedicated the kingdom to Lord Padmanabha. The capital of Travancore was shifted to Thiruvananthapuram in 1795, leading to the palace's decline. In 1935, it was converted into a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was converted into a museum with support from the Travancore royal family.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Traditional Kerala architecture with structures like the four-storeyed building, Thekkae Kottaram, and Uppirikka Malika. Features include murals, herbal and medicinal wood bedsteads, and built-in recesses for weapons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is a prime example of traditional Kerala architecture and holds historical importance as the former capital of Travancore. It was dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, symbolizing the kingdom's devotion.
world knowledge.Details: The palace complex includes several structures such as the four-storeyed building, Thekkae Kottaram, and Uppirikka Malika. It is maintained by the Archaeology Department of the Kerala Government despite being located in Tamil Nadu.

world knowledge.Name: Stade Pierre-Mauroy
world knowledge.Address: 261 boulevard de Tournai, 59650 Villeneuve-d'Ascq, Nord, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stade Pierre-Mauroy, initially named Grand Stade Lille Métropole, was renamed in 2013 after the former Mayor of Lille and Prime Minister of France, Pierre Mauroy. It was built to replace the outdated Stade Grimonprez-Jooris, which did not meet UEFA standards. The project faced delays due to preservationist concerns but was eventually completed in 2012. The stadium has since hosted major events like UEFA Euro 2016, the 2023 Rugby World Cup, and will host events for the 2024 Summer Olympics.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium hosted several matches during the UEFA Euro 2016 tournament.
The stadium was one of the venues for the 2023 Rugby World Cup.
The stadium will host basketball and handball tournaments for the 2024 Summer Olympics.
The knock-out phase of EuroBasket 2015 was held at the stadium, including the final.
The stadium hosted several matches during the 2017 World Men's Handball Championship.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a retractable roof that opens and shuts in 15 minutes, and a unique hydraulic system that lifts half of the field to create a lower-level floor for indoor events. It has two main levels: the Grand Stade with a capacity of 50,186 seats and the Boîte à Spectacles, which can be configured for 6,900 to 30,000 seats. The stadium is also an HQE Building with solar panels and windmills for electrical supply.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Stade Pierre-Mauroy is a symbol of modern engineering and multi-purpose functionality, hosting major sports events, concerts, and cultural shows. It is a key venue for French football and rugby, and its retractable roof and adjustable seating make it a versatile landmark in European sports infrastructure.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use retractable roof stadium for sports, concerts, and cultural events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a seating capacity of 50,186, making it the fourth-largest in France. It is the home of French professional football club Lille. The total construction cost was €618 million, funded by the city of Lille, LOSC, and the Nord-Pas-de-Calais regional council. The stadium is fully accessible by metro and road, with 7,000 parking spaces.

world knowledge.Name: University of Hamburg
world knowledge.Address: Moorweide opposite Hamburg Dammtor station, Rotherbaum, Hamburg, Germany
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Over 180 properties scattered throughout the city
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Hamburg was founded on 28 March 1919 by combining the previous General Lecture System, the Hamburg Colonial Institute, and the Academic College. It has grown to become one of the largest universities in Germany, with significant historical events shaping its development, including its role during the Weimar Republic, the Nazi era, and post-World War II reforms.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the University of Hamburg
Major_Events.Description: The university was established by combining the General Lecture System, the Hamburg Colonial Institute, and the Academic College.
The university was heavily influenced by the Nazi regime, leading to the removal of books and the expulsion of numerous scholars.
The university reopened after World War II with 17,800 employees and 2,872 students.
The student movements led to significant structural reforms, including the dissolution of faculties and increased student involvement in administration.

Major_Events.Event: Merger with Hamburg University of Economy and Politics
Major_Events.Description: The two institutions were merged by a political act, restructuring the university into six faculties.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's main campus is located in the Rotherbaum quarter, featuring a mix of historical and modern buildings. Notable structures include the Main Building, the Auditorium, the Philosopher's Tower, and the Geomatikum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Hamburg is a major center for research and education in Germany, contributing significantly to the cultural and intellectual life of Hamburg. It has been associated with seven Nobel Prize winners and one Wolf Prize winner.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Hamburg offers 149 different majors across six faculties, with over 44,000 students and 5,500 doctoral candidates enrolled. It supports seven Collaborative Research Centers and is ranked among the top universities globally. The university also oversees three museums and the Hamburg State and University Library Carl von Ossietzky, which contains over 5 million volumes.

world knowledge.Name: Estrela Basilica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Estrela Basilica, also known as the Royal Basilica and Convent of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, was ordered built by Queen Maria I of Portugal as the fulfilment of a vow. It remains the most important architectural endeavour of her reign and was the first church in the world dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. The construction began in 1779 and was completed in 1789.

Major_Events.Description: The groundbreaking ceremony took place on 24 October 1779, with Queen Maria I's husband, Peter III, laying the first cornerstone.
The Basilica was consecrated on 15 November 1789.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Estrela Basilica features a late Baroque and Neoclassical style, with a giant dome, twin bell towers, and statues of saints and allegoric figures. The interior includes intricate geometric patterns made of grey, pink, and yellow marble, and several paintings by Pompeo Batoni.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Basilica is culturally and historically significant as it was the first church in the world dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and represents the most important architectural endeavour of Queen Maria I's reign. It also houses the tomb of Queen Maria I and a famous nativity scene by sculptor Joaquim Machado de Castro.
world knowledge.Details: The Basilica is located on a hill in the western part of Lisbon and can be viewed from far away. It includes a famous nativity scene with more than 500 figures in cork and terra cotta, and the tomb of Queen Maria I is in the right transept.

world knowledge.Name: Balbriggan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Balbriggan evolved from a small fishing village into a manufacturing and commercial hub, primarily due to the textile industry established by Baron George Hamilton in the late 18th century. It played a role in the Irish War of Independence, notably during the 'Sack of Balbriggan' in 1920. The town has a rich industrial heritage, particularly in cotton and linen production, and was once a holiday destination for Dubliners.

Major_Events.Description: A conflict between rival families and English forces during the medieval period.
Baron George Hamilton founded cotton factories, transforming the town's economy.
Black and Tans attacked the town, destroying homes and a factory, and killing two residents during the Irish War of Independence.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Balbriggan features a mix of historical and modern structures, including a 19th-century Martello Tower, the remnants of industrial mills, and St. George's Chapel (rebuilt after a fire). The town's layout reflects its development from a coastal village to a commuter suburb.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Balbriggan is notable for its industrial heritage, particularly in textile manufacturing (e.g., 'Balbriggans' underwear). It is also significant for its role in Irish history, including the War of Independence. The town's diverse population and cultural institutions reflect its evolving identity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historically an industrial and fishing town; now a commuter suburb of Dublin with cultural and recreational amenities.
Notable_Visitors: Queen Victoria (indirectly, as a wearer of 'Balbriggans')
Czarina of Russia (indirectly, as a wearer of 'Balbriggans')

Transport.Bus: Dublin Bus routes 33, 33A, 33X; Bus Éireann routes 101, B1

Education.Primary_Schools: Multiple (Roman Catholic, Church of Ireland, gaelscoil, Educate Together)

Sports.Soccer: Balbriggan FC, Glebe North FC, Hyde Park FC, etc.
Sports.Other: Cricket, golf, tennis, pitch and putt

Religious_Sites.Catholic: Church of Ss. Peter and Paul (with Harry Clarke stained glass)

world knowledge.Name: Patcham Place
world knowledge.Address: London Road, Patcham, Brighton and Hove BN1 8YD, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Patcham Place is a mansion built in 1558 as part of the Patcham Place estate. It was owned by Anthony Stapley, one of the signatories of King Charles I's death warrant. The house was extended and almost completely rebuilt in 1764. It has served various purposes, including as a youth hostel and is currently used as commercial premises. The parish of Patcham has Saxon origins, and the territory includes several valleys with intermittent streams. The manor of Patcham was held by William de Warenne, 1st Earl of Surrey at the time of the Domesday survey in 1086.

Major_Events.Description: Built for William West, 1st Baron De La Warr.
Major John Payne extended and rebuilt the house, eliminating traces of the 16th-century structure.
Patcham Place was listed Grade II* for its architectural and historical importance.
Brighton Corporation bought the house and its grounds for £6,000.
Brighton and Hove City Council sold the lease to Mark Ratcliffe, Chris Gargan, and Peter McDonnell for £1.3 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Patcham Place's present appearance is entirely 18th-century. Its style is Classical, featuring a three-bay pediment and Tuscan-columned entrance porch. The northwest and northeast walls are hung with glazed black mathematical tiles, a signature feature of Brighton buildings of the era. The roof is laid with slates and tiles. The interior includes large fireplaces, an ornate chimney-breast, and an elaborate stair-rail.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Patcham Place is listed Grade II* for its architectural and historical importance. It represents a significant example of 18th-century Classical architecture in Brighton and Hove and has connections to notable historical figures such as Anthony Stapley.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently used as commercial premises (head office of KSD Support Services Limited). Previously served as a youth hostel and private residence.
world knowledge.Details: The property was restored and is now used as a business and community centre. The parish of Patcham covers 4,325 acres of chalk downland north of Brighton and has Saxon origins. The Wellesbourne, 'Brighton's lost river', rises near the centre of the village and flows through the present city centre to the English Channel.

world knowledge.Name: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Quimper
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée des Beaux-Arts de Quimper was founded after Jean-Marie de Silguy left a legacy of 1200 paintings and 2000 drawings to the town of Quimper on condition that the town build a museum to accommodate them. The museum was built in Quimper's main square, facing the cathedral and adjacent to the Hôtel de Ville. The building's construction was left to architect Joseph Bigot in 1867, and the museum was opened on August 15, 1872. It was entirely renovated by architect Jean-Paul Philippon under the direction of André Cariou in 1993.

Major_Events.Description: Jean-Marie de Silguy left a legacy of 1200 paintings and 2000 drawings to the town of Quimper on condition that the town build a museum to accommodate them.
The museum was built by architect Joseph Bigot and opened on August 15, 1872.
The museum was entirely renovated by architect Jean-Paul Philippon under the direction of André Cariou, modernizing its architecture and improving the display of works.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was originally designed by Joseph Bigot in a traditional style, facing the cathedral and adjacent to the Hôtel de Ville. The 1993 renovation by Jean-Paul Philippon introduced modern architectural choices, focusing on transparency to better expose the works and improve the museum's functionality.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is one of the principal art museums in western France, with rich collections of French, Italian, Flemish, and Dutch paintings from the 14th century to the present day. It holds significant works from Breton painters and artists attracted by Brittany's landscapes and peasantry, including the School of Pont-Aven. The museum also features a dedicated space for Max Jacob, a Quimper native, and his entourage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include paintings and sculptures from the 14th to 20th centuries, drawings, prints, and antiques. It has an auditorium, a reception service, and a bookstore. A room is dedicated to Max Jacob, featuring his works and those of his entourage. The museum also displays an exceptional ensemble of Jean-Julien Lemordant’s paintings.

world knowledge.Name: Cedar Rapids Museum of Art
world knowledge.Address: 410 Third Avenue SE Cedar Rapids, Iowa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cedar Rapids Museum of Art is a museum in downtown Cedar Rapids, Iowa, United States. The museum is privately owned and was established in 1905. The museum acquired the old Cedar Rapids Public Library building after the library moved into a new location in 1985. The current home of the museum, designed by post-modern architect Charles Moore, was built adjoining the old library in 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The museum moved into a new building designed by architect Charles Moore, adjoining the old Cedar Rapids Public Library building.
The CRMA was given the building that houses the original studio of Grant Wood, located just three blocks from the Museum.

The downtown of Cedar Rapids was devastated by the worst flood in the city’s recorded history. The lower storage areas and basements of the Museum were severely damaged by flooding that also threatened the exhibition spaces. The Museum’s collection was moved to the higher levels and none of the artwork is known to have been damaged.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Post-modern design by architect Charles Moore, adjoining the old Cedar Rapids Public Library building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum has significant collections from several prominent Iowa artists, including the world's largest collection of works by Grant Wood, Marvin Cone, and Bertha Jaques. It also holds works by Mauricio Lasansky and the Riley Collection of ancient Roman portrait busts. The Grant Wood collection includes his paintings Woman with Plants and Young Corn.
world knowledge.Details: The mission of the Cedar Rapids Museum of Art is to excite, engage, and educate its community and visitors through its collection, exhibitions and programs. The Grant Wood Studio is open to the public for guided tours on Saturdays and Sundays. The museum also includes significant pieces by Mauricio Lasansky, Malvina Hoffman, Ann Royer, Carl Van Vechten and many others.

world knowledge.Name: Limbe Botanic Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Limbe Botanic Garden, originally created in 1892 during the German colonial era, was initially a trial garden for acclimatising tropical species like rubber, coffee, and cocoa. It became a major botanical garden under British administration post-1920, and after Cameroon's independence in 1961, it was managed by the government. The garden was renovated in 1988 through a partnership with the United Kingdom, shifting its focus from agriculture to conservation, education, science, tourism, and leisure.

Major_Events.Description: Established by a German team led by Paul Rudolph Preuss as a trial garden for tropical species.
The British took over the garden in collaboration with the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.
The garden was taken over by the Cameroonian government.
A partnership with the United Kingdom allowed for the garden's renovation and reorientation towards conservation, education, and tourism.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features landscaped tracks, a herbarium, and a cultural centre called 'Jungle Village.' Some original buildings have been repurposed, such as the laboratory and library, which were transformed into a hospital.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Limbe Botanic Garden is a significant cultural and historical site, representing Cameroon's colonial history and its transition to independence. It is a major tourist attraction and a centre for conservation and education.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Botanic garden, conservation, education, tourism, and leisure
world knowledge.Details: The garden houses around 1,500 taxa, including rare and threatened plants. It also contains a herbarium with over 30,000 specimens and the graves of Commonwealth soldiers from World Wars I and II. A luxury hotel is now located within the garden.

world knowledge.Name: Hinulugang Taktak
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 15 July 1952 (Recreation area) 18 September 1990 (National park) 17 November 2000 (Protected landscape)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hinulugang Taktak Protected Landscape, also known as Hinulugan Taktak, is a protected area in Rizal, Philippines. Initially assigned as a recreation area, the waterfall area has been designated as a national park by virtue of Republic Act No. 6964 in 1990. Ten years later, it became a protected landscape under Proclamation No. 412. It is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources and the Rizal Provincial Government. Folk knowledge has it that the name was derived from a large bell (taktak) that was thrown (hinulog) into the falls during the 15th century or the 16th century because the local villagers considered it too loud. Since then, it has become known as Hinulugang Taktak or the place where the bell fell.

Major_Events.Description: Designated as a national park by virtue of Republic Act No. 6964.
Became a protected landscape under Proclamation No. 412.
An oil spill forced the closure of the park, intensifying rehabilitation efforts.
Reopened to the public after a long year of rehabilitation, featuring new recreational activities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park contains the headwaters of the Sapang Baho River (also known as Antipolo River and Taktak River), which flows to Laguna de Bay through the Manggahan Floodway. The falls have a height of 21.5 meters (70.5 feet) and a width of 25.8 meters (84.6 feet). The rocks beneath the Quaternary soil are Miocene layers. However, the area is susceptible to erosion, landslides, and earthquakes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of Antipolo's iconic destinations, the other being the Antipolo Cathedral, Hinulugang Taktak is featured in the hymn Antipolo composed by German San Jose in 1929. The lyrics indicate that even at the time, it was already a popular recreational area.
world knowledge.Details: At least 11 species of trees can be found in the area, including Senna spectabilis, Cananga odorata, Swietenia macrophylla, Pterocarpus indicus, Chrysophyllum cainito, Artocarpus heterophyllus, Persea americana, Sandoricum koetjape, Mangifera indica, Averrhoa bilimbi, and Cocos nucifera. While there is no report of endemic or endangered species present, animal species in the area include Varanus salvator, Python reticulatus, and Draco volans. Starting in 2002, facilities began to be built as part of the continuing rehabilitation effort. Due to water pollution, the river itself was deemed unsafe for swimming. As an alternative, a nearby pool was constructed for swimmers. Private resorts and hotels have also been built near the area. Since its designation as a national park and its consequent rehabilitation, visitors have steadily increased from 45,563 in 1995 to 83,431 in 2004. This raised the profile of Hinulugang Taktak as the nation's second most popular national park, following the Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center. As of 2008, it recorded the third largest income for any protected area in the Philippines with 11.1 million pesos, following the Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center (first) and the Mount Apo Natural Park (second).

world knowledge.Name: Rajabhakti Park
world knowledge.Area: Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rajabhakti Park is a historically themed park honoring past Thai kings from the Sukhothai period to the current royal house of Chakri. It was built by the Royal Thai Army with funds donated by the public and private sectors. King Bhumibol Adulyadej named the park, which means 'the park that has been built with people's loyalty to the monarchs'.

Major_Events.Description: Crown Prince Maha Vajiralongkorn, accompanied by his daughter, Princess Bajrakitiyabha, presided over the park's opening ceremonies on 26 September 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features bronze statues of seven notable Thai kings, each with an average height of 13.9 meters, designed by Thailand's Fine Arts Department. The base of the statues is 134 m long, 43 m wide, and 8 m high, housing a museum of Thai history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it honors the legacy of Thai kings and serves as a symbol of loyalty to the monarchy. It also includes a museum focusing on the biographies and achievements of the seven kings on display.
world knowledge.Details: The park consists of three distinct areas: the statues of seven Thai kings, a museum, and a large plaza used for parades and ceremonies. There were controversies regarding funding and procurement, with allegations of kickbacks and shady dealings.

world knowledge.Name: Great Himalayan National Park
world knowledge.Address: Banjar sub-division of Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP) was established in 1984 and is located in the Banjar sub-division of Kullu in Himachal Pradesh, India. It spans an area of 1,171 km² with elevations ranging from 1,500 to 6,000 meters. The park is a habitat to numerous flora and over 375 fauna species, including 31 mammals, 181 birds, 3 reptiles, 9 amphibians, 11 annelids, 17 mollusks, and 127 insects. In June 2014, it was added to the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites for its outstanding significance for biodiversity conservation. The park is at the junction of the Indomalayan and Palearctic biogeographic realms, resulting in a unique biodiversity. The park's establishment involved a 20-year process, including surveys, community rights settlements, and conservation projects.

Major_Events.Description: Survey of the watersheds of Tirthan, Sainj, and Jiwanal in Banjar area of Kullu district.

Major_Events.Event: World Bank funds Conservation of Biodiversity project
Major_Events.Description: During this period, 16 village eco-development committees were founded to involve local communities in biodiversity conservation.

Major_Events.Event: GHNP instated as India’s newest national park
Major_Events.Description: Compensation awarded to local communities previously identified as having traditional forest rights.

Major_Events.Event: GHNP awarded World Heritage Natural Site status
Major_Events.Description: Awarded in the proceedings of the 38th World Heritage Committee meeting at Doha, Qatar.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse range of ecosystems, including alpine, glacial, temperate, and subtropical forests. It is characterized by its wide elevation range and relatively undisturbed habitats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The GHNP is culturally and historically significant due to its unique biodiversity and its role in conservation. It represents the westernmost extension of the Sino-Japanese Region and has common plant elements with the adjacent Western and Central Asiatic region. The park's biodiversity is a result of the geological evolution of the Himalayas.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of biodiversity, ecotourism.
world knowledge.Details: The GHNP supports a great diversity of plant life, from pines and spruces in the lower valleys to alpine herbs and junipers in higher elevations. It has emerged as a popular trekking and ecotourism destination, with several trekking routes ranging from day trips to multi-day treks. The park office at Sai Ropa issues permits for treks. Ecotourism and homestay tourism are also gaining popularity in areas near the park. The office of the Director, GHNP, is located at Shamshi in the Kullu valley.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Ciudad de los Deportes
world knowledge.Area: Ciudad de los Deportes, Mexico City
world knowledge.Address: Calle Indiana 255, Mexico City, Mexico C.P. 03810
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estadio Ciudad de los Deportes is a multi-purpose stadium in Mexico City, initially opened in 1946. It has undergone several renovations (1996, 2004, 2010) and has been home to football clubs like Club América and Cruz Azul. Plans for demolition were announced in 2016 but put on hold in 2018. The stadium faced closure in 2024 due to safety issues but reopened with new regulations.

Major_Events.Description: American football games held at the stadium.
Closed indefinitely on 2 November 2024 due to lack of safety certifications and infrastructure problems. Reopened on 7 November with new regulations.
Cruz Azul announced relocation to Estadio Olímpico Universitario on 8 January 2025.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built as a pit with the playing field below street level. Features 92 executive suites and a capacity of 34,253 seats.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Mexico City, hosting football and American football events. It is located beside Plaza México, the world's largest bullring, adding to its cultural and sports importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for association football and American football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has faced challenges such as complex traffic patterns and parking facilities, which prevented it from hosting World Cup matches. Recent renovations aimed to improve safety and comfort for fans. Adjacent to Plaza México, the world's largest bullring.

world knowledge.Name: Cape Hatteras
world knowledge.Location: Hatteras Island, Dare County, North Carolina, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Part of Cape Hatteras National Seashore, which includes parts of Bodie Island, Hatteras Island, and Ocracoke Island
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cape Hatteras is a cape located at a pronounced bend in Hatteras Island, one of the barrier islands of North Carolina. The treacherous waters off the coast of the Outer Banks are known as the Graveyard of the Atlantic, with over 600 ships wrecked here due to shallow shoals, storms, and war. The first lighthouse at the cape was built in 1803, and the current Cape Hatteras Lighthouse was built in 1870. The cape has been shaped by wind, waves, and storms, and is part of the Cape Hatteras National Seashore.

Major_Events.Description: Devastated the entire Outer Banks and split Hatteras Island between the towns of Frisco and Hatteras. NC 12 was washed out, creating a new inlet that took nearly two months to fill.
Made landfall at Cape Hatteras, causing significant damage.
The lighthouse was lifted and moved inland 2,900 feet due to the receding shoreline.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Cape Hatteras Lighthouse is the tallest lighthouse in the United States, standing at 198.48 feet from the ground to the tip of its lightning rod. It is one of the tallest brick lighthouses in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cape Hatteras is culturally and historically significant due to its role in maritime history, its treacherous waters known as the Graveyard of the Atlantic, and its iconic lighthouse. It is also a key part of the Cape Hatteras National Seashore, protecting unique ecosystems and providing recreational opportunities.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigation aid for mariners, conservation of natural and cultural resources, and recreational use.

Details.Climate: Cape Hatteras has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cfa), with long, hot summers and short, mild winters. It is the wettest coastal location in North Carolina, with over 61 inches of precipitation per year.
Details.Wildlife: The cape is the northern limit of tropical fauna.
Details.SOSUS Facility: From 1956 to 1982, the Naval Facility Cape Hatteras served as a shore terminal for the Atlantic Sound Surveillance System (SOSUS).
Details.Education: Residents are zoned to Dare County Schools, including Cape Hatteras Elementary School and Cape Hatteras Secondary School.

world knowledge.Name: North Carolina Museum of Art
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The North Carolina Museum of Art (NCMA) was established in 1947 as the first major museum collection in the country to be formed by state legislation and funding. It opened in 1956 and has since grown to encompass a collection spanning over 5,000 years of artistic work. The museum's current location on Blue Ridge Road was opened in 1983, designed by Edward Durrell Stone and Associates. A major expansion in 2010 added the West Building, designed by Thomas Phifer and Partners.

Major_Events.Description: The state legislature appropriated $1 million to purchase a collection of artworks for the people of North Carolina, matched by a gift of 71 works from the Samuel H. Kress Foundation.
The museum opened in the renovated State Highway Division Building on Morgan Street in downtown Raleigh.
The museum moved to its current location on Blue Ridge Road, designed by Edward Durrell Stone and Associates.
The museum opened the new 127,000-square-foot West Building, designed by Thomas Phifer and Partners, and transformed the East Building into a center for temporary exhibitions and public programs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's West Building features anodized aluminum panels with steel bands and a roof with parabolic-shaped coffers that admit natural light. The East Building, originally designed by Edward Durrell Stone, uses a square as a basic unit for spatial experimentation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The NCMA is a model of enlightened public policy with free admission to the permanent collection. It houses a diverse collection spanning over 5,000 years of artistic work and is one of the leading art museums in the American South. The museum's Judaic Art Gallery is one of only two in an American art museum.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's permanent collection includes European paintings, Egyptian funerary art, ancient Greek and Roman artifacts, American art, African art, ancient American art, and contemporary art. The Museum Park features over a dozen site-specific works of art and two miles of trails. The museum also hosts outdoor movies and concerts at the Joseph M. Bryan, Jr., Amphitheater.

world knowledge.Name: Ardabil University of Medical Sciences
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ardabil University of Medical Sciences is a medical university in Ardabil province of Iran established in 1993.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is a significant institution for medical education in Ardabil province, contributing to the region's healthcare and academic development.
world knowledge.Details: This university has over 3400 students studying in six Schools in Ardabil city including Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, Nursing & Midwifery, health and international Pardis schools. In addition, there are two academic units in other cities of Ardabil province including, nursing college of Germi, health educational institution of Meshkinshahr.

world knowledge.Name: Samaria Gorge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Samariá Gorge became a National Park of Greece in 1962 and is a World's Biosphere Reserve. It was created by a small river running between the White Mountains and Mt. Volakias. The village of Samariá, located within the gorge, was abandoned in 1962 to make way for the park.

Major_Events.Description: The gorge was designated as a National Park of Greece to protect its unique ecosystem and as a refuge for the rare kri-kri (Cretan goat).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural gorge with steep sides, reaching up to 300 meters in height, and narrowing to a width of only four meters at the 'Gates'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gorge is a major tourist attraction and an important natural reserve, home to several endemic species, including the kri-kri. It is also culturally significant due to the ancient church Óssia María, from which the gorge and village derive their names.
world knowledge.Details: The walk through the gorge is 15 km long, starting at an altitude of 1,250 m and ending at the shores of the Libyan Sea in Agia Roumeli. Visitors can complete the hike in five to seven hours, and local tourist operators provide organized tours. Ferries from Agia Roumeli to nearby villages are available for return trips.

world knowledge.Name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
world knowledge.Address: 3000 North Meridian Street, Indianapolis, Indiana, 46208-4716, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1925 by Mary Stewart Carey, the museum is the world's largest children's museum. It moved to its current location in 1946, and the current building was constructed in 1976 with several expansions since then. The museum focuses on family learning with interactive exhibits.

Major_Events.Description: Founded by Mary Stewart Carey with support from local civic leaders and organizations.
The museum relocated to its current location on North Meridian Street.
The current museum building was completed, featuring modern facilities and expanded exhibit space.
The Dinosphere exhibit underwent a $27.5 million renovation as part of the Mission Jurassic initiative, adding new exhibits about the Jurassic period.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Five floors of exhibit halls with a central spiral ramp. Features include a glass sculpture by Dale Chihuly, a large-format theater (formerly CineDome), and a mix of modern and historic architectural elements. The museum includes interactive and immersive exhibit spaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is a world leader in children's education and interactive exhibits. It has been ranked as the best children's museum in the U.S. and is accredited by the American Alliance of Museums. It plays a significant role in family learning and community engagement.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Children's museum focused on interactive learning and family engagement.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features over 130,000 artifacts divided into Arts & Humanities and Natural Sciences. Key exhibits include Dinosphere, a carousel, a steam locomotive, and the Fireworks of Glass Tower. It hosts thousands of annual activities, including plays, workshops, and traveling exhibits. The museum also has a branch of the Indianapolis Public Library called the InfoZone.

world knowledge.Name: Burton Agnes Manor House
world knowledge.Address: Burton Agnes, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built between 1170 and 1180 by Roger de Stuteville, the manor house and village were named after his daughter. It passed through the Somerville and Griffith families by marriage. Sir Walter Griffith restored the hall and added the present roof in the 15th century. In 1654, the estate passed to Sir Francis Boynton and remains in the Boynton family's ownership.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Roger de Stuteville.
Sir Walter Griffith restored the hall and added the present roof.
Estate passed from Sir Henry Griffith to his nephew Sir Francis Boynton.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Norman manor house with a well-preserved Norman undercroft; later encased in 18th-century brickwork. Much of the undercroft is built with local chalk.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A surviving example of a Norman manor house, now a Grade I listed building, reflecting medieval architecture and historical family ownership.
world knowledge.Details: Open to the public from 11 am to 5 pm from April to October.

world knowledge.Name: Aleksandar Nikolić Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Aleksandar Nikolić Hall, formerly known as Pionir Hall, is an indoor sports arena located in Palilula, Belgrade, Serbia. It was renamed in 2016 in honor of Serbian basketball player and coach Aleksandar Nikolić. Constructed in 1973 by Ljiljana and Dragoljub Bakić, the modernist building won the architects a 'Grand Prix of the Belgrade Architecture Salon'. The structure was noted for its use of repeated elements and natural light.

Major_Events.Description: The arena hosted the final round of EuroBasket 1975.
The final of the EuroLeague's 1976–77 season took place here, where Maccabi Tel Aviv defeated Pallacanestro Varese.
The FIBA EuroCup's 1997–98 season final was held in the arena.
The 16th World Judo Championships took place in Pionir Hall.
The arena hosted several preliminary round games of EuroBasket 2005.

Major_Events.Event: 2013 World Women's Handball Championship Preliminary Round
Major_Events.Description: The arena hosted several preliminary round games of the 2013 World Women's Handball Championship.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Aleksandar Nikolić Hall
Major_Events.Description: The name of the arena was changed from Pionir Hall to Hall Aleksandar Nikolić, after the former basketball player and coach, Aleksandar 'Aca' Nikolić.
The arena played host to the Davis Cup World Group Quarterfinal between Serbia and Spain, with Serbia winning the tie 4-1 to advance to the semifinals.

The hall was thoroughly renovated, at a cost of €2 million euros. The renovation included new seats, telescopic stands, a new hardwood court and screens, new lighting, modernization of the ventilation and air-conditioning systems, and an increased seating capacity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The modernist building was constructed with repeated elements and natural light, designed by Ljiljana and Dragoljub Bakić.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The hall is well known for its frequent matches between different basketball clubs, especially Crvena Zvezda (Red Star Belgrade), Partizan, and foreign clubs. It has been described as the 'architectural icon of the postmodernist Belgrade'.
world knowledge.Details: The official seating capacity of the arena is 8,000. It was projected by Ljiljana and Dragoljub Bakić and constructed under a tight deadline. The general contractor was Energoprojekt. The hall is owned by the City of Belgrade and operated by Tašmajdan SRC.

world knowledge.Name: Fox Theatre (Detroit)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fox Theatre is a performing arts center opened in 1928 as a flagship movie palace in the Fox Theatres chain. It was the largest theater in Detroit with over 5,000 seats. Designed by architect C. Howard Crane, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1985 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 1989. The theater underwent a full restoration in 1988 after being closed in the early 1980s.

Major_Events.Description: Featured the silent film 'Street Angel' starring Janet Gaynor and a live show depicting the history of Detroit.
Hosted three performances by Elvis Presley in May 1956.
The theater was fully restored and reopened with a concert featuring Joe Williams and the Count Basie Orchestra.
Hosted the WWE Hall of Fame ceremony the night before WrestleMania 23.
Hosted a two-night primary debate among candidates for the Democratic nomination for the 2020 presidential race.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in Art Deco style with a blend of Burmese, Indian, Persian, Chinese, and Hindu motifs. The interior features three levels of seating, ornate plasterwork, vermillion scagliola columns, and a grand lobby with terrazzo floors. The exterior includes a 10-story office building with Asian motifs. The theater also houses a 4-manual 36-rank Wurlitzer organ, one of the few remaining in its original installation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fox Theatre is the largest surviving movie palace of the 1920s and a prime example of exotic theatrical architecture. It played a significant role in Detroit's cultural life, hosting premieres, concerts, and performances by notable artists. Its restoration in the 1980s helped revitalize the surrounding area, now nicknamed Foxtown.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts center and live event venue
world knowledge.Details: The Fox Theatre has a seating capacity of 5,174 (including removable seats in the orchestra pit). It is part of the original Fox Theatres chain built by William Fox in the late 1920s. The adjacent office building houses the headquarters of Olympia Entertainment and Little Caesars. The theater has hosted a wide range of events, from concerts and films to Broadway shows and political debates. The marquee was updated in 2015 with digital video screens and LEDs.

world knowledge.Name: Pembroke House, Whitehall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pembroke House was the London residence of the earls of Pembroke. It was built on ground leased by the earl amidst the ruins of parts of Whitehall Palace that burned down in 1698. The house underwent a major rebuild in 1756–59 and was later used by the French Ambassador. The lease was renewed multiple times until it became crown freehold around 1853, housing various ministries before being demolished in 1938 to build the Ministry of Defence main building.

Major_Events.Description: Built by the architect earl Henry Herbert, under Colen Campbell and his assistant Roger Morris.
Major rebuild by the 10th Earl.
Demolished to build the Ministry of Defence main building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Henry Herbert, possibly inspired the 9th earl's designs for Marble Hill House. Gardens were created in 1818 by demolishing the house's riding-house and stables.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pembroke House was a significant residence for the earls of Pembroke and later housed important government ministries. Some rooms survive as 'Historic Rooms' within the MOD building.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residence for the earls of Pembroke, later used by government ministries.
world knowledge.Details: The house was the subject of a major rebuild in 1756–59 and was used by the French Ambassador in 1762. The lease passed to the Earl of Harrington before becoming crown freehold. Some rooms from Pembroke House survive within the MOD building.

world knowledge.Name: Silver Mine Bay Beach
world knowledge.Address: Tung Wan Tau Road, Mui Wo, Lantau Island, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The beach is named "Silver Mine Bay" because there was a silver mine in Mui Wo in the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The beach underwent improvement works from 21 November 2016 to July 2018, which included a new barbecue pit area, a sitting-out area, and a viewing deck near the beach’s entrance. The new facilities were officially opened on 22 July 2018, and lifeguard services were introduced for the first time at the beach.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The beach is a popular recreational spot managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department of the Hong Kong Government, offering views of Hei Ling Chau and featuring calm sea conditions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational beach with barbecue pits and swimming facilities

Details.Water_Quality: Rated as good to fair by the Environmental Protection Department for its water quality in the past twenty years.

world knowledge.Name: City Park
world knowledge.Details: City Park can refer to multiple locations; specific details are not provided.

world knowledge.Name: Shanghai Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shanghai Museum is a municipal public museum of ancient Chinese art, founded in 1952. It was first open to the public in the former Shanghai Racecourse club house. The founding collections came from artifacts gathered by the Communist 3rd Field Army, confiscations by the customs service, and items sold by private collectors due to political pressure. The museum moved to the Zhonghui Building in 1959 and later to its current location in 1996. The museum's collections were enriched from private and institutional collections, and it played a role in rescuing artifacts during political campaigns like the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded with collections from various sources, including artifacts gathered by the Communist 3rd Field Army and confiscations by the customs service.
The museum moved into the Zhonghui Building at 16 South Henan Road, which housed insurance companies and bank offices.
The museum was rebuilt at its current location on People's Square, funded by donations and government support, and designed by architect Xing Tonghe.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is designed in the shape of an ancient bronze cooking vessel called a ding, inspired by the Da Ke ding. It has a round top and a square base, symbolizing the ancient Chinese perception of the world as 'round sky, square earth'. The building is 29.5 meters high with five floors.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Shanghai Museum is one of China's most important museums, housing over 120,000 pieces of ancient Chinese art, including bronze, ceramics, calligraphy, and more. It holds items of national importance, such as a 'transparent' bronze mirror from the Han dynasty, and has a significant collection of ancient coins from the Silk Road.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has eleven galleries and three special temporary exhibition halls. It also houses an important collection of ancient coins from the Silk Road, donated by Linda and Roger Doo. The museum's director from 1985 to 1999, Ma Chengyuan, played a key role in securing its current location and funding.

world knowledge.Name: Parco della Musica
world knowledge.Address: Via Pietro de Coubertin, 30 00196 Rome, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Auditorium Parco della Musica is a public music complex in Rome, Italy, designed by Italian architect Renzo Piano. During construction, excavations uncovered the foundations of a villa and an oil-press dating from the sixth century BC. Renzo Piano adjusted his design scheme to accommodate the archaeological remains and included a small museum to house artifacts discovered, delaying the project's completion by a year.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Parco della Musica began on 15 January 1995.
Parco della Musica was opened on 21 April 2002.
Parco della Musica was inaugurated on 21 December 2002.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex features three concert halls (Sala Santa Cecilia, Sala Sinopoli, and Sala Petrassi) and an outdoor theater (Cavea). The halls are structurally separated for sound-proofing but joined at the base by a continuous lobby. Their outer architectural form has led to nicknames such as 'the blobs,' 'the beetles,' 'the turtles,' and 'the computer mouses.' The outdoor theater recalls ancient Greek or Roman performance spaces and is fan-shaped around a central piazza.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parco della Musica is home to most of the facilities of the Accademia Nazionale di Santa Cecilia. Within a few years of its inauguration, it became Europe's most-visited music facility. In 2014, it had over two million visitors, making it the second-most-visited cultural music venue in the world, after Lincoln Center in New York.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public music complex hosting concerts and cultural events
world knowledge.Details: The complex was designed by Renzo Piano, with Jürgen Reinhold of Müller-BBM in charge of acoustics for the halls and Franco Zagari as the landscape architect for the outdoor spaces. It lies with the Foro Italico in the north area of Rome's ancient center.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Cuscatlán
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Estadio Cuscatlán is a football stadium located in the city of San Salvador, El Salvador. It was inaugurated in 1976 as a replacement to what at the time was El Salvador's largest stadium, Estadio Nacional de la Flor Blanca. Its creation was made possible by EDESSA (Estadios Deportivos de El Salvador) who in 1969 first proposed the idea of a new national stadium.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was opened and held its first game on 24 July 1976, with German Bundesliga champions Borussia Mönchengladbach playing the El Salvador national team, ending 2–0 to the German side.
EDESSA agreed to and signed a 599-year lease of the stadium to CLIMA (Asociación de Clubes de Liga Mayor A'), making CLIMA the operator of the stadium.
Estadio Cuscatlán became the first football stadium in Central America and Caribbean to have a large LED screen.
During a game between Alianza F.C. and C.D. FAS, a crowd crush occurred resulting in twelve deaths and dozens of injuries due to fake tickets being sold.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a lawn and French drain field, digital and electronic scoreboard, and has undergone several renovations including the installation of a new 100m² 4K LED screen and 54 new 1,500-watt metal halide luminaires.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Estadio Cuscatlán is the largest football venue in El Salvador and Central America, meeting FIFA requirements for international matches. It is used for various events including concerts, cultural events, religious events, and political rallies.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a parking lot capacity of 8,500 cars and includes two other football pitches, one for training and one for junior football. It has been the site of various significant events, including a world record for the most people brushing their teeth at the same time in 2005.

world knowledge.Name: Manora Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Manora is a peninsula that forms a protective barrier between Karachi Harbour and the Arabian Sea. It was formerly an island but is now connected to the mainland by a natural sand bridge. The area was known to the ancient Greeks and was mentioned by the Ottoman admiral Seydi Ali Reis in 1554. Manora Fort was built by the Talpur dynasty in 1797 to protect the port from pirate raids. The British captured the fort in 1839 and later upgraded it. The Manora Point Lighthouse was completed in 1889. After Pakistan's independence, Manora became a main base for the Pakistan Navy.

Major_Events.Description: Built by the Talpur dynasty to protect the port from pirate raids.
British troops stormed the fort, which was lightly guarded, and quickly captured it.
Designed by Canadian engineer Alain-Chartier-de-Lotbiniere Joly de Lotbinière to assist vessels approaching Karachi harbor.
The resort was upgraded with modern features and inaugurated by Murad Ali Shah, Chief Minister of Sindh.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Manora Fort was initially built in the 1790s and later upgraded by the British and Pakistan Navy. The Manora Point Lighthouse has a tower 38 metres (125 ft) high, making it one of the tallest in Pakistan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Manora has historical significance as a protective barrier for Karachi Harbour and was mentioned in ancient Greek and Ottoman texts. It is also a popular tourist destination with sandy beaches and recreational facilities.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a protective fort and naval base, now also a tourist destination.
world knowledge.Details: Manora has a population of approximately 4,273 residents (as of 2017). The peninsula is home to several ethnic groups, including Sindhis, Punjabis, Kashmiris, Seraikis, Pakhtuns, Balochis, Brahuis, Memons, and Bohris. The western bay of the harbor contains mangrove forests, and the coastline is home to the Peelu tree (Salvadora persica) that protects Manora's coast from erosion. The area is also planned to be linked with a harbour-crossing bridge to reduce travel distance to Defence and Clifton areas.

world knowledge.Name: Causeway Point
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Causeway Point is the seventh largest suburban shopping mall in Singapore, completed in 1998. It was developed by Frasers Centrepoint after Centrepoint Properties Limited won a bid for the land in 1995. The mall officially opened on 30 May 1999 and underwent a $72 million renovation from late 2010 to 2013 to increase net property income and improve facilities.

Major_Events.Description: Causeway Point had its soft opening on 17 October 1998.
Causeway Point officially opened on 30 May 1999.
Causeway Point underwent a $72 million renovation aimed at increasing net property income and adding new facilities like playgrounds and relocating the main food court.
Cotton On closed down on 25 May 2024 after 14 years of operation at the mall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Causeway Point is a nine-story shopping mall with a total retail floor area of 420,000 square feet. It features a mix of retail, entertainment, food and beverage, and office spaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Causeway Point is culturally significant as the first major shopping mall in Woodlands, Singapore, and a key commercial hub in the northern region of the country.
world knowledge.Details: Causeway Point has 250 retail outlets spread over five floors and a basement. Major tenants include Cathay Cineplexes, FairPrice Finest, Metro, Food Republic, Cantine by Kopitiam, Courts, G2000, Sephora, and Uniqlo. It is located beside the Woodlands MRT station and the underground Woodlands Bus Interchange.

world knowledge.Name: Oregon State Capitol
world knowledge.Address: 900 Court Street NE, Salem, Oregon, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Oregon State Capitol is the third building to house the state government in Salem, following two previous capitols destroyed by fire in 1855 and 1935. The current building, constructed during the Great Depression, was partially financed by the federal government's Public Works Administration. It was designed in Art Deco and Stripped Classicism styles by architects Trowbridge & Livingston in association with Francis Keally.

Major_Events.Description: A fire started in the basement of the east wing, quickly spreading and destroying the building, leaving only the outer walls standing. The loss was estimated at $1.5 million, and the state did not carry insurance.
The current capitol was constructed at a cost of $2.5 million, with the federal government covering 45% of the cost. It was dedicated on October 1, 1938.
Wings were added to the capitol, doubling its floor space to about 233,750 square feet at a cost of $12.5 million.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake damaged the cupola, requiring closure for repairs. The rotunda area remained closed for approximately two years.
The building became the first state capitol in the U.S. to produce solar power through the use of 60 photovoltaic panels generating 7.8 kilowatts.
