Armed protesters demonstrated at the capitol against health restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic. A security video later showed a representative allowing protesters to enter the building, leading to his expulsion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Oregon State Capitol is designed in Art Deco and Stripped Classicism styles. The exterior is finished with Vermont marble, and the lobby, rotunda, and halls are lined with polished rose travertine stone from Montana. The building features a cupola topped with a gold Oregon Pioneer statue. The rotunda includes murals depicting moments from Oregon history, and the legislative chambers feature custom carpets and furniture made of golden oak and black walnut.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Oregon State Capitol is a symbol of the state's government and history. It houses the state legislature and the offices of the governor, secretary of state, and treasurer. The building and its grounds feature artwork, memorials, and native flora, reflecting Oregon's cultural and natural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The capitol grounds cover three city blocks and include Willson and Capitol parks, featuring artwork, fountains, and native trees. The building has undergone several renovations and expansions, with ongoing projects to address seismic upgrades, ADA accessibility, and other improvements. The Oregon State Capitol Foundation was established in 1997 to enhance the building's dignity and beauty and foster cultural and educational opportunities.

world knowledge.Name: Lee Valley Park
world knowledge.Address: Trailheads: East India Docks, Greater London, Ware, Hertfordshire
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lee Valley Regional Park is a 10,000-acre, 26 miles long linear park, much of it green spaces, running through the northeast of Greater London, Essex and Hertfordshire. The park follows the course of the River Lea (Lee) along the Lea Valley from Ware in Hertfordshire through Essex and the north east of Greater London, through the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park to East India Docks Basin on the River Thames.

Major_Events.Description: Much of the southern half of the Lee Valley Park was developed to form the Olympic Park for the 2012 Summer Olympics and 2012 Summer Paralympics. Lee Valley Park was extended through the Olympic Park down to the River Thames, adding a further 2 miles of open space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is made up of a diverse mix of countryside areas, urban green spaces, heritage sites, country parks, nature reserves and lakes and riverside trails, as well as leading sports centres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lee Valley Park is culturally significant as it is the largest park in Greater London, extending beyond Greater London's borders into the neighbouring counties of Hertfordshire and Essex. It played a crucial role in the 2012 Summer Olympics and 2012 Summer Paralympics.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational activities such as walking, cycling, sport, angling, birdwatching, boating, camping, horse riding, ice skating, and golf.
world knowledge.Details: The park is managed by Lee Valley Regional Park Authority and includes notable parts such as Myddelton House Gardens, Temple Mills, Hackney Marshes, Walthamstow Marshes, Tottenham Marshes, River Lee Country Park, Bow Creek Ecology Park and Lee Valley Reservoir Chain. It also contains major reservoirs and water courses. The park owns 35% of the Olympic Park and manages three venues following the London 2012 Games: Lee Valley White Water Centre, Lee Valley VeloPark, and the Eton Manor hockey and tennis centres.

image_name: Iglesia de San Antonio de Padua

world knowledge.Name: Iglesia de San Antonio de Padua
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iglesia Parroquial de San Antonio de Padua is a historic, Roman Catholic parish church in Guayama, Puerto Rico. The parish was erected in 1736 and the first church building completed no later than 1775. The original appearance of the building is unknown, but some of the eighteenth century walls may survive in the present structure. The building was rebuilt twice in the nineteenth century and the present appearance dates from 1874.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The church was inscribed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Eclectic, Romanesque
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The church is a historic Roman Catholic parish church with significant architectural and historical value in Puerto Rico.
world knowledge.Details: The parish was erected in 1736 and the first church building completed no later than 1775. The building was rebuilt twice in the nineteenth century and the present appearance dates from 1874. It takes an overall Romanesque form, while the details exhibit the eclecticism that characterized much Puerto Rican architecture in the later 1800s.

world knowledge.Name: Waikato Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: FMG Stadium Waikato, originally known as Rugby Park, opened in 1925. It has undergone significant upgrades and transformations, including a major rebuild in 2000–2002, to become a modern multi-purpose stadium. It has hosted numerous significant sporting and cultural events, including international rugby matches, FIFA tournaments, and the Rugby World Cup.

Major_Events.Event: First radio broadcast of a rugby union match
Major_Events.Description: A match between Waikato and Great Britain was broadcast on the radio in Hamilton.
Waikato defeated the visiting Springboks Rugby team in front of over 31,000 spectators.
A match was cancelled due to a pitch invasion by anti-tour protestors.
Rugby Park hosted its first Rugby World Cup match, Fiji vs. Argentina.
The newly rebuilt Waikato Stadium officially opened with a Super 12 rugby match.

Major_Events.Event: New Zealand Māori Rugby Union Team victory
Major_Events.Description: The New Zealand Māori Rugby Union Team secured their first-ever win over the British & Irish Lions.
Hosted six group matches and two quarter-finals.
Hosted three pool matches: Wales vs. Samoa, Wales vs. Fiji, and New Zealand vs. Japan.
Hosted the 2012 Super Rugby Final between the Chiefs and the Sharks.
Hosted two Group B games: Samoa vs. Tonga and New Zealand vs. Tonga.
The Tongan rugby league team defeated the Great Britain Lions.
Hosted five matches and the inter-confederation play-offs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a grass surface and includes multiple stands: The Brian Perry Stand, WEL Networks Stand, Goal Line Terrace, and Greenzone. It is designed as a rectangular stadium, primarily for football-based sports.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Waikato Stadium is a key venue for rugby union and other sports in New Zealand. It has hosted significant international events, including the Rugby World Cup and FIFA tournaments, making it a central part of Hamilton's sporting and cultural identity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily for rugby union and other sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a total capacity of 25,800, which can be extended to 30,800 with temporary seating. It is owned by the Hamilton City Council and is the home field for the Waikato Mitre 10 Cup team and the Chiefs Super Rugby team. It also hosts private functions and events in its various facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Mykonos-Manto Mavrogenous Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mykonos-Manto Mavrogenous Airport is the international airport of the Greek island of Mykonos, located 4 kilometres from the town of Mykonos. It serves flights to domestic and European metropolitan destinations due to the island being a popular leisure destination. The airport first operated in 1971. In December 2015, the privatisation of Mykonos International Airport and 13 other regional airports of Greece was finalised with the signing of the agreement between the Fraport AG/Copelouzos Group joint venture and the state privatisation fund. Fraport started managing the airport from 11 April 2017.

Major_Events.Description: The privatisation of Mykonos International Airport and 13 other regional airports of Greece was finalised with the signing of the agreement between the Fraport AG/Copelouzos Group joint venture and the state privatisation fund.

Fraport started managing the airport from 11 April 2017. Immediate actions included general clean-up, decreasing wait times to check in, reducing flight delays, upgrading sanitary facilities, and enhancing services including new free Internet connection (WiFi).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is significant for facilitating tourism and connectivity to Mykonos, a popular leisure destination in Greece.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves flights to domestic and European metropolitan destinations. During the off-peak tourist season, the airport has limited flight connections and operating hours. The transfer time from the town to the airport is about 10 minutes. Transit bus service is provided between the Airport and the city of Mykonos (Chora) and other destinations, only during the summer season. By car, Mykonos Airport is located 3.5 km from the city of Mykonos (Chora) and is easily accessible via Mykonos provincial road. 24/7 taxi service is available outside the Mykonos Airport Terminal building.

world knowledge.Name: Primatial Cathedral of Bogotá
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Metropolitan and Primate Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception and Saint Peter of Bogotá, known as the Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica of Bogotá, is a Neoclassical style building located in the Plaza de Bolívar. It was designed by Friar Domingo de Petrés and built between 1807 and 1823. The cathedral is the seat of the Metropolitan Archbishop of Bogotá and Primate of Colombia, recognized with the honorary title of Primate of Colombia by Pope Leo XIII in 1902. It was declared a National Monument in 1975.

Major_Events.Description: Celebrated by Friar Domingo de las Casas in a modest chapel of mud and straw roofs.
Initiated by Friar Juan de los Barrios, but the roof collapsed in 1560.
Pope Pius IV granted it the title of Cathedral.
A strong earthquake seriously affected the construction, leading to partial demolition in 1805.
The cathedral was consecrated after completion of construction.
Pope Leo XIII recognized the cathedral with the honorary title of Primate of Colombia.
The cathedral was declared a National Monument by decree 1,584.
The pipe organ underwent a restoration financed by the Colombian Ministry of Culture, the National Tourism Fund, and the Archdiocese of Bogotá.
The restored organ was inaugurated with a blessing by Cardinal Rubén Salazar Gómez and an inaugural concert.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with a Classical basilica plan in the form of a Latin cross. It has five naves, a main altar, 16 chapels, a choir, and two sacristies. The portal is divided into two bodies with Corinthian and Ionic pilasters. The towers are 52 meters high and the main door is 7.20 meters high by 3.60 meters wide.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is culturally and historically significant as the seat of the Metropolitan Archbishop of Bogotá and Primate of Colombia. It has been a central site for religious and political events in Colombia's history and was declared a National Monument in 1975.
Notable_Visitors: Archbishop Metropolitan of Bogotá Luis José Rueda Aparicio
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral is located in the historic center of Bogotá, in the neighborhood of La Candelaria. It is part of the Episcopal Pastoral Zone of the Immaculate Conception and is surrounded by other significant buildings such as the Chapel del Sagrario, the Casa del Cabildo Eclesiástico, and the Archbishop's Palace. The cathedral's pipe organ, restored between 2013 and 2016, is the largest in Colombia.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Castelnau-Bretenoux
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Castelnau-Bretenoux is a castle in France, one of the most impressive in the Quercy region. Construction began around 1100 under Hugues, baron of Castelnau. It was enlarged several times between the 12th and 15th centuries. The castle was taken by Henry II of England in 1159 and returned to the barons of Castelnau at the end of the Hundred Years' War. It fell into disrepair after the death of the last Castelnau in 1715. The castle was neglected for many years until it was purchased and restored by Jean Mouliérat in 1896, who later donated it to the French state in 1932.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the castle began under Hugues, baron of Castelnau, who built a wall around his manor.

Major_Events.Event: Taken by Henry II of England
Major_Events.Description: The castle was taken by Henry II of England.
A decree was issued calling for the destruction of parts of the castle, but only the moat was emptied and the drawbridge permanently lowered.
A fire broke out in the castle, destroying the large gallery and buildings in the courtyard.
Jean Mouliérat donated the castle to the French state.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The castle is located on the top of a hill, with walls of red stone. The layout is nearly a triangle, with round towers at each angle. The square keep and the main building of the medieval period still remain. It originally had three enclosing walls, wide curtain walls, and nine round towers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is one of the most impressive in the Quercy region and has been listed as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture since 1862. It represents the power and prosperity of the Castelnau dynasty and the architectural evolution of medieval fortifications.
world knowledge.Details: Visitors can see seven rooms in this fortress, restored and furnished in the medieval style. A small village surrounds the castle, along the slopes of the hill.

world knowledge.Name: Apoyo Lagoon Natural Reserve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Laguna de Apoyo Nature Reserve is a nature reserve located between the departments of Masaya and Granada in Nicaragua. Lake Apoyo was declared a nature reserve in 1991 and is managed by the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources (MARENA). Geological data suggests that Lake Apoyo originated about 23,000 years ago.

Major_Events.Description: Lake Apoyo was declared a nature reserve in 1991 and is managed by the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources (MARENA).

Activities within the Laguna de Apoyo Nature Reserve are regulated by its management plan, approved in 2010, which prohibits the construction of housing within the reserve and use of motorized vehicles on the lake.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The reserve protects a volcanic lake, Laguna de Apoyo, and its drainage basin. It houses a tropical dry forest ecosystem with over 500 species of plants and a variety of fauna, including endemic species of cichlids. The reserve also contains petroglyphs and artifacts of indigenous peoples.
world knowledge.Details: Lake Apoyo attracts tourists with various tourist attractions such as dark sand beaches for swimming, kayaking, hiking, scuba diving, birdwatching, paragliding, boating, and nature. Pumice rocks abound in the lagoon, and are harvested by locals for use in the clothing industry. Strict laws limiting human activity exist in the reserve, and several residential construction projects have been stopped and many landowners have been engaged in legal processes by the Ministry of Natural Resources inside the reserve, in accordance with the laws regarding nature reserves in Nicaragua.

world knowledge.Name: Banjul International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Banjul International Airport, also known as Yundum International, is the international airport of Banjul, capital of Gambia, built during World War II. It is the country's only commercial airport. After World War II, Yundum airport was used for passenger flights. The airport was rebuilt in 1963 and the building is still in use today.

Major_Events.Event: Zambia Airways service from Lusaka to New York via Banjul
Major_Events.Description: Zambia Airways launched service from Lusaka to New York via Banjul in December 1990. The airline flew the route with a McDonnell Douglas DC-10. Financial difficulties forced the carrier to suspend it three months later.

Major_Events.Event: Ghana Airways flight from Banjul to Baltimore
Major_Events.Description: In February 2001, Ghana Airways commenced a flight from Banjul to Baltimore, which originated in Accra. Cooperation among Ghana Airways, Gambia International Airlines, and the Ghanaian and Gambian governments had given rise to the service.

Major_Events.Event: North American Airlines link to Baltimore
Major_Events.Description: In June 2006, North American Airlines inaugurated a link to Baltimore using Boeing 767s; the route lasted seven months.

Major_Events.Event: NASA Space Shuttle emergency landing site
Major_Events.Description: In the event of an emergency on any of the NASA Space Shuttles, Banjul International Airport had been selected as an augmented landing site. In 2001 NASA announced that Banjul airport would no longer be used as an augmented landing site because future shuttle launches would take place at inclinations of up at 51.6 degrees to reach the International Space Station, making air bases in Spain and France more suitable for an emergency landing.
The airport was the main hub of Gambia Bird until the airline ceased operations in late 2014.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Banjul International Airport is the only commercial airport in Gambia and serves as a critical transportation hub for the country.
world knowledge.Details: The head office of the Gambia Civil Aviation Authority is located on the airport property.

world knowledge.Name: Oxford Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oxford Town Hall is the third seat of government to have stood on the same site, with the current building completed in 1897. It replaced an earlier guildhall from 1292 and a 1752 Italianate-style building. The town hall has served as a public meeting place, entertainment venue, and housed the Museum of Oxford, a public library, and a police station. It was converted into a hospital during World War I and has undergone several functional changes over the years.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the new Town Hall
Major_Events.Description: The Prince of Wales opened the new building in May 1897. A large demonstration by University of Oxford undergraduates led to violent clashes with the Metropolitan Police, resulting in several injuries and the arrest of a young law don, FE Smith.

Major_Events.Event: Conversion into a hospital during WWI
Major_Events.Description: The building was converted into the Town Hall section of the 3rd Southern General Hospital, specializing in treating soldiers suffering from malaria.

Major_Events.Event: UK premiere of Ravel's opera and staged premiere of Stravinsky's Oedipus Rex
Major_Events.Description: The UK premiere of Ravel's opera 'L'enfant et les sortilèges' and the staged premiere of Stravinsky's 'Oedipus Rex' took place at the town hall on 3 December 1958.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Jacobethan style, designed by Henry Hare. The building includes features such as a central public library (now relocated), police station (now relocated), and city council chambers. The main hall was repainted in 2015.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Oxford Town Hall is a Grade II* listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. It has been a central venue for public meetings, cultural events, and governance in Oxford. The building also houses significant works of art, including portraits by Godfrey Kneller and paintings by Pietro da Cortona and Francesco Fontebasso.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of Oxford City Council, venue for public meetings, entertainment, and events, and home to the Museum of Oxford.
Notable_Visitors: Prince of Wales (opened the building in 1897)
FE Smith (young law don involved in the 1897 incident)
world knowledge.Details: The building cost £100,000, significantly exceeding its budget. It was designated as a listed building on 12 January 1954 (Reference no. 1047153). The town hall has undergone several functional changes, including housing the Oxford City Police and central public library, both of which have since relocated. The city council moved its main offices back into the town hall in 2022 after previously relocating to St Aldate's Chambers in 1967.

world knowledge.Name: Cité de l'Automobile
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The museum was built around the Schlumpf Collection of classic automobiles, assembled by brothers Hans and Fritz Schlumpf. The collection began in the 1950s and grew to become the largest displayed collection of automobiles, including the most comprehensive collection of Bugatti motor vehicles in the world. The museum was established in 1978 after the Schlumpf brothers fled due to labor disputes and financial issues.

Major_Events.Event: Workers' Strike and Discovery of Collection
Major_Events.Description: Textile-union activists staged a sit-in strike at Schlumpf offices and discovered the car collection. The workers' union opened the museum to the public to recoup lost wages.
The collection was classified as a French Historic Monument to prevent its destruction, break-up, or export.

Major_Events.Event: Sale to National Automobile Museum Association
Major_Events.Description: The collection, buildings, and residual land were sold to the National Automobile Museum Association (NAMAoM), a state-sanctioned public/private conglomerate.
Culturespaces renovated and modernized the museum, reopening it as the largest automobile museum in the world.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a repurposed spinning mill, with large-scale public spaces and a main hall featuring Pont Alexandre III lamp posts. The interior includes red tile walkways and gravel floors for the cars.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses the largest displayed collection of automobiles, including the most comprehensive collection of Bugatti motor vehicles. It is also a National Heritage site in France and dedicated to the Schlumpf brothers' mother, Jeanne Schlumpf.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Automobile museum showcasing classic and historic cars.

Notable_Exhibits: Three Bugatti Royales (two originals and one replica)
Cars from the Schlumpf Collection and the Malmerspach collection
Details.Visitor_Amenities: Free audioguides, driving simulators, robots, and sound programmes.
Details.Public_Transit_Access: From SNCF Mulhouse take tramway number 1

world knowledge.Name: Theodoros Kolokotronis Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1979 as a small stadium with about 100 seats, it was expanded and renovated multiple times as Asteras Tripolis advanced through the divisions. Major renovations occurred in 2005, 2007, 2008, 2010, and 2015. It was renamed in 2012 to honor Theodoros Kolokotronis, a hero of the Greek War of Independence.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium's attendance record was achieved with 6,150 tickets in the match between Asteras Tripolis and Olympiacos on 27 November 2011.
On 22 November 2012, the stadium was renamed in honor of Theodoros Kolokotronis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features multiple stands (eastern, western, south, and north), VIP seats, press booths, changing rooms, a gym, and a funeral parlor. The surface is grass, and it includes a scoreboard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named after Theodoros Kolokotronis, a prominent figure in the Greek War of Independence, reflecting its cultural and historical importance in Greece. It serves as a key sports venue in Tripoli.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium, home of Asteras Tripolis FC.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 7,442 seats and is owned and operated by Asteras Tripolis FC. It underwent significant renovations in 2015 for the 2015–16 Europa League.

world knowledge.Name: Stary Dom (Novosibirsk)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stary Dom is a drama theatre founded in 1933, originally called the Mobile Kolkhoz and Sovkhoz Theatre, aimed at developing art in the countryside. It underwent several name changes and played a significant role during the Great Patriotic War, performing for both rural audiences and military personnel. The theatre moved to its current building, constructed in 1912 by Andrey Kryachkov, in 1967.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as Mobile Kolkhoz and Sovkhoz Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was established to serve agricultural areas of West Siberian Krai, initially as a branch of the Red Torch Theatre.

Major_Events.Event: Renamed to Oblast Kolkhoz and Sovkhoz Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was renamed during the Great Patriotic War.
The theatre underwent another name change.
The theatre moved to a building constructed in 1912 by Andrey Kryachkov.

Major_Events.Event: Awarded Order of the Badge of Honor
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was awarded for its services to the development of Soviet theatrical art.

Major_Events.Event: Performance of Jazz Story in N City
Major_Events.Description: A performance with jazz music that became a sensation of the season.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was constructed in 1912 by Andrey Kryachkov, but specific architectural details are not provided.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stary Dom has played a significant role in the development of Soviet theatrical art, particularly in rural areas and during wartime. It has been recognized with awards and continues to be a cultural hub in Novosibirsk.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has staged numerous plays by notable Soviet authors and has a repertoire that includes popular children's performances. It was awarded the pennant of the USSR Ministry of Culture in 1982 and 1984.

world knowledge.Name: Restenneth Priory
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Restenneth Priory was a monastic house of Augustinian canons founded by Jedburgh Abbey, with the patronage of King Malcolm IV of Scotland, in 1153. There is speculation that Restenneth may have been the Pictish church dedicated to St Peter built in 710 for Nechtán mac Der Ilei, King of the Picts. The priory was always small and dependent on its mother-house at Jedburgh. It was turned into a secular lordship for Thomas Erskine, Viscount Fentoun, in 1606. The site was excavated in 1883 by William Galloway and Dr John Stuart. All except the tower is now in ruins.

Major_Events.Description: Restenneth Priory was founded by Jedburgh Abbey with the patronage of King Malcolm IV of Scotland.

Major_Events.Event: Attempted incorporation into the Royal Chapel
Major_Events.Description: An attempt was made to incorporate the priory into the Royal Chapel, but it failed.

Major_Events.Event: Incorporation into the archbishopric of St Andrews
Major_Events.Description: King James IV of Scotland suggested its incorporation into the archbishopric of St Andrews, but it did not occur.
The priory was turned into a secular lordship for Thomas Erskine, Viscount Fentoun.
The site was excavated by William Galloway and Dr John Stuart.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: All except the tower is now in ruins. The ruins are a Scheduled Ancient Monument.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Restenneth Priory is historically significant as a monastic house and a potential Pictish church site. It is also notable for its association with King Malcolm IV and its later transformation into a secular lordship.
world knowledge.Details: The priory is located just outside the town of Forfar and shares an access road with the Angus Archives. It is surrounded by fields and medieval architecture, with the town and nearby roads not visible from the site.

world knowledge.Name: Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland is the supreme court of the Swiss Confederation and the head of the Swiss judiciary. It is headquartered in the Federal Courthouse in Lausanne, with two divisions located in Lucerne. The court ensures the uniform application of federal law and protects constitutional rights. It was established under the Swiss Federal Constitution and has jurisdiction over civil law, public law, and disputes between cantons or between cantons and the Confederation.

Major_Events.Event: First woman elected to the Federal Supreme Court
Major_Events.Description: Margrith Bigler-Eggenberger became the first woman elected to the Federal Supreme Court, one year after women were permitted to participate in federal elections.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Federal Supreme Court is culturally and historically significant as the highest judicial authority in Switzerland, ensuring the uniform application of federal law and protecting constitutional rights. Its decisions contribute to the development of Swiss law and its adaptation to new circumstances.
world knowledge.Details: The Federal Supreme Court is composed of eight divisions, each covering different legal domains such as public law, private law, and criminal law. The court's decisions can be appealed to the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. The court also exercises administrative supervision over other federal courts.

world knowledge.Name: Meadow Brook Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Meadow Brook Hall is a Tudor revival style mansion built by Matilda Dodge Wilson, heiress to the Dodge automaker fortune, and her second husband, lumber baron Alfred Wilson. The estate was originally part of Meadow Brook Farms, purchased by Matilda's first husband, John F. Dodge. The mansion was constructed between 1926 and 1929 at a cost of $4 million. In 1957, the estate was donated to Michigan State University to fund what is now Oakland University. The mansion was named a National Historic Landmark in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Matilda Dodge Wilson and Alfred Wilson.
The estate was donated to fund Oakland University.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Recognized for its historical significance.
Officially recognized as a National Historic Landmark.
Annual collector car show held on the grounds.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tudor Revival style designed by William E. Kapp of Smith, Hinchman & Grylls. Features stonework and a plaster dining room ceiling by Corrado Parducci. Includes original artwork, Tiffany glass, Stickley furniture, Meissen porcelain, and Rookwood pottery.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the largest historic mansion museums in the United States, representing the opulence of the early 20th century. It reflects the lifestyle of the Dodge and Wilson families and is a significant example of Tudor Revival architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a 1,443-acre property with a golf course. The Wilsons also owned homes in Bar Harbor, Maine, and Scottsdale, Arizona. The Meadow Brook Concours d'Elegance was a major event held annually from 1979 to 2010. The mansion is the fourth largest historic house museum in the U.S.

world knowledge.Name: Naga Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Naga Airport (IATA: WNP, ICAO: RPUN) is an airport serving the city and metropolitan area of Naga (including the provincial capital Pili), located in the province of Camarines Sur in the Philippines. Although the airport is named after Naga, it is actually located in the provincial capital, Pili. The airport is classified as a Class 1 principal (major domestic) airport by the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines, a body of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) that is responsible for the operations of not only this airport but also of all other airports in the Philippines except the major international airports.

Major_Events.Description: As of March 2022, the airport is considered to be night-rated by the CAAP.

world knowledge.Details: In 2019, the DOTr announced that they intended to make the airport capable of handling flights at night by 2021. The airport is classified as a Class 1 principal (major domestic) airport by the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines.

world knowledge.Name: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Staten Island and Brooklyn, New York, NY, U.S.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 13,700 ft (4,176 m), Width: 103 ft (31 m), Height: 693 ft (211 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge is a suspension bridge connecting Staten Island and Brooklyn in New York City. It spans the Narrows, linking New York Harbor with Lower New York Bay and the Atlantic Ocean. Named after explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world upon completion in 1964. The bridge was designed by Othmar Ammann and constructed to alleviate traffic congestion and improve connectivity between Staten Island and the rest of the city.

Major_Events.Description: Groundbreaking ceremony held on August 13, 1959, marking the start of construction.
The upper deck of the bridge opened on November 21, 1964, with a ceremony attended by dignitaries.
The lower deck opened on June 28, 1969, to accommodate increasing traffic loads.
The bridge's name was officially corrected to 'Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge' after being misspelled since 1960.
Tolls were reinstated in both directions after being collected only westbound since 1986.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge is a suspension bridge with a central span of 4,260 ft (1.30 km). It features two suspension towers, each 693 ft (211 m) tall, and a double-deck design carrying 13 lanes of Interstate 278. The bridge's design accounts for thermal expansion, with the roadway height varying by 12 ft (3.66 m) between seasons. The towers are not parallel due to the Earth's curvature, being 1+5⁄8 in (41.275 mm) farther apart at their tops than at their bases.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a critical transportation link in New York City and a symbol of engineering prowess. It has been featured in literature, films, and cultural events, such as the New York City Marathon, which starts on the bridge. The bridge's name honors Italian explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano, reflecting the cultural heritage of Italian-Americans in New York.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (vehicular traffic between Staten Island and Brooklyn)

Details.Toll_Information: As of August 6, 2023: $6.94 (New York E-ZPass users outside Staten Island), $2.75 (Staten Island residents E-ZPass), $11.19 (Tolls By Mail and non–New York E-ZPass), $9.11 (Mid-Tier NYCSC E-Z Pass)
Details.Maintenance: Operated by MTA Bridges and Tunnels
Details.Notable_Features: The bridge's clearance of 228 ft (69.5 m) accommodates large ships, including the RMS Queen Mary 2. It is also a nesting site for peregrine falcons.
Details.Suicide_Prevention: The bridge has suicide hotlines and a prototype barrier installed in 2019 to deter jumps.

world knowledge.Name: Campuestohan Highland Resort
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Campuestohan Highland Resort is a theme park and resort in Talisay, Negros Occidental. The site was offered to the Tan family in 2009 and bought in 2010 by Ricardo Tan, initially planning to build a retirement home for his wife. Despite skepticism, Tan developed the area into an eco-tourism-oriented theme park and resort, which opened in May 2014.

Major_Events.Description: The Dinosaurs Park opened, featuring moving and stationary models of dinosaurs.
An assassination attempt on Ricardo and Nita Tan occurred in December 2018.
The rooster-shaped hotel building, Manok ni Cano Gwapo, was inaugurated and recognized by Guinness World Records as the tallest building in the shape of a chicken.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features a variety of attractions including the Dinosaurs Park, a water park with wave pools and foam baths, sky bike, zip lines, and the Manok ni Cano Gwapo hotel building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The resort is recognized as one of the top destinations in the Western Visayas region and was awarded in the Pagdayaw 2023 by the Department of Tourism.
world knowledge.Details: The resort covers an area of 11 hectares (27 acres) and is noted for its eco-tourism-oriented attractions. It continues to develop under the ownership of the Tans despite challenges.

world knowledge.Name: Buckhead Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Buckhead Theatre was built in 1930 in Spanish baroque style by the Atlanta architecture firm Daniell & Beutell. It initially functioned as a second-run movie theater and hosted civic functions and concerts. Over the years, it underwent several name changes and operational shifts, including being part of the Weis Theater chain as the Capri Theatre in 1961, and later becoming the Coca-Cola Roxy Theatre. After closing in 2008, it was purchased by Charles Loudermilk, renovated, and reopened in 2010 under its original name. Live Nation resumed control in 2017 as the sole booker and operator.

Major_Events.Description: The Buckhead Theatre opened on June 2, 1930, as a second-run movie theater and venue for civic functions and concerts.
The theater converted to a first-run policy and joined the Weis Theater chain as the Capri Theatre.
After two years of renovation, the venue reopened in June 2010 under the original name Buckhead Theatre.
Live Nation resumed control of the theater as sole booker and operator, investing at least $7 million in renovations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Spanish baroque style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Buckhead Theatre is a historic venue in Atlanta, serving as a significant concert venue and cultural hub since its opening in 1930. Its various transformations reflect the evolving entertainment and cultural landscape of the Buckhead neighborhood.

Details.Former_names: Buckhead Theatre (1930-61), Capri Theatre (1961-78), Capri Ballroom (1979-80), Buckhead Cinema & Drafthouse (1980-86), Buckhead Roxy (1987-88), The Roxy (1989-92), Coca-Cola Roxy Theatre (1992-2008)

world knowledge.Name: Leinster House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Leinster House, originally the ducal palace of the Dukes of Leinster, has been the seat of the Oireachtas, the parliament of Ireland, since 1922. It was built by James FitzGerald, 1st Duke of Leinster, and designed by architect Richard Cassels. The building has served various roles, including as the headquarters of the Royal Dublin Society and as the parliament building of the Irish Free State. It has undergone several extensions and restorations over the years.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted in the grounds of Leinster House.
Led to the creation of the Irish Free State and the use of Leinster House as the temporary parliament building.
Major restoration and conservation work was carried out on the building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Leinster House is designed in Georgian and Palladian styles, constructed with Ardbraccan limestone. The building has undergone several extensions, including the addition of wings for the National Library of Ireland and the National Museum of Ireland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Leinster House is culturally and historically significant as the seat of the Oireachtas and a symbol of Irish political activities. It was also the model for the White House in Washington, D.C.
world knowledge.Details: Leinster House has been the meeting place of Dáil Éireann and Seanad Éireann since 1922. It has undergone several extensions and restorations, most recently from 2017 to 2019. The building is a complex of structures, with the original ducal palace at its core.

world knowledge.Name: Woodlands Family Theme Park
world knowledge.Address: On the A3122, 5 miles from Dartmouth, South Devon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The site was purchased by the Bendall family in 1971 as a 200-acre dairy farm and diversified in 1989 to a 90-acre leisure park and caravan park. It remains a family-owned company, Bendalls Leisure Ltd. The first year that the park opened saw 60,000 visitors. The average annual Leisure Park visitor numbers are now around 350,000.

Major_Events.Description: A seasonal event hosted by the park.
Various redevelopment phases over the years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The layout, café, shop, buildings, play equipment, and landscaping were all designed by family Bendall members. The park features extensive play zones, indoor play centers, and a falconry display.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Woodlands Family Theme Park is a significant family attraction in South Devon, offering a wide range of activities and experiences for visitors of all ages. It is known for its all-weather fun and seasonal events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Family amusement park and falconry display
world knowledge.Details: The park comprises numerous play zones including 3 Watercoasters, Toboggan run, Arctic Gliders, Avalanche, Pedal Boats, Bumper Boats, Tango Trolls Mystic Maze, Sand Diggers & Big Dig, Swing Ship Ride, Dolphin Toddlers Play, Ninja Towers, Seascape Mirror Maze, Whistle Stop Junction, Pedal Karts, Commando Course, Safari Adventure Golf, and indoor attractions like Teddy Mountain, Masterblaster, Circusdrome & Empire of the Sea Dragon. More recent attractions include Dinotrek, Jumping Pillow, Farmyard Ride, and Vertigo. The park also features a large Zoo Farm Complex and Indoor Falconry Centre. It has approximately 60 permanent staff and 130 seasonal staff.

world knowledge.Name: Sierra Leone National Museum
world knowledge.Address: Junction of Siaka Stevens Street and Pademba Road, central Freetown
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sierra Leone National Museum, previously known as the Sierra Leone Museum and the Museum of the Sierra Leone Society, is the national museum of Sierra Leone. Its origin dates back to before the country's independence. The Monuments and Relics Commission was set up by a 1946 ordinance to preserve ancient, historical, and natural monuments. In 1953, Governor Sir Robert Hall encouraged the formation of the Sierra Leone Society and challenged its members to establish a museum. The museum was officially opened on 10 December 1957 by Sir Milton Margai. Sierra Leone gained independence from the UK in 1961, and the museum became the national museum in 1967. The government has rarely provided much support, and the museum still occupies its original, temporary location. The German embassy in Freetown provided funds for an extension, opened in 1987, to mark the bicentennial of the founding of Freetown.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Sierra Leone Museum
Major_Events.Description: The Sierra Leone Museum was officially opened on 10 December 1957 by Sir Milton Margai.
Sierra Leone gained its independence from the UK in 1961.
The Sierra Leone Museum became the national museum in 1967.
The German embassy in Freetown provided funds for an extension, opened in 1987, to mark the bicentennial of the founding of Freetown.
The museum displayed the only known photograph of the Temne guerrilla leader Bai Bureh, who in 1898 started a war against the British.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sierra Leone National Museum is culturally and historically important as it preserves and showcases the heritage and history of Sierra Leone. It serves as a repository for artifacts and objects of archaeological, ethnographical, historical, and scientific interest, reflecting the country's rich cultural legacy.
world knowledge.Details: University College London's "Reanimating Cultural Heritage: Digital Repatriation, Knowledge Networks and Civil Society Strengthening in Post-Conflict Sierra Leone" project, in conjunction with the Sierra Leonean Ministry of Cultural Affairs, the National Museum and other organizations and museums, has digitised 2000 objects from the museum, along with objects from other sources.

world knowledge.Name: Boulder Beach
world knowledge.Address: Boulder Beach, Otago Peninsula, Dunedin, New Zealand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Boulder Beach is a rocky beach on the Pacific Ocean, located on the south side of Otago Peninsula, some 15.7 kilometres (9.8 mi) by road east from central Dunedin, New Zealand.

Major_Events.Description: Boulder Beach Track has been closed to the public during the yellow-eyed penguins' breeding season since 2005, initially from December to February, but more recently from November to February.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Boulder Beach is a favoured nesting spot for yellow-eyed penguins, which are very shy about nesting or breeding where they may be seen by humans. The beach is also visited by New Zealand fur seals and New Zealand sea lions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural habitat for wildlife and recreational use.
world knowledge.Details: Boulder Beach is approximately 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) long, facing almost exactly due south. Near the eastern end a stretch of about 200 metres (660 ft) is sandy; the remainder is covered in boulders. Access to Boulder Beach is via the Highcliff Track system. The beach is considered a reasonably consistent surfing beach, offering both left- and right-hand waves. It is occasionally used by naturists for nude sunbathing. New Zealand has no official nude beaches, as public nudity is legal on any beach where it is 'known to occur'. Boulder Beach conservation is administered by the Department of Conservation (DOC) in two blocks: Boulder Beach / Highcliff Block and Boulder Beach / WWF Block.

world knowledge.Name: Sagrada Família
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, commonly known as Sagrada Família, is a church under construction in Barcelona, Spain. Designed by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, it is the largest unfinished Catholic church in the world. Construction began in 1882 under architect Francisco de Paula del Villar, and Gaudí took over in 1883, transforming the project with his unique architectural style. Gaudí devoted the remainder of his life to the project, and he is buried in the church's crypt. The construction has been ongoing for over a century, with interruptions due to events like the Spanish Civil War. The church was consecrated by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010 and is expected to be completed by 2026, the centenary of Gaudí's death.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of Sagrada Família began under architect Francisco de Paula del Villar.
Antoni Gaudí took over as chief architect, transforming the project with his unique architectural style.
Construction was interrupted by the Spanish Civil War, during which parts of the unfinished basilica and Gaudí's models were destroyed.
Pope Benedict XVI consecrated the church and proclaimed it a minor basilica.
Construction was temporarily halted due to the COVID-19 pandemic, marking the first interruption since the Spanish Civil War.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Sagrada Família is designed in a combination of Gothic Revival, Art Nouveau, and Modernista styles. The church features hyperboloid structures, intricate ornamentation, and a unique use of geometric forms. The interior columns branch to support their load, and the surfaces are the result of the intersection of various geometric forms. The church is planned to have 18 spires, representing the Twelve Apostles, the four Evangelists, the Virgin Mary, and Jesus Christ. The spires are decorated with sculptures and symbols, and the church's façades (Nativity, Passion, and Glory) depict various scenes from the life of Christ.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sagrada Família is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered one of the most extraordinary interpretations of Gothic architecture since the Middle Ages. It is a symbol of Barcelona and a testament to Antoni Gaudí's unique architectural vision. The church attracts millions of visitors annually and is a significant cultural and religious landmark.
world knowledge.Details: Sagrada Família is funded primarily through private donations and visitor entrance fees. The construction has faced various challenges, including the destruction of Gaudí's original plans during the Spanish Civil War and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The church is expected to be completed by 2026, with additional work on sculptures and decorative details continuing until 2034. The building's design has been polarizing, with some praising its creativity and others criticizing its unconventional appearance.

world knowledge.Name: Konaka Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Konaka Museum, founded in 1956, is located in a former Ottoman konak in Vidin, Bulgaria. Originally built in the 18th century, it served as the home of Osman Pazvantoğlu and later as a police office, with its central tower functioning as a lighthouse. After Bulgaria's liberation, the building was reconstructed and enriched with elements from Bulgarian Renaissance architecture. In 1956, it was repurposed for a historical weapon show.

Major_Events.Description: The building was repurposed as a museum for a historical weapon show.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a former Ottoman konak with a central tower that was once a lighthouse. It was reconstructed and enriched with elements from Bulgarian Renaissance architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Konaka Museum is a cultural memorial of the region, showcasing the historical and architectural heritage of Vidin, Bulgaria.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is among the cultural memorials of the region and is housed in a historically significant building.

world knowledge.Name: Disney's Blizzard Beach
world knowledge.Address: Walt Disney World Resort, Bay Lake, Florida, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Disney's Blizzard Beach is a water theme park that opened on April 1, 1995, as the third Walt Disney World water park. According to Disney "legend," a freak snowstorm in 1977 led to the development of Florida's first ski resort, which later transformed into the water park due to melting snow.

Major_Events.Description: The water park, along with all other Walt Disney World parks, closed in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It reopened on March 7, 2021, after being closed for nearly a year.

Blizzard Beach closed for refurbishment on May 1, 2025, before reopening on May 21, 2025. This marked the first time both water parks (Blizzard Beach and Typhoon Lagoon) were open together for the summer season since 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a winter theme with an artificial hill called Mount Gushmore (elevation: 90 feet). The design blends alpine lodge aesthetics with Caribbean colors and accents. Innovative elements include a beach chair-themed chair lift and pretend snow skis. The park combines tropical landscaping with simulated melting snow.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Blizzard Beach is one of the most visited water parks in the world, ranking third in 2016 with approximately 2,091,000 guests. Its unique theme and attractions make it a popular destination for families and tourists.
world knowledge.Details: Most major attractions are found atop Mount Gushmore, which is split into three colored slopes (Green, Red, and Purple) for navigation. The park's mascot is Ice Gator, a blue alligator. Water areas are heated to approximately 80°F (27°C), except for the ice cave of Cross Country Creek. Coolers are allowed, but glass and alcohol are restricted. Appropriate swimwear is required, and sharp objects are prohibited.

world knowledge.Name: Whitehaven Beach
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Whitehaven Beach is on Whitsunday Island, Queensland, Australia. The Ngaro people lived in the area for thousands of years before Europeans arrived. The beach was named in 1879 by Staff Commander EP Bedwell. 'Whitehaven' originates from the English town of the same name. It followed James Cook's 1770 naming of the island group, the Cumberland Islands.

Major_Events.Description: Awarded in Keep Australia Beautiful's Beach Challenge State Awards.

Major_Events.Event: Top Eco Friendly Beach in the world
Major_Events.Description: Named by CNN.com.
Placed in the top five on a list of the best beaches worldwide.
Caused severe erosion and damage to the beach, requiring intensive reconstruction work on the southern end.
Announced an investment of $3.9 million for the construction of a new long-distance walking track and the upgrade of the camping areas on the island.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Whitehaven Beach is culturally significant due to its bright white silica sands, turquoise water, and its recognition as one of the most beautiful and eco-friendly beaches in the world. It holds historical importance as it was named after the English town of Whitehaven and has been a part of the Ngaro people's heritage for thousands of years.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourism and recreation, including swimming, camping, and open swimming competitions.
world knowledge.Details: Whitehaven Beach is known for its bright white sand, which consists of 98% pure silica. The sand retains less heat from the sun, making it comfortable to walk barefoot on a hot day. The sand is very fine and can damage electronic equipment but can be used for polishing tarnished jewellery. Tourists and locals visit to swim and enjoy the beach. The Whitehaven Beach Ocean Swim is a two-kilometer open swimming competition held annually since 2009. The beach was featured in the racing video game Forza Horizon 3.

world knowledge.Name: Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally completed in 1947 as Tokyo Rugby Stadium, renamed in 1953 to honor Prince Chichibu, a rugby enthusiast and brother of Emperor Hirohito. Served as a venue for football in the 1964 Summer Olympics. It is the spiritual home of Japanese rugby and headquarters of the Japan Rugby Football Union.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted football matches during the 1964 Summer Olympics.
Japan vs Asian Barbarians, the send-off for Japan going to RWC 2007.
Hosted the Japan Sevens, part of the World Rugby Sevens Series.
Used for a concert by Nogizaka46, with performances also at the adjacent Meiji Jingu Stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Grass surface, partial stand coverage, large electronic scoreboard added in 2003. Future redevelopment plans include a roof over the field and stands.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Spiritual home of Japanese rugby, named after Prince Chichibu who was passionate about rugby. Features a statue of the prince in rugby uniform.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Rugby union and rugby sevens matches, concerts, and other events.
world knowledge.Details: Plans exist to demolish and replace the stadium along with the adjacent Meiji Jingu Stadium. The new rugby stadium will be built on the current site of Meiji Jingu Stadium Number 2 field. Current capacity is 27,188 spectators.

world knowledge.Name: Rietberg Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rietberg Museum was established in 1952 in the Wesendonck Villa, which was rebuilt to house the art collection donated by Baron von der Heydt. The museum has expanded over the years with the addition of several historic buildings and a new subterranean building called 'Smaragd' in 2007.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened on 24 May 1952, housed in the Wesendonck Villa, which was rebuilt for this purpose.
The Schönberg Villa was acquired by the city in 1976 and opened as an extension of the museum in 1978.
The new subterranean building 'Smaragd' was opened, more than doubling the museum's exhibition space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of several historic buildings including the Wesendonck Villa, the Remise, the Rieter Park-Villa, and the Schönberg Villa. The Smaragd building, designed by Alfred Grazioli and Adolf Krischanitz, is largely subterranean.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rietberg Museum is the largest art museum in Switzerland focusing on non-European art and design, making it a significant cultural institution for the study and appreciation of global art.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is operated by the presidential department of the city of Zürich and employs around one hundred people. It is funded by the city, revenue, sponsors, and donations. The museum also has an in-house press that publishes catalogues, monographs, and a biannual scholarly journal called Artibus Asiae.

world knowledge.Name: Gunung Mulu National Park
world knowledge.Area: Marudi District, Miri Division, Sarawak, Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gunung Mulu National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is renowned for its caves and karst formations in a mountainous equatorial rainforest setting. It was first referenced in 1858 by Spenser St. John. The park was officially gazetted in 1974 and has since been the site of numerous scientific expeditions, including the Royal Geographical Society Expedition of 1977–1978. It was designated as an ASEAN Heritage Park in 1984 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: Over 100 scientists explored the caves and surrounding rainforest for 15 months, initiating the Mulu Caves Project.
Discovered during a British expedition, it is one of the world's largest underground chambers.
Gunung Mulu National Park was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features extensive cave systems, including Sarawak Chamber, Deer Cave, and Clearwater Cave, which are notable for their size and length. The geology includes metamorphosed sedimentary sequences and karstic limestone formations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its unique karst landscape, extensive cave systems, and rich biodiversity. It is also important for the indigenous Orang Ulu, Kiput, Kenyah, Kayan, Mulut, and Penan tribes who have historical ties to the area.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural park and UNESCO World Heritage Site
world knowledge.Details: The park is dominated by three mountains: Mount Mulu, Mount Api, and Mount Benarat. It is home to 295 km of explored caves, millions of bats, and swiftlets. The park has 20,000 species of invertebrates, 81 species of mammals, 270 species of birds, 55 species of reptiles, 76 species of amphibians, and 48 species of fish. The park is managed by the Sarawak Forestry Corporation and Borsarmulu Park Management Sdn Bhd. It can be accessed by air or boat, with no road access available.

world knowledge.Name: Akinada Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Akinada Bridge is a suspension bridge completed in 1999, crossing the Seto Inland Sea. It is the first and largest bridge on the Akinada Tobishima Kaido and was constructed by Penta-Ocean Construction at a cost of 50 billion yen.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to traffic on 18 January 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a main span of 750 m (2,460 ft), clearance below of 40 m (131 ft) at mid-span.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Akinada Bridge is the longest bridge in Japan to be maintained by a prefecture and serves as a vital transportation link in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries motor vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles across the Seto Inland Sea.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is part of Hiroshima Prefecture Route 74, connecting Honshu to Shimo-kamagari Island. It is tolled and operated by the Hiroshima Prefecture Road Corporation. The average daily traffic volume was 4,000 vehicles by May 2000, exceeding the expected volume of 2,400 vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: Tallaght Stadium
world knowledge.Address: Whitestown Way, Tallaght, South Dublin, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tallaght Stadium was originally announced by Shamrock Rovers in 1996. Construction began in 2000 but was halted in 2001 due to financial issues. The stadium was eventually completed and opened in 2009 after a prolonged legal dispute with Thomas Davis GAA club. The stadium has undergone several expansions, including the addition of the South Stand in 2019 and the North Stand in 2024, increasing its capacity to over 10,000 seats.

Major_Events.Description: Shamrock Rovers defeated Sligo Rovers 2–1 in front of a sell-out crowd of 3,000.
Shamrock Rovers played Real Madrid, with Cristiano Ronaldo making his debut for Real Madrid. The match attracted a record attendance of 10,915.
Sporting Fingal defeated Sligo Rovers before 8,105 people.
Shamrock Rovers hosted games in the group stage, including a match against Tottenham Hotspur.
Ireland's women's football team secured a play-off spot for the 2023 World Cup with a 1–0 victory over Finland in front of a record crowd of 6,952.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features four covered stands: the main stand (west), east stand, south stand, and north stand. The pitch dimensions comply with UEFA standards, and the stadium includes facilities such as dressing rooms, a control room, refreshment stalls, and a club superstore. The North Stand expansion included additional media, conference, and meeting room facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tallaght Stadium is a significant sporting venue in Ireland, serving as the home ground for Shamrock Rovers and hosting major football matches, including European competitions and international fixtures. It has also been used for rugby, American football, and as a COVID-19 test center during the pandemic.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Association football stadium, also used for rugby, American football, and other events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned and operated by South Dublin County Council, with Shamrock Rovers as the anchor tenants. It has won multiple Airtricity League Pitch of the Year awards and has hosted events such as the UEFA European Under-17 Championship and the Rugby League European Championship.

world knowledge.Name: Belcourt Castle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Belcourt is a former summer cottage designed by architect Richard Morris Hunt for Oliver Hazard Perry Belmont. Construction began in 1891 and was completed in 1894. The mansion was intended for seasonal use, primarily six to eight weeks per year. Over the years, it underwent several ownership changes and renovations, serving various purposes including a private residence, antique auto museum, and venue for the Newport Jazz Festival. It was later converted into a museum of antiquities and architectural history before being purchased by Carolyn Rafaelian in 2012 for restoration and use as a tour house, art gallery, and event space.

Major_Events.Description: Belcourt was completed, featuring extensive stables and carriage areas on the first floor.

Major_Events.Event: Marriage of Oliver Belmont and Alva Vanderbilt
Major_Events.Description: Alva Vanderbilt redesigned parts of Belcourt, converting the carriage room into a banquet hall and a study into a boudoir.
Belcourt hosted the nation's first automobile parade.
The Tinney Family purchased Belcourt, renamed it Belcourt Castle, and filled it with their collection of antiques and reproductions.
The Lorillards used Belcourt as a venue for the Newport Jazz Festival, though protests from neighbors dimmed its future as a permanent venue.
Carolyn Rafaelian purchased Belcourt for $3.6 million, initiating extensive renovations to restore and repurpose the mansion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Belcourt was designed in a multitude of European styles, with a heavy emphasis on French Renaissance and Gothic decor, and borrowings from German, English, and Italian design. The building features a large quadrangle with two-story wings connecting to a three-story main block. The exterior is framed with brick and Westerly granite, and the roof is sheathed in Pennsylvania slate with oval dormer windows. The interior includes carved oak, mosaic marble floors, sculpted plaster ceilings, and walls finished with canvas paintings, imported paneling, and silk damasks. The mansion also features wrought iron and bronze railings with a shell motif and the monogram 'OB.'
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Belcourt is a notable example of Gilded Age architecture and reflects the opulence and eccentric tastes of its original owner, Oliver Belmont. It is the third-largest mansion in Newport and has served various cultural roles, including as a museum and event space. Its design and history make it an important landmark in Newport's architectural and social history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a summer residence, now serves as a tour house, art gallery, and event space.
world knowledge.Details: Belcourt has 60 rooms, with over a dozen viewable on tours. The mansion includes an English library, banquet hall, chapel, grand halls, music room, Empire-style dining room, French gothic-style ballroom, bedrooms, loggia, and gallery. The Tinney family's collection included furnishings, art, and artifacts from 33 European and Asian countries and 37 other Newport mansions. The mansion is currently undergoing restoration by Carolyn Rafaelian, who has invested millions in renovations, including a new roof.

world knowledge.Name: Manori Beach
world knowledge.Address: Manori, Mumbai Suburban, Maharashtra, India, PIN: 400092
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Manori is a village known for its beach and Manori Creek. It is dominated by the local fishing and farming community, with the East Indian community, Panchkalshi or Somvanshi Kshatriya Pathare (SKP), and Koli's being the native people. The village is divided into three sections: Koliwada, Bhandarwada, and Panchghar.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The village features a mix of local structures, including the largest bungalow "Green Villa" (also known as "Motha Ghar"), resorts designed like Spanish villas, and traditional fishing and farming community dwellings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Manori is culturally significant as a weekend destination for Mumbai residents, offering a mini-Goa experience with its beaches and culture. It is also home to religious sites like the Karjai Devi Mandir, a Hanuman temple, the Global Vipassana Pagoda, and ashrams of spiritual masters of Nath Sampradaya. The local cuisine, including East Indian and seafood dishes, adds to its cultural richness.
world knowledge.Details: Manori is a popular destination for cyclists and picnickers. The area is undergoing development under the MMRDAA plans for a tourism zone, which may convert agricultural lands into green zones with farmhouses, bungalows, and swimming pools. The local real estate is in high demand due to these plans. Popular dishes include Pork vindaloo, sorpotel, chicken raan, stuffed pomfret, dry Bombay duck chutney, and prawns chilly fry.

world knowledge.Name: Banggai Islands Regency
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Banggai Archipelago is a group of islands located at the far eastern end of Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. It became a regency of Central Sulawesi Province on 4 October 1999, created by splitting the existing Banggai Regency. On 14 December 2012, the more southerly seven districts were removed to form a separate Banggai Laut Regency.

Major_Events.Description: The Banggai Islands Regency was created by splitting the existing Banggai Regency.
The more southerly seven districts were removed from the Banggai Islands Regency to form a separate Banggai Laut Regency.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Banggai Islands are home to the Banggai cardinalfish, a species with an extremely limited geographic range and small total population size, threatened by extinction due to collection for the aquarium trade.
world knowledge.Details: The Banggai Islands Regency consists of the main island of Peleng and various small offshore islands. It is divided into twelve districts and has a population of 123,420 as of mid-2023. The archipelago is surrounded by the Banda Sea's Gulf of Tolo and the Molucca Sea. Salakan, the capital, has a tropical rainforest climate.

world knowledge.Name: Karađorđe's Park
world knowledge.Address: Boulevard of the Liberation, Nebojšina street, Vračar, Belgrade, Serbia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Karađorđe's Park is considered a predecessor of all green areas in Belgrade, with the first trees planted in 1806 during the siege of Belgrade in the First Serbian Uprising. It was officially planted as a park in 1848 and has since been a significant historical and cultural site. The park was added to the Historic Landmarks of Great Importance list in 1979 and is protected by the Republic of Serbia.

Major_Events.Description: During the First Serbian Uprising, the Serbian army set up a camp in the area where the park is now located. Soldiers killed in the battle on 30 November 1806 were buried here, and the first trees were planted at the burial site.
The burial site was arranged as the Insurgents Cemetery, and the Monument to the Liberators of Belgrade was erected. This marked the beginning of the park's development.
King Alexander Obrenović ordered the renovation of the cemetery and the creation of a memorial park, planting black locust seedlings and placing a metal fence around the monument.
Under King Peter I Karađorđević, the park was enlarged, pathways were created, and various trees and shrubs were planted, setting the present borders of the park.
A monument to the Third-Class Reservists was erected in the park, commemorating those who served in World War I.
A monument to Karađorđe, the leader of the First Serbian Uprising, was erected in the park, located across from the original site.
The park underwent massive reconstruction and beautification, including new benches, children's playgrounds, and candelabra, with plans to turn it into the first English-type park in Belgrade.
A monument to General Božidar Janković was dedicated in the park, marking the 120th anniversary of the Society of War Volunteers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of trees, including chestnut trees, black locusts, lindens, and decorative shrubs. It includes pathways, an artificial hill with a gazebo, and several monuments. The central pavilion, swimming pools, and a fountain are part of the park's design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Karađorđe's Park is culturally and historically significant as it is considered the oldest park in Belgrade and a predecessor to all green areas in the city. It is a memorial site for soldiers who died in the First Serbian Uprising and houses several important monuments, including the Monument to the Liberators of Belgrade and the Monument to Karađorđe.
world knowledge.Details: The park is one of the busiest parts of Belgrade, with very dense traffic. It is mostly non-residential, with public buildings such as the Faculty of the veterinarian medicine of the University of Belgrade, many clinics of the Belgrade Clinical Center, Children University Hospital, and Belgrade Meteorological Station. The park was declared a cultural monument in 1979 and has undergone several renovations and beautification projects over the years.

world knowledge.Name: Stanley Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stanley Park is a 405-hectare public park in British Columbia, Canada, that makes up the northwestern half of Vancouver's Downtown peninsula. The land was originally used by Indigenous peoples for thousands of years before British colonization. It was turned into Vancouver's first park in 1886 and named after Lord Stanley, the Governor General of Canada. The park has evolved over time, with many manmade structures built between 1911 and 1937. It was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1988.

Major_Events.Description: Lord Stanley officially opened the park, dedicating it to the public.
Stanley Park was designated a National Historic Site of Canada due to its cultural and natural significance.
A severe windstorm caused significant damage to the park, felling thousands of trees and destabilizing parts of the seawall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stanley Park is not the creation of a landscape architect but rather the evolution of a forest and urban space over many years. It features dense forests, the Vancouver Seawall, forest trails, beaches, lakes, and the Vancouver Aquarium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Stanley Park is culturally significant as it represents the relationship between natural environment and cultural elements developed over time. It is also a traditional territory of multiple coastal Indigenous peoples.
world knowledge.Details: Stanley Park is home to a variety of attractions, including the Vancouver Aquarium, Lost Lagoon, Beaver Lake, and the Stanley Park Railway. It also features numerous monuments, playgrounds, sandy beaches, gardens, and recreational facilities. The park is known for its dense forest, which includes tall Douglas fir, western red cedar, western hemlock, and Sitka spruce trees.

image_name: National Museum of Art of Romania

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Art of Romania
world knowledge.Address: Royal Palace, Revolution Square, Bucharest, Romania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Art of Romania is located in the Royal Palace in Revolution Square, central Bucharest. It features collections of medieval and modern Romanian art, as well as the international collection assembled by the Romanian royal family. The museum was damaged during the 1989 Romanian Revolution that led to the downfall of Nicolae Ceaușescu. In 2000, part of the museum reopened to the public, housing the modern Romanian collection and the international collection; the comprehensive Medieval art collection, which now features works salvaged from monasteries destroyed during the Ceaușescu era, reopened in spring 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The largest exhibition of French painting in Central and Eastern Europe since 1945, featuring masterpieces by painters such as Poussin, Chardin, Ingres, David, Delacroix, Corot, Cézanne, Matisse, Picasso, and Braque.
The museum was damaged during the revolution that led to the downfall of Nicolae Ceaușescu.
Part of the museum reopened to the public, housing the modern Romanian collection and the international collection.
The comprehensive Medieval art collection reopened, featuring works salvaged from monasteries destroyed during the Ceaușescu era.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its extensive collections of medieval and modern Romanian art, as well as the international collection assembled by the Romanian royal family. It also plays a role in preserving works salvaged from monasteries destroyed during the Ceaușescu era.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features collections of medieval and modern Romanian art, as well as the international collection assembled by the Romanian royal family. It includes works by Old Masters such as Domenico Veneziano, El Greco, Tintoretto, Jan van Eyck, Jan Brueghel the Elder, Peter Paul Rubens, and Rembrandt, plus a smattering of works by impressionists such as Claude Monet and Alfred Sisley. The European Museum Art Gallery was reopened in 2000, and the Romanian Modern Art Gallery reopened in spring 2001.

world knowledge.Name: Nara Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nara Park was established in 1880 as one of Japan's oldest parks. It expanded in 1889 to include Todai-ji, Kasugano, and Mount Wakakusa, reaching 535 hectares. The park's designation was later reduced to 500 hectares (1949-1951) and officially set at 502 hectares in 1960 under the Urban Park Act. The park is home to over 1,200 wild sika deer, considered sacred due to local folklore involving Takemikazuchi, a deity of Kasuga Grand Shrine. The deer were later designated as a natural monument after World War II.

Major_Events.Description: The park was initially established with a 14-hectare area within Kōfuku-ji's grounds.
Todai-ji, Kasugano, and Mount Wakakusa were added, expanding the park to 535 hectares.
Park designation within temple grounds was revoked, reducing the area to 500 hectares.

Major_Events.Event: Official designation under Urban Park Act
Major_Events.Description: The park was officially designated as Nara Park with an area of 502 hectares.
Due to overpopulation and environmental concerns, a culling program was initiated, with a limit of 120 deer to be culled in 2017.
Travel restrictions led to fewer tourists feeding the deer, causing them to forage outside the park and raising concerns about their health and safety.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Nara Park is a natural park featuring diverse vegetation, including pine trees, cherry blossom trees, maple trees, plum trees, Japanese cedar, and Japanese pieris. The park also includes the grounds of several historic temples and shrines, such as Tōdai-ji, Kōfuku-ji, and Kasuga Grand Shrine, which are architectural landmarks in their own right.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nara Park is culturally significant as one of Japan's oldest parks and a designated 'Place of Scenic Beauty.' It is home to over 1,200 wild sika deer, which are considered sacred and are protected as a natural monument. The park surrounds several World Heritage Sites, including Todai-ji, Kofuku-ji, Kasuga Grand Shrine, and the Kasugayama Primeval Forest. The park's deer have been protected for over 1,000 years as messengers of the deity Takemikazuchi, reflecting deep cultural and religious ties.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and conservation area for wildlife and historic sites.
world knowledge.Details: The park is serviced by Kintetsu Nara Station and is accessible via the Kintetsu Line from Osaka-Namba Station. Visitors can purchase 'deer-crackers' (Shika-senbei) to feed the deer, which are sold exclusively by the WNOW company. The deer in Nara Park form a unique genetic population, distinct from other sika deer on the Kii Peninsula, due to centuries of protection. The park has faced challenges with deer overpopulation, leading to culling programs and measures to protect both the deer and visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Biarritz
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Biarritz has a rich history dating back to the Middle Paleolithic era. It became a notable whaling center in the Middle Ages and later transitioned into a luxurious seaside tourist destination in the 18th century. The city gained prominence when Empress Eugénie built a palace there in 1854, attracting European royalty and aristocrats. Biarritz also played a role in post-World War II education for American servicemen and became a hub for surfing culture in the 1950s.
