Major_Events.Description: Empress Eugénie built a palace on the beach, which later became the Hôtel du Palais, elevating Biarritz's status as a luxury destination.
After World War II, Biarritz hosted a temporary university campus for demobilized American servicemen, operating until 1946.
Surfing was first practiced in Europe at Biarritz by an American visitor, leading to the city's reputation as a surfing hotspot.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Biarritz features a mix of luxurious seaside architecture, including the Hôtel du Palais, casinos, and Belle Époque-style buildings. The city also has historical structures like the église Saint-Martin and remnants of the château de Ferragus.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Biarritz is culturally significant as a historic whaling town, a luxurious spa and seaside resort, and a pioneering European surfing destination. It has hosted royalty, aristocrats, and celebrities, contributing to its reputation as a glamorous tourist spot.
world knowledge.Details: Biarritz is known for its surfing culture, hosting world-class competitions like the Quiksilver/Roxy Jam. The city also has a strong rugby tradition with Biarritz Olympique and celebrates Basque culture through events like Saint Martin's Day and the Biarritz en été music festival. The city's economy is now modern, with tourism as a key sector, and it participates in the management of the BAB Airport with Bayonne and Anglet.

world knowledge.Name: Great Seto Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Seto Bridge was envisioned as early as 1889 by Jinnojo Ōkubo, who advocated for better connectivity in Shikoku. The project gained urgency after a 1955 ferry disaster that killed 171 people, including 100 students. Construction began in 1978 after delays caused by the 1973 oil shock and was completed in 1988. The bridge was part of the Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project and remains the only route in the project to carry rail traffic.

Major_Events.Description: A collision of two ferries in dense fog off Takamatsu killed 171 people, including 100 students, prompting calls for a safer crossing.
The bridge was officially opened to road and rail traffic by then-Crown Prince Akihito on April 10, 1988.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Double-decked bridge system with an upper deck carrying 4 lanes of highway traffic and a lower deck carrying 2 rail lines. The longest span is the Minami Bisan-Seto Bridge at 1,100 m (3,600 ft). Constructed using 3.646 million cubic meters of concrete and 705,000 tons of steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes Japan's engineering prowess and fulfills a century-old vision of connecting Honshū and Shikoku, improving transportation and communication. It also stands as a memorial to the 1955 ferry disaster victims.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (road and rail connectivity between Honshū and Shikoku)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge consists of 11 bridges, six of which are separately named. It reduced the crossing time from about an hour by ferry to 20 minutes by car or train. The lower deck was designed to accommodate future Shinkansen tracks. The toll fee at opening was ¥6300 for a one-way drive.

world knowledge.Name: Whitesands Bay (Pembrokeshire)
world knowledge.Area: St David's peninsula, Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, Wales
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Whitesands Bay, also known as Porth Mawr, is a Blue Flag beach with a rich history. It is believed that St. Patrick set sail from this beach in 432 AD to convert Ireland to Christianity. The area has been a site of religious significance, with a Celtic chapel dedicated to St. Patrick located nearby. The bay has also been associated with St. David, who may have been educated at Ty Gwyn, a white farmhouse overlooking the beach. The burial ground in the area was in use from the 8th to 11th centuries, and remains have been moved to the National Museum of Wales to protect them from coastal erosion. At very low tide, the remains of an ancient, submerged forest can be seen on the beach.

Major_Events.Description: St. Patrick is believed to have set sail from Whitesands Bay to convert Ireland to Christianity.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Whitesands Bay is culturally significant due to its association with St. Patrick and St. David, as well as its historical use as a burial ground and site of religious activity. The remains of an ancient, submerged forest and animal remains found on the beach add to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Details: Whitesands Bay is described as the best surfing beach in Pembrokeshire. The area is dominated by Carn Llidi, a rocky outcrop, and is accessible via the Pembrokeshire Coast Path, which leads to other secluded bays and offers views of Ramsey Island. The site of a Celtic chapel dedicated to St. Patrick is located near the bay, and the remains of an ancient forest and animals have been found on the beach.

world knowledge.Name: Melbourne Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Melbourne Airport, also known as Tullamarine Airport, opened on 1 July 1970, replacing Essendon Airport as Melbourne's primary international airport. It was constructed due to the limitations of Essendon Airport, which could not handle increasing passenger demand and larger jets. The site at Tullamarine was chosen after considering several alternatives, and the airport has since undergone numerous expansions and upgrades to accommodate growing traffic and modern aircraft like the Airbus A380.

Major_Events.Description: The airport officially opened, replacing Essendon Airport as Melbourne's main international airport.
The airport was privatized and acquired by Australia Pacific Airports Corporation on a 50-year lease.
Melbourne Airport became the first in Australia to handle the Airbus A380, with a test flight occurring on 14 November 2005.
The expanded Terminal 4 opened, dedicated to budget airlines and linked to Terminal 3.
The Australian government approved the construction of a third runway to increase capacity, with completion expected by 2031.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Melbourne Airport features a mix of modern and functional design, with four main terminals (T1-T4) serving domestic and international flights. The airport includes grooved asphalt runways, multi-level car parks, and a satellite concourse for international flights. The control towers are notable, with the newer one standing at 75 meters tall. The terminals are equipped with aerobridges, retail spaces, and airline lounges.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Melbourne Airport is a critical infrastructure hub for Victoria, facilitating tourism, trade, and connectivity. It is the second busiest airport in Australia and serves as a major hub for airlines like Qantas and Virgin Australia. The airport's growth reflects Melbourne's status as a global city and its importance in Australia's aviation history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International and domestic air travel hub, including passenger, cargo, and freight services.
world knowledge.Details: Melbourne Airport operates 24/7 and handles over 35 million passengers annually. It has two intersecting runways, with plans for a third runway to be completed by 2031. The airport is accessible via the Tullamarine Freeway and SkyBus services, with a future rail link (Melbourne Airport Rail) expected by 2033. The airport has won numerous awards for service and construction excellence, including recognition from IATA and Skytrax.

world knowledge.Name: ISKCON Temple, Bengaluru
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sri Radha Krishna-Chandra Temple is one of the largest Krishna-Hindu temples in the world. It was inaugurated in May 1997 by the ninth president of India, Shankar Dayal Sharma. The society was registered in 1978 under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960. The temple is dedicated to Hindu deities Radha Krishna and propagates monotheism as mentioned in Chandogya Upanishad.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was inaugurated by the ninth president of India, Shankar Dayal Sharma.

The temple was inaugurated in a grand ceremony on 14 June 2022 by Shri Ram Nath Kovind, Former President of India, on the occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, Founder-Acharya of ISKCON.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple is constructed in the Dravidian style of architecture as per traditional Shilpa shastras. It features a gold-plated dhwaja-stambha (flag post) 17 m high and a gold plated kalash shikhara 8.5 m high. The design and aesthetics, including the seven doors to the sanctum, are inspired by the Sri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple in Tirumala.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The temple is culturally significant as it propagates the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and the practice of bhakti yoga. It is one of the largest Krishna-Hindu temples in the world and plays a vital role in promoting Vedic wisdom globally.
world knowledge.Details: ISKCON Bangalore has six shrines and celebrates festivals related to avatars of Lord Vishnu or Vedic culture. The temple provides free food to those in need through the Akshaya Patra Foundation, which has received praise from former US President Barack Obama for feeding and educating children across India.

world knowledge.Name: RDS Arena
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The RDS Arena was developed to host equestrian events, primarily the annual Dublin Horse Show, which was first held there in 1881. The site was acquired by the Royal Dublin Society (RDS) in 1879. Over the years, it has evolved into a multi-purpose sports stadium hosting rugby, soccer, wrestling, and concerts. The arena has undergone several renovations and expansions to accommodate various events and increase its capacity.

Major_Events.Description: The first Dublin Horse Show was held at the RDS Arena, marking the beginning of its primary function as an equestrian venue.
The stadium hosted its first international football match between Ireland and Wales.
Leinster Rugby played their first game at the RDS Arena against the Cardiff Blues, winning 34–15.
The arena hosted a WWE event featuring notable wrestlers like Kurt Angle, Eddie Guerrero, and John Cena.
The arena served as the principal venue for this major religious event, promoting awareness of the Eucharist in the Catholic Church.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The RDS Arena features a mix of permanent and demountable stands. The Grandstand and Anglesea Stand are permanent, while the north and south stands are removable for equestrian events. The Grandstand was rebuilt in 2006, and a roof was added in 2008–09. The arena has a grass surface and floodlights for evening events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The RDS Arena is culturally significant as a historic venue for equestrian events, rugby, and concerts. It has hosted major international events, including the Dublin Horse Show, rugby matches, and performances by world-renowned artists. Its role in promoting sports and entertainment in Ireland makes it a landmark of national importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose sports stadium (equestrian events, rugby, soccer, concerts)
world knowledge.Details: The RDS Arena has a capacity of 18,500 for sporting events and over 40,000 for concerts. It is owned by the Royal Dublin Society and has been the home of Leinster Rugby since 2007. Plans for redevelopment include increasing the capacity to 25,000 and selling naming rights to fund the project. The arena has hosted numerous high-profile concerts, sports events, and religious gatherings, making it a versatile and iconic venue in Ireland.

world knowledge.Name: Sansha Yongxing Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sansha Yongxing Airport is a civilian-military dual-use airport located on Yongxing Island, the largest of the disputed Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. It was expanded in 1990 to increase the combat range of Chinese warplanes. Further construction and reclamation of land commenced in 2012 to lengthen the airstrip, completed in October 2014.

Major_Events.Description: Military drills with fighter aircraft landing and taking off at Yongxing Island Airport were carried out and telecast on CCTV in December 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a runway that is 2,700 metres long, capable of handling any fourth generation fighter aircraft of the Chinese airforce such as the Sukhoi Su-30MK2. It includes four hangars, a radar navigation station, four large fuel tanks, and a two-storey 3,500 square metres terminal building with control tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a strategic military and civilian hub in the disputed Paracel Islands, enhancing China's presence and operational capabilities in the South China Sea.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is operated by the Sansha Yongxing Airport Administration (HNA Infrastructure Investment Group) and the PLA Air Force. It serves Sansha, Hainan, and has facilities for domestic arrival and departure areas with three gates to handle civil airliners.

world knowledge.Name: Chagres National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Chagres National Park is a nature park and protected area created in 1986, located in the Panamá and Colón provinces, in the Eastern sector of the Panama Canal. It was established to preserve the natural forest that composes it.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is considered a Key Biodiversity Area of international significance and has been designated an Important Bird Area (IBA) by BirdLife International. It contains tropical rain forests and a set of rivers which provide sufficient water to guarantee the operation of the Gatun Lake, the main lake of the Panama Canal.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains the Chagres River and the Gatun River, which are crucial for the Panama Canal's operation. The highest point of the park is Cerro Jefe, at 1,007 m above sea level.

world knowledge.Name: Abbeville County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Abbeville County Courthouse, built in 1908, is the sixth courthouse to serve Abbeville County. It was designed in the Beaux Arts style by William Augustus Edwards. The courthouse is located on land that once housed the law firm where John C. Calhoun practiced early in his career. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 30, 1981.

Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was built in the Beaux Arts style by architect William Augustus Edwards.
The courthouse was renovated by Lyles, Bissett, Carlisle, and Wolff of Columbia.
The courthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 30, 1981.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux Arts style, designed by William Augustus Edwards. An arcade connects it to the adjoining Abbeville Opera House and Municipal Center.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is historically significant as it is part of the Abbeville Historic District and is associated with John C. Calhoun, a prominent political figure in U.S. history. It also represents the architectural work of William Augustus Edwards, who designed several other South Carolina courthouses and academic buildings.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse includes a portrait of John C. Calhoun in its central hallway. It is part of the Courthouses in South Carolina Designed by William Augustus Edwards Thematic Resource and is connected to the Abbeville Opera House and Municipal Center.

world knowledge.Name: Arena AufSchalke
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Plans to construct a new stadium emerged in the late 1990s to replace the outdated Parkstadion. Following Schalke 04's 1996–97 UEFA Cup victory and anticipating the club's 100th anniversary in 2004, a contract to build the new stadium was awarded to the German construction firm HBM in 1998. The Veltins-Arena is located near the old Parkstadion on a club-owned property known as 'Berger Feld.' Due to the presence of two mine shafts beneath the site, the stadium's main axis was rotated to ensure structural integrity.

Major_Events.Description: The final between AS Monaco and Porto drew over 53,000 spectators.
The stadium hosted five matches, including a quarter-final.
Set a world record for ice hockey attendance with 77,803 spectators.
Achieved a record-breaking attendance of 20,210, the most ever at a darts event.
The stadium hosted four matches.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Veltins-Arena features a Teflon-coated fiberglass canvas retractable roof that spans the entire venue and is supported by a rectangular truss and 24 steel pylons. The pitch can slide out of the stadium, allowing for optimal grass growth and versatility for various events. The stadium also features a centrally suspended scoreboard, a first in football stadiums. The foundation was created out of cast concrete and 600,000 cubic metres of packed slag, a waste product from the steel smelting industry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Veltins-Arena is culturally significant as it serves as the home ground for FC Schalke 04 and has hosted major international events such as the UEFA Champions League final, FIFA World Cup matches, and the IIHF World Championship. Its innovative features like the retractable roof and slide-out pitch have inspired other stadiums globally.
world knowledge.Details: The Veltins-Arena has a capacity of 62,271 for league matches and 54,740 for international matches. It features extensive catering facilities, including 15 small restaurants, 50 grilling stations, and 35 cafés, all supplied by a 5km beer-line capable of dispensing 52,000 liters of beer per match day. The stadium has hosted concerts, sports events, and other major events, making it a versatile venue.

world knowledge.Name: Cusworth Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cusworth Hall is an 18th-century Grade I listed country house built by George Platt for William Wrightson. It replaced a previous house and was further altered by James Paine in 1749–1753. The Wrightson family held the lordship of Cusworth since 1669. The property passed through several generations of the Wrightson family, undergoing various alterations and expansions. In 1961, Doncaster Rural District Council purchased the hall and parkland, converting it into a museum.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase by Doncaster Rural District Council
Major_Events.Description: The hall and parkland were purchased by the council, leading to its conversion into a museum.
A £7.5 million renovation project was undertaken, involving conservation repairs to the hall and restoration of the landscape gardens.
The hall reopened with new displays documenting the history of South Yorkshire.
The first 5 km parkrun event was held in the grounds of Cusworth Hall.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cusworth Hall is a Georgian country house designed in the Palladian style by George Platt. It features a rectangular 6 x 5 bay plan main block linked to service wings. The house is constructed of ashlar with slate roofs. Later additions by James Paine include a chapel and library. The hall has decorative outbuildings such as a Brew House, Stable Block, and Lodge, as well as a decorative garden called Lady Isabella's Garden.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Cusworth Hall is a significant example of Georgian architecture and a well-preserved country house. It serves as a museum documenting the history of South Yorkshire and is a valued resource for local residents, students, and school groups.
world knowledge.Details: Cusworth Hall and Park underwent an extensive £7.5 million renovation between 2002 and 2005. The hall reopened to the public on 23 May 2007 and now hosts seasonal exhibitions, events, and activities. It is also the venue for a weekly 5 km parkrun. The museum offers educational sessions to schools and communities.

world knowledge.Name: University of Essex
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Essex is a public research university established by royal charter in 1965. It is one of the original plate glass universities. The university comprises three campuses in Essex, with its primary campus in Wivenhoe Park, Colchester. It has a diverse student community and partnerships with over 100 global higher education institutions.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Essex received university status by royal charter.
The Department of Government received Regius Professorship conferred by Queen Elizabeth II.
The university was awarded the Queen's Anniversary Prize for advancing human rights.
The university was awarded the Queen's Anniversary Prize for social and economic research.
The university was named University of the Year at the Times Higher Education Awards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university is typical of England's 1960s universities, heavily influenced by the international Brutalist architecture movement. It features prefabricated concrete and glass structures, including residential towers, The Hexagon, and the Albert Sloman Library.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Essex is culturally significant for its contributions to human rights, social and economic research, and its role as one of the original plate glass universities. It has produced notable alumni, including Nobel laureates, and has been recognized with prestigious awards.
world knowledge.Details: The university is organized into three faculties, comprising 21 schools and departments. It has three flagship institutes: the Human Rights Centre, the Institute for Analytics and Data Science, and the Institute for Social and Economic Research. The university has a strong international reputation and partnerships with over 100 global higher education institutions.

world knowledge.Name: Forum Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Forum Theatre, originally named the State Theatre, was built in 1929 as a historic theatre and former cinema. It was designed by US architect John Eberson in collaboration with local firm Bohringer, Taylor & Johnson. The theatre was renamed in 1962, converted into two cinemas in 1963, and later used for religious services before becoming a live music and event venue in 1995. It has since hosted numerous concerts, comedy acts, and film festivals.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened on 23 February 1929 with silent films 'The Fleet’s In' and 'The Cameraman.'
The first 'talkie' film, 'The Doctor's Secret,' premiered on 6 April 1929.
The theatre was converted into two separate cinemas, Forum I and Forum II.
The theatre was purchased by a Christian organization and fell into disrepair.
The theatre was purchased by David Marriner's Staged Developments Australia and redeveloped into a live music and event venue.
The theatre underwent a major renovation to restore its original features, including mosaic tiles and statues.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Forum Theatre features an exotic Moorish-style exterior with minarets and a clock tower. The interior is designed as a 'Florentine courtyard' with a curved, dark-blue ceiling mimicking a twilight sky. It is an 'atmospheric theatre,' a style pioneered by John Eberson, with elaborate eclectic Spanish Baroque/Renaissance influences.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Forum Theatre is listed on the Victorian Heritage Register and classified by the National Trust of Australia. It is a significant example of 1920s 'picture palace' architecture and has been a central venue for live music, comedy, and film festivals in Melbourne.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Live music, comedy, and film venue
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a capacity of 2,000 standing (Forum 1) and 520 seated (Forum 2). It hosts events such as the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, Melbourne International Film Festival, and Music Victoria Awards. In 2013, there was a proposal to build an apartment tower adjacent to the theatre, which was opposed and ultimately blocked. In 2024, urgent exterior restoration works were planned due to unstable decorative elements.

world knowledge.Name: St. Stephen's Basilica
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Length: 87.4 metres, Width: 55 metres, Height: 96 metres
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Stephen's Basilica is a Roman Catholic basilica in Budapest, Hungary, named in honor of Stephen, the first King of Hungary. It is the third largest church building in present-day Hungary and the largest in Budapest. The site was originally the location of the Hetz-Theater, known for hosting animal fights. After a devastating flood in 1838, the high ground provided refuge, leading to donations for the church's construction. Initially planned to be named after Saint Leopold, it was later dedicated to Saint Stephen I of Hungary. The church suffered serious damage during World War II but provided shelter for refugees and protected valuable collections of the Hungarian National Archives.

Major_Events.Description: The basilica served as the main venue for the 34th International Eucharistic Congress in May 1938.
The church suffered serious damage during World War II but provided shelter for many refugees and protected valuable collections of the Hungarian National Archives.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical and neo-Renaissance style, designed by József Hild and later modified by Miklós Ybl. The basilica has a Greek cross ground plan, two bell towers, and a dome. The tympanum over the main entrance holds an 1893 mosaic designed by Mór Than. The interior features mosaics, bronze reliefs, and statues by various artists.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Stephen's Basilica is a significant historical landmark within Budapest's UNESCO World Heritage Site Buffer Zone. It is the most important church building in Hungary and a major tourist attraction. The basilica symbolizes the equal importance of worldly and spiritual thinking, as it is one of the two tallest buildings in Budapest, equal in height to the Hungarian Parliament Building.
world knowledge.Details: The basilica has two bell towers with six bells, including the largest bell in Hungary, weighing 9250 kg. The dome can be accessed by elevator or 364 steps for a panoramic view. Organ concerts are performed every Monday, and the basilica hosts various musical performances. A Christmas fair is held in the square in front of the basilica during the Advent season, and the façade is decorated with special light paintings. Part of the 2016 movie Inferno was filmed in St. Stephen Square in front of the basilica.

world knowledge.Name: Dunnet Head Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dunnet Head Lighthouse is an active 19th century lighthouse that stands on the 300-foot (91 m) cliff top of Easter Head on Dunnet Head. The lighthouse was built in 1831 by Robert Stevenson, grandfather of Robert Louis Stevenson. It was automated in 1989, and the keepers were withdrawn. It is now checked remotely by the Northern Lighthouse Board operations centre in Edinburgh.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was automated, and the keepers were withdrawn.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: masonry tower, cylindrical tower with balcony and lantern, white tower with black lantern and ochre trim
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a category B listed building and stands on the northernmost point of the mainland of Great Britain.

world knowledge.Name: Pasinger Fabrik
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pasinger Fabrik was built in 1895 by architect August Exter as a manufacturing plant for the Heymann shoe factory. After a fire in 1904, it was acquired by household appliances manufacturer Ritter. In 1986, the city of Munich bought the buildings to repurpose them as a cultural center.

Major_Events.Description: A fire occurred at the factory, leading to its acquisition by Ritter.
The city of Munich purchased the buildings to transform them into a cultural center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Industrial buildings designed by August Exter.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pasinger Fabrik serves as a cultural hub, hosting theatre performances, concerts, exhibitions, and family-oriented projects. It is home to Munich's smallest opera house and the influential theatre VIEL LÄRM UM NICHTS, which has contributed significantly to its cultural development.
world knowledge.Details: The cultural center features the VIEL LÄRM UM NICHTS theatre, a restaurant, a bar, and a gallery. The theatre, founded by Margit Carls and Andreas Seyferth in 1985, is known for experimental performances and adaptations of classic plays. Pasinger Fabrik also hosts temporary exhibitions and small-scale operas or operettas.

image_name: Will Rogers Shrine of the Sun

world knowledge.Name: Will Rogers Shrine of the Sun
world knowledge.Address: 4250 Cheyenne Mountain Zoo Road, Colorado Springs, Colorado
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Will Rogers Shrine of the Sun is a commemorative tower and chapel on Cheyenne Mountain, built in 1937 by Spencer Penrose. It honors Will Rogers, the American humorist who died in a plane crash in 1935 during the shrine's construction. The shrine also serves as a tomb for Spencer Penrose and his wife Julie Penrose, who were prominent developers in Colorado Springs.

Major_Events.Description: The shrine was completed and dedicated on September 6, 1937, as a memorial to Will Rogers and the Penroses.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The shrine was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its artistic and architectural qualities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shrine is a 100-foot (30 m) tall, five-story observation tower made of Romanesque Revival architecture with buttresses, an ornately decorated iron and brass door, and narrow leaded windows. It is constructed of granite, steel, cement, iron, and brass, with a ceramic tile roof. The interior features terrazzo floors, marble, and ironwork. The adjoining one-story chapel contains European and Eastern works of art.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The shrine is culturally significant as a memorial to Will Rogers, Spencer Penrose, and Julie Penrose, as well as for its artistic and architectural qualities. It also depicts the history of the Pikes Peak Region through murals and serves as a notable landmark in Colorado Springs.
world knowledge.Details: The shrine includes a 340-square-foot (32 m2) mural by Randall Davey depicting the Pikes Peak Region's history. The site features a stone gateway, a stone wall made from pink granite, and landscaping with native plants. Westminster chimes are played every quarter-hour or hour, audible up to 20 miles (32 km) away. The shrine is illuminated by floodlights at night.

world knowledge.Name: Tidal Basin
world knowledge.Address: West Potomac Park, Washington, D.C., U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tidal Basin is a man-made reservoir designed to serve as a visual centerpiece and to flush the Washington Channel. It was initially named the Tidal Reservoir and later Twining Lake. The Basin has been a focal point for events like the National Cherry Blossom Festival and has undergone various modifications and restorations over the years.

Major_Events.Description: A racially-segregated beach opened in front of the site of the present-day Jefferson Memorial. It attracted large crowds but was dismantled in 1925 due to opposition to integration.
Congressman Wilbur Mills was involved in an incident where a stripper, Fanne Foxe, jumped into the Tidal Basin after being stopped by police.
The National Park Service announced plans to renovate the seawall to address flooding caused by sea level rise and land subsidence.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tidal Basin is an artificial reservoir with inlet and outlet gates designed to manage water flow and sediment. The nearby Kutz Memorial Bridge is a multi-span plate girder bridge made of concrete and steel with granite facing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tidal Basin is a focal point of the National Cherry Blossom Festival and is surrounded by significant memorials like the Jefferson Memorial, Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, and Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial. It also has historical significance due to events like the Tidal Basin Bathing Beach and the Wilbur Mills incident.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational and aesthetic purposes, including paddle-boat rentals and serving as a centerpiece for the National Cherry Blossom Festival.
world knowledge.Details: The Tidal Basin's seawall is being renovated to address flooding issues. The project includes raising the seawall and widening walkways. The Basin's gates are maintained by the Army Corps of Engineers, and water from the Basin is used to fill the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

world knowledge.Name: Indooroopilly Railway Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Indooroopilly Railway Bridge was built as part of the quadruplication of the Ipswich Line. It was constructed just upstream and parallel to the Albert Bridge, linking Indooroopilly and Chelmer stations. The bridge was designed by the Coordinator-General's Department and constructed by the Electric Power Transmission Pty Coy, with its superstructure fabricated in Italy by Societa Anonima Elettrificazione S.P.A.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge is being refurbished, including cleaning, sandblasting, repainting, replacing bridge transoms, and adding a walkway and handrails for future maintenance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel truss design with two long spans and one central pier. The superstructure is a parallel chord truss bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important part of the rail transport infrastructure in Queensland, facilitating connectivity between Indooroopilly and Chelmer stations.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge crosses the Brisbane River and is officially named the Indooroopilly Railway Bridge. It was opened in 1957.

world knowledge.Name: Patong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Patong refers to the beach and town on Phuket's west coast. It became popular with Western tourists, especially Europeans, in the late-1980s. It has numerous hotels and the area has expanded into a tourist place.

Major_Events.Description: On 26 December 2004, Patong Beach along with many other areas along the west coast of Phuket and Thailand were struck by a tsunami caused by the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake. The wave caused a great deal of destruction to the waterfront of the beach and immediately inland. Patong was one of the worst affected areas of Phuket, although the destruction was not as bad as nearby Khao Lak. Patong has largely recovered since the tsunami.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Patong Beach is the main tourist resort on the island of Phuket and is the centre of Phuket's nightlife and shopping. It is known for its nightlife and 2850-metre beach that runs the entire length of Patong's west side.
world knowledge.Details: Patong Beach is known for its nightlife, centered in two main areas, Bangla Road and the "Paradise Complex". Prostitution in Thailand is illegal but tolerated, as is the case in Patong. As of 2015, the waters off Patong Beach exceeded Thai Pollution Control Department standards for fecal coliform bacteria (FCB) and enterococci bacteria. Many households discharge their wastewater untreated into canals and the sea. The municipal wastewater treatment plant is nearing its capacity of 28,000 m3 a day, with an upgrade expected to increase capacity by an extra 9,000 m3 per day by 2018. Bangla is considered the most popular walking street in Phuket, lined with beer bars and go-go bars.

world knowledge.Name: Pakokku Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main bridge: 3.4 km (2.1 mi) long; Motorway: 4 km (2.5 mi); Railroad: 6.17 km (3.83 mi); Motorway width: 28 ft; Roadway width: 14 ft; Pedestrian walkways: 3 ft 3 in; Clearance area: 52 ft high, 262 ft wide; Approach bridge: 512 ft long; Approach embankment: 850 ft long
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pakokku Bridge is a rail and road bridge across the Irrawaddy River in Myanmar's Pakokku town. It is the longest bridge in Myanmar and part of the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway. The bridge was inaugurated on 1 January 2012 by Vice-president Tin Aung Myint Oo.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was inaugurated on 1 January 2012 by Vice-president Tin Aung Myint Oo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Broad crested type bridge with a 28 ft wide motorway, a 14 ft wide roadway, and two pedestrian walkways measuring 3 ft 3 in. It has a 52 ft high and 262 ft wide clearance area, a 512 ft long approach bridge, and an 850 ft long approach embankment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is the longest in Myanmar and a key part of the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway, enhancing regional connectivity and economic development.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge connects the town of Pakokku with the administrative district of Nyaung-U. It was designed by Crown Advanced Construction and the Myanmar Ministry of Construction.

world knowledge.Name: Zabaykalsky National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zaybaykalsky National Park covers the middle section of the eastern shore of Lake Baikal, the west slope of the Barguzin mountains to the east, the Ushkany Islands, and the only large peninsula on the lake, Svyatoy Nos ("Holy Nose"). Of the 2,690 km2 (1,040 sq mi) of the park, 38.8 km2 are protected water areas of the lake itself. The park is bounded on the west by the shores of Lake Baikal, on the north by the Barguzin Nature Reserve, and on the south and east by the Barguzin mountain range.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zabaykalsky National Park is significant for its diverse ecosystems, including the East Siberian taiga ecoregion, and its role in preserving the unique flora and fauna of the region, such as the Baikal seal and the black-capped marmot. The park also contains archaeological sites with evidence of human habitation from the Neolithic age.
world knowledge.Details: The park is characterized by steep terrain, with 55% of the park on a slope of more than 26°. The Svyatoy Noy peninsula is known for its mountain complex and "singing sand" Marokov beach. The Ushkany Islands are famous as the central home of the Baikal seal and contain caves with Neolithic evidence. The climate is subarctic with dry winters, and the forests display strong altitude zoning with conifers dominating. Tourism is encouraged, with certain sensitive areas requiring special permits. Activities include hiking, ice fishing, and cross-country skiing. The park management runs a floating ecotourist hostel and offers guest cabins.

world knowledge.Name: Air and Space Museum
world knowledge.Details: Air and Space Museum may refer to:

world knowledge.Name: Kabul Zoo
world knowledge.Address: District 3, Kabul, Afghanistan, adjacent to the Deh Mazang Circle
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kabul Zoo was inaugurated in 1967 with a focus on Afghan fauna. It suffered significant damage during the 1990s civil war, including shelling and the loss of animals. The Taliban initially considered closing it but kept it open after research showed that Muhammad kept pets. The zoo has been a popular tourist attraction, visited by around a million people annually.

Major_Events.Description: The zoo suffered significant damage during the civil war, including shelling, loss of animals, and smuggling of exotic species.
Marjan the Lion, the most famous resident of the zoo, died and was buried there. A bronze statue of Marjan stands at the zoo's entrance.
The zoo took in four white lions that were saved from a smuggling attempt.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo is located on the bank of the Kabul River and adjacent to the Deh Mazang Circle. It is next to City Park and nearby the Gardens of Babur and Kabul University.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kabul Zoo is one of the popular tourist attractions in Kabul, visited by around a million people annually. It has been a significant part of the city's cultural and social life, surviving through periods of conflict and political change.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo once had more than 500 animals, including 45 species of birds and mammals, and 36 species of fish. It generated 15 million afghanis ($268,000) in revenue in 2012, which increased to 33 million in 2020. The zoo is planned to be expanded from its current 17.5 acres of land to 71 acres.

world knowledge.Name: Stade Ernest-Wallon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stade Ernest-Wallon was built after Stade Toulousain's original home ground, the Stade des Ponts Jumeaux, was expropriated by the local government for a motorway. The club was offered land and funding to build a new stadium, which opened on 4 December 1983 with an international rugby match between France and Romania.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was inaugurated with a first-division FIRA Trophy match where France's national rugby union team defeated Romania.
Hosted a single pool match between Romania and Canada.
Japan recorded their biggest winning margin over Tonga (33 points) in a relocated test match.

Major_Events.Event: France Sevens and France Women's Sevens
Major_Events.Description: Became the new venue for these annual rugby sevens tournaments, replacing Stade Jean-Bouin in Paris.

Major_Events.Event: Toulouse Olympique's First Super League Game
Major_Events.Description: Hosted Toulouse Olympique's debut in Super League against Huddersfield Giants.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium primarily designed for rugby, with a capacity of 19,500 spectators. No specific architectural style is mentioned.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Described as a 'temple to the oval ball,' it is the home ground for Stade Toulousain (rugby union) and Toulouse Olympique (rugby league). It has hosted international rugby matches and tournaments, contributing to the sport's growth in France.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Rugby stadium (union and league), also used for other sporting events.
Notable_Visitors: New Zealand National Rugby League Team
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was expanded in 2003. It has hosted international rugby league matches, including a 2004 friendly between France and Australia. Catalans Dragons played a Super League game here in 2013 to promote rugby league in France. The stadium is also used for the France Sevens tournaments, where the women's series champion is crowned.

world knowledge.Name: Earth and Man National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Earth and Man National Museum is a mineralogical museum located in the center of Sofia, Bulgaria. It was founded on 1 January 1986 and opened to visitors on 19 June 1987. The museum is housed in a historic building constructed at the end of the 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The museum opened its doors to visitors on 19 June 1987.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is situated in a reconstructed and adapted historic building from the late 19th century. It includes exhibition halls, stock premises, laboratories, a video room, and a conference room.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is one of the largest mineralogical museums in the world, housing 40% of all known naturally occurring minerals and man-made ceramics prepared by Bulgarian scientists. It also hosts various exhibitions and cultural events, including chamber music concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection covers a wide range of minerals and ceramics, and it often hosts exhibitions on various topics and cultural events.

world knowledge.Name: Ponte Sisto
world knowledge.Address: Connects Via dei Pettinari in the Rione of Regola to Piazza Trilussa in Trastevere
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ponte Sisto was commissioned by Pope Sixtus IV and built by architect Baccio Pontelli, reusing the foundations of the ancient Pons Aurelius bridge, which was destroyed in the early Middle Ages. The bridge was named after Pope Sixtus IV and has undergone several modifications over the centuries, including the addition and later removal of pedestrian gangways.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was built by Pope Sixtus IV using foundations from the ancient Pons Aurelius.
A brawl between Corsican soldiers and Frenchmen led to the disbanding of the Corsican Guard.
The cast-iron pedestrian gangways added in 1877 were removed to restore the bridge's original appearance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge features an 'oculus' or eye in its central spandrel to reduce pressure during floods. It originally had two marble slabs with Latin inscriptions, now replaced due to vandalism. The bridge carries water pipes for the Acqua Paola.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ponte Sisto is a historic bridge connecting key areas of Rome, including the lively Campo de' Fiori and Trastevere. It played a role in the city's infrastructure and social life, particularly during the Jubilee events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Pedestrian bridge spanning the Tiber River
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was built using blocks from the Colosseum. It was designed to prevent crowding disasters like those at the Bridge of S. Angelo during the Jubilee of 1450. The Fontanone di Ponte Sisto fountain once stood nearby, relaying water from the Acqua Paola.

world knowledge.Name: Cavan Courthouse
world knowledge.Address: Farnham Street, Cavan, County Cavan, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cavan Courthouse is a judicial and municipal facility in Farnham Street, Cavan, County Cavan, Ireland. It was designed by William Farrell in a neoclassical style and built in ashlar limestone, completed in 1824. Originally used for dispensing justice, it became the meeting place for Cavan County Council following the implementation of the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1898.

Major_Events.Event: Implementation of the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1898
Major_Events.Description: Established county councils in every county, leading to the building also becoming the meeting place for Cavan County Council.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style, built in ashlar limestone, symmetrical main frontage with five bays, central section of three bays featuring a tetrastyle portico with Doric order columns supporting an entablature, three sash windows on the first floor, and a pediment above.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is a significant judicial and municipal facility in County Cavan, and it houses a memorial commemorating Thomas Ashe, a notable member of the Gaelic League, the Gaelic Athletic Association, the Irish Republican Brotherhood (IRB), and a founding member of the Irish Volunteers.
world knowledge.Details: A memorial outside the building commemorates Thomas Ashe.

world knowledge.Name: Curraghs Wildlife Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Curraghs Wildlife Park is a wildlife park in The Curraghs, an area of wetland in the north-west of the Isle of Man. Founded in 1963 under the Curraghs Acquisition Act 1963, the park was formally opened on 23 July 1965 by the Lieutenant Governor of the Isle of Man, Sir Ronald Garvey. The park is owned by the Isle of Man Government and administered by the Department of Environment, Food & Agriculture.

Major_Events.Event: Annual meeting of the British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums (BIAZA)
Major_Events.Description: Hosted as part of the park's 40th-anniversary celebrations.

Major_Events.Event: Small Collection award for Best Education Project with schools
Major_Events.Description: Received from BIAZA in recognition of the park's work in education.
Red-necked Wallabies escaped and established a feral population across the island.
A species of bird from China and Vietnam escaped and established a nearby feral population, which died out after several years.
Two lemurs were killed when a fire destroyed their enclosure.
Kush escaped and was missing for almost three weeks.
Kush escaped again and was missing for around a week.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features walk-through enclosures and includes a variety of habitats such as bogs, Molinia grasslands, open water peat diggings, birch woodland, and hay meadows. Nature trails run through the undeveloped area with signage describing the ecology and history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Curraghs Wildlife Park is designated as a wetland site of international importance under the Ramsar Convention. It plays a significant role in conservation and education, housing about 100 primarily wetland species from around the world.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes educational facilities, a children's farm (Close Beg) with domestic animals, play areas, and The Orchid Line miniature railway. Animals at the park include various species from around the world.

world knowledge.Name: Clock Tower, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Address: Southern shore of Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Clock Tower is the only remnant of the original site of the former Kowloon station on the Kowloon–Canton Railway. It was built as part of the Kowloon-Canton Railway terminus, which was inaugurated in 1910 but construction began in 1913. The tower was completed in 1915 and the entire station opened in 1916. The clock faces were installed in 1920 and began operation in 1921. The tower has been a declared monument since 1990.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the Clock Tower began in 1913 and was completed in 1915 as part of the Kowloon-Canton Railway terminus.
The remaining three sides of the Clock Tower were installed with clock faces in 1920, which began operation in 1921.
During the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong, the clock tower was painted camouflage grey and bell chiming was halted.
The Clock Tower was gazetted as a declared monument under the Antiquities and Monuments Ordinance on 13 July 1990.
On 9 December 2021, the use of the Clock Tower's bell chimes was resumed, ringing hourly between 8am to midnight.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built out of red bricks and granite, the Clock Tower peaks at 44 metres and is topped by a 7-metre lightning rod. It features an Edwardian architectural style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Clock Tower is a significant landmark in Hong Kong, representing the history of the Kowloon-Canton Railway and the development of Tsim Sha Tsui. It is a declared monument and a symbol of Hong Kong's colonial past.
world knowledge.Details: The Clock Tower is located near Victoria Harbour and the western end of Salisbury Road. It is accompanied by the Hong Kong Space Museum, Hong Kong Museum of Art, and Hong Kong Cultural Centre, all built on former station grounds. The bell inside the Clock Tower was moved back to the tower in 2010 after being displayed in various locations since the mid-1980s.

world knowledge.Name: Moulsecoomb Place
world knowledge.Address: Lewes Road, Moulsecoomb, Brighton and Hove BN2 4GA, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a farmhouse in the parish of Patcham, Moulsecoomb Place was bought and extensively remodeled in 1790 by Benjamin Tillstone. It served as the seat of the Tillstone family for over 100 years before being acquired by the local council in the interwar period. The building later became part of the University of Brighton, with student housing added to the rear. The house is a Grade II Listed building and has undergone various uses over the years, including as offices, a library, and a place of worship.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase and remodeling by Benjamin Tillstone
Major_Events.Description: Benjamin Tillstone bought the farmhouse and converted it into a rural retreat, extending the façade and refacing it in yellow brick.
The Tillstone family sold Moulsecoomb Place and its estate to Brighton Corporation, which used the land to develop the Moulsecoomb housing estates.
Moulsecoomb Place was designated a Grade II Listed building on 20 August 1971.
The University of Brighton acquired Moulsecoomb Place and its grounds, converting the building and the old tithe barn into the headquarters of its Student Services division and a children's nursery.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Moulsecoomb Place is a Neoclassical/Palladian-style mansion with a seven-bay façade of yellow brick in a Flemish bond pattern. The central three-bay section projects slightly and is set beneath a pediment. The building features elements of the Palladian and Neoclassical Adam styles, with mahogany doors, Gothic Revival-style balusters, and stained glass. A timber-framed hall house, believed to be the oldest secular building in Brighton, is attached to the rear.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Moulsecoomb Place is historically significant as the former seat of the Tillstone family and for its association with the Prince Regent (later King George IV). It is also notable for its architectural features, including the oldest timber-framed building in Brighton, and its role in the development of the Moulsecoomb housing estates.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a farmhouse and rural retreat, later used as offices, a library, and currently part of the University of Brighton's campus.
world knowledge.Details: The building includes a timber-framed hall house and a tithe barn, both of historical significance. The hall house was converted into stables in the 19th century and later used as a social club and bar. The tithe barn, originally a 16th-century wooden structure, was extended in flint. The university has built student housing to the rear, and plans for redevelopment into a 'student village' were announced in 2022. In 2025, the building was leased to charities for use as an events, community, and music production venue.

world knowledge.Name: Sleeping Giant (Connecticut)
world knowledge.Address: Sleeping Giant State Park, Hamden, Connecticut
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sleeping Giant, also known as the Blue Hills and Mount Carmel (Hobbomock in Quinnipiac), is a rugged traprock mountain with a high point of 739 feet (225 m). It is part of the Metacomet Ridge and was formed 200 million years ago during the Triassic and Jurassic periods. Conservation efforts began in 1924 due to quarrying threats, leading to the establishment of Sleeping Giant State Park.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Sleeping Giant Park Association
Major_Events.Description: A group of local residents formed the SGPA to combat traprock quarrying on the Giant's head.
Sleeping Giant State Park was created when the SGPA donated 600 acres to the Park and Forest Commission.
The Works Progress Administration constructed the tower on the Left Hip.
The tower was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
A 100-mph microburst caused extensive damage, leading to a year-long closure for restoration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Sleeping Giant Tower, built in 1936 by the Works Progress Administration, features Romanesque architectural style. The mountain itself is composed of traprock (basalt), with distinct cliff faces and columnar jointing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The mountain is significant for its Native American legend involving the giant spirit Hobbomock. It is also a popular recreational site with ecological diversity and scenic vistas.
world knowledge.Details: Sleeping Giant State Park offers over 30 miles of hiking trails, including part of the Quinnipiac Trail. It is open year-round for hiking, rock climbing, bird watching, and other passive activities. The park is collaboratively maintained by the Sleeping Giant Park Association and the State of Connecticut.

world knowledge.Name: Hussain Sagar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hussain Sagar is a heart-shaped lake built by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah in 1562. It was the main source of water supply to Hyderabad before Himayat Sagar and Osman Sagar were built. The lake features a large monolithic statue of Gautama Buddha, erected in 1992, and is known for its historical and cultural significance.

Major_Events.Description: A large monolithic statue of Gautama Buddha was erected on Gibraltar Rock in the middle of the lake.

Major_Events.Event: Widening and beautification of Tank Bund
Major_Events.Description: The road on the Tank Bund was widened and beautified with fountains, colored lights, and bronze statues of renowned personalities.
The largest seamless stainless-steel memorial in the world was inaugurated by Chief Minister K. Chandrashekar Rao.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lake is an artificial water body with a heart shape, featuring a monolithic Buddha statue on Gibraltar Rock. The surrounding area includes various parks, statues, and architectural landmarks.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hussain Sagar is culturally significant as a historical water source, a site for the Buddha statue, and a hub for recreational activities. It was declared the 'Heart of the World' by UNWTO in 2012 for being the largest heart-shaped mark on Earth.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Water supply, recreational activities, and cultural landmark
world knowledge.Details: Hussain Sagar is a popular spot for sailing and has hosted regattas since 1971. The lake has faced environmental challenges due to urbanization and pollution, leading to efforts for conservation and restoration.

world knowledge.Name: Kingdom of the Little People
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded by Chen Mingjing, a person of small stature, as part of a complex near Dian Lake that also includes the World Butterfly Ecological Park. The park was created to provide employment for people with dwarfism.

Major_Events.Description: The Kingdom of the Little People was founded in September 2009 by Chen Mingjing.
Vice filmed a piece for their show, The VICE Guide to Travel, at the Kingdom of the Little People, interviewing staff and touring the park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features small mushroom-shaped houses and dormitories specifically constructed to be accessible to short people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park provides employment to people with dwarfism, allowing them to build self-respect and reduce feelings of loneliness. However, it has been criticized for treating dwarfism as a humorous condition and resembling a human zoo.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theme park featuring comic performances by people with dwarfism, including singing, dancing, and acting out scenes from fairy tales or ballets.
world knowledge.Details: As of 2010, there were over 100 employees aged 19 to 48, all under 51 inches (130 cm) tall. The park aims to eventually employ 1,000 people with dwarfism. Performances often feature a 'Dwarf King' who wears a gold silk cape and rides a three-wheeled motorcycle. Employees receive English lessons to interact with foreign tourists.

world knowledge.Name: Kaduna International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kaduna Airport is an airport serving Kaduna, the capital of Kaduna State in Nigeria. It opened in 1982 and is located around 22 kilometres northwest of the city. There is also an older airport, Old Kaduna Airport, located in the northern part of the city.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was attacked by bandits on March 26, 2022, killing a security guard.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway with a length of 3,000 meters and a surface made of asphalt.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As a major transportation hub, Kaduna International Airport plays a crucial role in connecting Kaduna with other parts of Nigeria and the world, facilitating economic and cultural exchanges.
world knowledge.Details: Kaduna Airport (IATA: KAD, ICAO: DNKA) is owned and operated by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN). It serves both public and military purposes. The airport is situated at an elevation of 2,073 feet (632 meters) above mean sea level.

world knowledge.Name: University of Tripoli
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Tripoli (UOT) is the largest university in Libya, founded in 1957 as a branch of the University of Libya. It was divided in 1973 to become the University of Tripoli. It offers undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate studies and has several faculties including Science, Agriculture, Engineering, Veterinary Medicine, Fine Arts and Media, Law, Education, and Medicine. The university was renamed Al Fateh University in 1976 and reverted to its original name in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The university was the site of a student uprising by the Students' Union during the August 2011 Battle of Tripoli, part of the 2011 Libyan Civil War.
The university was renamed Al Fateh University after student unrest in April 1976.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming back to University of Tripoli
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed from Al Fateh University back to the original name of University of Tripoli.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Tripoli is the largest and one of the most significant educational institutions in Libya, playing a crucial role in the country's higher education and research.
world knowledge.Details: The university has several faculties including Science, Agriculture, Engineering, Veterinary Medicine, Fine Arts and Media, Law, Education, and Medicine. It was initially part of the University of Libya before becoming independent in 1973. The university has undergone several name changes and has been a site of significant political activity, especially during the Gaddafi era and the 2011 Libyan Civil War.

world knowledge.Name: Mambilla Plateau
world knowledge.Area: Taraba State and southern Adamawa State, Nigeria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mambilla Plateau is the highest plateau in Nigeria, with an average elevation of about 1,600 metres (5,249 ft) above sea level. It is located in the southeastern part of Taraba State and is bounded by an escarpment that is about 900 m (2,953 ft) high in some places. The plateau is hilly with deep gorges and is dissected by many streams, notably the Donga River and Taraba River. The Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station is proposed for construction in Western Mambilla near the Nigeria-Cameroon border, with an anticipated completion date of 2030. The plateau is also home to Nigeria's largest game reserve, the Gashaka/Gumti Game Reserve.

Major_Events.Event: Proposal of Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station
Major_Events.Description: The Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station is proposed for construction in Western Mambilla near the Nigeria-Cameroon border, with an anticipated completion date of 2030.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mambilla Plateau is culturally significant as it is the only region of Nigeria that grows the tea plant on a large scale. It is also home to the Gashaka Gumti National Park, which is the largest national park and protected area in Nigeria. The plateau has a rich cultural history, with the Mambilla people being the major, original, and predominant group. The plateau has also seen immigration of other groups including the Yamba, Fulani, and trading communities of Igbo, Wimbum (Kambu), Hausa, and Banso.
world knowledge.Details: The climate of the plateau is comparatively cold, with daytime temperatures hardly ever exceeding 25 °C (77.0 °F). The rainy season lasts from mid-March until the end of November, and the plateau receives over 1850 millimetres of rainfall annually. Vegetation on the plateau comprises low grasses with trees being noticeably absent except for man-made forests planted by German colonialists during the period of German administration of the Cameroons (c. 1906-1915) and other Nigerian government tree planting programs. The eucalyptus tree is the dominant tree in these man-made forests. The plateau is also home to the Gashaka Gumti National Park and the Majang Forest, known officially as Ngel Nyaki Forest Reserve, both of which harbor rare and endangered West/Central African plant and animal species endemic to the area.

world knowledge.Name: Surajkund
world knowledge.Area: Southern Delhi Ridge of Aravalli range
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Surajkund is an ancient reservoir built in the 10th century by King Surajpal of the Tomara Rajput dynasty. It was constructed as an artificial lake in the backdrop of the Aravalli hills with a semicircular embankment. The site also housed a Sun temple built by Surajpal, who was a sun worshipper. The reservoir has undergone several renovations over the centuries, including during the Tughlaq Dynasty.

Major_Events.Description: An annual fair held from 1–15 February, showcasing traditional crafts from across India and other countries. The event attracts over 1.2 million visitors, including foreigners, and features crafts, food, and cultural performances.
The reservoir was refurbished during the Tughlaq Dynasty, with steps and terraces rebuilt using stones in lime mortar. A garhi (cave-like structure) was also constructed near the Sun temple site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The reservoir is built in the shape of a rising sun with a semicircular embankment made of stepped stones. It has a diameter of 130 m (427 ft) and was designed to intercept rainfall and address water shortages in Delhi.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Surajkund is culturally significant as an ancient reservoir and a site of historical importance linked to the Tomara Rajput dynasty. It is also known for its annual Surajkund International Craft Mela, which promotes Indian crafts and culture globally.
world knowledge.Details: Surajkund is part of the Northern Aravalli leopard wildlife corridor and is near several historical sites, including Badkhal Lake, Anangpur Dam, and Tughlaqabad Fort. The area has been affected by illegal mining, leading to ecological concerns. Efforts are underway to protect and restore the site, including proposals to notify the area as a protected archaeological site.

world knowledge.Name: Caesars Superdome
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 70 acres (28 ha), interior space of 125 million cubic feet (3,500,000 m³), height of 253 feet (77.1 m), dome diameter of 680 feet (207.3 m), total floor area of 269,000 square feet (24,991 m²)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Louisiana Superdome, it was conceived in 1967 by architect Curtis and Davis and opened in 1975. It was designed as a multi-purpose stadium for football, baseball, and basketball. The Superdome became a shelter during Hurricane Katrina in 2005, suffering significant damage and reopening in 2006 after extensive repairs.

Major_Events.Description: The Superdome housed thousands of evacuees during Hurricane Katrina, suffering damage from the storm. It reopened in September 2006 after repairs.
First Super Bowl held at the Superdome, notable for being the first prime-time Super Bowl.
Featured Brock Lesnar ending The Undertaker's WrestleMania streak and Daniel Bryan winning the WWE World Heavyweight Championship.
A statue commemorating Steve Gleason's blocked punt during the Saints' first post-Katrina game was unveiled.
A partial power failure halted the game for 34 minutes during the third quarter.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Curtis and Davis, the dome features a lamellar multi-ringed steel frame covering 13 acres (5.3 ha), with a diameter of 680 feet (207 m). It includes a synthetic turf system and has undergone multiple renovations to modernize facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Superdome is a symbol of resilience for New Orleans, especially after Hurricane Katrina. It hosts major sports events, concerts, and cultural gatherings, serving as a central venue for the community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium (NFL games, college sports, concerts, major events)
world knowledge.Details: The Superdome has hosted eight Super Bowls, six NCAA Men's Final Fours, and major concerts. It is known for its loud atmosphere during Saints games, creating a strong home-field advantage. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including updates to seating, lighting, and technology.

world knowledge.Name: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, originally known as Shenzhen Huangtian Airport, was opened on 12 October 1991. It has undergone significant expansions, including the addition of a second runway in 2011 and a new terminal in 2013. The airport serves as a major hub for several airlines and is one of the three largest airports in the Pearl River Delta region.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened on 12 October 1991.
A second runway was added to accommodate increasing air traffic.
Terminal 3 was opened on 28 November 2013, replacing the older terminals A, B, and D.
Air China launched the first intercontinental air route from Shenzhen to Frankfurt Airport, Germany, on 21 May 2016.
A new satellite concourse opened in December 2021, increasing the airport's capacity by 22 million passengers per year.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern design with a main terminal building and two large corridors forming a cross shape. The terminal has four floors above ground and two underground, with a total floor space of 450,000 square meters. It includes 62 boarding gates and can accommodate any type of aircraft. The satellite concourse is connected to the main terminal by an automated people mover (APM) system.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport is a key transportation hub in the Pearl River Delta, facilitating economic growth and connectivity in the region. It is also a symbol of Shenzhen's rapid development and modernization.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving passenger and cargo flights.

Transportation.Metro: Line 11 and Line 20 of Shenzhen Metro
Transportation.Ferry: Fast ferries to Macau and Hong Kong International Airport
Transportation.Future connections: Guangzhou-Dongguan-Shenzhen Intercity Railway, Shenzhen–Maoming High-Speed Railway, Hong Kong–Shenzhen Western Express Railway

world knowledge.Name: Lake Nokoué
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lake Nokoué is a lake in the southern part of Benin, fed by the Ouémé River and the Sô River. It serves as an important source of food and economic activity for nearby towns like Cotonou and Ganvié. The lake's ecology is influenced by sediment deposits, climate change, and human activities such as fishing and pollution.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lake Nokoué is culturally and economically significant due to its diverse wildlife, which supports local fishing communities. It is also a site for Acadja, a traditional fish breeding facility.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Ecological and economic resource (fishing, fish breeding)
world knowledge.Details: The lake is expected to double in size and flood due to climate change, risking future salinisation. It contains at least 78 species of fish and supports various bird species and otters. The lake floor consists of sand, muddy-sand, and mud layers. It is also affected by pesticides and heavy metals from upstream industries.

image_name: The Repertory Theatre of St. Louis

world knowledge.Name: The Repertory Theatre of St. Louis
world knowledge.Address: 130 Edgar Road, Webster Groves, Missouri 63119, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1966, The Repertory Theatre of St. Louis (often referred to as 'The Rep') is a repertory theater based in Webster Groves, Missouri. It made its home at Webster University's Loretto-Hilton Center for the Performing Arts. The first production was two Peter Shaffer plays presented together. The theater has undergone leadership changes and program expansions over the years, including the creation of the Imaginary Theater Company in 1975, the Off-Ramp performance series in 2005, and the Ignite Festival of New Plays in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The Repertory Theatre of St. Louis was founded and made its home at Webster University's Loretto-Hilton Center for the Performing Arts. The first production was two Peter Shaffer plays, 'The Private Ear' and 'The Public Eye.'
The Imaginary Theater Company was established to bring The Rep's work to schools and younger audiences.
The Rep began a new performance series, the 'Off-Ramp performance series,' with performances at The Grandel Theatre in Grand Center.
The Rep created the Ignite Festival of New Plays to support its new play development work.
The Rep participated in the Play At Home program, commissioning short plays for audiences to perform while stuck at home.
The 50th anniversary season included notable productions such as 'Follies,' 'Until the Flood,' 'A Christmas Carol,' 'All My Sons,' 'To Kill a Mockingbird,' and 'Million Dollar Quartet.'

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Repertory Theatre of St. Louis is a significant cultural institution in the region, known for its contributions to theater arts, including new play development, educational outreach, and high-quality productions. It has played a vital role in the cultural life of St. Louis and its suburbs.
world knowledge.Details: The Rep's home at Loretto-Hilton Center is shared with the Opera Theatre of Saint Louis, The Conservatory of Theatre Arts at Webster University, and Webster University's dance department. In early 2007, The Rep considered moving from the Loretto-Hilton Center to an alternate venue. The theater has a capacity of 763 to 963 and was renovated and expanded in 2002.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Vesuvius
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Vesuvius is a somma-stratovolcano located on the Gulf of Naples in Campania, Italy. It is famous for its eruption in AD 79 that destroyed the Roman cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum, Oplontis, and Stabiae. Vesuvius has erupted many times since and is regarded as one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world due to the dense population living nearby.

Major_Events.Description: The eruption destroyed the Roman cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum, Oplontis, and Stabiae. It ejected a cloud of stones, ash, and volcanic gases to a height of 33 km, releasing molten rock and pulverized pumice at a rate of 6×10^5 cubic meters per second.
The last eruption occurred from March 17–23, 1944, causing significant damage to nearby villages and aircraft at Pompeii Airfield.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Vesuvius consists of a large cone partially encircled by the steep rim of a summit caldera, resulting from the collapse of an earlier, much higher structure. The volcano's slopes are scarred by lava flows and are heavily vegetated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vesuvius has a long historic and literary tradition. It was considered a divinity in Roman times and was associated with Hercules. The eruption of AD 79 is one of the most famous volcanic events in history, preserving the cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice.
world knowledge.Details: Mount Vesuvius is the only volcano on Europe's mainland to have erupted in the last hundred years. It is closely monitored due to the potential danger it poses to the surrounding population. The area around Vesuvius was declared a national park on June 5, 1995, and the summit is open to visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Seri Kenangan Beach
world knowledge.Area: Mukim Pekan Tutong, Tutong District, Brunei
world knowledge.Address: Mukim Pekan Tutong, Tutong District, Brunei
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Seri Kenangan Beach, developed as a recreational area, was officially opened on 26 March 1972. The project was initiated by Pengiran Dato Paduka Othman bin Pengiran Anak Mohd. Salleh, the Tutong district officer, to transform the beach into a picnic destination and establish a weekly market. The initiative involved community clean-up campaigns and the construction of amenities using local natural materials.

Major_Events.Description: The official ceremony to inaugurate Seri Kenangan Beach as a recreational area and establish the weekly market was held on 26 March 1972, officiated by Isa bin Ibrahim.
A beach clean-up campaign was carried out on 1 October 1971, involving government officers, staff, and Tutong residents, particularly the youth, to prepare the beach for visitors.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The beach features amenities constructed from local natural materials such as nibung palm, rattan, and forest timber. Facilities include beach huts, pavilions, tables with benches, and unique structures like a mushroom-shaped resting area and a fish-shaped stall.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Seri Kenangan Beach is culturally significant as a popular recreational area that promotes local community engagement and showcases traditional materials and craftsmanship in its facilities. It also hosts a weekly market that supports local agriculture and handicrafts.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is equipped with amenities such as a parking area, clean water supplies, chalets, a children's playground, a restaurant, and a memorial monument shaped like a gong and gendang gulingtangan. The Istana Pantai, built in the early 1950s as a resting place for Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien III, is also located here.

world knowledge.Name: Carthage National Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Carthage National Museum, founded in 1875 as the "Musée Saint-Louis" within the Chapelle Saint-Louis de Carthage, was established to house the finds from the excavations of Alfred Louis Delattre. It became a national museum in 1956 and underwent extensive restructuring in the 1990s. The museum is a collaboration of specialists and volunteers dedicated to preserving the ancient site of Carthage.

Major_Events.Event: Excavations exposed a Late Roman house
Major_Events.Description: Excavations exposed a Late Roman house with fragments of Roman mosaics and a large church dating to the 5th century.
The museum opened through financial donations from 59 members of a non-profit organization EARTHWATCH.
The museum was redesigned to accommodate new discoveries from the international campaign of UNESCO.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum contains many archaeological items from the Punic era and other periods, including limestone/marble carvings, Roman mosaics, and a marble sarcophagus of a priest and priestess from the 3rd century BC.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the history of Carthage, including its connections with the Levant, Ancient Egypt, and Greece. It also highlights the Phoenician civilization and the Roman era.
