world knowledge.Details: The museum is currently closed for an indefinite period. It contains a vast collection of Roman amphoras, masks, jewelry in cast glass, and funerary inscriptions. Notable items include the "Lady of Carthage" mosaic and the sarcophagus of a priest and priestess.

world knowledge.Name: Phu Bai International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Phu Bai International Airport is located just south of the central city of Huế, the former capital of Vietnam. It was allowed to receive international flights by the Vietnamese government in 2002 and officially welcomed its first international flight on October 30, 2005. The airport has undergone significant development, including a Memorandum of Understanding signed with Changi Airports International in 2007 and major runway repairs in 2013. A new terminal, Terminal T2, was completed by the end of 2021.

Major_Events.Description: On October 30, 2005, Phú Bài Airport officially welcomed its first international flight since it was allowed to receive international flights by Vietnamese government in 2002. The charter flight operated by Austrian Airlines carried Austrian tourists from Luang Prabang, Laos.

On May 24, 2007, Changi Airports International (CAI) announced that it had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the People's Committee of Thua Thien Hue Province for the development of Phu Bai–Hue International Airport.

On February 23, 2013, Phú Bài Airport was expected to close for eight months for runway repairs and upgrades, estimated between 500 and 600 billion Vietnam Dong. The airport was actually closed from March 20 to September 20, two months less than planned.
A new terminal invested by The Airports Corporation of Vietnam with total investment of about VNĐ2.250 trillion (US$96.9 million) was completed by the end of 2021.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Terminal T2 has two floors, with the first floor including the arrival hall, baggage conveyor belt, immigration area, port authority, customs, VIP waiting room, lost luggage room, and security control. The second floor is the area for domestic and international check-in procedures, security control, departure, and waiting to board the plane. The terminal also has two waiting areas for businessmen and VIP passengers. Terminal T2 is connected to the aircraft parking area by 4 telescopic bridges, including 3 code C bridges and one double telescopic bridge, which can handle one code E aircraft or 2 code C aircraft at the same time.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Phu Bai International Airport is significant as it serves Huế, the former capital of Vietnam, and plays a crucial role in the development of Thua Thien Hue Province as an international tourism destination.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a new terminal, Terminal T2, which has a capacity of five million passengers per year by 2020 and up to 6.5-7 million passengers by 2025. The terminal includes auxiliary facilities such as car, taxi, bus, and convoy parking lots built in front of the terminal.

world knowledge.Name: Teatro Nacional (Santo Domingo)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Eduardo Brito National Theater, originally known as the National Theater of Santo Domingo, opened on August 16, 1973. It was renamed in 2006 after the Dominican baritone Eduardo Brito by presidential decree. The theater was designed by architect Teófilo Carbonell, who was selected by then-president Joaquín Balaguer to create a world-class theater. Carbonell's design was inspired by the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and utilized Dominican materials such as marble, mahogany, and onyx.

Major_Events.Description: First held in 1997 featuring pianists such as André Watts and José Feghali, the Santo Domingo Music Festival is hosted biennially at the National Theater. The festival was proposed by French pianist and conductor Philippe Entremont after he conducted the National Symphony at the theater in 1995.

Major_Events.Event: Swearing-in ceremony for President Luis Abinader
Major_Events.Description: On 16 August 2024, the Eduardo Brito National Theater was the venue of the swearing-in ceremony for President Luis Abinader, attended by 17 heads of state and other international delegations. It was the first time that the presidential inauguration ceremony was held at a location other than the Assembly Hall of the National Congress.
In 2025, the theater hosted a memorial service for merengue singer Rubby Pérez, who died in the Jet Set nightclub roof collapse on 8 April.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theater's design evokes the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and uses Dominican materials including marble, mahogany, and onyx.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Eduardo Brito National Theater is a cultural hub in the Dominican Republic, hosting opera, ballet, classical music performances, and Latin pop concerts. It is the centerpiece of the Plaza de la Cultura complex and has played a significant role in the country's cultural and political events.
world knowledge.Details: The theater has a capacity of 1,700 seats and is a prominent venue for both cultural and political events in the Dominican Republic.

world knowledge.Name: Florida Citrus Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1956 to showcase the thriving citrus industry, the Florida Citrus Tower was once a major landmark in the Orlando area. It was funded by public stock sales and constructed with 5 million pounds of concrete and 149,000 pounds of reinforcing steel. The tower's popularity declined after the extension of Florida's Turnpike in 1964 and harsh freezes in the 1980s that killed most citrus groves. It was repainted in its original colors in 2015 and sold to Simchat Torah Beit Midrash in 2022.

Major_Events.Description: The tower opened on July 14, 1956, with representatives from Silver Springs and Cypress Gardens in attendance.
Three harsh freezes killed most of the citrus groves in Lake County, leading to decreased visitation.
The tower was repainted in its original orange and white color scheme.
The tower was sold to Simchat Torah Beit Midrash for $3.3 million.
The tower reopened after renovations aimed at restoring its original appearance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 226-foot-tall observation tower constructed with 5 million pounds of concrete and 149,000 pounds of reinforcing steel. Features a coin drop, banquet facility, gift shop, and museum.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The tower was built to showcase Florida's citrus industry and was once a major tourist attraction. Its history reflects changes in Florida's agricultural and transportation landscapes.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Observation tower and radio broadcasting tower
world knowledge.Details: Includes a coin drop, ROOM: Valencia banquet facility, gift shop, and museum. Nearby is the Presidents Hall of Fame with wax tributes to U.S. Presidents and a model of the White House interior.

world knowledge.Name: Bronte Beach
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Small sandy area (reduced since 1914 due to construction)
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Promenade and sea wall constructed in 1914, storm water drain built in 1918
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bronte Beach was named after Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson, Duke of Bronté, not the Brontë sisters as commonly misconceived. Originally known as 'Nelson Bay', the name 'Bronte' was first used in 1957 for land sales. The beach has historical ties to local indigenous people, evidenced by a sandstone cave.

Major_Events.Event: Rescue of children from storm water drain
Major_Events.Description: Six children were washed into pipes during heavy wave conditions but were safely rescued by Waverley Council Life Guards and Bronte lifesavers.
A long-distance ocean swimming event held every December between Bondi Beach and Bronte.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Features a promenade, sea wall, 30-meter ocean pool (bogey hole), and a naturally formed sandstone cave. The area includes picnic seats, barbecue hotplates, and limited parking.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bronte Beach is culturally significant as the home of the oldest surf lifesaving club in the world (formed in 1903). It is a popular recreational spot with ties to British military history and local indigenous heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational beach for swimming, surfing, and coastal walks.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is patrolled by Waverley Council lifeguards daily (except winter) and volunteer lifesavers on weekends/public holidays. It is linked to Bondi and Coogee Beaches via a coastal footpath. Known for the dangerous rip called the 'Bronte Express,' it is served by the 379 bus from Bondi Junction station.

world knowledge.Name: University of Oviedo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Oviedo was established under the terms and conditions of the will of Archbishop Fernando de Valdés Salas, who was the General Inquisitor under Philip II of Spain, and funded by his estate. In 1574 Pope Gregory XIII granted the papal bull to create the university and in 1604 Philip III issued its charter. It first opened for the teaching of classes on September 21, 1608. The university has three campuses and research centres, located in Oviedo, Gijón, and Mieres. It was rebuilt after the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939).

Major_Events.Description: The Historical Building of the university was occupied by invading troops and lectures were suspended until the War ended.
The university (including its Library and the Art Gallery) was set fire either by the revolutionaries or the government bomber airplanes.
The university was rebuilt after the Spanish Civil War.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Oviedo is the only university in the region of Asturias and has a rich history dating back to the 16th century. It played a significant role in the educational and cultural development of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university has 31 faculties and professional schools, offering degrees and diplomas in over 150 fields of study. It has a large number of classrooms and laboratories, including 6 classrooms with capacities ranging from 75 to 171 seats, and 15 laboratories equipped with both PC and MAC computers. The coordinates of the university are 43°21′42″N 5°50′47″W.

world knowledge.Name: Comoé National Park
world knowledge.Area: Zanzan and Savanes districts of north-eastern Ivory Coast
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Comoé National Park is a Biosphere Reserve and UNESCO World Heritage Site, established in 1983. It is the largest protected area in West Africa, covering 11,500 square kilometers. The park was initially added as a World Heritage Site due to the diversity of plant life around the Komoé River. It was listed as a World Heritage Site in Danger in 2003 due to poaching, absence of management, and overgrazing, but was removed from the list in 2017 following improvements in conservation.

Major_Events.Event: Declaration as Refuge Nord de la Côte d'Ivoire
Major_Events.Description: The area between the Comoé River and Bouna was declared a refuge.

Major_Events.Event: Enlargement to Réserve de Faune de Bouna
Major_Events.Description: The area was enlarged and given rudimentary protection.
The area west of the Comoé river was added, and the park was elevated to National Park status.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: The park was pronounced a biosphere reserve and a UNESCO World Heritage site due to its unique biodiversity.

Major_Events.Event: Listed as World Heritage in Danger
Major_Events.Description: The park was listed as a World Heritage Site in Danger due to poaching, absence of management, and overgrazing.

Major_Events.Event: Removed from List of World Heritage in Danger
Major_Events.Description: The park was removed from the List of World Heritage in Danger following improvements in conservation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park consists of large plains through which the Comoé River and its tributaries flow. It includes various habitats such as savannas, forest islands, gallery forests, and riparian grasslands. The park also features granite inselbergs rising up to 600 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Comoé National Park is culturally and historically important due to its unique biodiversity and status as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It serves as a sanctuary for many animal and plant species, some of which are endangered.
world knowledge.Details: The park has the most biodiverse savannah in the world and forms the northern limit for many animal species. It is home to 135 mammal species, over 500 bird species, 60 fish species, 35 amphibian species, and 71 reptile species. The park also contains around 620 plant species. The Comoé National Park Research Station, founded in 1989/90, focuses on conservation, tropical ecology, and behavior.

world knowledge.Name: Smock Alley Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Smock Alley Theatre has a history dating back to the 17th century, with the current theatre being a 21st-century conversion from a 19th-century church building. It incorporates structural material from an 18th-century theatre and is built on the site of the 17th-century Theatre Royal. The present theatre opened in 2012 after a €3.5 million investment. The site includes multiple performance spaces with varying capacities.

Major_Events.Description: The upper galleries collapsed, killing several people and injuring many more, including the son of the Lord Lieutenant of Ireland.
A partial collapse led to the demolition and rebuilding of the theatre in 1735.
A riot occurred due to new rules restricting audience access backstage, sparked by a drunk Trinity College student.
The Theatre Royal at Smock Alley closed due to competition from a rival theatre.
An excavation revealed foundations from the original 1662 theatre and the full basement of the 1735 theatre.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current theatre is a conversion from a 19th-century church, incorporating elements from an 18th-century theatre. It features ornate stained glass windows and ceiling plasterwork from the early 20th century. The original Theatre Royal had a classical proscenium stage, pit, boxes, galleries, and a music loft, with excellent acoustics.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Smock Alley Theatre is culturally significant as one of Dublin's oldest theatres, hosting plays by notable playwrights like George Farquhar, Oliver Goldsmith, and Richard Brinsley Sheridan. It was a venue for famous actors such as Peg Woffington and David Garrick, and it played a key role in Dublin's theatrical and social history.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre site includes Smock Alley Theatre (177 seats), The Boys School (60-100 capacity), Black Box (80 capacity), and The Banquet Hall (150 capacity). Artefacts recovered from excavations include medieval pottery, glass finds, clay tobacco-pipe fragments, and an actor's wig curler.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Mogan
world knowledge.Area: Deqing County, Huzhou, Zhejiang Province, China
world knowledge.Address: Moganshan National Park, Deqing County, Huzhou, Zhejiang Province, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Mogan has been a retreat since the 1880s, initially for foreigners who built European-style villas. It was a summer home for Shanghai's elite and later became a resort area after the Communist party took over in 1949. The mountain is named after the legendary swordsmith Ganjiang and his wife Moye from the Spring and Autumn period (770-476 BC).

Major_Events.Description: Foreigners, mostly Americans and British, began renting and building villas on the mountain.
Foreigners left, and villas were redistributed to work units from Hangzhou and Shanghai.
Mark Kitto renovated a villa and opened a restaurant and guest lodges.
Grant Horsfield and Delphine Yip opened the first platinum-level LEED certified resort in Mainland China.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: European-style villas, houses, churches, and public halls built in the early 20th century, many of which have been converted into hotels and guesthouses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Mogan is culturally significant for its historical role as a retreat for Shanghai's elite and foreigners, its connection to Chinese legend (Ganjiang and Moye), and its architectural heritage of early 20th-century villas.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreation and tourism (hiking, relaxation, historical visits).
world knowledge.Details: Mount Mogan is part of the Tianmu mountain range, known for its cool temperatures and lush bamboo forests. It features attractions like Sword Pond and the Bai & Yun Art Museum.

world knowledge.Name: Lego-Brücke
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lego-Brücke is a concrete beam bridge crossing over the Schwesterstraße in Wuppertal. In 2011, graffiti artist Martin Heuwold repainted the bridge in the style of Lego bricks, gaining international attention. The project was part of a bikeway and footway development by Wuppertal Bewegung on a decommissioned railway.

Major_Events.Description: Artist Martin Heuwold repainted the bridge in the style of Lego bricks, inspired by his daughters' toys. The project was approved by Lego A/S and completed in 13 days.
The bridge's redesign won the Deutscher Fassadenpreis for its creative and impactful transformation.

Major_Events.Event: Formal opening of the redesigned bridge
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was officially opened on 7 October 2011 after completion of the repainting project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Concrete beam bridge painted to resemble Lego bricks, covering an area of over 250 m². The design mimics the colorful and blocky appearance of Lego toys.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge gained national and international media attention for its unique and playful redesign, blending urban art with public infrastructure. It symbolizes creativity and community engagement in urban renewal projects.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Pedestrian and bicycle bridge connecting the Elberfeld (Ostersbaum) and Barmen (Clausen) districts of Wuppertal.
world knowledge.Details: The project was funded by Wuppertal Bewegung and sponsors Akzenta and Klauser Schuhe. Martin Heuwold was assisted by underemployed workers recruited by Wichernhaus GmbH. The bridge was part of a decommissioned railway line repurposed for recreational use.

world knowledge.Name: Cross Insurance Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cross Insurance Center is a multi-purpose arena built to replace the Bangor Auditorium and Civic Center. The city of Bangor began discussions in the late 2000s to replace the aging facilities, and a public referendum in May 2011 supported the construction of a new arena by a 3 to 1 margin. The new arena was completed in 2013 and is part of the city's Bass Park complex.

Major_Events.Description: The city of Bangor held a public referendum in May 2011, where voters supported building new facilities to replace the Bangor Auditorium and Civic Center by a margin of 3 to 1.

Major_Events.Event: Demolition of Bangor Auditorium and Civic Center
Major_Events.Description: Demolition began at the Bangor Auditorium and Civic Center on June 3, 2013, to make way for the new Cross Insurance Center.
The Cross Insurance Center officially opened on September 10, 2013.

Major_Events.Event: Naming rights purchase by Cross Insurance Agency
Major_Events.Description: On July 20, 2012, Cross Insurance Agency purchased the naming rights to the arena for $3 million, changing its name from 'Bangor Arena' to 'Cross Insurance Center'.

Major_Events.Event: University of Maine basketball games announcement
Major_Events.Description: On July 31, 2013, the University of Maine announced that the Maine Black Bears basketball teams would play over half of their games at the new arena.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The arena was designed by Sink Combs Dethlefs and WBRC Architects Engineers, with structural engineering by Martin/Martin, Inc. and services engineering by M–E Engineers, Inc. It features a multi-surface and has a seating capacity of 5,800 (plus 1,500 retractable), with the ability to hold up to 8,500 people for concerts and 2,000 for conventions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cross Insurance Center replaced the Bangor Auditorium, a statewide icon that hosted the Maine Principals' Association basketball tournament. The new arena continues to serve as a major venue for sports, concerts, and conventions in the region, contributing to the cultural and economic vitality of Bangor.
world knowledge.Details: The facility is managed by Spectra, a division of Comcast. It is located across from Hollywood Casino Bangor and is the home of the basketball teams of the Maine Black Bears. The construction cost was approximately $65 million ($87.7 million in 2024 dollars).

world knowledge.Name: Euralille
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Conceived as a major European business district in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Euralille is strategically located at the intersection of high-speed railway lines linking Paris, Brussels, and London. The master plan was commissioned in 1988 to the Office of Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) led by Rem Koolhaas. The project was financed as a private-public partnership, established in 1990. The ambitious program was delayed in part because of the mid-1990s real-estate market crisis.

Major_Events.Description: The master plan was commissioned to the Office of Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) led by Rem Koolhaas.
The first phase of the project opened.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of Tour de Lille and Tour Lilleurope
Major_Events.Description: The Tour de Lille and Tour Lilleurope office towers were completed.
The Suite Hôtel was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The masterplan defined several distinct areas: a mixed-use precinct comprising a shopping mall named Triangle des Gares designed by Jean Nouvel, the TGV station designed by Jean-Marie Duthilleul with two office towers above by architects Christian de Portzamparc and Claude Vasconi, a park designed by Gilles Clément and a congress centre known as the Grand Palais designed by OMA. The masterplan also re-organized the infrastructure, a complicated junction of various transportation systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Euralille is a significant urban development project that transformed Lille into a major European business district. It is a hub for high-speed rail travel between Paris, Brussels, and London, and it incorporates a mix of shopping, offices, hotels, housing, a concert hall, and a congress centre.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mixed-use urban quarter (shopping, offices, hotels, housing, concert hall, congress centre)
world knowledge.Details: The initial development area has been extended since 2000 by another 22 hectares, named Euralille 2. The planned functional mix has been subject to change and in 2006 comprised 40% office, 20% residential and 40% amenities space.

image_name: Tauber Bridge, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

world knowledge.Name: Tauber Bridge, Rothenburg ob der Tauber
world knowledge.Address: Tauber Valley, Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Bavaria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tauber Bridge is an historic road bridge that spans the Tauber Valley west of the town centre of Rothenburg ob der Tauber. It was part of a trade route from Augsburg to Würzburg. The bridge was renovated in 1791 after the four upper arches collapsed the year before. In 1945, it was blown up by German troops and later rebuilt in 1955-1956.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was renovated after the four upper arches collapsed in 1790.
The eastern approach to the bridge was widened.
The bridge was blown up by German troops during World War II.
The bridge was rebuilt and opened on 10 November 1956.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Double bridge with two rows of arches, one on top of the other.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important historical structure that was part of a major trade route and showcases medieval engineering.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Road bridge for local link road to Leuzenbronn and the Tauber Valley Way.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge lies at the foot of the southwestern valley side below Rothenburg ob der Tauber.

image_name: Mahalia Jackson Theater of the Performing Arts

world knowledge.Name: Mahalia Jackson Theater of the Performing Arts
world knowledge.Address: 1419 Basin Street New Orleans, Louisiana United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mahalia Jackson Theater of the Performing Arts is a theater located in Louis Armstrong Park in New Orleans, Louisiana. It was named after gospel singer Mahalia Jackson, who was born in New Orleans. The theater first opened in January 1973 and was severely damaged by Hurricane Katrina in 2005. It reopened in January 2009 after extensive renovations.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened with a performance of Giuseppe Verdi's Messa da Requiem, starring New Orleans native Norman Treigle and the New Orleans Philharmonic-Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Werner Torkanowsky.
The theater sustained 14 ft. of water, damaging motor control center, orchestra lifts, heating and air-conditioning controls, sewerage ejector pumps, and other structural components.

The theater reopened with a week of events, including performances by Kermit Ruffins, Irma Thomas, Marva Wright, Allen Toussaint, Yolanda Adams, the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra with Itzhak Perlman, and others.
The theater hosted the 2012 NFL Honors, honoring the best National Football League players and performances.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theater is named after gospel singer Mahalia Jackson, a New Orleans native, and serves as a key cultural venue for performing arts in the city. It was the first major theater in New Orleans to reopen after Hurricane Katrina, symbolizing the city's recovery.
world knowledge.Details: The theater serves as the long-term residence of the New Orleans Ballet Association, the New Orleans Opera Association, and the Broadway Across America touring productions. It has a seating capacity of 2,100 and underwent a $27 million renovation after Hurricane Katrina.

world knowledge.Name: Veer Savarkar International Airport
world knowledge.Location: Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally known as Port Blair Airport, it was renamed in 2002 after Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, who was detained in the Cellular Jail in Port Blair for 11 years during India’s freedom struggle. It serves as the primary airport for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and operates as a civil enclave, sharing airside facilities with INS Utkrosh of the Indian Navy.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Veer Savarkar International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed in honor of Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, a prominent figure in India’s freedom struggle.
A new passenger terminal was constructed to handle increasing traffic, with a capacity of 5 million passengers per annum.
The new terminal was inaugurated on 18 July 2023.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new terminal has three floors: one for arrivals, one for departures, and one for waiting. It includes 28 check-in counters, four conveyor belts, and three aerobridges. The runway is 3,290 meters long, accommodating narrow-body aircraft like Airbus A320, A321, and Boeing 737.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, a key figure in India’s independence movement, highlighting its historical importance in the context of India’s freedom struggle.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Airport serving domestic and international flights.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a single runway and operates as a civil enclave, sharing airside facilities with the Indian Navy. The old terminal, with a capacity of 400 passengers, is no longer operational. The new terminal can handle 1,200 passengers at peak hours and 5 million passengers annually.

world knowledge.Name: Fox Theatre (St. Louis)
world knowledge.Address: 527 N. Grand Blvd. St. Louis, Missouri, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fox Theatre, also known as "The Fabulous Fox", was built in 1929 by movie pioneer William Fox as a showcase for the films of the Fox Film Corporation and elaborate stage shows. It was one of a group of five spectacular Fox Theatres built by Fox in the late 1920s. The theater opened on January 31, 1929, and was reportedly the second-largest theater in the United States at the time with 5,060 seats. It was restored in 1982 after closing in 1978.

Major_Events.Description: The theater reopened in September 1982 with the Broadway musical Barnum after a $3 million restoration.
The theatre hosted a 60th birthday concert for Chuck Berry, with Keith Richards as the musical director. The concert was later incorporated into the documentary film 'Hail! Hail! Rock 'n' Roll'.
The theatre hosted a performance by Pearl Jam as part of the politically motivated Vote for Change Tour.
The Fox Theatre hosted tapings for the NBC show America's Got Talent, featuring over 75 contenders and judges Howie Mandel, Sharon Osbourne, Howard Stern, and host Nick Cannon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect C. Howard Crane in an eclectic blend of Asian decorative motifs sometimes called Siamese Byzantine. The interior is the architectural twin of another Fox Theatre built in Detroit in 1928. The style was nicknamed the "Eve Leo Style" in tribute to William Fox's wife, who decorated the interior with furnishings, paintings, and sculpture from her overseas trips.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fox Theatre is a historic performing arts center that has survived as a versatile venue from its origins as a movie palace. It is culturally significant for its architectural grandeur, its role in St. Louis's arts district, and its hosting of major cultural and musical events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Performing arts center and concert venue
world knowledge.Details: The Fox Theatre seats 4,192 theatergoers plus 234 in the private Fox Club. It features a Wurlitzer pipe organ with four manuals, 36 ranks, and 348 stops, restored in 1981. The theatre briefly appeared in the 1981 film 'Escape from New York'. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 8, 1976.

world knowledge.Name: Marcelo Fernan Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Mandaue, Cebu to Lapu-Lapu City, Mactan Island
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,230.2 meters (4,036 ft) total length, 185 meters (607 ft) longest span
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Marcelo Fernan Bridge, originally named Consolacion Bridge, was opened in August 1999 to decongest traffic from the older Mactan-Mandaue Bridge. It was constructed with Japanese government assistance and named after Senator Marcelo Fernan, a political figure from Cebu City.

Major_Events.Description: Inaugurated by Philippine President Joseph Estrada on August 3, 1999.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Extradosed cable-stayed bridge design, featuring two pedestrian walkways on the north and south sides.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a vital infrastructure in Metro Cebu, facilitating transportation and commerce between Cebu and Mactan Island. It also features the Millennium Park and the Filipino Seafarers Memorial on the Mactan side.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (vehicular and pedestrian traffic across the Mactan Channel)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is one of three bridges crossing the Mactan Channel, alongside the Mactan-Mandaue Bridge and the Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway. It sits near the Cebu International Port, a major hub for domestic and international shipping in the Philippines.

world knowledge.Name: Victory Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Victory Stadium was an American football stadium located in Roanoke, Virginia. It opened in 1942 and was demolished in 2006. The stadium was built on land donated to the city of Roanoke by the Norfolk & Western Railway. It was the largest football stadium in the state of Virginia at the time of its opening.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium opened on Labor Day, September 7, 1942, with a War Bond rally featuring actress Greer Garson.
The first football game at the stadium, on September 12, 1942, featured Roanoke's William Fleming High School and Jefferson High School. Jefferson won 33-0.
The first college football game at the stadium, on September 19, 1942, matched Virginia Tech against Catawba College. Tech won 28-14.

The Baltimore Colts and the Pittsburgh Steelers scheduled a pre-season game at the stadium. The NAACP sued Roanoke over segregation laws, leading to a resolution where Civil Rights activists bought tickets in the white section and claimed their seats without confrontation.
The stadium was demolished on June 26, 2006, after years of debate about its future.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium featured two identical concrete and steel grandstands with wooden bleachers, built parallel to the east and west sidelines of the field. Each grandstand had an external façade trimmed in red brick.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Victory Stadium was culturally significant as the largest football stadium in Virginia at the time of its opening and for its role in the Civil Rights Movement in 1961.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was initially referred to as 'Roanoke Municipal Stadium' but was renamed 'Victory Stadium' in 1942. It was demolished in 2006 after years of debate about its future. The site now has several athletic fields and an amphitheatre.

world knowledge.Name: Wakato Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main span of 367 meters, total length of two kilometers
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wakato Bridge, opened on September 26, 1962, connects the wards of Wakamatsu and Tobata across Dōkai Bay. It was named after these two wards. The bridge passed into the control of Kitakyūshū on September 30, 2005. Before the bridge was built, the Wakato ferry served as the primary means of crossing, which has been retained for pedestrians and cyclists due to the bridge being reserved for motor vehicle traffic only after a large number of suicides occurred from its deck.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to the public on September 26, 1962.
The bridge passed into the control of Kitakyūshū on September 30, 2005.
The bridge was lifted and destroyed by the space monster Dogora in the 1964 Toho dai Kaiju movie Space Monster Dogora.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a main span of 367 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant infrastructure project connecting the wards of Wakamatsu and Tobata, facilitating transportation and economic activity in the region. It also holds cultural relevance due to its depiction in the 1964 film Space Monster Dogora.
world knowledge.Details: The Wakato ferry, which existed before the bridge was built, is still operational for pedestrians and cyclists. The ferry ride costs 100 yen each way for adults, and 50 yen for children and older people. Bicycles can be transported for an additional 100 yen.

world knowledge.Name: Alderney Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Alderney Airport, built in 1935, is the only airport on the island of Alderney and was the first airport in the Channel Islands. It is located southwest of St Anne and is the closest Channel Island airport to the south coast of England and France. The airport has three operational runways and has undergone several upgrades and expansions over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The runway was resurfaced with a material designed to last 12 to 15 years.
Major patch and repair work was undertaken on the eastern end of the runway.
During the COVID-19 lockdown, airport staff refurbished the terminal and patched the runway.
Plans were backed to extend the runway to accommodate larger aircraft and improve terminal and fire station facilities.
The States of Guernsey agreed to spend £24m on extending, widening, and strengthening the runway, constructing a new terminal building, and refurbishing the fire service facilities.
Land acquisition for the runway extension began, with tenders expected to be issued soon and work to start in 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features three runways: the main runway (08/26) is 880m long and mainly asphalt, while the secondary runways (13/31 and 03/21) are grass. The terminal building, erected in 1968, includes an arrivals room, departure lounge, and a check-in desk. The airport also has a non-directional beacon and GPS approaches for runways 08 and 26.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Alderney Airport is culturally significant as the first airport in the Channel Islands and a vital link for the island of Alderney, connecting it to mainland England and France.
world knowledge.Details: The airport serves as the base for Air Alderney, though the airline has faced operational challenges since 2017. It currently offers direct scheduled links to Southampton and Guernsey. The airport has undergone several upgrades, including runway resurfacing and terminal refurbishment, and is planning a major expansion to accommodate larger aircraft and improve facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Chao Lake
world knowledge.Historical_Background: According to legend, the site of the lake was once a prosperous city named Chaozhou, which was destroyed by flooding due to the sins of its people. The lake is situated on the intersection of several major faults, including the Tan-Lu fault.

Major_Events.Description: The Tan-Lu fault, which runs through Chao Lake, caused the great 1976 Tangshan earthquake in its northern section.
The Chinese government borrowed $250 million from the Asian Development Bank to fund cleanup efforts due to severe pollution from rapid economic growth and heavy use since the 1990s.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chao Lake is the largest lake in Anhui and one of the five major freshwater lakes in China. It is nicknamed 'The Land of Fish and Rice' due to its abundant aquatic life. The lake is also associated with local legends and geological significance.
world knowledge.Details: Tourist sites around the lake include Mushan Island, Zhongmiao Temple, Tongyang River, Mount Yinping, and the Immortals Cave. The lake's silver fish, shrimps, and crabs are known as the Three Treasures. About 5 million people live near the lake and rely on it for various purposes. Cleanup efforts have been successful due to strong political leadership and integrated planning.

world knowledge.Name: Sumy State University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sumy State University (SumDU) was established in 1948 as a department of Kharkiv Polytechnic Institute. It evolved through several stages, becoming a branch of Kharkiv Polytechnical Institute in 1966, Sumy Institute of Physics and Technology in 1990, and finally Sumy State University in 1993. The university's development was significantly influenced by the Sumy Machine-Building Plant and key figures like I.H. Kovalev, who served as rector from 1993 to 2004. In 2015, the Ukrainian Academy of Banking was reorganized by joining SSU.

Major_Events.Description: The Sumy Institute of Physics and Technology was reorganized into Sumy State University.

Major_Events.Event: Reorganization with Ukrainian Academy of Banking
Major_Events.Description: The Ukrainian Academy of Banking was reorganized by joining Sumy State University.
A large explosion occurred near the university building during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sumy State University is a significant educational institution in Ukraine, known for its high scientific and educational standards. It has a diverse student body, including many international students, and is a member of several international academic organizations. The university has played a crucial role in the community, especially during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, by providing support and shelter to students and residents.
world knowledge.Details: Sumy State University enrolls about 12,000 students in 55 majors and 23 fields, with around 1,900 foreign students from nearly 50 countries. The university has over 3,000 employees, including Corresponding Members of the National Academy of Science of Ukraine, and offers postgraduate and post-doctoral programs. The library has over 3 million items and has won the All-Ukrainian contest 'Library of the Year'. The university is a signatory of Magna Charta Universitatum and Talloires Declaration and cooperates with more than 280 partners from 50 countries. During the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the university prioritized the safety of international students, providing food, shelter, and support.

world knowledge.Name: Hamilton New Zealand Temple
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hamilton New Zealand Temple is the 13th constructed and 11th operating temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It was the church's first temple in the Southern Hemisphere, the second built in Polynesia, and the second outside the United States and Canada. The temple was announced on February 17, 1955, and dedicated on April 20, 1958. It underwent renovations from 2018 to 2022 and was rededicated on October 16, 2022.

Major_Events.Description: The intent to build the temple was announced by church president David O. McKay on February 17, 1955.
The groundbreaking ceremony and site dedication were held on December 21, 1955.
The temple was dedicated by David O. McKay on April 20, 1958.
The temple underwent renovations focusing on seismic strengthening, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical upgrades, and interior layout improvements.
The temple was rededicated by Dieter F. Uchtdorf on October 16, 2022.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features a modern contemporary design with a single spire. It is constructed with concrete block and white-painted structural steel. The interior includes murals, glass and crystal chandeliers, and gold detailing. The design incorporates elements of Māori and Polynesian cultures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The temple is culturally significant as it integrates Māori and Polynesian cultural elements with traditional Latter-day Saint temple designs. It serves as a central place of worship and spiritual ceremonies for church members in New Zealand and New Caledonia.
world knowledge.Details: The temple sits on an 86-acre plot and features large lawns, gardens, and paved concrete masonry pavers. It includes two instruction rooms, eight sealing rooms, and one baptistry. The temple has undergone several renovations to preserve its structural integrity and update facilities. It was rededicated on October 16, 2022, after a four-week open house that attracted over 55,000 visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Estádio 24 de Setembro
world knowledge.Address: Av. 3 de Agosto Bissau , Guinea Bissau
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Estádio Nacional 24 de Setembro is a multi-purpose stadium in Bissau, Guinea Bissau. The stadium opened its doors in 1989. It is currently used primarily for football matches.

Major_Events.Description: Record attendance of 22,000 on 10 October 2003.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a grass surface and a capacity of 20,000 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the home ground of the Guinea-Bissau national football team and hosts popular football clubs like Benfica Bissau and Sporting Bissau.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for football matches and athletics.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was renovated in 2011–2013 and 2021–2023. It is operated by the Federação de Futebol da Guiné-Bissau (FFGB).

world knowledge.Name: Arena Joinville
world knowledge.Address: Bucarein neighborhood, near Boa Vista and Guanabara neighborhoods, Joinville, Santa Catarina, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Arena Joinville is a multi-use stadium inaugurated on September 25, 2004. It is one of Brazil's most modern football stadiums, inspired by European football arenas like the Amsterdam ArenA. The stadium is owned by Joinville City Hall.

Major_Events.Description: A friendly match where Masters All-Stars beat All-Stars of Joinville 3-1. The first goal was scored by Masters' player Donizete Pantera. The attendance record was 15,000 people.
The stadium's capacity was expanded from 15,000 to 22,400 people, with plans to further expand to 30,000 (24,000 seated). The estimated budget for the expansion was R$7 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Modern football stadium inspired by European football arenas, featuring a grass surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arena Joinville is a significant sports and entertainment venue in Brazil, hosting football matches and international shows. It is a symbol of modern infrastructure in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium for football matches and entertainment events.
world knowledge.Details: A shopping mall is being constructed inside the stadium, which will include over a hundred stores, making it one of the biggest shopping malls in the city.

world knowledge.Name: Scurdie Ness Lighthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Scurdie Ness is a headland located on the South side of the River South Esk estuary. The lighthouse was built in 1870 by David and Thomas Stevenson due to numerous shipwrecks and loss of life in the area. During World War II, the lighthouse was painted black to avoid being a reference point for German bombers. It was automated in 1987.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was built to address the high number of shipwrecks and loss of life along the coast.
The lighthouse was temporarily painted black to prevent use by German bombers as a reference point.
The lighthouse was converted to automatic operation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a tapered cylindrical stone tower with a balcony and lantern, standing 39 meters tall. It is painted white with a black lantern and ochre balcony and trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Scurdie Ness is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a Geological Conservation Review site. It is renowned for its agates and volcanic rock formations. The lighthouse is a category B listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The lighthouse serves as a navigational aid for ships entering the River South Esk estuary and Montrose Harbour.
world knowledge.Details: The coastline from Scurdie Ness to Rickle Craig is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. The area is known for sightings of seals, dolphins, and occasionally whales. The lighthouse's light has an intensity of 182,000 candela and can be seen up to 43 km away. The buildings within the lighthouse grounds are now privately owned.

world knowledge.Name: Rauma Old Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rauma Old Town Hall was built in 1776 by German architect Christian Friedrich Schröder. It represents late Baroque style and is one of the only two preserved 18th-century town halls in Finland, alongside Porvoo. Since the completion of the new town hall in 1910, it has housed the Rauma Museum.

Major_Events.Description: The Old Town Hall ceased to function as the administrative center and became the home of Rauma Museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Late Baroque style with a basic structure of two stories and a clock tower, a common feature in Medieval European towns.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Old Rauma and represents a rare example of 18th-century Finnish civic architecture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a town hall, now serves as the Rauma Museum.
world knowledge.Details: Porvoo and Rauma are the only preserved 18th-century town halls in Finland. The building is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Finland.

world knowledge.Name: Norwegian Aviation Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Norwegian Aviation Museum was opened by King Harald V on May 15, 1994. It is the Norwegian national museum of aviation and the largest aviation museum in the Nordic countries. The decision to locate the museum in Bodø was made by the Norwegian parliament on March 31, 1992, after intense debates between the aviation communities in Gardermoen and Bodø.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was officially opened by King Harald V on May 15, 1994.

Major_Events.Event: Parliamentary decision to build in Bodø
Major_Events.Description: On March 31, 1992, the Norwegian parliament decided to build the museum in Bodø, ending a long debate between the aviation communities in Gardermoen and Bodø.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is shaped like a huge propeller and contains both civilian and military aircraft. It was designed by Per Morten Wik at Boarch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is the Norwegian national museum of aviation and the largest in the Nordic countries. It tells the story of aviation with a focus on Norwegian history, from its early beginnings to the present time.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is located in Bodø, Northern Norway, roughly 1.5 kilometres from the town centre. It is situated across the street of 'Olav V gate' and is near Bodø Spektrum and the shopping centre of City Nord. Visitors traveling by car from Bodø Airport towards Fauske will pass under the museum.

world knowledge.Name: Polihale State Park
world knowledge.Address: Western side of Kauai, Hawaii, near Kekaha
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Several miles long shoreline with sand dunes up to 100 feet high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Polihale State Park is a remote wild beach with strong roots in Hawaiian mythology. It is believed to be a place where spirits traveled to the coastal plain adjacent to the beach, staying in a temple known as the heiau, before climbing the cliffs to the north and jumping into the sea to reach the mythical Po. The name "Polihale" translates as "House Bosom," with roots in the concept of "source of life."

Major_Events.Description: In December 2008, flooding damaged facilities and closed the access road. Local residents and businesses volunteered to repair the road on their own, completing the job in eight days by March 31, 2009, avoiding a potential $4 million government repair cost and a 1-2 year delay.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Natural landscape with sand dunes, shoreline, and adjacent mountain ridges. The park features running cold water, flush toilets, simple semi-private showers, and a few pavilions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Polihale is deeply rooted in Hawaiian mythology and is considered a sacred place. It is associated with the journey of spirits to the afterlife and is blessed by Na-maka-o-Kaha'i, the Goddess of the Ocean. The unique sea lettuce, pahapaha, found here is said to revive when soaked in water, a quality bestowed by the goddess.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational use, including camping and safe swimming at Queen's Pond.
world knowledge.Details: Polihale State Park is the most western publicly accessible area in Hawaii. It is remote, with difficult access via a dirt road, preferably requiring a 4-wheel drive vehicle. The beach is unprotected from the open ocean, with strong rip currents, making swimming unsafe except at Queen's Pond. The park is the terminus for Kauai's road network on the western side of the island, with no further overland access along the coast. Kayak trips along the Nā Pali Coast often end at Polihale Beach due to ocean currents. Visitors should bring all necessary supplies, as nothing is available for purchase in the park.

world knowledge.Name: Playa Blanca
world knowledge.Location: Yaiza, Las Palmas, Canary Islands, Spain
world knowledge.Address: Playa Blanca, 35580 Yaiza, Las Palmas, Spain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Playa Blanca is the southernmost town of the Spanish island of Lanzarote and the newest resort on the island. It has developed into a significant tourist destination with various amenities and attractions.

Major_Events.Description: Playa Blanca became the first town on the island to have a dedicated local bus service.
Playa Flamingo was virtually destroyed during Tropical Storm Delta.

Major_Events.Event: Rebuilding of Playa Flamingo sea wall
Major_Events.Description: The sea wall at Playa Flamingo was rebuilt after its destruction in 2005.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features a mix of modern resort architecture and traditional Canarian elements. Notable structures include the Rubicon Marina and Castillo de las Coloradas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Playa Blanca is culturally significant as a major tourist destination in the Canary Islands, offering a blend of natural beauty, historical sites, and modern amenities. The Atlantic Museum contributes to marine conservation and education.
world knowledge.Details: Playa Blanca is known for its sheltered beaches, vibrant marina, and the Atlantic Museum, an underwater museum featuring life-size sculptures. The town has a diverse population and offers various activities, including water sports, hiking, and exploring volcanic landscapes.

world knowledge.Name: Musée d'Aquitaine
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Musée d'Aquitaine is a museum that houses a collection of objects and documents from the history of Bordeaux and Aquitaine. The site originally housed the convent of the Feuillants in the 16th century, which was destroyed during the Revolution. It later became a high school and then a university. The museum was established in 1963, combining collections from other museums, and moved to its current location in 1987.

Major_Events.Description: The Lapidary Museum was created by the Academy of Bordeaux, which later evolved into the Musée d'Aquitaine.
The Lapidary Museum changed its primary vocation and combined collections from other museums to form the Musée d'Aquitaine.
The museum moved into the premises of the former Faculty of Letters and Sciences.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of permanent rooms on slave trade
Major_Events.Description: The museum opened new permanent rooms dedicated to the role of Bordeaux in the slave trade.
Rooms devoted to the 19th century were reopened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a building constructed in the 1880s by the municipal architect Charles Durand, located on the site of former convents.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the history of Bordeaux and Aquitaine, including its role in the Atlantic trade and slavery, and houses extensive collections from Prehistory to the present day.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include over 70,000 pieces, tracing the history of Bordeaux and Aquitaine from Prehistory to today, including 5,000 pieces of art from Africa and Oceania. It features permanent collections and temporary exhibitions, with permanent collections displayed on two floors covering various historical periods. The museum is accessible by the Bordeaux tramway and is located near Tour Pey-Berland and St. Andrew's Cathedral.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Golf Dar Es Salam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Royal Golf Dar Es Salam is a golf club located in Rabat, the capital of Morocco. It was established by the late King Hassan II who wanted to build a flagship 36-hole complex in Morocco's capital. The property, situated in a cork oak forest, was designed by Robert Trent Jones and Cabell Robinson and opened in 1971.

Major_Events.Description: The Red Course has hosted the Trophée Hassan II since it opened. Before becoming a European Tour event in 2001, it was held on an invitational basis from 1971.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Robert Trent Jones and Cabell Robinson, the Red Course is known for its sandy, tree-lined property with a rolling contour. It was redesigned in 2017–2018 by James Duncan, focusing on tree removal, bunker reconstruction, and green enlargement.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Royal Golf Dar Es Salam is a flagship golf complex in Morocco, hosting significant tournaments and being ranked among the World's Top 100 courses in the early 1990s.
world knowledge.Details: The Royal Golf Dar Es Salam has hosted tournaments on the European Tour, Ladies European Tour, Asian Tour, and PGA Tour Champions. The Red Course is a strong contender for the title of best course by Robert Trent Jones.

world knowledge.Name: Deutsches Schauspielhaus
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Deutsches Schauspielhaus, also known as the Hamburg Schauspielhaus or Hamburg Theatre, was co-founded by stage actress Franziska Ellmenreich. It was designed by Austrian architects Fellner & Helmer, built between 1899 and 1900, and opened in 1901. The theatre underwent renovation in 2013/2014.

Major_Events.Event: The Infernal Comedy – Confessions of a Serial Killer
Major_Events.Description: An operatic production about the life of Austrian serial killer Jack Unterweger, written by American actor John Malkovich and directed by Michael Sturminger, performed at the Deutsches Schauspielhaus, with Malkovich starring.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Austrian architects Fellner & Helmer.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Deutsches Schauspielhaus is a significant cultural landmark in Hamburg, known for its theatrical productions and historical architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has a capacity of 1192 and is owned by the Free and Hanseatic city of Hamburg. Public transit access is available via Hauptbahnhof Nord.

world knowledge.Name: Brantford
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brantford was founded on the Grand River and named after Joseph Brant, a Mohawk leader. It played a significant role in the development of the telephone, with Alexander Graham Bell inventing the first telephone here. The city has a rich Indigenous history and was a key location during the American Revolutionary War and the War of 1812.

Major_Events.Description: Alexander Graham Bell invented the first telephone at his father's homestead in Brantford.
Brantford became the first city in Canada to fluoridate its water supply.
Brantford's city council expropriated and demolished 41 historic downtown buildings, sparking controversy.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Brantford features a mix of historical and modern architecture, including the Greek Revival-style Brant County Courthouse and the Bell Homestead, a preserved 19th-century farmhouse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Brantford is culturally significant as the birthplace of the telephone and home to notable figures like Wayne Gretzky and Phil Hartman. It also has deep Indigenous roots and is located on the Haldimand Tract, a land grant to the Mohawk people.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Brantford serves as a single-tier municipality with a mix of residential, industrial, and cultural functions.
world knowledge.Details: Brantford is known as the 'Telephone City' and has a diverse economy, though it faced challenges in the 1980s with the decline of manufacturing. The city has a humid continental climate and a population of 104,688 as of 2021. It is home to several museums, annual festivals, and cultural institutions.

world knowledge.Name: Mercedes-Benz Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mercedes-Benz Museum, located in Stuttgart, Germany, covers the history of the Mercedes-Benz brand and associated brands. The current building, designed by UN Studio, was completed and opened on 19 May 2006. It is situated directly outside the main gate of the Daimler factory in Stuttgart.

Major_Events.Description: The current building of the Mercedes-Benz Museum, designed by UN Studio, was completed and opened on 19 May 2006.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is based on a unique cloverleaf concept using three overlapping circles with the center removed to form a triangular atrium, recalling the shape of a Wankel engine. It features a 'double helix' interior designed to maximize space, providing 16,500 square metres of exhibition space on a footprint of just 4,800 square metres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it showcases the history and evolution of the Mercedes-Benz brand, which is a major part of automotive history and innovation.
world knowledge.Details: The museum contains more than 160 vehicles, some dating back to the earliest days of the motorcar engine. It offers free audio tours in various languages and had 800,245 visitors in 2023. Visitors can also tour the nearby Untertürkheim engine factory, which produces many of the company's diesel engines.

world knowledge.Name: Isle of Man Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Isle of Man Airport, also known as Ronaldsway Airport, is the main civilian airport on the Isle of Man. It was first used as an airfield in 1928, with passenger services starting in 1933. The airport has a rich history, including its use by the Royal Air Force during World War II and subsequent development by the Admiralty. It reverted to civilian use after the war and has undergone several expansions and renovations since.

Major_Events.Description: During the 1936 expansion of the airport, workers discovered a mass grave believed to hold the remains of soldiers who died during the Battle of Ronaldsway in 1275.
The airfield came under Royal Air Force control at the outbreak of World War II, known as RAF Ronaldsway, and continued operating civilian flights throughout the war.
The airfield was handed over to the Admiralty for development as a Fleet Air Arm training station, becoming RNAS Ronaldsway.
The airport reverted to civilian use after World War II, with the Isle of Man Government purchasing it in 1948.
A project by Ellis Brown Architects extended the airport and improved passenger facilities, including a new arrivals area, baggage hall, and departure lounge.
A major runway extension and resurfacing project was completed, extending the runway by 245 meters into the Irish Sea.
Flybe announced it would shut down its base operations at the airport by Spring 2020.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modern terminal with 5 gates, a lounge, duty-free shops, a bar, and a café. The runway is asphalt/concrete, and the airport has undergone several expansions and renovations to improve facilities and comply with international safety standards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Isle of Man Airport is a key gateway to the island, facilitating travel and commerce. It has a rich history tied to aviation development and military use during World War II. The airport also hosts the Manx Military and Aviation Museum, which preserves the island's aviation history.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has one terminal with 5 gates, a duty-free shop, a bar, and a Costa Coffee café. It is served by several airlines, including Loganair. The airport also has its own fire service and previously had an independent police service, which was disbanded in 2019. Bus services and a nearby railway station provide additional transportation options for passengers.

world knowledge.Name: Sino–Korean Friendship Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connects Dandong, Liaoning, China and Sinuiju, North Pyongan, North Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was constructed by the Imperial Japanese Army during its occupation of Korea and Manchukuo. It was renamed in 1990 from Yalu (Amnok) River Bridge. Both this bridge and an older bridge (Yalu River Broken Bridge) were bombed during the Korean War, with the older bridge left in ruins and the newer bridge repaired and put back into use after the war.

Major_Events.Description: Built during the occupation of Korea and Manchukuo.
Attacked by USAF to cut off military supplies; repeatedly repaired by China.
Renamed from Yalu (Amnok) River Bridge to Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Steel bridge carrying one lane of AH1, road, and rail traffic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the few entry points into North Korea; part of the Yalu River Scenic Area, a major tourist attraction in China.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (road and rail) between China and North Korea.
world knowledge.Details: Flanked by parks and promenades on the Chinese side; tourist boats offer views of both bridges and the North Korean waterfront. The older Yalu River Broken Bridge remains in ruins as a historical artifact.

world knowledge.Name: Brussels Airport
world knowledge.Area: Brussels Capital Region, Flemish Brabant, Walloon Brabant
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Brussels Airport, originally established by the German occupying force in 1940, was developed into Belgium's main international airport. It has undergone significant expansions and modernizations, including the construction of new terminals and runways, and has played a crucial role in European aviation. The airport was severely damaged by terrorist bombings in 2016 but has since returned to full operations.

Major_Events.Description: On 22 March 2016, two explosions severely damaged the airport's departures hall, leading to its temporary closure. The airport reopened with limited capacity on 3 April 2016.
The airport was expanded and modernized in preparation for the 1958 World's Fair, including the construction of a new terminal.
On 18 February 2013, armed men stole an estimated $50 million worth of diamonds from a plane at the airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a one-terminal concept with multiple levels, including a railway station, bus and taxi access, arrivals and departures halls, and two piers (A and B). The terminal building is designed for efficiency and passenger convenience, with modern facilities and extensive use of glass and steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As Belgium's main international airport, Brussels Airport is a key hub for European and global travel. It has significant economic and cultural importance, serving as a gateway to Brussels and the broader region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving passenger and cargo flights.
world knowledge.Details: Brussels Airport is home to around 260 companies and directly employs 20,000 people. It serves as the home base for Brussels Airlines and TUI fly Belgium. The airport has a direct train link to various Belgian cities and offers extensive amenities, including shops, restaurants, and meeting facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Austin Stack Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Austin Stack Park is a GAA stadium named after Austin Stack, an Irish revolutionary and captain of the All-Ireland winning Kerry Gaelic football team of 1904. Originally known as The Sportsfield, it was owned by the County Kerry Athletic and Cricket Club before being rented to a GAA committee in 1903 and purchased by the Kerry County Board in 1929. The grounds were renamed in 1944 in honor of Austin Stack. The stadium has undergone several renovations, including in 1994, 2001, and 2015.

Major_Events.Event: All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship final
Major_Events.Description: Kerry took the title by beating London in the final.
Tralee IT won the final.
The first game in Kerry GAA played under floodlights took place here in November 2001.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a rectangular pitch, a stand, terracing, and floodlights. The original oval-shaped pitch and cinder track were converted in 1934 to accommodate Gaelic games.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Austin Stack Park is culturally significant as a historic venue for Gaelic games in Ireland, particularly for Kerry GAA. It honors Austin Stack, a notable figure in Irish history and sports. The stadium has hosted numerous important matches and events in Gaelic football and hurling.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: GAA stadium for Gaelic football and hurling matches.
world knowledge.Details: The Kerry County Board has had its offices in the ground since 1985. Plans for relocation to Ballybeggan Racecourse were put on hold due to economic downturn. Recent refurbishments include upgrading the pitch, scoreboard, lighting system, and terracing.

world knowledge.Name: Court Green
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Court Green is a house in North Tawton, Devon, England. It was the home of poets Ted Hughes and Sylvia Plath, who moved there in late August 1961. Sylvia Plath left the house on 10 December 1962, while Ted Hughes lived there on and off for the rest of his life. It is currently the home of his widow, Carol Hughes.

Major_Events.Description: Sylvia Plath wrote most of the Ariel (1965) poems at Court Green, including 'The Moon and the Yew Tree' and 'The Bee Meeting'.
Ted Hughes wrote Crow (1970) and most of his later work at the house, often standing at a lectern.
Ted Hughes died in 1998, and his friend Seamus Heaney read at the funeral service at the church across the lawn.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is listed Grade II on the National Heritage List for England.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Court Green is culturally significant as the home of renowned poets Ted Hughes and Sylvia Plath, where much of their notable work was written. The house and its surroundings inspired several of Plath's poems, including 'The Moon and the Yew Tree' and 'The Bee Meeting.'
world knowledge.Details: The ancient yew tree mentioned in Sylvia Plath's poem 'The Moon and the Yew Tree' can still be seen today in the nearby churchyard. Percy Keys, a neighbour of the Hughes during their time at Court Green, is mentioned in The Journals of Sylvia Plath, and his funeral is remembered in Plath's poem 'Berck-Plage.' Keys is buried in the graveyard on the hill above the house.

world knowledge.Name: Sittwe
world knowledge.Location: Estuarial island at the confluence of the Kaladan, Mayu, and Lay Mro rivers, Bay of Bengal
world knowledge.Address: Sittwe Township, Sittwe District, Rakhine State, Myanmar
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sittwe, formerly Akyab, is the capital of Rakhine State. It was a small fishing village during the British conquest of Burma. The name Sittwe is derived from the Burmese pronunciation of Arakanese, meaning 'the place where the war meets'. It became an important maritime base under British occupation and was a significant site during World War II. It is also the birthplace of political monks in Myanmar, including U Ottama, who protested against colonial British rule.

Major_Events.Description: Burmese king Bodawpaya invaded the Mrauk U Kingdom, leading to a battle at the mouth of the Kaladan river where the Mrauk U forces were defeated.
The British under Gen. Morrison stormed local defenses during the First Anglo-Burmese War, leading to the port being chosen as Arakan's seat of government in 1826.
Sittwe was an important site of many battles during the Burma Campaign due to its possession of both an airfield and a deepwater port.
Monks in Sittwe started protests against the military government in Myanmar.
The Myanmar government held tens of thousands of Rohingyas in camps at Sittwe under poor conditions.
Sittwe was surrounded by Arakan Army forces, leading to a mass population exodus.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features four stupas (Akyattaw, Thingyittawdhāt, Letyatalundaw, and Letwetalundaw) rebuilt plainly in the late 19th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sittwe is culturally significant as the birthplace of political monks in Myanmar and a key site in the country's colonial and wartime history. It also holds Buddhist relics and is a center of Theravada Buddhism and Islam.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Administrative capital of Rakhine State and a major port city.

Details.Ethnicities: Rakhine, Rohingya, Bamar, Daingnet, Bengali, Kaman, Maramagyi, Mro, Thet
Details.Climate: Tropical monsoon climate (Am) with a dry season from December to April and a wet season from May to November.
Details.Infrastructure: Port of Sittwe is part of the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, linking Indian north-eastern states to Myanmar.
Details.Sports: Wai Thar Li Stadium (home of Rakhine United F.C.) and Dhanyawaddy Stadium (home of Arakan United FC).
Details.Notable_Person: Hector Hugh Munro (Saki), British writer, born in Sittwe in 1870.

world knowledge.Name: Wanzhou Railway Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Yiwan Railway Wanzhou Yangtze River Bridge is an arch bridge completed in 2005. It carries the Yichang-Wanzhou Railway across the Yangtze River.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began on 3 December 2002.
The bridge was completed and opened in 2005.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a steel arch bridge with a longest span of 360 metres (1,180 ft), making it one of the longest arch bridges in the world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is significant for its engineering and as a critical transportation link in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries the Yichang-Wanzhou Railway across the Yangtze River.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a specific bridge or group of bridges in China is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Wolverhampton Art Gallery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wolverhampton Art Gallery was funded and constructed by local contractor Philip Horsman and built on land provided by the municipal authority. It opened in May 1884. The building was designed by Birmingham architect Julius Chatwin and is a Grade II* listed building. It was refurbished and extended in 2006–07 to create additional exhibition spaces.

Major_Events.Description: The gallery opened to the public.
The building was refurbished and extended to create additional exhibition spaces.

Major_Events.Event: Acquisition of Peace and Plenty Binding the Arrows of War
Major_Events.Description: The gallery acquired the large-scale painting by Abraham Janssens van Nuyssen, a significant piece of Flemish Baroque art.
A significant collection of Eastern weapons was donated by councilor Davis Green.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The two-storey building is made of Bath stone with six red granite columns at the main entrance. It features a decorative sculptural frieze on the facade representing the Arts and Crafts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gallery is culturally significant for its collection of artworks, including Flemish Baroque paintings, Old Masters, and works by local artists. It also houses collections of Eastern weapons, japanned ware, and Bilston enamels, reflecting the industrial heritage of Wolverhampton.
world knowledge.Details: The gallery's collection includes over 20,000 objects, with significant holdings of Victorian art, pop art, and artworks documenting the Troubles in Northern Ireland. It also features interactive displays and workshops for artists and makers.

world knowledge.Name: Bannerghatta National Park
world knowledge.Address: Bengaluru and Ramanagara District, Karnataka, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bannerghatta National Park was founded in 1970 and declared a national park in 1974. In 2002, a portion of the park became a zoological garden known as the Bannerghatta Biological Park. The park is known for its diverse wildlife, ancient temples, and trekking opportunities. It has faced challenges such as deforestation due to agricultural expansion and urbanization.

Major_Events.Description: Bannerghatta National Park was officially declared a national park.
A portion of the national park was converted into a zoological garden.
Four bore wells were opened to provide water during dry seasons.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a hilly terrain of granite sheets under moist deciduous forest valleys and scrubland on higher areas. It includes artificial forests and introduced wildlife.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bannerghatta National Park is culturally significant as a conservation area for diverse wildlife and a destination for tourism and recreation. It also houses ancient temples and is part of a wildlife corridor for elephants.
world knowledge.Details: The park is located about 22 km south of Bangalore in the Anekal range, with an elevation of 1245 - 1634m. It is part of a wildlife corridor connecting the BR Hills and the Sathyamangalam forest. The park is threatened by granite quarries operating nearby, which adversely affect wildlife. A 2021 Malayalam movie, 'Bannerghatta', is based on the park.

world knowledge.Name: Monastery of Saint Naum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Monastery of Saint Naum is a Macedonian Orthodox monastery named after the medieval Bulgarian writer and enlightener Saint Naum who founded it. It was established in the Bulgarian Empire in 905. The monastery is situated along Lake Ohrid, 29 kilometres south of the city of Ohrid, within the boundary of the village of Ljubaništa. The area belonged to Albania from 1912 until June 28, 1925, when Zog of Albania ceded it to Yugoslavia as a result of negotiations between Albania and Yugoslavia and as a gesture of goodwill.

Major_Events.Description: The area where the monastery of St Naum lies belonged to Albania from 1912 until June 28, 1925, when Zog of Albania ceded it to Yugoslavia as a result of negotiations between Albania and Yugoslavia and as a gesture of goodwill.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Monastery of Saint Naum is culturally and historically important as it was founded by Saint Naum, a key figure in the medieval Bulgarian literary and educational tradition. It is also a significant religious site for the Macedonian Orthodox Church and a popular tourist destination in North Macedonia.
world knowledge.Details: The Lake Ohrid area, including St Naum, is one of the most popular tourist destinations in North Macedonia. Since the 16th century, a Greek school had functioned in the monastery. The monastery had close ties with the printing house of Moscopole, a former prosperous Aromanian city now in Albania. Rebecca West devoted a chapter of Black Lamb and Grey Falcon to her visit to Sveti Naum, which occurred in 1937.

world knowledge.Name: Darwin International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Darwin International Airport originated as Parap Airfield in 1919 for the England to Australia air race. It served as a military and civilian airport during World War II, enduring Japanese bombing.
