world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a capacity of 18,000 people. The Wenzhou Olympic Shooting Hall is a two-story frame structure with air rifle, pistol, and rifle ranges. The Wenzhou Gymnasium has a competition hall with fixed and activity seats, elevators, and disabled seating. The natatorium includes standard, diving, training, and warm-up pools. The stadium features a wide square with a music fountain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wenzhou Sports Centre is significant for its role in promoting sports and cultural events in Wenzhou. It hosts football matches, concerts, and other gatherings, contributing to the local economy and community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium primarily for football matches and sports events.
world knowledge.Details: The Wenzhou Olympic Shooting Hall covers an area of 57.57 mu with an investment of 19.48 million yuan. The Wenzhou Gymnasium has a floor area of 20,206 m² and a height of 27.2 meters. The Wenzhou Natatorium was designated by the Chinese Swimming Association as the national advanced swimming hall and includes multiple pools. The stadium's square features a 1,350 m² music fountain with 1003 sprinklers and 333 lights.

world knowledge.Name: Joy Theater
world knowledge.Address: 1200 Canal Street New Orleans, Louisiana, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Joy Theater, named after owner Joy Houck, is a theater and historic landmark built in 1947 on Canal Street in downtown New Orleans, Louisiana. Renovations in 2011 transformed the former movie palace into a multi-purpose theater for live music, stand-up comedy, private functions, and corporate events. The theater's iconic marquee sign was restored, as was the building's original art deco architecture.

Major_Events.Description: The Joy Theater opened at a cost of $275,000, with seats for 1,250 patrons. It was hailed as "New Orleans' newest and most modern film temple" and featured a crying room for parents with young children. The opening feature was 'Lover Come Back', starring Lucille Ball.
The Joy Theater closed, succumbing to competition from megaplexes with stadium-style seating and multiple screens.
The flood following Hurricane Katrina inundated the structure.
The Joy Theater reopened after renovations that transformed it into a multi-purpose venue.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Joy Theater features original art deco architecture and an iconic marquee sign. It was equipped with a crying room, a glass-enclosed area for parents with young children.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Joy Theater is a historic landmark in New Orleans, representing the city's mid-20th century entertainment culture and its resilience through challenges like Hurricane Katrina. Its restoration preserves its art deco architecture and adapts it for modern use.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose theater for live music, stand-up comedy, private functions, and corporate events.
world knowledge.Details: The theater was built by Joy Houck (the theater's namesake) and Levere Montgomery, Sr. The architect was B. W. Stevens. It currently has a capacity of 1,200.

world knowledge.Name: Caraga State University
world knowledge.Address: Main Campus, Ampayon, Butuan, Agusan del Norte, Philippines
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1937 (initial framework), 1990 (CEIT building), 1987 (CAA main college building), 1975 (CHASS building)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1946 as Agusan Agricultural High School, it evolved through several name changes and legislative acts, culminating in its current form as Caraga State University in 2009. The university was formed by merging Northern Mindanao State Institute of Science and Technology and Northern Mindanao College of Arts, Science and Technology.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Agusan Agricultural High School
Major_Events.Description: Following World War II, the Agusan Agricultural High School was established in the reserved area of Ampayon, Butuan.

Major_Events.Event: Conversion to Northern Mindanao National Agricultural College
Major_Events.Description: Republic Act 3604 converted the school into the Northern Mindanao National Agricultural College (NORMINAC).

Major_Events.Event: Conversion to Northern Mindanao State Institute of Science and Technology
Major_Events.Description: Batas Pambansa Blg. 241 converted NORMINAC to the Northern Mindanao State Institute of Science and Technology (NORMISIST).
Republic Act No. 9854 merged NORMISIST and Northern Mindanao College of Arts, Science and Technology to form Caraga State University.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features multiple buildings constructed over different periods, including the CEIT building (1990), CAA main college building (1987), and CHASS building (1975). The buildings are designed for academic and administrative functions, with capacities ranging from 200 to 720 people.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Caraga State University is a prominent educational institution in the Caraga region, offering a wide range of academic programs. It plays a crucial role in regional development through education, research, and community service.
world knowledge.Details: The university's main campus is located along the Phil-Japan Friendship Highway. It offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs, technical and vocational courses, and has a strong emphasis on sustainable forest management and environmental conservation. The university's colors are green, gold yellow, orange, and white, symbolizing various aspects of its mission and history.

world knowledge.Name: National Theatre of Cuba
world knowledge.Address: Plaza de la Revolución, Havana, Cuba
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Theatre of Cuba was approved in 1951 under Carlos Prío Socarrás' administration, with construction beginning in 1952 under Fulgencio Batista. Inspired by Radio City Music Hall in New York, it was designed with three rooms for various performances. Construction was slow, and much remained unfinished by 1959. The theatre was fully inaugurated in 1979.

Major_Events.Description: President Fulgencio Batista laid the foundation stone for the National Theatre.
The Sala Covarrubias was inaugurated, hosting cultural activities until 1961 when it was repurposed due to poor conditions.
The National Theatre was fully completed and officially inaugurated on September 3, 1979.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: International style, designed with three rooms: a large one for opera and ballet, a small one for dramatic theatre, and an experimental room. It also includes dressing rooms, workshops, a library, and academies.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theatre is one of the largest in Cuba and hosts a variety of cultural events, including ballet, theatre productions, musicals, and lectures, making it a central hub for Cuban arts and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre has two auditoriums, Sala Covarrubias and Sala Avellaneda, with a combined capacity of 3,500 people. It was inspired by Radio City Music Hall and was constructed by Purdy & Henderson with Julio Conesa as the architect.

world knowledge.Name: Birla Mandir
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Birla Mandirs are a series of Hindu temples built by the Birla family in different cities across India. The first temple, the Laxminarayan Temple in Delhi, was built in 1939 to fulfill a cultural void in cities historically ruled by Muslim dynasties, which did not permit the construction of grand Hindu temples with shikharas. These temples were designed to be lofty and spacious, suitable for congregational worship or discourses, and often incorporate modern construction materials and techniques while conforming to traditional architectural styles.

Major_Events.Description: The first Birla Mandir, the Laxminarayan Temple in Delhi, was opened in 1939. It was designed to be lofty and spacious, suitable for congregational worship or discourses, and marked the beginning of the Birla family's temple construction projects.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Birla temples are built using modern construction materials and techniques, often in the classical style of Māru-Gurjara architecture from the 10-12th century, with some elements of local, regional styles. For example, the Saraswati temple in the BITS Pilani campus is a replica of the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple of Khajuraho, built of white marble and adorned with images of Gods, philosophers, and scientists. The Gwalior Sun temple is a smaller replica of the Konark Sun Temple.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Birla Mandirs are culturally significant as they were built to fill a cultural void in cities historically ruled by Muslim dynasties, which did not permit the construction of grand Hindu temples. These temples serve as prominent places of worship and cultural centers, often incorporating elements of traditional Hindu architecture while utilizing modern construction techniques.
world knowledge.Details: The Birla temples are generally located in prominent locations, carefully designed to accommodate a large number of visitors. The worship and discourses are well organized. The Birlas also built the adjoining Buddhist temple in Delhi and donated it to the Mahabodhi Society.

world knowledge.Name: Peover Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Peover Hall is a country house built in 1585 for Sir Ralph Mainwaring. It has undergone several alterations and additions over the centuries. During World War II, it was requisitioned and used by General George Patton and his staff, and also served as a prisoner of war camp and resettlement home. The house was returned to the Brooks family in 1950 and underwent further modifications in the 1960s.

Major_Events.Description: The house was refaced for Sir Ralph Mainwaring.
A stable block was built, which is now listed at Grade I.
A wing was added at a right-angle to the house, making it T-shaped, along with a new stable block and coach house.
The house was used by General George Patton and his staff, and also served as a prisoner of war camp and resettlement home.
The 1760s wing was demolished, reducing the house from 21 to 11 bedrooms, and other modifications were made.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is built in red brick with stone dressings and a tiled roof. Early parts are partly two-storeyed with gables and partly three-storeyed with flat roofs. Windows are mullioned and transomed. The stable block features Tuscan style columns and a decorated panelled ceiling. The house includes 16th-century woodwork and furniture, 18th-century paintings and furniture, and antique furniture and toys.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Peover Hall is a designated Grade II* listed building and features a Grade I listed stable block. The gardens are listed at Grade II on the Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in England. The hall has historical significance due to its use during World War II and its association with the Mainwaring family.
world knowledge.Details: The hall has a formal garden and stands in a landscape park, likely landscaped by William Emes. The gardens were laid out between 1890 and 1905, remodelled in the 1920s, and further developed from the 1960s. The gardens are open to the public at advertised times, and tours of the house are available.

world knowledge.Name: Malahide Cricket Club Ground
world knowledge.Address: Lady Acre field of Malahide Castle grounds, Malahide, Dublin, Republic of Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Malahide Cricket Club was founded in 1861 by the 5th Baron Talbot of Malahide, Richard Wogan Talbot, who established the cricket ground in the grounds of Malahide Castle. The ground hosted its first first-class match in 1991 between Ireland and Scotland. It was developed to a capacity of 11,500 and officially opened for international cricket in 2013, becoming Ireland's biggest cricket venue.

Major_Events.Description: Ireland played against England, with England winning by six wickets. Eoin Morgan, the England captain, scored 124 not out on his former home ground.
Ireland played Pakistan in their inaugural Test match at the venue, with Kevin O'Brien scoring the maiden Test century for Ireland.
The ground was selected as a venue to host matches in the tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The ground features temporary grandstands and hospitality tents to accommodate up to 11,500 spectators, making it the largest cricket venue in Ireland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Malahide Cricket Club Ground is culturally significant as Ireland's biggest cricket venue and the site of the country's first men's Test match. It has hosted numerous international matches, contributing to the growth of cricket in Ireland.
world knowledge.Details: The ground has hosted 16 ODI centuries and seven five-wicket hauls in international matches. It is one of Ireland's three international cricket venues, alongside Castle Avenue in Dublin and the Civil Service Cricket Club Ground at Stormont.

world knowledge.Name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Azerbaijan National Carpet Museum, originally established in 1967, was first located in the Juma Mosque in Icheri Sheher. It moved to the Baku Museum Center in 1992 and then to its current location on Baku's seafront park in 2014. The museum houses the largest collection of Azerbaijani carpets in the world, showcasing historical and modern weaving techniques and materials.

Major_Events.Description: The museum's first exhibition was held in 1972.
After the collapse of the USSR, the museum was moved to the second floor of the Baku Museum Center, a building that had originally been the Lenin museum.
The museum moved to a new purpose-built building designed to look like a rolled carpet, opening on 26 August 2014.
The Garagoyunlu carpet was included in the museum's collection.
The museum presented its newest exhibit, the Lampa carpet, originally woven in Shusha during the 1930s.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The structure of the building is designed to look like a rolled carpet. It was designed by Austrian architect Franz Janz and took over six years to construct.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses the largest collection of Azerbaijani carpets in the world, reflecting the nation's history, art, and cultural identity. It also plays a role in promoting Azerbaijani culture internationally through exhibitions and research.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes over 10,000 items, including ceramics, metal works from the 14th century, jewellery from the Bronze Age, carpets from the 17th-20th centuries, national garments, and embroidery. The museum organizes public lectures, study courses, and international exhibitions. It also has a bookstore selling books on Azerbaijani crafts and carpet art.

world knowledge.Name: Atascosa County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Atascosa County was formed in 1856. The first Atascosa County Courthouse was a log building erected in Amphion in 1856. The second a frame building raised in Pleasanton in 1857. The county built a larger frame courthouse in 1868. The fourth courthouse, built in 1885 was made from red stone and served as the Pleasanton City Hall when the county seat was moved to Jourdanton. The current Atascosa County Courthouse is the fifth structure to serve as the seat of Atascosa County government.

Major_Events.Description: The current Atascosa County Courthouse was built in 1912 in Jourdanton, Texas, designed by architect Henry T. Phelps in the Mission Revival Style.
The lower floor, originally open for wood storage, was enclosed to create more office space.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places on December 30, 1997.
The courthouse was designated as a Texas State Antiquities Landmark on January 1, 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mission Revival style courthouse with towers, balconies, and a Spanish-tiled roof. It is finished in red-brown brick and cast stone. The courthouse sits on a circular plot of land in contrast to the typical Texas courthouse square. It is the only existing Mission Revival style courthouse in Texas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Atascosa County Courthouse is historically significant as the fifth and current seat of Atascosa County government, showcasing unique Mission Revival architecture. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and designated as a Texas State Antiquities Landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serves as the seat of Atascosa County government.
world knowledge.Details: The building contract was awarded to the Gordon Jones Construction Co. of San Antonio, based on a bid of $65,000. The courthouse is located on Circle Dr in Jourdanton, Texas.

world knowledge.Name: Maison Bonaparte
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Maison Bonaparte is the ancestral home of the Bonaparte family, owned almost continuously from 1682 to 1923. It was expanded and re-decorated by Carlo Buonaparte after his marriage. The family fled Corsica in 1793 due to conflict with Pasquale Paoli, and the house was looted and burned. After the British withdrawal in 1797, the family returned and repaired the house. It was later passed through the family and eventually donated to the French government, becoming a national museum in 1967.

Major_Events.Description: The Bonaparte family fled to the French mainland due to conflict with Pasquale Paoli, and the house was looted and burned by Paoli's followers.
British officers were billeted in the house after the arrival of Admiral Samuel Hood.
The Bonaparte family returned and repaired the house with funds provided by the Directory.
Zénaïde, Joseph's daughter, gave the house to Napoleon III and Empress Eugénie, who later passed it to Prince Victor Napoleon, who donated it to the French government.
The house was made into a museum and declared a national museum.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house was expanded and re-decorated by Carlo Buonaparte. It was later refurbished and expanded by Empress Eugénie in the 19th century.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Maison Bonaparte is culturally significant as the ancestral home of the Bonaparte family, including Napoleon Bonaparte. It represents the family's history and legacy in Corsica and France.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a family residence, now a museum.
world knowledge.Details: The house was partitioned between different families initially but was later unified under Giuseppe Buonaparte. Napoleon's mother's cousin, André Ramolino, and later other family members took possession of the house. It was refurbished by Empress Eugénie to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Napoleon's birth.

world knowledge.Name: Hawke's Bay Beach
world knowledge.Address: 20 km southwest of Karachi city, Pakistan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The beach is named after Bladen Wilmer Hawke, who owned a house on the beach during the 1930s.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of wetland centre by WWF
Major_Events.Description: The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) organised a wetland centre on the beach for information regarding turtles.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The beach is a nesting ground for green sea turtle and olive ridley sea turtle during winter months, making it ecologically significant.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational beach for swimming, camel and horse riding, and vacations.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is very popular, with hundreds of people visiting daily. Various accidents have occurred due to lack of proper security and damaged boats used for giving rides to people.

world knowledge.Name: Abbey of the Dormition
world knowledge.Address: Mount Zion, just outside the walls of the Old City near the Zion Gate
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Abbey of the Dormition is a Catholic abbey belonging to the Benedictine Order in Jerusalem, on Mount Zion, just outside the walls of the Old City near the Zion Gate. The Abbey is said to mark the spot where Mary, mother of Jesus, died. The Byzantine basilica Hagia Sion was built under John II, Bishop of Jerusalem in the early 5th century. It was destroyed in the 614 sack of Jerusalem by Sasanian king Khosrau II. The present church was built in the early 20th century after Kaiser Wilhelm II bought the land and presented it to the German Association of the Holy Land.

Major_Events.Description: The Byzantine basilica Hagia Sion was destroyed in the sack of Jerusalem by Sasanian king Khosrau II.
The cornerstone was laid on 7 October 1900. Construction was completed in 1910.
The abbey was vandalized with anti-Christian graffiti and insults in Hebrew.
The abbey was vandalized again with anti-Christian graffiti and insults in Hebrew.
A box of wooden crosses was set ablaze inside the Dormition Abbey.
A vandal entered the premises and damaged a crucifix, a bench, and a number of statues in the cemetery.
Vandals wrote slogans on the walls of the Abbey such as "Death to the heathen Christians, the enemies of Israel" and "May his name be obliterated".

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Abbey was built in an ecclesiastical, neo-Romanesque style that had become the state style of the new Imperial Germany. The present church is a circular building with several niches containing altars, and a choir. Two spiral staircases lead to the crypt, the site ascribed to the Dormition of the Virgin Mary, and also to the organ-loft and the gallery, from where two of the church's four towers are accessible.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Abbey of the Dormition is culturally and historically significant as it is believed to mark the spot where Mary, mother of Jesus, died. It also represents the long-standing Christian presence in Jerusalem and the complex interreligious dynamics of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The Abbey of the Dormition has been the target of occasional vandalism as a form of "price tag" terrorism by extremist Israeli nationalist religious youths. The community elected its own abbot for the first time in 1979. Since 1973 the abbey has been hosting an ecumenical year of study for students of theology from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

world knowledge.Name: Toward Point Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: Near the village of Toward, Argyll and Bute, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Toward Point Lighthouse was completed in 1812 by Robert Stevenson for the Cumbrae Lighthouse Trust. It marks the point where Loch Striven meets the Firth of Clyde. Two lighthouse keepers' houses were added in the later 1800s. The foghorn mechanism, originally a steam engine and later diesel engines, was housed in a white building on the foreshore but was decommissioned in the 1990s. The keeper's cottages were sold in 2012 and are now a private home.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was built by Robert Stevenson for the Cumbrae Lighthouse Trust.
The foghorn, originally powered by a steam engine and later diesel engines, was taken out of operation.
The keeper's cottages were sold and converted into a private home.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: White circular tower, 19 m (62 ft) in height.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Toward Point Lighthouse marks the extreme south-westerly point of the Highland Boundary Fault as it crosses the Scottish mainland. It is a category B listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigation aid for ships entering the Firth of Clyde.
world knowledge.Details: The Highland Boundary Fault does not run through Toward Point but can be located about one kilometre to the west by the presence of Serpentinite and the sudden change from younger sedimentary rocks to much older metamorphic rocks, notably Psammite. The lighthouse has a focal height of 21 m (69 ft) and a range of 22 nautical miles, with a light characteristic of Fl. W 10sec.

world knowledge.Name: Brown County Courthouse (Illinois)
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by North Street, East Court Street, Washington Street, and West Court Street, Mount Sterling, Illinois
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Brown County Courthouse is the second courthouse in the county's history, completed in 1868 and rebuilt around 1940 after a fire. The county was formed in 1839, and Mount Sterling was chosen as the county seat due to its convenient location and residents' financial contributions for public buildings. The first courthouse, built in 1841-1843, was deemed unsafe by 1864, leading to the construction of the current courthouse.

Major_Events.Description: The first courthouse was built by contractor George Tebo but was poorly constructed, requiring significant repairs by 1859 and deemed unsafe by 1864.
The second courthouse was built to replace the unsafe first courthouse and featured a two-story gable-roofed structure with a central portico and cupola.
A fire largely destroyed the 1868 courthouse, leading to a three-year rebuilding process. The cupola was not rebuilt, and the roof was changed to a hip roof.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed as part of the Mount Sterling Commercial Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse is a two-story structure with a mix of Neoclassical and Italianate architectural styles. It features a central portico with Doric columns and a hip roof. The general plan resembles the letter 'H'.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a prominent building in Mount Sterling, separating commercial areas from residential neighborhoods. It is part of the Mount Sterling Commercial Historic District, reflecting the community's historical and architectural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government building serving as the county courthouse for Brown County.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse remains in use into the 21st century and is located at the northern end of the Mount Sterling Commercial Historic District.

world knowledge.Name: Château de Compiègne
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château de Compiègne is a former royal residence built for Louis XV and later restored by Napoleon. It was one of three seats of royal government, alongside Versailles and Fontainebleau. The site was a preferred summer residence for French monarchs due to its proximity to the Forest of Compiègne. The first royal residence was built in 1374 for Charles V, with subsequent modifications by later monarchs. The château was neoclassically renovated between 1751 and 1788, gutted during the French Revolution, and restored under Napoleon in the early 19th century.

Major_Events.Description: The château underwent a thorough neoclassical renovation led by architect Ange-Jacques Gabriel and completed by his student Le Dreux de La Châtre.
The château was gutted, with furniture sold and artworks sent to the Muséum Central.
Napoleon ordered the château to be restored and updated in the Empire style, with alterations to its layout and gardens.

Major_Events.Event: Wedding of Leopold I and Louise of Orléans
Major_Events.Description: The wedding of the future King of Belgium and the daughter of Louis Philippe I took place here.
Napoleon III and Eugénie made it their autumn residence and redecorated some rooms in the Second Empire style.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical style with simplicity and clarity in both external and interior features. Later additions include Empire and Second Empire styles. The triangular plan was dictated by ancient town ramparts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The château represents French royal and imperial history, serving as a key residence for monarchs from Louis XV to Napoleon III. It reflects evolving architectural tastes from neoclassicism to Empire and Second Empire styles.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former royal and imperial residence, now a public museum complex.
world knowledge.Details: Today the château houses three museums: the royal/imperial apartments, the Museum of the Second Empire, and the National Car and Tourism Museum (featuring carriages, bicycles, and automobiles). The estate is directly linked to the Forest of Compiègne, historically used for royal hunting.

world knowledge.Name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
world knowledge.Address: 100 Raoul Wallenberg Place, Southwest, Washington, D.C.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) is the United States' official memorial to the Holocaust. It was established to document, study, and interpret Holocaust history, and to help leaders and citizens confront hatred, prevent genocide, promote human dignity, and strengthen democracy. The museum was dedicated on April 22, 1993, and has since welcomed millions of visitors from around the world.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the President's Commission on the Holocaust
Major_Events.Description: President Jimmy Carter established the Commission, chaired by Elie Wiesel, to investigate the creation of a memorial to Holocaust victims.
President Ronald Reagan helped lay the cornerstone of the museum building.
The museum was dedicated with speeches by President Bill Clinton, Israeli President Chaim Herzog, and Elie Wiesel.
James von Brunn, an antisemite, shot and killed Museum Special Police Officer Stephen Tyrone Johns.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect James Ingo Freed, the building is intended to evoke deception, fear, and solemnity, contrasting with the grandeur of typical Washington, D.C. public buildings. The design incorporates elements alluding to the Holocaust, with industrial elevators and a chronological exhibition layout.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum serves as a national memorial to the Holocaust, educating visitors about the atrocities committed during World War II and promoting human dignity and genocide prevention. It houses extensive collections of artifacts, documents, and testimonies to preserve the memory of the Holocaust.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum and memorial dedicated to Holocaust education and remembrance.
world knowledge.Details: The museum features permanent and rotating exhibitions, including the Hall of Remembrance and 'Remember the Children: Daniel's Story.' It also conducts educational programs, research initiatives, and human rights advocacy through the Committee on Conscience. The museum's collections include over 12,750 artifacts, 49 million archival documents, and 9,000 oral history testimonies.

world knowledge.Name: Fitzroy Gardens
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by Clarendon Street, Albert Street, Lansdowne Street, and Wellington Parade, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fitzroy Gardens are a major Victorian-era landscaped garden in Australia, originally swampy land drained by a creek. Designed by Clement Hodgkinson and planted by James Sinclair, it evolved from dense woodland to include sweeping lawns and ornamental flowerbeds. Over the years, features like the Conservatory and Cooks' Cottage were added. The gardens are home to diverse wildlife and serve as a significant green space in Melbourne.

Major_Events.Description: The gardens were initially designed as a dense woodland with meandering avenues.
Improved the creek water quality by diverting sewage from East Melbourne residences.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the Conservatory and arrival of Cooks' Cottage
Major_Events.Description: Added significant features to the gardens.
Converted previously used depot space into garden area with a stormwater harvesting system, café, and visitor center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Victorian-era landscaped gardens with ornamental lake, scarred tree, conservatory, Cooks' Cottage, model Tudor village, band pavilion, rotunda, fountains, and sculptures. Tree-lined avenues and diverse vegetation including Australian native plants and non-native traditional gardens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The gardens are a significant example of Victorian-era landscaping in Australia and contribute to Melbourne's reputation as the garden city. They house historical features like Cooks' Cottage and a preserved scarred tree, reflecting both colonial and Indigenous heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The gardens are home to brushtail and ringtail possums, rainbow lorikeets, ducks, microbats, grey-headed flying foxes, and powerful owls. They feature a visitor information centre, café, and are accessible via Parliament railway station and tram routes 48 and 75. The gardens are open all year with sealed paths, flat terrain, and facilities like toilets, drinking fountains, and seating.

world knowledge.Name: Yangluo Yangtze River Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 2,725 m (8,940 ft), Width: 38.5 m (126 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Yangluo Yangtze River Bridge is the fourth bridge constructed over the Yangtze in Wuhan. The first was the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge, built in 1957. To alleviate congestion and promote development, Wuhan's government began an ambitious infrastructure program in the early 1990s, leading to the construction of this bridge.

Major_Events.Description: Construction on the bridge began on November 4, 2003.
The bridge opened to traffic on December 26, 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a suspension bridge with a main span of 1,280 m (4,200 ft). It has a deck made of prefabricated concrete sections with an epoxy asphalt roadbed. The main cables are 83 cm (33 in) in diameter, consisting of 19,558 steel wires. The support towers are 163.3 m (536 ft) and 169.8 m (557 ft) tall, constructed of reinforced concrete with prestressed concrete x-braces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a key part of the G4201 Wuhan Ring Expressway, promoting development in the eastern portion of Wuhan. Its main span is the same length as the Golden Gate Bridge, adding to its notable engineering achievements.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries the G70 Fuzhou–Yinchuan Expressway and G4201 Wuhan Ring Expressway over the Yangtze River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by the China Communications Construction Company with assistance from Dorman Long, a UK-based contractor. It was the final major portion of the G4201 Wuhan Ring Expressway, including 10 km of new expressway constructed concurrently.

world knowledge.Name: Haslington Hall
world knowledge.Address: 1 km east of the village of Haslington, Cheshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Haslington Hall is a country house built by Admiral Sir Francis Vernon in 1545, incorporating parts of the original medieval manor house dating back to 1480. The manor was acquired by the Vernon family through marriage in the 14th century. The house underwent additions and alterations in the 16th, 17th, and 19th centuries. It served as a farmhouse in the late 19th century and was extensively repaired and altered in 1931. The house was restored by Tony Vernon from 1970 to 2000 and later by Peter Jans from 2019.

Major_Events.Event: World War II bombing destruction of documents
Major_Events.Description: All early documents relating to the hall were destroyed in a bank vault in Manchester during World War II bombing.
Mohammed Isaq was fined for nine serious breaches of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.
A fire occurred at Haslington Hall, and Mohammed Isaq was later jailed for 20 months for breaching fire safety rules.
The hall and estate were sold in a derelict state to retired property developer Peter Jans, who restored it.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is built partly in timber framing and partly in brick, with a slate roof. It has two storeys and six bays. The timber-framed areas are decorated with herringbone bracing, quatrefoils, and cusped concave-sided lozenges. The rear elevation is mainly in brickwork.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Haslington Hall is a designated Grade I listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance. It has connections to notable figures such as the Vernon family, Colonel H Watts, and Air Commodore Dame Felicity Peake.
world knowledge.Details: The house is claimed to have timbers salvaged from ships of the Spanish Armada in 1588. It was listed in the National Heritage List for England on 10 June 1952 with reference number 1136283. The hall was put on the market for £800,000 in 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Swansea.com Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Swansea.com Stadium, formerly known as Liberty Stadium, is an all-seated multi-use sports stadium and conferencing venue located in the Landore area of Swansea, Wales. It opened in 2005 and is the home stadium of EFL Championship club Swansea City and the Ospreys rugby team. The stadium became the first Premier League ground in Wales following Swansea City's promotion in 2011. It was built to replace outdated venues like Swansea City's Vetch Field and Ospreys' St Helen's and The Gnoll.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was officially opened on 23 July 2005 with a friendly match between Swansea City and Fulham, ending in a 1–1 draw.
The first league game was held on 6 August 2005, with Swansea defeating Tranmere Rovers 1–0.
The first capacity crowd was recorded on 1 November 2006 when The Ospreys beat Australia A 24–16.
The first competitive game and first victory for Wales was a 2–0 win over Switzerland in UEFA Euro 2012 qualification on 7 October 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium was designed by TTH Architects and features a sustainable 'bowl' design with a Desso GrassMaster surface. It has a seating capacity of 21,088.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as the first Premier League ground in Wales and a major venue for both football and rugby in the region. It has hosted numerous international matches and events, including Wales football fixtures and a UK Independence Party conference.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone several name changes, including White Rock Stadium, New Stadium Swansea, Liberty Stadium, and its current name, Swansea.com Stadium. It is the third-largest stadium in Wales and has plans for future expansions to increase capacity to 33,000 and eventually above 40,000. The stadium is also known as Swansea Stadium in UEFA competitions due to advertising regulations.

world knowledge.Name: Stadttheater Klagenfurt
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stadttheater Klagenfurt is the municipal theatre in Klagenfurt, Austria. The first theatre in Klagenfurt was installed between 1605 and 1620 as Ballhaus for the aristocracy. In 1811, the wooden structure was rebuilt in stone, called Altes Theater (Old Theatre). The present house was designed by the Viennese architecture office Fellner & Helmer and completed in 1910. It was opened on the occasion of the 60th jubilee of Franz Joseph I of Austria and named 'Kaiser Franz Joseph I. Jubiläumstheater'. The theatre was renovated in the 1960s and again from 1996 to 1998.

Major_Events.Description: The new house was opened on the occasion of the 60th jubilee of Franz Joseph I of Austria and named 'Kaiser Franz Joseph I. Jubiläumstheater'.
The house was renovated in the 1960s.
The house was renovated after designs by Günther Domenig.
The Stadttheater Klagenfurt was awarded the Nestroy Theatre Prize in different categories in these years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by the Viennese architecture office Fellner & Helmer, who had already built similar theatres in Gießen and Gablonz.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Stadttheater Klagenfurt is culturally significant as a historic municipal theatre that has hosted numerous performances and received prestigious awards like the Nestroy Theatre Prize.
world knowledge.Details: The Stadttheater Klagenfurt was awarded the Nestroy Theatre Prize in different categories in 2003, 2006 and 2011. Artists who received the prize and worked for this theatre have included Martin Kušej, Bernd Liepold-Mosser, Michael Maertens, Michael Schottenberg and Martin Zehetgruber.

world knowledge.Name: Fremantle Arts Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fremantle Arts Centre is a historic building complex built using convict labour between 1861 and 1868. It was initially used as a psychiatric hospital, known as the Fremantle Lunatic Asylum, and later renamed the Asylum for the Criminally Insane. Over the years, it served various purposes, including housing for homeless women, a midwifery school, and headquarters for the American armed services during World War II. After the war, it was used as an annexe of Fremantle Technical School and later restored to house the Western Australian Maritime Museum and Fremantle Arts Centre.

Major_Events.Description: Built using convict labour to accommodate mentally ill patients.
Patients were moved to alternative locations due to overcrowding and unsuitable conditions.
The building was repurposed to house homeless women and delinquent girls.
Served as the headquarters for the American armed services in Western Australia.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration and conversion to Arts Centre
Major_Events.Description: Major restoration project led to the establishment of the Fremantle Arts Centre.
Gable finials on the west façade were restored to their original state.
A new plan was adopted, with works including the replacement of asbestos roof cladding.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Colonial Gothic style, designed by Lieutenant-Colonel Edmund Henderson. The building features large public architecture with convict-built structures, including a north-east wing and southern wings added later.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fremantle Arts Centre is a heritage-listed building that represents the colonial history of Western Australia, including its convict past and the evolution of mental health care. It now serves as a cultural hub for arts and exhibitions, contributing to the local and regional arts scene.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a psychiatric hospital, now a cultural center hosting exhibitions, residencies, art courses, and live music.
world knowledge.Details: The site is owned by the state of Western Australia and managed by the City of Fremantle. It receives funding from the City of Fremantle and the Western Australian State Government's Department of Culture and the Arts. The center is located near other cultural and educational institutions, including the Fremantle Leisure and Aquatic Centre, John Curtin College of the Arts, and Christian Brothers College.

world knowledge.Name: Mob Museum
world knowledge.Area: Downtown Las Vegas, Nevada, United States
world knowledge.Address: 300 E Stewart Avenue, Las Vegas, NV 89101, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mob Museum, officially the National Museum of Organized Crime and Law Enforcement, is a history museum dedicated to featuring the artifacts, stories, and history of organized crime in the United States, as well as the actions and initiatives by law enforcement to prevent such crimes. The museum is housed in the former Las Vegas Post Office and Courthouse, which was built in 1933 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The idea for the museum was proposed by then-Mayor Oscar Goodman in 2002, and it opened on February 14, 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The second floor courtroom was the location of one of fourteen national Kefauver Committee hearings to expose organized crime.
The museum opened on February 14, 2012, with ceremonies reserved for press and dignitaries.
The museum opened a fully operational speakeasy and distillery in their basement exhibit, The Underground.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the former Las Vegas Post Office and Courthouse, which was built in 1933 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The building was restored to its original look as part of the museum's development.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is dedicated to the contentious relationship between organized crime and law enforcement within the historical context of Las Vegas and the entire United States. It features exhibits on Mob violence, casino revenue skimming operations, and wiretapping by law enforcement, among other topics.
world knowledge.Details: The museum offers a wide array of thematically oriented sections addressing the Mob's involvement in illegal activities such as gambling, drugs, prostitution, or bootlegging and the efforts of law enforcement to counteract and eliminate those criminal operations. The museum also features interactive exhibits, a gift shop, and a fully operational speakeasy and distillery in their basement exhibit, The Underground. The museum distills its own 100 proof, 100% corn moonshine in a custom-built pot still located in the Underground.

world knowledge.Name: Gaelic Grounds
world knowledge.Address: Ennis Road, Limerick, County Limerick, V94 CF77, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Gaelic Grounds, initially developed on a 12-acre farm purchased in 1926, was officially opened in 1928. It has undergone several renovations, including the addition of stands in 1958, 1988, and a major rejuvenation in 2004. The stadium has hosted numerous significant GAA events and other sports, including an American college football game in 1991 and an International Rules Series match in 2010.

Major_Events.Description: Record paid attendance of 61,174 for the match between Cork and Tipperary, with an estimated additional 10,000 spectators entering without paying after the gates were broken down.
An American college football game between Fordham Rams and Holy Cross Crusaders, won by Holy Cross 24-19.
Hosted a match between Australia and Ireland as part of the 2010 International Rules Series.
First time in over thirty years that a semi-final of the SFC was played outside Croke Park, attended by over 36,000 spectators.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features grass surface, a 12,000-seater uncovered stand, and two terraces behind the goals. The Old Hogan Stand from Croke Park was reassembled here in 1958.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gaelic Grounds is the principal GAA stadium in Limerick, hosting hurling and football matches. It holds significant cultural importance as a venue for major sporting events and community activities, including its use as a drive-through COVID-19 test center during the pandemic.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium, primarily for GAA hurling and football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was renamed LIT Gaelic Grounds in 2019 following a partnership agreement between Limerick GAA and Limerick Institute of Technology (LIT). It has a current capacity of 44,023, reduced from 49,866 due to health and safety restrictions and renovations.

world knowledge.Name: Jade Buddha Temple
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jade Buddha Temple was founded in 1882 with two jade Buddha statues imported from Myanmar. It was initially built in Jiang-wan, Shanghai, but the statues were later moved to Maigen Road due to the 1911 uprising. A new temple was constructed between 1918 and 1928 on land donated by Sheng Xuanhuai. The temple has undergone various events, including the Cultural Revolution, and has been a center for Buddhist activities and education.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was founded with two jade Buddha statues imported from Myanmar.
The statues were moved to Maigen Road due to the 1911 uprising.
A new temple was built on land donated by Sheng Xuanhuai.
Reverend Dixian was invited to lecture on Buddhism in a grand ceremony.
Master Taixu died in the Jade Buddha Temple.
A ceremony was held by the Shanghai Buddhist Association.
The monks made a living by selling handicrafts.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Shanghai Institute of Buddhism
Major_Events.Description: The institute was established at the temple under the Shanghai Buddhist Association.
Regular scripture lectures, meditation, and other features of temple life were resumed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple features various halls and chambers, including the Chamber of Four Heavenly Kings, the Grand Hall, and the Jade Buddha Chamber. The temple also includes public and private restaurants, a visitor services office, and a Buddhist library.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jade Buddha Temple is culturally significant as a center for Buddhism in Shanghai. It houses important jade and marble Buddha statues and has been a site for Buddhist education and ceremonies. The temple's history reflects the spread of Buddhism in China and its resilience through political and social changes.
world knowledge.Details: The temple contains a sitting Buddha (1.95 meters tall, 3 tons) and a smaller reclining Buddha, both made of jade, as well as a larger reclining Buddha made of marble. The temple is accessible via public buses and the Shanghai Metro. It also features public and private restaurants, with the public restaurant serving affordable noodle dishes.

world knowledge.Name: Verdun Memorial
world knowledge.Address: Close to the destroyed village of Fleury-devant-Douaumont, Meuse, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Verdun Memorial is a war memorial to commemorate the Battle of Verdun, fought in 1916 as part of the First World War. It remembers both French and German combatants as well as the civilian populations lost during the battle.

Major_Events.Description: A major battle during the First World War, fought between French and German forces.
The Verdun Memorial was opened to the public on September 17, 1967.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The memorial serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made during the Battle of Verdun and is a symbol of reconciliation between France and Germany. It also functions as a military museum, displaying artifacts from the battle.
world knowledge.Details: The museum displays French and German armaments, military vehicles, uniforms, and equipment from the Battle of Verdun. The nearby Douaumont ossuary contains the remains of soldiers who died during the battle.

world knowledge.Name: Imagicaa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Imagicaa is a 130-acre theme park in Khopoli, Raigad District, Maharashtra, India. It is owned by Imagicaa World Entertainment Ltd. The park opened in April 2013 and includes a hotel, water park, and snow park. It is India's largest snow park with edible snow. The parks have an estimated daily capacity of 15,000 visitors and have hosted over 10.5 million visitors.

Major_Events.Description: Imagicaa theme park opened to the public.
The park was temporarily closed in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Imagicaa reopened on 22 October 2021 following a second lockdown due to the pandemic.
An indoor snow-based theme park was opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The central park is split into six zones: Viva Europa, Americana, Jambo Africa, Asiana, Arabia, and India. The park features three roller coasters and many other rides, including one based on the 1987 Bollywood film “Mr. India” and another based on the animated character Chhota Bheem.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Imagicaa is culturally significant as it features the first official Bollywood Hall of Fame and hosts events like a special parade and carnival to celebrate Christmas.
world knowledge.Details: The park also features a comedy show, an evening lights show, and a water park that opened in 2014. The snow park is spread across an area of 15,000 sq ft (1,400 m2).

world knowledge.Name: The Avenues, Bahrain
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Avenues is a waterfront shopping center developed by the King Faisal Corniche Development Company. It was officially opened to the public on 29 October 2017. The project was created by Al Sorouh Management Company W.L.L., in partnership with M. H. Alshaya and the Kuwait-based Mabanee Corporation. Funding was provided by the National Bank of Kuwait, and construction was contracted to Nass Corporation B.S.C.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid by the Deputy Prime Minister of Bahrain, Shaikh Khalid bin Abdullah Al Khalifa.
The Mabanee Corporation announced delays due to design changes.
The Avenues was officially opened to the public on 29 October 2017.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mall is designed with a single floor to limit vertical height, featuring a family-friendly environment with numerous playgrounds, outdoor jogging tracks, a gym, waterfront restaurants, cafes, arcades, a souq, and cinemas. The design consultancy was awarded to Gensler.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Avenues aims to boost family tourism to Bahrain by providing a family-friendly environment and numerous recreational facilities. It is also a popular location due to its proximity to iconic landmarks.
world knowledge.Details: The development includes 75,000 m² of gardens, a 40m wide promenade, and public parks. The total leasable area is 38,000 m², accounting for 15% of the total development area. Parking facilities can accommodate up to 1,400 vehicles. The mall features a water taxi service for transporting passengers to and from various jetties around Bahrain.

world knowledge.Name: South Solitary Island Light
world knowledge.Address: South Solitary Island, Solitary Islands Marine Park, 15 kilometres northeast of Coffs Harbour, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: South Solitary Island Light is an active lighthouse on South Solitary Island, part of the Solitary Islands Marine Park. It was the first lighthouse in New South Wales to use kerosene over colza oil and the last to convert to electric power. Designed by Colonial Architect James Barnet, it was constructed in harsh conditions, with materials transported to the island. The lighthouse was automated and electrified in 1975, and the site was transferred to the National Parks and Wildlife Service in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first exhibited on 18 March 1880, though construction was expected to finish by 1879.
The lighthouse was extinguished for the only time in its life during World War II due to enemy submarine activity near the island.
The lighthouse was electrified using solar power and automated on 22 August 1975, officially de-manned on 28 December of that year.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to National Parks and Wildlife Service
Major_Events.Description: The station was transferred to the National Parks and Wildlife Service.
The Department of Environment, Climate Change and Water spent $440,000 AUD restoring the buildings, making them weatherproof and secure.
The Australian Maritime Safety Authority conducted a restoration of the crumbling cement and renewed paintwork at a cost of A$1.5 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower is 40 feet (12 m) tall, made of mass concrete with a round external plan, unique among its contemporaries. It features a concrete oversailing cornice topped by a gallery made of basalt blocks. The tower has three levels of cast-iron stairs leading to the lantern room. The lighthouse keepers' residence consists of one chief keeper cottage and two semidetached assistant keeper cottages, all made of mass concrete, rendered and painted. The site also includes the remains of a jetty and a small storehouse.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is considered the most isolated on the New South Wales coast and is listed on the Register of the National Estate. It represents a significant period in maritime history, being the first and last to use kerosene in New South Wales. Its construction and operation reflect the challenges of maintaining navigational aids in remote locations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Active lighthouse aiding navigation for maritime traffic.
world knowledge.Details: The current light source is a solar-powered lamp with an intensity of 38,000 candela, displaying one white flash every five seconds. The light is maintained by helicopter. The site is managed by the New South Wales Maritime Parks Authority as part of the Solitary Islands Marine Park and is usually inaccessible to the public, though it can be seen by boat tours from Coffs Harbour. The island is open for tours two weekends every year, accessible only by helicopter and guided by National Parks and Wildlife rangers.

world knowledge.Name: Kyoto Tower
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kyoto Tower was proposed in the early 1960s and constructed to coincide with the 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. It was built on the former site of Kyoto's central post office and opened to the public on December 28, 1964. The tower was controversial due to its modern design and cost, contrasting with Kyoto's traditional aesthetic.

Major_Events.Description: The tower was completed and opened to the public on December 28, 1964.
Observation deck ticket sales dropped to less than 400,000 a year, or about 1,100 a day.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tower's interior structure consists of many steel rings stacked on top of each other, covered with lightweight steel sheets welded together and painted white. It was designed to resemble a Japanese candle. The tower was built to withstand earthquakes and typhoons, capable of enduring winds up to 201 mph (90 m/s) and severe earthquakes.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kyoto Tower is a symbol of modernity in the ancient capital, contrasting with traditional Kyoto. It has been both criticized and embraced by locals for its modern design. It remains the tallest structure in Kyoto due to height restrictions in the city.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Observation tower and tourist attraction, with additional commercial and hotel facilities.
world knowledge.Details: The tower features a 100-metre-high observation deck with 360-degree views of Kyoto, including the mountains of Higashiyama, Arashiyama, and Kitayama. The supporting nine-story building houses commercial areas, a spa, and the Kyoto Tower Hotel. The tower is wheelchair accessible with adaptations like stair lifts and ramps.

world knowledge.Name: Pará State University
world knowledge.Address: Belém (five campuses), Paragominas, Conceição do Araguaia, Marabá, Altamira, Igarapé-Açu, São Miguel do Guamá, Santarém, Tucuruí, Moju, Redenção, Barcarena, Vigia de Nazaré, Cametá, Salvaterra, Castanhal, Pará, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pará State University (UEPA) is the only public university maintained by the state government of Pará, Brazil. It was established on May 18, 1993, and has grown to include 20 campuses across multiple cities in Pará.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded on May 18, 1993, as the only public university maintained by the state government of Pará.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UEPA is culturally significant as the only state-maintained public university in Pará, providing higher education opportunities across 20 campuses in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university has over 14,000 students enrolled in its 57 courses, including 23 undergraduate and 34 graduate programs. It employs 803 academic staff and 1,120 administrative staff.

world knowledge.Name: University of Nebraska–Lincoln
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Nebraska–Lincoln was chartered in 1869 by the Nebraska Legislature as part of the Morrill Act of 1862. It was the University of Nebraska until 1968, when it absorbed the Municipal University of Omaha to form the University of Nebraska system. It is the state's oldest university and the flagship institution of the state-wide system.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the University of Nebraska
Major_Events.Description: The university was established by an act of the Nebraska Legislature.

Major_Events.Event: Absorption of the Municipal University of Omaha
Major_Events.Description: The university absorbed the Municipal University of Omaha to form the University of Nebraska system.
The stadium was built to honor Nebraskans who served in various wars.
The university announced it would end its affiliation with the Big 12 Conference and join the Big Ten.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features a mix of historic and modern buildings, including the oldest building on campus, Architecture Hall (originally University Library). The campus includes large city-style buildings and agricultural facilities on East Campus.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Nebraska–Lincoln is the state's oldest university and a flagship institution. It has a rich history in academics, athletics, and research, contributing significantly to the cultural and intellectual life of Nebraska.
world knowledge.Details: The university is organized into nine colleges: Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources, Architecture, Arts and Sciences, Business, Education and Human Sciences, Engineering, Fine and Performing Arts, Journalism and Mass Communications, and Law. It is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity" and has a significant athletic program known as the Cornhuskers.

world knowledge.Name: Wattay International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wattay International Airport is Laos's main international gateway, serving the capital Vientiane. It began operations in 1999 and has undergone several expansions and renovations, including the renovation of its international terminal in 2005, the construction of a cargo terminal in 2011, and various expansion projects funded by the Japanese government and other entities.

Major_Events.Description: The airport's international terminal was renovated using grant money from the Japanese government.
The cargo terminal was built by the Lao-Japan Airport Terminal Building Service with funding from the Bank of Japan.
The single asphalt runway was elongated by 260 meters to 3,000 meters, and several other improvements were made, funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency.
The domestic terminal was expanded with funding from the Bouathip Lao Company.
The international terminal was expanded, a new domestic terminal was constructed, and several facilities were improved, funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a single asphalt runway, 45 meters wide and 3,000 meters long, capable of handling aircraft as large as the Boeing 747-400. It includes an international terminal, a domestic terminal, and a bonded warehouse building for air cargo.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As Laos's main international gateway, Wattay International Airport plays a crucial role in connecting the country to the rest of the world, facilitating tourism, trade, and cultural exchange.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is operated by the Lao Airport Authority (LAA) and serves as a hub for Lao Skyway, Lanexang Airways International, and Lao Airlines. The Lao Air Force also operates an installation at one end of the airport. The airport can be accessed by shuttle bus, taxi, car, tuk-tuk, and on foot.

world knowledge.Name: Ciudad Encantada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ciudad Encantada (English: Enchanted City) is a geological site near the city of Cuenca, in the autonomous community of Castilla–La Mancha, Spain, in which the erosive forces of weather and the waters of the nearby Júcar river have formed rocks into distinctive and memorable shapes. It was declared a Natural Site of National Interest on 11 June 1929. The rock formations of Ciudad Encantada are karst formations made of limestone and dolomite, which date back to the Cretaceous period, approximately 90 million years ago. Rain falling on the original limestone plateau wore down the porous limestone, leaving behind the more resistant dolomite. Because the dolomite was not always distributed evenly in the original rock, the result was the irregularly eroded shapes that form the Ciudad Encantada.

Major_Events.Event: Declared a Natural Site of National Interest
Major_Events.Description: Ciudad Encantada was declared a Natural Site of National Interest on 11 June 1929.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The rock formations are karst formations made of limestone and dolomite, resulting in irregularly eroded shapes due to the uneven distribution of dolomite in the original rock.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ciudad Encantada is culturally significant as a unique geological site with distinctive rock formations shaped by natural erosive forces, and it has been recognized as a Natural Site of National Interest.
world knowledge.Details: Ciudad Encantada appears as a location in several films. This article about a location in the autonomous community of Castilla–La Mancha, Spain is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Montaza Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Montaza Palace is a palace, museum, and extensive gardens in Alexandria, Egypt. It was built on a low plateau east of central Alexandria overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. The Salamlek Palace was built in 1892 by Khedive Abbas II as a hunting lodge and residence. The larger El-Haramlek Palace and royal gardens were added in 1932 by King Fuad I as a summer palace. President Anwar El-Sadat renovated the original Salamlek Palace as an official presidential residence, later used by Hosni Mubarak.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Khedive Abbas II as a hunting lodge and residence.
Added by King Fuad I as a summer palace.
Renovated the Salamlek Palace as an official presidential residence.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mixture of Ottoman and Florentine styles, with two towers. One tower has Italian Renaissance design details. The palace has long open arcades facing the sea along each floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Montaza Palace is a significant historical site representing the Muhammad Ali Dynasty and Egypt's royal history. It serves as a public museum and park, preserving cultural heritage and providing recreational space.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a royal residence, now a public museum, park, and presidential residence.
world knowledge.Details: El-Montaza Park, the former royal gardens, is now a public landscape park and forest reserve. El-Haramlek Palace is a museum of the Muhammad Ali Dynasty family history and objects d'art. El Salamlek Palace is now an adjacent hotel.

image_name: Burlington Bay James N. Allan Skyway

world knowledge.Name: Burlington Bay James N. Allan Skyway
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 2,560 metres (8,400 ft) - 1958 span; 2,215 metres (7,267 ft) - 1985 span
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called the Burlington Bay Skyway, the bridge was built to span the Burlington Bay Canal, linking Fort Erie with Toronto as part of the Queen Elizabeth Way (QEW). The first bridge opened in 1958, and a second bridge was added in 1985 to accommodate increased traffic. Tolls were removed in 1973 due to traffic flow issues. The bridge was named after James Noble Allan, a former Ontario Minister of Highways.

Major_Events.Description: The first bridge (steel structure) officially opened on October 30, 1958.
Tolls were removed on December 28, 1973, after they were found to impede traffic flow.
The second bridge (concrete structure) opened on October 11, 1985.
The original bridge was extensively rehabilitated after the new bridge opened.
A dump truck crashed into the bridge on July 31, 2014, causing temporary closure and requiring extensive repairs.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 1958 bridge is a steel through-arch truss bridge with a suspended deck, while the 1985 bridge is a precast concrete box girder. The 1958 span has a main span of 151 metres (495 ft) and a total length of 2,560 metres (8,400 ft). The 1985 span is 2,215 metres (7,267 ft) long. Both bridges have a width of 30 metres (98 ft) and a clearance below of 36.7 metres (120 ft).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Skyway is a vital transportation link in the Golden Horseshoe region, facilitating traffic between Toronto and Fort Erie. It is also an engineering landmark, showcasing mid-20th-century bridge design and construction techniques.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (freeway bridge carrying the Queen Elizabeth Way)
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by John Turner Bell and constructed with 20,000 short tons of steel and 90,000 cubic yards of concrete. The twinning project in the 1980s included upgrades to the freeway approaches and the installation of Ontario's first freeway traffic management system. The bridge was renamed in 1988 to honor James N. Allan.

world knowledge.Name: Saltmarshe Hall
world knowledge.Address: Saltmarshe, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Saltmarshe Hall is a grade II* listed 19th-century country house. The estate has belonged to the Saltmarshe family since the Norman Conquest in 1066. The present house was built in 1825-8 by Prichett and Watson for Philip Saltmarshe. It descended to Colonel Phillip Saltmarshe, who fought in the Afghan and Boer Wars. The last family member, Captain Philip Saltmarshe, died in the early 1970s without an heir, and the house was sold. In 2009, it was purchased by the Whyte family.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Prichett and Watson (James Pigott Pritchett and Charles Watson) for Philip Saltmarshe at a cost of £4000.
Stables were added to the estate.
Captain Philip Saltmarshe, the last family member, died without an heir, and the house was sold to Philip and Sally Bean.
The house was offered for sale and purchased by the Whyte family.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Constructed of brick faced with ashlar with Welsh slate roofs. The square two-storey main building has a five-bay frontage with a five-bay servant's wing attached.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Saltmarshe Hall is a grade II* listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. The estate has been in the Saltmarshe family since the Norman Conquest, adding to its historical significance.
world knowledge.Details: The house stands on the north bank of the River Ouse across from Goole.

world knowledge.Name: Madinat Jumeirah
world knowledge.Address: Madinat Jumeirah, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Madinat Jumeirah is designed to resemble a traditional Arabian town and is the largest resort in the Emirate of Dubai. It encompasses three boutique hotels and a cluster of summerhouses, all designed with traditional Arabian architectural elements.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The resort features middle eastern architecture with geometric patterns, extensive use of wooden structures, and calligraphic designs. It includes 5.4 km of waterways linking different areas of the resort.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Madinat Jumeirah is culturally significant as it embodies traditional Arabian architecture and lifestyle, offering a unique cultural experience in a modern resort setting.
world knowledge.Details: Madinat Jumeirah comprises three boutique hotels (Jumeirah Al Qasr, Jumeirah Mina A'Salam, and Jumeirah Al Naseem) and a courtyard of 29 summer houses called Jumeirah Dar Al Masyaf. The resort is located along two kilometres of private beachfront adjacent to Jumeirah Beach Hotel, Burj Al Arab, and Wild Wadi Water Park. It is one mile away from the Mall of the Emirates station on the red line metro.

world knowledge.Name: Kenneth Kaunda International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Off the Great East Road, approximately 27 kilometres northeast of the city centre of Lusaka, Zambia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Opened in 1967 as Lusaka International Airport, it was renamed in 2011 in honour of Kenneth Kaunda, the nation's first president. The airport underwent a significant expansion from 2015 to 2021, funded by the Exim Bank of China, which included the construction of a new terminal and other facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Inauguration of Zambia Airways route to New York
Major_Events.Description: Zambia Airways inaugurated a route to New York via Monrovia, which was suspended in March 1991 due to financial constraints.

Major_Events.Event: KLM begins operating flights to Lusaka
Major_Events.Description: KLM began operating a flight three times a week between Amsterdam and Lusaka using an Airbus A330-200, which was later restructured to also serve Harare.
The new terminal, Terminal Two, was officially opened on 5 August 2021, handling all international flights, while Terminal One continues to serve domestic flights.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two terminals. Terminal One has no jet bridges and is used for domestic traffic. Terminal Two, opened in August 2021, has six gates and handles all international flights. The expansion included a new two-story terminal building, 22 check-in counters, 12 border channels, six security check counters, a presidential terminal, a new air traffic control building and tower, and a new hotel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Kenneth Kaunda, the first president of Zambia, and serves as a major hub for air travel in the region, accounting for 75% of all passenger airport traffic in Zambia in 2022.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a capacity of 6 million passengers and is the largest in Zambia. It serves as a hub for Zambia Airways, Proflight Zambia, Royal Zambian Airlines, and Mahogany Air. Taxis are the most common form of transport to and from the city, with a 15 to 20-minute ride to the city centre. There are also car rental companies (Avis and Europcar) and hotel shuttle services available. A bus line connects the airport to the Chelston bus station, but it does not run on a regular schedule.

world knowledge.Name: Nong Han Lake
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nong Han Lake is the largest natural lake in northeast Thailand, located northeast of the provincial capital town of Sakon Nakhon. It is fed by the Nam Pung river, which originates in the Phu Phan Mountains, and its outflow is the Huai Nam Khan, which flows into the Mekong. The lake has ecological and cultural significance, with local folklore associated with it. During 2012, there were protests over the Dhammakaya Buddhist sect's application for a title deed for 80% of the main island on the lake, Heavenly Hill Island, due to ecological and traditional access concerns.

Major_Events.Event: Protests over Dhammakaya Buddhist sect's land claim
Major_Events.Description: Local residents objected to the Dhammakaya Buddhist sect's application for a title deed for 80% of the main island on the lake, Heavenly Hill Island, due to ecological and traditional access concerns. The conflict also involved the local chamber of commerce and other organizations.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nong Han Lake is culturally significant as it is the largest natural lake in northeast Thailand and shares folklore associated with Nong Han Kumphawapi Lake in Udon Thani Province. It also serves as a public park for the nearby city of Sakon Nakhon.
world knowledge.Details: The lake is fished, with 20% of the fish caught being Puntius brevis. Swimming in the lake is risky due to parasitic liver flukes. Sakon Nakhon Hospital is located adjacent to the lake.

world knowledge.Name: King Fahd Causeway
world knowledge.Address: Khobar, Saudi Arabia, and Al Jasra, Bahrain
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 25 km (16 mi) long, 23 m (75 ft) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The King Fahd Causeway is a 25 km long series of bridges and causeways connecting Khobar, Saudi Arabia, and Al Jasra, Bahrain. The idea of building a bridge linking Bahrain to the eastern region of Saudi Arabia had been of great interest to the two kingdoms for generations. The project began during an official visit to Bahrain in 1954 by King Saud, with the aim of nurturing and further solidifying the bonds between the two countries. Construction officially started in 1981 and was completed in 1986.

Major_Events.Description: The causeway was officially inaugurated on 26 November 1986 in the presence of King Fahd and Sheikh Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa.
The causeway was used by Saudi-led forces to cross into Bahrain on 14 March 2011 to assist the Bahraini government in suppressing an anti-government uprising.
One-stop crossing was introduced on the King Fahd Causeway from 6 March 2017, easing travel for commuters and reducing traffic congestion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The causeway consists of five bridges resting on 536 concrete pylons, with seven embankments in the Gulf's shallower water. It was built using 350,000 m³ of concrete and 147,000 metric tonnes of reinforced steel. The border station, known as Middle Island, includes customs and immigration facilities, a mosque, gardens, and fast food restaurants.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The King Fahd Causeway is a symbol of the strong cultural and social bonds between Saudi Arabia and Bahrain. It has significantly improved connectivity and economic ties between the two countries.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation link between Saudi Arabia and Bahrain
Notable_Visitors: Sheikh Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa
world knowledge.Details: The causeway spans long stretches of sea and reclaimed land. It includes an artificial island with customs and immigration facilities, a mosque, and gardens. The project cost a total of US$800 million and was constructed by Ballast Nedam, based in the Netherlands. As of 2010, an estimated 25,104 vehicles use the causeway daily, with 19.1 million passengers crossing annually.

world knowledge.Name: Centraal Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Centraal Museum is the main museum in Utrecht, Netherlands, founded in 1838. Initially, the collection was exhibited on the top floor of the Utrecht town hall and was limited to art related to the city of Utrecht. In 1921, the collection merged with various private collections in the new 'centralised museum' located in the former medieval monastery at the Nicolaaskerkhof. The museum's collection comprises pre-1850 art, modern art, applied art, fashion, and the city history of Utrecht. Since 1980, it includes the collection of the Van Baaren Museum and since 2006, it also runs the Miffy Museum and the Rietveld Schröder House.

Major_Events.Description: The collection merged with various private collections in the new 'centralised museum' located in the former medieval monastery at the Nicolaaskerkhof.

Major_Events.Event: Inclusion of Van Baaren Museum collection
