It is a primitive Greek Revival house originally built in 1844 for Robert B Sheegog, an Irish immigrant enslaver from Tennessee. Faulkner purchased the house when it was in disrepair in 1930, and resided there until his death in 1962. The home has been owned and operated by the University of Mississippi since 1972, and is open to the public year-round.

Major_Events.Description: Faulkner purchased the house when it was in disrepair and renamed it 'Rowan Oak' in 1931.
Faulkner won the Nobel Prize for Literature during his time at Rowan Oak.

Major_Events.Event: Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award
Major_Events.Description: Faulkner won the Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award for 'A Fable'.
The University of Mississippi purchased Rowan Oak and preserved it as it was at the time of Faulkner's death.
Rowan Oak was declared a National Historic Landmark.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Greek Revival style, originally designed with an L-shaped layout with a 450 square foot center hall connecting a parlor and dining room on one side with a library on the other. Features from the antebellum era remain on the property including the alley of Eastern Red Cedar trees, a Concentric Circle Garden, Post Oak Barn, and Slave Dwelling.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rowan Oak is culturally significant as the home of Nobel Prize-winning author William Faulkner, where he wrote many of his famous works. The property is preserved to promote Faulkner's literary legacy and is a National Historic Landmark.
world knowledge.Details: House admission is $5.00 each cash only. Free admission to children under 12 and University of Mississippi students, faculty, and staff. The home contains 90% of all the original furnishings and is preserved as it was at the time of Faulkner's death in 1962. The current curators are William Griffith and Rachel Hudson.

world knowledge.Name: Drumlane
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Drumlane, meaning 'The Broad Ridge', is a townland and civil parish in County Cavan, Ireland. Saint Columba brought Christianity to Drumlane in 555, and Saint Máedóc of Ferns founded an early monastery here. The site has been a significant religious and political center, with connections to the O'Rourke and O'Reilly clans. It was attacked by Vikings in 836 and later burned during clan feuds. The Augustinian priory was established in the 12th century and dissolved in the 16th century. The site includes a ruined church and round tower, now under the care of the OPW.

Major_Events.Description: Drumlane was attacked by Viking raiders along with other abbeys in the region.
Drumlane church was burned during a feud between the O'Rourke and O'Reilly clans.
Battles took place between the O'Conors, O'Ruaircs, and O'Reillys, with peace eventually settled in 1391.
Drumlane priory was confiscated under Henry VIII's rule and later granted to Hugh O'Reilly in 1567.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original monastic structures were built from wood, later rebuilt in stone in Romanesque and Gothic styles. The church features a nave and chancel, with rounded and Gothic arched doorways and windows. The round tower, standing 11.6 meters tall, is a key example of Romanesque craftsmanship. The site includes decorative masonry, tomb niches, and sedilia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Drumlane is a significant monastic site with connections to early Irish Christianity, clan politics, and medieval architecture. It represents the religious and political history of the Breifne region and is a key example of Irish ecclesiastical architecture.
world knowledge.Details: The site includes a cemetery still in use today. A 2021 survey identified the sub-surface footprint of the priory buildings. Drumlane is designated as a National Monument and is open to visitors.

world knowledge.Name: Shimotsui–Seto Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Connecting Okayama and Kagawa prefectures, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Great Seto Bridge was built to connect Honshū and Shikoku islands, fulfilling a vision that began in the late 19th century. The project gained urgency after a 1955 ferry disaster that killed 171 people. Construction faced delays due to the 1973 oil shock but was completed in 1988.

Major_Events.Description: A collision of two ferries in dense fog off Takamatsu killed 171 people, including 100 students, prompting calls for a safer crossing.
The bridge was officially opened to road and rail traffic by then-Crown Prince Akihito.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Double-decked bridge system with two lanes of highway traffic on the upper deck and one railway track in each direction on the lower deck. Constructed using 3.646 million cubic meters of concrete and 705,000 tons of steel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge symbolizes the unification of Honshū and Shikoku, improving transportation and communication. It also honors the vision of Jinnojo Ōkubo, who advocated for better connectivity in Shikoku in the late 19th century.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is part of the Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project and is the only route to carry rail traffic. It consists of six named bridges and five viaducts. The toll fee at opening was ¥6300 for a one-way drive.

world knowledge.Name: Camp d'Esports
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Camp d'Esports is a multi-use stadium in Lleida, Catalonia. Construction began in 1918 and finished in 1919. It was officially opened on January 1, 1919. The stadium underwent extensive renovations in 1993 and 1994.

Major_Events.Description: The sports complex named 'Camp d'Esports' was officially opened.
The stadium underwent extensive renovations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a grass surface and a capacity of 13,500 seats. The football field dimensions are 102x68 meters. The original architect was Adolf Florensa, and the 1993 renovation was led by Robert Brufau.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Camp d'Esports is the home ground of Lleida Esportiu and is an important sports venue in Catalonia.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-use stadium, primarily for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a sports venue in Catalonia is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Badminton House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Badminton House is a large country house and Grade I Listed Building in Badminton, Gloucestershire, England, which has been the principal seat of the Dukes of Beaufort since the late 17th century. The house, which has given its name to the sport of badminton, is set among 52,000 acres of land. The gardens and park surrounding the house are listed at Grade I on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. The property was acquired by the Dukes of Beaufort in the late 17th century, when the family moved from Raglan Castle, Monmouthshire, which had been ruined in the Civil War. The house has undergone several renovations and extensions over the centuries, incorporating various architectural styles.

Major_Events.Description: The sport of badminton was either re-introduced from British India or invented during the hard winter of 1863 by the children of the eighth duke in the Great Hall. It was popularised at the house, hence the sport's name.
Queen Mary stayed at Badminton House for much of World War II. Her staff occupied most of the building, to the inconvenience of the Duke and Duchess of Beaufort.
The annual Badminton Horse Trials have been held at Badminton House since 1949, making the house well-known for this event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Badminton House features a Palladian architectural style with earlier elements. The house includes a grand Jonesian centrepiece on the north front, domed crowning pavilions by James Gibbs, and various gabled ranges around the courtyard. The house was renovated and extended by William Kent in the Palladian style, but many earlier elements remain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Badminton House is culturally significant as the principal seat of the Dukes of Beaufort and for giving its name to the sport of badminton. It has been a center for fox hunting and is associated with the Beaufort Hunt. The house has also been featured in several films and TV series, adding to its cultural prominence.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Country house and estate, hosting events such as weddings, parties, and the Badminton Horse Trials.
world knowledge.Details: Adjacent to Badminton House is the Grade I listed parish church of St Michael and All Angels, built in 1785. It serves as the principal burial place of the Somerset family; nearly all Dukes and Duchesses of Beaufort are interred here. At the north entrance to the park is the Grade I listed Worcester Lodge, designed in 1746 by William Kent. Several buildings and follies were designed by Thomas Wright of Durham around 1750. The estate has been used as a location for films such as The Remains of the Day, 28 Days Later, Pearl Harbor, and TV series like Bridgerton, Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story, and The Gentlemen.

world knowledge.Name: Ponte dei Trepponti
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Trepponti bridge was commissioned by Cardinal Giovan Battista Pallotta as part of Comacchio's renovation under the Papal States in the 16th century. Designed by architect Luca Danese, it was completed in 1638 to serve as a city gate and entryway into Comacchio's internal canal network. Guard towers were added in 1695, and parapets were later replaced with decorative columns in 1823.

Major_Events.Description: Completed as part of Comacchio's renovation and defensive works.
Towers were added under Cardinal Giuseppe Renato Imperiali to reinforce defensive parapets.
Engineer Giovanni Tosi oversaw the removal of parapets and their replacement with decorative columns.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Trepponti bridge is a rare five-way masonry arch bridge made of Istrian stone. It features a central pentagonal public square held up by a cross-vaulted ceiling, five staircases connecting to city streets, and two guard towers. Decorative columns and a plaque with a passage from Torquato Tasso are also present.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a notable example of 17th-century defensive and architectural engineering, serving as a historic gateway to Comacchio. Its unique five-way design and poetic inscription highlight its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a defensive city gate and entryway into Comacchio's canal network; later included a fish market.
world knowledge.Details: The name 'Trepponti' refers to the three-way split in the canal, though the bridge technically consists of five arches. A fish market was established at the site at an unspecified later date.

world knowledge.Name: Tokushima University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tokushima University was founded in 1949 by merging six national education facilities into one. It was originally named the University of Tokushima but was renamed Tokushima University on April 1, 2015.

Major_Events.Description: Six national education facilities were merged to form Tokushima University, establishing the Faculty of Integrated Arts and Sciences, Faculty of Engineering, and Faculty of Medicine.
The university was renamed from the University of Tokushima to Tokushima University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tokushima University is a prominent national university in Japan with seven graduate schools and five undergraduate faculties. It is notable for its contributions to education and research, including producing Nobel Prize laureate Shuji Nakamura.
world knowledge.Details: Tokushima University has 7,482 full-time students and connections with over 70 higher education institutions across Europe and Asia. It operates on three campuses: Shinkura (administrative head office), Jōsanjima, and Kuramoto. Notable alumni include Shuji Nakamura, inventor of the first high-brightness GaN LED and 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics laureate, and Shigenori Maruyama, a Purple Honour Medal recipient for his work related to plume tectonics.

world knowledge.Name: Sabina Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sabina Park is a cricket ground and the home of the Kingston Cricket Club, and is the only Test cricket ground in Kingston, Jamaica. Originally a Pen (urban residence and adjoining land of a wealthy merchant, shopkeeper or professional), part of which was eventually sold to the Kingston Cricket Club for their grounds. The name is a 'transfer name', copied from the region around Rome of Magliano Sabina. Sabina Park, the slave, was owned by Joseph Gordon, father of National Hero George William Gordon. Known ownership of Sabina Park Pen includes rental by Kingston Cricket Club from Mrs. Blakely in 1880, and its purchase in 1890.

Major_Events.Description: West Indies v England
West Indies v Pakistan
West Indies v Australia
West Indies v Ireland
West Indies v Ireland
West Indies v South Africa
West Indies v Australia
West Indies v New Zealand
West Indies v England
Involving the touring England team, abandoned due to the pitch being deemed unfit for play

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The members pavilion lies square of the wicket on the west side. The George Headley Stand dominates the south end, and the Eastern Stands have given way to a 'Party Stand'. The ground has a five-level concrete stand hosting outside broadcast facilities, players facilities, and private boxes. Floodlights were commissioned in August 2014, making it capable of hosting day/night matches.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sabina Park is significant in Test cricket history, recording the first triple century by England's Andy Sandham and Sir Garfield Sobers' 365 not out, which stood as a Test record for over 36 years. It also hosted the Jamaica national football team prior to Independence Park opening in 1962.
world knowledge.Details: Sabina Park became a Test cricket ground in 1930. A mural featuring 19 famous Jamaican cricketers was constructed outside the ground in 2021. The ground's capacity has increased to 20,000 with refurbishing. It is the home ground for the Jamaica cricket team and the Jamaica Tallawahs.

world knowledge.Name: Royal Villa of Durrës
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Royal Villa of Durrës, also known as Vila e Zogut, is a historical building in Durrës, Albania. It served as the summer residence of King Zog and was a symbol of the monarchy in the city. The villa was designed by Kristo Sotiri, an architect with experience from the University of Padova and the University of Venice, Italy. It was completed in 1937 and was used as a government reception building after World War II. The interior was vandalized during the 1997 unrest in Albania, and Prince Leka has outlined a reconstruction plan.

Major_Events.Description: The villa was restored to Leka Crown Prince of Albania in 2007, following all legal procedures without contest.
The interior of the villa was vandalized during the 1997 unrest in Albania.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The villa is designed in the Rationalism and Monumental Rationalism architectural styles. It is set on a hill 98 meters above sea level, with views of the sea from three sides. The building is extended in the form of an eagle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The villa is a symbol of the Albanian monarchy and has hosted notable figures such as Soviet first secretary Nikita Khrushchev, Cambodian prince Samde Norodom Sihanuk, and former US President Jimmy Carter.
world knowledge.Details: The villa was a gift from the Durrës business community to King Zog as a sign of prosperity. It was designed by Kristo Sotiri, who had previously worked for the Court of Queen Elisabeth of Wied of Romania. The building was completed in 1937, just before King Zog married Queen Géraldine Apponyi de Nagyappony.

world knowledge.Name: Hardinge Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Ishwardi, Pabna and Bheramara, Kushtia, Bangladesh
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hardinge Bridge is a steel railway truss bridge over the Padma River, named after Lord Hardinge, the Viceroy of India from 1910 to 1916. Construction began in 1910 and was completed in 1912, with trains starting to use it in 1915. The bridge was proposed in 1889 for easier communication between Calcutta and Eastern Bengal and Assam. It was severely damaged during the Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971 and later reconstructed with help from the Japanese government.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed after two years of construction.
Lord Hardinge officially opened the bridge on 4 March 1915.
The bridge was severely damaged during the Liberation War of Bangladesh when the Indian Air Force bombed it to disrupt Pakistani army movements.
The bridge was reconstructed with help from the Japanese government and reopened on 12 October 1972.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a steel truss bridge with 15 steel trusses and modified 'Petit' type main girders. It features two guide banks of the 'Bell-bund' type to prevent bank erosion and ensure the river flows permanently under the bridge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hardinge Bridge is a significant historical and engineering landmark in Bangladesh, symbolizing colonial-era infrastructure and playing a crucial role in the country's railway network. Its reconstruction after the 1971 war also marks a period of national resilience and international cooperation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Railway transportation across the Padma River.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is the second longest railway bridge in Bangladesh. Another bridge named Lalon Shah Bridge for road transport has been constructed beside the Hardinge Bridge.

image_name: Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History

world knowledge.Name: Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History
world knowledge.Address: Şoseaua Pavel D. Kiseleff, Bucharest, Romania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History was originally established as the National Museum of Natural History on 3 November 1834. It was renamed in 1933 after Grigore Antipa, who administered the museum for 51 years. The museum was reorganized in a new building designed by the architect Grigore Cerchez and inaugurated by Carol I of Romania in 1908. It underwent a $14 million renovation and reopened in 2011.

Major_Events.Description: The new building of the museum, designed by architect Grigore Cerchez, was inaugurated by Carol I of Romania.
The museum was renamed after Grigore Antipa, who administered it for 51 years.
The museum was reopened after a $14 million renovation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a building designed by the architect Grigore Cerchez.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is regarded as one of the most prestigious and well-organized natural history museums in the world, with a collection of over 2 million specimens.
world knowledge.Details: The museum’s collection consists of over 2 million specimens. It is located in Bucharest, Romania, and its website is www.antipa.ro.

world knowledge.Name: Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro
world knowledge.Address: Copacabana Beach, Avenida Atlântica, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally called Sacopenapã, meaning 'the way of the socós' in Tupi language, it was renamed after the construction of a chapel holding a replica of the Virgen de Copacabana, the patron saint of Bolivia. The district became prominent in the mid-18th century and was considered one of the best neighborhoods in Brazil when Rio was the capital.

Major_Events.Description: Copacabana Beach has hosted 11 of the 15 FIFA Beach Soccer World Cups, including the first three editions.

The beach hosts millions of revellers during New Year's Eve, featuring one of the largest fireworks displays in the world, concerts, and cultural celebrations. The event became a major tourist attraction, especially from the 1990s onwards.
Copacabana served as one of the four 'Olympic Zones' during the 2016 Summer Olympics.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Copacabana promenade is a 4-kilometer-long pavement landscape with a distinctive black and white Portuguese pavement design featuring a geometric wave, designed by Roberto Burle Marx in the 1970s. The area is dominated by high-rise residential buildings (11-13 stories) with few houses or low-rise structures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Copacabana is one of the most famous beaches in the world, symbolizing Rio de Janeiro's vibrant culture and lifestyle. It is a hub for tourism, sports, and major events like New Year's Eve celebrations and beach soccer tournaments. The area also reflects historical and urban development trends in Brazil.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational (beach, tourism, sports, and cultural events)

Details.Transportation: Served by 40+ bus routes and 3 subway stations (Cantagalo, Siqueira Campos, Cardeal Arcoverde)
Details.Major_Roads: Avenida Atlântica (6-lane, 4 km), Nossa Senhora de Copacabana Avenue, Barata Ribeiro/Raul Pompéia Street
Details.Special_Notes: No New Year's Eve celebration in 2020-21 due to COVID-19, but fireworks display continued.

world knowledge.Name: National Assembly Building of Suriname
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a military park established in 1872, later became a private club in 1877. The park house was confiscated by the military regime after the 1980 Surinamese coup d'état. Since 1996, it has housed the National Assembly of Suriname after their original building burned down.

Major_Events.Description: The square was turned into a military park maintained by the army but accessible to the public.
The park became the property of the private club Buiten-Sociëteit ‘Het Park’.
The bandstand was moved to the square following public protests.
The park house was confiscated after the 1980 Surinamese coup d'état.
The National Assembly moved to the park house after their original building burned down.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park house was extended in 1960, and a new building was constructed in 1968. The original club house was rebuilt from the plantation house of plantation Dordrecht.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The site has served as a public park, a private club, and now houses the National Assembly, reflecting Suriname's colonial and post-colonial history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently serves as the seat of the National Assembly of Suriname; previously a private club and public park.
world knowledge.Details: The park originally featured a buffet, bandstand, and bowling alley. Musical performances were held every Sunday afternoon until the early 20th century. Plans to construct a new parliament building have been delayed, with the National Assembly remaining in the park house as of 2021.

world knowledge.Name: Burj Khalifa
world knowledge.Address: 1 Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Burj Khalifa is a skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates and the world's tallest structure. It was designed to be the centerpiece of large-scale, mixed-use development. The building is named after the former president of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The United Arab Emirates government provided Dubai with financial support as the developer, Emaar Properties, experienced financial problems during the Great Recession.

Major_Events.Description: The exterior of the structure was completed.
The building was officially opened.
French BASE jumpers Vince Reffet and Fred Fugen broke the Guinness world record for the highest BASE jump from a building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The design is derived from the Islamic architecture of the region, such as in the Great Mosque of Samarra. The Y-shaped tripartite floor geometry is designed to optimise residential and hotel space. A buttressed central core and wings are used to support the height of the building. The structure also features a cladding system which is designed to withstand Dubai's hot summer temperatures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Burj Khalifa is a symbol of Dubai's rapid growth and diversification from an oil-based economy to one that is service and tourism based. It has garnered international recognition and investment.
world knowledge.Details: The Burj Khalifa set several world records, including the tallest structure and building in the world. It features 57 elevators and 8 escalators, and has an outdoor observation deck named At the Top on the 124th floor. The building is surrounded by an eleven-hectare park designed by landscape architects SWA Group.

world knowledge.Name: Sipadan
world knowledge.Address: Off the east coast of Sabah, Malaysia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Rising 600 metres (2,000 ft) from the seabed
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sipadan is the only oceanic island in Malaysia, formed by living corals growing on top of an extinct volcanic cone. It was at the center of a territorial dispute between Malaysia and Indonesia, which was resolved by the International Court of Justice in 2002, awarding the island to Malaysia. It was declared a bird sanctuary in 1933 and re-gazetted in 1963.

Major_Events.Description: The International Court of Justice awarded Sipadan and Ligitan islands to Malaysia based on effective occupation.
21 people were kidnapped by the Filipino Moro pirate group Abu Sayyaf, leading to increased security measures.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad agreed to return the management of Sipadan and Ligitan islands from the Malaysian National Security Council to the Sabah government.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sipadan is at the heart of the Indo-Pacific basin, home to one of the richest marine habitats in the world, with over 400 species of fish and hundreds of coral species. It is also known for its turtle nesting sites and diverse marine life.
world knowledge.Details: Visiting Sipadan Island requires a permit issued by Sabah Parks, with 178 permits available each day since 2019. The island features unique dive sites, including a turtle tomb formed by an underwater limestone cave.

world knowledge.Name: Lan Sang National Park
world knowledge.Area: Dawna Range, Tak Province, northern Thailand
world knowledge.Address: Tak-Mae Sot Highway, Mueang Tak District, Tak Province, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1979, Lan Sang National Park is an IUCN Category II protected area and became Thailand's 15th national park. The precise meaning of the name is not known, as each of the two words have various interpretations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lan Sang National Park is significant for its diverse ecosystems and as a protected area contributing to biodiversity conservation in Thailand.
world knowledge.Details: Lan Sang National Park covers an area of 65,000 rai and includes various types of forest such as rain forest, coniferous forest, hill evergreen forest, deciduous dipterocarp forest, and mixed deciduous forest. Wildlife includes common wild pig, barking deer, Siamese big-headed turtle, serow, civet, Black-crested Bulbul, and flying lizards.

world knowledge.Name: Vágar Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Vágar Airport was built by British Army Royal Engineers during World War II on the island of Vágar, known as RAF Vagar/Vaagar. It was chosen for its concealment from potential German warships. The first aeroplane landed in Autumn 1942. After the war, it was abandoned until 1963 when it was reopened as a civilian airport. The airport has since undergone several expansions and upgrades, including runway extensions and a new terminal.

Major_Events.Description: The first aeroplane landed at Vágar Airport, which was built by British Army Royal Engineers during World War II.
The airport was reopened as a civilian airport by Sørvágur residents Hugo Fjørðoy and Lars Larsen, with scheduled flights operated by Icelandair.
The runway was extended from 1,250 m to 1,799 m, allowing a greater variety of aircraft types and further destinations.
A new airport terminal opened with increased passenger capacity.
Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) began flying from Copenhagen to Vágar, the first airline other than Atlantic Airways to do so in many years.
Atlantic Airways inaugurated seasonal service to Stewart Airport, near New York City, which was later cancelled.
Icelandair resumed seasonal service to Iceland with De Havilland Canada Dash-8 aircraft from Reykjavík-Keflavík International Airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway of 1,800 meters with an asphalt surface, a modern terminal building, and advanced navigation systems including the Required Navigation Performance procedure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Vágar Airport is the only airport in the Faroe Islands, making it a crucial transportation hub for the archipelago. It has played a significant role in the region's history, from its origins as a military airfield during World War II to its current status as a civilian airport connecting the Faroe Islands to the rest of the world.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is managed by the Danish Transport Authority, although ownership was handed over to the Faroese government in May 2007. It serves as the main operating base for Atlantic Airways and has seen various airlines operate flights over the years, including Icelandair, Maersk Air, and Scandinavian Airlines. The airport is connected to the main towns and villages in the Faroe Islands via the Vágatunnilin tunnel, which opened in 2002.

world knowledge.Name: Miami International Airport
world knowledge.Address: Miami-Dade County, Florida, U.S., adjacent to the cities of Miami and Miami Springs, and the village of Virginia Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established in 1928 as Pan American Field, it was the first mainland U.S. airport with international port of entry facilities. It expanded post-WWII and was renamed Miami International Airport in 1945. The airport has grown significantly, becoming a major hub for international flights, especially to Latin America and the Caribbean.

Major_Events.Event: Official Dedication of Pan American Field
Major_Events.Description: Pan American Airport, also known as Pan American Field, was officially dedicated with a ceremony attended by thousands, including Amelia Earhart.
The airport was renamed after Dade County Port Authority acquired Pan Am’s N.W. 36th Street airport and expanded it.
A new terminal was inaugurated at 20th Street, marking the beginning of the modern Miami International Airport.
MIA began offering nonstop flights to Europe, expanding its international reach.
American Airlines announced it would establish a hub at MIA, which grew to become its largest air freight hub.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features multiple terminals and concourses, including the North Terminal (exclusive to American Airlines), Central Terminal, and South Terminal. It includes advanced facilities like the MIA Mover people mover system, Skytrain, and gates capable of accommodating Airbus A380 aircraft.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: MIA is a critical gateway between the U.S. and Latin America, the Caribbean, and other international destinations. It plays a vital role in global trade, tourism, and cultural exchange, particularly for the Southeastern United States.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving passenger and cargo flights
world knowledge.Details: MIA is the busiest U.S. gateway for international passengers and the busiest international cargo airport in the U.S. It serves as a major hub for American Airlines and a focus city for other carriers like Avianca and LATAM. The airport has extensive cargo facilities and is a key player in global logistics. Future expansion plans aim to accommodate growing passenger and cargo demand.

world knowledge.Name: Karlsruhe Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Karlsruhe Palace was built in 1715 for Margrave Charles III William of Baden-Durlach after a dispute with the citizens of his previous capital, Durlach. The city of Karlsruhe has since grown around it. The building is now home to the main museum of the Badisches Landesmuseum. Originally partially made of wood, the palace had to be rebuilt in 1746, using stone. It was further altered by Balthasar Neumann and Friedrich von Kesslau until 1770, adding larger windows and doors, pavilions and wings. In 1785, Wilhelm Jeremias Müller shortened the tower, adding a cupola. Much of the city centre, including the palace, was reduced to rubble by Allied bombing during World War II but was quickly rebuilt after the war.

Major_Events.Description: Leopold, Grand Duke of Baden, was expelled for some time.
The last monarch, Frederick II, Grand Duke of Baden, had to move out.
Much of the city centre, including the palace, was reduced to rubble by Allied bombing but was quickly rebuilt after the war.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally partially made of wood, the palace was rebuilt in 1746 using stone. It was altered by Balthasar Neumann and Friedrich von Kesslau until 1770, adding larger windows and doors, pavilions and wings. In 1785, Wilhelm Jeremias Müller shortened the tower, adding a cupola.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The palace is the former residence of the rulers of Baden and is now used as the Badisches Landesmuseum Karlsruhe. It is a significant historical and cultural landmark in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The city was planned with the tower of the palace at the centre and 32 streets radiating out from it like spokes on a wheel, or ribs on a folding fan, so that a nickname for Karlsruhe in German is the 'fan city' (Fächerstadt).

world knowledge.Name: Ukrainska Besida Theatre
world knowledge.Address: The Ukrainian National Home (Narodnyi dim) in Lviv
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ukrainska Besida Theatre was the first Ukrainian professional theatre, operating from 1864 to 1924. It was subsidized by the Ruska Besida Society and occasionally supported by the Galician Diet. The theatre played a significant role in the revival of Ukrainian language and culture, introducing historical, household, and bourgeois dramas, operas, and Western European works. It ceased operations in 1924 due to lack of funds.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre premiered with the play 'Marusia' based on the novel by Hryhorii Kvitka-Osnovianenko in The Ukrainian National Home in Lviv.

Major_Events.Event: Golden Age of the Galician theatre
Major_Events.Description: Under the directorship of Ivan Biberovych and Ivan Mykolaiovych Hrynevetskyi, the theatre introduced Ukrainian historical drama, household drama, bourgeois drama, operas, and Western European dramas and operettas.
The theatre ceased to exist due to lack of funds.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre was a cornerstone in the revival of Ukrainian language and culture, contributing to the rise of modern Ukrainian theatre in Central and Eastern Ukraine. It introduced Ukrainian audiences to a wide range of domestic and international works, fostering national consciousness.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre's repertoire included works by Friedrich Schiller, Eugène Scribe, Heinrich von Kleist, Carlo Goldoni, Jacques Offenbach, Johann Strauss II, Hermann Sudermann, Gotthold Ephraim Lessing, Gerhart Hauptmann, Henrik Ibsen, August Strindberg, Edmond Rostand, Pierre Beaumarchais, Molière, Oscar Wilde, George Bernard Shaw, William Shakespeare, Nikolai Gogol, Leo Tolstoy, Anton Chekhov, Aleksander Fredro, and Stanisław Przybyszewski. It also performed operas by Mykola Lysenko, Mykola Arkas, Fromental Halévy, Giacomo Puccini, Georges Bizet, Giuseppe Verdi, Charles Gounod, Jacques Offenbach, Pietro Mascagni, Bedřich Smetana, and Stanisław Moniuszko.

world knowledge.Name: Hitchin Town Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Hitchin Town Hall was built in 1901 to replace an earlier town hall from 1840. It served as the headquarters of Hitchin Urban District Council until 1974 when the North Hertfordshire District Council was formed. The hall underwent a major renovation in 2012, which included an extension to house the North Hertfordshire Museum, opened in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: Emmeline Pankhurst visited the town hall and made a speech supporting women's suffrage.

Major_Events.Event: Concert by Bob Marley and the Wailers
Major_Events.Description: The Jamaican reggae band Bob Marley and the Wailers performed a concert at the town hall.
The town hall was extended to create the North Hertfordshire Museum, which opened in July 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town hall was designed in the Neo-Georgian style by Edward Mountford and Thomas Lucas. It features a symmetrical main frontage with seven bays, an arched doorway with a large keystone, mullioned windows, full-height pilasters, a modillioned pediment with the town's coat of arms, and a cupola at roof level. The building is constructed of red brick with stone dressings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Hitchin Town Hall is a Grade II listed building, recognized for its architectural and historical importance. It has hosted significant cultural and political events, including speeches by suffragettes and concerts by notable musicians.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as the headquarters of Hitchin Urban District Council. Now functions as a venue for events and houses the North Hertfordshire Museum.
world knowledge.Details: The town hall was officially opened on 18 March 1901 by Mrs Hudson, the wife of the local member of parliament, George Hudson. The building was designated a Grade II listed building on 14 October 2010 with reference number 1394494.

world knowledge.Name: U. J. Esuene Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The U. J. Esuene Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Calabar, Nigeria. It was inaugurated on 2 April, 1977 with a match between Benin's Bendel Insurance F.C. and newly formed Calabar Rovers of Calabar. Two weeks later, the stadium hosted an international encounter between Enugu Rangers and Tonnerre Yaoundé.

Major_Events.Description: Games at the 2003 All-Africa Games were played at the U. J. Esuene Stadium in October 2003.
Nigeria's qualifiers for the 2008 Africa Cup of Nations were played at the stadium.
The stadium was shortlisted as a venue for the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup and hosted eight games, including the South Korea-Nigeria quarterfinal.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium includes an ultra-modern electronic video-matrix scoreboard and impressive floodlights.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Nigeria, hosting important football matches and international events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches and multi-purpose sports events
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 16,000 and is the home stadium of Calabar Rovers and previously Dolphins F.C.

world knowledge.Name: Old Town Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Crosses the Nidelva River from Kjøpmannsgata to Bakklandet, Trondheim, Norway
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed by Johan Caspar von Cicignon in 1681 as part of the reconstruction of Trondheim after the great fire of 1681. King Christian V of Denmark funded the construction. The bridge replaced the original Elgeseter Bridge and has undergone many changes since its completion.

Major_Events.Description: Led to the reconstruction of Trondheim, including the construction of Gamle Bybro.
Engineer Carl Adolf Dahl reconstructed the bridge.
Oskar Hoddø, a Norwegian resistance fighter and composer, was executed by Nazi forces.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally constructed of wood supported on three stone piers, with an iron gate in the middle. The bridge was reconstructed in 1861 and features toll and guardhouses at each end, with the west end access house still standing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gamle Bybro is a characteristic landmark of Trondheim and is also known as 'Lykkens portal' (Gate of Happiness) due to its association with the popular waltz 'Nidelven stille og vakker du er' by Oskar Hoddø. The bridge holds historical significance as part of Trondheim's fortification and reconstruction.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally served as a strategic military bridge and city gate; now functions as a pedestrian bridge and cultural landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is associated with the Norwegian resistance movement during World War II, particularly with Oskar Hoddø, who composed a waltz about the Nidelva River while standing at the bridge. The iron gate remained a guarded city gate until 1816.

world knowledge.Name: Orchard Beach State Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Orchard Beach State Park was developed by the Manistee, Filer City and Eastlake Railway Company and opened in 1892. It was purchased by the Manistee Board of Commerce and deeded to the state to become part of the Michigan state park system in 1921. The Civilian Conservation Corps was active in the park in the 1930s, constructing several limestone structures. In 2009, the park was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places.

Major_Events.Event: Development by Manistee, Filer City and Eastlake Railway Company
Major_Events.Description: The park was developed and opened by the railway company.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to Michigan state park system
Major_Events.Description: The site was purchased by the Manistee Board of Commerce and deeded to the state.
The Corps constructed several limestone structures including a pavilion, toilet, line house, and pump house.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The park was cited as one of the most intact examples of a Michigan state park developed in the 1930s and 1940s under National Park Service guidelines.
The CCC-built pavilion was moved away from the shore due to erosion threats from high Lake Michigan levels.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features several limestone structures built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, including a pavilion, toilet, line house, and pump house. It retains the majority of its CCC-era buildings and physical layout.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is one of the most intact examples of a Michigan state park developed in the 1930s and 1940s under National Park Service guidelines. It retains the majority of its CCC-era buildings and physical layout, earning it a place on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public recreation area offering camping, hiking trails, and scenic views over Lake Michigan.
world knowledge.Details: The park offers three miles of hiking trails, picnicking facilities, and a 166-site campground. The beach has been closed due to high lake levels. The park is administered by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources.

world knowledge.Name: Crawford County Courthouse (Iowa)
world knowledge.Address: Broadway between Ave. B and Ave. C, Denison, Iowa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Crawford County Courthouse is the second building used for court functions and county administration in Crawford County. The first courthouse, a clay structure completed in 1859, served multiple purposes including as a lecture hall, church auditorium, banquet hall, and Sunday school. The current courthouse was completed in 1905 after a bond issue was passed in 1902. The first Crawford County Fair was held on the courthouse property in October 1860.

Major_Events.Description: A clay structure was completed, serving as the first courthouse and also functioning as a lecture hall, church auditorium, banquet hall, and Sunday school.
Held on the courthouse property in October 1860.
The present courthouse was completed for about $115,000, designed by George A. Berlinghof in the Beaux-Arts style.
The dome became too heavy for the structure and was removed around 1945.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 2, 1981.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by George A. Berlinghof in the Beaux-Arts style. The exterior is covered with blocks of Ohio marble, some of which weigh seven tons. Originally had a dome that was removed around 1945.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a historic landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It represents the architectural and administrative history of Crawford County.
world knowledge.Details: The old courthouse was sold in 1903 and moved across the street, where it was used for various commercial enterprises. The current courthouse was built after a $75,000 bond issue was passed in 1902, with an additional $40,000 needed later.

world knowledge.Name: Stephen the Great Central Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stephen the Great Central Park, originally laid out in 1818 by Russian military engineers during the reign of Alexander I, is the oldest park in Moldova. It was developed under the direction of architect Bogdan Eitner, who created the present-day alleys and planted hundreds of acacias, limes, and flower beds. The park has undergone several transformations, including the addition of a cast-iron fence in 1863 and various monuments and facilities over the years.

Major_Events.Description: A statue of Pushkin, designed by Russian sculptor Alexander Opekushin, was erected in the park, making Chișinău the second city after Moscow to have a Pushkin monument.

Major_Events.Event: Construction of Ștefan cel Mare statue
Major_Events.Description: A statue of Ștefan cel Mare was erected at the park's entrance, designed by sculptor Alexandru Plămădeală.
The statue of Ștefan cel Mare was the focal point of meetings and violent clashes between Moldova's Nationalists and pro-Soviet supporters.
Free park Wi-Fi access was launched.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a variety of trees, including mulberries and acacias aged between 130 and 180 years. It includes the Alley of Classics, with statues and busts of Romanian and Moldovan authors and social figures, and the Alley of Friendship, where prominent guests planted trees. The park also contains four fountains, the main one located at the center where all paths and alleys meet.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as the oldest park in Moldova and a popular meeting spot for couples, earning it the nickname "The Park of the Lovers." It houses several historical monuments and has been a site of important historical events, including nationalist and pro-Soviet clashes.
world knowledge.Details: The park contains 50 species of trees, a gymnasium, hothouse, and various recreational facilities. It has been a site for communal graves, theaters, and cinemas over the years. The Avenue of the Classics of Moldovan Literature, opened in 1958, is lined with statues and busts of notable figures.

world knowledge.Name: National Theatre of Uganda
world knowledge.Address: Corner of Said Barre Avenue and De Winton Street, Kampala, Uganda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Uganda National Cultural Centre (UNCC) is a Ugandan statutory body established by the Uganda National Cultural Centre Act, a 1959 Act of Parliament (amended 1965). It was officially inaugurated on 2 December 1959. The Honourable A.G. Mehta, mayor of Kampala in 1968, was a supporter of the National Theatre and opened its first exhibition on the Baháʼí Faith in Uganda.

Major_Events.Description: Officially inaugurated on 2 December 1959.

Major_Events.Event: First exhibition on the Baháʼí Faith
Major_Events.Description: Opened by the Honourable A.G. Mehta, mayor of Kampala in 1968.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UNCC is charged with providing and establishing theatres and cultural centres in the country, encouraging and developing cultural and artistic activities, and providing a home to societies, groups and organisations that deal in art, culture and entertainment.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Cultural and artistic activities, including stage performances, cinema, art exhibitions, and sale of locally made handicrafts.
world knowledge.Details: The centre has two main components: the National Theatre and the Nommo Gallery. The National Theatre provides a venue for stage performances and cinema. The Nommo Gallery features exhibitions of works of art by both Ugandan and foreign artists. The centre also offers a snack bar and the Craft Village, where locally made handicrafts are sold. Oversight of the UNCC is the responsibility of an eight-member Board of Trustees, appointed by the Minister of Gender, Labour and Social Development.

world knowledge.Name: Praia Grande, São Paulo
world knowledge.Location: Southern coast of the Brazilian state of São Paulo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Praia Grande was one of the first areas colonized by the Portuguese, beginning with the arrival of Martim Afonso in 1532. The area was part of St. Vincent village until its emancipation on 19 January 1967. The city experienced accelerated growth post-emancipation, especially after infrastructure improvements in the 1980s and 1990s.

Major_Events.Description: Praia Grande became an independent municipality, separating from São Vicente.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Small Sea Bridge
Major_Events.Description: The bridge linked São Vicente to Praia Grande, improving access and relieving traffic on the Suspension Bridge.
The city underwent significant improvements, including street paving, sewage system expansion, and re-urbanization of tourist spots.
Part of the park is located within Praia Grande's municipality.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Praia Grande is one of 15 cities in São Paulo state designated as spas, which grants it additional state funding for tourism promotion. It is also notable for its extensive surveillance system and infrastructure advancements.

Details.Neighborhoods: Classified into coastal, peripheral, and mountainous regions, each identified by a different color since 1992.
Details.Surveillance: Largest number of surveillance cameras in the Americas, second only to London worldwide.
Details.Telecommunications: Served by Telefónica (Vivo brand), offering cell phones, fixed lines, internet, and television services.

world knowledge.Name: Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport
world knowledge.Address: 5900 Messer Airport Highway, Birmingham, AL 35212, USA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as Birmingham Municipal Airport in 1931, it was renamed Birmingham International Airport in 1993 and later Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport in 2008 to honor civil rights activist Fred Shuttlesworth. The airport has undergone several expansions and renovations, including a major terminal modernization project completed in 2014.

Major_Events.Description: The airport opened with a two-story, white, Georgian style terminal and a single east–west runway.

Major_Events.Event: World War II Lease to US Army Air Forces
Major_Events.Description: The airport was leased to the United States Army Air Forces for $1 a year to support national defense.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Birmingham International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed to reflect its international status.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport
Major_Events.Description: The airport was renamed to honor civil rights activist Fred Shuttlesworth.
A comprehensive terminal modernization project was completed, nearly doubling the airport's footprint.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a mix of architectural styles, including the International style of the 1974 terminal and modern designs from the 2014 renovation. The new terminal and concourses feature open spaces, abundant natural light, and neutral colors accented with soft blue and chrome.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is named after Fred Shuttlesworth, a prominent civil rights activist, reflecting its importance in the civil rights movement. It also serves as a key transportation hub for the Birmingham and Tuscaloosa metropolitan areas.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial, military, and general aviation needs.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has two asphalt runways, a staffed U.S. Customs and Border Protection facility, and serves as a hub for AirMed International. It also houses the Southern Museum of Flight and features various artworks and dining options. The airport is a primary diversion airport for Atlanta Hartsfield–Jackson International Airport due to its long runway.

world knowledge.Name: Imam Khomeini International University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Imam Khomeini International University (IKIU), informally Qazvin International University, is an international university in Iran that was founded after the Islamic Revolution. The bill of IKIU’s constitution was ratified by the Iranian Parliament in 1984. Constituent organs of IKIU include Board of trustees, president, and council. Deputies for Education, Research, and Students and Culture are some of the other departments. The university was established in 1991 to further culture, civilization, and thought of Muslim world.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: IKIU was established to further culture, civilization, and thought of the Muslim world. It serves as an educational, research, and cultural institution under the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology.
world knowledge.Details: IKIU has seven faculties and offers 30 undergraduate courses and 13 master courses with a faculty of 183 staff teachers. The Persian Language Teaching Center has hosted students from more than 96 countries. The main campus is in Qazvin, Iran, with a Science and Technology Park and a residential complex near the main campus.

world knowledge.Name: National Museum of Somaliland
world knowledge.Address: 26 June Street - Ex Khairia Building 26 June District
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museum of Somaliland is a national museum in Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland. It was inaugurated by president Muse Bihi Abdi on 29 July 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was inaugurated by president Muse Bihi Abdi.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum serves as a national repository for the cultural and historical heritage of Somaliland.
world knowledge.Details: The National Museum of Somaliland is located in Hargeisa and is managed by the Government of Somaliland. It was designed by architect Rashid Ali of Rio Architects Somaliland.

world knowledge.Name: Emory University
world knowledge.Address: 201 Dowman Dr, Atlanta, GA 30322, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Emory University was founded in 1836 as Emory College by the Methodist Episcopal Church and named in honor of Methodist bishop John Emory. It relocated to its current Atlanta campus in 1915 after accepting a land grant from Asa Griggs Candler, founder of The Coca-Cola Company. The university has grown into a major private research institution with significant contributions to education, healthcare, and public health.

Major_Events.Description: Emory College was closed in November 1861, and its students enlisted on the Confederate side. The campus was used as a hospital and later as a headquarters for the Union Army. Thirty-five Emory students lost their lives, and much of the campus was destroyed.
Emory College relocated to Druid Hills and was rechartered as Emory University after accepting a land grant from Asa Griggs Candler.
Emory University organized medical units and contributed to the war efforts, including the Emory Unit, Base Hospital 43, which served in France during WWI and in North Africa and Europe during WWII.

Emory University became racially integrated after the Supreme Court of Georgia ruled in favor of the university's challenge to Georgia laws denying tax-exempt status to racially integrated private universities.
Emory's campus was annexed into the City of Atlanta, marking the city's largest annexation in 65 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Atlanta Campus was designed with a Beaux-Arts master plan by architect Henry Hornbostel. Many buildings feature multi-hued granite and Spanish Saltillo tile. The campus includes Neoclassical and Gothic Revival architecture, particularly in the original Oxford campus.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Emory University is a leading private research institution with significant contributions to education, healthcare, and public health. It is known for its partnerships with the CDC, global health initiatives, and its role in treating Ebola patients during the 2014 outbreak. The university has a rich history of promoting racial equality and global human rights.
world knowledge.Details: Emory University comprises nine undergraduate, graduate, and professional schools, including Emory College of Arts and Sciences, Goizueta Business School, and Rollins School of Public Health. It operates Emory Healthcare, the largest healthcare system in Georgia, and has a significant research focus, particularly in public health, medicine, and global health. The university has a strong endowment and is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity." Notable alumni include Vice President Alben Barkley, golfer Bobby Jones, and Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich.

world knowledge.Name: Bolata
world knowledge.Location: Near the village of Bulgarevo and the town of Kavarna
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bolata is a small cove and nature reserve with remnants of an ancient settlement dating back to the 4th century B.C. It also contains evidence of trade relations between the Second Bulgarian Empire and the Republic of Venice and Genoa, such as a Maltese cross. During the communist regime, a top-secret base was built here, including a telephone cable connecting Bulgarian and Soviet leaders.

Major_Events.Description: Remnants of an ancient settlement were found in the caves of Bolata.
A Maltese cross was found, testifying to trade relations with Venice and Genoa.
A top-secret base was built, including a telephone cable connecting Bulgarian and Soviet leaders.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cove features a semi-circular sandy beach surrounded by brick-colored high cliffs and a rocky canyon. The area includes limestone rocks with red coloration due to iron oxides in the clay. There are also remnants of a communist-era base, including semi-abandoned buildings and a watch-tower.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bolata is a nature reserve of great ecological importance, part of the Natura 2000 Kaliakra Complex. It is a key habitat for rare plant and animal species and lies on the Via Pontica migratory bird route. The area also holds historical significance due to its ancient settlement and trade artifacts.
world knowledge.Details: Bolata is the only reserve in Bulgaria that includes a sea area. It is home to species like the short-beaked common dolphin, various amphibians, reptiles, and migratory birds. The beach is popular among locals and tourists despite environmental concerns due to human activity. The area also features stone circles, sacrificial stones, and rock caves from ancient times.

world knowledge.Name: Katerini Stadium
world knowledge.Address: District of National Stadium, Katerini, Greece
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named National Stadium of Katerini, it was later renamed to 1st Municipal Athletic Center of Katerini after being transferred to the Municipality of Katerini. It underwent modernization projects from 2007 to 2009 and major reconstructions in 2015 for the UEFA European Under-19 Championship.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted the final match between Spain and Russia.
Record attendance of 12,000 during Pierikos F.C. vs Aris F.C. on 8/2/1970.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with two stands (no stands behind the goalposts), a covered central part of the west stand, light projectors for night matches, and a tartan perimeter with 8 tracks and spaces for classic sports.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a key sports venue in Katerini, hosting local football teams and significant events like the UEFA European Under-19 Championship. It serves as a central athletic hub for the region.
world knowledge.Details: Home stadium of Pierikos F.C., occasionally used by other local teams like Vataniakos F.C. and Ethnikos Katerini F.C. due to lack of other qualifying stadiums in Katerini. Capacity is 4,995 spectators after renovations reduced it by 700 seats. Owned by the Municipality of Katerini and operated by Pierikos FC.

image_name: Estadio Verónica Boquete de San Lázaro

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Verónica Boquete de San Lázaro
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Estadio Multiusos de San Lázaro, the stadium was inaugurated on 24 June 1993. It was renamed on 8 November 2018 to honor Verónica Boquete, a renowned Spanish footballer.

Major_Events.Description: A four-way tournament featuring Deportivo de La Coruña, CD Tenerife, CA River Plate, and São Paulo FC. The first match was between Deportivo and River Plate, with Bebeto scoring the first goal.
The stadium was renamed to honor Verónica Boquete, one of the greatest Spanish footballers of all time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Oval-shaped stadium with a terracotta-coloured roof that rises on the west side to incorporate director's seating and press facilities on a second tier. The pitch is surrounded by a 400 m athletics track, and the majority of the 16,666 seats are on a single, covered tier.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant as the home ground of SD Compostela and for honoring Verónica Boquete, a key figure in Spanish football history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multipurpose stadium, primarily used for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 16,666 and was constructed at a cost of 3,000,000,000 Ptas in 1993. It is owned and operated by Concello de Santiago and was designed by architect Andrés Fernández-Albalat Lois.

world knowledge.Name: Royal University of Phnom Penh
world knowledge.Address: Russian Federation Blvd, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1960 as the Royal Khmer University, it underwent several name changes and expansions, reflecting Cambodia's turbulent history. It was closed during the Khmer Rouge regime and reopened in the 1980s. The university has grown significantly and now includes multiple faculties and institutes.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as the Royal Khmer University during a period of intense growth in Cambodia.
The university was closed and many of its staff and students were killed during the Khmer Rouge regime.
Reopened under the People's Republic of Kampuchea, initially teaching in French.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Royal University of Phnom Penh
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed to its current name.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Influenced by New Khmer Architecture, which blends Bauhaus, European post-modern architecture, and Angkor traditions. Features ponds and bridges inspired by Angkor Wat.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As Cambodia's largest and oldest university, it plays a crucial role in the country's education system and has been a center for academic and cultural development.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: National research university offering undergraduate and postgraduate programs in various fields.
world knowledge.Details: The university has over 420 full-time staff and offers degrees in sciences, humanities, social sciences, environment, engineering, and vocational courses. It is a member of the ASEAN University Network and maintains international linkages.

world knowledge.Name: National Mall
world knowledge.Address: Between Independence and Constitution Avenues from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Approximately 1 mile in length and 400 feet wide
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1791 (initial design), various constructions through the 20th century
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Designed by Pierre L'Enfant in 1791 as a 'grand avenue' for public use, the National Mall has evolved into a democratic and egalitarian space, unlike the palace gardens of Europe. It has been the site of numerous historical events, protests, and cultural gatherings.

Major_Events.Event: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
Major_Events.Description: A pivotal civil rights rally where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech.
The largest officially recorded rally on the Mall, protesting the Vietnam War.
An estimated 2 million people attended, marking a historic moment as the first African American president was sworn in.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Mall features a long, open expanse of grass lined with American elm trees, flanked by museums and memorials in the Beaux-Arts style. Key structures include the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, and numerous Smithsonian museums.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Mall symbolizes democratic ideals and serves as a focal point for national celebrations, protests, and public gatherings. It is a testament to the nation's history and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park, cultural and historical site, venue for national events and protests
world knowledge.Details: The National Mall is administered by the National Park Service and receives approximately 24 million visitors annually. It includes landmarks such as the Smithsonian museums, the Washington Monument, and the Lincoln Memorial. The Mall is also a popular site for recreational activities and annual events like the Smithsonian Folklife Festival and Independence Day celebrations.

world knowledge.Name: Edgbaston Cricket Ground
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Edgbaston Cricket Ground, located in the Edgbaston area of Birmingham, England, was established in 1882. It is home to Warwickshire County Cricket Club and its T20 team Birmingham Bears. The ground has hosted numerous Test matches, One-Day Internationals, and Twenty20 Internationals. It was the first English ground outside Lord's to host a major international one-day tournament final and has been a venue for major tournaments like the ICC Cricket World Cup 2019 and the ICC Champions Trophy 2017. The land was originally owned by the Calthorpe Estate, who developed it into an exclusive Birmingham suburb. The club initially considered other locations but chose Edgbaston due to its proximity to Birmingham's large population and railway connections.

Major_Events.Description: The first Test match at Edgbaston was part of The Ashes series against Australia.
The first One-Day International at Edgbaston was between England and Australia.
The first Twenty20 International at Edgbaston was between Australia and Pakistan.
The first women's Test at Edgbaston was between England and Australia.
The first women's Twenty20 International at Edgbaston was between England and South Africa.
Edgbaston hosted the ICC Champions Trophy final, the first English ground outside Lord's to do so.
Edgbaston hosted matches in the ICC Cricket World Cup 2019, where England won its first World Cup.

Major_Events.Event: First day/night Test match in England
Major_Events.Description: Edgbaston hosted the first day/night Test match in England, between England and the West Indies.
Edgbaston hosted the first women's T20 event at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, where Australia won the gold medal match.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Edgbaston Cricket Ground has undergone several developments over the years, including the construction of the Rea Bank and the Thwaite Memorial Scoreboard in 1950, an Indoor Cricket School in 1956, and the Pavilion Suite in the same year. The William Ansell Stand opened in 1967, and executive boxes were added in 1989. The ground was redeveloped between 2010 and 2011, with the construction of the new South and West Stands, increasing the capacity to 25,000. The redevelopment included the demolition of the old pavilion and stands, and the erection of permanent floodlight pylons.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Edgbaston is considered one of England's leading cricket grounds, often compared to Lord's. It has a reputation for having one of the most hostile atmospheres for visiting teams, inspiring home players. The ground has hosted numerous significant cricket events and has been a venue for major international tournaments. Its development and facilities have been praised, with the England and Wales Cricket Board noting that the facilities are cutting edge.
world knowledge.Details: Edgbaston has a capacity of 25,000 spectators, making it the fourth-largest cricketing venue in England. It has hosted the T20 Finals Day more than any other cricket ground. The ground is also the main home ground for the Birmingham Phoenix in The Hundred competition. The record attendance for a County Championship match is 28,000, and for a single day of a test match is 32,000. Edgbaston had a distinctive motorized rain cover system known as the Brumbrella until 2000.

world knowledge.Name: Cheyne Beach Whaling Station
world knowledge.Address: Frenchman Bay, King George Sound, Albany, Western Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cheyne Beach Whaling Station is a defunct whaling station that operated from the 1950s until 1978. It was built to process whales caught in the area and was later converted into a museum. The station was established by the Cheynes Beach Whaling Company, which hunted humpback and sperm whales. It ceased operations in 1978 when the last whale was legally caught in Australian waters. The site was later donated to the Jaycees Community Foundation and converted into a museum named Whaleworld, which opened in 1985. It is now known as Albany's Historic Whaling Station.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Cheynes Beach Whaling Company
Major_Events.Description: The Cheynes Beach Whaling Company was formed by a syndicate of fishermen and began operations at Frenchman Bay.
After a disastrous season with low humpback catches, the station began hunting sperm whales due to changes in International Whaling Commission regulations.
The company recorded a net profit of A$304,329 due to a record catch of 764 sperm whales and high global demand for whale oil.
The station ceased operations after the last whale was legally caught in Australian waters.
The site was converted into a museum named Whaleworld, which officially opened in May 1985.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The station consists of large steel and concrete sheds, workshops, timber-framed offices, amenities buildings, tanks, and boilers. Much of the equipment was repurposed from old mining machinery and an alcohol distillation plant. The flensing deck was built over a natural rock slipway with steam winches for hauling whale carcasses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cheyne Beach Whaling Station is a significant historical site representing Australia's whaling industry. It highlights the economic and environmental history of whaling and its eventual cessation due to conservation efforts. The museum preserves this history and educates the public about marine conservation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a whaling station, now operates as a museum and tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Details: The site includes the Australian Wildlife Park Albany, a 1.3-hectare wildlife park featuring native Australian animals such as koalas, kangaroos, wombats, and various bird species. The museum is also known by previous names such as Whaleworld or Whale World. A total of 1,136 humpback whales and 14,695 sperm whales were caught at the station between 1952 and 1978.

world knowledge.Name: Ajou University
world knowledge.Address: South Korea, Gyeonggi-do, Suwon, Yeongtong-gu, World cup-ro, 206 KR , Suwon , Gyeonggi-do , South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ajou University, founded in 1973 as Ajou Engineering College, was established to facilitate technology and cultural exchange between France and South Korea. It has grown into a comprehensive private research university with a significant impact on higher education in South Korea and internationally.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Ajou University in Tashkent
Major_Events.Description: Ajou University established an international branch in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, in collaboration with the Uzbekistan government, aiming to extend its educational influence into Central Asia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features a modern urban campus with facilities like the Central Library, multiple dormitories, and various academic buildings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ajou University plays a pivotal role in South Korea's educational landscape, particularly in engineering and business, and has extended its influence internationally through its branch in Uzbekistan.
world knowledge.Details: Ajou University includes a variety of facilities such as a research hospital, bio-technology valley, and multiple restaurants and dormitories. It also has a strong focus on international collaboration and research, particularly in the fields of medicine and technology.

world knowledge.Name: Jekyll Island
world knowledge.Address: Jekyll Island, Glynn County, Georgia, U.S.
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 5,700 acres (23 km²), including 4,400 acres (18 km²) of solid earth and a 240-acre (0.97 km²) Jekyll Island Club Historic District
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jekyll Island has a rich history, from indigenous use by the Guale and Mocama peoples, through British colonial plantations, to its development as a winter retreat for the wealthy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It was acquired by the State of Georgia in 1947 for preservation and public use.

Major_Events.Description: The Jekyll Island Club was established as a winter retreat for the wealthy, with a clubhouse completed in 1888.
The Wanderer illegally brought 465 enslaved Africans to Jekyll Island, marking one of the last successful slave shipments to the U.S.
A secret meeting of financiers at the Jekyll Island Club led to the creation of the Federal Reserve System.
The State of Georgia acquired Jekyll Island for $675,000, ensuring its preservation and public access.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island features a mix of historic structures, including the tabby-built Horton House (1742), the Jekyll Island Club Hotel, and numerous elaborate 'cottages' from the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The architectural style reflects the Gilded Age and colonial periods.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jekyll Island is culturally significant for its role in American history, including indigenous heritage, colonial plantations, the illegal slave trade, and its use as a retreat for America's elite. It is also notable for its contribution to the creation of the Federal Reserve System.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourist destination, historic site, and nature preserve
world knowledge.Details: Jekyll Island is a popular tourist destination with beaches, historic tours, bike trails, and wildlife. It has been featured in films like 'Glory' and 'The Walking Dead.' The island is managed by the Jekyll Island Authority and includes the Georgia Sea Turtle Center, which rehabilitates endangered sea turtles. A daily toll is required for entry, with annual passes available.

world knowledge.Name: Vaile Mansion
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Harvey M. Vaile Mansion was built in 1881 for businessman Harvey M. Vaile, a prominent figure in Independence business and social circles. Vaile was a strong supporter of the abolitionism movement and among the founders of the Republican Party in Jackson County. The mansion became the showplace of Jackson County, hosting notables of the 1880s and 1890s. After Vaile's death in 1894, the house changed hands multiple times, serving as a sanatorium, nursing home, and water bottling company before being acquired by the City of Independence in 1983 and restored as a historic house museum.

Major_Events.Description: The mansion was completed at a cost of $150,000 (equivalent to about $4.7 million in 2025).
Vaile was charged with defrauding the government but was found not guilty in two trials, though he spent over $100,000 in trial expenses.
Vaile's wife, Sophia, was found dead at home from a morphine overdose, suspected to be a suicide.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The mansion was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The mansion was acquired by the City of Independence through a donation by Mrs. DeWitt and underwent a long-term restoration project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The mansion is a locally significant example of Second Empire architecture, designed by architect Asa Beebe Cross. It features a symmetrical structure with a two-and-a-half-story block surmounted by a three-story central tower. Constructed of hand-pressed red brick, it includes an elaborate one-story porch, limestone moldings, heavy bracketed cornices, dormered mansard roofs, and multicolor slate shingles. The interiors boast original paintwork, nine marble fireplaces, and two of the three original chandeliers intended for the White House. State-of-the-art amenities original to the house include speaking tubes, gasoliers, indoor running hot and cold water, and flush toilets.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Vaile Mansion is culturally and historically significant as a prime example of Second Empire architecture and as a symbol of the wealth and social status of Harvey M. Vaile. It reflects the High Victorian taste for elaborate ornamentation and was the first house in Jackson County with indoor plumbing. The mansion's history is intertwined with the social and political life of the late 19th century, hosting many U.S. Senators and congressional representatives.
world knowledge.Details: The mansion features thirty-one rooms with fourteen-feet-high ceilings decorated by French, German, and Italian artists. It was originally surrounded by a 630-acre estate, which included a grape vineyard, an apple orchard, a wine processing plant, and a wine cellar capable of holding 48,000 gallons. The mansion is now operated by the Vaile Victorian Society, a non-profit organization established in 1983.

world knowledge.Name: Walterdale Playhouse
