world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Walterdale Playhouse was founded in 1959 by the Walterdale Theatre Associates and is one of Western Canada's oldest amateur theatre groups. Since 1974, it has been located in the oldest fire hall in Alberta, Strathcona Firehall No. 1 (later Edmonton No. 6), which was converted into the Walterdale Playhouse. The firehall, built in 1909, is now designated a Provincial Registered Historical Resource. The theatre celebrated 50 years of operation in 2008 and is mainly run by donations and volunteers.

Major_Events.Description: The venue celebrated 50 years of theatre.

Major_Events.Event: Award for Outstanding Contribution to Performing Arts
Major_Events.Description: The theatre received an award for its contributions to the performing arts.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The two-story brick firehall was designed by Wilson and Herrald and built by J. M. Eaton. Originally, it had space for nine horses and three fire wagons, with the upper and ground floors connected by two fire poles. The chief's office, general hall, bedrooms, band room, and bathroom were upstairs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Walterdale Playhouse is a meaningful part of the arts and theatre culture in Edmonton. It is one of Western Canada's oldest amateur theatre groups and operates in a historically significant building designated as a Provincial Registered Historical Resource.
world knowledge.Details: The venue seats 145 people. The firehall remained in service until 1954 and served as a storage facility from 1954 to 1974 before being converted into the Walterdale Playhouse.

world knowledge.Name: Beijing Capital International Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Beijing Capital International Airport was opened on 1 March 1958 with a small terminal and a single runway. It has undergone multiple expansions, including the addition of Terminal 2 in 1999 and Terminal 3 in 2008, coinciding with the 2008 Beijing Summer Olympics. The airport has grown to become one of the busiest in Asia.

Major_Events.Description: Terminal 1 opened to replace the original small terminal from 1958, featuring docks for 10-12 aircraft.
Terminal 2 opened to handle increased traffic while Terminal 1 underwent renovation.
Terminal 3, the largest airport terminal-building complex in the world at the time, opened for the 2008 Beijing Summer Olympics.
A man in a wheelchair detonated small homemade explosives in Terminal 3, injuring himself but no others.
An Air China Airbus A330 caught fire during boarding, leading to the evacuation of all passengers and crew.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Terminal 3, designed by a consortium including Foster and Partners, features a red roof (symbolizing good luck in Chinese culture), white ceiling strips for directional guidance, and traditional Chinese decorative elements. It includes a 98.3 m monitoring tower, a 300,000 m² transportation hub, and advanced luggage-transfer systems.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As the busiest airport in Asia at one point, it symbolizes China's rapid economic growth and modernization. Its design incorporates traditional Chinese elements, blending cultural heritage with modern technology.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International and domestic air travel hub

Details.Owner/Operator: Beijing Capital International Airport Company Limited

world knowledge.Name: History of Science Museum, Oxford
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The History of Science Museum in Broad Street, Oxford, England, holds a leading collection of scientific instruments from Middle Ages to the 19th century. The museum building is also known as the Old Ashmolean Building to distinguish it from the newer Ashmolean Museum building completed in 1894. The museum was built in 1683, and it is the world's oldest surviving purpose-built museum. Built in 1683 to house Elias Ashmole's collection, the building was the world's first purpose-built museum building and was also open to the public. The original concept of the museum was to institutionalize the new learning about nature that appeared in the 17th century and experiments concerning natural philosophy were undertaken in a chemical laboratory in the basement, while lectures and demonstration took place in the School of Natural History, on the middle floor. Ashmole's collection was expanded to include a broad range of activities associated with the history of natural knowledge. In 1924, Lewis Evans donated his collection of historic scientific instruments, creating the Lewis Evans Collection. In 1935, with more donations, the museum's name was changed to the Museum of the History of Science. In 2018, the museum was renamed the History of Science Museum.

Major_Events.Description: Lewis Evans donated his collection of historic scientific instruments, creating the Lewis Evans Collection.

Major_Events.Event: Name Change to Museum of the History of Science
Major_Events.Description: With more donations, the museum's name was changed to the Museum of the History of Science.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to History of Science Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum was renamed the History of Science Museum.
From October 2009 until February 2010, the Museum hosted the first major exhibition of Steampunk art objects, curated by Art Donovan and presented by Dr Jim Bennett, then the museum director.

The museum joined six similar museums in Germany, Italy, Greece and Switzerland, creating the international Multaka network. This intercultural museum project organizes guided tours for refugees and migrants designed and offered for free by specially trained Arabic-speaking Multaka guides.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building is known as the Old Ashmolean Building, which is the world's oldest surviving purpose-built museum building. It was built in 1683 to house Elias Ashmole's collection and was the world's first purpose-built museum building.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum holds a leading collection of scientific instruments from the Middle Ages to the 19th century and is the world's oldest surviving purpose-built museum. It occupies a special position in the study of the history of science and in the development of western culture and collecting.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection contains around 18,000 objects from antiquity to the early 20th century, representing almost all aspects of the history of science. One of the most iconic objects in the collection is Einstein's Blackboard that Albert Einstein used on 16 May 1931 in his lectures while visiting the University of Oxford. The museum also contains a wide range of scientific instruments, such as quadrants, astrolabes, sundials, early mathematical instruments, optical instruments, equipment associated with chemistry, natural philosophy and medicine, and a reference library regarding the history of scientific instruments. The museum is also home to the Rochester Avionic Archive, which includes a collection of avionics that originated with the Elliot Brothers, but also includes pieces from Marconi and BAE Systems.

world knowledge.Name: Jefman Airport
world knowledge.Area: North Salawati, Raja Ampat, Southwest Papua, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jefman Airport (IATA: SOQ, ICAO: WASS) was an airport in North Salawati, Raja Ampat Regency, Southwest Papua, Indonesia. It closed when the new Domine Eduard Osok Airport became operational.

Major_Events.Description: Jefman Airport was opened on 16 March 1947.
Jefman Airport was closed on 20 March 2004 when the new Domine Eduard Osok Airport became operational.

world knowledge.Details: Jefman Airport was operated by the Ministry of Transportation and served the city of Sorong. It had an elevation of 10 ft / 3 m and a runway with a direction of 04/22, length of 1,650 m / 5,413 ft, and an asphalt surface (now closed).

world knowledge.Name: Egao Kenko Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in March 1998 as Kumamoto Athletics Stadium, it was later renamed Umakana-Yokana Stadium (2013–2017) and then Egao Kenko Stadium in 2017 due to a naming rights contract. It has been a key venue for football and rugby events, including hosting matches during the 2019 Rugby World Cup.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted matches for the 2019 Rugby World Cup, the first Rugby World Cup held in Asia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass surface and a Diamond Vision scoreboard.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is culturally significant as a major sports venue in Kumamoto, hosting football and rugby matches, including international events like the Rugby World Cup. It is also the home stadium for J2 League club Roasso Kumamoto.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports venue for association football and rugby matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 30,228 people and is owned by the Kumamoto Sports Promotion Agency. It is accessible via JR Kyushu's Hohi Main Line at Hikarinomori station.

world knowledge.Name: Copenhagen Opera House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Copenhagen Opera House is the national opera house of Denmark, donated to the Danish state by the A.P. Møller og Hustru Chastine Mc-Kinney Møllers Fond til almene Formaal in August 2000. It is one of the most modern and expensive opera houses ever built, costing 2.5 billion DKK. Designed by architect Henning Larsen, it was inaugurated on 15 January 2005.

Major_Events.Description: The opera house was inaugurated on 15 January 2005 in the presence of Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller, Danish Prime Minister Anders Fogh Rasmussen, and Queen Margrethe II.
Plácido Domingo performed as Sigmund in Wagner's Die Walküre on 7 April 2006, attended by Queen Margrethe II.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The opera house is designed in the Neo-futurism style by architect Henning Larsen. It features a large glass front, Jura Gelb limestone exterior, and a gilded auditorium ceiling with 105,000 sheets of gold leaf. The building includes six main stages, a large orchestral rehearsal room, and advanced acoustic design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Copenhagen Opera House is a symbol of modern Danish architecture and cultural heritage. It serves as the national opera house and is a major venue for opera, ballet, and other performances, contributing significantly to the cultural life of Denmark.
world knowledge.Details: The opera house is located on the island of Holmen in central Copenhagen, opposite the main palace Amalienborg. It has a seating capacity of 1,700 and is administered by the Royal Danish Theatre. The building includes a small experimental theatre called Takkelloftet and features advanced stage technology, including stage elevators and movable ballet floors. The foyer includes Sicilian Perlatino marble and spherical chandeliers by Olafur Eliasson. The building's design and construction were marked by significant collaboration and conflict between architect Henning Larsen and Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller.

world knowledge.Name: Olympiastadion Berlin
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally designed by Werner March for the 1936 Summer Olympics, the Olympiastadion was part of a larger sports complex called the Reichssportfeld. It was built under the orders of Adolf Hitler and has since been a significant venue for various international sports events, including the FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was the main venue for the 1936 Summer Olympics, where notable events included Jesse Owens winning four gold medals.
Hosted three matches during the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
Hosted six matches, including the final, during the 2006 FIFA World Cup.
FC Barcelona won their fifth title and completed a second treble.
Hosted six matches, including the final, during UEFA Euro 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Werner March with assistance from Albert Speer, the stadium features a symmetrical layout with a recessed lower half 12 meters below ground level. It includes a VIP stand, Marathon Gate, and a capacity of 110,000 spectators during its initial construction. The recent renovations included lowering the playing field, extending the roof, and modernizing facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Olympiastadion is a symbol of both the 1936 Olympics and modern international sports. It represents a blend of historical architecture and contemporary sports facilities, hosting significant events that have shaped global sports history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has undergone several renovations, most notably between 2000 and 2004 for the 2006 FIFA World Cup. It is the home venue for Hertha BSC and has hosted numerous international football matches, athletics events, and cultural festivals. The stadium is equipped with modern technology, including artificial illumination and sound systems, and has a permanent capacity of 74,475 seats.

world knowledge.Name: Teatre Lliure
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Teatre Lliure was created in 1976 in the Gràcia neighborhood by professionals from Barcelona's independent theater scene. It is known for presenting theatre in Catalan, revisiting classics, and contemporary theatre. In 2001, it moved to its current location in the old Palace of Agriculture on Montjuïc.

Major_Events.Description: The first play staged at its original location (La Lleialtat factory in Gràcia) was Camí de nit, by Lluís Pasqual.

Major_Events.Event: Founding member of Union of the Theatres of Europe
Major_Events.Description: The theatre became one of the founding members of the Union of the Theatres of Europe.
The theatre opened at its new location in the old Palace of Agriculture on Montjuïc, featuring advanced technology for staging.
Julio Manrique was appointed as the new director of the Teatre Lliure.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre is housed in the old Palace of Agriculture, featuring several halls with advanced technology that allows quick reconfiguration of staging elements.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Teatre Lliure is considered one of the most prestigious theatres in Catalonia, known for its contributions to Catalan-language theatre, revisiting classics, and contemporary performances. It has also exported productions to other cities in Europe and America.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theatre productions, music, and dance performances.
world knowledge.Details: The Teatre Lliure operates as a cooperative society, producing its own shows. It has been directed by notable figures such as Fabià Puigserver, Lluís Pasqual, and Lluís Homar, among others.

world knowledge.Name: Mid-Hudson Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Between Poughkeepsie and Highland, New York
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 3,000 feet (910 m) long with a clearance of 135 feet (41 m) above the Hudson
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Proposals for the Mid-Hudson span were made by state legislature in 1923. Construction began in 1925 and was completed in 1930. The bridge was renamed the 'Franklin Delano Roosevelt Mid-Hudson Bridge' in 1994.

Major_Events.Description: Then-Governor Franklin D. Roosevelt and his wife Eleanor attended the opening ceremony on August 25, 1930.
The toll plaza was moved to the western side in Ulster County when a new highway approach was opened on December 20, 1967.
In August 1970, the toll was abolished for westbound drivers, and eastbound drivers saw their tolls doubled.
The Mid-Hudson Bridge was designated as a New York State Historic Civil Engineering Landmark by the American Society of Civil Engineers in 1983.
Composer Joseph Bertolozzi completed Bridge Music, a project which allows listeners to hear the Mid-Hudson bridge played like a musical instrument.
At midnight on March 1, 2022, the bridge was converted to all-electronic tolling in the eastbound direction.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with 315-foot-tall (96 m) Gothic steel towers. The span contains stiffening trusses intentionally constructed on top of the deck instead of below the deck. Designed by Polish immigrant Ralph Modjeski.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a historic civil engineering landmark and a key transportation link across the Hudson River. It also has cultural significance due to the Bridge Music project, which uses the bridge as a musical instrument.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Carries US 44 and NY 55 across the Hudson River, connecting Poughkeepsie and Highland.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge carries three lanes of US 44 and NY 55 and a pedestrian/bicycle walkway over the Hudson. It has a computer-controlled LED decorative lighting system for holidays. Tolls are collected eastbound only, with current rates at $2.15 cash and $1.65 E-ZPass.

world knowledge.Name: The Fairfax Theatre
world knowledge.Address: Northwest corner of Fairfax Ave and Beverly Blvd, Los Angeles, CA
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fairfax Theatre is a mixed-use Art Deco style building constructed in 1930. It was the first movie theatre and one of the first commercial and professional buildings in the Beverly-Fairfax neighborhood. It played an important role in fundraising for Jewish cultural institutions migrating from Boyle Heights to the Beverly Fairfax neighborhood.

Major_Events.Description: The Fairfax Theatre debuted on March 26, 1930, with the premiere of 'Troopers Three', a Tiffany Productions movie starring Rex Lease.

Fundraisers were held for synagogues including Etz Jacob and Fairfax Temple in 1933, and the Western Jewish Institute in 1934. The first benefits for the Beverly-Fairfax Jewish Community Center (JCC) were held in 1935.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: On July 30, 2021, the State Historic Resources Commission voted unanimously to add the theatre to the National Register of Historic Places.
The LA City Council voted unanimously to add the Fairfax Theatre to the list of LA Historic-Cultural Monuments on December 7, 2021.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Art Deco style building with a repeating angled motif creating a zig-zag aesthetic. Features include a marquee with neon lights and Plexiglas lettering, a red-tiled lobby with terrazzo floor, original proscenium arch, decorative organ screens, and Art Deco metal light fixtures.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Fairfax Theatre is significant for its importance to the Jewish heritage of the Fairfax district and its Art Deco architecture. It was a hub for fundraising for Jewish synagogues, temples, clubs, and charities, and housed the first Jewish delicatessen, bakery, and kosher meat market on Fairfax.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Mixed-use building consisting of a cinema triplex, retail shops, and second-floor offices.
world knowledge.Details: The building was developed by Nelson C. Stein and designed by W.C. Pennel. It was added to the list of Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monuments in 2021 and declared eligible for the National Register of Historic Places. Preservation efforts have been supported by various organizations including the Art Deco Society of LA, LA Conservancy, and Hollywood Heritage.

world knowledge.Name: St. Boniface Cathedral
world knowledge.Address: 190 avenue de la Cathédrale, St. Boniface, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Boniface Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral in St. Boniface, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. It is the principal church in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Saint Boniface, serving the eastern part of Manitoba province as well as the local Franco-Manitoban community. The original church was built in 1818, with subsequent structures in 1832, 1862, and 1906. The 1906 cathedral was damaged by a fire in 1968, and a new, smaller cathedral was built behind the 1906 façade in 1972.

Major_Events.Description: Rev. Norbert Provencher and two colleagues constructed the first church on land donated by Thomas Douglas, 5th Earl of Selkirk.
Bishop Provencher built the first cathedral.
A fire destroyed Provencher’s cathedral.
Monsignor Louis-Philippe Adélard Langevin dedicated the cathedral, which became one of the most imposing churches in Western Canada.
A fire destroyed many of the structure's features and contents, including the rose window, vestments, 1860 bells, and parish records.
A new, smaller cathedral was built behind the 1906 façade.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 1906 cathedral was designed by Montreal architect Jean-Omer Marchand. The current cathedral, built in 1972, was designed by Étienne Gaboury and Denis Lussier, and features the preserved façade of the 1906 structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Boniface Cathedral is an important building in Winnipeg and serves as the principal church for the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Saint Boniface. It is significant to the local Franco-Manitoban community and has historical ties to the early settlement of the region.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral cemetery includes the remains of notable figures such as Chief One Arrow, whose body was exhumed and sent to One Arrow First Nation in Saskatchewan in 2007. The Institute for stained glass in Canada has documented the stained glass at St. Boniface Cathedral.

world knowledge.Name: University of Wasit
world knowledge.Historical_Background: University of Wasit (Arabic: جامعة واسط) is one of the Iraqi Universities established in 2003 in Al Kut, Wasit, Iraq. Wasit University was established in January 2003. The university included three colleges belonging to Al Qadisiyah University before establishment. In 2005 the university expanded to include four new colleges, new departments, and new colleges.

Major_Events.Description: University of Wasit was established in January 2003.
The university expanded to include four new colleges, new departments, and new colleges.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: University of Wasit is one of the Iraqi Universities, contributing to higher education in the region.
world knowledge.Details: The university included three colleges belonging to Al Qadisiyah University before establishment. The campus is urban, and the official website is Wasit.edu.

world knowledge.Name: Badrinath Temple
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Badrinath Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, established as a pilgrimage site by Adi Shankara in the ninth century. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams and part of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. The temple has undergone several renovations due to its age and damage by natural disasters.

Major_Events.Description: The temple was significantly damaged and largely rebuilt by the King of Jaipur.
The festival held every twelve years raises the number of visitors to 50,000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The temple has three structures: the Garbhagriha (sanctum), the Darshan Mandapa (worship hall), and Sabha Mandapa (convention hall). The conical-shaped roof of the sanctum is approximately 15 m tall with a gold gilt cupola. The facade is built of stone with arched windows, and the walls and pillars are covered with intricate carvings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Badrinath Temple is one of the holiest Hindu Char Dham sites and is revered in ancient texts like Vishnu Purana and Skanda Purana. It is a major pilgrimage center, attracting millions of devotees annually.
world knowledge.Details: The temple is open for six months every year due to extreme weather conditions. It houses a 1 ft black granite deity of Vishnu in the form of Badrinarayan. The Tapt Kund, hot sulphur springs below the temple, are considered medicinal. The temple is administered by the Shri Badarinath Kedarnath Temple Committee.

world knowledge.Name: Rona Lighthouse
world knowledge.Address: South Rona, Highland, Portree, United Kingdom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rona Lighthouse is a lighthouse in South Rona, Scotland. It was built to the design and engineering of Thomas Stevenson and David Stevenson and was first lighted on 10 November 1857. The lighthouse was manned with keepers' cottages onsite until it was converted to automatic operation in 1975. During the 20th century, supplies and the keepers were taken by boat from Portree to the Rona quay. By 1930, only the lighthouse keepers remained on Rona as all other residents had relocated to the mainland.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was first lighted on 10 November 1857.
The lighthouse was converted to automatic operation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: 13 m (43 ft) cylindrical masonry tower with balcony and lantern, marked white (tower), black (lantern), ochre (trim).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is a Category B listed building, managed by the Northern Lighthouse Board, and represents an important part of Scotland's maritime history.
world knowledge.Details: The light should not be confused with the 1984 light located on the island of North Rona. The records of the manned lighthouse, including the shipwreck return book, stores and visitor books were transferred to the National Records of Scotland.

world knowledge.Name: Fine Arts Museum of Nantes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fine Arts Museum of Nantes was created by consular decree on 31 August 1801. It was founded under the Consulate by Napoléon Bonaparte and initially received works purchased by the state and deposits from the Louvre. The museum's collection was significantly enriched by the purchase of the Cacault brothers' collection in 1810. The current building, designed by architect Clément-Marie Josso, was inaugurated in 1900. The museum underwent major expansion work from 2011 to 2017, increasing its area and modernizing its facilities.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was created by consular decree on 31 August 1801.

Major_Events.Event: Purchase of the Cacault brothers' collection
Major_Events.Description: The city of Nantes purchased the collection of the Cacault brothers, significantly enriching the museum's holdings.
The current building, designed by architect Clément-Marie Josso, was inaugurated.
The museum closed for major expansion work, initially expected to last two years.
The museum fully reopened on 23 June 2017 after delays caused by the discovery of ground water in the foundations.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is an eclectic architectural monument from the late 19th century, designed by Clément-Marie Josso. It features a central courtyard covered with a glass roof, dual circuit galleries, and a monumental double staircase. The rooms on the ground floor are lit by large windows, while those on the upper floor have modern overhead lighting. The facade, roof, and stairs are registered as historical monuments.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is one of the largest in the region and offers an overview of French and European art movements from the 13th century to modern art. Its collections are among the largest public collections in France outside of Paris. The museum plays a significant role in the cultural life of Nantes and the region, hosting both permanent collections and temporary exhibitions.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include paintings from the 13th century to modern art. It benefits from deposits from the Regional Contemporary Art Funds of the Loire and the Centre Pompidou. The museum also features an auditorium, improved access, and renovated glass roofs to utilize natural light. The Jules-Dupré course, a paved road along the west side of the museum, is named after the painter Jules Dupré.

world knowledge.Name: Bihar Legislative Assembly
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bihar Legislative Assembly, also known as the Bihar Vidhan Sabha, is the lower house of the bicameral Bihar Legislature of the state of Bihar in India. The first state elections were held in 1952. Before the partition of Bihar, the total strength of membership in the assembly was 331, including one nominated member. After the partition, the seats were reduced to 243 members. Shri Krishna Singh became the first leader of the House and the first chief minister, Anugrah Narayan Singh was elected as the first deputy leader of the house and the first deputy chief minister. After the passing of the Government of India Act 1935, Bihar and Orissa became separate states. A bicameral system of legislature was introduced according to the act. On 22 July 1936, the first Bihar legislative council was set up. It had 30 members and Rajiv Ranjan Prasad was the chairman. The first joint session of the two houses of the Bihar Assembly took place on 22 July 1937. Ram Dayalu Singh was elected as the speaker of the Bihar Assembly.

Major_Events.Description: The first state elections were held in 1952.
Before the partition of Bihar, the total strength of membership in the assembly was 331, including one nominated member. After the partition, the seats were reduced to 243 members.
On 22 July 1936, the first Bihar legislative council was set up. It had 30 members and Rajiv Ranjan Prasad was the chairman.

Major_Events.Event: First joint session of the Bihar Assembly
Major_Events.Description: The first joint session of the two houses of the Bihar Assembly took place on 22 July 1937. Ram Dayalu Singh was elected as the speaker of the Bihar Assembly.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Bihar Legislative Assembly is a significant government building in Bihar, India, representing the state's legislative authority and political history.
world knowledge.Details: The Bihar Legislative Assembly is not a permanent body and is subject to dissolution. The tenure of the legislative assembly is five years from the date appointed for its first sitting unless dissolved sooner. Members of the legislative assembly are directly elected by the people. There are three sessions every year: budget session, monsoon session, and winter session. The sessions of the legislative assembly are presided over by the speaker. The speaker certifies whether a bill is ordinary bill or money bill. Generally, the speaker does not participate in voting, except in the case of a tie. Nand Kishore Yadav is the current speaker of the Bihar Legislative Assembly. The legislative assembly also has a Secretariat. The secretary is under the disciplinary control of the speaker. The function of the secretary is to assist the speaker. Bateshwar Nath Pandey is the current secretary of the Bihar Legislative Assembly.

world knowledge.Name: Howrah Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 705 m (2,313.0 ft) long, 21.6 m (70.9 ft) wide with two footpaths of 4.6 m (15.1 ft) on either side
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Howrah Bridge is a balanced steel bridge over the Hooghly River in West Bengal, India. Commissioned in 1943, it replaced a pontoon bridge at the same location linking the cities of Kolkata and Howrah. It was renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965 after the Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore. The bridge is a famous symbol of Kolkata and West Bengal, and it is one of four bridges on the Hooghly River.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was renamed in honor of Rabindranath Tagore, the first Indian and Asian Nobel laureate.
The bridge was officially opened to traffic on 3 February 1943.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a suspension type balanced cantilever and truss arch bridge made of steel. It has a total length of 705 m, a width of 21.6 m, and a height of 82 m. The longest span is 457.2 m. The bridge does not have nuts and bolts but was formed by riveting the whole structure.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Howrah Bridge is a famous symbol of Kolkata and West Bengal, connecting the city to Howrah Station. It is regarded as the 'gateway to Kolkata' and has been featured in numerous films, making it an iconic landmark in Indian cinema.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Roadway with pedestrians and bicycles, connecting Kolkata and Howrah.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge carries a daily traffic of approximately 100,000 vehicles and more than 150,000 pedestrians, making it one of the busiest cantilever bridges in the world. It is maintained by the Kolkata Port Trust and has been subject to damage from vehicles and corrosion due to atmospheric conditions and biological wastes.

world knowledge.Name: Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino
world knowledge.Address: Piazzale Grande Torino, Santa Rita district, Turin, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Stadio Municipale Benito Mussolini, the stadium was built in the 1930s to host the Littoriali Games of the fascist era. It served as the home ground for both Juventus and Torino until the 1990s, when it was abandoned in favor of Stadio delle Alpi. It was renovated and renamed for the 2006 Winter Olympics, and Torino FC continues to use it as their home stadium.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was built to host these games during the fascist era.
Hosted several matches of the tournament.
The stadium was renovated and used for the opening and closing ceremonies.
Hosted the final match of the tournament.

Major_Events.Event: Italy vs. Australia Rugby Union International
Major_Events.Description: Hosted Italy's end-of-year rugby union match against Australia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally designed with an ellipsoid ring, white granite base, and red plaster plinth. Renovations included a full roof with translucent sections, a third ring of tiers with 44 boxes, and modern amenities like heating coils and an automatic rain cover system. The current capacity is 28,177 seats, all covered and seated.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is named in honor of the Grande Torino team, a legendary football squad from the 1940s. It has been a central venue for major sporting events in Italy, including the 2006 Winter Olympics, and remains a symbol of Turin's sporting heritage.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium, primarily for football matches and major events.
Notable_Visitors: Representatives of the International Olympic Committee
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was the first in Italy to fully comply with the 'Pisanu Law' on stadium security, featuring over 80 surveillance cameras and movable glass enclosures. It also includes facilities for disabled spectators and has undergone multiple renovations to improve capacity and safety.

world knowledge.Name: El Molinón
world knowledge.Historical_Background: El Molinón is the oldest professional football field in Spain, in use since at least 1908. It is located on the site of an old watermill, hence its name, which means 'big mill' in Spanish. Real Sporting de Gijón started using it as their official ground in 1917. The stadium has undergone several renovations and expansions, including in 1968 when floodlights were installed, and in 1997–98 to comply with UEFA and FIFA security legislation. It was renamed in 2018 to honor Real Sporting's all-time top scorer, Quini.

Major_Events.Description: The first official match was held on April 22, 1917, between Real Sporting and Arenas Club de Getxo as part of the 1917 Copa del Rey. Arenas won 0–1.
El Molinón held the 1920 Copa del Rey Final, where Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao by 2–0.
In 1968, four floodlights were installed, and the first night match was played against Mestalla.
On 28 January 1970, the first match to be televised in Spain was played at El Molinón. Real Sporting defeated Osasuna by 3–0.
On 28 June 1995, Real Sporting beat the record attendance for the club at El Molinón, with 42,000 people at the relegation playoffs against Lleida.
The stadium hosted West Germany’s three matches in Group B, including the infamous 'Disgrace of Gijón' match against Austria.
The stadium hosted its first women's football match ever on 21 April 2019, with 9,700 spectators attending the local derby between Real Sporting and Gijón FF.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium has a grass surface and has undergone several renovations, including the installation of floodlights and seating to comply with modern safety standards. It was the first all-covered stadium in Spain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: El Molinón is culturally significant as the oldest professional football stadium in Spain and a historic venue for football matches, including international games and the 1982 FIFA World Cup. It is also a symbol of local pride for Gijón and Real Sporting de Gijón.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has hosted concerts by many famous artists and was used for filming scenes of the Academy Award-winning film 'Volver a empezar.' It is one of the potential host cities for the 2030 FIFA World Cup, which Spain will co-host along with Morocco and Portugal.

world knowledge.Name: Rigi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rigi, also known as Mount Rigi or Queen of the Mountains, is a mountain massif of the Alps located in Central Switzerland. It is almost entirely surrounded by Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug, and Lake Lauerz. The name Rigi originates from Swiss Old High German *rigî, meaning 'horizontal stratification, strip, band'. The name was first recorded in 1350 as Riginun. The mountain has been a popular destination for centuries, with the Rigi Kulm Hotel established in 1816. The area is served by Europe's oldest mountain railways, the Rigi Railways.

Major_Events.Description: Gerard Manley Hopkins ascended Rigi-Kulm, the highest peak of the Rigi massif, during a three-week tour through Switzerland.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rigi has been featured in many works of art, including paintings by J. M. W. Turner and literary publications by Mark Twain. It is also a destination for winter sports and other recreational activities.
world knowledge.Details: The Rigi is not geologically part of the Alps but belongs to the Swiss plateau. It is mostly composed of molasse and other conglomerate. The area offers many activities such as skiing or sledging in the winter, and hiking in the summer. There are multiple public transport options available to ascend Mount Rigi, including trains and cable-cars.

world knowledge.Name: International Antarctic Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The International Antarctic Centre is a visitor attraction and public science discovery centre located in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was established to highlight Christchurch's role as a gateway to Antarctica and to support the Antarctic programmes of the US, New Zealand, and Italy. The centre opened in 1990 and expanded in 1992 to include a visitor centre. It draws on the 100-year history of Christchurch's association with Antarctic exploration and research.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the International Antarctic Centre
Major_Events.Description: The first stage of the centre opened, providing office and warehouse storage facilities for the Antarctic programmes of New Zealand, the United States, and Italy.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Antarctic visitor centre
Major_Events.Description: The second stage of the development, the Antarctic visitor centre, was opened as a tourism venture.
The 10th anniversary was celebrated with an attempt to create the world's biggest birthday card by a group of 625 children.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Antarctic Storm attraction
Major_Events.Description: The Antarctic Storm attraction was opened, providing visitors with a simulated Antarctic blizzard experience.
The Christchurch earthquake caused major disruption to tourism in the city, leading to a significant drop in visitor numbers to the centre.
The International Antarctic Centre was sold to the owners of the Willowbank Wildlife Reserve.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The visitor centre building is described as a series of fan-shaped solids of varying height, appearing as large wedges of ice squeezed outwards from the Antarctic continent.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The centre highlights Christchurch's historical and ongoing role as a gateway to Antarctica, celebrating over a century of Antarctic exploration and research. It serves as an educational and tourist attraction, providing insights into Antarctic life and history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Visitor attraction and public science discovery centre
world knowledge.Details: The centre features Antarctic exhibits, a café, a bar, an Antarctic snow storm room, audiovisual displays, husky dog meetups, rides in Hägglunds all-terrain vehicles, and a little blue penguins exhibit. It also provides educational programmes and has been recognized in various tourism awards.

world knowledge.Name: Palanga Amber Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palanga Amber Museum, established in 1963, is housed in the restored 19th-century Tiškevičiai Palace, designed by German architect Franz Heinrich Schwechten. The palace fell into disrepair after World War I and World War II but was restored in 1957 by architect Alfredas Brusokas. The museum's collection includes about 28,000 pieces of amber, with 15,000 containing inclusions of insects, spiders, or plants. The Baltic Sea coast has been a source of amber trade since prehistoric times, and Lithuanian mythology, folklore, and art have long associations with amber.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was restored according to plans by architect Alfredas Brusokas.
The Palanga Amber Museum opened as a branch of the Lithuanian Museum of Fine Arts.
The museum received its millionth visitor on August 13, 1970.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a Neo-Renaissance-style palace designed by Franz Heinrich Schwechten. The palace features 15 exhibition rooms covering about 750 square meters and includes a chapel for temporary exhibitions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant due to its extensive collection of amber, which has been a part of Lithuanian mythology, folklore, and art for centuries. The museum also highlights the historical importance of amber trade in the Baltic region.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes the 'Sun Stone,' Europe's third largest amber specimen, which has been stolen twice. The surrounding Palanga Botanical Garden, designed by Édouard André and his son, covers about 100 hectares and features a variety of plant species, a rose garden, greenhouse, rotunda, and a Holocaust memorial. The park also includes Birutė's Hill, a site of historical and legendary significance.

world knowledge.Name: University of Tokyo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Tokyo was founded in 1877 as the nation's first modern university by the merger of several pre-westernisation era institutions. Its direct precursors include the Tenmongata, founded in 1684, and the Shoheizaka Institute. It was renamed Imperial University in 1886 and Tokyo Imperial University in 1897, reverting to its original name in 1947 after the dissolution of the Empire of Japan.

Major_Events.Description: The earthquake caused immense damage to the university, including the destruction of almost all main buildings and the loss of precious scientific and historical samples. This led to a reconstruction effort supported by international aid, including donations from John D. Rockefeller Jr. and the League of Nations.

During the war, 1,652 students and alumni were killed. The university's facilities were largely immune from air raids, allowing education and research to continue. The Imperial Army attempted to use the university's facilities, but President Yoshikazu Uchida prevented this.

Student protests began with medical students demanding improvements in internship conditions. The conflict escalated with the occupation of Yasuda Auditorium and was resolved by a police operation in 1969.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Hongo Campus features Collegiate Gothic style buildings known as Uchida Gothic, designed by Yoshikazu Uchida. The campus includes landmarks like Akamon (the Red Gate), a relic from the Edo period.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Tokyo is considered the most prestigious university in Japan and has produced numerous notable alumni, including 17 prime ministers, 20 Nobel Prize laureates, and founders of major companies like Toyota and Hitachi. It plays a central role in Japan's academic and cultural life.

Details.Faculties: 10 faculties including Law, Science, Letters, and Medicine
Details.Library_System: Over 10 million books, second-largest in Japan
Details.Hospital: University of Tokyo Hospital, ranked 17th in the world by Newsweek (2023)

world knowledge.Name: Folklore Museum of Kastoria
world knowledge.Address: 10 Kapetan Lazou Street, Kastoria, Macedonia, Greece
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Folklore Museum of Kastoria, also known as Folklore Museum “Nerantzis-Aivazis”, is housed in one of the city's oldest mansions, the Nerantzis-Aivazis residence. The museum has been operating since 1972 and is run by Harmony, a music and literary society. The two-storey premises were built between the 16th and 17th centuries and survived in such good condition that the museum was able to open without restoration. All the original furniture is still present.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in a two-storey mansion built between the 16th and 17th centuries. The ground floor includes three cellars for wine, pickles, and cereals, along with a well, boat shelter, and kitchen in the courtyard. The first floor features two family living rooms (one for summer and one for winter), with the summer room also used as a fur workshop. The second floor contains two bedrooms, two sitting-rooms, a lavatory with a secret exit passageway, and a balcony for unmarried women to observe ceremonies.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum preserves and showcases the traditional lifestyle and culture of Kastoria, including its historical architecture, household items, and fur trade heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes original furniture and artifacts, such as the first sewing machine for furs from France in 1884. It also features traditional places for hosts, the metropolitan bishop, and Turkish dignitaries in the main reception room.

world knowledge.Name: Studio City (Macau)
world knowledge.Address: Estr. Flor de Lotus, Cotai, Macau, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Studio City is a Hollywood studio-themed leisure resort on the Cotai Strip in Macau. It is the first in Asia to integrate television and film production facilities, retail, gaming, and hotels. The resort was developed by Melco Resorts & Entertainment and officially opened on 27 October 2015. The project was initially developed without a casino by U.S. investment firms Silver Point Capital LP and Oaktree Capital Management LLC, with a 40 per cent interest through a joint subsidiary, New Cotai Holdings, and Hong Kong entertainment company eSun Holdings Ltd. Melco Crown Entertainment acquired eSun's 60 per cent controlling interest in June 2011.

Major_Events.Description: The $3.2 billion Studio City officially opened on 27 October 2015 on Macau's Cotai Strip. Melco Crown Entertainment commissioned a $70 million film for the grand opening, produced by Brett Ratner and directed by Martin Scorsese, featuring Robert De Niro and Leonardo DiCaprio.

In December 2020, Star Tower at Studio City and Altira Macau, along with other Melco Resorts properties, were named among the first hotels in the world to receive Sharecare Health Security certification by Forbes Travel Guide.
On 28 December 2021, it was announced that W Macau – Studio City is scheduled to open in December 2022 as part of Phase 2 with 557 guestrooms, including 127 suites.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Studio City features an Art Deco design inspired by two asteroids shooting through a Gotham City building. The resort was designed by Goddard Group, a Los Angeles–based entertainment design firm. The two hotel towers – Star Tower and Celebrity Tower – are connected by the Golden Reel, the world's first and highest figure-8 ferris wheel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Studio City is culturally significant as it is the first Hollywood studio-themed leisure resort in Asia, integrating television and film production facilities, retail, gaming, and hotels. It celebrates the Golden Age of Hollywood and features attractions and designs inspired by iconic Hollywood elements.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement Park, Hotel, Casino, Entertainment Complex
world knowledge.Details: Studio City includes a 30,000-square-foot Family Entertainment Center in collaboration with Warner Bros and DC Comics, featuring characters such as Superman, Wonder Woman, and The Flash. The resort also houses a 5,000-seat live performance arena, an indoor/outdoor water park, and various award-winning restaurants. Phase 2 of Studio City's expansion will add two hotel towers with approximately 900 rooms, additional gaming areas, a cineplex, and an indoor/outdoor water park touted as one of the world's largest.

world knowledge.Name: Mahamasina Municipal Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kianja Barea Mahamasina is a multi-purpose stadium used for rugby union, football, concerts, and athletics. It is the largest stadium in Madagascar.

Major_Events.Event: Stampede during Kaizer Chiefs vs USJF Ravinala match
Major_Events.Description: A stampede during a match between South African side Kaizer Chiefs and Madagascar's USJF Ravinala killed two people.
The stadium hosted the 2007 Indian Ocean Games.
A grenade thrown at the stadium during a musical production killed one child and wounded 33.
A bomb detonated in the stadium during a free concert, killing two people and injuring around 80.

Major_Events.Event: Stampede during Africa Cup of Nations qualification match
Major_Events.Description: A stampede to enter the stadium killed one person and injured 37. Long queues had formed to see the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification match against Senegal.
At least 16 people were killed and 101 injured in a human crush before the concert of Rossy on independence day. The police had left the doors closed, and people tried to force them open.

Major_Events.Event: Crush incident during Indian Ocean Island Games
Major_Events.Description: At least 12 people died during a crush incident at the stadium during the opening of the Indian Ocean Island Games.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mahamasina Municipal Stadium is the largest stadium in Madagascar and has hosted significant sports and cultural events, making it a central venue in the country.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium for rugby, football, concerts, and athletics
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 40,880 for football and rugby matches.

image_name: United States Public Health Service Building

world knowledge.Name: United States Public Health Service Building
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The building served as the headquarters of the U.S. Public Health Service during 1933–1942 and 1946–1947. It was also used by the Combined Chiefs of Staff, Atomic Energy Commission, National Science Foundation, and Department of the Interior. In 2018, it was transferred to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.

Major_Events.Event: Headquarters of the U.S. Public Health Service
Major_Events.Description: The building served as the headquarters of the U.S. Public Health Service during these periods.
During World War II, the building was occupied by the Combined Chiefs of Staff and was the site of planning for the Manhattan Project.
The Atomic Energy Commission occupied the building from its creation until its relocation to Germantown, Maryland.
The building served as the headquarters of the National Science Foundation during this period.

Major_Events.Event: Bureau of Indian Affairs and Office of Surface Mining
Major_Events.Description: The building was used by the Department of the Interior, housing the Bureau of Indian Affairs and Office of Surface Mining.
Around 500 American Indians with the AIM took over the building to bring attention to American Indian issues, occupying it from November 3 to November 9, 1972.
The building was transferred to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, with plans for renovation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building is a three-story E-shaped structure with a raised basement, shallow projecting corner pavilions, and a gabled tile roof. It features a concealed steel frame and concrete floors. The primary facade is faced in white Georgia marble with a thirteen-bay, engaged double-height colonnade of fluted Doric pilasters. Notable interior spaces include a marble entrance lobby, marble stair and elevator lobbies, an ornamental auditorium, and an elaborate wood-paneled executive office suite.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is historically significant for its roles in various government agencies, including the U.S. Public Health Service, Combined Chiefs of Staff, Atomic Energy Commission, and Bureau of Indian Affairs. It was also a site of protest by the American Indian Movement in 1972.
world knowledge.Details: The building was designed by Jules Henri de Sibour in the Neoclassical style. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on July 5, 2007. The site was previously home to a YWCA.

world knowledge.Name: Cheyenne Mountain Zoo
world knowledge.Address: Southwest of downtown Colorado Springs, Colorado
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 140 acres (57 ha) (40 acres (16 ha) in use)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cheyenne Mountain Zoo was founded in 1926 by businessman Spencer Penrose to house his collection of exotic animals, which began with a gift of a bear in 1916. The animals were initially housed at Penrose's Broadmoor Hotel until a monkey bit a guest, prompting the creation of the zoo. In 1938, it was incorporated as a non-profit public trust. The zoo is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization and does not receive local or regional public tax support.

Major_Events.Description: On August 6, 2018, the zoo was hit by fast-moving and unexpected severe weather that brought baseball-sized hail. The staff used the incident command system to swiftly move animals and visitors indoors. Three zoo employees were hospitalized, and five animals died due to injuries from the hail.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of International Center for the Care and Conservation of Giraffe
Major_Events.Description: In 2022, the zoo established the International Center for the Care and Conservation of Giraffe, which hosts workshops and offers consulting services to improve the lives of giraffes in human care.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cheyenne Mountain Zoo is the highest zoo in the United States and is known for its large and prolific giraffe herd, with 203 giraffe calves born since 1954. It is a trusted source for giraffe care and maintains a collection of giraffe plasma for emergencies. The zoo also breeds endangered species and participates in over 30 Species Survival Plan programs.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo houses more than 750 animals representing nearly 170 species, including over 30 endangered species. It was ranked the #4 best zoo in North America in 2018 by USA Today. The zoo financially supports field conservation programs through Quarters for Conservation, raising over $2 million since 2008. It also participates in the Panama Amphibian Rescue and Conservation project.

world knowledge.Name: Priory Palace
world knowledge.Address: Gatchina, Leningrad oblast, Northwest Russia, a suburb of Saint Petersburg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Priory Palace was built in 1799 by the architect Nikolay Lvov on the shore of the Black Lake. It was constructed for the Russian Grand Priory of the Order of St John and presented to the Order by a decree of Paul I of Russia dated August 23, 1799.

Major_Events.Event: Presentation to the Order of St John
Major_Events.Description: The palace was presented to the Russian Grand Priory of the Order of St John by a decree of Paul I of Russia dated August 23, 1799.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Priory is the only surviving architectural monument in Russia built mainly by the technology of earthwork: layers of compacted loam are poured with lime mortar. The walls of the palace, the fence, and the court buildings were built using this technology. The retaining wall is made of the famous Pudost stone. Researchers note the precision of the layout, the original composition, and the characteristic refusal of symmetry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Priory Palace is an original palace and the only surviving architectural monument in Russia built mainly by the technology of earthwork. It is significant for its unique construction method and historical association with the Order of St John.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a castle in Russia is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Poya Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 851.6 metres (2,794 ft) in length, 19.25 metres (63.2 ft) in width
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Poya Bridge was constructed to alleviate traffic from the Zaehringen Bridge and surrounding neighborhoods in Fribourg. Planning began in 1959, with detailed studies and proposals in the 1980s and 1990s. The project was approved by the Grand Council of Fribourg in 2006, and construction started on 31 October 2008. The bridge opened on 12 October 2014.

Major_Events.Description: The Grand Council of Fribourg approved the project, and financing was approved by 81% of voters.
Construction of the bridge began on 31 October 2008.
The bridge was inaugurated on 10 October 2014.
The bridge opened to vehicular traffic on 12 October 2014.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Poya Bridge is a multi-span, cable-stayed bridge with a main span of 196.00 metres (643.04 ft), the longest in Switzerland. It features two pylons of unequal height, with the southeast pylon rising 107.65 metres (353.2 ft) and the northwest pylon rising 90.96 metres (298.4 ft). The bridge deck carries three lanes of traffic and a shared path for pedestrians and cyclists. The deck is inclined, with the southeast end approximately 18 metres (59 ft) higher than the northwest end. The bridge includes noise-reducing covers and barriers to prevent suicide attempts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Poya Bridge is significant for its role in reducing traffic congestion in Fribourg's historic center, improving the quality of life for residents, and preserving the Fribourg Cathedral. It is also notable for having the longest main span of any bridge in Switzerland.
world knowledge.Details: The northwest end of the bridge leads into the Poya Tunnel, a 272-metre (892 ft) cut-and-cover tunnel that travels beneath the Berne-Fribourg rail line and Palatinat Park. The tunnel includes an underground roundabout intersecting Rue de Morat. The speed limit is 60 km/h on the bridge and 50 km/h in the tunnel. The bridge cost CHF 211 million to construct, with the tunnel costing an additional CHF 28 million.

world knowledge.Name: Tybee Island
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Land: 2.88 sq mi (7.46 km²), Water: 0.30 sq mi (0.79 km²)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tybee Island is a city and barrier island in Georgia, historically significant for its lighthouse, military fortifications, and as a vacation destination. It was originally inhabited by the Euchee tribe and later became a strategic location for Spanish and English settlers. The island played roles in the Civil War and World War II, and it was the site of an accidental atomic bomb drop in 1958.

Major_Events.Description: A U.S. Air Force B-47 Stratojet accidentally dropped a Mark 15 hydrogen bomb off the coast of Tybee Island during a training exercise. The bomb was never recovered.
Union Army batteries on Tybee Island bombarded and captured Fort Pulaski, marking the first significant use of rifled cannons against masonry fortifications.
An annual pirate-themed festival began, celebrating the island's history with pirates and maritime culture.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The island features historic structures like the Tybee Island Light Station (a lighthouse with preserved support buildings) and Fort Screven's remaining buildings, including Battery Garland and Officer's Row. The architecture reflects coastal defense and recreational uses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tybee Island is culturally significant for its lighthouse (one of the few 18th-century lighthouses still operational in North America), its role in military history, and as a long-standing beach vacation destination. It also hosts annual events like the Beach Bum parade and Tybee Pirate Fest.
world knowledge.Details: Tybee Island is part of the Savannah metropolitan area and is known for its sandy beaches, salt marshes, and maritime forests. It was briefly renamed Savannah Beach in 1929 but reverted to its original name in 1978. The island has a mix of historic sites, vacation cottages, and modern amenities.

world knowledge.Name: Nickelodeon Universe
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened as Knott's Camp Snoopy in 1992, themed around the Peanuts comic strip characters. In 2006, the Peanuts branding was removed due to licensing disputes, and the park was temporarily renamed The Park at MOA. In 2008, it was rebranded as Nickelodeon Universe, featuring attractions based on Nickelodeon franchises. A second location opened at American Dream in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and a third is under construction in Chongqing, China.

Major_Events.Description: The park was rebranded from The Park at MOA to Nickelodeon Universe, featuring new rides and attractions themed around Nickelodeon shows.
The park closed temporarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic and reopened with limited capacity and modified ticketing policies.
A second Nickelodeon Universe location opened at American Dream in East Rutherford, New Jersey, featuring record-breaking roller coasters.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Indoor amusement park with themed areas based on Nickelodeon franchises. Features roller coasters, drop towers, and other rides designed to fit within a mall environment.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As one of the few indoor amusement parks in the world, Nickelodeon Universe is a significant entertainment destination. Its rebranding from Camp Snoopy to Nickelodeon Universe marked a major shift in thematic focus, appealing to a younger audience familiar with Nickelodeon's popular shows.
world knowledge.Details: The park features 27+ attractions, including 5 roller coasters and 1 water ride. It operates year-round as an indoor facility. Pricing for admission and annual passes has evolved over the years, with current options including tiered annual passes. The park is owned by the Triple Five Group under license from Paramount Global.

world knowledge.Name: Holy Family Shrine
world knowledge.Address: 23132 Pflug Road, Gretna, Nebraska 68028, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Holy Family Shrine is a Roman Catholic shrine located along Interstate 80 outside of Omaha, Nebraska, near the town of Gretna. The idea to build a shrine for travelers on the Interstate was conceived in 1993 when four Catholics—a priest, two architects, and another layperson—were inspired to build a chapel for travelers 'of the road and of the spirit'. The land was purchased in 1995, but funding and administrative difficulties delayed the project for two years. Construction of the parking lot and visitor center began in 1997, but further funding to begin construction of the chapel was not secured until 1999. The chapel building topped out in July 2000, but a windstorm destroyed the structure the following week. The chapel was opened to the public in July 2002.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the parking lot and visitor center began.
A windstorm destroyed the chapel structure shortly after it topped out.
The chapel was officially opened to the public.

Major_Events.Event: Stations of the cross path built
Major_Events.Description: A path of life-size depictions of the stations of the cross was built.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The chapel stands on bluffs overlooking Interstate 80. Inspired by Thorncrown Chapel, it is made of western red cedar beams and glass walls. The southern window features an etching of the Holy Family. The primarily glass construction allows for unobstructed views of the surrounding landscape. A visitor center inspired by a prairie dugout contains a gift shop, meeting spaces, and restrooms. The entrance to the visitor center is meant to evoke the tomb of Jesus, and a sculpture hanging from a skylight evokes his shroud. A 40-foot (12 m) cross towers over the interstate below.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The shrine serves as a spiritual refuge for travelers and locals alike, symbolizing faith and resilience. Its unique architectural design and scenic location make it a notable landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The shrine was designed by Jim Dennel of the Omaha-based firm BCDM Architects. In 2016, 20,000 people visited the chapel. The project was conceived to serve travelers 'of the road and of the spirit'.

world knowledge.Name: Palácio Rio Negro
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palácio Rio Negro is a palace located in Petrópolis, Brazil. It was built in 1889 as a summer residence for the Baron of Rio Negro. Later, it became the official residence of the state Governor and then the summer residence of the Presidents of Brazil. It was frequently used when Rio de Janeiro was the capital of Brazil but saw a decline in use after the capital moved to Brasília in 1960.

Major_Events.Event: Wedding of President Hermes da Fonseca and Nair de Tefé
Major_Events.Description: The Palace lived its most brilliant moment during the administration of Hermes da Fonseca, with the wedding of the President and Nair de Tefé, a celebrity known for her beauty, intelligence, and caricatures.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Italian architect Antonio Jannuzzi, the palace features an architectural style typical of late 19th-century Brazilian elite residences.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Palácio Rio Negro is one of the official residences of the President of Brazil and has hosted numerous presidents and notable events, making it a significant historical and political landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Official summer residence of the President of Brazil.
world knowledge.Details: The palace was not used at all in the 1970s and 1980s but was briefly used by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in the 1990s. Today, it is rarely used.

world knowledge.Name: Cloud County Courthouse (Kansas)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The county was created on February 27, 1860, as Shirley County; the county seat was set at Clyde. It was moved to Rochester (now defunct) in 1866. The county was renamed Cloud County in 1867 with the county seat set at Concordia in 1870. The first courthouse was a three-story brick structure with an imposing central cupola, which was later removed. It was constructed by John S. Huntley and designed by W. R. Parson & Sons.

Major_Events.Description: The county seat was set at Concordia in 1870.
The current courthouse was built by Rhode Construction Company and designed by Williamson-Loebsack & Associates.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The courthouse is designed in the Modern style. It is three stories and faces west. It is constructed of gray limestone, glass, and concrete with a flat roof. The north section is two stories, constructed of glass, and has an entrance on the west side which serves as a foyer. On the east side of the courthouse is the old county jail.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cloud County Courthouse is the seat of the government of Cloud County, Kansas, and represents the administrative and historical center of the county.
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse is located on spacious landscaped grounds in the city's center. Williamson-Loebsack & Associates also designed courthouses in Greenwood County, Ottawa County, and Sumner County.

world knowledge.Name: Chaoyin Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Chaoyang Subdistrict, Wuxing District of Huzhou, Zhejiang, China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 50 metres (160 ft) long, 5 metres (16 ft) wide, approximately 7 metres (23 ft) high
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1539 during the Ming dynasty under Jiajing Emperor's reign. The present version was completed in 1605 during Wanli Emperor's rule.

Major_Events.Event: Listed as Major National Historical and Cultural Site
Major_Events.Description: On 7 October 2019, it was listed among the eighth batch of Major National Historical and Cultural Sites in Zhejiang by the State Council of China.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Stone arch bridge design, measuring 50 metres long, 5 metres wide, and approximately 7 metres high.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A historic bridge named after 'Chaoyin Ferry,' recognized as a Major National Historical and Cultural Site in China.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge spans the Tiao Stream and is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Zhejiang, China.

world knowledge.Name: Gachon University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gachon University is a private university in South Korea, formed through mergers of several institutions including Gachon University of Medicine and Science, Gachon-gil College, Kyungwon University, and Kyungwon College between 2007 and 2012. It has three campuses for undergraduates and a School of Medicine. The university has a history of educational reform and internationalization, with partnerships and exchange agreements with numerous prestigious universities worldwide.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Gachon University of Medicine and Science and Gachon-gil College
Major_Events.Description: The first of several mergers that would eventually form the current structure of Gachon University.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Kyungwon University and Kyungwon College
Major_Events.Description: Further consolidation in the formation of Gachon University.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Gachon University of Medicine and Science and Kyungwon University
Major_Events.Description: Final merger completing the formation of the current Gachon University.
Agreement allowing Gachon students to study at Hawaii Pacific University.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Gachon University is significant for its contributions to education and research in South Korea, particularly in the fields of science, technology, and medicine. Its international partnerships enhance its global cultural and educational impact.
world knowledge.Details: Gachon University has three campuses for undergraduates, the Global Campus (primary) located in Seongnam, satellite campuses on Ganghwa Island and in Yeonsu-dong, and the School of Medicine in Guwol-dong, Namdong-gu, Incheon, South Korea. It was ranked 30th among Korean universities and 852nd in the world by Center for World University Rankings for the 2018–2019 period.

world knowledge.Name: Galleria dell'Accademia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Galleria dell'Accademia di Firenze, or 'Gallery of the Academy of Florence', is an art museum in Florence, Italy. It is best known as the home of Michelangelo's sculpture David. It also has other sculptures by Michelangelo and a large collection of paintings by Florentine artists, mostly from the period 1300–1600 (the Trecento to the Late Renaissance). It is smaller and more specialized than the Uffizi, the main art museum in Florence. It adjoins the Accademia di Belle Arti or academy of fine arts of Florence, but despite the name has no other connection with it. The Galleria dell'Accademia was founded in 1784 by Pietro Leopoldo, Grand Duke of Tuscany.

Major_Events.Event: Museo degli strumenti musicali collection opening
Major_Events.Description: It includes musical instruments made by Stradivarius, Niccolò Amati and Bartolomeo Cristofori which were acquired by the Florence Conservatory.

The museum successfully sued a magazine publisher for using an image of Michelangelo's David without the museum's permission, even though the artwork (which is physically in the museum) belongs to the public domain.

The Galleria dell'Accademia has housed the original David by Michelangelo since 1873. The sculpture was allegedly brought to the Accademia for reasons of conservation, although other factors were involved in its move from its previous outdoor location on Piazza della Signoria.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Galleria dell'Accademia is culturally and historically important as it houses Michelangelo's sculpture David and a large collection of paintings by Florentine artists from the 13th to the 16th centuries. It also includes other sculptures by Michelangelo and works by notable artists such as Paolo Uccello, Domenico Ghirlandaio, Sandro Botticelli, and Andrea del Sarto.
world knowledge.Details: In 2016, it had 1.46 million visitors, making it the second-most-visited art museum in Italy, after the Uffizi (2.02 million). The gallery's small collection of Michelangelo's work includes his four unfinished Prisoners, intended for the tomb of Pope Julius II, and a statue of Saint Matthew, also unfinished. In 1939, these were joined by the Palestrina Pietà, discovered in the Barberini chapel in Palestrina, though experts now consider its attribution to Michelangelo to be dubious. Other works on display are Florentine paintings from the 13th and 16th centuries, including works by Paolo Uccello, Domenico Ghirlandaio, Sandro Botticelli and Andrea del Sarto; and, from the High Renaissance, Giambologna's original full-size plaster modello for the Rape of the Sabine Women. As well as a number of Florentine Gothic paintings, the gallery houses the collection of Russian icons assembled by the Grand Dukes of the House of Lorraine, of which Leopoldo was one.

world knowledge.Name: Conishead Priory
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Conishead Priory was originally founded as a hospital in the 12th century by Gamel de Pennington and later developed into a priory under the Canons Regular of Saint Augustine. After the dissolution of the monasteries, the lands changed hands multiple times. The current Gothic Revival building was constructed in the 19th century, designed by Philip William Wyatt and later George Webster. It served various roles, including a private residence, spa hotel, and convalescent home for miners. Since 1976, it has been home to Buddhist communities.

Major_Events.Description: The original priory was dissolved, and the lands were leased to Thomas Stanley, 2nd Baron Monteagle.
The current Gothic Revival building was constructed, designed by Philip William Wyatt and later George Webster.
The priory was converted into a spa hotel by a Scottish syndicate.
The priory was opened as a convalescent home for miners by the Durham Miners Welfare Committee.
The priory served as an emergency hospital for wounded servicemen.
The priory became the home of Buddhist communities, including the Kadampa Temple for World Peace.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Gothic Revival style, large and elaborate structure with significant interior and exterior detailing.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Conishead Priory is historically significant for its medieval origins, its transformation through various ownerships and uses, and its current role as a center for Buddhist practice and education.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a priory, later a private residence, spa hotel, convalescent home, and now a Buddhist center.
world knowledge.Details: The priory has undergone numerous changes in ownership and function over the centuries. It was once a popular spa hotel with its own railway station. Today, it houses the Kadampa Temple for World Peace, a significant Buddhist temple.

world knowledge.Name: Wrexham University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Wrexham University originated as the Wrexham School of Science and Art in 1887. It underwent several name changes and mergers, becoming the North East Wales Institute of Higher Education in 1975. It gained full university status in 2008 and was renamed Glyndŵr University. In 2023, it adopted its current name, Wrexham University. The university has campuses in Wrexham, Northop, and St Asaph.

Major_Events.Description: The institution was granted full university status and renamed Glyndŵr University.
The university officially changed its name to Wrexham University, dropping 'Glyndŵr' from its name.
The Queen visited the university.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Birgitte, Duchess of Gloucester
Major_Events.Description: Birgitte, Duchess of Gloucester, visited the university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's main campus at Plas Coch features over 70 seminar suites, conference suites, lecture theatres, workshops, laboratories, a library, sports centre, and various specialized centres such as the Centre for the Creative Industries and the Glyndŵr University Racecourse Stadium.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Wrexham University is culturally significant as it is named after Owain Glyndŵr, a fifteenth-century Welsh leader who advocated for the establishment of universities in Wales. It plays a key role in higher education in North Wales and has a strong focus on creative arts, engineering, and science.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education institution offering undergraduate, postgraduate, and professional courses.
world knowledge.Details: Wrexham University has various sites in Wrexham and north-east Wales, including the Plas Coch campus and the North Wales School of Art and Design. It offers a wide range of programs and has international partnerships across Europe, Africa, and Asia. The university is known for its strong employability rates and is a member of the Fair Trade Coalition.

world knowledge.Name: St Paul's Cathedral, Melbourne
world knowledge.Address: Eastern corner of Swanston and Flinders streets, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St Paul's Cathedral is an Anglican cathedral in Melbourne, Australia, and the seat of the Archbishop of Melbourne. It was designed by English Gothic Revival architect William Butterfield and completed in 1891, except for the spires which were built from 1926 to 1932. The cathedral marks the site of the first Christian service held in Melbourne in 1835. Previous buildings on this site include a corn market and St Paul's Parish Church.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral (without the spires) was consecrated on 22 January 1891 by the Rt Revd Field Flowers Goe, Bishop of Melbourne.
The central spire, named the Moorhouse Spire, reached its full height of 312 ft (95m) in 1932.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by Pope John Paul II
