Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II visited St Paul's Cathedral on 28 November 1986, marking a historic occasion for Anglican and Roman Catholic dialogue.
A seven-year restoration project was completed in 2009, restoring the spires and improving the interior of the building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral is designed in the Gothic Revival style by William Butterfield. It features a traditional Latin cross plan with a long nave, side aisles, short transepts, and a tower at the crossing. The stonework is a mixture of sandstone from the Barrabool Hills and Waurn Ponds limestone. The interior features rich colours and strident colour contrasts, characteristic of Butterfield's work, with polychromatic stonework, Devonshire marble, alabaster, and Venetian glass mosaics in the reredos. The floor is paved with encaustic tiles imported from England.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St Paul's Cathedral is one of Melbourne's major architectural landmarks and holds significant historical and religious importance as the site of the first Christian service in Melbourne. It is the cathedral church of the Diocese of Melbourne and the seat of the Archbishop of Melbourne. The cathedral also plays a key role in the city's cultural and musical life, hosting state funerals, significant events, and maintaining a daily choral Evensong tradition.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Anglican cathedral and place of worship

Details.Organist: Siegfried Franke, Lachlan Redd, Roslyn Carolane, Mark Slavec

Music.Organ: Built by T. C. Lewis and Co, restored in 1990
Music.Choir: Includes Boys' and Girls' Voices, established in 2016

Bells.Foundry: Mears & Stainbank of Whitechapel Bell Foundry

world knowledge.Name: St. Joseph's Church, Beijing
world knowledge.Historical_Background: St. Joseph's Church, also known as Wangfujing Church or Dongtang, is one of the four historic Catholic churches in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Beijing. Founded in 1653 by Jesuit missionaries Lodovico Buglio and Gabriel de Magalhães, the church has undergone multiple reconstructions due to natural disasters, anti-Western sentiments, and political upheavals. The current structure dates back to 1904. The church was expropriated by the Chinese government in the 1950s and used as an elementary school, later reopening in 1980 after restoration.

Major_Events.Description: An earthquake struck Beijing, damaging the church building.
The church was obliterated by fire and further destroyed due to anti-Western policies. It was later rebuilt by foreign missionaries after the Second Opium War.
The church was burned to the ground during the Boxer Rebellion.
The church was rebuilt in Romanesque Revival style.
The church was expropriated by the Communist government and turned into an elementary school.
The church was closed and suffered further damage during the Cultural Revolution.
The church was restored and reopened for Catholic services.
A significant renovation of the church was completed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romanesque Revival style with a mixture of European and local Chinese features. The church features pilasters and three bell towers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: St. Joseph's Church is one of the oldest and most historically significant Catholic churches in Beijing, reflecting the turbulent history of Christianity in China. It is a symbol of the resilience of the Catholic community despite political and social challenges.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Parish church for the Roman Catholic community.
world knowledge.Details: The church is under the administration of the Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association (CPCA). It appears in Cixin Liu's novel 'The Three Body Problem'. The surrounding area includes a large square and park with a statue of the Madonna and Child.

world knowledge.Name: Anglesey Sea Zoo
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anglesey Sea Zoo was opened in 1983 by David and Alison Lea-Wilson, who later founded the next door Halen Môn sea salt business. As owners of a lobster wholesale business, they realized lobster tanks had become attractions in themselves. In 2007 the attraction was sold to research ecologists who have since gone on to develop research and conservation projects based at the aquarium, as well as several community conservation initiatives.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Anglesey Sea Zoo
Major_Events.Description: The Anglesey Sea Zoo was opened by David and Alison Lea-Wilson.
The attraction was sold to research ecologists who developed research and conservation projects.

Major_Events.Event: Rescue of a stranded striped dolphin
Major_Events.Description: The zoo successfully rescued a stranded striped dolphin, leading to the establishment of a rescue center for marine animals.

Major_Events.Event: Away shirt sponsorship for Bangor City F.C.
Major_Events.Description: The zoo sponsored the away shirts for Welsh Premier League side Bangor City F.C.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Anglesey Sea Zoo is a conservation zoo and tourist activity centre, involved in captive breeding programs and national and international consultancy. It is one of the few places in the world that has been able to successfully breed and sustain native short-snouted seahorse. The zoo also contains a rescue center for sick or stranded marine animals, contributing to marine conservation efforts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Aquarium and independent research and marine education centre
world knowledge.Details: The zoo hosts a conger eel, a shark pool, a kelp forest, and runs the Lobster Hatchery of Wales. It currently has two species of sea horses—the short snouted seahorse found around the UK and Mediterranean, and the drab seahorse found in the Red Sea. The aquarium also houses one of the only shops and bistros that sell almost exclusively fair trade and locally sourced products. Around 85% of the food served in the bistro comes from within 10 miles of the centre.

world knowledge.Name: Eden Project
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Rainforest Biome: 1.56 ha, Mediterranean Biome: 0.654 ha
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Eden Project, located in a reclaimed china clay pit in Cornwall, England, was conceived by Tim Smit and Jonathan Ball. Construction began in 1998, with the visitor centre opening in May 2000 and the full site opening on 17 March 2001. The project features two large biomes simulating rainforest and Mediterranean environments, alongside an outdoor botanical garden.

Major_Events.Description: The Eden Project officially opened to the public on 17 March 2001.
The Eden Project hosted the "Africa Calling" concert as part of the Live 8 concert series on 2 July 2005.
The World Pasty Championships, an international competition for Cornish pasties, have been held annually at the Eden Project since 2012.
The Eden Project hosted an event during the 2021 G7 Summit.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Eden Project features two large biomes constructed from a tubular steel frame with hexagonal and pentagonal ethylene tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE) inflated cells. The Rainforest Biome is 55 m high, 100 m wide, and 200 m long, while the Mediterranean Biome is 35 m high, 65 m wide, and 135 m long. The biomes are self-supporting geodesic structures with no internal supports.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Eden Project is significant for its focus on environmental education and the interdependence of plants and people. It has contributed over £1 billion to the Cornish economy and is home to Europe's second-largest redwood forest.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Visitor attraction and environmental education center
world knowledge.Details: The Eden Project includes a Rainforest Biome, a Mediterranean Biome, and an outdoor botanical garden. It uses Green Tariff Electricity and has plans for a geothermal electricity plant. The project has inspired similar developments in Morecambe, Dundee, Qingdao, and other locations. It has also hosted various cultural and musical events, including the Eden Sessions.

world knowledge.Name: Wuyi Mountains
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wuyi Mountains have a history of human settlement dating back 4,000 years. They were an important center of Taoism and later Buddhism, and are the cradle of Neo-Confucianism. The area was the capital of the Minyue kingdom during the Western Han dynasty. The mountains have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999 for their cultural, scenic, and biodiversity values.

Major_Events.Description: The Wuyi Mountains were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for their cultural, scenic, and biodiversity values.
The UNESCO World Heritage Site designation was modified.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The landscape is characterized by beautiful winding river valleys flanked by columnar or dome-shaped cliffs as well as cave systems. The region features remains of 35 academies, Taoist temples, and monasteries, with some well-preserved examples like the Taoyuan Temple, Wannian Palace, and Tianxin Temple.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wuyi Mountains are culturally significant for their role in the development of Taoism, Buddhism, and Neo-Confucianism. They are also renowned for their tea culture, including the production of famous teas like Da Hong Pao and Lapsang souchong. The area is also the birthplace of tea-picking opera, reflecting the rural and Hakka culture of the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary functions of the Wuyi Mountains include biodiversity conservation, cultural preservation, and tourism. The area is also a major tea-producing region.
world knowledge.Details: The Wuyi Mountains are known for their high biodiversity, including many rare and endemic species. The area is divided into four core parts: the Nine-bend Stream Ecological Protection Area, Wuyishan National Nature Reserve, Wuyishan National Scenic Area, and the Protection Area for the Remains of the Ancient Han Dynasty. The region is also famous for its tea production, including the 'Four Great Cultivars' teas, and hosts the world's first landscape surroundings theater showcasing Chinese tea culture, 'Impression Da Hong Pao'.

world knowledge.Name: Campo Ma'an National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Campo Ma'an National Park was established in 2000 as a compensation for the environmental damages expected from the Chad-Cameroon oil pipeline. It was originally the Campo Wildlife Reserve, established in 1932, and the adjacent Ma’an forest plantation was set up in 1980. The park is recognized as a site of the Global Environmental Facility, World Bank Biodiversity Conservation and Management Project.

Major_Events.Description: Established as an agreement between the Government of Cameroon and the Campo Forest Company.
Set up for conservation of Aucoumea klaineana (okoumé), a tree species with high economic logging value.
The forest was upgraded to a Technical Operational Unit (TOU) of 771,000 ha.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Campo Ma'an National Park
Major_Events.Description: The protected area and protected forest became the current Campo Ma'an National Park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a closed evergreen canopy forest, described as Atlantic Biafran forest with many plant species in the Caesalpiniaceae family.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a biodiversity hotspot and a priority landscape for conservation of western lowland gorillas and central chimpanzees. It is also traditional territory of the Bagyeli (Pygmies) and Bantu indigenous groups.
world knowledge.Details: The park is subject to threats from logging, poaching, agricultural activities, and coastal development. It has been proposed as a pilot ecotourism site. The region is home to over 100 villages and has seen conflicts due to restricted hunting access. A formal co-management agreement has been signed with the Bagyeli, and some have been employed in great ape conservation initiatives.

world knowledge.Name: Garrick Theater (Chicago)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Schiller Theater Building was designed by Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler of the firm Adler & Sullivan for the German Opera Company. At the time of its construction, it was among the tallest buildings in Chicago. Its centerpiece was a 1,300-seat theater, considered one of the greatest collaborations between Adler and Sullivan. Originally funded by German investors, it was projected to be used for German-language operas and cultural events. After German investors backed out in the late 1890s, it ceased German performances and exhibited touring stage shows. It later became a movie theater, a television studio, and then a movie theater again before being demolished in 1961.

Major_Events.Description: The theater opened as the Schiller Theater, funded by German investors for German-language operas and cultural events.
The theater was briefly known as the Dearborn Theater from 1898 to 1903.
The theater settled on the name Garrick Theater after 1903.
The theater was acquired by Balaban & Katz and converted into a movie theater.
The theater became a television studio in 1950.
The theater returned to screening movies in 1957.
The Garrick Theater was razed in 1961 and replaced with a parking structure, sparking wide-scale preservation efforts in Chicago.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler, the building was among the tallest in Chicago at the time of its construction. Its centerpiece was a 1,300-seat theater, featuring a series of terra cotta busts of prominent German figures on the second story arcade.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theater is considered one of the greatest collaborations between Adler and Sullivan and played a significant role in Chicago's cultural history, initially hosting German-language operas and later various performances and films. Its demolition in 1961 instigated large-scale preservation efforts in the city.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a theater for German-language operas and cultural events, later a venue for touring stage shows, movies, and a television studio.
world knowledge.Details: The demolition of the Garrick Theater led to significant preservation efforts. Photographer and historic preservationist Richard Nickel salvaged hundreds of artifacts and ornaments from the building and recorded extensive notes, diagrams, and photographs of the structure.

world knowledge.Name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum
world knowledge.Address: Veer Mata Jijabai Bhonsle Udyan, Dr. Baba Saheb Ambedkar Marg, Byculla East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400027.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum, originally established in 1855 as a treasure house of the decorative and industrial arts, is the oldest museum in Mumbai. It was renamed in honour of Bhau Daji Lad, a philanthropist, historian, physician, and surgeon. The museum was initially known as The Victoria and Albert Museum, Bombay, and was opened on 2 May 1872. It was renamed on 1 November 1975. The museum's establishment was influenced by the Great Exhibition of 1851 in London, which aimed to showcase industrial arts and crafts from British colonies. The museum underwent extensive refurbishment in 2003 and reopened in 2008.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as The Victoria and Albert Museum, Bombay
Major_Events.Description: The museum was opened to the public on 2 May 1872.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming to Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum was renamed in honour of Bhau Daji Lad on 1 November 1975.
After extensive refurbishment, the museum reopened to the public on 4 January 2008.

Major_Events.Event: UNESCO's Asia-Pacific Award of Excellence in Cultural Conservation
Major_Events.Description: The museum won this award after being restored by conservation architect Vikas Dilawari.
The museum received this award in the gold category for its focus on quality, continuous innovation, and customer satisfaction.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum building, constructed between 1862 and 1871, features Victorian architecture. It was built with the patronage of wealthy Indian businessmen and philanthropists.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum is culturally significant as it preserves and showcases the decorative and industrial arts of Mumbai and the broader region. It houses a large number of archaeological finds, historical photographs, clay models, silver and copper ware, and costumes. The museum also plays a role in the cultural conservation and heritage of Mumbai.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is managed by a public-private partnership involving the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation, and the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH). It houses significant collections, including a 17th-century manuscript of Hatim Tai and the iconic Kala Ghoda statue. Outside the museum is a monolithic basalt elephant sculpture from Elephanta Island.

world knowledge.Name: Delta State University, Abraka
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Delta State University, Abraka started as a Government Teachers’ Training College during the colonial era and some years into the post-colonial era. It became a College of Education that was awarded the Nigerian Certificate of Education (N.C.E.) from 1971 to 1985. In 1981, it was affiliated to the University of Benin, Benin City and consequently offered degree programmes from 1981 till 1985 when it became the Faculty of Education of the then Bendel State University with its main campus at Ekpoma. The creation of Edo and Delta State in August 1991 and the conversion of the main campus of the then Bendel State University, Ekpoma to become Edo State University in December 1991, necessitated the establishment of an autonomous Delta State University, Abraka on 30 April 1992 by the then Executive Governor of the State, Olorogun Felix Ibru.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as a Government Teachers’ Training College
Major_Events.Description: Started as a Government Teachers’ Training College during the colonial era.
Affiliated to the University of Benin, Benin City and offered degree programmes.
Established as an autonomous Delta State University, Abraka on 30 April 1992.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Delta State University, Abraka is a center of education and has evolved from a Teachers’ Training College to a full-fledged university, contributing significantly to the educational development in Nigeria.
world knowledge.Details: The university has a main campus in Abraka and a sub-campus in Oleh. It offers a range of programmes from certificate to doctoral level, and has facilities such as a staff/student counselling centre, e-learning centre, student accommodation, and sporting facilities. The university also conducted the first ever solely online Students’ Union Government election in Nigeria.

world knowledge.Name: Vilnius Cathedral
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral Basilica of St Stanislaus and St Ladislaus of Vilnius, also known as Vilnius Cathedral, is the main Catholic cathedral in Lithuania. It is situated in Vilnius Old Town, just off Cathedral Square. Dedicated to the Christian saints Stanislaus and Ladislaus, the church is the heart of Catholic spiritual life in Lithuania. The cathedral was previously used for the inauguration ceremonies of Lithuanian monarchs with Gediminas' Cap, while in modern times it is a venue for masses dedicated to the elected Presidents of Lithuania after their inauguration ceremonies and giving of oaths to the Nation in the Seimas Palace.

Major_Events.Description: The Crown Prince and future King of Poland, Sigismund II Augustus, was crowned Grand Duke of Lithuania in the cathedral.
After the southern tower collapsed in 1769, Bishop of Vilnius Ignacy Jakub Massalski ordered the reconstruction of the cathedral, which was completed in 1783.
During the Soviet occupation, the cathedral was converted into a warehouse. Its status as a cathedral was restored in 1989.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a mix of Gothic, Baroque, and Neoclassical styles. It was reconstructed in the Neoclassical style by Laurynas Gucevičius, with a strict quadrangular shape common to local public buildings. The main facade is adorned with sculptures of the Four Evangelists by Italian sculptor Tommaso Righi. The cathedral also includes elements of Palladian architecture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The cathedral is the heart of Catholic spiritual life in Lithuania and has been a site of significant historical events, including the coronations of Lithuanian monarchs. It symbolizes the Christianization of Lithuania and the country's historical ties with Poland.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral contains more than forty works of art dating from the 16th through 19th centuries, including frescoes and paintings of various sizes. During restoration, the altars of a presumed pagan temple and the original floor, laid during the reign of King Mindaugas, were uncovered. The remains of the cathedral built in 1387 were also located. A fresco dating from the end of the 14th century, the oldest known fresco in Lithuania, was found on the wall of one of the cathedral's underground chapels.

world knowledge.Name: Sapara Monastery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sapara Monastery has existed from at least the 9th century and has been significant in Georgian ecclesiastical history. It became a possession of the Jakeli family at the end of the 13th century. The monastery was deserted from the end of the 16th century to the beginning of the 17th century due to Ottoman expansion.

Major_Events.Description: Sapara Monastery became a possession of the Jakeli family, whose leader, Sargis Jakeli, maintained peace with the Mongols.
Beka Jakeli built St. Saba's Church, one of the most architecturally important churches of its time.

Major_Events.Year: End of 16th century to beginning of 17th century
Major_Events.Description: The monastery was deserted, and its icons and treasures were taken to safer areas of Georgia.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The monastery is composed of church buildings, remnants of a palace, and fortification walls. The cross-in-square temple of St. Saba and St. Mary's Assumption Church are significant. The ensemble features pink and yellow stones, rich frescoes, and intricate exterior decorations.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sapara Monastery is a key site in Georgian ecclesiastical history and architecture, housing important frescoes and serving as a center for religious and cultural activities.
world knowledge.Details: The monastery is set in a green forested canyon and includes the oldest bell tower built in Georgia. The church interiors are adorned with 14th-century frescoes, and the exterior features polychromatic cladding and ornate window decorations.

world knowledge.Name: Croatian National Theatre, Osijek
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Croatian National Theatre in Osijek, opened in 1866, was expanded and fully completed in 1907 according to the plans of its local architect, Karlo Klausner. Designed in baroque style, it was damaged by the JNA during the Croatian War of Independence in the 1990s and has been extensively restored. The theatre was officially re-opened by then-President of Croatia, Franjo Tuđman in December 1994. The theatre has a rich history of performances dating back to the 18th century, with influences from German and Hungarian theater traditions.

Major_Events.Description: The Croatian National Theatre in Osijek was officially opened.
The theatre building was fully completed according to the plans of architect Karlo Klausner.

Major_Events.Event: Damage during Croatian War of Independence
Major_Events.Description: The theatre was damaged by the JNA during the Croatian War of Independence.
The theatre was officially re-opened by then-President of Croatia, Franjo Tuđman after extensive restoration.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in baroque style, the theatre features a baroque exterior.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Croatian National Theatre in Osijek is culturally significant as a historic venue for performances and as a symbol of resilience, having been restored after damage during the Croatian War of Independence. It reflects the rich theatrical traditions of the region, influenced by German and Hungarian elements.
world knowledge.Details: A McDonald's restaurant occupies the street-front area of the theatre. The theatre has a documented history of performances dating back to the 18th century, with influences from German and Hungarian theater traditions.

world knowledge.Name: University of Luhansk
world knowledge.Location: Poltava and Myrhorod and Lubny, Ukraine 48°33′54″N 39°19′00″E
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Luhansk, officially the Taras Shevchenko National University of Luhansk, is the oldest university in the Donbas region and has a reputation as one of Ukraine's most prestigious universities. It was established in 1921 as the Teachers' Training Institute by the Soviet authorities. Following the 2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine and the establishment of the Luhansk People's Republic (LPR), the university was partitioned into two institutions. One continues to operate in Luhansk, renamed the Luhansk State Pedagogical University in 2020, while the other was relocated to Ukraine-controlled areas, eventually settling in Poltava, Myrhorod, and Lubny due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Major_Events.Description: Following the 2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine and the establishment of the Luhansk People's Republic (LPR), the University of Luhansk was partitioned into two universities. One continued to operate in Luhansk, while the other was forcibly relocated to Ukraine-controlled areas.
Due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the relocated University of Luhansk was moved from Starobilsk to Poltava, Myrhorod, and Lubny.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Luhansk is culturally significant as the oldest university in the Donbas region and one of Ukraine's most prestigious universities. It is named after Taras Shevchenko, a prominent figure in Ukrainian literature and culture.
world knowledge.Details: The university participates in international projects, such as an MBA joint program with Franklin Pierce University. It is affiliated with the European University Association (EUA) and the International Association of Universities (IAU).

world knowledge.Name: Luoyang Museum
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 20,000 square metres (220,000 sq ft) with a floor space of 10,000 square metres (110,000 sq ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Luoyang Museum is a historical museum in Luoyang, Henan Province, China. It was first built in 1958 in Guanlin, seven kilometres south of Luoyang City, and was moved to the north side of Zhongzhou Road in 1973 near Wangcheng Park. The new museum opened on May 1, 1974. It houses relics from excavation sites on the outskirts of Luoyang, representing elements of the ancient city of nine capitals, from Neolithic times up to 937 AD.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was first built in Guanlin, seven kilometres south of Luoyang City.
The museum was moved to the north side of Zhongzhou Road near Wangcheng Park and reopened on May 1, 1974.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in ancient Tang dynasty Chinese architectural style, with an Eastern Han dynasty painting of the "hundred-flower" lantern displayed on the front facade. It has four display halls and five exhibition rooms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum offers exhibits of the rich cultural heritage of Luoyang, a major Chinese cultural centre and former capital of several Chinese dynasties including the Eastern Zhou and the Eastern Han. It houses relics that establish the historical past of Luoyang, representing elements of the ancient city of nine capitals.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Museum showcasing historical and cultural relics, research, and training centre.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include antiquaries from palaces and temples, arranged to demonstrate the evolution of social structure and ancient cultures. Major permanent exhibits are the Historical and Cultural Relics of Luoyang and the Selected Cultural Relics of Luoyang. Travelling collections are located in Japan, Germany, France, Singapore, and South Korea. Exhibits include bronze, pottery, porcelain, gold, silver, jade, and stone wares, as well as Ming and Qing dynasty articles like calligraphic works and paintings. Notable pieces include items excavated at Erlitou, a winged bronze figure with gold inlay from the Eastern Han dynasty, and relics from the Yongning Temple.

world knowledge.Name: Rouken Glen Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rouken Glen Park is a public park in East Renfrewshire, to the south-west of Glasgow, Scotland. The lands originally belonged to the Scottish Crown, and then to the Earl of Eglinton. It was gifted to the citizens of Glasgow by Archibald Cameron Corbett, M.P. for Tradeston, Glasgow (later Lord Rowallan) and officially opened on 25 May 1906. The park features a waterfall, a boating pond, and a walled garden.

Major_Events.Description: Rouken Glen Park won the UK's Best Park as voted by YOU! 2016 Award at the Fields in Trust awards ceremony on 30 November 2016, coming top in a public vote from 214 nominated parks across the UK.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park has many typical features of an Edwardian urban park, including a boating pond, a large waterfall, and a walled garden. The waterfall is based on a natural waterfall, doubled in height to form a reservoir.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it was gifted to the citizens of Glasgow and has been a popular public space since its opening. It has also been featured in films and TV series, including 'Trainspotting' and 'Rab C. Nesbitt'.
world knowledge.Details: The park features a 16th-century circular dovecote and a golf course to the south. The pondside cafeteria, 'Boaters', was featured in an episode of the BBC Scotland drama series 'Sea of Souls'.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Case–Espérance Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grand Case–Espérance Airport, also known as Grand Case Airport, is a public use airport located in Grand Case, on the French side of the Caribbean island of Saint Martin. It is the second and smaller airport of Saint Maarten, after Princess Juliana International Airport (SXM) which is located on the Dutch side of the island.

Major_Events.Description: The renovation included a modernized terminal building, fire station upgrade, extended parking apron, and new control tower.
A new hangar for line maintenance purposes was completed.

Major_Events.Event: Franco-Dutch treaty on Saint Martin border controls
Major_Events.Description: The treaty allows for joint Franco-Dutch border controls on so-called "risk flights". It was signed in 1994, ratified in November 2006, and entered into force on 1 August 2007.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a modernized terminal building, fire station, extended parking apron, and a new control tower. The runway is 1,200 meters long with an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is significant for its role in regional transportation, facilitating quick transfers for commercial inter-island aircraft and private aircraft. It also plays a part in the joint Franco-Dutch border controls established by the 1994 treaty.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is managed by EDEIS, a major player in airport operations and engineering in France. It targets more than 200,000 passenger movements a year. The air traffic control tower at Princess Juliana Airport on the Dutch side of St. Maarten manages airspace around the airport, including approach control for Grand Case airport. Larger aircraft, such as the ATR 72-500, powerback after lining up on the runway for departure due to the short runway.

world knowledge.Name: Gadjah Mada University
world knowledge.Location: 7°46′10″S 110°22′44″E, Sleman Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Gadjah Mada University (UGM) is a public research university located in Sleman, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Officially founded on 19 December 1949, UGM is one of the oldest and largest institutions of higher education in the country. It was the first state university in Indonesia, established during a period when Indonesia was facing threats from the Netherlands. The university was named after Gajah Mada, the leader of the Majapahit Empire of Java in the 14th century, who is considered to be the nation's first unifier by some historians.

Major_Events.Description: UGM was established through Government Regulation (PP) No. 23 of 1949, regarding the merger of colleges to form a university. The inauguration took place on 19 December 1949, intentionally chosen to coincide with the anniversary of the Dutch invasion of Yogyakarta.
UGM's chemistry undergraduate program received accreditation from the Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) in the United Kingdom, the first international accreditation ever received by the university.
More than 1000 of UGM's students and staff demonstrated against high tuition fees and the university's status as a 'state university with corporation status'.
A female student alleged that she was raped by a male fellow student during a student work experience program. The case was resolved internally by the university without involving law enforcement.
Students held a demonstration at UGM's rectorate building criticizing the high tuition fees that didn't match the students' financial capabilities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The UGM main building is called the Balairung, a rectorate building in Sleman. Nearby is the Grha Sabha Pramana, a large building utilized for graduation ceremonies, with an adjoining square used for sport and recreation. The campus also includes a university library, sports center, and the UGM Campus Mosque, which was designed by the students of the UGM Architecture Engineering department.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UGM is culturally significant as it is named after Gajah Mada, a historical figure who is considered to be the nation's first unifier. The university has played a pivotal role in the development of higher education in Indonesia and has been a center for academic excellence and research.
world knowledge.Details: UGM comprises 18 faculties and 27 research centers, offering 68 undergraduate, 23 diplomas, 104 master's and specialist, 43 doctorates, and 4 clusters of post-doctoral study programs. The university has enrolled approximately 55,000 students, including 1,187 foreign students, and has 2,500 faculty members. UGM maintains a campus of 360 acres with facilities that include a stadium and a fitness center. The university is ranked 2nd in Indonesia and 263rd in the world in the 2024 QS World University Rankings.

world knowledge.Name: Réserve Africaine de Sigean
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Réserve Africaine de Sigean is a 300-hectare zoo that opened in 1974 in Sigean, Aude, in the south of France. It was founded by Jean-Jacques Boisard and is home to approximately 3,800 animals representing about 160 species.

Major_Events.Description: The Réserve Africaine de Sigean officially opened to the public on April 8, 1974.

Major_Events.Event: First hatching of a North African ostrich in France
Major_Events.Description: The zoo announced the first hatching of a North African ostrich in France, which was also the first naturally hatched individual of this Critically Endangered subspecies in Europe.
A large aviary spanning 1 hectare was built to house various bird species.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Territoire des Carnivores
Major_Events.Description: A new section dedicated to carnivores, including Southeast African cheetahs and African wild dogs, was opened.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo features spacious and naturalistic enclosures designed to mimic the animals' natural habitats, with Mediterranean vegetation. The area is divided into eight parks representing different ecosystems such as scrubland, bush, predator enclosures, and savanna. There are also specialized areas like the Grande Volière (aviary) and the Territoire des Carnivores.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Réserve Africaine de Sigean is significant for its conservation efforts, participating in 47 breeding programs and coordinating the EAZA Ex situ Programme (EEP) for Hartmann's mountain zebras. It is also a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) and the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA).
world knowledge.Details: The zoo allows visitors to drive through different exhibits in their own vehicles or on guided tours. It houses a wide variety of species, including ungulates, birds, primates, and reptiles. Notable animals include reticulated giraffes, Hartmann's mountain zebras, African wild dogs, and various bird species in the Grande Volière. The zoo also features a tropical vivarium with reptiles and amphibians. Additionally, it has a large colony of flamingos and pelicans around the lakeshore.

world knowledge.Name: Jingshan Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jingshan Park is an imperial park covering 23 hectares immediately north of the Forbidden City in Beijing. Its history dates to the Liao and Jin dynasties, almost a thousand years ago. The artificial hill was constructed in the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty from soil excavated from the moats of the Imperial Palace and nearby canals. The park was opened to the public in 1928 and formally established in 1949.

Major_Events.Description: The last ruler of the Ming dynasty committed suicide by hanging himself from a tree in Jingshan after Beijing fell to rebel forces.
The grounds were opened to the public after being a private imperial garden.
The park was formally established as a public park.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a 45.7-meter high artificial hill with five individual peaks, each topped by an elaborate pavilion. The hill was constructed manually from excavated soil. The park's layout follows feng shui principles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jingshan Park is culturally significant as a former imperial garden, a historical axis of central Beijing, and a popular gathering place for cultural activities. It is also known for its feng shui importance and the historical event of the Chongzhen Emperor's suicide.
world knowledge.Details: The park has four entrances (only three open to the public) and is accessible by multiple bus routes. It is a popular place for elderly folks to engage in cultural activities like dancing and singing opera. The park is listed as a Key State Park and is separated from the Forbidden City by a moat.

world knowledge.Name: Michigan's Adventure
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Michigan's Adventure was founded as Deer Park in 1956 by L.R. Beardsley, Dr. E.S. Gillam, Hardin Dey, and Martin Kasichke. It originally featured a petting zoo and children's area. The park evolved over the decades, adding numerous rides and attractions, and underwent ownership changes from Cedar Fair to Six Flags in 2024.

Major_Events.Description: The park introduced WildWater Adventure to compete with a popular waterpark in Norton Shores. It originally featured eight water slides, a wave pool, a children's play area, and a lazy river.
Shivering Timbers, a wooden roller coaster, opened and was quickly considered one of the world's best wooden roller coasters.
Cedar Fair purchased Michigan's Adventure for $28,000,000, marking a significant ownership change.
Thunderhawk, Michigan's first suspended looping coaster, was moved from Geauga Lake and opened at Michigan's Adventure.
A merger of equals between Cedar Fair and Six Flags was completed, creating Six Flags Entertainment Corporation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a mix of amusement rides, water attractions, and themed areas. Notable structures include wooden and steel roller coasters, water slides, and a Grand Carousel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Michigan's Adventure is the largest amusement park in the state, offering a wide range of attractions and serving as a major recreational destination for families and thrill-seekers.

world knowledge.Name: Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1959 by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden (XTBG) is a comprehensive research institution focused on biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of plant resources. It has grown to become a leading establishment for tropical biology and conservation research.

Major_Events.Description: XTBG was founded by the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Since its implementation, XTBG has published 17 monographs, 60 books, and 829 scientific papers, with 91 published in internationally peer-reviewed journals.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features 35 living collections of tropical plants, two national field research stations, and various laboratories including Biogeochemistry, Molecular Biology & Biotechnology, and Plant Phylogenetics & Conservation Biology.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: XTBG serves as a 'Noah's arc for tropical plant conservation' and is a leading establishment for tropical biology and conservation research. It plays a crucial role in biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of plant resources.
world knowledge.Details: XTBG preserves over 13,000 species of tropical plants, including over 301 families and 2110 genera. It has 338 staff members, including 164 scientific researchers and technical personnel, and collaborates with institutions in over 50 countries. The garden has accomplished over 698 scientific research projects and has been awarded 13 ministerial or provincial prizes.

world knowledge.Name: Rotterdam City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rotterdam City Hall was built between 1914 and 1920 by Henri Evers. It is one of the few buildings in the center of Rotterdam that survived the bombing of May 14, 1940. Since 10 October 2000, it has been recognized as a Rijksmonument. The first city hall stood on Hoogstraat in a 14th-century urban boarding house, but by the end of the 19th century, it could no longer accommodate municipal activities, leading to the construction of the new building.

Major_Events.Description: The building survived the bombing of May 14, 1940, although the heat from the surrounding fires damaged the structure's concrete.
The inauguration took place after the work was completed with a special session of the city council on 1 September 1920.
There were controversies regarding Henri Evers' victory in the design competition due to support for Willem Kromhout's design and the mayor's ties to Evers.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in full Beaux-Arts style with Byzantine, Romanesque, and art deco influences. Built entirely of concrete covered with porous sandstone and hard stone. The clock tower stands 71 meters high with a gold statue of an angel by sculptor Johan Keller.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the few buildings in Rotterdam's center to survive the 1940 bombing and recognized as a Rijksmonument since 2000.
world knowledge.Details: The foundation stone was laid on 15 July 1915 in the presence of Queen Wilhelmina. The construction cost NLG 2,850,000.

world knowledge.Name: San Jose Civic
world knowledge.Address: 135 W San Carlos St, San Jose, CA 95113
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The San Jose Civic was created through a joint venture between the City of San Jose, Public Works Administration, and local property owners Mr. and Mrs. T. S. Montgomery, who donated the property. It opened on July 14, 1936, and has served as a major venue for entertainment, sports, and cultural events. The venue underwent a $25 million renovation from 2009 to 2012.

Major_Events.Description: Barbra Streisand appeared at the venue during her first concert tour.

Major_Events.Event: Bob Dylan and the Hawks concert
Major_Events.Description: Bob Dylan and the Hawks played a famous show on December 12, 1965, with a tape of the event held by Stanford University Libraries.
The Rolling Stones played a concert attended by Ken Kesey and his Merry Pranksters, who reportedly electrified a party afterward with Stones members in attendance.
Richard Nixon made national headlines during an anti-war demonstration at the San Jose Civic.
The Civic hosted the final day of the GENESIS 3 Super Smash Bros. tournament in January 2016.
The venue hosted the trampoline events of the inaugural World Games I in 1981.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed in the Spanish Colonial/California Mission Revival style by Binder & Curtis.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The San Jose Civic has been a central venue for entertainment, sports, and cultural events since 1936, hosting iconic performers and historic events. It is a significant part of San Jose's cultural and social history.

Details.Former_names: San Jose Municipal Auditorium (planning/construction), San Jose Civic Auditorium (1933–2013), City National Civic (2013–19)
Details.Other_designers: National Electric Pro, Advanced Design Consultants, The Shalleck Collaborative, BBI Engineering
Details.Montgomery_Theater: Attached to the east side of the building, seating 486, primary home of CMT San Jose.

world knowledge.Name: Pulau Bunting Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The bridge was built by the Malaysian Public Works Department (JKR) with Gamuda Berhad as the main contractor. It connects Bunting Island to mainland Yan, Kedah state. The project has been widely criticized for serving no purpose while incurring a cost of RM 120 million, as Bunting Island is uninhabited.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was constructed between 2002 and 2005, but remains underused and has become a white elephant project.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is an arch cable-stayed bridge with a main suspended span of 80 m in length and approach spans of precast concrete box beams with spans of 30 m in length. The causeways have fill embankments on piled foundations with rock armouring.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a notable example of infrastructure development in Malaysia, but its underuse and high cost have made it a subject of criticism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Connecting Bunting Island to mainland Yan, Kedah state
world knowledge.Details: The bridge consists of a 1.8-kilometre-long (1.1 mi) bridge, a 0.1-kilometre-long (0.062 mi) causeway connecting Bunting Island to the bridge, and a 0.4-kilometre-long (0.25 mi) causeway connecting mainland Kedah to the bridge.

world knowledge.Name: Silver Beach Amusement Park
world knowledge.Address: Silver Beach County Park, St. Joseph, Michigan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Silver Beach opened as a resort in 1891 by local businessmen Logan Drake and Louis D. Wallace. It expanded over the years with various attractions, including roller coasters, a dance hall, and a carousel. The park faced decline in the 1960s due to crime and unrest, closing in 1971. The site was later converted into Silver Beach County Park.

Major_Events.Description: Logan Archbold Vilas became the first person to fly across Lake Michigan, flying from Silver Beach to Chicago.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of Chase through the Clouds roller coaster
Major_Events.Description: The first roller coaster at Silver Beach, later replaced by the Velvet (the Comet) in 1923.
A violent incident on July 4, 1969, contributed to the park's closure in 1971.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of new Silver Beach Carousel
Major_Events.Description: A new carousel was built near Silver Beach County Park, accompanied by exhibits and attractions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park featured various structures, including a pavilion, roller rink, dance hall (later Shadowland Ballroom), and a carousel. The design was typical of early 20th-century amusement parks with a mix of recreational and entertainment facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Silver Beach Amusement Park was a popular recreational destination, contributing to the cultural and social life of the region. It was also a site of early aviation experiments and hosted notable performers and events.
world knowledge.Details: The park's original carousel was sold to Washington State, but a new one was built in 2010. The site now includes the Silver Beach Carousel, exhibits, a Kid's Discovery Zone, the Whirlpool Compass Fountain, and the Shadowland Ballroom for events.

world knowledge.Name: Fonte Luminosa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was inaugurated in 1951 and is named after Adhemar Pereira de Barros, a former governor of São Paulo state. It is primarily used for football matches and has undergone several renovations and expansions.

Major_Events.Description: Vasco da Gama beat Ferroviária 5–0. The first goal was scored by Vasco da Gama's Friaça.
The stadium's attendance record was set at 18,041 people when Palmeiras beat Ferroviária 1–0.
The stadium lighting was inaugurated with a match between Ferroviária and Ponte Preta, which ended in a 3–3 draw.
The stadium was reopened after renovations, expanding its capacity to over 20,000. The reopening match was between Palmeiras and Santo André for the Brasileirão.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Football stadium with natural grass surface and a capacity of 20,000.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Araraquara and has hosted numerous important football matches. It is named after a prominent political figure in São Paulo's history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is owned by the Araraquara City Hall and is the home ground for Associação Ferroviária de Esportes. It has undergone expansions in 1970 and 2009, and renovations in 1992 and 2009.

world knowledge.Name: Sfax Archaeological Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sfax Archaeological Museum was established in 1907, making it the third oldest museum in Tunisia. During World War II, the museum was hit by bombings. The first exhibition room opened in 1955, and three new rooms were added in 1966.

Major_Events.Description: The museum was hit by bombings during World War II.
The first exhibition room of the museum was opened.
Three new exhibition rooms were added to the museum.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum holds the country's largest collection of blown glass and most of its collection comes from the Roman period, including mosaics, glass, pottery, and coins. It displays artifacts from significant sites like Thenae, Taparura, Louza, and Mahres.
world knowledge.Details: The museum is located in the city's town hall and is a significant repository of Roman artifacts and blown glass.

world knowledge.Name: Carmen Thyssen Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Carmen Thyssen Museum is an art museum in Málaga, Spain, focusing on 19th-century Spanish painting, predominantly Andalusian. It is based on the collection of Carmen Cervera, fifth wife of Baron Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza. The museum opened to the public on 24 March 2011, after being developed around the 16th-century Baroque Palacio de Villalón. The site has a history of continuous occupation from the 1st to the 5th century AD, with significant Roman-era remains discovered during excavations.

Major_Events.Description: The Carmen Thyssen Museum opened to the public on 24 March 2011, showcasing the personal art collection of Carmen Cervera.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was developed by RG Arquitectos Asociados around the 16th-century Baroque Palacio de Villalón, which was partly reconstructed. The exhibition spaces, including three rooms for the permanent collection and two for temporary exhibitions, were newly built next to the palace.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant for its focus on 19th-century Spanish painting and its role in displaying the personal art collection of Carmen Cervera, contributing to the preservation and promotion of Andalusian art.
world knowledge.Details: The museum covers 7,147 square metres, with 5,185 square metres used to display art. Excavations at the site have uncovered significant Roman-era remains, including a monumental fountain, geometric mosaics, ceramics, coins, and remnants of a bronze sculpture.

world knowledge.Name: Varendra Research Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Varendra Museum is the oldest museum in Bangladesh, established in 1910. It started as the collection for Varendra Anushandhan Samiti (Varendra Investigation Society) and got its current name in 1919. The museum was founded by Kumar Sarat Kumar Ray, Aksaya Kumar Maitreya, and Ramaprasad Chanda to explore the history and culture of the Varendra region. It was formally inaugurated on 27 September 1910 and registered in 1914. The museum became part of Rajshahi University in 1964.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Varendra Research Society and Museum
Major_Events.Description: The museum was established to collect, preserve, study, and research the history and culture of the Varendra region.
Excavation was started by the society along with the University of Calcutta.
The museum became a part of Rajshahi University.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's front part is a load-bearing brick wall structure with two major functions: Administration and the Library. There is a Residential Block for officers and staff. The structures are constructed with brick, and there is a garden in front of the director's residence.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Varendra Museum is culturally and historically significant as it preserves the heritage of the Varendra region, which was a flourishing territory in ancient times. It houses artefacts that provide insights into the region's history, art, and archaeology.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has historical significance and is a heritage site of Bangladesh. It demands restoration due to inadequate gallery space for preserving and displaying all the artefacts. The restoration program has begun, and an extension project is planned to protect the old museum and preserve the increasing number of artefacts.

world knowledge.Name: Coolum Beach, Queensland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Coolum Beach's name originated from the indigenous term 'gulum' or 'kulum,' meaning 'blunt' or 'headless,' in reference to Mount Coolum's shape. The district encompasses the traditional land of the 'Inabara' or 'Yinneburra' clan from the Undanbi tribe, a subset of the Kabi Kabi (or Gubbi Gubbi) group. The area saw development in the early 20th century, including the opening of Coolum Provisional School in 1917 and land auctions in the 1920s. The town grew as a beachside destination, hosting events like the 2002 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

Major_Events.Description: Coolum Provisional School opened on 2 April 1917, later becoming Coolum State School in 1930.

Major_Events.Event: Mt Coolum Beach Estate land auction
Major_Events.Description: Land in the Mt Coolum Beach Estate second section went to auction in December 1923, following the successful sale of portions in the first section and the opening of the Moreton Central Sugar Mill Cane Tramway extension to Coolum.
Coolum hosted the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, replacing the 2001 meeting that was postponed and moved from Brisbane due to the September 11 attacks.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Coolum Beach is culturally significant as a traditional land of the 'Inabara' or 'Yinneburra' clan from the Undanbi tribe. Its name and landscape are tied to Indigenous heritage. The area also represents the development of Queensland's coastal regions as holiday and residential destinations.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Beachside town and coastal suburb, popular for tourism and recreation.

Details.Nearby_Locations: 26.8 km NE of Nambour, 37.8 km N of Caloundra, 118 km N of Brisbane

Education.Coolum State School: Government primary school (Prep–6) at School Road.
Education.Coolum State High School: Government secondary school (7–12) at Havana Road East.

Transport.Bus: Kinetic Group operates local buses under contract to Translink.
Transport.Rail: Nearest railway station is Yandina Railway Station, with connections to Brisbane, Ipswich, and North Gympie.

Tourist_Attractions.Lows Lookout: Tourist attraction at the top of Grandview Drive on Toboggan Hill.
Tourist_Attractions.Beach: Patrolled beach offering swimming and surfing, surrounded by parks, a boardwalk, and shops.

world knowledge.Name: Volta Regional Museum
world knowledge.Address: 43 Glala Road, P. O. Box 43, Ho, Ghana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Volta Regional Museum is a museum in Ho, Ghana, dedicated to the history and traditions of the Volta Region. Before it was used as a museum, the building served as the Office of the Regional House of Chiefs. The building was sold to the government in 1967 and the museum was opened in 1973.

Major_Events.Description: The museum collaborated with Evangelical Presbyterian University College to hold the first memorial lecture to pay tribute to several contributors who have dedicated themselves to the study of the Ewe language.
Germany's ambassador to Ghana, Christoph Retzlaff, visited the museum and spoke about plans to rehabilitate sites in the Volta region.
Renovations were completed to the museum which was partly financed by the German government who gave 25000 euros and Ghana Museums and Monuments Board who contributed 200000 Ghanaian cedi.
An event on tourism development in the region was organized by Tourism Aid Ghana at the museum.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally and historically important as it showcases the ethnography of the Volta Region, including collections of handicrafts, contemporary art, and artifacts from the periods of German Togoland and British colonization.
world knowledge.Details: Exhibits on display at the museum include the Chair of State of the last German colonial governor, woodcraft, pottery, Kente textiles, masks and Asante shrines. The museum also has several collections of cultural artifacts including swords, stone relics, musical instruments such as drums, maps of the Ewe State, stools and earthenware cooking vessels. In addition, the museum contains paintings and sculptures by artists from the Volta region.

world knowledge.Name: Kigoma Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kigoma Airport is an airport in western Tanzania serving Kigoma. It is located at the east area of Ujiji. The government of Tanzania is planning to improve the airport. The Kigoma non-directional beacon (Ident: KG) is located on the field. Ground handling at the airport is conducted by the Livingstone Aviation Services Limited.
world knowledge.Details: Kigoma Airport (IATA: TKQ, ICAO: HTKA) is a public airport owned by the Government of Tanzania and operated by the Tanzania Airports Authority. It serves the city of Kigoma and has an elevation of 2,700 ft / 823 m. The airport features a runway with direction 15/33, length 1,805 m / 5,922 ft, and an asphalt surface. In a given period, it handled 28,454 passengers, 1,725 aircraft movements, and 40,350 kg of cargo. More information can be found on the official website: www.taa.go.tz.

world knowledge.Name: Rathtrevor Beach Provincial Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rathtrevor Beach Provincial Park was established on April 20, 1967. The park takes its name from the Rath family who homesteaded on the land in the late 19th century. The family established a private campground on the site, adding 'trevor' to give it a more romantic name. In 1967, the campground became a provincial park. The park has historical connections to Wells Gray Provincial Park due to a controversial land swap deal in the 1960s involving timber rights.

Major_Events.Event: Land swap deal with Clearwater Timber Products
Major_Events.Description: The Social Credit Government passed an order-in-council allowing the government to receive 47 hectares of Rathtrevor Beach in exchange for timber rights in 137 square km of southwestern Wells Gray Park. The deal was controversial due to the low stumpage fees and alleged government interference.

Major_Events.Event: Cancellation of the Clearwater Timber arrangement
Major_Events.Description: The New Democratic Party government cancelled the arrangement with Clearwater Timber, and the access road to the Flourmill Volcanoes logging area was permanently closed by demolishing the Mahood River bridge.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rathtrevor Beach Provincial Park is culturally significant as a popular recreational area and an important stopover for migratory birds, notably brant geese. It also has historical significance due to its connection to the Rath family and the controversial land swap deal in the 1960s.
world knowledge.Details: The park features a two-kilometre long stretch of sandy beach, a stand of old-growth Douglas fir trees, and 250 vehicle-accessible and 25 walk-in camping spaces. It is an important stopover area for migratory birds and is home to various wildlife such as deer, raccoons, minks, squirrels, and otters. The park also houses the Rathtrevor Beach Nature House, which offers natural history displays and environmental education programs.

world knowledge.Name: Parliament House, New Delhi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Parliament House in New Delhi is the seat of the Parliament of India, housing the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The Old Parliament House was constructed in 1927, but due to ageing and space constraints, proposals for a new building emerged in the 2010s. The new building was constructed as part of the Central Vista Redevelopment Project and was inaugurated on 28 May 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The groundbreaking ceremony for the new Parliament House was held on 1 October 2020.
The foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 10 December 2020, following an interfaith prayer service.
The new Parliament House was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 28 May 2023, with a homam and an all-religious prayer ceremony.
The building was first used for official business on 19 September 2023 during a special session of the parliament.
On 13 December 2023, two intruders entered the Lok Sabha chamber and threw smoke bombs, leading to a security probe and changes in visitor rules.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The new Parliament House is triangular in shape, spans four floors, and covers an area of 64,500 m². It is designed to be earthquake-resistant and has a lifespan of over 150 years. The building features three gates (Gyan Dwar, Shakti Dwar, Karma Dwar) and six entrances named after mythological creatures. The Lok Sabha chamber is themed on a peacock with a seating capacity of 888, while the Rajya Sabha chamber is lotus-themed with 384 seats. The building also includes a central Grand Constitution Hall, a banyan tree in the open sky area, and a 6.5 m high national emblem sculpture.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Parliament House is a symbol of India's democracy and governance. It represents the country's bicameral legislature and is a central administrative landmark. The building's design incorporates national symbols and themes, reflecting India's cultural heritage. The inclusion of crafts from artisans across the country and the installation of the Sengol (a historic sceptre) highlight its cultural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the Parliament of India, housing the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
world knowledge.Details: The new Parliament House was designed by architect Bimal Patel and constructed by Tata Projects. Materials were sourced from across India, including sandstone from Rajasthan, teak wood from Maharashtra, and carpets from Uttar Pradesh. The building features a Foucault pendulum, statues of leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Chanakya, and a crafts gallery with themes representing Indian culture. The mural depicting the Maurya Empire's map sparked diplomatic reactions from Nepal, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. The building was completed on 20 May 2023 and opened for official use on 19 September 2023.

world knowledge.Name: Museum aan de Stroom
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Museum aan de Stroom (MAS) was established to consolidate collections from various museums in Antwerp, including the Ethnographic Museum and the Maritime Museum, which ceased to exist. The museum was built on the site of the former Hanzahuis, which was destroyed by fire in the 19th century. The MAS opened to the public on May 17, 2011, and has since become the largest museum in Antwerp.

Major_Events.Description: On September 14, 2006, the first brick of the MAS building was laid, marking the beginning of its construction.
The MAS officially opened to the public on May 17, 2011, showcasing its extensive collection and innovative exhibits.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The MAS is a 60-meter-high building designed by Neutelings Riedijk Architects. It features a façade made of Indian red sandstone and curved glass panels, exemplifying postmodern Art Deco architecture. The building includes a 'visible store' that displays 180,000 items from its collection.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The MAS is culturally significant as it highlights Antwerp's connection to the world through its diverse collections, which include maritime objects, local history, and global art and culture. It also engages the community through initiatives like MAS IN YOUNG HANDS, which involves young people in curating and organizing events.
world knowledge.Details: The MAS houses 470,000 objects, with a focus on themes that connect local and global culture, art, and history. It is recognized for its innovative use of new media and immersive presentations to educate the public.

world knowledge.Name: Leicester Museum & Art Gallery
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Leicester Museum & Art Gallery, originally known as New Walk Museum and Art Gallery, opened in 1849 as one of the first public museums in the United Kingdom. It was designed by Joseph Hansom, the designer of the hansom cab. The museum has been expanded several times, most recently in 2011, and houses a variety of exhibits including science, history, and art.

Major_Events.Description: The museum expanded its Dinosaur Gallery, reorganizing fossils, adding a new room, and modifying the gallery itself. The new gallery predominantly features extinct marine reptiles and was opened by David Attenborough.

The museum was relaunched under a new name, Leicester Museum & Art Gallery, after a lengthy closure due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The new name was chosen to emphasize its status as Leicester's leading museum and to improve online searchability.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The original building was designed by Joseph Hansom, known for designing the hansom cab. The museum has undergone several expansions, with the most recent in 2011.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as one of the first public museums in the UK. It houses important collections including the first Charnia fossil, a significant collection of extinct lifeforms, and the UK's largest collection of German Expressionist art. It also holds a notable Egyptology exhibit with four Egyptian mummies.
world knowledge.Details: The museum contains permanent exhibits on dinosaurs, Egyptology, and local minerals. It also features a collection of taxidermy animals, including a stuffed polar bear named Peppy, the mascot of Fox's Glacier Mints. The museum holds the UK's largest collection of German Expressionist art, including works by George Grosz, Wassily Kandinsky, and Paul Klee. In 2007, over 100 pieces of Picasso ceramic art donated by Richard Attenborough were displayed. The museum also hosts temporary exhibitions, such as a display on the search for the remains of Richard III and a Wallace and Gromit display.

world knowledge.Name: Everest base camps
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Everest base camps are rudimentary campsites at the base of Mount Everest used by climbers during their ascent and descent. There are two base camps: South Base Camp in Nepal and North Base Camp in Tibet. The camps serve as starting points for climbers attempting to summit Everest via different routes.

Major_Events.Description: An earthquake measuring 7.8 on the moment magnitude scale struck Nepal, triggering an avalanche on Pumori that swept through the South Base Camp, killing at least 19 people.
A second quake measuring 7.3 on the moment magnitude scale struck Nepal, causing further damage to trails leading to Everest Base Camp.
The South Base Camp was announced to be moved 200 to 400 metres lower due to the rapid melting and thinning of the Khumbu Glacier, making it unsafe for trekkers.

A new signboard was unveiled at Everest Base Camp in March 2024, sparking reactions from trekkers and mountaineers. It was removed in May 2024, with authorities stating plans to reinstate it with additional information and protection.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rudimentary campsites with basic facilities such as a field hospital and heliport.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Everest base camps are iconic starting points for climbers attempting to summit Mount Everest, the world's highest peak. They hold cultural significance for the Sherpa community and are a symbol of human endurance and adventure.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serving as base camps for climbers and trekkers attempting to summit or visit Mount Everest.

South_Base_Camp.Access: Supplies are shipped by porters and yaks. Trekkers typically fly from Kathmandu to Lukla and then trek to the base camp.

North_Base_Camp.Access: Accessed by a paved road branching from China National Highway 318. A permit from the Government of China is required, and tourists must take horse-drawn carriages or small buses for the last stretch.

Details.Trekking_Route: The Everest Base Camp trek on the south side is one of the most popular trekking routes in the Himalayas, attracting about 40,000 people per year. The trek involves stops at Namche Bazaar and Dingboche for acclimatization.

world knowledge.Name: Oaxaca Ethnobotanical Garden
world knowledge.Address: Adjacent to the Church of Santo Domingo, Oaxaca City, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jardín Etnobotánico de Oaxaca was proposed in 1993 by Francisco Toledo, a renowned artist from Oaxaca, and the civil association PRO-OAX. Toledo aimed to preserve and promote the traditional knowledge of the Zapotec and Mixtec peoples. The garden was designed in collaboration with anthropologist Alejandro de Ávila Blomberg and showcases the rich diversity of plant species used by indigenous communities for food, medicine, and cultural practices.

Major_Events.Event: Proposal for the creation of the Ethnobotanical Garden
Major_Events.Description: Francisco Toledo and PRO-OAX proposed the creation of the garden to preserve and promote the traditional knowledge of the Zapotec and Mixtec peoples.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden includes an herbarium, a library, and a laboratory for the study of ethnobotany. It is designed to showcase the rich biodiversity of the region and the importance of plants to the local communities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The garden is culturally significant as it preserves and promotes the traditional knowledge of the Zapotec and Mixtec peoples, showcasing the rich diversity of plant species used by these communities for food, medicine, and cultural practices.
world knowledge.Details: The garden is administered by the state government of Oaxaca and is located adjacent to the Church of Santo Domingo. It was part of a larger effort to prevent the conversion of the former Convent of Santo Domingo de Guzmán into a parking lot, turning it into the current Santo Domingo Cultural Center.

world knowledge.Name: William H. Natcher Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 4,505 feet (1,373 m) in length, 67 feet (20 m) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The William H. Natcher Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge that carries U.S. Highway 231 over the Ohio River. It was named in honor of William Huston Natcher, a former United States Representative who served Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District from 1954 until his death in 1994. The concept for the bridge dates back to 1987, and construction began in the late 1990s after numerous funding delays. The bridge was completed and opened to traffic on October 21, 2002.

Major_Events.Description: Construction on the bridge itself began after the concrete piers were installed in 1995.
The bridge was dedicated on August 16, 2002, but did not open to traffic until October 21, 2002.
The U.S. 231 connection to I-64 in Indiana fully opened to traffic on March 15, 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a cable-stayed bridge supported by cables connected to two identical diamond-shaped towers, each 374 feet (114 m) tall. It was the United States' longest cable-supported bridge over an inland waterway at the time of its construction.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is named in honor of William Huston Natcher, a long-serving U.S. Representative, and serves as a vital transportation link between Kentucky and Indiana, relieving traffic congestion and improving regional connectivity.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: To carry U.S. Highway 231 over the Ohio River, relieving traffic congestion on the aging Owensboro Bridge and improving regional transportation infrastructure.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was constructed at a cost of US$70 million (approximately $40 million from federal sources, $30 million from state sources). It was designed by Parsons, Brinckerhoff, Quade & Douglas, Inc. and built by Traylor Brothers of Evansville. The bridge is owned by the Commonwealth of Kentucky and was commissioned by the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, in cooperation with the Indiana Department of Transportation and the Federal Highway Administration.

world knowledge.Name: Holloways Beach, Queensland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Holloways Beach is situated in the traditional Djabugay (Tjapukai) Aboriginal country. Richard Holloway came to Cairns in 1910 and was farming in the area in 1926. The area was officially named Holloway in 1951 by the Queensland Surveyor-General, renamed Holloway Beach in 1971 and then Holloways Beach in 1981. In 2002, the area was gazetted as a suburb of Cairns rather than as a rural locality.

Major_Events.Description: Land was acquired in October 1951 for a school.
In December 1951, a school bus service was established to take the students to Cairns Intermediate School and Cairns North State School.
Holloway's Beach State School opened on 23 May 1955.
Holloway's Beach State School closed on 13 June 1966.

Major_Events.Event: Gazetted as a suburb of Cairns
Major_Events.Description: In 2002, the area was gazetted as a suburb of Cairns rather than as a rural locality.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Holloways Beach is situated in the traditional Djabugay (Tjapukai) Aboriginal country and has historical significance related to its development and naming.

Beach_Features.Erosion: Heavy erosion since ca. 2020, with investments in rock groynes and sand nourishment

Education.Current_Schools: Machans Beach State School or other schools further away

Amenities.Shopping: Convenience store on Holloways Beach Road, closest major shopping centre in Smithfield
Amenities.Community_Hall: Capable of seating up to 80 people
Amenities.Boat_Ramp: Managed by Cairns Regional Council, with warning signs about crocodiles

Emergency_Services.SES_Group: Meets at Syd and Jane Granville Memorial Park in Cassia Street

world knowledge.Name: Mississauga
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1805 (as Toronto Township), 1968 (as Town of Mississauga), 1974 (as City of Mississauga)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mississauga is situated on the traditional territory of the Huron-Wendat, Haudenosaunee, and Anishinaabeg people. It was founded in 1805 as Toronto Township and became part of Peel County in 1851. The city was established in 1968 as a town and reincorporated as a city in 1974. The name Mississauga comes from the Anishinaabe word Misi-zaagiing, meaning '[those at the] Great River-mouth'.

Major_Events.Event: Incorporation as the City of Mississauga
Major_Events.Description: Mississauga was reincorporated as a city, amalgamating Port Credit and Streetsville.
A freight train derailment caused the evacuation of 218,000 people due to the risk of chlorine gas exposure.
The Mississaugas and the federal government settled a land claim, with the band receiving $145,000,000 as compensation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Mississauga is a modern city with a mix of suburban and urban architecture, featuring high-rise buildings in the City Centre, residential neighborhoods, and industrial areas. The city's development was influenced by its proximity to Toronto and its role as a suburban hub.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mississauga is a multicultural city with a diverse population. It hosts numerous cultural festivals, including Carassauga, the second-largest cultural festival in Canada. The city is also home to significant Indigenous history and landmarks.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Residential, commercial, and industrial hub in the Greater Toronto Area.

Details.Climate: Humid continental climate (Dfa/Dfb) with moderate summers and cold winters.
Details.Economy: Home to over 60 Fortune 500 companies, with strong industries in pharmaceuticals, banking, finance, electronics, and aerospace.
Details.Transportation: Served by major highways (401, 403, QEW), Pearson International Airport, GO Transit, and MiWay public transit.
Details.Education: Hosts the University of Toronto Mississauga and Sheridan College.
Details.Recreation: Over 481 parks, 100 km of trails, and numerous cultural and sports events.

world knowledge.Name: Zhangye National Geopark
world knowledge.Area: Linze County and Sunan County, Gansu, China
world knowledge.Address: Linze County and Sunan County, Gansu, China
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Zhangye National Geopark is known for its colorful rock formations, which are the result of deposits of sandstone and other minerals that occurred over 24 million years. The formations were tilted by tectonic activity and sculpted by wind, rain, and time into extraordinary shapes.
