The park was established as a provincial geopark in 2005 and later designated as a national geopark in 2016. It became a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2019.

Major_Events.Description: Zhangye Danxia was established as a provincial geopark on 27 December 2005.
The site became a quasi-national geopark on 23 April 2012 under the provisional name Zhangye Danxia Geopark.
The park was formally designated as Zhangye National Geopark by the Ministry of Land and Resources on 16 June 2016 after passing an on-site acceptance test.
The Binggou scenic area was officially inaugurated on 3 August 2014.
The park was designated as a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features colorful rock formations, including towers, pillars, and ravines, with varying colors, patterns, and sizes. The formations are smooth, sharp, and several hundred meters tall, resulting from millions of years of mineral deposits and erosion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Zhangye Danxia is considered one of China's most beautiful landforms, voted by Chinese media and National Geography magazine. It is a top tourist attraction and showcases the natural beauty and geological history of the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Tourism and conservation of geological heritage
world knowledge.Details: The park includes several scenic areas: Linze Danxia Scenic Area (most developed and visited), Binggou (inaugurated in 2014), and Sunan Danxia Scenic Area. Boardwalks and access roads have been built to facilitate visitor exploration. In 2014, 100 million yuan was invested to improve facilities in the Binggou area.

world knowledge.Name: St. Johns Twin Cinema
world knowledge.Address: 8704 N Lombard St Portland, Oregon United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally opened in 1913 by the People's Amusement Company in the then-city of St. Johns, which was annexed by Portland in 1915. The theater underwent renovations in 1983 and 2004.

Major_Events.Description: The St. Johns City Council enacted a censorship ordinance for films, supported by the theater managers.

Major_Events.Event: Town hall event for St. Johns Bridge
Major_Events.Description: The theater hosted a town hall event discussing the proposition of the St. Johns Bridge, completed in 1931.
A fire occurred in an apartment above the theater due to a firecracker thrown into a waste basket.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Concrete 2+1⁄2-story building with a 650-seat auditorium initially, later modified to 350 seats on the main floor and 225 seats upstairs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of the oldest movie theaters in Portland, reflecting the cultural and historical evolution of the St. Johns neighborhood.
world knowledge.Details: Originally named Northgate Theater and St. Johns Theater, it was renovated in 1983 by David A. Jones and David H. Evans. The theater has been a significant community venue for over a century.

world knowledge.Name: Firstsite
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Firstsite is a visual arts organisation based in Colchester, Essex, which opened in 1993 as Colchester and District Visual Arts Trust, changing its name to Firstsite in 1995. Its current building was opened in 2011. It was the national Art Fund's Museum of the Year in 2021.

Major_Events.Description: The current building of Firstsite was opened in 2011, designed by Rafael Viñoly.
Firstsite was awarded the national Art Fund Museum of the Year prize in 2021.

Major_Events.Event: Return to Arts Council 'National Portfolio Organisation' status
Major_Events.Description: In February 2018, Firstsite returned to Arts Council 'National Portfolio Organisation' status despite having only recorded 131,663 visitors in the previous year and having made a loss of £243,000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building was designed by Rafael Viñoly and features sloping walls. It is situated in Colchester's 'Cultural Quarter' near other significant cultural and historical sites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Firstsite is a significant cultural institution in Colchester, promoting visual arts and hosting rolling exhibitions. It has received national recognition, including the Art Fund Museum of the Year prize in 2021.
world knowledge.Details: Firstsite has no permanent art collection of its own and operates as a registered charity under English law. It has faced both praise and criticism in the press for its architecture, economic impact, and visitor statistics. The gallery's opening exhibition was Camulodunum, and it has cooperated with Essex University to show South American art until 2013.

world knowledge.Name: Ramsar Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ramsar Palace or Marmar Palace is a historic royal residence in Iran. The palace is in Ramsar, a city on the coast of the Caspian Sea. The Ramsar Palace was established on a land of 60,000 square meters in 1937. The area was a historical garden in Ramsar. Crown Prince Mohammad Reza Pahlavi's companion Ernest Perron was sent to the palace to work as the head gardener shortly after the completion of the construction. The palace was used as a summer residence by Reza Shah and then by his son, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.

Major_Events.Event: Honeymoon of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Soraya Esfendiary-Bakhtiary
Major_Events.Description: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and his second spouse Soraya Esfendiary-Bakhtiary spent their honeymoon in the palace.
The palace has been used as a museum since 2000.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Ramsar Palace is a compact and modest residence with 600 square metres (6,500 sq ft) square meters area although it lies on a land of 60,000 square meters. It is a rectangular building with a single story, and is decorated with works by famous Iranian sculptors and painters. The front line of the palace is made up of carved marble stones which were made by local artists. The common materials used are plaster and mirror in addition to marble. There is a reception hall or central hall in the place which has wooden floor.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ramsar Palace is a historic royal residence and has been used as a museum since 2000, known as the Ramsar Palace museum or the Caspian museum, and is locally referred to as “Tamashagah Khazar".
world knowledge.Details: The palace was frequently visited by Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Soraya Esfendiary-Bakhtiary during political crises in Tehran.

world knowledge.Name: Sherwood Forest
world knowledge.Address: Sherwood Forest National Nature Reserve, Edwinstowe, Nottinghamshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sherwood Forest is the remnants of an ancient royal forest in Nottinghamshire, England, historically associated with the legend of Robin Hood. It has been wooded since the end of the Last Glacial Period. The forest was designated a Royal Hunting Forest by King William the Conqueror in 1066 and has been visited by various kings throughout history. After the dissolution of the monasteries by King Henry VIII in 1536, the land was sold into private ownership. The forest has been used for military purposes during the Second World War and was later opened to the public as a country park in 1969. In 2002, a portion of the forest was designated a national nature reserve.

Major_Events.Description: King William the Conqueror designated Sherwood Forest as a Royal Hunting Forest.
King Henry VIII dissolved the monasteries, leading to the sale of Sherwood Forest into private ownership.

Major_Events.Event: Military use during World War II
Major_Events.Description: Parts of Sherwood Forest were used extensively by the military for ammunition stores, POW camps, and training areas.
Sherwood Forest was opened to the public as a country park by Nottinghamshire County Council.
A portion of Sherwood Forest was designated a national nature reserve by English Nature.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Sherwood Forest is characterized by ancient oaks, wood pasture, and diverse flora and fauna. The forest includes remnants of historical structures such as King John's Palace and various ducal estates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sherwood Forest is culturally significant due to its association with the legend of Robin Hood. It is also an important site for ancient oaks, wood pasture, invertebrates, and fungi. The forest has historical importance as a Royal Hunting Forest and a site of military activity during World War II.
world knowledge.Details: Sherwood Forest attracts around 350,000 tourists annually and hosts the Robin Hood Festival each August. The forest is home to the Major Oak, an oak tree between 800 and 1,000 years old. The Sherwood Forest Trust aims to conserve the forest's heritage and promote tourism. The forest includes several local sites such as Thoresby Hall Park, Rufford Abbey country park, and Clumber Park.

world knowledge.Name: Jinling Hotel
world knowledge.Address: 2 Hanzhong Road, Xinjiekou district, Nanjing, People's Republic of China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 16,000 square meters (lawns and ornamental tree planting)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Jinling Hotel was Nanjing's first modern hotel managed by Chinese and is still often regarded as the pre-eminent five-star hotel in Nanjing. It was the first luxury five-star hotel in Jiangsu Province and the tallest building in China from 1983 to 1985. The hotel was built to cater to overseas tourists and became a symbol of China's reform and opening up.

Major_Events.Description: Jinling Hotel was successfully established on 21 February 1983, becoming the first luxury five-star hotel in Jiangsu Province and the tallest building in China at the time.
The Nanjing World Trade Center (Phase II) was completed and started operation, adding a 17-floor building to the complex.
The main building of Asia Pacific Tower (Phase III) was completed, making Jinling Hotel the largest hotel complex in Jiangsu Province with a 53-floor, 243-meter-tall tower.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Palmer & Turner Group (P&T), the hotel features a modern architectural style. It includes 37 floors (in the original phase), a high-speed elevator, a high-rise revolving restaurant, and a high-rise helipad.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Jinling Hotel is a symbol of China's reform and opening up, often referred to as the 'window of China's reform and opening up' by international media. It was a mystery to Nanjing residents initially and became a landmark representing modernity and luxury.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Hotel and commercial services, including chain fast food restaurants, travel agency services, car rental, communications, and advertising.
Notable_Visitors: Hundreds of celebrities and politicians from different countries (specific names not mentioned)
world knowledge.Details: The hotel has nine restaurants of differing cuisine types. It vigorously carries out environmental protection activities and advocates green consumption and green living. Jinling Hotel paid off its capital construction debts of US$45 million in only 10 years.

world knowledge.Name: Felsenreitschule
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Felsenreitschule, originally a Baroque theatre built in 1693–94 at the behest of the Salzburg prince-archbishop Johann Ernst von Thun, was designed by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach. It was constructed in the former Mönchsberg quarry for conglomerate rock used in the new Salzburg Cathedral. Initially used as a summer riding school and for animal hunts, it later served the Austrian Imperial-Royal Army and Bundesheer forces after World War I. Since 1926, it has been a venue for the Salzburg Festival.

Major_Events.Event: First production as an open-air theatre
Major_Events.Description: Carlo Goldoni's The Servant of Two Masters, directed by Max Reinhardt.
Clemens Holzmeister designed a multiple-stage setting for Max Reinhardt's production of Goethe's Faust.
Herbert von Karajan conducted Christoph Willibald Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice.
Conducted by Ferenc Fricsay, it was a setting of the ancient tragedy by Sophocles, translated into German by Friedrich Hölderlin.
Remodeled by Clemens Holzmeister, inaugurated with Ludwig van Beethoven's Fidelio under Karl Böhm.
The roof was renewed, adding 700 square metres of floor space and improving stage equipment and sound insulation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Originally a Baroque theatre with 96 arcades carved into the Mönchsberg rock on three floors. Renovations included a cantilevered grandstand, a light-tight rain tarp, and a new pitched roof with mobile segment surfaces on telescopic arms.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Felsenreitschule is a significant venue for the Salzburg Festival and has hosted numerous important performances. It also gained fame as a location in the 1965 film The Sound of Music.
world knowledge.Details: The stage has a width of 40 metres and 4 metres understage. The theater holds 1412 seats and 25 standing places. It shares its foyer with the Kleines Festspielhaus (House for Mozart).

world knowledge.Name: San Sebastián
world knowledge.Historical_Background: San Sebastián, officially known by the bilingual name Donostia / San Sebastián, is a city and municipality located in the Basque Autonomous Community, Spain. It lies on the coast of the Bay of Biscay, 20 km from the France–Spain border. The city was founded in 1180 and has a rich history involving Roman settlements, medieval charters, and significant events such as the Peninsular War and the Spanish Civil War.

Major_Events.Description: Established to stimulate the economic life and profile of the city, it has become one of the most important film festivals in the world.
San Sebastián, along with Wrocław, Poland, was selected as the European Capital of Culture, highlighting its vibrant cultural scene.
The city was besieged and ransacked by British and Portuguese troops, leading to significant destruction and subsequent reconstruction.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The city features a mix of neoclassical and modernist architecture, with notable structures such as the Miramar Palace, La Concha Promenade, and the Kursaal Congress Centre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: San Sebastián is culturally significant for its festivals, cuisine, and historical events. It is renowned for its Basque cuisine, hosting numerous Michelin-starred restaurants, and is a hub for cultural events like the San Sebastián International Film Festival and the San Sebastian Jazz Festival.
world knowledge.Details: San Sebastián is a major tourist destination known for its beaches, culinary excellence, and cultural festivals. The city has a dynamic cultural scene and is home to several universities and research centers, making it an important educational and scientific hub in Spain.

world knowledge.Name: Cathedral of Syracuse
world knowledge.Address: Piazza Duomo, Ortygia Island, Syracuse, Sicily, Italy
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Cathedral of Syracuse, formally known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Most Holy Nativity of Mary, is an ancient Catholic church in Syracuse, Sicily. Originally a Greek Doric temple built in the 6th century BC, it was converted into a cathedral in the 7th century by Saint Bishop Zosimo of Syracuse. The temple was converted into a mosque in 878 and back into a cathedral in 1086. The current structure incorporates elements from its Greek origins, Norman modifications, and a Sicilian Baroque façade redesigned in the 18th century.

Major_Events.Description: The cathedral was converted into a mosque during the Arab rule of Sicily.
The cathedral was reconverted to a Christian place of worship after the Norman conquest of Sicily.
The façade of the cathedral was redesigned in the Sicilian Baroque style by architect Andrea Palma.
The cathedral, along with the city of Syracuse and the Necropolis of Pantalica, was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The cathedral features a combination of Greek Doric columns, Norman mosaics, and Sicilian Baroque architecture. The façade, designed by Andrea Palma, includes double-order Corinthian columns with carved Acanthus leaves and statues by Ignazio Marabitti. The interior has a nave and two aisles with rustic walls and Baroque details, including a 12th or 13th-century marble font, a ciborium by Luigi Vanvitelli, and a statue of the Madonna della Neve by Antonello Gagini.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Cathedral of Syracuse is a significant example of architectural evolution, incorporating Greek, Roman, and Baroque elements. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site designated in 2005, recognized for its outstanding architectural creation and its connection to events, ideas, and literary works of universal significance.
world knowledge.Details: The cathedral holds relics of St. Lucy, including bone fragments, a robe, a veil, and a pair of shoes. A statue of St. Lucy by Pietro Rizzo is paraded through the streets on her feast days. The cathedral shares the Piazza Duomo with the Church of Santa Lucia alla Badia, which formerly displayed Caravaggio's 'Burial of St. Lucy'.

world knowledge.Name: Layer Marney Tower
world knowledge.Address: Layer Marney, Essex, England, between Colchester and Maldon
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Main range measuring some 300 feet (91 m) long, principal gatehouse about 80 feet (24 m) tall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Layer Marney Tower is an incomplete early Tudor country house, with gardens and parkland, dating from about 1523. The building was designated Grade I listed in 1952. It was principally the creation of Henry 1st Lord Marney, who died in 1523, and his son John, who continued the building work but died just two years later, leaving no male heirs to continue the family line or the construction. The buildings suffered considerable damage from the Great English earthquake of 1884. The repairs were begun by brother and sister Alfred Peache and Kezia Peache, who re-floored and re-roofed the gatehouse, as well as creating the garden to the south of the Tower. The next owner was Walter de Zoete who carried on and expanded the work. Walter de Zoete lost money in the Japanese stock market crash, and sold the house to a Dr and Mrs Campbell. The house came to the present owners, the Charringtons, in 1959.

Major_Events.Description: The buildings suffered considerable damage from the Great English earthquake of 1884.
In September 2010, episode 5 of the BBC's Climbing Great Buildings explored the tower in detail.
In December 2011, it was the venue for BBC1's Antiques Roadshow.

Major_Events.Event: Channel 4 show Four in a Bed
Major_Events.Description: In 2019 the tower was featured in Channel 4 show Four in a Bed, where the hosts received positive feedback.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Tudor architectural style, brick and terracotta construction, tallest Tudor gatehouse in Britain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Layer Marney Tower is culturally and historically important as the apotheosis of the Tudor gatehouse and the tallest example in Britain. It is also significant for its Grade I listed status and its role in various media productions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Country house, wedding venue, conference location, media location
world knowledge.Details: The gardens are listed as Grade II on the English Heritage Register of Historic Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in England. The tower and gardens are open to the public from mid-April to 1 October for a small admission fee. It has proved popular as a media location, featuring in films and television programs such as Preaching to the Perverted, Pasolini's Canterbury Tales, and Lovejoy.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Trianon
world knowledge.Area: Northwestern part of the Domain of Versailles
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grand Trianon was built as a retreat for Louis XIV and his mistress, the Marquise de Montespan, to escape the strict etiquette of the royal court. It replaced the earlier Trianon de porcelaine, which deteriorated due to its fragile materials. Over the centuries, it served as a residence for various members of the French royal family and hosted significant historical events.

Major_Events.Description: Louis XIV commissioned the porcelain pavilion, which was later demolished due to deterioration.
The Grand Trianon was built to replace the porcelain pavilion, using red marble from Languedoc.
The building underwent significant renovation.

Major_Events.Event: Signing of the Treaty of Trianon
Major_Events.Description: The treaty was negotiated and signed here, significantly reducing Hungary's territory after World War I.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: French Baroque, Louis XIV Style, Neoclassical, and Empire Style. Built with red marble from Languedoc, featuring an open-air peristyle with red marble columns. The interior design includes delicately carved wood boiseries, plaster friezes, pilasters, and capitals.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Grand Trianon is a symbol of French Baroque architecture and royal leisure. It played a role in significant historical events, such as the signing of the Treaty of Trianon. Today, it serves as a presidential residence for hosting foreign dignitaries and is a popular tourist attraction.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a royal retreat, now a presidential residence and tourist site.
Notable_Visitors: Maria Amalia of the Two Sicilies
world knowledge.Details: The Grand Trianon is set within its own park, which includes the Petit Trianon. It has been used by various French rulers and their families over the centuries and remains an important cultural and historical site.

world knowledge.Name: Jardin du Luxembourg
world knowledge.Address: Rue de Médicis - Rue de Vaugirard, 75006 Paris, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Jardin du Luxembourg was created in 1612 by Marie de' Medici, the widow of King Henry IV, as part of the Luxembourg Palace. The garden was inspired by the Boboli Gardens in Florence and has undergone several expansions and modifications over the centuries. It was owned by the French Senate and features a mix of French and English garden styles.

Major_Events.Description: Marie de' Medici begins construction of the Luxembourg Palace and the garden.
Marie de' Medici buys additional land and enlarges the garden to thirty hectares.
The garden is expanded to forty hectares by confiscating land from the Carthusian monks.
Rue de l'Abbé de l'Épée is extended into the park, cutting off about seven hectares. The Medici Fountain is moved to its present location.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The garden features a mix of French formal garden design and English landscape garden elements. It includes tree-lined promenades, flowerbeds, fountains, statues, and an octagonal Grand Bassin. The Medici Fountain is a notable feature, designed in the style of a grotto.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Jardin du Luxembourg is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Paris, known for its beauty and tranquility. It has inspired numerous works of literature, art, and music. The garden is also a popular recreational space for Parisians and tourists alike.
world knowledge.Details: The garden includes a marionette theater, a music kiosk, greenhouses, an apiary, an orangerie, a rose garden, and a fruit orchard. It is also home to over a hundred statues, monuments, and fountains. The garden is open to the public with varying hours depending on the season.

world knowledge.Name: Margalla Hills National Park
world knowledge.Address: Islamabad Capital Territory, near its northern boundary with Haripur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Margalla Hills National Park is located in Islamabad Capital Territory, near its northern boundary with Haripur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The park includes the Margalla Hills, which form the foothills of the Himalayas, along with Shakarparian Park and Rawal Lake. Established in 1980, it is the third-largest national park in Pakistan. The rock formations are 40 million years old, and fossils of marine life abound, indicating that before the continent collision around 40 to 50 million years ago, these hills were the seabed of the ancient ocean.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Margalla Hills National Park
Major_Events.Description: The park was established to conserve the existing flora and fauna.

Major_Events.Event: Demolition of Monal and LaMontana restaurant
Major_Events.Description: Despite heavy public backlash, the famous Monal and LaMontana restaurant, which offered a scenic view of Islamabad, was demolished by order of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features diverse vegetation, including deciduous and evergreen trees, pines, and groves of oak. It is also home to a variety of wildlife, including mammals, birds, and reptiles.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is a significant hub for bird lovers and a major tourist destination. It is also a site for hiking and rock climbing, with several trails and crags available for exploration.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of flora and fauna, tourism, and recreation
world knowledge.Details: The park is rich in biodiversity, especially Sino-Himalayan fauna. It is home to around 600 plant species, 402 bird varieties, 38 mammals, and 27 species of reptiles. The Himalayan Wildlife Foundation is running a project on a sustainable management strategy for the park. The Margalla Hills Society, established in 1989, aims to preserve the natural environment and promote public interest in conservation.

world knowledge.Name: Mandrem Beach
world knowledge.Location: Coastal village in North Goa, 21 km from Panaji
world knowledge.Address: Mandrem, Pernem taluka, North Goa, Goa, India, PIN: 403527
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally named Manjrey, renamed to Mandrem by the Portuguese. The 'D' is pronounced as 'J' in Portuguese.

Major_Events.Description: Mandrem Beach was notified as a turtle nesting site under CRZ 2011.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mandrem is a culturally significant coastal village with a small fishing community and is known for its serene beaches and natural beauty. It is also a notified turtle nesting site.
world knowledge.Details: Mandrem is famous for its white sand beaches with clear water, particularly Mandrem Beach, which lies between Morjim and Arambol beaches. The beach is quiet and peaceful, especially during high tide when seawater rushes into the Mandrem Creek. The village has 11 wards and is part of the Mandrem (Goa Assembly constituency) and North Goa (Lok Sabha constituency). The official language is Konkani, and the time zone is UTC+5:30 (IST).

world knowledge.Name: Watonwan County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Watonwan County Courthouse in St. James, Minnesota, is the seat of government for Watonwan County, in continual use since it was completed in 1896. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1987 for having state-level significance in the themes of architecture and politics/government. The courthouse was built as a show of government strength and traditional values in a city that was only 25 years old.

Major_Events.Description: A heated battle for county seat status erupted between Madelia and St. James. After the original wood-frame courthouse in Madelia burned down in 1872, St. James petitioned for a vote, and in 1874 voters approved the move of the county seat to St. James.
The present courthouse was designed by architect H.C. Gerlach and built by contractor Otto Kleinschmidt. It replaced the earlier wood-frame structure in St. James.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its state-level significance in architecture and politics/government.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Romanesque Revival architecture, monumental in size and design. It is one of Minnesota's remaining monumental Victorian courthouses.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is significant for its exemplary Romanesque Revival architecture, its status as one of Minnesota's remaining monumental Victorian courthouses and as a local landmark, and its longstanding service as county seat.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of government for Watonwan County
world knowledge.Details: The building was nominated for the National Register of Historic Places for its architectural significance and its role in local government. A county-wide survey of historic properties identified it as one of the most architecturally significant Victorian buildings in the county.

world knowledge.Name: Puthia Rajbari
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Puthia Rajbari is a palace built in 1895 by Maharani Hemanta Kumari Devi in memory of her mother-in-law Maharani Saratsundari Devi. It is an example of Indo-Saracenic Revival architecture. Initially, Puthia was a village named Laskarpur Pargana, named after Laskar Khan Nilamber, the brother of the first zamindar of Puthia, who received the title of Raja from Mughal emperor Jahangir. The estate was partitioned in 1744, dividing the zamindari among four co-shares.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features Indo-Saracenic Revival architecture with semi-Corinthian columns, arcaded loggias, and terracotta carvings. It is divided into four courts, with rooms built around them. The Kachari Angan has porticos on both ends, supported by semi-Corinthian columns. The northern block is double-storeyed with a wide hall and verandahs. The Pancharatna Gobinda temple, located within the palace, is ornamented with terracotta carvings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Puthia Rajbari is culturally significant as a historical palace that reflects the architectural and cultural heritage of the region. It also houses a museum narrating the history of Puthia and its adjoining areas.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is surrounded by ditches and was originally enclosed by strong walls, now damaged. Many rooms are in ruins, and terracotta artifacts from nearby temples have been destroyed or stolen due to lack of preservation efforts. Cattle roam the area, and there is no boundary wall for protection. Reports of missing and looted items are frequent, highlighting the need for government intervention to preserve this heritage site.

world knowledge.Name: Benton County Courthouse (Iowa)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Benton County Courthouse, built in 1906, is the fourth building used for court functions and county administration. The first courthouse was a log structure without a roof or floor, and the second was destroyed by fire. The third courthouse, built in 1856, was a two-story Federal-style brick building. The current courthouse was completed in 1906 for $105,000.

Major_Events.Description: The first courthouse was a log structure without a roof or floor, and court met in a log home during inclement weather.
The second courthouse was destroyed by fire, and county records were rescued by three men, one of whom died from injuries sustained in the fire.
The third courthouse was a two-story Federal-style brick building with an octagon-shaped cupola, built at a cost of $13,000.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: A simplified version of the Beaux Arts style, the building features a 112-foot central tower, a four-faced illuminated clock, a 1,500-pound B-flat bell, and a dome. The two-story structure sits on a raised basement and is made up of a central pavilion flanked by two side pavilions. The basement is composed of rusticated Kettle River sandstone, while the upper two floors are clad in Buckeye gray sandstone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is one of the local community's most prominent landmarks and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.
world knowledge.Details: Designed by Bell & Detweiler of Minneapolis, the courthouse was built by George Rickman & Sons. The cornerstone was laid on October 14, 1905, and it was completed in 1906 for $105,000.

world knowledge.Name: Rodney Parade
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rodney Parade is a stadium in Newport, South Wales, located on the east bank of the River Usk. It was established in 1877 by the Newport Athletic Club, which secured the land from Godfrey Morgan, 1st Viscount Tredegar. The stadium has hosted rugby union, football, cricket, and other sports events. It is the home ground of Dragons RFC and Newport County football club. The stadium has undergone several redevelopments and ownership changes, including a recent purchase by a private consortium in 2023.

Major_Events.Event: First floodlit rugby match in Wales
Major_Events.Description: Newport RFC played Cardiff RFC in a floodlit game at Rodney Parade, the first ground in Wales to have floodlights installed.
Plans were announced to redevelop Rodney Parade into a 15,000-capacity stadium by the beginning of the 2010–11 rugby union season.
The record attendance for a Newport County match at Rodney Parade was set at 9,836 against Tottenham Hotspur in the FA cup fourth round.
The memorial gates, erected in 1923–24 to commemorate members of Newport Athletic Club killed in the First World War, were given Grade II listed building status.
The pitch and drainage redevelopment, including a hybrid grass surface, was completed in August 2021.
A consortium headed by former Just Eat CEO David Buttress bought the Rodney Parade site and the Dragons rugby union team from the Welsh Rugby Union.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Rodney Parade has two covered stands: the two-tier Candleston Stand (west) and the Bisley Stand (east). The upper tier of the west stand is seated with 1,996 seats, and the lower tier is a standing terrace. The east stand is all-seated with a 2,526 capacity, including 144 seats in 13 hospitality boxes. The North Terrace is uncovered standing, and the South End houses players' changing rooms, a media centre, and a small uncovered stand with 222 seats for away football fans.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rodney Parade is historically significant as the third-oldest sports venue in the Football League and the first ground in Wales to have floodlights installed. It has hosted numerous important rugby and football matches, including international games. The memorial gates commemorate members of Newport Athletic Club who were killed in the First World War, adding to its cultural and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sports stadium hosting rugby union and football matches
world knowledge.Details: Rodney Parade has hosted six full-cap rugby union international matches for the Wales national rugby union team and one match for the Wales women's national football team. The stadium has a hybrid grass surface and has won awards for the best pitch in EFL League Two. It continues to be a key venue for sports in Newport, with ongoing redevelopments and long-term leases for its primary tenants.

world knowledge.Name: National Museums of Kenya
world knowledge.Location: Museum Hill, near Uhuru Highway between Central Business District and Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya
world knowledge.Address: Museum Hill, near Uhuru Highway between Central Business District and Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Museums of Kenya (NMK) was founded by the East Africa Natural History Society (E.A.N.H.S.) in 1910. The society's main goal has always been to conduct an ongoing critical scientific examination of the natural attributes of the East African habitat. The museum was officially opened on 22 September 1930, as Coryndon Museum. Kenya became independent in 1963, and the Coryndon Museum was renamed "National Museum" in 1964 and was included in a new system, the "National Museums of Kenya."

Major_Events.Event: Founding of the National Museum of Kenya
Major_Events.Description: The National Museum of Kenya was founded by the East Africa Natural History Society (E.A.N.H.S.) in 1910.
The museum was officially opened on 22 September 1930, as Coryndon Museum.
The Coryndon Museum was renamed "National Museum" in 1964 and was included in a new system, the "National Museums of Kenya."
Nairobi Museum Galleries closed until December 2007 for an extensive rebuilding program. This was the first major renovation of Nairobi Museum since 1930.
The museum re-opened in June 2008. It houses both temporary and permanent exhibitions.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum's building has undergone significant changes since its initial construction in 1910. The current structure includes a new administration block and commercial center, built during the 2005-2007 renovation.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Museums of Kenya is a state corporation that manages museums, sites, and monuments in Kenya. It carries out heritage research and has expertise in subjects ranging from palaeontology, archeology, ethnography, and biodiversity research and conservation. It plays a crucial role in preserving Kenya's natural and cultural heritage.
world knowledge.Details: The National Museums of Kenya manages over 22 regional museums, many sites, and monuments across the country. Within the grounds are also the Nairobi Snake Park and the Botanic Garden and nature trail. The museum's commercial wing has restaurants and shops.

world knowledge.Name: Şanlıurfa Archaeology and Mosaic Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Şanlıurfa Archaeology and Mosaic Museum, also known as Şanlıurfa Museum, is located in the south-eastern city of Şanlıurfa, Turkey. The museum contains remains from various ancient sites including Şanlıurfa (Edessa), Göbekli Tepe, Karahan Tepe, and Harran. It also features findings from the Southeastern Anatolia Project and ruins from hydroelectric dam reservoirs. The museum opened in 2015, replacing the former museum on Çamlık street, which was established in 1969.

Major_Events.Description: The new Şanlıurfa Archaeology and Mosaic Museum opened in 2015, replacing the former museum on Çamlık street.
The mosaic of Orpheus, created in 184 A.D. in Edessa, was returned to Şanlıurfa from the Dallas Museum in 2015 after being taken to the United States by illegal means.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum consists of two major buildings: the archaeology museum to the north and the mosaic museum to the south. It has 3 floors and covers 2,500 square meters of indoor space. The museum features exhibition halls showcasing artifacts from various historical periods and an ethnographic section with cultural items.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses important archaeological finds from the region, including the Urfa Man statue, which is considered the oldest life-sized sculpture of a human ever discovered. It also preserves and displays artifacts from various ancient civilizations, contributing to the understanding of the region's rich history.
world knowledge.Details: The museum includes the Urfa Man statue, dated c. 9000 BC (11,000 years ago), being considered as the oldest life-sized sculpture of a human already discovered. It also features a 9500-year-old sculpture, the oldest-known life-size human sculpture.

world knowledge.Name: Stornoway Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: South Beach, Stornoway, Isle of Lewis, Scotland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Stornoway Town Hall is a former municipal building that served as the headquarters of Stornoway Town Council. Proposals for a town hall in Stornoway were first considered in 1897. The foundation stone was laid in 1903, and it was opened in 1905. The original structure was gutted by fire in 1918 and was rebuilt in 1929. It was designated as a Category B listed building in 1980. The building was extensively refurbished for £2.1 million and re-opened for community use in 2012.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone for the new building was laid by Major Duncan Matheson of Lews Castle.
The town hall was opened by the former Prime Minister, the Earl of Rosebery.
The original structure was gutted by fire.
The town hall was re-opened by Thomas Bassett Macaulay, President of the Sun Life Assurance Company of Canada.
The town hall was extensively refurbished for £2.1 million and re-opened for community use.

Major_Events.Event: Visit by the Earl and Countess of Wessex
Major_Events.Description: The Earl and Countess of Wessex visited the town hall and met local leaders of the Duke of Edinburgh's Award scheme.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The design involved a symmetrical frontage with eleven bays facing South Beach; the central section featured a round-headed doorway on the ground floor flanked by turreted bays; there were four triple windows, each with an ogee moulding, on the first floor; the building also turreted corner bays and a central clock tower with a cupola. Internally, the principal room was the public hall, which was in the centre of the building, lying parallel to the main frontage.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The town hall is a Category B listed building and has been a significant community and cultural hub in Stornoway. The clock tower gained fame from the song 'Lovely Stornoway' sung by Calum Kennedy in the 1960s.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former municipal building, now used for community purposes
world knowledge.Details: The town hall was the headquarters of Stornoway Town Council until it was absorbed into Comhairle nan Eilean Siar in 1975. It was then used as the home of the arts centre, An Lanntair, until October 2005 when the centre moved to a purpose-built facility on the seafront. The refurbishment works included the reinstatement of the original fourteen roof lights in the main hall and the removal of the stage in the main hall, revealing three stained glass windows in the western gable.

world knowledge.Name: Dankook University
world knowledge.Location: Jukjeon Campus: Yongin, Gyeonggi, South Korea; Cheonan Campus: Cheonan, Chungnam, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dankook University, abbreviated as DKU, is a private research university established on November 3, 1947. It was the first university established after the National Liberation Day of Korea, originally located in Jongno District and Yongsan District, Seoul. The university now features 20 undergraduate colleges and 10 professional graduate schools divided between its Jukjeon campus, constructed in 2007, and its Cheonan campus.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation of Dankook University was approved on November 1, 1947, and it opened on November 3 at Nakwon-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul.
The Seok Juseon museum opened based on a donation of over 3,000 items by Seok Ju-Seon. The museum curates and conserves Korean costumes.
Dankook University Hospital (DKUH) opened in April 1994. It is the largest general hospital in South Chungcheong province, South Korea, with 878 certified beds and 33 specialty clinics.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dankook University is culturally significant as the first private university established after Korea gained independence in 1947. It has a global affiliate network of universities and institutes and hosts more than 30,000 students with an instructional faculty of about 2,700 professors and teachers.
world knowledge.Details: Dankook University has a global affiliate network of universities and institutes, including collaborations with Stockholm University in Sweden; California State University and Ohio Northern University in the USA; and La Trobe University in Australia. The university hosts international summer schools programs, student exchanges, and short-term visits. It is ranked #751-800 in QS World University Rankings 2023 and generally accepts students with a CSAT score in the top 10% of the nation.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Municipal de Concepción
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built in 1962 as Estadio Regional with a capacity of 35,000 people, the stadium was renamed in 2010 after Ester Roa Rebolledo, a former Concepción city mayor. It underwent a major renovation from 2013 to 2015, reducing its capacity to 30,448 seats. The stadium has hosted numerous significant football matches and events.

Major_Events.Description: Highest recorded attendance of 43,340.
One of the venues for the tournament.
Featured as a venue for the tournament.
Co-hosted the tournament.
Hosted three matches after reopening post-renovation.
One of the venues for the tournament.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with grass surface, featuring a roof and seating for 30,448 spectators. Designed by architect Mario Recordón.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a key sports venue in Chile, hosting major football matches and international tournaments. It is named in honor of a former city mayor, reflecting its importance to the local community.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football matches, music concerts, and athletics tournaments.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is home to Universidad de Concepción, Fernández Vial, and Deportes Concepción. It has also hosted important games for Huachipato and Lota Schwager. Renovations were initially handled by Spanish company COPASA but were later completed by Chilean company Claro Vicuña Valenzuela.

world knowledge.Name: Goodman Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1925 as a tribute to playwright Kenneth Sawyer Goodman, who died in the 1918 influenza pandemic. Initially funded by Goodman's parents, it became a fully professional company in 1969. The drama school became part of DePaul University in 1978. The current facility opened in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: Featured three of Kenneth Sawyer Goodman's plays: Back of the Yards, The Green Scarf, and The Game of Chess.
Presented John Galsworthy's The Forest.
Under artistic director John Reich.
Relocated to 170 North Dearborn in Chicago's theater district.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Michael Maggio Emerging Designer Award
Major_Events.Description: Honoring associate artistic director Michael Maggio after his death.
Received the prestigious award, joining other Chicago-based recipients.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by KPMB Architects, DLK Architecture Inc., and McClier Corporation. Features two modern auditoriums named the Albert and the Owen.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chicago's oldest currently active nonprofit theater organization. A major part of the Chicago theatre scene, it has won numerous awards including the Regional Theatre Tony Award and Joseph Jefferson awards.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Professional theater company and drama school.
world knowledge.Details: Notable productions include Inherit the Wind (2024), The Nacirema Society (2023), Lucha Teotl (2023), Highway Patrol (2024), The Matchbox Magic Flute (2024), The Penelopiad (2024), Joe Turner's Come and Gone (2024), English (2024), and Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (2024).

world knowledge.Name: Our Lady of Lebanon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon, also known as Our Lady of Harissa, is a Marian shrine and pilgrimage site in Harissa, Lebanon. It was established in 1904 and is administered by the Congregation of Maronite Lebanese Missionaries. The shrine features a large bronze statue of the Virgin Mary, which was erected in 1907 and inaugurated in 1908. It has become a significant pilgrimage destination for both Christians and Muslims.

Major_Events.Event: 50th Jubilee and Centennial of the Immaculate Conception
Major_Events.Description: Pope Pius XII sent Cardinal Angelo Roncalli (later Pope John XXIII) to Lebanon for the celebrations.

Major_Events.Event: Visit of Pope John Paul II
Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II visited the shrine and conducted a mass in the modern Basilica.
The Vatican announced that the World Day of the Sick would be celebrated at Our Lady of Lebanon in Harissa.

Major_Events.Event: Appeal for Peace by Pope Benedict XVI
Major_Events.Description: Pope Benedict XVI invoked the protection of Our Lady of Lebanon for peace in Lebanon and Gaza.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The shrine features a large bronze statue of the Virgin Mary with outstretched hands, crowned with a bronze crown. The statue is 8.5 meters high and 5.5 meters in diameter, mounted on a stone base with a bottom perimeter of 64 meters and an upper perimeter of 12 meters, and an overall height of 20 meters.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The shrine is one of the most important Marian shrines in the world, drawing millions of faithful from various religious backgrounds. It is a symbol of unity and devotion for Lebanese Christians, Druze, and Muslims. The Maronite Patriarch of Antioch named Mary the 'Queen of Lebanon' in 1908.
world knowledge.Details: The statue was donated by an anonymous French woman and was made in France. The land for the shrine was donated by Yousef Khazen. The shrine overlooks the bay of Jounieh and is accessible via a gondola lift, the Téléphérique, from Jounieh to Harissa. The Apostolic Nuncio to Lebanon and the residences of four Eastern Catholic Churches patriarchs are located near the shrine.

world knowledge.Name: Hungaroring
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hungaroring is a motorsport racetrack where the Formula One Hungarian Grand Prix is held. It became the location of the first Formula One Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. The circuit was built in eight months, less time than any other Formula One circuit. The first race was held on 24 March 1986, in memory of János Drapál, the first Hungarian who won motorcycle Grand Prix races.

Major_Events.Description: The first Formula One Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain.
International GT racing event.
Porsche racing event.
Grand Prix motorcycle racing event.
Endurance racing event.
Touring car racing event.
Truck racing event.
Touring car racing event.
GT racing event.
German touring car racing event.
Superbike racing event.
GT racing event.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The circuit has a length of 4.381 km (2.722 mi) with 16 turns. It was designed by István Papp & Ferenc Gulácsi. The track is known for its twisty and bumpy nature, making overtaking difficult in dry conditions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hungaroring is significant as it was the first Formula One Grand Prix location behind the Iron Curtain. It has hosted numerous major motorsport events and is a key destination for motorsport fans. The circuit has also seen many memorable races and has been a venue for several historic moments in Formula One.
world knowledge.Details: The Hungaroring is known for its challenging layout and has hosted a variety of motorsport events. It has undergone several changes in its layout to improve overtaking opportunities. The circuit has a rich history in Formula One and has been the site of many memorable races. It continues to be a popular venue for motorsport events and is a key part of Hungarian motorsport culture.

world knowledge.Name: University of Putra Malaysia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally established as the School of Agriculture in 1931, it became the College of Agriculture Malaya in 1947 and was officially established as Universiti Pertanian Malaysia (Agricultural University of Malaysia) in 1971. In 1997, it was renamed Universiti Putra Malaysia to reflect its diversification into fields beyond agriculture, including science, technology, and humanities.

Major_Events.Description: The university was officially established through the merger of the College of Agriculture Malaya and the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Malaya.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to Universiti Putra Malaysia
Major_Events.Description: The university was renamed to reflect its expanded focus on science and technology, among other fields.
UPM was recognized as one of Malaysia's research universities.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The campus features a mix of modern and traditional architectural styles, with facilities such as the Sultan Abdul Samad Library, the UPM Mosque, and the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Arts and Cultural Centre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: UPM is a leading public research university in Malaysia, known for its contributions to agricultural sciences, technology, and education. It plays a significant role in Malaysia's academic and research landscape.
world knowledge.Details: UPM has 15 faculties, 11 institutes, and 2 schools, offering a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs. The university has branch campuses in Bintulu, Sarawak, and previously in Kuala Terengganu. It is ranked 24th in the UI GreenMetric World University Rankings 2024.

world knowledge.Name: High Wycombe Guildhall
world knowledge.Address: High Street, High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The High Wycombe Guildhall is a Grade I listed building designed by Henry Keene and completed in 1757. It replaced a medieval guildhall that stood until the mid-17th century and a later structure built in 1604, which was destroyed by fire in the mid-18th century. The current guildhall was funded by the Earl of Shelburne and renovated in 1859 by Sir George Henry Dashwood. It served as the meeting place for the municipal borough of High Wycombe until the early 1930s.

Major_Events.Description: A scene of public disorder broke out during a debate on the Swing Riots when councillors started fighting with each other.
The council was incorporated under the Municipal Corporations Act 1835.
The guildhall continues to host the annual weighing-in ceremony where the elected mayor is weighed to ensure they have not been indulging excessively at the rate payers' expense.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The guildhall is designed in the neo-classical style with five bays and arcading on the ground floor. The first floor features windows in each bay on the east, west, and north elevations. At roof level, there is an octagonal cupola with Doric order columns and a wrought iron weather vane. The interior includes a council chamber (now the Carrington Room) with seating for 100 people and the Shelburne Room.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The High Wycombe Guildhall is a Grade I listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. It has been a central civic building for centuries, hosting council meetings and significant events. The annual weighing-in ceremony is a unique tradition that underscores its ongoing role in local governance and culture.
world knowledge.Details: A portrait of the Prince of Wales was presented to the town by Lord Carrington in 1876 and hung in the council chamber, now known as the Carrington Room. The building was designated as a Grade I listed structure on 9 January 1954 (Reference no. 1332349).

world knowledge.Name: Higashiyama Zoo and Botanical Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1937, the Higashiyama Zoo is one of Asia's largest attractions, featuring a botanical garden and an amusement park. The logo for the koala exhibit was designed by manga artist Akira Toriyama in 1984.

Major_Events.Description: The logo for the koala exhibit was designed by manga artist Akira Toriyama.

Major_Events.Event: Social media coverage of Shabani the gorilla
Major_Events.Description: Shabani, a silverback gorilla, received significant social media coverage for being termed as "handsome" and "metrosexual", leading to an increase in young female visitors to the zoo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The botanical gardens feature wild flora, as well as a greenhouse, insect hall, and a Japanese garden. The Higashiyama Sky Tower allows visitors a view of Nagoya from its observation decks, and also features a restaurant 100 metres above ground.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: As of 2010, Higashiyama Zoo had the 2nd most annual park visits of any zoo in Japan, behind only the Ueno Zoo in Tokyo. It keeps more than 450 species, which is the largest number in Japan.
world knowledge.Details: The Higashiyama Zoo and Botanical Gardens is a joint zoo and botanical garden. It is open every day except Monday, and charges a modest admission fee. The zoo's collection consists of 469 species.

world knowledge.Name: Bardejov
world knowledge.Location: North-Eastern Slovakia, on a floodplain terrace of the Topľa River, in the hills of the Beskyd Mountains
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Bardejov has been inhabited since the Stone Age, with its first written reference dating back to the 1240s. It became a center of trade with Poland in the 14th century and gained the status of a royal town in 1376. The town's golden age ended in the 16th century due to wars and pandemics. It saw revival in the 18th century with the arrival of Slovaks and Hasidic Jews. Bardejov was declared a protected city core in 1950 and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

Major_Events.Description: Polish King Władysław II Jagiełło defeated King Sigismund of Hungary and Croatia.

Major_Events.Event: Annexation and establishment of the first Czechoslovak Republic
Major_Events.Description: Bardejov became a backward farming region.
Bardejov was taken by Soviet troops of the 1st Guards Army on 20 January 1945.
Extensive restoration of its cultural heritage began.
Recognized for its Jewish Suburbia and historic town center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features a completely intact medieval town center with Gothic, Renaissance, and Gothic architecture. The Church of St. Aegidius is a three-nave basilica with multiple chapels completed in 1464, hosting eleven precious Gothic winged altars. The town hall, built in 1505, combines Gothic and Renaissance styles. The fortification system and town walls from the 14th and 15th centuries are among the most elaborate and best preserved in Slovakia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bardejov is a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its well-preserved medieval town center and Jewish Suburbia. It is a symbol of medieval urban development and cultural heritage in Central Europe. The town also has a rich Jewish history, though most of its Jewish population was deported during World War II.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historic town and cultural heritage site
world knowledge.Details: Bardejov is known for its authentic old town square and annual cultural traditions like the Roland Games. The nearby spa town Bardejovské Kúpele features therapeutic mineral water springs and an open-air museum of folk architecture. The town has a population of about 33,000, with a diverse ethnic and religious makeup. Bardejov is also twinned with several cities and has a rich genealogical research archive in Prešov.

world knowledge.Name: Smeaton's Tower
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 72 feet (22 m) in height, diameter at the base of 26 feet (8 m) and at the top of 17 feet (5 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Smeaton's Tower is a redundant lighthouse, now a memorial to civil engineer John Smeaton, designer of the third and most notable Eddystone Lighthouse. A major step forward in lighthouse design, Smeaton's structure was in use from 1759 to 1877, until erosion of the ledge it was built upon forced new construction. The tower was largely dismantled and rebuilt on Plymouth Hoe in Plymouth, Devon, where it stands today.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse's 24 candles were lit on 16 October 1759.

Major_Events.Event: Replacement of candles with oil lamps and reflectors
Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse candles were replaced by oil lamps and reflectors.
Engineer Henry Norris carried out major renovations, including the filling of a hole in the rock close to the tower's foundation.
Smeaton's Tower ceased operation in February 1882 following the installation of a temporary light atop its successor (Douglass's Tower).
The site was opened to the public by the Mayor of Plymouth on 24 September 1884.

A home-made bomb with the words 'votes for women' and 'death in ten minutes' painted on the outside was found in the entrance to Smeaton's Tower, presumably as part of the campaign for women's suffrage. The wick had been lit but blew out in the wind, preventing detonation.
The lantern of Smeaton's Tower was once again lit with 24 candles to mark the 250th anniversary of the lighthouse's first illumination.
A Cornish granite bust of Smeaton by Philip Chatfield was installed in the tower's lantern chamber before its reopening.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Smeaton designed his lighthouse to resemble an oak tree, making the tower into a strong shape. He rediscovered the use of hydraulic lime, a form of concrete used in Roman times. The technique allowed concrete to set under water, as Smeaton put granite blocks together using dovetail joints and marble dowels.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Smeaton's Tower is considered a major step forward in lighthouse design and is a memorial to civil engineer John Smeaton, who is considered the father of civil engineering. The lighthouse was depicted on a new penny coin from 1860 to 1894 and on a number of tokens issued during the 19th century in Devon.
world knowledge.Details: The foundation and stub of the old tower remain on Eddystone Rocks, close to the current lighthouse. An 1850 replica of Smeaton's lighthouse, Hoad Monument, still stands above the town of Ulverston, Cumbria as a memorial to naval administrator Sir John Barrow. Smeaton's Tower has been a Grade I-listed building since 1954. It is open for visitors, who may climb 93 steps, including steep ladders, to the lantern room, and observe Plymouth Sound and the city.

world knowledge.Name: Dom Luís I Bridge
world knowledge.Area: Porto, between the City of Porto proper and Vila Nova de Gaia
world knowledge.Address: Between Porto and Vila Nova de Gaia, Portugal
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Two decks of varying lengths: 172 metres (lower deck) and 395.25 metres (upper deck)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Dom Luís I Bridge is a double-deck metal arch bridge spanning the river Douro between Porto and Vila Nova de Gaia in Portugal. At its construction, its 172 metres span was the longest of its type in the world. It was designed by Théophile Seyrig and constructed by Société de Willebroek. The bridge was inaugurated on 31 October 1886 and has since been a significant part of the urban landscape, evolving in its use and function over the years.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was inaugurated on 31 October 1886, marking the completion of its construction.
The toll system was extinguished on 1 January 1944, and the bridge began to function as free infrastructure.

Major_Events.Event: Designated as Property of Public Interest
Major_Events.Description: The bridge was designated a cultural heritage Imóvel de Interesse Público by national agency IGESPAR.

Major_Events.Event: Upper deck closed to motor traffic
Major_Events.Description: The upper deck was closed to motor traffic on 27 June 2003 to adapt the structure for the metro system.
The lower deck closed temporarily to all traffic in October 2021 for repairs and renovation work, reopening in April 2023 with restricted access.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a two-hinged double-deck arch bridge made of iron with granite trough construction and asphalt pier construction. It features a large central arch supporting the upper and lower decks, with masonry piers mooring the decks to the riverbanks. The bridge has an asphalt pavement for vehicular traffic, separated by cast iron guards, and pedestrian walkways protected by cast iron guards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Dom Luís I Bridge is a significant cultural and historical landmark in Portugal, representing a major engineering achievement of the 19th century. It is a key part of the Historic Centre of Porto, recognized by UNESCO, and has been designated as a Monument of Public Interest.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Transportation (light rail, public transport, pedestrians) and urban connectivity
world knowledge.Details: The bridge's upper level is used by pedestrians and by line D of the Porto Metro, whilst the lower level is used by buses, taxis, cyclists and pedestrians. It connects significant urban areas and landmarks in Porto and Vila Nova de Gaia, including the Praça da Ribeira, the Guindais Funicular, the Serra do Pilar Monastery, and the Gaia Cable Car.

world knowledge.Name: Mobberley Old Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built in 1612 for Robert Robinson, son of a Yorkshire wool merchant. Extended later in the 17th century, probably for Laurence Wright of Offerton. Passed to Jane Wright and her husband John Blakiston, who built Mobberley Hall in 1845, renaming the older house as Mobberley Old Hall. Owned by Rev Herbert Leigh Mallory in the late 19th century, sold in 1900. Bought by Miss Elsie H. Bishop in 1924, bequeathed to Manchester University in 1955. Rented by Professor John Frederick Wilkinson and his wife Marion until 2003. Purchased by Mohammed Isaq in 2004 and by another buyer in 2005 for £3 million.

Major_Events.Description: Built for Robert Robinson, son of a Yorkshire wool merchant.
Extended probably for Laurence Wright of Offerton, making the house larger and grander.
After Jane Wright and her husband John Blakiston built Mobberley Hall, the older house became known as Mobberley Old Hall.

Major_Events.Event: Ownership by Rev Herbert Leigh Mallory
Major_Events.Description: Father of mountaineer George Mallory, sold the house in 1900.
Miss Elsie H. Bishop, who bought the house in 1924, bequeathed it to Manchester University upon her death.
The house and its estate were bought by Mohammed Isaq.
The house and estate were purchased by a different buyer for £3 million.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Jacobean style. Constructed in red and orange brick with stone dressings and stone slate roofs. Two storeys plus an attic and basement. Irregular plan with an asymmetrical northwest front (four bays from 1612 and two bays from later extension) and a symmetrical southwest front with three bays and a central arched doorway. Features a two-storey semi-octagonal bay window. Gardens include lawns, a kitchen garden, a paved garden, woodland, part of the moat, and an ancient yew hedge.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Grade II* listed building, recognized for its historical and architectural importance. The grounds contain two Grade II listed buildings: a barn dated 1686 and a 17th-century wall with gate piers. The house is a notable example of Jacobean architecture and has connections to several historical figures, including the Mallory family.
world knowledge.Details: The house is described by architectural historian Nikolaus Pevsner as having an irregular plan and being 'evidently only a fragment.' The lack of a proper entrance front suggests the house may have been truncated or intended to be larger. The gardens retain part of the moat and ancient yew trees, with the line of the rest of the moat marked by an ancient yew hedge.

world knowledge.Name: Castelvecchio Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Built by Cangrande II della Scala to provide a safe escape route from the annexed castle in case of rebellion. The bridge was destroyed by retreating German troops in 1945 and reconstructed between 1949 and 1951.

Major_Events.Description: French troops destroyed the tower on the left bank.
The bridge was totally destroyed by retreating German troops on April 24, 1945.
The bridge was reconstructed by architect Libero Cecchini, except for the left tower.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Red brick in the upper part and white marble in the lower part. Includes three spans of decreasing length starting from pentagonal towers. The largest span measures 48.70 m, the others measure 29.15 and 24.11 meters. The two pylons are 12.10 x 19.40 and 6.30 x 17.30 meters respectively.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a notable example of medieval engineering and architecture, featuring the world's largest bridge arch at the time of its construction. It is also associated with legends involving its designer, Guglielmo Bevilacqua.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Fortified bridge for safe passage and escape from the castle.
world knowledge.Details: According to legend, Cangrande awarded the designer of the bridge, Guglielmo Bevilacqua, with a sword that belonged to Saint Martin. Another legend tells that the designer presented himself at the inauguration riding a horse, ready to flee in case the bridge collapsed.

world knowledge.Name: Kemer Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bridge near Seydikemer was a Roman segmental arch bridge near the ancient city of Xanthos in Lycia. Its remains are located on the upper reaches of the Xanthos river (Koca Çayı), 4 km upstream from the town of Seydikemer. The bridge represents a noteworthy example of the early use of segmental arches and hollow chambers in bridge building.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was presumably built as part of a Roman road in the area, possibly linking to routes from Kadyanda (Üzümlü) or the pass trail to Oinoanda.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge features segmental arches and hollow chambers, with three arches of 4 to 4.45 m clear span. The arch vaults were constructed from locally hewn limestone ashlar bound by mortar, and the interior was built of a mixture of rubble and fluid mortar. The bridge also includes hollow chambers to reduce load and save building material, as well as circular ducts interpreted as remnants of Roman scaffolding.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important example of early Roman engineering, showcasing advanced techniques such as segmental arches and hollow chambers, which were not widely used until later periods. It provides insight into Roman construction methods and infrastructure in Asia Minor.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Bridge for crossing the Xanthos river
world knowledge.Details: The visible remains include a 29 m long and 4.5 m wide section on the right river bank, which served as an approach to the bridge proper. The bridge's height of 8 m above the sediments and the 500 m wide river bed indicate it was a significant engineering feat. A well-preserved example of a similar bridge is the Limyra Bridge, also in Lycia.

world knowledge.Name: Detroit Repertory Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1957 as a children's musical touring company, the Detroit Repertory Theatre established itself in Detroit in 1963. It survived the 1967 race riots and has been a key professional non-profit theatre in Detroit for nearly 60 years. The theatre has a strong commitment to social justice and diversity, employing interracial and color-blind casting techniques since its early days.

Major_Events.Description: Founded as a children's musical touring company, performing in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, and Pennsylvania.
The theatre established itself at its current location on Woodrow Wilson Avenue in Detroit.
The theatre endured and survived the 1967 race riots in Detroit.
With help from a grant from The Kresge Foundation, the theatre began renovations, upgrading the exterior and building a new parking lot.
Co-founder and artistic director Bruce Millan stepped down, and Leah Smith was appointed as the new artistic director.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Detroit Repertory Theatre is Michigan's oldest professional theatre and has been a progressive force in the arts, promoting diversity and social justice. It has a strong commitment to portraying its largely Black neighborhood on stage and employs diverse casting techniques. The theatre also nurtures the local community through various outreach programs.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Professional theatre producing plays and fostering community engagement through the arts.

Details.Season_Structure: Produces four shows a season with eight-week-long runs.
Outreach_Programs: Lobby gallery dedicated to Gilden Snowden
Details.Current_Status: Operates as an Actors' Equity Association Small Professional Theatre and owns two additional buildings for rehearsal, design, and construction purposes.

world knowledge.Name: Legislative Palace (Peru)
world knowledge.Area: Barrios Altos, historic centre of Lima
world knowledge.Address: Ayacucho (formerly Urubamba) street, next to Bolivar Square
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The site was originally the location of San Juan de la Penitencia, built in 1550. It later housed the University of San Marcos until the Constituent Congress was installed in 1822. Construction of the current Legislative Palace began in 1904, replacing a hospital and church. It was permanently occupied in 1938.

Major_Events.Description: The Constituent Congress was installed in the building, as established in its provisional internal regulations.
Congress authorized President José Balta to construct a Legislative Palace.
Construction on the new legislative building began based on the design of Emilio Robert.
The building was permanently occupied during the presidency of Óscar R. Benavides.
The building was damaged due to a strong earthquake, leading to the temporary closure of the third floor.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts style, designed by Emilio Robert and Ricardo de Jaxa Malachowski.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Serves as the seat of the Congress of Peru and has been a central location for legislative activities since the 19th century. It also has historical significance as the site of earlier institutions like San Juan de la Penitencia and the University of San Marcos.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of the Congress of Peru, housing congressional chambers, offices, and hosting presidential inaugurations.
world knowledge.Details: The palace contains the Raúl Porras Barrenechea Hall, the Hall of the Lost Steps, and offices of congressional leaders. Behind the building is José Faustino Sánchez Carrión Square, a public square maintained by Congress.

world knowledge.Name: Dromiskin
world knowledge.Location: 10 km south of Dundalk, about 1 km inland from the Irish coast
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Dromiskin was home to a monastery for hundreds of years, reputedly associated with Saint Patrick. The first bishop was Lughaidh, son of Aengus mac Nadfraoch, the first Christian king of Munster. The village suffered from Viking and Irish plundering, leading to the destruction of the Abbey and dispersal of the monks. It later served as the home to the Archbishops of Armagh for a time.

Major_Events.Description: Áed Findliath, monarch of Ireland, retired to and died at Dromiskin.
Annudh macRuaire rampaged through the territory, destroying Dromiskin and leading to the abandonment of the ecclesiastical site.
Dromiskin saw an increase in population, from 992 in 2006 to 1,195 in 2016.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The old ninth-century round tower and parts of the Abbey still remain. The tower offers a view of Dundalk Bay and the surrounding countryside.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Dromiskin is historically significant due to its association with Saint Patrick, its role as a monastic site, and its connection to the Archbishops of Armagh. The village also reflects the broader historical and cultural developments in Ireland, including Viking raids and ecclesiastical history.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Historically a monastic and ecclesiastical site; currently a residential village.
world knowledge.Details: The village is part of the parish of Darver and Dromiskin, bounded by the Fane River on the north and the Glyde River on the south. The local Gaelic football club, St. Joseph's, was formed in 1961 and covers the entire parish. Bus Éireann route 168 serves Dromiskin Mondays to Fridays.

world knowledge.Name: Tianhe Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tianhe Stadium was constructed on the former site of Guangzhou Tianhe Airport, with construction beginning on 4 July 1984. It was opened in August 1987 for the 1987 National Games of China. The stadium has hosted significant football events, including the final match of the inaugural FIFA Women's World Cup in 1991. It is currently used by Guangzhou Evergrande for football matches.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was opened for this event.
Hosted the final match between the United States and Norway.
Hosted the football finals of the 2010 Asian Games.
Hosted the final match of the AFC Champions League.
Hosted the final match of the AFC Champions League for the second time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass surface, featuring a capacity of 54,856 spectators.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tianhe Stadium is a significant sports venue in China, having hosted major international and national football events. It is a symbol of Guangzhou's sporting culture and history.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is accessible via Guangzhou Metro Line 1 to Tianhe Sports Center Station (East Gate), Line 3 to Linhexi Station (North Gate), and Line 1 or 3 to Tiyu Xilu Station (West Gate and South Gate). It has undergone renovations in 2001, 2009, 2016, and 2018.

world knowledge.Name: Hanna Theatre
world knowledge.Address: East 14th Street Cleveland, Ohio, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hanna Theatre was envisioned by industrialist and publisher Daniel Rhodes Hanna as part of a larger complex in memorial to his father, late U.S. Senator Mark A. Hanna. It opened on March 28, 1921, and was one of the original five venues built in Playhouse Square. The theatre closed in 1989 but was fully restored and reopened in 2008 as the new home of Great Lakes Theater Festival.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre's first production was William Faversham's adaptation of 'The Prince and the Pauper' by Mark Twain. 1,500 people attended despite freezing cold temperatures.
The theatre closed but was later saved from destruction by Ray Shepardson, who launched a campaign to preserve it.
The Hanna Theatre underwent a $14.7 million renovation and reopened as a performing arts center under the management of Great Lakes Theater.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architect Charles A. Platt, the interior decorations included green and gold carpets, dark green seats, frescoed walls, a fireplace, and Louis XVI gilt furniture.
