The ceiling was coffered with circular and octagonal medallions containing gilded classical figures. The stage was forty feet in width and depth, equipped with a thirty-six foot proscenium arch.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Hanna Theatre is a historic venue in Playhouse Square, representing early 20th-century theatre architecture and cultural entertainment in Cleveland. Its restoration preserved its original ornate décor while adapting it for modern use.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre initially had a capacity of 1,421 seats but was reduced to 550 after renovation. It was the last Playhouse Square theater to be renovated, with the process beginning in 1981. The Shubert brothers and Abraham Lincoln Erlanger were key figures in its early management.

world knowledge.Name: Parker's Piece
world knowledge.Address: Bounded by Park Terrace, Parkside, Gonville Place, and Regent Terrace, Cambridge, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parker's Piece is a 25-acre flat and roughly square green common located near the centre of Cambridge, England, regarded by some as the birthplace of the rules of association football. The Cambridge University Football Club Laws were first used on Parker's Piece and adopted by the Football Association in 1863. Before 1613, Parker's Piece was owned by Trinity College. In that year, the college exchanged it with the town of Cambridge for Garrett Hostel Green. Parker's Piece takes its name from Edward Parker, a Trinity College cook who had leased the land from the college since 1587.

Major_Events.Description: A feast for 15,000 guests was held on Parker's Piece to celebrate the coronation of Queen Victoria.
Parker's Piece was used for first-class cricket matches from 1817 to 1864.

Major_Events.Event: Publication of the 1863 Football Association rules
Major_Events.Description: The 1863 Cambridge rules, advertised in sporting newspapers as newly created for a game played on Parker's Piece, played a significant role in the creation of the first laws of the Football Association.
A monument titled "Cambridge Rules 1848" was installed on Parker's Piece. The monument consists of four stone pillars, engraved with the 1856 Cambridge Rules translated into several languages.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Flat and roughly square green common with two main diagonal walking and cycling paths and a single lamp-post known as Reality Checkpoint.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parker's Piece is culturally significant as it is regarded by some as the birthplace of the rules of association football. The Cambridge Rules established here became the defining influence on the 1863 Football Association rules.
world knowledge.Details: Parker's Piece is known today chiefly as a spot for picnics and games of football and cricket, and serves as the games field for nearby Parkside Community College. Fairs tend to be held on the rougher ground of Midsummer Common. Daytime events and concerts are occasionally held on the Regent's Terrace side of Parker's Piece, while the north-western quarter is still maintained as a venue for league cricket.

world knowledge.Name: Castello di Vezio
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Castello di Vezio is a castle located nearby Varenna and Perledo, northern Italy. It was built in the late 11th-early 12th century and was restored several times in the following centuries. In the late 19th century, and in 1956, remains of tombs from the Iron Age, as well as weapons and armors, were found in the area. The castle also had dungeons built during the First World War, as part of the defensive linea Cadorna planned by General Luigi Cadorna, Chief of Staff of the Italian army, to halt any German invasion southward from Switzerland. It currently houses gardens and a group of birds of prey, raised by a local falconer. It became open to the public in 1999. The tower houses a permanent exhibition dedicated to Lariosaurus, an extinct sea reptile from the Middle Triassic period, which takes its name from the lake after its discovery in Perledo in 1830. The castle is currently owned by the Greppi family from Milan.

Major_Events.Year: Several times in the following centuries
Major_Events.Description: The castle was restored several times after its initial construction.
Remains of tombs from the Iron Age, as well as weapons and armors, were found in the area.
Dungeons were built as part of the defensive linea Cadorna planned by General Luigi Cadorna to halt any German invasion southward from Switzerland.
The castle became open to the public.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Characterized in the main tower by square merlons, similar to Cly Castle in Aosta Valley.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The castle is significant for its historical role in defense during the First World War and its current role in housing a permanent exhibition dedicated to Lariosaurus, an extinct sea reptile.
world knowledge.Details: The castle currently houses gardens and a group of birds of prey, raised by a local falconer. The tower houses a permanent exhibition dedicated to Lariosaurus, an extinct sea reptile from the Middle Triassic period, which takes its name from the lake after its discovery in Perledo in 1830. The castle is currently owned by the Greppi family from Milan.

world knowledge.Name: Ignatyevo Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ignatyevo Airport is an international airport in Amur Oblast, Russia, located near the village of Ignatyevo. The construction began in 1959 next to the village of Ignatyevo. The first terminal was made of wood and was located approximately on the spot where the current terminal stands. During the early 1990s, the airport's activity declined due to economic difficulties following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. In July 1997, the Governor of Amur Oblast signed a decree on the establishment of Airport Blagoveshchensk, a unitary enterprise fully owned by the government of Amur Oblast to own and operate Ignatiyevo Airport. In the 2000s, a partial reconstruction of the airport began to increase the volume of transportation and improve the quality of passenger service. In 2007, plans for the construction of a new terminal were resumed after being halted in 1988, and it was commissioned in December 2010.

Major_Events.Description: The Governor of Amur Oblast signed a decree on the establishment of Airport Blagoveshchensk, a unitary enterprise fully owned by the government of Amur Oblast to own and operate Ignatiyevo Airport.
IrAero Flight 103, operated by Antonov An-24 RA-46561, overran the runway on landing. Of the five crew and 31 passengers on board, twelve people were injured.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The first terminal was made of wood. The current terminal was commissioned in December 2010.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ignatyevo Airport is a significant transportation hub in Amur Oblast, facilitating both civilian and military air traffic. It plays a crucial role in the region's connectivity and economic development.
world knowledge.Details: Ignatyevo Airport is state-owned by Amur Oblast and jointly operated with the Russian Air Force, with a military pad on the north-west side of the airport. It services up to medium-sized airliners with parking space for 44 civilian aircraft and conducts 24-hour flight operation.

world knowledge.Name: Government House of Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Government House refers to the offices of the Prime Minister of Thailand and appointed cabinet ministers. It was originally called Baan Norasingha and was intended as a family residence for General Chao Phraya Ram Rakop. It became the prime minister's office in 1941. The main building was designed by Annibale Rigotti and later completed by Corrado Feroci and Ercole Manfredi.

Major_Events.Description: People's Alliance for Democracy (PAD) protesters besieged Government House. The cabinet temporarily moved to Don Mueang International Airport.
Government House was besieged again during the 2013–2014 Thai political crisis.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Venetian Gothic style with Byzantine art elements. The main building is crowned with a golden dome housing a statue of Phra Phrom and its façade resembles that of the Ca' d'Oro Palazzo in Venice.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the official office of the Prime Minister of Thailand and a site for state functions and receptions of foreign guests.
world knowledge.Details: The Thai-Khu-Fah Building is an important building on the Government House grounds, housing the Cabinet of Thailand and the Office of the Prime Minister. The Phitsanulok Mansion nearby is the official residence of the prime minister. The building has two floors with a neo-Venetian Gothic architecture combined with Byzantine art and one staircase. On the roof there is a small shrine to Phra Phrom. Downstairs are three lounges: the Golden Dome Room, the Ivory Room, and the Purple Room. The building has a small conference room called the Green Room for the Board of Committees, chaired by the prime minister. The upper floor houses the prime minister's office, the offices of political officers, and the old cabinet conference room.

world knowledge.Name: Red Terror Martyrs' Memorial Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Red Terror Martyrs' Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa was established in 2010 as a memorial to those who died during the Red Terror under the Derg government.

Major_Events.Description: A period of violent political repression in Ethiopia under the Derg government, targeting citizens who opposed the regime.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum serves as a memorial to the victims of the Red Terror, preserving the history and memory of the atrocities committed during that period.
world knowledge.Details: The museum has displays of torture instruments, skulls and bones, coffins, bloody clothes, and photographs of victims. It offers free tours where guides describe the history leading up to the Red Terror, the actions taken toward citizens who opposed the Derg, how the prisoners were treated, and how they secretly communicated among each other. The museum also features a pictorial history of the Red Terror.

world knowledge.Name: Grand Park of Tirana
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Grand Park of Tirana, also known as the Park on the Artificial Lake, is a 289-hectare public park located in the southern part of Tirana, Albania. It was built between 1955 and 1956 based on a Bulgarian plan and was initially called the Gogo stable. The park includes an artificial lake, the Saint Procopius Church, the Presidential Palace, and memorials to several Albanian personalities. It has been a significant public space for the citizens of Tirana, offering a relaxing environment with diverse flora and fauna.

Major_Events.Description: The Municipality organized the 'Green Fair' to collect ideas for the rehabilitation of the park.
A competition was held to create an urban and ecologic masterplan for the future of the district, aiming to develop a new dense urban neighborhood with public facilities at the shore of the lake.
Albania unveiled a Holocaust memorial at an entrance to the park to honor the dead and the Albanians who protected Jews from the Nazis.
A competition was held to design the park's entrance, which sparked controversy due to the potential impact on the park's integrity.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse range of plants, an artificial lake, and several landmarks including the Saint Procopius Church, the Presidential Palace, and various memorials. The park also includes a Botanical Garden, a Zoo, and an amphitheatre.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Grand Park of Tirana is culturally significant as it serves as a major public space for the citizens of Tirana, offering a relaxing environment with diverse flora and fauna. It also includes memorials to significant historical figures and events, including a Holocaust memorial honoring those who protected Jews during WWII.
world knowledge.Details: The park has faced issues with litter, pollutants, and crime. Major construction plans have sparked controversy due to the potential reduction of green areas. The Botanical Gardens are set to be destroyed to build the new Tirana ring motorway. The park is often referred to as the 'Lung of the City' due to its diverse plant life.

world knowledge.Name: National Library of Mauritania
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Library of Mauritania, established in 1965, is located in Nouakchott, Mauritania, within the building of the National Museum of Mauritania. It serves as a repository of national knowledge with a collection of 10,000 volumes and employs 41 staff members.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The library is a significant cultural institution in Mauritania, preserving national literature and knowledge.
world knowledge.Details: The library has seven branches and operates under a legal deposit system. It is directed by Mohamed Mahmoud Ould.

world knowledge.Name: Maputo City Hall
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Maputo City Hall, also known as the Municipal Council Building of Maputo, is the seat of the local government of the capital of Mozambique. It was erected in 1947 following a competition won by the Portuguese-Brazilian architect Carlos César dos Santos in 1938. The building was constructed to address the growing needs of the colonial city of Lourenço Marques (now Maputo). It became the focal point of the city due to its strategic location and neoclassical design.

Major_Events.Description: The Maputo City Hall was inaugurated as the new seat of the Lourenço Marques government.
After Mozambique's independence, the building continued to serve as the seat of the Maputo city government.
The Maputo City Hall was added to the list of cultural monuments of Maputo.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features a neoclassical design with a trapezoidal layout situated on a hill. It has a façade of 65 metres and follows the architectonic beaux-art rules. Due to financial constraints, artificial stone was used instead of dimension stone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Maputo City Hall is culturally significant as it represents the architectural and administrative history of Maputo, from its colonial past to its role as the capital of independent Mozambique. It is also listed in the Portuguese heritage database Sistema de Informação para o Património Arquitectónico (SIPA).
world knowledge.Details: The building is listed in the Portuguese heritage database Sistema de Informação para o Património Arquitectónico (SIPA) under the number 31708.

world knowledge.Name: Pilot Knob State Park
world knowledge.Address: southeast of Forest City, Iowa, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pilot Knob State Park is one of the oldest state parks in Iowa, founded in 1923. A group of local citizens contributed $7,000 to buy the land in 1920, and the state acquired it in 1921. The park was partially developed in the 1920s, with major buildings and structures built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in 1934. The park has grown and evolved over the years, with several structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Major_Events.Description: Local citizens contributed funds to buy the land, which was later acquired by the state and dedicated as a park in 1923.
The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) built several major buildings and structures and landscaped the park.

Major_Events.Event: National Register of Historic Places listings
Major_Events.Description: Several structures and areas within the park were listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features structures designed in the rustic style, including an observation tower, picnic shelter, amphitheater, and entrance portals. Materials used include rubble granite, random rubble limestone, and round timbers. The observation tower rises to 33.6 feet, and the picnic shelter measures 25.75 by 42.5 feet. The amphitheater measures 128 by 130 feet and features wood plank seating on stone piers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Pilot Knob State Park is culturally and historically significant as one of Iowa's oldest state parks and for its CCC-built structures. It includes the only floating sphagnum bog in Iowa and features several structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Details: The park includes Pilot Knob Lake and Dead Man's Lake, a floating sphagnum bog. It offers activities such as boating, fishing, ice skating, hiking, horseback riding, camping, and picnicking. There is also a warming house for winter sports enthusiasts. The adjacent Pilot Knob Recreation Area offers hunting, hiking, and snowmobiling.

world knowledge.Name: Parliament House, Canberra
world knowledge.Address: Parliament House, Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, Australia
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 80 acres (32 hectares), Floor area: 250,000 m² (2,700,000 sq ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parliament House is the meeting place of the Parliament of Australia, replacing Old Parliament House where the Federal Parliament sat from 1927 until 1988. The site was chosen after much debate, with construction beginning in 1981 and the building officially opened on 9 May 1988 by Queen Elizabeth II. It was designed to symbolize democracy and the people's authority over government.

Major_Events.Description: Opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 9 May 1988, marking the anniversary of the opening of the first Federal Parliament in Melbourne in 1901 and the Provisional Parliament House in Canberra in 1927.
A 43.3 kW photovoltaic system was installed, one of the largest in Australia at the time, providing power for lighting in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Romaldo Giurgola of Mitchell/Giurgola & Thorp Architects, the building is mostly buried under Capital Hill, with a large spire topped by an Australian flag. The design includes curved walls dividing the structure into four quadrants, with green and red chambers for the House of Representatives and Senate, respectively. The building features extensive use of Australian granite, marble, and timber marquetry panels depicting native flora and fauna.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Parliament House symbolizes Australian democracy, with its design emphasizing the people's authority over government. It houses the legislative and executive branches of the Australian government and is a gathering place for national events. The building's art collection includes works significant to Australian history and culture.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Serves as the meeting place of the Parliament of Australia and houses the core of the executive branch, including the Cabinet room and offices of the Prime Minister and other federal ministers.
world knowledge.Details: The building includes over 4,500 rooms, a large flagpole (81 m) flying a 12.8 x 6.4 m Australian flag, and public spaces like the Great Hall and Members' Hall. The forecourt features a mosaic by Indigenous artist Michael Nelson Jagamarra, symbolizing Aboriginal connection to the land. The building has faced criticism for its design, which some believe discourages collegiality among members. It also hosts private events and has a significant solar power system.

world knowledge.Name: University of Liverpool
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Liverpool was founded in 1881 as University College Liverpool, affiliated with Victoria University. It received its Royal Charter in 1903, allowing it to award degrees independently. It is recognized as the original redbrick university, inspired by the Victoria Building. The university has been a pioneer in various academic fields and has a rich history of notable achievements and contributions.

Major_Events.Description: Oliver Lodge, a professor at the university, made the world's first public radio transmission.

Major_Events.Event: First surgical X-ray in the UK
Major_Events.Description: Oliver Lodge took the first surgical X-ray in the United Kingdom.
The university received its Royal Charter, becoming an independent institution.
Sir Charles Sherrington discovered the synapse.

Major_Events.Event: Founding member of the Russell Group
Major_Events.Description: The university became a founding member of the Russell Group, a collaboration of leading research-intensive universities.
The university established the first Sino-British university in China.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university is known for its redbrick architecture, particularly the Victoria Building, which has been restored as the Victoria Gallery and Museum. The campus features a mix of historic and modern buildings, including the Central Teaching Hub.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Liverpool is culturally significant as the original redbrick university and a pioneer in various academic fields. It has produced ten Nobel Prize laureates and has made significant contributions to science, medicine, and technology.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Liverpool is a founding member of the Russell Group and the N8 Group. It has a significant endowment and a large student body. The university is involved in various research initiatives, including contributions to the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. It also has a strong focus on sustainability and has established the Interdisciplinary Centre for Sustainability Research (ICSR) to tackle the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

world knowledge.Name: Samui Airport
world knowledge.Location: Bo Phut, Ko Samui, Surat Thani, Thailand
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Samui International Airport, also known as Ko Samui Airport or Koh Samui Airport, is a privately owned international airport on the island of Ko Samui in Thailand. It was built by Bangkok Airways and officially opened in April 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was officially opened on 25 April 1989.
Thai Airways International operated two daily flights from Bangkok between 2008 and 2018.
Scoot started a Singapore-Koh Samui route operated by the Embraer E190 jet starting from 13 May 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has a unique, open-air design, with the indoor areas being the gift shop, ticket office, toilets, and VIP lounge area. It has terminals (domestic and international), plus a building for check-in and baggage claim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Samui Airport is the country's seventh-busiest airport, handling more than a million passengers annually. It serves as a key gateway to the island of Ko Samui, a popular tourist destination in Thailand.
world knowledge.Details: Samui Airport is located roughly 2 km north of Chaweng, the main city and largest resort centre on the island. It is near the Big Buddha Pier, where ferries depart for Ko Pha-ngan. High-speed ferries to Ko Tao and Chumphon depart from the Maenam Beach Pier, approximately 6 km northwest of the airport. Since the airport is privately owned by Bangkok Airways, it has a near-monopoly on flights.

world knowledge.Name: Lo So Shing Beach
world knowledge.Location: Lo So Shing, west of Lamma Island, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Lo So Shing Beach was gazetted by the Hong Kong Government and opened in 1972.

Major_Events.Event: Temporary closure due to oil pollution
Major_Events.Description: The beach had to be temporarily closed in June and August 2015 due to oil pollution at the sea that caused the public not to swim at the beach.

Major_Events.Event: Temporary closure due to oil pollution
Major_Events.Description: The beach had to be temporarily closed in August 2017 also due to oil pollution.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Lo So Shing Beach is a quiet and remote beach, often practically deserted even on weekends, making it a unique getaway spot in Hong Kong.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department of the Hong Kong Government and is rated as Grade 1 by the Environmental Protection Department for its water quality. It is accessible from the Lamma Island Family Walk and has no road connection. Features include barbecue pits.

world knowledge.Name: University of Madeira
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Madeira (UMa) is a Portuguese public university established in September 1988 in Funchal, Madeira. Its campus dates back to a 16th-century Jesuit college. The first higher education institution, a medical school, was founded in Funchal in the 18th century. In 1978, the University of Lisbon established a satellite campus in Madeira, and from 1983 to 1986, today's campus began taking shape, offering courses in science and technology, arts, humanities, and social sciences. In 1996, the Portuguese government and the University of Lisbon formally established the University of Madeira as an independent institution.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the University of Madeira
Major_Events.Description: The University of Madeira was formally established as an independent institution.
The university celebrated its 20-year anniversary.
Madeira's Mathematics and Engineering Department, along with Carnegie Mellon's Human Computer Interaction Institute (HCII), established a dual-degree Master's in Human-Computer Interaction program.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Madeira is a significant educational institution in Madeira, offering a wide range of academic programs and fostering international partnerships, particularly with Carnegie Mellon University.
world knowledge.Details: The university offers first, second cycle, and Doctorate academic degrees in various fields. It is under the CMU/Portugal agreement with Carnegie Mellon University, offering master programs in Computer Engineering, Human Computer Interaction, and Entertainment Technology. The Madeira Interactive Technologies Institute, founded in January 2010, focuses on building international partnerships with other educational institutes and industry. The Academic Association of UMa (AAUMA) provides extracurricular activities for students, including film screenings, sports events, boating trips, and volunteer opportunities.

world knowledge.Name: Playa Baracoa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Playa Baracoa was founded in 1862 on a sugar cane mill named San Cristóbal de Baracoa, established in the 18th century. Between 1930 and 1940, members of the upper class from Havana built summer houses in the village, many of which still stand today.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The village features wooden houses built by the upper class in the 1930s and 1940s, some of which are still used as summer residences.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Playa Baracoa is part of the Havana metropolitan area and has historical significance as a summer retreat for Havana's upper class in the early 20th century.
world knowledge.Details: Playa Baracoa is located along the Atlantic Coast, Gulf of Mexico, and the Straits of Florida. It is near the Latin American School of Medicine (ELAM) and is crossed by the Havana–Mariel motorway. The village spans between the river mouths of Santa Ana and Baracoa and is divided into quarters such as Cinco Casitas, Hollywood, La Loma, and Los Cocos.

world knowledge.Name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Opened in 1969, the Hakone Open-Air Museum is Japan's first open-air museum. It is affiliated with the Fujisankei Communications Group media conglomerate.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is split into five indoor exhibitions and features outdoor interactive sculptures. It includes the Picasso Pavilion hall, showcasing around 300 of Picasso's works.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is culturally significant as it houses over 1,000 artworks, including pieces by renowned artists such as Pablo Picasso, Henry Moore, and Constantin Brâncuși. It also features 120 sculptural works on permanent display.
world knowledge.Details: The museum offers outdoor interactive sculptures for children and a naturally fed onsen footbath for guests. It includes works by artists like Taro Okamoto, Yasuo Mizui, Churyo Sato, Susumu Shingu, Barbara Hepworth, Rokuzan Ogiwara, and Kōtarō Takamura.

world knowledge.Name: Al Akhawayn University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Al Akhawayn University was founded by Royal Decree (Dahir) in 1993 and officially inaugurated by the former King Hassan II of Morocco on January 16, 1995. The university was largely funded by King Fahd of Saudi Arabia from an endowment initially intended for an oil spill cleanup off the coast of Morocco, which was never realized as the wind blew the oil spill away.

Major_Events.Description: The university was officially inaugurated by the former King Hassan II of Morocco on January 16, 1995.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is culturally significant as it represents a collaboration between Morocco and Saudi Arabia, symbolized by its name 'al-akhawayn,' meaning 'the two brothers,' referring to the two respective kings. It also plays a crucial role in promoting higher education in Morocco based on the American liberal arts model.
world knowledge.Details: Al Akhawayn University is an independent, public, not-for-profit, coeducational university located in Ifrane, Morocco, 70 km from the imperial city of Fez. The medium of instruction is English, and it offers undergraduate and graduate programs in the Humanities and Social Sciences, Science and Engineering, and Business Administration.

world knowledge.Name: Maastricht Aachen Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Maastricht Aachen Airport, originally constructed as a temporary airfield by the USAAF Ninth Air Force during World War II, was later developed into a major cargo hub and regional passenger airport. It has undergone numerous expansions and upgrades since its inception.

Major_Events.Description: The USAAF Ninth Air Force constructed a temporary airfield near Maastricht to support the advancing front during World War II.
The first civilian aircraft landed on 26 September 1945, operated by the Regeeringsvliegdienst.

Major_Events.Event: Pope John Paul II's open-air mass
Major_Events.Description: Pope John Paul II held an open-air mass for 50,000 people at the airport during his visit to the Netherlands.
Air Force One carrying US president George W. Bush landed at the airport.
Ryanair announced Maastricht as a new base, the first on Dutch soil, with one Boeing 737-800 based at the airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features multiple runways, including a main runway of 2,750 meters, and has undergone several upgrades such as the installation of an ILS system and category III ILS for low visibility landings.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport serves as a major cargo hub and regional passenger airport, facilitating international trade and travel. It also hosts the Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre (MUAC) of EUROCONTROL.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is a focus city for Corendon Dutch Airlines and has undergone significant infrastructure investments since its privatization in 2004. It is located along motorway A2 and offers various transportation options including bus services and cycling routes.

world knowledge.Name: Guru Gobind Singh Stadium

Major_Events.Description: Kabbadi matches are organized at this stadium.
Live music shows are organized at this stadium.
Award ceremonies are organized at this stadium.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with floodlights, Bermuda Grass surface, and parking lots on each side.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is used by locals for fitness activities like jogging, playing football, and weight-lifting, and hosts various cultural and sports events.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for football matches and fitness activities.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a capacity of 22,000 people and is owned by the Punjab Football Association. It opens at 5:00 a.m. and closes at 10:00 p.m. daily.

world knowledge.Name: Boris Yeltsin Presidential Center
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Boris Yeltsin Presidential Center, also known as the Yeltsin Center, is a social, cultural, and educational center opened in Yekaterinburg in 2015. It was established in accordance with the 2008 law 'On centers of historical heritage of presidents of the Russian Federation ceased to carry out its powers' for the preservation, study, and public presentation of the heritage of the first President of the Russian Federation, Boris Yeltsin.

Major_Events.Description: The center was unveiled on November 25, 2015, attended by about 500 people including President Vladimir Putin, Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev, Yeltsin's widow Naina, Yeltsin's daughter Tatyana, and other cultural figures.

Major_Events.Event: Recognition as the best museum in Europe
Major_Events.Description: The Yeltsin Center was recognized as the best museum in Europe by the Council of Europe, the first of the museums in Russia.
In June 2023, Russia began an investigation into the Yeltsin Center on grounds of potential 'foreign agent activity'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architect of the project is Boris Bernaskoni, the founder of BERNASKONI interdisciplinary bureau that works on the intersection of architecture, communication, art, and industrial design.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Yeltsin Center is culturally significant as it preserves, studies, and publicly presents the heritage of Boris Yeltsin, the first President of the Russian Federation, in the context of the recent history of Russia, the development of democratic institutions, and the rule of law.
world knowledge.Details: The Yeltsin Center has been criticized for 'distortion of historical events' and 'propaganda.' It has hosted various events such as the Ekaterinburg Jewish Film Festival and has been the subject of public protests demanding its closure. The museum consists of 9 rooms and has hosted over 250,000 visitors in its first year of operation.

world knowledge.Name: Phoenix Art Museum
world knowledge.Address: 1625 North Central Avenue, Phoenix, Arizona 85004, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Phoenix Art Museum was established on November 18, 1959, as part of a community effort that began in 1912 with the Phoenix Women's Club. The museum has undergone several expansions, including in 1965, 1996, and 2006, growing from 25,000 square feet to its current size. It has hosted over 400 exhibitions and houses more than 18,000 works of art.

Major_Events.Description: The Phoenix Art Museum officially opened on November 18, 1959, and was dedicated on November 21, 1959.
The museum was enlarged from 25,000 square feet to 72,000 square feet.
Led by Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects, the museum more than doubled its size, adding new galleries, a theater, a research library, and other facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the Ellen and Howard C. Katz Wing for Modern Art
Major_Events.Description: This wing, along with other new facilities, was opened as part of the 2006 expansion.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum was designed by architect Alden Dow and expanded by Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects. It features a cantilevered canopy at the north entrance, creating an outdoor pavilion area. The museum includes a landscaped Sculpture Garden and modern exhibition spaces.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Phoenix Art Museum is the largest museum for visual art in the southwest United States and has been designated a Phoenix Point of Pride. It serves as a community center, hosting festivals, performances, and educational programs. Its collection includes over 18,000 works of art from various cultures and periods.
world knowledge.Details: The museum offers educational programs, including a nationally competitive internship program. It houses the Lemon Art Research Library, the largest specialized fine arts library in the region. The museum's revenue comes largely from community support, with government and corporate contributions making up smaller portions.

world knowledge.Name: Palacký University Olomouc
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Palacký University Olomouc is the oldest university in Moravia and the second-oldest in the Czech Republic. Established in 1573 as a public university led by the Jesuit order, it initially taught only theology, later expanding to include philosophy, law, and medicine. It played a significant role in the Counter-Reformation and has undergone various transformations, including state-directed reforms and closures during political upheavals. It was fully re-established in 1946 and named after František Palacký, a 19th-century Moravian historian and politician.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established by the Jesuit order in Olomouc, initially teaching theology.
The university became increasingly state-directed following reforms by Bohemian King Joseph II.
University students and professors played an active role in the democratisation movement.
Most faculties were closed by King Francis Joseph I, but they were reopened in 1946.
The university was fully re-established and renamed Palacký University Olomouc.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university features a mix of Baroque and modern architectural styles, with several buildings constructed during the Jesuit period and later expansions.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is a symbol of the Counter-Reformation in Moravia and has played a crucial role in the region's educational and cultural development. It is also significant for its contributions to the Czech National Revival.
world knowledge.Details: The university comprises eight faculties: Theology, Arts, Law, Medicine and Dentistry, Education, Science, Physical Culture, and Health Sciences. It has a student population of around 24,000 and is known for its research contributions in various fields, including medicine, law, and the humanities.

world knowledge.Name: Ranthambore National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ranthambore National Park was established as the Sawai Madhopur Game Sanctuary in 1955, initially covering an area of 282 km² (109 sq mi). It was declared one of the Project Tiger reserves in 1974 and as a national park in 1980. The park is named after the historic Ranthambore Fort, which lies within the park and was built in the 10th century by Chahamanas of Ranastambhapura.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment as Sawai Madhopur Game Sanctuary
Major_Events.Description: Initially covering an area of 282 km² (109 sq mi).
Part of the Project Tiger initiative to protect Bengal tigers.
Expanded to cover a total area of 1,334 km² (515 sq mi).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features dense tropical dry forest, open bushland, and rocky terrain interspersed with lakes and streams. It includes the Ranthambore Fort, built in the 10th century, and three red stone temples devoted to Ganesh, Shiva, and Ramlalaji. There is also a Digamber Jain temple of Sumatinatha and Sambhavanatha.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Ranthambore National Park is culturally and historically significant due to its association with the Ranthambore Fort and its role in wildlife conservation, particularly for the Bengal tiger. It also provides important ecological services such as gene-pool protection, water provisioning, and carbon sequestration.
world knowledge.Details: The park hosts over 300 species of trees, including over 100 of medicinal importance. It is home to many wild animals, including chital, sambar, blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai, langurs, rhesus macaques, jackals, striped hyenas, jungle cats, caracals, leopard, tiger, and sloth bear. The park also hosts over 270 species of birds. As of the 2022 census, there were 52 tigers in the national park. Economic valuation of the tiger reserve estimated its annual flow benefits at 8.3 billion rupees.

image_name: Ivano-Frankivsk National Technical University of Oil and Gas

world knowledge.Name: Ivano-Frankivsk National Technical University of Oil and Gas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1967, the university has been known for preparing qualified and experienced specialists for the oil and gas industries. It has expanded to offer education in economics, management, and law that is directly related to the needs of the energy industry.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university plays a crucial role in educating specialists for the oil and gas industries, contributing significantly to the energy sector in Ukraine.
world knowledge.Details: The university employs a two-pronged approach toward education: theoretical knowledge in classrooms and practical experience through university "field-classrooms" and internships with regional businesses and organizations.

world knowledge.Name: Kwun Yam Beach
world knowledge.Address: Kwun Yam Wan, East Coast of Cheung Chau, Hong Kong
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kwun Yam Beach, also known as Afternoon Beach, is a gazetted beach facing Kwun Yam Wan on the east coast of Cheung Chau, Hong Kong. The name Kwun Yam refers to the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. The beach was gazetted by the Hong Kong Government and opened in 1971.

Major_Events.Description: A body of a 52-year-old angler was found at the beach more than a day after he was reported missing.
Since the 1996 Summer Olympics, Kwun Yam Beach had become a tourist spot for local visitors as well as being the home base for Hong Kong's first Olympic gold medallist, windsurfer Lee Lai-shan.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kwun Yam Beach is culturally significant as one of the two gazetted beaches in Cheung Chau and as the home base for Hong Kong's first Olympic gold medallist, windsurfer Lee Lai-shan. The name Kwun Yam refers to the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
world knowledge.Details: The beach is managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department of the Hong Kong Government. It is 100 metres long and rated as Grade 1 by the Environmental Protection Department for its water quality. It is smaller than Cheung Chau Tung Wan Beach. The beach is beautiful, fine, and white and is situated on the east coast of Cheung Chau.

world knowledge.Name: Palazzo Buonaccorsi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Palazzo Buonaccorsi is an 18th-century aristocratic palace, now the civic museum of Macerata. It was built by the Buonaccorsi family, who rose to prominence in the mid-17th century. The palace was constructed on a site with some houses just inside the former medieval city walls. The Buonaccorsi family, led by Simone the Elder, began the project, which was continued by his son Raimondo and other family members. The palace was decorated with significant artworks, including ceiling paintings and canvas paintings depicting episodes from the Aeneid. The family later moved to Rome but returned in 1853 to refurbish the palace.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was built by the Buonaccorsi family, led by Simone the Elder, and continued by his son Raimondo.
After the death of Raimondo, the Buonaccorsi family was elevated to the Roman Patriciate by Pope Benedict XIV, leading them to abandon Macerata for Rome.
The Buonaccorsi family returned to Macerata under Conte Flavio and began needed refurbishments of the palace.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace features 18th-century aristocratic architecture with significant interior decorations, including ceiling paintings by Carlo Antonio Rambaldi and Antonio Dardani, and canvas paintings depicting episodes from the Aeneid. The Sala dell'Eneide (Hall of the Aeneid) is particularly notable for its panels displaying events from Virgil's epic.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Palazzo Buonaccorsi is culturally significant as a representation of 18th-century aristocratic life and art. It houses the Musei Civici di Palazzo Buonaccorsi, which includes a pinacoteca, a carriage museum, and a library, preserving and displaying art and artifacts from the medieval period to modern times.
world knowledge.Details: The palace accommodates the Musei Civici di Palazzo Buonaccorsi, including a pinacoteca, a carriage museum (Museo della Carrozza), and a library (biblioteca "Amedeo Ricci"). The museum galleries feature a broad representation of art from the past centuries, including works by prominent Italian artists.

world knowledge.Name: Chuvash State Pedagogical University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chuvash State Pedagogical University, founded in 1930, is the first national higher educational institution of the Chuvash Republic. It was established by the decree of the Central Executive Committee and the Council of People's Commissars of the RSFSR. In 1934, the departments were reorganized into faculties of History, Language and Literature, Natural Science, and Physics and Mathematics. In 1958, it was named after the Chuvash teacher-educator Ivan Yakovlevich Yakovlev.

Major_Events.Description: The university was founded as the Chuvash State Pedagogical Institute.
Departments were reorganized into faculties of History, Language and Literature, Natural Science, and Physics and Mathematics.
The university was named after Ivan Yakovlevich Yakovlev.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is the first national higher educational institution of the Chuvash Republic and is named after the prominent Chuvash teacher-educator Ivan Yakovlevich Yakovlev.
world knowledge.Details: The university has more than 5,500 students and publishes the newspapers "Pedvuzovets" and scientific journals such as "Bulletin of the I. Ya. Yakovlev ChSPU" and "Bulletin of the I. Ya. Yakovlev CHSPU: The series" Mechanics of the limit state.

world knowledge.Name: Strule Arts Centre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Strule Arts Centre is a multi-purpose arts venue in Omagh, County Tyrone, Northern Ireland. It was built on the site of the former Omagh Town Hall, which was demolished in 2003. The centre opened on 8 June 2007 and is part of a wider regeneration project for the High Street, George Street, and Riverside area of Omagh.

Major_Events.Description: The Strule Arts Centre was officially opened in January 2008 by Edwin Poots, then Minister for Culture, Arts and Leisure, and Margaret Ritchie, Minister for Social Development.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by architects Kennedy Fitzgerald and Associates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Strule Arts Centre is a significant cultural hub in Omagh, contributing to the local arts scene and the broader regeneration of the town centre.
world knowledge.Details: The Omagh tourist information office is located on the ground floor of the Strule Arts Centre. The centre is owned and run by Omagh District Council.

world knowledge.Name: Point Charles Light
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Point Charles Light, established in 1893, is the oldest lighthouse in the Northern Territory. It was constructed to address the high number of shipwrecks near Port Darwin in the 1880s. The lighthouse was built by Chance Bros of Birmingham, England, and shipped to Australia. It was officially opened on 1 February 1893. Over the years, it underwent several modifications, including automation in 1933 and changes to its light source. The lighthouse survived Cyclone Tracy in 1974 and remains operational today.

Major_Events.Description: The lighthouse was constructed to improve maritime safety near Port Darwin. It was officially opened on 1 February 1893 by Charles James Dashwood, the Government Resident of the Northern Territory.
The lighthouse was automated and demanned, changing its light source to acetylene gas.
Cyclone Tracy devastated the area, damaging nearby Radio Australia masts but leaving the lighthouse largely intact. A temporary low-powered lamp was installed shortly after.
The tower was fully electrified, and a powerful 1,000,000 cd lamp was installed, later replaced by a solar-powered light.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The lighthouse is a 105 feet (32 m) hexagonal tower with a central cylinder, balcony, and lantern. It is constructed of cast wrought iron and features a red tower with a horizontal white band and white lantern. The original lens was a 1st order Chance Brothers dioptric lens.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Point Charles Light is the oldest lighthouse in the Northern Territory and played a crucial role in maritime safety. It is listed on the now-defunct Register of the National Estate, reflecting its historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid for maritime traffic approaching Port Darwin.
world knowledge.Details: The lighthouse is currently operated by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority and is powered by solar energy. It emits a white flash every five seconds, visible for 17 nautical miles. Public access to the site has been restricted at times due to leasing agreements with broadcasting services.

world knowledge.Name: Kampala Serena Hotel
world knowledge.Address: Kintu Road on Nakasero Hill, Kampala Central Division, Kampala, Uganda
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kampala Serena Hotel opened on 31 July 2006 after eighteen months of renovations and refurbishment at a cost of US$30.5 million. It is part of the Serena Hotels Group. The adjacent International Conference Center was constructed in 1975 to host the 13th Summit of the Organization of African Unity (OAU). The venue was subsequently used by Idi Amin's regime for personal activities and, according to some sources, for the torture of Amin's opponents and enemies.

Major_Events.Description: The hotel hosted Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom for four nights during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2007 in Kampala.

In March 2016, the hotel began renovations to create 36 new residential rooms, a new state-of-the-art suite, and refurbish meeting rooms. The US$8 million expansion was partly funded by PROPARCO of France and lasted 12 months.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The hotel features a 7-floor building with 152 rooms, including thirteen suites, one of which is a presidential suite. The adjacent International Conference Center is a hexagonal building completed by Energoprojekt holding from the Non-Aligned Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Kampala Serena Hotel is a significant landmark in Uganda, hosting international events and dignitaries, including Queen Elizabeth II. It is also a symbol of the country's tourism and hospitality industry, being rated 5-stars by the Uganda Tourism Board.
world knowledge.Details: The hotel is owned by a consortium that includes Tourism Promotion Services (Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development), the Uganda National Social Security Fund, and Proparco, a French property investment company. It has its own helipad for easy transport between the hotel and Entebbe International Airport. The adjacent Kampala Serena International Conference Center has a seating capacity of 1,500 and multilingual translation facilities for up to nine languages simultaneously.

world knowledge.Name: Thousand Islands
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,864 islands, ranging from over 40 square miles to smaller islands
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Thousand Islands region was home to the Iroquois Confederacy and Ojibwa people prior to European colonization. It was a part of the War of 1812 and became a prominent summer resort in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Major_Events.Description: The region was a part of the War of 1812 between the British Empire and the United States, with many sites from the war still present.
The Thousand Islands – Frontenac Arch region was designated a World Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The region features several masonry "castles" built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including Singer Castle and Boldt Castle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Thousand Islands are culturally significant for their historical role in the War of 1812, their status as a summer resort for wealthy families, and their designation as a World Biosphere Reserve.
world knowledge.Details: The Thousand Islands region includes the Thousand Islands National Park, 30 New York state parks, and is known for recreational boating and the origin of Thousand Island dressing.

world knowledge.Name: Riverbanks Zoo
world knowledge.Area: Columbia and West Columbia, South Carolina, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Riverbanks Zoo and Garden was conceived in the early 1960s by Columbia-area businessmen. The idea progressed in 1969 with the creation of the Rich-Lex Riverbanks Park Special Purpose District. The zoo opened on April 25, 1974, after five years of planning, which included considerations for four archaeological sites on the property. The zoo struggled financially initially, leading to the formation of the Riverbanks Zoological Society to raise funds. Palmer "Satch" Krantz was appointed executive director during this period. The original design featured mountainous, moated exhibits for big cats and bears.

Major_Events.Description: The zoo opened to the public after five years of planning.

Major_Events.Event: Zoo II Plan - Aquarium Reptile Complex
Major_Events.Description: A 20,000-square-foot building with a 50,000-U.S.-gallon tank for Pacific coral reef species and exhibits for various reptiles.
An exhibit featuring domestic animals where guests can feed goats and alpacas.
A 70-acre garden with over 4,200 species of plants and a trail system.
Additions included exhibits for African elephants, gorillas, and koalas. The Birdhouse at Riverbanks, opened in 2001, received a Significant Achievement Award from the AZA.
Included a new sea lion and harbor seal exhibit, renovated entrance, otter exhibit, grizzly bear exhibit, and a children's garden.

Major_Events.Event: Bridge to the Wild Plan Announcement
Major_Events.Description: A plan to extend the zoo into the gardens, including new species like orangutans, gibbons, and red wolves, and new facilities like a restaurant.
A female Caribbean flamingo, who had been at the zoo since its opening, died.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo features mountainous, moated exhibits for big cats and bears, a 20,000-square-foot Aquarium Reptile Complex, and various modern exhibits like the African Plains and Ndoki Forest. The botanical garden includes a trail system through hardwood forests.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Riverbanks Zoo and Garden is South Carolina's largest gated attraction, averaging over one million visitors annually. It has won multiple awards, including the Southeastern Tourism Society's Shining Example Award and the SC Parks Recreation and Tourism Governor's Cup Award. The zoo plays a significant role in local education, tourism, and conservation efforts.
world knowledge.Details: Riverbanks Zoo and Garden is home to over 2,000 animals, including mammals, birds, reptiles, and fish. Notable exhibits include African Plains, Aquarium Reptile Complex, Ndoki Forest, and Riverbanks Farm. The zoo is an accredited member of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA). The botanical garden features over 4,200 species of plants and a children's play area called Waterfall Junction. The zoo continues to expand with plans like the Bridge to the Wild project.

world knowledge.Name: Fengjie Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 893 metres (2,930 ft), Width: 18.5 metres (61 ft), Height: 211.6 metres (694 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fengjie Yangtze River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge completed in 2005. It was constructed 110 metres above the original river level, but the reservoir created by the Three Gorges Dam has since increased the water level, reducing the clearance below the bridge.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the bridge began.
The bridge was completed and opened to traffic.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed design with a main span of 460 metres (1,510 ft), making it one of the longest cable-stayed spans in the world. The bridge carries 4 lanes of traffic on the S201 provincial road.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important infrastructure project in Chongqing, facilitating transportation across the Yangtze River and contributing to regional development.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is also known as Kuimen Yangtze River Bridge. The clearance below the bridge was originally 110 metres (360 ft) but has been reduced to 18 metres (59 ft) due to the rising water level from the Three Gorges Dam reservoir.

world knowledge.Name: South Caicos Airport
world knowledge.Area: South Caicos, Turks and Caicos Islands
world knowledge.Historical_Background: South Caicos Airport serves South Caicos, the seventh largest of the Turks and Caicos Islands. It is a public airport located at an elevation of 6 ft (2 m) above mean sea level.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport has one runway designated 11/29 with an asphalt surface.
world knowledge.Details: South Caicos Airport (IATA: XSC, ICAO: MBSC) is an airport serving South Caicos, the seventh largest of the Turks and Caicos Islands. The airport is at an elevation of 6 ft (2 m) above mean sea level. It has one runway designated 11/29 with an asphalt surface measuring 1,826 m × 30 m (5,991 ft × 98 ft). This article about a Caribbean airport is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it. This Turks and Caicos Islands location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by expanding it.

world knowledge.Name: Chungnam National University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chungnam National University (CNU) is one of ten Flagship Korean National Universities located in Daejeon, South Korea. Founded in 1952, its motto is "Creativity, Development, and Service to the community". Situated in the central region of the Korean peninsula, CNU is located near the Daedeok R&D Special District, the Multifunctional Administrative City, the Daejeon Government Complex, and the Headquarters of the Korean Army, Air Force, and Navy.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the College of Humanities
Major_Events.Description: The College of Humanities was established on March 1, 1990, as a separate division from the College of Humanities and College of Law.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a State Policy College of Engineering
Major_Events.Description: In 1994, the College of Engineering was designated a State Policy College of Engineering.

Major_Events.Event: Selection as a specialized college for agriculture and life sciences
Major_Events.Description: In 1996, the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences was selected as a specialized college to cultivate ginseng, fruits, and vegetables.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of the College of Education
Major_Events.Description: The College of Education was established on March 1, 2009, yet the university has been providing teacher training since 1970.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chungnam National University is culturally significant as one of the ten Flagship Korean National Universities, contributing to the development of industry, education, and research in South Korea.
world knowledge.Details: Chungnam National University offers a wide range of academic programs through its various colleges, including the College of Humanities, College of Social Sciences, College of Natural Sciences, College of Economics and Management, College of Engineering, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Law, College of Pharmacy, College of Home Economics, College of Art and Music, College of Veterinary Medicine, and College of Education. The university is known for its strong emphasis on research and collaboration with nearby research centers and industries.

world knowledge.Name: Sioux County Courthouse (Iowa)
world knowledge.Address: Off Iowa Highway 10, Orange City, Iowa
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sioux County was organized on January 20, 1860, on land occupied by the indigenous Sioux until they were forced to abandon it under the terms of the fourth Treaty of Prairie du Chien in 1830. The original courthouse was a log structure on the Big Sioux River in the hamlet of Calliope, Iowa (now part of Hawarden). The county seat was moved to Orange City in 1872, and the present courthouse was completed over 30 years later.

Major_Events.Description: Construction began in June 1902 but was delayed due to the bankruptcy of the construction company, completing in October 1904.
Lightning destroyed the top of the tower, which was replaced with a hip roof and a 10-foot-tall cast bronze statue personifying Justice.
The building was extensively renovated during this period.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places on April 11, 1977.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Classic, muscular Richardsonian Romanesque style, designed by Wilfred Warren (W.W.) Beach. The building features a deep rusticated arch at the principal entrance, six-story central tower, and dark red sandstone with light buff sandstone trim.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse is a high-quality example of Richardsonian Romanesque architecture, unusual for its time in Iowa. It represents the historical and governmental development of Sioux County and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
world knowledge.Details: The clock mechanism was originally weight-driven, built by E. Howard & Co., and later converted to an electric motor. The architect, W.W. Beach, hired William L. Steele as his draftsman, and the two later formed a brief partnership.

world knowledge.Name: Neermahal
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Neermahal, also known as Twijilikma Nuyung (lit. 'Water Palace'), is a former royal palace of the Tripura Kingdom, built by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya Bahadur in 1930. It is the largest water palace in India and was constructed as a summer residence for the royal family. The palace was designed and built by the British company Martin and Burns, blending Hindu and Mughal architectural styles. It took nine years to complete and is the only water palace in Eastern India.

Major_Events.Description: A festival observed by locals for three days, featuring colorful cultural programs, boat races, and swimming competitions in Rudrasagar Lake.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace blends Hindu and Mughal architectural styles, featuring marble and sandstone extensively. It includes balconies, towers, pavilions, bridges, and dome-shaped minars, giving it a fort-like appearance. The palace is divided into two parts: the western side (Andar Mahal) for the royal family and the eastern side, an open-air theatre for cultural events.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Neermahal is culturally significant as the largest water palace in India and the only one in Eastern India. It represents the architectural and cultural heritage of the Tripura Kingdom and the Manikya Dynasty, one of the longest remaining dynasties in the world.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Former royal summer residence and cultural event venue.
world knowledge.Details: The palace has 24 rooms and features two stairways leading down to a landing on the water of Rudrasagar Lake. It also houses one of the most beautiful terrace gardens in India, though its splendor has diminished due to poor maintenance and lack of exposure to tourists.

world knowledge.Name: Marseille Provence Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Marseille Provence Airport, formerly known as Marseille–Marignane Airport, has been managed since 1934 by the Marseille-Provence Chamber of Commerce and Industry. In the 1920s and 1930s, Marignane was one of France's main points of operation for flying boats, serving as a terminal for Pan American World Airways Clipper flying boats. It was also a production site for hydroplanes by Lioré et Olivier.

Major_Events.Description: The airport was opened on 22 October 1922.
In September 2006, the airport opened its new terminal MP2 for budget airlines.

Major_Events.Event: Expansion of shopping and dining options
Major_Events.Description: In 2013, the airport expanded its shopping and dining options, with 30 new shops and restaurants, including the first Burger King restaurant in France since 1997.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features two runways: 13L/31R (3,500 m, asphalt) and 13R/31L (2,370 m, asphalt).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Marseille Provence Airport is the fifth busiest French airport by passenger traffic and third largest for cargo traffic. It serves as a focus city for Air France and has a significant historical role in the development of aviation in France, particularly with flying boats.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: International airport serving Marseille and the surrounding region.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is served by the Vitrolles Marseille Provence Airport rail station on the TER network. A public bus runs between the airport and the station. It serves as a focus city for Air France and an operating base for Ryanair. In 2023, the airport handled 10,800,254 passengers with an 18.1% change from the previous year, and 56,132 tons of freight.

world knowledge.Name: Dent Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Clearwater County, Idaho, U.S. (north of Orofino)
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Overall length: 1,550 feet (472 m); Main span: 1,050 feet (320 m)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Dent Bridge was built in conjunction with the Dworshak Dam by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers during the early 1970s. It replaced a smaller bridge that crossed the river prior to the flooding by the Dworshak Reservoir. The bridge was named after Charles and Katherine Dent, who owned land on the western side of where the bridge now stands. The settlement of Dent was razed prior to being flooded by the reservoir.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed in 1971 at a cost of $7,848,950 to provide local access over the flooded river, now Dworshak Reservoir.
The settlement of Dent was razed prior to being flooded by the Dworshak Reservoir.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Suspension bridge with a main span of 1,050 feet (320 m) and an overall length of 1,550 feet (472 m). Constructed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is vital for local access, connecting Ahsahka to the small community of Elk River. Without it, vehicle access would be blocked off, and building a new road around the reservoir would be expensive and inconvenient.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Provides vehicle access over the Dworshak Reservoir, replacing a smaller bridge that was flooded by the reservoir.
world knowledge.Details: The exact location of the bridge was chosen based on topography suitable for road access and bridge construction. The construction cost was $7.85 million ($60.9 million in 2025 dollars).

world knowledge.Name: University of Bordeaux
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The University of Bordeaux was established by Pope Eugene IV on 7 June 1441 when Bordeaux was an English town. It was abolished in 1793 during the French Revolution and re-opened in 1896. In 1970, it was split into three universities (Bordeaux 1, Bordeaux 2, and Bordeaux 3), and Bordeaux 4 split off from Bordeaux 1 in 1995. Since 2014, these universities (except Bordeaux 3) have been reunited to form the University of Bordeaux.

Major_Events.Description: The university was established by Pope Eugene IV.
The university was abolished during the French Revolution by the National Convention.
The university re-opened as a result of the law of 18 July 1896.
The university was divided into Bordeaux 1, Bordeaux 2, and Bordeaux 3.
Bordeaux 4 split off from Bordeaux 1.
The universities (except Bordeaux 3) were reunited to form the University of Bordeaux.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Bordeaux is a historic institution with roots dating back to the 15th century. It is a major center for education and research in France, contributing significantly to academia and culture in the region.

Details.Motto: Sit lumine illustrant millennii. (French: Que la lumière illumine les millénaires) (English: May the light illuminate the millennia)
Details.Campuses: Bordeaux, Dax, Gradignan, Périgueux, Pessac, and Talence

world knowledge.Name: Christiansborg Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Christiansborg Palace is a palace and government building on the islet of Slotsholmen in central Copenhagen, Denmark. It is the seat of the Danish Parliament, the Danish Prime Minister's Office, and the Supreme Court of Denmark. The palace is home to the three supreme powers: the executive power, the legislative power, and the judicial power. It is the only building in the world that houses all three of a country's branches of government. The present building is the third with this name, following two serious fires in 1794 and 1884. The palace today bears witness to three eras of Danish architecture.

Major_Events.Description: The palace was ruined by a fire, but the showgrounds were saved.
The second Christiansborg burned down, but the showgrounds, including the Riding School, court theatre, and chapel were saved.
Thorvald Jørgensen designed the third (and current) Christiansborg, built in Neo-baroque style in reinforced concrete with granite-covered facades.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is a mix of Baroque, Neoclassicism, and Neo-baroque styles. The main part of the current palace is in the historicist Neo-baroque style, the chapel is in a neoclassical style, and the showgrounds are in a baroque style.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Christiansborg Palace is culturally and historically important as it houses the three supreme powers of Denmark: the executive, legislative, and judicial branches. It is also a symbol of the Danish political system and has been a central administration base since the early fifteenth century.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is roughly divided in the middle, with the Parliament located in the southern wing and the Royal Reception Rooms, the Supreme Court, and the Prime Minister's Office in the northern wing. Several parts of the palace are open to the public, including the ruins of Bishop Absalon's Castle and Copenhagen Castle, which were excavated and made publicly accessible in 1924.

world knowledge.Name: Kopu Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Spanning the Waihou River near the Firth of Thames
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Kopu Bridge, originally named Hauraki Bridge, was completed in 1928 as part of State Highway 25. It was the longest and oldest single-lane bridge in New Zealand's state highway network and the only remaining operational swing bridge. It played a crucial role in connecting the Hauraki Plains and Coromandel Peninsula, marking the shift from river to road transport. The bridge was a significant project under Prime Minister Gordon Coates to develop the rural economy.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was completed, replacing barges and ferries for crossing the Waihou River.
Traffic lights were installed to manage increasing traffic and reduce confrontations between motorists.
A new two-lane bridge opened south of the old bridge to alleviate traffic congestion.
The old bridge was transferred to a community trust with plans to repurpose it as a pedestrian and cycleway.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Design: Swing bridge; Materials: Timber piling, concrete piers, steel plate girder spans; Spans: 23; Longest span: 42.7 m (swing span); Features: Passing bays (later discontinued), swing span creating a 15.3 m wide shipping channel.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is listed as a Category 1 historic place by Heritage New Zealand and is on the IPENZ Engineering Heritage Register. It represents a significant engineering achievement and a shift in transportation dominance from river to road in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a single-lane vehicular bridge, now proposed for pedestrian and cycle use.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was notorious for traffic delays, especially during holidays, with queues up to three hours. A webcam was installed in 2009 to monitor queue lengths. The bridge was deemed unsafe for earthquakes stronger than a 300-500-year return period. The new bridge, completed in 2011, is 587 m long with 16 spans and incorporates cultural designs like waka and taniwha. The old bridge remains under threat of demolition but is advocated for preservation by the Historic Kopu Bridge Society.

world knowledge.Name: Veliko Tarnovo University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The St. Cyril and St. Methodius University of Veliko Tarnovo is a Bulgarian university based in Veliko Tarnovo. It was established on 15 September 1963, inheriting the cultural and education traditions of Turnovo Literary School. In the first academic year, 25 professors, assistants, and teachers came from universities in Sofia and the Bulgarian Academy of Science. The first subjects were Bulgarian Philology, Russian Philology, History, and Art. The university was founded by Aleksandar Burmov and Penio Rusev. In 1971, the school was accredited as Veliko Tarnovo University "St. Cyril and St. Methodius".

Major_Events.Description: The university was established on 15 September 1963, inheriting the cultural and education traditions of Turnovo Literary School.

Major_Events.Event: Accreditation as Veliko Tarnovo University "St. Cyril and St. Methodius"
Major_Events.Description: The school was accredited as Veliko Tarnovo University "St. Cyril and St. Methodius".

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The university is significant for its role in continuing the educational traditions of the Turnovo Literary School and for its contributions to Bulgarian higher education.
world knowledge.Details: The university is divided into 9 faculties and has over 18,000 students. The current rector is Prof. Dr. Dimiter Dimitrov.

world knowledge.Name: Muson Centre
world knowledge.Address: Onikan, Lagos Island, Lagos, Lagos State, Nigeria
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The MUSON Centre (Musical Society of Nigeria) is a performance hall in Lagos. It was established in 1983 on the site of the former 'Love Garden' and its facilities were unveiled by Prince Charles in 1995. The society was founded to provide facilities for classical music performances in Nigeria, especially in Lagos. The need for musical training and instruction spurred the establishment of the Muson School of Music in 1989.

Major_Events.Description: The facilities of the MUSON Centre were unveiled by Prince Charles.
The MUSON choir commenced performances in 1995.

Major_Events.Event: Commencement of MUSON Symphony Orchestra performances
Major_Events.Description: The MUSON Symphony Orchestra, Nigeria’s only professional symphony orchestra at the time, commenced performances in 2005.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The MUSON Centre is a multipurpose civic auditorium located in the centre of Lagos Island, situated between the National Museum, the City Mall, the Onikan Stadium and the former official residence of Nigeria's Governors-General, and adjacent to Tafawa Balewa Square.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: MUSON was founded to provide facilities for classical music performances in Nigeria, especially in Lagos. It represents the Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music (ABRSM) in Nigeria and offers ABRSM theory and practical examinations. The MUSON choir and the MUSON Symphony Orchestra perform regularly at the annual MUSON Festival and during the society’s concert season. The MUSON School of Music is Nigeria’s premier classical music conservatoire for all age groups.
world knowledge.Details: The MUSON Centre includes the Muson Choir, Muson School of Music, Muson Symphony Orchestra, and Muson Festival. It organizes concerts of both Nigerian and Western genres. The MUSON School of Music, founded in 1989 by the Musical Society of Nigeria and accredited by the Federal Government of Nigeria, is a comprehensive institution of music encompassing a basic school of music and the diploma school.

world knowledge.Name: Atatürk Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Atatürk Park is a public park in Mersin, Turkey, created from the fill area of Mersin Harbor dredging in the 1950s. It was designed in the 1970s for coffee houses and open-air theaters and was used for domestic fairs until the 2000s. After the establishment of a new fair ground, the park lost most of its former activities but is now being transformed into a culture park as part of a renewal project.

Major_Events.Event: Establishment of Congress and Exhibition Center
Major_Events.Description: A 3,160 m2 (34,000 sq ft) complex of Congress and Exhibition Center was established in the north east of the park, featuring conference and performance halls, a pool, and related services.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features flower beds, a monument called Refah Şehitleri Abidesi (Martyrs of Refah), and a Congress and Exhibition Center. The park's layout includes a main excursion area by the sea side and an amateur fishermen's club next to the old marina.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park commemorates the deaths of the sunken ship Refah during World War II and the Ottoman frigate Ertuğrul, which sank in Japan in the late 19th century. It is a significant public space in Mersin, serving as a cultural and recreational area.
world knowledge.Details: The park is bounded by the harbour facilities to the east, the old Mersin marina and Efrenk River to the west, and İsmet İnönü Boulevard to the north. The coastal park extends 7 km (4.3 mi) to the south west beyond Müftü river, but the name Atatürk Park is used only for the section between the harbour facilities and the marina.

world knowledge.Name: Mount Edgcumbe House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Mount Edgcumbe House is a Grade II listed building and the principal seat of the Edgcumbe family since Tudor times. The original house was built by Sir Richard Edgcumbe between 1547 and 1553. It was completely gutted during World War II by German bombs in 1941 and restored starting in 1958. The estate was sold to Cornwall County Council and Plymouth City Council in 1971 and has been open to the public since 1988.

Major_Events.Description: The house was completely gutted during World War II by German bombs.
The restoration process began at the 6th Earl's instigation.

Major_Events.Event: Sale to Cornwall County Council and Plymouth City Council
