Major_Events.Description: The 7th Earl sold the estate to Cornwall County Council and Plymouth City Council.
The estate has been open to the public since 1988.
Mount Edgcumbe was the camp site of the "Westcounty Jamboree", a large scout camp of Devon and Cornwall scouts hosting international guests.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The house is a Grade II listed building with interiors restored to 18th-century styles. The estate includes Italian, English, and French style gardens, as well as recent additions like the New Zealand and American gardens (1989) and the Jubilee Gardens (2003).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Mount Edgcumbe House is culturally significant as the principal seat of the Edgcumbe family and one of South East Cornwall's most popular historic tourist attractions. Its gardens and parkland are listed as Grade I in the Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in England.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes the National Camellia Collection, a classic car show held annually, and various other events such as art classes, theatre performances, and a forestry school. The House and the adjoining Earl's Garden are only open to visitors during the summer months, from the beginning of April until the end of September.

world knowledge.Name: Ada Bridge
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total length: 996 m, Width: 45.04 m, Height: 200 m
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Ada Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge over the Sava river in Belgrade, Serbia. It connects the municipalities of Čukarica and New Belgrade. The bridge pylon is located on the tip of the Ada Ciganlija island, which has been reinforced with large amounts of concrete. Construction began in 2008, and the bridge opened on 1 January 2012. The bridge is part of the Belgrade Inner City Semi-Ring Road and provides the only direct connection between New Belgrade and Čukarica.

Major_Events.Description: Construction of the Ada Bridge began.
The Ada Bridge was opened to public traffic on 1 January 2012.
Tram traffic across the bridge started on 4 July 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Cable-stayed bridge with a harp design, A-shaped design, single pylon, and cable-stayed cradle-system. The main span is constructed from 8,600 tons of bridge construction steel, supported by 80 stay cables. The bridge has a post-tensioned, reinforced concrete back span of 200 m.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Ada Bridge has become one of the symbols of Belgrade, frequently featured in music videos, TV serials, movies, commercials, video cards, and photo shoots. It is referred to as the 'most representative bridge in the capital'.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The bridge carries 6 lanes of future Belgrade Inner City Semi-Ring Road, 2 metro lanes, and 2 pedestrian/bicycle lanes, providing a direct connection between New Belgrade and Čukarica.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed by Viktor Markelj and Peter Gabrijelčič. It was constructed by a consortium of companies including Porr AG, Slovenija ceste Tehnika, and DSD Brückenbau GmbH. The total construction cost was €360.2 million. The bridge is designed to reduce traffic passing through the city centre by up to 40%. It is also planned to be part of the future Belgrade Metro lines.

image_name: Casa de Apostas Arena Fonte Nova

world knowledge.Name: Casa de Apostas Arena Fonte Nova
world knowledge.Address: Ladeira da Fonte das Pedras, Nazaré, Salvador, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built to replace the older Estádio Fonte Nova, which collapsed in 2007, killing seven people and injuring forty more. The new stadium was designed by German architects and inaugurated in 2013. It has hosted major international events such as the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, the 2014 FIFA World Cup, and the 2016 Summer Olympics football matches.

Major_Events.Description: The stadium was used as one of the venues for the tournament.
Hosted several matches, including the 5–1 win of The Netherlands over reigning World Champions Spain.
Used as one of the venues for the football competition.
Selected to host matches for the tournament.
A section of the roof collapsed after heavy rain.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The stadium features a modern roof covering all seats, inspired by the AWD-Arena in Hanover, Germany. The roof consists of a lightweight metal structure based on the ray and ring system, covered with a PTFE membrane and supported by external pillars. The design preserves the horseshoe shape of the original stadium with an opening to the Dique do Tororó.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Arena Fonte Nova is a significant sports venue in Brazil, having hosted major international football events. It is also a symbol of modernization and urban development in Salvador, replacing the older, unsafe stadium with a state-of-the-art facility.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Football stadium and multipurpose venue for concerts, entertainment, and business events.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium's naming rights were initially held by Itaipava (2013-2023) and later by Casa de Apostas (2024 onwards). It has a maximum capacity of 47,915 people and is the primary home of Esporte Clube Bahia. The stadium faced some issues during its inaugural match, including blind spots, excessive dust, and puddles.

world knowledge.Name: Stearns County Courthouse
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stearns County Courthouse is the seat of government for Stearns County in St. Cloud, Minnesota. The Beaux-Arts style building was constructed in 1921 to replace Stearns County's original 1864 courthouse. It stands in a prominent square in downtown St. Cloud, flanked by other government buildings. A Prairie School style jail was built to the northeast in 1922, and the two buildings were listed as the Stearns County Courthouse and Jail on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982 for having local significance in the themes of architecture and politics/government. They were nominated for being prominent symbols of Stearns County government. The 1922 jail building was demolished in 1987.

Major_Events.Description: The Beaux-Arts style courthouse was constructed to replace the original 1864 courthouse.
A Prairie School style jail was built to the northeast of the courthouse.

Major_Events.Event: Listing on National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse and jail were listed on the National Register of Historic Places for their local significance in architecture and politics/government.
The 1922 jail building was demolished.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beaux-Arts style (courthouse), Prairie School style (jail). The courthouse was designed by Toltz, King & Day, and the jail was designed by Louis Pinault.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Stearns County Courthouse and Jail were prominent symbols of Stearns County government and were listed on the National Register of Historic Places for their local significance in architecture and politics/government.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of government for Stearns County
world knowledge.Details: The courthouse and jail were part of the Stearns County MRA (Multiple Resource Area) and were added to the National Register of Historic Places on April 15, 1982, with reference number 82003056.

world knowledge.Name: Randers Tropical Zoo
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Total area not specified, but includes three domes: South American dome (2,000 m²), African dome (500 m²), and Asian dome (700 m²)
world knowledge.Construction_Period: 1996 (opened with two domes, third dome built later)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Randers Tropical Zoo, also known as Randers Regnskov, is an indoor zoo located in Randers, Denmark. It opened in 1996 with two domes representing the biomes of Africa and Asia. A third dome representing South America was added later. The zoo features controlled tropical climates within its domes, housing approximately 275 animal species, including 200 in the domes and 75 in a saltwater aquarium. In 2015, an exhibit for jaguars was opened outside the domes.

Major_Events.Description: Randers Tropical Zoo opened with two domes representing the biomes of Africa and Asia.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of the South American dome
Major_Events.Description: The third dome, representing South America, was built after the initial opening.
An exhibit for jaguars was opened, marking the first exhibit located outside the domes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The zoo is housed in three large domes representing the biomes of Africa, Asia, and South America. The domes feature controlled tropical climates, with computer-controlled lighting to simulate tropical daylight hours. The domes are designed to allow most animals to live freely within them.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Randers Tropical Zoo is culturally significant as it provides a unique experience of tropical ecosystems in a non-tropical country. It is an educational and recreational site that promotes awareness of biodiversity and conservation.
world knowledge.Details: The zoo includes a saltwater aquarium, a snakeyard with free harmless snakes, and Danmarksparken ("Denmark Park") with farm animals and playgrounds. It is a member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA).

world knowledge.Name: Parc Olympique Lyonnais
world knowledge.Address: 10 Avenue Simone Veil, Décines-Charpieu, Metropolis of Lyon, France
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Parc Olympique Lyonnais, known for sponsorship reasons as Groupama Stadium, is a 59,186-seat stadium in Décines-Charpieu, in the Metropolis of Lyon. The home of French football club Olympique Lyonnais (OL), it replaced their previous stadium, the Stade de Gerland, in January 2016. The Stade de Gerland became the home of Lyon OU Rugby. It is the third largest stadium in France, behind Stade de France in Saint-Denis (Paris) and Orange Velodrome in Marseille.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted six games at the tournament, including the hosts' 2–1 win over the Republic of Ireland in the last 16, and eventual champions Portugal's 2–0 win over Wales in the semi-finals.
Paris Saint-Germain won 4–1 against Monaco.
Hosted the final on 16 May 2018.
Staged the semi-finals and the final.
Hosted 11 matches, 5 men's and 6 women's.

Major_Events.Event: Outdoor Ligue Magnus ice hockey game
Major_Events.Description: Grenoble defeated Lyon 5–2; the attendance at that game was 25,142, which turned out to be the all-time record attendance for an ice hockey game in France.

Major_Events.Event: European Rugby Champions Cup and European Rugby Challenge Cup finals
Major_Events.Description: Hosted the finals of rugby union's European Rugby Champions Cup and European Rugby Challenge Cup.
One of nine venues chosen for France's hosting of the 2023 Rugby World Cup.
Hosted the match between France and England on the final weekend of the 2024 Six Nations on 16 March 2024.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Designed by Populous, with structural and services engineering by Vinci SA. Features AirFibr hybrid grass surface and 105 executive suites.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in France, hosting major football, rugby, and ice hockey events, as well as musical concerts. It is the third largest stadium in France and has been a key venue for international tournaments like UEFA Euro 2016 and the 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for football matches, also hosting rugby, ice hockey, and concerts.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was built with a construction cost of €480 million and includes state-of-the-art sporting facilities, two hotels, a leisure center, and commercial and business offices. It has a record attendance of 58,664 for a rugby match and 58,230 for a football match.

world knowledge.Name: Lekan Salami Stadium
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The stadium was built on land formerly occupied by the Ibadan race course, which had become unused and occupied by illegal structures. The military government of David Jemibewon initiated the project in 1976 to reclaim the land for a recreational and sports complex. It was opened on May 28, 1988, and named Lekan Salami Stadium in 1998 in honor of Chief Lekan Salami by the Oyo State Military Governor Ahmed Usman.

Major_Events.Description: Shooting Stars FC won the championship in 1993 but later declined in performance.
The stadium was renovated with FIFA-recommended natural grass.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The complex initially included a football field, tennis courts, squash court, and indoor sports hall. Additional facilities for shops were later added.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports venue in Nigeria, serving as the home ground for local teams like Shooting Stars FC. It was named in honor of Chief Lekan Salami, reflecting its cultural importance in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium primarily used for football matches.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium has a seating capacity of 10,000 spectators. Shooting Stars FC drew an average home attendance of 4,421 in the 2023–24 Nigeria Premier Football League.

world knowledge.Name: Central University of Ecuador
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Central University of Ecuador is the oldest and largest university in Ecuador and one of the oldest universities in the Americas. It was established in 1620 and has a significant historical and cultural impact in the region.

Major_Events.Description: The University Choir was created on November 22, 1960, under the direction of Maestro Victor Austrian Bürger. It has represented the Central University of Ecuador both nationally and internationally.

The Art School was founded in 1967, offering programs in ceramics, printmaking, visual arts, fine arts, and performing arts. It continues the tradition of the Fine Arts School of Quito, founded in 1904.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Central University of Ecuador is culturally significant as it is the oldest university in Ecuador and one of the oldest in the Americas. It has played a crucial role in the education and cultural development of the country.
world knowledge.Details: The university has a strong emphasis on medical education and arts. It also has a rich tradition in music and dance, with groups like 'The Chakana' and the University Choir. The university is accessible via the Universidad Central metro station.

image_name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry

world knowledge.Name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry
world knowledge.Address: 1945 SE Water Ave, Portland, OR 97214, U.S.
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1944, OMSI began as a collection of artifacts displayed in Portland City Hall. It moved to various locations before settling in its current site in 1992, which includes a historic power plant. The museum has expanded over the years to include multiple exhibit halls, a planetarium, and a submarine exhibit.

Major_Events.Event: First public planetarium in the Pacific Northwest
Major_Events.Description: A dome on the front lawn of the Hassalo St. location housed the region's first public planetarium.
OMSI relocated to a new site in Washington Park, featuring a hands-on museum and a planetarium.
The museum moved to its current location, integrating the historic Station L power plant and adding an OMNIMAX theater.
The submarine was purchased and opened to the public, later being added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The OMNIMAX theater was converted into a conventional flat-screen theater with an extra-large screen.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum integrates the historic Station L power plant, featuring industrial and modern architectural elements. It includes a distinctive dodecahedral planetarium building from its Washington Park era.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: OMSI is a cornerstone of science education in the Pacific Northwest, offering interactive exhibits, a planetarium, and a submarine. It plays a vital role in promoting STEM education and community engagement.

Educational_Programs: Outreach programs (school presentations, summer camps, star parties)

world knowledge.Name: Dallas County Courthouse (Alabama)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Joseph T. Smitherman Historic Building, completed in 1847, has served various functions over its 160+ years of existence. Initially built as a school for orphans and children of indigent Masons, it later became a Confederate hospital during the American Civil War, a Freedman's Bureau Hospital, the Dallas County Courthouse, a military school, and Vaughan Memorial Hospital. It was preserved and restored under the leadership of Mayor Joseph T. Smitherman and now houses the Vaughan-Smitherman Museum.

Major_Events.Description: Built by the Selma Fraternal Lodge No. 27 of the Free and Accepted Masons as a school for orphans and children of indigent Masons.
Served as a hospital during the American Civil War and later as a Freedman's Bureau Hospital.
Used as the Dallas County Courthouse after Selma became the county seat.
Converted into a hospital and operated until a new hospital building was completed.

Major_Events.Event: Added to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: Recognized for its architectural and historical significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Greek Revival-style three-story red brick structure with a centrally placed tetrastyle portico featuring monumental Ionic columns. The facade has seven bays with stretcher bond brickwork and a belt course between each floor. The pedimented portico covers three central bays with balconies at each upper level, featuring wrought iron railings with an open diamond pattern (crowfoot baluster).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The building is significant for its architectural style and historical roles, including its use as a school, hospital, courthouse, and museum. It reflects the social and civic history of Selma and was preserved due to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Currently serves as the Vaughan-Smitherman Museum, showcasing Selma's history, Civil War artifacts, political collections, and a recreated hospital setting.
world knowledge.Details: The museum houses Civil War collections, slavery documents, political collections, and mid-19th century antique furniture. It also features Native American artifacts, meeting rooms, and parlors for social events.

world knowledge.Name: Wyoming State Capitol
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Wyoming State Capitol was constructed prior to Wyoming gaining statehood. Cheyenne, established in 1867 along the transcontinental railroad, became the seat of the Territorial government in 1869. The capitol was authorized in 1886, with construction beginning the same year. It has undergone several renovations, including a major restoration from 2016 to 2019.

Major_Events.Description: The Ninth Territorial Legislative Assembly authorized the construction of the State Capitol.
The capitol was completed, including the two small wings on the east and west.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of House and Senate Chambers
Major_Events.Description: The House and Senate Chambers were completed to address crowded conditions.
The capitol underwent its first major renovation, including modernization of systems and restoration of original designs.
The capitol was designated a U.S. National Historic Landmark for its role in Wyoming's history, including women's suffrage.
A comprehensive restoration project was completed, including improvements to infrastructure and restoration of historical features.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The building features Renaissance Revival architecture, reminiscent of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. It includes a copper dome covered in 24-carat gold leaf, stained glass imported from England, and sandstone from Rawlins, Wyoming, and Fort Collins, Colorado. The interior features checkerboard marble floors, cherry wood staircases, and murals depicting Wyoming's culture and history.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Wyoming State Capitol is culturally and historically significant as the seat of Wyoming's government and for its role in hosting conventions that ensured women's suffrage in the state constitution. It is also a National Historic Landmark.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Government Building (Houses the Wyoming State Legislature and the office of the Governor of Wyoming)
world knowledge.Details: The capitol's dome is a key architectural feature, visible from all roads entering Cheyenne. The building underwent a major restoration from 2016 to 2019, which included the discovery and restoration of hidden paintings and architectural elements. The dome was re-covered in gold leaf in 2009 and has a life expectancy of 90 years post-restoration. The capitol also features six vaults with unique paintings, originally made by Mosler Safe and Lock Company.

world knowledge.Name: Walters Art Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded in 1934, the Walters Art Museum holds collections amassed by William Thompson Walters and his son Henry Walters. William began collecting during the American Civil War, and Henry expanded the collection and arranged for the construction of the museum. The museum was bequeathed to the City of Baltimore in 1931 for public benefit.

Major_Events.Event: Name change to The Walters Art Museum
Major_Events.Description: Changed from 'The Walters Art Gallery' to reflect its image as a large public institution.
The original main building reopened after a three-year renovation.
Admission became free year-round due to grants from Baltimore City and Baltimore County.

Major_Events.Event: Release of images on Creative Commons
Major_Events.Description: Released nearly 20,000 images of its collections on a Creative Commons license, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Original gallery designed by William Adams Delano in Renaissance-revival style, inspired by Hôtel Pourtalès in Paris. Annex building designed in Brutalist style by Shepley, Bulfinch, Richardson & Abbott, with later renovations by Kallmann McKinnell and Wood, Architects, adding a glass atrium and modern facilities.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The museum is renowned for its extensive collections spanning ancient Egypt, Greece, Rome, medieval Europe, Renaissance and Baroque art, and Asian art. It is one of the best collections of medieval art in the U.S. and has significant holdings in Islamic and Asian art.
Notable_Visitors: Prince of Wales (future King Edward VII)
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collections include masterworks from ancient Egypt, Greek sculpture, Roman sarcophagi, medieval ivories, illuminated manuscripts, Renaissance bronzes, Old Master paintings, Chinese ceramics, Art Deco jewelry, and ancient Near East artifacts. It also features significant works by French academic masters and Impressionists, as well as 18th-century French courtly arts.

world knowledge.Name: Crescent University
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Crescent University is a private university established by Judge Bola Ajibola under the banner of the Islamic Mission for Africa. The Educational Board of the Islamic Mission for Africa (IMA) recommended its establishment in 2002, and it was approved by the National Universities Commission in 2005. The university commenced its academic program in December 2005.

Major_Events.Description: The National Universities Commission approved the establishment of Crescent University, Abeokuta, and it commenced its academic program in December 2005.

Major_Events.Event: Donation of Alhaja Seliat Adebutu Library
Major_Events.Description: The University Library, known as Alhaja Seliat Adebutu Library, was built and donated by Chief Kesington Adebutu in remembrance of his mother.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Crescent University is significant as a private institution established under the Islamic Mission for Africa, promoting academic and moral excellence.
world knowledge.Details: Crescent University has the following colleges: The Bola Ajibola College of Law, The College of Environmental Sciences, The College of Information and Communication Technology, The College of Natural and Applied Sciences, The College of Arts, Social and Management Sciences, and The College of Health Sciences.

world knowledge.Name: National Theatre of Strasbourg
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally built to house the legislative assembly of the regional parliament of Alsace-Lorraine after the area came under German control with the Treaty of Frankfurt (1871). In 1919, Alsace-Lorraine returned to France, and the building was offered to the city of Strasbourg. It was later used by the Strasbourg music conservatory. On 25 September 1944, the east wing was destroyed by American bombing and was reconstructed between 1950 and 1957 with a theatre auditorium replacing the assembly chamber.

Major_Events.Description: The east wing of the building, which contained the Chamber of the Assembly, was destroyed by American bombing.
The building was reconstructed with a theatre auditorium replacing the assembly chamber.
The façade, roofing, and the entrance on Place de la République were classified as a Monument historique.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in Neorenaissance style by architects August Hartel and Skjold Neckelmann. The building features two main rooms: the salle Bernard-Marie Koltès (470 or 600 seats) and the salle Hubert Gignoux (a 200-seat modular room).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theatre of Strasbourg is a significant cultural institution and a historical landmark, representing the architectural and political history of Alsace-Lorraine. It is also a key venue for performing arts in France.
world knowledge.Details: The building originally housed the Strasbourg music conservatory from 1922 until 1995, when it was relocated. The concert hall has remained unused since. In 2016, the monumental pipe organ by Curt Schwenkedel was restored and moved to Saint Stephen’s Church. The TNS also uses two additional theater rooms in Espace Klaus Michael Grüber.

world knowledge.Name: Plantin–Moretus Museum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Plantin–Moretus Museum is a printing museum in Antwerp, Belgium, focusing on the work of the 16th-century printers Christophe Plantin and Jan Moretus. It is located in their former residence and printing establishment, the Plantin Press. The museum has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005. The printing company was founded by Christophe Plantin, who was a major figure in contemporary printing with interests in humanism. After Plantin's death, it was owned by his son-in-law Jan Moretus. The company preserved its collection of older type, unlike most printing concerns of the time. Four women ran the family-owned Plantin–Moretus printing house over the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries. In 1876, Edward Moretus sold the company to the city of Antwerp, and it was opened to the public a year later.

Major_Events.Description: The Plantin–Moretus Museum was inscribed onto the UNESCO World Heritage list.
The museum reopened after a thorough renovation and with a new building, including a reading room and paper heritage depot.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is located in the former residence and printing establishment of Christophe Plantin and Jan Moretus. It features a richly decorated interior and a new building with a facade that refers to a letterbox.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Plantin–Moretus Museum is culturally significant as it preserves the history of printing and the work of Christophe Plantin and Jan Moretus. It houses the two oldest surviving printing presses in the world, complete sets of dies and matrices, an extensive library, and the entire archives of the Plantin business, which were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Programme Register in 2001.
world knowledge.Details: The museum possesses an exceptional collection of typographical material, including the two oldest surviving printing presses in the world and complete sets of dies and matrices. The archives of the Plantin business were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Programme Register in 2001. The museum reopened in 2016 after a thorough renovation and with a new building.

world knowledge.Name: Château d'Anet
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Château d'Anet was built by Philibert de l'Orme for Diane de Poitiers, the mistress of Henry II of France, on the former château at the center of the domains of Diane's deceased husband, Louis de Brézé. It was constructed between 1548 and 1552 and formed around three courts. The château faced destruction in 1595 due to a conspiracy against Henry IV but was saved. It underwent major alterations in the 17th century and was later owned by descendants of Louis XIV. The château was designated as a protected monument historique in 1889.

Major_Events.Description: Built by Philibert de l'Orme for Diane de Poitiers.
Charles, Duke of Aumale, was implicated in a conspiracy, leading to a decree to demolish the château, which was saved by Henry IV.

Major_Events.Event: Major alterations by Louis Joseph, Duke of Vendôme
Major_Events.Description: Many original Renaissance features were removed, and the gardens were redesigned by André Le Nôtre.
The château was designated by the French government as a protected national heritage site.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The château was built partly upon the foundations of a feudal castle and features a centralized Greek cross floor plan under a diagonally-coffered dome in its chapel. Notable elements include the Fountain of Diana and the Nymph of Anet relief by Benvenuto Cellini. The gardens were among the first Italianate parterre gardens in France.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Château d'Anet is a significant example of French Renaissance architecture and garden design. It was built for Diane de Poitiers, a prominent historical figure, and features works by renowned artists like Benvenuto Cellini. The château also played a role in French history, surviving political conspiracies and revolutions.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally built as a residence for Diane de Poitiers, it later served as a luxury estate for various nobles and is now a historical monument.
world knowledge.Details: The château was used as a filming location in the 1965 James Bond film Thunderball and the 1976 film The Pink Panther Strikes Again. The entry pavilion inspired the façade of Robert Venturi's 1966 Guild House for the Elderly in Philadelphia. The chapel contains stained-glass windows made by Charles Lorin from Chartres around 1904.

world knowledge.Name: Englefield House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Englefield House is an Elizabethan country house with a rich history. It was originally home to the Englefield family, confiscated in 1559 from Sir Francis Englefield for consorting with enemies of Elizabeth I. The estate passed through various owners, including the Paulet and Benyon families, and has been a significant historical site with ties to notable figures and events.

Major_Events.Description: The house was confiscated from Sir Francis Englefield for consorting with enemies of the new Protestant monarch, Elizabeth I.
Pippa Middleton married financier James Matthews at St Mark's Church on the Englefield Estate, with a reception held at Englefield House.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Elizabethan architectural style with substantial alterations by Thomas Hopper in the 1820s. The house and its adjoining entrance courtyard are listed Grade II*, with formal gardens and parkland listed at Grade II.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Englefield House is culturally significant due to its historical ties to prominent families, its architectural heritage, and its use as a filming location for numerous movies and TV series. It is also listed on the National Heritage List for England.
world knowledge.Details: The estate includes a 700m grass airstrip and has been used as a filming location for movies like X-Men: First Class, The King's Speech, and TV series like Black Mirror and The Crown. It is currently owned by Richard, Baron Benyon, a former MP.

world knowledge.Name: High Head Castle
world knowledge.Address: Between Carlisle and Penrith, Cumbria, England
world knowledge.Historical_Background: High Head Castle is a large fortified manor house with origins dating back to 1272. Originally a medieval square pele tower within a curtain wall, it was later acquired by Sir William L'Engleys, Chief Forester of Inglewood. The Richmond family extended the house in the 16th century, and the Brougham and Vaux family made further alterations in the 18th century. The castle was largely destroyed by fire in 1956 and is now mostly a ruin.

Major_Events.Description: The castle was largely destroyed by fire, leaving it mostly a ruin.
The Richmond family bought and extended the house.
Henry Richmond Brougham had a new facade built.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The surviving western wing features straight-headed mullioned windows with round-arched lights under hood moulds. The facade built in 1744-1748 is eleven bays long with a pedimented three-bay centre and a walled front garden with coupled Ionic columns. Adjacent is a stable quadrangle with heavy rustication, a steep pediment gable, and cupola.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: High Head Castle is a Grade II* listed building, reflecting its historical and architectural importance. It represents the evolution of fortified manor houses in England from the medieval period through the 18th century.
world knowledge.Details: The castle is currently privately owned and not open to the public. The owners are attempting to restore it. The right-hand wing has had a roof re-instated and may be usable again. The castle was previously occupied by the Hills family and was the childhood home of soldier and astronomer Edmond Hills. The Thornborrow family rented the castle and farmed the land between 1851-1881, and the Cavaghan family lived there from 1921 to 1929.

world knowledge.Name: Sfalassà Viaduct
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sfalassà Viaduct is a 254-metre-high viaduct near Bagnara Calabra, Calabria, Italy. It is the highest and longest span frame bridge in the world and among the 50 highest bridges of any type as of 2019. It is the second highest bridge in Italy after the Italia Viaduct.

Major_Events.Description: The Sfalassà Viaduct won the CECM European award three times.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Beam bridge (Portal frame) made of steel with a main span of 376 metres.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sfalassà Viaduct is significant for its engineering achievements, being the highest and longest span frame bridge in the world.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge is located on Autostrada A2 Salerno-Reggio Calabria Motorway. It was designed by architect Silvano Zorzi and opened in 1974.

world knowledge.Name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
world knowledge.Physical_Area: Height: 112.5 metres (369 ft), Diameter: 100 metres (330 ft)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tempozan Ferris Wheel opened to the public on July 12, 1997, and was the tallest Ferris wheel in the world at the time. It is located next to Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan, one of the largest aquariums in the world.

Major_Events.Description: The Tempozan Ferris Wheel opened on July 12, 1997, becoming the tallest Ferris wheel in the world at the time.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Ferris wheel has a height of 112.5 metres (369 ft) and a diameter of 100 metres (330 ft). It features colored lights that provide a weather forecast for the next day: orange for sunny, green for cloudy, and blue for rain.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tempozan Ferris Wheel is a notable landmark in Osaka, offering panoramic views of Osaka Bay and surrounding areas, including Mount Ikoma, Akashi Kaikyō Bridge, Kansai International Airport, and the Rokko Mountains. Its weather-forecasting lights add a unique cultural feature.
world knowledge.Details: The wheel offers a 17-minute ride with views of the surrounding area. It was surpassed in height by other Ferris wheels in Japan, such as the Daikanransha Ferris wheel in Tokyo and the Sky Dream Fukuoka (now closed). The Diamond and Flower Ferris Wheel in Tokyo also exceeds its height.

world knowledge.Name: Ba Be National Park
world knowledge.Address: Bắc Kạn Province, Northeast region of Vietnam
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Ba Bể National Park was established in 1992 to protect Ba Bể Lake and surrounding limestone and evergreen forests. It is located about 240 kilometers northwest of Hanoi.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as a Wetland of International Importance
Major_Events.Description: Ba Bể National Park was designated as a Wetland of International Importance on 2 February 2011.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a diverse landscape including Ba Bể Lake, limestone forests, evergreen forests, and various caves such as Puong Cave and the Fairy Pond.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its unique natural features, including the largest natural freshwater lake in Vietnam, and its role in local legends, such as the story of Widow Island.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of natural habitats and biodiversity
world knowledge.Details: Ba Bể Lake is the largest natural freshwater lake in Vietnam, with a surface area fluctuating between 3 and 5 km². The lake is fed by the Ta Han, Bo Lu, and Leng Rivers and drains into the Nang River. The park is home to 65 mammal species, 233 bird species, 43 reptile and amphibian species, 106 fish species, and 354 butterfly species. Facilities include an information center, guest houses, a lake management station, and an ecological research station opened in 2004.

world knowledge.Name: Cedar Point Shores
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Cedar Point Shores, originally named Soak City, opened in 1988. It expanded over the years with new slides and attractions, including a wave pool and activity pools in 1997, SplashH20 in 2004, and a major rebranding and expansion in 2016 when it was renamed Cedar Point Shores.

Major_Events.Description: The waterpark opened with ten slides.
Added Main Stream, Tadpole Town, Zoom Flume, Choo Choo Lagoon, and Renegade River.
6.5-acre expansion including a wave pool, activity pools, and multiple enclosed slides.
An interactive water playground was added.
Renamed and expanded to include a new slide complex and family water playground, Lemmy's Lagoon.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Water park featuring various water slides, pools, and interactive water playgrounds.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: A popular water park offering recreational activities for families and visitors, contributing to the local tourism industry.

Details.Operating_season: Memorial Day Weekend to Labor Day

world knowledge.Name: Rock Creek Park
world knowledge.Area: Northwest quadrant of Washington, D.C. to Montgomery County, Maryland border
world knowledge.Address: From Klingle Road in Washington, D.C. to Montgomery County, Maryland border
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Rock Creek Park was established by an Act of Congress in 1890, signed into law by President Benjamin Harrison. It was the third national park in the U.S. and the oldest natural urban park in the National Park System. The park was created following advocacy by civic leaders like Charles C. Glover and expanded over the years to include various recreational and cultural facilities.

Major_Events.Description: President Benjamin Harrison signed the Act of Congress establishing Rock Creek Park.

Major_Events.Event: Addition to National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The Rock Creek Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The skeletal remains of federal intern Chandra Levy were found in the park, drawing national media attention.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Late 19th and 20th Century Revivals, Early Republic, and NPS Rustic styles. Features include Peirce Mill (a water-powered grist mill), various bridges, and park facilities designed by Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. and John Charles Olmsted.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Rock Creek Park is a significant urban green space offering recreational and cultural amenities. It is historically important as one of the earliest national parks and serves as a natural refuge within the city. The park also includes landmarks like Peirce Mill and the Jean Jules Jusserand memorial bench.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and recreational area with facilities for hiking, biking, golf, equestrian activities, and cultural exhibits.
world knowledge.Details: Rock Creek Park is administered by the National Park Service and includes over 2,000 acres when accounting for adjacent green spaces. It features trails, a golf course, equestrian center, and cultural sites like Peirce Mill. The park has been a focal point for urban recreation and conservation efforts since its establishment.

world knowledge.Name: Iloilo City Hall
world knowledge.Address: De la Rama Street, Plaza Libertad, Iloilo City Proper, Iloilo City, Philippines
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iloilo City Hall is the official seat of government of the City of Iloilo. Originally located at the corner of General Luna Street and Infante Street, it was donated to the University of the Philippines Visayas in 1947. The city government temporarily operated from Casa Real de Iloilo before moving to the current location in 2011, which is the first green building in the Visayas.

Major_Events.Description: The new city hall at Plaza Libertad was completed, becoming the first green building in the Visayas.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of Iloilo City Legislative Building
Major_Events.Description: An eight-story legislative building was completed behind the city hall to accommodate city councilors and provide additional office space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neoclassical and Art Deco styles, featuring uniformly arched windows, high ceilings, a dome, and extensive use of patio furniture. It includes eco-friendly innovations like a solar-powered air-conditioning system, rooftop garden, and rainwater harvesting area.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The landmark symbolizes the governance and progress of Iloilo City. It features 'Lin-ay sang Iloilo,' an 18-foot bronze statue atop its dome, representing prosperity, hope, and peace.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Seat of government for the City of Iloilo, housing the Mayor's office, the Iloilo City Council, and various city government offices.
world knowledge.Details: The city hall is connected to the Iloilo City Legislative Building via a bridge. A six-story multilevel parking building is under construction adjacent to the city hall. The statue 'Lin-ay sang Iloilo' was conceptualized by artist Ed Defensor and cast by Franz Herbich.

world knowledge.Name: Pawnee County Courthouse (Nebraska)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Pawnee County Courthouse was built in 1911 and designed by architect William F. Gernandt in Classical Revival style. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1990.

Major_Events.Event: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Major_Events.Description: The courthouse was recognized for its historical and architectural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The tan brick building has three stories over an ashlar limestone raised basement. The third story is partly hidden behind a brick parapet. The building features a monumental four-column entry portico on its north facade with complex capitals and squared pilasters. The pediment includes terra cotta allegorical figures and symbols representing agriculture and the fertility of the county.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse symbolizes the enduring nature of county government and democratic ideals. Its architectural design and historical value make it a significant landmark.
world knowledge.Details: The pedimental sculpture includes two bearded men in togas holding a shovel and a pitchfork, flanked by women with baskets of apples and other produce, symbolizing agriculture and the fertility of the county. The centered torch likely refers to the enduring nature of county government and democratic ideals.

world knowledge.Name: Nagoya Station
world knowledge.Address: Meieki, Nakamura-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Nagoya Station first opened on 1 May 1886. The current station complex was completed on December 20, 1999. It is Japan's, and one of the world's largest train stations by floor area, and houses the headquarters of the Central Japan Railway Company (JR Central).

Major_Events.Description: Nagoya Station first opened on 1 May 1886.
The current station complex was completed on December 20, 1999.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The station features twin towers rising over 50 storeys, making it the tallest railway-station building in the world. It includes six island platforms for the Tōkaidō Main Line, Chuo Line, and Kansai Line, and two island platforms for the Tokaido Shinkansen. The station also has underground concourses and platform gates.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Nagoya Station is a major transportation hub in Japan and one of the world's largest train stations by floor area. It is a symbol of modern railway infrastructure and urban development in Nagoya.
world knowledge.Details: The station is adjacent to Meitetsu Nagoya Station and Kintetsu Nagoya Station. It serves multiple railway lines including the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, Tōkaidō Main Line, Chūō Main Line, Kansai Main Line, Higashiyama Line, Sakura-dōri Line, and Aonami Line. The station and the area around it is officially called Meieki in the Japanese addressing system.

world knowledge.Name: Seapoint
world knowledge.Address: Seapoint, between Blackrock and Monkstown, Dublin, Ireland
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Seapoint is a small seafront area known for its beach and bathing areas, beside a Martello Tower on the Dublin Bay seashore. The Martello Tower is now the headquarters of the Genealogical Society of Ireland. In 1924, Michael Mahony of Dun Laoghaire built six B.R.A. 12 ft. dinghies which became the core of the sailing club which survived for about 10 years.

Major_Events.Description: Michael Mahony of Dun Laoghaire built six B.R.A. 12 ft. dinghies which became the core of the sailing club which survived for about 10 years.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Martello Tower, a small defensive fort, now repurposed as the headquarters of the Genealogical Society of Ireland.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Seapoint is culturally significant for its beach and bathing areas, as well as the Martello Tower which now serves as the headquarters of the Genealogical Society of Ireland. The beach has an International Blue flag award and a national Green flag award.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Recreational area (beach and bathing) and historical site (Martello Tower).
world knowledge.Details: The route linking Dún Laoghaire harbour to the N11 National primary route has itself been designated a National primary route, the N31. Part of the route includes Seapoint Avenue, and the Seapoint area is located on the strip of land, which includes the railway line, between the road and the sea.

world knowledge.Name: Qiantang River Bridge
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Qiantang River Bridge is a combined road and railway bridge across the Qiantang River at Hangzhou in Zhejiang Province, China. It was designed by Mao Yisheng and built by Dorman Long. Construction started on 8 August 1934 and was completed on 29 September 1937.

Major_Events.Event: Preparation for demolition during the Battle of Shanghai
Major_Events.Description: On 17 November 1937, during the Battle of Shanghai, the Bridge Construction Office was ordered to make preparations to blow up the bridge to delay the advancing Imperial Japanese Army.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Two-tier truss bridge comprising 16 spans
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is an important engineering feat and a historical landmark in China, representing early 20th-century bridge construction technology and resilience during wartime.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge measures 1,072 metres long and 9.1 meters wide. It was opened on 29 September 1937.

world knowledge.Name: Technical University of Madrid
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Technical University of Madrid (UPM) was founded in 1971 through the merger of various Technical Schools of Engineering and Architecture, some of which date back to the 18th century. It is considered the top technical university in Spain and is part of the TIME network of European engineering schools. The university has a rich history of contributing to Spanish technology and has educated many notable figures in engineering and architecture.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the Royal Academy of Mathematics
Major_Events.Description: Founded by King Philip II to improve Spanish cartography and train engineers and architects.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the Corps of Army, Cities, Ports and Frontiers Engineers
Major_Events.Description: Established by King Philip V, marking the organized profession of Spanish engineers.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the School of Naval Architecture
Major_Events.Description: Founded by King Charles III to train naval architects.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the School of Mining Engineering
Major_Events.Description: Established by King Charles III in Almadén to utilize mercury mines.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the School of Civil Engineering
Major_Events.Description: Founded by Agustín de Betancourt, considered the best civil engineering school in Spain.

Major_Events.Event: Foundation of the Technical University of Madrid
Major_Events.Description: Formed by merging various technical schools, becoming Spain's top technical university.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The university's campuses and buildings reflect a mix of historical and modern architectural styles, with some schools located in buildings dating back to the 18th and 19th centuries.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The UPM has played a pivotal role in the development of Spanish technology and engineering. It has educated many of Spain's leading engineers and architects and continues to be a center of innovation and research.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Higher education and research in engineering, architecture, and related fields.
world knowledge.Details: The UPM is known for its high academic standards and rigorous programs, particularly in engineering and architecture. It has numerous international agreements and double degree programs with leading universities worldwide. The university's schools are spread across Madrid, and it has a strong focus on research and development, supported by its Scientific and Technological Park.

world knowledge.Name: Raghadan Palace
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Raghadan Palace, the first Hashemite structure in Jordan, was built by King Abdullah I, the founding monarch of the country. It was constructed on an elevated location in 1924 to serve as an official royal residence overlooking downtown Amman. The palace symbolizes prosperity and comfort and was designed to reflect both grandeur and simplicity, harmonizing with the historical significance of the city. The architectural design was influenced by Islamic styles, with contributions from architects from Damascus, Nablus, and Jerusalem.

Major_Events.Description: The palace's first official event was a gathering where Prince Abdullah I hosted poets.
Raghadan Palace hosted Arab political and nationalist gathering, during which poets Mustafa Wahbi Tal and Fouad Al-Khatib recited their works.

Major_Events.Event: Pledging allegiance to King Abdullah I
Major_Events.Description: The Throne Hall witnessed the official ceremony of pledging allegiance to King Abdullah I bin Al-Hussein as ruler.
The Throne Hall hosted the coronation ceremony of King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The palace is constructed of gray stone sourced from Ma'an. Its architecture was designed by skilled architects from Damascus, Nablus, and Jerusalem. The palace features stained glass windows inspired by the style of Al-Aqsa Mosque, lilies, spearheads, arched windows, carved columns, and a grand entrance. The Throne Hall includes a grand oval-shaped iwan with stained glass windows and the Hashemite Throne.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Raghadan Palace is recognized as the first Hashemite residence and the central seat of governance in Jordan. It serves as the heart of political activity in the country, where decisions on state affairs, foreign relations, and royal decrees are made. The palace has a rich cultural history as a center for literature and poetry, where King Abdullah I hosted prominent poets and literary figures. It also served as a refuge for Arab nationalists during times of crisis in the Arab world.
world knowledge.Details: The palace is surrounded by a large wall that connects to Jabal Al-Qal'a (the Citadel). The entrance to Raghadan Palace is through the main gate, which opens onto the central courtyard. The palace includes a special room dedicated to Sharif Hussein bin Ali, who returned to reside in Raghadan Palace in 1930. The upper floors of the palace contain multiple halls designated for meetings, receptions, dining, and hospitality, as well as housing private offices for managing state affairs. Throughout the palace, glass showcases and cabinets built into the walls display swords and various items gifted to the Hashemite kings.

world knowledge.Name: University of Toronto
world knowledge.Address: Toronto, Ontario, Canada, located on the grounds that surround Queen's Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Founded by royal charter in 1827 as King's College, the first institution of higher learning in Upper Canada. Originally controlled by the Church of England, the university assumed its present name in 1850 upon becoming a secular institution.

Major_Events.Description: The University of Toronto was founded by royal charter as King's College, the first institution of higher learning in Upper Canada.
The university was secularized and renamed the University of Toronto.
The discovery of insulin by Banting and Best at the University of Toronto is considered among the most significant events in the history of medicine.
The first artificial cardiac pacemaker was developed at the University of Toronto.
The first successful single-lung transplant was performed at the University of Toronto.
The first nerve transplant was performed at the University of Toronto.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The architecture is epitomized by a combination of Romanesque and Gothic Revival buildings spread across the eastern and central portions of campus, most dating between 1858 and 1929. The traditional heart of the university, known as Front Campus, is near the campus centre in an oval lawn enclosed by King's College Circle.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The University of Toronto is one of the leading research universities in the world and has made significant contributions to various fields including medicine, science, and technology. It is also culturally significant as it has produced numerous notable alumni including five Prime Ministers of Canada, three Governors General of Canada, and numerous other leaders and innovators.
world knowledge.Details: The University of Toronto offers over 700 undergraduate and 200 graduate programs. It is one of two members of the Association of American Universities outside the United States, alongside McGill University. The university is noted for influential movements and curricula in literary criticism and communication theory, known collectively as the Toronto School.

world knowledge.Name: Tamarindo, Costa Rica
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tamarindo began as a small fishing village in the 20th century. It transformed into a tourism hub after the 1994 surfing documentary 'The Endless Summer II' featured the town. It was officially incorporated as a town on November 27, 1995.

Major_Events.Description: Texas businessman Russell Wenrich purchased land and began developing beachside cabanas, marking the start of Tamarindo's tourism development.
The documentary featured Tamarindo, leading to a tourism boom that transformed the town into a popular destination.
Tamarindo was officially incorporated as a town by Executive Order 24820-G.

Major_Events.Event: Liberia International Airport handling international flights
Major_Events.Description: The nearby airport began handling international flights, making Tamarindo more accessible to tourists.

Major_Events.Event: Loss and regain of Blue Flag designation
Major_Events.Description: Tamarindo's beach lost its Blue Flag designation due to pollution in 2004, regained it in 2006, lost it again in 2007, and reportedly regained it in 2018 after years of cleanup efforts.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tamarindo is culturally significant as a former fishing village that evolved into a major tourism and surfing destination. It is also known for its eco-tourism, digital nomad community, and expatriate population.

Activities: Golf at Hacienda Pinilla Golf Club, Reserva Conchal Beach Resort, and Four Seasons Resort Peninsula Papagayo
Night market and food truck park
Electronic dance music festivals (The BPM Festival, Ocaso Underground Music Festival)

Transportation.International_Airport: Liberia International Airport (about an hour away)
Transportation.Bus_Service: Scheduled daily bus service to and from San José
Transportation.Highway: Paved highway to San José (3.5 to 6 hours driving time)

Details.Education: Villareal has a public elementary school and high school

Facilities.Stores: Two large stores, multiple hardware stores
Facilities.Services: Police station, church, car-repair shops, gas station

world knowledge.Name: St. John's International Airport
world knowledge.Address: St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Constructed during World War II as a defense facility, the airport was officially opened on 15 December 1941. It was used by the RCAF, RAF, and the United States Army Air Corps until December 1946. The airport transitioned to civilian use under the Canadian Department of Transport in 1946 and has since undergone several renovations and expansions.

Major_Events.Description: Three American B-17 Flying Fortress and one RCAF Digby made the first unofficial landings on the only serviceable runway available.
The first commercial air service began with the arrival of a Trans-Canada Air Lines Lockheed Lodestar aircraft with five passengers and three crew.
The airport underwent a $50 million renovation, modernizing the terminal to meet North American standards.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features multiple asphalt runways, a modernized terminal building, and facilities for fire and rescue services. The control tower is equipped with advanced navigation and landing aids.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport played a crucial role during World War II as a defense facility and has since become a vital transportation hub for the St. John's metropolitan area and the Avalon Peninsula.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public airport serving commercial, military, and emergency services.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is part of the National Airports System and is designated as an international airport by Transport Canada. It has been used as an emergency landing site for the Space Shuttle orbiter and continues to serve as a key transportation link for Newfoundland and Labrador.

world knowledge.Name: Grayson County Courthouse (Texas)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Grayson County, established in 1846, has had seven courthouses, with three during 1847 to 1853, then successors built in 1853, 1859, 1876, and 1936.

Major_Events.Event: Lynch mob burning of previous courthouse
Major_Events.Description: The previous Grayson County Courthouse was burned by a lynch mob on May 9, 1930, killing a black man who had been accused of raping a white woman.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Built in Moderne style, designed by architects Voelcker and Dixon, and constructed of concrete and limestone.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The courthouse represents the judicial and administrative history of Grayson County, as well as a dark chapter in its racial history.
world knowledge.Details: This article about a building or structure in Texas is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Fair Lane
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Fair Lane was the estate of Ford Motor Company founder Henry Ford and his wife, Clara Ford. Named after an area in Cork, Ireland, where Ford's adoptive grandfather was born, the estate included a large limestone house, power plant, greenhouse, boathouse, stables, and extensive gardens. The residence and part of the estate grounds are open to the public as a historical landscape and house museum, preserved as a National Historic Landmark.

Major_Events.Description: The estate was donated to the University of Michigan for a new Dearborn campus.
Fair Lane was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
Fair Lane was designated a National Historic Landmark District.
The University closed Fair Lane to the public.
Stewardship of the estate was transferred to a non-profit group that operates the Edsel and Eleanor Ford House.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The 31,000-square-foot (2,900 m2) house features 56 rooms, an indoor pool (now covered), and a bowling alley. Built in a mix of Baronial and Prairie styles, the estate includes a limestone powerhouse with a garage and laboratory. The landscape, designed by Jens Jensen, employs a 'delayed view' approach with dense woodlands, meadows, and gardens aligned to the summer solstice.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Fair Lane is culturally significant as the estate of Henry Ford, founder of Ford Motor Company, and reflects the lifestyle and innovations of the early 20th century industrial elite. Its architectural and landscape design contributions by notable figures like Frank Lloyd Wright and Jens Jensen add to its historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Originally a private residence, now a historical landscape and house museum.
world knowledge.Details: The estate's hydropower plant not only powered the estate but also part of Dearborn. The Ford Fairlane automobile model was named after the estate. The private rail car of Henry and Clara Ford, named 'Fair Lane', was kept on standby in Dearborn.

world knowledge.Name: Archer Point Light
world knowledge.Address: Archer Point, about 29km southeast of Cooktown, Queensland, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Archer Point Light is an active lighthouse established in 1883. The original lighthouse was a timber frame covered with galvanised iron, replaced in 1975 with a modern concrete structure. It served as a lead light for navigation, marking safe passages between reefs and the mainland. The original lenses are now displayed at the Queensland Maritime Museum.

Major_Events.Description: A timber frame lighthouse covered with galvanised iron was built.
The original lighthouse was replaced with a square concrete equipment room topped with a lantern.
The lighthouse was automated and electrically operated.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The current lighthouse is a square concrete equipment room topped with a lantern, standing 19 feet (5.8 m) tall. The original lighthouse had four floors including the gallery floor, with ladders connecting each level.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The lighthouse is part of Australia's maritime history, aiding navigation along the Queensland coast. It represents advancements in lighthouse construction and technology, from timber and iron to concrete and automation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Navigational aid for ships, marking safe passages between reefs and the mainland.

Details.Light_Characteristics: Fl (4) WRG 20s. (Four flashes separated by two seconds, every twenty seconds, with white, green, and red sectors indicating clear passage or deviations from the channel.)
Details.Light_Source: 35,000 cd 120 Volt 1000 Watt Tungsten-halogen bulb, with diesel backup.
Details.Range: White: 17 nmi (31 km), Green: 17 nmi (31 km), Red: 13 nmi (24 km).
Details.Accessibility: The site is open to the public via a gravel road, but the tower is closed.

world knowledge.Name: Estadio Universitario (UANL)
world knowledge.Address: Campus of the Universidad Autónoma de Nuevo León, San Nicolás de los Garza, Nuevo León, Mexico
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Estadio Universitario, nicknamed El Volcán, was completed in 1967 with a construction cost of $23 million MXN. Originally planned to hold nearly 90,000 spectators, the plan was downscaled to meet financial needs. After the 1986 FIFA World Cup, the stadium's official capacity was 52,000. Later modifications reduced the capacity to 41,615. The stadium is the home venue for the Tigres UANL and has hosted numerous significant sports and music events.

Major_Events.Description: Hosted 4 matches during the tournament.
Hosted matches when Tigres qualified for the tournament.
Hosted several matches during the championship.
Hosted several matches during the tournament.
Hosted the Kansas City Chiefs vs. Dallas Cowboys game, with the Chiefs winning 32-6.
British rock band Queen performed during The Game Tour to more than 150,000 fans.
Hosted 8 matches during the championship.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Football stadium with a grass surface, originally planned for nearly 90,000 spectators but scaled down to 41,615 due to financial and safety modifications.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is a significant sports and cultural venue in Mexico, hosting major football matches, international tournaments, and concerts by world-famous artists. It is nicknamed El Volcán and is a central part of the local community.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium was given to Sinergia Deportiva, the for-profit company that administers Tigres, as part of the club's assets. It also hosted C.F. Monterrey between 1973 and 1980. The Auténticos Tigres, the university's American football team, use the stadium for playoff games and ONEFA championships. A proposal to build an 80,000-seat replacement venue was rejected in 2016 due to potential impact on the Santa Catarina River.

world knowledge.Name: Saint Louis Art Museum
world knowledge.Address: Forest Park, St. Louis, Missouri, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Saint Louis Art Museum (SLAM) originated in 1879 as the Saint Louis School and Museum of Fine Arts, part of Washington University. It moved to its current location in Forest Park after the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition. The museum separated from the university in 1909 and has since grown into a major cultural institution supported by public taxes and private donations. A significant expansion was completed in 2013, adding extensive gallery space and modern facilities.

Major_Events.Event: Founding of Saint Louis School and Museum of Fine Arts
Major_Events.Description: The museum was founded as part of Washington University.
The museum moved to the Palace of Fine Arts building in Forest Park after the 1904 World's Fair.
The museum became an independent entity after a legal dispute over tax funding.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of Metropolitan Zoological Park and Museum District
Major_Events.Description: Voters approved expanding the tax base to include St. Louis County, securing the museum's financial future.
A significant expansion designed by David Chipperfield added over 224,000 square feet of gallery space.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The museum is housed in the Cass Gilbert-designed Palace of Fine Arts, a Beaux-Arts structure built for the 1904 World's Fair. The 2013 expansion by David Chipperfield added modern gallery spaces while preserving the historic facade.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: SLAM is a major cultural institution in the Midwest, offering free admission and housing over 34,000 artworks spanning antiquity to the present. It holds significant collections in modern art, Oceanic and Mesoamerican works, and American art, including the world's largest Max Beckmann collection.
world knowledge.Details: The museum's collection includes works by Matisse, Gauguin, Monet, Picasso, and Van Gogh, as well as significant holdings of 20th-century German art. It also features ancient artifacts, including Egyptian mummies, and a strong collection of American art, particularly works by George Caleb Bingham. The museum actively acquires post-war German art and has received significant donations, including a 2021 gift of 22 works from Emily Rauh Pulitzer.

world knowledge.Name: Shahid Sadooghi Airport
world knowledge.Address: 10 kilometers away from the city center of Yazd, Iran
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1970, Shahid Sadooghi Airport serves as a crucial part of the north–south transportation corridor in Iran. It primarily serves Yazd and surrounding counties, with occasional charter flights and scheduled services to neighboring countries like Iraq and Syria, as well as routine international services to Jeddah and Medina during the Hajj season.
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a runway with asphalt surface, measuring 4,098 meters in length.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is significant for its role in facilitating transportation within Iran and for providing essential services during the Hajj season.
world knowledge.Details: The airport operates at 40-50% capacity and was the eleventh busiest airport in Iran in terms of passenger traffic and number of flight operations in 2012, with 431,500 passengers traveling through it that year.

world knowledge.Name: Keoladeo National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally a duck shooting reserve in 1899, it became Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary in 1956, was declared a protected sanctuary in 1971, and established as Keoladeo National Park on 10 March 1982. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.

Major_Events.Description: The park was designated under the Ramsar Convention due to its importance as a wetland.

Major_Events.Event: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Major_Events.Description: Recognized for its exceptional avian biodiversity and importance as a wintering ground for migratory birds.
A severe drought caused significant harm to the park's flora and fauna.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a human-made regulated wetland, dry grasslands, woodlands, swamps, and seasonal wetlands. It includes mounds, dykes, and open water areas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is crucial for the conservation of avian biodiversity, serving as a wintering ground for migratory birds, including the rare Siberian crane. It also provides water for local communities and protects against flash floods.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of biodiversity, particularly avian species, and providing a habitat for migratory and resident birds.
world knowledge.Details: Keoladeo National Park is a Ramsar Wetland Site and a World Heritage Site. It faces acute water scarcity, affecting its ecosystem and the arrival of migratory birds. The park is managed by the Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation and receives water from Ajan Bund and Khokhar Weir.

world knowledge.Name: Hayden Orpheum Picture Palace
world knowledge.Address: 380 Military Road, Cremorne, North Sydney Council, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hayden Orpheum Picture Palace, originally known as the Cremorne Orpheum Theatre, was built in 1935 by F. T. Eastment and Sons. It was designed by George Newton Kenworthy in the Art Deco style. Commissioned by the Virgona family, it opened on 3 October 1935. After closing in 1979, it was restored in 1987 by Mike Walsh and reopened as a multiplex cinema. It has since expanded to six screens and features a 1925 Wurlitzer pipe-organ.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre was officially opened on 3 October 1935 by Reginald Weaver, the local Member for Neutral Bay.
The theatre closed in 1979 due to declining popularity of suburban cinemas.

Major_Events.Event: Restoration and Reopening as Hayden Orpheum Picture Palace
Major_Events.Description: Restored by Mike Walsh and reopened on 9 December 1987 as a multiplex cinema with the feature 'Planes, Trains and Automobiles'.
Two more screens were added in the 1990s and another two in 2000, bringing the total to six screens.
The cinema celebrated its 80th birthday in 2015.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Inter-war Art Deco style, designed by George Newton Kenworthy. Features include modern acoustic design and internal furnishings, and a 1925 Wurlitzer pipe-organ.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is heritage-listed and recognized by the National Trust of Australia (New South Wales) for its architectural and historical value. It is a notable example of Art Deco cinema design in Australia.
world knowledge.Details: The cinema was originally used for stage productions and later transformed into a multiplex. It is a longtime favourite of film critic David Stratton and features a historic Wurlitzer pipe-organ played at selected screenings.

world knowledge.Name: Lexington Opera House
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Lexington Opera House was built in 1886 to replace a former theatre destroyed by fire. Designed by architect Oscar Cobb, it opened on July 19, 1887, and quickly became a regional hub for performances. It faced decline due to cultural shifts but was saved from demolition through public and private efforts, undergoing major renovations in the 1970s.

Major_Events.Description: The Opera House officially opened with a concert by the Cincinnati Symphony.
First production hosted by the Lizzie Evans Stock Company.
Stage was flooded, and much of the performance took place in rowboats.
Featured 100 animals in a mile-long parade.
Significant remodeling occurred to house an on-stage chariot race.
Marked the end of live performances before conversion to a movie house.
Windstorm caused the false ceiling to collapse.
Second windstorm caused the roof to collapse.
Restoration efforts concluded, reopening the Opera House.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Three-story building with two balconies and box seats. Intricate design work included Turkish Morocco and velvet upholstery, 250 gaslights, 37 sets of scenery, and a drop curtain. Featured innovations like the Edison light board and trap doors for animal use. Constructed with standpipes for fire safety.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: One of 14 pre-1900 theatres in the U.S. still operating as a live performance venue. A historic and architectural landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Serves as a premier cultural destination in Lexington.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Theater (hosts ballets, opera, children's productions, family shows, comedy, music, and Broadway tours)
world knowledge.Details: Originally seated 1,250; now under 1,000 seats. Hosts 85,000 patrons annually. Owned by Lexington Center Corporation. Renovated in 1975-1976, restoring its 19th-century aesthetic while modernizing stage equipment. The Opera House Fund supports its operations and local arts groups.

world knowledge.Name: Oecusse Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Oecusse Airport, originally known as Palaban Airport, was established in the 1960s and has undergone significant redevelopment. Initially serving domestic flights, it was essentially abandoned by the 2010s. A major overhaul between 2015 and 2018 transformed it into an international airport.

Major_Events.Description: The redeveloped Oecusse Airport was inaugurated by Timor-Leste President Francisco Guterres on 18 June 2019, marking its transformation into an international airport.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features modern facilities including an air traffic control tower, terminal building, quarantine facilities, fuel depot, and upgraded radar and navigation systems. The runway was widened and lengthened to accommodate international standards.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The airport is a symbol of the Oecusse-Ambeno Special Administrative Region's development, though it has been criticized for excessive investment. It aims to boost regional connectivity and economic growth.
world knowledge.Details: The airport has a runway of 2,000 m in length and 45 m wide, capable of handling Airbus A320 or Boeing 737-800 aircraft. It can process more than 500 passengers per hour and has facilities for cargo and live animals, including quarantine services.

world knowledge.Name: Aliguay
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Aliguay is an island in the Philippines, and a barangay of Dapitan. The island is an established marine sanctuary. The island is surrounded by white sand beaches and coral reefs. There are no water sources on the island. A few residents live on Aliguay Island, mostly selling fish to tourists.

Major_Events.Description: More than 10 armed men abducted at dawn Monday, May 4, 2015. Rodolfo Buligao, Aliguay's Barangay Captain at the time, and two members of the Philippine Coast Guard were kidnapped by the Abu Sayyaf. The suspects turned to these 3 men after failing to see foreign tourists in what could have been a plan for kidnapping-for-ransom. The military found a beheaded body of a man believed to be Buligao. It was spotted along an intersection in Barangay Laum Maimbung, Maimbung town, Province of Sulu.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Aliguay Island is an established marine sanctuary, known for its white sand beaches and coral reefs.
world knowledge.Details: The island has a population of 720 (2020). It is adjacent to the Bohol Sea and Sulu Sea.

world knowledge.Name: National Theatre (Budapest)
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The National Theatre in Budapest was originally opened in 1837 and has occupied several locations over the years. The concept of a national theatre was promoted by influential thinkers like Ferenc Kazinczy and Baron István Széchenyi.
