The current building opened on March 15, 2002, after decades of planning and political delays.

Major_Events.Description: The theatre opened as Pesti Magyar Színház (Hungarian Theatre of Pest) on August 22, 1837, with the goal of promoting national drama and showcasing world literature classics.
The theatre was nationalized and renamed to the National Theatre.
The original National Theatre building was demolished, and the company moved to the People's Theatre at Blaha Lujza Square in 1908.
The People's Theatre was demolished on April 23, 1965, due to metro line construction.
The current National Theatre building opened on March 15, 2002, on the bank of the Danube in the Ferencváros district.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The theatre is a modern performing arts center with an open-air stage. It was designed by Mária Siklós and György Vadász, and it is functionally separated into three parts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The National Theatre is a symbol of Hungarian cultural heritage and has played a key role in promoting national drama and literature. It has been a focal point for Hungary's theatrical and artistic community since its inception.
world knowledge.Details: The nearby Palace of Arts was opened in 2005. The theatre has a capacity of 619. The Memorial of the Old National Theatre is located on the National Theatre grounds. The theatre has had several directors, including György Schwajda, Tamás Jordán, Róbert Alföldi, and Attila Vidnyánszky.

world knowledge.Name: Port Douglas
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Port Douglas was established in 1877 after the discovery of gold at Hodgkinson River by James Venture Mulligan. It grew quickly due to the mining industry and timber cutting. The town's importance dwindled after the completion of the Kuranda Railway in 1891 and a devastating cyclone in 1911. Tourism boomed in the late-1980s after the construction of the Sheraton Mirage Port Douglas Resort.

Major_Events.Description: Led to the establishment of Port Douglas.
Demolished or severely damaged all but seven residential buildings and 4 commercial buildings.

Major_Events.Event: Sheraton Mirage Port Douglas Resort construction
Major_Events.Description: Boosted tourism in the region.
United States President Bill Clinton and First Lady Hillary Clinton chose the town as their only holiday stop on their historic visit to Australia.
Bill Clinton was dining in Port Douglas when he was advised of the attacks.
Television personality and conservationist Steve Irwin died at Batt Reef, off Port Douglas, after a stingray barb pierced his chest.
Port Douglas was a popular location to view the solar eclipse.
Caused critical water supply issues in the town.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The town features a mix of historical and modern buildings, including heritage-listed sites and five-star resorts.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Port Douglas is adjacent to two World Heritage areas, the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree Rainforest. It was ranked No. 3 on Australian Traveller magazine's list of 100 Best Towns in Australia.
world knowledge.Details: Port Douglas has a tropical monsoon climate with heavy rainfall from January to March. The town is known for its many restaurants, walks, golf courses, and wildlife park. It also hosts annual events like the Port Douglas Carnivale and the Great Barrier Reef Marathon Festival.

world knowledge.Name: Edion Stadium Hiroshima
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Hiroshima Big Arch, originally known as Hiroshima Park Stadium, opened in 1992 as the venue for the 1992 AFC Asian Cup. It was later renamed Edion Stadium Hiroshima and is currently known as Hot Staff Field Hiroshima under sponsorship. It served as the home stadium for J.League club Sanfrecce Hiroshima until 2023.

Major_Events.Description: The host nation Japan won the Asian Cup title for the first time, defeating defending champion Saudi Arabia 1–0 in the final at this stadium.
The stadium hosted the 1994 Asian Games.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Multi-purpose stadium with a grass surface and an all-seater capacity of 36,894.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The stadium is significant for hosting major football matches and athletics events, including the 1992 AFC Asian Cup and the 1994 Asian Games. It was the home ground for Sanfrecce Hiroshima until 2023.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Multi-purpose stadium used for association football matches and athletics.
world knowledge.Details: The stadium is accessible via train services, with the Kōiki-kōen-mae Station on the Astram Line located only 5 minutes' walk from the stadium. It is owned by Hiroshima City and operated by the Hiroshima City Sports Association.

world knowledge.Name: Peterborough, Ontario
world knowledge.Location: On the Otonabee River, about 125 kilometres northeast of Toronto
world knowledge.Construction_Period: Established in 1819 as Scott's Plains, incorporated as a town in 1850, and as a city on July 1, 1905
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Peterborough was originally settled by Adam Scott in 1818 and renamed in honor of Peter Robinson, who led Irish immigrants to the area in 1825. The city grew as a manufacturing hub and was the first in Canada to use electric streetlights, earning the nickname 'The Electric City.' It played a significant role in early hydro-electrical power generation and industrial development.

Major_Events.Event: Completion of the Peterborough Lift Lock
Major_Events.Description: The Peterborough Lift Lock, the world's largest hydraulic lift lock at the time, was completed, becoming a key feature of the Trent-Severn Waterway.
Peterborough was officially incorporated as a city with a population of about 14,300.
A severe flood caused significant damage, with the sewage treatment plant recording 32 million litres of water compared to the usual 5.9 million litres.
The mosque was set on fire, leading to a community fundraising effort that raised over $110,000 for repairs in less than two days.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Peterborough features a mix of historical and modern architecture, including the Peterborough Lift Lock, the Peterborough County Courthouse (built between 1838-1840), and the Carnegie Library (now part of City Hall). The city's layout is influenced by glacial formations, with drumlins and moraines shaping its topography.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Peterborough is known as the gateway to the Kawarthas, a major recreational region. It has a rich industrial history, being a pioneer in hydro-electrical power and manufacturing. The city is also a cultural hub with museums, theaters, and a vibrant arts community. It hosts the longest-running free admission music fest in Canada.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The city serves as a regional center for commerce, education, and tourism, with a focus on service industries and manufacturing.

Details.Climate: Humid continental (Köppen Dfb), with unpredictable weather patterns influenced by the Oak Ridges Moraine.
Details.Economy: Service industries dominate, with significant contributions from manufacturing, food processing, and tourism. Major employers include Quaker Oats (PepsiCo), Peterborough Regional Health Centre, and Trent University.
Details.Transportation: Highway 115 connects to Toronto, and public transit includes Peterborough Transit and GO Transit bus services. Plans are underway to reinstate passenger rail service to Toronto by 2025.
Details.Education: Home to Trent University and Fleming College, offering diverse academic and vocational programs.
Details.Media: Hosts multiple radio stations, CHEX-DT (Global O&O), and newspapers like the Peterborough Examiner and Peterborough This Week.
Details.Recreation: Features the Riverview Park & Zoo, Del Crary Park, and numerous trails like the Rotary Greenway Trail and Jackson Creek Kiwanis Trail.

world knowledge.Name: Sydney Town Hall
world knowledge.Address: 483 George Street, Sydney CBD, New South Wales, Australia
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Sydney Town Hall is a late 19th-century heritage-listed town hall building in the city of Sydney, housing the chambers of the Lord Mayor of Sydney, council offices, and venues for meetings and functions. It was built on the site of the Old Sydney Burial Ground, Sydney's first permanent cemetery, which operated from 1792 to 1820. The Town Hall was designed by John H. Wilson and completed by several architects, including Edward Bell, Albert Bond, Thomas Sapsford, John Hennessy, and George McRae. The building has undergone several renovations and restorations, including major upgrades in 2008-2009 and 1991-1992.

Major_Events.Description: The foundation stone was laid by Prince Alfred, the Duke of Edinburgh.
The first stage of the Town Hall, including the vestibule and offices, was completed.
The second stage, including the Centennial Hall, was completed.

Major_Events.Event: Formation of the Australasian Federation League
Major_Events.Description: The Town Hall was the venue for the formation and official launch of the Australasian Federation League, a pro-federation organization in NSW.
During World War II, the Town Hall played an active role in maintaining civilian morale and safety, with areas set aside for administration of National Emergency Services.
A major restoration program was undertaken, including redecorating the vestibule and Main Hall, upgrading stormwater and sewage systems, and installing a protective roof over the Vestibule Dome.
The Town Hall hosted ceremonial events for the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Sydney Town Hall is built in the Victorian Second Empire style, inspired by the French Second Empire Hôtel de Ville in Paris. It features a lavishly ornamented composition with a focal tower and fanciful roofs. The building is constructed from local Sydney sandstone, with brick and plaster internal walls, timber, concrete, and tile floors, and timber roof trusses. The Centennial Hall houses the Grand Organ, the world's largest pipe organ with tubular pneumatic action. The building includes elaborate interiors with fine design and craftsmanship, including a vestibule glass dome, mosaic floors, carved cedar joinery, and carved sandstone and marble.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Sydney Town Hall is a symbol of the city's wealth and status, serving as the centre of city politics and the venue for major civic and cultural events. It is the most elaborate and exuberant work of Second Empire Style architecture in Australia, exhibiting the highest level of craftsmanship and quality of materials. The site has high historical and archaeological importance as it was built on the former Old Sydney Burial Ground, Sydney's first permanent cemetery. The Town Hall is listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register and is a site of State heritage significance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The Town Hall serves as the offices of the Council of the City of Sydney and as the city's civic and cultural centre, hosting meetings, functions, concerts, and public events.
Notable_Visitors: Prince Alfred, the Duke of Edinburgh
world knowledge.Details: The Sydney Town Hall is known for its rich decoration, craftsmanship, Victorian interiors, intricate fenestration, and complex roof profiles. It houses the Sydney City Council Chamber, reception rooms, the Centennial Hall, and offices for the Lord Mayor and elected councillors. The building has undergone several modifications and restorations to preserve its heritage and improve sustainability, including energy-efficient lighting, solar panels, and new hydraulics and stormwater infrastructure. The site has exceptional archaeological potential due to its location on the Old Sydney Burial Ground, with numerous graves still intact below the existing foundations.

world knowledge.Name: Songdo Central Park
world knowledge.Area: Songdo district of Incheon, South Korea
world knowledge.Address: 160, Convensia-daero, Yeonsu District, Incheon, South Korea
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Songdo Central Park is a public park in the Songdo district of Incheon, South Korea. It is the centerpiece of Songdo IBD's green space plan, inspired by New York City's Central Park. The park covers almost 10% of Songdo IBD’s total area and serves to connect various civic and cultural destinations by providing a seawater canal that refreshes itself every 24 hours.

Major_Events.Event: Filming of Gangnam Style music video
Major_Events.Description: Several scenes of the 2012 Gangnam Style music video by Psy were filmed in Songdo Central Park. This included a dance battle scene in the underground parking lot and a scene in the elevator of the same building.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a seawater canal that refreshes itself every 24 hours, a forested area, a patio with cafes and small restaurants, and a water-taxi service crossing the lake.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Songdo Central Park is culturally significant as it is a central green space in Korea's first international city, inspired by New York City's Central Park. It has become a popular destination for families and day-visitors from the Seoul area.
world knowledge.Details: The park is accessible from the nearby Canal Walk shopping court or by Central Park Station of Incheon Metro Line 1. It also features a water-taxi service and kayak rentals.

world knowledge.Name: Buochs Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Buochs Airport is a regional airport in Buochs, Switzerland, serving both military and civil purposes. It was active as a military airfield until 2003, primarily used by the Swiss Air Force. Since January 1, 2004, it has been a 'sleeping base' for the Air Force, with the capability to be reactivated in extraordinary situations. The airport is also used by Pilatus Aircraft for test and delivery flights.

Major_Events.Description: Buochs was activated by the Air Command Meiringen for 4 days, with missions flown using F-5E and F/A-18 aircraft.

Major_Events.Event: World Championship of the Army paratroopers
Major_Events.Description: The 35th World Championship of the Army paratroopers took place at Buochs Airport, alongside a concert by Bonnie Tyler.
The PC-7 Team performed with smoke generators on Swiss National Day, celebrating the 25th anniversary of the PC-7 Team and the roll-out of the Pilatus PC-24.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The airport features a concrete runway, taxiways, hangars, and an underground aircraft cavern. It is equipped with retractable arresting gear devices at both ends of the runway.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Buochs Airport is significant for its dual role in military and civil aviation in Switzerland. It has been a key location for the Swiss Air Force and is now a hub for Pilatus Aircraft, contributing to the region's aviation industry.
world knowledge.Details: The airport is operated by Civil Airport Buochs AG and is used for various events, including trade shows and air shows. It was previously home to militia Squadron 8 and reconnaissance squadron 10 of the Swiss Air Force.

world knowledge.Name: Pic Macaya National Park
world knowledge.Area: Massif de la Hotte, southern peninsula
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Pic Macaya National Park is one of the two largest national parks in Haiti, established in 1984 under Jean-Claude Duvalier's administration. It was expanded in March 2013 as part of the Macaya Project, which aims to protect its natural resources through reforestation, infrastructure development, and enforcement of conservation laws.

Major_Events.Description: The park was expanded to more than 8,000 hectares as part of the Macaya Project.
$12 million was pledged through 2017 by international development agencies to improve land management and conservation efforts.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally and ecologically significant as it contains Haiti's last stand of virgin cloud forest and is home to numerous endemic species of plants and animals. It plays a crucial role in biodiversity conservation and environmental protection in the region.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation and protection of natural resources
world knowledge.Details: The park features endangered plant and animal life, including 220 species of birds, 141 species of orchids, and 367 flowering plants. It includes two tall peaks, Pic Macaya and Pic Formon, with elevations reaching up to 2,347 meters. The park is threatened by the practice of 'charcoal burning,' which involves burning biomass to produce charcoal.

world knowledge.Name: Santa Monica Pier
world knowledge.Address: Foot of Colorado Avenue, Santa Monica, California, United States
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 1,651.5 feet (500 m) long, 301.2 feet (90 m) wide
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Santa Monica Pier is a historic amusement pier consisting of two originally separate piers: the Municipal Pier (opened 1909) and the Pleasure Pier (built 1916). It has evolved from a utilitarian structure carrying sewer pipes to a major entertainment destination featuring an amusement park, aquarium, shops, and restaurants. The pier faced threats of demolition in the 1960s-70s but was saved by community efforts.

Major_Events.Description: The Municipal Pier opened primarily to carry sewer pipes beyond the breakers.
Built by Charles I. D. Looff and his son Arthur, featuring amusement attractions.
Largest dance hall on the west coast, later converted to roller rink and demolished in 1963.
The privately owned Pleasure Pier was acquired by the city.
Winter storms destroyed one-third of the pier, leading to major repairs.
First new amusement park attraction since the 1930s.
Man climbed Ferris wheel claiming to have a bomb, leading to evacuation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Combination of two distinct pier structures (long narrow Municipal Pier and short wide Pleasure Pier). Features include the historic Looff Hippodrome building (National Register of Historic Places), solar-paneled Ferris wheel, and original 1922 carousel with hand-carved horses. The entry gate and bridge were built in 1938 by Works Project Administration.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Iconic Southern California landmark representing beach culture and amusement history. Saved from demolition by community efforts in 1970s. Featured in numerous films and popular culture. Part of Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area. Houses historic carousel and is a popular filming location.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Amusement and recreation (includes amusement park, aquarium, shops, restaurants, fishing, and event venue)
world knowledge.Details: Contains Pacific Park amusement park with solar-powered Ferris wheel, Santa Monica Pier Aquarium, trapeze school, and fishing area. Featured in numerous films including The Sting, Forrest Gump, Iron Man, and Pacific Rim Uprising. Appears in Cassandra Clare's The Dark Artifices book series. Managed by Santa Monica Pier Corporation (SMPC). Subject of fishing advisories due to mercury and PCB levels.

world knowledge.Name: Princes Street Gardens
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Princes Street Gardens are two adjacent public parks in the centre of Edinburgh, Scotland, lying in the shadow of Edinburgh Castle. The Gardens were created in the 1820s following the long draining of the Nor Loch and building of the New Town, beginning in the 1760s. The loch, situated on the north side of the town, was originally an artificial creation forming part of its medieval defences and made expansion northwards difficult. The water was habitually polluted from sewage draining downhill from the Old Town.

Major_Events.Description: The railway was built in the valley to connect the Edinburgh-Glasgow line at Haymarket with the new northern terminus of the North British line from Berwick-upon-Tweed at Waverley Station.
Despite much opposition from residents, the town council reacquired the ground for use as a public park.
The Ross Fountain was gifted by Edinburgh gunsmith Daniel Ross and was originally installed in 1872.
Four huge air-raid shelters were created within the northern embankment.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of the baby elephant monument
Major_Events.Description: A new monument, in the form of a baby elephant by sculptor Andy Scott, was added to the gardens on 2 February 2019.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The gardens run along the south side of Princes Street and are divided by The Mound, on which the National Gallery of Scotland and the Royal Scottish Academy buildings are located. East Princes Street Gardens run from The Mound to Waverley Bridge, and cover 8.5 acres (3.4 ha). The larger West Princes Street Gardens cover 29 acres (12 ha) and extend to the adjacent churches of St. John's and St. Cuthbert's, near Lothian Road in the west.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Gardens are the best known parks in Edinburgh, having the highest awareness and visitor figures for both residents and visitors to the city. They are home to many statues and monuments, including the Scott Monument, statues of David Livingstone, Adam Black, and John Wilson, and the Ross Fountain.
world knowledge.Details: Every year, in the weeks leading up to the end of the year, the East Gardens are transformed into 'Edinburgh's Christmas'. This includes a variety of amusement park rides and the Christmas Market, which has food and gifts from all around the world. The most notable attraction is the 33 metre (108 feet) high Ferris wheel, often dubbed 'The Edinburgh Eye'.

world knowledge.Name: Stanislavski and Nemirovich-Danchenko Theatre
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Stanislavski and Nemirovich-Danchenko Moscow Academic Music Theatre was founded in 1941 when two companies directed by Konstantin Stanislavski and Vladimir Nemirovich-Danchenko merged: the Stanislavsky Opera Theatre and the Nemirovich-Danchenko Music Theatre. The theatre has a rich history, including performances during World War II, collaborations with international opera houses, and surviving management crises and fires.

Major_Events.Event: Merger of Stanislavsky Opera Theatre and Nemirovich-Danchenko Music Theatre
Major_Events.Description: The two companies merged to form the Moscow State Musical Theatre of Stanislavski and Nemirovich-Danchenko.
The theatre performed for troops during the war, with part of the company evacuated and others staying in Moscow.
A fire destroyed the props storage, leading to the cancellation of 20 titles for years.
The company refused to perform in a strike action against the management, leading to a temporary shutdown.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The theatre is culturally significant as it was founded by two legendary reformers of 20th-century theatre, Konstantin Stanislavski and Vladimir Nemirovich-Danchenko. It has played a key role in the development of opera and musical theatre in Russia and has collaborated with international opera houses.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Music theatre, hosting opera, ballet, and musical performances.
world knowledge.Details: The theatre's repertoire includes classical opera and musical comedy shows. It has faced challenges such as fires and management crises but continues to operate as a prominent cultural institution in Moscow.

world knowledge.Name: Rudolfinum
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rudolfinum is a building in Prague, Czech Republic, designed in the neo-Renaissance style and situated on Jan Palach Square on the bank of the river Vltava. Since its opening in 1885, it has been associated with music and art. It was designed by architect Josef Zítek and his student Josef Schulz and is named in honour of Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria, who presided over the opening. Between 1919 and 1939, the building was used as the seat of the Czechoslovak parliament.

Major_Events.Event: First concert of the Czech Philharmonic
Major_Events.Description: On 4 January 1896, Antonín Dvořák himself conducted the Czech Philharmonic in the hall in its first ever concert.

Major_Events.Event: Seat of the Chamber of Deputies
Major_Events.Description: During the First Czechoslovak Republic, the building served as the seat of the Chamber of Deputies.
The Galerie Rudolfinum, an art gallery focusing mainly on contemporary art, opened on 1 January 1994.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Neo-Renaissance style
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rudolfinum is culturally significant as a major venue for music and art in Prague. It is the home of the Czech Philharmonic Orchestra and one of the main venues of the Prague Spring International Music Festival. Its Dvořák Hall is one of the oldest concert halls in Europe and is noted for its excellent acoustics.
world knowledge.Details: The Rudolfinum's Dvořák Hall is one of the oldest concert halls in Europe. The building also contains the Galerie Rudolfinum, an art gallery that focuses mainly on contemporary art. It has around 1,500 square metres of exhibition space and hosts a series of temporary exhibitions. Major exhibitions have included works by artists such as Andy Warhol, Cindy Sherman, and Neo Rauch.

world knowledge.Name: Punta del Este
world knowledge.Location: Southeastern Uruguay, on the Atlantic Coast
world knowledge.Address: Intersection of Route 10 with Route 39, southeast of Maldonado
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Punta del Este started as a small town and grew into a resort for the Latin and North American jet set. It was declared a village in 1907 and a city in 1957. The area was initially uninhabited until Antonio Lussich bought land in 1896 and started a botanical garden. The city faced a decline in tourists during the 1970s due to terrorist threats but experienced a real estate boom in the 1980s.

Major_Events.Event: Whitbread Around the World yacht races
Major_Events.Description: Punta del Este hosted the yacht races and participated with its own yacht 'Uruguay Natural'.
Attended by U.S. President Lyndon Johnson.

Major_Events.Event: Uruguay Round of international trade negotiations
Major_Events.Description: Led to the creation of the World Trade Organization in 1994.
Hosted the Punta del Este ePrix, a street circuit race.
Took place in the Punta del Este Convention Center.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The city features colonial architecture contrasting with modern buildings, scenic shores, resort houses, and a port. Notable structures include the La Mano giant sculpture, Casapueblo (Santorini-styled complex), Puente Garzón bridge, and the Museum of the Sea.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Punta del Este is a major tourist destination known as 'The Hamptons of South America,' 'The Monaco of the South,' and 'The St. Tropez of South America.' It hosts international film festivals, gastronomy events, and has protected natural reserves. The city is also significant for its role in international trade negotiations and sports events.
Notable_Visitors: Various Latin and North American jet set members

Details.Climate: Oceanic climate (Cfb), with pleasant summers and cool winters. Average yearly temperature is 16.4°C (61.5°F).
Details.Beaches: Divided into Brava (fierce) and Mansa (tame) regions, with public access to all beaches.
Details.Wildlife: Southern right whales re-colonizing the area; appearances of orcas documented around Isla de Lobos.
Details.Cultural_Institutions: Fundación Pablo Atchugarry promotes arts and culture with exhibitions, concerts, and a sculpture park.
Details.Transportation: Served by Capitán de Corbeta Carlos A. Curbelo International Airport, with connections to Montevideo.
Details.Religious_Sites: Numerous Jewish temples and Catholic churches.
Details.Real_Estate: Experienced a boom in the 1980s, with ongoing growth as a year-round residence for Argentines, Brazilians, and Europeans.

world knowledge.Name: Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge
world knowledge.Address: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, Wulingyuan area, Hunan, China
world knowledge.Physical_Area: 430 metres (1,410 ft) in length, 6 metres (20 ft) in width, 300 metres (980 ft) above ground
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge was built as a tourist attraction and opened to the public on 20 August 2016. It was the longest and tallest glass-bottomed bridge in the world at the time of its opening. The bridge spans the canyon between two mountain cliffs in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park.

Major_Events.Description: The bridge was opened to the public on 20 August 2016.
Due to overwhelming visitor traffic, the bridge was closed on 2 September 2016, just 13 days after opening. It was reopened on 30 September 2016 after improvements to facilities and services.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The bridge is a suspension bridge made of a steel frame with over 120 glass panels. Each panel is three-layered and 5.1-centimetre-thick (2 in) tempered glass. It has four support pillars on the edges of the canyon walls and features three long swings attached to the underside. The bridge was designed by Israeli architect Haim Dotan.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The bridge is a significant tourist attraction and engineering marvel, setting ten world records in its design and construction. It highlights advancements in architectural and engineering techniques and draws attention to Zhangjiajie National Forest Park.
world knowledge.Details: The bridge was designed to carry up to 800 visitors at a time and was expected to be visited by about 8,000 people per day, but it attracted over 80,000 visitors per day initially. There is a provision for a 285-metre (935 ft) bungee jump, considered the highest in the world. The bridge's record as the longest glass bridge has since been surpassed by a bridge in the Grand Canyon Scenic Area, Hebei.

world knowledge.Name: Pannonian mixed forests
world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The plant communities include mixed oak-hornbeam forests, azoal floodplain vegetation and lowland to montane herb-grass steppes. Mixed oak-hornbeam forests are mixed forests of pedunculate oak and sessile oak and hornbeam. Sub-Mediterranean thermophilous bitter oak forests grow in warmer areas. Higher elevation areas are dominated by European beech and silver birch, downy birch, European aspen and sometimes by conifers Abies alba, Picea abies, Pinus sylvestris, Pinus nigra. Riparian forest and azoal floodplain vegetation occurs along rivers and lakes. Lowland to montane herb-grass steppes dominate large areas of the ecoregion.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Pannonian mixed forests is a temperate broadleaf and mixed forests ecoregion in Europe, covering a vast area and hosting diverse plant communities.

world knowledge.Name: Chinju no Mori
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Chinju-no-mori are forests established and maintained in or around shrines (Chinjugami) in Japan, surrounding temples, Sando, and places of worship. These forests have been preserved since ancient times and are considered to have preserved the original vegetation of the area. They are often the subject of surveys in forest ecology in Japan and are protected as natural monuments.

Major_Events.Description: Many shrines were abolished, and at the same time, their guardian forests were cut down. This was intended to incorporate indigenous beliefs into State Shinto by organizing only one shrine per administrative village.
Widespread deforestation took place as part of national land development, separate from the state Shinto religion. This led to increased reflection on the consequences of excessive development.
There has been a push to maintain and restore the forests affected by the disaster.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Chinju no mori refers to the forest that surrounded many Shinto shrines. In modern Shinto, the shintai of shrine Shinto is understood to be the shrine, such as the main hall and Shinto architecture, which are covered with shimenawa, and the surrounding forests are understood to be the chinju-no-mori.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Chinju no mori are culturally significant as they preserve the original vegetation of the area and are often one of the few clues to the former nature of the area. They are also important in Shinto religion, where nature itself is an object of faith.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: The primary function of Chinju no mori is to serve as sacred groves or forests where kami (spirits or gods) are present. They are also used for forest ecology studies and conservation efforts.
world knowledge.Details: In modern times, the belief in Shinto deities has become more abstract, and the reverence for the dense forests of Shinto shrines has waned. There have been many cases where the shrine forest was cut down to make room for road repairs, agricultural and residential land development, and public facilities such as daycare centers. Some shrines that consist entirely of torii gates and main shrines have completely lost their forests, diminishing the original meaning of shrines based on nature worship.

world knowledge.Name: Higashikurumeshi Chikurin Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Higashikurumeshi Chikurin Park is a bamboo grove with natural spring water, created by taking advantage of the natural shape of the land. It was constructed in 1974 and was selected as one of the 100 New Tokyo Views in 1983.

Major_Events.Event: Selected as one of the 100 New Tokyo Views
Major_Events.Description: The park was recognized as one of the 100 New Tokyo Views, highlighting its scenic and cultural significance.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features a bamboo grove with over 2,000 bamboo trees and a path through the grove, utilizing the natural landscape and spring water.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant for its natural beauty, bamboo grove, and recognition as one of the 100 New Tokyo Views.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Public park and scenic natural area
world knowledge.Details: The park has a path through the bamboo grove and is accessible via Higashi-Kurume Station. This article about a national/quasi-national park or protected area in Japan, or related topic is a stub.

world knowledge.Name: Kasugayama Primeval Forest
world knowledge.Address: Nara Park, Nara, Nara Prefecture, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Kasugayama Primeval Forest is a protected area of primeval forest in Nara, Japan, designated as a Special Natural Monument and part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara. Hunting and logging have been prohibited since 841 during the reign of Emperor Ninmyō.

Major_Events.Description: During the reign of Emperor Ninmyō, hunting and logging on Mount Kasuga were prohibited.
Nara Park was opened after a proclamation by the Dajō-kan in 1873.
Nara Park was extended to include Mount Kasuga and Mount Wakakusa. A typhoon felled around two thousand trees on Mount Kasuga the same year.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as Place of Scenic Beauty
Major_Events.Description: Nara Park was designated a Place of Scenic Beauty under the 1919 Historical Sites, Places of Scenic Beauty, and Natural Monuments Preservation Law.
Kasugayama Primeval Forest was designated a Natural Monument.
Kasugayama Primeval Forest's designation was upgraded to Special Natural Monument under the 1950 Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Kasugayama Primeval Forest is culturally significant as a sacred area protected for over a millennium, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and a rare example of a primeval forest in Japan.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is located east of Kasuga Taisha and is considered a Chinju no Mori (sacred forest). It has been protected from hunting and logging since 841.

world knowledge.Name: Tadasu no Mori
world knowledge.Address: Near the banks of the Kamo River, north of where the Takano River joins the Kamo River, northeast Kyoto city, Japan
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Tadasu no Mori is a sacred grove associated with the Kamo-jinja (Shimogamo Shrine and Kamigamo Shrine), serving to protect Kyoto from malign influences. It is the last remnant of a primeval forest reputed to have never been burned down, though it suffered damage during wars and revolts. The forest was originally much larger but was reduced due to the Onin War and land forfeit ordinances during the Meiji era.

Major_Events.Description: 70% of Tadasu no Mori was burned to the ground during the Onin War.
Some areas of the forest were taken by the Shogunate, reducing its territory to its current size.
Severe flooding drowned much of the forest's vegetation, leading to the planting of camphor trees.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest is left to grow in its natural state, neither planted nor pruned. It is composed mostly of deciduous tree species, especially those commonly found along riversides, including elm, zelkova, and hackberry. The area is bright due to the absence of dense coniferous trees.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Tadasu no Mori is a historic landmark mentioned in ancient texts like "Tale of Genji" and "The Pillow Book." It is part of the Shimogamo Shrine grounds, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto. The forest is a refuge of rest and relaxation and holds ecological and cultural importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sacred grove for Shinto rituals and ecological preservation
world knowledge.Details: The forest spans from the Kamo River to the Takano River upon a narrow strip of land running north-south between the two waterways. It contains about 4,700 trees of 40 distinct species, with many clear-water streams flowing throughout. The forest was designated as a National Historic Site in 1983 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994. It is home to various bird species, including the Brown Hawk-Owl, but large mammals like the Japanese Squirrel have vanished in recent years.

world knowledge.Name: Þjórsárdalur
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Þjórsárdalur is a valley in Iceland that has been shaped by repeated eruptions of nearby volcanoes, including Hekla and the Vatnaöldur volcanic system. The valley features landmarks such as Þjóðveldisbærinn Stöng, a farm covered by Hekla's 1104 eruption and later excavated and rebuilt as a museum.

Major_Events.Description: The eruption covered the farm Þjóðveldisbærinn Stöng in ashes.
The farm was excavated and later rebuilt as a museum to showcase life during the Saga Age.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The valley features natural landmarks like waterfalls, cliffs, and ravines, as well as the reconstructed farm museum Þjóðveldisbærinn Stöng, which illustrates house fixtures and fireplaces from the Saga Age (ca 930-1030).
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Þjórsárdalur is significant for its natural beauty, historical landmarks, and insights into Iceland's Saga Age. The valley's reconstruction efforts and soil reclamation also highlight environmental conservation efforts.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Natural and historical tourism, environmental conservation.
world knowledge.Details: The valley is divided into two parts: Rauðukamba in the east and Bergólfsstaðaá in the west. It features lush vegetation in areas like Gjáin and Búrfell's woods, alongside extensive soil reclamation efforts. Landmarks include Háifoss (one of Iceland's highest waterfalls), Hjálparfoss, and Vegghamrar cliffs. The area also has a hot spring bath and a golf course near Búrfellsvirkjun hydroelectric power station.

world knowledge.Name: Þórsmörk
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Thórsmörk is a mountain ridge named after the Norse god Thor (Þór). It is situated between the glaciers Tindfjallajökull and Eyjafjallajökull. The name properly refers to the mountain ridge between the rivers Krossá, Þröngá, and Markarfljót, but is sometimes used informally to describe a wider area.

Major_Events.Description: During the spring 2010 eruptions of Eyjafjallajökull, much of the area was covered in a thick layer of volcanic ash. Several months were needed for nature to return to normal.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Thórsmörk is named after the Norse god Thor and is one of the most popular hiking areas in Iceland. Its unique geography and warm climate make it culturally and naturally significant.
world knowledge.Details: Thórsmörk is popular amongst hikers, with many different tours possible, including glacier hikes, treks like Laugavegur up to Landmannalaugar, and smaller excursions to places like the canyon Stakkholtsgjá with its waterfall. The Krossá river is a cold, fast river coming down from glaciers, and a bridge allows pedestrians to cross. Coaches arrive daily from Reykjavík and other towns in Iceland. The valley is known for its green vegetation of moss, fern, birchwood, and other small shrubs due to its protected and warm climate.

world knowledge.Name: Abujmarh
world knowledge.Address: Narayanpur district, Bijapur district, Dantewada district, Chhattisgarh, India
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Abujhmarh is a hilly forest area in Chhattisgarh, home to indigenous tribes like Gond, Muria, Abujhmarhia, Madiya, and Halba. It was isolated and restricted from public entry until 2009. The area is known for its inaccessibility and as a hub of Naxalite-Maoist insurgency. It was proposed as a biosphere reserve in 2007 by the Indian government. The name means 'the unknown hills' in the Gondi language.

Major_Events.Description: The Government of Chhattisgarh lifted the restriction on the entry of common people imposed in the early 1980s.
The Government of Chhattisgarh initiated a project to map the area through an aerial survey at the cost of ₹55 million (US$650,000).
Naxals made a coordinated attack on two police outposts adjoining the hills, leading to a 6-hour gun-battle and requiring an army helicopter for rescue.
Maoists attacked a police camp at Ranibodli, killing 55 policemen, including Special Police Officers (SPOs).
Launched in April 2010, but on 7 April, in an ambush by People's Liberation Guerilla Army (PLGA), 76 security persons were killed in Chintalnar.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Abujhmarh is culturally significant as it is home to indigenous tribes and has remained largely untouched by modern civilization. It is also known for its dense forests, rich mineral deposits, and as a hub of Naxalite-Maoist insurgency. The area is mentioned in the Hindu epic Ramayana as Dandakaranya.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Forest area and habitat for indigenous tribes
world knowledge.Details: The area has a population density of less than 4 inhabitants per square kilometre and is home to nearly 27% of the tribal population of Chhattisgarh. The tribes survive on traditional shifting cultivation and forest products. The area remains largely inaccessible for six months a year. It was proposed as a biosphere reserve in 2008 by the Indian government.

world knowledge.Name: Baikunthapur Forest
world knowledge.Area: Terai forest region in the western part of the Dooars in West Bengal, India
world knowledge.Address: South of the Himalayan foothills, between the Mahananda River to the west and Teesta River to the east
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Historically, the Baikunthapur forests were the secure base of the Raikat princes in the time when Koch Bihar was an independent kingdom. The Raikat family were local rulers in the Baikunthapur area between 1523 and 1771, semi-independent rulers related to the Koch dynasty of the Kamata kingdom. The British annexed Baikanthapur in 1771 and the Raikats became Zamindars (tenants) of Baikunthapur. The last Raikat of Baikunthapur died intestate in 1946.

Major_Events.Description: The British annexed Baikanthapur and the Raikats became Zamindars (tenants) of Baikunthapur.
Commercial exploitation of Darjeeling tea began in the area.
An elephant that had strayed out of the Baikunthapur forest range near Jalpaiguri trampled to death one man and injured another.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: It is believed that Lord Krishna went into hiding in the jungles of Baikunthapur with his principal wife and queen Rukmini at one time. For this reason, ISKCON chose nearby Siliguri as the site for the biggest Krishna Centre in the Northeast.

Details.Ecological_Importance: Baikunthapur is an important ecological zone, home to many wild elephants, but is threatened by growth of the local population. The least disturbed areas are in the Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary.
Details.Geological_Features: The northern part of West Bengal is covered by fans of sediment washed down from the Himalayas. The Baikanthapur formation is the youngest fan in the area. It consists of very fine white sand inter-layered with ochre yellow sticky silty clay and overlain by dark grey to thick silty loam.
Details.Environmental_Concerns: Measurements have shown a maximum arsenic content well beyond the permissible limit within a depth range of 10–30m, raising concerns about the possibility of arsenic poisoning in the region and in downstream locations. Deforestation, land clearing, terracing, mining, and construction are contributing to soil erosion and degraded water quality.
Details.Climate: Three main seasons: summer (March to June), monsoons (June to September), and winter (September to February). Summer temperatures range in the mid-30s C. Monsoons bring severe rain, with annual rainfall possibly exceeding 250 cm. Winter temperatures may fall as low as 5 °C.
Details.Land_Use: Today, the area is just 25% forest, 15% tea garden, 43% cultivated and non-cultivated land, and 17% water bodies, residential, hill etc.
Details.Wildlife: Home to many wild elephants. The elephant population in West Bengal is healthy and expanding, leading to human-elephant clashes. The reservoir Gajoldoba is used by many water birds from Ladakh and Central Asia.
Details.Conservation_Efforts: Joint Forest Management activities started in the Baikunthapur area in 1994-95, but have not been fully effective due to lack of local involvement and illegal activities like felling and grazing.

world knowledge.Name: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary
world knowledge.Address: Lakkavalli, Karnataka; nearest cities: Tarikere, Birur, and Bhadravathi
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The area was first declared as 'Jagara Valley Wildlife Sanctuary' in 1951. It was extended and renamed to Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary in 1974. Declared a Project Tiger Reserve in 1998, it was the first tiger reserve in India to complete a successful village relocation program by 2002.

Major_Events.Event: Declaration as Jagara Valley Wildlife Sanctuary
Major_Events.Description: The sanctuary was initially established under this name.

Major_Events.Event: Renaming and extension to Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary
Major_Events.Description: The sanctuary was expanded and renamed.
Bhadra was designated as a tiger reserve under Project Tiger.
26 villages within the sanctuary were successfully relocated to M C Halli.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary is a biodiversity hotspot and a key tiger reserve under Project Tiger. It plays a crucial role in wildlife conservation and is a popular ecotourism destination.

Details.Flora: The sanctuary hosts over 120 plant species, including teak, rosewood, and medicinal plants. Common species include crepe myrtle, kadam, teak, and bamboo.
Details.Fauna: Home to 33 tigers, elephants, Indian leopards, gaurs, sloth bears, and various deer species. It also has over 300 bird species, including endemic and migratory birds.
Details.Topography: Elevation ranges from 615 m to 1,875 m, featuring hills like Mullayanagiri and Hebbegiri. The sanctuary includes waterfalls like Hebbe Falls and Manikyadhara Falls.
Details.Threats: Human encroachment, livestock grazing, timber smuggling, and poaching pose significant threats. Diseases from cattle have historically impacted wildlife populations.
Details.Management: Managed by the Karnataka Forest Department, efforts include habitat improvement, anti-poaching measures, and infrastructure development, though funding and staffing are challenges.

world knowledge.Name: Bhitarkanika Mangroves
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Bhitarkanika Mangroves were zamindari forests until 1952, when the government of Odisha abolished the zamindari system and put the forests under the state forest department. In 1975, an area of 672 km2 was declared the Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary. The core area of the sanctuary, with an area of 145 km2, was declared Bhitarkanika National Park in September 1998. The Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary, which bounds the Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary to the east, was created in September 1997. Bhitarkanika Mangroves were designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2002.

Major_Events.Description: The government of Odisha abolished the zamindari system, and put the zamindari forests in the control of the state forest department.
An area of 672 km2 was declared the Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary.
The core area of the sanctuary, with an area of 145 km2, was declared Bhitarkanika National Park.
Bhitarkanika Mangroves were designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Bhitarkanika Mangroves are ecologically significant as they host a diverse range of flora and fauna, including 62 mangrove species, saltwater crocodiles, king cobras, Indian pythons, and water monitors. It is also a critical nesting site for olive ridley turtles. The area is designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance, highlighting its global ecological value.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of biodiversity and natural habitat
world knowledge.Details: About 62 mangrove species occur in the Bhitarkanika Mangroves, including Avicenna, Bruguiera, Heritiera, and Rhizophora. Reptiles present include saltwater crocodile, king cobra, Indian python, and water monitor. Between August 2004 and December 2006, 263 bird species were recorded, encompassing 147 resident and 99 migrant species. A heronry encloses about 4 ha (9.9 acres), where 11,287 nests were counted in 2006. Olive ridley turtles arrive in January to March for nesting at Gahirmatha Beach. An average of 240,000 nests per season was estimated between 1976 and 1996. Up to 80,000 turtles were captured every year until 1982. Since 1983, collecting and marketing turtles and their eggs has been banned.

world knowledge.Name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Keibul Lamjao National Park is the only floating national park in the world, characterized by floating decomposed plant material called phumdi. It was created in 1966 as a wildlife sanctuary to protect the endangered Eld's deer (Cervus eldi eldi) and gazetted as a national park in 1977. The park is an integral part of Loktak Lake and is currently under the tentative lists of UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Major_Events.Description: Created to preserve the natural habitat of the endangered Eld's deer.
Upgraded to national park status to further protect the brow-antlered deer (Sangai).
The deer, thought extinct in 1951, was rediscovered in the park by environmentalist E.P. Gee.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park is a swamp with floating masses of vegetation (phumdis) formed by organic detritus and biomass. It features a unique aquatic, wetland, and terrestrial ecosystem with moist semi-evergreen forests and grasslands. The park's structure varies seasonally due to the floating phumdis.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant as it is home to the Sangai deer, which holds a pride of place in Manipuri folklore and culture. It is also the state animal of Manipur. The park's unique floating ecosystem is of global ecological importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation of the endangered brow-antlered deer (Sangai) and its unique floating habitat.

Details.Flora: Aquatic flora include Zizania latifolia, Tripidium bengalense, Eichhornia crassipes, and others. The park has two types of phumdis: floating (ataoba) and sinking (aruppa).
Details.Fauna: Apart from the brow-antlered deer, the park hosts species like the East Himalayan pied kingfisher, black kite, and hooded crane.
Details.Threats: Threats include habitat degradation due to water level changes from the Loktak Hydro Electric Power Project and human encroachment.
Details.Conservation_Measures: Strict protection of core areas, habitat monitoring, and management plans for long-term conservation.
Details.Accessibility: Approachable by road, rail, and air via Imphal. Boat trips are the primary way to explore the park.
Details.Tourism: Best visited between 0600-1000 hrs and 1530-1800 hrs for deer sightings. Manipur Tourism Department arranges guided tours.
Details.Accommodation: Basic forest rest houses are available at Phubala and Sendra islands. Imphal offers better hotel facilities.

world knowledge.Name: Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary
world knowledge.Location: Verlem, Sanguem Taluka region, around 65km from Goa Airport
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The sanctuary hosts remnants of ancient forests featuring the distinctive Myristica swamp ecosystem, which dates back over 100 million years.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary constitutes one of the vital corridors of the Western Ghats and sustains a rich biodiversity, including rare and endangered species.

Details.Tributary: Netravali or Neturli, an important tributary of River Zuari, originates in the sanctuary.
Details.Vegetation: Forests mostly consist of moist deciduous vegetation interspersed with evergreen and semi-evergreen habitat.
Details.Waterfalls: There are two all-season waterfalls in the sanctuary.
Adjacent_Protected_Areas: Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park (northern side)

world knowledge.Name: Alto Tajo Nature Reserve
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The park was established as a Natural Reserve and gained recognition for its natural beauty and ecological importance. It has been featured in literature and film, including José Luis Sampedro's novel 'El río que nos lleva' (1961) and the TV series 'Game of Thrones' (season 6).

Major_Events.Description: Mining in the area began in the 1960s with an English multinational company called ECC being the sole miner for 20 years before they pulled out of the country.
The park was one of the filming locations for 'Game of Thrones' (season 6).

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The park features canyons and gorges formed by the Tagus river and its tributaries, pine forests, and imposing cliffs.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The park is culturally significant due to its natural beauty, ecological importance, and its role in literature and film. It is also a symbol of the conflict between environmental conservation and economic interests due to ongoing kaolinite mining.
world knowledge.Details: The park has been threatened by kaolinite mining, which contributes to 13.5% of all jobs in the area. Currently, two mines are operational in Poveda de la Sierra, affecting around 100 hectares. Runoffs from the mines are polluting the Tagus River and affecting its fauna. Mining companies hold rights for 90 years and have been reluctant to stop without proper compensation.

world knowledge.Name: Fageda d'en Jordà
world knowledge.Address: Can Serra car park, kilometer 4 of the road from Olot to Santa Pau
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Fageda d'en Jordà is a natural reserve featuring a beech forest that grows on a cooled lava flow from the volcano del Croscat. It is famous for the poem written by Catalan poet Joan Maragall. The forest is part of the Garrotxa Volcanic Zone natural park and is surrounded by several volcanoes.

Major_Events.Description: The Catalan poet Joan Maragall wrote a well-known poem about the beech forest, titled 'La fageda d'en Jordà.'

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest is characterized by medium and large beech trees growing on relatively flat terrain with spatter cones (tossols) that can reach more than 20 m in height. The substrate consists of reddish clays, andosols, and other brown soils.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The beech forest is culturally significant due to its unique characteristics in Catalonia and Spain, its association with Joan Maragall's poem, and its role as part of the Garrotxa Volcanic Zone natural park. It also hosts the La Fageda cooperative, which employs mentally handicapped people.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is located about 5.5 km from Olot and occupies parts of the municipalities of Santa Pau, Olot, and Les Preses. Motor vehicles are prohibited within the forest, but there are walking routes and options to rent a horse or horse-drawn carriage. The Can Jordà farmhouse, which gives the forest its name, is now a Cultivated Plant Conservation Center.

world knowledge.Name: Soto de Viñuelas
world knowledge.Address: North of Madrid, south of Tres Cantos and San Agustín del Guadalix, east of Monte de El Pardo, west of San Sebastián de los Reyes
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Originally part of the lordship of Real de Manzanares, owned by the Casa de Mendoza. Passed to Emperor Charles I in the 16th century. Acquired by Cristobal Alvarado Bracamonte in 1693, who rebuilt the manor house. Spanish Crown took over in 1751. Auctioned off after the fall of Isabella II of Spain. Served as Republican Army headquarters during the Spanish Civil War, later became Francisco Franco's official residence.

Major_Events.Description: Rebuilt the manor house, now known as Castle Viñuelas, to facilitate the stay of Philip V.
Added to the Royal Site of El Pardo at the request of Ferdinand VI.

Major_Events.Event: Auction after fall of Isabella II
Major_Events.Description: Site was auctioned off after the fall of Isabella II of Spain.
Castle served as headquarters of the Republican Army.
Chosen by Francisco Franco as his official residence, named the 'Royal Palace of El Pardo'.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Manor house rebuilt into Castle Viñuelas.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Important ecological, landscape, and artistic values. Part of the Regional Park of the Cuenca Alta del Manzanares, the largest protected natural area in the region. Classified as Special Protection Area for Birds.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Protected natural area and historical site.
world knowledge.Details: Much of it is a fenced property. Includes developments like Ciudalcampo and Fuente del Fresno. King's College, the British School of Madrid, is located nearby. Accessible via M-607 Freeway exit 20. Public transport options include bus line 716 and local bus line L-3.

world knowledge.Name: Açu National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Assu, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Açu Forest Park (Horto Florestal de Açu) was created by law 1.175 on 10 August 1950. It was made a national forest by ordinance 245 of 18 July 2001. It is the first national forest in Rio Grande do Norte and the third in the north east region. It was created due to a popular movement by the Defence Committee of the National Forest.

Major_Events.Description: The Açu Forest Park was created by law 1.175 on 10 August 1950.
The Açu Forest Park was made a national forest by ordinance 245 of 18 July 2001.
An advisory council was appointed on 28 August 2008.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The terrain is flat or slightly undulating. The only body of water is Lago do Piató, which has a maximum depth of 10 metres (33 ft). It used to be fed by flood water from the Piranhas River, but since the construction of a dam on the Piranhas no longer receives water from the river.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Açu National Forest is the first national forest in Rio Grande do Norte and the third in the north east region. It was created due to a popular movement by the Defence Committee of the National Forest.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is mostly covered by typical Caatinga shrub and trees, with many cactuses. There are small populations of carnauba. 62 species from 46 genera have been identified, mostly from the families Fabaceae, Euphorbiaceae, Cactaceae and Boraginaceae. Typical species are Croton sonderianus, Caesalpinia pyramidalis, Auxemma glazioviana, Dipteryx odorata and Tabebuia impetiginosa. The forest, with its rich vegetation, is home to various species of birds, reptiles and mammals such as armadillos, cavy, pampas deer and marmoset.

world knowledge.Name: Amaná National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Amaná National Forest was created by decree on 13 February 2006 as part of the planning process for land management and environment protection along the BR-163 trans-Amazon highway. It is administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio).

Major_Events.Description: The Amaná National Forest was established by decree on 13 February 2006.
The 2009 annual plan authorized the grant of five forestry units totaling 210,000 hectares (520,000 acres).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Amaná National Forest is culturally and environmentally significant as it supports sustainable multiple use of forest resources, maintains and protects water resources and biodiversity, and allows for sustainable exploitation of natural resources, including mining under its management plan.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable forestry, community forestry, and biodiversity conservation

Details.Administrator: Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation
Details.Land_Usage_Zones: Six land usage zones defined by the management plan
Details.Protected_Areas: Part of a region containing 12 sustainable use conservation areas and 6 fully protected areas, including national parks, biological reserves, and ecological stations.

world knowledge.Name: Anauá National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Anauá National Forest was created as an initiative of the citizens of Rorainópolis in cooperation with the local logging association to establish a protected area with sustainable land use. It is managed by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation.

Major_Events.Description: The forest was officially established as a protected area to promote sustainable land use.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is named after the Anauá River, which means 'flowering tree' in the Tupi language. It represents an effort to balance environmental conservation with sustainable economic activities.
world knowledge.Details: The Anauá National Forest is a densely forested rainforest influenced by several tributaries of the Branco River. A threat to the forest is the activity of illegal loggers.

world knowledge.Name: Balata-Tufari National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Balata-Tufari National Forest was created to support sustainable extraction of forest products such as timber subject to restrictions and regulations defined by law or the responsible agency, ICMBio. It covers parts of the municipalities of Canutama (90.85%) and Tapauá (9.15%) in the state of Amazonas.

Major_Events.Description: The Balata-Tufari National Forest was created by decree on 17 February 2005.
On 8 May 2008, a fourth area was added to the national forest, Area 4 with 275,836 hectares (681,610 acres).
The advisory council was formed on 14 December 2010.
An ordinance of 9 January 2012 provided for a consistent and integrated approach to preparing management plans for the conservation units in the BR-319 area of influence.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Balata-Tufari National Forest is culturally significant for its role in sustainable forest management and conservation. It supports local communities, including about 2000 families, mostly farmers who own or lease small plots. The forest also has great potential for sustainable extraction of timber and other forest products like oils, resins, nuts, seeds, and fruits.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests.
world knowledge.Details: The national forest is bounded by the Purus River to the west, by the first section of the Trans-Amazonian Highway (BR-230) from Lábrea to Humaitá which cuts across its southern end, and by BR-319 to the east. The Mucuim River runs through the forest, flowing north from the Mapinguari National Park, which lies to the south of BR-230. The Mucuim is joined within the forest by the Açuã River, which rises in the Mapinguari National Park. 2.47% of the national forest's area overlaps with the Mapinguari National Park. The national forest is in the Amazon biome and contains 91.44% open rainforest, 6.45% dense rainforest and 2.11% contact between savannah and rainforest. It is classed as IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources). The forest had three areas when created: Gleba Balata with 282,781 hectares (698,770 acres), Gleba Tufari with 360,168 hectares (889,990 acres) and Gleba Jacaré with 159,074 hectares (393,080 acres).

world knowledge.Name: Carajás National Forest
world knowledge.Area: Serra dos Carajás (Carajás Mountains), Pará, Brazil
world knowledge.Address: Covers parts of the municipalities of Canaã dos Carajás, Parauapebas and Água Azul do Norte in the state of Pará
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Carajás National Forest was created by decree on 2 February 1998. It covers the Serra dos Carajás, an area with large deposits of iron ore discovered accidentally by U.S. Steel in the 1960s. In 1970, a joint venture was formed to exploit the deposit, with Vale acquiring full ownership in 1977. Mining operations began in 1985. The forest was established to reconcile mineral extraction with environmental preservation and biodiversity.

Major_Events.Description: Discovered accidentally by U.S. Steel.
Vale and U.S. Steel formed a joint venture to exploit the iron ore deposits.
Vale acquired full ownership of the mining operations.
Vale began mining operations in the Carajás Mountains.
Established by decree to combine mineral extraction with environmental preservation.
Management plan prepared by Brazilian Institute of Environment and Renewable Natural Resources and Vale was approved.
Vale obtained an installation license for the Carajás S11D iron ore project, the largest in the company's history.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Carajás National Forest is significant for its efforts to balance mineral extraction with environmental conservation. It protects biodiversity, including species like Uta Hick's bearded saki and the jaguar, and supports scientific research and ecotourism.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources, scientific research, and mineral extraction.

Details.Biodiversity: 594 species of birds, 68 amphibians, 131 reptiles, and 44 large and medium-sized mammals have been catalogued.
Details.Administration: Administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio).
Details.IUCN_Category: VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources)
Details.Mining_Operations: Vale occupies only 3% of the concession area. The Carajás Mine produced 301Mt of iron ore in 2008.
Details.Ecological_Corridor: Proposed South Amazon Ecological Corridor would link the forest to other protected areas and indigenous territories.

world knowledge.Name: Iquiri National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Iquiri National Forest was created by decree on 8 May 2008 and is administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio). It is a sustainable use conservation unit, allowing harvesting of forest resources in accordance with a management plan.

Major_Events.Description: An advisory council for the Iquiri forest was created on 26 October 2012.
An ordinance of 9 January 2012 provided for a consistent and integrated approach to preparing management plans for the conservation units in the BR-319 area of influence.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Iquiri National Forest is culturally and environmentally significant as it supports sustainable multiple use of forest resources, maintenance and protection of water resources and biodiversity, recovery of degraded areas, and scientific research. It is part of the Amazon biome and contains dense and open rainforest.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources, biodiversity conservation, and scientific research.
world knowledge.Details: The forest contains 73.05% dense rainforest and 26.95% open rainforest. It has great potential for sustainable harvesting of timber and other forest products such as oils, resins, nuts, seeds, and fruits. It is classed as IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources).

world knowledge.Name: Itaituba I National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Municipalities of Itaituba and Trairão, state of Pará, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Itaituba I National Forest was created by decree nº 2.481 of 2 February 1998. It is part of a region that contains multiple sustainable use and fully protected areas.

Major_Events.Description: Law 12678 of 25 June 2012 amended the limits of the Itaituba I National Forest, reducing it by 7,705.34 hectares (19,040.3 acres).

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is significant for its sustainable use of natural resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research.

Details.Access: Accessible by land via BR-163 and BR-230 highways, or by boat via the Tapajós and Jamanxim rivers and their tributaries. There are some airstrips in and around the forest.
Details.Rivers: Tributaries of the Tapajos include the Cururu, das Tropas, Cupari, and Jamanxim.
Details.Vegetation: 98.9% of the area is occupied by natural forests, including 27.8% open submontane rainforest and 65.96% a mixture of dense and open submontane rainforest.
Details.Administration: Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio)
Details.Protected_Area_Status: IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources).
Details.Adjacent_Areas: The national forest is in a region that contains 12 sustainable use conservation areas and 6 fully protected areas.

world knowledge.Name: Macauã National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Municipality of Sena Madureira, Acre, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Macauã National Forest was created by presidential decree 96.189 of 21 June 1988. It is administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio). The forest is home to families descended from rubber tappers who came to the region in the late 19th century. After the decline of the rubber industry, they turned to raising crops and extracting timber and nuts for money.

Major_Events.Description: Established by presidential decree 96.189 on 21 June 1988.
A consultative council for the Macauã and São Francisco national forests was created on 18 January 2002.
Recognized by the Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária as an agro-extractive project for 35 families on 23 August 2006.
The management plan for the Macauã and São Francisco national forests was approved on 20 May 2016.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest supports sustainable use of forest resources and scientific research with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests. It is also home to families with a historical connection to the rubber-tapping industry, preserving their way of life and traditional practices.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable use of forest resources, scientific research, and conservation.

Details.Bounding_Areas: Cazumbá-Iracema Extractive Reserve (west and north), São Francisco National Forest (southeast)
Details.Boundary_River: Macauã River (forms most of its southeast boundary)
Details.IUCN_Category: VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources)

Residents.Organization: Associação de Extrativistas da Floresta Nacional do Macauã e Área de Entorno (ASSEXMA)

Economic_Activities.Wood_Production: 32,000 hectares (79,000 acres) producing 24,000 cubic metres (850,000 cu ft) annually

world knowledge.Name: Mapiá-Inauini National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Mapiá-Inauini National Forest was created by federal decree 98.051 on 14 August 1989. It is administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio) and is classed as IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources). The objectives are sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research with emphasis on methods of sustainable exploitation of native forests.

Major_Events.Description: The Mapiá-Inauini National Forest was established by federal decree 98.051 on 14 August 1989.

On 26 September 2005, the Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (INCRA) recognized the state forest as supporting 100 families of small rural producers, who would qualify for PRONAF support.
On 31 December 2008, the number of families supported by the forest was modified to 200.
The management plan was approved on 18 August 2009.
The consultative council was created on 11 March 2010.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Mapiá-Inauini National Forest is culturally significant as it supports sustainable use of forest resources and scientific research. It also provides livelihoods for local communities who gather Brazil nuts and plant cassava, selling these products in Boca do Acre.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is divided between the municipalities of Boca do Acre (92.37%) and Pauini (7.63%) in the state of Amazonas. It is in the Purus River basin and adjoins the Purus National Forest to the east and the Arapixi Extractive Reserve to the south. The Inauini/Teuini Indigenous Territory is to the north, and the Igarapé Capanã and Camicuã indigenous territories adjoin the forest to the south. The national forest overlaps 1.39% with indigenous territories. Vegetation is 70% dense rainforest and 30% open rainforest. Local residents have complained about intruders fishing and collecting turtles, leading to a sharp drop in the turtle population.

world knowledge.Name: Passa Quatro National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Passa Quatro National Forest was created by federal ordinance 562 of 25 October 1968. It was initially administered by the Instituto Nacional do Pinho (INP) and is now managed by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation.

Major_Events.Description: The forest was established by federal ordinance on 25 October 1968.
The forest became part of the Mantiqueira Mosaic of conservation units.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is important for its remnants of Atlantic Forest and its role in conservation of water resources and biological diversity. It also serves as a location for environmental education and outdoor recreation.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests.
world knowledge.Details: The forest contains important remnants of Atlantic Forest as well as monocultures of Araucaria angustifolia, Pinus species, and Eucalyptus species. Protected species include the maned wolf, ocelot, and cougar. The Iporã waterfall is the main attraction, and the forest features picnic areas, ornamental lakes, squares, gardens, a gazebo, a playground, and a plant nursery. It is part of the Serra da Mantiqueira Ecological Corridor and is classified as IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources).

world knowledge.Name: São Francisco National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Municipality of Sena Madureira, Acre, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The São Francisco National Forest was created by federal decree on 7 August 2001. It is administered by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation (ICMBio). It is classed as IUCN protected area category VI (protected area with sustainable use of natural resources). The objective is to support sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests.

Major_Events.Description: The consultative council of the Macauã and São Francisco national forests was created.
The Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (National Institute for Colonization and Agrarian Reform, INCRA) recognised the forest as an agro-extractive project for 25 families.
INCRA assigned the forest to ICMBio.
The management plan was approved.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The São Francisco National Forest is culturally significant as it supports sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for sustainable exploitation of native forests. It is part of the Amazon biome and adjoins other protected areas like the Macauã National Forest and the Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research
world knowledge.Details: The Macauã River runs through the northern part of the forest. It adjoins the Macauã National Forest, which lies to the north. The Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve is some distance to the south, on the opposite side of the Iaco River.

image_name: São Francisco de Paula National Forest

world knowledge.Name: São Francisco de Paula National Forest
world knowledge.Address: São Francisco de Paula, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The São Francisco de Paula National Forest was established by the National Pine Institute, a federal agency created in 1941 to manage pine trees. It became a national forest under the Forest Code of 1965. The forest is part of the Atlantic Forest biome and plays a key role in biodiversity conservation and sustainable resource use.

Major_Events.Event: Creation of the National Pine Institute
Major_Events.Description: Decree law 3.124 created the National Pine Institute, which later established the national forests in southern and southeastern Brazil.
By ordinance 561, the forest was officially classed as a national forest under the Forest Code of 1965.
