Burned 18,247 acres (73.84 km²) and 346 homes.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: Much of the bedrock within Pike National Forest is made up of the coarse, pink to orange Pikes Peak granite.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is culturally significant due to its association with American explorer Zebulon Pike and its role in conservation and recreation. It also plays a vital role in the local ecosystem and water supply.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and natural resource management.
world knowledge.Details: The forest encompasses 1,106,604 acres (4,478 km²) within Clear Creek, Teller, Park, Jefferson, Douglas and El Paso counties. The major rivers draining the forest are the South Platte and Fountain Creek. Rampart Reservoir is a large artificial body of water located within the forest. The forest experiences a Highland climate with warm summers and cold winters, receiving more than 100 inches of snow a year in most areas. There are three officially designated wilderness areas within the forest. The Pike and San Isabel National Forest was awarded a major reclamation project to fix the damage from the Hayman wildfire, sponsored by The National Arbor Day Foundation and several university bookstores.

world knowledge.Name: Plumas National Forest
world knowledge.Address: Plumas National Forest Supervisor's office in Quincy, California
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Plumas National Forest was established as the Plumas Forest Reserve by the United States General Land Office on March 27, 1905. It was transferred to the United States Forest Service in 1906 and became a National Forest on March 4, 1907. A portion of Diamond Mountain National Forest was added on July 1, 1908. The Bucks Lake Wilderness was officially designated in 1984 as a part of the National Wilderness Preservation System.

Major_Events.Description: The forest was established by the United States General Land Office.

Major_Events.Event: Transfer to United States Forest Service
Major_Events.Description: The forest was transferred to the United States Forest Service.
The forest became a National Forest.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of Diamond Mountain National Forest
Major_Events.Description: A portion of Diamond Mountain National Forest was added to Plumas National Forest.
The Bucks Lake Wilderness was officially designated as a part of the National Wilderness Preservation System.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest features mixed conifer forests, with 127,000 acres identified as old-growth in a 2002 study. Virtually no virgin timberland exists due to extensive logging since the gold rush.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Plumas National Forest is culturally significant due to its historical role in logging and its designation as part of the National Wilderness Preservation System. It is also named after its primary watershed, the Feather River.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and natural resource management.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is managed by the United States Forest Service under the Department of Agriculture. It is subdivided into three Ranger Districts: the Beckwourth Ranger District, the Feather River Ranger District, and the Mt. Hough Ranger District. About 85% of the forest lies in Plumas County, with portions extending into eastern Butte, northern Sierra, southern Lassen, and northeastern Yuba counties.

world knowledge.Name: Rogue River–Siskiyou National Forest
world knowledge.Area: Southern Oregon and Northern California, United States
world knowledge.Address: Forest headquarters are located in Medford, Oregon
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Rogue River–Siskiyou National Forest was formed by the administrative combination of the formerly separate Rogue River and Siskiyou National Forests in 2004. The Siskiyou National Forest was established on October 5, 1906, and the Rogue River National Forest traces its establishment back to the creation of the Ashland Forest Reserve on September 28, 1893. The lands were transferred to the Forest Service in 1906, and it became a National Forest on March 4, 1907.

Major_Events.Description: An airplane dropped bombs on Mount Emily in the Siskiyou National Forest, which exploded and started a fire. Bomb fragments had Japanese markings, and it was later confirmed that the plane was indeed Japanese. This was the second bombing of the continental United States by an enemy aircraft.
A massive fire burned nearly 500,000 acres (200,000 ha), including much of the Kalmiopsis Wilderness.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The national forest is mountainous and includes parts of the Southern Oregon Coast Range, the Klamath Mountains, and the Cascade Range. It contains stands of old growth, including Port Orford cedar and Douglas fir, as well as Blue Oak and Canyon live oak. The world's tallest pine tree, a 268.35-foot (81.79 m) ponderosa, is located in the forest.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Rogue River–Siskiyou National Forest is significant for its biodiversity, old-growth forests, and historical events such as the Lookout Air Raids. It also contains eight separate wilderness areas, adding up to 565,900 acres (229,000 ha).
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and natural resource management
world knowledge.Details: The forest is home to the Rogue River, which originates in the Cascade Range and flows through the Klamath Mountains and Coast Range. Other major rivers include the Illinois River, Sixes, Elk, Pistol, Chetco, and Winchuck rivers. The forest receives approximately 915,000 visitors annually.

world knowledge.Name: Sawtooth National Forest
world knowledge.Area: Blaine, Boise, Camas, Cassia, Custer, Elmore, Oneida, Power, and Twin Falls counties, Idaho, and Box Elder County, Utah, United States
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sawtooth National Forest was originally named the Sawtooth Forest Reserve in a proclamation issued by President Theodore Roosevelt on May 29, 1905. It was later designated as the Sawtooth National Recreation Area (SNRA) on August 22, 1972. The forest has a rich history of Native American occupation, early European exploration, mining, and logging. It is now managed for conservation, recreation, and resource extraction.

Major_Events.Description: President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed the area as the Sawtooth Forest Reserve.

Major_Events.Event: Designation as Sawtooth National Recreation Area
Major_Events.Description: A portion of the forest was designated as the Sawtooth National Recreation Area (SNRA), which includes several wilderness areas.
President Barack Obama signed the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and Jerry Peak Wilderness Additions Act, creating three new wilderness areas.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest features diverse landscapes including sagebrush steppe, spruce-fir forests, alpine tundra, and over 1,100 lakes and 3,500 miles of rivers and streams. It includes mountain ranges such as the Sawtooth, White Cloud, and Boulder Mountains.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Sawtooth National Forest is culturally significant for its Native American heritage, early European exploration, and its role in conservation and recreation. It is home to unique species and ecosystems, and it provides opportunities for outdoor activities and scientific research.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and resource extraction including timber, grazing, and mineral resources.
world knowledge.Details: The forest is managed by the U.S. Forest Service and includes four units: the SNRA and the Fairfield, Ketchum, and Minidoka Ranger Districts. It offers facilities for recreation, including skiing, boating, hunting, camping, and hiking. The forest is also home to unique species such as Christ's Indian paintbrush and the South Hills crossbill.

world knowledge.Name: Sequoia National Forest
world knowledge.Area: southern Sierra Nevada mountains of California
world knowledge.Address: Tulare / Kern / Fresno counties, California, US
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Sequoia National Forest was established on July 1, 1908, from a portion of Sierra Forest Reserve. On March 2, 1909, Theodore Roosevelt added land by Presidential Proclamation. On July 1, 1910, 1,951,191 acres were removed to create the Kern National Forest, but this land was returned on July 1, 1915. The Giant Sequoia National Monument was proclaimed by President Bill Clinton on April 15, 2000.

Major_Events.Description: Created from a portion of Sierra Forest Reserve.

Major_Events.Event: Addition of land by Theodore Roosevelt
Major_Events.Description: Land was added by Presidential Proclamation.
1,951,191 acres were removed from Sequoia National Forest to create Kern National Forest.

Major_Events.Event: Return of land to Sequoia National Forest
Major_Events.Description: Land previously removed for Kern National Forest was returned.

Major_Events.Event: Proclamation of Giant Sequoia National Monument
Major_Events.Description: President Bill Clinton proclaimed 328,000 acres of the forest as the Giant Sequoia National Monument.
Burned 131,087 acres, including 13,600 acres of giant sequoia groves, killing over 7500-10,600 mature sequoia trees.
Burned over 97,528 acres, including over 1,000 giant sequoias destroyed.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest features glacier-carved landscapes, impressive granite monoliths, and 38 distinct groves of Giant Sequoia trees. The Needles are a series of granite spires atop a narrow ridge above the Kern River.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is home to majestic Giant Sequoia trees, some of the largest and oldest living organisms on Earth. It is part of the National Wilderness Preservation System and includes the Giant Sequoia National Monument, highlighting its ecological and historical importance.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and education. The forest hosts camping, hiking, and other recreational activities while protecting biodiversity and natural landscapes.
world knowledge.Details: The forest contains over 2,500 miles of road and 850 miles of trails. It has six wilderness areas and four distinct ecological zones, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including black bears, mule deer, and the threatened Little Kern golden trout. The forest is adjacent to Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks.

world knowledge.Name: Siuslaw National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Established in 1908, the Siuslaw National Forest is made up of a wide variety of ecosystems, ranging from coastal forests to sand dunes. It encompasses more than 630,000 acres along the central Oregon Coast between Coos Bay and Tillamook.

Major_Events.Description: The forest was officially established on July 1, 1908.
Three officially designated wilderness areas were established within the forest as part of the National Wilderness Preservation System.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The forest features diverse ecosystems including coastal forests, sand dunes, rivers, streams, and lakes. Major vegetation zones include Sitka spruce near the coast and western hemlock and Douglas fir inland. Other tree species include western red cedar, red alder, and bigleaf maple.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Siuslaw National Forest is culturally and ecologically significant due to its diverse ecosystems, recreational opportunities, and preservation of old-growth forests. It includes designated wilderness areas and is a vital habitat for numerous aquatic and terrestrial species.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and natural resource management.
world knowledge.Details: The forest includes the Sand Lake Recreation Area and the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area. It is managed by the United States Forest Service, with the Forest Supervisor's office located in Corvallis. The forest is divided into two ranger districts: the Hebo Ranger District and the Central Coast Ranger District. Recreational activities include fishing, camping, hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking, exploring tide pools, and riding off-highway vehicles.

world knowledge.Name: Tongass National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: The Tongass National Forest, the largest U.S. National Forest, was established through a series of presidential proclamations starting in 1902. It was created by joining the Alexander Archipelago Forest Reserve and the Tongass National Forest in 1908. The forest has been a site of significant historical events, including legal battles over indigenous land rights and logging controversies.

Major_Events.Description: President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed the establishment of the Tongass National Forest.
A plane crash in the Tongass National Forest killed all 111 people on board.
This act reshaped the logging industry's relationship with the Tongass National Forest, canceling subsidies and establishing new wilderness areas.
The Roadless Initiative passed, preventing the construction of new roads in roadless areas of U.S. national forests, including the Tongass.
The Biden administration announced the end of large-scale, old-growth timber sales in the Tongass National Forest, focusing instead on restoration and recreation.

world knowledge.Architectural_Characteristics: The Tongass National Forest is primarily a temperate rainforest, featuring islands of the Alexander Archipelago, fjords, glaciers, and peaks of the Coast Mountains. The terrain includes karst (limestone rock) and granite, with diverse flora and fauna.
world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The Tongass is culturally significant as the traditional land of the Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian peoples. It is also a critical area for biodiversity, often referred to as the 'crown jewel' of the U.S. National Forest system. The forest plays a vital role in the local economy through tourism, recreation, and subsistence activities.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and sustainable resource management.
world knowledge.Details: The Tongass National Forest is Earth's largest remaining temperate rainforest, home to unique wildlife such as the Haida ermine, five species of salmon, brown and black bears, and bald eagles. It includes 19 designated wilderness areas, more than any other national forest. The forest is a major carbon sink and supports over 10,000 jobs through tourism and fishing.

world knowledge.Name: White River National Forest
world knowledge.Historical_Background: White River National Forest is named after the White River that passes through its northern section. It is the most visited National Forest in the United States, primarily due to the twelve ski areas within its boundaries. It provides significant habitat for various wildlife species and contains numerous streams, lakes, and reservoirs.

Major_Events.Description: The Dillon Ranger district was transferred from the Arapahoe National Forest to the White River National Forest.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: The forest is culturally significant due to its recreational opportunities, including skiing, hiking, and wildlife observation. It also plays a crucial role in wildlife conservation and water resource management.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Conservation, recreation, and wildlife habitat protection

Details.Wildlife: Deer, elk, mountain sheep, mountain goat, bear, mountain lion, bobcat, lynx, moose, raptors, waterfowl, trout, and many other species.
Details.Infrastructure: 1,900 mi. (3,058 km) of forest system roads, 2,500 mi (4,023 km) of trails, and the Dillon, Green Mountain, Ruedi, and Homestake reservoirs.
Details.Counties: Eagle, Pitkin, Garfield, Summit, Rio Blanco, Mesa, Gunnison, Routt, and Moffat counties.
Details.Ski_Areas: Twelve ski areas are located within the forest.
Details.Peaks: Ten peaks with an elevation higher than 14,000 ft (4,267 m), colloquially known as 14ers.
Details.Management: Managed from Forest Service offices in Glenwood Springs with local ranger district offices in Aspen, Carbondale, Eagle, Meeker, Minturn, Rifle, and Silverthorne.
Details.Wilderness_Areas: Eight officially designated wilderness areas within the forest.

world knowledge.Name: Krokskogen
world knowledge.Historical_Background: Krokskogen is a forested area outside Oslo, Norway, part of Oslomarka. It is bordered by Oslo and the municipalities of Ringerike, Hole, and Bærum. The old road through Krokskogen, opened in 1805, was part of the King's Road (Ringeriksveien) from Oslo to Bergen.

Major_Events.Event: Opening of the old road through Krokskogen
Major_Events.Description: The road was part of the King's Road (Ringeriksveien) from Oslo to Bergen.

world knowledge.Cultural_Significance: Krokskogen is a significant natural area with historical importance due to its role as part of the King's Road between Oslo and Bergen. It is now a popular area for hiking and timber transport.
world knowledge.Primary_Function: Forested area used for hiking, bridle path in season, and timber transport during winter.
world knowledge.Details: The highest points in the landscape are Oppkuven (704 m.), Ringkollen (702 m), and Gyrihaugen (682 m). The old road is now mostly used as a hiking trail and bridle path in season and for timber transport during the winter.
